idea-plugin.name: smart-code-pdx
idea-plugin.description:
Smart Code PDX is an IntelliJ IDEA productivity plugin for everyday Java development. It helps developers collect code snippets, generate MyBatis Plus style code from MySQL CREATE TABLE SQL, create variable names, and translate between Chinese and English.

派大星助手 是一个面向日常 Java 开发的 IntelliJ IDEA 辅助插件。

  • 选中代码后右键收藏，并在右侧工具窗口中浏览、复制、删除代码片段。
  • 框选 MySQL 建表 SQL 后生成 MyBatis Plus 风格的 Entity、Controller、Service、Mapper 和 XML 代码。
  • 变量命名支持中文含义转英文 lowerCamelCase 命名。
  • 中英翻译支持腾讯翻译和有道翻译多环境密钥配置，并支持接口失败后自动兜底。
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Added encrypted import and export for code favorites, generator package settings, and translation profiles.
  • Improved plugin icons and added a dedicated configuration transfer page.
  • 支持加密导入导出代码收藏夹、代码生成包路径和翻译密钥配置。

idea-plugin.name: GenAI Capture
idea-plugin.description:
Capture and annotate screenshots without ever leaving your IDE. Grab the whole desktop, mark it up with a full annotation toolkit, then copy, save, or pin the result — in a single keystroke.

What you can do

  • Capture the full (multi-monitor) desktop instantly, after a countdown, or with the IDE hidden so you snap whatever is behind it.
  • Annotate with arrows, rectangles, ellipses, lines, freehand pen, numbered steps, text, highlighter, mosaic/blur redaction, and tiled watermarks.
  • Redact sensitive data with the mosaic tool before sharing.
  • Finish by copying to the clipboard, saving to disk, or pinning the shot as an always-on-top floating window for reference.

Entry points

  • Tools > Take Screenshot — capture now (⌘⇧1 / Ctrl+Shift+1), with a camera button in the status bar.
  • Tools > Capture Desktop (Hide IDE) — hide the IDE, capture the desktop behind it; the IDE stays hidden until you close the overlay (⌘⇧2 / Ctrl+Shift+2), with a monitor button in the status bar.
  • Tools > Take Delayed Screenshot > 3s / 5s / 10s — an on-screen countdown before the grab, so you can switch windows or open a menu first.
  • Every action also appears in Find Action and is rebindable in Settings > Keymap.

Settings (Settings > Tools > GenAI Capture)

  • Watermark — default text plus opacity, size, rotation, spacing, blur and colour, with a live preview; optionally stamp every capture automatically.
  • Toolbar — pick which annotation tools appear on the capture toolbar and drag to reorder them.

Why you'll like it

  • Stays in your flow — no context switch to a separate screenshot app.
  • Runs everywhere — works in every JetBrains IDE (IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, WebStorm, PhpStorm, CLion, Rider, RubyMine, …).
  • Lightweight & private — pure Java/Swing, no external services or telemetry; captures never leave your machine.
  • Multi-monitor and HiDPI aware.

macOS: grant the IDE Screen Recording permission (System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording), or captures come back black — the same one-time grant any screen-capture tool needs.

idea-plugin.name: JSON to Swagger / OpenAPI
idea-plugin.description:
Convert JSON payloads (API requests/responses) into Swagger 2.0 or OpenAPI 3.0 schema definitions in YAML or JSON. Inspired by SwagDefGen, with smart format inference (date, date-time, email, uri, uuid), enum detection, array-element merging, nullable detection, and configurable root schema name.

Open via View → Tool Windows → JSON to Swagger, or select JSON in any editor and choose Convert JSON to Swagger / OpenAPI from the context menu.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Extended format inference: time, ipv6, duration, and hostname (on top of date, date-time, email, uri, uuid, ipv4).
  • Live conversion — output updates as you type (debounced).
  • Open JSON from a file, or drag-and-drop a file onto the input area.
  • Export the generated output to a YAML/JSON file.
  • Toolbar options (spec, format, root name, toggles) now persist across IDE sessions.

Changed

  • Parse errors now report the line and column of the problem.
  • Clearer icons for the Sample / Open / Export toolbar buttons.

Fixed

  • Local Gradle builds no longer fail on newer default JDKs: the daemon JVM is pinned to Java 17 (auto-detected or Foojay-provisioned), so no manual JAVA_HOME is needed.
  • CI build image aligned to JDK 17 so the daemon-JVM pin resolves and release pipelines publish.

idea-plugin.name: Open in Obsidian
idea-plugin.description:
Open the current Obsidian note with one click.

The toolbar button is enabled when the currently open file is a Markdown note inside an Obsidian vault. The plugin finds the nearest parent directory containing .obsidian/, so the vault may be nested anywhere in the IntelliJ project, then opens the current note in Obsidian.

The button is disabled for non-Markdown files and Markdown files outside an Obsidian vault. Also available via Find Action (⌘⇧A / Ctrl+Shift+A).

idea-plugin.name: Sequence Diagram Generator
idea-plugin.description:
Generates a sequence diagram from a Java method directly inside IntelliJ IDEA.

Right-click any method, choose Generate Sequence Diagram, and the plugin

walks the call graph from that entry point and renders the diagram in a

tool window. The diagram is interactive — search methods, click headers to

jump to source, zoom/pan around large diagrams, and export the result as PNG.

Found a bug or have a feature request? Open an issue at

https://github.com/trannghia190/sequence-generator-java-intellij/issues.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
[0.1.0]

Added

  • Initial release.
  • Generate a sequence diagram from any Java method via right-click or the editor gutter action.
  • Self-rendered diagram with zoom, pan, search, and click-to-source navigation.
  • Toolbar with Fit view, 100%, Zoom in, Zoom out, Export (PNG), and Copy.
  • Search with "Find next" and highlighted matches.
  • Configurable options: max depth, project-only filtering, skip simple methods, and skip getters/setters.
  • Polymorphic call resolution.
  • Export to PNG, copy to clipboard.

idea-plugin.name: Editor Sessions
idea-plugin.description:
Named editor sessions ("modes") for switching between working contexts. Runs entirely on the frontend, so it works in local IDEs and over remote development (JetBrains Client).
  • Each session remembers its own open tabs (with caret and scroll positions), the active tab, and the Project view tree state.
  • Leaving a session saves it automatically; switching back restores it in full.
  • A searchable popup filters existing sessions as you type, or creates a new one from an unmatched name.
  • A status bar widget shows the current session and opens the picker on click.
  • Sessions are stored client-side and survive IDE restarts; the last session is reopened on startup.
The plugin contributes actions only — bind keys to Session: Switch and Session: Delete through the Keymap or IdeaVim.
idea-plugin.change-notes: 1.0.0 — Initial release.

idea-plugin.name: Work Box Toolbox
idea-plugin.description:
A lightweight toolbox for IntelliJ IDEA and PhpStorm.
Includes timestamp conversion, timestamp-to-date conversion, Base64 encode/decode, and JSON formatting.
Built to stay small, fast, and easy to extend with more developer utilities later.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 新增 IP 地址查询工具，支持查询当前公网 IP 和指定 IP。
  • 保留时间戳转换、Base64 编解码和 JSON 格式化工具。

idea-plugin.name: MyLog
idea-plugin.description: One-click log statement generation for Java, Kotlin, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Go, and PHP development. Select any variable and generate a log statement with file name, line number, and variable name automatically filled in. Supports customizable log templates through Settings | Tools | MyLog.

idea-plugin.name: CD Open Window
idea-plugin.description:
Open any directory in a new IDE window by typing a cd command.

Instead of navigating the native File | Open dialog, just invoke the action, paste a shell-style path such as cd worktrees/aigc-dag-sync-success-metrics/creation_workspace, and press Enter — the target directory opens in a brand-new project window, exactly as if you had picked it in Open with "open in new window" checked.

Features
  • Relative paths are resolved against the current project's root directory (or your home directory when no project is open).
  • Absolute paths and ~ expansion are supported.
  • The leading cd, surrounding quotes, and ../ segments are all handled.
  • Invalid or non-directory paths are reported instead of opening an empty window.
Trigger it from File | Open Window by cd..., Tools | Open Window by cd..., or the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+Alt+Shift+O.

输入一段 cd 命令，自动以该路径打开一个新的 IDE 窗口，等同于手动 Open 并勾选「在新窗口打开」。 支持相对当前项目根目录的路径、绝对路径与 ~ 展开。

idea-plugin.name: GenAI PHP Portable
idea-plugin.description:
Write & run PHP code in IntelliJ IDEA Community for free. PHP Portable is a lightweight, feature-rich way to add PHP support to the free IDE — no PhpStorm license and no system-wide PHP install required.

Minimal PHP support for IntelliJ IDEA Community (which does not bundle the paid PhpStorm language plugin):

  • Portable PHP SDK — download a portable PHP interpreter from inside the IDE (like the JDK downloader); no system install required.
  • Run PHP script — a run configuration that executes a .php file with the selected PHP SDK or an explicit interpreter path.
  • Syntax highlighting — lightweight, lexer-based highlighting for .php files (tags, keywords, strings, comments, variables, numbers).

This is an MVP; semantic features (completion, go-to-def, inspections) are a later step, best delivered by wrapping a PHP language server via LSP4IJ.

Vendor: https://genai.io.vn
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.2.2
  • Added a plugin icon (shown in the Plugins list and on the Marketplace).
0.2.1
  • Refreshed the file/SDK icon to a cleaner monospace php mark.
0.2.0
  • PHP code intelligence. Completion, go-to-definition, hover documentation and error highlighting — powered by a local PHP language server (Phpactor) that runs on the portable PHP interpreter. Fully offline; no Node.js or system install. Requires the free LSP4IJ plugin. Active on IDEs without built-in PHP (IDEA Community, GoLand, …); on PhpStorm the native PHP support is used instead.
  • One-click setup. A banner on your first .php file offers Enable code intelligence: it downloads Phpactor automatically and takes you straight to the Plugins screen to install LSP4IJ — no hunting for what's needed.
  • Jump into PHP built-ins. Go-to-definition works on standard PHP functions and classes (\DateTime, json_encode, …) via bundled stubs.
  • Run Composer with portable PHP. Right-click ▸ Run Composer (Portable PHP) to run install / update / dump-autoload / require and more in a console — no system PHP or Composer required.
0.1.3
  • Forward compatibility: dropped an internal-only platform API and the platform APIs scheduled for removal in newer IDE builds (verified with the JetBrains Plugin Verifier). No functional changes.
0.1.2
  • Maintenance: replaced an internal-only platform API with its public equivalent and updated deprecated icon-loading calls, for forward compatibility with newer IDE builds. No functional changes.
0.1.1
  • Works alongside PhpStorm & IDEA Ultimate. No longer clashes with the bundled PHP plugin: the editor language support quietly steps aside where PHP is already supported, while the portable interpreter, run action, and setup tools keep working in every IDE.
  • Batteries-included PHP. Downloaded interpreters now bundle ~65 extensions (intl, gd, soap, curl, zip, sodium, mbstring, and more), so composer install and real-world projects run without hitting a missing-extension error.
  • Clearer run action. The run configuration is now named "PHP Script (Portable)" so it's easy to tell apart from PhpStorm's built-in "PHP Script".
  • Clearer settings. The interpreter settings page is now Settings ▸ Languages & Frameworks ▸ Portable PHP, so it no longer looks like a duplicate of PhpStorm's own PHP settings.

idea-plugin.name: GenAI Zendesk Explorer
idea-plugin.description:
Browse and query the Zendesk API from inside your JetBrains IDE.

A Postman-like explorer driven by Zendesk's OpenAPI spec — no more digging through docs for each endpoint's URL, params, and auth:
  • Endpoint tree grouped by resource, straight from the spec.
  • Auto-generated request form: fill path/query params (e.g. ticket_id) and Query.
  • Connection configured once (subdomain + email + API token, token stored in the IDE PasswordSafe).
  • Pretty-printed JSON responses.
Works in all JetBrains IDEs.

idea-plugin.name: Jenkinsfile Support
idea-plugin.description:
GenAI Jenkinsfile brings full editor support for Jenkinsfile (Jenkins declarative & scripted pipelines) to any JetBrains IDE — IntelliJ IDEA, GoLand, PyCharm, WebStorm, and the rest.

Editing

  • Semantic highlighting — directives, steps, annotations (@Library), named arguments, environment variables and types are coloured by meaning, not a word list.
  • Formatting — brace-depth reformat that lays out the declarative skeleton and the Groovy inside script blocks, plus Enter auto-indent.
  • Brace matching and line/block comment toggling.

Code assistance (driven by a data catalog you can extend per project)

  • Context-aware completion — only what's valid inside the current block (e.g. just post-conditions inside post).
  • Quick documentation (F1 / hover) — signature, description, parameters and where each construct is allowed.
  • Parameter info for step calls; named-argument completion.
  • Go to Declaration — in-file defs and environment vars, ${...} string interpolation, and a read-only "Jenkins Pipeline" library under External Libraries. Plus structure view and breadcrumbs.

Inspections

  • Directive placement ("Allowed in …") and cardinality ("only once") checks, with quick-fixes and intentions for common edits.

Embedded languages — Shell highlighting inside sh/bat/pwsh strings and YAML inside a kubernetes agent's yaml (toggleable).

Your Jenkins' own steps — generate a project stub from your instance's pipeline-syntax/gdsl (right-click a .gdsl file, or Tools ▸ Generate Jenkins Pipeline Stub…) and commit <project>/.jenkins/pipeline.jenkinsfile so the whole team gets completion and docs for shared-library and plugin steps.

Recognises Jenkinsfile, Jenkinsfile.* and *.jenkinsfile. Colours are customisable under Settings ▸ Editor ▸ Color Scheme ▸ Jenkinsfile.

Vendor: https://genai.io.vn

idea-plugin.name: Go Portable
idea-plugin.description:
Write & run Go in IntelliJ IDEA Community — for free. Go Portable adds lightweight Go support to the free IDE, with no GoLand license and no system-wide Go install required. IntelliJ IDEA Community doesn't bundle the official Go plugin (that's Ultimate / GoLand only), so this fills the gap.

  • Portable Go toolchain — download a Go toolchain from inside the IDE (like the JDK downloader), straight from go.dev/dl. Stored under ~/.go-portable; switch versions anytime.
  • Run with one click — a green ▶ gutter marker on func main(), plus right-click ▸ Run. Runs the whole package from the module root, so relative paths and .env config resolve just like GoLand — with an Environment variables field (and ENV_FILE auto-filled when a root .env exists).
  • Code intelligence (optional) — completion, go-to-definition, hover docs and error highlighting via gopls, the official Go language server, bridged with the free LSP4IJ plugin. One click installs gopls on your portable toolchain. Fully offline; no Node.js.
  • Syntax highlighting — for .go files (keywords, strings, comments, numbers), even without the language server.
  • Run go tools — go mod / go get / build / test / vet / fmt in a console.

Active on IDEs without built-in Go (IDEA Community, PyCharm, WebStorm, …). On GoLand / IDEA Ultimate the native Go support is used instead — this plugin steps aside.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.1
  • .go files are recognised right away. Syntax highlighting and the ▶ gutter marker now apply the moment a .go file is opened, instead of after the first project startup pass.
  • Cleanly steps aside for official Go support. On GoLand — or IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate with the Go plugin installed — this plugin no longer loads at all, so there is no chance of it competing for .go files. Everywhere else (IDEA Community, and Ultimate without the Go plugin) it works exactly as before.
0.1.0
  • Initial release.
  • Download a portable Go toolchain from inside the IDE (from go.dev/dl).
  • Run a .go file/package: ▶ gutter marker on func main(), runs the package from the module root, Environment variables field with ENV_FILE auto-fill.
  • Optional gopls code intelligence via LSP4IJ (one-click setup), lexer-based syntax highlighting, and a go mod/get/build/test/vet/fmt runner.

idea-plugin.name: Zoo Code
idea-plugin.description:
Zoo Code for JetBrains

Your AI-Powered Dev Team, Right in Your JetBrains IDE

Zoo Code for JetBrains brings the Zoo Code AI coding assistant to IntelliJ-based IDEs. It runs the Zoo Code extension through a bundled extension host and integrates it with JetBrains editors, terminals, menus, and tool windows.

What Can Zoo Code Do For You?

  • Generate code from natural-language descriptions and specifications
  • Adapt through Code, Architect, Ask, Debug, and Custom modes
  • Refactor and debug existing code
  • Write and update documentation
  • Answer questions about your codebase
  • Automate repetitive tasks
  • Use Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers

Modes

Zoo Code adapts to how you work:

  • Code Mode: everyday coding, edits, and file operations
  • Architect Mode: plan systems, specifications, and migrations
  • Ask Mode: get fast answers, explanations, and documentation
  • Debug Mode: trace issues, add logs, and isolate root causes
  • Custom Modes: create specialized modes for your team or workflow

Learn more: Using Modes | Custom Modes

Supported IDEs

Zoo Code supports JetBrains IDEs based on the IntelliJ Platform, including:

  • IntelliJ IDEA (Ultimate and Community)
  • WebStorm
  • PyCharm (Professional and Community)
  • PhpStorm
  • RubyMine
  • CLion
  • GoLand
  • DataGrip
  • Rider
  • Android Studio 2026.1.4 or newer (currently available as a preview)

The plugin targets IntelliJ Platform build 233 (JetBrains 2023.3) or newer. Android Studio requires version 2026.1.4 or newer because that release includes the JCEF support required by Zoo Code. At present, Android Studio 2026.1.4 is available through the preview channel.

Requirements

  • A supported JetBrains IDE based on IntelliJ Platform build 233 or newer
  • Android Studio 2026.1.4 or newer when using Android Studio; install a preview build until this version reaches the stable channel
  • A JCEF-enabled IDE runtime, which Zoo Code requires to render its interface
  • Node.js 20.6.0 or newer available on your PATH
idea-plugin.change-notes:
[3.88.0]

  • ✨ Provider and model support: Use Grok Build and improved custom-model support. This release also fixes Bedrock model limits and sends the Codex verbosity setting.
  • 🧭 Task reliability: This release fixes cancellation handling, tool-turn continuation, and task-message saving.
  • ⚡ Faster editing and chat: File writes no longer use artificial delays by default. Chat messages carry less file data, and code actions reach the last active chat.

Provider and Model Support

  • Add Grok Build model metadata for xAI (#407 by @edelauna, PR #1687 by @myk1yt)
  • Honor custom model IDs for OpenAI-compatible providers (#1845 by @p12tic, PR #1846 by @p12tic)
  • Update OpenAI sane-default parameter values for custom models (#1845 by @p12tic, PR #1847 by @p12tic)
  • Add an openAiStrictToolSchemas setting for OpenAI-compatible gateways (#1827 by @easonLiangWorldedtech, PR #1828 by @easonLiangWorldedtech)
  • Send the Codex verbosity setting in requests (#1958 by @WebMad, PR #1977 by @tosinxt)
  • Expose the Opus 5.5 output token limit on Bedrock (PR #1903 by @PierrunoYT)
  • Resolve custom ARN capabilities from the underlying Bedrock model (#1968 by @kw-bivanov, PR #1970 by @kw-bivanov)

Task Reliability

  • Recover completed tool-turn continuation (#1883 by @jaszhix, PR #1884 by @jaszhix)
  • Make task-message saving stage-independent and finalize open partial tool asks (#1933 by @easonLiangWorldedtech, PR #1927 by @easonLiangWorldedtech)
  • Check abort before an ask row posts (#1803 by @edelauna, PR #1895 by @edelauna)
  • Add shared abort-signal cancellation-scope helpers (PR #1651 by @easonLiangWorldedtech)
  • Forward the task abort signal in OpenAI and LM Studio handlers (#1450 by @allo-, PR #1686 by @myk1yt)
  • Fix permanent DeepSeek and OpenAI request failures from lone UTF-16 surrogates in task history (#461 by @yoloseeyou, PR #1831 by @app/zoomote)
  • Reject unsupported MIME types in image blocks (PR #1961 by @WebMad)

Faster Editing and Chat

  • Remove artificial write delays by default (part of #1375) (PR #1381 by @easonLiangWorldedtech)
  • Omit originalContent from webview messages and fetch it on demand (#1885 by @daewoongoh, PR #1943 by @daewoongoh)
  • Route code actions to the last active chat (#1944 by @WebMad, PR #1946 by @WebMad)
  • Preserve Unicode when clipping file lines (PR #1960 by @WebMad)
  • Keep the streamed read path empty until content is available (PR #1962 by @WebMad)

Safety, Code Index, and Maintenance

  • Add blanket auto-deny for unapproved commands in hands-free mode (#1569 by @DaubnerF, PR #1760 by @DaubnerF)
  • Remove automatic startup embedder validation (PR #1879 by @WebMad)
  • Refresh code-index status routing on workspace-folder changes (#1857 by @WebMad, PR #1957 by @tosinxt)
  • Parse MCP tool names with double underscores in server names (#1731 by @myk1yt, PR #1737 by @myk1yt)
  • Add the pure run-state kernel module (RSK-01) (#1791 by @edelauna, PR #1942 by @edelauna)
  • Remove the dead Task.isPaused field (RSK-12) (#1793 by @edelauna, PR #1894 by @edelauna)
  • Disable extensions when launching the Extension Host for debugging (#1859 by @daewoongoh, PR #1860 by @daewoongoh)
  • Revert the apply_diff line-number prompt guidance (PR #1908 by @app/zoomote)
  • Add packages/types to changed-code mutation testing (#1892 by @edelauna, PR #1893 by @app/zoomote)
  • Wait for the resolved context window in the visual chat scenario (PR #1941 by @p12tic)
  • Remove the stray tab before the Tool Use Guidelines heading (#1415 by @daewoongoh, PR #1440 by @easonLiangWorldedtech)
  • Update posthog-js to v1.435.3 (PR #1586 by @app/renovate)
  • Update posthog-node to v5.55.0 (PR #1587 by @app/renovate)
  • Merge the previous v3.86.0 release preparation after its publication; this is prior-release housekeeping, not a v3.88.0 feature (PR #1897 by @taltas)

idea-plugin.name: Python Portable
idea-plugin.description:
Run Python in IntelliJ IDEA with zero setup — no install required. Python Portable is for the moment you're working in IntelliJ IDEA and just need to run a quick .py script: it downloads a self-contained Python for you and runs the file in one click. No system Python, no separate IDE.

  • Portable Python — download a self-contained CPython from inside the IDE (astral's python-build-standalone, the same builds uv uses). Stored under ~/.python-portable; pick any version.
  • Run with one click — a green ▶ gutter marker and right-click ▸ Run execute your .py file with the portable interpreter. Environment-variables field included for quick scripts.
  • Syntax highlighting — for .py files (keywords, strings incl. f/triple-quoted, comments, numbers), even without a language server.
  • Code intelligence (optional) — completion, go-to-definition, hover docs and error highlighting via pylsp (python-lsp-server), pip-installed onto your portable interpreter and bridged with the free LSP4IJ plugin. Fully offline; no Node.js.
  • Run pip — pip install / list / freeze in a console, no system Python required.
  • Install requirements with venv — one click creates a virtualenv with the portable Python, sets it as the interpreter, and runs pip install -r requirements.txt. The usual project setup, done for you.

Not a replacement for PyCharm or the official Python plugin — it's the lightweight "just run a script" option. Where the official Python support owns .py, this plugin steps aside.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.1
  • .py files are recognised right away. Syntax highlighting and the ▶ gutter marker now apply the moment a .py file is opened, instead of after the first project startup pass.
  • Cleanly steps aside for official Python support. When the Python or Python Community Edition plugin is installed, this plugin no longer loads at all, so there is no chance of it competing for .py files. Everywhere else it works exactly as before.
0.1.0
  • Initial release.
  • Download a self-contained portable Python from inside the IDE (python-build-standalone).
  • Run a .py file with the portable interpreter (gutter ▶ / right-click), with an Environment variables field.
  • Optional pylsp code intelligence via LSP4IJ (one-click setup), lexer-based syntax highlighting, and a pip runner.
  • One-click Install Requirements with venv: create a virtualenv + run pip install -r requirements.txt, and use it as the interpreter.

idea-plugin.name: Chalk
idea-plugin.description:
Chalk provides language intelligence and typechecking for Chalk projects.

  • Python semantic analysis and diagnostics
  • Navigation for Chalk SQL resolvers
  • Validation for chalk.yml and chalk.yaml
  • Managed, checksum-verified installation of chalk-lsp
  • Project-root isolation and suppression of competing built-in Python type inspections

The language server starts only for files beneath a Chalk project root. Server updates are explicit and independent of plugin releases.

Documentation · Source code · Issue tracker
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.2.0

  • Make Python support optional so the plugin can be installed when PythonCore is unavailable.
  • Use the current LSP client API on IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1.4 and newer.

1.1.3

  • Run the native chalk-lsp through JetBrains' LSP API.
  • Install and update the server with checksum verification and safe replacement.
  • Add Chalk settings, status, restart, update, and log actions.
  • Scope server activation and Python inspection suppression to Chalk roots.

idea-plugin.name: Cag (Clean Architecture Generator)
idea-plugin.description:
Gere automaticamente os arquivos de uma nova feature seguindo os princípios de Clean Architecture.

O plugin lê a configuração definida no arquivo .cag/config.json do projeto e cria todos os arquivos necessários — models, repositories, use cases, controllers e demais camadas — nas pastas corretas, com packages e imports já resolvidos.

Como utilizar:
1. Configure a arquitetura no arquivo .cag/config.json na raiz do projeto
2. Pressione Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N ou acesse via menu Tools
3. Digite o nome da feature e confirme os arquivos no preview

Recursos:
• Suporte a projetos multi-módulo
• Preview interativo antes da geração
• Templates customizáveis por projeto
• Resolução automática de packages e imports
• Múltiplos perfis de configuração
• Parse automático de campos para templates
• Compatível com Kotlin 2 (K2)
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Suporte a múltiplos perfis de configuração (arquivos .json em .cag/)
  • Dropdown de seleção de perfil no dialog de geração
  • Gerenciamento de perfis no settings (criar, editar, selecionar)
  • Parse automático de campos de classes existentes para templates
  • Variáveis {fields.<slotId>} e {assigns.<slotId>} para templates
  • Template de exemplo mapper.template com mapeamento automático
  • README de referência de variáveis em .cag/templates/

Changed

  • Otimização do parse JSON em CagConfigService (single parse)
  • Consolidação de loops em PlanBuilder.build()
  • Reutilização de ArchitectureResolver no GenerateFeatureDialog
  • Atualização da descrição do plugin no plugin.xml
  • Adicionado change-notes no plugin.xml para Marketplace

idea-plugin.name: Large File Compare
idea-plugin.description:
Large File Compare

Sort and diff very large text files (200k–2M lines) that your IDE's built-in diff viewer chokes on — SQL exports, CSV dumps, structured logs, and configuration files.

Features

  • Side-by-side diff view with per-row colour coding: added / removed / changed / unchanged
  • Three diff modes: Positional (line order, default), Set (sorted order, no pairing), Key Column (record reconciliation by a unique ID field)
  • Sort before diffing: alphabetical or numeric, ascending or descending
  • Find across both panes with case and regular-expression options and previous / next navigation
  • Export the diff to CSV or plain text, all rows or changed rows only
  • Ignore-whitespace and “show edits as changed” toggles
  • Case-insensitive comparison toggle
  • Patience diff algorithm: stays fast on 200k–1M line files where a naive O(m×n) LCS would collapse
  • Works in every IntelliJ-platform IDE (IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, CLion, …)

Usage

  1. Open Tools → Large File Compare: Compare Two Files
  2. Pick the left file, then the right file
  3. The Large File Compare tool window opens with the side-by-side diff
  4. Adjust mode, sort, and key-column options in the toolbar and click Recompute to re-diff; use the find box and Export button to search and save results

idea-plugin.name: SIE IIDP
idea-plugin.description:
SIE IIDP SDK Code Generator for IntelliJ IDEA

IIDP SDK 代码生成器

面向 IIDP SDK 开发场景，帮助开发者在 IntelliJ IDEA 中快速生成常用代码， 减少重复编写，并提升 Model 字段与访问器的导航效率。

适用场景

  • 基于 IIDP SDK 开发 Def、请求体、返回对象和服务类。
  • 需要统一生成代码结构，并按项目规则管理源路径和目标路径。
  • 需要在 Model 字段及其 Getter / Setter 之间快速定位。

核心功能

  • 代码生成：支持生成 Def、Req、Res、SDK Svc 和 Service 类。
  • 一键生成：使用 IIDP GenAll，一次生成 Def、Req、Res、SDK Svc 和 Service 类。
  • 注解支持：支持 @Getter、@Setter 和 @StaticVar 注解。
  • 导航定位：支持 Model 字段与 Get / Set 访问器之间的导航定位。
  • 路径配置：支持自定义源路径和目标路径，适配不同项目目录结构。
  • 辅助生成：支持为 ManyToOne 字段生成特殊 Setter。

快速开始

支持与反馈

idea-plugin.name: Desktop Capture
idea-plugin.description:
Capture and annotate screenshots without ever leaving your IDE. Grab the whole desktop, mark it up with a full annotation toolkit, then copy, save, or pin the result — in a single keystroke.

What you can do

  • Capture the full (multi-monitor) desktop instantly, after a countdown, or with the IDE hidden so you snap whatever is behind it.
  • Annotate with arrows, rectangles, ellipses, lines, freehand pen, numbered steps, text, highlighter, mosaic/blur redaction, and tiled watermarks.
  • Redact sensitive data with the mosaic tool before sharing.
  • Finish by copying to the clipboard, saving to disk, or pinning the shot as an always-on-top floating window for reference.

AI agents (MCP) — Desktop Capture registers tools with the IDE's built-in MCP server, so AI assistants (Claude, and other MCP clients) can capture your screen and annotate an image (arrows, boxes, text, highlight, blur/redact) on request. Everything runs locally.

Requires IntelliJ IDEA (or any JetBrains IDE) 2025.2 or newer.

Entry points

  • Tools > Take Screenshot — capture now (⌘⇧1 / Ctrl+Shift+1), with a camera button in the status bar.
  • Tools > Capture Desktop (Hide IDE) — hide the IDE, capture the desktop behind it; the IDE stays hidden until you close the overlay (⌘⇧2 / Ctrl+Shift+2), with a monitor button in the status bar.
  • Tools > Take Delayed Screenshot > 3s / 5s / 10s — an on-screen countdown before the grab, so you can switch windows or open a menu first.
  • Every action also appears in Find Action and is rebindable in Settings > Keymap.

Settings (Settings > Tools > Desktop Capture)

  • Watermark — default text plus opacity, size, rotation, spacing, blur and colour, with a live preview; optionally stamp every capture automatically.
  • Toolbar — pick which annotation tools appear on the capture toolbar and drag to reorder them.

Why you'll like it

  • Stays in your flow — no context switch to a separate screenshot app.
  • Runs everywhere — works in every JetBrains IDE (IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, WebStorm, PhpStorm, CLion, Rider, RubyMine, …).
  • Lightweight & private — pure Java/Swing, no external services or telemetry; captures never leave your machine.
  • Multi-monitor and HiDPI aware.

macOS: grant the IDE Screen Recording permission (System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording), or captures come back black — the same one-time grant any screen-capture tool needs.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.2 — first release. Requires a JetBrains IDE 2025.2 or newer.

  • Capture the desktop (instant, delayed, or IDE-hidden) and annotate with arrows, shapes, text, numbered steps, highlighter, blur/redact and watermarks — then copy, save, or pin.
  • AI agent tools (MCP). Registers capture_screen_to_file and annotate_image with the IDE's built-in MCP server, so an AI assistant can capture and mark up your screen on request.

CursorSwitch is a JetBrains IDE plugin that enables seamless switching between IDE and Cursor while maintaining precise cursor position.

Key Features

  • Open files in Cursor with one click

  • Support opening entire projects in Cursor
  • Convenient shortcuts (customizable):
    • Alt+Shift+O - Open current file

    • Tools menu → Open File In Cursor
  • Open project:

    • Tools menu → Open Project In Cursor

Configuration

idea-plugin.name: Camel Case Converter
idea-plugin.description:
Camel Case Converter

Quickly cycle selected text through common naming conventions with a single shortcut. Ideal for renaming variables, constants, CSS classes, database fields, and more.

Supported Formats

Each press of the shortcut cycles to the next format in this fixed order:

  1. kebab-case
  2. SNAKE_CASE (screaming snake)
  3. Camel Case (title space)
  4. CamelCase (PascalCase)
  5. camelCase
  6. snake_case
  7. space case

After the last format it wraps back to kebab-case. Text that does not match any of the seven formats is first normalized to kebab-case, then continues cycling.

Single Words

A single word cycles only by case: area → AREA → area. Mixed case is normalized to lowercase first, so Area becomes area.

Usage

  1. Select text in an editor or an IDEA text input, such as Find in Files, Replace, Search Everywhere, Go to Class, or Go to File.
  2. Press Shift + Alt + U (Windows/Linux) or Shift + Option + U (macOS).
  3. The selection is replaced with the next format and stays selected, so you can keep pressing to cycle.

The action is only enabled when a non-empty selection exists.

Tokenization Rules

Words are split at delimiters (_, -, spaces, dots), camel-case boundaries, and digit boundaries.

Example: XMLHttpRequest2 → xml, http, request, 2

FormatResult
kebab-casexml-http-request-2
SNAKE_CASEXML_HTTP_REQUEST_2
Camel CaseXml Http Request 2
CamelCaseXmlHttpRequest2
camelCasexmlHttpRequest2
snake_casexml_http_request_2
space casexml http request 2

Compatibility

Compatible with IntelliJ IDEA 2021.2 and later (Community and Ultimate).
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.0

  • Added single-word case cycling: area → AREA → area.
  • Added support for selected text in standard IDEA input fields, including Find in Files, Replace, Search Everywhere, Go to Class, and Go to File.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
  • Cycle selected text through 7 naming formats: kebab-case, SNAKE_CASE, Camel Case, CamelCase, camelCase, snake_case, space case.
  • Shortcut: Shift + Alt + U.
  • Smart tokenization supporting abbreviations and digit boundaries (e.g. XMLHttpRequest2).
  • Selection is preserved after conversion for continuous cycling.
  • Compatible with IntelliJ IDEA 2021.2+.

idea-plugin.name: Git Hooks
idea-plugin.description:
Understand and test your git hooks — without making a commit. Git hooks (commit-msg, pre-commit, pre-push…) are just scripts, so no IDE surfaces them. This plugin gives them an icon, basic highlighting, docs, and a test runner — in any JetBrains IDE (GoLand, PhpStorm, IDEA, WebStorm…), no language plugin required.

  • Recognizes the common local hooks — in .git/hooks, a configured core.hooksPath, or conventional folders (.githooks, .husky). The rarer ones (git am, git p4, server-side) are documented too.
  • Test runner — right-click a hook ▸ Test Git Hook…: for commit-msg, type a commit message and see PASS/FAIL against the real hook, before you ever commit.
  • Docs per hook — when it runs, its arguments / stdin, and what a non-zero exit does.
  • Create hooks — New ▸ Git Hook lists every supported hook.

Not affiliated with Git. Server-side hooks (pre-receive, update…) are documented but can't be run on a dev machine.
idea-plugin.change-notes: • Narrowed the declared Git Hook file names to the local hooks the plugin actively supports. The rarer hooks (git am, git p4, server-side and protocol hooks) are still documented in the tool window.

idea-plugin.name: SQL Visualizer
idea-plugin.description:
See the exact SQL your code will run. Renders MyBatis-Plus, JPA and JdbcTemplate queries into executable SQL with real parameter values, before the server starts.

服务未启，SQL 先知——在 IntelliJ IDEA 内把 MyBatis-Plus、JPA、JdbcTemplate 查询还原为可执行 SQL，参数自动回填。

中文文档 · English Docs · 需求池 / Feedback · Screenshots

中文

  • 编码期预览 · SQL 来源全覆盖：Lambda / Query / Update / Delete Wrapper 及服务链、MPJ 联表、mapper XML 动态标签（if / foreach / choose）、@Select 注解 SQL、Spring Data 派生查询、Specification / CriteriaQuery、HQL / @Query、JdbcTemplate / 自研 DAO 字符串 SQL、Querydsl / EasyQuery / Xbatis / MDS，Java 与 Kotlin 通用；mapper XML、注解与 Wrapper 链内补全表名、列名与 #{} 参数
  • 真实参数一键回填：? 替换为实际值（LIKE 自动拼百分号、按字段类型加引号），命名参数 :name 按名回填；OGNL 条件勾选；逻辑删除 / 乐观锁 / 多租户 / 数据权限按 MyBatis-Plus 拦截器语义还原；11 种数据库方言自动格式化
  • 运行期捕获 · 控制台 SQL 日志：MyBatis / Hibernate / JdbcTemplate 三族日志还原为可执行 SQL，按线程分桶、去重过滤、着色标记、精确跳转源码；保活刷屏一键屏蔽，历史 SQL 自动落盘
  • 增强捕获（默认开启，首次使用一次性确认）：向运行中的应用挂载轻量 agent 采集真实执行，不依赖日志格式，附目标库、毫秒级耗时与影响行数
  • 生成与转换 · SQL 反向转 Java：一键生成可直接编译的 QueryWrapper / LambdaQueryWrapper / Wrappers / MPJLambdaWrapper 代码（增删改查与多表 JOIN）
  • CRUD SQL 一步直出：实体类 / 数据库表右键生成 INSERT / UPDATE / SELECT / DELETE
  • 一键回滚 SQL：对预览的 INSERT 推导逆向 DELETE（SQL Server / 达梦自增列自动包装）；UPDATE / DELETE 支持快照回填恢复
  • 执行与分析 · 执行 SQL 与执行计划：内嵌原生 Database 控制台执行，一键 EXPLAIN 按方言提交，JOIN 关系图支持 PNG / SVG 导出；执行前有 ${} 注入确认、无界写清单与超时护栏（需 Ultimate，社区版自动降级）
  • 调用栈悬停与最近执行记录：调用栈悬停弹出调试器风格弹层（帧数可配置、跳转源码）；最近执行记录弹框浏览并跳转源码
  • 面向 AI · MCP 工具：接入平台 MCP Server（近版 IDE 内置），sqlv_* 10 个确定性只读工具覆盖渲染 / 日志还原 / 核查 / 执行计划 / 回滚预案 / CRUD / 反向转换等，设置页逐项门控

触发方式：代码左侧 gutter 图标 / 右键菜单 / Alt+Shift+Q。

要求：IntelliJ IDEA 2024.3 及之后全部版本（基线 2026.x）；执行 SQL、EXPLAIN 与原生 JOIN 图需 Ultimate；MCP 工具需平台 MCP Server。

English

  • Preview · all SQL sources covered: Wrapper chains (Lambda / Query / Update / Delete, service chains, MPJ joins), mapper XML dynamic tags (if / foreach / choose), @Select annotation SQL, Spring Data derived queries, Specification / CriteriaQuery, HQL / @Query, JdbcTemplate / custom-DAO string SQL, Querydsl / EasyQuery / Xbatis / MDS — Java and Kotlin; completion for table / column names and #{} parameters in mapper XML, annotations and Wrapper chains
  • Real parameters: ? replaced with actual values (LIKE auto-wildcard, type-aware quoting), named parameters :name; OGNL condition checkboxes; logic-delete / optimistic-lock / multi-tenant / data-permission replay as MyBatis-Plus interceptors would; formatting for 11 database dialects
  • Runtime capture · live SQL log: MyBatis / Hibernate / JdbcTemplate logs restored to executable SQL, bucketed by thread, de-dup / filtering, color marks per statement, jump-to-source; one-click suppression for keep-alive noise; history archiving
  • Enhanced capture (on by default, one-time confirmation): an agent attached to the running app reports every statement with target database, exact duration and affected rows, no log format required
  • Generate · SQL to Java: convert any SQL back into compilable QueryWrapper / LambdaQueryWrapper / Wrappers / MPJLambdaWrapper code (CRUD and joins)
  • CRUD SQL in one step: right-click an entity class or database table to generate INSERT / UPDATE / SELECT / DELETE
  • Rollback SQL in one click: derive the reverse DELETE for an INSERT preview (identity-column wrapping for SQL Server and DM); snapshot recovery for UPDATE / DELETE
  • Analyze · execution and EXPLAIN: run SQL in the embedded native Database console, one-click EXPLAIN, JOIN diagram with PNG / SVG export; ${} injection confirmation, unbounded-write findings and a timeout guard (Ultimate; Community degrades gracefully)
  • Call stack hover and recent executions: debugger-style stack popup (configurable frame count, jump-to-source) and a recent-executions dialog
  • AI agents · MCP tools: 10 deterministic read-only sqlv_* tools on the platform MCP Server (render, log restore, checks, EXPLAIN, rollback plan, CRUD, reverse SQL), per-tool gating in settings

Trigger: gutter icon / context menu / Alt+Shift+Q (rebindable).

Requirements: IntelliJ IDEA 2024.3+ (baseline 2026.x); Execute SQL, EXPLAIN and the native JOIN diagram need Ultimate; MCP tools need the platform MCP Server.

idea-plugin.name: Class-finder
idea-plugin.description:
Class-finder starts a local HTTP server inside IntelliJ IDEA so external tools (such as Claude Code or scripts) can query the structure of Java classes in your open projects.

What it does
  • Resolve a class by simple name and return its qualified name, file path, superclass, implemented interfaces, generic type parameters, inner classes, fields, methods, and constructors (with signatures and JavaDoc comments).
  • Search both project source code and dependency libraries (Maven / Gradle jars); library JavaDoc is read from the matching -sources.jar when available.
  • Disambiguate same-name classes via package-name fuzzy filtering, with pagination support.
HTTP endpoints
  • GET /health — health check, returns {"status":"ok"}.
  • GET /projects — list the base paths of all projects currently open in the IDE.
  • GET /class?projectPath=&name= — query class details by project path and class simple name; optional package (fuzzy package filter), page, size.
  • GET /batch?projectPath=&names=A,B,C — batch-query multiple classes by comma-separated simple names; returns a map of simple name to matched classes.
  • GET /debug?projectPath= — diagnostic endpoint for troubleshooting class resolution.
Usage
  • curl http://127.0.0.1:6789/health
  • curl http://127.0.0.1:6789/projects
  • curl "http://127.0.0.1:6789/class?projectPath=C:/your/project&name=Order"
  • curl "http://127.0.0.1:6789/batch?projectPath=C:/your/project&names=Order,User"
  • curl "http://127.0.0.1:6789/debug?projectPath=C:/your/project"
Requires IntelliJ IDEA 2024.1 or later.

插件作用
Class-finder 在 IntelliJ IDEA 内部启动一个本地 HTTP 服务（127.0.0.1:6789），供外部工具（如 Claude Code、脚本）按类名查询已打开项目的 Java 类结构，返回全限定名、父类、实现接口、泛型参数、内部类、字段、方法、构造器及 JavaDoc 注释等。检索范围覆盖项目源码与依赖库（Maven / Gradle jar）。 HTTP 接口及作用
  • GET /health — 健康检查，返回 {"status":"ok"}。
  • GET /projects — 列出 IDEA 中所有已打开项目的根路径。
  • GET /class?projectPath=&name= — 按「项目路径 + 类简单名」查询类详情，可选 package（包名模糊过滤）、page、size。
  • GET /batch?projectPath=&names=A,B,C — 批量查询多个类（逗号分隔的简单名），返回「简单名 → 匹配类列表」的映射。
  • GET /debug?projectPath= — 诊断接口，用于排查类检索问题。
使用示例
  • curl http://127.0.0.1:6789/health
  • curl http://127.0.0.1:6789/projects
  • curl "http://127.0.0.1:6789/class?projectPath=C:/你的项目路径&name=Order"
  • curl "http://127.0.0.1:6789/batch?projectPath=C:/你的项目路径&names=Order,User"
  • curl "http://127.0.0.1:6789/debug?projectPath=C:/你的项目路径"
需要 IntelliJ IDEA 2024.1 及以上版本。

idea-plugin.name: SnippetVeil
idea-plugin.description:
Anonymize a Java or Kotlin snippet, a stack trace, or a database execution plan, before you paste it into an AI chat.

Every name your project owns — classes, methods, fields, packages, string literals — is replaced with a placeholder before the snippet leaves the editor. The structure, the control flow, and the libraries you call go as-is.

How it works

  • Select Java or Kotlin code, then right-click → SnippetVeil → Copy Anonymized. The anonymized text is on your clipboard.
  • Commented-out code is kept, with its names replaced. In a .java or .kt file, a comment whose text is code, such as // this.customer.setOrder(order);, comes out as // this.field2.method3(param4);: every name in it takes the placeholder that name gets in the code around it. A comment that is prose, such as a TODO or an explanation, is stripped.
  • Anonymize with Preview… shows the code that will be copied beside its mapping table, with counts: 14 renamed · 3 unknown · 22 preserved · 2 comments stripped. It is the only place you can anonymize less — keep comments for this snippet, or preserve a name and send it exactly as written. Names SnippetVeil could not resolve can be preserved directly; every other name becomes preservable once you unlock the column, which warns you first and is locked again the next time you open the preview.
  • Renaming a placeholder in that same table gives the model the word your question is about: double-click a Placeholder cell and Type1 becomes FilterType1. The stem is yours, the number always stays, and your real name never leaves the machine. Only names this snippet introduced can be renamed — one an earlier snippet already used keeps the name that snippet's replies are written in.
  • De-anonymize Clipboard turns the placeholders in a reply back into your real names.
  • De-anonymize Clipboard and Paste does the same and inserts the result at the caret, replacing the selection. It will not paste a reply it could not restore in full, so placeholders never reach your source; the clipboard keeps the anonymized reply either way.
  • The mapping is per-project and stays on your machine. Placeholders are stable across invocations and IDE restarts, so a second snippet never contradicts the first.
  • SQL in a Java file is read name by name where the IDE recognises it as SQL or JPQL. "SELECT state FROM billing.customers" comes out as "SELECT col1 FROM schema2.table3", and a JPQL query's entity and field names take the placeholders the class and its fields get everywhere else. A query SnippetVeil cannot read in full is replaced whole, as one "str1": SQL holding a parameter, a string or a comment, JPQL with a name that does not resolve, and every query in a Kotlin file. Which queries the IDE recognises depends on the plugins it has.
  • Anonymize Execution Plan… reads an execution plan from the clipboard — PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server or Oracle, in the output forms each engine prints unambiguously — and gives back the same plan with its table, column, index and alias names replaced and the values in its conditions redacted. Every cost, row estimate and timing stays exactly as printed. Copy the plan, then right-click → SnippetVeil → Anonymize Execution Plan…; it always opens the preview first. A plan SnippetVeil cannot read safely is refused, your clipboard is left as it was, and the message names the output option that works where there is one. A plan's names are not added to the project's mapping, so the same plan pasted twice comes back under different numbers.
  • Anonymize Stack Trace… reads a Java or Kotlin exception trace from the clipboard and gives back the same trace with the package, class, method and file names your project owns replaced by the placeholders your snippets already use, so its frames line up with the code you sent beside it. Every line number stays as printed, and JDK and library frames keep their names unless the library is your organization's; the module or classloader prefix on a frame, such as java.base/, is removed. Every exception message and the thread name become str placeholders, and a name the IDE cannot find becomes Unknown. Copy the trace, then right-click → SnippetVeil → Anonymize Stack Trace…; it always opens the preview first. A clipboard holding anything besides the trace is refused, and your clipboard is left as it was.

No network

SnippetVeil makes no network calls. No networking code — enforced on every pull request, scanned in every release build, and public from the first commit.

What SnippetVeil does not hide

  • Your stack. Frameworks, libraries, the identity provider, the persistence layer — preserved by design, because they are what make the snippet answerable.
  • Your structure and your algorithm. Control flow and logic survive intact. If your proprietary value is the algorithm, SnippetVeil does nothing for you.
  • The prompt you type around the snippet. SnippetVeil anonymizes the code, not the sentence above it.

What it does not preserve

  • The text inside your strings — a string literal in your own code becomes "str1" → retype the value that matters into your prompt.
  • Your comment prose, by default.
  • Your exception messages → retype the message that matters into your prompt.

Non-goals

Not a secret scanner. Anonymizing code is unavailable outside supported source files; an execution plan or a stack trace is read from the clipboard, wherever you are. The reversal actions are not gated by language.

Source

Apache-2.0. Source and issue tracker: https://github.com/snippetveil/snippetveil · Threat model, including the limits of the no-network checks: https://github.com/snippetveil/snippetveil/blob/main/THREAT-MODEL.md
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Commented-out Java and Kotlin code is kept, with its names replaced. Copy Anonymized used to strip every comment, so a line such as // this.customer.setOrder(order); was lost on every paste. In a .java or .kt file a comment whose text parses as code of that language where it is written is now kept, and every name in it is replaced with the placeholder that name gets in the code around it: // this.field2.method3(param4);. A string in it becomes "str1", as it does anywhere else. A commented-out field or property, method or function, import or top-level class counts, not only a statement. A comment that does not parse — a TODO, an explanation, a javadoc or KDoc block with @param in it — is still stripped, and so is prose written after the code on a kept line, or inside a kept block comment. A name in the kept line that no longer resolves becomes an Unknown, and the line is kept. Prose that parses is prose in both languages: Kotlin reads // retry on timeout, // TODO or // value in range as code — a call of three names, a name on its own, a containment check — and such a comment is stripped in a .kt file exactly as it is in a .java file. A comment is kept as code only when it holds something prose does not: a bracket, =, ., ;, :: or ->, one of the operators +=, -=, ==, !=, ?., <= or >=, a literal, or a keyword such as val, fun or if. So // retry(onTimeout), // x = 1, // x += y and // foo?.bar are kept, and // it is fine, // done as planned and // return later are stripped. Other operators do not count: // x *= y is stripped. A real commented-out line with none of these, such as // return result, is stripped with the prose; // return result; and // return total(items) are kept. A commented-out Kotlin enum entry or function argument does not parse where it is written and is stripped.
  • Keep comments and javadoc now keeps prose only. Commented-out Java and Kotlin code is kept and anonymized whether the preview's tick is on or off; the tick keeps the comments that are not code, exactly as written, for that snippet.
  • The comment count reads 2 comments stripped, in the preview and in the notification. It used to add , 1 of them commented-out code, to point at the tick as the way to keep that code; in a .java or .kt file the code is kept without it now. The count includes only the comments that were removed.
  • A kept comment is counted: 1 comment anonymized. The preview's counts and the Copy Anonymized notification now say how many commented-out Java or Kotlin lines were kept with their names replaced. It appears only when there is at least one; a snippet with no commented-out code shows no such entry, not a zero. It is a count, beside the others, and not part of 2 comments stripped, which still counts only the comments that were removed. A commented-out line with no name or string in it, such as // return;, has nothing to anonymize and is not counted.
  • The unknown count now says how many came from comments: 3 unknown (1 from comments). Commented-out code is often out of date, so the names in it that no longer resolve used to swell unknown on every paste from a file with commented-out history. The total is unchanged; the bracket says how many of those names appear only in kept comments. A name that is unresolved in live code and in a comment is counted once, as live code. The bracket is absent when none came from comments. Show mapping shows the same numbers as the notification it was opened from. An execution plan's counts are unchanged.
  • A Java stack trace can be anonymized from the clipboard. Anonymize Stack Trace…, the sixth item in the SnippetVeil menu, reads an exception trace off the clipboard and replaces every name in it that belongs to your project with the placeholder your snippets already use, so a frame reads at com.pkg1.pkg2.Type3.method4(Type3.java:42) and lines up with the code you sent alongside it. A name the trace mentions for the first time gets a new placeholder and is remembered, as it would be from a snippet. JDK and library frames are kept as printed. A class or method that no longer resolves becomes a single Unknown, and so does a file name that no public class is named after. An inner class's file is named after its outer class. Line numbers, (Native Method), (Unknown Source), Caused by:, Suppressed: and ... 12 more are kept as printed; the thread name and every exception message, a library exception's included, become str literals. Module and classloader prefixes such as java.base/ and app// are removed, so the output is not the input byte for byte. The item is enabled whatever is on the clipboard and reads the clipboard only when you invoke it. Like Copy Anonymized, it is greyed out while the IDE is indexing. It always opens the preview, whose button reads Copy Anonymized Trace. The clipboard has to hold the trace and nothing else: a line that is not part of a trace, such as a log line above it, refuses the whole paste and leaves the clipboard as it was. Two shapes are not read yet and are refused the same way: a message that runs over more than one line, and a frame of a hidden class such as a lambda (Foo$$Lambda/0x…). A JDK or library frame whose method the IDE cannot find, such as lambda$main$0, has that method replaced with an Unknown.
  • A stack trace frame of a generated class resolves as far as the IDE can take it. A lambda, a coroutine, a proxy or an anonymous class used to turn the whole frame into Unknowns even when its owning class was yours and resolved. Now the longest part of the name the IDE finds is replaced as usual and only the rest becomes one Unknown: com.acme.BillingService$charge$1.invokeSuspend(BillingService.java:42) reads com.pkg1.Type2$Unknown3.invokeSuspend(Type2.java:42), and charge$suspendImpl reads method4$Unknown5. invokeSuspend is kept as printed, like <init>. The part that did not resolve is replaced whole, so no piece of it, such as charge in $charge$1, is ever printed. In the preview its row reads (generated) rather than its text, and it has no Preserve box, because preserving it would print your own method name; an Unknown for a whole frame still has one. De-anonymize Clipboard restores these names exactly, and an exported mapping lists what each one stood for. The unknown count falls for the same trace: the frame above used to count three unknowns, its class, its method and its file name, and now counts one, because more of it resolved.
  • A Kotlin coroutine trace can be anonymized, and a coroutine dump is refused by name. A failing coroutine's trace carries marker lines that kotlinx.coroutines writes into it, and these used to refuse the whole trace as not a stack trace. They are now kept as printed and count as nothing: at _COROUTINE._BOUNDARY._(CoroutineDebugging.kt:42) and at _COROUTINE._CREATION._(…) whatever line number your version of the library puts there, and the older markers from before its 1.7.0 release, (Coroutine boundary) and (Coroutine creation stacktrace), in both the form a terminal shows and the form a copy holds, with its backspace characters. The frames under a creation marker are anonymized like the rest of the trace. kotlinx.* frames are library frames and are kept as printed, so a coroutine trace comes out mostly as it went in. In a Kotlin frame, the file name is replaced with the placeholder of the file's facade class, so Billing.kt reads Type1.kt beside a frame of any class in that file. A .kt file with no top-level function or property has no facade, and its file name becomes a bare Unknown. The output of DebugProbes.dumpCoroutines and a printJob tree are refused with a message that says the clipboard holds a coroutine dump rather than a stack trace; the clipboard is left as it was. A trace containing [CIRCULAR REFERENCE: …] is still refused as not a stack trace.
  • A stack trace's own frames decide which libraries are your organization's. For a snippet, a library class under your file's root package, such as com.acme, is treated as your organization's code and anonymized. A trace has no file, so its library frames used to be kept as printed, and com.acme.platform.HttpClient showed your organization's package names. Now the root packages come from the trace's frames that resolve to your project: com.acme.billing.BillingService in your project makes com.acme a root, and a com.acme.platform.HttpClient frame is anonymized. Frames under a coroutine creation marker count too. Your internal-library prefix list applies as before. A trace from another project comes back mostly Unknown, and that is intended. A trace from a colleague's project or an old build has classes your IDE cannot find. Each one becomes an Unknown, and the preview opens as usual. Nothing in such a trace resolves to your project, so it has no root package, and only your prefix list decides which libraries are anonymized. The same com.acme.platform.HttpClient frame can then be kept as printed in that trace and anonymized in one of your own. A frame whose class resolves gets a placeholder and is remembered, as it would be from a snippet. A frame whose class does not resolve is not remembered. Cancelling the preview leaves your placeholders and their numbering as they were. Confirming a foreign trace advances the placeholder numbers: each Unknown uses up a number that is not remembered, so after a few such traces your next snippet's placeholders can jump, from Type4 to Type340 for example.
  • A stack trace indented with spaces is read. Anonymize Stack Trace… used to read a trace only when its frames were indented with tabs, as the JVM prints them. Traces copied from chat, issue trackers and web pages have usually had their tabs turned into spaces, or into no-break spaces, and were refused with Clipboard is not a stack trace. Now a frame, Suppressed:, ... 12 more or coroutine marker line may be indented with tabs, spaces or no-break spaces, in any mix and any amount, and the output keeps each line's indentation exactly as it was pasted. The first line still has to start at the left edge, and an indented line that is not part of a trace, such as a log line, still refuses the whole paste. A coroutine dump indented with spaces is still refused as a dump.
  • The stack trace preview says when Kotlin support is unavailable. Anonymize Stack Trace… reads the clipboard rather than a file, so it never showed the Kotlin support is not available message, and on an IDE where SnippetVeil's Kotlin support was missing a Kotlin frame simply came back Unknown. Now, when Kotlin support is unavailable and the trace has at least one Unknown, the preview adds a line under the counts naming the cause, with the same link the message offers: Open Plugins when the Kotlin plugin is not running, and Open Kotlin settings when it is running in K1 mode. The line says this is one possible reason a name is unknown, not that it is the reason: it appears on a Java-only trace too, because SnippetVeil does not guess a trace's language from its text. The trace is anonymized and copied as before.
  • The listing, the README and the threat model stop saying a stack trace is not anonymized. What SnippetVeil does not hide no longer lists your stack trace, and nothing takes its place. What it does not preserve gains your exception messages, which Anonymize Stack Trace… always replaces: retype the message that matters into your prompt. The strings line above it gains the same kind of recourse: retype the value that matters into your prompt. How it works describes the action, and the first-run notice gives its path beside the execution plan's: copy the trace, then right-click → SnippetVeil → Anonymize Stack Trace…. The threat model's section on the stack trace now says what is true: the action is opt-in and reads the clipboard only when you invoke it, so a trace pasted straight from the run console is as exposed as before; the module and classloader prefix it drops makes a module-layer bug undiagnosable from the anonymized copy; the line numbers it keeps, with the shape of the trace, can identify a public codebase; and once you confirm the preview, every name in the trace that resolves to your project is added to the mapping, including classes you never selected.

idea-plugin.name: Ticket Repo Analyzer
idea-plugin.description: Analyzes a Jira ticket against the repository currently open in IntelliJ IDEA. Paste the ticket text, optionally add screenshots from the clipboard, and get a concise change-impact report with extracted search keywords, likely affected files, implementation guidance, test suggestions, and risks/questions. Repository scanning is performed locally. Analysis continues to work locally without an API key.

idea-plugin.name: Go Project Starter
idea-plugin.description: Creates Go services from New Project | Generators | Go Boot or incrementally completes an existing project from the Tools menu. Choose the module path, Go version, project type, Web framework, runnable infrastructure clients, license, Docker, dependency preview, go mod tidy, and Git initialization.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Add Cobra-based command lifecycle with config, debug, and version flags to every runnable starter.
  • Add optional embedded Swagger UI and OpenAPI starter files for REST API projects.
  • Make the Go plugin dependency optional so verification in IntelliJ IDEA does not fail when the Go plugin is unavailable.
  • Improve generated service startup, shutdown, error propagation, Makefile, and project documentation.
  • Replace expanded dependency checkboxes with compact multi-select dialogs for Database, Cache, and Middleware & Tools.
  • Add runnable Prometheus metrics and Zap structured logging starters.
  • Document the generated architecture and directory layout for every project type.
  • Create only the command, API, transport, cache, and messaging directories required by the selected project type and components.
  • Add REST API, gRPC Service, CLI Application, and Background Worker project types.
  • Generate runnable PostgreSQL, MySQL, GORM, Redis, Kafka, and gRPC initialization code.
  • Add .env.example and dependency-free environment configuration loading.
  • Add a pre-generation file, conflict, dependency, and command preview.
  • Run go mod tidy in the background with success/error notifications and a persistent log.
  • Add MySQL support and expand generated Docker and README instructions by project type.
  • Add compile smoke tests for generated project types, Web frameworks, and infrastructure combinations.
  • Add BSD-3-Clause, GPL-3.0-only, LGPL-3.0-only, AGPL-3.0-only, and proprietary license options.
  • Detect Go SDK versions from GoLand, GOROOT, and PATH in an editable dropdown.
  • Add dedicated 16x16 generator and 40x40 plugin icons.
  • Fix the blank Go Boot settings panel in GoLand's compatibility New Project dialog.
  • Match the Go Boot generator icon to the standard 16x16 sidebar icon size.
  • Fix Go Boot visibility in the GoLand 2025.2 New Project dialog.
  • Register both modern and legacy-compatible project generator entry points.
  • Add Go Boot under New Project | Generators.
  • Configure module path, Go version, HTTP port, Web example, Dockerfile, license, and Git.
  • Choose Standard Library, Gin, Echo, or Fiber.
  • Add optional GORM, pgx, Redis, gRPC, and Kafka module dependencies.
  • Keep the existing Tools initializer as a second entry point.
  • Initialize empty or partially populated projects incrementally.
  • Preserve every existing file and directory.
  • Avoid creating a second entry point when a main.go already exists.
  • Report path conflicts while continuing with independent items.
  • Offer optional Git repository initialization when Git is available.

idea-plugin.name: Selection Annotation
idea-plugin.description:
Copy a selected code or text fragment as a source-aware Markdown annotation.
  • Open the annotation input from the floating code toolbar or editor context menu.
  • Include the absolute source path and selected line range automatically.
  • Add an optional multiline comment and copy the result to the clipboard.
idea-plugin.change-notes: • Removed leading whitespace from single-line selection fragments instead of padding them to their original source column. Multiline selections retain their relative indentation.

idea-plugin.name: CodeBind Docs
idea-plugin.description:
CodeBind Docs binds design documents to source files in JetBrains IDEs without modifying the code. Docs live as local Git-friendly Markdown. When the doc pane is already open, it follows the file you switch to; it does not pop open by itself.

Works in IntelliJ IDEA, Android Studio, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, CLion, PhpStorm, Rider, DataGrip, and other IntelliJ-based IDEs. Supports file / range / directory bindings, drift detection, Vditor live preview, and AGENTS.md scaffolding. The YAML header is compatible with the VS Code / Cursor extension.

中文说明

CodeBind Docs 把设计文档绑定到源文件，不修改源码。文档是本地、可 Git 的 Markdown。文档面板已打开时随源文件切换；面板隐藏时打开代码不会自动弹出。

适用于 IntelliJ IDEA、Android Studio、PyCharm、WebStorm、GoLand、CLion、PhpStorm、Rider、DataGrip 等基于 IntelliJ 平台的 IDE。支持整文件 / 代码块 / 目录绑定、漂移检测、Vditor 即时预览，以及 AGENTS.md 脚手架。YAML 文件头与 VS Code / Cursor 扩展兼容。

idea-plugin.name: YiluPush
idea-plugin.description:
YiluPush is a Git multi-level branch merge and push toolkit for IntelliJ IDEA. It solves the repetitive manual work of merging across multiple cascading branches.

Core Features
• Multi-level forward merge: merge along the pipeline A → B → C step by step, automatically pulling and pushing each involved branch; pauses on conflict for manual resolution, avoiding force-push overwrites.
• Multi-level reverse merge: merge backward from the pipeline end, e.g. C → B → A, to flow downstream changes back upstream.
• Configurable branch protection: mark any branch as "do not merge into other branches". Protected branches are highlighted in red with a hint in the pipeline; they cannot be forward-merged downstream nor used as a source in reverse merge (e.g. protect the public test branch to prevent its code leaking into business branches).
• Integrated commit: commit in one place with three actions — commit only / commit and push to current branch / commit and run multi-level merge — each with a confirmation dialog listing the exact steps.
• Visual pipeline builder: add branches one by one via dropdowns to build the A → B → C chain, with move-up, move-down, remove, clear and live preview.
• Live status: the tool window shows current branch and pending change count in real time, with step-by-step logs during merge.

Use cases
Teams and individuals who need to cascade a feature branch through multiple environment branches (dev → test → pre → prod) or sync code back and forth across branches.

idea-plugin.name: Cron Expression Explainer
idea-plugin.description:
Explains cron expressions where you actually write them, so you never have to copy one into a website to find out what it does.

Hover a schedule to see what it means in plain English and the next five times it runs:
  • GitHub Actions workflows and Kubernetes CronJobs (YAML)
  • Spring @Scheduled, in Java and in Kotlin
  • Terraform schedule_expression and recurrence, including AWS's cron(...) wrapper
Each of those reads cron slightly differently, and the plugin reads each one in its own dialect — five-field Unix, six-field seconds-first for Spring, and AWS EventBridge, which adds a year and numbers Sunday as 1. The same six characters can mean two different days in two files in the same repository.

It also warns about expressions that are perfectly legal and probably not what you meant: a step that leaves a gap at the end of each hour, a day-of-month and day-of-week pair that cron treats as OR rather than AND, a day several months do not have, or yet another job landing on the busiest minute on the machine.

The same explainer runs in the browser, alongside our other developer tools, at devxhub.com/tools.

Donate | GitHub | Issues
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changed

  • The plugin description now ends with Donate, GitHub and Issues links. The IDE's plugin panel does not render the Marketplace's own donation field, so the description is the only place a link reaches someone browsing from inside the IDE.

Added

  • Completion inside a string that is going to hold a schedule: the expressions people actually write, each with what it means shown beside it. Offered per dialect, so a workflow file gets five-field expressions, Spring gets seconds-first ones, and Terraform gets them wrapped in cron(...) where AWS requires it.

idea-plugin.name: Pi GUI
idea-plugin.description:
A JetBrains UI for the pi AI coding agent. Not affiliated with JetBrains or with the authors of pi.

Chat with pi inside the IDE. Conversation and settings surfaces use the IDE's bundled JCEF runtime, with no local web server or remote UI origin. Native IDE APIs still provide file pickers, diffs, confirmations and project integration.

What it does

  • Sessions — every pi session recorded for the current project, read straight from disk, so history opens without starting an agent.
  • Streaming chat — assistant text, thinking blocks and tool calls arrive live, each collapsible so the conversation stays readable.
  • Slash commands — type / to complete pi's built-ins plus your own extension commands, prompt templates and skills.
  • Edits — the files a conversation actually changed, with per-file line counts; click one to open the IDE's own diff viewer.
  • Attachments — drag, paste or pick files; images go to the model inline, anything else is referenced by path so it stays out of the context window.
  • Context meter — how much of the context window the session occupies, with one-click compaction.
  • Providers, models and thinking level — switched from the composer.
  • Send file path — right-click any file, folder or selection to drop it into the composer as an @mention.
  • Console selection — right-click selected console output to insert it at the current composer caret.

Available in English, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese.

AI credential access and privacy

Pi GUI does not read cc-switch or imported AI credentials until you explicitly allow it in a permission dialog. The dialog appears before the first credential import and identifies the files, credential names and purpose of the access.

  • Sources: ~/.cc-switch/cc-switch.db, ~/.cc-switch/config.json, a cc-switch.db file you select, and the specifically named AI environment variables below.
  • Values: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, provider base URLs and model names. Pi GUI never reads the complete environment.
  • Purpose: copy the selected provider configuration to local Pi files (~/.pi/agent/providers.import.json and managed entries in ~/.pi/agent/models.json) so the locally installed pi CLI can authenticate with the selected AI provider.
  • Handling: credentials remain on your computer. Pi GUI does not send them to the plugin developer and does not collect telemetry. When used, the local pi CLI sends a credential only to the AI provider you selected.

If permission is denied, Pi GUI does not read these credential files or AI environment variables, and provider import remains disabled.

Requirements

The pi CLI must be installed and authenticated on your machine; this plugin drives it, it does not bundle or replace it. The pi CLI settings page detects an existing installation and, with explicit confirmation, can run the installer published by pi.dev:

macOS/Linux: curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh
Windows: powershell -c "irm https://pi.dev/install.ps1 | iex"

  • Keep stored API keys out of the JCEF page and preserve them on blank edits.

idea-plugin.name: Lark Env
idea-plugin.description:
Load environment variables from a Feishu/Lark cloud document before local Java Run or Debug.

Lark Env is an independent third-party plugin by wufly, not affiliated with or endorsed by Feishu/Lark or JetBrains.

  • Select a document URL and a unique heading containing one KEY=value code block.
  • Fetch the latest configuration on every launch; no environment-value disk cache.
  • Leave run configuration names empty to apply to all supported configurations in the current project, or restrict by exact names.
  • Existing IDEA launch variables take precedence over document variables.
  • Abort launch on retrieval errors, invalid configuration, timeout or cancellation.

Requirements: IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2.x, Java plugin, and a separately installed lark-cli authenticated as a user with access to the document. Windows requires the native lark-cli.exe, not a .cmd or .ps1 shim.

Setup: Settings > Tools > Lark Env. Enable for the project, enter the document URL and heading, then use Test Read before launching.

Scope: Local Application and Spring Boot Run/Debug. Maven/Gradle delegated execution, JUnit, remote targets and offline mode are not supported.

Privacy: The plugin calls the local CLI to retrieve the document into memory, then selects the configured section. It does not send document contents to the publisher or intentionally persist environment values. CLI authentication, logging and network behavior are managed separately by lark-cli. Document metadata is saved in project-local IDEA settings.

Restrict access to configuration documents. Do not use ordinary cloud documents to store production secrets.

Support and feedback | Privacy notice | End user license agreement

idea-plugin.name: Pettering Around
idea-plugin.description:
A tiny pixel-art cat that lives in your editor.

It walks along the lines of your code, springs up to the first line of a block, curls up in a deeply nested one, and naps on the left margin. When you scroll away it follows you. When you leave it alone it grooms, stretches, and eventually falls asleep.

It stays out of your way. The cat never scrolls your editor, never moves the caret, never opens a tool window, and never takes focus. While you are reading and still, it holds still too — motion in the corner of your eye is an interruption, and how much it is allowed to do is yours to set.

Four coats: Ginger, Tuxedo, Calico and Midnight.

No network requests, ever. No accounts, no analytics, no telemetry. Nothing about your code, your project or you leaves your machine — there is no code in the plugin that could send it.

Light. The simulation runs at a fixed 50Hz but the plugin only wakes as often as the cat is worth looking at: thirty times a second while it is walking, four while it is sitting, under once a second while it sleeps — and not at all once every cat has settled and the IDE is not focused.

Works in every JetBrains IDE: IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, Rider, CLion, PhpStorm, RubyMine, DataGrip and Android Studio.

Settings live in Settings → Tools → Pettering Around. Show or hide the cat from View → Show or hide your pet.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.0 — first release

  • A cat that walks on your code: it reads the visible lines of the editor, treats each one as a surface, and walks, jumps and climbs between them.
  • Four coats, chosen in Settings → Tools → Pettering Around.
  • A liveliness slider, from an ornament that never roams to a cat that is always up to something.
  • Show or hide from the View menu, with no default shortcut — deliberately, so it cannot collide with a binding your hands already know.
  • English and Turkish.
