idea-plugin.name: Refalcon
idea-plugin.description:
Refalcon brings fast, sharp-eyed Refal-5λ language support to IntelliJ IDEA. It swoops in on your .ref and .refi files with lexer-based syntax highlighting (including string escapes and distinctly colored activation brackets) and a configurable color settings page, brace matching for { } ( ) < > [ ], line and block comments, code folding, a structure view of a file's functions, code completion (directives, built-ins, in-file functions, and in-scope variables), navigation that scales — Go to Declaration, Go to Symbol, Find Usages and Rename, including across files via $EXTERN, backed by a cached project-wide symbol index — quick documentation, an Unused function inspection, instant compiler-free error highlighting with quick-fixes (create function / add $EXTERN), a code formatter in the canonical 2-space Refal style (column-0 * comments stay pinned), fast background syntax checks via rlc --grammar-check shown inline, and a run configuration that compiles and runs programs with the rlc toolchain — or rlmake for multi-file programs (follows *$FROM) — auto-detected on the PATH and in standard install locations (on Windows, rlc.bat under %APPDATA%\Refal-5-lambda is found even when the IDE's PATH is stale). Dialect-aware: classic Refal-5 sources work as-is, and Refal-2 files are detected by content (name start headers, bare entry/extrn, k/name/ calls) and get their own lexer with highlighting, structure view, brace matching and case-insensitive go-to-definition.
Token rules were informed by the community VS Code extension (GDVFox/vscode-refal-5-lambda); the instant error highlighting is inspired by the Grammar-Kit coursework plugin bmstu-iu9/RefalFiveLambdaPlugin.
idea-plugin.change-notes: 0.0.1 — initial release. Syntax highlighting (string escapes, distinct activation brackets) and a color settings page; brace matching; line/block comments; code folding; a structure view of functions; a sentence/pattern parser; code completion for directives, built-ins, in-file functions and in-scope variables; navigation backed by a cached project-wide symbol index — Go to Declaration, Go to Symbol, Find Usages, Rename, including across files via $EXTERN; quick documentation; instant compiler-free error highlighting (Unresolved function/Unresolved variable) with quick-fixes (create function / add $EXTERN); a code formatter (canonical 2-space style, column-0 * comments stay pinned); an Unused function inspection; fast inline compiler diagnostics via rlc --grammar-check; a run configuration that compiles and runs with rlc or rlmake (multi-file via *$FROM; auto-detected, incl. rlc.bat in %APPDATA%\Refal-5-lambda on Windows), a run arrow at Go/GO, clickable diagnostics (absolute Windows paths included), helpful guidance when the compiler is missing; a New → Refal File template and live templates; Refal-2 dialect support (content-detected on .ref: dedicated lexer/parser, highlighting incl. /123/ macrodigits and k/name/ … . calls, structure view, brace matching, find usages, case-insensitive navigation) and an Indented asterisk inspection with a move-to-column-0 quick-fix (all dialects); an Unreachable sentences after a catch-all pattern inspection; Refal-2 functions in Navigate → Symbol; a Duplicate function definition inspection; TODO/FIXME markers and breadcrumbs in both dialects; and more live templates (call, extern, proutq); content-aware dialect detection (ignores Refal-2-looking tokens inside strings/comments; a brace block or $-directive marks Refal-5/5λ) with an explicit * refal-2 / * refal-5 override comment; and a distinct Refal-2 file icon.

idea-plugin.name: Subway Coders
idea-plugin.description:
Subway Coders plays looping gameplay clips — Subway Surfers, Temple Run, Minecraft parkour/story and other "brain-rot" loops — in tool windows right inside your IDE. Keep your subconscious maximally engaged while the rest of you reads code.
  • Four independent players, one per screen edge (left / right / top / bottom)
  • Clips render with JCEF — a YouTube link plays as an embed, any other URL as a looping video
  • Config-driven categories (Subway Surfers, Temple Run, Minecraft Parkour/Story, and more); each holds several clips and "Shuffle" picks another
  • Paste any YouTube or direct video URL to play your own clip
  • Doomscroll mode — scroll the endless YouTube Shorts feed instead of a looping clip
  • Playback pauses when a player is hidden and resumes when it's shown again
  • Focus terminal on Claude Code events — when Claude Code asks a question or finishes, the players hide and the built-in Terminal takes focus so you snap back from the feed (on by default, toggle in the options menu)
  • Per-window category, plus "open in browser" and a config editor in the options menu
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Doomscroll mode — a Doomscroll (YouTube Shorts) entry in the category selector that scrolls the endless YouTube Shorts feed instead of a looping clip. Loads the real feed in the embedded browser; no API keys or curated lists. The mode persists per window, and the feed follows the IDE's light/dark theme (and live theme switches).
  • Pause when hidden — playback now pauses when a player's tool window is collapsed or another tab takes over its anchor, and resumes in place when it's shown again.
  • Focus terminal on Claude Code events — when Claude Code asks a question or finishes, the four players are hidden and the built-in Terminal is focused so you snap back from the feed. Detection uses Claude Code hooks that the plugin auto-installs into ~/.claude/settings.json (removed again when you turn the feature off). On by default; toggle it via the tool window's options (gear) menu.

idea-plugin.name: Rubber Duck Buddy
idea-plugin.description:
A rubber duck floats in the corner of your editor and reacts with its "face" to the state of your project — it breathes while you work, panics on a failed build, cheers up on a clean one, and quietly nods when you tell it what's wrong.

This is rubber-duck debugging, made literal: explaining the problem out loud is what helps. The duck never reads, analyses, or answers what you type — that's the whole point. Zero usefulness, maximum delight.

How to use
  • Open a file — the duck appears in the editor corner and breathes.
  • Build with errors → it panics; a clean build → it's happy.
  • Press Ctrl+Alt+D (or click the duck) → tell it what's wrong; it nods.
It never sends anything anywhere, and it has no settings to fiddle with.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.0.1
  • First release: editor-corner duck that reacts to build status and live problems.
  • "Tell the Duck" ritual popup (Ctrl+Alt+D) — the duck nods, then quacks.

idea-plugin.name: Pokemon
idea-plugin.description:
Adorable walking pixel art Pokemon pets that live in a tool window while you code. This is a JetBrains port of the popular vscode-pokemon extension by Jakob Hoeg Mørk, and it reuses the original animation engine and sprites, so the Pokémon behave exactly like they do in VS Code.

Features

  • Spawn any of 565 Pokémon from generations 1–4, searchable by name.
  • Random spawn with authentic 1-in-8192 shiny odds — shiny variants included ✨
  • Pokémon walk around, take naps, and befriend each other ❤️
  • Four sprite sizes: nano, small, medium, large.
  • Themed backgrounds: forest, castle, beach (light & dark variants follow your IDE theme).
  • Your Pokémon roster is remembered across IDE restarts.

Usage

Open the Pokemon tool window (right sidebar). Use the title-bar buttons to spawn a chosen Pokémon (+), spawn a random one (⚡), or remove one (−). The gear menu (⚙) has Pokémon size, background theme, roll call, and remove-all.

Works in PyCharm, DataSpell, IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, and every other IntelliJ-Platform IDE (2024.2+).

Credits: all Pokémon logic, sprites and assets come from the MIT-licensed jakobhoeg/vscode-pokemon project (also on the VS Code Marketplace). Pokémon sprites are property of Nintendo/Game Freak; this is a non-commercial fan project.

idea-plugin.name: SCM Jump to Source
idea-plugin.description: Adds an inline "Jump to Source" button to file rows in the Commit / Local Changes tree. Hover a changed file and click the pencil icon at the end of the row to open the file in the editor — no right-click context menu needed.

idea-plugin.name: GHC GitHub Auth
idea-plugin.description:
Companion login methods for the bundled GitHub plugin, for organizations that block the "JetBrains IDE Integration" OAuth app via OAuth App access restrictions.
  • Log in with GitHub CLI — reuses the token of your locally authenticated gh CLI (the GitHub CLI OAuth app is commonly allow-listed).
  • Log in with Device Flow — runs the GitHub Device Flow against an OAuth app client id you provide (e.g. one your organization has approved).
Acquired tokens are stored into the bundled GitHub plugin's normal account store, so Pull Requests, Gists and clone integration work as usual.

idea-plugin.name: IDE Book Shelf
idea-plugin.description:
IDE Book Shelf is a compact local TXT and EPUB reader for IntelliJ IDEA.

在 IDEA 底部提供紧凑的本地 TXT / EPUB 阅读器。

快捷按钮：上一页、下一页、章节选择，以及一个设置菜单，统一管理打开书籍、书架、字体、字号和行距。

一行缩小模式：隐藏工具栏，只保留一行阅读内容；可用左右方向键翻页，不离开编码界面。

每本书的阅读进度仅保存在本地。

English: A compact local TXT and EPUB reader with chapter navigation, bookshelf management, local progress, and a one-line mode for unobtrusive reading while coding.

idea-plugin.name: Finance 7x24 News
idea-plugin.description:
Finance 7x24 News shows public financial news, watchlist quotes and AI-powered analysis in IntelliJ IDEA. It supports 7x24 news updates, stock/ETF/index watchlists for A-share, HK, US and international gold markets, automatic refresh per market hours, multi-source fallback quote data, one-click AI news interpretation, and AI portfolio analysis with multi-turn chat.

在 IDEA 中查看公开财经快讯、自选行情并进行 AI 分析。支持 A股、港股、美股、国际金价自选行情，多数据源兜底，各市场按开市时段自动刷新；AI 支持快讯解读与自选股分析、多轮追问，模型可选商汤 SenseNova、智谱 GLM，也支持自定义任意 OpenAI 兼容接口。

本插件为非官方插件，与相关数据服务商及其关联公司无隶属、授权、认可或赞助关系。 插件仅用于便捷查看公开财经资讯，不提供投资建议，行情数据可能存在延迟、遗漏或错误。

idea-plugin.name: PowerShell Novel Reader
idea-plugin.description: A novel reader disguised as a Windows PowerShell terminal inside your JetBrains IDE. 伪装成 PowerShell 小说阅读器 It looks exactly like a real terminal with dark theme, blue title bar, PS prompt and Consolas font, so nobody can tell you are reading novels. 一款伪装成 PowerShell 终端的小说阅读器，支持六种伪装模式（日志/Diff/进度条/tail -f 等），阅读进度自动保存，可自定义翻页快捷键和每页行数。打开 Settings - Tools - PowerShell Novel Reader 选择 txt 文件后，在底部 PowerShell 窗口输入 cat book 即可阅读。

idea-plugin.name: BrawlCode
idea-plugin.description:
Your Claude Code sessions power an RPG hero. This plugin is the Stormcasters side of the game.

The plugin captures nothing. It connects your account, drops the public filter script into ~/.claude/brawlcode/, registers it as a Claude Code hook, and shows your hero. Every event that reaches the server is sent by that script — a few hundred lines of dependency-free Node you can read.

Your code, prompts and file paths never leave your machine.

Independent project. Not affiliated with Anthropic, JetBrains, or Microsoft.
idea-plugin.change-notes: • 0.1.0 — First release. Connect your account, drop the public, auditable filter script, register the Claude Code hooks, and watch your Stormcasters hero level up in a tool-window panel.

idea-plugin.name: PokeCode
idea-plugin.description:
Develop side-by-side with your favorite Pokémon!

Turn your IDE into a real adventure. You can catch Pokémon by throwing Poké Balls, which can be bought using Poké-Dollars earned simply by writing code.

idea-plugin.name: IDE-Radio
idea-plugin.description:
IDE Radio plays YouTube and Bilibili audio directly inside your IDE, featuring a live waveform and spectrum visualizer in a dedicated Tool Window.

Features

  • Audio Playback: Stream audio directly from YouTube and Bilibili URLs without video rendering overhead.
  • Dedicated Settings: Configure independent source slots for YouTube and Bilibili under Settings → Tools → IDE Radio. Preview track titles and duration before saving.
  • Mutually Exclusive Sources: Easily switch between active platforms with atomic source switching and unified session controls.
  • Transport Controls: Play, pause, stop, and loop playback (single-track loop enabled by default) from both the Settings page and the Tool Window.
  • Live Visualizer Tool Window: Real-time audio visualizer tool window at the bottom. Click the canvas to toggle between waveform and spectrum bar displays.
  • Cookie Support & Advanced Settings: Configure browser cookies or cookies.txt under Advanced Settings to mitigate Bilibili 412 rate-limiting.
  • Automatic Retries & Error Handling: Automatic retries (up to 3 times) with exponential backoff on network/412/429/5xx errors, featuring a manual [Retry] button.
  • Privacy Conscious: Stream URLs and authentication tokens are kept strictly in memory and sanitized in UI and logs.

Requirements

IDE Radio relies on local CLI tools to resolve and stream audio:

  • yt-dlp: Extracts audio stream info and metadata.
  • ffmpeg: Decodes remote audio streams to PCM for playback.

Note: yt-dlp and ffmpeg are not bundled with the plugin and must be installed on your system PATH or configured in Settings.

idea-plugin.name: PopType Zoom
idea-plugin.description:
Adds colorful zoom-and-fade animations to characters as you type in JetBrains editors.

Each typed glyph is painted as a temporary enlarged overlay, then smoothly shrinks and fades. Your document contents and normal editor behavior are never modified.

  • Vivid rotating colors or the editor's normal text color

idea-plugin.name: Preflight - Terraform Plan Viewer for AWS
idea-plugin.description:
Review Terraform plans and states of AWS infrastructure without scrolling through terraform plan output.

Preflight opens the JSON output of terraform show -json (plans or states) and terraform.tfstate files in a Preflight tab next to the text editor:

  • plan summary with filters by action (create, update, replace, destroy, read, forget, no-op);
  • attribute-by-attribute diff of each resource, unified or split, with known after apply and sensitive values, and IAM policies expanded and diffed key by key;
  • a graph of who can access what through IAM: execution roles, trust policies, attached, inline and resource policies, permissions boundaries, with the allowed actions and conditions;
  • AWS service icon next to each resource.

Open a plan with View as Terraform Plan (project view, editor tab or Tools menu), a state with View as Terraform State, which can also read the current state of a Terraform folder with terraform show -json (remote backends included).

Preflight is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Amazon Web Services or HashiCorp.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • JetBrains plugin for IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm and the other JetBrains IDEs (2025.1 and later): the same viewer in a Preflight tab next to the text editor of Terraform states and of terraform show -json output, with View as Terraform Plan / View as Terraform State (project view, editor tab, Tools menu), including Read with terraform show -json.

Changed

  • Graph tab: layouts are computed in the background (Web Worker) as soon as a plan is opened, for every layout option, so switching between them is instant and the view never freezes; layout and link routing also take about a third less time, with the same result.
  • Computed layouts are kept between sessions: reopening a plan already seen shows its graph at once.

Development

  • Repository split into core/ (parsers, graph, viewer page), vsc/ (VS Code extension) and jetbrains/ (IntelliJ Platform plugin, Gradle), with a pnpm workspace.
  • make dist builds both packages into build/; make install / make install-jetbrains install them; make version V=x.y.z sets the version of both and releases this changelog section.
  • Test environments: core unit tests (mocha), VS Code integration tests, JetBrains unit and platform tests, sandbox IntelliJ IDEA / PyCharm (make jb-run, make jb-run-pycharm), Plugin Verifier.

idea-plugin.name: HCL AppScan
idea-plugin.description:
HCL AppScan Plugin

The HCL AppScan JetBrains plugin allows developers to build secure applications directly within their JetBrains IDE. It combines the strengths of Static Application Security Testing (SAST) for early code analysis and Interactive Application Security Testing (IAST) for runtime vulnerability detection.

Integrating HCL CodeSweep with the HCL AppScan JetBrains plugin lets you scan source code early in the development lifecycle:
  • Mark CodeSweep scan results as noise or remediate using the quick-fix feature.
  • View all supported rules, and enable or disable rules, in the rules panel.
  • View fix groups and scan data from HCL AppScan on Cloud applications.
  • Import results of executed scans from AppScan Source.
  • Triage fix groups or their underlying issues within the IDE.
  • Add comments during a status change.


The HCL AppScan JetBrains plugin offers seamless integration with IAST, enabling you to leverage its capabilities within your JetBrains IDE. This integration enhances the "shift-left" strategy by allowing swift identification of vulnerabilities early in the development process. Seamlessly analyze new and existing code sections as soon as they are debugged, thereby strengthening the overall security of your applications.

Not yet an HCL AppScan customer? Start a free trial.

idea-plugin.name: Snyk Security
idea-plugin.description:
JetBrains plugin

Scan early, fix as you develop: elevate your security posture

Integrating security checks early in your development lifecycle helps you pass security reviews seamlessly and avoid expensive fixes down the line.

The Snyk JetBrains plugin allows you to analyze your code, open-source dependencies and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) configurations. With actionable insights directly in your IDE, you can address issues as they arise.

Key features:

  • In-line issue highlighting: Security issues are flagged directly within your code, categorized by type and severity for quick identification and resolution.
  • Comprehensive scanning: The extension scans for a wide range of security issues, including:
    • Open Source Security: Detects vulnerabilities and license issues in both direct and transitive open-source dependencies. Automated fix suggestions simplify remediation. Explore more in the Snyk Open Source documentation.
    • Code Security: Identifies security vulnerabilities in your custom code. Explore more in the Snyk Code documentation.
    • IaC Security: Uncovers configuration issues in your Infrastructure as Code templates (Terraform, Kubernetes, CloudFormation, Azure Resource Manager). Explore more in the IaC documentation.
  • Broad language and framework support: Snyk Open Source and Snyk Code cover a wide array of package managers, programming languages, and frameworks, with ongoing updates to support the latest technologies. For the most up-to-date information on supported languages, package managers, and frameworks, see the supported language technologies pages.

How to install and set up the extension

Note: For information about the versions of JetBrains supported by the JetBrains plugin, see Snyk IDE plugins and extensions. Snyk recommends always using the latest version of the JetBrains plugin.

You can use the Snyk JetBrains plugin in the following environments:

  • Linux: 386, AMD64, and ARM64
  • Linux Alpine: 386 and AMD64
  • Windows: 386, AMD64, and ARM64
  • MacOS: AMD64 and ARM64

Install the plugin at any time free of charge from the JetBrains marketplace and use it with any Snyk account, including the Free plan. For more information, see the IDEA plugin installation guide.

When the extension is installed, it automatically downloads the Snyk CLI, which includes the Language Server.

Continue by following the instructions in the other JetBrains plugin docs:

  • Configuration for the Snyk JetBrains plugin and IDE proxy
  • Authentication for the JetBrains plugin
  • JetBrains plugin folder trust
  • Run an analysis with the JetBrains plugin

Support

For troubleshooting and known issues, see Troubleshooting for the JetBrains plugin.

If you need help, submit a request to Snyk Support.

idea-plugin.name: Mend Advise
idea-plugin.description:
Mend Advise (previously WhiteSource Advise)

Get the insights you need, when you need them most. The extension provides full visibility over your open source components, real-time security alerts, and actionable remediation insights. The Mend plugin integrates seamlessly into your coding environment without interrupting or delaying your workflow.

You will need to purchase Mend to activate the plugin. If you do not have a Mend account, you can request a free trial here.

Key Benefits
  • Save time and resources: Detect vulnerabilities early when coding, run security tests before committing your code, and speed-up your development process.
  • Get detailed alerts: Each alert provides you with all of the information you need, within your IDE, like the component name, CVE ID, severity score, and more.
  • Speed-up remediation: Alerts contain proactive remediation guidance to help developers fix the issues.
  • Non-intrusive integration: You control when to scan and receive alerts. The plugin will mark vulnerable packages inside your dependency file, as well as in the Problems or Inspection Results Tool Window.
Getting Started

After installing the extension, please check out our documentation for more details.

Supported Languages

Mend Advise provides support for Java, Kotlin and Scala projects using Maven, and Java projects using Gradle.

Useful Links

IDE integrations
Full list of Mend supported integrations

idea-plugin.name: Yagaan SAST
idea-plugin.description:
Review the security vulnerabilities found by your Yagaan scans directly in your JetBrains IDE. Understand each finding with its diagnostic and data-flow path, apply the suggested remediation, and track the work in action plans — without switching to a browser.

The plugin does not scan your code locally. It links the project open in your IDE to the matching analysis on your Yagaan platform, then keeps the results in sync in the background.

What you can do

  • Triage by risk — The Top Priority view combines a severity gate, contextual CVSS risk estimation and a configurable cap on the number of results, so you get a shortlist sized to your sprint instead of a wall of findings.
  • Browse every finding — Dedicated views for the whole project and for the file currently open in the editor. Select a finding to jump straight to the vulnerable line.
  • Understand before you fix — For each finding: Diagnostic (what the analyzer detected and why), Paths (how untrusted data flows from source to sink, step by step) and Remediation (concrete fix proposals, with examples aligned to your own code).
  • Read the rule documentation — The Yagaan Doc tool window shows the documentation attached to the selected finding or rule.
  • Plan and track remediation — Group findings into named action plans and move each item through to do, in progress, done or ignored. Plans are stored on the platform, so the IDE stays aligned with your team's workflow.

Works in IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PhpStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, Android Studio and other JetBrains IDEs from 2024.3 onwards.

Requirements

  • Access to a Yagaan scan platform, as a service or on-premise, and an account on it. Sign in with your email and password, or with access and secret keys.
  • An existing analysis of your project on that platform.

Yagaan is the static application security testing (SAST) solution from Pradeo. See pradeo.com for product information and support.

idea-plugin.name: Cycode
idea-plugin.description:
The Cycode IntelliJ Platform Plugin is a plugin for JetBrains IDEs (e.g., IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm) that helps users to adopt a shift-left strategy, by enabling code scanning early in the development lifecycle, which could significantly help businesses avoid costly repairs and potential complications down the line.

Features

Cycode IntelliJ Platform Plugin scans your code for exposed secrets, passwords, tokens, keys, and other credentials, as well as open-source package`s vulnerabilities. The extension provides functionalities such as:

  • Scanning your code for exposed secrets, passwords, tokens, keys, and other credentials.
  • Scanning your code for open-source package`s vulnerabilities.
  • Scanning your code for Infrastructure as Code (IaC).
  • Scanning your code for Code Security (SAST).
  • Company’s Custom Remediation Guidelines - If your company has set custom remediation guidelines via the Cycode portal, you'll see a field for "Company Guidelines" that contains those guidelines.
  • Running a new scan from your IDE even before committing the code.
  • Triggering a scan automatically whenever a file is saved.
  • Highlighting vulnerable code in the editor - syntax highlighting for Cycode-specific code and configuration files, making it easy for users to identify and work with these files in their projects.
  • Removing a detected secret or ignoring it by secret value, rule (type) or by path.
  • Upgrading a detected vulnerable package or ignoring it by rule (type) or by path.

Installation

To install the Cycode IntelliJ Platform Plugin, follow these steps:

  1. Open the editor.
  2. Navigate to the Plugins Section:
    1. In the left-hand sidebar of the Settings/Preferences dialog, select "Plugins".
  3. Search for "Cycode" in the search bar:
    1. In the "Plugins" section, you'll see a "Marketplace" tab. Click on this tab, and then use the search bar at the top to search for the plugin you wish to install.
  4. Click on the "Install" button next to the Cycode plugin.
  5. Wait for the installation to complete (plugin downloading, verifying and running core engine).
  6. Restart the JetBrains editor.

Alternatively, you can install the plugin from the plugin page: https://plugins.jetbrains.com/plugin/23079-cycode

Note: If it's your first time using the plugin, it may take a bit longer to download the core.

Authentication

To authenticate the Cycode IntelliJ Platform Plugin, follow these steps:

  1. Open the editor.
  2. Click on the Cycode icon in the sidebar.
  3. Click on the "Authenticate" button.

Configuring the Plugin

To configure the plugin, go to the plugin settings to change the default settings:

  1. In the Additional Parameters field, you can submit additional CLI parameters, such as --verbose mode for debugging purposes.
  2. Use the API URL and APP URL fields to change the base URLs:
    1. On-premises Cycode customers should ask their admin for the relevant base URLs.
    2. For EU tenants, you'll need to adjust the API and APP URLs to include the EU tag:
      1. API URL: https://api.eu.cycode.com
      2. APP URL: https://app.eu.cycode.com
  3. Use CLI PATH to set the path to the Cycode CLI executable. In cases where the CLI can't be downloaded due to your network configuration (for example, due to firewall rules), use this option.
  4. Clear the Scan on Save option to prevent Cycode from scanning your code every time you save your work. Instead, use the Scan on-Demand option.

Note: If the "Scan on Save" option is enabled in the extension settings, Cycode will scan the file in focus (including manifest files, such as package.json and dockerfile) for hardcoded secrets.

Usage

To use the Cycode IntelliJ Platform Plugin, follow these steps:

  1. Open the editor.
  2. Open a project that uses the Cycode platform.
  3. Open a file to scan.
    1. Press Ctrl+S or Cmd+S on Mac to save a file → A scan will automatically be triggered.
    2. If the "Scan on Save File" option is enabled in the plugin settings, Cycode will scan the file in focus (including manifest files, such as package.json and dockerfile) for hardcoded secrets.
  4. Also applies for auto-save.
  5. Wait for the scan to complete and to display a success message.

Viewing Scan Results

Handling Detected Secrets

  1. The scan displays a list of hardcoded secrets found in the application code.
  2. Once the scan completes (either on save or on-demand), you’ll then see the violation(s) highlighted in your main window.
  3. Hover over the violation to see the violation summary.
  4. To view the details of the violation, select it in the list.
  5. Next, choose how to address the detected violation(s) by selecting the Quick Fix button.
  6. If the violation is a secret, you can choose to ignore it — either by secret value, secret rule (i.e., secret type) or the specific file. Note that Ignore occurs locally on the developer’s machine.
  7. Go back to viewing the problem in the main window by clicking View problem.
  8. You can also view a summary of all the problems by selecting the Problems tab.

Support

If you encounter any issues or have any questions about the Cycode IntelliJ Platform Plugin, please reach out to the Cycode support team at support@cycode.com.

License

The Cycode IntelliJ Platform Plugin is released under the MIT license. See the LICENSE file for more details.

idea-plugin.name: Aikido Security
idea-plugin.description:
Aikido Security Extension for Jetbrains IDE

Secure code as it’s written (and generated). Real-time static analysis (SAST), secrets, and open-source dependency (SCA) scanning, plus AI AutoFix for one-click fixes so you can address issues before they reach PRs.

Requirements

  • Free Aikido Account

What it does

  • Real-time scanning on open/save for code security problems, secrets, and open source dependency vulnerabilities. Findings appear inline, in sidebar and with hover details for fast triage.
  • AI AutoTriage noise reduction: Aikido prioritizes and de-emphasizes issues based on reachability/ and impact.
  • AI AutoFix in the IDE: When a fix is available, preview and apply a safe change for supported SAST and SCA findings, without leaving VS Code.
  • Policy-aware and custom SAST results in the IDE ensure workspace severities, ignores, and Aikido-defined custom SAST rules are applied so developers see the most relevant issues first.

Usage

Install & authenticate

  1. Install the Aikido extension.
  2. Connect to Aikido by entering your PAT
    • Create a token in Aikido and paste it when prompted.
  3. You’re ready to scan! Issues will be highlighted as you edit.

Scanning

The integration scans your codebase for secrets, API keys, SAST code issues and open-source dependency vulnerabilities. It runs scans whenever you open or save a file.

Every time you make and save changes in a file, a scan runs. If any issues are detected, they are highlighted in the editor and Aikido sidebar. When you hover over a detected SAST issue, additional context about the problem is provided.

Aikido AI AutoFix and AutoTriage

For supported SAST and SCA issues, Aikido will provide the option to assess the issue’s impact with AI AutoTriage, and optionally apply a code fix with AI AutoFix. This fix is applied directly in IDE.

How to test this extension

If this is your first time using this extension and you want to explore its capabilities, we suggest testing it with our example file below.

  • Create a folder on your local machine.
  • Open this folder in your IDE.
  • Within this workspace, create a file containing the code you want to scan.
  • Save the file.
  • Any identified issues will appear as highlights in the editor and in the Problems panel below.

Below you can find an example index.js file that can be used to verify if the extension is working correctly, it should detect one SAST issue (SQL injection) and one exposed secret (Stripe Access Token).

const app = {}

app.get("/payments", (req, res) => {
    const PW = "sk_live_fakestripeapikeyleaked12"
    res.status(200).send(STRIPE_API_KEY)
})

app.get("/user", (req, res) => {
    const username = req.query.username
    const unsafeQuery = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = '${username}'`
    db.query(unsafeQuery, (err, result) => {
        res.status(200).send(result)
    })
})

Commands

Execute Aikido Plugin Actions by clicking on the Aikido icon in the lower left.

  • Connect to Aikido: Enter an access token to connect with the Aikido Platform.
  • Disconnect from Aikido: Clears your access token.
  • Reload rules: Fetches all SAST rules from the Aikido Platform. Useful when you add new custom rules.

How does the extension perform scans on a repository

The integration does three types of scanning: secret, SAST and open-source dependency scanning. It uses Aikido-defined rules, supplemented by any custom rules you add to Aikido. The integration then processes any results to check for false positives or ignored issues.

How does the extension connect to Aikido

Using the access token that you provided, the extensions will connect and detect the matching repository in Aikido using the Git remote URL or the name of the project folder.

idea-plugin.name: NPM Safety Guard
idea-plugin.description:
NPM Safety Guard

Catches malicious npm packages, CVEs, and supply-chain threats directly in your package.json and package-lock.json — no command-line setup required.

Detection layers (10 total)

  • Malicious package database — bundled, offline-first list of known-malicious packages (event-stream, node-ipc, Axios DPRK RAT, and more). Flagged with red error squiggles.
  • CVE lookup via OSV.dev — queries the Open Source Vulnerabilities database for known CVEs. Results are cached to disk (24 h). No API key required.
  • Maintainer-change alerts — detects when the npm maintainer set changed in the last 30 days (account takeover signal).
  • Maintainer email domain change (NSG-014) — flags packages where a maintainer's email domain changed between published versions — a strong account-compromise indicator.
  • Typosquat & homoglyph detector — Damerau-Levenshtein distance check against top packages; Cyrillic/Greek lookalike character normalisation.
  • Install-script auditor — flags every preinstall/postinstall hook with a bundled whitelist of known-safe packages.
  • Dependency confusion detector — version-inflation and fresh-plant heuristics for scoped packages that may have been planted on public npm.
  • OSSF Scorecard (optional) — flags packages below a configurable security score.
  • Lockfile audit — walks package-lock.json transitive deps and flags malicious packages invisible in package.json.
  • Phantom dependency detector — scans project JS/TS source files for imports not declared in any package.json dependency section.

Smart workflow integration

  • Quick fix: Remove from dependencies — deletes the entry and cleans trailing commas.
  • Quick fix: Add to ignore list — suppresses false positives per-package, instantly.
  • Status bar widget — live finding count (NSG: 0 / NSG: 3 ⚠). Click to open the Problems panel.
  • Balloon notification when a new critical threat is detected.

Settings

Settings → Tools → NPM Safety Guard

  • Enable/disable each detection category independently
  • Severity threshold — hide findings below a chosen level (info → critical)
  • Ignore list — package names to suppress, one per line
  • Optional OSV.dev API token for higher rate limits

Privacy

No telemetry. No tracking. The only external calls are to api.osv.dev (CVE data) and registry.npmjs.org (maintainer history), both cached locally for 24 hours.

By SendWaveHub.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.2.0 — Phantom dependency detection, NSG-014, DB auto-publish

  • New (Layer 9): Phantom dependency detector — scans project JS/TS source files for import/require statements and flags packages that are imported but not declared in any package.json dependency section. Async, cached per declared-dep fingerprint, capped at 5 000 files.
  • New (Layer 10 / NSG-014): Maintainer email domain change detector — compares the email domain of each maintainer across consecutive published versions. A domain change (e.g. alice@company.com → alice@attacker.io) is a strong account-compromise signal and fires a WARNING.
  • Both new layers have dedicated on/off toggles in Settings → NPM Safety Guard → Detection Layers.
  • DB auto-publish: @sendwavehub/nsg-db npm package now auto-publishes on every daily malware-DB update merge.

0.1.9 — Team config, CLI, public dashboard

  • New: .nsgrc.json team configuration — commit a shared policy file to your repo (score thresholds, whitelists, disabled checkers). The plugin reads it from the project root and merges with per-user settings.
  • New: CLI mode via npx npm-safety-guard — run all detection layers in CI without an IDE.
  • New: public findings dashboard auto-generated from the malware DB diff (GitHub Pages).

0.1.8 — Lockfile integrity, repo/publisher mismatch, download inflation

  • New: package-lock.json integrity checker — flags entries whose resolved URL points outside registry.npmjs.org or registry.yarnpkg.com (supply-chain redirect attack pattern).
  • New: GitHub repo / npm publisher mismatch detector (NSG-015) — flags scoped packages where the GitHub org in repository.url differs from the npm publisher username.
  • New: Download inflation detector (NSG-016) — flags packages published fewer than 30 days ago with abnormally high download counts (coordinated artificial inflation signal).

0.1.7 — Settings UI refresh, PinToSafeVersion, OpenInBrowser

  • Settings UI redesigned with grouped sections: Detection Layers, Severity Threshold, OSSF Scorecard, Ignore List, Typosquat Ignore List, Install-Script Whitelist, API Tokens.
  • New quick fix: Pin to safe version — rewrites the version literal in package.json to the known-safe version from the malicious-package DB entry.
  • New quick fix: Open in browser — opens the npm page or advisory URL directly from the problem popup.

0.1.6 — JetBrains feature parity (typosquat, install-script, dep confusion, OSSF)

  • New: Typosquat & homoglyph detector — Damerau-Levenshtein distance ≤ 2 against the top-packages list; Cyrillic/Greek lookalike normalisation; 30 % relative-distance cap to suppress false positives on short names.
  • New: Install-script auditor — flags packages with preinstall/postinstall hooks; bundled whitelist of known-safe packages; per-project user whitelist; Allow install scripts quick fix.
  • New: Dependency confusion detector — version-inflation heuristic (public major far ahead of pinned) and fresh-plant heuristic (new package, near-zero downloads); skips well-known public scopes.
  • New: OSSF Scorecard checker (optional) — flags packages below a configurable score threshold; optional GitHub token for higher rate limits.
  • Malware DB updated to schema v2 with schemaVersion field and ETag-based conditional GET for bandwidth efficiency.
  • Unit test suite added for malicious DB lookup, OSV response parsing, and packument parsing.

0.1.5 — AI Config Guard

  • New: AI Config Guard scans installed node_modules for JS/TS code that reads, writes, or exfiltrates AI assistant credentials (Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, 1Password CLI)
  • Detects the Nx Console v18.95.0 attack pattern (GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w) and related supply-chain campaigns
  • 13 seed signatures: credential reads, cloud key exfiltration, DNS tunnelling, orphan-commit injection, persistence, and AI tool targeting
  • Obfuscation detection: base64-encoded strings, hex-encoded strings, single-level string concatenation
  • Async scanning with per-project coroutine service and in-memory cache — non-blocking, fires once per installed version
  • New toggle in Settings → NPM Safety Guard → Detection Rules: "AI Config Guard"

0.1.4 — CI release pipeline fix

  • Fix automated publish workflow (task rename: runPluginVerifier → verifyPlugin for IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.x)
  • No functional changes from 0.1.3

0.1.3 — Status bar counter: Kotlin object singleton

  • Replace service-based NsgFindingsState with a plain Kotlin object — eliminates all service-lookup race conditions and guarantees the inspection and widget share the exact same counter instance

0.1.2 — Status bar counter fix (root cause)

  • Fixed NSG counter always showing 0 — findings state is now app-level, guaranteeing the inspection and status bar widget share the same instance

0.1.1 — Status bar timer

  • Replaced daemon-event subscription with 1-second timer for reliable status bar repaints

0.1.0 — Initial release

  • Malicious package database with 100+ known-malicious packages (offline, bundled)
  • CVE detection via OSV.dev with 24-hour disk cache
  • Maintainer-change alerts (30-day window, npm registry API)
  • Lockfile audit for package-lock.json transitive dependencies
  • Quick fixes: remove dependency, add to ignore list
  • Settings panel: per-category toggles, severity threshold, ignore list, OSV token
  • Status bar widget with live finding count
  • Balloon notification on new critical findings
  • Supports WebStorm, IntelliJ IDEA, and all IntelliJ-based IDEs 2024.2+

idea-plugin.name: Insomnia SAST
idea-plugin.description:
Insomnia SAST — catch secrets & vulnerabilities before they leave your IDE

The same static-analysis engine that powers the Insomnia CI pipeline and the VS Code extension, now inside your JetBrains IDE — no rule drift between your editor and your build. Scan a file, a folder, or the whole project and review every finding with severity, CWE and one-click navigation to the offending line.

Works in PyCharm, IntelliJ IDEA, PhpStorm, WebStorm, GoLand, RubyMine, CLion, Rider, DataGrip and every other IntelliJ-platform IDE — one plugin, all of them.

What it finds

  • Hardcoded secrets — API keys, tokens and credentials, with live key validation that tells you whether a leaked key is still active.
  • Code vulnerabilities — SQL & command injection, path traversal, SSRF, XSS, insecure deserialization and more, across 16 languages with AST + cross-file taint analysis (not just regex).
  • Vulnerable dependencies (SCA) — known CVEs in your project's packages, matched against an offline-capable advisory database.
  • CMS advisories — WordPress / Joomla / Drupal and other platform CVEs.
  • Web-shells & malware — suspicious code patterns and known payloads.

How it works

  1. Right-click a file or folder in the Project view, or run Tools → Scan with Insomnia SAST.
  2. Findings stream into the Insomnia SAST tool window with severity, CWE and a short description.
  3. Double-click any finding to jump to the exact line, with remediation guidance.

Setup

The plugin uses the standalone insomnia-sast scanner engine, resolved automatically from a bundled dist_sast/ build, the sast pip-launcher cache (pip install sast), or your PATH. If none is found, install the launcher and the engine downloads on first run — SHA-256-verified and OS-matched. No API key, no account, no telemetry; it runs fully offline once installed.

Learn more at insom.ai.

idea-plugin.name: Cert Companion
idea-plugin.description:
A native, client-side viewer for X.509 certificates and keystores — .pem, .crt, .cer, .der, .jks, .p12, .pfx. Shows subject, issuer, serial number, validity (with a clear warning when a certificate is expired or expiring soon), signature algorithm, SHA-256 fingerprint, and every alias in a multi-entry keystore.

PEM bundles with multiple certificates are rendered one certificate at a time, each with its own "Copy Raw PEM" button — no unreadable multi-cert block, and a real way to copy the raw certificate content.

100% client-side, using only the JDK's own java.security.KeyStore and java.security.cert APIs — no bundled crypto library, no network access. Keystore passwords are only ever asked for on demand and never cached.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, and it works correctly in both dark and light themes.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • A certificate's serial number is now shown as unsigned hex even when the issuing CA encoded it without the DER padding byte that keeps it positive (a real, documented bug in some CAs' certificates, not hypothetical) -- matches the convention openssl x509 -serial and other tools use, instead of a literal minus sign.

Added

  • Review/star CTA: after 5 successfully decoded certificates/keystores, a one-time notification asks whether to rate the plugin on Marketplace, with a permanent "Don't ask again" option. Standard mechanism used catalog-wide; this plugin (built before the rollout) had been missed.

idea-plugin.name: API Security Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Lightweight, 100% local API-security checks for Java and Kotlin: hardcoded secrets and API keys, plaintext HTTP URLs, TLS trust managers that accept every certificate, REST endpoints that expose a persistence entity directly (OWASP API Security Top 10 — Excessive Data Exposure / Mass Assignment), and OpenAPI spec checks for missing authentication and permissive CORS.

Also finds known-format API tokens — OpenAI, Anthropic, Hugging Face, GitHub, GitLab, npm, Stripe, AWS and more — in JSON, YAML, .properties and .env files, including the MCP server configs AI tools read (mcp.json, claude_desktop_config.json), where keys are routinely pasted in by mistake. Free.

No network calls, no cloud dashboard, no background processes — every check runs in-process during the IDE's own background highlighting pass. Built after reviewing real, recent complaints against the market-leading security scanners: recurring IDE freezes and crashes during scans, broken suppression/ignore controls, and an "Ultimate Plus" paywall undocumented until checkout. Every rule here can be turned off individually, and none of them are held back behind a paid tier.

API Security Companion Pro (optional paid tier): Kotlin support for Excessive Data Exposure/Mass Assignment (the free tier's checks are Java-only), two more OWASP API Security Top 10 checks — Broken Object Level Authorization and Unrestricted Resource Consumption — team rules shared via a .gaphunter-security-rules file committed to your repo, so a rule the team agreed on can't be silently disabled by one person's local settings — and an optional, off-by-default local ML model that reduces false positives on generic high-entropy secret matches (never on a recognized format like an AWS key or a JWT — those stay exact-match). Runs 100% on-device, tuned to only suppress a warning when very confident, and can be turned on from Settings once you've read what it does. Pro also adds a stricter name-plus-entropy check for credential-named keys in configuration files (client_secret, DB_PASSWORD, Authorization: Bearer ...).
idea-plugin.change-notes:

idea-plugin.name: JWT Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Decode and verify JSON Web Tokens directly in the IDE. A dedicated tool window decodes the header and payload (Base64URL, not standard Base64) into two independently scrollable panels — no fixed-height table that becomes unusable once a token has more than a couple of claims.

Signature verification for the twelve JWS algorithms the JDK implements — HS256/HS384/HS512, RS256/RS384/RS512, PS256/PS384/PS512 and ES256/ES384/ES512 — using only javax.crypto/java.security, with no bundled crypto library. Paste the shared secret for HMAC or a public key/certificate PEM for the rest: the token's own alg header decides which one is used. An unsigned token (alg: none) is reported as unsigned rather than as an unsupported algorithm.

iat/exp/nbf claims are rendered as human-readable dates with a clear expired/expiring-soon/valid indicator.

Nothing typed into the tool window is ever saved or cached between sessions — the token, secret, and key are held in memory only.

idea-plugin.name: SPHIOR CODE
idea-plugin.description:
SPHIOR CODE — deterministic secrets + insecure-pattern (CWE) detection with tamper-evident audit evidence, right in your JetBrains IDE.

  • No AI, no source upload. Detection is 100% deterministic and runs locally via a bundled language server. Your code never leaves your machine.

idea-plugin.name: JWT Signature Verification Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning icon on a jjwt Jwts.parser()...parse(token) call chain -- jjwt's own parse method accepts a JWT whose signature is empty or doesn't match, even when a signing key has been configured on the parser. This is a documented real vulnerability class: CodeQL ships a dedicated "Missing JWT signature check" query for exactly this pattern, and jjwt's own issue tracker confirms it. The fix is simple but easy to miss -- use parseClaimsJws(), parseSignedClaims(), or parsePlaintextJws() instead, which actually verify the signature.

100% static text/PSI analysis -- matches the call chain by simple text ("jwt" + "parser"/"parserBuilder" in the receiver, plus a bare parse(...) call), so it works whether the real jjwt jar is on the classpath or not. Java and Kotlin.

Stated honestly: v0.1 targets jjwt specifically (the most common Java JWT library) and matches by simple text, not real type resolution -- an unrelated .parse(...) method on a variable that happens to be named/called like a JWT parser is a possible (rare) false positive, and an aliased or wrapped jjwt parser call isn't covered.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: ReDoS Catastrophic-Backtracking Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on a Pattern.compile("...")/ "...".matches("...") call in Java whose literal regex argument has a structural catastrophic-backtracking pattern: a nested unbounded quantifier ((a+)+), or an unbounded-quantified alternation with overlapping branches ((a|a)*). A single crafted input against either pattern can hang a server thread indefinitely (CWE-400, Uncontrolled Resource Consumption -- Regular Expression Denial of Service).

Parses the regex literal with its own hand-rolled grammar -- never depends on java.util.regex internally, since the platform exposes no PSI for the interior of a regex string. No plugin on the JetBrains Marketplace was found dedicated to this specific check.

Stated honestly: v0.1 covers Java only, only the two structural patterns named above -- not a full backtracking-cost engine -- and only a static string literal argument, never a regex built dynamically at runtime.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: AWS S3 Public ACL via SDK Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on a real AWS SDK for Java call (application code, not infrastructure-as-code) that sets a PUBLIC ACL on an S3 bucket or object: SDK 1.x's AmazonS3.setBucketAcl(bucket, CannedAccessControlList.PublicRead)/ PutObjectRequest.withCannedAcl(...)/ .setCannedAcl(...), and SDK 2.x's fluent .acl(ObjectCannedACL.PUBLIC_READ)/ .acl("public-read").

Public exposure of data via application code, not just infrastructure configuration -- a category with its own dedicated detector in the AWS CodeGuru Detector Library. Different angle from IaC-level S3 misconfig (already covered by CLI tools like Checkov/tfsec); no Marketplace plugin found dedicated to this specific application-code category.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only these known method forms of AWS SDK 1.x and 2.x -- never analyzes an IAM policy embedded as a JSON string, never follows an ACL value passed as a parameter between methods. The ACL argument is resolved as a direct literal/enum reference, or through ONE level of local-variable indirection within the same method.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: JWT Webhook Signature Timing-Safe Comparison Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on a webhook/HMAC signature comparison that uses .equals()/Arrays.equals() (short-circuits on the first differing byte) instead of MessageDigest.isEqual(...) (constant-time) -- CWE-208, Observable Timing Discrepancy. An attacker can reconstruct a valid HMAC signature byte-by-byte by measuring response times, forging webhook events.

Flags the comparison site inside a method that itself computes an HMAC, recognizing signature-related identifiers by naming convention (sig/hmac/hash/ digest/mac). This pattern is real and widely documented (Svix, Stripe-style HMAC guides, OWASP); webhook-signature-companion (this catalog) verifies that a signature-verification mechanism exists at all -- a different angle from whether the comparison itself is constant-time.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only detects the pattern within the SAME method where both the HMAC computation and the comparison happen -- never follows a signature value passed to another method for comparison. A method already using MessageDigest.isEqual anywhere in its body is assumed already safe.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: Kubernetes RBAC Wildcard Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on a Role/ClusterRole rule that combines a wildcard ("*") in verbs or resources with a sensitive resource -- secrets, pods/exec, clusterrolebindings. This is the most common path to privilege escalation after a single pod is compromised in a cluster (OWASP Kubernetes Top 10, K03 -- Overly Permissive RBAC Configurations).

100% static text analysis -- an indentation-based line scanner, not a real YAML parser, so it works whether the real Kubernetes/YAML plugin is installed or not. Handles both list shapes YAML allows for resources/verbs: flow style (resources: ["secrets"]) and block style (resources: followed by - secrets on its own line).

Stated honestly: v0.1 only scans Role/ ClusterRole manifests in the standard rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 shape -- it never resolves a RoleBinding/ClusterRoleBinding to know who is actually granted the permission, only flags the dangerous rule itself.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: Terraform IAM Wildcard Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on an IAM policy statement (inside a Terraform aws_iam_policy/aws_iam_role_policy resource's jsonencode({...}) block) whose Action or Resource is "*" with no Condition scoping it down -- a direct violation of least-privilege, documented as a dedicated check by tfsec (no-policy-wildcards) and Tenable, a real vector for privilege escalation in cloud incidents.

Not a JSON parser -- despite the name jsonencode, its argument is an HCL map/list literal (evaluated to a JSON string only at Terraform apply time), walked directly via brace/bracket balancing that respects string literals. No Terraform/HCL PSI dependency -- the platform bundles none for a Kotlin-only plugin.

An Effect = "Deny" statement is never flagged, even with unscoped wildcards -- that's the most restrictive statement possible (AWS's own "quarantine" pattern for a compromised principal), not a least-privilege violation. Handles both a statement list and a single statement object.

Stated honestly: only the direct HCL pattern (jsonencode({...}) embedded directly in the resource) -- never follows a policy loaded from an external .json file via file(...), and never parses the aws_iam_policy_document data source (a different, common HCL shape for the same thing).

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • An Effect = "Deny" statement was flagged as an overly permissive wildcard the same as Effect = "Allow" -- but Deny on Action = "*"/Resource = "*" with no Condition is the most restrictive statement possible (AWS's own documented "quarantine" pattern for isolating a compromised principal), the opposite of a least-privilege violation. Deny statements are never flagged now.
  • Statement as a single object (Statement = {...}), not wrapped in a list, was never scanned at all -- a real false negative, since AWS IAM allows both forms when there's exactly one statement and real Terraform code uses the object form for simple single-permission policies. Both forms are handled now.

idea-plugin.name: Dockerfile Missing USER Instruction Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning when a Dockerfile's FINAL build stage never sets a non-root USER -- Docker runs a container as root by default when USER is absent, a real risk documented explicitly by Docker's own guide for the instruction (container escape/privilege escalation if a volume mount is misconfigured).

Reasons over real multi-stage structure -- a USER instruction in an EARLIER stage never counts on its own; only the file's last FROM (the stage a plain docker build with no --target actually runs) is checked. When that last stage builds on a PREVIOUS named stage from the same file (FROM base AS final, not an external image), the check follows Docker's own inheritance and picks up whatever USER that stage chain last set. Confirmed with the strongest evidence available: an open issue in hadolint's own repository (hadolint/hadolint#1089, still open as of 2026-09) asking for exactly this rule -- not even the standard Dockerfile CLI linter has it implemented yet.

Stated honestly: never validates that the referenced user actually exists (USER appuser with no prior RUN useradd appuser is a different problem, out of scope here), and a USER instruction split across lines with a trailing \ is not recognized.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • The final stage's effective USER now follows Docker's own stage inheritance: when it builds on a previous named stage from the same file (FROM base AS final, not an external image), the check picks up whatever USER that stage chain last set instead of resetting to "no USER seen" on every FROM. Confirmed with 3 tests that failed against the 0.1.0 scanner before the fix -- a real false positive on the common pattern of a shared base stage that switches to a non-root user once.
  • A file named Dockerfile.md/.markdown/.mdx/.rst/.adoc is no longer treated as a real Dockerfile -- found via a 220-file real-world corpus check, where ~10% of files matching the old dockerfile.* rule by name turned out to be Markdown cheatsheets with unrelated FROM lines used as documentation examples. Real variant Dockerfiles (Dockerfile.prod, Dockerfile.arm64) are still recognized.
  • "Rate on Marketplace" now links to this plugin's own reviews page instead of the vendor page (the numeric plugin ID wasn't known yet at 0.1.0 time).

idea-plugin.name: Redis/Redisson Distributed Lock Missing TTL Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on a SET ... NX call (Jedis's SetParams.nx()/Lettuce's SetArgs.Builder.nx() manual distributed-lock pattern) with no EX/PX expiry chained onto the same builder -- a lock acquired this way never expires on its own if the process holding it crashes before releasing it, permanently blocking the resource for every other caller (documented risk in Redisson's own distributed-lock guide).

Redisson is explicitly considered, and deliberately never flagged for its own plain RLock.lock() (no leaseTime argument) -- Redisson's own watchdog mechanism automatically renews the lock while the holder is alive precisely BECAUSE no lease time was given. Flagging that shape the same way as Jedis/Lettuce's SET NX would be a real, wrong false positive -- resolving which concrete client is behind the call is the real mechanism here, same discipline as redisson-client-reuse-companion (this catalog, different angle: client-instance reuse, not TTL).

Stated honestly: v0.1 matches by text within the .set(...) call's own argument -- never resolves the real client type, never follows an expiry value passed in from a variable computed elsewhere.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: Unsafe Deserialization Sink Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on a new ObjectInputStream(...).readObject() call inside a Spring MVC/JAX-RS endpoint method whose constructor argument traces back (within the same method, one direct hop) to an untrusted parameter -- CWE-502, Deserialization of Untrusted Data, one of the most-cited OWASP Top 10 categories for Java, a real path to remote code execution via gadget chains.

Same source-to-sink principle CodeQL uses for this exact category, implemented with PSI alone -- no external analysis engine, no CI pipeline. CodeQL covers this as a batch/CI query, not an inline IDE inspection; no Marketplace plugin found with this specific mechanism.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only follows the data within the SAME method and one direct hop to a parameter -- never crosses more than one method of distance. The untrusted source is a closed list of known Spring MVC/JAX-RS controller signatures, not a general taint analysis of the whole project.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: SSRF via Unsanitized URL Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on an HTTP call (HttpRequest.newBuilder(...)/ Spring RestTemplate/OkHttp's Request.Builder) whose URL/host argument traces back (within the same method, one direct hop) to an untrusted Spring MVC/JAX-RS controller parameter, with no allowlist validation found in the same method -- CWE-918, Server-Side Request Forgery. An attacker uses the server itself as a proxy toward internal resources (cloud metadata endpoints, internal services with no perimeter authentication).

Same source-to-sink flow-following mechanism as unsafe-deserialization-sink-companion (this catalog), applied to a different sink category. This exact category has a dedicated CodeQL query and a dedicated AWS CodeGuru Detector Library detector; no Marketplace plugin found doing it as an inline IDE inspection.

Stated honestly: v0.1 uses the same one-method-of-distance bound as its sibling plugin, a closed list of known HTTP sinks (java.net.http.HttpClient, RestTemplate, OkHttp), no general taint analysis of the whole project.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: PII via toString() Leak Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on a logging/print call passed an instance of a class whose toString() exposes a PII field (email, SSN, phone, date of birth, credit card...) -- toString() on a user object often serializes the whole model, including PII, unlike log.info(user.getEmail()) which explicitly picks only what should be logged. A well-documented pattern of real incidents (Piiano, New Relic, Guidewire Security).

Different angle from pii-field-annotation-companion (this catalog): that plugin flags a PII field itself passed directly to a logger; here the field never appears textually at the call site at all -- it leaks implicitly through toString()'s serialization of the whole object.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only toString() generated by the IDE or Lombok @ToString (a predictable field-listing shape) -- a fully hand-written toString() with arbitrary logic is out of scope. Also covers implicit string concatenation (log.info("User: " + user)), not just a direct single argument.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: CompletableFuture Cancellation Propagation Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on a .thenCompose(...) chain whose result future can be cancelled (a .cancel(true) call found elsewhere in the same method), where the lambda passed to .thenCompose directly constructs and returns another CompletableFuture with no evidence that cancellation is ever forwarded to it -- orphaned work keeps running and consuming resources after the caller believes it cancelled the whole operation.

A documented, real gap in issues of established libraries (Reactor Core, Failsafe, OpenTelemetry Java instrumentation) -- CompletableFuture.thenCompose never propagates cancellation into the inner stage on its own. No dedicated IDE plugin found for this.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only the pattern where the lambda's body directly returns another CompletableFuture CONSTRUCTED in the same method (CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(...)/ .runAsync(...)/new CompletableFuture<>()) -- never follows the cancellation through a call to an external method that returns one.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: Environment-Specific Constant Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on a hardcoded URL or host:port string literal in Java source that also appears, textually, as a value in one of the project's own config files (.properties/.yml/.yaml/ .env) -- the value clearly belongs to config, and the code copy can now silently drift out of sync with it.

Real, documented impact: configuration/IaC drift -- a value that one day gets updated only in the config file (the "correct" place) leaves real code still pointing at the old endpoint/port, with no compile error to catch it. Adjacent to this catalog's own config-secrets-file-companion/ env-diff-companion, but neither checks specifically for code-vs-config value divergence.

Stated honestly: v0.1 matches only full URLs (http(s)://...) and explicit host:port pairs -- never a bare port number without host context, to keep the false-positive rate low. Exact string match only against config values found in .properties/.yml/.yaml files and the single exact filename .env (no .env.* variants yet).

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: CafeBabe
idea-plugin.description: This plugin integrates CafeBabe Bytecode editor with Intellij IDEA.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
This plugin integrates CafeBabe Bytecode Editor with Intellij IDEA.

How to use Class Viewer/Editor

  • Select class file in the files tree or click on "Open File" icon within plugin toolwindow;
  • Activate context menu for the selected file;
  • Select "Open in CafeBabe" item from the context menu;
  • Class will be disassembled and represented in CafeBabe toolwindow.
  • If you want to disassemble some method, navigate to methods list, select one method and activate context menu. Follow "Go to method body" link. You will be redirected to "Bytecode Editor" toolwindow.
  • Now you can create/delete/edit bytecode instructions.
  • In constant pool you can modify UTF strings;
  • If you want to get explanation for a given instruction, click on Help icon.
  • If you modified the file and then trying to save it, "Save as" dialog will be initiated, allowing you to save modified class.
  • You can click on "Save as" icon any time when you want to save your modifications.

How to use ClassHound

  • Click on ClassHound icon - new toolwindow will be open;
  • In ClassHound toolwindow select archive, then package, class, fileld or method. You can select only package or only package class;
  • By double clicking on package, class, field or method - selected item will be loaded into Class Viewer/Editor. If it's field or method, Class File Viewer/Ediror will be positioned on selected field/method;
  • You can add new archive to the list of available archives - then you can explore it in standard way.
Changes:
  • 1.0.1

    • Warning when choosing nginx executable. Running "nginx -V" can be cancelled and default parameter values will be used.
    0.0.4
    • Basic $variable support. Autocompletion and name checks are available. No checks for parent context and no support for variables in strings yet.
    0.0.3
    • Log files can be shown in tabs next to console
    0.0.2
    • Autocompletion is context-aware
    • Directive list is taken from sources, not from docs
    • More advanced inspections like checking if a directive can reside in a context
    • Should work on Mac
    0.0.1
    • First release. Won't work for Mac.
    • Basic autocompletion and inspections.

idea-plugin.name: JRebel and XRebel
idea-plugin.description:
JRebel is a productivity tool that allows developers to reload code changes instantly. It skips the rebuild, restart, and redeploy cycle common in Java development. JRebel enables developers to get more done in the same amount of time and stay in the flow while coding. JRebel supports a majority of real-world enterprise java stacks and is easy to install into existing development environments.


XRebel is a performance tool for Java development which gives developers real time performance insights to help them understand and resolve potential issues faster and earlier, during the development phase.

idea-plugin.name: Gerrit
idea-plugin.description:
Gerrit Code Review integration: review, fetch and push changes without leaving your IDE.

Requires Gerrit 2.9 or newer (older versions lack parts of the REST API).

Features:

  • Review changes in the IDE: vote, reply and comment on files and lines
    Add a comment with a right click on a line in the diff or with the "C" key; click a comment's icon to edit or remove it while it is unpublished. "Reply..." or a vote publishes your comments.
    The comments of a checked out change show in the editor too, on their lines as you edit the file.
  • Diff changes against your local clone, with the IDE's syntax highlighting and navigation
  • List and query changes, and get notified of new changes waiting for your review
  • Push to Gerrit from the push dialog: target branch, topic, reviewers and CC with account suggestions, and on Gerrit 2.15+ a hashtag, WIP and private changes
  • Check out, cherry-pick and reset to changes in your local clone
  • Submit, abandon, restore, rebase and revert changes, star them and add reviewers; publish and delete draft changes (Gerrit older than 2.15)
  • Run the IDE's inspections on the files a change touches
  • Clone Gerrit projects from the IDE, with the commit-msg hook installed
  • Open files and commits in Gitiles, and the Gerrit changes of commits selected in the VCS log
  • Several Gerrit accounts, one per project

Please report issues on the GitHub issue tracker rather than in reviews.

The plugin talks to the Gerrit REST API through gerrit-rest-java-client, which you can use in your own Java applications as well.

If you like this plugin, you can support it:

  • Spread it: tell your friends who use IntelliJ and Gerrit about it.
  • Rate it on the JetBrains Marketplace.
  • Star it on GitHub.
  • Improve it: report bugs and request features, or fix and build them yourself, everything is open source.
  • Donate: see the README.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
See for all changes: https://github.com/uwolfer/gerrit-intellij-plugin/commits/

  • Important Note: You can report exception-issues directly from your IDE. Please add at least a comment what you have done when it occurred / how you can reproduce it. It would be even better when add an email address so I can contact you in case of questions.
  • Would you like to try test-builds of this plugin before official release? Please check out: https://github.com/uwolfer/gerrit-intellij-plugin#pre-releases.
  • 2.2.0
    • add comments in the editor for a checked out change and in the unified diff viewer, mark them on the scroll bar, and go to the next and previous comment in a diff
    • add change actions: "Rebase", "Restore" and "Revert", and "Open in Gerrit" in the annotate gutter menu
    • add reviewers and CCs to "Create Feature Merge Change"
    • add "Mark as Reviewed / Not Reviewed" and show reviewed files in the changes tree
    • add accounts to the settings with name, avatar and login state, switch the project's account from the tool window, and offer to log in again when Gerrit refuses a login
    • let a project pick which Gerrit instance it talks to, and suggest accounts for reviewers and CC on push
    • add Chinese, Japanese and Korean translations
    • show why the change list is empty, keep its filters and search history, reload it when the tool window is shown, and add keyboard support
    • show and hide list columns from the header menu, and show avatars next to the owner
    • hide automated change messages by default
    • hide files only a rebase changed in patch set diffs
    • edit comments as Markdown and render code fences
    • require Gerrit 2.9 or newer
    • use themed monochrome icons for the tool window and actions
    • fix comments in the editor going astray
    • fix Gerrit being given the wrong credentials by git
    • fix the push to Gerrit default only applying after a restart
    • fix the Gitiles line of a file with a glob name
    • keep the review dialogs responsive on a slow Gerrit
  • 2.1.0
    • add "Use Gerrit in this project" to the settings, which turns the push dialog options, the tool window, the notifications, the commit-msg hook check and the "Open in Gerrit" and "Open in Gitiles" actions off in a project which is not on Gerrit
    • add "Inspect Code..." to a change's context menu, which inspects the files the change touches
    • warn when the commit-msg hook is missing in a Gerrit repository and offer to install it
    • add change actions: "Cherry-Pick", "Reset Current Branch to Here", "Set Assignee", "Copy URL", "Open in Gitiles" and replying to a change without voting
    • show work-in-progress changes, reviewers without a vote apart from CCs, and the voter behind a label icon
    • connect to Gerrit through a SOCKS proxy and give up after the IDE's timeout
    • fetch changes without the download-commands plugin and fall back to other Gerrit remotes
    • diff a merge change against its first parent
    • fix the Reset action on IntelliJ 2026.2
    • fix password field and Test button in settings
    • fix comments on deleted or renamed files, and on the line they were started on
    • fix the change list and details being replaced by an older or late load
    • fix reviewers whose name has a comma and unescaped change subjects in notifications
    • fix the IDE freezing while waiting for the commit-msg hook
  • 2.0.1
    • add "Create Feature Merge Change" action
    • fix push dialog selecting every repository in a multi-repo project when "push to Gerrit by default" is enabled
    • fix "Open in Gerrit" sending the browser to an invalid URL when no host is configured
    • fix percent-encoding of the asterisk in patch set descriptions
    • fix reviewer names with non-breaking spaces not being trimmed before sending them to Gerrit
    • fix the diff "add comment" shortcut no longer reaching the keymap, and make it configurable
    • fix focus handling of the inline comment popup breaking composed input (e.g. IME)
    • fix settings page being shared between projects instead of built per project
    • read and write Gerrit credentials off the event dispatch thread to avoid blocking the IDE

idea-plugin.name: Dash
idea-plugin.description:
A smart and simple plugin that provides keyboard shortcut access for Dash, Velocity or Zeal in IntelliJ IDEA, RubyMine, WebStorm, PhpStorm, PyCharm, DataGrip, CLion, GoLand and Android Studio.

Usage

The default shortcut assigned to smart-search is Cmd-Shift-D (Mac OS X) or Ctrl-Shift-D (Windows, Linux).

A menubar command named either "Smart-Search Documentation" can be found in the "Tools" menu.

The plugin either searches for the statement at caret position or the current selection. It will identify the programming language in use and request filtered results accordingly. A non filtered search over all documentation entries can be invoked by adding the Alt modifier key to the shortcut. "Search all Documentation" is also available in the tools menu.

Configuration

Shortcut

You can change the shortcut at Preferences -> Keymap -> Plug-ins -> Dash.

Toolbar Icon

You can add a button to the toolbar. Right-click the menubar -> Customize […]. You will find the button under "Plug-ins -> Dash".

Supported API Documentation Browsers

Kapeli Dash (Mac OS X)

Dash is an API Documentation Browser and Code Snippet Manager. Dash stores snippets of code and instantly searches offline documentation sets for 150+ APIs (for a full list, see below). You can even generate your own docsets or request docsets to be included. http://kapeli.com/dash

Velocity (Windows)

Velocity gives your Windows desktop offline access to over 150 API documentation sets (provided by Dash for OS X). https://velocity.silverlakesoftware.com

Zeal (Linux & Windows)

Zeal is a simple offline API documentation browser inspired by Dash (OS X app). http://zealdocs.org
