idea-plugin.name: SOAR
idea-plugin.description:
SOAR(SQL optimizer And Rewrite) is plugin of SOAR which for analysis SQL performance and optimize.


How to use it

  1. SOAR dependent GO environment, so you need install and configure Go environment first
  2. Open settings and find SOAR configuration panel, click Init button
  3. Execute download and modify permission command like content in dialog
  4. After executed the command, input SOAR location and click check button to verify SOAR is installed correctly
  5. Modify configuration of database as your's by file or manual config
  6. Choose SQL content you need to analysis or format, right click call Editor popup, find SOAR and click relevant menu, then show analysis result dialog or replace origin content as formatted SQL

You can get more help of configuration or report issue in soar-jetbrains-plugin


SOAR(SQL optimizer And Rewrite) 是一为小米数据库工具 SOAR 开发的 IDE 插件，用于 SQL 优化改写

如何使用

  1. SOAR 执行依赖于 GO 运行环境，请先确保 GO 环境安装配置正确
  2. 打开设置，找到 SOAR 的设置面板，点击 Init 按钮获取安装命令
  3. 执行弹窗内的命令，下载 SOAR 并修改执行权限
  4. 执行完命令后，将 SOAR 的路径填写在配置中，点击 Check 按钮检查是否正确配置
  5. 修改配置文件，可以选择使用文件配置或者手动配置
  6. 选择需要分析或格式化的 SQL 内容，右键选择编辑弹窗，找到 SOAR 菜单并选择需要的功能，执行完成之后会弹窗显示分析结果或用格式化后的 SQL 替换原来的内容

可以在 soar-jetbrains-plugin 获取详细配置信息或反馈问题

idea-plugin.name: Redis
idea-plugin.description:
IntelliJ IDEA Redis Integration Plugin

A powerful, high-performance Redis management tool fully integrated into IntelliJ IDEA. Connect, browse, query, and edit Redis data without leaving your IDE.

Key Features

  • Connection Modes: Standalone, Redis Cluster, Sentinel, SSH Tunnel, SSL/TLS, and RESP2/RESP3 protocol support.
  • All Data Types Supported: String, Hash, List, Set, Sorted Set (ZSet), Stream, RedisJSON, and interactive Bitmap visualization.
  • Value Edit History & Rollback: Automatic pre-write snapshots with one-click rollback, field-level restore, and conflict warnings.
  • Custom Value Codecs: Built-in Gzip, Zlib, Base64, Hex, Auto-Detect viewers, plus user-defined Groovy script codecs.
  • Intelligent Console: DataGrip-style header with live database switcher, smart command & key autocompletion, and non-blocking result panel (Text, JSON, Table).
  • Developer Utilities: Generate Java code (Spring Data Redis, Redisson, Jedis), real-time server status dashboard, TTL presets, and large collection pagination.

Links & Community

GitHub Repository | Issue Tracker | QQ Group: 674948973

idea-plugin.change-notes:
The current version is 1.5.6. The following changes were made since 1.5.4:

  • Added a first-use approval prompt before creating a database connection from project-stored settings.

  • Stopped automatic database connections when a project or Schema Explorer opens. Users now explicitly refresh to connect and load schema information.

  • Validated On-prem and CloudSim endpoint URLs so they must use http or https, include a host, and avoid embedded credentials.

  • Moved sensitive connection values to IntelliJ PasswordSafe, including On-prem passwords, On-prem truststore passphrases, Cloud private-key passphrases, and CloudSim tenant identifiers.

  • Added automatic migration for existing project connection settings from older plugin versions.

  • Changed CloudSim tenant handling to require an explicit alphanumeric tenant identifier and reject blank values and exampleId.

  • Stopped showing CloudSim tenant token text in connection display output.

  • Scoped On-prem SSL truststore settings to the Oracle NoSQL connection instead of IntelliJ IDEA JVM-wide TLS settings.

  • Updated the plugin distribution build so ./gradlew buildPlugin creates Oracle-NoSQL-Database-Connector-<version>.zip.

  • Added a restricted-network build option: -Poracle.nosql.skipSearchableOptions=true.

  • Updated Gradle to 9.3.0 and the IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin to 2.16.0.

  • Updated plugin dependencies, including Oracle NoSQL Java SDK 5.4.22, org.json 20250517, Gson 2.13.2, and RSyntaxTextArea 3.6.0.

  • Fixed build instability after the Gradle IntelliJ Platform Plugin 2.x upgrade.

  • Fixed record-view and update-row shared-state issues that could affect concurrent row update, JSON download, and binary download actions.

  • Fixed deprecated IntelliJ API usage and plugin configuration for newer IntelliJ Platform compatibility.

idea-plugin.name: SQL Server Backup And Restore
idea-plugin.description:
A plugin that allows creating backups and restoring them from the DataGrip context for Microsoft SQLServer databases.

The plugin built for my own personal use case which means that it will work for databases that are connected through an SSH tunnel. It supports downloading backups from the remote server to the local machine without using xp_cmdshell command.

Features:

  • Creating a backup, storing it and download it right after
  • Reading a backup into an existing database
  • Reading a backup into a newly created database

Note: AWS and probably also Azure don't seem to support file based backing up and are not supported by this plugin.

idea-plugin.name: Database Generator
idea-plugin.description:
Github | Gitee | Document

English (Google Translate) / 中文

A code generator that relies on the IDEA Database tool to generate the corresponding Java code through the database table structure. The plug-in provides a simple set of add, delete, and modify code templates. You can also add custom templates to generate front-end code or other related code.

Provide all-variable.ftl template file to illustrate all variable usage and corresponding results.

This plugin supports beetl/freemarker/velocity code templates of three template engines. You can choose which template engine to use for the file suffix (btl/ftl/vm). For custom templates, please Read Template Variable Document to understand the contents of related variables before custom development.

This plug-in supports calling the methods in the Groovy script defined by yourself in the template file, please refer to the Groovy Script Instructions for details 。

Please check the Code Template Upgrade Guide, and check the detailed writing Template Variable Document, or check out the code template that covers the use of all variables all-variable.ftl


中文 / English

一个依赖 IDEA Database 工具的代码生成器，通过数据库表结构生成相应的Java代码，插件提供一套简单的增删查改代码模板，也可以新增自定义模板来生成前端代码或其他相关的代码。

提供 all-variable.ftl 模板文件来说明所有的变量使用和对应结果。

idea-plugin.name: JPA Buddy
idea-plugin.description:
Helps developers work efficiently with Hibernate, EclipseLink, Spring Data JPA, Flyway, Liquibase, Lombok, MapStruct, and other related technologies in both Java and Kotlin.

The plugin is intended to:

  • Lower barrier to entry into development with JPA
  • Boost developer’s productivity
  • Make sure your code follows best practices

JPA Buddy delivers:

  • Intuitive wizards to work with JPA
  • Automatic database versioning changelog generation
  • Smart inspections to make the code better
  • JPA Entities generation based on tables (reverse engineering)
  • Visual DTO designer and mapper code generator

You can use JPA Buddy in any project with Spring Boot, Jakarta Enterprise Edition, Quarkus, Micronaut, or even without any framework.


Most loved features

Find a brief list of features below. Take a look at our website and see all the features in action in our YouTube videos.

Use intuitive wizards to work with JPA entities more efficient

  • Generate new entities
  • Create basic attributes and associations
  • Manage indexes and constraints
  • Named Queries
  • Utility methods: equals/hashCode, toString
  • Lombok Support
  • Kotlin Support

Make sure your data model follows best practices with smart inspections

  • Find the right fix if your entity is incorrect
  • Check that your Spring Data repository is correct
  • Detect possible issues using Lombok annotations
  • Make sure you use only the best performing mapping declarations

Use Spring Data JPA with pleasure

  • New repositories generation
  • Convenient wizard for derived and JPQL queries generation
  • Extract JPQL queries from derived methods to keep your code clean
  • Spring Data projections wizard
  • Build EntityGraph for repository methods
  • Audit Support

Convert entities into DDL statements

  • Generate DDL by Entities
  • Append DDL statements into the existing .sql file
  • Resolve validation fails issue right from the stack trace

Save time and efforts on database versioning by automatic generation of Liquibase changelogs and Flyway migrations

  • Differential scripts generation
  • Generating scripts for DB scratch initialization
  • Use smart preview to make sure your differential scripts will not fail on update
  • Generate differential scripts into the existing file

Generate JPA entities from the existing database tables and views (Reverse Engineering)

  • Generate JPA entities from the existing database tables and views
  • Generate attributes into the exiting entity from table columns
  • Support for references that are not backed with a column: OneToMany, OneToOne, ManyToMany

Create DTOs and mappers from JPA entities (DTO Generator)

  • Generate DTOs from JPA entities
  • MapStruct & ModelMapper Support
  • Java Record Support
  • Create JPA entities from POJOs
  • Keep DTOs in sync with its JPA entity
  • Generate DTOs from any POJOs

Coding Assistance

  • Apply intelligent postfix autocompletion and in-code injects for JPA entities, DTOs and MapStruct mappers
  • Edit Liquibase changelog with autocompletion for tables and colum names
  • Use shortcuts to become extremely productive
  • Kotlin Support

idea-plugin.name: Laravel Query
idea-plugin.description:
This plugin provides database integration for Laravel query builder. It works with DataGrip to provide autocompletion for database schemas, tables, views, and columns.

Features

  • Schemas, tables, views and columns completion for query and schema builder methods
  • Completion for database assertion test methods
  • Completion for migrations
  • Inspection of unknown database elements
  • Table alias support
  • Table name resolving from model for eloquent builder methods
  • Model relation table name resolving for eloquent builder relation closure methods
  • Text linking with database elements for navigation and refactoring
  • Configurable table prefix and datasource filtering

Prerequisites

Connect your database

See https://www.jetbrains.com/help/phpstorm/connecting-to-a-database.html#connect-to-mysql-database for instructions.

Laravel tools

You also need either Laravel Idea plugin (paid) or Laravel IDE helper added to your project and run

php artisan ide-helper:generate
php artisan ide-helper:meta
php artisan ide-helper:models
php artisan artisan ide-helper:eloquent

which will generate some helper files so your IDE could see Eloquent methods.

Laravel Query plugin needs either of those to work otherwise, it cannot understand for which methods to trigger autocompletion.

idea-plugin.name: Diff-GenerateSql
idea-plugin.description:
This plugin can help you quickly get the difference in the table structure between the two databases, thereby reducing communication time with developers

It can run in any product that uses the plug-in Database, such as IntelliJ IDEA, DataGrip

steps

  1. click on Database
  2. Choose two My SQL databases (If not, you need to add the My SQL data source first)
  3. right click "Diff-GenerateSql"
  4. Select which database is the source and which database is the target, and click OK
  5. Wait a moment (a few seconds)
  6. Get the difference between the source and target databases,can be executed directly in the database

PS: At this stage,Only Supports MYSQL Database
idea-plugin.change-notes:

idea-plugin.name: Databee: Database Client & SQL
idea-plugin.description:
A database client that lives in your IDE.

Databee is a database client that lives in your IDE: browse your schemas, write SQL the editor understands, run it, and edit the results in place. Works in IntelliJ IDEA and other IntelliJ-based IDEs.

Databases: MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Oracle, Microsoft SQL Server, SQLite, MongoDB, Redis.

SQL editor — every dialect has its own parser, so the editor reads what you wrote instead of guessing:

  • Completion of tables, columns, aliases and CTEs from the schema you are connected to
  • Table and column names the connected data source does not have are marked in the editor, plus an inspection for checking a whole directory at once
  • DELETE / UPDATE without a WHERE is flagged while you type; TRUNCATE and DROP are confirmed before they run
  • Formatting, code folding, comment/uncomment, live templates, Oracle PL/SQL packages (.pkb / .pks)
  • SQL inside Java, Kotlin and XML string literals gets the same highlighting and completion, MyBatis mappers included
  • Ctrl+Enter runs the statement under the caret, and every top-level statement has a run icon in the gutter
  • The dialect is a project setting and can be overridden per file

Data

  • Browse databases, schemas, tables, views, columns and indexes
  • Edit result-grid cells, insert and delete rows, then submit the DML; paging, sorting and filtering included
  • Create / alter / rename / drop / truncate, with the SQL shown before it is applied
  • Export a query or a table as CSV or as INSERT / UPDATE statements; import CSV
  • Run a whole .sql file against the connection you pick

Connections

  • JDBC drivers download from Maven in one click, or point at your own jars
  • SSH tunnels, SSL with custom CA and client certificates
  • Passwords live in the IDE password safe, never in the project files

MCP (IDE 2025.2+): dbtool_* tools for connections, metadata, query and execute, export/import and drivers — enable them in Settings → Tools → MCP Server. Passwords are never returned.

How to use: open the Databee window → add a data source → open a SQL file → pick the connection → Ctrl+Enter.

GitHub · Issues
idea-plugin.change-notes:
New

  • Transactions in the SQL console. Pick Tx: Auto or Tx: Manual on the SQL toolbar. Auto saves each statement right away. Manual keeps your changes until you click Commit, or throws them away with Rollback. The same menu sets the isolation level. Redis, Valkey, MongoDB and ClickHouse always save right away.
  • Each console keeps its own connection. A green or grey dot in front of the data source name shows whether it is connected; click it to connect or disconnect.
  • The red stop button on the SQL toolbar, or Ctrl+F2, stops a statement that is taking too long. Your connection and any changes you have not committed are kept.
  • Disconnect on the database tree. A red square means the data source is connected, a grey one means it is not.
  • Results open in tabs: one for each console, and one for each table you open from the database tree. Changes you make in a table tab are committed or rolled back from that tab. If a tab still has changes that are not committed, you are asked before it closes.
  • History on the SQL toolbar lists the queries you ran recently. Pick one to run it again, or remove it with Remove or the Delete key.
  • Explain on the SQL toolbar shows how the database plans to run the statement under the cursor, without changing any data. Not available for Redis, Valkey and MongoDB.
  • Query results can be exported as Excel or JSON, in addition to CSV and INSERT / UPDATE statements.
  • New databases: ClickHouse, TiDB, OceanBase, YugabyteDB and Valkey.
  • JSON, XML, long text and UUID cells in query results open in their own editor. JSON can be formatted and is checked before it is saved. UUID cells can generate a new value. Columns that only allow a few fixed values offer them in a list.
  • Schemas... on the database tree picks which schemas a data source shows, without opening the connection settings.
  • The password window has a Save password option, on by default. Turn it off to use the password just this once.
  • Databee checks for updates every two hours while the IDE is open.

Fixed

  • Pressing Enter in the SQL editor starts the new line at the left edge.
  • Columns and indexes show "Loading..." while they are being read, instead of looking empty.
  • When several connections to the same database ask for a password at once, you only see one password window.
  • Comments in Oracle files are shown in the comment color.
  • Dates and times copied from query results keep the text you see, and paste back as the same value.
  • A SQLite PRAGMA is no longer marked as an unknown table.
  • When a statement fails, the error is shown in the editor without an extra IDE error.
  • Reformatting is more careful in everyday cases: a column named value, OVER (...), comments in the middle of a statement, #temp tables, \N values, ON EMPTY / ON ERROR, and a / on its own line in Oracle scripts.
  • More Oracle and PL/SQL scripts are read correctly.
  • SQL Server: an UPDATE ... SET you are still typing, and table hints such as (NOLOCK), are read correctly.
  • The toolbar above query results no longer looks squashed on high-resolution screens.
  • If JetBrains Database Tools is also installed, your SQL files stay with it, and consoles opened from Databee stay with Databee.
  • Works with IntelliJ IDEA 2026.3.
  • If an error report cannot be sent, you are told instead of it failing silently.

idea-plugin.name: Graph Database
idea-plugin.description:
See this plugin on Github.

This plugin provides useful features for working with graph databases. It adds syntax highlighting and autocompletion for the Cypher query language, and it supports connecting to and querying remote graph databases.

Features:

  • Write and execute Cypher queries.
  • Explore query results in graph or table view.
  • Manage data sources.

Supported databases:

  • Neo4j 3.4+ (Bolt), including AuraDB

Supported query languages:

  • Cypher
    • Understands queries in `.cyp`, `.cypher` or `.cql` files.
    • Syntax highlight and error reporting.
    • Refactoring support for identifiers, labels, relationship types and properties.
    • Autocompletion support for identifiers, labels, relationship types, properties and stored procedures. Information gathered from existing queries and configured data sources.
    • Code reformatting.
    • Inspections: database warnings, function checks, type system.
    • Auto-inject Cypher language for: neo4j, neo4j-ogm, spring-data-neo4j, neo4j-harness, py2neo.

This plugin is based on the 'Graph Database Support plugin' developed by Neueda Technologies, Ltd. The original plugin has not been updated in a long time.

This plugin has been updated to run with modern versions of IntelliJ and related IDEs. Just like the original plugin, it supports Neo4j and Cypher data sources; however, support for Gremlin data sources (such as Cosmos DB) has been dropped.

idea-plugin.name: Tree View By Default
idea-plugin.description:
If you use document databases (like MongoDB), it is more convenient to preview the query results in Tree mode instead of the standard Table mode. Unfortunately, DataGrip does not provide any way to set Tree as default presentation mode, so you have to switch it manually every time.

This plugin comes to rescue!

What it does:
  • Changes default presentation mode of the query results to Tree
  • If there is only one result, it is automatically expanded
  • You can copy value of the leaf node without the containing JSON via Cmd+Option+C

It is recommended to use this plugin in DataGrip, but it should also work in other IDEs with database support.

idea-plugin.name: Sqlite Remote
idea-plugin.description:
Sqlite Remote

A simple SQLite database extension for synchronizing remote SQLite database file over SSH. Literally can be used on any database modules of Intellij-based IDEs or Datagrip.

Getting Started

  1. Create a Sqlite database connection, choose a local Sqlite file or empty file with an absolute path.
  2. Right-click the database connection you just created, click Sqlite Remote - Config, enter the remote config like this username:password@host:port/path/to/sqlite/file.
  3. Click Sqlite Remote - Download to download the file from remote, which will overwrite the local file.
  4. Click Sqlite Remote - Upload to upload the file to remote, which will overwrite the remote file.
  5. Trigger Sqlite Remote - Auto, then the extension will download/upload database file when the database connection is open/closed.

Notice

These features are designed intentionally, not bugs. Please be aware.

  • The file path of local or remote Sqlite file must be an absolute path. The relative path is different when extension reads.
  • Due to limitations in the IntelliJ SDK, when Auto triggered, the extension may not be able to catch a database connection opening/closing as you expect. This could potentially cause some issues. Anyway, this function is usable.
  • In case of potential issues, please close the database connection before manual upload, refresh the database connection after manual download. In Auto mode, remember to refresh the connection before you use and close it after you use.
  • In Auto mode, the download will only occur if the remote file has a more recent modification time compared to the local file. In other words, the upload will only take place if the local file is newer.
  • The regular expression of Config input is as follows: ^([a-zA-Z0-9_\-]+):(\S+)@([a-zA-Z0-9.\-]+):(\d+)/([a-zA-Z0-9 _\-./]+)$. Since a regular expression is needed to split the fields here, so the input has to be limited.
  • The SSH password in the Config will be replaced with '*' when displayed. But when updating it, please remember to use plaintext instead.
  • Due to limitations in the IntelliJ SDK, passwords or SSH key pairs stored in the SSH configuration of IDEA is unable to be accessed. So the current way may be the simplest one that works.
  • The SSH configuration and file path are primarily designed for Linux, and the support for Windows is currently not optimal.

idea-plugin.name: ERD Editor
idea-plugin.description:
Design a database schema visually, without leaving your IDE. Diagrams are plain JSON files in your project, so they diff and review like any other source file.

The editor never connects to a database — it reads and writes files only. You bring a schema in from a .sql dump or a GraphQL SDL file, and take one back out as DDL.

Getting started

Create an empty file with a .erd.json extension and open it. The diagram opens in the ERD Editor instead of the text editor.

To start from a schema you already have, right-click the canvas and choose Import → Schema SQL for a .sql dump, or Import → GraphQL for a .graphql, .gql or .graphqls file. The editor opens its own file chooser for both; the file does not have to be inside the project.

Features

  • Visual schema design — tables, columns, memos, and four relationship cardinalities (zero-one, zero-N, one-only, one-N)
  • SQL DDL import — bring in a .sql dump from any of the six vendors below. The parser reads CREATE TABLE, CREATE INDEX and ALTER TABLE constraints and skips what it does not recognize, so an awkward dump imports partially rather than failing outright
  • GraphQL SDL import — bring in a schema from any tool that emits SDL. Object types become tables, scalars map to the diagram's own dialect, and the fields pointing at another type become the relationships; the generated types an API layer wraps its rows in are left out rather than drawn as tables
  • DBML import — bring in a .dbml file written for dbdiagram.io or dbdocs.io, or emitted by sql2dbml or prisma-dbml-generator. Tables, columns, indexes, enums and every Ref spelling arrive; a Project, TableGroup or sticky Note is skipped rather than refused
  • AML import — bring in an .aml file written for Azimutt, in either the v2 or the legacy v1 spelling. Entities, attributes, indexes, enums and every relation arrow arrive; a check, a struct type and a view are skipped rather than refused
  • SQL DDL export — MariaDB, MSSQL, MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL, SQLite
  • Code generation — TypeScript, GraphQL, C#, Java, JPA, Kotlin, Scala, Go, SQLAlchemy, TypeORM, Sequelize, Drizzle, DBML, AML
  • Visualization — a force-directed view of how the tables actually relate
  • Export — .erd.json, .sql, .png
  • Quick search over commands, and over tables, columns, comments and memos after #, @ or :, find and replace across names, comments and memos, time travel through this session's edit history, and undo / redo
  • Theming — pick the appearance, gray color and accent color on the canvas or under Settings | Tools | ERD Editor, remembered across restarts. Auto, the default appearance, follows the IDE's light or dark theme and switches with it

Edits are written to the file a fraction of a second after you stop changing it; the tab never shows as modified.

Coding agents

A coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex can edit the diagrams open in this IDE through the @dineug/erd-editor-mcp MCP server. The agent joins the editor like a collaborator: each change shows up on the canvas as it happens, and the agent's undo reverts only its own edits.

Install the MCP server

The server needs Node.js 22.12 or later. npx downloads it the first time the agent starts it, so there is nothing else to install.

  • Claude Code — run claude mcp add --transport stdio erd-editor -- npx -y @dineug/erd-editor-mcp in your project folder
  • Codex — add a [mcp_servers.erd-editor] table with command = "npx" and args = ["-y", "@dineug/erd-editor-mcp"] to ~/.codex/config.toml, or to .codex/config.toml in a trusted project
  • Any other MCP client — run npx -y @dineug/erd-editor-mcp as a stdio server. Start it in your project folder: it resolves relative document paths against its working directory

Edit with an agent

  1. Open the project in the IDE and trust it.
  2. Start the agent in the project folder and ask in plain words, for example "Add a reviews table to schema.erd.json, related to users and products".
  3. Watch the change land on the canvas. The IDE writes it to the file a fraction of a second after editing stops, as it writes your own edits; asking the agent to save writes it at once.

A diagram that is not open yet opens in the ERD Editor on the agent's first edit, without taking the keyboard focus. One IDE serves the diagrams of every project open in it. With no IDE, VS Code window or Obsidian vault window with ERD Editor serving the document's folder, the agent edits the file on disk instead.

Unticking Settings | Tools | ERD Editor → Coding agents, which is on by default, turns the connection off for the whole IDE. The agent can still read the diagrams of the open projects from disk, but it never writes one behind the editor, where the next save would overwrite the change. A project you have not trusted, opened in safe mode, is kept the same way: agents read its diagrams but never change them. The MCP documentation lists every tool with its arguments.

The settings page says when coding agents are unavailable: in an IDE without JCEF, where the editor cannot run either, and in an IDE installed as a Flatpak, whose sandbox the MCP server cannot reach. There the agent edits the files on disk. The ERD Editor does not reload a diagram changed on disk while it is open, and your next edit in it would overwrite the agent's, so close the diagram first.

Requirements

  • An IntelliJ-based IDE, 2025.2 or later.
  • The IDE must be running on the JetBrains Runtime. The editor is a JCEF webview, which is unavailable when the IDE is started on an alternative OpenJDK build.

Documentation

  • Editing Guide — editing, import and export, relationships, quick search, visualization, code generation, settings
  • MCP — installing the MCP server, live and headless editing, every tool
  • Documentation

Also available

  • Web app — installable PWA with real-time collaboration
  • Google Drive app — open and save diagrams in Google Drive
  • VS Code extension
  • Obsidian plugin
  • @dineug/erd-editor — the editor as a custom element for your own app
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Find and replace across table and column names, comments and memos, with match case, whole word and regular expressions. Open it with the new button beside Search on the toolbar, from the quick search or from the context menu. It starts on names alone, and one undo takes back a Replace All.
  • Quick search lists the editor's commands, and jumps to a table after #, a column after @, and a comment or memo after :. Korean matches while you are still typing a syllable, and by initial consonants alone: ㅅㅇㅈ finds 사용자.
  • Set ON DELETE and ON UPDATE on a relationship from the On Delete and On Update menus of its line. SQL export writes them, SQL, DBML and AML import keep them, and the TypeORM, Sequelize, Drizzle, SQLAlchemy, DBML and AML code carries them. The menu notes an action the selected database's DDL leaves out, such as SET DEFAULT on MySQL.
  • A relationship line shows those actions at its child end, D: for ON DELETE and U: for ON UPDATE (C, R, SN, SD or NA), and hovering it spells them out. View Option → Referential Actions hides the labels.
  • View Option → Alternate Key marks the columns of each unique index on the diagram as AK1.1, AK1.2 and so on, as ERwin and IDEF1X write them.
  • The Indexes tab of Table Properties lists the primary key and the unique columns above the indexes. Table Properties has a title and a close button, and says when the document is read only.
  • A coding agent can set ON DELETE and ON UPDATE and the two new view options too.

Changed

  • A new diagram saves neither the scroll position nor the zoom level (Save Scroll Information and Save Zoom Information start off), so looking around never changes the file. An existing file keeps the settings it was saved with.
  • Drawing a relationship names each new foreign key column after the parent table: key id of table user gives user_id, not one more id. A key named in several words (member_id, userId) keeps its name, and a name the table already holds is numbered _2, _3.
  • SQL import reads a UNIQUE over several columns as one unique index under its name, instead of a unique flag on each column.

Fixed

  • With Save Scroll Information and Save Zoom Information off, scrolling or zooming no longer rewrites the file, even one another release or machine wrote, and neither does a save a coding agent asks for while nothing changed.
  • SQL import keeps user-defined and extension types (an enum made with CREATE TYPE, a domain, hstore, citext, "MyType", public.mood), the brackets of integer[] and the quoted values of ENUM('a','b'), which came in empty or broken. A doubled quote such as 'it''s' reads as one quote, a column's inline REFERENCES makes a relationship, and every unique key an ALTER TABLE or a dump's CREATE UNIQUE INDEX adds is kept.
  • Exported DDL escapes a quote inside a comment, and the Schema SQL tab of Table Properties writes the table's unique columns.

idea-plugin.name: db-external-command-auth
idea-plugin.description:
Use an external command to acquire database connection credentials.

Executes an external command and extracts database and username from its output. The command is executed in the project’s root directory, if that can be resolved.

The plugin will first attempt to extract the information from output from a Vault-like JSON with the following format:

{
  "data": {
    "username": "username",
    "password": "password"
  }
}

Any extra fields are ignored.

If JSON parsing fails, the output is expected to be password and username separated by a newline:

password
username

The prefix username: is removed from the username, so the following also works:

password
Username: username

AutoDDL 插件 for IntelliJ IDEA

AutoDDL 插件 为IntelliJ IDEA扩展一些元数据操作 。 用户可选择调用AI自动生成Table，或手动编写表单生成 DDL。

生成菜单

  • GenDDL 根据当前类生成ddl语句
  • GenJimmerDTO 根据当前类生成生成jimmer各种DTO样板代码
  • GenExcelDTO 根据当前类生成生成fastexcel框架的实体

功能特性

  • 表创建：基于结构化表单元数据生成 CREATE TABLE SQL 语句。
  • AI支持：调用AI（LLM）自动生成表单元数据。
  • Java 类型映射：自动将 Java 类型映射为数据库字段类型。

使用说明

  1. 插件建表功能入口：在 Tools -> AutoDDL 中找到插件。
  2. 初始配置：在 IDEA 设置 中配置AI API Key
  3. 调用AI生成表单：
    • 使用AI生成表单元数据，支持手动编辑DDL表单。生成的sql在项目根目录下,可以二次编辑

常用意图(alt+回车)

   /**

 */

你可以尝试可以在项目中定义@Shit注解,插件会扫描被注解标记的代码,插件可以批量删除并跳转这些代码

idea-plugin.name: DataBaseManager
idea-plugin.description:
Database development, scripting and navigation tool
This software solution enhances the capabilities of the IntelliJ IDEA development environment and its associated products by providing comprehensive features for database development and maintenance. It includes a robust SQL and PL/SQL editor that adheres to the IDE standards, along with advanced functionality for managing database connections, executing scripts, browsing database objects, editing data and code, supporting database compiler operations, executing and debugging methods, and facilitating the creation of database objects. Additionally, it offers diverse navigation capabilities that seamlessly integrate across all its components, providing a powerful toolset for efficient and effective database development and management.
Supported Databases:
  • Oracle
  • MySQL
  • SQLite
  • PostgreSQL
  • Any JDBC compliant database (EXPERIMENTAL)

Fork code from Database Navigator
This tool is free for personal and commercial use.
Donations are very welcome though.
用于管理数据库
通过为数据库开发和维护提供全面的功能，增强了IntelliJ IDEA开发环境及其相关产品的能力。它包括一个符合IDE标准的强大的SQL和PL/SQL编辑器， 以及用于管理数据库连接、执行脚本、浏览数据库对象、编辑数据和代码、支持数据库编译器操作、执行和调试方法以及促进数据库对象创建的高级功能。 此外，它还提供了多种导航功能，可无缝集成其所有组件，为高效和有效的数据库开发和管理提供了强大的工具集。
支持数据库:
  • Oracle
  • MySQL
  • SQLite
  • PostgreSQL
  • 任何兼容jdbc的数据库 (实验性质)
主要功能如下:
  • 支持 MyBatis mapper.xml 文件的 SQL 识别
  • 支持提取控制台 MyBatis 打印的 SQL
  • 集成 MyBatis Generator
  • MyBatis Generator 支持动态 plugin 功能
  • 支持悬浮展示表元数据信息
  • 支持悬浮展示列元数据信息
  • 支持输入表名时智能提示
  • 支持输入列名时智能提示
  • SQL 结构的跳转等

idea-plugin.name: Mybatis Log Ultra
idea-plugin.description:
A description that is at least 40 characters long

摆脱繁杂日志，精准定位关键 SQL

MyBatis Log Ultra 是一款好用的 IDEA 插件（MyBatis Log Plugin），通过强大的工具改变您的调试工作流，旨在为您节省时间

核心特性

智能 SQL 过滤 - 即时过滤噪音。通过表名、方法名或任何 SQL 片段搜索，秒级定位您所需内容。

一键导航 - 不再猜测 SQL 来自何处。点击任何日志条目即可直接跳转到编辑器中的确切代码行。

请求隔离 - 按 HTTP 请求分组 SQL 执行。无干扰地分析单个 API 调用的数据库影响。

可执行 SQL 还原 - 自动将参数组装到预处理语句中，为您提供可直接在数据库客户端运行的 SQL 查询。

方法级分组 - 按 Mapper 方法名组织日志。一眼即可看出特定查询的执行次数。

零配置 - 安装即用。无需复杂的设置或配置文件。与您现有的 MyBatis 设置开箱即用。

idea-plugin.name: Log SQL Converter
idea-plugin.description:
Log SQL Converter is a useful plugin for developers. It helps to quickly convert SQL templates and parameters in logs into executable SQL statements, with enhanced compatibility and usability.

Core functions:

  • Multi-framework log adaptation: Automatically identify and parse SQL templates/parameters in JPA (Hibernate) and MyBatis logs (supports common formats like "Preparing:/Parameters:" and "Hibernate:/binding parameter").
  • Intelligently replace "?" placeholders to generate complete, directly runnable SQL statements.
  • Enhanced UI experience: Added scrollbars to input/output areas in the tool window, supporting smooth scrolling for long log content or SQL results.
  • One-click copy of conversion results to the clipboard, facilitating direct execution in database clients (e.g., Navicat, DBeaver).
  • Dual operation entrances: Independent tool window in the right toolbar (for pasting logs) + right-click menu in the editor (for selected log text), flexible for different usage scenarios.

Applicable scenarios: During debugging, quickly convert parameterized SQL in JPA/MyBatis logs into executable statements without manual parameter concatenation, greatly improving development efficiency for database-related tasks.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2.0.0

  • Added JPA (Hibernate) log parsing: Supports extraction of SQL templates and parameters from logs with "Hibernate:" and "binding parameter" keywords.
  • Optimized MyBatis log compatibility: Enhanced parsing for MyBatis logs in "Preparing:/Parameters:" format (supports multi-line parameters and type annotation filtering).
  • Added scrollbars to tool window input/output areas: Enables smooth scrolling for long log content or large SQL results, improving usability.
  • Fixed minor issues with parameter extraction for special character values (e.g., single quotes, null values).

SchemaLens - Comprehensive Database Schema Inspector

SchemaLens is a powerful DataGrip plugin that provides a comprehensive, tabbed interface for viewing database table structures. Inspect tables, indexes, foreign keys, triggers, constraints, and more—all in one convenient view.

✨ Key Features

  • 📊 Structure Tab - View detailed column information (name, type, nullability, defaults, primary keys, auto-increment, comments)
  • 🔑 Index Tab - Comprehensive index information (name, type, columns, uniqueness, comments)
  • 🔗 Foreign Key Tab - Complete foreign key relationships (columns, referenced tables, update/delete rules)
  • ⚡ Trigger Tab - View all table triggers (name, events, timing, statements, comments)
  • ✅ Check Tab - Inspect check constraints (name, condition, comments)
  • 💬 Comment Tab - View table-level comments with multi-line support
  • 📝 SQL Preview Tab - View complete CREATE TABLE statements with dark mode support

🎯 Additional Features

  • Long Text Support - Multi-line tooltips and double-click popup for viewing full content
  • Smart Rendering - Automatic text wrapping and HTML escaping
  • Dark Mode - Automatic theme adaptation
  • Performance Optimized - Efficient data extraction and background loading
  • User-Friendly - Clean, intuitive interface with copy-to-clipboard functionality

🚀 Usage

Right-click on any table in the Database tool window and select "Table Structure" to open the comprehensive schema viewer.

📋 Requirements

DataGrip 2024.3 or later. Works with all databases supported by DataGrip (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, SQLite, and more).

KongQuery is the ultimate SQL companion for Spring Data JPA developers. This intelligent IntelliJ plugin automatically formats your SQL queries and even generates Java projection interfaces — making your database code cleaner, more readable, and more maintainable.

It seamlessly detects inline SQL strings within your @Query and @NativeQuery annotations, transforming them from messy one-liners into beautifully formatted queries with proper indentation, line breaks, and keyword alignment.

Key Features
• Auto-format SQL inside @Query, @NativeQuery, and repository methods
• Generate Projection Interfaces from SQL SELECT aliases (Alt+Shift+P on Windows/Linux, ⌥+⇧+P on macOS)
• Multi-dialect Support - MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, and more
• Smart Parameter Preservation - keeps your placeholders and parameters intact
• Code Style Integration - respects your existing formatting preferences
• Multiple Access Points - auto-format on save, context menu, or keyboard shortcuts

Whether you're writing complex joins or simple selects, KongQuery ensures your SQL looks as professional as your Java code. Boost your productivity and code quality — because your queries deserve the same care as the rest of your application.

Perfect for Spring Data JPA projects! Works instantly with no configuration required.

idea-plugin.name: Neo4j Toolkit
idea-plugin.description:
Neo4j Toolkit — Neo4j / Bolt Database Manager for JetBrains IDEs

Neo4j Toolkit brings Neo4j graph database tooling directly into your JetBrains IDE. Connect to any Neo4j instance via the Bolt protocol, write and execute Cypher queries with full language support, and explore results as an interactive graph canvas or a data table — without leaving your editor.

What you can do today

  • Data source management — add, edit and delete Bolt connections with per-source colour coding; supports all URL schemes (bolt://, bolt+s://, neo4j://, neo4j+s://, etc.)
  • Secure credentials — passwords are stored in the OS keychain via the IDE's built-in PasswordSafe; never written to disk in plain text
  • Test Connection — verify connectivity (including SSL and named databases) before saving
  • Persistent data sources — your connections survive IDE restarts
  • Cypher editor — dedicated .cypher / .cql file type with syntax highlighting (keywords, functions, operators, strings, comments), auto-completion, live error annotations, and // / /* */ commenting shortcuts
  • Run queries — execute with Ctrl+F5 (Windows/Linux) or Cmd+F5 (macOS) against the selected data source and target database
  • Graph visualisation — interactive force-directed canvas; scroll to pan, Ctrl+scroll to zoom, drag to reposition, double-click a node to inspect all its properties; colour-coded legend by node label
  • Table view — raw rows and columns for scalar and list results
  • Query log — terminal-style history of every query run in the session
  • Parameters panel — set named $param values as JSON before running

Planned for upcoming releases

  • Schema browser — explore labels, relationship types, property keys and indexes live from the connected database
  • Query history and saved/favourite queries
  • Export results as CSV or JSON
  • Multi-statement execution and transaction control
  • Expanded IDE compatibility (WebStorm, PyCharm, Rider, …)

Bugs and feature requests

Please open an issue or start a discussion on GitHub. Include your IDE version, plugin version, and steps to reproduce for bug reports.

Requires IntelliJ IDEA 2024.3 or later and a running Neo4j 5.x instance.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.6.0
  • The plugin is now named Neo4j Toolkit (previously "GraphDB for Neo4j"). No functional changes — this is a branding update only, and the plugin ID (com.graphdbplugin) is unchanged, so existing installs update in place.
  • Fixed a deprecated-API usage flagged by the IntelliJ Plugin Verifier: the Cypher auto-popup completion handler now overrides the current CompletionConfidence.shouldSkipAutopopup(Editor, PsiElement, PsiFile, int) overload instead of the deprecated 3-argument one.
1.5.1
  • Extended IDE compatibility to cover IntelliJ IDEA and GoLand 2026.2 (build 262). Verified with the IntelliJ Plugin Verifier against both IDEs: no breaking API changes, only pre-existing deprecated-API usages.
1.5.0
  • Double-clicking a data source that already has an editor tab open now focuses the existing tab instead of opening a duplicate one.
  • The Cypher editor now supports multiple semicolon-separated statements in one tab. Each detected statement gets its own gutter run icon so it can be executed individually.
  • Run Query (toolbar button / Ctrl+F5 / Meta+F5) is now caret-aware: with no selection it runs the statement under the caret; with a text selection it runs exactly the selected text as a single query.
1.4.5
  • Multiline queries no longer push the result pane off-screen. The query summary bar now displays queries on a single line with newlines collapsed into spaces and text truncated at 120 characters.
  • Graph result panel now auto-fits all nodes into view on load, so the full graph is visible without manual zooming.
  • Mouse scroll in the graph pane now works immediately on hover without requiring a click first.
  • Clicking a data-source item no longer accidentally opens the edit-connection dialog. Edit is only triggered via the toolbar Edit button.
  • Non-ready data-source items (connecting or failed) are greyed out and show an italic status hint explaining why they are unavailable.
1.4.4
  • Fixed data-source list losing all field values (name, URL, credentials) after a plugin update. BoltDataSource properties were declared val (immutable), so IntelliJ's XML deserialiser could construct each item but could not set any fields — every entry appeared with an empty name and default URL. Properties are now var so the deserialiser can populate them correctly.
  • Active data-source selection is now persisted per project to graphdb-project.xml and survives IDE restarts and plugin updates.
1.4.3
  • Removed use of internal API ApplicationInitializedListener. CypherLanguage is now a plain class whose singleton instance is initialised eagerly in a companion-object static initialiser, guaranteeing language registration on the main thread at class-load time without relying on any internal platform hooks. GoLand 2026.1 compatibility is preserved.
1.4.2
  • Fixed CI/CD publish workflow failing on Ubuntu runner due to macOS-specific Homebrew JDK path in gradle.properties.
1.4.1
  • Updated Marketplace listing: vendor details, full plugin description covering all current features, issue/feature-request link, and plugin icon.
  • Added CI/CD workflow to publish automatically to JetBrains Marketplace on release.
1.4.0
  • Fixed URL validation to accept TLS-scheme URLs (bolt+s://, bolt+ssc://, neo4j+s://, neo4j+ssc://). Previously these were rejected by the "Add / Edit Data Source" dialog, making it impossible to save SSL-enabled data sources.
  • Fixed connection-test in the tool window: the configured database is now passed to the session, so the test accurately reflects connectivity to the target database rather than always pinging the server's default database.
1.3.0
  • Fixed NoClassDefFoundError: CypherLanguage crash when opening a Cypher editor in GoLand 2026.1 (build 261). The IntelliJ Platform 261 tightened language-registration timing; CypherLanguage is now eagerly registered at application startup via ApplicationInitializedListener.
  • All token-type, composite-element-type and parser-companion fields that reference CypherLanguage are now lazily initialised, eliminating the premature class-load race that caused the crash.
  • Fixed data-source persistence: multiple data sources now survive IDE restarts (DataSourceManagerState.dataSources changed to var; BoltDataSource.name given a default value to support XML deserialisation).
1.2.0
  • Extended IDE compatibility to cover GoLand 2026.1 (build 261).
1.1.0
  • Extended IDE compatibility to cover GoLand 2025.1 – 2025.3 (builds 251–253).
1.0.0
  • Initial Phase 1 release: data-source management, Bolt connectivity, OS keychain password storage.

idea-plugin.name: Drift Locator
idea-plugin.description:
Provides database schema comparison across different instances. It helps developers identify differences between diferent environments, ensuring smooth deployments and early detection of schema drift.

Note: Drift Locator currently supports PostgreSQL 12+, MySQL 8.0+, and SQLite 3.x. Metadata coverage is database-specific and may differ by object type.

Features

  • Schema Comparison — Compare database schemas between two instances
  • Comprehensive Object Support:
    • PostgreSQL: tables, views, materialized views, functions, procedures, sequences, triggers, domains, enums, policies, comments, grants, and more
    • MySQL: tables, views, routines, triggers, events, partitions, grants, users, and more
    • SQLite: tables, columns, indexes, foreign keys, views, triggers, generated columns, and DDL-only table options such as STRICT and WITHOUT ROWID
  • Visual Diff Viewer — Built-in IntelliJ IDEA diff viewer for side-by-side schema comparison
  • Export Reports — Automatic export of schema snapshots to text files in your project
  • Multiple Connections — Manage and compare multiple database connections within your project

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA: 2024.1 or later (build 241+)
  • PostgreSQL: 12 or later
  • MySQL: 8.0 or later
  • SQLite: 3.x database files

Getting Started

Installation

From JetBrains Marketplace

  1. Open IntelliJ IDEA
  2. Go to Settings/Preferences → Plugins → Marketplace
  3. Search for "Drift Locator"
  4. Click Install
  5. Restart the IDE

Manual Installation

  1. Download the latest plugin distribution .zip file from Releases
  2. Open IntelliJ IDEA
  3. Go to Settings/Preferences → Plugins → ⚙️ → Install from Disk...
  4. Select the downloaded .zip file
  5. Restart the IDE

Usage

  1. Open the Drift Locator tool window from View → Tool Windows → Drift Locator
  2. Add database connections using the Add Connection button
  3. Select two connections and click Compare to analyze schema differences
  4. Review results in the built-in Diff Viewer and exported snapshot files
  5. To perform a repeatable diff, select stored files (see File locations) and press Ctrl+D

Connection settings include standard database credentials for PostgreSQL/MySQL and a database file picker for SQLite. Default values are automatically populated from your last connection to speed up configuration.

Managing Connections

  • Edit — Select a connection and click "Edit Connection" to change database-specific settings
  • Delete — Select a connection and click "Delete" to remove it
  • All changes are automatically saved to your project

File Locations

Schema snapshots are exported to .driftLocator/YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM/ directory within your project.

idea-plugin.name: Flowix DB Tool
idea-plugin.description:
Flowix DB Tool puts PostgreSQL traffic under control - without rewriting your application - and this plugin keeps the whole loop inside your IDE.

Flowix DB Tool is a TCP proxy that understands the PostgreSQL wire protocol. It can record traces, serve declarative mocks (YAML + datasets), and run autonomous scenarios when a live database is unavailable. The JetBrains plugin makes that workflow practical day-to-day: install from Marketplace, manage versions/updates, and drive the proxy with project-aware settings instead of juggling terminals and ad-hoc scripts. Point your JDBC client at the local proxy port - your code stays the same - while the IDE helps you start/stop, tune ports and paths, and keep mocks/traces aligned with the repository you're already working in.

Features:

  • One-click lifecycle from the IDE - install/update via JetBrains Marketplace and run the proxy without leaving the editor.
  • Project-native configuration - mock directory, trace output, ports, and modes wired to your module/repo layout.
  • PostgreSQL wire-protocol aware - transparent proxy; JDBC and other PG clients behave normally.
  • Declarative mocks - version rules + data alongside tests.
  • Trace capture - record traffic to debug and refine mocks (with filtering where supported).
  • Autonomous mode - exercise flows without a live PostgreSQL instance.
  • Operational ergonomics - clear run actions / run configurations for repeatable local and team workflows.
  • Enterprise-friendly - predictable CI behavior, reproducible datasets, and less dependency on shared “magic” databases.

    • Use cases:

  • Developer velocity - spin up Flowix DB Tool from the IDE while coding; iterate on mocks without context switching.
  • Stable integration tests - deterministic responses instead of a shared database changing underneath you.
  • Edge cases on demand - rare rows, nulls, wide results, and failure-like outcomes without fragile DB state.
  • Faster CI - fewer heavyweight DB dependencies; autonomous runs where appropriate.
  • Team consistency - the same proxy settings and paths, discoverable from the project and easy to document.
  • Incident debugging - traces to compare client requests vs server responses when behavior is unclear.

    • Submit issue

    Getting Started Guide

idea-plugin.name: dbt-helper
idea-plugin.description:
dbt Helper — Lineage, Code Intelligence & Runner for dbt

A powerful plugin that brings lineage visualization, code intelligence, and a command runner for dbt projects directly into your JetBrains IDE.

Lineage Graph

  • Interactive DAG visualization powered by Cytoscape.js
  • Click nodes to navigate to source files
  • Expand boundary nodes to explore deeper dependencies
  • Configurable depth, layout direction, and edge style
  • Shows models, sources, seeds, snapshots, exposures, and tests
  • Auto-updates when manifest changes; adapts to light/dark themes

Code Intelligence

  • Autocompletion — ref(), source(), macro() suggestions with descriptions
  • Go to Definition — Ctrl/Cmd+Click on ref() / source() to jump to the file
  • Documentation on Hover — columns, materialization, tags, descriptions
  • Annotations — unresolved ref() / source() highlighted as warnings
  • Works in .sql, .jinja, and .jinja2 files

Runner

  • Run / Test / Compile the current model with one click
  • Full Refresh checkbox for incremental models
  • Preview — execute dbt show on any model or selected SQL
  • Docs Generate — rebuild documentation
  • Target selector, stop button, streaming output log
  • Native OS notifications when commands finish

Copy & Paste

  • Copy for Target DB (Cmd+Shift+C) — ref()/source() replaced by database.schema.table
  • Paste as dbt Refs (Cmd+Shift+V) — table names replaced by ref()/source() calls

Docs Viewer

Browse model documentation in a built-in panel — columns, descriptions, tags, and dependencies.

This plugin is not affiliated with or endorsed by dbt Labs.

idea-plugin.name: Oracle Dictionary Inspector
idea-plugin.description:
Oracle dictionary inspector for DataGrip / IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate

Toad-style describe dialogs for Oracle objects, plus a dedicated tool window for sessions, locks, and execution plans — all inside IntelliJ.

How to open

  • Database panel → right-click a table / view / procedure / function / package / sequence / synonym → Oracle Dictionary Info
  • SQL editor → select an identifier (or place the caret on it) → right-click → Oracle Dictionary Info
  • Shortcut anywhere: Alt+Shift+O (macOS: ⌥+Shift+O)

What it does

  • Tables / Views — Columns, Keys, FK, Indexes, Checks, Triggers, plus a Data preview with 500-row paging + WHERE/ORDER BY filters, DDL and SELECT
  • Procedures / Functions / Packages — IntelliJ-editor source with line numbers, SQL syntax, and compile-error line markers; double-click an Errors row to jump to the line
  • Oracle Sessions tool window — V$SESSION browser, Locks, Long Ops, with per-session Current SQL / Wait History / Session Stats / Explain Plan sub-tabs; right-click → Kill Session
  • Localised: English (default) + Korean (한국어)
  • 100% read-only — except the explicitly confirmed Kill Session, every command is a SELECT

Full manual, screenshots, and setup guide on the GitHub repository.

DataGrip / IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate용 Oracle 딕셔너리 조회 플러그인

Toad 스타일의 객체 Describe 다이얼로그 + 세션·락·실행 계획 전용 Tool Window를 IntelliJ 안에서 그대로 제공합니다.

여는 방법

  • Database 패널에서 테이블/뷰/프로시저/펑션/패키지/시퀀스/시노님 우클릭 → Oracle Dictionary Info
  • SQL 에디터에서 식별자 선택(또는 캐럿 위치) → 우클릭 → Oracle Dictionary Info
  • 어디서나 단축키: Alt+Shift+O (macOS: ⌥+Shift+O)

주요 기능

  • 테이블·뷰 — Columns / Keys / FK / Indexes / Checks / Triggers + 500행 페이징 데이터 미리보기 + WHERE/ORDER BY 필터 + DDL / SELECT
  • 프로시저·펑션·패키지 — IntelliJ Editor 본문 (라인 번호, 신택스, 컴파일 오류 라인 강조). Errors 행 더블클릭 → Source 점프
  • Oracle Sessions Tool Window — V$SESSION 브라우저, Locks, Long Ops + 세션별 Current SQL / Wait History / Stats / Explain Plan sub-tab. 우클릭 → Kill Session
  • 다국어 — 영문(기본) + 한국어 (IDE 로케일 자동)
  • 100% 읽기 전용 — 명시 확인을 거치는 Kill Session 외 모든 명령은 SELECT

전체 사용 매뉴얼, 스크린샷, 설치 가이드는 GitHub 저장소에서 확인하세요.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.7 — Metadata cache extended to tables, views, sequences & synonyms

  • The in-memory metadata cache and the "● Changed in DB — refresh" badge (introduced in 1.0.6 for procedures/packages) now also cover table, view, sequence, and synonym dialogs.
  • Same rules as before: caches only what was fetched via JDBC fallback, never replaces IntelliJ's own model, never holds table data or live V$ data, LRU-capped at 200, and never auto-refetches — it just lets you know when a manual refresh is worthwhile.

1.0.6 — Metadata cache for procedures & packages

  • Procedure / Function / Package dialogs now cache the JDBC-fetched source in memory, so reopening the same object no longer re-queries the database. The cache never replaces IntelliJ's own model — it only remembers what IntelliJ couldn't fully introspect, and never holds table data or live V$ data.
  • Change awareness: on a cache hit, a lightweight ALL_OBJECTS.LAST_DDL_TIME check runs in the background. If the object changed in the database, the refresh icon and a "● Changed in DB — refresh" notice appear — it never auto-refetches, you stay in control.
  • Cache is per data source + schema + object, capped at 200 entries (LRU), and cleared when the project closes.

1.0.5 — Live theme switching

  • All plugin tables (Sessions, Locks, Long Ops, Wait History, Stats, Explain Plan, table/view dialog tabs, package routines, sequence/synonym property tables, etc.) now follow the IDE theme immediately when you toggle Light/Dark, without having to close and reopen the dialog.
  • Internal fix: cell renderers no longer cache UIManager.getColor("Table.background") at instantiation time; the colour is read on every paint, the way IntelliJ's own components do.

1.0.4 — Preserve session selection across Auto 5s refresh

  • The Sessions tool window now remembers which session row you had selected and the column sort order when the 5-second auto-refresh fires. Previously the selection (and therefore the Current SQL / Wait History / Stats / Explain Plan sub-tabs) flickered away every cycle.
  • If the previously selected session is still alive after the refresh, the row is re-selected and scrolled into view; if it has logged out or been killed, the sub-tabs clear gracefully.

1.0.3 — Slimmer in-IDE description

  • Trimmed the in-IDE Plugins-screen description to a concise summary (How to open + key features + GitHub link). The Marketplace listing page itself can host the full Getting Started content via the dashboard.
  • "How to open" section now spells out the right-click entry points on the Database panel and the SQL editor in addition to the Alt+Shift+O shortcut.
  • No runtime or behaviour changes from 1.0.2.

1.0.2 — Marketplace listing polish

  • Expanded plugin description with the full feature inventory in both English and Korean, so the in-IDE Plugins screen now matches the Marketplace page.
  • Synced README.md project structure and roadmap with the current codebase (PackageInfo, SimpleObjectInfo, Sessions UI, etc.).
  • No runtime or behaviour changes from 1.0.1.

1.0.1 — Marketplace moderation fixes

  • Replaced internal DbDataSource.getDelegate() with the public DbImplUtil.getMaybeLocalDataSource() across all JDBC repositories and the editor describe action.
  • Rewrote the Sessions tool window factory in Java so Kotlin no longer emits synthetic overrides of internal ToolWindowFactory default methods.

1.0.0 — initial release

Object dialogs

  • Tables / Views — Columns / Keys / FK / Indexes / Checks / Triggers / Data preview (500-row paging + WHERE/ORDER BY) / DDL / SELECT / Comments SQL.
  • Views use ALL_VIEWS.TEXT for the DDL tab (CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW).
  • Standalone Procedures / Functions — Source (IntelliJ editor, syntax + line-number markers for compile errors) / Execute template / Errors (double-click jumps to source line) / Arguments.
  • Packages — Spec / Body / Routines / Errors with per-source-type error highlighting and double-click jump.
  • Sequences / Synonyms — Property/Value dialogs.

Oracle Sessions tool window

  • Sessions / Locks / Long Ops tabs with auto-refresh (5s).
  • Sessions tab has client-side USER / STATUS / PROGRAM / MODULE filter.
  • Bottom sub-tabs: Current SQL, Wait History (V$SESSION_WAIT_HISTORY), Session Stats (curated V$SESSTAT), Explain Plan (V$SQL_PLAN with expensive-operation highlighting).
  • Right-click → Kill Session / Kill Holder with confirmation dialog.

Editor describe action

  • Single Alt+Shift+O shortcut handles every object type, supports SCHEMA.NAME, prefers the current dialog's OWNER.

Cross-cutting

  • Inline search on every table (just start typing).
  • Column widths persist via PropertiesComponent.
  • Localised: English (default) + Korean.

idea-plugin.name: FastORM Builder

idea-plugin.name: SSH Tunnel Exporter
idea-plugin.description:
Generates the standalone ssh -L port-forwarding command for any data source that is configured with an SSH tunnel — so you can open the exact same bridge outside the IDE (for psql, mysql, a dump tool, or anything else).

  • Right-click a data source in the Database tool window → Copy SSH Tunnel Command, or use Tools → Copy SSH Tunnel Command… to pick one.
  • Reads the data source's SSH configuration (host, port, user, key) and the database host/port, then builds the command for you.
  • Editable local port and SSH option toggles — -N, -f, -C, -v, ConnectTimeout, IdentitiesOnly, ExitOnForwardFailure and keep-alive (ServerAliveInterval/ServerAliveCountMax) — reflected live in the command; one click to copy.
  • Or copy the equivalent ~/.ssh/config Host stanza, with an editable host alias (defaults to the SSH configuration name, else the data source name).
  • Shows a small “how it works” flow picture and, for known DBMS, the matching client command to connect through the tunnel (e.g. psql -h localhost -p 5432).
  • Never emits passwords — key-pair auth adds -i <key>; password/agent auth is left for ssh to resolve.

Works in DataGrip (and other JetBrains IDEs with the Database Tools & SQL plugin).

Bug Fixes

idea-plugin.name: SQLAlchemy Tools

idea-plugin.name: Dataset Downloader
idea-plugin.description:
Dataset Downloader - Streamlined Database Table Exports

A lightweight, high-performance database table exporter for DataGrip and IntelliJ Database Tools. Configure download profiles for your schemas and tables to download them as CSV or Excel (XLSX) files in a single click.

Key Features:

  • One-Click Exports: Save target schemas, tables, and paths as profiles to run downloads instantly.
  • High-Performance Excel Engine: Powered by the ultra-lightweight fastexcel library, reducing memory usage and packaging overhead.
  • OOM Prevention: Handles millions of rows using streaming query cursors and transactional batch fetches.
  • Inline Profile Editor: Manage profiles directly in the grid tool window without interrupting popups.
  • Context-Aware Execution: Run, edit, or delete profiles directly via a convenient right-click context menu.
  • Quick Navigation: Click the "Open Folder" button in the download-complete notification balloon to locate your files instantly.

Supported Formats:

  • CSV: Standard CSV format with UTF-8 BOM, ensuring Korean and other non-ASCII characters display correctly in MS Excel.
  • XLSX: Pure Excel spreadsheets built via a zero-overhead stream writer.

How to Use:

  1. Open the Data Downloader panel on the right sidebar.
  2. Click Add Profile to register your Data Source, Schema, Table, and output directory.
  3. Right-click any profile in the table to execute the download process.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changed

  • Refactored export engine to use a multithreaded Producer-Consumer architecture, maximizing non-blocking IO performance.
  • Eliminated CPU and GC overhead by removing String Pool and implementing Zero-Allocation type mapping via ResultSetMetaData.

idea-plugin.name: Docker Compose Postgres Datasources
idea-plugin.description:
Turns the PostgreSQL services in your docker-compose files into ready-to-use database connections.

On project open — and on demand via Tools | Sync Docker Compose Datasources — the plugin scans docker-compose*.yml / compose*.yml for postgres / postgis services and registers each as a PostgreSQL data source pointing at the published host port, with the user, database and password filled in so you can connect in one click.

  • Reads POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_DB, POSTGRES_PASSWORD and the host port published for container port 5432 (short and long ports syntax).
  • Reconciles on every sync: adds new services, updates changed ones, and removes services that were deleted from compose.
  • Only ever touches data sources it created — your own connections are never modified.
  • Skips build output, node_modules, cdk.out and other IDE-excluded or VCS-ignored locations.

Requires IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate (uses the bundled Database Tools).
idea-plugin.change-notes: • Update to current IntelliJ Platform APIs (no deprecated usages; verified compatible with 2024.3 through 2026.2).

idea-plugin.name: StarRocks Support
idea-plugin.description:
StarRocks Support provides a dedicated StarRocks SQL dialect and database integration for DataGrip and other JetBrains IDEs with Database Tools.

Features

  • StarRocks SQL parsing and syntax highlighting.
  • Code completion for StarRocks keywords, types, functions, snippets, and table properties.
  • Platform-based SQL formatting for the StarRocks dialect.
  • Dedicated StarRocks DBMS and data source integration.
  • JDBC metadata, StarRocks type system, object resolution, and native SHOW CREATE support.
  • Syntax coverage aligned with the StarRocks 4.1 documentation baseline.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Data source integration

The default data source driver is now StarRocks Connector/J, replacing MySQL Connector/J.

  • Improved external catalog browsing and database switching.
  • Improved data source organization and synchronization of tables, columns, and views.

Upgrade existing data sources

Existing data sources need a driver update. Install the update and restart the IDE, then complete these steps:

  1. Update the driver files. In Data Sources and Drivers > Drivers, select StarRocks and restore its default configuration.
    Download the StarRocks driver and remove the old MySQL driver files.
  2. Check the driver class: com.starrocks.cj.jdbc.Driver.
  3. Update the URL prefix: jdbc:mysql:// to jdbc:starrocks://.
  4. Reconnect and fully refresh the data source.

Alternative: You can recreate the data source, but make sure it uses the updated StarRocks driver.

SQL resolution and formatting

  • Fixed unresolved column and column alias references when their letter case differs from the definition, including backtick-quoted references, connected data sources, subqueries, and CTEs.
  • Improved materialized view definitions and SQL formatting.

Syntax support

  • Fixed false syntax errors for SET CATALOG, SHOW [FULL] PROCESSLIST, and KILL QUERY/CONNECTION.
  • Added syntax support for SHOW [FULL] TABLES, SHOW [FULL] COLUMNS/FIELDS, and SHOW [GLOBAL/SESSION/LOCAL] VARIABLES, including LIKE and WHERE filters.

Function signatures

  • Fixed false argument warnings for zero-argument functions such as DATABASE(), CATALOG(), and session information functions, while preserving warnings for invalid argument counts.
  • Added explicit overloads for RAND, RANDOM, and UNIX_TIMESTAMP, and corrected the LOCALTIME return type to DATETIME.

idea-plugin.name: Database Plus
idea-plugin.description:
Database Plus is a focused database workflow for JetBrains IDEs — query SQL and browse Redis / MongoDB without leaving the editor, and without needing a separate full database IDE for everyday work.

Built for developers who:

  • Jump between MySQL / PostgreSQL and Redis or Mongo while coding
  • Want a data source from application.yml in one click
  • Prefer a lighter daily tool than switching to a heavyweight DB client

Why try it

  • One window — relational + Redis + MongoDB side by side with your code
  • Project-native — gutter actions on Spring / config JDBC & Redis lines
  • Safe defaults — dangerous SQL confirmation and production read-only options
  • 30-day full trial — evaluate real work, then subscribe on Marketplace

Relational & NoSQL

  • JDBC: MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite, SQL Server, Oracle, ClickHouse, Generic JDBC
  • NoSQL: Redis key browser and MongoDB document panels
  • Drivers on demand — Tools → Drivers downloads to ~/.database-plus/drivers/

Explorer & SQL workflow

  • Lazy tree — schemas, tables, views, procedures, functions, columns, indexes, DDL
  • SQL console — highlighting, completion, gutter execute, batch scripts
  • Result grid — export CSV / JSON / SQL / Markdown / XLSX; editable pending changes
  • CSV import with INSERT SQL review
  • SSH tunnel, SSL, query history, ER diagram, schema diff

Compatibility & licensing

  • IntelliJ IDEA and compatible JetBrains IDEs — minimum build 243 (2024.3+)
  • Paid via JetBrains Marketplace — activate in Settings → Plugins → Database Plus

Support: 1143543316@qq.com · Vendor page
