idea-plugin.name: SQL Dialect for Apache Doris
idea-plugin.description:
First-class Apache Doris support for DataGrip and IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate — a dedicated SQL dialect, a multi-catalog database tree, table-function completion, and a Stop button that actually cancels your Doris query. Compatible with the 2026.1 through 2026.3 IDE lines.

  • Multi-catalog database tree. Doris external catalogs (Hive, Iceberg, JDBC, ...) appear as a real catalog → database → table hierarchy, with three-part catalog.db.table completion and resolution and a stepped console catalog/database switcher
  • Table-valued-function completion. tasks(), jobs(), mv_infos(), partitions(), backends() and more complete their property keys and enum values, and their output columns resolve — including schema-by-argument (tasks("type"="mv"))
  • Reliable query cancel. The Stop button kills the running Doris query even behind a load balancer, where the driver's own cancel silently misses
  • Doris Pipes (optional). Write GoogleSQL-style pipe syntax (FROM t |> WHERE ... |> AGGREGATE ...) directly in Doris consoles — it transpiles to standard Doris SQL on run, with per-stage completion, run-to-stage, generated-SQL preview, and errors mapped back to the pipe line you wrote. Enable it per project under Settings → Tools → Apache Doris PIPE. Disabled by default; no SQL Transpiler plugin installation is required
  • Automatic targeted introspection. Reference a table in a catalog or schema that hasn't been introspected yet and the plugin introspects just that schema in the background — no more hunting for the right refresh checkbox
  • Dedicated DorisSQL dialect with correct statement and run-block boundaries for Doris syntax the generic MySQL dialect mis-parses: INSERT OVERWRITE, SELECT * EXCEPT(...), QUALIFY, CREATE JOB, materialized views, DISTRIBUTED BY / PROPERTIES DDL, REFRESH, WARM UP, and more — plus native typed parsing for navigation inside DDL bodies
  • Window functions, CTEs, Doris cast targets (STRING, LARGEINT, ARRAY<...>, MAP<...>), TRY_CAST, and map access (col['key']) parse with full structure and completion
  • Completion for Doris built-in functions and Doris data types (VARIANT, BITMAP, HLL, AGG_STATE, ...)
  • Doris-accurate syntax validation via an embedded build of the Doris SQL parser
  • Ready-to-use Apache Doris data-source template: MySQL Connector/J download, default port 9030, connection validation, SHOW CREATE definitions

This is an independent, community plugin developed by Sortdev SRL. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by the Apache Software Foundation. "Apache Doris", Doris, and the Doris logo are trademarks of the Apache Software Foundation, used here only to identify the database this plugin supports. For the official project see doris.apache.org.

Source, issues and documentation: github.com/sort-dev/doris-intellij-plugin
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.5.2 - fixes SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE exports and a parameter-expansion crash.
  • SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE ... [FORMAT AS ...] [PROPERTIES (...)], including after WITH, no longer fails with "Statement.executeQuery() cannot issue statements that do not produce result sets" (S1009).
  • With parameter expansion inside SQL strings enabled, a double-quoted string containing ' after a ${name} parameter no longer breaks the editor with "Token sequence broken" and IndexOutOfBoundsException.
  • The console asks for ${name} parameter values again inside Doris PROPERTIES (...) and other Doris-only clauses, such as export options.
1.5.1 - uses only public action-registration API.
  • Registers the PIPE Execute wrappers through the public dynamic action customizer instead of the internal ActionConfigurationCustomizer.
  • Unloading the plugin restores the previous Execute actions. If another plugin has wrapped them since, the Doris wrapper only passes execution through.
1.5.0 - Doris 4.1.4 grammar and brikk-sql 0.16.0.
  • Uses the exact Doris 4.1.4 native grammar for editor diagnostics and generated-SQL validation.
  • Updates the embedded SQL engine for DEFAULT(column), nested-column ADD/MODIFY, tablet compaction, and SHOW COMPUTE GROUPS.
  • Preserves TIMESTAMPTZ in generated SQL, including ISO timestamp conversion.
  • Adds completion metadata for PARSE_TO_VARIANT, TRY_PARSE_TO_VARIANT, and VECTOR_SEARCH, including vector-search property completion.
  • Updates Variant type inference and generic-function nullability in the embedded engine.
1.4.4 - fixes INSERT execution bounds after range-partition DDL.
  • Doris half-open partition bounds such as VALUES [('start'), ('end')) no longer corrupt statement detection later in the file.
  • Resets lexer context at statement delimiters and ignores semicolons inside comments and literals when restoring context after edits.
1.4.3 - preserves temporary-partition INSERT bounds after incremental editor reparsing.
  • Restores Doris statement context when IntelliJ restarts lexing in the middle of INSERT INTO ... TEMPORARY PARTITION(...) SELECT ....
  • Tests DataGrip's executable ScriptModel ranges for both fresh and edited consoles.
1.4.2 - fixes temporary-partition INSERT parsing and execution bounds.
  • Keeps multiline INSERT INTO ... TEMPORARY PARTITION(...) SELECT ... as one typed statement for execution.
  • Embeds brikk-sql 0.15.1, which parses and round-trips Doris temporary-partition INSERT targets.
1.4.1 - fixes newer 262 builds and adds 263 compatibility.
  • Reports affected tables and views during partial-schema introspection on newer 262 builds.
  • Uses the registered database action promoter through its public interface.
  • Schedules targeted introspection through the coroutine API in a project-owned scope.
1.4.0 - PIPE execution and embedded SQL engine updates.
  • Embeds brikk-sql 0.15.0, including updated Doris reserved identifiers, arithmetic grouping, and SQL parsing/generation fixes.
  • Executes PIPE statements from the current editor text, with DataGrip statement scope, parameter storage, generated-SQL validation, and initiating-console ownership.
  • Handles catalog-mode DDL safety refusals in quick documentation without an unhandled exception.
1.3.6 - updates the embedded brikk-sql engine and metadata to 0.15.0, including updated Doris reserved identifiers and SQL parsing/generation fixes, for local dogfooding.
1.3.5 - updates the embedded brikk-sql engine and metadata to 0.14.0 for local dogfooding.
1.3.4 - prevents quick documentation from surfacing the catalog-mode DDL safety refusal as an unhandled exception.
1.3.3 - executes PIPE statements from the current editor text instead of a stale per-statement DataGrip model snapshot.
1.3.2 - updates the embedded brikk-sql engine and metadata to 0.13.0, including safer quoted-identifier handling in inferred PIPE shapes.
1.3.1 — safer PIPE execution and catalog handling.
  • PIPE execution follows DataGrip. Statement scope, parameters, request ownership, generated-SQL validation, diagnostics, completion, stage execution and Explain Plan now retain platform behavior while failing closed on unsafe translations.
  • Catalog refreshes preserve good metadata. Failed or malformed catalog, database, table and column inventories no longer erase the last successful model; catalog-qualified definition retrieval and fallback restoration avoid wrong-catalog results.
  • Connector/J URL validation supports real deployments. Multi-host, load-balance, replication, IPv6 and host-property URLs are validated without false missing-host errors.
1.3.0 — smarter function completion and fresher introspection.
  • Function completion shows signatures. Doris built-in functions now complete with their argument types and return type (e.g. regexp_count(VARCHAR, VARCHAR) → INT), MySQL-style, from the Doris function catalog.
  • Completion matches your connected server. On connect the plugin reads the server's SHOW BUILTIN FUNCTIONS and reconciles the offered list to that Doris version — functions your server doesn't have are dropped, ones it adds appear.
  • No more non-Doris functions. Functions inherited from the underlying MySQL dialect that Doris doesn't have (regexp_like, the ST_* / MBR* geometry family, GTID / lock / crypto helpers, ...) are no longer suggested.
  • Introspection replaces instead of merging. Recreating a view or table with a different set of columns — or dropping a table / view / database — now updates the database tree and completion instead of leaving the old columns and objects behind.
  • Reliability: a cancelled introspection no longer persists a half-populated model; unreachable external catalogs no longer flood the log with failed retries; and the catalog-scoped introspection fallback restores the pooled connection's catalog on older Doris (no wrong-catalog for the next user of that connection).
1.2.0 — a working Explain Plan, plus Doris UDF / alias function statements.
  • Explain Plan works: the Explain Plan action now runs EXPLAIN <query> and shows the plan in a resizable popup — monospaced and scrolling both ways, with Copy All and Close, so the plan reads the way it does in the Doris CLI (indentation intact). Previously the menu item did nothing: Doris returns a line-per-row text plan that the stock graphical diagram could not render.
  • Doris UDF / alias functions are executable: CREATE [GLOBAL|SESSION|LOCAL] [AGGREGATE|ALIAS] FUNCTION and DROP [GLOBAL] [ALIAS] FUNCTION now parse as a single statement, so the run-block selects and executes them — completing the Doris-only statement coverage started in 1.1.0 (MySQL has no shape for these and left no statement boundary).
1.1.0 — editor fixes: SELECT-list aliases in HAVING / GROUP BY / ORDER BY, positional ordinals, and correct line comments.
  • Column aliases resolve and complete in HAVING / GROUP BY / ORDER BY: a SELECT-list alias (e.g. count(*) AS n) can now be referenced in these clauses — HAVING n > 10 — with working code completion and navigation, exactly as in MySQL. This also silences the spurious "aggregate-free conditions in HAVING … might be inefficient" warning that appeared when a HAVING condition referenced an aggregate through its alias.
  • Positional GROUP BY 1 / ORDER BY 2: a bare integer in GROUP BY or ORDER BY is now understood as an ordinal reference to the Nth select item (and resolves to it), rather than a plain number — matching MySQL and improving grouping analysis.
  • More Doris-only statements are executable: statements MySQL has no shape for now parse as a single statement, so the run-block selects and executes them (previously they had no statement boundary) — CREATE / DROP / SHOW INVERTED INDEX ANALYZER / TOKENIZER / TOKEN_FILTER, CLEAN, UNSET, LOAD LABEL, and ANALYZE DATABASE.
  • Line comments fixed: commenting (Ctrl+/) now inserts a proper -- (with the trailing space Doris requires — a bare -- is not a valid comment and highlighted as code), comments every line of a selection, and round-trips — matching standard SQL.
1.0.0 — Stop tells the truth on statements Doris can't cancel, and hands your console back.
  • Uncancellable INSERT / CTAS are detected, not faked: Doris cannot actually stop a running INSERT or CREATE TABLE AS SELECT once it has started — the server accepts the cancel but the statement keeps running. Stop now verifies whether the cancel really took; when it didn't, instead of hanging on "Cancelling…" forever it tells you the statement is still running, gives you its QueryId to follow with SHOW PROCESSLIST / SHOW LOAD, and offers to detach just this console and reconnect so you can keep working (your other consoles on the same data source are untouched). The detection is behavioral, so it disappears on its own once the server can cancel these statements.
  • Cancelling a multi-statement script stops the whole script: pressing Stop no longer lets the next queued statement launch — the remaining statements are dropped along with the running one.
0.9.0 — native double-quoted strings; SQL highlighting inside query().
  • Double-quoted string handling is now native: "..." lexes as a real string literal — correct string coloring everywhere (multi-line included), honest statement structure, and property pairs like 'k' = "v" parse as string = string. (0.8.0 suppressed the false errors and painted over the color; 0.9.0 removes the mis-lex at the root. Backtick identifiers are unaffected.)
  • Generic SQL syntax highlighting inside query() payload strings: the SQL in the 'query' property of the query() table function is now colored (keywords, identifiers, numbers; both quote styles, multi-line) so embedded remote queries read as SQL instead of one solid string.
0.8.0 — double-quoted strings behave like Doris strings.
  • Double-quoted values — e.g. query('catalog' = 'c', 'query' = "select ...") — are treated as what they are in Doris: string literals. The false "Identifier is too long" / unresolved errors are gone anywhere in a statement, and the text is now colored as a string instead of an identifier. (Doris reads "..." as a string everywhere — only backticks quote identifiers; the underlying MySQL grammar read it as an ANSI quoted identifier. Backtick identifier checks are unaffected.)
  • Enter inside a string inserts a plain newline. Doris string literals are multi-line, so the editor no longer splits them into a '...' || '...' concatenation on Enter — multi-line property values (a query() body spanning several lines, escapes and all) are now comfortable to type.
0.7.1 — internal-API cleanup flagged by Marketplace verification (one platform accessor replaced with its public equivalent). No functional changes.
0.7.0 — Doris Pipes (pipe-syntax SQL, optional) and automatic targeted introspection.
  • Doris Pipes: author queries in GoogleSQL-style pipe syntax (FROM t |> WHERE ... |> AGGREGATE ...) in Doris consoles and run them against any Doris — the plugin transpiles them to standard Doris SQL at execution time (the generated SQL is what the server sees). Includes pipe-aware statement boundaries and syntax checking, per-stage column completion (aliases and join relations included), a right-click Doris Pipes menu with Preview Generated SQL (syntax-highlighted) and Run Stages up to Caret, and server errors mapped back to the exact line and column of the pipe SQL you wrote. Requires the free SQL Transpiler plugin (dev.sort.sql-transpiler-intellij-plugin) from the Marketplace — install it and restart the IDE; without it, this plugin simply keeps its regular Doris behavior. Escape hatch: -Ddoris.pipes=false.
  • Automatic targeted introspection: when completion or a query references a catalog or schema that is enumerated but not yet introspected, the plugin now widens the introspection scope to just that schema and refreshes only it — columns appear moments later, and an editor banner tells you when a table has no column data yet. Works for plain Doris SQL and pipe syntax alike.
0.6.0 — enhanced query cancelling across console windows.
  • Cancel works across console windows: with several consoles running queries against the same data source, Stop now kills exactly the query of the console you pressed it in — the other consoles' queries keep running. (Previously the plugin refused to guess in that situation and fell back to the IDE's stock cancel, which could show the "Deactivate the Data Source?" dialog.) Repeat cancels are also faster.
  • Function completion shows each function's kind: scalar, aggregate, window, and table functions get distinct icons and labels, sourced from Doris's own function registry (via the shared brikk-sql-metadata catalog).
0.5.0 — reliable query cancel, native typed parsing, calmer completion.
  • Reliable query cancel (on by default): the Stop button now actually kills the running Doris query — even behind a load balancer, where the driver's own cancel can miss the frontend or kill the wrong session. The console session stays alive, and the spurious "Cancelling Failed. Deactivate the Data Source?" dialog no longer appears when the cancel succeeds. Opt out with -Ddoris.cancel.experimental=false.
  • Native typed parsing (on by default): Doris DDL/statements parse into real typed structure for navigation inside CREATE VIEW/TABLE/ MATERIALIZED VIEW/JOB bodies, falling back safely to the lenient parse on anything it can't cleanly type. Opt out with -Ddoris.replay.poc=false.
  • Function completion no longer interrupts typing: function suggestions auto-pop only in expression positions, so keywords and literals (e.g. GROUP BY 1, ... AS name) type cleanly. Explicit completion (Ctrl+Space) still offers the full list everywhere.
  • More Doris DDL variants recognized (aggregate/unique-key tables, dynamic/list/range partitioning, routine load, catalog/resource/workload DDL, UPDATE/DELETE), and more * EXCEPT(...) false-error cases silenced.
0.4.0 — 2026.2-ready, plus introspection and editor fixes.
  • Compatible with the upcoming 2026.2 IDE line (one artifact spans 2026.1 and 2026.2; compatibility range raised accordingly).
  • Fixed an IDE-internal error ("Session not started") that could appear during multi-catalog introspection.
  • SELECT * EXCEPT(...): two more false-error cases silenced — UNION operand-count mismatches and "ambiguous column" when the column is in the EXCEPT list. Genuine errors still flagged.
  • Completion after a table alias (v.) now offers only that relation's columns — no more stray function suggestions.
0.3.0 — catalogs, table-valued functions, and a much quieter editor.
  • Multi-catalog support (on by default): Doris external catalogs (Hive, Iceberg, JDBC, ...) appear as a real catalog → database → table tree. The internal catalog introspects automatically; enable external catalogs per-catalog in the schemas pane. Three-part catalog.db.table references resolve and complete, the console switcher picks catalog then database, and real Doris column types (variant, array<...>, ...) display throughout. Opt out with the VM option -Ddoris.catalogs.experimental=false.
  • Upgrade note: existing Doris data sources rebuild their cached model once (silently) on first launch — the tree repopulates on next connect/refresh.
  • Table-valued function completion: tasks(), jobs(), mv_infos(), partitions(), backends() and friends complete their property keys and enum values, and their output columns resolve — including schema-by-argument (tasks("type"="mv")). File TVFs (s3(), hdfs(), ...) stay quiet without fabricating columns.
  • SELECT * EXCEPT(...) no longer raises false errors (column-count mismatch and dependent noise suppressed; genuine mismatches still flagged).
  • Quieter editor across real Doris SQL: session variables, USE @group, SWITCH, materialized-view schedules, CREATE JOB, partition specs, GROUP BY aliases, CTAS key clauses.
  • View columns now introspect correctly (completion inside queries over views).
  • Experimental (off by default): native typed parsing for Doris DDL/statements via -Ddoris.replay.poc=true.
0.2.3 — first public release.
  • DorisSQL dialect on the MySQL foundation with correct statement/run-block boundaries for Doris-specific syntax
  • Native parsing for window functions, IF(), CTE chains, and INSERT OVERWRITE pipelines
  • SELECT * EXCEPT(...), Doris cast targets, TRY_CAST, and REGEXP(...) handled without breaking resolution or completion
  • 825-function completion, Doris data types, Doris-accurate error checking
  • Apache Doris driver template with automatic MySQL Connector/J download

idea-plugin.name: MyBatis SQL Log
idea-plugin.description:
MyBatis SQL Log

Zero-invasion, fully automatic MyBatis SQL log monitoring tool.
View every complete SQL statement executed by your application in real-time within the IDE without modifying any code or configuration.

零侵入、全自动的 MyBatis SQL 日志监控工具。
无需修改任何代码或配置，即可在 IDE 中实时查看应用运行时执行的每一条完整 SQL。

Core Features / 核心特性

  • Zero invasion — No code changes, no additional dependencies required
  • Fully automatic — Agent injection via JavaProgramPatcher
  • Complete SQL — Parameter placeholder replacement with actual values
  • Interceptor compatible — Works with tenant, pagination, data permission interceptors
  • Multi-process — Support with PID and process name identification
  • Configurable port — Customizable listening port
  • JSON to Fields — Generate entity fields from JSON via Generate menu
idea-plugin.change-notes:
v1.0.9

  • 新增 JSON to Fields — 在实体类中通过 Generate 菜单粘贴 JSON，自动生成对应字段（支持嵌套对象与数组）
  • JSON to Fields 字段名自动转标准驼峰命名，与 JSON 键不一致时添加 @JsonProperty 注解保留原始名称
  • JSON to Fields 数组元素自动生成单数命名的静态内部类（如 orders -> Order）

v1.0.8

  • 端口占用窗口支持点击切换 — 再次点击"端口占用"按钮时关闭已打开的窗口，不再重复新建

v1.0.7

  • 新增端口占用查看功能 — 查看所有 Java 进程端口占用，支持按端口/进程名搜索，支持停止进程
  • 修复简单类型参数（如 Long id）SQL 占位符未正确填充的问题
  • 修复 NULL 参数值显示为 = NULL 而非 IS NULL 的问题

v1.0.6

  • 修复 JDK 8 环境下 sql 未打印问题

v1.0.5

  • 修复 macOS 路径含空格（Application Support）导致无法找到 agent jar 的问题
  • 修复 URL 编码路径（%20）未解码导致文件查找失败的问题
  • 增强错误提示，显示插件实际安装路径便于诊断

v1.0.3

  • 修复从 Marketplace 安装后无法找到 agent jar 的问题
  • 增强插件目录路径解析，兼容 JAR 和解压两种加载方式

v1.0.2

  • 修复 @Select 注解 SQL 未被捕获的问题
  • Agent 编译目标降级为 Java 8，兼容所有 JVM 版本
  • 修复内部 API 使用警告
  • 修复集合 API 兼容性警告

v1.0.0

  • 首次发布
  • 支持 MyBatis SQL 实时捕获与展示
  • 支持参数占位符自动填充
  • 支持租户、分页等拦截器改写后的 SQL
  • 支持多进程同时监控
  • 支持自定义监听端口

idea-plugin.name: SQL Transpiler
idea-plugin.description:
Cross-dialect SQL transpilation inside DataGrip and IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate, powered by brikk-sql (a full Kotlin port of sqlglot). Mark any SQL with -- dialect: xyz and execute it against the current engine through transpilation, or transpile any SQL between MySQL, Doris, Trino, Presto, DuckDB, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Hive, Spark, DataFusion, and BigQuery.

  • Execute via transpilation: write a block in one dialect, run it on whatever engine the console is attached to — transpile, review the generated SQL and its diagnostics, execute; unchanged re-runs skip the review
  • Transpile To / From: preview as a before/after diff, then replace in place, insert after, copy, or send to an open console
  • Exact diagnostics: unsupported constructs flagged by the generator, plus functions the target engine does not register (checked against real engine function catalogs)
  • Brikk SQL scratches (.bsql): a lenient polyglot file type where mixed-dialect marker blocks live grumble-free, with gutter actions per block
  • Pipe syntax (|>): write pipe-syntax SQL and generate standard SQL out of it automatically
  • AST viewer tool window over the brikk-sql expression tree

An independent plugin by Sortdev SRL, built on the open-source brikk-sql transpiler.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.3.0
  • Transpile To… / Transpile From… dialect pickers are alphabetical.
0.2.0
  • brikk-sql 0.6.0: expanded cross-dialect function verdicts (incl. new Doris ↔ ClickHouse coverage), hardened dialect guards, and the ClickHouse count() fix.
  • Verifier errors map back to the source more often: nearest-span fallback (shown as "≈ source line N") when no exact emit-span covers the error.
  • Syntax errors in .bsql scratches underline exactly the offending token instead of the rest of the line.
  • 7 MB smaller: dropped a transitive Groovy runtime the SQL parsers never use.
0.1.0
  • Dialects: MySQL, Doris, Trino, Presto, DuckDB, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Hive, Spark, DataFusion, BigQuery.
  • Native verification tiers: authoritative parsers for Trino/Doris/DuckDB, advisory grammar oracles for PostgreSQL/MySQL/Hive/ClickHouse.
  • Brikk SQL scratches: quiet editor (schema-bound inspections and substrate syntax errors suppressed), with brikk-sql's own dialect parsers supplying the real syntax errors per block.
  • File | New | Brikk SQL Scratch, and "Brikk SQL" in the Scratch File language list.

idea-plugin.name: Protobuf DB Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
Decode and edit protobuf-encoded binary values directly from IntelliJ IDEA database result grids.
Configure one or more directories containing .proto files, select a binary cell, choose a protobuf message, and inspect the decoded value as formatted JSON in a live preview tool window.
Enable the "Allow editing" checkbox in the preview to modify the JSON and write it back to the cell as protobuf bytes through the database grid's own mutation API, then submit the change to persist it.
The live preview follows the selected row and caches the message mapping per result grid.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Live preview tool window.

  • Decode selected binary database cells as protobuf JSON.
  • Edit the decoded JSON and write it back to the cell as protobuf bytes (enable the "Allow editing" checkbox in the preview window).
  • Live preview updates automatically when the selected database row changes.
  • Project-level configuration with multiple proto roots.
  • Automatic descriptor generation and per-grid message selection cache.
  • Rewritten in Kotlin with debounced refreshes and cached decoders.

idea-plugin.name: SQL Dialect for DuckDB (embedded & Quack)
idea-plugin.description:
A real DuckDB SQL dialect for DataGrip and IntelliJ-family IDEs, with ready-to-use data sources for local/embedded DuckDB and GizmoSQL servers (Arrow-free quack-jdbc driver).

  • DuckDB syntax, measured: correct statement and run-block boundaries across the DuckDB statement surface — SELECT * EXCLUDE(...), QUALIFY, GROUP BY ALL, struct/list literals, lambdas, PIVOT/UNPIVOT, FROM-first queries, ATTACH, SUMMARIZE, CREATE MACRO/SECRET. Coverage is scored against DuckDB's own test suite: 226/226 sampled syntax families at DuckDB 1.5.5.
  • Engine-exact error checking: statements are validated by a real DuckDB (from your data source's driver; EXPLAIN-based, never executes) — squiggles carry the engine's own messages, so there is zero grammar drift.
  • Completion that follows your engine: on connect the catalog is harvested live from duckdb_functions() — your engine version, your loaded extensions. Run INSTALL/LOAD and completion updates itself; autoloaded extensions arrive via Refresh DuckDB Catalog (editor right-click). Offline you get the bundled 943-function snapshot, plus "requires <extension>" hints for extension functions.
  • Two data sources, one dialect: local file / in-memory DuckDB, and GizmoSQL over jdbc:quack:// (default port 9494). Driver versions are pinned and auto-download from Maven Central, matched to the tested engine.

GizmoSQL connection notes: paste your token into the Password field (stored in the IDE's secure storage) and leave User blank; TLS is off by default — add tls=true in the URL parameters for HTTPS endpoints.

Known issue: cancelling a running query over a GizmoSQL connection is currently a no-op in the quack driver — the query keeps running server-side. Local/embedded cancel works. A driver fix is tracked.

This is an independent, community plugin developed by Sortdev SRL, not affiliated with DuckDB Labs, the DuckDB Foundation, or GizmoSQL. "DuckDB" is a trademark of the DuckDB Foundation, used only to identify the database this plugin supports. DuckDB logo used per the DuckDB design manual.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.2.0 — the injected-SQL language id is now DuckDBSQL (was DuckDBBrikk), so embedding DuckDB SQL in a host language (Kotlin/Java string injection, @Language) reads cleanly. If you had manually set a file's dialect, re-pick DuckDB (sort.dev) once; connected data sources are unaffected.
0.1.1 — polish.
  • Fixed the DuckDB icon rendering oversized in the data source / driver UI.
  • Clearer names: the dialect is DuckDB (sort.dev), and the data-source drivers are DuckDB Embedded (sort.dev) and DuckDB via Quack (sort.dev) — distinct from the stock generic DuckDB driver.
  • Refreshed README; Kotlin/build toolchain updated. No behavior changes.

0.1.0 — first public release.
  • DuckDB dialect with correct statement/run-block boundaries — coverage measured against DuckDB's own test suite (226/226 sampled syntax families at DuckDB 1.5.5).
  • Engine-exact error checking by a real DuckDB from your driver (EXPLAIN-based, never executes).
  • Live per-connection completion: functions/keywords harvested from the connected engine (version- and extension-exact), refreshed automatically when INSTALL/LOAD runs in a console, or on demand via Refresh DuckDB Catalog; bundled 943-function snapshot offline, with "requires <extension>" hints.
  • Object tree from DuckDB's JDBC metadata — ATTACHed databases appear as catalogs, on both drivers.
  • Ready-made data sources: local/embedded DuckDB and GizmoSQL (token-auth quack-jdbc, port 9494); pinned drivers auto-download from Maven Central.
  • Known issue: query cancel over GizmoSQL is a quack-driver no-op (local cancel works); driver fix tracked.

idea-plugin.name: SQL Dialect for Trino
idea-plugin.description:
A real Trino SQL dialect for DataGrip and IntelliJ-family IDEs. Stock IDEs treat Trino/Presto/Athena as generic data sources with the Generic SQL editor; this plugin gives Trino SQL first-class treatment, validated by Trino's own parser (io.trino:trino-parser, bundled, version 483).

  • Measured coverage: 150/150 syntax families (490 statements) from Trino's own repository at tag 483 parse clean — SQL routines, MATCH_RECOGNIZE, PIVOT, JSON clause functions, GRANT/DENY, prepared statements and more.
  • Engine-exact errors, zero setup: the bundled trino-parser validates every statement — Trino's own grammar, exact positions, no server needed.
  • Function completion: 442 functions (kind icons, return types) harvested from Trino 483, plus its 83 reserved words.
  • Schema tree that fills in as you type: connectors appear as catalogs on connect; drilling into a catalog or schema during completion introspects just that namespace, one level at a time — so a huge hive/iceberg catalog is never bulk-loaded. Query cancel verified client- and server-side.
  • Trino auth & TLS built in: no-TLS uses sessionUser (User field; Trino refuses passwords without TLS — leave Password empty). For HTTPS, enable TLS on the SSH/SSL tab (add your CA there for a private CA) — it maps to trino-jdbc's real SSL settings and User & Password auth just works.

Built on the architecture of our SQL Dialect for Apache Doris and SQL Dialect for DuckDB plugins.

This is an independent, community plugin developed by Sortdev SRL, not affiliated with the Trino Software Foundation. "Trino" is a trademark of the Trino Software Foundation, used only to identify the query engine this plugin supports.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.2.0 — the injected-SQL language id is now TrinoSQL (was TrinoBrikk), so embedding Trino SQL in a host language (@Language, string injection) reads cleanly. If you had manually set a file's dialect, re-pick Trino (sort.dev) once; connected data sources are unaffected.
0.1.0 — first public release.
  • Trino dialect with correct statement/run-block boundaries — coverage measured against Trino's own repository at tag 483: 150/150 sampled syntax families (490 statements), zero degraded shapes.
  • Engine-exact error checking by the bundled trino-parser 483 (Trino's own grammar; exact line/column; works with no data source configured).
  • Function completion: 442 functions with kind icons + 83 reserved words, harvested from Trino 483.
  • Schema tree via the generic JDBC introspector (deliberately forced — Trino's version number would otherwise select the PostgreSQL introspector against a server with no pg_catalog); connectors appear as catalogs, and completion deepens the tree lazily one namespace at a time as you type.
  • Data sources with Trino's auth model built in: no-TLS uses sessionUser (User field), never a password; TLS is enabled from the SSH/SSL tab (CA-cert aware) and mapped to trino-jdbc's own SSL settings. Official trino-jdbc 483 pinned, auto-downloaded from Maven Central.

idea-plugin.name: DbTemplate Smart Completion
idea-plugin.description: Provides intelligent code completion for db-template-optimized ORM framework. Auto-completes table names and column names in string parameters.

idea-plugin.name: Safe Result Export
idea-plugin.description:
Mask database results before CSV export.

Choose one transformation per column, compare the original and transformed sample, and write a local UTF-8 CSV.

  • Keep, Redact, and Fixed replacement
  • Session-scoped deterministic tokens
  • Email and phone masking
  • Numeric mapping and date shifting
  • Before/after preview
  • Failure-closed, row-at-a-time local export

The plugin does not modify the source database and includes no telemetry, cloud processing, accounts, or remote AI.

Rules are manual and mappings last only for the current preview/export session. Review every preview before sharing the exported file. The plugin does not certify legal or organizational compliance.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Initial free release.

  • Added eight manual per-column rules.
  • Added local before/after preview.
  • Added UTF-8 CSV export with atomic target replacement.
  • Added session-scoped deterministic mappings.
  • Added failure-closed validation for incomplete grids and invalid values.

idea-plugin.name: Firestore Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Browse Firestore collections, documents, and subcollections in a tool window, authenticating with a GCP service account key -- entirely local REST calls, no gRPC/heavy SDK dependency. A real paid competitor's reviewers reported, three separate times over 8+ months: "'Connection test failed: java.util.NoSuchElementException: Collection contains no element matching the predicate.'" -- an opaque error that says nothing about what's actually wrong. This plugin looks up every required service-account field explicitly and reports the exact missing or malformed field by name; there is no bare `.first {}`/`.single {}` anywhere in the auth path for that exception to come from.

Another cited complaint: "it works very poorly with sub-collections. I would like to see these sub-collections in tabular form as well, not just in JSON." The tool window lists each collection's documents in a real table, with a button to drill into a selected document's own subcollections. All network calls run off the EDT; the service account JSON's contents and the resulting access token are held in memory only, never logged or persisted -- only the file path and project ID are saved. Scalar fields (string, integer, double, boolean) are editable in place from the same table.

Firestore Companion Pro: saved project profiles to switch between dev/staging/prod service accounts without retyping both fields every time; a query/filter builder (field + operator + value) against Firestore's own :runQuery endpoint, instead of always listing an entire collection; and exporting a collection's documents to a pretty-printed JSON file for a quick local backup/debug snapshot, preserving int64 precision exactly as Firestore stores it.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Firestore Companion Pro, an optional paid tier on top of everything below (all free-tier features stay free, no exceptions): saved multi-project profiles (dev/staging/prod, switchable without retyping the service account path and project ID every time), a query/filter builder (field + operator + typed value) against Firestore's own :runQuery structured-query endpoint instead of always listing an entire collection, and exporting a collection's documents to a pretty-printed JSON file, preserving int64 precision exactly as Firestore stores it (same rule already applied to editing). Version scheme moves from semver to a date-based scheme (required for the Freemium <product-descriptor> JetBrains assigns by release-version, not a stylistic choice).

idea-plugin.name: SQL Heading Folding / SQL 标题折叠
idea-plugin.description:
Adds hierarchical comment headings, native code folding, reading-mode labels, and outline navigation to SQL consoles.

Use -- # through -- ##### to organize long SQL scripts in any JetBrains IDE that provides Database Tools and SQL, including IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate and DataGrip.

适用于所有提供 Database Tools and SQL 的 JetBrains IDE（包括 IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate 和 DataGrip），为 SQL 控制台提供分级注释标题、原生代码折叠、阅读态标签与目录导航。
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.8

  • Optionally show colored comment nodes in the SQL outline and render them with their configured colors.
  • Keep one trailing blank line visible when a folded section already ends with blank lines.
  • Move to JDK 21 with an IntelliJ Platform 2024.2 compatibility baseline while retaining support for newer releases.
  • Place the colored-node checkbox at the end of the outline toolbar and preserve expanded tree nodes while editing.
  • Add spacing and a tooltip to the colored-node checkbox.
  • Remove Tool Window Factory API verifier warnings caused by generated Kotlin interface bridges.
  • Add text-only SQL import/export actions for local files and other open consoles of the same database type.
  • Use the current non-deprecated file saver descriptor API.
  • Select the available file saver descriptor constructor at runtime across supported IDE versions.
  • Clarify that the collapse and expand actions control SQL sections in the editor, not the outline tree.
  • Add spacing around the active SQL file name at the top of the outline.

idea-plugin.name: Env Data Sources
idea-plugin.description:
Creates IDE database connections from your project's .env file — no manual setup of host, port, user and password for every project and every service.

On project open the plugin reads .env and creates one data source per group of keys. Keys named DB_<GROUP>_<FIELD> become separate data sources, while missing fields (host, port, driver) are inherited from the base DB_* set — so a typical Laravel .env with several connections yields several ready-to-use data sources.

  • Re-syncs when .env changes; connections are matched by a marker property, so they are updated instead of duplicated.
  • Connections you created by hand are never touched.
  • Passwords go to the IDE password store, not to dataSources.xml.
  • Supports MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite, SQL Server, Oracle and ClickHouse, including Doctrine-style aliases such as pdo_mysql.
  • Manual run: Tools | Sync Data Sources from .env. Settings: Settings | Tools | Env Data Sources.

Requires the bundled Database Tools and SQL plugin (included in PhpStorm, IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate and other paid IDEs).

idea-plugin.name: MongoDB Client Reuse Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning icon on a new MongoClient(...) (legacy driver) or MongoClients.create(...) (modern com.mongodb.client driver) construction written inside a regular method body -- MongoDB's own documentation states "you will only need one instance of class MongoClient even with multiple threads", and that not following the singleton pattern "may lead to too many open connections in MongoDB". A MongoClient holds an internal connection pool (default size 100) -- building one inside a regular method means a brand new pool on every call.

100% static text/PSI analysis -- matches the class name by simple text, so it works whether the real MongoDB driver jar is on the classpath or not. Java and Kotlin.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only flags the "build from scratch" shape -- a client obtained by reference from an existing shared instance/dependency injection is never flagged (correctly, since it isn't the anti-pattern this plugin targets).

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: CMS Sync
idea-plugin.description:
Turns a Microsoft SQL Server Central Management Server into the source of truth for your connections. Point the plugin at the instance that stores the registrations, and every registered server becomes a data source in the IDE, inside folders that mirror the CMS group tree.

It runs on demand, showing exactly what would change before writing anything, or on a schedule that keeps the list current on its own.

What it does

  • Preview first. Additions, renames, moved folders and driver changes are listed before a single connection is written. Cancel and nothing happens.
  • Folders mirror the CMS groups, nesting included, under a folder prefix of your choice.
  • Stays in sync. Renaming an instance, moving it to another group or changing its address in the CMS updates the existing connection instead of duplicating it.
  • Automatic sync, if you want it. Pick an interval and the plugin applies changes on its own, reporting each cycle in the IDE's Notifications. It never opens a password prompt by itself.
  • Beyond SQL Server — one line in the registration description turns an entry into a PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle or MongoDB connection. See below.
  • Nothing is silently dropped. An unknown engine, a missing driver or an address that cannot be a host is skipped with the reason spelled out — never turned into a connection that only fails later.

Beyond SQL Server: the db_engine directive

A Central Management Server does not check what you register: the address field is free text, and nothing connects until someone asks it to. So the registry you already keep can hold every database your team runs — it only needs somewhere to say which engine each entry is. That place is the registration description.

Register the server in SSMS as usual, put its real address in Server name, and add one line to Registered server description:

db_engine: postgres

That entry now becomes a PostgreSQL data source: the PostgreSQL driver, and a URL in the format that driver expects. Three optional keys refine it:

  • db_port: 5432 — the port, when it is not already part of the address. Writing the address as 10.0.0.5:5432 works just as well.
  • db_name: analytics — the initial database.
  • db_url: jdbc:postgresql://10.0.0.5:5432/analytics — a complete JDBC URL, for whatever the composition above does not cover. It wins over the other keys.

A full description might read:

Reporting database for the BI team.
Ask Maria before restarting it.
db_engine: postgres
db_port: 5432
db_name: analytics

The directive lives among your own text: it can sit on any line, in any case, and keys the plugin does not know are ignored. Without a db_engine line the entry is a SQL Server, exactly as it has always been — nothing changes for a registry that never uses this.

Engine names you can write

postgres (or postgresql, pg) · mysql · mariadb · oracle · mongo (or mongodb) · db2 · sqlite · h2 · duckdb · clickhouse · snowflake · redshift · bigquery · databricks · trino · vertica · teradata · hana · cassandra · redis · cockroach (or cockroachdb) · sybase · sqlserver (or mssql) · azuresql · synapse

Anything else is taken as a DataGrip driver id, which is the escape hatch for the variants: db_engine: postgresql.aws_wrapper, db_engine: mysql.cloud_sql.8, db_engine: oracle for the legacy driver instead of oracle.19. The full list of ids is the one your IDE shows under Database Drivers.

An engine with no matching driver in your IDE, or an address that cannot be a host, is skipped with the reason spelled out in the preview — never turned into a connection that only fails when you try to use it. And a skipped entry keeps whatever connection it already had: a typo in the CMS never costs you a connection.

One caveat worth knowing: these entries also appear in SSMS, where they look like ordinary SQL Servers and will fail if something tries to connect to them — a double-click, a multi-server query, or an Agent job aimed at the group. A dedicated CMS group, with the purpose written in its description, keeps that out of everyone's way.

What it never does

  • Touch connections you created by hand. The plugin acts only on what it created itself.
  • Delete by default. An instance dropped from the CMS is moved to an Orphans folder, because deleting a connection also discards its query history, consoles and saved password, and cannot be undone. Deleting is available, but you have to ask for it.
  • Overwrite your settings. Only name, address and folder are kept in step with the CMS. Driver options, SSL, SSH tunnels, read-only mode and introspection scope stay exactly as you left them.

Requirements

Read permission on msdb at the CMS instance — ServerGroupReaderRole is enough. That connection is created with Windows credentials, the only method a CMS accepts.

A CMS stores no credentials of its own, so registered instances are created with address, name, description and folder only. They default to user and password with no user filled in; the IDE asks on first connect, and the method you pick there is never overwritten by later syncs.
idea-plugin.change-notes:

  • Registering a connection that is not SQL Server writes the db_engine: line for you, so the entry comes back with the right driver.
  • What is registered reconstructs the same URL when it comes back: named instances travel inside the address (SERVER\INSTANCE), and port and database travel as directives for the other engines.
  • The new registration is linked to the connection it came from, so syncing keeps that one up to date instead of creating a second one beside it.

0.2.0

  • An instance that cannot be mapped is skipped with a reason and keeps the connection it already has, instead of being treated as removed from the CMS.
  • Sync now button on the settings page.
  • Cancelling a preview while automatic sync is on now warns that the same changes would be applied by the next cycle, and offers to turn it off.

  • The connection used to read the CMS is created with Windows credentials.
  • Fixed: the automatic cycle failed with "no ProgressIndicator in this thread".

idea-plugin.name: Enum-Ordinal Persistence Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on a JPA @Enumerated field with no explicit EnumType.STRING, on a real @Entity class -- JPA's own default is ORDINAL, and reordering or inserting a value in the middle of the enum after data has already been persisted silently corrupts existing records (the stored ordinal no longer corresponds to the same constant).

Confirms the field genuinely reaches persistent storage (the containing class is a real JPA @Entity), not just an annotation checked in isolation. A well-documented fragility (Baeldung and official JPA persistence guides); no Marketplace plugin found that flags it, despite several enum-tooling plugins existing.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only standard JPA @Enumerated on an @Entity class -- doesn't cover custom serialization (Jackson @JsonValue, protobuf enum) or non-JPA persistence frameworks.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: Short DB Tab Titles
idea-plugin.description:
Removes the data source name from database editor tabs.

As soon as a project holds more than one connection, every table tab carries the connection name appended to it, for example customers [@localhost - postgres:postgres]. With long connection names the part that matters — the table name — gets squeezed out of sight, and a row of tabs becomes hard to read at a glance.

With this plugin the same tab simply reads customers. Nothing is lost: the full connection name is one hover away in the tab tooltip, and it stays visible in the navigation bar above the editor.

There is nothing to configure — install it and the suffix is gone. Tabs that are not database editors, such as SQL files, scratches and consoles, are left untouched.

Works in any IDE with database support.

1.0.1

idea-plugin.name: JDBC Double-Close Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags a JDBC resource (Connection/ Statement/PreparedStatement/ CallableStatement/ResultSet) .close() reached with the resource already closed -- on EVERY path reaching it (a certain double-close) or on SOME path (a real, path-dependent risk) -- plus a use of the resource reached with it already closed on every path.

Built on a real path-sensitive typestate analysis: every tracked resource variable's possible states are propagated through the method's own statement structure, MERGING (set union) the two branches of every if/else, try/catch, and loop body -- the same "meet over all paths" idea a real dataflow framework uses, implemented via AST-structural recursion rather than an explicit CFG graph (Java's structured control flow doesn't need one for this to be genuinely path-sensitive).

Stated honestly: the platform's own bundled "JDBC resource opened but not safely closed" inspection covers LEAKS (never closing) -- a different bug class entirely, never double-close or use-after-close with real branch sensitivity. No dedicated Marketplace plugin found for this exact angle.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: Second-Order SQLi Field Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags a SQL sink concatenating a @Entity field's getter/direct read, when that SAME field is ALSO confirmed, elsewhere in the project, to be written from unsanitized HTTP input -- CWE-89, the second-order form: the tainted value passes through persistent storage (a real database) between the write and the read, invisible to any single-method or single-call-chain taint check.

Built on a real FIELD-SENSITIVE, two-phase, whole-project points-to analysis -- the write site and the read site can live in completely unrelated classes with no call-graph relationship whatsoever; the field NAME itself is the only thing connecting them, exactly the shape documented as the real blind spot of simple pattern-matching SAST tools ("SAST tools excel at direct input-to-query flows but struggle when malicious data is stored and later used in a different execution context").

Stated honestly: Checkmarx and Fortify (real, confirmed enterprise SAST tools) model this exact pattern -- neither is free, an inline IDE plugin, or Community-Edition-compatible. No dedicated Marketplace plugin found.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: ES REST Data Source
idea-plugin.description:
ES REST Data Source connects DataGrip to Elasticsearch through its REST API.

It provides a DataGrip data source backed by the Elasticsearch REST API and a Dev Tools-style .esrest query console, without using Elasticsearch SQL.

Features

  • Connect through the Elasticsearch REST API.
  • Browse indices and mapping fields in database tools.
  • Execute REST requests from .esrest files.
  • Complete API paths, parameters, request bodies, Query DSL, aggregations, and mapping fields.
  • Offer dynamic completion for indices, aliases, data streams, and mapping fields.
  • Support JSON and NDJSON request bodies.
  • Support Basic and API Key authentication, with configurable TLS certificate verification.
  • Support Elasticsearch 7.x, 8.x, and 9.x.

ES REST Data Source is an independent open-source project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Elasticsearch B.V., Elastic, or JetBrains.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Initial public release.

  • REST-based Elasticsearch data source for DataGrip.
  • Index and mapping metadata browsing.
  • Dev Tools-style .esrest query console.
  • API, request body, Query DSL, aggregation, and mapping-field completion.

  • Configurable TLS certificate verification.

idea-plugin.name: MigrationGuard
idea-plugin.description:
Review risky SQL migrations before they run.

MigrationGuard checks migration SQL inside your JetBrains IDE. It flags potential data loss, unqualified updates or deletes, table locking and changes that may break rolling deployments. Every finding explains the impact and a safer approach. Analysis runs locally: the plugin does not connect to a database or upload SQL.

Free — useful on every migration

  • Inline warnings for destructive SQL, UPDATE/DELETE without WHERE, risky type changes and PostgreSQL indexes without CONCURRENTLY when the dialect is known.
  • A Findings window with severity, explanation and direct navigation to the statement.
  • Visible line or file suppressions and project settings through .migrationguard.yml.

Pro — review a release at scale

  • Audit SQL migrations across the project instead of opening files one by one.
  • See six additional PostgreSQL and MySQL availability checks with locations and guidance.
  • Export JSON or SARIF 2.1.0 reports for review and CI ingestion.

Open a .sql file to start. MigrationGuard works with plain SQL, Flyway migrations and Liquibase Formatted SQL for PostgreSQL 12+ and MySQL 8+. If Auto cannot identify the database, choose the dialect in settings to enable database-specific checks. Current pricing and trial terms are in the Pricing tab.

MigrationGuard is a source-based review aid. It cannot know your table size, live schema or migration runner's transaction mode. In particular, CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY requires a non-transactional PostgreSQL migration; the plugin explains that prerequisite and does not rewrite the statement automatically. No account or usage telemetry is required for Free.

Revisa migraciones SQL peligrosas antes de ejecutarlas.

MigrationGuard analiza el SQL de tus migraciones dentro del IDE. Señala posibles pérdidas de datos, modificaciones sin WHERE, bloqueos de tablas y cambios que pueden romper despliegues graduales. Cada hallazgo explica el impacto y propone un enfoque más seguro. El análisis es local: el plugin no se conecta a la base de datos ni sube el SQL.

Gratis — útil en cada migración

  • Avisos en el editor para SQL destructivo, UPDATE/DELETE sin WHERE, cambios de tipo arriesgados e índices PostgreSQL sin CONCURRENTLY cuando se conoce el dialecto.
  • Ventana de hallazgos con severidad, explicación y navegación directa a la sentencia.
  • Supresiones visibles por línea o archivo y configuración mediante .migrationguard.yml.

Pro — revisa un release completo

  • Audita las migraciones SQL de todo el proyecto sin abrir cada archivo.
  • Activa seis controles adicionales de disponibilidad para PostgreSQL y MySQL, con ubicación y recomendaciones.
  • Exporta informes JSON o SARIF 2.1.0 para revisión e ingestión en CI.

Abre un archivo .sql para empezar. Funciona con SQL normal, migraciones Flyway y Liquibase Formatted SQL para PostgreSQL 12+ y MySQL 8+. Si Auto no identifica la base de datos, elige el dialecto en los ajustes. Los precios y condiciones actuales de prueba aparecen en la pestaña Pricing.

MigrationGuard analiza código fuente: no conoce el tamaño real de las tablas, el esquema activo ni el modo de transacción del ejecutor. CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY exige una migración PostgreSQL fuera de una transacción; el plugin explica este requisito y no reescribe la sentencia automáticamente. La versión gratuita no requiere cuenta ni envía telemetría de uso.

idea-plugin.name: QueryGuard
idea-plugin.description:
QueryGuard reviews PostgreSQL SQL in DataGrip while you write and when you choose Check Query Safety. It flags risky statements such as DELETE or UPDATE without WHERE, DROP, TRUNCATE and multi-statement scripts, then explains what to review before execution. QueryGuard advises; it does not prevent DataGrip from running SQL.

All analysis runs locally in the IDE. QueryGuard does not send SQL text, results, credentials, connection URLs or product telemetry to a service.

What you get

  • Free: editor warnings, on-demand review and datasource classification as DEV, TEST, STAGING or PROD. An unclassified connection is never described as safe.
  • Pro: shared review rules in a project .queryguard.yml file, production review acknowledgement and local audit summary and export. The audit contains metadata, not SQL text.

QueryGuard focuses on PostgreSQL and uses static analysis. Review the actual datasource and query before execution. A review with no supported findings is not a guarantee of safety.

Pro licensing is handled by JetBrains Marketplace. A 7-day trial is available; prices shown by Marketplace depend on your region. Compatible with DataGrip 2025.3 and newer.

idea-plugin.name: Code Comment Navigator
idea-plugin.description:
Navigate SQL and HTTP comments in a collapsible outline on the right side of the editor.

Code Comment Navigator is free and open source under the MIT License. Individuals and organizations may use it for personal or commercial purposes. No purchase, subscription, or activation key is required.

Keep long database schemas, reporting queries, migration scripts, and HTTP request collections easy to navigate. Group sections by business domain and jump directly to the query or request you need.

Features

  • SQL, HTTP, and REST files: organize comment headings into six Markdown levels.
  • Navigate to a heading with a click or Enter; search headings by typing in the outline.
  • Follow the selected editor and refresh the outline after edits, without saving.
  • Expand or collapse headings, with folding state retained while editing the same file.
  • Browse SQL and HTTP Scratch files from the outline header, search by filename, drag files into folders, create files or folders, and use IDEA file actions and keymap shortcuts from the context menu.
  • Recognize HTTP request separators and fall back to ordinary comments when no headings exist.
  • Java and Kotlin: open the existing comment navigation popup from the editor context menu.

Getting started

Open a SQL or HTTP file, then select View > Tool Windows > Comment Outline. Project files and Scratches are supported.

Use -- # Heading in SQL and // # Heading in HTTP. Add more hash characters for deeper levels. An HTTP ### Request name separator is treated as a level-two heading.

The editor context menu and Edit menu also provide the Comment Structure action.

License and support

The MIT License permits use, modification, and redistribution, including commercial use, subject to retaining the copyright and license notices. The software is provided as is, without warranty.

No fixed update schedule or support response time is promised.

idea-plugin.name: Migration Guard
idea-plugin.description:
Catches the migrations that take production down — while you are still writing them.

Flyway and Liquibase run your SQL. Neither one tells you that the statement you just wrote will lock a table for the length of the deploy, fail the moment the table has a row in it, or break every application instance still running the previous version. Migration Guard underlines those as you type, and the tooltip says why it breaks and what to write instead.

It knows who runs the migration

Every generic SQL linter tells you the same thing: add CONCURRENTLY to your CREATE INDEX. With Flyway, that advice is wrong and the failure is the worst kind. Flyway wraps each migration in a transaction; CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY waits for every earlier transaction to finish, including that one. They wait on each other, and the application hangs at startup with nothing in the log, holding a connection forever (flyway/flyway issue #3961).

Migration Guard flags it, and the quick fix creates the .sql.conf with executeInTransaction=false next to your migration — without touching a line of your SQL. That is the difference between a SQL linter and one that understands your migration tool.

Ten rules, each with the rewrite
MG001 — CONCURRENTLY inside Flyway's transaction
MG002 — CONCURRENTLY sharing the file with other statements
MG003 — CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY on an existing table
MG004 — ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL without a DEFAULT
MG005 — SET NOT NULL on an existing column
MG006 — ADD CONSTRAINT (foreign key or check) without NOT VALID
MG007 — RENAME of a table or column
MG008 — DROP COLUMN
MG009 — ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE
MG010 — DDL without a lock_timeout

No finding is a bare complaint. MG005 hands you the three migrations — CHECK ... NOT VALID, VALIDATE CONSTRAINT, SET NOT NULL — already written with your table and column names.

Built not to be noisy
Tables and columns created in the same migration are never reported: they are empty and nothing uses them yet. A migration that builds a schema from scratch is silent.
SQL inside comments, string literals and function bodies is never mistaken for real SQL.
No style or opinion rules. Only operations that break production.
Suppress one line with -- migration-guard-disable-next-line MG003, a whole file with -- migration-guard-disable-file, or any rule in the inspection profile.
Liquibase formatted SQL is skipped rather than given Flyway-specific advice.
Works everywhere

Analyses plain .sql files in every IntelliJ-based IDE — IntelliJ IDEA (including the free one), PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, Rider — with or without the Database tools, because it reads the text rather than the SQL PSI. PostgreSQL + Flyway. Free to use.

idea-plugin.name: DataChart

idea-plugin.name: DataModelRobot
idea-plugin.description:
DataModelRobot extracts the data model of a Spring Boot project: it parses source code together with the database schema, then outputs table information and a relationship diagram in which every table relation carries a confidence score.

实际项目普遍不建外键，表关系只能从业务代码推断，而研发可能误解数据关系写出错误代码。 因此本插件不只给出关系，还给出证据链与冲突列表：
  • 每条证据可追溯到 文件:行号——MPJ 显式 JOIN、LambdaQueryWrapper 条件、命名约定各自计权
  • 冲突检测：JOIN 两侧类型不匹配、租户/逻辑删除隔离缺失、多义指向、双向不一致、孤儿字段
  • 置信度由证据与冲突算出，不由 LLM 直接给分，保证可复现、可追溯
首期聚焦 MyBatis-Plus 技术栈（MyBatis-Plus + MyBatis-Plus-Join + dynamic-datasource + Lombok）。

Requires the bundled Database Tools plugin for schema access and JDBC drivers.

idea-plugin.name: TableBridge - Database Object Copy
idea-plugin.description:
Copy database objects between DataGrip connections. Review the SQL, then transfer.

TableBridge adds a familiar Copy → Paste workflow to the database tree. Select source objects, paste onto a destination database or schema, and use a three-step wizard to configure and review the transfer.

  • Tables and records: copy structure and data, structure only, or records into an existing table.
  • Per-object control: search, select, rename destinations, and review field mappings or complete destination definitions.
  • MySQL and PostgreSQL: same-engine transfer and supported cross-engine conversions, with explicit conversion notes.
  • Database objects: supported views, functions, procedures, sequences, and types; complex definitions use an editable review workflow.
  • Recovery and synchronization: optional durable checkpoints, bounded retries, primary-key insert/update, and mirror delete.
  • Execution visibility: SQL preview, dependency checks, destructive-operation confirmation, and exportable per-object results.

Getting started: refresh source/destination metadata; copy objects in the database tree with Ctrl+C (⌘C on macOS); select the destination database/schema and paste with Ctrl+V (⌘V); configure, review, and start.

Compatibility: DataGrip 2026.2 (262.*). The current version is 0.3.3-alpha. MySQL 8.0.43 and PostgreSQL 18.3 have isolated integration-test evidence. Oracle 19c has isolated bidirectional table/type/data-helper acceptance with MySQL and PostgreSQL; complex Oracle objects and end-to-end UI paths remain experimental. SQL Server is outside this release's supported scope.

Boundaries: arbitrary dynamic SQL, complex collations, vendor-specific types, and ambiguous overloads are not promised to convert automatically. Checkpoint/sync mode requires matching complete primary keys and destination staging space; MySQL destinations require InnoDB. Existing triggers and constraints remain active. DDL can commit implicitly and failures may leave structures; this plugin is not a database backup tool.

Database authentication stays with DataGrip. TableBridge does not add a password store or cloud transfer service. Review definitions and test with disposable data before important transfers.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Fix PostgreSQL boolean-to-numeric full-content verification for Oracle transfers. Add real isolated Oracle/MySQL/PostgreSQL bidirectional acceptance coverage.

idea-plugin.name: Orkitekt
idea-plugin.description:
Generates an entity-relationship diagram of your JPA entities as an Excalidraw file.
  • Works with javax.persistence (Spring Boot 2.7) and jakarta.persistence (Spring Boot 3.x).
  • Detects @Entity, @MappedSuperclass, @Embeddable, all association types, inheritance, embedded ids and element collections. Bidirectional relations are merged into a single arrow.
  • Arrows are bound to the boxes, labelled with their cardinality (1:1, 1:N, N:1, N:M); LAZY relations are dashed.
  • Layered layout with orthogonal routing (Eclipse Layout Kernel).
  • Deterministic output: the same model always produces the same file, so diagrams can be kept in Git.
Right-click a project or package and choose Orkitekt: Generate Diagram. Output folder, file name and displayed details can be configured in Settings | Tools | Orkitekt.

idea-plugin.name: SOPSie
idea-plugin.description:
Seamless SOPS (Secrets OPerationS) integration for JetBrains IDEs. Edit encrypted secrets directly in your IDE without leaving your workflow.

Features

  • Encrypt & Decrypt — One-click encryption and decryption from the editor, project view, or Tools menu
  • Decrypted Preview — View decrypted content in a read-only preview without modifying the original file
  • Edit-in-Place — Edit decrypted content in a temporary file with automatic re-encryption on save
  • Auto-Decrypt — Optionally auto-decrypt files when opened, with configurable auto-encrypt on save
  • Key Management — Rotate data keys and update encryption keys from .sops.yaml
  • Auto-Detection — Automatically detects SOPS-encrypted files and shows encryption status
  • Visual Indicators — Custom file icons and status bar widget show encryption state at a glance
  • Editor Notifications — Smart banners with quick actions when opening encrypted files
  • Configuration Hot-Reload — Automatically picks up .sops.yaml changes without restarting
  • Configurable Behavior — Customize open/save behaviors, auto-close tabs, confirmations, and more

Supported Formats

Works with all SOPS-supported file types: YAML, JSON, ENV, INI, and binary files.

Requirements

  • SOPS CLI installed and available in PATH (or configured in settings)
  • Encryption keys configured (AGE, GPG, AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, or HashiCorp Vault)

Getting Started

  1. Install the SOPS CLI: brew install sops (macOS) or see installation docs
  2. Configure your encryption keys
  3. Create a .sops.yaml in your project root to define encryption rules
  4. Right-click any file and select SOPS > Encrypt File to get started

### Fixed
- Encrypt stdin content without temp files - Encrypt before save to prevent plaintext on disk - Restrict permissions on decrypted temp files - Restrict ACL on Windows and clean up on failure - Encrypt synchronously so save reflects ciphertext - Honour cancel choice instead of saving plaintext - Follow renames and moves of decrypted files - Write stdin on a separate thread to avoid deadlock - Shut down config debounce scheduler on unload

idea-plugin.name: Obfuscation Pro
idea-plugin.description:
Obfuscation Pro helps you ship obfuscated Java, Kotlin, Android, and IntelliJ plugin projects without losing the runtime entry points your app depends on.

It detects ProGuard, R8, yGuard, and Allatori projects, then surfaces inspections for the places where obfuscation most often breaks production code: Android manifests, ServiceLoader files, resource class names, reflection, executable jars, IntelliJ plugin.xml, Jackson, Moshi, JPA/Hibernate, WorkManager, AndroidX Startup, Glide, Dagger/Hilt, picocli, Kotlin reflection, JNI, Retrofit, Room, Parcelable, WebView bridges, Spring, serialization, and more.

For many warnings, Obfuscation Pro offers quick-fixes that append the right keep rule to your configured ProGuard/R8 file or add a @Keep annotation. It also warns when the config itself undermines reliable results, such as keep-everything rules, allowobfuscation on name-based entry points, missing mapping/seeds/usage outputs, stale obfuscation outputs, and keep rules for classes that no longer exist.

When you ship a minified build, Obfuscation Pro reads the generated mapping.txt, seeds.txt and usage.txt, and shows the obfuscation state of every class right next to your code: gutter icons, project-view decorations, a coverage tool window, exportable HTML/CSV reports, and a stack-trace retrace tool window so production crashes resolve to source. Kept classes also show the exact matching keep directive and its source location, so you can understand why a name survived obfuscation and navigate directly to the responsible rule.

Obfuscation Pro understands ProGuard, R8 (compat and full mode), yGuard, and Allatori, and generates rule syntax appropriate to each.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changed

  • Speeds up project-wide inspections and keep-rule analysis by reusing results until project files change.

Fixed

  • Secures Allatori and yGuard mapping imports against external entities and remote DTD or schema access.
  • Retraces overloaded and inlined methods accurately with the built-in mapping parser, including original line-number mappings.
  • Stops packaging and linking to the GPL-covered Guardsquare ReTrace and ProGuard runtime libraries.
  • Preserves R8 detection when Android mapping output is discovered automatically.
  • Avoids adding keep annotations that are not available on the project classpath.
  • Matches coverage to exact member signatures and overloads, and keeps coverage and mappings for identically named classes separate across modules.
  • Reports malformed seeds and usage outputs in notifications and diagnostics instead of treating them as empty coverage data.
  • Releases coverage tool-window listeners when their content is disposed.
  • Keeps the Kotlin integration isolated so the plugin can load when the optional Kotlin plugin is unavailable.

idea-plugin.name: AsciiDoc
idea-plugin.description:
Edit AsciiDoc files in the IDE with syntax highlighting, auto-completion and a live preview.

AsciiDoc is a text document format, similar to formats like Markdown, for writing notes, documentation, articles, books, ebooks, slideshows, web pages, man pages and blogs. AsciiDoc files can be translated to many formats including HTML, PDF, EPUB, man page. AsciiDoc comes with, in contrast to Markdown, a well-defined syntax for tables, includes and cross-references.

Learn how to use this plugin in the official ûdemy course! This plugin includes support for Antora and Spring REST Docs. By using pandoc, it converts AsciiDoc to Microsoft Word (DOCX).

Quick start | User Guide | FAQ | Issue tracker

To support the authors of Asciidoctor, please consider supporting us via OpenCollective.

For better legibility in the preview, this package includes DejaVu fonts (license). It can render Mermaid diagrams (MIT License) and MathML via MathJax (Apache License 2.0). It bundles Graphviz (Common Public License Version 1.0).
