idea-plugin.name: Dreamshader Language Extension
idea-plugin.description:
Comprehensive DreamShaderLang support for JetBrains Rider, covering .dsm, .dsf, and .dsh files from language core to tooling.

Language core

  • Lexer, parser, PSI, and symbol model foundations
  • Syntax highlighting with semantic classification, color settings, and inline color previews for vector constructors, color aliases, hex colors, and conservative 0-255 channel values
  • Formatter with DreamShader code style settings, section assignment alignment, commenter, quote handling, brace matching, folding, and structure view

Editing and navigation

  • Context-aware completion for sections, types, settings values, catalog-driven UE.* / Substrate.*, HLSL, and imports
  • Goto declaration, find usages, references, Rename, Safe Delete, Copy/Paste Reference, breadcrumbs, Context Info, hover docs, signature help, plain-text symbol completion, and rename suggestions, with UE.* / Substrate.* served from the shared material-expression catalog
  • Inlay parameter hints, Code Vision hints, declaration/import gutter markers, and Bridge diagnostic line markers with source-location navigation
  • IDE include/dependency integration for DreamShader import "..." statements

Diagnostics and project integration

  • Cached semantic diagnostics (syntax, section-shape, semantic) plus Bridge diagnostics mapping, with parser recovery and targeted Bridge-failure-prevention checks
  • Configurable project settings: project root, manifest path, Unreal Engine source root with auto-detect, material-expression scan toggle and cache path, status bar, code lens, inlay parameter hints, out placeholder suffix, import extension strategy, hover doc overrides, and Bridge commands
  • Bridge tool window and workflow actions (refresh diagnostics, recompile current or all, clean generated shaders, open Bridge paths)

Packages, templates, and hub

  • Package tooling: package store dialog with search/filter/details/install-state markers, background install-update-remove, add-remove index sources, GitHub install/update/remove, open packages folder, and package-aware import resolution
  • Native File and Code Templates plus template tools for material/function/header, texture sample, noise material, package scaffold, and package wizard workflows
  • Material preview tool window backed by the portable DreamShader Bridge file transport
  • Unified DreamShader Hub entry and shared card-based UI surface for settings, diagnostics, preview, package, and template workflows

面向 JetBrains Rider 的完整 DreamShaderLang 支持，覆盖 .dsm、.dsf、.dsh 文件，从语言核心到工具集成。

语言核心

  • 词法、语法、PSI 与符号模型基础
  • 语法高亮，含语义分类、颜色设置，以及向量构造、颜色别名、十六进制颜色和保守 0-255 通道值的内联预览
  • 格式化、DreamShader 代码样式设置、section 赋值对齐、注释、引号处理、括号匹配、折叠与结构视图

编辑与导航

  • 上下文感知补全：sections、类型、设置值、catalog 驱动的 UE.* / Substrate.*、HLSL 与 imports
  • 跳转声明、查找用法、引用、重命名、安全删除、Copy/Paste Reference、面包屑、Context Info、悬浮文档、签名帮助、纯文本符号补全与重命名建议，UE.* / Substrate.* 由共享的 material-expression catalog 提供
  • 内联参数提示、Code Vision 提示、声明/import gutter 标记，以及可跳转源码位置的 Bridge 诊断行标记
  • 将 DreamShader import "..." 接入 IDE include/dependency 机制

诊断与项目集成

  • 带缓存的语义诊断（语法、section-shape、语义）以及 Bridge 诊断映射，包含 parser 恢复与针对 Bridge 失败的预防性检查
  • 可配置项目设置：项目根、manifest 路径、可自动检测的 Unreal Engine 源码根、material-expression 扫描开关与缓存路径、状态栏、code lens、内联参数提示、out 占位后缀、import 扩展名策略、悬浮文档覆盖与 Bridge 命令
  • Bridge 工具窗口与工作流操作（刷新诊断、重编译当前或全部、清理生成的 shader、打开 Bridge 路径）

包、模板与 Hub

  • 包工具：带搜索/筛选/详情/安装状态标记的 package store 对话框、后台安装-更新-移除、增删索引源、GitHub 安装/更新/移除、打开包目录，以及包感知的 import 解析
  • 原生 File and Code Templates，以及材质/函数/头文件、贴图采样、噪声材质、包脚手架与包向导的模板工具
  • 基于 DreamShader Bridge 文件传输的材质预览工具窗口
  • 统一的 DreamShader Hub 入口与卡片化共享 UI 表面，整合设置、诊断、预览、包与模板工作流
idea-plugin.change-notes:
### Added

- DreamShader 1.8 source-root-aware imports. Project and plugin `DShader` trees are isolated by default; explicit `Project:`, `Plugin.<Name>:` and compatible `Plugins/<Name>:` qualifiers cross roots.
- Bridge diagnostic metadata support for upstream `code`, `stage`, `detail`, `assetPath`, `source`, shader platform, and quality level fields. Diagnostic codes are displayed in editor annotations.
- Coverage for plugin-owned imports, explicit cross-root imports, and containment enforcement.

### Changed

- Language and integration baseline updated from DreamShaderLang 1.6.3 to DreamShader 1.8.0/current main as checked on 2026-09-01.
- Preview request files are written to a temporary file and atomically moved into the Bridge request queue, preventing Unreal from consuming partial JSON.

### Fixed

- Import resolution no longer allows an owned DreamShader source to escape its source/packages root through `..` or an absolute path.
- Plugin sources no longer accidentally resolve an unqualified import from the project `DShader` tree when a same-named dependency belongs to another root.
- Imported declarations resolve correctly in IntelliJ temporary/light virtual files, restoring imported hover docs and parameter hints.
- Texture-sample and noise material generators no longer emit unresolved `Builtin/Texture.dsh` / `Builtin/Noise.dsh` imports; they now generate self-contained DreamShader 1.8 syntax.

idea-plugin.name: ColdFusion CFML
idea-plugin.description: Advanced support for ColdFusion files (.cfm, .cfc) with syntax highlighting, code completion, and language features.

idea-plugin.name: pell
idea-plugin.description:
Write PL/SQL like it's 2026

pell is a statically-typed surface language that compiles to clean, idiomatic Oracle PL/SQL 19c / 23ai. Modern syntax, real type checking, ergonomic SQL — and the emitted PL/SQL is a deployable, human-readable, SHA-anchored artifact you commit, audit, and git blame like any other code.

This plugin makes IntelliJ IDEA, DataGrip, PyCharm, and the rest of the JetBrains family a real editor for pell: split-view live preview, gutter run/build buttons, an embedded REPL, project scaffold, and full LSP-backed diagnostics / completion / go-to-definition.

One look at the lowering

// src/hr/staffing.pell
module hr::staffing;

pub record Employee { id: number, name: text, level: number }
pub error NotFound { id: number }

pub fn promote(id: number) -> Result<Employee, NotFound> {
    let row: Employee = sql! {
        select id, name, level from employees where id = :id
    }.one()?;
    return Ok(Employee {
        id:    row.id,
        name:  row.name,
        level: row.level + 1,
    });
}

…lowers to PL/SQL you'd write by hand:

CREATE OR REPLACE PACKAGE hr.staffing AS
  TYPE t_employee IS RECORD (
    id    NUMBER,
    name  VARCHAR2(4000),
    level NUMBER
  );
  FUNCTION promote(p_id IN NUMBER) RETURN t_employee;
END staffing;
/

CREATE OR REPLACE PACKAGE BODY hr.staffing AS
  FUNCTION promote(p_id IN NUMBER) RETURN t_employee IS
    l_row t_employee;
    l_ret t_employee;
  BEGIN
    SELECT id, name, level
      INTO l_row
      FROM employees
     WHERE id = p_id;
    l_ret.id    := l_row.id;
    l_ret.name  := l_row.name;
    l_ret.level := (l_row.level + 1);
    RETURN l_ret;
  EXCEPTION
    WHEN NO_DATA_FOUND THEN
      RAISE pell_runtime.hr_staffing_notfound;
  END promote;
END staffing;
/

What you get inside the IDE

  • Side-by-side split editor. Edit a .pell file, see the lowered PL/SQL update in real time on the right pane. Click a pub fn in the source → preview scrolls to the function body and highlights the line. ~400 ms debounce, error banner stays out of your way.
  • Gutter actions. Hammer icon on every .pell file: build, exec, parse, tokens, REPL. Play arrow on every .sql file: install on the connected Oracle. Works on IntelliJ Community — no Ultimate Database plugin required.
  • Embedded REPL. Notebook-style cells with variable persistence (auto-stringify, snapshot/replay across cells), \load a file into the session, full p() printing, catalog:: data dictionary helpers, and live SQL execution.
  • New Project wizard. File → New → Project → pell scaffolds src/hello.pell, tests/, plsql/ (committed!), a portable ./pell shim, and a one-click Deploy run configuration.
  • Tool window. Project module tree with per-row build/deploy state, build-all, deploy-all, install pell_runtime, open REPL, all wired to the connected Oracle.
  • LSP-backed intelligence. Pell-LSP via LSP4IJ — real-time diagnostics, hover, completion (keywords + project identifiers + dotted-method menus), go-to-definition, outline, dotted-symbol completion (catalog::columns_of suggests the right pre-existing methods on the returned list<ColumnInfo>).
  • Save-to-target-dir. Save the .pell → the lowered SQL is rewritten to plsql/<name>.sql with --reproducible on. Commit both files; git blame shows you exactly how each deployment artifact evolved.

Why pell exists

PL/SQL the language has aged in places that bite — verbose package/spec/body duplication, awkward error handling, no real type checking across boundaries, terrible string interpolation, no module system. But Oracle the database is excellent, and the runtime semantics of PL/SQL are uniquely powerful. Pell keeps the database, replaces the surface:

  • Generics & sum types (Result<T, E>, Option<T>, list<T>) that compile to the right PL/SQL collection / exception shapes.
  • Real string interpolation with auto-stringify for any type ("got {n} tables") — number, date, timestamp, json, list, record, all handled.
  • Embedded SQL via sql! { ... } with .one() / .collect() / .first() terminators that drive the right INTO clause shape.
  • JSON, regex, jq-style queries as first-class — Oracle 23ai JSON_OBJECT_T under the hood with no SELECT FROM dual ceremony.
  • The lowered PL/SQL is the deployment artifact: SHA- anchored, byte-stable with --reproducible, meant to be committed and reviewed.

Learn more

  • Docs & tutorial: batterts.github.io/pell
  • Examples (30+ .pell files with their compiled output): github.com/batterts/pell/tree/main/compiler/examples
  • Source / contributing: github.com/batterts/pell
  • Issues: github.com/batterts/pell/issues

Requires the pell CLI installed locally — the plugin shells out to it for compile, deploy, and REPL. Get it with pip install -e .[repl] from the repo, or open a new pell project in the wizard and it sets up a portable ./pell shim for you.

Keywords: PL/SQL, plsql, Oracle, Oracle database, Oracle 23ai, SQL, transpiler, statically-typed, modern PL/SQL.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.9.18 — grammar: null literal + default parameters

  • The editor now parses and highlights the new null literal and default parameter values (fn f(scope: text = "user")), matching the compiler — no more spurious red on either.

0.9.17 — qualified types in type position parse cleanly

  • The grammar only accepted a bare IDENT as a type, so a cross-package type like catalog::IndexDetail in a return/field/param position (e.g. catalog_all's -> catalog::IndexDetail) showed a spurious red syntax error. typeAtomBase now accepts IDENT (:: IDENT)*, matching the compiler.

0.9.16 — drop an internal-API call

  • The debugger printed its own plugin version in the startup banner, which required an internal API the Marketplace verifier rejects (and the public alternative was still flagged). Removed the plugin-version line — the IDE already shows it. The banner still prints the CLI path + version. No behavior change.

0.9.14 — preview survives lowered SQL containing a CR

  • Fixed the real cause of a preview stuck on "(compiling…)": lowered SQL can carry a raw carriage-return byte inside a string literal (e.g. the CSV library's "\r" for CRLF), and IntelliJ documents reject anything but \n separators — so setText threw "Wrong line separators" and the pane never updated. The preview now normalizes separators before display. Pair with the CLI, which now emits CR as CHR(13) rather than a raw byte (git/editor CRLF normalization could otherwise corrupt the deployed literal).

0.9.13 — preview can't get stuck on "(compiling…)"

  • The split-editor preview now has a 30s watchdog: if a pell build never returns (e.g. the project scan is walking a huge directory because the IDE root is a big parent folder), it's killed and the pane shows an actionable timeout instead of spinning forever.
  • A build that's cancelled mid-flight (superseded by a newer edit, or killed) now always resolves the preview exactly once — no more lost callbacks leaving the placeholder up.

0.9.12 — preview pane works for annotated modules

  • The split-editor preview now lowers a module via pell build even when the file opens with an annotation (e.g. @suite(…) above module …;, as every utPLSQL suite does). It previously checked only the first line, saw the annotation, treated the file as a script, and ran pell exec — which fails on a module. Module detection now matches a top-level module declaration anywhere, mirroring the CLI exactly.

0.9.11 — stop flagging Result<Unit, E> calls

  • The discarded-return inspection no longer false-positives on a function returning Result<Unit, E> called as a statement (e.g. enqueue_job("x")?; in a utPLSQL test). Such a function lowers to a PL/SQL procedure — the Ok carries no value, so there is nothing to discard and no PLS-00221. The inspection now mirrors the emitter exactly.

0.9.10 — query collections in the Evaluate box

  • The Evaluate box / watches now query a collection's debug shadow: rows[100].user_id, rows.where(user_id == 1).first().movie_id, rows.where(rating >= 5).collect(), rows.len(). Runs locally on the snapshot via pell debug-eval (no live frame access — Oracle doesn't allow it). The shadow now holds the whole array (up to ~30KB) with a truncation flag, not a 50-element sample. Pull the CLI for the emitter + engine half.

0.9.9 — collection/record values show via debug shadow

  • A list<Record> local (e.g. b2's rows) now shows its JSON debug shadow in the Variables view instead of "(opaque)". The shadow pairing was gated on the mirror type being exactly $Oracle.Builtin.OPAQUE (true for JSON), but a collection boxes under its own type name ($Oracle.PackageBody.S.PKG.T_X_LIST), so the shadow was never consulted. Now gated on "no readable scalar value", which covers JSON, collections, and records alike. Pairs with the emitter's collection JSON shadow (pull the CLI for that half).

0.9.8 — debug stubs build record arguments for you

  • A `pub fn` taking a record argument now generates a stub that binds the record first with a qualified struct literal — let args = mod::Rec { a: 1, b: "x", c: true }; mod::fn(args) — instead of an un-compilable /* TODO */ "" placeholder. Edit the placeholder field values and Debug.

0.9.7 — srcmap class match fix + debug diagnostics

  • Fixed PellSrcMap.matches() over-matching: it accepted nested types (record collection types like T_X_LIST) as breakpoint candidates, so the debugger could arm a breakpoint on a collection accessor — a debug-hostile spot inside a FORALL. Now only the exact package body / block class matches.
  • Debug start now prints the plugin + CLI version, the breakpoint candidate classes, and where each breakpoint is armed — so a pasted log pins down exactly what runs.

0.9.6 — ship the ClassPrepare fix for real (clean build)

  • 0.9.5 carried the FORALL/bulk ClassPrepare fix in source but an incremental build packaged a stale class, so installs still crashed. This is a clean rebuild that actually contains it. The debug console now prints ClassPrepare scoped to <class> so you can confirm the scoping is active.

0.9.5 — debug FORALL / bulk code without crashing the session

  • Fixed an Oracle ORA-00600 [15419] / PLS-707 that killed the debug session when stepping a unit containing a FORALL over a record collection (BULK COLLECT + forall). Root cause was a blanket all-classes ClassPrepare request: pell emits record collections as nested types that Oracle prepares lazily inside the FORALL, and delivering a prepare event for one mid-loop crashed the session. The debugger now scopes ClassPrepare to exactly the classes your breakpoints target, so those internal types prepare silently and the FORALL is fully steppable — a breakpoint after it is hit normally. (No code rewriting; this is how SQL Developer handles it.)

0.9.4 — friendlier utPLSQL setup

  • pell test now fails fast with install instructions (the headless SYSDBA one-liner) when utPLSQL isn't present on the database, instead of a cryptic PLS-00201.
  • New Settings → Tools → pell → utPLSQL schema field for the rare install that has no public synonyms — names the owner schema (e.g. UT3) so ut / ut_* get qualified. Plumbed as PELL_UT_SCHEMA; also available as pell test --ut-schema.

0.9.3 — utPLSQL "run test" gutter icons

  • A green run arrow now appears in the gutter next to the module keyword of any @suite module (runs the whole suite) and next to every @test pub fn (runs that single test). Backed by pell test → ut.run(...) against the deployed package. Suite names are derived from the module declaration (module hr::a.b.checks → hr.checks).
  • These stack with the existing per-pub fn Run/Debug stub icons, so a @test fn can be run as a utPLSQL test or stepped through via a generated stub.
  • Fixed a latent gutter-marker contract violation for .pell files whose first line is an annotation (e.g. @suite).

0.9.2 — breakpoints bind to the right anonymous block

  • Fixed breakpoints silently never firing in debug sessions: the dbms_debug_jdwp.connect_tcp call is itself an anonymous block, and at attach time it is the only $Oracle.Block class visible — breakpoints were armed against it, found "no code", and were permanently dropped before the real script block ever PREPAREd. Arming now tries every matching class and keeps breakpoints pending until a class that actually has code at the mapped line appears.
  • The compiler no longer stamps a source marker on the synthesized anon-block header line, so a breakpoint on the script's first statement maps to the statement itself.

0.9.1 — return-type-aware stubs + honest cross-schema deploys

  • Generated debug stubs respect the fn's return type: procedures and Result<Unit,…> fns are called without a bogus result binding; record/list returns bind for the Variables view without unsupported printing; scalar/json returns print as before.
  • Cross-package record returns now lower fully qualified (hr.staffing.t_employee) — stubs for record-returning fns compile.
  • Breakpoints landing on declaration lines snap forward to the next executable line instead of being dropped.
  • Compiler-side: pell deploy no longer reports ✓ when a cross-schema unit compiled with errors (it checked USER_ERRORS, which can't see other schemas) — this exposed and fixed 11 latently-broken examples, an emitter comment-placement bug in transaction blocks, and two examples whose module name collided with their table name (packages and tables share a namespace — now hr::staffing and inventory::stock).

0.9.0 — paired execution line in the split-view preview

  • While debugging, the split editor highlights both sides: XDebugger's band on the pell source and a matching band + gutter arrow on the lowered PL/SQL in the preview pane, stepping in lock-step. During the session the preview compiles with --debug so it shows exactly the deployed text (including the @pell line markers); it returns to the normal build when the session ends. Units without an open preview still fall back to a read-only ALL_SOURCE tab.

0.8.9 — readable values over JDWP, pell names, pell-sized steps

  • Scalar values now read correctly over JDWP. Oracle's variable mirrors carry the value in a _value field (they have no methods at all — the prior toString approach could never work). name = "world" instead of {opaque}.
  • Variables show pell names — name, not P_NAME; j, not L_J — on both transports.
  • Steps are pell-sized. One pell statement can lower to dozens of PL/SQL rows; step over/into/out now advance until the mapped pell line changes. Raw PL/SQL-granular stepping still applies automatically inside units with no pell source.
  • The execution marker in the deployed .sql gained a gutter arrow + guaranteed-visible band (some themes render the standard execution color background-less).

0.8.8 — module-less scripts are first-class

  • A .pell file without a module declaration is now a script (top-level statements — debug stubs, REPL snippets, pell exec files) everywhere: the PSI grammar accepts it (no more "module expected" red squiggles) and the LSP validates it through the same anonymous-block path pell exec uses. No marker annotation, no separate file extension — if it starts with module it's a package, otherwise it's a script. Restart the pell LSP server after updating.

0.8.7 — debugger restart + stub-preview fixes

  • Restarting a debug session on a pinned port no longer fails with "Already listening" — the stale listener is cleared and rebound.
  • Generated debug stubs (and other module-less scripts) now preview their lowered anonymous block instead of erroring with "expected module".
  • Breakpoints registered during debug startup are deferred until the line maps are built, instead of being dropped with a spurious "no line map" warning; breakpoints in files outside the session are noted once, quietly.

0.8.6 — see a function's return value before stepping out

  • At a return x; line, the Variables view now shows ↩ return with the value the function is about to return — inspect it before you step out. Debug builds capture bare-identifier returns into a readable shadow; works on both transports, including JSON and other opaque types.

0.8.5 — paired execution line in the lowered PL/SQL

  • While debugging, the deployed .sql opens beside your pell source (read-only) with the current execution line highlighted in sync — step on the left, watch the PL/SQL it became light up on the right. Works on both transports; clears on resume/stop. The .sql opens without stealing focus from the pell editor.

0.8.4 — JSON values are readable in the debugger

  • Opaque object locals now show their real value. Debug builds emit a VARCHAR2 shadow scalar for each opaque local (JSON to start) holding its stringified value — the one thing both Oracle debug APIs can read. A json local now shows {"name":"Alice",...} in the Variables view instead of <OPAQUE>, on both transports. The shadow and compiler temporaries stay hidden.

0.8.3 — cleaner debugger variables view

  • Compiler-internal temporaries (the l_pell_jobj_* JSON DOM scaffolding and friends) are hidden from the Variables view — you see your own locals, not emission internals.
  • Opaque object locals (JSON, JSON_OBJECT_T, collections, records) are now labeled by their type instead of a bare <OPAQUE>. Their values remain unreadable — that's an Oracle debug-API limitation (both JDWP and DBMS_DEBUG can only read scalar variables); to inspect a JSON value at a breakpoint, assign it to a text local.

0.8.2 — per-config environment variables + DB URL setting

  • Run configurations now have an Environment field (the standard env-vars editor) — set PELL_DB_URL per config to target different databases. Settings → Tools → pell also gained a project-default DB URL. Precedence: run-config env > settings DB URL > the IDE's inherited environment. Applies to exec/build runs and both debugger transports.

0.8.1 — debugger settings in the UI

  • Settings → Tools → pell now has the debugger knobs: transport (jdwp/sql), fixed JDWP listener port, and callback host — no more wrestling env vars into GUI-launched IDEs for reverse-tunnel setups. Env vars still work as fallback.

0.8.0 — SQL-transport debugging (outbound-only)

Debug with nothing but outbound database connections. Set PELL_DEBUG_TRANSPORT=sql and the debugger drives Oracle's Probe API (DBMS_DEBUG) over two ordinary SQL sessions — no JDWP listener, no network ACE, no inbound path. If pell exec works through your tunnel, debugging now does too. Module breakpoints, stepping, locals, and stack all work; script-level breakpoints remain a jdwp-transport feature. Needs only the DEBUG CONNECT SESSION grant.

0.7.2 — debug through SSH tunnels

  • Set PELL_DEBUG_JDWP_PORT to pin the IDE's JDWP listener port and PELL_DEBUG_CALLBACK_HOST=127.0.0.1 to debug across a reverse SSH tunnel (ssh -R 5005:localhost:5005 dbhost) — see docs/DEBUGGER.md. Also new: pell exec --trace, a zero-privilege line-by-line execution trace for users who can't get DEBUG CONNECT SESSION granted.

0.7.1 — debugger gutter fix

  • The per-fn run/debug gutter icon now actually appears on pub fn (0.7.0 looked for pub inside the fn node; it lives on the wrapping item).

0.7.0 — The pell debugger

Step through pell running inside Oracle. Built on DBMS_DEBUG_JDWP (the SQL Developer mechanism): the database session connects back to the IDE and the IDE drives it.

  • Breakpoints in .pell files — gutter breakpoints map through compiler line markers to the deployed PL/SQL and snap to the nearest statement.
  • Per-fn run/debug gutter actions — every pub fn gets "Debug" which generates an editable stub (.pell-debug/debug_<module>_<fn>.pell) calling it with placeholder args. Step through the stub AND the fn.
  • Falls through to PL/SQL — frames outside pell source (runtime packages, hand-written PL/SQL) open the deployed ALL_SOURCE read-only and stepping continues.
  • Variables view, stack, step over/into/out, console; uses PELL_DB_URL; needs DEBUG CONNECT SESSION + a JDWP network ACE (see docs/DEBUGGER.md).

0.6.1 — Extract Method works on loops and other nested-block statements

  • Extract a whole for/if/match statement. Selecting a complete loop no longer fails with "selection must lie inside a single block" — the analyzer now finds the deepest block containing the whole selection instead of comparing the endpoints' blocks (the closing } belongs to the nested body).
  • Loop variables are real declarations. Extracting from inside a loop body captures i as a typed parameter (number for range loops); extracting the whole loop correctly keeps i internal.

0.6.0 — Module access domains + smarter refactorings

The module hierarchy is now an access-control boundary, enforced by Oracle itself. Plus refactoring polish across the board.

  • New module naming: module schema::a.b.c; — the schema gets its own ::-separated slot; the dotted path is unambiguously the package name (lowered to schema.a_b_c). No more "is the first segment a schema?" ambiguity.
  • Access domains. Non-root modules (app.parsing) emit ACCESSIBLE BY (…) listing every other package in their domain — Oracle rejects outside callers (PLS-00904), and pell rejects them earlier at compile time with a clear message. Root modules are the public interface. @open opts a module out.
  • Move Symbol rewrites references project-wide: qualified callers flip to the new module, bare uses in the old home get qualified, and missing imports are added.
  • Extract Method infers param types from the captured locals' declarations — no more any params that fail at deploy.
  • Editor grammar parity: schema:: module declarations, dotted imports (import app.parsing;), and module-level annotations (@stub, @open) all parse without squiggles. Parser snapshot tests are now committed so grammar drift fails CI.

0.5.3 — Range expressions in the editor

The Grammar-Kit grammar now accepts range expressions (for i in 1..=10, for i in 0..5) and for-over-list-literal (for x in [1, 2, 3]) — the compiler already lowered these; the IDE parser had been red-squiggling them. Grammar + Python parser are back in sync.

0.5.2 — Refactorings actually work now

The PSI refactoring + navigation stack is real. Every feature below is covered by headless platform tests that run the true IntelliJ pipelines (ReferencesSearch, rename, extract), so they don't silently rot.

  • Find Usages works — same-file and across files. The root cause was deep: Grammar-Kit's generated PSI elements aren't ContributedReferenceHost, so the reference contributor's references were silently dropped. References are now attached via getReference() mixins, which the platform consults unconditionally.
  • All five refactorings work and appear in the Refactor menu:
    • Rename — declaration + every call site, same-file and cross-file (needed ElementManipulators).
    • Extract Method — captures inputs as params AND outputs: a local declared in the selection but used afterwards is returned from the new fn and rebound at the call site.
    • Parameters → Record — synthesizes the record, rewrites the signature + body refs + call sites.
    • Move Symbol — moves the declaration (with its leading pub / annotations) to another module.
    • Inline and Change Signature.
    Extract Method is now wired through a real RefactoringSupportProvider; the four action refactorings got the required getActionUpdateThread() so they show on modern IntelliJ.
  • Go-to-definition lands the cursor on the symbol name, not the leading fn/record keyword — so a follow-up Find Usages resolves correctly.
  • Cross-package records resolve from the REPL and pell exec the same as in a build, including dotted modules referred to by their short name.

0.4.1 — Parsed-lookup index (O(1) symbol resolution)

Performance + architecture cleanup. Every symbol lookup (inspections, refactorings, completion, references) now goes through one project-level facade PellSymbolService, backed by an in-memory index (PellProjectIndex) refreshed by a VFS listener. Replaces the per-query PsiTreeUtil walk that landed in 0.4.0 — same behaviour, O(1) lookups instead of O(project · file).

  • New facade. PellSymbolService is the single API every PSI consumer talks to. Returns rich PellSymbolInfo records (name, qualified name, kind, structured PellType, params, fields, source, PSI location). L3 will wire stdlib symbols (catalog::*, logger::*, p) into the same facade via a custom LSP method; no consumer change needed.
  • Sealed type hierarchy. PellType.parse() recognises every pell type form — primitives, list<T>, Result<T, E>, T?, T | U, named user types — and renders them back via displayName() for completion popup "type" labels and inspection messages.
  • Cached index, refreshed by VFS listener. PellProjectIndex indexes every project .pell file at first read and incrementally reindexes any file the IDE writes / creates / moves / deletes. Lives in memory; rebuilds on project open. Real disk-persistent StubIndex is the v0.5.0 upgrade if the in-memory rebuild ever feels heavy.
  • Internal: PellSymbolScanner deleted — PellProjectIndex is the new home for project-wide lookup. PellReferenceContributor, PellInlineAction, PellMoveSymbolAction, PellParamsToRecordHandler all routed through the new index. No user-visible API or UI change.

0.4.0 — Real PSI parser + refactorings

Big release. Pell gets a real IntelliJ-native PSI layer alongside the existing LSP. The LSP still drives diagnostics + hover; the PSI layer drives navigation, refactoring, structure view, and a growing set of inspections and intentions. The two are designed to co-exist.

  • Grammar-Kit + JFlex parser. Full port of the Python parser/lexer (1100+ lines of pell grammar) to Java/Kotlin so IntelliJ has a real AST to reason about, not just LSP-shaped diagnostics. Structure View (Cmd-7) now renders module / fn / record / error / type / enum / aggregate / seq children as real PSI elements.
  • Cross-file navigation. Cmd-Click on a pell symbol jumps to its declaration anywhere in the project. Cmd-Opt-O (Go To Symbol) lists every pub fn / record / type / enum across the project. Cmd-G (Find Usages) shows every call site of the symbol under the caret, traversing module boundaries.
  • Rename refactoring. Shift-F6 on any pell name — fn, record, error, type, enum, field, param, let, loop variable — propagates the rename through every reference in the project atomically. Names are validated against pell's keyword set before the rewrite commits.
  • Extract Method. Select a contiguous stmt run inside a fn body → Refactor → Extract Method. The new pub fn (or private fn) lands after the enclosing fn; captured locals become parameters; the selection becomes a call site. Won't extract selections that contain a return mixed with other stmts (refuses with a clear message).
  • Parameters to Record. Caret in a fn → Refactor This → Parameters to Record. Synthesizes a pub record <FnName>Args, rewrites the fn's signature to a single args: FnNameArgs parameter, rewrites parameter references in the body to args.<name>, and rewrites every call site to the struct-literal form.
  • Move to Module / Inline / Change Signature. Three more refactorings under Refactor This, working against any top-level pub declaration.
  • Generate menu (Cmd-N). Three pell-specific templates:
    • Field — add a field to a record (with a chooser when the caret isn't already inside one).
    • CRUD for record — pick a record, get select_* / insert_* / update_* / delete_* fns with sql!{ } bodies, plus a matching pub error <Record>NotFound.
    • Aggregate skeleton — full state / step / merge / finish ODCI aggregate body with sensible accumulator stubs.
  • Alt-Enter intentions. On a bare expression-statement like user_tables();:
    • Introduce local variable → let result = user_tables();
    • Assign to local variable → let result: list<text> = user_tables();
    • Wrap in for-loop → for row in user_tables() { /* TODO */ }
  • Inspection: discarded function return value. Yellow squiggle on bare-call statements where the callee is a project fn with a non-Unit return type — the edit-time defense for the PLS-00221 pattern. Resolution is qualifier-aware (logger::info(x); only fires if a project module logger; defines info with a return type), and skips procedures (no -> T clause), built-ins (p(), dbms_output::*, catalog::*), and member-access calls (obj.method() — type inference comes next release).
  • Completion popup is richer. Ctrl-Space now lists pell primitive types (number, text, bool, date, timestamp, interval, bytes, json, Unit, bigtext, int) first, then keywords, then project pub fns + records, then in-scope locals. Coexists with the LSP4IJ completion feed.

Coexistence with LSP4IJ: diagnostics, hover, and existing LSP-side completion continue to work as before. Phase L1+L2 of the LSP_PSI_UNIFICATION.md plan will unify the two stacks via a single PellSymbolService facade backed by a StubIndex, replacing the current PsiTreeUtil walks with O(1) lookups.

0.3.13

  • One-click pell install + first-launch detection. Project open now probes for a working pell CLI on $PELL_HOME, the project shim, and $PATH. If none is found, a friendly notification surfaces with an "Install pell" button that jumps to Settings → Tools → pell, where the CLI status row + an Install button live.
  • The Install button runs pip install --user "pell[repl]" in a background task and notifies on success / failure. On macOS / Linux this leaves pell in ~/.local/bin (Python user-base) — restart the IDE after install so the updated PATH is picked up.

0.3.12

  • Rewritten Marketplace description — opens with a side-by-side `.pell` → emitted PL/SQL example so people searching plsql / Oracle see the lowering immediately. Links to docs, examples repo, and source. No behavior change in the IDE itself; the rest of the 0.3.x line ships as-is.

0.3.11

  • "Run preview on PELL_DB_URL" can no longer fire on a broken preview. Three layered defenses:
    1. The error preview body is fully `-- `-prefixed, so even if you shell ./pell sql on the temp file by hand, Oracle sees a comment block — no ORA-00900 on path strings.
    2. The gutter Run icon is removed when the preview is showing an error, not just when there's a good compile.
    3. Defensive bail in runOnPellDbUrl(): if the preview isn't currently showing valid compiled PL/SQL, surface an IntelliJ notification ("preview isn't a valid compile yet") instead of writing garbage to a temp file.
    Fixes the symptom of [1/2] /Users/.../pell FAIL — ORA-00900 that you'd see if you ran the gutter icon on a broken preview.

0.3.10

  • Caret-sync lands on the body, not the spec. Click pub fn greet(...) in the source and the preview now scrolls to FUNCTION greet IS / BEGIN inside PACKAGE BODY — where the code lives — instead of the signature line in the spec. Search begins at the CREATE OR REPLACE PACKAGE BODY marker and matches the `IS`-prefixed body shape.
  • Highlighted target line. The line you jumped to is now painted with the IDE's caret-row background color so your eye finds it immediately. Only one line is highlighted at a time; the previous mark clears on the next nav (and when the preview re-compiles).

0.3.9

  • plsql/ everywhere. The build-output dir is now `plsql/` by default (was `built/`) — the lowered SQL is the deployment artifact, meant to be committed and git-blamed, not hidden away as ephemeral build output.
    • New Project wizard scaffolds plsql/.gitkeep instead of built/, and the .gitignore no longer excludes it.
    • Tool window's Build / Run SQL / Install runtime buttons all honor Settings → Tools → pell → "Target directory".
    • Module-state scan looks at both the configured target dir AND the legacy built/, so pre-existing projects keep working until migrated.
  • New CLI: pell migrate — idempotent helper for existing projects. pell migrate renames built/ → plsql/ and drops the corresponding .gitignore entry. Dry-run with --dry-run first to preview.
  • pell deploy default output dir is now plsql/. Override with --out-dir if you've kept the legacy name.

0.3.8

  • Save-to-target-dir wired up. When you save a .pell file (Cmd-S), the plugin now runs ./pell build <source> -o <targetDir>/<name>.sql and refreshes the VFS so the file pops into the project tree. The committed PL/SQL artifact stays in lockstep with the authored .pell. Target directory configured in Settings → Tools → pell (default plsql). Hook: VFS_CHANGES → VFileContentChangeEvent on the source file. Async — doesn't block the save callback. Failures are silent (the preview pane already shows compile errors).

0.3.7

  • Project settings (Settings → Tools → pell) with one knob today: Target directory (where the lowered PL/SQL is written / read by pell deploy). Default plsql; you can pick sql, built, or anything else. Persisted per-project in .idea/pell.xml. Setting is in place; the IntelliJ flows that write output will pick it up in the next iteration.

0.3.6

  • Caret sync between source and preview. Click on pub fn greet(...) in the .pell source and the preview scrolls to FUNCTION greet. Works for fn / record / type / error / aggregate / enum / sealed declarations. Name-based mapping (no source-map yet); good enough for most navigation.
  • .pell gutter menu trimmed. Removed Run pell build and Run pell build → file — the split-editor preview already shows the lowered PL/SQL live, so these were just noise. Menu is now: exec, exec (dry-run), Open REPL, parse (debug), tokens (debug).

0.3.5

  • The .pell gutter icon is now a hammer (compile), not a play arrow (run). A .pell file's primary action is build — `pell build` compiles to PL/SQL — not execution. The play arrow is now exclusive to the preview pane's "Run on PELL_DB_URL" button (which actually does execute). The dropdown items in the .pell gutter are unchanged.

0.3.4

  • Run-on-PELL_DB_URL gutter button in the PL/SQL preview pane. The split editor's right-hand preview now has a green-play gutter icon on line 1. Click it to install the currently-displayed PL/SQL against the connected database — no need to save the .pell, no need to open a terminal. The plugin writes the in-memory preview to a temp .sql, opens a terminal tab, and runs ./pell sql with the output streaming inline. Reinstalls on every successful re-compile, so you always run the latest lowering.

0.3.3

  • Clears all Marketplace verifier warnings: replaces three deprecated / internal API usages with their stable successors.
    • TerminalToolWindowManager.createLocalShellWidget(...) → createShellWidget(cwd, name, focus, defer) + TerminalWidget.sendCommandToExecute(...)
    • StartupManager.runAfterOpened(...) (internal) → scaffold directly in generateProject
    • ProjectGeneratorPeer.getComponent() override (deprecated) removed; settings go through buildUI(SettingsStep) only
    • DirectoryProjectGenerator.getLogo() → getIcon()
    • SyntaxHighlighterFactory.LANGUAGE_FACTORY.forLanguage(...) → SyntaxHighlighterFactory.getSyntaxHighlighter(lang, ...)
    • LightVirtualFile from testFramework (internal) — no longer needed; SQL highlighter built directly via the language-aware factory
    • PsiAwareTextEditorProvider() ctor (internal) → TextEditorProvider.getInstance()
    No user-visible behavior change — same UI, same flows, but the binary is now forward-compatible with 2025.x and 2026.x EAPs without verifier warnings.

0.3.2

  • Preview no longer flickers while you type. When the source has incomplete syntax (mid-typing pub fn foo(), the PL/SQL preview now stays frozen on the last successful compile. A red banner above the preview surfaces the compile error — no more blanking out and re-rendering on every keystroke.

0.3.1

  • Plugin ID renamed from dev.pell.intellij to dev.pell. JetBrains Marketplace rejects IDs containing the word "intellij" — required for the first public submission. If you installed 0.3.0 manually, uninstall it before installing 0.3.1 (different ID means the IDE treats them as separate plugins).

0.3.0

  • Side-by-side pell ↔ PL/SQL split editor. Opening any .pell file now shows the source on the left and a live PL/SQL preview on the right (Markdown-style). Recompiles debounced (~400ms) as you type. Toggle text-only / split / preview-only via the icons in the editor's top-right corner — same UI as the Markdown plugin. Preview gets SQL syntax highlighting when available. Compile errors render in the preview pane with header + stderr.

0.2.4

  • Build / install pell_runtime from the tool window. Two new toolbar buttons:
    • Build pell_runtime.sql — aggregates every pell error declared in the project into built/pell_runtime.sql.
    • Install pell_runtime on PELL_DB_URL — same build, then installs the generated SQL against the connected database. Fires the install only if the build half exited 0.
    Previously this only happened as a side-effect of Deploy all when at least one module referenced pell_runtime.<exception>. Standalone access makes the workflow explicit.

0.2.3

  • Tool window now falls back to project.basePath when the project has no modules / no content roots. Fixes the empty-tree case for brand-new IDEA projects created via the New Project wizard, where IDEA doesn't auto-create a module — the previous code iterated zero roots and found zero files even though the scaffold was on disk.

0.2.2

  • Tool window auto-refreshes when .pell or .sql files appear or disappear under the project's content roots. Fixes the empty-tree case in brand-new projects: the wizard's scaffold writes files after the tool window's initial scan, so the tree used to be empty until the user clicked Refresh. Now the VFS subscription catches the post-startup writes and the tree populates without a click.

0.2.1

  • New Project entry now actually shows up in IntelliJ IDEA. 0.2.0 used <directoryProjectGenerator> which only surfaces in PyCharm / WebStorm / RubyMine / DataGrip. IDEA's Generators list reads from <moduleBuilder> with a GeneratorNewProjectWizardBuilderAdapter (same surface Maven Archetype uses). Now registered both ways so the "pell" entry appears in every JetBrains IDE.

0.2.0

  • Tool window: new "pell" tab on the right strip with a module tree (per-row build/deploy state), toolbar (Build, Build all, Run SQL, Deploy all, Open REPL, Open source, Open built SQL), and a streaming log panel.
  • Open pell REPL gutter action — opens IntelliJ's terminal and auto-\\loads the current .pell file into a fresh session.
  • Run SQL gutter on .sql files — uses the pell driver instead of Ultimate's Database plugin.
  • New Project wizard: File → New → Project → pell scaffolds a complete starter project with the ./pell wrapper, src/, built/, and a Deploy all run config.
  • Build-arg ordering fixed for pell build -o (file before flag, matches the CLI).

0.1.0

  • Initial run-configuration type and gutter-icon popup (exec / build / parse / tokens).
  • .pell file-type registration.
  • LSP4IJ wiring for diagnostics / hover / outline.

JetBrains language support for the Chicken esoteric programming language.

Provides .chicken file recognition, syntax highlighting, and a bundled Chicken runner.

Language support for Tengo, a small, dynamic, fast, secure scripting language embeddable in Go applications.

idea-plugin.name: Kusto Hero
idea-plugin.description:
Kusto Hero is an IntelliJ Platform plugin for Kusto Query Language (KQL), the language used by Azure Data Explorer, Microsoft Fabric, Azure Monitor, Microsoft Sentinel, and related Microsoft services.

The plugin provides IntelliJ-native KQL editing support with syntax highlighting, parsing, navigation, completion, formatting, documentation, inspections, and optional project-local schema metadata through optional .kusto/schema.json.

Features

  • .kql, compatibility .csl, and common .kusto file support.
  • Completion for statements, pipe operators, symbols, functions, operator parameters.
  • Navigation, rename/find usages, documentation, parameter info, inspections, quick fixes, intentions.
  • Optional project-local schema support for tables, columns, materialized views, functions, and query parameters.

Support

Please report bugs and feature requests in the issue tracker.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Initial Kusto Hero language support for .kql, .csl, and .kusto files.
  • GrammarKit/JFlex lexer and parser with PSI, parser recovery, and curated corpus tests.
  • Syntax highlighting, commenter, brace/quote handling, folding, breadcrumbs, structure view, formatter, and code style settings.
  • Completion, navigation, rename/find usages, documentation, parameter info, inspections, quick fixes, intentions, and language injections.
  • Optional project-local .kusto/schema.json support for schema-aware code insight.
  • Kusto live templates, file templates, plugin/file icons, and marketplace verification wiring.

idea-plugin.name: Wiremark
idea-plugin.description:
Sketch user interfaces as plain text and see them rendered as hand-drawn, Balsamiq-style wireframes right inside your IDE. Wiremark brings wiremark — a concise, markdown-embeddable wireframing format (think "YAML-flavored Material UI") — to IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, and every other JetBrains IDE.

It renders wiremark in two places:

  • Standalone *.wiremark files open in a split text-and-preview editor with a live, hand-drawn SVG that updates as you type — the same editing experience the IDE gives Markdown and SVG files.
  • Fenced code blocks in Markdown. A ```wireframe (or ```wiremark) block in any .md file renders as a wireframe in the Markdown preview, exactly the way Mermaid diagrams do.

Wireframes are written by indentation, so they read like an outline and diff cleanly in version control. Multi-frame files automatically render as a flow chart, with connectors drawn between screens you link with to=#id. Rendering happens entirely inside the IDE — no Node.js, no external tools, and no network calls.

New to the format? The wiremark documentation has the language guide, component reference, and icon gallery. The engine is open source at github.com/Blackburn-Labs/wiremark.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Theme-aware preview: the rendered wireframe now follows the active IDE theme, displaying with a dark palette under dark IDE themes instead of always rendering on a light card. This applies to both the *.wiremark split editor and the Markdown preview, and re-renders live when you switch the IDE look-and-feel. (Completes the dark-theme support anticipated in 0.1.1, now that the bundled engine's theme render option is wired to IDE-theme detection.)
  • Cross-block backgrounds in the Markdown preview: a Wireframe ... background=#id in one fenced wiremark / wireframe block can now use a wireframe declared in a different block of the same document as its background (and resolve an anchor=#id against it). Previously each fence rendered in isolation, so such a reference produced a "background frame not found" warning and rendered without the background. Self-contained documents are unaffected and render exactly as before.

Changed

  • Updated the bundled @wiremark/core rendering engine to 0.0.7 (adds keyless Wireframe direction such as Wireframe ... row, plus new components and connector-routing/spacing refinements).

idea-plugin.name: Affogato
idea-plugin.description:
Language support for Affogato (.aff) source files.

  • Syntax highlighting, formatting, and brace matching
  • Completion, navigation, find usages, and rename
  • Compiler diagnostics via the Affogato transpiler
  • Run configurations for Affogato main entry points

Requires the bundled Java and Gradle IntelliJ plugins. Targets IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1 and newer.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Test release.

idea-plugin.name: balsa-tml
idea-plugin.description:
IntelliJ IDEA plugin that provides language support for TML (Typhoon Modeling Language) — a DSL used for defining simulation components in the Typhoon HIL toolchain.

Language features are powered by a bundled LSP server (tml-lsp) written in Rust.

Features

  • Syntax highlighting — semantic token-based coloring for keywords, variables, functions, types, namespaces and constants
  • Diagnostics — real-time error reporting for undefined variables, undefined functions, duplicate declarations, empty bodies, and namespace violations
  • Hover — type and scope information on hover over variables and function calls
  • Go to definition — navigate to variable declarations and function definitions; supports multiple results for overloaded functions
  • Document highlight — highlights matching keyword pairs (fn/end, if/end, for/end, etc.)
  • Code folding — fold functions, if/elseif/else blocks, for/while loops, and macro constructs
  • Formatting — full document formatting and on-type formatting
  • Code completion — context-aware snippets for TML constructs
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • LSP server version management: download, switch between, and remove installed tml-lsp versions from Settings → Tools → TML Language Server
  • Automatic check for new tml-lsp releases on IDE startup, with a notification offering to download and install (or just download) the update
  • Manual "Check for Updates" action in the TML Language Server settings panel
  • Both Windows and Linux tml-lsp binaries are downloaded together on update, so the installed version works regardless of platform
  • Bundled tml-lsp binary is auto-discovered and registered as the active version on first run, avoiding a false "update available" notification

Changed

  • LSP server binary resolution now goes through the version manager instead of a single hardcoded path

idea-plugin.name: Hoverfly
idea-plugin.description:
Language support for Hoverfly simulation files.

Adds diagnostics, completions, hover documentation, and semantic highlighting for Hoverfly JSON simulation files (*.hoverfly.json, *.hfy, hoverfly-simulation.json) in any JetBrains IDE, including the free Community edition.

The Hoverfly language server is bundled with this plugin and started automatically — no manual LSP configuration is required. A Node.js runtime (20+) must be available; it is auto-detected from common locations, or set the HOVERFLY_LSP_NODE environment variable to point at a specific node binary.

Powered by the @jterrazz/hoverfly-lsp language server and LSP4IJ (auto-installed).

  • Diagnostics for invalid simulation structure and fields
  • Completion for matchers, fields, and known enums
  • Hover documentation
  • Semantic-token highlighting (including Handlebars templates)
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.1 — Packaging fix: remove internal API usage (server resolved via classpath resource) and raise compatibility floor to 2025.2.

0.1.0 — First release: diagnostics, completion, hover, and semantic highlighting for Hoverfly simulation files.

idea-plugin.name: BoxBreaker (BBK)
idea-plugin.description:
BoxBreaker (BBK) adds full BBK language support to IntelliJ IDEA and other JetBrains-platform IDEs.

BBK es un lenguaje estructurado de estilo libre, heredero del RPG free-format, pensado para escribirse y leerse como código moderno. Este plugin aporta una experiencia de edición de primera clase:

  • Resaltado de sintaxis y emparejado de llaves.
  • Autocompletado sensible al contexto (palabras clave, declaraciones visibles, miembros de estructuras de datos).
  • Plantillas dinámicas (live templates) para las construcciones más comunes.
  • Resolución de referencias: ir a la declaración, buscar usos y navegación entre archivos mediante índices del proyecto.
  • Refactorización Rename con validación de identificadores.
  • Inspecciones con conocimiento de tipos: incompatibilidades en asignaciones, retornos, argumentos y valores INZ; condiciones que no son BOOL; referencias sin resolver.
  • Información de parámetros (Ctrl+P) y documentación rápida (Ctrl+Q).
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.0

  • Primera versión pública.
  • Resaltado de sintaxis, emparejado de llaves y tipado inteligente.
  • Autocompletado sensible al contexto y plantillas dinámicas.
  • Resolución de referencias entre archivos, búsqueda de usos y refactorización Rename.
  • Siete inspecciones con conocimiento de tipos.
  • Información de parámetros y documentación rápida.

idea-plugin.name: Thrift Hero
idea-plugin.description:
Thrift Hero adds first-class support for Apache Thrift IDL to IntelliJ IDEA and other JetBrains IDEs.

Installation

Once you install the plugin, .thrift files open with IntelliJ-native Thrift language support.

Features

  • Syntax highlighting, parsing, folding, structure view, breadcrumbs, spellchecking, and code style settings.
  • Completion, quick docs, and parameter info for Thrift keywords, types, annotations, namespaces, containers, fields, constants, and services.
  • Go to Definition, Find Usages, Rename, and include-aware navigation for local and imported Thrift symbols.
  • Formatting, live templates, file templates, intentions, comments, and typing helpers for IDL authoring.
  • Inspections for include unresolved or duplicate symbols, const/default type issues, legacy syntax, and more.

Support

The plugin is new, so feedback is especially useful. Please report bugs and feature requests in the issue tracker.

  • Syntax highlighting, parsing, folding, structure view, breadcrumbs,
  • Spellchecking, typing helpers, live templates, file templates, formatting, and code style settings.
  • Completion, quick docs, parameter info, navigation,

idea-plugin.name: Solidity Pro
idea-plugin.description:
Solidity support for JetBrains IDEs, focused on productive smart contract development and audit review.

The plugin provides Solidity and Yul syntax support, parsing, highlighting, formatting, completion, navigation, refactoring, documentation, parameter hints, live templates, and project-aware imports.

Built-in inspections cover correctness, security, gas optimization, naming, NatSpec/source compliance, ERC compatibility, visibility, unresolved symbols, unused elements, and common Solidity pitfalls.

Tooling integrations include Foundry and Hardhat project workflows, Forge test run configurations, Solidity breaking-change migrations, solc compiler tooling, Solhint and Slither diagnostics, LSP4IJ language-server support, DAP-based Solidity/EVM debugging, storage-layout analysis, audit reports, and Etherscan import, flatten, and verification workflows.

Solidity Pro builds on the excellent foundation laid by the original IntelliJ Solidity plugin and its contributors. We are grateful for the substantial work that established Solidity support across JetBrains IDEs.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changed

  • Updated the plugin description to acknowledge the original IntelliJ Solidity plugin and the foundation its contributors provided.

Fixed

  • Restored the original author's MIT attribution and now include the license in every plugin distribution.
  • Import optimization now preserves required imports when dependency roots such as node_modules are excluded from IDE indexes.

idea-plugin.name: COBOL
idea-plugin.description:
The complete COBOL & mainframe IDE for IntelliJ

Turn IntelliJ IDEA, and any IntelliJ-based IDE, into a first-class workbench for COBOL, JCL, DB2 and CICS. Stop reading legacy code in a green-screen emulator and a plain text editor. Get the same rich editing, navigation, refactoring and diagnostics you already expect from modern languages — now for the code that runs the world's banks, insurers and governments.

Built on a native parser with deep understanding of fixed-form and free-form COBOL, this plugin doesn't just color your code — it understands it.

Write and read COBOL with confidence

  • Fast, accurate syntax highlighting for COBOL, embedded EXEC SQL (DB2), EXEC CICS and many vendor dialects (BMS, ACU, ILE and more).
  • Fixed-form aware editing — column area shading, smart TAB stops that snap to Area A / Area B, hyphen-aware word selection, quote & brace matching.
  • Code folding and a live Structure view for divisions, sections, paragraphs and data hierarchies — navigate thousand-line programs in seconds.
  • Rich inline documentation on hover for intrinsic functions, vendor APIs, data items (with PICTURE/VALUE), files, paragraphs, copybooks, hex literals and DB2 cursor lifecycles.

Navigate decades-old code like it's yours

  • Go to Declaration from any PERFORM / GO TO to its paragraph, and from CALL 'PGM' straight to the called program.
  • Go to Symbol across the whole project — every PROGRAM-ID, paragraph, section and data item.
  • Call Hierarchy, Find Usages and Code Vision usage counts above every paragraph and data item show you the blast radius before you touch a thing.
  • Cross-file gutter links wire together COPY → copybook, CALL → program, and COBOL ASSIGN ↔ JCL DD.

Catch bugs before the compiler — or production — does

  • 130+ built-in inspections covering control flow (dead code, undefined targets, orphan scope terminators, recursive PERFORM), data definitions (REDEFINES overflow, illegal OCCURS, malformed PICTURE), file I/O (unclosed files, mode mismatches, missing keys), tables and subscripts, arithmetic and MOVE truncation/overflow, conditionals, obsolete language elements, and more.
  • Deep DB2 / EXEC SQL analysis — cursor lifecycle (DECLARE→OPEN→FETCH→CLOSE), host-variable resolution, WHERE-less UPDATE/DELETE, positioned-update safety, SELECT * and duplicate-include warnings.
  • CICS validation — HANDLE targets, missing PROGRAM operands, and CICS+SQL transaction conflicts.
  • Optional live compiler linting for instant, on-keystroke feedback.

Refactor and modernize without fear

  • Safe rename for paragraphs and data names, Extract paragraph / section / copybook.
  • Source-format conversion between fixed, free and variable form, plus an expanded (COPY-resolved) read-only view.
  • Bulk cleanups — case normalization for keywords, fields and PERFORM targets; renumber / unnumber sequence areas; align data; pad, indent and strip comments.

First-class JCL & z/OS workflow

  • JCL as a real language — highlighting, parsing, Structure view, folding, completion for EXEC PGM / DD, and navigation from a step straight into the COBOL program or included member.
  • SYSPRINT / JES log triage — parse compiler and job output into clickable, navigable diagnostics.
  • Mainframe-ready file templates for plain, CICS and z/OS programs.

Understand whole systems, not just files

  • 50+ analysis actions — program metrics, cyclomatic & cognitive complexity, control-flow and data-flow graphs, PERFORM and CALL graphs, record layouts with byte offsets, table and file inventories, copybook dependency graphs and cross-references.
  • Project-wide insight — cross-file call graphs, duplicate PROGRAM-ID detection, SQL table and cursor inventories.
  • Export everything to HTML, Markdown, CSV, JSON or XML for reviews, audits and documentation.

Compile, run and debug locally

  • One-click run configurations — compile and execute right from the editor with a green gutter icon on your PROGRAM-ID.
  • Full source-level debugging — line breakpoints, stepping and variable inspection, so you can debug COBOL without ever leaving the IDE.

Whether you're maintaining a 40-year-old core-banking system, onboarding a new generation of developers, or migrating off the mainframe, this plugin gives your team a modern, productive home for COBOL. Install it today and feel the difference on your very first program.

idea-plugin.name: Maude Language Support
idea-plugin.description:
Language support for the Maude system.
  • All IDEs: syntax highlighting, code folding, brace matching, and comment toggling for .maude files.
  • Diagnostics, go-to-definition, hover and completion via the bundled Maude language server. These activate in IDEs that include the LSP API (paid IDEs such as IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate) and require Node.js and the maude executable on your PATH.

0.1.0 — Initial release: highlighting, folding, and (in paid IDEs) LSP diagnostics, go-to-definition, hover, and completion.

idea-plugin.name: Batch Files Support (.bat/.cmd)
idea-plugin.description:
Windows Batch (.bat / .cmd) language support for JetBrains IDEs.

A lightweight, actively-maintained plugin that recognizes Batch files and adds syntax highlighting for:

  • Comments — REM and ::
  • Keywords — echo, set, if, for, goto, call, and more
  • Labels — :label
  • Quoted strings

Works in the current IntelliJ-based IDEs (IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, and others). Free and open — more features are planned based on your feedback.

idea-plugin.name: Pyfun
idea-plugin.description:
Language support for Pyfun, an F#-inspired, functional-first language that compiles to readable Python.

Diagnostics, hover types & effects, go-to-definition, rename, and completion via the bundled pyfun lsp language server (install with pip install pyfun-lang), plus TextMate syntax highlighting.

idea-plugin.name: Promela
idea-plugin.description:
The plugin adds support for the Promela language and the Spin model checker.

Features:

  • Coding assistance (highlighting, context-aware completion, formatting, etc.)
  • Navigation and search (jump to declarations, find usages, structure view, documentation)
  • Verification and simulation (integrated Spin execution via Run Configurations)
  • State automata rendering for opened models
  • Partial support for preprocessor directives in Promela source doe (#include not included)

Getting Started

  1. Install a compatible JetBrains IDE, such as IntelliJ IDEA (2026.1+)
  2. Ensure the Spin binary and a C compiler are installed on your system
  3. Launch the IDE, search for "Promela" in plugin settings, and click install

Spin integration

To make use of Spin-related features (automata, simulation/verification runs). Modules containing Promela files must have sdk set to "Spin SDK" and must be located inside a source content root.

idea-plugin.name: HOCON Support
idea-plugin.description:
Language support for HOCON (Human-Optimized Config Object Notation) — the Typesafe/Lightbend Config format used by application.conf, Akka, Play, Kora and others.

Features

  • Quick file jumping — Ctrl-click / ⌘B on the path in {% render %}, {% include %}, {% section %} or {% block %} opens the referenced file

idea-plugin.name: Quarkdown
idea-plugin.description:
An IntelliJ IDEA plugin that provides comprehensive support for Quarkdown language syntax with .qd files,
enabling developers to write and edit Quarkdown documents with full IDE assistance.

Features & Advantages

Writing & Editing

  • Full Syntax Highlighting — Every Quarkdown directive and Markdown element is color-highlighted in the editor, using a dedicated color scheme you can fully customize to suit your taste.
  • Smart Code Completion — As you type, get instant suggestions for functions, parameters, and file paths, together with documentation tooltips and parameter hints so you can write faster and more accurately.
  • Real-time Error Detection — Unknown functions, invalid parameters, missing arguments, and undefined references are flagged in the editor the moment they appear, so problems are caught before they reach the final document.
  • Effortless Navigation — Jump from a reference to its definition, find every usage of a label, rename it everywhere at once, and navigate into included or referenced files with a single click.
  • Document Overview — A structure view and breadcrumbs show the outline of chapters, tables, and images, while code folding lets you collapse long sections for focused editing.

Smart Editing

  • Visual Table Editing — Insert, remove, move, select, and align table rows and columns from floating handles and a toolbar, without ever touching the raw table syntax.
  • Convenient Image Handling — Drag and drop or paste images directly into the document; the correct syntax is generated for you, image sizes can be adjusted visually, and invalid paths are called out.
  • Effortless Formatting — Reformat documents and code blocks with proper rules, comment lines quickly with a shortcut, and enjoy auto-closing of paired symbols such as {}, [], and quotes.
  • Handy Formatting Shortcuts — Commonly used operations such as bold, italic, strikethrough, code blocks, links, images, and tables are just one keypress away, making formatting quick and effortless.
  • File Assistance — Path completion and existence checks for includes, stylesheets, code files, images, and cross-references help you wire documents together without typos.
  • Live Word Count — A word and paragraph counter in the status bar keeps track of your progress as you write (excluding function calls and code blocks).

Preview & Build

  • Quick Preview Panel — A fast preview panel right inside the IDE that refreshes automatically whenever you save, letting you see the rendered result while you write.
  • External Browser Preview — Prefer a real browser? Open the live preview in your default browser with a single click.
  • One-click Build — Turn your document into final output such as PDF straight from the IDE's Run window, using your own compile options.
  • Auto-compile on Save — Documents are recompiled automatically when you save, so the preview and build output are always up to date.
  • Dedicated Run Configuration — A dedicated run configuration for .qd files makes compiling and previewing your document as simple as pressing Run.

Integration & Management

  • Instant File Creation — Create new Quarkdown documents right from the File → New menu with a ready-made template.
  • Centralized Settings — Configure the Quarkdown installation path, compile and preview options, and editor appearance all from one settings page.
  • Bilingual Interface — The entire plugin UI is available in both English and Chinese.

Support and Donation

If you appreciate this plugin, consider supporting me with a donation at GitHub Sponsors or 爱发电 !

Thank you for supporting open-source projects!

Many thanks to JetBrains for kindly providing a license for us to work on this and other open-source projects.

Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please feel free to submit a Pull Request. For major changes, please open an issue first to discuss what you would like to change.

Please make sure to update tests as appropriate.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
• feat(fold) .ref previews follow the IDE language
    • The reference type shown for a collapsed .ref {id} (Section / Figure / Table / Code / Equation) and the unresolved Reference(id) fallback were hard-coded English; they now come from the message bundle, so a Chinese IDE shows 章节 / 图 / 表 / 代码 / 公式 and 引用（id）.
  • fix(latex) an equation closed before punctuation no longer swallows the rest of the document
    • Quarkdown only requires a non-word character after the closing $, so $ d_k $, is an equation. The closing delimiter used to be accepted only when whitespace followed it, which made the scan run on to the next $ and pair the opening delimiter with one far below; every {#id} tag and heading in between was then analysed as TeX and reported bogus errors such as Parameter marker "#" must be followed by a number.
  • fix(table) tables whose separator cells use a single dash are recognized again
    • GFM — and therefore Quarkdown, which renders | -: | as a right-aligned cell — requires only one dash per separator cell, but the plugin demanded three. Every table using a short cell (| :-------: | ---: | :-------: | -: |) was invisible to the plugin: no gutter icon, no floating row/column bars, no table actions and no structure-view entry. The rule now lives in one place (QuarkdownTableParser.isSeparatorRow) shared by the parser, the gutter marker, the table editor and the status bar.
  • fix(heading) decorative headings (#!) and CRLF documents are recognized as headings
    • Quarkdown's heading pattern is ^ {0,3}(#{1,6})(!?)(?=\s|$), where the ! marks the heading as decorative: unnumbered and out of the table of contents, but still an anchor that .ref {id} resolves to. The plugin required a space right after the #s, so an appendix written entirely with #! / ##! headings had no heading at all — an empty structure view, no heading gutter icons, no go-to-symbol entries — and .ref could not resolve them.
    • QuarkdownHeadingSyntax.parseHeadingLine also rejected every heading of a CRLF document, because callers pass the line including its carriage return and . never matches one; the heading gutter icon was therefore missing on Windows-authored files. The decorative ! is preserved when a heading is edited (buildHeadingLine) and can be produced by buildHeadingInsert.

idea-plugin.name: Go Timer Leak Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on a case <-time.After(...) inside a select block in a module that targets Go before 1.23. Until Go 1.23, the Timer created by time.After is not recovered by the garbage collector until it fires, and a select inside any repeatedly-executed loop (the overwhelmingly common place a select appears) creates a new one on every iteration, leaking memory until each one's duration elapses. time.NewTimer(...) plus a deferred/explicit .Stop() is the documented, correct alternative.

Go 1.23 changed this: when the module's go.mod declares go 1.23 or later, unstopped timers are garbage collected, and nothing is reported. A module without a go line keeps the warning.

100% static text analysis -- a brace/keyword-based line scanner, not a real Go PSI parser, so it works whether the Go plugin is installed or not.

Confirmed real and undetected: GoLand 2025.3's new resource leak inspection covers types implementing io.Closer (files, network connections, sql.Rows, etc.) -- time.After's returned channel does not implement io.Closer, so it's structurally outside that inspection's scope (confirmed by reading the feature's own announcement post).

Stated honestly: v0.1 flags time.After( as a select case regardless of whether the enclosing select is itself inside a loop -- reliably detecting "inside a loop" via text alone across nested braces would be fragile. A select that only ever runs once is a rare, low-cost false positive.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • A description page for the inspection in Settings | Editor | Inspections, which showed "Under construction".

Changed

  • The rating prompt's local counter keeps one-way fingerprints of findings instead of their file paths, and deletes the list that earlier versions kept.
  • PRIVACY.md describes the values the plugin keeps in the IDE's local settings.

Fixed

  • time.After inside a select is no longer reported in modules whose go.mod declares Go 1.23 or later: since Go 1.23 the garbage collector recovers unstopped timers, so those warnings were false positives.

idea-plugin.name: Ruby Net::HTTP Reuse Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on a Net::HTTP.get/ .get_response/.post shorthand call found inside a loop/iterator block (.each do, .times do, while, for, brace-block { }) -- Ruby's own Net::HTTP documentation explains why this matters: "Creating a new HTTP connection for every request involves an extra TCP round-trip and causes TCP congestion avoidance negotiation to start over". The shorthand class methods open and close a connection on every single call, so using them inside a loop means paying that cost on every iteration instead of once via Net::HTTP.start(...).

100% static text analysis -- a `do`/`end`/brace nesting-depth line scanner, not a real Ruby parser, so it works whether the Ruby plugin is installed or not.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only recognizes the common .each do/.times do/while/ for ... do/brace-block loop-header shapes -- a loop built some other way (recursion, an unusual loop { } form) isn't specially tracked. Matches by simple text, not real call resolution -- an unrelated .get/.post method on some other object is a possible (rare) false positive.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: Ruby Shell Injection Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on system(...), exec(...), backticks (` `), or %x[...] whose command string contains #{...} interpolation -- Ruby's own official documentation states: "Some Ruby core methods accept string data that includes text to be executed as a system command and should not be called with unknown or unsanitized commands", specifically naming Kernel#exec, Kernel#spawn, Kernel#system, and the backtick method.

Confirmed real and undetected: none of RuboCop's 7 Security cops (Eval, Open, IoMethods, MarshalLoad, YAMLLoad, JSONLoad, CompoundHash) cover shell command injection -- confirmed by reading RuboCop's own Security cops documentation page directly before building this.

100% static text analysis -- a regex-based line scanner, not a real Ruby parser, so it works whether the Ruby plugin is installed or not.

Stated honestly: v0.1 doesn't trace whether the interpolated value actually originates from untrusted input, so a #{} interpolation of a hardcoded constant is a possible (rare) false positive. The safe system(cmd, arg1, arg2) array form (separate arguments, no shell interpretation) is correctly never flagged.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: Rails Mass Assignment Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on params.permit! (or xxx_params.permit!) -- Rails' own official documentation states: "Extreme care should be taken when using permit!, as it will allow all current and future model attributes to be mass-assigned". This is the exact anti-pattern strong parameters exist to prevent: it disables the whitelist entirely, permitting whatever attributes an attacker sends in the request body, including ones the developer never intended to be settable (the well-known real-world case: a role/admin boolean flipped via mass assignment).

Confirmed real gap: none of RuboCop's 7 Security cops (Eval, Open, IoMethods, MarshalLoad, YAMLLoad, JSONLoad, CompoundHash) cover Rails strong parameters/mass assignment -- confirmed by reading RuboCop's own Security cops documentation page directly before building this.

100% static text analysis -- a regex-based line scanner, not a real Ruby parser, so it works whether the Ruby plugin is installed or not.

Stated honestly: v0.1 doesn't resolve whether the receiver is actually an ActionController::Parameters instance, so an unrelated custom .permit! method on some other object is a possible (rare) false positive.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: RxJava Disposable Leak Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning icon on an RxJava xxx.subscribe(...) call (Observable/Flowable/Single/Maybe/Completable, RxJava 2.x/3.x) written as a bare expression statement -- the returned Disposable is discarded immediately, with no way to ever call .dispose() on it later. RxJava's own guidance is explicit: always dispose of subscriptions when no longer needed, or this is a well-documented source of memory/ resource leaks.

100% static text/PSI analysis -- matches the method name and argument shape by simple text, so it works whether the real RxJava jar is on the classpath or not. Java and Kotlin. Confirmed gap: JetBrains' own bundled "Reactive Streams" plugin (Ultimate-only) has 12 real inspections for Reactor/RxJava/Mutiny -- none of them cover a discarded subscribe() Disposable.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only flags the lambda/callback-based subscribe(...) overloads (0 to 4 lambda/method- reference arguments), which are the overloads that actually return Disposable. The single-argument subscribe(Observer) overload returns void/Unit and is never flagged. Matches by simple method name, not real type resolution.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: Redisson Client Reuse Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Gutter warning icon on a Redisson.create(...) call built inside a regular method body -- Redisson's own Getting Started guide states: "RedissonClient is thread-safe, so create a single instance and reuse it as a shared singleton across your application." A client built inside a method means a brand new connection pool to the Redis/Valkey server gets created on every call.

100% static text/PSI analysis -- matches the class/ method name by simple text, so it works whether the real Redisson jar is on the classpath or not. Java and Kotlin. Confirmed gap: every Redis-related plugin found on Marketplace is a data browser/client tool (Redis Helper, Redis Manager, Redis Client, Redis-Cli), none check RedissonClient reuse in application code.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only flags the direct Redisson.create(...) call. Never flags a call inside a constructor (a legitimate "create once" location).

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
