idea-plugin.name: JS Toolbox
idea-plugin.description:
JS Toolbox

An Intellij / Webstorm plugin that provides several tools for javascript development.

Here is a list of available actions:

  • Go to test [Alt T], [Ctrl Command T] on Mac
  • Go to view [Alt V], [Ctrl Command V] on Mac
  • Go to constructor [Alt G], [Ctrl Command G] on a mac
  • Join multi-line strings and variable declarations [Ctrl SHIFT Alt J], [Ctrl Command J] on Mac
  • Open current file in browser [Ctrl SHIFT Alt G], [SHIFT Option Command G] on Mac
  • Add a semi-color at the end of the line [Ctrl SHIFT ;], [Command SHIFT ;] on Mac
  • Sort the selection using a user-defined splitter [SHIFT alt 1], [Command SHIFT 1] on Mac

See all the JS Toolbox actions from two locations:

  • From Tools > JS Toolbox
  • From the editor, right click > JS Toolbox

Go to test [Alt T], [Ctrl Command T] on Mac

Jump between a javascript file and its unit test. You can configure the file name patterns under:

Settings > JS Toolbox

And set values for Unit test suffix and File suffix

If you need multiple patterns use comma. For example:

Unit test suffix: "Spec.js,-spec.js"
File suffix: "-controller.js,.js"

With this configuration the action will take you from:

"my-component.js" or "my-component-controller.js"

to

"my-componentSpec.js" or "my-component-spec.js"

Go to view [Alt V], [Ctrl Command V] on Mac

Jump between a javascript file and its associated view. You can configure the file name patterns under:

Settings > JS Toolbox

And set values for View suffix and File suffix

If you need multiple patterns use comma. For example:

File suffix: "-controller.js,.js"
View suffix: "-view.html,.html"

With this configuration the action will take you from:

"my-component.js" or "my-component-controller.js"

to

"my-component.html" or "my-component-view.html"

Toggle camel and dash case

Select some text and then choose the "Toggle camel and dash case" action 

one-two-three

Will turn into

oneTwoThree
oneTwoThree

Will turn into

one-two-three

Go to constructor [Alt G], [Ctrl Command G] on a mac

Jump to the constructor of the current javascript file.

Join multi-line strings and variable declarations [Ctrl SHIFT Alt J], [Ctrl Command J] on Mac

Join strings and variable declarations

Turn a multi-line string into a single string. Press Ctrl SHIFT Alt J on any of the string lines or select a block of text and join.

    var s = 'one ' +
        'two ' +
        'three';

Into a single string:

    var s = 'one two three';

Join multiple vars into a single var:

    var foo = 1;
    var bar = 2;

Into a single var declaration:

    var foo = 1,
        bar = 2;

Open current file in browser [Ctrl SHIFT Alt G], [SHIFT Option Command G] on Mac

Open the current file in the browser. Configure the URL that you want to use when opening the browser under Settings > JS Toolbox.

Sort the selection using a user-defined splitter [Ctrl SHIFT 1], [Command SHIFT 1] on Mac

For example, select a bunch of arguments, choose sort, and enter a text (eg. ,) to split and sort the result.

Requirements

  • Ext JS 4+ or Sencha Touch 2+
  • Sencha Cmd 4+ (optional)

Features

Code Completion (ctrl-space)

  • config, method, and property names for all Ext JS and user classes
  • values for alias properties such as xtype, controller, viewModel, layout, etc...
  • event names in Component.on, .mon, .un, .mun, and listeners objects
  • css class names in all config properties and methods ending in 'cls'
  • this.lookupReference(...) in controllers with an alias
  • controller methods in listeners: { (event): (here) } as well as handler config property
  • model/store fields for Ext.grid.Column.dataIndex
  • properties from the ViewModel in bind configs

Inspections/Quick Fixes

  • flags unused classes in the requires/uses arrays (can be configured to remove unused classes automatically via Preferences... Other Settings... Sencha)
  • flags classes in the uses/requires arrays which are already listed in parent classes
  • flags references to classes not in the requires/uses arrays (can be configured to add referenced classes automatically via Preferences... Other Settings... Sencha)
  • flags initComponent method without this.callParent()
  • flags references to unknown aliases such as controller: 'missingcontroller' and xtype: 'missingxtype'
  • flags references to unknown classes
  • flags class when namespace does not match the directory structure
  • flags class when name does not match the file name
  • flags references to missing controller methods in view event handlers, provides a quickfix to create the missing method.

Find Usages

  • Right click on any class name to find usages

Project Tree Actions

  • New Class (will automatically create subdirectories if "." is included - only available within an app or package)
  • New View Package (creates a directory containing a view, view model, and view controller - only available within the view directory of an app)
  • New App (requires Sencha Cmd - only available outside of an existing app)
  • New Workspace (requires Sencha Cmd - only available outside of an existing workspace)

Navigation

  • provides click-through support for this.callParent() to navigate to the appropriate method on the parent class
  • provides click-through support for css class names in configs and methods ending in *cls

Refactoring

  • rename file - updates the class name
  • move file - updates the class namespace

Project Templates

  • New Ext JS App creates a new single app project using sencha cmd (sencha generate app - requires Sencha Cmd)

  • Classes are now ordered alphabetically in the requires/uses arrays automatically.
  • Classes in the uses or requires array of the parent class or application are no longer flagged if they do not appear in the uses or requires array of the child class.
  • If a class exists in both the uses or requires array for both a parent and child class, the child’s requires statement will be flagged as redundant.
  • Toolbar shorthand classes are added to requires array when used.

idea-plugin.name: Vue Component Creator
idea-plugin.description:
vue-component-creator

An Brainstorm Plugin to create single file vue.js components with a Sass file along them and complete vuex modules. This plugins does a couple of things in order to simplify your dev experience.

Install

Search for Vue Component Creator in the plugins settings. Or download the plugin from the release site

Customize Templates

In the settings you can define custom templates to use. Read here to learn what the default templates look like and what variables are available for your custom templates

Vue single file component

Right click in the project tree view where you want to place the new module. Then New File -> Vue Module. This will open a dialog to define the module's name. This name is used later to name the directory, vue- and sass-file as well as the sass root name, and a root node in the vue file with the given name.

Structure

  • my-module
    • my-module.vue
    • _my-module.scss

Vuex module

By creating a new Vuex module, a couple of files will be generated.

Structure

  • name
    • actions.js
    • index.js
    • mutations.js
    • state.js
    • mutation-types.js (depending whether you set the Mutationstypes File
    • getters.js (depending wether you checked Getters File

Icons

Icons provided by https://www.iconfinder.com/justicon via https://www.iconfinder.com

basic feature

idea-plugin.name: AxiosCodeGen
idea-plugin.description:
Adds support for generating Axios code and JSDoc from SpringMVC Controller classes.

Features：

  • Support generating "xxxApi.js" file from "xxxController.java" through the right-click menu item named "Generate Axios Code" in the current editor or any package(s).
  • Support generating axios code snippet for single method through Intention on method name.
    • Press alt+enter on controller method name and select "Generate Axios Code", then a preview dialog will pop up for editing and copying.
  • Support converting POJO to type definition information in JSDoc(@typedef) through Intention on POJO class name.
    • Press alt+enter on POJO class name and select "Generate JSDoc", then a preview dialog will pop up for editing and copying.
  • Support modifying templates in the group named "AxiosCodeGen" under the Other section of the Settings | Editor | File and Code Templates settings page.

本插件支持从 SpringMVC Controller 类生成前端 Axios 请求代码和相应的 JSDoc。

功能点：

  • 通过在当前编辑器或项目目录树的右键菜单上点击 "Generate Axios Code"，可以从 "xxxController.java" 生成包含 Axios 请求代码和 JSDoc 的 "xxxApi.js" 文件。
  • 通过在 Controller 中的方法名上按下 alt+enter, 选择 "Generate Axios Code" 可以只生成该方法的 Axios 请求代码片段，会弹出预览窗口供编辑和复制。
  • 通过在 POJO 类名上按下 alt+enter, 选择 "Generate JSDoc" 可以生成对应类的 JSDoc 类型定义信息，会弹出预览窗口供编辑和复制。
  • 如果想要微调输出模板，可以在 Settings | Editor | File and Code Templates 的 Other 标签页下找到 "AxiosCodeGen" 分组。

Rules:

  • First, ensure that IDEA has completed indexing the SDK and current project (it's best to ensure the project can be compiled correctly), otherwise inaccurate results may be generated, such as inability to recognize some types or inherited properties.
  • Only processes classes annotated with @RequestMapping.
  • Only processes methods annotated with @RequestMapping, @GetMapping and other @XxxMapping annotations.
  • Only processes parameters annotated with @RequestParam, @PathVariable, @RequestBody, or @RequestPart.
    • Parameters annotated with @RequestParam will be treated as params parameters in Axios;
    • Parameters annotated with @PathVariable will be concatenated to the Axios request url in the form of ${xxx};
    • Parameters annotated with @RequestBody will be treated as the data parameter in Axios;
    • Parameters annotated with @RequestPart will be treated as FormData elements and passed to the Axios data parameter.
  • About parameter type conversion:
    • Basic types will be converted to string, number, boolean;
    • Collection types will be converted to Array;
    • Map types will be converted to Object<K,T>;
    • MultipartFile will be converted to File;
    • Date、LocalDate... will be converted to string;
    • Unknown objects will be converted to Object;
    • Enum types will be converted to the type of the property annotated with @JsonValue (com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation) in the enum class, defaulting to string if not found;
    • Generic wildcard types or unknown generic types will be converted to Object.
  • About POJO class conversion:
    • Only classes under the POJO Package(s) selected in the configuration dialog and their sub-packages will be parsed, otherwise they will be treated as Object;
    • If a POJO class is a generic class, the generic parameters (T, E...) will be output as-is using JSDoc's @Template;
    • Properties in POJO classes decorated with static, final, or transient will be ignored, and other properties will be processed using the same rules as parameter type conversion.
  • Supports recognition of @Tag, @Operation, @Parameter, and @Schema annotations from the io.swagger.v3.oas.annotations package.
    • Prioritizes extracting class, method, and parameter description information from these annotations, and attempts to extract corresponding information from JavaDoc if not found.

规则：

  • 首先，请确保 IDEA 已完成 SDK 和当前项目的索引工作(最好保证项目已可以正确编译)，否则可能生成不准确的结果，例如无法识别一些类型或继承的属性。
  • 只会处理被 @RequestMapping 修饰的类。
  • 只会处理被 @RequestMapping 和 @GetMapping 等 @XxxMapping 修饰的方法。
  • 只会处理被 @RequestParam、@PathVariable、@RequestBody、@RequestPart 修饰的参数。
    • @RequestParam 修饰的参数将被视作 Axios 中的 params 参数;
    • @PathVariable 修饰的参数会以 ${xxx} 的方式被拼接到 Axios 请求 url 中;
    • @RequestBody 修饰的参数将被视作 Axios 的 data 参数;
    • @RequestPart 修饰的参数将被视作 FormData 元素，传递给 Axios 的 data 参数。
  • 关于参数类型转换：
    • 基本类型将被转换为 string、number、boolean;
    • Collection 类型将被转换为 Array;
    • Map 类型将被转换为 Object<K,T>;
    • MultipartFile 将被转换为 File;
    • Date、LocalDate 等将被转换为 string;
    • 未知的对象将被转换为 Object;
    • 枚举类型将被转换为枚举类中被 @JsonValue(com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation) 注解修饰的属性的类型，若未找到则默认为 string;
    • 泛型通配符类型或未知的泛型类型将被转换为 Object.
  • 关于 POJO 类的转换：
    • 只有在配置弹窗中选择的 POJO Package(s) 及其子包下的类才会被解析，否则将被视为 Object;
    • POJO 类若是泛型类，则泛型参数(T、E...) 将使用 JSDoc 的 @Template 原样输出;
    • POJO 类中被 static、final、transient 修饰的属性会被忽略，其他属性将应用和参数类型转换一样的规则进行处理。
  • 支持识别 @Tag、@Operation、@Parameter、@Schema 这几个 io.swagger.v3.oas.annotations 包下的注解。
    • 优先从这些注解中提取类、方法、参数的描述信息，若未找到则尝试从 JavaDoc 中提取对应信息。

Example：

/**
 * class comment from JavaDoc
 */
@RestController
@RequestMapping(value = "user")
@Tag(name = "comment from @Tag name", description = "comment from @Tag description")
public class UserInfoController {

    /**
     * function comment from JavaDoc
     *
     * @param userInfo param comment from JavaDoc
     */
    // @Operation(summary = "comment from @Operation summary")
    @PostMapping("create")
    public ResultBody create(@RequestBody @Parameter(description = "comment from @Parameter description") UserInfo userInfo) {return ResultBody.success();}

    /**
     * remove user (JavaDoc)
     *
     * @param id user id (JavaDoc)
     */
    @Operation(summary = "remove user (@Operation)")
    @PostMapping("remove")
    public ResultBody remove(@RequestParam UUID id) {return ResultBody.success();}

    @Operation(summary = "update userInfo")
    @PostMapping("update")
    public ResultBody update(@Validated({UpdateGroup.class}) @RequestBody UserInfo userInfo) {return ResultBody.success();}

    /**
     * 分页查询
     *
     * @param query 查询参数
     */
    @PostMapping("page")
    public ResultBody<List<UserInfo>> page(@RequestBody PageQuery<UserInfo, ?> query) {return ResultBody.success();}

    @Operation(summary = "获取单个用户信息")
    @GetMapping("info/{userId}")
    public ResultBody<UserInfo> info(@PathVariable("userId") UUID id) {return ResultBody.success();}

    @Operation(summary = "上传文件")
    @PostMapping("/upload")
    public ResultBody upload(@RequestParam String q,
                             @RequestPart UserInfo userInfo,
                             @RequestPart MultipartFile file,
                             @RequestPart List<MultipartFile> fileList
    ) {return ResultBody.success();}

}

Generate file: UserInfoApi.js:

/**
 * comment from @Tag name, comment from @Tag description
 */
import api from "@/utils/request.js";

const prefix = '/user'

/**
 * function comment from JavaDoc
 * @param {UserInfo} userInfo  comment from @Parameter description
 */
export function create(userInfo) {
  return api.post(`${prefix}/create`, userInfo);
}

/**
 * remove user (@Operation)
 * @param {string} id  user id (JavaDoc)
 */
export function remove(id) {
  return api.post(`${prefix}/remove`, null, {params: {id}});
}

/**
 * update userInfo
 * @param {UserInfo} userInfo
 */
export function update(userInfo) {
  return api.post(`${prefix}/update`, userInfo);
}

/**
 * 分页查询
 * @param {PageQuery<UserInfo, Object>} query  查询参数
 */
export function page(query) {
  return api.post(`${prefix}/page`, query);
}

/**
 * 获取单个用户信息
 * @param {string} userId
 */
export function info(userId) {
  return api.get(`${prefix}/info/${userId}`);
}

/**
 * 上传文件
 * @param {string} q
 * @param {UserInfo} userInfo
 * @param {File} file
 * @param {Array<File>} fileList
 */
export function upload({q, userInfo, file, fileList}) {
  let formData = new FormData();
  formData.append('userInfo', new Blob([JSON.stringify(userInfo)], {type: 'application/json'}))
  formData.append('file', file);
  for (const f of fileList) {
    formData.append('fileList', f);
  }
  return api.post(`${prefix}/upload`, formData, {params: {q}});
}

// region pojo def

/**
 * 测试分页查询参数
 * @template T
 * @template E

idea-plugin.name: Kensington
idea-plugin.description:
CSS class name completions and validation for the Kensington JS template library.

Completion

Autocomplete triggers inside { class: '...' } and { class: ['...'] } expressions in JavaScript and TypeScript files. Multiple classes in one string are handled correctly — completion applies only to the word being typed, not the whole value. Each suggestion shows the source filename (e.g. styles.css) or CDN as a type hint.

Class names are sourced from:

  • Local files — all .css, .scss, and .less files in the project.
  • CDN stylesheets — any https://…​.css URL found in HTML, CSS, SCSS, Less, JS, or TS files (including <link href="…">, CSS @import url("…"), and Kensington t.link({ href: '…' }) calls). CDN files are fetched in the background, cached for 24 hours, and refreshed automatically when a relevant file is saved. Commented-out URLs are ignored.

Go to declaration

Cmd+Click (macOS) or Ctrl+B (Windows/Linux) on a class name inside a Kensington template jumps directly to the CSS selector definition in the local stylesheet.

Find usages

Invoking Find Usages on a CSS class selector finds all Kensington templates that reference that class.

Unknown class inspection

Class names that don't exist in any local or CDN stylesheet are highlighted with a warning. Two quick fixes are available via Alt+Enter:

  • Ignore class '…' — suppresses the warning for that specific class name permanently. The ignored list is saved in the project's inspection profile and can be viewed and edited in Settings → Editor → Inspections → Kensington → Unknown CSS class → Ignored Classes.
  • Disable 'Unknown CSS class' inspection — turns off the inspection for the whole project. A Re-enable link appears in the notification that follows. The inspection can also be re-enabled at any time in Settings → Editor → Inspections → Kensington.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 1.0.4 — Resolve non-CDN CSS link references (e.g. t.link({ href: '/vendor/bootstrap/…' }) served out of node_modules via express.static-style rewrites) so their classes are recognized. Uses progressive path-suffix matching, so URL prefixes that don't correspond to a real directory still resolve. Go-to-definition now jumps into externally-resolved CSS files. Fix cmd-click/hover: only the first class in a class: attribute could be navigated, and class: literals nested inside a children-array (e.g. t.header({ class: '…' }, [t.span({ class: '…' })])) were silently skipped.
  • 1.0.3 — Prevent EDT freezes during project scans by pruning dependency and generated directories, honoring excluded content, and yielding to pending write actions.
  • 1.0.2 — Fix EDT freeze when the TypeScript service restarts during a CSS scan.
  • 1.0.1 — Fix compatibility declaration for RubyMine 2025.x and 2026.x.
  • 1.0.0 — Initial release: CSS class completions, unknown-class inspection, go-to-definition, find usages, and CDN stylesheet support.

idea-plugin.name: ServiceNow Dev Pro
idea-plugin.description:
ServiceNow Dev Pro brings ServiceNow server-side development into JetBrains IDEs: connect to a ServiceNow instance and pull/edit/push server scripts (Script Includes, Business Rules, Client Scripts, UI Actions) and manage Update Sets — without leaving your JetBrains IDE for VS Code. Edit scripts locally and sync them back over the Table API — scripts run on your ServiceNow instance, not in the IDE.

Passwordless authentication: connect with a ServiceNow REST API key — the plugin never sees your ServiceNow account password.

Before you install. Setup takes about 5 minutes and needs admin rights on the ServiceNow instance — creating the API key is admin-only. Setup uses an API Key auth profile, a REST API key, and method-specific Table API access policies. Existing GET/POST policies can be reused, but every required policy must persist the profile under Inbound authentication profiles; an active policy with an empty list still returns 401. Save the inline profile row, click the policy's main Update button, then reload to confirm it remained. On a free Personal Developer Instance you are the admin, so you can do all of this yourself. On a corporate instance without admin rights, send your ServiceNow admin the setup guide — you only need the resulting key back.
  • Browse what's actually there. Business Rules, Client Scripts, and UI Actions are grouped under the table they apply to, so same-named records are never ambiguous. Counts show the instance's real totals ("100 of 4,878") and further pages load as you go.
  • Find it fast. One search field with an explicit scope — search the whole instance, or filter what's already loaded. Browse by recently updated, modified by me, or everything.
  • Edit in your IDE. Records open as local JavaScript files with bundled Glide type stubs for highlighting and completion. Jump straight from a script name in your code to its record with Open Script Under Caret.
  • See exactly what changed. Diff opens IntelliJ's native diff window — your working copy on the left, the instance on the right, always labelled — with change counts. Locally edited records are grouped at the top of the tree.
  • Push with fresh verification. Each push is bound to one connection, checks remote content before PATCH, and verifies it with a new GET afterward. GET-before-PATCH is not atomic overwrite protection; concurrent changes between requests remain possible.
  • Update Sets. Select the current Update Set from the tool window. Confirmation describes the set observed before push; capture is not reported as verified unless separately observed.
  • Credentials in PasswordSafe. Your API key lives in IntelliJ's credential store, backed by your OS keychain — never in project files or logs. The plugin never collects or stores your ServiceNow account password.
  • Talks only to your instance. A bounded, HTTPS-only Table API client. No external servers, no analytics, no telemetry.
Free and API-key-only. No license checks, paid upgrade, or OAuth runtime.

Note. ServiceNow Dev Pro is an editor bridge, not a script runner: your scripts execute on your ServiceNow instance, not in the IDE.

Configure via Settings → Tools → ServiceNow Dev Pro.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.2.0 — Reliability and cleanup release; supersedes the unpublished 2026.1.1 candidate.
  • Binds operations to the selected connection and confirms successful writes with an independent remote read.
  • Uses stable per-instance working copies, durable recovery journals and filesystem coordination; preserves migration originals and later local edits.
  • Bounds complete HTTP response consumption, fixes raw-row paging offsets and respects unsaved editor text.
  • Removes dormant OAuth and paid licensing runtime. The product remains free and API-key-only.
  • Prevents overlapping pushes to the same ServiceNow record from different IDE actions.
  • Reports the important partial-success case where ServiceNow accepted a push but the local working-copy metadata could not be refreshed.
  • Hardens ServiceNow-controlled names and messages before rendering them in IDE UI.
  • Clears stored credentials against the saved connection even when Settings contains an unapplied URL edit.
2026.1.0 — Redesigned tool window.
  • Records show their type and the table they apply to, so same-named Business Rules, Client Scripts, and UI Actions are finally distinguishable.
  • Honest counts: the tree reports the instance's real totals (e.g. "100 of 4,878") and loads further pages automatically instead of making you click "Load more".
  • One search field with an explicit scope — search the whole instance or filter what's loaded — plus browse scopes for recently updated, modified by me, or everything.
  • The editor is now the detail view: a banner on managed scripts carries status, Push, Diff, and Open in browser.
  • Diff opens IntelliJ's native diff window — your working copy on the left, the instance on the right, always labelled — with change counts.
  • Push confirms which instance and update set it will write to, warns when the record changed on the instance since you pulled, runs with cancellable progress, and reports exactly what landed.
  • Clearer first run and clearer failures — including specific guidance to reconnect when an API key is rejected or expired.
  • Passwordless authentication: connect with a ServiceNow REST API key. Basic Auth (username/password) has been removed entirely — the plugin never sees your ServiceNow account password. Existing Basic Auth users are prompted to reconnect with an API key.

idea-plugin.name: NPM Peer Dependency Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning icon on a package.json peerDependencies entry whose real installed version (from node_modules) doesn't satisfy the declared semver range -- or isn't installed at all. npm's own peer dependency model is opt-in and silent: since npm 7 it auto-installs a compatible peer if it can, but a version mismatch, an unresolved conflict, or a peer installed via a workspace/hoisting quirk all produce no warning in the editor, only a runtime failure the first time the mismatched API is actually called.

100% static JSON PSI analysis -- reads peerDependencies and the installed package's own package.json "version" field using the bundled JSON plugin's real PSI, no npm CLI invocation, no network calls.

Stated honestly: v0.1's semver-range checker covers ^/~/comparison/exact/* ranges -- an OR range (||) or a hyphen range is skipped, never reported as a false failure. A monorepo/workspace layout where node_modules lives at a different level than this package.json isn't resolved (no hoisting simulation), a possible false positive in that specific setup.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: Collector
idea-plugin.description:
Collector - A collection's plugin for PhpStorm

This plugin adds support for Laravel Collections.

It contains a bunch of handy refactorings for making your collections better. It can also convert normal PHP statements into collections.

Installation

The plugin has no stable version, only manual and EAP is possible.

  • Using IDE built-in plugin system:

    Preferences > Plugins > Marketplace > Search for "Collector" > Install Plugin

  • Manually:

    Download the latest release and install it manually using Preferences > Plugins > ⚙️ > Install plugin from disk...

Configuration

:warning: The inspections might be disabled by default! Go to preferences for enabling them.

All the features are added as inspections in PhpStorm, this means you can disable the ones you don't like or change how severe the warning are on them.

For example, by default refactoring foreach to collection is not highlighting the text.
However, if you would like to enforce yourself to never use foreach, you can change the severity to error.

Features

foreach to collection

array_map to collection

map(...)->flatten(1) to flatMap

Remove nested collections

Closure to arrow functions

where(...)->first() to firstWhere

idea-plugin.name: Lombok To Builder
idea-plugin.description:
Converts constructor calls and setter blocks into the Lombok-generated builder pattern.
  • Place the caret on a new Foo(...) call and convert it to Foo.builder()....build().
  • Place the caret on a Foo f = new Foo(); f.setX(...); ... block and fold it into a single builder chain.
  • Right-click in the editor (no selection = whole file, selection = that range) or on a folder/module/project in the Project view to batch-convert every applicable usage.
Actions only appear when the target class carries Lombok's @Builder (or @SuperBuilder). Enabling the Lombok plugin is recommended so generated constructors resolve.

When folding setters, a setter whose value references the object being built (e.g. a child pointing back at its parent) is kept as a trailing setter after the builder so the result still compiles. This is configurable under Settings | Tools | Lombok To Builder.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 0.5.1 — Long, mostly-null constructor calls now convert. The Minimum values to convert threshold counts the constructor's arguments (before null values are skipped), so a call like new Foo(0, null, null, null, null) is no longer suppressed; it becomes Foo.builder().a(0).build(). An all-null call is still left alone, since its builder would be an empty Foo.builder().build().
  • 0.5.0 — Calls to hand-written constructors are now left alone by default, since such a constructor may run logic a builder would bypass. A constructor Lombok generates from a class-level @Builder, or one you annotate with @Builder directly, stays convertible. New setting Convert calls to hand-written constructors (default off) re-enables conversion.
  • 0.4.0 — A converted local that is returned on the very next line is now inlined into the return, dropping the throwaway variable (Foo f = Foo.builder()…build(); return f; → return Foo.builder()…build();). New setting Inline a converted local that is returned on the next line (default on).
  • 0.3.0 — Setter folding now handles self-references: a setter whose value references the object being built (e.g. a child pointing back at its parent) is kept as a trailing setter after the builder instead of producing code that won't compile. New setting Keep self-referencing setters after the builder (default on; turn off to skip such blocks entirely).
  • 0.2.6 — Replaced a deprecated ReadAction.compute call in the batch action (flagged by newer IDEs); no change to behavior.
  • 0.2.5 — Added a plugin icon. Internal: static analysis (detekt) and more tests; no change to conversion behavior.
  • 0.2.4 — The batch action (folder/module/project) now runs in a cancellable background task and converts one file per write command, so it no longer freezes the IDE while processing many files.
  • 0.2.3 — Nested @Builder classes now keep their outer-class qualifier (e.g. Outer.Inner.builder()); previously the outer class was dropped, producing an uncompilable Inner.builder().
  • 0.2.2 — Minimum values to convert now gates constructor calls only; setter blocks are always converted regardless of the threshold.
  • 0.2.1 — Fixes: primitive boolean isFoo fields now map to the correct builder method, and constructors whose parameter names don't match the fields are left unconverted instead of producing invalid builder calls.
  • 0.2.0 — New settings: Skip setting null values (default on) drops .x(null) calls, and Minimum values to convert (default 3) skips converting usages with fewer than N values.
  • 0.1.0 — Initial release: constructor → builder and setters → builder intentions, plus a batch action for the editor (file/selection) and the Project view (folders/modules/project).

idea-plugin.name: Refactor Simulator
idea-plugin.description:
Preview every refactoring before committing it. Simulates a rename or extract refactor in an isolated in-memory sandbox — using IntelliJ's own PSI and refactoring APIs, never a custom engine — and shows a full impact report, validation results, and a side-by-side diff before anything touches a real file.

Unlike the native preview dialog, everything stays isolated until you explicitly choose Apply to Disk. Discard leaves the project exactly as it was — no exceptions.

Free. No AI, no confidence scores, no probabilistic heuristics — every reported number comes directly from Find Usages and IntelliJ's own refactoring processors.

idea-plugin.name: JFormDesigner
idea-plugin.description:
Advanced Swing GUI designer with outstanding support for MigLayout, JGoodies FormLayout, GroupLayout (Free Design), TableLayout and GridBagLayout, which makes it easy to create professional looking forms.

Key features

  • MigLayout support
    MigLayout is a superbly versatile and powerful open-source layout manager. It is grid-based, but also supports docking and grouping.
  • GroupLayout (Free Design) support
    GroupLayout support brings the "Free Design" paradigm to IntelliJ IDEA (as in NetBeans GUI Builder; formerly Project Matisse). You can lay out your forms by simply placing components where you want them. Visual guidelines suggest optimal spacing, alignment and resizing of components. This makes it easy to design professional-looking GUIs.
  • JGoodies FormLayout and TableLayout support
    These open-source layout managers allow you to design high quality forms.
  • Advanced GridBagLayout support
    The advanced GridBagLayout support allows the specification of horizontal and vertical gaps (as in TableLayout).
  • Column and row headers
    The column and row headers (for grid-based layout managers) show the structure of the layout and allow you to insert or delete columns/rows and change column/row properties. It's also possible to drag and drop columns/rows (incl. contained components and gaps).
  • Localization support
    Localizing forms using properties files has never been easier. Specify a resource bundle name and a prefix for keys when creating a new form and then forget about it. JFormDesigner automatically puts all strings into the specified resource bundle (auto-externalizing).
  • Beans Binding (JSR 295) support
    Using Beans Binding (JSR 295) helps you to keep UI state and model in sync. It drastically reduces the amount of listener code that is usually necessary.
  • BeanInfo Annotations
    The @BeanInfo and @PropertyDesc annotations make it very easy to specify BeanInfo information directly in the custom component. Its no longer necessary to implement extra BeanInfo classes. This drastically reduces time and code needed to create BeanInfo information.
  • Java code generator or runtime library
    Either let JFormDesigner generate Java source code for your forms (the default) or use the open-source (BSD license) runtime library to load JFormDesigner .jfd files at runtime. Your choice.
  • Generation of nested classes
    The Java code generator is able to generate and update nested classes. You can specify a class name for each component in your form. This allows you to organize your source code in an object-oriented way.
  • IDE plugins and stand-alone application
    JFormDesigner is available as IDE plugins for IntelliJ IDEA, NetBeans, Eclipse and as stand-alone application.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
What's New in 8.3

  • FlatLaf: Added FlatLaf Client Properties to Properties view.
  • Client Properties: Added "Configure" action to "Client Properties" row in Properties view. Support more data types in client properties (Color, Dimension, Insets, Point, Rectangle and Icon).
  • Support custom values for properties. You can either use subclasses of property type, or use factory classes that provide static fields or methods of property type. Right-click on property (in Properties view) and choose "Custom Value" from context menu. To remove custom value use "Restore Default Value".
  • SVG icons: Optionally specify custom width, height, scale factor and color mapping.
  • Use IntelliJ balloon notifications, instead of modal dialogs, for problem reporting (e.g. code generation problems).
  • Java 25 support.
  • Support for IntelliJ IDEA 2025.3.
  • and more...

idea-plugin.name: Penstock
idea-plugin.description:
Penstock edits BPMN 2.0 diagrams, DMN decisions and Camunda forms for Camunda 7, Camunda 8 (Zeebe), Operaton, and CIB seven in your JetBrains IDE - a Camunda Modeler that lives next to your code. Files with the .bpmn, .bpmn.xml, .bpmn20.xml, .dmn and .form extensions open in a visual modeler built on bpmn-js, next to the raw file in the same editor. Diagrams stay in the project and in version control, so process models are reviewed the same way as code.

Documentation and setup guides: kern0x1b.github.io/penstock-release. Bugs and feature requests: GitHub issues.

Penstock was previously published as "Camunda BPMN Editor". Same plugin, same vendor, new name - it updates in place and nothing needs to be reinstalled.

Features

  • Five modeling profiles - Classic BPMN, Camunda 7, Camunda 8, Operaton, and CIB seven, selected per project and written to penstock.yaml.
  • Properties panel - edit element properties, including Camunda extension attributes.
  • Comments - a note on any element, kept in the file so it travels with it through git, with what is still open counted on the element.
  • Script editor - inline Groovy and JavaScript scripts open as regular IDE tabs with syntax highlighting and completion, and are written back into the diagram as you type (Camunda 7).
  • Element templates - load Camunda 8 connector templates from the project, or browse connectors in the templates marketplace, downloaded on demand from GitHub to ~/.penstock/connectors.
  • Deployment - deploy the open diagram to Camunda 7 REST or Camunda 8, with basic-auth or OAuth 2.0 credentials stored in the IDE password safe rather than in project files.
  • Validation - bpmnlint runs against your own .bpmnlintrc and reports errors and warnings on the diagram.
  • Problems in the IDE - the check also runs in the background with no diagram open, and its findings are in the IDE's own Problems window and in Code > Inspect Code, as an inspection you can switch off.
  • Camunda 7 to Camunda 8 - see what does not carry over, convert a diagram with the visual diff before anything is written, and start job workers from your Java delegates. Analysis and the report are free; converting is Pro.
  • Token simulation - step a token through the process to check the flow.
  • Trace paths - select a step and see every path that runs through it, the steps before and the steps after, with the rest of the diagram dimmed. Follow message flows to cross pools, and trace a decision in a requirements diagram to what it needs and what depends on it.
  • DMN - decision tables, the requirements diagram and literal expressions, in the same editor, with a table you can run against values you type.
  • Forms - a Camunda form on the canvas with a live preview, the JSON it takes and the JSON it submits.
  • Monitor - the instances of the open diagram on your engine, what is waiting at each step, any incident, and an expression run against a real instance's variables.
  • Share and import - one offline HTML file with a viewer for the diagram and its documentation, and draw.io, Visio, Signavio and Bizagi diagrams turned into BPMN 2.0.
  • Export - SVG, PNG, and PDF.
  • Tool window - the processes, workers, messages, decisions, forms and element templates of the whole project, with every BPMN file in one tree.
  • MCP server - penstock mcp lets an AI agent list, read and check your diagrams for free across projects; flow analysis, scenarios, code links and editing need Pro, the same as from the command line. In Claude Code: claude mcp add penstock -- npx --yes @kern0x1b/penstock-cli mcp.
  • Visual Studio Code - the same editors, the same penstock.yaml and the same licence as an extension for VS Code, which also registers the MCP server with Copilot.
  • Themes - follow the IDE, or pick Light, Dark or Dracula for the editor, plus an optional hand-drawn diagram style.

Penstock Pro

Everything above is free, and so is going from a Camunda 7 delegate to its class or bean. Pro adds what only Penstock does, and every new machine gets thirty days of it:

  • Diagrams linked to the code - from a step to the worker that runs it and back, usages in code, Code Vision, variables and error codes checked across diagrams and code, tests run and debugged from the diagram, coverage on it, other repositories counted as part of the project, and Check Workers against the engine.
  • Flow analysis - finds deadlocks, branches that run twice, steps that can never run and loops with no way out, and outlines the path that leads there on the diagram.
  • Auto layout - reflows a tangled diagram into a readable left-to-right flow, with a preview before it is applied.
  • Scenarios and documentation - every distinct way through a process with its conditions, and a page per process with its picture, steps, decisions, events and data.
  • Test-case runs - Scenarios on the toolbar runs a process step by step against a local Camunda 7 or 8 engine, with mocks, and shows on the diagram what every step received, sent and changed. Test cases use Camunda Process Test's format and run in the IDE's test runner, and in CI with Team.
  • Visual diagram diff in version control, and modelling conventions from penstock.yaml.

Team adds the review bot for pull and merge requests and the checks for CI. Buy from Tools | Penstock licence… - the licence arrives in the IDE by itself, with no key to copy.

Getting started

  1. Open a .bpmn, .dmn or .form file. It opens in its editor; the raw XML or JSON is the tab beside it, in the same editor tab strip.
  2. The first time a folder is opened, Penstock asks which engine runs it - Camunda 7, Camunda 8, Operaton, CIB seven or plain Classic BPMN. The answer is written to penstock.yaml in that folder, so it is shared with everyone who clones the project and with the command line. Edit that file, or run penstock init, to change it later.
  3. For deployment, add a deployment: block to the same penstock.yaml with the engine's URL, and a profiles: block for each other environment. Passwords and client secrets are asked for in the Deploy popover and kept in the IDE password safe, never in the file.
  4. For Camunda 8 connector templates, list the files and folders in elementTemplates: in that file, or download them from the templates marketplace with Templates... in the More menu.

Validation with bpmnlint

The check works with no setup: it uses the project's .bpmnlintrc, or bpmnlint:recommended when there is none, and it runs in the background whenever a diagram is open. A minimal .bpmnlintrc in the project root: 

{
  "extends": ["bpmnlint:recommended"],
  "rules": {
    "label-required": "error",
    "no-implicit-split": "warn"
  }
}

Rules from your own bpmnlint plugin are the one thing the editor cannot read from node_modules, because it is a browser page and not a Node process. Bundle them into a single file with bpmnlint-pack-config and name that file in penstock.yaml: 

lint:
  configPath: .bpmnlintrc
  clientBundlePath: .bpmnlint/client.bundle.js

The bundle has to be inside the project, and Penstock only loads it from a project you have trusted. The command line needs none of this: penstock check runs the same rules with the plugins from the project's node_modules. The findings are in the editor's Problems tab, in the floating check card on the canvas, and in the IDE's own Problems window, so nothing has to be open for them to be there.

Requirements

Any JetBrains IDE from 2024.2 with JCEF enabled - the default in the standard distributions.

Trademarks

Penstock is an independent product. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Camunda Services GmbH. "Camunda" and "BPMN" are used only to describe the process engines and the notation the plugin works with. BPMN is a trademark of the Object Management Group; Camunda is a trademark of Camunda Services GmbH.

Open source components

This plugin bundles open-source components that remain under their own licenses. The full notices, including a source offer for the LGPL-licensed components, are available in Settings | Tools | Penstock | About | Open source licenses, and online at the notices page.

  • penstock mcp --config also prints the one line Claude Code takes, and says VS Code needs no entry.
  • The editor takes the colours of the look and feel you are running instead of a set of its own, so Islands, the classic themes, Darcula, High Contrast and any third-party theme look exactly as they do and the editor follows a theme change while it is open, including an accent colour you have changed. The colours each piece of the editor uses, and the IDE key behind each one, are written down in docs/design/theme-mapping.md
  • The three editors now read the same: one set of colours, one set of text roles, and one grid on both diagram canvases, so the DMN requirements diagram no longer looks different from a BPMN diagram in the dark theme. Text is 13px, 12px and 11px as the IDE itself sets them, and a user who has changed the IDE's font size gets their size
  • Every control now has the states the IDE has - hover, pressed, selected, selected when the editor has lost focus, focus and disabled - each in the running theme's own shade, and a disabled label stays readable. Labels, help and hints are at the contrast WCAG asks for, and a test fails the build if one of them is not
  • The licence is now a signed token. A small Cloudflare Worker (licence-worker/) turns Polar's answers into a token signed with a key only it holds, and the plugin, the CLI and the editor verify the signature themselves, offline, against public keys built into them, so a hand-edited file, a redirected address or a fake server can no longer make a machine Pro. The token is bound to the machine, lasts 30 days and is renewed once a day when online; offline it works until it runs out. ~/.penstock/license.json now holds only the token, PENSTOCK_LICENSE is exchanged for a six-hour pipeline token, and penstock license key and Copy Key for CI find the key again through the e-mail sign-in because the machine no longer keeps it. A licence file from an earlier version is exchanged for a token once, when the machine is online. A pipeline key now needs a Team key and the CI variable, a freed seat keeps counting against the limit for 30 days (one free move per seat per 30 days), and a machine clock set back below a time the machine already saw is refused.
  • The 30-day Pro trial is now kept by the licence service, so deleting files no longer starts a new one. We are moving from JetBrains Marketplace licensing to Polar, so every machine starts a fresh 30-day Pro trial from the new service: an old trial.json is ignored and deleted, and no trial date carries over.
  • The command line is published as a minified bundle, and the plugin's licence package is obfuscated in the release build.
  • The editor no longer takes the tier from a flag: it verifies the token the host gives it, and a host that cannot show one leaves the paid features locked. Asking for a feature fails closed instead of open.
  • One standard for every dialog, popover and form: the same sizes, footer, focus and Esc behaviour, labels without colons, help as permanent text, and errors as text under the field with a red outline once a field has been left. Export, Import report, the connection settings, Run with input, Save as scenario, Open run and the connector templates use it; the templates browser shows a template's details inside itself instead of in a second window
  • The buttons of a dialog follow the IDE: primary on the right on macOS, primary first on Windows and Linux
  • The MCP server no longer gates itself as a whole: list_diagrams, show_diagram and check_diagram are free, since they only read and explain a diagram. analyze_flow, list_scenarios, check_code_links and edit_diagram still need the same licence their CLI equivalent does, and say so, with how to buy or sign in, when called without one; tools/list notes it on each of them too
  • Camunda connector element templates are no longer vendored in the repository. They are downloaded on-demand from GitHub (api.github.com and codeload.github.com) when the user opens the connector marketplace or clicks Download on a missing template (never at IDE startup or on diagram open without user action), and cached in ~/.penstock/connectors/<ref>/ shared between the IDE and the CLI. Opening an existing diagram resolves templates from the local cache without network requests. Downloads are refreshed at most once a day, send no credentials, cookies, or project data, respect IDE proxy settings, and fall back to the existing cache when offline.
  • The line that says a feature is paid no longer makes a verb agree with the feature's name: "Process scenarios: part of Penstock Pro. Lists every distinct way through a process...", in the command line and in the IDE
  • The command line names its scenario commands after what they do: penstock scenarios list (was paths), scenarios run (was test-cases), scenarios generate (was test-cases --generate) and penstock junit (was tests). The old names still work and are left out of the help
  • Converting into a folder that already holds the converted files is not a dead end: the preview offers "Replace the files in <folder>", with a warning when the folder is not under version control, and writes over them only when it is ticked
  • The form editor's Check is free: it is lint, and no longer asks for a Pro licence. The decision editor's overlap and gap analysis stays Pro
  • Auto Layout leaves a small bar at the bottom centre of the canvas - "Laid out 24 elements", Undo and a close button - instead of a toast that disappears. It goes away when you close it, edit the diagram or undo
  • A diagram that cannot be read shows a message instead of an empty canvas with a palette and a toast: what is wrong with the parser's line, that the file was not changed, and a button that opens the XML in the Text tab at that line
  • Camunda 7 transaction boundaries are drawn in the accent colour instead of the error red, and each bar says "Transaction boundary: the engine commits here" when you rest the pointer on it
  • The import report no longer paints what could not be mapped in error red: it uses the warning colour, red is kept for a file that could not be read, and the heading leads with the count ("3 not imported")
  • The tool window's Migrate to Camunda 8 root shows the folder beside a file name when two files share it, and sits after Deployment and Files unless every diagram in the project is Camunda 7, Operaton or CIB seven
  • The More menu is grouped under View, Edit, File and Help headings (11px uppercase), and the pin is a quiet grey on pinned rows and appears on the other rows only when the pointer or the keyboard is on them
  • The Connection dialog opened from the deploy menu's Connection... offers Save, which only saves, and Save and Deploy; the dialog a deploy opens because nothing is set up yet still offers Save and Deploy
  • The form editor's Preview tooltip says that the palette is hidden while the preview is open
  • The engine-neutral mode is called Classic BPMN everywhere in the interface: the engine question above an empty diagram said Plain BPMN. The penstock.yaml value stays engine: classic
  • Copy as image is part of the Export dialog: Copy beside Save copies the picture with the chosen settings, and the dialog now opens light on white. The separate Copy as image entries in the More menu and the context menu are gone, and Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+C opens the dialog
  • The editor's stylesheets take every colour from the theme: the check flags, tooltips, context menu, dialogs, marketplace, simulation frame and error page no longer carry hardcoded colours, shadows and scrims come from theme tokens, and radii are on the design table (2px, 5px and 16px are gone)
  • The form checks are free on the command line too: penstock check (and --only flow) checks .form files without a licence, matching the form editor. Flow analysis of processes and decision analysis stay Pro
  • The More menu has Fit diagram (with its Ctrl/Cmd+0 shortcut), Zoom in and Zoom out under View
  • The Export dialog follows the design rules: 28px controls, 12px labels without colons, the actions Cancel, Copy and Save in one row at the bottom right, and the preview shows the whole diagram centred in its pane
  • The screen for a diagram that cannot be read has a Reload button beside Open the XML, and says "This diagram cannot be opened" since the cause is not always broken XML
  • The command line is published to npm as @kern0x1b/penstock-cli: the scope @penstock belongs to somebody else, and the free kern0x1b organisation is ours. The package was never published, so there is nothing to migrate and no old name left behind. The command is still penstock, and what runs it - the npx lines in the README, the entry penstock mcp --config prints, the pre-commit hook penstock init --hooks writes, the penstockw wrapper and the Homebrew formula - names the package @kern0x1b/penstock-cli
  • The sidebar toggle in the BPMN, DMN and form editors is a plain button in both states; the sidebar itself shows whether it is open
  • A --format value a command does not take is refused with exit code 2 and a message that lists the accepted values; before, check, show, scenarios list and others read it as text
Fixed
  • In the IDE, a diagram, a decision or a form opened while the IDE was still indexing showed "This view is not available until indexes are built" instead of the editor: the editor kept none of the data the platform puts on it, so the platform took it for one that cannot run during indexing
  • Closing a project while the editor page was still asking the IDE for its files wrote an "IDE error" for each of those requests
  • The editor the IDE ships could not start: the minifier renamed the parameters bpmn-js reads a module's dependencies from, so the injector could not build the modeler and no diagram opened at all. Every module in this repository that went through bpmn-js already declared its injection list for exactly this reason; three factories had been missed, and they declare theirs now
  • The pieces of the interface that still came out in English are translated in the other eight languages: the state of an element template, the pass or fail of a test case, every tool description and every refusal the MCP server sends an agent, the schema penstock edit --schema prints, the "Why it matters" and "See" around a SARIF or GitHub annotation, the prose in the configuration files penstock init and the IDE write, the open source licenses tab of the settings, the four editors VS Code offers, the labels of a deployment that is not set up, and the Create label of the properties panel
  • penstock diff with its default base always answered "Could not find the base HEAD~1": a ref written with ~ was refused as a name, so penstock diff, penstock diff HEAD~1 and penstock report without a base could never run. ~ is read now, ^ still is not, and a base that is not a plain name no longer sends git looking for it on a remote that may not be there
  • penstock help scenarios run and penstock help scenarios generate printed what Ctrl-C twice does under the exit code 1 and said nothing about a case that failed, in every language
  • The licence action described itself as part of Penstock Pro, and Team in a pipeline, and Team in a pipeline, with the clause twice
  • The editor asked for the embedded browser without asking whether the IDE has one, and an IDE without that module got no editor instead of a line naming what is missing
  • The sidebar toggle sits next to the sidebar it opens instead of 20px away from it, and while pressed it keeps its icon readable in a light theme
  • The review bot answers a /penstock comment only from someone who is an owner, a member or a collaborator of the repository, and never on a pull request from a fork: it says so in one line naming both repositories and does not check the fork out or run anything from it, so a fork cannot be executed with a token that writes to the repository. Both guards are in the bot as well as in the workflow penstock init --ci writes, so an older template is protected the same way
  • A branch, commit or tag named in a /penstock diff comment is checked before any git command sees it, so a name that git would read as an option, a range or a path out of the repository is refused and the bot asks what to compare with
  • A second run of the bot edits the answer it wrote before, on a pull request with a long comment thread, and it reads the comments page by page on GitHub and GitLab instead of only the first hundred
  • A picture the platform will not host is named and pointed at the build's artifacts instead of leaving a link with no target, and a run with no artifact link at all says the pictures are in the build's artifacts
  • A pipeline missing a token says which variable to set and where to set it - a Bitbucket repository access token, the Azure DevOps $(System.AccessToken) - instead of failing with a stack trace, and the GitLab setup says that the trigger token in the webhook URL is a secret to keep out of files, comments and logs
  • Run with input sizes to its content - Small with no step to answer, Medium once there is one - instead of always opening as a 752x524 dialog with the bottom half empty
  • Renaming a diagram no longer orphans its scenarios: the Scenarios tab resolves a diagram's test-case file by the process id inside it once the file name no longer matches, and renaming a diagram in the IDE offers to rename the matching test-case file alongside it
  • A deprecated connector template in the marketplace is badged Deprecated with its own reason where the template gives one, and sorted after the current ones instead of interspersed alphabetically; Install's save panel now opens in the nearest .camunda/element-templates folder above the diagram, an existing one if the project already has one
  • Clicking a finding in the check card or the Problems tab opens the properties field it names for far more rules than before - job type, form key or id, correlation key, history time to live, called element, error, escalation, message and signal references, timer definition and code findings for a missing job type, topic, class or delegate expression - and switches the sidebar to Properties even for a finding with no single field
  • penstock check, docs, share, migrate analyze and the MCP tools read DMN 1.1 and 1.2 files by moving them to 1.3 first, as the decision editor does; a file that cannot be read is one finding with its file and line, and the run goes on
  • Test cases are checked against the Camunda test-case schema before they run, in penstock test-cases and in the Scenarios panel: a case that lacks what the schema requires (an assertion without processInstanceSelector, an instruction with a property the schema does not allow) is not run and says what it lacks
  • A test-case run no longer touches the definitions you deployed: its test build carries ids of its own (penstock.<run>. in front of every process, decision and form id, and of the calls between them), so what the run deploys and removes is only what it deployed itself, and the process id you start stays what you deployed
  • In a project with Camunda 7 and Camunda 8 diagrams, code links keep the two apart: a Camunda 8 job type finds its job worker and never an external task subscription of the same name, a Camunda 7 topic finds the subscription and never a job worker (Go to Declaration, Find Usages, the Monitor incident's code list, Code Vision)
  • A deployment the engine refuses says which files it refused and why, one line for each, in the editor and in penstock deploy, instead of the engine's raw list of element errors
  • A deploy the engine answers with 401 or 403 offers Edit connection in the editor's message, and penstock deploy says what to set (deployment.auth in penstock.local.yaml, PENSTOCK_PASSWORD, PENSTOCK_CLIENT_SECRET or PENSTOCK_TOKEN)
  • penstock deploy and penstock doctor say so when deployment.auth.type is basic and there is no PENSTOCK_PASSWORD, before anything is sent; a password: key in penstock.local.yaml is still not used, and both commands say a password comes from PENSTOCK_PASSWORD or the IDE password safe
  • The publish workflow that penstock init --ci github writes runs when a .bpmn, .bpmn20.xml, .bpmn.xml, .dmn or .form file changes, not only a .bpmn
  • The command line no longer prints "(s)": counts are followed by the word in the right number (3 files, 1 file), and penstock docs ends with 3 pages written (1 process, 1 decision, 1 form)
  • penstock license key during the trial says the Pro trial is on, until when and how to enter a key, instead of "There is no licence"
  • penstock doctor prints its settings without a PROPERTY / VALUE header
  • The conversion preview centres each diagram in its pane, next to the single title and no check pill it already has
  • The bot and the Azure pipeline that penstock init --ci writes also run when a decision, a form or a .bpmn.xml diagram changes, and penstock license prints its status without a PROPERTY / VALUE header
  • A diagram opens fitted into the canvas instead of cut off at the edge, at 100% at most. Ctrl/Cmd+0 fits it again, and a panel that opens over a fitted diagram fits it again unless you have moved or zoomed it. Toggling the properties panel no longer rebuilds the editor and drops the undo history
  • Switching the IDE theme keeps the zoom, the pan and the selection of the diagram, and of the requirements diagram in the decision editor, instead of resetting the view
  • The problems pill on the canvas is hidden while the check card is open, and it counts the same findings as the card: compat findings the linter reports as info count as warnings, findings a compat rule repeats from bpmnlint count once, and the card's header shows its warnings too
  • A failure after a diagram has loaded, or a reload while it loads, is no longer reported as an unreadable file
  • After Auto Layout the diagram is fitted into the canvas like on open, instead of being left off the edge under the palette
  • The layout bar after Auto Layout is set in JetBrains Mono at 13px, with a 28px button
  • Warning strokes and markers read on white: the light theme's warning colour is a darker amber
  • A row of controls in the sidebar never leaves the sidebar: the Scenarios tab's footer and its file name line wrap onto a second line at a narrow sidebar instead of wrapping their own labels and clipping the last one, the Run output panel's header keeps its title on one line and lets the path be the thing that shortens, and every one of those controls keeps its 28px target
  • The palette is a two-column grid of 28px entries with a 16px icon, the shape design.md describes, and it scrolls inside its island instead of hiding the shapes that do not fit: on a tall editor all fifteen entries now fit, and on a short one - a run output panel open, say - the five that do not are still reachable rather than cut off
  • The row of the toolbar and the sidebar's tab row is 36px, one 28px control with 4px above and below it, instead of 37px: the 1px line under the toolbar that no design rule asks for is gone, the row's two sides now both stand 12px from the seam between them - so the sidebar toggle no longer has an odd extra gap on its right - and that 12px no longer jumps to 8px below 768px
  • The sidebar as a drawer reaches the bottom of the editor instead of stopping 44px short of it and leaving a strip of canvas and the watermark showing below
  • Every target on the bar is 28px: the pin on a command palette row, the pin in the More menu and the half of a split button
  • The floating surfaces use the padding design.md gives each of them: a popover and a card are 8px inside, the Deploy popover's groups are 16px apart instead of 12, the check card and the bar after Auto Layout are 8px on every side, and a dialog's header is 12px above, 16px at the sides and 8px below
  • The sidebar is a drawer below 960px rather than below 840: at an 840 to 960px editor, docking a 320px sidebar left the canvas too narrow for its own toolbar, and Monitor and Scenarios fell off the bar. Every action now fits from 700px up
  • The form palette's search field is the 28px it is declared to be instead of being squeezed to 19px on a short editor, and the list between the header and the search is the only part that gives way
  • In VS Code a host call could be dropped on the floor with nothing said anywhere. Six schemas of openapi.yaml marked a value nullable without naming its type, which is not a schema Ajv can build, so every call that carried one of them - saving the preferences, which is what remembers the sidebar tab, the column width and the pinned actions - threw in the extension host and never reached its handler. The schemas name their type now, and a host call that fails for any other reason answers the editor with the failure instead of leaving the call hanging
  • The integration suite of the VS Code extension reported success while the extension host threw three times per run, never finished when it did not, and left VS Code running; it now exits non-zero on the first failed behaviour, takes the VS Code it started down with it on a failure, on a timeout and on a Ctrl-C, and writes nothing outside its own temporary folder
  • The integration suite opened a window on the owner's screen and then slid it off the screen with AppleScript, which could also move the owner's own VS Code; it now runs a copy of the app it downloaded, marked as an agent app, so the window stays where it opened, never comes to the front and has no dock icon
  • A diagram with a reference to an element that is not in the file no longer crashes penstock check with a stack trace: the dangling reference is a finding that names the element and the missing id, the rules that cannot read such a model are skipped, and the command exits 1
  • penstock migrate --format json writes its JSON to stdout when the migration finds errors, as every machine format does, instead of to stderr
  • Paste in VS Code: copied elements are kept through the host's own clipboard operation, since the synchronous request the editor used before never reached the VS Code host
  • Cancelling a deploy hook in VS Code ends its process; before, cancelling only changed a label and the hook kept running
  • Closing a VS Code editor no longer leaves a pending request that answers a closed webview
  • The wrapper's penstock-wrapper.properties version and distribution are checked before npm install runs, so a value like ../.. cannot leave the downloads folder or reach a shell on Windows
  • The Camunda Form file type has a fixed internal name, so the IDE no longer logs an incorrect file type name at start-up in a translated IDE
  • The IDE no longer runs an action it queued for a project after that project has closed, and a failed class navigation is logged instead of swallowed
  • A test-case run no longer puts decisions and forms from out and dist on the test classpath; process, decision and form ids are read with an XML parser, so a commented-out <process> is not a declared id
  • The command line called a diagram it could not read - no permission, a folder, a symlink loop - "not valid BPMN XML: EACCES ...", and called a failed write the diagram's fault; both now name the file or folder and the reason, and export and share leave nothing half written
  • diff and report read a diagram over 1 MiB as new, because git's output was cut off at the default buffer
  • init --hooks failed in a git worktree or submodule, where .git is a file, and ignored core.hooksPath; a hook that cannot be written is now a skipped line instead of a failed init
  • fmt --write and layout --write stopped at the first file they could not read; they now report that file and go on with the others, and layout lists a failed file on stdout like fmt does
  • penstock constructor, toString and other names every object has crashed the argument parser, and edit accepted them as properties, elements and events
  • doctor --format json printed passwords and secrets written into penstock.yaml
  • An MCP edit_diagram call with dryRun that is not a boolean wrote the file; it is refused now
  • check --only "" passed without checking anything, migrate on a path that is not there said there was nothing to migrate, import of a folder exited 2 with a raw system error, docs with no page to write left an empty folder and index, and show and edit blamed the diagram for a penstock.yaml that could not be read
  • export --format png called a browser failure "not valid BPMN XML"; report now writes its "wrote" line to stdout when it found problems, as check does
  • Auto layout of a very dense diagram could hold the editor for minutes; it now stops after 15 seconds and says the diagram is too dense, and the diagram stays as it was
  • The webview's WebAssembly module was served with a generic content type, so the browser logged a compile failure each time an editor opened; it is served as WebAssembly now
  • The sidebar's tab row overflowed at its narrowest width and the selected tab squeezed its icon; the selected tab now gives way first. The form editor's palette scrolls inside its island instead of being cut off
  • The running instances of a diagram: an engine answer such as 401 or 500 was reported as "nothing deployed"; it now says the engine could not be reached, with the status
  • The file chooser reported a dialog that could not be shown as a cancel; it now says so
  • A save that failed after announcing itself hid the next real change made to the file outside the editor
  • Script tabs kept an arbitrary one open instead of the oldest once there were more than 32
  • Exporting a PNG or a PDF leaked one object URL each time
  • The Monitor listed every variable a step reads as never set after the engine refused the list of variable names, and the Comments tab crashed when the selection service threw
Changed
  • The sketchy drawing style uses Architects Daughter, under the SIL Open Font License, instead of the Virgil build it bundled before, which was licensed for personal use only. Its licence and JetBrains Mono's are now in the third-party notices

idea-plugin.name: Makinda Icons
idea-plugin.description:
Beautiful, consistent file icons for the IntelliJ Platform — the same icon set as the Makinda Icons VS Code extension.

102 file icons — Solid style, auto-adapts to light and dark IDE themes.

Covers: JavaScript · TypeScript · Python · Rust · Go · Java · PHP · C/C++ · Ruby · Vue · Svelte · Astro · Dart · SQL · TOML · Shell scripts (bash, zsh, fish, powershell, nushell) · Git dotfiles · .env / dotenv · README · CHANGELOG · SECURITY · CONTRIBUTING · Next.js config · and many more.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.0

  • Added 29 new file icons: dart, bash, zsh, fish, powershell, nushell, batch, sql, toml, tsv, binary, env, dotenv, editorconfig, gitignore, gitattributes, gitmodules, npmignore, readme, changelog, notice, authors, contributing, code-of-conduct, security, todo, next, javascript, typescript

idea-plugin.name: Flatpak DevTools
idea-plugin.description:
Build, run, and validate Flatpak applications from your JetBrains IDE. Flatpak DevTools turns flatpak-builder into a first-class workflow with dedicated Run Configurations and schema-aware editing — so you can develop and package sandboxed Linux apps without leaving your IDE.

Flatpak

  • Automatic manifest detection — manifest.json, flatpak.json, flatpak-manifest.json and app-id style files (org.example.App.json/.yaml/.yml) are bound to the official Flatpak schema automatically
  • Code completion & validation — schema-driven completion and inline validation for app-id, runtime, sdk, modules, finish-args, command and every other manifest field
  • One-click Flatpak actions — a dedicated Flatpak Run Configuration with Build, Run, Export, Clean, Validate and Custom commands
  • Smart project detection — Flatpak manifests are detected on project open with a one-time balloon offering to create run configurations; right-click any manifest to run Build <app-id>
  • Smart run — the Run command launches the built app inside the sandbox, executing the manifest's command (falling back to the app-id), with optional cleanup and portal sandbox flags
  • Flatpak Builder SDK integration — commands execute through the official org.flatpak.Builder SDK, with output streamed to the Run console
  • Configurable binaries — custom flatpak/flatpak-builder binaries, picked with a file chooser or typed directly in Settings

GtkBuilder XML support

  • Code completion and validation for .ui/.glade interface files, driven by a GtkBuilder schema generated from the project's GNOME SDK
  • GNOME SDK autodetection — the schema branch follows the sdk/runtime declared in your Flatpak manifest, falling back to a bundled schema when no SDK is recognized
  • .xml files whose root element is <interface> are also supported once a Flatpak project is recognized

GTK Support

  • Code completion and validation for .ui/.glade interface files, driven by a GtkBuilder schema generated from the project's GNOME SDK
  • Planned: Basic window/widget preview directly from the IDE
  • Planned: Autodetected unregistered files from GResource
  • Planned: Blueprint format support

Qt/KDE support

Planned — future roadmap, no ETA yet.

Basic privacy

This plugin contains a special opt-in section to enable Sentry reports under Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Flatpak Binaries. We appreciate the use of this options, since it is the way we have to track bugs and problems. No personal data or identification is collected.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Stop button terminates flatpak forcefully and leaves dead ro-files FUSE mounts
    • The wrongful termination caused Error: opendir(rofiles-...): Transport endpoint is not connected
    • A new silent (unless errored) UNMOUNT_STALE pre-step detects and unmounts these mounts before a build
    • Killing a flatpak process now terminates the whole process chain
  • A wrong validation was creating an output folder inside the $HOME (user's folder). We removed this validation completely.
  • Remove invalid io.sentry.jvm.gradle from plugin.xml dependency, which led to an initialization error
  • The ./gradlew build now produces an installable ZIP inside ./build/distributions
  • Silently check for Sentry or fallback to log only (on missing Sentry lib, or jar installed directly, for instance)

idea-plugin.name: Prettify python
idea-plugin.description:
Prettify Python

Enhance the readability of your Python code with beautiful mathematical symbols!

This plugin automatically replaces standard Python operators with their mathematical equivalents, making your code more elegant and readable.

Key Features

  • Automatic operator replacement with mathematical symbols
  • Customizable replacement rules
  • Instant changes application

Supported Replacements

  • >= → ≥ (greater than or equal)
  • <= → ≤ (less than or equal)
  • != → ≠ (not equal)
  • -> → ➔ (arrow)
  • lambda → λ (lambda)
  • ** → ^ (power)

How to Use

  1. Install the plugin
  2. Open any Python file
  3. Enjoy automatic formatting!

Configuration

You can customize replacement rules in the plugin settings:

  1. Go to Settings/Preferences
  2. Find "Prettify Python" in the plugins list
  3. Here you can:
    • Enable/disable specific replacements
    • Add new custom replacements
    • Edit existing replacements
    • Organize replacements by categories
    • Import/Export your replacement settings

Note: If you're using a font with ligatures, you can disable the replacements that your font already provides and keep only the ones you need!

Support

If you have any questions or suggestions, visit the plugin page.

Enjoy more beautiful Python code! 🐍✨

idea-plugin.name: Unclutter Java
idea-plugin.description:
Reduce cognitive load when parsing Java code by folding some verbose syntax.

Functional Interfaces

Reduces usages of functional interfaces (interfaces annotated with @FunctionalInterface) to what you would expect when you come from a language like Python.

Examples


Function<Baz, Buzz> f = foo::bar;
f.apply(baz);  // unfolded
f(baz);        // folded

Predicate<String> isBlank = String::isBlank;
if (isBlank.test("not blank")) { … } // unfolded
if (isBlank("not blank")) { … }      // folded
Note, only the sole non-default and non-static method of a functional interface is folded.

Creating instances

Removes visual noise from constructor calls.

Examples


new Foo(bar, baz); // unfolded
Foo(bar, baz);     // folded

new Foo<>(bar, baz); // unfolded
Foo⋄(bar, baz);            // folded

new com.example.Foo<String>(bar, baz); // unfolded
…Foo⋄(bar, baz);                             // folded

express-json

Folds (simple) express-json compositions into something that looks like JSON.

Examples


new Object(
   new Member("a", "b"),
   new Member("c", new Array(1, 2, 3))
); // unfolded

{
   "a": "b",
   "c": [1, 2, 3]
};  // folded

Logging

Folds log statements and consumers into a "comment". This reduces distraction and helps to focus on the actual functionality.

Examples


log.trace("some trace log"); // unfolded

/*log*/  // folded

rxflowable
    .map(mapFunction)
    .doOnNext(value -> log.trace("next value was {}", value)) // unfolded
    .subscribe(subscriber);

rxflowable
    .map(mapFunction)
    .doOnNext(/*log*/) // folded
    .subscribe(subscriber);

Comparable.compareTo

Readable calls to compareTo

Examples


foo.compareTo(baz) < 0 // unfolded
foo < baz     // folded

Source Code

Sources available at https://github.com/dmfs/unclutter-java

idea-plugin.name: Foldable Project View
idea-plugin.description:
Support Foldable Project View
If you find this plugin useful, support its development via GitHub Sponsors, Ko-fi, or PayPal. You can also find my other projects on GitHub.

The Foldable Project View is a plugin for the IntelliJ-based IDEs that lets you fold files located in the root of your project.

Available features:
  • Fold matching root elements of the project modules in the Project View
  • Multiple named folding rules with custom foreground/background colors
  • Enable/disable folding via Preferences or Project View options menu
  • Optionally fold directories
  • Fold VCS-ignored files
  • Hide empty groups
  • Hide all groups
  • Case-insensitive matching
  • Search scopes based on the folding rules
  • Live Project View preview
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Support for multiple rules/groups in the Project View
  • Possibility for specifying the background/foreground of the rule
  • Folding rules are available as search scopes (e.g., in Find in Files)
  • Ignored files (VCS ignore files like .gitignore) are folded into a dedicated Ignored files group (#4)
  • Folding groups show the number of folded elements
  • Support for IDE Settings Sync: the last saved settings are synchronized and used as defaults for projects without stored settings (#41)

Changed

  • Use a separated storage file within the .idea directory: FoldableProjectView.xml
  • Patterns are matched against the path relative to the module content root, using gitignore-like glob syntax
  • Folding groups are sorted right after directories
  • Require IntelliJ Platform 2025.3+

Fixed

  • Ignored files located outside of a module were not folded into the Ignored files group (#11)
  • Avoid Project View refresh on the wrong thread, which could freeze Rider (#28)
  • Folding was not applied to folders attached to a Rider solution (#46)
  • Matched elements were duplicated in the Project View instead of being moved into the group, and folding was not applied to module roots reached through other Project View parent nodes or content roots (#92)
  • Hide empty groups, Hide all groups, and Fold ignored files options were not applied
  • Project View was not refreshed after applying the settings
  • Space-separated patterns in a single rule were treated as one pattern; patterns can now be separated by spaces, commas, or both (#64)
  • Select Opened File was delayed on large projects due to excessive pattern matching (#93)
  • Select Opened File did not highlight files located in folded groups or folded directories (#15)
  • Fold Root Files and Fold Ignored Files actions were shown on the Welcome screen, where no project is available (#82)
  • Folders matched by VCS ignore rules, like .idea, stopped folding after .gitignore was added to git (#9)
