idea-plugin.description:
Peekaboo (IdeaVim extension)

An IdeaVim extension that shows register contents in a popup window when pressing " in normal mode or Ctrl-R in insert mode.

This extension is inspired from the vim-peekaboo plugin.

Features

  • Shows register contents in a popup window
  • Works with both normal mode " and insert mode Ctrl-R
  • Respects your own key mappings (e.g., if you've remapped these keys)
  • Organized sections:
    • Special registers (", *, +, etc.)
    • Named registers (a-z)
    • Last yank (register 0)
    • Delete/Change history (registers 1-9)

Installation

  1. Install IdeaVim if you haven't already
  2. Install this plugin:
    • In IntelliJ IDEA: Settings/Preferences → Plugins → Marketplace → Search for "Vim-Peekaboo"
    • Or download from JetBrains Marketplace
  3. Add set peekaboo to your ~/.ideavimrc file, then run :source ~/.ideavimrc or restart the IDE.

Usage

  1. In normal mode: Press " to see registers before using them in commands
  2. In insert mode: Press Ctrl-R to see registers before pasting their contents

The popup will show automatically and disappear once you:

  • Select a register
  • Press any other key
  • Click outside the popup

Customization

The plugin works with your own mappings. For example, if you have these in your ~/.ideavimrc:

" Alt-R instead of Ctrl-R in insert mode
inoremap <A-r> <C-r>
" & instead of " in normal mode
nnoremap & "

The popup will appear when you use your custom mappings too.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Fixed compatibility with IdeaVim 2.18.1

idea-plugin.name: Vim FunctionTextObj
idea-plugin.description:
FunctionTextObj (IdeaVim extension)

An extension for IdeaVim that adds text objects for manipulating functions/methods in your code. Similar to how iw operates on words or i" operates on quoted strings, this plugin provides if and af to operate on functions.

Features

  • if - "inner function" - selects the function body (excluding braces)
  • af - "around function" - selects the entire function (including braces and signature)

These text objects work with all Vim operators and in visual mode:

dif  - delete the function body
caf  - change the entire function
vif  - visually select the function body
yaf  - yank (copy) the entire function

Supported Languages

This extension supports function/method selection in the following languages using the Jetbrains language plugins:

  • C# using Rider
  • C and C++ using CLion
  • Dart
  • Go
  • Java: : Already included by default in IntelliJ
  • JavaScript/ECMAScript 6/TypeScript: Already included by default in IntelliJ
  • Kotlin
  • PHP
  • Perl 5
  • Python
  • R
  • Ruby
  • Rust
  • Scala

Installation

  1. Install IdeaVim if you haven't already
  2. Install this plugin:
    • In IntelliJ IDEA: Settings/Preferences → Plugins → Marketplace → Search for "Vim FunctionTextObj"
    • Or download from JetBrains Marketplace
  3. Add set functiontextobj to your ~/.ideavimrc file, then run :source ~/.ideavimrc or restart the IDE.

Customization

Don't like the default f mapping? You can remap the text objects in your .ideavimrc:

" Use 'm' instead
omap im <Plug>InnerFunction
omap am <Plug>OuterFunction
vmap im <Plug>InnerFunction
vmap am <Plug>OuterFunction
idea-plugin.change-notes: • Fixed issue with Kotlin expression body functions (#11)

idea-plugin.name: Vim Switch
idea-plugin.description:
IdeaVim Switch

An IdeaVim extension inspired from switch.vim to switch between related text segments.

Installation

  1. Install IdeaVim if you haven't already
  2. Install this plugin:
    • In IntelliJ IDEA: Settings/Preferences → Plugins → Marketplace → Search for "Vim-Switch"
    • Or download from JetBrains Marketplace
  3. Add set switch to your ~/.ideavimrc file, then run :source ~/.ideavimrc or restart the IDE.

Usage

Place your cursor on a term and use:

  • :Switch to cycle forward through alternatives
  • :SwitchReverse to cycle backward

You might want to map these commands, for example:

" Map to <leader>s and <leader>S
nnoremap <C-s> :Switch<CR>
nnoremap <C-S-s> :SwitchReverse<CR>

" Or use - and +
nnoremap - :Switch<CR>
nnoremap + :SwitchReverse<CR>

Configuration

Enable patterns in your .ideavimrc either by group or individual patterns:

" Enable all patterns from multiple groups
let g:switch_definitions = 'group:basic,group:java,group:rspec'

" Enable specific patterns
let g:switch_definitions = 'basic_true_false,java_visibility,rspec_should'

" Mix groups and individual patterns
let g:switch_definitions = 'group:basic,java_visibility,rspec_should'

Built-in Patterns

Basic (group:basic)

  • Binary (basic_binary): 0 ↔ 1
  • Directional (basic_up_down_left_right): up ↔ down ↔ left ↔ right (case insensitive)
  • Logical operators (basic_logical_ops): && ↔ ||
  • Bitwise operators (basic_bitwise_ops): & ↔ |
  • Boolean (basic_true_false): true ↔ false (case-insensitive)
  • Boolean operators (basic_and_or): and ↔ or (case-insensitive)
  • Equality (basic_equality): == ↔ !=
  • Is checks (basic_is_is_not): is ↔ is not
  • Single/double quotes (basic_quotes): "string" ↔ 'string' ↔ `string`

Java (group:java)

  • Assertions (java_assert_equals): assertEquals ↔ assertNotEquals
  • Boolean assertions (java_assert_true_false): assertTrue ↔ assertFalse
  • Null assertions (java_assert_null): assertNull ↔ assertNotNull
  • Visibility (java_visibility): private ↔ protected ↔ public
  • Optional checks (java_optional_check): isPresent() ↔ isEmpty()

JavaScript (group:javascript)

  • Functions (javascript_function): Transform between function syntaxes
    • function name() { ↔ const name = () => {
    • async function name() { ↔ const name = async () => {
  • Arrow functions (javascript_arrow_function): function(x) { ↔ (x) => {
  • Variable declarations (javascript_es6_declarations): var ↔ let ↔ const

RSpec (group:rspec)

RSpec patterns:

  • Should syntax (rspec_should): should ↔ should_not
  • Expectation chains (rspec_to): .to ↔ .not_to ↔ .to_not
  • Truthiness (rspec_be_truthy_falsey): be_truthy ↔ be_falsey
  • Presence (rspec_be_present_blank): be_present ↔ be_blank

Ruby (group:ruby)

  • Hash syntax (ruby_hash_style): :key => value ↔ key: value
  • One-line hash (ruby_oneline_hash): Similar to hash_style but for compact syntax
  • Lambda syntax (ruby_lambda):
    • lambda { |x| } ↔ -> (x) { }
    • lambda { } ↔ -> { }
  • Conditionals (ruby_if_clause):
    • if condition ↔ if true or (condition)
    • if true or (condition) ↔ if false and (condition)
    • if false and (condition) ↔ if condition
  • Array syntax (ruby_array_shorthand): ['a', 'b'] ↔ %w(a b)
  • Hash access (ruby_fetch): hash[key] ↔ hash.fetch(key)
  • Nil assertions (ruby_assert_nil): assert_nil x ↔ assert_equal nil, x

Rust (group:rust)

  • Void type checks (rust_void_typecheck):
    • let x = ↔ let x: () =
  • Turbofish (rust_turbofish):
    • parse() ↔ parse::<Todo>()
  • String types (rust_string):
    • "text" ↔ r"text" ↔ r#"text"#
  • Optional checks (rust_is_some): is_some ↔ is_none
  • Assertions (rust_assert): assert_eq! ↔ assert_ne!
  • Cargo dependencies (cargo_dependency_version):
    • package = "1.0" ↔ package = { version = "1.0" }

Scala (group:scala)

String interpolation (scala_string), cycles through:

  • Regular strings: "text"
  • String interpolation: s"text"
  • Formatted strings: f"text"
  • Multiline strings: """text"""
  • And combinations: s"""text""", f"""text"""

Markdown (group:markdown)

  • Task items (markdown_task_item): - [ ] Buy milk ↔ - [x] Buy milk

Custom Patterns

Define your own patterns using the provided VimScript functions:

let g:switch_custom_definitions = [
    " Basic word cycling (with word boundaries)
    \ switchWords(['debug', 'info', 'warn', 'error']),
    
    " Case-insensitive word cycling (with word boundaries)
    \ switchNormalizedCaseWords(['GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'DELETE']),
    
    " Custom regex patterns (each pattern is a pair of [match, replacement])
    \ ['width:\s*(\d+)px', 'width: \1em'],
    \ ['height:\s*(\d+)px', 'height: \1em']
\ ]

Available functions:

  • switchWords(words): Creates patterns that cycle through words in order, matching exact words with word boundaries

    • Example: switchWords(['yes', 'no']) matches exactly 'yes' or 'no' and cycles between them

  • switchNormalizedCaseWords(words): Like switchWords but case-insensitive

    • Example: switchNormalizedCaseWords(['GET', 'POST']) matches 'GET'/'get'/'Get' and cycles to 'POST'/'post'/'Post' preserving the original case

idea-plugin.name: Curl2py
idea-plugin.description:
Curl2py plugin for IntelliJ based IDEs

Quickly generate python requests code based on the cURL(bash) command copied by the browser.

根据浏览器复制的cURL(bash)命令生成 Python requests 代码，爬虫学习好帮手。

Getting started

1. Open the web page with browser and use F12 to enter developer mode.
2. Click the Network tab and select the URL you want to crawl.
3. Right-click on it and select "Copy -> Copy as cURL(bash)".
4. Go back to the IDE, right-click on "Curl2py" in the context menu.
5. The generated python code will be displayed in the editor window.
idea-plugin.change-notes: • Generate python requests code based on the cURL(bash) command.

idea-plugin.name: MLIR ODS
idea-plugin.description: Plugin adding language support for MLIR ODS to IntelliJ-based IDEs via tblgen-lsp-server.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Quick documentation (Ctrl+Q or hover) for class, multiclass, def and defvar statements as well as fields. It shows the element's syntax-highlighted definition together with the comment block written directly above the element, rendered as Markdown.
  • Typing ! now offers completion for every bang operator known to the plugin, inserting the parentheses of its argument list and, in the case of !cast, also the angle brackets of its type argument. Delimiters that have already been written are reused and, if left unclosed, completed to a balanced pair, and the Tab key moves the caret out of an inserted pair — for !cast, from the type argument into the parentheses and finally behind them.
  • Completing a class or the list and bits types now also enters angled brackets that were already written but are still empty, and the Tab key moves the caret out of the brackets after the content has been written.
  • Added an error for bang operators that are missing their mandatory <type> argument, such as !cast(x), or that are given one although they do not take any, such as !add<int>(1, 2).

Fixed

  • Files reachable from the compile commands are now indexed right after opening a project, rather than only once a module's content roots happened to change afterwards. Their classes, defs and other definitions were previously not found by references, completion or find usages until e.g. CMake reconfigured.
  • Completing list or bits in front of already written angled brackets no longer inserts a second empty pair.
  • Selecting a class, list or bits completion by typing < no longer types that < into the angled brackets inserted by the completion.
  • Fixed an exception when an include points to a file that isn't a TableGen file.
  • TableGen files are now recognized based on the IDE's filetype setting rather than by extension.
  • Completion no longer pops up on its own while an integer literal is being written. Since TableGen identifiers may start with digits, typing e.g. 1 previously offered every identifier starting with that digit. The popup appears as soon as the text can no longer become an integer literal, and explicitly requesting completion still offers those identifiers.
  • A #ifdef, #ifndef, #define, #else or #endif in the middle of a line is no longer highlighted as a preprocessor directive after the line has been edited.

idea-plugin.name: Kolesa Commit Prefixer
idea-plugin.description:
Adds the name of the current Git branch to the beginning of the commit message and warns you before committing if the message does not reference it. Standard branches (main, master, develop) are left alone.
Works in every IntelliJ Platform IDE: IntelliJ IDEA, PhpStorm, GoLand, PyCharm, WebStorm, RubyMine, CLion, RustRover and Rider.

Добавляет название текущей git-ветки в начало сообщения коммита и предупреждает перед коммитом, если ссылки на неё в сообщении нет. Стандартные ветки (main, master, develop) не трогает.
Работает во всех IDE на IntelliJ Platform: IntelliJ IDEA, PhpStorm, GoLand, PyCharm, WebStorm, RubyMine, CLion, RustRover и Rider.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
3.1.0

  • ♻️ Improved: the button no longer stacks prefixes. If the message already starts with an issue key left over from another branch (KL-100 fix search), that key is replaced by the current branch instead of a second prefix being prepended.
  • ✅ Improved: if the leading key already points at the current branch's issue, the message is left untouched — including when the branch is feature/KL-123-fix and the message says just KL-123.
  • 🔕 Fixed: the pre-commit check accepts the branch's issue key on its own, so it stops asking about messages the button considers correct.

3.0.0

  • 🧩 Compatibility: supports 2023.3 and every newer build, including 2026.2. The upper bound is gone, so the plugin no longer stops working after an IDE update.
  • 🖇 Fixed: the button now works in the non-modal commit tool window, which is the default in all IDEs since 2020.3.
  • 🌿 Fixed: the branch is read through the Git plugin API instead of parsing .git/HEAD — worktrees, submodules and multi-root projects are handled correctly, and detached HEAD no longer produces garbage prefixes.
  • 🔕 Fixed: no more "Missing Issue Reference" dialog on main, master and develop — the button does not prefix those branches either.

idea-plugin.name: Highlight Status
idea-plugin.description:
Adds a status marker icon and/or a text behind the class name in the project view based on comment tags. E.g. // STATUS: DONE, // STATUS: TODO, // STATUS: INACTIVE, // STATUS: WIP. Also supports // ICON to show a custom icon.
The plugin is designed to be used in a team environment, where multiple developers are working on the same codebase. It helps to keep track of the status of each class and to communicate the progress of the work to other team members.
The plugin is not intended to be used as a task management tool, but rather as a way to visualize the status of the code in the project view.
If you want to exclude a specifc file from the status marker, you can add the comment // EXCLUDE FROM STATUS to the file. This will remove the status marker from the file in the project view.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Added Plugin Icon.

idea-plugin.name: Win1251ToUtf8
idea-plugin.description:
There are cases when old Java files contain multiple encodings — for example, a single file might include both Windows-1251 and UTF-8. In such situations, converting the file to one specific encoding often results in some lines being properly converted while others become corrupted. This plugin helps resolve such issues by safely converting Java files (or entire folders containing Java files) to UTF-8 only.

Using the plugin is simple: just select a file or folder, right-click it, and choose the "Convert to UTF-8" option — that's it! All lines with different encodings, as well as the file itself, will be correctly detected and converted to UTF-8.

For any questions, feel free to contact me via email: mr.kh0kh@yandex.ru
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Version 1.0.6

  • The chosen files will remain unchanged if their current encoding already matches the target encoding.

idea-plugin.name: Upcaser
idea-plugin.description:
Upcaser is an IntelliJ Platform plugin that automatically capitalises the first letter of sentences in any text file.

When you type a lowercase letter after sentence-ending punctuation (period, exclamation mark, or question mark) followed by whitespace, the plugin automatically converts it to uppercase.

Features:

  • Automatic capitalisation after periods (.), exclamation marks (!), question marks (?), ellipsis (...), and Markdown headers (#)
  • Works with any text file format, with special support for Markdown
  • Handles multiple spaces between punctuation and the next word

idea-plugin.name: Zoones IDE Assistant
idea-plugin.description:
Zoones IDE Assistant

Zoones IDE Assistant streamlines working across Java backends and JavaScript/TypeScript frontends and adds useful developer tooling. It helps you:

  • Cross-navigate between Java controller methods and JS/TS endpoints using JSDoc links like {@code {@link com.example.Controller#method}}.
  • See JS/TS usages of your Java endpoint when using Find Usages (Alt/Option+F7 on a Java method).
  • Highlight forbidden-apis usages directly in the Java editor based on your Maven configuration (de.thetaphi:forbiddenapis).
  • Run the test that covers a piece of code straight from a // Tested via ... comment, via a gutter icon.
  • Quickly convert concatenated strings to Java text blocks via an intention action.
  • Auto-generate the First-class support field required by the project datenwort.at/commons/first-class-property for classes annotated with @FirstClassSupport or @PropertyChangeSupport.

Prerequisites

  • IntelliJ IDEA with Java support.
  • For JS/TS features: the official JavaScript/TypeScript plugin must be enabled. This plugin declares an optional dependency to it.
  • For forbidden-apis highlighting: a Maven project using de.thetaphi:forbiddenapis configured in your pom.xml.

How the Java ↔ JS/TS navigation works

The plugin matches JSDoc references of the form {@code {@link #}} inside JS/TS function comments. It adds a gutter icon in JS/TS to jump to the referenced Java method, and a gutter icon in Java to jump to any JS/TS function(s) that reference the Java method.

JSDoc format

/**
 * Fetches items from backend
 * {@link com.example.api.ItemController#getItems}
 */
export function getItems() { /* ... */ }

Use the fully-qualified name (package + class) and the exact Java method name after #.

Find Usages integration (Java → JS/TS)

When you run Find Usages on a Java method, the results will include any JS/TS functions that reference it via the JSDoc link shown above. The search is narrowed to likely frontend files using configurable Java→TypeScript name mappings (see next section) for performance and precision.

Configuring TypeScript name mappings

Open Settings/Preferences → Tools → Zoones IDE Assistant. Configure how Java class names map to TypeScript file base names. Each rule has a Java regular expression (applied to the Java simple class name) and a replacement used as the TS file base name. The plugin also automatically considers a kebab-case variant of your replacement.

  • Default example rule: ^Ng(.*)$ → $1.service
    This maps NgBulkDataManager → BulkDataManager.service and also considers bulk-data-manager.service.
  • Rules are evaluated in order; the first match wins. Leave the table empty to fall back to a generic heuristic (*Service.ts or .service.ts).

The settings page includes a live preview that shows which TS base names your current Java file would map to.

forbidden-apis highlighting

If your module's pom.xml configures the de.thetaphi:forbiddenapis Maven plugin, this plugin parses the configuration and highlights forbidden method/constructor/field usages as you type. It supports bundled signatures, external signature files, and simple include/exclude patterns.

  • Messages from your signatures can be shown along with the highlight when available.
  • Exclusions in forbidden-apis config are respected (e.g., specific files or patterns), including class file paths relative to the classesDirectory (e.g., pkg/Clazz.class).
  • Support for <suppressAnnotations> in the Maven configuration: annotated methods or classes are ignored as configured.
  • Pre-Compile task runs as a visible, cancelable background task; scans only changed files or all files on rebuild.
  • Quick fixes: when a signature message includes a suggestion like Use '...' instead!, the editor offers one-click replacements:
    • Replace constructors (e.g., new HashMap(...) → new LinkedHashMap(...)).
    • Replace method calls (e.g., Collectors.toMap(...) → at.datenwort...CollectionUtils.toLinkedMap(...)).
    • Rewrite imports for package migrations (e.g., javax.* → jakarta.*, commons lang/collections upgrades).

First-class support auto-field

Automatically adds the required static field (default name p) to classes annotated with @FirstClassSupport or @PropertyChangeSupport, as specified by the First-class Property project. Enable this feature via Settings/Preferences → Tools → Zoones IDE Assistant → "First-class support" and optionally configure the field name. You can also trigger it manually from Tools → Zoones → "Generate First-class support field(s)" or from the Generate menu.

Run a test from a "Tested via" comment

Mark the code a test covers with a comment and start that test from the gutter icon next to it: 

// Tested via com.example.TestCommissionActions
// Tested via TestCommissionActions
// Tested via com.example.TestCommissionActions#testDistribution
// Tested via TestFoo, TestBar#testBaz
  • The class may be fully qualified or written as a plain simple name.
  • Append #methodName to run a single test method instead of the whole class.
  • Several references can be listed on one line, separated by commas; the icon then lets you pick one.
  • The marker is case-insensitive and works in any language that has comments — Java and Groovy scriptlets alike.
  • The icon only appears when the reference actually resolves to a class (or method) in your project, so prose such as tested via the nightly job stays untouched.
  • Running reuses an existing run configuration when there is one, otherwise it creates a temporary one, exactly like the run icons the IDE itself puts next to a test.
  • The icon can be switched off under Settings/Preferences → Editor → General → Gutter Icons → "Tested via".

Intention: Replace '+' with a text block using newlines

In Java files, use the intention on a concatenated multi-line string to convert it into a Java text block, inserting newlines at concatenation points. In contrast to the default tools IDEA provides, this feature changes our string in that regard. Invoke intentions with Alt/Option+Enter.

Troubleshooting

  • No gutter icons between Java and JS/TS?
    • Ensure your JSDoc uses the exact format: {@link <FQN>#<method>}, e.g., {@link com.example.Controller#getItems}.
    • Verify that the JavaScript/TypeScript plugin is enabled.
    • Adjust TypeScript name mappings in Settings → Tools → Zoones IDE Assistant so your frontend files are included in the search scope.
  • forbidden-apis highlights missing?
    • Confirm the Maven plugin is present and configured in your pom.xml for the module.
    • Check that your signature files/bundles resolve correctly and contain the expected entries.

Notes

  • The JS/TS features are only active when the JavaScript plugin is installed (optional dependency).
  • Mapping rules are stored per-project and can be edited at any time.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 2026-09-14 (1.13)
    • Forbidden-apis fix: @includeBundled directives in signature files were ignored. Every jdk-unsafe-* bundle from JDK 11 on consists of nothing else, so all of them silently contributed zero rules; they are now followed (with cycle protection).
    • Forbidden-apis fix: the pom.xml reader looked up child elements anywhere in the subtree instead of directly beneath their parent. As a result the first <signaturesFile> inside a <signaturesFiles> list was parsed twice, and an <execution>'s <configuration> was additionally read as if it were the plugin-wide one, producing a spurious extra configuration.
    • Text block intention fix: the conversion wrote straight to the editor document without asking for write permission first, so invoking it on a read-only (for example VCS-locked) file failed with an error instead of offering to unlock it.
    • Test coverage now spans every feature of the plugin (10 → 115 tests); the three fixes above were all found by writing it.
  • 2026-09-14 (1.12)
    • New: run a test straight from a // Tested via ... comment through a gutter icon. Accepts a fully qualified or simple class name, an optional #methodName to run a single test method, and a comma separated list. The icon appears only when the reference resolves in the project, works in any language with comments (Groovy scriptlets included), and can be turned off under Settings → Editor → General → Gutter Icons → "Tested via".
    • Forbidden-apis: updated the bundled de.thetaphi:forbiddenapis signatures from 3.8 to 3.10, which adds the jdk-deprecated-24/25 and jdk-internal-24/25 bundles along with newer commons-io-unsafe entries, so those bundled signatures now resolve instead of being silently skipped.
    • Build: upgraded Gradle wrapper to 9.7.1, IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin to 2.18.1, Kotlin plugin to 2.4.20 and AssertJ to 3.27.7. The pluginVerification.ides block moved from the removed ide(...) helper to create(...), and options.release is now pinned to 21 — since IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.16.0 it is derived from the Java toolchain and overrides source/targetCompatibility, which would otherwise have shipped Java 25 bytecode.
    • Verified as compatible against IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate 2024.2.5, 2025.2.6.3 and 2026.2.2.
  • 2026-04-27
    • Fix high CPU caused by FirstClassSupportAutoFieldService: every PSI tree change in a Java file used to submit (and almost immediately cancel) a background read action, which thrashed the app pool during typing. Events are now debounced through a per-file pending set drained by a 300 ms idle pooled-thread alarm. The listener also filters out non-writable, non-source, and library-content files.
  • 2026-04-26
    • Fix EDT freeze caused by FirstClassSupportAutoFieldService: PSI discovery now runs in a non-blocking read action off the EDT; the write action only applies the resulting field add/remove operations. Replaced getAllInnerClasses() (which walked the super-class hierarchy and triggered index updates) with direct-children recursion.
    • Replaced deprecated IntelliJ Platform API usages: ReadAction.run/compute, commons-lang3 StringUtils.contains, and the single-arg PsiManager.removePsiTreeChangeListener (now uses a child Disposable).
    • Build: upgraded Gradle wrapper to 9.1.0, IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin to 2.9.0, and Kotlin plugin to 2.2.0; project now compiles with a JDK 25 toolchain (output remains Java 21 to match the IntelliJ JBR).
  • 2025-10-01
    • Forbidden-apis: Configuration lookup fixed.
  • 2025-08-21
    • Forbidden-apis: Action to navigate to where the rule is configured in your pom.xml.
  • 2025-08-17
    • More configuration options.
  • 2025-08-16
    • Forbidden-apis: do not scan generated source, bugfixing.
  • 2025-08-15
    • Forbidden-apis: parameter-aware signatures — now() matches only zero-arg calls, now(**) matches any args.
    • Forbidden-apis: configuration auto-reloads on changes to pom.xml or signature files (VFS listener with per-module cache invalidation).
    • Forbidden-apis: Pre-Compile task runs as a visible, cancelable background task; scans only changed files or all files on rebuild.
  • 2025-08-14
    • Forbidden-apis: support excludes that are class-file paths relative to the classesDirectory (e.g., pkg/Clazz.class).
    • Forbidden-apis: support <suppressAnnotations> to ignore annotated classes/methods as configured.
    • Forbidden-apis: add quick fixes based on “Use '…' instead!” suggestions in signatures: constructor/method replacements and import rewrite for package migrations (e.g., javax→jakarta, commons upgrades).
  • Add: Auto-generate First-class support field (@FirstClassSupport/@PropertyChangeSupport). See: https://gitlab.com/datenwort.at/commons/first-class-property

idea-plugin.name: Google Apps Script Support
idea-plugin.description:
Google Apps Script Support

Professional IDE support for Google Apps Script development with advanced language features and comprehensive API completion.

✨ Key Features (FREE)

Modern JavaScript/ES2020+ Syntax Support:

  • Classes with getters/setters and private fields/methods (#privateField, #privateMethod)
  • Modern operators: optional chaining (?.), nullish coalescing (??), spread (...), exponentiation (**)
  • Async/await in arrow functions and generators (function*, yield)
  • Template literals with expression interpolation
  • Destructuring with nested patterns, defaults, rest, and skipped array elements in functions and callbacks
  • Modern control flow: logical assignments and catch blocks without an unused error parameter
  • For await...of loops
  • Bitwise operators, including compound shift assignments

Smart Code Completion (17 GAS Services, 230+ methods):

  • SpreadsheetApp - Complete Spreadsheet, Sheet, Range API
  • DocumentApp - Document manipulation and formatting
  • GmailApp - Email management and thread operations
  • DriveApp - File and folder operations
  • CalendarApp - Calendar and event management
  • FormApp, SlidesApp - Forms and Presentations
  • HtmlService, UrlFetchApp - Web apps and HTTP requests
  • ScriptApp, PropertiesService - Script configuration
  • CacheService, LockService - Performance optimization
  • Utilities, MailApp, ContentService, GroupsApp

Code Navigation:

  • Go to Definition - Jump to function, variable, class declarations
  • Find Usages - Find all references across your project
  • Smart navigation for functions, variables, parameters, classes

Development Experience:

  • Beautiful syntax highlighting for all Google Apps Script files
  • Intelligent refactoring support for renaming and restructuring code
  • Error detection and quick fixes
  • Project configuration management

🚀 Premium Google Integration

  • Connect one Google account with the verified read-only Apps Script scope.
  • Compare the current file in a valid clasp project with Apps Script remote HEAD in an IDE-native diff.
  • No push, pull, deployment, execution, or local/remote content changes.

All existing editing features remain free.

Perfect for: Professional developers building Google Apps Script projects, add-ons, and automation solutions.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Version 3.0.0

  • Premium Google sign-in: Connect one Google account through the verified OAuth flow.
  • Read-only remote comparison: Compare the current local clasp file with Apps Script remote HEAD in an IDE-native diff.
  • Safe by design: Uses only the read-only Apps Script project-content scope and never pushes, pulls, deploys, executes, or changes source.
  • All existing editing, completion, navigation, and project-file support remains free.

Version 2.0.0

  • More expressive functions and callbacks: Use nested object and array destructuring, default values, rest parameters, and skipped array elements when processing rows and structured data.
  • Flexible lists: Write sparse arrays and trailing commas in function parameters and calls.
  • Modern operators and error handling: Use &&=, ||=, >>=, and catch { ... } without false syntax errors.
  • Property access fixes: Access private members and properties named with keywords, including optional chains.
  • Apps Script project recognition: Recognizes .clasp.json, appsscript.json, and .claspignore as project files supported by the plugin.
  • Work has started on synchronization with Google; it is not available in this release.

Version 1.0.0 - First Stable Release

🎉 Major Features

  • Complete ES2020+ JavaScript Support:
    • Modern class syntax with private fields and methods (#privateField, #privateMethod)
    • Optional chaining (?.), nullish coalescing (??), spread operator (...)
    • Async/await, generator functions (function*, yield)
    • Template literals with expression interpolation
    • Arrow functions with destructuring parameters
    • For await...of loops
    • Bitwise operators and exponentiation (**)
  • Comprehensive Google Apps Script API Completion:
    • 17 GAS services with 230+ methods and properties
    • SpreadsheetApp with complete Sheet, Range, Spreadsheet classes
    • DocumentApp, GmailApp, DriveApp, CalendarApp
    • FormApp, SlidesApp, HtmlService, UrlFetchApp
    • ScriptApp, PropertiesService, Utilities
    • CacheService, LockService, ContentService, GroupsApp
    • Smart context-aware completion
  • Smart Code Navigation:
    • Go to Definition for functions, variables, classes, parameters
    • Find Usages across entire project
    • Scope-aware symbol resolution

🛠 Development Experience

  • Beautiful syntax highlighting for all Google Apps Script code
  • Intelligent code analysis and error detection
  • Fast and responsive IDE integration
  • Seamless error reporting to help improve the plugin

📦 Platform Support

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2025.2+ (build 252+)
  • All JetBrains IDEs with language support
  • Java 21+ required

💡 Freemium Model Introduced

  • All core editing features are FREE forever
  • Premium features (cloud integration, remote execution) coming soon
  • No feature limitations in this initial release

Note: This is the first stable release. Cloud integration features (OAuth2, project sync, remote execution) are planned for future premium versions.

idea-plugin.name: Ravel Remapper
idea-plugin.description:
Ravel is a plugin for IntelliJ IDEA to remap source files, based on PSI and Mapping-IO.

Install it from JetBrains Marketplace or download it manually from GitHub Release.

Supports remapping:

  • Java
  • Kotlin
  • Mixin and MixinExtras1
  • Class Tweaker / Access Widener

1MixinExtras Expression is not supported.

Usage

See the page at Fabric Docs for remapping Fabric Mods!

  1. Commit any changes before attempting to remap your sources!

  2. Right-click the code editor and go to Refactor - Remap Using Ravel

idea-plugin.name: LookML Support

Findings appear in the Looker Validation tool window, where severity counts filter the list, identical findings are grouped with a count, and a click opens the file and line. Everything else an IDE should give you, for LookML. Jump to where a field or view is defined, even through extends and refinements. Rename it everywhere at once. Complete dashboard properties instead of looking them up. Reformat a dashboard and get the layout Looker itself writes. All of it on your own machine, at editor speed.

Buy once, keep it, including everything added later. Pro is a one-time purchase with no subscription, and every future Pro feature arrives as a free update. The price rises as those features ship, so today is the cheapest it will ever be. Current offers: andriikobtsev.github.io/lookml-plugin/#offer. Pro is free during the trial, and the free features never expire.

Getting started guide | Website | End User License Agreement

Free and Pro

Free (no license, no expiry, no network): syntax highlighting, file type recognition, code folding, commenting, brace matching, quote handling, and color settings.

Pro: Validate with Looker, code completion (150+ dashboard properties plus in-sql: field suggestions), dashboard property validation, code formatting for LookML and YAML dashboards, and code navigation - go-to-definition, find usages, rename, and go-to-implementation/super across extended and refined views and YAML dashboards. Try Pro free during the evaluation period (length shown on the listing); after the trial, activate via Help | Register (JetBrains account + license). The free features keep working regardless.

Everything in the box

  • Validate with Looker - Looker's own project validator, run on demand against the files you have on disk, with findings you can click through to. Needs a Looker instance URL and API credentials, entered under Settings | Tools | Looker Connection; the secret goes to the IDE credential store, never to a file. Setup takes five minutes: getting started guide.
  • Code navigation - go-to-definition, find usages, rename, and go-to-implementation/super for LookML fields and views, across extended and refined views and YAML dashboards.
  • Code formatting - Reformat Code for traditional LookML; YAML Looker dashboards use the same action plus an optional Reformat YAML Dashboard shortcut (see change notes for keys).
  • YAML dashboard formatting - the layout Looker itself writes, so a reformat never turns a working dashboard into one Looker rejects.
  • YAML dashboard completion - 150+ properties with descriptions.
  • Validation - syntax errors for traditional LookML, plus checks for YAML dashboard properties and duplicate dashboard file names.
  • Syntax highlighting - keywords, strings, SQL blocks, field references.
  • Commenting, brace matching, folding - standard IDE editing aids.
  • Manifest files - manifest.lkml support (project_name, constant, local_dependency, remote_dependency, and more).
  • Code style - Settings | Editor | Code Style | LookML (default 2-space indent).
  • File types - .lkml, .lookml.

Supported syntax

  • YAML-style Looker dashboards

Roadmap

A Pro license includes future Pro features as free updates. Next up: content validation - asking Looker which saved dashboards and Looks a code change breaks, and jumping from that answer to the code responsible. These are planned directions, not dated commitments; the price rises as they ship.

Source code & license (GitHub)

idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.3.0 - Validate with Looker (Pro)

Find Looker validation errors before you commit. Run Looker's own validator from the IDE on the LookML you have on disk, instead of finding out from a failed pull request. Findings appear in the Looker Validation tool window, where severity counts filter the list, identical findings are grouped with a count, and a click opens the file and line. Connect your instance once under Settings | Tools | Looker Connection, then run Validate with Looker whenever you like; it never runs on its own. Your secret is kept in the IDE credential store. Test Connection tells you which of three things is wrong, the URL, the credentials, or a missing develop permission, and Copy Request for Admin puts a ready-to-send request on your clipboard when only an administrator can fix it. Setup takes five minutes: getting started guide.

Validation runs in your own Looker development workspace, never in production, and never resets a branch or force pushes. When you have committed and pushed, run Reset Looker Workspace to Local Files and the Looker web IDE will pull without first asking you to commit. It asks before discarding anything, never touches your local files, and stops with an explanation when it cannot do the job safely.

Also new: new files and new folders validate too, so a brand new dashboard folder can be checked without opening the Looker web IDE. A duplicate dashboard name is reported on its dashboard: line as you work, since Looker keeps dashboard names in one namespace, and a failed upload names the file it collided with.

Fixed

  • Reformatting a traditional view or explore could strip its indentation entirely if the file happened to mention a dashboard, for instance in an include: path. Such files were mistaken for YAML dashboards; they are now laid out as the LookML they are.
  • Reformatting a YAML dashboard could move a nested block such as conditional_formatting: out from under the key that owned it, turning a working dashboard into one Looker rejects. Files Looker wrote come back unchanged, over-long fields: arrays are wrapped the way Looker wraps them, and unsafe reformats are refused rather than written.
  • Visualisation settings inside a dashboard element, such as y_axes: and the series: list in it, are no longer flagged as unknown properties.
  • Field exclusions such as fields: [ALL_FIELDS*, -orders.status] are no longer reported as syntax errors, and navigation and rename work on the properties around them.
  • field: in YAML dashboards now works with Go to Definition, Find Usages and Rename.

Free for everyone: set: blocks fold, each YAML dashboard element has its own fold arrow labelled with its title, and the file icon renders identically on every platform.

One-time price, and it rises as features ship. Pro includes every future Pro feature as a free update, so buying now locks in the lowest price. Current offers: andriikobtsev.github.io/lookml-plugin/#offer.

Tell me what to build next. I build this alone, and a review, a GitHub issue, or an email to andrii.kobtsev@gmail.com reaches me directly. I answer every one.

The release-version moves to 20263, so active trials restart.

2026.2.1 - what changed

Fewer interruptions. The Pro notice no longer returns on every project open: it appears at most once per version, and only when you open a LookML file, so it never interrupts unrelated work. It also now correctly lists code navigation, find usages, and rename among the Pro features. The formatting notice is remembered across restarts instead of coming back every session, and the license dialog opens the plugin's Marketplace page directly.

New: a single, dismissible prompt asking you to review the plugin, shown only after you have actually used it across several separate days. Dismiss it once and it never returns.

No feature or licensing changes. Nothing you rely on has moved.

2026.2.0 - Code navigation (Pro)

New Pro navigation for LookML fields and views, across extended and refined views and YAML dashboards:

  • Go to Definition - jump from a ${field} / view.field reference to its dimension, measure, set, constant, or named_value_format; from from: / view_name: to the view; and from dashboard fields/explores/models to their declarations.
  • Find Usages (Alt+F7) and Rename - project-wide, scoped to the view family (base + refinements + extends), so unrelated same-named fields are left alone.
  • Go to Implementation(s) (Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+B) and Go to Super (Ctrl/Cmd+U) - move between a base view and the views that extend or refine it; matching gutter icons too.
  • Field completion in sql: - inside ${...}, suggests the fields available to the view, including everything inherited up the extends chain.

Formatting fixes:

  • Function calls in sql: keep the name tight to the parenthesis (DATE_TRUNC(...), not DATE_TRUNC (...)), and there is no space before a comma (SELECT a, b).
  • Multi-line sql: blocks (e.g. a derived_table query) keep their line breaks and indentation instead of collapsing onto one line.
  • derived_table and explore_source blocks are laid out one property per line instead of collapsing onto a single line.

Also: Pro features now turn on right after you activate a license, without needing an IDE restart.

These are Pro features (free during the trial). All free editing features are unchanged. Known limitations: navigation inside Liquid expressions is not yet resolved, and Find Usages on a dimension_group does not yet list its generated timeframe fields (e.g. created_month).

Existing users - thank you. The productivity features are now Pro, but your free features keep working with no license. For pricing and any current offer, see the website. Buy at the founding price and lock it in - future Pro features arrive as free updates.

2026.1.0

Important for existing users: LookML Support is moving to a freemium model. Code completion, dashboard validation, and code formatting are becoming Pro features, with a free trial. The plugin stays free to install, and syntax highlighting and basic editing stay free forever. Start the trial or activate Pro via Help | Register.

  • Pro (free trial included): code completion (150+ properties), schema-backed dashboard validation, and formatting (Reformat Code Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+L, Reformat YAML Dashboard Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Y).
  • Free: syntax highlighting, file type recognition, folding, commenting, brace matching, and quote handling.
  • Founding offer: Pro is available at an early one-time price. Buy once to own it for good and get all future features (go-to-definition planned) as free updates. The price rises as the plugin grows.

Also new in this release:

  • Manifest files: manifest.lkml support for project_name, constant, local_dependency, remote_dependency, override_constant, and new_lookml_runtime.
  • Better dashboard validation: fewer false "unknown property" warnings; covers table calculations (dynamic_fields), filters, and text tiles.
  • More robust dashboard formatting: arrays stay arrays, block scalars and nested blocks (such as dynamic_fields) are preserved, and multi-line field lists are handled.
  • Fixes: dashboards with a leading comment before --- now parse correctly; emoji in text tiles are supported; formatting runs only on an explicit reformat, not while typing.
  • Code style: LookML indent defaults in Settings | Editor | Code Style | LookML.
  • Compatibility: sinceBuild 251 (IntelliJ 2025.1+).

Version 1.2.0 - Code Formatter

  • NEW: Code formatter for traditional LookML (Cmd/Ctrl+Alt/Option+L)
  • NEW: SQL formatting - blocks on single line with proper spacing
  • NEW: Template expressions formatted: ${TABLE} with no spaces
  • NEW: Smart 2-space indentation based on block structure
  • FIXED: Lexer now parses numbers correctly (prevents "100" becoming "1 0 0")
  • FIXED: SQL tokens no longer include trailing whitespace

Version 1.1.0 - YAML Dashboard Autocomplete

  • NEW: YAML dashboard autocomplete with 150+ properties
  • NEW: Dashboard-level properties (title, layout, filters, elements, etc.)
  • NEW: Element properties (type, model, explore, fields, charts, tables, maps)
  • NEW: Filter properties (name, type, ui_config, listens_to_filters, etc.)
  • NEW: Visualization type suggestions (looker_line, looker_column, single_value, etc.)
  • NEW: Context-aware property suggestions based on YAML structure
  • Type a few letters and press Ctrl+Space to see intelligent suggestions!

Version 1.0.0 - Initial Release

  • Full LookML syntax highlighting

  • Code commenting (line and block)

idea-plugin.name: Lazyime
idea-plugin.description:
Lazyime is an intelligent Input Method Editor (IME) switcher for JetBrains IDEs.
It leverages Tree-sitter for real-time syntax analysis to automatically switch between English and your native language based on the cursor context (Code vs. Comment). It also switches automatically when using the IDE tool window.

Lazyime

智能感知上下文，自动切换输入法

基于 Tree-sitter 语法分析 | 适配 JetBrains 全家桶 | 低延迟体验

✨ 简介

Lazyime 是一款专为 JetBrains IDE 设计的智能输入法切换插件。它通过与高性能的 Rust 后端服务 LazyInputSwitcher 通信，利用 Tree-sitter 进行实时的代码语法分析。

它能精确识别你当前的光标是在 编写代码 还是 撰写注释，并据此自动切换系统输入法，让你在编码时无需频繁手动切换中英文。

🚀 核心功能

  • ⚡️ 语法感知切换：
    • 代码区域 (Code) ➔ 自动切换为 英文模式。
    • 注释区域 (Comment) ➔ 自动切换为 系统输入法 (中文/母语)。
  • 🪟 工具窗口适配：
    • 针对 Project (项目)、Run (运行)、Commit (提交)、Terminal (终端) 常用工具窗口提供独立的输入法预设。
  • 🔌 配置管理：
    • 插件内置管理界面，支持设置工具窗口的目标输入法与手动安装、更新后端服务。

⚙️ 架构原理

插件作为客户端，通过 TCP 协议与本地运行的 Rust 服务端 (LazyInputSwitcher) 通信。

  1. 事件触发：当你在 IDE 中移动光标或修改代码时，插件会收集当前文档的内容、语言类型及光标位置。
  2. 异步分析与切换：插件将数据发送给服务端，服务端进行语法分析与输入法切换（响应通常 < 5ms）。

📦 安装与配置

1. 安装插件

在 JetBrains IDE 中打开 Settings -> Plugins -> Marketplace，搜索 Lazyime 并安装。

2. 配置服务端 (必要步骤)

由于服务端包含不同平台的二进制文件，默认不随插件打包。你需要手动进行初始化：

  1. 打开 Settings。
  2. 找到Lazyime 设置页。
  3. 在 服务端 分组下，点击 安装 按钮。
  4. 等待安装完成后，重启 IDE。

3. 设置页面

在设置页面的 工具窗口输入法分组中，你可以为不同的 IDE 工具窗口指定默认输入法行为：

  • Run Window: 默认 English
  • Project View: 默认 English
  • Commit Dialog: 默认 English
  • Terminal: 默认 English

在设置页面的 Ide窗口行为分组中，同时可以为Ide焦点设置不同的行为：

  • 无： 不做任何操作
  • 英语： 将输入法切换到英文输入法
  • 母语： 将输入法切换到母语输入法

注意：在windows平台下，由于windows的安全策略，在Ide失焦时尝试输入法切换大概率失败

💻 操作系统支持与注意事项

由于涉及到底层输入法切换，不同操作系统的配置略有差异。

Windows

  • 支持：微软拼音输入法 (默认支持: 简体中文, 美国英语)。
  • 注意：受限于 Windows 安全机制，系统中必须安装 至少两种 语言的键盘布局（例如：中文 + 英文），切换功能才能正常工作。

Linux

  • 支持：Fcitx5 输入法框架 (默认支持: rime, pinyin , keyboard-us)。
  • 注意：如果自动下载的二进制文件无法运行，请检查插件 bin 目录下文件的执行权限 (chmod +x)。

macOS

  • 支持：系统默认输入法 (默认支持: ABC / 简体拼音)。
  • 注意：
    • 自动安装的可执行文件可能因安全策略无法直接运行。
    • 解决方案：建议手动编译 Rust 服务端，或前往插件安装目录的 bin 文件夹下，通过终端赋予可执行权限，并在“安全性与隐私”中允许运行。

自定义输入法

如果你使用的输入法不在上述预定义列表中

你需要克隆服务端仓库，修改对应平台的源码中预定义的输入法 ID 或 字符串

  • src/switch/
    • /windows/mod.rs: NATIVE_LANGUAGE_ID
    • /linux/fcitx5.rs: NATIVE_METHOD
    • /macos/mod.rs: NATIVE_LANGUAGE_ID

并重新编译服务端替换插件 bin 目录下的文件。

💖 贡献者

🔗 链接

  • 服务端源码: LazyInputSwitcher
  • 问题反馈: GitHub Issues

idea-plugin.name: cztctl
idea-plugin.description:
cztctl - DSL Plugin for go-zero Microservice Framework

IDE plugin for cztctl, an extended code generation tool for the go-zero microservice framework. Provides syntax highlighting, semantic coloring, syntax error checking, code completion, code navigation, and live templates for .cron (scheduled tasks), .rabbitmq (message queue) and .task (dingtalk-stream event/stream consumers) DSL files.

语法高亮 + 语义着色

基于 ANTLR4 全量解析，覆盖 DSL 全部语法元素，并提供上下文感知的语义配色：

  • 关键字 — syntax、info、import、type、service（模块关键字加粗斜体高亮）
  • 注解 — @server（独立配色）、@doc、@handler、@cron、@cronRetry；.task 的 @topic/@topicRef/@parse/@parseType/@parseImport（dingtalk-stream，紫色）及任意自定义 @注解
  • 类型系统 — 结构体名称（加粗）、字段名称、字段类型、struct tag 各有独立颜色
  • 路由行 — cron 任务标识符、rabbitmq 队列名称、路由参数（加粗斜体）
  • info / @server 模块 — KV 键名独立配色，@server 非字符串值斜体高亮
  • service 模块 — 服务名称、handler 名称、注解关键字各有独立颜色
  • 注释 — 单行注释 //、块注释 /* */
  • 字符串 — 双引号字符串、反引号原始字符串

语法错误检查

基于 ANTLR4 Parser 全量解析，实时检测语法错误并以红色波浪线标注：

  • 缺少必填声明（syntax / service）
  • 括号/大括号不匹配
  • 注解格式错误（@cron / @handler / @doc）
  • 结构体字段定义错误
  • service route 格式错误

代码导航

Ctrl+Click（或 Cmd+Click）跳转：

  • 路由参数 — 点击路由行中的类型参数（如 OrderCancelReq），跳转到对应的 type 定义
  • import 路径 — 点击 import 的文件路径字符串，打开对应文件
  • 支持跨文件解析：自动在当前文件和 import 引入的文件中查找类型定义

代码补全

上下文感知补全（Ctrl+Space，或输入 @ 自动触发）：

  • service 块内 — 按文件类型补全路由注解：@doc、@handler；.cron 追加 @cron/@cronRetry；.task 追加 @topic/@topicRef/@parse/@parseType/@parseImport（标注 dingtalk-stream）
  • 顶层 — 补全模块关键字：syntax、info、import、type、service、@server
  • 选中后插入带占位骨架并定位光标（如 @topic "" 光标落入引号内）
  • 补全不限制输入：.task 的注解是开放的，具体哪些生效由远程 -template 决定，可自由输入任意 @注解

快速创建文件

右键目录 → New 菜单中提供：

  • Cron File (.cron) — 创建带基础结构的 .cron 定时任务文件
  • RabbitMQ File (.rabbitmq) — 创建带基础结构的 .rabbitmq 消息队列文件
  • Task File (.task) — 创建带基础结构的 .task 事件/流消费文件

Live Templates（代码模板）

输入缩写后按 Tab 键即可快速展开，共 26 个模板：

缩写说明
syntaxsyntax 版本声明
infoinfo 元信息块
importimport 单文件导入
typetype 结构体声明
typegtype 分组结构体声明
server@server 注解块
serverfull@server 完整注解块（tags/summary/group/middleware）
serviceservice 服务块
@doc@doc 字符串文档注解
@dockv@doc KV 文档注解
@handler@handler 处理器名称
@cron@cron 定时表达式
@cronRetry@cronRetry 重试次数
crontask完整的内部定时任务（@doc + @cron + @cronRetry + @handler + 路由）
exttask外部触发任务（无 @cron，仅 @doc + @handler + 路由）
consumerRabbitMQ 消费者（@doc + @handler + 队列路由）
cronfile.cron 完整文件模板
mqfile.rabbitmq 完整文件模板
@topic.task dingtalk-stream 事件 topic
@topicRef.task dingtalk-stream topic 常量引用
@parse.task dingtalk-stream 解析函数引用
@parseType.task dingtalk-stream 解析目标类型
@parseImport.task dingtalk-stream 解析类型 import 路径
streamtask.task EVENT 型 stream 任务（@topic）
streamtaskfull.task CALLBACK 型 stream 任务（@topicRef + @parse）
taskfile.task 完整文件模板

支持的文件类型

  • *.cron — 定时任务服务定义文件
  • *.rabbitmq — RabbitMQ 消息队列消费者服务定义文件
  • *.task — 钉钉 dingtalk-stream 事件/流消费服务定义文件

DSL 语法示例

.cron 文件：


syntax = "v1"

info (
    title: "定时任务服务"
    desc: "订单超时自动取消"
)

type OrderCancelReq {
    OrderId int64 `json:"orderId"`
}

@server (
    group: order
)
service order-cron {
    @doc "订单超时取消"
    @cron "*/5 * * * *"
    @cronRetry 3
    @handler OrderCancel
    OrderCancelTask(OrderCancelReq)
}

.rabbitmq 文件：


syntax = "v1"

type PaymentMsg {
    OrderId int64  `json:"orderId"`
    Amount  string `json:"amount"`
}

service payment-mq {
    @doc "支付成功回调"
    @handler PaymentSuccess
    payment.success(PaymentMsg)
}

.task 文件（dingtalk-stream）：


syntax = "v1"

type (
    BpmsInstanceChangeMsg {
        ProcessInstanceId string `json:"processInstanceId"`
    }
)

@server (
    group: dingtalk
)
service streamSvc {
    @doc "审批实例变更事件（EVENT）"
    @topic "bpms_instance_change"
    @handler BpmsInstanceChange
    BpmsInstanceChangeTask(BpmsInstanceChangeMsg)

    @doc "机器人消息（CALLBACK）"
    @topicRef stream.TopicChatBot
    @parse stream.ParseChatBotMessage
    @parseType "*chatbot.BotCallbackDataModel"
    @parseImport "github.com/open-dingtalk/dingtalk-stream-sdk-go/chatbot"
    @handler ChatBotMessage
    ChatBotMessageTask
}

idea-plugin.name: Code Line Tracker
idea-plugin.description:
Code Line Tracker gives you real-time visibility into your coding activity, right in the status bar. Ever wondered how many lines you actually write, refactor, or delete in a session? Now you can see it at a glance.

Features

  • Live Line Counter — See +added and -deleted lines updating in real-time as you code
  • Commit Mode — Automatically activates when you open the Commit panel, showing VCS diff stats for your staged changes
  • Per-File Breakdown — Click the widget to see detailed stats for each file you have touched
  • File Selection — Select specific files in the popup to see aggregated stats, with Select All / None shortcuts
  • Sort Toggle — Switch between alphabetical (A-Z) and most-changed-first sorting
  • Commit Selected — Exclude files from commit directly from the popup, then press Commit Selected to open the Commit panel with only your chosen files
  • Changes Tab Decoration — Each changelist shows its own diff totals based on the files it contains

Why Use It?

  • Track your daily coding output for standups and reports
  • Prove your productivity — especially useful when your company tracks lines-per-commit metrics
  • Get a quick overview before committing: how big is this change?
  • Zero configuration — install and it just works

How It Works

  1. Session Mode — Tracks every edit in real-time using git diff
  2. Commit Mode — Auto-switches when the Commit panel opens, calculates actual VCS diffs for staged files
  3. Click the Total : N || +N -N widget in the status bar for the full per-file breakdown

idea-plugin.name: emacsJump
idea-plugin.description:
Porting some great extensions of emacs to Intellij IDEA. such as AceJump, CopyWithoutSelectAction. And new created EditWithoutSelection (Cut/Move/Replace without selection).

AceJump

  • C-L 't' 'm' : Basic Word Jump | Type C-L, then type target char (eg. 't') to jump to, then type marker char (eg. 'm') to move caret.
  • C-J 't' 'm' : Basic Char Jump

AceJump, jump to special place

  • C-L ' ' 'm' : Jump to line end or start. | To show marker on line end and line start, type space ' ' as target char
  • C-L ',' 'm' : Jump to symbol key | Show markers on .{}(|`/\;.{}()[]?_=-+'"!@#$%^&*)_=

Copy without selection:

  • C-c w : Copy word
  • C-c s : Copy string
  • C-c l : Copy line
  • C-c b : Copy block between balanced { and }
  • C-c q : Copy quoted, such as abcd in "abcd"
  • C-c a : Copy to line beginning
  • C-c A : Copy to file beginning
  • C-c e : Copy to line end
  • C-c E : Copy to file end
  • C-c p : Copy paragraph
  • C-c g : Copy paragraph group (e.g.: entire function including white lines)
  • C-c u : Copy to paragraph begining
  • C-c d : Copy to paragraph end
  • C-c , : Copy current argument in the current innermost argument list
  • C-c 9 : Copy arguments before caret in the current innermost argument list
  • C-c 0 : Copy arguments after caret in the current innermost argument list
  • C-c ' ' (w | s | l | q | a | A | e | E | p | g | u | d | b) : Type one space to cut related area
  • C-c ' ' ' ' (w | s | l | q | a | A | e | E | p | g | u | d | b) : Type two space to select related area

Argument-aware selectors:

  • , : current argument in the current innermost argument list
  • 9 : arguments before caret in the current innermost argument list
  • 0 : arguments after caret in the current innermost argument list
  • , / 9 / 0 can be used with C-c, C-w, C-d, C-o, C-i, and C-x
  • C-w C-(, | 9 | 0), C-d C-(, | 9 | 0), C-o C-(, | 9 | 0), C-i C-(, | 9 | 0), and C-x C-(, | 9 | 0) now jump by immediate markers on visible argument anchors

Replace target (word | line | paragraph) with text at current caret:

  • C-i C-w 't' 'm' : replace target word
  • C-i C-s 't' 'm' : replace target string
  • C-i C-l 't' 'm' : replace target line
  • C-i C-b 't' 'm' : replace target block
  • C-i C-q 't' 'm' : replace target quote
  • C-i C-a 't' 'm' : replace target to line begining
  • C-i C-e 't' 'm' : replace target char to line end
  • C-i C-p 't' 'm' : replace target paragraph
  • C-i C-g 't' 'm' : replace target paragraph group
  • C-i C-u 't' 'm' : replace target to paragraph beginning
  • C-i C-d 't' 'm' : replace target to paragraph end

Obtain target (word | line | paragraph), then replace text at current caret:

  • C-o C-w 't' 'm' : obtain target word, then replace current word
  • C-o C-s 't' 'm' : obtain target string, then replace current string
  • C-o C-l 't' 'm' : obtain target line, then replace current line
  • C-o C-b 't' 'm' : obtain target block
  • C-o C-q 't' 'm' : obtain target quote
  • C-o C-a 't' 'm' : obtain target to line beginning
  • C-o C-e 't' 'm' : obtain target char to line end
  • C-o C-p 't' 'm' : obtain target paragraph
  • C-o C-g 't' 'm' : obtain target paragraph group
  • C-o C-u 't' 'm' : obtain target to paragraph beginning
  • C-o C-d 't' 'm' : obtain target to paragraph end

Copy target (word | line | paragraph), then insert text at current caret:

  • C-w C-w 't' 'm' : Copy target word, then insert at current caret
  • C-w C-s 't' 'm' : Copy target string, then insert at current caret
  • C-w C-l 't' 'm' : Copy target line, then insert at current caret
  • C-w C-b 't' 'm' : Copy target block
  • C-w C-q 't' 'm' : Copy target quote
  • C-w C-a 't' 'm' : Copy target to line beginning
  • C-w C-e 't' 'm' : Copy target char to line end
  • C-w C-p 't' 'm' : Copy target paragraph
  • C-w C-g 't' 'm' : Copy target paragraph group
  • C-w C-u 't' 'm' : Copy target to paragraph beginning
  • C-w C-d 't' 'm' : Copy target to paragraph end

Cut target (word | line | paragraph), then insert text at current caret:

  • C-x C-w 't' 'm' : Cut target word, then insert at current caret
  • C-x C-s 't' 'm' : Cut target string, then insert at current caret
  • C-x C-l 't' 'm' : Cut target line, then insert at current caret
  • C-x C-b 't' 'm' : Cut target block
  • C-x C-q 't' 'm' : Cut target quote
  • C-x C-a 't' 'm' : Cut target to line beginning
  • C-x C-e 't' 'm' : Cut target char to line end
  • C-x C-p 't' 'm' : Cut target paragraph
  • C-x C-g 't' 'm' : Cut target paragraph group
  • C-x C-u 't' 'm' : Cut target to paragraph beginning
  • C-x C-d 't' 'm' : Cut target to paragraph end

Delete target (word | line | paragraph...)

  • C-d C-w 't' 'm' : delete target word
  • C-d C-s 't' 'm' : delete target string
  • C-d C-l 't' 'm' : delete target line
  • C-d C-b 't' 'm' : delete target block
  • C-d C-q 't' 'm' : delete target quote
  • C-d C-a 't' 'm' : delete target to line beginning
  • C-d C-e 't' 'm' : delete target char to line end
  • C-d C-p 't' 'm' : delete target paragraph
  • C-d C-g 't' 'm' : delete target paragraph group
  • C-d C-u 't' 'm' : delete target to paragraph beginning
  • C-d C-d 't' 'm' : delete target to paragraph end


Highlight symbol:

  • C-, : hightlight-symbol-prev | Jump to prev occurrence of symbol that around caret
  • C-. : hightlight-symbol-next | Jump to next occurrence of symbol that around caret

Just one space:

  • C-M-Space : Make just one space around caret by Ctrl-Cmd-Space.

Separate AceJump copy,cut,select command:

  • C-i C-c 't' 'm' : Copy jump area
    • | C-i C-c means type C-i then continue type C-c
  • C-i C-x 't' 'm' : Cut jump area
  • C-i C-i 't' 'm' : Select jump area
  • C-i C-f 't' 'm' : Basic Jump alias

Copy and Replace:

  • C-I C-R (w | s | l | q | a | A | e | E | p | g | u | d) 't' 'm' : copy current word/line/paragraph, jump, then replace target word/line/paragraph

idea-plugin.name: Notification Bridge
idea-plugin.description:
Push notifications, progress bars, and status bar widgets into your IntelliJ IDE from external tools via a local REST API and WebSocket server.

Features

  • Balloon Notifications — Post info, warning, and error notifications from scripts, CI, or AI agents
  • Action Buttons — Interactive notifications with clickable actions and WebSocket callbacks
  • Progress Bars — Create and update IDE progress indicators for long-running tasks
  • Status Bar Widgets — Persistent status indicators in the IDE footer
  • Notification Channels — Group and rate-limit notifications by source
  • WebSocket Events — Real-time stream of notification lifecycle events
  • Web Dashboard — Built-in notification center at localhost
  • Zero Config — Works immediately when your IDE opens

Use Cases

  • AI agent completion alerts — "Refactoring complete: 12 files modified"
  • CI/CD pipeline results with "View Logs" action buttons
  • Deployment progress bars showing stages
  • Monitoring alerts as status bar widgets
  • Code review reminders with "Open GitHub" actions

Runs entirely on localhost. No data leaves your machine.

API available at http://localhost:9878/api/
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.6

  • Removed the until-build compatibility cap entirely (previously re-capped each IDE release, e.g. 262.*) so the plugin no longer needs republishing every time a new IDE version ships.

1.5

  • Compatibility extended to IntelliJ 2026.2 (262.*) so the plugin continues to load in the new IDE release.

1.1

  • Notification channels with per-channel rate limiting
  • Status bar widget management (create, update, remove)
  • Progress bar tracking with indeterminate and fractional modes
  • WebSocket event stream for real-time notification lifecycle
  • Web dashboard with notification center at localhost:9878
  • Configurable settings (port, auto-start, CORS, rate limits)

1.0

  • Initial release — REST API for pushing notifications into IntelliJ
  • Balloon, sticky, and action notifications with clickable buttons
  • Notification history with dismissal tracking
  • Freemium licensing via JetBrains Marketplace

idea-plugin.name: DSM Language Support
idea-plugin.description:
Official IntelliJ IDEA extension for the Digital Substrate Model (DSM) language

The DSM extension provides comprehensive language support for .dsm files, including syntax highlighting, code formatting, intelligent code completion, advanced navigation, and validation via dsm_util.py.

Features

Syntax Highlighting

  • Keywords: namespace, concept, club, membership, enum, struct, attachment, function_pool, attachment_function_pool
  • Types: All primitive types (bool, int8-64, uint8-64, float, double, string, uuid, blob_id, commit_id)
  • Collections: vec, mat, tuple, optional, vector, set, map, xarray, variant, key
  • UUIDs: Automatic recognition and highlighting of UUID patterns
  • Comments: Line comments (//) and docstrings ("""...""")
  • Enumerations: Enum value syntax (.EnumValue)
  • Semantic Coloring: Concepts, structs, enums, and function pools each have distinct colors

Code Formatting

  • Automatic Formatting: Reformat code with Cmd+Alt+L (macOS) / Ctrl+Alt+L (Windows/Linux)
  • Smart Indentation: Proper indentation for struct and enum fields (4 spaces default)
  • Consistent Spacing: Automatic spacing around operators, commas, and type parameters
  • List Literals: Keeps list initializers on a single line (e.g., {0.0, 0.0, 0.0})
  • Configurable: Customize indent size, tab size, and spacing in Code Style settings

Brace Matching

  • Highlight Matching Braces: Automatically highlights corresponding { }, [ ], ( ), and < > pairs
  • Quick Navigation: Jump between matching braces with Cmd+Shift+M (macOS) / Ctrl+Shift+M (Windows/Linux)
  • Block Selection: Expand selection to enclosing blocks with Cmd+W / Ctrl+W

Smart Snippets

Type prefixes and press Tab to insert common DSM constructs:

Primitive Types:

  • bool, string, uuid, blob_id
  • int8, int16, int32, int64
  • uint8, uint16, uint32, uint64
  • float, double

Collections:

  • vec → vec<T, size> (numeric vectors)
  • mat → mat<T, cols, rows> (matrices)
  • optional → optional<T> (nullable values)
  • vector → vector<T> (dynamic arrays)
  • set → set<T> (unique collections)
  • map → map<K, V> (key-value pairs)
  • tuple → tuple<T0, T1> (fixed tuples)
  • variant → variant<T0, T1> (union types)
  • xarray → xarray<T> (multi-dimensional arrays)
  • key → key<T> (entity references)

Structures:

  • namespace → Full namespace template with UUID placeholder
  • concept → Concept declaration
  • club → Club declaration
  • membership → Membership declaration
  • enum → Enumeration template
  • struct → Structure template
  • attachment → Attachment declaration
  • function_pool → Function pool template with UUID
  • attachment_function_pool → Attachment function pool template
  • docstr → Documentation string ("""...""")

Advanced Patterns:

  • isa → Concept inheritance (concept Derived is a Base;)
  • struct-defaults → Structure with default field values
  • enum-field → Enum field with default value (.enumValue)
  • keyfield → Key field with naming convention (key<Concept> fieldKey;)
  • opt-key → Optional key field (optional<key<Concept>> fieldKey;)
  • mutable → Mutable function in attachment function pool (state-modifying)
  • query → Query function in attachment function pool (read-only)

Symbol Search

Quick navigation to DSM types by name with Alt+Cmd+O (macOS) / Ctrl+Alt+N (Windows/Linux)

  • Global Search: Find concepts, structs, enums, clubs, and function pools across all project files
  • Type-Specific Icons: Differentiated icons for each element type
  • Concepts: class icon (blue C)
  • Structs: static icon (orange S)
  • Enums: enum icon (purple E)
  • Clubs: interface icon
  • Function pools: function icon
  • File Location: Shows the containing file for each result
  • Direct Navigation: Jump to definition by selecting any search result

Documentation on Hover

View quick documentation for DSM elements with F1 (macOS) / Ctrl+Q (Windows/Linux)

  • Docstring Display: Shows triple-quoted documentation strings ("""...""") in formatted popup
  • Element Support: Concepts, structs, enums, clubs, attachments, function pools, fields, functions, enum values
  • Type Information: Displays type signatures and inheritance relationships
  • File Location: Shows containing file for each element
  • Rich Formatting: Definition headers, content sections, and metadata sections

Code Completion

  • Context-Aware for key<T>: Inside key<>, suggests only concepts and clubs (not primitives or structs)
  • Context-Aware for attachment<T, D>: First parameter suggests concepts/clubs, second parameter accepts any type
  • Keywords: is a, true, false
  • Primitive Types: bool, int8-64, uint8-64, float, double, string, uuid, blob_id, commit_id
  • Special Types: any, any_concept

Navigation & Structure

  • Find usages and references
  • Structure view for namespaces, concepts, structs, enums
  • Go to definition for user-defined types

DSM Validation

Manual validation with dsm_util.py triggered via Ctrl+Alt+V keyboard shortcut.

  • Dedicated DSM Validation tool window with sortable error table
  • Red wavy underlines on errors in editor with hover tooltips
  • Double-click errors to jump to location
  • Toolbar with "Validate", "Previous Error" (Alt+Shift+F2), and "Next Error" (Alt+F2) buttons
  • Error navigation cycles through all errors across all files
  • Configurable timeout for validation execution

Key DSM Concepts

Concepts: Hierarchical types with single inheritance using is a keyword

Attachments: Associate data structures with concepts for domain modeling

Attachment Function Pools: Define mutable operations for collaborative editing with undo/redo support
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.2.3

  • Context-Aware Code Completion: Smart completion for type parameters - inside key<T> suggests only concepts and clubs; inside attachment<T, D> first parameter suggests concepts/clubs
  • Documentation Provider: Refactored to use PSI-based extraction following IntelliJ Platform best practices
  • File Template: Create new DSM files via New → DSM File with auto-generated namespace and UUID

1.2.2

  • Added Symbol Search (Alt+Cmd+O / Ctrl+Alt+N) for quick navigation to DSM types
  • Added Documentation on Hover (F1 / Ctrl+Q) for docstrings
  • Added Live Templates for rapid DSM development
  • Added Rename Refactoring with cross-file support

1.2.0

  • Code Formatting with smart indentation (Cmd+Alt+L / Ctrl+Alt+L)
  • Brace Matching for all delimiter types
  • Code Folding for namespaces, structs, enums, function pools

1.0.0

  • Initial release with full DSM language support
  • Syntax and semantic highlighting
  • Code completion, navigation, and structure view
  • DSM validation via dsm_util.py integration

idea-plugin.name: Lisette

idea-plugin.name: Viritin Color
idea-plugin.description:
Color swatches and a color picker for the Viritin Color Java library (in.virit:color).
  • Shows a color swatch in the editor gutter next to RgbColor, HexColor, HslColor and NamedColor expressions.
  • Click the swatch to open the standard IDE color picker and rewrite the source to the chosen color.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Gutter swatches and color picker support for the CSS Color 4 types: HwbColor, LabColor, LchColor, OklabColor, OklchColor and ColorFunction (with ColorSpace.SRGB / DISPLAY_P3 / REC2020 / PROPHOTO_RGB / A98_RGB / XYZ / XYZ_D50 / XYZ_D65), plus their .of("...") factories and matching Color.parseCssColor("hwb(...)" / "oklch(...)" / "color(display-p3 ...)" / ...) strings.
  • The plugin now bundles the Viritin Color library and renders swatches via its own math, so plugin and library stay in sync without re-implementing CSS Color 4 conversions inside the plugin.

Changed

  • Bumped the bundled in.virit:color from 0.0.4 to 0.0.5 (adds CSS Color 4 types, normalised HSL hue parsing with turn/fractional angles, and IllegalArgumentException for malformed rgb() / hsl()).
  • Picking a new color on a CSS Color 4 expression (e.g. new OklchColor(...), HwbColor.of("...")) rewrites the whole expression as new RgbColor(r, g, b[, a]) because the IDE picker yields sRGB and round-tripping into Lab/OkLCh/HWB needs gamut mapping the user rarely expects in this flow.

Fixed

  • LineMarker is supposed to be registered for leaf elements only performance warnings from c.i.c.d.LineMarkerInfo — color recognition now anchors on the new keyword leaf, the method-name identifier (of / parseCssColor), or the constant-name identifier (RED in NamedColor.RED) instead of the surrounding composite expression.

idea-plugin.name: OXP - Open Extension Protocol
idea-plugin.description:
Run universal OXP extensions (.oxp bundles) inside any JetBrains IDE. One extension binary, every editor — write it once, ship it to IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, Rider, RustRover, CLion, DataGrip, and VS Code and Neovim simultaneously.

What is OXP?

OXP (Open Extension Protocol) is an open spec for editor extensions distributed as sandboxed WebAssembly components (WASI Preview 2). The same .oxp bundle runs unchanged in every OXP-compatible host — no recompilation, no platform-specific code.

HostStatusWhere
JetBrains (all IDEs)✅ StableThis plugin
VS Code & forks✅ Stableoxprotocol.oxp-vscode
Neovim🔵 Betagithub.com/oxprotocol/oxp

Features

  • OXP Lens — Switchboard
    A management panel listing all installed extensions with toggle switches. Toggle ON → the extension gets its own native JetBrains tool window in the sidebar. Toggle OFF → it disappears instantly. Pin what you need, hide what you don't.
  • Native tool windows per extension
    Each enabled extension registers as an independent LEFT-anchor tool window — same level as Project, Structure, and Git views. Pop it out as a floating window with the ↗ button for full-screen use.
  • JCEF-powered rendering with OXP bridge
    Extensions render their HTML + React UIs in embedded Chromium (JCEF). The full OXP bridge is injected automatically: oxp.fs, oxp.shell, oxp.net, oxp.secrets — all sandboxed behind capability-based permission checks.
  • Automatic theme bridge
    IntelliJ's active color scheme is mapped to ~150 VS Code CSS custom properties on every page load. Extensions look native in any IDE theme, light or dark, without any extra configuration.
  • Shared install store
    Extensions live in ~/.oxp/host-store/extensions/. Run oxp install @publisher/slug once and the extension immediately appears in every open IDE — JetBrains, VS Code, and Neovim — without a reload.
  • OXP Dev — live reload panel
    Run oxp dev in your terminal and see extension changes reflected in the IDE in real time. Full Chromium DevTools available for debugging.
  • Capability-based permissions
    Every extension declares the capabilities it needs before activation. You review and approve them. Cancel = no install, zero ambient access.

Quick start

  1. Install the OXP CLI: npm i -g @oxprotocol/cli
  2. Install an extension: oxp install @publisher/slug
  3. Open OXP Lens in the right sidebar and toggle the extension ON.

Building your own extension

oxp create my-ext    # scaffold (templates: html, react, rust, tree)
cd my-ext
oxp dev              # live reload in your running IDE
oxp pack             # build a reproducible signed .oxp bundle
oxp publish          # ship to https://oxp.sh

Security model

  • Sandboxed — no ambient FS, network, or process access.
  • Verified — sha256 + Ed25519 signature checked on every install.
  • Allowlisted — net.fetch scopable to specific hosts; fs.read to paths.
  • No native code — every extension is a pure .wasm component.

Links

  • Website — oxp.sh
  • Specification — oxp.sh/spec
  • CLI & SDK — npmjs.com/@oxprotocol/cli
  • Source — github.com/oxprotocol/oxp
  • Issues — github.com/oxprotocol/oxp/issues

Apache-2.0 licensed.
