idea-plugin.name: Ansible Pro
idea-plugin.description:
Move from Ansible YAML to a controlled automation workflow without leaving your JetBrains IDE.

Ansible Pro connects project-aware editing, inventory navigation, Vault, validation, playbook runs, and AAP/AWX. It activates only in Ansible-shaped projects and stays out of Kubernetes, Helm, GitHub Actions, Docker Compose, and generic YAML.

Start free

  • Scope-safe Ansible editing. Completion, hover documentation, navigation, and diagnostics use the official Ansible language server only where the project structure identifies Ansible.
  • Local collection intelligence. Module FQCNs and descriptions come from the project's configured ansible-doc environment, so completion and Ctrl+Q documentation reflect the collections installed for that project.
  • Inventory and variable navigation. Jump between playbook usages, inventory declarations, group_vars, and host_vars; complete known groups and hosts; inspect variable precedence without grepping the repository.
  • Role and project support. Navigate roles across monorepos, edit ansible.cfg with highlighting and completion, and configure external Ansible tools from Settings.
  • Repair missing local targets. Create an unresolved local role, add a missing group_vars file, or create a missing literal file referenced by vars_files, include_vars, task includes, or import_playbook. Every workflow uses normal IDE Undo and stays hidden when the destination is dynamic, external, or ambiguous.

Professional workflows

Try every Professional workflow with the 14-day full-feature trial.

  • Route Vault access instead of repeatedly entering secrets. View, encrypt, decrypt, and transparently edit Vault files and inline values. Map project vault-id values such as prod, staging, and dev to 1Password CLI, macOS Keychain, or pass.
  • Validate and run with IDE-native feedback. Use dedicated playbook, ansible-lint, and syntax-check run configurations, controlled presets, and clickable console locations that open the failing task.
  • Operate AAP/AWX from the IDE. Test the connection, list job templates, launch a template with remembered extra-vars, follow job output while it runs, and repeat the previous launch from the Tools menu.
  • Trace variables across the project. Extend variable provenance into inventory-embedded vars, static vars_files, and static include_vars; use the editor gutter to open every known declaration.
  • Work across the project. Open the inventory graph, propagate variable renames across inventory and vars files, and run Molecule tests from the IDE.

Requirements and limitations

The plugin uses your installed ansible-language-server, ansible-doc, ansible-playbook, ansible-lint, ansible-vault, and ansible-galaxy tools. Settings → Tools → Ansible shows their status, installation guidance, and per-tool override paths. Missing tools fail non-fatally with actionable feedback.

Targets unified IntelliJ IDEA 2025.2+ and compatible paid JetBrains IDEs. Legacy Community editions are out of scope. Galaxy reads are local; network access occurs only after an explicit Install or Update action.

See the Ansible Pro workflow and documentation.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
7.0.0

  • Create a missing local role where it is referenced (Free). An editor inspection reports an unresolved exact local role when the project has one deterministic role root; its quick fix creates roles/<role>/tasks/main.yml and opens the file.
  • Add group variables without leaving inventory YAML (Free). An intention on a known inventory group creates its exact group_vars/<group>.yml file when the inventory context is unambiguous.
  • Keep project edits predictable. Creation never overwrites an existing file, stays silent for dynamic, external, collection, ambiguous, and non-Ansible targets, and can be reverted with ordinary IDE Undo.
  • Repair broken static playbook links (Free). Missing literal files referenced by vars_files, include_vars, import_tasks, include_tasks, and import_playbook have deterministic create-file quick fixes with valid minimal YAML.
  • See Galaxy drift before it breaks a playbook (Free). A dedicated Galaxy Dependencies tool window compares locally installed roles and collections with root, role, and collection requirements files and marks missing, mismatched, and unpinned entries.
  • Act from the same panel (Professional). Explicit toolbar actions install missing dependencies or update requirements through the configured ansible-galaxy executable, show the exact command and bounded output, and refresh the result after success.
  • Keep navigation and network behavior predictable. Requirements rows open their exact YAML declaration; refresh is read-only and installation never starts in the background.
  • Explore inventory structure without leaving the IDE (Professional). The inventory graph now lives in a persistent tool window with inline group and host filters and exact declaration navigation.
  • Export a presentation-ready graph (Professional). Distinct PNG and SVG toolbar actions save a styled node diagram with connectors anchored to card boundaries; PNG uses a high-density canvas so labels and connectors remain crisp.
  • Recognize each workspace action at a glance. Inventory Graph and AAP/AWX tool windows and their actions now use dedicated icons for their actual operation.
  • Repeat AAP/AWX launches with less setup (Professional). Each job template remembers its latest extra-vars, and Relaunch Last AAP/AWX Job repeats the exact previous template and variables.
  • Follow job output while it runs (Professional). A persistent tool window refreshes stdout, reports final status, and provides toolbar actions to cancel monitoring or relaunch the previous job.
  • Deeper variable provenance (Professional). Ctrl+Q and Ctrl+B now include variables embedded in inventory group and host declarations plus statically resolvable vars_files and include_vars files and directories. Results keep deterministic precedence and link to the exact declaration; dynamic Jinja paths remain intentionally unresolved.
  • All definitions from the editor gutter (Professional). A gutter action beside a Jinja variable use opens every known declaration. It is available with an active license or trial and stays absent from generic YAML.
  • The existing variable workflow remains Free. Ctrl+Q and Ctrl+B continue to cover role defaults and vars, group_vars, host_vars, play and task vars, set_fact, and register without a license.

6.0.0

  • Local collection intelligence (Free). The plugin indexes installed module FQCNs and descriptions from the configured ansible-doc, adds them to completion and Ctrl+Q documentation only in Ansible-scoped YAML, and keeps unknown modules on the existing LSP path. The project cache refreshes at Ansible project startup, after observed ansible_collections changes, after an ansible-doc override change, or manually from Tools → Ansible. Discovery runs off the EDT with cancellation and actionable non-fatal failures. Completion merges identical FQCNs from the LSP and the local index into one item.
  • AAP/AWX settings responsiveness. PasswordSafe token reads and writes now stay off the EDT, so opening or resetting the AAP/AWX Settings page does not report prohibited slow operations.

5.0.0

  • Syntax check run configuration. A first-class ansible-playbook --syntax-check run configuration — right-click any playbook or use the gutter icon on hosts: to spawn it. Supports the full playbook option set (inventory, extra-vars, --limit, --tags, --skip-tags, --vault-password-file, working directory) and turns quoted YAML error headers in the console output into hyperlinks that jump straight to the failing task. Zero-config: reuses the existing ansible-playbook resolution chain (Tools → Ansible override / ANSIBLE_PLAYBOOK_PATH / PATH). Paid tier; free tier sees a paywall notification with a link to Settings.
  • Multi vault-id orchestration. Settings → Tools → Ansible → Vault password providers now hosts a per-project table that maps each vault-id to a specific password provider — ideal for multi-environment setups (prod, staging, dev) where every vault has a different owner and a different secret store. A fallback row handles vault-ids that are not in the table; an empty table keeps the zero-config behaviour (application-level default provider). Encrypt and decrypt flows consult the mapping automatically — the user is never asked to pick a provider by hand, and unknown / unavailable providers fall back to the interactive prompt. All Vault operations require an active plugin license or trial.
  • Vault password providers. A new pluggable password source replaces the hard-wired modal prompt. Licensed users can keep the interactive dialog as the default or pick the macOS Keychain provider (Settings → Tools → Ansible → Vault password providers) — it stores each vault-id under a namespaced service (dev.meanmail.ansible.vault) via the built-in security CLI, so passwords no longer live in plaintext temp files on the plugin side. Non-macOS platforms transparently fall back to the modal prompt.
  • pass (passwordstore.org) vault password provider. The de-facto password manager for Ansible operators on Linux is first-class — the plugin shells out to pass show <entry> non-interactively and reads the first stdout line as the vault password. The entry path is derived from a configurable template (Settings → Tools → Ansible → Vault password providers), defaulting to ansible-vault/<vault-id>, so multi-vault-id setups fan out cleanly across the password store. The binary is discovered on PATH (or via the PASS_BIN environment variable) and cached for the process; missing binary / missing entry failures surface actionable errors instead of a generic stack trace. All Vault operations require an active plugin license or trial.
  • 1Password (op) vault password provider. Rounds out the provider chain for teams that already standardise on 1Password — the plugin shells out to op read <secret-reference> non-interactively and uses the CLI's output as the vault password. Sessions are inherited from the environment (op signin, or OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN for headless use); the plugin never prompts for the 1Password master password itself. The secret reference is derived from a configurable template (Settings → Tools → Ansible → Vault password providers), defaulting to op://Private/ansible-vault/<vault-id>/password. The op binary is discovered on PATH (or via OP_BIN) and cached for the process; missing binary, not-signed-in, and missing-item failures surface actionable errors instead of a generic stack trace. All Vault operations require an active plugin license or trial.
  • Every vault flow — whole-file view / decrypt / encrypt, transparent editing, inline !vault value decrypt, and inline encrypt from the editor popup — now routes through the provider chain, so a single Keychain, pass or 1Password entry is enough for the whole IDE session.

4.0.0

  • Variable provenance — “where does this variable come from?” Press Ctrl+Q on a variable inside a {{ }} expression and the plugin lists every place the project defines it — role defaults / vars, group_vars / host_vars, play and task vars, set_fact and register — ranked by Ansible’s real variable precedence, with the effective (winning) source called out and a clickable link to each declaration. No more grepping across a large infrastructure repo to find which file actually sets a value.
  • Jump to a variable’s definition. Ctrl+B / Ctrl+Click on a variable inside {{ }} navigates straight to where it is defined, offering every source in precedence order when more than one declares it. Unknown names (facts, loop vars, --extra-vars) are never flagged as errors.
  • Variables stand out. Ansible variable references inside Jinja expressions are now syntax-highlighted, so they no longer blend into the surrounding YAML string.
  • Like every editor feature, it stays completely silent outside Ansible scope — plain Kubernetes / Helm / GitHub Actions YAML is untouched.

3.0.0

  • Run ansible-lint from the IDE. A dedicated run configuration lints your playbooks and roles with clickable output — every reported rule jumps straight to the offending task in the editor. Right-click any Ansible YAML to lint just that file, or run the linter across the whole project.
  • A settings page for every tool. Settings → Tools → Ansible now has a dedicated page per tool (ansible-language-server, ansible-lint, ansible-playbook, molecule, ansible-vault), each showing whether the tool is installed, a one-click in-IDE installer (npm / pnpm / yarn / bun for the language server; pip / pipx / brew for Ansible), and an override path when you keep a tool in a virtualenv or a non-standard location.
  • On-the-fly linting respects your setup. The background ansible-lint diagnostics shown as you type now use the exact ansible-lint you configured above — the same one the run configuration uses — instead of whatever happened to be on the language server's PATH, so a custom or virtualenv install is finally picked up.
  • Changing the ansible-lint or ansible-language-server path in Settings now takes effect immediately, with no need to reopen the project.

2.0.0

  • Major update focused on execution and automation workflows in the IDE.
  • Vault flow hardening: transparent decrypted editing in memory with reliable re-encrypt on save/close, optional vault-id support, and safer background processing outside EDT.
  • Playbook execution overhaul: run line marker on playbooks, selectable run presets (dry-run, syntax check, tags, start-at-task, inventory), and a dedicated ansible-playbook run configuration.
  • AAP/AWX integration: connection settings and test, job template listing, launch from IDE, and stdout retrieval after completion.
  • Inventory and refactoring upgrades: inventory graph action, role-aware tag/task pickers, project-relative inventory labels, and vars rename propagation across shared vars/inventory usage.
  • Tooling and UX updates: Molecule test action, improved action grouping, and chooser migration from deprecated APIs.

1.0.0

  • First public release after an extended internal hardening cycle.
  • Scope-aware activation (only inside Ansible projects, never in Helm / Kubernetes / GitHub Actions / Docker Compose).
  • Native LSP integration via Red Hat's @ansible/ansible-language-server.
  • Inventory layer: navigation between inventory keys and group_vars / host_vars, back-navigation banner, completion of group and host names in playbook hosts:.
  • Ansible Vault operations available in the paid tier.
  • Settings page with dependency status, in-IDE installer and auto-start of the LSP once the binary appears on PATH.

idea-plugin.name: AutoTyper - Live Coding Simulator
idea-plugin.description:
AutoTyper - Live Coding Simulator

Simulate realistic, structured typing of Java classes in the editor.

Perfect for live coding demonstrations in lectures and presentations. Instead of typing code line-by-line from top to bottom, AutoTyper types code in the natural development order — just like a real developer would write it.

✨ Key Features

  • Structured Typing with Step Markers — Define the typing order using simple // @step N comments in your Java files
  • Automatic File Creation — The plugin automatically creates the Java file in the correct package directory and opens it in the editor
  • Package-Aware — Detects package declarations and creates the proper directory structure
  • Keyboard Shortcut: Alt+N — Press Alt+N anywhere in IntelliJ to advance to the next step. Works even when the editor has focus!
  • Natural Development Flow — First the empty class, then fields, then constructor, then methods
  • Adjustable Speed — From slow (30 WPM) to turbo (600 WPM)
  • Auto-Pause Between Steps — Pauses after each step for explanations
  • Pause/Resume/Stop Controls — Full control during typing
  • Progress Indicator — Shows current step and overall progress

⌨️ Keyboard Shortcuts

Alt+NNext Step (works globally, even when editor has focus)

Customizable via Settings → Keymap → search "AutoTyper"

📝 How Step Markers Work

Add // @step N comments to your Java files:

// @step 1
package ch.demo;

// @step 1
public class Calculator {

// @step 2
    private double result;

// @step 3
    public Calculator() {
        this.result = 0;
    }

// @step 4
    public double add(double a, double b) {
        result = a + b;
        return result;
    }

// @step 1
}

🚀 Quick Start

  1. Place annotated .java files in ~/autotyper-snippets/
  2. Open the AutoTyper tool window (right sidebar)
  3. Select a file, adjust speed, click Start
  4. The file is auto-created and opened in the editor
  5. After each step: press Alt+N or click Next Step

💡 Tips for Lecturers

  • Use 100-150 WPM for a natural look
  • Enable auto-pause to explain each step
  • Press Alt+N to advance — works without switching focus!
  • Organize snippets in folders per lecture topic


Created by Rolf — info@rolfsblog.ch

idea-plugin.name: AppleScript Toolkit
idea-plugin.description:
AppleScript support for modern JetBrains IDEs.

A maintained Kotlin rewrite and revival of the original Apache-2.0 AppleScript plugin, updated for current IntelliJ Platform releases.

  • Syntax highlighting, parsing, structure view, and code completion for AppleScript files.
  • Application dictionary support for scriptable applications and SDEF/XML dictionary files.
  • Run configurations, live templates, navigation, find usages, documentation, and rename support where available.

AppleScript execution and automatic application dictionary discovery require macOS. This plugin is not affiliated with Apple, JetBrains, or the original maintainer.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2.0.13

  • [Fix] Imported application properties now remain available in completion when Cocoa terminology contains a command with the same name; only matching properties are filtered out.
  • [Fix] Manually loading application dictionaries no longer freezes the IDE while generation and parsing run, and failures now identify the exact application and source file.
  • [Fix] Timed-out or interrupted dictionary generation now terminates the complete process tree, preventing orphaned subprocesses while preserving the original load failure.

2.0.12

  • [Fix] Handlers whose names start with with (for example on with_options()) no longer break parsing at their closing end with_... line — the end with comparison-operator spelling no longer swallows the start of the handler name.
  • [Fix] Rename refactoring now accepts index as the new variable name, matching the parser-level support for index as an identifier.
  • [Fix] Using index as a variable name (for example repeat with index from 1 to n, handler parameters, or item index of myList) no longer produces cascading false parse errors — the parser now accepts the word wherever AppleScript itself allows it as an identifier, while item index 1-style reference forms keep working.

2.0.11

  • [Fix] Application-specific dictionary terms (commands, classes, properties, and constants) are no longer briefly flagged as unknown during IDE startup while their application dictionaries are still loading — the editor now waits for application-dictionary indexing to finish before treating such a term as unresolved.
  • [Fix] The AppleScript code style page under Settings | Editor | Code Style is now bound to the AppleScript language, so its options apply to AppleScript reformatting.
  • [Fix] When a cached application dictionary fails to load, the plugin now records the specific cause and file in the IDE log instead of a generic message, so missing application completions are easier to diagnose.

2.0.10

  • [Change] The plugin now stays available on current and future JetBrains IDEs, including the upcoming 2026.2 — the fixed upper IDE-version limit was removed.

2.0.9

  • [Fix] Dynamic tell application blocks now parse correctly when the target application name comes from a variable or expression instead of a string literal.
  • [Fix] Real-world Standard Additions commands such as choose file ... of type, choose from list, open for access, write ... starting at, and close access no longer produce false parser errors.
  • [Fix] UI-scripting object references such as tab group, process, window, group, and slider keep parsing cleanly inside System Events automation scripts.
  • [Fix] Dictionary-backed command parameters now preserve selector and class highlighting while accepting valid AppleScript command tails.
  • [Fix] Valid object-reference command arguments such as close every window and anchored property phrases such as require password to wake of security preferences no longer show false parser errors.
  • [Fix] Launcher-style scripts with a final top-level end after conditional branches now parse without a spurious error on the last line.
  • [Fix] Semantic highlighting now better matches Script Editor-style AppleScript coloring for variables, dictionary terms, application references, handler calls, constants, and System Events process references.
  • [Fix] Literal System Events process names that are not known local applications now get a weak warning instead of being confused with parser errors.
  • [Fix] Application gutter markers now resolve real macOS app icons more reliably, including cached dictionaries and app bundles with icons stored in nested resources or extensions.
  • [Fix] Malformed generated dictionary cache files no longer evict persisted dictionary information during gutter icon refresh.

2.0.8

  • [Fix] Valid AppleScript property-update statements no longer show false parser errors when assigning values to application object properties.
  • [Fix] Dictionary commands with bracketed argument values now keep parsing following selector parameters instead of marking correct command calls as incomplete.
  • [Fix] Command handlers inside using terms from application blocks now parse cleanly, preserving navigation and Find Usages behavior for handler names.

2.0.7

  • Fixed Structure View to show AppleScript handlers, properties, and script objects at the root level instead of showing an empty tree.
  • Restored dictionary quick documentation when hovering over dictionary terms such as track inside tell application "Music".
  • Local variable references inside tell…whose filters now resolve for Find Usages and quick documentation.
  • Added regression coverage for documentation, Find Usages, and Structure View.

2.0.6

  • Replaced deprecated IntelliJ Platform APIs so AppleScript Toolkit verifies cleanly on the supported IDE versions.
  • Improved Find Usages accuracy for AppleScript handler calls and dictionary commands.
  • Verified against IntelliJ IDEA 2025.1, 2025.2, and 2026.1 without deprecated, internal, or experimental API warnings.

2.0.5

  • Fixed parser freezes and blocking dictionary lookups when AppleScript dictionaries are still loading.
  • Improved parsing for Standard Additions command parameters such as display notification, write ... starting at eof, and choose from list.
  • Fixed Typinator-style dictionary class references such as rule set and containing set.
  • Added regression coverage for real-world AppleScript parser edge cases.

2.0.3

  • Improved parsing for real-world AppleScript command phrases that use dictionary-style labeled arguments.
  • Accepted additional folder-action and system handler signatures without surfacing spurious parse errors.
  • Preserved parser diagnostics for malformed bracketed command arguments instead of swallowing following statements.

2.0.2

  • Fixed Marketplace release notes so the listing shows only the current release's What's New content.

2.0.1

  • Capped published Marketplace compatibility to IntelliJ Platform 2025.1 and 2025.2 while newer IDE lines are verified separately.

2.0.0

  • AppleScript Toolkit is now prepared as a separate paid Marketplace listing under a vendor-owned plugin id.
  • Standard Additions object tokens, application-specific object references, and non-ASCII operators are parsed more accurately.
  • Improved parsing for whose clauses, nested tell blocks, and on-error handlers.

ESPHome support for JetBrains IDEs: context-aware completion, hover documentation, live validation, and navigation for ESPHome YAML device configurations — driven by the ESPHome component catalog.

idea-plugin.name: TabMaster
idea-plugin.description:
TabMaster adds smarter bulk close actions to the editor tab context menu. Right-click any open file's tab and you'll find them in the usual close block, right next to Close, Close Others and Close All to the Left/Right.

When you have dozens of tabs open, closing them one by one — or nuking them all and reopening what you needed — is tedious. TabMaster lets you close exactly the group you mean in a single click.

Close All <Type>

Closes every open file of the same type as the tab you clicked. The label tells you precisely what it will close.

  • Right-click a .java tab → Close All JAVA closes every open Java file and leaves everything else untouched.
  • Right-click a .json tab → Close All JSON. Done reviewing config files? Clear them in one go.

Matching is by file extension (case-insensitive); files without an extension fall back to the IDE's detected file type.

Close Files in Directory

A submenu listing every directory from the file's own folder up to the project root. Pick one to close all open files in or below it.

Example — the tab is src/main/java/com/acme/web/UserController.java. The submenu offers com/acme/web, com/acme, src/main/java, … up to my-project (project root). Choosing com/acme/web closes every open file under the web package and keeps the rest.

Close Files Not in Directory

The same directory list, but inverted: keep only the files in or below the directory you pick and close everything else.

Example — you're about to focus on the web package. Choose com/acme/web here and every tab outside it is closed, leaving you with just the files you're working on.

idea-plugin.name: KTE
idea-plugin.description:
Support for Kotlin jte templates (.kte) in IntelliJ IDEA.

Features

  • .kte file type support.
  • Kotlin K2 completion, resolve, references, documentation, and injected-fragment diagnostics.
  • Template navigation, parameter checks, formatting, folding, brace matching, and live templates.

Requires IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1 or newer. Kotlin semantics are backed by scoped injected fragments.

  • Replaces the synthetic Kotlin model with scoped injected Kotlin fragments.
  • Adds new KTE branding and a dedicated .kte file icon.
  • Updates compatibility with IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1 APIs.

0.1.0

  • First standalone KTE plugin release.
  • Supports Kotlin K2 semantics for .kte templates.
  • Routes completion through scoped injected Kotlin fragments.
  • Registers only KTE file types and actions.

idea-plugin.name: Yii2Helper
idea-plugin.description:
Navigation and tooling for the Yii2 PHP framework.
  • Ctrl/Cmd+Click a view name in render(), renderPartial(), renderAjax(), renderFile() or the mailer compose() to jump to the view file.
  • Warns when a referenced view file is missing and offers a quick fix to create it.
  • Ctrl/Cmd+Click an action name in a route (redirect(), Url::to(), Url::toRoute(), Url::remember(), Html::a(), Html::beginForm(), UrlManager::createUrl() / createAbsoluteUrl(), and the action option of ActiveForm::begin()) to jump to the controller action — from controllers and view files alike.
  • Warns when a route's action method is missing and offers a quick fix to create it.

Changed

Converts a TYPO3 Fluid ViewHelper / component tag into its inline notation via the editor right-click menu or the Alt+Enter (⌥⏎) intention popup.

idea-plugin.name: Bril
idea-plugin.description:
Editor support for Bril, the Big Red Intermediate Language — a small instruction-representation language built for compilers education. The plugin understands Bril's human-readable text format (the one produced by bril2txt).

Features

  • File type — recognizes .bril files.
  • Lexing & parsing — a full lexer and parser for the Bril text format (functions, typed arguments and return types, const/value/effect operations, labels, and parameterized types such as ptr<int>), with error highlighting.
  • Syntax highlighting — comments, literals, @function and .label identifiers, primitive types (int, bool, float, char, ptr), and core/extension opcodes (add, br, call, print, alloc, phi, …). Colors are configurable under Settings | Editor | Color Scheme | Bril.
  • Editing aids — # line-comment toggling and brace matching for {}, (), and <>.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Go to Declaration — operands now resolve to their definitions: variables to their arg/const/value destinations, @-operands to functions, and .-operands to labels.
  • Find Usages — support for finding usages of Bril definitions.

idea-plugin.name: Spring Bean Injector
idea-plugin.description:
Spring Bean Injector is an IntelliJ IDEA plugin that helps you inject Spring Beans into Java classes instantly — via right-click dialog or inline code completion.

Spring Bean Injector

Right-click or type a bean class name + "." to inject Spring Beans instantly. Field Injection, Constructor Injection, code completion injection, smart scanning, @Qualifier auto-detection, categorized UI, i18n, and customizable settings.

Features

  • Two Injection Modes — Dialog (Alt+A / right-click) or inline Code Completion (type class name + ".")
  • Bean Scanning — @Component, @Service, @Controller, @RestController, @Repository, @Configuration, @Bean methods (Configuration + lite mode), MyBatis @Mapper, custom annotation registration
  • Field Injection — @Autowired or @Resource (auto-detects javax vs jakarta)
  • Constructor Injection — Lombok @RequiredArgsConstructor or explicit constructor (auto-merge into existing constructors)
  • @Qualifier Support — auto-detected when multiple beans share the same injection type; in code completion, all conflicting beans are listed with qualifier names for precise selection; always placed on constructor parameters (not fields) for explicit constructor injection
  • Interface-aware Injection — injects by interface type when a class implements exactly one business interface; framework interfaces (Spring, Jakarta, etc.) are automatically filtered out
  • Smart Naming — I-prefix stripping, JavaBeans decapitalize, @Bean/@Service custom name support, duplicate prevention
  • Batch Injection — select multiple beans at once, all injected in a single undoable operation
  • Settings — Tools → Spring Bean Injector: Language (English/Chinese), Bean Type Filter, Injection Method Filter, Autocomplete Prompt Filter (independent control over completion vs popup menu)

Usage

  1. Dialog mode: Right-click in a Java class or press Alt+A, select injection type, search and pick bean(s)
  2. Completion mode: Type a bean class name followed by "." (e.g. DishService.), select injection method from completion list
  3. Annotations, imports and fields are generated automatically

Spring Bean 注入器

右键菜单或输入类名 + "." 即可快速注入 Spring Bean。支持字段注入、构造器注入、代码补全注入、智能扫描、@Qualifier 自动标记、分类 UI、国际化、自定义设置。

功能

  • 两种注入方式 — 对话框模式（Alt+A / 右键菜单）或内联代码补全模式（输入类名 + "."）
  • Bean 扫描 — @Component, @Service, @Controller, @RestController, @Repository, @Configuration, @Bean（含 lite mode）, MyBatis @Mapper, 自定义注解
  • 字段注入 — @Autowired 或 @Resource（自动识别 javax/jakarta）
  • 构造器注入 — Lombok @RequiredArgsConstructor 或显式构造函数（自动合并已有构造器）
  • @Qualifier — 同注入类型多实现时自动添加；代码补全时列出所有冲突 Bean 及其限定名供精确选择；显式构造函数模式下仅在参数上添加
  • 接口感知注入 — 实现类仅有一个业务接口时以接口类型注入；自动过滤框架接口（Spring、Jakarta 等）
  • 智能命名 — I 前缀剥离、标准 JavaBeans 命名、@Bean/@Service 自定义名、重复检测
  • 批量注入 — 一次选择多个 Bean，在单个可撤销操作中完成注入
  • 设置 — Tools → Spring Bean Injector：语言、Bean 类型过滤、注入方式过滤、补全提示过滤（独立控制补全与弹窗菜单）

使用

  1. 对话框模式：右键 Java 类 或 按 Alt+A，选择注入方式，搜索并选择目标 Bean（可多选）
  2. 补全模式：输入 Bean 类名后加 "."（如 DishService.），在补全列表中选择注入方式
  3. 注解、导入和字段自动生成
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.1

  • Code completion injection: type a bean class name + "." (e.g. DishService.) and select injection method inline
  • @Qualifier multi-bean selection: when multiple beans share the same injection type, all are listed in completion with qualifier names for precise selection
  • Autocomplete prompt filter: separate settings section to independently control which injection methods appear in code completion vs popup menu
  • Unified injection position: all injection methods now insert fields after the last bean field
  • Performance: HashMap O(1) bean lookup, completion pre-filter, VFS debounce, import caching
  • Batch injection: all selected beans injected in a single undoable WriteCommandAction
  • Code quality: eliminated field creation duplication via shared FieldFactory, thread safety fixes, dead code removal
  • Fixed: Controller classes no longer misidentified when implementing framework interfaces
  • Fixed: code completion injection now resolves class by qualified name, fixing incorrect fully-qualified type names
  • Fixed: cross-package same-name beans no longer false-positive on duplicate detection
  • Fixed: primitive/String constants no longer misidentified as bean fields for insertion anchoring

1.0.0 — Initial Release

  • Spring stereotype + @Bean method + MyBatis @Mapper scanning, custom annotation support
  • Field Injection (@Autowired / @Resource, javax/jakarta auto-detect)
  • Constructor Injection (Lombok @RequiredArgsConstructor / explicit constructor with auto-merge)
  • @Qualifier auto-detection, interface-aware injection, duplicate prevention
  • Settings UI — language (EN/ZH), bean type filter, injection method filter

idea-plugin.name: ZenMark Editor
idea-plugin.description:
ZenMark: The Ultimate WYSIWYG Markdown Experience

ZenMark transforms your IntelliJ IDEA into a modern, distraction-free Markdown editor. It completely hides the raw Markdown syntax and provides a true "What You See Is What You Get" editing experience.


Core Features:
  • Seamless Theme Sync: Automatically adapts to your IDE's dark/light themes with zero delay. Supports manual override via IDE Settings.
  • Smart Context Menu: Right-click anywhere to quickly insert tables, images, or code blocks. Right-click inside a table for advanced cell/row/column manipulations.
  • Aesthetic Color Palette: Curated, design-grade text colors and highlighters accessible via an intuitive floating bubble menu.
  • Interactive Code Blocks: Built-in syntax highlighting (GitHub Dark style) with a smart corner dropdown to switch languages instantly.
  • Pure Focus: An ultra-clean, minimalistic interface that lets you focus purely on writing and creation.

idea-plugin.name: Markdown Theme Pack
idea-plugin.description: Beautiful Markdown preview themes for JetBrains IDEs. 12 built-in themes (GitHub, Typora, Notion, Solarized, One Dark, Bear and more). Auto-applies to every project — no per-project setup needed. Save and reuse your own custom CSS themes.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Fix: apply theme on first .md file open via FileEditorManagerListener. Remove usage of internal MarkdownSettingsState API.

idea-plugin.name: Faust Studio
idea-plugin.description:
Full IDE support for the Faust audio programming language, plus a real-time DSP visualization environment and an offline analysis bench embedded directly in your IDE.

Language Features

  • Syntax highlighting with semantic color groups (keywords, operators, built-ins, UI primitives)
  • Arity inlay hints — shows signal flow n→m next to every definition
  • Signature help — parameter names as you type a call, for user functions and, when a local Faust installation is detected, the standard library
  • Named-argument inlay hints — fi.lowpass(N: 3, fc: 1000) at call sites
  • Code completion — keywords, built-ins, standard library prefixes, and user-defined symbols
  • Go-to-definition (Ctrl+Click) and Find Usages (Alt+F7) across files
  • Rename refactoring (Shift+F6) across the project
  • Documentation on hover (Ctrl+Q) for built-ins and user-defined symbols
  • Structure view, brace matching, code folding, line and block commenting
  • Error and warning annotations: unresolved references, arity mismatches, unused parameters, unreachable code, missing process
  • Quick-fixes (Alt+Enter) — "Did you mean …?", add a missing process, add import("stdfaust.lib"), remove an unused parameter
  • Customizable color scheme under Settings > Editor > Color Scheme > Faust

Real-time Visualization

  • Compiles Faust DSP to WebAssembly in-browser — no local Faust installation required
  • Multi-channel oscilloscope and spectroscope / spectrogram updated at 60 fps
  • Interactive DSP parameter controls (sliders, buttons, checkboxes)
  • Virtual MIDI keyboard and hardware MIDI device support
  • Audio input sources: microphone, sine wave, white noise
  • File watcher: recompiles and updates the visualization on every save
  • Polyphonic synthesis via declare nvoices

Offline Analysis Bench

  • A dedicated tool window that renders a test signal through your DSP offline (no audio playback) to plot its frequency, impulse, step, THD, transfer, and spectrum responses
  • Trigger from a gutter icon on any definition or by selecting an expression; overlay runs to compare; export plots to PNG/CSV
  • Sessions autosave per project and can be saved / loaded

Works in all JetBrains IDEs — IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, CLion, Rider, GoLand, WebStorm, and more.

Privacy: the plugin runs entirely on your machine. The visualization and analysis views are served by a local HTTP server bound to localhost only; no code, telemetry, or usage data is ever sent off your machine.

Faust is developed by GRAME, Centre National de Création Musicale. Faust Studio is an independent, third-party plugin and is not affiliated with or endorsed by GRAME.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Large .dsp scripts no longer hang the compiler ("compiling" forever) in the installed plugin. libfaust's in-browser (WASM) compile overflows the JCEF worker's default V8 stack on big scripts; the required --stack-size flag was only applied in the development sandbox, never shipped. It is now shipped with the plugin so installed users get it too.
  • A DSP too heavy to run in real-time (e.g. a dense modal reverb) no longer silently produces no audio and then freezes the panel when audio is toggled. The plugin now detects the real-time overload, shows a clear warning, and stops the overloaded node so the UI stays responsive — recompile a lighter script (or use the offline Analysis Bench) for heavy DSPs. Audio toggle is also guarded so a stuck AudioContext can never hang the UI.

idea-plugin.name: TabBuilder
idea-plugin.description:
Enterprise Project Generator for JetBrains IDEs.
Generate production-ready projects using official CLIs and best practices — Spring Boot, FastAPI, Laravel, ASP.NET, Next.js and more.
Reutiliza el mismo motor probado de TabBuilder para VS Code.

idea-plugin.name: Codebase Notes
idea-plugin.description:
Shared, Git-versioned notes for your codebase structure — across JetBrains IDEs, VS Code, and TRAE.

Put explanations such as “why this directory exists”, “where the project core is”, and “where new features plug in” directly beside files and directories in the Project view — instead of losing them in chat history, personal notes, or outdated documentation.

Codebase Notes stores all notes in a repository-local .codebase-notes.json file. Commit it to Git so teammates and users of other supported editors can share the same context.

What it helps with

  • Onboarding: mark the core order flow or the main application entry.
  • Architecture: identify public API boundaries and important modules.
  • Maintenance: explain generated files and paths that should not be edited manually.
  • Navigation: mark stable sources of truth and extension points.

Core features

  • Edit, style, or remove notes from the Project view context menu.
  • Display short notes directly beside files and directories.
  • Use six semantic colors to turn the project tree into a code map.
  • Keep note paths in sync when files or directories are renamed or moved.
  • Share one open JSON format with VS Code and TRAE.
  • English and Simplified Chinese UI that follows the IDE language.
  • No account, cloud service, telemetry, or proprietary database.

Six code-map styles

  • Core (red): the project backbone — learn this first.
  • Focus (yellow): easy-to-miss relationships, constraints, or details.
  • Important (blue): important modules and engineering entry points.
  • Stable (green): trusted sources of truth and reliable baselines.
  • Extension (purple): places where new capabilities plug in.
  • Default (gray): ordinary responsibility descriptions.

Colors describe code structure rather than errors or runtime status: red for the backbone, yellow for details, blue for importance, green for trusted baselines, and purple for extension points.

Getting started

  1. Open a project in a supported JetBrains IDE.
  2. Right-click a file or directory in the Project view.
  3. Choose Codebase Notes → Edit Text Note.
  4. Commit .codebase-notes.json to Git if the note should be shared.

Default shortcuts: Option+R on macOS or Alt+R on Windows/Linux to edit text; Shift+Option+R or Shift+Alt+R to set a style.

Data and privacy

  • Notes stay inside the opened project.
  • Writes use locking, temporary files, and conflict detection to avoid silent overwrites.
  • The JSON format is validated by a shared schema and cross-language conformance tests.
  • The plugin does not collect or transmit project data.

idea-plugin.name: OptionalGetter for Lombok

idea-plugin.name: Lombok Builder Linker
idea-plugin.description:
Reconnect what Lombok @Builder disconnects.

A linker resolves the symbol references a compiler leaves dangling. This plugin does the same job inside the editor: it restores the references IntelliJ drops around @Builder, so navigation, Find Usages, and Rename start working where they silently did nothing before.

What breaks today. Every claim below was measured across all 21 documented ways to use @Builder — not inferred:

  • Name strings point nowhere. builderMethodName, buildMethodName, builderClassName, setterPrefix, @Builder.ObtainVia(method), @Builder.ObtainVia(field) and @Singular("item") carry no reference. Ctrl+Click reports "Cannot find declaration to go to".
  • Parameters do not reach their setters. A setter's origin is a field when @Builder sits on the class, but a parameter when it sits on a constructor or factory method. The Lombok plugin links fields only, so from a parameter Find Usages is empty and Rename leaves the call sites behind — and they still compile, because a setter with the new name is generated.
  • ObtainVia breaks code silently. It names a method you wrote by hand, so the IDE shows that method as unused: Rename leaves the string stale and Safe Delete removes it without warning. Nothing checks the shape of what it points at either — Lombok writes the call into the generated toBuilder(), so a missing member or a wrong signature breaks a file that has no source. Either way, nothing shows up until you build.
  • Usages of the annotated constructor or method come back empty. The only caller is the generated build(), which has no source, so Find Usages finds nothing and Code Vision shows "no usages" — even with call sites right there.
  • The declaration goes grey. A constructor or method carrying @Builder is reported as never used.

Placement decides everything. Put @Builder on a class and all of this works. Put it on a constructor — which the Lombok docs recommend once you have written a constructor yourself — or on a static or instance method, and every link above breaks. This plugin closes that gap without touching the class-level case, which already works.

Works in IntelliJ IDEA Community and Ultimate. It reads members the bundled Lombok support already generates and adds references to them, so there is no dependency on Lombok internals; with Lombok support disabled it quietly does nothing.

Source code and issue tracker on GitHub
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 1.1.0
    • @Singular("item") is linked like the other name strings, and renaming it keeps the setter prefix (withItem → withTask).
    • Find Usages and Rename on a parameter of a @Builder constructor or factory method now reach the generated setter's call sites. Fields are left to the Lombok plugin, which already handles them.
    • New inspection: @Builder.ObtainVia whose target is missing or has a signature Lombok cannot call. Lombok checks the annotation's syntax but never the signature, and the call it breaks lives in generated code — so until now this only showed up as a build error.
    • @SuperBuilder already worked, including across the inheritance chain; that is now documented and pinned by tests. No behaviour change.
  • 1.0.1 — Fixed: usages of a private constructor carrying @Builder were not found. Java narrows a private member's search scope to its own class body, while the real call sites reach it from other files through the generated entry method. Hiding the constructor so the builder is the only way to construct the object is a common idiom, so this affected many real-world classes.
  • 1.0.0 — First release.
    • All six @Builder name strings carry a reference — builderMethodName, buildMethodName, builderClassName, setterPrefix and both @Builder.ObtainVia forms. Safe Delete and Rename of a member named by ObtainVia now see the string instead of silently breaking it.
    • Ctrl+Click on a name string opens the IDE's own usages popup, listing the call sites of the member that string names.
    • Shift+F6 on a name string renames in place and updates every call site in one undoable step. Renaming setterPrefix rewrites each generated setter with its own name (withName → setName).
    • Usages of a constructor or method carrying @Builder now include the builder call sites, and such declarations are no longer reported as unused.

idea-plugin.name: Mermaid Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Syntax highlighting and real validation for .mmd/.mermaid diagram source files (flowchart, sequence, and class diagrams): a real paid competitor's reviewers reported it "shows false warnings for valid non-ASCII subgraph identifiers" and "false errors for valid node shapes where the node contains non-ASCII characters" -- this plugin's lexer is Unicode-aware throughout (no ASCII-only character-class check anywhere in the identifier/label path), so those exact false positives structurally cannot happen here.

Unterminated string literals, unmatched/mismatched node-shape brackets, and `subgraph` blocks missing their `end` are flagged as real errors -- exactly the "does it actually validate my syntax" gap the cited 1-star review described.

A "Preview" tab renders the diagram visually via the real mermaid.js (bundled), next to the text editor -- the direct fix for that same review ("It opens and shows me a bunch of icons on page. That's it. No other functionality at all."). The preview zooms and pans (Ctrl+mouse wheel or pinch to zoom, drag or scroll to pan, fit and 100% buttons), switches diagram theme independently of the editor theme (a light, printable diagram in a dark IDE), and exports the diagram as SVG or PNG. If this IDE build doesn't support embedded browser rendering, the tab shows a plain message instead; everything else in the plugin is unaffected.

Works alongside JetBrains's own Mermaid plugin (bundled with IntelliJ IDEA from 2026.2): when both are installed, you're asked once which editor should own .mmd/.mermaid files, and the Preview tab stays available with either one.

Mermaid Companion Pro is an optional paid tier; everything described above stays free. Export on Save keeps a diagram's SVG and/or PNG export up to date every time you save the file, written next to it. A diagram that doesn't render leaves the existing exports untouched, and an unchanged diagram leaves the files alone.
idea-plugin.change-notes:

idea-plugin.name: JSON Schema Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Go-to-definition (Ctrl+Click) for `$ref` values inside JSON Schema files, resolved entirely against local files. A real paid competitor's reviewers reported: "the plugin seems not to be able to resolve the references via an internal database but tries to download them from the URI used as ID. This makes references unusable in local development." This plugin never makes a network call -- `$ref` resolution walks local `VirtualFile`s only, and an `http(s)://` `$ref` simply shows as unresolved rather than attempting to fetch it.

JSON Schema files are recognized by real content (a top-level `"$schema"` property referencing a real json-schema.org meta-schema), never by file extension guessing -- the other cited complaint: "Activates if you figure out the file extension it triggers on... the plugin randomly recognizes JSON schemas." Broken `$ref`s are flagged with a warning.

idea-plugin.name: Format Converter Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Converts JSON, YAML, and XML directly in the editor -- select text (or convert the whole file) and pick a target format from the editor popup menu. No file-path dialog, no "paste into a browser tab" detour: a real paid competitor's reviewers asked for exactly this ("I was expecting that I can convert editor content without extra dialog that asks me to enter two file paths").

Parsing/serialization run off the EDT on a pooled thread, so converting a large paste never freezes the IDE -- the other cited complaint against that competitor. JSON and YAML are hand-rolled parsers (no bundled Jackson/SnakeYAML dependency to avoid classpath fragility); XML uses the JDK's own javax.xml DOM APIs, hardened against XXE. Source format is detected from content, not file extension, so pasted/untitled text with no extension still detects correctly.

idea-plugin.name: XSD Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Go-to-definition and a real structure tree for XSD/WSDL schemas split across multiple files — resolved through <xs:include>/<xs:import>/ <xs:redefine>/<xs:override> and <wsdl:import>, entirely against local files.

Works the same whether the schema is one file or forty, and whether it is an .xsd or a .wsdl: inside a WSDL the schema sits under <wsdl:types>, and a WSDL splits across files through <wsdl:import location="..."> rather than schemaLocation. Both are followed.

Ctrl+Click (or Ctrl+B) on any schemaLocation or <wsdl:import> location value navigates straight to the referenced file — unresolved locations are flagged inline, naming the attribute that failed. The "XSD Structure" tool window follows the active editor and shows every element/complexType/ simpleType/attributeGroup/group declared across the whole include/import graph, not just the one file currently open.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network access — an http(s):// schemaLocation is never fetched, only ever shown as unresolved.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: FlatBuffers Format
idea-plugin.description:
Syntax highlighting and code formatting for FlatBuffers (.fbs) schema files. Formatting runs through the platform's own formatting service, so Reformat Code (Ctrl/⌘+Alt+L) works, and enabling Settings → Tools → Actions on Save → Reformat code gives you format-on-save with no extra plugin. The formatter delegates to the flatbuffers-format CLI for byte-for-byte parity with the published engine — same output you'd get from the VS Code extension, Prettier plugin, npx flatbuffers-format, or the pre-commit hook.

Features

  • Recognises .fbs as the FlatBuffers language.
  • Syntax highlighting (keywords, types, attributes, numbers, strings, comments) via a hand-rolled lexer mirroring the engine grammar.
  • Format the current file with Ctrl/⌘ + Alt + L (the usual Reformat Code shortcut) — shells out to flatbuffers-format asynchronously.
  • Settings page at Preferences → Tools → FlatBuffers for engine discovery and every format option the engine exposes.

Prerequisites

None, on a machine with Node 20+: the plugin ships the formatter as a JavaScript bundle and runs it on the Node you already have — including one installed by nvm, fnm, Volta, asdf, nodenv or mise, which an IDE launched from the Dock or a desktop shortcut cannot see on its own PATH. Otherwise:

  • Click "Download bundled engine" on the settings page (Preferences → Tools → FlatBuffers). The plugin fetches the matching native binary from the engine's GitHub Release and caches it under the IDE system directory. No Node, no npm required.
  • Or install via npm if you prefer to manage updates yourself: npm install -g flatbuffers-format. Auto-detected on PATH after install.

Supported IDEs

All JetBrains IDEs built on the IntelliJ Platform 2024.2 or newer: IntelliJ IDEA (Community + Ultimate), Rider, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, CLion, RustRover, RubyMine, PhpStorm, Aqua, DataGrip, DataSpell, MPS, and the Android Studio fork (2024.2-aligned).
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.2.0

  • First public release on the JetBrains Marketplace.
  • The formatter now ships inside the plugin as a JavaScript bundle and runs on any Node 20+ on your machine, including one installed by nvm, fnm, Volta, asdf, nodenv or mise — which an IDE started from the Dock or a desktop shortcut could not previously find. A Node below that floor is refused rather than used, and every fallback is reported once with the action that fixes it.
  • Bundled-engine download: if the flatbuffers-format CLI isn't on your PATH, the settings page can fetch a matching prebuilt binary from the project's GitHub Release and verify it against its published SHA256 sidecar.
  • The formatter's options are now real fields on the settings page — indent width, indent with tabs, line width, single-line collapsing of small enum/union/single-field bodies, max blank lines, comment reflow and comment width — each labelled with the engine's default and validated before it is saved. They used to be reachable only by typing flags into the free-text "Extra arguments" box, where a typo did nothing and said nothing. That box stays, for options the fields don't cover; anything you leave alone is still decided by the engine, not by the plugin.
  • Removed a non-functional "Format on save" checkbox. Use Settings → Tools → Actions on Save → Reformat code, which drives this formatter through the platform's formatting service.

0.1.0

  • Initial release.
  • .fbs file-type registration.
  • Lexer-driven syntax highlighting.
  • External formatter integration via AsyncDocumentFormattingService.
  • Settings page under Tools → FlatBuffers.
  • Line/block comment toggle support (Ctrl/⌘ + /, Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + /).

idea-plugin.name: TideStack Develop
idea-plugin.description:
TideStack Develop connects IntelliJ IDEA with the TideStack development platform. It helps developers edit TideStack metadata visually, bind local projects to a development platform, and run deploy-and-debug workflows from inside the IDE.

Highlights

  • Visual editors for TideStack JSON metadata files.
  • Dedicated UI Schema visual editor powered by the shared AMIS editor runtime.
  • Support for the new src/main/metadata convention.
  • Compatibility with legacy resources/META-INF/ouroboros metadata paths.
  • Built-in metadata file templates from the IDE's New menu.
  • Project-level TideStack Develop Config for platform binding.
  • One-click Deploy & Debug for Java extension projects.

Metadata Editing

TideStack Develop opens a visual editing tab for supported JSON metadata files while keeping the normal source editor available. It supports common TideStack metadata types including:

  • Authority metadata
  • Menu and development menu metadata
  • UI model metadata
  • UI Schema metadata
  • Business model metadata
  • Logic flow and approval workflow metadata
  • Field type metadata
  • Logic flow node metadata
  • Widget metadata
  • Micro web metadata
  • RPC model, RPC auth, and WebAPI metadata
  • Notification, business log, and data initialization metadata
  • MQ binding, schedule task, i18n locale, data dictionary, and position metadata
  • Error code collections
  • Application metadata and module tree diffs
  • Application modules
  • Configuration and configuration groups

File Conventions

The plugin supports both the new filename-based convention and the legacy resource directory convention. New projects can place metadata under src/main/metadata using files such as *.menu.json, *.authority.json, *.ui-model.json, *.ui-schema.json, *.business.json, *.field-type.json, *.flow-node.json, *.logicflow.json, *.workflow.json, *.widget.json, *.micro-web.json, *.rpc.json, *.rpc.auth.json, *.webapi.json, *.notification.json, *.business-log.json, *.data-init.json, *.mq.json, *.schedule.json, *.i18n.json, *.dict.json, *.position.json, error-codes.error.json, app.metadata.json, modules.diff.json, app-modules.json, configurations.json, and configuration-groups.json.

TideStack Develop Config

The configuration UI helps bind a local project to a TideStack development platform. Shared project settings such as the development server URL and application name can be stored in the project, while private local values such as the dev key remain in a local-only file.

Deploy & Debug

For Java extension projects, TideStack Develop can build the project, locate the generated JAR, upload it to the development platform, restart the target container, create a remote debug session, and attach IntelliJ IDEA's Remote JVM Debug configuration automatically.

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2023.1 or later.
  • Java 17 or later for plugin execution and project builds.
  • A TideStack development platform with the required development APIs enabled.

idea-plugin.name: Maven Dependency Overrides
idea-plugin.description:
Detects Maven <dependencyManagement> version overrides that have become stale because an imported BOM chain has caught up — the typical case is a version manually pinned ahead of a CVE fix that Spring Boot's own dependency management later provides at or above the pinned version.

What it does

  • Compares each pinned version against what the BOM chain actually manages it at, and warns directly in the editor, as a weak warning on the <version> tag, on the two cases worth acting on: a pin the BOM has exactly caught up to (now redundant) and a pin sitting below the BOM's own version (holding the dependency back). A pin still raising the version above the BOM stays silent — it's still doing its job. Quick fixes remove the override once it's no longer needed, or suppress the warning with a shared marker comment.
  • Provides a Maven Overrides tool window that lists every detected override across all pom.xml files in the project in one table, with a Status column, add / edit / remove actions, and click-to-navigate to the exact <version> tag.
  • Shows the full parent-chain path from the module down to the BOM that actually manages the version (e.g. spring-boot-starter-parent → spring-boot-dependencies → jackson-bom:2.21.2) — not just the bare BOM name, which is often something the developer never wrote themselves.
  • From the tool window's context menu, Show BOM Chain opens the complete chain for a row: every BOM consulted in precedence order, the one whose version actually applies, the ones that don't manage the dependency, and the ones that couldn't be read from the local repository. Where an unreadable BOM outranks the one that would otherwise win, the chain says the answer isn't known rather than naming a winner it can't vouch for — which is exactly what an inconclusive verdict is telling you. Analyze Dependencies hands the artifact off to IntelliJ's own Maven Dependency Analyzer to see what pulls it in.
  • Adding an override is guided: the tool window's + Add action offers separate Group ID and Artifact ID fields, each backed by what the target module's BOM chain actually manages, with type-to-filter and a browsable dropdown. The version field prefills from what's already managed, alongside a live note on what the version you type would mean — redundant, above the BOM, below it, or not comparable.

How it decides

Detection is local-only: it reads whatever BOM POMs are already in your local Maven repository. When a BOM in the chain can't be resolved there, the override is reported as inconclusive instead of confirmed, and no "safe to remove" quick fix is offered — a wrong "safe to remove" recommendation could silently reintroduce a patched CVE.

Requirements

IntelliJ IDEA (Community or Ultimate) with the bundled Maven support enabled. Any BOMs involved in the check must be present in the local Maven repository (i.e. the project has been imported at least once).
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • The Override Overview toolbar has a Filter by Status button: check or uncheck any of the six statuses to show only matching rows. The filter stays applied across Refresh, and a note above the table says how many rows it's currently hiding.

idea-plugin.name: Bean Copy Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Generates a real, compiling object-copy method between two Java or Kotlin classes -- select exactly two class files in the Project view, pick the copy direction, and get a new copier file with fields matched by name and type. The #1 complaint against the closest existing competitor in this space (a plugin with real crash reports and a "does not support Kotlin" review) is exactly what this plugin is built to not do: every field it can't safely map (type mismatch, no matching name, no way to set it) becomes an honest // TODO comment in the generated file instead of a crash or a silently wrong copy. The generated text is parsed against a throwaway in-memory PSI file and checked for syntax errors before anything touches disk -- same discipline already proven in this catalog's Test Scaffold Companion and Refactor Simulator.

Real support for what the competitor lacks: Kotlin data class targets (constructor-based, since val properties have no setter), Java 17+ record targets (canonical constructor), and Lombok @Builder targets -- all detected from the plain PSI tree, no Lombok/Kotlin compiler plugin dependency required.

100% local -- no network call, no account, no telemetry. All PSI analysis runs off the EDT; only the final file write touches it, and only after validation already passed.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: Change Case Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Select an identifier (or just place the caret on one -- no selection needed) and instantly convert it between camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, kebab-case, and CONSTANT_CASE. Understands acronyms correctly (XMLHttpRequest splits into XML/Http/Request, not letter-by-letter) and works starting from any of those styles, not just camelCase.

Ports a pattern that's genuinely popular elsewhere (VS Code's various "change case" extensions, millions of combined installs) with no real equivalent anywhere in JetBrains Marketplace -- confirmed by search before building, not assumed.

Works on Editor text directly, not PSI -- so it works identically in any file type, not just Java/Kotlin. 100% local -- no network call, no account, no telemetry.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: JSON to Code Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Select a JSON object -- in a .json file, a string literal, anywhere -- run "Generate Class from JSON", and get a real Java POJO or Kotlin data class with field types inferred from the actual JSON values, including nested objects (their own nested/sibling classes) and arrays (List<T>, typed from the first element).

Ports a pattern that's genuinely popular elsewhere ("Paste JSON as Code"-style tools, widely used across editors) with no real equivalent anywhere in JetBrains Marketplace -- confirmed by search before building, not assumed.

Never guesses past what the JSON actually shows: a null value or an empty/mixed-type array becomes an honest Object/Any field with a TODO comment, not an invented type. A JSON key that isn't a valid identifier gets sanitized into one, with the original key preserved in a comment. Every generated file is validated against an in-memory PSI copy before anything touches disk.

100% local -- no network call, no account, no telemetry.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: Env Diff Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Select exactly two env-style files in the Project view -- .env vs .env.example, .env.development vs .env.production, anything with KEY=VALUE lines -- run "Compare Env Files", and get a real report of which keys are missing from each side. The #1 real-world .env bug this catches: a new environment variable added to .env during development and never added to .env.example, so the next person to set up the project has no idea it's required.

Pure text comparison, not a values diff -- deliberately. Different values per environment (a dev vs. prod database URL) are usually intentional, not a bug; only presence/absence of a key is a real signal worth flagging.

100% local -- no network call, no account, no telemetry. Works on any file, `.env`-named or not; never depends on a `.env` PSI plugin being installed.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: Import Cost Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Run "Check Import Sizes" on a JS/TS file and get a real report of every node_modules package it imports, sorted by on-disk size, with unusually large ones flagged.

Born from real evidence in JetBrains Marketplace reviews of the closest existing plugin in this space (135K downloads, 75% of reviews at 3 stars or fewer): a documented, years-long pattern of severe CPU spikes and IDE freezes -- "drains 100% CPU... battery lasts one hour", "freezes my IDE and I cannot work" -- from recalculating package sizes continuously, inline, on every keystroke.

This plugin's whole design exists to not do that: it runs only when you ask it to, reads real on-disk package sizes (never invokes a bundler), and never recomputes anything automatically in the background. The direct fix for a performance complaint is a design that structurally can't reproduce it, not a faster version of the same always-on computation.

100% local -- no network call, no account, no telemetry.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • A package imported through subpaths (lodash and lodash/debounce) was listed once per import, each with the whole package's size. The report now has one line per package, naming its imports.
  • Node.js built-in modules (fs, node:path) were reported as "not found locally". They are listed apart as built-ins, unless a package of that name is installed (browser polyfills such as buffer).
  • Dynamic import('x') was not detected.

idea-plugin.name: Regex Preview Companion
idea-plugin.description:
A tool window with a pattern field and a sample-text area -- type a regex, type or paste sample text, and every match is highlighted live as you type, with a real match count. Case insensitive, multiline, and dot-all flags are real checkboxes, not something you have to remember inline syntax for. An invalid pattern shows the real PatternSyntaxException message instead of just going blank.

Ports a pattern that's genuinely popular elsewhere (standalone regex testers like regex101 are a daily tool for many developers) directly into the IDE, with no real equivalent already in JetBrains Marketplace -- confirmed by search before building, not assumed.

Self-contained -- a Swing panel with java.util.regex, never hooked into the IDE's own highlighting pipeline. 100% local -- no network call, no account, no telemetry.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: Error Lens Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Shows errors and warnings inline, at the end of the line that has them, instead of only as a gutter icon or squiggly underline you have to hover to read. Ports the "Error Lens" concept (VS Code's Error Lens extension: 10M+ installs) into the IDE's own highlighting pipeline -- it reads the diagnostics the IDE already computed, it never re-analyzes anything itself.

Reads only already-finished HighlightInfo results from a pass registered to run after the IDE's own general highlighting pass, and refreshes them once the IDE has finished highlighting the file -- no duplicate analysis, no network call, no telemetry. One hint per line (the most severe diagnostic wins), so it never turns into unreadable clutter on a line with several problems.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Every inline error started with an empty box: the error icon "✖" has no glyph in JetBrains Mono, the default editor font. Each icon is now checked against the editor font, with a fallback (×, !, i) when the font can't draw it.
  • A fixed problem could keep its inline hint (typing a missing ; left "';' expected" at the end of the line): the hints were read before the IDE dropped obsolete highlights. They are now refreshed once highlighting of the file has finished.

idea-plugin.name: Binary Template Support
idea-plugin.description:
Language support for 010 Editor Binary Template (.bt) files in IntelliJ-based IDEs.

Provides syntax highlighting, completion for the official language vocabulary, comment support, brace matching, and optional Hex Support structure analysis for 010 Editor Binary Template files with Hex Support 3.0.0 or later.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 1.0.2: Add the shared Hex Support structure analysis phrase to Marketplace metadata so Hex Support can discover this provider without maintaining a plugin ID.
  • 1.0.1: Make the optional Hex Support integration version-aware at runtime, so Hex Support 2.x remains loadable while 3.0.0 and later provide binary structure analysis, and avoid unresolved 3.0 API packages during Marketplace verification.
  • 1.0.0: Add .bt file recognition, native editor syntax highlighting, completion for keywords, built-in types, template attributes, constants and official built-in functions, comment and brace support, configurable colors, and an optional Hex Support structure provider.
