idea-plugin.name: HTTP Status Code Inline Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Shows the official name of any HTTP status code (404 -> Not Found, 503 -> Service Unavailable) inline, right after the numeric literal, in Java and Kotlin code -- no need to look it up. Works in any code context, not tied to a specific HTTP framework's own annotations.

Only lights up in places with real HTTP signal: a call whose method name looks like status handling (setStatus(404), sendError(500)), an annotation like @ResponseStatus(404), or a comparison against something named like a status holder (statusCode == 404). An ordinary loop bound or an unrelated numeric literal that happens to match a real status code (for (i in 0..500)) never shows a hint -- see the plugin's README for the full heuristic and worked examples.

The status table is the real IANA HTTP Status Code Registry (RFC 9110 and related RFCs) -- a number that merely looks plausible (3 digits, in range) but isn't a registered code, like 499 or 250, never gets an invented name.

100% local -- no network call, no account, no telemetry.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Inlay hint: any Java or Kotlin integer literal that is a real IANA-registered HTTP status code (RFC 9110 and related RFCs) shows its official name inline, right after the number (404 -> Not Found), when it sits in a context with reasonable HTTP signal -- a call whose method name looks like status handling (setStatus(404), sendError(500), HttpStatus.valueOf(404)), an annotation like @ResponseStatus(404)/@ApiResponse(code = 404), or a comparison against a status-shaped identifier (statusCode == 404).
  • Deliberately does not hint on an ordinary numeric literal with no HTTP signal (a loop bound, an unrelated field, an argument to an unrelated method) even when the number happens to match a real status code -- see README "Detection heuristic" for the full rule and worked examples.
  • A number that merely looks plausible (3 digits, in the 100-599 range) but isn't a real IANA-registered code -- 499 (an Nginx convention), 250, 419 (a Laravel convention) -- never gets an invented name, even in a strong-signal context.

idea-plugin.name: Dockerfile Layer Size Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Shows the real, on-disk size of each COPY/ADD layer in an open Dockerfile, inline -- computed by summing the actual file sizes of what gets copied from your local build context, respecting .dockerignore. No Docker daemon, no build, no network call: 100% static analysis of the project already open in the IDE.

For RUN instructions, there is no way to know the real size a command will add to a layer without actually running it -- so this plugin never invents a number for RUN. Instead it flags well-documented, known-expensive patterns (apt-get install without --no-install-recommends, apt-get update without cleaning the package cache in the same instruction, pip install without --no-cache-dir, several separate RUN instructions that could be combined) with an honest "known-expensive pattern" label, never a fabricated size.

Multi-stage COPY --from=<stage> and ADD <url> (a network download, not a local file) are both recognized and labeled honestly as not calculable, rather than silently guessing or crashing.

Free. 100% local -- no network call, no account, no telemetry.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • A file named Dockerfile.md/.markdown/.mdx/.rst/.adoc is no longer treated as a real Dockerfile. Unlike a plain warning, this plugin does real filesystem I/O for COPY/ADD sizing, so misdetecting a doc file meant resolving and sizing paths against a directory that had nothing to do with a real build context. Real variants (Dockerfile.prod, Dockerfile.arm64) are still recognized.
  • ADD <url> <dest> (a real Docker feature -- downloads over the network at build time) is now labeled "downloads from a URL -- not calculable without fetching it" instead of the misleading "source not found in build context", which implied a broken local file rather than a network source.
  • The known-expensive curl/wget check no longer fires on apt-get install curl/apk add wget -- installing the tool never downloads anything during the build. It still fires on a real invocation, including one in the same RUN that also installs the package.

Added

  • Review/star CTA: after 10 distinct known-expensive-pattern warnings, a one-time notification asks whether to rate the plugin on Marketplace, with a permanent "Don't ask again" option. Standard mechanism used catalog-wide; this plugin had been missed.

idea-plugin.name: Unused npm Script Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Gutter icon on every entry of an open package.json's "scripts" section, showing whether that script is actually referenced anywhere in your project -- or an orphan nobody calls, a real candidate for cleanup.

Where it looks:

  • The package.json's own other scripts ("build": "npm run clean && npm run compile" marks clean/compile as used).
  • GitHub Actions workflows (.github/workflows/*.yml), GitLab CI (.gitlab-ci.yml), and CircleCI (.circleci/config.yml) next to the package.json.
  • README.md next to the package.json.

Only real invocations count -- npm run <name> (or npm run-script), yarn [run] <name>, pnpm [run] <name>, bun [run] <name>, with or without options before the name, and the npm-run-all CLIs (run-s, run-p, npm-run-all, globs included) -- never a bare word match, so a script named build is never flagged as "used" just because the word appears unrelated somewhere in a README paragraph.

npm lifecycle scripts (pretest/test/ posttest, prepare/prepublishOnly, preinstall/postinstall, preversion/postversion, start/stop/restart, and any real script's own pre/post hook) are never flagged as orphaned, even with zero text references -- npm runs those automatically by convention.

100% static text/PSI analysis of files already open in your project -- no network call, no Node.js/npm process spawned. A project with no package.json, or one with no "scripts" section, is handled as an honest no-op, never a crash.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no popups.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • A script called with yarn run <name> (a common CI form) was flagged "possibly unused" while it was in use. Also recognized now: npm run-script, bun / bun run, options before the name (npm run -s build), and the npm-run-all CLIs run-s, run-p and npm-run-all, including globs (lint:*).
  • stop and restart are run by npm stop / npm restart and are no longer flagged as orphaned.

idea-plugin.name: Env Var Missing Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Cross-checks every real environment-variable access in your open file (process.env.PORT, process.env["PORT"], os.environ["DEBUG"], os.environ.get("DEBUG"), os.getenv("TIMEOUT")) against your project's real .env/.env.example files, and warns on any variable that's used in code but never declared anywhere -- with a real quick-fix to add it.

Scope (v0.1, deliberate):

  • Scans the file currently open in the editor, not the whole project on every keystroke -- the real, common case (you just typed a new process.env.X reference and want to know right now if it's declared).
  • JavaScript/TypeScript and Python -- the two ecosystems where reading env vars by string key (process.env.X/os.environ[...]) is the dominant pattern. Java/Kotlin are out of v0.1: that ecosystem's dominant pattern is Spring's @Value/application.properties injection, not direct System.getenv calls, so this specific code↔.env cross-check pattern is comparatively far less common there.
  • A variable with an explicit default right in the code (process.env.PORT || 3000, os.environ.get("DEBUG", "false"), os.getenv("TIMEOUT", 30)) is flagged as a weaker warning, not a full warning -- the code still runs fine without it declared, so it's real but less urgent.

Quick-fix: "Add VARNAME to .env.example" appends VARNAME= to your project's real .env.example -- or creates one from scratch (with a header comment noting it was generated) if your project has none at all.

Complements Env Diff Companion (which compares two .env files against each other) -- this plugin compares your actual code against your .env files instead.

100% static text analysis of files already open in your project -- no network call, no external process spawned. A project with no .env* file at all is handled as an honest "everything referenced is unmatched" case, never a crash.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no popups.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: SQL String Concatenation Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags SQL queries built by unparameterized string concatenation or interpolation -- the classic SQL-injection shape -- in Java, Kotlin, and Python, and offers a real quick-fix toward parameterization.

What triggers it (both conditions required):

  • A string literal that looks like the start of a real SQL statement (SELECT/INSERT/ UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE/ WITH, or CREATE/ALTER/ DROP/TRUNCATE), built with +, a Kotlin template, a Python f-string, .format() or % from a value that could carry injected SQL -- e.g. "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'" (Java/Kotlin), "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $userId" (Kotlin template), f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = {user_id}" (Python), or "... WHERE id = %s" % user_id.
  • The resulting string is used near a call that looks like it executes SQL: Statement.executeQuery/executeUpdate/execute, cursor.execute/executemany (Python DB-API), rawQuery (Android), createQuery/createNativeQuery, and .query(...).

What does NOT trigger it (the anti-false-positive design, see README for the full worked list):

  • Literals and constants ("SELECT * FROM " + TABLE_USERS + " WHERE id = ?"), numbers (an int parameter, %d placeholders), and locals last assigned a literal.
  • A SQL-keyword-shaped string with no nearby execution call -- a log message -- and commented-out code.
  • A value already parameterized correctly (? placeholders with PreparedStatement.setX(...), or a DB-API parameter tuple like cursor.execute(query, (param,))).

On 271 public Java, Kotlin and Python files that execute SQL, 28 of a random sample of 30 warnings were real queries built from a variable.

Where it fits: IntelliJ IDEA with Database Tools has a built-in data-flow inspection for Java/Kotlin ("Non-safe string is used as SQL"); with both on you'll see two warnings on the same line. Without it -- IntelliJ IDEA without Database Tools, Android Studio, PyCharm -- this plugin works on its own, with no server and no build.

Quick-fix, honest scope: replaces the interpolated value with a ? placeholder and adds a TODO(sql-concat) comment naming the variable that still needs to be bound as a real parameter (.setString(1, ...)/cursor.execute(query, (param,))). It does not infer the value's real type or its correct positional index across a multi-placeholder query -- stated here rather than pretended to be handled.

Deliberately narrow (not a full SAST scanner like Qodana): one specific pattern, near-zero configuration, tuned hard against false positives.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no popups.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: Feature Flag Reference Companion
idea-plugin.description:

Until the first refresh, call sites show a neutral "not yet scanned" icon instead of guessing.

Java and Kotlin in v0.1. 100% static analysis of files already open in your project -- no network call, no provider connection, no telemetry.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no popups.

idea-plugin.name: Log Format String Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags a log message whose placeholder count doesn't match its argument count -- a common bug that today only surfaces at runtime: a leftover placeholder stays literal in the log output, or an extra argument is silently dropped.

What triggers it:

  • SLF4J-style, Java/Kotlin -- log.info("User {} logged in from {}", userId, ipAddress): counts {} occurrences in the message literal and compares against the trailing arguments.
  • Python %-style logging -- logger.info("User %s logged in", user_id): counts %s/%d/etc. specifiers and compares the same way.

The SLF4J trailing-exception case, handled correctly: SLF4J treats a last argument as the exception to log (not a placeholder argument) when the call has exactly one more argument than placeholders -- the conventional shape log.error("Failed for {}", userId, exception) (1 placeholder, 2 arguments) is correct, never flagged.

What does NOT trigger it (tuned hard against false positives, see README for the full list): a message with no placeholders and no extra arguments, an exact placeholder/ argument match, the conventional trailing-exception shape above, and any case where the last argument's type can't be determined with certainty -- conservative by design, a missed real mismatch beats a false alarm.

Scope, honest about what's out: SLF4J-style Java/Kotlin and Python %-style logging only. Python f-strings are deliberately NOT scanned -- their interpolations are inline expressions, not separate arguments, so there's no placeholder-count-vs-argument-count mismatch to detect in the same shape (see README). Log4j2/structlog/Kotlin logging framework support and placeholder-type-mismatch detection are future work, not silently pretended to be handled.

Deliberately narrow: one specific pattern, near-zero configuration, tuned hard against false positives.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no popups.

idea-plugin.name: Commit Message Convention Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Validates the commit message you are currently writing, live, in the IntelliJ VCS Commit dialog -- against the Conventional Commits convention -- and shows the exact rule it breaks before you commit, instead of silently accepting or rejecting.

What it checks (v0.1, Conventional Commits standard, all Free):

  • First line matches <type>(<scope>): <description> or <type>: <description> (scope is optional).
  • <type> is one of the standard, case-sensitive types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, revert.
  • Subject line length: a hard warning past 72 characters (the widely-used "hard cap" for `git log --oneline` readability), a softer heads-up between 51 and 72 (above the 50-character "ideal" but still commonly accepted).
  • Description does not end with a period.

What it deliberately skips: merge commits (git-generated messages like Merge branch 'x' into 'y' are never written by hand and are never validated).

What v0.1 does NOT cover (honest scope, see README for the full list): commit footers (BREAKING CHANGE:, Refs:), the ! breaking-change marker after type/scope, and configurable team rules (custom scope whitelist, custom regex, team-specific length limits) -- that is a distinct, larger feature intentionally left for a future version, not silently half-implemented here.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no popups.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Live validation of the commit message you are currently writing, in the IntelliJ VCS Commit dialog, against the Conventional Commits convention -- via a real CheckinHandlerFactory/CheckinHandler (confirmed signature, first use of this platform mechanism in the Gap Hunter Labs catalog).
  • Rules checked: <type>(<scope>): <description> / <type>: <description> header shape; the 11 standard, case-sensitive Conventional Commits types (feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, revert); subject line length (hard warning past 72 characters, soft suggestion between 51-72); description must not end with a period.
  • Merge commits are always skipped -- a git-generated message (Merge branch 'x' into 'y', Merge pull request #N from ...) is never written by hand and is never validated.
  • Exact violation shown before committing, not a silent accept/reject -- e.g. "missing type prefix", "unknown type 'xyz', expected one of: build, chore, ci, ...", "subject line exceeds 72 characters (currently 80)".
  • Honest v0.1 scope: commit footers (BREAKING CHANGE:, Refs:), the ! breaking-change marker after type/scope (feat!: ...), and configurable per-team rules (custom scope whitelist, custom regex, team-specific length limits shared via VCS) are NOT covered -- documented as real, deliberate gaps for a possible future version, not silently half-implemented.
  • 100% local text validation of the commit message string -- no network call, no external process spawned, no PSI/file parsing needed.

idea-plugin.name: FlashJump
idea-plugin.description:
FlashJump provides keyboard-driven label navigation for JetBrains IDEs.

Type a search character, then press the label displayed at the destination to jump there without leaving the keyboard.

Features:

  • Real-time, case-insensitive matching.
  • Distance-aware labels that keep nearby targets easy to reach.
  • Character, word, line, forward, backward, jump-end, and selection modes.
  • Navigation across multiple editor windows.
  • Configurable labels, colors, search range, highlighting, backdrop, and automatic jump behavior.

Default shortcuts:

  • Ctrl+; — activate FlashJump or cycle to the next jump mode.
  • Ctrl+Alt+; — start target selection mode.
  • Ctrl+Shift+; — start line jump mode.
  • Enter — jump to the default match.
  • Backspace — clear the current search and start again.
  • Esc — cancel the active FlashJump session.

FlashJump 是一个面向 JetBrains IDE 的键盘快速跳转插件。输入搜索字符，再按目标位置显示的标签即可完成跳转。

idea-plugin.name: Line Numbers
idea-plugin.description:
Line Numbers display relative line numbers in your editor gutter, making navigation faster and more intuitive. Perfect for developers who prefer line numbers that adapt to their current cursor position.

Key Features

  • Relative Numbering: Shows the distance from your current line
  • Clean Interface: Optionally hide the IDE's default absolute line numbers
  • Smart Navigation: Quick jumps with distance-based mental math
  • Instant Toggle: Turn relative numbering on or off with a keyboard shortcut
  • Current Line Highlight: Clearly highlights the line where your cursor is located

How It Works

Lines show their distance from your caret position:

             2 | code
             1 | code
            20 | code <- current line (highlighted, shows actual line number)
             1 | code
             2 | code

Configuration

Settings → Editor → Line Numbers

  • Enable/disable the feature
  • Option to hide built-in line numbers for a cleaner look

Keyboard Shortcuts

  • Windows/Linux: Ctrl + Alt + N
  • macOS: ⌘ + ⌥ + N (Cmd + Option + N)

Why Flexible Numbers?

Relative line numbers help you navigate code faster by showing exactly how many lines to move up or down, rather than forcing you to calculate distances from absolute line numbers. Popular among Vim users and developers working with large codebases.

A tool window (reusing Regex Preview Companion's own matching engine) lets you test a pattern against real sample text and see every named group's actual extracted value per match (year: "2024"), not just the overall match highlighted.

An invalid pattern shows the real PatternSyntaxException message instead of just going blank, and a pattern with zero named groups shows no inlay at all -- never a false hint on an ordinary string.

idea-plugin.name: Webhook Signature Companion
idea-plugin.description:

100% static text/PSI analysis -- matches the mapping path and a broad set of signature-verification signals (method names like verifySignature, or raw text like hmac/Mac.getInstance) by simple text, so it works whether the real Spring/crypto libraries are on the classpath or not. Java and Kotlin.

idea-plugin.name: Merge Conflict Leftover Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags real Git merge-conflict markers (<<<<<<<, the diff3 |||||||, =======, >>>>>>>) left behind in any file -- a real, distinct problem from an active unresolved merge (which the IDE's own Commit window already flags in red): a merge that was already resolved and committed, but with the markers themselves accidentally left in the file.

100% plain-text scan, any file type -- no PSI-per- language dependency, no network calls.

Stated honestly: a <<<<<<< or >>>>>>> line is always flagged, including documentation that cites the literal marker syntax as an example -- a real, accepted trade-off (favoring not missing a genuine leftover marker over filtering out rare documentation false positives). A line of exactly seven = is also a Markdown or reStructuredText title underline, so ======= and ||||||| are only flagged in a file that also has one of the angle-bracket markers.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • A title underlined with exactly seven = -- a Markdown (setext) heading or a reStructuredText section such as "License" or "Changes" -- was flagged as a conflict separator. ======= and ||||||| are now only reported in a file that also has a <<<<<<< or >>>>>>> line.
  • In YAML (and any language whose tokens split the marker line), the ||||||| and >>>>>>> markers were silently not reported, and others were underlined only partly. Each warning now covers the whole marker line.
  • In a Markdown file every marker was reported twice.

idea-plugin.name: CORS Policy Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning icon on any Java/Kotlin Spring @CrossOrigin(origins = "*", allowCredentials = "true") annotation (class- or method-level) -- this exact combination is forbidden by the CORS spec itself: browsers reject a wildcard origin combined with credentials, so requests silently fail (or, worse, the intent behind the annotation is misunderstood entirely).

Also covers the programmatic WebMvcConfigurer registration -- registry.addMapping(...) .allowedOrigins("*").allowCredentials(true) -- as a single-statement fluent chain, regardless of call order.

The wildcard origin pattern with credentials (allowedOriginPatterns("*"), originPatterns = "*") gets its own warning: Spring allows it and the requests work, because every origin is echoed back -- so any website can make credentialed requests and read the responses. Only a literal "*" counts as the wildcard (https://*.example.com is not reported).

100% static PSI analysis -- matches by simple name only, works whether the real Spring jar is on the classpath or not. Java and Kotlin.

Stated honestly: does not cover a CorsConfigurationSource/ UrlBasedCorsConfigurationSource setup where the wildcard origin and the credentials flag are set on separate statements against a CorsConfiguration object built up over multiple lines.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • A wildcard origin pattern with credentials (allowedOriginPatterns("*")) was explained as "invalid per the CORS spec, browsers reject it" -- false: Spring allows it, the requests work, and every origin is echoed back, so any website can make credentialed requests and read the responses. It now has its own warning saying exactly that; @CrossOrigin(originPatterns = "*") is covered too.
  • A * inside an origin (https://*.example.com) was taken for the wildcard; only a literal "*" is reported now.
  • @CrossOrigin(value = "*", ...) (the alias of origins) and Kotlin's positional @CrossOrigin("*", ...) were not checked.

idea-plugin.name: PHP Composer Script Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Gutter icon per "scripts" entry of an open composer.json, showing whether it's used or an orphan candidate. A script counts as used when another script reuses it (@name, as Composer documents), or when a real invocation -- composer run-script <name>, composer run <name>, composer <name>, with options, composer.phar or @composer -- appears in:

  • CI configs: GitHub Actions workflows and composite actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Travis CI, Bitbucket Pipelines, Jenkins, Azure Pipelines;
  • build and container files: Makefile, package.json, Dockerfile, compose files, shell scripts in the project root, bin/, scripts/ and build/;
  • git hooks: CaptainHook, GrumPHP;
  • docs: README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md (and the other instructions files for coding agents), Markdown files in docs/, and READMEs one folder down.

A script's scripts-aliases (Composer 2.7+) count as the script, and a CI matrix picked by composer ${{ matrix.task }} is recognized.

Recognizes Composer's own documented script event names (pre-install-cmd, post-autoload-dump, etc.) as always-used, same as npm lifecycle scripts.

100% static text analysis, no Composer CLI invocation. Not read: files outside those paths, PHP code that runs Composer itself, and commands only ever typed by hand -- a script used only that way shows as an orphan candidate, which is exactly what the icon says: nothing in the project calls it.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: Semver Bump Mismatch Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags a CHANGELOG.md release entry (Keep a Changelog format) whose own body text reads as a breaking change -- the word "BREAKING", or a ### Removed section (removing a feature is breaking by definition, even without the word appearing) -- but whose version, versus the release right before it, only bumped MINOR or PATCH -- SemVer expects a MAJOR bump for a breaking change, and this is a real, easy mistake: bumping the version by copy-pasting the previous release's shape without checking whether this release's actual content warrants MAJOR.

100% plain-text scan of your own CHANGELOG.md -- no external changelog/semver library, no network calls.

Stated honestly: only looks for the literal word "BREAKING" (not negated -- "non-breaking"/"no breaking changes" don't count) or a ### Removed section in the release body -- a breaking change described without either signal isn't caught. Releases under major 0 are never flagged -- SemVer itself treats the whole 0.x line as "anything can break".

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • The warning underlines the whole release header (## [1.5.0]).

    With the Markdown support every IntelliJ IDE bundles, it only underlined the ## marker, which was easy to miss and hard to hover.

  • Each mismatch is reported once. In the IDE a CHANGELOG.md is read through more than one syntax tree, and the same warning appeared twice (the problem count read 2 for a single release).

  • The inspection has a description page (Settings | Editor | Inspections, and the expanded warning) instead of "Under construction".

idea-plugin.name: Prometheus Metric Naming Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning icon on any Java/Kotlin metric name literal that violates Prometheus's own documented naming conventions (prometheus.io/docs/practices/naming) -- recognizes the two most common real registration shapes: the Prometheus Java client's Counter.build("name", "help") and Micrometer's Counter.builder("name") (same for Gauge/Histogram/Summary/Timer).

Checks: the name should be lowercase snake_case, a counter's name should end in _total, and a Histogram/Summary's name should never manually carry _bucket/_count/_sum (the client library appends those itself when exposing the metric). All three cited directly in Prometheus's own naming documentation.

Micrometer names follow Micrometer's own convention: lowercase words separated by dots (http.server.requests), with no _total required -- its Prometheus registry converts the name and the Prometheus client adds _total to counters itself. Only an uppercase/camelCase Micrometer name is reported.

100% static PSI analysis -- matches by simple class/ method name only, works whether the real Prometheus/Micrometer jar is on the classpath or not. Java and Kotlin.

Stated honestly: only checks the name literal passed directly to build(...)/builder(...) -- the Prometheus client's alternate chained form (Counter.build().name("x")) isn't covered yet.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Micrometer meters are checked against Micrometer's naming convention, not Prometheus's. Counter.builder("orders.created") (lowercase words separated by dots, the style Micrometer documents) was flagged as not snake_case, and a Micrometer counter was told to end in _total, which its Prometheus registry leaves to the Prometheus client (it appends _total itself and rejects a name that already has it). Now only an uppercase/camelCase Micrometer name, or a manual _bucket/_count/_sum, is reported. The Prometheus Java client's Counter.build("name", "help") keeps its three rules.

idea-plugin.name: Correlation ID Propagation Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Gutter warning icon on any Java/Kotlin Spring MVC handler method that receives a correlation/trace-id header via @RequestHeader and makes an outbound HTTP call in its own body, but never references that header parameter again anywhere in the body -- the common footgun where the incoming id is captured and then silently dropped instead of being forwarded to the downstream call, breaking distributed tracing and making cross-service log correlation impossible for that request.

100% static text/PSI analysis -- matches the header parameter name (correlation-id, trace-id, request-id, etc.) and a broad set of outbound-HTTP call signals (RestTemplate, WebClient, OkHttpClient, .exchange(, and similar) by simple text, so it works whether the real HTTP client libraries are on the classpath or not. Java and Kotlin.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only checks whether the header parameter's identifier is referenced again anywhere in the same method body -- it can't confirm the id is forwarded correctly to the *specific* outbound call (e.g. as the right header on the right request), only that it isn't obviously dropped. Calls made from a different method than the one receiving the header aren't covered.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: API Deprecation Header Companion
idea-plugin.description:

The @Deprecated annotation only warns people reading or compiling the source; it tells real API consumers (a mobile app, a third-party integration, another team's service) nothing at all, since nothing in the actual HTTP response signals it.

100% static text/PSI analysis -- matches the mapping annotation, the @Deprecated annotation, and a broad set of header-setting signals by simple text, so it works whether the real Spring classes are on the classpath or not. Java and Kotlin.

100% static text/PSI analysis -- matches the method name by simple text, so it works whether the real OpenTelemetry SDK is on the classpath or not. Java and Kotlin.

idea-plugin.name: Config Secrets File Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on a suspected real secret (AWS access key, GitHub/ Slack token, JWT, PEM private key, or a high-entropy value assigned to a secret-shaped key name) hardcoded directly in a config file -- .properties, .env (and its variants), or a .yml/.yaml file. 100% static text analysis -- known credential-format signatures (AWS/GitHub/Slack/JWT/PEM) plus a variable-name + Shannon-entropy heuristic for the generic case, no network calls, works offline. The entropy heuristic is a real heuristic, not a guarantee -- it can miss a real secret with unusually low entropy, or (rarely) flag a long random-looking non-secret value.

idea-plugin.description:

idea-plugin.name: PII Field Annotation Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Gutter warning icon on any Java/Kotlin class field whose name looks like it holds PII (email, ssn, phoneNumber, dateOfBirth, creditCard, passportNumber, nationalId, taxId, and similar) with no annotation of any kind on it -- no way for masking, redaction, or access-control tooling built around annotations to ever pick it up.

100% static text/PSI analysis -- matches the field name by simple text, and accepts any annotation as "classified" (there's no single standard PII annotation across teams -- a Bean Validation constraint, a Jackson view, a custom @Pii/@Sensitive, anything counts). Java and Kotlin, including Kotlin primary-constructor properties.

Stated honestly: v0.1 covers the most common, unambiguous PII field-name shapes only -- it is not an exhaustive privacy-law taxonomy (GDPR/CCPA "personal data" is far broader and inherently contextual). A field with an unusual name that still holds PII isn't covered.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: Dockerfile Unused Stage Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on a named multi-stage Dockerfile build stage (FROM ... AS name) that's never referenced by a later COPY --from=name and isn't the file's own final stage -- an orphaned intermediate stage that's real, wasted build time and a confusing read for the next person touching the file (usually left behind after a refactor that moved what it built into another stage).

100% static text analysis -- a plain-text line scanner, not a Dockerfile-language parser, so it works whether the real Docker plugin is installed or not.

Stated honestly: v0.1 can't see a stage referenced only via an explicit docker build --target=name invocation outside the file -- that will be flagged as a false positive. Stage names are matched case-insensitively, same as Docker itself.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: Ruby Gemfile Group Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on a well-known dev/test gem (RSpec, RuboCop, Pry, FactoryBot, Capybara, SimpleCov, WebMock, VCR, and similar) declared at a Gemfile's top level instead of inside a group :development/group :test block -- it ships in every environment, including production, bloating the bundle and (for something like Pry or letter_opener) a real footgun if it's ever accidentally reachable in production.

100% static text analysis -- a plain-text line scanner, not a Ruby-language parser, so it works whether the real Bundler/RubyMine plugin is installed or not.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only recognizes the common group :development, :test do ... end block form -- the single-line gem "x", group: :test inline form (a valid alternative Bundler syntax) isn't specially handled. The gem list is curated, not exhaustive -- only gems whose entire purpose is dev/test tooling are included.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: Rate Limiter Fallback Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Gutter warning icon on any Java/Kotlin method annotated with a Resilience4j resilience annotation (@RateLimiter, @CircuitBreaker, @Retry, @Bulkhead, @TimeLimiter) whose fallbackMethod = "name" doesn't match any method in the enclosing class -- a real, silent footgun: nothing fails at compile time, but Resilience4j throws at runtime the first time the fallback is actually triggered (rate limited, circuit open, retry exhausted), which can be a rare code path that isn't exercised until production.

100% static text/PSI analysis -- matches the annotation and the referenced method name by simple text, so it works whether the real Resilience4j jar is on the classpath or not. Java and Kotlin.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only checks that a method with the given name exists somewhere in the class -- it doesn't validate the fallback's parameter/return-type signature actually matches what Resilience4j requires. A wrong-signature fallback with the right name isn't covered (yet).

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: AWS SDK Client Reuse Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Gutter warning icon on an AWS SDK for Java 2.x service client (S3Client, DynamoDbClient, SqsClient, SnsClient, LambdaClient, and similar) built via XxxClient.builder().build() inside a regular method body -- AWS's own documentation states service clients are thread-safe and meant to be created once and reused; a client built inside a method means a brand new client (and its own connection pool) gets created on every call, a real, documented performance footgun.

100% static text/PSI analysis -- matches the client class name by simple text, so it works whether the real AWS SDK jar is on the classpath or not. Java and Kotlin.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only flags the direct .builder().build() chain -- a builder assigned to an intermediate variable before .build() is called isn't specially traced. Never flags a build call inside a constructor or a field/property initializer (legitimate "create once" locations).

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: Object Mapper Reuse Companion

Building one inside a method means the real construction/configuration cost is paid on every call.

100% static text/PSI analysis -- matches the mapper class name by simple text, so it works whether the real Jackson jar is on the classpath or not. Java and Kotlin.

Stated honestly: v0.1 never flags a construction inside a constructor or a field/property initializer (legitimate "create once" locations). Doesn't trace a mapper built once and passed around -- only the construction site itself is checked.

idea-plugin.name: OkHttp Client Reuse Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Gutter warning icon on an OkHttpClient built via new OkHttpClient() or new OkHttpClient.Builder().build() inside a regular method body -- OkHttp's own documentation states "OkHttp performs best when you create a single OkHttpClient instance and reuse it for all of your HTTP calls, because each client holds its own connection pool and thread pools... creating a client for each request wastes resources on idle pools". Building one inside a method means a brand new connection pool (and thread pools) gets created on every call.

100% static text/PSI analysis -- matches the class name by simple text, so it works whether the real OkHttp jar is on the classpath or not. Java and Kotlin.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only flags the "build from scratch" shape -- existingClient.newBuilder()....build(), OkHttp's own documented pattern for customizing a shared client without duplicating its connection pool, is never flagged (correctly, since it isn't the anti-pattern this plugin targets). Never flags a build call inside a constructor or a field/property initializer.

idea-plugin.name: Kafka Producer Reuse Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Gutter warning icon on a new KafkaProducer<>(...) construction written inside a regular method body -- Apache Kafka's own javadoc, unchanged across every released version, states "The producer is thread safe and sharing a single producer instance across threads will generally be faster than having multiple instances." Building one inside a method means the real connection/initialization cost is paid on every call, and defeats internal batching across calls.

100% static text/PSI analysis -- matches the class name by simple text, so it works whether the real Kafka client jar is on the classpath or not. Java and Kotlin.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only checks KafkaProducer -- KafkaConsumer is deliberately excluded (unlike the producer, a single consumer instance is not safe to use from multiple threads concurrently, so "build once, reuse" isn't the same unqualified recommendation there). Never flags a construction inside a constructor or a field initializer.

idea-plugin.name: gRPC Error Status Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Gutter warning icon on a streamObserver.onError(rawException) call where the argument isn't converted through gRPC's own Status type -- gRPC's own StreamObserver.onError javadoc states the parameter "should be a StatusException or StatusRuntimeException, and callers should generally convert from a Status via Status.asException() or Status.asRuntimeException()". Passing a raw exception means its real type/message never reaches the client -- gRPC only transmits the Status code and description across the wire, not the original exception.

100% static text/PSI analysis -- matches the receiver variable name and the argument's converted-Status signals by simple text, so it works whether the real gRPC jar is on the classpath or not. Java and Kotlin.

Stated honestly: v0.1 doesn't resolve the receiver's real type -- a variable named observer that isn't actually a StreamObserver is a possible (rare) false positive, and a real StreamObserver with an unusual variable name isn't covered.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: Ecko
idea-plugin.description:
Language support for Ecko - the language where ai is a keyword, not an import. Works in every IntelliJ-based IDE, including the free Community editions.

An LLM call is a language construct rather than a client library, so it composes like any other expression. Ask for one of your own types and the answer arrives already checked against it:

type Sentiment = Positive | Negative | Neutral

@tool("look up which plan a customer is on")
fn plan_for(customer) = "enterprise"

fn triage(message) = ai[Sentiment] message using [plan_for]

print(match triage("The build has been broken for three days.") {
    Positive => "no action"
    Negative => "escalate"
    Neutral => "queue"
})

That runs with no API key. Ecko has a deterministic mock mode, so typed calls return schema-valid values and your pipelines, tools and contracts keep working before a provider is configured.

What this plugin gives you

  • Diagnostics, completion, hover, go-to-definition and symbols from ecko lsp - which is the compiler itself, so the editor cannot disagree with a build.
  • Find Usages, quick fixes, Reformat Code and semantic highlighting, also from the server. Find Usages is scope-aware and scoped to the open file; the lightbulb repairs a misspelled name, an unused import, an unused binding, or a non-exhaustive match. Needs Ecko 0.16.0 or later.
  • Syntax highlighting for .ecko, with no server needed: the ai clauses (using, with, on, via, -> stream), ## documentation comments, contract and tool annotations, sql { ... } blocks, string interpolation, and byte and decimal literals.

Requirements. The ecko binary, installed with curl -fsSL https://ecko.sh/install | sh. The plugin checks ECKO_BINARY, then PATH, then ~/.local/bin, ~/.ecko/bin and /usr/local/bin - an IDE started from a launcher or Toolbox often does not inherit a shell's PATH, which is almost always why a server will not start. LSP4IJ is a required dependency and the IDE offers to install it for you.

Ecko is proprietary software: free for personal and educational use, and for evaluating it in a business for 30 days. Other business use needs a commercial licence - see ecko.sh/enterprise.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.59.1

  • Operators highlight as one token. ==, |>, -> and // were each split in two, because the shorter pattern was tried first. Fixed, along with the compound assignments Ecko 0.58 added (+= through %=).
  • New syntax is coloured: \u{...} escapes (they used to open an interpolation hole), the via clause, typed parameters and x in xs.
  • Version now matches the language release it was checked against.

0.22.0

  • Version caught up to the language. Everything ecko lsp gained since 0.16.0 - references, document highlight, code actions, semantic tokens - arrives through the client with no plugin change.

0.16.0

  • Find Usages and occurrence highlighting. Scoped to the open file, and scope-aware: a name shadowed in an inner block resolves to its own declaration rather than to every occurrence of the spelling.
  • Quick fixes. A lightbulb on four diagnostics - correct a misspelled name to the suggestion the compiler already computed, remove an unused import, prefix an unused binding with _, or fill in the missing arms of a non-exhaustive match.
  • Semantic highlighting. Colour from the compiler rather than the grammar, so standard-library modules and types are distinguished from ordinary names.
  • Reformat Code now comes over LSP. Same result as ecko fmt, but the plugin no longer shells out to the binary through a temporary file - and no longer uses the experimental ExternalFormatProcessor API, which was the only thing verifyPlugin flagged.

Requires Ecko 0.16.0. On an older binary the server does not serve these, and Reformat Code will do nothing - use the 0.15.0 plugin instead.

0.15.0

  • First release on the JetBrains Marketplace.
  • Grammar updated for Ecko 0.15.0, shared byte-for-byte with the VS Code extension.
  • New logo, replacing a retired version of the mark that was illegible at the 16px the file-type icon is drawn at.
  • Syntax highlighting works. It never had in any earlier version: the grammar was registered against an extension point that does not exist, it was read from inside the plugin archive in a way that throws once packaged, and nothing gave the Ecko file type a highlighter at all. All three are fixed and covered by tests.
  • Editor basics. Ctrl+/ comments a line, brackets match, and quotes and brackets close themselves - none of which worked before.
  • 37 live templates, the same shortcuts the VS Code extension ships: ai, ait, @tool, match, sql and the rest.
  • Reformat Code runs ecko fmt, so the IDE formats a file exactly the way a build would.
  • The ecko binary is now also looked for in ~/.local/bin, where the public installer puts it.

idea-plugin.name: JSON Path Builder Companion
idea-plugin.description:
A tool window with a JSONPath field and a sample-JSON text area -- type an expression, type or paste sample JSON, and every matched node is highlighted live as you type, with a real match count.

Covers the common JSONPath subset: $ root, .key, ['key'], [n] (array index), .*/[*] (wildcard), and ..key (recursive descent -- every value named key at any depth). An invalid expression shows the real parse error and position instead of silently matching nothing.

100% static PSI analysis of your typed sample -- no external JSONPath library, no network call. Stated honestly: v0.1 does not cover filter expressions ([?(...)]), array slices, union syntax, or recursive wildcard (..*) -- real, documented limitations, not bugs.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry.

idea-plugin.name: N+1 Query Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Gutter icon on any Java/Kotlin for loop whose body accesses a lazy-loaded JPA association (@OneToMany/ @ManyToMany by default, or @ManyToOne/ @OneToOne with an explicit fetch = FetchType.LAZY) directly on the raw loop variable -- the classic N+1 query shape: fetch a collection, then trigger one extra query per element while iterating it.

Unlike a pure hover/visualization tool, the tooltip names the exact association and annotation responsible so the fix (an explicit JOIN FETCH/@EntityGraph, or an eager fetch where that's the right trade-off) is obvious at the exact loop that needs it.

v0.2 (Java): one method-call hop into a same-class helper. for (Customer c : customers) { process(c); } where process's own body accesses a lazy association on its corresponding parameter is now flagged too -- the query lives in a helper method rather than inline, exactly how well-factored code tends to look. Bounded to exactly ONE hop, a same-class call only -- never a chain of two or more hops.

100% static PSI analysis -- matches JPA annotations by simple name only, so it works whether the real jakarta.persistence/javax.persistence jar is on the classpath or not. Stated honestly: v0.1 only checks direct access on the raw loop variable (a variable derived from it isn't matched yet), and only classic for/for (x in y) loops, not .forEach/stream chains -- real, documented limitations, not bugs.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: Changelog Fragment Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Manages per-PR changelog fragments, the towncrier-style convention: instead of every PR editing the same CHANGELOG.md and fighting merge conflicts, each PR adds a small changelog.d/<issue>.<type>.md file, later collected into a real changelog at release time.

New Changelog Fragment (Tools menu) prompts for an issue/PR number, a type, and a one-line description, and writes the file for you -- no need to remember the naming convention by hand. An inspection flags any file inside changelog.d/ whose name doesn't match the convention (typo'd type, missing issue number, wrong extension) before it ships in a release.

100% local file convention, no towncrier/external tool required. Stated honestly: v0.1 hardcodes the common default type set (feature/bugfix/doc/removal/misc) and only checks a directory literally named changelog.d -- a custom type list or a differently-named fragments directory isn't covered yet.

idea-plugin.name: Batch Script Support
idea-plugin.description:
Modern support for Windows batch files (.bat, .cmd) in JetBrains IDEs.

The existing batch plugins are syntax highlighters with no semantic layer, and both have been unmaintained for years. This one understands your script.

Inspections that catch real bugs

  • Delayed expansion errors — !VAR! without setlocal enabledelayedexpansion silently expands to literal text instead of the value. It is the most common batch bug there is, and it fails quietly.
  • Undefined labels — goto :typo is caught before you run it.
  • Unused labels — dead code and misspellings.

Navigation and editing

  • Ctrl-click goto :build to jump to :build
  • Find usages and rename refactoring for labels
  • Structure view outlining every label in the file
  • Completion for labels, variables, and built-in commands
  • Hover documentation for built-in commands
  • Block indentation, brace matching, comment/uncomment
  • Run configuration for executing scripts

A lexer that gets the awkward parts right

Batch is genuinely hard to parse. This handles :: versus REM versus :label, all four meanings of % (%VAR%, %1, %~dp0, %%i), delayed expansion, ^ line continuation, and redirections like 2>&1 — each covered by tests.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.0

  • Initial release: lexer, semantic highlighting, three inspections, label navigation, find usages and rename, structure view, completion, hover docs, formatter, and run configurations.

idea-plugin.name: Kubernetes Missing Readiness/Liveness Probe Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on any container entry in a Kubernetes workload manifest (Deployment, Pod, StatefulSet, DaemonSet) with no readinessProbe: and/or no livenessProbe:. Without a readiness probe, Kubernetes can't take a sick pod out of the load balancer -- real traffic keeps being routed to a broken instance. Without a liveness probe, a hung (not crashed) process is never automatically restarted. Both are a real, recurring cause of documented availability incidents.

100% static text analysis -- an indentation-based line scanner, not a real YAML parser, so it works whether the real Kubernetes/YAML plugin is installed or not. Same scanner shape as this catalog's own k8s-resource-limit-companion. Only scans files whose top-level kind: is a workload kind that keeps long-lived containers (Deployment, Pod, StatefulSet, DaemonSet) -- Job/CronJob are out of scope, since a run-to-completion pod isn't kept behind a Service the same way.

Stated honestly: v0.1 handles the common single-document, `containers:`/`- name: x` shape -- multi-doc files (`---` separators) and YAML anchors/aliases aren't specially resolved. Never validates that `initialDelaySeconds`/`periodSeconds` values are reasonable, only the total absence of the probe block.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: Optimus Accessibility
idea-plugin.description:
Optimus Accessibility is a real-time web accessibility (a11y) inspection tool for JetBrains IDEs. It works with React, Angular, and Vue, as well as vanilla HTML/JS/TS — performing a single-pass PSI tree traversal to check your HTML, JS, JSX, TS, TSX, and Vue files — including injected template strings — against WCAG/ARIA accessibility rules as you type, with one-click quick fixes.

📌 v1.0 Release: This is the 1.0 release of Optimus Accessibility. The real-time accessibility linter described here is just one aspect of the plugin — it is the first part of a larger roadmap — see below.

✨ Core Features

  • Real-Time Inspection: one optimized traversal delegates each element to every active rule — no per-rule inspection overhead.
  • 27 Accessibility Rules: across General, Anchor, ARIA, and Role categories, covering WCAG & ARIA standards.
  • Quick Fixes: add/remove attributes, remove elements, or rename tags to resolve violations instantly.
  • Framework-Aware: full inspection support for React (JSX/TSX), Angular, and Vue, as well as vanilla HTML/JS/TS — distinguishing native HTML from framework components so rules aren't misapplied to custom elements.
  • Flexible Configuration: enable/disable rules individually in Settings > Editor > Optimus Accessibility, grouped by category; export your configuration to a shareable optimus-accessibility.json; or point the plugin at a project-level JSON config file to drive rule state directly (JSON mode takes priority over manual settings).

🚀 Rule Categories

  • General & Images: Image alt text checks, form label association, heading contents, iframe titles, autofocus/accesskey rules.
  • Anchors & Links: Link validity, ambiguous text detection, and content checks.
  • ARIA Attributes: ARIA attribute validation, active descendant checks, aria-hidden focus safety.
  • Roles & Elements: Semantic tag preference over roles, role-attribute constraints, element-to-role compatibility.

🔮 What's Next

Optimus Accessibility is the first phase of a larger project. Planned for future releases:

  • Deep Project-Level Analysis: Advanced cross-file a11y auditing and compliance summaries.
  • AI-Powered Suggestions: Intelligent AI assistance for auto-generating alt text, aria labels, and structural accessibility repairs.
  • Framework-Specific Rule Sets: Today's rules are framework-aware but generic (the same 27 checks run everywhere); future rules will target patterns specific to React, Vue, Angular, and common UI design systems.
  • Expanded WCAG Coverage: Additional rules to cover more WCAG success criteria beyond the current 27.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Real-time accessibility inspection (GlobalAccessibilityInspection) via a single PSI tree traversal that checks every active rule in one pass, including elements inside injected template strings.
  • 27 accessibility rules covering WCAG & ARIA standards, grouped into General, Anchor, ARIA, and Role categories.
  • Automated quick fixes to add/remove attributes, remove elements, and rename tags.
  • Multi-framework support for Angular, React (JSX/TSX), Vue, and vanilla HTML/JS/TS, distinguishing native HTML elements from framework components.
  • Settings page (Settings > Editor > Optimus Accessibility) to enable/disable individual rules, grouped by category.
  • Project-level JSON configuration file support to control rule state outside the IDE, taking priority over manual settings when enabled.
  • Export current rule configuration to a shareable optimus-accessibility.json file.
  • Multi-module plugin architecture separating the core implementation (core) from the plugin assembly module.

idea-plugin.name: Markdown Link Keeper
idea-plugin.description:
Keeps your Markdown links working when files move.

When you move or rename a file, this plugin automatically updates every relative Markdown link that pointed to it, across the whole project. The change is a single undoable command, so one Ctrl+Z reverts it.

The bundled Markdown support only highlights a broken link once you open the file that contains it. In a documentation set with hundreds of pages, moving one file silently breaks links scattered everywhere.

  • Automatic link updates on file move and rename
  • Project-wide scan listing every link that points to a missing file
  • Never touches external URLs, mailto links, anchors, or fenced code blocks

  • 檔案搬移或改名時，自動更新所有指向它的相對連結（可用 Ctrl+Z 復原）
  • 一鍵掃描全專案，列出所有指向不存在檔案的連結
  • 絕不動到外部網址、mailto、錨點，以及程式碼區塊裡的連結

idea-plugin.name: JQuick Java Language Support
idea-plugin.description:
JQuick Java Language Support — IntelliJ support for jquick-java rule scripts (.jquick), reusing the built-in ANTLR4 engine of jquick-java. Provides token-level syntax highlighting, real-time syntax diagnostics rendered as error squiggles, code completion covering keywords, built-in types plus functions / variables / parameters / import aliases defined in the current file, and paired-bracket support with auto-closing brackets and matching highlight. No external language-server process required; works on both Community and Ultimate editions.

中文：面向 jquick-java 规则脚本（.jquick）的 IntelliJ 插件， 复用 jquick-java 内置的 ANTLR4 引擎，在 IDE 内直接提供：

  • 语法高亮：关键字 / 字符串 / 数字 / 注释 / 运算符 / 括号等分组着色；

idea-plugin.name: SqlD-Lite Syntax
idea-plugin.description:
Syntax highlighting and code navigation for SqlDelight .sq and .sqm files. It does the same job as the official SqlDelight plugin with less in it. It generates no code; the SqlDelight Gradle plugin does that.

  • Highlighting for SQL and for what SqlDelight adds: query labels, :named and ? bind arguments, imports and AS column types. Every colour can be changed under Editor | Color Scheme | SqlDelight.
  • PostgreSQL syntax that core SQL rejects, such as ON CONFLICT, RETURNING, SELECT DISTINCT ON, window functions, array types, GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY, the :: cast, the ->> JSON operators and the PostgreSQL ALTER TABLE actions. A migration written for PostgreSQL is not painted red.
  • Go To Declaration from a Kotlin query call to its query label, from a named argument to the bind argument it fills, and from a label to every Kotlin call. It reads an index, so it works before you build the project.
  • Find Usages on a table, view or column name reports the whole migration chain: the CREATE, every ALTER after it and every statement that uses it. The same list comes back from any of them, and occurrences in .sql files come with it.
  • Quick Documentation and cmd-hover on a query, a bind argument or a table, view or column name show what it declares.
  • A gutter icon on a query label lists the Kotlin calls to it, and an inspection reports a query that nothing calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changed

  • Cmd-hover and Quick Documentation on a query or a bind argument show the function SqlDelight generated, with its parameter types and its return type, read from the generated Kotlin. Quick Documentation no longer repeats the query statement, which the reader is already looking at.

Fixed

  • A Kotlin argument reached from a bind argument is titled query argument, not query call.

idea-plugin.name: Dynamic Query
idea-plugin.description:
IDE support for @DynamicQuery, where [ ... ] marks an optional predicate that the runtime keeps or drops depending on whether its parameters are bound. The annotation's nativeQuery attribute picks the dialect:

  • nativeQuery = false (the default) — JPQL
  • nativeQuery = true — Native SQL

The plugin injects JPAQL or SQL into the annotation's value and optional countQuery while leaving the [ ] markers out of the injected fragment, so IntelliJ's own parsers see a plain query. You keep syntax highlighting, entity/table and field/column resolution, completion and parameter inspections — and no longer need @Language("JPAQL") or @Language("SQL").

@DynamicQuery("""
    SELECT u FROM UserEntity u
    WHERE 1 = 1
    [ AND u.name = :name ]
    [ AND u.age = :age ]
    """)

idea-plugin.name: Semantic Syntax
idea-plugin.description:
Semantic Programming Language for JetBrains

High-quality editor support for the Semantic Programming Language in JetBrains IDEs.

Semantic Programming Language is a universal, matrix-driven programming language and compiler architecture based on canonical SemanticProgram / Universal Abstract Syntax Tree (UAST) representations.

This plugin focuses on fast, lightweight language support for readable Semantic source files and integrates .se and .sp files directly into IntelliJ Platform editors.

Features

  • Syntax highlighting for .se and .sp
  • Semantic keyword and constant highlighting
  • Strings, numbers and Semantic references
  • # line comments
  • Semantic operators and delimiters
  • JetBrains file-type integration
  • Semantic file and plugin icons

Semantic source

se 1

# Semantic Programming Language
program Demo
object Main

scope example {
    node item
    relations

    true
    %12
    @42
    "Hello Semantic"
    123
}

About Semantic

The broader Semantic architecture represents programs independently of their original source language. Source code can be lowered into a canonical SemanticProgram/UAST representation and processed through shared validation, transformation, transpilation and compiler stages.

Publisher: Tarek Wasfy

Website: https://www.semantic-programming-language.com/

GitHub: https://github.com/SemanticProgrammingLanguage/Semantic-Programming-Language-for-JetBrains

License: MIT License — View license
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Metadata update

  • Added official publisher information.
  • Added website, GitHub and license links.
  • Expanded the JetBrains Marketplace overview.

idea-plugin.name: Blade Vue Connector
idea-plugin.description:
Connects Vue components used in Laravel Blade views to their .vue files.

For Vue apps mounted on Blade layouts, where component tags such as <text-input> are written directly in Blade views:

  • Go to declaration: Ctrl+click a component tag to open its .vue file.
  • Component tags are recognised: they are coloured (Settings | Editor | Color Scheme | Blade Vue Connector) and no longer reported as unknown HTML tags.
  • Unregistered components: an inspection reports tags that look like components but aren't registered in any Vue app.
  • Find Usages on a .vue file lists the Blade views that use it, under every name it is registered as.

Components are found by following registrations in your JavaScript and TypeScript files: app.component(...), Vue.component(...) and components: {} on createApp(...) / new Vue(...), including require(...).default, defineAsyncComponent(...) and dynamic import(...). A tag that isn't registered falls back to a .vue file with the same name.

idea-plugin.name: Block Banner Generator
idea-plugin.description:
Turns a few words into a big block-letter banner comment, in any language: English, Korean, Japanese, Chinese, symbols, mixed. Instead of FIGlet fonts it rasterizes the text with a font installed on your machine, so anything your system font can draw becomes a banner.

Styles
  • Shadow: █ block body with a ╗║╝═ box-drawing shadow (ANSI Shadow look)
  • 3D: block body extruded down-right with ▒
  • Shade: brightness mapped to .:-=+*#%@
Usage
  • Quick: select text and press Alt+Shift+B (macOS ⌥⇧B). The selected lines are replaced by a banner with your last-used settings, no dialog.
  • Dialog: right-click and choose Block Banner…, or Code → Generate. The dialog opens with the selected text filled in; pick font, rows and style with a live preview, then OK replaces the selection.
  • With nothing selected, both open the dialog and insert the banner above the caret line.
  • Several selected lines become stacked banners. A leading comment marker on the selected lines is removed first.
The comment prefix (//, #, --, <!-- -->, …) comes from the file's language and can be edited in the dialog.

Default shortcut: Alt+Shift+B on Windows/Linux, ⌥⇧B on macOS (Quick Block Banner). Change it in Settings → Keymap, search "Block Banner".

한국어
몇 단어를 큼직한 블록 글자 배너 주석으로 바꿔 줍니다. 영어, 한글, 일본어, 중국어, 기호, 혼합 등 모든 문자가 됩니다. FIGlet 폰트 대신 PC 에 설치된 폰트로 글자를 직접 그리기 때문에, 시스템 폰트가 표시할 수 있는 문자는 전부 배너가 됩니다.

스타일
  • Shadow: █ 블록 몸체 + ╗║╝═ 박스 문자 그림자 (ANSI Shadow 느낌)
  • 3D: 블록 몸체를 오른쪽 아래로 ▒ 로 압출
  • Shade: 밝기를 .:-=+*#%@ 문자로 표현
사용법
  • 빠른 실행: 텍스트를 드래그하고 Alt+Shift+B (macOS ⌥⇧B). 마지막 설정값으로 선택 줄이 즉시 배너로 바뀝니다. 다이얼로그 없음.
  • 다이얼로그: 드래그 후 우클릭 → Block Banner…, 또는 Code → Generate. 선택한 글자가 채워진 채 열리고, 폰트·행수·스타일을 미리보기로 고른 뒤 OK 하면 선택 줄이 교체됩니다.
  • 선택이 없으면 둘 다 다이얼로그가 열리고 커서 줄 위에 삽입됩니다.
  • 여러 줄을 선택하면 줄마다 배너가 쌓입니다. 선택 줄 앞의 주석 기호는 먼저 뗍니다.
주석 기호(//, #, --, <!-- --> 등)는 파일 언어에서 가져오며 다이얼로그에서 고칠 수 있습니다.

기본 단축키: Windows/Linux Alt+Shift+B, macOS ⌥⇧B (Quick Block Banner). Settings → Keymap 에서 "Block Banner" 를 검색해 바꿀 수 있습니다.
idea-plugin.change-notes:

idea-plugin.name: Intellij plugin development with Maven
idea-plugin.description:
This plugin provides minimal support for developing IntelliJ plugins using IntelliJ Maven integration.

First, this plugin imports Maven module as plugin modules (PLUGIN_MODULE) if one of the following is true:
  • Packaging is set to 'ij-plugin'
  • Packaging is set to 'jar' and 'ij.plugin' property is set to 'true'
  • Packaging is set to 'jar' and 'com.guidewire.build:ijplugin-maven-plugin' Maven plugin is configured for the module

Second, it removes all dependencies which have groupId starting with 'com.jetbrains.intellij.' after the import, assuming they would be provided through the IDEA SDK (so you can use these dependencies during the command-line build and have them fulfilled by IDEA SDK automatically when you import your module)

Third, this plugin updates plugin descriptor location using one of the following:
  • Explicitly configured value in the ijplugin-maven-plugin configuration.
  • Value of the 'ij.pluginDescriptor' property in the POM
  • Default value of "META-INF/plugin.xml"

If maven-surefire-plugin is configured to skip or exclude the test, 'verify' goal will be used, see different configuration styles at https://github.com/harishkannarao/MavenSurefireFailsafeExamples

idea-plugin.name: Maven Executor
idea-plugin.description:
Maven Executor is a plugin for IntelliJ IDEA that provides new tool window with maven run parameters. It is an alternative for the standard Maven Project Tool Window.

Functionality
Toolbar Menu
  • Execute Goals For Selected Projects - executes goals with a current parameter for selected Maven modules.
  • Execute Goals For All Projects - always executes goals with a current parameter for all projects or project chosen from Project ComboBox.
  • Current Maven Run Settings - opens detailed Current Maven Run Settings, more bellow.
  • Reimport Maven Projects - standard reimport all maven projects action.
  • Generate Sources and Update Folders For All Projects - standard maven generation sources and updating folders action.
  • Maven General Settings - opens general Maven Settings.
  • Save Current Settings as... - saves favorite settings, saving is possible only when Favorite List is visible.
  • Visible Properties Settings - allows adjusting visible properties to own preferences on Tool Window.
Main Configuration
  • Goals - maven goals to execute.
  • More Parameters - parameters which will be added to result command.
  • Offline - enable/disable maven --offline flag.
  • Update Snapshots - enable/disable --update-snapshots flag.
  • Threads - number of thread to run parallel, -T option (currently not supported "thread per cpu").
  • Profiles - list of Maven profiles.
  • Jvm Options - optional JVM Options, when checkbox is selected, parameters are added to main JVM parameters (from dialog window).
  • Projects ComboBox - list of Maven Project, allows narrowing visible project in Tree of Projects.
  • Expand All - expands all nodes in Tree of Projects.
  • Collapse All - collapses all nodes in Tree of Projects, information about collapsed nodes is persisted.
Tree of Projects
  • Tree of checkbox representing structure of maven projects. Each node is maven module. If all nodes are selected, project is built normally. When only some nodes are selected, project is built with --projects option. In both cases, order of building modules is calculated by Maven Reactor.
  • Build This Now - actions visible after pressing right mouse button. Build immediately hovered module with current settings.
  • Select/Deselect Others - actions visible after pressing right mouse button.
Favorite List
  • Mode Button - allows changing width of Favorite List. In addition, it is possible to hide this section via Visible Properties Settings.
  • DEFAULT - it is a label to default settings - always available.
  • Favorite - list of shortcuts to saved settings, every change is immediately saved.
Selection Buttons
  • Open - selects modules by current open files (open, not selected and visible in editor Tab).
  • Modified - selects module by modified files since last build (list of modified files is cleared after each build).
Current Maven Run Configuration
  • Settings available from ToolBar menu contain all Maven settings with JVM Options and Environment Variables.
  • Result Command - shows real command (in Advance Mode) which Maven will execute. There is also Simple Mode for increasing readability.
  • Always add a parent POMs modules to build - when module is selected in the tree, parent POMs module will be added to build, even if not all the leaves are selected.

idea-plugin.name: Package Checker
idea-plugin.description:
This plugin checks your third-party dependencies for known vulnerabilities. It suggests a safe version, if available, to make your code more secure. It also scans source code for vulnerable API calls to highlight the most critical problems.

The following package managers and build files are supported:

  • Amper build system (module.yaml, module.amper, project.yaml, project.amper, and module template files)
  • Gradle (build.gradle, build.gradle.kts)
  • Maven (pom.xml, pom-4.0.0.xml, pom.*, *.pom)
  • npm, pnpm and Yarn (package.json)
  • PyPI (setup.py, requirements.txt)
  • Poetry and Pipenv (pyproject.toml, Pipfile)
  • Go Modules (go.mod)
  • Composer (composer.json)
  • JPS - JetBrains Project System (*.iml)
  • sbt (build.sbt), provided by the Scala plugin

The plugin provides the following security inspections:

  • Vulnerable declared dependency scans packages defined in your code (such as packages added to a supported build file).
  • Vulnerable imported dependency detects packages that are not defined in the source code (such as transitive dependencies).
  • Vulnerable API usage shows vulnerable methods and functions in Java source code (out of the box) and in Kotlin source code (if you have the Kotlin plugin installed).
  • Malicious dependencies detects malicious NPM and PyPI dependencies in your project to prevent your software from being compromised.

Vulnerable API inspections are language-specific and provided as part of the corresponding language plugins: JavaScript and TypeScript, Python, and Go.

Here is a list of the plugins required to support the related functionality: Gradle, Maven, JavaScript and TypeScript, Python, Go, PHP, and Scala.

Problems identified by Package Checker are reported on the Problems | Vulnerable Dependencies tab. The plugin also provides the Analyze | Vulnerable Dependencies action.

Package Checker doesn't send information about packages to the JetBrains server in cleartext form. It sends only hashed names of packages. We never log or process hashes we don't have in our database, and we don't analyze your proprietary or confidential packages.

Vulnerability data provided by Mend.io and OSV.dev.

Plugin source code © 2024, JetBrains s.r.o..

idea-plugin.name: MavenHelperPro
idea-plugin.description:
MavenHelperPro is a must have plugin for working with Maven.

Abstract

  • Analyzing and excluding conflicting dependencies.
  • Dependencies version check and upgrade.
  • Search dependency without open the browser.

Features

  • Display the list of dependent components for the current project based on the analysis of the pom file.
  • Conflict analysis and elimination of dependent component versions.
  • Display the space size and filter search of each component.
  • Analyze the current pom file to display the latest version of the current dependent components.
  • Provide single and batch upgrades for components with the latest version available.
  • Provide search functions for aliyun, nexus, sonatype, and mvn central repository components on the right tab, supporting keywords and GAV searches.
  • Click on the search results to obtain each version of the selected component, and double-click on each version list to obtain specific Maven and Gradle configurations.
  • Provide an optional NPM package search tab.

How to use

  • Open pom file and click on the 'Dependency Analyzer' tab to maven dependency analysis and version conflict resolution.
  • Open pom file and click on the 'Dependency Version Checker' tab to check if the current dependency has the latest version.
  • You can perform individual and batch upgrades as needed.
  • Click on the 'MavenSearch' tab on the right to support searching for components in the central repository of aliyun, nexus, sonatype, and mvn based on keywords and GAV coordinates.
  • In the table displaying specific components, the configuration of Maven coordinates and Gradle coordinates can be obtained by double clicking the mouse.

  • 在右侧MavenSearch选项卡中支持按关键字和GAV信息从阿里云、本地Nexus等中央仓库中搜索组件

注：本插件由“Maven With Me(MPVP)”插件拆分而来，如您同时有项目版本更新、项目版本搜索、项目版本显示、项目版本徽章生成、项目配置同步(自动同步JDK等配置)的场景需求，可直接单独安装“Maven With Me(MPVP)”插件。



✨Features / 核心功能



More Strategy To Update Version.

Default Strategy

- must have new version and changed version.

- when version exist and matched will replace and support dependency version is special value (e.g: ${version} / [1.6, 1.8]) will continue replace.

General Strategy

- must have new version.

- when version exist and matched will replace.

Support Must Same Version (Before)

- if checked: project or dependency version not equals project before replacement version will continue replace.

- if not checked: new version will to replace.



Maven项目版本更新支持多策略.

默认策略

- 必须存在新版本并且变更版本.

- 当版本存在且匹配时将会替换；并且支持依赖版本是特殊值 (e.g: ${version} / [1.6, 1.8]) 将会跳过替换.（依赖中使用项目版本占位符的会跳过替换，但会修改对应的变量属性版本值；如果依赖中使用的是版本范围的将不做处理）.

常规策略

- 必须存在新版本.

- 当版本存在并且匹配时将替换. （即将依赖中的版本替换为当前要应用的新版本）

支持必须同一版本 (变更前)

- 选中: 项目或依赖版本如果不等于替换之前的版本将跳过替换.

- 未选中: 新版本会直接替换.
