idea-plugin.name: devradar
idea-plugin.description:
devradar shows which of your teammates currently have the same git repository open and are coding right now — and lets you chat with them 1-to-1 inside the IDE. Works in any IntelliJ-based IDE (Rider, IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, WebStorm, and more), and alongside the matching VS Code extension and Visual Studio extension — your teammates can be on any of them and you'll all land in the same room.

Zero configuration: your identity comes from git (user.name / user.email), and the "room" is derived from the repository's remote URL — so everyone who opened the same repo is automatically in the same room. No login, no token, no setup.

What you get:
  • Status-bar widget with a live "N online" count; click it for a popup that lists every teammate and which file they're editing.
  • Chat tool window (View → Tool Windows → devradar Chat): pick a peer, send messages, with "last seen N minutes ago" for offline teammates and banners when the connection is down.
  • Balloon notifications when someone messages you — even when the chat tool window is closed — with an Open action that jumps straight into the conversation.
  • Settings at Tools → devradar: custom server URL, display-name override, and an optional team key for private rooms (only people who know the phrase can join).
Intentionally not included (this is presence + quick coordination, not a chat product): no read receipts, no typing indicators, no message persistence (offline messages aren't delivered), no group chats.

The presence server is open source (Cloudflare Workers + Durable Objects): github.com/mertkont/devradar

idea-plugin.name: Open in Azure DevOps
idea-plugin.description:

Features

idea-plugin.description:
Log time to Clockify directly from your JetBrains IDE — no context switching required.

Features

  • Tool window — log time at any moment from the Clockify sidebar panel.
  • Pre-filled from Git — the time entry description is pre-populated with your latest commit message.

Getting started

  2. Paste your Clockify API token (found at clockify.me → Profile → API) and click Validate.

idea-plugin.name: GitLab Pipeline Watcher
idea-plugin.description:
Watches GitLab CI pipelines for the current project, reusing the authentication configured in the official JetBrains GitLab plugin (works with self-hosted GitLab too).

  • Lists recent pipelines with status, ref, SHA and duration.
  • Detects git push --tags and follows the pipeline triggered by the tag until it finishes.
  • Disables itself when the project has no .gitlab-ci.yml.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• +N en lugar del icono de tag (toolWindow/PipelineTreeRenderer.kt) — el icono AllIcons.Nodes.Tag que añadió la 1.0.1 para los commits con varios tags se ve en el New UI como un <> sin significado, y como solo aparecía en esas filas, las descuadraba respecto a las demás. Se quita el RowIcon: todas las filas vuelven a llevar solo el punto de estado, y los tags hermanos se cuentan con un +N tras la versión, en negrita pequeña con el color de enlace del tema (Link.activeForeground), para distinguirlo del texto gris. El tooltip sigue listando los tags ("También etiquetado en este commit: …").
  • Franja de detalle del pipeline seleccionado (toolWindow/PipelineToolWindowFactory.kt, messages/PipelineBundle{,_es,_zh_CN}.properties) — al seleccionar un pipeline aparece bajo el árbol, encima de la tira de stages, "Detalles del commit: [#id]". Si el commit tiene varios tags, se añaden un separador y "Tags: [tag] [tag] …", con el tag de la propia fila incluido. Cada elemento es un botón con icono de copiar: el #id copia el número sin # y cada tag copia su nombre. Las líneas usan WrapLayout, así que los tags largos bajan de línea en vez de cortarse. Al seleccionar un job o nada, la franja se oculta. El #id sale de la fila del árbol (push/v1.1.2 +2 · hace 17 h) y queda solo aquí; la copia del id por clic derecho sigue igual. Keys nuevas en los tres idiomas: details.commit, details.commitTags, details.copyTag.
  • Fix: coroutines del plugin rechazadas por el stdlib del IDE (build.gradle.kts) — el compilador Kotlin 2.4.20 escribe en las coroutines @DebugMetadata(v=2), y el stdlib 2.2 que trae IntelliJ 2025.2 solo acepta v=1: cuando las debug probes de coroutines recorren una continuation nuestra, lanzan Debug metadata version mismatch. Expected: 1, got 2. En el sandbox (runIde, modo internal, probes siempre activas) rompía la lectura del token de GitLab (GitLabAuthBridge.tokenFor): salía "No GitLab account configured" y el globo "IDE error occurred". Se fija apiVersion/languageVersion = KOTLIN_2_2; verificado con javap que la metadata vuelve a v=1. Hay que subirlo a la vez que el sinceBuild.
  • Dev: autoReload = false para runIde (build.gradle.kts) — nada más arrancar, el sandbox veía el .jar recién copiado como modificado y recargaba el plugin en caliente. Con eso desaparecía el tool window y PluginSearchableOptionContributor fallaba con el descriptor ya descargado (Can't find bundle for base name messages.PipelineBundle). Solo afecta al desarrollo: después de un buildPlugin hay que reiniciar el sandbox.
  • Docs — README: línea de features al día (+N, franja de detalle; el doble clic copia la versión, no abre el navegador), "Stack" con IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.19 y dos Build notes nuevas (apiVersion 2.2, autoReload), a las que apuntan los comentarios de build.gradle.kts.
  • Tests — suite completa verde (./gradlew test); testBundlesSameKeysAndPlaceholders cubre las keys nuevas en los tres idiomas.

idea-plugin.name: Copilot Cost Lens
idea-plugin.description:
Copilot Cost Lens — AI Usage & Spend Tracker

Know exactly what your AI coding tools cost you — per repository, per model, per day. 100% local and private. Copilot Cost Lens reads the logs that GitHub Copilot (VS Code Chat and the Copilot CLI), Claude Code and ChatGPT Codex already keep on your machine, attributes every request to the repository you were working in, prices it using the providers' model rates, and shows it all in a live dashboard tool window.

Features

  • Cost per repository — every request attributed to its repo via the git remote.
  • All your AI tools in one ledger — VS Code Copilot Chat, GitHub Copilot CLI, Claude Code and ChatGPT Codex, with a per-provider spend split.
  • Token anatomy & effective $/1M — input, output, cache read and cache write tokens per model, and the blended price actually paid.
  • Dashboard — spend, today's running total, allowance gauge, end-of-month forecast and burn-rate, cost-by-repo and model charts, daily trend and an activity heatmap.
  • Project groups & per-project budgets — roll several repositories into one project; combined receipt PDF and a monthly USD budget per project.
  • Organize — rename repositories, hide noise repos, filter, sort and star; built for 100+ repositories.
  • Receipt PDF export — per repository, per project, or one summary receipt for the whole period.
  • Summary exports — copy the month as a Markdown table or export a pivot-ready per-repository CSV.
  • Budgets & alerts — plan allowance, AI-credit thresholds, monthly budget and runaway-session warnings.
  • Display currency — show amounts in your currency with a manual exchange rate; status bar can show spend, today or credits remaining.

Privacy: everything happens on your machine — no network requests, no telemetry.

Independent open-source project, not affiliated with GitHub, Microsoft, Anthropic or OpenAI.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.22.5 - Compatibility fix

  • Fixed: the dashboard failed to open on IntelliJ 2026.2 - 2026.2 moved JCEF out of the core platform into a separate bundled plugin, so the panel could no longer resolve JBCefApp and threw NoClassDefFoundError. The plugin now declares the JCEF module, and a missing embedded browser degrades to the existing fallback message instead of failing
  • 1.22.4 — Fixes under-counted spend. Claude Code subagent and workflow turns are now counted: they are written to <sessionId>/subagents/… rather than the flat project directory, so a scan that only looked one level deep missed the majority of real usage on agent-heavy months. Claude Opus 5 and Sonnet 5 now have prices instead of falling through to the generic fallback rate, which billed Opus 5 at $2/$10 per 1M instead of $5/$25. GPT-5.6 rates refreshed: Luna dropped to $0.20/$1.20, Sol and Terra gained cache-write and long-context tiers. Added Gemini 3.6/3.7 Flash, Grok 4.5/4.6, Kimi K2.7 Code, Kimi K3 and MAI-Code-1.1-Flash.
  • 1.22.3 — Parity with the VS Code edition 1.22.3: ChatGPT Codex as a new data source; VS Code ≥ 1.128 chat-session logs (.jsonl) with exact token counts; rename & hide repositories (with a manage view); today's spend & tokens on the dashboard and in the status bar; status-bar modes (spend / remaining / today) with a 7-day sparkline; display currency with a manual rate; summary receipt for the whole period; Copy Summary as Markdown and Export Summary CSV actions; per-project budgets and runaway-session alerts; Add Storage Root from the empty state; GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna pricing; remote (SSH/dev-container/WSL) workspaces named correctly.
  • 1.13.3 — Full parity with the VS Code edition: export usage as CSV/JSON, AI-credit and monthly-budget alert notifications, a localized dashboard (Czech, German, Japanese), and settings for budget, credit thresholds and extra storage roots.
  • 1.0.0 — Initial release: dashboard, per-repository cost tracking across Copilot Chat, Copilot CLI and Claude Code, project groups, receipts, budgets and the activity heatmap.

idea-plugin.name: Caddyfile Pro
idea-plugin.description:
Stop editing your Caddy config blind. Caddyfile Pro turns any JetBrains IDE into a first-class Caddyfile editor — completion, documentation, validation, and formatting that actually understand Caddy.

Completion that knows Caddy. All standard directives, their subdirectives (reverse_proxy alone has 40+), matcher types, and every global option — generated directly from the official Caddy documentation.

Documentation inline. Every directive carries its syntax and summary, with a one-click link to the official docs page.

Environment variables just work. {$UPSTREAM}, {env.DEPLOY_ENV}, {http.request.uri} — placeholders are first-class syntax, not errors. Your parametrized configs highlight and complete correctly.

Works in IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PhpStorm, GoLand, PyCharm, RustRover, CLion, and every other IntelliJ-platform IDE (2024.2+). 30-day free trial; the annual subscription includes a perpetual fallback license.

Caddy is a trademark of its respective owners. This plugin is an independent product and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Caddy project.

idea-plugin.name: App Monitor
idea-plugin.description:
App Monitor turns the IDE into a live runtime dashboard for the apps you care about - independent of how they were started (IDE run config, terminal, docker, system service). Add an app by name + port and the panel shows its memory, CPU, listening ports, uptime and up/down status, refreshing automatically like docker stats.

Unlike a launcher, App Monitor tracks targets (a TCP port, a process name, a PID), not the process the IDE launched - so it can watch anything running on your machine. If an app is not found on a refresh it shows down, and flips back to up when it reappears.

MVP features:

  • Tool window with a live table: Name, Port(s), PID, Uptime, Status, Memory, Mem %, CPU %.
  • Add an app by port (optional: process-name / PID target, health URL, alert limits, tag).
  • Kill the process listening on a port (and its whole tree) - goodbye EADDRINUSE.
  • The list of monitored apps is persisted per project.
  • Works on Linux, macOS and Windows.

Spun off from the Multiple Run Monitor (part of the Multiple Run plugin).
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.13.1 (internal):

  • Internal: the plugin is now 100% Kotlin - the last Java class (the process/port sampler) was converted, with no change in behaviour.

0.13.0 (action rules):

  • New: automated action rules per app. Tick Restart when it goes down to auto-run the app's start command whenever it crashes, and set an if memory ≥ N MB held for M minutes → notify / kill / restart rule. Rules are edge-triggered (fire once, re-arm on recovery) and each firing is logged in the Events tab.

0.12.0 (per-app dashboard: events):

  • New: the memory dialog gained an Events tab - a per-app timeline of started / stopped / restarted, healthy / unhealthy and memory / CPU / leak alerts, each timestamped. Events are recorded even when notifications are turned off.

0.11.0 (persistent history):

  • New: each app's memory session is saved to disk, so the chart and leak analysis survive IDE restarts. When the process restarts, the finished session is kept as the previous one and the memory chart draws it dashed underneath the current one, with a peak comparison - so you can tell if this run is heavier than the last.

0.10.0 (multiple targets per app):

  • New: an app can now aggregate several targets in one row. Add Extra ports (comma-separated) in the Add/Edit dialog to fold an app that listens on more than one port - or a process-name target plus a port - into a single measurement (memory, CPU and ports are summed over the union of the process trees).

0.9.0 (env viewer):

  • New: Env Viewer - for an app with a .env file configured, a toolbar button shows its variables in a read-only table. Secret-looking values (password / token / key / …) are masked by default, with a Show values toggle to reveal them.

0.8.0 (docker-aware):

  • New: monitor a docker container as a target. Add an app with the Docker container target and its CPU, memory, published ports, uptime and up/down come from docker stats / docker inspect - the memory chart and leak analysis work the same as for a process.

0.7.0 (settings page):

  • New: Settings → Tools → App Monitor - set the refresh interval and toggle alert notifications. Applies without restarting the IDE.

0.6.0 (start / stop / restart):

  • New: give an app a start command (and optional stop command, working directory and .env file) and Start / Stop / Restart it from the toolbar - App Monitor becomes a small process manager for apps it did not launch. Stop falls back to killing the tree when no stop command is set.

0.5.0 (tags & filter):

  • New: give each app a tag and a colour - a new Tag column shows it in that colour, so backend/frontend/infra apps are easy to tell apart.
  • New: a filter field in the toolbar narrows the table by name, tag or port.

0.4.0 (discovery & status bar):

  • New: auto-discovery - a toolbar button scans the machine's listening TCP ports and lists the ones you are not monitoring yet (with the owning command), so you can add several at once, each with an editable name.
  • New: status-bar widget - "App Monitor: ▲up ▼down" with the total memory in the tooltip; click it to open the tool window. Toggle it from the status-bar widgets menu.

0.3.0 (alerts, process breakdown, column chooser):

  • New: alerts & notifications - a balloon fires when an app goes down, its memory or CPU crosses the alert you set, or a steady memory leak is detected. Each fires once and re-arms when the app recovers.
  • New: per-process breakdown - the memory chart has a Processes tab listing every PID of the app's tree with its command, memory and share of the tree.
  • New: show/hide columns from the toolbar, persisted per project.

0.2.0 (rich memory observability):

  • New: Mem trend sparkline per app (last minute of memory), red when climbing, green when flat/falling. Click it for the full chart.
  • New: full-session memory chart with labelled axes and the peak marked, a leak analysis (growth rate, per-hour projection, R², how often memory was never freed) and a verdict; export the history to CSV or the analysis to a report.
  • New: HTTP health check - set a health URL and the Status column refines to healthy/unhealthy (2xx/3xx = healthy), on top of up/down.

0.1.0 (MVP):

  • New: "App Monitor" tool window - add an app by port and watch its memory, CPU, ports, uptime and up/down status live, whatever launched it.
  • New: kill the process listening on a TCP port (whole process tree).
  • The monitored apps list is persisted per project. Linux, macOS and Windows.

idea-plugin.name: Lanes
idea-plugin.description:
Thank you so much for your support!

This project is built and maintained with dedication in my own time. Your contribution helps cover maintenance costs and allows me to continue creating free tools, improving existing ones, and building new projects for the community.

Every contribution, no matter the size, makes a real difference. Thank you for being part of this journey! 🎉 ❤️

☕ Buy me a coffee

Run, monitor and manage multiple run configurations at once. Group your apps, servers, microservices or tests and start them with a single click - one by one with "ready when" (port / HTTP / log) checks when you need startup ordering. Then watch everything live in a docker-stats-style monitor: memory, CPU, listening ports, uptime and health, with memory-leak analysis, per-process memory charts and aggregated logs.

Manage environments without leaving the IDE: load .env environment files per app or group, switch between environment profiles on the fly, and import a docker-compose file to create run configurations. Not only application and test configurations can be grouped - other Lanes configurations can be nested into a single one.

Fork of the Multirun plugin by Ruslan Khmeliuk. It replaces the original plugin (uninstall Multirun before installing this one).

Use cases:

  • Start batch of tests for multiple modules or applications
  • Start multiple applications, like multiple servers or backend + web application

Usage:

  1. Run -> Edit Configurations...
  2. Find and add a new Lanes configuration
  3. Add other run configurations to the Lanes configuration
  4. Pick options you'd like
  5. Ready to use

Lanes + Before Launch Tasks gives even more functionality: read more at https://github.com/PixelC0d3/lanes/wiki
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.14:

  • The monitor, the status bar widget and the memory/CPU watcher no longer scan the machine's process table separately - they share one scan when their schedules coincide (measured ~600 ms down to ~95 ms for that moment). Force Kill and the memory chart still take a fresh scan.
  • Fixes columns you un-hid coming back hidden the next time the monitor opened.

1.0.13:

  • The Lanes Monitor now works like docker ps -a: an application that exits stays in the list as history instead of disappearing, greyed out and frozen at the last values it had (PID, ports, memory, CPU). Restart brings it back with one click. Running applications stay at the top of the list.
  • The Status column says "stopped" when you stop or kill an application and "paused" while monitoring is paused; a real failure still shows its exit code. Starting an app on the port of a stopped one replaces that history row, and Pause/Resume Monitoring are disabled for applications that are not running.
  • Running applications are marked with the same green dot the IDE puts on its Run button, so running and stopped rows are told apart at a glance.
  • New "Remove from List" action for stopped applications (toolbar and right-click): drops them from the monitor and forgets their history. Running apps stay - use Pause Monitoring to take one out of sampling.

1.0.12:

  • Fixes an internal error (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException) reported when stopping several applications at once: the platform fires their termination callbacks on several threads and removing the registry entries was not atomic. The apps did stop correctly, but the IDE reported an error afterwards.

1.0.11:

  • Much cheaper monitoring. Sampling no longer walks the machine's whole process table once per application (that scan costs ~94 ms with ~640 processes running, and each of the three sampling loops did it per app); a single scan now resolves every process tree, so a refresh with 10 apps went from ~600 ms to ~130 ms of tree walking and no longer grows with the number of apps.
  • The listening-ports lookup now runs lsof with -b -w, skipping the calls that block on every mounted file system - 889 ms to 190 ms on a Docker host, same ports reported. The status bar widget also stopped resolving each app's process tree twice per tick (it runs even with the monitor closed).

1.0.10:

  • Maintenance release - no functional changes since 1.0.9 (which never reached the Marketplace because of a description formatting issue, now fixed).

1.0.9:

  • The "Environment file (profile)" field on native run configurations is now offered only on Node.js and npm/pnpm/yarn - the types where the IDE actually applies it at launch. On Mocha/Karma/Jest the IDE never invokes plugin launch extensions, so the field silently did nothing there; it is hidden instead of pretending. For test runners, use the native Environment variables field or run them through a Lanes group (group env injection works for every type). The pre-Play env combo follows the same rule.

1.0.8:

  • Lanes Monitor: an app started standalone with the IDE's own Play/Debug no longer borrows a Lanes group's name/env just because a same-named app exists in a group. The Lanes column shows "-" and the Env column shows what the run actually loaded (matched by the real process, not by name).

1.0.7:

  • Lanes Monitor: apps launched through a nested Lanes group now show the top-level group you actually started (and its env profile) in the Lanes/Env columns, instead of the inner group's name. Display-only fix; restart/switch of a single app is unchanged.

1.0.6:

  • The Lanes Monitor can pause monitoring for selected apps (Pause/Resume Monitoring): the app keeps running but is no longer sampled (no memory/CPU polling), so heavy apps can be excluded on demand. Paused rows stay in the table, greyed and frozen at their last values.

1.0.5:

  • Clearer crash message when a Memory limit's NODE_OPTIONS injection conflicts with the app's own start script reassigning NODE_OPTIONS (a real Node/bash interaction) - explains the likely cause instead of just the exit code.

1.0.4:

  • The .env picker now renders like a combo box, matching the run configuration selector next to it (icon, active profile name, dropdown arrow) - picking a profile updates the name shown right there, no separate popup.

1.0.3:

  • Fixes 1.0.2 (which never actually rendered): a toolbar button next to the run configuration selector now lets you pick which .env profile the selected Lanes group or native Node run configuration runs with next, once it has 2 or more saved profiles - no modal, persists as the active profile.

1.0.1:

  • Internal: the project moved to the PixelC0d3 GitHub organization. The plugin id is now io.github.pixelcodes.lanes and the Kotlin package moved accordingly.
  • No functional change; Welington Monteiro remains the plugin's maintainer/vendor.

1.0: Initial release

Grouping

  • Group any number of run configurations into a single Lanes configuration and start them with one click.
  • Nesting / composite configurations: a Lanes configuration can contain other Lanes configurations, so you can build a "master" configuration that starts several groups at once - with loop protection (detects and prevents cycles).

Execution modes

  • Parallel or one by one (the next configuration starts only after the previous one has started - useful when "Before launch" tasks would otherwise collide).
  • Enable/disable per application - an On checkbox per row; unchecked apps stay in the list (keeping their settings) but are not launched.
  • Ready when (docker-compose-style depends_on): with one-by-one, the next application only starts once the previous one is actually ready - port:3003, an http(s) health URL (2xx/3xx), or log:some text (console output contains it). Capped at 2 minutes, then the chain continues anyway. Also feeds the monitor's Status column (healthy/down, re-checked every refresh).
  • Delay between configurations (one-by-one only): 0 starts immediately, a positive value waits up to N seconds (with a countdown), a negative value waits for the previous process to complete first (serial execution). Locale-aware (accepts "," or "." as the decimal separator).

Environment variables & .env files

  • Define environment variables directly on the Lanes configuration - applied to every child configuration, overriding same-named variables, and propagating through nested Lanes configurations too.
  • Environment file with profiles: point the Environment file field at one or more .env files (multi-select browse) and switch between them from a dropdown - no retyping paths. Re-read on every run; the configuration's own Environment variables field still wins on conflicts.
  • Per-application env file override: an Env file (app) column lets a single app use its own .env file instead of the group's.
  • Native Play/Debug support: the same .env-profile loading is available directly on Node.js and npm/pnpm/yarn run configurations - not just inside a Lanes group. A switch button on the run toolbar restarts that same run with the chosen profile. Optional module: only active in IDEs with the JavaScript plugin; uninstalling the plugin removes it cleanly.
  • Works with any configuration type that exposes environment variables (Node.js, npm, Java Application, ...); other types run unchanged.

Execution presets

  • Save the current On/Off selection of applications plus the active environment profile as a named preset, and switch between scenarios ("backend only", "full stack", ...) from a dropdown - no more re-checking boxes by hand.

Import from docker-compose.yml

  • Reads a compose file and applies it to run configurations already in the list whose name matches a service: mem_limit (and deploy.resources.limits.memory) becomes the Memory limit, env_file becomes an environment profile, depends_on reorders the list and adds a port:<published> Ready when gate. Services without a matching configuration are reported and skipped - it never creates one.

Per-application memory limit

  • An editable Memory limit (MB) column applies a heap cap at launch (NODE_OPTIONS --max-old-space-size for Node.js, JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS -Xmx for the JVM) - the process-level analog of Docker's mem_limit.

Lanes Monitor (docker-stats-style process table)

  • Lists every process the IDE is running - apps started by Lanes and standalone (singleton) runs - with PID, ports, uptime, status, memory usage/limit, memory %, memory trend and CPU %. Each application is measured as its whole process tree, refreshed automatically every 2 seconds. A distinct "configured" icon marks every saved Lanes instance everywhere the platform shows it.
  • Env column shows the active profile - click to view the variables actually loaded (with a name filter and a mask-values toggle for screen sharing) - for grouped apps and standalone runs alike.
  • Ports are clickable (opens the URL in the browser); Kill Process on Port... stops whatever is listening on a port, even processes the plugin didn't start.
  • Mem trend sparkline (color-coded by proximity to the limit) opens a full-session memory chart with labeled axes, CSV export, and a leak-analysis tab (growth rate, projected growth/hour, R², a per-process breakdown, and a text export).
  • Restart / Stop / Force Kill per row or in batch (multi-select survives the automatic refresh); Restart All and Restart Unhealthy toolbar actions; Switch Environment per-row or group-wide, preserving each app's executor.
  • Show/Hide columns picker; Aggregated Logs tab merges every running app's console into one color-coded stream, with an app selector, composable filters (substring/regex, show/hide, case-sensitive, minimum log level) and an ANSI toggle.
  • Shows a branded empty-state illustration when nothing is running.
  • Windows support via PowerShell Get-Process for memory/CPU (Ports and Kill-by-Port need lsof, Linux/macOS only).

Status bar widget

  • A compact indicator shows how many applications Lanes is running, their combined memory and how many are unhealthy. Click it to open the Lanes Monitor; it hides itself when nothing is running.

Restart policies & alerts (docker style)

  • Restart application on crash - relaunches an app that exits with a crash code (max 3 attempts per run); intentional stops never trigger it.
  • Crash notification with Restart - a one-click Restart button when crash-restart is off or exhausted.
  • Unhealthy alert - an app whose readiness condition stays down for 3 consecutive checks is reported unhealthy with a Restart button; re-arms on recovery.
  • Sustained CPU alert - a configurable CPU % threshold held for 3 consecutive checks raises a notification with Restart.
  • Memory limit alert - configurable threshold (default 90%) with a Notify or Restart application action, docker-like OOM handling.

Console tab handling

  • Mark the tab of a failed configuration; optionally close tabs of successfully completed ones; reuse tabs for succeeded and/or failed runs.
  • Save console logs to folder - writes each configuration's output as a log file via the IDE's standard mechanism.

Restarting and stopping

  • Restart on rerun (default on) - running a Lanes configuration that's already running stops its own processes first, then starts again; other running Lanes groups are untouched. Can be disabled per configuration.
  • Stop Lanes action stops everything the plugin started, available from Run -> Stop Lanes and via Shift+Alt+K (macOS: Control+Alt+K).

Supported executors

  • Run, Debug, Run with Coverage, Profiler, and JRebel (Run and Debug).

Copy Text Anywhere（复制文本到任意位置）是一款 IntelliJ IDEA 插件，

idea-plugin.name: GfhApiMate
idea-plugin.description:
GfhApiMate

GfhApiMate is an IntelliJ IDEA plugin for Spring Boot developers that keeps API testing, debugging, asset management, and documentation generation inside the IDE.

Highlights

  • Fast API launch from code - Click the gutter icon on any Spring endpoint to restore request data into the HTTP panel and send it without leaving IDEA.
  • Lightweight HTTP tab - Enter a full URL directly, edit query params, headers, auth, body, multipart files, repeat send, generate cURL, compare responses, and cancel in-flight requests.
  • Clear error feedback - Network failures such as connection refused, timeout, DNS failure, SSL failure, and protocol errors are shown with concrete details instead of a generic error.
  • Request history upgrade - Rich two-line history cards with status, duration, size, search, favorites, groups, and right-click actions for reopen, resend, inspect, copy, and export.
  • Request assets - Save reusable requests with name, group, tags, description, source method info, import/export JSON, and reopen them anytime.
  • API discovery center - Scan Spring controllers across the project, browse endpoints by controller, and filter by module or package path before opening them into the request panel.
  • WebSocket client - Connect, send, receive, and inspect real-time messages with custom handshake headers.
  • Call chain visualization - Explore Controller to Service to Mapper or Repository invocation paths with timing-oriented analysis and optimization hints.
  • Markdown API docs - Generate endpoint or controller documentation with recursive response type parsing and export docs directly from the plugin.
  • Built-in utilities - JSON formatter, regex tester, cron expression generator, and a small stress-relief mini game are included in the tool window.

Tool Window Tabs

  • HTTP Request - Compose and send HTTP requests with a minimal direct-URL flow.
  • Call Chain - Inspect method invocation trees and related optimization suggestions.
  • WebSocket - Test WebSocket endpoints in real time.
  • History - Search and manage request history with quick actions.
  • Assets - Manage reusable request assets and import or export them.
  • Discovery - Discover project APIs and filter by module or package.
  • JSON Tool - Format, validate, and inspect JSON.
  • Regex Tool - Test patterns and review match results.
  • Cron - Generate cron expressions and preview execution times.
  • Game - A simple interactive stress-relief panel.

GfhApiMate 中文介绍

GfhApiMate 是一款面向 Spring Boot 开发者的 IntelliJ IDEA 插件，把接口调试、请求资产管理、接口发现和文档生成都放回 IDE 里完成。

核心亮点

  • 从源码一键发起接口调试 - 点击任意 Spring 接口左侧图标，即可把请求信息恢复到 HTTP 面板中继续调试。
  • 极简类 请求页 - 直接输入完整 URL，编辑 Query、Header、鉴权、Body、文件上传，支持重复发送、cURL 生成、响应对比和请求取消。
  • 具体错误直接可见 - 连接失败、超时、主机解析失败、SSL 失败、协议异常等都会展示具体原因，不再只有笼统报错。
  • 历史记录全面升级 - 双行卡片展示状态码、耗时、大小，支持搜索、收藏、分组以及右键恢复、重发、查看详情、复制、导出等快捷操作。
  • 请求资产化 - 可将请求保存为资产，支持当前工作资产联动、按分组管理、来源方法信息，以及 JSON 导入导出。
  • 接口发现中心 - 扫描项目内 Spring Controller，按控制器浏览接口，并支持按模块或包路径筛选后打开到请求页。
  • WebSocket 调试 - 支持实时连接、收发消息和自定义握手 Header。
  • 调用链路可视化 - 查看 Controller 到 Service 再到 Mapper 或 Repository 的调用路径，并给出性能分析和优化建议。
  • Markdown 文档生成 - 支持接口级和 Controller 级文档导出，并递归解析响应类型结构。
  • 内置效率工具 - 提供 JSON 工具、正则工具、Cron 表达式生成器，以及一个轻量解压小游戏。

工具窗口标签页

  • HTTP 请求 - 用最短路径构建并发送 HTTP 请求。
  • 调用链路 - 查看方法调用树和优化建议。
  • WebSocket - 实时调试 WebSocket 接口。
  • 历史记录 - 搜索和管理历史请求，支持快捷操作。
  • 资产中心 - 管理可复用请求资产，支持与请求页选择、加载、保存、重命名、删除联动，以及导入导出。
  • 接口发现 - 浏览项目接口，并按模块或包路径筛选。
  • JSON 工具 - 格式化、校验和查看 JSON。
  • 正则工具 - 测试正则并查看匹配结果。
  • Cron - 生成 Cron 表达式并预览执行时间。
  • 解压小游戏 - 一个简单的交互式解压面板。

0.1.2:

idea-plugin.name: SQL Agent
idea-plugin.description:
Manage Microsoft SQL Server Agent from your IDE: jobs, steps, schedules, alerts, operators and proxies — reusing the data sources you already have, including SSH tunnels, SSL and saved credentials.

Adds a SQL Agent tool window for any Microsoft SQL Server connection, plus a SQL Server Agent entry in the Database Explorer context menu.

  • Job activity — status, last outcome, duration and next run, with failures sorted to the top and multi-server (MSX/TSX) targets aggregated.
  • Run and toggle jobs — start, stop, enable and disable, with a confirmation that names the server. Blocked when the data source is marked read-only in the IDE.
  • Schedules in plain language — freq_type=8, freq_interval=18 reads as "Monday and Thursday, at 03:00".
  • Run history with per-step drill-down and the full error message, with an explicit row limit and the total count.
  • T-SQL generation for jobs, alerts and operators, opened in an editor already bound to the source connection. The plugin never applies schema changes itself.
  • Compare a job across servers side by side, highlighting divergences.
  • Search every server at once — which job calls this stored procedure, where is this operator, who uses this proxy.
  • Configuration checks the built-in tools do not surface: steps that report success on failure, jobs that notify nobody, operators disabled but still referenced, proxies with no subsystem granted.

Requires permission on msdb (SQLAgentReaderRole or higher). Azure SQL Database has no SQL Server Agent and is detected and reported.

If you liked the plugin and are able to help someone in need, I’ve included a link to a fundraiser to help a member of the database community.
https://www.vakinha.com.br/vaquinha/vaquinha-do-aislan
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.0

  • First release: job activity, run control, step and schedule detail, run history, T-SQL generation, cross-server comparison and global search.

idea-plugin.name: Codex App Launcher [Beta]
idea-plugin.description:
English

Codex App Launcher [Beta] connects IntelliJ IDEA with the Codex desktop app, making it easier to open projects and send precise code references without manually copying file paths or line numbers.

Platform support: Opening Codex App supports Windows and macOS. Sending code or file references currently supports Windows only; macOS reference sending is not supported yet.

  • Open the current IntelliJ IDEA project directly in Codex App from the main toolbar.
  • Send selected code with its project-relative file path and exact line range on Windows.
  • Send the selected code reference, or the current file reference when there is no selection, from the editor context menu using Send to Codex App.
  • Append references to the current Codex App input without automatically submitting the message.
  • Customize the Windows PowerShell launch command in the IDE settings.

Project paths are resolved to their real absolute locations before Codex App is launched. Project launching supports Windows and macOS. Reference insertion currently supports Windows only.

中文

Codex App Launcher [Beta] 用于连接 IntelliJ IDEA 与 Codex 桌面应用， 让开发者无需手动复制文件路径和行号，即可快速打开项目并发送准确的代码引用。

平台支持：打开 Codex App 支持 Windows 和 macOS；发送代码或文件引用目前仅支持 Windows，暂不支持 macOS 引用发送。

  • 通过 IDEA 主工具栏直接在 Codex App 中打开当前项目。
  • 在 Windows 上发送选中的代码，并自动携带项目相对路径和准确行号范围。
  • 通过编辑器右键菜单中的 Send to Codex App 发送选中的代码引用；未选中代码时发送当前文件引用。
  • 引用只会追加到 Codex App 当前输入框，不会自动提交消息。
  • 可以在 IDEA 设置中自定义 Windows PowerShell 启动命令。

插件会先将项目路径解析为真实绝对路径，再启动 Codex App。 项目启动支持 Windows 和 macOS；当前引用追加仅支持 Windows。

idea-plugin.name: Queue Studio for RabbitMQ
idea-plugin.description:
Browse RabbitMQ from your IDE: vhosts, exchanges and queues, message peek and publish, JSON payloads with highlighting, bulk requeue and move from dead-letter queues.

Moving messages out of a dead-letter queue never loses them: each one is removed from the source only after the broker confirms its copy on the target.

Peek up to 65,535 messages of a classic queue or a stream (5,000 of a quorum queue), delete or edit one in the middle of a queue, watch live traffic, read streams from any offset or time, see which policy applies and why, and trace a routing key through a graph of exchanges and bindings.

Peeking a quorum queue never counts toward its delivery-limit, so browsing does not drop messages; delete and edit, which must hold the messages ahead of the one you pick, are refused when that would push any of them past the limit.

Private clusters are reached through an SSH bastion with a key, the SSH agent or a password.

The plugin collects no data: it talks only to the brokers and SSH hosts you configure, and passwords stay in the IDE password safe.

Uses the RabbitMQ management HTTP API and AMQP 0-9-1; moves and edits use publisher confirms.

RabbitMQ is a trademark of Broadcom, Inc.; this plugin is an independent tool and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Broadcom.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.2 — corrected description: peek limits per queue type, and how delete and edit treat a quorum queue's delivery-limit. Vendor contact is support@factodus.com.

1.0.1 — new plugin icon; no deprecated or experimental platform API in use; ready for IntelliJ 2026.3.

1.0.0 — first release: connections, topology, message browser, publish, purge, safe move from dead-letter queues, delete and edit in place, live view, streams, policies, routing graph, SSH tunnel.

Views open in editor tabs, and every tree node shows its content. Queues are grouped by name prefix, system exchanges sit apart, and custom folders collect queues from several connections. Tooltips explain queue and exchange types.

idea-plugin.name: Azure Toolkit for IntelliJ
idea-plugin.description:
The plugin allows Java developers to easily develop, configure, test, and deploy highly available and scalable Java applications to Azure. The plugin supports Azure App Service, Azure Functions, Azure Spring Apps, Azure Kubernetes, Azure Container Apps, Virtual Machines, Azure Database for MySQL, Azure Cosmos DB, SQL Server, Azure Storage, and Application Insights. It also supports Azure Synapse data engineers, Azure HDInsight developers and Apache Spark on SQL Server users to create, test and submit Apache Spark/Hadoop jobs to Azure from IntelliJ on all supported platforms.

This plugin also includes Azure MCP Server that adds smart, context-aware AI tools right inside GitHub Copilot for IntelliJ IDEA to help you work more efficiently with Azure resources. The Azure MCP Server supercharges your agents with Azure context across all the popular Azure services. For more details, please refer to Azure MCP Server documentation.

  • Azure Web App Workflow: Run your web applications on Azure Web App and view logs.
  • Azure Functions Workflow: Scaffold, run, debug your Functions App locally and deploy it on Azure.
  • Azure Spring Apps Workflow: Run your Spring microservices applications on Azure Spring Apps and view logs.
  • Azure Container Apps Workflow: Dockerize and run applications on Azure Container Apps and view logs.
  • Azure Kubernetes Support: Create and manage your Kubernetes Services directly in Azure Explorer.
  • Getting Started Guide: Follow the steps in the getting started guide and deploy an application within several minutes.
  • Azure Explorer: View and manage your cloud resources on Azure with embedded Azure Explorer.
  • Azure Resource Management template: Create and update your Azure resource deployments with ARM template support.
  • Azure Synapse: List workspaces and Apache Spark Pools, compose an Apache Spark project, author and submit Apache Spark jobs to Azure Synapse Spark pools.
  • Azure HDInsight: Create an Apache Spark project, author and submit Apache Spark jobs to HDInsight cluster; Monitor and debug Apache Spark jobs easily; Support HDInsight ESP cluster MFA Authentication.
  • SQL Server Big Data Cluster: Link to SQL Server Big Data Cluster; Create an Apache Spark project, author and submit Apache Spark jobs to cluster; Monitor and debug Apache Spark jobs easily.
idea-plugin.change-notes:

  • Migrate IntelliJ Platform integrations to APIs supported by IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2

idea-plugin.name: Google Cloud Code
idea-plugin.description:
Use Google Cloud Code right from your IDE to build applications and integrate with GCP services faster and easier. Cloud Code helps you increase agility and speed to develop scalable cloud-based applications. Cloud Code automates tasks such as setting up local/remote dev environments, building containers, and deploying services, and comes packed with tools to help you write, run, and debug your applications. In addition, Cloud Code makes it easy to build secured applications to protect sensitive data.

Key Features

  • Ready-to-go dev environment - comes with pre-configured tools you need to create, build, test and debug cloud-based applications.
  • Real debugging in local or remote clusters - no more debugging via logs or having to manually set up port forwarding to debug!
  • Authentication - securely connect to Google Cloud using the gcloud command-line tool to access resources.
  • Kubernetes - deploy to clusters, browse Kubernetes resources with one-click access to monitor progress, debug, stream logs, and connect to pod terminals, among a variety of other actions.
  • Serverless with Cloud Run - browse Cloud Run services, deploy to Cloud Run, and debug using a local emulator.
  • Compute Engine - view the Compute Engine VMs running your applications, establish connections to your VMs using SSH, view application logs, and upload files to a VM.
  • Google Cloud SQL - view Cloud SQL instances, connect to a Cloud SQL database locally, and create new IDE data sources.
  • App Engine - create a new project to run and debug locally for applications in the standard environment, and to deploy projects in either the standard or flexible environment.
  • YAML editing support - use snippets, linting, smart completion, and automatic YAML validation to easily configure resources. Supports hundreds of custom resources (CRDs).
  • Cloud APIs - access most Google Cloud services with Cloud APIs for Go, Java, Python and Node.js.
  • Store application secrets securely with Secret Manager - create and securely manage secrets by storing sensitive information with Secret Manager instead of in the codebase.
  • Custom Samples - set up and share repositories of application samples, custom to your organization, to get your team started quickly.
  • Speed up development - Harness the power of Skaffold, minikube, and GKE right from the IDE! Containerize with Docker, jib, buildpacks.

Refer to Google Cloud Code documentation for more information.

Cloud Code telemetry overall is handled in accordance with the Google Privacy Policy. When you use Cloud Code to interact with or utilize GCP Services (including via Cloud SDK), your information is handled in accordance with the Google Cloud Privacy Notice

Before using this app, you can review Cloud Code’s privacy policy and terms of service.
idea-plugin.change-notes: View Cloud Code Release Notes

idea-plugin.name: Kubernetes
idea-plugin.description:
Provides advanced editor and runtime support for Kubernetes.

Features:

Cluster interaction

  • Browsing cluster objects, extracting and editing their configurations, describing them
  • Viewing events
  • Cluster-Level Kubernetes log streaming and analysis with Pattern Matching
  • Attaching pod console
  • Running shell in pod
  • Forwarding ports to pod
  • Applying resource YAML configurations from the editor
  • Deleting resources from cluster
  • Completion of ConfigMap/Secret entries from the cluster
  • Configuring path to kubectl
  • Configuring custom kubeconfig files globally and per project
  • Switching contexts and namespaces
  • Using API schema (including CRD) from the active cluster for editing resource manifests

Editing resource configurations (API 1.16 – 1.31)

Rich YAML support

  • Auto-completion of keys/values/resource kinds/API versions
  • "Deep" key auto-completion: invoke Smart Completion when you type -- matching keys from all levels below will be offered
  • Quick documentation
  • Detection of invalid/missing/duplicated keys
  • Detection of non-editable (read only) keys and resources
  • Detection of deprecated keys and resources
  • Completion/navigation/find usages/rename of Kubernetes meta-information labels
  • Completion/navigation/find usages/rename of ConfigMap/Secret entries
  • Quick jump to matching selector targets and back
  • Docker image completion (powered by JetBrains Docker plugin)
  • Enhancements for original Kubernetes model (enums instead of plain strings where applicable)

Support for editing Helm templates

  • Helm 2.x/3.x file structure/schema support
  • Go Template syntax support (powered by JetBrains Go Template plugin)
  • Object values auto-completion/navigation/rename/inspections
  • Named templates auto-completion/navigation/rename/inspections
  • Dependency name/version/repository auto-completion
  • Template result preview
  • External tgz dependencies content browsing in the project tree
  • Limited editor support for Werf (https://werf.io) templates and werf.yaml
  • Quick documentation
  • validation of values.yaml by values.schema.json (powered by JetBrains JSON plugin)
  • Useful actions: lint, update dependencies, create chart, create dependency, add repository, convert dependencies from Helm 2.x format to Helm 3.x

Editor support for Kustomize configurations (kustomization.yaml)

  • Fields completion/validation
  • Local file path completion/validation
  • Quick documentation
  • Kustomize version selection (kubectl embedded, standalone)
  • Kustomize 3.x inline patches editing support (experimental)

Custom resource definition (CRD) support

Custom resources can be validated by providing complementary OpenAPI 2.0 files with CRD schemas and/or CRD resource definitions (YAML) (limited support).
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2025.3
  • Pod status info in editor: pod statuses now shown inline right in Kubernetes YAML.
  • Active Cluster and Namespace selection available from the editor.

  • Easier port forwarding: new in-editor action to start port-forward from manifests.

  • Support for kubectl debug / ephemeral containers.
  • Enhanced remote development experience.
  • Support for Gateway API resources.
  • Support for Istio objects (Gateway, VirtualService, DestinationRule, etc.).
  • Bundled Kubernetes 1.34 schemas.
2025.2
  • Enhanced port forwarding with auto-suggested local and destination ports, as well as dynamic port availability checks, simplifying the setup process.
  • Kubernetes newest 1.33 schema supported, ensuring compatibility with the latest features.
  • Improved UX with features like a "Clear Logs" button, better secrets auto-completion, and automatically marking a cluster as the default if it's the only one added.
  • Logs tab can now handle large log sets with better performance, addressing previously significant delays on huge logs.
  • Fixed an issue where misconfigured kubectl paths were not replaced with the binary installed through Settings, ensuring smooth kubectl tool detection.
  • Made kubectl detection more stable, reducing the likelihood of connection issues.
  • Expanded cluster insights with additional pod statuses, enriched displayed pod information, and improved visualization of cluster events.
  • Enabled quick navigation from logs to sources, streamlining issue investigation and troubleshooting.
  • Fixed WSL cluster connection issues, ensuring reliable access for Windows Subsystem for Linux users.
  • Fixed bugs with live templates to ensure better stability and usability during development.
2025.1
  • Kubernetes Plugin now supports the newest Kubernetes version – 1.32, ensuring up-to-date compatibility and features.
  • Logs now load lazily, improving performance by fetching logs faster and on-demand as you scroll through them.
  • Added an option to quickly create a connection to your Kubernetes cluster when editing a Kubernetes file, streamlining the workflow.
  • Enhanced auto-refresh functionality to keep cluster objects updated without manual intervention.
  • Significantly improved the experience of working with Kubernetes files during indexing for a smoother development process.
  • Code completion in Kubernetes files now starts from the very first line, making your editing experience more intuitive.
  • Introduced a new quick fix to mark a file as non-Kubernetes, helping users better manage unrelated files in their projects.
  • Pod status updates are now more detailed and informative in the Pods list, giving you better insights into the state of your Kubernetes workloads.
  • Improved support for merging Kubernetes configuration files, simplifying configuration management.
  • Resolved several cluster connectivity issues, resulting in a more reliable plugin experience.
  • The comparison mode for Helm files was refined to enhance clarity and ease of use.
2024.3
  • Centralized log access is now available across all Pods, Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, ReplicaSets, Jobs, CronJobs and Cluster Events. Real-time log streaming supports immediate issue detection, and pattern matching facilitates automated tracking of key events, such as memory errors or unusual network activity.
  • A new Port Forwarding section has been added to the Kubernetes UI network settings, making application debugging in Kubernetes easier.
  • The Kubernetes UI now offers full control over all pod container types, enhancing management and monitoring directly in the interface. Init containers handle initial setup, while sidecar containers provide logging, monitoring, and proxying. Ambassador containers enable external service interaction, adapters standardize logs and metrics, and ephemeral containers support temporary debugging access.
  • Logs for multiple selected items can now be downloaded simultaneously, improving log management in large clusters.
  • Log filtering by levels allows users to focus on specific messages, enhancing the debugging and monitoring experience.
  • Syntax highlighting has been added to Kubernetes logs, making it easier to navigate and quickly identify relevant information.
  • Support for Kustomize 5 has been added, allowing seamless configuration management in Kubernetes. Users can now leverage Kustomize’s latest features for advanced customization of Kubernetes resources, ensuring more flexible and reusable configurations across environments.
  • The Kubernetes section in the Services Tool Window has expanded resources: 'Configuration' -> 'Secret' allows direct editing of Kubernetes secrets, while 'Network' -> 'Endpoints' and 'Network' -> 'NetworkPolicy' provide enhanced control and visibility for service endpoints and network policies, accessible directly in the UI.
  • The latest version of Kubernetes 1.31 is now supported.
  • Duplicate clusters in Services Tool Window are now handled separately to reduce confusion and simplify multi-connection management.
  • Users can now customize kubectl requests to the API, allowing more tailored Kubernetes cluster management.
2024.2
  • Support for authentication plugins has been added. Authentication is performed using the kubelogin plugin. If the plugin is required but not installed, the installation is suggested automatically. The exec section of kubeconfig is used to obtain authentication parameters.
  • Implemented Connect / Disconnect logic. By default, clusters are added to the Service View by the user in a disabled state. Clicking Connect updates the data from the kubeconfig file and enables cluster updates via the Watch API, eliminating the need to press Refresh to update items in the Service View tree for the cluster. If the user has modified the kubeconfig file, it is necessary to click Disconnect, and then Connect to apply the updated context from the file.
  • Performance has been optimized for working with large Kubernetes clusters.
  • In the user interface, "Contexts" have been renamed to "Clusters". This change was made based on user feedback for better understanding. The logic for working with Kubernetes remains unchanged.
  • Included support for Kubernetes 1.29, 1.30.
  • Updated element icons in the Kubernetes plugin. Now they are closer to the reference Kubernetes icons suggested by the developers.
2024.1
  • AutoRefresh Cluster (Watch API) in Kubernetes: Automatically refreshes the cluster information to keep the environment up to date without manual intervention.
  • Add new context from clipboard: Allows adding new Kubernetes context directly from the clipboard, simplifying the setup process for new cluster connections.
  • Suggested installation of kubectl and helm upon testing to streamline tool setup.
  • Improved context addition flow from files by not selecting all contexts by default and adding a 'select all' checkbox for convenience.
  • Addressed user experience issues when the cluster selected for deployment is deleted, improving error handling and feedback.
  • Added additional Kubernetes Resource Sets.

idea-plugin.name: Codewind
idea-plugin.description:
Codewind

Adds tools to help build cloud-native, containerized Java applications. Create an application from a template project and launch, update, test, and debug in containers on the desktop. Supports Codewind version 0.11.0. For more information, see the Codewind website.

Why use Codewind?

  • Get started with templates or samples to create and deploy applications that run in containers.
  • Create containerized applications in languages and runtimes that you're already familiar with.
  • Pull in your existing applications and use Codewind to help get them cloud ready.
  • See code changes reflected in your containerized application.

Features

  • Create new containerized projects or add existing ones.
  • View your containerized projects, including the application and build status.
  • Access application, build, and container logs in the Output view.
  • Toggle the project auto build setting and manually initiate project builds.
  • Open your application in a browser.

Getting started with Codewind

For more information, see Installing Codewind for IntelliJ.

Contributing

Submit issues and contributions:

  • Submitting issues: https://github.com/eclipse/codewind/issues.
  • Contributing: https://github.com/eclipse/codewind-intellij/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md.

Developing

To develop and debug Codewind for IntelliJ, see Developing.

idea-plugin.name: Httpx Requests
idea-plugin.description:
httpx plugin is a plugin for JetBrains IDE to execute httpx requests in HTTP file.

The following features are available for httpx plugin:

  • GraphQL: application/graphql with Language injection(GraphQL plugin required), HTTP/WebSocket transport
  • Pub/Sub for Kafka, Pulsar, RabbitMQ, NATS, Redis, MQTT3/5, AWS SNS/SQN/EventBridge, Aliyun MNS/EventBridge etc
  • Email: send email by SMTP
  • Cloud OpenAPI: AWS and Aliyun
  • Apache Thrift: TJSON support now
  • Memcache: set/get/delete
  • Redis: rset/hmset/eval, and Pub/Sub
  • SSH: execute script on remote host
  • msgpack-rpc: msgpack/Neovim RPC
  • json-rpc: HTTP and TCP protocols
  • ChatGPT support: Call OpenAI ChatGPT API by Markdown format
  • tRPC: query and mutate support
  • Live templates: graphql, kafka, email
  • JSON Schema support:
    • Content-Type: application/cloudevents+json
    • HTTP Headers: X-JSON-Schema, X-JSON-Type, X-JSON-Path

How to use?

  • GitHub GraphQL API test
### GitHub API test
GRAPHQL https://api.github.com/graphql
Authorization: token {{GITHUB_TOKEN}}
Content-Type: application/graphql

query {
    viewer { login }
}
  • Publish Apache Kafka Message
### Publish kafka message
//@name kafka-pub
PUB testTopic
Host: kafka://localhost:9092
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "Jackie"
}

For more please visit https://httpx.sh or httpx cheat sheet

idea-plugin.name: Douyin Cloud ToolKit
idea-plugin.description:
Douyin Cloud ToolKit is a plugin worked for Douyin Cloud Platform. With this tool, Developers can code, debug, test and deploy their douyin cloud project more efficiently.

插件介绍

抖音云针对Jetbrains系列的IDE平台提供了Douyin Cloud ToolKit插件(后面简称抖音云插件)，开发者通过该插件可以更高效的在本地完成应用程序的开发、调试和测试，并且可以一键将本地应用程序部署到云端，提高开发和部署的效率。

插件功能

  • 多语言支持：支持java、go、python、php的Jetbrains系列的多款IDE软件，包括IntelliJ IDEA、Goland、Pycharm 以及PhpStorm。
  • 本地打通云上VPC访问：服务本地容器启动后，通过本地容器可以访问抖音云端VPC内的数据库资源(MySQL、Redis、MongoDB等)，而无需开启对应组件的公网访问地址，保证安全。
  • 本地接口调试：开发者可以通过抖音云插件内嵌的接口调试界面完成本地接口调试，可以模拟选择小程序用户态登录。
  • 一键部署：开发者可以通过抖音云插件一键将项目工程镜像打包、上传并部署到抖音云端的Dev环境，并且可以本地查看部署日志，无需自行分开操作。
  • 前后端联调: 开发者通过抖音云插件启动本地微服务应用后，小程序开发者可以在小程序开发者工具中配置后端服务ip地址,便可以在本地模拟云上环境进行联调测试。

idea-plugin.name: CodeArts Agent
idea-plugin.description:
CodeArts Agent: Your AI-Powered Dev Sidekick

Basic Features

  • Code generation
  • R&D Q&A
  • Code commenting
  • Unit testing
  • Code explanation
  • Code optimization

Shortcuts

  • Enter: Trigger auto-generation under functions or method signatures.
  • Tab: Accept the current suggestion.
  • Esc: Dismiss the current suggestion.
  • Alt (Option)+U: Pop open the chat panel.
  • Alt (Option)+]: View the next suggestion.
  • Alt (Option)+[: View the previous suggestion.
  • Alt (Option)+X: Trigger single-line code generation.
  • Alt (Option)+C: Trigger multi-line code generation.
  • Alt (Option)+R: Regenerate code.

Slash Commands

  • /explain: Provide breakdowns for the selected code.
  • /comment: Generate method or line comments for the selected code.
  • /tests: Spawn unit tests for the selected code.
  • /optimize: Level up the selected code.
  • /clear: Flush context memory mid-session.
  • /help: Find out how CodeArts Agent can give you a boost.

Note: The ask supports all commands, the agent only supports /clear.

Function Settings

CodeArts Agent hooks into your coding muscle memory. Code as usual. Watch suggestions pop in when you need them.

Examining Default Settings

1. Click File on the menu bar of IDE, and select Settings. On the displayed page, choose CodeArts Agent.

2. Choose CodeArts Agent > Code Generation.

3. Choose CodeArts Agent > Unit Test Case Generation.

Intelligent Functions

1. Code Generation

Press Alt+C for multi-line code. For just one line, press Alt+X. Smart triggers in settings include Enter keystroke and pauses.

2. Code Explanation

Right-click on a code snippet and choose CodeArts Agent > > Explain Code. You'll get a breakdown and doc that help you speed through unfamiliar code.

3. Code Commenting

Right-click on a code snippet and choose CodeArts Agent > Generate Comment. CodeArts Agent then crafts clear, clean, and comprehensive comments that match your repo's style, giving you instant insights into code smells.

4. Unit Testing

Right-click on a code snippet and choose CodeArts Agent > Generate Unit Tests. CodeArts Agent then spins up unit test cases to hit coverage goals.

5. Code Optimization

Right-click on a code snippet and choose CodeArts Agent > Optimize Code. CodeArts Agent then analyzes the code and proposes quality-tuned rewrites.

6. R&D Q&A

Got questions about research, development, or anything in between? Just ask in the chat box.

7. Convenient Functionality Access

Press Alt+U or open the toolbar on the right. Type a slash (/) in the input box to see all available commands.

CodeArts Agent Service Statement

For details of the service statement, please click the link below: https://www.huaweicloud.com/declaration/tsa-codearts-doer.html.

华为云码道CodeArts代码智能体

基础特性

  • 代码生成
  • 研发问答
  • 代码注释
  • 单元测试
  • 代码解释
  • 代码优化

快捷键

  • Enter：在函数/方法签名下触发自动生成
  • Tab：接受当前生成结果
  • Esc：忽略当前生成结果
  • Alt(Option)+U：打开问答对话框
  • Alt(Option)+]：查看下一个推荐
  • Alt(Option)+[：查看上一个推荐
  • Alt(Option)+X：主动触发单行代码生成
  • Alt(Option)+C：主动触发多行代码生成
  • Alt(Option)+R：重新生成代码

快捷指令

  • /explain: 解释选中的代码
  • /comment: 为选中的代码生成方法注释或行间注释
  • /tests: 为选中的代码生成单元测试
  • /optimize：优化选中的代码
  • /clear: 当你在会话中时，清空上下文记忆
  • /help: 学习如何使用华为云码道CodeArts代码智能体

注：智能问答支持全部指令，智能体仅支持/clear

功能、设置

小伙伴们无需改变日常的开发习惯，只需要正常敲击键盘进行编程， 华为云码道CodeArts代码智能体 智能编码助手将在合适时候主动生成代码给予协助。

华为云码道CodeArts代码智能体 默认设置

1.点击 IDE 菜单栏中 "File" --> "Settings" 打开设置面板，选中 华为云码道CodeArts代码智能体。

2.展开 华为云码道CodeArts代码智能体 --> "代码生成"，可以看到默认设置功能键。

3.展开 华为云码道CodeArts代码智能体 --> "单元测试用例生成"，可以看到默认设置功能键。

功能介绍

1. 代码生成

在任意位置使用Alt + C快捷键可以触发代码生成；在设置里可打开"回车触发"以及"停顿触发"使用其他功能触发方式。同时也支持代码单行生成，快捷键为Alt + X。

2. 代码解释

选中合适的代码片段，点击右键在华为云码道CodeArts代码智能体下选中"代码解释"功能，快速分析代码并自动生成文档，提高阅读代码的速度和效率。

3. 代码注释

选中合适的代码片段，点击右键在华为云码道CodeArts代码智能体下选中"代码注释"功能，快速分析代码，自动生成有意义的完整注释，增加代码可读性，同一个代码库注释风格的一致性，提高研发问题的解决效率。

4. 单元测试

选中合适的代码片段，点击右键在华为云码道CodeArts代码智能体下选中"单元测试"功能，能够自动创建单元测试用例，提高测试覆盖率，确保每个功能和场景都被测试到。

5. 代码优化

选择需要优化的代码，点击右键在华为云码道CodeArts代码智能体下选中代码优化功能，对代码进行检查，并提供优化建议，提升代码质量。

6. 研发知识问答

在交互框中进行研发相关提问，提高研发问题的解决效率。

7. 快捷功能

使用热键Alt + U或打开右边工具栏，点击输入框内敲下"/"可看到快捷功能使用选择。

华为云码道CodeArts代码智能体服务声明

服务声明详情请点击链接查阅：https://www.huaweicloud.com/declaration/tsa-codearts-doer.html。
idea-plugin.change-notes:
v26.9.500

  1. UT Agent now supports more languages, including Python, C, C++, Go, TypeScript, and JavaScript, covering a broader range of enterprise tech stacks.
  2. Added Skill auto-evolution: the AI reviews and refines its approach after each completed task, continuously improving its adaptation to your personal habits.
  3. Introduced Agent startup tool self-checks and a three-level dynamic loading mechanism (resident/deferred/retrieval) to reduce misinvocations and save context.
  4. Enhanced the code agent's self-Q&A capability, automatically invoking documentation Skills to provide operational guidance.
  5. Upgraded the multimodal model from Qwen3-VL to Kimi K2.6, improving stability and complex visual reasoning.
  6. Added support for reading image content to assist UI design, optimizing the image recognition experience in the console.
  7. CodeArts CLI now supports CodebaseWiki.
  8. Added a feedback entry to CodeArts CLI: report violations or issues via the /report-center command.
  9. Now supports purchasing multi-month or annual plans at subscription, while credits are still issued monthly.
  10. Enables viewing per-turn credit consumption details in the console for fine-grained cost analysis and optimization.
  1. UT Agent多语言支持扩展至Python、C、C++、Go、TypeScript、JavaScript等，覆盖更多企业技术栈。
  2. 新增 Skill 自动进化，AI 每完成一次任务即自我复盘优化，持续提升对个人习惯的适配度。
  3. 引入Agent启动工具自检与三级动态加载机制（常驻/延迟/检索），降低误调用、节约上下文。
  4. 增强代码智能体资料自问自答能力，自动调用文档skill返回操作指导。
  5. 多模态模型由千问Qwen3-VL切换至Kimi K2.6，提升稳定性与复杂视觉推理能力。
  6. 支持读取图片内容辅助UI设计，优化控制台图片识别体验。
  7. 码道CLI新增CodebaseWiki。
  8. 码道CLI新增反馈入口，可通过命令/report-center上报违规内容，反馈问题。
  9. 支持开通套餐时购买多个月或1年的套餐，但积分仍按月发放。
  10. 支持控制台逐轮查看积分消耗明细，助力精细化成本分析与调优。

v26.9.100

  1. Supports embedded Wiki documentation with one-click generation, incremental updates, and code synchronization, serving both human reading and Agent memory scenarios.
  2. CodeArts VS Code/JetBrains plugins now support macOS.
  3. Experience/Performance Optimization
    • Optimized tool call display with simplified process presentation.
    • Scheduled tasks can be bound to Feishu (Lark) messages;
    • Support exporting and sending back session prompts and complete conversations;
    • CodeArts plugin adapted to PyCharm 2026.2;
    • Differentiated highlighting in billing documentation;
  1. 支持一键生成、增量更新、代码同步的嵌入式Wiki文档，兼顾人类阅读与Agent记忆双场景。
  2. 码道VS Code/Jetbrains插件支持MacOS系统
  3. 体验/性能优化
    • 优化工具调用展示，简化过程呈现。
    • 定时任务绑定飞书消息；
    • 支持Session提示词与完整会话导出回传；
    • 码道插件适配PyCharm 2026.2；
    • 计费文档差异化高亮；

v26.8.300

New Project-Level Cross-Session Memory Capability

  • Supports recording identity preferences, project milestones, collaboration feedback, and external reference clues. Even a brand-new conversation can carry forward the core project context, with no need to repeat information over and over.

New Enterprise Knowledge Management with Automatic Experience Accumulation

  • Automatically extracts personal experience from daily coding, bug fixing, and code reviews to build an exclusive knowledge base.
  • Automatically identifies high-frequency bug patterns, key technical decisions, and best practices within projects, accumulating them into a project-level experience library.
  • Automatically triggers a daily work reflection mechanism to discover and accumulate new experiences, and periodically generates experience summaries and reuse reports.

New Session Token Details

  • Displays in real time the input tokens, output tokens, cache-hit token count, and cache-hit ratio of the current session.
  • The console supports viewing token consumption details round by round, enabling refined cost analysis and tuning.

Subscription and Billing System Upgrade: Switching from the Token Mechanism to the Credits Mechanism

  • Supports both personal and enterprise subscriptions, with newly added Credits resource package purchases, delivering a more flexible billing model that adapts to the needs of teams of all sizes.

No Limit on the Number of Multimodal Image Uploads

  • Multimodal input capability upgraded: the image upload count limit has been removed, allowing multiple images to be passed in at once.

Experience/Performance Optimization

  • Optimized the performance of the HarmonyOS-exclusive agent, delivering faster responses for code-related tasks.
  • When adding file/folder type context, you can click a file to jump directly to its directory with one click.
  • When creating a new custom agent, you can freely specify the base model.
  • During one-click prompt optimization, you can cancel the ongoing optimization task at any time.
  • Added model thinking intensity adjustment capability, allowing you to balance AI reasoning depth and response speed as needed.

新增项目级跨会话记忆能力

  • 支持记录身份偏好、项目里程碑、协作反馈和外部参考线索，新开对话也能延续核心项目上下文，无需反复重复信息。

新增企业知识管理，支持经验自动沉淀

  • 自动提取日常编码、Bug 修复与代码评审中的个人经验，构建专属知识库。
  • 自动识别项目内高频 Bug 模式、关键技术决策与最佳实践，沉淀为项目级经验库。
  • 每日自动触发工作反思机制，发现并沉淀新经验，定期生成经验总结与复用报告。

新增会话 Token 明细

  • 实时展示当前会话的输入 Token、输出 Token、缓存命中 Token 数及缓存命中占比。
  • 控制台支持逐轮查看 Token 消耗明细，助力精细化成本分析与调优。

订阅与计费体系升级：Token 机制切换为 Credits 机制

  • 支持个人订阅与企业订阅，新增 Credits 资源包购买，计费模式更灵活，适配不同规模团队需求。

支持多模态图片上传数量无上限

  • 多模态输入能力升级，移除图片上传数量限制，支持一次性传入多张图片。

体验/性能优化

  • 优化鸿蒙专属智能体性能，代码相关任务处理响应更迅速。

v26.6.0

CodeArts Agent version 630 release: Cloud CodeBase multi-endpoint collaboration, enhanced expert agent capabilities, and upgraded interaction experience and security

Incremental development for existing projects

  • Cloud CodeBase multi-endpoint support for more precise large-repo development
    IDE client, VSCode extension, and CLI/TUI tools now connect to Cloud CodeBase. Supports indexing and retrieval for repositories with tens of millions of lines of code, enabling cloud-local collaborative code understanding. With CodeBase enabled, code generation accuracy improves significantly, and token consumption decreases substantially for equivalent tasks — making AI-assisted development in large incremental development scenarios more precise and efficient.
  • Local LSP deep integration for more accurate code understanding
    New local LSP capability supports Java, TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, and other mainstream languages. When enabled, the agent leverages language service diagnostics, navigation, and symbol information for more precise code understanding and modification — significantly improving the accuracy of code completion, navigation, and refactoring.
  • Expert Skill marketplace expanded, covering mainstream development scenarios
    The Skill marketplace now offers a rich collection of expert Skills across multiple domain categories: unit testing, code review, document generation, security inspection, build, and code refactoring. Each Skill passes automated testing and compliance review, providing developers with ready-to-use professional capabilities.
  • SDD (Spec-Driven Development) effectiveness comprehensively improved
    Optimized the SDD full pipeline (Spec → Design → Code → Test) quality, improving requirement document completeness, code generation accuracy, and unit test coverage — strengthening core competitiveness in incremental development scenarios for existing projects.

Enterprise features

  • Secure code repository isolation for enterprise data protection
    New security settings page supports code repository isolation configuration. When a repository is set as a secure isolated repository, all CodeArts AI features (IDE, VSCode extension, JetBrains extension) are blocked from accessing it — protecting enterprise core code security.
  • SSO login and IP allowlist for enhanced enterprise security compliance
    SSO single sign-on configuration based on IAM enables unified authentication for IDE and Portal access; new public IP allowlist configuration restricts access sources, improving enterprise data security and compliance.
  • Paid user queue optimization for faster peak-hour response
    Reserved dedicated queue positions for paid users, enabling immediate processing during peak hours without waiting; Basic and Professional edition users can continue with downgraded queuing after quota exhaustion, preventing service interruptions that affect development efficiency.

Interaction experience

  • Task completion sound and message notifications to never miss progress
    New task completion sound and system notifications display a prompt in the bottom-right corner when the user is focused on another window — ensuring timely awareness of agent task completion status.

Defect fixes

  • Fixed the issue where the IDE login page could not be reopened after closing the login browser window
  • Fixed compatibility issues where installation and execution were frequently blocked by enterprise security software
  • Fixed the issue where enterprise members in the CodeArts console were not synchronized after IAM user deletion
  • Fixed other known issues

idea-plugin.name: Oracle OCI Toolkit
idea-plugin.description:
Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Toolkit for IntelliJ

Overview

The Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Toolkit for IntelliJ is an open source plugin maintained by Oracle for the IntelliJ IDEA Integrated Development Environment (IDE).

The toolkit plugin supports the following OCI technologies:

  • App Stack for Java
  • DevOps Projects
  • Autonomous Databases

AppStack for Java

The App Stack for Java on OCI deploys existing Java applications using Serverless Resources, perfect for Spring Boot applications. See our example app.

With the toolkit you can control the lifecycle of your App Stack for Java:

  • Create, Apply and Delete your Stack
  • View the related Jobs
  • Browse the Terraform logs after Apply and Re-apply

DevOps

An OCI service for your CI/CD source repositories, build pipelines and deployments.

Supports DevOps features that include:

  • Mirror a github repository into an OCI DevOps project
  • View the status of your existing code repositories
  • Associate your IntelliJ project with an OCI Project

Autonomous Database

The toolkit for IntelliJ IDEA features support for creating the Autonomous Database with the following workload types:

  • Data Warehouse
  • Transaction Processing
  • JSON
  • APEX

The toolkit also features support for the following actions on the database instances:

  • Administrator Password Change
  • Clone Autonomous Database Instance
  • Download Client Credentials (Wallet)
  • Restore Instance
  • Scale Up / Down
  • Start / Stop Database Instance
  • Terminate Database Instance
  • Update License Type
  • Display Autonomous Database Instance Information

For More Information

Please visit our GitHub project. If you encounter problems or have questions that you need answered, please open an issue. You can also browse the full source for the plugin and find the most up-to-date release notes.
