idea-plugin.name: Jump to Line
idea-plugin.description:
The Jump to Line plugin allows you to get to any line of code while debugging. Drag and drop a yellow arrow to the desired place in the gutter, and it will put an execution point there. In contrast to stepping, the plugin enables you to start running your program from that point without executing the preceding code.

Jumping to lines is possible both forward and backward within a function. Jump to line highlights the lines suitable for jumps in green. Making changes to some lines may break the workflow. That’s why the IDE will highlight any risky lines in yellow. You can still move to them, but you should first consider the possible inconsistencies that may result.

idea-plugin.name: DubboTest
idea-plugin.description:
DubboTest can directly request your dubbo interface, and hope to bring you some convenience when developing and debugging.

Quick start:

1.First, you need to start the dubbo service first to expose your interface

2.Find the interface method you need to debug, right-click and select RunDubboTest, then you can see the DubboTest window pops up, and some parameters are randomly generated, you can change your input parameters. After the parameters are determined, click the run button.

The address input box can choose the following two types.

use zookeeper: zookeeper://127.0.0.1:2181

use dubbo: dubbo://127.0.0.1:2288

tips:

1.The methodType field needs to correspond to the input parameter type of your interface, and generally does not need to be changed, because it will be automatically generated for you after you right-click and select it. When your input parameter is not a regular object, you need to add a class field to tell dubbo which class you are using.

2.There is a save button behind the input box了‘, you can choose to save the current address for selection next time, or you can click the delete button to delete the current address

idea-plugin.name: Lightrun
idea-plugin.description:
Lightrun is a suite of tools for adding real-time information to your running applications. It allows you to instrument code-level logs, snapshots and metrics at runtime - no hotfixes, hot-swapping or redeployments necessary.

Using Lightrun, you can:

  • See the full content (variables, arrays and objects) of any stack frame along a user’s journey through your application - without stopping the running process
  • Measure the size of data structures in memory without predefined, code-level instrumentation
  • Count the number of times an arbitrary line in the code was executed
  • Investigate why a long-running big data worker died - with the full context of the thrown exception
  • Evaluate any expression, anywhere in the code, without changing the state of the running application or causing side effects
  • Get real-time alerts in Slack (or any application with a webhook) for every piece of instrumentation added

Lightrun features

Lightrun's IDE plugin enables the addition of real-time, code-level information to your running production applications. After a short download and configuration process, you would be able to:

  • Add log lines - including the evaluation of expressions - without redeploying, recompiling or even restarting the application
  • Capture a snapshot (our version of a "virtual" breakpoint) to your running applications - without stopping the running program
  • Add real-time metrics that track any type of numerical value in the code - from simple variable to complex calculations
  • Measure the execution time of a selected method without additional instrumentation
  • Measure the execution time of an arbitrary block of code
  • Export any numeric expression (e.g data.size() ) into a metric
idea-plugin.change-notes: Read the latest release notes at https://docs.lightrun.com/release_notes/lightrun-release-notes/

idea-plugin.name: Debug Variable Save Load
idea-plugin.description:
Save and load objects in debugger variable tree. Extract debug variable as a Java code or a JSON object.

Usage

In a debugger breakpoint stack frame, right click on a variable, pick "Save Value", "Load Value..." or "Extract Value..." menu item.

  • "Save Value" will directly save the selected value.
  • "Load Value..." will popup a list of previously saved values, you can select one and load it to the variable. It works just like "Set Value".
  • "Extract Value..." will extract value as a Java or JSON code with possibility to copy the result to the clipboard.

Notes

  • The plugin applies Kryo to serialize and persist the objects. It is basically designed to save/load pure data objects. If the type of the object is not supported by Kryo's default serializer, it cannot be saved.
  • All Kryo data are saved in USER_HOME/.IntelliJPlugin/DebuggerVariableSaveLoader/
  • Last tested IDEA version is 2024.3, the author may not follow and test later versions. Any feedback is welcomed.

idea-plugin.name: Line Profiler
idea-plugin.description:
A PyCharm Line Profiler plugin

This plugin uses the python line-profiler package to create and visualize line profiles into PyCharm. The following data is displayed inline at the corresponding code:
  • % Time spent at line: colormapped and displayed numerically
  • Hits of line: displayed numerically
  • Time spent at line: displayed numerically
  • Time / hit spent at line: displayed numerically

Getting started

Profiling code with PyCharm Line Profiler is done in 3 steps:
  1. import line-profiler-pycharm decorator
    Add the following import to the python files in which you want to profile functions:

    from line_profiler_pycharm import profile

  2. decorate your functions
    Decorate the functions you want to profile with the decorator:

    @profile
    def some_method():
      # some code you want to profile
  3. profile!
    Execute with 'Line Profile' that is installed with this plugin
    4. When the execution is finished, Line Profiler will visualize the profile automatically.
See the screenshots for examples.

Helper package

As seen in 'Getting started', the plugin uses a helper package called 'line-profiler-pycharm'. The first time you profile your code with Line Profiler, the plugin will ask whether it should install this package into your python environment.
Alternatively you can install the package yourself with pip:

pip install line-profiler-pycharm

3rd party code

This project uses the following opensource software:
  1. line-profiler
  2. jViridis

idea-plugin.name: Byte Code Analyzer
idea-plugin.description:
This IntelliJ plugin provides a modern and powerful tool window to analyze byte code. Its supports Java, Kotlin, Groovy, and other JVM language class files. Based on ASM 9.7.1, it currently supports class files up to Java 24.

Features

(Please take a look at the README.md to get a more detailed description and screenshots.)

Class File Views

  • The Structure View gives depth and human-readable insights into the individual elements of a given class file.
  • The Plain View gives a textified representation of the byte code.
  • The ASM View provides Java source code that contains all instructions to generate the class via the ASM library.
  • The Decompiled View that provides the result of the de-compilation of the class file using IntelliJ's built-in decompilers.
  • The Constant Pool View provides insights into the constant pool entries.

Byte Code Tools

The following tools are providing a general way to better understand certain aspects of the byte code specification:

  • An access Converter to split the compressed access value into single readable values or calculate a compressed one.
  • A signature parser to split a signature down into its components.
  • A built-in overview of all byte code instructions.

Other

  • Action to list all method frames, which are containing the state of the locals and the stack after each instruction.
  • Action to verify the byte code of a class file.

The tool window is available via View | Tool Windows | Byte Code and will be shown by default in the lower right corner of IntelliJ.

Class files can be either opened directly from the tool window or from the "Analyze Byte Code" action. This action is available in the project view and in the editor for JVM class or source files

idea-plugin.name: Rename Files Refactor Batch
idea-plugin.description:
This is an IntelliJ-based plugin that adds an action to batch replace the names of files in a directory selected in the project view.
The renaming uses the standard IntelliJ refactor function, so if the source file is in an object-oriented language, it will automatically replace the corresponding class name, etc. in the source code.
Operation confirmed at Java source files.

How to run

Right-click on the directory in the Project View > Refactor > Bulk Rename

Specification

  • Regular expression support
  • Do not change the directory name.
  • Files in subdirectories are also searchable.
  • Multiple selection of search directories is not supported.
  • If more than one class is written in one source file, only the file name will be renamed.
  • If the class name written in the source code is different from the file name, only the file name will be renamed.


プロジェクトビューで選択したディレクトリ内のファイルの名前を一括置換するアクションを追加するIntelliJ IDEAプラグインです。
名前変更にはIntelliJ標準のリファクタ機能を使用しているので、オブジェクト指向言語のソースファイルならソースコード上の対応するクラス名なども自動で置換してくれます。
Javaのソースファイルで動作確認済みです。

仕様

  • 正規表現対応
  • ディレクトリ名は変更しない
  • サブディレクトリ内のファイルも検索範囲とする
  • 検索ディレクトリの複数選択は非対応
  • １つのソースファイルに2つ以上のクラスが書かれているファイルは、ファイル名だけのリネームが行われる
  • ソースファイルに書いてあるクラス名とファイル名が異なる場合は、ファイル名だけのリネームが行われる
  • クラス定義の無いファイルは、ファイル名だけのリネームが行われる

実行方法

プロジェクトビューでディレクトリを選択して右クリック > Refactor > Bulk Rename
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed so that all renames from a single Bulk Rename action can be undone together with one Ctrl+Z.

idea-plugin.name: Sputnik
idea-plugin.description:
Allows to debug programs with printf.
Parses program console output, detects lines in a special format, and builds a histogram shown in a dedicated tool window.
Commands have the format '0x01cmd(args)\n', i.e. byte 1 followed by a command name and command arguments in parentheses. In java one can print a command like this: System.out.println("\1h('Histogram name','bucket name')").
Supported commands:
h('histName','bucketName') - adds 1 to the bucket in the specified histogram
hr('histName') - resets the specified histogram

c('chartName','counterName') - adds 1 to the counter with the given name in the given chart

Hi(123) - adds 123 to the integer histogram

A lot of printing will slow down the program, so it is suitable only for quick experiments.
To make processing a bit faster, clear the folding patterns at 'File | Settings | Editor | General | Console'
idea-plugin.change-notes: • Now it is possible to see cumulative distribution for integer histograms by clicking on it

Ballast's pluggable architecture can be adapted to support a variety of UI targets, while sharing the same core business logic. Additionally, Ballast is also suitable for use in non-UI applications, such as for managing the caching/repository layer of your application.

idea-plugin.name: breakpoint-log-selection
idea-plugin.description:
Breakpoints can be used for temporary logging. This kind of logging will never accidentally be pushed to your VCS or to production, because a breakpoint is not code. Therefore, you cannot push it.

A breakpoint is a logging breakpoint when it fulfills the following criteria:

  • it is non suspending
  • it has a log expression

If both conditions are true we are talking about a logging breakpoint. These are fantastic tools to use, but there is a downside: you can only create one by doing multiple clicks with the mouse. With this plugin you can do the same but with a keyboard shortcut.

It works as follows:

  1. select the variable or expression that you would like to log
  2. press the assigned shortcut (default: ctrl-command-F8)

This will create a non suspending breakpoint that will log the selected variable or expression on the next line that support breakpoints. The main reason for the next line is to prevent the logging of empty variables.

The default shortcut can be replaced by assigning a new shortcut to the action 'Log Selection with Breakpoint'.

idea-plugin.name: Dynatrace Live Debugger
idea-plugin.description:
Dynatrace Live Debugger

The only remote debugger you'll ever need. Get real-time data from any production system without stopping your app! Set breakpoints, connect to your instance and start receiving messages. Try our services today!

Overview

Instantly access live, code-level data to troubleshoot and understand complex, modern applications - with no extra coding, redeployments, or restarts. ​

Dynatrace Live Debugger by Dynatrace allows you to get the real-time debug data you need from running applications, allowing you to troubleshoot and debug quickly, in any environment, from dev to production. With a single click, developers can access the relevant data without adding additional code, waiting for redeployment, or attempting to reproduce issues locally. Instantly see the full state of your app, including stack trace, variable values, and more, all without stopping or breaking your running code.

This is the first tool offered within the Dynatrace Live Debugger extension, with more to come soon!

Requirements

  • A Dynatrace account
  • Access to Live Debugging on Dynatrace

Installation

You can install the extension from the Jetbrains Marketplace or directly from the IDE by going to Settings > Plugins > Marketplace.

How to use

  1. Install the extension.
  2. Open the Dynatrace Live Debugger panel.
    The panel is located at the bottom of the IDE.
  3. Log in to your Dynatrace account.
    1. Go to your device’s default browser. Ensure you are logged in to your Dynatrace account.
    2. In the Dynatrace Live Debugger panel of the IDE, click Log In. You will be redirected to your default broswer where the session will automatically be authenticated.
  4. Select the environment you’d like to debug by clicking on the dropdown in the panel header. The environment picker displays all Dynatrace environments where you have Live Debugging permissions. Select an environment from the list.
  5. Configure your debug session by clicking “Filter applications” in the panel header.
    Only instances with Live Debugging enabled will appear. Select filters for the instances you’d like to debug and click “Apply”.
  6. Add a Live Debugging breakpoint.
    Click next to a line number and select “Live Debugging Breakpoint”.
    The breakpoint will be applied to instances matching the filters you configured in step 5, within the environment selected in step 4.
  7. View data.
    When your breakpoints are triggered data will stream into the Dynatrace Live Debugger panel. Click on a snapshot to see local variables, stack trace, process information and tracing data.

More info

For more info, see the docs.

idea-plugin.name: TcpTunnelJ
idea-plugin.description:
TcpTunnelJ is a TCP tunnel that lives inside your IDE. It listens on a local port, forwards every connection to the host and port you choose, and shows what travels in both directions — so you can see exactly what your application sends and what the server answers, without leaving the IDE or setting up an external proxy.

Features

  • Capture any TCP traffic: point a client at the local port and every connection appears in the calls list, with its request line, source and destination, request and response size and duration
  • Side-by-side request and response viewers built on the IDE editor: soft wrap toggle, and Ctrl+F search and the usual editor navigation work inside the captured text, even on very long single-line JSON bodies
  • HTTP-aware response view: chunked transfer encoding is undone and gzip / deflate bodies are decompressed, so the payload is readable instead of a wall of bytes
  • Copy exactly what you need: "Copy body (decoded)" puts the bare payload on the clipboard, ready to paste into a .json file; "Copy response (decoded)" and "Copy response (raw)" cover the full response, with or without the wire framing
  • Work on several calls at once: multiple selection, "Copy requests" (Ctrl/Cmd+C) and "Remove selected calls"
  • Save calls to a file at any time, also while the tunnel is running
  • Start on Boot: the tunnel starts by itself when the project opens
  • Per-project settings: each open project, in one or more IDE instances, keeps its own ports and destination
  • Works with plain-text socket protocols as well as HTTP, in every JetBrains IDE from 2023.3 onwards

This plugin is an enhanced and updated version of the original TunnelliJ plugin (available at TunnelliJ GitHub Repository), offering additional features and improvements to streamline your workflow.

  • "Save calls" also while the tunnel is running
  • Chunked and gzip/deflate responses decoded in viewer, copy and save

  • Viewers are now IDE editors: long JSON lines render correctly, Ctrl+F works

Free and open source

CallGraph is completely free and open source under the GPL v3 license. Explore the implementation, report problems, request features, or contribute improvements directly on GitHub.

View source code  ·  Report an issue  ·  View releases

CallGraph visualizes caller–callee relationships for any Java or Kotlin method and lets you jump straight to definitions or call sites. Supports pure Java, pure Kotlin, and mixed Java/Kotlin projects.

How to use

  1. Right-click on a method and select Generate Call Graph from the context menu

  • Interactive call graph visualization with pan and zoom
  • Direct navigation to method definitions and call sites
  • Export diagrams as standalone HTML files
  • Community-driven development with public source code and issue tracking

idea-plugin.name: Enhanced Debug View
idea-plugin.description:
Enhanced Debug View extends PyCharm's debugger by adding the ability to view available object methods, sorted private and protected fields, and all dunder methods and fields during debugging sessions.

Features

  • Automatic Mode: Optionally show methods, grouped private and protected fields, and dunder methods for all objects automatically.
  • Flexible Configuration: Filter private methods, magic (dunder) methods.
  • Method Signatures: Display method signatures with parameters.
  • Manual Mode: Display additional data only for specific objects.
  • One-Session Automatic Mode: Activate through context menu in debugging mode for one session.

Requirements

  • PyCharm 2023.1 or higher

Usage

Manual Mode (Default)

  1. Start debugging a Python script.
  2. Stop at a breakpoint.
  3. In the Variables panel, right-click on any object.
  4. Select "Add extra data to the object" from the context menu.
  5. The selected object will display additional lists with user methods, private and protected fields, dunder methods and fields, based on plugin settings.

Automatic Mode

  1. Open File → Settings → Tools → Enhanced Debug View.
  2. Enable the "Automatically apply for all objects in the variable panel" option.
  3. Configure filters as desired:
    • Show object methods (starting with _)
    • Show magic methods and fields (__init__, __str__, etc.)
    • Show protected fields
    • Show private fields
  4. Apply settings.

Automatic Mode for One Debugging Session Only

  1. Run code in debugging mode.
  2. Wait for your code to stop at your first breakpoint.
  3. In the Threads & Variables tab, right-click in an empty area to open the context menu and select Enable Auto adding extra data for the current session.
  4. A popup window will inform you about activating automatic mode for the current session.
  5. When navigating through the object tree, additional information will be added when expanding each object.

Settings

The plugin provides the following configuration options:

  • Automatic method display: Automatically show methods for all objects.
  • Show private fields: Methods starting with __ underscores, displayed as __privatemethod instead of __Classname__privatemethod.
  • Show protected fields: Methods starting with _ underscore.
  • Show user methods: Show methods including signatures, which the standard debugger does not display.
  • Show all available dunder methods and fields: Displays standard fields and methods like __init__, __dict__, etc.

Usage Example

class Example:
    def __init__(self, value: int):
        self.public_field = value
        self._protected_field = "protected"
        self.__private_field = "private"

    def public_method(self, x: int, y: str = "default") -> str:
        return f"{x}: {y}"

    def _protected_method(self, data: list) -> bool:
        return len(data) > 0

    def __private_method(self) -> None:
        pass

obj = Example(1)
obj # Set breakpoint here

# In the Threads & Variables tab, when expanding object tabs, new fields with new information will be automatically added

When using the plugin, you will see methods:

  • methods (if method display is enabled)
    • --__private_method().
    • --_protected_method().
    • --public_method().
  • dunder_methods (if magic (dunder) methods are enabled)
    • --('__class__', 'Example(value: int)')
    • --...
  • private_fields (if private methods are enabled)
    • --__private_field
  • protected_fields (if protected methods are enabled)
    • --_protected_field
  • And other inherited methods from object

Troubleshooting

Plugin Doesn't Work

  • Make sure you're using PyCharm (not IntelliJ IDEA).
  • Ensure you've configured the plugin in settings.
  • Restart PyCharm after installation.

Methods Don't Display

  • Make sure you're in Python debugging mode.
  • Check plugin settings.
  • Ensure the object is a Python object (not a primitive; primitives won't display anything, e.g., list).

Contributing

  1. Fork the project.
  2. Create a feature branch (git checkout -b feature/amazing-feature).
  3. Commit your changes (git commit -m 'Add amazing feature').
  4. Push to the branch (git push origin feature/amazing-feature).
  5. Open a Pull Request.

Known Limitations

  • Works only with Python objects.
  • Requires an active debugging session.
  • Automatic mode may affect performance with a large number of variables; use targeted manual mode for specific objects if needed.
  • In manual mode, if data doesn't appear after selecting "Add extra data to the object," step to the next line (F9) or avoid expanding the object before adding data.
  • Some built-in types may display a limited set of methods.

License

Licensed under GPLv3. You are allowed to fork, modify, and redistribute it, but any derivative work must also be licensed under GPLv3. Include a link to the original repository: https://github.com/trulander/EnhancedDebugView.

idea-plugin.name: Spring Transaction Inspector
idea-plugin.description:
Spring Transaction Inspector

Catch Spring @Transactional pitfalls before they reach production! This plugin performs static analysis to detect common transaction anti-patterns and configuration issues.

🎯 Key Features (11 Inspections)

  • AOP Proxy Bypass Detection - Warns when calling @Transactional methods within the same class
  • Invalid Method Modifiers - Detects @Transactional on private/final/static methods that Spring cannot intercept
  • Transaction Propagation Conflicts - Detects MANDATORY/NEVER/REQUIRES_NEW conflicts that cause runtime exceptions or data inconsistency
  • N+1 Query Detection - Identifies lazy-loaded relationships (@OneToMany, @ManyToOne, etc.) accessed in loops and streams
  • ReadOnly Transaction Violations - Detects write operations in @Transactional(readOnly=true) methods
  • Checked Exception Rollback - Warns when checked exceptions won't trigger rollback without proper configuration
  • @Async + @Transactional Conflicts - Detects when transactions won't propagate to async threads
  • @Retryable + @Transactional Conflicts - Detects retry-around-transaction on the same bean that can re-run side effects on every attempt
  • Swallowed Exceptions - Detects exceptions caught inside @Transactional without re-throw or setRollbackOnly, which silently commits partial data
  • External Calls in Transactions - Detects HTTP/email/file I/O and Thread.sleep inside @Transactional that hold the DB connection too long
  • ReadOnly Calling Write Methods - Smart detection of propagation conflicts between read-only and write transactions
  • Visual Indicators - Gutter icons show transactional methods at a glance
  • Quick Fixes - One-click solutions for common issues
  • Fully Customizable - Enable/disable specific inspections in Settings

💡 Perfect For

  • Spring Boot developers working with JPA/Hibernate
  • Teams wanting to catch transaction bugs during code review
  • Developers learning Spring transaction management best practices

📖 Learn More

GitHub Repository | Report Issues
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Version 1.2.1 - IDE Compatibility Update

  • IDE Compatibility: Extended support to IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2 (build 262.*)

Version 1.2.0 - Three New Inspections

  • External calls inside @Transactional: New inspection flags HTTP calls (RestTemplate/WebClient/RestClient/HttpClient/OkHttp/Feign), email sends, file I/O and Thread.sleep() made inside a transaction — these hold the DB connection for the whole method and can exhaust the pool under load.
  • Swallowed exceptions inside @Transactional: New inspection flags catch blocks that neither re-throw nor call setRollbackOnly(), which makes Spring silently commit partial data.
  • @Retryable + @Transactional conflict: New inspection warns when both annotations sit on the same bean — the transaction commits before the retry fires, so side effects can re-run on every attempt.

Version 1.1.0 - Quality & Reliability Release

  • Jakarta/javax parity: Propagation conflict detection (MANDATORY/NEVER/REQUIRES_NEW) and rollbackOn awareness now work for jakarta.transaction.Transactional and javax.transaction.Transactional, not only Spring.
  • Deeper async detection: Lazy-relationship access in @Async methods is now caught anywhere in a call chain (e.g. user.getOrders().get(0).getItems()), not just first-level getters.
  • OSIV-friendly N+1: New optional setting "Also detect outside @Transactional (OSIV)" for projects relying on Open-EntityManager-In-View.
  • Robust readOnly handling: @Transactional(readOnly = ...) is now resolved via constant evaluation, so Boolean.TRUE, parenthesized expressions and constant references all work.
  • Memory: Replaced an unbounded repository cache with CachedValuesManager tied to PsiModificationTracker, eliminating stale PsiClass retention on long sessions.
  • Quick-fix bug: Remove @Transactional on an @Async/@Transactional pair was deleting @Async instead of @Transactional — fixed.
  • Performance: Each inspection short-circuits at the visitor entry when its toggle is disabled.
  • CI: Tests now run on every PR; release notes are no longer hard-coded in the workflow.

Version 1.0.6 - Build Toolchain Update

  • Build: Upgraded to Gradle 9.4 and IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.12.0 to fix plugin archive extraction issue on IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1 (build 261.*)

Version 1.0.5 - IDE Compatibility Update

  • IDE Compatibility: Extended support to IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1 (build 261.*)

Version 1.0.4 - Improved Same-Class Call Detection

  • Context-Aware Warnings: Same-class @Transactional method call inspection now differentiates between scenarios:
    • INFO level: When caller has @Transactional and no special propagation - annotation is redundant but joins existing transaction (expected behavior)
    • WARNING level: When called method has special propagation (REQUIRES_NEW, MANDATORY, etc.) - won't work as expected
    • WARNING level: When caller has no @Transactional - annotation will be completely ignored
  • Better Developer Experience: Reduces false positives and helps developers understand when same-class calls are acceptable vs. problematic

Version 1.0.3 - Jakarta EE Support

  • Jakarta Transaction Support: Now detects jakarta.transaction.Transactional and javax.transaction.Transactional
  • IDE Compatibility: Extended support to IntelliJ IDEA 2025.3 (build 253.*)

Version 1.0.2 - Enhanced Detection

  • New Inspection: Transaction Propagation Conflict Detection (MANDATORY/NEVER/REQUIRES_NEW)
  • N+1 Query Detection Improvements: @ManyToOne/@OneToOne(fetch = LAZY) support

Version 1.0.1 - Major Improvements

  • Fixed memory leak, type-based detection, settings toggles

Version 1.0.0 - Initial Release

  • 7 inspections for @Transactional anti-patterns

idea-plugin.name: Logspace
idea-plugin.description:
Logspace - AI-Powered Production Bug Analysis

Analyze production bugs and logs directly in your IDE with GitHub Copilot integration through MCP (Model Context Protocol).

Quick Start

  1. Login: Go to Tools -> Logspace -> Login and authenticate with your Logspace account
  2. Restart IDE: Restart WebStorm to activate the MCP server (happens automatically after login)
  3. Enable MCP in GitHub Copilot: In GitHub Copilot chat, click the Agent dropdown -> Configure Tools -> Enable logspace by clicking Start
  4. Start Using: Type @logspace in GitHub Copilot chat to analyze bugs

Features

  • AI-Powered Analysis: Use GitHub Copilot with @logspace to analyze production bugs
  • Smart Session Analysis: Get comprehensive bug reports with errors, network requests, console logs, and user interactions
  • Error Context: View what happened before errors occurred with detailed timeline
  • Network Debugging: Filter and analyze API calls by status code, method, or URL
  • Console Logs: Search and filter console output (log, error, warn, debug)
  • OAuth2 Authentication: Secure device flow authentication with your Logspace account

Example Commands

After enabling the MCP server in GitHub Copilot, use these commands:

  • @logspace analyze session 123 - Analyze a specific bug/session
  • @logspace smart analysis 123 - Get AI-powered insights and recommendations
  • @logspace get console logs 123 - View console output from a session
  • @logspace list network requests 123 - See all API calls with filtering options
  • @logspace get error context 123 - Get detailed error information with timeline

Configuration Note

Important: After login and restart, you must enable the logspace MCP server in GitHub Copilot:

  1. Open GitHub Copilot chat window
  2. Click the Agent dropdown at the bottom
  3. Select Configure Tools
  4. Find logspace in the list and click Start (it will show a green "ON" indicator)
  5. Click Apply to save

Requirements

  • GitHub Copilot subscription and plugin installed
  • Logspace account (sign up at logspace.io)
  • Node.js installed (required for MCP server runtime)

Troubleshooting

MCP Tools Not Working?

  1. Enable in Copilot: GitHub Copilot chat -> Agent dropdown -> Configure Tools -> Enable logspace by clicking Start
  2. Verify Login: Check Tools -> Logspace - you should see Logout option (not Login)
  3. Check MCP Config: Verify GitHub Copilot's MCP configuration file contains logspace server entry (see format below)
  4. Restart IDE: Restart WebStorm completely after login (MCP setup runs automatically)

MCP Configuration Format: The config file should have a "logspace" entry like this:


  {
	"servers": {
		"logspace": {
			"command": "npx",
			"args": ["-y", "@logspace/mcp-server@latest"],
			"env": {
				"API_BASE_URL": "http://your-server-address",
				"LOG_LEVEL": "info"
			}
		}
	}
}

Common Issues

  • Plugin not loading: Requires IDE 2025.2+ (Build 252+) and JDK 21+
  • Authentication fails: Check server URL in Settings → Tools → Logspace
  • Node.js not found: Install Node.js 18+ from nodejs.org

idea-plugin.name: Ignite
idea-plugin.description:
Ignite: Execute Java Methods Instantly with Arthas Integration

Ignite is a powerful developer tool designed for IntelliJ IDEA. It acts as a bridge between your code editor and the running JVM, allowing you to execute any Java method (Spring Beans, Services, Utils) directly from the IDE context menu without writing temporary controllers or test cases.

Under the hood, Ignite automatically leverages Arthas to attach to your process and invoke methods via vmtool.

Key Features

  • One-Click Execution: Right-click on any method name -> "Ignite Run". No more "Restart Server" just to test a small logic change.
  • Microservices Ready: Automatically detects all running Java processes. Select target service (PID) via a dropdown menu.
  • Smart JSON Editor: Built-in JSON editor with syntax highlighting and auto-formatting for method arguments.
  • Professional Console: Dedicated "Ignite Console" tool window to view structured execution reports (Parameters & Return Values formatted as JSON).
  • Parameter History: Remembers your last used arguments for every method.
  • Zero Configuration: Auto-downloads and attaches Arthas in the background. Handles Chinese character encoding automatically.


Ignite: IDEA 专属 Arthas 集成与方法热调用工具

Ignite 是一款专为 IntelliJ IDEA 打造的效能插件。它打通了代码编辑器与运行中 JVM 的隔阂，让你无需编写 Controller 或测试用例，即可通过右键菜单直接调用运行中项目（Spring Boot 等）的任意 Java 方法。

idea-plugin.name: emitter-navigator
idea-plugin.description:
Features

  • Press F12 on an event name string inside an emit() or on() call to jump to all paired counterparts across the project
  • Results are shown in a popup sorted by: current file first, then by line number
  • Supports .js, .ts, .jsx, .tsx, and .vue files
  • Supports event names passed as variables (const key = "event")

Configuration

Open Settings → Tools → Emitter Navigation to customize which methods are treated as emitters or listeners.

Format

One method per line. Optionally specify the argument index (0-based) where the event name is located:

methodName           # match any string argument (up to 9)
methodName:argIndex  # match only the argument at the given index

Examples

SettingMatches
emitemit("event"), this.emit("type", data) — any string arg
send_io_room:1send_io_room(room, "event", ...) — second arg only

Default emit methods: emit

Default on methods: on

Supported Patterns

// Direct string literal
socket.emit("connect", data);
this.on("connect", handler);

// Variable reference (const/let with string initializer)
const key = "connect";
socket.emit(key, data);
this.on(key, handler);

// Custom method with event at a specific argument position
send_io_room(room, "connect", data);   // configured as send_io_room:1
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • F12 Go-to-Declaration navigation between emit/on call pairs across the project
  • Results popup sorted by current file first, then by line number
  • Support for .js, .ts, .jsx, .tsx, .vue files
  • Settings UI under Settings → Tools → Emitter Navigation to customize emit/on method names
  • Per-method event argument index configuration (e.g. send_io_room:1)
  • Methods without an explicit index match any string argument (up to 9 arguments)
  • Variable reference support: const key = "event" can be used as the event name argument
  • Context menu action Find Emitter Pairs to summarize emit/on pairs in the current file

idea-plugin.name: JSON Utilities
idea-plugin.description:
JSON Utilities is an IntelliJ IDEA API Workbench for backend developers, combining HTTP Client endpoint context with fast JSON inspection and data transformation.

English: Open the current .http request, switch between request and imported response data, run JSON formatting, repair, conversion, Java, JSONPath, JWT, and SQL operations, preview diffs, and safely write results back only after the source snapshot is checked. Standalone text processing remains available when no endpoint context exists.

中文： JSON Utilities 是面向后端开发者的 IntelliJ IDEA API Workbench：可以打开当前 .http 请求，在请求与导入的响应之间切换，执行 JSON 格式化、清理修复、YAML/Properties/Java/JSONPath/JWT/SQL 处理，预览差异，并在源内容快照未变化时安全写回。没有接口上下文时仍可作为独立文本工具使用。

Key Features / 主要功能

  • API Workbench / 接口工作台： open the current HTTP Client request and keep request/response context in the tool window
  • Safe Output / 安全结果出口： copy results, preview native IDEA diffs, or write back only when the source has not changed
  • Formatting / 格式化： beautify and compact JSON with configurable indentation
  • Cleaning / 清理修复： repair single quotes, trailing commas, comments, BOM, and wrapped payloads
  • Decode & Escape / 解码与转义： handle escaped JSON, URL-encoded data, and Base64 payloads
  • Conversions / 格式转换： JSON ⇌ YAML, JSON ⇌ Properties, JSON ⇌ SQL
  • Code Generation / 代码生成： generate Java entity classes from JSON
  • JSONPath / 查询： query and extract data with JSONPath expressions

  • Multiple Entry Points / 多入口： editor popup menu, console popup menu, tool window, and intention actions

Usage / 使用方式

  • Open the JSON Utilities tool window for conversion, validation, and structure inspection

idea-plugin.name: RepoBuddy
idea-plugin.description:
RepoBuddy — Run & Inspect Spring Data Repositories from IntelliJ

RepoBuddy lets you execute any Spring Data JPA repository method directly from the editor — without writing a test, opening a REST client, or redeploying your app. Click the gutter icon next to a repository method, fill in the parameters, and see the real query result, the captured SQL, and the execution time instantly.

Who is it for?

  • Spring Boot developers who debug data-layer issues daily
  • Teams building complex JPA queries who need fast feedback
  • Developers reviewing or refactoring repository logic

Key Features

  • Run ▶ gutter icon — every Spring Data repository method gets a clickable run marker. One click opens the execution popup.
  • Live execution against your running app — RepoBuddy injects a lightweight agent into your Spring Boot process. The real JPA context executes the method; no simulation or mocking.
  • SQL capture — Hibernate's StatementInspector intercepts every SQL statement triggered by the call. You see the exact queries, in order, with timestamps.
  • JSON result viewer — the return value is serialized and displayed with execution time colour-coded green / amber / red by speed.
  • Smart parameter form — input fields are generated per parameter type. Supports String, Long, Boolean, Pageable, UUID, LocalDate, enums, and arbitrary JSON objects.
  • 🎲 Random data generation — fill fields instantly with type-aware sample values. Recognises 30+ name hints (email, phone, city, status, …) and known types (Pageable, UUID, LocalDate, BigDecimal, …). A 🎲 Generate All button fills every field at once; individual per-field dice buttons let you randomise one parameter at a time.
  • Pageable / PageRequest support — JSON-driven input with page, size, and sort direction. The agent deserialises it into a real PageRequest — no Jackson abstract-type crash.
  • Enum reflection — enum parameters are resolved against the app's loaded constants via reflection. Falls back to the first real constant (with a helpful log message listing all available values) so execution never crashes on an unknown placeholder.
  • ● Agent status indicator — the popup header shows a live ● Agent Ready / ● Offline badge so you know at a glance whether the agent is reachable before hitting Run.
  • Call chain tracer — pick any Spring MVC endpoint from the combo box and trace every repository method reachable from it. Results appear as an expandable tree with double-click navigation to source. HTTP method badges are colour-coded (GET=green, POST=blue, PUT=amber, DELETE=red). Expand All / Collapse All and Clear Cache controls are built in. A summary bar counts READ / WRITE / @Transactional calls and unique entity types.
  • Repository usage table — lists all repository methods with call-count badges (red = never called, amber = rarely called, green = frequently called). Live search filters by repository or method name. A Show Unused Only toggle lets you focus on dead code. Export to CSV with one click.
  • Zero configuration — the plugin automatically injects -javaagent into your run configurations on project open. No extra dependencies or properties needed. Compatible with IntelliJ 2024.1+ via the ProjectActivity API.
  • Colorful, theme-aware UI — all panels use a unified UITheme palette built on JBColor, so the plugin looks great in both IntelliJ Light and Dark themes with zero configuration.

How it works

  1. Open a Spring Boot project. RepoBuddy patches your run configuration automatically.
  2. Start your app with the ▶ button. The agent binds to a free port and writes it to a temp file.
  3. Click the ▶ gutter icon next to any repository method.
  4. Fill in parameters (or hit 🎲 Generate All), then click Run.
  5. See the JSON result, captured SQL, and execution time — all in the popup.

Supported parameter types

String, Long, Integer, Boolean, Double, Float, Short, Byte, BigDecimal, UUID, LocalDate, LocalDateTime, ZonedDateTime, Pageable / PageRequest (with sort), Sort, Enum (resolved against real constants via reflection), List<String>, List<Long>, and any other type accepted as JSON.

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2024.1 or later (Community or Ultimate)
  • Java 17 or later
  • Spring Boot 3.x with Spring Data JPA on the classpath
  • App must be running locally (started from IntelliJ)
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.8 - Unified CLI, MCP, and Project Inspections

  • Added one cross-platform repobuddy entry point for setup, checks, diagnostics, and MCP.
  • Added repobuddy check --changed for Git-aware introduced-finding checks.

  • Added one-click, verified MCP setup for Codex and Claude Code, configuration copying, installation-folder access, and guided PATH setup.
  • Removed checkout launchers that exposed Gradle tasks and generated JAR locations to users.

1.0.7 - Java Agent Handling

  • Prevented RepoBuddy from persisting machine-specific -javaagent paths in shared run configurations.
  • Added runtime-only Java agent injection for supported Java launches.
  • Added a setting to enable or disable RepoBuddy Java agent integration.
  • Cleaned up legacy RepoBuddy agent entries while preserving unrelated Java agents and VM options.
  • Prevented duplicate RepoBuddy agent arguments across Windows, macOS, and Linux paths.

1.0.6 - Code Quality Inspections & IDE Integration

  • New Self-Invocation inspection: detects @Transactional and @Cacheable methods called via this., which bypasses Spring's proxy and silently drops the annotation's effect.
  • New Issues Panel tool window with a dedicated status bar widget and editor banner for at-a-glance code quality feedback.
  • Expanded @Transactional and N+1 query detection to cover more Spring Data and JPA patterns.
  • Added per-project Settings page to enable or disable individual inspections.

idea-plugin.name: Remote Log Tail: SSH Server Log Explorer
idea-plugin.description:
Remote Log Tail — SSH Log Viewer for Server Monitoring

Securely tail and correlate remote server logs over SSH without leaving your JetBrains IDE.

Core Features

  • Verified SSH: Password/private-key authentication, explicit host fingerprint trust, project-scoped session sharing, and fail-closed IDE proxy routing.
  • Resilient Streaming: Incremental charset decoding, bounded backpressure, EDT batch rendering, sleep recovery, and automatic EOF reconnect.
  • Structured Queries: Combine text, regex, severity, server, and source clauses; save presets or reuse them as alert rules.
  • JSON Log Reader: Read Spring Boot, Logback and Log4j2 JSON as compact events; inspect decoded stacks and fields, follow exact trace IDs, customize field mapping, and copy original lines.
  • Managed Environments: Create environments once, assign servers from a selector, duplicate hosts safely, and open environment-wide merged timelines.
  • Clickable Stack Traces: Filenames and line numbers (e.g. UserService.kt:128) become hyperlinks that jump to your local source code.
  • Time-Shift: Shift recognized server timestamps without modifying the source stream.
  • SFTP File Browser: Browse remote directories to pick log paths visually.
  • Snapshot Export: Dump the current log buffer to a local .log file with one click.
  • Diagnostics & Extensibility: Inspect pooled sessions and add custom line redaction/enrichment through a dynamic extension point.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2.1.0 — Readable JSON Logs

  • JSON log reader: View structured logs as readable events with timestamps, levels, services and messages in both single-source tabs and merged timelines. Automatically detects common Spring Boot, Logback and Log4j2 fields, with custom field mapping available.
  • Details on demand: Inspect messages and decoded exception stacks, search fields, view formatted JSON, and copy original log lines. Filter related events by trace ID or a selected field.
  • Richer local queries: Filter by service, message, logger, thread, exact trace IDs and JSON field values. Reuse these queries in presets and alerts.
  • Original-line export: Export matching retained history from single-source tabs before JSON formatting or time shifting, while respecting configured line transformations.
  • Cleaner layout: Aligned JSON reader and Time Shift controls, a lighter Field mapping link, and grouped settings that wrap in narrow tool windows while keeping search fields visible.
  • More reliable filtering: JSON severity follows the level field. Switching views or filters preserves matching buffered events, and invalid queries keep the last valid filter active.

JSON reader is enabled by default and can be turned off to show original lines without reconnecting. It recognizes one complete JSON object per line; plain text and unsupported input remain readable as text. No server logging changes are required.

idea-plugin.name: Inline Call Unfold
idea-plugin.description:
Inline Call Unfold — inline call expansion for Go and TypeScript

Put the caret on a function call and Unfold splices the callee's body inline, between the lines — rendered over the real source file so the expanded code keeps native semantic colors, hover/quick-doc, go-to-definition, find-usages, and code folding. Read a call chain top-to-bottom without losing your place or opening a dozen tabs.

  • Expand inline — splice the callee body below the current line; expand again to collapse.
  • Nested expansion — expand calls inside an expanded frame; the frame grows to fit.
  • In-frame folding — fold blocks inside a frame; the frame re-fits as you collapse.
  • Keyboard navigation — descend into a frame, jump back to the call site, or collapse it.
  • Recursion aware — re-entered callees are flagged so deep chains stay legible.

Go support requires the Go plugin; TypeScript/JavaScript support requires the JavaScript plugin. Both are bundled in GoLand (and available in IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate).

idea-plugin.name: TCP/HTTP Monitor
idea-plugin.description:
TCP/HTTP Monitor

A lightweight TCP/HTTP monitoring tool integrated directly into your IDE. Capture, observe, and debug network traffic without leaving your development environment.

Key Features

  • TCP Monitor – Forward raw TCP connections with full byte-level logging, ideal for debugging database, messaging, or custom binary protocols.
  • HTTP Monitor – Intercept HTTP requests and responses with detailed header and payload inspection, including Host header rewriting and Location header rewriting support.
  • TLS/SSL Support – Enable TLS on the incoming side, the target side, or both, with configurable certificate trust options.
  • Multi-Tab Management – Run multiple monitor instances simultaneously, each in its own tab with independent configuration and logs.
  • Connection Filtering – Quickly filter connections by keyword to locate the traffic you care about.
  • Persistent Configuration – Save monitor configurations to disk so they are automatically restored when you reopen the IDE.
  • Custom Encoding – Configure the character encoding used to display TCP payloads for human-readable output.

Use Cases

  • Debug API calls between a frontend and backend service
  • Expose services running on remote hosts to a local port for inspection
  • Inspect TLS-encrypted traffic from a target service by trusting its certificate, then expose the decrypted traffic on a local TLS or non-TLS port for debugging

Getting Started

Open the Monitor tool window from the bottom toolbar of the IDE, then click the + button to create a new monitor configuration.

Basic Configuration

  • Monitor Type – Select TCP or HTTP.
  • Local Port – The port the monitor listens on (e.g. 8080).
  • Remote Host – The target server hostname or IP (e.g. 192.168.1.100).
  • Remote Port – The target server port (e.g. 3306).
  • Encoding – Character encoding used to display TCP payloads (default: system charset).

Using TCP Monitor

  1. Select TCP as the monitor type.
  2. Enter the local port to listen on and the remote host/port to forward to.
  3. Optionally set the Encoding field (e.g. UTF-8, GBK) to decode raw bytes into readable text.
  4. Click OK to start the monitor. All raw byte traffic between the client and the target will be captured and displayed in the log panel.

Example: Forward local port 3307 to a MySQL server at 192.168.1.100:3306 to inspect the wire protocol.

Using HTTP Monitor

  1. Select HTTP as the monitor type.
  2. Enter the local port and the remote host/port of the target HTTP service.
  3. Enable Replace Host header with target to rewrite the Host request header to match the target server, avoiding virtual-host mismatches.
  4. Enable Rewrite Location header to localhost to rewrite Location response headers so redirects point back to the monitor, keeping traffic flowing through it.
  5. Click OK to start. HTTP requests and responses are logged with method, URI, status code, headers, and payload.

Example: Forward local port 8080 to an API server at api.example.com:443 with TLS enabled on the target side.

TLS Configuration

TLS options apply to both TCP and HTTP monitor types:

  • Enable TLS for incoming requests – The monitor accepts TLS-encrypted connections from clients. A built-in keystore is used for the server certificate.
  • Enable TLS for target server – The monitor connects to the target server over TLS. This is required when the target service uses HTTPS or any TLS-wrapped protocol.
  • Trust target server certificate – When enabled, the monitor accepts the target server's certificate without validation (useful for self-signed certificates in development environments). This option is only available when Enable TLS for target server is checked.

Example: To forward HTTPS traffic to a local dev server with a self-signed cert, enable both Enable TLS for target server and Trust target server certificate.

Saving and Managing Configurations

  • Click Save in the dialog to persist the configuration. Saved monitors are restored automatically on the next IDE startup (in a stopped state).
  • Use the Edit (ℹ) button to modify an existing monitor. Click Unsave to remove it from persistent storage while keeping the current tab open.
  • Use the ▶ / ■ buttons to start and stop individual monitors, and the 🗑 button to clear the connection log.

idea-plugin.name: SecretLoader
idea-plugin.description:
SecretLoader pulls application secrets from a secrets manager and supplies them to your run and debug sessions as environment variables, so credentials don't have to live in appsettings.json, .env files, or run-configuration dialogs. Your code reads them like any other environment variable, and nothing about how you run the project changes.

It works with any command-line tool that can print secrets as JSON. Infisical is configured by default, and presets are included for HashiCorp Vault, Doppler, and AWS Secrets Manager. A command template adapts it to an in-house tool:

  • {cli} export --format=json --env={env} --projectId={project}

It has been tested with Infisical; the other vaults run through the same generic engine.

Switching environments

Move between dev, staging, and prod without touching code. The active environment is resolved by precedence, highest first:

  • a SECRETLOADER_ENV variable set on the run configuration
  • a per-project setting
  • a git-branch to environment mapping in .infisical.json
  • the repository default, then the global default

Details

  • If secrets can't be loaded, the launch is stopped rather than started against blank configuration. An environment that legitimately has no secrets still launches.
  • A per-project, in-memory cache keyed by project, path, and environment, with a configurable TTL.
  • A key blacklist to exclude specific keys from injection.
  • Secret values are kept out of console output.
  • The CLI is run directly rather than through a shell, and the environment and project id interpolated into the command are validated first.
  • An optional pre-commit check that blocks commits containing known secret values.

In the editor

  • No changes to application code or run configurations.
  • A status-bar widget showing the active project and environment.
  • One-click detection of the project id from .infisical.json.
  • A dry-run panel that previews which keys will be injected.

Works across IntelliJ-based IDEs, including IntelliJ IDEA, JetBrains Rider (.NET), PyCharm, WebStorm, and GoLand.

If you find SecretLoader useful, you can buy me a coffee.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Fix the dry-run panel's "Shadows local?" column showing blank for run configs (notably Rider/.NET) that carry an empty env field on the configuration while the real variables live deeper in a launch-settings profile. findEnvMap now unions every env map reachable on the profile (searching the full class hierarchy) instead of stopping at the first — which was often the empty shallow one — with the shallower/primary value winning on key conflicts.
  • Replace the deprecated ReadAction.compute (flagged by the 2026.2 plugin verifier) with Application.runReadAction, which is not deprecated and exists on all supported IDEs. Its suggested successor computeBlocking was not an option — it doesn't exist before 2025.2 and would break the plugin's 2022.3+ compatibility range. No behavior change.

idea-plugin.name: DelveSwap

idea-plugin.name: Live-Invoke
idea-plugin.description:
Live-Invoke

Invoke methods in a running JVM directly from the IntelliJ IDEA editor and view results in real-time.

在 IntelliJ IDEA 中直接调用运行中 JVM 的方法，实时查看返回结果。

🔌 核心功能

  • Gutter 图标调用 — 点击编辑器行号旁的绿色图标，一键唤起调用面板
  • JVM Attach — 通过 Java Agent 动态附加到本地 Java 进程，无需预设启动参数
  • Spring Bean 集成 — 自动类型查找 + 名称区分，支持 newInstance 回退
  • JSON 模板生成 — 复杂参数一键生成 JSON 骨架
  • 双视图结果展示 — Tree 树形浏览 + 原始 JSON 编辑器（含搜索和行号）
  • Ctrl+Enter 快捷执行 — 键盘操作，无需鼠标
  • 历史记录持久化 — 搜索、回放、复制、管理调用历史
  • 健康检查 — Agent 失联后自动断开，避免残留连接
  • 中英文双语界面 — 自动跟随 IDE 语言设置

📖 快速开始

  1. 本地启动你的 Java / Spring Boot 应用
  2. 打开 LiveInvoke ToolWindow（View → Tool Windows → LiveInvoke）
  3. 点击 Connect 选择目标 JVM 进程
  4. 在 Java 源文件中点击 public 方法旁的 gutter 图标
  5. 填写参数，点击 Execute 或按 Ctrl+Enter
  6. 在结果面板中浏览返回数据（Tree / Raw 双视图）

⚙️ 技术原理

插件通过 com.sun.tools.attach API 连接到目标 JVM，加载内嵌的 Agent JAR。Agent 在目标 JVM 中启动嵌入式 HTTP 服务器，插件通过 HTTP POST 发送调用请求（类名、方法名、参数 JSON），Agent 通过反射执行方法并返回 JSON 结果。

🌐 国际化

中文 / English 双语界面，自动跟随 IDE 显示语言设置切换。

适用于 IntelliJ IDEA 2025.3+ ~ 2026.1，支持 Java 和 Spring Boot 应用。

🔌 Key Features

  • Gutter Icon Invocation — Click the green icon next to the line number to instantly activate the invocation panel
  • JVM Attach — Dynamically attach to a local Java process via Java Agent, no startup parameters required
  • Spring Bean Integration — Auto type lookup + name disambiguation, with newInstance fallback
  • JSON Template Generation — One-click JSON skeleton generation for complex parameters
  • Dual-View Result Display — Tree view browsing + raw JSON editor with search and line numbers
  • Ctrl+Enter Shortcut — Keyboard-driven execution, no mouse needed
  • Persistent History — Search, replay, copy, and manage invocation history
  • Health Check — Auto-disconnect when the Agent becomes unreachable
  • i18n Support — Chinese and English UI, automatically follows IDE language settings

📖 Quick Start

  1. Start your Java / Spring Boot application locally
  2. Open the LiveInvoke ToolWindow (View → Tool Windows → LiveInvoke)
  3. Click Connect and select the target JVM process
  4. Click the gutter icon next to any public method in a Java source file
  5. Fill in parameters and click Execute (or press Ctrl+Enter)
  6. Browse the returned data in the result panel (Tree / Raw views)

⚙️ How It Works

The plugin connects to the target JVM via the com.sun.tools.attach API and loads the embedded Agent JAR. The Agent starts an embedded HTTP server inside the target JVM. The plugin sends invocation requests (class name, method name, parameter JSON) via HTTP POST. The Agent executes the method via reflection and returns the JSON result.

🌐 i18n

Chinese and English bilingual UI. Automatically follows the IDE display language setting.

Compatible with IntelliJ IDEA 2025.3 ~ 2026.1, supports Java and Spring Boot applications.

idea-plugin.name: DLQ Workbench
idea-plugin.description:
The problem

A message fails and lands in the DLQ. You need to find out why, how many others failed for the same reason — 4,000 messages are usually 3 or 4 root causes, not 4,000 different problems — and replay only those, without duplicating. Today that means the management UI, an ad-hoc script and a lot of copy/paste. DLQ Workbench turns that workflow into a single screen.

Free

  • Connect to a RabbitMQ broker (credentials stored securely via PasswordSafe)
  • Queue and exchange listing, with dead-letter queues visually highlighted
  • Individual message view: payload, headers, properties — non-destructive read (the message is not consumed from the queue)
  • Publish a test message manually

PRO

  • Automatic root cause grouping — clusters thousands of DLQ messages into a handful of actionable groups by exception, stack trace or structural payload signature. Works even for legacy services with no error instrumentation (RabbitMQ only guarantees the x-death header — the exception and stack trace only exist if the application adds them)
  • Selective replay — replay an entire group or a single message, to the original queue or an alternative one, with dry-run as the safe default and traceability headers (x-replay-count, x-replayed-by, x-replayed-at)
  • Payload editing before replay — fix the bad data and resend, no script required
  • Jump to code — from the dead message's stack trace straight to the consumer line in your open project. The differentiator no web tool has, because none of them run inside your IDE
  • Multiple connections with clear visual separation between environments, and a highlighted warning when the active connection is marked as PRODUCTION

Privacy

The plugin runs entirely on your machine. No backend, no intermediate server — the connection goes straight from your IDE to your broker. No message data passes through third parties.

Languages

English, Portuguese (Brazil) and Spanish, switchable from the tool window without restarting the IDE.

Why RabbitMQ first

JetBrains ships an official Kafka plugin; RabbitMQ has none. Dead-lettering is native and explicit in RabbitMQ (DLX/DLQ) — a direct conceptual fit. Kafka is on the roadmap for v2.

Feedback

Early-stage plugin — suggestions, bugs and feature requests are welcome at mauricio.bernardes88@gmail.com.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Connect to RabbitMQ (Management API + AMQP)
  • Queue listing with dead-letter highlighting and live message counts
  • Individual message view (payload, headers, properties), non-destructive read
  • Manual test message publishing
  • Secure credential storage via the IDE's PasswordSafe
  • UI in English, Portuguese (Brazil) and Spanish, switchable without restarting the IDE

First release ships the free tier. PRO features are in development.

idea-plugin.name: gRPC Call Navigator
idea-plugin.description:
gRPC Call Navigator adds bidirectional gRPC source navigation to IntelliJ IDEA.

Navigate directly from a generated gRPC client-stub call to the concrete server RPC implementation, or move in the opposite direction from a server override to its direct client call sites.

  • Java blocking, asynchronous, and future-stub client calls
  • Kotlin calls to generated Java stubs and Kotlin coroutine stubs
  • Java ImplBase and Kotlin coroutine server implementations
  • Gutter icons, Navigate menu actions, editor context actions, and an Alt+Enter intention
  • Green right arrows for client-to-server navigation and red left arrows for server-to-client navigation, with light and dark theme variants
  • Searchable selection when more than one implementation or caller is available
  • Project settings for test sources, generated fallbacks, and uncertain candidates
  • Local diagnostics explaining resolution and no-result states

gRPC Call Navigator uses semantic PSI and index-backed searches inside the currently open project. It does not replace IntelliJ IDEA's standard Ctrl/Cmd+Click declaration navigation, make runtime network calls, upload source code, or query remote repositories.

Current scope: direct gRPC client calls and server implementations in Java and Kotlin. Wrapper/data-flow tracing, streaming RPC shapes, and other service protocols are not included in this release.

idea-plugin.name: Turbo Log Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Place the caret on a variable, parameter, or field, run "Insert Log Statement", and get a real println (Kotlin) / System.out.println (Java) right after the enclosing statement -- with the class, method, and line number already baked in as literal text, so it works identically whether the surrounding code is static, instance, or top-level. Every inserted statement carries the same TCLC marker, so "Remove All Log Statements" can find and clean up every one it added, anywhere in the file, in one action -- never leaves debug prints behind by accident.

Ports a pattern that's genuinely popular elsewhere (VS Code's Turbo Console Log, ~2M installs) with no equivalent anywhere in JetBrains Marketplace -- confirmed by search before building, not assumed. Real Java AND Kotlin support, not just one language.

100% local -- no network call, no account, no telemetry. Every insertion is validated against an in-memory PSI copy before anything touches disk: if it can't be inserted safely, nothing is written, and you get an honest notification instead of broken code.

idea-plugin.name: CloudFormation Deploy Watcher
idea-plugin.description:
Watch a CloudFormation deploy in the IDE and see why it failed. It still works after the IDE updates.

Run cdk deploy or sam deploy in the terminal, turn on Live, and the events arrive in a tool window next to your code. When something breaks, the first real failure is already at the top, and one click takes you to it in the event list.

Why this one

Deploy tooling is only useful during a deploy. That is exactly the wrong moment to find out the plugin was disabled by an IDE update because it declared a narrow supported build range.

Compatibility, in concrete terms

  • No upper IDE build limit is declared. An IDE update does not switch this plugin off.
  • Every release is run through the JetBrains Plugin Verifier against multiple IDE versions before it ships.
  • It targets one AWS service and nothing else. A small surface is what makes "still works next month" a promise worth making.

What it does

  • List stacks with their current status; star the ones you watch
  • Show events newest-first, with failures marked in red
  • Live mode: keep refreshing while a deploy runs
  • The first real failure, with rollback filler like "Resource creation cancelled" skipped and SDK boilerplate trimmed. The full original text stays one click away
  • Click the cause line to jump straight to that event
  • Works with CDK, SAM, and Serverless Framework, since they all deploy CloudFormation stacks
  • Point Endpoint at LocalStack when you deploy locally

Read-only by design. It reads stacks and their events. It cannot deploy, update, roll back, or delete anything.

Free and paid

  • Free: see your stacks and their current status.
  • Paid: reading the event history with the root cause, live auto-refresh, and favorites.

Every paid feature is included in a 30-day free trial, and no card is needed to start it. Buying and invoicing are handled by JetBrains.

Credentials come from your existing ~/.aws/config profiles, environment variables, and SSO sessions. Nothing is uploaded anywhere. The plugin talks to AWS directly from your machine.

Needs only cloudformation:ListStacks, cloudformation:DescribeStacks, and cloudformation:DescribeStackEvents.

idea-plugin.name: Gleam Pro
idea-plugin.description:
Build, test, refactor, and debug production Gleam projects without leaving your JetBrains IDE.

Gleam Pro combines a detailed IntelliJ PSI model with the official gleam lsp server, then adds the IDE-native workflows that make a commercial tool valuable:

  • Source-level JavaScript debugging with Gleam breakpoints, stepping, stack frames, variables, watches, and console output through the Debug Adapter Protocol.
  • Native test explorer with package, module, and test nodes; gutter execution; source navigation; duration reporting; focused runs; and isolated reruns.
  • Safe refactoring for rename, extract variable, move module, optimize imports, and inspection quick fixes, backed by PSI-aware analysis and real-compiler tests.
  • Package management with workspace dependency graphs, Hex search, atomic dependency changes, manifest assistance, resolved source libraries, and a dedicated Packages tool window.

Start quickly with the New Project wizard and live templates. Navigate and complete symbols from generated typed PSI, see TODOs and spelling feedback, choose either the fast internal formatter or official gleam format, and run against Erlang or JavaScript with managed or local toolchains.

Features

idea-plugin.name: Thread-Confinement Escape Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags a mutable local variable (List/ Map/Set) captured by a task handed to a background thread (ExecutorService.submit/execute, new Thread(...).start()) that the SAME method also touches afterward outside any synchronized block -- real shared mutable state with no real protection (CWE-362/366). Java has no language-level way to enforce thread confinement, which is exactly the gap a static analyzer needs to cover.

Real escape analysis over a boundary this catalog has never analyzed before: which outer-scope variables a lambda/anonymous class body actually CAPTURES (the opposite of what this catalog's interprocedural analyzers do when they deliberately refuse to descend into a lambda body at all).

Stated honestly: v0.1 only `List`/`Map`/`Set` local variables declared in the same method; only an inline lambda or anonymous class passed directly at the call site. No dedicated Marketplace plugin found for this exact angle.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: VisuaL - Algorithm Debugger Visualizer
idea-plugin.description:
VisuaL is an algorithm visualizer plugin for IntelliJ IDEA that animates algorithms live as you step through your code in the IntelliJ native debugger.

VisuaL opens an interactive dashboard in your external system browser (avoiding heavy embedded in-IDE browser overhead) and consumes live execution states over a lightweight embedded HTTP server at http://localhost:7777/steps.

Supported Algorithm Visualizations:

  • Sliding Window / Two Pointers: Live array cells, moving window bounds [left, right], current window sum, and best sum tracking.
  • Dynamic Programming Grid: 2D table computation with dependency highlighting in purple, target cell highlight in blue, formula banner, and settled states.
  • Recursion & Backtracking Tree: Hierarchical call tree with non-overlapping Buchheim subtree layout, vibrant blue active call path, faded dead-end branches, resolved return value badges, argument tooltips, and pan/zoom/fit navigation.
  • Graph Traversal (BFS & DFS): Node and edge traversal with vibrant blue active node glow, amber frontier queue/stack indicators, green visited node styling, live frontier/visited strips, and interactive draggable nodes.
  • Binary Search: Live line of cells with active [low, high] span highlight, distinct amber mid pointer, smooth span shrinking animation without jump-cuts, and value comparison banner.

idea-plugin.name: BPMN Compare
idea-plugin.description:
Visual comparison of BPMN 2.0 diagrams against any Git revision, powered by bpmn.io (bpmn-js and bpmn-js-differ).
  • Current version of the diagram on the left, a branch, tag or commit of your choice on the right.
  • Added, removed, changed and moved elements are highlighted; a change list lets you jump to each change.
  • Optional synchronization of mouse cursor, hover and pan/zoom between both diagrams.
Open a .bpmn file and switch to the BPMN Diff tab, or use Compare BPMN with Branch or Commit… from the context menu.

The plugin is open source under the MIT license. Diagram rendering and diffing uses bpmn-js (© Camunda Services GmbH, bpmn.io license) and bpmn-js-differ (MIT). Copyright and license notices of all bundled third-party packages are included in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt of the plugin distribution.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added
  • The BPMN view is available in every IDE diff window — the commit dialog, the Git log, Compare with Branch, Compare Two Files. Pick BPMN diagram in the diff tool selector; the text diff stays the default. This is also the only way to compare two revisions of a diagram with each other, which the editor tab cannot do.
  • Changes inside extensionElements are reported too — Camunda execution listeners, input/output mappings and form fields, and Zeebe task definitions. bpmn-js-differ ignores them, so until now an edit that touched only a Camunda listener showed no change at all.
  • F7 / Shift+F7 step through the visible changes, wrapping around and skipping kinds hidden by a filter chip; the change list highlights where you are, the top bar has the same two buttons, and Escape closes the list.
  • Navigation between the diagram and the XML: double-click an element to open the editor with the caret on it, and Follow caret (off by default) does the reverse, selecting the element the caret is in.
  • Export: the change list as Markdown into the clipboard, ready for a pull request and honouring the filter chips, or the left diagram as SVG or PNG with the change markers included.
Changed
  • The compared revision reloads by itself after a commit, checkout, fetch or rebase, instead of showing the previous content until Refresh was pressed.
Fixed
  • Tooltips in the diff view are shown at last. None of them had ever been visible — not on the top bar buttons or the filter chips, and not on the change badges, even though the badge tooltip listing the changed attributes is a documented feature. Inside JCEF a native tooltip only appears if the host draws it, so the view now draws its own.

idea-plugin.name: SqlLogLens - Restore SQL from Logs
idea-plugin.description:
Turn Hibernate, MyBatis and p6spy logs back into SQL you can run.

Your application logs every statement with ? placeholders and prints the real values somewhere else. SqlLogLens puts the values back in, quoted correctly for their types, and gives you one statement ready to paste into a database console.

Free: restore from a selection

  • Select log lines in any editor or Run console, right-click, Restore SQL from Selection. The statements are rebuilt, formatted and copied to the clipboard.
  • Hibernate 5 and 6 bind logs, including formatted SQL spread over several lines.
  • MyBatis Preparing and Parameters blocks.
  • p6spy single-line logs.
  • Strings are quoted, numbers and booleans left bare, nulls written as NULL, and a statement whose values do not add up is marked so you check it.

Pro: capture while your application runs

  • (Pro) Automatic capture. Run or debug your application from the IDE and every statement it logs appears in the SQL Log tool window, values already in place. No selecting, no copying log lines, and nothing is added to your application.
  • (Pro) History with a filter. The last 500 statements, newest first. Type a table name to find the query you are after, double-click to copy it.
  • (Pro) Every format, every process. Hibernate, MyBatis and p6spy statements are captured from every process the IDE starts.

Private by design. SqlLogLens makes no network requests. Captured statements contain real values from your data, so they stay in memory and are gone when the project closes.

Pricing

  • Restoring SQL from a selection is free, with no time limit.
  • SqlLogLens Pro, personal: $1.50 per month, or $15 per year.
  • SqlLogLens Pro, commercial: $4.90 per month, or $49 per year.
  • 30-day free trial of Pro. Start it from the link in the SQL Log tool window.

Known limits

  • Your application has to log its SQL and its bind values. The SQL Log window shows the logger settings for each framework when nothing has been captured yet.
  • Strings use standard SQL quoting. MySQL backslash escaping is not applied.
  • A MyBatis value containing the text "), " and a p6spy line with "|" inside the SQL can be split in the wrong place, because those formats are ambiguous there.
  • log4jdbc, jOOQ and Spring JdbcTemplate log formats are not read yet.
  • Capture covers processes started from the IDE. Log files written elsewhere can be opened and restored from a selection.

Works in IntelliJ-based IDEs from version 2025.2 on. SqlLogLens depends only on the platform, so it installs in IntelliJ IDEA, Android Studio and the other JetBrains IDEs.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.1.0: first release.

  • Free: restore runnable SQL from a selection of Hibernate 5 and 6, MyBatis and p6spy log lines, formatted and copied to the clipboard.
  • SqlLogLens Pro: automatic capture from every Run and Debug session into the SQL Log tool window, with a filterable history of the last 500 statements.
  • Monthly or yearly subscription, with a 30-day free trial of Pro.

idea-plugin.name: Call Stack Explorer
idea-plugin.description:
Captures a debugger's call stack — frames and variables — the moment a breakpoint is hit, and persists it independently of the debug session's lifetime.

When a remote debug session times out or drops (network blip, server restart, session lease expiry), the call stack and locals are normally gone for good, forcing you to reproduce the conditions and re-hit the same breakpoint. This plugin keeps a snapshot around so you can keep inspecting it after the JVM on the other end is long gone.

Features:

  • "Save Call Stack" action, available whenever a debug session is suspended
  • Optional automatic capture on every breakpoint pause
  • Persists thread(s), frames (class, method, file, line), and locals as string previews, to a configurable depth
  • A dedicated "Call Stack Explorer" tool window listing saved snapshots in a tree: snapshot → thread → frame → variables
  • Double-click a frame to jump straight to that source line
  • Snapshots survive IDE restart — stored on disk per project
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.0

  • Initial release: manual and auto-capture of call stacks on breakpoint pause
  • Call Stack Explorer tool window with snapshot/thread/frame/variable tree and source navigation

idea-plugin.name: Bun Console
idea-plugin.description:
Interactive console for JavaScript and TypeScript code of your project, running on Bun.

  • Call your code directly. Functions, classes and variables of the file open in the editor are available by name, exported or not, with no imports.
  • Debug from the console. Breakpoints stop console calls; while any JavaScript program you debug is paused, the console evaluates in the selected stack frame.
  • Iterate freely. Variables persist between commands, and const, let and class can be declared again as you refine a snippet.
  • Safe by default. Switching editor tabs never runs code: a file runs only when the console first uses it. Uncaught errors are printed, never fatal.

Also: top-level await that never blocks the console, import statements, highlighting, completion of runtime names, command history, and more files in context with Add File to Bun Console or Add Symbol to Bun Console. If you use the browser developer console, it will feel familiar.

Requires Bun 1.4 or newer. Open View | Tool Windows | Bun Console. Documentation: bunconsole.dev
