idea-plugin.name: Compose HotSwan
idea-plugin.description:
Compose HotSwan: fast, reliable hot reload for Compose — Android, JVM Desktop, and the iOS simulator.

Edit Kotlin, save, and the change appears in the already-running app — no reinstall, and on Android and JVM Desktop no restart at all. On the iOS simulator the two fast tiers keep the process and the composition; the fallback tier restarts the Kotlin world in place and restores saveable state.

Platforms:
  • Android (Jetpack Compose) — Stable. Measured on a physical device: a warm edit lands end to end in 2.6–3.1s, against 23.1s for the first cold push of a session. A literal-only edit (a colour, a dp, a string) bypasses Gradle entirely.
  • JVM Desktop (Compose Multiplatform) — Supported. The same interpreter drives a desktop window and a device from one save.
  • iOS simulator (Compose Multiplatform) — Stable. Three reload tiers — an op-stream pushed over a socket, a dlopen-able reload delta, and a Kotlin/Native warm restart. The two fast tiers keep the process and the composition; the warm restart re-seeds saveable state from disk. Non-serializable remember does not survive it, and an edit that moves a composable's slot shape may reset that one composable's state. Real iOS devices are not supported.
Key features:
  • Beyond composables: ViewModels, repositories and ordinary Kotlin reload too, not just composable function bodies
  • Resource Hot Reload: change strings, colors, drawables and dimensions without restarting the app (Android)
  • Honest reporting: a reload that did not reach the screen says so, by name, instead of reporting a green
  • Screenshot Snapshot: captures device screenshots after each reload with code diff tracking and a visual gallery
  • Multi-Module Support: works across all Gradle modules in your project automatically
  • One-Click Setup: add the Gradle plugin, press Start, and you're ready to go
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2.2.0

Most of this release is Android: structural saves spend far less time in HotSwan, keep more of your state and end amber far less often, and several stale screens and crashes are fixed. It also fixes two 2.1.0 problems that stopped a launch or a build.

  • Run your app once after upgrading, before your first save. On Android and Compose Desktop, a structural save into an app another HotSwan version built is now refused before anything is applied, instead of pushing thousands of classes into it (which ran one app out of memory).
  • Fixed: release builds of apps with an Android KMP library crashed at launch, and so did every HotSwan app in Android Studio's "Profile with low overhead". Release builds no longer carry HotSwan, and a profileable build no longer instruments your code, so both launch.
  • Fixed: the iOS simulator build failed to link when a remembered lambda declared its own by delegate. Remove the hotswanIosMemoEveryCapture=false workaround.
  • Android: a structural save that edits composable bodies spends far less time in HotSwan: 385 ms with these changes and 944 ms without (median, our sample app on the emulator). Compose Desktop gets the same changes.
  • Android: more of your state survives an edit. A value edit that changes the value's length no longer rebuilds every visible LazyColumn item, and rememberSaveable state survives adding or removing a call around it.
  • Android: far fewer amber results for edits that fully applied, starting with the first save after every app start, which asked you to rebuild and reinstall.
  • Android: fewer crashes and stale screens, from changing a rememberSaveable's type to adding a launch above a running ViewModel coroutine, and a save into an app Android has frozen (behind a sleeping screen, say) now fails in about 14 s with the remedy.
  • iOS: an edited LaunchedEffect or DisposableEffect block runs after an instant reload instead of leaving the old block running.

2.1.0

Most of this release is the iOS simulator: a structural save compiles only the files you changed, far more edits skip the native build, and many cases where a reload said "applied" over a stale screen, lost state or crashed the app are fixed.

  • HotSwan's state is in the status bar, so a session that did not start after an IDE restart no longer leaves your saves doing nothing in silence.
  • Each save's Gradle build starts through a kept connection, on every platform. "Launch Gradle through a kept connection (faster start)" in Settings → Tools → Compose HotSwan turns it off.
  • Fixed: saves lost without a word. A project under a folder named src could have every save ignored, and an agent's reload dropped your saves; a save that is dropped or left in a queue is now named in an amber line.
  • Fixed: Cancel and literal edits. After a Cancel the next save no longer starts a second build, a literal edit no longer lands on the wrong value, and a second copy of your project (a git worktree) no longer sends every literal edit to the structural reload.
  • iOS resident saves, on by default: a structural save compiles only the files you changed, in a warm compiler. Build and run the app once from Xcode after upgrading.
  • iOS: far fewer full reloads, and many more edits take the instant path, from early returns and type checks to adding a private composable.
  • iOS: a literal edit reaches code the instant path installed, so a colour or size you tune right after a structural save shows on screen instead of reading "patched" over the old value.
  • iOS: state stays where it belongs, and no more "applied" over a stale screen after a relaunch, a replaced literal edit, or a mixed revert.

2.0.2

Two reported problems that each stopped people using HotSwan at all, and a round of iOS work that removes the long waits from the start of a session.

  • Fixed: an app could crash at launch on Kotlin 2.4, before you made a single edit. A class holding a property declared with by over a state value would fail during the first composition. The failure surfaced somewhere else entirely, usually as a layout error inside Compose, so it read like a bug in your own UI code. Reinstalling did not help and no setting avoided it. Nothing in your code needs to change now.
  • Fixed: the License tab could sit on "Initializing…" forever, and every save opened the pricing page in a browser. That word was never a loading state: it meant the IDE could not reach its licensing service, which is a state you can stay in indefinitely, so waiting and restarting never helped. HotSwan now tells you which state your licence is actually in and what to do about it, and when it cannot read your licence at all it says so instead of sending you to a purchase page.
  • Fixed: excluding more than one class pattern now works. A second pattern used to fail the build.
  • Your first edit in a file on iOS is fast again. Editing a value such as a colour or a dimension used to fall back to a full reload the first time you touched each file.
  • A save no longer queues behind HotSwan's own background work, and HotSwan now warms the slowest iOS step once after your simulator boots. It installs nothing and steps aside the moment you save.
  • Honest reporting throughout the iOS path. Steps that decided to skip used to do so silently, so a slow reload arrived with no explanation. Each now says what it did and what it cost you.

2.0.1

A patch release led by one user-reported crash, plus a wider agent surface and more of your code reloading instantly on the iOS simulator.

  • Fixed a crash on Compose Desktop. Code that builds an object on the fly and hands it to a dependency-injection graph could crash the app instead of reloading. It affected Compose Desktop and plain JVM modules; Android was never affected. No configuration change was ever needed to avoid it, and none is needed now.
  • The opt-out annotation now works on individual functions, not only on whole classes, which is what it always said it did.
  • Clearer answers when several Android devices are attached. A save reaches one Android device. HotSwan now tells you which one, and which are left untouched, instead of implying all of them. Compose Desktop and your booted iOS simulators still reload together in that same save.
  • Snapshots are no longer hidden from AI agents that drive HotSwan without opening the tool window.
  • AI agents can now read your app's own log, which is where stack traces live, and can find out which screenshots are actually comparable before asking for a comparison. A reload also reports the screenshot it captured, so an agent can check its own work.
  • More of your code reloads instantly on the iOS simulator, including icon properties and simple repeat loops, so fewer saves fall back to the slower path.
  • A transport diagnostic for iOS on a physical device. If you have one, you can now run a measurement that reports whether a connection to it is possible. It reloads nothing. The result would genuinely help us decide what to build next.

Full notes at hotswan.dev/docs/releases.

2.0.0

v2 changes the mechanism, not just the numbers. 1.x reloaded what a running app was willing to accept: colours, padding, text, the value edits a virtual machine can be talked into. Anything that changed the shape of a screen fell back to a rebuild. v2 ships its own interpreter engine inside your app: new code is executed rather than installed, so a structural edit is routed around the runtime instead of being forced through it.

What that buys is a different class of edit. Add and remove composables, change how a screen branches, wrap or unwrap layout, split one composable into three, replace a whole screen with code that looks nothing like what was there before, while the process stays alive and your state stays where you left it. Scroll position, navigation backstack and remember { } survive the edit.

  • Three platforms, one save. Android: the edit reaches the running app on a device or emulator, with no reinstall, no Activity recreate and no navigation loss. iOS simulator, new in 2.0: edit shared Kotlin and the change appears in the already-running simulator app, with no Xcode rebuild, reinstall or relaunch. Compose Desktop (JVM): the same save updates the running desktop window, alongside Android when both are attached; the runtime self-bootstraps, so applying the Gradle plugin is the setup.
  • Written for AI agents as well as for people. The reload pipeline is exposed over an MCP server, so an agent can drive it directly, to reload, screenshot, and read the layout and semantics of what is actually on screen. You watch an agent rewrite a screen and the device updates as it works, so the loop stops being generate, build, look and becomes a decision you make while looking at the result.
  • What 2.0 does not claim. The iOS leg ships with its own scoreboard rather than a release-day claim of completeness, and the corners that are still open are named instead of hidden. On iOS the target is the simulator. Hot reload is a debug-build tool, so your release configuration is left alone.
  • Verified compatibility, not assumed. Kotlin, Compose Multiplatform, Xcode, deployment target, Gradle, JDK, architecture and KMP project shape are each tracked, with every entry marked verified, inferred or unknown. Published at hotswan.dev/docs/compatibility.

Background reading: Compose HotSwan v2 and Compose Multiplatform desktop hot reload. Full release notes at hotswan.dev/docs/releases.

2.0.0-beta05

Fifth beta of HotSwan v2. A reporting-honesty release: every case where the IDE said a reload had succeeded while the edit had not reached the screen was tracked down and closed. Nothing here changes what reloads — it changes what you are told about it.

  • "Reloaded" now means the composition ran. The push makes a second, post-settle round-trip and the app reports what its composition did, not what the pusher wrote. A reload whose composition threw now says so instead of reporting a clean green.
  • The literal fast path no longer patches literals the compiler never wrapped. The compiler now records, per source file, every literal key it actually stamped, and the IDE refuses to fast-path a key that is not listed — falling back to a full reload, which does land the edit. This closes the silent no-op on literals inside remember { }, annotations and comments.
  • The first push after an install no longer silently drops the edited class, and a push whose classes were all filtered out is reported as withheld instead of as "no changed classes — the app is unchanged".
  • The pusher names the source files it is sending, and refuses by name rather than failing green.
  • A push can no longer reach an app the build does not produce. The app states its applicationId on the heartbeat and the pusher re-targets by identity, so a second running HotSwan app can no longer absorb your reload behind a success message.
  • Structural edits keep their state. An edit that changed a source length used to collapse the composition tree; call sites nested in lambdas are now keyed as leaves.
  • Your own compile errors reach the IDE. Kotlin diagnostics are no longer filtered out before display, every log line now reaches idea.log, and the restart-required message states what the VM actually reported instead of guessing.
  • An edit the interpreter cannot apply is declined by name. When an incremental compile and the installed APK disagree on a method's slot layout, that one method is declined and named, rather than dropping the whole composition.
  • A second attached device no longer breaks the push; verified on Android 12 (API 31) hardware as well as API 37.

2.0.0-beta04

  • Simultaneous Android + Compose Desktop (JVM) hot reload: Compose Desktop targets reload through the same interpreter as Android, with no adb and no JVMTI. The tool window lists a Desktop entry alongside connected devices; selecting Desktop and a device reloads both from one save in a single Gradle invocation.
  • New published artifact interpreter-runtime-core: the portable interpreter, extracted so the identical engine runs on ART and desktop HotSpot. Android consumers get it transitively — there is nothing to add to a build script.
  • Fixed: every non-constructor super.foo() failed on Compose Desktop (an API-33 ART gate fired on the desktop JVM, where the API level reads as 0).
  • Fixed: a reload that did not apply is no longer reported as a success — the "nothing applied" / "partial" signals were logged at a level the IDE's -q Gradle invocation suppressed.
  • Fixed: a stale desktop instance can no longer absorb a reload behind a green; a destroyed Activity is no longer retained by the reload server (debug-only, so no published app was ever affected).

2.0.0-beta03

  • A constructor / DI signature change no longer leaves a silent blank screen (#20): HotSwan now detects a reload-attributable caught error after the reload settles and requests a clean restart with an actionable message.
  • Classes with init { } blocks populate correctly (#19): the constructor helper ran field initializers but skipped init { } blocks, so a top-bar action factory silently produced an empty list.
  • Structural reload failures show the real reason instead of a bare exit 1 (#18), with an actionable JDK remedy when the cause is a Gradle JVM mismatch.

2.0.0-beta02

  • Release builds no longer crash on launch: hot reload is now strictly debug-only (hotSwanCompiler { debugOnly }, default on), so a normal app's release build carries zero hotswan.
  • Coroutine resumptions run on the correct thread: DEX-stripped suspend lambdas now cross to ART as a real ContinuationImpl, so LaunchedEffect { delay(...) } followed by a view touch no longer throws CalledFromWrongThreadException.

2.0.0-beta01

  • First public beta of HotSwan v2 — the user-code interpreter architecture, with zero JVMTI redefineClasses calls. v1 (1.x) continues on the JVMTI track.
  • Kotlin 2.3.x and 2.4.x from a single artifact: the v2 compiler plugin runs unchanged on both consumer compilers — no dual variant, apply only the plugin.

1.3.7

  • Kotlin 2.4.0 launch crash fix: Fixed a java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: No static method get$stable()I crash on app launch with Kotlin 2.4.0. The function and ViewModel isolation passes were rewriting the Compose compiler's synthetic $stable stability accessor (emitted as a property with a getter on Kotlin/Compose 2.4.0, a bare field on 2.3.x), desyncing the field/property/getter linkage cross-module stability reads rely on. The Compose $stable member is now left exactly as the compiler emits it. Reported in #18.

1.3.6

  • License update: The user license has been updated following hotswan.dev/license.

1.3.5

  • Kotlin 2.4.0 support: The compiler plugin now targets the Kotlin 2.4.0 compiler API, including the new IR annotation representation introduced in 2.4.0. HotSwan 1.3.5 requires projects building with Kotlin 2.4.0 or later; projects on Kotlin 2.2.x - 2.3.x should stay on HotSwan 1.3.4.
  • Agent app-driving MCP tools: New MCP tools let an AI agent see and drive the running app, enabling autonomous edit, hot reload, and verify loops: hotswan_get_semantic_tree returns the live Compose semantic tree (roles, text, bounds, available actions) and hotswan_click, hotswan_long_click, hotswan_type_text, hotswan_scroll, and hotswan_scroll_to_index perform input on semantic nodes. Input is dispatched through the app's own Compose SemanticsActions first, with an adb input fallback.
  • Function isolation fix for same-name composable overloads: Fixed a Platform declaration clash compile error from the isolation pass on files declaring same-name @Composable overloads together with property delegates (by). Local declarations moved into the isolated function body are now reparented correctly, so the generated lambda classes no longer collide.
  • Agent attach fix for legacy native-library packaging: Fixed the hot reload agent failing to attach on apps that package native libraries with jniLibs.useLegacyPackaging = true (extractNativeLibs). The installed native library path can contain = characters, which Debug.attachJvmtiAgent treats as the library/options separator and rejects. The agent library is now copied to a safe path before attaching.

1.3.4

  • Multipreview support in captureAllPreviews: The preview catalog now detects composables annotated with a custom multipreview annotation (a custom annotation meta-annotated with @Preview, e.g. @DevicePreviews), not just functions annotated with @Preview directly; previously such functions were invisible to the catalog. Detection scans the compiled .class output with ASM and resolves meta-annotations the way the Compose tooling does, so custom multipreviews, the repeatable @Preview container shape, and the AndroidX built-ins (@PreviewLightDark, @PreviewScreenSizes, @PreviewFontScale, @PreviewDynamicColors) are handled. The scan is decoupled from the hot-reload compiler plugin and falls back to the previous source scan when the project has not been built. A multipreview function is captured once in the device's default configuration
  • Selective capture with tags: Group previews with @PreviewScreenshot(tags = ["..."]) and capture only some of them. captureAllPreviews -Photswan.preview.tags=smoke,detail captures only previews whose tags include any of the requested labels; with no filter every preview is captured, as before.
  • Plugin coexistence fix: HotSwan no longer fails with extension 'hotSwanCompiler' already registered when a module both applies it and receives it through automatic propagation (which could surface when another buildscript plugin such as KSP is present). Applying the plugin more than once is now a safe no-op.

1.3.3

  • Release build (R8) compatibility with Compose stack-trace mapping: Fixed release builds (minifyReleaseWithR8) failing with Failed to collect Compose stack trace mapping (Failed to tokenize ...$Fn$...) on toolchains where the Compose group-key stack-trace mapping is active (Kotlin 2.3+/AGP 9.1+ with R8 enabled). HotSwan's $Fn isolated method shapes could not be tokenized by the Compose compiler's mapping task, which surfaced as a build warning that fails the build under allWarningsAsErrors. For plain Android and legacy KMP modules, $Fn isolation is now correctly confined to debug variants and no longer leaks into release (a previously over-broad variant match applied it to release builds as well). For Kotlin Multiplatform shared modules (com.android.kotlin.multiplatform.library), whose single build-type-agnostic main links $Fn into release, the plugin disables composeCompiler.includeComposeMappingFile on the consuming application so the tokenizer no longer processes the isolated methods. Reported in #16

1.3.2

  • Kotlin compiler classpath compatibility (1.3.1 follow-up): Fixed an additional NoSuchMethodError at compile time where the 1.3.1 compatibility shim inadvertently retained a direct reference to a Kotlin compiler internal as a default-parameter expression. That direct reference produced the same class of cross-version ABI mismatch the shim was meant to fix. The default is now routed through the existing reflection-based compatibility layer, and two further internal-constant references that exhibit the same companion-object getter ABI shape have been hardened the same way as a proactive measure, so the same class of failure cannot recur from these surfaces

1.3.1

  • Kotlin compiler classpath compatibility: Fixed a NoSuchMethodError at compile time on builds where the active Kotlin compiler classpath did not match the Kotlin version the plugin was compiled against. The failure surfaced as an internal Kotlin IR API being reported as missing on the consumer's compiler, despite the consumer's project declaring a Kotlin version that contained that API. Root cause was the consumer's effective compiler classpath being transitively pinned to an older Kotlin through AGP, the Compose compiler plugin, or KSP, regardless of the declared kotlin("android") version. The compiler plugin now adapts its compile-time interactions to the Kotlin compiler version actually resolved at build time instead of binding to a single fixed version when the plugin itself was built, so the same plugin artifact runs cleanly across Kotlin 2.2.x and 2.3.x classpaths and is no longer sensitive to this class of transitive-version mismatch
  • Hot reload safety for nested local classes inside remember { }: Fixed a StackOverflowError that surfaced at hot reload time on composables declaring a nested local class inside remember { } — most commonly an anonymous object : <interface> literal whose properties were initialized via expressions like tween(...) or spring(). Reading any property of the nested local class after the isolation pass entered an infinite recursion through the auto-generated accessor body and tore down the app on the first reuse of the affected scope. The accessor rewrite now applies only to fields owned by the composable's own enclosing scope and leaves fields declared on nested local classes untouched, so the reload preserves the developer's intended behavior
  • Hot reload compatibility for internal and protected state holders: Fixed an IllegalAccessError at hot reload time on composables that read or wrote internal or protected properties of a state holder whose backing class participates in the isolation pass. The previous accessor-inlining guard covered only the public-accessor path, so internal-visibility state holders — the dominant pattern in modular library code — crashed on the first cross-class property access after isolation. The guard now covers every non-private accessor, matching the JVM-level visibility of the generated backing fields, so internal and protected properties round-trip cleanly through the hot reload pipeline

1.3.0

  • HotSwan Palette — AI-driven visual iteration with zero-failure edits: New IDE-integrated design exploration surface that turns the inner loop for color, spacing, corner radius, typography, and density tuning into a side-by-side visual pick. An AI agent generates N variants of whatever screen the developer currently has on the device, every variant lands in well under a second through HotSwan's literal-patching path without rebuilding the app, and the chosen variant is written back to source as the new canonical value. Exposed both as a built-in IDE panel (web-based 9-grid with click-to-pick) and as a first-class MCP tool (hotswan_explore_palette) so any compatible agent runtime can drive it from outside the IDE. Hard guarantee by construction: every edit Palette can ever propose passes through the literal-patching pipeline, so the worst case for any individual variant is a "weird color, pick another" decision rather than a broken app, a compile error, or a structural recovery cycle. Five iteration axes shipped at MVP — color (Material 3 dynamic schemes plus curated palette sets), spacing (snapped to a 4dp grid), radius (sharp/rounded/pill), typography (compact/default/comfortable scales with optional weight axis), and density (composite macro)
  • Compile-time-emitted reload metadata for sub-millisecond classification: The compiler plugin now emits a family of binary reload metadata directly on every transformed composable, replacing the ASM bytecode walks the IDE plugin previously performed on every save with constant-time annotation-attribute reads. The metadata captures, in compact canonical form, per-composable dependency closures, per-scope structural fingerprints with a risk discriminator, per-slot remember { } and cache() fingerprints split into key-type and init-body axes, and position-stable call-site identity. The runtime classifier uses this collectively to make sharper decisions across the full reload pipeline without re-walking bytecode. Concrete improvements end users see: changes to non-composable utility code invalidate exactly the right composables; cached remember { } values are preserved across reloads when the slot's keys are unchanged (previously the entire slot was conservatively dropped, throwing away expensive cached state on edits that should have been transparent to it); and the structural pre-check no longer relies on heuristic key matching between baseline and new bytecode, eliminating a class of subtle mismatches that used to surface as inner-lambda body edits being incorrectly classified as structural
  • Foundational hot reload reliability for the new Compose runtime: Substantial rework of the device-side invalidation chain to address a class of "screen does not update" symptoms surfaced by the latest Compose runtime. Hot reloads of inner-lambda body changes inside complex lazy and subcompose containers used to appear successful in the IDE while producing no visible change on the device until the developer navigated away and back; the reload now drives invalidation along a strictly stronger path the new runtime cannot short-circuit, and affected scopes recompose on the very next frame. New automatic resolution of the outer container that owns an inner composable lambda when only the inner body changes — previously, downstream code that still held a reference to the outer container kept a stale snapshot of the lambda alive across the reload, so the visible result diverged from what the developer wrote. Restored correct behavior on the "first hot reload after launch" boundary by deferring the initial baseline capture until the runtime reaches a stable state instead of capturing a transient mid-startup snapshot. Hardened the recovery path for the small set of edits that still cannot be applied in place under the new runtime: it now prefers a narrowly targeted recovery and reserves the heavy reset path for the narrow case where it is provably the only safe option, eliminating the brief flash and loss of cached child state inside lazy and subcompose containers that occasionally surfaced on edge-case reloads
  • Closure-capture invariance detection in the structural pre-check: The reload classifier now performs a constructor-arity invariance check on anonymous closure subclasses generated by the Compose and Kotlin lowerings before deciding whether a change can be applied in-place. The check catches a narrow but high-impact class of edits — most commonly lifting a CompositionLocal.current read or a derived state value into a previously-closed composable lambda — where the resulting bytecode would have appeared body-equivalent but actually carried an incompatible constructor signature. Without the gate, the IDE reported a clean reload while the device-side runtime tripped on the first reuse of the affected lambda inside LazyLayout's subcomposition machinery, surfacing as a hard NoSuchMethodError that was difficult to attribute back to the originating edit. Affected reloads now fall back transparently to the full-rebuild path; ordinary inner-lambda body edits continue to take the sub-second in-place path
  • Cross-generation bytecode compatibility for synthetic property accessors: Fixed a class of "the app crashes immediately on launch as soon as the compiler plugin is enabled" failures rooted in an interaction between the isolation pass and Kotlin's synthetic property-accessor generation. The previous code path applied a uniform visibility transform to every private member of an isolated container, which silently invalidated the bytecode-level invariants of accessor synthetics emitted by the Kotlin frontend in earlier compilation phases. The result was a runtime invocation that resolved into a phantom super-class lookup the JVM verifier had no way to satisfy, producing a NoSuchMethodError: No super method ... against a method that demonstrably exists in the declaring class. The visibility transform is now scoped to fully private declarations only; mixed-visibility properties — the dominant var foo: X; private set pattern in modern Android state holders — preserve their accessor invariants intact and let Kotlin's downstream synthetic-accessor lowering resolve any cross-class access introduced by the isolation pass through its own indirection. Surfaced first on production multi-module Android applications using standard ViewModel state-holder patterns

1.2.10

  • Dramatically faster first hot reload: The first reload after launching the app used to spend 20 to 60 seconds in "Compiling…" status before the UI updated, even after the daemon warm-up phase had completed. Three coordinated fixes inside the warm-up and reload pipeline now keep that work continuous instead of throwing it away on every reload, so the first reload completes in roughly the same time as every subsequent reload
  • Compose hoisted lambda detection for literal patching: Fixed primitive literal hot-reload silently doing nothing for any composable whose body the Compose compiler hoists into a ComposableSingletons$<File>Kt$lambda-N field. The hoist transform erases the @Composable annotation off the inner lambda, so our pre-compiler's "is this lambda inside a @Composable context" check returned false and skipped wrapping. Affected most Lazy containers, Scaffold slots, and any composable whose entire body went through composableLambdaInstance(...)
  • Automatic client-literals dependency: Adding debugImplementation("com.github.skydoves.compose.hotswan:client") no longer requires a separate client-literals line. The literal-patch runtime is now an api dependency of client, so HotSwanLiterals is on the consumer's compile classpath automatically. Without this, the pre-compiler would silently skip wrapping every literal at compile time while the IDE still reported "patched" on each save: a perfectly green console with no visible change on the device
  • literalPatching opt-out: New literalPatching: Property<Boolean> flag on the hotSwanCompiler { ... } extension and a matching IDE Settings checkbox, default true in both places. Setting hotSwanCompiler { literalPatching.set(false) } stops the pre-compiler from emitting lookup wrappers around literals; unchecking the IDE setting stops the IDE from sending literal-patch frames to the device. Both knobs are needed to fully disable the feature

1.2.9

  • Multi-module first-class support: Hot reload now works out-of-the-box for the dominant modern Android pattern — Composables in :features:* / :core:* library modules with an app aggregator on top. Previous default silently skipped Compose bytecode transformation inside any com.android.library module, so multi-module setups saw the IDE-side reload succeed but no UI change on the device. New applyHotReloadTransformationToLibraries flag (default true) on the hotSwanCompiler { } extension covers an entire repo from a single :app setting
  • Kotlin Multiplatform shared module support: The new com.android.kotlin.multiplatform.library plugin (KGP 2.x) is now properly recognized. Literal hot-reload wiring now reaches KMP shared modules' androidMain / androidDebug source sets, so primitive value edits in apps like kotlinconf-app, conference-app-2025, and any project where Composables live in a shared module take effect on the next recomposition
  • rememberSaveable ClassCastException fixed: First use of any rememberSaveable {} inside a transformed composable threw a hard ClassCastException because the movable-group wrapper grabbed the wrong argument from the call. The fix locates the composer argument by type instead of by ordinal so other movable-group call sites are unaffected
  • Inner-lambda edits no longer trigger full rebuild: Edits like .background(Color(0xEFC2929A)), swapping a RoundedCornerShape, or any other modifier-chain change inside a Lazy item / Scaffold slot were misclassified as structural and forced a full app rebuild. Direct bytecode comparison confirms these edits change zero method signatures and add zero classes; they are now correctly routed through the in-place reload path and complete in well under a second
  • Reliable recomposition after patch: Composables that read patched values but observe no other Compose state — common in literal edits inside a lazy container — sometimes failed to display the new value on the next frame even though the reload reported success. The literal-patch and body-only fallback paths now drive a stronger invalidation that bypasses the skip path for the next recomposition and reaches SubcomposeLayout subcompositions directly
  • Other: KMP source-set filenames (Foo.android.kt) compile cleanly; Kotlin context(...) parameter composables route through the dispatcher path instead of crashing the build; balloon diagnostics for "0 transformed classes detected" and app-module-mismatch suggestions; stale version constant baked into the client library fixed

1.2.8

  • KMP configuration cache fix: Kotlin Multiplatform projects with org.gradle.configuration-cache=true would silently push stale bytecode to the device, so edits only became visible after navigating away and back. HotSwan now auto-detects KMP projects and disables the Gradle configuration cache for its own invocations only. Pure Android projects and your regular ./gradlew builds are untouched
  • Literal patch subcomposition coverage: Literal-only edits (numeric, string, float values inside composable bodies) inside LazyColumn/LazyRow/Scaffold/LazyVerticalGrid items or any other SubcomposeLayout-based container now reflect on the first frame instead of requiring navigation back-and-forth. The invalidation path now reaches both root compositions and active SubcomposeLayout subcompositions for this safe subset of changes
  • Failed composition recovery restored: Fixed a "first few reloads work, then the screen freezes" regression on Compose 1.8+ apps. The client was reading Recomposer._failedCompositions as kotlin.collections.Set, but it has been a MutableScatterSet (from androidx.collection) since Compose 1.8, so the size check always returned -1 and the surgical reset + Activity.recreate() recovery chain never fired after a transient recompose failure

1.2.7

  • Compose 1.11 LinkBuffer compatibility: Apps using the new linkbuffer SlotTable implementation (ComposeRuntimeFlags.isLinkBufferComposerEnabled = true) no longer crash on hot reload. The client auto-detects which SlotTable backend the running app uses (gapbuffer vs linkbuffer) and adapts reflection and slot-table operations accordingly
  • Zero behavior change for existing users: Compose 1.10 and earlier (plus Compose 1.11 with linkbuffer flag disabled — the default) continue to work identically. The gapbuffer code path is preserved bit-for-bit
  • Wider subcomposition coverage: SubcomposeLayout scanning now also picks up paused prefetched compositions, so lazy item subcompositions are pre-expanded correctly before invalidation

idea-plugin.name: String Resource Finder
idea-plugin.description:
String Resource Finder

Fixes Go to Declaration (Cmd+Click / Ctrl+Click) for Android string resource keys that use dots as separators in strings.xml files.

The Problem

In strings.xml, keys use dots:

name="payment_method.add.whitescreen.body"

But in code (Kotlin/Java/XML layouts), they are referenced with underscores:

R.string.payment_method_add_whitescreen_body

So Cmd+Click on a dotted key in strings.xml finds nothing useful.

What This Plugin Does

  • When you Cmd+Click a string name attribute in strings.xml, it converts dots to underscores
  • Single usage found → navigates directly to the usage
  • Multiple usages found → opens the Find in Files search overlay with the correct R.string.* reference pre-filled
  • No usages found → falls back to default Android Studio behavior

Searches In

  • Kotlin and Java files for R.string.<name>
  • XML layout/menu files for @string/<name>
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.0

  • Migrated to the IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.x toolchain
  • Rebuilt against the 2024.2 platform SDK; now compatible with 2024.2 and all newer IDEs, including 2025.x and 2026.x
  • Updated to Kotlin 2.4 and Java 21
  • Usage search now runs against the PSI index instead of scanning every project file, making Cmd+Click noticeably faster on large projects

1.0.1

  • Removed upper IDE version limit for broader compatibility (supports 2023.1+)

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • Cmd+Click on dotted string resource names in strings.xml to find usages
  • Dot-to-underscore conversion for R.string and @string references
  • Single result: direct navigation; multiple results: Find in Files overlay
  • Fallback to default Android Studio behavior when no usages are found

idea-plugin.name: SharedPrefs & DataStore Explorer
idea-plugin.description:
Browse, inspect, and edit AndroidX DataStore files on connected Android devices directly from Android Studio.

DataStore Explorer provides a convenient tool window for reading and modifying app data stored in Preferences DataStore, Proto DataStore, and SharedPreferences formats — without needing to pull files manually or write debug code.

Features

  • Auto-detect connected ADB devices with real-time tracking
  • Discover debuggable packages from device and Gradle project files
  • Browse Preferences DataStore (.preferences_pb) with typed key/value editing
  • Inspect Proto DataStore (.pb) files with raw wire-format decoding
  • Read and edit SharedPreferences (.xml) files
  • Auto-monitor files for live changes with a configurable polling interval
  • Upload, download, and delete data files on device
  • Root mode for accessing all apps on rooted devices and emulators

Requirements

  • Android SDK with ADB installed
  • A connected device or emulator with a debuggable app (or root access for all apps)

idea-plugin.name: Peek
idea-plugin.description:
Peek is an Android Studio and IntelliJ plugin for inspecting and editing an app's key-value storage: SharedPreferences, Jetpack DataStore (Preferences and Proto), and Multiplatform Settings.

Pick a connected device or emulator and a debuggable app, and Peek reads its stores over adb and renders them as typed, searchable tables, no changes to your app required. Values keep their real types, changes highlight as they happen, and you can edit, add, and delete keys. Add the optional peek-runtime dependency for live mode: instant push updates and edits that apply while the app runs.

idea-plugin.name: Envpilot
idea-plugin.description:
Envpilot keeps your environment variables and secret files in one secure, central place — and this plugin brings them straight into IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, Rider, Android Studio and every other JetBrains IDE.


How it works:

  • Sign in from Tools ▸ Envpilot ▸ Sign In. A WorkOS device-flow login opens in your browser — approve it once and the IDE stays connected.
  • Browse your organizations and projects in the Envpilot tool window (View ▸ Tool Windows ▸ Envpilot).
  • Link any project folder to a project + environment (development, staging or production).
  • Pull decrypted variables into your target .env file and materialize secret files with their correct permissions — manually, or automatically on a sync interval.
  • Protect local secrets with value cloaking, clipboard blocking, drift detection, timed and permission-checked reveals, and an optional Git commit guard.
  • Request variables through the existing approval flow. Project eligibility and environment scope come from Envpilot's role capability registry.
  • Switch accounts without mixing project links or tokens. Sessions stay in the IDE password store.

Secrets stay encrypted server-side (WorkOS Vault), every delivery is audit-logged, and pulls stop before writing if data is incomplete or cannot be decrypted.


Requires an Envpilot account — create one at envpilot.dev.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.9

  • File drift detection runs again; it was registered under an extension point the platform does not have. Cloaking, the copy guard and hover work on Windows.
  • "Delete unchanged pulled files when the IDE closes" is honored, and plugin updates no longer delete synced files. Link state moved out of .idea into the workspace file and existing links are migrated automatically.
  • Variable requests no longer fail on submit. Focus no longer triggers a full pull when auto-sync is off.
  • The Convex connection sends in order, queues calls while offline, re-authenticates before the token expires and shuts down on unload. Sign-in polling can be cancelled and the device code is shown.
  • Secret file paths under .git, .husky, .idea, .vscode or named like an env file are rejected.

0.1.8

  • Error reporting only covers Envpilot's own code. Crashes from the IDE and other plugins are no longer captured.
  • Offline, timeout and expired-session failures stay in idea.log instead of being reported as errors.

0.1.7

  • Expected failures (offline, timeouts, expired sessions) are no longer reported to error tracking.

0.1.6

  • Pulled values are quoted on write, so newlines, hashes and quotes no longer corrupt the env file or escape the editor cloak.
  • Every background scope and global editor hook is tied to the plugin's lifetime; dynamic unload and reload are clean.
  • The tool window refreshes on sign-in, sign-out and every sync. Sync status and the sync lock are per project.
  • The organization tier gate now covers reveal and request actions. Session changes are serialized and a rotated token is never refreshed twice.

0.1.5

  • The plugin now honours the organization tier gate: an owner who disables JetBrains access stops new links and sync cycles, and the tool window says so.

0.1.4

  • Marketplace verifier clean on every supported IDE: no internal API, no scheduled-for-removal and no deprecated platform calls.
  • Sign-in uses the AuthKit device flow: a code in your browser, no loopback port, no admin configuration.
  • Startup runs on the background post-startup extension point, so project opening stays fast.
  • Cleaner tool window tree, Open Dashboard action, and richer settings: cloaking, hover, conflict resolution, auto-unsync and commit guard controls.
  • Switch Account uses a native chooser popup, and gutter markers expose accessible names for screen readers.

0.1.1

  • Token parsing fixed for WorkOS snake_case responses; sign-in now completes after browser approval.

0.1.0

  • Initial public release: link directories, pull variables and secret files, real-time sync, value cloaking, clipboard guard, drift detection, variable requests and the git commit guard.

idea-plugin.name: ADB Controller by Samsad
idea-plugin.description:
ADB Controller by Samsad is a comprehensive, 100% offline Android developer control panel built directly into the Android Studio and IntelliJ IDEA sidebar. It eliminates repetitive terminal typing and provides essential debugging controls, live data inspectors, power simulators, and navigation tools in 1 click.

Whether you are testing Room/SQLite database migrations, editing SharedPreferences on the fly, testing low-battery edge cases, or capturing pixel-perfect screenshots, ADB Controller streamlines your entire mobile development workflow.

✨ Key Features

1. 🗄️ SQLite Database Live Inspector & SQL Query Simulator

  • Live Table Viewer: Select any SQLite database (.db, .sqlite) and view all tables.
  • Inline Cell Editing: Double-click any table cell to update data values live on-device.
  • Insert & Delete Rows: Append new test fixtures or delete existing records in 1 click.
  • SQL Console: Write arbitrary SQL queries (SELECT, UPDATE, INSERT, DELETE, PRAGMA) with keyboard shortcut support (Ctrl/Cmd + Enter).
  • Save & Restart App: Automatically checkpoints SQLite WAL files, pushes changes back to the device, and restarts the app to immediately see UI updates.

2. 📝 Live SharedPreferences XML Editor

  • Browse Preference Files: Dropdown list of all XML preference files in your application.
  • Type-Safe Editing: Edit String, Boolean, Int, Long, and Float values inline.
  • Add & Remove Keys: Add new preference keys or delete existing ones directly from the IDE.
  • Live Sync: Save changes and restart your app to sync in-memory Singletons instantly.

3. 🪫 Battery & Doze Simulator

  • Level Presets: 1-click simulation of 5% (critical), 20% (low), 50% (half), and 100% (full) battery levels.
  • Unplug (Discharge): Sets device battery status to discharging while maintaining USB connection.
  • Reset Battery: Restores battery charging state and percentage to real hardware defaults.
  • Enter/Exit Doze Mode: Force Deep Doze idle state to verify WorkManager jobs, alarms, and background sync.
  • App Standby: Puts your package into standby buckets to test background restrictions.

4. 🕹️ Virtual Hardware Navigation Bar

  • Back (Keycode 4): Dispatches back button event.
  • Home (Keycode 3): Returns to default launcher screen.
  • Recents (Keycode 187): Opens multi-tasking app switcher.
  • Lock / Wake (Keycode 26): Toggles screen power state.
  • Volume +/- (Keycodes 25/24): Adjusts media volume up or down.

5. ⚡ 1-Click App Lifecycle & Storage Controls

  • Restart App: Force-stops and relaunches main launcher activity.
  • Clear App Data: Resets app cache, local storage, and databases via pm clear.
  • Clear & Restart: Resets storage and immediately opens the app in a pristine first-launch state.
  • Force Stop: Instantly terminates all background and foreground processes.
  • Uninstall App: Completely uninstalls the application APK from the device.
  • App Info: Directly opens the Android System Settings page for the app.

6. 🎨 Device Quick Tools

  • Screenshot to Clipboard: Captures full-resolution PNG screenshots straight to your OS clipboard (paste into Slack, Jira, or Figma with Ctrl/Cmd+V).
  • Toggle Dark Mode: Instantly switches between Day and Night themes.
  • Toggle Layout Bounds: Shows/hides visual clip boundaries, margins, and padding boxes.
  • Toggle Animations: Toggles animator durations between 0.0x (fast testing) and 1.0x.

7. 🔗 Deep Link & Broadcast Tester

  • Deep Link Dispatcher: Enter custom URI schemes (e.g. myapp://checkout?id=101) or web URLs to launch target activities.
  • Broadcast Sender: Send custom intents with optional key=value extras to trigger local receivers.

💡 Usage Notes

  • Debuggable Builds: SharedPreferences and Database Inspection features use Android's standard secure run-as permissions. Ensure your app is built with debuggable true.
  • No Root Required: All features work seamlessly on non-rooted physical devices and official Google Play emulators.
  • Wireless Debugging Supported: Full support for USB connections as well as wireless debugging (adb connect <ip>:<port>).
idea-plugin.change-notes:
v1.1.0

  • SQLite Database Live Inspector & SQL Query Simulator: Live table browser, inline cell editing, insert/delete rows, arbitrary SQL query console (Ctrl/Cmd+Enter), and 1-click Save & Restart.
  • Embedded SQLite Engine: Direct WAL checkpointing and host-side SQLite execution supporting Android 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, and 15 without requiring on-device sqlite3 binary.
  • Live SharedPreferences XML Editor: View, add, delete, and modify key-value pairs live on-device with in-memory app sync.
  • Battery & Doze Simulator: Level presets (5%, 20%, 50%, 100%), AC/USB discharge, Doze Mode idle/unidle triggers, and App Standby.
  • Enhanced Device Auto-Discovery: Multi-candidate ADB runner with support for USB and Wireless Debugging.

idea-plugin.description:
5 USD per year - Try it before you buy it


ANSI Highlighter Premium enables the fast rendering of ANSI control-code sequences in log files, regardless their size, from within the text editor of all IntelliJ Platform-based products. The following features are available.

Customizable ANSI colors:

  • Go to Settings | Editor | Colors Scheme | Console Colors
  • Expand 'ANSI Colors'
  • Customize foreground and background colors as needed
  • Press 'Apply'
  • Default foreground can be customized from Settings | Editor | Colors Scheme | Console Colors | Console | Standard Output | Foreground

Customizable 'ANSI Aware' file extensions:

  • Go to Settings | Editor | File Types
  • Under 'Recognized File Types' select 'ANSI Aware'
  • Under 'File name patterns' add your custom 'ANSI Aware' file extensions, *.log is added by default
  • Press 'Apply'

Double display mode:

Use any of the following options to switch between ANSI Highlighter vs Plain modes:

  • Click 'Show Plain Mode' from the banner on top of the editor
  • Switch between 'Plain' and 'ANSI Highlighter' tabs at the bottom
  • Right click on the editor and press 'Switch to Plain / ANSI Highlighter mode'
  • Alternatively place the caret on the editor and use the keyboard shortcut 'ctrl meta A' (customizable from Settings | Keymap | Plugins | ANSI Highlighter Premium)

Optional extended ANSI viewer:

  • Enable/disable under Settings | Editor | ANSI Highlighter | Use the extended ANSI viewer for smaller files
  • Activates 'Paste as ANSI' and line numbers gutter within the IDE file size limit
  • The status bar shows the displayed line/column and selection size, plus the source file's line endings, encoding, and indentation settings. Click the position to go to a line.
  • The fast restricted ANSI viewer continues to be used when extended viewer is disabled, or file size exceeds IDE file size limit.
  • Keep the option disabled for continuously growing logs: substantial growth can cause memory overflow / IDE errors.
  • Disabled by default: user should be aware of growing files risk before they optin

Copy/Paste as ANSI:

  • Select highlighted text in ANSI Highlighter mode and activate 'Copy as ANSI' from the context menu.
  • Use 'Paste as ANSI' to paste, save the target file and trigger ANSI code detection.
  • 'Paste as ANSI' under ANSI Highlight mode offers optional line breaks before and after the pasted text.
  • Shortcuts can be assigned under Settings | Keymap | Plugins | ANSI Highlighter Premium.
  • Copied fragment starts and ends with a reset.
  • ANSI Highlight mode restores trailing text styles after reset, plain mode doesn't.
  • 'Paste as ANSI' is available only within the IDE file size limit.
  • 'Paste as ANSI' is not available under ANSI Highlight mode when extended ANSI viewer is disabled.
  • Undo/Redo is supported under ANSI Highlight mode when extended ANSI viewer is enabled.
  • Normal Copy/Paste continues to copy/paste plain text.

Supported ANSI codes:

  • Reset code (0)
  • Bold code (1)
  • Dim / faint code (2)
  • Italic code (3)
  • Single Underline code (4)
  • All text foreground color codes (30-37)
  • All text high intensity foreground color codes (90-97)
  • All text background color codes (40-47)
  • All text high intensity background color codes (100-107)

Hyperlinks:

  • Clickable JVM stack trace locations
  • Clickable URL/URI links
  • Clickable absolute local file paths
  • Clickable file paths with line numbers when available

Soft Wrap:

  • Go to Settings | Editor | General | Console
  • Toggle 'Use soft wraps in console'
  • To force soft wrap when line length is too large go to Settings | Advanced Settings
  • Customize 'Force soft wrap in documents with lines larger than...'

idea-plugin.name: GapStyle Color Scheme
idea-plugin.description:
Being Productive Beyond Your Status Quo.

The world-first* productivity-oriented color scheme for intelliJ, VSCode to fill the gap between programming languages and human.


Uniqueness

GapStyle is a world-first* productivity-oriented color scheme that each supported language is tailored with rich colors while maintaining a comfortable contrast to help developers boost reading and writing speed in different programming languages.

GapStyle is designed based on some key colors of the 'Darcula' and 'Monokai' color schemes.

Each supported language is tailored and carefully tuned with its rationale.

  • Objective 1: Optimize languages' color schemes to boost productivity on reading/writing code (Especially the language your are not familiar)
  • Objective 2: Quickly learn similar syntax with a universal designed color across different languages.
  • Supported Languages: Kotlin, Java, Swift, Dart, Rust, Scala, Javascript, Typescript, Go, Python, R, Android Logcat, Android Native (C / C++), Objective-C, SQL, HTML, CSS, PHP, Ruby, Erlang, Elixir

* 'world-first' color scheme uses affinitive color platte design to boost developers' productivity by using similar colors to represent semantically similar syntax, i.e. class, abstract class, and interface in Java.

idea-plugin.name: CobaltM Color Scheme
idea-plugin.description:
A colourful scheme based on Cobalt, reorganised by semantic meanings of language features.

Different colours are used for different semantic items:

yellow: generic identifiers
orange: keywords (bold) and special identifiers (normal)
red: constants
pink: variables (grey for parameters)
purple: functions
teal: classes (light cyan for type parameters)
light green: predefined identifiers
light yellow: namespaces

Different font styles are used for modifiers:

For objects:
bold: global
italic: member
bold italic: static member

For classes:
bold: normal classes
italic: interfaces
non-bold: type aliases

idea-plugin.name: Painless Language Syntax Highlighting
idea-plugin.description:
Painless Language Syntax Highlighting provides syntax highlighting for Elasticsearch's Painless scripting language in IntelliJ-based IDEs.

Features

  • Syntax highlighting for .painless files
  • Keyword highlighting (if, else, for, while, return, try, catch, etc.)
  • Type highlighting (def, int, long, boolean, String, etc.)
  • Literal highlighting (strings, numbers, booleans, regex patterns)
  • Operator highlighting (including Painless-specific operators like ?., ?:, =~, ==~)
  • Comment support (// and /* */)
  • Brace matching
  • Comment toggling (Cmd/Ctrl + /)

Supported Syntax

Based on the official Elasticsearch Painless ANTLR grammar:

  • Keywords: if, else, while, do, for, in, continue, break, return, new, try, catch, throw, this, instanceof
  • Types: boolean, byte, short, char, int, long, float, double, def, void
  • Operators: All arithmetic, comparison, logical, bitwise, and assignment operators, plus Painless-specific ?. (null-safe), ?: (elvis), -> (lambda), :: (method reference), =~/==~ (regex match)
  • Literals: Strings (single/double quoted), numbers (decimal, hex, octal), booleans, null, regex patterns
idea-plugin.change-notes:

Changed

idea-plugin.name: Yaml inline annotate
idea-plugin.description:
YAML Inline Annotate improves editing of OpenAPI YAML schemas in IntelliJ-based IDEs.

The plugin displays bidirectional inline hints between enum values and their corresponding x-enum-varnames, making generated constant names visible directly in the editor without switching to source code or documentation.

It can also detect Cyrillic characters in places intended for code identifiers:

  • enum keys declared in x-enum-varnames, or directly in enum when x-enum-varnames is absent;
  • DTO names declared directly under components.schemas;
  • DTO property names declared under properties, including inline and nested schemas.

When x-enum-varnames is present, regular enum values are treated as display values and may contain Cyrillic characters.

Each invalid character is highlighted individually with a colored wave underline and an explanatory tooltip. Validation is applied only to YAML documents containing a top-level openapi key, so unrelated YAML files are not affected.

Inline hint colors, validation color, and all validation locations can be configured independently in Settings | YAML Annotate.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Version 1.2.3

  • Removed deprecated IntelliJ Platform API usage when refreshing code analysis after settings changes.
  • Kept immediate analysis refresh compatible with IntelliJ Platform 2023.3 and newer.

idea-plugin.name: Atlin Language Support
idea-plugin.description:
Full language support for the Atlin (.atlin) key-value data format inside JetBrains IDEs (PhpStorm, IntelliJ IDEA, and others).

Atlin is a minimal, human-friendly data format for key-value content.
Learn more: Atlin Format — Official Article
Source code: GitHub Repository

Features

  • Syntax Highlighting — Keys, values, and comments are highlighted with distinct colors.
  • Separator Highlighting — Blank lines before keys get a background color to visually separate entries.
  • Multiline Values — Values spanning multiple lines are fully supported, including Emoji.
  • Configurable Key Prefix — Default prefix is @, but you can change it to any character (e.g. |) via Settings.
  • Code Folding — Multiline values can be folded and unfolded in the editor.
  • Autocomplete — Suggests existing keys from the current file while typing.
  • Validation — Shows an error for empty key names and a warning when a key does not start with the configured prefix.
  • Customizable Colors — All highlighting colors are configurable via Settings → Editor → Color Scheme → Atlin.
  • Bundled Color Schemes — Includes default schemes for both light and Darcula themes.

Atlin Format Overview

        # This is a comment

        @name
        Hdi Akbarzadeh

        @bio
        A software developer.
        Loves clean code.

        @skills
        PHP, Java, JavaScript

Configuration

Go to Settings → Editor → Atlin to change the key prefix character.
Go to Settings → Editor → Color Scheme → Atlin to customize all highlight colors.

idea-plugin.name: Window Accent
idea-plugin.description:
Window Accent

Window Accent helps you distinguish between multiple JetBrains IDE windows with visual cues.

The Challenge 🤔

When you have multiple IDE windows open, it can be difficult to quickly identify which one is which, especially if they are all running the same project or have similar titles.

The Solution ✨

Window Accent allows you to apply different accents to each IDE window, making it easier to visually differentiate them at a glance.

Configuration ⚙️

Some configuration is available through the tool window as well as the settings. Please refer to screenshots etc. for insights into the features and configuration options.

Related Plugins 📚

Although similar to the following plugins, Window Accent is a separate implementation, created independently:

  • Project Color
  • Colorized Project

Source Code & Contributions 🛠️

The source code for Window Accent is available on GitHub. Feedback is welcome. Requests / Bugs can be modeled as an Issue on Github

AI Agents were crucial to the speed of development, however all code is owned by the commit author.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.2.0

Added

  • Go to definition: Ctrl/Cmd+click (or Go to Declaration) on a macro name jumps to its def declaration, searching every .fj file in the project. The clicked dotted segment is used alone, so xor in hex.xor finds def xor; multiple matches open the usual navigation popup.

Fixed

  • Namespace-relative macro calls that start with leading dots — .zero, ..foo, .a.b — are now highlighted as macro calls (previously a leading dot fell back to a plain identifier colour), as are calls inside a rep(...) clause (e.g. rep(n, i) bit.exact_xor …). A lone . and names with consecutive dots after a segment are no longer mis-coloured as calls.

idea-plugin.name: Kwezal Vibrant Color Scheme
idea-plugin.description:
Kwezal Vibrant Color Scheme

The color scheme for JetBrains IDEs, based on the Islands Dark scheme and the Kwezal Essential Color Palette.

Supported languages and formats

  • Angular Template
  • CSS
  • CSV
  • Dart
  • Groovy
  • HTML
  • Java
  • JavaScript
  • JPA, Hibernate QL
  • JSON
  • Kotlin
  • Markdown
  • Properties
  • Python
  • RegExp
  • Rust
  • Sass/SCSS
  • Shell Script
  • SQL
  • TOML
  • TypeScript
  • XML
  • YAML

Design

This color scheme is an implementation of the Kwezal Essential Color Palette for syntax highlighting.

Apart from the use of a specific color palette, the Kwezal Vibrant Color Scheme was designed according to the following ideas:

  • The color scheme should not only be visually appealing but also increase productivity.
  • As much information as possible should be conveyed by as few colors as possible.
  • Similar language constructs (e.g., classes, structs, interfaces, traits) should have similar colors.
  • Errors and warnings should be annoying but not glaring.
  • Unsafe and error-prone code (e.g., unresolvable references) should be as conspicuous as warnings or errors.
  • Identifiers under the caret should be as eye-catching as search results.
  • Coloring should be consistent across all languages.

idea-plugin.name: GlowStick MHL
idea-plugin.description:
GlowStick MHL

Frame your IDE with color for instant visual identification of projects.

GlowStick is visual expansion plugin for IntelliJ IDEA based IDEs that helps you visually distinct each IDE window per project which allows instant visual identification and navigation across your projects.

Features:

  • Draws colorful frame around the IDE window for opened project,
  • Each project gets its own color automatically, based on project name,
  • Color is freely pickable per-project,
  • Visuals can be customized on per-project basis,
  • Configurable frame profile with segments and opacity gradients,

Usage:

There is nothing to set up. Every project starts with a color derived from its name, so your windows are already telling themselves apart.

To choose the color yourself, go to Settings → Appearance & Behavior → GlowStick MHL, untick Auto next to Color and pick whatever you like. Should two projects happen to share the same automatic color, this is how you separate them.

Aside from using knobs and sliders to tweak your frame shape, you can also drag the handles on the preview idea.

Settings

You can tweak plugin settings by going to Settings → Appearance & Behavior → GlowStick Frame.

idea-plugin.name: wxBackgroundPro
idea-plugin.description:
Set IDE Background from Local or Cloud Storage

Personalize your IntelliJ IDEA editor with background images from local folders or cloud object storage — with keyboard shortcuts, auto-switch, and timed rotation.

Features

  • Local Folder — scan a directory for images and use them as background
  • Cloud Object Storage — Huawei Cloud OBS / AWS S3 / Alibaba Cloud OSS / Tencent Cloud COS / MinIO
  • Zero Runtime Dependencies — all cloud access via JDK HttpClient, no third-party SDKs
  • Switch Modes — sequential or random
  • Keyboard Shortcuts — next/previous image (customizable in Settings | Keymap)
  • Timed Auto-Switch — set interval in seconds, minutes, or hours
  • Opacity & Fill Style — control transparency and image placement (center/stretch/tile/fit)
  • Secure Credentials — cloud credentials encrypted via IDE PasswordSafe
  • Image Cache — local caching with ETag-based incremental update

Cloud Providers

Huawei Cloud OBS · AWS S3 · Alibaba Cloud OSS · Tencent Cloud COS · MinIO

Getting Started

  1. Go to Settings → Tools → wxBackgroundPro
  2. Select image source (Local Folder / Cloud Object Storage)
  3. Configure source details and switch mode
  4. Use shortcuts or enable auto-switch


本地或云端图片设为 IDE 背景

将本地文件夹或对象存储中的图片设为 IntelliJ IDEA 编辑器背景， 支持快捷键切换、顺序/随机切换和定时轮换。

功能特性

  • 本地文件夹 — 扫描目录中的图片用作背景
  • 云端对象存储 — 华为云 OBS / AWS S3 / 阿里云 OSS / 腾讯云 COS / MinIO
  • 零运行时依赖 — 使用 JDK HttpClient 直连云服务，无第三方 SDK
  • 切换模式 — 顺序切换 / 随机切换
  • 快捷键 — 上一张/下一张（可在 Settings | Keymap 中自定义）
  • 定时自动切换 — 支持秒/分/小时级别间隔
  • 透明度与填充 — 调节不透明度及图片放置方式（居中/拉伸/平铺/适应）
  • 凭证安全 — 云端凭证通过 IDE PasswordSafe 加密存储
  • 图片缓存 — 本地缓存，基于 ETag 增量更新

支持云平台

华为云 OBS · AWS S3 · 阿里云 OSS · 腾讯云 COS · MinIO

快速开始

idea-plugin.name: Get Off Color Scheme Font
idea-plugin.description:
Does Use color scheme font instead of the default keep turning itself back on? This plugin keeps it off. No settings, no actions, no tool window: install it and forget about it.

What it does:

  • Turns off Use color scheme font instead of the default (Settings | Editor | Color Scheme | Color Scheme Font) on the active color scheme and on every editable scheme, so the editor always uses the font from Settings | Editor | Font.
  • Reapplies it the moment something turns it back on: switching the color scheme or the theme, applying changes in Settings, a scheme reloaded by Backup and Sync, or a Ctrl+Mouse Wheel zoom in All editors mode — which is what silently writes a font into the scheme.
  • Never loses your font size. When the IDE writes a size into the active scheme (that is what the zoom does), the plugin moves it to Settings | Editor | Font before turning the option off. Zoom works as usual. Font family, line spacing and ligatures always come from Settings | Editor | Font: that is what the option being off means.
  • Also runs when the IDE starts, when a project opens, and right after installing the plugin with the IDE already open.
  • Refreshes the open editors right away. The IDE saves the corrected scheme on its own.

No cost. It reacts to events — no timers, no polling — and each check is a handful of boolean reads.

Free. No trial, no license, no account: install it and forget about it.

  • La reaplica apenas algo la vuelve a encender: cambiar de esquema o de tema, aplicar cambios en Settings, un esquema recargado por Backup and Sync, o un zoom con Ctrl+rueda en modo All editors, que es lo que escribe una fuente en el esquema sin avisar.
  • Nunca pierde tu tamaño de fuente. Cuando el IDE escribe un tamaño en el esquema activo (eso es lo que hace el zoom), el plugin lo traslada a Settings | Editor | Font antes de apagar la opción. El zoom funciona como siempre. La familia, el interlineado y las ligaduras salen siempre de Settings | Editor | Font: eso es lo que significa tener la opción apagada.
  • También corre al iniciar el IDE, al abrir un proyecto y apenas se instala el plugin con el IDE ya abierto.
  • Refresca en el momento los editores abiertos. El IDE guarda solo el esquema corregido.

Sin costo. Reacciona a eventos, sin timers ni polling, y cada chequeo son un puñado de lecturas booleanas.

Gratis. Sin período de prueba, sin licencia, sin cuenta: instalalo y olvidate.

O zoom funciona como sempre. A família, o espaçamento entre linhas e as ligaturas vêm sempre de Settings | Editor | Font: é isso que significa ter a opção desligada.

idea-plugin.name: Selectrum
idea-plugin.description:
Selectrum is a JetBrains plugin that automatically switches the IDE's UI theme and editor color scheme based on the time of day. It reads a local YAML configuration file to schedule theme transitions and updates the IDE appearance in the background.

Installation

  1. Open your JetBrains IDE.
  2. Navigate to Settings/Preferences > Plugins > Marketplace.
  3. Search for Selectrum.
  4. Click Install and restart the IDE if prompted.

Configuration

To set up your daily schedule, go to Tools → Selectrum → Open Configuration from the main menu at the very top of the IDE window. This will open the selectrum.yaml configuration file.

Configuration Format

The configuration uses a simple YAML format. Each entry under schedule is an hour in 24h format (H:mm or HH:mm). The last entry whose hour has passed will determine the active theme.

# Selectrum — Theme Schedule Configuration

schedule:
  # At 8:00 AM, apply the 'IntelliJ Light' theme
  08:00:
    theme: IntelliJ Light
    
  # At 6:00 PM, apply the 'Darcula' theme and explicitly use the 'Monokai' editor scheme
  18:00:
    theme: Darcula
    editor: Monokai

Fields:

  • theme (required): The exact name of an installed IDE theme. (Find available themes in Settings → Appearance & Behavior → Appearance → Theme)
  • editor (optional): The name of an editor color scheme. If omitted, Selectrum will try to use the scheme that matches the theme name. (Find available editors in Settings → Editor → Color Scheme)

Usage

Once your schedule is configured and saved, Selectrum takes care of the rest automatically.

If you temporarily need to disable automatic switching, click the Selectrum widget in the bottom-right status bar of your IDE and uncheck Theme Switching. Click it again to resume your schedule.

idea-plugin.name: Folder Text Color
idea-plugin.description:
Color the text of folder names in the Project tool window, so the parts of a large project you care about stand out at a glance.

Unlike File Colors and scope-based highlighting, which tint the whole row background, this plugin changes only the color of the folder name. The tree stays clean and readable in both light and dark themes.

How to use

Right-click one or more folders in the Project view → Folder Text Color, then pick:

  • one of nine preset colors, chosen to read well on light and dark themes;
  • Custom… to pick any color from the color picker;
  • Clear to restore the default color.

Details

  • A color follows its folder when the folder is renamed or moved inside the IDE, and is dropped when the folder is deleted.
  • On module roots only the name is recolored; hints such as [module] keep their style.
  • Colors are stored per project in .idea/workspace.xml, so they are personal and never end up in version control.
  • Works in every IntelliJ-based IDE: PyCharm, IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, GoLand, and others.
idea-plugin.change-notes: • 1.0.0 — First release: preset and custom folder text colors, rename/move tracking.

idea-plugin.name: Material Theme UI
idea-plugin.description:
Material Theme UI Plugin

Material Design Experience for JetBrains IDEs

Material Theme UI is a plugin for JetBrains IDE (IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, Android Studio and so on) that changes the original appearance to a Material Design look and feel, all the while providing an extensive set of options to configure your IDE the way YOU want.

Originally inspired by the Material Theme for Sublime Text, this plugin offers a panoply of settings to tweak up the IDEs the way you want. Aside for its impressive palette of themes, it also offers:

  • Beautiful color schemes supporting a vast majority of languages
  • Replacement of all icons with colorful Material Design icons (from a separate plugin)
  • Customization of most of the IDE's controls and components
  • A lot of options, such as accent colors, padded menus, custom indent, arrow styles and such
  • Some useful tweaks, such as Project View Decorators, Language Additions, etc...

And it gets updated pretty frequently!


Take a look at the beautiful website for more information and for questions and answers.


Donate

This theme is backed up by OpenCollective. If you like this plugin, don't hesitate to give it a star or donate via Paypal or OpenCollective
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Features

  • New Themes!
    • Winter Is Coming
    • Shades of Purple
    • Noctis
  • Redesign of the Omni and Cobalt2 themes to improve their color schemes and overall look.
  • Custom Theme Colors: You can now edit in-place the theme colors of any theme
    • Inside "Current Theme" settings
    • Edit any property and it will persist for this specific theme
    • Select a color among the current theme's colors or pick a new one.
    • Search for a specific property or color
    • Reset a property or all properties to their defaults.
    • Note: This feature is only available for Premium and Custom Theme license owners.
    • Note: Any properties listed in the Theme Ignores will be ignored, no matter what color you give it.

Fixes

  • Fix Theme Color Overrides being silently overwritten by other subsystems (contrast, islands, compact mode, etc.) during theme activation.
  • Fix the Ctrl-Click behavior setting itself even after removing the shortcut from the keymap.

idea-plugin.name: Espresso Light Theme
idea-plugin.description:
A warm light theme for IntelliJ IDEA and the other JetBrains IDEs: cream surfaces, a pink accent and a soft green syntax family.

The plugin ships a UI theme together with a matching editor colour scheme, including dedicated highlighting for Dart, Go, JavaScript, CSS and SASS, HTML and XML, YAML, Bash and .gitignore.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Released together: 1.4.1 was prepared but never published, so everything below ships in this version.

Added

  • New UI coverage (IDEA 2022.3 and newer): MainToolbar, MainMenu, RunWidget, Tag, Counter, OnePixelDivider, TableHeader and DefaultTabs. The theme described 38 components and now describes 46; on any recent IDE those surfaces previously fell back to platform defaults. Key names come from the platform's own expUI_light.theme.json.
  • tools/check_theme.py, run in CI: it rejects invalid colour values, palette names that resolve to nothing, a selection painted in its own background colour, a tab underline the colour of its tab, borders the colour of the background, a focused selection weaker than an unfocused one, and any editor-scheme colour below 1.5:1.
  • 2019.1.4 in the plugin verifier list — the oldest release pluginSinceBuild claims, and until now never actually tested.

Fixed

  • Focused selection was fainter than unfocused selection in lists and tables: List read 1.11:1 focused against 1.24:1 unfocused, Table 1.03:1 against 1.24:1. Focused selection is now the deeper cream the menus use, unfocused the lighter one.
  • Selected labels in lists and tables were hard to read at 3.21:1 and 2.72:1; they now sit at 5.02:1.
  • Unfocused tree selection was pure white on a #f5f5f5 tree.
  • Menu separators were white on a cream menu.

Changed

  • Migrated from the Gradle IntelliJ Plugin 1.8.0 to the IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.18.1, which is the maintained one. The old plugin only worked on Gradle 7: it breaks on Gradle 8 (ArchivePublishArtifact) and on Gradle 9 (JavaPluginConvention).
  • Gradle 7.5.1 to 9.7.1, and the build now targets IntelliJ Platform 2025.2.6 instead of 2021.3.3. CI runs on Java 21, which build 252 requires.
  • buildSearchableOptions is off: a colour theme has no searchable settings, and building them starts a full IDE.
  • Plugin signing is now skipped by the platform plugin itself when no certificate is configured, so the local onlyIf guard added in 1.4.1 is gone.
  • Dropped Qodana. It analyses source code, and this project has none.

Removed

  • pluginUntilBuild and platformPlugins properties, both unused: until-build is now unset directly in the build script, and the theme depends on no plugins.

idea-plugin.name: Helsing
idea-plugin.description:
Dark color theme for working under the sunlight. It is designed to be visible even in enormously bright environment. Here are some tips for working on plain air.
  1. Wear dark. Your screen will reflect your bright clothes. Even a matte display won't help if the sun shines on your white T-shirt.
  2. Try to find a shadow. But try to not use trees. A lot of trees produce tiny drops of a resin. They are hard to clean from your screen.
  3. Set the brightness level to the maximum.
  4. Have a cleaning cloth with you. A dust is very distracting in the sunlight.

idea-plugin.name: Monokai Pro
idea-plugin.description:
Monokai Pro

Monokai Pro is a color scheme, customized user interface theme and icon pack for JetBrains IDEs. It has been designed with beautiful functionality in mind. Carefully selected shades of colors are the foundation of an uncompromising, non-distractive user interface.

Monokai Pro is designed by the same author of the original Monokai color scheme, Wimer Hazenberg. Back in 2006 he created the original Monokai colors. Since then, Monokai has been ported to every code editor on the planet and is used by millions of developers every day.

Licensing options

Monokai Pro is available under two licensing models:

  • Freemium: Free to use with occasional reminders to register, with an optional monthly subscription that removes the reminder pop-ups.
  • Lifetime License: A one-time purchase that unlocks all features for all JetBrains IDEs, removes pop-ups, and supports ongoing development.

Color filters

Monokai Pro comes with a set of color filters to suit your mood. Monokai Pro also offers official light versions that are perfect for brighter environments.

Icons

The icons of Monokai Pro have all been created from scratch to ensure they are easily recognizable on small sizes in the side bar. They are designed to help you quickly find the right files in your project. The icon shapes align perfectly to the pixel grid so the icons always stay sharp.

Customization settings

Monokai Pro for JetBrains IDEs offers a few additional settings to further customize your Monokai Pro experience. You can choose between monochrome or colorful icons, and can turn your IDE into a minimal UI experience that offers an even more calm view.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
v0.3

Added support for the new ui (which is still in beta). You can now select the 'naysayer88 (exp ui)' theme and editor scheme as well if you are using the new ui

Please note that there are a ton of differences in what the old UI has and what this new UI permits you to customize

So due to that the exp ui theme looks way different than what the legacy theme looks like, you'll immediately notice the toolbars for example don't fill in with the tan color. Things like this are not my choice and are a reflection of the new UI customization properties

So you may or may not like it, that's ok, but change is hard and the new ui is a drastic change if you're coming from the old UI

A ton of work has gone into supporting this new UI, even down to customizing the git ref labels, but a lot of work is needed to support it still, specifically with icons, due to how they changed some things, especially considering how difficult it is to view all the components possible in all the different combinations they exist so consider this version a 'working draft'. It's enough to feel complete but due to all the changes it's hard to catch everything

So please bring things to my attention if you think it should look different based on your experiences in a github issue
