About

Burnt is a dark theme for JetBrains IDEs (2019.1+) with the right visual clues to assist you in your long coding journeys. The accompanying color scheme features a rich, vibrant palette, carefully tuned to help you stay focused and productive.

Why the Burnt theme?

Because other dark themes are not dark or good enouhg for my taste. This is a really dark theme, crafted with great attention to the detail, and trying to cover the whole IDE to provide a comprehensive coding experience. It's main purpose is to let you focus on what matters: the code.

idea-plugin.name: Espresso Lightgram
idea-plugin.description:
Espresso Lightgram is a Full Theme plugin (UI + Editor color Scheme) It fusions 2 wonderful things I love:
  • An adapted version of the UI theme "Espresso Light"
    (thanks Rasarts, I fixed/corrected 2 colors).
  • An adapted version of the editor color scheme "Gruvbox Light Medium"
    (thanks Vincent Parizet, I enhanced 3 or 4 colors).


A couple images of this "theme fusion"!

The name "Espresso Lightgram" is because this plugin
is based on Espresso Light for the UI,
and there is also a HUGE vintage/ig vibe in those colors.

I really love this combination of light schemes.

I don't claim to be author nor have any copyright of/over the aforementioned plugins/themes.
I just took what I love from both
and fixed the things that I found MOST annoying for me.


In Espresso Light, when you hover a menu element, the shortcut key (aka "accelerator")
can't be read cause font color of the hovered menu element is white and the elem's bg is beige.
I've chosen to use 2 beautiful tones of fucksia that were in the theme itself.

Important: The fact that I fusioned a UI theme and a Color Scheme plugin is not casual.
When you want to set a UI and a Color Scheme that is not associated with that UI theme,
you have to set the UI first in Settings -> Appearance, then OK the dialog,
then open the Settings again, go to Editor -> Color Scheme, then set it, then hit apply WITH CARE
because you're gonna get asked if you wanna turn the entire UI with the same darkness as the Color Scheme
(hence with the potential risk of accidentally rollbacking the UI setting we've just set earlier!)

So I decided to RTFM and dive into this awesome experience of fine tuning my IDE's aesthetics.
After all... I stare at it LOTS of time per day. I better LOVE how it looks!

Enjoy!

idea-plugin.description:
Adds Visual Studio Code styled Bright and Sheen color theme to IntelliJ

Notable features:

Theme is specifically created to work well with Java and Spring projects. Makes the code readability better and faster productivity.



To install:

  • Go to Settings | Plugins, find the theme plugin and install it
  • Restart the IDE
  • Go to Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Appearance and select Bright and Shine in the Theme dropdown
  • Or to select only an editor scheme go to Settings | Editor | Color Scheme and select Bright and Shine in the Scheme dropdown

idea-plugin.name: Noctumsempra's Color MEGAPACK
idea-plugin.description:
The MEGAPACK IS BACK !!!

This is a Super MEGAPACK compound by themes & colorschemes from different sources and also some editing touches by myself!

* It features the famous theme pack Rainglow Color Schemes by Dayle Rees, but with NO CUSTOM FONT properties set by default!
* So every color scheme in this Rainglow pack will use your IDE's default font face/size.

* NO more having to UNCHECK manually the "Use color scheme font instead of the default" anymore!
* Console Font family automatically taken from IDE's default font.
* Console Font line-spacing to 1.0 by default for compact consoles.

NEW #1!!! Added ALL Themes and Schemes from "The DOKI Theme" (also inherits global font!)
NEW #2!!! Upgraded ALL Themes and Schemes from "The DOKI Theme" (also added the new ones!)
NEW #3!!! And all DOKI themes WORK in the modern versions of the IDE!!!
NEW #4!!! Added MyGruvbox theme and its corresponding color scheme


If you think this is worth, I have a PayPal profile for donations (to support present and future developments):
https://www.paypal.me/lcom86

  • Rainglow Color Schemes by Dayle Rees
  • UI theme from "Nescode Espresso" by Noctumsempra (myself) inspired in Codely Dark
  • All Themes & Schemes from "The Doki Theme" by Unthrottled
  • My Gruvbox by xiaopihai7256

idea-plugin.name: Glowing Darcula
idea-plugin.description:
Adding a high contrast theme based on the iconic Darcula theme from JetBrains.

The Glowing Darcula Theme is excellent for sunny days when working outside or close to a window. Carefully selected bright colors work great with dimmed backgrounds. The theme provides a smaller contrast between the dark mode editor and other light windows outside the IDE. Thoroughly implemented, with attention to detail, it provides a stable addition to JetBrains IDE. In addition to improving almost every single colour, Glowing Darcula brings beautiful blue accents to the Editor Tabs, Progress Bar and Buttons.

idea-plugin.name: Catppuccin Theme
idea-plugin.description:
Soothing pastel theme for JetBrains IDEs

Catppuccin is a community-driven pastel theme that aims to be the middle ground between low and high contrast themes. It consists of 4 soothing warm palettes with 26 eye-candy colors each, perfect for coding, designing, and much more!

Design Philosophy

  • Colorful is better than colorless: the colorfulness of something contributes to the distinction amongst the parts of that something, making it marginally easier to understand how things are structured.
  • There should be balance: not too dull, not too bright. Suitability under various light conditions is a must.
  • Harmony is superior to dissonance: vivacious colors must complement each other.

Usage

There are 4 lovely flavours for you to choose from: Latte, Frappé, Macchiato and Mocha.

User Interface

  • Head to Settings → Appearance & Behaviour → Appearance
  • Pick your favourite flavour
  • (Optional) Restart your IDE

Code Editor

  • Head to Settings → Editor → Color Scheme
  • Pick your favourite flavour
  • (Optional) Restart your IDE

Icon Pack

We have created an icon pack to compliment this theme! Search the marketplace for "**Catppuccin Icons**" to install it.

Help

For further help, see also:
  • GitHub Repository
  • Issue Tracker

Copyright © 2021-present Catppuccin Org

LICENSE: MIT

idea-plugin.name: Skol - Calm Semantic Themes
idea-plugin.description:
Calm by default. Clear when it matters.

Skol is a family of six semantic themes for JetBrains IDEs, designed for developers who spend long sessions in code, diffs, terminals, and reviews. The interface stays quiet while the states that matter remain easy to scan.

Start your 30-day free trial →

Skol costs $2/month or $20/year — best value, save two months.

One color language across your whole IDE

  • Teal communicates additions, success, and healthy states.
  • Blue communicates focus, modification, and active work.
  • Rose communicates deletion, failure, and critical states.
  • Amber communicates warnings, conflicts, and attention.
  • Violet communicates review, merge, and collaboration.

Syntax, project trees, selections, diagnostics, diffs, terminal colors, and recurring IDE surfaces all use that same language. Meaning never depends on color alone: outlines, gutters, icon shapes, and local emphasis reinforce the important states.

Six coordinated moods

ThemeRoleBest forAppearance
Norrskenaurora glowBalanced everyday developmentdark
Morkdeep calmLong, distraction-free coding sessionsdark
Skyggesoft contrastA gentler dark workspacedark
Blatimefocused blueFocused implementation workdark
Ettersynreview modeReviews, refactoring, and change-heavy workdark
Dagrdaylight clarityBright rooms and daytime worklight

More than an editor color scheme

  • Readable side-by-side diffs with quiet line fills and clear local cues.
  • Semantic terminal colors whose bright variants keep the same meaning.
  • Polished Island UI surfaces, project trees, controls, and notifications.
  • One compact Skol Appearance controller for theme, accent, project frame, matching editor colors, and optional Skol Rune icons.
  • A reversible setup: native JetBrains icons remain the default and one action restores Skol's appearance defaults.

If Skol makes your editor easier to live in, a short Marketplace review helps other developers discover it.

Documentation · Support · License
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Added a compact Skol Appearance controller for choosing the theme, palette-aware accent, project frame, matching editor colors, and optional Skol Rune icons from one place.

Changed

  • Refined recurring IDE surfaces, editor states, terminal colors, and diffs across all six themes for a calmer, more consistent working environment.
  • Distinguished Mork’s charcoal surfaces from Blatime’s blue palette.
  • Strengthened Ettersyn diffs while preserving readable code syntax.
  • Synchronized generated IDE and editor colors with the shared palettes.
  • Increased editor line spacing and refreshed all six theme previews.

idea-plugin.name: Solarized Chandrian Themes
idea-plugin.description:
Adds Solarized Black, Dark, and Light Chandrian color themes.
Derived from 4lex4's Intellij Solarized themes for Intellij: https://github.com/4lex4/intellij-platform-solarized and from narenranjit's VSCode Theme Chandrian: https://github.com/narenranjit/chandrian-theme

Notable features:
  • High quality and consistent both the UI and editor schemes with an adaptation of minor colors (for the supported IDE version) avoiding any usage of Default or Darcula colors
  • Usage of inheritance mechanism to achieve unified look and feel between various languages (so, for example, syntax highlighting for such statically typed languages as Java, Kotlin, C#, Go or C++ and so on is as similar as possible and the same for the other kinds of languages)


To install:
  1. Go to Settings | Plugins, find the theme plugin and install it
  2. Restart the IDE
  3. Go to Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Appearance and select Solarized Light Chandrian or Solarized Dark Chandrian or Solarized Black Chandrian in the Theme dropdown
    • Or to select only an editor scheme go to Settings | Editor | Color Scheme and select Solarized Light Chandrian or Solarized Dark Chandrian or Solarized Black Chandrian in the Scheme dropdown

A dark green UI theme for IntelliJ IDE provides a stylish and visually soothing environment for coding. The theme's deep green color scheme can help reduce eye strain and improve contrast, making it easier to read code for long periods of time.

Green is a particularly important color for human eye perception because it falls in the middle of the visible light spectrum, meaning our eyes can easily detect it. In the design of the theme, there is an intentional attempt to strike a balance between retro-looking greens reminiscent of old computers and modern UI elements that highlight important parts of the code and IDE. This balance is achieved through the use of carefully chosen shades of green, which give a nod to the past while also providing a modern and functional look and feel while staying simple and minimalistic.

Currently, theme is in experimental, "work in progress" stage.

idea-plugin.name: Fluorescent
idea-plugin.description:
A vibrant, high-contrast editor color scheme featuring bold syntax highlighting optimized for readability and visual distinction.

Designed for dark themes — Pair Fluorescent with your preferred dark UI theme (Islands Dark, Darcula, or similar). Fluorescent focuses on code highlighting while respecting your UI preferences. Not recommended for light themes.

Supported Languages

  • Scala (immutable collections, lazy vals, semicolons)
  • Python (decorators, f-strings, built-ins)
  • Go (exported/unexported members)
  • JavaScript / TypeScript
  • Markdown (header hierarchy, code blocks)
  • Mermaid diagrams
  • YAML (anchors, aliases, keys)

Two Variants

  • Fluorescent — Modern styling with semantic color consistency
  • Fluorescent Classic — Original styling for long-time users

Note: Screenshots may show previous version styling. Updated screenshots coming soon.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2.0.0 - Major Release

This release marks a significant architectural change in how Fluorescent integrates with your IDE.

Why This Change?

Fluorescent was originally designed with Darcula as its base theme. However, JetBrains has since transitioned to the Islands theme as the default across their IDEs. Rather than forcing users to choose between Fluorescent and their preferred UI theme, we've restructured Fluorescent to be an editor-only color scheme. This gives you the freedom to pair Fluorescent's vibrant syntax highlighting with whichever UI theme you prefer—whether that's Darcula, Islands Dark, or any other.

What's Changed

  • Editor-only color scheme: Fluorescent now focuses exclusively on code syntax highlighting, leaving UI elements to your chosen IDE theme.
  • Enhanced language support: Comprehensive syntax highlighting for Scala, Python, Go, JavaScript, Markdown, Mermaid diagrams, and YAML.
  • Improved color semantics: Consistent color meanings across all supported languages—green for functions, cyan for types, orange for keywords, and more.

For Existing Users

If you prefer the original full-theme experience, select Fluorescent Classic from the color scheme options. This variant preserves the styling from earlier versions.

Configuration

  • UI Theme: Settings → Appearance & Behavior → Appearance → Theme
  • Color Scheme: Settings → Editor → Color Scheme → Fluorescent (or Fluorescent Classic)

Feedback Welcome

We acknowledge that this architectural change may have introduced subtle visual differences from previous versions. If you notice anything that looks off or have suggestions for improvement, we would greatly appreciate your feedback via the plugin's marketplace page or repository. We are committed to addressing reported issues promptly and ensuring Fluorescent continues to meet your expectations.

idea-plugin.name: Obsidian Sunset Theme
idea-plugin.description:
Obsidian Sunset is a dark and colorful theme for Visual Studio Code that enhances the readability and aesthetics of your code. The theme is inspired by the colors of the sky during sunset, with orange, yellow, purple, and blue hues. It features a deep black background with vibrant syntax highlighting in orange, green, blue, and grey. Whether you are coding in C#, Python, JS, or any other language, Obsidian Sunset will make your code stand out with its rich contrast and elegant design. Obsidian Sunset is ideal for developers who prefer a dark theme that is not too harsh on the eyes, but still provides a clear and pleasing visual experience.

Why another theme?

The inception of this theme is rooted in my personal desire to have a single theme that is versatile across all programming languages I use.
  • Often, a theme that complements C# well may not be as visually coherent with Python.
  • Background brightness of many themes is another issue; they are either too bright, causing eye strain, or too dark, making it difficult to view the screen in daylight.
  • Lastly, a significant concern is the lack of color differentiation between various language components such as variables, properties, and functions. In many VS Code themes, these elements are often colored identically, making it challenging to quickly scan the code and distinguish between them.

With this theme, I aim to address all these issues and provide a visually pleasing, versatile, and user-friendly coding environment that enhances readability and productivity.

idea-plugin.name: JustSemantics
idea-plugin.description:
Theme highlighting only variables, functions, etc. In other words, just the semantics.

Let's face it, after your first hello world, you already know all of your language's keywords by heart. Hell, you then know them from most of the other languages too. Yet your editor is happily highlighting every if and class in bright colors like they need your full attention.

What we actually need my friend, is just the semantics. Everything else is replaced by 'yada yada' by our brain anyway. So this plugin provides a highlighting scheme that only makes the semantics pop out, with everything else in neutral colors. Try it! It might save your brain a few percent of attention juice and lets you focus on debugging the bad code that that amateur 'past you' wrote.

Warning: Highlighting like this is very language specific and needs a lot of tweaking before it makes sense. More to come, but currently acceptable for:

  • Kotlin
  • Java
  • Python

idea-plugin.name: Deep Oceanic Next Theme
idea-plugin.description:
Deep Oceanic Next theme is inspired by oceanic-next-color-theme and Deep Ocean Theme.

🌊 Deep Oceanic Next

It’s a place where light bends and dances, where the colors shift and deepen in ways you can only imagine. For most of us, the deep ocean is a mystery—vast, quiet, and endlessly captivating. It’s a place we rarely touch, yet it feels like it touches us.

For years, I’ve been both fascinated and terrified by the ocean. I can’t swim—not even in water as shallow as my height. The fear of being swept away, of sinking, is real. But so is the wonder. The deep ocean, to me, is like a dream: unattainable yet vivid in my imagination.

The Deep Oceanic Next color theme was born from this paradox. It’s a palette inspired by the gradients of the ocean’s depths—from the near-black shadows to the glimmers of light that pierce through. It reflects the courage to embrace what we don’t understand and the beauty that lies in exploring the unknown.

This theme isn’t just about colors; it’s about a journey. A reminder that even if we can’t dive into the deep blue ourselves, we can bring a piece of it into our world—into our screens, our workspaces, and our creative expressions.

So, have you ever wondered what it’s like to dive into the unknown? To explore the depths that so few have seen? Maybe, together with this theme, you can take that step into your own deep ocean?

Feel free to use and enjoy this theme!

🎨 Deep Oceanic Next Color Theme - Palette

Background and Foreground Colors

NameHex CodeDescription
Base00#00191dPrimary Background
Base01#002d36Secondary Background
Base02#00424fTertiary Background
Base03#006170Low Contrast Text Background
Base04#00b8c7Dark Foreground
Base05#d8f3f5Foreground
Base06#eafffbHigh Foreground
Base07#ffffffBright Foreground

Syntax Highlighting Colors

NameHex CodeDescription
Base08#ff4d6dWarm Red - Variables, Errors
Base09#ffc061Warm Orange - Constants
Base0A#fff44fMuted Gold - Classes, Functions
Base0B#00ff9cFresh Green - Strings
Base0C#00f5ffAqua Cyan - Support, Regex
Base0D#33b5ffOceanic Blue - Keywords
Base0E#d966ffVibrant Purple - Markup
Base0F#ff7fcbWarm Pink - Deprecated

Additional Colors

NameHex CodeDescription
Base10#001014Darker Black for Highlights
Base11#00090bDarkest Black for Shadows
Base12#ff7890Bright Red - Warnings
Base13#fff87aBright Yellow - Highlights
Base14#5cffb8Bright Green - Success Indicators
Base15#59fbffBright Cyan - Links
Base16#7dccffBright Blue - Active States
Base17#e0a8ffBright Purple - Accents

❣️ Deep Oceanic Next Color Theme: Inspirations

The creation of the Deep Oceanic Next Theme has been an incredible journey of inspiration and collaboration. This theme is deeply influenced by two stunning color schemes: the Oceanic Next Color Scheme and the Deep Ocean Theme. These projects sparked the vision of capturing the tranquility and mystery of the deep ocean within a single palette.

Throughout the process, I relied heavily on Chat GPT for brainstorming and iterative refinement. This collaboration allowed me to conceptualize and finalize the theme across multiple iterations.

After settling on the color palette, I leveraged tools like Tinted Theming to ensure the colors were consistent and beautifully applied across various platforms. Using the following repositories, I integrated the palette into multiple environments:

  • Intellij Platform Plugin Template for JetBrains IDEs.
  • Chrome Theme Studio for creating a customized Chrome theme.
  • Starship for terminal theming.

To visually represent the theme’s essence, I selected a breathtaking image by Jeremy Bishop on Unsplash. The image perfectly embodies the serenity and depth that inspired this theme.

Creating Deep Oceanic Next Theme has been a rewarding endeavor. It’s more than just a set of colors; it’s a celebration of creativity and a tribute to the beauty of the unexplored deep.

🏳️‍🌈 Various Themes with Deep Oceanic Next Colors

  • iTerm2
  • starship
  • IntelliJ IDEA
  • Chrome Theme
  • Alfred Theme

idea-plugin.name: One Pauintxi Theme
idea-plugin.description:
One Pauintxi Theme - IntelliJ

One Pauintxi Theme es un tema oscuro minimalista para IntelliJ, inspirado en el popular tema One Dark. Está diseñado para desarrolladores que disfrutan de un entorno de codificación visualmente cómodo, con alto contraste y colores vibrantes que mejoran la legibilidad sin forzar la vista.

Screenshots

One Pauintxi Theme Blue

One Pauintxi Theme Blue++

One Pauintxi Theme Orange

One Pauintxi Theme Orange++

Características

  • 🌓 Modo Oscuro: Un fondo oscuro suave con colores vibrantes en primer plano.
  • 🎨 Alto Contraste: Distinción clara entre palabras clave, cadenas, comentarios y otros elementos de sintaxis.
  • ✨ Inspirado en One Dark: Familiar para los usuarios de One Dark, pero con ajustes sutiles para una experiencia más refinada.
  • 🖼️ Hermosos Elementos UI: Estilo personalizado para elementos de UI como barras laterales, pestañas y barra de estado para integrarse perfectamente con el tema oscuro.
  • 🔧 Soporte de Lenguajes: Optimizado para varios lenguajes como Java, Kotlin, Python, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, TypeScript y más.

Instalación

  1. Abre IntelliJ IDEA.
  2. Ve a File > Settings > Plugins.
  3. Haz clic en Marketplace y busca One Pauintxi Theme.
  4. Haz clic en Instalar.
  5. Ve a File > Settings > Appearance & Behavior > Appearance.
  6. En Theme, selecciona One Pauintxi Theme y aplica los cambios.

Personalización

Si deseas ajustar el tema a tu gusto, puedes personalizarlo siguiendo estos pasos:

  1. Ve a File > Settings > Editor > Color Scheme.
  2. Elige el esquema de color que deseas modificar.
  3. Personaliza los colores según tus preferencias y guarda los cambios.

Problemas y Feedback

Si encuentras algún problema, tienes sugerencias o deseas solicitar nuevas funciones, no dudes en abrir un issue en GitHub.

Contribuciones

¡Las contribuciones son bienvenidas! Siéntete libre de hacer un fork del repositorio y crear un pull request con tus cambios. Si planeas agregar cambios significativos, abre primero un issue para discutir lo que te gustaría cambiar.

Licencia

Este tema está bajo la licencia MIT.

¡Disfruta codificando con One Pauintxi Theme y mantente productivo! 🚀

idea-plugin.name: Spacegray Dark Theme
idea-plugin.description:
Spacegray Dark Theme


Themes provide six styles (three standard + three Islands variants).

Standard Variants:
- Primary is the basic style of Dark theme based on JetBrains, and the UI area and editor are the same color.
- Pro is the basic style of Dark theme based on JetBrains, and the UI area and editor are different colors.
- SE is based on the basic dark blue of the original SpaceGray, and the UI area and the editor are different colors.

Islands Variants:
- Primary Islands, Pro Islands, and SE Islands provide modern floating UI design with rounded corners and elevated panels (IntelliJ 2025.3+).

主题提供了6种样式（3种标准 + 3种Islands变体）:

标准变体:
- Primary样式是基于Jetbrains Dark Theme基础UI样式，UI区和编辑器是相同的颜色。
- Pro样式是基于Jetbrains Dark Theme基础UI样式， UI区和编辑器是不相同的颜色。
- SE样式是基于原SpaceGray主题暗蓝色UI样式，UI区和编辑器是不相同的颜色.

Islands变体:
- Primary Islands、Pro Islands和SE Islands提供现代化的浮动UI设计，具有圆角和立体面板（IntelliJ 2025.3+）。


Spacegray theme for IntelliJ, inspired by one made by Gadzhi Kharkharov for SublimeText.

idea-plugin.name: Armada Core Themes
idea-plugin.description:
Armada Core Themes brings the look of JetBrains Fleet's default light and dark themes to IntelliJ-based IDEs. With Fleet deprecated, Armada now also takes its cues from JetBrains Air, so the themes keep evolving alongside JetBrains' current design direction.

This plugin is part of the Armada family of themes, which includes both free and premium themes for JetBrains IDEs, adapted from or inspired by the design aesthetics of JetBrains Fleet and JetBrains Air. The complete list of Armada premium themes can be found here.

If you enjoy Armada Core Themes, but are looking for a more colorful UI, you might consider exploring the Armada Dark Purple and Armada Deep premium themes. Dark Purple offers an additional color scheme inspired by Fleet's design, and Deep is an original theme built on Fleet's design principles.

Features

Includes Fleet- and Air-inspired Dark and Light UI themes/editor color schemes

Supports all three UI generations!

  • Islands
  • New UI
  • Classic UI

Enhanced Syntax Highlighting

Leverages the Armada Syntax Highlighter plugin for more precise syntax highlighting in 13 programming languages and counting.

Supports 25+ Programming Languages

Armada Core Themes have been optimized for syntax highlighting of 25+ programing languages, including:

C#✅✅
CSS✅✅

This plugin includes the default theme, classic theme, and four filters: Machine, Octagon, Ristretto, and Spectrum. Credit goes to the original designer: https://monokai.pro.

Contributions are welcome with GitHub. Screenshots were taken with Atom Material Icons and Operator Mono.

#ebdbb2

idea-plugin.name: Cobalt2 Theme (Reshaded)
idea-plugin.description:
An unofficial faithful re-implementation of Cobalt2 for JetBrains IDEs; forked from Dennis Koch's version

Key features:

  • IDE theming using the color palette from Wes Bos' original theme Cobalt2
  • Accompanying color scheme with extended support for many languages out-of-the-box
  • Adapted token colors to better accommodate languages outside of HTML/CSS/JS

Contribution and Support

This plugin is authored by personal needs, hence feature support from the theme author is only provided for select issues. You are encouraged to adapt the color scheme for missing programming languages or legibility issues yourself and to share your changes with the repository. Below are steps how to do that:

  1. Go to: Settings -> Editor -> Color Scheme -> [Your desired language]
  2. Adapt the color scheme to your liking; The recommended color palette might help you
  3. Open the menu Show Scheme Actions by pressing the cog symbol next to the Scheme dropdown menu
  4. Choose Export -> (.icls) and save the file
  5. Rename the file, such that its extension changes from .icls to .xml (e.g. Cobalt2.icls -> Cobalt2.xml) (it's easiest to do the renaming in a JetBrains IDE)
  6. Send a pull-request to the git repository

idea-plugin.name: Neumorphism Theme Collection
idea-plugin.description:
Professional Themes for AI-Native Development — Eye Comfort + Production-Ready Semantic Highlighting

Do you still need a professional theme now that AI writes so much of your code? More than ever. As AI generates a growing share of your codebase, your role shifts from writing to reading, reviewing, and verifying—and that is exactly where clear, meaningful color does the heavy lifting. Production-ready semantic highlighting turns AI-generated code into something you can scan, validate, and trust at a glance. In an AI-native workflow, semantic highlighting is no longer a cosmetic nicety—it is essential infrastructure for fast, confident code review.


Built for developers who refuse to choose between beautiful aesthetics and professional code clarity. Neumorphism Theme Collection pairs soft, eye-friendly neumorphic design with comprehensive semantic highlighting—so every function, type, parameter, and decorator reads distinctly, whether you wrote it or your AI assistant did.


11 themes. Just $5 (one coffee) to support indie dev. No subscription. Lifetime access.

🎨 What Makes This Different

  • Production-Grade Semantic Highlighting – 256 attributes across Kotlin, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, SASS, Angular, and foundation languages for precise syntax distinction across your entire stack
  • 11 Unique Semantic Palettes – Every theme gets its own professional color scheme, not just hue shifts
  • 100% WCAG AA Certified – Full accessibility compliance with professional contrast testing
  • Eye-Friendly Neumorphic Design – Soft shadows replace harsh borders for marathon coding sessions
  • Zero Performance Impact – Uses IntelliJ built-ins, no custom annotators slowing your IDE

💡 Semantic Highlighting Done Right

Language Attributes
Kotlin 65
Java 34
JavaScript / TypeScript 50
CSS / SASS/SCSS 38
HTML / XML 12
Angular 10
Python 15
Foundation 32
Total 256


65 Kotlin attributes – functions, properties, type parameters, annotations, companion objects, extension functions, context receivers, and more all get distinct, meaningful colors.

34 Java attributes – variables, fields, methods, constructors, types, annotations, and visibility modifiers with smart font style differentiation (bold for declarations, italic for static/abstract, underline for reassigned variables).

50 JavaScript & TypeScript attributes – local variables, exported symbols (bold), decorators, JSX components, enums, type aliases, type guards, and more. Cross-language consistent: decorators match annotations in Kotlin/Java.

38 CSS & SASS/SCSS attributes – property names, selectors, pseudo-classes, functions, mixins, @rules, interpolation, and SASS-specific modifiers like !default and !global.

12 HTML & XML attributes – tag names, attributes, values, custom elements, namespace prefixes, and entity references.

10 Angular attributes – signals, template variables, two-way/event/property bindings, structural directives, Angular 17+ @if/@for/@switch syntax, interpolation delimiters, and ::ng-deep.

15 Python attributes – function definitions and calls, classes, parameters, the self parameter (distinct color from regular params), keyword arguments, type hints, type parameters, decorators, builtins, and magic methods. Full Django, Flask, and FastAPI coverage via standard Python highlighting.

32 foundation attributes cascade to all languages – keywords, strings, numbers, comments work consistently across every file type you open.

11 unique palettes mean Ocean Breeze's calming blues feel different from Recording Studio's precision tones—your theme matches your workflow.

🎨 All 11 Themes Included

  • Lavender – Gentle focus with royal blue functions
  • Sunset – Vibrant energy with horizon blue clarity
  • Midnight – Pure concentration with city cyan functions
  • Recording Studio – Studio-grade precision in light mode
  • Recording Studio Live – High-contrast performance mode

💰 Support Indie Development

  • $5 (Individual) / $10 (Organization) – Just one coffee to support indie dev work
  • All 8 Premium Themes – Plus all future themes and semantic language additions
  • 30-Minute Trials – Test every premium theme before deciding
  • No Subscription – One payment, lifetime access, zero surprise charges

idea-plugin.name: Monokai Pro Lifetime
idea-plugin.description:
Monokai Pro

Monokai Pro is a color scheme, customized user interface theme and icon pack for JetBrains IDEs. It has been designed with beautiful functionality in mind. Carefully selected shades of colors are the foundation of an uncompromising, non-distractive user interface.

Monokai Pro is designed by the same author of the original Monokai color scheme, Wimer Hazenberg. Back in 2006 he created the original Monokai colors. Since then, Monokai has been ported to every code editor on the planet and is used by millions of developers every day.

Licensing options

Monokai Pro is available under two licensing models:

  • Freemium: Free to use with occasional reminders to register, with an optional monthly subscription that removes the reminder pop-ups.
  • Lifetime License: A one-time purchase that unlocks all features for all JetBrains IDEs, removes pop-ups, and supports ongoing development.

Color filters

Monokai Pro comes with a set of color filters to suit your mood. Monokai Pro also offers official light versions that are perfect for brighter environments.

Icons

The icons of Monokai Pro have all been created from scratch to ensure they are easily recognizable on small sizes in the side bar. They are designed to help you quickly find the right files in your project. The icon shapes align perfectly to the pixel grid so the icons always stay sharp.

Customization settings

Monokai Pro for JetBrains IDEs offers a few additional settings to further customize your Monokai Pro experience. You can choose between monochrome or colorful icons, and can turn your IDE into a minimal UI experience that offers an even more calm view.

Every theme is designed for the modern IntelliJ Islands interface, with clear separation between the editor and tool windows, softly rounded surfaces, focused tabs, and consistent colors throughout the IDE.

Meet Islands Moonstone

Moonstone is a new IntelliJ-first theme with a calm slate workspace, cool turquoise accents, and balanced syntax colors. It is designed to feel polished and comfortable during long coding sessions.

What you get

  • A theme for every mood: understated classics, vivid palettes, soft pastels, OLED black, light themes, and high-contrast options
  • Modern Islands styling: polished editor tabs, tool windows, menus, popups, buttons, trees, scrollbars, and status bars
  • Comfortable editor colors: readable syntax highlighting, inactive text, search matches, and diff views
  • Broad language coverage: Java, Kotlin, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, Rust, PHP, HTML, CSS, JSON, YAML, Markdown, and more
  • Bearded Icons: distinctive icons for common languages, frameworks, folders, and configuration files

Easy to personalize

Select your theme from Settings > Appearance & Behavior > Appearance. The dedicated Bearded Theme settings page lets you enable or disable the matching file icons separately, with a direct reminder of where to change colors.

Requires IntelliJ Platform 2025.3 or newer.

The Marketplace subscription supports delivery, updates, and continued theme improvements. Copies you receive remain free software under GPLv3.

  • Show hidden elements toggle — toolbar button to render game-hidden elements at reduced opacity for design inspection.
  • Knowledge base library refresh — library roots refresh after indexing and when the active Hytale version changes.

idea-plugin.name: Ayu Islands
idea-plugin.description:
Not another color swap — a unified aesthetic engine for every JetBrains IDE.

Ayu Islands goes beyond color porting. It synchronizes palette, font, glow, and accent into a cohesive look — one click, the entire mood shift. Built on ayu-colors (MIT) and endorsed by the original Ayu creator. Free to install — all premium features unlocked for 30 days.

What sets it apart

  • Aesthetic engine, not a skin — 500+ hand-tuned UI properties, expanded semantic highlighting, and dedicated settings panels to shape how the IDE looks and feels
  • 4 curated presets — Whisper, Ambient, Neon, Cyberpunk. Each synchronizes font, glow intensity, and indent colors into one cohesive mood
  • Syntax control surface — language-aware syntax presets for everyone, plus Pro-level Custom tuning and readability controls when you want comments, docs, and operators to recede.
  • Plugin ecosystem — accent color propagates into CodeGlance Pro and Indent Rainbow. One palette, everywhere — no other theme does this
  • Creator-endorsed — Ike Ku (@dempfi), the author of the original Ayu theme, called this project "brilliant" and invited it to ayutheme.com

Premium — make the IDE feel yours

  • Glow — a soft light beneath tabs and panels: Soft, Sharp Neon, or Gradient. Add Pulse, Breathe, or Reactive animation. Control intensity, width, and which of the 7 panels glow.
  • Accent control — decide exactly where your accent color appears: scrollbars, links, caret line, search highlights, progress bars, bracket matches, inlay hints, tag matches. Eight independent switches.
  • Accent rotation — automatic preset cycling or contrast-aware random. Your IDE palette evolves on its own.
  • Per-project accent pins — bind a color to a specific project; it applies whenever you focus that window, no keyboard shortcut needed.
  • Per-language accent pins — bind a color to a language (Kotlin → cyan, Python → gold); applies when the project's dominant language matches and no project override exists. Settings shows a live language-proportions breakdown for the current project so you can see which pin takes effect. Language override diagnostics explain detected, polyglot, forced-language, and project-fallback decisions without changing the default dominance logic. Rescan Project Language on demand from the proportions row or the Tools menu.
  • Peacock-parity chrome tinting — when a project / language accent fires, every chrome surface (status bar, nav bar, tool stripes, panel borders) tints automatically. Intensity slider in Settings → Theme Synchronization. WCAG-aware foreground keeps text readable at any saturation. Inspired by Peacock for VS Code (johnpapa.net), built on JetBrains primitives — not ported.
  • Accent from project icon — when enabled, projects without a pin take their accent from the project icon (.idea/icon.png) automatically on open; the Add Override dialog offers the icon's dominant color as a one-click pick.
  • VCS color customization — Settings → Ayu Islands → VCS tunes intensity across five surfaces (diff viewer, Project View file status, editor gutter, conflict markers, Git blame annotations). Per-section profiles: Whisper, Ambient, Neon, Cyberpunk, or Custom with per-surface sliders. Master toggle stays off by default so 2.6.2 colors are byte-identical until users opt in.
  • Syntax tuning — Settings → Ayu Islands → Syntax adds a Custom mode with per-language sliders for declarations, identifiers, keywords, docs, literals, and operators, plus global readability switches for dimming comments, softening docs, quieting operators, and emphasizing declarations.
  • Workspace — auto-fit or fixed width for Project View, Commit, and Git panels with min/max bounds. Git panel splitter control for branches and file changes trees. Hide the filesystem path and scrollbar from the Project View. Commit Panel path display can move full paths to tooltips or shorten leading directories inline.
  • Tab styling — Islands UI: underline, full accent bar, or none. Classic UI: underline thickness from hairline to bold.
  • Plugin sync — accent into CodeGlance Pro minimap and Indent Rainbow guides (3 Ayu presets). More integrations in development.
  • Bracket scope — a colored gutter stripe showing the full scope when your cursor lands on a bracket.
  • Onboarding wizard — a full-tab welcome on first install with preset cards, theme variant picker, and accent swatches. After upgrades, a release showcase tab opens automatically with captioned screenshots of the marquee features; reopen anytime from Tools → Ayu Islands.
  • Font presets — 4 curated Nerd Fonts with one-click apply. Install, delete, or reinstall fonts directly from Settings — every filesystem change gets a consent dialog showing the exact folder path.
  • Quick-Switcher Widget — a chip in the main toolbar reflects your current accent. Left-click for variant, accent, related toggles, and quick actions; right-click for the same actions in a keyboard- friendly context menu.

Try everything free for 30 days. No credit card. Install, explore, decide later.

Free — a complete theme, not a teaser

6 theme variants (Mirage, Dark, Light — Classic & Islands UI). 40+ individually crafted language syntaxes, expanded semantic highlighting, and four one-click syntax presets. 12 accent presets + custom picker + macOS system sync. 4 font presets with one-click apply and live preview. Full VCS/diff colors and a 16-color terminal scheme. All free. No time limit. No feature degradation.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2.8.7

  • [Paid] Universal per-language syntax tuning — Custom syntax settings now follow the active file in the active project window and expose only controls supported by the installed language tooling. Tune intensity against a representative native preview with immediate editor feedback; Apply keeps the result, while Cancel restores the exact previous scheme and preferences. Existing presets and saved choices remain unchanged until edited.
  • [Paid] Bold and Italic for individual syntax primitives — each available language primitive can independently add Bold, Italic, or both while keeping its inherited color and font style, with an explicit option to replace the inherited style when needed.
  • [Fix] Reliable startup in IntelliJ Platform 2025.1 — coroutine-backed Ayu features now retain metadata compatible with the oldest supported IDE runtime instead of failing when the platform reads newer debug metadata.
  • [Fix] Stable Retina preview and Glow buffers — offscreen rendering keeps logical-pixel geometry on HiDPI displays instead of multiplying cache size and memory use with the ambient display scale.

2.8.6

  • [Fix] Contained chaotic waveform borders — Chaotic ECG traces stay inside their editor and tool-window islands instead of spilling across neighboring panels, while route connectors remain visible during focus and window transitions.

2.8.5

  • [Fix] Smoother Glow in large and background windows — Glow keeps the same visuals while using less memory for large panels, pauses waveform work in inactive IDE windows, and stops deferred updates after their host is hidden or the project is closed.
  • [Fix] Reliable startup in 2026.2 IDEs — fixes the write-unsafe startup exception reported in #330 while Ayu refreshes the interface, syntax colors, accents, or fonts.
  • [Fix] Correct translucent syntax colors — diff and caret backgrounds keep their intended opacity instead of loading as corrupted colors or emitting parsing warnings.

2.8.4

  • [Fix] Reliable editor color refreshes in Rider — startup and settings changes no longer trigger write-thread access errors while Ayu refreshes the active editor color scheme.
  • [Fix] Syntax preview highlighting in WebStorm — syntax preset previews now use an available language in the host IDE instead of falling back to a plain-text Kotlin sample.

2.8.3

  • [Fix] Safer Accent settings reset — resetting the Accent section now restores only its default accent mode without resetting Glow, rotation, project icons, syntax, or other Ayu preferences. The change still requires Apply and can be discarded with Cancel.
  • [Fix] Reliable Accent override editing — project and language mappings now preserve one consistent pending state across Add, Edit, Remove, Pin, Reset, Cancel, and Apply. Losing Pro access no longer discards pending mappings or partially applies related Accent settings.
  • [Fix] Accurate Accent override preview — the “Currently active” preview and diagnostics now refresh from the same detected-language result after a rescan, while reopening Settings no longer duplicates or blanks the Projects and Languages controls.

2.8.2

  • [Fix] Java syntax colors — classes, fields, constants, and annotations keep their colors wherever they are referenced, not only where they are declared. Java code no longer flattens to a single gray tone, and editor schemes that already lost these colors are repaired automatically the first time each one is used.

2.8.1

  • [Paid] Connected-island ECG routing — Chaotic waveform mode can finish its current loop and continue across adjacent editor, tool-window, and neighboring IDE-window islands. Routes stay continuous through focus changes, empty editors, touching perimeters, and window lifecycle transitions without rewriting existing Glow preferences.
  • [Fix] License and trial transitions — premium effects and integrations return to free behavior immediately when access ends, while saved premium preferences remain untouched and resume after relicensing. Premium font installs are blocked without access, uninstall remains available, and temporary entitlement failures retry instead of becoming permanent.
  • [Fix] Editor color-scheme ownership — Ayu restores only caret, matched brace, link, inlay-hint, matching-tag, progress-bar, scrollbar, and VCS values it still owns. Manual edits, inherited values, editable copies, and foreign schemes survive theme changes, OS appearance changes, restarts, and feature toggles.

2.8.0

  • [Paid] Chrome tint on external themes — selected chrome surfaces and the active tab underline can follow the Ayu accent on non-Ayu themes when explicitly enabled. It stays off by default, respects individual tint targets, and restores the host theme cleanly when disabled.
  • [Paid] Glow placement — render solid glow around the full island or only along its straight side edges, independently for editors and tool windows. Placement changes preview immediately; Apply keeps them and Cancel restores the previous layout.
  • [Paid] ECG waveform glow — trace the focused island with a compact, angular phosphor-comet loop whose signal and brightness respond to typing. The fixed-length trace travels continuously around islands of any size, stays correctly oriented inside floating windows, and settles into a visible resting waveform when focus moves elsewhere.
  • [Paid] ECG controls and preview — configure direction, loop duration, 1x–4x spike density, trace length, border position, amplitude, and intensity with snapping sliders whose ticks match real values. The live preview mirrors the selected behavior, fresh installs start from the calibrated centered profile, and existing solid-glow preferences remain untouched.
  • [Paid] Accent from project icon — projects without an override can take their accent from .idea/icon.png automatically, and the Add Override dialog offers the icon's dominant color as a one-click pick. Existing manual project accents are never overwritten.
  • [Free] Find what's new faster — the settings page points at newly added controls with a "New in this release" index, Review jump link, tab dots, and small row marks. Tab and group dots clear as their controls become visible, while row marks disappear the next time Settings opens. Expired badges retire on the next IDE startup, and fresh installs show none.
  • [Fix] Commit panel accessibility crash — screen-reader and macOS accessibility walks over the commit changes tree no longer flood idea.log with "Attempt to take read lock was prevented" errors; the path renderer serves plain text when the platform forbids model access mid-walk.

2.7.8

  • [Fix] What's New and onboarding tabs — a failed tab open no longer blocks the What's New tab or the license wizard for the rest of the IDE session; the next trigger simply retries.
  • [Fix] Accent apply recovery — when applying an accent fails midway, the color now recovers on the next window focus instead of freezing until restart, and startup only trusts cached accents from a cleanly finished apply.
  • [Fix] Accent rotation reliability — rotation now counts failed applies and stops with the "accent rotation stopped" notification instead of silently ticking forever against a broken apply.
  • [Fix] License downgrade revert — the "restart to complete the reset" notice now appears when the free-tier revert could not finish cleanly.
  • [Fix] Settings overrides preview — opening the Accent → Overrides resolution preview is now strictly read-only and never schedules background language scans.
  • [Fix] Resolution diagnostics consistency — the "Currently active" label, the diagnostics row, and the accent actually applied now always name the same resolution source.
  • [Fix] Project-language accent scans — background detection now cancels when a project closes, checks cancellation during large repository scans, and drops late cache or publish results so reopened projects do not inherit stale language accents.
  • [Fix] Large project language accents — language detection now keeps exact scans for projects under the file cap and uses bounded sampling for larger repositories, so accents resolve consistently without walking every file in a monorepo.
  • [Fix] Font installer fallbacks — fallback font download URLs are now smoke-checked in CI before release, catching broken upstream links before a bundled font install reaches users.

2.7.7

  • [Fix] Language override diagnostics — Settings and Quick-Switcher now show the detected project-language breakdown, manual forced-language state, polyglot fallback detail, and the language that actually won accent resolution.
  • [Fix] Mapped accents in mixed-language projects — polyglot scans can now choose the highest-weight detected language that has a user accent mapping, so balanced projects can still use a configured language color instead of falling back to the global accent.
  • [Fix] Swift and Noctule Swift highlighting — Swift declaration and reference aliases, predefined symbols, and nil fallback now use Ayu-native semantic colors across Dark, Mirage, and Light.
  • [Fix] Project fallback accents — project fallback resolution now warms and reuses the detector verdict consistently, keeping diagnostics aligned with the accent that gets applied.
  • [Fix] Font install consent — Settings and onboarding font installs now require the exact catalog entry that the user approved before any font files are queued for installation.

2.7.6

  • [Fix] Language override diagnostics — Quick-Switcher now keeps dominant-language proportions and fallback detail in the expanded resolution chain instead of crowding or overlapping the collapsed widget.
  • [Fix] Groovy and Jenkinsfile semantic highlighting — Jenkinsfile pipeline calls, named arguments, dynamic Jenkins bindings, and unresolved chained calls now resolve to Ayu-native Groovy semantic colors across Dark, Mirage, and Light.
  • [Fix] Jenkinsfile unresolved references — pipeline DSL symbols such as properties, parameters, podTemplate, and containerTemplate no longer render as near-background text or carry noisy dotted underlines.
  • [Fix] Focus-based accent refresh — switching project windows now reapplies project and language accents through IntelliJ's write-safe dispatch path instead of a raw Swing callback.
  • [Fix] Chrome tinting dividers — shared IntelliJ divider peers no longer pick up project accent tint and draw a colored editor frame outside the intended accent surfaces.

2.7.5

  • [Paid] Accent Source status-bar widget — Pro users can add a status-bar widget that shows which accent source won for the current project and opens the full resolution chain.
  • [Paid] Language override controls — language accent detection now shows dominance and fallback details in Settings, and forced language or fallback choices take precedence over the global accent.
  • [Free] Quick-Switcher accent diagnostics — the toolbar widget now shows the resolved accent source inline, with an expandable chain for project pins, language overrides, fallbacks, external themes, and global accents.
  • [Free] Groovy and Jenkinsfile syntax colors — Groovy and Jenkinsfile roles now have explicit Ayu colors across Dark, Mirage, and Light, including methods, fields, map keys, strings, GStrings, keywords, documentation, and inlay type hints.
  • [Fix] Quick-Switcher widget buttons — related toggle buttons now apply Chrome tinting, Glow, Accent rotation, and Follow system accent changes reliably from the widget.
  • [Fix] Chrome tinting target preservation — widget toggles and Settings Apply now preserve the exact chrome tint targets you selected instead of turning every tint surface on or off together.
  • [Fix] Language override precedence — forced-language and fallback choices now take precedence over project/global fallback when resolving the active accent.
  • [Fix] Accent diagnostics accuracy — Quick-Switcher and status-bar diagnostics now match the actual resolver for language fallback, project fallback, and external automatic accents.
  • [Fix] Editor Glow with pinned tabs — Glow overlays now align with editor content when only pinned tabs remain, instead of using a fixed tab-strip fallback.

2.7.4

  • [Paid] Language override diagnostics — Settings now explains whether a project's language accent is detected, polyglot, forced to a specific language, or using a project fallback.
  • [Free] Swift semantic highlighting — Noctule Swift files now render parameters, labels, properties, functions, and types with distinct Ayu colors across 109 semantic tokens.
  • [Free] Swift syntax colors — Swift keywords, strings, numbers, and comments use Ayu palette colors in base themes.

2.7.3

  • [Paid] Commit Panel path display — Pro users can move full Commit Panel paths to tooltips or shorten leading directories inline.
  • [Free] Syntax preview — native highlighting now updates reliably when switching syntax presets and readability options.

2.7.2

  • [Paid] External theme accent inheritance — Pro project and language accent pins can now drive selected Ayu integrations while another IDE theme is active.
  • [Paid] Glow on external themes — Glow can follow Ayu accents on non-Ayu themes when explicitly enabled; external Glow stays off by default.
  • [Paid] Plugin sync on external themes — CodeGlance Pro and Indent Rainbow can now sync to Ayu's external accent context on non-Ayu themes.
  • [Paid] External Quick-Switcher actions — premium actions like Random, Lighter, and Darker now persist the chosen external accent on non-Ayu themes.
  • [Free] External theme support — use selected Ayu accent enhancements on non-Ayu JetBrains themes without switching the active IDE theme to Ayu.
  • [Free] Quick-Switcher on external themes — Quick-Switcher now supports external themes, including accent preset apply and copy flows when external theme support is enabled.
  • [Free] Automatic external accent sources — external accents can resolve from Material Theme, IDE accent colors, or a manual fallback.

2.7.1

  • Added: when the optional .ignore plugin is installed, its files use dedicated Ayu colors across Dark, Mirage, and Light editor schemes, including Syntax preset transformations and a Plugins-tab opt-out.
  • Changed: free users can inspect premium Settings controls in their real layout, with controls greyed out until a license or trial unlocks them.
  • Changed: the VCS tab now shows one compact code-style preview that reflects diff, merge/conflict, blame, and file-status presets together.
  • Changed: the Font tab now uses the same editor-style preview treatment as VCS, with clearer depth and file context.
  • Fixed: premium Settings controls stay visible-but-locked across VCS, Glow, Workspace, Chrome tinting, Accent Elements, plugin integrations, and accent overrides instead of disappearing behind a Pro notice.
  • Fixed: locked premium controls no longer mark Settings as modified when clicked by unlicensed users, and Reset/Revert restores nested plugin-integration rows correctly.
  • Fixed: Settings tabs and preview panels shrink more consistently in narrow Settings windows.
  • Fixed: Accent Settings preview stays synchronized with the selected color instead of restoring stale shuffle state.
  • Fixed: visible managed tool windows re-measure after layout and theme refreshes, so auto-fit sizing stays consistent.
  • Compatibility: release builds now block IntelliJ Plugin Verifier internal API findings before Marketplace upload.

2.7.0

  • [Free] Expanded semantic highlighting — Ayu Islands now covers hundreds more editor keys across 26+ language families, with focused passes for YAML/HCL, Scala docs, Kotlin gaps, Dart accessors, Groovy, and Go exported identifiers.
  • [Free] Syntax presets — the new Settings → Ayu Islands → Syntax tab gives everyone four one-click syntax moods: Whisper, Ambient, Neon, and Cyberpunk.
  • [Paid] Custom syntax tuning — Pro users can tune each language separately with sliders for declarations, identifiers, keywords/docs, literals, and operators while untouched cells inherit the selected base preset.
  • [Paid] Readability controls — Dim comments, Soften documentation, Quiet operators, and Emphasize declarations layer on top of the active preset so dense code gets quieter without manual per-key Color Scheme editing.
  • Fixed: matching tag highlights are calmer, status bar text stays readable on tinted chrome, and low chrome-tint values stay subtle instead of jumping straight to saturated accent color.
  • Fixed: YAML/HCL semantic keys, HCL block names, Syntax Custom layout/opening, preset intensity ordering, and custom reapply now behave consistently across newer IDEs and theme changes.

2.6.4

  • [Free] Quick-Switcher Widget — a new chip in the main toolbar reflects the focused project's accent. Left-click opens a popup with the variant and Islands UI toggle, the full accent grid, related toggles (Chrome tinting, Glow, Accent rotation, Follow system), and quick actions (Pin, Random, Lighter, Darker, Copy Hex). Right-click opens the same actions as a context menu for a keyboard-friendly workflow.
  • Premium rows (toggles and quick actions) appear when your license is active or in trial; the FREE block (variant and accent grid) is available to everyone.
  • Hide the widget anytime from Settings → Ayu Islands → General if you prefer a cleaner toolbar.

2.6.3

  • [Paid] A new VCS tab — tune VCS color intensity across five surfaces (diff viewer, Project View file status, editor gutter, conflict markers, Git blame annotations). Pick a named profile — Whisper (calmer), Ambient (2.6.2 defaults), Neon (brighter, pre-2.6.2 punch), or Cyberpunk (peak) — or dial each surface independently in Custom mode. The master toggle stays off by default, so colors are byte-identical to 2.6.2 until you opt in.
  • Settings → Ayu Islands → VCS tab now lives between Glow and Workspace.
  • Project tool window no longer changes width when toggled on/off in Mirage Islands UI under auto-fit mode (issue #169).

2.6.2

  • VCS modified-line color is now distinct from added — modified shifts to a saturated blue (Dark #73B8FF, Mirage #80BFFF) so it stops blending into the green added band on dense diffs. Bluer file-status colors in Project View and tabs as well.
  • Editor selection background returns to translucent (alpha 25%) on Dark and Mirage, so highlighted text doesn't read as a solid blue block.
  • The Settings page no longer freezes on "Loading…" forever when a Custom font preset is active (issue #164) — non-curated presets now skip the font installation pipeline cleanly instead of crashing the panel build.
  • The font preview pane now renders the user's chosen Custom font family when Settings opens instead of falling back to "Install JetBrains Mono to preview" — a UX bug previously masked by the panel-build freeze.

2.6.1

  • Calmed diff backgrounds across Dark, Light, and Mirage variants — modified diff no longer blends with text selection

2.6.0

  • [Paid] Peacock parity for JetBrains — pin an accent to a project window or to a programming language and every chrome surface (status bar, nav bar, tool stripes, panel borders) tints with that accent automatically. WCAG-aware foreground keeps text readable at any saturation. Inspired by Peacock for VS Code (johnpapa.net) — built on JetBrains primitives, not ported.
  • Auto-bind the matching editor color scheme on theme change — switch Ayu Mirage / Dark / Light variants and the editor scheme follows. Default ON; opt-out toggle in Settings → Theme Synchronization preserves your custom scheme (Solarized, Material, etc.) untouched.
  • Fix glow lingering after switching to a non-Ayu theme — overlays now dispose cleanly when the active theme leaves the Ayu family
  • Fix sticky-line panel transparency in the editor — code under the scope-header line no longer bleeds through
  • Fix Indent Rainbow and CodeGlance Pro integrations not reverting cleanly when their sync toggles are turned off
  • Fix path widget breadcrumb on IntelliJ 2026.1 New UI Compact Navigation — chrome tinting reads with stable contrast at every intensity, slider visibly tints in a single Apply click
  • Coming next: commit your accent into .idea/ so a whole team sees one color · distinguish Remote / WSL / DevContainer / Code With Me windows at a glance · one-keystroke darken/lighten on the active accent · named favorite colors · every Peacock command available through Find Action

2.5.3

  • [Paid] Rescan project language on demand — new "Rescan" link in the Overrides proportions row and "Tools → Ayu Islands → Rescan Project Language" menu action, for when you want the detected breakdown to refresh without waiting for the next Gradle sync
  • Bug fixes

2.5.2

  • [Paid] Per-Language Accent Pins now show a live breakdown of the detected languages in your project (e.g. "Detected: Kotlin 78% • Java 15% • other 7%") or a clear "polyglot" notice when no single language dominates
  • Fix accent rotation overriding pinned project colors — tabs and glow now stay on your pinned accent across rotation ticks
  • Fix the Settings panel readouts for currently active and detected projects binding to the wrong project when two or more windows are open.

2.5.1

  • Updated Marketplace "About" description to cover all v2.5.0 features — per-project and per-language accent pins, onboarding wizard, and the first-launch release showcase tab — that hadn't made it onto the listing page

2.5.0

  • [Paid] Pin an accent color to a specific project — set it once from Settings, and every time you switch to that window, your accent is there.
  • [Paid] Pin an accent color to a programming language — e.g., Kotlin → lime, Python → sky. It applies when a project's dominant language matches and no project override exists.
  • Recent projects populate the add-project dialog so you can configure overrides without opening the project first

2.4.2

  • [Paid] Install, delete, or reinstall curated fonts directly from Settings without opening the wizard
  • Every font installation and deletion now shows a consent dialog with the exact font folder path — no silent filesystem changes.
  • When you delete a font, the editor reverts to JetBrains Mono and warns that complete removal takes effect after an IDE restart.
  • The Settings page now shows "Installed ✓", "file missing — Reinstall", or "Install automatically" based on the actual disk state.

2.4.1

  • Fix the font installation retry getting stuck on a corrupted download cache

2.4.0

  • Onboarding wizard — full-tab welcome experience with preset cards, theme variant picker, and accent swatches
  • [Paid] Font installation — download and apply curated coding fonts directly from the wizard
  • Responsive scaling — wizard adapts to split editors and small windows
  • Fix trial day calculation timezone drift (UTC instead of system default)
  • Renewing a license preserves your existing settings
  • Mid-session license changes apply immediately

2.3.7

  • [Free] Fix tool window width jumping when switching between panels
  • [Paid] Hide editor scrollbars while preserving scroll functionality

2.3.6

  • Bug fixes

2.3.5

  • Fix selection overlap bands when accent color is active on multi-row selections

2.3.4

  • Fix glow color desyncing from accent after rotation

2.3.3

  • Fix "Write-unsafe context" crash during accent rotation with Indent Rainbow
  • Rewrite Marketplace description

2.3.2

  • [Paid] Accent rotation — automatic preset cycling or contrast-aware random
  • [Free] Shuffle UI redesign with heroic accent indicator
  • Fix trial

2.3.1

2.3.0

  • [Paid] Auto-fit with configurable min/max width for Project View, Commit, and Git panels
  • [Paid] Git panel internal splitter control — auto-resize branches tree and file changes tree
  • [Paid] Project View cleanup — hide the filesystem path and horizontal scrollbar

idea-plugin.name: Bluloco Dark Theme
idea-plugin.description:
Bluloco brings vivid, easy-to-scan syntax colors to the modern IntelliJ Islands UI.

Choose Bluloco Dark for the original balanced charcoal appearance, or Bluloco Midnight for a deeper canvas with quieter IDE chrome. Both variants are designed to keep code prominent while preserving clear separation between editors, tool windows, popups, and navigation.

Based on the popular Bluloco Dark VS Code theme by Umut Topuzoğlu and carefully adapted for IntelliJ-based IDEs.

The JetBrains Marketplace charges for access to its delivery channel, updates, and support. Once received, the plugin remains free software under GPLv3, including the rights to use, study, modify, and redistribute it.

Features:

  • Two complete themes: balanced Bluloco Dark and deeper Bluloco Midnight
  • Purposeful syntax colors that make keywords, types, functions, strings, and values easy to distinguish
  • Native Islands styling with layered work areas, rounded surfaces, and a clear active tab
  • Coordinated action, object, and checkbox icons using Bluloco accent colors
  • Consistent colors across the editor, completion popups, settings, tool windows, terminal, VCS, and diff views
  • Broad language support, including Java, Kotlin, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, JSON, YAML, Markdown, and SQL

idea-plugin.name: Kokedera Theme
idea-plugin.description:
Kokedera Theme

Bring the quiet of a moss-covered temple into your editor. Kokedera offers nine hand-tuned color themes inspired by forest greens, weathered stone, and warm lantern light — seven dark palettes and two light palettes.

Each palette includes matching IDE colors and an editor color scheme for JetBrains IDEs.

Nine palettes

  • Morning and Winter — Two light themes, from warm paper to cool pale grounds
  • Dusk and Night — Forest greens and lantern warmth, from deep shade to near-black
  • Spring, Summer, and Autumn — Fresh growth, dense greens, and rust over dark earth
  • Rain and Mist — Wet teal and quiet, desaturated greens

Pair it with Kokedera Icons for file and folder icons in matching colors.

Explore the temple and all nine palettes at kokedera.style.

idea-plugin.name: Subliminal
idea-plugin.description:
A high-contrast professional theme ported from the Subliminal Neovim setup. Available in dark and light variants. Optimized for long coding sessions with a focus on readability and aesthetic consistency across the terminal and IDE.
Also bundles Stix — a muted, low-contrast companion palette in dark and light variants, matching the Stix themes for Zed and Neovim.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.2.1

  • Fixed unreadable text in multi-line input fields. Only TextField was themed, so TextArea, TextPane, EditorPane, PasswordField and FormattedTextField fell back to the base look-and-feel — affecting any plugin that uses a multi-line text input. All five are now themed in every variant.

1.2.0

  • Added Stix Dark and Stix Light — a muted, low-contrast companion palette matching the Stix themes for Zed and Neovim. Stix Dark uses flat chrome with steel-blue selection; Stix Light is a warm cream/sepia scheme with a terracotta accent.
  • Fixed terminal and console colors across all themes: the top-level Terminal block and the CONSOLE_FOREGROUND_KEY / CONSOLE_SELECTION_BACKGROUND keys were not recognized by the platform and had no effect.
  • Added the full 16-color ANSI palette to every editor scheme. Previously only the six bright colors were defined, so normal-intensity ANSI output fell back to the parent scheme's colors.

idea-plugin.name: Warm Burnout
idea-plugin.description:
The theme for developers who are already burned out but still have deadlines.

Mostly warm palette, one cool type accent, contrast-audited to WCAG standards. Full UI theme: editor, sidebar, tabs, toolbar, popups, everything.

  • Dark: AAA contrast (7:1+) on every syntax token. For the 3am sessions.
  • Light: AA contrast (4.5:1+) on warm sepia cream. For when someone opens the blinds.

Bold keywords, italic types, readable comments. The style system adds non-color cues for code structure when the warm palette starts to blur together.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.8.0: Suite gains three platforms (Bat, WezTerm, OpenCode) and a Home Assistant migration to the 2026.5 webawesome stack. VS Code patches an italic bleed from the entity.name catch-all into function and other sub-scopes. JetBrains unchanged from 1.7.0; bumped to track the suite.

1.7.0: Codegen rebuild with full language coverage across the editor scheme. Classic non-Islands variants restored alongside the Islands themes. Synced with the rest of the suite (matches the v1.7.0 GitHub release).

1.0.2: Dropped classic variants. Islands themes only. Fixed toolbar borders and project gradient.

1.0.1: Fix editor color scheme not loading when selecting the UI theme.

1.0.0: Initial release.

idea-plugin.name: ColorSafe Themes
idea-plugin.description:
ColorSafe Themes is a collection of accessible, high-contrast color schemes for JetBrains IDEs, built specifically for developers with color vision deficiency (color blindness) — and anyone who wants a cleaner, more readable coding environment.

Most IDE themes rely on color distinctions that are invisible to colorblind developers. ColorSafe replaces those with perceptually distinct color axes grounded in color science, so syntax, errors, and warnings are always unambiguous — whether you have Deuteranopia, Protanopia, Tritanopia, or typical color vision.

Themes included:

Pro-Deutan Dark — High-contrast dark theme for Deuteranopia and Protanopia

  • Blue-Amber syntax axis replaces the red-green confusion of standard themes
  • WCAG AA contrast ratios throughout — readable at a glance, no squinting required
  • Triple-encoded errors: color + squiggly underline shape + font weight — never miss a bug
  • Bold keywords for instant visual hierarchy and reduced cognitive load

Tritan Dark — High-contrast dark theme for Tritanopia

  • Red-Teal syntax axis replaces the blue-yellow confusion of standard themes
  • WCAG AA contrast ratios throughout — readable at a glance, no squinting required
  • Triple-encoded errors: color + squiggly underline shape + font weight — never miss a bug
  • Bold keywords for instant visual hierarchy and reduced cognitive load

More themes coming — low-vision and light variants are planned.

Works with all JetBrains IDEs: IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, Rider, CLion, DataGrip, Android Studio, and more.

Keywords: colorblind theme · color blindness · deuteranopia · protanopia · tritanopia · color vision deficiency · accessible IDE theme · WCAG · high contrast · dark theme · accessibility

If ColorSafe makes your day easier, you can support the project here. Thank you!
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Tritan Dark theme — high-contrast dark theme engineered for Tritanopia
  • Red-Teal syntax axis replaces the blue-yellow distinctions that are invisible to tritanopic developers

Midnight Tide

A cool-blue dark theme built for JetBrains' Islands layout. Forked directly from Islands Dark with three surgical changes:

  • Editor background remapped to #151719 on a cooler chrome tier
  • Teal accent (#0891B2) for selection, focus rings, and the action button
  • Diff line colors swapped to JetBrains' deuteranopia palette — colorblind-safe out of the box

Syntax highlighting inherits Islands Dark's tokens unchanged: purple keywords, teal identifiers and numbers, sky-blue strings. Selection, gutter, popups, and all ~190 other color keys carry over from Islands Dark verbatim.

Setup: Settings → Appearance & Behavior → Appearance → Theme → Midnight Tide. Then Settings → Editor → Color Scheme → Midnight Tide. For the floating-panel look, also enable "Different tool window background" in the Appearance settings.

idea-plugin.name: Koehler Theme
idea-plugin.description:
A deep-black dark theme inspired by the classic Vim koehler color scheme by Ron Aaron.

Highlights

  • Pure-black editor background (#000000) with #101010 UI chrome — ideal on OLED displays and easy on the eyes in dim rooms.
  • Vim koehler hue mapping: yellow bold keywords, blue comments and annotations, pink-red strings and numbers, pink methods and fields, white identifiers and class names, orange punctuation, light-gray caret.
  • Toned-down accents — saturation dialed back from Vim's vivid originals for sustained-use readability.
  • Consistent UI surfaces — settings dialogs, popups, menus, tool windows, terminal, and notifications all unified on the same palette. No stray Darcula-blue rows.
  • Dimmed editor chrome — folding lines, indent guides, whitespace dots, and scrollbars sit just above the background.
  • Restrained selection and highlight backgrounds — current line, identifier-under-caret, and search matches stay legible.

Activate

  • Settings → Appearance & Behavior → Appearance → Theme: Koehler
  • Settings → Editor → Color Scheme → Scheme: Koehler

No fonts, no icons, no keymap changes — just the theme and a matching editor scheme.

idea-plugin.name: Cloud9 JetStream
idea-plugin.description:
Cloud9 JetStream

A dark theme for JetBrains IDEs built for long coding sessions. Deep navy-black backgrounds, restrained Cloud9-blue accents, and a palette that stays out of your way.

Design philosophy

Most dark themes settle for flat charcoal. Cloud9 JetStream uses a layered navy-black palette with five distinct background tiers from #060A10 through #1E293B, so the editor, tool windows, and popups feel like distinct surfaces, not one blob of gray.

The color story is deliberately restrained:

  • Blue carries syntax structure: keywords, operators, focus indicators
  • Cyan marks type information: classes, types, interfaces
  • Purple/violet/indigo flag meta-language: annotations, constants, decorators
  • Amber is reserved for strings. One warm accent. Like stars against a dark sky.
  • Steel-blue punctuation that recedes so logic stands out

Every color has a job. No competing accents.

What's covered

  • 90+ syntax tokens
  • Language-specific tuning for Kotlin, Java, Python, JS/TS, SQL, CSS, Shell/Bash
  • Every UI surface: main menu, tool windows, completion, run widget, terminal, debugger, VCS log
  • Tuned console ANSI palette
  • Rainbow brackets cascade (blue → cyan → indigo → violet → purple)
  • File-status colors that make VCS changes legible at a glance
idea-plugin.change-notes:

  • Changed hyperlink color from gray to blue to improve contrast

1.0.1

  • Ctrl-F search matches now appear as markers on the editor scrollbar
  • New pale-teal color for object members (fields, properties, attributes) for clearer contrast against identifiers
  • Consistent comment styling across embedded code blocks in Markdown
  • Unified inline parameter hint styling
  • Softened the primary blue accent for easier reading on dark backgrounds

1.0.0: First release

Initial release of Cloud9 JetStream. A dark theme for JetBrains IDEs with a layered navy-black palette and restrained Cloud9-blue accents.

idea-plugin.name: Shogun's DevPack
idea-plugin.description:
Shogun's DevPack is a personal productivity plugin for JetBrains IDEs. It bundles a dark IDE theme, editor utilities, project/file helpers, code sharing tools, and AI terminal integrations aimed at reducing repetitive project setup work.

Core features:

  • A dark JetBrains theme and matching editor color scheme.
  • File creation actions for C#, Vue, JSON, Markdown, Git helper files, and general project files.
  • C# namespace detection when creating C# files.
  • Vue component bundle and store/composable templates with bundle index export handling.
  • Git helper files, including CODEOWNERS, LICENSE, .gitignore, .gitkeep, and .editorconfig templates.
  • License generation for common GitHub license templates.
  • Code Share uploads for selected code or selected files through GitHub Gist, Pastebin, or a custom server.
  • Code Shot screenshot creation from the current editor selection, with clipboard, Freeimage.host, ImgBB, and custom server outputs.

idea-plugin.name: Guttenbergovitz UI Theme
idea-plugin.description:
Guttenbergovitz UI Theme

A warm, vintage-inspired UI theme for JetBrains IDEs. Like a well-aged whiskey or a Miles Davis solo — complex but not overwhelming. Reduces blue light and visual noise while maintaining depth and character.


Features:

  • 🌙 Dark + Light variants — two meticulously crafted versions included
  • 🏝️ Full Islands Theme support — native experience on JetBrains 2025.3+ with floating panels, proper border radius, and transparent sidebar borders
  • ✨ New UI ready — complete support for the modern JetBrains UI (2023.3+)
  • 🎨 60+ themed components — tool windows, tabs, menus, dialogs, popups, notifications, welcome screen, search everywhere, and more
  • 🔗 Cross-platform parity — consistent colors across all ports (VS Code, Neovim, Vim, Zed, Helix, terminals), sourced from a single palette.json
  • 👁️ Reduced eye strain — warm browns and oranges replace cool blues, less blue light emission
  • 🎯 Intentional ANSI remap — blue → orange, magenta → warm red, cyan → warm green

Color Philosophy:

  • 📖 Inspired by vintage book printing and jazz aesthetics
  • 🔥 Less blue light, more warmth
  • 🎯 Minimal but meaningful highlighting — every color has a purpose
  • 📐 Readability first, beauty second (they usually align)
  • 🎺 "It's not the notes you play, it's the notes you don't play" — Miles Davis

Designed for all JetBrains IDEs: IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, PhpStorm, RubyMine, CLion, Rider, DataGrip, Android Studio.


Install the matching Guttenbergovitz editor color scheme (available on the Marketplace or via Settings → Editor → Color Scheme) for the complete experience.


📦 Note: This plugin themes the entire IDE interface. If you only want editor syntax colors, install the Guttenbergovitz color scheme separately — it's free and simpler to set up.
