idea-plugin.change-notes:
3.4.2: C/C++/Objective-C namespaces (e.g. the "std" in std::string) are now plain foreground text instead of cyan, so they no longer compete visually with the actual class/type name that follows.
3.4.1: Fixed #include highlighting in C/C++/Objective-C — the directive itself (OC.DIRECTIVE) now uses the scheme's cyan, and the header path/filename (OC.HEADER_PATH) now uses the string color, both of which were previously unset and fell back to plain, unstyled text.
3.4.0: VCS file status colors (the green/blue tint on tabs and file trees for added/modified files) now use the scheme's bright green (#a6e22e) and cyan (#66d9ef) instead of Darcula's muted defaults, which the scheme never overrode before.
3.2.2: New plugin icon — six overlapping circles in the scheme's core colors (pink, orange, yellow, green, cyan, purple), arranged so hue-related colors sit next to each other, with the pink circle standing out on top.
3.2.1: Corrected 3.2.0 — JS object properties (e.g. obj.foo) stay #ffb31e bold as originally intended; only the object reference itself (obj) is now green (#a6e22e), matching other variables.
3.2.0: JavaScript-specific tweak — object variables are now explicitly green (#a6e22e) rather than relying on inherited defaults, so they read the same as any other variable.
3.1.2: Fixed "Unresolved reference access" (unknown/unresolved method and symbol calls) which was left unset and fell back to the IDE's default gray — now uses #65d5ea to match resolved methods. This is a generic, language-agnostic attribute, so the fix applies across JS/TS, PHP, Python, Ruby, Go, Java, Kotlin, and C/C++ alike.
3.1.1: Fixed string literals rendering bold in C/C++/Objective-C, Ruby, and GraphQL (OC.STRING, RUBY_STRING, RUBY_INTERPOLATED_STRING, QL_STRING) — now regular weight in all languages, matching PHP.
3.1.0: Cross-language semantic color unification — variables, parameters, functions, methods, classes/objects, properties, strings, and literals now use the same colors in every supported language as they do in PHP (e.g. variables always green, strings always yellow, properties always orange, functions/classes always cyan, numbers/ constants always purple), across C/C++/Objective-C, JavaScript, Python, Ruby, Go, Kotlin, and CoffeeScript.
3.0.0: Palette cleanup — off-brand syntax colors (Go/PHP/Kotlin/Python parameters, enum constants, Obj-C ivars/macros, Ruby constants, CoffeeScript/JS members, etc.) remapped onto the core Monokai Sublime 3 palette for a more consistent look across languages. Background shifted to #282822. Comment color updated to #827e68. Format specifiers (%s, %i, etc.) now use the scheme's green instead of plain red.
2.0.0: Added a full IDE theme variant — editor colors stay Monokai Sublime 3, but the surrounding IDE chrome (toolbars, menus, panels) now picks up a matching dark palette adapted from Neokai (Classic).
1.0.0: Initial release (editor color scheme only).

idea-plugin.name: Syntalume Theme
idea-plugin.description:
Comfort-first themes for long coding sessions.

Syntalume is the new name for Auralis — same product, same themes, same update path.

Syntalume brings the same contrast-audited palette system to JetBrains IDEs, VS Code, and popular terminals. Every release includes nine coordinated UI themes and editor schemes:

  • Noir, Frost, Paper, Botanica, Void, and Dimmed
  • Noir High Contrast and Paper High Contrast
  • Frost Colorblind

All variants include explicit Islands UI separation, unmistakable active tabs, semantic icon colors, scoped action/file-icon substitutions, terminal ANSI colors, debugger and VCS states, and carefully layered editor and tool-window surfaces.

Subscription access: new and existing users receive 30 days from the first presentation of the in-IDE notice, followed by annual subscriptions of $9/$12/$20 for 1/3/6 activations. Installing never authorizes a charge.

Private by design: license activation and periodic validation contact Polar after consent using your key and installation label. No project contents or analytics are transmitted. Previously verified access can continue for up to 72 hours during temporary failures, bounded by the known license expiry; confirmed revocation clears that grace. Theme works without Companion.

Product site · Documentation · Support & visual bug reports

The plugin never prompts for feedback. A short review on this page tells other developers what to expect and guides what improves next.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• The non-blocking notice starts the full 30-day period when shown; closing it preserves access and IDE startup stays responsive.
  • Previously verified paid access survives temporary connection/service failures for up to 72 hours, bounded by its known expiry. Unverified keys never obtain that grace.
  • Appearance replaced when access ends is retained for safe restoration on recovery; later manual choices are preserved. License management remains available.
  • Standalone Theme remains compatible with IDE build 223 and newer and does not require Companion.
  • No re-install needed: this is the same plugin with the same update path, and existing installs upgrade in place.

idea-plugin.name: Islands Light with Test-Aware Tabs
idea-plugin.description:
!!! Note: You may NOT want this anymore. The UI is improved recently and so the current active test file is easily recognizable.

Islands Light fork that flags atypical files in the editor tab strip. The file in the active tab gets the IDE's Tests scope icon (red/green triangles) when it lives in a test source root, or a warning icon when it's a non-project file from outside the project — inactive tabs keep their regular icons. The active tab's island fill is also translucent, so a test file's scope color shows through. Based on JetBrains' Islands Light theme (Apache 2.0).

Once the plugin is enabled, the file icons stay patched, which means switching to a different theme doesn't reset them.
The off switch is the plugin itself: disable or uninstall it in Settings → Plugins. That takes effect without a restart, because fileIconPatcher is a dynamic extension point.

idea-plugin.name: Nova Theme
idea-plugin.description:
Nova is a vibrant, space-inspired theme built for the Islands UI and tuned for Go development.

Editor and tool windows float as rounded islands over a deep-space canvas, while the syntax palette bursts with supernova energy: magenta keywords, electric cyan variables, nebula purple types, star gold functions and aurora green strings.

Six variants:

  • Nova Dark: deep-space navy islands over a near-black cosmic canvas.
  • Nova Light: bright stellar islands with the same high-energy accents, contrast-corrected for daylight.
  • Nova Dark High Contrast: pure black canvas and brighter accents for high-glare screens and accessibility.
  • Nova Dim: a softer, lower-contrast dark variant for long sessions.
  • Nova Dark Classic and Nova Light Classic: the same palettes without the Islands layout, for the classic New UI look.

Go-specific highlighting covers struct tags, build constraints, struct versus interface references, method receivers, shadowed variables, builtin values, doc comment references and go fix syntax updates, plus Go templates.

Full IDE coverage beyond the editor: the block terminal, the profiler tool window with flame graphs and CPU/memory charts, line profiling gutters, the debugger with inline values, test coverage gutters, VCS file status and annotations, inlay hints, AI inline suggestions and next-edit highlights, diff and merge, plus YAML, JSON, Markdown, Terraform HCL, Protobuf, Docker Compose, Kubernetes, SQL, HTTP client and regular expressions.

Ships with the Commit Mono coding font (SIL OFL 1.1) with ligatures. The font is registered automatically and offered through a notification the first time a Nova scheme is active, so your editor font is never changed without asking.

AI Lens shows which code was written by AI and whether you have reviewed it:

  • Lines inserted by AI assistants in the IDE and files rewritten on disk by external agents get a tinted background and a gutter bar in Nova magenta.
  • Lines turn reviewed as the caret rests on them, or through the Code menu. The status bar counts what is left and jumps to the next block, and the commit dialog asks before committing unreviewed AI code.
  • Lines whose last commit carries an AI co-author trailer, such as Co-Authored-By: Claude, are marked with a dashed gutter bar.

AI Lens colors can be customized under Editor | Color Scheme | Nova AI Lens and its behavior under Tools | Nova AI Lens.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.2.0
  • AI Lens: highlight code written by AI assistants in the IDE and by external agents that change files on disk.
  • Review tracking for AI-written lines, with a status bar counter, next and previous navigation and a confirmation before committing unreviewed AI code.
  • Highlight lines that come from commits with an AI co-author trailer.
1.1.0
  • New variants: Nova Dark High Contrast, Nova Dim, Nova Dark Classic and Nova Light Classic.
  • Theming for the profiler tool window: flame graphs, CPU and memory charts, line profiling gutters.
  • Theming for the block terminal, including its own ANSI palette, block backgrounds and error strokes.
  • Go highlighting extended to struct tags, build constraints, interfaces versus structs, builtin variables, comment references, go fix syntax updates and Go templates.
  • Debugger, test coverage, inlay hints, breadcrumbs, bookmarks and live template colors.
  • AI inline suggestions, inline prompt and next-edit diff colors.
  • VCS file status colors, annotation stripes and merge status colors.
  • Language coverage for YAML, JSON, Markdown, Terraform HCL, Protobuf, Docker Compose, Kubernetes, SQL, HTTP client, XML, HTML, CSS and regular expressions.
  • Islands compact metrics, alternative window backgrounds, badges, banners and project gradients.

idea-plugin.name: InfiniTint Theme Tuner
idea-plugin.description:
InfiniTint recolors the theme you already use, in any color, with a single click. Pick a preset tint and the window chrome, the editor canvas, and the controls change together.

Free on any installed theme

  • Preset tints — eight presets on the IDE's bundled themes, three on any other theme you have installed
  • Borders — turn tool window header, island panel, and editor tab strip borders on or off, even on themes that don't draw their own
  • Editor harmonization — the structural colors of your theme's default editor color scheme follow the tint

With a license (14-day free trial)

  • Unlimited custom tints — any color, tuned with hue and chroma sliders
  • Tone curves — brightness and contrast across the whole theme, from sharp layering to a flat, quiet look
  • Text contrast — set your own, with minimum contrast targets as a readability floor
  • Scenes — a complete look saved under a name, ready to reapply any time
  • Automatic switching — clock schedules, sunrise and sunset, timed rotation, and per-project scenes that follow the window you focus
  • Cross-theme harmonization — borrow an editor color scheme from another theme and its structural palette (editor background, tabs, line colors, indent guides, etc.) adapts to your active theme

Limitations

  • You may encounter some changes to how your scenes and tints render on plugin updates in the near term as the palette detection and recoloring systems are tuned to better support a wider variety of custom themes.
  • Text contrast tuning depends on how a theme is built. Text drawn through keys or attributes InfiniTint does not recognize will not follow your contrast settings. InfiniTint also never inverts a theme's lightness relationships, so a minimum contrast target may not be reachable at the extremes.
  • Surface and accent palette detection is tuned to support a number of popular themes, but some custom themes may tint with inconsistencies. The free presets can be used to evaluate whether InfiniTint works on your favorite custom theme.

If your preferred theme does not tint correctly, or you have a feature request, email infinitint-support@tachilabs.dev.

Learn more at infinitint.dev, or see the FAQ for common questions.

Works with any IntelliJ-based IDE on platform 2025.3 or later, light and dark themes alike.

idea-plugin.name: Terra Pastel
idea-plugin.description:
Terra Pastel is a pastel-earth theme collection for IntelliJ-based IDEs — one soft landscape of lavender skies, golden fields, and terracotta soil, seen at three moments: twilight, open daylight, and softened haze. Crafted for Software Engineers, Full-Stack Developers, DevOps, and QA Professionals who read code for hours and want a palette that stays calm without going flat.

Compatible with IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2 · Theme Edition 1.0


The Concept

Terra Pastel isn't three unrelated themes bundled together — it's one landscape observed at three different moments. The same lavender-violet accent, golden wheat, and terracotta clay carry through every variant; only the light around them changes. Pick the variant that matches your room, not a different color language each time.


The Three Variants

  • Terra Pastel Dusk — dark. Deep indigo background, the boldest contrast of the three. Twilight · Deep · Focused
  • Terra Pastel Meadow — light. Full daylight, white-and-cream islands on a warm parchment sea. Bright · Airy · Daylight
  • Terra Pastel Haze — soft. A softened, warmer dark, halfway between Dusk and Meadow. Softened · Warm · Balanced

Features & Visual Ergonomics:
  • True Islands UI: Seamless floating panels with rounded corners and clean borders.
  • Islux Dual-Tone Architecture: ExpUI and Classic dual-mapping ensuring every toolbar, project tree element, and action button renders with our signature 1.5px dual-tone styling.
  • Comprehensive Syntax Highlighting: hand-tuned attributes for Java, Python, JavaScript, YAML, JSON, Properties, and Cucumber/Gherkin, plus matched braces and selected indent guides in every variant, so nested blocks stay legible in long sessions.
  • WCAG AA-verified contrast: every syntax color and UI text pair is checked against its editor background in all three variants — not eyeballed.
  • Rainbow Brackets Ready: ships matching 5-level bracket colors for the popular Rainbow Brackets plugin — install it alongside for depth-based bracket coloring in your own palette.
  • Custom checkbox & radio icons: hand-drawn in the theme's own palette, not a generic recolor.
  • Consistent across every JetBrains IDE — IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, CLion, GoLand, Rider, and more, since it ships as a platform theme.
  • Pastel Earth Concept: a single soft landscape — lavender sky, golden wheat, terracotta clay — rendered across three moments, from twilight to open meadow.

Why Terra Pastel over a generic theme pack

  • Most theme packs give you many unrelated single-mood themes. Terra Pastel gives you one deeply-tuned concept in 3 coherent variants that share the exact same semantic-role mapping — so switching Dusk → Meadow → Haze never breaks your muscle memory the way jumping between dozens of unrelated palettes does.
  • Syntax highlighting is tuned by language, not just generically — Java, Python, JavaScript, YAML, JSON, Properties and Gherkin/Cucumber each get purposeful, distinct treatment, useful for real polyglot QA-automation and full-stack workflows.
  • Matched-brace and indent-guide visibility is a deliberate, verified design decision in every variant — not an inherited near-invisible default.

Issue Tracker · Website · Contact


Looking for more Islux VillAge Studio themes? Terra Pastel is also included in The Collection — 8 full theme families, 24 variants, one license.

idea-plugin.name: Islux VillAge Studio - Theme Collection
idea-plugin.description:
8 professionally engineered theme families, 24 coherent variants, one true color system.
Every Islux VillAge Studio theme is built from the same 12-token model — not colors picked one at a time by eye, but a calculated system of hue and lightness so every palette holds together on its own, with no clashes and no patch-ups. This isn't a pack of loose themes — it's an architecture. Compatible with IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2 · Collection Edition 1.0


Why this isn't "another theme pack"
  • 12-token system per theme — background, border, selection, text, icon outline, and 6 semantic accents (structure, strings, static methods, tertiary, error) all derived from the same hue axis, not picked independently.
  • Dual-Tone on every icon — a sober outline color plus the theme's live accent for the detail. No icon is flat or arbitrarily multicolor.
  • Double ExpUI + Classic mapping verified with UI Inspector — zero icons that "disappear" when switching between New UI and Classic UI.
  • Indent guide and matched brace always visible in the theme's own accent — never a muted tone that gets lost against the background.
  • Programming ligatures enabled by default — JetBrains Mono renders ->, !=, >= and similar operators as single glyphs in all 24 variants.
  • Themed debugger session — breakpoint markers and the current execution-point line use the theme's own accent colors, not the IDE default, across every variant.
  • Themed current-line highlight (caret row) in every variant — consistent with the rest of the palette, not a generic overlay.
  • Identifier-under-caret highlighting — click a variable or method and every other occurrence in the file highlights in the theme's own accent, at two distinct intensities for read vs. write usages.
  • Themed folded-code blocks — a collapsed method or block keeps the theme's palette instead of falling back to a generic gray placeholder.
  • Themed TODO/FIXME highlighting — bold and colored so incomplete work never blends into regular comments.
  • Themed search results — find-in-file and find-usages highlights use the theme's palette instead of IntelliJ's default harsh yellow.
  • Themed VCS diff colors — added/deleted/modified line backgrounds tuned per theme, useful for the code-review-heavy workflows of QA and DevOps engineers.
  • Real syntax coverage: Java, Python, JavaScript, YAML, JSON, Properties and Cucumber/Gherkin — not just generic highlighting.
  • 3 variants per theme (dark / soft / light) — the same chromatic identity across 3 different light exposures, never a different palette per variant.
  • Rainbow Brackets compatible — the full 15 nesting-depth color keys, in every one of the 8 themes.
  • WCAG AA contrast verified — every syntax color was measured against its real editor background across all 24 variants, not picked by eye.
  • Dark → Light → Soft order consistent across all 24 variants and in this very list — never a different order per theme.

The 8 themes in this collection
Abyssal Bloom
Trench · Surface · Tide		 a bioluminescent coral garden in the deep sea
Amber Cay
Deep Moon · Dawn · Dusk		 a tropical cay bathed in amber light
Colores
Negro · Blanco · Gris		 a neutral, versatile system for anyone who wants the code itself to be the protagonist
Embermoor
Dusk · Dawn · Haze		 a misty moor at nightfall, crossed by a copper ember
Ignis
Forja · Aire · Ceniza		 the heat of a forge — vivid orange over ash and charcoal
Kukulkán
Serpiente Nocturna · Piedra de Cal · Ocaso de Jade		 Maya jade and gold, inspired by Mesoamerican civilization
Linaria
Dusk · Dawn · Haze		 the wildflower that pairs yellow and violet — a color combination almost never seen in editor themes
Sunset Oasis
Nightfall · Daybreak · Twilight		 a warm sunset over an oasis, earth and amber tones

Every theme goes through the same checklist before publishing: JSON/XML validated, Level-1 icons confirmed with UI Inspector, correct parent_scheme for variant clarity, and the full 15 Rainbow Brackets keys for compatibility with that plugin. This isn't marketing language — it's the same documented process for all 8 themes in this collection.


Want to try the studio's style before buying? Terra Pastel is available as a standalone entry-level theme.


Issue Tracker · Website · Contact

  • No telemetry, analytics, accounts, or network requests.

Tideglass Dark is designed for long development sessions where syntax should remain expressive and easy to parse without turning the editor into a rainbow.

idea-plugin.name: Gruvbox Islands
idea-plugin.description:
Description

Gruvbox Islands brings the warm, retro-groove of the Gruvbox color palette to IntelliJ-based IDEs, reimagined for the modern Islands (New UI) aesthetic.

Unlike a single dark/light pair, this plugin ships the full Gruvbox contrast matrix: dark and light, each in hard, medium and soft.

Note

This theme derives from the theme created by nowheremat @ https://plugins.jetbrains.com/plugin/29610-gruvbox-island

Variants

Theme Editor background Window chrome
Gruvbox Dark Hard Islands #1d2021 #101415
Gruvbox Dark Medium Islands #282828 #1d2021
Gruvbox Dark Soft Islands #32302f #282828
Gruvbox Light Hard Islands #f9f5d7 #f2e5bc
Gruvbox Light Medium Islands #fbf1c7 #ebdbb2
Gruvbox Light Soft Islands #f2e5bc #d5c4a1

As in upstream Gruvbox, hard / medium / soft differ only in the background ladder — foreground, accent and syntax colors are identical across the three.

Features

Designed for the "Islands" UI

Every variant is registered with targetUi="islands", so toolbars, project trees and editor tabs blend seamlessly with the Gruvbox palette. The Islands UI layers a darker window chrome behind lighter island panels; all three background tiers shift together per variant so that layering stays visible in hard and soft as well as medium.

Enhanced Syntax Highlighting

Each variant ships a dedicated editor scheme applying Gruvbox colors to your code, supporting a wide range of languages including Java, Kotlin, Python, JavaScript, Rust, Go, and more.

Gruvbox-tinted controls

Checkboxes and radio buttons are recolored to the Gruvbox palette rather than the stock JetBrains blue.

idea-plugin.name: Cydecient Themes
idea-plugin.description:
Cydecient Themes - 11 dark worlds, one code palette

Nature
#050c03		Retro
#111a2e		Crimson
#0e0204		Obsidian
#050505		Blue
#000517		Light
#181c23
Coffee
#0c0803		Violet
#070111		Gamer
#17000b		Ember
#100400		Abyss
#010b0e

Rounded Islands, built in. On IntelliJ 2025.2 and newer every Cydecient world renders in JetBrains' new Islands look: the editor and each tool window float as rounded panels over a darker gap, and because every panel shares the editor's exact background, your code sits inside the world instead of on top of a grey frame. One switch, once: Settings -> Advanced Settings -> "Enable Islands UI for custom themes", then restart. Older IDEs get the same worlds with flat panels.

Tired of milky grey themes and washed-out pastels? Cydecient Themes is built for people who live in dark spaces. Eleven deep, saturated worlds, each committed to a single color so completely that opening one feels like stepping somewhere, not just recoloring a window. The code stays lit and razor-sharp on near-black backgrounds; the world around it is what changes.

  • 11 dark worlds: Nature, Retro, Crimson, Obsidian, Blue, Light, Coffee, Violet, Gamer, Ember, Abyss.
  • One shared code palette: keywords, strings, methods, classes and variables read the same in every world.
  • The editor color scheme is bound to each theme; switching the theme switches the scheme.
  • Rounded Islands panels on 2025.2 and newer, with every panel matching the editor background.
  • Contrast-checked: muted text, line numbers, selections and buttons pass fixed readability floors in every world.
  • Works in every IntelliJ-based IDE from 2022.3 (build 223) on, including PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, Rider and CLion.

One palette, every world. Keywords, strings, methods, classes and variables are identical in every theme, tuned once on the green Nature world and carried everywhere, so you can chase a mood without relearning your syntax. Switch the theme and the editor scheme follows on its own. Rounded "Islands" panels are supported on 2025.2 and newer.

Distinguishable, dark, easy on the eyes. Every world is verified, not eyeballed: panel and editor share the exact same background, muted and disabled text clear real contrast floors, and no color bleeds between worlds. Let green pull you into a forest, let purple pull you into dusk.

Free, all of it. Every world in the pack and every world added later, with no subscription, no license key and nothing locked. Install once, then switch worlds as your mood or your room lighting asks.

Cydecient Nature

Matte forest green, the world every other is tuned against. A moss-dark canvas that makes lime strings and gold types glow like undergrowth catching light. Calm, grounded, the one you can live in from morning to last commit.

Cydecient Retro

Deep midnight navy lit by warm amber, the glow of an old terminal under a blueprint lamp. Cool and a little nostalgic, with just enough yellow to feel analog without ever going bright.

Cydecient Crimson

Dark red, ember-lit. A low, intense world for heads-down focus, like working by the light of coals. Coral accents keep it warm rather than harsh.

Cydecient Obsidian

Near-pure black volcanic glass, with translucent grey island edges that let your panels float. The most minimal, highest-contrast world in the pack: nothing between you and the code.

Cydecient Blue

The deep-space midnight of Dark Blue Angel, a near-black blue that started this whole pack. Cool, quiet, timeless, the classic dark that never tires.

Cydecient Light

The softest dark: a moonlit graphite for overcast afternoons and bright rooms. Still fully dark and still code-first, just a gentler night. Not a milky light theme; the code colors never change.

Cydecient Coffee

Dark roast brown, warm and close, an espresso-lit study where caramel accents rest on cocoa shadow. Cozy without ever going soft.

Cydecient Violet

Deep violet dusk, a saturated purple world for late, creative sessions. Neon-adjacent, a little electric, the kind of dark you disappear into.

Cydecient Gamer

Neon pink on black with glowing island edges, synthwave and arcade cabinet and 2am energy. The loudest world here, and proud of it.

Cydecient Ember

Deep amber and burnt orange, a forge at dusk. Warm light pooling on dark iron, for anyone who finds blue themes cold.

Cydecient Abyss

Deep ocean teal, submerged and cool and quiet, a mile down. Aqua accents drift over near-black water, a calm counterpart to the green.

Setup

  1. Appearance and Behavior -> Appearance -> Theme: pick a Cydecient world.
  2. The editor color scheme switches with it automatically. If you had pinned another scheme, set Editor -> Color Scheme back to the matching Cydecient name once.
  3. Rounded panels (2025.2+): Advanced Settings -> "Enable Islands UI for custom themes", then restart.

idea-plugin.name: Starry Night Theme
idea-plugin.description:
A dark theme inspired by Van Gogh's Starry Night for Visual Studio Code, Cursor, JetBrains IDEs (IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, ...) and every VS Code-compatible editor (VSCodium, Windsurf, ...).

Immerse yourself in the beauty and mystery of Van Gogh's Starry Night with this theme. The vibrant colors and expressive swirls of the painting bring your development environment to life, inspiring creativity and focus.
idea-plugin.change-notes: JetBrains editor scheme: every text attribute is now a real platform key. The previous names (KEYWORD, STRING, NUMBER, LINE_COMMENT, FUNCTION_CALL, CLASS_NAME, …) do not exist in any scheme the IDE reads — languages register their own keys with a fallback to the "Language Defaults" pair (JAVA_KEYWORD → DEFAULT_KEYWORD), so those entries themed nothing and the editor silently kept Darcula's token colours while the chrome looked right. The scheme now sets the DEFAULT_* family plus the platform attributes (breadcrumbs, hyperlinks, search results, matched braces, diffs, folded text, inlay hints, console/Logcat/log output), and the build fails if a known-invented name comes back. 46 → 130 attributes, 21 → 52 keys. JetBrains token colours now resolve exactly like TextMate/VS Code: the deepest matching selector wins, later rules break ties. Before, the "first selector that matches" heuristic fed the wrong colour to whole classes of tokens — comments came out accent-blue instead of the comment grey, strings fell back to the plain foreground instead of the yellow, class names were orange instead of blue and keywords picked up this/self. Bold/italic were also inverted (IntelliJ's FONT_TYPE is 1 = BOLD, 2 = ITALIC) and are now derived from the source's fontStyle. JetBrains editor scheme has no alpha channel: a #RRGGBBAA colour is now composited over the editor background instead of being painted at full strength (search results, diffs, identifier-under-caret, gutter marks), and a fully transparent #RRGGBB00 becomes an empty value = inherit, so the separators VS Code deliberately removed do not grow back in the IDE. JetBrains UI theme: ActionButton, ToggleButton, Counter, CheckBoxMenuItem, ComboBox.ArrowButton, PasswordField, CompletionPopup, DragAndDrop, Bookmark, FileColor, VersionControl, WelcomeScreen, ValidationTooltip, Notification.ToolWindow/error colours, NotificationsToolwindow and the ProgressBar passed/failed/indeterminate states; the * block now carries the same property list as JetBrains' own New UI dark theme (inactiveBackground, caretForeground, textForeground, disabledBorderColor, selection*Inactive). Fixed: TabbedPane.contentAreaColor was emitted as a component instead of a colour, and Component.border / TextField.border were not real keys (both removed). 64 → 76 components, 243 → 312 colour properties. VS Code: four keys that were left blank were not actually "no border" — a blank theme key falls back to the base theme's own value, and dark_vs/ dark_plus do define them: editorGroupHeader.tabsBorder (#303031, the tab strip separator 2.0.2 meant to remove), menu.separatorBackground (#454545), editor.lineHighlightBorder and editor.inactiveSelectionBackground (#3A3D41, the base theme's grey for a selection in an unfocused editor). All four now use the palette explicitly, and the remaining blank keys resolve to *nothing* in the base theme, so they stay blank. VS Code: added the missing inline-chat colours (inlineChat.*, inlineChatDiff.*) — the theme painted none of them, so Copilot's inline chat fell back to the editor defaults.

idea-plugin.name: Neon Glow
idea-plugin.description:
Neon Glow is a free and open-source plugin for JetBrains IDEs. Keep your theme, add some light.

Neon Glow paints a soft, blurred halo behind text and icons across the whole IDE: editor, tool windows, tabs, menus, popups and dialogs. Coloured code gets layered neon in the style of SynthWave '84. Plain text stays crisp unless you ask for it to glow too.

Settings (Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Neon Glow)
  • Separate switches and strengths for editor text, UI text and icons
  • Brightness, radius and intensity sliders
  • Neon text styling on or off, regular text glow on or off
  • Performance mode that caps new glow work per repaint
  • Quick toggle: View | Appearance | Neon Glow
Changes apply without restarting the IDE. Glow is static (no animation) and switches itself off in Power Save mode.

Themes (optional)
Three dark themes with matching editor, console and terminal colours: Neon Glow, Neon Glow Midnight and Neon Glow Accessible. Pick one under Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Appearance, or keep the theme you already use. Themes and glow are independent.

Good to know
The glow is drawn with Java2D and covers Swing text and standard icons. Native menu bars, embedded browsers, terminal panes that bypass Swing text drawing and icons painted from vector shapes are not covered.

Inspired by Robb Owen's SynthWave '84 for VS Code, with no affiliation to its author. A personal project, not an official JetBrains product.

idea-plugin.name: Custom Postfix Templates
idea-plugin.description:
Documentation | Screencast | Predefined templates

This open source plugin lets you define your own postfix templates for Java, Scala, SQL, PHP, Kotlin, Python, Dart, JavaScript, Ruby, Rust, Go and Groovy. It also comes with hundreds of useful postfix templates shared by the community. You're welcome to contribute your templates as well.

Apart from the community approach, how does the plugin differ from IDEA's postfix templates?

Since IDEA 2018 you are now able to define your own postfix templates for some languages in the settings UI (Editor → General → Postfix Templates). However, this is a pretty new feature and it's less functional than this plugin. Here are some of the advantages of this plugin:

  • You can define different template rules (context based) for the same template name, e.g. .toList should behave differently for arrays and for sets.
  • You can use template variables (e.g. $varName$) which are filled in by the user while applying the template.
  • You can use live template macros to automatically fill some of the template variables (e.g. $var:suggestVariableName()$) as well as you can define default values.
  • You can restrict the availability of templates or template rules to the availability of certain classes or libraries (e.g. expand "test".val to val s = "test" if Lombok is available).
  • It allows you to use static imports instead of class imports (e.g. array.toList can be expanded to asList(array) instead of Arrays.asList(array) if you add [USE_STATIC_IMPORTS] to the rule).
  • It comes with more than 500 editable postfix templates with more than 700 template rules, e.g.
    • string.toInt → Integer.parse(string)
    • array.toList → Arrays.asList(array)
    • file.lines → Files.readAllLines(file.toPath(), Charset.forName("UTF-8"))
    • file.getName().val → final String name = file.getName();
  • There are multiple ways to easily share your templates with others.

idea-plugin.name: LNKD.tech Editor
idea-plugin.description:
Editor for Turtle (Terse RDF Triple Language, TTL) files. This is a plugin for IntelliJ IDEA, and others IDE environments based onIntelliJ Platform.

Issue tracker

Settings:

  • Plugin specific settings - 'Settings' → 'Other Settings' → 'LNKD.tech Editor' or 'Settings' → 'LNKD.tech Editor' - depends how many other plugins are installed.
  • Code formatting - 'Settings'→'Editor'→'Code Style'→'Turtle (LtE)'.
  • Code annotation - 'Settings'→'Editor'→'Color Scheme'→'Turtle (LtE)'.
  • Code inspections - 'Settings'→'Editor'→'Inspections' then 'Turtle (LtE)'.

Features:

  • SHACL Inspection - inspection that reads projects shape definitions and runs inspection on graphs.
  • Global graphs - graphs visible in project but not part of the project (plugin settings→'Global graphs').
  • Turtle file support - highlighting, completion, inspections, indexing, navigation.
  • Editorial support - hierarchy (Ctrl+H), structure (Alt+7), quick documentation (Ctrl+Q), code folding
  • Triple count - Status bar widget (enabled by default).
  • Transaction count - Status bar widget (disabled by default).
  • Language injection into literals (option under Alt+Enter).

Known limitations and issues:

  • 'Assisted edit' file size limitation - current default limitation of JetBrains IDEs is 2.5MB (details). Changing any of these settings settings comes with bigger resource usage.
  • 'Index' file size limitation - depending on setting (plugin settings→'Triplestore/index') limit is the same as for 'assisted edit' (default) or current content load limitation of JetBrains IDEs (20MB) (details). Changing any of these settings settings comes with bigger resource usage.
  • No SPARQL support - not yet.
  • No known schema or ontology resolution - you need to include all schemas and ontologies to be able to go to definitions.
  • Growing plugin's folder in IDE's System Folder - This is the index ( triple-store). If it will get too large you can clear all IDE caches ("File" → "Invalidate Caches / Restart...")

Powered by opensource:

  • ICU4J - license: Unicode
  • Eclipse Collections - license: EPL
  • Apache Jena - license: Apache License 2.0
  • ...
idea-plugin.change-notes:

Changed

  • LTE-418 Better resource completion and symbol search
    • Background:
      • IRI completion (old functionality) and symbol search (introduced in the last version), both for performance reasons were looking only for resources that have specific predicates (the same predicates used in Hierarchy view - general feature of IntelliJ: Ctrl+H, e.g. rdf:type or rdfs:subClassOf).
      • This most likely caused user confusion when a lot of suggestions were ignored only because the resource did not have one of the required predicates. Especially for a model that is just being created.

idea-plugin.name: Nginx Configuration
idea-plugin.description:
Nginx Configuration — fast editing inside JetBrains IDE

Work with Nginx configs faster — without breaking them.

This plugin brings full IDE support for Nginx configuration files: syntax highlighting, code completion, navigation, and structure view — so you can read and edit configs without constantly switching to documentation.

What you get

  • Syntax highlighting — directives, variables, strings, comments, and regex patterns are color-coded for readability
  • Directive auto-completion — suggests directive names as you type, with context filtering
  • Basic validation — catches unknown directives and common structural errors
  • Navigation — Ctrl+Click on include paths to jump to the referenced file
  • Structure view — see the outline of your config with server, location, and upstream blocks
  • Code folding — collapse blocks to focus on what matters
  • Lua block support — syntax highlighting inside content_by_lua_block and similar directives (requires a Lua plugin)
  • File recognition — auto-detects nginx.conf, mime.types, fastcgi_params, *.conf, *.nginx, and more

Need more power?

Nginx Configuration Pro adds 14 inspections with quick fixes, refactoring (rename, safe delete, extract to include), 30+ live templates, context-aware completion for 1090+ directives, Find Usages, Docker/envsubst support, and OpenResty module support.

idea-plugin.name: Spring Boot Assistant
idea-plugin.description:
NOTE: This plugin is intended for IntelliJ IDEA Community Edition ONLY. It is not compatible with IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate Edition, and using it in Ultimate may cause feature conflicts.

This plugin adds support for Spring Boot external-config files (application.yaml/properties, etc.).

Features:

  • Completion
    • Auto-completion of the configuration properties in your application.yaml/properties files based on the spring boot's autoconfiguration jars are present in the classpath.
    • Auto-completion of the configuration properties in your application.yaml/properties files if you have classes annotated with @ConfigurationProperties, if your build is properly configured.
    • Short form search & search for element deep within is also supported. i.e, sp.d will show you spring.data, spring.datasource, also, port would show server.port as a suggestion.
    • Auto-completion of the configuration property values, with support for the value providers.
  • Documentation
    • Quick documentation for groups & properties (not all groups & properties will have documentation, depends on whether the original author specified documentation or not for any given element).
  • Inspection
    • Key not defined: Report problem if the property in config file is not defined in any metadata.
    • Property deprecated: Report problem if using a deprecated property.
    • Invalid value: Report problem if the value does not match the property type.
  • Navigation
    • Support for IDE feature Go to Declaration or Usages (Ctrl+B) in application.yaml/properties files.
  • Editing
    • Add line separator in yaml key (press Enter), will split yaml key in proper format.
    • Enhanced Join Lines (Ctrl+Shift+J/⌃ ⇧ J) command, which join yaml keys in proper format.

idea-plugin.name: Nginx Configuration Pro
idea-plugin.description:
Nginx Configuration Pro is an IDE-native nginx security analyzer and config linter. It audits your nginx.conf against a Gixy-parity check set, warns about CVEs affecting the target nginx version, and flags ReDoS-prone regex patterns — while you type, with one-click fixes, and without leaving the IDE.

Built-in Nginx Security Analyzer

  • Gixy-parity security audit — full parity with Gixy-Next 0.3.4: all 38 upstream checks implemented plus regex_redos as a separate heuristic inspection. Covers alias_traversal, explicit client-derived Host forwarding, response-header splitting, upstream header injection, unsafe redirects and proxy targets, if_is_evil, origins/CORS validators (wildcard + credentials, $http_referrer typo, missing regex anchors, unescaped hostname dots), hsts_header (weak max-age, missing includeSubDomains, http-level inheritance), ssrf, ssl_stapling_without_resolver, weak_ssl_tls, version_disclosure, add_header_redefinition, proxy_pass_normalized, quic_bpf_reuseport, http2_misdirected_request, stale_dns_cache, unanchored_regex, invalid_regex, and more.
  • CVE advisor inspection — uses the project's target nginx version by default and accepts an installed-version override in the inspection settings. It reports CVEs affecting the effective version, with config-trigger pattern matching where relevant: CVE-2026-9256, CVE-2026-42945 (NGINX Rift, rewrite-rift trigger), CVE-2026-42946 (scgi/uwsgi), CVE-2026-40460 (HTTP/3), CVE-2021-23017 (resolver), CVE-2019-9511, CVE-2024-7347 (mp4), CVE-2022-41741 (mp4), CVE-2017-7529.
  • ReDoS detection — a dedicated heuristic analyzer parses regex patterns from location ~/~*, if regex conditions, map source values with ~/~*, and the rewrite pattern, and flags nested unbounded quantifiers (exponential (a+)+), overlapping alternatives inside a quantified group (polynomial (a|ab)+), and adjacent broad greedy quantifiers (polynomial .*.*end).
  • Extra checks beyond Gixy — CVE matching, SSL certificate path existence, autoindex on exposure, CORS wildcard combined with credentials, HTTPS→HTTP downgrade, open-proxy patterns, and generic security-header checks.

Catch Errors Before They Reach Production

  • 30 inspections, most with quick fixes — choose a project target under Settings | Tools | Nginx Pro | Inspections (nginx 1.31.3 by default) or the Nginx Operations tool window; this target is used for inspections only and does not affect runtime instance selection. The setting controls wrong-context checks, invalid parameters, missing semicolons, undefined upstreams and variables, SSL best practices, deprecated listen parameters, performance checks, and the security analyzer above. Validates 1090+ directives from the built-in catalog.
  • Run nginx -t from the IDE — the Nginx Operations tool window validates every nginx root config in your project against a local nginx binary or any running Docker container, shows results in a per-root tree with clickable error hyperlinks, switches environments from a single selector, and exposes error logs, access logs, and reported modules with their type and conservative availability in dedicated tabs.
  • Context-aware autocomplete — suggests only directives valid in the current block. Completes upstream names in proxy_pass, paths in include, and variable names.
  • Quick documentation — hover over any directive or variable to see its description, allowed contexts, and a link to official nginx docs.

Navigate and Refactor with Confidence

  • Go to Definition — Ctrl+Click on include paths, upstream names, variables, and named locations. Supports glob patterns in includes.
  • Find Usages — see where any upstream, variable, or named location is referenced across your project.
  • Rename — rename upstreams, variables, and named locations with automatic reference updates across all config files.
  • Safe Delete — checks usages before removing upstreams or files.
  • Breadcrumbs — always see where you are: http > server > location /api.

Write Configs Faster

  • 30+ live templates — type proxy + Tab for a reverse proxy block, ssl + Tab for SSL config. Covers WebSocket, PHP-FPM, static files, CORS, rate limiting, caching, and more.
  • Intentions — extract blocks to include files, inline includes, convert listen to IPv6, add SSL redirects — all via Alt+Enter.
  • Code formatting — reformat entire configs with column alignment in map, geo, and types blocks.

Beyond Standard Nginx

  • Custom directives — define your own directives with allowed contexts and parameter descriptions. Share definitions with your team via Settings > Tools > Nginx Custom Directives.
  • Docker support — recognizes *.conf.template files with ${VARNAME} envsubst placeholders.
  • Third-party modules — OpenResty (Lua, Echo, Headers More), Brotli, MaxMind GeoIP2.
  • Lua blocks — syntax highlighting inside content_by_lua_block and similar directives (requires a Lua plugin).

Getting Started

  1. Install the plugin and open any .conf or nginx.conf file — inspections and autocomplete work immediately
  2. Open the Nginx Operations tool window and click Validate to run nginx -t on every root config — pick a local binary or a running Docker container in the environment selector
  3. Try Ctrl+Click on an include path or upstream name to navigate
  4. Type proxy + Tab inside a location block to insert a reverse proxy template

Links

  • Documentation
  • Report an issue
  • Other plugins by meanmail

Privacy

No automatic plugin usage analytics, analytics identity, or queued event uploads. The inspection suggestion stores only a local shown flag. Error reports are submitted explicitly; JetBrains licensing remains in place.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
202622.0 (September, 7, 2026)

  • Keep following server blocks available for highlighting and navigation when an if condition is malformed.
  • Update the directive catalog for nginx 1.31.5: JSON extraction, early request-body reading and predicate location signatures. Add license_pending_token and refresh directive documentation; JSON member paths no longer use filesystem validation or completion, and extracted variables resolve to their json_set declarations.
  • Keep highlighting stable after edits and correctly parse Lua strings and comments, escaped arguments and geo proxy_recursive. Preserve following blocks after a missing semicolon and flag invalid text after a quoted argument.
  • Add an optional weak warning for custom variables without static references, with conservative dynamic-script exclusions.
  • Show clickable gutter counts for directives referencing upstream and variable definitions.
  • Browse include, upstream and variable relationships with Call Hierarchy, including incoming usages, dependencies and cycle-safe navigation.
  • Go to Symbol: find upstreams, declared variables and location paths with distinct file and line entries.
  • Move and copy server blocks: copy a server to a new file, or extract a block with a configuration-root-relative include path. Existing files are protected and both actions support Undo.
  • Postfix completion: expand 80.listen, backend.upstream and /api.location into directives and blocks.
  • Spelling support: check comments and quoted text with the IDE dictionaries and spelling settings. Directive names and variable tokens are excluded.
  • Surround selected directives: wrap complete directives and their comments in a location, if, server, or upstream block through the standard Surround With action.
  • Customizable syntax colors: adjust every Nginx highlighting style in Settings | Editor | Color Scheme | Nginx Configuration Pro, with a configuration preview.
  • Directive signatures while typing: Parameter Info shows argument names, optional values, and alternative forms for the current directive.
  • Parameter names in the editor: inline hints explain unambiguous directive arguments, including listening ports, paths, and timeouts. Toggle them in Settings | Editor | Inlay Hints.
  • Easier support requests: Report an issue now opens a filled-in GitHub draft in the public support tracker. Reports from Nginx Pro settings include plugin and IDE details; reports for unknown directives also identify the directive. Review the draft before submitting.

  • New: ReDoS detection inspection (NginxRegexRedosInspection) — heuristic ReDoS analyzer that parses regex patterns from location ~/~*, if regex conditions, map source values with ~/~*, and the rewrite pattern, and flags nested unbounded quantifiers (exponential (a+)+, ((ab)+)+), overlapping alternatives in quantified groups (polynomial (a|ab)+, (.|x)+), and adjacent broad greedy quantifiers (polynomial .*.*end); skips patterns it cannot parse or where the inner quantifier has a provably safe boundary to keep false positives low

      • Fixed validation bug: EMPTY_BOOLEAN always returned true without checking value matches parameter name
      • Reduced type system from 14 to 13 types (later expanded to 14 with REGEX type)
      • KEYWORD now handles all literal keyword cases (positional and named)
      • Updated 73 directive parameters across 27+ module files
      • Cleaner architecture with proper validation for literal keywords like "off", "merge", "unix:"
    • Improved ADDRESS validation with proper IPv6 and hostname support:
      • Replaced heuristic IPv6 validation with proper RFC-compliant checking
      • Added support for IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses: ::ffff:192.0.2.1
      • Added RFC 1123 hostname validation (length limits, label format, special characters)
      • Smart IPv4 detection: values like 256.1.1.1 now correctly rejected as malformed IPv4 (not accepted as hostname)
      • Added support for wildcard address: *
      • Improved CIDR validation to use new IPv6 validator
      • Comprehensive test coverage with 160+ test cases for edge cases
    • Added URI validation with proper format checking:
      • Now validates URI format instead of accepting any string
      • Accepts absolute HTTP/HTTPS URLs: http://example.com/path, https://api.example.com/v1/users
      • Accepts absolute paths: /path/to/resource, /api/v1/users?query=value
      • Rejects invalid formats: relative paths, unsupported protocols (ftp://, file://), protocol-relative URLs (//example.com)
      • Rejects URIs with whitespace or control characters
      • Nginx variables in URIs bypass validation (resolved at runtime): http://backend$request_uri
      • Empty URI allowed for directives that support it
      • Comprehensive test coverage with 180+ test cases
    • Improved CIDR validation with detailed error messages:
      • Replaced generic "Invalid value for type CIDR" with specific, actionable error messages
      • Format errors: "CIDR must be in format: address/prefix" for missing or malformed notation
      • Prefix validation: "Invalid prefix length: must be a number" for non-numeric prefixes
      • Range validation with actual values: "IPv4 prefix must be between 0 and 32, got 33"
      • Range validation with actual values: "IPv6 prefix must be between 0 and 128, got 129"
      • Address validation: "Invalid CIDR notation: address must be valid IPv4 or IPv6"
      • Already uses improved IPv6 validator from ADDRESS validation (supports IPv4-mapped IPv6 in CIDR)
      • Comprehensive test coverage with 150+ test cases covering all error scenarios
    • Fixed range validation to work with partial bounds:
      • Previous implementation required BOTH minValue and maxValue to be set for validation to work
      • Now works correctly with only minimum bound: validates that value >= minimum
      • Now works correctly with only maximum bound: validates that value <= maximum
      • Improved error messages: "Value 5 is less than minimum 10" (includes actual values)
      • Improved error messages: "Value 150 is greater than maximum 100" (includes actual values)
      • Correctly handles TIME values (converted to milliseconds), SIZE values (converted to bytes), PORT values
      • Nginx variables automatically bypass range validation (resolved at runtime)
      • Non-numeric values safely ignored by range validation
      • Comprehensive test coverage with 200+ test cases for all numeric types and edge cases
    • Added REGEX type for regular expression validation:
      • New value type for directive parameters that accept regular expressions
      • Validates regex syntax at edit time: catches syntax errors before deployment
      • Detailed error messages: "Invalid regular expression: Unclosed group near index 4" shows exactly what's wrong
      • Use cases: location ~ patterns, rewrite rules, map patterns
      • Supports all Kotlin regex features: character classes, quantifiers, groups, alternation, anchors, lookahead/lookbehind
      • Correctly handles common Nginx patterns: ^/api/, \\.(gif|jpg|png)$, ^/(.*)$
      • Nginx variables in patterns automatically bypass validation: ^\$uri
      • Expanded type system from 13 to 14 types
      • Comprehensive test coverage with 400+ test cases for valid/invalid patterns and edge cases
  • Improved directive documentation:
    • Updated descriptions for 85+ parameters to match official nginx.org documentation
    • All 951 nginx.org directives now have accurate, clear, and up-to-date descriptions
    • Removed configuration examples from parameter descriptions for better clarity
    • Fixed duplicated and incorrect content in directive documentation
  • Enhanced quick documentation for directives:
    • aio: Clearer "threads" parameter description
    • auth_basic_user_file: More concise "file" parameter description
    • auth_jwt: Better explanation of "off" parameter behavior
    • image_filter: Fixed "size" and "rotate" parameter descriptions
    • open_log_file_cache: Separated combined descriptions into clear individual parameter docs
    • log_format: Corrected "escape" parameter description (stream module)
    • listen: Updated 11 parameters with complete documentation including usage warnings

202528.0 (December, 28, 2025)

  • Parser bug fixes:
    • Fixed parsing of try_files directive with status code syntax (e.g., try_files $uri =404;)
    • Fixed error_page directive parameter structure to correctly handle both simple and response code forms
  • Improved parameter validation and autocompletion for directives:
    • log_format: improved validation for escape parameter with proper allowedValues [default, json, none]
    • js_shared_dict_zone and keyval_zone (http/stream): fixed type parameter to correctly validate string/number/ip/prefix values
    • limit_req: improved parameter set variants for nodelay and delay optional parameters
    • js_import (http/stream): fixed parameter structure for alternative syntax with export name (e.g., js_import export_name from module.js;)
  • Directive parameter type detection improvements:
    • Introduced centralized classification of nginx literal keywords (none, max, nodelay, epoch, always, merge, test, from)
    • Fixed parameter type detection for ssl_session_cache, userid_expires, health_check, expires, and valid_referers directives
    • Improved normalization of parameter sets to prevent incorrect STRING conversion for literal keywords
    • Enhanced handling of assignment parameters with multiple=true flag
    • Improved keyword folding logic: keywords are now folded into STRING with allowedValues only when STRING alternatives are present (e.g., valid_referers), while pure literal keyword alternatives remain as separate KEYWORD parameters (e.g., expires, ssl_session_cache)
  • Updated directive catalog for nginx 1.29.4:
    • Added ssl_ech_file directive for TLS 1.3 ECH (Encrypted ClientHello) support in HTTP and Stream modules
    • Split expires directive epoch and max parameters into separate KEYWORD parameter sets
    • Fixed health_check directive parameters to support multiple assignment parameters
    • Updated HTTP/2 upstream support documentation:
      • proxy_http_version now supports version "2" for HTTP/2 upstream connections
      • Updated keepalive, ntlm, proxy_request_buffering, and proxy_set_header descriptions to mention HTTP/2 support

202527.0 (December, 05, 2025)

  • New directives from nginx 1.29.3:
    • Added ngx_http_tunnel_module for CONNECT request handling
    • Added ngx_http_num_map_module and ngx_stream_num_map_module
    • New commercial directives: *_allow_upstream, *_bind_dynamic, *_request_dynamic

  • Go to Definition for include: Navigate directly to included files:

  • Go to Definition for upstream: Navigate directly to upstream definitions:
    • Ctrl+Click on upstream name in proxy_pass http://backend navigates to definition
    • Find Usages: right-click on upstream to find all proxy_pass references
    • Warning highlighting if upstream is not defined with quick fix
    • Autocomplete upstream names in proxy_pass, fastcgi_pass, uwsgi_pass, scgi_pass, grpc_pass
  • Inspection Suppression: Suppress inspections with comments:
    • # noinspection NginxMissingIncludeInspection for server paths
    • # noinspection ALL to suppress all inspections
    • Quick fix available to add suppress comment
  • File Type Recognition: Standard nginx files now recognized automatically:

  • Live Templates: Added 30+ context-aware code snippets for common Nginx patterns

idea-plugin.name: Spring Boot Helper
idea-plugin.description:
Assist in Spring application development. Adds support for navigation, code inspections, and intelligent autocompletion for Spring configuration files , Spring reference configuration, Spring metadata documentation.(Support: Java, Kotlin, application-*.yaml and bootstrap-*.properties)

Features

Configuration File Assistance

  • Smart Autocompletion: Offers suggestions for both Spring Boot and custom configuration properties. Supports abbreviated (sp.d) and partial (port) matching.

  • Quick Documentation: Displays Javadoc on hover for properties and groups.

  • Go to Definition: Navigates directly to a property's source definition with Ctrl+Click.

Productivity Tools

  • File Conversion: Convert configuration files between YAML (.yml) and Properties (.properties) formats. 🔀

  • Copy Property Keys: Right-click a key to copy it as plain text or an environment variable.

  • Copy as cURL: Right-click a request mapping in a @RestController to copy it as a cURL command.🧭 (beta).

Spring Initializr

Note: This feature has been moved to its own plugin: Spring Initializr helper

  • Bootstrap new projects or modules using the File / New / Project / Spring Initializr wizard.

Usage

Assuming that you have Spring boot's autoconfiguration jars are present in the classpath, this plugin will automatically allows you to autocomplete properties as suggestions in all your yml files

Suggestions would appear as soon as you type/press Ctrl+Space.

Short form suggestions are also supported such as, sp.d will show you spring.data, spring.datasource, e.t.c as suggestions that make your typing faster

In addition to libraries in the classpath, the plugin also allows you to have your own @ConfigurationProperties available as suggestions in all your yml files.

For this to work, you need to ensure the following steps are followed for your project/module

Configuring the Annotation Processor

idea-plugin.name: JsonToAnyLanguage
idea-plugin.description:
JsonToAnyLanguage Plugin Introduction

A plugin for converting json strings to any language entity, currently supported languages are:

Java、Kotlin、Dart、TypeScript、OC、Swift、C++、Go、C#、Rust、PHP、Python

1. Business Background

In daily development, we often use plug-ins to convert JSON to business entities, but at present, there is no plug-in in the plug-in market that can support generating multiple languages at the same time, resulting in the need to download many plug-ins, which is unacceptable for many obsessive-compulsive disorder patients.

Based on this background, I developed this plug-in to integrate these functions into one plug-in.

2. Plug-in download and configuration

Download

You can search for JsonToAnyLanguage directly in the plugin market to download

Plugin configuration

There is no need to configure the plugin by default. Only when the request for the QuickTypeNode service fails, you can build the QuickTypeNode service locally, and then configure the access link into the settings.

3.The use of plug-ins and effects

The plugin is also very simple to use. Just right-click on the directory where you want to generate code to invoke the plugin menu, then paste the Json string in the plugin pop-up window and select the language you want to generate.

idea-plugin.name: GenerateAllSetter Postfix Completion
idea-plugin.description:
类似于 GenerateAllSetter，但由后缀触发（即类似于 .var 的用法）！ | Similar to GenerateAllSetter, but triggered by a suffix (i.e. similar to .var usage)!

GitHub | Issues | Get Started | LICENSE

若图片显示不全，请点此打开到网页上查看

English 🇺🇸

GenerateAllSetter Postfix Completion 是做什么的？

  • 是一个 IDEA 插件，仅支持 Java 。
  • 参考了 GenerateAllSetter 插件，作为其补充，添加了几个 Postfix 语法，功能与 GenerateAllSetter 基本一致。
  • 在 pojo 变量之后通过 .allset 生成所有 setter
  • 在 pojo 变量之后通过 .allsetn 生成所有设置器（但没有默认值）
  • 在 pojo 变量之后通过 .allget 生成所有 getter
  • 在使用 @lombok.Builder 的 pojo 变量之后通过 .allbuilder 生成所有 setter 调用链

为什么这个项目有用？

  • 多一个选择，另外本人认为 Postfix 比较顺手，有助于进一步提高效率。
  • 给大家提供一个 Postfix 插件开发模板，希望大家多开发一些提高效率的插件。

我该如何开始？

1.安装插件

快点击 Install 吧!

2.打开俺提供的示例项目

示例项目地址： docer-savior-plugin-usage-examples 

或
git clone https://github.com/docer-savior/docer-savior-plugin-usage-examples

下载后，找到 cn.gudqs.example.genset.GenerateSetterAndGetterUsage 文件

3.插件使用

演示所使用的基础类 

					
import lombok.AllArgsConstructor;
import lombok.Builder;
import lombok.Data;
import lombok.NoArgsConstructor;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

@Data
@Builder
@NoArgsConstructor
@AllArgsConstructor
class Foo {

    private Integer testInt;

    private Long testLong;

    private Float testFloat;

    private Double testDouble;

    private Boolean testBoolean;

}

生成 set

					public void usage01() {
    // 用法1, 生成所有 set 方法, 带默认值, 通过 postfix
    Foo foo = new Foo();
    // 取消下面的注释, 光标位于 allset 后面, 按下 Tab 键
//        foo.allset
    // 即可得到下面结果, 且 foo.allset 会自动消失
    foo.setTestInt(0);
    foo.setTestLong(0L);
    foo.setTestFloat(0f);
    foo.setTestDouble(0D);
    foo.setTestBoolean(false);
}

生成 get

					public void usage03() {
    // 用法3, 生成所有 get 方法, 通过 postfix
    Foo foo = new Foo();
    // 取消下面的注释, 光标位于 allget 后面, 按下 Tab 键
//        foo.allget
    // 即可得到下面结果, 且 foo.allget 会自动消失
    Integer testInt = foo.getTestInt();
    Long testLong = foo.getTestLong();
    Float testFloat = foo.getTestFloat();
    Double testDouble = foo.getTestDouble();
    Boolean testBoolean = foo.getTestBoolean();
}

Lombok 的 @Builder 快速生成所有赋值方法的调用链

					public void usage04() {
    // 用法4, 生成所有 set 方法, 通过 builder, 通过 postfix
    // 取消下面的注释, 光标位于 allbuilder 后面, 按下 Tab 键
//        Foo.builder().allbuilder
    // 即可得到下面结果
    Foo foo = Foo.builder()
            .testInt(0)
            .testLong(0L)
            .testFloat(0f)
            .testDouble(0D)
            .testBoolean(false)
            .build();
}

根据一段含有源对象（a）/目标对象（b）的 b.setXxx(a.getXxx()) 方法代码生成所有 set 方法以快速实现对象转换

					public void usage05() {
    // 用法5, 将 src 的数据赋值给 dest, 常用于两个不同类直接进行 convert(需字段名称相同), 通过 postfix
    Foo src = new Foo();
    Foo dest = new Foo();
    // 取消下面的注释, 光标位于 convert 后面, 按下 Tab 键
//        dest.setTestInt(src.getTestInt());.convert
    // 即可得到下面结果
    dest.setTestInt(src.getTestInt());
    dest.setTestLong(src.getTestLong());
    dest.setTestFloat(src.getTestFloat());
    dest.setTestDouble(src.getTestDouble());
    dest.setTestBoolean(src.getTestBoolean());
}

如果需要，我可以从哪里获得更多帮助？

通过提交 Issue 来获取帮助

点击访问 Github Issue

欢迎大家提问，欢迎大家一起完善它！

另外，我接入了 IDEA 的错误处理组件，因此当发现插件报错提示时，按照 IDEA 提示，可查看错误信息，并一键上报给我（即自动生成一个 Issue）

通过查看 Wiki 来获取更多说明

idea-plugin.name: PrologCode
idea-plugin.description:
PrologCode is a plugin for IntelliJ IDEA that provides support for the Prolog language. Specifically, it provides:

  • Prolog syntax highlighting
  • Prolog code completion
  • Prolog code folding
  • Prolog code navigation
  • Three different ways to run a GNU Prolog REPL
  • Real-time background syntax checking

Initially, this plugin was developed as part of a project for the course "Programmation logique" at HEIA-FR.

Usage


Installation:

  • For the plugin to work, you need to have GNU Prolog installed on your system. You can download it from here.
  • Once you have installed GNU Prolog, you can create a new Prolog project by going to File > New > Project and selecting Prolog from the list of project types.
  • Once you have created a Prolog project, you can set the path to the GNU Prolog executable by going in project settings (File > Project Structure) and selecting the Project SDK tab. You can then click on the New button and select Prolog from the list of available SDKs. You can then select the path to the GNU Prolog executable.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Show a "Multiple definitions found" chooser when a keyword call (Run Keyword And Return Status), an import name (Library SomeName), or a variable reference (${SOME_VAR}) resolves to more than one definition across attached SDKs, venvs, or imported resources. RobotKeywordReference, RobotArgumentReference, and RobotVariableReference are now poly-variant (PsiPolyVariantReferenceBase) and a new RobotGotoDeclarationHandler extension bridges them into IntelliJ 2024.2+'s modern Ctrl+Click pipeline so the chooser actually appears.
  • Stop mis-resolving Library DateTime to the typeshed stub class openpyxl.descriptors.base.DateTime (or any other PyCharm-generated skeleton stub) when no real class is found. The Python class and module indices now skip auto-generated stubs in python_stubs/, typeshed/stubs/, typeshed-fallback/, and the IDE's bundled helpers/typeshed/, so resolution lands on the real robot.libraries.DateTime module instead.
  • Promote the standard robot.libraries.<Name> module lookup to first priority in RobotFileManager.findPython and findPythonAll. Without this, the resolver could pick a non-robot class (e.g. click.types.DateTime) sharing the same short name as a standard Robot library.
  • Register every candidate from a Library X import (not just the first one) as a keyword source. Previously HeadingImpl.collectImportFiles called resolveImport which collapses poly-variant references to a single result; now it calls resolveImportAll so two libraries sharing X actually feed the multi-resolution chooser for both the import line and the keyword calls inside the suite.
  • Stop flagging keywords and variables that have multiple valid definitions as "definition not found". The RobotKeywordNotFound and RobotVariableNotFound inspections now call multiResolve(false) on poly-variant references and treat any non-empty result as "found", instead of relying on resolve() (which deliberately returns null on 2+ candidates to enable the chooser).

For Codeium Enterprise customers only

Other Codeium users should use the standard Codeium extension in the JetBrains Marketplace.

Codeium Enterprise Updater

Installs the latest version of the Codeium Enterprise plugin from your organization's self-hosted server and keeps it up to date.

Upon installation, the plugin will prompt you for your organization's Codeium Portal URL.

The Codeium Enterprise Updater extension will automatically install the latest version of Codeium Enterprise from your organization's self-hosted server. Once it has done so, it will prompt you to reload your IDE.

Once you've done so you should be redirected back to your IDE and be ready to use Codeium.

At any point in time you should be able to restart the installation process by running Help -> Find Action -> Reset Codeium Enterprise Updater.

idea-plugin.name: Atlas
idea-plugin.description:
Atlas is a modern schema management tool that streamlines database schema migrations through a declarative, Schema-as-Code approach. The Atlas plugin for JetBrains enhances your workflow with features like auto-completion for schemas, support for SQL dialects, qualified table referencing, and advanced linting capabilities.

How to Use the Plugin

By default, the plugin will recognize files with the name atlas.hcl.

Follow this file naming convention to help the plugin recognize the correct dialect:

  • MySQL and MariaDB: *.my.hcl
  • PostgreSQL: *.pg.hcl
  • SQLite: *.lt.hcl
  • ClickHouse: *.ch.hcl
  • SQL Server: *.ms.hcl
  • Redshift: *.rs.hcl
  • Spanner: *.sp.hcl
  • Snowflake: *.sf.hcl
  • Atlas' test files: *.test.hcl
  • Migrate plan files: *.plan.hcl

Features

Auto-completion for schema resources

This refers to a feature that automatically suggests or completes the names of schema resources (e.g. tables, columns, etc.) as the user types, based on the database dialect being used. For a comprehensive list of the supported resources, please visit the following link: https://atlasgo.io/atlas-schema/hcl.

Syntax Highlighting

This refers to a feature that highlights syntax in a file based on the HashiCorp Configuration Language (HCL) syntax.

Txtar Support

The plugin provides syntax highlighting support for txtar files. Features include:

  • Syntax highlighting for file markers, filenames, and comments
  • Language injection for file contents based on filename
  • Customizable comment language via Settings > Languages & Frameworks > Atlas (default is Shell script)

Referencing Qualified tables

This refers to a feature that allows for referencing tables and their columns in a structured manner, either relative to the current location (e.g. column.id) or absolute to the table (e.g. table.user.column.id).

Linting

The tool provides linting capabilities, including duplicate resources/attributes, required attributes, and resource hierarchy validation.

Module Paths Configuration

Configure paths to Atlas modules for cross-module references. This feature allows schema files to reference schema definitions outside their immediate directory scope.

To configure module paths:

  1. Go to Settings > Languages & Frameworks > Atlas
  2. Under the Module Paths section, use the + button to add directories
  3. Enter either a relative path (resolved against project root) or absolute path to a directory that should be treated as a module root

How it works:

  • By default, schema files can only reference resources within their current directory
  • Adding a parent directory as a module path allows files in subdirectories to reference each other
  • For example, with a structure like: 
    /home/user/projects/atlas-project
  ├── schema.hcl
  ├── tables/
  │   └── users.hcl
  └── views/
      └── user_views.hcl
  • Adding /home/user/projects/atlas-project as a module path enables views/user_views.hcl to reference resources defined in tables/users.hcl or schema.hcl

This configuration is particularly useful in large projects with schema definitions split across multiple directories for better organization.

Need help? File issues on the Atlas Issue Tracker or join our Discord server.

idea-plugin.name: ZigBrains
idea-plugin.description:
Adds support for the Zig Language, utilizing the ZLS language server for advanced coding assistance.

Before you can properly use the plugin, you need to select or download the Zig toolchain and language server in Settings -> Languages & Frameworks -> Zig.

Debugging

Debugger settings are available in the Settings | Build, Execution, Deployment | Debugger menu, under the Zig section.

IDE Compatibility

Debugging Zig code is supported in any native debugging capable IDE. The following have been verified to work so far:

  • CLion
  • IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate
  • RustRover (including the non-commercial free version too)
  • GoLand
  • PyCharm Professional
  • Android Studio

Additionally, in CLion, the plugin uses the C++ Toolchains for sourcing the debugger (this can be toggled off in the settings).

The open-source Community edition IDEs don't have the native debugging code as it's a proprietary module, so you cannot debug zig code with them. You can still use those IDEs to develop code and use everything else the plugin has to offer.

Windows

Supported debuggers: LLDB, GDB

Linux

Supported debuggers: LLDB, GDB

MacOS

Supported debuggers: LLDB
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changed

  • Added support for running on Java 21 in IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1
  • Improved plugin zip file compression
  • Commenter improvements (https://codeberg.org/FalsePattern/zigbrains/issues/16)
    • Pressing enter at the end of comments/string no longer appends a new comment line
    • Regular comments also no longer get a comment prefix inserted on enter
  • Modified the per-file line markers to no longer interact with the build.zig system
    • This allows running individual tests in files and debugging test at the cost of not using build.zig for them (https://codeberg.org/FalsePattern/zigbrains/issues/14)
    • This feature needs to be revisited once Zig 0.17 is fully supported

Removed

idea-plugin.name: Flexible Freemarker
idea-plugin.description:
Full FreeMarker IDE with deep language support, custom macros, smart autocomplete, documentation and collaboration features.

Send us your feedback! Weâ€™d love to hear what you think. Bug reports, feature requests, and constructive criticism are incredibly valuable to us. Please reach out on GitHub or via email â€” we actively listen and iterate.

Features:

  • Complete Freemarker language implementation with full IDE support
    • Dedicated Freemarker editor built from scratch (Change file association to "Flexible Freemarker" on ftl files to enable)
    • Define your own Freemarker macros & functions with documentation & autocomplete through our Project Editor (File -> Settings -> Tools > Flexible Freemarker)
    • Import & Export all customizations to share with your team
    • Full autocomplete, element documentation, syntax highlighting and error detection
    • Recognizes inline expressions, directives, expressions and user directives
    • Supports structure view for template navigation
    • Context-aware code completion for all Freemarker constructs
    • Real-time validation and error detection
    • Smart handling of mixed HTML/CSS/JS within templates
    • Gutter icons for macros, functions, includes and imports
    • Inlay hints for macro parameters (Settings > Editor > Inlay Hints > FreeMarker)
    • "Surround With" (Ctrl+Alt+T) for quick directive wrapping
    • "Go to Symbol" (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N) for macro and function navigation
    • File templates for new FreeMarker files (File > New > FreeMarker File)
    • Breadcrumbs navigation showing macro and directive hierarchy
    • Full support for FreeMarker square bracket (alternate) tag syntax ([#if], [/@macro], [#-- comment --])
  • Load macro/function definitions from a shared URL for team collaboration (Settings > Tools > Flexible Freemarker)
  • Auto-detect freemarkerexport.yaml in project root for shared team definitions
  • Import Wizard: scan project FreeMarker files for macros/functions with documentation comment support

Hints

  • Create your own functions and macros with our settings editor (File -> Settings -> Tools > Flexible Freemarker)
  • Settings are stored per project
  • Configure inlay hints via Settings > Editor > Inlay Hints > FreeMarker (uses your custom macro definitions)
  • For the Freemarker editor, we strongly recommend setting the severity level for html elements during code inspection to a lower level as HTML can sometimes be interrupted by templating code
  • "Help, my autocomplete seems broken in .ftl files": Validate the file type association. A quick indicator is the file icon, which should display the scipio logo in the lower right corner. If missing, go to "Settings" > "File Types" > "Flexible Freemarker" > List should include ".ftl". Add if missing

Made by developers with a love for Freemarker

The integration is the work of Ilscipio:

We use Freemarker for many of our project frameworks (e.g.: Scipio ERP, Magnolia CMS) and love the framework for the power it provides. We have had great interaction with the community in the past.

This plugin is a complete reimplementation of Freemarker language support. We built it because we needed better IDE support for our extensive use of custom macros and functions. Rather than just adding basic highlighting, we created a full Freemarker development environment that understands the entire language and lets you extend it with your own definitions.

We figured this could be a useful tool to have for all the other Freemarker developers out there, so here it is :)

  • Special discounts are available for individual developers & of course for the whole Open Source community.
  • Original Freemarker contributors can contact us for a 100% discount.

Bugs & Feature Requests

If you have any questions, feature requests or stumble upon the occasional bug, come leave us a message at Ilscipio
