idea-plugin.name: Contextive
idea-plugin.description:
Contextive README

Documentation | Releases | Subscribe for Updates

Contextive is an IntelliJ Platform Plugin to assist developers in environments with a complex domain or project specific language, where words have a special meaning in the context of the project.

It should help new team members get up to speed more quickly in understanding domain-specific terms. By storing the glossary in your repository, and surfacing the definitions as you work on the code, it encourages the use of the domain-specific terms in your code, and regularly updating the definitions as the team's understanding evolves.

Installation

See IntelliJ IDEs (e.g. IDEA) Installation Instructions.

Getting Started

See setting up glossaries and defining terminology usage guides for details on getting started with Contextive.

Supported IDEs

The plugin uses the IntelliJ Language Server Protocol support, so it's only available in the IDEs where that feature is offered. See the JetBrains LSP Documentation for the latest list.

At time of writing, it includes:

  • IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate
  • WebStorm
  • PhpStorm
  • PyCharm Professional
  • DataSpell
  • RubyMine
  • CLion
  • Aqua
  • DataGrip
  • GoLand
  • Rider - not working in C# files
  • RustRover

IntelliJ Platform Compatibility

Contextive relies on the IntelliJ Platform Language Server Protocol APIs which were marked as experimental until IntelliJ Platform 2025.1.

Due to binary incompatibilities from v1.17.6, Contextive is marked as only compatible with 2025.1 onwards:

  • For IntelliJ Platform 2025.* or later, use Contextive's latest release (Recommended)
  • For IntelliJ Platform 2024.* or earlier, use Contextive v1.17.2

Features

  • Auto-complete from your Contextive Glossary
    • Shows definitions in auto-complete details
      • Note: Press F1 while the auto-complete list is shown to see the definition, and choose Show Automatically During Completion from the documentation panel's '3-dots' menu to have it show every time.)
  • Hover to show definitions from your Contextive Glossary
    • Hover over elements with suffixes & prefixes
    • Hover over usage of multiple terms combined using camelCase, PascalCase and snake_case
    • Hover over multi-word terms
    • Hover over plural of defined terms
    • Hover over aliases of defined terms
  • Put your glossaries near the code they support:
    • Terms relevant for the whole repository
    • Different terms relevant in different repositories
    • Terms relevant only in a subfolder of the repository
    • Multi-root workspaces
  • Works in all files

Coming Soon

  • IDE command to initialize the glossary file
  • UI to edit/manage Contextive Glossary
  • Internationalization support
  • Better support for key word identification in different languages (e.g. different syntax delimiters)

Known Issues

  • Auto-completion does not work at certain positions. See Issue #63
  • In Rider, C# files do not show documentation on hover, or 'quick documentation shortcut', or documentation during auto-complete, when opened in Solution mode. It does work when opening in file/folder mode. See Issue #65
  • When Contextive is installed, sometimes the 'native' language documentation is not shown. See Issue #89 and IJPL-181566

idea-plugin.name: SRD CodeFree
idea-plugin.description:
CodeFree is an AI tool provided by China Telecom's SRDCloud.It is a comprehensive solution that leverages AI capabilities to assist in code development. This tool is integrated on the IDE side to implement features such as code completion, code generation, code optimization, and programming assistance. Moreover, it seamlessly integrates with various existing capabilities within the SRDCloud, extending the development workflow into the IDE. The ultimate goal is to enhance the efficiency of code writing and development by bringing the entire development process into the IDE environment.

The features we currently support include:

  • Code Completion: Use the Tab key to select when the code auto-completion appears.

  • Code Q&A: Open the programming assistant page using the shortcut Alt+Shift+K.

  • Code Explanation: Right-click on the selected code and choose “SRD Codefree” > “Code Explanation”.

  • Code Annotation: Right-click on the selected code and choose “SRD Codefree” > “Code Annotation”.

  • Generate Unit Tests: Right-click on the selected code and choose “SRD Codefree” > “Generate Unit Tests.”

  • Code Optimization：Right-click on the selected code and choose “SRD Codefree” > “Code Optimization.”

  • Error message explanation: Click "CodeFree" at the error location in the console.

  • Knowledge Base: Select a srdcloud knowledge base to ask questions, and code can be generated directly based on the API documentation within the knowledge base.

  • Generate Commit Message: Click the CodeFree button in the IDE's commit message field to generate a commit message and link project work items

  • Agent: Tackle complex coding tasks in Agent mode

  • WorkItems: View the work items of the current project, and check details, toggle status, and log working hours.

  • Security Scan: Select project files for security scanning, supporting AI analysis and remediation of scan results

  • Diff Comment: Add and view comments on changed files in commits of the current repository branch.

  • Front-end Project:Generates front-end code and project files based on design mockups from the UX tool.

 

研发云CodeFree AI编程助手

研发云CodeFree是中国电信研发云的AI工具。CodeFree AI编程工具是使用AI能力协助用户进行代码开发的综合解决方案。这个工具在IDE侧实现了代码补全、编程助手等功能，更进一步和研发云各种已有的能力拉通，实现将研发流程下沉到IDE，以提高代码编写开发效率的目标。

我们目前支持的功能有：

  • 代码补全：当补全代码出现后，用tab键选择

  • 开发问答：使用快捷键Alt+Shift+K打开编程助手页面

  • 代码解释：选中代码后右键，选择“研发云codefree”>“代码解释”

  • 代码注释：选中代码后右键，选择“研发云codefree”>“代码注释”

  • 生成单元测试：选中代码后右键，选择“研发云codefree”>“生成单元测试”

  • 代码优化：选中代码后右键，选择“研发云codefree”>“生成优化建议”

  • 异常报错解释：在console的报错处点击“CodeFree“

  • 知识库：选择研发云的知识库进行提问，可根据知识库中的API文档直接生成代码

  • 生成提交信息：在IDE提交信息处点击CodeFree按钮生成提交信息，并关联项目工作项

  • 智能体：在智能体模式下完成复杂的编程任务

  • 工作项：查看当前项目的工作项，并查看详情、翻转状态和登记工时

  • 安全扫描：选择项目文件进行安全扫描，支持对扫描结果进行AI分析和修复

  • 代码评论：对当前代码库分支提交中的变更文件添加和查看评论

  • 前端工程：根据研发云UX工具的设计图生成前端代码工程文件

 

主要功能Features

代码补全 Code Completion

代码补全是本插件主要功能之一，通过本功能用户可以在编写代码过程中得到代码提示从而加快代码编写速度。代码补全功能包括触发、选择、确认和取消。具体功能如下：

  • 自动补全：在IDE输入代码时自动触发的补全

  • 手动补全：在代码中合适的位置，通过按组合键发起的补全，默认快捷键为ctrl+enter

  • 确认选择：当补全代码出现后，用tab键选择

  • 禁用补全：默认使用ctrl+shift+alt+o禁用代码补全

开发问答Code Q&A

开发问答，是以技术问答的形式，向用户提供开发和技术方面的建议。用户通过编程助手问答，可以在不离开IDE的情况下，获得解决当前代码工程的编程上的关键帮助，从而提升开发的质量和效率。具体操作如下：

  • 点击页面侧边栏的图标或使用快捷键Alt+Shift+K打开编程助手页面

  • 输入框输入问题，默认使用enter发送问题

  • AI生成问题答案，其中代码部分单独列出，并可单独复制

  • 查看历史问题，问题和答案均可复制

  • 新建会话，自动保存当前会话

  • 可以使用指令模板辅助提问

  • 支持重新回答

代码解释Code Explanation

支持代码解释功能，选中代码后执行“代码解释”的命令，AI将为您详细解析代码，让您轻松跨越语言障碍，快速了解代码的功能逻辑，提高开发效率。具体操作如下：

  • 在编辑器中选中代码后点击右键，选择“代码解释”功能

  • 在对话框中查看生成结果

生成代码注释Code Annotation

支持生成代码注释功能，为选中的代码一键生成函数注释及行间注释，节省编写注释的时间，使代码变得清晰易读。具体操作如下：

  • 在编辑器中选中代码后点击右键，选择“生成代码注释”功能

  • 在对话框中查看生成结果

生成单元测试Generate Unit Tests

支持生成单元测试功能，为选中的代码生成单元测试，同时支持一键生成新文件，节省宝贵的开发时间，使开发过程更加高效。具体操作如下：

  • 在编辑器中选中代码后点击右键，选择“生成单元测试”功能

  • 在对话框中查看生成结果

代码优化Code Optimization

支持代码优化功能，为选中的代码生成优化建议，提升代码质量。具体操作如下：

  • 在编辑器中选中代码后点击右键，选择“生成优化建议”功能

  • 在对话框中查看生成结果

异常报错解释Explanation of Exception Error

在IDEA中，支持对代码运行后的报错信息进行分析和提供修复建议，具体操作如下：

  • 在console中的报错处点击“CodeFree"按钮

  • 在对话框中查看生成结果

知识库提问Knowledge Base Inquiry

支持对研发云上您有权限的知识库进行提问，具体操作如下：

  • 在输入框上方选择知识库，输入问题进行提问

  • 当提问到知识库中的接口时，知识库提供相关的备选API可以进行选择

  • 选择后可在对话框中直接生成调用代码

生成提交信息Generate Commit Message

在IDE提交信息处点击CodeFree按钮生成提交信息，并关联项目工作项

  • 生成提交信息：在IDE提交信息处点击CodeFree按钮，则根据此次提交内容生成提交信息

  • 关联工作项：可选择一个或多个工作项关联此次提交

智能体Agent

能够端到端完成编码任务：根据任务描述，自主决策并感知环境，运用工程检索、文件编辑、终端等多种内置工具，实现对工程内多个文件的修改

  • 工具使用：支持文件阅读、编辑、创建、工程检索、终端等多种内置工具，并且支持用户配置MCP工具，扩展智能体的能力。

  • MCP：支持配置和使用MCP工具，扩展智能体的能力，同时在MCP市场可新建发布和安装使用 MCP

  • 规则：支持全局和项目级的规则文件配置

  • Skills：支持导入、使用项目级和用户级Skills，同时在Skills市场可新建发布和下载使用Skills

工作项WorkItems

查看当前本地打开的研发云项目的工作项，并查看详情、翻转状态和登记工时。

  • 工作项操作：支持查看和筛选当前项目的工作项，可以查看详情和翻转状态

  • 工时登记：对于工作项进行工时登记，数据同步研发云平台

安全扫描Security Scan

支持对当前项目代码文件进行安全扫描，快速发现潜在风险，提升代码安全性与质量。

  • 智能安全扫描：自由选择项目文件进行扫描，支持按严重程度和问题类型分类查看漏洞

  • AI 修复建议：提供漏洞智能分析，支持一键应用修复建议至代码文件

代码评论Diff Comment

对当前代码库分支提交中的变更文件添加和查看评论，评论信息会实时同步至研发云平台的代码中心，确保团队信息无缝流转。

  • 查看和添加评论：对当前代码库分支提交中的变更文件添加和查看评论

  • 评论更新通知：当前代码库分支下提交的变更文件有评论信息更新时，会及时通知

前端工程UX2Code

基于UX设计稿、前端脚手架、项目规则，一键生成高还原的前端代码。

  • 企业级定制支持：支持上传自有组件库、自定义脚手架，提升组件复用率

  • 多技术栈：兼容 React/Vue/uniapp，支持 Element、Vant等主流组件库

idea-plugin.name: HTMX Pro
idea-plugin.description:
HTMX Pro plugin provides comprehensive support for the HTMX, hyperscript and fixi.js libraries in JetBrains IDEs.

Features

  • Provides advanced coding assistance for HTMX, including syntax highlighting, code completions, quick documentation, inspections, and intentions
  • Supports both HTMX 2.x and HTMX 4.x
  • Works in HTML-compatible templating languages (Jinja2/Django, Thymeleaf, Handlebars, Twig, ...), and in JSX and TSX
  • Enables JavaScript language features with full type information in hx-on event handlers, hx-trigger event filters, and hx-vals, hx-request and hx-headers attributes
  • Enables CSS language features in selectors with support for the extended CSS selector syntax
  • Provides support for navigating and auto-completing endpoints within URLs
  • Provides support for HTMX extensions (enabled from Settings → Languages & Frameworks → HTMX)
  • Provides support for the fixi library, including code completion and quick documentation for fx-* attributes and events, CSS selectors in fx-target, and endpoint navigation in fx-action (enabled from Settings → Languages & Frameworks → Fixi.js)
  • Provides support for hyperscript, including syntax highlighting, code completion, quick documentation, formatting, inspections, type inference, and navigation (enabled from Settings → Languages & Frameworks → Hyperscript)

Licenses

Due to marketplace limitations, different licensing options are offered as separate plugins:
  • HTMX Pro (Lifetime) offers perpetual licenses.
  • HTMX Pro offers monthly and yearly licenses.
Both plugins share the same functionality.

idea-plugin.name: BeanCopy
idea-plugin.description:
Usage Instructions:
  1. Place the cursor on the variable name where you want to copy the fields from other variables.
  2. Click on the menu Code -> Generate, then select Copy properties.
  3. Enter the name of the variable to copy fields from, select the fields to copy, and the relevant code will be generated automatically.
Note:
  • The variable to copy from must be declared before the target variable.
  • Both variables must have the same fields, and these fields must have corresponding get and set methods.
  • The fields will only appear in the selection box if they have matching types and are eligible for copying.

idea-plugin.name: Thymeleaf Support
idea-plugin.description:
Thymeleaf Support is an IntelliJ IDEA plugin designed to enhance the development experience for building web applications using Thymeleaf templates. This plugin provides comprehensive autocompletion for common Thymeleaf attributes and dialects, allowing developers to quickly and accurately build templates with ease.

Supported Thymeleaf namespaces:

  • th: Thymeleaf core attributes (e.g., th:text, th:if, th:each, and more)
  • sec: Spring Security attributes (e.g., sec:authorize, sec:authentication)
  • layout: Layout dialect attributes (e.g., layout:decorator, layout:fragment)

Key Features:

  • Autocompletion for Thymeleaf, Spring Security, and Layout dialect attributes
  • Detailed tooltips for attributes with descriptions
  • Seamless integration with IntelliJ IDEA’s HTML and XML editors

This plugin is perfect for developers working with Spring Boot and Thymeleaf, reducing the manual effort required to build dynamic templates and enhancing the overall productivity of Thymeleaf-based projects.

For more information, visit the Thymeleaf project website.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Version 1.2.2 - IntelliJ IDEA Compatibility Update

Compatibility

  • Kept the plugin build on the supported IntelliJ IDEA 2024.2 platform baseline.
  • Removed the explicit upper build cap to allow compatibility with IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2 and future IntelliJ versions.
  • Kept the build aligned with the Java 21 runtime requirements for the supported baseline.
  • Updated the IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin to the current 2.x toolchain.

Developer Experience

  • Aligned CI with the Java 21 toolchain required by the plugin build.
  • Updated release automation to run plugin verification before publishing to JetBrains Marketplace.

Release Date: September 4, 2026

Version 1.2.1 - IntelliJ Platform Compatibility Update

Compatibility

  • Updated the plugin build to the current IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.x toolchain.
  • Raised the supported IntelliJ baseline to 2024.2 and verified compatibility through 2026.1.
  • Aligned the build with the current Java runtime requirements for newer IntelliJ IDEA versions.

Internal Changes

  • Modernized the Gradle wrapper and plugin packaging configuration for current IntelliJ platform releases.
  • Removed brittle internal HTML descriptor checks from attribute descriptor providers to reduce platform-coupling risk.
  • Verified the packaged plugin successfully with JetBrains Plugin Verifier against current IDEA builds.

Release Date: May 18, 2026

Version 1.2.0 - New Features and Enhancements

New Features

  • Added support for <th:block> synthetic tags, enabling IntelliJ IDEA to fully recognize and autocomplete the non-rendered <th:block> element used in Thymeleaf templates.
  • Introduced smart URL completion for th:href and th:action attributes, automatically detecting mappings from Spring @Controller classes and suggesting valid URL paths.
  • Added Spring model attribute discovery, providing IntelliJ with awareness of @ModelAttribute methods and parameters to enhance context-based completion and validation.
  • Overhauled expression completion with intelligent suggestions for ${...}, *{...}, and #{...} expressions, including property chain resolution and auto-insertion of proper syntax.

Enhancements

  • Added new attribute completions for th:errors, th:errorclass, and th:field to improve support for form validation and binding.
  • Expanded attribute descriptions and tooltips for greater clarity and consistency across Thymeleaf, Layout, and Spring Security dialects.
  • Improved internal caching for PSI-based model inspection, resulting in faster and more responsive code completion.
  • Simplified Gradle build configuration with java.toolchain support and unified Kotlin/Java compile targets for JDK 17.
  • Updated IntelliJ platform compatibility to support versions 2023.1 through 2025.2.

Developer Experience

  • Renamed the default run configuration to “Run Plugin with debug” for clarity during development.
  • Refined project structure and logging to align with current IntelliJ Gradle plugin best practices.
  • Updated documentation, README.md, and CHANGELOG.md to reflect new features and usage details.

Summary

  • Template Tags: Full support for <th:block>
  • Form Handling: Added th:field, th:errors, th:errorclass
  • Spring Integration: Model and Controller awareness for smarter completions
  • URL Completion: Auto-suggests mappings from Spring controllers
  • Expression Completion: Rich suggestions for ${}, *{}, and #{} expressions
  • Build & Compatibility: Modernized Gradle setup and extended IDE support

Release Date: November 5, 2025

Version 1.1.0 - Enhancements and Bug Fixes

New Features

  • Added menu options to insert Thymeleaf, Thymeleaf Layout, and Spring Security namespaces directly into HTML files.
  • Automatic registration of common Thymeleaf namespaces into the IntelliJ schema registry, reducing manual configuration effort.

Enhancements

  • Improved internal structure for managing and accessing namespace attributes and values.
  • Refined UI integration to provide a better user experience when working with HTML files.
  • Added support for ignoring unknown namespaces in the schema registry upon plugin installation.
  • Updated compatibility settings for better support with newer IntelliJ versions.

Bug Fixes

  • Resolved issues with namespace attributes not being recognized properly in some cases.
  • Fixed potential conflicts when registering namespaces in the IntelliJ schema registry.
  • Addressed stability issues with autocompletion for certain namespace attributes.

Notes

  • The Spring Security Thymeleaf namespace defaults to the latest version. If using an earlier version, please update the namespace manually and add it to Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Schemas and DTDs | Ignored Schemas and DTDs.

idea-plugin.name: G-pilot
idea-plugin.description:
G-pilot IDEA Extension Plugin

Introduction

G-pilot is a code completion tool developed by the Technology Center, designed to provide a private deployment within the company, particularly optimized for languages such as GS, C#, and Lua.

Currently, G-pilot has developed IDE plugins for VSCode, VS2022, and JetBrains series (IDEA, PyCharm, CLion). Users can choose based on their needs.

  • G-pilot Model Training: G-pilot GitLab
  • G-pilot VSCode Plugin: G-pilot VSCode Plugin
  • G-pilot VSCode Plugin Backend: G-pilot LSP
  • G-pilot VS Extension Plugin: G-pilot VS Plugin
  • G-pilot JetBrains Series Extension Plugin: G-pilot IDEA Plugin
  • G-pilot VS and JetBrains Series Backend: G-pilot VS LSP

Feishu User Communication Group

G-pilot is continuously being iterated and optimized. We invite you to click the Feishu user group link to join the group and provide us with valuable suggestions for modifications and optimizations. You can also communicate and exchange ideas directly in the group for any issues encountered while using the plugin. Notifications for new version releases will also be shared in the group.

Features

Currently, G-pilot supports single-line code completion, multi-line code completion, and comment generation features. Additional AI features will be developed based on user demand.

Installation Method

Note: Before using the G-pilot plugin, other code completion plugins such as Copilot, Comate, Marscode, TabNine, etc., must be disabled to avoid conflicts in code completion functionality.

In the IDEA menu bar, select File, then click Settings to open the settings window. In the left sidebar, click Plugins, then select Marketplace. Search for G-pilot in the search bar below, and after clicking Install, restart IDEA to complete the installation:

Usage Instructions

1. Single-Line Code Completion

Trigger Methods

  1. Code changes will automatically trigger completion prompts.
  2. Press the combination Shift + Ctrl + Space to manually trigger a single-line code completion prompt.

Completion Display

Upon successful triggering of completion, the result will be displayed in gray text after the cursor, as shown below:

Accepting Completion

Press the Tab key to accept the complete completion.

Closing Completion Display

Press the Esc key to close the current completion result display.

2. Multi-Line Code Completion

Trigger Method

Press the combination Shift + Ctrl + Enter to manually trigger a multi-line code completion prompt.

Completion Display, Acceptance, and Closing

These are consistent with the single-line code completion functionality.

3. Comment Generation Code Feature

Trigger Method

Similarly, at a comment line or the line after a comment, press the combination Shift + Ctrl + Enter to trigger comment generation code prompts.

Completion Display, Acceptance, and Closing

These are consistent with the single-line code completion functionality.

4. Important Parameter Settings

In the IDEA menu bar, select File, then click Settings to open the settings interface. Expand the Tools option in the left sidebar, find G-pilot, and select it to display the relevant parameter settings, as shown below:

Important Parameters

  • Code Completion Recommendation Display Threshold
    • Default Value: 3
    • Range: 0 to positive infinity
    • Description: A smaller value indicates stricter judgment, resulting in fewer displayed completion recommendations but higher quality.
    • Special Values: 0 means no completion recommendations will be displayed. An empty value represents positive infinity, showing all completion recommendations.
  • Consent for Code Data Collection
    • Default: Checked
    • Description: If checked, data will be sent to the backend for recording every time a completion recommendation is accepted (the sent data does not include user information and is anonymous). This data will be used for the ongoing iteration and upgrade of the G-pilot model.
  • Automatically Jump to End of Line After Accepting Completion
    • Default: Checked
    • Description: If checked, the cursor will automatically jump to the end of the line after accepting a completion recommendation.

G-pilot IDEA扩展插件

简介

G-pilot是技术中心开发的代码补全工具，旨在为大家提供公司内网私有部署的、针对GS、C#、Lua等语言特别优化过的代码补全工具。

目前G-pilot已开发了VSCode、VS2022、jetbrains系列（IDEA、pycharm、Clion）等IDE插件，大家可以根据自己的需求选择使用。

G-pilot模型训练：https://m68gitlab.g-bits.com/aigc/g-pilot

G-pilot vscode插件：https://m68gitlab.g-bits.com/aigc/g-pilot-vscode

G-pilot vscode插件后端：https://m68gitlab.g-bits.com/aigc/g-pilot-lsp

G-pilot VS扩展插件：https://m68gitlab.g-bits.com/aigc/g-pilot-vs

G-pilot jetbrains系列（IDEA、pycharm、Clion）扩展插件：https://m68gitlab.g-bits.com/aigc/g-pilot-idea

G-pilot VS、jetbrains系列（IDEA、pycharm、Clion）扩展插件后端：https://m68gitlab.g-bits.com/aigc/g-pilot-vs-lsp

飞书使用交流群

目前G-pilot还在不断迭代和优化过程，欢迎大家点击飞书使用交流群链接加入飞书使用交流群给我们提供宝贵的修改和优化建议。大家在使用过程遇到任何问题都可以直接在群里沟通和交流，插件的新版本发布也会在群里进行通知。

功能

目前G-pilot支持单行代码补全功能、多行代码补全功能、注释生成代码功能，其他AI功能后续根据大家需求来开发。

安装方式

注意：使用G-pilot插件前，需要将其他代码补全插件如Copilot、Comate、Marscode、TabNine等禁用，避免代码补全的功能发生冲突。

在IDEA菜单栏中选择文件，再点击设置打开设置界面，在左边栏中点击插件，然后选择Marketplace，在下方搜索：G-pilot，然后点击安装成功后，重启IDEA即可：

使用方法

1. 单行代码补全功能

触发方式

  1. 代码文本发生改动时，会自动触发补全提示。
  2. 按组合键Shift + Ctrl + 空格，可以主动触发一次单行代码补全提示。

补全显示

补全成功触发后，会在光标后方以灰色字体显示补全结果，如下图所示：

补全采用

按Tab键即可采用全部补全。

关闭补全显示

按Esc键即可关闭本次补全结果的显示。

2. 多行代码补全功能

触发方式

按组合键Shift + Ctrl + Enter，可以主动触发多行代码补全提示。

补全显示、补全采用、关闭补全显示

与单行代码补全功能一致。

3. 注释生成代码功能

触发方式

与多行代码补全功能同理，在注释行处或者注释行下一行通过组合键Shift + Ctrl + Enter，也可主动触发注释生成代码提示。

补全显示、补全采用、关闭补全显示

与单行代码补全功能一致。

4. 重要参数设置

在IDEA菜单栏中选择文件，再点击设置打开设置界面。在左边栏点击展开工具选项，找到G-pilot，选择后则会显示出G-pilot相关的参数设置，如下图所示：

其中比较重要的参数如下：

  • 代码补全推荐显示阈值
    • 默认值：3
    • 范围：0~正无穷
    • 说明：数值越小则判断越严格，显示的补全代码推荐越少，显示的补全代码质量越高。
    • 特殊值：0代表所有补全代码推荐都不进行显示。空代表正无穷，所有补全推荐都会显示出来。
  • 是否同意进行代码数据收集
    • 默认：勾选
    • 说明：如果勾选了，则会在你每次采纳补全推荐时，将该数据发送给后端进行记录（发送的数据不包含用户信息，收集的是匿名数据）。这些数据将会用于后续G-pilot模型的持续迭代升级。
  • 采纳补全后是否自动跳转到行尾
    • 默认：勾选
    • 说明：如果勾选了，则会在你每次采纳补全推荐后自动跳转到行尾。

idea-plugin.name: CI Aid for GitLab
idea-plugin.description:
Do you frequently work with GitLab CI Yaml files in Intellij and find yourself constantly using Shift Shift to search for stages, script files or included files? CI Aid for GitLab to the rescue. With this plugin, enjoy automatic GitLab™ schema provision, navigation across elements, stage/job autocompletion, and prominent error notifications when issues are detected in configuration. Reduce errors and accelerate your pipeline development.

GITLAB is a trademark of GitLab Inc. in the United States and other countries and regions. This plugin is not affiliated, endorsed, sponsored, or approved with or by GitLab Inc.

Features

  • Autocomplete & Syntax Highlighting: Write GitLab CI YAML files with confidence. Autocompletion suggestions and multi level syntax highlighting will make your code easy to navigate and work with.
  • Local Path Resolution: Effortless navigation with one-click access to scripts, included files, job needs and more.
  • Remote Includes Caching: Ability to cache remote includes e.g., components, templates etc. to seamlessly work with remote files as local files
  • Errors and Quick fix: IDE integrated inspections for undefined needs, missing scripts/includes and quick fix to create files on the fly
  • Script Language Injection: Injection of shell language in script blocks for .sh autocompletes, suggestions and shortcuts
  • Schema Support: Auto detection of GitLab CI YAML and auto schema configuration, with descriptions, errors and suggestions for GitLab known keywords

Getting Started

  • Installation: Download the plugin from JetBrains Marketplace
  • Usage: Enjoy autocomplete, syntax highlighting, and much more with GitLab CI YAML files.

idea-plugin.name: OllamAssist
idea-plugin.description:
OllamAssist Plugin for IntelliJ IDEA

OllamAssist is a plugin designed to integrate seamlessly with IntelliJ IDEA, leveraging the power of Ollama to enhance developer productivity. This intelligent assistant offers conversational interactions with your code, insightful discussions, and smart code autocompletion, making it your ultimate coding companion. All processing is done locally, ensuring maximum privacy and allowing you to work without an internet connection.

Key Features

  • In-IDE Chat with Ollama Models: Engage directly with AI for insights and explanations, all within your JetBrains IDE. The model has access to your project's indexed sources via RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), enabling context-aware responses based on your codebase.
  • Enhanced Context Awareness: Boost model accuracy by providing your workspace for tailored suggestions.
  • Generate commit message: OllamAssist can generate a commit message based on the current git diff, following the Conventional Commits specification..
  • Offline Mode: Enjoy full functionality offline after loading the model and data.
  • Experimental Smart Code Autocomplete: Anticipates your next steps in coding, offering intelligent suggestions when pressing Shift+Space.
    • Press Enter to insert the suggested code.
    • Press any other key to dismiss the suggestion.

Customizable Model Settings

Developers can choose the AI model to be used via the plugin's Settings page, ensuring flexibility and alignment with their specific requirements.

Minimum Requirements

For the latest system requirements, please refer to the official Ollama requirements page.

Get Started in 5 Minutes

  1. Download and start Ollama.
  2. Open a terminal and download a model using the command: ollama run llama3.1.
  3. Start IntelliJ IDEA, go to Plugins > Marketplace, and search for "OllamAssist".
  4. Install the "OllamAssist" plugin.
  5. In the OllamAssist settings window, select the Ollama model if it isn't already set to llama3.1.
  6. Start coding with your smart OllamAssist!
idea-plugin.change-notes:
V1.14.1 — Project Context Works on Every Supported IDE

  • fix: On IDE 2025.3 and later, every chat message logged "Hybrid retrieval failed" and the answer came without any context from your project. The keyword search relied on a Lucene module compiled for a different Lucene version than the one the IDE ships. It now uses only what the IDE provides, so it works on Lucene 9 (up to 2025.2) and Lucene 10 (from 2025.3) alike. Thanks to Simon Farrant for the report and the diagnosis (#182).

V1.14.0 — Switch Off What You Don't Want

  • feat: Inline code completion can be turned off — Settings > OllamAssist > Actions > Enable inline code completion. Off means no inlay, no suggestion, and Enter behaves exactly as it does without the plugin. The chat, RAG and the other features keep working.
  • fix: The Enter key handler was replaced IDE-wide and never restored, and each completion request wrapped the previous wrapper. Typing Enter could trigger the plugin long after the last suggestion, in every editor of the IDE.
  • fix: A key listener was attached to the editor on every completion request instead of once, so listeners accumulated for the whole session.
  • fix: Completion could raise "Read access is allowed from inside read-action only" instead of returning a suggestion. Its fallback path read the editor from a background thread without a read action — so the code meant to survive a failure was the code that threw.
  • fix: Completion no longer holds a read action while calling Ollama for embeddings and searching the index. Holding one across a network call blocks write actions, which freezes typing until the call returns.
  • [Alpha] fix: Agent edits landed at the wrong line in any file longer than 150 lines. The planner was shown excerpts numbered from 1 while being told the numbers were absolute, and the edit was then applied to the real file. Line numbers sent to the planner are now those of the file, and each gap names the lines it hides.
  • feat: "Don't show again" — mute release notifications for good, from the update balloon or from the What's New dialog.
  • feat: The decision is reversible in Settings > OllamAssist > UI > Notifications ("Show release notifications after an update").
  • fix: The update balloon no longer reappears at every IDE start — it was only acknowledged when the balloon expired, which never happens for a balloon left untouched in the Notifications tool window.
  • fix: Changing a setting in the UI tab alone is now applied — the tab was missing from the settings modification check, so the font size multiplier could be silently discarded.

V1.13.1 — Custom Prompts Are Persisted

  • fix/issue-170: The Chat System Prompt and Refactor User Prompt no longer revert to their defaults when the IDE restarts — customised prompts are now written to disk.
  • fix: The Actions settings (auto-approve file creation, tools enabled) were silently affected by the same defect and are persisted as well.
  • fix: Removed emoji from the default chat prompt — the settings serializer cannot store characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane and dropped them silently when the prompt was saved.

V1.13.0 — API Key / Bearer Authentication

  • feat/issue-166: Bearer token / API key authentication — connect to an Ollama endpoint behind an authenticated proxy (e.g. OpenWebUI), in addition to Basic Auth.
  • feat: Authentication mode selector in Settings > OllamAssist > Ollama (None / Basic Auth / API Key).
  • feat: The Authorization header is now applied to every Ollama request, including the startup prerequisite health checks.
  • fix: Existing Basic Auth configurations remain fully backward compatible — no reconfiguration required.
  • fix: Remove a reflection error (NoSuchMethodException) logged on every keystroke in the settings panel.

V1.12.0 — Agent Mode (Alpha)

  • [Alpha] Agent mode — give a natural-language goal, the agent discovers relevant files, generates a plan and executes it step by step with your approval before any change.
  • feat: Discover → Plan → Execute pipeline — workspace search, single LLM planning call, deterministic Java execution.
  • feat: Supported operations — create file, edit file (line-based), delete file, append to file.
  • feat: One approval dialog for the full plan — review all steps before any file is touched.
  • feat: Dedicated agent model selector — pick a function-calling-capable model without changing your chat model.
  • feat: Agent execution history popup — view past executions with per-step success/failure status.
  • feat: Colored diff view in approval dialogs — removed/added lines highlighted in red/green.
  • feat: Stop button cancels agent execution between phases.
  • feat: Step progress counter shown next to the Stop button during execution.
  • security: SecretDetector blocks writing secrets to files; path traversal guards on all file operations.
  • security: Shell chaining operators (;, &&, ||) in commands always require user confirmation.

V1.11.0

  • feat: Conversation management - Conversations are now persisted per project across IDE sessions.
  • feat: Create multiple named conversations and switch between them from the chat panel.
  • feat: Conversation titles are auto-generated from the first message (60 characters max).
  • feat: Delete individual conversations with a confirmation dialog.
  • feat: Resume any conversation exactly where you left it after restarting the IDE.
  • feat: RAG sources panel - each AI response now shows the retrieved code chunks used to generate it.
  • feat: Clickable source links navigate directly to the corresponding file in the editor.
  • feat: Source icons match IntelliJ's native file type icons based on extension.
  • feat: Hybrid retrieval with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (KNN + BM25) for more accurate code search.
  • feat: PSI-aware chunking splits Java files by class and method for higher retrieval precision.
  • feat: Index versioning with automatic migration - stale indexes are rebuilt transparently on upgrade.
  • feat: Cross-IDE compatibility - PSI chunking degrades gracefully in PyCharm, CLion, and other JetBrains products.
  • fix: ConcurrentModificationException in FontUtils caused by recursive computeIfAbsent on shared HashMap.

V1.10.4

  • feat: Interactive font size slider (50% to 200%) with real-time preview in settings panel.
  • feat: All UI components now respect IDE font settings with semantic font levels (title, subtitle, normal, small, code).
  • feat: Improved support for HiDPI and 2K displays with automatic DPI-aware scaling.
  • feat: Centralized FontUtils class for consistent font management across the plugin.

idea-plugin.name: Kotlin External FIR Support
idea-plugin.description:
Run Kotlin compiler plugins in the IDE.

TLDR

  • Automatic Plugin Resolution and Safe Loading
  • Exception Analysis
  • Diagnostics & Management UI
  • Manual Control
  • Preconfigured for known plugins (kotlinx-rpc) and highly configurable for any other

Guides

Check out our advanced usage guide: GUIDE.md

If you are a compiler plugin developer, check out our plugin development guide.

Use Any Kotlin Compiler Plugin Inside IDE

By default, the IDE cannot safely run external Kotlin compiler plugins that are not bundled with the compiler itself (like kotlinx-rpc) because their version often conflicts with the IDE's internal Kotlin compiler. This incompatibility can lead to exceptions that freeze your UI, syntax highlighting, and code analysis.

This plugin enables you to use these compiler plugins safely in your IDE

  1. It enables plugins: KEFS intercepts requests for plugins and automatically finds, downloads, and loads an IDE-compatible version in the background.
  2. It improves stability: Even if a compatible plugin breaks and throws an exception, KEFS detects it, notifies you via a banner, and provides actions (like disabling the plugin) to restore your IDE's functionality immediately.

This solves the core instability problem and allows you to benefit from your compiler plugins' IDE-specific features, like custom diagnostics, all within the editor.

Preconfigured for known plugins (kotlinx-rpc) and highly configurable for any other.

Core Features

1. Automatic Plugin Resolution

KEFS automatically detects the compiler plugins used in your project. It then finds and downloads a compatible version from a configurable list of Maven repositories (including local ones).

  • Flexible Version Matching: Configure how the plugin finds compatible versions with strategies like Exact, Same Major, or Latest.
  • Background Caching: All downloads and resolutions happen in the background to never block your UI. Resolved plugins are cached locally for instant access.
  • Local Development Hot-Reload: Actively watches local Maven repositories for changes. When you re-publish a new version of your plugin locally, KEFS detects the file change and reloads it in the IDE automatically.

Compiler Plugin DevKit

Plugins built with the Compiler Plugin DevKit need no configuration at all. Their jars already contain a build for every supported Kotlin compiler version, so KEFS detects them by their content and loads them as is – nothing is searched for or downloaded. Exception analysis, hot-reload and the diagnostics UI work for them the same way.

The dev kit is available only internally at JetBrains for now.

2. Exception Analysis

Compiler plugins should never throw exceptions, as this can freeze IDE analysis. KEFS actively monitors the IDE for exceptions thrown by loaded compiler plugins.

When a failure is detected, KEFS provides immediate, actionable solutions:

  • Editor Banner: A non-intrusive banner appears at the top of your editor, identifying the failing plugin.
  • Disable Plugin: Instantly disable the failing plugin from the banner to restore your IDE's highlighting and analysis.
  • Auto-Disable: A "set it and forget it" option that will automatically disable any plugin that throws an exception, notifying you with a small pop-up.

3. Diagnostics & Management UI

KEFS provides a full suite of UI tools to give you complete visibility and control over your compiler plugins.

  • "KEFS Diagnostics" Tool Window: A dedicated window that shows you every detected plugin and its status.
    • See which plugins were successfully loaded, which failed (e.g., Failed To Fetch, Not Found), and which haven't been requested yet.
    • Inspect detailed error messages for fetch/resolution failures.
    • View detailed reports for runtime exceptions, including stack traces, to help debug plugin failures.
  • Settings Page (Tools > Kotlin External FIR Support): A new settings panel to manage all plugin behavior.
    • Artifacts: Configure your plugin "bundles" (e.g. if a plugin consists of multiple jars), set their version-matching strategy, and assign them to specific repositories, or use the default.
    • Repositories: Add, edit, and remove remote (URL) or local (file path) Maven repositories.
    • General: Toggle the Exception Analyzer on/off and manage the "auto-disable" feature.

4. Manual Control

Quickly manage the plugin's state from the Find Action (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+A) menu:

  • Update Plugins: Forces a check for new plugin versions in your repositories.
  • Refresh Plugins: Clears the in-memory state and re-runs resolution.
  • Clear Caches: Deletes all downloaded plugin jars from the disk cache.
  • Copy Kotlin IDE Version: Copies the IDE's internal Kotlin compiler version to the clipboard.

Support

If you encounter any issues, report them on GitHub.

If any exceptions are thrown, you can use the built-in Report to the 3rd Party action to send a bug report to us.

Exception analysis, hot-reload and statuses in the tool window work for them as for any other plugin. idea-plugin.name: Typescript Namespace Imports
idea-plugin.description:
Description

This plugin helps you with namespace imports when writing code.

A namespace import is an import like:

import * as moduleName from 'path/to/module_name';

This plugin offers the camelCase version of every typescript file in your workspace as a module inside of autocomplete.

For example if the file module_name exists in your workspace, it will offer to import it as a module called moduleName.

  • As you type "moduleNa", you will see "moduleName" as an autocomplete suggestion.
  • If you select it, then import * as moduleName from 'path/to/module_name'; will automatically be added to the top of the file.

Settings

Under "Settings" > "Tools" > "Typescript Namespace Imports", you can choose whether single or double quotes are used for the auto-inserted import statement.

idea-plugin.name: Artemis String Normalizer
idea-plugin.description:
Artemis String Normalizer

This plugin is an independent tool and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to Artemis or TUM.

A postfix template tool that converts Artemis-encoded strings into clean, readable Java code.

Features

  • Replaces the special symbol ⎵ with a real space
  • Converts variables inside <...> into Java identifiers
  • Ignores invalid placeholders (e.g. with spaces or symbols)
  • Escapes strings safely for Java source code
  • Works in .java files via postfix templates
  • .artemis – converts into Java string expressions using concatenation
  • .artemisf – converts into a complete System.out.printf statement with matching arguments

Examples

String expression: 
"(<X>/<Y>)⎵Enter⎵your⎵guess:".artemis
-->
"(" + X + "/" + Y + ") Enter your guess:"
Printf output: 
"(<X>/<Y>)⎵Enter⎵your⎵guess:".artemisf
-->
System.out.printf("(%s/%s) Enter your guess:", X, Y);
idea-plugin.change-notes: Allow whitespaces in variable names

idea-plugin.name: Structurizr DSL
idea-plugin.description:
Structurizr DSL — Architecture Diagrams as Code in Your IDE

Full language support for Structurizr DSL — the industry-standard text-based language for defining C4 model architecture diagrams. Write, navigate, and preview your software architecture directly in your JetBrains IDE with all the features developers expect.

Editing and Authoring

  • Syntax Highlighting — Full colorization for keywords, strings, comments, identifiers, and variable substitutions
  • Intelligent Code Completion — Context-aware suggestions for elements, relationships, views, and properties, including smart relationship-target completion
  • 21 Live Templates — Quick scaffolding for workspaces, systems, containers, components, views, groups, and more
  • Color Preview — Gutter swatches for hex colors in styles with a built-in color picker
  • Code Folding and Formatting — Collapse blocks and auto-format DSL files with configurable style

Navigation and Analysis

  • Go to Definition — Ctrl+Click to jump to element definitions
  • Find Usages — Alt+F7 to find all references to an element
  • Structure View — Hierarchical tree of workspace, model, views, and elements
  • 10 Code Inspections — Detects errors like undefined references, duplicate identifiers, duplicate view keys, and invalid colors with quick fixes

Diagram Preview and Export

  • Live Diagram Preview — Real-time C4 diagram rendering as you type
  • Split Editor — Side-by-side DSL code and diagram view
  • Multi-Format Export — Export as SVG, PNG, PlantUML, or Mermaid
  • Copy to Clipboard — Copy diagrams in any format for instant sharing
  • CLI Integration — Auto-download and manage the Structurizr CLI

Requirements

  • JetBrains IDE 2024.3+ (IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, CLion, and all others)
  • Windows, macOS, or Linux

Support

  • Issue Tracker
  • Structurizr DSL Language Reference
  • C4 Model Documentation
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.6.1 — Compatibility Fix

  • Critical fix: .dsl files would not open on IntelliJ 2026.2 — IntelliJ 2026.2 moved JCEF out of the core platform into a separate bundled plugin, so the diagram preview could no longer resolve JBCefApp. The resulting NoClassDefFoundError took down the whole split editor: the tab flashed open and closed again, leaving no way to edit a .dsl file. The plugin now declares the JCEF module and the preview degrades to a message instead of failing
  • Editing never depends on the preview any more — if the embedded browser is missing or fails to start for any reason, the text editor, inspections and navigation keep working; only the diagram pane is replaced by an explanatory placeholder
  • Preview tool window hardened — the same guard now covers the Structurizr Preview tool window, which previously created a JCEF browser unconditionally

2026.6.0 — Productivity Release

  • Critical fix: language engine restored — A lexer table-unpacking defect made every file tokenize as one bad character, silently disabling the parser, inspections, navigation, structure view, and identifier completion. All language features now actually work as advertised
  • Color Preview & Picker — Hex colors in element/relationship styles now show a swatch in the editor gutter; click it to change the color with the IDE color picker
  • Smart Relationship Completion (FR-306) — Completing after -> now suggests only defined elements (excluding the source), ranked above keywords
  • Duplicate View Key Inspection (FR-507) — Detects views sharing the same key, which Structurizr rejects at export time
  • 4 New Live Templates — grp (group), props (properties), anim (animation), autolay (autoLayout) — 21 templates total
  • Fixed: colour (British spelling) values are now validated by the invalid-color inspection
  • Performance: Duplicate identifier inspection no longer rescans the file for every element

2026.4.5 — Freemium Release

  • Freemium licensing — Released with product-descriptor for JetBrains Marketplace freemium model (code: PSTRUCTURIZRDSL)

What's New

  • Syntax Highlighting - Full colorization for keywords, strings, comments, identifiers, and variable substitutions in Structurizr DSL files
  • Intelligent Code Completion - Context-aware suggestions for elements, relationships, views, and all DSL keywords

idea-plugin.name: Google Cloud Dataform
idea-plugin.description:
A comprehensive IntelliJ IDEA plugin that brings full language support for Google Cloud Dataform projects, letting you write, navigate, run and debug SQLX pipelines without leaving the IDE.

SQLX Language Support

  • Full syntax highlighting for SQLX files, covering embedded SQL, JavaScript and config blocks.
  • Smart code completion for built-in Dataform functions (ref(), declare(), publish(), etc.), JavaScript/TypeScript symbols, and Dataform template expressions (${...}), with automatic completion popup on $.
  • Native BigQuery SQL dialect support, including syntax validation and real-time error highlighting.
  • JSON Schema–powered validation and autocompletion for workflow_settings.yaml, generated dynamically from your project's Dataform configuration.

Navigation & Code Intelligence

  • Jump between references, includes and declarations with Ctrl+Click / Ctrl+B.
  • Column-level navigation: Ctrl+Click a column in a SQLX query to jump straight to its declaration in the source table.
  • Show Column Usages (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+U, also available from the editor context menu): list every downstream place where a given column is read across the project — the reverse direction of Go to Declaration.
  • Quick Documentation (Ctrl+Q) for table references, resolved schemas, column metadata, and the built-in BigQuery function catalog (signatures, descriptions, examples).
  • Clickable links to workflow configuration properties.

Refactoring

  • In-place column rename (Shift+F6) with its own dedicated engine: it walks the plugin's column lineage graph to propagate the new name across every file where the column flows — not just the current statement — including through SELECT * resolution, incremental actions, and unrelated join chains, then refreshes the resolved schema.

Data Lineage

  • Built-in lineage graph view (Open Lineage View action) that visualizes upstream/downstream dependencies between Dataform actions.
  • Column-level lineage tracing, so you can trace exactly where a given column's data originates across your pipeline, including through renamed/aliased columns.

Run & Execute

  • Native run configurations for Dataform workflows, launched straight from IntelliJ's Run/Debug toolbar.
  • One-click gutter icons in the SQLX editor to execute the current action's workflow without leaving the file.

Formatting

  • Built-in formatter aware of injected SQL, JavaScript and config blocks inside SQLX files.
  • Optional integration with Sqlfluff for external, configurable SQL formatting.

Project Tooling

  • New Project wizard to scaffold Dataform projects with the correct structure.
  • New SQLX File action with ready-made templates for every Dataform action type: Table, View, Incremental table, Assertion, Operations, and Declaration.
  • Automatic Dataform CLI detection, installation and setup.
  • Fast project indexing of Dataform core definitions and JavaScript symbols for responsive completion and search.

Notes internes :

  • Column rename is real and implemented via a custom DataformColumnRenameHandler (registered as renameHandler order="first", overriding the default SQL rename), backed by the plugin's own lineage plan/apply/target/usage packages — not by BigQuery's injected-language rename mechanism.
  • "Show Column Usages" is bound to Ctrl+Alt+Shift+U and the editor context menu, not Ctrl+Click (which is reserved for Go to Declaration).
  • New SQLX File action (Dataform.NewSqlxFile) exposes 6 templates via the SqlxFileTemplate enum: TABLE, VIEW, INCREMENTAL, ASSERTION, OPERATIONS, DECLARATION.
  • Data Lineage, Run & Execute (run configurations + gutter icon), and the workflow_settings.yaml JSON Schema validation are not documented in the public README — confirmed directly from plugin.xml and source.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
New

  • Unit test support for type: "test" actions: run tests from the gutter or a dedicated run configuration, results in the IDE test runner with an expected/actual diff, and a test preview in the SQLX split editor.
  • Inline error messages: Dataform compilation errors and BigQuery dry-run errors are placed on the exact tokens of the SQLX file, with "did you mean" hints and quick fixes; errors that cannot be placed are listed in an editor banner.
  • New SQLX File action gains a Test template.

Improvements

  • Config block: the config schema now accepts the legacy assertions shorthands (uniqueKey: "id", nonNull: "col", uniqueKeys: [["a", "b"]]) and dependency targets written as objects, whose keys are now validated.
  • Config block: completing a property that already has a value moves the caret to that value instead of inserting a second one.
  • Config block: completion shows every shape a property accepts (e.g. string[] | string).
  • Lower memory and CPU usage for lineage, schema resolution, expression evaluation and BigQuery result grids.

Fixes

  • Column dependencies, Go to Declaration and usages on Windows.
  • Column resolution for dataset-qualified tables, the multi-argument ref() forms and WITH ${include()} templates.
  • Generated config typings wrongly typed arrays of several shapes.

idea-plugin.name: CPLEX OPL
idea-plugin.description:
CPLEX OPL Support for JetBrains IDEs

Native, high-performance language support and solver integration for IBM ILOG CPLEX Optimization Programming Language (OPL) in IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, CLion, DataSpell, and other JetBrains IDEs.

A modern, fast, and feature-rich alternative to the legacy Eclipse-based CPLEX Studio IDE.

🚀 Key Features & Highlights

  • Intelligent Infeasibility Diagnosis: Automatically captures solver conflict logs (ctInfeasible at ...) and generates direct, clickable console hyperlinks to conflicting constraints in .mod and .dat files.
  • Universal Run Integration: Dedicated Run Opl Model configuration supporting Local, WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux), and Docker containers with automatic path translation.
  • Solver Auto-Detection: Automatically discovers oplrun binaries in standard installation paths across Windows, Linux, and macOS.
  • Constraint Programming (CP) & Scheduling: Full syntax support, keyword highlighting, and intelligent code completion for over 30 CP Optimizer functions (e.g. span, alternative, synchronize, forbidStart, stepAt, cumulFunction, stateFunction).
  • Semantic Analysis & Inspections: Real-time validation including scope-aware variable resolution, type checks, missing semicolon warnings, and automatic quick-fixes (e.g. Alt+Enter to insert missing using CP;).
  • Python & Data Science Interoperability: Context-menu action to generate executable doopl/docplex Python runner scripts directly from .mod files in PyCharm.
  • Dedicated File Types & Icons: Full support and dedicated SVG icons for models (.mod), data (.dat), and settings (.ops) files with starter templates.
  • Dynamic .ops Settings Engine: Parses and injects XML configuration files (e.g. memory limits, tuning parameters) directly into the execution pipeline with XXE security protection.
  • Developer Experience: Structure view side panel (variables, objectives, constraints), smart code formatter, live templates, brace matching, and rename refactoring (Shift+F6).

⚡ Quick Start in 60 Seconds

  1. Create an OPL file: Right-click your project folder → New → OPL File (choose Model file or Data file).
  2. Configure Solver: Open Settings → Tools → CPLEX OPL and click Auto-Detect (or enter the path to oplrun).
  3. Run your model: Press Shift+F10 or click the green run triangle next to your model.

📦 Supported Environments & Solvers

  • JetBrains IDEs: IntelliJ IDEA (Community & Ultimate), PyCharm (Community & Professional), CLion, DataSpell, WebStorm, and other IntelliJ-based IDEs (2024.3+ and 2025.x).
  • CPLEX Studio Versions: IBM ILOG CPLEX Optimization Studio 12.x, 20.x, and 22.x.
  • Execution Environments: Local Host, WSL (Ubuntu/Debian), and Docker.

💬 Community & Feedback

Found a bug or have an idea for a new feature?

  • GitHub Repository & Issue Tracker
  • Reference Models & Examples

If you find this plugin helpful for your research, studies, or industrial optimization projects, please consider leaving a rating and review on the JetBrains Marketplace!
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • CP Optimizer & Scheduling Vocabulary: Added comprehensive syntax recognition and code completion for over 30 Constraint Programming (CP) functions and scheduling constraints (span, alternative, synchronize, forbidStart, forbidEnd, forbidExtent, startBeforeStart, endBeforeEnd, startOfNext, startOfPrev, endOfNext, endOfPrev, stepAt, stepAtStart, stepAtEnd, count, distribute, inverse, lexicographic, element, powerset, standardDeviation, sgn, dist, etc.).
  • IBM ILOG Script Autocompletion: Added code completion and icon categorization for scripting global instances (thisOplModel, cplex, cp, Opl), scripting functions (writeln, write, IloOplCallJava, IloOplImportJava), and scripting classes (IloOplOutputFile, IloOplInputFile, IloOplModel, IloOplDataElements, IloOplConflictIterator, IloOplProfiler, etc.).
  • Code Completion UX: Added intelligent parentheses insertion handler for function completions that automatically inserts () and places the caret inside without duplicating existing parentheses.
  • CP Engine Inspection & Quick-Fix: Added an inspection warning in OplAnnotator when Constraint Programming functions are used without a using CP; declaration, accompanied by a quick-fix (Alt+Enter) that automatically inserts using CP; at the top of the file.
  • Language Grammar & Lexer: Added support for missing CPLEX OPL keywords (CPLEX, constraint, constraints, setof, struct, initial), set operations (union, inter, diff, symdiff), modulo/div, logical operators, and indexed constraint labels (label[i]:).
  • Code Completion & Highlighting: Full syntax highlighting for all 60+ OPL keywords and operators, comprehensive code completion for OPL built-in math and CP scheduling functions, and a deprecation inspection with Quick-Fix for struct.
  • File Types & Icons: Added dedicated OplOpsFileType registration and custom SVG icon (oplOps.svg) for CPLEX OPL settings files (.ops).
  • File Templates: Added OplSettings file template and integrated Settings file (.ops) creation into the New -> OPL File action dialog.

Testing

  • Unified Test Reporting Architecture: Migrated test reports from src/test/reports to root reports/ with automatic .gitignore exclusion, keeping source trees 100% clean. Implemented dual-format reporting (machine-readable JSON + human-readable Markdown) with timestamps, and added scripts/generate_github_summary.py for automated GitHub Actions Step Summaries.
  • Test Suite Architecture & Optimization: Reorganized tests into fast unit/platform suite (OplTestSuite), dedicated stress/performance suite (OplPerformanceTestSuite), and full aggregation suite (OplAllTestSuite).
  • Performance Testing & CLI: Standardized performance benchmarks using PlatformTestUtil.startPerformanceTest, added dedicated perf and test:all modes to scripts/test.py, and optimized JSON test reports to a compact tabular schema with environment metadata.
  • Test Coverage: Added OplFileTypeTest to verify file type registrations and icons, and added previously unlinked test classes (OplPathTranslatorTest, OplErrorReportSubmitterTest, OplRunConfigurationIntegrationTest) to the active test suite.

idea-plugin.name: Programmers Main Generator
idea-plugin.description:
Programmers Main Generator

Programmers Main Generator is an IntelliJ plugin that helps you start Programmers coding test problems quickly.
프로그래머스 코딩테스트 문제를 IDE 안에서 바로 시작할 수 있도록 도와주는 플러그인입니다.

✨ 주요 기능

Overview

  • 우측 Tool Window에서 문제 목록을 이름으로 검색
  • 문제 선택 시 템플릿 코드를 즉시 미리보기
  • 📄 파일 생성 — 원하는 폴더를 선택하면 템플릿 파일을 생성하고 에디터에서 자동으로 열기
  • 📋 클립보드 복사 — 템플릿 코드를 클립보드에 복사하여 원하는 위치에 붙여넣기
  • 현재 Java 템플릿 중심으로 제공

🚀 사용 방법

  1. IDE 우측의 Programmers Main Generator Tool Window를 엽니다.
  2. 상단 검색창에 문제 이름을 입력합니다. (현재 Java 템플릿 제공)
  3. 목록에서 풀고 싶은 문제를 클릭하면 우측에 코드가 미리보기됩니다.

    • 📋 클립보드 복사 : 코드를 복사한 뒤 원하는 파일에 붙여넣습니다.
  5. 생성된 파일의 solution 메소드 안에 풀이를 작성하고 main을 실행하여 결과를 확인합니다.

idea-plugin.name: SQL to Java
idea-plugin.description:
SQL to Java DTO & DB Service Generator

Automatically generates Java DTO classes and database service classes from SQL CREATE TABLE statements.

DTO Generation

  • Paste SQL and instantly get Java classes with fields, constructors, getters, and toString()
  • Detects shared columns across tables and offers to generate an abstract superclass with subclasses
  • Generates Java records for simple tables (6 fields or fewer)
  • Automatically adds required imports (e.g. java.time.LocalDate)

DB Service Generation

  • Generate a full database service class with JDBC logic
  • Pick which CRUD operations you need: INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE
  • Handles inheritance correctly — child classes get constructor args in the right order
  • Uses record accessors (field()) or class getters (getField()) as appropriate
  • Automatic LocalDate ↔ java.sql.Date conversion

International Support

Automatically converts non-ASCII characters to safe Java identifiers:

  • Scandinavian: æ/ø/å, ä/ö → ae/oe/aa
  • German: ä/ö/ü/ß → ae/oe/ue/ss
  • Icelandic: þ/ð → th/d
  • Romance languages: accented characters (é, ñ, ç, etc.) stripped to base letters

Save to Project

Generated files are saved directly to your project's source folder:

  • DTOs → src/dto/
  • DB services → src/db/

Usage

  1. Open the "SQL to Java" tool window from the sidebar
  2. Paste your CREATE TABLE statements
  3. Click "Convert to Java" for DTOs, or "Generate DB Service" for a service class
  4. Click "Save to Project" to create the files

idea-plugin.name: SaltStack Toolkit
idea-plugin.description:
SaltStack Toolkit

Comprehensive SaltStack support for IntelliJ-based IDEs: syntax highlighting, inspections, formatting, navigation, completion and snippets for SLS and Jinja2 files.

Compatible with IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, WebStorm, RubyMine, RustRover, CLion and other IntelliJ Platform IDEs (2024.1+).

Features

Syntax highlighting

  • SLS files (.sls) — YAML structure with embedded Jinja
  • Jinja2 files (.jinja, .j2, .jinja2)
  • Configurable colors via Settings → Editor → Color Scheme → SaltStack Toolkit

Inspections (real-time linter)

  • Duplicate top-level keys (state IDs in state files, pillar keys in pillar files)
  • Unclosed Jinja blocks ({% if %} without {% endif %}, etc.)
  • Tab characters (Salt/YAML requires spaces)
  • Trailing whitespace
  • Empty state blocks (state ID without module call)
  • Requisite references to non-existent state IDs in the same file

Formatting

  • Auto-format on save (toggle in settings)
  • Manual format via Shift+Alt+F
  • Enforces {%- on opening Jinja tags (configurable)
  • Preserves closing -%} for explicit whitespace control
  • Tag spacing normalization: {%if x%} → {%- if x %}, {{var}} → {{ var }}
  • Comments {# ... #} content is left untouched
  • Tabs to spaces, trailing whitespace removal
  • Collapses multiple blank lines, ensures final newline

Navigation

  • Structure View (Cmd+7) — outline of state IDs, includes, Jinja imports/variables
  • Go-to-Definition (Cmd+Click):
    • Jinja imports: {% from "formula/map.jinja" import ... %}
    • Jinja includes: {% include "..." %}
    • salt:// source references
    • SLS includes: - .substate, - formula.substate
    • Pillar includes
    • Requisite references inside the current file
    • Reverse navigation: click on a top-level pillar key → find all usages (pillar.KEY, pillar['KEY'], pillar.get('KEY')) in state files
  • Hover documentation for 50+ state modules, all requisites, Salt builtins, execution modules (sdb.get, defaults.merge, fast_yaml.hosts, etc.)

Auto-completion

  • 50+ state modules (file.managed, service.running, etc.)
  • Module parameters (context-aware — suggests parameters of the parent module)
  • All requisites (require, watch, onchanges, etc.)
  • Salt execution modules inside salt[...] and salt.

Live Templates (snippets)

40+ snippets for common Salt patterns:

  • State modules: file.managed, pkg.installed, service.running, cmd.run, user.present, cron.present, git.latest, docker_container.running, archive.extracted, etc.
  • Jinja constructs: if, ifelse, for, set, from, import, include, macro, block
  • Salt patterns: map.jinja, sdb.get, defaults.merge, grains.filter_by, saltutil.runner, pillar.get
  • Boilerplates: sls-boilerplate, sls-full

Configuration

Settings → Tools → SaltStack Toolkit:

  • State roots / Pillar roots — comma-separated paths (relative or absolute) for navigation resolution
  • Toggle individual lint checks
  • Toggle auto-format on save
  • Toggle {%- dash enforcement

Source code

github.com/akrikun/saltstack-toolkit-jetbrains
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.6.6

  • Formatter keeps indentation of standalone closers: a closing %} / }} on its own line (e.g. ending a multi-line {%- set x = {...} %}) no longer has its leading indentation collapsed to a single space on save/format.
  • Standalone -%} / -}} no longer broken: a whitespace-control closer on its own line was rewritten to - %}, which is invalid Jinja.

1.6.5

  • Structure View crash fixed: PsiInvalidElementAccessException when the IDE rebuilt PSI after a roots change (e.g. an SDK update) while the Minimap/Structure View was reading an SLS file's structure. Stale PSI is now detected and skipped instead of throwing.

1.6.4

  • Compatibility with 2026.2 (build 262) and later: removed the until-build upper bound so the plugin stays available on new IDE releases without requiring a re-publish.

1.6.3

  • Formatter never breaks {% include %}: content-injecting tags are kept dashless regardless of the enforceDashTags setting, and any existing leading or trailing whitespace-control dash is stripped. A leading {%- include "foo.sls" %} where the included file starts with a top-level YAML key (e.g. alertmanager:) strips the preceding newline, fuses that key onto the previous line, and corrupts the rendered pillar (SaltRenderError: expected '<document start>', but found '<block mapping start>'). Other tags (set, for, if, import*, …) are unaffected — they produce no output, so the dash form stays safe.

1.6.2

  • Comment hotkey fixed: Cmd+/ (line comment) and Cmd+Shift+/ (block comment) now work in .sls and .jinja files. .sls uses # for line and {# … #} for block; .jinja uses {# … #} for both (Jinja has no line-comment primitive). Right-click "Comment with..." also works.

1.6.1

  • Cmd+Click navigation now also handles {% import_yaml "..." as foo %}, {% import_json "..." %}, and {% import_text "..." %}.
  • Cmd+Click on the string argument of salt.fast_yaml.hosts("name") (also bracket form salt['fast_yaml.hosts']("name")) opens the matching name.{yaml,yml,sls,json} from any configured state/pillar root.

1.6.0

  • Safer formatter default: enforceDashTags is now off by default. The dash style changes Jinja runtime whitespace semantics, so we no longer enforce it on save without explicit opt-in.
  • Plugin Verifier task wired into the GitHub Actions CI matrix.
  • Marketplace-ready README: full feature list, compatibility matrix (IDEA / PyCharm / WebStorm / GoLand / RubyMine / RustRover / CLion).
  • Shared fixtures with the VS Code plugin (fixtures/) so a regression on either side fails both CIs.

1.5.4

Fixes

  • Completion in Jinja files: completion now also fires in .jinja/.j2 files for salt[...], salt., pillar.get, grains.get, sdb.get, defaults.merge. Previously only worked in .sls.
  • Jinja block checker: {% set X = ... %} no longer falsely required {% endset %}. Block-form {% set X %}…{% endset %} with whitespace control {%- ... -%} is now recognized correctly. Filters/named-args ({% set x | upper(first=true) %}) no longer trigger a false positive.
  • salt:// resolver: supports quoted forms ("salt://..." / 'salt://...'), strips ?query, #hash, and trailing comments. Cursor-aware so multiple salt:// on one line resolve correctly.
  • Requisite diagnostics: removed the hardcoded 6-space indent assumption (now uses indent relative to the requisite-block header). Typed requisites (- file: foo, - pkg: nginx) are no longer flagged as false positives — they target by-name across formulas.

Tests

  • JUnit 5 test suite added (42 tests across formatter, set detection, salt:// extraction, and requisite checks).

1.5.0

Pillar navigation overhaul

  • Nested key paths — Cmd+Click on any pillar key (top-level or nested) now finds usages by full YAML path. Click on data: inside netbox: > data: searches for pillar.netbox.data (and deeper).
  • Local Jinja aliases — detects {% set foo = pillar.x %} and tracks foo.y references as pillar.x.y.
  • Cross-file dict maps — detects {% set bar = { 'key': pillar.foo.key } %} in one file and {% from "X.jinja" import bar %} in another, then resolves bar.key references back to pillar.foo.key across files.

Pillar hover with state.apply

When hovering over a pillar key in a pillar file, the popup now shows:

  • Full YAML key path
  • All access forms (pillar.x.y, pillar['x']['y'], salt['pillar.get']('x:y'))
  • List of state formulas that consume this key, with ready-to-run salt '<minion>' state.apply <formula> commands and per-formula usage counts

Performance

  • Two-level cache for pillar usage search:
    • File list cache (invalidated on file create/delete or stateRoots change)
    • Per-file content + analysis cache with mtime check (invalidated on file save/change)
  • Subsequent searches with unchanged files skip disk reads entirely.

1.4.1

  • Fix: settings (state/pillar roots, toggles) now persist correctly after Apply/OK.

1.4.0

  • Initial release for JetBrains IDEs.
  • Syntax highlighting, inspections, formatting, navigation, completion, hover, live templates.
  • Settings panel with configurable State/Pillar roots and lint toggles.

0.5.0 - 2026-07-12

Added

  • File path auto-completion inside include path, dependency config_path, terraform source, and read_terragrunt_config() — type ../ or ${get_repo_root()}/ to get file/directory suggestions with function evaluation (auto-popup on /)
  • Unused local variables inspection — flags locals attributes not referenced via local.X (skips shared configs)
  • Unused local variables (cross-file) inspection — scans entire project for references (disabled by default, enable in Settings → Inspections)
  • Duplicate attributes inspection — flags same key appearing twice in the same block body
  • Unused dependencies inspection — flags dependency blocks whose label is never referenced via dependency.X
  • Input calculator tool window (View → Tool Windows → Terragrunt Inputs) — shows final merged inputs with deep recursive resolution through local chains, include chains, interpolated strings, and include.X.inputs.Y. Detail panel for objects, right-click "Jump to Input" navigation, pin support.
  • Autoinclude support — autoinclude block recognized inside unit/stack blocks, unit.<name>.path and stack.<name>.path completion and navigation, inspection flags invalid content (locals/values/nested autoinclude)

Fixed

  • Duplicate block inspection now flags multiple locals blocks (Terragrunt does not support this)

idea-plugin.name: ActionLens
idea-plugin.description:
Inspect GitHub Actions workflow runs, jobs, and full job logs without leaving your JetBrains IDE.

  • Browse workflow runs → jobs → steps in a dedicated tool window.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.0
