idea-plugin.name: Ren'Py
idea-plugin.description:
Ren'Py

Full IDE support for Ren'Py, the visual novel engine. Works standalone in any IntelliJ-based IDE that has the Python plugin (PyCharm Community / Professional, IntelliJ IDEA with Python plugin, DataSpell, etc).

Unofficial plugin. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or maintained by the Ren'Py project or its developers.

Editor

  • Syntax highlighting tuned to Ren'Py keywords, properties, classes, booleans, numbers, and string interpolation, in both light and dark IDE themes.
  • Brace and bracket matching, smart auto-indent on Enter, code folding, Structure View.
  • Python language injection inside string [interp] regions, with token-aware highlighting of {tag} markup and \escape sequences.
  • Per-attribute layered-image awareness: composed sprite preview on hover, navigation, completion.
  • More than 30 live templates (code snippets) for common constructs: label, menu, screen, Character, default / define, play music, transitions, loops, and more.
  • Color swatch in the gutter next to hex color strings such as color="#c8ffc8"; click it to pick a new color and rewrite it in place.

Navigation

  • Cross-file Ctrl+Click and Find Usages for labels, screens, characters, transforms, styles, images, layered-image attributes, variables, and Python defs/classes inside init python: blocks.
  • Goto Symbol (Shift+Shift) finds labels, screens, characters.
  • Relative (local) labels such as label .choice: are recognized and resolved by Ctrl+Click and Find Usages.
  • Asset preview: hover or Ctrl+Q on show / scene / hide and image / layeredimage declarations renders the resolved image, path, and pixel dimensions. Composed sprites show the actual visible character (base + each attribute layered).

Code completion

  • Context-aware: keywords at line start, labels after jump/call, images after show/scene/hide, attributes after the base image name, screens after use / show screen / hide screen, transforms after at, characters at dialogue line start, Ren'Py defines/images/characters inside [interp] brackets.

Inspections (with quick fixes)

  • Unresolved label on jump / call targets, with rename-to-nearest and create-label fixes.
  • Unresolved image on show / scene / hide targets, with declare-image and rename-to-nearest fixes. Built-in Ren'Py images (black, white, text) and screen targets are auto-skipped.
  • Unresolved character on dialogue speakers, with rename-to-nearest and declare-character fixes.
  • Unused declaration (label, define, default, Python def, class) with Safe Delete fix. Ren'Py engine entry points (start, after_load, splashscreen, etc) are never flagged.

Refactoring

  • F2 / Shift+F6 rename for every Ren'Py element type: labels, screens, characters, variables (including persistent.foo and store.foo), images (multi-token names rewritten as a unit), transforms, styles, Python defs / classes inside init python:.

Formatting

  • Smart auto-indent on Enter, configurable indent size, EditorConfig support per project.

Run

  • "Ren'Py Game" run configuration that launches the project against a configured Ren'Py SDK. Traceback console filter turns engine errors into clickable navigation.

Story analytics

  • A "Ren'Py Analytics" tool window with word count per character and per chapter, an estimated reading time, and a map of where each variable is changed and where it is read, with one click to jump straight to that spot. Switch between the current file and the whole project, and filter long lists with a search box.

Story flow

  • A "Ren'Py Story Flow" tool window that draws your script as a graph: labels as nodes, and jumps, calls, menu choices, fall-through, and screen navigation as connecting lines. Node shapes show each label's role (scene, branch, ending, subroutine, screen, hub), a legend decodes the shapes and lines, unreachable labels are dimmed, and the view follows your caret, filters by folder or name, zooms to fit, and jumps to the label when you click a node.

Requires

  • IntelliJ Platform 2025.2 or later (currently tested through 2026.2).
  • Python plugin (PyCharm-bundled by default, installable in IDEA Community via Settings > Plugins).

Feedback

Found a bug or have a suggestion? Send it to contact@oldhiccup.com.

Support the developer

If this plugin saves you time, consider supporting development at oldhiccup.com.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.3.0

Python is now a first-class citizen. Ren'Py accepts Python in four places and the plugin understands all four: $ one-liners, python: blocks, init python: blocks and _ren.py files.

  • What you write inside a block is indexed: Find Usages finds it, and the "unused declaration" warning stops firing on a function or a variable that is only used from Python.
  • A variable created at the top level of an init python: block counts as a declaration, the same way define and default do.
  • The body of a block is handed to the Python plugin, so you get real Python highlighting, completion and error checking inside it.
  • A name written in Python resolves to its Ren'Py declaration: Ctrl+Click on a name inside a block jumps to its define line, and a name declared in a _ren.py file resolves from any script.
  • Because names resolve now, the plugin stopped hiding every Python warning inside .rpy files: inside a block you see real mistakes again, and only engine-provided names (renpy, persistent, config, ...) stay silent.

Rename works where it used to fail. Renaming a def or a class written in Python, a variable that appears inside a [interpolation], a screen used through show screen, or an image whose name has more than one word (bg city day) all failed before, some with an error popup.

Pasting code lands with the right indentation: the block keeps its own internal shape and moves as a whole to the indentation of the line where you paste it.

Sprites: layers declared with group NAME auto: now show up in the preview, and a layer positioned with pos (x, y) is drawn in that position.

Also fixed:

  • A blank line between init python: and the code no longer breaks the block. This is how most real scripts are written, and the whole block was being dropped.
  • init with any priority works, positive or negative, with or without an explicit sign: init -30 python:, init 999 python:, init +7 python:. Before, a signed priority was not recognised at all and the whole block was lost.
  • A line whose speaker is a string is no longer reported as a mistake: "Child 1" "No..." and " " "..." are both valid Ren'Py.
  • Comments written right after a python: block no longer produce a false syntax error.
  • In _ren.py files, a module imported inside the """renpy ...""" block is recognised in the rest of the file, and Python builtins are no longer marked as unresolved when the project has no interpreter configured.
  • A function or class named after a Ren'Py keyword (def bar(), def text()) is recognised and indexed.
  • # noinspection RenpyUndefinedLabel on the line above a statement silences the warning again.
  • A variable declared as default persistent.foo is no longer reported as unused when the code reads it through a longer path such as persistent.foo.bar.
  • A traceback line in the console links to the file even when the path the engine printed is not relative to the project folder.

The index format changed, so a one-time reindex runs on first launch after upgrading.

1.2.0

New: Ren'Py Story Flow. A tool window that draws your script as a graph so you can see how the story branches and where it ends.

  • Labels are nodes; jumps, calls, menu choices, fall-through, and screen navigation are the connecting lines. The node shape shows each label's role (scene, branch, ending, subroutine, screen, hub), a legend decodes it, and unreachable labels are dimmed.
  • The view follows your caret, filters by folder or name, zooms to fit, and jumps to the label when you click a node.

Light theme. Syntax highlighting now has a light palette, so code stays readable on a light IDE theme. The dark theme is unchanged.

Color picker. A color swatch appears next to hex color strings such as color="#c8ffc8"; click it to pick and rewrite the color.

Also fixed: image names with hyphens (show bg main-menu) resolve correctly; menus with non-string choices no longer freeze the parser; and editing large files stays responsive, as the analytics work moved off the UI thread. A one-time reindex runs on first launch after upgrading.

1.1.0

New: Ren'Py Analytics. A tool window that turns your script into the numbers you need to plan and pitch a visual novel.

  • Word count for the whole project and for the file you are editing, broken down by character and by chapter.
  • An estimated reading time, so you can tell players (and a store page) roughly how long the game is.
  • A variable map: see where each flag is changed and where it is read, and click any entry to jump straight to that spot in the script.
  • A search box to filter long lists, and a switch between "this file" and the whole project.

Also in this release: the bundled code snippets (live templates) now total 31 ready-to-use shortcuts for the most common Ren'Py statements.

1.0.6

  • Relative (local) labels are now supported. label .clearing: is recognised as shorthand for <preceding label>.clearing and is no longer flagged as a syntax error. Ctrl+Click and Find Usages resolve both the relative form (jump .clearing / call .clearing) and the fully qualified form (jump forest_path.clearing) to the same label.

1.0.5

  • Declarations inside an init: block (define, default, image, layeredimage) are now recognised. Characters declared inside an init: block, for example define eileen = Character("Eileen"), no longer flag dialogue lines (eileen "...") as "Unresolved character", and Ctrl+Click navigates to the declaration.

1.0.4

  • In _ren.py files, Ren'Py engine names (persistent, config, renpy, store, gui, ...), variables declared via default or define inside a """renpy ...""" docstring, and the classes or functions written at the top of the file are no longer marked as unresolved.
  • Underscored runtime variables (_in_replay, _history, _window, _skipping, _preferences, _save_directory, ...) are no longer flagged as undefined.
  • In .rpy files, engine names like persistent, config, or renpy and the identifier after a dot (for example persistent.example_flag, inventory.items) no longer get red squiggles.
  • Code inside .rpy string interpolations (for example [helper_fn(x)], [clock.format_now()]) and screen alt (...) clauses is no longer flagged with red squiggles for names that cannot be resolved in isolation, including screen-local variables created with $ x = ....
  • Variables declared inside the """renpy ...""" block of one _ren.py file (for example default state_registry = []) no longer appear as unresolved when used from .rpy scripts or other _ren.py files.
  • The "Unused declaration" warning on namespaced defaults such as default persistent.example_flag = True now uses the full name; before it could mention only the first word.

1.0.3

  • Fixed an error notification that could pop up when you opened another project or used Search Everywhere. It was harmless, but now it is gone.

1.0.0, Initial release

First public release of the Ren'Py plugin.

Editor

  • Syntax highlighting for Ren'Py keywords, properties, classes, booleans, numbers, and string interpolation.
  • Brace and bracket matching, smart auto-indent on Enter, code folding, Structure View.
  • Python language injection inside string interpolations, with token-aware highlighting of markup tags and escape sequences. Conversion flags ([name!tq]) and format specs ([value:>10]) are correctly excluded from the Python region.
  • EditorConfig support for indent style and size.

Navigation

  • Cross-file Ctrl+Click and Find Usages for labels, screens, characters, transforms, styles, images, layered-image attributes, variables, and Python defs/classes inside init python: blocks.
  • Goto Symbol (Shift+Shift) for labels, screens, and characters.

Asset awareness

  • Hover or Ctrl+Q on show, scene, hide targets and on image or layeredimage declarations renders the resolved image with its absolute path and pixel dimensions (max 400 px wide).
  • Composed sprite preview: layered images render base plus each referenced attribute stacked, including bare attributes resolved via the <base>_<group>_<attr> convention.
  • Per-attribute Ctrl+Click navigation, Find Usages, and completion after the base name.

Code completion

  • Context-aware proposals for keywords, labels after jump/call, images after show/scene/hide, attributes after a layered-image base, screens after use or show screen, transforms after at, characters at dialogue line start, and Ren'Py defines/images/characters inside string interpolations.

Inspections (with quick fixes)

  • Unresolved label on jump/call targets, with rename-to-nearest and create-label fixes. Skips call screen NAME, jump screen NAME, call expression EXPR, and jump expression EXPR.
  • Unresolved image on show/scene/hide targets, with declare-image and rename-to-nearest fixes. Skips built-in engine images (black, white, text) and screen targets.
  • Unresolved character on dialogue speakers, with rename-to-nearest and declare-character fixes. Statement keywords (play, extend, voice, etc.) and screen DSL property names (auto, idle, hover, etc.) are skipped automatically.
  • Unused declaration for labels, defines, defaults, Python defs and classes, with Safe Delete quick fix. Ren'Py engine entry points (start, after_load, splashscreen, etc.) are never flagged.

Refactoring

  • F2 / Shift+F6 rename for every Ren'Py element type: labels, screens, characters, variables (including persistent.foo / store.foo), images (multi-token names rewritten as a unit), transforms, styles, Python defs and classes inside init python:.

Run

  • Ren'Py Game run configuration that launches the project against a configured Ren'Py SDK. Traceback console filter turns engine errors into clickable navigation back to the source.

idea-plugin.name: Antlers
idea-plugin.description:
Full language support for Statamic Antlers templates (*.antlers.html, *.antlers.php, and *.antlers.xml) in IntelliJ-based IDEs.

Antlers is parsed as a template language layered over HTML/CSS (or XML for .antlers.xml sitemaps/feeds), so you get real Antlers intelligence inside {{ }} while keeping the regular markup tooling in the surrounding content. The plugin reads your project's blueprints, fieldsets, collections, taxonomies, navigations, forms, and a view's YAML front matter, so completion, navigation, and documentation are blueprint- and view-aware — and scope-aware: the variables offered and resolved are the ones actually available where your cursor is (inside a {{ collection }} loop, a related entry, a {{ nav }} tree, a {{ form }}, a page-mapped template, or an @collection-hinted view).

Highlights

  • Editing — syntax highlighting with customizable colors, including operators read as keywords (the word operators and/or/not, the query/builder operators where/take/groupby/…, the inline switch operator, and void); Antlers interpolation inside strings ("object-position: {logo:focus_css}") highlighted as real Antlers; Antlers-generated <script>/<style> content (e.g. a JSON-LD graph built with {{ if }} loops) without false JS/CSS/JSON parser errors; a view's ---…--- front matter editable as a real YAML island; brace matching, commenting, and {{ }} auto-insert; code folding; a Structure view outline; and Template IDE hints ({{# @name / @param / @deprecated / @collection … #}}).
  • Smart block editing — completing a tag drops the caret where you'll type (a parameter slot, or straight into the block); Tab walks parameter slots and then the block; a single Enter expands an empty {{ tag }}{{ /tag }} to an indented body.
  • Completion — tags, tag methods/sub-tags, parameter names and values (partial paths, collection/taxonomy handles, sort fields, booleans); tag query conditions (title:contains="…" on collection/taxonomy/users — the operators, the target blueprint fields, and the values); logic keywords and the query/builder operators (where/orderby/groupby/…); modifiers and their arguments (incl. inside conditions); colon shorthand ({{ collection:… }}); and variables (blueprint fields, system, loop — incl. next:/prev:, foreach key/value, and groupby key/values — nav, form, view: front-matter keys, plus member/relationship completion when dotting into grid/group fields and related entries). Backed by a bundled Statamic 5 & 6 catalog tailored to the version detected in your composer.json, extended by custom tags/modifiers discovered in your project.
  • Navigation & docs — go to a variable's blueprint field, a partial file, a view: key, the svg tag's file ({{ svg:trash }}), a literal media path (glide/asset src/url, a bare image path) under public/, or a custom tag/modifier's PHP class (including the inline {{ x = {your_tag …} }} form); quick documentation on hover and parameter info for modifier arguments.
  • Diagnostics — a tag-balance annotator (unclosed/stray/ mismatched conditions and paired tags) that leaves unknown/addon tags alone, plus unknown-modifier and unresolved-partial inspections — all with quick-fixes (insert the missing closing tag, remove a stray closer, change a mistyped modifier to the closest known one, or create the missing partial view file).
  • Refactoring — Rename and Find Usages for partials and for blueprint field handles (the YAML handle: ↔ every {{ … }} usage, including a field used inside a tag query condition such as title:contains="…").
  • Formatting — indentation-only Reformat Code designed to coexist with Prettier: normalizes spacing in {{ }}, indents tag/condition bodies, dedents else/elseif, bracket-nests multi-line arrays, and indents multi-line and template-named HTML tags. Configurable via Code Style → Antlers, with a toggle to defer entirely to Prettier.
  • Convenience — Antlers live templates and a New → Antlers Template action.

Works with Statamic 5 and 6 on the IntelliJ 2025.2 platform (IntelliJ IDEA, PhpStorm, WebStorm, and friends). PHP inside {{$ … $}} / {{? … ?}} and native <?php … ?> blocks is highlighted where the JetBrains PHP plugin is available (PhpStorm / IDEA Ultimate); everything else works everywhere.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Quick-fixes on diagnostics. An unknown modifier offers "Change to '…'" suggestions (the closest known modifiers, for typos like uppr → upper); an unclosed pair tag / condition offers "Insert closing '{{ /… }}'" — keeping the shorthand handle ({{ /collection:drinks }}, not {{ /collection }}, for {{ collection:drinks type:is="tiki" … }}); a stray closer with no opener offers "Remove stray closing tag"; and a {{ partial:… }} that resolves to no local view file is flagged with a "Create partial" fix that creates it. Dynamic paths (src="page_builder/{type}") and vendor-namespaced partials (partial:addon::snippets/seo) are not flagged (no false positives).

  • Vendor-namespaced partials (partial:addon::path) resolve for go-to-declaration — to the published view under resources/views/vendor/<namespace>/… if present, otherwise to the addon's own view in vendor/<org>/<namespace>/resources/views/… — so Ctrl/⌘-click jumps straight to the real partial.

  • @deprecated Template IDE Hint directive. {{# @deprecated <param> <message> #}} is now a

    recognized directive — highlighted, and suggested after @ alongside @param/@name/… A partial's deprecated parameters are still offered at the include (so existing usages resolve) but shown struck through with a Deprecated marker, and hovering one shows its migration note.

  • Go-to-declaration for the svg tag. {{ svg:trash }} and {{ svg src="trash" }} resolve to the SVG file — Ctrl/⌘-click opens it — through Statamic's path cascade (resources/svg → resources → public/svg → public, with .svg appended when absent, verified against the Statamic source).

  • Go-to-declaration for literal media paths. A literal image/media path written in Antlers — glide src="/img/hero.jpg", asset url="photos/x.webp", or a bare {{ "/img/logo.png" }} — resolves to the file under the web root (public/, then the default asset container public/assets/).

  • .antlers.xml views (sitemaps, RSS/Atom feeds) are now recognized — Antlers layered over XML instead of HTML, so the markup gets XML tooling while the {{ }} stay Antlers. Conditionally-emitted elements ({{ if }}<url>…</url>{{ /if }}), Antlers in tag-attribute position (<urlset {{ yield:namespace }}>), and {var} interpolations in params (from="{handle}") don't trigger false well-formedness errors.

Fixed

  • A {var} string interpolation whose variable shares a pair tag's name (from="{taxonomy}" inside {{ taxonomy … }}) no longer makes the enclosing tag falsely report "is never closed" — the injected interpolation fragment, a tiny variable expression, is no longer balance-checked. (Affected .antlers.html too.)
  • No more false JS/CSS/JSON errors in Antlers-templated <script>/<style> blocks. When a script or style's content is generated by Antlers (<script type="application/ld+json"> … {{ if … }} … </script>, inline {{ … }} in JS, {{ … }} in CSS values), the injected language can't parse the {{ }} — those spurious "Expression expected" / "<value> expected" errors are now suppressed. Real errors in a block with no Antlers are still reported, and Antlers/HTML highlighting is untouched.
  • The : of a ternary / elvis operator (a ? b : c, x ?: y) is now colored as an operator to match the ?, instead of as subtle path punctuation. Path / modifier / bound-parameter colons (collection:blog, upper:2, :src) stay subtle.

idea-plugin.name: Pascal Flow
idea-plugin.description:
Pascal Flow brings modern, high-performance language support for the Pascal ecosystem to JetBrains IDEs — built for reading, navigating and confidently working with both fresh and large-scale legacy Delphi and Free Pascal projects. It understands real-world code, including multiple dialects, conditional compilation and shared include files, so you get accurate highlighting, navigation and code insight out of the box.

Supported files

  • Pascal sources: .pas, .dpr, .lpr, .pp, .dpk
  • Include fragments: .inc
  • Form files: .dfm, .lfm, .fmx
  • Project files: .lpi, .lpk, .dproj, .groupproj

Editor

  • Syntax highlighting for Pascal and DFM/LFM forms, with a configurable color scheme
  • Code folding, brace matching, line and block comments
  • Code completion, including compiler directives
  • Code formatting and dedicated code style settings
  • Quick documentation (Ctrl+Q and on-hover popup) and breadcrumbs: the popup shows the real Pascal signature — parameters, return type, ancestor class, property accessors, const value, field type — with the leading doc-comment attached to the declaration included when present
  • Dialect-aware highlighting of contextual keywords and inactive (conditionally compiled) code

Navigation & refactoring

  • Go to Class and Go to Symbol for units, types, routines, constants, properties and fields
  • Go to Declaration on a uses clause jumps to the referenced unit (dotted, aliased and in '…' forms included), including units whose directory is declared as a unit search path in your .dpr / .dpk / .dproj / .lpi / .lpk project file
  • Gutter markers between a routine's interface declaration and its implementation — in both directions, even when the body lives in an {$I} include
  • Class and interface hierarchy gutter markers: jump from a type to its supertypes, subclasses or implementing classes, and from a method to the one it overrides, the methods overriding it, the interface method it implements, or the classes implementing an interface method — across units
  • Project-wide, case-insensitive Find Usages backed by the stub index — call sites, type references, property and field reads/writes are listed across every unit
  • Reference resolution and Find Usages, including compiler-directive include navigation, generic / specialize types, and nested-procedure and anonymous-method scopes
  • Rename refactoring backed by named-element PSI
  • Structure view for fast in-file navigation

Code inspections

  • Empty begin/end block
  • Duplicate class/record/interface member
  • Unused local declaration
  • Missing override directive
  • Redundant routine directive
  • Unbalanced compiler directive
  • Trailing comma in uses clause
  • Quick-fix: add missing unit to the uses clause when the unresolved identifier is declared in another indexed unit

Parser & conditional compilation

  • Realistic Delphi/FPC parsing of generics, anonymous methods, inline variables, helpers, class operators, variant records and assembler blocks
  • Wide dialect coverage — Delphi, Free Pascal, Turbo Pascal and MacPas — including context-sensitive operators, objc classes, specialize-qualified types and the full range of routine and variable modifiers
  • {$IFDEF} evaluation with project-configurable conditional defines, plus MacPas {$ifc}/{$setc}/{$endc} directives
  • Include-aware indexing that propagates {$I} include defines across the project, including units whose interface or program body is supplied by an include
  • Tolerant of real-world quirks: keyword-named identifiers, trailing tokens after end. and label-less case statements
idea-plugin.change-notes:
7.0.0

  • Classes and following declarations remain available for navigation when an unsupported attribute appears around a class variable or constant section.
  • Reduce parsing stalls for deeply nested named generic type specializations.
  • Comparison arguments such as WriteLn(a < b, c > d) remain separate expressions without false generic-call errors.
  • Go to Declaration and Find Usages recognize inline variables and constants within their declaring blocks, including grouped variables and nested shadowing.
  • Numeric literal helper calls remain valid when whitespace or comments follow the member dot.
  • Objective-C categories with a literal parent in an include file keep following declarations available for navigation.
  • Requires a JetBrains IDE version 2025.3 or later.
  • Completed units report routine declarations that are missing their implementation body.
  • Types following an empty type declaration remain available for navigation while its syntax error is shown.
  • Types and routines following an empty Objective-C category parent list remain available while its syntax error is shown.
  • Following types remain available for navigation while a category's closing end; is missing in a complete unit.
  • Reformat Code preserves code and comments in conditional branches for other compiler settings.
  • Find Usages and Rename keep matching routine declarations, implementations and calls together without changing source layout.
  • Saving Pascal sources in Remote Development avoids local unit and routine reference-resolution failures.
  • Pascal declarations remain available in Structure View on IDE 2025.3.
  • Form previews display captions and controls for custom form classes with a declared client size.

6.0.0

  • Updating from an earlier 6.0 development build no longer causes crashes when opening advanced records with class properties.
  • Parser and conditional-compilation support is substantially broader across Delphi, Free Pascal, MacPas and legacy code. Shared includes, declaration macros, procedural types, variant records, Objective-C declarations, inline assembly and malformed-code recovery preserve following declarations instead of breaking the rest of the file.
  • Code insight now understands Pascal's implicit symbols and scopes: function Result, method Self, compiler-provided System symbols, program header parameters, labels, escaped identifiers, and identifiers that shadow built-in Boolean constants resolve without false unresolved-reference or import warnings. Background highlighting remains stable when function declarations are reparsed while editing.
  • Completion is context-aware for expressions, declarations, member access, routine calls, compiler built-ins, and visible units. It filters unrelated declarations, preserves target-specific candidates, inserts required built-in arguments, and no longer suggests imports for symbols already supplied by the current scope or an owning include file. Indexed completion no longer fails while collecting project symbols in JetBrains 2026.2.
  • Parameter info and quick documentation show Pascal and compiler-built-in signatures, including required parameters, return types, and overloads. Hover documentation now identifies the implicit Self and function Result with their types, preserves declarations supplied by shared include files, and shows a built-in type instead of the signature that happens to contain it, without failing to open the popup.
  • Reference highlighting and navigation respect unit visibility, used-unit exports, inherited members, property accessors, externally defined routines, target-specific declarations, project unit-search paths, and the host context of shared .inc files.
  • Find Usages works project-wide for routines, types, constants, properties, variables, fields and parameters. Include filenames support navigation, Find Usages and Rename in both directions.
  • Inspections now account for overloads, reintroduce, eligible overrides, nested declaration scopes, and include hosts, avoiding duplicate-member, unused, missing-override, and missing-unit suggestions where the declaration is already valid.
  • The new Add unit to uses quick-fix offers eligible exported units for unresolved identifiers and inserts the selected unit into the correct interface or implementation section without suggesting imports for built-ins or symbols already in scope.
  • Syntax highlighting covers soft keywords, package sections, routine directives, compiler built-ins, resolved references, and inactive conditional branches, and refreshes open editors after dialect or project settings change.
  • Structure View, breadcrumbs, formatter spacing, Rename validation and optional IDE integrations now handle program, library, package, Unicode and escaped-name cases consistently.
  • Opening the project summary or refreshing DFM/LFM/FMX previews no longer freezes the editor while large projects and forms are processed. The Pascal tool window also refreshes safely after editor-selection and dialect-setting changes.

5.0.0

Pascal now respects your editor's indentation settings instead of forcing a fixed two-space indent.

  • The Tabs and Indents page is now available under Settings | Editor | Code Style | Pascal, so you can choose tabs or spaces and set the indent, tab and continuation-indent sizes for Pascal files
  • .editorconfig is now honoured for Pascal files, including indent_style, indent_size, tab_width and continuation_indent_size — previously these were silently ignored and the editor always fell back to a two-space indent
  • Fixed parsing of Free Pascal compiler sources where conditional {$I} includes provide constant initializers and terminators from CPU-specific include directories
  • Replaced a deprecated platform API in the dialect tool window so Pascal Flow stays compatible with upcoming JetBrains IDE releases

4.0.0

A major update centred on code navigation, making it faster to move around real-world Delphi and Free Pascal projects — across units, include files and class hierarchies.

  • Go to Declaration on a unit name in a uses clause now opens that unit, including dotted namespaces, Alias = Unit aliases and Delphi in '…' paths
  • New gutter markers link a routine's interface declaration and its implementation in both directions, even when the body comes from an {$I} include
  • New class- and interface-hierarchy gutter markers navigate from a type to its supertypes, subclasses and implementing classes, and from a method to the member it overrides, the members overriding it, the interface method it implements, and the classes implementing an interface method — project-wide
  • More accurate reference resolution for generic and specialize-qualified types, and inside nested procedures and anonymous methods
  • Fixed Go to Class for generic types, which were previously indexed under the generic keyword instead of their real name

3.0.0

A major update that significantly widens real-world Delphi and Free Pascal coverage, validated against large open-source codebases, so files parse cleanly and highlighting, navigation and inspections stay accurate even in dialect-heavy and macro-heavy projects.

  • Much broader Free Pascal and Delphi dialect support, including MacPas, FPC objc classes, context-sensitive operators (as, is), specialize-qualified types, Turbo Pascal inline() machine-code blocks and a wide range of routine and variable modifiers and directives
  • Smarter conditional compilation: MacPas {$ifc}/{$setc}/{$endc} directives are evaluated, unresolved {$if} branches stay visible, and units whose interface or program body comes from an {$I} include now parse
  • More tolerant parsing of awkward real-world code: keyword-named parameters and unit-name segments, trailing tokens after the terminating end., label-less case statements and forward object declarations
  • Refined health corpus that excludes verified-malformed and non-standalone sources, giving a cleaner picture of genuine parser gaps
  • Numerous stability and accuracy improvements across a wide range of production projects

2.0.0

A major update focused on understanding more real-world Delphi and Free Pascal code, so highlighting, navigation and inspections stay accurate even in large, dialect-heavy projects.

  • Broader, more reliable support for modern Delphi and Free Pascal syntax, including generics, anonymous methods, inline variables, helpers, class operators, variant records and assembler blocks
  • Better handling of conditionally compiled code: {$IFDEF} branches and {$I} includes are taken into account, with project-configurable defines
  • More accurate code completion, navigation (Go to Class / Symbol, Find Usages, include navigation) and Rename refactoring across units
  • Code inspections to catch common issues, such as empty begin/end blocks, duplicate members, unused declarations, missing override, redundant directives, unbalanced compiler directives and trailing commas in uses
  • Dedicated support for DFM, LFM and FMX form files and Delphi/Lazarus project files
  • Numerous stability and parsing improvements across a wide range of real-world codebases

idea-plugin.name: Slidev
idea-plugin.description:
Integrated support for Slidev presentations.
  • Auto-detects slides.md Slidev projects in your workspace
  • Starts, adopts, and stops the Slidev dev server (configurable dev command and port)
  • Live side-by-side preview with bidirectional editor ↔ preview navigation sync, click stepping, and an overview mode
  • Slides tree with drag-and-drop reordering and a projects tree for multi-entry workspaces
  • Per-slide code folding, slide-number annotations, and frontmatter highlighting in the editor
  • Schema-driven completion, quick documentation, and validation for slide frontmatter (headmatter and per-slide)
Port of the official Slidev VS Code extension.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Slidev project detection: scans the workspace for slides.md entries (configurable include/exclude globs), with a projects tree to add, remove, rescan, and switch the active entry
  • Dev-server management: start, stop, and adoption of already-running servers, with automatic port allocation and a configurable dev command (${args}, ${port} substitution); server output in the Run tool window
  • Embedded preview (JCEF) with bidirectional editor ↔ preview sync, click stepping, slide/overview modes, and IDE theme propagation; "Open in Browser" fallback when JCEF is unavailable
  • Slidev split editor: deck entry files open with an editor/preview split (like the Markdown preview), with the embedded live preview as the preview half; selecting a deck's editor makes it the active entry
  • Slides tree with drag-and-drop slide reordering and caret sync
  • Editor support: slide-number annotations, frontmatter tint, virtual code-block line numbers, per-slide folding, and Alt+Up/Alt+Down slide navigation
  • Frontmatter language support: schema-driven completion, quick documentation, and validation for headmatter and per-slide frontmatter (vendored Slidev JSON schemas)
  • Compat-mode handling for older Slidev servers (navigation/overview actions hidden, warning notification)
  • Built-in markdown preview compatibility: Vue template attributes in slides (@click, :class, ...) no longer crash the preview with InvalidCharacterError
  • New Project wizard generator: scaffolds the official create-slidev starter template (demo deck, components, snippets, deploy configs) with a package-manager choice and optional dependency install; template content is a snapshot of create-slidev 52.16.0 and should be refreshed per release

idea-plugin.name: SchemaLock
idea-plugin.description:
Versioned, integrity-pinned schemas for YAML files.
Provides autocomplete and validation for Kubernetes CRDs and other ecosystems from cdn.schemalock.dev. Pin schema versions per directory with an optional schemalock.yaml file; unpinned resources resolve to the latest version from the CDN.

idea-plugin.name: Idris 2 (JVM)
idea-plugin.description:
IDE support for Idris 2, talking directly to the compiler's IDE-mode protocol - works great with the JVM backend (and any idris2 build).
  • Syntax highlighting (lexical + compiler semantic highlighting)
  • Compiler diagnostics as you save
  • Type-at-point hover documentation and go-to-definition
  • Type-driven interactive editing: case split, add clause, proof search, generate definition, make lemma, make case, make with (Alt-Enter)
  • Integrated REPL tool window
Configure the idris2 executable under Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Idris 2.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Java-FFI member completion and auto-import. When the receiver resolves to a generated Java marker, completion now offers the class's full callable surface from the :jvm-ffi-list catalog — including members not yet emitted into the binding module — with the rendered signature shown inline. Accepting a member that has not yet been generated automatically (re)generates its binding via idris2 --jvm-ffi-import in the background, so the inserted reference resolves. The catalog is cached per resolved module classpath, so a dependency change yields a fresh key. Requires an Idris 2 JVM backend build of 0.8.4 or later (the --jvm-ffi-list/--jvm-ffi-import flags this depends on are not present in earlier builds).

idea-plugin.name: SingleStore Language Server Client
idea-plugin.description:
Integrates the SingleStore language server into JetBrains IDEs to provide SQL intelligence for .s2db.sql files.

Features

  • Schema-aware completions — table, column, and procedure suggestions powered by your live SingleStore engine.
  • Syntax highlighting & diagnostics — grammar-based highlighting and error reporting even without a database connection.
  • TCP and WebSocket transport — connects to the language server over a plain TCP socket or a WebSocket (including TLS); the protocol is inferred automatically from the address you enter.
  • Live configuration updates — server address and database credential changes take effect immediately without restarting the IDE.
  • Custom file icon — .s2db.sql files get a SingleStore icon in the Project tree and editor tabs.

idea-plugin.name: Procfile
idea-plugin.description:
The Procfile plugin adds first-class support for Procfile files in JetBrains IDEs. A Procfile declares the process types and commands used to run an application (for example with Foreman, Heroku, or Honcho), and this plugin makes editing and running them effortless.
Features:
  • Syntax Highlighting: Distinct coloring for process names, separators, and commands, with a configurable color settings page.
  • Code Completion: Smart completion for common process names such as web and release.
  • Formatting: Built-in formatter to keep your Procfile clean and consistent.
  • Commenting: Quick line commenting support.
  • Run Configurations: Run individual processes or all processes directly from the editor via gutter icons and context-menu actions.
  • Inspections: Detect duplicate process names, empty commands, invalid process names, multiple release processes, and a missing web process.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Versions:
  • All IntelliJ products support: 1.1.1

Plugin updates:
  • 1.1.1 (2026-06-23) - Add support for jetbrains gateway 262
  • 1.0.2 (2026-06-23) - Add support for jetbrains gateway 253
  • 1.1.0 (2026-06-21) - Support api 262
  • 1.0.1 (2026-06-21) - Initial release of Procfile
    • Add Procfile language support with syntax highlighting and color settings page
    • Add code completion for common process names
    • Add formatter and line commenter
    • Add run configurations to run a single process or all processes
    • Add inspections: duplicate process name, empty command, invalid process name, multiple release, and missing web process

idea-plugin.name: Firebase Rules (HotRulez)
idea-plugin.description:
Language support for Firebase Security Rules — both Cloud Firestore and Cloud Storage — in .rules files in JetBrains IDEs. The dialect (service name, root match shape, and request/resource members) is detected from the service declaration in each file.

Features:

  • Syntax highlighting with a configurable color scheme
  • Structural validation and inspections (file-structure and suspicious-usage warnings)
  • Unknown-member inspection — a conservative, dialect-aware weak warning when a member access on a closed built-in (request, resource, …) names a member that dialect does not define, with did-you-mean rename fixes; it never flags user data, custom auth claims, or object metadata, and infers no types
  • Code formatting, brace matching, quote handling, and line/block commenting
  • Symbol intelligence — go to definition, find usages, and rename for functions, parameters, let bindings, and path variables, with Firebase-aware scoping and path-variable shadowing
  • Scope-aware code completion for keywords, allow operations, in-scope symbols, built-ins (request, resource), helper functions, and shallow request./resource. members
  • Structure view — a navigable outline of the file's services, matches, functions, and allow rules
  • Code folding for service, match, and function blocks and block comments
  • Quick documentation (Ctrl+Q) — doc-grounded descriptions with an external Firebase link for operations, built-ins, dialect-correct members, and helpers, plus signatures for your own functions, parameters, let bindings, and path variables
  • Parameter info (Ctrl+P) for user-function and fixed-arity path-helper calls

HotRulez is purely structural: it never connects to Firebase, runs the emulator, or evaluates whether a rule authorizes a request.

This is an unofficial, community-maintained open-source plugin. Firebase, Cloud Firestore, and Cloud Storage for Firebase are trademarks of Google LLC; HotRulez is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Google.

HotRulez is free and open source — if it saves you time, you can buy me a coffee. Thank you!
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Bug Fixes

  • point Storage quick-doc links at live Firebase page

idea-plugin.name: Cosmoteer Language Server
idea-plugin.description: Language support for Cosmoteer .rules and .shader files: diagnostics, completion, hover, navigation, rename, formatting, semantic highlighting, inlay hints, shader preview and more.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Inlay hints and hover on a &:/… reference show what each inheritor reads, such as = 300 | 500, instead of only the base's own value.
  • A &:/… reference whose member the base leaves out is flagged when an inheritor does not set it either, which the game refuses to load.
  • Cosmoteer 0.30.5 RC2 and RC3 support. AllowVertexContiguity, a resource's StatusResponse and a weapon's rest direction complete, hover with docs and validate. StatusType and ValueRange written directly in a StatusResponse, as vanilla does, are recognized.

idea-plugin.name: RuleScribe for Kraken Rules
idea-plugin.description:
RuleScribe — IntelliJ language support for the Kraken Rules DSL (.rules files / KEL, eisgroup/kraken-rules).
  • Syntax highlighting
  • Code completion (keywords, payloads, @Dimension, rule names, functions)
  • Built-in KEL functions: completion, parameter info and quick documentation for the engine's 55 native functions
  • Inspections (rule without name, unresolved rule reference, unresolved identifier, incompatible types)
  • Intention: add missing 'On' clause
  • Navigation between EntryPoint items, Rule declarations and 'Function' declarations, and from any identifier in an expression to its declaration
  • Clickable 'N usages' inlays above declarations, opening the standard usages popup
  • Rename refactoring for rules and functions

This is an independent community plugin. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by EIS Group. "Kraken" refers to the open-source Kraken Rules engine (Apache-2.0).
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.0
  • No new feature. 1.0.0 says the plugin is done being proven, not that it grew: the code is the same as 0.17.0.
  • What it rests on. Binary compatibility is checked weekly against the latest patch of every IntelliJ major since 2024.1, all reporting the plugin compatible. Every release is signed and ships with SLSA build provenance and a CycloneDX SBOM, verifiable against the published artifact. The plugin makes no network call and executes nothing, which a test enforces by reading the shipped jar rather than by asserting it. CodeQL, Qodana, poutine, Dependabot and an OWASP scan run on every change, with no open alert.
  • The roadmap no longer has an item waiting on a decision. Extract rule and Extract function are dropped rather than deferred, with the reasoning recorded.
0.17.0
  • An EntryPoint can be moved to another file with F6, like a rule. It is counted in both directions, because an entry point references as well as being referenced: the entry points that name it, and its own items, which a move can leave behind. Sending one where its rules are not visible empties it without a line changing inside it, so both counts are shown before anything is written and you can cancel.
  • An Import Rule declared where the entry point is going counts too: an item it rescues is not reported as broken.
0.16.0
  • A build-side release. The plugin is now produced by the IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.x on Gradle 9, which changes how the artifact is assembled, signed and verified. Nothing changes in the editor, and compatibility is unchanged: still verified against the latest patch of every IntelliJ major since 2024.1, each reporting the plugin compatible.
  • The build no longer claims it can download a JDK 17 for you when your machine has none. Every released foojay resolver names a vendor constant Gradle 9 removed, so that path throws at the one moment it is useful. Install a JDK 17 and the build finds it.
0.15.0
  • Function declarations are now validated the way the engine validates them. Two bounds for the same generic, a bound that is itself generic, a parameter or return type mixing a union with a generic, two parameters of the same name, and a KEL function carrying the name of a native are each reported with the code that appears in the build log. A declaration without a body is a function signature for the engine, validated by a different class, so it gets that class's codes instead.
  • Unknown types and mismatched body return types stay unchecked. Those fire when a name is missing from an inventory, and the plugin cannot see a project's full type model, so it would report valid code as broken.
0.14.0
  • A rule can be moved to another file with F6, and the plugin says what that would break before writing anything. Kraken references name a rule, not a file, so a move changes no reference text at all — only whether those references still find their target. Sending a rule where a referring file cannot see it breaks every one of its entry point entries without a line changing over there, so the count is shown first and nothing happens until you accept. 'Import Rule' is weighed separately: one naming the destination namespace keeps working, one naming the old namespace does not.
  • Union types parse. 'Function GetDay(Date | DateTime d)' is valid Kraken and was reported as a syntax error, in return position and in a bare signature too — which is how a built-in gets redeclared. Parenthesised types and the '<T>' generic reference are covered as well, so the whole of the engine's type production is now accepted.
0.13.0
  • Nothing changes in the editor: this release is about what guards it. Compatibility is now checked against the latest build of every IntelliJ major since the supported one, rather than only the oldest and the newest, so an API removed in a version in between no longer slips past. The build attestation moves off an action GitHub deprecated, keeping the published verification command working unchanged.
0.12.0
  • Brackets are coloured by nesting depth, which helps most in the deeply nested expressions KEL encourages. Red is kept out of that palette and marks a bracket with no partner, or one whose pairing is ambiguous because a pair inside it is unbalanced; it stays visible when the depth colours are switched off, since it reports a problem rather than decorating. The switch is the platform's own Rainbow checkbox, under Color Scheme.
  • Syntax errors are readable again. A broken expression used to produce a message over four hundred characters long, every token prefixed with the parser's class name and each of the thirteen binary operators spelled out. The same case now reads: '(', ')', ',', <bracket access>, <dot access> or <operator> expected, got ']'.
  • Two inspections offer a fix instead of only reporting: an undeclared '@Dimension' name can declare itself, and a duplicate rule can take the annotation that tells it apart. Neither invents a value, since a dimension's type and the value separating two rules cannot be derived from the file.
  • References are coloured by what they resolve to, a context name apart from a field or variable. A name that resolves to nothing keeps the ordinary identifier colour: painting it as a field would claim it denotes one.
  • Spellchecking covers the text a person reads — comments, a 'Description', and the message of an 'Error' clause. Rule names, entry point names and error codes are left alone, since flagging business vocabulary on every line would bury the real typos.
0.11.0
  • Diagnostics now carry the engine's own code and wording, so '[kvr027] Missing context definition with name ...' reads the same in the IDE as in the build log and the code can be searched across both. Severity comes from the engine's declaration as well, which moves six inspections from a warning to an error.
  • Two checks have no engine equivalent and say so by carrying no code: a rule that no entry point references, and an undeclared '@Dimension' name, which the engine ignores rather than validating.
  • Comparison checking follows the engine more closely. Ordering ('<', '>') and equality ('=', '!=') answer to different rules there: two strings can be compared for equality but not ordered. Treating them alike let 'a < b' on two strings pass.
  • The lexer accepts only the operators the grammar defines. 'a &|&~ b' used to parse as valid Kraken; a typo now points at the offending character instead of failing further along the expression. This also made '>=' and '<=' whole tokens rather than two, which is why no wide comparison had ever been type-checked.
0.10.4
  • The 'unknown function' inspection is removed. 0.10.1 through 0.10.3 tried three different ways to recognize a project's own Java functions so it would not misreport them, and the last of those still found nothing on a real project it was tested against. Verifying this needs a project with a real custom function library to test against, which is not available, so the inspection is gone rather than left half-working.
  • Completion, parameter info, quick documentation, navigation and highlighting for the engine's 55 built-in functions and for DSL-declared 'Function's are unaffected.
0.10.3
  • Function discovery is faster on large projects. It now uses the platform's word index to find the handful of files that mention the annotation instead of reading every '.java' file, and the compiled-class scan is now scoped to library dependencies instead of the whole classpath. No behavior change.
0.10.2
  • Custom functions declared in a Maven dependency, not just the project's own sources, are now found too. A '@Native' function library shipped as a compiled JAR was still being reported as hundreds of unknown-function warnings after 0.10.1, which only read '.java' files. Requires the bundled Java plugin; unaffected otherwise.
0.10.1
  • Custom functions a project implements in Java are now found automatically: the plugin reads the project sources for '@ExpressionFunction' and stops reporting those calls as unknown. A project shipping a large '@Native' function library was seeing hundreds of warnings on perfectly valid rules (issue #43).
  • Because the Java signature is not analysed, a discovered function is accepted at any number of arguments. What the scan cannot see — functions inside a JAR, or implemented only in TypeScript — can still be listed by name in the inspection options.
0.10.0
  • KEL types are now inferred, and two incompatibilities reported. Comparing a 'Date' with a 'DateTime' — which the engine refuses, and which nothing revealed before running it — is flagged, as is passing an argument of the wrong type to a built-in function.
  • Inference follows the engine: 'Integer' and 'Decimal' are both 'Number', 'Money' widens to 'Number' one way only, projecting a field over a collection yields a collection, and type names are case-insensitive.
  • Anything the plugin cannot type is left alone. Operators, iteration variables, union parameters, generics and collections all make the check abstain rather than guess.
0.9.0
  • Identifiers inside rule bodies now resolve. Ctrl+Click on a field in an 'Assert', 'When' or 'Default To' expression opens its declaration, and so do context names, 'set' variables, 'for' and quantifier variables, and function parameters — following the same scope order as the engine, where expression variables shadow the fields of the 'On' target, which shadow context names.
  • Access chains resolve too: in 'AddressInfo.Country.isoCode' each segment navigates, as long as the previous one denotes a known context. Inside a filter, 'Vehicle[model = "P01"]' resolves against the fields of the filtered item, nested filters included.
  • New inspection: unresolved identifier. It is deliberately conservative — with no type inference yet, it stays silent on path segments, on rules whose 'On' target does not resolve, and on the external-context root, so that it never underlines valid code.
0.8.2
  • Declarations now also show who last changed them and when, next to the usage count — the same author inlay other languages get. Clicking it opens the annotation gutter, where every line carries its own commit. Rules, EntryPoints, functions and contexts are all covered; the inlay appears only when the file is under version control.
0.8.1
  • Declarations now carry a clickable 'N usages' inlay, like any other language on the platform. Rules, EntryPoints and functions all get one, and the count follows Kraken namespace visibility: a reference from a namespace that cannot see the declaration is not counted.
  • Ctrl+Click on a declaration name now opens the platform's own usages popup — grouped by file, with a preview of each line — instead of the flat list of labels it used to build. Ctrl+Click on a reference is unchanged, and still offers every '@Dimension' variant of a rule.
0.8.0
  • Functions are now understood inside rule bodies. The engine's 55 built-in functions ship as a catalogue generated from kraken-expression-language, so completion, parameter info (Ctrl+P) and quick documentation (Ctrl+Q) show their real signatures, descriptions and examples.
  • 'Function' declarations resolve like any other declaration: Ctrl+Click from a call, Find Usages and rename, all following namespace visibility. Doc comments ('@since', '@example', '@parameter') are rendered in quick documentation, and a signature declared without a body is labelled as implemented in Java.
  • New inspection: unknown function. It matches the engine's own criterion — a function is identified by name AND parameter count — so a call with the wrong number of arguments reports which arities exist instead of claiming the name is unknown. Projects shipping their own '@Native' Java function library can list those names in the inspection options.
  • Function calls are highlighted, with distinct colors for built-in and project-declared functions; both are customizable in the color settings page.
0.7.3
  • Ctrl+Click on a rule or EntryPoint reference now offers every valid implementation instead of a single one. A rule declared in several '@Dimension' variants previously navigated to whichever variant the index happened to return first; each variant is now listed, labelled with its annotation so same-file variants are distinguishable.
0.7.2
  • New icon: a parchment held by an off-screen kraken, with a quill. The same drawing is now used for the plugin logo and for the .rules file type, and it reads on both light and dark IDE themes.
0.7.1
  • Clearer navigation popup: when a rule or EntryPoint has several usages, Ctrl+Click now lists each one by the EntryPoint that references it, with its file name (and namespace when declared), instead of repeating identical entries.
0.7.0
  • Performance: the namespace-visibility model (used by nearly every resolution, completion and inspection) is now cached and only recomputed on edits, instead of re-reading every file on each lookup — noticeably faster on large multi-file projects.
0.6.0
  • 'Import Rule "X" From Ns' is now fully resolved: an imported rule behaves as if it were declared in the importing namespace — navigation, completion, Find Usages and the unused-rule inspection all work through imports, independently of Include (mirrors the Kraken engine's rule-import semantics).
  • 4 new inspections mirroring the engine's rule-import validation: unknown source namespace, imported rule missing from the source namespace, import colliding with a locally declared rule, and ambiguous (duplicated) import.
0.5.7
  • Relicensed under the PolyForm Shield License 1.0.0: free to use, modify and redistribute, no competing use, and (unlike the previous FSL license) the non-compete restriction does not expire. Applies to this and future releases; earlier releases keep their original license.
0.5.6
  • Fixed copy-paste and reformat destroying the indentation of multi-line KEL expressions (if/then/else continuation lines were flattened): the formatter now preserves manual indentation inside expressions.
0.5.5
  • Fixed false-positive syntax errors on KEL type casts: "(Type) value", including the chained form "((Type) expr).field".
  • Removed deprecated IntelliJ stub API usages (StubBasedPsiElementBase.getElementType / StubElement.getStubType).
  • Renamed to "RuleScribe for Kraken Rules".
  • Relicensed under the Functional Source License 1.1 (FSL-1.1-ALv2): free to use and modify, no competing use, converts to Apache-2.0 after two years.
  • README translated to English.
0.5.2
  • Strict namespace semantics for reverse references: gutter icons, declaration-to-usage navigation, Find Usages and the unused-rule inspection now only count references whose namespace can actually see the declaration (mirrors the Kraken engine).
0.5.1
  • Ctrl+click on a Rule or EntryPoint declaration name now navigates to the entry point items referencing it (popup when several).
  • Find Usages now works reliably for multi-word names ("Policy code mandatory") via a dedicated references searcher.
0.5.0
  • Nested EntryPoint items ("EntryPoint \"X\"") are now real references: Ctrl+B navigation, rename refactoring, unknown-reference inspection, gutter icon on entry points included by others.
  • Reworked completion inside EntryPoint blocks: icons, origin file, other entry points suggested, already-listed items and the current entry point excluded.
0.4.1
  • Fixed false-positive syntax errors when Info/Error/Warn is used as a reference or context name in expressions ("Assert Info.additionalInfo = ...", "x instanceof Info") or as a function call ("Warn(x)").
  • The bundled grammar simulator (tools/sim_parser.py) now emulates Grammar-Kit pin semantics to catch this class of bug.
0.4.0
  • Stub-based index for rule declarations: reference resolution, completion and navigation no longer load file ASTs — fast on large projects (hundreds of .rules files).
0.3.0
  • Structured KEL expression grammar (ported from the official Kel.g4/Value.g4): if/then/else, for/return, every/some/satisfies, function calls, access chains with filters and spread (a.b[*].c[filter]), null-safe access (?. and ?[), exponent (**), collection literals, variable blocks (set x to ... return ...).
  • Field completion now also works inside expressions (When Policy.<caret>).
  • Grammar still validated 103/103 against the official kraken-rules corpus.
0.2.0
  • Structure view, code folding, code formatter and live templates (rule, ep, ctx, dim).
  • Field completion after "On Context." (inheritance-aware).
  • Namespace-aware resolution (Namespace / Include).
  • Gutter icon on rules referenced by entry points.
  • Quick documentation (Ctrl+Q) for rules.
  • New inspections: unknown context, duplicate rule, unused rule, undeclared dimension.
0.1.0
  • Initial release: syntax highlighting, code completion, inspections, intention action, navigation and rename refactoring for Kraken .rules files.
  • Grammar validated against the full test corpus of the official eisgroup/kraken-rules repository.

idea-plugin.name: Melos
idea-plugin.description:
Discover and run Melos monorepo scripts declared in a workspace root pubspec.yaml. Adds run gutter icons beside melos.scripts entries, a Melos run configuration type, and a Run | Melos menu group. Automatically resolves between a workspace-local melos dependency (dart run melos:melos) and a globally activated melos installation.

Source code | Report an issue
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Discover and run Melos scripts from gutter icons, the Run menu, and a searchable action.
  • Browse workspace packages, dependencies, dependents, and scripts in the Melos tool window.
  • Visualize package dependencies in an interactive graph editor.
  • Add YAML completion, navigation, workspace-path inspections, and quick fixes.
  • Synchronize generated run configurations and suggest bootstrap after branch changes.

idea-plugin.name: Cfml Extra Completion
idea-plugin.description:
Cfml Extra Completion fills gaps in the bundled CFML plugin's code completion. The built-in completion only sees symbols declared in the current file; this plugin adds the project-wide symbols it misses, and stops flagging them as "unresolved". Suggestions are added on top of the built-in CFML completion — nothing is removed or replaced.

Where the symbols come from

  • Variables and functions declared in the nearest Application.cfm, offered in every page under that directory.
  • application.*, session.*, request.* and custom this.* symbols set in the nearest Application.cfc (e.g. from onApplicationStart / onSessionStart).
  • Variables and functions from files pulled in via cfinclude / script include in the current file (followed recursively, cycle-safe).

They complete unscoped or after the matching scope prefix (application., session., request., this.), shown qualified and highlighted to match the built-in.

And for those same symbols

  • Parameter info — function signatures in completion, plus the argument hint (after ( and while typing arguments).
  • Documentation — a function's preceding comment or hint, in the completion doc pane and Quick Documentation (Ctrl+Q).
  • Go to Declaration — Ctrl/Cmd+Click jumps to the declaration, and follows cfinclude paths resolved through a this.mappings alias.
  • No false "unresolved" warnings — the wavy underline is suppressed for symbols we know exist, while genuinely unknown identifiers stay flagged.

Same-file symbols and standard Application.cfc settings are left to the built-in, so nothing is offered twice.

Optional features (off by default, under Settings | Other Settings | Cfml Extra Completion)

idea-plugin.name: GEDCOM
idea-plugin.description:
GEDCOM language support by Domorium. Read and edit .ged and .gedcom files with confidence using structure-aware suggestions and diagnostics as you type.

Features

idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.7.1

  • A GEDCOM 5.5.1 date names its calendar where the specification puts it. The escape sits inside <DATE>, which comes after the modifier, so ABT @#DHEBREW@ TSH 5760 and a Julian FROM/TO range were reported as invalid dates, while @#DJULIAN@ FROM 1 JAN 1700 TO 1 JAN 1710, which the grammar does not admit, passed. Each date now carries its own calendar and is read in that calendar’s months
  • An exact date is Gregorian, and says so. 1 CHAN / 2 DATE @#DHEBREW@ 1 TSH 5760 validated clean in a 5.5.1 file where the GEDCOM 7 rule for the same payload rejects it: DATE_EXACT has no slot for a calendar
  • A day is measured against the calendar its own date names. FROM JULIAN 1 JAN 1700 TO 29 FEB 1900 reported nothing — the second date is Gregorian, 1900 is not a Gregorian leap year, and it was measured by the Julian rule, which has no exception for a century

1.7.0

  • A hover below a line carrying no tag no longer fails. 0 @I1@, what a truncated export leaves behind, still becomes a line and adopts the lines indented under it; hovering one of those threw where the honest answer was silence, so the request failed instead of answering nothing
  • A file with more than about 125k problems reports all of them. Past that count the whole document came back with none at all, not a shortened list, because every level of the walk spread its findings into its parent's and the runtime refuses past roughly 125k arguments
  • A tag typed in lower case is completed. 1 sex offered nothing where 1 SEX offered the values of the enumeration, though the file itself is read either way
  • Completion on a large file answers in under a millisecond. A 300,000-line document paid 69 ms per keystroke rebuilding a tree that had not changed since the last parse
  • A GEDCOM 5.5.1 date is read against the calendar its escape names, and completion offers that calendar's months. @#DHEBREW@ 45 XXX 5760 passed unexamined, and a 5.5.1 date was offered no month at all where a 7.0 date was offered twelve
  • A 5.5.1 multimedia format and the four LDS ordinance statuses are held to the values the specification lists. 2 FORM png is reported — 5.5.1 has no spelling for it — while 2 FORM JPG is not, since that list is read without regard to case
  • An unresolved pointer names the identifier that failed instead of listing the document's families. A FAMC pointing at a family the file does not declare was answered with a list of up to ten families that were not the problem

1.6.2

  • A .ged file no longer sits silent where the IDE cannot find Node.js. The bundled language server was launched as node against whatever the IDE’s PATH held; with node missing the process failed to start and left a line in the log, so the file arrived with no diagnostics, no completion, no hover and no colour — indistinguishable from the plugin not being installed. An IDE opened from Spotlight, the Dock or Toolbox inherits no login shell’s PATH, so node installed by nvm, fnm, asdf or Volta is invisible to it while it works in a terminal. Node is resolved before launch, and where it is nowhere to be found a sticky balloon names the cause and offers the download page

1.6.1

  • A note written as text in a GEDCOM 5.5.1 file is no longer reported. 1 NOTE plain text was told to be a pointer to a NOTE record, and a source citation carrying its description — 1 SOUR Parish register — was told the same, with TEXT beneath it called an unknown tag. Both are forms the specification provides, and files exported by MyHeritage, Ancestry and Gramps are full of them

1.6.0

  • A file is coloured by what each part of a line is. A tag reads as a keyword rather than a string, an XREF as an identifier rather than a keyword, and the value of a line — which carried no colour at all — as a string. A .ged file will look different after the update
  • An XREF is coloured, and the record it declares is set apart from a reference to it. Both arrived in the colour of ordinary text: the colour scheme has no rule for the key an identifier fell back to, and there is no key at all for a declared one. The plugin now names two keys of the scheme, so the colours are still the ones you chose

1.5.1

  • The same plugin as 1.5.0, which never became installable. Everything below is what this release brings

1.5.0

  • A file whose version cannot be checked no longer looks clean. 2 VERS 4.0, a misspelled version and a file with no version line were all checked against GEDCOM 7 and reported nothing, because none of those rules applied to them. They now carry one error saying so, and the rest of the checking goes quiet rather than judging the file by the wrong specification. Levels, syntax, highlighting, folding and navigation still work
  • 2 VERS 5.5, 5.5.5 and 5.5EL are checked against the 5.5.1 rules with a warning that says the two differ, so some marks may not apply and others may be missing. Those files previously collected the 5.5.1 marks with no explanation of where they came from
  • Completions and file links go quiet for a version with no rules, and a 4.0 file is no longer offered GEDCOM 7 record creation
  • Anything written under a structure that cannot hold it is now marked. A line beneath 1 TITL, or beneath the trailer in a 5.5.1 file, was accepted without comment
  • 2 VERS 5.5.1 written with two spaces was read as GEDCOM 7, so a 5.5.1 file was checked against the wrong rules and an absolute media path stopped being a clickable link. Both are fixed
  • 1 OBJE with FILE and TITL written beneath it, the inline form of a 5.5.1 media link, no longer reports Unknown tag FILE

1.4.0

  • Stopped marking an extension tag used as an enumeration value: 2 PEDI _ENUMVAL and 2 ROLE _CHILD were underlined, though the specification permits extending an enumeration this way. One never declared in HEAD.SCHMA is now a warning instead
  • Read a HEAD.SCHMA tag declared as an abbreviation for a standard URI as the structure it names, so a record written under such an alias satisfies a pointer to the standard tag and a date in an aliased calendar is accepted
  • Stopped reporting 1 EVEN with a TYPE beneath it as missing a value in a GEDCOM 5.5.1 file
  • A count that is not a number is now marked. 1 NCHI abc was accepted, and so were 3.7, 12abc and Infinity
  • An event with neither a value nor anything beneath it is a warning rather than an error, and says what is actually wrong: the line asserts nothing and other software may drop it
  • A source citation pointing at a record type the file does not contain no longer offers an empty list of candidates
  • Problems now carry a distinct code for each kind, so they can be filtered and suppressed separately

1.3.0

  • Stopped marking dates that name their calendar: JULIAN 1401, HEBREW 1 TSH 5761 and even GREGORIAN 1 JAN 2000 were all underlined in a GEDCOM 7 file. Each calendar's own months and epochs now apply, so a Hebrew date carrying a Gregorian month is still caught
  • Three older date forms are now marked in a 7.0 file, so a file that was clean may not be: the @#DGREGORIAN@ calendar escape, a slashed year such as 1 JAN 1857/58, and phrases like INT 1950 (around 1950) or (unknown). Version 7.0 removed all three — a date phrase belongs in a PHRASE line beneath the date. GEDCOM 5.5.1 files are unaffected
  • Stopped reporting a missing value where the specification allows the payload to be left out: 1 EVEN with only a TYPE beneath it was flagged, along with 60 other kinds of line, and so were AGE and DATE left empty with a PHRASE instead
  • Stopped warning on the first line of a file that begins with a byte order mark
  • Reworded the message for a source citation that carries text instead of a pointer, so it says what belongs there rather than naming the rule

1.2.0

  • Kept the spaces that belong to a value: a NOTE beginning with spaces no longer loses them, and CONC continuations no longer change the text they rejoin
  • Stopped the hint for a broken pointer from covering the editor; it listed every matching record in the file and offered a quick fix for each, and now names ten and says how many more there are, with completion still offering all of them
  • Coloured and validated large files without the editor stalling: highlighting is built for the visible lines, the problems view refreshes once typing pauses, and validation cost no longer grows with records times lines
  • Drew the file icon on the 16 pixel grid, so it no longer looks blurred beside the platform's own icons
  • Rebuilt the bundled language server when the language service changes, so a plugin build can no longer ship a stale server

1.1.0

  • Accepted application-defined extension tags (_XXXX) instead of reporting every one of them as an unknown tag, so files exported by other genealogy applications no longer fill the problems view with false warnings
  • Read extension tag declarations from HEAD.SCHMA in GEDCOM 7 documents: hover shows the URI a tag is bound to, and autocomplete offers the declared tags
  • Warned when a GEDCOM 7 document uses an extension tag it never declares in HEAD.SCHMA; GEDCOM 5.5.1 files, which have no such structure, are unaffected
  • Stopped offering top-level record tags as completions inside a structure whose type cannot be resolved

1.0.0

  • First stable release: context-aware autocomplete, real-time validation against the GEDCOM 5.5.1 and 7.0 specifications, semantic highlighting, hover, go to definition, find all references, safe XREF rename, quick fixes, and folding
  • No functional change from 0.3.1

0.3.1

  • Presented the plugin as GEDCOM while retaining Domorium as the ecosystem identity

0.3.0

  • Rebranded the plugin as Domorium: GEDCOM Tools
  • Moved to the new domorium.gedcom plugin ID and @domorium package scope

0.2.1

  • Renamed the plugin to GEDCOM and moved to the new gedcom.jetbrains plugin ID
  • Updated package namespaces, repository links, and bundled language-service dependencies

0.2.0

  • Added Find All References and read/write XREF highlights
  • Added safe, atomic XREF rename with stale-edit protection
  • Added clickable web and local-file links
  • Added quick fixes for broken references and invalid GEDCOM levels

0.1.1

  • Moved the product screenshot from the description to the Marketplace media gallery

0.1.0

  • Initial JetBrains Marketplace release
  • Context-aware GEDCOM autocomplete
  • Real-time validation and semantic highlighting
  • Hover information and go to definition for cross-references
  • Document navigation and code folding

idea-plugin.name: dbt Navigator
idea-plugin.description:
dbt Navigator — models, refs & lineage for dbt, offline

Understand your dbt project inside your IntelliJ-based IDE (IntelliJ IDEA, DataGrip, PyCharm) without leaving the editor or spinning up dbt. The plugin reads your models and their ref() calls to build the model lineage — statically, no dbt runtime, no warehouse connection, fully offline.

Open the tool window from View ▸ Tool Windows ▸ dbt. More on the roadmap: ref() completion, compile preview and model runs.

Not affiliated with dbt Labs. "dbt" is a trademark of dbt Labs, Inc.; used here descriptively.
