idea-plugin.name: DotVVM
idea-plugin.description:
DotVVM support for JetBrains Rider: syntax highlighting, completion, navigation and validation for .dothtml, .dotmaster and .dotcontrol files.

The files are treated as an HTML superset, so the IDE's HTML, CSS and JavaScript support keeps working. Binding expressions are a language of their own, with completion of the kinds and of the members the data context actually has. Directives are highlighted, offered and navigable, and the errors a build would report show while editing - they come from DotVVM's own view compiler rather than from a guess.

Needs a .NET runtime on the machine, version 8 or newer. A language server ships with the plugin and is started as a separate process; Rider's own runtime is not used. With none found the editor still works and the status bar stays empty.

An unofficial plugin, written and maintained independently. It is neither affiliated with nor endorsed by Riganti, who make DotVVM.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.5.0

  • Projects targeting .NET 10 are supported. The probe and the view compiler ship a variant per framework and the newest was net9.0, so on a newer project the plugin lost the project's own controls and had nothing to compile views with
  • The bundled language server now runs on a newer .NET than it was built against. It is built as net8.0 and used to demand exactly that, so a machine carrying only .NET 9 or 10 got an empty status bar and no explanation
  • The plugin no longer uses API the platform has deprecated or keeps to itself, which is what keeps it loading on the IDEs to come

0.4.0

  • Completion inside a binding expression: an opening brace offers the kinds a file may use - value:, command:, staticCommand:, resource: - and after the colon come the members of the data context, which follows the view
  • A dot walks into whatever the expression evaluates to, however long the chain - Customer.Address.City, Items[0].Name
  • Which methods are offered depends on the kind of binding: one evaluated in the browser takes only what DotVVM can translate to JavaScript, one evaluated on the server takes the view model's own methods
  • Typing {{ writes the closing braces, and what is offered inside a binding is kept to what may be written there - no HTML tags, no Emmet abbreviations
  • Needs a project that has been built, the same as live validation and through the same process, so DOTVVM_LS_LIVE_VALIDATION=off switches it off as well

0.3.0

  • Live validation: the errors a build would report now show while editing - a mistyped property in a binding, an identifier the data context does not have, a value of the wrong type. The messages come from DotVVM's own view compiler
  • Saving compiles at once; typing waits half a second for the keystrokes to stop
  • Needs a project built on DotVVM 4.3.0 or newer; set DOTVVM_LS_LIVE_VALIDATION=off to switch it off

0.2.1

  • Completion offers the property families - Class-, Style-, Param- - on controls and on plain HTML elements alike
  • Cmd-click on a control tag opens the .dotcontrol file registered for it, or the class declaring it
  • A control read from the serialized configuration no longer loses what it inherits

0.2.0

  • Completion of a control's properties and of a directive's value - the view model type, a namespace, the path to a master page
  • Validation of the file header: a repeated or misspelt directive, a missing value, a type or master page that is not there
  • Server-side comments <%-- --%> are painted, parsed and produced as comments, between a tag's attributes as well
  • Cmd-click in a directive opens the type's source, or the project building the assembly named after the comma
  • Hover reports the properties of the project's own controls, markup controls included

0.1.0

  • Highlighting for binding expressions, including nested braces and quotes inside the expression
  • Directives: highlighting, name completion, navigation to the master page
  • Tag validation, control completion and navigation to the view model from the directive
  • A status bar indicator naming what the language server knows about the project
  • Suppression of messages the platform reports only because it does not know DotVVM

idea-plugin.name: JimmerCraft
idea-plugin.description:
JimmerCraft

IDE support for the Jimmer framework.

Jimmer trades static guarantees for flexibility — it moves a set of invariants from compile time to runtime:

  • object shapes
  • property references inside annotations
  • the existence of generated types

The type system says nothing about any of them.

JimmerCraft brings the ones that can be brought forward back to edit time.

JimmerCraft depends on JimmerDTO, installing JimmerCraft installs it as well, and it stays installed on its own if you later remove JimmerCraft.

Install JimmerDTO alone if you only write .dto files.

JimmerCraft works in both Java and Kotlin.

Features

Property names written as strings

Jimmer annotations carry property names as plain strings; the IDE checks none of them.

JimmerCraft resolves them against the entity model. Covered so far:

mappedBy — @OneToOne, @OneToMany, @ManyToMany

mappedBy names a property on the target entity.

Rename that property, or mistype the name, and nothing tells you until the annotation processor runs.

  • reports invalid names
    • no such property on the target entity
    • the property is not an association
    • it does not point back to this entity
    • it lacks the matching annotation
    • it already declares its own mappedBy
  • completes the properties that can be the inverse side
  • navigates to the property declaration on Ctrl+Click

The name resolves to a property, and hovering shows it.

Ctrl+hover previews the declaration; Ctrl+Click goes there.

A name that points somewhere else is reported in place.

Completion offers only the properties that can be the inverse side.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changelog

Unreleased

0.1.0

Added

  • Report invalid property names in mappedBy of @OneToOne, @OneToMany and @ManyToMany.
  • Complete valid property names in mappedBy of @OneToOne, @OneToMany and @ManyToMany.
  • Ctrl+Click on the mappedBy value in @OneToOne, @OneToMany and @ManyToMany now navigates to the referenced property.

idea-plugin.name: Ansible Sense
idea-plugin.description:
Ansible support that knows which of your YAML files are Ansible, and leaves every other one alone.

Every other Ansible plugin claims *.yml and *.yaml as a file type. The moment you install one, your Kubernetes manifests, Helm charts, docker-compose files, CloudFormation templates and GitHub workflows start showing errors that are not there, and you end up deleting file type associations by hand to get your project back.

This plugin registers no file type at all. It reads what is actually inside each file and decides one file at a time. When it is not sure, it does nothing, and your IDE behaves exactly as if it were not installed. Exclusions are checked before anything else and always win: a false positive breaks someone else's work, a false negative only costs a suggestion.

What you get

  • Module completion, with the full name. Both ansible.builtin.systemd_service and the short systemd_service are offered and understood, each with a one-line description of what it does. Fully qualified collection names are first-class, not an afterthought.
  • Your own variables, from anywhere in the project. Every group_vars, host_vars, vars and defaults directory is read, at any depth, whether it is a single file or a directory of files. Inside {{ }} you get your variables with the place they were defined shown next to them, plus the facts Ansible always provides. Variables created by set_fact, by a vars: block and by register: are picked up too.
  • Roles, wherever you keep them. A role is not a path, it is a directory that contains tasks/. So roles outside roles/ are found like any other, and role names complete inside a roles: block.
  • Jinja2 is understood, not tripped over. {{ }}, {% %} and {# #} are parsed, and a filter or an attribute is not mistaken for a variable.
  • A warning only where it is certain. An unknown module is flagged only inside ansible.builtin, the one collection whose contents are known in full, and the closest real name is offered. A module from a collection this plugin does not know, including your own internal ones, is never touched. Not knowing is not an error.

Free, and no upper IDE version bound: it keeps working after upgrades.
idea-plugin.change-notes: • 0.1.0 — first release: content-based recognition of Ansible files with no file type registration, module completion with fully qualified names, project-wide variable and role completion, Jinja2 parsing, and an unknown-module warning limited to ansible.builtin.

idea-plugin.name: Spec Checker for OpenAPI
idea-plugin.description:
Checks and navigates OpenAPI and Swagger documents in YAML and JSON. Supports Swagger 2.0 and OpenAPI 3.0, 3.1 and 3.2.

In the editor

  • Structure checks against the official OpenAPI JSON Schema for the document's version: unknown fields (with a reminder that extensions start with x-), missing required fields, an object where a list or a value is expected (and the reverse), and values outside a fixed list, such as in: body in OpenAPI 3.x.
  • Unresolved $ref: a file that doesn't exist, or a JSON pointer (#/components/schemas/Pet) that isn't in the target document, in the same file or a relative file. The warning clears when the missing file or component is added.
  • Operations: duplicate operationIds; path template variables such as {petId} with no matching in: path parameter; path parameters whose name isn't in the path.
  • Navigation: Go to Declaration on a $ref jumps to its target, in the same file or a relative file. Navigate | OpenAPI Operation or Component… (also in the editor's context menu) lists the document's operations, webhooks and components to search and jump to.
  • Rename a component and the $refs to it in the document are updated.
  • Completion: field names for the object at the caret, from the schema of the document's version; values where the schema gives a fixed list; $ref pointers to the document's components (definitions, parameters and responses in Swagger 2.0).

The checks are three inspections for YAML and three for JSON under Settings | Editor | Inspections | Spec Checker for OpenAPI; each can be switched off or given another severity.

How it works

A file counts as an OpenAPI document only if its root has an openapi: 3.x or swagger: 2.x field. Other YAML and JSON files get only the $ref check; JSON files with a root $schema are left to the IDE's JSON Schema support.

Checks run in the IDE's background highlighting and work one file at a time: the document being checked and the files its $refs name. The plugin builds no project-wide index and adds no file type of its own; it works on the IDE's bundled YAML and JSON support. The field tables are generated by a script from the official OpenAPI JSON Schemas. No network access (remote https:// references are neither fetched nor checked), no telemetry, no account.

It doesn't need JetBrains' OpenAPI Specifications plugin; the two have not been tested together.

Limits

  • No preview (Swagger UI, Redoc), no try-it console, no code generation.
  • Schema Objects are not validated keyword by keyword. Rules in the official schemas that depend on other fields (for example, which fields a querystring parameter may have) are not checked.
  • Objects that use $ref or a YAML merge key (<<) are not checked for required fields.
  • Specs split over several files: files reached through $ref (for example paths/orders.yaml) get only the $ref check, not the structure or operation checks; path items kept in other files appear in the Navigate list by path only.
  • Anchor-style fragments (#name) are not checked.
  • Files over the IDE's code-insight size limit (2.5 MB by default) get no checks, navigation or completion, as with any plugin. To include them, raise idea.max.intellisense.filesize (in KB) via Help | Edit Custom Properties.

Compatibility

IntelliJ-based IDEs, builds 243–262 (2024.3 to 2026.2), with the bundled YAML and JSON plugins. Checked with the IntelliJ Plugin Verifier against IntelliJ IDEA Community 2024.3.5 and IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2 (both Compatible). Other IDEs and versions in the range are expected to work but have not been verified.

About

Built and maintained with AI agents by Madrasco. Support: support@madrasco.dev.

OpenAPI is a trademark of The Linux Foundation. Swagger is a trademark of SmartBear Software. This plugin is not affiliated with or endorsed by either.

idea-plugin.name: Claudex Autocomplete
idea-plugin.description:
Inline code completion in your editor, using the Claude Code or Codex CLI you already have installed and logged in. Uses your existing subscription login, no API key needed.

Features

  • Inline gray-text suggestions as you type
  • Choose Claude Code or Codex as the provider
  • Accept the whole suggestion, the next word or the rest of the line
  • Context from the current file, open tabs and, for PHP, imported classes
  • Persistent Claude Code process for lower latency
  • Animated spinner with elapsed time while a suggestion is generated
  • Status bar widget with request state and usage windows
  • Custom prompt additions and per-language disable list

Requirements

  • IntelliJ-based IDE 2025.3 or newer
  • Claude Code CLI (claude) or Codex CLI (codex), installed and logged in

Getting started

  1. Log in: run claude and then /login, or run codex login.
  2. Choose Enable in the first-run notification, or turn on Enable completions in Settings | Tools | Claudex Autocomplete, and select the provider.
  3. Start typing. Press Tab to accept, Esc to dismiss, Shift+Alt+\ (Shift+Option+\ on macOS) to trigger manually, or use Tools | Trigger Claudex Autocomplete to force a completion mid-line.

Privacy

The plugin runs your local CLI with your existing subscription login. Code context around the caret, and optionally from open tabs, is sent to Anthropic or OpenAI through that CLI and is subject to their terms. Files that look like secrets (such as .env, keys and credentials) and files ignored by VCS are never sent. Nothing is sent until you enable completions.

Claudex Autocomplete is an independent project and is not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by Anthropic or OpenAI. Claude is a trademark of Anthropic; Codex is a trademark of OpenAI.

  • First-run consent: nothing is sent and no CLI is started before you enable completions
  • Secret-like and VCS-ignored files are never sent as context

idea-plugin.name: Nagi
idea-plugin.description:
Nagi language support for IntelliJ IDEA and PyCharm. This is an unreleased 0.1.3 candidate, not a published release; full IDE GUI verification is pending.

Provides syntax highlighting for High (.nagi) and Low (.low) files, code folding, indentation support, compiler-backed completion and current-snapshot diagnostics, source navigation when the compiler returns an exact target, and a standard Nagi Run Configuration with the IDE's Run and Stop controls.

The plugin's High/Low syntax highlighting does not require a compiler; published nagic 0.1.11 continues to support manual Check/Run and normal Run Configuration execution. Semantic assistance is partial editor analysis, not a full build check; diagnostics report only the first compiler error returned. Completion, diagnostics, and navigation require a development compiler built from the same PR source commit. Published 0.1.11 does not provide the assist protocol; use the matching compiler CI artifact.

Nagi: Check and Nagi: Run remain available for a Nagi file or the nearest project containing nagi.toml. Commands and Run Configurations require a trusted project and save open files before starting.

The compiler is installed separately and is not bundled with the plugin. Published compiler releases are available from GitHub Releases. The matching compiler for semantic assistance in this unreleased candidate is a PR CI artifact, not a formal release. The candidate plugin itself is not yet published to GitHub Releases or Marketplace.

日本語

IntelliJ IDEA・PyCharm向けのNagi言語サポートです。未公開の0.1.3候補であり、正式公開版ではありません。IDE全体のGUI検証は未完了です。

High（.nagi）・Low（.low）のシンタックスハイライト、コードの折りたたみ、インデント支援、コンパイラによる補完と現在のsnapshotに基づく診断、正確な参照先が返された場合の定義への移動、IDE標準のRun/Stopを使うNagi Run Configurationを提供します。

プラグインのHigh/Low syntax highlightingはcompilerに依存せず、公開済みnagic 0.1.11は手動のCheck/Runと通常のRun Configuration実行に引き続き使えます。semantic assistanceはエディター向けの部分解析で、完全なbuild検査ではなく、診断にはcompilerが最初に返すエラーだけが表示されます。補完・診断・定義への移動には同じPR source commitから作成した開発版compilerが必要です。公開済み0.1.11にassist protocolはないため、PRのmatching compiler CI artifactを使用してください。

Nagi: Check / Nagi: Runに加えて、Nagiファイルまたは最寄りのnagi.tomlを含むプロジェクトを標準Run Configurationから実行できます。各操作にはproject trustが必要で、起動前に開いているfileを保存します。

コンパイラは別途インストールしてください。プラグインには同梱されていません。公開済みcompilerはGitHub Releasesから取得できます。semantic assistanceに対応するcompilerはPRのCI artifactで、正式releaseではありません。この候補pluginはGitHub ReleaseやMarketplaceへまだ公開していません。

Teamscale analyzes source code incrementally with every commit, which means, it can provide feedback to your IDE in a matter of seconds. idea-plugin.name: Better Highlights
idea-plugin.description:
Features:

  • Colorize comments.
  • Reference source code in comments.
  • Show cognitive complexity for methods.
  • Use gutter icons for highlights.
  • Highlight regions (whole line highlight).
  • Reference files in comments.
  • Reference other comments inside comments.
  • [PAID] Highlight keywords, methods and functions (syntax highlight).
  • [PAID] Highlight anything by RegExp.
  • [PAID] Define highlight severity for comment/tokens/regexp.
  • [PAID] Display settings for cognitive complexity.
  • [PAID] Define custom start/end tokens for wikilink format.
  • [PAID] Reference source code in comments outside wikilink.
  • [PAID] Genese Cpx cognitive complexity algorithm.
  • [PAID] Add custom gutter icons.
  • [PAID] Wikilink support in Markdown and plain text files.

Elevate your coding experience with "Better Highlights", one of the best plugins designed for JetBrains products. Unleash the power of keyword, methods and comment highlighting, seamless code referencing in comments, and real-time cognitive complexity metrics. Compatible with all JetBrains IDEs, including IntelliJ IDEA, Android Studio, PyCharm, PhpStorm, Webstorm and more, this top plugin guarantees coding excellence, no matter the JetBrains tool you use.

Comment/Region/Keyword/Method/Functions/RegExp plugin functionality description:

  • "Highlighting" means ability of changing color of programming language keywords, comments etc.
  • Highlighting is based on first word in commented line. By default, are used tokens *, !, ?.
  • User can add own custom tokens for colorizing comment lines.
  • Comment highlighting supports default color settings change - color, background color, bold, italic, effects.
  • Region highlighting is used to colorize whole commented line with some background color to visually separate blocks of code.
  • Keyword highlighting is used to colorize programming language keywords in other words custom syntax highlight. Method keywords is used to colorize keywords, which are part of method signature (most often used to change color of access modifiers private/public/protected on methods, but not classes).
  • Method/Functions highlighting is used to colorize methods and functions implementation and usage/reference. Methods/Functions are defined with RegExp (most often used to change color of getter and setters).
  • RegExp highlighting is used to colorize anything by RegExp. Usually is used to colorize language constructions, which are not keywords or to colorize some phrases, not just single keyword.
  • RegExp highlighting can be limited to certain files with file name regexps.
  • Simple word is also a valid RegExp, so could be used to colorize regular language constructions, which are not keywords.
  • User can select different highlight severity to override Error and Warning highlights and display highlights in list of errors/warnings.
  • User can select gutter icon for comment/region/keyword/method/function/regexp highlighting.

Wikilink plugin functionality description:

  • Wikilink is a format of linking articles used in Wikipedia, where links are wrapped with double square brackets. For example, [[this is wikilink]].
  • Highlights wikilinks in comments.
  • Wikilink highlighting supports default color settings change - color, background color, bold, italic, effects.
  • Support wikilink references to files (absolute or relative path) (link to file in comment).
  • Support wikilink references to tagged comments (link comments).
  • Support wikilink references to classes and class methods/fields (link source code). This is one of the best feature of plugin.
  • Support wikilink references for non-OOP languages via file name with [[filename.ext#funcitonName]]
  • Wikilink references supports "Go to definition", "Find usages" and "Rename refactoring" intellij out of the box functionality.
  • Intellij Inspection to find and highlight unresolved references in wikilink(not existing links) for file and project levels.
  • Support tagged comments autocompletion in wikilink.
  • Support class names and methods autocompletion in wikilink.
  • Define user start/end tokens instead of using wikilink format.
  • Support source code references in comments outside wikilink (any word would be resolved as source code reference).
  • Support wikilinks in Markdown and plain text files with references to Markdown file without extension. This can be used for Personal Knowledge Management (Second Brain) to create links between notes.

Cognitive complexity plugin functionality description:

  • Calculates SonarQube Cognitive Complexity metric for methods, which was proposed by G. Ann Campbell in Cognitive Complexity - A new way of measuring understandability.
  • Calculates Genese Cpx Cognitive Complexity metric for methods, which was described by Gilles Fabre in a github repo.
  • Metric is shown as inlay hint with realtime live calculation. This is one of the most recommended feature of plugin.
  • User can adjust position of inlay hint, define custom description text, custom description background and display complexity icon in gutter.
  • "high cognitive complexity" inspection is available to find in project all methods with high complexity.

Plugin functionality support by language:

Language Comment, Region,

highlighting		 Keyword

complexity		 Source code
reference

* Highlighting should work with any language, not only mentioned in table (for example, lua, groovy, scala, haskell, erlang, elixir etc.)

If you need support for another language or some additional functionality - feel free to create a ticket in bugtracker.


Examples of commonly used keyword highlights:

  • abstract - usually used with "Highlight only in method definitions" to ease determining of abstract methods in abstract classes.
  • public - usually used with "Highlight only in method definitions" to ease determining of public methods in Util/Helper classes.
  • ! - usually used to ease determining of "not" inversion in "if" clauses. Note that in C# "!" is not keyword, so regexp should be used instead in Rider.
  • return - usually used to ease determining of method exists in long methods.

How-to:

  • How to use highlighting.
  • How to use wikilinks.
  • How to use cognitive complexity.
  • How to import/export settings.

Your coding journey doesn't have to be ordinary - take your coding experience to new heights with the most useful and top-rated "Better Highlights" plugin. Enhance code readability with highlighting keywords and comments, bringing brilliance to every line. Level up code clarity instantly with real-time cognitive complexity metrics. This cool plugin is your go-to for optimizing your workflow, seamlessly referencing source code from comments. Ready to transform your code now? Install "Better Highlights" and witness the future of coding clarity.


Supports all Jetbrains products: IntelliJ IDEA, Android Studio, Aqua, CLion, GoLand, PhpStorm, PyCharm, Rider, RubyMine, RustRover, WebStorm.

idea-plugin.name: BlackConnect
idea-plugin.description:
Connect to blackd and format your Python code without creating a new black process!


Avoid overhead of starting a new black process on each file save by making a quick HTTP call to blackd instead.


Features supported:


– Automatically starting blackd when IDE opens.
– Automatic Python type stub (.pyi) detection.
– Configurable options: hostname, port, preferred line length, etc.
– Trigger automatically when saving changed files.
- Ability to reformat only selected code fragment.
– Support for [tool.black] section in pyproject.toml.
– Rough support for "Jupyter" file type.


Steps to use:

  1. pip install "black[d]"
  2. Start blackd daemon.
  3. Press "Alt + Shift + B" to reformat your code...
    ...or enable "on file save" option.
  4. Enjoy!

idea-plugin.name: Codespector
idea-plugin.description:
The Codespector plugin helps you detect missing annotations in your kotlin data classes and adds them. This is especially critical in Android applications. Currently, the following annotations are supported:

  • SerializedName - If you are using Gson
  • Json - If you are using Moshi
  • SerialName - If you are using Kotlinx-Serialization


You can specify the packages which need inspection via the setting. When packages are provided then the plugin inspects data classes in only those packages. When no packages are provided then the plugin continues to inspect all the data classes.

If you wish to contribute or require support for other languages please feel free to open an issue or discussion here.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
v0.4.5:
The plugin is now compatible with K2 compiler.


v0.4.3:
Now the plugin has a setting using which the users can specify which packages need inspection. This is specially useful in large projects which have multiple modules. If no packages are provided then the plugin will continue to inspect all the data classes.

Fix inner class not detecting required annotation


v0.3.1:
Added support for Json (Moshi) and SerialName (Kotlinx-Serialization) annotations


Initial Release v0.2.3:
Inspect kotlin data classes for missing SerializedName annotations

idea-plugin.name: Ruff
idea-plugin.description:
Features

  • Inspection and highlighting
  • Integrating Reformat Code with ⌥⇧ ⌘ L or Ctrl+Alt+L
  • Quick Fix (from mouse-over, ⌥⏎ or Alt+Enter)
    • Show fix message
    • Suppressing warnings with # noqa:
  • Show code explanation tooltips when hovering # noqa: <code>
  • Run ruff --fix as an action
  • Run ruff --fix for a file when the file is saved
  • Detect both global and project-specific instances of ruff
    • Always use global ruff command
    • Custom global ruff executable path
    • Detect a project ruff after packages refreshed
  • Execute ruff command as a new process
  • Support ruff config file path as an option
  • Detect ruff executable in Conda environment
  • Detect ruff executable in WSL
  • Support Ruff LSP feature
    • LSP Client
      • JetBrains LSP integration for unified PyCharm, including free mode
      • LSP4IJ by RedHat (Requires installation of the LSP4IJ plugin)
    • LSP Server
      • ruff-lsp integration
      • ruff server integration
    • Live Config Reload: Automatically updates from pyproject.toml and ruff.toml without restarting
  • Support ruff format for ruff version 0.0.289 or later [Experimental]

JetBrains LSP client support

In unified PyCharm builds, including free mode, you can enable the JetBrains LSP client in Preferences/Settings -> Tools -> Ruff.

PyCharm made the LSP client APIs available without a paid subscription starting with 2025.1: https://platform.jetbrains.com/t/update-on-lsp-and-template-language-apis-in-pycharm/1453

The lsp integration applies only below features:

  • Errors/warnings highlighting (textDocument/publishDiagnostics)
  • Quick-fixes for these errors/warnings (textDocument/codeAction

This is experimental feature.

idea-plugin.name: ProxyAI
idea-plugin.description:
ProxyAI is an AI-powered code assistant designed to help you with various programming activities. It's a powerful alternative to Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, AI Assistant, and other JetBrains plugins.

Highly Configurable

Access top-tier language models (LLMs) with your own API key or use privately hosted models within your corporate network.

  • Cloud Providers & Custom Setups: Integrate top-tier models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Mistral, or use self-hosted models for offline use.
  • Bring Your Own Key: Connect with your preferred provider using your API key.
  • Custom Setup: Integrate privately hosted models with OpenAI API-compatible configuration.

Build Your Own Local AI Assistant

ProxyAI is the leading open-source extension for connecting your locally running LLM with JetBrains IDEs. Enjoy full AI assistance without sending data externally or needing an internet connection.

  • Ollama Integration: Automatically detect and utilize Ollama-managed models.
  • GGUF Support: Easily connect custom models.
  • LLaMA C/C++ Integration: Run various open-source LLMs without third-party software.

Core Features

ProxyAI offers a wide range of features to enhance your development experience:

Chat

Get instant coding advice through a ChatGPT-like interface that accepts image input. Ask questions, share screenshots, seek explanations, or get guidance on your projects without leaving your IDE.

Auto Apply

Stream AI-suggested code changes directly into your editor. Preview modifications in diff view and approve or reject them with a single click.

Use images

Chat with your images. Upload manually or let ProxyAI auto-detect your screenshots.

Reference your files and folders

Quickly access and reference your project files and folders for context-aware coding assistance.

Reference web documentations

Easily pull in relevant web documentation into your chat for quick reference—whether it’s API docs, library guides, framework manuals, or something else.

Search the web

Connect your favourite LLM to the web. ProxyAI will search for the most relevant information to answer your questions.

Customize your assistant

Choose between multiple different personas for your specific needs, whether you're looking to learn, write or proofread.

Code

Get helpful code completions as you type, edit your code using natural language, create clear and concise commit messages automatically, and more. ProxyAI equips you with cutting-edge tools to streamline your workflow.

Next edits

Get multi-line edits based on your recent activity as you type.

Autocomplete your code

Receive single-line or whole-function autocomplete suggestions as you type.

Edit code in natural language

Highlight the code you want to modify, describe the desired changes, and watch ProxyAI work its magic.

Get name suggestions

Get context-aware naming suggestions for methods, variables, and more.

Generate commit messages

Generate concise and descriptive commit messages based on the changes made in your codebase.

Offline Development Support (llama.cpp and Ollama)

Integrate local open-source language models into your coding environment and enjoy a full experience without sending your data anywhere or needing an internet connection.

Privacy

Your data stays yours. ProxyAI does not collect or store any sensitive information. With users' consent, we collect anonymous usage data to understand how users interact with the extension, including the most-used features and preferred providers.

License

ProxyAI's code is open source under the Apache License 2.0.

Feedback

Your input helps us grow. Reach out through:

  • Homepage
  • Issue Tracker
  • Discord
  • Email

idea-plugin.name: Armadillo-new
idea-plugin.description:
Armadillo is an IntelliJ IDEA plugin designed to speed up and simplify debugging by letting you capture and persist snapshots of debugger variables directly inside the IDE.

Instead of taking screenshots or manually comparing variable states, Armadillo saves variable snapshots into a dedicated tool window, where they remain accessible across your debugging session. The tool window can be placed on a second monitor, allowing you to work side by side with your code while reviewing past states.

Key benefits

  • Efficient analysis of complex scenarios
    Capture variable states at different breakpoints and review them later without interrupting your debugging flow. This makes it much easier to understand how data evolves and where things start to go wrong.
  • Side-by-side workflow on multiple screens
    Keep Armadillo’s tool window open on another screen while continuing to debug and write code, so historical state is always visible without context switching.
  • Fast comparison with built-in diffing
    Diff any two snapshots side by side to immediately spot changes in variable values without manual visual comparison.
  • Quick search and organization
    Snapshots are persisted in Armadillo’s own tool window, with search capabilities that help you locate specific variables or states quickly.
  • Reduced cognitive overhead
    By eliminating screenshots and manual note-taking, Armadillo keeps all debugging context inside the IDE, saving time and reducing errors.
  • Free tier with practical limits
    The free version allows up to 10 saved snapshots, making it easy to try the workflow before upgrading.

idea-plugin.name: Microservices Annotator Annotations Extension
idea-plugin.description:
Microservices Annotator plugin with annotation support.

Usage:

  • Add Microservices Annotator dependency

<dependency>
    <groupId>org.mvnsearch</groupId>
    <artifactId>microservices-annotator</artifactId>
    <version>0.2.3</version>
</dependency>
  • Add annotation for class/field/parameter/variable.

@RemoteAccess
public interface UserService {
    String findNickById(Integer id);
}

// or 
public class UserController {
    @RemoteAccess
    private UserService userService;
}
  • Microservices annotator icon will be in the gutter when APIs called.
String nick = userService.findNickById(1);

Microservices Annotator interaction types and annotations:

  • Broadcast Data transmission: @Broadcast
  • Cloud Storage Access: @CloudStorage
  • Database Access: @DatabaseAccess
  • Data Access: @DataAccess
  • File System Operations: @FileOps
  • IO Read: @IORead
  • IO Write: @IOWrite
  • Message Receive: @MessageReceive
  • Message Send: @MessageSend
  • Streaming: @Streaming
  • Network Request: @RemoteAccess
  • External Process: @ExternalProcess
  • JNI/FFI(Foreign Function Interface) Call: @ForeignAccess

Extra highlight for comment:

// ! Please note that this method is some expensive operation

Extra: annotator's interaction framework hint from annotation's value attribute.

idea-plugin.name: Biome
idea-plugin.description:
Biome IntelliJ Plugin

The Biome IntelliJ Plugin provides comprehensive support for Biome within IntelliJ IDEA.

Features:
  • Linting
  • Quick Fix (from mouse-over, ⌥⏎ or Alt+Enter)
  • Reformat your code with ⌥⇧ ⌘ L or Ctrl+Alt+L

Biome is a fast formatter for JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, TSX, JSON, CSS, and GraphQL that scores 97% compatibility with Prettier, saving CI and developer time.

It is also a performant linter for JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, CSS, and GraphQL, featuring 281 rules from ESLint, TypeScript ESLint, and other sources.

Not only can you format and lint your code separately, you can do it all at once with a single command!

  • Fast Built with Rust and an innovative architecture inspired by rust-analyzer.
  • Zero configuration needed to get started. Extensive options available for when you need them.
  • Scalable Designed to handle codebases of any size. Focus on growing product instead of your tools.
  • With tight internal integration we are able to reuse previous work and any improvement to one tool improves them all.
  • Actionable & Informative Avoid obscure error messages, when we tell you something is wrong, we tell you exactly where the problem is and how to fix it.
  • Out of the box support for all the language features you use today. First class support for TypeScript and JSX.
Resources:
  • Biome Official Website
  • Biome Official Discord Server
  • Biome Intellij Repository
  • Issue Tracker

idea-plugin.name: VisualDDD
idea-plugin.description:
Development Cloud - VisualDDD (Visual Development Platform for Domain-Driven Design)

Environment Setup

  1. Set up the environment for VisualDDD development platform.

  2. Enter VisualDDD development platform and create a project, associate the required business domains and scenarios.

Quick Start

  1. Install the VisualDDD plugin (Visual Development Platform for Domain-Driven Design)
  • Search for the VisualDDD plugin.
  1. Log in to the platform account.

Tips: Use the same platform account.

  1. Associate platform configuration.

Associate and bind the current project with the platform application.

  1. Generate code.
  • Click Refresh to fetch the latest application information, associated business domains, and scenarios.
  • Support custom project information (does not affect platform data, only valid for code generation)
    • Unique identifier - default application identifier, can be overridden by the project name
    • Package path - default application package path, can be overridden by the project package structure
    • Version number - default application version number, can be overridden by the project version number
  • Support selecting the business domains and scenarios to generate.
  • Support custom output path.
    • Default generate to the current project.
    • If you want to add the generated code to the current project, you can output it to the parent directory of the current project.
  • Support generating project framework.

idea-plugin.name: Fitten Code:Faster and Better AI Assistant
idea-plugin.description:
Fitten Code: Your Professional AI Coding Assistant

English Introduction | 中文介绍

Fitten Code is an AI coding assistant powered by a large-scale code model developed by Fitten Tech. It supports multiple languages, including Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, C, C++, and more. With Fitten Code, you can automatically complete code, generate code, generate comments, edit code, explain code, generate tests, find errors, and more, all within the sidebar.

Fitten Code aims to make your coding experience more enjoyable and efficient.

Features

Super Fast Code Autocompletion

In less than 250ms, Fitten Code automatically completes your code by predicting what comes next. It can save you valuable development time, increase your work efficiency, accelerate your development process, and provide the convenience of seamless code completion.

  • Press tab to accept all completion suggestions.
  • Press CTRL+⬇️ (Windows, Linux) / CMD+⬇️ (macOS) to accept a line of completion suggestions.
  • Press CTRL+➡️ (Windows, Linux) / CMD+➡️ (macOS) to accept a single word completion suggestion.

Code Generation

Fitten Code can generate code based on your needs, including classes, functions, variables, comments, and more.

Code Translation

Fitten Code provides semantic-level code translation between multiple languages.

Comment Generation

Automatically add line-level comments to your code, saving you valuable development time.

More Features

Code Editing

Select the code, type in how you would like to edit the code in the chatbox. Fitten Code will edit the code for you.

Code Explanation

Select the code, ask questions about it in the chatbox. Fitten Code will explain to you.

Test Generation

Fitten Code can generate test cases for the code you select.

Error Finding

Fitten Code can find potential defects in your code.

For any issues or suggestions related to Fitten Code, feel free to scan the QR code below to provide feedback, or contact us via email: code@fittentech.com.

Join us and make programming more efficient and enjoyable with Fitten Code!

Fitten Code: 你的专业 AI 代码助手

Fitten Code 是一个由非十科技自研代码大模型驱动的 AI 代码助手。它支持多种语言，包括 Python、JavaScript、TypeScript、Java、C、C++ 等。使用 Fitten Code，你可以自动进行代码补全，并可以在侧边栏内生成代码、生成注释、编辑代码、解释代码、生成测试、查找错误等。

Fitten Code 旨在使你的编程体验更加愉快和高效。

特性

超快的代码自动补全

延迟小于250ms，Fitten Code 通过预测自动为你补全后续代码，它能够节省您宝贵的开发时间，提升工作效率，加速开发进程，享受无缝补全代码的便利。

  • 按下 tab 接受所有补全建议。
  • 按下 CTRL+⬇️ (Windows, Linux) / CMD+⬇️ (macOS) 接受一行补全建议。
  • 按下 CTRL+➡️ (Windows, Linux) / CMD+➡️ (macOS) 接收单个词补全建议。

代码生成

Fitten Code 能够根据你的需求生成代码，包括类、函数、变量、注释等。

代码翻译

Fitten Code 提供多种语言之间的语义级别的代码翻译。

注释生成

自动为你的代码添加行级注释，节省你宝贵的开发时间。

更多特性

编辑代码

Fitten Code 对你选定的代码进行编辑。

解释代码

让 Fitten Code 向你解释选定的代码。

生成测试

为你选定的代码生成测试用例。

查找错误

使用 Fitten Code 在你的代码中找出潜在的缺陷。

如有 Fitten Code 相关问题或建议欢迎扫描下方二维码进行反馈。

加入我们，与 Fitten Code 一起让编程更高效、更愉快！

idea-plugin.name: Soteri Secret Scanner
idea-plugin.description:
Detect Secrets While Developing

A real-time IntelliJ vulnerability scanner that detects secrets in your code and queries. Mitigate data leaks early in the development process with this local scanner.

Secrets should trigger warnings just like forgotten commas. With Soteri Secret Scanner they do.

Soteri Secret Scanner helps developers and teams:

  • Commit code and run queries without secrets

  • Gain peace of mind knowing a common mistake doesn't go undetected

  • Protect your company from a data breach rooting from data leaks

  • Mitigate security vulnerabilities as early as possible

Features

  • Real-time detection of API keys, passwords, financial information, and other secrets

  • 40+ built-in detection patterns for a wide range of secrets

  • Ignore false positives with a click of a button (which adds a pragma next to the alleged secret)

How the Scanner Works

  • Add a secret such as an API key

  • A warning will show up similar to the ones for syntax issues

  • Hovering over the secret will give you the options to remove it or add a pragma to ignore it

Privacy 🔒

Soteri respects data sovereignty, ensuring your sensitive information remains secure, confined and never transmitted elsewhere. In other words, we don't phone home.

How to Install

  1. Open settings and select "Plugins"

  2. Click the "Marketplace" tab

  3. Search for "Soteri Secret Scanner"

  4. Click install

FAQs

Do you have access to my code or secrets?

Absolutely not. This plugin is 100% local and never transmits data elsewhere.

What types of security vulnerabilities does this scan for?

Soteri is dedicated to mitigating one of the most dangerous security vulnerabilities – data leaks. Therefore, the scanner is focused on finding secrets in your code and queries.

Will this stop my code from compiling?

No, Soteri Secret Scanner is a visual inspection tool that detects security issues as you type.

I'm looking for a feature that doesn't exist. Where can I request it?

We'd love to hear ideas from you! Please submit any feedback here.

What languages does this support?

Soteri Secret Scanner is language agnostic. You can use any language or framework and the scanner will effectively detect secrets. That's because the scanner works by detecting various patterns in the secrets, not variable names, for example.

Why use this locally?

Preventing data leaks requires multiple layers. Ideally, they are caught before ever leaving your computer. If a secret winds up in a commit or log, the secret should be considered compromised and should be immediately revoked or rotated. It's essential to treat any exposed secret as a potential security breach, acting swiftly to mitigate risks. Therefore, it's an essential proactive step to mitigate mistakes early on, i.e., locally

Data Leak Detection at All Stages

Take a comprehensive approach to mitigating data leaks by catching them throughout the development process:

  1. Get warned about secrets in your own code as you paste them in (this plugin)

  2. Block commits containing secrets (Security for Bitbucket)

  3. Find secrets in the codebase and all past commits (Security for Bitbucket)

Install now to proactively detect secrets in your code!

idea-plugin.name: MongoDB
idea-plugin.description:
MongoDB Plugin for IntelliJ

The MongoDB Plugin for IntelliJ provides seamless integration with MongoDB deployments, whether they are local, containerized, or hosted on MongoDB Atlas (including those managed via atlascli). The plugin aims to enhance your development workflow with intelligent code autocompletion, valuable performance and correctness insights, and a dedicated query runner. It supports Java queries written with the MongoDB Java Driver and Spring Data MongoDB Criteria.

Features

  • Effortless Connectivity: Connect your IDE directly to any MongoDB cluster using your Data Explorer using a user-friendly side panel.
  • Intelligent Autocompletion: Get smart suggestions for database names, collection names, and field names as you type.
  • Performance Insights: Analyze your project for potential performance bottlenecks and receive actionable index suggestions.
  • Smart Type Checking: Validate your schema and ensure the correctness of your queries with intelligent type checking.
  • Integrated Query Runner: Transform your Java queries into valid mongosh queries and execute them directly within your IDE.

Screenshots & Gifs

Connecting to a Cluster

Intelligent Autocompletion in Java

Performance Insights & Create Index

Run Java Queries

Documentation

To get more information about plugin features and usage, please visit the documentation.

Troubleshooting

You can report new bugs by creating a new issue either in JIRA or GitHub. Please include as much information as possible about your environment and include any relevant logs.

FAQ

When I open the MongoDB Side Panel it shows empty

We are aware of a bug in Skiko, the rendering library used by Desktop Compose that doesn't fall back to software rendering when a GPU accelerated driver is not available. This should be fixed in version 0.1.0 so please update the plugin to the latest available version in the Marketplace.

If you are in the latest version, and it doesn't work for you, do the following:

  1. Open IntelliJ IDEA
  2. Go to the main menu and select Help | Edit Custom VM Options
  3. Add the following line to the end of the file: -Dskiko.renderApi=SOFTWARE
  4. Save the file and restart IntelliJ IDEA

The MongoDB Side Panel feels slow

It might be related to using the software renderer in Skiko. To confirm this situation:

  1. Open IntelliJ IDEA
  2. Go to the main menu and select Help | Show log in Files
  3. Open the idea.log
  4. Search the following string: Could not use GPU accelerated rendering
  5. If it's there, Skiko is using your CPU to render instead of the GPU.

In case the log line is not there, please share the entire log file in a bug report.

My query is not picked up by the plugin

The plugin doesn't support yet all the possible query variants. Notable unsupported features are:

  • Atlas Search and Atlas Vector Search queries
  • $lookup queries
  • $text queries

In case you think we should prioritise your query, or it's a bug, please fill a bug report with a sample query.

ICCheck finds inconsistent changes in your copy-pasted codes!

idea-plugin.name: CodeScene
idea-plugin.description:
CodeScene is the only code analysis tool with a proven business impact.

What is CodeScene for JetBrains?

It serves as a safeguard against introducing code changes that could negatively affect your business outcomes.

CodeScene promotes healthy, maintainable code by providing clear, actionable insights and guidance on how to improve your codebase.

By using CodeScene, developers can spend less time deciphering and refactoring code, and more time focusing on what truly matters: solving problems and delivering value.

The CodeScene CodeHealth™ metric

CodeScene’s CodeHealth™ metric is the software industry’s only code-level metric with proven business impact, measured through fact-based, winning research. It’s a metric that you can trust. The extension analyses and scores your code as you type, and adds diagnostic items that highlights any code smells. CodeScene supports most popular languages.

Safeguarding your code changes

Instant feedback is vital for maintaining high-quality code during development. By analyzing code as it’s written, developers may identify issues immediately. This interactive feedback loop encourages better coding habits, speeds up learning, and reduces the need for extensive rework later.

Continuous feedback fosters a sense of flow and confidence, as you instantly can see the impact of your changes on overall code health. In short, interactive monitoring turns code quality from a delayed review process into a continuous, integrated part of writing code, ensuring long-term maintainability and faster, safer development.

The Code Health Monitor flags for drops in code health in real time and offers instant recommendations to keep your code maintainable.

NOTE: The Code Health Monitor is currently available to all users for a limited time period. However, this capability will become accessible only to CodeScene customers in future.

Overview of Available Features

FeatureDescription
Code Health Monitor*The Code Health Monitor continuously tracks changes in your code, highlighting any improvements or degradations you introduce. Each file displays both its previous and current Code Health score, along with a clear delta value showing the overall change. You can easily see the impact of your modifications at the file or function level, including the status of any associated Code Smells—whether you’ve introduced new ones or resolved existing issues. With this level of visibility, there’s no longer any excuse for allowing Code Health to decline in your codebase.
Inline Code Smell detectionCode smells often lead to issues such as increased technical debt, more bugs, and reduced overall quality of the software. You can find detailed information for each code smell by either clicking the corresponding inline action notation in the editor, by examining the diagnostics (squigglies, Code Vision or in the Problems view).
Refactoring GuidanceOur mission is to educate and raise awareness about Code Health and its impact on your efficiency as a developer. The CodeScene extension equips you with rich insights into Code Smells and provides clear, actionable guidance on how to address issues that may exist in your codebase. We include relevant examples that illustrate the essence of Code Smells, along with common patterns and practical solutions to help you write cleaner, more maintainable code.
Problems ViewWhen a file is opened in the editor, it is instantly scanned for existing Code Health issues. All discovered issues are then listed as warnings in the IDE Problems View. This way you instantly get an overview of all opportunities a file has for improvements.
Custom Code Health rulesTo customize the code analysis you can either use local Code Comment Directives or create a code-health-rules.json file which applies to the entire project.

Configuration

You can add configuration files to the git repository to customize and control behavior in the Extension. They should be located in a .codescene folder, at the repository root. In addition, we also have a Settings page for personalized configuration of the extension.

code-health-rules.json

Location: .codescene/code-health-rules.json

You can find more documentation on its content here

config.json

Location: .codescene/config.json

Example configuration:

{
  "baseline_branch": "develop"
}
PropertyTypeDefaultDescription
baseline_branchStringorigin/HEAD (default branch)The name of the branch that the Code Health Monitor should compare against when running its delta analysis. If no origin/HEAD or config present, it will look for the nearest merge-base among common shared branches (main, master, develop etc)

Settings

Location: Code Health Monitor > Extension Settings

PropertyTypeDefaultDescription
Enable Review Code VisionBooleantrueEnables/Disables showing Code Health Score and Code Smells in the active documents
Auth TokenString-CodeScene PAT Token for authentication. Providing a token enables ACE features.
StatisticsBooleantrueEnable/Disable collecting anonymized telemetry for tracking usage and feature engagement.

Debug logging

CodeScene follows Jetbrains internal configuration for Log level. Check with your IDE and version on how to set it

Android Studio Support

To use the CodeScene plugin in Android Studio, you must enable JCEF (Java Chromium Embedded Framework). The plugin relies on JCEF, but it is not bundled with the default IDE runtime. Follow these steps to enable JCEF and view documentation: Markdown Editor and Preview Not Working in Android Studio.

Rider Support

The plugin is expected to work with Rider, but the level of support has not been fully assessed. Some features may function as intended, while others could have limitations. If you encounter any issues, please open a support ticket here.

* Available time-limited for non CodeScene customers.

idea-plugin.name: Spectral-Linter
idea-plugin.description:
This plugin is a wrapper for the tool Spectral, a linter for OpenApi schemas. It is a fork of https://github.com/SchwarzIT/spectral-intellij-plugin

Installation

  • Using IDE built-in plugin system:

    Settings/Preferences > Plugins > Marketplace > Search for "Spectral Linter" > Install Plugin

  • Manually:

    Install it manually using Settings/Preferences > Plugins > ⚙️ > Install plugin from disk...

This plugin it is required to have the spectral CLI installed on your system. For windows it is recommended to install the binary without going through Nodejs.

Warning Should you still want to use the spectral package via NodeJs on Windows then you must check "Use node package on Windows" in the plugin settings. This is necessary for the node packages to work and will have a performance cost.

If you don't have it installed yet make sure to follow this guide: Installing Spectral

Note: The CLI needs to be in your path and executable from the command line.

Features

Automatic linting

Automatic linting of your OpenApi specifications and highlighting in your editor

Configurable Ruleset

Specify your own ruleset in the plugins settings, under Preferences -> Tools -> Spectral -> Ruleset.

There you can specify a file on your local machine or just paste the URL of a ruleset available on the internet e.g.: Zalando Ruleset.

Examples:

  • Link to a hosted ruleset: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baloise-incubator/spectral-ruleset/main/zalando.yml
  • Local ruleset relative to Project base-path: .spectral.yaml
  • Fully-qualified path: /Users/user/.spectral.yaml

Configurable Included path patterns

Select the files that will be linted. By default, every file called "openapi.json", "openapi.yml" or "openapi.yaml" within the Project root will be matched for linting by the plugin when it's opened.

You can adjust this in the settings under Preferences -> Tools -> Spectral Linter -> Included path patterns. All paths are relative to the project's root directory unless absolute.

Examples:

  • openapi.json: Matches the file called "openapi.json" inside the root directory of the project
  • components/**/*.yaml: Matches all files inside the project subdirectory "components" that end with ".yaml"
  • /Users/user/code/**/openapi*.yaml: Matches all YAML files within the absolute path "/Users/mick/code" that start with "openapi" and end with ".yaml"

Note: Each file must also be recognised by the IDE as a JSON or YAML file - that is with a suitable File Type association. If it is detected as a plain text (or any other type) it will be ignored.

Possibility to use file level overrides

Spectral offers the possibility to add file based overrides as described here. These don't work by default. If you want to make use of them, then you need to check "Use file level overrides" in the plugin settings.

Warning If turned on, this has a important caveat; you need to save the file for the linting output to match your changes again.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changed

  • Fixed issue where malformed results were returned by the tool by @lupor in https://github.com/lupor/spectral-linter-intellij-plugin/pull/20

idea-plugin.name: Koin Dependency Injection (Official)
idea-plugin.description:
Official plugin for Koin DI!

The pragmatic Kotlin and Kotlin Multiplatform Dependency Injection framework now with native support for IntelliJ IDEA and Android Studio.

The primary goal of the plugin is to provide real-time configuration safety. It's in active development and we're looking for your feedback!
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Connect supported AI coding assistants to Kotzilla MCP from one IDE dialog, giving them Koin dependency graph and live production issue context while they help with your code.
  • Guided assistant setup supports shared sign-in with Node, Bun, or pnpm where available, native HTTP where supported, and exact manual steps when automatic setup is not available.
  • Disconnect plugin-managed assistant setups or get exact cleanup steps for assistants that require manual setup.
  • Choose exactly which AI assistants to connect with per-assistant checkboxes, instead of configuring every detected assistant at once.

Improved

  • The Connect dialog now shows which AI assistants are already connected, with a Disconnect option for each, so reopening it reflects your real setup instead of looking like a fresh start.
  • The "Connect AI agents" suggestion now reflects your real setup: it stays hidden while an assistant is connected and returns if you later disconnect them all.
  • Faster, steadier Koin indexing with near-instant updates after small edits and fewer full graph rebuilds.
  • More accurate Koin DSL and Koin Annotations understanding, including scoped definitions, dynamic parameters, fully qualified calls, receiver-style calls, typed constructor declarations, and @KoinWorker.
  • Better Android ViewModel navigation and Koin Configuration tree behavior, including searchable app selection, source autoscroll, mutable list bindings, and smoother multi-project switching.
  • More useful Kotzilla Insights for critical performance and crash issues, with better AI analysis prompts and more reliable background refresh.
  • More reliable SDK detection and signed-in sessions across IDE restarts and long inactivity.

Fixed

  • Compatibility with IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1 and upcoming IDE versions.
  • Restored compatibility with JetBrains Marketplace verification across all supported IDE versions, including IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2: the plugin no longer relies on internal IntelliJ Platform APIs.
  • Fewer error popups, freezes, and stale project states during indexing, editing, sign-out, and project switching.
  • More Koin declarations are recognised before indexing completes.
  • Koin Configuration tree now shows the real bound class for constructor and lambda definitions instead of an internal "unresolved name" placeholder when type resolution is momentarily unavailable, so entries no longer look identical or duplicated.
  • Koin Configuration tree no longer marks production modules as test code (green background) when the project folder path happens to contain "test"; test detection now follows the actual source set, so genuine test modules still show correctly.

Changed

  • Automatic SDK setup wizard is paused while SDK 2.x support is prepared.
  • The Manage Kotzilla MCP action now has a distinct icon so it stands out from other tool-window settings.

Functions

  • Koin dependency graph visualisation
  • Navigation between declarations and injection points
  • Koin configuration validation (Beta)
  • Kotzilla performance and crash issue insights
  • Kotzilla MCP context for AI coding assistants

idea-plugin.name: NestKit
idea-plugin.description:
NestKit - Essential Tools for NestJS Development

Boost your NestJS development with powerful code inspections, navigation tools, and a comprehensive project explorer.

Key Features

🔍 Smart Code Inspections (16 total)

  • Detect console.log statements and replace with proper Logger
  • Find circular module dependencies
  • Validate endpoint parameters and decorators
  • Warn when returning entities instead of DTOs
  • Detect hardcoded configuration values
  • Find missing exception handling
  • Identify N+1 query problems
  • And many more...

🧭 Project Explorer Tool Window

  • Module Explorer - Visualize module dependencies and structure
  • Route Explorer - Browse all HTTP endpoints with quick navigation
  • Service Explorer - Track service dependencies and injections
  • Entity Explorer - View TypeORM entities and their relationships
  • DTO Explorer - Find where DTOs are used across your app
  • Config Explorer - Browse configuration values

⚡ Code Generation & Navigation

  • Generate modules, controllers, services from the context menu and file templates
  • Create complete CRUD resources automatically
  • Gutter markers on controllers, endpoints, injectables, modules, services, tests and entities, each jumping to the piece it belongs to
  • Route Code Vision above controller handlers
  • Gutter markers for the NestJS Logger
  • A chooser when a symbol resolves to more than one place
  • Smart code completion for NestJS decorators

Works with the rest of the IDE

  • NestJS routes appear in the IDE's own Endpoints tool window, grouped by controller
  • TypeORM entities and their fields resolve to the actual database tables and columns
  • DTOs list the controller endpoints that consume them
  • GraphQL resolvers jump to the schema type they serve, with the schema files taken from the index and node_modules left out

🎯 Developer Experience

  • Custom file icons for NestJS components
  • Enhanced structure view
  • SQL completion in TypeORM queries
  • Configurable inspection severities

Perfect for: NestJS developers who want better code quality, easier navigation, and powerful development tools integrated directly into their IDE.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Users upgrade to this release straight from 1.1.0. Versions 1.2.0 and 1.3.0 were tagged but never reached the Marketplace: the upload reported success and delivered nothing. Everything those two releases contained is therefore listed here as well.

Added

  • Entity and DTO explorers in the NestJS tool window, as IntelliJ-native trees with module grouping, validator annotations and links between a DTO and the entity behind it
  • TypeORM entities linked to the database: entity classes and their fields resolve to the actual tables and columns, with DB column icons in the tree
  • Controller endpoints listed under the DTO that they consume
  • NestJS routes in the IDE's own Endpoints tool window, grouped by controller and sorted
  • GraphQL resolver to schema navigation: a resolver class or a @Query/@Mutation method carries a gutter icon to the type it serves. Schema files come from the index and node_modules is left out, so a monorepo resolver points at its own app's schema. Turn it off under Settings → Tools → NestJS Companion → Enable GraphQL Type Sync.
  • Route Code Vision above controller handlers
  • Gutter markers for the NestJS Logger
  • Multi-target navigation popup where a symbol resolves to more than one place
  • Codegen parity for guards, pipes, interceptors and filters

Changed

  • Index lookups are scoped per module, so a monorepo no longer resolves symbols across unrelated projects
  • The compatibility range now reaches 262.*, covering the 2026.2 IDEs
  • The Generator tab has been removed from the tool window. It duplicated the context-menu actions and file templates with an inferior implementation; both remain

Fixed

  • Custom parameter decorators such as @CurrentUser are recognised by the inspections instead of being reported as errors
  • An IDE deadlock in the endpoints provider
  • Duplicate route gutter icons on controller methods
  • Index access in the config explorer no longer runs before the project is smart
  • Two cross-version API breaks that made the plugin fail on newer IDEs
  • Inspection settings and suppressions apply to the inspection they name. Two identifiers for the same inspection had drifted apart, so severity changes and // @ts-ignore-style suppressions could silently target nothing
  • Toolbar actions in the explorer panels target the right component

Assista is a comprehensive plugin that enhances productivity by providing context-aware completions for views, fields, menus, and actions, making it easier to write and maintain Odoo code.

  • Context-Aware Smart Suggestions – Intelligent autocompletion for model names, fields, decorators, view elements, manifest paths, and OWL IDs

idea-plugin.name: CodeMetrics With Kotlin
idea-plugin.description:
Provides inlay indicators based on a customizable complexity calculation for Java and Kotlin files.

This plugin is based on the original CodeMetrics by Tamas Kisst (MIT License) and has been extended to support Kotlin with updated UI compatibility for modern IntelliJ versions.

The plugin calculates cyclomatic complexity by parsing the AST and walking through each node, displaying scores inline with customizable thresholds and color coding.

Features

  • Real-time cyclomatic complexity calculation for Java and Kotlin
  • Inline complexity hints in the editor with color-coded severity
  • AI-powered refactoring suggestions via Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, or Codex (ChatGPT OAuth)
  • Project-wide complexity analysis tool window with batch refactoring support
  • Refactoring diff viewer with side-by-side comparison and one-click apply
  • Customizable thresholds and colors with automatic validation
  • Click on hints to see detailed breakdowns
  • Full Kotlin K2 compiler mode support
  • Supports classes, methods, control flow statements, properties, and lambda expressions
  • Granular Kotlin visibility controls - toggle metrics for individual constructs (if, when, for, while, try, properties)
  • Specialized handling for Kotlin constructs (Elvis operator, when expressions, etc.)
  • Robust error handling with user-friendly validation messages

Installation

  • Using IDE built-in plugin system: Settings/Preferences > Plugins > Marketplace > Search for "CodeMetrics With Kotlin" > Install

Configuration

Settings/Preferences > Code Metrics With Kotlin to customize:

  • Complexity thresholds for different colors (low/normal/high/extreme)
  • Which elements to measure (methods, classes, lambda expressions, properties)
  • Granular Kotlin visibility controls (classes, functions, properties, lambdas, if/when/for/while/try)
  • Calculation weights for different constructs
  • Kotlin-specific settings (Elvis operator, when expressions)

Note: The plugin automatically validates configuration to prevent invalid threshold combinations.

AI Refactoring Settings

Settings/Preferences > Code Metrics With Kotlin > AI Refactoring tab:

  • Provider: Choose from Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, or Codex (ChatGPT OAuth login)
  • Credentials:
    • Claude, OpenAI, and Gemini use API keys stored securely via IntelliJ PasswordSafe.
    • Codex uses ChatGPT OAuth login; stored OAuth tokens are kept in IntelliJ PasswordSafe. If browser automation is unavailable, the OAuth flow prompts for the callback URL.
  • Model: Select model per provider (editable dropdown with current defaults)
    • Claude defaults to claude-opus-5-5; OpenAI defaults to gpt-6.1-sol; Gemini defaults to gemini-3.8-flash; Codex defaults to gpt-6.1-sol.
  • Custom Prompt: Add custom instructions appended to the auto-generated prompt
  • Provider parameters:
    • OpenAI / Codex reasoning effort: none / minimal / low / medium / high / xhigh / max (unsupported levels are omitted or normalized per selected model)
    • OpenAI text verbosity for GPT-5 / GPT-6 models: low / medium / high
    • Claude effort: default / low / medium / high / xhigh / max
    • Gemini thinking level for Gemini 3 models: default / minimal / low / medium / high (levels a model does not support, such as minimal on Gemini 3.1 Pro or Gemini 3.7+ Flash, are normalized)

Usage

  1. Inline Hints: Complexity scores appear as inlay hints next to methods and classes
  2. Tool Window: Access project-wide complexity analysis via View > Tool Windows > CodeMetrics
    • Sortable by complexity score
    • Click to navigate to code
    • Suggest Refactoring for single methods, Batch Refactoring for multiple
  3. AI Refactoring: Right-click on a complexity hint > Suggest AI Refactoring, or use the lightbulb (Alt+Enter) on complex methods
  4. Interactive: Click on any complexity hint to see detailed breakdown
  5. Configuration: Fine-tune visibility, thresholds, and AI provider settings

Supported Platforms

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2024.3+
  • Kotlin K1 and K2 compiler modes
  • Java and Kotlin languages

Test Samples

The complexity-test-samples/ directory is a standalone Gradle project with comprehensive test cases:

  • Java: Simple to extreme complexity (1-25+), lambda expressions, anonymous classes, nested conditions
  • Kotlin: when/if/for/while/try expressions, Elvis operator, properties, sealed classes

Open complexity-test-samples as a separate project in IntelliJ IDEA to test the plugin.

Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please see CONTRIBUTING.md for guidelines.

For Contributors

Prerequisites:

  • Java 17+ (required for building)
  • Java 21 recommended for Gradle JVM to avoid validation warnings with newer JDK versions

Quick start:

git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/codemetrics-idea.git
cd codemetrics-idea
./gradlew runIde

See CONTRIBUTING.md for full setup instructions and development tips.

License

Licensed under the MIT License.
idea-plugin.vendor: ehs208 (based on CodeMetrics by Tamas Kisst)
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changed

  • Update default AI models to the current lineups: Claude claude-opus-5-5, OpenAI gpt-6.1-sol, Gemini gemini-3.8-flash, and Codex gpt-6.1-sol.
  • Add Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1, and Opus 5; OpenAI GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Luna, GPT-5.6 Sol, and GPT-5.6 Terra; and Gemini 3.8 / 3.7 / 3.6 Flash and 3.5 Flash-Lite to the model dropdowns. Remove older models from the dropdowns (Claude 4.7 and earlier except Haiku 4.5, GPT-5.4 and earlier, Gemini 3 Flash Preview and 2.5, and pre-GPT-6 Codex models). The dropdowns stay editable, so a saved older model keeps working.
  • Add the max reasoning effort for GPT-6 and GPT-5.6 models (normalized to xhigh/high on older models).
  • Raise the default Max Output Tokens to 16000 and the Claude request timeout to 300 seconds, since current Claude models always think before answering.
  • Show the current Claude prices in the cost estimate (Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.x, Fable).

Fixed

  • Apply Claude effort to Claude 5-generation models (Opus 5.5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5.5, Sonnet 5, Fable); claude-sonnet-5 previously ignored the effort setting.
  • Stop sending minimal thinking to Gemini 3.1 Pro and Gemini 3.7+ Flash, which reject it; it is now sent as low.
  • Stop sending none reasoning effort to GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol, which return HTTP 400 for it.
  • Move Codex users off models retired from ChatGPT sign-in (gpt-5.5, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5.3-codex-spark) to gpt-6.1-sol.
  • Show a clear error when Claude declines a request or uses the whole output budget before answering.

idea-plugin.name: Odoo
idea-plugin.description:
Language server support for Odoo projects in PyCharm.

This PyCharm plugin integrates the OdooLS language server for Odoo projects.

It provides advanced language features, including:

  • Hover information

  • Go to definition

  • Autocompletion

  • Diagnostics

For installation instructions and configuration details, see the OdooLS repository, and its wiki.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Server

  • Use OXC and tsserver to provide features for JavaScript files, as well as OWL templates.
  • Provide semantic tokens for Python, XML and JS files.
  • Store all symbols in an arena, and stop using Rc<RefCell<>> to store references.
    • Add GDB scripts to help debug this new memory management
  • Switch the internal hasher from SipHash to FxHash for performance.
  • Set codegen-units to 1 in release builds to improve runtime performance, at the cost of slower compilation.
  • On Linux/macOS, switch the memory allocator to jemalloc.
  • Support for the new access operator in search domains for Odoo >= 19.4
  • Refactor the entire config parser to make adding new options easier in the future.
  • Report loading progress as a percentage instead of number of items during initial loading.
  • Lots of various optimizations.
  • Improve unpacking evaluations, resolving code like for a, b in [(1, 2), (2, 3)]. a and b will now properly be evaluated as int
  • Remove logs that were created on each string occurence of opened files.
  • Configuration files that now contains invalid key or syntax errors will be reported in VsCode.
  • Update gungraun to 0.19.4
  • Various code style enhancements
  • Handle special characters ' ', '"', '#', '%', '<', '>', '?', '[', ']', '^', '`', '{', '}', '|', '\\' in file URLs
  • Semantic tokens can now be disabled in configuration with disable_semantic_tokens_X = true, with X in [python, javascript, xml]
  • Fix and bring back OLS05001 in Xml fields references - Unknown XML ID
  • Small refactoring of BuildSteps and SymbolKey replacement to improve stability by removing possible invalid states
  • Windows builds now include line tables for better tracebacks in case of crash
  • Add a warning diagnostic for calls to attributes that are not in dependencies
  • GoTo features now select only the headers of classes and functions range. It allows us to bring back the default feature that call gotoreference instead of gotodefinition when clicking on the definition of the symbol
  • Add features for depends field keyword argument to work in the same way as that for api.depends decorator arguments.
  • Improve some feature preformances by not cloning the whole AST on requests, by introducing a lightweight enum ASTKind.
  • More robust and extensive tests for JavaScript features and core.
  • Correctly handle Javascript modules (correctly handle @odoo-module headers).
  • Properly support assets at .../static/tests and .../static/lib.
  • Implement completions for Javascript files.
  • Properly store JS Symbols under a module's static dir as assets, and as children of the ModuleSymbol they are under.
  • Improve and add new diagnostics for Javscript
  • Add a new ComponentManager to manage the javascript components in a safe localized way
  • Add features for newly added compute_sql field keyword argument to work like compute for odoo versions over 19.1
  • Add fearures for more Keyword/Positonal Arguments (group_expand, selection and init_storage (>= 20.0))

VsCode

  • Display configuration errors to draw user attention to invalid settings.
  • Add a popup that strongly suggests disabling the built-in JS plugin in VS Code for your workspace. It will avoid having 2 instances of tsserver running serving the same answers to your requests.
  • Notification that suggests disabling the built-in JavaScript plugin will now only be displayed if tsserver is configured and activated
  • Remove the editor.gotoLocation.alternativeDefinitionCommand setting that was blocking GoToReference from Ctrl-Clicking a class name for example
  • Only show Javascript messages if the server has typescript server running

Fixes

  • The server could sometimes get stuck in a state that consumed 100% CPU until the next request (typing, hover, etc.).
  • Remove duplicate references found on the same line in XML files.
  • Fix some missing references in the GoToReferences features (all references found in functions)
  • Fix crash that occur on files that does not contain valid UTF-8
  • Fix crash on invalid cycling evaluations.
  • Fix Goto location when going on a python package
  • Fix default config selection on non-odoo related workspace
  • Fix Javascript internal dependency if the file is not part of the project
  • Fix issues with compiled Python files.
  • Warning about missing tsserver now suggests typescript@6 instead of typescript
  • Fix diagnostic OLS05071 that was activating on t-name that contains a dot, which is valid
  • Fix various hooks in ORM that could stop working after edits
  • Fix cycle prevention in reference evaluation that was incorrectly preventing some valid results due to a different context.
  • Fix crash on JavaScript file validation that can happen if AST is not ready or has been dropped
  • Ensure that diagnostics are properly cleared when rebuilding an AST
  • Fix useless custom entrypoint creation on files that were not opened by the user but modified on disk
  • Fix internal file versioning for file info updates of opened files
  • Fix range of hook on IrRule to apply only to Odoo < 19.4
  • Fix panic on invalid syntax with missing type annotation in tuple assignment, like a, b: int
  • Fix panic when calling super with an invalid argument like None

Fixes not included in previous 1.5.2

  • Fix an issue where builtins or other Python library files were dropped from the index if one of those files were opened and then closed
  • Fix a bug where the workspace symbols were duplicated
  • Fix the lifecycle of deleted addons, such that they can be recreated easily to avoid having odoo modules disappear forever
  • Fix an issue where magic fields ("id", "display_name", ...) were added on every class in the model inheritence tree
  • Fix an issue where completion items on class/model number could be duplicated due to multiple defintions
  • Filter out magic fields on magic string features, for example trying to go to "id" field that just led to the class
  • Fix the check for AST is_built for Javascript
  • Fix the missing label details in completion for Javascript
  • Fixes multiple JS missing or incorrect suggestiins in completions
  • Fix the logical errors in the lifecycle of Javascript files, now CRUD is handled properly
  • Fix a completion issue where <lambda> was shown in the list of member symbols
  • Fix the look up of check_js_symbol_path_vacant to use path instead of name
  • Fix a crash that happens when you request references on a relational field that is references in CSV without /or:
  • Fix wrong semantic tokens on keys in the manifest
  • Filter out virtual file artifacts from completions
  • Fix shim paths being shown in import completion suggestions
