idea-plugin.name: bean-copy-helper
idea-plugin.description:
BeanCopy Assistant

Currently supports recognition and conversion of property copying for org.springframework.beans.BeanUtils, org.springframework.cglib.beans.BeanCopier, org.apache.commons.beanutils.BeanUtils, and cn.hutool.core.bean.BeanUtil.

1. Identify property copy and convert it to a reference to the corresponding Getter/Setter methods

Usage: Right-click on the Getter/Setter method. If there are corresponding property copies, the Find Property Copy Usages option will appear. Click this option.

2. Static check for property copying: Warn for inconsistent types of identical property names, copying with no matching properties, and incorrect usage

Usage: Simply open the file to automatically scan. When the cursor is placed on the property copy method, warning information will be displayed.

3. Preview and generate comments comparing source and target class properties

Usage: Place the cursor on the property copy method, invoke the intention action (⌥ + Enter for Mac; Alt + Enter for Win/Linux), select "BeanCopyHelper - Show properties compare" to preview. Press Enter to generate the preview comment.

4. Generate corresponding Getter/Setter code for property copying

Usage: Place the cursor on the property copy method, invoke the intention action (⌥ + Enter for Mac; Alt + Enter for Win/Linux), select "BeanCopyHelper - Generate method" to preview. Press Enter to generate the preview code.

5. Preview and generate comments for successfully copied properties between the source and target classes

Usage: Place the cursor on the property copy method, invoke the intention action (⌥ + Enter for Mac; Alt + Enter for Win/Linux), select "BeanCopyHelper - Show copy properties" to preview. Press Enter to generate the preview comment.

6. Configure font size

To adapt to different platforms and various versions of IDEA, the plugin provides a font size configuration option, with the default set to 100% (percentage). If you need to adjust the font size, just modify the percentage.
Configuration path: Settings -> Other Settings -> Bean Copy Helper Plugin

BeanCopy助手

当前已支持org.springframework.beans.BeanUtils、org.springframework.cglib.beans.BeanCopier、org.apache.commons.beanutils.BeanUtils、cn.hutool.core.bean.BeanUtil等属性复制的识别和转换

1.识别属性复制将其转为对应的Getter/Setter方法的引用

使用方式：右击Getter方法/Setter方法/Field(Lombok)后如果存在对应的属性复制会有 Find Property Copy Usages 选项，点击该选项

2.属性复制静态检查，对属性名相同类型不一致的复制、没有相同属性的复制和错误用法做告警

使用方式：打开文件即可自动扫描，将光标放置在属性复制方法上时即可显示告警信息

3.可以预览源类和目标类属性的对比并生成相应注释

使用方式：将光标放置在属性复制方法上，唤起意图动作 ( ⌥ + Enter for Mac; Alt + Enter for Win/Linux )，选择 "BeanCopyHelper - Show properties compare"即可预览，回车生成预览注释

4.生成属性复制对应的Getter/Setter代码

使用方式：将光标放置在属性复制方法上，唤起意图动作 ( ⌥ + Enter for Mac; Alt + Enter for Win/Linux )，选择 "BeanCopyHelper - Generate method"即可预览，回车生成预览代码

5.可以预览源类和目标类复制成功的属性并生成相应注释

使用方式：将光标放置在属性复制方法上，唤起意图动作 ( ⌥ + Enter for Mac; Alt + Enter for Win/Linux )，选择 "BeanCopyHelper - Show copy properties"即可预览，回车生成预览注释

6.配置字体大小

为了适配不同平台不同版本的IDEA，插件提供了配置项字体大小，该选项为百分比默认为100%，如果需要调整字体大小修改百分比即可。
配置路径: Settings -> Other Settings -> Bean Copy Helper Plugin

idea-plugin.name: Enhanced NASM Assembly Support
idea-plugin.description:
Enhanced IDE support for NASM x86_64 assembly language development.

idea-plugin.name: CODE Methodology
idea-plugin.description:
CODE – a code base management methodology based on adapting the PDCA cycle to industrial software development processes. The plugin integrates the four stages of the methodology directly into the IntelliJ IDEA / Android Studio workflow: the Prepare stage checks the correctness of the branch and the start of development; the Develop stage ensures compliance with code style rules; the Control stage analyzes test coverage and generates recommendations; the Apply stage evaluates the integration readiness of changes and helps generate Pull Requests.

The methodology forms a manageable quality control cycle, combining formal metrics, requirements for change structure, and intelligent recommendations based on a generative language model.

CODE method diagram:

   ┌────────────┐      ┌─────────────┐      ┌─────────────┐      ┌────────────┐
   │  PREPARE   │──→───│   DEVELOP   │──→───│   CONTROL   │──→───│   APPLY    │
   └─────┬──────┘      └──────┬──────┘      └──────┬──────┘      └─────┬──────┘
         └──────────────←─────┴──────────────←─────┴──────────────←────┘

A detailed description of the methodology is available in the article:
METHODOLOGY FOR MANAGING THE CODE BASE OF SOFTWARE SYSTEMS IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY

idea-plugin.name: Azure Templates Navigator
idea-plugin.description:
Azure Templates Navigator supercharges your Azure DevOps pipeline development in IntelliJ-based IDEs.

Working with Azure Pipelines templates across multiple repositories? This plugin gives you full IDE support for template references — hover documentation, go-to-declaration, autocompletion, and real-time validation.

Features

  • Hover Documentation — hover over any template reference to see its parameters, types, and default values
  • Go-to-Declaration — Ctrl+Click (or Cmd+Click) on a template path to jump directly to the template file
  • Parameter Autocompletion — get intelligent suggestions for template parameters as you type
  • Parameter Validation — real-time inspections flag missing required parameters and unknown parameter names
  • Variable Hover — hover over pipeline variables to see their values
  • Dependency Tree — visualize the full template dependency hierarchy in a dedicated tool window

Supported File Types

YAML files containing Azure Pipelines definitions (azure-pipelines.yml, templates, stages, jobs, etc.)
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.8.4

  • Fix: crash on IntelliJ 2025.3+ resolved — removed the "Open to side" link from the hover popup; it relied on the internal EditorWindow.split() API which was removed in build 253 and caused a NoSuchMethodError at runtime. The "⎆ Open" link remains fully functional.

1.8.3

  • Compatibility extended to all future IntelliJ versions — untilBuild is now explicitly set to null (no upper bound), making the plugin available in IntelliJ 2025.3 and all future versions

1.8.2

  • Compatibility extended to all future IntelliJ versions — removed the upper build-number cap (untilBuild) so the plugin is available in IntelliJ 2025.3 and beyond without requiring a re-release for each new IDE version

1.8.1

  • Fix: object parameter passed as YAML sequence no longer triggers false "unknown parameter" warnings — when an object parameter is passed as a list of mappings (e.g. checkoutProperties: followed by - reference: … / - reference: … alias: … items), keys inside those list items (such as alias) are no longer mistakenly collected as top-level parameters and reported as unknown

1.8.0

  • Fix: object-valued parameters no longer flagged as unknown — when a parameter of type object is passed as a multi-line YAML mapping (e.g. deployConfig: with nested replicas, strategy keys), the nested property lines are no longer mistakenly collected as top-level parameters and reported as "unknown parameter"
  • Fix: ${{ each parameter in parameters }}: pass-through no longer causes false "missing required parameter" errors — the call-site validator now detects the each-passthrough idiom and skips all missing/unknown/type-mismatch checks for that call site, since every declared parameter is implicitly forwarded

1.7.0

  • VS Code-inspired hover popup design — redesigned parameter popup with higher contrast, theme-aware colours (blue for types, orange/rust for defaults, red for required), and improved spacing that adapts to both light and dark IDE themes
  • Open / Open to side links — the hover popup header now shows clickable "⎆ Open" and "⊞ Open to side" links; "Open to side" splits the editor window vertically and opens the template file in the new right pane
  • Header separator — a thin separator line visually divides the template path + action links from the parameters list
  • HiDPI-aware borders — all padding now uses JBUI.Borders for correct scaling on high-DPI displays

1.6.0

  • Errors Only filter in Dependency Tree — new toolbar button hides all non-error nodes from the tree entirely; only files with ERROR-level diagnostics are shown, making it instant to spot every broken template at a glance
  • Deep error surfacing — when Errors Only is active, errors nested deep in the dependency chain are promoted to the nearest visible ancestor so no error is ever hidden
  • Hide Warnings renamed — the previous "Errors Only" toggle (which only suppressed amber colouring) is now correctly labelled "Hide Warnings" to distinguish it from the new structural filter
  • Empty group nodes suppressed — "Called by" and "Is calling" section headers are omitted when all their children are filtered out, keeping the tree clean

1.5.0

  • Searchable parameter popup — hovering over a template reference now opens a dedicated Swing popup (instead of a plain HTML tooltip) with a live search field; type to instantly filter parameters by name
  • Keyboard navigation in popup — use ↓/↑ arrow keys from the search field to move through the parameter list; press Enter (or double-click) to jump directly to the parameter declaration in the template file
  • Go-to-parameter-declaration — selecting a parameter in the hover popup and pressing Enter or double-clicking opens the template file at the exact line where that parameter is declared
  • Removed absolute file path from hover — the tooltip previously showed both the relative template path and the absolute file path; now only the relative path is shown
  • Proper HTML styling in popup — required parameters render in bold + configured colour, optional parameters in bold, types in code style, defaults and (required) badges all styled correctly

1.4.0

  • Fuzzy search in Dependency Tree — new search bar at the top of the Dependencies panel lets you find any indexed template by typing; results appear in a popup with filename (bold) and directory path (grey), navigable with Up/Down/Enter/Escape
  • Typo-tolerant matching — the underlying FuzzySearch engine combines subsequence scoring, word-boundary bonuses, camel-case bonuses, and Levenshtein-based segment fuzzy matching so queries like "templete" still find "template"
  • Debounced search input — search fires 150 ms after the last keystroke to avoid redundant work on fast typing
  • Configurable graph depth — the Graph tool window now shows −/+ depth controls in the toolbar; in file-scope mode you can expand or narrow how many upstream/downstream levels are rendered (1–10)
  • Multi-level BFS in file graph — GraphBuilder.buildFileGraph() now performs a proper breadth-first traversal for both downstream templates and upstream callers up to the configured depth, instead of always stopping at depth 1

1.3.0

  • Severity indicators in Dependency Tree — tree nodes are coloured red/amber and suffixed with ✖/⚠ based on their worst diagnostic severity, so issues are visible without opening the Diagnostics panel
  • File header severity badge — the header label in the Dependency Tree panel shows an error/warning icon and coloured filename for the currently active file
  • Hide Warnings toggle — new toolbar action suppresses amber warning highlights in the tree so only errors are shown in colour
  • Open in Diagnostics action — toolbar button jumps from the Dependency Tree panel directly to the matching file node in the Diagnostics tool window
  • Copy Path action — copies the workspace-relative path of the active file to the clipboard with a brief checkmark icon feedback
  • Diagnostics cache in index service — TemplateIndexService now maintains a per-file worst-severity cache (getFileSeverity()) rebuilt on every index update, eliminating redundant re-validation in the UI layer
  • Diagnostics panel: programmatic file selection — new selectFile() API scrolls and expands the matching file node in the Diagnostics tree

1.2.0

  • Unused Parameter diagnostic — new template-side inspection detects parameters declared in parameters: that are never referenced via ${{ parameters.name }} in the template body; reported as a Warning with a one-click "Remove unused parameter declaration" quick-fix
  • Diagnostics panel integration — the Diagnostics tool window now surfaces unused-parameter warnings project-wide alongside caller-side errors, so dead parameters are visible without opening each file
  • Precise highlight range — the unused-parameter squiggly now covers only the parameter name token, not the leading whitespace on the declaration line

1.1.0

  • Quick-fix actions — one-click fixes for missing required parameters, unknown parameters, and type mismatches directly in the editor
  • Performance improvements — background indexing prevents IDE freezes on large workspaces; VFS-based file reads replace blocking I/O
  • Full path toggle — switch between short and full file paths in the Dependency Tree and Graph tool windows
  • Graph enhancements — zoom controls, improved force-directed layout, and a legend for node types
  • Improved documentation styling — richer hover tooltips with better HTML formatting
  • Better template resolution — more robust go-to-declaration for cross-repo and relative template paths
  • Robustness fixes — regex constants extracted to companion objects, mutable data class fields eliminated, flexible indent detection in parameter parser

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • Template parameter hover documentation
  • Go-to-declaration for template references
  • Parameter autocompletion with type information
  • Real-time template parameter validation inspections
  • Gutter icons for template references
  • Dependency tree tool window
  • Interactive D3.js template graph visualization
  • Diagnostics tool window for project-wide template issues
  • Cross-repository template resolution
  • Configurable sibling repository paths

idea-plugin.name: SaltStack
idea-plugin.description:
SaltStack Support for JetBrains IDEs

Full-featured IDE support for SaltStack .sls formula files — the YAML + Jinja2 hybrid format used for Salt states, pillars, top files, reactors, and orchestration. Works in IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, and all other JetBrains IDEs based on the IntelliJ Platform.

Smart Completion

  • State function completion — suggests module.function entries (e.g. pkg.installed, file.managed, service.running) based on built-in Salt metadata. Filters by prefix as you type.
  • Argument completion — inside a state function block, suggests valid arguments for the specific function along with all global state arguments (onlyif, unless, order, listen, …). Already-used keys are deprioritized.
  • Requisite completion — suggests requisite keywords (require, watch, onchanges, onfail, …) including reverse forms (require_in, watch_in, …) and _any variants. Completes module names and state IDs inside requisite lists.
  • Smart Enter in argument lists — pressing Enter inside a - key: value argument block automatically continues with -  at the correct indentation, keeping completion and validation context intact.
  • Jinja2 import path completion — path completion for import_yaml / import_json / import_text tags and {% include %} / {% extends %} template paths.

Validation and Diagnostics

  • State ID checks — detects empty IDs, reserved prefixes, trailing whitespace, and naming convention violations.
  • Duplicate state IDs — highlights duplicate top-level state IDs within a single file. Jinja2-templated IDs ({{ id }}) are safely skipped.
  • Unknown state functions — warns when a module.function key does not match the built-in metadata. No false positives when metadata is unavailable.
  • Unknown arguments — warns on unrecognized arguments in a state function call. Global args and requisites are never flagged.
  • Requisite structure validation — checks requisite list shape, item format, and resolves referenced state IDs within the file.
  • Global args validation — validates onlyif, unless, creates, order, and other global state arguments.
  • Directive validation — validates include, extend, and exclude blocks for correct structure and resolvable targets.
  • Top file validation — checks matcher syntax (glob, grain, pillar, compound) and validates the environment field structure.
  • Reactor and Orchestrate validation — validates reactor event declarations and orchestration step structure (runner/state references and requisites).
  • Jinja2 import path inspection — warns on unresolved import_yaml / import_json / import_text paths.
  • Duplicate key false positives suppressed — the standard YAML Duplicated keys inspection is automatically silenced for keys separated by {% if %}/{% else %} blocks — a valid and common Salt pattern.

Navigation and References

  • Go to state declaration — Ctrl+Click on a requisite state ID jumps to its declaration in the current or included file.
  • Go to included file — Ctrl+Click on an include entry opens the target .sls file. Falls back to init.sls when resolving package-style paths (e.g. nginx.config → nginx/config/init.sls).
  • salt:// URL navigation — Ctrl+Click on salt:// paths resolves and opens the referenced file relative to the configured state roots.
  • Find Usages — supported for all reference types above.
  • Pillar target navigation — Ctrl+Click on targets in pillar top files resolves to the corresponding pillar data files.
  • Jinja2 import navigation — Ctrl+Click on import_yaml / import_json / import_text paths opens the imported file, with strict guards to avoid firing on keywords or aliases.
  • Jinja2 alias navigation — Ctrl+Click on an alias defined via import_yaml … as config or {% import … as X %} jumps to the import binding declaration. Find Usages and Rename refactoring are supported.

Quick Documentation (Ctrl+Q)

  • Hover or press Ctrl+Q on a state function to see its description, supported arguments, and types from Salt metadata.
  • Documentation is also available for individual function arguments, requisite keywords, and global state arguments.
  • Pillar, top, and Saltfile elements have documentation popups as well.
  • Jinja2 variables (grains, pillar, opts, …) and filters show Salt-specific documentation when the Jinja2 Enhanced plugin is active.

Syntax Highlighting

  • Full YAML highlighting inside state and pillar files.
  • Distinct colors for Jinja2 expressions ({{ }}), statements ({% %}), and comments ({# #}).
  • Customizable via Settings → Editor → Color Scheme → SaltStack.

Editor Helpers

  • Smart Jinja2 delimiter closing — typing {{, {%, or {# automatically inserts the matching closing delimiter. Already-present closing characters are reused rather than duplicated.
  • Multi-language commenter — Ctrl+/ inserts # comments in YAML regions and {# #} block comments inside Jinja2 regions, with correct uncomment detection across both languages.
  • Import snippet inlay hints — when using import_yaml / import_json, the plugin renders the imported data structure as inlay hints directly on the import statement.
  • Spellcheck suppression — spellcheck is automatically disabled inside Jinja2 expressions and statements to avoid false-positive typo warnings.

File Role Detection

  • Automatically classifies each .sls file as State, Pillar, Top, Reactor, or Orchestrate based on filename, directory structure, and configured roots.
  • Distinct file icons for each role — visible in the project tree and editor tabs.
  • Saltfile (Salt CLI config) is detected and highlighted separately.
  • Render mode (yaml, jinja|yaml, py) is detected from the shebang line and applied per file.

Project Configuration

  • Mark directories as State Root, Pillar Root, Master Root, or Module Dirs via right-click → Mark Directory As. This drives file role detection, path completion, and reference resolution.
  • Configure the target Salt version for metadata matching.
  • Configure a remote metadata URL and cache TTL for up-to-date module and function metadata (falls back to bundled resources when unavailable).
  • Per-domain feature flags — enable or disable IDE features for individual Salt domains (state, pillar, top, reactor, orchestrate) independently.
  • All settings are project-scoped — different projects can use different configurations.
  • A Reset Plugin Caches button is available in settings for troubleshooting.

Jinja2 Integration

When the Jinja2 Enhanced plugin is installed, the following additional features become available:

  • Full Jinja2 PSI inside Salt files — syntax checks, variable resolution, filter completion.
  • Salt-specific Jinja2 variable documentation (grains, pillar, opts, saltenv, …).
  • Salt-specific Jinja2 filter documentation (tojson, yaml_encode, …).
  • Template path completion for {% include %} and similar tags.
  • Alias binding resolution — variables bound via import_yaml … as X are tracked for type inference, completion, Find Usages, and Rename refactoring.
  • Type schema inference — the structure of imported YAML/JSON files is used to validate and complete attribute access on alias variables.

The plugin works standalone without Jinja2 Enhanced — Jinja2 features are simply not active.

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2024.1+, PyCharm 2024.1+, or any JetBrains IDE based on the IntelliJ Platform 2024.1+
  • Jinja2 Enhanced plugin — required for full template support
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.2.1

New Features

  • Top file support — full validation and code completion for top.sls files: environment structure validation, matcher key diagnostics, and SLS path resolution.
  • Matcher validation — 13 matcher types are now validated in top.sls: glob, pcre, grain, grain_pcre, pillar, pillar_exact, compound, ipcidr, list, nodegroup, range, data, and explicit match: <type> declarations.
  • Top file completion — code completion for environments, matcher types, and SLS entry paths (dot-notation) based on configured file and pillar roots.
  • Quick Documentation for top files — Ctrl+Q now provides context-sensitive documentation for environments and matcher keys in top.sls.
  • SLS path validation — dot-notation SLS paths are validated against the project file tree; Jinja expressions in paths are recognized and skipped.
  • Pillar root support — completions and validation in pillar top.sls files now resolve paths against configured pillar roots.
  • What's New notifications — in-IDE notifications about plugin updates with an embedded "What's New" tab.
  • File type conflict handling — improved detection and resolution of .sls file type conflicts with other plugins.
  • IntelliJ Platform 2026.2 support — compatible with build 262.*.

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed SLS completion for quoted YAML entries.
  • Fixed init.sls files being shown as raw paths instead of parent state names in completion results.
  • Top files (top.sls) are no longer suggested as SLS entries in completions.

2.0.1

New Features

  • Jinja2 alias navigation — Ctrl+Click on an alias defined via import_yaml … as config or {% import … as X %} now jumps to its import declaration. Find Usages and Rename refactoring are fully supported for alias bindings.
  • Documentation in YAML regions — Ctrl+Q quick documentation now works inside YAML regions of Salt files, not only in Salt-specific regions.
  • No interference with plain YAML files — Salt completions, navigation, and validation no longer activate in regular .yaml / .yml files that are not part of a Salt project.
  • IntelliJ Platform 2026.1 support — compatible with build 261.*.

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed a crash when opening .sls files that start with one or more blank lines.

idea-plugin.name: Git Commit Message MCP
idea-plugin.description:
Connect your IDE to a self-hosted git-commit-server to generate Git commit messages and structured Jira work-story text from selected VCS changes — without leaving the Commit dialog.

Current version: 1.4.16

Git commit message generation

  • Commit window assistant: embedded panel in the Commit tool window — pick changed files, choose prefix, click generate.
  • Prefix modes: Jira ticket #comment, #ignore_scan#, or plain (no prefix). Each mode remembers your last choice.
  • Shortcut: Ctrl+Alt+G (macOS ⌃⌥G) skips the prefix dialog and reuses the last prefix.
  • Draft polish: optional draft parameter for refinement (commit box content is not auto-sent as draft).
  • Preview & apply: review and edit the generated message before filling the commit field.
  • Custom prompt: optional server-side style hints (e.g. feat/fix wording) in Settings.
  • Limits: configurable diff / per-file size caps and request timeout.

Work story (Jira) generation

  • Generate structured story text from the same VCS selection via POST /generateJiraStory.
  • Output sections: feature name, description, implementation flow, acceptance criteria, algorithm, UI design, prototype.
  • Source modes: from change records (diff) or from full post-change file content.
  • Configurable default implementation steps and acceptance-criteria count (1–12).
  • Entry points: Commit message toolbar and Tools menu → 生成事务故事说明.

One-click Jira form fill (Chrome extension)

  • After generation, click 填充到 Jira — the plugin publishes parsed fields to a local bridge (127.0.0.1:7422).
  • Companion Chrome extension fills the Jira create dialog: Summary, Description (wiki editor), Acceptance criteria.
  • Also fills story points fields (功能点数 / 故事点数 / 故事点) from your “implementation steps” setting.
  • Defaults “user-operable UI” to No; description section numbers are renumbered consecutively.
  • Optional: auto-open Jira in browser and auto-click Create to open the issue form.

Configuration

Settings → Git Commit Message (MCP): server URL, model, timeouts, story defaults, Jira URL, bridge port, browser automation toggles.

Privacy

Only selected diffs / file content are sent to your configured server. API keys live on the server; the plugin does not store secrets.

中文说明

连接自建 git-commit-server，在 Commit 窗口内根据勾选变更生成提交说明与结构化事务故事，并配合 Chrome 扩展一键填入 Jira 建故事表单。

提交说明生成

  • Commit 助手面板：提交窗口内置，勾选变更 → 选前缀 → 生成。
  • 三种前缀：工单 #comment、#ignore_scan#、无前缀；各模式分别记住上次选择。
  • 快捷键 Ctrl+Alt+G（macOS ⌃⌥G）跳过前缀框，直接用上次前缀生成。
  • 草稿润色：仅显式传入草稿时润色；不会把提交框里上次生成结果自动当作草稿。
  • 预览确认：生成后可编辑，再写入提交说明框。
  • 设置页可配服务地址、model、超时、diff 长度上限、customPrompt 等。

事务故事说明生成

  • 按规范输出：一功能名称、二功能说明、三实现流程、四验收标准、五～七算法/界面/原型。
  • 素材来源：根据改动记录（代码 diff）或根据文件内容（变更后完整文件）。
  • 可配置实现流程大点数、验收标准条数（1～12）。
  • 入口：Commit 工具栏或 Tools → 生成事务故事说明。

Jira 一键填充（需安装 Chrome 扩展）

  • 生成后点 填充到 Jira，插件经本机桥接（默认端口 7422）下发字段。
  • 扩展自动填写：主题（功能名称）、描述（功能说明+流程+算法/界面/原型，序号连贯）、验收标准。
  • 同步填入功能点数 / 故事点数 / 故事点（与「实现流程大点」相同）；「是否包含用户可操作界面」默认选否。
  • 可开启：自动打开 Jira 页面、自动点击「创建」弹出表单。

隐私与安全

仅将所选变更发送至您配置的自建服务；密钥在服务端配置，插件不保存 API Key。

Setting Meaning

Organization Organization
Project Project
Module Module of the project where the interfaces will be imported

idea-plugin.name: WoW Lua Language Server
idea-plugin.description:
A language server for World of Warcraft addon development, powered by wowlua_ls. Built specifically for WoW Lua - not a general-purpose Lua LS with WoW bolted on.

Features

  • 9,000+ WoW API stubs built in - every function, frame type, enum, and global for retail, classic, and classic era
  • Event handler typing - SetScript("OnEvent", handler) types self, event, and per-event payload params
  • XML frame scanning - automatically scans .xml files for frame definitions, virtual templates, and mixin attributes
  • TOC file support - hover, completions, go-to-definition, and diagnostics for .toc files
  • Metatable inference - understands setmetatable + __index, chained metatables, operator metamethods
  • Correlated narrowing - check one return value, and the LS narrows the rest
  • Mixin and template support - CreateFrame returns intersection types automatically
  • Flavor filtering - warns on APIs unavailable in your target game version
  • 70 diagnostics for type safety, nil checking, annotation correctness, and WoW-specific checks
  • Diagnostic plugins - write custom Lua scripts to enforce project-specific conventions
  • Powerful generics, builder patterns, signature help with overload resolution
  • Code completion, go-to-definition, find references, rename, semantic tokens

Setup

The plugin bundles the wowlua_ls binary — no separate install needed. If no bundled binary ships for your platform, it falls back to a wowlua_ls on your PATH.

The plugin drives the language server through the LSP4IJ plugin, which the Marketplace installs automatically as a dependency.

idea-plugin.name: Copy All Problems
idea-plugin.description:
Adds an action to copy every diagnostic (errors, warnings, weak warnings, info) for the currently active file to the clipboard, one per line, formatted as:

sample/SampleWithProblems.kt:7:1 [WARNING] Unused import directive
sample/SampleWithProblems.kt:10:7 [WARNING] Class "SampleWithProblems" is never used
sample/SampleWithProblems.kt:13:17 [WARNING] Property "unusedField" is never used

Useful when you need to paste a file's full problem list into an external tool (chat, ticket, code review) and the standard Problems window copy doesn't include line numbers in your build.

Scope: copy problems from just the active file (default), all open editors, every VCS-changed file in your git working tree, or the active file's directory (recursive) — selectable under Settings → Tools → Copy All Problems.

Formats: copy as plain text, a Markdown table, or a JSON array of {path, line, col, severity, message} objects — selectable in the same settings panel.

AI prompt: the separate Copy All Problems as AI Prompt action (Ctrl+Shift+Alt+A / ⌘+Shift+Alt+A) copies the list in your chosen format prefixed with a customizable instruction header, ready to paste straight into an AI assistant.

Source-line context: optionally attach each problem's offending line of code, integrated into the active format (an indented line in plain text, a Code column in Markdown, a code field in JSON) — off by default, handy with the AI prompt.

Reformat before copying: optionally run the IDE "Reformat Code" action first, so whitespace/formatting warnings are fixed and dropped from the copied list (off by default).

How to use: right-click in the editor → Copy All Problems with Line Numbers, or press Ctrl+Shift+Alt+P (Windows/Linux) / ⌘+Shift+Alt+P (Mac).

Multi-file scopes emit a per-file grouped list with a # path header for each file.
  • Open editors and the active file read already-computed diagnostics; the VCS-changed and directory scopes run analysis on demand (with a cancelable progress bar) and report errors and warnings.
  • New Output format setting: copy the problems as plain text (the original path:line:col [SEVERITY] description lines, default), a Markdown table (pastes cleanly into a PR or issue), or a JSON array of {path, line, col, severity, message} objects (handy for piping into a script or an AI assistant).
  • New Copy All Problems as AI Prompt action (editor right-click / Tools menu / Ctrl+Shift+Alt+A): copies the problem list (in your chosen output format) prefixed with a customizable instruction header, ready to paste straight into an AI assistant.

idea-plugin.name: javafmt
idea-plugin.description:
An opinionated, zero-configuration Java formatter. Replaces IntelliJ's built-in formatter on projects that apply the dev.javafmt.gradle plugin, so Reformat Code and format-on-save route through javafmt automatically.

idea-plugin.name: phpstan-type-trace
idea-plugin.description:
See exactly why PHPStan thinks a variable has the type it does — without leaving the editor.

PHPStan tells you the final type at the call site:

Parameter #1 $amount of method format() expects float, float|null given.

It does not tell you which assignment, which param default, or which missed narrow put the null there. This plugin replays every event that shaped a variable up to a given line and renders the chain in a tool window.

What it does

Place the caret on a variable, run Trace Type at Caret from the editor right-click menu (or Find Action), and the tool window shows the full inference chain, one row per event:

$amount · App\PriceCalculator::format    src/PriceCalculator.php:25
  L16  param   float|null
  L20  narrow  Assert::notNull($amount)  →  float    via AssertTypeSpecifyingExtension
  L25  read    float
                                                     Final type: float

What gets captured

  • param — entry types from function / method / closure / arrow-fn signatures
  • assign / assign-op / assign-ref — every write, including $x ??= 'd' and reference assignments
  • array-write — $x[] = 'y';, $x['k'] = $v;
  • read — bare variables, property fetches ($this->foo), static fetches (Foo::$bar)
  • narrow — if (is_string($x)), $x instanceof Foo, $x ?? 'd', ternaries — anchored to the branch where the narrow holds, with the predicate shown as the reason

Third-party extension attribution

When the inferred type was shaped by a third-party PHPStan extension, the chain row shows via <ExtensionShortName>. Three categories are attributed today:

  • Dynamic return type extensions on assign / assign-op — e.g. larastan's NewModelQueryDynamicMethodReturnTypeExtension
  • Type-specifying extensions on narrow — e.g. AssertTypeSpecifyingExtension from phpstan-webmozart-assert
  • Properties class reflection extensions on read — e.g. larastan's Eloquent magic attributes

When a type surprises you, via tells you which extension to blame or thank — no grepping the vendor tree.

Editor niceties

  • Click any line number to jump to the source position
  • Select & copy any type, FQN, or narrowing predicate (drag-select, then Cmd/Ctrl+C)
  • When a line has multiple tracked variables, candidates render as clickable links
  • Clean error panels with one-click composer commands when the CLI is missing or outdated

Installation

The CLI must be installed in your project's vendor/ — a global install will not work because PHPStan extensions are project-scoped:

composer require --dev kayw-geek/phpstan-type-trace

Auto-registered via phpstan-extension-installer; otherwise include vendor/kayw-geek/phpstan-type-trace/extension.neon in your phpstan.neon.

Limitations

  • Loops report the post-fixpoint type, not per-iteration deltas
  • Cannot follow values across function boundaries
  • Same-named vars across sibling closures inside one function may collide

CLI source, live examples & JSON contract: github.com/kayw-geek/phpstan-type-trace

idea-plugin.name: alint
idea-plugin.description:
In-editor diagnostics, hover-to-explain, and quick-fixes for alint — the language-agnostic linter for repository structure, file existence, filename conventions, and content rules.

The plugin launches alint lsp (the alint language server) via LSP4IJ and lets the IDE render the results. Works across the JetBrains suite (IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, WebStorm, RustRover, CLion, Rider, Android Studio).

idea-plugin.name: IOSP Analyzer for Java
idea-plugin.description:
Highlights violations of the Integration Operation Segregation Principle (IOSP) in Java code.

A method should either integrate (only call other methods) or operate (only perform API calls and evaluate expressions) — never both. This plugin warns when a method mixes the two.

Configurable under Settings | Tools | IOSP Analyzer (minimum metric, ignored package prefixes, and excluding test methods). Severity can be changed under Settings | Editor | Inspections (search for "IOSP violation").

Source & issue tracker: gitlab.com/slieser/iosp-analyzer
idea-plugin.change-notes:
- Additional list of package prefixes to be ignored in test methods, configured separately from the production prefixes under *Tools | IOSP Analyzer*.
- Ignored prefixes now also match the called type, so an entry like `java.lang.System` ignores calls such as `System.gc()` even though `System` is a class and not part of the package. Applies to both production and test methods.

idea-plugin.name: IOSP Analyzer for Python
idea-plugin.description:
Highlights violations of the Integration Operation Segregation Principle (IOSP) in Python code.

A function should either integrate (only call other functions) or operate (only perform library/API calls and evaluate expressions) — never both. This plugin warns when a function mixes the two.

Configurable under Settings | Tools | IOSP Analyzer (minimum metric, ignored module prefixes, and excluding test functions). Severity can be changed under Settings | Editor | Inspections (search for "IOSP violation").

Source & issue tracker: gitlab.com/slieser/iosp-analyzer
idea-plugin.change-notes:
- Additional list of module prefixes to be ignored in test functions, configured separately from the production prefixes under *Tools | IOSP Analyzer*.
- Ignored prefixes now also match the resolved symbol's fully qualified name, so a prefix like `os.getcwd` or `requests.Session` ignores a specific function/class/method rather than only a whole module. Applies to both production and test functions.
- Replaced all usages of experimental Python `PyAst*` PSI API with stable equivalents, removing the JetBrains Marketplace experimental-API warnings. No change in behaviour.

idea-plugin.name: Orderly - JSON Normalizer
idea-plugin.description:
Orderly — JSON Canonical Normalizer & Formatter

Orderly is a JSON tool that recursively sorts and normalizes any JSON data into a fully deterministic, canonical form. Whether you need to compare two JSON responses, generate stable cache keys, or just make sense of deeply nested JSON, Orderly handles it instantly.

Simply paste any JSON into the left panel, click Normalize, and get a perfectly sorted, stable JSON output on the right — ready to copy, diff, or use in tests.

What it does

  • JSON object key sorting — all keys sorted by Unicode dictionary order (case-sensitive)
  • JSON array sorting — array elements sorted by their compact JSON serialization string
  • JSON value preservation — strings, numbers, booleans and null kept exactly as-is
  • JSON formatter — output is always pretty-printed with 2-space indentation
  • JSON validator — invalid JSON triggers a clear error notification

Key features

  • Side-by-side JSON editor: raw input on the left, normalized output on the right
  • Line numbers on both panels
  • Case-insensitive JSON search with match highlighting and Previous / Next navigation
  • Right-click context menu (Cut / Copy / Paste / Select All)
  • One-click copy of the full normalized JSON result
  • Memory guard: refuses to process JSON input that would exhaust available heap
  • Non-blocking: JSON normalization runs on a background thread — the IDE stays responsive
  • Zero third-party dependencies — pure Java 21, RFC 8259 compliant JSON parser

Use cases

  • JSON comparison & diffing — normalize both sides, then compare as plain strings
  • JSON API response testing — canonical output is stable across any environment
  • JSON cache key generation — use the normalized string as a reliable hash input
  • JSON data deduplication — detect structurally equivalent JSON objects
  • JSON schema consistency checks

Quick start

  1. Open the Orderly panel from the right sidebar (View → Tool Windows → Orderly)
  2. Paste your JSON into the left panel
  3. Click Normalize
  4. Click Copy Result to copy the output


Orderly — JSON 规范化 & 排序工具

Orderly 是一款 JSON 工具，可将任意 JSON 数据递归排序并转换为唯一确定的标准结构（Canonical JSON）。 无论嵌套层级多深、结构多复杂，都能一键完成规范化。

将 JSON 粘贴到左侧面板，点击 Normalize（规范化），右侧立即输出排序稳定、结构一致的 JSON，可直接复制、对比或用于测试。

核心功能

  • 对象 key 排序 — 所有 key 按 Unicode 字典序排序（区分大小写，A–Z 优先于 a–z）
  • 数组元素排序 — 每个元素先递归规范化，再按其紧凑 JSON 序列化字符串排序
  • 内容原样保留 — 字符串、数字、布尔值、null 完全不做任何修改
  • JSON 格式化 — 输出统一使用 2 空格缩进的美化格式
  • JSON 校验 — 输入非法 JSON 时会弹出清晰的错误通知

特色亮点

  • 左右双栏编辑器：左侧输入原始 JSON，右侧实时展示规范化结果
  • 两栏均显示行号
  • 大小写不敏感搜索，高亮所有匹配项，支持上一个 / 下一个导航
  • 右键菜单：剪切 / 复制选中 / 粘贴 / 全选 / 清空
  • 一键复制完整规范化结果
  • 内存保护：输入过大时自动拒绝并给出提示，不会导致 IDE 崩溃
  • 非阻塞处理：规范化在后台线程执行，IDE 始终保持响应
  • 零第三方依赖，纯 Java 21 实现，符合 RFC 8259 规范

适用场景

  • 接口返回数据对比 — 两份 JSON 规范化后直接做字符串比较
  • 自动化测试断言 — 规范化输出在任何环境下稳定一致
  • 缓存 key 生成 — 以规范化字符串作为可靠的哈希输入
  • 数据去重 — 识别结构上等价的 JSON 对象
  • JSON 一致性校验

快速上手

  1. 从右侧边栏打开 Orderly 面板（View → Tool Windows → Orderly）
  2. 在左侧面板粘贴 JSON
  3. 点击 Normalize（规范化）
  4. 点击 Copy Result（复制结果） 复制输出

idea-plugin.name: Codeup
idea-plugin.description:
Surfaces anti-patterns in your codebase using the Anthropic Claude API. Findings are persisted as YAML files under .codeup/ so they travel with the repo and go through PR review. The .codeup/ format is compatible with the Codeup VS Code extension — teams on mixed editors share a single findings directory.

What it detects

107 catalogued patterns spanning:

  • Single-file smells — god class, anemic domain model, long methods, primitive obsession, deep nesting, high cognitive complexity, error swallowing, function-name mismatches.
  • Inheritance & OO shape — non-exclusive subtypes, procedural shell classes (Manager/Handler/Processor), base classes that depend on subclasses, parallel inheritance hierarchies.
  • Cross-file structure — type leakage across boundaries, shotgun surgery, feature envy with neighbour context.
  • Module dependency — deterministic cyclic-dependency detection (Tarjan SCC), layer-boundary violations driven by an optional .codeup/intent.yaml.
  • Service-level — distributed monolith indicators, shared-database anti-patterns, reach-through reads, god service.
  • Data / persistence — N+1 queries, lost updates, cache-as-source-of-truth, EAV overuse, god tables.
  • Exception handling — overbroad catches, lossy translation, exceptions as validation, log-and-rethrow cargo cult.
  • Code security (10 patterns) — untrusted input in interpreting contexts, path traversal, unsafe deserialization, inconsistent validation across ingress paths, credentials scoped to identity rather than destination, and more.
  • Process / judgement — premature optimisation/abstraction, copy-paste programming, golden hammer, lava flow.

Setup

  1. Install the plugin from the marketplace (or install the ZIP via Settings → Plugins → ⚙ → Install Plugin from Disk…).
  2. Set an Anthropic API key via Tools → Codeup → Set Anthropic API Key. The key is stored in the IDE's secure credential store (macOS Keychain / Windows DPAPI / Linux libsecret) — never written to disk or committed to your repo.
  3. Open a project and run Tools → Codeup → Run Full Scan. The first run shows a cost estimate before making any API calls.

An Anthropic API key is required. Get one at console.anthropic.com. The default model is claude-sonnet-4-6, configurable via Settings → Tools → Codeup.

Daily flow

  1. Run a scan — Tools → Codeup → Run Full Scan (whole project) or Scan Current File. A cost estimate is shown before any full scan.
  2. Triage findings in the Codeup tool window (right panel):
    • Click a finding to open the file at the right line.
    • Confirm — becomes a positive exemplar in .codeup/knowledge/exemplars.yaml.
    • Dismiss… — prompts for a rationale saved to .codeup/knowledge/dismissals.yaml; future scans learn from it.
    • Mark Fixed once the change is made.
  3. Rescan — unchanged files come from cache (no API cost).

Commands (Tools → Codeup)

Run Full ScanScan every supported file. Shows cost estimate first.
Scan Current FileScan the active editor file only.
Scan Open TabsScan all currently open editor tabs.
Suggest Architectural IntentDraft a .codeup/intent.yaml from your project layout.
Set / Clear Anthropic API KeyManage the API key in the IDE credential store.
Check for UpdatesCheck GitHub Releases for a newer version (also auto-runs on startup).

Settings (Settings → Tools → Codeup)

ModelAnthropic model used for analysis (default: claude-sonnet-4-6).
Scan on saveRun an incremental scan on file save (default: off).
Findings directoryWhere findings YAML files live (default: .codeup/findings).
File size warn / critical (bytes)Thresholds for oversized-file findings (30 000 / 60 000).
Enable update checksPoll GitHub Releases for new versions on startup.

Data handling

Codeup sends source code to the Anthropic API. If you point Codeup at a client repository, source from that repository will leave your machine. Confirm this is acceptable under any NDA or data-handling agreement that applies.

What gets sent (over HTTPS to api.anthropic.com): the full text of each analysed file, up to 6 neighbour files (truncated to 8 000 chars each), dismissal rationales and exemplars from .codeup/knowledge/, and catalogue pattern hints.

What is never sent: files excluded by .gitignore or .codeupignore, files over 512 KB, unchanged files (cache hit), deterministic findings (cycles, layer violations), or your API key as content.

Anthropic's commercial API terms: inputs and outputs are not used to train models. Zero Data Retention agreements and AWS Bedrock / GCP Vertex deployments are available for stricter requirements.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.3

  • Suggest Architectural Intent — completely reworked: Claude now receives a structured project summary (top directories by file count + most-frequent cross-directory imports) and returns layer rules via a typed tool call instead of free-text YAML. Result is a clean, commented intent.yaml; falls back to heuristic default if the model call fails.
  • HTTP timeouts added to the Anthropic client (30 s connect/write, 120 s read) — prevents requests from hanging indefinitely on slow or dropped connections.
  • Fixed a .gitignore matching bug where plain-name patterns (e.g. .git) did not match directory paths that ended with a trailing slash.

1.0.2

  • Inline finding detail panel embedded in a split pane below the findings tree — details visible on selection without a separate view.
  • Status-aware action buttons: available actions update as a finding moves through Unconfirmed → Confirmed → Dismissed / Fixed, with a Reopen action on all terminal states.
  • History table in the detail panel showing every status transition with timestamp and note.
  • Priority and confidence now shown alongside severity in the detail view.
  • Direct Open Code link navigates to the exact file and line of a finding.
  • Explanation and remediation text rendered with paragraph breaks.

1.0.1

  • Initial Marketplace release.
  • 107 catalogued anti-patterns across single-file, OO shape, cross-file, module dependency, service-level, data/persistence, exception handling, security, and process categories.
  • Findings persisted as YAML under .codeup/ — compatible with the Codeup VS Code extension.
  • Triage workflow: Confirm, Dismiss (with rationale), Mark Fixed.
  • Incremental scanning with file-level cache (no API cost for unchanged files).
  • Cost estimate shown before any full-project scan.

idea-plugin.name: JSON Orderly: Sort, Diff, Compare and Formatter
idea-plugin.description:
JSON Orderly — an all-in-one IntelliJ IDEA plugin for sorting, comparing, formatting, and viewing JSON data. Deep sort JSON by keys, diff two JSON structures side by side, and pretty-print with syntax highlighting.

JSON Formatter and Beautifier

  • Pretty Print — Paste messy or minified JSON and get clean, indented, human-readable output
  • Deep Key Sorting — Recursively sorts all object keys at every nesting level, including objects inside arrays
  • Value Integrity — All original values (numbers, strings, booleans) are strictly preserved without any transformation
  • Lenient JSON Parser — Handles trailing commas, single-quoted strings, unquoted keys, and comments (// and /* */)

JSON Diff and Compare

  • Side-by-Side Comparison — Compare two JSON structures and identify all structural differences
  • Color-Coded Diff Table — Red for value changed, purple for only in JSON 1, teal for only in JSON 2
  • Three Diff Types — Value changed, removed (only in JSON 1), and added (only in JSON 2)

Navigation and Productivity

  • Click-to-Locate — Double-click any key or value in the diff table to jump directly to its position in the JSON text
  • Search and Highlight — Built-in case-insensitive search with match highlighting and keyboard navigation
  • Line Numbers — Line numbers displayed alongside JSON input areas
  • Copy Support — Right-click to copy cell values from the diff table or text selections
  • Memory Safety — Pre-checks available memory before processing large JSON inputs

How It Works

  1. Open the JSON Compare tool window from the right sidebar
  2. Paste or type JSON into both input areas
  3. Click Start Compare
  4. Both JSONs are deep-sorted by keys, pretty-printed, and compared
  5. Review differences in the color-coded diff table
  6. Double-click any key or value to locate it in the JSON text

Ideal For

  • Comparing API responses before and after code changes
  • Verifying JSON structure after refactoring or migration
  • Identifying missing or extra fields between environments
  • Sorting and formatting unordered JSON for readability
  • Debugging configuration file differences

This plugin is fully self-contained with a built-in JSON parser — no external libraries required.

Compatible with all IntelliJ Platform IDEs: IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, Rider, CLion, RubyMine, PhpStorm, Android Studio, and more.

JSON Orderly — 一款集排序、对比、格式化、查看于一体的 IntelliJ IDEA JSON 插件。支持按 key 深度排序、并排 diff 对比、美化输出。

JSON 格式化与美化

  • 美化输出 — 粘贴混乱或压缩的 JSON，获得整洁的缩进格式
  • 深度 Key 排序 — 递归排序所有层级的对象 key，包括数组内的对象
  • 值完整性 — 所有原始值（数字、字符串、布尔值）严格保留，不做任何变换
  • 宽松解析器 — 支持尾部逗号、单引号字符串、无引号 key 和注释（// 和 /* */）

JSON 对比与 Diff

  • 并排对比 — 对比两个 JSON 结构，发现所有差异
  • 色彩编码差异表 — 红色表示值变更，紫色表示仅在 JSON 1 中，青色表示仅在 JSON 2 中
  • 三种差异类型 — 值变更、已删除（仅在 JSON 1）、已新增（仅在 JSON 2）

导航与效率

  • 双击定位 — 双击差异表中的任意 key 或 value，直接跳转到 JSON 文本中的对应位置
  • 搜索高亮 — 内置不区分大小写的搜索，支持匹配高亮和键盘导航
  • 行号显示 — JSON 输入区域旁显示行号
  • 复制支持 — 右键复制差异表中的单元格值或文本选区
  • 内存安全 — 处理大型 JSON 前预检可用内存

使用方法

  1. 从右侧边栏打开 JSON Compare 工具窗口
  2. 将 JSON 粘贴到两个输入框中
  3. 点击 Start Compare
  4. 两个 JSON 会被深度排序、美化输出并进行对比
  5. 在色彩编码的差异表中查看差异
  6. 双击任意 key 或 value 跳转到 JSON 文本中的对应位置

适用场景

  • 对比代码修改前后的 API 响应
  • 重构或迁移后验证 JSON 结构
  • 识别不同环境间缺失或多余的字段
  • 对无序 JSON 进行排序和格式化以提升可读性
  • 调试配置文件差异

本插件完全自包含，内置 JSON 解析器，无需任何外部库。

兼容所有 IntelliJ 平台 IDE：IntelliJ IDEA、PyCharm、WebStorm、GoLand、Rider、CLion、RubyMine、PhpStorm、Android Studio 等。
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Line numbers in input areas now correctly align with wrapped lines using precise character-position lookup instead of fixed line-height estimation

Fixed

  • Fixed line number misalignment when text wraps due to narrow input area width
  • Fixed stale diff highlights appearing when a new comparison is started before the previous one finishes rendering

idea-plugin.name: TOML EnvVar
idea-plugin.description:
TOML Environment Variable Inspection Suppressor is a lightweight utility designed for developers using extended TOML configurations that support environment variable interpolation (such as the env_toml crate or similar tooling). 
db_url = ${DB_URL} # Required: Fails if not set
db_port = ${DB_PORT:8080} # Optional: Defaults to 8080
default_port = ${MISSING_PORT:8080}  # Optional: Defaults to 8080
empty_default = ${ENV_VALUE:} # Optional: Defaults to `None` for optional fields, or an empty string for other types

By default, the standard JetBrains TOML plugin flags environment variable placeholder syntax like ${MY_VAR} as a syntax error because it falls outside the TOML specification. This plugin automatically suppresses those specific false-positive inspection warnings so you can work with env-var-interpolated TOML files without noisy red squiggles.

Features:

  • Zero configuration required — install and it just works
  • No impact on legitimate TOML syntax errors

idea-plugin.name: DartDoc-er - Dart Doc Generator
idea-plugin.description:
DartDoc-er is a smart, lightweight DartDoc generator for Dart in IntelliJ IDEA and Android Studio.

It produces natural, readable documentation from your code -- not boilerplate. A template-driven NLP engine builds descriptions from declaration names, understands async/Future/Stream patterns, and recognises Flutter frameworks like StatelessWidget, StatefulWidget, ChangeNotifier, and @freezed.

Non-destructive by default -- regenerating never overwrites your hand-written documentation. The merge engine preserves your summaries and inline references while filling in missing parameter and return documentation.

Customise everything per project via a .dartdocer.yaml style sheet, or use the settings panel.

Features

Smart DartDoc Generation

DartDoc uses /// triple-slash comments -- not /** */ block comments. DartDoc-er generates idiomatic Dart documentation following the official Effective Dart: Documentation guidelines.

  • NLP-aware descriptions -- verb maps, word splitting, and pluralisation produce natural sentences (getUserById -> "Returns the user by id.") instead of generic placeholders.
  • No @param/@return tags -- Dart documents parameters using [paramName] inline bracket references in prose, not tag-based annotations. DartDoc-er follows this convention.
  • Prose return descriptions -- returns are documented naturally: "Returns the..." rather than a separate @return tag.
  • Prose throws descriptions -- exceptions are documented as "Throws [ExceptionType] if..." following Dart conventions.
  • Async/Future/Stream awareness -- async functions, Future<T> and Stream<T> return types are documented automatically with appropriate context.
  • Flutter framework detection -- recognises StatelessWidget, StatefulWidget, State<T>, ChangeNotifier, ValueNotifier, InheritedWidget, @freezed, @immutable, mixins, and extensions, and adds tailored notes.
  • Throws detection -- scans function bodies for throw expressions and emits "Throws [ExceptionType]" documentation.
  • @since version stamp -- optionally appends a version tag to every generated doc comment.
  • Cross-references -- links override methods to their super declaration using [SuperClass.method] bracket syntax.
  • Usage examples -- optionally appends a fenced code sample to function docs.

Dart-Idiomatic Output

DartDoc-er generates documentation that follows Dart conventions:

/// Returns the user by id.
///
/// The [id] parameter identifies the user to retrieve.
///
/// Returns the matching [User], or `null` if not found.
///
/// Throws [NotFoundException] if the user does not exist.
Future<User?> getUserById(String id) async { ... }

Compare with KDoc (Kotlin) style -- DartDoc-er uses the correct format for each language:

AspectKDoc (Kotlin)DartDoc (Dart)
Comment style/** ... *//// triple-slash
Parameters@param name description[name] inline in prose
Returns@return description"Returns the..." in prose
Throws@throws Type description"Throws [Type] if..." in prose
References[ClassName][ClassName]

Non-Destructive Merge

Three policies for handling existing doc comments:

PolicyBehaviour
Merge (default)Keeps your summary and prose, adds only missing parameter references and return documentation
KeepLeaves existing doc comments completely untouched
ReplaceRegenerates the entire comment from scratch

Multiple Ways to Generate

ActionWhereWhat it does
Type /// + EnterEditorGenerates DartDoc for the element at the cursor
Create DartDoc for ElementGenerate menu (Alt+Insert) / Code menuSingle-element generation
Create DartDocs for All ElementsGenerate menu / Code menuDocuments every qualifying element in the file
Create DartDocs in FolderRight-click folder in Project viewBatch-generates across all .dart files with progress bar
Remove DartDoc for ElementCode menuRemoves the doc comment from the element at the cursor
Remove DartDocs for All ElementsCode menu / right-clickRemoves every doc comment in the file

Missing DartDoc Inspection

An inspection (enabled by default) suggests adding documentation to undocumented declarations. Use Alt+Enter to generate the missing DartDoc via the quick-fix.

Configure or disable it in Settings > Editor > Inspections > DartDoc-er > Missing DartDoc comment.

Project-Level Configuration

Create a .dartdocer.yaml at the project root to override settings per project. Generate a starter file with every option commented out:

Tools > Create .dartdocer.yaml Config

style:
  appendName: true            # prepend a generated description sentence
  splitNames: true            # split camelCase/snake_case into readable phrases
  frameworkAware: true        # detect Flutter widgets / ChangeNotifier / freezed
  usageExample: false         # append a fenced sample call to function docs
  existingDoc: merge          # merge | keep | replace
  throwsDetection: false      # scan function bodies for throw and emit Throws docs
  sinceTag: false             # stamp docs with a version string
  sinceVersion: "1.0.0"       # version string for the since stamp
  seeReferences: false        # add cross-references for overrides
  verbMapping:                # extend/override the verb -> phrase map
    fetch: "Fetches the {noun} from the remote source"
    sync: "Synchronises the {noun}"

aspects:
  notes:                      # override framework note wording
    stateless-widget: "A stateless Flutter widget for {name}."
    stateful-widget: "A stateful Flutter widget for {name}."
    change-notifier: "Notifies listeners when {name} state changes."

templates:
  function:
    description: "{description}"
    param: "[{name}]"
    return: "Returns {description}"
  class:
    description: "{description}"
  property:
    description: "{description}"

Settings

All options are available under Settings > Tools > DartDoc-er (independent from KDoc-er):

  • Generate DartDoc For -- classes, functions, properties, extensions, mixins
  • Visibility -- public, private (underscore-prefixed), overridden members
  • Description -- prepend element name, split camelCase names
  • Framework Awareness -- detect and annotate Flutter/Dart patterns
  • Throws Detection -- scan for throw expressions
  • @since Tag -- stamp with a version string
  • Cross-References -- link overrides
  • Usage Example -- append sample call to function docs
  • Existing Doc -- Merge / Keep / Replace policy
  • Templates -- override description and documentation templates with {placeholder} tokens

Customization Guide

Every part of the generated DartDoc can be customized. Configuration is resolved in order: .dartdocer.yaml > IDE settings > built-in defaults.

How the NLP Description Engine Works

DartDoc-er uses the same NLP engine as KDoc-er. It splits an identifier into words, matches the leading word against a verb map, and fills in the remaining words as the noun:

fetchUserProfile
  -> split
[fetch, user, profile]
  -> verb map lookup: "fetch" -> "Returns the {noun}"
  -> noun = remaining words joined: "user profile"
Returns the user profile

For classes and properties (no verb prefix), the name itself becomes the description:

UserRepository -> "User repository"
sessionToken   -> "Session token"

Pluralisation is automatic for collection return types -- if a function returns List<User>, the noun user becomes users:

List<User> getUsers() => ...;
/// Returns the users.

Built-in Verb Map Reference

Every function name prefix below is recognised out of the box. The {noun} placeholder is replaced with the remaining words of the function name.

Verb prefix(es)Generated phrase
get, fetch, load, retrieve, find, read, obtain, of, fromReturns the {noun}
set, update, save, store, write, put, assignSets the {noun}
is, has, can, should, are, was, will, mustReturns true if {noun}
check, contains, equals, matches, supports, allowsReturns true if {noun}
create, build, make, new, generate, produce, constructCreates a new {noun}
delete, remove, clear, drop, destroy, discard, eraseRemoves the {noun}
add, append, insert, push, register, attachAdds the {noun}
init, initialize, initialise, setup, configure, prepareInitialises the {noun}
convert, parse, map, transform, serialize, deserialize, to, asConverts the {noun}
validate, verify, ensure, assert, requireValidates the {noun}
calculate, compute, count, sum, measureCalculates the {noun}
handle, process, execute, run, perform, apply, invoke, callHandles the {noun}
send, emit, publish, dispatch, post, submit, notifySends the {noun}
receive, collect, consume, observe, subscribe, listenReceives the {noun}
start, begin, launch, open, connectStarts the {noun}
stop, end, close, cancel, finish, disconnect, shutdownStops the {noun}
toggle, switchToggles the {noun}
reset, refresh, reload, syncResets the {noun}
show, display, render, draw, printDisplays the {noun}
hide, dismissHides the {noun}
filter, select, query, searchFilters the {noun}
sort, order, arrangeSorts the {noun}
copy, clone, duplicateCopies the {noun}
merge, combine, join, concatMerges the {noun}
enableEnables the {noun}
disableDisables the {noun}

Custom Verb Mappings

You can override any built-in verb or add new ones for verbs specific to your project:

# .dartdocer.yaml
style:
  verbMapping:
    fetch: "Fetches the {noun} from the remote source"
    navigate: "Navigates to the {noun} screen"
    inject: "Injects the {noun} dependency"
    dispose: "Disposes the {noun} and releases resources"

Flutter Framework Notes

When framework awareness is enabled (the default), DartDoc-er detects Flutter patterns and appends contextual notes:

/// User profile screen.
/// Stateless widget -- renders UI based on its configuration without mutable state.
class UserProfileScreen extends StatelessWidget { ... }

Available aspect IDs and their default notes

IDMatchesDefault note
stateless-widgetStatelessWidget subclassesStateless widget -- renders UI based on its configuration without mutable state.
stateful-widgetStatefulWidget subclassesStateful widget -- maintains mutable state via its companion State object.
stateState<T> subclassesState object -- holds the mutable state for its associated StatefulWidget.
change-notifierChangeNotifier / ValueNotifier subclassesChange notifier -- call notifyListeners() to update observers.
inherited-widgetInheritedWidget subclassesInherited widget -- provides data down the widget tree via of(context).
freezedClasses annotated with @freezed / @unfreezedFreezed union/data class -- immutable with generated copyWith, ==, and pattern matching.
immutableClasses annotated with @immutableImmutable class -- all fields must be final.
mixinmixin declarationsMixin -- provides reusable members to classes via with.
extensionextension declarationsExtension -- adds methods to an existing type without modifying it.

Controlling Framework Notes

# .dartdocer.yaml
aspects:
  notes:
    stateless-widget: "Flutter UI component for {name}."
    freezed: ""    # suppress freezed notes

Throws Detection

When enabled, DartDoc-er scans function bodies for throw expressions and documents them:

# .dartdocer.yaml
style:
  throwsDetection: true

/// Requires the active user.
///
/// The [userId] identifies the user.
///
/// Returns the active [User].
///
/// Throws [NotFoundException] if the user does not exist.
/// Throws [StateError] if the user is not active.
User requireActive(String userId) { ... }

Template Overrides

Override the structure of generated documentation using {placeholder} tokens:

templates:
  function:
    description: "{description}"
    param: "[{name}]"
    return: "Returns {description}"
  class:
    description: "{description}"
  property:
    description: "{description}"

Full Configuration Example

# .dartdocer.yaml
style:
  appendName: true
  splitNames: true
  frameworkAware: true
  usageExample: false
  existingDoc: merge           # merge | keep | replace
  throwsDetection: true
  sinceTag: true
  sinceVersion: "2.0.0"
  seeReferences: true
  verbMapping:
    sync: "Synchronises the {noun} with the backend"
    navigate: "Navigates to the {noun} route"
    dispose: "Disposes the {noun} and releases resources"

aspects:
  notes:
    stateful-widget: "Manages mutable state for {name}."
    freezed: ""                # suppress freezed notes
    change-notifier: "Reactive state holder for {name}."

templates:
  function:
    description: "{description}"
    param: "[{name}]"
    return: "Returns {description}"
  class:
    description: "{description}"
  property:
    description: "{description}"
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • @throws detection — scans function bodies for throw expressions and emits @throws tags with the exception type. Enabled by default.
  • @since version stamp — appends @since <version> to every generated KDoc. Configure the version string per project via settings or sinceVersion in .kdocer.yaml. Disabled by default.
  • @see cross-references — links override methods to their super declaration (@see SuperClass.method), sealed subtypes to the parent sealed type, and object singletons to their implemented interface/superclass. Disabled by default; enable via settings or seeReferences: true in .kdocer.yaml.
  • Two inspection levels — "Missing KDoc comment (suggestion)" (enabled by default, Alt+Enter only) and "Missing KDoc comment (warning)" (disabled by default, subtle underline). Both offer a quick-fix to generate the KDoc.
  • Non-destructive merge — existing KDocs are preserved by default. New three-way policy: Merge (keeps your text, adds missing tags), Keep (leave untouched), or Replace (regenerate). Default is Merge.
  • Inferred return types — expression-body functions (fun f() = …) now resolve the return type via the K2 Analysis API and emit a meaningful @return tag.
  • Smart @return descriptions — return tags now carry type-derived text (e.g. @return the user, @return the users, @return \true` if the condition holds`) instead of being empty.
  • @constructor toggle — new setting to include or omit the @constructor line for classes.
  • Usage example generation — optional fenced code sample appended to function KDocs (e.g. val user = getUser(id)), configurable on/off.
  • Folder / project batch generation — right-click a folder in the Project view to generate KDocs for every Kotlin file underneath, with background progress and cancel support.
  • Generate .kdocer.yaml action — Tools menu and Project-view action to scaffold a fully-commented config file at the project root.
  • Missing KDoc inspection — optional LocalInspectionTool (disabled by default, WEAK WARNING) with Alt+Enter quick-fix to generate KDoc.
  • Unified settings page — single scrollable Kotlin UI DSL page under Settings > Tools > KDoc-er with grouped sections: element types, visibility, description, framework awareness, usage example, existing KDoc policy, templates, notifications, and support links.

Changed

  • Bumped target platform to IntelliJ 2025.1 (since-build 241, open-ended).
  • All actions now use ActionUpdateThread.BGT — eliminates OLD_EDT SEVERE exceptions on 2024.1+.
  • Modernised notification API to use NotificationGroupManager with registered <notificationGroup>.
  • Notification throttling changed from time-based to count-based (shows after every 20 generations, then resets).
  • Redundant @param descriptions eliminated — @param key the key now collapses to @param key.
  • Empty @return tags are no longer emitted; only generated when there is meaningful content.
  • Consolidated two settings pages (Configuration + Templates & AI) into one clean page.
  • Remove actions (single + all) fully rewritten and working correctly.
  • Generate actions no longer gate on SMART_INDENT_ON_ENTER.
  • Removed com.intellij.modules.java dependency — plugin now works on any JetBrains IDE with the Kotlin plugin, not just Java-capable IDEs.

Removed

  • AI/MCP backend layer — stripped entirely; the plugin focuses on the rule-based NLP engine.
  • Old Java Swing settings panel (.form + .java).
  • ServiceManager usage (replaced with ApplicationManager.getApplication().getService()).

idea-plugin.name: GoPrism
idea-plugin.description:
GoPrism helps Go developers inspect struct memory layout directly in GoLand. It shows size, alignment, field offsets, and padding for Go structs, then offers an optimization action when fields can be reordered to reduce wasted space. Current features:
  • Struct size and alignment indicators above declarations
  • Inline field offset and padding visualization
  • Offset table, memory range, heatmap, and raw struct views
  • One-click field reordering to optimize struct padding
  • Struct locking for types that should not be automatically reordered
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Initial public release.
  • Added Go struct size, alignment, offset, and padding insights.
  • Added layout views for offsets, memory ranges, heatmap, and raw structs.
  • Added one-click struct field reordering to reduce padding.

idea-plugin.name: Advanced Magento Support
idea-plugin.description:
Magento 2 fights your IDE. di.xml is untyped strings. ACL resources, config paths, translations and layout blocks are referenced by name across dozens of files. Every new module, plugin or observer is boilerplate. Out of the box, PhpStorm treats most of it as plain text — so you grep, guess, and find out at runtime when bin/magento blows up.

Advanced Magento Support teaches your IDE to actually understand Magento 2. Navigate, validate, refactor and scaffold across XML and PHP — catch mistakes before they ship, and build extensions faster.

See and navigate Dependency Injection

  • Visual DI graph tool window for di.xml — types, preferences, virtual types and plugins, with caret sync and one-click graph-to-source navigation
  • Plugin interception diagrams: nested around-layers by sortOrder, before/after at their chain depth
  • Code Vision on <plugin> declarations links straight to the before/around/after interceptor methods
  • Bidirectional PHP ↔ di.xml navigation, argument & declaration completion, extract-to-virtual-type, safe rename and find usages
  • DI validation: constructor signature checks, virtual-type cycles, duplicate preferences and invalid class references

Navigate everything, not just PHP

  • Jump between XML and PHP for plugins, observers, routes, DI preferences, templates, ACL resources, config paths, translations, layout blocks, the admin menu, email templates, indexers, message-queue topics, db_schema tables, GraphQL resolvers, MFTF sections, Web API and widgets
  • Gutter icons, Go to Definition and Find Usages wherever Magento uses a string identifier
  • Quick Documentation on block names, block classes and templates
  • $block in templates is typed as the block that renders the template, so its methods navigate
  • Several Magento installations in one workspace: translation phrases resolve inside the installation the file belongs to (setting, on by default)

Catch errors before runtime

  • Inspections for unresolved references, missing classes and files, wrong interfaces, duplicate declarations, dependency cycles and argument type mismatches — with quick-fixes to create the missing file, class or service method
  • Unused code you can trust: PHP that Magento calls from configuration, layout, GraphQL schemas, templates, plugin interceptors and the Web API serializer counts as used
  • Safe cross-file rename for layout blocks, ACL resource ids and DI virtual types

Generate the boilerplate

  • New → Magento: module, controller, plugin (interceptor), observer, queue consumer, CRUD entity, CLI command, email template, admin menu item, block/view model, EAV attribute, data & schema patches, customer section
  • Test scaffolding: unit, integration and MFTF (test, section, action group, test suite)

Testing & frontend

  • Code Vision navigation between production code and PHPUnit tests, plus one-click test creation
  • MFTF section / action-group navigation, completion and inspections
  • Frontend: layout XML, RequireJS, Less, translations, UI components, themes and widgets

Built for developers and teams shipping production Magento 2 extensions who want their IDE to pull its weight: less grepping, fewer runtime surprises, more shipping.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Editing a PHP file no longer re-reads every routes.xml. Route groups and the route-problem list stay until routes.xml changes or indexing finishes. The URL-to-controller map and the controllers under a route still refresh when a PHP file changes, without parsing routes.xml again. A layout edit drops neither.
  • The Web API reachable-type set stays until webapi.xml changes or indexing finishes. Highlighting a getter no longer rebuilds it. A getter signature can stay stale until then.
  • Go to Declaration during indexing no longer queries FileBasedIndex or PhpIndex. Layout names, ACL resources, menu ids and the other soft references stay soft. A missing class or method in webapi.xml, crontab.xml, a queue handler, a GraphQL resolver, a customer-section source, a UI component object or a di.xml object argument is underlined once indexing has finished.

idea-plugin.name: go-doc
idea-plugin.description:
go-doc adds typed Go template support to GoLand for .gohtml, .tmpl, and .html files.

It runs the shared go-doc language server and provides:

  • contract-aware completions and diagnostics
  • hover, go-to-definition, and document symbols
  • semantic highlighting for roots, fields, methods, functions, generated namespaces, and included templates
  • static FuncMap discovery and provider package support

Declare template contracts with annotations such as @model, @dot, @func, and @gen, or use .go-doc/config.json for shared project configuration.

Static analysis only: go-doc never executes application code.

idea-plugin.name: Rods Themes
idea-plugin.description:
Temas dark/neon para VS Code inspirados nas seleções da Copa do Mundo.

Dark/neon themes inspired by World Cup national teams, preserving absolute black backgrounds and bright country accents.

idea-plugin.name: Qiansitu
idea-plugin.description:
Qiansitu is an IntelliJ IDEA plugin for Java and Spring projects. Before you change a class, method, or interface, it builds a layered impact graph covering call chains, implementors, affected interfaces, Spring injection, HTTP endpoints, YAML and Properties references, and same-module tests, plus a damage score to assess risk before touching public APIs. Mark each hit as reviewed with a green check when it has no impact, track progress, and jump to source with a double-click.


作者：画卿晚(YCJ)


简介

牵丝图 — 改代码前的「冲击波」雷达。Find Usages 只能看静态引用；改接口前，你往往不知道配置里的 bean 名、application.yml 的 key、同模块测试会不会一起炸。


牵丝而动，改动可见。它在传统「查找引用」之上，做多维度改动影响分析，用分层牵丝图把一次修改可能波及的代码与配置串起来，帮助你在动手改 public API 之前评估风险。


为什么需要它？

日常重构里，真正难的不是找到谁调用了某个方法，而是：哪些实现类 / 子类会跟着变？Spring 容器里有没有通过 @Autowired、@Resource 或 @Bean 间接依赖？哪些 HTTP 接口会受影响？application.yml / .properties 里有没有引用到相关类名或 bean？同模块测试会不会一起挂？牵丝图把这些维度汇总成一张改动冲击波图，并给出破坏面评分，让「改一行代码会炸多大」一目了然。


核心能力


分层冲击分析
选中类 / 方法 / 接口，一键构建七个维度的冲击报告：直接 / 间接调用链、实现类 / 子类、受影响的接口、Spring @Bean / 注入链、Controller HTTP Web 层、YAML / Properties 配置引用、同模块测试引用。按影响层级与 public API 暴露程度综合给出破坏面评分与风险等级。


牵丝图可视化
右侧工具窗口「改动冲击波」展示分层牵丝图，自上而下呈现「HTTP 入口 → 调用链 → 改动点 → 契约接口」等冲击路径；单击牵丝图节点或标题可跳转源码，双击冲击列表条目同样可跳转，改 public API 前先看清波及面。


排查打标 · 已排查无影响
冲击列表每一行左侧有 ○ 标记区：单击 ○ 打绿色 ✓，该行显示删除线并标注「已排查 · 无影响」，表示此项已人工确认、改动无波及；再次单击可取消标记。按 空格 也可快速切换标记。顶部实时显示已排查 x/y 进度，逐项确认后再改代码，避免遗漏或重复排查。


点击查看
冲击列表支持单击文字在完整类名与短名之间切换，便于在窄侧栏中查看长路径；双击条目跳转对应源码位置；标题栏点击可回到当前分析目标。底部状态栏汇总常用操作提示。


自动刷新
编辑 Java 代码后自动更新分析结果与牵丝图，无需手动重复触发；可在设置或工具窗口中按需关闭。


适用场景

重构接口或 public 方法前的风险评估；修改 Spring Bean / Controller 前的波及面排查；改配置相关类名时的连锁影响检查；Code Review 前快速了解改动破坏面。


使用方式
编辑器或项目树右键 → 改动冲击波分析；快捷键 Alt + Shift + I。兼容 IntelliJ IDEA 2024.1+（Build 241+），依赖 Java 模块。


「Find Usages 看引用，牵丝图看冲击波 — 改之前，先牵丝。」

idea-plugin.name: Semconv Guard - OpenTelemetry Naming Safety
idea-plugin.description:
Keep your OpenTelemetry instrumentation on the current semantic conventions — inline, as you edit. Semconv Guard flags deprecated, renamed, and misspelled OTel attribute, metric, and span names in string literals at your instrumentation call sites (Java and Kotlin), names the stable replacement, and offers a one-click rename.

100% local: reads your source on your machine. No network, no telemetry.

idea-plugin.name: Upgrade Guard - Kubernetes API Upgrade Safety
idea-plugin.description:
Catch removed and deprecated Kubernetes API versions in your manifests before a cluster upgrade breaks prod — inline, as you edit. Pick your target cluster version; Upgrade Guard flags any apiVersion+kind that is removed (error) or deprecated (warning) at that version, names the removal version and replacement, and offers a one-click rewrite to the current apiVersion.

100% local: reads YAML on your machine. No network, no telemetry, no cluster access.

idea-plugin.name: EagleAudit
idea-plugin.description:
EagleAudit is a baseline-first code audit plugin for IntelliJ IDEA, deeply compatible with the SonarQube ecosystem: dual-engine scanning (server or fully offline), baseline-focused incremental auditing, quality gate verdicts and six report formats — everything an audit team needs, right inside the IDE.

Main Features

  • Dual-engine scanning — sonar-scanner upload analysis when a SonarQube server is configured; a bundled local engine (sonarlint-core + sonar-java) for fully offline analysis otherwise. Scanner and analyzer are auto-downloaded: zero manual installation.
  • Baseline-first workflow — freeze legacy issues into a committable eagleaudit-baseline.json; issue tree, editor annotations and reports then focus on NEW issues only. Line-number-free signature matching survives code shifting.
  • Tri-state triage — New / Unchanged / Fixed filter chips with per-issue badges; add single issues or bulk-move batches into the baseline.
  • Quality gate — configure failThreshold in eagleaudit.yaml and every scan ends with a PASS / FAIL verdict, shown in the status bar, notification and report.
  • Configuration as code — commit eagleaudit.yaml (server, rule profile, scope excludes, thresholds) so the whole team and CI share one audit standard; tokens stay in the IDE keychain.
  • Rule management — sync quality profiles and rule descriptions from the server; import / export standard SonarQube backup XML rule files and switch the active rule set from the tool window.
  • Issue tool window — issues grouped by severity / file / rule with rule description and code-snippet detail pane, one-click navigation, false-positive exemption list.
  • Statistics overview — two-ring sunburst (severity / top rules); click a ring segment to filter, tick rows to move them into the baseline in bulk.
  • Editor annotations — precise text-range highlighting for new issues only, severity-mapped, with hover tooltips.
  • Six report formats — interactive HTML (self-contained single file with in-browser baseline governance and baseline file download), static HTML with custom Velocity templates, PDF (CJK fonts embedded), Word, Markdown, SARIF 2.1.0 (with baselineState) and CSV.

主要功能

EagleAudit 是一款以「基线」为核心的 IntelliJ IDEA 代码审计插件，深度兼容 SonarQube 生态： 双引擎扫描（服务器 / 完全离线）、基线聚焦增量审计、质量门禁结论、六种审计报告格式。

  • 双引擎扫描 —— 配置了 SonarQube 服务器时走 sonar-scanner 上传分析；未配置时使用内置 本地引擎（sonarlint-core + sonar-java）完全离线分析。scanner 与分析器自动下载，零手动安装。
  • 基线工作流 —— 存量问题冻结为可提交版本库的 eagleaudit-baseline.json， 问题树、编辑器标注与报告默认聚焦「新增」；签名匹配不含行号，代码上下移动不脱基线。
  • 三态处置 —— 新增 / 基线内 / 已修复过滤与逐条徽章；支持单条加入与批量移入基线。
  • 质量门禁 —— eagleaudit.yaml 配置 failThreshold 后，每次扫描输出 PASS / FAIL 结论，状态条、通知与报告三处同源展示。
  • 配置即代码 —— eagleaudit.yaml（服务器、规则集、排除、阈值）提交版本库， 团队与 CI 共用同一套审计标准；Token 始终保存在 IDE 钥匙串。
  • 规则管理 —— 同步服务器质量配置与规则说明；导入 / 导出 SonarQube 标准备份 XML 规则文件，工具窗口内切换活动规则集。
  • 问题工具窗口 —— 按严重级别 / 文件 / 规则分组，详情面板含规则说明与代码片段， 一键跳转，误报豁免清单。
  • 统计概览 —— 双环旭日图（严重级别 / Top 规则），点击环段过滤，勾选批量移入基线。
  • 编辑器标注 —— 仅标注新增问题，textRange 精确高亮，按级别映射并悬浮提示。
  • 六种报告格式 —— 交互式 HTML（自包含单文件，网页内基线治理与基线文件下载）、 静态 HTML（自定义 Velocity 模板）、PDF（自动嵌入中文字体）、Word、Markdown、 SARIF 2.1.0（含 baselineState）、CSV。
