idea-plugin.name: Cool Request(REST Client)
idea-plugin.description:
Help

Cool Request

API Request Tool

It is used to solve the call of the Controller method and the regular timer method. It is very convenient.

Main Features

1. It can bypass the interceptor. If your project uses spring boot security, it can ignore the spring boot security authentication, and you don’t need to configure anything.

2. It supports pre- and post-scripts and is written in Java. It can call any third-party library and the project's own class.

主要功能

1. 它可以绕过拦截器，如果你的项目使用了spring boot security，他可以无视spring boot security的认证，并且不需要配置什么

2. 它支持前后置脚本，并且使用java编写，可以调用任意第三方库，和项目自身的class

Features

  1. ✓ Show all api information defined in Spring Boot, supporting HTTP/Reflection call
  2. ✓ Display timers defined in Spring Boot, manually trigger without waiting for the specified time
  3. ✓ Bypass interceptors during requests
  4. ✓ Specify proxy/original objects during requests
  5. ✓ One-click export to openapi format
  6. ✓ One-click import to apifox/apipost
  7. ✓ Copy request as curl
  8. ✓ Compatible with gradle, maven multi-module projects
  9. ✓ Compatible with Java/Kotlin languages
  10. ✓ Powerful HTTP request parameter guessing, reducing developers' time to fill in keys
  11. ✓ Use Java syntax to handle pre/post request scripts
  12. ✓ Save response results to files
  13. ✓ Quickly preview json, xml, img, html, text responses
  14. ✓ Multiple layout switching

Steps for usage:

  1. Install it
  2. Select Cool Request in View → Tool Window
  3. Restart your idea
官方文档

Cool Request

API请求工具

用来解决api的调用,以及Spring容器内任意方法的调用,非常方便.

特性

  1. ✓ 显示在Spring Boot中定义的所有API信息，支持 HTTP/反射 调用
  2. ✓ 显示在Spring Boot中定义的定时器,在不等待指定时间的情况下手动触发
  3. ✓ 在请求期间绕过拦截器
  4. ✓ 在请求期间指定代理/原始对象
  5. ✓ 一键导出为OpenAPI格式
  6. ✓ 一键导入到ApiFox、ApiPost
  7. ✓ 将请求复制为cURL
  8. ✓ 兼容Gradle、Maven多模块项目
  9. ✓ 兼容Java/Kotlin语言
  10. ✓ 强大的HTTP请求参数猜测功能,减少开发人员填写参数的时间
  11. ✓ 使用Java语言编写请求前/后脚本
  12. ✓ 快速将响应结果保存到文件中
  13. ✓ 快速预览JSON、XML、图像、HTML、文本响应
  14. ✓ 多种布局切换

使用方法:

  1. 点击Install
  2. 选择 Cool Request,他位于 View → Tool Window
  3. 重新启动您的idea

idea-plugin.name: Magnolia CMS Integration
idea-plugin.description:
Best IDE for Magnolia CMS development: Intelligent YAML & Freemarker autocomplete, navigation, on-hover documentation, schema validation, definition generators, run-on-Tomcat, error detection and seamless refactoring tools. Supports Magnolia 6.4+!

The plugin significantly reduces development time for Magnolia projects. Created by Magnolia developers with 15 years of experience, it automates the most time-consuming tasks:

  • instant access to comprehensive Magnolia documentation (Ctrl+Hover on any element)
  • intelligent autocomplete for Freemarker templates and YAML schemas
  • seamless navigation between templates, dialogs, and components
  • automatic error detection and smart refactoring support
  • a built-in AI assistant and an MCP server that let Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor or OpenAI work on your light modules

Features

Advanced Freemarker Editor

The plugin provides a professional Freemarker development environment specifically designed for Magnolia:

  • Intelligent Autocomplete: Full autocomplete for all Magnolia functions, directives ([#directive]), and user directives ([@cms.*])
  • Instant Documentation: Comprehensive Magnolia documentation on hover (Ctrl+Hover) or quick docs (Ctrl+Shift+Q) for every function and directive, with a direct link to the online Magnolia docs (Shift+F1 for external documentation)
  • Statement Completion: Complete Current Statement (Ctrl+Shift+Enter / â‡§âŒ˜â�Ž) auto-inserts the matching closing tag for an unclosed directive or user directive ([#if] â†’ [/#if], [@cms.area] â†’ [/@cms.area])
  • Smart Syntax Highlighting: Configurable color schemes (Light/Dark) with proper detection of inline expressions, directives, and user directives
  • Code Intelligence: Structure view, code folding, smart comments, and automatic formatting for better code organization
  • Error Detection: Real-time syntax validation with inspections for unclosed directives, wrong closing tags, and syntax errors
  • Advanced Navigation: Find usages, in-file variable/macro/function detection, and jump-to-definition for user directives
  • Refactoring Support: Rename and move operations with automatic reference updates

YAML Schema Support

Comprehensive support for Magnolia light module development:

  • Definition-Aware Key Completion: Completes the valid keys for each definition type â€” page and component templates, dialogs, content types, blocks, REST delivery endpoints and apps â€” detected automatically from the light-module folder structure. Known keys carry inline documentation and value-type hints, and required keys are highlighted
  • Field Completion: Autocomplete for field $type values â€” a built-in baseline of the standard Magnolia fields (textField, richTextField, linkField, multiField, â€¦) that works even without Magnolia on the classpath â€” plus field sub-properties (label, required, i18n, â€¦) inside each field
  • Hybrid Intelligence: When the Magnolia libraries are on the project classpath, additional keys and field types are discovered from the actual definition classes and merged on top of the built-in baseline
  • New UI Forms Support: Completion for javascriptField and its keys (fieldScript, height, parameters), field validators (validators â†’ $type: emailValidator, regex) and converters (converterClass), plus a compatibility inspection that flags field types not yet supported by Magnolia 6.4's React-based New UI Forms in content-app definitions (which would fall back to Vaadin)
  • Definition Validation: Flags unknown/misspelled keys with a "did you mean" rename quick-fix, and warns about missing required keys â€” without false positives on nested or custom structures
  • Type Completion: Intelligent completion for dialog types, action types, datasource types, column types, and content-view types
  • On-Hover Documentation: Hover any definition key (renderType, templateScript, dialog, workspace, â€¦) for its description
  • Definition Generators: Right-click New â†’ Magnolia Definitionâ€¦ to scaffold a dialog, page/component template, content type, REST delivery endpoint, block or app in the correct folder â€” with a companion .ftl for templates and components
  • Java Class Navigation: Jump-to-definition for all class attributes:
    • class, implementationClass, generatorClass, modelClass, entityClass
    • appClass, subAppClass, formatterClass, dropConstraintClass, contentPreviewClass
  • Module Path Detection: Automatic resolution of template references (templateScript) and dialog references (dialogId)
  • FTL Reference Linking: Navigate from YAML to Freemarker templates with a single click
  • Live Templates: Quick scaffolding for common Magnolia patterns (start typing m: for options)

Run & Deploy

Run a Magnolia instance straight from the IDE:

  • Magnolia Run Configuration: Launch Magnolia on a local Tomcat with one click â€” the plugin manages an isolated CATALINA_BASE, patches the HTTP port, and deploys your webapp
  • Bundle Auto-Download: Optionally download a Magnolia Tomcat bundle (Community or DX Core) from Nexus and run it, no local Tomcat required
  • Auto-Open Browser: Automatically opens AdminCentral (or any configured URL) in your browser once the server has started

AI Assistant & MCP Server

An AI chat that knows Magnolia, right in the Magnolia tool window:

  • AI Tab: Chat with Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Windsurf or Aider â€” the installed agents are detected automatically. Answers render as Markdown with highlighted FreeMarker and YAML code blocks, with sessions, file references (@), screenshots, slash commands and permission prompts
  • External AI Providers: Connect OpenAI, the Anthropic API, Gemini or a local Ollama; API keys are stored in the IDE password safe
  • Quick Actions: Explain Code, Improve Code, Fix This Problem, Add Comments and Ask Magnolia AI from the editor context menu, the Tools menu and a floating toolbar over a selection; Alt+Enter offers Fix this problem with Magnolia AI on any warning
  • Explain Last Server Error: Sends the last stack trace or FreeMarker template error from the Magnolia server log to the AI for a cause and a fix
  • MCP Server: Lets any MCP-capable agent work with your project through 15 tools â€” list light modules and definitions with their Magnolia ids, read definition schemas and field types, validate YAML definitions, resolve ids, look up cmsfn/damfn/[@cms.*] documentation, and start Magnolia and read its log. Localhost only, token-protected, one-click install into Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Windsurf and Antigravity
  • Settings: Settings > Languages & Frameworks > Magnolia > AI for the agent, permission mode, providers and the MCP server; Magnolia Defaults for IDE-wide defaults

Project Setup

  • New Project Wizard: Create a Magnolia project (Community or DX Core) with a ready-to-use light-module scaffold and a pre-configured run configuration
  • Light-Module Scaffold: Generates the standard dialogs/, templates/, decorations/ and i18n/ structure so you can start authoring immediately

Project Intelligence

  • Automatic Detection: Recognizes both Java modules and Light modules in your project
  • Framework Integration: Magnolia facet for proper project structure recognition
  • Plugin Recommendations: Automatically suggests the plugin when opening .ftl files or Magnolia projects

The plugin was developed for and tested with Magnolia version 6+.

Configuration Tips

  • Freemarker File Association: For full functionality, set file association to "Magnolia Freemarker" for .ftl files. The file icon should display the Scipio logo in the lower right corner.
    • If autocomplete isn't working: Settings > File Types > Magnolia Freemarker > Verify *.ftl is in the list
  • HTML Inspection Levels: Set HTML element inspection severity to a lower level (Settings > Editor > Inspections > HTML) as Freemarker code can interrupt HTML structure

Developed by Magnolia Experts

Created by Magnolia developers with 15 years of experience building enterprise solutions. The plugin is developed and maintained by Ilscipio, based on real-world project needs and daily usage in production environments.

After developing numerous Magnolia projects, we identified key productivity bottlenecks and built this plugin to solve them. With prior experience creating JetBrains plugins (including for our e-commerce framework "Scipio ERP"), we applied best practices to create a tool we use every day.

Bugs & Feature Requests

If you have any questions, feature requests or stumble upon the occasional bug, come leave us a message at Ilscipio

idea-plugin.name: Export Source to Clipboard
idea-plugin.description:
Supercharge your AI-driven development! This plugin automates packaging source code and its full context into your clipboard, streamlining the process of building high-quality prompts for Large Language Models (LLMs). Including file paths, dependencies, and related files gives immediate context to the AI, dramatically improving the accuracy and relevance of its responses. This is essential for complex analysis, refactoring, and code generation tasks.
  • 🚀 Get Superior AI Results: Effortlessly prepare detailed, context-rich code snippets for immediate AI analysis.
  • 🧠 Build Complete Context: Instantly provide AI assistants with rich, accurate code context, including dependencies, tests, and more.
  • 📋 Automated Efficiency: Automatically attach file paths to clipboard content, eliminating manual errors and speeding up your workflow.
  • 📂 Intelligent Directory Handling: Quickly export entire directories into an AI-friendly format while smartly skipping irrelevant files.
  • 🤖 Full Token Control: Fine-tune every export to stay within LLM token limits, optimizing for cost and performance.
Export Source to Clipboard is an essential tool for developers looking to leverage AI in their coding process, offering a powerful bridge between your IDE and the latest generative AI technologies.
idea-plugin.change-notes:

Version 2.1.3 – UTF-8 Detection Fix

Version 2.1 – Workflow Polish and Accuracy ⚙️

  • Accurate Diff & History: Export history now stores the actual files included after .gitignore, filter, size, and binary checks. The Diff view reflects real added/removed files.
  • Deterministic Ordering: Files are now sorted by relative path for more readable, stable outputs and cleaner diffs.
  • Filter Controls in Settings: Added an explicit "Enable file extension filters" checkbox and a clarifying note about empty lists.
  • Richer Export Notification: The "Content Copied" notification includes a concise summary of processed/excluded files and active filters.
  • Better Special File Support: Improved handling for files without extensions (e.g., Dockerfile/Makefile) for correct filename prefixes and Markdown language hints.
  • Consistency & Stability: Unified token estimation in repository summaries; early cancellation when hitting file limits; streamed sampling for binary detection to avoid heavy reads.
  • macOS Keymap Support: Added modern "macOS" keymap entries to ensure shortcuts work across IDEs.

Version 2.0 – The Context-Aware Update for AI Workflows 🎯

A complete redesign focused on providing deep, contextual code exports with ease. Build better AI prompts, faster.

🚀 Major New Features & Enhancements

  • 🎯 Smart Export Actions: A powerful new menu to export code with its full context. Right-click and choose "Export with Context" to access:
    • Dependencies: Export with Direct Imports, Transitive Imports, or find Dependents (for impact analysis).
    • Code Structure: Export with related Tests, Implementations/Subclasses, or all files in the current Package.
    • Related Resources: Export with Configuration Files, Templates & Styles, or All Related Tests and resources.
    • Version History: Export files from Recent Changes or the Last Git Commit.
  • 🌍 Enhanced Multi-Language Support: Full support for TypeScript, JavaScript, React, and Next.js across all smart actions, with modern framework awareness.
  • 🧪 Comprehensive Test Discovery: The "All Tests" action now finds unit, integration, E2E, and performance tests, plus related fixtures and helper utilities.
  • 🎨 Framework-Aware Resource Finding: Intelligently detects and includes related templates and styles for frameworks like Spring, React, Vue, and Angular.

✨ UI & Workflow Improvements

  • 📋 Organized Menu Structure: An intuitive, hierarchical menu with logical grouping and visual separators for better discoverability.
  • 📝 Export History & Diff View: A new "Compare with Last Export" action lets you see what's changed. The history tracks your last 10 exports, and the diff view shows added/removed files and updated stats.
  • ⌨️ New Keyboard Shortcuts: Added `Ctrl+Shift+C` for standard export and `Ctrl+Shift+Alt+C` to toggle filters.
  • 🎯 Smarter Defaults: Increased file count/size limits (200 files, 500KB) and enabled line numbers by default for better AI context.
  • 👁️ Preview Export Button: A new button in Settings shows you exactly what an export will look like with your current configuration.
  • 📊 Enhanced Notifications: Copy notifications now show file count, total size (KB/MB), and estimated token count.

⚙️ Under the Hood

  • ⚡ Performance Improvements: Exporting now uses parallel processing based on your system's CPU count for faster results on large selections.
  • ⚠️ Large Operation Warning: A confirmation dialog now appears when exporting over 100 files to prevent accidental large operations.

Version 1.7 – Enhanced Stack Traces & Gitignore Magic ✨

  • 📌 Stack Trace Folding: Introduced intelligent stack trace folding in console views. Library frames are neatly collapsed, highlighting your project code clearly.
  • 🧙 Gitignore Mastery: Significantly upgraded gitignore parsing with hierarchical rule handling and caching for accurate, git-consistent exclusions.
  • 🚀 Accuracy Boosts: Optimized token counting for GPT-4 accuracy using the Jtokkit library, enhancing export speed and responsiveness.

Version 1.6 – Powerful New Improvements

  • 🧮 Token Count Insights: Added token count estimation to help avoid LLM context overflow.

idea-plugin.name: Terminal Tab Tailor
idea-plugin.description:
Terminal Tab Tailor significantly enhances the IntelliJ IDEA workflow by dynamically renaming terminal tabs to reflect the currently selected item in your project tree. This feature greatly aids in organizing your workspace and navigating effortlessly between numerous terminal sessions.

Simply select a file or folder within your project tree and initiate a terminal session from that context.

Pro-tip: Ctrl+Shift+X opens a terminal for the current selection right away. Rebind it under Settings > Keymap if it clashes with your own shortcuts.

Three ways to open a tailored tab

  • Open In > Terminal - Terminal Tab Tailor takes over the IDE's own "open in terminal" entries, offering Terminal (Reworked) and Terminal (Classic) so you pick the engine on the spot. Every place you already open a terminal from produces a tailored tab.
  • The TTT Button - the "Open in Terminal" action in one click, from the terminal toolbar, using your most recent selection.
  • Rename Session - right-click any tab to name it yourself. Your sort order is re-applied straight away and the renamed tab stays selected.

Choose what the TTT Button follows:

  • Use the last selection from the Project Tree.
  • Use the last selected Tab from the File Editor.
  • Use the most recent selection, whether from the Project Tree or the File Editor Manager.
  • Use the project name, always.

Options & Sort

  • Reuse an existing tab when the names match.
  • Prompt the renaming dialogue each time a new terminal tab is opened.
  • Add parent folders to a tab's name, so it reads TerminalTabTailor/src rather than src.
  • Incorporate the current date into tab names (with a customizable pattern, defaulting to dd-MM-yy).
  • Maintain tabs in perpetual alphabetical order.
  • Maintain tabs sorted by descending date.
  • Do not sort tabs.

Whichever you choose, opening or reusing a tab brings the terminal window to the front and selects that tab.

Choose from a variety of naming conventions to suit your workflow:

  • Permit the use of file names directly.
  • Default to directory names, utilizing the parent directory's name for files.
  • Adopt the name of the parent module.
  • Use the parent module's directory name for a more structured approach.
  • Consistently use the project's name for all terminal tabs.
  • Follow the shell's current folder, renaming the tab as it changes directory (Reworked Terminal only with PowerShell and cmd on Windows; bash, zsh, sh, fish, dash and ksh elsewhere).

Configurability is at the heart of Terminal Tab Tailor. Find the settings in Settings > Tools > Terminal Tab Tailor, or via Terminal Tab Tailor Settings in the dropdown next to + in the Terminal tool window.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
What's New ?

Requirement
  • IntelliJ IDEA 2025.3 or later: the API that lets a plugin open the terminal engine you selected only exists from 2025.3. If you are on an earlier version, 1.5.1 remains available and keeps working.
Fixed
  • "Follow the shell's current folder" no longer claims to work for PowerShell and pwsh on the classic engine. It never actually did: Set-Location doesn't call Win32's SetCurrentDirectory(), an open upstream PowerShell issue, so the OS-level query this plugin's classic engine relies on stayed frozen at the shell's launch directory no matter how many times it was asked - not something this plugin can read around. Verified end to end before landing this fix: every layer between this plugin and the OS query was checked for a cache on our side, there was none. Classic + cmd is unaffected and keeps following normally, and PowerShell/pwsh follow correctly on the reworked engine, which reads shell integration instead of the OS. A PowerShell/pwsh tab on the classic engine now simply keeps the name it opened with, like any other shell this plugin cannot follow, instead of silently freezing on the wrong name.

idea-plugin.name: gRPC Federation
idea-plugin.description:
gRPC Federation Language Server for JetBrains

The gRPC Federation Language Server for JetBrains is a plugin designed for JetBrains IDEs to integrate with the gRPC Federation language server, providing enhanced development experience for Protocol Buffer files with gRPC Federation annotations.

Features

  • Go to Definition - Navigate to proto message and field definitions
  • Diagnostics - Real-time error detection and validation
  • Code Completion - Intelligent suggestions for gRPC Federation annotations

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate 2023.3 or newer (This plugin requires Ultimate Edition)
  • grpc-federation-language-server installed and available in PATH

Installation

Step 1: Install the Language Server

The plugin requires grpc-federation-language-server to be accessible in the system PATH. If Go is available, install it with:

$ go install github.com/mercari/grpc-federation/cmd/grpc-federation-language-server@latest

Verify the installation:

$ which grpc-federation-language-server

Step 2: Install the Plugin

Install the plugin from JetBrains Marketplace:

  1. Open Settings/Preferences → Plugins
  2. Select Marketplace tab
  3. Search for "gRPC Federation"
  4. Click Install and restart the IDE

Configuration

Setting Import Paths

Configure proto import paths for the language server to resolve dependencies:

  1. Navigate to Settings/Preferences → Tools → gRPC Federation
  2. In the Proto Import Paths section:
    • Click + to add a new path
    • Use the file browser to select directories
    • Enable/disable paths using checkboxes
    • Reorder paths using ↑/↓ buttons
    • Click Validate Paths to verify all directories exist

Supported Path Variables

  • ~/ - User's home directory
  • ${PROJECT_ROOT} - Current project root directory

Example paths:

/usr/local/include
${PROJECT_ROOT}/proto
~/workspace/shared-protos

Troubleshooting

Language Server Not Found

If you see "grpc-federation-language-server not found" error:

  1. Ensure the language server is installed (see Installation section)
  2. Check if it's in your PATH: which grpc-federation-language-server
  3. Restart the IDE after installation

Proto Files Not Recognized

If proto files are not being analyzed:

  1. Ensure the file extension is .proto
  2. Check that import paths are correctly configured
  3. Validate paths using the Validate Paths button
  4. Check the IDE logs: Help → Show Log in Finder/Explorer

Import Resolution Issues

If imports are not being resolved:

  1. Add all necessary proto directories to import paths
  2. Ensure paths are in the correct order (more specific paths first)
  3. Check that all proto dependencies are available

Support

  • Issues: GitHub Issues
  • Documentation: gRPC Federation Documentation

idea-plugin.name: Module Mold
idea-plugin.description:
Create module for Android project from your own template

What This Tries To Solve

In an Android's typical multi-module project, we often need to create new modules. And the Android Studio's built-in New Module... isn't for everyone because, for instance, you may have an established pattern in your project of how the build.gradle of a module would look like. Traditionally we need to copy from an existent module in your project. Then we need to tweak the copy by deleting some irrelevant files, changing build.gradle, registering the new module to settings.gradle, etc.

It'll be good to automate this process so that minimum intervene is required from the developer, such as the module name.

How It Works

Assuming you have different types of modules in your project, such as some non-user-facing library modules and some other user-facing feature modules, etc. You can create a config file, for the plugin, in your project to dictate how each type of module should be created. Then the plugin will read the config file and loads up menu options in Tools in Android Studio (or Intellij in general). From the menu options you can choose what type of module you'd want to create. Then you'd be prompted to input the module name. Then the automation will do as follows:

  • Copy the corresponding module template to a temporary directory
  • Replace placeholders in build.gradle file in the copy
  • Create source folder as per the package of the module
  • Copy the copy in the temporary directory into the project
  • Register the new module settings.gradle
  • Invoke a Gradle Sync for the project

Steps To Set Up

1. Install Module Mold plugin from Intellij Marketplace

2. Create module-mold.yaml config in root directory of the project

And it'll look something like this:

templateRootDir: module-template
rootPackage: com.example
moduleTypes:
  - type: feature # Notice here 'feature' will also be used as the root folder for all the created modules of this type
    template: android-lib
  - type: kotlin library
    template: kotlin-lib
    rootDir: library  # Use 'rootDir' when the module needs to be under a folder that's different from the name of the 'type'
  - type: android library
    template: android-lib
    rootDir: library
  - type: top-level library
    template: android-lib
    rootDir: .  # Notice here the module can be directly put under project root folder

In the example above:

  • templateRootDir: The relative path of the directory that'll contain the templates you're going to create
  • rootPackage: This will be used to concatenate with module name to form the package of the module. For example if the rootPackage is com.example and if you create a module named foo, then the package for the module will be com.example.foo. The package will be inserted into build.gradle, and also to create source folder in src/main/java etc.
  • moduleTypes: List out all the possible module types in your project
    • type: This will a directory resides under the root directory of the project.
    • template: This is a directory under the templateRootDir. And you can put whatever you want in this directory, and they'll be copied over to the new module in the end.
    • rootDir: Use this when the dir that you want to put the new module into is different from the name of 'type'. And use '.' to indicate you want the new module to be directly under root directory of the project

3. Create your template(s)

Like described above, you'll need to designate the templateRootDir in the config file. Let's assume it is module-template, in which I have a template android-lib for android modules, and 'kotlin-lib' for plain Kotlin modules. Now I'm having the template(s) directory structure as this:

module-template
├── android-lib
│   ├── build.gradle
│   └── src
│       ├── main
│       │   ├── AndroidManifest.xml
│       │   ├── java
│       │   └── res
│       └── test
│           └── java
└── kotlin-lib
    ├── build.gradle
    └── src
        └── main
            └── java

Obviously you can create as many templates as you want.

4. About Placeholders

If you have the following placeholders in your template's build.gradle, the plugin will replace the placeholders with real values:

  • MODULE_MOLD_MODULE_NAME: The module name you've provided when you create the module, such as foo as above example
  • MODULE_MOLD_MODULE_PACKAGE: The package of the new module, such as com.example.foo as above example
    • You can also create a folder named MODULE_MOLD_MODULE_PACKAGE anywhere under src directory of the template. And it'll be automatically replaced with package folders (e.g. com/example/foo)

Compatibility

  • This plugin also works for projects that have build.gradle.kts and settings.gradle.kts

Common Issues and Resolutions

1. Empty folders (such as MODULE_MOLD_MODULE_PACKAGE) in template can't be commited to git

You can put a .gitkeep empty file under the otherwise empty directory in order to commit the folder to git. And the .gitkeep will not be copied over to the new module when you come to create a module.

Contributing

You're welcome to contribute to this project (https://github.com/totrit/module-mold) to cater for different project structures than current assumptions.

idea-plugin.description:
Amazon Q Developer IDE plugins: end of support

On April 30, 2027, AWS will discontinue support for Amazon Q Developer IDE plugins. For capabilities similar to Amazon Q Developer IDE plugins, explore Kiro to access the latest models and features, including agentic coding, chat and MCP support.

Learn more

The most capable generative AI-powered assistant for building, operating, and transforming software, with advanced capabilities for managing data and AI

Agentic coding experience

Amazon Q Developer uses information across native and MCP server-based tools to intelligently perform actions beyond code suggestions, such as reading files, generating code diffs, and running commands based on your natural language instruction. Simply type your prompt in your preferred language and Q Developer will provide continuous status updates and iteratively apply changes based on your feedback, helping you accomplish tasks faster.

Implement new features

Generate new code across your entire project and implement features.

Generate documentation

Write API, technical design, and onboarding documentation.

Automate code reviews

Perform code reviews, flagging suspicious code patterns and assessing deployment risk.

Generate unit tests

Generate unit tests and add them to your project, helping you improve code quality, fast.

Transform workloads

/transform to upgrade your Java applications in minutes, not weeks.

Core features

MCP support

Add Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers to give Amazon Q Developer access to important context.

Inline suggestions

Receive real-time code suggestions ranging from snippets to full functions based on your comments and existing code.

15+ languages supported including Python, TypeScript, Rust, Terraform, AWS Cloudformation, and more

Inline chat

Seamlessly initial chat within the inline coding experience. Select a section of code that you need assistance with and initiate chat within the editor to request actions such as "Optimize this code", "Add comments", or "Write tests".

Chat

Generate code, explain code, and get answers about software development.

Code reference log

Attribute code from Amazon Q that is similar to training data. When code suggestions similar to training data are accepted, they will be added to the code reference log.

Getting Started

Free Tier - create or log in with an AWS Builder ID (a personal profile from AWS).

Pro Tier - if your organization is on the Amazon Q Developer Pro tier, log in with single sign-on.

Troubleshooting & feedback

File a bug or submit a feature request on our Github repository.

idea-plugin.name: Monitor
idea-plugin.description:
Monitor is a lightweight system monitoring widget based on OSHI. It shows the real-time transfer rate of the selected network adapter, CPU usage and memory usage in the IDE status bar, refreshed every second.

Features

  • Status bar widget: selectable metrics (at least one, all on by default) — network adapter download/upload rate, CPU usage, memory usage, CPU temperature (shown when supported by hardware; Celsius or Fahrenheit selectable in Settings)
  • Selectable rate unit in Settings: KB/s (binary, auto KB/s -> MB/s -> GB/s) or kbps (decimal bits, auto kbps -> Mbps -> Gbps)
  • Click the widget to switch the monitored network adapter in a popup, or open the Monitor settings page
  • CPU or memory above the alert threshold (default 80%, adjustable via sliders in Settings) is highlighted in red
  • Sampling is shared by all open project windows (identical values) and pauses while the IDE window is in the background, resuming right away when it comes back; this pause can be turned off in Settings (always sample)
  • Network adapter selection in Settings -> Tools -> Monitor

中文说明

Monitor 是一款基于 OSHI 的轻量系统监控插件：在 IDE 状态栏实时显示所选网卡的上传/下载速率、CPU 使用率与内存使用率，数据每秒刷新一次。

主要功能

  • 状态栏小部件：每秒刷新显示所选网卡速率、CPU 使用率、内存使用率、CPU 温度（硬件支持时；设置可选摄氏/华氏），定宽排版不抖动
  • 显示参数可在设置中勾选（至少一项，默认全选）
  • 速率单位可选：KB/s（二进制，自动 KB/s→MB/s→GB/s）或 kbps（十进制按位，自动 kbps→Mbps→Gbps）
  • 点击小部件可在弹出菜单中直接切换监控网卡，或跳转 Monitor 设置页
  • CPU 或内存超过告警阈值（默认 80%，设置页滑杆可调）时标红提示
  • 所有工程窗口共享同一份采样（各窗口数值一致）；IDE 窗口处于后台/最小化时自动暂停采集，回到前台立即恢复（该行为可在设置页关闭，改为始终采样）
  • 设置 -> 工具 -> Monitor 中可切换监控的网卡、选择显示参数、选择单位、调整阈值

idea-plugin.name: Tabdir Redux
idea-plugin.description:
Tabdir Redux

This plugin will allow you to have directory names added to tab labels, and use various ways to shorten them, including regex.

This is an updated and extended fork of IntelliJ plugin Tabdir, originally found on GitHub at crazyproger/Tabdir and IntelliJ Plugin Marketplace here.

You can install this fork of the plugin from the IntelliJ Marketplace here. You will have to uninstall the old version first.

Description

Awesome replacement for IDEA's 'Show directory in editor tabs for non-unique filenames'. This plugin will allow you to have directory names added to tab labels. It can also show only path differences, so if you have blog/controllers/index and news/controllers/index, it will add either [blog] or [news]. You can control how prefixes will be formatted in Settings tab 'Tabdir'.

Tip: If you're having trouble managing dozens of open files, try enabling vertical tabs and 'Sort tabs alphabetically'.

Features

  • add file's path to tab title
  • shorten the file's path in table title, limit folder name length and number of nested folders
  • configure different tab prefixes for any folder
  • set empty path prefixes - if the file's path is shortened to an empty string, e.g. file is at top level of a folder, you can assign it a custom prefix to keep these files ordered together
  • regex replacements for tab titles

Configuration

Per-project configuration allows specifying different formatting rules for each directory in project.

To enable per-project configuration, enable "Use per project configuration" checkbox and reopen settings window (needs close with Ok or Apply buttons). After this you will find 'Tabdir Project Settings' configuration in "Other Settings".

Note: you should turn off IDE Settings → Editor tabs → Show directory in editor tabs for non-unique filenames.

Usage notes

  • There is some weirdness around the global configuration, so create at least one Per project configuration and set its `Configuration for directory` and `Always show path relative to` to your project's folder.
  • If the path (`[{0}]`) part after the tab title replacement ends up empty, nothing in `[]` brackets is shown, so use unique `Empty path replacement` to differentiate the folders. `Empty path replacement` will be prepended to the filename.
  • Use e.g. a `space` or some special character as `Empty path replacement` for your project's root folder, that way you can keep all the files in root together.
  • Regex title replacements work on full tab title you get after the Tab title format (`[{0}] $1` by default, which means `[folder] filename`). The regex is in `java.util.regex` format, regexes are newline delimited and `::` separated strings of `match::replacement`.
  • You can use any Java's regex syntax tricks, e.g., capture groups in both match and replacement, so running e.g. `app/(.*)/routes/(.*)\.ts::foo $1 $2` on `app/web/routes/my-route.ts` will end up with `foo web my-route`.
  • Regex results are chained, the result of a first regex is an input for the second one, and so on, and run top to bottom, so you can run multiple regexes on the same title. As a result, you have to take care about unexpected matches and replacements.
  • If the opened file is outside your project, the directory won't be shown unless you configure `Tabdir Project Settings` and add folder for e.g. the root of the drive the file is in - for example, Configuration for directory: `C:\`, Always show path relative to: `C:\`, Tab title format: `[C:/{0}] {1}`, Reduce dir names: unchecked.
  • To show tab title format changes for the already open files, you will either have to reopen the files, or change Tabs placement (`Settings -> Editor -> General -> Editor Tabs`), from e.g., `Left` to `Top`, click `Apply`, and then set it back to your preference and click `Ok` (haven't found a better way to update the tab titles yet, sorry).

As the original author seems to have lost access to publish new versions of the original plugin, with his permission, this is a fork under a new name.

idea-plugin.name: Extra Tools Pack
idea-plugin.description:
Extra Tools Pack provides the exact same features as Extra Icons, Extra IDE Tweaks and Extra ToolWindow Colorful Icons. It's offered at a lower price than if you bought each plugin individually.

License types
— Extra Tools Pack offers monthly and yearly licenses.
— Extra Tools Pack Lifetime (new!) offers lifetime licenses: pay once, use it, and get updates forever.

There are two different plugins because JetBrains does not allow plugin developers to offer all the license types (monthly/yearly and lifetime) for the same plugin. Both plugins offer the exact same features. The only difference is the license.

Features from Extra Icons

Make your IDE more pleasant to use:
  • Adds 500+ icons for files like Travis YML, GitLab YML, Angular files, etc. Many icons have variants, so if you are not happy with the default icon, you can choose another.
  • Shows an icon for Git submodule folders.
  • Highly configurable: see File > Settings > Appearance & Behavior > Extra Icons to select extra icons to (de)activate. This is configurable at the IDE and project level.
  • You can register your own icons in order to define custom icons for certain files or file patterns.
  • You can override almost all IDE icons, including toolbars, menus, etc.
  • You can import and export icons from external files. This also means you can easily share icon themes with friends. You can also download online icon packs (example: restore the old file icons when using the new UI).
  • For more information, please see the online documentation.
  • JetBrains Gateway is no longer supported (it actually has never been fully supported).

Features from Extra ToolWindow Colorful Icons

Makes tool window and control icons colorful. This feature is based on the ToolWindow Colorful Icons plugin and adds several new icons. You can also choose icons to (de)activate: see Settings > Appearance & Behavior > Extra ToolWindow Colorful Icons.
You will get the exact same features as using Extra ToolWindow Colorful Icons with a paid license.

Features from Extra IDE Tweaks

Some utilities for IDE maintenance and tweaking, plus workarounds for a few IDE issues. See Tools > Extra IDE Tweaks. Features:
  • The Open Editors tool window shows opened files in all editors belonging to the opened project, as in VSCode. It can also display a list of recently opened files, as in the Recent Files action.
  • New experimental feature: the Updates tool window lists the dependencies updates of Gradle, Maven, and Node.js projects. It also lists the dependencies relocations of Gradle and Maven projects.
  • Can make folder icons more visible (with no outline style) when using the New UI. You can also use it with the regular UI.
  • Can change most tool windows label. Per example, rename the "Pull Requests" tool window to "PR".
  • Can confirm the opening of sensitive files. May be useful when streaming and/or accidentally opening a sensitive file in situations where you can leak critical information.
  • Can open projects located in trusted locations directly via File > Trusted Locations, just after Recent Projects.
  • Can register your favorite projects, organize them with optional groups, and gain fast access to your favorite projects via File > Favorite Projects, just after Recent Projects and Trusted Locations.
  • Can define default Excluded Folders (not per-project). There is now a global list of excluded folders. Go to Extra IDE Tweaks settings for details.
  • Commit Alert: this inspection allows you to define keywords that will show a confirmation dialog before committing files containing any of those keywords. Per example, define the COMMIT_ALERT keyword, modify, delete or move one or multiple files containing it, then commit. A confirmation dialog will appear asking if you still want to commit.
  • Activate All Tool Windows: this action activates all available tool windows in the current project. Enable it in settings, then see the "Window > Activate All Tool Windows" menu item. It's like clicking on the "..." button on the left-side toolbar, then clicking on each available tool window.
  • Can register any program and add it to the "Open In" list when doing a right-click on a file, a folder, or a project. Your program will be added next to the "Open In" Terminal action. That means you can open files and folders with your favorite program (like ForkLift, Total Commander, Vim...). You can register up to 2 "Open In" actions. Go to Extra IDE Tweaks settings for details.
    You can also open files with Associated Application. This additional action is enabled for IDEs prior to 2024 only, as it is already implemented by 2024+ IDEs.
  • Can open a folder as a Project via the "Open In" menu.
  • Can rename tab names to remove the parenthesis after the file names if they're located in the root project or module. Per example, renames "build.gradle.kts (my-module)" to "build.gradle.kts". For now, it works with "build.gradle", "build.gradle.kts", "build.gradle.dcl", "settings.gradle", "settings.gradle.kts" "settings.gradle.dcl" and "src/main/resources/META-INF/plugin.xml" files only.
  • Can purge IDE's plugin download cache. This is a workaround for known IDE limitation 🐛 IJPL-6179.
  • Can schedule the IDE's GC.
  • Can schedule the GC on local JVMs. May be useful when having multiple Gradle or Kotlin Compiler daemons consuming too much memory. You can choose to run the GC on selected JVMs: all local JVMs, or by filtering by JVM instance name with your own regexes.
  • Adds a Properties action to the File and Folder context menu that shows information like size, number of files, etc.
  • Adds a menu item under Tools in order to access the Plugins Manager faster.
  • Offers a workaround for known IDE issue 🐛 IDEA-341174: the Git tool window may display the wrong label "Version Control" instead of "Git".
Plugin's Chinese UI (插件的中文用户界面).
Huawei DevEco Studio support.

Check also my other plugins.

idea-plugin.name: Multi-Project Workspace
idea-plugin.description:
Enables multiple open projects in a single workspace in the IDE. The plugin provides a smooth editing, launching, and debugging experience across all projects in the workspace.

You can:
  • Import projects from different repositories.
  • Add only the required projects from a monorepository.
  • Use different build tools in the same workspace.
  • Edit code in different programming languages in the same workspace.
Usage examples:
  • Develop a backend API service and a complementary front-end application from different repositories.
  • Update and debug particular microservices from a big monorepository.
  • Create a "side" project in the workspace folder to simplify testing and debugging the "main" project.
The plugin is not invasive, so it does not add anything to project settings. You can create several workspaces and include the same project in them.

idea-plugin.name: Awesome Console X
idea-plugin.description:
Special thanks to anthraxx intellij-awesome-console for providing the open-source code, which has enabled me to continue using such an excellent plugin.

Finally a plugin that makes links in your console and terminal at least 200% more awesome!


With this plugin all files and links in the console and terminal will be highlighted and can be clicked. Source code files will be opened in the IDE, other links with the default viewer/browser for this type.

Now you just need to configure your favorite Logger to include the file path, or for Java the fully qualified class name (and optionally a line number), and you can instantly jump to that file that throws this stupid error.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1337.42

  • A path in the console now opens only the file it names. A bare name such as MyClass.java no longer jumps to a same-named file in another folder.
  • Loggers that print only the file name (Log4j %F, Logback %file) are no longer linked. Print a full path, or for Java a class name like com.example.MyClass:42 (%C:%L / %class:%line).
  • A missing or deleted path is no longer linked to a different file that merely ends with the same name, including git delete and status lines.
  • Shortened git .../ paths still open the matching file.
  • Rebuilding the file index no longer reports success when the reload is canceled, the filter is disposed, or the rebuild fails.
0.1337.41
  • Fixed bare words such as "app" or "tools" in CLI help text being linked to same-named project directories
  • Dropped start|dev|test from the default ignore pattern; bare command words are already skipped by path citation rules
0.1337.40
  • Added support for git --stat truncated paths with disk search fallback and unique-file resolution among homonyms
  • Enhanced git rename/delete handling to link the new path and avoid unrelated same-named files after deletion
  • Added real-time index progress listeners and cache-ready API so settings UI reflects live rebuild status
  • Improved index status display with last-rebuild tooltip, cached file counts, and layout that no longer stretches the settings panel
  • Replaced JOptionPane with IntelliJ Messages for error and confirmation dialogs to match IDE UI style
  • Tightened disk search safety: bounded firstDir/memo caches, no symlink walk outside roots, generation-aware cache puts, and dispose that cannot swap a stale cache
  • Fixed ignore pattern validation to allow empty values when ignore is disabled, and sync the UI from storage after apply
  • Added extensive tests for git operations, truncated paths, disk search, indexing, and settings UI (~2800 lines)
0.1337.39
  • Fixed Windows illegal paths causing excessive SEVERE log errors by adding VALID_WINDOWS_PATH regex pre-check before Paths.get() (PR #18)
  • Merged duplicate logger.error calls into single statement with exception parameter in resolveFile
  • Cached SystemUtils.isWindows() result in static final field to avoid repeated System.getProperty() calls on every resolveFile invocation
  • Added WindowsPathValidationTest with 26 unit tests covering valid paths, URLs, pseudo-schemes, host:port, wildcards and edge cases
  • Added 9 integration tests in AwesomeLinkFilterTest for PR #18 scenarios including WSL paths, Node.js pseudo-schemes, webpack URIs and mixed content
0.1337.38
  • Added rethrowIfExceptionMustNotBeLogged calls across all catch blocks to prevent swallowing ControlFlowException (issue #17)
  • Upgraded IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin from 2.2.1 to 2.5.0
  • Removed untilBuild upper limit to support all future IDE versions
  • Added explicit opentest4j dependency for test framework compatibility (IJPL-157292)
  • Fixed code indentation in AwesomeLinkFilterProvider and FileUtils.resolveSymlink
0.1337.37
  • Fixed potential deadlock by making initial file cache build fully asynchronous (issue #16)
  • Replaced parallelStream with stream inside cacheReadLock to avoid ForkJoinPool blocking risk
  • Moved VFS event cache updates to pooled thread to prevent UI freeze from write lock contention
  • Optimized getIndexStatistics to access maps directly under single lock, avoiding nested read lock overhead
  • Added detailed thread-safety documentation for scheduleManualRebuild method
0.1337.36
  • Refactored cache rebuild to two-phase strategy: lock-free build + atomic swap with brief write lock
  • Added timeout protection for synchronous cache rebuild to prevent indefinite blocking
  • Skip synchronous cache init on EDT to avoid UI freeze
  • Promoted scheduleReloadAsync to public API, eliminating reflection-based test access
  • Simplified pending reload scheduling logic by removing redundant synchronized block
0.1337.35
  • Added "Underline Only" option to display hyperlinks with underline only without changing text color
  • Unified ignore file checking logic with new shouldIgnoreFile() method
  • Optimized file filtering at index stage to reduce invalid indexing
  • Refactored progress callback logic with dedicated triggerProgressCallback() method
  • Improved ignore pattern change handling with forced full cache rebuild
  • Enhanced VFS file addition event processing with ignore pattern filtering
  • Cleaned up redundant code comments and simplified implementation
  • Added exception handling for file indexing process to prevent interruption on errors
  • Added exception handling for VFS event processing to improve plugin stability
  • Optimized getVirtualFileFromPath to avoid deadlock when called under read lock

idea-plugin.name: Spring Debugger
idea-plugin.description:
The Spring Debugger plugin for IntelliJ IDEA gives you instant insight into your Spring application while debugging. It brings Spring’s complex runtime behavior into focus by integrating seamlessly with IntelliJ IDEA. See how beans are wired, trace configuration values, inspect database connections, and monitor a transaction state—without leaving your IDE.

The Spring Debugger helps you understand what’s going on behind the scenes, so you can resolve issues faster, verify application state, and write high-quality, maintainable code.

Key features:

  • Application Context Insight

    • Context Visibility: Displays the state and details (name, type, scope) of instantiated Spring beans in the code editor, debugger tool window, and project view during active debug sessions.
    • Extended Watches: Enhances the standard Watches view with live runtime data for loaded Spring beans.
    • Direct Bean Method Invocation: Lets you access Spring bean methods and properties directly in the debugger’s expression evaluator.

  • Properties & Configuration

    • Actual Values Display: Shows the final resolved values of Spring configuration properties directly in the editor.
    • Property Evaluation in Debugger: Allows you to check property values at runtime using the debugger.
    • Value Source Tracking: Reveals where each property came from and its final value in the Watches view.
    • Loaded Configuration Files: Lists the configuration files that contributed to the current environment.

  • Data Access & Transactions

    • Active DB Connection Display: Automatically shows active database connections, including testcontainers, with no manual setup.
    • Transaction Status Display: Displays the current status of Spring-managed transactions inside the debugger tool window.
    • Entity State in Watches: Adds support for viewing JPA entity lifecycle states (e.g., managed, detached) directly in the Watches view.

  • Spring Security Support

    • Endpoint Security Indicators: Shows inline hints on controller endpoints and HTTP Client requests indicating whether authentication is required and which roles or authorities are needed.
    • Instant Endpoint Unlocking: Lets you unlock a secured endpoint during a debug session with a default or custom test user, bypassing the real login flow.
    • Security Configuration Navigation: Jumps directly from the security hint to the bean or class that declares the application's security filter chain.

  • Supports both X11 and Wayland (using the KDE appmenu protocol)

Notes:
  • This plugin does not hide the menu UI integrated in IDEA. Configure it to use the hamburger menu, then it shouldn't get in your way.
  • This plugin is developed for x86_64 Linux systems and will not do anything elsewhere
  • This plugin is not dependent on KDE, even though the KDE appmenu protocol is used.
    Available features will automatically be detected.
  • Because it needs access to protocol-level structures, this plugin may not work as intended with modified IDEs or JVMs

idea-plugin.name: Base64 File
idea-plugin.description:
Base64 File makes it easy to encode, decode, and manage Base64 content directly in your JetBrains IDE.

Encode files such as PNG, JPG, SVG, fonts, and other binary files as Base64 or Base64 Data URIs, insert them directly into your code, and decode Base64 values back into files — without leaving the IDE.

For workflows that require an editable source file, you can link Base64 values to their source files and keep the encoded content automatically synchronized when the source changes.

Key Features

  • Encode files as Base64 — insert files directly into your code as Base64 or Base64 Data URIs.
  • Decode Base64 to files — turn Base64 content from your editor into a project file.
  • Keep Base64 synchronized — link encoded values to source files and automatically update them when the source changes.
  • Support multiple encoded files — manage multiple Base64 values within a single file.
  • Navigate between files and Base64 — quickly jump from a linked Base64 value to its source file.
  • Visual indicators — easily identify linked Base64 values in the Project Tree and editor.
  • Multiple encoding schemes — use the appropriate Base64 encoding scheme for your use case.

Free Features

  • Encode files as Base64
  • Insert files as Base64 Data URIs
  • Decode Base64 values to files
  • Remove links between Base64 values and files

Paid Features

idea-plugin.name: MJump
idea-plugin.description:
A powerful navigation plugin ported from vim-EasyMotion for JetBrains IDEs. MJump enhances your code navigation experience by providing quick jump capabilities to characters, words, and lines. It seamlessly integrates with IdeaVim for a more natural Vim-like experience.

IMPORTANT!

  • This is NOT my plugin. All rights and credit belong to github user a690700752 for this amazing plugin.
  • The official and original repository is at https://github.com/a690700752/KJump and is still maintained.
  • Currently the only differences to KJump is that MJump is able to do the jumping across all open editors and is compatible with new IntelliJ versions.
  • Since I actively use this plugin, I’ll keep it updated to fix bugs and ensure compatibility with future IntelliJ releases.

Features

  • Quick character jump: Jump to any character in the visible area
  • Word navigation: Jump to any word or word starting with a specific character
  • Line jumping: Quickly navigate to any line
  • IdeaVim integration: Works seamlessly with IdeaVim
  • Minimal keystrokes: Reach your target with just a few keystrokes

Usage

Keyboard Shortcuts

There are no default activated shortcuts. You can assign MJump activation shortcuts in: Settings → Keymap → MJump

Common shortcut suggestions:

  • Ctrl+, for character jump
  • Ctrl+; for word jump

IdeaVim Integration

Add the following commands to your ~/.ideavimrc:

" Basic jumps
nmap <leader><leader>s :action MJumpAction<cr>
nmap <leader><leader>w :action MJumpAction.Word0<cr>
nmap <leader><leader>l :action MJumpAction.Line<cr>

" Additional jumps
nmap <leader><leader>c :action MJumpAction.Char2<cr>
nmap <leader><leader>f :action MJumpAction.Word1<cr>

Available Actions

NameActionDescription
MJump Char 1MJumpAction.Char1Input 1 character and jump to any same character
MJump Char 2MJumpAction.Char2Input 2 characters and jump to any matching position
MJump Word 0MJumpAction.Word0Jump to any word
MJump Word 1MJumpAction.Word1Input 1 character and jump to any word starting with this character
MJump LineMJumpAction.LineJump to any line

idea-plugin.description:
IDE Sync - VSCode-JetBrains Sync

Synchronizes a JetBrains IDE with a Visual Studio Code IDE, enabling seamless navigation between both editors.

This synchronization system is suitable for VSCode, VSCode forks like Cursor or Windsurf as well as JetBrains IntelliJ-based IDEs like Rider, IntelliJ IDEA, and WebStorm.

Features

  • Automatic cursor position synchronization
  • Automatic active file synchronization
  • Easy configuration through settings

Installation

  1. Install the JetBrains plugin in JetBrains IDE called "IDE Sync - Connect to VSCode"
  2. Install the corresponding VS Code extension called "IDE Sync - Connect to JetBrains IDE"

Usage

  1. After installation, you'll find a toggle button in the JetBrains IDE status bar
  2. Click the button to enable/disable synchronization
  3. The button shows the current status:
    • "Turn IDE Sync On" - Sync disabled
    • "IDE Sync On" - Sync enabled

Configuration

You can adjust the WebSocket port in the settings:

  • Open JetBrains IDE settings
  • Search for "IDE Sync - Connect to VSCode"
  • Adjust the port (default: 3000)

Troubleshooting

If you can't establish a connection:

  • Make sure both plugins are installed
  • Check if the IDE Sync is turned on in both IDEs
  • Verify that the port settings match in both plugins
  • Restart both editors

Feedback & Issues

Please report issues or suggestions on GitHub.

idea-plugin.name: KDocGen
idea-plugin.description:
KDocGen: Code & Documentation Generator

🛠️ Overview

KDocGen is a powerful IntelliJ IDEA plugin designed to streamline code generation and documentation creation for Kotlin developers.
With a single shortcut, you can instantly generate structured code, comprehensive documentation, and well-organized test cases—reducing manual effort and boosting productivity.

Whether you're writing new functions, documenting existing ones, or setting up test cases, KDocGen ensures your codebase remains clean, well-documented, and maintainable.
By leveraging AI-assisted automation, this plugin helps you focus on writing high-quality logic while handling repetitive tasks.

🔥 Why Use KDocGen?

✅ Automate documentation – No more writing KDocs manually.
✅ Generate missing code – Quickly create function bodies and method stubs.
✅ Simplify testing – Instantly generate Kotest test files for your functions.
✅ Enhance readability – Insert meaningful comments effortlessly.
✅ Generate QA reports – Gain insights into potential issues and improvements.
✅ Seamless IntelliJ IDEA integration – Works smoothly with a single shortcut.

Stay productive, write better code, and let KDocGen handle the rest! 🚀

✨ Features

  • 🔹 Generate function documentation – Insert AI-assisted KDoc for selected functions.
  • 🔹 Process code with AI – Modify, enhance, or analyze selected code based on AI instructions.
  • 🔹 Generate comments – Add meaningful, AI-generated comments to code.
  • 🔹 Generate Kotest tests – Instantly create Kotest test files for selected functions.
  • 🔹 Generate QA reports – Analyze functions and produce detailed reports.
  • 🔹 Seamless integration – Works effortlessly within IntelliJ IDEA using a single shortcut.
  • 🔹 Provider selection – Choose between API providers, including OpenAI, Groq, and a Custom option.

🛠️ Installation

  1. Open IntelliJ IDEA.
  2. Go to Plugins → Marketplace.
  3. Search for KDocGen.
  4. Click Install.
  5. Go to Settings → KDocGen Settings.
  6. Click Save, and you're ready to go!

🚀 Usage

⚠️ No OpenAI Account Needed! Use Groq for Free!

Good news! You no longer need an OpenAI account to use KDocGen's AI-powered features.
Simply get a free Groq API key here: Groq Console and start using the plugin instantly!

Alternatively, if you prefer OpenAI, you can still use an OpenAI API Token.

Generating Documentation for a Function

  1. Navigate to the function.
  2. Press [⌘ + N] (on macOS).
  3. Select ✨ Generate KDoc.
  4. The plugin will generate KDoc for the selected function automatically.

Processing Selected Code with AI

  1. Write a comment describing the AI task (e.g., add a function, check for errors, enhance logic, etc.).
  2. Select the relevant code.
  3. Press [⌘ + N] (on macOS).
  4. Select ✨ Process with AI.
  5. The plugin will modify or enhance the selection based on your request.

Generating a Kotest Test for a Function

  1. Navigate to the function.
  2. Press [⌘ + N] (on macOS).
  3. Select ✨ Generate Kotest File.
  4. The plugin will generate a scratch file with a test using BehaviorSpec.

Generating a QA Report

  1. Navigate to the function.
  2. Press [⌘ + N] (on macOS).
  3. Select ✨ Generate QA Report.
  4. The plugin will generate a report highlighting potential issues and improvements.

Generating a Comment for Selected Code

  1. Select a piece of code (e.g., a function or class).
  2. Press [⌘ + N] (on macOS).
  3. Select ✨ Describe Selection.
  4. The plugin will automatically generate a comment.

⚡ Shortcut

ActionShortcut (macOS)
Generate Code & Docs⌘ + N

📌 Future Enhancements

  • 🔹 Full K2 support for AI-powered features.
  • 🔹 Improved AI-based documentation generation.
  • 🔹 Support for additional languages (e.g., Java).

💡 Enhance your development workflow with automated code & documentation generation!

💖 Support the Project

If you’d like to support the author or have an idea, visit Boosty.

idea-plugin.name: Folder Structure Generator (Clean and Own)
idea-plugin.description:
Folder Structure Generator Plugin

Overview

Folder Structure Generator is a powerful plugin designed to help developers quickly set up and manage folder structures like Clean Architecture. It allows users to define custom structures using a simple JSON format within the settings panel, making it highly flexible and adaptable to different project architectures.

Features

  • Multiple Configuration Templates: Choose from different architecture templates like Clean Architecture, MVC, and more.
  • Customizable Structures: Define your own folder structures using JSON.
  • User-Friendly Settings Panel: Modify and manage folder structures with ease.
  • Dynamic File Naming: Use $feature in file names to automatically replace with your feature name.
  • Supports Multiple Architectures: Adaptable to various architectural patterns.

Installation

  1. Download and install the plugin.
  2. Open your project and access the plugin settings in tools section.
  3. Define or select a folder structure template.

Usage

  1. Right click on any folder in your project.
  2. Select Structured Folder from New in the context menu.
  3. Choose your desired folder structure template from the submenu.
  4. Enter feature name (e.g., "home").

Dynamic File Naming

You can use the $feature variable in your file names, which will be replaced with the feature name you enter. For example:

  • If you define a file named $featurePage and enter "home" as your feature name, the file will be created as homePage.dart.
  • This makes it easy to create standardized file naming conventions across your project.

Multiple Configuration Templates

The plugin now supports multiple configuration templates that you can manage in the settings:

  • Switch between different architecture styles (Clean Architecture, MVC, etc.)
  • Add your own custom templates
  • Edit existing templates to suit your needs
  • Select the appropriate template directly from the context menu

Default Clean Architecture Template

The plugin comes with a predefined Clean Architecture structure. Below is an example JSON configuration:

{
  "domain": {
    "type": "d",
    "children": {
      "repository": { "type": "d" },
      "entities": { "type": "d" }
    }
  },
  "data": {
    "type": "d",
    "children": {
      "datasources": { "type": "d" },
      "dtoes": { "type": "d" },
      "repositories": { "type": "d" }
    }
  },
  "presentation": {
    "type": "d",
    "children": {
      "pages": {
        "type": "d",
        "children": {
          "$featurePage": { "type": "f", "ext": "dart" }
        }
      },
      "components": { "type": "d" },
      "providers": { "type": "d" }
    }
  }
}

Customization

You can define your own structures by modifying the JSON configuration. The format follows these rules:

  • Folders: Defined with { "type": "d" }.
  • Files: Defined with { "type": "f", "ext": "<extension>" }.
  • Nested Folders: Use the children property to define subdirectories.
  • Dynamic Names: Use $feature in file names for automatic replacement.

Example:

{
  "src": {
    "type": "d",
    "children": {
      "utils": { "type": "d" },
      "$feature_main": { "type": "f", "ext": "dart" }
    }
  }
}

Contributing

  1. Fork the repository.
  2. Create a new branch (feature/my-feature).
  3. Commit your changes.
  4. Push to the branch.
  5. Open a pull request.

License

idea-plugin.name: MavenVersionUploadX
idea-plugin.description:
MavenVersionUploadX plugin Features:

1. Maven Project Version, Submodule, and Dependency Version Upgrade

  • The system should support the upgrade of Maven project versions, submodule versions, and dependency versions. This includes:
  • Upgrading the version of the root Maven project.
  • Upgrading the versions of all submodules within the Maven project.
  • Upgrading the versions of dependencies referenced within the Maven project.

2. Batch Upgrade of Multiple Maven Projects via ArtifactId Fuzzy Matching

  • The system should allow users to select multiple Maven projects for version upgrades through a dropdown menu in the Root Project selection. The selection should support fuzzy matching of ArtifactId to facilitate the selection of multiple Maven projects simultaneously. The system should then perform the following upgrades:
  • Upgrade the versions of the selected Maven projects.
  • Upgrade the versions of all submodules within the selected Maven projects.
  • Upgrade the versions of dependencies referenced within the selected Maven projects.

3. Automatic Version Increment for New Versions

  • The system should provide an option for automatic version incrementation when specifying new versions. This feature should:
  • Automatically generate the next version number based on the current version.
  • Allow users to specify a custom increment pattern (e.g., major, minor, patch).
  • Ensure that the new version number is unique and follows semantic versioning principles.

  • Effortlessly prepare AI prompts: Quickly gather relevant context by automatically including open files or code changes in your clipboard, making it easy to generate effective prompts for ChatGPT, Gemini, or other AI tools.
  • Powerful templates: Use configurable templates to automatically add a prefix or suffix to every copied item. Imagine instantly wrapping selected text in <strong> tags for bolding, or adding <br> tags to the end of each line for creating HTML lists.

How to Use

  • Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + S, C: Copy/Append to clipboard
  • Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + S, D: Delete all from clipboard

Install ClippS now and experience the difference!

idea-plugin.name: JSONinja
idea-plugin.description:
JSONinja is a powerful JSON processing plugin for JetBrains IDEs.
It provides advanced tools for JSON data manipulation, allowing you to work efficiently without disrupting your development workflow.

Key Features:
• JSON Prettify: Format JSON data for improved readability
• JSON Uglify: Compress JSON data into a single line for transmission or storage
• JSON Escape/Unescape: Process and restore escaped JSON strings
• JMES Path / Jayway JsonPath Support: Find and filter specific values within complex JSON data
• JSON Diff Viewer: Show diffs in an editor tab or a separate window with automatic formatting
• Multi-tab Interface: Work with multiple JSON documents simultaneously
• JSON Generator: Configure root type, depth, and counts to generate sample JSON
• Copy JSON Query: Quickly copy JsonPath/JMESPath for the current cursor position
• Advanced Formatting Options: Customize indentation size, key sorting, compact arrays, and paste formatting

[Under Development]
• Enhanced JSON Validation
• JSON Schema Support
• JSON to Various Format Converters
• History and Favorites Management

JSONinja is ideal for analyzing REST API responses, editing configuration files, and performing data transformation tasks. Streamline your JSON-related work with our intuitive and efficient interface!

The Birth of JSONinja 😄
Inspired by the need for reliable JSON tools! When we faced compatibility challenges with existing solutions after an IDE update, we saw an opportunity to create something new. Our development journey took a bit longer than expected, but we're excited to finally share JSONinja with the community. Sometimes the best tools come from personal necessity!
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • JSON Diff:
    • Compare selected JSON from an editor's context menu, or compare the whole document when nothing is selected. The source opens on the left side of the comparison.
    • Choose alphabetical object-key order or keep the left side's key order and align the right side to it. You can also align matching array elements when their order differs.
    • Turn automatic sorting on or off for each comparison, restore both sides to their text before the last sort if neither side has been edited, and rename the left and right side labels.
  • Type Conversion:
    • Convert JSON to C, C++, C#, Python, Rust, Scala, or JSDoc type declarations, and generate sample JSON from those declarations. Type-to-JSON previews for these languages also show conversion warnings.
    • Type input and generated code now have syntax highlighting for all supported languages, even without the corresponding IDE language plugins.
  • Random JSON Generation:
    • Keep separate structure and value seeds to reproduce a result with the same settings in the same JSONinja version.
    • Choose New values to change the data while keeping the same keys and value types, or New structure to generate a different shape. The dialog remembers the last successfully used settings while the project is open.

Changed

  • JSON Diff: Automatic object-key sorting is now enabled by default for new settings.
  • Icon Pack: The new Version 3 icons are the default for new settings. Versions 1 and 2 remain available in the Icon Pack setting.
  • Random JSON Generation: Generated fields now have meaningful names and matching values, such as email addresses and dates, without randomly inserted nulls. Objects within each array share the same keys and value types.
  • JSON Generation:
    • Review the expected result structure, count, format, and destination before generating. Including optional schema properties as comments selects JSON5 in the output format selector and explains why it is required.
    • Numeric fields now show range errors and enforce limits of 1–100 for object, property, and schema result counts, and 1–10 for maximum nesting depth.
  • Type Conversion Dialog: Settings now appear beside the input and preview. Preview status and destination labels show when the result is ready and whether it will replace editor text, open in a new tab, or be copied.
  • Load JSON from API: The dialog now summarizes the request and its destination, highlights and focuses invalid URL or authentication fields, and disables request settings while loading.

Fixed

  • Random JSON Generation: Arrays generated with a maximum depth of 1 now contain the requested object fields instead of depth-limit placeholders.
  • Schema-Based JSON Generation: Errors for unsupported JSON Schema dialects now use the interface language instead of always appearing in English.

idea-plugin.name: TabSplitter
idea-plugin.description:
What's TabSplitter?

This is an IntelliJ extension that allows you to horizontally split the editor.

While there are already several extensions that offer this feature, I found some of them a bit inconvenient, so I made it.

What Makes It Different

  • Implements a tab switcher that only switches files within the current editor window.
  • Allows directly splitting a file to the left side—most tools only initialize the splitter on the right.
  • Lets you jump directly to a specific splitter, instead of moving step by step.

Hotkeys

Some hotkeys may conflict with your default keymap, so you might need to customize them.

Move file rightAlt + Right

Switch to previous fileCtrl + Shift + Tab

Switch to previous file(when switching)Ctrl + Up
Toggle Current Tab SizeAlt + T
Select Tab 1Ctrl + 1
Select Tab 2Ctrl + 2
Select Tab 3Ctrl + 3
Select Tab 4Ctrl + 4
Select Tab 5Ctrl + 5
Select Tab 6Ctrl + 6
Select Tab 7Ctrl + 7
Select Tab 8Ctrl + 8
Select Tab 9Ctrl + 9

Plugin to help read and write GitHub action's workflow files.
Provide extra highlighting for:
