idea-plugin.name: Properties Placeholder Resolver
idea-plugin.description:
Property Placeholder Resolver enhances your experience when working with property files by enabling smart navigation and error detection for property references.

  • Navigation: Jump directly from property placeholders (e.g. propKey=${refToProp} or propKey=${refToProp:defaultVal}) to their declaration or usage.
  • Highlighting: Correctly highlights references: normal for valid ones, warning for unresolved.
  • Renaming: Renaming the declaration leads to automatic rename of all property references (usages). If there's a single declaration — rename refactoring can be done from usage. If there are multiple declarations it is possible to perform such refactoring only from the specific declaration (standard IDEA behavior).

Scope: A placeholder is recognized only when the referenced text can legally be used as a property key (letters, digits, dots or underscores). Any other pattern is ignored and left untouched by the plugin.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Placeholder-aware copy: When the caret sits inside a ${…} placeholder in a .properties value (with no selection), pressing Ctrl/Cmd + C now copies only the key inside the braces.
  • Settings toggle: A new checkbox “Enable placeholder-aware copy” in Settings ▸ Tools ▸ Properties Placeholder lets you turn this behavior on or off. Disabling it restores the IDE’s default copy action.

idea-plugin.name: Django PowerTools
idea-plugin.description:
IDE Plugin for Django projects

Django PowerTools adds a dedicated tool window that analyzes your Django project and presents a navigable structure of key components. It runs analysis in the background, caches results, and updates automatically on file changes.

Features

  • Django Project Structure Tool Window with comprehensive project visualization:
    • Models — classes, fields, and relationships with navigation to source and field-type icons
    • Admin — registered models and configurations with direct access to each model's Admin changelist
    • URLs — URL patterns preserving Django's processing order, grouped by prefix
    • Templates — template hierarchy grouped by app and folder path
    • Forms — ModelForms and regular forms with their fields
    • Serializers — DRF serializers with fields, read-only and nested serializer info
    • ViewSets — DRF viewsets with actions, permissions, authentication classes
    • Signals — project-defined signals and handlers; known receiver order and model-sender flows with Premium
    • Celery Tasks — tasks with queue, rate limits, retries, time limits; declared workflow relationships with Premium
    • Settings — grouped by category, with clear source availability and a project-only filter
    • Migrations — migration history with dependencies, guarded run and rollback actions, and a read-only missing-migration check
    • Static Files — static files structure grouped by path
    • Management Commands — custom commands with descriptions, run directly from context menu
  • Run management commands directly from context menu (with or without arguments)
  • Works during project indexing (DumbAware)
  • Context-aware icons for all tree nodes
  • Automatic background analysis with smart caching
  • Search analyzed Django symbols with app and component-type filters
  • Custom icons for Django-related folders
  • Quick navigation from the structure tree to source code

More info

  • meanmail.dev

Your ratings and feedback help prioritize features.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
16.0.0 (September 25, 2026)

  • Analyze large Django projects faster while keeping settings navigation accurate, with phase timings available for diagnostics.
  • Keep Django Structure analysis running for large projects while progress continues, with cancellable background work and bounded cleanup for stalled processes.
  • Refresh Signals and Celery Tasks faster in large projects while preserving runtime receiver order, sender identity and task details.
  • Keep Django Structure refreshes reliable when Python files are deleted or replaced during analysis.
  • Find serializers, ViewSets and forms in older or package-structured Django projects, navigate DRF routes to their concrete ViewSets, and associate multi-signal receivers with each declared signal.

15.0.0 (September 23, 2026)

  • Browse signal receivers and Celery tasks for free. Known execution order, model-sender flows and declared Celery workflows are marked as Premium, with access options shown only when selected explicitly.
  • Check for model changes that need migrations directly from Django Structure without creating files or changing the database.
  • Distinguish common Django model field types in Django Structure, including relationship cardinality (N:1, 1:N, 1:1, N:N) and primary keys.
  • Search Django Structure across models, URLs, templates, forms, signals, tasks, settings and more, then narrow results by app and component type.
  • Keep Django Structure current through rapid edit bursts with one trailing refresh, while discarding outdated analysis results.
  • Resolve sender models for Django built-in model signals such as post_save when Django has loaded their handlers; inspect registered receiver order with Premium.
  • With Premium, follow model sender registrations to applicable signal receivers and their source locations, with unresolved sender filters shown separately.
  • Inspect literal template inheritance and include relationships in the Templates tree, open uniquely resolved targets, and see unresolved, dynamic, or cyclic links without guessed navigation.
  • Jump from a literal template URL tag to its view when the route has one clear target.
  • Add core project navigation for Django 1.5–1.11 on Python 3 and restore analyzer imports on Python 3.8 and 3.9.
  • Preserve Django URL resolution order through nested includes and show when Django 4.x does not execute async signal receivers.
  • Open registered models directly in Django Admin from the structure tree.
  • See when a setting has no exact source line, including dynamic settings with unrelated same-name assignments; filter to project-defined settings directly inside the Settings tree and keep reliable navigation for settings with a known source.
  • Find signals and Celery tasks in stable groups; Premium shows known receiver order and declared task sequences or parallel branches. Uncertain order is identified without guessing.

14.0.0 (August 21, 2026)

  • Improved migration workflow — refined the experience after generating a migration SQL preview.
  • Migration quick actions — run or roll back a selected migration from the Django Structure tree with current-state validation and explicit rollback confirmation.

13.0.0 (April 15, 2026)

  • NEW: Trie-based URL tree — URLs are now displayed as a hierarchical tree built from path segments, with automatic collapsing of single-child chains. Works correctly with i18n prefixes and any URL depth.
  • NEW: Context-aware URL icons — folder groups, root URLs (/), named endpoints, and namespace nodes each have distinct icons.
  • NEW: Static files follow Django resolution order — static files now mirror collectstatic resolution (STATICFILES_DIRS first, then app dirs), with override detection matching the Templates behavior.
  • NEW: Native file type icons — static files and templates show their actual file type icon (CSS, JS, HTML, etc.) matching the IDE Project tree.
  • NEW: Async middleware indicator — middleware with async_capable or __acall__ shows an "async" prefix in the tree.
  • FIXED: VfsUtil deadlock — synchronous VFS refresh under read lock caused deadlocks; switched to non-refreshing file lookup.
  • FIXED: Redundant analysis failure notification — removed balloon notification since errors are already shown in the tool window.

12.0.0 (April 12, 2026)

  • FIXED: ModelForm discovery on Django 6+ — ModelForm no longer inherits from Form in Django 6; the analyzer now uses BaseForm as the common ancestor, so all ModelForm subclasses appear in the Forms section.
  • FIXED: Missing tree nodes when file resolution fails — forms, serializers, viewsets, signals, and celery tasks are now displayed even when their source file cannot be resolved, instead of being silently dropped.
  • IMPROVED: Templates follow Django resolution order — the Templates section now mirrors the exact order Django uses to resolve template names (DIRS first, then APP_DIRS in INSTALLED_APPS order).
  • NEW: Template override detection — when a template overrides another (same relative name in a higher-priority root), the overridden template is shown under a separate "Overridden" node with the source of the override.
  • IMPROVED: Cleaner Templates tree — project-level templates from DIRS are shown directly under the Templates node without a redundant "Project" wrapper.

11.0.0 (April 6, 2026)

  • FIXED: Missing static files — projects using Django's tuple format in STATICFILES_DIRS (e.g. ("prefix", "/path")) now correctly display all static files.
  • IMPROVED: URL tree display — grouped URLs no longer show a redundant prefix in child entries, making the tree cleaner and easier to read.
  • IMPROVED: URL error resilience — a single broken URL pattern no longer prevents the rest of the URLs from being displayed.

10.0.0 (March 29, 2026)

  • Smoother startup experience — the Django Structure panel now appears populated right away and then refreshes automatically in the background.
  • Clearer Settings section — the settings module name appears more reliably and the Settings icon is displayed correctly.
  • More reliable Settings navigation — opening a setting now leads to the source that Django actually uses at runtime, including project files, default Django settings, and third-party modules.
  • More complete Templates view — template roots are now aligned with Django runtime loaders, including project overrides and installed app templates.
  • Improved Signals and Celery Tasks detection — better discovery in real-world codebases with wrappers and custom wiring patterns.
  • New Migrations view modes — switch between grouping by application and migration-plan order.
  • Faster Migrations workflow — migration display mode can now be changed directly from the Migrations node context menu.
  • Clearer Celery Tasks structure — modules are grouped by parent module and sorted alphabetically for easier scanning.
  • Better stability with other meanmail plugins — reduced startup conflicts when multiple plugins are installed.
  • More responsive UI — improved behavior in places that could previously feel temporarily stuck.
  • Improved diagnostics and error reporting — issues are now surfaced more consistently to make troubleshooting easier.

  • NEW: Error status banner in Django Structure panel — analysis errors are now displayed directly in the panel instead of only as notification balloons
  • IMPROVED: Error diagnostics — detailed error messages for common issues (missing interpreter, Django not installed, settings misconfiguration)
  • IMPROVED: Python error reporting — setup errors are always captured in stderr for better troubleshooting

  • FIXED: Scheduled task cleanup — periodic refresh task is now properly cancelled on dispose, preventing work on disposed components
  • FIXED: Excessive error logging — non-Django projects no longer produce error-level log entries for missing interpreter/project root

  • NEW: DRF ViewSets support — display viewsets with actions, HTTP methods, permissions, authentication classes

idea-plugin.name: OpenAPI GUI Editor
idea-plugin.description:
Visual editor for OpenAPI 3.0, 3.1, and 3.2.

  • Convenient editing of complex schemas.
  • Guided editing that makes common OpenAPI mistakes harder.
  • Easy navigation through complex documents.
  • One-click example generation based on referenced schemas.
  • Tested on real-world OpenAPI documents.
  • Actively maintained with quick bug fixes.

Update May 10, 2026: Now supports OpenAPI 3.2!

Why does the plugin exist?

While the OpenAPI (formerly Swagger) specification was initially designed to be human-editable, it has grown increasingly complex over time. Even with syntax highlighting and robust autocompletion tools, creating and maintaining OpenAPI documents remains challenging. The verbose format is easy to get lost in and requires familiarity with numerous technical details.

OpenAPI GUI Editor solves these problems by providing an intuitive visual interface that allows you to create and modify valid OpenAPI documents in seconds - no deep specification knowledge required.

Restrictions

  • The plugin supports OpenAPI 3.0, 3.1, and 3.2 documents.
  • If your openapi.yml references multiple files, the plugin will only work with the main one.

Issues

If you have any problems or ideas of improvements, please feel free to create a new issue on Github or contact me personally on Telegram (@antonokolelov).

idea-plugin.name: Select Content Pair
idea-plugin.description:
Select Pair Content is a JetBrains IDE plugin that allows you to quickly select content within a file. It has two main functions:

  • Selecting content between matching pairs of tokens such as parentheses (), brackets [], braces {}, quotes '' "" ` `, and angle brackets <>.
  • Select content based on the underlying PSI Elements that make up a file.

For both pair and element based selection, the plugin supports expanding a selection and shrinking it. Repeated invocations of the plugin action will expand out the given selection. Exact behavior is determined by the given action as follows:

  • Pair Select
    • Expand: Repeated expand action invocations will expand out the selection to the next pair of matching tokens.
    • Shrink: Repeated shrink action invocations will shrink the selection to the next pair of matching tokens within the existing selection.
  • Element Select
    • Expand: Repeated expand action invocations will select the given element's parent element.
    • Shrink:Repeated shrink action invocations will shrink the selection to the given element's child element that contains the caret.

Keyboard Shortcuts

ActionWindows/LinuxMacOS
Expand Pair Content SelectionAlt+QOption+Q
Shrink Pair Content SelectionAlt+AOption+A
Expand Element SelectionAlt+WOption+W
Shrink Element SelectionAlt+SOption+S

idea-plugin.name: AEM VLT Tool
idea-plugin.description:
The AEM VLT IntelliJ Plugin is an integration tool for developers working with Adobe Experience Manager (AEM). It provides a seamless way to push data (files, configurations) from your project (file system) to the AEM repository and pull data from the AEM repository to your project on the file system.

This plugin relies on the Apache Jackrabbit File Vault library to handle content synchronization between your local environment and AEM instances.

✨ Features

  • Push to AEM: Easily push content from your local file system to AEM repository
  • Pull from AEM: Quickly pull content from AEM repository to your local file system
  • Multiple Server Support: Configure and manage multiple AEM server connections
  • Progress Tracking: Visual progress indicators for push and pull operations
  • Detailed Results: Get detailed operation results with statistics on added, updated, and deleted files
  • Context Menu Integration: Access AEM operations directly from the project view context menu

🔧 Installation

Using the IDE built-in plugin system:

  1. Open your IntelliJ IDEA
  2. Navigate to Settings/Preferences → Plugins → Marketplace
  3. Search for "AEM VLT Tool"
  4. Click Install

Using JetBrains Marketplace:

  1. Go to JetBrains Marketplace
  2. Click the Install to ... button

Manual Installation:

  1. Download the latest release
  2. In IntelliJ IDEA, go to Settings/Preferences → Plugins → ⚙️ → Install plugin from disk...
  3. Select the downloaded plugin file

🚀 Usage

Configuration

  1. Go to Settings/Preferences > AEM VLT Settings
  2. Add your AEM server configurations:
    • Server Name (e.g AEM Author)
    • URL
    • Username and Password
    • Set as default (optional)

Push Content to AEM

  1. Right-click on a file or directory in the Project view
  2. Select AEM VLT → Push to AEM (Default)
  3. If multiple servers are configured, select the target server
  4. The plugin will push the content to the corresponding path in AEM

Pull Content from AEM

  1. Right-click on a file or directory in the Project view
  2. Select AEM VLT → Pull from AEM (Default)
  3. If multiple servers are configured, select the source server
  4. The plugin will pull the content from the corresponding path in AEM

idea-plugin.name: EzMode
idea-plugin.description:
Modal editing without the steep learning curve.

What is modal editing?

In a modal editor, keys that normally insert characters can perform different actions based on the current mode.

For example, in EzMode you can press a to select a word, and c to copy it. This is less work than double-clicking with your mouse and pressing Ctrl-c.

Then how do I type?

Press t to enter type mode, and press Tab to go back to ez mode.

So it's like Vim?

Yes, but a lot simpler. EzMode focuses just on modes. It does not:

  • use any Ctrl or Alt shortcuts
  • use a block cursor
  • change how copy/paste works
  • use hjkl for arrow keys. EzMode uses ijkl.

EzMode is built for modern IDEs. It works well with viewing diffs, using multi-cursor, and managing tool windows.

More info on GitHub

idea-plugin.name: Reader
idea-plugin.description:
Reader

A lightweight reader plugin for JetBrains IDEs that supports viewing PDF, EPUB, text, and Markdown files directly within the IDE. It provides two viewing modes: a tool window panel for opening any file from the filesystem, and an integrated editor tab for PDF files opened from the project tree. Designed to give engineers a more convenient reading experience (and make it easier to browse and relax).

Core Features

  • PDF File Viewing: High-quality PDF rendering powered by Apache PDFBox. Supports zoom in/out, fit-to-width, page navigation (mouse wheel, keyboard arrows, direct page input), page rotation, opacity adjustment, centered display with mouse drag panning, and integrated editor tab via Chromium.
  • EPUB File Viewing: Renders EPUB book content in an embedded Chromium browser within the tool window.
  • Text File Viewing: Supports loading local TXT files with adjustable font size.
  • Markdown File Viewing: Supports previewing local Markdown files with Mermaid diagram rendering (offline and theme-configurable).
  • Internationalization: Supports 7 languages: 简体中文, English, Deutsch, Français, 日本語, 한국어, Русский.
  • Dual Viewing Modes: Tool window (right sidebar) for any supported file, and editor tab integration for PDF files in the project tree.

Contact Us

Under continuous development; feedback and suggestions are welcome.

Contact: wocaishiryr@163.com

Reader

一款轻量级的 JetBrains IDE 阅读器插件，支持在 IDE 中直接查看 PDF、EPUB、文本和 Markdown 文件。提供两种查看模式：工具窗口面板（可从文件系统打开任意文件）和集成编辑器标签页（从项目树打开 PDF 文件）。旨在为各位工程师提供更加方便的阅（方）读（便）体（摸）验（鱼）。

主要功能

  • PDF文件查看： 基于 Apache PDFBox 的高质量 PDF 渲染。支持缩放、自适应宽度、页面导航（鼠标滚轮、键盘方向键、直接输入页码）、页面旋转、透明度调整、居中展示与鼠标拖动平移，以及通过 Chromium 的编辑器标签页集成。
  • EPUB文件查看： 在工具窗口内通过内嵌 Chromium 浏览器渲染 EPUB 书籍内容。
  • 文本文件查看： 支持加载本地 TXT 文件，可调节字体大小。
  • Markdown文件查看： 支持预览本地 Markdown 文件，支持 Mermaid 图表渲染（离线与主题可配置）。
  • 国际化： 支持7种语言：简体中文、English、Deutsch、Français、日本語、한국어、Русский。
  • 双模式查看： 右侧边栏工具窗口支持打开任意格式文件，项目树中的 PDF 文件可直接在编辑器标签页中打开。

联系我们

持续更新中，欢迎反馈建议

联系方式：wocaishiryr@163.com

idea-plugin.name: Kotlin Compiler DevKit
idea-plugin.description:
This plugin enhances the development experience when working with compiler tests in the Kotlin project or Kotlin compiler plugins.

Setup

The plugin enhances the editor for .kt files located in directories specified in the plugin settings. These settings are stored per project in .idea/kotlinTestDataPluginTestDataPaths.xml.

The plugin identifies related test files using the following convention: for a test file named someName.kt, all files that begin with someName. are considered related and will appear in the left combo box of the split mode view. You can configure the plugin to search for related files in additional locations beyond the test file's directory. This feature is particularly useful when working with Kotlin/JS tests, where you might want to view generated code alongside the test file.

The plugin identifies test methods for the opened file using these rules:

  1. For a test file named someName.kt, the corresponding test method should be named testSomeName and marked with a test annotation (e.g., @Test from JUnit)
  2. The test method must be annotated with @org.jetbrains.kotlin.test.TestMetadata, with the filename as its argument: @TestMetadata("someName.kt")
  3. The class containing the test method must also be annotated with @TestMetadata, where the argument specifies the path to the directory containing someName.kt

The plugin scans your project for methods meeting these conditions and adds run configuration buttons to the editor toolbar.

Features

Test Data Editor

When opening a test data file, the special editor can be opened using the tabs in the bottom left (1).

It allows opening a related file in a split view in addition to the main file (2). The button with the arrows will open a diff between the two files.

In the top right, a toolbar (3) can be found that offers the following features:

  • Selecting a test runner
  • Running or debugging the test using the selected runner
  • Going to a runner source
  • Running the test with all runners
  • Reloading test runners
  • Regenerating test runners (will run the generateTests Gradle task or an optimized set of tasks for diagnostic tests)
  • Running one or all test runners and applying diffs (see Apply Diffs), optionally after regenerating tests
  • Create a reproducer commit (see "Create Reproducer Commit")

Run Tests from Various Menus

Using the context menu of one or multiple files or directories containing test data files (e.g. in the Project tool window, in breadcrumbs, in VCS), you can run or debug the test(s) using one or all test runners (1).

In the commit tool window, an action (2) is available to run all tests on all modified test data files.

Apply Diffs

When tests fail with assertion errors related to files, the diffs can be applied using the context menu in the test tool window. It works on individual tests, groups of tests or all tests.

Create Reproducer Commit

This action will

  • prompt you for a ticket number
  • generate tests
  • rerun tests until they are green
  • apply diffs
  • commit changes with the commit message

[Tests] Reproduce #KT-XXX

If tests fail without a diff or applying diffs leads to a conflict, it will ask you to resolve the problems before continuing.

This action is also available in the three dots menu in the editor.

Running Tests from Arbitrary Modules

The plugin adds a Run Anything provider that introduces a command testGlobally. It accepts a sequence of test filters, finds the relevant modules and then calls their :test Gradle tasks with the relevant filters.

The syntax is: testGlobally [--tests <pattern>]*. For example: testGlobally --tests 'a.b.Test$Sub.testSomething' --tests a.b.*.

There's a limitation, though: the packages must be fully specified, and only their initial part that doesn't contain wildcards will be considered for searching for the relevant modules. Also note that specifying a filter without a package (--tests SomeTestGenerated) will result in all modules with test source sets being called via :test. The algorithm searches for the relevant module by comparing the package with the directory structure, and the empty package represents the source set root which is always present for every source set.

Copying Test Data without Metadata

This action will copy the selected testdata text in the editor with stripped metadata: diagnostics and tags like <caret>, <expr>, <selection>. You can also assign a custom shortcut to this action.

Rebasing and Checkout on Green master Commit

Note: Requires the bundled Git plugin to be enabled.

Rebase onto the Latest Green master

Rebases the current branch onto the latest successfully built commit from master. All pending local changes are automatically stashed.

Reset to the Latest Green Commit

Resets the master branch to the latest successfully built commit. Doesn't modify or change the current branch.

idea-plugin.name: cteXecutor
idea-plugin.description:
Execute a single CTE, subquery, or UNION branch directly from the editor in DataGrip and IntelliJ-based IDEs, without manually assembling the surrounding WITH clause.

Execute from Here resolves the CTEs a statement depends on and lets you run, edit, or copy any step in that chain. Navigate Dependency Graph shows what a statement depends on and what depends on it.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
4.0.0 - 2026-09-17

feat

  • Navigate Dependency Graph action, showing dependencies and consumers of the statement at the caret, navigable with the same shortcuts as Execute from Here
  • Execute from Here now shows the current statement and its needed CTEs as a single navigable list instead of a flat popup, with fixed numbering that follows the focused row
  • E (insert into editor) and C (copy to clipboard) shortcuts inside both popups, acting on whichever row is currently focused

fix

  • Editing a statement now places the cursor at its original position within the inserted SQL where possible, instead of always at the end
  • Dependency and correlation analysis now uses PSI reference resolving instead of name matching, correctly handling nested WITH clauses with shadowed CTE names, WITH RECURSIVE self-references, and uncorrelated subqueries
  • A recursive CTE executed on its own no longer produces invalid SQL with an undefined self-reference
  • Dependencies shown in Navigate Dependency Graph are now ordered by their position in the file; the one closest to the current statement is shown nearest to it instead of farthest away
  • Navigating the dependency graph from a keyboard shortcut no longer risks a threading assertion failure

break

  • Removed the separate Copy CT-Query SQL and Edit and Run SQL actions; their functionality is now available as E and C shortcuts inside Execute from Here and Navigate Dependency Graph

  • Execute from Here no longer has a Ctrl+# then Space alternate shortcut; Ctrl+# then Enter remains

  • Execute from Here now falls back to the standard execute shortcut if code is already selected, instead of showing the dependency popup

  • Navigate Dependency Graph shortcut changed from Ctrl+# then N to Ctrl+# then D

idea-plugin.name: Context Copier
idea-plugin.description:
Copy multiple files into one shareable text block.

Context Copier combines selected files, folders, or eligible local editor tabs with labeled file boundaries. Use the result in a code review, issue, document, or coding assistant.

  • Include unsaved changes from open editors.
  • Choose full or short file headers. Both keep the source text unchanged.
  • Preview the output in a temporary, read-only plain-text tab without creating a file or changing the clipboard.
  • Copy the filtered project file list as JSON and as one path per line.

Read through the result

Set a pace in seconds per visible screen and scroll continuously, with two lines of overlap. Pause, resume, change direction, or adjust the pace using the floating controls. Manual editor input pauses paced scrolling. Esc stops it.

Middle-click auto-scroll is off by default. Enable it in Settings > Tools > Context Copier to control speed and direction by moving the pointer. On Linux, this replaces middle-click paste in the code area.

Know what you are sharing

Exports use project-relative paths; external files receive anonymous path aliases. Common credential filenames, generated folders, symbolic links, binary files, IDE exclusions, and positive project .gitignore rules are skipped. Ignore negations do not restore excluded files, and global Git ignore rules are not read.

Limits are 500 files, 1 MiB per file, and 5 MiB of source text per export. Large or filtered selections offer a review step. Cancellation and failed exports leave the clipboard unchanged. Filename filters cannot catch every secret, so review the output before sharing it.

File contents are processed locally. The plugin does not upload source code or send usage analytics. Optional support-request timing uses counters stored only on your computer.

idea-plugin.name: Vim AnyObject
idea-plugin.description:
Vim AnyObject

Edit code the way you think it

An extension for IdeaVim plugin that adds useful text objects to improve your productivity on JetBrains IDEs.

Text objects provide a more natural way to tell the editor what to edit, select or jump. Instead of working with characters, words, lines, or paragraphs, you can use the same concepts programmers use to think about code: classes, functions, arguments, loops, comments, quotes, brackets, subwords, and more.

Available Text Objects

Text ObjectDescriptionDefault mappingCount motions
AnyArgumentFunction arguments, method parameters, and callable expressionsa✓
AnyFunctionFunctions, methods, and proceduresfx
AnyLambdaOrFunctionFunctions, methods, procedures, lambdas and arrow functionsmx
AnyClassClass, interface, struct, and similar type definitionscx
AnyVariableField/variable declarations and assignmentsvx
AnyLoopLoop statements (for, while, do, repeat, until, loop, etc.)lx
AnyConditionalConditional statements (if-else, switch, try-catch)yx
AnyItemItems within collections, tuples, lists, or arraysi✓
AnyArgOrItemCombines objects targeted by AnyArgument and AnyItemx✓
AnyQuoteContent enclosed between any type of quotes (single, double, backticks)q✗
AnyStringString contentg✗
AnyBracketContent enclosed between any type of brackets (parentheses, square, curly, angle, etc.)o✗
AnySubwordWords nested in longer words (camelCase, snake_case, dash-case)u✓
AnyDocumentEntire document contentd✗
AnyCommentComments across different programming languages (/* */, <!-- -->, etc.)k✗
AnyIndentBlockCode blocks based on indentation levelsn✗
  • Inner/Outer: All text objects support both i (inner) and a (around/outer) selection modes following standard Vim conventions
  • Jump: All text objects allow navigation using ] (next) and [ (previous) motions unless other mappings are specified (see Customization)
  • Count motions: Text objects with count support allow selecting multiple consecutive instances. For example d2aa will delete two arguments including their separators

Usage

Deletion, Change, Visual Selection

The plugin follows standard Vim text object conventions with i (inner) and a (around) modifiers

Jump

The plugin supports jumping to the next/previous text object using ] (next) and [ (previous). A common use case is to visually select an argument vaa, and jump to next ones to extend the selection ]a. This is analogous to count visual selection (i.e. v3aa)

Example with argument text object (a)

  • dia - Delete argument
  • daa - Delete argument and its separator
  • d2ia - Deletes argument and the next without including separators
  • cia - Change argument
  • caa - Change argument and its separator
  • c2aa - Change argument and next one including separator
  • yia - Yank/Copy argument
  • yaa - Yank/Copy argument and its separator
  • via - Visually select argument
  • v3aa - Visually select three arguments including separator
  • v3ia - Visually select three arguments without including separator
  • ]a - Jump to next argument
  • [a - Jump to previous argument

Provided text objects

AnySubword (u)

Nested words in different case styles:

Case typeExample
Camel casefooBar
Snake casefoo_bar
Dash casefoo-bar

AnyQuote (q)

Content enclosed between any type of quotes:

Quote TypeExample
Single quotes'text'
Double quotes"text"
Backticks`text`

AnyBracket (o)

Content enclosed between any type of brackets:

Bracket TypeExampleDescription
Parentheses(text)Function calls, grouping
Square brackets[text]Arrays, indexing
Curly braces{text}Objects, code blocks
Angle brackets<text>Generics
HTML/XML brackets<text/>HTML/XML tags, generics

AnyDocument (d)

Entire document content.

AnyComment (k)

Comments across different programming languages:

Comment TypeLanguagesExample
/* */, //C, C++, Java, C#, JavaScript, TypeScript, Kotlin, Scala, Swift, Go, Rust, PHP, CSS, SQL/* comment */
/** */Java (Javadoc), Rust (doc comments)/** documentation */
<!-- -->HTML, XML, XHTML, Markdown<!-- comment -->
""" """, #Python (docstrings)"""comment"""
''' '''Python (docstrings)'''comment'''
--[[ ]]Lua--[[ comment ]]
--[=[ ]=]Lua (custom delimiters)--[=[ comment ]=]
#' to 'R (roxygen comments)#' comment '

AnyString (g)

String data to assign to a variable or field.

  • Inner selection (ig): Selects only the string content
  • Outer selection (ag): Selects the entire string including quotes and leading formatting symbols

AnyItem (i)

Items within collections, tuples, lists, or arrays:

Structure TypeExample
Arrays[item1, item2, item3]
List literals(item1, item2, item3)
  • Inner selection (ii): Selects only the item itself
  • Outer selection (ai): Selects the entire item including the separator and the item itself

Multiple outer selections are supported. For example d2ai will delete the current item and the next one including separator

AnyArgument (a)

Function arguments, method parameters, and callable expressions.

  • Inner selection (ia): Selects only the argument itself
  • Outer selection (ia): Selects the entire argument including the separator and the argument itself

Multiple outer selections are supported. For example d2aa will delete the current argument and the next one including separator

AnyArgOrItem (x)

Combines objects targeted by AnyArgument and AnyItem. Selects any function argument, method parameter, callable expression, or collection items.

AnyVariable (v)

Field/variable declarations and assignments.

  • Inner selection (iv): Selects only the value assigned to the field/variable if any
  • Outer selection (av): Selects the entire field/variable declaration

AnyFunction (f)

Functions, methods, and procedures.

  • Inner selection (if): Selects only the function body
  • Outer selection (af): Selects the entire function including the function name, decorators, and the body

AnyLambdaOrFunction (m)

Extends AnyFunction to include lambda or arrow functions.

AnyClass (c)

Class, interface, struct, and similar type definitions.

  • Inner selection (ic): Selects only the class body
  • Outer selection (ac): Selects the entire class including the name, decorators, and the body

AnyLoop (l)

Loop statements and iterative constructs like for, foreach, while, until, do, repeat, until, loop, for, foreach, while, until, do, repeat, until, loop.

  • Inner Selection (il): Selects only the statements within the current loop/iteration where the cursor is positioned
  • Outer Selection (al): Selects the entire loop construct including all branches and control keywords

AnyConditional (y)

Conditional statements and expressions like if-else, switch or try-catch statements.

  • Inner Selection (iy): Selects only the statements within the current branch/case where the cursor is positioned
  • Outer Selection (ay): Selects the entire conditional construct including all branches and control keywords

AnyIndentBlock (n)

Code blocks based on indentation levels. This is particularly useful for indentation-based languages like Python, YAML, or Haskell, but also works with brace-based languages to select logical indentation blocks.

  • Inner Selection (in): Selects from first to last character of the current block
  • Outer Selection (an): Selects entire lines of the current block

Configuration

Configure which transformation groups to enable in your .ideavimrc:

" Activate plugin
set anyobject

Customization

Don't want to use all the provided text objects? Specify which ones to enable using anyobject_included variable in your .ideavimrc:

let g:anyobject_included = "anyDocument,anyFunction"

If you prefer to specify which ones to exclude, use the anyobject_excluded variable instead:

let g:anyobject_excluded = "anyDocument,anyFunction"

You can also customize the mappings by adding the following to your .ideavimrc. For example:

" Use 'm' instead of default 'f' for any function text object
let g:anyobject_map_anyfunction = "m"

" Use 's' instead of default 'd' for any document text object
let g:anyobject_map_anydocument = "s"

In case of mapping conflicts, the custom mappings will take precedence and invalidate any other handler using the same mapping.

Jump motion can be also customized:

" Use '<' instead of default '[' for jumping to the previous text object
let g:anyobject_map_jump_prev = "<" 

" Use '>' instead of default ']' for jumping to the next text object
let g:anyobject_map_jump_next = ">"

idea-plugin.name: Project Identifier
idea-plugin.description:
Project Identifier helps you tell multiple IDE projects apart by adding a subtle, low-opacity text watermark to the editor background.

🌟 What It Does

The IntelliJ Project Identifier plugin solves a simple problem for developers who work with many projects at once: telling them apart at a glance.

When you open a project, this plugin automatically adds a unique text identifier—derived from the project's name—as a subtle, low-opacity background watermark. This allows you to quickly distinguish between different IDE windows when using a task switcher like the Windows key or Alt+Tab.

⚙️ How It Works

The plugin automates the process of creating and applying a visual identifier. It works by:

  1. Listening for project open events.
  2. Taking the project's name to generate a short text string.
  3. Programmatically creating a transparent PNG image with this text and saving it to a local directory.
  4. Using the IDE's internal API to set this newly created image as the editor background for the current project.

Any changes to the plugin's settings will trigger this process again, creating a new image and updating the background automatically. The generated image file is stored locally, but you are free to edit the background image setting at any time.

📋 Plugin Settings

The plugin provides a simple configuration panel to customize the identifier's behavior. You can access it via File | Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Project Identifier Settings.

The settings are split into two sections:

  • Project Identifier Settings: Global settings that apply to all projects.
  • Project Settings: Settings specific to the current project, nested under the main settings menu.

🔀 Dynamic placeholders

In the per-project Identifier override field you can embed placeholders that are resolved automatically. Type ${branch} (for example XXX - ${branch}) to include the current Git branch in the watermark. The watermark refreshes automatically when you switch branches. If the project is not a Git repository (or is on a detached HEAD), ${branch} resolves to an empty string.

idea-plugin.name: DebugMate
idea-plugin.description:
Introduction

DebugMate is an IntelliJ IDEA companion plugin that enhances database debugging and runtime configuration by surfacing SQL/Mongo execution details, keeping project views tidy, and aligning launch settings with team conventions.

Features

  • SQL/Mongo log insights: Captures execution parameters, timing, and code locations, while providing one-click copying from the console for rapid sharing and investigation.
  • Automatic directory exclusion: Removes noisy folders such as module-level logs from the project view and search results to maintain focus.
  • Readable properties files: Displays Unicode content as human-readable text in properties files to simplify editing.
  • Consistent launch configuration: Applies ShortenCommandLine policies automatically so large projects start without manual adjustments.
  • Environment variable injection: Pushes custom variables into Java processes at either global or project scope to synchronize local debugging environments.
  • MyBatis XML hot reload: Propagates mapper edits instantly through the built-in DMA module so you can verify SQL tweaks without restarting the IDE run config.
  • DMA plugin control: Pick which agent modules (jdbc-logger, mongo-logger, mybatis-hotswap) stay active per environment using the new multi-select dropdown with instant status summaries.
  • Configurable Java breakpoints: Choose whether new Java breakpoints suspend the current thread, all threads, or follow the IDE default to match team workflows.

Getting Started

  1. Install DebugMate and open the IDE settings to inherit or override logging, exclusion, encoding, command line, and environment preferences.
  2. Add team-specific directory patterns and environment variables, then apply the configuration.
  3. Run any Java application to view copy-ready SQL/Mongo logs in the console while the workspace stays clean and consistent.

简介

DebugMate 面向 IntelliJ IDEA 开发者，提供数据库调试与运行配置增强能力，可展示 SQL/Mongo 调用细节、保持项目视图整洁，并自动同步团队约定的启动策略。

功能亮点

  • SQL/Mongo 日志洞察：记录执行参数、耗时与代码调用位置，控制台点击即可复制完整语句，便于联调与问题追踪。
  • 自动排除目录：批量排除各模块下的 logs 等噪音目录，避免干扰工程视图与全局搜索。
  • Properties 中文展示：自动将 properties 文件中的 Unicode 内容以可读中文呈现，提升编辑效率。
  • 启动项命令行治理：统一应用 ShortenCommandLine 规则，解决大型项目每次启动都要手动配置的烦恼。
  • 环境变量注入：支持全局或项目级向 Java 程序注入自定义环境变量，保持多环境调试配置一致。
  • MyBatis XML 热重载：内置 DMA 模块可实时刷新 Mapper 变更，无需重启运行配置即可验证 SQL 调整。
  • DMA 模块按需启停：通过新的多选下拉框随时选择启用 jdbc-logger、mongo-logger、mybatis-hotswap 模块，并即时查看摘要状态。
  • 断点挂起策略：为新建的 Java 断点选择挂起当前线程、挂起全部线程或沿用 IDE 默认，适配不同联调模式。

快速开始

  1. 安装 DebugMate 后，在 IDE 设置页选择继承或自定义日志、目录排除、编码、命令行与环境变量策略。
  2. 补充团队需要的排除模式和环境变量后保存配置。
  3. 运行 Java 应用，即可在控制台查看可复制的 SQL/Mongo 日志，并体验整洁一致的工作空间。

idea-plugin.name: Firebase Pro
idea-plugin.description:
Firebase Pro provides rich language support, validation, navigation, and tooling for Firebase configuration and rules files.

Gain a comprehensive suite of Firebase development features directly in your favorite IDE:

  • Smart file recognition for Firebase configuration, rules, and indexes files
  • Context-aware completion for all Firebase-specific languages
  • Built-in schema validation for correctness
  • Powerful inspections and quick fixes for error prevention
  • Seamless navigation, documentation, and structure views
  • Customizable formatting and color schemes for a better development experience

Supports the majority of the Firebase products:

  • Firebase Configuration (firebase.json): file recognition, documentation, validation, completion, navigation, and more.
  • Firestore security rules: file recognition, documentation, completion, inspection, navigation, formatting, highlighting, structuring, and more.
  • Firestore indexes: file recognition, documentation, completion, validation, and more.
  • Storage security rules: file recognition, documentation, completion, inspection, navigation, formatting, highlighting, structuring, and more.
  • Realtime database: file recognition, documentation, completion, inspection, navigation, formatting, highlighting, structuring, and more.
  • Remote config: file recognition, documentation, completion, validation, and more.
  • Data Connect: file recognition, documentation, completion, inspection, navigation, validation, and more.
  • Firebase Extension: file recognition, documentation, completion, validation, and more.
  • Firebase Runtime Configuration (.firebaserc): file recognition, documentation, completion, validation, and more.
  • Firebase Local Emulators: start any or all local emulators directly from your favorite IDE!

This plugin streamlines Firebase configuration and rule authoring, reducing errors and improving productivity for teams working with Firebase-backed projects.

Firebase configuration file (firebase.json)

File recognition

The plugin automatically recognizes the firebase.json file in the root directory of your project.
Once detected, the file icon is replaced with a distinctive Firebase-specific icon, making it easily identifiable as the Firebase configuration file.

Completion

Enjoy intelligent code completion for your firebase.json configuration.
The plugin provides context-aware suggestions for available keys and values — for example, typing "data" at the top level suggests "dataconnect" and "database".
This helps configure Firebase faster and more accurately.

Reference

Clickable references are provided for filenames linked within the Firebase configuration.
When you reference files such as Firestore rules, Firestore indexes, Storage rules, or Realtime Database rules (e.g., "firestore.rules"), clicking the filename opens that file directly in the editor.

Inspection

The plugin includes multiple inspections to help detect and fix configuration issues in firebase.json:

  • Detects missing configurations for the default Firestore database.
  • Detects duplicate configurations for the same Firestore database.
  • Detects and offers quick fixes for missing Firestore Rules, Firestore Indexes, Storage Rules, and Realtime Database Rules files automatically creating them with default templates.

These and many other inspections help maintain a consistent and valid Firebase setup across your project.

Schema Validation

The plugin validates that your firebase.json file adheres to Firebase’s official schema.
It checks for invalid or missing properties to ensure the configuration is complete and deploy-ready.

Firebase Security Rules

File recognition

The plugin recognizes any *.rules files defined in the firebase.json file.
It assigns unique icons for Firestore Security Rules and Storage Security Rules, helping you easily distinguish rule types.

Documentation

In-editor documentation is provided for all Firebase Security Rules language elements, including functions, variables, interfaces, and their properties.
For example, hovering over request.auth.token displays all authentication token properties with their descriptions.

Completion

The plugin supports intelligent completion for:

  • Built-in language constructs (functions, variables, interfaces, properties)
  • Local variables and user-defined functions
  • Path parameters
  • Service-specific keywords for Firestore and Storage

Inspection

Advanced inspections detect common issues such as:

  • Recursive or overly deep function calls
  • Invalid allow methods
  • Invalid service names
  • Incorrect type checks
  • Undefined function calls

These and many other inspections help ensure your security rules are both syntactically valid and semantically correct, reducing runtime errors and improving maintainability.

Reference

Supports navigation from function calls to their declarations and variable usages, improving readability and maintainability.

Code style (formatting)

Provides a built-in formatter for Firebase Security Rules with customizable styling options in the IDE.

Color scheme

Includes syntax highlighting for all Firebase Security Rules language elements with configurable colors and styles.

Structure view

Displays a hierarchical Structure View showing services, match blocks, and functions, allowing easy exploration of rule files.

Firestore indexes

File recognition

Recognizes Firestore index files configured in the firebase.json file and assigns a distinctive Firestore index icon for easy identification.

Completion

Provides auto-completion for Firestore index configuration keys and values.
For example, typing "co" suggests "collectionGroup".

idea-plugin.name: Ever Present Filenames
idea-plugin.description:
Displays the current file name at the bottom-right corner of the editor.

Why?

I don't like tabs, so I disable them via the Tab placement | None settings toggle. However, when you do this, and you also use split editor windows, JetBrains IDEs do not tell you what file is currently open in a given split unless that split currently has focus.

This completely resolves this problem by always showing you the filename at the bottom right of the editor view, even when that editor does not have focus.

Basically - I made this because this issue never got traction.

Features

  • Show the filename for each visible "split" in the IDE, even when tabs have been disabled.
  • Smart duplicate filename handling: shows distinguishing paths when multiple files with the same name are open
  • The UI shows when there are pending unsaved changes, as well as how many lines have been added / removed based on git diff --numstat HEAD.
  • Take the following actions using just your mouse:
    • Click on the file icon to close the file.
    • Click on the filename itself to reveal the file in the Project Outline
    • Click on the numbered diff to open the diff view for that file
    • Right-click on the filename to copy the path to the file

Configuration

Go to "Appearance" > "Ever Present Filenames" to edit the settings for the plugin.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.4.0
  • Verified compatible with the latest IntelliJ-based IDEs (up to 2026.2)

  • Rebuilt local overrides with a UI: a "Local (this machine)" scope lets you tweak, mute, or add personal tabs without editing JSON by hand
  • Overrides attach to a stable tab id (not the tab name), so renaming a shared tab no longer detaches its override
  • Live "Effective (what will run)" preview shows the merged result with each tab's source (Shared / Overridden / Personal / Orphaned)
  • One-click offer to add .terminals/startup-terminals.local.json to .gitignore
  • Per-tab environment variables (set in the shared or local layer)
  • Conditional tabs: "Open If" opens a tab only when a given project-relative path exists
  • Open any configured tab on demand from the terminal toolbar
1.3.0
  • Added local config overrides: create .terminals/startup-terminals.local.json to override individual settings from the shared config
  • Local overrides use nullable fields — only specified values replace the base config
  • Tabs matched by name: override specific tab properties without redefining the entire config
  • Info banner in settings UI when local overrides are active
  • Tab color coding: assign colors (red, green, blue, yellow, orange, purple, cyan, pink) to terminal tabs for easy identification
  • Now supports IDE versions from 2025.1 up to 2026.1
1.2.0
  • Added startup commands - execute a command when terminal opens
  • Security-focused opt-in model: commands only run if project is explicitly trusted
  • Trust setting stored locally per-machine, not in project config

idea-plugin.name: Reclaim
idea-plugin.description:
An IntelliJ IDEA plugin that integrates file deletion with your operating system's native trash or recycle bin. It replaces the default permanent deletion behaviour with a "move to trash" action, providing an extra layer of safety and preventing accidental data loss.

Features:
  • Safe File Deletion: Routes deletions to the system trash (Reclaim) instead of permanent delete.
  • Standard Undo Support: Supports standard IDE undo (`Ctrl/Cmd + Z`) for move-to-trash operations.
  • Project View Integration: A top‑level "Reclaim" node appears under the Project root (also in Project Files and Open Files panes).
  • Search/Filter: Search bar in the Reclaim tool window to quickly find deleted files.
  • Exclusion Patterns: Configure global or project-specific exclusion patterns to bypass Reclaim for certain files.
  • Project-Specific Settings: Override global settings on a per-project basis.
  • Drag and Drop: Drag files from the Project tool window onto the Reclaim node to move them to trash.
  • Explicit Action: "Move to Reclaim" action available in Project View and Editor tab popups.
  • Cross-Platform: Linux (Freedesktop.org Trash) and Windows (Recycle Bin) fully supported. macOS (Trash) fully supported via native macOS APIs.
  • Configurable: A settings panel allows you to enable or disable the plugin's functionality at any time.
Premium Features:
  • Secure Scrubbing: Permanently erase files bypassing the trash and Local History with three scrubbing methods:
    • Overwrite with 0's: Fast, basic scrubbing.
    • Random Noise: Overwrites file content with random patterns.
    • Cryptographic Entropy: Overwrite using collected entropy for maximum security.
  • Restore To...: Restore reclaimed files to a custom location instead of their original path.
  • File Preview: Preview reclaimed files directly from the Reclaim tool window before restoring.
Known Limitations:
  • Behaviour on network drives and non-standard filesystems may depend on the underlying OS trash implementation.
  • Remote / container-based development setups may not be fully supported yet.
Privacy:
  • Reclaim does not send file or project contents off your machine.
  • No telemetry or analytics are collected by the plugin.
Contact / Support:
  • Website: https://gitlab.com/sysrqassociates/Jetbrains/plugins/Reclaim/
  • Email: reclaim@sysrqassociates.net
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Missing Context Menu Options: Fixed a bug where right-click context menu options (Restore, Restore To, Restore All, Empty Reclaim, Refresh) were not appearing when selecting items in the Reclaim section of the Project panel. The issue was caused by incomplete node type detection in the selection handling logic.
  • Drag and Drop Hijacking: Fixed a bug where the Reclaim plugin's drag-and-drop handler was intercepting all Project View drag-and-drop operations, preventing normal file moves between folders. The handler now only claims drops when the mouse is over the Reclaim root node.
  • Drag and Drop Restoration: Fixed and improved ability to restore files by dragging them out of the Reclaim node (Fixes #26).
  • Drag and Drop Robustness: Improved robustness and file naming during drag-and-drop operations (Fixes #27).
  • Node Property Access: Corrected property access in `ReclaimItemNode` checks.

idea-plugin.name: Split-Pro
idea-plugin.description:
This plugin adds some optimizations for people that love to work with split editors.

Why?
By using multiple editor windows in parallel, you can also use the space on big screens better.

How?
It will provide two new actions, Open in Horizontal Split and Open in Vertical Split which will open the selected file either right or left / above or below the current editor. If there is no splitter yet, it will split the editor.
For an optimized workflow, the plugin also provides a toolbar on top of each editor displaying the current file path as replacement of the tab bar. The advantage is that you will never search for tab titles anymore and it will be easier to avoid using the mouse. For navigating between your files, you have several options, e.g.:
  • The "Recent Files" popup (Ctrl+E)
  • "Search Everywhere" (Shift+Shift)
  • The project tree (Alt+1)
  • Bookmarks (Alt-2)

When you select a file, you can...
  • hit "Enter" to open the file in the current editor.
  • "Shift+Enter" to open it in the editor right or left of the current one
  • "Alt+Shift+Enter" to open it in the editor above or below the current one

What about the tabs?
For the best experience set Tab Placement to None and Tab Limit to 1 in the IDE settings.
However, this is completely optional and of course using tabs is supported.
Also, you have to remove the default keyboard shortcut for "Open In Right Split" as this plugin replaces it using the Action "Open in Horizontal Split".

Editor tweaks:
  • New bar with breadcrumbs for current file path for each editor (Can be disabled in View > Appearance > Editor Navigation Bar)
  • Action: Open in Horizontal Split — open selected file in a new editor left or right of the current one. This works from the dialogs like Search Everywhere or Recent Files. Default Shortcut: Shift+Enter
  • Action: Open in Vertical Split — open selected file in a new editor below or above the current one. This works from the dialogs like Search Everywhere or Recent Files. Default Shortcut: Alt+Shift+Enter
  • Action: Open in Chosen Split... — highlight all editors and open the selected file in the chosen splitter. This works from the dialogs like Search Everywhere or Recent Files. Default Shortcut: Ctrl+Shift+Enter

  • 0.1.2 — Ensure the "Add to watches" keyboard shortcut is still working in the Immediate window.

idea-plugin.name: LogZen
idea-plugin.description:
LogZen brings peace to your code by automatically silencing the noise of logging statements in Python, PHP, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, and C# (Rider). Focus on your business logic, not the logs.

Features
  • Automatic Folding: Instantly folds common logging calls to reduce visual clutter.
  • Guarded Logging Blocks: Collapses a supported logger-level check and its entire block - if (logger.is<Level>Enabled()) { ... } becomes a single … logging … line.
  • Zen Mode: Collapsed logs are replaced with a subtle … logging … indicator, keeping them accessible but out of the way.
  • Standard Integration: Works seamlessly with JetBrains' code folding actions (Expand/Collapse).
  • Custom actions:
    • ZenLog: Collapse logs - collapse all logs in the current file.
    • ZenLog: Expand logs - expand all logs in the current file.

Supported languages
  • Python:
    • Supports logger.* (e.g., logger.info("..."))
    • Supports self.logger.* (e.g., self.logger.debug("..."))
    • Supports logging.* (e.g., logging.warning("..."))
    • Guards: if logger.isEnabledFor(logging.<LEVEL>):
  • PHP:
    • Supports $logger->* (e.g., $logger->info("..."))
    • Supports field access $this->logger->* (e.g., $this->logger->error("..."))
    • Guards: if ($logger->isHandling(Logger::<LEVEL>)) (Monolog)
  • JavaScript/TypeScript:
    • Supports console.* (e.g., console.log("..."))
  • Java:
    • Supports logger.* (e.g., logger.info("..."))
    • Supports this.logger.* (e.g., this.logger.debug("..."))
    • Guards: if (logger.is<Level>Enabled()), if (logger.isLoggable(Level.<LEVEL>)), and if (logger.isEnabled(Level.<LEVEL>))
  • C# (Rider):
    • Supports logger.* (e.g., logger.Info("..."))
    • Supports log.* (e.g., log.Debug("..."))
    • Supports logger.LogInformation("...")
    • Guards: if (logger.IsEnabled(LogLevel.<LEVEL>)) (Microsoft.Extensions.Logging), if (logger.IsEnabled(LogEventLevel.<LEVEL>)) (Serilog), if (logger.IsLevelEnabled(LogLevel.<LEVEL>)) (NLog), and if (logger.Is<Level>Enabled) (NLog, log4net)

Guarded logging blocks
Guarded logging blocks fold the logger level check and the entire block, including any statements besides the log call. For example, if (logger.is<Level>Enabled()) { ... } becomes a single … logging … line.

Missing a language? Let me know at lukas@vokracko.cz
Silence the noise. Reveal the code.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.9.20
  • Java: Added support for folding SLF4J isEnabledForLevel(Level.<LEVEL>) guards.
2026.9.18
  • Guarded logging blocks: LogZen collapses a supported logger-level check and its entire block, including statements besides the log call, into a single … logging … line.
  • Supported guards:
    • Java: is<Level>Enabled(), isLoggable(Level.<LEVEL>) and isEnabled(Level.<LEVEL>)
    • Python: isEnabledFor(logging.<LEVEL>)
    • PHP: isHandling(...) (Monolog)
    • C#: IsEnabled(LogLevel.<LEVEL>) (Microsoft.Extensions.Logging), IsEnabled(LogEventLevel.<LEVEL>) (Serilog), IsLevelEnabled(LogLevel.<LEVEL>) (NLog) and Is<Level>Enabled (NLog, log4net)
  • A plain logging guard with no else / elif / elseif branch folds its entire block, including statements besides the log call.

idea-plugin.name: PyUI Helper
idea-plugin.description:
Gradio, Streamlit, NiceGUI, FastAPI, Django, Flask, Flet, Reflex. Full framework support with a component palette, app outline, run/debug, documentation & autocomplete and config file support.

This is a new plugin, made by developers with a real love for python frameworks. But we need your help: Please leave a review, reach out to us on github, the community or email and tell us your thoughts, issues and more.

Features

Broad Framework Support

  • Gradio 5.x / 6.x - 85+ components, 6 themes, 23 launch() parameters, 15 environment variables
  • Streamlit 1.40+ - 120+ API functions, 45+ config.toml options, column_config classes
  • NiceGUI 3.x - 110+ UI elements, Quasar component props (200+), Tailwind CSS classes, 5 storage APIs
  • FastAPI - Route decorators, dependency injection, response models, middleware
  • Django - Models, views, forms, admin, URLs, signals, class-based views
  • Flask - Routes, blueprints, request/response handling, lifecycle hooks
  • Flet - UI controls, layouts, event handlers, cross-platform support
  • Reflex - Components, state management, routing, reactive UI

Component Palette and App Outline

  • Component Palette - A searchable, categorized browser for every component in all 8 frameworks. Follows the file you are editing, shows full parameter tables, and inserts at the caret or by drag and drop
  • Smart Insert - Inserted code uses your file's own import alias and adds the import if it is missing
  • App Outline - See the UI tree your code builds. Python GUI structure is built with with blocks and nested calls, so it is normally invisible. FastAPI, Flask and Django show a route map instead

Code Intelligence

  • Smart Completion - Context-aware completion for all framework APIs, CSS classes, and component props
  • Parameter Hints - Inline parameter information with types and defaults
  • Documentation - Rich hover documentation for every component and function
  • Line Markers - Visual indicators for decorators and UI components
  • Config Support - Full config.toml completion for Streamlit, environment variables for Gradio

Code Quality

  • Inspections - Detect common issues, deprecated APIs, and best practice violations
  • Quick Fixes - One-click automatic fixes for detected problems

Productivity

  • 150+ Live Templates - Quick scaffolding with gr:, st:, ui:, fa:, dj:, fl:, ft:, rx: prefixes
  • File Templates - Create new framework apps from pre-built templates
  • Wrap Actions - Quickly wrap selections in layout containers
  • Runtime Configurations - Preconfigured runtime configurations - start/stop/debug from within the IDE
  • Hot Reload - Framework-native hot reload for Gradio, Streamlit, FastAPI, Django, Flask, Flet, and Reflex
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Component palette tool window - browse, search and insert components for all 8 frameworks
  • App outline tool window - UI tree for Gradio, Streamlit, NiceGUI, Flet and Reflex, route map for FastAPI, Flask and Django
  • Drag and drop components from the palette into the editor
  • Insert respects the file's own import alias and adds the import when missing
  • Settings panels for FastAPI, Django, Flask, Flet and Reflex, which previously had none
  • Custom YAML definition override field per framework in settings
  • New project wizard can create a virtual environment and install requirements
  • New project wizard creates a matching run configuration so Run works immediately
  • Add framework to an existing project action
  • Gradio Sidebar, Navbar, Dialogue, Workflow, WorkflowCanvas, ParamViewer, BrowserState, DeepLinkButton, Walkthrough, Step and the top level Warning, Error and Info functions
  • Streamlit skeleton, mermaid_chart, bottom, iframe, menu_button, App and pagination
  • NiceGUI input_chips, xterm, page_scroller, list, item, altair, anywidget, date_input, slide_item, sub_pages, keep_alive and more
  • Reflex theme_panel, memo, clipboard, segmented_control, auto_scroll, data_editor, the upload component, storage classes and seven additional chart types
  • Django async ORM methods, 15 class based views, 19 form fields, 10 signals and Django 5.2 model fields including CompositePrimaryKey
  • FastAPI app and router methods, StaticFiles, Jinja2Templates, lifespan, middleware and security classes
  • Flask class based views, 9 signals, streaming template helpers and context helpers
  • Deprecation warnings for removed API including gr.Box, gr.Series, gr.Parallel, st.bokeh_chart, FLASK_ENV, FastAPI on_event, ORJSONResponse and UJSONResponse

Fixed

  • Inspections no longer warn on 79 valid components including gr.ImageEditor, gr.Code, gr.Timer, ui.codemirror, ui.rating, st.chat_message and st.data_editor
  • Completion no longer offers environment variables, config keys, CSS selectors and event names as module attributes
  • Streamlit completion no longer offers config.toml keys in Python files
  • Flask completion no longer offers FLASK_ environment variables as app attributes
  • Reflex and Flet hover docs no longer show component docs for unrelated local names
  • Streamlit and NiceGUI hover docs now show full parameter tables instead of one line
  • Nested attribute completion now works for gr.themes., st.column_config. and ui.storage.
  • Parameter completion now works for names imported with from gradio import Button
  • Inspection descriptions now resolve, they were named after the class instead of the declared short name and none of them ever loaded
  • Enable All in the framework notification banner now covers all 8 frameworks
  • Flask and Flet completion no longer insert an unmatched opening parenthesis
  • Django model inspection now resolves import aliases instead of matching the literal name
  • Duplicate YAML definitions that silently overwrote each other removed across Gradio, NiceGUI, Flet and Quasar props
  • Framework icons now shown for all 8 frameworks instead of only three
  • Flask environment file template no longer sets FLASK_APP to the project name

idea-plugin.name: Mesfavoris
idea-plugin.description:
Mes Favoris is an advanced bookmark management plugin for IntelliJ IDEA — a powerful alternative to the built-in bookmark system.

Features

  • Hierarchical bookmarks — organize in folders and subfolders with drag-and-drop
  • Multiple bookmark types — files, URLs, code snippets, Java members, notes, shortcuts, IDE actions
  • Tags — tag any bookmark and browse them grouped by tag
  • Path placeholders — portable bookmarks across machines using variables like ${HOME}
  • Remote sync — share bookmarks with your team via Google Drive or GitHub Gists
  • Resilient file bookmarks — survive refactoring and edits thanks to the Bitap algorithm
  • Search Everywhere — find any bookmark with double Shift
  • Virtual folders — automatic Recent, Latest Visited, and Most Visited views
  • Inlay hints — display bookmark comments inline in the editor
  • MCP integration — manage bookmarks from any MCP-compatible AI assistant (Claude, etc.)
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changed

  • GitHub Gist sync now goes through a local git clone of each Gist, kept in the IDE system directory: loading fetches and saving commits and pushes, so only the changes go over the network. Requires Git 2.31 or later, as configured in IntelliJ.
  • Importing a large (truncated) GitHub Gist now uses a shallow clone, which makes it faster.

Fixed

  • The bookmarks file is now written atomically, so a crash or a full disk during a save can no longer leave it truncated. An unreadable bookmarks file no longer prevents the plugin from starting: it is moved aside to bookmarks.json.corrupted-<date> and a notification tells what is wrong with it (e.g. a duplicate bookmark id and where it is).
  • Saving a shared folder to a remote store now gives up after repeated conflicts instead of retrying forever, which blocked all later bookmark saves.
  • Importing a remote bookmark folder under another remote folder is now prevented.
  • The notification shown when connecting to a remote store fails no longer displays null as the reason.
  • Moving a folder into itself or one of its subfolders now fails with an explicit error message.
  • The GitHub token is now passed to git through its environment instead of its command line, so it no longer shows up in the process list.

FreqFiles - Smart File Access Assistant for JetBrains IDEs

Keymap Conflict?
If you encounter a keymap conflict, you can resolve it by reassigning the keybinding for FreqFiles.

Go to: Settings → KeyMap → Plugins → FreqFiles → find the action freqfiles.toggle.panel and change it to your preferred key combination.

New: Recently Used Section

FreqFiles helps you quickly access your favorite files and frequently used files across JetBrains IDEs. It provides an elegant floating ball (hover to expand) and a classic floating panel to keep your workflow fast and focused.

GitHub Repository: https://github.com/Mo-HanQing/FreqFiles

Highlights

  • Floating Ball: always available, hover to expand, draggable, snap-to-edge, position persistence
  • Two Modes: Mode A (Hover) / Mode B (Click to Pin)
  • Frequent Files: automatic tracking based on click count + stay time, Top 50 ranking
  • Favorite Files: manage a curated list with add/remove/reorder
  • Recently Used: a separate list below Frequent Files, showing your latest files
  • Settings: customize floating ball behavior and ranking weights

Features

🔮 Floating Ball

  • Auto show on project startup (when enabled)
  • Hover to expand panel
  • Mode A: hover-to-expand, mouse-leave-to-collapse
  • Mode B: hover-to-expand + click to pin/unpin
  • Draggable, snap-to-edge, and position persists across restarts
  • Customizable ball size and auto-hide delay

🎯 Favorite Files

  • Manually add and maintain your favorite files
  • Supports files inside and outside the project
  • Reorder items with up/down
  • Double-click to open files

📊 Frequent Files

  • Automatically tracks file usage statistics
  • Records both click count and stay time
  • Shows top 50 frequent files
  • Statistics shown as: Clicks, Stay time (ms/s/m/h)

🎨 Classic Floating Panel

  • Resizable and movable popup panel
  • Split view: Favorite Files (left) and Frequent Files + Recently used (right)
  • When floating ball is disabled, toggle with Shift+Alt+F

⚙️ Settings

  • Floating ball: enable/disable, Mode A/B, size, auto-hide delay, snap-to-edge
  • Ranking algorithm: adjust click weight vs stay time weight
  • Access via: File → Settings → Tools → FreqFiles

🔗 Context Menu Integration

  • Add to favorites from:
    • Project view
    • Editor tabs
    • Editor content

💾 Persistent Storage

  • Favorites, statistics, and floating ball position persist across restarts

Usage

Toggle / Show

  1. Press Shift+Alt+F to toggle visibility
  2. Configure via: Tools → Toggle Quick File Panel

Manage Favorites

  • Use the + button in the Favorite Files panel
  • Or right-click any file → Add to Favorite Files

Adjust Ranking Weights

  • Go to File → Settings → Tools → FreqFiles
  • Adjust click weight vs stay time weight

idea-plugin.name: EzCord Utils
idea-plugin.description:
EzCord Utils - Supercharge Your Discord Bot Development!

A powerful IntelliJ plugin designed to streamline your Discord bot development workflow with EzCord.

Say goodbye to manual language file navigation and hello to intelligent autocomplete!

✨ Features

  • Smart Language Key Autocomplete - Instantly suggests available language keys as you type
  • Quick Documentation - Hover over any language key to see its translation in real-time
  • One-Click Navigation - Jump directly to language definitions in YAML files with gutter icons (use Ctrl+Click for jumping to fallback)
  • Language Keys Tool Window - View all language keys and translations in a dedicated tool window with detailed information
  • Live Templates - Speed up your coding with pre-defined templates for common discord features

🎯 Perfect For

Developers working with EzCord who want to boost productivity and reduce errors when managing multi-language support.

Sponsors

idea-plugin.name: ClipboardToSelectionDiff
idea-plugin.description:
Instantly compare your selected code with clipboard content using IntelliJ's powerful built-in diff viewer. Perfect for evaluating Stack Overflow solutions, comparing code variations, or reviewing snippets before pasting—all without cluttering your workspace with temporary files.

🎯 Why Use This Plugin?

Ever found yourself:

  • 📋 Copying code from Stack Overflow and wanting to see how it differs from your current implementation?
  • 🔄 Comparing two code variations by awkwardly creating scratch files?
  • 🤔 Wondering if that clipboard snippet is really different from your selection?

This plugin solves that. Right-click your selection, choose "Diff with Clipboard," and see a beautiful side-by-side comparison instantly.

✨ Features

  • 🚀 One-Click Comparison: Right-click any selection → "Diff with Clipboard"
  • 🎨 Native Diff Viewer: Uses IntelliJ's built-in diff tool with syntax highlighting
  • ⚡ Zero Setup: No configuration needed—just install and use
  • 🧹 Clean Workflow: No temporary files, no extra steps, no mess

🎬 How to Use

  1. Select code in your editor
  2. Copy a different snippet to your clipboard (Ctrl/Cmd+C)
  3. Right-click on your selection
  4. Click "Diff with Clipboard"
  5. See the differences highlighted instantly!

💡 Use Cases

  • 🔍 Code Review: Compare online solutions with your implementation
  • 📝 Documentation: Check if your code matches examples
  • 🔄 Refactoring: See what changed between code versions
  • 🎓 Learning: Understand differences between similar code patterns
idea-plugin.change-notes:
🎉 Initial Release

  • 📋 Instant Diff Comparison: Right-click any selection and choose "Diff with Clipboard" to see a side-by-side comparison
  • 🎨 Native IntelliJ Diff Viewer: Leverages the built-in DiffManager with full syntax highlighting and theme support
  • 🛡️ Smart Validation:
    • Gracefully handles empty selections with helpful notifications
    • Detects empty clipboard and alerts the user
    • Automatically enables/disables based on context
  • ⚡ Zero Configuration: Works out of the box—no setup required
  • 🎯 Editor Integration: Seamlessly integrated into the editor context menu

idea-plugin.name: BreakpointStudio
idea-plugin.description:
BreakpointStudio

BreakpointStudio is the ultimate toolkit for power users who spend a lot of time in the debugger.

断点工作室 插件为开发者提供更强大的断点管理工具包。支持断点撤销、移除动画 (Poof)、以及自动生成方法出入口断点。

Features

Poof effect

Remove breakpoints with a satisfying poof animation.
Check settings (Tools → Breakpoint Studio) to customize or disable the effect.

Undo/redo breakpoint action

Easily revert or reapply your last breakpoint-related actions.

Debug with muted breakpoints

One-click debugging that temporarily enables muted breakpoints.
After the debugging session finishes, the breakpoints return to their previous muted/unmuted states.

Generate entry/exit breakpoints

Automatically add breakpoints to all function/method entry and exit points (e.g. returns) in your code by
right-clicking the method/class name or empty line to target the whole file.

Setup Guide

Check the plugin settings page for more customization: Tools → Breakpoint Studio

If the buttons are missing:

  1. Right-click the Debug Tools toolbar
  2. Select Add → Search for 'Breakpoint Studio'
  3. Add the undo/redo/debug buttons

idea-plugin.name: SmartIgnoreGenerator
idea-plugin.description:
Smart Ignore Generator

Smart Ignore Generator automatically creates optimized .gitignore, .dockerignore, and .eslintignore files for your projects based on detected project type. Stop wasting time manually writing ignore files and let the plugin do it for you with industry-standard templates for 10+ programming languages.

Never commit node_modules, .env files, or build artifacts again!

✨ Why You'll Love It

🔍 Zero Configuration

Just right-click and go! The plugin automatically detects your project type and generates the perfect ignore files.

🧠 Intelligent Detection

Supports 10+ languages and frameworks:

  • 🟢 Node.js/JavaScript - Never commit node_modules/ again
  • 🐍 Python - Keep __pycache__/ and .venv/ out
  • ☕ Java/Kotlin - Ignore target/, build/, and .class files
  • 🦀 Rust - Auto-ignore target/ and Cargo.lock
  • 🐹 Go - Clean repos without vendor/
  • 💎 Ruby - Skip .bundle/ and vendor/
  • 🐘 PHP - Exclude vendor/ from commits
  • ⚙️ C/C++ - Ignore build artifacts and binaries
  • 🌐 Multi-language projects supported!

🛡️ Smart & Safe

  • ✅ Detects existing files and asks before overwriting
  • ✅ Industry-standard patterns from GitHub's gitignore repository
  • ✅ Prevents common mistakes that plague beginners and pros alike

⚡ Lightning Fast

One click. Instant results. Professional-grade ignore files ready to go.

🚀 Features

  • Automatic Project Detection: Intelligently detects your project type (Node.js, Python, Java, Kotlin, Go, Rust, C/C++, PHP, Ruby, or General)
  • Industry-Standard Templates: Pre-configured with best practices from GitHub's official gitignore repository
  • Multi-Language Support: Handles projects using multiple languages simultaneously
  • Smart Overwrite Protection: Warns you before overwriting existing files with options to skip or overwrite
  • One-Click Generation: Simple right-click action on any project directory

📦 What Gets Generated

Language/FrameworkFiles Created
Node.js/JavaScript.gitignore, .dockerignore, .eslintignore
Python.gitignore, .dockerignore
Java.gitignore, .dockerignore
Kotlin.gitignore, .dockerignore
Go.gitignore, .dockerignore
Rust.gitignore, .dockerignore
C/C++.gitignore, .dockerignore
PHP.gitignore, .dockerignore
Ruby.gitignore, .dockerignore
General/Multi-language.gitignore

🎯 How to Use

Step 1: Right-Click

Right-click on your project root directory in the Project view

Step 2: Select Action

Choose "Generate Optimized Ignore Files" from the context menu

Step 3: Done! 🎉

The plugin will:

  • ✅ Detect your project type
  • ✅ Generate appropriate ignore files
  • ✅ Notify you of the results

That's it! Your ignore files are ready with industry-standard patterns.

💡 What Gets Ignored

Common Patterns Across All Languages

  • 🗂️ IDE Files: .idea/, .vscode/, *.swp
  • 💻 OS Files: .DS_Store, Thumbs.db
  • 🔐 Environment: .env, .env.local
  • 📝 Logs: *.log

Language-Specific Patterns

  • Node.js: node_modules/, dist/, build/, .next/, .cache/
  • Python: __pycache__/, *.pyc, .venv/, *.egg-info/
  • Java/Kotlin: target/, build/, *.class, .gradle/
  • Rust: target/, Cargo.lock (in libraries)
  • Go: vendor/, bin/
  • And many more!

🛡️ Prevents Common Mistakes

❌ Before Smart Ignore Generator:

git add .
# Oops! Just committed 500MB of node_modules/
# Leaked .env with production secrets
# Pushed build artifacts and IDE configs

✅ After Smart Ignore Generator:

git add .
# Only source code committed
# Secrets stay local
# Clean, professional repository

🎨 Beautiful Integration

  • 🌓 Theme-Aware Icons: Gorgeous icons for both light and dark IDE themes
  • 🔔 Smart Notifications: Clear feedback on what was generated
  • 🎯 Context-Aware: Action only appears where it makes sense

🐛 Issues & Feedback

Have questions? Found a bug? Want to request a feature?

  • 🐛 Report Issues
  • 💡 Request Features
  • ⭐ Star on GitHub

🙏 Support

If this plugin saves you time, consider:

  • ⭐ Starring the repository
  • 📝 Writing a review on the JetBrains Marketplace
  • 📢 Sharing with fellow developers

Made with ❤️ for developers who value clean repositories

Stop manually writing ignore files. Start building features. 🚀

    • Supports 10+ languages: Node.js, Python, Java, Kotlin, Go, Rust, C/C++, PHP, Ruby, and more
    • Handles multi-language projects seamlessly
