idea-plugin.name: DDLABS-Gitifier
idea-plugin.description:
Gitifier is a free and open-source light-weight IntelliJ IDEA plugin that allows developers to easily share their complete codebase directly to GitHub.com, GitLab.com or Bitbucket.com. This plugin does not provide complete git functionality, it only provides an easy way to keep the code in GitHub.com, GitLab.com or Bitbucket.com for future references. This plugin is not intended to replace full Git functionality. Instead, it provides a simple way to preserve and reference code on these platforms. Often, valuable code written for proofs of concept (POCs) is lost or forgotten over time. Gitifier helps prevent this by offering a convenient solution to save and share your work for future use and collaboration. With Gitifier, you can preserve, showcase, and share your code with ease, keeping your ideas alive for future inspiration and collaboration. Gitifier supports the following environments:
  • Windows: 386, AMD64, and ARM64
  • MacOS: AMD64 and ARM64
  • Linux Alpine: 386 and AMD64
  • Linux: 386, AMD64, and ARM64

🔑Key Features:

  • Idea/Poc Preservation: Your ideas deserve to be saved. Gitifier makes sharing effortless.
  • One Click Sharing: From IntelliJ idea to GitHub, Gitlab, or Bitbucket—Gitifier keeps your code future-ready.

🌟 Why Gitifier:

In modern development, valuable code is often created during experiments, prototypes, or proofs of concept. Unfortunately, much of this work is left behind and eventually forgotten. Gitifier addresses this problem by making it effortless to preserve and share entire codebases directly from IntelliJ IDEA to platforms like GitHub, Gitlab, or Bitbucket.

❤️ Why You’ll Love It

Gitifier is a small light-weight plugin which ensures the following.
  • Ideas aren’t lost: Even quick prototypes can be saved for future reference.
  • Collaboration is easier: Teams can access and build upon shared codebases without complex Git setup.
  • Knowledge is retained: Developers can revisit past work, learn from it, or repurpose it for new projects.
  • Time is saved: Instead of manually configuring repositories, Gitifier provides a streamlined path to keep code safe and accessible.

🌐 How to generate token and usage in Gitifier Setting

❌ Do not generate Github fine grained token

💻Generate Github Classic Token

Follow the steps below:
  • Log in to github.com
  • Click on your profile picture in the upper-right corner of any page, then select Settings from the dropdown menu.
  • In the left sidebar, scroll down and click on Developer settings.
  • In the left sidebar, under "Personal access tokens," click on Tokens (classic)
  • Click the Generate new token button, then select Generate new token (classic).
  • In the "Note" field, enter a descriptive name for your token to help you remember its purpose.
  • Set an expiration date for the token.
  • Select the scopes (permissions), click on the following checkbox.
    • repo, workflow, write:packages, delete:packages, admin:org, notifications, user, delete_repo, codespace, project
  • Finally click on Generate token button at the bottom of the page.
  • Immediately copy the generated token and save it in a secure location.
  • Go to Use Gitifier setting, double click Username column and provide your username along with email id and paste the generated token in the Token column.

💻Generate Gitlab Personal Access Token

  • Sign in to your GitLab account.
  • In the upper-right corner, select your avatar from the dropdown menu, then choose Edit profile.
  • On the left sidebar, select Personal Access Tokens.
  • Click the Add new token button.
  • In the Token name field, enter a descriptive name for the token.
  • In the Expiration date field, set an expiration date as a security best practice.
  • Select the following desired scopes (permissions) for the token:
    • read_user, read_repository, read_api, self_rotate, write_repository, api
  • Finally click on Create token
  • Immediately copy the generated token and save it in a secure location
  • Go to Use Gitifier setting, double click Username column and provide your username along with email id and paste the generated token in the Token column.

💻Generate Bitbucket Access Token

  • Go to bitbucket.org, click on the settings icon, or use this link: Bitbucket App Passwords.
  • Click on this link: Atlassian API Tokens.
  • Click the blue button "Create API token with scopes".
  • Provide a name and expiration date, then click Next and select the "Bitbucket" radio button.
  • Open the Scope actions dropdown, select All, and check all boxes to save time.
  • Click the Create token button.
  • Immediately copy the generated token and save it in a secure location.
  • Go to Use Gitifier setting, double click Username column and provide your username along with email id and paste the generated token in the Token column.

👉 Gitifier: A creation from Tornado

From the visionary mind at Tornado comes Gitifier — creafted by an Engineer to solve real problems and simplify developers’ lives. 🧐 Wanna to 🤝 join with me to a new challenging technical task ?

idea-plugin.name: Copy Setting Path
idea-plugin.description:
Adds Copy Setting Path action which copies the full navigation path to any UI setting in IDE dialogs or main menu items to the clipboard.

Features

  • Copy full path to any option in Settings dialogs (e.g., Settings | Editor | Code Style | Java)
  • Copy full path from main menu items (e.g., File | Manage IDE Settings | Export Settings)
  • Works with Project Structure dialog in IntelliJ IDEA and EDU products
  • Supports navigation via Ctrl+Click (Cmd+Click on macOS)
  • Handles tree structures, tabs, titled panels, buttons, labels, and tables
  • Configurable path separator style (pipe, arrow, or breadcrumb) via Advanced Settings
  • Optional mouse click interception via Advanced Settings
  • Toast notification with path segment highlighting
  • Optional sound feedback when path is copied

Usage

  • Settings/Dialogs: Use Ctrl+Click (Cmd+Click on macOS) on any UI element
  • Main Menu: Enable mouse interception in Advanced Settings, then Ctrl+Click on any menu item to copy its path (the menu action will not execute)
  • The full path is copied to the clipboard

Configuration

Go to Settings | Advanced Settings | Copy Setting Path to configure:

  • Path separator style: Choose between pipe (|), arrow (→) and other styles
  • Mouse click interception: Enable to copy paths without activating UI components, and to enable main menu path copying
  • Balloon notification: Toggle the brief popup that appears near the mouse cursor when a path is copied (enabled by default)
  • Notification animations: Enable the rise animation and sequential path segment highlighting
  • Sound feedback: Play a brief sound when a path is copied
  • Display duration: Configure how long the notification stays visible (supports decimal values)

Shortcut Conflict

The default Ctrl+Click (Cmd+Click on macOS) shortcut conflicts with multiple selection in lists and trees. When mouse interception is enabled, a warning notification will appear with a link to Keymap settings.

Recommendation: Change the shortcut in Settings | Keymap to use:

  • Right-click shortcuts — e.g., Ctrl+Right Click or Shift+Right Click
  • Additional modifiers — e.g., Ctrl+Shift+Click or Ctrl+Alt+Click

Platform Limitations

Main menu path copying is not supported when the IDE uses native (OS-provided) menus:

  • macOS: Native menu bar is enabled by default
  • Linux: Native menu integration may be enabled depending on your desktop environment

Important Notice

This plugin is incompatible with the legacy Copy Option Path plugin. If you have the old plugin installed, please uninstall it before using this plugin. The IDE will prevent both plugins from running simultaneously.

Comprehensive Action Tracking

Supports 20+ refactoring types including:

Quest System

  • Extract Expert - Master the Extract Method refactoring

Statistics Dashboard

Real-time Notifications

Export Your Progress

Installation

  1. Open IntelliJ IDEA

Usage

idea-plugin.name: Konfigomatik
idea-plugin.description:
Sync IDE settings and AI rules across your team. Konfigomatik applies, per Git repository — and per branch when your team gives one its own configuration — the code style, actions on save (reformat, optimize imports, rearrange), Prettier, annotation processing, Maven settings and JDK governed from one dashboard — no shared .idea folder. It also writes the rules your AI agents follow, composed on that same dashboard, into the CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md of each repository.

What it applies

  • Code style — the project scheme.
  • Actions on save — reformat (whole file or changed lines), optimize imports, rearrange; Prettier on or off.
  • Java projects — annotation processing on or off, Maven settings.xml and local repository (outside the project), a JDK downloaded from the URL your team sets — the build matching the workstation, carrying your company's certificates — and used as project SDK.

The open file's repository governs, else the project root's, else the first alphabetically; a branch without its own configuration follows its repository's. Applied on project open, on switching to a file of another repository, on checking out another branch, on Refresh from Server, and when a 10-minute check finds new settings — written only when it differs. Offline, the last configuration received stays applied.

  • Shared rules for AI agents — a managed block in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, built from the rules layers composed on the dashboard, each following a branch or tag of its rules repository. The plugin keeps it up to date on project open, after a pull, checkout or commit, every 10 minutes and on Refresh from Server. The block belongs to Konfigomatik: any change inside it is replaced, and your text outside it is never touched. On its own, the plugin leaves alone a file with uncommitted changes outside the block, and tells you each time it writes. The Status tab shows the block's state, previews the update and applies it when you ask.

Developers propose, administrators review

  • Local changes — a hand-changed code style, on-save, annotation processing or Prettier setting is re-applied at the next pass, and kept as a session draft.
  • Publish tab — capture those settings (not Maven or JDK), tick what you propose, add a comment; a proposal made on a branch with its own configuration targets that configuration. Every proposal waits for an administrator's review.
  • Proposals tab — waiting for review, approved, or rejected with a reason.
  • Status tab — per repository and governing branch, what is applied and what needs you. Per repository, how many times Konfigomatik set up, put back or updated the settings, the JDK, Maven and the AI rules on this workstation, this month — or last month while this one has nothing yet. After an update, it also shows what the new version brings.

What leaves your machine

  • Sign in with an administrator's one-time Device Access Token; the token it returns stays in the IDE password safe. Signing in also sends a random installation id.
  • Sent automatically: each repository's Git remote host and path, plugin version, IDE version and product, the rules block marker (bundle, the commits its rules were read at, checksum, intact or edited) — not its content — and how many changes it applied, per repository, month, family (settings, JDK, Maven, AI rules) and nature (set up, put back, updated). The current branch name is sent only when your server declared a configuration for that branch: a feature branch name never leaves the workstation.
  • Sent on Publish only: the ticked settings and values, the target repository or group, a hash of its server settings, your comment.
  • Never sent: source code, file names, keystrokes, coding time. In your project, the plugin writes CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and .idea/prettier.xml, and nothing else.

Where your Git server answers your network but not ours, an administrator can have a signed-in workstation list its projects (id, name, path) and send that list back.

Compatibility

IntelliJ-based IDEs 2025.2 or newer with Git integration, verified with the JetBrains Plugin Verifier up to 2026.2. Java, Maven and Prettier features need the matching IDE plugin. Paid, 30-day trial.

Documentation · Privacy policy · Get started · Pricing

idea-plugin.name: ADR Companion
idea-plugin.description:
ADR Companion — Architecture Decision Records in Your IDE

Stop losing architectural decisions in wikis and chat threads. ADR Companion brings Architecture Decision Record management directly into IntelliJ IDEA, so decisions stay version-controlled, discoverable, and colocated with the code they describe.

Create & Capture

  • ADR Creation — Create ADRs from Nygard, MADR, RFC, Y-Statement, Tyree & Akerman or your own Custom templates, with automatic numbering
  • Create ADR from Pull Request — Turn a merged PR into an ADR: pick a recent merge commit and the plugin extracts Context, Decision and Consequences straight from the PR description
  • Create ADR from Code — Start a decision record pre-populated with the file, line and selected code that prompted it
  • React Server Components Support — Scan for 'use client'/'use server' boundaries (incl. inline Server Actions) and see which are documented by an ADR

Browse & Navigate

  • ADR Explorer — Browse all ADRs in a dedicated tool window with full-text search (title, status and Context/Decision/Consequences body) and status filtering
  • Go to ADR (Search Everywhere) — Double-Shift, type a number or title, jump straight to the decision from a dedicated ADRs tab
  • Code-to-ADR Navigation — Use @adr annotations in your code to link directly to decisions, with clickable gutter icons, a rich hover card, and @adr: code completion in every language
  • Link Code to an ADR (Alt+Enter) — Pick a decision from the intention list and the @adr reference is written in the current language's comment syntax
  • ADR-to-Code Navigation — From any ADR, list every code location that references it and jump there
  • Status Banner — An open decision record states its status above the document, and links to the successor when it has been superseded
  • Status Bar Widget — See the live ADR count and per-status breakdown at a glance; click to open the Explorer
  • Auto-Discovery — Automatically finds ADR directories (doc/adr, docs/adr, docs/decisions, …), no configuration needed
  • Graph & Timeline Views — Visualize relationships and decision history

Govern & Share

  • Team Configuration — Commit a .adr-config.yaml and the whole team shares one convention: ADR directory, default template, thresholds and gates, overriding each developer's IDE settings
  • Lifecycle Management — Track ADR status through Proposed → Accepted → Deprecated → Superseded, with automatic bidirectional supersede backlinks
  • Workflow Validator — Lint illegal status transitions, missing fields, duplicate ADR numbers and stale proposals (with CLI for CI gating)
  • Renumber ADR — Change a decision's number and every reference to it across the project is rewritten in one undoable step
  • Pre-Commit ADR Gate — Validate the decision log before every commit, and flag changes to architecturally significant paths that record no decision (toggle in Settings)
  • CI Annotations — --format=github puts workflow violations and orphaned ADRs straight onto the pull-request diff
  • Coverage & Impact Report — Find code that references each ADR and surface orphaned decisions
  • Copy ADR Status Summary — One click copies a Markdown badge + status table of every ADR, ready to paste into a README or PR
  • Index & Graph Export — Generate a consolidated Markdown index, or export the relationship graph as Mermaid / Graphviz DOT
  • Export to HTML — Share decisions with stakeholders outside the IDE
  • Built-in Inspections — Catch missing fields, stale records, and @adr references that point at missing, Deprecated or Superseded decisions — as you type

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2025.1+ (build 251+) and other IntelliJ-based IDEs
  • Java 17+
  • Optional: Git4Idea plugin (bundled with most JetBrains IDEs) — enables Create ADR from Pull Request

Getting Started

  1. Install ADR Companion from the JetBrains Marketplace
  2. Open a project — the plugin auto-discovers existing ADR directories
  3. Create your first ADR with the New ADR action or from the Project view context menu
  4. Open the ADR Explorer tool window to browse and manage all decisions

Support

  • Documentation
  • Issue Tracker (GitHub)
  • Email Support: support@jakubjirak.com
  • Changelog
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2027.1.0

  • Team configuration - Commit a .adr-config.yaml to the project root and the whole team shares one ADR convention: directory, default template, staleness thresholds, commit gate. It overrides each developer's IDE settings key by key; generate a documented one with Tools | ADR Companion | Create Team Configuration File
  • Require an ADR for protected paths - List architecturally significant globs under requireAdrForPaths, and the pre-commit gate speaks up when a commit changes an API, a schema migration or a contract without recording a decision
  • Duplicate ADR number detection - Two branches landing "ADR-0007" merge without a git conflict and every reference to them becomes ambiguous. The workflow validator now reports it as an error, in the IDE, in the commit gate and in CI
  • Renumber ADR… - Give a decision record a different number and the file name, title heading, front matter and every @adr:NNN, ADR-NNN and Markdown link across the project are rewritten in one undoable step
  • Link this code to an ADR (Alt+Enter) - Pick a decision from the intention list and the reference is written in the current language's comment syntax, right where you are typing
  • ADR status banner - Open a decision record and its status sits above the document, with a link to the successor when it has been superseded — no more acting on a superseded decision that reads like a current one
  • GitHub Actions annotations - --format=github on both CLIs puts workflow violations and orphaned ADRs on the pull-request diff instead of inside a job log

2026.9.0

  • @adr code completion - Type @adr: in any comment, in any language, and complete against your project's ADRs by number or title — inserts the canonical @adr:NNN annotation
  • Go to ADR in Search Everywhere - A dedicated ADRs tab in Double-Shift search: type 7, adr-7 or part of a title and open the decision record instantly
  • Outdated-reference inspection - New "Reference to missing or outdated ADR" inspection flags @adr:NNN annotations that point at a missing ADR, or one that is Deprecated/Superseded (shown strikethrough)
  • Find Code References to ADR - Reverse navigation: from any ADR file, list every code location that references it (annotations, ADR-NNN mentions, Markdown links) and jump straight there

2026.7.0

  • Full-text ADR search - The ADR Explorer search box now matches across the title, status and the Context/Decision/Consequences body (plus the raw and zero-padded adr-NNN id), with multi-term AND semantics — type several words to narrow instantly
  • Pre-commit ADR gate - A VCS check-in handler validates your decision log before each commit: blocking errors (missing required fields, dangling supersede links, illegal transitions) prompt to confirm, warnings stay informational. Toggle it in Settings → Tools → ADR Companion → Version Control
  • Status bar widget - A live ADR: N counter with a per-status breakdown tooltip; click it to open the ADR Explorer
  • ADR quick-doc on hover - Hovering an @adr reference in code now shows a rich card — ADR number, title, status, date and a context excerpt — instead of a one-line tooltip

2026.5.0

  • Create ADR from Pull Request - New "Create ADR from Pull Request…" action reads recent merge commits from your Git repository, lets you pick one (or paste a PR description), and extracts Context, Decision and Consequences into a numbered ADR — including the PR number and source branch
  • Copy ADR Status Summary - New "Copy ADR Status Summary" action copies a shareable Markdown badge and status table of every ADR to the clipboard, ready to drop into a README or pull request
  • Accurate Marketplace listing - Reworked the feature list to describe exactly what ships today and corrected the minimum-IDE requirement to 2025.1+ (build 251+)
  • Refreshed plugin icon - New decision-graph icon for light and dark themes

2026.4.1

  • Code-quality hardening - Internal refactor resolving all static-analysis findings (zero detekt issues) with no user-facing changes; all 256 tests pass

2026.4.0

  • React Server Components Support - New "Analyze React Server Components…" action scans for 'use client'/'use server' boundaries (including inline Server Actions) and reports which boundaries are documented by an ADR — with navigation, Markdown export, and coverage metrics
  • Three New ADR Formats - RFC (Request for Comments), Y-Statement, and Tyree & Akerman templates join Nygard and MADR — selectable in the Create New ADR dialog and as the default format in Settings
  • Bidirectional Supersede Backlinks - Superseding an ADR now automatically writes a "Supersedes ADR N" backlink (and YAML front matter entry) into the superseding record

ECProperty Completion

idea-plugin.name: Copy Selection Context
idea-plugin.description:
Copy file paths, line numbers, and code to clipboard for AI assistant workflows.

One shortcut (Ctrl+Alt+C / Cmd+Alt+C) copies your current selection — or the current line when nothing is selected — in a format ready to paste into Claude, ChatGPT, or any AI coding assistant.

Features

  • One-shortcut copy — Ctrl+Alt+C (Windows/Linux) / Cmd+Alt+C (macOS) copies path + line numbers based on your settings
  • Relative or absolute paths — choose project-relative or full absolute paths per your workflow
  • Code content as markdown — include the selected code as a fenced markdown code block with language tag
  • Session context collection — Add selections from several files, open the Context Collection tool window, review frozen code and final output, reorder or remove captures, then Copy All. Collection actions are assignable in Keymap without new default shortcuts.
  • Captured snapshots — Source edits, renames and deletion do not rewrite captured code. Built-in output labels multiple versions of the same range; custom templates keep their substitutions and may need confirmation.
  • Session privacy and fixed limits — Collections stay in project memory until project/plugin close, survive tool-window hiding and copying, and never enter persistent copy history. Clear All requires confirmation. Limits: 100 items, 256 KiB raw UTF-8 code per item, 2 MiB raw total; final output above 256 KiB needs confirmation and above 4 MiB is blocked. No truncation. OS and external clipboard history are separate.
  • Private copy history — Ctrl+Alt+H opens locally stored history with clear-all and disable controls
  • GitHub/GitLab permalink — generate a permanent link to the exact lines in your remote repository
  • Template-based output formatting — choose from built-in presets (Claude Code, Path:Line, Custom) or define your own template with variable placeholders
  • Live template preview — settings UI shows a real-time preview and validates template variables before you save
  • Smart line handling — copies the current line number when no text is selected, so the shortcut always produces useful output
  • Status bar widget — displays the last copied text in the IDE status bar; click it to copy again
  • Configurable settings — path type, output format, code trimming, notification toggle, and local history size (set to 0 to disable) all adjustable at Settings → Tools → Copy Selection Context
  • Context menu integration — all actions available in the editor right-click menu under the Copy Selection Context submenu

Output Format

Output follows the @path#Lline convention:

Path only: @src/main/kotlin/App.kt#L42
Range: @src/main/kotlin/App.kt#L250-253
With code: path + fenced code block in markdown

Source and issue tracker: github.com/hon454/copy-selection-context

idea-plugin.name: Env Desk
idea-plugin.description:
Env Desk - Environment Manager for IntelliJ IDEA

Manage your entire local development environment from a single tool window. Switch environment profiles, start Docker containers, launch mock servers, and handle secrets — all with one click.

Note: This plugin is currently in beta. Features are being actively developed and improved. Check the FAQ tab for the complete feature list, supported frameworks, and usage details.

Getting Started

  1. Open the Env Desk tool window (View → Tool Windows → Env Desk)
  2. Click "Detect Apps" to auto-discover your projects (Spring Boot, Quarkus, Micronaut, Node.js)
  3. Create a profile, customize your properties, and activate it

Support

For bug reports and feature requests, please visit our GitHub Issues page.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.0.0.3-beta

  • Performance Improvements: Internal optimizations for improved stability and responsiveness.

2026.0.0.2-beta

  • Performance Improvements: Internal optimizations for improved stability and responsiveness.

2026.0.0.1-beta

First Public Beta Release

  • Multi-App Workspace — Auto-detect Spring Boot, Quarkus, Micronaut, Node.js, and Generic apps in a single IDE window; each app gets its own independent set of profiles
  • Baseline + Override Model — Profiles store only what differs from the source config file; effective config computed on the fly as baseline + overrides + customKeys − removedKeys
  • Profile Editor — Full-featured editor with application properties table (color-coded by state), Java system properties, environment variables, sensitive value masking, and per-row actions (remove, restore, reset)
  • Injection Modes — Three modes: -D flags (inline JVM args), Config file (generated file with framework-specific flag), and Environment variables (for Node.js and non-JVM apps)
  • Debug Mode Toggle — Right-click any profile to enable debug mode; injects framework-specific logging properties (logging.level.root=DEBUG, quarkus.log.level=DEBUG, logger.levels.ROOT=DEBUG)
  • Node.js Support — Detect package.json projects, use .env as config source, support npm/yarn/pnpm, default to environment variable injection
  • Drift Detection — VFS watcher monitors source config files; balloon notification and review dialog when changes are detected
  • Profile Comparison — Side-by-side comparison of any two profiles with color-coded diff view
  • Bulk Edit — Edit all application properties as plain text in IntelliJ's standard editor
  • Docker Containers — 10 built-in templates (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redis, Kafka, etc.); start/stop/restart from the IDE; link to profiles; export as docker-compose.yml
  • Mock Servers — REST (OpenAPI 3.0) and SOAP (WSDL) mock servers with auto-generated response templates; link to profiles for automatic URL injection
  • Secrets Management — Credentials stored in OS credential manager via PasswordSafe; reference in profiles with {{secret}} syntax

idea-plugin.name: Project & Task Organizer
idea-plugin.description:
Project & Task Organizer turns a messy Recent Projects list into a structured catalog with nested groups, tags, favorites, linked projects, notes, docs links, and fast search — right inside your JetBrains IDE.

Key Features

  • Hierarchical groups — organize projects by teams, clients, or architecture with unlimited nesting and colored icons.
  • Linked Projects — bind related microservices together and open the entire set in one action.
  • Tags & filtering — label projects (backend, frontend, client-X…) and filter instantly with autocomplete.
  • Favorites — star important projects so they always appear at the top.
  • Quick Open (Ctrl+Shift+P / Cmd+Shift+P) — find and open any project in a second without leaving the editor.
  • Auto-discover — point to a folder and the plugin detects all projects inside by markers (.idea, .git, pom.xml, build.gradle, package.json, etc.).
  • Drag & Drop — drop a folder from Finder / Explorer straight into the catalog.
  • Notes & documentation links — attach context, Wiki URLs, Jira links, or Confluence pages to each project.
  • Startup Command — run a terminal command automatically when a project opens (docker-compose up, npm install, etc.).
  • Usage statistics — see open counts and last-used dates for every project.
  • NDA Filter — hide confidential projects during screen sharing.
  • Import / Export — back up or transfer your entire catalog as JSON.
  • Settings Sync — automatic catalog synchronization between machines via IntelliJ Settings Sync.
  • Sync notification — balloon notification when the catalog is updated from the cloud.
  • Plans — a simple task planner built right on top of your project structure: create tasks under any group or project, set due dates, and follow them in a sectioned list (Today / Tomorrow / Upcoming / Backlog / Done) with a mini-month calendar in the sidebar.

Multilingual UI: English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean.

Free and open for all JetBrains IDE users who juggle many repositories and want a fast, structured project hub.

idea-plugin.name: zMyBatis - MyBatis Dynamic SQL Runner with Parameters. mybatis
idea-plugin.description:
zMyBatis is a JetBrains IDE plugin that lets you execute MyBatis mapper queries directly from XML mapper files or Java/Kotlin annotation-based mappers — without leaving the IDE.

It evaluates MyBatis dynamic SQL, prompts you for parameter values, converts the result to native SQL, and runs it on a DataGrip database console in one step.

Features

One-Click Execution

Right-click → Execute (zMyBatis) while the caret is inside:

  • A MyBatis XML mapper statement tag (select, insert, update, delete)
  • A @Select / @Insert / @Update / @Delete annotation method (Java/Kotlin)

The plugin evaluates the MyBatis dynamic SQL and runs it through the DataGrip execution pipeline. DataGrip's own Execute and Explain Plan actions are untouched and work as usual.

Dynamic SQL Evaluation

Fully evaluates all MyBatis dynamic SQL tags:
if, choose / when / otherwise, foreach, where, set, trim, bind

Powered by the actual MyBatis XMLScriptBuilder engine (mybatis 3.5.x) for accurate results.

Parameter Input Dialog

  • Automatically detects #{param}, ${param}, and OGNL expression parameters
  • Excludes internal variables (bind, foreach item, foreach index) — only user-supplied parameters are prompted
  • Scalar parameters — one-line input: null, numbers, strings, booleans, lists (e.g. [1,2,3])
  • Object / nested parameters — multi-line JSON editor for dot-notation params (e.g. #{user.name} -> enter {"name":"Alice","id":1})
  • Supports nested objects ({key:{nestedKey:value}}), and object arrays ([{key:value},{key:value}])
  • JSON validation on object parameters before execution

Data Source and Schema Selection

On first execution from a mapper file, a popup lets you choose the target data source and schema. The selection is cached per mapper file and automatically restored across IDE restarts.

Annotation Support

  • Works with multi-line string arrays in @Select({...})
  • Resolves constant field references (e.g. @Select(SqlConstants.FIND_USER))
  • Shows a clear notice for unsupported @SelectProvider / @InsertProvider / @UpdateProvider / @DeleteProvider annotations

Seamless DataGrip Integration

The resolved native SQL is injected directly into the DataGrip execution pipeline, so all DataGrip features work as usual:

  • Result grid, export, explain plan
  • SQL history and console tabs

Settings

Configure via Settings -> Tools -> zMyBatis:

CategoryOptionDescription
Execution and OutputSQL PreviewShow a preview dialog to review resolved SQL before execution
Auto-format SQLReformat resolved SQL using IntelliJ's built-in SQL code style
Copy to ClipboardAuto-copy the final SQL to clipboard after execution
Console Session PolicyREUSE (default) — reuse existing console per mapper file / NEW_EACH — always open a new console
Parameter DialogRemember Last InputsPre-fill the parameter dialog with last-used values per Mapper statement
Empty Input HandlingNULL (default) — blank fields bind as SQL NULL / EMPTY_STRING — blank fields bind as empty string
Parsing EngineStrict OGNL ModePropagate OGNL evaluation errors immediately instead of silently skipping blocks
Ignore Unknown TagsStrip unrecognised/custom XML tags before parsing (preserves their text content)

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate, DataGrip, or any JetBrains IDE with the Database plugin
  • IDE version 2025.3 or later
  • A configured data source (database connection) in the Database tool window
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changed

  • Execute (zMyBatis) is now a standalone action (right-click menu / Run context group) instead of overriding DataGrip's built-in Execute action — DataGrip's own Execute, Explain Plan, and all other actions are no longer affected
  • Session management redesigned — ConsoleCacheService.put() now persists session data (dsName + schemaName) atomically; startup restore uses pruneStaleIndex() to cross-check the index against saved session data and drops entries that are no longer valid; markShuttingDown() / dispose() explicitly re-persist all live sessions before clearing the cache, eliminating the shutdown-flag race condition that caused deleted consoles to reappear after restart

Added

  • Execute MyBatis mapper queries directly from XML mapper files and Java annotation-based mappers via the DataGrip execution pipeline
  • Dynamic SQL evaluation: <if>, <choose>/<when>/<otherwise>, <foreach>, <where>, <set>, <trim>, <bind> tags fully supported
  • Supports @Select, @Insert, @Update, @Delete annotation-based mappers including multi-line string arrays and constant field references
  • @SelectProvider / @InsertProvider / @UpdateProvider / @DeleteProvider methods show a clear unsupported notice instead of failing silently

idea-plugin.name: Run In Terminal (macOS)
idea-plugin.description:
Reuse the active macOS Terminal window to execute selected shell script lines directly from the editor, preserving the same working directory, environment variables, and command history.

Platform Support

Available only on macOS.

Features

  • Execute a single-line at the caret position or the entire selection
  • Automatically ignore commented lines
  • Reuse the current Terminal session for continuous workflows

Note: The plugin uses the macOS osascript command to send the selection to the active Terminal window or automatically launch a new one if none is available.
It does not modify files or intercept terminal output.
To continue using the same session, keep the desired Terminal window open and active.

Plugin Scope

The action is enabled when:

  • Editing a .sh file
  • Editing a .md file and the caret is inside an injected shell code block (shell, bash, zsh, sh)

Default Shortcut

Command + Enter

Feedback and Contributions

Suggestions, new usage scenarios, and contributions are welcome to help improve the plugin.

idea-plugin.name: gouse
idea-plugin.description:
gouse toggles 'declared and not used errors' in Go.

Toggle ‘declared and not used’ errors in Go by using idiomatic _ = notUsedVar and leaving a TODO comment.

Quick Action

One-Click Install

Context Menu

Find Action

Dependencies

gouse is required.

go install github.com/looshch/gouse/v2@latest

Usage

gouse: Toggle ‘declared and not used’ errors toggles the errors in a file.

The plugin also adds a light-bulb quick action that runs gouse for the current file.

You can run the same action from the editor right-click context menu or from Find Action.

If gouse is missing, the plugin can offer a one-click install. That still requires the Go toolchain to be available on your PATH.

If gouse is installed somewhere non-standard, set the executable path in Settings | Tools | gouse.

By default, if gouse.path is empty and gouse is already installed, the plugin tries to update gouse to the latest version in the background on startup. You can disable this with the startup auto-update checkbox in settings.

idea-plugin.name: DevTomcat
idea-plugin.description:
DevTomcat

Apache Tomcat integration for IntelliJ IDEA with built-in diagnostics, observability, and secure connector defaults. DevTomcat takes a specific position on Tomcat development: catch errors before they bite, isolate server instances per launch, make deployment activity visible, and apply security-by-default to the connectors Tomcat exposes. Free and open source.

Smart Diagnostics

  • Error Diagnostics Engine — Detects 20+ common Tomcat errors (ClassNotFound, BindException, OOM, SSL, JDBC, etc.) with categorized severity, actionable suggestions, and quick-fix IDs
  • Version Compatibility Checker — Validates Tomcat/JDK compatibility before launch (Tomcat 7–11 matrix) and warns about Jakarta EE namespace changes
  • JDK / Tomcat mismatch quick-fix — When the configured JDK doesn't satisfy the Tomcat version's Java requirement, surfaces a balloon with two one-click actions: open the Run Configuration editor (to switch the JRE) or open Project Structure (to register a missing JDK)
  • End-of-life Tomcat warning — Detects EOL branches (7.x, 8.0.x, 8.5.x, 10.0.x) and recommends a tailored upgrade path (Tomcat 9 for javax.servlet, Tomcat 10.1 / 11 for jakarta.servlet)
  • ECJ JAR auto-swap — When Tomcat's bundled Eclipse JDT compiler is too old to read your webapp's class files (e.g. ECJ 3.7.x on Tomcat 7 vs Java 17 classes), one-click downloads a modern ECJ from Maven Central, verifies the SHA-1, and atomic-moves it into tomcat/lib/ with a reversible backup
  • Legacy-Tomcat compatibility shims — Suppresses the BCEL Invalid byte tag in constant pool: 19 flood on Tomcat 7.x, 8.0.x, 8.5.x < 51, and 9.0.x < 31 (where the bundled BCEL parser doesn't recognise module-info.class), and routes container-provided JAR scan-skips through catalina.properties on Tomcat 7 / 8.0 (where the Digester ruleset has no rule for <JarScanFilter>)
  • Auto-Port Resolution — Detects port conflicts at startup and auto-resolves to available ports with console warnings

Security & Safety

  • AJP bound to localhost by default — Closes CVE-2020-1938 (Ghostcat) for IDE-managed installs by setting address="127.0.0.1" on the AJP connector unless you explicitly bind elsewhere
  • JMX and RMI registry bound to localhost by default — JMX monitoring is enabled-on-demand and always binds 127.0.0.1 (override via VM options if remote monitoring is intentional)
  • CATALINA_BASE wipe protection — Refuses configuration copy operations that would overwrite a user's conf/ directory; stale-deployment cleanup gated to the IDE-managed run-base; parallel-run cleanup uses NOFOLLOW_LINKS so a symlink at the run-base root cannot be followed off-tree

Live Deployment Dashboard

  • Live Status Tracking — Real-time server and per-artifact status (Starting, Deploying, Reloading, Running, Failed) in the Services tool window
  • Run History — Persistent history of Tomcat run sessions with duration, startup time, artifact activity, and consecutive failure tracking
  • Startup Time Trends — Tracks startup performance across runs and shows trend comparisons

Enhanced Console & Config

  • Smart Console Filter — Clickable URLs (opens browser) and file paths (opens in editor) in Tomcat console output
  • Config Export/Import — Export and import run configurations as XML files for team sharing
  • Per-mode Runner Settings — Separate environment variables and startup scripts for Run, Debug, and Coverage modes
  • Multi-log Monitoring — Catalina, localhost, access, and custom log files as dedicated console tabs

Tomcat Workflow

  • Full Tomcat lifecycle — start, stop, debug, and redeploy from the IDE
  • Deploy WAR files and exploded directories with auto-detected artifacts
  • Multi-artifact deployment with independent context paths
  • Debug with full breakpoint and hot-swap support
  • Code coverage via IntelliJ's coverage engine (uses your IDE-configured runner — JaCoCo or IntelliJ's own agent)
  • Hot deployment and Update Running Application (Ctrl+F10)
  • CATALINA_BASE isolation — each configuration gets its own instance directory
  • server.xml auto-generation with HTTP, HTTPS, AJP, and shutdown connectors
  • JMX monitoring support
  • Remote deployment via Tomcat Manager API

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2025.1+
  • Apache Tomcat 7+ (legacy installs supported via auto-applied compatibility shims)
  • Java 17+
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.4.4

Changed

  • Container-provided jars recognised by their classes, not a name list.
  • Classpath-duplicate warning lists jar pairs with examples, not every path.
  • JDK frames in leaked-thread stacks fold.
  • Class-sync overlay bookkeeping no longer printed to the console.
  • Redeploy runs the same packaging-duplicate checks as a launch.

Added

  • Update says when a changed resource is still served from its module's jar.

Fixed

  • Module jars matched by their classes, not their file name.
  • Tomcat warnings and errors no longer printed twice.
  • One leak advisory per web application, not one per thread; it names the fix.
  • One library at two versions reported once, by preflight.

1.4.3

Changed

  • Console paths shown relative to the project, catalina.base and home.
  • Warn when an artifact packages modules the class sync can't cover.
  • Opt-in: run Maven package before Redeploy.
  • Sync skips surface as notifications with the fix.
  • JVM hot-swap ceiling noted in docs and console.
  • Redeploy tooltip states the as-last-built contract.

Added

  • Console shows where launch-preparation and update time goes, per phase.
  • Deployment Freshness view: per module, how it's delivered and whether it's current.
  • Experimental WSL mode: Tomcat and JDK inside a WSL distribution.

Fixed

  • Webapp INFO and WARN lines reach the run console, not just errors.
  • A canceled toolbar update no longer leaves the run-configuration template without a Tomcat server.
  • IDE cancellation propagates through deploy, update, service-view and editor code instead of being swallowed.
  • No internal API use flagged by the Marketplace verifier on 2026.2.
  • Maven modules with a custom finalName deploy from their real build output; their .war is no longer dropped as stale.
  • A blocked launch names the artifacts at fault in the balloon, instead of pointing at a run console that never opens.
  • A saved deployment whose build output was renamed follows the module's current output instead of failing the launch.
  • Orphan Tomcats get a real chance to stop cleanly before being force-killed.
  • Duplicate-classpath warning no longer reports the sync's own class overlays.
  • Update reloads only the contexts that actually changed; a no-op update reloads nothing.
  • Auto-detected deployments stored at a source path are served from the build output.
  • Unchanged dependency jars not reopened by the duplicate scan; container-jar keys memoised.
  • Compiled JSPs kept across launches when nothing they depend on changed.
  • Launch preparation no longer holds the IDE read lock.
  • Unchanged-file sync no longer re-stats every file or rewrites its manifest.
  • Only real web modules offered for deployment.
  • Deployment list names the actual archive, not always war.
  • Duplicate-classpath scanner filters by JAR-spec rules instead of product allowlists.
  • Lock scan probes any -D directory, not a fixed list of library properties.
  • Environment mode reads only DevTomcat's own switches.
  • Launch-preparation console output no longer lost before the console opens.
  • Lock scan no longer probes target-side persistence paths on the host.
  • Preflight lock warnings name the actual directory, not always catalina.base.
  • JDK from a different WSL distribution refused instead of silently re-rooted.
  • Cross-distribution path references surface in the run console.
  • Coverage refusal decided before stopping the running server.
  • Path system properties not judged against the host filesystem in WSL mode.
  • Unmappable WSL working directory fails cleanly instead of leaking ports.
  • Web resources sync no longer deletes build-produced webapp files.
  • Class sync covers every module a multi-module artifact packages.
  • Removed WAR deployments no longer linger as ghost contexts.
  • Hot-reload recompiles every module a multi-module artifact packages.
  • No duplicate run configs from run-from-context.
  • Context-created configs deploy real build outputs.
  • Child pom coordinates no longer shadowed by the parent's.
  • Class sync never writes into your source tree.
  • Auto-detected modules deploy build output, not sources.
  • Build the exploded webapp when no artifact or package step does (Community).
  • No false "artifact not found" warning before the first build.
  • Artifact-based configs from older versions deploy on Community.
  • No DevTomcat metadata files inside your webapp; leftovers cleaned up.
  • Unchanged WARs aren't re-copied; no needless context restart.
  • Stale class overlay yields to a rebuilt jar.
  • Hot-reload-off external paths get a visible warning.
  • Stale WAR deploys blocked; Deploy Anyway to override.
  • Outdated dependency jars called out.
  • Deployment tab finds artifacts in qualified-name projects.
  • Freshness view separates "not rebuilt" from "not redeployed".
  • Freshness view names the build tool when the sync can't help.
  • Outdated-jar warning matches Gradle and renamed modules.
  • Same-named configs in two projects no longer steal each other's ports.

1.4.2

Changed

  • Configurable ECJ download mirror for restricted networks.

Fixed

  • Webapp source overlay no longer shadows deployed build output.
  • Class sync no longer deletes deployed classes it didn't produce.

idea-plugin.name: Safe Paste
idea-plugin.description:
Prevents accidental execution of multiline commands when pasting into the terminal.

When using shells like PowerShell that do not support bracketed paste mode, pasting multiple lines can immediately execute each line as a separate command.

Safe Paste intercepts multiline paste operations and lets you choose:

  • Paste as Plain Text – safe, non-executing paste
  • Paste Anyway – execute commands line by line
  • Cancel – abort paste

Single-line paste remains unchanged.

Note: Requires the new terminal (Gen 2), available in IntelliJ IDEA 2024.2+. Make sure "Enable New Terminal" is active in Settings → Tools → Terminal.

idea-plugin.description:
Karma-Lens: Runtime Metrics and Code Insights for IntelliJ IDEA

Karma-Lens brings runtime and usage intelligence directly into the editor, so you can identify slow paths, high-traffic methods, and unused code while navigating Java sources.

What You Get

  • Method Inlay Metrics
    Inline method-level signals for throughput, error rate, and runtime behavior, with caching-aware refresh for responsive editor performance.

    Popup visualizations for method and API metric timelines to analyze trends and spikes over time.
  • Code Block Coverage and Throughput
    Branch/block-level indicators in the gutter to inspect execution distribution inside methods, available to signed-in users with a codekarma.tech email.
  • Dead/Unused Method Insights
    Project-level insights to surface methods that are likely unused and improve maintainability.
  • Real-Time and Cached Refresh Modes
    Quick cache refresh and real-time API refresh actions for balancing speed and freshness.

Who This Helps

  • Backend teams debugging production bottlenecks
  • Developers optimizing hot methods and expensive code paths
  • Teams improving maintainability with usage-based cleanups

Keywords: intellij plugin, java performance, method metrics, call hierarchy, dead code detection, throughput, code coverage, hotspots, runtime analysis

idea-plugin.change-notes:
Version 3.1.24

  • API Details: new Error chart with 4xx/5xx and HTTP status codes, plus total traffic and error percentages.
  • Method Details: charts show exception types.
  • The Update button now checks for plugin updates right away.

Version 3.1.23

  • New settings: show throughput in QPM or QPS (inlays and graph popups), and filter endpoint errors by 4xx or 5xx.
  • Call hierarchy detects async callers missed before.
  • Settings panel and Insights view tidied up to match the IDE theme.
  • Stability and reliability improvements.

Version 3.1.22

  • Improved editor refresh reliability and feature access.

Version 3.1.21

  • Performance enhancements.
  • Stability and reliability improvements.

Version 3.1.20

  • Performance enhancements.
  • Stability and reliability improvements.

Version 3.1.19

  • Performance enhancements.
  • Stability and reliability improvements.

Version 3.1.18

  • You can now select "--" in the service dropdown to turn Karma-Lens off for a project that has no instrumented service. Previously the selection snapped back to the previous service, and the only ways to clear it were switching domain or logging out.
  • Selecting "--" clears inlays and gutter markers and resets the insights counters, rather than reporting every method as dead code against a service the project does not run.
  • The periodic version check no longer switches Karma-Lens back on for a project you deliberately disabled, whether by logging out or by selecting "--".

Version 3.1.17

  • Karma-Lens no longer shows inlays or gutter markers while you are logged out, including when a session expires on its own rather than through an explicit logout.
  • Logging out now sticks - the plugin no longer switches itself back on at its next version check.
  • Code blocks whose status could not be fetched are no longer marked as dead code. They stay in a loading state instead of reporting working code as unused.
  • Gutter markers no longer flicker while metrics are unavailable.
  • Methods on inner classes now get correct inlays and block analysis, instead of being looked up under their enclosing class.
  • Methods on abstract base classes now resolve to their implementations' metrics instead of loading indefinitely.
  • Inlays keep updating after logging out and back in, without needing an IDE restart.

Version 3.1.16

  • Daemon restarts are now limited to visible editors, so refreshing a background tab no longer cancels highlighting in the file you are actually looking at.
  • A temporary backend error or expired session while a project is opening no longer disables Karma-Lens for the rest of the IDE session - the availability check is retried, and a failed check is no longer mistaken for "this service is not available".
  • Background failures (status refreshes, cache updates, call-hierarchy lookups) are recorded in the IDE log instead of raising notification popups, since none of them are user-actionable.
  • Cancelling background work - because a project was re-initialized, disabled, or closed - is no longer reported as an error.
  • Repeated identical notifications are collapsed instead of stacking up.

Version 3.1.15

  • Reduced daemon restarts racing Gradle/Maven project reimports, avoiding a rare IDE-internal disposal error.

Version 3.1.14

  • Fixed the version-outdated panel's Update button to avoid a private internal API.

Version 3.1.13

  • The Karma Lens panel now shows an outdated-version notice (with an Update button) whenever a newer version is available, so it's clear at a glance why functionality might be paused.

Version 3.1.12

  • Karma-Lens now checks for the latest version on startup and pauses functionality with a notification if you're not on the latest version - update from the notification to re-enable.

Version 3.1.10

  • Performance improvements: reduced memory usage and eliminated intermittent slowdowns on large projects.
  • Added lightweight runtime diagnostics: per-minute cache/restart/inlay summary line, payload telemetry on status fetches, and slow PSI-search warnings.

Version 3.1.9

  • Added support for dead code mode.

Version 3.1.8

  • Fixed an authentication freeze caused by OAuth discovery network calls running on the IDE event dispatch thread.
  • Improved login cancellation and cleanup while authentication startup is preparing the browser flow.

idea-plugin.name: FreeMarker Templates PRO
idea-plugin.description:
Full-featured FreeMarker template support for IntelliJ IDEA. Works with both angle-bracket (<#if>) and square-bracket ([#if]) syntax modes.

Editing

  • Syntax highlighting for directives, built-ins, macro calls, variables, strings, and operators
  • Smart completion auto-popup after [#, <#, [/@, </@, and ?
  • End-tag completion ([/@name]) ranked by innermost unclosed macro call
  • Named-argument completion for macro parameters
  • Built-in completion covering most of 100+ FTL built-ins
  • Code folding for macro declarations, #if/#list blocks, and macro call bodies

Navigation

  • Go to definition for local and imported macro declarations
  • Find usages across template files
  • Namespace-aware completion for ns.macro calls via [#import]
  • Cross-file reference resolution through macro libraries

Validation

  • Unresolved macro detection — both local and imported
  • Mismatched end-tag errors — [/@wrong] when a different macro is open
  • Orphan end-tag detection — [/@name] with no matching open tag
  • Unknown directive and unsupported built-in warnings
  • Misplaced #nested usage outside a macro or function body
  • Unresolvable [#import] and [#include] paths — warning on the path string
  • Unresolved import namespace — distinct from an unresolvable file

Language Support

  • Full expression grammar: operators, hash/sequence literals, lambdas, range expressions
  • Macro call body syntax: [@foo args]…[/@foo] and [@foo /] self-closing
  • Loop variable syntax: [@macro ; a, b, c]
  • Inline data-model annotations (@ftl-model, @ftl-var) for completion hints
  • Generic Java types in @ftl-model — java.util.List<com.example.Order> resolves field completions from Order
  • Loop variable completion — ${order.<caret>} inside <#list orders as order> offers fields from the list's item type
  • Multiple named models in one directive — @ftl-model orders: List<Order>, customers: List<Customer>
  • FTL output syntax control directives
  • Optional Java integration: data model from compiled classes

  • New: Generics support in @ftl-model annotator
  • New: Unresolvable [#import] and [#include] paths highlighted as warnings on the path string — distinct from unresolved namespace errors

idea-plugin.name: Dependency Assistant
idea-plugin.description:
Provides assisted upgrading of Maven, Gradle, GitHub Actions, NPM, and Antora dependencies, plus Maven and Gradle wrapper properties, in your IDE. The plugin highlights dependency declarations for newer versions and offers a controlled path to apply updates without replacing your own judgment about when to upgrade.

The support includes:

  • Maven: pom.xml, .mvn/extensions.xml, and maven-wrapper.properties
  • Gradle: build.gradle(.kts), settings.gradle(.kts), gradle.properties, gradle-wrapper.properties, and *.versions.toml version catalogs (Gradle)
  • GitHub Actions: .github/workflows/*.yml and action.yml
  • NPM: package.json (NPM)
  • Antora: antora-playbook.yml (Antora)
  • Determining upgrade candidates against Maven Central and custom Maven repositories (including settings.xml credentials and mirrors), the Gradle Plugin Portal, Gradle distributions, npmjs, GitHub releases, and Git tags
  • Completion, quick documentation, and gutter markers for versions in the editor
  • Interactive upgrade review: pick target versions per dependency, with patch, minor, major, preview, and release upgrade strategies
  • Upgrade Plan tool window to stage upgrades, preview changes, create GitHub tickets, and apply upgrades as a batch or one commit per upgrade
  • Dependency rules via dependencyfile.json to pin artifacts to generations and restrict upgrade strategies per branch
  • Inspections for version and declaration drift, dependency rule violations, unpinned GitHub Actions, and wrapper URL issues; intentions to insert wrapper SHA-256 checksums, open release notes, and report issues
  • Package Checker vulnerability information for Maven and npm packages when that IDE service is available, including safe-version remediation

First Steps

  • Open a build file in the editor.
  • Use the intention action (light bulb) on a dependency or plugin version and choose Upgrade dependencies….
  • Or use the menu action Tools | Dependency Assistant | Upgrade dependencies….

Requires IntelliJ IDEA 2025.2 or newer and installs on any IntelliJ-based IDE. Ecosystem support activates with the corresponding IDE plugins.

Source code | Wiki | Issue tracker
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.0

  • GitHub-specific template for ticket close references in commit messages.

  • Upgrade Plan refinements: Create All Tickets no longer depends on the current selection, and Git versions are restored as expected when a plan is loaded.

  • Upgrade notifications now offer a commit action for applied updates. Notifications expire once their action has been triggered, after subsequent edits, or after a global undo, so they do not linger beyond their usefulness.

  • Release metadata reminders come with refined dismissal options, clearer notification groups, and consistent title formatting.

  • Gradle refinements: Kotlin plugin helpers such as kotlin("jvm") are resolved, Kotlin val property parsing has been improved, and nested properties are excluded. Version element detection in Gradle and TOML files is more precise as a result.

  • Project state no longer goes stale after build files are removed or renamed. Maven and Gradle project contexts are cached.

  • npm Git dependency updates and version expression handling have been improved. Registry response parsing has been reduced to what is actually needed, with a fallback for oversized responses.

  • Antora dependency highlighting, version handling, and updates have been fixed, along with refined playbook detection and analysis.

  • Upgrades applied from the documentation panel now use the correct version identifiers.

  • Cancellation is handled consistently across services, with virtual-thread task scopes for parallel background work.

0.5.0-RC2

  • Plugin update notification. After updating the plugin, a notification summarizes the changes since the previously installed version. Change notes are taken from the plugin descriptor, no network lookup required.

  • Apply… and Apply and Commit… actions for selected Upgrade Plan items. Apply only the selected planned upgrades, optionally followed by a commit. Complements the existing Apply All actions.

  • Implicit upgrade groups for shared version properties. Upgrades bound to the same version property are grouped under that property instead of being listed as separate items. Reduces noise in the review dialog and in the Upgrade Plan.

  • Dependency Site Search now uses the Usage View. Declaration sites are listed as usages with refined icons and tooltips, so you can navigate and inspect them like any other Find Usages result.

  • Upgrade Plan refinements: badge on the tool window icon, clipboard paste validation with progress and notifications, adjusted batch limits for vulnerability scans.

  • Unpinned GitHub Action inspection considers the full uses: declaration, not only the version literal.

  • Updates are applied one-by-one; the completion notification distinguishes upgraded declarations from ones already up to date.

  • Refined ticket creation, error handling, and consistent notification messages.

  • Debounced Maven sync refresh and code analysis restart after Maven and Gradle imports.

  • Fix pom.xml updates writing to stale cached PSI elements for declarations and properties.

  • Fix release version detection for semver suffixes that are not pre-releases; snapshots are excluded.

  • Fix optional Kotlin module declaration; Gradle support no longer breaks without the Kotlin plugin.

  • Fix DumbAware on GitHub-related components during indexing.

  • Unified repository URL handling with artifact and group ID validation.

  • Stronger BOM caching and PsiFile-level caching.

  • Move off internal and deprecated Plugin SDK API.

  • Refactor ProjectName, and split SingleTableRow/GroupRow to decouple name rendering along with separating concerns. #10

0.5.0-RC1

  • Gradle support. Scans build.gradle(.kts), settings.gradle(.kts), gradle.properties, and version catalogs including multiple TOML catalogs, rich version constraints, version ranges, and platform/BOM blocks. Provides completion, documentation, and upgrades for Groovy and Kotlin DSL declarations.

  • GitHub Actions support. Scans workflows and action.yaml, resolves versions from GitHub releases and tags, and supports SHA pinning with release comments. Adds the Unpinned GitHub Action inspection with a quick-fix to pin to a known commit SHA (#1).

  • npm support. Scans package.json, resolves releases from npmjs, and handles version prefixes, ranges, and project version resolution. Shows release documentation and upgrade suggestions in completion.

  • Antora support. Scans antora-playbook.yml for ui.bundle.url versions and offers completion and upgrades. Resolves releases through GitHub release metadata.

  • Maven and Gradle wrapper support. Inspections flag wrapper URLs with plaintext credentials or non-canonical coordinates and offer quick-fixes to rewrite them. Intentions compute and insert SHA-256 distribution and wrapper checksums, guarded by trust checks.

  • Package Checker integration (#2). Vulnerability information for Maven and npm packages surfaces in gutter markers, completion, documentation, quick-fixes, color schemes, and the upgrade dialog. Vulnerable dependencies expose a safe target version, and BOM resolution detects vulnerable managed dependencies.

  • Upgrade Plan (#5). A tool window to stage dependency upgrades for later review, create tickets from planned upgrades, and apply the plan as a batch. Includes badges, preview of changes, ticket linking, and release notes navigation.

  • Dependency rules via dependencyfile.json. Pin artifacts to generations per artifact pattern and per branch, across multiple generations, with an optional semver toggle. Ships a JSON schema, completion, a creation action, an Add to dependencyfile action, and the Dependency Rule inspection.

  • Upgrade groups and grouping policies. Candidates are grouped by version agreement, name shape, or release history, either governed by rules or inferred. Groups render as one unit in the upgrade dialog.

  • Version and declaration drift inspection. Reports dependencies declared with different versions or mixed declaration styles across build files, with a Show all declaration sites quick-fix. Drift for SHA-pinned GitHub Actions is reported correctly (#3).

  • Dependency Site Search. Finds all declaration sites of an artifact across the project. Accessible from the upgrade dialog and the Upgrade Plan.

  • Intentions to open release notes and report a ticket (#6). Reuses project metadata to link to release notes on GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg, and SourceForge, and to the issue tracker.

  • Maven refinements. Mirrors, settings.xml credentials, parent updates, extensions and reporting plugins, extensions.xml, profile-specific repositories, and multi-file upgrades. Property updates through the update dependency action.

  • Upgrade strategies. RELEASE strategy, version-age category, snapshot and preview handling, versioning-scheme-specific ordering, and development-line based release proposals in completion.

  • Dependency check dialog refinements: artifact-focused navigation, balloon and upgrades-done notifications, cache age display.

  • Plugin no longer requires com.intellij.modules.java.

  • Honor trusted-projects gate for GitHub account resolution.

  • Color scheme options and icon refinements.

  • Fixes: TOML parsing and updating, NPM prefix baseline parsing, $-prefixed expression evaluation, Gradle build file enumeration, GitHub comment positioning and rendering, recoverable GitHub failures, cancellation handling, cache synchronization.

  • ArchUnit package boundary tests, CodeQL workflow, contribution guide.

0.5.0-M2

  • Externalize messages into a message bundle.

  • Migrate enforced text attributes to TextAttributeKey with proper defaults.

  • Move off deprecated and internal API.

0.5.0-M1

  • Initial release.

idea-plugin.name: Extra Tools Pack Lifetime
idea-plugin.description:
Same plugin as Extra Tools Pack, with a lifetime license (pay once, get updates for life).
Extra Tools Pack provides the exact same features as Extra Icons, Extra IDE Tweaks and Extra ToolWindow Colorful Icons. It's offered at a lower price than if you bought each plugin individually.

License types
— Extra Tools Pack offers monthly and yearly licenses.
— Extra Tools Pack Lifetime (new!) offers lifetime licenses: pay once, use it, and get updates forever.

There are two different plugins because JetBrains does not allow plugin developers to offer all the license types (monthly/yearly and lifetime) for the same plugin. Both plugins offer the exact same features. The only difference is the license.

Features from Extra Icons

Make your IDE more pleasant to use:
  • Adds 500+ icons for files like Travis YML, GitLab YML, Angular files, etc. Many icons have variants, so if you are not happy with the default icon, you can choose another.
  • Shows an icon for Git submodule folders.
  • Highly configurable: see File > Settings > Appearance & Behavior > Extra Icons to select extra icons to (de)activate. This is configurable at the IDE and project level.
  • You can register your own icons in order to define custom icons for certain files or file patterns.
  • You can override almost all IDE icons, including toolbars, menus, etc.
  • You can import and export icons from external files. This also means you can easily share icon themes with friends. You can also download online icon packs (example: restore the old file icons when using the new UI).
  • For more information, please see the online documentation.
  • JetBrains Gateway is no longer supported (it actually has never been fully supported).

Features from Extra ToolWindow Colorful Icons

Makes tool window and control icons colorful. This feature is based on the ToolWindow Colorful Icons plugin and adds several new icons. You can also choose icons to (de)activate: see Settings > Appearance & Behavior > Extra ToolWindow Colorful Icons.
You will get the exact same features as using Extra ToolWindow Colorful Icons with a paid license.

Features from Extra IDE Tweaks

Some utilities for IDE maintenance and tweaking, plus workarounds for a few IDE issues. See Tools > Extra IDE Tweaks. Features:
  • The Open Editors tool window shows opened files in all editors belonging to the opened project, as in VSCode. It can also display a list of recently opened files, as in the Recent Files action.
  • New experimental feature: the Updates tool window lists the dependencies updates of Gradle, Maven, and Node.js projects. It also lists the dependencies relocations of Gradle and Maven projects.
  • Can make folder icons more visible (with no outline style) when using the New UI. You can also use it with the regular UI.
  • Can change most tool windows label. Per example, rename the "Pull Requests" tool window to "PR".
  • Can confirm the opening of sensitive files. May be useful when streaming and/or accidentally opening a sensitive file in situations where you can leak critical information.
  • Can open projects located in trusted locations directly via File > Trusted Locations, just after Recent Projects.
  • Can register your favorite projects, organize them with optional groups, and gain fast access to your favorite projects via File > Favorite Projects, just after Recent Projects and Trusted Locations.
  • Can define default Excluded Folders (not per-project). There is now a global list of excluded folders. Go to Extra IDE Tweaks settings for details.
  • Commit Alert: this inspection allows you to define keywords that will show a confirmation dialog before committing files containing any of those keywords. Per example, define the COMMIT_ALERT keyword, modify, delete or move one or multiple files containing it, then commit. A confirmation dialog will appear asking if you still want to commit.
  • Activate All Tool Windows: this action activates all available tool windows in the current project. Enable it in settings, then see the "Window > Activate All Tool Windows" menu item. It's like clicking on the "..." button on the left-side toolbar, then clicking on each available tool window.
  • Can register any program and add it to the "Open In" list when doing a right-click on a file, a folder, or a project. Your program will be added next to the "Open In" Terminal action. That means you can open files and folders with your favorite program (like ForkLift, Total Commander, Vim...). You can register up to 2 "Open In" actions. Go to Extra IDE Tweaks settings for details.
    You can also open files with Associated Application. This additional action is enabled for IDEs prior to 2024 only, as it is already implemented by 2024+ IDEs.
  • Can open a folder as a Project via the "Open In" menu.
  • Can rename tab names to remove the parenthesis after the file names if they're located in the root project or module. Per example, renames "build.gradle.kts (my-module)" to "build.gradle.kts". For now, it works with "build.gradle", "build.gradle.kts", "build.gradle.dcl", "settings.gradle", "settings.gradle.kts" "settings.gradle.dcl" and "src/main/resources/META-INF/plugin.xml" files only.
  • Can purge IDE's plugin download cache. This is a workaround for known IDE limitation 🐛 IJPL-6179.
  • Can schedule the IDE's GC.
  • Can schedule the GC on local JVMs. May be useful when having multiple Gradle or Kotlin Compiler daemons consuming too much memory. You can choose to run the GC on selected JVMs: all local JVMs, or by filtering by JVM instance name with your own regexes.
  • Adds a Properties action to the File and Folder context menu that shows information like size, number of files, etc.
  • Adds a menu item under Tools in order to access the Plugins Manager faster.
  • Offers a workaround for known IDE issue 🐛 IDEA-341174: the Git tool window may display the wrong label "Version Control" instead of "Git".
Plugin's Chinese UI (插件的中文用户界面).
Huawei DevEco Studio support.

  • Smart Assignee Fallback: If the @username is not a collaborator on the repo, the plugin gracefully retries issue creation without the assignee instead of failing.
  • IDE Balloon Notifications: GitHub operations now show native IntelliJ balloon notifications with clear success/failure messages instead of silent log entries.

📋 Task Metadata

  • Creation Date: Every new task automatically records a created:YYYY-MM-DD timestamp when created via the + button.
  • Due Date (Optional): Assign an optional due:YYYY-MM-DD deadline to any task. Tasks are now sorted by due date first — closest deadlines float to the top.
  • GitHub User Assignment: Tag a GitHub username with @username directly in your TODO comments. Assigned users are displayed as a bold blue badge in the panel.
  • GitHub Issue Badge: Tasks linked to a GitHub Issue display a green [#142] badge for instant visual identification.

🔍 Advanced Filtering

  • User Filter: A new "All Users" dropdown dynamically populates with all @username tags found in your codebase, letting you filter tasks by assignee.
  • GitHub Status Filter: A new "All Tasks" dropdown lets you filter between tasks that are "Linked to Issue" vs "Not Linked", making triage effortless.

🔧 Settings

  • GitHub Integration Panel: A new "GitHub Integration" section in Preferences → Tools → SmartTodo with fields for Personal Access Token (masked), Repository Owner, and Repository Name.

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Metadata Preservation: Fixed a critical bug where changing a task's status (e.g., TODO → DONE) would silently strip all metadata (assignee, dates, issue ID) from the comment. All fields are now faithfully preserved on every rewrite.

idea-plugin.name: GitHub Account Switcher
idea-plugin.description:
Manage multiple GitHub accounts in one place. Stop re-entering tokens every time you push to a repo under a different account.

Features

  • Store multiple GitHub accounts with Personal Access Tokens
  • Tokens stored securely in IntelliJ's PasswordSafe — never written to disk in plain text
  • Per-project active account (persists across IDE restarts)
  • One-click switching from a status bar widget
  • Auto-detects GitHub remotes in each repository
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.3.1

  • Fix: GitHub Enterprise Server accounts could not be added — token verification called https://api.<host>/user, but Enterprise Server serves its API at https://<host>/api/v3. Verification, the startup health check and the Verify Token button now use the correct URL. GHE.com (*.ghe.com) is unaffected.

1.3.0

  • Account colour labels — tag each account with a colour so you can tell them apart at a glance. Shows in the settings list, the switcher popup and the status bar widget, alongside (not instead of) the token health dot.
  • Export / import accounts — save your account list to a file and restore it on another machine. Tokens are never exported; you re-enter and verify each one after importing. Accounts that already exist are skipped, not duplicated.
  • Auto-switch suggestion — opening a project owned by a different account than the active one now offers to switch. Fires only on an unambiguous match, and can be dismissed permanently per owner.
  • Pre-commit identity warning — if the email git is about to author with does not match the active account, you get a warning with the option to fix it inline, commit anyway, or cancel.
  • Fix: the startup token health check verified every token against api.github.com regardless of the account host, so GitHub Enterprise accounts could be reported as invalid while working fine. The same applied to the Verify Token button in settings.
  • Fix: the same username on github.com and on an Enterprise server was rejected as a duplicate. Both can now be added.

1.2.2

  • Fix: credentials not applied on new projects — switching accounts on a project with no remote yet (or a remote just added in the terminal) no longer requires an IDE restart or re-switch. The credential rule is written immediately and activates the moment a matching remote is added.

1.2.1

  • Security notice on first account apply — a one-time IDE balloon explains that the token in .git/config is local only, never committed to the repository, and not a security risk. Addresses false positives from AI assistants and security scanners that flag the url.insteadOf credential rewrite entry.

1.2.0

  • GitHub Enterprise Server support — add accounts hosted on a private GitHub Enterprise instance by entering the custom hostname (e.g. github.mycompany.com) in the new optional Host field. All credential injection and token verification use the configured host automatically.
  • Host field in Add / Edit Account dialog — leave blank for standard github.com; fill in only for GitHub Enterprise or custom GHES deployments. Changing the host after a successful verify resets the verification state, requiring a re-verify against the correct server.
  • Provider groundwork — internal model now carries a host field (default github.com) on every account. Existing accounts load without any migration — they get the default automatically.

1.1.0

  • Token health check on project open — the plugin silently re-verifies the active account's token each time a project opens. If the token has expired or been revoked you see an IDE balloon notification with an "Update Token" action before your first push.
  • Re-verify button in account list — a refresh button in the Settings → GitHub Accounts toolbar re-checks the selected account's token against the GitHub API and updates the status dot (● green = valid, ● red = invalid, ● grey = not yet checked).
  • Token scope warnings — after a successful verification, the dialog now warns if the classic PAT is missing the repo scope (push to private repos will fail) or the user:email scope (commit email unavailable). Fine-grained PATs (github_pat_ prefix) show an info note about required per-repo permissions.
  • Keyboard shortcut — the Switch GitHub Account popup is now bound to Ctrl+Shift+Alt+G by default (remappable via Settings → Keymap).
  • Email in status bar tooltip — hovering the status bar widget now shows the active account's commit email alongside the username.

1.0.2

  • Plugin icon — added recognisable icon (shown in the Marketplace listing and IDE plugin list), with a separate dark-theme variant.
  • Mandatory token verification — the OK button in Add / Edit Account is now disabled until the token has been verified against the GitHub API. The token field resets verification state automatically if edited after a successful verify.
  • No more silent failures — git config write errors are now surfaced as IDE balloon notifications instead of being silently swallowed.
  • Orphan rule cleanup — if an account is deleted while a repo still holds its credentials, the plugin now scans for and removes any leftover credential-embedded url.*.insteadOf rules automatically.
  • Identity backup & restore — pre-existing user.name / user.email values are backed up before the plugin overwrites them, and restored when the account is cleared.
  • Duplicate account guard — adding an account with a username that already exists now shows a warning and blocks the save.

1.0.1

  • Commit identity fix — switching accounts now also sets user.name and user.email in the repository's local git config so commit author matches the selected account.
  • New "Commit email" field in the Add/Edit Account dialog, auto-filled from the GitHub API on token verification and editable for accounts with a private GitHub email.
  • API fallback at switch time — if an existing account has no stored email, the plugin fetches it live using the stored token and caches the result.
  • widget and configurable extension IDs scoped under ghswitcher to allow future plugins from the same vendor to coexist cleanly. Plugin ID itself is unchanged — no user action required.

1.0.0

  • Initial release — multi-account management with per-project active selection and status bar widget.
