idea-plugin.name: Inline Unified Diff
idea-plugin.description:
You want to review your uncommitted changes before committing — but that means opening a diff panel, hunting for the file, scrolling to the right chunk, and then scrolling back to where you were in the editor. That context switch breaks flow, and it adds up.

Inline Unified Diff eliminates the round-trip. It overlays your uncommitted Git changes directly on your code — right where they happened — without leaving the editor.

When you toggle the diff on, every changed region is annotated inline:

  • Deleted lines appear as a red ghost block at the exact location where they were removed, showing the original text from HEAD.
  • Modified lines show the old version as a red ghost block immediately above the new (green-highlighted) lines.
  • Added lines are highlighted in green.

Each chunk shows a ✓ Keep and an ↩ Undo button:

  • Keep dismisses the diff overlay for that chunk, leaving your current text as-is.
  • Undo reverts the chunk back to the HEAD version (wrapped in a normal undoable write command).

Smart safety labels classify low-risk changes — whitespace adjustments, comment edits, dead code removal — so genuinely risky edits stand out at a glance.

How to activate

  • Press Ctrl+Alt+Shift+D to toggle the diff on/off for the current file.
  • Or click the status-bar icon at the bottom of the IDE window.
  • Or right-click in the editor and choose Toggle Inline Diff View.

Works with all JetBrains IDEs: IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, Rider, CLion, DataGrip, Android Studio, and more.

If you find this plugin useful, consider buying me a coffee ☕ — it helps keep the project alive!

Keywords: git, diff, code review, vcs, uncommitted changes, inline diff, unified diff, git diff, highlight changes, editor overlay, gutter diff

idea-plugin.name: erdMaid - Mermaid ERD Export for Database Tables
idea-plugin.description:
erdMaid is a Mermaid ERD export plugin for the IntelliJ Database tool window.

It is designed for developers who want a fast, accurate way to turn selected database tables into Mermaid erDiagram syntax without manually rewriting table metadata.

Key benefits:

  • Exports tables selected under a schema's Tables node in the Database tool window.
  • Works from the schema-level table list, where all tables for that schema are visible.
  • Preserves the actual column order from database metadata.
  • Includes primary keys, foreign key relationships, column types, and column comments.
  • Renders size information in a Mermaid-safe format.
  • Copies the generated diagram to the clipboard and shows a completion notification.

Typical workflow:

  1. In the Database tool window, expand a schema and open its Tables node.
  2. Select the Tables node to export every table in that schema, or select one or more individual tables under it to export only those tables.
  3. Right-click and choose Export as Mermaid ERD (erdMaid).
  4. Paste the generated Mermaid code into Markdown, docs, or any Mermaid-enabled editor.

Output details:

  • Table comments are emitted as %% Mermaid comments.
  • Column lines follow type name [PK] ["comment"].
  • Type names with whitespace are normalized to underscores.
  • Column comments are sanitized so Mermaid can parse the output safely.
  • Numeric precision and scale are rendered in a Mermaid-safe way.

Requirements:

  • IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate, DataGrip, or another IntelliJ-based IDE with database tooling.
  • A database connection with table metadata available in the Database tool window.

Notes:

  • classDiagram is intentionally not supported.
  • View support is out of scope for now.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Mermaid erDiagram export for physical database-table selections from the IntelliJ Database tool window.
  • Immutable canonical schema snapshots with datasource/origin-aware table and column identity, ordered PK/FK mappings, relation provenance, explicit unavailable/unknown states, and deterministic ordering.
  • Pure semantic compilation for relation constraints, multiplicity, and identifying/non-identifying semantics before Mermaid rendering.
  • Deterministic Mermaid serialization with context-specific hostile-text encoding, canonical entity IDs/aliases, PK/comments, physical/virtual provenance labels, and evidence-derived cardinality markers.
  • Executable Mermaid 11.17.2 grammar evidence bound to production fixtures and exact package integrity.
  • Exact maintained compatibility evidence split into compile/test runtime, Plugin Verifier binary compatibility, and DatabaseTools Host API Inventory classes for the documented IntelliJ IDEA/DataGrip targets.
  • Reproducible large-selection proof for 1000 tables x 40 columns / 3000 relations, including separate stage measurements, deterministic repeated output, bounded cooperative cancellation, no-publication, recovery, and concurrent-invocation isolation evidence.

Changed

  • Replaced the legacy synchronous generator/resolver/sanitizer path with a JetBrains host shell -> immutable snapshot -> pure semantic graph -> pure Mermaid serializer -> typed outcome -> guarded publication pipeline.
  • Selection handling now fails closed for mixed unsupported objects, cross-datasource selections, expansion/platform failures, stale completion, and unavailable structural evidence instead of silently filtering or guessing.
  • Relationship rendering no longer uses a universal legacy ||--o{ marker. Cardinality and identification connectors are emitted only from proven semantic evidence; unavailable required facts produce a degraded unpublished outcome.
  • Clipboard publication occurs only after complete success and final lifecycle/freshness checks; cancellation, failure, unsupported/degraded results, disposal/invalidation, and stale completion leave the clipboard untouched.
  • Consolidated repository/build identity now uses luceat-lux-vestra/erdMaid / erdMaid instead of the former erdMaid-private / erdMaid-public split names.

Evidence limits

  • DataGrip 2026.2.5 has maintained Plugin Verifier and exact DatabaseTools Host API Inventory evidence, but live GUI/database-tool-window runtime integration remains unverified.
  • IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate 2026.2.2 has maintained Plugin Verifier evidence, but a full Host API Inventory/runtime-test claim is not inferred from it.
  • Invocation-owned heap/GC retention after terminal completion remains unverified because no deterministic hosted-CI observation mechanism is claimed.

idea-plugin.name: GaussDB JDBC Driver
idea-plugin.description:
Bundles and automatically installs the GaussDB JDBC driver into JetBrains DataGrip and other IntelliJ-based IDEs.

GaussDB is a distributed relational database developed by Huawei, based on the openGauss kernel and compatible with PostgreSQL. This plugin ships the driver JAR files directly — no manual download or configuration is required. The driver is installed automatically on IDE startup and is immediately available for use in database connections.

Bundled driver version: 8.6.1 (huaweicloud-dws-jdbc)

Connection URL formats:

Standard connection: jdbc:gaussdb://<host>:<port>/<database>

IAM (Access Key) authentication: jdbc:dws:iam://<cluster-name>:<region>/<database>

IAM Authentication:

The plugin provides a dedicated GaussDB IAM (Access Key) authentication method for connecting via Huawei Cloud IAM credentials. When selected, the following fields are available in the authentication panel:

  • Access Key ID — IAM access key
  • Secret Access Key — IAM secret key (stored securely in the OS keychain)
  • IAM Username (DbUser) — the IAM username to map to a database user; hyphens (-) are not supported
  • Auto-create user — when enabled, automatically creates the DbUser in the database if it does not exist
idea-plugin.change-notes:

  • Standard connection support via jdbc:gaussdb:// URL
  • IAM (Access Key) authentication support via jdbc:dws:iam:// URL

idea-plugin.name: Agentic Review
idea-plugin.description:
Agentic Review brings a lightweight, PR-style review workflow into IntelliJ IDEA without requiring a remote pull request.

Its goal is to help you review uncommitted work, commits, commit ranges, or branch diffs inside the IDE, keep review comments as local workspace state, and hand unresolved work to coding agents in a structured way.

How to use it:

  • Open Tools | Open Agentic Review to start from your uncommitted changes.
  • Use Create Agentic Review from the VCS Log to review one or more commits.
  • Browse changed files, inspect diffs, and add inline review comments.
  • Copy the generated agent prompt or use the bundled MCP toolset to pass open comments to an agent for implementation.

Agentic Review is designed for local-first development workflows: self-review before commit, branch review before push, and agent-assisted follow-up on concrete review comments.

idea-plugin.name: MailKit
idea-plugin.description:
A comprehensive toolkit for working with email messages (EML / RFC 822 / MSG) directly in your IDE. MailKit offers syntax highlighting, code folding, smart inspections, and a fully featured embedded SMTP client for testing.

Editor & Formatting

  • Syntax Highlighting: Colorize headers, MIME boundaries, and body content. Customize colors per-header in the color scheme settings.
  • Code Folding: Collapse and expand nested MIME parts. RFC 2047 encoded header values (e.g. =?UTF-8?...?=) are automatically folded into human-readable text.
  • Customization: Add custom headers to the highlight list and toggle highlighting globally via Settings.
  • EML Comparison: Compare two .eml messages in the diff viewer. Headers, decoded bodies and attachments (matched by SHA-256) are normalized so encoding noise (base64 / quoted-printable, RFC 2047 encoded words, reordered headers, random MIME boundaries) no longer shows up as differences; a toolbar toggle flips between the decoded view and the raw source.

Attachments & Conversion

  • Attachment Management: Save attachments to disk or open them directly with the system app. Supports decoding for base64, quoted-printable, 7bit, 8bit, and binary parts. Includes confirmation prompts before opening executables.
  • Outlook MSG Conversion: Convert .msg files to standards-compliant .eml right from the Project view, complete with full internet transport header extraction. If original headers are missing, MailKit synthesizes them from MAPI properties and documents them in an X-MailKit-Synthesized-Headers field for full transparency. It also features multipart/alternative body selection and recursive embedded-message support. S/MIME messages keep their signed/encrypted envelope verifiable, calendar items export an invite.ics (with recurrence support and a stable meeting UID), contacts a vCard and tasks a VTODO, OLE-embedded objects survive as .ole attachments, and threading, importance, sensitivity, reply-to, categories and delegate-send (From/Sender) metadata is preserved.
  • Outlook PST/OST Conversion: Convert entire .pst or .ost archives into a directory tree of standard EML files, with duplicate handling, optional message limits, and seamless support for Highly Encrypted and Password Protected files. Automatically falls back to internal legacyExchangeDN routing addresses when standard SMTP information is missing. As with MSG conversion, messages lacking original internet headers have them synthesized from MAPI properties and recorded in an X-MailKit-Synthesized-Headers field. Optionally recovers soft-deleted and orphaned messages that are no longer linked into the folder tree. Calendar appointments and meeting requests are exported with an attached invite.ics — recurring series keep their recurrence rule, time zone and deleted occurrences, meeting responses record the attendee's accept/decline/tentative status, and a meeting's stable identifier is carried as the calendar UID so a later response or cancellation correlates with the original event. Delivery-status notifications and read receipts are reconstructed as a proper multipart/report, and S/MIME messages keep their signed/encrypted envelope verifiable (multipart/signed / application/pkcs7-mime) — parity with the MSG conversion. Contacts (vCard), tasks (VTODO), sticky notes, journal entries and distribution lists can be converted too via an opt-in checkbox; most other Outlook item types (documents, recall/remote/resend utility items, item-status reports) now convert as plain messages instead of being skipped, and an optional checksum-verification mode surfaces archive corruption that would otherwise pass silently. Sensitivity, conversation threading (Thread-Topic/Thread-Index), Reply-To and attachment Content-Location metadata survives the conversion.

Inspections & Validation

  • EML Inspections: Flag RFC 5322 / MIME violations inline. Includes checks for missing required headers, unterminated boundaries, base64 alphabet errors, charset mismatches, unparseable dates, and more.
  • Quick-Fixes: Easily resolve structural violations with Alt+Enter.

SMTP & Delivery Testing

  • Send EML: A powerful, swaks-equivalent embedded client. Send EMLs through configured profiles using STARTTLS, TLS-on-connect, and SASL (including SCRAM-SHA-256).
  • Quick Access: A MailKit button in the editor toolbar groups the per-file actions — Send EML… and Compare EML With… — in a dropdown; each can be toggled off in settings.
  • Batch Sending: Select several EML files and send them in one go — a shared envelope, per-file progress right in the dialog, and a choice to continue or stop when a message fails.
  • Advanced SMTP Features: ESMTP extensions, XCLIENT, HAProxy PROXY v1/v2, and per-send envelope overrides.
  • Save Overrides to Profile: Tweak the host, port, or envelope right in the Send dialog and optionally write the new values back to the selected profile — perfect for switching environments.
  • Verbatim Send: Your .eml is transmitted byte-for-byte and never rewritten (so a Bcc: header in the file is sent and visible to recipients); the envelope accepts display-name addresses and comma-separated recipient lists, and an optional "Normalize line endings (LF→CRLF)" toggle (on by default) can be turned off for true byte-for-byte transmission.
  • Profile Management: PasswordSafe-backed profiles manage everything from Security/TLS to Relay framing. Live tool-window transcript keeps you informed.

Source Code | Donation
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.3.1 - 2026-06-23

Fixed (conversion correctness)

  • An inline image in a converted .pst/.ost whose stored Content-ID happened to include angle brackets now displays in the message body instead of being demoted to a separate, non-displayed attachment — the .msg conversion already did this, so the two now match.
  • A digitally signed or encrypted (S/MIME) message converted from .msg/.pst/.ost whose secure envelope carries a non-ASCII filename now encodes that filename correctly in the attachment's MIME parameters instead of placing raw non-ASCII bytes there, so strict mail clients no longer reject or mis-display the name. The usual ASCII smime.p7m envelope is unchanged.
  • An HTML message converted from a .msg/.pst/.ost that stored its body only as rich text (HTML-encapsulated RTF) no longer loses a run of body text that immediately followed certain RTF escapes — such as a non-breaking space, optional hyphen, or a literal backslash or brace — and the literal backslash and brace characters those escapes represent are now kept in the recovered HTML instead of being dropped along with the text after them.
  • A recurring appointment converted from .msg/.pst/.ost whose stored monthly recurrence is corrupt — an out-of-range day-of-the-month or week-of-the-month value — no longer produces an invalid repeat rule that a strict calendar client rejects outright (silently dropping the entire series); the event is now exported as a single clean occurrence instead.
  • An attachment converted from .msg/.pst/.ost whose filename is unusually long no longer emits an over-length header line that violates the email line-length limit and that strict mail clients may reject or truncate; an over-long name is now wrapped across RFC 2231 continuation parameters, while ordinary-length filenames are unchanged.
  • A meeting that was originally received from a non-Outlook calendar program and then converted from .msg/.pst/.ost now keeps that meeting's own original identifier as the calendar entry's UID, so a later acceptance, update, or cancellation still matches the original meeting in your calendar client instead of appearing as a separate, unrelated event.
  • A meeting response converted from a .pst/.ost no longer names a blind-carbon-copy (Bcc) recipient as the meeting's organizer in the generated calendar entry — matching the .msg conversion, which already hid Bcc recipients — so a blind recipient is not disclosed to the other attendees.
  • A delivery-status (bounce / non-delivery) report converted from .msg/.pst/.ost that no longer carried the failed recipient's address no longer places a list of display names where an email address belongs in the report's Final-Recipient field; it now reports unknown there instead, so the report stays valid for mail clients and tools that parse it.
  • An HTML message converted from a .pst/.ost that stored its body only as rich text (HTML-encapsulated RTF) no longer leaves a stray backslash or brace character in the recovered text when a non-Latin character was followed by an alternate plain-text version (its fallback) that itself started with one of those escapes — matching the .msg conversion, which already discarded the fallback.
  • An HTML message converted from a .pst/.ost no longer loses the rest of a <meta> character-set tag — a trailing parameter such as ; format=flowed, or any attribute that follows the character set — when the declared character set is rewritten to UTF-8; only the character-set value is changed now, and the remainder of the tag is preserved.
  • A read-receipt notification converted from .msg/.pst/.ost now writes the acknowledged message's identifier in angle brackets in the receipt's Original-Message-ID field when the stored value lacked them, so strict mail clients accept the receipt and can match it back to the message it confirms.

idea-plugin.name: LogTrace
idea-plugin.description:
LogTrace - Java Log Source Tracing Tool

LogTrace is a powerful IDE plugin that helps developers quickly locate the source code where log statements are printed. Simply paste log lines and jump directly to the corresponding source code location, eliminating the need for manual keyword searching.

LogTrace - JAVA日志溯源工具

粘贴日志行，一键跳转到打印该日志的源代码位置。告别手动搜索日志关键词的低效流程。

How to Use / 使用方式

  1. Copy log text from Kibana / Console / 复制日志文本
  2. Paste into the LogTrace tool window / 粘贴到 LogTrace 工具窗口
  3. Click "Parse" button / 点击"解析"按钮
  4. Click a match result to jump to source code / 在匹配结果列表中点击，跳转到源代码

Key Features / 核心功能

  • Log Parsing / 日志解析: Auto-detect Tab-separated (Kibana export), Logback, and other common formats / 自动识别 Tab 分隔（Kibana 导出）、Logback 等常见日志格式
  • Smart Matching / 智能匹配: Exact → Parameterized → Fuzzy, three-level matching strategy for high hit rate / 精确匹配 → 参数化匹配 → 模糊匹配，三级匹配策略确保高命中率
  • One-Click Jump / 一键跳转: Click match results to navigate directly to the source code line / 点击匹配结果直接跳转到源代码行
  • Multi-Framework / 多框架支持: SLF4J / Logback / Log4j2 / JUL / Lombok @Slf4j
  • Project Indexing / 项目索引: Scan project log statements to build an index for faster matching / 扫描项目日志语句建立索引，加速后续匹配
  • Logback Config Auto-Detection / Logback配置自动检测: Automatically reads project logback.xml patterns for precise parsing / 自动读取项目 logback.xml 配置，实现精准解析
  • Language Switching / 语言切换: Toggle between Chinese and English interfaces in Settings → Tools → LogTrace / 在 Settings → Tools → LogTrace 中切换中英文界面

idea-plugin.name: Branch Lens
idea-plugin.description:
Branch Lens shows how the file you are editing differs across your active Git branches—without checking out those branches or leaving the editor.

Small gutter badges identify changed lines and blocks. Hover for the affected branches, author, date, and commit subject; click to open IntelliJ's diff viewer at that line. Right-click a badge to inspect or copy its commit, open it in Git Log, copy the summary, or configure branch scope. The Branch Lens tool window groups identical results by originating change by default; switch off By Change for the traditional branch-first view.

Choose the branches that matter to your project:

  • Recent — analyze recently updated branches.
  • Pinned — focus on branches such as main, release/*, or a teammate's feature.
  • All — analyze every branch within the configured safety limit.
  • Include remote-tracking refs already present in the local repository by default. Matching local/upstream refs at the same commit are shown once as a paired entry; diverged pairs remain separate and show their outgoing/incoming commit counts as diverged ↑ahead ↓behind.

Branch Lens never fetches and makes no network requests. Git's own diff and blame remain the source of truth, and ambiguous edits are shown as changed blocks instead of invented line mappings. When a file was renamed on another branch, Branch Lens resolves its branch-side path before comparing it.

Diff windows opened by Branch Lens include author/date annotation columns on both sides. Current-only lines use current-snapshot blame, so committed additions show their author and date while working-tree additions are labeled uncommitted.

Branch Lens compares each side's blame commit with the branches' merge base to distinguish changes such as added on current, removed on branch, and modified independently. This is history-based evidence rather than a guess from the diff direction; rewritten or cherry-picked history may still be labeled history unclear.

When many branches produce the same outcome at a line, the gutter popup shows one summary such as 8 branches — present only in current. Choose that row only when you need to drill down to a particular branch's full-file diff.

Contiguous lines affecting the same branch cohort share one badge at the start and a vertical gutter marker spanning the region. Line pairing and branch-side blame may vary inside the region without fragmenting it. If every grouped branch would produce the exact same full-file diff and attribution, Branch Lens opens one common diff labeled 8 equivalent branches; otherwise it keeps the branch drill-down.

The change-first tool-window header shows the origin commit, affected line range, how many selected branches differ, and how many branch tips contain that exact commit. Right-click it for commit details, Git Log navigation, hash copying, or a newline-separated list of affected branches. Its toolbar provides immediate Recent / Pinned / All / Remotes scope controls.

Badge meanings:

BadgeMeaning
1–9Number of selected branches where this line differs.
9+10 or more branches differ.
±At least one changed-block difference (ambiguous).
+Only branch-side insertions anchor to this line.
?File is missing in (at least one of) the branches.

The action Compare File with Git Branch… is available from the editor context menu and Find Action. Configure branch scope and performance limits under Settings → Tools → Branch Lens.

Documentation · Report an issue · Source code
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Merge-base-aware lineage labels distinguish additions, removals, one-sided modifications, independently modified lines, pre-divergence differences, and uncommitted current changes.
  • The tool window defaults to a change-first view: one header per contiguous change shows its origin commit, affected line range, differing-branch count, and exact commit propagation across the selected branch tips. By Change toggles back to the branch-first view.
  • Tool-window scope controls switch directly between Recent, Pinned, and All, with a separate Remotes toggle.
  • Commit context actions show commit details, open the revision in IntelliJ Git Log, copy its hash, and copy all affected branch names from a change header. Commit actions are also available from gutter and Branch Lens diff annotations.
  • Current-snapshot blame identifies the author and date of committed current-side changes and clearly marks unsaved or uncommitted lines.
  • Branch Lens diff windows show built-in author/date annotation columns for both sides, including revision data that IntelliJ's disabled generic Annotate action cannot provide for synthetic branch content.
  • Gutter popups collapse branches with the same line-level outcome into one summary row. Selecting it reveals the individual branches for a specific full-file diff.
  • Consecutive lines affecting the same branch cohort render as one gutter region, even when line pairing or branch-side blame changes inside the Git hunk.
  • Multiline regions use one count badge plus a vertical gutter marker spanning the affected lines instead of repeating the badge on every line.
  • When grouped branches have identical file snapshots, paths, and relevant blame, Branch Lens opens one shared diff labeled with the equivalent-branch count.
  • Project-specific branch scopes: recent branches, pinned branches only, or all branches within the configured limit.
  • Optional analysis of locally available remote-tracking refs. Branch Lens still performs no fetches and makes no network requests.
  • Automatic refresh when Git4Idea reports a branch or repository-state change.
  • Rename-aware lookup when the current file has a different path at a branch tip.
  • A grouped tool-window view with one section per affected branch and accurate unique-line and affected-branch counts.
  • Diff viewers opened from a gutter badge or tool-window row now start at the selected line.
  • Accessible names for gutter badges.
  • Gutter context actions for opening the branch diff, copying a plain-text summary, and configuring branch scope.

Changed

  • Locally available remote-tracking branches are included by default.
  • A local branch and its configured upstream are collapsed into one local ↔ remote entry when both refs point to the same commit. Diverged pairs remain separate.
  • The analysis header and branch entries show upstream status with commit counts: ahead ↑N, behind ↓N, or diverged ↑N ↓N.
  • Current-side-only lines are described as “present only in current” or “absent in branch” when history cannot resolve their lineage; otherwise the merge-base-aware label identifies whether the current branch added the line or the other branch removed it.
  • Branch analysis now runs concurrently within the configured Git process limit.
  • Blame is limited to the branch-line range involved in the diff instead of the entire file.
  • Analysis and blame caches are bounded by estimated memory weight as well as entry count.
  • Settings changes invalidate cached results and immediately reanalyze open files.
  • The Marketplace description now leads with the user workflow instead of internal model names.
  • IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin updated to 2.18.1, with verification extended through the 2026.1 platform line.

Fixed

  • Repository-relative paths are canonicalized, fixing false “file missing” results for macOS path aliases such as /var and /private/var.
  • Unequal changed blocks no longer produce duplicate rows for every line in the block.
  • Insertions before line 1 are now visible in both the gutter and tool window.
  • Files over the configured byte limit are skipped on both sides of the comparison.
  • maxFileBytes and branch-scope settings now participate in cache invalidation.
  • Missing files are no longer listed twice in the tool window.

idea-plugin.name: Inheritance Lens

Use it when you want to understand a child class without jumping back and forth through its parent classes and interfaces.

idea-plugin.name: Task Worktree
idea-plugin.description:
Create git worktrees from IntelliJ tasks, or define custom ones — branch a folder next to your repo and open it as a new IntelliJ project in a single step.

Features

  • Pick from open tasks across any configured task server (TargetProcess, Jira, YouTrack, GitHub, …) and spawn a worktree for the matching branch, or create a custom worktree on any new or existing local branch.
  • Searchable, two-section picker (existing worktrees + tasks) with type-to-filter for both the item list and the branch selector.
  • Create a new branch from any chosen base ref (local or remote) — branch a worktree off e.g. main without switching to the main worktree first. Picking a remote branch creates a local tracking branch.
  • Open or remove existing worktrees inline. Select several at once (Shift+Arrows, Cmd/Ctrl+Click) and remove them in one pass, with a single confirmation and a batched force retry for any worktree git refuses. The main repo worktree is protected from deletion.
  • Optionally copies the source repo's .idea/ into each new worktree so the IDE opens with project settings intact.
  • Copy additional un-tracked files (e.g. .env, config/**) from the main repo working tree into every new worktree using configurable glob patterns — directories are copied recursively.
  • Automatically drops the removed worktree's path from Recent Projects; one-click bulk cleanup of stranded greyed-out entries.

Settings under Settings | Tools | Task Worktree (applied globally across projects): base worktrees directory, the .idea/ copy toggle, additional files-to-copy glob patterns, configurable branch and worktree folder name patterns (variables: id, number, type, summary, project), and a task type remapping table.

Default shortcut: Alt+Shift+P.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.5

  • Remove several worktrees in one pass. Select multiple rows in the picker with Shift+Arrows or Cmd/Ctrl+Click, then press the right arrow for a Remove menu. A single confirmation lists everything that will be deleted.
  • Worktrees git refuses to remove (modified or untracked files, locked) are collected into one batched --force retry prompt instead of a dialog each, and the result arrives as a single summary notification.
  • Rows that cannot be removed — the main worktree, full clones, task rows — are ignored inside a multi-row selection, so an overshot Shift+Arrow does not block the removal. Selecting a single row behaves exactly as before.

0.1.4

  • Compatibility with IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2 (build 262). Task Management, which this plugin requires, was unbundled from the IDE in 2026.2 — it now installs automatically from the Marketplace alongside this plugin.

0.1.3

  • New Show all worktrees checkbox in the picker popup: when checked, the list also includes worktrees of other repositories found in the configured worktrees directory, labeled with their owning repo. Pressing the action's shortcut again while the popup is open toggles the checkbox.
  • External worktrees can be opened and removed (removal runs against their own repository); full clones living in the worktrees directory are open-only.

0.1.2

  • Fixed a NoClassDefFoundError that crashed the picker when the GitHub plugin was disabled. The PR-status availability check no longer forces the GitHub-dependent code to load, so the action works again with GitHub off and still shows PR badges when it is enabled.

0.1.0

  • Existing worktrees now show their GitHub pull-request status as an outlined badge (DRAFT, OPEN, MERGED, CLOSED) on the right of each row in the picker. Statuses load asynchronously via the bundled GitHub plugin and are skipped silently when it is disabled or no GitHub account is configured.

0.0.7

  • Refreshed the plugin description to cover base-ref selection and the additional files-to-copy setting.

0.0.6

  • New Additional files to copy setting: copy un-tracked files (e.g. .env, config/**, *.local.properties) from the main repo working tree into every new worktree. Paths are relative to the repo root, glob syntax is supported, directories are copied recursively, and patterns matching nothing are skipped.

0.0.5

  • Branch and worktree folder names are now driven by configurable patterns under Settings | Tools | Task Worktree, with variables ${id}, ${number}, ${type}, ${summary} and ${project} (both default to ${id}).
  • Task summaries are sanitized before use — spaces become _ and special characters are dropped.

idea-plugin.name: Waypoints
idea-plugin.description:
Filtered back/forward navigation. Only intentional jumps (Go to Declaration, Find Usages, Go to Implementation, etc.) become waypoints; the incidental cursor movements the platform's Back action records every time you click around in the editor are ignored.

By default the plugin overrides the platform Back and Forward actions, so your existing Ctrl+Alt+Left / Ctrl+Alt+Right shortcuts (and the toolbar arrows) drive the filtered waypoint stack. Turn the override off in Settings | Tools | Waypoints to keep the platform's original behavior; the waypoint stack remains reachable via the dedicated Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Left / Right shortcuts.

The whitelist of which action IDs count as a waypoint is configurable in the same settings page.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.4.0
  • Forward after Back returns to the original waypoint target, not your last manual click — manual cursor movements no longer pollute the back/forward stack.
  • Recording is more reliable: jumps where the target snapshot lands on the same line (popup-driven actions like GotoFile) are no longer dropped. Tail-dedup keeps the back stack from growing on rapid-fire actions from the same spot.
  • Internal: platform Back / Forward override is now installed programmatically and no longer pins the plugin to descriptor- level overrides. Updates still require restart (replaceAction is detected as shared-state mutation by the IntelliJ Platform's dynamic-unload check).
0.3.0 — First release under the Waypoints name (renamed from Jump-Only Navigation). Override of platform Back / Forward is now a setting (on by default). Dedicated Waypoints Back / Forward actions at Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Left / Right stay reachable regardless of the override setting. First-run balloon explains the override and links to the toggle.

idea-plugin.name: Chevron Lists
idea-plugin.description:
Chevron Lists turns your JetBrains IDE into a fully-featured task, notes, and project management system - without leaving markdown. It layers >, >>, >>> blockquote nesting onto plain .md files for clean, readable hierarchies that render the same everywhere markdown is supported.

Features

  • Syntax highlighting - chevron prefixes are coloured so section structure stands out at a glance.
  • Live diagnostics - duplicate > Section headers, duplicate ## markdown subheadings, broken numbered-list sequences, and empty sections all get warning underlines with helpful hover messages.
  • Smart Enter key - pressing Enter on a chevron line continues the list automatically (>> - after a bullet, >> 2. after >> 1., etc.). Empty list items break out of the list.
  • Auto-fix numbering - broken sequences like >> 1., >> 2., >> 2. renumber themselves silently as you type. Lists in different sections stay independent.
  • Item actions - toggle done (Ctrl+Alt+D), star (⭐), pin (📌), flag (🚩), and note (📝) on a single item or across a multi-line selection. Right-click in the editor or use Ctrl+Shift+A → CL:.
  • Settings panel - under Settings → Tools → Chevron Lists you can choose the bullet character (-, *, etc.), make new lists default to numbered, and toggle auto-fix.

Example

> Today's Tasks
>> 1. Review PR #142
>> 2. ⭐ Ship Chevron Lists JetBrains v0.8
>> 3. 🚩 Investigate memory leak report

> Notes
>> - 📌 Team retro on Friday at 14:00

About

This is the official JetBrains port of the Chevron Lists VS Code extension. Markdown files written in either editor render identically in the other - both plugins share the same syntax and conventions.

Source code, issue tracker, and contributions: github.com/LewisIsWorking/ChevronListsJetBrains
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Filter by Tag (right-click menu, or Find Action). Pick a #tag from those the file's items carry, with how many items have each, then pick one of those items to jump to it. Both lists filter as you type. Tags follow this plugin's rule (a letter first) and match in any case.
  • Archive Done Items (right-click menu, or Find Action). Moves the done ([x]) items of the section at the caret into a > Archive section, created at the end of the file if there is none. Each done item takes everything nested under it along, so no children are left behind under the wrong item.
  • Go to Section (right-click menu, or Find Action; bind a key under Keymap if you like). A searchable list of the file's > Header sections with their item counts; type to filter, Enter to jump. The JetBrains counterpart of the VS Code extension's Filter Sections.
  • Sections fold. Every > Header section gets a fold in the gutter, so Fold All / Unfold All and the gutter arrows work on sections. A folded section shows its header and item count, such as > Groceries (12 items), and it is this fold, not the Markdown plugin's block quote fold, that Collapse All shows. The fold ends at the section's last line, so the blank line before the next header stays visible.
  • Mark All Done / Mark All Undone (Section) (right-click menu, or Find Action). Ticks or clears every checkbox item in the section at the caret; an item without a checkbox is left alone, as in the VS Code extension.

idea-plugin.name: Koog Strategy Graph
idea-plugin.description:
Visualization for Koog agent strategy { ... } DSL blocks.

A gutter icon next to every recognized strategy(...) call renders the strategy as a Mermaid state diagram in the Koog Strategy tool window. The diagram is produced by Koog's own MermaidDiagramGenerator: the plugin lifts the strategy { } snippet into a temporary program, compiles it against your module, runs it, and displays the result — so the graph always matches Koog's real interpretation of the strategy. This requires the code to compile.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.11

  • Performance improvements: rendering a diagram is noticeably faster, and the background workers that compile and run it use much less memory and CPU, including when idle.

0.1.10

  • Strategies whose enclosing function declares Kotlin's context(name: Type) parameters now render, instead of always failing with a "This file has compile errors" notice: the snippet compile now enables the feature (needed on IDEs bundling a Kotlin compiler older than 2.4, which stabilized it), and the generated runner supplies a mock receiver for each context parameter.

0.1.9

  • The diagram no longer leaves behind a stray, half-rendered graph when a render fails: orphaned SVG elements are cleaned up so the next render starts from a clean slate.
  • More robust graph generation for the different kinds of strategy declarations, including strategies produced by generic factory functions, which now resolve and render more reliably.

0.1.8

  • Fix occasional IndexNotReadyException error on startup

0.1.7

  • Compile failures are no longer shown as raw kotlinc diagnostics (whose temporary-directory paths looked like a plugin error). When the strategy can't compile because of another file — typically a stale or unbuilt dependency — the graph now shows a clear "There are compile errors. Rebuild your project and refresh." notice, where refresh is a link that re-generates the graph just like the toolbar button.
  • Compile errors in the strategy's own file are no longer surfaced separately — you already see them in the editor. A previously rendered diagram stays on screen while you fix them; if there is no diagram yet, a brief "fix the compile errors" notice is shown instead of a stuck spinner.
  • Errors no longer blank the canvas: while a valid diagram is on screen, a compile or graph error appears in an unobtrusive strip along the bottom, so live edits don't flip the view back and forth between the graph and an error message.
  • Graph (strategy) errors and compile errors are now clearly distinguished, and the old "Graph problems" list was removed in favour of the single relevant message.

0.1.6

  • Node factories defined in a separate file (e.g. a helper object) are now supported: when the snippet-only compile can't resolve them — typically an unbuilt module — the referenced same-module sources are pulled into the compile, so the graph renders instead of failing.
  • The compile's JVM target is now taken from the module's SDK, so strategies in modules whose dependencies target a newer JVM no longer fail with an "cannot inline bytecode built with JVM target …" error.
  • Click-to-navigate and caret highlighting now follow node factories across files (including Receiver.factory() calls), jumping to the helper's declaration.
  • Navigating to a node/edge no longer recenters the editor when the target line is already visible — it only scrolls when needed.
  • A small, unobtrusive gray hourglass appears in the corner of the diagram while it is regenerating.
  • Reformatting-only edits (whitespace, comments) no longer trigger a re-render; editing a same-file helper now does.
  • Performance: graph generation and the PSI work behind caret highlighting and click navigation now run off the UI thread, so they no longer cause editor hangs or slow-operation warnings.

0.1.5

  • The tool window now has an always-visible list of every strategy { } in the project (found via the IDE's index, so it's instant). Click a strategy to preview its graph beneath the list; double-click or press Enter to jump to its source, or use the right-click Open in New Tab to open it in its own pinned tab.
  • Graph tabs can be detached into their own floating window (the Detach to Window toolbar button, or the list's right-click Open in New Window), so several strategies can be compared side by side.
  • Added a refresh button to the tool window that re-generates the open graphs (and detached windows).
  • Graphs (and the list) refresh automatically after a project build finishes, so they reflect freshly compiled module output.
  • Reverse navigation: moving the editor caret onto a node declaration or an edge(…) highlights the matching node/edge in the graph — including subgraphs and edges inside them.
  • Strategies that are members of a class with non-mockable constructor parameters (String, primitives) now render: those arguments get a literal default instead of a mock.

0.1.4

  • Strategies defined as members of a class, object or companion object are now supported: the class is instantiated with mockk(relaxed = true) per constructor parameter, so member helpers and injected dependencies resolve.

0.1.3

  • Fixed unresolved references to sibling files/declarations when rendering a strategy in a Gradle-delegated module: the module's compiled output directories are now added to the compile classpath and friend paths.

0.1.2

  • Graphs are now rendered with Koog's own MermaidDiagramGenerator: the strategy { } snippet is compiled against your module and run, so the diagram always matches Koog's real interpretation.
  • Click a node to jump to its declaration, and click an edge (with a forgiving hit area) to jump to its edge(from forwardTo to) definition.
  • The graph refreshes automatically as you edit, keeping the last valid diagram while the code is incomplete.
  • Graph validation and compile errors are listed in a Problems-style panel without discarding the current diagram.
  • Strategy tabs are pinnable and closable, like search results.

0.1.0

  • Initial release: gutter icon + popup graph.

idea-plugin.name: LinkedIn Connected Apps
idea-plugin.description:
This plugin generates a proficiency level based on how you actually work with your IDE and lets you share it directly on your LinkedIn profile.

Features

  • Proficiency level based on real usage – the plugin monitors how you use IDE features in the background and calculates your proficiency level automatically.
  • LinkedIn integration – securely connect to LinkedIn via OAuth and share your proficiency level as real-time work experience, on your profile.
  • Status bar widget — a convenient widget in the IDE status bar shows your current proficiency level and provides quick access to all plugin actions.

How to get started

Once installed, the plugin starts observing how you use your IDE locally. A LinkedIn icon appears in the status bar at the bottom of your IDE window. Click the status bar icon to open a popup that displays your current proficiency level.

Sharing your proficiency to LinkedIn

  1. Click the LinkedIn icon in the status bar to open the plugin popup.
  2. Click the "Connect to LinkedIn" button.
  3. If you are not yet logged in, a browser window will open asking you to authorize the plugin with your LinkedIn account. Complete the authorization flow in the browser.
  4. Your proficiency will be automatically shared to LinkedIn as soon as you get a new level, and you can see it under your connected apps.

Leveling up

Your proficiency level updates automatically as you use more IDE features. When your level increases, the status bar widget reflects the change.

Requirements

  • A JetBrains IDE version 2025.3 or later.
  • A LinkedIn account to share your proficiency level.
  • A JetBrains account to link to your LinkedIn account.

Privacy

The plugin uses OAuth to securely authenticate with LinkedIn. The plugin never stores your LinkedIn credentials — only access and refresh tokens are kept in the IDE's secure credential store. The plugin communicates with LinkedIn's API solely to create or update your proficiency level.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Added social login

idea-plugin.name: Glowtrace for Python
idea-plugin.description:
Runtime values for Python, without stopping your program

Glowtrace for Python captures values, output, exceptions, and execution history while you run Python code normally from the IDE. It is designed for the moments when print debugging is too noisy and the debugger is too slow or intrusive: hot loops, data transformations, algorithm demos, flaky state changes, and quick "what did this variable become?" checks.

Unlike debugger-only inline values, Glowtrace works with plain Run. Your process keeps moving, breakpoints are not required, and captured values stay available after the run finishes.

Inline runtime values

  • Shows the latest captured value directly beside the source line.
  • Captures values from marked probe lines and displays them in the editor.
  • Updates inline hints when new data arrives, including for editors opened after a run.
  • Click an inline value to inspect it without switching context.

Debugger-style value inspection

  • Inline popups use the same tree-style value presentation as the IDE debugger.
  • Expand nested lists, dictionaries, objects, and child values when captured by the agent.
  • Switch between the latest run and all captured runs for a line.
  • Copy the latest value or open the selected line in the Glowtrace tool window.

Glowtrace tool window

  • Browse all captured events in a dedicated bottom tool window.
  • Use either a flat event table or a lazy tree grouped by file, line, run, and nested value.
  • Filter by search text and event kind: value, output, or exception.
  • Open source locations with Enter, F4, double-click, or autoscroll.
  • Inspect full values in a details pane without leaving the tool window.
  • Delete noisy captured events from the current session.
  • Load large sessions incrementally so stress runs remain responsive.

Run history and comparison

  • Keeps per-line history across reruns when history retention is enabled.
  • Shows repeated captures for loops and reruns instead of only the final value.
  • Displays compact timing information for repeated captures, including average and max gaps.
  • Compare the two most recent runs in the IDE diff viewer.
  • When multiple rows are selected, Compare Runs narrows the diff to that selection.

Pinned watchpoints

  • Pin important file, line, and variable combinations so they stay visible while you explore.
  • Pins are stored per project and restored by the IDE.
  • Pinned rows resolve the latest value for the specific variable name, not just the latest event on the line.

Coverage and exception signals

  • Tracks which source lines emitted Glowtrace events during a run.
  • Marks lines that raised exceptions with a gutter indicator.
  • Highlights failure signals without turning every executed line into visual noise.

AI and MCP export

  • Export the current trace as deterministic JSON for AI-assisted debugging.
  • Export the whole session or only selected events from the tool window.
  • Includes a standalone Python MCP server resource for clients that can read trace snapshots.
  • Snapshot data includes locations, values, exceptions, output, timestamps, sessions, and nested children.

Settings and safeguards

  • Enable or disable Glowtrace globally.
  • Configure maximum value length, collection size, and retained events per line.
  • Exclude paths by glob to avoid capturing vendor or generated code.
  • Control whether history is retained between runs.
  • Event updates are coalesced to keep the IDE responsive during high-volume traces.

Pro features

  • History retention across runs.
  • Pinned watchpoints.
  • Run comparison.
  • Coverage indicators.
  • MCP snapshot export.

Glowtrace is especially useful for understanding code that changes quickly over time: dynamic data structures, algorithm steps, parser state, pandas or pydantic transformations, loop-heavy code, and intermittent exceptions where stopping at a breakpoint changes the behavior you are trying to observe.

idea-plugin.name: Input Remapper

It can be toggled from the status bar, through the Tools menu, or by using a customizable keyboard shortcut configured in the IDE Keymap. The plugin can be configured through the IDE settings. idea-plugin.name: GLoC Reactor Generator
idea-plugin.description:
GLoC Reactor Generator

A RustRover plugin that scaffolds GLoC reactor files directly from the Project view, so you never have to write the boilerplate by hand.

Features

  • New → GLoC Reactor context-menu action on any directory in the Project view
  • Live preview of the generated Rust source before the file is created
  • Two reactor modes:
    • Simple — state struct + #[reactor(state = …)] with self.emit(…) stubs
    • With Neutrons — adds a #[derive(Debug)] neutron enum and a fire() / on_event() dispatch handler
  • PascalCase name validation with inline error messages
  • File opens automatically in the editor after creation

Usage

  1. Right-click a directory in the Project tool window.
  2. Choose New → GLoC Reactor.
  3. Enter a PascalCase reactor name (e.g. Counter, CartItem).
  4. Select Without Neutrons or With Neutrons.
  5. Review the preview, then click OK.

The plugin creates <Name>.rs in the chosen directory with the correct GLoC macros wired up and ready to fill in.

Generated code examples

Simple reactor

use gloc::prelude::*;

#[reactor_state]
pub struct CounterState {
    // TODO: add state fields
}

impl Default for CounterState {
    fn default() -> Self { Self {} }
}

#[reactor(state = CounterState)]
pub struct CounterReactor {}

impl CounterReactor {
    // TODO: add methods that call self.emit(...)
}

Reactor with neutrons

use gloc::prelude::*;

#[reactor_state]
pub struct CounterState {
    // TODO: add state fields
}

impl Default for CounterState {
    fn default() -> Self { Self {} }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum CounterNeutron {
    // TODO: add neutron variants
}

#[reactor(state = CounterState, neutrons = CounterNeutron)]
pub struct CounterReactor {}

impl CounterReactor {
    fn on_event(&mut self, neutron: CounterNeutron) {
        match neutron {
            // TODO: handle neutron variants
        }
    }
}

Requirements

  • RustRover 2024.3 or later
  • GLoC added to your Cargo.toml

All notable changes to the GLoC Reactor Generator plugin are documented here.

idea-plugin.name: Vue.js Pro
idea-plugin.description:
Vue.js Pro brings Vue 3 Single File Component support to IntelliJ-based IDEs, including project creation, editor assistance, navigation, inspections, refactoring, and Vue Router, Pinia, and web-types integration.

Work with Vue projects directly in the IDE, from creating a new app to navigating and refactoring component code.

Compatibility: Vue.js Pro replaces JetBrains' bundled Vue.js support for .vue files. If the bundled JetBrains Vue.js plugin (org.jetbrains.plugins.vue) is enabled, Vue.js Pro shows a notification action to disable it and restart the IDE.

  • Create new Vue projects from the New Project wizard using create-vue@latest, with the same choices as the official Vue starter: TypeScript, JSX, Router, Pinia, Vitest, end-to-end testing, ESLint, Prettier, Oxfmt, Vue 3.6 Beta, package manager, bare template, and overwrite options.
  • Generated projects automatically get IDE run configurations for the scripts exposed by package.json, so commands such as dev, build, preview, and type-check are ready to run.
  • Syntax highlighting, folding, formatting, commenting, typing helpers, and configurable colors for .vue files.
  • JavaScript, TypeScript, CSS, SCSS, Less, and Pug support through SFC block injection.
  • Completion for directives, modifiers, components, props, emits, slots, CSS modules, CSS v-bind(), Vue Router route names, and Pinia store state, getters, and actions.
  • Template expressions understand script setup bindings, including props declared with defineProps(), with navigation, rename refactoring, find usages, and unknown-variable inspections across template and script code.
  • Vue Router support includes route-name completion and inspections for unknown named routes or missing required route params in RouterLink bindings.
  • Pinia support for defineStore() includes member completion, navigation to store declarations, storeToRefs() and destructured aliases, setup-store action aliases, find usages from store members, unknown-member inspections, and action-call validation.
  • Navigation, references, find usages, rename, safe delete, breadcrumbs, structure view, go to symbol, documentation, parameter info, inlay hints, and extract component refactoring.
  • Component metadata extraction from Options API, script setup macros, defineModel(), web-types metadata, and large projects with 1000+ components.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Pinia 4 support, including diagnostics for invalid storeToRefs() destructuring and support for object-form defineStore({ id, ... }) stores.
  • Go to Symbol now includes Vue component names and named Vue Router routes.

Improved

idea-plugin.name: Amber Language
idea-plugin.description:
JetBrains Amber Language Plugin is a plugin to support Amber Language in JetBrains IDEs.

Amber is a modern, type-safe programming language that can be compiled to Bash/Ksh/Zsh.

Amber features:

  • Modern Syntax: ECMA Script-like syntax
  • Runtime Safety: Amber ensures that you handle everything that could fail
  • Type Safety: use strong typing to catch bugs at compile time
  • Instant Docs: generate documentation automatically
  • Shell Ready: Interoperate with Bash/Ksh/Zsh scripts
  • Library baked in: Standard library with many useful functions

Amber JetBrains plugin features:

  • Amber language and file types
  • Syntax highlight
  • Amber file structure
  • Run a script from shebang or main function
  • Run a test case from the test gutter icon
  • Run configuration support: Run -> Edit Configurations -> Amber or right-click in an Amber script
  • Amberfile task file support: define tasks and run them with Amber language
  • Code completion: std library, imported members, function, keywords, etc.
  • Navigation support for function
  • Basic support for formatting
  • live templates for import and function call
  • External annotator to use amber check to collect errors and warnings
  • Inspection: auto-import for unresolved function from std library

How to get started?

  • Download and install amber command line from https://docs.amber-lang.com/getting_started/installation
  • Install JetBrains Amber plugin
  • Create a simple Amber script with the following code:
#!/usr/bin/env amber

main {
 echo("Hello world")
}
  • Run amber script from the shebang gutter run icon

Enjoy shell scripting with Amber!

idea-plugin.name: EdgeTrim - Figma edge/seam fixer
idea-plugin.description:
EdgeTrim finds and fixes the faint 1px line Figma sometimes bakes into the edges of exported images — the thin white / transparent border (a "ghost pixel" or edge seam) that shows up when a frame is exported at a fractional scale or off a whole-pixel position. It inspects all four edges — top, bottom, left, right — independently.

Instead of a naive "is the edge white?" test, EdgeTrim uses a delta-based heuristic: it flags an edge line only when it differs from the line just inside it far more than lines normally vary, leans toward the background, and is uniform. That catches real seams (often only slightly lightened) while avoiding false positives on gradients and transparent padding.

How to use — right-click a folder in the Project view and choose EdgeTrim:

  • Recursively scans the folder for png / jpg assets that have the artifact.
  • Opens a review dialog — affected images with a per-edge fix combo and a magnified before/after of the focused edge (a checkerboard reveals transparency; a red marker shows the seam). When several edges are flagged, switch which one to magnify; the before/after comparison can be zoomed (mouse wheel or the zoom buttons) and panned (drag), kept in sync.
  • Per edge, choose trim (remove the 1px line; the image shrinks by 1 on that axis) or extend (replace the 1px line with a copy of the line just inside it; size is kept).
  • Bulk toggles: all trim · all extend · select all · deselect all.
  • Save overwrites the originals.

Made for frontend developers who receive Figma assets (folders of PNG/JPG) and want to clean edge seams in batch, inside the IDE — without round-tripping to the designer or opening an image editor. It complements the fix-at-export-time approach for cases where you don't own the Figma file.

Note: saving re-encodes the whole file. PNG stays pixel-lossless (but may lose palette/PNG8 size optimization); JPEG is recompressed at high quality (q ≈ 0.95). Run image optimizers such as TinyPNG/JPG after EdgeTrim, not before.

Works in any JetBrains IDE (IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, …) — it depends only on the platform module.

The UI follows your OS language — Korean on a Korean system, English otherwise.





EdgeTrim 은 Figma가 내보낸 이미지의 가장자리에 생기는 희미한 1px 줄(흰색/투명 테두리, "고스트 픽셀", 엣지 seam)을 감지하고 고치는 JetBrains IDE 플러그인입니다. 프레임을 소수 배율로 내보내거나 정수 좌표에서 어긋난 위치에서 export할 때 흔히 나타나며, 상·하·좌·우 네 변을 각각 검사합니다.

"가장자리가 흰색인가?"로 단순 판단하지 않고 델타 기반 휴리스틱을 씁니다: 가장자리 줄이 바로 안쪽 줄과 정상 변화보다 훨씬 크게 다르고, 배경 방향(더 밝거나 더 투명)이며, 균일할 때만 seam으로 판정합니다. 덕분에 실제 seam(살짝만 밝아진 경우가 많음)은 잡으면서 그라데이션·투명 패딩에서의 오탐은 피합니다.

사용법 — Project view에서 폴더 우클릭 → EdgeTrim:

  • 폴더를 재귀적으로 스캔해 아티팩트가 있는 png / jpg 를 찾습니다.
  • 검토 다이얼로그: 변별 처리 콤보가 있는 대상 목록 + 포커스 변의 확대 전/후 비교 (체커보드로 투명 표시, 1px seam은 빨간 마커). 여러 변이 감지되면 확대할 변을 전환할 수 있고, 전/후 비교는 동기화된 상태로 줌(마우스 휠·줌 버튼)·패닝(드래그)할 수 있습니다.
  • 변마다 trim(1px 줄 제거, 해당 축 −1) 또는 extend(1px 줄을 바로 안쪽 줄 복사로 교체, 크기 유지) 선택.
  • 일괄 토글: 모두 trim · 모두 extend · 전체 선택 · 전체 해제.
  • 저장 시 원본을 덮어씁니다.

Figma 에셋(PNG/JPG 폴더)을 전달받는 프론트엔드 개발자가, 디자이너에게 다시 요청하거나 이미지 편집기를 열지 않고 IDE 안에서 seam을 일괄 정리하려는 경우를 위해 만들었습니다. Figma 파일을 직접 소유하지 않을 때 export 시점 수정 방식을 보완합니다.

주의: 저장은 파일 전체 재인코딩입니다. PNG는 픽셀 무손실(단 팔레트/PNG8 최적화는 사라질 수 있음), JPEG는 고품질(q ≈ 0.95) 재압축입니다. TinyPNG/JPG 같은 최적화 도구는 EdgeTrim 적용 후에 돌리세요.

모든 JetBrains IDE(IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm …)에서 동작합니다 — 플랫폼 모듈에만 의존합니다.

UI는 OS 언어를 따릅니다 — 한국어 시스템이면 한국어, 그 외에는 영어로 표시됩니다.

idea-plugin.name: FishBook-X
idea-plugin.description:
FishBook-X — Read Novels in IDEA

Notice: This plugin is a fork of jogeen/FishBook (original author: jogeen, 2020). The original project targets the old IntelliJ Platform API; this fork adapts it to IDEA 2025.3.4 and adds new features. All original design and code belong to the original author.

What is FishBook?

A lightweight plugin that lets you read TXT novels directly in your IntelliJ IDEA side tool window.

Features (inherited from the original project)

  • 📖 Read TXT e-books in a dedicated tool window
  • 🔖 Auto-save reading progress (bookmark-like)
  • ⏭️ Page turning (previous/next/first/last)
  • 🔢 Custom page size

New in FishBook-X (added in this fork)

  • 🆕 Chapter detection & quick jump — auto-detects 第N章 / Chapter N / 序章 / 楔子 etc., and lets you jump straight to a chapter's first page from a dropdown.
  • 🆕 Remember last-read chapter — the chapter dropdown restores your last position after a restart.
  • 🆕 Keyboard page turning — press ← / → in the reader to flip pages.
  • 🆕 Performance rewrite — the book is now loaded into memory once with a BufferedReader; page turning is O(1).
  • 🆕 Modern platform APIs — migrated to Light Service, NotificationGroupManager, ContentFactory.getInstance(), compatible with IntelliJ IDEA 2025.3.4 (build 253.x).

How to Use

  1. Open Settings → Tools → FishBook Config
  2. Click 选择... to pick a TXT e-book file
  3. Set the page size (default: 10 lines per page)
  4. Click Apply
  5. Open the FishBook tool window on the right side
  6. Use the chapter dropdown to jump to any chapter

Chapter Detection

Supports common chapter formats:

  • 第N章 / 第N回 / 第N节 / 第N卷
  • Chapter N
  • 序章 / 楔子 / 尾声 / 番外

Credits & License

Original project: github.com/jogeen/FishBook

This fork: github.com/SagitTariuse/FishBook-X

License: Apache 2.0
idea-plugin.change-notes:
FishBook-X 2.0.2 (2026-09-28) — chapter detection fixes

  • 🐛 Fix: chapter list was truncated from a certain chapter onwards
    • Affected books include 凡人, where the heading style switches mid-book from 第一千九百九十九章 to 第两千章. The Chinese-numeral character set was missing 两, so every chapter from that point on failed to match — 447 of 2463 chapters disappeared and the dropdown appeared to stop at 第十一卷.
    • Fix: added 两 to the character set.
  • 🐛 Fix: chapter headings indented with full-width spaces were not detected
    • Root cause: Java's \s matches ASCII whitespace only, not U+3000 (full-width space) — which is what most Chinese TXT novels use for indentation. Also, String.trim() only strips ASCII whitespace, so detected chapter names kept their 　　 prefix.
    • Fix: match U+3000 / U+00A0 explicitly in all chapter patterns, and switch trim() to strip().
  • ✨ Support spaced headings such as 第 2000 章 — whitespace is now tolerated both after 第 and before the chapter measure (章/回/节/卷/部/集/篇).

FishBook-X 2.0.1 (2026-06-12) — bug fix

  • 🐛 Fix: chapter dropdown jumped to first chapter after page turning
    • Root cause: loadChapters() was called on every page turn, and cbChapter.setSelectedIndex(...) fired the chapter's ActionListener, which recursively called turnPage() and reset the dropdown to the first chapter.
    • Fix: split the UI initialization into firstInitUi() (runs only once) and the page-turn hot path. Added a suppressChapterEvent reentry guard around all setSelectedIndex calls so the chapter dropdown no longer triggers recursive page jumps.
  • 🐛 Fix: chapter dropdown did not update when turning pages
    • Root cause: Chapter did not override equals(), so JComboBox.setSelectedItem(newChapter) could not find the matching item already inside the dropdown (it relies on equals to look up the model). The call returned silently and the dropdown display did not change.
    • Fix: rewrote syncChapterByPage() to compute the matched chapter's index first, then call setSelectedIndex(matchedIndex) with the reentry guard. Index-based selection is independent of the Chapter.equals() behavior, so the dropdown now updates reliably.
  • 🎨 Chapter dropdown width: 210px → 294px (~15 → ~21 Chinese chars) so longer chapter titles (e.g. 第 1234 章 长长的标题文字示例) fit in the closed dropdown.

FishBook-X 2.0.0 (2026-06-11) — first fork release

This is a fork of jogeen/FishBook. All original credits belong to the original author.

  • ✅ Adapted for IntelliJ IDEA 2025.3.4 (build 253.x)
  • 🚀 Performance: file is now loaded into memory once via BufferedReader; page turning is O(1)
  • 📑 New: auto-detect chapters (第N章 / Chapter N / 序章 / 楔子), quick chapter jump
  • 🔖 New: remember last-read chapter
  • ⌨️ New: keyboard shortcuts (← / →) for page turning
  • 🐛 Fix: replaced deprecated APIs (ServiceManager, NotificationGroup constructor, etc.)
  • 🎨 UI: rewrote both ReadUI and SettingUI as pure code (no GUI Designer bytecode instrumentation dependency — fixes the "Select configuration element in the tree" error)

idea-plugin.name: Unicode Guard
idea-plugin.description:
The Unicode Insight plugin helps developers detect and manage potentially dangerous or invisible Unicode characters in their source code. It provides tools to prevent "Trojan Source" attacks and identify hidden characters that could cause bugs or security issues.
Features:
  • Trojan Source Detection: Identifies Unicode bidirectional control characters that can be used to visually reorder source code (CVE-2021-42574).
  • Invisible Character Detection: Finds zero-width spaces, non-joiners, and other invisible characters that may be hidden in your files.
  • Unicode Preview: Provides real-time inlay hints showing the decoded version of Unicode escape sequences (e.g., \uXXXX).
  • Quick-fixes: Easily remove detected problematic characters with a single click.
  • Line Markers: Gutter icons highlight lines containing Unicode threats for quick identification.

idea-plugin.name: Elixir Pro
idea-plugin.description:
Elixir Pro turns your JetBrains IDE into a full-featured Elixir development environment: professional editing, a graphical debugger, first-class Phoenix and LiveView support, ExUnit testing, and zero-friction SDK setup — for everything from a single Mix project to large umbrella applications.

Elixir Pro builds on the strong foundation established by the original Elixir plugin and its open-source contributors. Their work brought rich Elixir support to JetBrains IDEs, and Elixir Pro is proud to carry that foundation forward with additional tooling, integrations, and dedicated support.

Why Elixir Pro

  • A parser you can trust. The grammar is continuously verified against Elixir's own compiler output — it is so accurate it has uncovered bugs in the native Elixir tokenizer and parser. Highlighting, navigation, and refactoring work on a faithful model of your code, not a regex approximation.
  • Debug real Elixir, graphically. Set breakpoints in .ex and .exs files — and even inside Elixir segments of .eex, .leex, and .heex templates. Step, inspect, and evaluate without leaving the IDE.
  • From zero to coding in one click. The plugin detects Elixir and Erlang installs from Homebrew, asdf, mise, vfox, Nix, and system locations — or downloads and configures a matching Elixir + Erlang/OTP pair for you.
  • Up to date. Built for current toolchains: Elixir 1.20 and OTP 29, with clickable type-warning locations from the new compiler.

Smart editing

  • Syntax highlighting and semantic annotation, with customizable colors that follow your JetBrains theme by default
  • Code completion for module names, functions and macros, module attributes, parameters, and variables — including names decompiled from .beam files in your SDKs and _build
  • Go to definition, go to symbol, go to test / test subject, and find usages — across source and decompiled code, including {Module, :function, arity} MFA tuples
  • Native semantic rename for functions and macros (including protocol functions and implementations), modules, named types, callbacks, variables, parameters, and module attributes
  • Native Extract Variable, Extract Function, Inline Variable, Change Signature for simple fixed-arity functions, and Move Module for single-module source files, with usage preview, conflict checks, and undo/redo
  • Quick documentation with hover support and direct HexDocs links for Elixir, Erlang, and library modules
  • Code formatting, plus one-action mix format for the current file or every Mix root in the project
  • Structure view, code folding, brace matching and auto-insertion, commenter, and spellchecking with Elixir and Ecto dictionaries
  • Live templates for Elixir, OTP, ExUnit, Phoenix, LiveView, Ecto, Mix, and telemetry workflows

Phoenix, LiveView, and templates

  • EEx, LEEx, and HEEx template support with Elixir injection
  • Completion for assigns, component attributes, slots, built-in Phoenix components, phx-* bindings, and route paths
  • New-file templates for Phoenix controllers, LiveViews, LiveComponents, Ecto schemas, and Mix tasks

Debugging

  • Graphical debugger that works on all run configurations
  • Step into, step over, and step out; navigate the stack without stepping
  • Elixir-aware variable inspection: structs, maps, tuples, binaries, bitstrings, charlists, lists, pids, ports, and refs
  • Evaluate expressions in any stack frame
  • Customizable module filters to control what gets interpreted

Run, test, and ship

  • Run configurations for Elixir scripts, Mix tasks, ExUnit, IEx, IEx with Mix, Mix releases, and Distillery releases
  • ExUnit integration with the IDE test runner — results, re-run failed tests, and navigation from failures to code
  • Background compiler diagnostics from mix compile shown directly in the editor, and clickable warning locations in Mix, ExUnit, and test consoles
  • Credo and Dialyzer integration, including an insert-@spec quick fix when a provider can infer the spec
  • Inspections with quick fixes — from ambiguous parentheses and type-spec mistakes to missing @moduledoc, deprecated calls, unused variables, and unresolvable module qualifiers
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Fixed ExUnit and ESpec test-runner compatibility on IntelliJ 2026.2 and later.
