idea-plugin.name: Be Water JSON YAML Converter
idea-plugin.description:
Convert between JSON, YAML, XML, CSV, TOML and Protobuf, generate Java POJOs, Kotlin data classes and JSON Schema, and decode Protobuf payloads.

It works in a tool window with syntax-highlighted editors on the right side of your IDE, and it runs locally, so your data never goes to a website. Be water, my friend: let your data flow between formats.

Conversions

  • JSON to YAML and YAML to JSON, XML to JSON and JSON to XML, CSV to JSON and JSON to CSV, TOML to JSON and JSON to TOML: each format converts to every other
  • JSON to Java POJO from any supported input, with optional Lombok annotations and ISO-8601 date detection (LocalDate / OffsetDateTime)
  • JSON to Kotlin data class from any supported input
  • JSON to JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) from any supported input
  • Protobuf schema to JSON, and JSON to a .proto schema
  • Decode Protobuf payloads: paste a binary message as hex or base64 and read it as JSON, by field number as protoc --decode_raw does, or by name against its .proto file

Works where you already are

  • Right-click a file or an editor selection to open it in the converter, or convert it straight to another format
  • Results open as scratch files, in a real IDE editor
  • Compare two documents as canonical JSON — the same data in YAML and JSON compares as equal, so only real differences show
  • Subtree filter to convert only the part of a document you care about

Protobuf

  • Full structural parsing of nested message, oneof, and enum blocks
  • Field types that reference known messages are resolved to nested JSON objects
  • JSON to Protobuf generates inline nested messages
  • Payloads decode as protobuf parses them: proto2, proto3 and editions schemas, maps, oneofs, groups, and fields the schema does not declare

CSV & XML

  • Two CSV expansion modes: FLAT_FIRST (safe default) and CROSS_JOIN (full Cartesian product)
  • Comma, semicolon or tab delimiters for reading and writing
  • Configurable row-warning threshold: conversions above it ask before running, in either mode
  • Type inference for CSV and XML input — numbers, booleans and null become typed JSON values

Editor & UI

  • Format-aware pretty-printing, including lenient auto-repair of truncated JSON and tolerant parsing of comments, trailing commas and single quotes
  • Conversion history — restore any of the last 20 conversions from the toolbar
  • Drag-and-drop files onto the input editor with automatic format detection
  • Cancellable background conversions, find bar (Ctrl+F), soft-wrap toggle, one-click swap, copy to clipboard, file import/export
  • Options persist across IDE restarts

Documentation · Report an issue · Source code
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.6.0

  • Protobuf payload decoding — a new input format, Protobuf payload, reads a binary Protobuf message pasted as hex, however it is spaced, prefixed or separated, or as base64, and converts it to JSON or any other output. Without a schema it is decoded as protoc --decode_raw decodes it, by field number. With the .proto file it was written with, chosen in the options bar, and its message type, it is decoded to what protobuf's own JSON printer writes for it: field names, enums by name, bytes in base64, maps as objects, and no proto3 field that holds its default. It is read as protobuf parses it, keeping a field's last value, merging a message or group set twice, and keeping a oneof's last member. A payload that breaks the wire format is refused with the byte it breaks at, and one that contradicts the schema with the field it contradicts. The decoder is tested against Google's protobuf-java on random proto2, proto3 and editions schemas and payloads.
  • Groups keep what they declare — a oneof, message or enum declared inside a proto2 group is the group's own. Protobuf to JSON took a oneof there for the enclosing message's fields, and refused the schema when one of their numbers met another of that message's.
  • Listed as Be Water JSON YAML Converter — the plugin's name in the Marketplace and in the plugin manager now says what it converts, and its description opens with the conversions it offers. The tool window and its menu items keep their names.

1.5.3

  • Format keeps numbers as written — JSON Format keeps each number's spelling, so 1.5e1, 1.0e2, -0.0 and 1e400 stay as they are, with sorted keys too. YAML and TOML Format refuse a number they would write back differently, such as 1.5e1 as 15 (a float turned into an integer) or YAML's 0x1F as 31, and say what it would become.
  • XML Format writes the document as it was written — it re-indents only elements that hold nothing but other elements. Mixed content such as <p>Hello <b>world</b></p>, xml:space="preserve" elements, CDATA sections and elements holding only a comment are written as they are, instead of being refused or re-indented into a different value, and entity references an external DTD declares, such as XHTML's   and ©, are no longer deleted from text; the parser drops one inside an attribute value, so Format refuses such a document instead. The declaration keeps its standalone, a document without one gets none, each comment or processing instruction before the root keeps its own line, and a document nested more than 1,000 levels deep is refused, as conversion refuses it. XML 1.1 keeps its control characters, NEL and line separator as character references, and text of Unicode spaces between elements is no longer taken for indentation. In XHTML, told by its DOCTYPE or by its namespace as XHTML5 writes it, only HTML's void elements, such as <br />, are minimized: an empty <script src="a.js"></script> was written as <script src="a.js" />, which an HTML parser reads as an opening tag.
  • XML keeps text, names, nulls and whitespace — a document that declares a non-UTF-8 encoding is no longer decoded twice (José read as JosÃ©, and UTF-16 failed). JSON null is written as xsi:nil="true" and reads back as null rather than "". Element names follow the name rules XML readers apply, so a key such as latency_µs, or one in Ethiopic, Cherokee or Sinhala, no longer produces XML the plugin then refused to read; characters a name cannot hold become underscores. A value holding a character XML cannot hold, such as a control character or U+FFFE, is refused with a message naming it. A key that is already a valid name keeps it and only renamed keys are numbered, so first_name is no longer written as first_name_2 because first name came first. Format keeps whitespace that is an element's whole value.
  • CSV keeps cells and rows as written — the first cell of each row keeps its leading spaces, as the other cells always did: Format no longer strips them, and type inference no longer reads a space-padded first cell as a number. A row whose only cell is empty is written quoted and survives the round trip, and a row of empty cells (,,) is kept instead of being dropped as blank. Delimiter detection picks the delimiter that splits the header and the first rows into the most columns, reading a quoted cell that spans lines as one cell, so a tab-separated file whose values contain commas is read as tab-separated. .tsv files open as tab-separated CSV.
  • Format detection reads real documents — CSV whose rows hold Re: or Fwd: is CSV, not YAML; YAML carrying a .proto, as a Kubernetes ConfigMap does, is YAML; a Protobuf editions file (edition = "2023";) is Protobuf while Cargo.toml's edition = "2021" stays TOML; and a TOML table header may be followed by a comment.
  • Files open in the encoding the IDE has for them — Open and the context-menu actions read a file by its byte-order mark, then by its encoding in the IDE (File Encodings, .editorconfig), then as UTF-8, then as Windows-1252. A UTF-16 file no longer opens as NUL-interleaved text, and a Windows-1252 file keeps its € and curly quotes. The status bar names the encoding when it was not UTF-8.
  • YAML reads 0o octal and deep documents, and writes for YAML 1.1 readers — 0o17 is the number 15, as YAML 1.2 writes octal; it was read as text. Documents may nest 500 levels deep, where anything past 50 was refused, including YAML the plugin had just written. Strings that YAML 1.1 readers such as PyYAML and docker-compose take for numbers or dates, like 22:22 and 2024-01-01, are written quoted, so Format no longer strips the quotes a docker-compose file put around its ports. A string holding a NEL (U+0085), which YAML 1.1 reads as a line break, or opening the document with U+FEFF, which reads as a byte-order mark, is written quoted, where it came back changed; half of a surrogate pair is refused rather than written as another character. A standard tag on the wrong kind of node, such as !!binary on a mapping, and a mapping that merges itself are YAML errors at their line, not internal exceptions.
  • Type inference leaves hash-like text alone — a digit run with an e in it, such as the short git hash 1234e56, stays text; 1e3 and 1.5e3 are still numbers.
  • The subtree filter reads $ as the root only before ., [ or the end — keys such as $id, and paths such as $defs.Address in the plugin's own JSON Schema output, select what they name.
  • Protobuf reads options, numbers, extensions and proto2 as protoc does — a field whose options hold a list or a message, as protovalidate writes them, is no longer dropped; an extend block inside a message no longer adds fields to it; map<string,string>labels, hex field numbers and octal numbers such as 010 read as protoc reads them. proto2 schemas read too: a group is a nested message and a field named after it, [default = …] values are the values the fields start with, extensions ranges and an edition line are declarations rather than errors, and an aggregate option may separate its fields with ;. An escape such as \303\251 reads as the UTF-8 bytes it spells, é. A schema that would expand to more than two million values, or that nests more than 1,000 levels deep, is refused instead of exhausting memory or the stack, and Format no longer stalls on a line with a long run of spaces.
  • Generated Protobuf is accepted by protoc — keys such as user_id and userId, or name and Name, become distinct field names, and a field whose JSON name would clash carries its key as json_name, so every key still reads back as itself. Values of mixed kinds, and lists holding null, are google.protobuf.Value, with its import, instead of repeated string, which proto3's JSON mapping cannot read them back into; a key such as [id], a form protoc reserves for extensions, is refused with a message instead of being emitted.
  • Generated Java and Kotlin compile and read their own JSON — Lombok classes with a $ref key compile; classes with keys such as xAxis, eTag, or both id and ID, bind through their fields with @JsonAutoDetect; and class names are unique ignoring case, so objects under url and URL no longer compile to the same class file on Windows and macOS. An empty object is a Map<String, Object> (Map<String, Any?> in Kotlin) instead of an empty class that failed on whatever the real data held there. A Lombok class with more than 1,000 fields uses @Getter and @Setter, since @Data's equals is too large for javac, and one with more than 500 leaves its fields out of toString, which javac cannot compile.
  • Compare shows plain numbers — whole numbers are written out (30, 12000) instead of 3E+1 and 1.2E+4, and equal values still compare equal however they are spelled.
  • Output uses LF line breaks on every system, and Format keeps CRLF — on Windows, JSON, XML and JSON Schema output took the system's CRLF. Every output now uses LF, and Format keeps the line breaks of the document it formats. Line breaks inside quoted CSV cells are data, and Format and Save leave them as written.
  • Save keeps a file's permissions, symbolic links, line breaks and encoding — on Linux and macOS a saved file keeps its permissions instead of becoming readable by its owner only, and saving through a symbolic link updates the file it points to instead of replacing the link. A file keeps its CRLF or LF line breaks, and a new one gets the project's line separator. A CSV, Java or Kotlin file keeps its encoding and byte-order mark, so Excel still reads a Windows-1252 or "CSV UTF-8" file correctly after a save; JSON, XML, YAML, TOML and Protobuf are written as UTF-8, the encoding their tools read. On Windows, a save retries for a moment when another program, such as a virus scanner, holds the file.
  • Context-menu actions appear where they can work — Open in Be Water Converter and Convert with Be Water are offered on JSON, XML (SVG and XHTML included), YAML, TOML, CSV, TSV and Protobuf files, on plain-text files whose start reads as one of them, and on any selection that does. They no longer appear on Java classes, scripts, READMEs or gradle.properties because a line looked like key = value. The menu reads only the start of a large selection, so it opens at once, and Cancel stops a conversion under way, not only the read before it.
  • Options follow across projects — each open project has its own panel, and a choice made in one (CSV mode and delimiter, row warning, Lombok, dates, type inference, sort keys) now shows in the others. A panel saves only the option that changed, so it no longer writes its stale choices over one just made in another project.
  • Keys the IDE owns are left to it — Ctrl+D (Cmd+D on macOS) no longer deletes the line in the panel's editors, where the IDE's Duplicate Line does not reach. The panel no longer binds Alt+Shift+L, Alt+Shift+C and Ctrl+Shift+O, which never reached it past the IDE's Load Context, Recent Changes and Load Gradle Changes: Format Input, Copy Output and Open File take any shortcut you give them in Settings | Keymap.
  • Find's Previous reaches a match at the end of the document — when the document ended with a match, Shift+Enter and the Previous button skipped it and selected the first match again, every time.
  • The tool window follows the IDE — fonts follow the IDE's font size and Zoom IDE, and a new theme, editor color scheme or font size restyles the panel at once. Confirmations use the IDE's own dialogs, context-menu error balloons keep XML tag names and line breaks, Convert with Be Water greys out the file's own format, and an XML Format error moves the caret to the problem like other parse errors do. The editors are RSyntaxTextArea 4.0.1.
  • Syntax errors read as one line — a JSON, XML, TOML or CSV syntax error says what is wrong and ends with its line and column, where the caret goes, instead of opening a balloon of the parser's own location text ("at [Source: REDACTED …]"). TOML Format of a number too large to read reports the parser's error, which names it, rather than "Too many nonzero exponent digits."
  • Keyboard and screen-reader use — opening the tool window puts the caret in the input editor, toolbar buttons show a focus ring when Tab reaches them, and screen readers name the editors, format selectors, option controls and the find field.
  • Large documents stay responsive — soft wrap is never applied to a document too large to highlight, where each resize took seconds, and a wrap turned on meanwhile applies once a smaller document replaces it. Pressing Format while it runs says so instead of starting a second pass.

1.5.2

  • Fixed: CSV headers beginning with # were mistaken for comments — comma, semicolon and tab exports retain their format and delimiter detection, including files with just a header and one data row.
  • Background results respect newer edits — Convert, Format, Compare and file loading discard results that belong to an older document. Clear, Swap and history restoration also invalidate pending results, and a late Cancel still stops a completed conversion from replacing the output.
  • History restores conversion options along with the documents and formats, including the CSV delimiter, type inference, date detection and subtree filter.
  • YAML Format refuses changes it cannot preserve — non-string mapping keys, timestamps, sets and other unsupported YAML types leave the document untouched with an explanation. Explicit null documents remain convertible.
  • TOML safeguards distinguish keys from values — numeric and date-looking table names no longer trigger value warnings, escaped quotes in multiline strings are handled correctly, and lowercase date-time separators are recognised.
  • Sorting preserves decimal scale — values such as 1.10 keep their written precision through Format and conversion. Compare treats equivalent numeric forms as equal while preserving differences in their values.
  • Generated code handles numeric and JVM limits — Java and Kotlin use exact numeric types when needed. Oversized Kotlin data classes are refused with an explanation, and Lombok output omits an all-args constructor when it would exceed the JVM parameter limit. Protobuf generation refuses numbers its scalar types cannot preserve.
  • Protobuf preserves explicit JSON names, including escaped names in nested messages and oneof blocks, and rejects conflicting names. Package and global type references resolve in their declared scope, and generated field numbers skip the reserved 19000–19999 range.
  • Subtree paths handle quoted keys, including empty names, escaped quotes and brackets. JSON Pointer spaces are preserved, malformed paths are rejected, and JSON Schema deduplication keeps distinct property names separate.
  • Large documents use less memory when merging sparse array shapes, and highlighting is disabled for oversized input as well as output. Concurrent saves use separate temporary files so they cannot overwrite each other's temporary data.
  • Expanded regression coverage includes asynchronous editor actions, generated Java and Kotlin compilation, real Lombok processing and a constrained-heap array test. CI runs both the plain JVM and IntelliJ test suites.

1.5.1

  • Fixed: JSON→CSV merged two keys into one column — a key containing a dot and a nested key with the same path (a.b and a → b) wrote one column and kept only the last value. It is refused now, with the column named.
  • Fixed: JSON with a trailing comment could not be auto-closed — the missing brace was appended inside the comment; and a comment-only JSON document is refused instead of converting to null.
  • Format detection looks past leading comments, so a // or # line above a JSON document no longer hides it, and a commented JSON array is no longer taken for TOML.
  • XML Format keeps a DOCTYPE — plist, XHTML and SVG files can be formatted; only a DOCTYPE with an internal subset is refused, with a plain explanation.
  • Files with a UTF-16 or UTF-32 byte-order mark open correctly instead of as garbage; YAML parse errors move the caret like the other formats; Protobuf Format works on CRLF files; a YAML null key converts as "null".
  • Format keeps your place — the caret stays on its line, and an already formatted document is left untouched rather than replaced with itself. Save proposes the same file name the scratch files use (Root.java for Java), and Open in Be Water Converter asks before loading a very large file.
  • Numbers keep their written form in YAML and TOML too — 1.10 no longer becomes 1.1, 1e400 no longer becomes the text "Infinity", and long decimals keep every digit. Format used to write the rewritten values back over the document.
  • YAML output quotes exactly what the reader would retype — strings such as "1_000", "0x1F" and "1e3" came back as numbers after a round trip.
  • Fixed: Format split a ----prefixed YAML list into one document per element, and treated a --- line inside a block scalar as a separator.
  • Fixed: CSV Format rewrote the document — headers were renamed (id,id,, became id,id_2,column_3), a ragged row dropped the headers it lacked, and a header-only file was refused. Format now rewrites CSV row by row and never interprets it. Blank lines no longer become empty rows on conversion.
  • Fixed: Protobuf nested types leaked across messages — two messages each declaring an Inner or a Status both resolved to the last one defined, a nested type hid a top-level one from every other message, and dotted references such as Outer.Inner resolved to nothing. Names now resolve the way protoc resolves them.
  • Repeated JSON keys are refused rather than silently keeping the last value.
  • Format asks before dropping comments — YAML, TOML and JSON-with-comments keep only the data through Format; it now says how many comments (and YAML anchors) would go and waits for a yes. It also refuses TOML hex/octal/binary, underscore-separated and inf/nan literals, YAML .inf/.nan, and XML mixed content, each of which it could only rewrite by changing it; and it no longer adds standalone="no" to an XML declaration.
  • Semicolon and tab CSV are recognised on paste, and the Delimiter option follows the document — also when a .csv file is opened or converted from the Project view.
  • Open and Save talk to the IDE's file system — opening a file with unsaved editor changes loads the editor's text, and a saved file shows up in the project without a manual sync. Saves go through a temporary file and a rename, so a failure part-way leaves the previous file intact. Format discards its result if the input was edited while it ran.
  • YAML booleans follow YAML 1.2 — yes, no, on and off are text, so the on: key of a GitHub Actions workflow no longer converts to "true". Anchors that form a cycle, or whose aliases would expand to millions of values, are refused instead of crashing or exhausting memory.
  • Generated Java, Kotlin and Protobuf type arrays from every element — objects contribute the union of their keys, numbers widen, and mixed kinds fall back to Object/Any. Kotlin marks a key that some element lacked as nullable. Generated Java is compiled by javac in the test suite.
  • Protobuf — a oneof inside a nested message no longer leaks into the outer message (which reported a false duplicate field number); field numbers protoc rejects (0, 19000–19999, above 536870911) are rejected; and JSON→Proto keeps a key its field name cannot spell through json_name.
  • Fixed: a TOML multi-line string ending in a quote hid the rest of the document from the 19-digit integer guard, so such an integer came back as 0.
  • XML names are compared by namespace, not prefix — two prefixes bound to the same namespace are one repeated element, and are no longer refused as a collision.
  • Fixed: format detection froze the editor on a paste with thousands of blank lines; it is linear now.
  • Convert with Be Water asks before a large CSV — the row-count confirmation the tool window gives applies to context-menu conversions too.

1.5.0

  • Open in editor — a toolbar button sends the output to a scratch file, so you get the IDE's own highlighting, folding and keymap on a result.
  • TOML is syntax-highlighted in the panel; it was the one supported format being shown as plain text.
  • Kotlin data class output — data class declarations with val properties, @JsonProperty where the key differs, and the same nested-class and name-collision handling as the Java generator.
  • Fixed several ways input could be silently mangled — JSONL and any content after the first JSON value were truncated without warning; YAML anchors resolved to the anchor name and <<: merge keys were discarded; a UTF-8 BOM (what Excel writes on "CSV UTF-8" export) became part of the first column name; repeated CSV headers overwrote one another; and very large or very precise numbers lost their value. Format, which rewrites your editor in place, was the most damaging path for several of these.
  • Format no longer retypes CSV cells — it is a layout action, so 1.50 stays 1.50 and a literal null cell stays text. Convert still infers types.
  • Protobuf field options parse — [deprecated = true] and friends no longer fail the whole message, and an option on an enum's zero value no longer silently promotes the next constant to be the default.
  • JSON Schema output — generate a draft 2020-12 schema from any supported input. Mixed-type arrays produce anyOf rather than guessing from the first element.
  • CSV delimiter selection — read and write comma, semicolon or tab separated files. Semicolon CSV (the norm across much of Europe) previously parsed as a single column.
  • Sort keys — sort object keys alphabetically so output is stable and diffable; array order is preserved. Applies to every target format.
  • Automatic format detection on paste — pasting or dropping content sets the input format for you; it never overrides a format you picked yourself.
  • Works from the editor and Project view — right-click a file or a selection for Open in Be Water Converter, or Convert with Be Water to convert straight to any format. No more pasting into the tool window to get started.
  • Results open as scratch files — conversions started from a context menu open in a real IDE editor, with full highlighting, folding and your own keymap.
  • Subtree filter — convert only part of a document with a JSON Pointer (/users/0/name) or dotted path (users[0].name).
  • Compare — diff the two editors in the IDE's diff viewer. Both sides are normalised and key-sorted first, so the same data in YAML and JSON compares as equal and only real differences are shown.
  • Parse errors move the caret to the reported line and column instead of only describing where the problem is.

1.4.1

Not published on the JetBrains Marketplace: these changes first reached it in 1.5.0.

  • Fixed: generated Java POJOs now compile — the output declared every class public, which is illegal for more than one top-level type in a single file. Only the root class is public now.
  • Fixed: JSON→XML no longer drops values on key collisions — keys that sanitize to the same element name ("a b" and "a+b") are numbered instead of silently overwriting each other.
  • Fixed: colliding POJO class names — two differently-shaped objects that map to the same class name each get their own class instead of the second being typed with the first one's fields.
  • Fixed: JSON→Proto emitted duplicate message names — keys like user and User produced two message User blocks in one scope, which is invalid proto3.
  • Fixed: Protobuf input with braces or // inside string literals — a valid schema containing option x = "{"; was rejected as having unbalanced braces.
  • Faster, leaner conversions — the internal JSON pivot is no longer pretty-printed, which removed about a third of its size on large inputs, and CSV output no longer copies every row a second time.
  • Fixed: saving output no longer freezes the IDE — writes moved off the UI thread, matching how files are read.
  • Cancel is now reliable — cancelling before the conversion starts is honoured, and row expansion checks for cancellation as it runs.
  • Row-count warning now covers FLAT_FIRST, not just CROSS_JOIN.
  • Generated POJO imports are emitted only when used — List, BigDecimal, BigInteger and @JsonProperty are no longer added unconditionally.
  • Minimum IDE version is now 2025.1 — the save-file dialog moved to the current FileSaverDescriptor API, which removes the last deprecated platform API usage. Users on 2024.3 should stay on 1.4.0.

1.4.0

  • Fixed: Format no longer corrupts XML input — pretty-printing now preserves the original root element and attributes instead of renaming the root to <root>.
  • Fixed: FLAT_FIRST CSV no longer drops data — non-object elements (primitives, nested arrays) of the expanded array now become rows instead of silently disappearing.
  • CSV type inference — CSV input cells that look like numbers, booleans or null become typed JSON values; toggleable via the new Infer types option (leading-zero values like 007 stay strings).
  • Cancellable conversions — the Convert button turns into Cancel while a conversion runs.
  • Conversion history — a toolbar history button lists the last 20 conversions; selecting one restores both editors and formats.
  • Date detection for Java POJOs — ISO-8601 values are typed as LocalDate, LocalDateTime or OffsetDateTime (toggleable via Detect dates); java.time imports are emitted only when used.
  • Fixed: JSON→XML always emits well-formed XML — keys that are not valid element names (spaces, leading digits) are sanitized instead of producing unparseable output.
  • Fixed: JSON→Proto emits valid identifiers — kebab-case and other hostile keys are sanitized to snake_case and deduplicated.
  • Type inference for XML input — the Infer types option now also applies to XML.
  • Lenient JSON input — comments, trailing commas, single quotes and unquoted field names are accepted and normalised.
  • Multi-document YAML — "---"-separated documents (e.g. Kubernetes manifests) convert to a JSON array.
  • Find bar and soft-wrap — Ctrl+F searches the focused editor; a toolbar button toggles soft-wrap in both editors.
  • Clear no longer resets saved preferences, and restoring from history first saves the current editors so the restore can be undone.
  • Options persist across restarts — CSV mode, row-warning threshold, Lombok toggle, type inference and split orientation are remembered.
  • Better error reporting — multi-line validation errors are shown as an IDE notification balloon instead of being cut off in the status bar.
  • Protobuf — enum fields resolve to their first declared value; duplicate field numbers are now also rejected across oneof blocks.
  • Java POJO generation — colliding field names are deduplicated, all name segments are sanitized, BigInteger is supported, and empty arrays map to List<Object>.
  • UI robustness — file loading moved off the UI thread with a large-file guard, save asks before overwriting, syntax highlighting is disabled for very large outputs, actions are registered in the Keymap for custom shortcuts, and the tool window is available during indexing.

1.3.1

  • Updated shortcut documentation — only the confirmed Ctrl+Enter conversion shortcut is documented; other actions remain available from the toolbar.
  • Improved swap handling — Java POJO output is now treated as output-only and no longer leaves the UI in an invalid input-format state when swap is requested.
  • Added UI regression coverage for output-only swap behavior.

1.3.0

The first release on the JetBrains Marketplace; 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 were not published there.

  • Fixed dependency bundling — all Jackson dataformat modules and RSyntaxTextArea are now correctly included in the plugin distribution, resolving "Package not found" errors across supported IDE versions.
  • Replaced deprecated JsonNode.fields() — migrated all 10 usages to JsonNode.properties() for forward-compatibility with Jackson 2.21+.
  • Extended compatibility range — removed the upper build cap for IntelliJ Platform 2024.3+ forward compatibility.

1.1.0

  • Drag-and-drop file input — drop a file onto the input editor to load it with automatic format detection.
  • Configurable CROSS_JOIN row-warning threshold — adjust the row limit via a spinner in the CSV options bar.
  • Full Protobuf structural parsing — nested message, oneof, and enum blocks are parsed correctly; field types referencing known messages resolve to nested JSON objects; JSON-to-Proto generates inline nested messages.

1.0.0

  • Initial release: JSON, XML, YAML, CSV, TOML and Protobuf conversion plus Java POJO generation.

idea-plugin.name: Project Quick Notes
idea-plugin.description:
Project Quick Notes adds a lightweight tool window for keeping short notes per project.
Use it to record temporary context, TODOs, review reminders, or handoff notes without leaving the IDE.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Added the Project Quick Notes tool window.
  • Added project-local note saving and clearing.
  • Added Marketplace-ready plugin metadata for the learning release.

idea-plugin.name: Rails View
idea-plugin.description:
Provides a Rails View like the one removed from RubyMine 2025.3 — and goes further. A dedicated Rails View tab in the Project tool window replaces the raw filesystem tree with a Rails-aware view of your project.

Sections

Models · Controllers · Views · Helpers · Mailers · Jobs · Services · Channels · GraphQL · Policies · Serializers · Decorators · Uploaders · Assets · JavaScript · Config · Database · Lib · Spec / Test · Project Files · External Libraries · Scratches and Consoles

Models

  • Files shown by Ruby class name (User, OrderItem, …)
  • Database columns from db/schema.rb listed directly under each model
  • Associations (has_many, belongs_to, …), scopes, and attribute macros
  • typed_store blocks expanded to show each individual typed attribute
  • Methods grouped into Class Methods, Instance Methods, and Private Methods

Controllers

  • Inline Views › … shortcut linking directly to the matching views directory
  • Matching helper file shown as an expandable child node
  • Partials collected under a Partials folder
  • Actions listed with their matching view files as children

Database

  • Migrations sorted newest-first
  • Filenames reformatted for readability: 2026-06-17-113427 CreateNats

Routes

  • Parses config/routes.rb and displays all routes with HTTP verb and path
  • Nested path view: api › v1 › users folder hierarchy (or switch to a flat controller list)
  • Supports resources / resource, namespace, concern, match, and all HTTP verb helpers

External Libraries & Scratches

  • External Libraries: shows installed gems and the Ruby SDK — identical to RubyMine’s built-in node
  • Scratches and Consoles: shows IDE scratch files and console history — identical to RubyMine’s built-in node
  • Both are opt-in via Settings → Tools → Rails View and fully positionable in the section order

Navigation

  • Auto-scroll from editor keeps the tree in sync as you move between files
  • Select in Rails View action available in the editor context menu

Configurable

Fine-tune the view under Settings → Tools → Rails View:

Display Section Options

  • Show or hide the Routes section
  • Show or hide Spec / Test sections
  • Show or hide the Project Files node
  • Show or hide the External Libraries node (gems + SDK)
  • Show or hide the Scratches and Consoles node

Section Behaviour Options

  • Toggle the Views shortcut under each controller
  • Toggle method grouping (Class / Instance / Private)
  • Toggle model macro grouping (Schema / Associations / Scopes / Attributes)
  • Toggle nested vs. flat route display

Use the up/down arrows in Settings to reorder sections, or commit a .railsview file to the project root to share the layout with your team. Every node participates in the order. Prefix a key with ! (e.g. !spec) to hide that section for everyone, overriding individual Settings.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.8 - 2026-07-24

Fixed

  • VCS status coloring in the Controllers and Database (migrations) sections no longer triggers a spurious IDE error report on RubyMine 2026.2 when a third-party UI theme (e.g. Night Owl Material) references a missing color scheme. Status colors are now read from the global editor scheme directly instead of going through the current UI theme's scheme lookup.

idea-plugin.name: Tree View
idea-plugin.description:
Simplify and beautify your projects with Farsroidx - Tree View!

Tired of JetBrains' default project view messing up your clean structures? This plugin completely reimagines how you navigate through your code, keeping everything organized and ultra-fast.

🛠️ Supported Projects (Current Version):
    Maven Project:
    • 📦 Maven Single-Module Projects (Perfect, clean layout for standalone applications)
    • 🗂️ Maven Multi-Module Projects (Beautifully nested hierarchy for large, complex architectures)
    • 🔄 Hybrid Maven Projects (Perfectly supports both Single and Multi-Module structures side-by-side in the same project view!)
* Note: Gradle and other build systems are coming soon in future updates!

⚡ Key Features:
  • 🌳 Clean Package Compacting: Displays your Java/Kotlin packages in a beautiful, compacted hierarchy, keeping the layout clean and intuitive.
  • 🎨 Real-time VCS Integration: Visualizes Git statuses with accurate file-color syncing instantly.
  • 🌀 Flicker-Free UI: Built with a smart loading manager (and a sleek spinner!) to eliminate annoying UI blinks and jumps during project syncs.
  • 🔄 Smart Tree-State Memory: Automatically remembers your expanded/collapsed folders even after reopening the project.
  • 🎯 Smart Sorting: Keeps your primary modules sorted by your build configuration, while keeping internal files beautifully alphabetized (Folders first, then files!).

💡 Missing Source Folders? (Quick Fix): If IntelliJ indexing gets stuck and some of your source or resource roots (like src/main/java) don't show up correctly, don't panic! You can easily force-sync them in 2 clicks:
  1. Right-click anywhere on the Project Tree View.
  2. Look right below the New ➕ menu and click on "Sync Project Source Roots". 🔄✨

Say goodbye to chaotic file lists and welcome a supercharged, clean development workflow!

And this is just the beginning. Stay tuned for more exciting updates and features in the future!! 🔥😎
idea-plugin.change-notes:
v1.1.1 - Tree View Loading Fix & Refresh Stability 🛠️

This patch release resolves a critical UI state issue that could cause the custom project tree to remain stuck on the loading screen after switching between Project View panes.

  • ✅ Fixed Loading State Restoration: Resolved an issue where returning to the Farsroidx Tree View could incorrectly keep the view on the loading screen instead of showing the restored tree.
  • 🔄 Improved Tree Refresh Flow: Refined the refresh lifecycle to better handle pane switching, project view restoration, and Maven readiness checks.
  • 🧯 Prevented Refresh Storms: Removed unnecessary recursive file status refresh triggers that could cause repeated tree invalidations and UI pressure.
  • ⚡ Smoother View Switching: Improved stability when switching between different Project View modes, reducing unnecessary rebuilds and repaint operations.

v1.1.0 - Refined Visuals & Stability 🚀

This update focuses on visual consistency and platform stability to ensure the best development experience.

  • 🎨 Professional Test Highlighting: Recalibrated test folder background colors to align perfectly with JetBrains' design language (Muted Olive).
  • ⚙️ Updated IDE Compatibility: Bumped minimum IDEA version to 2023.3+ to leverage newer platform APIs and improved performance.
  • 🛠️ Internal Optimization: Refined the project tree rendering engine for even smoother navigation and better resource handling.

v1.0.0 - Initial Release 🎉

Say hello to the ultimate Project Tree View! This release introduces a highly optimized, fully customized tree view for JetBrains IDEs to supercharge your project navigation.

  • 🌳 Compact Package View: Displays Kotlin/Java package structures in a compact, organized hierarchy just like standard package views.
  • 🔤 Smart Alphabetical Sorting: Internal directories and package nodes are now sorted alphabetically, placing folders perfectly at the top and files right below them.
  • 📜 Single & Multi-Module Support: Fully supports both Maven Single-Module and Multi-Module structures, keeping modules sorted exactly as defined in your root configurations.
  • 🎨 Seamless VCS Colors: Active Git status colors are fully synced in real-time, providing an immediate visual cue for your modified files.
  • 💾 Tree State Restoration: Never lose your place! The plugin remembers your exact expanded folders and tree state across IDE restarts.
  • ⚡ Zero Flicker Loading: Features a smooth CardLayout loading screen with an animated spinner, preventing UI jumps during initial sync.

idea-plugin.name: Secret Bridge for AWS
idea-plugin.description:
Secret Bridge for AWS helps developers work with cloud-managed secrets inside JetBrains IDEs without copying them into local files.

It fetches secrets from AWS Secrets Manager, supports both standard AWS profiles with access key and secret key credentials and AWS SSO profiles, keeps secrets in memory, and injects them into run/debug configurations and new terminal sessions, including WSL.

This makes it easier to run applications locally with the right environment variables, reduce secret exposure on disk, and keep development workflows fast and consistent across projects.

Secrets can be refreshed when needed, cleared manually, and are flushed from memory when the IDE restarts.

AWS Secret Bridge is an unofficial plugin that uses the official AWS Java SDK to communicate with AWS Secrets Manager. It does not perform any other outbound network calls, and this can be independently verified by inspecting network traffic while the plugin is in use.

Disclaimer: Secret Bridge may not work with every existing run configuration, depending on the IDE and configuration type. Because compatibility may vary across JetBrains IDEs and run configuration types, please verify your most important workflows during the trial period before purchasing.

idea-plugin.name: Atomica Brackets
idea-plugin.description: Rainbow brackets highlighting for nested parentheses, braces, and square brackets. Each nesting level gets a distinct color to make code structure easier to read.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.2.2

  • Highlighting refresh now uses the reason-taking daemon restart on 2024.3+ platforms while staying compatible with 2024.2, removing the last verifier warning.

1.2.1

  • Removed all deprecated IntelliJ Platform API usages flagged by the plugin verifier: highlighting now restarts per open file, and default colors are registered through color scheme files.

1.2.0

  • New: Shuffle Colors button generates a random bracket palette that is always readable — every color is contrast-checked against your editor background, and each color scheme keeps its own palette.
  • New: Reset Default Colors button restores the built-in palette for the current scheme.

  • Fixed: the toggle action now refreshes every open editor instead of only the active file, and shows a checkmark reflecting the current state.

idea-plugin.name: Nimbus - Local Apex Runtime
idea-plugin.description:
Run Salesforce Apex tests locally — no deploy, no org, no Docker.

Nimbus gives you a full Apex runtime on your machine with an embedded PostgreSQL database. Open a Salesforce project and start testing in seconds. Built for the same feedback loop you expect from unit-testing frameworks in any other ecosystem.

What you get:
• Code lenses — Run, Debug, Coverage, and Trace buttons above every @IsTest method. Results stream into the standard test runner tree.
• Local debugger — set breakpoints in .cls and .trigger files, step over/into/out, inspect variables and the call stack. No replay log, no org round-trip.
• Coverage gutters — green/red bars in the editor gutter after every coverage-enabled run.
• Language intelligence — completion, hover documentation, go-to-definition, find-references, rename, diagnostics, inlay hints, and code actions via LSP.
• Execution traces — call-tree, timeline waterfall, and variable inspector for every test run.
• Governor limits dashboard — per-method SOQL, DML, CPU, and heap usage vs Salesforce limits.
• Test history — trends charts, flaky-test detection, and run comparison diff.
• Schema explorer — browse the local PostgreSQL schema, tables, columns, and foreign-key relationships.
• Watch mode — auto-run tests when you save Apex files.
• Method execution — run any public method (not just tests) directly from the editor, with parameter input.

Getting started:
1. Install the CLI: curl -fsSL https://install.testnimbus.dev | sh
2. Open your Salesforce project (must have sfdx-project.json)
3. The plugin starts automatically — click Run on any @IsTest method

Works in IntelliJ IDEA Community, Ultimate, and all JetBrains IDEs that support the Apex Language plugin. Requires JDK 17+.

Full docs at testnimbus.dev. Licensed under the Nimbus EULA.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.23

  • Interactive dependency graph. An interactive graph of your classes, triggers, and their references — hover a class and its direct neighbourhood lights up, click to pin, search by name, hide test classes or unconnected nodes, and double-click to open the class. Cycles are detected and highlighted. Same renderer as the Nimbus DevUI and VS Code extension.
  • The graph is one click away. A graph button on the Nimbus tool-window header, an entry in the editor right-click menu, and Nimbus → Show Dependency Graph in the main menu.
  • Fuller editor right-click menu. Validate Current File and Show Dependency Graph join Run Tests, Execute Anonymous, and View Trace in the Apex editor context menu.

1.0.22

  • Watch runs use the test runner. Auto-runs on save now open the same Run tool window console as a run started from a gutter icon — full test tree, failure details, click-through to the failing line. Previously they reported only as a balloon notification in the corner with a pass count.
  • Watch runs report failures honestly. A watch run that couldn't start, or that matched no tests because the file you just saved doesn't compile, now says so instead of showing "0/0 passed".
  • Class-level code lenses are visible again. Run class / Bench class / Coverage were anchored to the first line of the file rather than to the class, so on any file opening with a doc block or license header they sat inside the comment — and collapsing it took them along. They now sit on the class line. Requires nimbus 1.9.2 or later.
  • Code-lens buttons stay clickable while the IDE indexes. The Run / Debug / Coverage / View Trace handlers were not dumb-aware, so during indexing the IDE disabled them and a click was discarded with no feedback. They also now run on the UI thread explicitly rather than depending on the thread the click arrived on.

1.0.20

  • Run tests without LSP4IJ. Clickable run icons now appear in the editor gutter for every @IsTest class and method — Run, Debug, Run with Coverage, and View Trace — with pass/fail state after each run. Previously the only in-editor run affordance was the LSP code lens, which required the optional LSP4IJ plugin.
  • Code lenses work out of the box. LSP4IJ (the LSP client that powers completion, hover, diagnostics, and the Run/Debug code lenses) is a required dependency again, so the Marketplace installs it together with Nimbus. In 1.0.19 it was optional and a fresh install without it silently had no code lenses.
  • Compatible with future IDEs. Removed the upper IDE-version cap so the plugin stays available on 2026.2 (build 262) and later — previously it would have been hidden as "incompatible" after an IDE upgrade.

1.0.19

  • Coexists with Illuminated Cloud. Nimbus no longer registers its own Apex language/file type, so installing it alongside Illuminated Cloud (or any other Apex plugin) no longer triggers the IDE's "Conflicting Plugins" dialog. Both run at once.
  • Defer language intelligence. New setting under Tools → Nimbus to turn off Nimbus completion, hover, and diagnostics and let another Apex plugin own them — while keeping Run/Debug/Coverage and the rest of the runtime.
  • Cleaned up deprecated-API usage and restored compatibility with 2024.2–2025.2 (a coverage-refresh call had briefly required 2025.3+).

1.0.17

  • Coverage delta in the gutter. Snapshot a run with Set Coverage Baseline, then Toggle Coverage Delta to highlight what changed since — green for newly-covered lines, orange for regressions.
  • Code generation. Yellow-bulb refactors on a class declaration: generate a constructor, generate getters and setters, implement interface methods (incl. Queueable / Schedulable / Comparable / Database.Batchable), and override a superclass's virtual/abstract methods.
  • Relationship-aware SOQL & SOSL completion. Owner. / Account.Parent. resolve through relationships; child subqueries and RETURNING Object(…) complete too. Relationship fields are validated.
  • Apex / SOQL live templates. ~20 bundled templates (sysd, tm, soqlf, bulkt, …) under Settings → Editor → Live Templates → Nimbus Apex.
  • Plugin brand icon; dropped internal-platform-API usage for Marketplace compatibility.

idea-plugin.name: Property Key Support
idea-plugin.description:
Bean Validation and Jakarta Validation annotations often reference message keys in braces, such as {name.required}, instead of plain property names. IntelliJ does not treat these as links to messages.properties by default.

Property Key Support adds IDE support for that pattern so property keys stay easy to navigate and maintain.

Features

  • Go to declaration — Ctrl+Click a braced key in a Java message attribute to open the matching entry in messages.properties
  • Find usages — from a property key in messages.properties, jump to every annotation that references it
  • Code completion — suggests available keys while editing message values and inserts them in braced form
  • Unresolved key highlighting — references are resolved through the standard IntelliJ reference mechanism, with a gutter icon and quick fix to create missing entries
  • Rename refactoring — renaming a key in Java or in a property file updates linked usages

Supported usage

Works with string literals on the message attribute of Java validation annotations, for example:

@NotNull(message = "{user.email.required}")
@Size(min = 1, message = "{user.name.required}")

Keys are resolved against message property files in the project, including messages.properties, ValidationMessages.properties, and locale variants such as messages_en.properties.

Compatibility

  • IntelliJ IDEA Community Edition and Ultimate Edition
  • Java projects with the bundled Properties plugin
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.5

  • Fixed IDE error when typing inside non-message string literals such as @Query text blocks

1.1.4

  • Replaced deprecated LineMarkerInfo constructor for current platform API

1.1.3

1.1.0

  • Richer code completion with message text preview and source file name
  • Support for ValidationMessages.properties and messages_*.properties locale files
  • Rename refactoring between Java keys and property files
  • Quick fix to create missing keys in messages.properties

1.0.0

  • Navigation and Find Usages between braced property keys and messages.properties
  • Autocompletion for message attributes in Java annotations
  • Unresolved key highlighting

idea-plugin.name: TODO Highlighter & Comment Manager
idea-plugin.description:
TODO Highlighter & Comment Manager highlights and tracks TODO, FIXME, HACK, NOTE, and XXX comments across your source code — in any language, with editor highlighting, a dedicated tool window, structured metadata, and two-way editing.

It understands a structured comment format:

// TODO [tag] (priority) description

Features

  • Tool window with a tree view of every TODO in the project, grouped by file, tag, or priority.
  • Locate & preview — show each item's file name or full path, hover for its path in a tooltip, and optionally preview items in a single reusable tab on click.
  • Bidirectional editing — change a TODO's description, tag, or priority from the panel and the source comment is rewritten in place (with full undo support).
  • Editor highlighting — keywords, tags, priorities, description text, and comment delimiters are colorized directly in the editor.
  • Add & complete — insert new TODOs at the caret, or mark them done.
  • Precise matching — choose how keyword case is matched (any / upper-only / lower-only) and optionally require a keyword to be the first word on its line, so words like "note" mid-sentence aren't picked up. Optionally suppress the IDE's own built-in TODO highlighting so it doesn't double up with this plugin.
  • Fully configurable — customize keywords and all colors under Settings > Tools > TODO Manager.
  • Auto-refresh as you edit files.

Works in all IntelliJ-based IDEs — IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, PhpStorm, Rider, CLion, RubyMine, Android Studio, and more.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.7.1

  • Group by keyword in Settings — the Keyword grouping was only reachable from the toolbar; it is now also offered in the Group by dropdown under Settings > Tools > TODO Manager.
  • Completed items are highlighted in the editor — DONE comments are now colorized in the editor just like they are listed in the tool window.
  • Fix — changing your keyword list no longer leaves the toolbar's keyword filter pointing at a removed keyword (which could silently hide every item); the filter options now update live and fall back to All when the selected keyword is gone.
  • Internal — priorities and the group-by options now come from a single source of truth, so the scanner, editor highlighting, dialogs, menus, and settings can no longer drift apart.

1.7.0

  • File path in the tool window — each item can show just the file name (default), the path from the project root, or the full absolute path. Configure it under Settings > Tools > TODO Manager.
  • Hover tooltip — hovering an item reveals its path (project-relative by default, or absolute / file name), handy for reading long paths at a glance. It can be turned off entirely.
  • Preview on single click — optionally open items in the editor's reusable preview tab with a single click, so clicking through TODOs doesn't pile up tabs. Editing the file or double-clicking promotes it to a normal tab. (Turning this on enables the IDE's "Open files in preview tab" option; it is restored when turned off.)

1.6.1

  • Fix — the getting-started tour is now offered through a first-run notification instead of opening automatically as a dialog, so it never interrupts startup (and no longer blocks automated IDE/plugin-install checks). Click Start tour in the notification, or open it any time from Help > TODO Manager: Getting Started.

1.6.0

  • Getting-started tour — a short, visual onboarding shown on first run: how markers are highlighted, the KEYWORD [tag] (priority) description format, and where the tool window lives. It can drop you straight into creating your first TODO.
  • Re-open the tour any time from Help > TODO Manager: Getting Started.

1.5.0

  • Scans the whole project by default — TODOs in folders with any name (and their sub-folders) are now picked up, instead of only auto-detected source directories. Excluded and IDE-ignored folders are still skipped, and source-only scanning can be re-enabled in settings.
  • Empty-state guidance — when there is nothing to show, the tool window now says so; if scanning is limited to source directories but none exist, it offers a link straight into the settings to add one.
  • Fix — no longer throws a Read access is allowed from inside read-action only error when marking a TODO as done or deleting it.
  • Fix — the settings page now scrolls with the mouse wheel, not only the scrollbar.

1.4.0

  • Group by keyword — a new Keyword option in the Group by menu.
  • Keyword filter — a toolbar dropdown to show only items with a chosen keyword, or All to show every keyword.

1.3.1

  • Collapse by default — a Collapse toolbar toggle to start groups collapsed instead of fully expanded.
  • Expand/collapse state preserved on refresh — refreshing keeps each group the way you left it; newly appearing groups follow the collapse-by-default setting.
  • Reverse sort — a Reverse toolbar toggle that flips the group order and the items within each group.
  • Live updates — the tool window now refreshes as TODOs are added, changed, or removed in the editor, without waiting for the file to be saved.
  • Fix — no longer logs a write-unsafe context error while typing; the live re-scan now runs only once the edited document's PSI is committed.

1.2.1

  • Fix — no longer throws an IndexOutOfBoundsException when scanning a file whose content has just changed (the comment offsets could briefly outrun the reloaded document). Affected files now re-scan once the editor catches up.

1.2.0

  • Keyword case matching — choose Any case, Upper-case only, or Lower-case only so a lower-case note in prose isn't mistaken for the NOTE keyword.
  • First-word matching — optionally only recognize a keyword when it's the first word on its line, so keywords appearing mid-sentence are ignored.
  • Suppress IDE TODO highlighting — optionally clear the IDE's own built-in TODO highlighting so it doesn't double up with this plugin (restored when turned off).

1.1.0

  • Create general (code-free) TODOs from the panel — check "General TODO" in the New TODO dialog to track items that aren't attached to any comment.
  • Mark as Done now stamps the completion with your git user name and the date, e.g. DONE fix login (done by J4sp3r on 2026-06-29).
  • Completed items stay visible — DONE comments and done general todos are shown struck through with a "done by … on …" label. Toggle them with Show done in the toolbar.

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • Tool window with tree view of all TODO/FIXME/HACK/NOTE comments
  • Structured comment format: // TODO [tag] (priority) description
  • Group by file, tag, or priority
  • Bidirectional editing: change priority/tag/description in panel → updates source
  • Add new TODOs from the panel
  • Mark TODOs as done
  • Configurable keywords and patterns
  • Auto-refresh on file changes

idea-plugin.name: Pomo-BREAK
idea-plugin.description:
A focus timer with a built-in brick-breaker game to enjoy during your breaks.
  • Classic Pomodoro flow: configurable Focus / Short break / Long break.
  • Long break automatically after every 4 focus sessions.
  • When a focus session ends, a Breakout-style game appears for your break.
  • Move the paddle with the mouse or the ◀ ▶ arrow keys; Space launches the ball.
Open it from View | Tool Windows | Pomo-BREAK! (right side bar).
idea-plugin.change-notes:

  • HUD and overlay text gained a subtle shadow so they stay readable on any background.
  • Fixed a flicker where the game background flashed on the timer tick.
1.0.0 — Initial release: Pomodoro timer + brick-breaker break game.

idea-plugin.name: World Cup Flags
idea-plugin.description:
World Cup Flags lets you fly a country's flag right in your IDE toolbar — pick your home nation, your World Cup favorite, or whatever flag puts a smile on your face.

  • Choose from 260+ country and territory flags
  • Your flag appears as a button on the main toolbar

idea-plugin.name: Chauffeur
idea-plugin.description: Chauffeur captures and restores your open JetBrains IDE projects and editor files through the local Chauffeur desktop app. 100% local — no cloud, no tracking. Requires the Windows Chauffeur desktop application.

  • 1.2.7 — Optionally closes open JetBrains IDE projects before a restore, so a restored context replaces the current one cleanly instead of stacking on top.

  • 1.2.0 — Restore of captured projects and editor files.

idea-plugin.name: OpenApi-Helper
idea-plugin.description: OpenAPI Helper is an IntelliJ IDEA plugin that enables seamless navigation from OpenAPI YAML contracts to their corresponding Java or Kotlin implementations.

idea-plugin.name: VgScript
idea-plugin.description:
Write branching video-game narratives in clean, readable plain text.

VgScript turns .vgs files into a first-class language in your JetBrains IDE, helping writers and developers work faster and catch mistakes before they reach the game.

  • Syntax and semantic highlighting
  • Live validation as you type
  • One-click tools to fix, reconcile, and manage scripts
  • Consistent results across JetBrains IDEs and VS Code

Highlighting and live validation work immediately. The vgs engine is bundled on Windows and configurable on macOS and Linux. The bundled engine is also installed as a vgs command for terminals and AI agents.

Learn VgScript →

idea-plugin.name: SSH Plus
idea-plugin.description:
All-in-one SSH workspace for JetBrains IDEs — manage hosts, open interactive terminals, browse remote files, transfer data, and forward ports without leaving the IDE.

  • Connection hub — saved hosts, groups, tags, jump hosts, Quick Connect (Ctrl+Shift+S), and OpenSSH config import/export
  • Interactive terminal — multi-tab JediTerm sessions with reconnect, ANSI colors, shell history, and TUI support
  • Remote files & transfers — browse, edit, upload/download with cancel/retry, drag-and-drop, Open Terminal Here
  • Port forwarding — create and manage local SSH tunnels from a dedicated tab
  • Built for production — host key verification, PasswordSafe secrets, production confirmations, and redacted diagnostics
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Tunnels: multiple local port forwards per connection, persisted with OpenSSH LocalForward and backup import/export; park when switching connections.
  • Disconnect soft-ends terminals (tabs stay with Reconnect) and stops that connection’s tunnels; terminal tabs stay global across connections.
  • Delete group removes member connections instead of moving them to Ungrouped.
  • Logs UI polish (card chrome, status chips, Tab path completion) and transfer progress in the IDE status bar.
  • Files: Upload and Download support multi-select.

idea-plugin.name: Break Reminder
idea-plugin.description: A simple break reminder plugin for IntelliJ IDEA that uses Cron expressions to schedule rest notifications. Supports customizable reminder content, background image, opacity, and font color. Keep your eyes healthy and take regular breaks during long coding sessions.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Changelog 1.1.0: - 重构设置面板：输入框统一宽度，添加图片缩略图预览和颜色色块回显 - 放宽 idea-version 兼容范围，最低支持 IDEA 2022.3（build 223.0）

idea-plugin.name: Fish Browser
idea-plugin.description:
Fish Browser is a translucent, always-on-top web browser overlaid on your IDE, powered by the bundled JCEF (Chromium). Read docs or just browse while you work, then press the "boss key" to hide it instantly.

Features
  • Two modes — a draggable floating window, or a "background" that covers only the current editor area. Toggle with one shortcut.
  • Web vs. code — one key switches between using the page and writing code; in code mode the mouse clicks through to your editor (optional dimming, off by default; Windows only).
  • Zen mode — a hotkey hides the toolbar, address bar and bookmarks so only the web page shows.
  • Boss key to show/hide instantly. All shortcuts are customizable in Settings.
  • Follows the IDE — hides on minimize / when the IDE isn't focused; links open in place.
Note: the IDE's bundled Chromium ships without proprietary codecs (H.264/AAC), so many video sites (e.g. Bilibili) report "unsupported"; sites using VP9/WebM (e.g. YouTube) work. Best for text / reading. Mouse click-through is Windows-only.

中文：在 IDE 上浮一个半透明、可调透明度、可置顶的浏览器（基于 IDE 内置的 JCEF/Chromium）。 一边写代码一边看，老板来了一键隐藏。
  • 两种形态：可拖动的浮窗，或只盖住当前编辑区的「背景」，一个快捷键互转。
  • 网页 / 代码切换：一键在「用网页」和「写代码」间切；代码模式下鼠标穿透到编辑器（可选变暗，默认关；仅 Windows）。
  • 沉浸模式：一个快捷键隐藏工具栏/地址栏/书签，只看网页本身。
  • 老板键一键隐藏；所有快捷键都能在设置里自定义。
  • 跟随 IDE：最小化 / 失焦自动隐藏；链接原地打开。
注意：IDE 自带的 Chromium 没有商业编解码器（H.264/AAC），B 站等用 H.264 的视频站会提示「不支持」， YouTube 等 VP9/WebM 站可放；更适合看文字/阅读。鼠标穿透仅 Windows。
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.2.0
  • Zen / immersive mode — one hotkey (default Ctrl+Alt+Shift+`) hides the toolbar, address bar and bookmarks so only the web page shows; press again to restore (also the toolbar's “沉浸” button / Tools menu). 沉浸模式：一个快捷键（默认 Ctrl+Alt+Shift+`）只看网页，隐藏工具栏/地址栏/书签，再按还原（也有工具栏「沉浸」按钮 / 工具菜单）。
  • Loading indicator — a spinner plus a thin top progress bar appear the instant you press Enter/Go (and stay visible in Zen mode), so a slow page no longer feels frozen. 载入特效：一按回车/Go 立刻出现转圈 + 顶部细加载条（沉浸模式下也显示），慢页面不再像卡住。
  • Optional code-mode dimming — switching Web⇄Code no longer changes brightness by default; re-enable dimming in Settings if you want it. 代码模式明暗可控：默认切换 网页⇄代码 不再变暗，需要的话在设置里开启。
  • HTTP login prompt — sites behind HTTP Basic auth (e.g. self-hosted SillyTavern) now show a proper username/password dialog instead of a blank window. HTTP 登录框：HTTP Basic 认证的站点（如自建 SillyTavern）现在会弹出正常的用户名/密码框，不再是空白窗口。
  • Fix — keystrokes no longer leak into the code editor when the floating window overlaps it. 修复：浮窗压在代码上时，键盘输入不再跑到后面的编辑器。
1.1.0
  • Background auto-fits the editor — it now follows your editor pane as you resize the IDE, toggle tool windows, or split editors. 背景自动跟随当前编辑器（拉伸 IDE / 开关工具窗 / 分屏都会重贴）。
  • Page zoom — from the toolbar, with Ctrl+Wheel, or in Settings; Ctrl+Shift+Wheel adjusts opacity. 页面缩放（工具栏 / Ctrl+滚轮 / 设置）；Ctrl+Shift+滚轮 调透明度。
  • Loading state — Reload becomes Stop while a page loads; Back/Forward disable when unavailable. 加载状态：刷新 ⇄ 停止、前进/后退自动置灰。
  • Search engine choice — Bing / Google / Baidu for address-bar searches; bare domains open directly. 地址栏可选搜索引擎 + 智能识别网址。
  • Bookmarks bar — star the current page; left-click to open, right-click to remove. 书签栏：☆ 收藏，左键打开、右键删除。
1.0.0

idea-plugin.name: WSL Remote Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Small quality-of-life helpers for JetBrains Remote Development over WSL.

When the IDE backend runs on WSL (Linux), IntelliJ hides the actions that reach the Windows host. This plugin brings them back, using WSL interop (wslpath + explorer.exe):
  • Open in Explorer — reveal the selected file/folder in Windows Explorer.
  • Open in Windows native application — open the file with its associated Windows app.
  • Copy → Windows Path — copy the Windows form of the path (e.g. C:\… or \\wsl$\…).
The actions appear only when the backend is a WSL distro.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Please kindly report any problem... and Rate & Review this plugin !

Change notes :
  • 1.0.1 Initial version — restores Windows host integration when working over WSL Remote Development: Open in Explorer, Open in Windows native application, and Copy Windows path.

idea-plugin.name: Show Contributors
idea-plugin.description:
Show Contributors

Analyze code ownership with contributor stats and recent ticket activity for files or folders - instantly from your IDE.

Who worked on this?

  • Right-click any file or folder and see every contributor ranked by how much they own.
  • Click a contributor to open their full profile - avatar, name, contribution share, commit count, and last active date.
  • Your own name is highlighted so you always know where you stand.

Recent Ticket Activity

  • See which tickets a contributor has worked on for the selected file or folder.
  • Ticket IDs link directly to your issue tracker (e.g. Jira) when you set your team's URL prefix once.
  • Commits with no ticket are shown in an "Untagged Commits" card - nothing is hidden.
  • Expand commit messages per ticket to see exactly what changed.

Ticket Actions (⋮ menu)

  • Open Ticket - jump straight to the ticket in your browser.
  • Copy Ticket ID / Link - paste into Slack, email, or a PR description.
  • Copy Commit Messages - grab all related commit notes in one click.

Reviewer Suggestions

  • Top code owners are automatically tagged with a green ✓ Reviewer label directly in the contributor list.
  • The suggestion is based on who owns the most code in the selected area - no manual configuration needed.
  • Your own name is never suggested - you don't review your own work.
  • The details pane also shows a Recommended Reviewer badge when you click that contributor.

Smart Contributor Tags

  • Each contributor's details shows colored tag chips that summarize their role at a glance.
  • Owner – owns ≥ 80 % of all contributions. Lead – top contributor by ownership share.
  • 🔥 Hot – 3 or more commits in the last 7 days. New – first-time contributor within the last 30 days.
  • Active – last commit within 7 days. Frequent – high contribution share or 10+ total commits.
  • Consistent – commits spread across multiple calendar weeks. Occasional – low share or very few commits.
  • Legacy Contributor – no commits in the last 6 months.
  • Tags are mutually exclusive where appropriate and capped at 5 per contributor.

Search, Sort & Filter

  • Search contributors by name as you type.
  • Sort by: Recent Activity · Contribution % · Name.
  • Filter to: All · Above 5% · Top 5 · Active last 7 or 30 days.

Avatars

  • Initials shown instantly; real profile photos load quietly in the background.
  • Works with GitLab, GitHub, and Bitbucket - detected automatically from your remote URL.

Whole-Project View

  • Tools → Show Project Contributors gives you ownership stats across the entire repo with no file selected.

Requirements

All you need is git on your system PATH.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
v2.3.0

  • Split-pane UI: contributor list (30%) + details pane (70%) with identity card, stats, and reviewer badge.
  • Smart contributor tags in the contributor details: Owner, Lead, Reviewer, 🔥 Hot, New, Active, Frequent, Consistent, Occasional, Legacy Contributor.
  • Lazy-loaded ticket cards per contributor and scope.
  • Commit timestamps shown below each commit message in ticket cards (relative time with exact date tooltip).
  • Ticket ID chips: clickable when a tracker URL prefix is configured via ⚙ Configure.
  • Untagged commits shown in a dedicated "Untagged Commits" card - never silently dropped.
  • ⋮ actions menu on every ticket card: Open Ticket, Copy ID, Copy Link, Copy Commit Messages, Show PR/MR.
  • Batch ticket expansion: 5 → 10 → 20 → 50 more with progressive load steps.
  • Merge-commit filter: auto-generated merge subjects excluded from ticket cards.
  • Tracker URL prefix persisted in IDE application settings.
  • Tools → Show Project Contributors: analyses the full repo with no file selection required.
  • CardLayout loading states: spinner while fetching, empty-state and error messages.
  • 120 px avatar in the details pane with bicubic high-quality rendering and retry logic.
  • Ticket section header: original-case filename highlighted with accent colour, [File]/[Folder] type tag.
  • Case-insensitive email matching for ticket fetching (fixes missing tickets for mixed-case git authors).
  • Default sort changed to Recent Activity.

v2.2.0

  • Search field: live filter contributors by name.
  • Sort options: Contribution %, Name (A–Z), Recent Activity.
  • Filter options: All, Above 5%, Top 5, Active Last 7/30 days.
  • Dynamic footer with PR/MR reviewer recommendations based on contributor distribution.
  • Current user highlighted with (You) badge and blue row tint.
  • Last contribution time shown per row (e.g. "last commit 3d ago").
  • [File] / [Folder] label in dialog title.

v2.1.0

  • Multi-platform avatar support: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket.
  • Platform auto-detection via git remote URL.
  • Fixed Gravatar default-image issue (d=identicon → d=404).
  • GitHub noreply address parsing for direct avatar resolution.

v2.0.0

  • Lazy avatar loading - only visible rows trigger network requests.
  • In-memory avatar cache and contributor cache with 5-minute TTL.

v1.0

  • Initial release.

idea-plugin.name: App Config Manager
idea-plugin.description:
App Config Manager helps inspect, compare, and edit Spring Boot application configuration files by module.

  • Available for JetBrains IDEs with Java support.
  • Supports Spring Boot YAML and properties configuration files.
  • Lists application.yml, application.yaml, application.properties and application-{profile} files per module.
  • Detects active Spring profiles from spring.profiles.active.
  • Shows the effective merged configuration in a custom editor.
  • Automatically saves merged edits to their source files and validates YAML before writing.
  • Uses IntelliJ's three-way merge to reconcile concurrent source changes without discarding editor edits on cancellation.
  • Supports properties escapes, Unicode, and continuation lines, plus simple YAML lists and block scalars.
  • Highlights overridden values and active profile values.
  • Keeps normal IntelliJ editor behavior when files are opened outside the tool window.
  • Supports editable local override config stored under .idea/app-config-manager.
  • Stores local config as delta overrides instead of copying the whole effective configuration.
  • Updates Spring Boot run configurations with spring.config.additional-location for local overrides.
  • Runs, debugs, and stops the selected module using IntelliJ's execution infrastructure.
  • Shows live execution state for modules started from either the plugin or IntelliJ.
  • Supports saved and temporary run configurations in multi-module projects.
  • Excludes application config files from test source roots.
  • Automatically refreshes when application config files change.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.8

  • Removed a YAML API dependency unavailable in IntelliJ IDEA IU-261.27258.48 while retaining explicit-key validation.
  • Improved merged editor saving, YAML insertion boundaries, and source mappings for list items and parent keys.
  • Preserved properties escapes, Unicode, and continuation lines when reading and editing configuration values.
  • Supported YAML lists whose items have the same indentation as their header and preserved explicit YAML null values.
  • Added IntelliJ's three-way merge for source files changed while the merged editor has unsaved edits; cancelling keeps the editor changes.
  • Added YAML validation before merged saves and prevented incomplete local YAML edits from silently removing existing values.
  • Protected unsaved edits from asynchronous reloads and stopped rewriting existing local overrides during refresh.
  • Respected active profile order and supported profile expressions with negation, conjunction, disjunction, and parentheses.
  • Reduced redundant background scans, grouped split modules into one entry, and preserved quoting and whitespace in existing VM options.

0.1.7

  • Added module-aware Run, Debug, and Stop controls with live execution state.
  • Placed compact execution controls beside each module in multi-module projects.
  • Highlighted the active Run or Debug action in green and the available Stop action in red.
  • Added live PID and listening TCP port details, including child application processes.
  • Detected module processes started from either App Config Manager or IntelliJ.
  • Kept the module tree visible while Gradle roots and local run configurations are synchronized.
  • Improved compatibility with Java 25-based IntelliJ builds while preserving Java 21 plugin bytecode.
  • Replaced internal execution APIs with public project-level execution events for IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1 compatibility.

0.1.6

  • Fixed delegated Gradle runs using a stale JRE instead of the selected module SDK.
  • Fixed Spring Boot modules being created or launched as generic Application configurations.
  • Preserved explicitly selected alternative JRE settings.

0.1.5

  • Fixed Gradle project task runner read-access failures when launching modules from the plugin.
  • Fixed IntelliJ IDEA 2025.3 binary compatibility by avoiding a newer read-action API.
  • Switched automatic run configuration creation to IntelliJ's standard context producers.
  • Preserved the module, JRE, working directory, and Gradle execution settings used by IntelliJ's normal Run action.
  • Improved Java main-class detection for Gradle split modules such as module.main.
  • Added fallback support for standard Java main classes without a SpringBootApplication annotation.

0.1.4

  • Added a Run action for launching the selected module from the App Configs tool window.
  • Added automatic IntelliJ Application configuration creation from Spring Boot and standard Java main classes.
  • Improved module resolution for Gradle-style split modules such as module.main.
  • Applied local config settings to the correct saved or temporary run configuration in multi-module projects.
  • Excluded application config files located under test source roots.
  • Placed the Run action and local config switch in a compact horizontal toolbar.
  • Removed synchronous VFS refresh calls from read-locked config resolution.

Instantly switch between 'en' and 'ru' folders for the same file with a shortcut. Works with single or multiple file selection, preserves caret position and scroll offset.
Switching in diff view is also supported

Version 1.4.3
