idea-plugin.name: CodeSpotlight
idea-plugin.description:
CodeSpotlight

Make Your Selected Code the Visual Focus.

CodeSpotlight transforms standard IntelliJ IDEA code selection into a customizable animated visual focus with glowing borders, moving lights, and smooth visual effects — without modifying your source code.

How to Customize CodeSpotlight

Customize your selection effect directly from Settings → Tools → Animated Selection (CodeSpotlight). Enable the effect, choose your colors and animation mode, adjust the visual controls, and return to the editor to see your changes instantly.

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Go to Tools → Animated Selection (CodeSpotlight).
  3. Enable animated selection.
  4. Choose your colors and animation mode.
  5. Adjust the available visual parameters.
  6. Return to the editor and select code.
Customize everything from IntelliJ IDEA Settings — no code changes required.

What CodeSpotlight Does

  • Visually highlights selected code, including multi-line selections.
  • Preserves IntelliJ IDEA's normal selection and editing behavior.
  • Provides animated visual effects without modifying source code.
  • Offers multiple animation styles including Traveling Border, Pulse, Breathing Glow, and Static Glow.
  • Provides controls for colors, animation speed, glow intensity, border thickness, glow radius, corner radius, animation FPS, moving light segments, light trails, and saved presets.
  • Includes Focus Mode with CodeSpotlight Pro.

Customize the Experience

Appearance

  • Built-in color presets.
  • Custom primary and secondary colors — Pro.
  • Border thickness, glow radius, corner radius, and glow intensity.

Animation

  • Animation mode and speed.
  • Moving light segments and animation FPS.
  • Light trail controls.
  • Advanced trail length and intensity/fade controls — Pro.

Free vs Pro

Feature Free Pro
Animated selection highlighting Included Included
Animation modes Traveling Border, Pulse, Breathing Glow, Static Glow Everything in Free, plus Travel + Pulse, Energy Sweep, Aurora, and Orbit
Colors Built-in color presets Everything in Free, plus custom primary and secondary colors
Moving light segments One One to four
Light trail Standard trail and trail enablement Everything in Free, plus trail length and intensity/fade controls
Visual controls Speed, glow intensity, border thickness, glow radius, corner radius, and animation FPS Everything in Free
Saved presets Up to two Unlimited
Editor color scheme Optional CodeSpotlight Dark color-scheme integration Included
Focus Mode — Included

Why CodeSpotlight?

CodeSpotlight helps selected code remain visually easy to follow during presentations, technical tutorials, screen recordings, live coding, code demonstrations, reviews, and everyday development workflows. It stays inside IntelliJ IDEA and does not require changes to your code.

Designed for Developers

CodeSpotlight is designed to stay out of the way. Your code remains native IntelliJ IDEA code while the plugin adds a configurable visual focus layer around the current selection. Appearance and animation settings are available directly inside IntelliJ IDEA.

Unlock CodeSpotlight Pro

Take your coding presentations and visual workflow further with custom colors, advanced animation modes, multiple moving light segments, advanced light trails, Focus Mode, and unlimited saved presets.

Select. Focus. Customize. Code.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
What's New

  • Refined Focus Mode with a darker selected-code surface and an unchanged surrounding editor.
  • Clearer ✦ PRO indicators and Free/Pro feature separation in settings.
  • Expanded visual customization, animation modes, trails, moving-light segments, and saved presets.
  • Updated CodeSpotlight branding and Marketplace overview.

idea-plugin.name: insrc
idea-plugin.description:
insrc brings the insrc code-knowledge system into the JetBrains IDE family — IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, and WebStorm — from a single install. It is a thin orchestrator that owns no reasoning of its own: it wires insrc's grounded-analyze and tracked-workflow capabilities into the IDE's own AI assistant and manages the backing daemon, so your assistant answers from a citation-grounded model of your codebase rather than guessing.

What is insrc?

insrc is a local-first code-knowledge daemon. It parses your repos with tree-sitter into a typed entity/relation graph (backed by LMDB) and a vector store (LanceDB) for semantic search, then serves two things to your AI assistant over a private MCP server:

  • Grounded analyze — every answer about your code is built from real graph queries and embedded search, and each claim is cited to a specific file and symbol. No raw file dumps, no hallucinated paths — the assistant reasons over a verified, dependency-scoped model of the codebase.
  • A tracked workflow — a human-in-the-loop authoring pipeline that takes one request from triage → design → review → plan → build → code-review, producing an approved, cited artifact at every stage and refusing to advance until you approve the one before it. Every change, large or small, is tracked; a defect fix routes through a first-class bugfix path that captures reproduction and root cause and can open, link, and close a GitHub issue for you.

All of this runs on your machine and reasons through your assistant's existing claude / codex CLI sessions — there are no API keys and no direct cloud calls from insrc itself.

What the plugin does

  • One integration, four IDEs. A single artifact activates identically in IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, and WebStorm — it depends only on the shared platform module, so there is nothing IDE-specific to install or configure per product.
  • Wires your AI host automatically. On project open it detects your agentic assistant (JetBrains AI Assistant or Junie) and registers the insrc MCP server into that host's own configuration, plus the tracked-workflow steering into its rules file — so the assistant immediately knows to ground its answers and route features through insrc.
  • One-click project enablement. An "Enable insrc for this project" prompt registers the open project with the insrc daemon; every capability call is scoped to that project's own path, so a multi-project window keeps each repo's knowledge separate.
  • Manages the backing daemon for you. It ensures the daemon is present and up to date, and provisions a private, pinned Node runtime when the system one is missing or unsuitable — first-time setup is a single explicit consent, and later updates are silent and automatic.
  • Grounded analyze + tracked workflow, in your assistant. Once wired, your existing IDE assistant explores the code through the citation-grounded graph and can drive the full tracked design → review → plan → build workflow without leaving the IDE.
  • Clean and reversible. Every write into a host config or rules file is marker-delimited and preserves your own surrounding content. Uninstalling the plugin removes exactly those blocks and nothing else; a mere disable leaves them intact so re-enabling is instant.

How it works

The plugin holds no model logic of its own. It is a configuration orchestrator: it detects the host, writes the MCP + steering registration, registers the project with the daemon, and keeps the daemon healthy. All reasoning happens in your assistant, grounded by the daemon — the plugin simply makes the connection and stays out of the way.

Privacy

The plugin opens no cloud path and stores no credentials. The graph and vectors live on your disk; embeddings are computed locally; and all LLM access goes through your assistant's existing CLI/OAuth sessions. Nothing about your code leaves your machine because of this plugin.

Requirements

  • A JetBrains AI host (AI Assistant or Junie) — without one the plugin stays dormant and re-checks on later project opens, so it is safe to install ahead of time.
  • Node (used by the daemon); the plugin provisions a private runtime automatically if the system Node is missing or unsuitable.
  • The insrc daemon, which the plugin installs and keeps current on first use, with your consent.
  • Ollama — required for local embeddings (default qwen3-embedding:0.6b; a no-Ollama ONNX alternative, nomic-embed-text-v1.5, is also available), and optional for the core model (run it on Ollama, or through your existing claude / codex CLI instead).

Full setup → Getting Started.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.5.2

  • Ollama called out in Requirements + a Getting Started link. The description now lists Ollama in Requirements — required for local embeddings (default qwen3-embedding:0.6b; a no-Ollama ONNX alternative, nomic-embed-text-v1.5, is also available) and optional for the core model (run it on Ollama, or through your existing claude / codex CLI) — and points to the Getting Started guide for full setup.

0.5.1

  • Reload nudge after a daemon update. When a daemon self-update succeeds, the plugin now reminds you to restart your claude / codex session so the insrc MCP connection reconnects to the freshly-updated daemon (the previous session still talks to the old daemon process until then). Notification-only — the IDE cannot restart the CLI-owned MCP host in place.

0.5.0

  • Keeps the backing daemon current. When a project opens (only if the daemon is already reachable) the plugin checks whether the installed daemon has fallen behind its upstream, and if so shows an Update / Dismiss balloon that updates the daemon in place on your OK. When you update the plugin itself, it brings the daemon current automatically. The check runs off the UI thread and never blocks project opening; a failed update surfaces once with the raw reason and is not retried or rolled back — the daemon owns its own state.

0.4.0

  • Pick a tier's model from a dropdown. On the insrc Settings page the Model tiers section now offers each global tier (core / mid / cheap) a provider chooser plus a model dropdown filtered to exactly what the daemon reports for that tier's provider — Ollama's installed models, or the curated Claude / Codex catalog — so you pick a model instead of typing a raw id. A Refresh button re-queries after an outage; a provider with no models shows no models available; a saved model that isn't in the list is shown as (current, not in catalog); and switching a tier's provider clears the model so you choose one from the new list.

0.3.1

  • Polished the Project-view insrc menu & status popup. The insrc context-menu item now shows the insrc icon, and the Show Repo status popup presents the repo's stats as expandable sections (Repository, Files by language, Entities by kind) with tidy tables in a fixed-size, scrollable popup — long paths and values stay readable (hover to see the full value).

0.3.0

  • New: an insrc entry on the Project-view right-click menu. Right-click in the Project tool window and pick insrc. The item is context-aware: when the open project is already registered with the insrc daemon it reads Show Repo status and opens a popup with that repo's index stats — indexed file count (and a per-language breakdown), entity and relation counts (by kind), on-disk size, pending index jobs, and last-indexed time. When the project is not yet registered it reads Register Repo and opens a popup that registers it, with optional toggles to inject the insrc steering block into CLAUDE.md and/or AGENTS.md.

0.2.10

  • Vertical scrolling fix. The Settings page is now itself a scroll pane, so the IDE bounds it to the window and its vertical scrollbar reliably reaches all content — expanding a section no longer clips rows or makes the scrollbar flash and vanish.

0.2.8

  • Fixed vertical scrolling on the Settings page. The page stays bounded to the window and its vertical scrollbar reaches all content; the earlier horizontal-growth glitch is gone (the page never scrolls sideways — it fills the width).

0.2.7

  • Compatibility: removed all internal/deprecated platform-API usage flagged by the Plugin Verifier on newer IDEs — host detection uses the stable isPluginInstalled, and the Settings apply path no longer calls a deprecated exception accessor. The build now verifies against recent IDE releases so this class of drift is caught at build time.

0.2.6

  • Fixed: the Settings page clipped its content on expand. Expanding a section grew the whole page to fit and pushed the scrollbar out, so content past the fold became unreachable. The page now stays bounded to the window and its scrollbar scrolls the overflow.

0.2.5

  • Compatibility: the AI-host detection no longer calls an internal platform API (PluginManager.findEnabledPlugin, which newer IDEs mark internal); it now uses the public getLoadedPlugins() with the same installed-and-enabled semantics, keeping the plugin clean under the Plugin Verifier.

0.2.4

  • Fixed: per-repository overrides failed to load ("class com.google.gson.JsonArray cannot be cast to…JsonObject"). The daemon's repo.list returns a bare JSON array; the transport now reads an array result correctly instead of crashing, so the per-repo override editor and its add-repository picker populate again.
  • This also clears a brief scrollbar flicker that the long error message caused on the Settings page.

0.2.3

  • Settings page is now collapsible sections. Settings › Tools › insrc is a single scrolling page of expand/collapse category sections — click a ▾/▸ header to open a category into its editable key / value / default table. General is expanded on load, the rest collapsed.
  • The whole page scrolls as one, each table sized to its content, and the page fills the Settings window rather than a fixed size.
  • The per-role and per-repository override editors are their own collapsible sections on the same page.

0.2.2

  • Reworked Settings page. Settings › Tools › insrc is now an expandable category tree on the left with a key / value / default table on the right — every setting's current value and default are shown at a glance, and the page scrolls properly when there is a lot of content.
  • Edit a value inline in the table (chooser / toggle / text by type) with a per-row reset-to-default; the General category is open by default.
  • The per-role and per-repository override editors are now their own nodes in the same tree.

0.2.1

  • New: a native insrc Settings page. Under Settings › Tools › insrc you can now see and edit every daemon setting from the IDE — grouped into collapsible sections and rendered entirely from the daemon's own description, so the plugin never forks or hardcodes the schema.
  • Edit global settings with type-appropriate controls (choosers, toggles, number and text fields), reset any setting to its default, and Apply — writes go straight to the daemon's config.
  • Per-role overrides: pick the model tier for each reasoning role, or fall back to the default routing.
  • Per-repository overrides: add an override for a registered repository and tune its full per-repo tiering — the accuracy floor, per-role tiers, and per-tier runner/model — without touching the global defaults; remove it to return the repo to global.

0.2.0

  • New: the in-IDE artifact review panel. An "insrc Review" tool window lists the workflow artifacts awaiting your approval, and you can now handle each one in place without leaving the IDE:
  • Read an artifact's fully rendered content (design, plan, and review documents) in the panel.
  • Annotate it with PR-style inline comments anchored to the exact section or passage you're commenting on.
  • Submit your comments back as tracked open-question resolutions, so your feedback lands on the artifact itself.
  • Approve a pending artifact directly from the panel — with a clear block notice when a review verdict withholds approval, and an explicit "Approve anyway" override when you choose to proceed.
  • Expanded the Marketplace listing with a fuller description of what insrc is (local-first code-knowledge daemon: grounded analyze + tracked workflow) and how the plugin wires it into your IDE assistant.

0.1.1

  • Compatibility: removed the upper IDE-build bound — the plugin now loads on current and future IDE releases (2024.2 and later), since it depends only on the stable platform module.

0.1.0

  • Initial release.
  • Single-artifact activation across IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, and WebStorm.
  • AI-host detection (AI Assistant / Junie) with automatic MCP-server and tracked-workflow steering registration.
  • One-click project registration against the insrc daemon.
  • Daemon lifecycle management: presence/staleness check, consented first-time setup, tiered Node runtime.
  • Clean, reversible uninstall of all host-file writes.

idea-plugin.name: Send Code to Terminal
idea-plugin.description:
Send the current line or selected code directly to the active IDE terminal and execute it.

Works with single-line and multi-line selections while keeping focus in the editor.
idea-plugin.change-notes: • Lowered the minimum supported IDE build to 262 (2026.2), so the plugin now also installs in 2026.2-based IDEs.

idea-plugin.name: Slang [Unofficial] Refined
idea-plugin.description:
I didn't find any working slang lsps here, so I just took one and added a lot of features that make it work.

So this plugin gives you everything, code completion, syntax highlight, docs in popup, go-to-definition, find usages, rename, clang-format support, vcpkg-installed slang support etc

This is a refined fork of Slang [Unofficial], props to 16-Bit-Dog
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Slang Refined — supported features

  • Language support for .slang and .slangh files through Slang's language server and LSP4IJ
  • Syntax highlighting and semantic colors
  • Code completion
  • Language-server diagnostics, document symbols in the Structure view, and configurable inlay hints
  • Go to Declaration/Definition
  • Hover and Quick Documentation
  • Find Usages
  • Native usage navigation from declarations
  • Rename
  • Document, selection, and on-type formatting through clang-format
  • Automatic discovery of locally installed vcpkg slangd packages, plus an explicit server directory and PATH-based discovery
  • Project settings for additional include/search paths, predefined macros, and searching workspace subdirectories

The rename fallback covers project Slang files under the current server configuration. It cannot check inactive code, external references, or new-name conflicts. Built-in/external declarations and ambiguous or unverified targets are rejected; changes to project files during search or preview require a new search.

Requires LSP4IJ and a working slangd installation. Formatting additionally requires clang-format. Server-provided features depend on the installed Slang version.

  • Optional mnemonic number on gutter icon

idea-plugin.name: Notebook+
idea-plugin.description:
Project notebook for IntelliJ IDEA / Android Studio:
  • Notes with categories
  • Pin important notes

idea-plugin.name: Teal
idea-plugin.description:
Teal (.tl) support for IntelliJ IDEA: syntax highlighting, inline diagnostics, hover, go-to-definition (including from a require string to the module's file), type definition, completion, signature help, Find Usages (same-document), and a quick fix that adds the missing require for an unknown global type.

Language intelligence comes from a small language server bundled with the plugin and built on the tl compiler, run through LSP4IJ. It needs Lua and the tl rock installed (luarocks install tl). Syntax highlighting reuses vscode-teal's MIT-licensed TextMate grammar.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 0.5.0: Teal support now comes from a language server bundled with the plugin, built on the tl compiler. It needs Lua and luarocks install tl; teal-language-server is no longer needed. Adds completion, signature help and type definition, better hover and go-to-definition, Find Usages on record fields, and spell-checking limited to comments and strings.
  • 0.4.0: Cmd/Ctrl+Click on a require("...") string opens the required module's file.
  • 0.3.0: Quick fix for unknown type X errors: Alt+Enter adds the require of the module that declares the global type.
  • 0.2.0: Find Usages for .tl files (current document), implemented in the plugin itself since teal-language-server doesn't support it.
  • 0.1.0: Initial release — syntax highlighting, inline diagnostics, hover, and go-to-definition for .tl files, plus a distinct file icon in the project tree.

idea-plugin.name: IconDeck
idea-plugin.description:
Recognize important files and folders at a glance in the Project view.

IconDeck adds local icons for build tools, CI, containers, cloud, databases, tests, and documentation. Right-click a file or folder to assign an icon to that name.

  • Free: built-in icons, category controls, and unlimited rules for file names, folder names, and extensions.
  • Pro: path, glob, segment, and regular-expression rules for project conventions.
  • Pro: import and export rules as JSON to share conventions across IDEs or a team.
  • Keep project-specific conventions visible without sending file names or paths anywhere.

Privacy policy | License agreement
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Assign an icon from the Project view and create unlimited name and extension rules for free.
  • Path and pattern rules, plus JSON sharing, are Pro.
  • Fix category fallback and rule resolution behavior.

idea-plugin.name: PrismTabs
idea-plugin.description:
Colour-coded tab groups for editor tabs in JetBrains IDEs.

Right-click a tab for the colour swatch popup: pick one of 8 preset colours to start a new group and name it, or "Add to Group…" to put the tab in a group you already have. "Manage Groups…" lets you list a group's files, rename, recolour, delete, or mark a group active — files opened while a group is active join it automatically, and a file that was already open joins it in one click, from the same popup.

The PrismTabs tool window lists every group with its colour and member count, expands each one to the files it holds, and can hide a group (closing its tabs, remembering them) or show it again. Right-clicking one of those files removes it from its group — no need to open the file first, which is the one thing a tab's own menu cannot offer. Assignments persist across restarts, along with the tabs a hidden group remembers, and follow a file through a rename or move. The preset palette itself is editable under Settings | Tools | PrismTabs.

Free forever
  • Assign tabs to 8 preset colours, each measured for contrast on both light and dark editor tabs
  • Unlimited named groups — create, rename, recolour, delete
  • "Files…" lists everything in a group, open tab or not, and reopens any of it
  • Assignments persist across restarts and survive file renames and moves
Paid — a 14-day free trial, then a subscription
  • The PrismTabs tool window for managing every group at a glance, each group expanding to the files it holds
  • Hide a group to close its tabs and remember them, then show it to reopen them together
  • Mark a group active so newly opened files join it automatically
  • Rename or repaint any preset colour under Settings | Tools | PrismTabs
When the trial ends, PrismTabs drops to the Free tier — never a lockout. Your groups and colours stay either way.

prismtabs.com has the manual, the tier breakdown and the licence agreement. Bugs and feature requests, for every edition, go to the public feedback tracker — anything touching a purchase should be emailed instead, as that tracker is public.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • The message in the PrismTabs tool window for a user without a licence was cut off at both edges at the default tool window width. It now wraps onto two lines.

idea-plugin.name: TabCue: Visual Terminal Tabs
idea-plugin.description:
Give every terminal tab its own colour, emoji, icon and text colour, so five open terminals stop looking like one terminal.

I kept losing track of which was which. npm run dev, a couple of Claude sessions, and an ssh into something I would rather not typo in. They all look identical, and the IDE numbers them "Local (2)", "Local (3)" and leaves you to remember the rest.

Right-click any Terminal tab and choose Tab Style. Everything is there.

What it does

  • Colours. Eight presets, or any colour at all from the IDE's own colour picker, with live preview as you drag. Painted as the tab background and as a small dot beside the name.
  • Emoji. Twelve common ones are a single click in the tab menu, and Custom… takes anything else, including the system emoji palette on macOS.
  • Icons. Ten of the IDE's own, for when an emoji is too much.
  • Text colour. White, black or custom. This is the cue that stays put while a tab is selected.
  • Rules. Style tabs automatically by title or working directory, first match wins. Paint anything matching ssh prod red so you always know which machine you are on.
  • Background tint. Optionally tint the terminal output area too, not just the tab, at a strength you choose.

It does something before you configure anything: each terminal is given its own colour, derived from the tab's name and directory so it is still that colour tomorrow. Rules, auto colours and tint strength all live in Settings ▸ Tools ▸ TabCue, and auto colours can be switched off there if you would rather choose every one yourself.

Good to know

  • The IDE throws away a tab's background colour while that tab is selected, and paints its hover colour over it on hover. The dot, the emoji and the text colour are the cues that survive in every state, which is why the dot is on by default.
  • Split terminals share one colour, because a split is several sessions inside a single tab.
  • An AI agent tab the IDE has already marked with a vendor logo keeps it. The colour still applies, and an emoji you pick yourself still replaces the logo.
  • Works with both the reworked and the classic terminal engine, in any IntelliJ-based IDE that bundles the Terminal.
  • Rules live in .idea/terminalTabStyle.xml so you can commit and share them. Per-tab styles go in workspace.xml, because their keys contain local paths. Nothing leaves your machine.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Per-tab colours and icons for Terminal tool-window tabs, set from the tab's context menu. A colour is drawn both as the tab background and as a small dot, because the IDE's tab painter discards a custom tab colour while a tab is selected or hovered, so the dot is what stays visible in every state.
  • Any colour, not just the presets. Custom… opens the IDE's own colour picker as a popup, with hex entry, RGB fields and the screen eyedropper, and the tab updates live as you drag. Custom colours work in rules too.
  • The tab background is derived from the chosen colour rather than being it: the colour is mixed part-way into the tab-strip background, and then pre-compensated for the translucent overlay JBDefaultTabPainter composites on top. On the dark default that overlay is 60% opaque, which is why an uncompensated tab colour looked washed out. The full-strength colour goes to the dot and the tint, neither of which sits behind text, so no colour can make a tab label unreadable.
  • Emoji tab icons. Twelve common emoji are items in the tab menu, so choosing one is a single click; Custom… opens a small popup for anything else, with a button that opens the system Emoji & Symbols palette on macOS.
  • Rules that style tabs automatically by tab title or working directory, first match wins. The motivating cases: give each AI agent session its own emoji, and paint anything matching ssh prod red so you always know which machine you are on.
  • Optional background tint of the terminal output area itself, not just the tab, with an adjustable strength.
  • Clear Style records an explicit "leave this tab alone" marker, with Use Rules Again to undo it, so clearing a tab is not immediately repainted by a matching rule.
  • Configure Rules… in the tab menu, and a settings page under Tools ▸ TabCue that is findable from Settings search.
  • Auto-assigned colours are on for a fresh install, so the plugin does something visible before it is configured. No rules are invented: guessing which tools you run means naming vendors, picking colours that only look like brand colours, and replacing icons the IDE set itself. Seeded once, so switching it off sticks.
  • Per-tab text colour. White, black or custom, from the Text Color submenu. This is the only cue that survives selection: JBDefaultTabPainter.getCustomBackground does not blend a custom tab colour when the tab is selected, it discards it and substitutes a theme colour.
  • Auto-assigned colours are now derived from the tab, meaning its title and working directory, rather than handed out as "the first palette entry no other tab is using". A tab therefore keeps its colour across restarts and across machines, instead of being reshuffled every time a project reopened, which taught you to stop reading the colours. Distinctness still wins on a collision: the derivation only chooses where to start looking.

Polish

  • The tab menu is grouped into Color, Icon and Emoji submenus. Flat, it had grown to 38 items and five separators, around 950px, which scrolls on a 1080p display. Grouping also disambiguates the two Custom… entries, which read identically side by side, and means the platform only has to update the handful of items actually on screen.
  • Emoji rows are [glyph] Name. Passing the emoji as both the row's icon and its text drew it twice side by side, which reads as a rendering fault; the name also makes the menu searchable by word rather than by pictogram.
  • The custom-emoji popup opens on the next EDT pass rather than synchronously. Opened immediately, it was created while the context menu was still dismissing, so the mouse event that closed the menu landed outside the new popup and setCancelOnClickOutside closed it again at once. The symptom was a popup that never appeared.
  • Tint strength moved under the switch that gates it, follows its enabled state, and shows its value as you drag. A live slider for a feature that is switched off is a dead control.
  • New plugin logo: three differently coloured tabs rather than one highlighted tab, since telling several terminals apart is the point.
  • Asking for a tab's identity no longer performs a reflective terminal lookup and a shell working-directory query when the answer is already pinned, which it is for any tab styled by hand. It was being asked once per menu item.
  • Colours and icons in the rule editor and in the rules list are shown, not just named. Each dropdown row carries the colour or icon it stands for, and the rules list carries the rule's own colour, matching the tab menu, which had been the only place a colour was actually drawn. Custom… shows its swatch button only while it is selected: a greyed-out swatch sitting beside a dropdown that reads Teal is simply wrong.

Hardened

  • An icon set by another plugin is never destroyed. PhpStorm 2026.2's "AI Agents" terminal feature marks the tabs it launches with an agent logo using exactly the two calls this plugin uses, putUserData(SHOW_CONTENT_ICON, true) and content.icon = …. Since every terminal tab is restyled whether or not it has a style, clearing unconditionally would wipe that logo the moment a tab was touched. Only icons this plugin set are cleared, and whatever was there beforehand is restored when a style is removed. The colour dot goes further and yields entirely: it is only this plugin's stand-in for the tab colour, so it never replaces a real icon, while an emoji or an icon chosen by hand still does. Ownership is checked against the icon actually on the tab, because the IDE brands an agent tab moments after creating it, which is after the first restyle.
  • A tab's text colour survives switching tabs. ContentTabLabel.update reassigns both of BaseLabel's foreground fields from the theme, and the platform calls it for every tab whenever the selection changes, so a colour set by hand was gone on the next click. The colour is now put back while the label paints, which is the last point it can be restored without a second repaint, so there is no flicker.
  • The tab fill resolves lazily, so it follows a theme switch instead of freezing at whatever theme was in force when the tab was styled. It is memoised on the theme values it derives from, because JBColor calls its supplier on every channel read.
  • A style is no longer written to a torn-down tab. The colour picker commits continuously while it is open, and once a session is gone the tab's identity falls back to a weak label-based key, so the write would have landed under a key shared with every other unresolved tab.
  • Colour-picker commits are coalesced. Each one restyles every known tab, and the platform fires its colour listener on every mouse-move.
  • A rule this build cannot parse now returns to the position it held rather than the end of the list. Rules are first-match-wins, so appending changed which style a tab got.
  • Emoji are normalised on the way in, so what is stored is the single grapheme that is actually drawn rather than an arbitrarily long pasted string.
  • XML non-characters are escaped alongside surrogates and control characters; a shell-supplied title containing one could previously stop the whole settings file from being written.
  • Menu labels built from user input no longer have _ or & eaten as mnemonic markers.

Notes

  • Works in every IntelliJ-based IDE that bundles the Terminal, on platform branch 253 (2025.3) or newer, with both the reworked and the classic terminal engine. Verified against IntelliJ IDEA, PhpStorm (2025.3 and 2026.2), WebStorm and PyCharm.
  • Rules live in .idea/terminalTabStyle.xml so they can be shared. Per-tab styles live in workspace.xml, because their identifiers are derived from working directories and shell-reported titles and so contain absolute paths and hostnames that do not belong in a committed .idea/ file.
  • Split terminals share one tab colour: a split is several sessions inside a single tab, and tab colour is a property of the tab.

idea-plugin.name: Secret Scanner for Git
idea-plugin.description:
Finds API keys, tokens and passwords in your code and in your Git™ history. Deleting a key in a later commit does not remove it: every clone of the repository still has the commit that added it. This plugin reads past commits, not only the files you have open, and tells you which commit, file and author added each secret.

The scan runs on your machine, and there is no account to create with us and no API key to enter. The plugin itself makes no network connections, and in a partial clone the history scan asks git not to download missing history from your remote. Git follows this request from version 2.45 (and in the April 2024 security releases of 2.39 to 2.44); older Git versions ignore it and may download the missing history themselves. If an error occurs inside the plugin, the IDE may offer to send an error report to JetBrains Marketplace (or sends it automatically if you turned on automatic error reporting in the IDE). For the failures the plugin detects itself, the error text is removed first, so that such a report holds the kind of error and where in the plugin's code it happened, not file contents, file names or secrets.

Scan the Git history
Run Tools | Scan Git History for Secrets. The plugin reads the added lines of the 2,000 most recent Git commits across all branches, in the background with a progress indicator, so the IDE stays usable. If the repository has more commits than that, the result says so instead of reporting that everything is clean. The same applies when git stops with an error, for example in a damaged repository or in a partial clone whose older history is not on your computer. Each secret is reported once per file, together with the earliest scanned commit, date and author that added it.

An audit report you can share
Findings are written to secret-scan-report.csv in the project folder: commit, date, author, file, type, masked value, severity and what to do about it. Keys are masked so that only their first and last four characters remain, and passwords in connection strings and URLs are hidden completely, so the report itself does not leak the secret. Delete the file or add it to .gitignore once you have reviewed it. If the file cannot be written (for example, it is open in a spreadsheet program), the notification gives the number of findings and says that the report was not saved.

Highlights secrets as you type
An inspection marks hardcoded secrets in the editor in any file type, with one line of advice for each (for example, where to revoke a GitHub token). It skips files over 1 MB and the .git, node_modules, build, out, .gradle, .idea, dist and vendor folders of your project.

What it recognizes

  • AWS access key IDs, and AWS secret access keys on lines that label them as AWS secrets
  • GitHub classic and fine-grained tokens, GitLab personal access tokens
  • OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Hugging Face API keys
  • Stripe secret and restricted keys, SendGrid keys, Twilio Account SIDs
  • Slack tokens and incoming webhooks
  • npm and PyPI tokens
  • Private key blocks (PKCS#8, RSA, EC, DSA, OpenSSH) and JSON Web Tokens
  • Passwords inside database connection strings and URLs
  • In the editor only: long, random-looking values assigned to a variable whose name contains api_key, token, secret, password or credential, for keys whose format is not published

Fewer false alarms
Obvious placeholders such as EXAMPLE, dummy, xxxx, your-key-here, REPLACE_ME or <TOKEN> are ignored, and so are references to environment variables such as ${DB_PASSWORD}, documentation-style connection strings such as postgres://USER:PASSWORD@HOST, default local credentials such as postgres:postgres@localhost, and private key blocks whose body is a placeholder. A real password is still reported even when the connection points at localhost. To silence a line on purpose, add a secretscan:ignore comment to it.

Limits
Lines longer than 2,000 characters (for example, minified files) are not read. The history scan stops after 500 findings and says so.

Requirements
The history scan uses the git command installed on your machine. The editor inspection works without it. Compatible with IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, PhpStorm, GoLand, RubyMine, CLion and Android Studio, build 252 and later.

If it finds something
Revoke the key with its provider first. Removing it from history does not help once it has been pushed, because anyone who cloned the repository already has it.

Every feature is available during the free trial — nothing is held back for the paid version. Run it on the repository you actually work in, and decide then.

An annual subscription includes a perpetual fallback license, so you keep a working version even if you stop subscribing.

Git is a trademark of Software Freedom Conservancy. This plugin is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Git project.

Documentation: gramshift.com/plugins · Issues: github.com/gramshiftofficial/jetbrains-plugins · Support: gramshift.official@gmail.com
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed: when git stopped with an error partway through the history (for example, in a damaged repository), the scan reported "No secrets found" for the commits it had read. It now says that older commits were not checked.

Fixed: when secret-scan-report.csv was open in another program or read-only, the scan ended with an IDE error and no result was shown. The notification now gives the number of findings and says that the report could not be saved.

Fixed: a secret on the last line of a file that does not end with a line break was underlined in the wrong place.

In a partial clone, the history scan now asks git not to download missing history from your remote (Git 2.45 or later, or a 2024 security release of 2.39 to 2.44); the result says the scan is incomplete instead.

Findings from the commits read before a scan is canceled are now saved to the report.

Errors inside the plugin can now be sent to the developer through the IDE's error reporting.

idea-plugin.name: SmsMurilo Resilience
idea-plugin.description:
SmsMurilo Resilience

Assistant for configuring, analyzing, and testing resilience in Spring Boot projects that use the smsmurilo-resilience-spring-boot-starter library.

Resilience Assistant

  • Analyzes the open project (Java and Kotlin, via PSI/UAST) and lists HTTP and messaging integrations without changing files.
  • Visual diagram editor to compose timeout, retry, circuit breaker, bulkhead, rate limit and fallback, with an explicit execution order separated from success, failure, timeout and recovery paths.
  • Validation that blocks unsafe policies, such as retry on operations with side effects and unknown idempotency.
  • Local, deterministic failure simulation (virtual clock, no network calls).
  • Reviewable and reversible changes: full diff of every file before applying, IDE Undo and "Undo application", divergence detection after manual edits.
  • Guidance, problems, sanitized logs and simulation timeline in a bottom panel; keyboard alternatives and screen-reader names.

Project analysis and monitoring

  • Detects the SmsMurilo Resilience library, application.properties settings and external calls, with recommendations.
  • Optional probing of a production health endpoint with observed latency, availability and error rate.

Available in English and Brazilian Portuguese, following the IDE language.

Free edition: this version does not require a commercial license or activation key.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.2.5

  • Removed the only deprecated API usage reported by the Plugin Verifier on IntelliJ IDEA 2025.1 and later: exports (JSON, SVG, PNG, logs) now ask for the destination folder, save with the default file name and confirm before overwriting an existing file.

2026.2.4

New: Resilience Assistant (Tools > Prepare Project Resilience)

  • PSI/UAST analysis of RestTemplate, RestClient, java.net.http, OkHttp, WebClient, Kafka and RabbitMQ usages (Java and Kotlin), classified as detected, inferred or confirmed by the user.
  • Diagram editor: palette, typed ports, connection and reconnection with compatibility feedback, routes, multi-selection, align/distribute/group, zoom, minimap, automatic layout, integration map, drawing undo/redo and keyboard alternatives.
  • Semantic validation with severity, cause, affected object and suggested fix.
  • Deterministic simulation: immediate success, transient failure, persistent timeout, permanent failure, open circuit and recovery, concurrency saturation, fallback, unknown outcome after timeout, DLQ and reprocessing (synthetic messages).
  • Generation for the SmsMurilo starter: @Resilient on the method, a managed block in application.properties, the starter dependency (Gradle or Maven) and a JUnit test. Every file diff is reviewed before applying; changes can be undone; reapplying does not duplicate configuration.
  • Model saved to smsmurilo-resilience.json; export to JSON, SVG and PNG with legend.

Fixes

  • Tools menu actions now show their translated names instead of raw message keys.

Compatibility verified with IntelliJ IDEA Community 2024.1–2025.2 and Ultimate 2024.1–2026.2. The Java plugin is an optional dependency: without it the analysis is unavailable and the rest keeps working.

2026.2.3

  • Message bundle migrated to the supported DynamicBundle(Class, String) API.

2026.2.2

  • Package rebuilt and signed after compatibility fixes.

2026.2.1

  • Compatibility fixes for the IntelliJ Plugin Verifier.
  • Monitoring validation messages internationalized; English documentation added.

2026.2.0

  • SmsMurilo Resilience tool window and project analysis (Spring Boot, starter, properties, external calls).
  • Optional production endpoint monitoring (latency, availability, error rate, P95).
  • Free edition with Brazilian Portuguese translation and English fallback.

idea-plugin.name: sMiv - Modal Editing
idea-plugin.description:
sMiv is modal editing for PhpStorm, based on MIV for VS Code: in NAV typed characters are commands, in INSERT you type as usual.

Getting started

  • Esc – NAV: typed characters are commands and are never inserted
  • i – INSERT after the character under the caret
  • Space – INSERT before the character under the caret
  • Status bar – shows sMiv NAV, sMiv INSERT or sMiv SELECT and the keys typed so far
  • Other keys – Enter, Tab, Backspace, arrow keys and all shortcuts work as usual in NAV

Everyday keys

  • w a s d – up, left, down, right
  • W S – page up, page down
  • A D – start, end of the line
  • q e – start of the previous word, end of the next word
  • Q E – end of the previous word, start of the next word
  • x – delete the character under the caret
  • b – delete the line
  • y – yank (copy) the line
  • p P – paste before, after the caret (a yanked line: above, below)
  • u – undo; the caret and the view stay put
  • o O – new line below, above, then INSERT

Counts and more commands

  • 5s 3x 2b 4y – a number first repeats the key or takes that many
  • g 12g – line 1, line 12, in the same column
  • G 3G – end of the document, the 3rd line from the bottom
  • m > – middle of the document; 3m 30 %, 25m 25 %
  • < – middle of the text on the line; 3< 30 %, 25< 25 %
  • - _ – first, last line inside the surrounding (), [] or {}; 3- 30 % from the top, 3_ from the bottom
  • % – matching bracket or quote, or the closing one around the caret
  • I k – start, end of the line, then INSERT
  • c – change to the end of the line; 2c also the next line
  • C – change from the start of the line, keeping the indentation
  • r + character – replace the character under the caret
  • R – change the word
  • X – delete the word
  • B – delete to the end of the line
  • Y – yank the word
  • § ° – toggle the case of the character, the word
  • & – join with the next line
  • J K – move the line down, up
  • L H – indent, outdent
  • . – repeat the last edit, search or replace
  • U – revert to the saved version in one step; u brings the changes back

Registers

  • 0–9 – registers: 0 last yank, 8 last delete, 9 the system clipboard
  • 3p 3P – paste register 3 before, after the caret
  • 2 y 5 2y – yank 1, 5 lines into register 2
  • 3 x 5 3x – delete 1, 5 characters into register 3
  • V – register viewer: type a digit or pick a row to paste it, Esc closes
  • 2V – store the clipboard in register 2
  • Named register – never touches the clipboard; a plain yank goes to register 0 and the clipboard
  • Yank – the yanked text flashes briefly

Selection

  • v – selection mode on, off; moves, arrow keys and searches extend the selection
  • x y c C § ° p P – act on the selection, also one made with the mouse or Shift; p P replace it
  • ( [ { " ' ` ´ – in selection mode: wrap the selection, for example (foo)
  • =new ==new – in selection mode: replace only inside the selection

Search and replace

  • /text Enter – search forward
  • \text Enter – search backward
  • ,regex Enter – regex search, shown as ~
  • n N – next, previous match; 3n three on; wraps around at the ends
  • f F – search the character under the caret forward, backward
  • * # – search the word under the caret forward, backward
  • Smart case – lower case finds both cases, a capital makes the search exact; f F * # are always exact
  • =new Enter – step through the matches of the last search: Enter or . replaces, n N skip
  • ==new Enter – replace all matches at once
  • =old new ==old new – the same for the literal text old; 'a b' quotes spaces
  • = == Enter – replace the current match, all matches, with the current rule
  • $1 $& $<name> – groups in the replacement after a regex search
  • Backspace Esc – edit, cancel the command line; Esc also hides the matches

Text objects

  • ! " ' ` ´ ( [ { – the nearest pair around the caret; ! takes any pair, also < >
  • "y – yank the contents into register 0 and the clipboard
  • "x – delete the contents into register 8
  • "c – delete the contents into register 8, then INSERT
  • "p – replace the contents with the clipboard
  • "Y "X – yank, delete including the delimiters
  • " 3y ( 3x { 3p [ 3c – use only register 3; not with !

Anchors, navigation and menu

  • Z Alt+Z – set the anchor
  • z Alt+X – jump to the anchor and back again, also across files
  • 3Z 3z – numbered anchors 0–9
  • Alt+Q Alt+E – previous, next paragraph
  • Alt+A Alt+D – navigate back, forward
  • Ctrl+F – the find bar
  • Status bar click – menu: Registers, Command Stats, Toggle Search Highlight, Change Keybindings, Open KEYMAP

Settings

  • Settings → Tools → sMiv – give any NAV key another character; digits and Space are fixed; Restore Defaults
  • Settings → Keymap → sMiv – change the Alt shortcuts and Ctrl+F

Good to know

  • IdeaVim – do not use it at the same time; sMiv warns and can turn itself off for the session
  • Enable, disable – PhpStorm needs a restart
  • Carets – NAV commands only use the primary caret
  • Editors – sMiv works in code editors, not in consoles, commit messages or dialogs
  • One mode – NAV and INSERT apply to all editors at once

idea-plugin.name: Vertical Tabs
idea-plugin.description:
Vertical Tabs

Vertical Tabs is an open-files navigator for JetBrains IDEs. It docks on the left side of the IDE,
groups files by their owning IDE module or .NET project, and gives each group a consistent color. It can replace the IDE's
native editor tab bar while preserving normal editor behavior.

Features

  • Vertical Tabs tool window docked on the left side of the IDE.
  • Visual Studio-style grouping by the nearest .csproj, .fsproj, or .vbproj file.
  • Generic module and content-root grouping in IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, CLion, RubyMine, PhpStorm, and other IntelliJ Platform IDEs.
  • Files outside an MSBuild project are placed in their .sln or .slnx solution group.
  • Custom glob rules such as *.cs or */Tests/*.cs; separate multiple patterns with ;.
  • One stable color for every group or project, independent of file extension.
  • Configurable single-click or double-click file activation.
  • Alphabetical, recently used, recently opened, or oldest-opened file ordering.
  • Alphabetical, recently used, or custom-rule-priority group ordering.
  • Configurable file icons, extensions, close buttons, and full-path tooltips.
  • Rules can be added, removed, edited, and reordered to control their priority.
  • Close files with the × button, middle mouse button, or context menu.
  • Context-menu commands for closing one file, other files, an entire group, or all files.
  • Native editor tabs can be hidden automatically and restored from the plugin settings.
  • Settings are stored separately for each solution in .idea/solutionTabs.xml.
  • Minimum supported IntelliJ Platform version: build 261. No upper build limit is declared.

idea-plugin.name: Atlassian Teamwork Graph CLI
idea-plugin.description:
Teamwork Graph CLI is Atlassian's agent-first interface to your entire work context: Jira issues, Confluence pages, Bitbucket pull requests, and connected third-party data.

Use it from your terminal or coding agent to:

  • Search connected work and find the most relevant context.
  • Map ownership, experts, dependencies, and related work.
  • Summarize status, triage reviews, prepare handoffs, and update work.

Try: "What PRs are waiting on me, and which reviews are stale?"

Run TWG: Set Up from Find Action or the Tools menu. The plugin opens a visible, interactive terminal and starts the official installer after you confirm. Teamwork Graph CLI owns installation, browser sign-in, credential storage, skills, and health checks.

Teamwork Graph CLI documentation
idea-plugin.change-notes: • Added fresh-install onboarding with a direct Teamwork Graph CLI setup action.

idea-plugin.name: Architect
idea-plugin.description:
Architect is an all-in-one code and infrastructure generation tool for IntelliJ IDEA designed to quickly bootstrap Spring Boot applications and eliminate repetitive setup work.

🚀 Key Features

  • Spring Boot Code Generator: Instantly generates Entities, DTOs, MapStruct mappers, Services, Repositories, and REST Controllers.
  • Liquibase Migration Generator: Generates ready-to-use Liquibase changelogs for your database structure.
  • Docker & Infrastructure Automation: Generates Docker configuration for Spring Boot projects, including PostgreSQL and other infrastructure components.
  • Maven Dependency Management: Automatically adds and configures the dependencies required by generated components.
  • PSI-Powered Generation: Uses IntelliJ IDEA's Program Structure Interface (PSI) to work directly with your project's structure and source files.

💡 Built for Engineers

Architect is built for Java and Spring Boot developers who want to spend less time creating boilerplate and project infrastructure, and more time building application logic.

idea-plugin.name: RepoLeap
idea-plugin.description:
Leap to any local Git repository in a few keystrokes: one shortcut, fuzzy search across all your repos, done.

Option+Command+I (macOS) or Alt+Shift+P (Windows/Linux) opens a search popup with every Git repository in the folders you configured. Type a few letters of the name or path, press Enter – and you are in the project.

Main features

  • One popup for all your repositories – any number of root folders, searched recursively (worktrees included) with a configurable depth and ignored folder names
  • Free-text search – several words in any order, matched against names and paths, fuzzy on names, with highlighted matches
  • Always the right order – pinned repositories first, then the one in the current window, then those open in other windows, then the rest; the best matches and recently opened repositories lead within each group
  • Jump instead of reopening – open repositories are marked (current window, other window) and choosing one brings exactly that window to the front
  • macOS window tabs – bring a repository that is open in another window into the current window as a tab (Shift+Enter)
  • Open the way you like – new window, current window or the IDE setting; Shift+Enter uses the alternative

More features

Press Tab (or right-click) on a repository for its actions:

  • Info – branch, upstream with ahead/behind, last commit, remotes, uncommitted and untracked files, commits that are not pushed anywhere, stashes
  • Open the remote in the browser – GitHub, GitLab, Gitea/Forgejo, Bitbucket Cloud, Bitbucket Server / Data Center, Azure DevOps, AWS CodeCommit, SourceHut, or your own rules
  • Close the project, show the folder in the system file manager, copy the path
  • Pin favorites to the top, hide repositories you never need
  • Rename the folder or move it to the Trash – with a warning about everything that would otherwise be lost (uncommitted changes, unpushed commits, stashes, no remote)

Scanning runs in the background, so the popup opens instantly.

Getting started

  1. Open Settings | Tools | RepoLeap and add the folders that contain your repositories.
  2. Press the shortcut, or use File | Open Repository….

The shortcut can be changed in Settings | Keymap (search for “Open Repository”).

Privacy

RepoLeap does not collect or transmit any data. Only if the type of a self-hosted git server can not be told from the remote URL, it asks that git server once whether it is a Bitbucket Server (can be switched off in the settings).

Feedback

Found a bug or have an idea? Open an issue on GitHub.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Search popup for local Git repositories: Option+Command+I (macOS) / Alt+Shift+P (Windows/Linux), also available via File | Open Repository… and the Welcome screen
  • Settings page (Settings | Tools | RepoLeap): any number of root folders, search depth, ignored folder names, skipping of hidden folders
  • Free-text search with multiple words in any order, fuzzy matching on repository names and highlighted matches
  • Fixed order: pinned repositories, current window, other windows, rest - inside each group best match and recently opened first
  • Open repositories are marked with colored tags (green: current window, blue: other window); choosing one of them brings its window (or macOS window tab) to the front instead of opening it again
  • Open mode: new window, current window or IDE setting; Shift+Enter uses the alternative
  • macOS window tabs: bring a repository from another window into the current window as a tab (Shift+Enter or Merge into This Window); the actions only offer what fits the state of the repository
  • Open Remote in Browser shows the complete web page it will open
  • Actions per repository via Tab or right click: close project, info dialog with git and working tree state, show in the system file manager, copy path, open remote in browser, pin to top, hide (restorable in the settings), rename and move to Trash with a warning about uncommitted changes, untracked files, unpushed commits and stashes
  • Web pages of remotes for GitHub, GitLab, Gitea/Forgejo, Bitbucket Cloud, Bitbucket Server / Data Center, Azure DevOps, AWS CodeCommit and SourceHut; self-hosted Bitbucket Servers with a neutral host name are recognized by asking the server once (can be switched off), custom rules per host in the settings

idea-plugin.name: DiffSense Semantic Compare
idea-plugin.description:
Compare files. Understand what changed.

DiffSense adds a semantic layer on top of the IDE's own diff viewer. Instead of only showing which lines changed, it tells you what changed and whether it matters.

  • JSON, YAML and XML are compared by structure: reordered keys and reformatting are not changes, and every changed value is listed with its path.
  • API responses: compare an expected response with an actual one (raw HTTP, JSON envelope or bare body) and get a pass/fail verdict with every check listed.
  • Impact estimates (informational to critical) with the reason for each one.
  • Ignore rules for paths, order, case and whitespace, in Settings or a project .diffsense.json.
  • EDIFACT files are compared segment by segment (NAD[BY], LOC[7].2.1), whether they arrive on one line or many.
  • Format File re-indents JSON and XML and splits EDIFACT into one segment per line, without changing any value.
  • Copy or export the summary as Markdown.

Right-click one or two files in the Project view and choose DiffSense | Compare with DiffSense, or use the DiffSense actions in the Tools menu.

Fully local: no network access, no account, no telemetry. Your files never leave your machine.

Java semantic analysis and the test-automation rules from the VS Code extension are planned for a later release.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.2.0 EDIFACT comparison, Format File (JSON, XML, EDIFACT), fix for a deprecated API usage reported for IntelliJ IDEA 2026.3.
0.1.0 First release: text, JSON, YAML, XML and API response comparison, impact estimates, Markdown export.

idea-plugin.name: Invisible Notes
idea-plugin.description:
Private notes on lines of code that are never written into your files.

Invisible Notes shows your notes in the editor, between the lines of code, while the file itself stays untouched: there is nothing to commit and nothing for version control to pick up. Use them to record what you worked out while reading unfamiliar code, to leave yourself reminders, or to keep questions for later.

Features

  • Notes in the editor. Right-click a line and choose Add Invisible Note, or press Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Z (⌘⌥⇧Z on macOS). Enter saves, Shift+Enter starts a new line, Esc cancels. Double-click a note to edit it.
  • Notes follow the code. A note stays with its line when you edit, reformat, pull changes or switch branches, and when files are renamed or moved. If the code it belonged to is gone, the note is kept and marked as orphaned, not deleted.
  • Notes wait for their file. Notes on a file that doesn't exist on the current branch come back when the file does.
  • See where the notes are. Each note has a mark next to the scrollbar, and the editor's top-right corner shows how many notes the file has. Click the count to list them.
  • All notes in one place. The Invisible Notes tool window lists the notes of the current file or of the whole project. Click a note to jump to it, or edit and delete notes from there.
  • Delete them all at once. Delete every note of a file, or of the whole project, in one step, from the tool window or the editor's right-click menu. You're asked first.
  • Undo. Deleted a note by mistake? Undo brings it back, also after deleting them all.
  • Notes for AI tools. An AI tool connected to the IDE's MCP server can list, add, change and delete notes. Ask it to explain or review code, and its remarks appear as notes next to the code, not as changes to your files.
  • Stored on your computer. Notes are kept locally, outside the project, and the plugin doesn't send them anywhere. Clearing the IDE caches doesn't remove them, and they stay with a project whose folder you move or rename.

If you use AI tools with your notes: an AI tool connected to the IDE's MCP server can read, add, change and delete all notes of the projects you open, and what it reads is sent to the AI service behind it. For AI tools outside the IDE, that server is off unless you turn it on (Settings | Tools | MCP Server). AI agents built into the IDE may be given the same tools without that setting.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.4.0

  • Delete all notes of a file, or of the whole project, in one step: a button in the Invisible Notes tool window, Delete All Invisible Notes in File in the editor's right-click menu, and Delete All Invisible Notes in Project in Find Action. You're asked first, and Undo brings the notes back.
  • Notes stay with a project whose folder is moved or renamed.
  • AI tools connected to the IDE's MCP server can list, add, change and delete notes, to explain or review code with notes. They get access to all notes of the open projects.

This version needs IDE version 2025.2 or newer. For 2025.1, version 1.0.0 remains available.

1.0.0

First release.

idea-plugin.name: ArkUIBuilder Tool
idea-plugin.description:
Browse ready-made ArkUI widgets from the ArkUIBuilder catalog and insert their ArkTS code into the current editor in DevEco Studio or any IntelliJ-based IDE.

idea-plugin.name: epher
idea-plugin.description:
A calculator language with the answers inline: write ordinary math, with units that convert, and every statement's answer appears next to the line that produced it, right in your JetBrains IDE.

Type a formula and the answer is already there. No REPL in a side panel, no print statements: the editor is the calculator.

What you get

  • Answers inline: each statement's result renders next to its line: x = 40 + 2 shows = 42.
  • Units that convert: 6371 km, 55 mile/hr, 30 deg are quantities, not comments. speed in km/hr converts; the answer carries the right unit.
  • Live diagnostics: syntax errors point at the exact token, and evaluation errors carry the same message the epher calculator shows.
  • Hover signatures: hover any name for its canonical signature; your own functions show their definitions, catalog functions show their docs.
  • Completion: the whole catalog (math, astronomy, statistics), your own definitions, keywords, and snippets for the common statement shapes.
  • Run the script: Run Epher Script in the Tools menu (or the gutter play icon) evaluates the whole file; the transcript with every 2D or 3D graph opens in the epher results tool window.

First use

The plugin downloads the shared epher-lsp binary for your platform on first use (a few megabytes) and caches it; after that everything is local. All understanding lives in the language server, so every IDE behaves identically.

Requirements

A commercial JetBrains IDE, 2024.2 or newer: IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate, PyCharm Professional, WebStorm, PhpStorm, RubyMine, CLion, DataGrip, GoLand, Rider, Aqua, or RustRover. The platform's built-in LSP client ships only in the commercial IDEs, so IntelliJ IDEA Community and Android Studio cannot load this plugin.

epher.org has the full documentation, the standalone calculator, and a library of ready-made scripts.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Answers inline, units that convert, live diagnostics, hover signatures, completion, and the results pane with 2D and 3D graphs. See the release notes for what each version brings.

idea-plugin.name: Rally Work Items
idea-plugin.description:
Browse, update, and export Rally work items in the IDE. A dedicated tool window lists your User Stories, Defects, and Test Cases from Rally (Broadcom Agile Central), shows their details, and lets you create tickets, change their state, and start a Git branch for one.

Features

  • Ticket list: search by ID or name, filter by scope (All Tickets, My Tickets, User Stories, Defects, Test Cases, Recent Activity), state, project, and sprint.
  • Detail panel: HTML description with inline images, plus tabs for linked Test Cases, Tasks, and Attachments. Double-click a test case to see its steps.
  • Create: User Stories and Defects (with project, sprint, severity, priority, and an optional attachment), and Tasks under a story or defect.
  • Update: move tickets to Defined, In-Progress, or Completed (multi-select supported) and edit story points.
  • Start Working: create and check out a Git branch for the ticket, move it to In-Progress and assign it to you.
  • Export: save tickets and their linked test cases to JSON and Markdown, including attachments and inline images.
  • Sprint summary: ticket counts, story points, planned velocity, and days remaining.
  • Open any ticket in the Rally web UI or copy its ID.

Setup

  1. Open Settings | Tools | Rally.
  2. Enter your Rally server URL (for example, https://rally1.rallydev.com).
  3. Enter your Rally API key (Rally: your profile | API Keys). It is stored in the IDE's password safe.
  4. Enter your workspace and username, then click Test Connection.
  5. Open the Rally tool window.

Report an issue · Source code

This is an independent, community-built plugin. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Broadcom Inc. Rally and Agile Central are trademarks of Broadcom Inc.

idea-plugin.name: Prismio
idea-plugin.description:
Support for the Prismio programming language: .psm source files and build.ums project files.

Writing code

  • Syntax highlighting, with separate colours for types, functions, fields and variables
  • Completion that knows the type in front of the dot. Type name. and you get the methods of a String
  • Imports are added for you. Pick println from the list and import std.io appears at the top
  • Errors from the compiler as you type, with a quick fix to add a missing import
  • Parameter hints while you fill in a call, and the type of a let shown inline
  • Formatting, folding, comment toggling, brace matching and live templates

Finding your way

  • Go to declaration, including from an import to the file it names
  • Find usages and rename
  • Structure view and Go to Symbol
  • Documentation from your /// and /** */ comments, rendered in the editor (turned on once, under Settings | Editor | General | Appearance)

Starting a project

  • New Project | Prismio: pick the compiler (auto-detected, with its version shown), optionally create a Git repository, and get a build.ums and a main program
  • New | UMS Manifest adds a build.ums to a folder

Running

  • Your build.ums fills the run menu: one entry per executable, plus Build, Test and every command you declare
  • Run buttons in the gutter next to fn main and next to each target and command in build.ums
  • Compiler errors in the output link back to the line, and program output keeps its colours

build.ums

  • Highlighting, completion and formatting
  • Warnings for names the build system does not know, and errors for values it will reject
  • Structure view of blocks, targets and commands

Getting started

Install the Prismio toolchain. The plugin looks for prismio on your PATH; to use a different compiler, set it in Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Prismio. Completion and error checking follow the version of the compiler you pick.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.0

First release.

  • Highlighting, formatting and folding for .psm and build.ums
  • Type-aware completion with automatic imports
  • Compiler errors as you type, with import quick fixes
  • Go to declaration, find usages and rename
  • Parameter hints and inline type hints
  • Run configurations created from build.ums, with coloured output
  • New Project wizard and New | UMS Manifest

idea-plugin.name: Duplicate Image Finder
idea-plugin.description:
Find identical and similar static PNG, JPEG, and WebP images in Android and Compose Multiplatform resource directories.

idea-plugin.name: Selvage
idea-plugin.description:
Edit the same project together, live, each from your own IDE. Host a session from the project you have open and send the invite link it gives you; the other person joins from that link.

  • Type into the same files at the same time, with each other's carets and selections in the editor.
  • See who is in the session and which file they are in, and go to or follow any of them.
  • Encrypted end to end. The key travels in the invite link and never reaches the server, so the server cannot read the files, the edits, the carets or the list of shared files.
  • Host on the public demo server, or run your own selvaged.
  • Works with the Selvage clients for VS Code, Neovim and the browser.

A guest gets a copy of the shared files in a new project window, opened in safe mode because the code comes from someone else, and the copy is removed when the session ends. A host never shares dependency or build folders, secrets such as .env and private keys, or anything the folder's ignore files leave out.

Source code and documentation · Report an issue
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.4.0

  • Hosting shares every folder of the project, instead of only the folder the window was opened on.
  • With more than one folder shared, each path in the room carries the name of the folder it is in, and two folders of the same name are told apart by a number.
  • A folder inside another shared folder is shared once, by the outermost folder that holds it.

0.3.1

  • A peer's selection is drawn as soon as their document is open in this window, instead of at their next move.
  • A caret or selection made while the room is confirming your connection reaches the others as soon as it does, instead of a renewal window later.
  • A caret or selection made before a document's text has arrived reaches the others when it arrives, instead of at your next move.

0.3.0

  • An invite that names a room, a token or a key more than once is refused by name instead of silently joining the first one it names.
  • A full server is recognized from its code, so the server-is-full sentence no longer depends on the wording the server happens to use.
  • A reconnect no longer treats an unrecognized close as a final refusal, and a capacity close is retried.
  • Engine faults are written to the IDE log with their stack trace, and a guest's project that fails to open records why.

0.2.0

  • A guest's copy of the room opens as a project named "Selvage session" instead of a random id.
  • Following someone lands on their first move, including into a file you do not have open yet.
  • Joining a session no longer logs a write-unsafe context error in the IDE.
  • Plainer wording on the settings page, and the go-to refusals, the first download notice and the host's leave question say the same words as the VS Code client.

0.1.0, the first release.

  • Host a session from the open project, or join one from an invite link.
  • Shared editing with the other participants' carets, selections and project view badges.
  • Open or fetch a document from the room, list the people in it, and go to or follow one of them.
  • The same twelve commands as the VS Code client, under Tools | Selvage.

idea-plugin.name: Clean Terminal Copy
idea-plugin.description:
Copying text from the IDE terminal, e.g. replies of Claude Code or other CLI agents, brings along the layout of the terminal: a margin of spaces in front of every line and hard line breaks wherever the text wrapped at the terminal width.

This plugin cleans the clipboard right after you copy from the terminal (Ctrl+C or the context menu Copy). It
  • removes the margin shared by all lines, keeping relative indentation;
  • re-joins lines that were wrapped only because the terminal was too narrow, including wrapped list items;
  • drops trailing padding spaces and the agent's leading message bullet (●).
Nothing changes about Ctrl+C itself: with no selection it still interrupts.
