idea-plugin.name: Interface Exception Divergence Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags a call through an interface-typed reference, wrapped in a broad silent catch (Exception e), where real implementations of that interface method actually diverge on which RuntimeException they throw directly -- a Liskov Substitution violation the static interface type alone can't warn you about: the caller was written assuming ONE implementation's behavior (e.g. "PayPalGateway never throws this"), but dependency injection can hand it any real implementation at runtime.

Built on real Class Hierarchy Analysis (CHA) -- resolves EVERY concrete implementation of the interface in the project (the same mechanism a compiler/JIT uses to decide whether a virtual call can be devirtualized), the opposite of how every other mechanism in this catalog treats "more than one real implementation" (always discarded as ambiguity elsewhere -- here it's the precondition).

Stated honestly: v0.1 only RuntimeException subtypes thrown DIRECTLY in an implementation's own override body -- never follows a call to another method to infer transitive exceptions. No PMD/SonarQube/CodeQL rule found with this exact angle; no dedicated Marketplace plugin found.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: Mutable State Leak Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags a real mutation (`.add`/`.put`/`.remove`/`.clear`/an array-index write) of a value returned by a getter that hands back one of its OWN mutable fields (`List`/`Map`/`Set`/array) directly -- the real `EI_EXPOSE_REP` bug class (SpotBugs' own name for it), but PROVEN exploited here, not just a getter shaped in a risky way (CWE-374/375).

Built on real interprocedural alias tracking: the getter can live in a completely different class/file than the caller -- real PSI method resolution crosses that boundary naturally, no custom whole-project graph needed for this one-hop shape. SpotBugs' own heuristic only checks the getter's shape and never verifies a caller actually mutates the result -- this plugin requires BOTH.

Stated honestly: SpotBugs (bytecode, CI/build-step only, not an inline IDE inspection) is the real, confirmed prior art for the getter-shape half of this check. No dedicated Marketplace plugin found that also verifies real exploitation.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: Mismatched Lock Object Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags a synchronized block whose lock object is PROVEN to never be the same as another lock guarding the SAME field elsewhere in the class -- broken mutual exclusion that looks like real thread-safety but isn't. SEI CERT LCK06-J/ LCK00-J; FindBugs has related detectors for this class of bug (bytecode/CI only, not an inline IDE inspection).

Built on real alias analysis proving NON-identity (not identity, the opposite direction of this catalog's own Deadlock Lock-Order Companion): both lock fields are `final`, each initialized to its OWN separate `new` expression -- the strongest guarantee Java offers that two references are never the same object short of full points-to analysis.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only an unqualified lock reference (implicit `this`), and only a field's OWN direct initializer (`private final Object lockA = new Object();`) -- a constructor-assigned field is never treated as provably distinct, a real limitation rather than a guess. No dedicated Marketplace plugin found for this exact angle.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: Interprocedural Resource Leak Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags a resource (JDBC or I/O stream) delegated to a helper method that does NOT guarantee closing it on every path, where the caller never closes it either -- a real interprocedural resource leak (CWE-772), not the simple never-touched-at-all case the platform's own bundled inspection already covers.

Combines TWO techniques this catalog already proved separately: the real, from-scratch Tarjan's SCC algorithm and fixed-point summary computation from Log Injection Companion (interprocedural) with the branch-merging path-sensitive typestate engine from JDBC Double-Close Companion (path-sensitive) -- applied together for the first time in this catalog. A helper method's own "does it close this parameter on every path" summary is itself computed path-sensitively, then propagated across the whole project's call graph via the same SCC-ordered fixed point.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only `Connection`/`Statement`/`PreparedStatement`/ `CallableStatement`/`ResultSet`/`InputStream`/`OutputStream`/ `Reader`/`Writer`; only direct reference arguments (no wrapping expression); a project with more than 3,000 analyzable methods skips analysis entirely.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: Interface Sink Divergence Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags a call through an interface-typed reference, passing tainted HTTP input, where SOME real implementations log that input unsanitized (CWE-117/CWE-532) while at least one other real implementation never does -- the interface type alone never guarantees which behavior you get once dependency injection swaps implementations.

Combines TWO techniques this catalog already proved separately: the real Class Hierarchy Analysis from Interface Exception Divergence Companion (resolve EVERY concrete implementation, never discard for "ambiguity") with the taint-to-sink pattern from Log Injection Companion/the SpEL/ XPath/LDAP sink finders -- run INSIDE each real implementation's own body, not just at the call site.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only interfaces with 2-10 real implementations; taint only through a bare reference or one-hop concatenation, both at the call site and inside each implementation. No dedicated Marketplace plugin found for this exact angle.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:

idea-plugin.name: Interface Resource-Close Divergence Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags a call through an interface-typed reference, passing a resource (JDBC or I/O stream), where SOME real implementations guarantee closing it on every path (CWE-772) while at least one other real implementation never does -- the interface type alone never guarantees which behavior you get once dependency injection swaps implementations.

The TRIPLE combination this catalog's Tier -3 batch is built around: real Class Hierarchy Analysis (Interface Exception Divergence Companion's own resolution of EVERY real implementation) applied over whole-project summaries that are THEMSELVES the product of a real Tarjan-SCC interprocedural fixed point (Log Injection Companion's own technique) computed via a branch-merging path-sensitive engine (JDBC Double-Close Companion's own technique) -- three previously-separate analysis techniques combined in one mechanism for the first time in this catalog.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only interfaces with 2-10 real implementations; same resource types and taint scope as its two base mechanisms. No dedicated Marketplace plugin found for this exact angle.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: Try/Catch Consistency Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Learns the dominant checked-exception-handling convention YOUR OWN FILE already established for a given method -- not a rule this plugin knew in advance -- and flags a gutter warning on the call sites that break with it. If 8 or more calls to the same method in a file all catch the same checked exception (or all deliberately let it propagate uncaught), and one new call site disagrees, that is a real, concrete signal something was missed -- without the plugin needing to know anything about the method, the framework, or the exception type in advance.

A convention learned from your own code, not a pre-written rule -- this is fundamentally different from every other plugin in this catalog: instead of shipping a fixed pattern to detect, it builds a per-file statistical consensus (via real PSI: resolveMethod(), throws-list resolution, try/ catch ancestor walking) and flags the minority that contradicts the majority it just observed. No Marketplace plugin found doing this kind of self-referential, learned- from-the-codebase consistency check.

Stated honestly: v0.1 is bounded to the current file only (comparing against every call site in the whole project would require an unbounded-cost project-wide search on every background highlight pass) and to checked exceptions only (unchecked/RuntimeException handling is never required by the compiler, so "inconsistent" carries much weaker signal there). Requires at least 8 calls to the same method in one file before it says anything -- small files never trigger a false "convention".

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: Background ReadAction Freeze Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags a background-thread entry point (a `Task.Backgroundable` override, a method annotated `@RequiresBackgroundThread`, an `Application#executeOnPooledThread(...)` task, a task submitted to `AppExecutorUtil`'s pooled executor, or a task passed to `BackgroundTaskUtil#executeOnPooledThread(...)`) that can reach a blocking, non-cancellable read-lock call -- either directly, or transitively through a project method whose own summary already proves it. Java and Kotlin. Every sink is verified against the real `intellij-community` source, and each warning quotes the reason that applies to that exact API: `ReadAction.compute()`/ `run()` are deprecated; `ReadAction.computeBlocking()`/ `runBlocking()` and `runReadActionBlocking {}` are not deprecated, but their own documentation says "Avoid usage in background threads as it will likely cause UI freezes"; `DumbService#runReadActionInSmartMode(...)` runs a blocking read action after smart mode starts; `Application#runReadAction(...)` is not formally deprecated, but its own Javadoc says "Avoid using this method directly in applied/plugins code".

Motivated by JetBrains' own Platform Blog: "Investigating IntelliJ Platform UI Freezes" (Sept 2025) and "UI Freezes and the Dangers of Non-Cancellable Read Actions in Background Threads" (March 2026), which states that "many reports actually show problems in plugins that contain that single erroneous pattern" -- and that detection today is manual, post-mortem thread-dump analysis, not static prevention. This plugin is an attempt at the static side.

Interprocedural: reuses the same real, from-scratch Tarjan's SCC algorithm and whole-project fixed-point summary computation already proven in this catalog's Log Injection Companion and Interprocedural Resource Leak Companion, applied to a simpler reachability lattice.

Validated by hand against real code from `intellij-community` itself (`plugins/hg4idea`): confirmed a real EDT-reachable call correctly NOT flagged (no false positive), and found the `BackgroundTaskUtil#executeOnPooledThread` entry point missing from the original 3-entry list -- added rather than left as a documented gap.

The same rule, applied to IntelliJ's own source, found the blocking read actions reported as IDEA-393501 (`SearchForTestsTask`) and IJPL-257836 (`DependenciesUsagesPanel`).

Stated honestly: Java code is analyzed across the whole project; Kotlin code follows calls only into functions of the same file, matched by name (it works the same in K1 and K2 mode). Kotlin coroutine entry points are out of scope -- JetBrains' own DevKit already reports blocking calls in suspend contexts. `call.resolveMethod()` resolves a virtual Java call to a single candidate (no CHA, no points-to); a project with more than 3,000 analyzable Java methods skips the Java analysis; a hit where the same method also calls `checkCanceled()` is downgraded to a weaker warning, not suppressed -- the write lock can still block. `ReadAction.computeCancellable()` is not reported since 0.3.0: it gives way to a pending write action.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Kotlin support: a second inspection reports Kotlin code that runs on a background thread and reaches a blocking read action. It follows calls into functions of the same file and works the same in K1 and K2 mode.
  • New blocking calls, verified against the current IntelliJ Platform source: ReadAction.computeBlocking()/runBlocking(), runReadActionBlocking {}, the top-level runReadAction {} and DumbService#runReadActionInSmartMode(...).
  • New entry point: a method or function annotated @RequiresBackgroundThread.
  • Each warning names the exact blocking call and quotes the reason that applies to it. computeBlocking() and Application#runReadAction(...) are never described as deprecated, because they are not.
  • A description page for the inspection in Settings | Editor | Inspections, which showed "Under construction".

Fixed

  • ReadAction.computeCancellable() is no longer reported. It gives way to a pending write action (it throws CannotReadException), so it does not block the write lock. Earlier versions reported it by mistake.

Changed

  • The rating prompt's local counter keeps one-way fingerprints of findings instead of their file paths, and deletes the list that earlier versions kept.
  • PRIVACY.md describes the values the plugin keeps in the IDE's local settings.

idea-plugin.name: Dependency Vulnerability Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags dependencies in pom.xml, build.gradle/build.gradle.kts, package.json, and requirements.txt whose pinned version is a known-vulnerable one -- matched against a vulnerability database bundled inside the plugin, sourced from real OSV.dev records. No account, no token, no cloud dashboard: unlike every SCA plugin on this Marketplace that bundles this kind of check (Aikido, Xygeni, JFrog), this one makes zero network calls, ever -- verifiable in the source, works fully air-gapped.

A Dependency Graph tab next to the text editor shows the same findings visually -- click any dependency for its CVE details. Rendered with a bundled copy of Cytoscape.js, same zero-network architecture already proven in this vendor's mermaid-companion diagram preview. Maven/Gradle and pip nodes expand into their real dependencies on click -- local .m2 cache and pip show only, never a network call even though this is opt-in resolution.

Stated honestly: it ships a bundled snapshot of about 10,000 GitHub-reviewed high and critical advisories (Maven, npm and PyPI) taken at build time, not a live feed -- a newer advisory reaches you with the next plugin release. Advisory data: GitHub Advisory Database via OSV.dev, CC BY 4.0. Property- interpolated/version-catalog versions (Maven/Gradle) and non-pinned/lockfile-resolved versions (npm ranges, pip specifiers other than ==) are documented scope cuts for this version.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • The suggested upgrade matches the version you use. When an advisory has fixes on several release lines, the warning suggested the lowest fix of all of them: log4j-core 2.14.1 was told "Upgrade to 2.3.1 or later" for Log4Shell (a downgrade that is still vulnerable). It now suggests the fix on your own line, 2.15.0. The same applies to the Dependency Graph's node details.
  • A follow-up advisory was labelled with the CVE of the advisory it follows up on, so two different lodash warnings both read CVE-2021-23337. Each advisory now shows its own CVE (the _.template imports one is CVE-2026-4800).
  • Warning text: the summary ends with a period before "Upgrade to ...", and npm and PyPI packages are named without a stray leading colon (lodash 4.17.20, not :lodash 4.17.20).
  • The Dependency Graph tab uses the editor's colors instead of a white page (it glared in dark themes), and a graph with a few dependencies is no longer zoomed in to fill the whole tab. After switching the IDE theme, reopen the file to recolor an open graph.

Changed

  • Vulnerability snapshot refreshed: 10,099 records of 8,736 GitHub-reviewed high or critical advisories for 4,563 packages.

idea-plugin.name: OpenAPI Guard
idea-plugin.description:
Catch drift between your OpenAPI spec and your API implementation as you type.

OpenAPI Guard compares a local OpenAPI 3.x specification with your Spring MVC controllers in Java and Kotlin, your Express routes, and your AWS Lambda (API Gateway HTTP API) handlers in TypeScript or JavaScript. It flags operations nobody implemented, endpoints the spec does not document, and HTTP methods that disagree. It understands spec-first projects built with openapi-generator, including interface and delegate styles.

Free features

  • Drift inspections on both the implementation and the spec, with per-rule severity, @SuppressWarnings / @Suppress, and Code | Inspect Code.
  • Express and AWS Lambda: Express app/router routes and routers mounted across files; Lambda route maps and switch statements on event.routeKey, with alias maps and an openapi-guard.routes.json manifest for custom routers. Routes it cannot read are marked as analysis limitations instead of being reported as missing.
  • Quick fixes: add an undocumented endpoint to a YAML spec, implement a missing operation in the best-matching controller, or align the HTTP method on either side.
  • Operations tool window: every operation's status (implemented, missing, mismatched, undocumented), with search, a problems-only filter, and Copy as Markdown for pull requests and reviews.
  • Path completion from the spec inside @GetMapping, @RequestMapping, and the other mapping annotations.
  • Navigation both ways: gutter icons and Go to Declaration between mappings or routes and operations.
  • Finds specs by content, handles several per project, or uses the paths you configure.
  • Works in IntelliJ IDEA Community and Ultimate, 2024.1 and later. Supports OpenAPI 3.x; Swagger 2.0 is not supported.

Private by design. Analysis runs entirely on your machine. OpenAPI Guard never uploads source code, specifications, or diagnostics, and needs no account or network access.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.4.1

  • TypeScript build output (outDir/declarationDir of any tsconfig*.json) is no longer analyzed, as sources or as specs; imports of build output resolve to their sources.
  • Legacy route aliases are scoped by their target's module.
  • A routeKey only copied into an object (such as a log entry) is no longer treated as unrecognized dispatch.
  • The Operations tool window counts analysis limitations in its summary, with a Go to Analysis Limitation toolbar action.

0.4.0

  • Express support in TypeScript and JavaScript: app/router routes, route() chains, and routers mounted with use() across files, with Express 4 optional parameters and Express 5 optional groups.
  • AWS Lambda (API Gateway HTTP API) support: route maps and switch statements dispatched on event.routeKey, imported and spread route maps, alias maps, and openapi-guard.routes.json for custom routers.
  • In TypeScript and JavaScript files, drift is highlighted on the route's line and routes get gutter icons to their OpenAPI operations.
  • New OpenAPI Guard analysis limitation inspection: routes and mappings that cannot be analyzed are marked, and the operations they may implement show as Could not verify instead of missing. The Operations tool window opens the limitation behind each one.
  • Inspection names and messages no longer say "Spring"; suppression IDs are unchanged.
  • The vendor link points to stackblender.com.

0.3.0

  • Operations tool window: Copy as Markdown (toolbar) and Copy Selected as Markdown (row menu) export the coverage summary and the rows shown, for pull requests, issues, and reviews.
  • The Operations tool window refreshes as soon as OpenAPI Guard settings change.
  • The first-run summary waits for the Gradle/Maven import, so it no longer reports every operation as missing on a freshly opened project.
  • Path completion keeps unimplemented operations first when ML-assisted completion is on.
  • Plugin description rewritten.

0.2.0

  • Drift is reported by three inspections under Settings | Editor | Inspections | OpenAPI Guard, with suppression (@SuppressWarnings/@Suppress, springdoc @Hidden, x-openapi-guard-ignore) and Inspect Code support.
  • Quick fixes: add operation to spec, implement in controller (Java or Kotlin), change method.
  • OpenAPI Guard tool window: every operation's coverage status, searchable on any column.
  • Path completion from the spec in mapping annotations.
  • Specs found by content; multiple specs per project; explicit spec paths in settings.
  • First-run summary, and explanations for specs that cannot be analyzed.
  • Disabling OpenAPI Guard now also turns off its navigation.
  • Severity is now set per inspection; the old severity setting is removed.

0.1.2

  • Supports spec-first projects generated by openapi-generator: mappings on implemented interfaces, base classes, and interface defaults, including constant paths and the delegate pattern (Java and Kotlin).
  • Resolves ${...} placeholders in mapping paths from application.properties/yml, falling back to their defaults.
  • Aligns OpenAPI servers base paths with Spring's servlet context path.
  • No false "missing implementation" warnings where a mapping cannot be resolved (for example, before generated sources are built).
  • Faster: project analysis is cached and shared by diagnostics and navigation.

0.1.1

  • Brand-consistent plugin icon (matches the VS Code extension).

0.1.0

  • Initial release: endpoint-level OpenAPI ↔ Spring drift detection for Java and Kotlin.
  • Diagnostics for missing, undocumented, and method-mismatched endpoints.
  • Bidirectional gutter navigation between mappings and OpenAPI operations.

idea-plugin.name: ArchVerity
idea-plugin.description:
Detect Spring HTTP/Kafka contract drift. ArchVerity helps Java and Kotlin teams map service contracts, inspect both sides of a change, and review source evidence before release. Analysis is source-based; a running application is not required for the architecture workflow.

Use the Workspace as a connected path from system map to finding: locate a contract, review the change and its evidence, then save a same-scope baseline or share an export.

Choose a job

  • Map a system: trace supported HTTP, Kafka and declared AMQP/RabbitMQ relationships, DTO wire shape and dependencies through Inventory, Topology and Relations. Missing or ambiguous evidence remains Unknown.
  • Review a change: compare HEAD or a selected Git base with the working tree, inspect before/after fields and both source locations, then review direct Impact separately from downstream candidates.
  • Explore the Workspace: search findings, filter protocols, navigate to source and use Diagnostics to understand incomplete or unsupported evidence and recovery options.
  • Call an API: compose HTTP requests, connect to WebSocket or gRPC, or run bounded sequential HTTP scenarios from the API Client.
  • Share for team review: save JSON, export topology and SARIF, configure policy inputs, or gate saved snapshots in CI. Fresh headless analysis has separate IDE and entitlement prerequisites.

Developer Suite

Nine focused tools share the IntelliJ workspace. Choose a task, then follow its inputs, output and limits in the Marketplace Documentation.

  • API Client: HTTP requests and environments, bounded Before/After scripts and sequential scenarios with assertions and captured variables, WebSocket send/receive, unary or server-streaming gRPC.
  • Spring configuration: inspect keys, profiles and usages; navigate source and use supported editor intelligence, conversion helpers and live templates.
  • MyBatis SQL: reconstruct logged SQL and parameters, passively capture console output and navigate to mapper sources; no database query is executed.
  • Ansible: scan local playbooks, roles and variables, edit/save Vault content, and run a configured external syntax check when available.
  • Shell and Bats: preview ShellCheck/shfmt, run Bats tests and debug Bash; POSIX and Zsh editor support is separate from the Bash debugger.
  • React Native: discover project scripts and use supported platform/Expo commands and available ADB device controls.
  • ANSI logs: render log output and browse large files by bounded pages with reader settings.
  • Dev Icons: compare three bundled styles, assign project/global rules and manage customer-authored packs.
  • Keystore and X.509: inspect supported store files and certificate, CRL, public-key, private-key-metadata and CSR artifacts read-only.

Customer-authored icon packs and rules work during the 14-day Trial. Bundled styles can be previewed in Trial; applying or exporting bundled styles requires paid entitlement. Private or secret key material is never displayed or exported.

Team workflows

Save or copy architecture and Impact JSON, export topology as Mermaid/SVG/PNG and findings as SARIF, then use repository manifests, evidence inputs and policy review. CI gates consume saved JSON; the companion CLI also has a separate committed-checkout analysis path requiring a provisioned and indexed compatible IDE/plugin runtime with an active Trial/Pro entitlement.

Optional JetBrains MCP exposes bounded read-only Impact, Findings, Contract Evidence and Flow Tracing queries when enabled. Imported verification reports remain imported evidence; they are not automatically rerun or authenticated by ArchVerity.

Local boundaries, compatibility and support

Project analysis runs locally in IntelliJ IDEA. The plugin does not send project source, findings or usage telemetry to the publisher. API requests contact endpoints you choose; Marketplace licensing and configured external tools use their respective services.

ArchVerity is a Paid-only Marketplace plugin with a 14-day Trial of the architecture guard and Developer Suite. After Trial/subscription expiry, paid functionality requires a valid Marketplace entitlement; there is no permanent limited tier. Check Marketplace Versions for current plugin and IDE compatibility.

The Evidence and Workspace crops in the gallery are labeled synthetic ArchVerity 2.0.8 examples, not current customer results. Read the Spring contract background. For help, email archverity.support@gmail.com with your IDE/plugin version, expected and actual behavior, and a minimal redacted example.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
4.0.5

  • Improves Marketplace license validation and checks certificate validity without repeating expensive signature work.
  • Keeps subscription access through the last paid day and ends a Trial at its verified expiration time.
  • Refreshes externally edited files before MCP change checks so agents receive current contract evidence.
  • Publishes a project's own contracts even when another team's contract registry is unavailable.
  • Clarifies that project mapping and change review require an active Trial or Pro license; downloading remains free.

4.0.4

  • See who uses a contract right above it: callers above an endpoint, consumers above a producer, producers above a listener, with breaking and unproven pairs. Click to jump to the other side.
  • Find Usages (Alt+F7) on an endpoint, a listener or a method that sends also lists the calls, listeners and senders in your other services.
  • Contract changelog for pull requests and releases: added, removed and changed endpoints, topics and payloads, with the consumers a change breaks first.
  • Contract cleanup report: deprecated operations still in use and who uses them, deprecated ones nothing uses, and operations with no counterpart.
  • For coding agents: the archverity_check_change MCP tool answers "does this change break another service?" with a fix for each broken consumer.
  • New Change review: one plain sentence says which consumer breaks and why, next to a field-by-field diff of what is sent and what is expected, the chain that matched both sides, and ways to fix.
  • One answer for the whole change before you merge: Not safe to merge, Can't confirm it's safe, or No breaking contracts.
  • Editor notes on changed DTOs show who reads them and which consumer still expects an old field; Alt+Enter keeps the old JSON name.
  • Accept a known rule finding with a reason and expiry, copy a pull request note, and filter the service map to problems only.
  • Kafka matrix verdict summary and plain-language pair descriptions; Developer tools stay open in the sidebar, with a launcher to find a tool by name.
  • Find ArchVerity Section from anywhere with Alt+Shift+K, or ⌃⇧⌘K on macOS. Breaking and unproven relations are marked on the map even when the embedded browser is unavailable.
  • Clearer licence messages: after a trial ends, ArchVerity offers a purchase instead of another trial.
  • Preserve the modern IDEA 2025.3.6.1–2026.2 package and separate IDEA 2024.3 package.
  • Pull request comments with a fix for each broken consumer, and contract manifests shared between repositories.
  • A service's contract manifest no longer redeclares an exchange it only sends to.
  • Contract manifests publish only a repository's own contracts, without runtime observations.
  • The plugin builds the published contract manifest from this repository's own sources.
  • Publishing contracts no longer depends on other teams' manifests, and the base reads manifests as committed.
  • Edits to team manifest files trigger a rescan and reach the working-tree base.
  • Published contract manifests always fit the importer and never replace a file.
  • A start screen with Review my change, Map this project and Open demo project. ArchVerity stays Paid-only with a 14-day Trial: without an active Trial or Pro licence it neither analyzes nor shows a previously cached map.

3.0.6

  • Compare captured Kafka producer and consumer deployments within their recorded environment, with separate key, value, physical cluster/topic identity, DTO, schema and historical replay outcomes.
  • Keep profile paths, missing environment overrides and observation provenance visible. Missing or ambiguous evidence remains UNKNOWN rather than proving compatibility or delivery.
  • Inspect transaction binding, acknowledgment, retry/DLT routes, tombstones, partition routing and saved external configuration as independent contract aspects.
  • Apply an environment-bound deployment policy consistently to Findings, JSON, review summaries and CI gates; required missing, expired or UNKNOWN evidence cannot pass.
  • Capture selected existing Spring/Kafka runtime objects with a passive JDK 17 helper that preserves observation time without invoking suppliers or contacting brokers.
  • Preview native capture imports with configured deployment identities, freshness and file checks; preserve cancellation, stale-dialog protection and rollback on partial writes.
  • Filter Findings by text, rule, subject and source path; clear the query to restore the current results.
  • Keep producer and consumer source actions reachable in the Kafka inspector, and reserve a full matrix row with readable filters and selected aspects in narrow panels.
  • Keep the import action readable with enlarged Linux IDE fonts, with the complete action name available to assistive technology.
  • Preserve the modern IDEA 2025.3.6.1–2026.2 package and separate IDEA 2024.3 package.

3.0.5

  • Find Workspace sections by tool name or task from the header search or Ctrl+Alt+K; navigate with arrow keys, Enter and Escape.
  • Return to Workspace home from compact navigation and keep section transitions in Back/Forward history.
  • Clear Impact search and recover filtered empty results with one Reset filters action while preserving the Git comparison base.
  • Keep category text and long section names readable with larger IDE fonts, in both themes and the existing Editor, Focus and Review views.
  • Preserve the modern IDEA 2025.3.6.1–2026.2 package and separate IDEA 2024.3 package.

3.0.4

  • Keep same-name Kafka topics separate across services unless a logical cluster scope is explicitly declared; topic names and bootstrap addresses do not establish a shared cluster.
  • Retain profile, property and serializer/deserializer evidence chains. Missing environment overrides, defaults and cyclic references remain explicit UNKNOWN outcomes.

  • Preserve scoped retry/DLT routes when importing manifests and provide twelve reproducible Kafka demo scenarios with an English and Russian walkthrough.

  • Work beside the editor in Companion, inspect changes with a persistent list in Focus, or read a result with its source inspector in Review.

idea-plugin.name: Error Prone
idea-plugin.description:
Error Prone's findings from your Gradle build, on the code they are about, with their fixes a keystroke away.

Error Prone already runs in your build. This plugin reads what it reports while the IDE builds and puts each finding in the editor, where you can fix it, suppress it or look it up. It uses your build's own Error Prone, its flags and its plugins, NullAway included: there is nothing to download and nothing to configure twice.

  • In the editor: an underline on the exact token, with the check, the message, Error Prone's suggested fixes and the check's documentation in the tooltip
  • Alt+Enter: apply Error Prone's own fix, imports included, with a preview of the line it writes, or suppress the check with @SuppressWarnings on the narrowest declaration
  • An Error Prone tab in the Problems tool window: group by check or by file, filter, step through with the keyboard, fix or suppress a whole check at once, and see only what your changes bring in
  • Apply All Error Prone Fixes for a scope, as Inspect Code asks for one, reviewed file by file in one patch
  • Build | Run Error Prone recompiles every Java source set and shows what it found
  • Current as you type: an edit near a diagnostic recompiles quietly in the background
  • Before a commit: diagnostics on the lines it changes are pointed out, with no build

Your build stays the source of truth. The plugin runs no checks of its own and never edits a build script. Diagnostics come from Gradle's Problems API through the Tooling API, with their file, line and column, not from parsing console output.

Requires Gradle 8.14 or newer with Error Prone set up in the build (for example with the net.ltgt.errorprone Gradle plugin), and builds run from the IDE. Getting started and known limitations are in the README.

Not affiliated with Google or the Error Prone project.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • The Error Prone tab works in IntelliJ IDEA 2026.3 EAP: there the Problems tool window became a plugin of its own, the tab failed to load with NoClassDefFoundError: ProblemsViewTab, and Show in Error Prone Tab after a commit check threw.

idea-plugin.name: Kubernetes Release Guard
idea-plugin.description:
Kubernetes Release Guard helps developers review production deployment risks in Kubernetes manifests before applying them — entirely inside their JetBrains IDE.

Review security and rollout-readiness risks in rendered YAML for Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Pod, Job and CronJob, without connecting to a Kubernetes cluster.

What it checks

  • Resource safety: missing or inconsistent CPU and memory requests/limits, including requests that exceed limits.
  • Workload privileges: privileged containers, root execution, privilege escalation, seccomp settings and Linux capabilities.
  • Host exposure: hostNetwork, hostPID, hostIPC, hostPort and hostPath volume configurations.
  • Release reliability: readiness/liveness probes for long-running services, context-aware startup probe guidance and image tag pinning.
  • Production readiness: explained findings with severity, confidence (explicit vs. contextual), and suggested remediation.

Your review workflow

  1. Open your Kubernetes YAML project.
  2. View inline inspection findings or open View → Tool Windows → Kubernetes Release Guard.
  3. Select Scan project to build a local risk summary and heuristic production-readiness score.
  4. Inspect each finding and double-click it to jump to its manifest.
  5. Export HTML, JSON or SARIF reports when you need release-review evidence.

Use a project-level .kubernetes-release-guard.json policy to adjust severity, require image digests, disable specific checks or document scoped exceptions with reasons and expiry dates.

Offline by design

The plugin never applies a Kubernetes resource, reads kubeconfig credentials, launches kubectl, downloads charts, calls an AI API or needs a running cluster. For Helm, inspect the already-rendered static manifest output of charts you have reviewed; raw templates are deliberately skipped.

This is a focused, static production-risk review — not an API-server schema validator, live cluster scanner, vulnerability scanner, admission-policy simulator or compliance guarantee. Missing settings are reported contextually where Kubernetes defaults or application behavior could justify them.

Documentation and getting started · Developer EULA · Support: info@afkmesh.com
idea-plugin.change-notes: First release: local workload analysis, production readiness dashboard, policy exceptions, exports.

idea-plugin.name: DevHelper
idea-plugin.description:
一个能够提高效率的开发助手插件，主要包括以下功能:
  • 生产密码：大小写字母、数字、特殊符号任意组合，长度任意指定，批量生成密码；
  • 生成序号：根据起始值、步长、位数生成一系列序号，并可添加前后缀；
  • Base64编码和解密，支持多种编码格式以及URL安全选项；
  • 散列哈希加密：支持MD5、SHA-1、SHA-224、SHA-256、SHA-384、SHA-512、HmacMD5、HmacSHA1、HmacSHA224、HmacSHA256、HmacSHA384、HmacSHA512的加密
  • 文本处理：可以对行文本进行格式化(去除空白、空行、重复行)、行编辑(合并、拆分、命名转换等)、行排序(按照字母或数据升序降序)
  • 生产UUID：支持大写/小写 UUID的生成，可以选择是否带有分隔符
  • 格式化：支持Json、xml、html的格式化
  • RSA非对称加解密：支持RSA的私钥/公钥分别进行加密或者解密，可以生成私钥和公钥对
A development assistant plug-in that can improve efficiency, mainly includes the following functions:
  • Production password: any combination of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special symbols, any length specified, batch generation of passwords;
  • Generate serial number: Generate a series of serial numbers according to the starting value, step length, and digits, and add prefixes and suffixes;
  • Base64 encoding and decryption, supporting multiple encoding formats and URL security options;
  • Hash hash encryption: support MD5, SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, HmacMD5, HmacSHA1, HmacSHA224, HmacSHA256, HmacSHA384, HmacSHA512 encryption
  • Text processing: line text can be formatted (removal of blanks, empty lines, repeated lines), line editing (merge, split, name conversion, etc.), line sorting (ascending and descending by alphabet or data)
  • Production UUID: support the generation of uppercase/lowercase UUID, you can choose whether to have a separator
  • Formatting: Support formatting of Json, xml, html
  • RSA asymmetric encryption and decryption: support RSA private key/public key for encryption or decryption respectively, can generate private key and public key pair

idea-plugin.name: Symfony Plugin
idea-plugin.description:
Support for Symfony framework / components.


Project Page / Documentation | Donate | Buy License

Freemium

  • All features which are inside GitHub are free to use, unless there is reason (e.g. Supporting old Symfony Version, ...)
  • Non-free features are flagged with [paid] inside Documentation and inside the CHANGELOG
  • There is ~15min grace period after project open where all features are available
  • A license must be activated via PhpStorm / Intellij: use menu "Help -> Register" or use "Search Everywhere" by searching for "Manage License..." action
A license can be bought at JetBrains Marketplace. Free Discount Code generator for open source contributions are planned.

Install

  • Activate plugin per project in "File -> PHP -> Symfony" or use auto configuration notification
  • (Required) Install PHP Annotations
  • (Optional) Configure a default project connection in "Remote Hosts Access / Remote Hosts" to enable support for remote files in plugin settings
  • (Optional) Ignore Symfony "cache" directory because of duplicate classes "Settings -> Project -> Directories"
  • (Optional) Install PHP Toolbox
  • (Optional) For XLIFF translations key navigation install Localization or add "*.xlf" / "*.xliff" to XML "Editor" -> "File Types"

AI / MCP Integration

This plugin extends IntelliJ/PhpStorm built-in MCP server enabling intelligent code assistance with Symfony project context.

Setup:

  1. Enable the built-in MCP server in IntelliJ/PhpStorm: Settings → Tools → Model Context Protocol → Enable MCP Server
  2. Configure your AI assistant (e.g., Claude Code) to connect to the IntelliJ MCP server

Features

Dependency Injection Container

  • References for services in ContainerInterface::get()
  • Detect ContainerInterface::get() result type
  • References for services, tags, events, methods, ... inside yaml, xml and php
  • Indexer to provide live editing without a compiled container
  • Tagged class indexer

Doctrine

  • ORM QueryBuilder support, including chaining and nested methods
  • References and TypeProvider for doctrine getRepository
  • TypeProvider for EntityRepository::find/findOneBy/findAll/findBy
  • Field and relations resolving and annotation and yaml

Templates/Twig

idea-plugin.name: PHP Advanced AutoComplete
idea-plugin.description:
Adds auto-completion support for various built-in PHP functions and methods, where parameter is a string literal.

The following functions are currently supported:

  • header/header_remove
    HTTP response headers, status codes, charsets, mime-types, locations, and much more

  • File and folder related functions and methods (fopen, file_get_contents, dir...)
    Files and/or folders paths relative to the current file (completion and reference)

  • date / strftime / DateTime::format etc
    Format characters and common format strings

  • strtotime / DateTime constructor / DateTime::modify
    DateTime notations

  • htmlentities/htmlspecialchars
    Supported charsets

  • mb_string functions
    Charset, where required; types for mb_get_info and supported languages for mb_language

  • ini_get/ini_set/ini_restore/get_cfg_var
    Known INI variable names

  • extension_loaded
    Known PHP extensions

  • fopen/popen/SplFileInfo::openFile
    File modes

  • mysql_connect/mysqli_connect/mysqli/PDO
    Hostnames, database names and usernames from data sources defined in project

  • mysql_select_db/mysqli_select_db/mysqli::select_db
    Database names from data sources defined in project

  • mysqli_change_user/mysqli::change_user
    Usernames and database names from data sources defined in project

  • mysql_set_charset/mysqli_set_charset/mysqli::set_charset
    Supported charsets for MySQL

  • getenv
    Common environment variables (like in $_SERVER array keys)

If you have further suggestions/ideas, just send me an e-mail.

Commend and rate this plugin here

idea-plugin.name: Zephir
idea-plugin.description:
Provides Zephir language support for IntelliJ IDEs.


GitHub | Issues | Donate

Zephir is a high level language that eases the creation and maintainability of extensions for PHP. Zephir extensions are exported to C code that can be compiled and optimized by major C compilers such as gcc/clang/vc++. Functionality is exposed to the PHP language.

Highlighted Features

  • Syntax highlighting
  • Syntax check support
  • Autocompletion — local variables, class/interface names from the project, PHP built-in functions, and member access (->) for Zephir-typed variables
  • Structure View — browse classes, interfaces, methods, properties, and constants via the IDE structure panel
  • Code Folding — fold class/interface bodies, method blocks, inline C blocks, and block comments
  • Live Templates — expand common Zephir snippets (class, functions, loops, try/catch) with short abbreviations
  • Rename Refactoring — rename classes, interfaces, methods, properties, and constants
  • Implementations Gutter — see subclass and implementation counts in the editor gutter
  • Go To Declaration — Ctrl+click a class or interface name to jump to its declaration; qualified names resolve via namespace path, aliases navigate to their use statement

idea-plugin.name: Php Inspections (EA Extended)
idea-plugin.description:
This free and open-source plugin (GitHub) is a code review and static code analysis tool for PHP that uses deterministic pattern recognition, data type analysis, and workflow evaluation.

It covers:
- architecture related issues
- weak types control and possible code construct simplifications
- performance issues
- non-optimal, duplicate and suspicious "if" conditions
- validation of magic methods usage
- regular expressions
- compatibility issues
- variety of time-consuming bugs
- PHPUnit API usage
- security issues

The enhanced commercial version, Php Inspections (EA Ultimate), provides additional and improved inspections. If you find the free version valuable, sharing a plugin review or upgrading to the commercial version helps support ongoing plugin development.

For Mac shortcuts, see this reference card. Windows/Linux ones are:
Alt + Shift + I to inspect current file with current profile
Ctrl + Alt + Shift + I to run inspection by name
Ctrl + Shift + F4 to close results of inspection.

A big thank you to our supporters: Pixel & Tonic (Bend, USA).

idea-plugin.name: Drupal Namespace Detector
idea-plugin.description:
Drupal Namespace Detector is a PhpStorm plugin that detects sources/tests folders in Drupal core, modules, themes, or recipes and marks the directories as Source Roots or Test Roots.

If folder has a namespace, it will also be automatically registered as the package prefix.

Registering the sources/tests folders and namespaces offers the following benefits:

  • When searching with Find in Files..., you can exclude or search only for test code
  • When creating a new class, the correct namespace is automatically entered
  • Namespace mismatches can be detected

The following folders can be detected:

  • Drupal core: Sources and Tests
  • Modules (core/contrib/custom): Sources and Tests
  • Themes (core/contrib/custom): Tests only
  • Drupal Recipes: Tests only

Supported Drupal Versions

Drupal 8 and later (including 9, 10, and 11)

  • Automatically set the bundled "Moodle" inspection profile as the Project profile on first project open (non‑intrusive: won’t override an existing custom selection).

    • Kotlin JVM: 2.2.10 → 2.2.20.
    • Kover: 0.9.1 → 0.9.2.
    • GitHub Actions: actions/setup-java 4 → 5, gradle/actions 4 → 5.
  • Removed MoodleManagerListener (registration moved to plugin.xml) and registered bundled inspection profile via <bundledInspectionProfile/>.

Fixed

  • Fixed compatibility and compilation in MoodlePHPNewClassAction with newer IntelliJ Platform/PHP plugin by calling getSelectedClassCreationType() and removing final hasCustomProperties override.
  • Resolved binary incompatibility by removing final getId() override in MoodlePluginGenerator.
  • Migrated MoodleBundle to the non-deprecated class-backed DynamicBundle constructor.
  • Robust parsing of version.php to correctly ignore PHP comments and remarks when detecting plugin names and versions.
  • Refactored namespace and module detection to use reliable absolute paths from IntelliJ's virtual file system, ensuring consistent behavior across different project structures and OSs.
  • Corrected automatic selection of the bundled "Moodle" inspection profile as the Project profile so it reliably appears in Settings | Editor | Inspections.
  • Replaced deprecated ProcessAdapter with ProcessListener in ComposerUtil.kt to maintain compatibility with the latest IntelliJ Platform SDK.
  • Removed usage of unstable UI DSL textFieldWithBrowseButton in MoodleSettingsForm; used Swing TextFieldWithBrowseButton within cell(...) to satisfy UnstableApiUsage inspection.

idea-plugin.name: NEON Nette Support
idea-plugin.description:

idea-plugin.change-notes:
For PhpStorm 2026.1+

Added

  • Segmented PSI model for file paths in includes: section — each path part is now a separate PSI element
    • Per-segment Ctrl-click navigation: clicking on a directory segment opens the directory, clicking on a file segment opens the file
    • Per-segment file path code completion: typing config/ offers files inside config/ subfolder
    • Per-segment rename refactoring: renaming a file or directory updates only the affected segment in includes:
    • Move file refactoring: moving an included file (or its directory) automatically updates the path in includes:
    • Works for both unquoted (- config/dev.neon) and quoted (- 'config/dev.neon') include values
  • Distinct syntax highlighting for file paths — segments and separators in includes: use a unified File path color (HIGHLIGHTED_REFERENCE), visually distinct from regular strings; configurable in Settings → Editor → Color Scheme

Internal

  • New NeonLookAheadLexer retypes tokens to T_NEON_FILE_PATH / T_NEON_FILE_PATH_SEPARATOR inside includes: scope (mirrors LattePro {include} design)
  • Flex lexer rule for T_SLASH token (slash is no longer absorbed into T_LITERAL)
  • New BNF rules includeFile / includePath and matching PSI elements NeonIncludeFile / NeonIncludePath
  • Upgraded to IntelliJ Platform 2026.1, Java 21, Kotlin 2.3, Gradle 9.5

idea-plugin.description:
Best and fastest Latte language plugin. Provides support for Latte – a template engine for PHP. It's a must have plugin for Nette developers.

!! For older Latte versions READ recommendations !!

  • Plugin page: IntelliJ plugin Latte
  • DOCS: Latte Pro plugin
  • Issue tracker: GitHub

Supported Features

  • Syntax highlighting
  • Code completion for PHP, classic HTML, attribute tags and more
  • Registering custom tags, filters and custom functions via XML
  • Reference to classes, methods, properties, ...
  • Reference to included files, link handlers and more
  • More inspections and intentions which helps

idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Full support for named Latte blocks — navigation, completion, Find Usages, rename and inspections
    • Declaration side: {block name}, {define name}, n:block (and the existing {snippet} / {snippetArea})
    • Reference side: {include name}, {include #name}, {includeBlock}, {embed}, {ifset name} and the hasBlock() function
    • References resolve across templates via {include name from 'file.latte'}, {import}, {layout} / {extends} and {embed}, respecting block scope (inheritance, imports, embed isolation)
    • Ctrl-click on a block reference jumps to its declaration; completion offers blocks visible in the current scope; rename updates the declaration and all references at once
    • New "unknown block" inspection for references that resolve to no block in scope; dynamic block names (e.g. {block "hi-$name"}) and dynamic layouts are left unresolved instead of being reported as errors
  • Support for the curly-brace syntax in n: attributes introduced in Latte 3.1, e.g. <a n:href={Home:default}>
    • The expression between { … } is lexed, parsed, highlighted, completed and resolved exactly like the quoted form, so link / component / file-path references and inspections keep working
  • n:elseif attribute (Latte 3.1) alongside the existing n:else
  • Built-in filters filter and stripTags
  • Built-in functions group and hasTemplate

1.8.2 - 2026-10-07

Changed

  • Renamed the plugin from Latte Support to Latte

Fixed

1.8.1 - 2026-09-13

Fixed

  • StubTextInconsistencyException when searching for usages of a PHP method, property or constant
  • ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException and missing references when getReferences() is called from several threads, and stale references in a {link} after an edit to a neighbouring part
  • StackOverflowError taking down a whole inspection pass on a variable defined from itself, such as {var $a = $a} read through a member
  • Template left unparsed, with refused to parse text with Language: XML in the log, after {contentType} is edited in an open file
  • Editor freeze on deeply nested arrays, on tags holding many arguments or statements, and on runs of unclosed brackets
  • {var $d = new DateTimeImmutable('…')} reported as an unknown function
  • {$items|batch:2} reported as missing required parameters
  • {var $a}, {var $a, $b} and {var App\Model\Thing $x} reported as a missing assignment
  • A method reported as missing on a type that resolves to no class

Performance

  • Finding usages of a PHP method or property resolves the reference once instead of once per candidate class

1.8.0 - 2026-07-11

Added

  • Support for the curly-brace syntax in n: attributes introduced in Latte 3.1, e.g. <a n:href={Home:default}>
  • Latte 3.0/3.1 built-in filters: clamp, column, commas, filter, firstLower, group, limit, localDate, stripTags, toggle, translate
  • Latte built-in functions: group, hasBlock, hasTemplate
  • {exitIf} and {translate} tags, plus the n:elseif and n:translate attributes

1.7.4 - 2026-05-22

Fixed

idea-plugin.name: Project Specific Autocomplete
idea-plugin.description:
Plugin which adds support of custom autocomplete & GoTo on the language you're writing your project.

Currently, supports:

  • Custom autocomplete based on your code (Ctrl + Space)
  • Custom GoTo based on your code (Ctrl/Command + Click)
  • Custom code templates (with variables) based on your code
  • Custom editor actions for convert parts of code to the needed format or perform some other actions
  • Static completions for faster experience
  • Resolving references (for static completions)
  • Intentions (for static completions)

Supported Languages

Any language that your IDE supports will be supported by plugin.

To check how to add custom autocomplete, GoTo and custom code templates, please read documentation
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.0.33 - 2026-06-29

  • [GoTo] The PSA script-based GoTo no longer runs when a reference at the caret resolves or another GoTo handler already provides a target, avoiding a synchronous script call when navigation is already possible
  • [JavaScript] Added an optional JavaScript extension (active when the bundled JavaScript plugin is present). Method argument providers resolve a jQuery-plugin dispatch string (e.g. $el.somePlugin('somePluginMethod', …)) to the target prototype method, enabling GoTo, Find Usages and Rename. Method-name completion (Ctrl+Space) lists the class's prototype methods, parameter info (Cmd/Ctrl+P) shows the resolved method's parameters for the dispatched arguments, and parameter-name inlay hints are shown on those arguments

idea-plugin.name: Suppressed Attributes
idea-plugin.description:
This plugin makes it possible to suppress the "Unused declaration" inspection on methods or fields that have a specific attributes that the user can choose.
The user can specify a list of the attributes considered.
This is similar to the "Suppressed annotations" feature in PhpStorm, but for attributes.

The user specifies an attribute by supplying its fully qualified name (FQN). The supplied FQN Should start with a backslash (\).
Example: \Fully\Qualified\Name\SuppressingAttribute

The user might need to reopen the files that should be affected if no result is immediately visible.

idea-plugin.name: PHP Serialized Object Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
PHP Serialized Object Viewer

A plugin that monitors clipboard and converts PHP serialized strings to JSON format for display.

Key Features

  • Real-time monitoring: Monitor clipboard content every 1 second
  • Automatic conversion: Automatically convert to JSON format when PHP serialized data is detected
  • Tool window display: Display conversion results in a dedicated tool window

Example

PHP Serialized:

a:1:{s:4:"name";s:4:"John";}

Converted to JSON:

{
  "name": "John"
}

Conversion library: php-json-deserializer-kt
idea-plugin.change-notes: Initial version

idea-plugin.name: PHP Companion
idea-plugin.description:
PHP Companion Intellij Plugin

A PhpStorm/IntelliJ plugin that enhances PHP development workflow with advanced navigation and code analysis features, particularly focused on Symfony Messenger pattern and peer navigation capabilities.

Features

🚀 Symfony Messenger navigation

  • Smart Navigation: Navigate from message dispatch calls directly to their corresponding handlers
  • Find Usages: Discover all dispatch calls for a specific message class or handler method
  • Message Detection: Automatically identify message classes based on naming patterns and interfaces
  • Handler Detection: Recognize message handlers through interfaces, attributes, or naming conventions
  • Multi-dispatch Support: Support for various dispatch method names (dispatch, query, command, handle)

🔗 Peer Navigation (code to test to code navigation)

  • Pattern-based Navigation: Navigate between related classes using regex patterns
  • Flexible Mapping: Define custom source-to-target class relationships
  • Go to Declaration: Jump between peer classes with a single keystroke
  • Associate Navigation: Navigate between associated classes based on custom relationships
  • Multi-direction Support: Navigate bidirectionally between associated classes

🧑‍💻 Attribute Navigation

  • Attribute-based Navigation: Open a intellij search with a formatted value of an attribute property
  • Flexible Mapping: Define custom attribute property and a formatter to generate a custom intellij search pattern
  • Click and search: Jump between peer classes with a single keystroke

📝 Source Export to LLM markdown

  • Markdown Export: Export source code to markdown format optimized for LLMs
  • Code Context Preservation: Maintain code structure and relationships in exported format, could also add all related classes found in specific namespaces.
  • Custom Formatting: Configure export format settings
  • Selective Export: Choose specific files or directories to export
  • .aiignore: .aiignore file is used to filter files to export
  • Freely inspired from https://github.com/keyboardsamurai/source-clipboard-export-intellij-plugin which was dedicated to Java project

🔍 CLI Dumper Parser

  • Command Output Analysis: Parse and analyze CLI dumper output
  • Structured Data Extraction: Convert raw CLI output into structured format (JSON ou short syntac PHP arrays)
  • Integration Support: Seamless integration with development workflow

Tool Window Panels

  • Supports filtering and searching
  • Double-click to navigate to command implementation
  • Provides direct navigation to route definitions
  • Commands Panel: Shows command descriptions and usage information
  • Routes Panel: Displays route path, name, and methods
  • Doctrine Entities Panel: Displays name, tableName and schema

⚙️ Configuration Management

  • Hot Reload: Configuration changes are automatically detected and applied
  • Multiple Formats: Support for JSON and YAML configuration files
  • Hierarchical Config: Local configuration files can override global settings
  • Real-time Notifications: Get notified when configuration is loaded or encounters errors

Configuration

The plugin uses configuration files placed in your project root. The plugin will automatically detect and load configuration from any of these files (in order of precedence):

  • .php-companion.yaml
  • .php-companion.json
  • .php-companion.local.yaml
  • .php-companion.local.json

Configuration Structure

Complete YAML Configuration Example

attributeNavigation:
  rules:
    - actionType: find_in_file
      attributeFQCN: \Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route
      fileMask: '*.yaml,*.yml,*.php'
      formatterScript: |
        return (value.replaceAll("(\\{.*?\\})", "[^/]*")+ ":");
      isDefault: true
      propertyName: path
commands:
  attributeFQCN: \Symfony\Component\Console\Attribute\AsCommand
  enabled: true
  namespaces:
    - \App
    - \Application
consoleCleaner:
  patterns:
    - ''
doctrineEntities:
  attributeFQCN: \Doctrine\ORM\Mapping\Table
  enabled: true
  namespaces:
    - \Domain
    - \Entity
exportSourceToMarkdown:
  contextualNamespaces:
    - App\Core\Models
  template: |
    [# th:each="file : ${files}"]
    ## [(${file.path})]

    ````[(${file.extension})]
    [(${file.content})]
    ````

    [/]
  useContextualNamespaces: true
  useIgnoreFile: true
openAPI:
  enabled: true
  specificationRoots:
    - ''
peerNavigation:
  associates:
    - classA: \\App\\Tests\\Func\\(?<type>.*)\\Web\\(?<path>.*)\\ControllerTest
      classB: \\App\\(?<type>.*)\\Web\\(?<path>.*)\\Controller
  peers:
    - source: ''
      target: ''
routes:
  attributeFQCN: \Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route
  enabled: true
  namespaces:
    - \App
    - \Application
symfonyMessenger:
  asMessageHandlerAttribute: Symfony\Component\Messenger\Attribute\AsMessageHandler
  dispatchMethods:
    - dispatch
    - query
    - command
    - handle
  handlerMethods:
    - __invoke
    - handle
  messageClassNamePatterns: .*(Message|Command|Query|Event|Input)$
  messageHandlerInterfaces:
    - Symfony\Component\Messenger\Handler\MessageHandlerInterface
  messageInterfaces:
    - ''
  projectRootNamespace: \App
  useNativeGoToDeclaration: false

Symfony Messenger Configuration

Properties

PropertyDescription
asMessageHandlerAttributeFQCN of the attribute used to mark handler classes
dispatchMethods[]Method names used to dispatch messages
enableExceptionInferenceEnable @throws inference for dispatch calls based on handler PHPDoc
handlerMethods[]Method names in handler classes
messageClassNamePatternsRegex pattern to identify message classes
messageHandlerInterfaces[]Interfaces that handler classes implement
messageInterfaces[]Interfaces that message classes implement
projectRootNamespaceRoot namespace for scanning classes
useNativeGoToDeclarationDisable ctrl+click to go to handler service
  • asMessageHandlerAttribute
    • FQCN of the attribute used to mark handler classes
    • Default Value: Symfony\Component\Messenger\Attribute\AsMessageHandler
  • dispatchMethods[]
    • Method names used to dispatch messages
  • enableExceptionInference
    • Enable @throws inference for dispatch calls based on handler PHPDoc
    • Default Value: true
  • handlerMethods[]
    • Method names in handler classes
  • messageClassNamePatterns
    • Regex pattern to identify message classes
    • Default Value: .*(Message|Command|Query|Event|Input)$
  • messageHandlerInterfaces[]
    • Interfaces that handler classes implement
  • messageInterfaces[]
    • Interfaces that message classes implement
  • projectRootNamespace
    • Root namespace for scanning classes
    • Default Value: \App
  • useNativeGoToDeclaration
    • Disable ctrl+click to go to handler service
    • Default Value: false

Example

symfonyMessenger:
  asMessageHandlerAttribute: Symfony\Component\Messenger\Attribute\AsMessageHandler
  dispatchMethods:
  - dispatch
  - query
  - command
  - handle
  enableExceptionInference: true
  handlerMethods:
  - __invoke
  - handle
  messageClassNamePatterns: .*(Message|Command|Query|Event|Input)$
  messageHandlerInterfaces:
  - Symfony\Component\Messenger\Handler\MessageHandlerInterface
  messageInterfaces:
  - ''
  projectRootNamespace: \App
  useNativeGoToDeclaration: false

Peer Navigation Configuration

Properties

PropertyDescription
associates[]Array of bidirectional navigation rules
associates[].classARegex pattern with named groups matching first class FQN
associates[].classBPattern for second class FQN using (?<groupName>.+) substitution from named groups
peers[]Array of one-way navigation rules
peers[].sourceRegex pattern with named groups matching source class FQN
peers[].targetTarget class FQN pattern using (?<groupName>.+) substitution from named groups
  • associates[]
    • Array of bidirectional navigation rules
  • associates[].classA
    • Regex pattern with named groups matching first class FQN
    • Example: \\App\\Tests\\Func\\(?<type>.*)\\Web\\(?<path>.*)\\ControllerTest
  • associates[].classB
    • Pattern for second class FQN using (?<groupName>.+) substitution from named groups
    • Example: \\App\\(?<type>.*)\\Web\\(?<path>.*)\\Controller
  • peers[]
    • Array of one-way navigation rules
  • peers[].source
    • Regex pattern with named groups matching source class FQN
  • peers[].target
    • Target class FQN pattern using (?<groupName>.+) substitution from named groups

Example

peerNavigation:
  associates:
  - classA: \\App\\Tests\\Func\\(?<type>.*)\\Web\\(?<path>.*)\\ControllerTest
    classB: \\App\\(?<type>.*)\\Web\\(?<path>.*)\\Controller
  peers:
  - source: ''
    target: ''

Note: Associates provide bidirectional navigation - you can navigate from classA to classB and vice versa.

Peer Navigation Examples

Bidirectional Navigation between Entities and Repositories:

peerNavigation:
  associates:
    - classA: \\App\\Domain\\Entity\\(?<entity>.+)
      classB: \\App\\Domain\\Repository\\(?<entity>.+)Repository

Bidirectional Navigation between Controllers and Services:

peerNavigation:
  associates:
    - classA: \\App\\Controller\\(?<controller>.+)Controller
      classB: \\App\\Service\\(?<controller>.+)Service

One-way Navigation from Commands to CommandHandlers using Named Groups:

peerNavigation:
  peers:
    - source: \\App\\Application\\(?<domain>.+)\\Command\\(?<command>.+)Command
      target: \\App\\Application\\(?<domain>.+)\\CommandHandler\\(?<command>.+)CommandHandler

One-way Navigation from Queries to QueryHandlers:

peerNavigation:
  peers:
    - source: \\App\\Application\\(?<domain>.+)\\Query\\(?<query>.+)Query
      target: \\App\\Application\\(?<domain>.+)\\QueryHandler\\(?<query>.+)QueryHandler

Complex Example with Multiple Named Groups:

peerNavigation:
  peers:
    - source: \\App\\(?<layer>Application|Domain)\\(?<module>.+)\\Entity\\(?<entity>.+)
      target: \\App\\(?<layer>Application|Domain)\\(?<module>.+)\\Repository\\(?<entity>.+)Repository
  associates:
    - classA: \\App\\Domain\\(?<module>.+)\\Entity\\(?<entity>.+)
      classB: \\App\\Domain\\(?<module>.+)\\Factory\\(?<entity>.+)Factory

Navigation by Attributes

Properties

PropertyDescription
rules[]Array of navigation rules
rules[].actionTypeHow search is triggered
rules[].attributeFQCNFQCN of the attribute searched
rules[].fileMaskFile mask to search for attribute usages, separated by comma
rules[].formatterScriptA groovy script to reformat raw attribute value
rules[].isDefaultIs this rule the default one?
rules[].propertyNameProperty of the attribute used
  • rules[]
    • Array of navigation rules
  • rules[].actionType
    • How search is triggered
    • Default Value: find_in_file
  • rules[].attributeFQCN
    • FQCN of the attribute searched
    • Default Value: \Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route
  • rules[].fileMask
    • File mask to search for attribute usages, separated by comma
    • Default Value: *.yaml,*.yml,*.php
  • rules[].formatterScript
    • A groovy script to reformat raw attribute value
    • Example: return (value.replaceAll("(\\{.*?\\})", "[^/]*")+ ":");
  • rules[].isDefault
    • Is this rule the default one?
    • Default Value: true
  • rules[].propertyName
    • Property of the attribute used
    • Default Value: path

Example

attributeNavigation:
  rules:
  - attributeFQCN: \Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route
    propertyName: path
    isDefault: true
    fileMask: '*.yaml,*.yml,*.php'
    actionType: find_in_file
    formatterScript: "\n        return (value.replaceAll(\"(\\\\{.*?\\\\})\", \"[^/]*\"\
      )+ \":\");\n        "

Export Source to Markdown Configuration

Properties

PropertyDescription
contextualNamespaces[]List of namespaces, if an import detected in an exported classes belong to one of those namespace, than the class is added in the context
templateTemplate Thymeleaf used to generate markdown export. Accès aux variables : files (FileData properties path, content, et extension)
useContextualNamespacesAre contextual namespaces used?
useIgnoreFileAre ignored files used?
  • contextualNamespaces[]
    • List of namespaces, if an import detected in an exported classes belong to one of those namespace, than the class is added in the context
  • template
    • Template Thymeleaf used to generate markdown export. Accès aux variables : files (FileData properties path, content, et extension)
    • Default Value: ``` [# th:each="file : ${files}"]

[(${file.path})]

[(${file.content})]

[/]

- **useContextualNamespaces**
 - Are contextual namespaces used?
 - **Default Value**: ``` true ```
- **useIgnoreFile**
 - Are ignored files used?
 - **Default Value**: ``` true ```
<!-- generateDocumentationEnd -->

#### Example
<!-- generateDocumentationExample("org.micoli.php.exportSourceToMarkdown.configuration.ExportSourceToMarkdownConfiguration","exportSourceToMarkdown") -->
```yaml
exportSourceToMarkdown:
 contextualNamespaces:
 - App\Core\Models
 template: |
   [# th:each="file : ${files}"]
   ## [(${file.path})]

   [(${file.content})]
   ````

   [/]

Properties

    • Label displayed for this folder in the hierarchical tree. User-friendly name for organizing tasks into logical groups
  • tree[].tasks[]
    • Array of child nodes contained in this folder. Can contain other folders (Path) or task references (Task)
  • watchers[]
    • File watchers configuration that automatically trigger tasks when specified files are modified
  • watchers[].debounce
    • Delay in milliseconds before task triggering after change detection. Prevents multiple executions during rapid successive modifications
    • Default Value: 1000
  • watchers[].events
    • List all events triggering the watcher, by default, all events
  • watchers[].notify
    • Indicates if a notification should be displayed to the user upon triggering. False by default to avoid too frequent notifications
    • Default Value: false
  • watchers[].taskId
    • Identifier of the task to execute when watched files are modified. Must match the ID of an existing task in the configuration
  • watchers[].watches[]
    • Array of file patterns to watch. Supports wildcards and regular expressions to match file paths

Example

tasks:
  enabled: false
  tasks:
  - type: builtin
    id: aTaskId
    label: null
    actionId: $Copy
    icon: debugger/threadRunning.svg
  - type: shell
    id: aTaskId
    label: null
    command: make clear-cache
    cwd: ''
    icon: debugger/threadRunning.svg
  - type: script
    id: aTaskId
    label: null
    source: ''
    extension: groovy
    icon: debugger/threadRunning.svg
  - type: observedFile
    id: aTaskId
    label: null
    commentPrefix: '#'
    filePath: ''
    variableName: ''
    activeIcon: actions/inlayRenameInComments.svg
    inactiveIcon: actions/inlayRenameInCommentsActive.svg
    unknownIcon: expui/fileTypes/unknown.svg
    postToggle:
      type: builtin
      id: aTaskId
      label: null
      actionId: null
      icon: debugger/threadRunning.svg
  - type: link
    id: aTaskId
    label: null
    url: http://www.github.com
    icon: expui/gutter/web.svg
  - type: bookmark
    id: aTaskId
    label: null
    path: http://www.github.com
    icon: expui/gutter/web.svg
  toolbar:
  - type: task
    taskId: aTaskId
    label: aLabel
  tree:
  - type: path
    label: ''
    tasks:
    - null
    - null
  - null
  watchers:
  - taskId: ''
    debounce: 1000
    notify: false
    watches:
    - ''
    events:
    - CREATE
    - CONTENT_CHANGED
    - COPY
    - DELETE
    - MOVE
    - PROPERTY_CHANGED

Symfony Profiler:

Properties

PropertyDescription
enabledEnabler for panel of SymfonyProfilers
excludeFilter[]List of regular expression used to filter URI in profilers
profilerDataExportModeMode used to export data from Symfony Profiler (CLI or HTTP)
profilerPathLocal path to Symfony Profiler dumps
profilerProjectPathPath to Symfony project root
profilerUrlRootProfiler URL root
urlRoots[]List of URL roots of symfony profiles
  • enabled
    • Enabler for panel of SymfonyProfilers
    • Default Value: false
  • excludeFilter[]
    • List of regular expression used to filter URI in profilers
  • profilerDataExportMode
    • Mode used to export data from Symfony Profiler (CLI or HTTP)
    • Default Value: HTTP
  • profilerPath
    • Local path to Symfony Profiler dumps
    • Default Value: var/cache/dev/profiler
  • profilerProjectPath
    • Path to Symfony project root
  • profilerUrlRoot
    • Profiler URL root
    • Default Value: https://127.0.0.1:8000/_profiler/
  • urlRoots[]
    • List of URL roots of symfony profiles

Example

symfonyProfiler:
  enabled: false
  excludeFilter:
  - ''
  profilerDataExportMode: HTTP
  profilerPath: var/cache/dev/profiler
  profilerProjectPath: ''
  profilerUrlRoot: https://127.0.0.1:8000/_profiler/
  urlRoots:
  - https://127.0.0.1:8000

Class Style:

Properties

PropertyDescription
enabledEnabler for Php Class style configuration
rules[]Array of rules to apply
rules[].fqcns[]Fully Qualified class name or interface
rules[].styleStyle to apply if class implements one of the FQCNs
  • enabled
    • Enabler for Php Class style configuration
    • Example: true
    • Default Value: false
  • rules[]
    • Array of rules to apply
  • rules[].fqcns[]
    • Fully Qualified class name or interface
  • rules[].style
    • Style to apply if class implements one of the FQCNs

Example

styles:
  enabled: false
  rules:
  - fqcns:
    - ''
    style:
      foregroundColor: null
      backgroundColor: null
      fontStyles: []
      effect: null
      effectColor: null

CodeStylesSynchronization:

Properties

PropertyDescription
enabledEnabler for panel of Code style synchronization
styles[]Array if code styles to synchronize
styles[].styleAttributeCode style field property as in com.intellij.psi.codeStyle.CommonCodeStyleSettings
styles[].valuea boolean value true/false or an int value
  • enabled
    • Enabler for panel of Code style synchronization
    • Example: true
    • Default Value: false
  • styles[]
    • Array if code styles to synchronize
  • styles[].styleAttribute
    • Code style field property as in com.intellij.psi.codeStyle.CommonCodeStyleSettings
    • Example: ALIGN_MULTILINE_PARAMETERS_IN_CALLS
  • styles[].value
    • a boolean value true/false or an int value
    • Example: false

Example

codeStyleSynchronization:
  enabled: false
  styles:
  - styleAttribute: ALIGN_MULTILINE_PARAMETERS_IN_CALLS
    value: 'false'

Scripting Classes

Core

  • runAction**

    • actionId: String

  • runActionInEditor**

    • actionId: String

FileSystem

  • clearPath**

    • path: String

  • clearPath**

    • path: String
    • mustBeGitIgnored: Boolean

UI

  • alert**

    • message: String

  • alert**

    • message: String
    • delayInMs: Int

Configuration Tips

  1. Named Groups: Use regex named groups (?<name>...) in patterns and reference them with (?<name>...) (same expression) in targets for better readability and maintainability
  2. Regex Escaping: In YAML configuration, use double backslashes (\\) for namespace separators in regex patterns
  3. Local Overrides: Use .php-companion.local.* files for project-specific settings that shouldn't be committed
  4. Hot Reload: The plugin checks for configuration changes every 2 seconds
  5. Error Handling: Configuration errors will be displayed as notifications in the IDE
  6. Peers vs Associates:
    • Use peers for one-way navigation (source → target)
    • Use associates for bidirectional navigation (classA ↔ classB)
  7. Pattern Matching: Both peers and associates support complex regex patterns with multiple named groups

idea-plugin.name: MDLCode — Moodle™ Development
idea-plugin.description:
Provides comprehensive support for Moodle development in PhpStorm and IntelliJ IDEA.

Lookup, navigation and inspections

MDLCode highlights, validates and provides go-to-definition for Moodle entities across PHP, JavaScript, Mustache and Gherkin files:

  • Language strings — references in get_string(), new lang_string(), JS Str.getString(), etc.
  • Capabilities — references in has_capability(), require_capability(), etc.
  • Database tables — references in $DB methods, XMLDB files, persistent classes, etc.
  • Mustache templates — references in render_from_template(), JS Templates.render(), etc.
  • JavaScript modules — AMD module references in PHP and JS
  • Web services — external function definitions and AJAX usages
  • Callbacks — dynamic callback function implementations
  • Behat steps — step definition references in $this->execute() calls
  • Behat selectors — named selector references in PHP behat files and .feature files
  • Form elements — element type references in addElement() / createElement()

Usage counts are shown as inlay hints above entity definitions. Unused entities are highlighted. Find Usages works across file types.

Mustache template preview

Open a .mustache file and click the preview button to see it rendered with full Moodle theme, CSS, and helpers. The preview auto-refreshes on save.

Plugin navigation

MDLCode adds a "Moodle" panel that shows only plugin code. It can be filtered to hide standard plugins and show only add-ons.

File templates

MDLCode helps create standard Moodle files by populating them with initial contents, with suggestions for file and directory names.

Customise the copyright text and boilerplate in Settings | Editor | File and Code Templates | Other.

Wizards

MDLCode wizards guide you through creating new plugins, strings, capabilities and other Moodle entities.

Type resolution

MDLCode resolves types of Moodle's "magic" functions and global variables, for example:


    $renderer = $PAGE->get_renderer('mod_quiz'); // Instance of \mod_quiz\output\renderer
    self::getDataGenerator()->get_plugin_generator('mod_forum'); // Instance of \mod_forum_generator
    $ADMIN; // Instance of \admin_root (when used in settings.php files)
    $settings; // Instance of \admin_settingpage (when used in settings.php files)

Availability

MDLCode for PhpStorm is currently free of charge. Plugin homepage: mdlcode.dev.

Matrix group for discussions: !yERsyuEZvnhLzhFMaL:matrix.org

Issue tracker: https://github.com/lmscloud-io/mdlcode-jetbrains/issues

idea-plugin.name: Phalcon Route
idea-plugin.description:
Phalcon Route is a helper plugin created to easily type your routes using a helper method like route() from phalcon named routes.

This plugin can easily be used in any PHP, Twig or Vue based files.

Key features

  • Using a route config file to read your route names for autocompletion
  • You can specify a php attribute class that can be used to check route attribute name property for the routes names.
  • Autocomplete support in selected file extensions.
  • Optionally you can select to show route path text in autocomplete. [Requires index invalidation]
  • Allows the option to select the preferred quotes used in your application
  • Allows the option to choose any file extensions as long as the particular file is associated with either PHP or Twig or Vue file type.
  • Allows the option to set your own route function name when generating routes in associated files, auto generating the entire route code automatically.

Example of content inside a config router file

<?php

// 1st. method
$route = $router->add(
    '/admin/{year:[0-9]{4}}/{month:[0-9]{2}}/{day:[0-9]{2}}/{id:[0-9]{4}',
    'Invoices::view'
);

$route->setName('invoices-view');

// 2nd. method using chain method
$router->add(
    '/admin/{year:[0-9]{4}}/{month:[0-9]{2}}/{day:[0-9]{2}}/{id:[0-9]{4}',
    'Invoices::view'
)->setName('invoices-view');

return $router

Example of content inside a controller using php Attribute route class

<?php

use App\Attributes\Route;

class HomeController extends Controller
{
    #[Route('/', name: 'home')]
    public function homeAction(): void
    {
        $this->view->pick('home');
    }
}
