ActionShortcutDescription
Comment Function (Single-Line)Ctrl+Alt+/Comments each line with //
Comment Function (Multi-Line)Ctrl+Alt+Shift+/Wraps function in /* */

Both actions are also available via right-click menu under Function Comments.

To uncomment, use the same shortcut on an already-commented function.

idea-plugin.name: php-trait-inline-viewer
idea-plugin.description:
A PhpStorm plugin that allows you to view PHP classes with their traits expanded inline, making it easier to understand the complete structure of classes that use traits.

Features

  • Inline Trait Viewer: View PHP classes with all trait methods and properties merged inline
  • Context Menu Integration: Right-click in the editor to access "View PHP Trait Inline"
  • Read-only Preview: Opens a read-only preview of the merged class for safe viewing
  • Trait Detection: Automatically detects and expands all traits used by the selected class

Usage

  1. Open a PHP file containing a class that uses traits
  2. Right-click anywhere in the editor
  3. Select "View PHP Trait Inline" from the context menu
  4. A new editor tab will open showing the class with all trait methods and properties expanded inline

idea-plugin.name: Magento 1 Types
idea-plugin.description:
Provides enhanced IDE support for Magento 1.x projects in PhpStorm and other JetBrains IDEs.

Features:

  • Type Resolution — Resolves types for Mage::getModel(), Mage::getSingleton(), and Mage::helper() calls, enabling code completion and type inference.
  • Go-to-Declaration — Ctrl+Click navigation from Magento alias strings (e.g., 'catalog/product') directly to the corresponding PHP class.
  • Rewrite Support — Automatically detects and resolves class rewrites defined in config.xml files.
  • Rewrite Conflict Detection — Inspection that warns when multiple modules attempt to rewrite the same Magento class, helping prevent common configuration conflicts.

idea-plugin.name: Herd Manager
idea-plugin.description:
Herd Manager — Laravel Herd Integration for PhpStorm

Manage Laravel Herd site configuration directly from your IDE. Auto-detects Herd installation, manages herd.yml project config files, and provides link/unlink/secure operations via the Herd CLI — all without leaving PhpStorm.

Features

  • Auto-detection — Detects Laravel Herd installation on Windows, macOS, and Linux
  • Project configuration — Create and edit herd.yml with site name, PHP version, and HTTPS settings
  • Site linking — Link/unlink projects to Herd with one click
  • SSL management — Secure sites with HTTPS directly from the IDE
  • Status bar widget — See link status at a glance in the IDE status bar
  • Tool window panel — Full configuration UI in the right sidebar
  • Smart notifications — Prompts to configure or link on project open
  • Reactive updates — UI auto-refreshes when herd.yml changes externally

Quick Start

  1. Open a Laravel project in PhpStorm
  2. The plugin auto-detects Herd and checks for herd.yml
  3. If no config exists, a notification offers to Configure Now
  4. Set your site name, PHP version, and HTTPS preference
  5. Click Link Site to register with Herd

Access the tool window via View → Tool Windows → Herd Manager or the Herd icon in the right sidebar. Actions also available under Tools → Herd.

idea-plugin.name: DDLess - PHP Debugger
idea-plugin.description:
Debug PHP from inside PhpStorm — without Xdebug, php.ini tweaks, or port forwarding.

This plugin connects your IDE to the DDLess desktop app and turns the editor into a full PHP debugger. Set breakpoints in the gutter, step through code with F8/F7/F9, watch expressions evolve across a request, and inspect every HTTP request and response — all without configuring Xdebug or wrestling with session cookies.

What you get

  • Click-to-set breakpoints directly in the PHP gutter. Regular, conditional, logpoint, dumppoint and conditional-dump breakpoints, all editable from the right-click menu.
  • Step debugging with familiar shortcuts — F9 to continue, F8 to step over, F7 to step into, Shift+F8 to step out.
  • Inspector tool window with tabs for Variables, Watch (with a per-expression value-evolution timeline), Call Stack, Logs, function-call Waterfall, PHP Playground, and Request / Response details.
  • Bidirectional sync with the DDLess desktop app — toggle a breakpoint in PhpStorm and it appears in DDLess; toggle in DDLess and it appears in the IDE. Same for watches.
  • Any PHP runtime — local, WSL, Docker, or SSH. The desktop app handles runtime detection; the plugin just talks to it over a localhost WebSocket.

How it works

Install this plugin and the DDLess desktop app. Open a project in DDLess, click Listen, and the plugin's Connect button finds it automatically. Run your PHP request normally (an HTTP call, a CLI command, or a method test) — when it hits a breakpoint, PhpStorm pauses on that line, the Inspector lights up with the live state, and your F9 / F8 / F7 controls drive the runtime directly. No xdebug.client_host, no fragile session cookies, no separate Postman dance.

Requirements

  • DDLess desktop app with a Pro subscription — the plugin's handshake validates the license.
  • PhpStorm 2026.1 or newer.
  • PHP 7.4+ in your project's runtime.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.4.0

  • Fix: breakpoint gutter — a native breakpoint could sometimes get stuck and never clear. It's now reliably removed.
  • Updated for the latest PhpStorm: removed deprecated and internal API usage and moved the inline variable hints to the new declarative Inlay Hints API. No visible change — the plugin is now warning-free in the JetBrains Plugin Verifier.

0.3.0

  • Fix: Playground editor stayed read-only when the Inspector was opened while paused on a breakpoint. The pause-time editor lock fired before the Playground could opt out, so the input never accepted typing. It now stays writable in every session state.

0.2.0

Double-click expands a node to see its public, protected and private properties via reflection — no method calls, so accessors and Doctrine lazy-loading stay quiet.
  • Dumppoint results now open inside PhpStorm. When the plugin is connected, hitting a dumppoint opens a result dialog in the IDE (with the first level of every object already expanded) instead of bouncing to the DDLess desktop window.
  • Multi-line dumppoint editor — the breakpoint popup now takes one expression per line, so values containing commas (function calls, method chains) parse correctly.

0.1.0 — Initial release

  • WebSocket bridge to the DDLess desktop app with handshake + Pro license validation.

  • Step controls bound to F9 / F8 / F7 / Shift+F8 / Ctrl+F2.
  • Inspector tool window with Variables, Watch (with history timeline), Call Stack, Breakpoints, Logs, Trace waterfall, Playground, and Request / Response tabs.
  • Bidirectional breakpoint and watch synchronization with the desktop app.
  • Project, runtime and PHP-version chips on the project picker so you always know what you're attaching to.

idea-plugin.name: GraphQL PHP Bridge

Connects your GraphQL schema and your PHP resolvers, so the IDE understands them as a single codebase.

Navigation

Code Completion

Refactoring

Documentation

Configurable Format

  • The Create resolver method template is editable too, so the generated stub matches your GraphQL library (Webonyx, Lighthouse, GraphQLite, …).

idea-plugin.name: Hot Path Heatmap
idea-plugin.description:
Spot the expensive call before production does. Hot Path Heatmap statically scores every method call in the editor and lights up the ones that may trigger costly downstream work - database and HTTP calls, N+1 query loops, deep call chains - for PHP, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, Kotlin, Groovy, and Scala.

In source, every call reads as equally cheap: user.getId() looks exactly like billing.recalculate(user) - yet one is a field access and the other may fan out through services, loops, and a repository. And the classic performance killer hides in plain sight: a harmless-looking call inside a loop that turns into hundreds of queries. The heatmap makes that difference visible at a glance.

  • Resource-aware scoring. Database, HTTP/API, cache, message-queue, search, mail and filesystem operations anywhere down the call chain dominate the score - a real DB call is never buried under trivial fan-out.
  • N+1 detection. A resource operation reached inside a loop is amplified and called out, so the classic N+1 pattern surfaces as a top offender.
  • Explains itself. Every flagged call gets a colored underline, a cost score in the gutter, and a tooltip that says why - which downstream operations, at which loop depth.
  • One-click tuning, shared with your team. Wrongly flagged? Exclude that target from the tooltip or with Alt+Enter. Exclusions and custom resource keywords live in a committable hotpath-heatmap.json at your project root.
  • Zero setup. No profiler, no instrumentation, no test traffic - a static estimate built from the IDE's own indexes, computed in the background for open files only.

Free vs Pro. The full single-developer experience is free, and stays free: all languages, resource-first scoring and N+1 detection, underlines, gutter scores and tooltips, personal one-click exclusions and custom resource keywords, and the sensitivity and color presets (including a colorblind-safe ramp).

Pro (for teams) adds the committable, team-shared hotpath-heatmap.json - exclusions and keywords synced to the whole team via version control - plus a configurable team-config location. Pro licensing arrives with version 1.0.0; nothing is purchasable before then, and until then a present team file is simply ignored in free mode.

It is an early-warning system, not a runtime profiler: scores are heuristic estimates of downstream cost, designed to make you look twice at the right lines.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.8.2
  • Copy cleanup. Polished the wording across the plugin description, settings page, tooltips and other UI text. No behavior changes.
0.8.1
  • Fixed: editing a line could clear the heatmap on nearby lines. Method summaries were cached against a single project-wide modification counter, so any keystroke anywhere invalidated every cached summary at once; the next analysis pass then had to recompute the whole call graph cold, ran out of its per-file time budget, and left surrounding lines unmarked. Summaries are now cached per file, so an edit only invalidates that file's own summaries.
  • Fixed: toggling the heatmap off and back on didn't always restore it. The toggle now restarts the whole daemon in one shot instead of restarting file-by-file, which could race a page still reparsing and leave annotations missing until a later, unrelated edit brought them back.
0.8.0
  • N+1 detection no longer slips through shared helpers. When a resource op sits under a helper that was first reached outside a loop and then again from inside one, the loop amplification is now kept, so the N+1 is scored at its true weight instead of being under-counted. This was the most credibility-critical signal, and it is now accurate across all supported languages.
  • Fewer classifier false positives. Over-broad resource triggers were tightened so ordinary code stops reading as a database call: prepare now matches only the real JDBC methods, insert and select only score fully when a database class corroborates them, and class-name tokens (elastic / caffeine / cosmos / prisma / pdo) match on a word boundary so names like Elasticity, Caffeineless, prismatic and Dropdown no longer trip. Real database operations keep the full signal.
  • Tidier editor right-click menu. The two editor popup actions are now grouped under a single "Hot Path Heatmap" submenu instead of sitting as two loose top-level items.
0.7.2
  • Gutter chip scales with your editor font. The score chip in the gutter now tracks the editor font size instead of a fixed pixel size, so it stays crisp and readable at any zoom level or font setting.
  • More accurate PHP cost scoring. Deferred closures and event handlers are no longer counted as if they run inline, so functions that merely register callbacks stop being over-scored. Verb-based classification is sharper (prefix matching is now word-boundary aware), and loop depth is reported correctly for resource operations reachable through multiple paths.
0.7.1
  • Marketplace compliance. Removed the last internal-API usage (PluginManagerCore.getPlugin, internal since 2026.2 EAP - the plugin version is now baked in at build time) and a deprecated-for-removal list renderer. The plugin verifier is clean across 2025.3 → 2026.2 EAP for both PhpStorm and IntelliJ IDEA.
0.7.0
  • Public cost API for other plugins. New stable service com.hotpath.heatmap.api.CallableCostService: given a method/function declaration, costOf(...) returns its estimated downstream cost (same scale as the gutter chips) plus an absolute 0-4 heat level derived from your active sensitivity preset. Used by the Callscape plugin to color its caller-graph nodes; respects the enable toggle, preset, exclusions and all analysis limits, so it can never slow the IDE down.
0.6.2
  • False-positive fix. A cheap method on a scary-named class (e.g. a pure lookup on a *Mapper class) is no longer counted as a database/resource operation: when the called method's own body provably does nothing expensive (no calls, no loops), a class-name-only match is ignored. Real data-mapper methods (interface-declared, e.g. MyBatis) are still detected.
  • Compatibility. Replaced an API deprecated in 2026.1 IDEs, keeping the plugin verifier report clean on current and next-gen IDE versions.
0.6.1
  • Future-IDE readiness. Replaced all deprecated and internal platform API usages flagged by the plugin verifier, so the plugin stays clean on 2026.x IDE versions.
  • Listing. The plugin description now includes a clear Free vs Pro section.
0.6.0
  • Free/Pro groundwork. Hot Path Heatmap is preparing a freemium 1.0. Everything you use today stays free: all languages, resource-first scoring, N+1 detection, underlines, gutter scores, tooltips, exclusions, keywords, presets and settings. The team-shared committable hotpath-heatmap.json becomes the Pro feature - without a Pro license a present file is ignored (a one-time notice explains this). Pro licenses arrive with 1.0.0; until then nothing is purchasable.
  • Personal exclusions & keywords (free). One-click "not expensive" exclusions and custom resource keywords are stored per-developer (workspace-local), so tuning the heatmap never requires the team file.
  • Configurable team-config location (Pro). The json's path/filename is now configurable per project (e.g. .config/team-heatmap.json), shared with the team via .idea.
  • Color presets. Deep Sea (default) · colorblind-safe · subtle/monochrome - selectable in settings; accessibility is never paywalled.
  • Gutter tooltip. The gutter score chip now carries the full "why" explanation, so it stays reachable when IDE warnings preempt the inline tooltip.
  • Bugfixes (JS/TS): calls to object-literal function values and overloaded signatures now resolve and score; first write into a not-yet-existing config file no longer fails.
0.5.2
  • Bugfix (JS/TS): calls to methods declared as arrow-function class fields (findAll = () => { … }, the common modern TypeScript style) are now resolved and scored. Previously they resolved to a field rather than a function, so such calls were silently unscored.
0.5.1
  • Bugfix: excluding a resource op (from the tooltip link or Alt+Enter) now takes effect immediately - the marker updates and the score reloads. The config file is located more reliably (via the project root), and the re-highlight after a settings toggle or a hotpath-heatmap.json change no longer occasionally fails to repaint (e.g. a quick off→on of the toolbar toggle).
0.5.0
  • Resource-first scoring. The cost score now leads with the operations that actually make code expensive - database, HTTP/API, cache (Redis), message queue, search, mail and filesystem access - detected from broad, multi-ecosystem class / method keyword tables. These heavily outweigh structural signals (fan-out, call depth), so a real DB or API call no longer gets buried under a pile of trivial method calls.
  • N+1 detection. A resource op reached inside a loop is amplified, so the classic N+1 pattern surfaces as a top offender. The tooltip now leads with the detected resource operations (and their loop context), then the structural context.
  • One-click false positives. If a call is wrongly flagged, click exclude in its tooltip (or use Alt+Enter) to stop counting that specific target as a resource op - everywhere. Exclusions and your own extra keywords live in a committable hotpath-heatmap.json at your project root, shared with your team.
0.4.1
  • Redesigned settings page. The same options, reorganized around what you're actually deciding: a single Enable Hot Path Heatmap master switch that gates everything below it, a Highlighting group (flagging threshold as a plain "More findings … Fewer findings" selector, which markers to show, baseline markers), a Scope group (skip excluded / test folders), and two collapsed advanced sections - Analysis Limits (the safety caps) and Cost Model (which score terms are on). Clearer labels and inline help throughout. No behavior or defaults changed - only the panel's layout and wording.
0.4.0
  • Show scores for all calls. A new option (on by default, toggleable from the Tools and editor right-click menus, or Settings) also paints a barely-visible neutral gray marker and gutter score on every call whose target method makes at least one call of its own - not only the flagged Watch/Costly/Hot-path calls. Genuine leaf calls (targets that make no calls) stay unmarked. Turn it off to see only the flagged hot calls, as before.
0.3.1
  • Bugfix: changing settings (Sensitivity preset, "Highlight from severity", traversal limits or heuristic toggles) now re-highlights already-open files immediately on Apply/OK, instead of leaving stale colors until the next edit.
0.3.0
  • File-relative hot-path coloring. The Hot-path band now spreads across three shades within each file - from that file's mildest hot call to its worst - so a "very high" and an "extremely high" call site are finally told apart (they used to share one flat color). Watch and Costly keep a fixed, absolute color in every file, and the gutter still shows the absolute score, so you keep a cross-file comparison. Colors move to a 5-level deep-sea ramp (teal → cyan → blue → violet → magenta); near-equal scores share a shade.
0.2.0
  • Added support for the JVM language family - Java, Kotlin, Groovy and Scala - via a single UAST-based analyzer, alongside the existing PHP and JavaScript/TypeScript support. Higher-order iteration methods (forEach, map, filter, …) are treated as loop levels, the JVM analog of a foreach body. Each language stays an optional dependency, so the plugin still installs and runs in PhpStorm, WebStorm, IntelliJ IDEA, and any other IntelliJ-based IDE, activating whichever supported languages are present.
0.1.17
  • Theme-aware severity colors that adapt automatically between light and dark themes (no restart). Three levels - Watch (teal), Costly (blue), Hot path (violet) - plus unmarked trivial calls. Every level uses the same underline weight (severity is carried by color), and the underline now sits a little below the text so it clears the descenders. The gutter score sits in a faint tinted chip. The hues deliberately avoid the yellow/orange/red inspection palette so a hot call reads as expensive, not as a warning.
0.1.16
  • Added a Sensitivity setting (Low / Medium / High) that controls how expensive a call site must be before it's flagged. Higher presets raise every band cutoff so fewer, only-costlier call sites light up. The previous thresholds are now the "Low" preset; the new default is Medium, so the heatmap is less noisy out of the box.
0.1.15
  • New icon set: refreshed plugin icon and toolbar toggle (on/off) icons.
0.1.14
  • Minimum IDE is now 2025.3. The toggle now uses the non-deprecated daemon-restart API (the old form was deprecated in 2025.3), so the plugin no longer reports a deprecated-API usage on 2025.3+. (If you are on 2024.2-2025.2, stay on 0.1.13.)
0.1.13
  • Made the "very high" score clearly distinct from "high": "high" is now a definite orange and "very high" a pure red, so the top two severity bands no longer look alike.
0.1.12
  • PHP and JavaScript are now optional dependencies. The plugin installs in any IntelliJ-based IDE (not only PhpStorm) and activates whichever of the two languages is present. This fixes the "binary incompatible - package com.jetbrains.php not found" error reported when verifying against IDEs that don't bundle PHP (e.g. IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm).
0.1.11
  • Added back an inline marker: a bold straight underline on the call name (distinct from the wavy underlines IDE diagnostics use), alongside the gutter score. It is emitted on the lowest highlighting layer, so any warning/error on the same token always takes precedence - the marker is suppressed there rather than doubling up or painting over the diagnostic.
0.1.10
  • The estimate now shows only as a colored score badge in the editor gutter - the inline marker on the code is gone. With nothing painted on the code text, the gutter number can use an intuitive warm yellow → orange → red heat ramp without ever colliding with IDE warnings or errors.
0.1.9
  • Call-site marker is now a purple background "heat tint" that deepens as the estimated cost rises - the literal heatmap look. It uses a single purple hue and no underline/box, so it never collides with IDE warnings or errors (which use wavy underlines and yellow/red).
0.1.8
  • Call-site marker is now a full boxed outline, and the palette moved to a cool blue → magenta → purple ramp (no warm yellow/orange/red tones, which read as warnings).
0.1.7
  • New call-site marker: a dotted underline instead of a solid box, so it no longer reads as an error. The severity ramp now tops out at purple (amber → orange → magenta → purple) rather than an alarming red.
0.1.6
  • Fixed call sites in TypeScript files being analyzed and painted twice (doubled gutter score and outline). TypeScript is now handled once, via its JavaScript base language.
0.1.5
  • Added a plugin icon (shown in the Plugins list and on the Marketplace).
0.1.4
  • Exclusion now follows the IDE's own directory marks instead of matching path strings: folders marked Excluded and Test Sources Root (via Mark Directory as…) are skipped by default, each toggleable in settings. Built-in/library code is always skipped.
  • Aligned the toolbar flame icon with the Run/Debug controls.
0.1.3
  • Added a show/hide toggle button to the main toolbar (next to Run/Debug), also available in the Tools and editor right-click menus. A lit flame means the heatmap is on; a slashed flame means it is off.
  • While hidden, no cost scores are calculated at all.
  • Expanded the plugin description with the motivation behind it.
0.1.2
  • Removed the upper IDE-compatibility bound so the plugin installs on 2024.2 and all future PhpStorm builds. Verified compatible against the 2024.2 and 2025.3 (253) lines.
0.1.1
  • Listing metadata: license, vendor, and description updates.
0.1.0
  • Initial release.
  • Static hot-path heatmap for PHP and JavaScript/TypeScript.
  • Severity-colored marker, gutter cost score, and an explanatory tooltip.
  • Configurable heuristics, traversal limits, and vendor/test exclusion.

idea-plugin.name: PhpDebugTools
idea-plugin.description: PhpDebugTools provides a local method invocation workbench for ThinkPHP projects in PhpStorm, including project detection, runtime installation, and controller or service method debug entry points.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changed

Added

Fixed

  • 修复首次从编辑器跳转时方法未预填，以及扫描刷新覆盖当前选择的问题。
  • 修复编辑器跳转后的当前方法未显示在可编辑下拉框中的问题。
  • 修复驼峰形式的路由动作与控制器方法的 ApiAuth 匹配。

idea-plugin.name: PHP Typehints Extra
idea-plugin.description: A PhpStorm plugin that adds extra type-hinting capabilities to PHP code.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • PHPDoc generics native-like view: folds @template docblocks and renders them as inline generic signatures (e.g. function foo<T of Foo>(T $p): T), with a typed handler to generate the docblock from <T of Foo> syntax. Toggle in Editor → General → Code Folding.
  • PHP type inlay hints (php.types): inferred-type hints for variable assignments, foreach values/keys, function/method return types, and multi-line method chains, each independently toggleable.

idea-plugin.name: navibus
idea-plugin.description:
Navigation from a PHP class to its handler methods — methods marked with some attribute and accepting the class as a parameter.

Works both as a gutter icon and via the keyboard — Navigate | Related Symbol (Ctrl+Alt+Home).

Intended to be useful for various message bus implementations.

The target attribute FQN is configured per project in Settings | Tools | Navibus.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Validation on the Settings | Tools | Navibus page: leaving Handler attribute FQN empty while Match handlers by parameter type is off is now flagged as an error and blocks Apply — that combination finds no handlers, so no navigation would be shown.
  • Class references inside extends/implements clauses no longer get a gutter marker. Previously a line like class Foo implements Message could show a second marker on the Message reference, merging into the class icon and adding a confusing extra target — most visible in Ignore handler attribute mode, where the base type almost always has a method accepting it.

Added

  • Message class filter by attribute: a new Message attribute FQNs field (one FQN per line) on the Settings | Tools | Navibus page. A class is treated as a message if it is annotated with any of these attributes on the class declaration itself.
  • Match handlers by parameter type mode: a new checkbox on the Settings | Tools | Navibus page (placed under Handler attribute FQN) for projects where handlers are not annotated. When enabled, a handler is any public method that accepts the message as a parameter, ignoring the handler attribute. Enabling it disables the Handler attribute FQN field; if no message filter is set, a warning is shown, since the mode produces no markers without a filter.

Changed

  • Custom gutter icon: the handler navigation marker now uses the plugin's own icon instead of the platform's "implemented method" icon.
  • The message class filter is now a set of rules combined with OR: a class gets the gutter icon if it matches the Message base type FQN (subtype rule) or the new Message attribute FQNs (attribute rule). Both fields empty disables the filter and keeps the previous behavior.

idea-plugin.name: Hyperf Base
idea-plugin.description:
Hyperf Base provides IDE support for the Hyperf PHP framework in PhpStorm, including route controller completion & navigation, config key indexing, translation key indexing, environment variable completion, and validation rule completion & hover docs.
Issues

功能特性

  • 路由：Router::get/post/put/patch/delete/options/addRoute 的控制器补全与跳转 —— 兼容 Hyperf 3.x 的 @method 魔术 Router 写法
  • API 路由：Search Everywhere 新增 "Routes" 标签页搜索路由并跳转控制器方法；路由方法名旁 API 图标点击生成 HTTP Client 请求到 Scratch 文件 —— 需安装 tw2066/api-docs 组件生成 runtime/container/http.json
  • 配置：config() / ConfigInterface::get/has 配置键的索引、补全与跳转 —— 支持 Hyperf 3.1+ 的点号配置文件（sub/a.php → sub.a，a.b.php → a.b）
  • 翻译：trans() / __() / TranslatorInterface::trans() 翻译键的索引、补全与跳转（需安装 hyperf/translation）
  • 环境变量：env() 环境变量键的补全与跳转（读取项目根目录 .env 文件）
  • 验证规则：验证规则字符串（required|max:255）的补全与悬停中文文档 —— 支持 FormRequest::rules()、ValidatorFactory::make()/validate() 规则数组、$scenes 值及 DTO 注解 #[Validation(...)]（需安装 hyperf/validation 或 hyperf/dto）
  • Hyperf 菜单：主菜单栏代码生成（devtool gen:*）与常用命令（describe:routes、migrate、start 等），在内置 Terminal 执行，支持 WSL 环境
  • 命令行标记运行：Hyperf\Command\Command 子类类名旁的运行按钮，点击在 Terminal 执行命令，有参数先弹输入框
  • XXL-JOB 标记运行：#[XxlJob] 注解的 Job 类/方法名旁的运行按钮，点击弹窗输入 --params 后在 Terminal 执行 execute:xxl-job（需安装 hyperf/xxl-job-incubator）

安装与设置

  • 安装插件后，在 Settings > Languages & Frameworks > PHP > Hyperf Base 中按项目启用
  • 未使用默认目录结构时，可配置翻译目录
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• DI 接口绑定：优先读 apidocs 组件启动时生成的 runtime/container/di-map.json（运行时真实容器映射，覆盖闭包工厂等静态分析收不到的绑定）；class 为空的映射点击链接打开工厂定义文件；文件缺失或未收录时回退原静态分析
  • 设置项 "Http Json Path" 改为 "Json Path Dir"：由 http.json 文件路径改为 apidocs JSON 目录（http.json、di-map.json 同目录），默认 runtime/container（留空按默认处理）；旧设置值失效后回退默认目录
  • API 路由标记：生成请求按 http.json 的 OpenAPI 参数定义补齐骨架——requestBody 生成 JSON body（解析 $ref DTO、嵌套对象/数组，样例值按 example > default > enum > 类型占位），query/path 参数拼入 URL；仅 2026.2+ 生效，低版本保持裸请求行
  • http.json / di-map.json 读取加 1s 复查间隔：间隔内直接用缓存（含文件不存在态），避免行标记逐元素回调反复 stat 磁盘
  • DI 绑定跳转不再用 refreshAndFindFileByPath 兜底（同步 VFS 刷新跑在 EDT 上会卡 UI）；行标记锚点改为叶子元素，消除平台 Performance warning

idea-plugin.name: Hyperf Query
idea-plugin.description:
This plugin provides database-integration for the Hyperf query builder. When used together with the IDE's data-source tool (DataGrip database tool), it delivers auto-completion, unknown-element validation, Ctrl-Click navigation and hover documentation for schemas, tables, views and columns.

本插件为 Hyperf 查询构建器提供数据库集成,配合 IDE 的数据源(DataGrip 数据库工具)为 schema、表、视图与列提供自动补全、未知元素检查、Ctrl+Click 跳转与悬停文档。

文档

功能特性

  • 查询构建器与 Schema 构建器方法中的 schema、表、视图与列名补全
  • 迁移(migration)文件内的补全
  • 未知数据库元素检查
  • 表别名支持
  • 构建器方法可从模型解析表名
  • 模型 relation 闭包方法的关联表名解析
  • 与数据库元素建立文本链接,支持跳转与重构
  • 查询构建器列参数的悬停/快速文档 —— 在 where()、select()、orderBy() 等方法的列名上悬停,可查看解析出的列类型、是否可空、默认值与注释;表名悬停显示轻量摘要(schema + 表注释),而非完整 DDL
  • 模型属性的列名补全、Ctrl+Click 跳转与悬停文档 —— $fillable、$guarded、$hidden、$visible、$dates 数组值与 $casts 数组键基于模型表(来自 $table 属性或类名约定)解析;$casts 数组值补全 Hyperf 属性转换类型(integer、datetime、decimal:<digits>、date:<format> 等)
  • 模型 $table 属性的表名补全、Ctrl+Click 跳转与未知表检查,作用域限定在模型的 $connection(遵守 schema 与表前缀)
  • Db::select()、Db::update() 等 Hyperf\DbConnection\Db 带 $bindings 方法的 SQL 命名占位符(:name)补全与跳转 —— 绑定数组键基于查询字符串中的占位符补全(name 与 :name 两种写法均可),Ctrl+Click 键名可跳转到 SQL 中的占位符
  • config/autoload/databases.php 中的数据库连接名在 Db::connection() / Schema::connection() 与模型 $connection 属性中补全,支持 Ctrl+Click 跳转到配置项与未知连接名检查告警;使用指定连接的链式调用(或模型)上的表/列补全、引用解析与检查都限定在该连接配置的 database schema 内(未指定时回退 default 连接),表名遵守连接的 prefix
  • 原生 SQL 片段(selectRaw()、whereRaw()、orderByRaw()、havingRaw()、groupByRaw()、Db::raw() 等)中的简单列表达式获得列补全、跳转与检查 —— 支持逗号分隔列表与带连接表前缀的表/别名引用;复杂 SQL(函数、算术运算)保持跳过,避免误报
  • 可配置表前缀与数据源过滤;设置面板顶部提供全局开关,可整体停用插件功能

注意事项

  1. 必须先配置 IDE 数据源:所有补全信息来自 Database 工具窗口中的数据源元数据。没有配置数据源,或数据源未刷新加载 schema,插件不会有任何补全。
  2. vendor 必须被索引:插件通过 PSI 类型解析判断调用链是否属于 Hyperf\Database\*,如果 vendor 目录被排除或依赖未安装,所有功能失效。
  3. 表前缀别重复设置:连接配置(databases.php 的 prefix)优先于插件全局 Table prefix,二者不会叠加;全局前缀只作用于未配置 prefix 的连接。
  4. env() 解析有限:连接配置中 env('DB_DATABASE', 'test') 只取默认值,插件不会读取真实 .env 文件。线上/本地 schema 不同时,以默认值为准或让配置写死。
  5. 多数据源项目建议开过滤:否则补全列表会包含所有数据源的所有 schema,既慢又干扰。
  6. 表悬停只看摘要:宽表的完整 DDL 渲染慢,所以悬停只显示表注释;需要 DDL 请 Ctrl+Click 跳转到 Database 工具窗口。
  7. 修改数据源后:补全基于 IDE 缓存,数据库结构变更后记得在数据源上 Refresh。

idea-plugin.name: XOOPS Support
idea-plugin.description:
XOOPS Support — PhpStorm / IntelliJ helper for XOOPS 2.5 / 2.7 / 4.0 Core and module development.

1.0.0 Alpha 3 — Goffy field-report fixes; language-constant navigation; unregistered templates; UNICODE dtype.

idea-plugin.name: PHP Inlay Hints
idea-plugin.description: Show resolved PHP constant values as inline hints in PhpStorm.
idea-plugin.change-notes: • Polished inline hint rendering and packaging metadata.

idea-plugin.name: Laravel Warrant
idea-plugin.description: Syntax highlighting for the Warrant authorization rule language. Highlights standalone .warrant files and, more importantly, the DSL embedded in PHP: heredocs/nowdocs labelled WARRANT, and strings wherever rule text is expected, such as warrant('...') and Warrant::parse('...').
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 0.5.0 — Highlight Warrant inside PHP wherever rule text is expected: the first argument of warrant(), Warrant::parse(), WarrantSyntax::parse(), WarrantParser::parse() and ->ifRaw() / ->orIfRaw(), and a string returned from rules() or a #[DerivedCondition] / #[RuleTemplate] method.

idea-plugin.name: PHP File Inclusion Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on include, include_once, require, or require_once whose path argument directly references a PHP superglobal ($_GET, $_POST, $_REQUEST, $_COOKIE). This is the textbook Local/Remote File Inclusion (LFI/RFI) anti-pattern -- an attacker can point this at an arbitrary file via directory traversal, or a remote URL if allow_url_include is on.

Confirmed real gap: "PHP Inspections (EA Extended)" has a related but distinct inspection -- it only flags a relative include path that depends on the include_path configuration setting, not a path built directly from a superglobal. Confirmed by reading its own documentation before building this.

100% static text analysis -- a regex-based line scanner, not a real PHP parser, so it works whether the PHP plugin is installed or not.

Stated honestly: v0.1 is deliberately narrow -- only flags a superglobal referenced directly in the include/require argument, the least ambiguous and highest-confidence shape. A path built from an intermediate variable that was itself assigned from a superglobal several lines earlier isn't traced (real data-flow analysis, out of scope for a text scanner).

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: PHP Function Injection Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on call_user_func( or call_user_func_array( whose function-name argument directly references a PHP superglobal ($_GET, $_POST, $_REQUEST, $_COOKIE). This is the textbook Function Injection anti-pattern: OWASP's own guidance documents that "when an attacker passes a function name with user input to call_user_func, it can lead to remote code execution by passing the system function with arbitrary commands" -- an attacker who controls the callable name can invoke any built-in function reachable by that call.

Confirmed real gap: "PHP Inspections (EA Extended)" (one of the most widely used PHP inspection plugins on Marketplace) does not cover function injection detection anywhere in its documented security feature list -- confirmed by reading it before building this.

100% static text analysis -- a regex-based line scanner, not a real PHP parser, so it works whether the PHP plugin is installed or not.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only flags a superglobal referenced within the call's own parentheses on the same line. A function name built from an intermediate variable assigned from a superglobal several lines earlier isn't traced (real data-flow analysis, out of scope for a text scanner).

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: PHP Open Redirect Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on a header('Location: ...') call whose argument is built directly from a PHP superglobal ($_GET, $_POST, $_REQUEST, $_COOKIE). This is the textbook Open Redirect anti-pattern (CWE-601): an attacker crafts a link to the trusted site that redirects the victim to an attacker-controlled domain, commonly used for phishing since the initial URL still shows the trusted host. OWASP's own "Unvalidated Redirects and Forwards" guidance documents this as a real, well-known vulnerability class.

Confirmed real gap: "PHP Inspections (EA Extended)" (one of the most widely used PHP inspection plugins on Marketplace) does not cover open redirect detection anywhere in its documented security feature list -- confirmed by reading it before building this.

100% static text analysis -- a regex-based line scanner, not a real PHP parser, so it works whether the PHP plugin is installed or not.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only flags a header( call whose argument text contains both Location: and a direct superglobal reference on the same line. A redirect built from an intermediate variable assigned from a superglobal several lines earlier isn't traced (real data-flow analysis, out of scope for a text scanner).

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: PHP Shell Injection Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on eval(, exec(, shell_exec(, system(, passthru(, or popen( whose argument is a double-quoted string with $variable interpolation, or a concatenation with a variable, rather than a static literal. PHP's own official manual states this for eval(): "pay special attention not to pass any user provided data into it without properly validating it beforehand" -- the same class of risk applies to the shell-executing functions, all of which run their string argument through a real system shell.

Confirmed real gap: "PHP Inspections (EA Extended)" (one of the most widely used PHP inspection plugins on Marketplace) covers unserialize(), weak crypto, SSL bypass, and several other security patterns, but not eval()/exec()/shell_exec()/ system() with dynamic arguments -- confirmed by reading its own documented security feature list before building this.

100% static text analysis -- a regex-based line scanner, not a real PHP parser, so it works whether the PHP plugin is installed or not.

Stated honestly: v0.1 doesn't trace whether the interpolated value actually originates from untrusted input, so interpolation of a hardcoded constant is a possible (rare) false positive. A call whose argument is entirely a static literal is correctly never flagged.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: PHP SQL Injection Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on mysqli_query(, ->query(, or ->exec( (the mysqli/PDO query methods) whose SQL string argument contains $variable interpolation or a concatenation with a variable, rather than a prepared-statement placeholder. This is the textbook SQL injection anti-pattern: prepared statements exist precisely so the SQL text and the data are sent to the database separately -- string-building a query defeats that protection entirely.

Confirmed real gap: "PHP Inspections (EA Extended)" (one of the most widely used PHP inspection plugins on Marketplace) covers unserialize(), weak crypto, extract()/parse_str(), and several other security patterns, but not SQL injection through query method parameters -- confirmed by reading its own documented security feature list before building this.

100% static text analysis -- a regex-based line scanner, not a real PHP parser, so it works whether the PHP plugin is installed or not.

Stated honestly: v0.1 doesn't trace whether the interpolated value actually originates from untrusted input, so interpolation of a hardcoded constant is a possible (rare) false positive. A call whose argument is entirely a static literal, or built with ?/named placeholders and a separate bind_param/execute call, is correctly never flagged.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: Latte+
idea-plugin.description:
Latte+ gives PhpStorm first-class support for the Latte templating engine and the Nette Framework. It reads the Latte syntax and the HTML, PHP, JavaScript and CSS embedded in the same file at the same time, so completion, navigation, inspections and refactoring behave the way they do in a language the IDE knows natively.

Works with Latte 3.x and PHP 8.1+ in PhpStorm 2023.3 and newer.

  • Documentation: features, configuration and a comparison of what Latte+ handles
  • Issue tracker: report a bug or request a feature
  • Licence terms: EULA

It knows the types in your template

  • {varType}, {templateType}, {parameters}, foreach item types and $object->method() chains feed one type model, so completion on your own variables knows what they hold.
  • Modern PHPDoc types are understood instead of rejected: generics such as list<Product>, array shapes, int<0, 100>, class-string, union and intersection types.
  • Hover documentation, parameter info and inlay hints show what a variable, filter or tag argument actually is.

HTML, JavaScript and CSS stay themselves

  • HTML completion and inspections work inside the template, n:attributes included, without false "tag is never closed" errors.
  • JavaScript and CSS inside <script>, <style>, style="" and on*="" behave as in a plain HTML file; a Latte tag in the middle does not break them.
  • Completion, inspections and refactoring work inside {php} and {do}, with the tag's strict or permissive mode detected for you.

Navigation and refactoring that cross files

  • Ctrl+click an {include} or {embed} to land on the block it renders; rename a block and every caller follows.
  • Ctrl+B on {link Product:detail} or n:href offers both places the destination stands for, with the action's template first and the presenter method second.
  • Find Usages on a template parameter lists every place that passes it, including the {include} arguments. On an optional parameter that tells you who actually sets it, not merely where the template is used.

Nette integration

  • {control} completes from your createComponent factories and from the component's render methods.
  • {link} and n:href resolve presenters, actions, signals and components, with the presenter mapping read from your NEON config.
  • {form}, {input} and {label} know the fields of the form they render; {snippet} and {snippetArea} are understood.
  • Tags, filters and functions from your own Latte extensions are found by scanning the project, so there is no separate configuration to keep in sync.

Inspections that stay quiet

What Latte+ reports is measured against what the Latte engine itself accepts, in both directions: a template Latte compiles stays clean, and a template Latte would refuse is reported, usually with a fix on the spot. The known limitations page lists the edge cases that are still open.

Comfort while you type

  • Sticky lines keep the enclosing {if}, {foreach} or {block} pinned to the top of the editor as you scroll.
  • Renaming an HTML tag updates its pair as you type, and a closing tag is offered where you need one.
  • Completion opens on its own after {, ' and #; Enter, Tab, End, Backspace and comment toggling behave the way the surrounding syntax calls for.
  • Structure view, breadcrumbs, code folding and a formatter that keeps Latte tags and HTML in one consistent shape.
  • Colors for Latte tags and n:attributes are configurable in the color scheme.

Licensing

Latte+ is a paid plugin with a free 30-day trial. Individual and organization licenses are available; see the Pricing section on this page.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Tag completion offers {else} inside {try}, {first}, {last}, {sep} and {ifchanged}.
  • On a Latte 3 project, a Latte tag on the other side of an HTML comment boundary than its pair is reported, because Latte 3 compiles a comment as a fragment of its own: a closer inside a comment whose opener is outside, a clause or a {case} inside a comment of a pair outside it, and a pair opened inside a comment and closed outside it. Hidden conditional comments such as <!--[if mso]>` are checked the same way. A comment with no `--> is reported where it starts. Latte 2 compiles all of these shapes, so nothing is reported there, nor on a project whose Latte version is unknown.
  • An {include} whose # marker is followed by a space and the word from, with nothing behind it, gets a weak warning that a block name between the marker and from is probably missing. Latte reads that line as a block named from, which is almost never what a half-written from-clause meant.
  • The name in n:block, n:define and n:snippetArea is highlighted as a block declaration, the same way it is in the braced tag.

Changed

  • On a Latte 3 project, closing-tag completion offers only tags opened on the same side of an HTML comment boundary as the caret.
  • {case} and {default} have to stand directly inside {switch}; one nested in another tag of the switch body is reported, and so is {default} with arguments inside a switch, where it is the clause and not the variable tag.
  • Custom paired tags are matched by name, so a closing tag of a custom pair with no opener is reported as unexpected, and an opener with no closer as unclosed. A tag registered as unpaired no longer waits for a closer.
  • {define name($x)} is read the way Latte reads it: the parenthesis makes the name a function call, so $x is not a parameter and is reported as undefined. Declare parameters as {define name, $x} or {define name $x}.
  • A dynamic snippet name that Latte can only know at run time gets the advice to wrap it in {snippetArea} in n:snippet too, and when it reads an array item such as {snippet $a['k']}.
  • The |noescape check inside HTML comments (Latte 3.1 and newer) also covers hidden conditional comments, no longer counts the text behind the first --> as part of the comment, and stays silent in text, JavaScript, CSS and iCal templates, where <!-- is ordinary text.
  • Backspace on an empty line inside {first}, {last}, {sep} and {ifchanged} unindents to the level of the tag, as it does in {foreach}, because an {else} may follow.
  • Quick documentation of {else} lists the tags that really take it, now including {try}, {first}, {last}, {sep} and {ifchanged}, and no longer {switch}.

Fixed

  • {else} inside {first}, {last}, {sep} and {ifchanged} is no longer reported as an error, and the rest of the template is checked again. A second {else} in these tags is reported as a duplicate, like in {if}.
  • A paired tag written whole inside an HTML comment, such as <!-- {if $a}…{/if} -->, no longer breaks the rest of the template, and a comment that holds a closing tag or a clause no longer stops the plugin from checking everything below it.
  • {else}, {elseif} or {elseifset} with no tag around them is reported as an unexpected tag, the way Latte reports it, instead of with an internal parser message that also switched off the rest of the template.
  • {rollback} is accepted anywhere inside {try}, also nested in another tag, and in an element with n:try. Completion inserts it at the indent of the surrounding code instead of at the column of {try}.
  • {l}, {r} and {} inside an HTML comment are read as literal braces, not reported as unknown tags.
  • The word from in the arguments of an {include} no longer breaks the tag: a call such as Foo::from($id), an array key or an argument named from is an ordinary name again. Until now the tag failed to parse and every tag below it lost its colours and checks. from separates a block from its template only between the target and the first argument, which is where Latte reads it.
  • A member read whose name is computed in braces, such as $item->{$name}, $item?->{$name} or Foo::{$name}, is no longer a syntax error.
  • A block name may be any expression Latte accepts, behind the block keyword and the # marker in {include} and {embed}, and in {block}, {define}, {snippet}, n:define, n:block and n:snippet: a property, an array item, a class constant, a call or an operator, such as {include block $item->name from 'x.latte'}, {define Foo::BAR} or {snippet $a + $b}. These were syntax errors, which on a paired tag took its body and the rest of the template with it.
  • {include block} and {include block, 5} include the block named block, as in Latte, instead of being a syntax error. The name is checked for a missing block and Ctrl+B follows it.
  • A block name glued with - or /, such as {block a/b} or {include block a/b}, is one name: it is no longer a syntax error, it is painted as one name, Ctrl+B and the missing-block check work over the whole of it, and block completion offers it whole. {include #content-2} now includes the block content-2 instead of content with -2 as an argument. An unmarked {include a/b} stays a file, as in Latte.
  • Holding Ctrl over a block name glued from several parts underlines the whole name instead of one part at a time.
  • A block named with a Latte keyword is highlighted and checked like any other: {include block from from 'x.latte'} and {include #from} now report a block that does not exist and navigate to one that does. The # marker followed by a space and from is painted as a block name too, and Ctrl+B follows it.
  • A block included from a template that only run time can tell, such as {include inner from $paths['layout']}, is no longer reported as missing, and the "Did you mean" fix no longer suggests the very name it reports.
  • A block name built by concatenation behind the block keyword, the # marker or a from-clause no longer offers Ctrl+B to a file on its pieces.
  • With the Czech language pack, every inspection, settings page, quick fix and notification is in Czech, instead of mixing in English wherever a translation was missing. The Czech missing-asset message shows the directory that was searched instead of always naming www/assets/.
  • PHP class names in the settings texts keep their backslashes, so Latte\Extension no longer shows as LatteExtension.
  • The notification and the preview of the "Add to custom Latte extensions" quick fix spell the attribute category as n:attribute, without a space.

idea-plugin.name: Lerd
idea-plugin.description:
Manage your Lerd local PHP environment from the IDE. The project you open resolves to exactly one Lerd site, and its logs, PHP version, workers, services, queries and dumps come with it, without a browser tab.

In the status bar

The site's domain and PHP version, greyed out when Lerd is stopped and not drawn at all for a project Lerd does not know. Click it to open the site, restart it, turn HTTPS on or off, pause it, switch PHP version or open the dashboard.

In the tool window

  • Site — domain, framework, branch and path, the PHP and Node version pickers, a toggle per worker and a row per service, laid out in columns that reflow as the window narrows. Services open in the IDE's own Database tool window on this site's database, or as a client shell.
  • Logs — a framework log collapsed into one row per distinct error with how often it happened, and a live tail for PHP-FPM, every worker, every service and nginx. Both are IDE consoles, so a path in a stack trace is one click from the line that threw it.
  • N+1 & Slow — the queries worth fixing, read from real captured traffic rather than from the code, worst first, each linked to the application line it came from and openable as a runnable SQL scratch.
  • Dumps — everything the site captured, split into the lenses the dashboard uses: dumps, queries, jobs, views, mail, cache, events, HTTP, logs, exceptions and messages. Stack traces are read rather than printed, with the first frame outside vendor/ pulled to the top.

Elsewhere in the IDE

The site's containers appear in the Services window with a terminal and a log to follow. The PHP language level, the CLI interpreter and the PHP server entry for Xdebug all follow whatever Lerd serves the site with.

Everything happens over loopback to the Lerd already running as your user. No account, no token, no telemetry, and nothing contacted but your own machine.

Requires Lerd running on the same machine.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.1

The plugin is named Lerd rather than lerd, everywhere the IDE shows it.

0.1.0

First release.

  • Status bar widget with the site's domain, PHP version and quick actions
  • Site, Logs, N+1 & Slow and Dumps in one tool window
  • Containers in the Services window, with a terminal into each
  • PHP language level, CLI interpreter and Xdebug server follow the site
  • Git worktrees resolve to their parent site plus the branch

idea-plugin.name: CN Comment Lens
idea-plugin.description:
Show Chinese comments for fields, constants and method parameters right at the end of code lines — no more jumping between files just to read a comment.

The plugin's Chinese name is 了然 (liǎorán), from 一目了然: "clear at a glance".

One package works in both IntelliJ IDEA and PhpStorm. Supported languages: Java and Kotlin (IDE-bundled plugins), PHP and Go (optional dependencies — a missing language plugin simply disables that language, the rest keeps working).

📖 User guide (Chinese): CN Comment Lens 使用说明
How to use every feature — inline comments, Project-view file comments, coverage inspections & report, and database schema lookup; its live-database chapter keeps probe / snapshot / scan apart: what each one reads, what triggers it, and where the result shows up.

Features

  • Inline Chinese comments: comments of fields, enum entries, class constants, method & constructor parameters rendered as line-end inlays; they never enter the text buffer
  • Project view file comments: a description appended after file names
  • Adjustable display & style: hint scope (current line / current method / whole file, default whole file), large-file guard (default 5000 lines) with a banner at the top of the editor, separate fonts / sizes / colors for identifiers and comments, assign symbol, separator, truncation length; click an identifier segment to jump to its declaration (cross-file works too), and lines with many hints collapse into a "+N ▸" chip that opens the full list
  • Comment coverage inspections & report: warnings for classes / public members missing a Chinese comment, with a one-click comment-skeleton fix; right-click a folder in the project view (or use the Tools menu) to scan with directory / package filters and export a Markdown report
  • Database schema lookup (ThinkPHP / MyBatis): string column names in query builders and column references in mapper XML (with or without a table alias) show the column comment and type — from the project's own .sql DDL files (📦) or from the data sources connected in the IDE Database tool window (🛢; data source strategy: .sql only / database only / mixed; zero credentials, .sql side works offline). Every line of a mapper statement also renders its columns' comments as line-end inlays; join qualified columns, column-name completion (with table comment and source), hover shows table & column type, a click goes to the CREATE TABLE line or the generated read-only DDL view; live snapshots have a configurable refresh interval and liveness probe (manual Probe now / Refresh now, optional per-database filtering — the candidate list mirrors what you introspected in the Database tool window and leaves out information_schema / mysql / performance_schema / sys); deterministic two-pass merge (ALTER always overrides CREATE) with cross-file comment conflicts arbitrated and surfaced on hover; in PHP query builders, Alt+Enter on a lookup miss opens the settings, refreshes the live source or rescans .sql
  • Hover the full comment (Java / PHP / Kotlin / Go): hovering a reference or call site (obj.getPayNo(), an assignment, OBJ.FIELD) shows the untruncated comment, its source (annotation / doc comment / line / trailing comment) and the line it is written on, with a clickable Open comment source; declarations keep the platform's own documentation
  • Table & value completion (PHP): Db::name / table('…'), model('…') and db('…') complete table names (short names are matched after stripping the configured table prefix and inserted short as well); the value position of where('status', …) completes model constants / enum cases and the values spelled out in the column comment
  • MyBatis mapper hover: one line per data source (🛢 / 📦 + field comment · field type · table) replaces the platform's Data Source + full DDL wall; when a column has several sources, clicking the comment on a source line jumps to that source (.sql line or read-only DDL view row); the column reference itself in the editor gets an underline and a hand cursor on hover, and a plain click jumps to where it was written (Ctrl / Cmd+Click keeps the platform's own Go-to)
  • Lookup settings, per project: the Database field lookup page holds every lookup option and is stored per project — master switch (on by default), table prefix shared by PHP and MyBatis, data source strategy, live probe / refresh / filters, the project's ".sql" scope (DDL path patterns, incremental script directories and order patterns), hover delay, comment truncation counted in Chinese characters, plus the index status and its action buttons — so several open projects keep their own data sources and filters. Labels stay short: the qualifiers and the button order live in the ? bubble next to each item; live-source options are greyed out while the strategy is ".sql only", and the saved filters apply when a project opens — no Apply needed, the live source is probed in the background; language pages keep only their own comment-source options
  • English & Chinese UI, configuration & getting started: the UI follows the IDE language or can be set manually; a Configuration page exports / imports every setting as JSON (import overwrites, confirmed first) and resets one settings group; a once-per-version notification links straight to the settings, a file without any Chinese comment gets an explanatory banner (one click turns it off for good), inline comments and Project view comments toggle with Ctrl+Alt+Shift+K / Ctrl+Alt+Shift+P, and a failed report write shows a persistent notification with Open report folder

Comment sources

  • Java: annotation values (Swagger / custom) → JavaDoc summary → adjacent / trailing comments
  • Kotlin: doc tags → KDoc summary → adjacent / trailing comments (stdlib excluded by default)
  • PHP: attributes / doc tags (incl. self::CONST references) → PHPDoc summary → adjacent / trailing comments
  • Go: doc tags → godoc → trailing comments
  • Call sites show per-argument descriptions from @param; falls back to the callee's own comment
  • Results can be filtered by "Chinese comments only" and are cached per project

Getting started

  • Settings: Settings | Tools | CN Comment Lens — every change takes effect after you click Apply
  • Toggle: Tools menu or editor popup → CN Comment Lens
  • Coverage: Settings | Editor | Inspections | CN Comment Lens; Alt+Enter to fix a flagged member; right-click a folder in the project view for a scoped coverage report

Known limitations

  • Hints appear after indexing finishes on first launch
  • No hints inside diff viewers
  • PHP: attribute constant references limited to self:: / the own class; magic methods are excluded from coverage inspections
  • Kotlin: enum entries and object declarations are out of scope for hints and coverage
  • Go: coverage covers exported members only (godoc convention); struct fields are not counted in coverage yet (inline hints do support them)
  • Database schema lookup: variable table names and sub-queries / closure where abort the anchor walk; joins are only used to build an "alias → table" map for alias.col (no ON-condition / multi-table inference); the index reflects the project's .sql files, not the live database; commented-out SQL statements are ignored; cross-file ALTER comment conflicts are arbitrated (same-file order → filename order patterns → incremental directories → path order) and reported on hover; MyBatis mapper lookup resolves only literal table names inside the same statement block (<include> fragments, dynamic tags and ${} concatenation are not guessed)

Acknowledgements: some features of this plugin were inspired by the Show Comment plugin — many thanks.

在代码行尾直接显示字段、常量、方法参数的中文注释，免去在多个类文件之间跳转查看注释的麻烦。

插件中文名「了然」，取「一目了然」之意。

同一份插件包同时适用于 IntelliJ IDEA 与 PhpStorm。支持 Java / Kotlin（IDE 内置插件）/ PHP / Go（后两者为可选依赖：IDE 缺哪个语言插件，就自动只启用其余语言，插件本身不受影响）。

📖 使用说明文档：CN Comment Lens 使用说明
全部功能的操作方式——行尾中文注释、Project 视图文件注释、覆盖率检查与报告、数据库 Schema 反查； 其中「实时数据库」一章把 探测 / 快照 / 扫描分开讲明：各自读什么、怎么触发、结果在哪里查看。

功能

  • 行尾中文注释：字段、枚举常量、类常量、方法与构造器形参的注释贴在代码行尾；inlay 不进入文本流，行尾输入、后缀补全不受影响
  • Project 视图文件注释：文件名后追加该文件的说明
  • 展示与样式可调：提示的展示范围（仅当前光标行 / 当前方法体内 / 整个文件，默认整个文件）、大文件保护（默认 5000 行，超出时编辑器顶部悬浮提示条）、标识符与注释各自的字体 / 字号 / 颜色、赋值符号、分隔符、截断长度（按汉字个数计，整条没有汉字时按字符数）；点击提示里的标识符段跳转到声明位置（跨文件亦可），多条提示折叠为「+N ▸」，点击展开全部
  • 注释覆盖率检查与报告：类及 public 成员缺少中文注释时告警，Alt+Enter 一键生成注释骨架；Project 视图右键目录（或 Tools 菜单）按目录 / 包名过滤扫描，导出 Markdown 报告
  • 数据库 Schema 反查（ThinkPHP / MyBatis）：查询构造器里的字符串列名与 Mapper XML 里的 列名（写不写表别名都行）显示列注释与类型——来源可以是项目内 .sql 建表文件（📦），也可以是 IDE Database 工具窗里已连好的数据源（🛢；数据源策略：仅 .sql / 仅数据库 / 混合；零凭据，.sql 侧离线可用）。 每条语句各行的行尾也会直接显示该行字段的中文注释； 支持 join 限定列、列名补全（附表注释与来源）、悬停看表名与列类型，点击跳转建表语句或自动生成的只读 DDL 视图； 实时快照的刷新间隔与存活探测可配（可手动「立即探测 / 立即刷新」，支持按库筛选——候选库与你在 Database 工具窗里内省过的库一致，并排除 information_schema / mysql / performance_schema / sys 四个系统库）； 两段式确定性合并——ALTER 始终覆盖 CREATE，跨文件注释冲突自动仲裁并在悬停中提示； PHP 查询构造器里 Alt+Enter 一键修复：打开设置 / 刷新实时库 / 重新扫描 .sql 索引
  • 悬停看完整注释（Java / PHP / Kotlin / Go）：在引用处 / 调用点（obj.getPayNo()、 赋值、OBJ.FIELD）悬停，显示不截断的完整中文注释与来源 （注解 / 文档注释 / 上方行注释 / 行尾注释）与所在行号，并可点击「打开注释原文」把编辑器定位到该行； 声明处交回平台原生文档
  • 表名与取值补全（PHP）：Db::name / table('…')、model('…')、 db('…') 补全表名（写短名时按去掉「表前缀」后的名字匹配、也插入短名）； where('status', …) 的取值位置补全模型类常量 / enum case 与列注释里写明的取值
  • MyBatis Mapper 补全与悬停：别名. 的候选覆盖平台自带那份（候选前带 Database 列图标、 尾部中文注释、类型位列类型）；悬停按数据源分行（每个存在的来源一行「📦 / 🛢 + 字段中文注释 · 字段类型 · 表中文名」， 末行是表英文名）替代平台那份 Data Source + 整段 DDL 的长文档；一列有多个来源时，点来源行的注释即可跳到该来源 （.sql 来源行或只读 DDL 视图列行）；编辑器里字段本身悬停即加下划线 + 手型光标， 无修饰键单击跳到该列的定义处（Ctrl / Cmd+单击仍是平台 Go-to）
  • 反查设置整页按项目保存：「数据库字段反查」一个页面承载全部反查项——总开关（默认开启）/ 表前缀 （PHP 与 MyBatis 共用）/ 数据源策略 / 实时源的探测 · 刷新与数据源 · 库两级筛选 / 本项目的 .sql 扫描范围 （DDL 路径模式 / 增量脚本目录与时序正则）/ 悬浮延迟 / 注释截取长度（按汉字个数计），以及索引状态与操作按钮； 同时打开多个项目可分别配置，互不串用数据源与筛选。标签只留短词：括号里的限定条件、各项完整说明与按钮 使用顺序都收在右侧的「?」气泡里；「仅 .sql」策略下活库项自动置灰； 设置装完即用——打开项目即按已保存的筛选生效并在后台探测一次活数据源，不必先打开设置页点「应用」； 语言页只留各自的注释来源项
  • 中英双语界面与配置管理：界面跟随 IDE 语言，也可在设置里指定；「配置管理」子页支持全部设置导出 / 导入 （JSON，覆盖式导入先确认）与按设置组恢复默认；每个插件版本首次打开项目弹一次引导通知（可直接打开设置）， 完全没有中文注释的文件在编辑器顶部说明「为什么行尾没有提示」（点一次即永久关闭）， 行尾提示 Ctrl+Alt+Shift+K、Project 视图注释 Ctrl+Alt+Shift+P 一键开关， 覆盖率报告写入失败时给出常驻通知 + 「打开报告目录」

注释来源（命中即用）

  • Java：注解值（Swagger 系 / 自定义）→ JavaDoc 摘要 → 相邻 / 行尾注释
  • Kotlin：docblock 标签 → KDoc 摘要 → 相邻 / 行尾注释（标准库默认排除）
  • PHP：Attribute / docblock 标签（含 self::CONST 常量引用）→ PHPDoc 摘要 → 相邻 / 行尾注释
  • Go：docblock 标签 → godoc → 行尾注释
  • Java / Kotlin / PHP 的方法调用按 @param 逐实参显示说明；形参没有说明时回退为被调方法 / 类自身的注释
  • 所有结果可按「仅显示含中文的注释」过滤，并写入项目级缓存

快速上手

  • 设置：Settings | Tools | CN Comment Lens，所有设置 Apply 后立即生效
  • 开关：Tools 或编辑器右键菜单 → CN Comment Lens，「行尾中文注释」「Project 视图文件注释」两个独立开关
  • 覆盖率检查：Settings | Editor | Inspections | CN Comment Lens，缺注释的成员用 Alt+Enter 生成注释骨架
  • 覆盖率报告：Project 视图右键目录 / Tools 菜单，按目录与包名过滤生成 Markdown 报告

已知限制

  • 首次启动需等索引完成后，行尾提示才会出现
  • Diff 视图（比较 / 历史对比）中不显示行尾提示
  • PHP：Attribute 常量引用仅支持 self:: / 本类短名；魔术方法不参与覆盖率检查
  • Kotlin：枚举条目与 object 声明暂不在行尾提示与覆盖率口径内
  • Go：覆盖率口径只查导出成员（首字母大写，godoc 约定）；结构体字段的覆盖率暂不统计（行尾提示支持）
  • 数据库 Schema 反查：变量表名与子查询 / 闭包 where 会中断锚点回溯；join 只用于建立「别名 → 表」映射以支持 别名.列（不做 ON 条件与多表推断）；索引反映的是项目内 .sql 文件的当前内容，不是数据库实况；被注释掉的 SQL 语句不参与索引；跨文件 ALTER 注释冲突按仲裁链取值（同文件语句序 → 文件名时序模式 → 增量目录 → 路径序）并在 hover 中提示；实时数据库源只展示已内省的表 / 列，🛢 提示跳转为生成的只读 DDL 视图；MyBatis Mapper 只解析同一语句块内的字面量表名（<include> 片段、动态标签与 ${} 拼接的表名不猜）

致谢：本插件的部分功能受 Show Comment 插件启发，特此致谢。
