idea-plugin.name: Igor-PHP
idea-plugin.description:
Igor-PHP — The faithful assistant for FrankenPHP Workers

Inspects your Symfony applications in real-time to detect shared state mutations, memory leaks, and worker lifecycle hazards under FrankenPHP.

  • Gutter icons for shared services recognized in the Symfony container map
  • Instant zero-latency feedback directly in PhpStorm
  • Status bar widget tracking service map and baseline health
  • Zero-pollution baseline workflow (Ignore in igor-baseline.json)
  • Report false positives and missing rules directly to GitHub

Requirements: Fully compatible with Symfony 6.4/7.x/8.x. Full IDE live inspection and baseline gutter markers are supported starting with igor-php/igor-php >= 0.9.8.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Regenerate/Prune Baseline actions now find vendor/bin/igor-php, honor the custom binary path from Settings, and report failures instead of a false success notification.
  • Igor processes are now killed after their timeout, so a hung or verbose binary can no longer freeze inspections.
  • The binary test button in Settings no longer crashes when --version times out.

idea-plugin.name: IdeaVim
idea-plugin.description:
Bring the power of Vim to your JetBrains IDE.


IdeaVim is a Vim emulation plugin that lets you edit code using Vim's modal editing, motions, text objects, and commands — all while keeping full access to your IDE's refactoring, debugging, and navigation features.


What's included

  • Normal, Insert, Visual, Select, Command-line, and Ex modes
  • Motions, operators, text objects, marks, registers, and macros
  • Key mappings and Vim script support
  • Full Vim regex for search and replace
  • Configuration via ~/.ideavimrc (XDG paths supported)
  • Map any IDE action to a key with <Action>

Vim plugins

Enable popular Vim plugins like surround, commentary, easymotion, sneak, NERDTree, multiple-cursors, highlightedyank, which-key, and more — right from your ideavimrc.


Works everywhere

Compatible with IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, CLion, Rider, Android Studio, and all other JetBrains IDEs.


Resources:

  • GitHub — documentation, setup guides, and contributing
  • Issue tracker — feature requests and bug reports
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Features:

  • VIM-3058 Added the "# register, which holds the name of the alternate file — the file you last switched away from, the one CTRL-^ jumps back to. "#p puts it into the text, @# reads it in an expression, and :registers lists it under %. Like %, it reports the path relative to the content root, since IdeaVim has no current directory, and it is read only — :let @# = 'other.txt' reports E354: Invalid register name: '#'

  • VIM-1370 Added the tag stack, so a jump to a definition can be retraced the way Vim does it. CTRL-] now records the position it was jumped from, CTRL-T and :pop walk back up those positions, :tag without an argument walks back down again, and :tags lists the stack with > marking where you are in it. All of them take a count, so 2<C-T> and :2pop step back two tag jumps at once. The stack holds twenty entries, dropping the oldest once it is full, and a new tag jump made after walking back drops the entries you walked past. gd and gD are not tag commands and leave the stack alone, as in Vim

  • Added the 'tagstack' option ('tgst'), on by default. With :set notagstack a tag jump still navigates but records nothing, which is useful for a mapping that should not disturb the stack. Walking the stack is unaffected — CTRL-T keeps using whatever is already on it

  • VIM-1347 Added built-in vim-signature extension — enable it with Plug 'kshenoy/vim-signature' and every local mark a-z of the file gets an icon in the gutter, so you can see where your marks are instead of having to remember. m, places the next free mark, m- clears the marks of the current line and m<Space> those of the whole buffer. ]' and [' walk through the marked lines in the order they appear, while '], '[, `] and `[ walk through the marks in the order of their letters — all of them take a count, and each one is a jump, so '' and <C-O> bring you back. Those last four are Vim's own marks of the last change or yank and the plugin takes them over, as the original does; every key is a mapping to a <Plug> name, so nmap gn <Plug>(SignatureGotoNextSpotAlpha) and friends let you keep Vim's. ]` and [` are left alone, since IdeaVim already implements them as real motions. Global marks A-Z are not drawn, because with the default ideamarks they are IDE bookmarks, which the IDE shows in the gutter itself

  • VIM-2168 Added the 'ideawindowjumps' option, which gives every split its own jump list as in Vim. IdeaVim has always kept one list per project, so <C-O> in one split could take you back to a position you jumped from in another; with :set ideawindowjumps a new split starts with a copy of the list of the window it was split from and the two lists then go their own ways, so :jumps, <C-O> and <C-I> only ever see the jumps made in the window you are in. The IDE's own Back and Forward navigation stays project wide either way. Since window ids do not survive a restart, only one list per project is saved between sessions — the list of the most recently used window, which a window with no list of its own starts from

  • VIM-934 Added the 'wildmenu' option ('wmnu'), so the completion popup that <Tab> opens on the : command line can now be turned off with :set nowildmenu — previously it was always shown. With it off, <Tab> and <S-Tab> still cycle through the matches one at a time, and <Left> and <Right> move the caret instead of moving through the match list. The option is on by default, which is what IdeaVim has always done

  • VIM-4314 % and its file name modifiers are now expanded when a command runs, not just when <Tab> completes it — :w %:h/backup.txt writes a copy next to the current file, :!mv % %:h/renamed.txt renames it, and :source, :split and :read take % as well. % is the buffer name, which stays relative while the file is under a content root; :p forces the full path, :h takes the directory, :t the file name, :r drops the last extension and :e gives it, and they chain left to right, so %:t:r is the file name without its extension and %:p:h:h the parent of its directory. A backslash removes the special meaning, so :!echo \% prints a bare %, and a file name that itself contains a % is no longer expanded a second time. As in Vim, :! expands only the file name specials and leaves $VAR and ~ to the shell. Completion understands the modifiers too, so :e %:h/<Tab> now lists the files next to the current one instead of treating %:h as the file name

  • Added built-in vim-textobj-line extension — enable it with Plug 'kana/vim-textobj-line' and you get two text objects for the current line: al selects every character of the line without the end of line character (the same as 0v$h), and il leaves the leading and trailing whitespace out of it (the same as ^vg_). So on an indented line, dil deletes the code and keeps the indent, while dal empties the line completely, and yil, cil, gUal and the rest work the same way from anywhere in the line, no matter where the caret is. As in the original, neither selects anything on an empty line, and il also does nothing on a line of whitespace only, since there is no text there to select. Set let g:textobj_line_no_default_key_mappings = 1 before enabling the plugin to keep al and il free and map <Plug>(textobj-line-al) and <Plug>(textobj-line-il) yourself

  • VIM-2089 Added built-in vim-visual-star-search extension — enable it with Plug 'bronson/vim-visual-star-search' and * and # in Visual mode search forwards and backwards for the selected text instead of for the word under the caret. The selection is searched for literally, without the word boundaries the built-in * adds, so selecting foo also finds it inside foobar, and characters such as ., *, [ and ~ match themselves instead of being read as a pattern. Every kind of selection works: V* searches for the whole line together with its end of line character, so it only matches text that ends a line, and a blockwise selection searches for its rows joined by end of line characters, as the original does. n and N repeat the search, gv brings back the text you searched for, and the position you searched from goes on the jump list, so '' and <C-O> return to it. Unlike the built-in *, the search honours 'ignorecase' and 'smartcase', because the original searches with a plain /. A count is applied, so 3* finds the third occurrence — the original loses it, as the :<C-u> in its mapping wipes the count off the command line. The plugin's <leader>* mapping, which greps the selection through the whole project, is not implemented

  • VIM-2663 Added the :startinsert (:star) and :startreplace (:startr) commands, the counterparts of :stopinsert. :startinsert enters Insert mode where the caret is, exactly as i does, and :startinsert! first moves to the end of the line, as A does. :startreplace enters Replace mode as R does, and :startreplace! works like $R, so it starts by overwriting the last character of the line rather than appending after it — with :set virtualedit=onemore it goes one further and appends, just as $ itself does. <BS> in the Replace mode they start restores the overwritten characters, like any other Replace session. Every caret takes part, so with several carets each one moves to the end of its own line. Like :stopinsert, they are meant for autocommands — autocmd BufEnter scratch startinsert opens a scratch buffer ready to type in. Neither takes a range or an argument; :1startinsert reports E481: No range allowed and :startinsert foo reports E488: Trailing characters

Fixes:

  • VIM-3667 Fixed mappings to IDE actions not working when no file is open. With map <leader>sf <Action>(GotoFile) in ~/.ideavimrc, pressing <leader>sf used to do nothing once every editor tab was closed, because IdeaVim only listened for keys inside an editor. The keys of such Normal mode mappings are now picked up while the focus is on a non-text component of a project with no open editor — the Project tool window, for example — and go through the regular mapping machinery, so counts, 'timeout' and recursive mappings behave as in an editor; <Esc> cancels a half-typed sequence. Only mappings whose right-hand side consists of <Action>(...) sequences take part, since there is no editor for anything else to act on: nmap j gj keeps j for the tool window, and the :action GotoFile<CR> form of the mapping is not picked up. Text fields such as Search Everywhere keep receiving typed characters, modal dialogs are left alone, and keys that do not start a mapping are left to the IDE
  • Fixed gx adding to the jump list — pressing gx used to record the caret position as a jump and overwrite the ' mark, so a following CTRL-O landed back on the caret's own line instead of returning to the previous jump. As in Vim, gx opens the URL without touching the jump list
  • Fixed the word text objects throwing an exception when they reached the very start of the file — growing a right-to-left Visual selection with iw, aw, iW or aW looks one character back to decide where the previous word begins, and at offset 0 there is no such character. Starting on the second character of the file and pressing v, h, iw now selects back to the start of the file instead of reporting an internal error
  • VIM-4308 Fixed the current search match being drawn with a box around it after the search was over. The box now only appears while 'incsearch' is previewing the pattern you are typing, and only in the window you are searching in — accepting the search with <CR>, cancelling it with <Esc>, n, N, moving the caret, editing the text, toggling 'hlsearch' and clicking into another window all leave every match looking the same. This is what a stock Vim looks like: its default colour scheme links the CurSearch highlight group to Search, so the match under the cursor is drawn no differently from the rest unless you define CurSearch yourself. Neovim does define it, which is why the box shows up there
  • Fixed gv reselecting one character too many. In Visual mode gv swaps the current selection for the previous one, and the restored selection ran one character past where it ended — with foo bar on the first line and bar foo on the second, viw on foo, <Esc>, j, viw and then gv selected foo instead of foo
  • Fixed da( inside a nested block swallowing the enclosing brackets. A characterwise delete or yank spanning several lines is promoted to linewise only when there is nothing but white space before its start and after its end, but the check for what comes after skipped the very first character following the range. So with an outer block opened on one line, an inner one opened on the next, and both closed by )) on a third, da( on the inner ( deleted the last two lines whole and took the outer ) with them, instead of deleting just the inner block
  • Fixed a yank with a blockwise-forced motion keeping only its first line. CTRL-V after the operator makes the motion cover a rectangle, but the yank stored just the top row of it, characterwise — with abcde above fghij, y<C-V>j followed by p now puts the two-row block a/f back as a block instead of pasting a single a. In builds with assertions enabled it reported an internal error instead
  • VIM-4319 Fixed IdeaVim reporting an internal error when it was disabled, uninstalled or updated without restarting the IDE. The plugin used to shut itself down after the platform had already unregistered its services, so the shutdown could no longer reach them and failed with a null pointer exception. It now shuts down just before the platform unloads it, while everything it needs is still there, which also means its listeners are properly removed and typing is handed back to the IDE — so after switching IdeaVim off the keys behave as they would with the plugin never installed, without a restart
  • Fixed CTRL-R CTRL-F reporting an internal error on the command line when the 'incsearch' match ended at the very end of the file. The file name is looked for just past the match, where there is nothing left, so searching for the last word of the file and pressing CTRL-R CTRL-F now reports E446: No file name under cursor, as Vim does
  • VIM-2010 Fixed . replaying an import that the IDE added while you were typing. IdeaVim records every change the document goes through during an insert, which is how auto-inserted brackets and indents get replayed too, but an import line put in by Add unambiguous imports on the fly, by the Alt+Enter fix or by the completion popup is not something you typed. Those changes are now left out of the recording — in a Java file with two Set<String> fields, changing the first one with cf>List<String> also adds import java.util.List; at the top of the file, and . on the second field now changes just that field instead of typing the text of the import into it as well. Picking the class from the completion popup is recorded correctly too: it inserts the fully qualified java.util.List, adds the import and then shortens the name again, and . used to replay that whole round trip and leave the caret in the middle of it

Changes:

  • IdeaVim's own options are now all prefixed with idea, so it is clear at a glance which options are IdeaVim's and which are Vim's. 'lookupkeys', 'pythonconsole', 'trackactionids' and 'visualdelay' are now 'idealookupkeys', 'ideapythonconsole', 'ideatrackactionids' and 'ideavisualdelay'. The old names still work, so an existing ~/.ideavimrc needs no changes, but they are deprecated and only the new name is reported by :set and :set all. 'trackactionids' keeps its 'tai' abbreviation
  • CTRL-T is no longer a second key for CTRL-O. It used to step back along the jump list; it now walks back up the tag stack as in Vim, and reports E73: Tag stack empty when no tag jump has been made. CTRL-O is unchanged and remains the way to walk the jump list

Merged PRs:

  • 2053 by 1grzyb1: VIM-2010 fix repeat insert with import
  • 2052 by 1grzyb1: VIM-2700 Navigate between split diff windows
  • 2049 by 1grzyb1: VIM-1974 implement textobj-line extension
  • 2046 by 1grzyb1: VIM-3667 handle vim shortcuts outside editor
  • 2045 by 1grzyb1: VIM-4321 Set configurable key in xml
  • 2044 by 1grzyb1: VIM-4319 turn off plugin before unload
  • 2037 by 1grzyb1: VIM-4314 Expand % signs in commands
  • 2034 by 1grzyb1: VIM-4308 Don't update the current search match highlight when no search is active
  • 2033 by AndDe-gourav: fix range of visual selection
  • 2021 by 1grzyb1: VIM-3058 alternate file name register
  • 2020 by 1grzyb1: VIM-1370 Implement tag stack in IdeaVim
  • 2018 by 1grzyb1: VIM-1347 Implements Signature marks plugin
  • 2014 by 1grzyb1: VIM-4312 correct linewise delete promotion when range end has trailing non-whitespace

idea-plugin.name: IJKL Shortcuts
idea-plugin.description:
This plugin adds `alt-ijkl` navigation shortcuts to the current keymap, tool windows, and popups. The idea is that these shortcuts are more ergonomic for navigation/editing than using keyboard arrows, so you can stop using arrows in the IDE editor. Some of the shortcuts:
  • alt-i - line up
  • alt-j - move to previous word
  • alt-k - line down
  • alt-l - move to next word
  • alt-n - move left
  • alt-m - move right
  • alt-u - move to start of line
  • alt-o - move to end of line
  • alt-shift-ijklmnuo - move with selection
Note that in macOS you will need to configure keyboard input source without dead keys. This can be done after plugin startup in notification popup.
For more details see GitHub.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Updated to work in the latest IDEs. Simplified internal working and not overriding mnemonics.

idea-plugin.name: ErgoKeys
idea-plugin.description:
Supercharge your productivity with the most efficient keybinding for IntelliJ family of IDEs.

A modal keybinding for IntelliJ family of IDEs (like vim), but based on command frequency and ergonomics.
Inspired by xah-fly-keys, independently implemented as a plugin for IntelliJ. 

Shift-Space  activate Command Mode
Alt-Space    activate Command Mode

F (qwerty)   activate Insert Mode
U (dvorak)   activate Insert Mode

idea-plugin.name: GlobalizationTranslator
idea-plugin.description:
GlobalizationTranslator

简体中文文档

More information：Github
Issues report: Issues

Intellij platform i18n plugin，Auto translate 131 languages for your application with one click，Support Android strings.xml and java .properties file

This plugin supports translate Android.xml and java .properties file, which can preserve the placeholders such as %1$s, %2$d, {0},{1} and can Reserved escape characters like \n,\",\', etc., support string, string-array, plurals tag.

Advantages of this plugin compared to other plugins: fast translation speed, translate files into 131 languages in less than two minutes, support for retaining placeholders, support for incremental translation.

Install

Dependency：Compose for IDE Plugin Development (Experimental)

Download Dependency:




Click Here Download
-> Settings -> Plugins -> Click Settings Icon Button -> Install Plugin form Disk

Usage

  1. Translate the entire document
    1. Select the values/strings.xml or .properties file
    2. Right click and select "Translate this file".
    3. Select the languages to be translated.
    4. Click OK.
  2. Incremental translation
    1. In the values/strings.xml or .properties file, select n lines of content you want to translate
    2. Right click and select "Translate to Other Languages".
    3. Select the languages to be translated.
    4. Click OK.

Skill

After translating Android strings.xml, many values-** folders will be generated, which is very confusing. At this time, we can create a new folder in the app/main directory and name it at will, such as res-i18n , Then create a new values directory in the res-i18n directory, and copy the previous res/value/strings.xml to the values directory Then edit build.gradle , add res.srcDirs += "src/main/res-i18n" under sourceSets/main, where res-i18n is the name of the newly created folder, and then click gradle sync. After that, the files generated by the translation are all in the res-i18n directory, which looks a lot more refreshing.

android {
    //...
    sourceSets {
        main {
            res.srcDirs += "src/main/res-i18n"
        }
    }
}

Notice

Be careful to choose the source language correctly, otherwise the translation may not be accurate

1.For Android strings.xml please add translatable="false" for strings not to be translated:

<string name="test" translatable="false">Test</string>

2.For .properties file，please store untranslated strings and translated strings in separate files

Sponsor

https://github.com/wilinz/Sponsor

idea-plugin.name: gpt-helper
idea-plugin.description:
Flutter l18n Flutter Gen-l18n IntelliJ IDEA Plugin

Use AI to internationalize your Flutter apps in Android Studio.

Features

  1. SetUp intl: If INTL is not yet set up: right click anywhere and click "Setup Flutter Intl". It will add imports, and fix your MaterialApp/CupertinoApps based on your settings

  2. Internationalize file/directory: Right click file or directory, select translate file/directory, choose strings to translate (e.g. print statements you may ignore). Get a best guess for the intl keys (i.e. based on context of the file, and also filename) by AI. Accept and translate to all languages configured in your project.

  3. Translate to new Language: You can right-click on an .arb (Application Resource Bundle) file in the project view and choose the "Translate this to new Arb file" option. This action translates the entire file.

  4. Translate missing keys: go to untranslated-messages.txt and right-click anywhere, choose "Translate missing keys" This will translate all missing keys in your project.

  5. Custom instructions: You can customize the instructions for the AI model to suit your translation needs. This allows you to provide specific guidelines or context for the translations.

  6. Select model: You can choose between different AI models (e.g., gemini-flash, ...). I choose Gemini, because it's affordable, ridiculously fast and works well for this use case. Initially I had used openAI, but you all know what happened to them. They got steamrolled.

Requirements

Nothing, but rate limits will apply - Please use a Gemini API Key.

Possible Improvements

Here are some ideas, if you want to improve (sorry for the code base)

separate tree for ignored entries

  • When localizing, some things are just never localized
  • Don't mark them by default
  • how to identify them? hash with file + context + string
  • show them in a separate view somehow.
  • mark them as ignored, when not translated, once
  • still show them (e.g. in a second tab, when tabbed (ignored from previous runs)

Performance Speedup by translating multiple keys per request instead of one

this is a bigger refactor starting with the request to the LLM, we need to request multi line json, we need to identify them back again and then we need to map them back correctly. we need chunking and upstream we need all the changes, too. e.g. translation task amount calculation.

But it's also valid to just fire 100 parallel tasks... it's just resource heavy and one needs an api key...

Check for existing keys

e.g. when we translate a file there are many common buttons, like e.g. Cancel, Save, .... we should provide all existing common keys to AI and let AI choose, if we can use them. If yes, use them, if not proceed with the translation (of the rest)

error on existing keys

currently you can add existing keys, which is an error

Disclaimer

This plugin was developed for the purpose of learning Kotlin and IntelliJ IDEA plugin development. The code quality may not be optimal as it was developed while experimenting with Domain-Driven Design (DDD) and faced time constraints.

Please note that this plugin is provided as-is, and I do not guarantee its compatibility with future versions of Flutter or IntelliJ IDEA. Use it at your own risk.

If you encounter any issues or have suggestions for improvement, feel free to report them on the project's GitHub repository.

Important: Keep in mind that the use of the Gemini API for translation may be subject to terms and conditions, including limitations on the number of requests or usage restrictions. Ensure you comply with OpenAI's guidelines and any applicable usage restrictions when using this plugin.

We hope you find this plugin helpful for your Flutter localization needs!

Installation

  1. Flutter l18n GPT here
  2. Open settings, find gpt-helper settings and add your Gemini API key

Gift me a coffee

I'd rather you check out my free iOS and Android App https://ai-klangwerk.com and leave a review if you like it! That would help me a lot :)

idea-plugin.name: NLSExchange
idea-plugin.description:
NLSExchange

Edit NLS files

For the NLS editor, a field with the NLS base name must exist in the interface. A Field with the name PATH, PATH_NLS, BASE_NAME or NLS_BASE_NAME. All other fields are listed as NLS keys. This can still be influenced by commenting.

NLSExchange:PATH : The associated field is used as a reference to the NLS base name.

NLSExchange:IGNORE : The associated field is ignored.

NLSExchange:KEY : By default, the associated field is the NLS base name (e.g. PATH), but in this case it is a key.

Example:

Standard nls with PATH and keys:

    package ch.abacus.lib.nls;

    public interface NLSGeneric {
        public static final String PATH = "lib.nls.generic";
        public static final String ACHTUNG = "ACHTUNG";
        public static final String BASIS = "BASIS";
        public static final String DATUM = "DATUM";
    }

Nls with special markings:

    package ch.abacus.lib.nls;

    public interface NLSGeneric {
        public static final String genericNlsPath = "lib.nls.generic"; // NLSExchange:PATH -> is our nls path
        public static final String ACHTUNG = "ACHTUNG";
        public static final String BASIS = "BASIS";
        public static final String PATH = "PATH"; // NLSExchange:KEY -> is not the nls path in this case, but a key
        public static final String DATUM = "DATUM";
        public static final String myPackage = "lib"; // NLSExchange:IGNORE -> no nls key
    }

idea-plugin.name: Translation-I18n
idea-plugin.description:
Translation-I18n is a plugin created to easily manage your translation files

I have created this mainly for my personal usage in Phalcon framework / Translate component, but this plugin can easily be used in any PHP based or Twig based application.

Key features

  • Using php array files to store translations
  • Select the translation folder path where the plugin will lookup translation files.
  • Autocomplete support in selected file extensions.
  • You can select the text you wish to translate, then use Actions / Add Translation action to add a new translation directly from your editor. You can also set key shortcuts for more ease.
  • Optionally you can select to show translation text in autocomplete. [Requires index invalidation]
  • Ability to select the default language in which your application works. [Requires index invalidation]
  • Allows the option to select the preferred quotes used in your application
  • Allows the option to choose any file extensions as long as the particular file is associated with either PHP or Twig or Vue file type.
  • Allows the option to set your own translation function name when generating translation in Twig associated files, auto generating the entire translation code automatically.

Translation folder structure

The translation folder structure has 2 options. Before that, ensure the folder translation path is added correctly.

You are optionally given the following structure to use, in this example, the translation path will be "translation"

  1. Using pattern translationPath/code/messages.php
    translation
    ├── de
    │   └── messages.php
    │   └── validation.php
    ├── en
    │   └── messages.php
    │   └── validation.php
    ├── it
    │   └── messages.php
    │   └── validation.php
    └── ro
        └── messages.php
        └── validation.php
  1. Using pattern translationPath/messages.code.php
    translation
    ├── messages.de.php
    ├── messages.en.php
    ├── messages.it.php
    └── messages.ro.php

The plugin will scan these paths and will index only the default selected language file translation keys.

Example of content inside a translation file

<?php

return [
    'title_login'     => 'Login',
    'label_username'  => 'Username',
    'input_username'  => 'Username',
    'label_password'  => 'Password',
    'label_btn_login' => 'Login',
];
or you can also organize your transaction and use require / include, this only works with static paths. 
<?php

return array_merge(
    required __DIR__ . '/validation.php',
    [
        'title_login'     => 'Login',
        'label_username'  => 'Username',
        'input_username'  => 'Username',
        'label_password'  => 'Password',
        'label_btn_login' => 'Login',
    ]
);
idea-plugin.change-notes:
New Feature

  • Changed indexing to use CacheValueManager, this allows to support organized translations files
  • Can now use require/include in the main messages file
  • Can now select the translation file name to save the translation

Bug Fixes

  • Wrap translation text inside php function as well

idea-plugin.name: SimpleLocalize
idea-plugin.description: SimpleLocalize plugin brings you the power of localization directly into your IntelliJ IDEA. Connect your SimpleLocalize project with your IDE and manage translations without leaving your code editor. Get smart code suggestions for translation keys, create missing translations in seconds, start auto-translation jobs, publish translations, browse the published translations, and keep your localization up to date with the integrated activity log.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Setting to turn translation-key code completion on/off, so projects with a large number of keys don't have their regular IDE code completion crowded out by translation key suggestions.
  • Detection of simplelocalize.yml CLI configuration files (editor banner + right-click action) with a "Run CLI command..." picker that runs the SimpleLocalize CLI and streams its output to a console.
  • Gutter icon on code that references a known translation key: hover for a live translation preview, click to jump to the key in the Translations tab or find all other usages in the project. Toggle in Settings.
  • Opt-in inspection that flags key-shaped strings (e.g. home.titel) that don't match any known translation key, with a quick-fix to create the key. Disabled by default since it's heuristic-based.
  • "Find Unused Keys" action on the Translations tab toolbar: scans the project for translation keys with no references anywhere in code and offers to delete them.
  • "Extract to SimpleLocalize translation key" intention: select a hardcoded UI string, create a new translation key/value from it via the API, and replace the selection with just the key name.
  • "Find Usages" right-click action on translation keys in the Translations tab, matching the same action already available from the gutter icon.
  • "Find Unused Keys" results are now shown in a non-modal window, so the rest of the IDE stays usable while it's open, and offer per-selection "Deprecate" (sets the key's deprecated flag) or "Delete" instead of a single all-or-nothing delete confirmation.
  • Gutter icon now also recognizes Android resource references (R.string.restart_hint, R.plurals.items_count) in Java/Kotlin code, in addition to plain string literals.
  • Deprecated translation keys are now marked (strikethrough + "DEPRECATED" label) in the Translations tab once a key is expanded, reusing the details already fetched for expansion rather than an extra request per key.
  • The "Start Auto-Translation" dialog now pre-selects all project languages except the default one on first use, instead of leaving every language unchecked.
  • The "Start Auto-Translation" dialog now lists languages in a single scrollable column instead of a two-column grid, and adds "Select All" / "Deselect All" buttons for faster (de)selection.

Fixed

  • Removed the upper IDE build compatibility limit (until-build), which had pinned the plugin to IntelliJ builds up to 261.* and made it show as incompatible with newer IDE versions (e.g. 262.x). The plugin now declares open-ended compatibility, so it keeps working on future IntelliJ Platform releases without needing another release just to bump this range.
  • Fixed IDE lag/freeze when saving plugin settings or switching tool window tabs: several network calls (token/project validation, loading translations, activity, and hosting environments) were running directly on the UI thread instead of a background task.
  • Fixed a crash (JsonSyntaxException followed by a NullPointerException) when opening the Activity tab or fetching hosting/auto-translate job status: the generated API model now represents timestamps as OffsetDateTime, but the Gson instance used to parse API responses had no adapter registered for it. Also hardened the Activity tab against any future fetch failure instead of crashing on a null result.

idea-plugin.name: Auto Localizer
idea-plugin.description:
Automatically translate XLIFF (.xlf/.xliff) and ARB (.arb) files. Uses existing translations to generate accurate and context-aware translations. High quality localization with one click!

Key features:

  • "Translate with Auto Localizer" action in the Project View and editor tab context menus for XLIFF and ARB files
  • Supports XLIFF 1.2, XLIFF 2.0, and Flutter-style ARB workflows
  • Configurable for different translation states (e.g., initial, new, ...)
  • Notifications for untranslated XLIFF segments and ARB translation on save
  • Powered by doloc.io, a translation service that uses AI to provide high-quality translations
  • Free and without registration for translation files with up to 100 texts

Getting started:

  1. Right-click on an XLIFF or ARB file in the Project View or an editor tab
  2. Select "Translate with Auto Localizer" from the context menu
  3. The plugin will automatically translate the selected file using the doloc service
  4. To configure, open File | Settings | Tools | Auto Localizer
Optionally:
  • Create a (free) account on doloc.io
  • Enter your API key in the settings (apply for a paid plan for larger text quota)
  • Configure XLIFF states and ARB untranslated rules
  • Enable/disable translation reminder notifications on save
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Improvements

  • Add ARB translation support with Flutter-aware base file heuristics, directory-scoped overrides, and ARB save reminders.
  • Update anonymous token if it was invalidated.

Bug Fixes

  • Show a clear dialog when manually translating malformed XLIFF files instead of surfacing a raw parse failure.
  • Show the translation action from Project View and file tabs context menu.

idea-plugin.name: AI Dev Tools
idea-plugin.description:
AI Tools — A intelligentAiToolCollection.

AI Tools — AI工具集

AI Tools 🤖 — 面向开发者的 AI 工具集

在 IntelliJ IDEA 中完成 代码提交、工作日报和命名翻译，减少日常开发中的重复操作，让开发流程更简单、更高效。⚡

通过右键菜单顶部的 🧰 AI工具，快速使用以下功能。

🚀 AI Commit & Push — 自动生成提交说明并推送

读取当前 Git 仓库的代码变更，由 Ai 生成提交说明，自动完成 commit 和 push。

  • 📝 根据实际代码改动生成提交说明。
  • 📦 提交当前仓库的修改、删除及未被 Git 忽略的新文件。
  • ⚠️ 遇到冲突时停止自动操作，提示在 IDEA 中手动处理。
  • 🛡️ 推送失败时保留本地提交，不自动解决冲突或强制推送。

📋 写日报 — 根据当天提交整理工作内容

根据指定分支和 Git 提交人，分析当天的提交记录与代码差异，生成工作日报。

  • 🌿 默认分支为 main，通常只需填写 Git 提交人名称。
  • ✏️ 支持修改分支、自定义日报提示词和输出格式。
  • 📄 生成的日报可以编辑并复制。
  • 🔍 没有符合条件的提交时给出提示，不凭空生成工作内容。

🌐 AI翻译 — 本地词库与 AI 配合的命名助手

将中文变量名、函数名转换为清晰的开发命名，支持 小驼峰（camelCase） 和 大驼峰（PascalCase）。

  • 📚 优先使用内置词库，支持拆词匹配与组合。
  • 🧩 部分命中时保留本地结果，仅让 AI 翻译未命中的片段。
  • ⚡ 全部命中时直接本地生成，无需请求 AI。
  • 🔄 翻译在后台执行，右下角显示进度，不阻塞编辑器。

💡 示例

创建客户 → createCustomer
批量删除客户 → batchDeleteCustomer

⚙️ 使用方式

  • 🖱️ 编辑器右键 → AI工具，选择所需功能。
  • 📁 项目树右键也可使用提交推送和日报功能。
  • ⚙️ 在 Settings → AI Tools 中设置翻译语言、命名风格及日报要求。
  • ⌨️ Windows / Linux：Alt + P
  • ⌨️ macOS：Option + P

🌍 注意事项

AI 请求需要网络连接。

自动提交推送需要：

  • Git 仓库有效
  • 已配置远程上游（upstream）
  • Git 认证可正常使用

🤖 AI Tools — AI utilities for everyday development

Bring Git commits, daily reports, and naming assistance into IntelliJ IDEA, reducing repetitive work in everyday development. ⚡

Access the tools from the 🧰 AI工具 group at the top of the context menu.

🚀 AI Commit & Push

Generate commit messages from actual code changes with Ai, then commit and push to the current branch's upstream.

  • 📝 Generates commit messages based on actual code changes.
  • 📦 Includes modified, deleted, and non-ignored new files.
  • ⚠️ Stops on conflicts and asks you to resolve them manually in IDEA.
  • 🛡️ Keeps local commits when pushing fails. It never force-pushes or resolves conflicts automatically.

📋 Daily Reports

Turn today's commits and code changes into an editable work report.

  • 🌿 The branch defaults to main.
  • 👤 Configure your Git author name to get started.
  • ✏️ Customize the branch, prompt, and report format.
  • 📄 Edit and copy the generated report.
  • 🔍 If there are no matching commits, the plugin reports that instead of making up work.

🌐 AI Naming Translation

Generate clear variable and function names with camelCase or PascalCase support.

  • 📚 The bundled dictionary takes priority, with word splitting and combination matching.
  • 🧩 When only part of a name is matched locally, only unmatched fragments are sent to AI.
  • ⚡ Fully matched names are generated locally without an AI request.
  • 🔄 Translation runs in the background with a progress indicator, without blocking the editor.

💡 Examples

创建客户 → createCustomer
批量删除客户 → batchDeleteCustomer

⚙️ Configuration & Shortcuts

Configure the plugin in Settings → AI Tools.

  • 🌍 Translation language
  • 🔤 Naming style
  • 📋 Daily report requirements
  • ⌨️ Windows / Linux: Alt + P
  • ⌨️ macOS: Option + P

🌍 Requirements

AI requests require a network connection.

Automatic commit and push requires a valid Git repository, a configured remote upstream, and working Git authentication.

idea-plugin.name: Transloco Overlay
idea-plugin.description:
A powerful translation management tool for Transloco in Angular projects. Create, edit, and navigate translations directly from your HTML templates.

✨ Key Features

  • Create Translations from Selection - Select text in HTML, Ctrl+Shift+Click to instantly create a new translation key
  • Existing Translation Detection - Automatically finds if your selected text already exists as a translation to avoid duplicates
  • Smart Parameter Detection - Detects Angular interpolations like {{user.name}} and converts them to transloco params
  • TRANSLOCO_SCOPE Detection - Auto-detects scoped translations from your component's providers
  • Real-time Key Validation - Shows warnings if a translation key already exists while you type
  • Method Selector - Choose between Pipe (| transloco) or Directive (t('key')) syntax
  • Directive Context Detection - Automatically detects *transloco variable names and scopes

🔧 Navigation & Editing

  • Hover over translation keys to see values across all languages
  • Ctrl+Click on keys in HTML to navigate to JSON translation files
  • Ctrl+Shift+Click on existing keys to open multi-language editor
  • Ctrl+Shift+Click on keys in JSON to find usages in templates
  • Autocomplete for translation keys with preview
  • Google Translate integration for auto-translation

📁 Supported Patterns

  • {{ 'key' | transloco }} - Pipe syntax
  • {{ 'key' | transloco:{ param: value } }} - Pipe with params
  • [transloco]="'key'" - Attribute binding
  • transloco="key" - Direct attribute
  • t('key') with *transloco directive - Structural directive

🏢 Enterprise Ready

  • Support for Nx monorepo scoped translations
  • Works with multiple translation file locations
  • Remembers your last used location and method preferences

Open Source & AI Transparency

This plugin was created using AI (Claude by Anthropic). The source code is fully open source on GitHub for review. You are encouraged to inspect the code, report issues, or fork it for your internationalization needs.

idea-plugin.name: LocalizedJPA
idea-plugin.description:
Provides IntelliJ IDEA support for the LocalizedJPA annotation processor.

Features

  • SQL Migration Generator: Generate Flyway DDL scripts directly from @LocalizedEntity classes via IDE action or gutter icon.
  • Code completion for both default methods (e.g., getName(), setName(String)) and locale-aware methods (e.g., getName(Locale), setName(String, Locale))
  • Automatic detection of LocalizedJPA library in project dependencies
  • One-click annotation processing configuration
  • Recognition of synthetic methods generated at compile-time
  • Support for @Localized fields and translations map accessors

⚠️ Migration Generator Requires LocalizedJPA 0.1.5+
To use the SQL Migration Generator without issues, your project must have LocalizedJPA 0.1.5 or newer installed: 
implementation 'com.localizedjpa:localized-jpa:0.1.5'

Getting started

Add the LocalizedJPA library to your Maven or Gradle project. The plugin will automatically detect the library and prompt you to enable annotation processing if needed. Annotate entity fields with @Localized to enable IDE autocomplete for localized methods.

For more information, visit the LocalizedJPA documentation.

idea-plugin.name: DevGlobe
idea-plugin.description:
Appear on a 3D globe in real time while you code. Your activity shows up live on devglobe.app — other developers can see you, discover your projects, and find your links.

How it works

  1. Sign in on devglobe.app with GitHub, X (Twitter), or Google
  2. Copy your API key from settings
  3. Open the DevGlobe tool window in your IDE and paste the key
  4. You appear on the globe

The extension sends a heartbeat every 30 seconds while you code. It pauses automatically after 1 minute of inactivity. After 10 minutes without activity, you disappear from the globe.

Features

  • Live heartbeat — your presence on the globe in real time
  • Language detection — uses your IDE's native FileType system, supports all languages
  • Git integration — detects your repo (commit data is never read or sent by the plugin)
  • Status message — tell others what you're working on
  • Repo sharing — you decide whether your repo name is visible (off by default)
  • Status bar — your coding time today displayed live
  • Notifications — native IDE notifications for every action

What DevGlobe gives you

  • Enhanced public profile — GitHub, X, projects, activity, tech stack and links on a single shareable page
  • Project directory — publish projects, invite teammates, get discovered and upvoted by the community
  • Comments & upvotes — threaded discussions on every project
  • Developer dashboard — manage profile, projects and extensions, track coding stats, badges and notifications
  • Discovery — browse and filter developers & projects by language, tools and platform
  • Light & dark mode — full theme support across the platform

Privacy

This plugin is open source. Your source code, file contents, keystrokes, and IP address are never sent. File paths are only sent relative to the git repo root — never an absolute home path. Local privacy flags (hide_file_names, hide_branch_names, hide_project_names) live in ~/.devglobe/config.toml. Your API key is stored in the IDE's native credential manager (PasswordSafe) and mirrored to ~/.devglobe/config.toml so the bundled core process can read it.

Compatible with all JetBrains IDEs: IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, Rider, PhpStorm, CLion, RubyMine, DataGrip, Android Studio, RustRover.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2.0.1

  • All endpoints now point to the new devglobe.app domain (migrated from devglobe.xyz).
  • Invalid API key (401) is now detected: the key is cleared and the user is prompted to reconnect.
  • New actions under Tools → DevGlobe: Debug (toggle verbose logging), Open Log File…, Open Config File….
  • Refreshed marketplace logo for brand consistency.
  • README: added a troubleshooting section with debug logging instructions; RustRover listed in compatible IDEs.

2.0.0

  • Multi-provider repo URL detection (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, self-hosted Gitea/Forgejo, Azure DevOps).
  • Pure file-system git detection — no git binary required, ~1 ms latency.
  • Sub-second file switching now correctly tracked (no more lost micro-edits).
  • File paths sent only when in a git repository, always relative to the repo root.
  • Privacy flags hide_file_names, hide_branch_names, hide_project_names in ~/.devglobe/config.toml.
  • Visibility settings (anonymous mode, repo sharing, profile mode) moved to the dashboard at devglobe.app/dashboard/settings.
  • Robust core process recovery, automatic retry on download failure.

idea-plugin.name: ARB Editor
idea-plugin.description:
ARB Editor is a powerful, synchronized ARB (Application Resource Bundle) translation editor built for Flutter developers. Open any folder of .arb files and manage all language translations in a single, unified table view — right inside your IDE.

FeatureDescription
📝Synchronized Table EditorEdit all languages side-by-side in one table. Changes auto-save instantly to .arb files.
⚠️Missing Translation DetectionBlank cells are highlighted in red so you never ship an incomplete translation.
🔍Placeholder ValidationValidates that {placeholder} tokens match across all languages — prevents Flutter runtime crashes.
📊Translation Progress BarsEach language column header shows a color-coded completion bar (green / yellow / red).
📥Import & Export CSVExport translations for external translators, then import their CSV back with a merge preview.
✏️Key Rename / RefactorRename a key across all .arb files at once, including @key metadata annotations.
🔎Duplicate DetectionFind translation keys with identical values — catch copy-paste errors or consolidation opportunities.
🏷️Key Grouping & Prefix FilterAuto-groups keys by prefix (home_, auth_, settings_) for focused editing.
📋Metadata EditorFull @key annotation editor — description, type, and placeholders with auto-detection of {var} tokens.
📂Recent Folders & Welcome ScreenQuick access to recent ARB folders with stats (keys, languages, missing count) at a glance.

🛠️ More Tools

  • Sort A→Z — Alphabetical key sorting across all files
  • Fill from Reference — Copy a reference language into blank cells as a translation placeholder
  • Add / Delete Key — Manage keys across all ARB files at once

  • Copy Flutter Code — Right-click to copy AppLocalizations.of(context)!.keyName

  3. Dán Google Apps Script Web App URL (phải kết thúc bằng /exec)
  4. Chọn module Android cần sync
  5. Chọn ngôn ngữ (plugin có thể tự detect từ res/values*)
  6. Chọn chế độ:
    • Add all – thêm hoặc cập nhật tất cả key
    • Add missing only – chỉ thêm key chưa tồn tại
    • Selected keys – chỉ sync các key được nhập
  7. Xem trước (preview) và áp dụng vào strings.xml

📌 Cách lấy Google Apps Script Web App URL

  1. Mở Google Sheet của bạn
  2. Vào Extensions → Apps Script
  3. Trong Apps Script:
    • Nhấn Deploy → New deployment
    • Chọn Web app
    • Execute as: Me
    • Who has access: Anyone
  4. Nhấn Deploy
  5. Copy URL dạng:
https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbxxxxxxx/exec

⚠ Lưu ý: URL bắt buộc phải kết thúc bằng /exec

🔒 Lưu ý

  • Plugin sẽ validate XML trước khi ghi
  • Đảm bảo placeholder (%s, %d, ...) giống nhau giữa các ngôn ngữ

idea-plugin.name: I18N Translate
idea-plugin.description:
I18N Translate Plugin Overview

This IntelliJ IDEA plugin helps you manage and translate i18n files (properties, json, yaml/yml). Key features include:

  • 1. Supports multiple translation engines: Alibaba Cloud Machine Translation, Tencent Cloud TMT, and DeepL
  • 2. Adds selected text from code into the source i18n file and translates it to target language files
  • 3. Translates selected keys from the source language file to one or multiple target language files
  • 4. Translates selected keys from the source language file to all target language files
  • 5. Supports languages: zh: Simplified Chinese zh-TW: Traditional Chinese en: English ja: Japanese ko: Korean fr: French es: Spanish it: Italian de: German tr: Turkish ru: Russian pt: Portuguese vi: Vietnamese id: Indonesian th: Thai ms: Malay ar: Arabic hi: Hindi

Notes:

  • Please ensure your source and target file paths are configured before using the plugin
  • Plugin logs are available in idea.log.
  • Plugin supports logging HTTP requests and responses, default is closed, can be opened in settings
  • Please ensure your proxy settings and access key configuration are correct.

I18N Translate 插件简介

这是一个支持国际化翻译的IntelliJ IDEA插件，提供对i18n文件（properties、json、yaml/yml）进行修改和翻译的核心功能：

  • 1、支持多种翻译引擎：阿里云机器翻译、腾讯云TMT、Deepl翻译服务
  • 2、支持选中代码中的文本到i18n源语言配置文件中，并且支持翻译到其他目标语言文件中
  • 3、支持选中源语言配置文件中的key，然后翻译到指定一个或者多个语言文件中
  • 4、支持选中源语言配置文件中的key，然后翻译到指定全部语言文件中
  • 5、支持语言 zh：简体中文 zh-TW：繁体中文 en：英语 ja：日语 ko：韩语 fr：法语 es：西班牙语 it：意大利语 de：德语 tr：土耳其语 ru：俄语 pt：葡萄牙语 vi：越南语 id：印尼语 th：泰语 ms：马来西亚语 ar：阿拉伯语 hi：印地语

注意事项:

  • 请提前设置源文件路径和目标文件路径才能使用
  • 插件日志在idea.log中

idea-plugin.name: LingMirror
idea-plugin.description:
LingMirror is a static diagnostic tool for Java ClassLoader leaks.

灵镜 LingMirror — 专注 Java 类加载器泄漏的静态诊断工具

点一下，60 秒找出让你 ClassLoader 永远卸载不掉的那条代码引用链。

为什么需要灵镜

在插件化系统、热部署、SPI 动态加载等场景中，ClassLoader 泄漏是最隐蔽也最致命的问题之一：

  • 应用/模块卸载后 ClassLoader 仍被 GC Root 间接引用，Metaspace 持续增长
  • 线上表现为神秘的 java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace，重启后消失、过段时间复现
  • 传统内存分析工具只能看到结果（哪些 ClassLoader 活着），无法定位根因（哪条引用链锁死了它）

灵镜从源码层面静态分析泄漏根因，直接定位到具体的代码行和引用链。

检测规则（18 条）

CR 系列 — ClassLoader 锁死根因

规则名称级别检测内容
CR-001静态字段持有 Class 锁死🔴 严重static Class<?> / static ClassLoader 直接锁死 ClassLoader
CR-002JDBC Driver 注册未释放🔴 严重DriverManager.register() 后未在 destroy 中 deregister()
CR-003静态集合持有自定义类型实例🔴 严重static Map<XxxType, ...> 持有业务类实例，隐式锁死 ClassLoader
CR-004静态单例持有内部集合🔴 严重静态单例的内部集合动态增长，间接持有 ClassLoader
CR-005静态集合持有通用包装类型🟡 中static Map<String, Object> 等"垃圾场"集合，无界堆积
CR-006静态集合持有匿名内部类/lambda🔴 严重匿名内部类隐式持有外部类引用，放入静态集合后 ClassLoader 永不释放
CR-007实例字段环形引用链🟡 中A→B→A 环形引用，被静态集合持有时整条对象图无法 GC；任一端为单例时降级为低风险

HI 系列 — 隐式引用泄漏

规则名称级别检测内容
HI-001ThreadLocal 逃逸未清理🟠 高ThreadLocal 赋值后未在 finally 中 remove，线程复用时泄漏
HI-002ThreadLocal 不完整清理🟠 高ThreadLocal 在部分分支清理，异常路径遗漏 remove
HI-003监听器注册未反注册🟠 高addListener() 后未在 destroy 中 removeListener()
HI-004Shutdown Hook 捕获外部引用🟠 高Runtime.addShutdownHook() 捕获了外部类引用，进程级锁死
HI-006ExecutorService 未 shutdown🟠 高持有 ExecutorService 但类无 close/shutdown 方法，线程池无法正确关闭
HI-007反射加载类持有 ClassLoader🟠 高Class.forName() / ClassLoader.loadClass() 加载的 Class 隐式持有 ClassLoader

LO 系列 — 低风险提示

规则名称级别检测内容
LO-001静态单例无清理机制⚪ 低static final Xxx INSTANCE 无 destroy/close/cleanup 方法，热部署场景钉住 ClassLoader
LO-002静态字段持有外部库类型⚪ 低static ObjectMapper MAPPER 等，热部署场景钉住库 ClassLoader；外部库非 final 类型不视为不可变
LO-003枚举单例持有可变状态⚪ 低枚举实例持有 Map/List 等可变集合，JVM 级单例无法释放
LO-004静态缓存 ServiceLoader 结果⚪ 低ServiceLoader.load() 加载的 SPI 实例缓存到静态上下文，钉住 ClassLoader
LO-005静态字段持有 Thread 子类⚪ 低static Thread 子类实例，线程生命周期可能超出预期

功能特性

  • 📌 一键跳转 — 点击结果直接定位到问题代码行
  • 🔗 引用链可视化 — 从 GC Root 到泄漏点的完整引用路径
  • 📊 扫描范围选择 — 支持整个项目 / 当前模块 / 当前文件
  • 📄 报告导出 — 导出文本报告，方便团队协作和归档
  • 🧠 智能降噪 — 自动过滤不可变常量、框架内部集合、shade 重定位库等误报
  • ⚙️ 规则配置 — 可单独开关每条规则，自定义风险等级覆盖
  • 🔍 结果过滤排序 — 按规则、风险等级、位置过滤，按严重度排序
  • 🚫 误报抑制 — 右键标记误报，后续扫描自动跳过

适用场景

  • 插件化系统 / 热部署架构（OSGi、SPI、自定义 ClassLoader）
  • 重度使用动态类加载的项目（规则引擎、脚本引擎、模板引擎）
  • 遇到神秘 Metaspace OOM 的项目
  • 长期运行的服务端应用（连接池、缓存、注册表等静态集合堆积）
  • 需要保证模块可卸载的微服务框架

关于灵珑 LingFrame

灵镜是灵珑（LingFrame）生态的诊断工具。灵珑提供运行时安全弹性治理，正在 Apache SeaTunnel 等项目中验证。

👉 https://gitee.com/LingFrame/LingFrame

idea-plugin.name: BundleSafe
idea-plugin.description:
Edit one Java resource-bundle key across every locale with an exact preview and a transactional write.

BundleSafe finds sibling .properties locale files, displays the selected key in each one, and marks missing values. Edit several locale values, review every affected file, then confirm one apply.

Only the selected values change. BundleSafe preserves unrelated bytes, including:

  • comments, blank lines, key order, and separators;
  • UTF-8 BOMs and native-to-ASCII \uXXXX escapes;
  • CRLF, LF, mixed line endings, and final-newline state; and
  • duplicate definitions and untouched continuation lines.

Before writing, BundleSafe refuses unsaved editors, stale previews, and read-only files. If a later file fails during a multi-file apply, earlier files are restored.

Right-click a .properties file in the editor or the project tree and choose Edit Bundle Key Across Locales.

BundleSafe works locally and has no account, network service, analytics, or telemetry. Raw-byte applies cannot be reverted with IDE Undo; use Local History or VCS.

  • Each file is read with its own encoding; a byte-level preview shows every file that will change before anything is written.
  • All files are written in one transaction and restored if any write fails.

idea-plugin.name: Yamlix for Ansible
idea-plugin.description:
Which value does this variable actually have — on which host, and why?

A variable in Ansible does not have a definition. It has as many as the precedence table allows, and which one wins depends on the host, the inventory, and where in the play you are. Yamlix models that properly.

  • Ansible tool window — every variable the open file uses and defines, its effective value, which playbooks reach the file and which hosts that means. Select a variable to see every definition site with the inventories and groups it holds on.
  • Ctrl/⌘+Click on {{ a_variable }} lists every definition site, ordered by what applies at the caret — not a name-based list that reads the same everywhere.
  • Quick Documentation shows the effective value per inventory and host, with hosts that agree collapsed and hosts that differ kept apart.
  • Navigation for roles, include_role, include_tasks, vars_files, include_vars, template/copy sources, notify handlers, and hosts: patterns into INI and YAML inventories.
  • Find Usages from a definition to every use, including through include_tasks.

It never guesses. Anything Ansible can only know at run time is rendered as unresolved with the raw template shown: a fact-templated include_vars lists every candidate and promotes none; register, hostvars, lookup() and vault are named explicitly. There is deliberately no code path that invents a value.

The precedence rules were verified by running ansible-playbook and ansible-inventory against a fixture project with ansible-core 2.20.4 — not reasoned from the documentation. Two fixture projects serve as the executable specification, and a test asserts the code cannot drift from them.

Reuses the platform's YAML PSI. Registers no file type, does not claim *.yml, and never shells out to ansible. Ansible context is detected structurally, per file, and the tool window does not appear in projects that have no Ansible in them.

It makes no network calls and collects nothing. Everything it knows comes from the files already open in your IDE.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Red Hat. Ansible is a trademark of Red Hat, Inc.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.0 — first release. It answers one question: which value a variable actually has, on which host, and why.

  • An Ansible tool window listing every variable the open file uses and defines, its effective value, and which playbooks and hosts reach the file.
  • Ctrl/⌘+Click on a variable, ordered by what applies at the caret rather than by name; Quick Documentation showing the effective value per inventory and host.
  • Navigation for roles, includes, vars_files, template and copy sources, handlers, and hosts: patterns into INI and YAML inventories, plus Find Usages in the other direction.
  • Anything only knowable at run time is shown as unresolved with the raw template. Nothing is guessed.

Precedence was verified against ansible-core 2.20.4 rather than read from the documentation. See the changelog.

idea-plugin.name: LocaleBreeze
idea-plugin.description:
LocaleBreeze turns i18next translation keys into IDE-aware symbols. It infers the namespace and key scope from your code, understands which dictionary entry each key refers to, and connects translation calls with their JSON definitions—without running a full TypeScript type checker.

  • Infer key context: understands useTranslation, i18next.t, namespaces, keyPrefix, and configurable scoped or full-key translation functions.
  • Navigate in both directions: go from a translation call to its JSON entry, or from a dictionary key to a popup containing every indexed usage.
  • Find and count usages: see how many references a key has and open each source location with its file, line number, and code preview.
  • Catch translation problems: highlights missing keys, invalid interpolation arguments, ignored-scope references, and optionally unused dictionary keys and scopes.
  • Complete the right key: suggests full, relative, and partial keys using the namespace and translator scope inferred at the cursor.
  • Understand values at a glance: hover over a key to preview its default-locale translation or inspect the children of a scope.
  • Monitor project health: view dictionary and key totals, unused-key counts, configuration issues, and an on-demand report for invalid usages.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.3.0

  • New tool window that shows status and can generate project health report.
  • Now supporting multiple namespaces.
  • Added missing-key, missing interpolation argument diagnostics.
  • Added workspace metrics and an on-demand project health report to the tool window.
  • Added automatic configuration discovery, starter configuration creation, and support for external dictionary directories.

idea-plugin.name: Tolgee
idea-plugin.description:
Tolgee for JetBrains

Bring the Tolgee localization platform into your IDE. Push, pull, and autocomplete translation keys — with ICU parameter support — without leaving the editor.

Features

  • Tool window — link an IDE project to a Tolgee project, browse local translation files, push/pull whole projects or single files.
  • Code completion — translation keys autocomplete inside recognized call sites in JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX/TSX, Java, Kotlin, and Android strings.xml.
  • ICU parameters — when a key uses parameters (including plurals), the plugin inserts an argument shaped for the host language ({ name: name } in JS, params={{ name: name }} in the <T> component, mapOf("name" to name) in Kotlin, Map.of("name", name) in Java) and pre-selects the first placeholder so you can start typing immediately.
  • Local-first cache — completion reads from the on-disk translation files, so it stays fast and works offline. Push and Pull refresh the cache automatically.
  • Scoped push / pull — right-click a namespace directory or a single <lang>.json to sync just that scope, or use the toolbar to sync the whole project.

Getting started

  1. Open the Tolgee tool window on the right sidebar.
  2. Click +, paste your Tolgee instance URL and API key (a Project API Key tgpak_… or a Personal Access Token tgpat_…).
  3. Click Load projects, pick one, hit Add. The plugin pulls translations and warms the completion cache.
  4. Start typing a key name inside t('…') or <T keyName="…" /> — suggestions appear immediately.

Compatibility

Requires IntelliJ Platform 2025.1 or later. Works in IntelliJ IDEA (Ultimate and Community), WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, RustRover, RubyMine, PhpStorm, Android Studio, and other IntelliJ-based IDEs. Language-specific completion loads only if the corresponding language plugin is present — everything else works everywhere.

Source and support

github.com/bdshadow/tolgee-intellij-plugin — issues, source, contributions welcome.

Community-maintained by a Tolgee core contributor. Not (yet) part of the official Tolgee product family — support and bug reports go through the plugin's GitHub repository, not through Tolgee's channels. "Tolgee" is a trademark of Tolgee s.r.o.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.0.2

  • Declare Kotlin K1/K2 compatibility so Kotlin completion loads on IDEs running the Kotlin plugin in K2 mode (default in 2024.2+).
  • Drop the deprecated VcsFileListenerContextHelper suppression from Pull — restores the standard "Add to VCS?" prompt on pull-created files and fixes an IncompatibleClassChangeError against IDEA 2026.x.
  • Migrate ReadAction.compute to runReadAction { … } in the key-cache builder.

idea-plugin.name: SnakeCharm
idea-plugin.description:
SnakeCharm plugin for PyCharm / IntelliJ Platform IDEs adds IDE support for Snakemake workflows language, that is widely used in Bioinformatics. The plugin is developed by JetBrains Research Team, for more details see project home page.

Please report features suggestions or found bugs to project issue tracker.

Features highlights:

NB: To activate all features please enable Snakemake support in Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Snakemake. Snakemake framework should be configured to use python interpreter with snakemake module installed.

Features available in Snakefile and *.smk, *.rule, *.rules files:

  • Python code syntax highlighting

  • Snakemake specific syntax highlighting

    • Highlight rule section names
    • Syntax highlighting for Snakemake string format language, e.g. in strings like "results/sample_{genome}.bam".
    • Special highlighting for rule wildcards and their usages

  • Code completion and goto to declaration for:

    • Snakemake specific variables (e.g. config, rules, etc);
    • Snakemake api methods like expand, temp, etc.
    • Rules names after rules., checkpoints after checkpoints.
    • Rules sections names after rules.my_rule_name.
    • Rule sections keywords arguments, e.g. after rules.my_rule_name.input.
    • Wildcards and sections names in shell, input, message, params and other sections
    • Paths in sections: configfile, workdir, conda, include.
    • Completion for wrappers names in wrapper: sections
    • Wrappers with detailed meta.yaml provides completion for rule section keyword arguments in output, input, params sections
    • Python methods and variables

  • Structure view for Snakemake files

  • Rules blocks folding

  • Open rule declaration by name using Navigate|Symbol...

  • Quick documentation for wrappers, that includes links to wrapper source code and paga in wrappers repository

  • Multiple code inspections for possible errors in snakemake files

Useful links:

  • Project Home Page
  • Full Changelog
  • SnakeCharm at GitHub
  • SnakeCharm in JetBrains Plugin Repository
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Released on 7.10.2026

We gratefully acknowledge external contributor Gaurav Vaidya (@gaurav) for his work porting the plugin to 2026.2.x platform API

Plugin

  • Compatibility with the unified PyCharm / IntelliJ Platform 2026.2 (build 262).
  • This release requires 2026.2 (build 262) or newer. The Python plugin API changes below are not source- or binary-compatible with earlier IDEs, so pluginSinceBuild was raised from 261 to 262. 2026.1 is not supported: the annotator API it offered was removed in 2026.2, and advertising compatibility the binary cannot honour is the failure mode #569 was rejected for.

Changed

  • 2026.2 removed the com.jetbrains.python.validation.PyAnnotator base class. Annotators are now plain PyElementVisitors that receive a PyAnnotationHolder at construction, matching the platform's own *AnnotatorVisitor classes, so SnakeCharm's annotators are built per annotation pass instead of being shared singletons.
  • 2026.2 ships Kotlin 2.4 metadata in the Python plugin, which the previous Kotlin 2.2 compiler cannot read; the build now compiles with Kotlin 2.3 and aligns the forced runtime kotlin-stdlib with the platform's 2.4.x.

Fixed

  • Implicitly imported snakemake names (expand, protected, lookup, …) stopped resolving after any change to the project roots — e.g. switching interpreter or attaching a library. The platform invalidates library PSI on a roots change, which emptied the implicit-symbol cache with nothing to rebuild it in time; the cache is now refreshed on rootsChanged (#578).

idea-plugin.name: Lets-Plot in SciView
idea-plugin.description:
The plugin adds support for interactive plots in IntelliJ-based IDEs with the Scientific mode enabled.

The Scientific mode in PyCharm and IntelliJ IDEA provides support for interactive scientific computing and data visualization.

To learn more about Scientific mode check these help pages:
  • Scientific mode in PyCharm
  • Scientific mode in IntelliJ IDEA

Lets-Plot is an open-source plotting library for statistical data.

This plugin requires the Lets-Plot Python package to be installed in the project Python environment.

You will find a couple examples in this GitHub repository: lets-plot-pycharm-samples.

The plugin is 100% compatible with Lets-Plot v 4.10.1. The compatibility will be kept up for the later versions of Lets-Plot.

idea-plugin.name: Kotlin Notebook
idea-plugin.description:
Please note: Starting with v2026.2, JetBrains will sunset Kotlin Notebook as a product and will no longer maintain it. Kotlin Notebook will be unbundled from IntelliJ IDEA and continue as an open-source, community-driven project hosted on GitHub.

Kotlin notebooks are interactive worksheets with rich outputs that allow you to explore and experiment with your Kotlin code without additional environment setup. The Kotlin Notebook plugin is a client for the Kotlin Jupyter kernel that enables you to create and edit notebooks directly within IntelliJ IDEA. There are other clients that support Kotlin notebooks, including Datalore, Jupyter Notebook, and JupyterLab.

The plugin comes with various features that are available in ordinary Kotlin files in the IDE, as well as additional Kotlin notebook-specific extensions. These include enhanced syntax highlighting, inlay hints, inspections, find usages, and refactorings, all of which help you write Kotlin code more efficiently. Many features are state-aware, meaning that finding usages or renaming will consider your current definitions and loaded libraries.

Notebooks have two key distinguishing features compared to regular REPLs. Firstly, they allow you to save the entire session to a file, preserving both the code and the execution results. Secondly, the execution results can include more than just plain text; they can also encompass images in various formats, arbitrary HTML (including JavaScript and CSS), and even specifications for Swing outputs that are rendered directly within IntelliJ IDEA. To learn more about the diverse range of outputs and their rendering, please refer to this link. Additionally, there is a sample notebook, showcasing different types of outputs.

With the Kotlin Notebook plugin, you can add binary dependencies from a remote Maven repository or a local one. For this, use @file:DependsOn annotation or Gradle-like syntax. Some libraries have special notebook integrations and can be imported with the %use line magic that comes with code insights to help you choose the correct library version. You can create a library descriptor or an integration for any library using this guide. Integrations allow libraries to have rich outputs, add default imports, provide reflection-based code generation, and more.

You can also use notebooks to explore the code in your current project – sources and binary dependencies can easily be added to the notebook context. To set this up or to adjust the Kotlin Notebook plugin appearance, use the following navigation in the IDE:


            File -> Settings... -> Tools -> Kotlin Notebook

To learn more about using Kotlin notebooks, check out the Kotlin Jupyter kernel documentation. If you have any questions or want to connect with other Kotlin developers who use notebooks, join the #notebooks channel in the Kotlin Slack. To file an issue, use Kotlin Notebook YouTrack. Stay tuned!
idea-plugin.change-notes:
What's New in Kotlin Notebook 2026.1

  • Debugger support – a new Debug Cell action lets you start a debugging session directly from a notebook cell. You can step through your project code and library dependencies while using the notebook as an executable entry point.
  • Kotlin API for Jupyter Widgets (%use widgets) – a Kotlin-first implementation of the Jupyter Widgets protocol for interactive notebook UI. It supports state synchronization over Jupyter Comms, property change listeners, custom messages, layouts, and rich output capture.
  • Improved AI – higher quality AI chat responses and more reliable notebook generation. Better context handling and more consistent results in real-world projects.
  • Notekit API (%use notekit) – programmatic access to the current notebook from Kotlin kernel code. It allows querying notebook structure, inserting, replacing, and deleting cells, modifying metadata, and executing cells via a synchronous request–response protocol over Jupyter Comms.

More details will be available in the upcoming Kotlin Notebook blog post.

idea-plugin.name: QueryTester
idea-plugin.description:
nscale Query Tester – NQL queries straight from IntelliJ IDEA

No more tool switching. Anyone who tests NQL queries against the nscale Application Layer knows the routine: launch another tool, retype the connection data, squint at raw output, switch back to the IDE. The nscale Query Tester turns all of that into a single move.

The plugin adds its own tool window at the bottom of your IDE: pick a connection, write your query, hit Ctrl+Enter – and the result appears as a clear, page-by-page browsable table. No context switch, no broken workflow, no waiting around.

Write NQL the way you write code

Autocompletion covers the full surface of the NQL language: keywords, named operators, query functions, $-constants and context variables – each shown with its category, functions inserted complete with parentheses and the caret already in the right place. On top of that, the plugin fetches the indexing property names of the selected document area live from the session and offers them as completions too. Whatever you queried last is one dropdown away in the query history.

Several queries in parallel

Every tab is an independent query context with its own connection, its own mode and its own result set. Compare, cross-check, iterate – all at once instead of one after another. Repository, Masterdata and Principals are available as query modes, each with its own options panel, rounded out by the Aggregate and Version variants.

Results you can actually work with

The result table follows the server's result table dynamically – no fixed schema, no lost columns. Paging is injected automatically: you write plain NQL and still get a paged table with a page counter. A padlock icon marks locked resources and updates immediately. Resource ids or entire rows go to the clipboard with a single click, using a configurable field separator.

Repository operations right from the hit list

A right-click is all it takes: search onward from a hit or jump to its parent level, show the full repository path, lock and unlock resources, create documents and folders – and, once you enable it in the settings, delete them as well. The search can be narrowed to a specific subtree via a root resource id.

Set up in two minutes

Connections are stored application-wide, so they are available in every project – including SSL and timeouts. Rows per page, history size, column visibility and the font of the result table adapt to your working style in the settings.

Requirements: IntelliJ IDEA 2024.3, a reachable nscale Application Layer instance and valid credentials.

Open source under the MIT license. Free on the JetBrains Marketplace – just search for "nscale Query Tester" and install.

idea-plugin.name: Livy Query Console
idea-plugin.description:
Livy Query Console lets you run Spark, PySpark, and Spark SQL code on a remote cluster via Apache Livy directly from your JetBrains IDE.

It is designed for quick exploration, debugging, and day-to-day data engineering workflows: write a snippet, run it in a Livy interactive session, inspect the output, and iterate — without leaving the IDE.

Key features

  • Livy work file: open a dedicated reusable Livy work surface, route editor selection/current line/whole file into it, and execute snippets without leaving the IDE workflow. The work file follows the bound execution kind (`sql`, `pyspark` / `python`, or fallback plain Spark text) and reuses host-IDE highlighting where available.
  • Result viewer: each run is added as a new tab with:
    • Raw response (full JSON output from Livy)
    • Pretty view (human-readable summary including errors and stack traces)
    • Table view for Spark ASCII tables (e.g. output of df.show())
  • Session logs: view Livy session logs in a separate dialog with refresh, copy, and quick find next/previous.
  • Statements browser: list recent statements in a session, inspect deeper details, copy code, and reopen statement code in a bound Livy work file.
  • Tool Window: a “Livy Sessions” tool window that shows active sessions with refresh/auto-refresh, configurable columns, logs/statements actions, and termination for plugin-managed sessions.
  • Connection profiles: keep multiple named Livy targets with per-profile session kind, resource parameters, verbose connection diagnostics, and session management strategy.
  • Managed sessions: reuse compatible plugin-managed sessions, cap managed session count per profile, and optionally clean up the oldest idle managed session when the limit is reached.
  • Browser-based authentication: for SSO/OAuth2-proxy protected Livy endpoints, open an embedded browser login, capture per-profile session cookies, store them in the IDE Password Safe, and prompt to sign in when API calls look authentication-gated.
  • Local history: recent snippets and the last draft per profile can be restored locally for quick rerun/reuse. This is plain-text local persistence, not notebook or remote session restore.

Typical usage

  1. Open Livy: Open Work File (Tools → Livy) or use the Livy editor/project popup actions.
  2. Choose the connection profile to bind the work file or run action to.
  3. If the endpoint is behind SSO/OAuth2 proxy, use Authenticate via Browser… in Settings → Tools → Livy or follow the sign-in prompt.
  4. Route a selection/current line/whole file into Livy, or use Run Current / Run File inside the work file.
  5. Inspect results, logs, and statements, then iterate.

Note: This plugin requires access to a running Apache Livy server. Authentication/SSL behavior depends on your environment (for corporate/self-signed certificates you may need to add the CA certificate to the JetBrains Runtime trust store).

Current scope: the plugin supports multiple named connection profiles for direct Livy HTTP(S) connectivity and SSO/OAuth2-proxy flows that can be satisfied by reusable browser-session cookies. Existing work files and loaded session views stay bound to the profile snapshot they were opened with. Optional local history stores recent snippets and the last draft per profile in plain text on the local machine only. SQL work files support a narrow semicolon-delimited current-statement heuristic; PySpark/plain Spark work files stay on selection-or-file execution semantics. This is a lightweight execution workflow, not notebook persistence or semantic Spark language tooling. Browser sign-in requires an IDE runtime with embedded browser support and stores captured per-profile session cookies in the IDE Password Safe. Manual auth headers/tokens, Kerberos, and generic OAuth token management outside browser-session cookies are still not implemented.

idea-plugin.name: Data Preprocessor
idea-plugin.description:
Stop writing repetitive pandas preprocessing scripts.

Data Preprocessor is an in-IDE toolkit for cleaning, transforming, and preparing datasets directly inside your JetBrains IDE.

Load a CSV, Excel (.xlsx), or JSON file, profile your data instantly, handle missing values, remove duplicates and outliers, normalize columns, and generate ready-to-run Python (pandas) code from your workflow. Pro unlocks R and SQL generation, reusable pipelines, column visualisations, custom regex rules, and batch processing — all without leaving the IDE.

Key features:
  • Column Profiling & Statistics — type, null count, unique count, mean, median, std dev, min, max, mode
  • Missing Value Handling — drop rows or fill with mean, median, mode, or a custom value
  • Duplicate Removal — detect and remove duplicate rows in one click
  • Outlier Detection (IQR) — identify and remove outliers using the IQR fence method
  • Data Normalization — Min-Max scaling [0, 1], Z-Score standardisation (mean=0, std=1), or Robust Scaler (median/IQR)
  • Column Type Casting — cast any column to int, float, boolean, or string
  • Label Encoding — encode categorical columns to integer indices
  • One-Hot Encoding — expand categorical columns into binary dummy columns
  • Train / Test Split — split the dataset with a configurable ratio; reflected in generated Python and Pro R code
  • Sort Column — sort the dataset ascending or descending by any column (numeric or text)
  • Filter Rows — keep only rows matching a condition (==, !=, >, <, >=, <=, contains)
  • Regex Replace [Pro] — clean text columns with custom regex find/replace rules, including capture-group replacements
  • Reusable Pipelines [Pro] — import/export cleaning pipelines as `.dpp` JSON files
  • Multi-File Batch Mode [Pro] — apply the current pipeline to many CSV, Excel, or JSON files and export cleaned CSV copies
  • Python Code Generation — one click produces a complete, ready-to-run pandas script
  • R Code Generation [Pro] — one click produces an equivalent base-R script; readxl / jsonlite / fastDummies imported only when needed
  • SQL Code Generation [Pro] — one click produces a PostgreSQL-style CTE template for database-side preprocessing
  • Undo / Redo — step back and forward through pipeline edits without losing work
  • Export cleaned CSV — choose where to save the transformed dataset via a file dialog
  • Copy cleaned data as TSV — paste applied results directly into Excel or Google Sheets
  • Column Visualisations [Pro] — histogram and box plot per numeric column rendered inside the tool window; charts update automatically after Apply
  • Settings — configure preview row limit, default normalization method, and default train/test ratio

Built for data scientists, analysts, and developers who want faster preprocessing without leaving their IDE.

Compatible with IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, DataGrip, and other JetBrains IDEs.


Privacy: This plugin does not collect, store, or transmit any user data. All processing is performed locally within the IDE.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 1.8.3 — Visualise Pro activation refresh: after a user starts a trial or activates a Pro license, the locked Visualise tab now swaps to the real chart UI without requiring an IDE restart. Pro gates also read JetBrains product license data and product expiration dates for active Marketplace trials.
