idea-plugin.name: I18n Support Plus
idea-plugin.description:
Turns i18n keys into first-class code symbols in WebStorm, IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate and PhpStorm: see each key's value and status, jump to it, rename it, translate it and keep every locale in sync.

Works with i18next / react-i18next, vue-i18n (Nuxt), next-intl, lingui, react-intl, ngx-translate, Transloco, svelte-i18n, i18n-js and Laravel / Blade, in JS, TS, JSX, TSX, Vue SFC, Angular templates and PHP, with JSON, JSON5, YAML, PO/POT and plain TS/JS catalogues. A setup wizard configures it on first launch, monorepo modules included.

  • See — gutter status per key (all / some / no locale), inline value hints, folding and hover in a preview locale, completion of real keys, namespaces included
  • Edit safely — extract hardcoded strings (variables and plural forms included), rename a key or a whole level across every locale and call site (Shift+F6), move a key to another namespace; one Ctrl+Z undoes the files and the code
  • Translate — opt-in machine translation of empty locales, for one key or a whole locale, through a local Ollama (nothing leaves the machine), DeepL, LibreTranslate, Google or any OpenAI-compatible API; variables, tags and the target language's plural forms are kept, and nothing is written before a preview
  • Plurals done right — i18next _one / _other keys and nested plural objects resolve, missing CLDR forms per language are reported, ICU messages are validated
  • Stay healthy — tool window with tree and table views, filters for missing, empty, duplicate and unreferenced keys, coverage per namespace and locale, a keep list for keys used outside the code, keys synchronizer, cleanup, CSV and XLIFF export / import, comparison with a Git branch
  • Your own calls — rules turn translate('key') or __('key') into translation calls, and a module can write its own wrapper's call at extraction
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.9.0 - 2026-10-10

Features

  • [Translation] Machine translation of empty locales, opt-in per project: Translate Empty Locales in a key's dialog fills its empty locales from the reference one, through the engines set in Settings | Tools | i18n Support Plus | Machine Translation — a local Ollama by default (nothing leaves the machine), any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, DeepL, LibreTranslate or Google. Off until the project opts in; API keys go to the password safe. Variables, tags and ICU syntax are protected, and a translation losing one is refused. A plural form follows the target language's forms: file_one is left empty in Japanese, and file_few, which English lacks, is translated from file_other and flagged for review
  • [Translation] Fill Missing Translations… machine-translates every key a module's locale lacks, from the reference locale, and previews the proposals before writing them in one undoable command. A refused proposal stays unchecked, an existing value is never replaced. A plural key gets the forms the target language has — few and many for Russian, other alone for Japanese — those translated from other left unchecked for review; an ICU plural is listed but not translated. It is also on the context menu of a locale column in the translations table, for that table's module and locale. DeepL, Google and OpenAI-compatible engines get several keys per request instead of one — up to 50, or 20 for an LLM
  • [Inspections] Keys used outside the code can be kept: a key received from an API, stored in a database or read by a library leaves no trace in the code. Keys used outside the code in the settings lists them — exact keys, prefixes (errors.) or globs (*.label), optionally with a namespace. A kept key is never reported nor offered for deletion; Keep this key on the inspection adds it (#367)
  • [i18next] fallbackNS is followed: under useTranslation('admin'), t('shared.ok') resolves in common when admin lacks it — navigation, hint, and no longer offered for deletion. Read from the i18next configuration, or set in Fallback namespaces (#368)
  • [Refactoring] Shift+F6 renames an intermediate level of a key: button.* becomes actions.* in every locale, at every call site and in a hook's keyPrefix, in one undo. A level that already exists is refused; keys built at runtime are listed, not rewritten (#366)
  • [Vue] <i18n-t keypath> and v-t are read as keys: <i18n-t keypath="terms.accept"> and v-t="'home.title'" (or its path) resolve, navigate and report unknown keys like $t(). No completion or folding yet (#363)
  • [VCS] Compare Translations with Branch…: the translation keys the working tree changes against a branch (origin/main by default), committed or not, and the locales left behind — the translations of a pull request. Needs the bundled Git plugin
  • [Setup wizard] Nuxt and next-intl are detected: @nuxtjs/i18n ticks vue-i18n, and next-intl becomes a framework of its own, with a preset that keeps its t, reads ICU {name} and lays files out as messages/{lang}.json (#360)
  • [Settings] A module preset fills the file layout: choosing i18next, vue-i18n, lingui, react-intl, ngx-translate or Transloco fills the path and key templates with the layout the framework documents. Hand-typed templates are replaced only after confirmation
  • [Settings] Suggest a layout as a new preset: a module whose templates leave its preset opens a pre-filled GitHub issue with them. Only the templates are sent, never a path or project name
  • [Extraction] A module can write its own wrapper's call: Call template (translate({key})) replaces the call the intention and Batch Extract write for that module's files
  • [Translation dialog] Delete the edited key: Delete removes it from every locale, plural forms included, with the usual warning when it is still used and a single undo

Documentation

  • [Marketplace] The plugin description says what the plugin does: the generic summary is replaced by what sets it apart — the IDEs it runs in, every framework and file format, machine translation, plural forms per language, safe renames with one undo, health checks and custom calls

Bug Fixes

  • [React] <Trans i18nKey="key"> resolves and is checked: listed among the i18next syntaxes, the attribute carried no reference — no Ctrl+click, in .jsx as in .tsx — and an unknown key went unreported. It now navigates, is annotated like t('key'), follows a module's key template and is left out under a module preset of another framework. Hovering it shows the translation table, and folding replaces it with its value, as for t('key')
  • [Inspections] Unused-key reports are trustworthy again: with two locales or more, Unused translation key never reported anything, a same-named JSON property counting as a usage, and Code Vision counted one usage per locale (#410). Keys used under a hook's keyPrefix or with an ns option were reported with a Delete quick fix (#408), and a key reached through a dynamic namespace (t(`${ns}:status.ok`)) was offered for deletion (#409)
  • [Inspections] "No reference found" instead of "unused": the plugin knows no code refers to a key, not that it is unused. Messages, the table's Usage column and the cleanup preview say so, and point to Keys used outside the code. Action names are unchanged (#370)
  • [Translations] A file outside the translations root no longer answers for a namespace: any common.json in the project — a serverless config in a monorepo — answered t('common:…') and showed as an extra locale
  • [Refactoring] Renaming a key no longer fails at random on a large project: Shift+F6 collected the key's call sites from the search threads into a set not made for them, which two threads adding at once could corrupt, and the rename then stopped on an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException

Tests

  • [References] Every path that reads a key runs the key resolution fixtures: KeyResolutionPathsFixtureTest takes the cases of KeyResolutionFixtureTest through the hint, the inlay hint, folding, the gutter icon and completion (a hook's namespace, a key prefix, a module's own keys), in a monorepo checking that no other module's value shows. The gaps it found — <Trans i18nKey> showed no hint and was not folded — are fixed
  • [References] One fixture project for the hard cases of key resolution: KeyResolutionFixtureTest runs an explicit and a default namespace, nested keys, a hook's namespace and key prefix, an ns option, a plural key, unknown keys and namespaces, a dynamic key and a three-module monorepo (each module resolving in its own files, a module key template) through annotation and Ctrl+click. The gaps it found — <Trans i18nKey> neither navigated nor reported an unknown key — are fixed
  • [Inspections] One fixture project for the hard cases of unused keys: UnusedKeysFixtureTest runs template literals, key rules, hook namespaces and prefixes, fallbackNS, the keep list and a two-module monorepo through the inspection, Scan Orphans and Cleanup Unused Keys, asserting both what is reported and what must never be (#369)

idea-plugin.name: SnipHive
idea-plugin.description:
Access your SnipHive code snippets directly in your JetBrains IDE.

Features:

  • Tool window for browsing and searching snippets and notes
  • Create snippets from selected code
  • Insert snippets via menu or code completion
  • Notes support with Markdown
  • Favorites and Archive views
  • Tags management with colors
  • Workspace switching
  • GitHub Gist import
  • Secure credential storage using IDE Password Safe
  • End-to-end encryption support (E2EE) with client-side encryption
  • Support for all JetBrains IDEs (IntelliJ IDEA, PhpStorm, PyCharm, WebStorm, etc.)

Security Note: E2EE uses RSA-4096 OAEP + AES-256-GCM encryption. Your encryption keys never leave your device.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.2

  • Added a Tags management tab for creating, editing, deleting, and refreshing tags from the tool window.
  • Refresh snippet and note lists automatically after creating new items.
  • Improved tag selection layout in create snippet and note dialogs so tag checkboxes wrap cleanly.

idea-plugin.name: SQLFolio
idea-plugin.description:
SQLFolio - your personal and team SQL query library inside DataGrip and all IntelliJ-based IDEs.

Save, organise and instantly reuse SQL snippets without leaving your IDE.

Two-section library
  • My Queries - stored locally, never synced
  • Shared - synced with the team in real time when sync is enabled
Query library
  • Folder-based organisation with unlimited nesting
  • Drag and drop reordering with live drop indicator
  • Inline rename (F2 or double-click)
  • Duplicate, delete, copy SQL to clipboard
  • SQL preview tooltip on hover
  • Live search by name and SQL content
  • Export and import JSON backup
Editor integration
  • Ctrl+Alt+Q saves selected text or the whole file to SQLFolio
  • Run any saved query directly in a DataGrip console
Team sync - bring your own backend
Connect your own database. Only the Shared section is synced.

  • Path-based history - every query tracked individually by its tree path; full audit trail per node
  • User identity - set your display name; the database assigns your numeric user ID automatically
  • Advisory locking - lock a single query or an entire folder subtree while editing
  • Recycle bin - deleted items kept for 30 days with one-click restore
  • Rename without duplicates - renaming or moving a folder updates the existing row, no history clutter
  • PostgreSQL - real-time via LISTEN/NOTIFY (under 200 ms)
  • SQLite - real-time via file watcher (under 1 s)
  • REST API - polling with configurable interval
  • Global version retention - keep the last N versions for the whole team (default 10)
  • Conflict detection - optimistic locking prevents accidental overwrites
  • Auto-push - changes pushed 2 seconds after last edit
  • Payload size limit - configurable max size to protect the database
Shortcuts
  • Ctrl+Alt+Q - save selected SQL to SQLFolio
  • F2 - rename selected item
  • Delete - delete selected item
SQLFolio stores queries locally using IntelliJ project storage. No data is sent anywhere by default. Sync only connects to the backend you configure.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.1
  • New workspace created in the database - creating a new workspace from the Browse dialog now inserts the row in the database immediately, so it appears in the list right away without needing a first push.
  • User registration persisted on Register click - clicking Register/Refresh ID now saves the display name together with the numeric ID. Previously, clicking Apply after registering would reset the ID because the stored name did not match yet.
  • Force Sync toolbar button - new Refresh button in the query tree toolbar (positioned after Capture from Editor). Resets the version cache and pulls everything fresh from the database. Useful when rows have been modified or deleted directly in the database outside the plugin.
  • Restore from bin now visible in tree - after restoring a deleted item the tree was not refreshing because the restore operation does not bump the workspace version counter. The pull after restore now bypasses the version cache.
  • Push failure on old schema fixed - databases created with an earlier version had a non-null "data" column on the workspaces table. A migration step now removes the NOT NULL constraint so inserts work correctly again.
1.1.0
  • Path-based history - each query and folder is stored as a separate row with a parent_id reference, forming a proper tree. Renaming or moving a node updates the existing row instead of creating a duplicate.
  • User identity - configure your display name in Settings; the database auto-assigns a numeric user ID used in every history entry.
  • Query locking - lock a single query or an entire folder subtree. Locked items show a padlock in the tree and a warning banner in the editor.
  • Recycle bin - deleted items are soft-deleted and kept for 30 days. Restore from the Bin toolbar button. Expired items are purged automatically on connect.
  • Global retention - version history is pruned globally on every push using the configured retention limit.
  • Auto-migration - new schema columns (parent_id, deleted_at) are added automatically to existing databases without data loss.
  • Reconnect fix - switching to a different database now correctly resets the local sync state and pulls fresh data.
1.0.0
  • Initial release
  • Folder-based query organisation with drag and drop
  • Live search by name and SQL content
  • Export and import JSON
  • My Queries and Shared sections
  • PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY and SQLite file watcher for real-time sync

idea-plugin.name: ZK Framework Variables Binding
idea-plugin.description:
Full ZK Framework MVVM binding support for IntelliJ IDEA

Enhances the development experience for ZK Framework projects by bridging .zul files and Java ViewModels.

Features:

  • Automatic Usage Detection: Getters, setters, and variables referenced in .zul files are recognised as "used" — no false "No usages" warnings.
  • Bidirectional Navigation: Ctrl+Click on a binding expression in a .zul file jumps to the corresponding Java method or field.
  • Gutter Icons: Gutter markers on Java methods show where they are used in .zul files.
  • Find Usages: Finds all usages of a method, including ZK binding expressions in .zul files.
  • Full Binding Support: @bind, @load, @save, @init, @command, and all other ZK MVVM binding annotations.
  • Safe Refactoring: Renaming a Java method updates all matching binding references in .zul files automatically.
  • Java in <zscript>: Full Java language support (completion, highlighting, navigation) inside <zscript> blocks in .zul files.

Supported binding patterns:

  • @bind(vm.propertyName)
  • @load(vm.propertyName)
  • @save(vm.propertyName)
  • @init(vm.propertyName)
  • @command('methodName')
  • All other ZK MVVM binding patterns
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Version 1.1.2

  • New: Java language injection inside <zscript> blocks — full code completion, syntax highlighting, and navigation available.
  • Fix: Import resolution logic reworked — methods and variables used in .zul files no longer show a spurious "No usages" tag in the IDE.

Version 1.0.0

  • Initial release.
  • Automatic usage detection for getters and setters referenced in .zul bindings.
  • Full Java ↔ ZUL navigation.
  • Support for all ZK binding types.
  • Gutter icons indicating .zul usages.

idea-plugin.name: QuickCommand
idea-plugin.description:
Quick Command

Turn your most-used terminal commands into clickable buttons. No more typing the same docker compose up, npm run dev, or ./gradlew test over and over.

Features

  • Terminal toolbar buttons — one click sends the command to the active terminal session.
  • Status bar widget — quick access from anywhere, even when the terminal is hidden.
  • Command groups — bundle related commands into a dropdown to keep the UI tidy.
  • Two execution modes — auto-run, or paste-only (review before pressing Enter).
  • Global + per-project config — share defaults across projects, override per repo.
  • JSON config with hot reload — edit the file and buttons refresh automatically.
  • Icon browser — pick from hundreds of bundled IntelliJ icons with click-to-copy.
  • Show-in control — choose which surfaces (toolbar, status bar) each button appears on.

Getting started

  1. Open any terminal — the Quick Command toolbar appears at the top.
  2. Click the gear icon → Copy Single/Group Button Example to seed your config.
  3. Open Global Settings or Project Settings, paste, save — buttons appear instantly.

Requires IntelliJ Platform 2025.3+ (build 253) and the bundled Terminal plugin.

idea-plugin.name: Antlers Toolbox
idea-plugin.description:
Rich Antlers language support for Statamic projects.

Antlers Toolbox understands your project. It reads your blueprints, collections, globals, and the rest of your YAML to power completions, documentation, and diagnostics that match what your templates can actually see, without any extra configuration.

  • Completes tags, modifiers, and parameters alongside your own data, including blueprint fields, collection handles, taxonomy terms, view names, and permissions
  • Debugs Antlers templates with breakpoints, scope variables, hover inspections, and inline render timings, with no extra dependencies needed
  • Ships more than twenty inspections with quick-fixes, covering everything from unknown modifiers and unresolved partials to Statamic version compatibility
  • Documents tags, modifiers, and fields on hover, including what each field exposes inside its loop and set examples for Bard and Replicator
  • Renames blueprint fields across YAML and templates, with Find Usages in both directions
  • Navigates to partials, custom PHP tags and modifiers, svg files, and blueprint declarations
  • Includes refactorings and editor comforts such as extract to partial, condition to ternary conversion, breadcrumbs, and live templates
  • Supports .antlers.html, .antlers.xml, and .antlers.php files, as well as Statamic component tags inside Blade
idea-plugin.change-notes:
What's New

  • Added support for the Antlers debugger, including breakpoints, scope variables, hover inspections, and inline performance timings
  • Project data is now read directly from your project's YAML files, with the PHP probe available as an opt-in for Eloquent-based sites
  • Added blueprint field renaming and Find Usages across YAML and templates
  • Added completions and navigation for custom tags, modifiers, and query scopes, including those provided by installed addons
  • Added permission completions for user:can, taxonomy term completions, and smarter condition values such as view names for current_template and set handles inside Replicator or Bard loops
  • Expanded query condition support with the full operator catalog, value suggestions, and operator documentation on hover
  • Added typed parameter validation, modifier chain type checking, and Statamic version compatibility warnings, with version data taken from the CMS release history
  • Added inspections for leftover dump output, partial recursion, overlapping tag pairs, purge-prone class names, deprecated modifiers, missing required partial parameters, and unaliased query builders
  • Added an Extract Partial refactoring and an intention to convert simple conditions to ternary or gatekeeper expressions
  • Field hovers now show loop variables, a set example for Bard and Replicator fields, and links to the official documentation
  • Added editor conveniences: Tab moves between parameter values, svg paths and idehelper directives complete, layout front matter offers view names, and quotes pair automatically

Fixes

idea-plugin.name: LSP Senior
idea-plugin.description:
LSP Senior transforma o IntelliJ IDEA num editor completo para a Linguagem Senior de Programação (LSP) — as regras, telas e relatórios do ERP Senior. Colorização, navegação, autocomplete e documentação que você não tem dentro do SGI, funcionando automaticamente em arquivos .lsp e .lspt.

O plugin entende a estrutura do seu código (blocos Se, Enquanto, Regra, Inicio/Fim), o escopo das variáveis e as funções do seu projeto — e traz embutido o catálogo de funções nativas (com assinatura e descrição) e de variáveis reservadas da linguagem.

Escrita e autocomplete

  • Autocomplete inteligente: palavras-chave, tipos, booleanos, funções do seu projeto e centenas de funções nativas com a assinatura ao lado — ex.: Concatena(Alfa Str1, Alfa Str2, Alfa Str3, Alfa End Destino). Ao aceitar uma função, o cursor entra entre os parênteses para você informar os argumentos.
  • Variáveis com o tipo: as variáveis do escopo aparecem no autocomplete já exibindo o tipo (Alfa, Numero, Data...).
  • Documentação inline (Ctrl+Q): mostra a assinatura completa e a descrição oficial das funções nativas.
  • Live Templates para os padrões do dia a dia (cursor SQL, validação de permissão, auditoria, paginação, resposta JSON...).

Leitura e colorização

  • Colorização de sintaxe por categoria: controle, tipos, declaração, funções, operadores, comentários e textos.
  • Variáveis reservadas em destaque (NomEmp, DatSis, Web_HTML...), reconhecidas sem diferenciar maiúsculas de minúsculas.
  • Corretor ortográfico desativado nesses arquivos — sem sublinhados em identificadores e texto em português.

Navegação

  • Ir para a declaração (Ctrl/Cmd+B): funções em qualquer arquivo do projeto; variáveis respeitando o escopo do bloco.
  • Localizar usos (Alt+Shift+F7) e realce de ocorrências no arquivo.
  • Renomear (Shift+F6) funções e variáveis com segurança de escopo.
  • Structure View (outline navegável da hierarquia de blocos) e breadcrumbs — o caminho de blocos (Regra / Se / Enquanto / Inicio...) que contêm o cursor aparece no topo do editor. Essenciais em arquivos com centenas de linhas.

Edição

  • Bracket matching e auto-close para { }, ( ), [ ] e Inicio/Fim.
  • Code folding de blocos { }, Inicio/Fim e banners de comentário.
  • Ícone próprio para arquivos .lsp e .lspt.

Requisitos: IntelliJ IDEA 2025.3 ou superior (Community ou Ultimate). O plugin TextMate, já incluso na IDE, é uma dependência.

Após instalar, reinicie a IDE — parte dos recursos (como o bundle de colorização) só carrega na inicialização.
idea-plugin.change-notes:

  • Cursor entre os parênteses ao completar uma função — pronto para digitar os argumentos.

idea-plugin.name: SnapLens
idea-plugin.description:
Copy Kotlin code to the clipboard as a polished image, ready to paste into chats, docs, PRs and slides.
  • Select lines and press ⌃⌘C (macOS) or Ctrl+Alt+Shift+P — the clipboard now holds a PNG of the selection.
  • Rendered with your current editor color scheme, including semantic highlighting, in your editor font with ligatures. Errors, warnings, the caret row and search hits are left out.
  • Context headers: the enclosing class and function signatures are included automatically, skipped lines collapse into a small "N lines" pill and matching closing braces keep the snippet balanced. The selection is re-indented one level under its nearest header, so deeply nested code isn't pushed right.
  • Real file line numbers, opaque image that pastes cleanly everywhere — including apps that flatten transparency, like Teams and Messenger — rendered at 2× for sharp results on HiDPI screens.
  • Focus on what matters: context is dimmed so the selection stands out, and inferred types and parameter names appear as inlay hints.
  • File header with the package-relative path and the current Git branch.
  • Multi-caret: combine several snippets of one file into a single image. Blocks the selection opens or closes are balanced automatically.
  • No selection? The whole enclosing function is captured.
Configure emphasis, inlay hints, header, fixed width, padding, scale, line numbers, context headers and the skipped-lines style under Settings → Tools → SnapLens, with a live preview.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 0.2.1
    • Fixed: expression-body functions whose body is a lambda (fun save() = withContext(IO) {) lost their closing brace. Every bracket opened or closed on a visible line is now balanced, including } else { chains.
    • The accent bar is gone; emphasis is now only the dimmed context.
    • The branch in the header uses a proper Git branch icon.
    • No more : Unit hints on expression-body functions.
  • 0.2.0
    • Emphasis: context lines are dimmed.
    • File header: package-relative path (compact package prefix stripped) and the current Git branch.
    • Inlay hints: inferred types of properties and locals, expression-body return types, and parameter names on positional arguments, computed from the Kotlin analysis.
    • Multi-caret: every caret or selection becomes its own segment of one image; a caret without a selection contributes its line.
    • Balance: blocks, calls and brackets opened or closed by the selection get their matching line, so every snippet stays balanced.
    • Optional fixed width at the code style's right margin, with soft-wrap and continuation indent.
    • Rendering now runs in the background with the Kotlin analysis, off the UI thread.
  • 0.1.0 — initial release.
    • Copy the selected Kotlin lines to the clipboard as a PNG: current color scheme with semantic highlighting, real line numbers, rounded card with transparent corners.
    • Context headers: enclosing class and function signatures are included, with skipped lines collapsed into a gap row and matching closing braces.
    • No selection captures the whole enclosing function.
    • Settings page with a live preview: line numbers, context headers, padding, corner radius, scale and maximum line length.

Solve tasks from the JavaRush course without leaving your IDE: the plugin brings the task list, the task text and the check results into the development environment you already work in.

How to use · FAQ · Support · Terms
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Version 251.1.186

New in this build

  • The plugin no longer heats up the computer to 100% CPU. On some machines — typically behind an antivirus or a corporate proxy that inspects encrypted traffic — the Java network client inside the IDE could get stuck in an endless loop after a connection closed, one CPU core per stuck connection, and the plugin opened such connections for every log line. Log records are now sent one at a time and only for warnings and errors, through the IDE's own network layer; downloads of the JDK and the game engine got a read timeout and a Cancel button (cancelling leaves a notification with an "Install JDK" button, so the course can still be set up), and the profile avatar can no longer hang the start of the IDE. If your IDE is older than 2026.2, updating it also removes the underlying Java bug
  • Rider, C# course: you can switch tasks again. Picking another task — "Open" in the preview, "Continue", "Next task" or the "Select Task" button — did nothing and the previous task stayed open, often with "Could not open the next task". The step that hides the previous task's folder from the Rider project failed when Rider did not know that folder, and the failure cancelled the switch itself. The switch no longer depends on that step
  • Filters no longer make levels and modules appear and then vanish. A level whose tasks did not pass the selected filter or the search stayed on screen with "No tasks match the selected filters" until the tree was rebuilt a moment later, and then disappeared — together with the whole module if all its levels were like that. Such a level is now hidden right away
  • Web and Python module courses: no more lock icons and "(solved/total)" counts borrowed from another level. On these courses the task keys number levels differently from the course outline — two levels share one number, or one key prefix is used by several modules — so a level could show another level's count or keep a lock after it opened. Where the plugin cannot tell which tasks belong to a level, it now shows no count and no lock until the module is loaded, instead of a wrong one
  • "Open Course Project" no longer ends with "IDE error occurred". Clicking the button in the notification, or "Open Course Project" and "Restore Project Structure" in the plugin menu, closes the project you clicked it from — and closing that project cancelled the click itself while it was still running, so the IDE reported an error from one of its own components. The course project opened anyway; now it opens without the error

Everything below arrived earlier and is new to you if you are updating from a build older than 251.1.172

Arrived in 251.1.172

  • The "Continue" button is back on the Java 25 course. The button never appeared there at all: the plugin counted the Games section as a second quest and gave up on guessing which one the course statuses describe. Games are not part of the course statuses in the first place, so they no longer get in the way. On the classic Java course the button is still not shown — the task keys there carry no level number, and the plugin cannot tell which task comes next; picking it in the tree is the way for now
  • Signing in with another key no longer leaves you looking at the previous student's course. The task tree with their solved cards, their level progress, the expanded nodes, the current task and the name and dark matter in the profile all stayed on screen until the IDE was restarted — signing out cleared them, signing in did not. Parts of a multi-file task downloaded by the previous student are kept apart from yours as well
  • A reply that arrives after you signed in as somebody else is now discarded instead of landing on your screen. Course statuses and the "Continue" chain travel for seconds and could still be in flight when the key changed: the plugin would then show the previous student's progress, and "Continue" could open a task picked from their solved list
  • "Nothing to continue: every task of the course is solved" is no longer said when it is not true. On courses where task keys number levels differently from the course outline, the plugin skips levels it cannot judge — and then reported the course as finished, even with seven unsolved levels out of eight. Such a case now says plainly that the next task could not be determined and asks you to pick it in the tree
  • The "Continue" button no longer stays greyed out for the rest of the IDE session when loading a level is cancelled or fails unexpectedly
  • The dashed frame around the keyboard-selected task card is drawn around the card itself — it used to start 28 pixels to the right, over the character's face, and stick out past the card's right edge
  • The task tree now shows where you are: the level of your current task is expanded and its card selected when the panel opens, locked levels carry a lock icon, and clicking a locked task shows a notification instead of a modal error. Network failures while loading a condition, sending a solution or fetching the correct solution are reported by notifications too. The search hint wraps instead of being cut off; profile numbers ("x11", "x7") got tooltips; "Restore Project Structure" is separated from its neighbours in the menu
  • The task filters ("All / New / In progress / Solved / Unavailable") moved from the top panel to the Tasks window, right under the search box. They used to disappear while a task was open and did not fit a narrow window; now they are always visible and wrap onto a second line. Deselecting a status chip while another is selected now really removes it from the filter
  • "Solution" now asks before showing the correct solution (with a "don't ask again" box): one accidental click used to give the answer away for free. "Publish" is shown only for games — on any other task it could only say "this is not a game". Panel buttons got tooltips with their full names and hotkeys; the "Switch to PRO mode" dialog is short, names your IDE instead of "IntelliJ IDEA" and has proper Yes/No buttons; Russian, Ukrainian, German, French and Portuguese texts address you consistently, and the update notice explains where to click
  • New setting "Show a preview before opening a task" (on by default). Switch it off and a click on a task card opens the task at once, without the preview popup
  • The plugin no longer changes the IDE theme when a course project opens and no longer hides the IDE main menu, toolbar and navigation bar in novice mode — the two most-complained-about behaviours on the marketplace. The day/night switch in the plugin panel still works; a menu hidden by an earlier build is shown again on the next start
  • After a solved task you are not thrown back to "select a task" any more. The condition and the task files stay where they were, and the greeting popup has a "Next task" button: the next unsolved task of the course opens with one click — a level that was not loaded yet is fetched on the way (levels you already finished are skipped without a request), the opened task is revealed in the tree, and a task you cannot open yet is explained instead of skipped
  • Clicking the "day/night" switch before your profile arrived no longer locks the interface language to English for good; applying the settings popup after the language was taken from the profile no longer reverts it — only the settings you actually moved are applied
  • On courses cut at a thousand tasks, level progress no longer flickers between a timer refresh and a submitted task; a settings change made while the profile arrives can no longer be overwritten on disk by stale values
  • Level progress "(solved/total)" and the exact filter on collapsed levels now appear as soon as the course statuses arrive, not after the first click on a filter: the tree rebuilds itself when the statuses change what it can tell about a module
  • The task tree redraws itself as soon as a level arrives showing that the course is numbered differently than the plugin assumed — before, the wrong levels could stay hidden under a filter until the next restart
  • The interface language chosen by hand is no longer overwritten by your profile — not while the settings dialog is open, not after a manual refresh, and not when the profile arrives a little later than the sign-in
  • The plugin no longer speaks two languages at once after the first sign-in. The top panel was built before the plugin learned your language from the profile and kept its English labels until an IDE restart, while the popups were already in your language. The panel now rebuilds itself as soon as the language is known
  • The note shown when you change the interface language said the opposite of what it meant in Russian ("will be unavailable after restart"); fixed. Two typos in the Russian texts fixed too
  • The Tasks and Condition panels no longer disappear while the IDE is indexing. Right after a project opened, both panels showed "This view is not available until indexes are built" for half a minute or longer and ignored clicks; the plugin never needed the indexes for them
  • The "Refresh" button above the task tree now says when the update failed — before, a lost connection left the screen unchanged and the reason only in the log. The message is shown once instead of piling up, is not shown before you sign in, and disappears as soon as a refresh succeeds
  • The "New", "In progress" and "Solved" filters no longer hide the wrong levels on SQL, Python, Frontend and Docker courses. On courses where a task key numbers levels differently from the course outline, the collapsed levels were judged by the wrong numbers: a student on level 13 could lose that level under "New" and see levels far ahead instead. Until the server tells the plugin the level of each task, collapsed levels on such courses are simply shown, as they always were on the classic Java course
  • Nothing says "0 lesson" any more. On courses where a task belongs to no lecture the server sends a zero, and both the task card and the preview popup printed it — every seventh task on Java 25 read like something is broken. The level is named alone now, the way the tooltip always did, and a task outside the levels says nothing instead of "0 level"
  • The "Code style" button is called that in German, Spanish, French, Italian, Polish and Portuguese too — it kept the old name "Analyze" there, which said nothing about what it checks. The verdict messages in the condition panel now follow the font size you set, instead of keeping the old one until you switch tasks
  • New icons for the Tasks and Condition windows and for the plugin buttons on the IDE toolbar, drawn in the style of the current IDE icons: they no longer look blurry on the side bars, and they follow the light and dark themes
  • Code in task conditions is highlighted the way it looks on the site — three tasks out of four mark up code in colour, and the condition panel used to show it as plain text. The panel has one background in every IDE theme instead of two, and the window no longer shows "Condition" and "Условие" as two headers one above the other; the window titles follow your interface language. In German, Polish and Portuguese the window was called "state" and even "disease" (Zustand, Stan, Doença); it is now the task statement there too
  • Code in task requirements is highlighted too: words marked as code in the condition get the same colour in the requirements, and code the author put in `backticks` is shown in the code font without the backticks (a backticked value with a significant space at its edge keeps its backticks, so you can see the space). Recommendations after a failed check are highlighted the same way
  • The task tree no longer opens as a wall of collapsed levels. If there is no current task and you left no level open yourself, a level is expanded for you — the first one with unsolved tasks where the plugin can tell, otherwise the first level of the course (a level the panel opened by itself is not remembered, so the choice is made afresh next time); and a level you had open no longer collapses by itself a second after the course statuses arrive
  • Task cards stretch with the Tasks panel: widen the panel and long task titles are no longer cut off. The status badge (solved, in progress, locked) moved from the character's face to the bottom right corner of the card
  • Characters on task cards are always in colour: tasks you cannot open yet used to show a grey face, and on a fresh course that turned almost the whole tree grey. The status badge still shows the lock
  • The text on the task filter buttons ("All / New / In progress / Solved / Unavailable") is sharp again: it used to look smeared on regular, non-Retina monitors
  • A level left empty by a filter now says so instead of opening onto nothing: the label tells you the level has tasks, but none of them match what you are filtering by
  • The mouse pointer turns into a hand over a task card you can open, and stays an arrow over one you cannot — the tree used to give no hint at all. The "x1" badge on your profile now has a tooltip explaining what it counts, and a locked task names your subscription in plain words instead of an internal code
  • The dashed frame around the selected card no longer overlaps the rows above and below it when the IDE interface is scaled up, and the progress "(solved/total)" with the lock icon no longer gets stuck on a level once shown

Arrived in 251.1.99

  • The plugin no longer reports an IDE error when a popup closes at the wrong moment. Opening the settings, help or sign-in popup — and the "task solved" greeting — could end with "IDE error occurred" instead of the popup, and every failed solution check with the task window open added one more. Both are gone
  • Signing in no longer ends with a grey screen in Rider. The plugin opened the course project in a way Rider cannot complete, and the IDE was left with no project at all — the one you had open was closed too. The project is now opened the same way the IDE opens projects itself; if it still cannot be opened, your own project stays where it was and the plugin says so instead of going quiet
  • The "Refresh" button always works now. It used to refuse with "available in N seconds" exactly when you needed it — when the panel was showing something stale.
  • The task tree no longer collapses on its own: opening levels used to be thrown away whenever the panel rebuilt itself, and you had to expand everything again.
  • Errors inside the plugin are reported again instead of being swallowed: if something breaks in the task panel, the IDE now shows it and lets you send a report to the plugin author.
  • Task files open on a click again. Clicking a file in the "Task Files" panel did nothing at all on recent IDEs — the plugin refreshed the file on the wrong thread and the editor never opened. Clicking anywhere on the row works too now, not only on the file name, and a click that drifts a pixel on a trackpad is no longer swallowed
  • Your key and session no longer travel to your other machines through IDE settings synchronization
  • If the JDK download fails, the plugin can try again: before, one failure disabled the setup silently until you restarted the IDE
  • After updating the plugin, the task panel recovers on its own when the first request for the course outline fails, instead of waiting for a manual refresh
  • An unknown panel mode left in the settings by another build no longer breaks the top panel
  • The task tree now loads as you open it. The plugin asks the server for the course outline first and fetches the tasks of a level when you expand it, instead of downloading the whole course up front. Opening the task panel got noticeably faster on large courses; filters and search still cover the whole course, not just what is already loaded
  • A stale session no longer leaves you looking at somebody else's course: the plugin notices, signs you in again and asks for your own course anew
  • If a task arrives without its files, the plugin says so instead of leaving you in the solving screen with nothing to write in
  • A character portrait that arrives while the tree is being redrawn is no longer lost: the card stops showing Amigo
  • Task cards keep their look when you switch the IDE theme
  • Scrolling the task list is smoother: cards you have already seen survive a filter click or a search keystroke instead of being rebuilt
  • Opening a task no longer greets you with "could not load the condition, check your connection" before the condition has even been asked for
  • If the condition really does not arrive, the panel says so instead of spinning forever
  • A first profile request that fails on a cold network no longer eats the one check that revives a dead session
  • The task condition no longer stays blank without a word: if it did not arrive, the panel says so
  • A task whose condition arrived empty is asked again instead of staying empty until an IDE restart
  • A session the server asked to delete is no longer stored and shared as a working one
  • A plugin that lost its session while the IDE window was in the background now notices it and signs in again by itself
  • A server refusal is told apart from a broken answer, so the log names the real reason
  • Publishing a game shows its progress in your language, not in English
  • The Task Files panel is translated too — its heading and the "task is not selected" line used to stay in English
  • The settings no longer offer a font family choice that changed nothing
  • The task panel says what is going on instead of showing an empty grey area: loading, failed to load, or not signed in
  • The task panel appears sooner on multi-module courses: the plugin asks for all course modules at once instead of one after another
  • The task panel loads over ten times less data: the plugin now asks the server for compressed responses
  • Buying a subscription unlocks the game tasks within minutes instead of after an IDE restart
  • Behind a corporate proxy the plugin no longer reports "no internet" when the connection is fine
  • Signing in works behind a corporate proxy that asks for a login and a password
  • The task panel opens in PyCharm, WebStorm, Rider, CLion and GoLand — there it used to fail at startup and report an error on every launch
  • The Task Files panel shows the path inside the task again, without your account name in it
  • Course modules are listed in the order the site uses, not shuffled
  • Tasks show their own characters: the ones missing from the plugin are downloaded instead of being drawn as Amigo
  • The "New" filter shows only tasks you have not started
  • Expanded levels survive a change in the tree, and signing out forgets them
  • The plugin keeps its settings in a JavaRush folder of its own and signs you in with the key left by the JavaRush installer
  • The interface language follows the language of your course
  • Hiding the panel hides it in every open project window, not only in the last one
  • The download is 9 MB smaller

Arrived in 251.1.43 — 251.1.99, new to you if you are updating from 251.1.42

Signing in

  • The plugin signs you in by itself, with the key left by the JavaRush installer — no more typing it by hand
  • An expired session is restored with the same key, without restarting the IDE
  • Your name and avatar appear in the corner instead of "User", and a change made on the site reaches the plugin without a restart
  • Switching accounts no longer leaves a second IDE window with someone else's project open

The task tree

  • A task you solved on the site turns green here within minutes — even when it is not open and the IDE window is minimised
  • That status no longer rolls back when you switch a filter, search, or restart the IDE
  • A refresh button above the tree picks up newly opened tasks without restarting the IDE
  • A search box above the tree finds a task by title or key, instead of scrolling through the whole course
  • One failed request no longer leaves the panel empty for good
  • A task closed by a subscription is shown locked and says which subscription it needs

Working on a task

  • A task started in another JavaRush tool — the site, VS Code — opens here at startup, together with its statement
  • Task text, requirements and tips are shown in full: fragments in angle brackets no longer disappear
  • Task files land inside the task folder instead of a look-alike folder next to it, and the right file opens right after you switch courses
  • The Task Files panel fills in as soon as the task is downloaded, shows full file names and opens a file on any click
  • Clicking the task you are already working on opens its preview again
  • Resetting a task works as expected, and a multi-part reset downloads the files of every part again

Sending a solution

  • Files that merely look like build output — a builder package, a Rebuild class, a buildSrc folder — are sent for review again
  • Editor backup files no longer break the submission, and a file that cannot be read cancels it with that file named
  • Validate and Publish no longer stay stuck until the IDE is restarted, and the verdict arrives even after a change on the server
  • When publishing a game fails, the plugin names the real reason instead of blaming your code
  • The style check gives the same verdict whatever language the IDE is in

Speed, memory and language

  • Synchronisation, signing in and out, the style check and opening a task moved off the UI thread — fewer freezes
  • Every network request now has a timeout, so a silent server no longer hangs the plugin
  • Task cards, avatars and closed projects no longer stay in memory until the IDE is restarted
  • Messages come in your language: Go, C# and C++ courses no longer show English text about a Python project
  • The learning project no longer greets you with 'JDK "13" is missing'
  • New values coming from the server no longer break the task tree
  • The plugin no longer silences the IDE's own log, and crash reports now reach the authors

idea-plugin.name: PALG: Programming Activity Log Generator
idea-plugin.description:
The Programming Activity Log Generator (PALG) is an IntelliJ IDEA plugin that generates log files based on user activity. The plugin logs various actions such as text insertions, deletions, pasting, file opening, closing, switching, running, debugging, and compilation/runtime errors.

You can navigate to the log file folder by using the "PALG: Open Log Folder" button after right-clicking in an open editor.

The purpose of PALG is to enable teachers to track student work by capturing their development activities in log files. PALA (Programming Activity Log Analyzer) can then be used as a web application to analyze the contents of these log files and provide concise analysis results. PALA is capable of opening zip files recursively, allowing for easy analysis of multiple student submissions in a zip file format. PALA works well with Moodle VPL's "Download all submissions" action, which provides a zip file in the format mentioned above.

Link to the PALA application
Link to the PALA repository
Link to the PALG repository

idea-plugin.name: CodeGym
idea-plugin.description:
Solve tasks from the CodeGym course without leaving your IDE: the plugin brings the task list, the task text and the check results into the development environment you already work in.
What you can do
  • Browse the tasks of your course and open any of them — files are downloaded into a ready-to-use project;
  • Read the task conditions and requirements next to the editor;
  • Run and debug your solution locally;
  • Send the solution for validation and see the verdict without switching to the browser;
  • Run the code style check;
  • Publish a finished game to your profile;
  • Reset the progress of a task and start it over.
Works in IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, Rider, CLion and GoLand. Available features depend on your course — Java, Python, Frontend, C#, C++, Go, SQL, Spring and others.
You need an account on codegym.cc with an active course; some tasks require a subscription.
How to use · FAQ · Support · Terms

The panel has one background in every IDE theme instead of two, and the window no longer shows "Condition" and "Условие" as two headers one above the other; the window titles follow your interface language. In German, Polish and Portuguese the window was called "state" and even "disease" (Zustand, Stan, Doença); it is now the task statement there too
  • Code in task requirements is highlighted too: words marked as code in the condition get the same colour in the requirements, and code the author put in `backticks` is shown in the code font without the backticks (a backticked value with a significant space at its edge keeps its backticks, so you can see the space). Recommendations after a failed check are highlighted the same way
  • The task tree no longer opens as a wall of collapsed levels. If there is no current task and you left no level open yourself, a level is expanded for you — the first one with unsolved tasks where the plugin can tell, otherwise the first level of the course (a level the panel opened by itself is not remembered, so the choice is made afresh next time); and a level you had open no longer collapses by itself a second after the course statuses arrive
  • Task cards stretch with the Tasks panel: widen the panel and long task titles are no longer cut off. The status badge (solved, in progress, locked) moved from the character's face to the bottom right corner of the card
  • Characters on task cards are always in colour: tasks you cannot open yet used to show a grey face, and on a fresh course that turned almost the whole tree grey. The status badge still shows the lock
  • The text on the task filter buttons ("All / New / In progress / Solved / Unavailable") is sharp again: it used to look smeared on regular, non-Retina monitors
  • A level left empty by a filter now says so instead of opening onto nothing: the label tells you the level has tasks, but none of them match what you are filtering by
  • The mouse pointer turns into a hand over a task card you can open, and stays an arrow over one you cannot — the tree used to give no hint at all. The "x1" badge on your profile now has a tooltip explaining what it counts, and a locked task names your subscription in plain words instead of an internal code
  • The dashed frame around the selected card no longer overlaps the rows above and below it when the IDE interface is scaled up, and the progress "(solved/total)" with the lock icon no longer gets stuck on a level once shown

Arrived in 251.1.99

  • The plugin no longer reports an IDE error when a popup closes at the wrong moment. Opening the settings, help or sign-in popup — and the "task solved" greeting — could end with "IDE error occurred" instead of the popup, and every failed solution check with the task window open added one more. Both are gone
  • Signing in no longer ends with a grey screen in Rider. The plugin opened the course project in a way Rider cannot complete, and the IDE was left with no project at all — the one you had open was closed too. The project is now opened the same way the IDE opens projects itself; if it still cannot be opened, your own project stays where it was and the plugin says so instead of going quiet
  • The "Refresh" button always works now. It used to refuse with "available in N seconds" exactly when you needed it — when the panel was showing something stale.
  • The task tree no longer collapses on its own: opening levels used to be thrown away whenever the panel rebuilt itself, and you had to expand everything again.
  • Errors inside the plugin are reported again instead of being swallowed: if something breaks in the task panel, the IDE now shows it and lets you send a report to the plugin author.
  • Task files open on a click again. Clicking a file in the "Task Files" panel did nothing at all on recent IDEs — the plugin refreshed the file on the wrong thread and the editor never opened. Clicking anywhere on the row works too now, not only on the file name, and a click that drifts a pixel on a trackpad is no longer swallowed
  • Your key and session no longer travel to your other machines through IDE settings synchronization
  • If the JDK download fails, the plugin can try again: before, one failure disabled the setup silently until you restarted the IDE
  • After updating the plugin, the task panel recovers on its own when the first request for the course outline fails, instead of waiting for a manual refresh
  • An unknown panel mode left in the settings by another build no longer breaks the top panel
  • The task tree now loads as you open it. The plugin asks the server for the course outline first and fetches the tasks of a level when you expand it, instead of downloading the whole course up front. Opening the task panel got noticeably faster on large courses; filters and search still cover the whole course, not just what is already loaded
  • A stale session no longer leaves you looking at somebody else's course: the plugin notices, signs you in again and asks for your own course anew
  • If a task arrives without its files, the plugin says so instead of leaving you in the solving screen with nothing to write in
  • A character portrait that arrives while the tree is being redrawn is no longer lost: the card stops showing Amigo
  • Task cards keep their look when you switch the IDE theme
  • Scrolling the task list is smoother: cards you have already seen survive a filter click or a search keystroke instead of being rebuilt
  • Opening a task no longer greets you with "could not load the condition, check your connection" before the condition has even been asked for
  • If the condition really does not arrive, the panel says so instead of spinning forever
  • A first profile request that fails on a cold network no longer eats the one check that revives a dead session
  • The task condition no longer stays blank without a word: if it did not arrive, the panel says so
  • A task whose condition arrived empty is asked again instead of staying empty until an IDE restart
  • A session the server asked to delete is no longer stored and shared as a working one
  • A plugin that lost its session while the IDE window was in the background now notices it and signs in again by itself
  • A server refusal is told apart from a broken answer, so the log names the real reason
  • Publishing a game shows its progress in your language, not in English
  • The Task Files panel is translated too — its heading and the "task is not selected" line used to stay in English
  • The settings no longer offer a font family choice that changed nothing
  • The task panel says what is going on instead of showing an empty grey area: loading, failed to load, or not signed in
  • The task panel appears sooner on multi-module courses: the plugin asks for all course modules at once instead of one after another
  • The task panel loads over ten times less data: the plugin now asks the server for compressed responses
  • Buying a subscription unlocks the game tasks within minutes instead of after an IDE restart
  • Behind a corporate proxy the plugin no longer reports "no internet" when the connection is fine
  • Signing in works behind a corporate proxy that asks for a login and a password
  • The task panel opens in PyCharm, WebStorm, Rider, CLion and GoLand — there it used to fail at startup and report an error on every launch
  • The Task Files panel shows the path inside the task again, without your account name in it
  • Course modules are listed in the order the site uses, not shuffled
  • Tasks show their own characters: the ones missing from the plugin are downloaded instead of being drawn as Amigo
  • The "New" filter shows only tasks you have not started
  • Expanded levels survive a change in the tree, and signing out forgets them
  • The plugin keeps its settings in a CodeGym folder of its own and signs you in with the key left by the CodeGym installer
  • The interface language follows the language of your course
  • Hiding the panel hides it in every open project window, not only in the last one
  • The download is 9 MB smaller

Arrived in 251.1.43 — 251.1.99, new to you if you are updating from 251.1.42

Signing in

  • The plugin signs you in by itself, with the key left by the CodeGym installer — no more typing it by hand
  • An expired session is restored with the same key, without restarting the IDE
  • Your name and avatar appear in the corner instead of "User", and a change made on the site reaches the plugin without a restart
  • Switching accounts no longer leaves a second IDE window with someone else's project open

The task tree

  • A task you solved on the site turns green here within minutes — even when it is not open and the IDE window is minimised
  • That status no longer rolls back when you switch a filter, search, or restart the IDE
  • A refresh button above the tree picks up newly opened tasks without restarting the IDE
  • A search box above the tree finds a task by title or key, instead of scrolling through the whole course
  • One failed request no longer leaves the panel empty for good
  • A task closed by a subscription is shown locked and says which subscription it needs

Working on a task

  • A task started in another CodeGym tool — the site, VS Code — opens here at startup, together with its statement
  • Task text, requirements and tips are shown in full: fragments in angle brackets no longer disappear
  • Task files land inside the task folder instead of a look-alike folder next to it, and the right file opens right after you switch courses
  • The Task Files panel fills in as soon as the task is downloaded, shows full file names and opens a file on any click
  • Clicking the task you are already working on opens its preview again
  • Resetting a task works as expected, and a multi-part reset downloads the files of every part again

Sending a solution

  • Files that merely look like build output — a builder package, a Rebuild class, a buildSrc folder — are sent for review again
  • Editor backup files no longer break the submission, and a file that cannot be read cancels it with that file named
  • Validate and Publish no longer stay stuck until the IDE is restarted, and the verdict arrives even after a change on the server
  • When publishing a game fails, the plugin names the real reason instead of blaming your code
  • The style check gives the same verdict whatever language the IDE is in

Speed, memory and language

  • Synchronisation, signing in and out, the style check and opening a task moved off the UI thread — fewer freezes
  • Every network request now has a timeout, so a silent server no longer hangs the plugin
  • Task cards, avatars and closed projects no longer stay in memory until the IDE is restarted
  • Messages come in your language: Go, C# and C++ courses no longer show English text about a Python project
  • The learning project no longer greets you with 'JDK "13" is missing'
  • New values coming from the server no longer break the task tree
  • The plugin no longer silences the IDE's own log, and crash reports now reach the authors

idea-plugin.name: fulibFeedback
idea-plugin.description:
fulibFeedback

This plugin allows grading code assignments with fulib.org.

Setup

  1. Install the plugin from the JetBrains Marketplace.
  2. Go to "Settings > Tools > fulibFeedback" and enter your full name. This is required for the plugin to figure out who you are.
  3. Open or create an Assignment on https://fulib.org/assignments
  4. Configure the plugin for use with the assignment:
    1. Use the "Options > Configure fulibFeedback" action to configure the plugin automatically, or
    2. Fill the fields API Server, Assignment ID and Assignment Token in the IDE under "Settings > Tools > fulibFeedback".

Usage

  1. Open or clone a repository from GitHub Classroom.
  2. Open a file from the repository.
  3. fulibFeedback will automatically detect the assignment and solution and show a notification.
  4. Start evaluation a task for a solution on fulib.org.
  5. Select code in the IDE.
  6. fulibFeedback will transfer the selection to fulib.org.

Challenge Your Coding Skills: Through our carefully designed coding exercises, you will face a variety of challenges, from basic algorithms to advanced programming techniques, gradually improving your coding abilities.

Personalized Learning: Based on your learning progress and interests, the "Starforge Coding Platform" customizes a learning path for you, providing personalized learning recommendations and suggestions to help you study efficiently.

Real-time Feedback: During your practice sessions, you'll receive instant evaluation and feedback, allowing you to understand your learning progress and areas for improvement, and adjust your learning strategies in a timely manner.

In this era of information explosion, mastering coding skills has become crucial for enhancing personal competitiveness. As a comprehensive platform integrating coding practice and learning exchange, the "Starforge Coding Platform" offers you an efficient, convenient, and diversified learning experience. Whether you are a beginner or a seasoned developer, you can find suitable learning resources here, continually advancing, exploring the stars of programming, and challenging the heights of wisdom!
在这个信息爆炸的时代，掌握编程技能已成为提升个人竞争力的关键。而《星斗平台》作为一个集编程练习、学习交流于一体的综合性平台，为您提供了高效、便捷、多样化的学习体验。无论您是初学者还是资深开发者，都能在这里找到适合自己的学习资源，不断前行，探索编程之星，挑战智慧巅峰！

Join now, the "Starforge Coding Platform," and become a star of coding!
立即加入，《星斗平台》，成为编程之星！

idea-plugin.name: Astagfirullah - Islamic Remembrance
idea-plugin.description:
Transform Your Waiting Time into Worship

Astagfirullah displays beautiful Islamic remembrance phrases (Dhikr) during Gradle builds, project sync, and other waiting periods in your IDE. Turn idle moments into opportunities for spiritual reflection with supplications, glorification, and blessings upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).


Key Features

Multilingual Support

  • 7 Languages: Arabic (العربية), English, Urdu (أردو), Farsi (فارسى), Turkish (Türkçe), Indonesian (Bahasa), Bengali (বাংলা)
  • 31+ authentic Islamic supplications and phrases
  • Dynamic phrases synced from server with offline support

Quran Audio Player

  • Listen to the Holy Quran inside your IDE - a dedicated Quran tool window
  • Choose from 200+ reciters and search any surah by name or number
  • Play, pause and skip between surahs, streamed online with no downloads
  • Reciter and surah names follow your chosen language (Arabic, English, Urdu, Farsi, Turkish, Indonesian, Bengali)

Daily Remembrance

  • A gentle dhikr window every time you open a project
  • Closes itself after 7 seconds with a visible countdown - never blocks your work
  • Right-to-left rendering for Arabic, Urdu and Farsi
  • Turn it off any time in Settings → Tools → Astagfirullah

Smart Integration

  • Automatically displays during Gradle builds and project sync
  • Dedicated Tool Window for quick access (View → Tool Windows → Astagfirullah)
  • Settings page under Settings → Tools → Astagfirullah
  • Manual trigger to show phrases anytime

Customization

  • Configurable display duration (1-10 seconds per phrase)
  • Optional blessing sound "صلى على سيدنا محمد"
  • First-run setup wizard for easy configuration

Statistics & Tracking

  • Track total phrases displayed
  • Daily usage count
  • Session statistics
  • Favorite language tracking

Privacy

The plugin sends anonymous, aggregate usage counts (how many remembrance phrases were displayed) to help improve the app. Only a random device identifier, a count, and the platform are sent — never your name, email, files, projects, or code. You can turn this off any time in Settings → Tools → Astagfirullah.


Available Everywhere

Astagfirullah goes wherever you do. Keep your dhikr going beyond the IDE:

  • Android & iOS apps - astaghfirullah.4fdev.com
  • Browser extensions for Chrome, Edge and Firefox - astaghfirullah.4fdev.com
  • More apps from AFApps - afapps.4fdev.com

Getting Started

  1. Install the plugin and restart your IDE
  2. Complete the setup wizard to choose your language
  3. Start a Gradle build or sync to see phrases
  4. Access settings via Tools → Astagfirullah

Open Source

This plugin is open source and welcomes contributions!

  • GitHub Repository - Source code and documentation
  • Report Issues - Bug reports and feature requests
  • Contribute - How to contribute code or translations
  • License - Apache 2.0

"Mention me in your good deeds"

Developer: Ali Al-Shahat Ali
Contact: LinkedIn | Email | GitHub
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Version 3.0.0 - Everywhere You Are

A major release: latest-IDE support, a daily moment of remembrance, and the whole Astagfirullah family in one place

  • NEW: Quran Audio Player - listen to the Holy Quran inside your IDE. Pick from 200+ reciters, search any surah, and play/pause/skip, streamed online. Names follow your chosen language
  • NEW: A "What's New" welcome the first time you open each new version
  • NEW: Available Everywhere - Astagfirullah is also on Android, iOS, and as Chrome / Edge / Firefox extensions. Find them all at astaghfirullah.4fdev.com and afapps.4fdev.com
  • NEW: Dhikr window every time you open a project - a random remembrance phrase, with a rotating link to our other apps, that closes itself after 7 seconds and never blocks your work
  • NEW: Right-to-left rendering for Arabic, Urdu and Farsi
  • FIXED: The plugin could not be installed on IntelliJ 2026.1 or 2026.2 at all. It now supports up to 2026.2, verified against every release in the range
  • FIXED: A stale internal version could prompt you to "update" to the build you were already running
  • IMPROVED: Lighter, faster sign-in - one less network round-trip
  • IMPROVED: Modernised build with continuous integration and a verified compatibility range
  • IMPORTANT: Minimum supported IDE is now 2024.2. IntelliJ 2024.2+ requires Java 21, which cannot run on older IDEs. If you are on 2023.2-2024.1, stay on version 2.0.1

Version 2.1.0 - Daily Dhikr & IntelliJ 2026.2 Support

Now runs on the latest IDEs, with a daily moment of remembrance

  • NEW: Daily dhikr window on IDE startup - a random remembrance phrase with a countdown that closes itself after 5 seconds. Shown at most once a day, never blocks your editor
  • NEW: Turn the daily window off any time in Settings → Tools → Astagfirullah → Behavior
  • NEW: Right-to-left rendering for Arabic, Urdu and Farsi in the daily window
  • FIXED: The plugin could not be installed on IntelliJ 2026.1 or 2026.2 at all. It now supports up to 2026.2, verified against every release in the range
  • FIXED: A stale internal version could prompt you to "update" to the build you were already running
  • IMPROVED: Removed the Firebase dependency from anonymous sign-in. Fewer network calls, same behaviour
  • IMPORTANT: Minimum supported IDE is now 2024.2. IntelliJ 2024.2+ requires Java 21, which cannot run on older IDEs. If you are on 2023.2-2024.1, stay on version 2.0.1

Version 2.0.1 - Authentication & Leaderboard

User accounts and global rankings

  • NEW: User Authentication - Login and Register with email
  • NEW: Global Leaderboard - Compete with users worldwide
  • NEW: Smart Update Notifications with dismiss options
  • NEW: Leaderboard UI with medal rankings (Gold, Silver, Bronze)
  • IMPROVED: Praise filtering by category from server
  • IMPROVED: Version comparison utilities
  • IMPROVED: API architecture with dedicated service layers
  • IMPROVED: Form validation with real-time feedback
  • IMPROVED: Cache management for offline support
  • FIXED: Sync reliability with version-based filtering

Version 2.0.0 - Major Release

Complete UI overhaul with professional settings and statistics

  • NEW: Professional Settings UI accessible from Settings → Tools → Astagfirullah
  • NEW: Tabbed interface with Settings, Statistics, and About sections
  • NEW: Beautiful Statistics dashboard with visual stat cards
  • NEW: Cache information panel showing sync status and version
  • NEW: "Days using plugin" tracker
  • NEW: Clear Cache button for troubleshooting
  • NEW: "Don't Ask Again" option in rating prompt
  • NEW: API integration for dynamic phrases from server
  • NEW: Offline caching with version-based sync
  • NEW: Daily auto-sync for Arabic and English phrases
  • IMPROVED: Rating prompt flow - shows only once per session
  • IMPROVED: Production-ready logging (debug logs hidden in release)
  • IMPROVED: Plugin description with better documentation
  • IMPROVED: Architecture with clean data layer separation
  • IMPROVED: Extended IDE compatibility to version 253 (IntelliJ 2025.3)
  • FIXED: JSON parsing error for API responses
  • FIXED: Rating notification showing repeatedly

Version 1.3.0

  • NEW: Dedicated Tool Window panel (View → Tool Windows → Astagfirullah)
  • NEW: Usage statistics tracking
  • NEW: Manual trigger button to show phrases anytime
  • NEW: Quick language switch from Tool Window

Version 1.2.0

  • NEW: 3 new languages: Turkish, Indonesian, Bengali
  • IMPROVED: Settings architecture with PersistentStateComponent
  • IMPROVED: Audio management with dedicated service
  • FIXED: Sound enable/disable logic

Version 1.1.4

  • Extended IDE compatibility to version 252

idea-plugin.name: Ethery
idea-plugin.description:
Ethery

Ethery enables developers to create, share, and use custom AI code assistants with our open-source JetBrains extension and hub of models, rules, prompts, docs, and other building blocks.

Chat

Chat makes it easy to ask for help from an LLM without needing to leave the IDE.

You send it a task, including any relevant information, and it replies with the text / code most likely to complete the task. If it does not give you what you want, then you can send follow up messages to clarify and adjust its approach until the task is completed.

Autocomplete

Autocomplete provides inline code suggestions as you type.

To enable it, simply click the "Ethery" button in the status bar at the bottom right of your IDE or ensure the "Enable Tab Autocomplete" option is checked in your IDE settings.

Edit

Edit is a convenient way to modify code without leaving your current file.

Highlight a block of code, describe your code changes, and a diff will be streamed inline to your file which you can accept or reject.

Agent

Agent enables you to make more substantial changes to your codebase

Agent equips the Chat model with the tools needed to handle a wide range of coding tasks, allowing the model to make decisions and save you the work of manually finding context and performing actions.

License

idea-plugin.name: Javasm
idea-plugin.description:
An IntelliJ IDEA plugin for JAL, a modern JVM assembly language that makes writing and exploring Java bytecode easy and smart, with rich IDE support.

Javasm & JAL

If you can't understand it, you don't belong here - Mike Gancarz

Javasm is the IntelliJ IDEA plugin for the **JAL (JVM Assembly Language) ** — a custom-designed assembly language for the Java Virtual Machine.
It makes exploring the internals of the JVM not just possible, but genuinely fun.

🚀 What is JAL?

JAL is a fresh take on Java assembly — a spiritual successor to projects like Jasmin, but with modern features and design.

Unlike Jasmin, which stopped development around 2022 and only supports outdated Java versions, JAL supports modern JVM features, including automatic generation of StackMapFrames, which are mandatory from Java 1.6 and up. Jasmin users may remember VerifyErrors haunting their dreams — JAL eliminates them.

Why JAL is cool:

  • Named local variables
    Instead of remembering slot numbers, you can name your variables:

    istore 0 [->example]  
iload example

  • Structured exception handling with labels
    Try-catch-finally blocks are declared with jump labels:

    tryStart: [~tryEnd, java/lang/Exception: catchStart, java/lang/Error: catchStart2 ->finallyStart]  
tryEnd:  
  
catchStart:  
catchStart2:  
finallyStart:

  • Readable member references
    Method and field calls separate class and member names for clarity:

    invokevirtual java/io/PrintStream->println(Ljava/lang/String;)V

Example: HelloWorld

public class HelloWorld {
    public static main([Ljava/lang/String;)

    V {
        // Print "Hello, World!"
        getstatic java/lang / System -> out:Ljava / io / PrintStream;
        ldc "Hello, World!"
        invokevirtual java/io / PrintStream -> println(Ljava / lang / String;)V

        // Return from main
        return
    }
}

Example2: FizzBuzz

public class FizzBuzz {
    public static main([Ljava/lang/String;)

    V {
        // int i = 1;
        iconst_1
                istore_1  // Store the value of i in local variable 1

        LoopStart:
        // if (i >= 101) goto LoopEnd;
        iload_1
        bipush 101
        if_icmpge LoopEnd

        // if (i % 15 = 0)
        iload_1
        bipush 15
        irem
        ifne NotFizzBuzz

        // System.out.println("FizzBuzz");
        getstatic java/lang / System -> out:Ljava / io / PrintStream;
        ldc "FizzBuzz"
        invokevirtual java/io / PrintStream -> println(Ljava / lang / String;)V
    goto LoopIncrement

        NotFizzBuzz:
        // else if (i % 3 == 0)
        iload_1
                iconst_3
        irem
        ifne NotFizz

        // System.out.println("Fizz");
        getstatic java/lang / System -> out:Ljava / io / PrintStream;
        ldc "Fizz"
        invokevirtual java/io / PrintStream -> println(Ljava / lang / String;)V
    goto LoopIncrement

        NotFizz:
        // else if (i % 5 == 0)
        iload_1
                iconst_5
        irem
        ifne PrintNumber

        // System.out.println("Buzz");
        getstatic java/lang / System -> out:Ljava / io / PrintStream;
        ldc "Buzz"
        invokevirtual java/io / PrintStream -> println(Ljava / lang / String;)V
    goto LoopIncrement

        PrintNumber:
        getstatic java/lang / System -> out:Ljava / io / PrintStream;
        iload_1
        invokevirtual java/io / PrintStream -> println(I) V

        LoopIncrement:
        // i++
        iinc 1 1
    goto LoopStart

        LoopEnd:
        // return;
        return
    }
}

🧠 StackMapFrame? Automatically Done.

One of the biggest pain points in JVM bytecode writing is StackMapFrame management.
JAL's compiler calculates and inserts StackMapFrames automatically — no more manual frame declaration, no more hair-pulling VerifyErrors.

🔌 Javasm IntelliJ Plugin Features

Javasm supercharges your JAL development inside IntelliJ IDEA:

  • ✅ Instruction name completion
    Start typing and get autocompletion for all instructions.

  • 📄 Hover documentation
    Hover over instructions to see inline documentation.

  • 🌀 Label navigation
    Ctrl+Click a label to jump to its declaration.

  • 🐞 Debugger integration
    Full integration with IntelliJ's standard JVM debugger (JDWP).
    Breakpoints, step-over, step-into — all supported.

  • 📊 Frame and Stack Viewer
    A custom tool window that shows:

    • Stack state at the selected instruction
    • Local variable states
    • Visualises the stack during live debugging sessions

📦 Installation

This plugin contains JAL implementation V1.3.1!

No manual build needed — just plug and play.

📄 Licence

MIT Licence. See the LICENCE file for details.

❤️ A project by someone who enjoys poking around the JVM bytecode guts.

DevRhythm — Coding Rhythm & Idle Analytics

DevRhythm tracks coding activity, idle behavior, and project engagement for research in programming education.

Features:

Development Team:

Developed by Rubash Mali under the supervision of Dr. John Edwards at Utah State University.

Privacy Notice:

This plugin collects content-free coding activity data for research purposes in programming education. Activity is measured using keystroke and mouse-click timing. It does not record source code, typed text, screenshots, file contents, or clipboard contents. Data is stored locally in a .devrhythm folder within each project.
