idea-plugin.name: LogSensei
idea-plugin.description:
LogSensei helps Java developers write better logging code by detecting missing logs and suggesting appropriate log levels.

Features:
  • Catch blocks — detects empty catch blocks, suggests ERROR/SEVERE level logging
  • Loops — warns about INFO logs in loops, suggests changing to DEBUG/FINE
  • Early returns — detects guard clauses without logging, suggests DEBUG/FINE level
  • Spring components — ensures @Service/@Controller/@RestController methods have entry/exit INFO logs

Smart automation:
  • Automatically adds Lombok annotations (@Slf4j, @Log4j2)
  • Adds missing dependencies to Maven/Gradle
  • Educational tooltips explaining log levels

Supported logging frameworks: SLF4J + Logback, Log4j2, java.util.logging

Usage: Press Alt+Enter on highlighted code and select the suggested fix.

Requirements: IntelliJ IDEA 2024.3+, Java 17+, Lombok plugin (recommended)

idea-plugin.name: Typing Training
idea-plugin.description:
Master the art of coding at the speed of thought.

While many developers focus on learning new frameworks and languages, the fundamental skill of touch typing is often overlooked. Efficient typing isn't just about speed; it's about reducing cognitive load. As Jeff Atwood (Coding Horror) puts it, "A programmer who can't type is like a writer who can't spell." When your fingers move automatically, your brain is free to focus on logic, architecture, and problem-solving.

This plugin brings deliberate typing practice directly into your IDE, allowing you to train on the very code you work with every day.

Key Benefits:
  • Real-World Practice: Type entire source files or specific selected blocks to build muscle memory for syntax and common patterns.
  • Code Familiarity: Practice on your own project's codebase to internalize its structure while improving your speed.
  • Seamless Integration: No need to switch to external apps. Start a session with a simple right-click in your editor.
  • Instant Feedback: Real-time highlighting of errors and a detailed summary of your speed (WPM) and accuracy.
The plugin is under active development. I value your feedback and suggestions to make this the best tool for developer productivity.

  • Enhanced Responsiveness: Doubled the content disappearance speed (0.15s -> 0.08s) for near-instant stealth when switching focus.

Version 1.4.2 - Focus-based Stealth Mode

  • Concentration Mode: Text content now automatically hides (becomes transparent) when the reader window loses focus. Ideal for maintaining privacy when switching tasks.
  • Instant Restore: Content instantly reappears as soon as you click back into the reader.

Version 1.4.1 - Privacy & Stealth

  • Hidden Title: The tool window title can now be set to empty (or a space) to hide the plugin more effectively. Perfect for "fishing" during work.
  • UX Polish: Removed unnecessary console logging for a cleaner experience.

Version 1.4.0 - Search & Layout Overhaul

  • New Search Engine: Implemented a lightning-fast, real-time search engine. Search as you type and see relevant context snippets immediately.
  • Direct Jump: Click on any search match to navigate directly to that specific page and highlight the text instantly.
  • Ultra-Narrow Margins: Reduced top/bottom margins to a microscopic 5px, reclaiming every possible pixel for your content.
  • Stability Refinements: Fixed rare bridge communication hangs and optimized script performance for large EPUB files.

Version 1.3.1

  • Native Toolwindow Controls: Removed the intrusive floating HTML toolbar. All reading controls (Open Book, Settings, Chapters, Search, Progress) are now elegantly integrated into the native IntelliJ Tool Window header bar.
  • Native Dialog Popups: Chapters, Settings, and Search results now open in clean, detached native IntelliJ dialog popups rather than covering the reading view.
  • Reading Progress Dialog: Added a new dedicated progress button to view your exact reading percentage.
  • Absolute Positioning & Resizing Fixes: Perfected window resize tracking. Expanding the sidebar will now snap you to the exact text node you were reading, ending the frustrating pagination offsets.
  • Persistent Settings: Themes, Font Family, and Zoom level changes now persist seamlessly across reading sessions.
  • Symmetric Layout Constraints: Finalized the vertical padding constraints to be perfectly symmetrical across the top and bottom edges.

Version 1.2.1

  • UX Polish: Refined the welcome screen with friendly, multi-lingual instructions and icons.
  • Marketplace: Updated the plugin description to highlight the immersive reading experience and new navigation mechanics.

Version 1.2.0 - Layout and UX Overhaul

  • Layout Polish: Completely overhauled multi-column margins. Margins are now flawlessly uniform, ultra-narrow (4px), and push right up against the window edge to maximize reading space.
  • Narrow Window Support: Drastically improved the reading experience in extremely thin IDE sidebars (single-character columns). Text will now perfectly wrap and break without horizontally overflowing or blanking out.
  • Keyboard Navigation Fix: Globally mapped the A/D and Left/Right Arrow keys to guarantee seamless page-turning regardless of UI focus issues.
  • Scroll Locking: Disabled messy native trackpad dragging and mouse scrolling. Replaced with strict page-by-page turning via mouse wheel for a pristine reading experience.
  • Search & Resize Precision: Replaced a flawed offset calculation with highly accurate getBoundingClientRect() logic. Jumping to search results and resizing the window is now completely accurate across chapters.
  • Toolbar Compaction: Significantly shrunk the top hover toolbar (height, icons, and text) to occupy minimal vertical space when summoned.
  • Footer Removal: Removed the bottom page number tracker that occasionally overlapped text in tight viewports.

idea-plugin.name: CodeRef - Smart Java & Kotlin Analyzer with ML Engine
idea-plugin.description:
An intelligent Java and Kotlin code analysis agent that learns from your workflow — adapting its findings, severity rankings, and fix priorities to your codebase over time. CodeRef combines multi-engine static analysis with an adaptive ML engine to inspect, refactor, and generate tests for your projects.

Intelligent Agent Capabilities

  • Learns as you work — the ML engine observes which findings you accept, dismiss, or fix, and adapts its predictions so each scan becomes more relevant than the last
  • Predicts where bugs hide — identifies bug-prone files and design anti-patterns before they surface in production, helping you focus review effort where it matters most
  • Eliminates false-positive noise — automatically suppresses findings that don't match your codebase's patterns, so code reviews stay focused on real issues
  • Re-ranks severity intelligently — adjusts issue priority based on your project's history, ensuring critical problems are always surfaced first

Java & Kotlin Analysis

  • Java version-aware analysis — automatically detects your project's target Java version from Maven, Gradle, or IntelliJ SDK and adapts all rules and auto-fixes to that version. Tracks 37 language features from Java 5 through Java 24 so fixes never suggest incompatible constructs
  • Multi-engine code inspection — PMD, SpotBugs, and 50+ custom rules run in parallel across Java and Kotlin sources
  • 42 Kotlin rules — comprehensive coverage for backend Spring/REST, Android security, lifecycle & memory leaks, coroutine anti-patterns, Jetpack Compose, and Kotlin idioms
  • Android & mobile analysis — detects hardcoded API keys, insecure SharedPreferences, cleartext traffic, WebView injection, Context leaks in singletons, GlobalScope misuse, runBlocking on the main thread, missing remember in Compose, and 20+ more mobile-specific issues
  • Context-aware detection — Android rules activate only when android/androidx imports are present; Compose rules scope to @Composable functions; coroutine rules engage when kotlinx.coroutines is in use
  • REST controller security — detects unrestricted CORS, missing authentication, unbounded endpoints, SQL injection, and missing rate limiting with auto-fixes
  • One-click refactoring — 37+ auto-fix strategies for security, complexity, Spring dependency injection, Apache Camel routes, Android lifecycle, Compose correctness, and Kotlin quality
  • Kotlin auto-fixes — migrates GlobalScope to lifecycleScope, replaces Thread.sleep with delay(), wraps state with remember{}, converts var to val, upgrades HTTP to HTTPS, rewrites observe(this) to observe(viewLifecycleOwner), and more
  • Spring modernization — automatically migrates field injection to constructor injection, fixes JPA constructor issues, and respects Lombok annotations
  • Apache Camel support — detects route anti-patterns, thread-safety risks, and missing error handlers with instant auto-fixes
  • SonarQube-compatible reporting — issues mapped to SonarQube rule IDs and Clean Code attributes without requiring a server

Test Generation

  • Full test scaffolding — generates JUnit 5 + Mockito + Spring Boot test cases with one click, covering service layers, REST controllers, JPA repositories, and Camel routes
  • Camel Exchange mocking — processor tests include body/DTO mocking, null/empty body validation, type verification via ArgumentCaptor, and dependency failure propagation
  • Works offline — all analysis, refactoring, and test generation runs locally with no server or internet connection required

From IDE to CI/CD

The same analysis engine that runs in IntelliJ now also runs across your entire delivery pipeline — so the issues you catch on your laptop are caught again at pull-request time and at build time, without standing up a separate analysis server.

  • Command-line analyzer — run CodeRef from any terminal or CI runner. Same rules as the IDE, no IntelliJ required. Useful for headless agents, scheduled scans, and pre-commit hooks.
  • Maven plugin — one entry in your pom.xml gates merges on issue severity, bound to the standard verify phase.
  • Gradle plugin — apply id("com.coderef") and the analyzer hooks into your existing check lifecycle.
  • Pull-request reviews on GitHub and GitLab — findings surface in the GitHub Security tab and as inline review comments, or in GitLab's merge-request widget showing new versus resolved issues across pipelines. Reviewers see what your branch introduced without leaving the PR.
  • Adopt on legacy code without noise — snapshot today's findings as a baseline, then only fail builds on new issues from then on. Teams can roll CodeRef out on large existing codebases without drowning in pre-existing warnings.
  • Pull-request-only mode — restrict reporting to lines your branch actually changed, so a stylistic warning on an untouched file never blocks a merge.
  • Multiple report formats — text, JSON, HTML, SARIF, or GitLab Code Quality JSON, produced from a single command.

Project Analysis with Runtime Impact

CodeRef scans your entire project on open — Maven and Gradle, Java and Kotlin — and shows every issue with a clear description of what will happen at runtime if the bug is not fixed.

Blocker-level detection — Spring proxy bypass, SQL injection, and other critical production failures identified instantly:

Critical-level detection — Deep nesting, complexity issues, and maintainability risks with auto-fix suggestions:
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.2.3 — Deprecated API cleanup

  • Removed deprecated platform API usage — file reads and VFS scans no longer use the deprecated ReadAction.compute, keeping the plugin binary-compatible with future IDE releases.

2026.2.2 — Compatibility fix

  • No longer fails on IDEs without JCEF — the report, refactored-code, and test-generation panels now detect when the embedded browser is unavailable and fall back to plain rendering instead of reporting an error. Affected IDE builds that ship without the JCEF runtime.

2026.2.1 — Security & thread-safety hardening

  • Stable ML data store under concurrency — all access to the per-project ML database is now serialized through a single lock, eliminating intermittent errors that could occur when background sync, analysis, and feedback ran at the same time.
  • No more leaked resources on project close — the ML engine now releases its background sync thread and database connection when a project or the IDE is closed.
  • Responsive editor during analysis — file reads and project scans now use the platform's read-action and managed background-thread APIs, keeping the IDE responsive and correctly cancelling work when a project closes.
  • Safer team sync — optional ML sync now enforces HTTPS and properly encodes all request parameters, protecting data in transit.
  • Hardened data-store queries — added defense-in-depth validation to internal database queries.

What's New in 2026.2.0 — From IDE to CI/CD

CodeRef now extends well beyond the IDE. The same analysis engine you use here also runs in your terminal, your build, and your code-review tooling — with no separate server to host, no separate ruleset to maintain, and no extra weight added to this plugin.

Run CodeRef anywhere

  • Command-line analyzer — ship a single download and run CodeRef on any developer machine, CI runner, or pre-commit hook. Catches the same issues as the IDE, no IntelliJ required at runtime.
  • Maven plugin — one entry in pom.xml gates merges on issue severity. Bound to the standard verify phase, so mvn verify is now an analysis check too.
  • Gradle plugin — apply id("com.coderef") and the analyzer hooks into your existing check lifecycle. Standard ./gradlew check now runs CodeRef.

Native code-review integrations

  • GitHub Code Scanning — findings appear in the Security tab and as inline review comments on pull requests, so reviewers see them without leaving the PR.
  • GitLab Code Quality — the merge-request widget shows new versus resolved findings across pipelines, with stable identifiers so the same issue isn't reported twice.
  • Bitbucket and other SARIF-aware tools — standard SARIF output works with any ingestion point that consumes the format.

Roll out on big codebases without the noise

  • Baseline mode — snapshot today's findings once, then have CI fail only on new issues from that day forward. Adopt CodeRef on a large legacy codebase without drowning the team in pre-existing warnings.
  • Pull-request-only mode — restrict reporting to the lines your branch actually changed, so a finding on an untouched file never blocks a merge.
  • Severity gates per environment — let the IDE surface everything while CI fails only on blockers, or tighten the gate as the codebase improves — same engine, different threshold.

Reports for every audience

  • Text for terminals and CI logs
  • HTML for sharing a single self-contained report
  • JSON for custom dashboards and tooling
  • SARIF for GitHub, Bitbucket, and any SARIF consumer
  • GitLab Code Quality for GitLab merge-request widgets

Important: these tools are sibling distributables — they do not add anything to this IDE plugin's footprint. The plugin you install from the marketplace remains the same lean download you already know.

What's New in 2026.1.9

Java Version-Aware Analysis & Auto-Fixes

CodeRef now detects the target Java version of your project and adapts all analysis rules and auto-fixes accordingly. No more suggestions that break compilation — every fix is guaranteed compatible with your project's language level.

  • Automatic detection — reads your project's Java version from Maven pom.xml (maven.compiler.source, maven.compiler.release), Gradle build files (sourceCompatibility, toolchain, jvmTarget), or falls back to the IntelliJ project SDK. Results are cached for zero-overhead repeat analysis
  • 37 language features tracked — from generics (Java 5) through stream gatherers (Java 24), each feature knows its minimum required version
  • Version-gated fixes — try-with-resources wrapping is skipped for Java 6 projects, var type inference is only used for Java 10+, Optional.orElseThrow() suggestions require Java 10+, and finalize() → AutoCloseable migration requires Java 7+
  • PMD version alignment — PMD now parses source at the correct language level instead of hardcoded Java 17, reducing false positives from syntax features the project doesn't use
  • SpotBugs compilation alignment — bytecode compilation uses the project's -source/-target flags for accurate bug detection
  • Easy to extend — adding version awareness to any fixer requires a single method override checking versionContext.supports(JavaFeature.XXX)

Supported Java Versions

FeatureMin VersionGated Fixes
Enhanced for-eachJava 5ForEachFixer skipped for Java 4 and below
Try-with-resources, diamond, multi-catchJava 7TryWithResourcesFixer, AutoCloseable migration
Lambdas, streams, Optional, method referencesJava 8OptionalGetFixer requires Java 8+
var local variableJava 10ForEachFixer uses Object below Java 10
Optional.orElseThrow() (no-arg)Java 10OptionalGetFixer skipped below Java 10
Records, pattern matching instanceofJava 16Future fixers will gate on these
Sealed classesJava 17Future fixers will gate on these
Pattern matching switch, virtual threadsJava 21Future fixers will gate on these
Stream gatherers, flexible constructorsJava 24Future fixers will gate on these

idea-plugin.name: BOJ Helper
idea-plugin.description:
View, test, and submit Baekjoon Online Judge problems directly in your JetBrains IDE.

백준 온라인 저지 문제를 JetBrains IDE에서 바로 보고, 테스트하고, 제출하세요.

주요 기능

문제 자동 불러오기

파일명에서 문제 번호를 자동 인식합니다. Boj1000.java, Main_1000.py 같은 파일을 열면 해당 문제가 자동으로 로딩됩니다. 직접 문제 번호를 입력할 수도 있습니다.

수식 렌더링

LaTeX 수식을 포함한 문제를 MathJax로 렌더링합니다. JCEF를 지원하는 IDE에서는 백준 웹사이트와 동일한 형태로 문제를 볼 수 있습니다.

샘플 테스트 실행

샘플 입출력을 로컬에서 실행하고 결과를 자동으로 비교합니다.

  • Pass — 출력이 예상 결과와 일치
  • Fail — 출력 불일치, 런타임 에러, 또는 시간 초과
  • 출력 비교 시 후행 공백과 빈 줄은 무시합니다

일반 테스트

백준 문제가 아닌 일반 코드 파일에서도 입출력 테스트를 실행할 수 있습니다. BOJ Helper 도구 창의 일반 탭에서 테스트 케이스를 추가하고 실행합니다.

커스텀 테스트 케이스

샘플 외에 직접 테스트 케이스를 추가하고 관리할 수 있습니다.

백준 제출

IDE 내에서 백준에 직접 소스코드를 제출할 수 있습니다. 제출 탭에서 로그인 후, 소스코드가 자동으로 입력되며 제출 버튼 영역으로 스크롤됩니다.

GitHub 업로드

제출 결과가 맞았습니다!! 일 때, GitHub 리포지토리에 소스코드를 업로드할 수 있습니다.

  • GitHub Device Flow 인증 — 브라우저에서 간편하게 로그인
  • 경로/커밋 메시지 템플릿 — {problemId}, {title}, {tier}, {language} 등 변수로 커스터마이징
  • README.md 자동 생성 — 문제 정보, 알고리즘 분류(solved.ac), 제출 결과를 포함한 README 생성
  • 설정: BOJ Helper 도구 창 → 제출 탭 → GitHub 버튼

코드 복사

백준 제출용으로 클립보드에 복사합니다. Java 코드의 경우, 클래스명을 Main으로 자동 변환합니다.

보일러플레이트 파일 생성

문제 번호를 기반으로 소스 파일을 자동 생성합니다.

  • 경로/코드 템플릿 — {problemId}, {title} 등 변수로 파일 경로와 초기 코드 커스터마이징
  • 마지막 선택 언어 기억 — 이전에 사용한 언어를 자동 선택
  • 설정: BOJ Helper 도구 창 → 설정 탭

문제 메모

문제별로 메모를 작성하고 관리할 수 있습니다. 테스트 결과 패널 하단에 통합되어 있습니다.

  • 탭 기반 편집 — 여러 메모를 탭으로 관리, 우클릭 컨텍스트 메뉴 지원
  • Ctrl+S 저장 / Ctrl+스크롤 폰트 크기 조절
  • 파일 기반 저장 — 프로젝트 내 .boj/ 디렉토리에 자동 저장

지원 언어

언어실행 방식동작 확인
Javajava 명령어로 실행✅
Python프로젝트 인터프리터 자동 감지✅
Kotlinkotlin 명령어로 실행
C/C++컴파일된 바이너리 실행
Gogo run으로 실행
JavaScriptnode로 실행
TypeScriptts-node로 실행
Bashbash로 실행

설치

JetBrains Marketplace

  1. Settings → Plugins → Marketplace
  2. "BOJ Helper" 검색
  3. Install 클릭

수동 설치

  1. Releases에서 .zip 파일 다운로드
  2. Settings → Plugins → ⚙️ → Install Plugin from Disk...

사용법

  1. 파일명에 문제 번호를 포함하여 파일을 생성합니다 (예: Boj1000.java)
  2. 우측 BOJ Helper 도구 창에서 문제가 자동으로 로딩됩니다
  3. 코드를 작성한 후 실행 버튼을 클릭합니다
  4. 하단 BOJ 테스트 도구 창에서 결과를 확인합니다

호환성

  • IDE: IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm 등 JetBrains IDE
  • 버전: 2021.3 이상
  • 수식 렌더링: JCEF 지원 IDE (미지원 시 텍스트 폴백)

피드백

버그 리포트나 기능 요청은 GitHub Issues에 남겨주세요.

idea-plugin.name: CodingTestKit
idea-plugin.description:
CodingTestKit - Algorithm Problem Solver

An all-in-one IntelliJ plugin to fetch, test, and submit algorithm problems — all without leaving your IDE.

Supported Platforms

  • Programmers – Fetch, test, submit, search, random
  • SWEA – Fetch, test, submit, search, random
  • LeetCode – Fetch, test, submit, search, random, my solved
  • Codeforces – Fetch, test, submit, search, random, my solved

Key Features

  • Fetch Problems – Auto-extract problem description and test cases by entering a number
  • Problem View & Translation – View problems in-IDE with KaTeX math rendering and one-click KR↔EN translation
  • Local Test – Run and compare code directly in the IDE with execution time & memory metrics
  • Login & Submit – Submit via built-in browser with auto language/code/problem selection
  • Search – Search by keyword, tag, difficulty on LeetCode, Codeforces, and Programmers
  • Random Picker – Tier/class/rating range, tag chips, solved filter, accepted count filter, exam collection filter
  • My Solved – Browse your solved problems per platform with search & pagination
  • Exam Mode – Disable autocomplete, hide code vision, block paste, detect focus loss
  • Timer – Stopwatch (lap records & memo) + circular dial countdown timer
  • Templates – Save and load code templates with syntax highlighting
  • GitHub Push – One-click login, repo selector, auto-push on accepted
  • i18n – Fully localized Korean / English UI, folder names, error messages, and GitHub push

Supported Languages

Java, Python, C++, Kotlin, JavaScript, Rust, Go, Ruby

Local test execution works for all languages on every platform. Submission availability depends on each platform — unsupported combinations show a warning at selection time.

Getting Started

  1. Open CodingTestKit from the right sidebar
  2. Select a platform (Programmers / SWEA / LeetCode / Codeforces) and language
  3. Enter a problem number and click Fetch
  4. Write your solution in the auto-generated code file
  5. Click Run All to test against all test cases
  6. Click Submit to submit via the built-in browser

Optional:

  • Login – Click login for each platform to enable submission and solved filters
  • GitHub – Settings → GitHub Integration → Login to auto-push accepted solutions
  • Exam Mode – Settings → Exam Mode to simulate real test conditions
  • Timer – Use the Timer tab for stopwatch or countdown

Privacy & Data

  • Login cookies and the GitHub token are stored locally in IntelliJ's PasswordSafe (OS keychain). Nothing is sent to the plugin author.
  • Network requests go only to official platform endpoints (school.programmers.co.kr, swexpertacademy.com, leetcode.com, codeforces.com, api.github.com, translate.googleapis.com).
  • No analytics, telemetry, or user tracking.
  • Full policy: PRIVACY.md

Bug Reports & Feature Requests

Found a bug or have a feature idea? Please let us know!

  • Feedback Form (1 min): https://forms.gle/Qqi5gDoHSi2HU1Xs5
  • GitHub Issues: github.com/dj258255/codingtestkit/issues
  • Email: dj258255@naver.com

Disclaimer

All problem content is copyrighted by its respective platform. This plugin is intended for personal study purposes only. Do not redistribute, commercially use, or publish fetched content. The plugin fetches problems locally for individual learning and does not store or redistribute any content externally.

  • Programmers: school.programmers.co.kr
  • SWEA: swexpertacademy.com
  • LeetCode: leetcode.com
  • Codeforces: codeforces.com

CodingTestKit - 알고리즘 문제 풀이 도구

IntelliJ IDE에서 알고리즘 문제를 가져오고, 테스트하고, 제출까지 한번에!

지원 플랫폼

  • 프로그래머스 – 문제 가져오기, 테스트, 제출, 검색, 랜덤
  • SWEA – 문제 가져오기, 테스트, 제출, 검색, 랜덤
  • LeetCode – 문제 가져오기, 테스트, 제출, 검색, 랜덤, 내 풀이
  • Codeforces – 문제 가져오기, 테스트, 제출, 검색, 랜덤, 내 풀이

주요 기능

  • 문제 가져오기 – 번호 입력만으로 문제 설명, 테스트 케이스 자동 추출
  • 문제 보기 & 번역 – IDE 내에서 문제 확인 + KaTeX 수식 렌더링 + 한/영 원클릭 번역
  • 로컬 테스트 – Java, Python, C++, Kotlin, JavaScript, Rust, Go, Ruby 코드를 IDE에서 바로 실행 + 실행 시간 & 메모리
  • 로그인 & 제출 – 내장 브라우저로 직접 제출 + 언어/코드/문제 자동 선택
  • 문제 검색 – LeetCode, Codeforces, 프로그래머스에서 키워드·태그·난이도로 검색
  • 랜덤 뽑기 – 티어/클래스/레이팅 범위, 태그 칩, 풀이 필터, 정답자 수 필터, 기출문제 모음 필터
  • 내 풀이 – 플랫폼별 풀이 기록 조회 (검색 & 페이지네이션)
  • 시험 모드 – 자동완성/검사/사용위치 힌트 끄기, 외부 붙여넣기 차단, 포커스 이탈 감지
  • 타이머 – 스톱워치(랩 기록·메모) + 원형 다이얼 카운트다운 타이머
  • 코드 템플릿 – 자주 쓰는 코드 템플릿 저장 및 불러오기
  • GitHub 연동 – 원클릭 로그인, 레포 선택, 채점 통과 시 자동 푸시
  • 다국어 – 한국어 / English UI 완전 지원 (폴더명, 에러 메시지, GitHub 푸시 포함)

지원 언어

Java, Python, C++, Kotlin, JavaScript, Rust, Go, Ruby

로컬 테스트 실행은 모든 플랫폼에서 전 언어 지원. 제출은 플랫폼별로 다르며, 미지원 조합 선택 시 즉시 경고가 표시됩니다.

시작하기

  1. 우측 사이드바에서 CodingTestKit 열기
  2. 플랫폼 (프로그래머스 / SWEA / LeetCode / Codeforces)과 언어 선택
  3. 문제 번호 입력 후 가져오기 클릭
  4. 자동 생성된 코드 파일에 풀이 작성
  5. 전체 실행으로 테스트 케이스 확인
  6. 제출 버튼으로 내장 브라우저에서 제출

추가 설정:

  • 로그인 – 각 플랫폼 로그인 → 제출 및 풀이 필터 사용 가능
  • GitHub – 설정 → GitHub 연동 → 로그인하면 채점 통과 시 자동 푸시
  • 시험 모드 – 설정 → 시험 모드로 실전 환경 재현
  • 타이머 – 타이머 탭에서 스톱워치/카운트다운 사용

개인정보 처리 방침

  • 로그인 쿠키와 GitHub 토큰은 IntelliJ의 PasswordSafe (OS 키체인)에 로컬로 저장됩니다. 플러그인 제작자에게 전송되는 정보는 없습니다.
  • 네트워크 요청은 공식 플랫폼(school.programmers.co.kr, swexpertacademy.com, leetcode.com, codeforces.com, api.github.com, translate.googleapis.com)으로만 전송됩니다.
  • 분석/수집/사용자 추적 기능 없음.
  • 전체 정책: PRIVACY.md

버그 제보 & 기능 제안

버그를 발견하셨거나 원하는 기능이 있으시면 알려주세요!

  • 피드백 폼 (1분 소요): https://forms.gle/Qqi5gDoHSi2HU1Xs5
  • GitHub Issues: github.com/dj258255/codingtestkit/issues
  • 이메일: dj258255@naver.com

면책 조항

모든 문제의 저작권은 해당 플랫폼에 있습니다. 이 플러그인은 개인 학습 목적으로만 사용해 주세요. 가져온 문제를 재배포, 상업적 이용, 외부 게시하지 마세요. 플러그인은 개인 학습을 위해 문제를 로컬에 가져올 뿐이며, 어떠한 콘텐츠도 외부에 저장하거나 재배포하지 않습니다.

  • 프로그래머스: school.programmers.co.kr
  • SWEA: swexpertacademy.com
  • LeetCode: leetcode.com
  • Codeforces: codeforces.com
idea-plugin.change-notes:
v1.8.1

LeetCode/Programmers case debugging for Python, C++, Rust, JavaScript and Ruby — and a C++ run fix.

English
  • [New] Debugging a test case on LeetCode/Programmers now works in Python, C++, Rust, JavaScript and Ruby – Previously only Java and Kotlin could do this; the other languages ran your file as-is, and since a wrapper-platform file has no main, the session started and ended without ever reaching a breakpoint. The plugin now runs a small harness that loads your file instead of replacing it, so your code keeps its own path and line numbers and your breakpoints bind normally. (#36)
  • [Fix] C++ on LeetCode/Programmers failed to compile – Arguments were passed as brace lists, which cannot bind to LeetCode's standard vector<int>& parameter, and the harness headers were prepended above your code so a file without <iostream> broke the build. Both are fixed, and because the headers no longer shift your lines, C++ compiler diagnostics on those platforms are now clickable in the Build window too. (#36, #32)
한국어
  • [신규] 리트코드·프로그래머스 케이스 디버깅이 Python·C++·Rust·JavaScript·Ruby에서도 됩니다 – 전에는 Java·Kotlin만 가능했고, 나머지 언어는 파일을 그대로 실행했습니다. 래퍼 플랫폼의 파일에는 main이 없어서 세션이 시작됐다가 브레이크포인트에 닿지 못하고 끝났습니다. 이제 사용자 파일을 불러오는 작은 하네스를 실행하므로, 코드가 자기 경로와 줄 번호를 그대로 유지하고 브레이크포인트가 정상적으로 바인딩됩니다. (#36)
  • [수정] 리트코드·프로그래머스에서 C++이 컴파일되지 않던 문제 – 인자를 중괄호 리스트로 넘겨 리트코드 표준 파라미터 vector<int>&에 바인딩되지 않았고, 하네스 헤더를 코드 위에 붙여서 <iostream>이 없는 파일은 빌드가 깨졌습니다. 둘 다 고쳤고, 헤더가 더 이상 줄을 밀지 않게 되면서 이 플랫폼의 C++ 컴파일 진단도 Build 창에서 클릭 이동이 됩니다. (#36, #32)

v1.8.0

Generator format for describing complex test inputs, plus fixes to Build Output diagnostics, embedded dark mode, and the template panel.

English
  • [New] Test input generator format – Describe a whole input format instead of a single array. Literals pass through and only name(...) calls are replaced; labels bind values for reuse (rand(1, 100, n) then array(n, a)), and _label binds without printing. Generators: const, rand, rand_float, array, array2d, string, perm0/perm1, tree (RANDOM/STAR/PATH/BAMBOO/CATERPILLAR/BINARY), graph (SIMPLE/CONNECTED/DAG/MULTI/TREE, optionally directed and weighted), bipartite_graph. Also repeat(t as i) { … } blocks (nestable), macros via def, aggregates sum/min/max/len, arithmetic, and integers beyond 2^64. Strings, 2-D arrays, trees and graphs now generate on stdin platforms (Codeforces/SWEA) too, not only LeetCode. Save as a .ctk-format file for syntax highlighting, or use the new "Advanced (format)" tab in the generator dialog. (#36)
  • [New] Adversarial number generator – anti_hash_int emits multiples of the bucket prime that libstdc++ will use, collapsing std::unordered_map/set into a single bucket (O(N) per operation) on GCC. anti_hash_str keeps the Thue–Morse colliding pair. (#36)
  • [Fix] Compiler diagnostics missing from Build Output – Since v1.7.0 the Build window showed only an empty "Compilation failed" node. Every diagnostic reused the build's event id and was silently dropped as an id collision. Diagnostics, with clickable file locations, appear again. (#32)
  • [Fix] Embedded page dark mode – A bright band no longer appears below pages shorter than the window, the Codeforces header logo is legible on dark, and already-dark pages (the Programmers problem view) are no longer inverted back to light. Pages that render late (SPA) are re-checked after load. (#34)
  • [Improved] Template panel – Right-click a template to load it, set it as a platform default (★), or delete it. Saving now asks what to save — the whole editor, the current selection, or a file — and asks for the name last. (#35)
  • [Fix] Compiler warnings now reach Build Output – Warnings were only forwarded when the compile also failed, so a clean-but-warning build sent nothing at all — the very case the feature was asked for. Diagnostics also stop jumping to the wrong line: two-class Java (Main + Solution) keeps its original line numbers, and diagnostics that come from the generated harness no longer navigate past the end of your file. (#32)
  • [Fix] Loading a template no longer breaks LeetCode submissions – "Replace all" wrote the raw template, so a template using the panel's own {{SOLUTION}} tip lost the required Solution class and left the literal placeholder behind. Loading now composes the same way new problem files do, and the stub is stored so it can always be restored. A template can also be the default for several platforms at once. (#35)
  • [Fix] Custom checker marked every generated case as failed – The checker ran before the neutral path and could only answer pass/fail, while the shipped template compared against an expected output that generated cases do not have. Checkers can now answer CHECK to hold the verdict, and a checker that crashes no longer fails your solution. (#36)
  • [Fix] Debugging a LeetCode case in Python/C++/Rust/JS/Ruby reported success without stopping anywhere – Those languages run your file as-is, which has no main on wrapper platforms. The plugin now says so instead, and points to where debugging does work. The generator's Advanced tab also gained the live preview. (#36)
한국어
  • [신규] 테스트 입력 생성 형식 – 배열 하나가 아니라 입력 형식 전체를 기술합니다. 글자·줄바꿈은 그대로 나오고 이름(...) 호출만 생성값으로 바뀌며, 라벨로 값을 묶어 뒤에서 재사용합니다(rand(1, 100, n) 뒤에 array(n, a)). _라벨은 묶기만 하고 출력하지 않습니다. 생성 함수: const, rand, rand_float, array, array2d, string, perm0/perm1, tree(RANDOM/STAR/PATH/BAMBOO/CATERPILLAR/BINARY), graph(SIMPLE/CONNECTED/DAG/MULTI/TREE, 방향·가중치 선택), bipartite_graph. 여기에 repeat(t as i) { … } 반복(중첩 가능), def 매크로, 집계 sum/min/max/len, 사칙연산, 2^64를 넘는 정수까지 지원합니다. 문자열·2차원 배열·트리·그래프 생성이 이제 리트코드뿐 아니라 stdin 플랫폼(코드포스·SWEA)에서도 됩니다. .ctk-format 파일로 저장하면 구문 강조와 함께 편집할 수 있고, 생성 다이얼로그의 "고급(형식)" 탭에서도 쓸 수 있습니다. (#36)
  • [신규] 저격용 수열 생성 – anti_hash_int는 libstdc++가 쓰게 될 버킷 소수의 배수를 만들어 GCC의 std::unordered_map/set을 한 버킷에 몰아 연산당 O(N)으로 떨어뜨립니다. anti_hash_str은 기존 Thue–Morse 충돌 쌍입니다. (#36)
  • [수정] 컴파일 진단이 Build Output에 표시되지 않던 문제 – v1.7.0부터 Build 창에 "컴파일 실패" 빈 노드만 떴습니다. 모든 진단이 빌드와 같은 이벤트 id를 써서 id 충돌로 조용히 버려지고 있었습니다. 이제 파일 위치를 클릭할 수 있는 진단이 다시 표시됩니다. (#32)
  • [수정] 임베드 페이지 다크 모드 – 창보다 짧은 페이지 아래에 밝은 띠가 생기지 않고, 코드포스 헤더 로고가 어두운 배경에서도 보이며, 이미 어두운 페이지(프로그래머스 문제 화면)가 밝게 반전되지 않습니다. 로드 후 늦게 그려지는 SPA는 다시 판정합니다. (#34)
  • [개선] 템플릿 패널 – 템플릿을 우클릭해 불러오기·플랫폼 기본 지정(★)·삭제를 할 수 있습니다. 저장은 무엇을 저장할지(에디터 전체·선택 영역·파일)를 먼저 묻고 이름은 마지막에 입력받습니다. (#35)
  • [수정] 컴파일 경고가 Build 창에 전달되지 않던 문제 – 경고는 컴파일이 함께 실패할 때만 전달돼, 경고만 있는 빌드는 아무것도 보내지 않았습니다 — 이 기능을 요청한 바로 그 상황입니다. 진단이 엉뚱한 줄로 이동하던 것도 고쳤습니다. 두 클래스 Java(Main + Solution)가 원래 줄 번호를 유지하고, 하네스가 낸 진단이 파일 끝을 넘는 줄로 점프하지 않습니다. (#32)
  • [수정] 템플릿 불러오기가 리트코드 제출을 깨뜨리던 문제 – '전체 교체'가 템플릿 원본을 그대로 써서, 패널이 안내한 {{SOLUTION}}을 쓴 템플릿이 오히려 필수 Solution 클래스를 잃고 자리표시자만 남겼습니다. 이제 새 문제 파일을 만들 때와 같은 방식으로 조합하고, 스텁을 저장해 언제든 되살릴 수 있습니다. 한 템플릿을 여러 플랫폼의 기본으로 지정하는 것도 가능해졌습니다. (#35)
  • [수정] 커스텀 체커가 생성 케이스를 전부 실패로 표시하던 문제 – 체커가 중립 판정보다 먼저 실행되면서 통과/불통과만 답할 수 있었고, 기본 템플릿은 생성 케이스에 없는 기대 출력과 비교했습니다. 이제 체커가 CHECK로 판정을 보류할 수 있고, 체커 자체가 실패해도 풀이를 불통과로 만들지 않습니다. (#36)
  • [수정] 리트코드 케이스를 Python/C++/Rust/JS/Ruby로 디버그하면 아무 데도 멈추지 않고 성공했다고 표시되던 문제 – 이 언어들은 파일을 그대로 실행하는데 래퍼 플랫폼의 파일에는 main이 없습니다. 이제 그 사실과 디버깅이 되는 곳을 안내합니다. 생성 다이얼로그 고급 탭에 라이브 미리보기도 추가했습니다. (#36)

idea-plugin.name: Provenance Recorder
idea-plugin.description:
Provenance Recorder keeps an honesty log of how your code came together while you work on a course assignment. You submit it alongside your code so your work can be reviewed as a process, not just a final file.

It only runs in assignment folders that have been authorized for recording — a project containing a valid, course-signed .provenance-manifest. In every other project the plugin does nothing: no recording, no indicator, no UI.

What you'll see

  • A “Provenance: recording” indicator in the status bar whenever the plugin is active — the only visible change. No popups, no toolbars, no slowdowns.
  • A hidden .provenance/ folder in the assignment where the log lives. Don't delete, commit, or edit it — the seal command bundles it for you.

Recording is meant to be fully transparent — there are no hidden signals. While you work in an authorized assignment, the plugin writes a timestamped, tamper-evident log of the editing process. Here is everything it captures:

Your files and edits

  • The full text of every edit you make in the assignment files — the exact characters inserted or deleted, and where.
  • The contents of an assignment file when it is opened (for files up to 64 KB; larger files are recorded as a cryptographic hash plus a line count).
  • A cryptographic hash of each file every time you save.

Pastes

  • Every paste into an assignment file: its location, length, a hash, and the pasted text itself (its beginning and end for very large pastes) — what makes it possible to tell which code came from outside your own typing.

Where your attention is

  • Which file is focused and when you switch between files; your cursor position and any text you select.
  • When the IDE window gains or loses focus, and how long you've been idle (sampled on a periodic heartbeat).

Terminal

  • Commands you run in the IDE's integrated terminal, including the command text and its exit code, plus which shell you're using.

Your environment

  • A note whenever a plugin activates while you're working.
  • Your IDE version and operating-system platform, and the recorder's own version.
  • A one-way fingerprint of your machine — not your name, email, or IP address, just a value used to notice if one submission was recorded across different computers.

Changes made outside your typing

  • When an assignment file changes by something other than your keystrokes — a formatter, a script, git, or an external editor — the before/after hashes, the size of the change, and (for small files) the new contents.
  • Git operations such as commits and checkouts.

Session and integrity bookkeeping

  • Session boundaries and the links between sessions when you reopen the project, the assignment manifest's signature, and a per-session signing key that makes the log tamper-evident.
  • Internal health signals: clock changes, paste anomalies, breaks in the log's hash chain, and any time the recorder enters a degraded mode or recovers a corrupted log.

The log is stored only on your computer until you upload the sealed .zip yourself; the plugin makes no network requests.

Submitting your work

When you're done, run Tools → Provenance: Prepare Submission Bundle. A sealed .zip is produced next to your assignment — upload it with your code per your assignment's instructions.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.3.1 — enrollment is now up to your course.

  • If your course does not use enrollment, the recorder no longer asks you to enroll. Previously every assignment showed “(not enrolled)” in the status bar and prompted you to get an enrollment token, even in courses that never issue one. Courses that do use enrollment are unchanged — you will still be asked, and your submissions still carry your signed identity.
  • If you have both kinds of course open in the same window, the recorder now keeps them straight: a course that does not use enrollment no longer hides the prompt for one that does, and an identity you have already enrolled in one course is no longer mistaken for being un-enrolled everywhere.

0.3.0 — enrollment, continuous sealing, and group work.

  • Your submissions can now prove they are yours. Use Tools → Provenance: Show My Enrollment Key to get the key your course staff asks for, then Tools → Provenance: Import Enrollment Token to paste back the token they send you. Until you enroll, recording works exactly as it did before, but nothing in the bundle says who produced it — the recorder now tells you that instead of leaving it silent, and enrolling mid-session takes effect right away.
  • Working on a second computer. Provenance: Export Student Identity Secret and Provenance: Import Student Identity Secret move your enrolled identity to another machine, so the work you do there is still attributed to you.
  • Assignments you submit with git push no longer need a seal step. The recorder keeps a sealed record up to date as you work, so whatever you commit is already a valid seal of your work at that moment. Prepare Submission Bundle is unchanged for assignments you upload as a file.
  • Partner and group work. When you and a partner both record in the same repository, each of you records the other's participation into your own signed history, so joint work is attributed to both of you.
  • Your git history — commits, branches and merges — is now part of the record, so a reviewer can see how the work was staged, not only how it was typed.
  • Course staff can now specify exactly which files a submission covers, so generated output and dependencies stay out of your bundle. The recorder tells you when it leaves files out, and that message is not a finding against you.
  • Fixed: when a file changed on disk outside the editor — a git pull, a code formatter, another program — reloading it could be recorded as though you had pasted the new contents.
  • Fixed: preparing a bundle could report files as missing that were present the whole time.
  • Fixed: saving a file could record the contents from before the save rather than what actually reached the disk.
  • Fixed: a file could be recorded as deleted when it had not been.
  • Fixed: a wrong system clock could cost part of your record its order. It can no longer cost it its authorship.

0.2.1 — reliability fixes. No change to what is recorded.

  • Fixed: on Windows, the recorder did not start at all for a project stored on the WSL filesystem — no recording, no indicator, and no “Prepare Submission Bundle” command. It now records there normally.
  • Fixed: an “IDE error occurred” notification could appear when opening a project.
  • Fixed: a file that was already open when recording began could be recorded without its starting contents, so a reviewer's replay of that file started from an empty page instead of the code you began with.
  • The status bar now tells you when recording has stopped working, instead of continuing to show the normal “recording” indicator. If you ever see it, tell your course staff — it means the log is incomplete.
  • Preparing a submission bundle now reports a clear error instead of failing quietly, and no longer leaves a stray temporary file behind.
  • Fixed: sealed bundles reported a recorder fingerprint that course staff's checker did not recognize, which flagged every submission for manual review.

0.2.0

  • Records every authorized assignment open in the project at once, including assignment folders nested inside a parent project, instead of only the project root. Each assignment gets its own independent log, and the status-bar indicator shows how many are recording.
  • Tools → Provenance: Prepare Submission Bundle now asks which assignment to seal when more than one is recording.
  • Opening a file records up to 64 KB of its contents inline (was 4 KB), so more of your starting point is captured directly rather than as a hash.
  • Suspending your machine no longer looks like unexplained missing time: the recorder marks the gap when the session resumes.
  • Fixed: saving a file could be misreported as a change made outside your editor.
  • Fixed: a paste is never recorded in a form the reviewer's replay cannot reproduce.

0.1.0 — first release.

  • Records the editing process in course-authorized assignment folders and seals it into a tamper-evident submission bundle via Tools → Provenance: Prepare Submission Bundle.
  • Bundles are format-compatible with the Provenance VS Code recorder.

idea-plugin.name: TypeGhost
idea-plugin.description:
A teleprompter for your code. Write it once, "type" it live.

TypeGhost replays pre-written code in your editor with human-like typing — irregular rhythm, thinking pauses, even typos that get noticed and fixed. Perfect for conference talks, screencasts, tutorials and classroom demos: no more typos in front of 300 people.

Two ways to fake it

  • Auto mode — the code types itself at a human pace while you narrate, stopping at checkpoints wherever you want to talk.
  • Hacker mode — you mash any keys, the real script comes out. You physically cannot make a typo.

Script directives

Comments with a ~ glued to the comment marker control playback and are stripped from the output: //~ pause 800, //~ checkpoint intro. Works in any language (#~, --~, ;;~, %~).

Find the commands under Tools → TypeGhost. Whatever the simulation does, the final buffer is byte-identical to your script — your demo cannot derail.

Works in IntelliJ IDEA, PhpStorm, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, Rider and every other IntelliJ-based IDE. Sources, web demo and VS Code extension on GitHub.
idea-plugin.change-notes: 0.1.0 — first release: auto mode with human-like typing and checkpoints, hacker mode, pause/resume, script directives.

idea-plugin.name: Morphingbird
idea-plugin.description:
Morphingbird shape-shifts to fit morphological-transducer source files you hand it, understanding ten formats — lexc, lexd, twol, twoc, CG3 (.rlx), lttoolbox .dix/.lsx/.metadix XML, the Apertium→UD .udx mapping and .spellrelax — and it builds a cross-file symbol graph underneath so a morphological tag is one logical node no matter which notation it's wearing. That lets you navigate "what comes from where" and "what depends on what" across the whole module.

Features: syntax highlighting with customizable color schemes, structure view, cross-file & cross-format go-to-definition and Find Usages (continuation classes, tags, archiphonemes, lexd patterns/lexicons), Go to Symbol, hover documentation with an Apertium tagset glossary, index-driven completion, two-tier validation (instant compiler-free cross-file checks plus a background pass that runs the real HFST / lttoolbox / CG3 compilers), a quick-fix to declare an undeclared tag, an "Apertium mode" run configuration with a modes.xml-driven picker and clickable compiler errors, a "Show Build Pipeline" view (a Mermaid diagram and plain-language tips reconstructed from modes.xml and the Makefile, with test-suite awareness), an "apertium-regtest" runner, and an "Analyze Tagger Model" report that decodes a .prob tagger file without running apertium-tagger.

Source and issues: github.com/alexeyev/morphingbird
idea-plugin.change-notes: 0.1.2 — a typo in plugin.xml format that ruined everything, fixed.

idea-plugin.name: LaTeX Pro
idea-plugin.description:
LaTeX brings first-class LaTeX and BibTeX authoring to IntelliJ Platform IDEs.

Write with IDE intelligence

  • Syntax and semantic highlighting, completion, documentation, formatting, folding, inspections, spellchecking, and Grazie prose support.
  • Project-aware diagnostics for undefined commands, include cycles, structural mistakes, unused declarations, duplicates, and obsolete constructs.
  • Project-aware navigation, rename and find usages for labels, citations, commands, environments, packages, and included files.
  • Explore document dependencies and edit multipage longtables while preserving repeated headers and footers.
  • Structure views, breadcrumbs, live and postfix templates, source intentions, a floating formatting toolbar, Cmd+N generation, visual table insertion, an equation editor, and Beamer support.

Manage bibliographies

  • Search bibliography entries by DOI or metadata, review DOI duplicate merges, and import editable DOI metadata previews.
  • Search rich citation completion by key, author, title, or year; navigate, rename, find usages, or safely delete entries.
  • Complete and refactor @string macros, format and fold BibTeX entries, validate styles, find unused entries, and open attached PDFs.
  • Keep chapterbib resources chapter-scoped; index exported .bib files or securely synchronize cached Zotero, Better BibTeX, Mendeley, and HTTPS bibliography sources.

Build and preview locally

  • Compile with latexmk, Tectonic, or pdfLaTeX/XeLaTeX/LuaLaTeX and navigate compiler diagnostics.
  • Infer or explicitly select the main document across multi-file projects.
  • Use a side-by-side PDF preview with continuous rebuilding, single-page or continuous-document display, zoom and navigation controls, and forward/reverse SyncTeX.

Convert documents

Convert LaTeX to Typst or Typst to LaTeX with locally installed Pandoc or Morph. Conversion is available from file context menus, Refactor, and Tools, with executable auto-detection and review-before-overwrite safeguards.

Language editing works without a TeX distribution. External tools are optional, run locally, and are never bundled. Shell escape is disabled by default. Conversion can be lossy and should always be reviewed. The plugin contains no telemetry and does not transmit document contents.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Find Papers… searches Crossref and arXiv from the Bibliography tool window, showing authors, year, venue, identifiers, abstracts, and existing local entries. Review editable metadata and file changes before importing a paper or importing it with a citation; missing bibliography resources can be created during import.
  • Missing required BibTeX fields now offer a quick fix that adds editable placeholders without replacing existing values.
  • Bibliography Health and Search finds DOI/key duplicates and metadata problems, searches local and cached libraries, inserts citations, reviews duplicate merges with reference updates, and imports editable DOI metadata previews.
  • BibTeX crossref, xref, xdata, related, and entryset fields now navigate and participate in entry rename/find usages and reviewed merges.
  • The LaTeX Dependencies tool window explores document roots, includes, bibliographies, resources, shared dependencies, unresolved paths, and cycles.
  • Multipage longtable editing preserves captions, repeated headers and footers, section markers, rules, comments, and page-break options.

Fixed

  • Cancelling bibliography creation or paper metadata review now returns focus to Find Papers, so the next import action responds immediately.
  • Bibliography source navigation and citation insertion no longer produce read-access errors. When a document lacks a bibliography declaration, citation insertion offers a choice of BibLaTeX or BibTeX resources and previews the changes.
  • Bibliography entries now use readable metadata rows, and the Bibliography and LaTeX Dependencies tool windows use native toolbars and light/dark icons.
  • Pasting unsupported or mismatched table data now explains why the paste was rejected.
  • Compiler errors and warnings now appear as navigable items in the IDE Problems window.
  • Literal bracket tests in TeX macros, including those in longtable.sty, no longer produce false missing-optional-argument warnings.
  • Run configurations now share the cancellable, bounded external-tool runner used by preview and conversion, including per-step timeouts.
  • Automatic build planning ignores commented and literal example commands and resolves imported and root-relative document dependencies consistently.
  • Concurrent document builds retain their own diagnostics, suppress stale results atomically, and update the Problems view in publication order.
  • Paginated Mendeley imports now allocate unique citation keys across the entire library rather than separately for each page.
  • Continuous preview saves only the active document's reachable source and resource files, preserving unrelated unsaved edits in the project.

idea-plugin.name: Alpaca
idea-plugin.description:
IDE support for custom languages defined with the Alpaca lexer/parser library for Scala.

An Alpaca-defined language is just Scala code, with no separate grammar file to point an IDE at. This plugin reads the grammar data your lexer{...}/parser macros already compute, exported to disk at compile time, and turns it into a working custom language in the IDE for any language you define, without writing any plugin code yourself.

  • Syntax highlighting inferred from each token's regex shape.
  • A real parser that drives your grammar's exact, conflict-resolved LR table and reports syntax errors as ordinary red squiggles.
  • Structure View and code folding that mirror the parsed tree.
  • Autocompletion of the fixed-spelling terminals valid at the caret.
  • Line comment toggling for grammars with a prefix.*-shaped ignored rule.
  • Reformat Code that spaces and indents around your grammar's brackets, commas, semicolons, and dots, however they're spelled.
  • Highlight occurrences of the identifier under the caret, everywhere it appears in the file.
  • TODO markers in comments feed the TODO tool window and the commit check.
  • Breadcrumbs showing the caret's nesting path through the parsed tree.
  • Quick Documentation (hover / Ctrl+Q) showing a token's pattern or a nonterminal's full set of production alternatives.
  • Pair-quote insertion for grammars whose strings are delimited by " or '.
  • An Alpaca Grammar tool window browsing the current file's whole grammar -- every token and every production alternative -- in one place.

Point Settings | Tools | Alpaca at your grammar export directory and map file extensions to grammars. See the documentation for details.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Grammars exported by Alpaca 0.3.2 and later failed to load: the plugin rejected the start/end offsets that exports now carry in source.

idea-plugin.name: Sourcebeam
idea-plugin.description:
Live code sharing from your IDE to a read-only browser page. This plugin broadcasts the open project to a sourcebeam viewer session: anyone with an invite link watches the code change live, with no editing and no code execution.

Think of it as a lightweight, read-only alternative to Code With Me for the cases where the audience only needs to watch: teaching, mentoring, code walkthroughs, demos and review sessions. Viewers need nothing but a link. The server runs on your own Cloudflare account; this plugin is the host side.

  • Every text file the project's .gitignore doesn't exclude is sent, up to a server-published size cap; binaries are skipped.
  • .gitignore decides what stays private, .env files and keys included; nothing under .git/ is ever sent.
  • The host token lives in the IDE password safe, never in a settings file.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.2

  • Editing a .gitignore while broadcasting now takes effect at once: files it newly excludes are removed from the server, files it no longer excludes are sent.
  • Plain ws:// server URLs are accepted only for localhost; anything else needs wss://, so code and the host token never travel unencrypted.

0.1.1

  • Invite links: the lifetime setting now limits how long a link can be opened. A viewer who opened it in time stays in the project until you revoke invite links or delete the project. Needs the matching server update (bun run deploy).
  • The viewer page reconnects on its own after a network drop, and shows "no access" or "deleted" once access is gone for good (server update).
  • No deprecated platform API usage left on 2026.1 and newer.

0.1.0

Initial release.

  • Broadcast the open project to a read-only live viewer: every text file the project's .gitignore doesn't exclude, up to the server's size cap, with invite links and a status bar widget.

idea-plugin.name: MetaMask Clone (Showcase)
idea-plugin.description:
Metamask Clone – Wallet Architecture Showcase

Overview

Metamask Clone – Wallet Architecture Showcase is an educational IntelliJ IDEA plugin designed to demonstrate how a wallet-like system can be modeled inside an IDE environment.

This plugin is a technical showcase, focusing on architecture, data flow, and system design, rather than a consumer-ready product.

Important:
This is NOT a production wallet.
No real funds are involved.

Purpose

This plugin exists for learning and demonstration purposes only, aimed at developers and system architects who want to understand:

  • How a wallet-style system can be structured
  • How transaction flows are modeled internally
  • How backend concepts map to UI components
  • How to build non-trivial IntelliJ plugins

It is not intended for real asset management or end-user usage.

Supported Networks

  • EVM Networks: Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Polygon (ERC20 tokens, transaction history via Etherscan)
  • TRON Network: TRON Mainnet, Shasta Testnet (TRC20 tokens, transaction history via TronGrid)
  • Bitcoin Network: Bitcoin Mainnet, Testnet, Regtest (via Bitcoin Core RPC)

Key Characteristics

  • Educational / showcase-oriented plugin
  • Multi-chain wallet architecture demonstration
  • No custody of private keys
  • No security guarantees
  • No financial functionality

All behaviors are either simulated or simplified for clarity.

Intended Audience

  • Backend engineers
  • Plugin developers
  • System architects
  • Developers learning wallet system architecture
  • Developers interested in IntelliJ Plugin development

Important Disclaimer

This plugin is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to MetaMask or any related organization.

The term “Metamask Clone” is used solely as a descriptive reference to indicate architectural inspiration and learning context.

Licensing & Responsibility

By installing this plugin, you acknowledge that:

  • This plugin is provided as-is
  • It should not be used for managing real assets
  • The author assumes no responsibility for misuse

Why This Plugin Exists

This plugin is part of a broader educational effort to explain wallet system design from a backend and architectural perspective, not to replicate or replace any existing product.

Video Tutorial Series

Learn how to build this plugin step-by-step with our comprehensive video tutorial series:

Watch the Full Playlist on YouTube

Episode Title
EP01 从零打造真实可商用钱包系统 | Build a Real & Monetizable Crypto Wallet System from Scratch
EP02 工程师级 Sub-Agent 重建钱包 UI | AI Multi-Agent Rebuild of MetaMask UI
EP03 Kotlin Web3j EVM交易流程 | EVM Tx Flow - Transaction vs Receipt
EP04 从钱包系统角度理解 ERC20 | ERC20 Explained from a Wallet System Perspective
EP05 从代码到 Marketplace | From Code to Marketplace
EP06 为什么TRON不是EVM(钱包系统视角) | Why TRON Is NOT EVM (Wallet System View)
EP07 TRON 钱包运行期: 从 Balance 到 Transfer | TRON Wallet Runtime: From Balance to Transfer
EP08 TRC20 钱包运行期：合约支付的执行行为 | TRC20 Wallet Runtime: Contract-Based Payment Execution
EP09 Bitcoin 钱包系统：从 Account 到 UTXO | Bitcoin Wallet System: From Account to UTXO
EP10 Explorer & Indexing：钱包交易历史 | Explorer & Indexing: Wallet Transaction History
EP11 从实现到责任 | From Implementation to Responsibility

Summary for reviewers:

  • Educational / demo plugin
  • No misleading claims
  • No real asset handling
  • Clear non-affiliation disclaimer

idea-plugin.change-notes:
Aiken Plugin 2.0.3 Changelog

  • Fixed code completion for constructors declared in public types from other project modules. Suggestions now appear both while typing and when completion is invoked manually.
  • Code completion no longer suggests a variable inside its own initializer while that variable is being declared.
  • Fixed the remaining auto-popup case where the declared variable could reappear after typing a space following =.
  • Completion now consistently hides names being declared in typed let, expect, and const initializers, regardless of how many spaces follow =.
  • Completion now recognizes values through chains of type aliases and ranks exact type matches above progressively more general underlying types, while still preferring nearer variables when their type match is equally close.
  • Fixed completion through long generic type-alias chains, including chains with more than three levels.
  • Concrete type matches now appear before loosely compatible generic suggestions such as unconstrained T results.
  • Code completion now suggests record fields after a dot. All fields on the current level remain available, while fields matching the surrounding expected type are shown first, including matches through type aliases.
  • Typed initializers inside else branches no longer suggest values narrowed only in the matching if is branch.
  • Untyped variables are no longer suggested inside their own initializers.
  • Typed and untyped initializer completion is now consistent across let, expect, and module const declarations. Destructuring and backpassing forms supported by let and expect follow the same behavior.
  • Completion now understands alternative when patterns separated by |: shared variables are available and correctly typed in the branch body, while constructors remain suggested when entering the next alternative.
  • Completion keeps imported symbols, same-file constants, and local variables in their intended order without showing constants twice.

idea-plugin.name: Midnight Compact Language
idea-plugin.description:
First-class development support for the Compact smart contract language on the Midnight blockchain.

This plugin equips IntelliJ IDEA with a comprehensive developer environment for writing, analyzing, navigating, and compiling zero-knowledge (ZK) smart contracts in Compact.

✨ Features

  • Remix-Style Compact Compiler Tool Window: Sidebar panel to switch compiler versions, auto-download versions into isolated directories, view real-time pragma compatibility, and compile contracts with one click.
  • Multi-Version Compiler Management: Isolated compiler version storage under ~/.compact/versions/<version>/ preventing cross-project compiler collisions with automatic installer support and project-level compiler selection in .idea/midnight.xml.
  • In-Editor Pragma Quick-Fixes: Alt + Enter context actions on pragma language_version to switch project compiler or download required versions on demand, plus quick-fixes for compiler version mismatch errors.
  • Bidirectional Interface & Implementation Navigation: Gutter line markers jumping between interface declarations, circuit definitions, and concrete contract implementations.
  • Syntax Highlighting & Formatting: Rich semantic token coloring, code formatting, smart indentation, brace matching, and code folding.
  • Intelligent Code Completion: Context-aware completion for keywords, built-in types, circuits, witnesses, exports, ledger state, and local bindings.
  • Code Navigation & Find Usages: Go to Declaration (Ctrl+B / Cmd+B), Go to Symbol, and Find Usages across files with split VALUE/TYPE namespaces.
  • Real-Time Inspections & Quick-Fixes:
    • Type mismatch detection
    • Unresolved reference & duplicate declaration checks
    • Pure circuit mutation & sealed field validations
    • Recursive circuit detection & undisclosed witness warnings
    • Unused local variable highlighting with quick-fixes
  • Structure View & Breadcrumbs: Visual outline view of contracts, circuits, witnesses, and type definitions.
  • Quick Documentation & Inlay Hints: Hover documentation with inferred signatures and inline parameter name hints.
  • Compiler & Toolchain Integration: Dedicated Run Configurations and gutter icons to build and verify Compact files using the compact compiler.
  • Live Templates & File Templates: Pre-built templates for new Compact files and common smart contract patterns.

🚀 Getting Started: Configuring the Midnight Compact Compiler

To enable on-the-fly error detection, syntax validation, and the editor Run/Compile button, configure the Compact compiler toolchain in IntelliJ IDEA:

Step 1: Open the Plugin Settings

  • Windows / Linux: Go to File → Settings → Languages & Frameworks → Midnight Compact
  • macOS: Go to IntelliJ IDEA → Settings (or Preferences) → Languages & Frameworks → Midnight Compact

Step 2: Configure the Compiler Executable Path

Option A: Auto-Detection (Recommended)

  1. When you open the settings page, the plugin automatically inspects standard locations (system PATH, WSL environments on Windows, and standard installation directories).
  2. If the compiler is detected, the path is populated automatically with a version confirmation (e.g. compact v0.x.x).
  3. Click Apply or OK.

Option B: Manual Selection (If Auto-Detection Fails)

If the compiler was not found automatically:

  1. Click the Browse (...) button next to Compact Compiler Path.
  2. Select the location of your compact executable:
    • Linux / macOS: Typically /usr/local/bin/compact, ~/.cargo/bin/compact, or your local installation path.
    • Windows (WSL): Select your WSL distribution or path (e.g. \\\\Ubuntu\\usr\\bin\\compact).
    • Windows (Native): Navigate to your installed compact.exe binary. (Note: Avoid C:\\Windows\\System32\\compact.exe, which is Windows' built-in NTFS compression tool).
  3. Click Test / Validate to verify that IntelliJ successfully communicates with the compiler.
  4. Click Apply and OK.

Step 3: Verify in the Editor

  • Open a Contract: Open any .compact smart contract file.
  • Background Error Checking: Compiler diagnostics (errors and warnings) will automatically highlight in the code and appear in the Problems tab.
  • Run / Compile: Click the green Run (▶) icon in the top toolbar or editor gutter to build your contract.

🔗 Resources & Links

  • GitHub Repository
  • Issue Tracker & Bug Reports
  • Midnight Network Documentation
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.4.0 - 2026-09-29

Added

  • Added typed generic right<L, R>(...) and left<L, R>(...) constructor helper completions when returning or assigning to Either<L, R> types, automatically inferring and populating concrete type arguments, positioning the caret within parentheses, and registering tab-out scopes.
  • Added member autocompletion (target.<caret>) for parameterized and generic struct variables (e.g., suggesting is_left, left, right for Either<Bytes<32>, ContractAddress>).
  • Added smart typed and generic Either struct literal completions (Either<T1, T2> { is_left: true, left: ..., right: default<T2> } and Either { ... }) with bracket-aware type argument parsing, expected type detection, and interactive live templates across type parameters and field values (is_left, left, right).
  • Added structured and contextual code completions for default<Type> with angle brackets, type parameter assistance, and smart type inference in expression contexts.
  • Added structured struct literal completions (Either { is_left: true, left: ..., right: default }) with multi-field live template tabbing across is_left, left, and right, as well as constructor helper completions (left(val) and right(val)) and parameterized type completions (Either<Left, Right>).
  • Added boolean literal completions for true and false with dynamic prioritization in boolean condition contexts (e.g. if (...), assert(...), is_left: fields).

Fixed

  • Fixed false-positive unresolved struct field warnings (left, right, is_left) and type mismatch errors when using generic structs (such as Either<A, B>), struct literals, and generic circuit calls with concrete type arguments.

idea-plugin.name: CryptoWatch

idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 1.0.10 - 修复中文/数字合约无法加入自选: 币种名校验由纯 ASCII 放宽为 Unicode 字母/数字, 支持 `龙虾`、`4` 这类币种; 同时把 「能否加入自选」与「能否订阅实时流」两个判断拆开——非 ASCII 币种可正常收藏并以占位行展示, 但不会向币安下发非法订阅流.
  • 1.0.7 - 修复「已连接但推送 0 / 价格不跳动」: 订阅流名被整体转成小写, 导致合约后缀 `@aggTrade`/`@miniTicker` 变成服务端不认的小写形式—— 虽回订阅成功但永不推送; 现仅对交易对部分小写, 后缀保持原样.
  • 1.0.6 - 缓解「已连接但推送 0」: REST 拉取会阻塞流服务的单线程调度器, 导致订阅下发被不断推迟、收到的行情全被丢弃; 现将阻塞的网络请求 移出调度线程, 订阅与广播不再被拖住.
  • 1.0.5 - 缓解频繁「重连中」: 该网络下合约入口握手本身约 80% 失败, 因此缩短握手超时并加快重试节奏, 同时移除成功率 0% 的备用域名 （避免每次失败都多等一个超时窗口）.
  • 1.0.4 - WebSocket 由现货切换为合约: 支持 TAKE 等仅在合约上市的山寨币实时行情, 并增加合约端点轮换以绕过被污染的域名; 现货不存在的交易对不再导致连接反复断开.
  • 1.0.3 - 修复「加入自选后一直卡在重连中」: 校验自选交易对并隔离被服务端拒绝的订阅流, 不再因为一个非法币种导致整条连接反复断开; 新增中/英文界面切换（设置 > 工具 > CryptoWatch）.
  • 1.0.2 - 移除插件图标（此前误用了 SDK 默认模板图标），改用平台默认图标.
  • 1.0.1 - 修复自选不更新: 手动加入的币种（如 ZEC）会立即出现在列表中； 修复实时推送数虚高（只增不减的缓存），刷新时严格按当前自选重新订阅； 界面精简: 去掉市值与来源、去掉「列表更新于」，信息框压缩为单行.
  • 1.0.0 - 实时行情看盘: 多数据源互备、自选、合约、走势图与 K 线.

idea-plugin.name: Code Time
idea-plugin.description:
Code Time

Code Time is an open source plugin for automatic programming metrics and time tracking in IntelliJ and JetBrains IDEs. Track your productivity, protect valuable code time, and stay in flow.

Join our community of over 150,000 developers who use Code Time to reclaim time for focused, uninterrupted coding.

Getting Started

Create an account to keep track of your coding data and unlock access to advanced data visualizations in the Code Time dashboard and web app. You can customize your profile, such as your work hours and office type, for advanced time tracking. You can also connect Outlook or Google Calendar to visualize your code time vs. meetings in a single calendar.

Registering an account also lets you connect multiple code editors on multiple devices using the same email account. Your code time data will sync automatically across your devices.

Open Code Time in the sidebar by clicking the Code Time timer in the status bar. Click Sign up to create a new account, or click Log in to sign into an existing account.

Protect Code Time

Flow Mode makes it easy to eliminate distractions, mute notifications, and stay focused when you are in flow.

You can quickly toggle the dock position or enter full screen. If you connect a Slack workspace, you can pause notifications, update your profile status, and set your presence to *away*. You can customize Flow Mode by clicking the settings option in the Flow section of the Code Time sidebar.

Click Enable Flow Mode to toggle your flow automations. Once you are in Flow Mode, click *Pause Flow Mode* to resume receiving notifications and reset your Slack status.

Track Development Metrics

Your coding stats can help you understand how you are improving over time.

Your status bar shows you in real-time how many hours and minutes you code each day. A rocket will appear if your active code time exceeds your daily average on this day of the week.

To see an overview of your coding activity and project metrics, open the Code Time panel by clicking on the Code Time icon in your sidebar. Click Dashboard to open your personalized Code Time dashboard in a new editor tab. Your dashboard summarizes your coding data—such as your code time by project, lines of code, and keystrokes—today, yesterday, last week, and over the last 90 days.

Your time in editor is the total time you have spent in your editor today. Your active code time is the time you spend actively writing and editing code in your editor or IDE. It captures periods of intense focus and flow. Each metric shows how you compare today to your personal averages. Each average is calculated by day of week over the last 90 days (e.g. a Friday average is an average of all previous Fridays).

Explore Data Visualizations

Click More data at antenna.dev in the Code Time sidebar or visit [app.antenna.dev](https://app.antenna.dev) to see more advanced data visualizations. You will need to create a free Software account to use the web app. In the Code Time dashboard, you will be able to track:

  • Active code time. Visualize your daily active code time. See productivity trends compared to weekly and monthly averages. See how you stack up against the Software community of over 150,000 developers.
  • Top projects. See how much time you spend per project per week. Get a breakdown of your top projects right in your dashboard.
  • Work-life balance. Connect your Google or Outlook Calendar to visualize meeting time versus code time. See how much coding happens during work hours versus nights and weekends so you can find ways to improve your work-life balance.

Invite Your Team

With Teams, you can defend code time, see the impact of meetings, and improve work-life balance across your entire team.

Remember, your data is for you, no one else. Your team data is for your team. When you create a team, you will only see aggregated and anonymized summary data at the team level—available to everyone on that team. In addition, to protect individual privacy, the minimum team size is five members.

To create a team, visit the [team dashboard](https://app.antenna.dev/team-dashboard) in the web app to get started. It's free to create a team, but you can upgrade to a premium plan to unlock additional features.

It’s Safe, Secure, and Free

We never access your code: We do not process, send, or store your proprietary code. We only provide metrics about programming, and we make it easy to see the data we collect.

Your data is private: We will never share your individually identifiable data with your boss. When you join a team, we only show aggregated and anonymized data. We encourage you to read [Data Privacy Matters](https://www.antenna.dev/data-privacy), an overview of the steps we take to protect your privacy and security.

Free for you, forever: We provide 90 days of data history for free, forever. We provide premium plans for advanced features and historical data access.

Code Time also collects basic usage metrics to help us make informed decisions about our roadmap.

Join the Community

Enjoying Code Time? Let us know how it’s going by tweeting or following us at @software_hq.

idea-plugin.name: legado reader
idea-plugin.description:
Legado Reader is a JetBrains IDE plugin based on the open-source reading app Legado

It brings a reading experience into the IDE, allowing developers to read anytime without leaving their coding environment.

Designed to provide inspiration and improve productivity during the coding process.

Legado Reader是 开源阅读APP 的Jetbrains IDE插件版，旨在随时随地在IDE中进行阅读，为编码过程带来灵感和效率的提升。

Legado Reader诞生

有一天，我在编码的时候，突然想起了一本书，于是我打开了手机，打开了阅读APP，然后打开了书，然后开始阅读，然后我发现，我在阅读的时候，编码的效率并不高。

于是我就想，能不能在编码的时候，随时随地阅读。当这个插件完成后，我发现，我在阅读的时候，编码的效率提高了。

因此，我希望，这个插件能够帮助到更多的人，让他们在编码的时候，随时随地阅读，提高编码效率。

已支持功能：

  1. 支持在插件窗口中阅读
  2. 支持在代码编辑器中阅读，在代码行后展示
  3. 支持查看书架目录
  4. 阅读章节正文
  5. 切换上下章
  6. 与阅读APP同步进度
  7. 支持自定义字体颜色、大小
  8. 支持全局保存配置；
  9. 支持服务版阅读;
  10. 阅读APP的web服务地址的历史记录; ……

idea-plugin.name: Pets
idea-plugin.description:
Adds a cute pet to your favourite IDE.

Inspired (very heavily) by vscode-pets created by Anthony Shaw.

Features

  • A pet that walks around, sits, follows you, interacts with you, basically a fwend
  • Pet variants: 5 cats, bunny, chicken, axolotl, hedgehog, 5 dogs, etc.
  • Pet scale setting, to adjust the size of your pet

How to use

  • After installation, you'll find a pet icon on the right toolbar of your IDE, click on it to open the tool window
  • To change the pet variant, go to Preferences > Tools > Pets, and select a pet variant (see screenshot)

Credits

  • Original idea from vscode-pets created by Anthony Shaw
  • All pet spritesheets created by SeethingSwarm (note: the assets were purchased, must not be resold, see itch.io page for details)

idea-plugin.name: Nau Time Tracker
idea-plugin.description:
An easy automatic time tracker: Increases your work efficiency and assists with time management. Featuring a modern web UI and a mobile application

Install
  • Inside your IDE, select Settings > Plugins
  • Search for Nau Time Tracker
  • Install plugin
  • Click on the Nau icon in the status bar and register at nautime.io
  • Enjoy your coding stats


Security
We do not store, transfer, or have access to your code. All collected statistics are private and available only to you
Nau Time plugin is open source and transparent

idea-plugin.name: Discord Integration V2
idea-plugin.description:
Show everyone on Discord what awesome projects you're working on!

Features:
  • Publish information about your current project to Discord
  • Highly customizable in using the plugins settings
  • Shows IDE, project name with description and file name
  • Can detect a wide range of languages and frameworks automatically
  • Supports from multiple icon themes
  • Add buttons to redirect users to your GitHub or project website
  • Automatically hides when you go AFK
  • Hide individual projects you don't want to show
  • Does *not* insert ads into your rich presence
For bug reports please take a look at the GitHub repository.
For feature requests and other feedback please use the Discord server.

Why "v2"? What happened with the original plugin?
This plugin is a fork of the original Jetbrains Discord Integration plugin by Aljoscha Grebe (Almighty Alpaca). I started this fork because the original plugin was not being updated anymore and left with a lot of bugs and compatibility issues. I also want to add some features that are missing from the original plugin to allow even more customization.

idea-plugin.name: Kasama
idea-plugin.description:
Improve your coding habits with Kasama!

Like a fitness tracker, Kasama helps you keeping an eye on your coding practices, such as coding sessions, testing habits, and many more.

Coding sessions

Get an overview on your IDE activity - how long are you active in the IDE and for which project?

Modules

Kasama tracks in which modules you are active and how the activity is split between test code and production code.

Version control (Git) interaction

Discover the frequency of your commits, the size of each commit, the longevity of your branches, and the types of branches you predominantly work on over time (such as feature or bugfix branches).

Testing habits

Learn about your testing habits, including how frequently you run test suites, their failure rate, and their size.

Refactoring usage

Find out which tool-driven refactorings you use and identify blind spots of lesser used refactorings.

Digital wellbeing

Activate break suggestions to keep being focussed in the long run.

And more to come

More features are coming soon...

Documentation

Please check out the Kasama documentation for details.

Contribution

If you would like to file a bug report or feature request, please open an issue.

Privacy

All data is stored locally in the $USER_HOME/kasama-intellij directory.
Kasama does not send any telemetry data.

Acknowledgments

"Black tea icon" Animated icons by Lordicon.com
"Free Pulse Icon in Line Style" by Amit Jakhu is licensed under CC BY 4.0 / adapted

idea-plugin.name: Zakker
idea-plugin.description:
Zakker

A Jetbrains IDE plugin that provides easy access to Islamic remembrances (Azkar) during your coding sessions, helping you stay connected with the words of Allah.

Features

  • Daily Azkar: Access a variety of Azkar (Islamic remembrances) to recite during your coding breaks.
  • Categorized Azkar: Azkar are organized into different categories for easy navigation.
  • Searchable Azkar: Quickly find specific Azkar using the built-in search functionality.
  • Convenient Access: Easily access your Azkar without leaving your Jetbrains IDE.

About the Data

The Azkar data used in this plugin is based on the collection curated by Eng:Osama Younis and available in his azkar-db repository.

Screenshots

Viewing the list of available Azkar categories.

Browsing the Azkar within a selected category.

Feedback and Contributions

We welcome your feedback and contributions to improve the Zakker plugin. If you have any suggestions or encounter any issues, please don't hesitate to create an issue in the project repository.

Happy coding and may the remembrance of Allah be with you!
