idea-plugin.name: NextTask TODO Task Manager
idea-plugin.description:
NextTask TODO Task Manager Plugin


Source Code

NextTask TODO Manager is the only task management plugin for JetBrains IDEs you will need. Allows you to track, organize, and manage your development tasks directly within your favorite IDE. Whether you're handling bugs, planning new features, or organizing code refactoring tasks, this plugin offers a robust and intuitive interface designed to boost your productivity.

Features

  • Multi-Language:
    🇩🇪 🇬🇧 🇫🇷 🇭🇺 🇵🇱 🇸🇰 🇷🇸 🇳🇱 🇷🇺 🇵🇹 🇪🇸 🇮🇹

  • Organizing Tasks:
    Add tasks and organize them by tags (e.g.: Bug, UI, Functionality, etc...), classify them by priority and sort them (Low, Medium, High, Critical) and change status (TODO, In Progress, Done)

  • User-Friendly Interface:
    Enjoy a clean, tabbed UI or floating window that integrates seamlessly with your IDE, making it easy to navigate and manage tasks.
  • Easy Editing:
    Quickly add, edit or delete tasks.
  • Exporting TODO comments:
    Export all TODO comments as JSON or as a .txt file
  • Sync easily with the NextTask website:
    Sync your tasks to and from the official NextTask website

How to use?

  • Install the plugin:
    In your JetBrains IDE navigate to plugins (File -> Settings -> Plugins), find the extension and click install.
  • Add the tool window:
    (View -> Tool Windows -> TODO Manager), move and size the tool window however you prefer.

  • Using the plugin:

    • Adding tasks: On the bottom, there is a button "Add New Task", on clicking it a pop-up window will appear where you can give the task a description, tags and Priority.
    • Editing a task: Above the "Add New Task" button there is one for "Edit", or you can also double click the task you want to change. Another pop-up window will appear where you can change the details about the task.
    • Changing status: Next to the "Edit" button, there is a "Change Status" button, or in the edit window, you can change the status of the selected task.
    • Deleting a task: Select a task and click the "Delete" button to delete.
    • Changing tabs: On the top there are 3 different tabs for the 3 different statuses, each displaying their respective tasks.

  • Converting TODO comments to tasks:

    • Click on the File that contains the TODO comments
    • Click on Add New Task
    • Click on the "Import from TODO Comments" button on the shown dialog
    • Search for the comment you want to import and select it

idea-plugin.name: CodeClocker
idea-plugin.description:
Automatic Time Tracking + AI Timesheets from Git Commits & Jira Worklog Sync

CodeClocker tracks active coding time per project in your JetBrains IDE and works locally by default — no account required. It helps you understand where your time went, prepare standup updates, and export activity data without leaving the IDE.

Optionally connect to CodeClocker Hub to turn IDE activity, commits, and branches into AI-generated weekly timesheet drafts, My Brief summaries, Jira exports, invoices, Team Pulse summaries, approvals, and billing-ready reports.

Use it locally (default)

  • Automatic time tracking — records active coding time per project in the background.
  • What I Was Doing — generate standup-ready summaries with time breakdowns, branch details, and commits.
  • Activity Report — review recent activity by project and commit history inside the IDE.
  • Daily & weekly goals — set coding targets globally or per project, and get notified when you hit them.
  • Pomodoro Timer — built-in timer with configurable work and break intervals.
  • CSV export — export activity data for invoicing or reporting.
  • Privacy first — all data stays on your machine in Local Mode.
  • Auto-pause — pauses tracking when the IDE loses focus or on inactivity timeout.

Connect to Hub for AI timesheets, exports, and team workflows

  • AI-generated weekly timesheets — turn IDE activity, commits, and branches into editable weekly timesheet drafts.
  • My Brief — get an AI-generated summary of your recent work across projects before standup or weekly review.
  • AI standup summaries — generate concise standup-ready updates from your actual work.
  • Jira worklog export — export approved timesheets to Jira and attach logged time to matching tickets using issue keys parsed from IDE activity.
  • CSV & PDF exports — export timesheets for payroll, accounting, client billing, or personal reporting.
  • Invoices — generate invoice-ready outputs for freelance and consulting work.
  • Team Pulse summaries — see AI-generated summaries of what moved across projects and across the team.
  • Approvals workflow — managers review submitted timesheets and request changes when needed.
  • Evidence-linked worklogs — connect timesheet entries to branches and commits.
  • Automated reminders — remind developers to submit and managers to review on time.

Supported IDEs

IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, Android Studio, WebStorm, PhpStorm, Rider, CLion, GoLand, DataGrip, RubyMine, AppCode, RustRover — and all other JetBrains IDEs.

Learn more at site.codeclocker.com.

idea-plugin.name: Fancy Event Sounds
idea-plugin.description:
Fancy Event Sounds adds audio notifications to IntelliJ-based IDEs so you hear when runs start or fail to start.

Give your IDE a voice 🔊

Fancy Event Sounds plays a sound when something happens in your IDE, so you get feedback without having to watch the Run window. You hit Run, look away at your browser or a second monitor, and your ears tell you what happened.

What it does

  • Run started — a sound the moment a run or debug configuration launches.
  • Run failed to start — instant feedback when a configuration cannot launch, instead of silently staring at an empty console.
  • Per-event toggles — turn on only the events you actually care about.
  • Your own sounds — point any event at a custom .mp3 file.
  • Never blocks the IDE — audio plays on a background thread, and a new event stops the previous sound so notifications never pile up.

Configuration

Everything lives under Settings/Preferences → Tools → Event Sounds. Toggle each event, and optionally browse for a custom .mp3. Leave a path empty to use the bundled sound. If a custom file goes missing, the plugin falls back to the bundled sound rather than failing.

Settings are stored application-wide, so they apply to every project in the IDE.

Why this plugin exists

Plugins that did this used to exist, but they stopped being maintained and broke on modern IDEs. This is a maintained fork, rebuilt against a current IntelliJ Platform and actively developed. It continues the work of Event Sounds, which itself continued the original.

Source, roadmap and issue tracker: github.com/mordisk10/event-sounds. Feature requests for new events are welcome.

idea-plugin.name: SonarQube Jira Issuer
idea-plugin.description:
SonarQube Jira Issuer — Load SonarQube issues and push them to Jira as structured, batched tickets — directly from your IDE. No copy-pasting required.

Connect to any SonarQube instance (SonarCloud or self-managed), load issues by type and status, then either export ticket descriptions to a local file or create Jira tickets directly via the Jira REST API.

Key features:
  • Direct Jira creation — push tickets straight to Jira Cloud or Server/DC
  • Sprint selection — assign tickets to an active or future sprint, or leave in backlog
  • Dynamic custom fields — all optional Jira fields for the chosen project/issue-type are shown automatically; fill in any you need
  • Auto story-point detection — finds the correct story-points field for your Jira setup (Next-Gen or Classic) and sets it automatically from calculated estimates
  • Optional team deduplication — when enabled, queries Jira by sq-<key> labels so two developers never create the same ticket twice
  • Secure token storage — SonarQube and Jira tokens stored in IntelliJ PasswordSafe (OS keychain / KeePass), never in plain text
  • Browse projects — discover accessible SonarQube projects directly from the IDE
  • Filter issues — by type (Bug, Code Smell, Vulnerability, Security Hotspot) and status
  • Smart batching — group issues into configurable Jira ticket batches
  • Automatic story-point calculation — effort estimated from issue data (1 SP = 1 working day), rounded to nearest 0.5
  • Epic link support — link created tickets to an existing Epic key
  • File export mode — Jira wiki-markup tables for copy-paste workflows
  • Incremental export — already-created tickets are never duplicated across runs (tracked via Jira labels and a local mapping file)
Supported Jira deployments:
  • Jira Cloud (*.atlassian.net) — API v3, ADF descriptions, Basic auth (email + API token)
  • Jira Server / Data Center — API v2, wiki-markup descriptions, Bearer PAT authentication

idea-plugin.name: AzDTasks
idea-plugin.description:
Azure DevOps Tasks Integration

Integrates Azure DevOps work items directly into your JetBrains IDE, letting you browse, track, and manage tasks without leaving the editor.

Features

  • Task Repository Integration – Connect to Azure DevOps as a native IDE task repository; search work items by title, description, or ID from the Open Task dialog.
  • Current Sprint Panel – Dedicated tool window showing your assigned work items for the current iteration, with auto-refresh.
  • Work Item State Management – Transition work items through their workflow states (e.g. Active → Resolved) directly from the IDE.
  • Time Tracking – Log time spent on tasks back to a configurable Azure DevOps numeric field.
  • Work Item Type Icons – Displays the native Azure DevOps icon for each work item type (Bug, Task, User Story, etc.).
  • PAT Authentication – Authenticates using a Personal Access Token with minimal required scopes.

Setup

  1. Go to Settings → Tools → Tasks → Servers and add a new Azure DevOps server.
  2. Enter your organization name (e.g. {@code myorg} from {@code dev.azure.com/myorg}).
  3. Create a Personal Access Token in Azure DevOps with Work Items (Read & Write) scope and paste it in.
  4. Click Test Connection — project and team dropdowns will populate automatically.
  5. Select your project and team, then save.

The Azure Tasks tool window (right panel) will show your current sprint items and refresh automatically.
idea-plugin.change-notes: added custom where clause

idea-plugin.name: Context Keeper
idea-plugin.description:
Stop losing your place. Save your IDE context and come back exactly where you left off.

Every time you switch tasks — a code review lands, a meeting starts, a colleague asks a question — you lose your train of thought. Context Keeper saves your entire IDE state in one keystroke and restores it instantly when you're ready to continue.

What gets saved in a snapshot:
  • All open tabs in their exact left-to-right order
  • Active file and exact cursor position
  • Git branch — automatically switched on restore
  • List of uncommitted files at the time of saving
  • Your note — what you were doing and why
  • Next step — what to pick up when you return
  • Optionally: all uncommitted changes stashed via git stash
What happens on restore:
  • Switches to the saved Git branch automatically
  • Reopens all tabs in the exact saved order
  • Focuses the active tab and moves cursor to the exact position
  • Automatically restores stashed changes if the snapshot had a stash
  • Snapshot is removed from the list after restore — no clutter
Auto-snapshot on branch switch:
When you switch a Git branch, Context Keeper automatically detects it and prompts you to save a snapshot of the context you are leaving — so you can always get back to exactly where you were on that branch.

Inline editing:
Double-click the detail panel (or press the Edit button in the toolbar) to edit the snapshot name, note, and next step directly in the side panel — no dialogs, no interruptions.

Git stash integration:
When saving a snapshot, you can optionally check "Stash uncommitted changes". Context Keeper will run git stash across all relevant repositories in your project (including submodules), hiding your in-progress work. When you restore the snapshot, the stash is automatically popped back — your changes return exactly as you left them. If you delete a snapshot with a stash, the stash is dropped from git as well.

Keyboard shortcuts:
  • Windows / Linux: Ctrl+Alt+S — Save  |  Ctrl+Alt+R — Restore
  • macOS: ⌃⇧S — Save  |  ⌃⇧R — Restore
You can also use the Context Keeper side panel (right toolbar) to browse all snapshots, see full details, restore with a double-click, and edit notes inline.

Snapshot age & stale warnings:
Each snapshot in the list shows its age ("today", "3d ago"). Snapshots older than a configurable threshold (default: 7 days) are highlighted in orange with a ⚠ badge — a gentle reminder that you may have forgotten about that context. The threshold is configurable in Settings → Tools → Context Keeper.

Hover tooltip:
Hover over any snapshot in the list to see a quick preview of your note — without having to click and open the detail panel.

Daily context reminder:
On the first IDE launch of each day, if you have snapshots with notes or next steps, Context Keeper shows a balloon with your oldest forgotten context — what you were doing and what you planned to do next. A one-click Restore button lets you jump straight back in.

Designed and tested for IntelliJ IDEA. May work in other JetBrains IDEs based on IntelliJ Platform — not officially tested.

idea-plugin.name: GoIT Tracker
idea-plugin.description:
GoIT Tracker

A lightweight and reliable activity tracking plugin for PyCharm that measures your coding time and sends it to the GoIT API.

The plugin is designed to provide accurate session tracking, support offline work, and offer flexible activity detection modes depending on your workflow.

Features

  • Accurate coding session tracking
  • Soft activity tracking (thinking, reading, navigation)
  • Hard key press activity tracking (default)
  • Offline queue with automatic retry
  • Local session logging and statistics
  • Reliable API communication with retry logic
  • Fully configurable tracking behavior
  • Native PyCharm UI integration

Configuration

Settings → Tools → GoIT PyCharm Tracker

idea-plugin.name: ByteSip
idea-plugin.description:
ByteSip — Healthy Coding Reminders for Developers

Tired of coding for hours without a break? ByteSip is your friendly wellness companion that lives inside your IDE. It quietly reminds you to take care of yourself with witty, non-intrusive balloon notifications — so you can keep shipping code without sacrificing your health.

Features

  • Water reminders — every 25 minutes, because your kidneys deserve better than coffee.
  • Eye-rest reminders — every 50 minutes, following the 20-20-20 rule for healthier eyes.
  • Movement reminders — every 90 minutes, so your spine doesn't file a critical bug report.

Why ByteSip?

  • 🎈 Non-blocking notifications — appears as a balloon at the bottom of your IDE, never interrupts your flow.
  • 😄 Funny, motivating messages — randomly picked from a curated pool to keep things fresh.
  • ⏸️ Snooze or Done actions — quickly dismiss or postpone with a single click.
  • ⚙️ Zero configuration — install it and it just works. No setup required.
  • 🪶 Lightweight — minimal resource usage, runs silently in the background.
  • 🦆 Rubber duck approved — your rubber duck is worried about you too.

⚠️ Side effects may include: better posture, actual human interaction, and vaguely remembering what sunlight looks like.

How It Works

ByteSip automatically starts when you open a project. It runs three independent timers — one for each reminder type — and displays a balloon notification at the bottom-right of your IDE when it's time for a break. Each notification includes a quick "Done" or "Snooze" action so you stay in control.

Code happy. Stay hydrated. Take breaks. Ship better code.

No developers were harmed in the making of this plugin. That's kind of the whole point.

idea-plugin.name: TakaTime
idea-plugin.description:
TakaTime is an open-source, privacy-first time tracker and coding telemetry engine built for developers. Track your coding activity, project time, and language usage directly inside your IDE without sending your personal data to third-party servers.

Key Features:

  • 100% Privacy & BYOD: Bring your own database. All telemetry is securely routed to your personal MongoDB instance.
  • Integrated TUI Dashboard: View your developer productivity analytics and coding stats natively inside the IDE's built-in terminal.
  • Smart Heartbeat Detection: Accurately calculates true coding duration and automatically pauses when you are away from the keyboard.
  • Cross-Platform Parity: Seamlessly syncs your coding metrics across JetBrains IDEs, VS Code, and Neovim.
  • The Open-Source Alternative: A lightweight, Go-based alternative to WakaTime, designed for maximum performance and zero UI freezing.

Take back control of your developer analytics. Configure your database, install the plugin, and start measuring your coding productivity today.

idea-plugin.name: Axiode
idea-plugin.description:
Metrics, insights, and time tracking automatically generated from your programming activity.

Installation

1. Inside your IDE, select Preferences -> Plugins -> Marketplace.

2. Search for axiode.

3. Click the Install button and confirm the installation.

4. Re-launch your IDE.

5. Enter your api key, then click Save.

6. Use your IDE like you normally do and your time will be tracked for you automatically.

7. Visit https://axiode.vercel.app to see your logged time.

idea-plugin.name: Feature Time
idea-plugin.description:
Feature Time automatically tracks the time you actually spend coding — no timers to start, no buttons to remember to press.

The plugin quietly observes your real activity in the IDE (editing, navigating, scrolling, switching files, and Git events), turns it into precise work sessions, and keeps a clear timeline of how your day was spent. When connected to Jira, it syncs the tracked time into work logs, so your reporting stays accurate without manual bookkeeping.

Features

  • Fully automatic tracking — time is recorded from genuine editor activity, and idle periods are excluded so totals reflect real focused work.
  • Smart work sessions — heartbeats are grouped into sessions with configurable gap, merge, and minimum-duration rules to avoid noise.
  • Daily timeline — a dedicated tool window shows today's and previous days' sessions, the files touched, and total time.
  • Manual control when you need it — edit a session's start/end time, remove a session, or pause and resume tracking from the status-bar widget.
  • Jira sync — push tracked time into Jira work logs automatically on a configurable interval.
  • Git aware — captures branch and push context so sessions carry meaningful metadata.
  • Privacy first — tracking can be disabled at any time, and data is retained only for as long as you configure.

Set your Jira URL and API key in Settings → Tools → Feature Time to enable sync, or use the plugin purely as a local time tracker.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Automatic time tracking based on real editor activity (editing, navigation, scrolling, file switching, and Git events)
  • Smart work sessions with configurable gap, merge, and minimum-duration rules
  • Daily timeline tool window showing sessions, touched files, and total time
  • Manual session editing, removal, and pause/resume from the status-bar widget
  • Jira work-log synchronization on a configurable interval
  • Configurable data retention

idea-plugin.name: Treadmill Buddy
idea-plugin.description:
Walking pad and treadmill desk tracker: time, distance, steps, and calories for every walk while you code.

Treadmill Buddy is a workout timer, step counter, and calorie tracker for an under-desk treadmill or a walking pad under your standing desk. It runs in every JetBrains IDE, with a large digital clock in its tool window, a status bar widget, and a floating clock that can stay on top.

Four workout modes

  • Marathon: an open-ended stopwatch that counts up.
  • Calorie burn: counts down the time needed to burn a calorie target.
  • KG burn: counts down the time needed to burn a target body mass, in kg or lb.
  • Interval walk: Pomodoro-style walking and break blocks, such as 25 and 5 minutes, with a chime at each switch.

Fitness and health tracking

  • Daily and weekly goals for steps, distance, or calories, with progress bars.
  • Today, last-7-days, and all-time totals, a 14-day distance chart, a six-month activity heatmap, and a walking streak with configurable rest days.
  • Personal records for the longest session and the best day's distance and steps.
  • Optional move reminders after a set time at the keyboard without walking.
  • Steps and calories are estimated from your speed, height, and weight.

Made for walking while you code

  • Auto-pause when the keyboard and mouse go idle, and resume as soon as you type again.
  • Metric or imperial units, speed presets, and four calorie algorithms, including an incline-aware treadmill model.
  • One session history shared by all your JetBrains IDEs, with CSV and JSON import and export, and TCX export for fitness apps.

Open source under the Apache License 2.0. Source code and issue tracker: GitHub.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• A clearer plugin description. The plugin itself is unchanged.

Full changelog

idea-plugin.name: WorkTracker
idea-plugin.description:
Stop reconstructing your timesheet from memory. WorkTracker watches your editing activity and git history, infers which Jira ticket each block of work belongs to, suggests the time spent and an AI-written worklog note — and lets you review, adjust, and submit it all to Jira Cloud without leaving the IDE.

What it does

  • Automatic worklog suggestions — inferred from your editor activity, current branch, and commits, with time spans and notes pre-filled.
  • Week calendar — see your week as draggable, resizable time blocks; create entries by clicking empty slots; submit unsaved drafts with one click.
  • Backfill from git — reconstruct past weeks you forgot to track: commits are attributed to tickets (message, branch, and merge history), placed at their real times, and offered as accept/dismiss ghost blocks.
  • AI notes, your choice of engine — Anthropic Claude, a fully local Ollama model, or a deterministic offline fallback with no AI at all.
  • Daily standup summary — a Yesterday/Today digest built from your worklogs, commits, and checked-out branches, ready to paste into chat.
  • Full Jira flow — search and create tickets, start/finish-work orchestration (branch, transition, assignee, push), comments, and worklog import — all from the tool window.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.1.0 — Initial release

  • Automatic worklog suggestions inferred from your editing activity, current git branch, and commits — time spans and notes pre-filled for review.
  • Week calendar with draggable/resizable blocks, click-to-create empty slots, one-click submit-to-Jira on unsaved drafts, and a go-to-week picker.
  • Backfill from git: reconstruct untracked past weeks — commits attributed to tickets via message, branch, and merge history (git-flow aware), placed at their real times, offered as accept/dismiss ghost blocks.
  • AI worklog notes via Anthropic Claude or a local Ollama model, with a deterministic offline fallback; note regeneration works from git history for older entries.
  • Daily standup summary from worklogs, commits, and checked-out branches.
  • Ticket picker with bare-number lookup ("2254" finds PROJ-2254 across your projects), full-text search, and inline ticket creation with AI titles.
  • Full Jira Cloud flow: submit/import worklogs, create tickets, start/finish-work orchestration (branch, transition, assignee, push), comments, and people editing.
  • Local-first: activity and drafts stay in an on-disk SQLite database; secrets live in the IDE's PasswordSafe. See Privacy & data above.

idea-plugin.name: Alarm & Timer
idea-plugin.description:
Set one-time alarms and time-based reminders, or run multiple countdown timers inside your JetBrains IDE.

Open and start

  1. Choose Tools → Alarm & Timer → Open Alarm & Timer. You can also use View → Tool Windows → Alarm & Timer.
  2. Select the Alarm or Timer tab, enter a time or duration, then click Set Alarm or Start Timer.

The Tools → Alarm & Timer menu also provides Set an Alarm and Start a Timer shortcuts.

Use the checkmarked Tools → Alarm & Timer → Alert Sound item to turn alert sound on or off. To change its volume or test it, choose Tools → Alarm & Timer → Settings…, then use the Alerts section.

Join a meeting at a specific time, check a build after a short wait, or remember to take a break without leaving your IDE.

  • Set one-time alarms in 12-hour or 24-hour time, with an optional date and label.
  • Start multiple countdown timers with flexible duration formats or six quick presets.
  • Edit or cancel alarms; pause, resume, restart, or cancel timers.
  • See the nearest active item as a countdown in the IDE status bar.
  • Receive a JetBrains IDE notification with a Dismiss action and optional local procedural sound.
  • Restore active items after restart and classify older overdue items as Missed using a configurable recovery window.

Items and settings are stored locally and shared across open projects. No audio files are downloaded, no project files are read, no telemetry is collected, and no automatic network requests are made.

The plugin follows the IDE UI language in English, Brazilian Portuguese, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Spanish, or Turkish, with English as the fallback.

IDE availability: Alarms and timers can alert you only while a compatible JetBrains IDE is running. Minimizing the IDE does not stop alerts. Closing the IDE or system sleep delays delivery. Eligible overdue items are handled after startup or activation.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Timers now count time spent in system sleep and preserve their overdue age when saved. Alert volume works on audio devices without hardware volume controls. Failed alarm edits keep your unsaved text. Release verification now includes Android Studio and independent checks for both provenance attestations.

idea-plugin.name: Todoso: Markdown Todo List
idea-plugin.description:
Todoso: Markdown Todo List

A simple IntelliJ plugin to manage your todo list directly from a todo.md file in your project root or local folder. Inspired by the clean Markdown workflows of Obsidian and Notion (100% local, no accounts or cloud sync).

I created Todoso because I wanted a quick way to keep track of tasks without leaving my code editor or opening external apps. It just reads and writes plain Markdown files on your computer.

  • Local Markdown Files: Reads todo.md in your project root by default, or any .md file on your disk (including local Obsidian vault files).
  • Smart Input Panel: Auto-suggests #tags, priorities ([H], [M], [L]), and preserves typed text if you switch modes.
  • Double-Click Action: Double-click tags, task IDs (🆔), or URLs to search or open links (prevents accidental misclicks when selecting a task).
  • Flexible Sorting & Search: Sort by status, priority, and date, or filter by tags, versions, and keywords (Ctrl + F).
  • Right-Click Menu:
    • Send task description & ID directly to the IDE Commit Tool Window.
    • Link tasks to IntelliJ Bookmarks and jump straight to code lines.
    • Add tasks to CHANGELOG.md under ## [Unreleased].
    • Pick a random task to work on.
    • Add metadata notes (//).
  • Time Tracking: Tracks start dates (🛫), completion dates (✅), and duration (e.g. 1h 45m).
  • if the plugin's screenshot slideshow appears, please avoid swiping to the left.

or Feel free to click— I promise it's not a Rickroll! Read more on GitHub
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Added task draft preservation feature: fixed an issue where typing a new task and switching actions (e.g., cancelling a task, editing a task, or adding a note) would cause the typed input to be lost or accidentally converted into a note.
  • Fixed a UX issue reported by @mouserd where selecting a task in the list left the item highlighted even when typing a new task in the input field, which could lead to accidental task deletions when pressing Delete/Backspace. Thanks for the report!
  • Added "Recent Tags" submenu under Manage Tags in the context menu to display tags ordered by task creation time (Popular Tags alone becomes less effective as the number of tags grows).
  • Added "Set as Commit Message" context menu feature to directly populate task descriptions into the IDE's Commit Tool Window (say goodbye to repetitive "update" commit messages!).
  • How did you know I often type "update" for every commit? AI, give me some humor.

idea-plugin.name: Branch Time Tracker
idea-plugin.description:
Tracks the time you spend working on the Git branches of your projects, across every open project in a single IDE-wide view.

  • Automatically creates a tracking entry when you check out a branch — or add one manually.
  • Start, pause, stop and delete tracking for each branch; only one timer runs at a time.

idea-plugin.name: Sumery Libra - Coding Time
idea-plugin.description:
Records coding time for Sumery Libra, only while you are editing code.

A heartbeat is written when you type into the file in the selected editor while the IDE has focus. Reading, scrolling, switching files, reloads after git checkout and time spent in other applications record nothing, so Libra ends each stretch at your last edit.

Heartbeats are appended to ~/.orea/ide-heartbeats.jsonl (or $OREA_HOME) and hold only the time, the IDE and the project root: never file names, contents or window titles. Switch collection off in Libra under Settings → Data sources.
idea-plugin.change-notes:

  • Reloads from disk, whole-text replacements and edits in background tabs are ignored.
  • Throttled to one heartbeat per 30 seconds; the last edit of a stretch is always written.
  • Records only the time, the IDE and the project root. Never file names or contents.

idea-plugin.name: AiGo123 - Claude Codex ChatGPT DeepSeek Gemini Kimi Qwen GLM GPT
idea-plugin.description:
AiGo123 — AI Coding Agent for JetBrains IDEs

AiGo123 brings a full AI agent development team into your JetBrains IDE. It runs a real VS Code Extension Host inside IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, CLion, PhpStorm, RubyMine, DataGrip, Rider and Android Studio, so the same agent you know from VS Code works natively in your JetBrains workflow.

AiGo123 is part of an ecosystem: the AiGo123.net model gateway, the KKSwitch local routing desktop app, and the AiGo123 agent itself. Use them together or independently.

What the plugin itself does

  • Real Extension Host runtime: launches a bundled VS Code Extension Host process and speaks the VS Code IPC/RPC protocol, so VS Code-based agents run as first-class citizens.
  • Automatic Node.js setup: downloads and installs a portable Node.js runtime (v20.19.2) into ~/.run-vs-agent/nodejs on first use — no manual Node.js installation required.
  • Native IDE integration: editor, document, diff, bulk-edit, tab-state, terminal and shell-integration sync between the IDE and the agent.
  • Tool Window UI: a dedicated AiGo123 tool window with theme-aware styling, drag & drop, and automatic reveal after indexing.
  • Dynamic actions: toolbar buttons and editor context-menu entries (Explain Code, Fix Code, Fix Logic, Improve Code, Add to Context, New Task) that adapt to the active agent.
  • Multiple agent providers: switch between AiGo123 / Roo Code, Cline, Kilo Code and Costrict.
  • Resilient VSIX delivery: multi-source, multi-threaded (5 parallel ranges) download with resume, ETag/Last-Modified validation and automatic failover.
  • JCEF compatibility & fallback: detects missing JCEF (including the IntelliJ 262 / 2026.2 split into com.intellij.modules.jcef) and shows a diagnostic panel instead of failing to load.

What the agent can do

  • Generate code from natural-language descriptions and specs
  • Refactor, debug and explain existing code
  • Write and update documentation
  • Answer questions about your codebase with codebase indexing
  • Automate repetitive tasks and run terminal commands
  • Use MCP servers, Skills, Slash Commands and custom Modes (Code, Architect, Ask, Debug)
  • Follow project rules such as AGENTS.md

KKSwitch — local all-in-one API token routing (recommended)

KKSwitch is a local, all-in-one API token aggregation, routing and AI Agent integration desktop app. It manages upstream providers, models and local Agent tools in one place, with model conversion, zero-config setup, isolated multi-window workspaces, IDE integration and LAN proxy forwarding.

  • Zero configuration: start mainstream AI Agent tools without editing JSON or config files.
  • Protocol conversion: heuristically detect and convert between OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages.
  • Unified model catalog: aggregate, deduplicate and sort models from enabled providers; switching takes effect immediately without restarting your tools.
  • Isolated runtime: run multiple Codex, Claude and other clients side by side across different workspaces.
  • Safe by design: redacted diffs, backups, atomic writes and post-write verification; API keys stay local and are never uploaded.
  • Local proxy: listens on 127.0.0.1 by default (ports 26001–26100) and exposes an OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint; LAN mode is opt-in.

When KKSwitch is running, AiGo123 detects it automatically and can route requests through it. Download it at www.kkswitch.com (Windows and macOS). KKSwitch is not bundled with the plugin and is not required.

AiGo123.net — model & API gateway

AiGo123.net is a next-generation large-model gateway and AI asset management platform. It provides API tokens and access to models such as Claude, Codex, DeepSeek, Gemini, Kimi, Qwen and GLM, with multi-protocol support (OpenAI Chat/Responses, Claude Messages, Google Gemini), smart routing with weighted channels and automatic retry, format conversion, and usage dashboards. It is compatible with Claude Code and other CLI tools. The plugin works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint you configure; AiGo123.net is the recommended, ready-to-use option.

Supported IDEs

  • IntelliJ IDEA (Ultimate & Community)
  • WebStorm — JavaScript and TypeScript
  • PyCharm (Professional & Community) — Python
  • PhpStorm — PHP
  • RubyMine — Ruby
  • CLion — C/C++
  • GoLand — Go
  • DataGrip — Databases
  • Rider — .NET
  • Android Studio — Android

Requirements & compatibility

  • JetBrains IDE 2022.3 (build 223) or later; declared compatible up to 271.*.
  • Node.js is prepared automatically (portable v20.19.2); the Extension Host requires Node.js 20.6.0+.
  • JCEF is required for the embedded UI. On IntelliJ Platform 262 (2026.2)+ it is provided by the bundled Web Browser (JCEF) plugin; if it is missing, the plugin shows a diagnostic panel with recovery hints.
  • Linux ARM is currently not supported by the runtime installer and is reported as unsupported in the UI.

简体中文

AiGo123 将完整的 AI 代理开发团队带入你的 JetBrains IDE。它在 IntelliJ IDEA、WebStorm、PyCharm、GoLand、CLion、PhpStorm、RubyMine、DataGrip、Rider 和 Android Studio 中运行真正的 VS Code 扩展宿主，让 VS Code 生态中的 AI 代理在 JetBrains 工作流中原生可用。

AiGo123 属于一个完整生态：AiGo123.net 模型网关、KKSwitch 本机路由桌面应用，以及 AiGo123 代理本身。可组合使用，也可独立使用。

插件本身的能力

  • 真实扩展宿主运行时：启动内置的 VS Code 扩展宿主进程，使用 VS Code IPC/RPC 协议通信。
  • 自动准备 Node.js：首次使用时自动下载便携版 Node.js（v20.19.2）到 ~/.run-vs-agent/nodejs，无需手动安装。
  • IDE 原生集成：编辑器、文档、Diff、批量编辑、标签状态、终端与 Shell Integration 双向同步。
  • 工具窗口界面：独立的 AiGo123 工具窗口，支持主题自适应、拖放，并在索引完成后自动展开。
  • 动态操作：工具栏按钮与编辑器右键菜单（解释代码、修复代码、修复逻辑、改进代码、加入上下文、新建任务）随当前代理动态变化。
  • 多代理提供商：可在 AiGo123 / Roo Code、Cline、Kilo Code、Costrict 之间切换。
  • 可靠的 VSIX 分发：多源、多线程（5 路并发分片）下载，支持断点续传、ETag/Last-Modified 校验与自动故障转移。
  • JCEF 兼容与降级：可检测 JCEF 缺失（包括 IntelliJ 262 / 2026.2 拆分为 com.intellij.modules.jcef），并显示诊断面板而非加载失败。

代理能做什么

  • 根据自然语言描述与规格生成代码
  • 重构、调试并解释现有代码
  • 编写与更新文档
  • 基于代码库索引回答代码相关问题
  • 自动化重复任务并执行终端命令
  • 使用 MCP 服务器、Skills、斜杠命令与自定义模式（Code、Architect、Ask、Debug）
  • 遵循 AGENTS.md 等项目规则

KKSwitch —— 本机一体化 API Token 路由（推荐）

KKSwitch 是一款本机一体化 API Token 聚合、路由与 AI Agent 集成桌面应用。它把上游渠道、模型与本地 Agent 工具集中管理，提供模型转换、零配置接入、多窗口隔离工作区、IDE 集成与局域网代理转发。

  • 零配置：无需编辑 JSON 或配置文件即可启动主流 AI Agent 工具。
  • 协议转换：在 OpenAI Chat、OpenAI Responses 与 Anthropic Messages 之间启发式检测与转换。
  • 统一模型目录：聚合、去重并排序已启用渠道的模型；切换实时生效，无需重启工具。
  • 隔离运行时：在不同工作区中并行运行多个 Codex、Claude 等客户端。
  • 安全设计：脱敏 diff、备份、原子写入与写后验证；API Key 仅保存在本地，绝不上传。
  • 本机代理：默认仅监听 127.0.0.1（端口 26001–26100），提供 OpenAI 兼容的 /v1 接口；局域网模式需显式开启。

当 KKSwitch 运行时，AiGo123 会自动检测并可经其转发请求。可在 www.kkswitch.com 下载（支持 Windows 与 macOS）。KKSwitch 不随插件捆绑，也非必需。

AiGo123.net —— 模型与 API 网关

AiGo123.net 是新一代大模型网关与 AI 资产管理系统，提供 API Token 以及对 Claude、Codex、DeepSeek、Gemini、Kimi、Qwen、GLM 等模型的访问，支持多协议（OpenAI Chat/Responses、Claude Messages、Google Gemini）、渠道加权随机与失败自动重试的智能路由、格式转换以及用量看板。它兼容 Claude Code 及其他 CLI 工具。插件也可使用任意 OpenAI 兼容端点，AiGo123.net 是推荐的开箱即用选项。

支持的 IDE

IntelliJ IDEA（Ultimate 与 Community）、WebStorm、PyCharm（Professional 与 Community）、PhpStorm、RubyMine、CLion、GoLand、DataGrip、Rider、Android Studio。

要求与兼容性

  • JetBrains IDE 2022.3（build 223）及以上，声明兼容至 271.*。
  • Node.js 自动准备（便携版 v20.19.2）；扩展宿主要求 Node.js 20.6.0+。
  • 内嵌界面需要 JCEF。在 IntelliJ Platform 262（2026.2）及以上由捆绑的 Web Browser (JCEF) 插件提供；若缺失，插件会显示带恢复建议的诊断面板。
  • Linux ARM 当前不受运行时安装器支持，界面中会提示不支持。

idea-plugin.name: Klikor IDE Bridge
idea-plugin.description:
Klikor IDE Bridge

Lets you control this IDE directly from the Klikor desktop app: run/debug configurations, step commands, and any other IDE action, triggered from Klikor buttons and macros.

Zero-config: install this plugin, point a Klikor button at the action ID you want, and it works. The Klikor app ships a set of curated action presets for common IDE actions, and any other IDE action id (including ones contributed by third-party plugins) works too.

Version 2.0.0 is a ground-up rewrite on stable, public IntelliJ Platform API only, keeping the exact same local HTTP action-execution protocol as earlier versions -- a drop-in upgrade. It installs, enables, and disables without an IDE restart.

Klikor IDE Bridge speaks the same local HTTP action-execution protocol as JetBrains' open-source intellij-streamdeck-plugin (originally built as the backend for the Elgato Stream Deck IntelliJ integration), licensed under Apache-2.0, from which earlier 1.x versions of this plugin were forked.

Note: this plugin doesn't support Gateway/JetBrains Client so far.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2.0.0
- Complete rewrite on stable, public IntelliJ Platform API only (zero internal API usage).
- Dynamic plugin: installs, enables, and disables without an IDE restart.
- ONE version for all IDEs 2024.3 and newer, replacing the 1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0 build-range ladder.
- Serves on a dedicated localhost port (21420-21430) instead of the IDE's built-in web server; Klikor 2.8.1+ auto-discovers it. Legacy Klikor IDE Bridge 1.x installs still work with Klikor.
- The in-IDE Action Browser settings page has been removed; use the Klikor desktop app's own action picker/presets to find action ids instead.
1.2.0
- Supports IntelliJ Platform 2026.2 and newer (sinceBuild 262), tracking upstream's fix for IDE 2026.2+ compatibility (ActionTreeGroupUtil keymap API). Install this version if your IDE is 2026.2 or later; Klikor IDE Bridge 1.1.0 remains available for IDEs 2025.2-2026.1, and 1.0.0 for IDEs 2024.3-2025.1.
1.1.0
- Supports IntelliJ Platform 2025.2 through 2026.1 (sinceBuild 252, untilBuild 261.*), tracking upstream's fix for IDE 2025.2+ compatibility. Install this version if your IDE is 2025.2-2026.1; Klikor IDE Bridge 1.0.0 remains available for IDEs 2024.3-2025.1, and 1.2.0 for IDEs 2026.2 and newer.
1.0.0
- Initial Klikor IDE Bridge release, forked from JetBrains' intellij-streamdeck-plugin (Apache-2.0).
- Same local/remote action-execution HTTP protocol as the upstream plugin (drop-in compatible with Klikor).
- "Perform action only when IDE window is focused" now defaults OFF, since Klikor buttons are expected to trigger IDE actions without stealing focus.

idea-plugin.name: Slint Pro
idea-plugin.description:
This is a community plugin developed and distributed by JetPlugins.

Slint Pro brings visual Slint development and JetBrains-native code intelligence into one workflow.

  • Design and preview: use the integrated Designer powered by upstream Slint preview tooling, with two-way source navigation, linked selections, and a searchable drag-and-drop component Gallery.
  • Code with confidence: get completion, diagnostics, formatting, documentation, auto-imports, configurable inspections, color editing, image and font previews, spellchecking, and TODO support.
  • Navigate and refactor: find usages and safely rename components, properties, callbacks, imports, and files; navigate to symbols, types, and base components; optimize imports; and extract reusable components or theme values.
  • Start projects quickly: create Slint applications from the IDE for Rust, C++, Node.js, Python, and embedded Rust.
  • Stay aligned with the project: automatically detect the Slint version and run a matching managed language server, or use a locally installed server.

Slint Pro supports IntelliJ IDEA, CLion, RustRover, PyCharm, WebStorm, Rider, and other compatible JetBrains IDEs.

Slint Pro builds on the excellent foundation established by the original Slint plugin. We're grateful for the thoughtful work that brought Slint support to JetBrains IDEs and made this plugin possible.

The plugin is a paid JetBrains Marketplace product. New installations receive the Marketplace-configured free trial; there is no reduced free edition.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changed

  • The plugin description now clearly identifies Slint Pro as a community plugin developed and distributed by JetPlugins.

idea-plugin.name: Curly Embedded Tools
idea-plugin.description:
Bare-metal ARMv8 (AArch64) embedded development tooling.
Adds custom language support for the three file kinds a QEMU + gdb-multiarch workflow revolves around:
  • ARMv8 assembly (.s, .S, .asm) — lexing, parsing, syntax highlighting, formatting, completion, inspections and intentions.
  • GDB scripts (.gdbinit, *.gdb) — command completion, block structure checking and folding.
  • GNU linker scripts (.ld, .lds) — section/region analysis with navigation from > REGION to its MEMORY declaration.

idea-plugin.name: KMP Project Wizard
idea-plugin.description:
KMP Project Wizard generates a Kotlin Multiplatform project straight from File → New Project in IntelliJ IDEA and Android Studio.

Instead of hand-wiring Gradle, DI, navigation and a database, it generates a clean, modular, test-covered KMP project that targets Android, Desktop (JVM) and iOS from a single dialog.

What you get out of the box

  • Compose Multiplatform UI shared across platforms, with type-safe Navigation 3.
  • Room 3 (SQLite) persistence, KMP-ready.
  • Koin dependency injection with annotation processing (KSP).
  • Clean Architecture: clear Domain / Data / UI layers and a feature API/impl split.
  • Gradle convention plugins + version catalog for tidy, scalable builds.
  • Coroutines & Flow, plus a full unit & UI test suite in every generated project.

How it works

  • Pick your targets and your feature & entity names — the wizard generates the rest.
  • Compatible with the latest IntelliJ IDEA and Android Studio (K2 Kotlin compiler).
  • Defaults mirror a real, open-source reference app.

Free & Pro: core templates for Android, iOS and Desktop are free. A Pro tier adds Claude Code agent config and GitHub Actions CI scaffolding to the generated project.

Free vs Pro

FeatureFreePro
KMP project generation (Android, Desktop, iOS)✓✓
Compose Multiplatform UI, Navigation 3, Room 3, Koin, Clean Architecture✓✓
Convention plugins, version catalog, unit & UI test suite✓✓
Claude Code agent config (CLAUDE.md, .claude/)—✓
GitHub Actions CI scaffolding (.github/)—✓

Pro is a one-time purchase. Personal and organization licenses available.

Requirements: IntelliJ IDEA or Android Studio (2026.1+). Generated projects build with Gradle and run on Android (SDK 24+), Desktop (JVM) and iOS.

Resources: the plugin is open source (MIT) — source code · issue tracker · documentation. Templates mirror the open-source kmp-ledger reference app.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changed

  • Ledger pin bumped to v1.9.1. Generated projects move to Kotlin 2.4.20, which is officially tested with the AGP 9.1.1 they pin. Other dependency upgrades: Compose Multiplatform 1.12.1, with Material3 Adaptive 1.3.0-rc01 and navigation3-ui 1.1.2 aligned to it, KSP 2.3.12 (the KSP pin is gone), Kover 0.9.11, Logback 1.6.5 (fixes CVE-2026-104721, which generated projects can't reach because they configure no MDC discriminator), SLF4J 2.0.20 / slf4j-android 2.0.20-0, and the Gradle wrapper 9.8.0.

Fixed

  • Kotlin and Java keywords are rejected as package segments and as feature or field names. Names like com.example.object or a field called val used to pass validation and produce a project that doesn't compile. The wizard now flags them as you type. The package it proposes from the project name is always valid too, so a project named "Object", "Class" or "2FA" no longer gets a broken default.
  • Android Studio: invalid feature and field names no longer produce an unbuildable project. Names are normalized (My Feature becomes my_feature). A name that can't become a valid identifier, such as 2fa, a non-Latin name or a keyword, stops generation with a notification that names the field, instead of reporting success.
  • Quotes, backslashes and $ in the test value are escaped. A value like Say "hi" used to break the generated tests, and cost $5 changed their meaning.
  • Stray spaces in the package name no longer reach generated packages and directories.
  • A failed generation no longer leaves a half-written or emptied project directory. Writing the project into its folder now either finishes or is rolled back. If it fails part-way, for example on a full disk or a file locked by antivirus, every file it wrote is removed and every file it replaced is put back. In Android Studio, the default project files are only replaced after rendering succeeds, and are restored if the write fails.
  • The post-sync apiDump runs at most once, even when two sync events arrive at the same moment.

idea-plugin.name: Quick Patch
idea-plugin.description:
Quick Patch plugin: Save your patches at one click!

Quick Patch is an IntelliJ IDEA plugin which allows you to save all the change lists you want as patches.

Idea

The major use case is you have a project with some "ancient" vcs (like svn) where branching is painful and you have some unfinished work you want to:
  • share it with someone
  • finish it later and/or at some other place (home vs office)

So in both cases you need to create a patch of what you have done so far. It's pretty easy to do that in Intellij, but we can do better. Quick Patch will save all your changes at one click or a key stroke (there is one assigned by default, but you can change it).

When you want to continue your hacking, let's say at home, you need to move your patches somehow. Dropbox to the rescue! Quick patch idea works really nice with Dropbox (and friends). You can set up plugin to save you patches into Dropbox directory and you are done! One key stroke and you ready to go, your patches are already waiting for you at home.

Settings

To configure the plugin go to Settings -> Tools -> Quick Patch

Save my patches to - select a directory where your patches should be stored. You will get a growl if you try to save patches without directory selected.
Save Default change list - Mark it if you want to save "Default" changelist. Marked by default.
Save empty change lists - Mark it if you want to save empty change lists as patch files. Unmarked by default.
Add project name as prefix - Useful when you work on multiple projects and want to distinguish your patches later.
Ignore change lists pattern - Type in a valid regex to ignore change lists you don't want to save. If the field is empty or regex isn't valid then this option will be ignored.

Usage

When the plugin is installed you get an additional action on IDEA's Changes panel. If you have at least one change list which satisfies your settings the action is enabled and you can click the icon or use associated shortcut to activate it. Voila, your patches are already in the specified folder.

idea-plugin.name: Git Extender
idea-plugin.description:
Git Extender adds an option to Update All local branches tracking a remote for all git roots in the current project
Local branches that will be updated are the branches that exist locally and have been configured to track a remote branch.

It requires IDE version 2022.2 or higher and Java 17+

It tries to fast-forward commits in remote branches to local branches. It can be configured through the settings to attempt a simple merge, if the local branch cannot be merged to the tracked remote using fast-forward only. In this case, if there are conflict errors, the merge will be aborted and an error notification will be shown. The update, then, should be performed manually for the reported branch, in order to resolve the conflicts. Any possible uncommitted changes to the current branch will be stashed
After updating a branch, if there were any file changes, they will be displayed in IntelliJ Version Control tab.
This plugin is available under Apache License, Version 2.0
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 0.8.2: Update dependencies
  • 0.8.1: Limit number of threads for updates. Closes [#55](https://github.com/JChrist/gitextender/issues/55)
  • 0.8.0: Fix no display name for configurable. Closes [#70](https://github.com/JChrist/gitextender/issues/70)
  • 0.7.0: Workaround issue with wrong thread creating the update tree, by disabling showing update tree
  • 0.6.0: Fixed plugin display in menu
  • 0.5.2: Fixed missing backgroundable task spinning notification and disabled concurrent executions
  • 0.5.1: Updated threading model for updating repositories
  • 0.5.0: Added an option for removing local branches that were tracking a remote one that was pruned
  • 0.4.1: Fix for issue #8: Create UpdateInfoTree from the event dispatch thread
  • 0.4.0: For projects with multiple modules as separate Git roots, a dialog will open up, offering the option to select which module(s) to update. Refactored persisted configuration settings.
  • 0.3.1: Removed until build version from plugin.xml, so that the plugin is compatible with latest releases
  • 0.3.0: Added configuration settings for GitExtender, offering options to control whether it will perform fast-forward-only merges, or if it will attempt simple merge and abort on error. Settings can be accessed via File->Settings->Other Settings->GitExtender Settings. Switched to java 8 support, so running it will require that the IDE runs on java 8
  • 0.2.0: Keeping track of updated files, as results to be displayed after updating. ***Requires latest version: 145*** The displayed updated files may show invalid/incorrect differences (in the show diff dialog)
  • 0.1.3: Changed pull method from rebase to merge, with the --ff-only flag (fast-forward only)
  • 0.1.2: Using GitFetcher to fetch and prune remotes and show results before starting the update
  • 0.1.1: Changed jdk to 1.7, so that the plugin works with IDEA running with 1.7 jdk Added check if any staged or unstaged changes exist in each repository, in order to stash only if needed
  • 0.1: Initial version of Git Extender, with support for updating all local branches tracking a remote of all git roots in the current project, using rebase for all local commits and automatic stashing/popping of uncommitted changes

idea-plugin.name: Git Scope
idea-plugin.description:
See all your feature branch changes at a glance—even after committing.

IntelliJ's built-in version control only shows uncommitted changes. Once you commit, all change indicators disappear. Git Scope solves this by letting you compare your current work against any Git reference—branches, tags, or commits—making it perfect for tracking feature branch progress across multiple commits.

Key Features:

  • Visual change tracking — See exactly what changed between HEAD and your target branch
  • Editor gutter indicators — Line-by-line change markers (added/modified/deleted) right in your editor
  • File tree diff browser — Browse all modified files in a dedicated tool window
  • Project file colors — Instantly spot changed files with color-coded highlighting
  • Smart scopes — Use Git Scope with IntelliJ's search, replace, and inspection features

Perfect for:

  • Reviewing all changes in a feature branch before creating a pull request
  • Tracking progress against your target branch (e.g., main, develop, release)
  • Performing code inspections or refactoring only on files you've changed
  • Understanding what's different between your work and any historical reference
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.2.4

Added

  • Added Copy Path/Reference to the file context menu in the Git Scope window, like the Project view

2026.2.3

Fixes

  • Fixed selected file text being hard to read when the Git Scope window is unfocused
    • The selection now turns to the theme's inactive colour when the focus leaves the tool window, like the Project view.

2026.2.2

Added

  • Added toggle buttons for untracked/deleted files in the Git Scope window, complementing the global setting with a per-project one

Fixes

  • Fixed Files that are not viewable by IntelliJ do not open at all
    • Opens such files in the associated application on double-click, like the Project view; explains why that's not possible over Remote Development instead of staying silent.
  • Fixed the scope still listing files that Git reports as unchanged, which the 2026.2.1 fix was meant to clear
    • The rescan that fix depends on ran before the IDE could accept it and was silently dropped; it now runs once VCS initialization finishes.
  • Fixed target branch selection silently falling back to HEAD after moving the project or repo
  • Fixed a blank tab showing on next launch after closing the IDE with an unconfigured "New*" tab active
  • Fixed scope warm-up for already-open files not running over Remote Development

Changed

  • Bumped versions of plugins and build tooling (IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin, Gradle, GitHub Actions)

2026.2.1

Fixes

  • Fixed "Only Changes Since Common Ancestor" collected every commit in the range instead of the pull-request diff
    • The scope is now git diff <selection>...HEAD: files reverted within the range disappear, and each file's diff, gutter markers and rollback use the merge base rather than a single intermediate commit.
  • Fixed Files are red even after resolving conflicts
  • Fixed missing gutter markers over slow or unstable Remote Development connections
  • Fixed the scope tab context menu (rename, reset, move left/right) missing in Remote Development, and the tooltip showing the original name of a renamed tab
  • Fixed reordering scope tabs by dragging them, which mixed up the tabs and lost one on the next IDE start
  • Fixed the step-between-changes actions jumping erratically: they now follow the order the scope tree shows, skip deleted, binary and directory entries, and keep the focus in the Git Scope window
  • Fixed the scope listing files that Git reports as unchanged, which survived IDE restarts and only cleared once an unrelated commit happened to force a refresh
    • The IDE restores its changelist on startup and afterwards only re-checks files it has marked as changed, so an entry whose file no longer exists was never looked at again. Git Scope now forces one full rescan once Git is ready, and ignores entries whose file is gone.

2026.2

Remote Development support, built on a split of the plugin into separate frontend and backend modules. Local IDE behavior, scope tabs and settings are unchanged. Given the size of the refactoring, please report any regression with your IDE version and whether you run locally or over Remote Development.

Added

  • Added support for remote development
    • Git access, scope resolution and change collection run on the host; the client handles gutter markers, the diff popup and change navigation.
    • Only the computed line ranges cross the network, so gutter markers stay responsive, and the client re-syncs automatically after a dropped connection.
  • Added actions/shortcuts to step between files and scope

Fixes

  • Fixed Right-click -> Show in Project doesn't switch to Project window
  • Fixed Right-click -> Show in Project for folder selects the first changed file rather than the folder

idea-plugin.name: Git Emoji Commit
idea-plugin.description:
Submit message template normalization plugin

1. The purpose of code submission standardization

  • In order to standardize the format of the code information submitted by the department
  • For better traceability code, screening
  • In order to more quickly locate the scope and implementation functions involved in submitting code
  • Automatically generate ChangeLog for subsequent code review

2. IDEA plug-in integration and use

Plugin use

Click the small airplane icon in the submission pop-up window to evoke the submission information to fill in the pop-up window, fill in the corresponding information and submit to generate the submission information

Custom submission template and type

This plugin supports modifying your own submission template, but several inherent variables @Type, @Scope, @ShortDescription, @LongDescription cannot be changed, and the input @ will automatically complete the prompt.

Generate ChangeLog

This plugin supports the function of generating ChangeLog according to the submission information. You can directly right-click on the branch and select Generate ChangeLog or directly use the shortcut key Alt+K to invoke the Generate ChangeLog pop-up window.

Enter the Tag you want to generate and the submission type in the pop-up window, and the ChangeLog will be automatically generated according to the selected submission type.

3. Feedback

idea-plugin.name: Context Buddy
idea-plugin.description:
The tool, that allows you to inspect project history in more details.

Context buddy analyze history based on tokens: method names, parameters, vars or words depending on language/format used rather then lines as git does.

It means that it assigns multiple commits to single line, ignores whitespace changes (if has no semantic meaning) or tracks renames properly.

Please check our website and plugin documentation.

If you are interested what is going under the hood please we've wrote a blogpost about that.

idea-plugin.name: Conventional Commit
idea-plugin.description:
The aim of this plugin is to provide completion for conventional commits, also named semantic commits, inside the VCS Commit dialog.


The plugin provides:

  • Standard completion - based on context
  • Template completion - initiated intentionally

It also offers a certain level of customization, which means allowing personalized and sharable default tokens, and attaching additional Providers for the various parts of the commit message: type, scope, subject, body, footer type and footer value.


Read the full description at GitHub.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.27.0 (03/08/2026)

This release contains the following enhancements and fixes:

  • Reimplemented commit message parsing, improving syntax handling and support for incomplete messages, bodies, footers, multiline footer values, and recent VCS commit tokens (closes #124 and #128).
  • Fixed an OOM issue when parsing a commit type that starts with ! (closes #161).
  • Improved template completion: move freely between segments without losing entered values and clean up empty footer fields when finishing a template.
  • Restored spellchecking for commit messages, which had stopped working after the migration to the Grazie-based platform implementation.
  • Added a confirmation before clearing the local commit message history (closes #147).
  • Moved Conventional Commit settings under Tools.
  • Used the IDE locale by default, while allowing an override through the com.github.lppedd.cc.locale registry option (closes #126).
  • Added the Fixes and Assisted-by built-in footer types (closes #164).
  • Improved custom token file handling: exported files now include the appropriate versioned schema reference.
  • Used the IDE file chooser consistently when selecting token-related files.
  • Loaded tokens in the plugin's Settings page on the appropriate background thread (closes #162).
  • Prevented errors when accessing VCS log providers (closes #150).
  • Expanded compatibility verification to IDEA 2026.1 and 2026.2.
  • And a lot of other stuff that I'm too lazy to list.

See the complete list of changes at 0.26.0...0.27.0.

idea-plugin.name: Git Commit Message Helper
idea-plugin.description:
Git Commit Message Helper helps you write cleaner, more consistent commit messages without leaving the IDE.

Git Commit Message Helper 帮助你在 IDE 内更高效地编写清晰、统一、规范的提交信息。

It combines a structured commit editor, customizable Conventional Commit style templates, and provider-aware LLM assistance in one IntelliJ plugin. You can create commit messages manually, generate them from selected changes, reformat existing drafts, and tune the final output to match your team's workflow.

它将结构化提交编辑器、可自定义的 Conventional Commit 风格模板，以及支持多 Provider 的 LLM 辅助能力整合到同一个 IntelliJ 插件中。你既可以手动编写提交信息，也可以根据所选变更生成草稿、重写已有内容，并按团队规范输出最终结果。

What It Does

  • Adds commit message actions directly to the IntelliJ VCS commit panel.
  • Helps compose commit messages with structured fields such as type, scope, subject, body, breaking change, closes, and skip ci.
  • Supports customizable commit templates powered by Apache Velocity.
  • Lets you manage allowed commit types and their descriptions.
  • Generates commit messages from the selected git changes with an LLM.
  • Rewrites existing commit messages to match the configured template.
  • Parses an existing message back into structured fields with Smart Echo.
  • Supports skip-CI presets, configurable field visibility, and action visibility.
  • Includes localized resources for English, Chinese, Japanese, and Korean.
  • 在 IntelliJ 的 VCS 提交面板中直接提供提交信息辅助动作。
  • 通过结构化字段组织提交信息，包括 type、scope、subject、body、breaking change、closes 和 skip ci。
  • 支持基于 Apache Velocity 的自定义提交模板。
  • 支持维护可用的提交类型及其描述。
  • 支持基于当前选中 Git 变更通过 LLM 生成提交信息。
  • 支持将已有提交信息按当前模板重新格式化。
  • 支持通过 Smart Echo 将现有提交信息回填为结构化字段。
  • 支持 Skip CI 预设、字段显隐以及动作可见性配置。
  • 内置英文、中文、日文、韩文本地化资源。

Main Actions

  • Generate Commit Message: create a draft from the currently selected git changes.
  • Format Commit Message: rewrite the current commit message using your configured template.
  • Create Commit Message: open the structured editor for manual commit composition.
  • Generate Commit Message：根据当前选中的 Git 变更生成提交信息草稿。
  • Format Commit Message：按照你配置的模板重写当前提交信息。
  • Create Commit Message：打开结构化编辑器，手动编写提交信息。

Each action can be shown or hidden independently, so teams can expose only the workflow they actually use.

这 3 个动作都可以单独控制是否显示，方便团队只保留实际使用的工作流入口。

Structured Commit Editing

The manual editor is designed for teams that want strict control over commit structure. Instead of editing a single plain text box, you can fill dedicated fields for the header, body, breaking changes, issue links, and optional skip-CI markers.

结构化编辑器适合对提交格式要求较高的团队使用。你不需要只面对一个纯文本输入框，而是可以分别填写标题、正文、 BREAKING CHANGE、关联 issue 以及可选的 Skip CI 标记等字段。

This makes commit messages easier to review, easier to standardize, and easier to adapt when your team uses a formal commit convention.

这种方式让提交信息更易审阅、更易统一，也更适合需要遵循正式提交规范的团队。

Default Commit Style

The plugin is ready to use out of the box with a Conventional Commit style template such as:

插件开箱即用，默认提供类似 Conventional Commits 的提交模板，例如：

type(scope): subject

body

BREAKING CHANGE: changes

Closes issue

[skip ci]

The built-in default types include feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, and revert.

插件默认内置的提交类型包括 feat、fix、docs、style、refactor、perf、test、build、ci、chore 和 revert。

The template text, visible fields, type list, display style, and skip-CI behavior are all configurable.

模板内容、字段显示、类型列表、展示方式以及 Skip CI 行为都可以按团队需要调整。

LLM Workflow

The plugin can use an LLM to generate commit messages from the selected changes, reformat an existing draft, or parse a free-form message back into structured fields. This reduces manual editing while still keeping the final result under your control.

插件可以通过 LLM 根据选中变更生成提交信息、重写已有草稿，或将自由文本提交信息重新解析为结构化字段。这样既能减少手工编辑， 也能保证最终结果仍然受你控制。

Smart Echo

When Smart Echo is enabled and the commit panel already contains text, the manual editor can ask the LLM to map that text back into fields like type, scope, subject, body, changes, closes, and skipCi.

当开启 Smart Echo 且提交面板中已经存在文本时，手动编辑器可以调用 LLM，把当前内容回填为 type、scope、subject、body、 changes、closes 和 skipCi 等结构化字段。

Provider Compatibility

The plugin currently supports two provider modes: OpenAI Compatible and Anthropic. This lets teams connect either official endpoints or compatible internal gateways, depending on their environment.

插件当前支持两种 Provider 模式：OpenAI Compatible 和 Anthropic。这让团队可以根据 实际环境接入官方接口或兼容的内部网关。

Configuration

Open File | Settings | GitCommitMessageHelper to configure the plugin. The settings are split into focused pages so you can tune both the authoring workflow and the LLM integration.

打开 File | Settings | GitCommitMessageHelper 即可配置插件。设置项按照不同功能拆分，便于分别调整提交编写流程和 LLM 集成能力。

General Settings

Choose how commit types are displayed, how many appear inline, which fields are hidden, whether skip-CI options are enabled, and which actions should be visible in the commit panel.

你可以设置提交类型的展示方式、内联显示数量、隐藏哪些字段、是否启用 Skip CI 选项，以及在提交面板中显示哪些动作。

Commit Template

Customize the final commit message with an Apache Velocity template so the generated output matches your team's exact format.

你可以通过 Apache Velocity 模板自定义最终提交信息的渲染格式，让输出结果严格符合团队规范。

Commit Types

Edit the allowed commit types and their descriptions to align with your workflow, terminology, and review conventions.

你可以自由维护允许使用的提交类型及其描述，使之与团队术语、工作流和评审习惯保持一致。

LLM Settings

Configure the provider, base URL, API key, model, temperature, response language, and Smart Echo behavior.

你可以配置 Provider、Base URL、API Key、模型、Temperature、返回语言以及 Smart Echo 行为。

For OpenAI-compatible services, the plugin can work with either a full /chat/completions endpoint or a base API URL. For Anthropic, it uses the native Messages API.

对于 OpenAI Compatible 服务，插件既支持直接填写完整的 /chat/completions 接口，也支持填写基础 API 地址。 对于 Anthropic，则会使用其原生 Messages API。

Project Background

This project started as an enhanced version of git-commit-template and has grown into a more configurable commit authoring assistant for IntelliJ-based IDEs.

这个项目最初基于 git-commit-template 增强而来，当前已经演进为一个面向 IntelliJ 平台、可配置能力更完整的提交信息辅助插件。

idea-plugin.name: Bitbucket Integration Pro
idea-plugin.description:
Bitbucket plugin for IntelliJ IDEA and other JetBrains IDEs (WebStorm, PyCharm, Rider, PhpStorm, Android Studio, GoLand, RubyMine, CLion, DataGrip, DataSpell, AppCode).

Bitbucket Integration Pro brings Atlassian Bitbucket Pull Request review directly into JetBrains IDEs. Review diffs, leave comments, create tasks, approve, and merge pull requests without leaving your IDE.

Supports Bitbucket Cloud and Bitbucket Data Center (6.x or later).

Key features

  • Review pull requests, leave comments, and create tasks
  • Navigate discussions directly in the diff view
  • Create new pull requests
  • Approve, decline, and merge pull requests; check out PR branches
  • Perform iterative reviews (Cloud and Data Center)
  • Integrate with AI agents via a built-in MCP (Model Context Protocol) server
  • Ask an AI agent to review a pull request with the "AI Review" action
  • Browse PR comments in a standard editor when the branch is checked out
  • Open pull requests from commits in the Git Log
  • Receive notifications (Bitbucket Cloud only)

Security

The plugin acts as a direct Bitbucket client and does not send any data to servers other than Bitbucket. Passwords and access tokens are stored locally using the IDE’s built-in password storage (configurable in IDE Settings).

idea-plugin.name: Tortoise Git Caller
idea-plugin.description:
Github | Plugin

Introduction

This plugin provides for IDEA launching TortoiseGit dialogs.

You can use it by

  • menu -> VCS -> Tortoise Git Operations Popup
  • Project view-> put mouse on a file -> right-click menu -> click 'Tortoise Git File Operations'
  • keyboard shortcuts

Before use this plugin, first you must install the TortoiseGit by you self and make sure the command "TortoiseGitProc" in Windows CMD is usable. This plugin just support to windows user. Because TortoiseGit only support Windows version.

Default shortcuts

Global shortcuts:

  • (G)it (C)ommit - Ctrl+G, C
  • (G)it (F)etch - Ctrl+G, F
  • (G)it (L)og - Ctrl+G, L
  • (G)it (M)erge - Ctrl+G, M
  • (G)it (P)ull - Ctrl+G, P
  • (G)it P(u)sh - Ctrl+G, U
  • (G)it (R)ebase - Ctrl+G, R
  • (G)it Re(v)ert - Ctrl+G, V
  • (G)it Stash-P(o)p - Ctrl+G, O
  • (G)it Stash-S(a)ve - Ctrl+G, A
  • (G)it (S)witch - Ctrl+G, S
  • (G)it Clea(n)up - Ctrl+G, N
  • (G)it Repository (D)iff - Ctrl+G, D
  • (G)it R(e)solve - Ctrl+G, E

Current file shortcuts:

  • (G)it File (L)og - Ctrl+Shift+G, L
  • (G)it File R(e)solve - Ctrl+Shift+G, E
  • (G)it File Re(v)ert - Ctrl+Shift+G, V
  • (G)it File (B)lame - Ctrl+Shift+G, B
  • (G)it File (D)iff - Ctrl+Shift+G, D

If you want to customize shortcuts, you can via File -> Settings -> keymap.

Shortcut conflicts

Since the default shortcuts will make Ctrl+G (Go To Line) inaccessible, you can change them, or just change the one for "Go To Line" to be Ctrl+G, G

BatchGit


BatchGit provides batch Git version management for multiple sub-projects.

Features

  • Multi-project branch batch switch


Usage

  • Batch clone of sub-projects

    1. To configure, open Settings/Preferences -> Tools -> BatchGit, Enter sub-projects repositories address information.

    2. To batch clone sub-projects, open Tools -> Batch Clone, after selecting the sub-projects, click the ok button to clone.

  • Multi-project branch batch switch

idea-plugin.name: CodeSync
idea-plugin.description:
AI-Powered Coding Summaries: Stay Synced Without the Overhead

CodeSync's AI-generated summaries offer a fast and efficient way to stay on top of your team's development progress. Whether you're a developer reviewing pull requests or a manager needing daily updates, CodeSync delivers clear, human-readable coding overviews directly from your IDE. No more manual tracking or sifting through code reviews—our summaries keep your entire team aligned, without the distractions. Integrate seamlessly with GitHub and Slack to streamline your workflow. Available now for JetBrains and VS Code!.

Key Features

  • AI-Generated Pull Request Summaries: Get concise, actionable overviews of pull requests, making code reviews quicker and easier. Reduce time spent digging into details by seeing the bigger picture immediately.
  • Daily Team Summaries in Slack: Keep everyone aligned with non-intrusive daily summaries posted in team channels. Perfect for quick stand-ups or catching up after a busy day.
  • Seamless GitHub Integration: Automatically generate summaries for every commit and pull request, so you never miss key changes or updates in your codebase.
  • Developer-Friendly: Stay in your flow—access pull request summaries and progress updates directly in your IDE without switching tools or reviewing long code histories.
  • Manager and Executive Reporting: Get high-level overviews of team progress. Track deliverables, spot blockers, and review progress toward business outcomes with biweekly and quarterly reports.

Benefits for Each Persona

  • Developers: Quick insights at your fingertips, without leaving your IDE. Focus on coding, not status updates. Let CodeSync handle the summaries, so you can spend less time managing pull requests and more time building great software.
  • Managers: AI-powered summaries save you from manually following up with the team. Get clear, actionable reports on team progress without diving into the code. Stay aligned with project timelines, identify blockers early, and keep communication efficient.
  • Executives: Turn raw data into valuable business insights effortlessly. Understand development progress at a glance. Quarterly reports tie technical achievements directly to business outcomes, giving you a clear picture of ROI and team efficiency.

Data Security

We support both cloud and self-hosting via AWS (on-prem). If you’d like your data and infrastructure to be within your own AWS account, contact us for a free trial of the on-prem option.

CodeSync is SOC-2 compliant and ensures the highest standards of security, privacy and encryption. Contact us for our SOC-2 report.

idea-plugin.description:
Welcome to Doraemon's Pocket :) The entrance of this plugin is at the last of MainToolBar icons or pressing keyboard-shortcut, COMMAND+SHIFT+J (CONTROL+SHIFT+J for Windows).



### Here are some daily DevTools, such as:

  • fetch debug-version app's database and open
  • create GitLab Merge Request






### Guide for Fetch & Open Database:
  1. only support debug version Android APPs
  2. input Android SDK location, as some as Android Studio's "SDK Location" setting in "Project Structure Settings"
  3. input Storage Location where the database will be saved in
  4. press OK button to fetch the databases


## Guide for create GitLab Merge Request:
  1. make sure current project is version-controlled by gitlab
  2. open the plugin and it'll auto get the project ID in GitLab by GitLab APIs
  3. config merge request parameters, and they are initialized from current git status
  4. press OK button to create merge request and it will open the merge request website automatically


Others are coming soon. If you have some great idea, please contact me





功能入口图标在主功能条的最后，也可以通过快捷键 COMMAND+SHIFT+J (Windows 系统: CONTROL+SHIFT+J) 进入

将日常开发中一些重复性、微耗时的事情整理为工具，放入此插件——哆啦A梦的口袋中。功能列表:

  • 拉取并打开 Android 测试应用的数据库
  • 创建 GitLab Merge Request




### 拉取并打开 Android 测试应用数据库使用说明:
  1. 只支持拉取 Android 应用 debug 包的数据库
  2. 需要输入 Android SDK 位置，和 Android Studio 中 "SDK Location" 配置相同即可
  3. 需要输入要存储拉取出数据库文件的本地位置
  4. 点击确认按钮，就会将数据库拉取出来，并根据设置是否自动打开


### 创建 GitLab Merge Request 使用说明:
  1. 确保打开的工程是 GitLab 版本控制的工程
  2. 在打开插件时，会自动通过 GitLab API 来获取工程 ID
  3. 插件会自动通过 Git 当前状态初始化参数，也可以自行修改
  4. 点击 OK 按钮后会创建 Merge Request，并自动打开对应网页

idea-plugin.name: TortoiseGit Actions
idea-plugin.description:
Launch common TortoiseGit dialogs using intuitive shortcuts

Repo-scoped shortcuts:

  • Git Commit - Ctrl+G, Ctrl+C
  • Git Fetch - Ctrl+G, Ctrl+F
  • Git Log - Ctrl+G, Ctrl+L
  • Git Merge - Ctrl+G, Ctrl+M
  • Git Pull - Ctrl+G, Ctrl+P
  • Git Push - Ctrl+G, Ctrl+U
  • Git Rebase - Ctrl+G, Ctrl+R
  • Git Revert - Ctrl+G, Ctrl+V
  • Git Stash-List - Ctrl+G, Ctrl+I
  • Git Stash-Pop - Ctrl+G, Ctrl+O
  • Git Stash-Save - Ctrl+G, Ctrl+A
  • Git Switch - Ctrl+G, Ctrl+S
  • Git Sync - Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Y
  • Git Cleanup - Ctrl+G, Ctrl+N
  • Git Repository Diff - Ctrl+G, Ctrl+D

Current file-scoped shortcuts:

  • Git Resolve - Ctrl+G, Ctrl+E
  • Git File Log - Ctrl+Shift+Alt+G, Ctrl+Shift+Alt+L
  • Git File Blame - Ctrl+Shift+Alt+G, Ctrl+Shift+Alt+B
  • Git File Diff - Ctrl+Shift+Alt+G, Ctrl+Shift+Alt+D

Shortcut Conflicts

Since the default shortcuts will make Ctrl+G (Go To Line) inaccessible, you can change them, or just change the one for "Go To Line" to be e.g. Ctrl+G, Ctrl+G.

More Actions

Bisect commands are also available, but with no preset shortcuts. You can reach them from the TortoiseGit menu, or search for TGit in the Shift Shift palette.

Optional Configuration

If you've installed TortoiseGit in a custom location, you can specify the path to TortoiseGitProc.exe under Settings/Preferences > Tools > TortoiseGit Actions.

idea-plugin.name: JetLab — Integration for GitLab
idea-plugin.description:
GitLab plugin for IntelliJ IDEA and other JetBrains IDEs (WebStorm, PyCharm, Rider, PhpStorm, Android Studio, GoLand, RubyMine, CLion, DataGrip, DataSpell, AppCode).

JetLab brings GitLab Merge Request review and GitLab Issues directly into JetBrains IDEs. Review diffs, participate in discussions, approve merge requests, and navigate between issues and MRs without leaving your IDE.

Supports GitLab SaaS (gitlab.com) and GitLab Self-Managed (12.x or later).

GITLAB is a trademark of GitLab Inc. in the United States and other countries and regions. This plugin is not affiliated, endorsed, sponsored, or approved with or by GitLab Inc.

Key features

  • Review merge requests and leave inline comments
  • Navigate discussions directly in the diff view
  • Create new merge requests
  • Approve, merge, and close merge requests; check out MR branches
  • Perform iterative reviews (see only what changed since your last review)
  • Integrate with AI agents via a built-in MCP (Model Context Protocol) server
  • Ask an AI agent to review a merge request with the "AI Review" action
  • Browse MR comments in a standard editor when the branch is checked out
  • Create and browse issues
  • Navigate between issues and merge requests
  • Open merge requests from commits in the Git Log

Security

JetLab acts as a direct GitLab client and does not send any data to servers other than GitLab. Passwords and access tokens are stored locally using the IDE’s built-in password storage (configurable in IDE Settings).

idea-plugin.name: Commit Checker
idea-plugin.description:
Checks files selected for commit for the specified files/keywords. If found it will ask for a confirmation upon commit, warning of a found file/keyword.

With keywords: it will only alarm for newly added words, not the ones that existed also before the commit.

To specify files/keywords, just create a file (anywhere inside of the Project) called `commit_checker.yml` and in there specify files and keywords in the following format:

keywords:
  - foo
  - bar
  ...
files:
  - foo.html
  - bar.component.ts
  - /.*\.html/
  ...
There is support for regexes, which have to be enclosed by `/` (e.g. to match FOO-1234 you can use /FOO-\d{4}/)

Alternatively, you can create a `commit_checker.txt` and in there specify words to look out for separated by comma (line breaks don't matter):
foo, bar, foo.java, bar.js, /.*\.html/

There is also a checkbox in Commit window that allows you to enable/disable commit checker.
