idea-plugin.name: TYPO3 Commit Template
idea-plugin.description:
Inspired by the commit guidelines of TYPO3 here.

Usage

Open your Commit-Dialog by clicking the module or pressing Control/CMD + K.
You can open the template dialog by pressing Control + Shift + K.


Once you are in the dialog, you can navigate by using the Tab Key.
Fill the form as you see fit.


If you are happy with your commit message, press Apply and the message will be templated and inserted into your commit message dialog.


Please note, that the template is dynamic. So filling breaking changes will result in the [!!!] flag being set.
This also works with the to-do list which results in the [WIP] flag being set.
If you do not want any flags, just fill the Done Tasks Section, so only the Type will be displayed.
As you can see in the Image above, by clicking the branch icon next to the resolves and related issue number list, the current issue number in the currently checked out branch will be inserted. For Example a branch named like this "feature/12345-a-new-feature" will result in an issue number "12345" being inserted into the relative inputfield. But when applied, will have the format #12345.
If you use your keyboard to traverse the dialog window, you will automatically get a new list item (* ) for each focus into an empty textarea or by pressing the return key, while you are focussed. If you leave a text area that only contains an empty list item (* ) it will be deleted.
If the Task-list becomes too long horizontal, the text will wrap. If it becomes to long vertically, you can scroll up and down inside the textarea.
For every Element in the Dialog, a placeholder shows you the suggested format and while hovering, you get a nice descriptive tool tip.
The Commit message gets parsed, after you hit Apply which leads to any list item starting with "- " to become "* " and the issue numbers will all be listed in separate lines and starting with an #. For more Information on why that is, please read the Guideline Documentation of TYPO3.


If you want to fix a typo or add items, simply click the TYPO3 Icon or hit the Shortcut again. Your Commit Message will be reopend and can be edited.



AI-Powered Commit Message Generation

This plugin now supports AI-powered commit message generation using a local LLM via Ollama!

Setup

  1. Install Ollama on your local machine
  2. Pull a model: ollama pull llama3.2
  3. Configure the plugin settings:
    • Go to Settings/Preferences > Tools > TYPO3 Commit Template
    • Set your Ollama URL (default: http://localhost:11434)
    • Set your preferred model (default: llama3.2)
    • Customize the prompts for subject and body generation

Usage

Quick Generation:

  • Click the "Generate with AI" button in the commit dialog (next to the template button)
  • Instant generation based on your settings

Template Dialog:

  1. Open the commit template dialog (Control + Shift + M)
  2. Click the "Generate with AI" button at the bottom
  3. The AI will analyze your git changes and populate the enabled fields
  4. Review and edit the generated content before applying

Features:

  • Strict prompts ensure clean, raw text output
  • Automatic cleaning of LLM artifacts (greetings, explanations, formatting)
  • Respects your enabled/disabled field settings
  • Background processing with progress indicators

For more details, see LLM_INTEGRATION.md.

Installation

  • Using IDE built-in plugin system:

    Settings/Preferences > Plugins > Marketplace > Search for "plugin-phpstorm-typo3-commit-template" > Install Plugin

  • Manually:

    Download the latest release and install it manually using Settings/Preferences > Plugins > ⚙️ > Install plugin from disk...

idea-plugin.name: Git Commit Message Format
idea-plugin.description:
Create a commit message with the following template.

  • Click birdie or press Alt + Q open formatter dialog
  • Click outside or press Alt + Enter to be completed

Commit Message Format

Each commit message consists of a header, a body and a footer. The header has a special format that includes a type, a scope and a subject:

<type>(<scope>): <subject>
<BLANK LINE>
<body>
<BLANK LINE>
<footer>

The header is mandatory and the scope of the header is optional.

Any line of the commit message cannot be longer than 100 characters! This allows the message to be easier to read on GitHub as well as in various git tools.

Revert

If the commit reverts a previous commit, it should begin with revert: , followed by the header of the reverted commit. In the body it should say: This reverts commit <hash>., where the hash is the SHA of the commit being reverted.

Type

Must be one of the following:

  • feat: A new feature
  • fix: A bug fix
  • docs: Documentation only changes
  • style: Changes that do not affect the meaning of the code (white-space, formatting, missing semi-colons, etc)
  • refactor: A code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature
  • perf: A code change that improves performance
  • test: Adding missing or correcting existing tests
  • chore: Changes to the build process or auxiliary tools and libraries such as documentation generation

Scope

The scope could be anything specifying place of the commit change. For example $location, $browser, $compile, $rootScope, ngHref, ngClick, ngView, etc...

You can use * when the change affects more than a single scope.

Subject

The subject contains succinct description of the change:

  • use the imperative, present tense: "change" not "changed" nor "changes"
  • don't capitalize first letter
  • no dot (.) at the end

Body

Just as in the subject, use the imperative, present tense: "change" not "changed" nor "changes". The body should include the motivation for the change and contrast this with previous behavior.

Footer

The footer should contain any information about Breaking Changes and is also the place to reference GitHub issues that this commit closes.

Breaking Changes should start with the word BREAKING CHANGE: with a space or two newlines. The rest of the commit message is then used for this.

A detailed explanation can be found in this document.

idea-plugin.name: AICommit
idea-plugin.description:
AI-generated commit messages for JetBrains IDEs. Reads your staged diff and writes a clear commit message in one click — from the commit dialog or the AI Commit tool window.

Bring your own provider, or run fully offline

  • OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Azure OpenAI, DeepSeek
  • Ollama — one-click local setup, so your code never leaves your machine
  • OpenAI-compatible endpoints — save multiple profiles and switch between them from the tool window

Built for real repositories

  • Parallel processing for changesets with many files
  • DeepSeek Thinking Mode with live reasoning progress — reasoning content is never inserted into your commit, stored in history, or sent in telemetry
  • Per-project message history, persisted across sessions
  • Custom prompts and adjustable generation parameters
  • Interface in English, 简体中文, 日本語, 한국어

Privacy

No code and no commit messages are collected. Telemetry is opt-out with a full disclosure in Settings → About. With Ollama, nothing leaves your machine at all.

Actively maintained

Published by a JetBrains Marketplace verified vendor, with regular releases — see the changelog for what shipped most recently.

  • Improved generation cleanup when cancelling or closing a project, and corrected terminal-result statistics so credential checks cannot consume an active generation's result.
  • Kept local UI-driver OpenAI credentials off command-line arguments and removed the environment-variable fallback.

idea-plugin.name: GitBashOpenHere
idea-plugin.description:
Built for developers who feel more at home in a real terminal than in another IDE Git dialog.

One right-click. The correct repository. The terminal and command you actually want.
GitBashOpenHere connects your project, the nearest Git root, and your favorite terminal without making you hunt for paths or type another long cd command.

What it can do:
• Open the current project, directory, or file location in Git Bash, macOS Terminal, or a new Warp tab.
• Run git status, git diff, git log, or git push from the nearest Git root while keeping the selected file context.
• Open the exact directory in Windows CMD or PowerShell when you do not want to jump to the Git root.
• Copy a file name, its file path, or the name without the extension.
• Reveal files from the Commit changes list or Repository Diff in macOS Finder or Windows File Explorer. This menu action is enabled by default.

• Optionally show the name of the current Git root directory in the main toolbar; this display is off by default.

• Work across Windows and macOS, with a custom git-bash.exe path when auto-detection is not enough.
• Keep the menu clean by hiding actions you do not use in Settings → Other Settings.

Built for AI-assisted coding:
Select code and the floating GBOH badge appears.
One click copies the file name and exact line range, ready to paste into Cursor, Codex, or your next AI conversation.
Less context switching, less explaining, more building. You can enable or disable the badge in Settings.

How to use it:
Right-click a project, directory, file, editor, or editor tab, then open Git Here: and choose your action.
That is it. The plugin figures out the useful path and gets out of your way.

Windows tip: If git-bash.exe is not detected automatically, set its path in Settings.

Your terminal workflow, now wired straight into the IDE.


--- 中文说明 ---

写给那些真正把终端当主场的开发者：IDE 里的 Git 面板可以用，但命令行才是自己人。

一次右键，自动找对仓库、打开对的终端、执行对的命令。
GitBashOpenHere 直接把项目、最近的 Git 根目录和你顺手的终端接到一起。不用翻路径，不用反复 cd，也不用在几个窗口之间来回横跳。

现在能干什么：
• 在项目、目录、文件、编辑器或标签页上右键，直接打开 Git Bash、macOS Terminal 或 Warp 新标签。
• 自动定位最近的 Git 根目录，带着当前文件上下文执行 git status、git diff、git log 和 git push。
• Windows 下可以绕过 Git 根目录，直接在当前文件所在目录打开 CMD 或 PowerShell。
• 一键复制文件名、文件路径或不带扩展名的文件名。
• 在 Commit 变更列表或 Repository Diff 中右键，将文件定位到 macOS Finder 或 Windows 文件资源管理器；该菜单默认开启。
• 可选择在主工具栏显示当前 Git 根目录名；此显示默认关闭。
• 支持 Windows/macOS；Windows 下找不到 git-bash.exe 也不慌，手动指定一下就行。
• 菜单也不用将就，可以在 Settings → Other Settings 里隐藏你用不上的功能。

AI 编程这块，也给你接上了：
选中代码，稍等一下就会出现 GBOH 浮动入口。
点一下就能复制文件名和精确行号范围，直接丢给 Cursor、Codex 或其他 AI 对话。
少切窗口，少解释上下文，把时间留给真正的开发。这个浮动入口也可以随时在设置里开关。

怎么用：
在项目、目录、文件、编辑器或编辑器标签页上右键，找到 Git Here:，然后选你要做的事。
就这么简单：你负责写代码，它负责把路找对。

Windows 提示：如果没有自动识别到 git-bash.exe，去设置里指定路径即可。

你的终端工作流，现在直接长在 IDE 里了。

idea-plugin.name: GitStats
idea-plugin.description:
Git activity statistics for JetBrains IDEs.

GitStats turns the Git history of your current project into a clear author-level activity report inside the IDE. Review contribution trends, compare code changes across teammates, and share the visible results without leaving your development workflow.

  • Author-level summaries: compare commits, added lines, deleted lines, and modified files.
  • Flexible date ranges: inspect this week, the last 7 days, this month, or a custom range.
  • Focused filtering: narrow reports by date range, branch scope, author, and project-relative paths.
  • Two calculation modes: use Fast Summary for quick line-based ranking, or Detailed mode when commit counts matter.
  • Noise control: exclude generated folders, vendor code, build outputs, or any project-relative paths.
  • Shareable results: copy selected rows, copy the full table, or export the visible statistics as CSV.

Getting Started

  1. Open a project backed by a Git repository in any supported JetBrains IDE.
  2. Open the Git Stats tool window.
  3. Choose a date range, branch scope, author, or paths to focus the report.
  4. Click Refresh to calculate the report.
  5. Use the settings action to switch modes or exclude noisy paths such as generated files and build outputs.

Privacy-friendly by design: GitStats uses the Git executable configured in your IDE and reads only local repository history. No source code, commit data, or statistics are sent to external services.

idea-plugin.name: ControlPlane
idea-plugin.description:
ControlPlane is a plugin for IntelliJ IDEA that streamlines your workflow by allowing you to checkout GitLab projects directly from a custom toolbox. The plugin interacts with the GitLab API to display a list of all available projects in your GitLab instance. With its integrated search functionality, you can easily find and select a project for checkout.

Please be aware that during the checkout process, specific directories in opened project will be automatically replaced without any prompts or confirmation messages. This behavior is designed for efficient file handling within the system. This means any uncommitted changes in these directories may be lost. Before performing a checkout, ensure that all important modifications have been properly saved, committed, or backed up elsewhere. Remember to always commit or stash your changes to prevent any loss of work.

Features

  • Direct access to your GitLab projects within IntelliJ IDEA.
  • Checkout functionality that allows you to clone GitLab projects directly from the custom toolbox.
  • Search functionality to find specific projects quickly.
  • Configurable GitLab API base URL and GitLab token.

idea-plugin.name: Gist Do It
idea-plugin.description:
View and edit your GitHub gists from inside the IDE.

Browsing

  • Gists are grouped by category. Trailing words starting with # in a gist description, like 'Gist description #category1 #category2', are treated as categories.
  • Click a gist file to open it with syntax coloring based on its extension. Files of a gist already open are reused instead of opening another tab.
  • Double-click a gist to open all its files. All files of a gist open in a single editor group, a new one to the right if none of its files are open yet.
  • Load the public gists of any GitHub user.

Speed search

  • Press Cmd+F (Ctrl+F) or just start typing in the tree. Matches are highlighted and collapsed nodes are expanded.
  • Use Up and Down arrow keys for the previous and next match, Escape to close the search. A hint is shown below the tree while searching.

Editing your own gists

  • Files of your own gists open editable. Gists of other users open read-only.
  • Edited files show * in the tab and a banner with Save to Gist, Show Diff and Revert.
  • Changes are saved to GitHub only with Save to Gist, from the banner or the editor and editor tab context menus. A notification confirms the save, with a link to open the gist on GitHub.
  • If the file was changed on GitHub since you opened it, you are warned and can show a diff before deciding to overwrite.
  • Closing a tab with unsaved changes keeps them and offers to save, reopen or discard.

GitHub account

Uses the GitHub account you have already configured in the IDE under Settings | Version Control | GitHub. If no account is configured, the IDE's own GitHub login dialog (browser sign-in or personal access token) is shown, and the token is stored securely in the IDE password safe. If the bundled GitHub plugin is disabled, the plugin falls back to asking for a personal access token for the current session.

Installation 🔧

  1. Navigate to the JetBrains Plugin Repository from your IntelliJ IDEA or use the link here.

  3. Click on Install to add the plugin to your IDE.

Usage 🛠️

Upon installation, a new widget will be displayed on the IntelliJ IDEA status bar. This widget will update automatically as you modify the code. If you wish, you can click on the widget to manually update the line count.

Settings > Tools > Kimi Commits

idea-plugin.name: Git Change Highlighter
idea-plugin.description:
The Git Change Highlighter is a plugin for the main JetBrains products that highlights lines in your code based on changes tracked by Git since your current branch creation. This plugin helps developers quickly identify which lines have been added or modified in the latest commits, enhancing code review and collaboration.

How It Works

  • Highlighting Committed Lines: The plugin highlights lines that have been committed after the creation of the current branch. This helps developers quickly identify changes relevant to the branch's development history.
  • Excluding Uncommitted/Unstaged Changes: The plugin does not highlight uncommitted or unstaged changes because the IDE already highlights these changes in the gutter by default.
  • Considering Uncommitted Changes: The plugin considers uncommitted changes to ensure that the highlights for committed changes remain accurate, even if those lines are moved by uncommitted changes.

Features

  • Highlighting Added Lines: Automatically highlights lines that have been added in the latest commits.
  • Customizable Highlighting: Choose from various highlight effect types and colors to suit your preferences.
  • Real-Time Updates: Highlights refresh automatically after commits, checkouts and other repository changes.
  • Integration with Git: Uses Git commands to fetch changes and apply highlights accurately.
  • Dynamic Git Change Highlighting: Considers newly added and removed lines in Git to ensure accurate highlighting.
  • Branch Exclusion Setting: Allows users to specify branches to exclude from highlighting.

Usage

  1. Open your JetBrains IDE and go to File > Settings (or [Your IDE] > Preferences on macOS).
  2. Navigate to Git Change Highlighter under the Other Settings section.
  3. Configure the color and form of highlighting as per your preference.
  4. Enter branch names to exclude from highlighting and manage the list using the + and - buttons.

Installation

  1. Open your JetBrains IDE.
  2. Go to File > Settings (or [Your IDE] > Preferences on macOS).
  3. Select Plugins from the left-hand menu.
  4. Click on the Marketplace tab.
  5. Search for Git Change Highlighter.
  6. Click Install.
  7. Restart your IDE to activate the plugin.

Accessing and Working with Settings

  1. Open your JetBrains IDE and go to File > Settings (or [Your IDE] > Preferences on macOS).
  2. Navigate to Git Change Highlighter under the Other Settings section.
  3. In the settings panel, you can:
    • Color of Highlighting: Choose the color for highlighting added lines.
    • Form of Highlighting: Select the effect type (e.g., Line Underscore, Wave Underscore, Strikeout, etc.).
    • Branches to Skip Highlighting: Enter branch names to exclude from highlighting and manage the list using the + and - buttons.
  4. After making changes, click Apply to save the settings and OK to close the settings window.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Version 1.3.0

  • Fixed the error shown at IDE start on recent IDE versions ("Plugin to blame: Git Change Highlighter"): the old startup hook accessed the editor from a background thread and was disabled by the platform, which also left highlights stale.
  • Automatic refresh: highlights update right after commits, checkouts and other repository changes instead of waiting for a tab switch.
  • Bug fixes: changed lines in single-line hunks and in newly added files were not detected; highlights next to uncommitted edits could land on the wrong line.
  • Quieter integration: the plugin's git queries no longer appear in the IDE's Git console.
  • Modernized build: IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.x, Kotlin 2.4, Gradle 9, JDK 21. Still compatible with IDEs from 2023.2 on.

Version 1.2.1

  • Compatibility Update: Increased compatibility of the plugin to support a wider range of IDE versions.

Version 1.2.0

  • New Feature: Added a setting to exclude specific branches from highlighting. Users can now manage a list of branches to skip highlighting, enhancing customization and control.

Version 1.1.1

  • Bug Fix: Fixed an issue where some updated lines were not being highlighted correctly.

Version 1.1.0

  • New Feature: Dynamic Git Change Highlighting
    • The plugin now dynamically considers newly added and removed lines in Git when highlighting changes.
    • Improved accuracy by tracking changes from both the initial commit and uncommitted changes.
    • Optimized performance for efficient processing of line number adjustments.
  • General Stability Improvements
  • Note: Highlighting may take a moment to refresh, especially for large files or numerous changes. Please allow a short time for the highlights to update.

idea-plugin.name: AI Git Commit
idea-plugin.description:
Generate AI-powered Git commit messages directly from the Commit tool window.

AI Git Commit builds focused context from the files and partial changes you select, then sends it to the AI service and model you configure.

Highlights

  • Generate messages from selected changes, partial commit hunks, and unversioned files.
  • Choose the output language and use editable model IDs.
  • Create reusable custom prompts or load commit-prompt.txt from the project root.
  • Compact large change sets and exclude generated files, lock files, or custom wildcard patterns.
  • Use the IDE system proxy, inspect the latest prompt, and stream responses where supported.

Supported AI Services

OrcaRouter, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenAI API, OpenAI-compatible providers, OpenRouter, Ollama, Alibaba Cloud Model Studio, SiliconFlow, VolcEngine, Cloudflare Workers AI, and Kimi.

Getting Started

  1. Open Settings/Preferences > Tools > AI Git Commit.
  2. Select a provider, model, and output language, then configure the endpoint and API key if required.
  3. Select changes in the Commit tool window and choose Generate AI Commit Message.

Privacy: Generating a message sends the selected change context and prompt to the AI service you configured. Review that provider's privacy and data-retention policies before sending sensitive source code.

Documentation and source code | Issue tracker | Prompt templates

idea-plugin.name: GitFlowTools
idea-plugin.description:
This is a branch management plugin for the mrtf git flow (master, release, test, feature) process Usage Guide .
The biggest advantage is to reduce the operation of switching branches and merging branches in the agile development process, and reduce the labor cost of branch management.

The main functions are as follows:
  1. Plug-in configuration files can be added to GIT version management and shared within the team
  2. New development branch and repair branch based on origin / master
  3. Rebuild test branch and release branch based on origin / master
  4. After the development is completed, merge the development branch into the test branch
  5. After the test is completed, the development branch is merged into the release branch, and the release branch is locked
  6. After the release is completed, merge the release branch into the origin / master branch
  7. Failure to release will unlock the release branch
  8. Only those who lock the release branch can click [release complete] and [release failed]
  9. All executed git commands can be viewed in "Event Log"
  10. Support to initiate Merge Request locally
  11. Batch delete branches
  12. When start test, you can choose to trigger the Kubesphere pipeline
  13. Connect to Kubesphere pod console
  14. Show Kubesphere pod log

Fork code from GitFlowPlus
这是一个适用于mrtf git flow (master,release,test,feature) 流程的分支管理插件 使用指南。
最大优势是减少敏捷开发过程中切换分支和合并分支的操作，降低分支管理的人力成本。

主要功能如下：
  1. 插件配置文件可以加入GIT版本管理，在团队内部共享
  2. 基于origin/master新建开发分支和修复分支

  4. 开发完成后将开发分支合并到测试分支
  5. 测试完成后将开发分支合并到发布分支，并锁定发布分支
  6. 发布完成后将发布分支合并到origin/master分支
  7. 发布失败将解除发布分支的锁定
  8. 只有锁定发布分支的人才能点[发布完成]和[发布失败]
  9. 所有执行的git命令都可以在"Event Log"查看
  10. 支持在本地发起Merge Request
  11. 批量删除分支
  12. 提测时可选择触发 Kubesphere 流水线

Summary:

PR-FlowTracker is a powerful and dynamic plugin that empowers you to track Pull Requests (PRs) on GitHub directly within your JetBrains IDE. Effortlessly monitor PR statuses and access essential information in a clear, organized manner, streamlining the journey from opening to merging your PRs and boosting project management efficiency.

Key Features:

  • Easy Access to Details: Directly access detailed information about each PR, facilitating navigation and speeding up the review process.
  • Conflict Management: Quickly identify and manage merge conflicts and other issues related to PRs.

Benefits:

  • Enhanced Efficiency: Save time navigating through multiple PRs by consolidating essential information in one place.
  • Improved Visibility: Gain quick insights into PR statuses and key details, aiding better project management.
  • Seamless Integration: Access PR information directly within your IDE, creating a smoother workflow.

Supported Operating Systems:

The plugin is recommended for macOS and Linux for optimal performance. It is also compatible with Windows.

Getting Started:

  • Installation:
    • Launch your JetBrains IDE and open the plugin settings at Preferences > Plugins > Marketplace.
    • Search for "PR-FlowTracker" and install it.
  • Prerequisites: Follow our Prerequisites guide for a step-by-step list of requirements to prepare your environment.
  • Quick Start Guide: Follow our Quick Start guide for a step-by-step guide with screenshots to get up and running quickly.

The Gitmoji Commit Column plugin adds a custom column in the Commit Log to display Gitmojis extracted from commit messages. Only the Gitmojis found in the commit messages are displayed in this column, making it easy to understand the purpose of each commit at a glance.

Features

  • Displays Gitmojis in a dedicated column in the Commit Log.
  • Parses and converts Gitmoji codes (e.g., :bug:, :rocket:) from commit messages into emojis.

Usage

  1. Install the plugin from the JetBrains Plugin Marketplace.
  2. Go to the Version Control tab in your IDE.
  3. Enable the Gitmoji column under the Show Columns menu (via the eye icon).

Supported IDEs

  • IntelliJ IDEA
  • PhpStorm

idea-plugin.name: Jira Branch Creator
idea-plugin.description:
Jira Branch Creator

Jira Branch Creator is an IntelliJ IDEA plugin that effectively integrates JIRA issues with Git workflow. This plugin allows you to easily create Git branches based on JIRA issues and automatically generate commit messages that include issue numbers.

Key Features

  • Create Git branches directly from JIRA issues assigned to the user
  • Generate new branches from a base branch (e.g. main, develop)
  • Support custom branch prefixes (feat/, bugfix/, etc.)
  • Include JIRA issue numbers in automatic commit messages
  • Convenient keyboard shortcuts

How to Use

Initial Setup

  1. Go to Settings/Preferences → Tools → Jira Branch Creator
  2. Enter JIRA connection information:
  • JIRA URL (e.g. https://your-domain.atlassian.net)
  • Username (JIRA account email)
  • API token (Click the issue button to get a token from the Atlassian website)
  1. Set base branch (default: main)
  2. Select desired branch prefix

Creating Branches from JIRA Issues

  1. Press keyboard shortcut Cmd + Shift + J (macOS) or Ctrl + Shift + J (Windows/Linux)
  2. Search or select JIRA issues in the search box
  3. Branch is automatically created and checked out based on the selected issue

Automatically Generate Commit Messages

  1. After completing code changes, press keyboard shortcut Cmd + Ctrl + J (macOS) or Ctrl + Alt + J (Windows/Linux)
  2. Enter commit message (JIRA issue number is automatically added)
  3. Click confirm button to complete commit

Detailed Features

Jira API Token Management

  • Secure token storage and management
  • Test connection functionality to validate settings
  • Simple logout function

Git Branch Creation

  • Create new branches from selected base branch (main, develop, etc.)
  • Apply configured branch prefix (feat/, bugfix/, etc.)
  • Branch naming convention including JIRA issue key (e.g. feat/DAP-999)

Git Commit Automation

  • Automatically generate commit messages that include JIRA issue numbers
  • Verify changes before proceeding with commit
  • Provide detailed error messages in case of failure

License

This project is distributed under the Apache License.

Jira Branch Creator is a third-party plugin created by an independent developer, not Atlassian. JIRA and related trademarks are the property of Atlassian.

idea-plugin.name: Crocodile for GitLab
idea-plugin.description:
Stop context-switching. Manage GitLab CI/CD directly inside your JetBrains IDE.

Crocodile for GitLab is a powerful, 100% free plugin built to eliminate the friction between your code and your DevOps workflow. Whether you use GitLab.com, Self-Managed, or GitLab Dedicated, Crocodile brings absolute control over variables, pipelines, environments, and logs right to your fingertips.

Why Crocodile?

  • Ultimate Variable Control: Create, edit, copy, or migrate CI/CD variables across environments effortlessly.
  • Smart Variable Tracking: Instantly scan and find exactly where your variables are used in the codebase.
  • Effortless Environments: Create, monitor, and clean up deployment environments without leaving the IDE.
  • Live Pipeline & Job Control: Run, stop, or retry jobs, stream live execution logs, and inspect associated Git history.
  • "Fire & Forget" Asynchronous Jobs: Trigger manual jobs and keep working. Crocodile handles the execution background and alerts you the second it starts or finishes.
  • IDE-Native Collaboration: Write persistent pipeline notes and discuss tasks securely with your team.
  • Fail-Safe History: Made a mistake? Undo or redo any variable or environment change with a single click.

Supercharge your GitLab workflow. Install Crocodile today and keep your focus where it belongs—on your code.

Advanced Variable Automation

  • Secure Local Storage: Save variables locally within your IDE's private configuration store.
  • Cross-Project Portability: Import existing variables directly into other GitLab projects.
  • Flexible Imports & Triggers: Populate environment configurations instantly from .env files, and create Git tags to trigger pipeline runs on demand.

Export Capabilities

  • Run Configurations: Export variables to .env files for fast local debugging.
  • Documentation-Ready: Export variables into structured Markdown tables to drop directly into your repository documentation.

Enterprise-Grade Security

  • Zero Data Leakage: Your access tokens, saved variables, and sensitive data are never transmitted to third parties.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
Version 4.2 - PR List Pagination & Project Filtering

New Features

  • Configurable PR list loading – Page size (PRs per request) and maximum PRs in list are now exposed in the plugin settings, with bounds matching the API client clamps.
  • Multi-select project filter – The PR filter panel preloads the project list and lets you scope the view to several projects at once; the selection is persisted across restarts.
  • Project-scoped PR fetching – With a project filter active only the selected projects are queried, instead of the whole organization.
  • Copy PR Link – New context-menu action in the Pull Requests list that copies the PR web URL to the clipboard.

Version 4.1 - Clone Dialog Overhaul

Performance

  • Per-project repo fetching – Replaced the old loop that called the org-wide repositories endpoint once per project (returning the full org each time) with bounded-parallel project-scoped calls. ~50x less data over the wire for large orgs.
  • Incremental tree population – Clone tree fills in as each project's repos arrive instead of waiting for everything; first results visible in <1s on big organizations.

New Features

  • Project filter – Multi-select popup with search and Select All / Deselect All. Selection is persisted per account so subsequent clones jump straight to the projects you care about.

idea-plugin.name: FB JSP Validator
idea-plugin.description:
Validates SI() translation calls in JSP files before Git commit.

Scans committed JSP files for incomplete or incorrect SI() translation function calls and blocks the commit with a detailed error report. Supports auto-fix via the MyMemory translation API.

What is SI()?

SI() is a JSP translation function that takes exactly 4 arguments: 

SI("Russian", "Uzbek Cyrillic", "Uzbek Latin", "English")

Checks performed on every commit

  • Wrong argument count — SI() must have exactly 4 quoted string arguments.
  • 3 or more empty translations — flags calls where 3+ fields are blank or whitespace only.
  • 3 or more identical translations — flags calls where the same text is repeated across 3+ language slots.
  • Wrong file encoding — JSP files must be encoded in Windows-1251. Files with other encodings are reported and skipped.
  • File size over 64 KB — oversized files are flagged but still fully scanned for SI() errors.

Commit dialog options

  • Commit — proceed despite errors.
  • Fix — auto-translate missing fields using MyMemory API, then commit.
  • Cancel — cancel the commit to fix manually.

Auto-fix behaviour

  • Translates Russian → Uzbek Latin via MyMemory API.
  • Converts Uzbek Latin → Uzbek Cyrillic using built-in transliteration.
  • Translates Russian → English via MyMemory API.
  • Only fixes calls where the Russian (first) argument is present.
  • Requires a configured HTTP proxy to reach the translation API (5000 character/day limit on free tier).

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2024.1 or later.
  • JSP files must be saved in Windows-1251 encoding.
  • HTTP proxy configured in Settings → Appearance & Behavior → System Settings → HTTP Proxy if direct internet access is not available.
idea-plugin.change-notes:

idea-plugin.name: Git Assume Unchanged
idea-plugin.description:
Easily manage Git's assume-unchanged flag directly from IntelliJ IDEA.

This plugin provides convenient actions to mark files as "assume-unchanged" or remove that flag, allowing you to tell Git to temporarily ignore changes to tracked files without modifying .gitignore.

Features

  • Assumed Files Tab - View all assume-unchanged files in commit dialog
  • Unassume multiple files at once from commit dialog
  • Mark single or multiple files as assume-unchanged
  • Remove assume-unchanged flag from files
  • Accessible via Git context menu
  • Multi-repository support
  • Automatic Git repository validation
  • Clear success/error notifications
  • Works with all JetBrains IDEs (IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, etc.)

Usage

  1. Right-click on any file(s) in the project view
  2. Navigate to Git → Git Assume
  3. Choose Assume Unchanged or No Assume Unchanged

What is Assume Unchanged?

Git's assume-unchanged flag tells Git to ignore changes to a tracked file in your working directory. This is useful when you need to modify configuration files locally without committing the changes.

idea-plugin.name: Truly Beyond Compare
idea-plugin.description:
Compare files across branches even when Git rename detection fails.

When major refactors move files across modules and rewrite packages, Git's rename detection breaks down. IntelliJ's "Compare with Branch" stops working because it relies on Git to correlate files.

This plugin bypasses Git rename detection entirely by matching files using their basename and path similarity, then feeding matched paths directly to IntelliJ's diff viewer.

Features:

  • Match files by basename across branches
  • Smart path similarity ranking when multiple matches exist
  • Backport commits with intelligent path mapping
  • Uses native IntelliJ diff viewer
  • Works with any Git repository

Usage:

  • Right-click a file → "[FM] Compare with Branch or Tag (By Filename)..."
  • Or use keyboard shortcut: Alt+A
  • Right-click a commit in Git Log → "[FM] Backport Commit..."
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Truly Beyond Compare 2.2.2

  • Improved: "Diff with Branch" search now uses IntelliJ's standard fuzzy matcher (MinusculeMatcher), so abbreviated inputs like ori/mainclisit or orimainclisit correctly match origin/main-client-sit. Matching also feels consistent with Search Everywhere and Goto File.
  • Improved: Filtered branches are now ranked by match quality, so the closest match appears at the top of each group instead of plain alphabetical order.
  • New: Pin frequently-used branches to the top of the popup via right-click → "Pin to Top" / "Unpin". Pinned branches appear in a new "Pinned" group at the top of the tree, with a yellow star icon visible anywhere the branch is shown.
  • New: "Recent" group now tracks the last 3 branches you actually picked in the popup (most recent first), replacing the prior behaviour of always showing only the current branch.
  • Fix: Search highlights now render correctly for remote branches when the query targets the full ref (e.g. ori/mainclisit or orimainclisit against origin/main-client-sit). Previously the row would appear in the filtered list but the matched characters would not be highlighted because the renderer only matched against the short branch name.

idea-plugin.name: Git Desk
idea-plugin.description:
Git Desk

Git Desk brings advanced Git workflows directly into your IDE with full support for GitHub and GitLab. It is organized around four focused tabs: Merge Sessions, Pull Requests, Repositories, and Worktrees.

Merge Sessions

Create logical, persistent merge operations that allow incremental conflict resolution. Import, export, and share sessions with teammates for collaborative merging. Execute only when ready. In multi-repo projects, a repository selector lets you switch context quickly.

Pull Requests

View and interact with GitHub and GitLab pull/merge requests directly in the IDE. Pull requests are aggregated across all configured repositories, with a multi-select repo filter to narrow results. Includes timeline, comments, reviews, commits, and GitLab-style status/author/reviewer filters. Requires a configured access token.

Repositories

Manage multiple Git repositories from a single interface. Add repositories to your list, view their status at a glance, and perform bulk operations like fetching updates or switching branches across multiple repositories.

Worktrees

Manage Git worktrees directly in your IDE. Create, delete, lock, and unlock worktrees to work on multiple branches simultaneously without stashing. View branch status, dirty state, and ahead/behind counts at a glance. Double-click to open any worktree in a new IDE window. Supports multi-repo projects.
idea-plugin.change-notes:

  • Worktree Details Panel: Select any worktree to view branch, path, HEAD commit, sync status, lock state, and dirty files at a glance.
  • Create Worktree Dialog: Create from existing branches or new branches with autocomplete, automatic path generation, and validation.
  • Delete Worktree Dialog: Confirmation with dirty-state warnings, file list preview, and optional branch deletion.
  • Search & Filter: Filter worktrees by branch name, path, commit message, or keywords (dirty, locked, clean).
  • Multi-Repository Support: Repository selector appears when the project contains multiple repos.

Changes

  • Removed File Tab and Help Tab: The plugin now focuses on four core tabs — Merge Sessions, Pull Requests, Repositories, and Worktrees.
  • Improved Theme Support: All tabs now adapt correctly to any IDE theme (light, dark, high-contrast).

Note: This is a beta release. Some features may change based on user feedback.

idea-plugin.name: Git Insight
idea-plugin.description:
Git Insight brings comprehensive code statistics to your JetBrains IDE. Track developer contributions, analyze codebase scale, detect problematic commits, and merge multiple Git identities—all without leaving your editor.

Project Statistics

  • File, line, and token counts by extension
  • Pie chart visualization of code distribution
  • Category filtering for focused analysis
  • Token counts for LLM context estimation

Developer Statistics

  • Track contributions (lines added/deleted) by developer
  • Interactive contribution charts over time
  • Date range filtering with quick presets (Last month, Last year)
  • Identity merging for developers with multiple accounts
  • Developer teams for tracking team performance
  • Drill-down to individual commits and file changes
  • Velocity metrics with workday adjustments

Suspicious Commits Detection

  • Mass formatting commits (10x average with balanced add/delete)
  • Oversized commits (100x larger than average)
  • Duplicate and revert commits
  • Exclude problematic commits from statistics

Multi-Repository Support

  • Add external git repositories and view aggregated statistics across all of them
  • Repository selector to switch between individual, combined, or current-project views
  • Smart concurrent scanning with per-repository caching
  • Settings synchronization: developer merges and exclusions propagate across all connected repositories automatically

Use Cases

  • Track developer productivity over time
  • Prepare performance review data
  • Monitor project scale and migration progress
  • Aggregate statistics across multiple microservices or related repositories
  • Answer "what was done?" questions with real data

Compatible with all JetBrains IDEs including IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, PhpStorm, GoLand, and more.

idea-plugin.name: JIRA Smart Commit
idea-plugin.description:
Generate intelligent commit messages, PR descriptions, and code changes using AI with JIRA integration.

Features:

  • Code Vibing (Multi-Session) - Tabbed AI chat panel: each session pins a JIRA ticket, creates a git worktree off a base branch, and writes code in that isolated worktree (Ctrl+Alt+V)
  • Per-Session Commit & PR - Inside each Code Vibing session, run the existing commit-message and PR-description flows against the session's worktree
  • Configurable System Prompt - Customize the Code Vibing system prompt (empty = plain chat, or restore the default file read/write template)
  • AI-Powered Commit Messages - Generate conventional commit messages based on staged changes and JIRA ticket context
  • File Selection Dialog - Choose which files to include in the commit with an intuitive checkbox interface
  • JIRA Integration - Automatically fetch ticket details from branch name
  • PR Title & Description Generation - Create comprehensive PR titles and descriptions from commit history
  • Create PR with One Click - Open PR creation page with auto-filled title and description (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket)
  • Automatic PR Creation via API - Create PRs directly via platform APIs without leaving the IDE (Bitbucket, GitHub, GitLab)
  • PR Reviewers Selection - Select reviewers from repository members with default reviewers pre-selected
  • Smart Branch Creation - Create branches from JIRA tickets with auto-generated names
  • Worktree Creation - Create an isolated git worktree on a new branch from a JIRA ticket, with optional base-branch fetch and open-in-new-window
  • Multiple AI Providers - Support for OpenAI (GPT-4) and Anthropic (Claude)

Usage:

  1. Configure JIRA and AI credentials in Settings → Tools → JIRA Smart Commit
  2. Make changes to your code
  3. Use Git → JIRA Smart Commit → Generate Commit Message (Ctrl+Alt+G)
  4. Select which files to include in the file selection dialog
  5. Review and edit the generated message
  6. Commit!
  7. Or use Start Code Vibing (Ctrl+Alt+V) to let AI generate code changes from your JIRA ticket

idea-plugin.name: Git Merge Into
idea-plugin.description:
Git Merge Into is a plugin that helps you quickly merge the current branch into another branch — without leaving your IDE.

How to Use

  1. Keyboard shortcut: Press Alt+G, then I to trigger the merge action.

  2. Action search: Press Ctrl+Shift+A (or ⌘+Shift+A on macOS), then type "Merge Into".

  3. Git Open menu: If you have the Git Open plugin installed, Merge Into will automatically appear in the Git Open action group.

Once triggered, you'll see the merge process in action:

What It Does

  • Checks out the target branch
  • Fetches and resets to the latest remote state
  • Merges your current branch into it
  • Optionally pushes the result
  • Checks out back to your original branch

Settings

Go to Settings > Tools > Git Merge Into to configure:

  • Target branch — the branch to merge into (default: develop)
  • Push after merge — automatically push after a successful merge
  • Run in background — run the merge process in the background
  • Abort merge when conflicts — automatically abort and return to your branch on conflicts

You can also override the target branch per project under the Git Merge Into (Project) settings.

idea-plugin.name: Git Flow Helper
idea-plugin.description:
GitFlow Helper

JetBrains Marketplace | GitHub | Buy Me a Coffee

WHAT'S NEW IN v2.10.0

  • CI/CD:Graphical visualization of Jenkins pipeline execution (others coming soon).

WHAT'S NEW IN v2.8.0 / 2.9.0

  • Proactive Divergence Indicator in Status Bar: Real-time badge showing commits behind develop (⬇ N) with instant 1-click branch synchronization!
  • Customizable Log Typography: Select custom font family and font size directly in the Logs tool window.
  • Repository Context in Logs & Flow: Interactive repo selection in the Flow diagram panel and clear repo name prefix in execution logs.
  • Optional Task Selection on Feature Start: Create feature branches with or without binding to an issue tracker task.
  • Safe Background Execution: GitFlow menu is automatically disabled during background operations to prevent branch conflicts.
  • New Interactive About Dialog: Comprehensive built-in documentation guide (UsageDialog).
  • CI/CD Config Dialog: It's now possible to trigger builds in Jenkins directly from the plugin.

OTHER IMPORTANT FEATURES

  • Extended Issue Tracker Integrations: Full support for Jira, GitHub, GitLab, and Redmine!
  • Dedicated 4-Tab Tool Window: Dedicated views for Logs, Issues (rich task detail & actions), Flow (visual GitFlow branch graph), and CI/CD (Jenkins pipeline tracking)!
  • Jenkins CI/CD Pipeline Monitoring: Real-time build status tracking and progressive console log streaming.
  • Comprehensive Safety Guardrails: Pre-finish checks for uncommitted changes, unpushed commits, and divergence blocking, plus protected branch commit warnings for main and develop.
  • Multi-Repository Workspace Support: Independent configuration and execution across multi-repo projects.

📖 Overview

GitFlow Helper brings the complete Vincent Driessen Git Flow branching strategy natively into JetBrains IDEs.

It executes all Git operations programmatically via asynchronous IntelliJ Platform APIs without requiring external Git Flow CLI tools. In addition to branch automation, it deeply integrates with your Issue Trackers (Jira, GitHub, GitLab, Redmine), CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins), and provides interactive visual flow diagrams right inside your IDE.

✨ Key Features

🌱 Git Flow Initialization & Configuration

  • Initialize Git Flow directly from your IDE with a single click.
  • Fully customizable parameters:
    • main production branch name
    • develop integration branch name
    • Branch prefixes for feature/, release/, and hotfix/
    • Version tag prefix (e.g. v)
  • Multi-repository workspace support: easily enable, disable, and configure Git Flow per repository.
  • Safe configuration reset action to reconfigure branch conventions whenever needed.

🌳 Git Flow Branching Model

The plugin follows the standard Git Flow strategy with zero CLI overhead:

  • Main Branch (main / master): Represents production-ready, release-tested code.
  • Develop Branch (develop): Central integration branch for ongoing development.
  • Feature Branches (feature/*): Created from develop. Finished features merge back into develop.
  • Release Branches (release/*): Forked from develop for stabilization, version bumping, and release preparation. Merged back into both main and develop with automated version tags.
  • Hotfix Branches (hotfix/*): Created directly from main for critical production fixes. Merged back into both main and develop with patch tags.

⚡ Proactive Divergence Indicator & 1-Click Sync

Never let your working branch become stale or drift far behind development:

  • Real-Time Status Bar Badge (⬇ N): Displays an interactive divergence badge whenever your active feature, release, or hotfix branch falls behind its base branch (develop or main).
  • 1-Click Synchronization: Click the status bar badge or select Feature Sync, Release Sync, or Hotfix Sync to automatically fetch remote changes and cleanly rebase/merge the base branch into your working branch.
  • Continuous Background Awareness: Triggers automatically on repository updates, IDE focus activation, and background scheduled checks.

🛡️ Safety Guardrails & Pre-Finish Checks

GitFlow Helper prevents broken states, untracked work loss, and accidental direct commits:

  1. Protected Branch Commit Guard (CheckinHandler): Intercepts commit attempts made directly to protected branches (main or develop). Displays a warning dialog urging developers to work within dedicated feature or hotfix branches.
  2. Uncommitted Changes Verification: Scans for dirty working tree files before finishing a branch. Prompts to commit changes or abort.
  3. Unpushed Commits Check: Verifies whether local commits have been pushed upstream before finishing to avoid history divergence.
  4. Divergence Blocker (isBehind): Blocks branch finishing if the branch is behind develop. Developers are instructed to synchronize first to resolve any potential merge conflicts in their own branch.

🔀 Flexible Finish & Approval Workflows

When finishing a feature, choose the workflow that best matches your team's code review process:

  • Integrate Immediately: Checks out develop, pulls latest changes, performs a merge (standard --no-ff or squashed into a single clean commit), pushes to remote, and optionally deletes local and remote branches.
  • Create Merge Request (GitLab): Uses native Git push options (-o merge_request.create, -o merge_request.target, etc.) to create an open MR automatically.
  • Self-Create (GitHub / Bitbucket / Azure DevOps): Pushes your feature branch to remote origin and keeps it alive for manual pull request opening and code review.
  • Automatic Task Closing: Automatically transitions and closes the linked issue tracker task upon successful completion.

🪟 Dedicated 4-Tab Tool Window

Monitor every aspect of your Git workflow in a dedicated bottom Tool Window:

  1. Logs Tab:
    • Real-time display of all Git commands executed by the plugin (stdout, stderr, exit codes).
    • Live activity indicator on the tool window icon when commands are running.
    • Customizable log font family and font size.
    • Multi-repository tagging: clear repository prefixes in logs when working with multi-root projects.
    • One-click log clearing.
  2. Issues Tab:
    • Side-by-side list and detail inspector for tasks assigned to you.
    • Rich task summary, description, and comments.
    • Direct buttons to start Feature or Hotfix branches directly from any task.
  3. Flow Tab:
    • Interactive visual graph of your local Git branches.
    • Color-coded branches: Main (Blue), Develop (Green), Features (Orange), Releases (Cyan), Hotfixes (Red).
    • Shows origin connection lines, active checkout markers, and per-repository selector.
  4. CI/CD Tab:
    • Dedicated Continuous Integration monitoring.
    • Live streaming of build console logs with color highlights.
    • Build status tracking and stop/clear controls.

🔗 Issue Trackers & Task Management

Seamlessly connects to IntelliJ IDEA's Task Management subsystem (com.intellij.tasks):

  • Supported Platforms:
    • GitHub Issues
    • GitLab Issues & Merge Requests
    • Jira Software
    • Redmine
  • Automated Workflow:
    • Automatically sanitizes issue keys and titles into clean branch names (e.g. feature/PROJ-1234-add-oauth-login).
    • Automatically assigns the issue to you and sets status to In Progress when starting work.
    • Quick action to open the active task directly in your default browser.
    • Automatically closes the task on the server when finishing the branch.

🚀 CI/CD Pipeline Monitoring (Jenkins)

Stay in your flow without switching back and forth to your browser:

  • Per-repository CI/CD server configuration.
  • Connects directly to Jenkins pipelines.
  • Automatically initiates build monitoring when pushing finished code.
  • Streams live console chunks progressively with smart ANSI color parsing.
  • Secure token storage backed by IntelliJ's PasswordSafe.

🗂️ Branch Navigation & Interactive Tree View

  • Status Bar Integration: Access all operations, view current branch status, and trigger actions directly from the IDE status bar.
  • Interactive Tree Explorer (Show as tree...):
    • Hierarchical visualization grouping branches into feature, release, hotfix, and base folders.
    • Speed Search: Start typing to immediately filter and highlight branches.
    • One-click checkout and branch deletion (local and remote).
    • Bookmark indicators for current active branch and production branches.

⌨️ Keyboard Shortcuts

All primary Git Flow operations have default keyboard shortcuts configured:

Action macOS Shortcut Windows / Linux Shortcut Target Base
Feature Start ⌃ ⌥ 1 Ctrl + Alt + 1 develop
Feature Publish ⌃ ⌥ 2 Ctrl + Alt + 2 remote origin
Feature Finish ⌃ ⌥ 3 Ctrl + Alt + 3 develop
Release Start ⌃ ⌥ 4 Ctrl + Alt + 4 develop
Release Publish ⌃ ⌥ 5 Ctrl + Alt + 5 remote origin
Release Finish ⌃ ⌥ 6 Ctrl + Alt + 6 main + develop
Hotfix Start ⌃ ⌥ 7 Ctrl + Alt + 7 main
Hotfix Publish ⌃ ⌥ 8 Ctrl + Alt + 8 remote origin
Hotfix Finish ⌃ ⌥ 9 Ctrl + Alt + 9 main + develop

Tip: You can customize any keybinding anytime under: Settings (Preferences) → Keymap → Plugins → GitFlow Helper

📋 Requirements & Compatibility

  • IDE Version: IntelliJ IDEA 2024.2+ (Community or Ultimate), Android Studio, or compatible JetBrains IDEs.
  • Java: Runtime Java 21+.
  • Git Plugin: Standard bundled Git4Idea plugin enabled.
  • Task Management (Optional): Bundled com.intellij.tasks plugin enabled for issue tracker features.

🛠️ Installation

  1. Open your JetBrains IDE.
  2. Go to Settings / Preferences (⌘, / Ctrl+Alt+S) → Plugins → Marketplace.
  3. Search for Git Flow Helper and click Install.
  4. Restart your IDE if prompted.

Alternatively, download the plugin release directly from the JetBrains Marketplace.

🤝 Contributing & Support

  • Bug Reports & Feature Requests: GitHub Issues
  • Source Code: wdvalle/gitflow-helper
  • Support the Project: If GitFlow Helper saves you time and simplifies your daily workflow, consider buying a coffee on Ko-fi!

idea-plugin.name: Gh-Workflows
idea-plugin.description:
Gh-Workflows lets you browse, monitor, and trigger GitHub Actions workflows directly from your IntelliJ-based IDE. Take full control of GitHub Actions without leaving your IDE.

Features

Workflow Browser Tree view displaying all workflows and recent runs at a glance. Each run uses a two-line layout: the first line shows run number, commit message, and status icon; the second line shows who triggered it, elapsed time, and branch name.

Trigger Workflows Dispatch workflow_dispatch workflows with branch/tag selection and input parameters. Type in the branch/tag dropdown to instantly filter the list and find the ref you need. Supports string, number, choice, boolean, and environment input types. Required inputs and default values are displayed automatically.

Status Icons Intuitive icons for every workflow run state: success, failure, in-progress, queued, cancelled, and skipped.

Favorites Save frequently used URLs as favorites for quick access. Click the star icon to open the Favorites popup, which shows your saved URL favorites with edit and ✕ buttons. Click the edit icon to modify a favorite's name or URL; click ✕ to remove it. Click [+ Add] to add a new favorite by entering a name and URL; click any favorite to open it in the browser. Hovering over a favorite highlights the row for clear visual feedback. Favorites persist across IDE restarts and work independently of GitHub authentication.

Run Management (Context Menu) Right-click any workflow run to re-run all jobs, re-run failed jobs, cancel, or delete. Dangerous actions like delete require confirmation before execution.

Failed Run Job Details Failed workflow runs automatically expand to show individual jobs with their status icons. Quickly identify which job failed and double-click to open it on GitHub.

Open in Browser Double-click any workflow or run node to jump directly to the GitHub page.

Auto-detect Repository Automatically identifies the GitHub repository from your project's git remotes. Supports SSH (git@github.com:owner/repo.git) and HTTPS formats.

Auto-Refresh Automatically refreshes workflow data in the background at a configurable interval (default: 10 minutes). Enable or disable auto-refresh and adjust the interval from the Settings dialog.

Seamless Auth Authenticates using your IntelliJ GitHub account (recommended) or a manual Personal Access Token as fallback. PAT requires repo and workflow scopes, stored securely in the IDE's PasswordSafe.

CI/CD Automatic deployment via GitHub Actions — when pluginVersion in gradle.properties is bumped on the main branch, the plugin is built, tested, verified, and published to JetBrains Marketplace automatically.

Getting Started

  1. Open a project with a GitHub remote
  2. Click the GitHub Workflows tab in the right sidebar
  3. Browse workflows and recent runs in the tree view
  4. Select a workflow and click Run Workflow to trigger it with custom inputs

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2025.2 or later
  • Git and GitHub plugins enabled
  • GitHub account configured in IDE, or a Personal Access Token

idea-plugin.name: gitee-vcs
idea-plugin.description:
Provides basic Gitee integration functions for IntelliJ IDEA / JetBrains IDE: share projects to Gitee within the IDE, create/view Pull Requests, sync Forks, clone repositories from Gitee, and provide an entry for configuring Access Tokens.

为 IntelliJ IDEA / JetBrains IDE 提供基础的 Gitee 集成功能：在 IDE 内分享项目到 Gitee、创建/查看 Pull Request、同步 Fork、从 Gitee 克隆仓库，并提供访问令牌（Access Token）配置入口。

功能

  • Share Project on Gitee：将当前本地项目推送到 Gitee 并创建仓库
  • Create Pull Request：从 IDE 发起 Gitee Pull Request
  • View Pull Requests：打开当前仓库的 PR 列表页
  • Sync Fork：将 fork 仓库与 upstream 同步
  • Clone from Gitee：从 Gitee 克隆仓库
  • Account Management：在 Settings 中管理 Access Token/默认可见性等

使用方法

  1. 生成 Access Token：打开 https://gitee.com/profile/personal_access_tokens
  2. 在 IDE 中配置：Settings/Preferences → Tools → Gitee
  3. 在菜单中使用：Tools → Gitee（或在对应动作搜索里输入 Gitee）

配置项说明

位置：Settings/Preferences → Tools → Gitee

  • Access Token：访问令牌（建议仅授予必要权限；仓库相关操作通常需要 repos scope）
  • Username：你的 Gitee 用户名（可选）
  • Default Visibility：分享项目时新建仓库的默认可见性（private / public）

开发与构建（本仓库）

该插件是本仓库的一个子模块，路径：plugins/gitee。

  • 入口描述：plugins/gitee/src/main/resources/META-INF/plugin.xml
  • 主要代码：plugins/gitee/src/main/kotlin/site/addzero/gitee
  • 依赖：使用 OkHttp 调用 Gitee API，依赖 IDE 的 Git4Idea 插件能力

一般情况下直接在项目根目录用 Gradle 运行/调试 IntelliJ 插件即可（以本仓库既有的 Gradle 配置为准）。

常见问题

  • 提示未配置 Token：先到 Settings/Preferences → Tools → Gitee 填写 Access Token
  • 找不到 Gitee 相关菜单：检查是否启用插件；或用 Find Action 搜索 Gitee
  • “No Gitee remote found”：当前 Git 仓库没有配置 gitee.com 的 remote（例如只配了 GitHub）

安全提示

Access Token 等同于账号授权凭证，请勿提交到仓库、截图公开或发给不可信的人；建议定期轮换 Token，并尽量只授予必需权限。

idea-plugin.name: Jujutsu VCS Integration
idea-plugin.description:
Native IntelliJ integration for Jujutsu (jj), a Git-compatible version control system with a fundamentally different approach to working with code.

Why Jujutsu?

Jujutsu treats your working copy as a commit—always. No staging area, no "dirty" state. Just describe what you're working on and keep coding. When you're ready to start something new, create a new change. It's version control that works the way you think.

Key Features

  • Describe-First Workflow — The Working Copy tool window (left side) lets you describe your current work and create new changes with one click. No more "WIP" commits.
  • Custom Log View — Visual commit graph with inline change IDs, descriptions, bookmarks, and author info. Filter by text, branch, author, or date range. Multi-select changes to see a combined diff or stacked metadata. Copy change IDs and descriptions from the context menu.
  • Change Operations — Edit, abandon, describe, rebase, squash, and split changes directly from the log. Right-click context menus for all common operations.
  • Rebase — Full rebase dialog with source mode selection (-r/-s/-b), visual destination picker with commit graph, and a live post-rebase graph preview showing exactly where commits will land.
  • Squash & Split — Squash changes into parent or any destination. Split into two with a dual file-tree UI that lets you write descriptions for both halves. Right-click files in the working copy, project view, or editor to squash or split with those files pre-selected.
  • Restore Files — Restore any file to its parent revision from the editor, project view, working copy panel, or commit details.
  • Compare & Diff — Compare any file against any revision or bookmark using a visual revision picker. Show diffs of working copy changes or historical commits. Compare historical versions against local working copy.
  • Git Remotes — Fetch and push to Git remotes without leaving the IDE. Push dialog with remote selector and bookmark scope options. Dry-run detection warns before non-fast-forward bookmark moves; sideways pushes require explicit confirmation.
  • File History & Annotations — Full file history with diff viewer and Show History for Selection (line-range history). Line-by-line blame annotations showing who changed what and when.
  • Conflict Resolution — Conflicted files are flagged in the working copy and log; open the 3-way merge editor from the context menu to resolve them, with bulk Accept Yours / Accept Theirs. Handles all three jj conflict marker formats (snapshot, diff, and git).
  • Open in GitHub / GitLab — Right-click any commit, file-history entry, or diff to jump to it on the remote, with line-number fragments for editor selections.
  • Bookmark Management — Create, delete, rename, and move bookmarks from the log. Track and untrack remote bookmarks; tracked vs. untracked are visually distinct.
  • Clone & First-Run Setup — Clone Git repos with jj from File > New > Project from Version Control, with colocate option. Plugin detects your jj install and walks you through user.name / user.email setup.
  • Configurable Log Revsets — Filter the log with any custom revset expression. A Test button validates the expression against each repo and shows how many changes match before you save.
  • Multi-Repository Support — Work with multiple JJ repositories in a single project. Unified log view with per-repo filtering, and per-repository overrides for identity, log limit, and revset.
  • Real-Time Status — Auto-refresh keeps the UI in sync as you edit files. See modified, added, and deleted files instantly.

For JJ Users

If you're already using JJ from the command line, this plugin brings that workflow into your IDE. All the power of jj describe, jj new, jj edit, jj abandon, and jj rebase—with visual feedback and keyboard shortcuts.

Getting Started

  1. Install Jujutsu if you haven't already
  2. Open a project with a .jj directory (or initialize one with VCS → Create JJ Repository)
  3. The Working Copy panel appears on the left; the Jujutsu log appears in the Version Control tool window

Roadmap

Coming soon: hunk-level squash & split, a branches panel, large repository support, issue tracker link rendering, operation log with undo/redo, and forge (PR/MR) integration. See the full roadmap.

idea-plugin.name: Git Worktree Toolbox
idea-plugin.description:
A native Git worktree manager built into your IDE. Create, browse, merge, and remove worktrees without leaving your editor.

Features

  • Dedicated Tool Window — View all worktrees with branch names, base branches, and status indicators (locked, prunable, missing directory). Auto-detects and highlights the current project's worktree.
  • Integrated Diff Viewer — Browse file-level changes between any worktree branch and a selectable comparison branch. Full side-by-side diff preview powered by IntelliJ's native diff engine.
  • File Explorer — Browse the complete directory tree of any worktree and open files directly in the editor.
  • Smart Worktree Creation — Create worktrees with branch validation, automatic remote fetch, and optional file copying from your main worktree. Configurable skip patterns filter out build artifacts and dependencies.
  • Merge and Reverse Merge — Merge a worktree branch into its base, or merge the current branch into a selected worktree. Force mode resolves conflicts automatically.
  • Revert Changes — Revert individual file changes in a worktree back to the base branch content.
  • Open in New Window — Launch any worktree as a full IDE project in a new frame.
  • Embedded Terminal — Open a terminal tab at any worktree's directory without leaving the editor.
  • GitHub PR Integration — Open GitHub's pull request creation page directly from a worktree, pre-filled with the correct branches.
  • Base Branch Tracking — Automatically tracks which branch each worktree was created from, enabling smart defaults for diffs, merges, and PRs.
  • Auto-Refresh — Worktree list refreshes automatically when Git state changes (commits, branch switches, fetches).

Getting Started

Open the Git Worktrees tool window from the right sidebar, or use Ctrl+Alt+W to create a new worktree. Configure default behaviors and skip patterns under Settings → Tools → Git Worktree Toolbox.

Screenshots

Requires the bundled Git and Terminal plugins.

idea-plugin.name: Lazygit
idea-plugin.description:
Bring the speed and elegance of Lazygit directly into your JetBrains IDE. No more context switching between your terminal and your editor.

✨ Zero-Config Native File Editing

Forget about writing custom bash scripts or fighting with complex $EDITOR configurations. This plugin features a custom, high-performance IPC (Inter-Process Communication) bridge. Simply press e on any file in Lazygit, and it will instantly open right in your IDE's editor. It works completely out of the box in any IntelliJ-based IDE without a single line of extra configuration.

Native integration of LazyGit directly in IntelliJ IDEs (such as IDEA, Rider, WebStorm, etc.).

This plugin is inspired by the lazygit-vscode extension. It allows you to toggle LazyGit in a full-screen editor tab, and use the e shortcut to open a file directly in the current IDE instance without any manual configuration.

Installation

  • Install the plugin from the JetBrains Marketplace.
  • Alternatively, search for "Lazygit" (by ckob) directly in your IDE via Settings -> Plugins -> Marketplace.

Usage

  • Search for the actions Lazygit: Toggle (Project Root) and Lazygit: Toggle (Current File Directory) in the IDE (Double Shift or Cmd+Shift+A).
  • Default Shortcut (Project Root): Ctrl+Alt+G (or Cmd+Option+G on macOS).
  • You can assign custom keyboard shortcuts in Settings -> Keymap.

IdeaVim Configuration

If you use IdeaVim, you can map the toggle actions in your .ideavimrc file. For example, to match LazyVim's default keybindings:

" Map <leader>gg to open LazyGit at the project root
nmap <leader>gg <Action>(Lazygit.Toggle)

" Map <leader>gG to open LazyGit at the current file's directory
nmap <leader>gG <Action>(Lazygit.ToggleCurrentDir)

Features

  • Zero Configuration: Works out of the box without any manual setup of $EDITOR or Lazygit config files.
  • Smart Routing: Files always open in the same IDE instance where Lazygit is running, even with multiple projects or IDEs open.
  • Immersive UI: Toggles LazyGit in a dedicated, full-screen editor tab rather than a tool window.
  • Re-uses existing tab: Automatically focuses the existing LazyGit tab if it's already open.
  • Native Edit: Use e to open a file (or multiple selected files via visual/select mode) in new tabs from the LazyGit window.
  • Automatic Cleanup: The editor tab closes automatically when you exit LazyGit (q).
  • Custom Configuration: Specify a custom Lazygit configuration file and executable path in Settings -> Tools -> Lazygit.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changed

  • Bumped Kotlin dependency versions and optimized Gradle platform configuration.
  • Disabled compiler-time bytecode instrumentation to resolve potential compilation failures.

idea-plugin.name: Git Branch Knife
idea-plugin.description:
Git Branch Knife — Split a Giant Git Branch into Focused PRs

Working in a monorepo? Made changes across multiple services in one branch? Git Branch Knife lets you visually split your Git branch changes into multiple focused, reviewable pull requests — one per service or module — directly inside IntelliJ IDEA.

No more giant PRs that touch 10 services at once. No more reviewers saying "this is too big to review."

The Problem It Solves

You're on feature/cross-service-update and your changes span payment-service, order-service, and auth-service. To get proper code reviews, you need three separate branches and PRs — but creating them manually is tedious and error-prone. Git Branch Knife does it in one click.

How It Works

  1. Trigger Slice by Service from the Git menu, Tools → Git Branch Knife, or right-click a branch in the Git Log.
  2. Your changed files appear in a tree on the left.
  3. Branch target cards are auto-created on the right — one per service, based on your branch-knife.paths config.
  4. Adjust assignments if needed, then click Execute Split.

Key Features

  • Visual branch splitter — See all changed files and assign them to target branches with a clear card-based UI.
  • Auto-detection — Automatically groups files by service using a simple path config file (branch-knife.paths).
  • Unassigned file tracking — Files not yet assigned to any branch are highlighted red in the left tree. Collapsed directories also turn red so nothing slips through.
  • Smart branch naming — New branches are named {current-branch}-{service}, e.g. feature/my-work-payment-service.
  • Hierarchical file tree — Files inside each card are shown as a collapsible tree, not a flat list.
  • Move all files — Bulk-move all files from one card to another in one click; the empty card is removed automatically.
  • Keyboard support — Press Delete / ⌫ to remove selected files or whole directory groups from a card.
  • Right-click context menu — Move single files or entire directories to another branch target.
  • Zero IDE restart — Edit branch-knife.paths and re-open the dialog; changes take effect immediately.
  • English / Chinese UI — Toggle language in the top-right corner of the dialog.

branch-knife.paths — Path Config Format

# path-prefix=branch-name, one rule per line
apps/payment-service=payment-service
apps/order-service=order-service
apps/auth-service=auth-service
# multiple paths → one branch:
apps/order-service/school=school-service

Files not matching any rule go into an Others card for manual assignment.

Entry Points

  • Git menu → Slice by Service…
  • Tools → Git Branch Knife → Slice by Service…
  • VCS Operations popup (Alt+`)
  • Right-click a branch in the Git Log branch panel
  • Find Action (⌘⇧A / Ctrl+Shift+A) → Slice by Service

No default shortcut — bind one in Settings → Keymap → Git Branch Knife.

idea-plugin.name: Reveal Deleted File Location
idea-plugin.description:
Helps you navigate to and inspect locally deleted or moved files in the Project view.

Context menu actions in the Commit tool window and the Git tool window's per-commit changed files list:
  • Reveal Deleted File Location — shown on a deleted file. Focuses the directory where the file used to be in the Project view.
  • Reveal Pre-Move Location — shown on a moved / renamed file. Focuses the directory the file was in before the move.
If the target directory itself no longer exists, the plugin walks up to the nearest existing ancestor directory.

Project view phantom entries — open the Project view tool window's options menu (the ⋮ three-dot button on the toolbar) and use the Reveal Deleted Files submenu to toggle:
  • Show Deleted Files — locally deleted files appear at their original location with strikethrough text. (Default: ON)
  • Show Moved Files (Pre-Move Location) — locally moved / renamed files appear at their pre-move location with italic text. (Default: ON)
The two toggles are independent. Phantom entries can be opened (Enter or double-click) to view the deleted/pre-move file content as a read-only editor, just like opening a deleted file from the Git tool window. Right-clicking a phantom entry offers a Rollback action that restores the file (or undoes the move) via the standard IDE rollback dialog.

ローカルで削除 / 移動されたファイルを「プロジェクト」ビュー上で確認・参照しやすくします。

コンテキストメニュー(「コミット」ツールウィンドウ、および「Git」ツールウィンドウのコミットごとの変更ファイル一覧):
  • Reveal Deleted File Location(削除ファイル向け): 元々存在していたディレクトリを 「プロジェクト」ビューでフォーカスします。
  • Reveal Pre-Move Location(移動 / リネームされたファイル向け): 移動前に存在していた ディレクトリを「プロジェクト」ビューでフォーカスします。
対象のディレクトリ自体も既に削除されていた場合は、存在している最も近い祖先ディレクトリまで 遡ってフォーカスします。

プロジェクトビュー上の擬似エントリ表示 — 「プロジェクト」ツールウィンドウのツールバー 右上にある ⋮(3 点リーダー)ボタンから Reveal Deleted Files サブメニューを開いて 以下を切り替えできます。
  • Show Deleted Files: ローカルで削除されたファイルを、元あった場所に取り消し線付きで表示します。 (デフォルト: ON)
  • Show Moved Files (Pre-Move Location): ローカルで移動 / リネームされたファイルを、 移動前の場所に斜体で表示します。(デフォルト: ON)
2 つのトグルは独立に切り替えられます。擬似エントリは Enter キーまたはダブルクリックで開くことができ、 Git ツールウィンドウから削除ファイルを開いたときと同様に、削除前 / 移動前のファイル内容が 読み取り専用エディタで表示されます。擬似エントリを右クリックすると Rollback メニューが表示され、 IDE 標準のロールバック確認ダイアログを通じて、削除されたファイルを復元したり、移動を元に戻したりできます。

Locally deleted files appear with strikethrough text at their original location; moved / renamed files appear with italic text at their pre-move location. The two toggles are independent and both ON by default.
  • Phantom entries can be opened (Enter or double-click) to view the deleted / pre-move file content as a read-only editor.

idea-plugin.name: CopyShortRevisionNumber
idea-plugin.description:
Adds short-revision and GitHub link copy actions to context menus.

  • Copy Short Revision Number — in the Git Log context menu, copies the abbreviated hash of the selected commit(s).
  • Copy URL(Short Revision Number) — in the Git Log context menu, copies the GitHub commit URL using the short revision hash (https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/commit/<short>).
  • GitHub Repository URL(Short Revision) — in Copy Path/Reference… and the editor's Copy / Paste Special submenu, copies the GitHub URL of the selected file or directory at the current commit (https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob/<short>/<path>). Includes #L<n> / #L<n>-L<m> when invoked from the editor.

Hash abbreviation modes:

  • Unique shortest (git rev-parse --short) — default
  • Fixed length — user-specified length (1–40 characters)

GitHub link actions are hidden when the repository has no github.com remote. Configure the abbreviation mode under Settings → Tools → Copy Short Revision Number.



短縮リビジョンと GitHub リンクをコピーするアクションをコンテキストメニューに追加します。

  • Copy Short Revision Number — Git ログメニューから、選択コミットの短縮ハッシュをコピー。
  • Copy URL(Short Revision Number) — Git ログメニューから、短縮ハッシュを使った GitHub コミット URL をコピー （https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/commit/<short>）。
  • GitHub Repository URL(Short Revision) — パス/参照のコピー およびエディタの Copy / Paste Special サブメニューから、選択ファイル/ディレクトリの現在コミットでの GitHub URL をコピー （https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob/<short>/<path>）。 エディタから呼んだ場合は #L<n> / #L<n>-L<m> を付与。

ハッシュ短縮モード:

  • Unique shortest（git rev-parse --short）— デフォルト
  • Fixed length — ユーザー指定の長さ（1〜40 文字）

GitHub リンク系アクションは github.com の remote が無い場合は非表示になります。 短縮モードは Settings → Tools → Copy Short Revision Number から設定できます。
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.2.0

  • Add Copy Short Revision Number to the Git Log branches popup (under the Checkout group) — copies the abbreviated hash of the selected branch, tag, or HEAD (Current Branch).

Git Prefix Committer

A simple tool to generate Git commands with a customizable prefix directly from the Commit tool window.
