idea-plugin.name: Pre-Push Compilation Checker
idea-plugin.description:
Blocks git pushes when your code has compilation errors — before they reach the remote.

How it works

  • One push guard: IntelliJ, terminal, and GUI Git clients all use the same managed pre-push hook. When IntelliJ is open, the hook uses its incremental compiler without opening a modal pre-push dialog.
  • Strict A/B preflight: When enabled, the plugin escalates only risky pushes to exact pushed-snapshot validation, so local-only dependent changes cannot silently hide a compile failure in the pushed commits. A symbolic check (git diff HEAD of unpushed local files vs. HEAD content of pushed files) catches A/B mismatches in milliseconds without invoking a build.
  • Silent success / failure-only UI: A clean check continues the original Git push silently. Confirmed errors block it and produce one notification linked to the navigable Compilation Checker tool window.
  • Terminal Push Guard: On project open, the plugin installs a managed pre-push Git hook that reuses the running IDE compiler when available, then falls back to a fast Gradle or Maven compile before allowing any push from a terminal or external git client. The fallback path builds a temporary detached HEAD worktree so old project output and local-only files cannot affect the result.

Important: The plugin is a local preflight. Required Merge Request CI with branch protection should remain the authoritative gate before changes reach main/master.

Features

  • Smart compile scope — changed modules plus dependent modules by default, project-level when necessary
  • IDE problem check — revalidates stale classpath/output diagnostics with at most one clean rebuild
  • Navigable error tool window — double-click any error to jump to the source file
  • Compilation Checker tool window — side panel showing errors with file navigation
  • Gradle (wrapper or system) and Maven (wrapper or system) support
  • Optional stash fallback for strict A/B validation when detached worktrees are unavailable
  • Respects PRE_PUSH_CHECKER_COMMAND env variable for custom check commands

AI Commit Message Generator (new in 1.8.0)

Generate a commit message from your staged diff with one click — from the Git Commit dialog toolbar or the Compilation Checker tool window. The button greys out automatically when there are no changes.

  • 9 providers: JetBrains AI, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, Codex (ChatGPT account), GitHub Copilot, Claude CLI, llm CLI
  • Codex (ChatGPT Account): reads ~/.codex/auth.json — sign in once with the Codex desktop app, no API key needed
  • Custom rules: Conventional Commits, max length, ticket prefix, language, scope, extra instructions
  • Team rules file: commit .github/commit-instructions.md to share prompt rules with your whole team
  • API keys in PasswordSafe — never written to plain XML state

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2023.3 or later
  • Java 17+
  • Java or Kotlin (JVM) project
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2.3.3 — Hook broken-pipe and tool window layout fixes

  • The pre-push hook no longer prints printf: write error: Broken pipe on pushes with large change lists.
  • Tool window settings rows no longer wrap and overlap in narrow windows.
  • Toolbar, bypass bar and footer no longer stretch or overlap; long text is clipped.

2.3.2 — Reliable hook install on first install

  • The pre-push hook is installed reliably right after the plugin is installed: installation waits for IntelliJ to register the project's Git repositories, so nested and multi-root repositories are no longer skipped.
  • New Pre-push hook not installed notification with an Install Pre-Push Hook button when the hook could not be installed.
  • Concurrent repairs are serialised and hook files are written atomically, preventing half-written or duplicated hooks.
  • Git queries use IntelliJ's configured Git executable, so core.hooksPath is honoured when the IDE has a minimal PATH.
  • Linked worktrees fall back to the main repository's hooks directory.
  • "Recheck / Repair Git Hooks" covers every Git root of the project.
  • Healthy hooks are no longer rewritten on every repository change.

2.3.1 — Process timeout and cancellation fixes

  • Subprocess timeouts include stdin writes, preventing hangs when a command does not consume large input.
  • Cancellation, timeout, and I/O failures terminate subprocess descendants and release streams instead of leaving commands and I/O workers behind.
  • Original subprocess I/O errors are preserved for clearer diagnostics.
  • JSON parsing preserves numeric types and rejects malformed numbers and unescaped control characters; control-character escaping avoids per-character formatter allocation.

2.3.0 — Security hardening and performance

Security

  • Authenticated IDE compiler server. The loopback server now requires a random per-session token. The token is written to the owner-only server.port file (line 2) and sent by the managed hook, so other local processes can no longer trigger compiles. Hooks are refreshed automatically on project open; older hooks fall back to the build tool.
  • Bounded requests. Request lines and header counts are capped, and client connections use a bounded thread pool, so a misbehaving local client cannot exhaust memory or threads.
  • Path scoping. Paths outside the project and its git roots are ignored.
  • Captured process output is capped at 8 MB per stream.
  • Gemini API key is sent in the x-goog-api-key header instead of the URL query string, so it cannot leak through URLs in logs or exceptions.

Performance

  • Process output is streamed into a capped buffer rather than read fully into memory, and the server no longer spawns an unbounded thread per connection.

2.2.0 — Bypass switch and tool window redesign

Changed

  • Bypass is now an on/off switch. The one-shot "Force Next Push" toolbar button is replaced by a Bypass push check switch at the top of the tool window. While on, every push skips the compilation check. It turns itself off after 1 hour (with a notification) and is always off when the IDE starts. The tool window icon shows a warning badge while the bypass is on.
  • Redesigned tool window. Settings and results sit in a resizable split, and settings can be hidden with the gear button. Settings are grouped into Validation, Commit SHA and Ignored Files, with shorter labels and ? help icons instead of truncated text.
  • Ignored files list. Uses a standard list with add, remove and search buttons. Rows show the file name with its folder dimmed; hover for the full path.
  • Clearer results. Errors show the file name in bold. Failures of the check itself (for example a timeout) get a warning icon and are not counted as compile errors. The footer shows a status icon and when the list last changed.
  • New Clear Results toolbar action.

2.1.1 — Fixed ignore rules not suppressing pushes

Fixed

  • Ignored files could still block a push. The always-blocking guard matched the word "exception" anywhere in a diagnostic, including the file path — so files such as PaymentException.java, or any error whose message mentioned a checked exception, stayed blocking even after being added to the ignore list. The guard now inspects only the message body for real compiler-infrastructure failures (internal compiler errors, OOM, stack overflow, aborted/timed-out builds), and the terminal-hook fallback was updated to match so IDE and build-tool verdicts agree.
  • "Add Files…" browsed the whole filesystem. The picker now opens scoped to the project and git roots and only lists compilable source files, so files outside the project or of the wrong type can no longer be selected only to be silently rejected. A rejected file now shows a warning instead of failing silently.
  • New "Search…" option. Find a project file by name instead of browsing a tree when adding an ignore rule.

2.1.0 — Exact-file compilation ignore controls

  • Local exact-file controls. Add files or ignore a selected navigable error, then enable, disable, or remove each project-relative entry in the tool window.
  • Consistent verdicts. IDE, Gradle, Maven, Kotlin, detached snapshot, macOS, and multi-root diagnostic paths use one matcher; terminal hooks receive synchronized state.
  • Fail-safe filtering. Only errors attributed to enabled files are ignored. Unknown, pathless, build/plugin, timeout, aborted, and infrastructure failures block.
  • Faster ignored-only checks. Ignored-only IDE results skip recovery rebuild.

Warning: Ignored files weaken local push validation. Keep required CI and branch protection enabled.

2.0.5 — Fast non-modal push validation

Fixed

  • No editor-blocking push popup. IntelliJ now uses the same managed Git hook as terminal and GUI clients; successful checks stay in the native background push task.
  • No duplicate or stale verdict reuse. Completed success caches were removed. Only identical callers waiting for the same active validation share work.
  • Automatic false-error recovery. Any failed incremental JPS check receives exactly one clean project rebuild before errors are published.
  • Branch-safe diagnostics. Repository or file changes during validation cause a retry result, and successful checks or branch changes clear old tool-window errors.
  • Reliable startup. Dynamic plugin loading starts the compiler server, log listener, and hook repair for every open Git root.

2.0.4 — Reliable bounded compilation recovery

Fixed

  • No stale failed verdicts. Failed IDE and hook results are shared only by callers waiting for the same active validation; later pushes run a fresh check. Exact clean results expire after 60 seconds.
  • One authoritative JPS recovery. Incremental checks rebuild the project once only for conservative stale classpath/output signatures. Ordinary source errors stop after the first compiler invocation.
  • Clean external snapshots. Build-tool fallback runs in a detached HEAD worktree, so old target/build output cannot create false package or annotation errors.
  • Bounded compiler waits. A missing JPS callback times out without occupying the shared validation worker indefinitely.

Performance

  • Maven keeps the parallel -T1C fast path and retries once sequentially with clean only for likely stale/reactor failures.

2.0.3 — Automatic stale-error recovery

Fixed

  • No manual recompilation for false errors. A failed incremental IDE check now triggers one forced project compile before the push is blocked. IntelliJ, terminal, and GUI Git-client pushes report and cache only the forced compile's final result, while clean incremental checks remain fast and single-flight validation is preserved.

2.0.2 — Single-flight push validation

Fixed

  • No duplicate builds from concurrent pushes. IntelliJ, terminal, and GUI Git-client pushes now share one snapshot-aware validation. Matching pushes wait for the active build and receive the same result.
  • No manual IntelliJ push retry. The original IntelliJ push now waits for validation and continues or aborts automatically instead of stopping for a background build and requiring another push.
  • Single-flight Maven and Gradle fallback. Generated hooks coordinate through a process-safe repository lock and atomically published result when the IDE compiler is unavailable.

Changed

  • Different snapshots wait for the active validation, reuse it only when the result safely covers the new push, and otherwise start one necessary follow-up check.
  • Validation waits are capped at 300 seconds and fail safely on timeout, cancellation, or compiler infrastructure errors.

2.0.1 — Reliable Git hook lifecycle

Fixed

  • Immediate hook installation after install/reinstall. Dynamically loading the plugin now repairs hooks for projects that are already open instead of waiting for a project reopen or manual Repair Hooks action.
  • Ownership-safe hook cleanup. The shared pre-push integration now uses an explicit BEGIN/END block. Disable and uninstall remove only that block and the dedicated managed hook, preserving hook logic created by users or other tools.
  • Legacy hook migration. Repair and uninstall recognize hooks written by older plugin versions, remove duplicate legacy snippets, and retain unrelated hook logic.

2.0.0 — Thread-safe startup and lighter recovery

Fixed

  • IntelliJ 2026.2 read-access assertion during project startup. Blocking hook installation, external-log loading, and local-server startup now run on the coroutine I/O dispatcher. Project SDK lookup is protected by an explicit IntelliJ read action, so startup no longer accesses project model state from a background worker without read access.

Changed

  • Lighter stale-error recovery. Failed scoped checks retry once with IntelliJ's incremental Build Project operation instead of forcing a full project compilation. Only the retry's final result can block the push.

1.9.9 — Push-only compilation

Fixed

  • Unexpected builds after edits. The plugin no longer starts IntelliJ compiler runs on source saves, Git repository changes, or project startup. Compilation now runs only for an explicit build or a pre-push validation, avoiding duplicate builds and transient JPS classpath diagnostics while editing.
  • Lighter stale-error recovery. Failed scoped checks now retry once with IntelliJ's incremental Build Project operation instead of forcing a full project-scope compilation. Only the retry's final result can block the push.

Performance

  • Single-flight external validation. Concurrent terminal and GUI-client push checks now share one fair per-project compiler flow and reuse its fresh result, preventing duplicate JPS builds.
  • Faster subprocess handling. Git stdout and stderr drain concurrently on dedicated daemon threads, preventing large output from stalling validation or consuming IntelliJ's shared common-pool workers.
  • Less path work. Duplicate changed-source paths are normalized and resolved once per external request.

1.9.8 — Stale-compiler recovery

Fixed

  • Stale JPS classpath/output errors blocking pushes. A failed incremental compile now triggers one project-wide recovery build before the error dialog appears. Clean recovery clears stale missing-package, missing-symbol, and dependency-classpath diagnostics across IDE and external Git pushes.

1.9.7 — Post-rebase SHA refresh and stale problem-cache fix

Fixed

  • SHA copied before rebase completed. After Commit now keeps watching HEAD for up to 10 seconds and recopies each new stable revision, so the final rebased commit SHA reaches the clipboard.
  • False push blocks from stale IntelliJ problem cache. Pre-push validation now recompiles files flagged by IntelliJ's problem cache and blocks only when the current compiler reports errors. Stale missing-package warnings are ignored after a clean compile.

1.9.5 — Stable post-commit SHA capture

Fixed

  • Wrong SHA copied during multi-step Git updates. After Commit now waits for three consecutive identical HEAD reads before copying, so transient parent or intermediate revisions are ignored.

1.9.4 — Clipboard SHA race and AI generation UI fix

Fixed

  • Wrong commit SHA after a branch switch. After Commit clipboard processing now captures the exact post-commit repository revision before background work starts, preventing a delayed task from reading the next branch's HEAD.

Changed

  • AI generation progress state. The generator action shows a stop icon and prevents duplicate clicks while an AI request is running, then restores the generator icon when complete.

1.9.3 — Nested-repo clipboard SHA regression fix

Fixed

  • Parent repo shadowed the nested repo when copying the SHA. The 1.9.2 root-lookup refactor appended every panel fallback root after the committed files, so in a nested-repository layout the enclosing parent repository could still be probed for HEAD and win over the nested repository that owns the commit — reintroducing the wrong-SHA symptom. The fallback roots are now reduced to the deepest/most-nested root that owns each committed file (never the full root set), so a nested repository is never shadowed by its parent.

Changed

  • Cleaned up CommitShaClipboardCheckinHandler: deepest-first root ordering factored into a single shared helper and the lookup-ordering Javadoc consolidated.

Tests

  • Reconciled the two preferredRepositoryLookupLocations regression tests in CommitShaClipboardCheckinHandlerTest with the sound deepest-owning-repository behaviour; the full suite is green again.

1.9.2 — Clipboard SHA nested-repo regression fix

Fixed

  • Wrong commit SHA copied in nested-repo layouts. The clipboard path could resolve a parent repository instead of the exact repository that owns the committed or pushed files, so the copied SHA could come from the wrong Git root. After Push now prefers the pushed tip directly from the push payload, and both clipboard paths keep their repository lookup scoped to the exact repository root before falling back to a raw path.

Tests

  • Added regression coverage for nested repository root selection in CommitShaClipboardCheckinHandlerTest.

1.9.1 — Branch prefix & commit-SHA correctness via IntelliJ Git integration

Fixed

  • Branch-wise prefix convention not followed (regression). The AI commit message generator resolved the current branch by shelling out to git against project.getBasePath() first, only consulting IntelliJ's Git integration as a fallback. In multi-root projects — or whenever the project base path is not the repository root that owns the staged changes — this returned the wrong or a stale branch, so the rules-file branch gate selected the wrong prefix (while GitHub Copilot, which reads the IDE's live branch, worked correctly with the same .md). Branch resolution now consults IntelliJ's GitRepositoryManager → GitRepository.getCurrentBranch() (the live, authoritative repository model that watches .git/HEAD) as the primary source for every repo root, falling back to a git subprocess only when the model is not populated (detached HEAD, non-git4idea/test contexts). No branch names or prefixes are hardcoded — the rules file still drives every decision, repository-agnostically.
  • Incorrect commit SHA copied to clipboard. The clipboard read HEAD from the raw commit.getRoot() / panel-root path, which can point at a submodule directory or an unrelated root in multi-root layouts, so the copied id was not the commit git actually created. Every committed/pushed root is now mapped to its enclosing repository via IntelliJ's Git integration (getRepositoryForRootQuick / getRepositoryForFileQuick) before the authoritative git rev-parse HEAD is run against that repository's canonical root. Applies to both the After Commit and After Push triggers.

1.8.9 — Default-branch gate fix for ISSUEFIX:

Fixed

  • ISSUEFIX: not applied on the default branch. 1.8.8 resolved the default branch only from git (origin/HEAD). When origin/HEAD is unset locally, or the team's default branch name does not match it, the gate wrongly classified the real default branch as non-default and suppressed ISSUEFIX: on it. Added an explicit Default branch (rules gate) setting under Settings → AI Commit Message Generator: when set it is authoritative, so ISSUEFIX:/DOCS: are allowed on that branch and forbidden on every other branch, exactly per the rules file. Auto-detection (now also using init.defaultBranch) is used only when the field is blank, and when nothing can be resolved the plugin no longer asserts a wrong verdict — it asks the model to run Step 0 itself. Branch comparison is case-insensitive and tolerant of refs/heads//origin/ prefixes.

1.8.8 — Branch-rule & commit-SHA correctness fixes

Fixed

  • Branch-specific commit rules applied inconsistently. The branch gate in a team rules file (e.g. .github/git-commit-instructions.md) relied entirely on the AI running git branch --show-current and guessing whether the current branch was the repository default — so the prefix (ISSUEFIX: vs METHOD_ENTRY:/TESTCASE:) applied on some branches but not others. The plugin now resolves the current branch AND the repository default branch (git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD) in code, and injects a concrete default / non-default verdict into the prompt so the branch gate is deterministic instead of guessed.
  • .github/git-commit-instructions.md not auto-detected. Added it to the default rules-file candidate list (previously only .github/commit-instructions.md and COMMIT_RULES.md were auto-detected).
  • YAML front-matter leaked into the AI prompt. A leading --- apply: always --- block is now stripped from the rules file before it is sent to the model; --- horizontal rules in the body are preserved.
  • Wrong commit SHA copied (After Push). The pushed tip was chosen by the highest committer timestamp, which is not the branch head after a rebase/amend/cherry-pick (commit dates are not monotonic with DAG order). The tip is now selected topologically — the commit that is not a parent of any other commit in the push set — with the timestamp heuristic kept only as a fallback when no unique tip exists.
  • Stale/parent SHA copied (After Commit). Switched the primary source to a synchronous git rev-parse HEAD subprocess (run after the commit is written) instead of git4idea's asynchronous repo.update() refresh, which could return the pre-commit (parent) revision. The git4idea model and base-path lookups are retained as ordered fallbacks.

1.8.7 — Fix wrong SHA copied to clipboard

Fixed

  • Wrong SHA copied after push (After Push trigger). The previous code called git rev-parse HEAD via commit.getRoot(). When a push includes submodule-update commits their root resolves to the submodule directory, so HEAD there is the submodule tip rather than the commit the user actually pushed. Fixed by reading the SHA directly from VcsFullCommitDetails.getId() (the commit with the highest timestamp in the push set), with the git-subprocess path retained as a fallback.
  • Stale or wrong SHA copied after commit (After Commit trigger). The previous code relied solely on a bare git rev-parse HEAD subprocess, which could return a pre-commit cached value on some systems or pick the wrong repository in multi-root projects. Fixed by using GitRepositoryManager → repo.update() → getCurrentRevision() as the primary path (forces a fresh read of .git/HEAD through git4idea's model), with the subprocess and project.getBasePath() retained as ordered fallbacks.

1.8.6 — Settings panel: Copy-on row moved to its own line

Improved

  • Settings panel layout. The "Copy on: ● After push ○ After commit" row now appears on its own line beneath "Format: ● Full ○ Short", instead of being placed to the right of the Format row. This prevents the sub-panel from wrapping or getting cut off on narrower tool-window widths.

1.8.5 — Auto-copy SHA reliability fix & settings panel alignment

Fixed

  • Auto-copy SHA not working on macOS (After Commit). CheckinProjectPanel.getRoots() was called from a background thread inside executeOnPooledThread. On macOS, AWT's threading model is stricter and this caused getRoots() to return an empty or invalid result, so the HEAD SHA was never resolved and nothing was copied to the clipboard. The roots are now captured on the EDT (where checkinSuccessful() is invoked) before dispatching to the background thread.
  • Auto-copy SHA not working on macOS (After Push) — edge-case fallback. When PushInfo.getCommits() returns commits without a resolvable VirtualFile root (certain force-push or empty-push scenarios), the SHA lookup fell through with a null result. A fallback to project.getBasePath() now covers these cases.
  • Settings panel: Format / Copy-on sub-row alignment. The "Format: … Copy on: …" row below the clipboard checkbox was misaligned in the tool window. In a BoxLayout Y_AXIS container the row's default CENTER_ALIGNMENT conflicted with the checkboxes' LEFT_ALIGNMENT, causing the row to shift right. Fixed by explicitly setting LEFT_ALIGNMENT on the sub-panel.

1.8.4 — Configurable clipboard SHA settings

Added

  • SHA format choice: the Compilation Checker settings panel now has Full SHA (40 chars) / Short SHA (7 chars) radio buttons so you can choose which form is copied to the clipboard.
  • Copy trigger choice: After Push (previous default) or After Commit — when set to "After Commit", the SHA is copied immediately after a successful IDE commit, before the push step.
  • Enable / disable toggle: a new "Copy commit SHA to clipboard automatically" checkbox lets you turn the whole feature off without losing your format/trigger preferences.

1.8.3 — Copy commit SHA to clipboard after push

Added

  • Commit SHA auto-copied to clipboard. Every time the pre-push check passes and the push is allowed, the full 40-character HEAD commit SHA is automatically written to the system clipboard. A balloon notification "Commit SHA Copied" confirms the action — the SHA is ready to paste immediately (PR description, ticket, Slack, etc.).

1.8.1 — Stability & API compatibility fixes

Added

  • ChatGPT browser OAuth device sign-in. The Codex settings card now has Sign In, Sign Out, and Refresh actions backed by a full OAuth 2.0 device-authorization flow. The browser opens for code approval, the plugin polls for the token in the background, and the result is stored in PasswordSafe.
  • CLI auth status labels. The settings cards for GitHub Copilot, llm CLI, and Claude CLI now show a live auth/availability status so you can confirm a provider is ready without leaving the IDE.

Fixed

  • Multi-repo diff collection: AI commit prompts now gather diffs from all Git roots (staged → unstaged → HEAD), fixing blank messages in multi-root projects and mono-repos with sub-modules.
  • EDT freeze on Codex auth refresh: auth-file reads and status checks moved to a background thread; label updates on the EDT.
  • Browse listener wiring for the rules-file picker — path was not populated in some IDE versions.
  • Commit control ClassCastException in the Git Commit dialog on recent platform builds.
  • OAuth browser launch now works on Linux and older macOS JDKs via xdg-open / open fallbacks.

Changed

  • Commit message injection uses the stable CommitWorkflowUi API.
  • AI plugin detection uses PluginManagerCore class-loader check instead of the deprecated isEnabled(), eliminating false "not available" warnings on current IDE versions.
  • OAuth token-refresh retry removed — stale token now fails fast and prompts re-authentication.

1.8.0 — AI Commit Message Generator

New feature: AI Commit Message Generator

Generates a ready-to-use git commit message from staged (or HEAD) diffs with one click. Accessible from the ⚡ button in the Compilation Checker tool window and from the Git Commit dialog toolbar (same row as the Copilot button). The button is greyed out automatically when there are no staged or local changes.

Nine AI providers

  • JetBrains AI — uses the AI Assistant plugin when installed (optional soft dependency).
  • OpenAI — calls gpt-4o (or any configured model) via API key.
  • Anthropic — calls Claude 3.5 Sonnet via API key.
  • Google Gemini — calls Gemini 1.5 Flash via API key.
  • Ollama — local model at localhost:11434, no key needed.
  • Codex (ChatGPT Account) — reads ~/.codex/auth.json written by the Codex desktop app. No API key required; sign in once with your ChatGPT account in the Codex app and the plugin uses that session automatically.
  • GitHub Copilot — calls the Copilot Chat API using gh auth token. Requires GitHub CLI and an active Copilot subscription.
  • Claude CLI — reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from your shell environment or PasswordSafe and calls the Anthropic API directly.
  • llm CLI — wraps Simon Willison's llm tool (60+ model providers via plugins). Install with pip install llm.

Custom commit message rules

  • Conventional Commits format (feat:, fix:, …)
  • Max subject line length, prefix/ticket template, language/tone
  • Auto-detect scope from changed file paths
  • Free-form extra instructions appended to every prompt

Project-level rules file

Place .github/commit-instructions.md (or COMMIT_RULES.md) in the project root and commit it — the plugin appends it to the AI prompt automatically so the whole team shares the same conventions. The Settings page has a file browser with project-relative path storage and a live exists/missing status label.

Settings page

Settings → Tools → Pre-Push Checker — AI Commit Message Generator: per-provider auth, auto-detect buttons, Codex live sign-in status, Test Connection, model overrides, and all rule options. API keys stored in PasswordSafe.

Security fix

Shell injection guard reinstated in CliPathResolver: only bare executable names matching [A-Za-z0-9._+-]+ are passed into sh -c scripts, blocking injection via user-controlled Settings values.

Bug fixes

  • CLI auto-detection: sources shell rc files and probes Homebrew, npm-global, asdf, pip, Cargo — fixes "tool not found" when IntelliJ has a stripped GUI PATH.
  • Codex infinite hang: dropped the PTY subprocess approach; now calls OpenAI API directly using the ChatGPT OAuth token from ~/.codex/auth.json.
  • node: No such file or directory: shell-augmented PATH is now injected into all CLI subprocess environments.

1.7.2

  • Consistent .kts handling: Kotlin script files are now recognized as compilable sources across both the in-IDE push handler and the external loopback server, matching the existing behaviour of the loopback server's file resolver. Build scripts such as build.gradle.kts and settings.gradle.kts remain classified as build files and continue to escalate to a project compile.
  • Stricter loopback protocol: the per-project pre-push server now requires an exact CHECK request instead of any line starting with CHECK, rejecting malformed or unexpected client traffic with a clear ERR unknown-request reply.
  • No more leaked snapshot subprocesses on cancel: when the user cancels a strict A/B snapshot validation mid-build (or any unexpected error occurs while waiting for git / Gradle / Maven), the spawned process is force-destroyed before the exception propagates, preventing background Gradle/Maven processes from outliving the cancelled check.
  • Atomic port-file writes: the loopback server's server.port file is now written via a temp file and atomic rename, so concurrent hook reads can never observe a zero-byte or partially-written port and silently fall back to the build-tool path.
  • External hook log fingerprint cache no longer leaks across project open/close cycles: the static dedup map (used to avoid re-parsing the same hook log on repeated VFS events) now drops its entry when the project is disposed.

1.7.1

  • Dedicated repair-hook icon: the Compilation Checker tool window now uses a plugin-specific repair icon for the Recheck / Repair Git Hooks action instead of the generic refresh icon.
  • Stale build-output retry: if external Maven/Gradle fallback reports bad class file / NoSuchFileException errors from target/classes, target/test-classes, or build/classes, the hook refreshes generated class output and retries once before blocking so the cached log reflects the updated compile result.

1.7.0

  • Hook repair action: the Compilation Checker tool window can repair and normalize managed Git hooks from the IDE, restoring missing or stale hook wiring without a manual reinstall.
  • Improved core.hooksPath handling: hook installation, repair, exclude cleanup, and current-state inspection now resolve custom hook directories and shared git directories more reliably, including canonical path comparisons for symlinked hook locations.

1.6.0

  • Clean-commit ledger: a successful compile now records the verified HEAD SHA. After a rebase, merge, or pull that fast-forwards onto an already-verified upstream commit, the pre-push handler reuses the cached clean verdict instead of recompiling. Backed by a new GitOperations utility that inspects local git state (HEAD SHA, merge/rebase-in-progress, upstream tracking) without invoking external git for every check.
  • Optional pre-compile rebase advisory: when enabled (prepushchecker.rebasePrecheck.enabled, off by default), the plugin fetches each push root before scheduling the compile and prompts the user to rebase first if the remote is ahead. Ensures the build runs against the integrated tree so locally-clean-but-remotely-stale pushes do not surprise CI. Off by default because every push would otherwise pay a network round-trip.
  • Repo-change-driven warmup compile: branch switches, fetches, pulls, and rebases now trigger a debounced background project compile (30s cooldown absorbs bursts of state-change events from a single git operation). The compiler cache is hot for the integrated tree by the time the user pushes, turning most post-VCS-operation pushes into no-ops.

1.5.3

  • Generated getter/setter/builder false positives fixed: when terminal, force-push, or GUI git client fallback compilation reports only generated-style get*, set*, is*, or *Builder missing-symbol errors, the hook now retries once with full compile scope before treating the output as a non-blocking generated-symbol false positive. This avoids the common “first push fails, second push succeeds” flow.
  • Force Push retry fixed: the plugin's force-push action now writes the one-shot bypass token before running git push --force-with-lease, so the retry is not blocked again by the managed pre-push hook.

1.5.2

  • First-time warmup compile: on the first project open after plugin install, a full background compile now runs automatically once indexing finishes. This primes the compiler cache so the first push from a terminal or GUI git client (Sublime Merge, SourceTree, GitHub Desktop) immediately reuses IntelliJ's incremental result instead of falling back to Maven/Gradle with a cold cache. Subsequent opens are unaffected.

1.5.1

  • External push race fix (Sublime Merge / terminal): the managed hook now waits longer for IntelliJ's local compiler socket before falling back to Maven/Gradle, preventing first-attempt false failures that succeeded on immediate retry.
  • Generated-symbol fallback rescue: when build-tool fallback reports getter/setter-style generated symbol errors (get*, set*, is*) and IntelliJ is running, the hook retries IntelliJ incremental compile once before aborting the push.
  • Explicit fallback diagnostics: hook logs now include the reason IntelliJ incremental compile was unavailable, so external push failures are easier to debug from .idea/pre-push-checker/last-run.log.
  • Proactive uninstall cleanup: the plugin now tracks managed repos and cleans their managed hook/cache/exclude artifacts during uninstall, including repos that are not currently open in the IDE.

1.5.0

  • Self-cleanup on uninstall: when the plugin is uninstalled, a global marker (~/.prepush-checker/installed) is removed. Orphaned hooks in repos that were not open during uninstall now detect the missing marker on the next push and automatically remove themselves, the managed hook script, the cache directory, and the .git/info/exclude block. No manual cleanup needed.
  • Push Anyway (IDE): the compilation error dialog now includes a Push Anyway button in both the synchronous (cached errors, IDE problems) and background compilation paths. A one-shot bypass token is written so the git hook also allows the push through.
  • Force Next Push (terminal / Sublime Merge / external clients): a new toggle action in the Compilation Checker toolbar lets users skip the compilation check for the next push attempt. The bypass is single-use (consumed on the next push) and expires after 1 hour to prevent stale flags.
  • Settings panel reorganized: checkboxes are now grouped under a titled “Settings” border for a cleaner, more organized look.

1.4.6

  • External hook now waits for a running IntelliJ before fallback: when the first IDE socket probe fails, the managed pre-push hook now detects an active IntelliJ process and retries the IDE compile request for a short window before dropping to Gradle/Maven fallback. This reduces false fallback usage when the IDE is running in the background and the loopback service is still initializing.
  • Fallback compile cache for unchanged HEAD: when IntelliJ is unavailable and the hook uses build-tool fallback, successful results are now reused for identical HEAD + compile mode (main/test/all). Repeated pushes without new commits avoid redundant backend compiles while preserving existing failure behavior.

1.4.5

  • External IntelliJ fast-path false positives fixed: terminal, Sublime Merge, and other external git clients no longer block pushes from stale IntelliJ editor problem-cache entries. The loopback server now reuses only cached successful compile verdicts; cached failures are rechecked with CompilerManager.make before the hook reports an error. This prevents stale generated-symbol failures for Lombok-style getters, setters, and builders from persisting until the user manually runs the IntelliJ compilation check. If the external fast-path's scoped make still reports errors, it now retries once with the same project-scope make used by the tool-window compilation check before blocking the push.

1.4.4

  • Lombok ghost errors in the Maven fallback fixed: when the IDE socket is unreachable and the hook (or the in-IDE strict snapshot guard) falls back to mvn / ./mvnw, Maven's incremental compiler could re-compile a consumer against a stale target/classes copy of an @Getter / @Setter class — emitting false cannot find symbol errors (e.g. setCloseIcon, setFromSheetView, isFromSheetView) immediately after a merge that introduced new Lombok-generated members. Both Maven invocation sites now pass -Dmaven.compiler.useIncrementalCompilation=false so annotation processing always sees fresh sources. The IDE fast path (PrePushLocalServer → CompilerManager.make) was unaffected and is still used whenever IntelliJ is running.

1.4.3

  • GUI git client PATH reconstruction: the managed hook now sources the user's shell rc files (.zshenv, .zprofile, .zshrc, .bash_profile, .bashrc, .profile) and appends known install locations (/opt/homebrew/bin, SDKMAN, jenv, asdf, $MAVEN_HOME/bin, $GRADLE_HOME/bin) so that mvn and gradle resolve correctly when the hook is launched from Sublime Merge, SourceTree, GitHub Desktop, or any other GUI client that strips the user's interactive PATH. No effect on repos that ship a ./mvnw or ./gradlew wrapper.

1.4.2

  • IntelliJ 2026.1 fix: All four projectActivity entrypoints (managed pre-push hook installer, external hook log loader, local TCP server, warmup service) are now Kotlin ProjectActivity implementations that delegate to the existing Java logic. IntelliJ 2026.1 silently stopped invoking Java ProjectActivity implementations, which caused the local TCP server to never start — terminal / Sublime Merge / SourceTree pushes fell through to the raw Maven/Gradle fallback (and surfaced false "cannot find symbol" errors in projects whose Maven build relies on the IDE for Lombok-style annotation processing). After upgrading and restarting the IDE, .idea/pre-push-checker/server.port is written again and external pushes reuse IntelliJ's incremental compiler.

1.4.1

  • Marketplace compatibility cleanup: removed deprecated PerformInBackgroundOption usage from background pre-push and auto-retry tasks while preserving always-background behavior. Plugin Verifier for IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1.1 now reports the plugin as compatible without deprecated API warnings.

1.4.0

  • Symbolic A/B detection: the strict guard now scans git diff HEAD of unpushed local files for newly added method/class/field declarations and checks HEAD content of pushed files for word-boundary references. Catches the canonical A/B case (push references a symbol defined only in an unpushed local edit) instantly, without invoking a build.
  • macOS path normalization: snapshot output now strips both /var/folders/... and /private/var/folders/... forms so filterSnapshotErrors retains errors actually in pushed files.
  • Auto-retry push on success: when the background pre-push check passes, the plugin runs git push per repository root with non-interactive credentials (GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0), /dev/null stdin, and a 120s timeout. Per-push elapsed-ms is logged to idea.log.
  • Failure-choice dialog: when errors are found, a modal dialog offers Reset Commit (soft-reset the pushed commits, keep changes), Push Anyway, Leave Commit, or Cancel.
  • HEAD-snapshot stash in the external pre-push hook fallback: when the IDE socket is unreachable, the hook stashes the working tree before running Gradle/Maven so the build sees only HEAD content; an EXIT INT TERM HUP trap guarantees stash pop on any interrupt. Closes the A/B coverage gap when the IDE is closed and pushes happen via terminal / Sublime Merge / GitHub Desktop.

1.3.1

  • Risk-scoped strict A/B dependency guard: the side-panel toggle now escalates only when local source/build changes can plausibly mask pushed-snapshot failures. Risky pushes are validated against committed HEAD in a clean temporary worktree; an explicit advanced stash fallback is available when worktrees cannot be created.
  • CI remains authoritative: required Merge Request CI and branch protection are documented as the non-bypassable safety net before main/master accepts changes.

1.3.0

  • External pushes reuse IntelliJ's incremental compiler: terminal and GUI-client pushes now contact a local loopback server when the IDE is open, then fall back to Gradle or Maven if IntelliJ is unavailable.
  • Zero-cost warmup path: debounced background compiles after source saves keep compiler caches hot so most pre-push checks reuse a fresh verdict.
  • Stronger dependency coverage: targeted compile scopes now include dependent modules, catching caller-side breakage without forcing full project builds for ordinary source changes.
  • Bounded error retention: compiler errors and external hook log entries are compacted, deduplicated, and truncated where needed to keep memory usage predictable.
  • Repository cleanliness: plugin-owned hook/log/cache paths are excluded via repo-local .git/info/exclude and cleaned up when the plugin is disabled or uninstalled.

1.2.0

  • External push guard (terminal, Sublime Merge, SourceTree, GitHub Desktop, etc.): hook installation now resolves the real hooks directory via git rev-parse --git-path hooks, so it works in worktrees, submodules, and repos that set core.hooksPath.
  • Stricter external check: the hook now also compiles test sources (classes testClasses / test-compile) so test-only breakage is caught.
  • Errors from external pushes surface inside IntelliJ: the hook writes a log to .idea/pre-push-checker/last-run.log. A new startup activity parses that log on project open and on every hook run, feeds errors into the Compilation Checker tool window, and raises a notification with an "Open Compilation Checker" action.
  • Managed wrapper is refreshed on every project open so hook upgrades ship automatically.

1.1.0

  • Tool window: Replaced the "Clear" action with a "Report Issue" action that opens the plugin's GitHub Issues page with a pre-populated, concise title (no large error payload stuffed into the URL).
  • Readable error list: Entries now render as FileName:line:col — message instead of the raw [full/deep/path (line, col)] message. The full entry is preserved as a tooltip on hover.
  • Navigation fix: Double-click / Enter now correctly opens the source file for entries that use the [path (line, col)] compiler format. Also supports paths containing spaces.
  • Pre-push EDT fix: Replaced ModalityState.any() with the progress indicator's modality (falling back to the default) when triggering a compilation from a background thread. Prevents "Write-unsafe context" errors during compile setup.
  • Robustness: Null-safe compiler-message formatting, exception-isolated listener fan-out in CompilationErrorService, and short-circuit when the new error list equals the previous snapshot.
  • Performance: Per-extension icon cache in the list renderer, allocation-free source-extension check in PushValidationPaths, reused StringBuilder when formatting compiler messages, and pre-sized result lists.

1.0.1

  • Fix EDT violation when triggering a compilation check from the tool window Run Check button

1.0.0 — Initial Release

  • Pre-push handler for the IntelliJ Git Push dialog
  • Smart module-level compile scope with automatic full-build fallback
  • IDE problem check using WolfTheProblemSolver before triggering a build
  • Compilation error dialog with file-type icons, navigation, and Refresh action
  • Compilation Checker tool window (right side panel)
  • Git hook installer for terminal push support (Gradle & Maven)
  • CompilationErrorService for cross-component error state sharing

idea-plugin.name: Dynamia Tasks
idea-plugin.description:
Dynamia Tasks is your developer task manager, living inside your IDE. Stop context-switching between browser tabs, issue trackers, and sticky notes. Dynamia Tasks brings all your tasks into a single, distraction-free panel right where you work — inside IntelliJ IDEA.

What it does

  • Unified task list — merges GitHub Issues, local task files, and any custom source into one clean checklist per project.
  • Task Explorer — browse, search, and cherry-pick tasks from any connector without leaving the IDE.
  • Workspace checklist — pin only the tasks you're working on now. Your personal sprint, per project.
  • Open files from tasks — jump directly to the relevant file mentioned in a task description with one click.
  • Connector system — plug in GitHub Issues out of the box, use local JSON task files, or connect any third-party tool with a custom connector.
  • Labels and filtering — keep things organised with labels, status filters, and grouping.

GitHub Issues integration

Connect any public or private GitHub repository and manage its issues directly from IntelliJ IDEA. You can view, create, edit, comment, and close issues without ever opening a browser tab.

To enable it, generate a GitHub Personal Access Token — classic token with the repo scope (add read:org too if you want to browse organization repositories), or a fine-grained token with Metadata + Issues permissions — at github.com/settings/tokens, then paste it in Settings → Dynamia Tasks → GitHub Issues → Personal Access Token. The token is stored locally on your machine and never sent to any external server.

Privacy-first, always

No cloud. No telemetry. No accounts.
Everything runs locally on your machine. Your tasks, your tokens, your data — 100% offline capable.

Get started in seconds

  1. Open a project in IntelliJ IDEA.
  2. Click the Dynamia Tasks icon in the right tool window.
  3. Add local tasks instantly — no config needed.
  4. Optionally connect GitHub Issues: go to Settings, enter your Personal Access Token and repository (e.g. owner/repo).

Built for developers who like their tools minimal, fast, and out of the way.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Added compatibility with 2026.2+ IDEs (JCEF is now an optional dependency, fixing a startup error on those versions)
  • Task descriptions and comments now render as Markdown (GitHub-flavored: tables, code blocks, task lists)
  • Clearer error notification when posting a comment fails, instead of failing silently

idea-plugin.name: Copy Git Ref Name
idea-plugin.description:
Copy Git branch, tag, and bookmark names from the VCS Log with one click.

Copy Git Ref Name adds click-to-copy behavior to Git reference labels in the VCS Log commit details panel. Hover a ref label to preview the exact text that will be copied, then click it to copy the raw ref name to the clipboard.

  • Copies branch, tag, and bookmark labels from the commit details reference panel.
  • Removes UI-only trailing commas before copying.
  • Skips collapsed labels such as "... more".
  • Does not change branches, check out refs, or modify repository state.

Copy Git Ref Name 为 VCS Log 提交详情面板中的 Git 引用标签增加点击复制能力。

鼠标悬停分支、标签或书签名称时，可以预览将要复制的内容；点击后，插件会把干净的原始 ref 名称写入剪贴板。

  • 支持从提交详情的引用区域复制分支、标签和书签名称。
  • 复制前会去掉界面展示用的尾随逗号。
  • 会跳过 "... more" 这类折叠提示标签。
  • 不会切换分支、检出 ref，也不会修改 Git 仓库状态。
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Added one-click copy support for Git ref labels in the VCS Log commit details panel.
  • Added hover tooltips that show the exact ref name to be copied.
  • Added clean text extraction for branch, tag, and bookmark labels.

中文：首个正式版本，支持在 VCS Log 提交详情面板中点击复制分支、标签和书签名称，并在复制前清理界面展示用的尾随逗号。

idea-plugin.name: Git Worktrees | GW4I
idea-plugin.description:
English

Manage linked Git worktrees from inside IntelliJ IDEA.

Git Worktrees | GW4I adds a focused Worktrees tab to the Git tool window, so you can see every linked worktree across one or many Git roots without leaving the IDE.

Highlights

  • Filter by Worktree, Branch, or Location. Narrow a large worktree list directly from the table header.
  • Sort one or more columns inside every repository group. Toggle ascending, descending, and unsorted order per column while keeping roots readable.
  • Use Speed Search with visible match highlights. Type to jump to matching rows and see matched fragments highlighted in the table.
  • Work naturally in multi-root projects. Repository rows group worktrees from console, api, android, or any other Git root in the project.
  • Keep repository context while scrolling. Long lists keep the current repository row pinned until the next repository group pushes it away.
  • Collapse repository groups when you need a tighter view. Use the chevron, double-click a repository row, or the context menu to hide or show its worktrees.
  • Open, checkout, and delete worktrees from the context menu, with Refresh kept in the toolbar.
  • Tune behavior from Settings. Configure relative locations and whether the Git tool window should restore the Worktrees tab, with global defaults plus project overrides.
  • Remove worktrees from the keyboard. Press Delete on a selected worktree row for the same remove flow as the toolbar action.
  • Keep normal Git branch workflows worktree-aware. Git Branch and Git Log branch-label menus can offer Checkout Anyway or Delete Branch / Worktree when a branch is already used by another worktree.
  • Stay oriented inside the IDE. The Git menu entry carries a subtle By GW4I marker, and the panel shows a small provider note at the toolbar edge.
  • Keep deletion responsive on Windows. Git unregisters worktrees first, then leftover non-empty directories are cleaned up as best-effort background work.
  • Spot dirty worktrees at a glance. A Dirty column shows which worktrees have uncommitted changes, highlighted in red.
  • Toggle the Worktrees tab with one click. The right-side Worktrees icon button cycles through opening VCS with the Worktrees tab, focusing it, and closing the VCS panel.

Screenshots

Header Filters

Filter each column independently. The filter is case-insensitive, and repository groups disappear when none of their worktrees match.

Column Sorting

Each sort button cycles through ascending, descending, and unsorted states. Multiple active sort buttons are applied in order inside each repository group, so roots remain readable.

Speed Search Highlighting

Use IntelliJ table Speed Search to jump through visible worktree rows, with matched fragments highlighted in place.

Multi-root Projects

Repository rows keep large projects organized. Each Git root has its own worktree rows, current worktree marker, branch names, and filesystem locations.

When the table is long, the active repository row stays visible at the top of the scroll area until the next repository group pushes it away.

Features

  • Open the Worktrees tab from the Git main menu, the Git tool window drop-down, or the right-side Worktrees icon button.
  • Click the right-side Worktrees icon button to cycle through three states: open VCS with the Worktrees tab, focus the already-open Worktrees tab, or close the VCS panel.
  • Reuse a closable Worktrees tab inside the Version Control / Git tool window; fall back to the standalone Git Worktrees tool window when needed.
  • List linked worktrees using git worktree list --porcelain.
  • Show Worktree, Branch, and Location columns.
  • Show worktree locations relative to their Git root when possible, and use absolute paths for worktrees outside that root.
  • Render the main worktree in bold and mark the currently opened worktree with a check icon.
  • Display detached worktrees as detached.
  • Show a Dirty column that marks worktrees with uncommitted changes in red.
  • Collapse or expand repository rows from the chevron, double-click, or context menu.
  • Keep the active repository row sticky while scrolling long tables, with a push-off transition when the next repository group reaches the top.
  • Keep Refresh in the toolbar and keep Checkout, Open, and Delete Worktree available in the popup.
  • Open the selected worktree as a project by double-clicking or using Open.
  • Checkout a selected worktree branch in the current repository with --ignore-other-worktrees.
  • Keep Checkout visible with an explanatory disabled hint when the selected row cannot be checked out, such as detached HEAD or the current worktree.
  • Ask before force checkout when local changes or untracked files would be overwritten.
  • Run checkout and delete operations in background tasks, then reload the panel when the operation completes.
  • Open Worktrees settings from the panel toolbar and configure global defaults or per-project overrides for relative locations and Git tab restore behavior.
  • Press Delete on a selected worktree row to trigger the same remove flow as the Delete Worktree action.
  • Delete a single worktree, or delete multiple selected worktrees in one batch.
  • Choose whether to delete only the worktree or delete both the worktree and its branch.
  • Protect main worktrees from delete actions.
  • Replace the native Git Branch checkout/delete actions only when the selected branch is already used by a linked worktree, keeping the regular Git menu behavior for ordinary branches.
  • Enhance Git Log branch-label menus so Checkout and Delete Branch actions handle linked-worktree branches, including branch names with /.
  • Resolve Git Log worktree branch conflicts from Git metadata and action data, avoiding slow full worktree listing during menu updates.
  • Mark the Worktrees tab entry with By GW4I in the Git menu and show a compact provider note in the panel toolbar.
  • Refresh each affected repository after Git operations and show success or failure notifications.
  • Defer best-effort leftover directory cleanup after single and bulk deletion, reducing visible task time on Windows.
  • Use long-path-safe cleanup for leftover Windows directories after Git has already unregistered a worktree.

Requirements

  • IntelliJ Platform IDE build 252 or newer.
  • Bundled Git plugin (Git4Idea) enabled.

中文

在 IntelliJ IDEA 里集中查看、过滤、切换和删除 Git worktree。

Git Worktrees | GW4I 会在 Git 工具窗口中加入一个专门的 Worktrees 标签页，让你不用离开 IDE，就能查看一个或多个 Git root 下的全部 linked worktree。

功能亮点

  • 按 Worktree、Branch、Location 过滤。 在表头输入关键词，就能快速收窄大量 worktree。
  • 在每个仓库分组内按一列或多列排序。 每列排序按钮支持升序、降序和取消排序，同时保持 Git root 分组清晰。
  • 支持 Speed Search 和命中高亮。 直接键入关键词即可定位匹配行，并在表格里高亮命中片段。
  • 自然支持多 root 项目。 console、api、android 等多个 Git root 会按仓库分组展示。
  • 滚动时保持仓库上下文。 长列表会把当前仓库分组行固定在顶部，直到下一个仓库分组把它推走。
  • 需要更紧凑视图时可以折叠仓库分组。 可通过左侧箭头、双击仓库行或右键菜单隐藏和展开该仓库下的 worktree。
  • 通过右键菜单打开、切换和删除 worktree，并把 Refresh 保留在工具栏。
  • 可在 Settings 中调整行为。 支持配置相对路径显示，以及 Git 工具窗口是否恢复 Worktrees 标签页，并区分全局默认值和项目覆盖。
  • 支持键盘删除 worktree。 选中 worktree 行后按 Delete，即可触发与工具栏删除动作一致的流程。
  • 让常用 Git 分支流程感知 worktree。 当分支已被另一个 worktree 使用时，Git Branch 菜单和 Git Log 分支标签菜单会提供 Checkout Anyway 或 Delete Branch / Worktree。
  • 在 IDE 里清楚标识来源。 Git 菜单入口会显示轻量的 By GW4I 标记，面板工具栏边缘也会显示简洁的来源说明。
  • 让 Windows 下的删除操作保持响应。 先完成 Git unregister，再把残留的非空目录放到后台尽力清理。
  • 一眼识别有未提交变更的 worktree。 Dirty 列以红色标记显示含有未提交变更的 worktree。
  • 一键切换 Worktrees 标签页。 右侧 Worktrees 图标按钮可循环执行：打开 VCS 并选中 Worktrees 标签页、聚焦已打开的 Worktrees 标签页、关闭 VCS 面板。

截图

表头过滤

每列都可以独立过滤。过滤不区分大小写；如果某个仓库分组下没有任何匹配的 worktree，该分组会自动隐藏。

列排序

每个排序按钮会在升序、降序和未排序之间切换。多个已启用的排序按钮会按顺序在各自仓库分组内生效，因此多 root 结构仍然清晰。

快速搜索高亮

使用 IntelliJ 表格 Speed Search 快速跳转到匹配行，命中的文字片段会直接在表格中高亮。

多 root 项目

仓库分组行会把大型项目整理清楚。每个 Git root 都有自己的 worktree 行、当前 worktree 标记、分支名和文件系统路径。

当列表很长时，当前仓库分组行会固定在滚动区域顶部，直到下一个仓库分组到达顶部并把它推走。

功能

  • 从 Git 主菜单、Git 工具窗口下拉菜单或右侧 Worktrees 图标按钮打开 Worktrees 标签页。
  • 点击右侧 Worktrees 图标按钮可循环切换三种状态：打开 VCS 并选中 Worktrees 标签页、聚焦已打开的 Worktrees 标签页、关闭 VCS 面板。
  • 优先复用 Version Control / Git 工具窗口内可关闭的 Worktrees 标签页；必要时回退到独立的 Git Worktrees 工具窗口。
  • 使用 git worktree list --porcelain 列出 linked worktree。
  • 展示 Worktree、Branch 和 Location 三列。
  • Worktree 位于当前 Git root 内时，Location 显示相对路径；位于 root 外时，回退显示绝对路径。
  • 主 worktree 加粗显示，当前打开的 worktree 显示勾选图标。
  • detached HEAD worktree 显示为 detached。
  • Dirty 列以红色标记显示有未提交变更的 worktree。
  • 可通过左侧箭头、双击或右键菜单折叠和展开仓库行。
  • 长表格滚动时，当前仓库分组行会固定在顶部，并在下一个仓库分组到达时自然推走。
  • 工具栏保留 Refresh，右键菜单提供 Checkout、Open、Delete Worktree。
  • 双击或点击 Open，可把选中的 worktree 作为项目打开。
  • 使用 --ignore-other-worktrees 在当前仓库切换到选中 worktree 的分支。
  • 当选中项不能 Checkout 时，保留 Checkout 入口并显示禁用原因，例如 detached HEAD 或当前 worktree。
  • 当本地变更或未跟踪文件可能被覆盖时，先弹窗确认再执行 force checkout。
  • Checkout 和 Delete 会在后台任务里执行，操作结束后自动重新加载面板。
  • 可从面板工具栏打开 Worktrees 设置，并为相对路径显示和 Git 标签页恢复行为配置全局默认值或项目级覆盖。
  • 选中 worktree 行后按 Delete，会触发与 Delete Worktree 动作一致的删除流程。
  • 支持删除单个 worktree，也支持一次批量删除多个选中的 worktree。
  • 删除时可选择只删除 worktree，或同时删除 worktree 和对应分支。
  • 主 worktree 不会出现在可删除操作中。
  • 只在选中分支已被 linked worktree 使用时替换原生 Git Branch checkout/delete 动作，普通分支仍保留 IDE 原有行为。
  • 增强 Git Log 分支标签菜单，让 Checkout 和 Delete Branch 能处理 linked-worktree 分支，包括带 / 的分支名。
  • 通过 Git metadata 和 action data 解析 Git Log 里的 worktree 分支冲突，避免菜单更新时完整扫描 worktree 列表。
  • 在 Git 菜单的 Worktrees 入口显示 By GW4I，并在面板工具栏显示紧凑的来源说明。
  • Git 操作后刷新受影响仓库，并通过通知提示成功或失败。
  • 单个和批量删除后都把残留目录清理放到后台尽力执行，降低 Windows 下可见删除任务的等待时间。
  • Git 已经 unregister worktree 后，Windows 残留目录清理会使用长路径安全的处理方式。

环境要求

  • IntelliJ Platform IDE build 252 或更新版本。
  • 需要启用 IDE 内置 Git 插件 (Git4Idea)。
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Implement a 3-state toggle for the right-side Worktrees icon button: activate VCS with the Worktrees tab, select an already-visible Worktrees tab, or hide the VCS panel.

Fixed

  • Hide the duplicate Delete branch menu item when Delete Branch / Worktree is shown for branches already linked to another worktree.
  • Speed up bulk worktree deletion by batching Git commands and reducing per-repository refreshes.
  • Handle Invalid argument errors during leftover worktree directory cleanup on Windows.

idea-plugin.name: BranchFocus
idea-plugin.description:
Adds a Focus in Log action to the Git Branches popup. When invoked on a branch or a tag, the Git Log tool window opens (if it isn't already) and the commit graph scrolls to and selects the tip commit of that reference.




Gitブランチ・ポップアップに Focus in Log アクションを追加します。ブランチまたはタグ上で実行すると、 Git Log ツールウィンドウが開き（未表示の場合）、コミットグラフがその参照の先端コミットへスクロール・選択されます。

idea-plugin.name: Git Log Stats Columns
idea-plugin.description:
Git Log Stats Columns

Adds two optional columns to the Git Log:

  • Files — number of files changed in the commit.
  • Lines (+/-) — added and deleted line counts, colored green and red. Colors stay visible when the row is selected.

Both columns can be toggled from View Options > Columns in the Git Log toolbar.

Stats are computed by batched git log --shortstat calls and cached per commit. Merge commits are summarized against the first parent.

Git Log Stats Columns（日本語）

Git ログに 2 つの列を追加します:

  • Files — そのコミットで変更されたファイル数。
  • Lines (+/-) — 追加・削除行数（緑/赤で色分け）。行を選択しても色は維持されます。

両列とも Git Log ツールバーの 表示オプション > 列 から表示/非表示を切り替えられます。

統計値は git log --shortstat をバッチ呼び出しで集計し、コミット単位でキャッシュされます。マージコミットは第一親との差分として集計されます。

idea-plugin.name: Git Commit Reminder
idea-plugin.description:
Reminds you to commit and push before walking away from unfinished Git work.

When you close a project (or quit the IDE), Git Commit Reminder checks the current state of every Git repository in the project and shows a confirmation dialog if either of the following is true:

  • Uncommitted changes — modified, added, or deleted files in your working tree.
  • Unpushed commits — local commits that have not been pushed to the upstream branch, or commits on a branch that has no upstream configured.

You can still close the project at any time — the dialog just makes sure it is intentional.
idea-plugin.change-notes: First stable release. No functional changes since 1.0.0-alpha.4.

idea-plugin.name: Branch in Project View
idea-plugin.description:
Shows the current git branch instead of the path (location string) next to each module / content root in the Project tool window.
  • Branch colored by name: green on main/master, orange otherwise.
  • ↑ / ↓ arrows for commits to push / pull vs origin.
  • An amber ● marker when the working tree has uncommitted changes.
  • Click the branch text (or use the context menu) to switch branch via the native Git popup.
In monorepos each module shows the branch of its own repository.

idea-plugin.name: Pull Request Viewer for Bitbucket, GitHub & Azure DevOps
idea-plugin.description:
Pull Request Viewer brings Bitbucket Cloud, GitHub, and Azure DevOps Services pull request review into IntelliJ IDEA. Pick your source in Settings and review PRs in the IDE with native diffs, inline comments, review decisions, review tracking, checklists, and CI triage.

30-day free trial, then paid — a per-user subscription license is required after the trial.

  • Pull request queue — browse PRs across configured Bitbucket, GitHub, or Azure DevOps repositories with All Open, Needs My Review, and My PRs filters, plus a title search to narrow the list
  • Native IntelliJ diffs — inspect the full pull request on every provider, or step through individual commits on Bitbucket and GitHub
  • Inline review comments — read, reply, start threaded comments on exact diff lines, and edit your own comments in place
  • Review ledger — mark files reviewed, needs-follow-up, or skipped with saved progress, a "next unreviewed" jump, and changed-since-review detection
  • Review checklists — built-in and custom checklist templates matched to your changed files, with a reminder before approving while required items are open
  • Comment snippets — insert reusable review comments from a customizable library
  • Review actions — submit review decisions without leaving the IDE, including Azure DevOps approve, wait-for-author, reject, and reset votes
  • CI triage — inspect Bitbucket Pipelines, GitHub Actions, and Azure Pipelines runs, steps/jobs, logs, failed tests, and available annotations; rerun, cancel, or queue work where the provider supports it
  • Activity — see the full Bitbucket or GitHub PR feed and Azure DevOps comment activity
  • Markdown PR descriptions — read formatted descriptions, with inline images on Bitbucket and GitHub
  • Copy a deep link — right-click any editor line to copy a Bitbucket or GitHub URL for that file and line
Configure every provider via Settings → Tools → Pull Request Viewer. Support: support@ngaio.dev.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
What's New

2026.3.0
  • Azure DevOps support — review pull requests, comments, diffs, and votes in the IDE
  • Azure Pipelines — inspect runs, jobs, logs, tests, and annotations
  • Improved settings, CI failure details, and reliability across all providers
2026.2.0
  • Free 30-day trial, then paid — starting with this version, Pull Request Viewer requires a license. After updating, start your free 30-day trial from the Start Free Trial button in the IDE toolbar (or Help → Register…); the plugin's tool windows stay hidden until a trial or license is active. A per-user subscription is required after the trial ends
  • Staying on your current version is safe — your currently installed version keeps working — no trial or license needed
  • Lapsed subscriptions keep a fallback license — this is an annual subscription with fallback coverage: if your paid subscription lapses after at least 12 months, JetBrains' perpetual fallback license keeps an earlier version working; updates and new versions require an active subscription
  • Compatibility fix for current IDE versions — replaced a deprecated API call flagged by the Marketplace plugin verifier
2026.1.1
  • Smoother Bitbucket sign-in infrastructure — OAuth moves to its permanent home; existing sessions carry over automatically, and if a sign-in ever truly expires the plugin now tells you clearly instead of failing silently
  • Search CI logs — Ctrl/Cmd+F (or the Find link) in the Pipelines log view: highlighted matches, match count, next/previous
  • Consistent text sizing — the whole plugin now follows your IDE font settings (Appearance, presentation mode, accessibility zoom); code and log areas use your editor font family
  • Description images now load — screenshots embedded in pull request descriptions render in the IDE; anything the IDE can't fetch becomes a click-to-open link
  • Jump from comment to code — the code snippet above an inline comment in Overview is syntax-highlighted and clicking it opens the file's diff at that line
  • Cleaner CI runs and colorized logs — compact run rows keep the branch visible, and step logs render ANSI colors or command/error/warning highlighting
  • New version scheme — releases now use year-based versions (2026.1.0 follows 1.4.1); a normal upgrade, nothing to do
  • Hide the review checklist — a Hide link on the checklist card; re-enable any time in Settings → Tools → Pull Request Viewer → Review Checklists
1.4.1

  • Cleaner review UI — tidier comment cards, file rows, and pull request list

  • Review Ledger: mark files reviewed / needs-follow-up / skipped with saved progress, notes, "next unreviewed" jump, changed-since-review detection, and a copyable summary
  • Review Checklists: templates matched to your changed files, with a gentle approval reminder when required items are still open; every template (including the built-in defaults) is editable and removable in settings, with a "Reset defaults"; posting a checklist summary now refreshes the comments
  • Comment Snippets: insert reusable review comments from the compose box, with a customizable library

1.0.38 — Pull request review polish

idea-plugin.name: TSC AI Commit Tool
idea-plugin.description:
TSC AI Commit Tool is an AI-enhanced commit template generator for IntelliJ-based IDEs. It generates structured commit messages from git diff, fills the commit panel, and copies the result to the clipboard. The plugin standardizes how teams record AI participation in every commit and feeds downstream statistics dashboards with structured data.

TSC AI Commit Tool

AI 增强型 Commit 模板生成器，适用于 IntelliJ 系列 IDE。 用于统一团队在提交代码时对 AI 参与信息的记录方式，为后续统计分析系统提供结构化数据， 并显著降低开发者填写 commit 的成本。

Commit 格式

<type>(<scope>): [ai:<tag>] <subject>

<body>

AI-Coauthored: true|false
AI-Ratio: 0.00 ~ 1.00
AI-Tool: idea | cursor | copilot | claude | gpt | other

AI 标记规范（必填）

  • [ai:full] — 80%+ 代码由 AI 生成
  • [ai:part] — 30% ~ 80% AI 参与
  • [ai:review] — AI 仅用于 review / 优化
  • [ai:none] — 无 AI 参与
  • [ai:migrate] — 迁移代码，项目初始化时

核心功能

  • 一键根据 git diff（已跟踪 + 未跟踪文件）生成提交消息。
  • 自动填充 IDE 的 Commit 消息面板，并复制到剪贴板。
  • 支持自定义模板和占位符：${aiTag}、${aiRatio}、 ${aiTool}、${aiGenerated}、${manualEdited}、 ${aiAssisted}、${fileCount}、${added}、 ${modified}、${deleted}、${renamed}、${files}。
  • 可在 Settings → Tools → TSC AI Commit Tool 中自定义默认 AI 标签、 AI-Ratio、AI 工具、Body 描述以及完整模板正文。

示例输出

feat(user): [ai:part] add login flow

- AI生成：根据 git diff 自动生成 commit 草稿
- 人工修改：待补充
- AI辅助：提交结构和措辞建议

AI-Coauthored: true
AI-Ratio: 0.65
AI-Tool: idea

使用方式：打开 VCS / Commit 面板，执行 TSC AI Commit 动作； 也可在 VCS 菜单中调用。

idea-plugin.name: Merge CLI Fixer
idea-plugin.description:
An IntelliJ IDEA plugin that adds a single CLI command, idea mergex, designed to be used as a git mergetool.

Why

As of IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1.2, the bundled idea merge command has these issues that make it unsuitable as a git mergetool driver (JetBrains may address them in a future release — please verify against your current IDE version before relying on this plugin):

  1. It nags about non-project files. When the file being merged sits outside any open project, the IDE displays a "you are editing a non-project file" confirmation dialog on every save.
  2. EDT errors. Threading bugs occasionally surface as event-dispatch thread violations.

idea mergex is a sibling command that:

  • Whitelists writes to the merged file while the merge is active (no non-project-file dialog).
  • Uses the modern coroutine-based application starter to stay on the correct thread.

Configure VCS

Git

Add the following to ~/.gitconfig (or run the equivalent git config --global commands):

[merge]
    tool = idea
[mergetool "idea"]
    cmd = idea mergex --wait $LOCAL $REMOTE $BASE $MERGED
    trustExitCode = true
[mergetool]
    keepBackup = false
  • Note that --wait option must be placed after mergex.
  • Make sure Toolbox is configured to generate launch scripts.

Jujutsu

Add the following to ~/.config/jj/config.toml.

[ui]
merge-editor = "idea"

[merge-tools.idea]
program = "idea"
merge-args = ["mergex", "--wait", "$left", "$right", "$base", "$output"]
  • Note that --wait option must be placed after mergex.
  • Make sure Toolbox is configured to generate launch scripts.

Hence this simple plugin helps you put that info in with a simple button click in the commit menu (above the commit message block).

idea-plugin.name: GitStratum
idea-plugin.description:
GitStratum turns your project's Git history into practical, in-IDE insight: which files are risky to change, which files move together, and who knows each part of the code. It is strictly read-only - it analyzes git log and never commits, pushes, or modifies your repository.

  • Hotspots - rank files by a score combining how often a file changes (recent activity weighted more) with how complex it is. Files that are both churn-heavy and complex are your highest-value refactoring targets. Pick the time window, scope the report to any folder, and sort by churn / complexity / author columns, each with a per-file activity trend.
  • Project-view heatmap - tint files and folders directly in the Project view by their hotspot score, so the riskiest areas of the codebase stand out while you browse. Toggle it on or off at any time.
  • Change Coupling - for any file, see the files that tend to change alongside it, so you know what to read for context before editing.
  • Pre-commit coupling check - an optional commit-time check warns you when you're committing a file without its usual companions, so related changes don't get left behind.
  • Ownership - see who has contributed most to a file, folder, or selected lines across full history. Rename-aware and mailmap-aware, so credit follows moves and merged identities.
  • Tunable scoring - adapt the analysis to your codebase from Settings | Tools | GitStratum: hotspot sensitivity (how far above average a file must score to count), a size cutoff that ignores sweeping commits (reformats, mass moves, generated-code refreshes) so they don't inflate churn or fabricate coupling, and coupling thresholds (minimum degree, co-change count, and depth).

Coupling, ownership, and hotspots are all a right-click away - launch them straight from the Project view or editor context menu on the file or folder in front of you.

idea-plugin.name: Git Arborist
idea-plugin.description:
Git Arborist makes Git worktrees first-class inside JetBrains IDEs. Create, open, and manage worktrees from a dedicated tool window, the Git menu, and the Project View — and carry your project setup (run configurations, code style, local tooling) into a new worktree automatically, before the IDE opens it for the first time.

A Git worktree checks out a second branch of the same repository into its own directory, so you can review a pull request without stashing, run a long build on one branch while you keep coding on another, or keep a release branch open beside main. This plugin removes the friction of driving that workflow from inside the IDE.

Features

  • Worktrees tool window — each worktree is one row with a branch title, a path / commit / age subtitle, and state badges (main, current, safe-to-delete, dirty, locked, prunable, detached, staged/unstaged/untracked counts, and divergence from main and the remote). Status loads asynchronously and never blocks the UI.
  • Search, filter, and sort across branch, path, commit, message, creator, and state.
  • New worktree from a remote branch — browse and filter the repository's remote branches, fetch to refresh them, and create a worktree with a new local branch that tracks the one you pick; also available by right-clicking a branch in the Git Log.
  • Every worktree operation through Git4Idea — list, create, open, remove (with optional force and backing-branch deletion), lock, unlock, move, prune, and repair, all on a background thread.
  • One-click open — opening a worktree hands off to the IDE's own project-open flow (open in this window, a new window, or cancel — honoring your IDE preferences); an already-open worktree is focused instead of opened twice.
  • Carry over project setup on first open — copies .idea/ and any paths listed in a .worktree-copy manifest into a new worktree before it opens. Secrets and heavy build directories are never copied.
  • Safe-to-delete detection — worktrees whose work is fully merged are dimmed and badged SAFE.

Requires an IntelliJ Platform IDE (2025.2 or later, build 252+) that bundles the Git4Idea plugin, such as IntelliJ IDEA or Android Studio.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • The Worktrees tool window now keeps itself current when worktrees are added, removed, or moved outside Git Arborist (the Git CLI, other plugins, or other IDE actions). It refreshes silently on Git4Idea repository changes while visible, and when the tool window is reopened, so the list no longer goes stale until a manual refresh.
  • Worktree rows now show contributor avatars on the first line, modeled on the Pull Requests list's assignees/reviewers: the branch creator's avatar, a separator, then up to five committer avatars (the fifth collapses to a "+N" counter) for everyone who has committed on the branch. Avatars start as initial monograms and are replaced in place once fetched — GitHub users.noreply.github.com commit emails resolve to the contributor's GitHub avatar (the same image the built-in Pull Requests window shows), and all other addresses fall back to Gravatar, with the monogram kept when neither exists. An opt-in Fetch real GitHub avatars setting (off by default, under Version Control > Git Arborist) additionally resolves any other commit email to its GitHub avatar through the GitHub commits API for worktrees whose remote is github.com, authenticating with the GitHub token Git already stores (git credential fill) for the higher rate limit and private repositories. Lookups are cached for the session; hovering names them.
  • New worktrees can now be created directly from a remote branch. A New Worktree from Remote Branch title action (and matching Git > Worktrees menu entry) opens a searchable list of the repository's remote-tracking branches, with a Fetch button that pulls every remote — authentication and progress handled by the IDE — and refreshes the list in place. Picking a branch seeds a new local branch that tracks it, defaults the target path from the branch name, and creates the worktree through the same flow as a manual create. This closes the gap where checking out a remote branch onto a fresh worktree previously required typing the full origin/… ref by hand.
  • Worktrees can also be created from the Git Log: right-click a commit that carries a branch label and choose Create Worktree from Branch…. A remote branch seeds a new local tracking branch; a local branch is checked out into the new worktree. This uses only the platform's public VCS Log data, so it stays compatible across IDE builds. (The Git Branches popup widget is intentionally not hooked: its branch-selection APIs are marked internal and off-limits to third-party plugins, and it already ships its own built-in "New Worktree" action.)

Fixed

  • Settings changed just before opening a worktree now carry over reliably. Carry-over reads the source project's .idea/ from disk, but the IDE debounces PersistentStateComponent writes and otherwise flushes them only on frame deactivation or project close — so settings edited moments earlier, most visibly Settings | Tools entries from third-party plugins (Detekt, Develocity, KtLint, …) persisted to .idea/ XML files, could be copied stale or missing. The open source project's settings are now flushed to disk before the copy runs.
  • The Worktrees tool window no longer pushes status badges and text off the right edge when the panel is narrow. Each row now tracks the tool window width (no horizontal scrollbar), the branch/path/commit text keeps a minimum width and truncates with an ellipsis, and the status badges shrink-then-clip while staying pinned to the right edge — so neither side disappears as the panel shrinks, matching the built-in Pull Requests tool window in constrained widths.

Changed

  • Reworked each worktree row for density and legibility, aligning with the Pull Requests tool window: the branch name is no longer bold, MAIN/CURRENT/DIRTY/SAFE sit as pills beside the title (where DRAFT appears), the commit message moves up to the second line, and the remaining detail (locked, prunable, detached, staged/unstaged/untracked counts, line delta, and main/remote divergence) drops to a third line. The relative path is hidden but still shown on hover.
  • Every third-party GitHub Actions step in the CI and release workflows is now pinned to a full commit SHA instead of a mutable tag (actions/checkout, actions/setup-java, actions/upload-artifact, gradle/actions/wrapper-validation, gradle/actions/setup-gradle). Tags such as @v7 are movable refs, so an upstream account compromise could have silently swapped the code that builds, verifies, and signs the released plugin. Each pin carries a trailing # vX.Y.Z comment, so Dependabot keeps updating them as before while the exact reviewed commit stays fixed.

idea-plugin.name: ScriptDock
idea-plugin.description:
ScriptDock keeps project-local SQL and workflow scripts organized around the way teams actually ship code.

Instead of hunting through folders or renaming files to track release order, ScriptDock gives every project a dedicated script workspace for branch work, release preparation, recurring common tasks, and archives.

Key Features:
  • Branch Workspaces - group scripts by Git branch without changing your repository structure.
  • Release Timeline - review active branch scripts by deadline and release window.
  • Common Scripts - keep frequently used project scripts, folders, favorites, and recent items close at hand.
  • Archive Flow - hide completed branch work without deleting project files or metadata.
  • Metadata Ordering - preserve business order in .metadata.json instead of forcing filename prefixes.
  • Safe Opening - open scripts in the current IDE, DataGrip, or a chooser; ScriptDock does not execute SQL or connect to databases.
  • Multi-Language UI - English, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, German, and Russian bundles are included.

Built for developers and release owners who need a calm, branch-aware place to prepare database scripts, migration notes, and repeatable project workflows.
