idea-plugin.name: EarthBuild
idea-plugin.description:
Adds comprehensive Earthly language support to IntelliJ IDEA and other JetBrains IDEs.

What is Earthly?

Earthly is a build automation tool that combines the best of Makefiles and Dockerfiles. It provides reproducible builds that run anywhere - on your laptop, in CI/CD, or in production.

Key Features

  • Syntax Highlighting - Full syntax highlighting for all Earthly commands and keywords
  • Code Navigation - Go to Definition (Ctrl/Cmd+Click) and Find Usages for targets and functions
  • Code Completion - Intelligent suggestions for target references and function calls
  • Editor Support - Comment/uncomment lines, automatic file type detection
  • Refactoring - Safe delete for targets and functions with reference validation

Supported File Types

  • Earthfile (standard name)
  • *.earth files
  • *.earthly files

Getting Started

Once installed, the plugin automatically recognizes Earthfile and *.earth files. Use Ctrl/Cmd+Click to navigate to target definitions, and Ctrl/Cmd+/ to comment lines.

Links

  • Earthly Documentation
  • Report Issues
  • Source Code

This plugin is a community fork of the original Earthly organization plugin, updated for compatibility with the latest IntelliJ platform.

idea-plugin.name: System Notifier
idea-plugin.description:
Add native system notifications to the IDE

What does this plugin do?

It turns important IDE events into native operating system notifications. This way, you can follow the status of your tasks without keeping the IDE in the foreground.


Key features:
  • Shows external system tasks (Gradle, Maven, ...) as system notifications when they finish.
  • Notifies when Run/Debug configurations start and finish.
  • Optional: mirror all IDE notifications as system notifications.
  • Option to add sound to notifications.
  • OS compatibility:
    • Windows: Action Center (tray).
    • macOS: Notification Center.
    • Linux: libnotify; with an in-IDE fallback when there is no D-Bus session.
  • Easy configuration under Settings/Preferences → Tools → System Notifier.

Notes
  • It does not collect or send personal data.
  • On Linux a D-Bus session is required for native notifications; otherwise, an in-IDE balloon is used.

idea-plugin.name: AEM Integration
idea-plugin.description:
HTL, Sling Model and Dispatcher support for AEM, with an AI assistant that knows your project. Deploy packages, tail logs, and browse OSGi bundles in the IDE. Edit dialogs, ClientLibs, and FreeMarker templates with completion and inspections. Start with Settings > Tools > AEM Servers.


We want this to be the best AEM tool in the IDE, and your feedback is critical: report a bug or an idea and tell us what is missing.


Paid plugin: AEM Integration is a paid plugin. Several groups get it with a discount:

  • Free for students and teachers, classroom assistance, open source projects, and the Developer Recognition Program
  • 50% off for universities and educational organizations, startups, and non-profit organizations
  • 40% off for former student license holders

Feedback: Leave a review, open an issue on GitHub, or write to info@ilscipio.com.


Documentation: Open the Tutorials tab on the Marketplace page. A welcome dialog with a guided tour opens on the first start.


AEM Integration is an independent plugin and is not affiliated with Adobe or JetBrains.


Core Features

HTL Templates

  • HTL grammar with expression language, syntax highlighting, and brace matching
  • Code completion for block statements, built-in objects, and context options
  • Inspections for XSS risks, missing i18n, deprecated syntax, unused variables and templates, and invalid block statements
  • Navigation from data-sly-use and data-sly-call to the Java class or template, with a structure view and code folding for HTL blocks

FreeMarker Templates

  • Directive and expression support with highlighting, formatting, and completion
  • Go to definition from variables and user directives
  • Structure view and code folding for directives
  • Inspections for unclosed and wrongly closed directives

Dialogs and Content

  • Touch UI dialogs with Granite and Coral UI property completion
  • Classic UI dialogs with xtype completion
  • cq:editConfig, .content.xml, and filter.xml completion, with checks for invalid filter paths, node types, and overlapping filter roots
  • ClientLibs category and file completion in js.txt and css.txt

Sling Models and OSGi

  • Inspections for Sling Models, Sling servlets, OSGi components, and ResourceResolver and JCR Session handling
  • Field generator for Sling Model injection, with ACS Commons annotations
  • OSGi configuration completion and checks for .cfg.json files
  • Bundle import from a running AEM instance for completion on runtime classes
  • Wizards and live templates for components, HTL templates, ClientLibs, Sling Models, services, servlets, schedulers, and event handlers

Dispatcher and Repoinit

  • Dispatcher .any and .farm files, and Apache .vhost, .rules, and .vars files, with highlighting, completion, and brace matching
  • Repoinit scripts with highlighting, completion, and syntax checks

Servers, Deployment, and Debugging

  • Server profiles for your AEM instances, with secure credential storage
  • Deployment with CRX package install, Maven, VLT sync, or the filesystem install folder
  • Remote debugging with a run configuration that finds the AEM debug port
  • Log viewer that tails the AEM log live, with search and filters
  • OSGi console access for bundles, components, and configurations
  • AEM Cloud RDE actions to deploy, check status, and reset

Universal Editor and Edge Delivery

  • Universal Editor attribute completion, checks, and a line marker for data-aue attributes, plus Open in Universal Editor
  • Model definition generator for Universal Editor components from a Sling Model
  • Edge Delivery block wizard and checks for block naming and performance

AI Assistant and MCP Server

  • AEM AI tool window to chat with the coding agent on your machine (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Windsurf, Aider, Antigravity) or an API provider
  • Editor actions to explain code, improve code, fix a problem, add comments, and explain the last AEM log error, from the right-click menu or a selection toolbar
  • Alt+Enter quick fix: Fix this problem with AEM AI
  • MCP server on localhost, installed into detected agents with one click. Agents read parse errors, file problems, the PSI tree, completion and resolve results, OSGi data, logs, JCR content, queries, run configurations, and breakpoints
  • Permission modes that decide whether the agent only plans, edits files, or acts on its own

Project

  • Project detection from the pom.xml structure, shown in the status bar
  • AEM SDK type and a spelling dictionary for AEM terms
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • New AEM AI tool window: chat with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Windsurf or Aider without leaving the IDE. The plugin finds the agent you already have installed.
  • External AI providers: chat with Ollama, the OpenAI API, the Anthropic API or the Gemini API from the same tool window.

Changed

Fixed

    • nuxi build - Production build
    • nuxi generate - Static site generation
    • nuxi preview - Preview production build
    • nuxi typecheck - TypeScript checking
    • nuxi cleanup - Clear .nuxt directory

Debug Features

Plugin Debug Options

Settings > Tools > Flexible Nuxt.js > Debug Options

  • Verbose debug logging - Enable detailed logging for plugin operations
  • Runtime definition reload - Reload YAML definitions without IDE restart

Nuxt App Debugging

Clicking Debug on a Nuxt run configuration automatically starts two debugger sessions:

  • Nuxt Debugger — attaches to the Node.js inspector for server-side code (Nitro routes, SSR, middleware)
  • Nuxt Browser — opens a managed browser window with Chrome DevTools Protocol for client-side Vue component debugging (.vue files, composables, event handlers)

Requires WebStorm or IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate with the JavaScript and Vue.js plugins active. Not available in IntelliJ IDEA Community.

Configure in Run/Debug Configurations:

  • Node.js Inspector - Enable --inspect or --inspect-brk
  • Debug port - Configure inspector port (default: 9229)
  • Break on start - Pause on the first line for initialization debugging
  • Source maps - Enable/disable source map generation
  • Open browser debugger - Toggle the automatic browser debug session (on by default)

To debug Vue components:

  1. Create a Nuxt run configuration and click Debug
  2. Set breakpoints in .vue or .ts files as normal
  3. For setup-phase code, open the browser's DevTools (⌘⌥I) before reloading — setup runs during page hydration
  4. onMounted and event handler breakpoints fire automatically without any extra steps

idea-plugin.name: Flexible ABAP
idea-plugin.description:
Professional SAP development: ABAP, CDS views, and RAP behavior definitions. Smart completion, 70+ templates, 25 postfix templates, hover docs.

We built this plugin from the ground up with an entirely new grammar architecture. Since neither the language spec nor existing implementations were publicly available, we recreated the logic from scratch. That means your feedback matters more than anything right now. Leave a review, open an issue on GitHub, or just shoot us an email. Tell us what works, what breaks, what you wish it did. Anyone who takes the time to share feedback gets 20% off their next purchase.

Supported Languages

LanguageExtensionsFeatures
ABAP.abap, .clas, .intf, .fugr, .progClasses, interfaces, reports, function modules, screen flow logic, enhancements
CDS.cds, .ddls, .dcls, .ddlx, .asddls, .asdcls, .asddlxs, .srvdsrvViews, entities, annotations, access control, service definitions
BDEF.bdef, .asbdefRAP behaviors, actions, validations, determinations

abapGit file names such as zcl_x.clas.abap, zcl_x.clas.testclasses.abap or zi_x.ddls.asddls open with the matching editor.

Key Features

Smart Code Assistance

  • Context-aware completion for 200+ ABAP keywords
  • CDS annotation completion (@UI, @ObjectModel, @Semantics, @Analytics)
  • RAP behavior definition completion (actions, validations, determinations)
  • Hover documentation with SAP Help links (Ctrl+Q)
  • Parameter info for methods and built-in functions

Refactoring and Navigation

  • Rename (Shift+F6) for variables, constants, field symbols, inline declarations (also @DATA(...) in ABAP SQL), method and form parameters, PARAMETERS and SELECT-OPTIONS (with the abapGit selection texts)
  • Find Usages (Alt+F7), Go to Declaration (Ctrl+B) and usage highlighting for the same data objects
  • Extract Method (Ctrl+Alt+M) into a new private method or FORM, with IMPORTING, CHANGING, EXPORTING and RETURNING parameters and their types

Productivity Tools

  • 70+ live templates - Type abap: or cds: for templates
  • 25 postfix templates - Type .if, .loop, .try, .data after expressions
  • Structure view for classes, methods, CDS entities, and BDEF behaviors
  • Code folding for blocks and comments
  • Brace matching for IF/ENDIF, LOOP/ENDLOOP, CLASS/ENDCLASS

Code Quality

  • 8 code inspections with quick fixes
  • Deprecated statement detection
  • Naming convention checks
  • Unused variable warnings
  • SQL injection prevention
  • Constant conditions (IF branches that never run)
  • Mismatched BEGIN OF / END OF names

Professional Themes

  • Optimized Darcula (dark) and Default (light) color schemes
  • Separate themes for ABAP, CDS, and BDEF
  • Customizable via Settings > Editor > Color Scheme

Postfix Templates

Type an expression followed by a dot and the template name:

TemplateInputOutput
.iflv_count > 0.ifIF lv_count > 0. ENDIF.
.looplt_items.loopLOOP AT lt_items INTO DATA(ls_item). ENDLOOP.
.loopfslt_items.loopfsLOOP AT lt_items ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_item>). ENDLOOP.
.tryexpr.tryTRY. expr. CATCH cx_root. ENDTRY.
.dataexpr.dataDATA(lv_result) = expr.
.writeexpr.writeWRITE: / expr.
.clearvar.clearCLEAR var.
.lineslt_items.lineslines( lt_items )
.existslt_items.existsline_exists( lt_items[ ] )

Live Templates

Type the prefix and press Tab:

ABAP templates: abap:class, abap:method, abap:select, abap:loop, abap:try, abap:if

CDS templates: cds:view, cds:entity, cds:annotation, cds:association

abapGit Repositories

Open an abapGit repository (a folder with .abapgit.xml) and work with it like any other project:

  • Every file maps to its SAP object, also class includes and function modules: zcl_x.clas.testclasses.abap is the test class include of ZCL_X. Breakpoints, the debugger and run configurations use this mapping.
  • The editor tab shows the SAP object, for example ZCL_X (Test Classes) or Z_FM (ZFG).
  • Sync writes abapGit file names into the package folders (folder logic PREFIX, FULL or MIXED, namespaces as #ns#). A new object also gets its abapGit XML metadata; existing metadata files stay unchanged.
  • Set the source layout (Auto-detect, abapGit, flat) and the abapGit package in Settings > Languages & Frameworks > Flexible ABAP.
  • New projects from the project wizard are abapGit repositories by default.

Connecting to SAP

The plugin connects to SAP systems for source browsing, deployment, and debugging. It uses the ADT REST protocol on modern systems and classic RFC on older ones.

  • On-Premise (ADT): Basic authentication with user and password. Full in-IDE debugger. Configure in Settings > Languages & Frameworks > Flexible ABAP.
  • SAP BTP Cloud: Browser-based IDP login. Paste your BTP service key to auto-fill connection details, then click the SAP status bar widget to authenticate. Full in-IDE debugger.
  • RFC / SOAP (NetWeaver 7.0+, no ADT): For older systems that predate ADT. Connects over /sap/bc/soap/rfc with nothing to install, and reads and writes program/report source via standard remote-enabled function modules.

Debugging

  • ADT systems (7.40+): set breakpoints and debug fully inside the IDE (breakpoints, stepping, and variables).
  • RFC systems (NetWeaver 7.0): a true in-IDE step debugger is not available on that release, since it depends on ADT. Instead, create an "ABAP via RFC (SAP GUI debug)" run configuration, set breakpoints in the opened source, and press Debug. The plugin registers them as external breakpoints and triggers the run; you then step and inspect variables in the SAP GUI debugger.

New to a system? Visit the Connecting page for how to set up On-Premise, Cloud, and RFC connections, and how debugging works on each.

SAP Tool Window

  • Systems: the connection details of each system, with Add System and Test Connection.
  • Sync: browse packages or search objects, check objects or whole packages, and download them into the project (flat sap-sources/ folder or abapGit layout).
  • Transports: a Transport Organizer like in Eclipse ADT. Workbench, customizing and transport of copies requests by target, with their tasks and objects. Create requests (type, description, target, CTS project, owner), release requests or tasks, delete, change the owner, add a user, remove objects, and open an object with a double-click.

AI Chat and MCP Server

  • AI chat panel (right side) with 7 CLI agents and 4 API formats (Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini)
  • MCP server with 12 ABAP tools for run, debug, workspace control, parser diagnostics (abap_parse_errors checks a file or a folder for syntax errors), and symbol usages (abap_symbol_usages lists the declarations and usages of a data object)
  • One-click MCP install into Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf
  • Master toggle to disable all AI features

Getting Started

  1. Install from JetBrains Marketplace
  2. Open any .abap, .cds, or .bdef file
  3. Type abap: + Tab for live templates
  4. Use Ctrl+Q for hover documentation
  5. Type expression + .if for postfix completion

idea-plugin.name: Direnv
idea-plugin.description:
This plugin provides an action to import environment variables from direnv and persistently apply them to all Run/Debug configurations in the project.

How It Works

When direnv environment variables are imported, the plugin merges them into the Environment Variables section of every Run/Debug configuration in the project. The variables are visible and editable in Run/Debug Configurations > Environment variables.

  • Direnv variables serve as defaults — any variable you manually set in a Run/Debug configuration takes priority over the direnv value.
  • The plugin supports standard run configurations (Java, Kotlin, Python, Node.js, etc.) as well as Gradle, Maven, and other external system configurations.

Automatic Import before every Run/Debug

To automatically load the environment variables from a <project_root>/.envrc file before each and every execution of a Run/Debug configuration, visit Settings > Tools > Direnv Settings and tick the relevant checkbox.

On starting a Run/Debug job, the plugin re-imports direnv and applies the latest environment to all run configurations. If you often work with multiple project windows open in a single IDE instance, this is probably the best option for you.

Automatic Import on Startup

To automatically load the environment variables from a <project_root>/.envrc file when you open the project, visit Settings > Tools > Direnv Settings and tick the relevant checkbox.

If "Automatic Import on Startup" is disabled, a popup notification will appear whenever a project with a .envrc file in the root is opened. You can load the .envrc file by clicking on the link in the notification.

Manual Import

To manually load an .envrc file:

  • You can right-click on any .envrc file and click Import Direnv to load its contents.

Note: This plugin handles only .envrc files in the project root automatically, but you can use the right click method to manually import any .envrc file that is in the project directory.

Note: You need direnv in your path, or you can specify the location of your direnv executable in Settings > Tools > Direnv Settings

idea-plugin.name: Flexible Haskell
idea-plugin.description:
Full Haskell IDE support: HLS-powered completion and diagnostics, a GHCi REPL and debugger, 100 live templates, code inspections and refactorings, first-class Cabal support, and an optional AI assistant with a 32-tool MCP server.

We are a young IDE extension and want to make it the best environment for Haskell developers.

So expect it to

a) still have the occasional bug

b) improve quickly â€” we ship updates constantly.

Please help us: leave a review, open a GitHub issue, or email us and let us know what you think, what works, and how to improve it further.

Core Features

Language Support

  • Complete Haskell grammar for GHC Haskell syntax, including CPP preprocessor directives and DataKinds type-level literals
  • Bluespec support â€” Bluespec Classic (.bs) shares the Haskell parser with hardware-specific keywords (rule, interface, method, action), and Bluespec SystemVerilog (.bsv) has a dedicated lexer for C-style comments and Verilog-sized literals
  • Cabal support â€” syntax highlighting, completion, and documentation for .cabal and cabal.project files, with one-click cabal-fmt formatting
  • HLS (Haskell Language Server) integration for completion, diagnostics, hover docs, inlay type hints, and code lenses (enable via Settings > Languages & Frameworks > Haskell)
  • Syntax highlighting with a dedicated color settings page and tuned defaults for the Default, Darcula, and VS Code Dark+ themes
  • Code folding for import blocks, functions, data types, classes, instances, and comments
  • Language injection into QuasiQuotes ([sql|â€¦|], [hamlet|â€¦|], â€¦) and string literals
  • Brace matching with auto-close for {, (, [, comment support for line (--) and block ({- â€¦ -}) comments, and Haddock highlighting (-- |)
  • Project SDK â€” configure a GHC / Stack / Cabal SDK from project settings, or download one via GHCup from Tools > Haskell

Code Inspections & Quick Fixes

  • 16 inspections â€” unused/duplicate imports and exports, missing type signatures, possibly incomplete pattern matches, variable shadowing, unknown/unused LANGUAGE pragmas, and HLint-style smells (use camelCase, redundant bind, many imports)
  • 6 intention actions â€” add a missing import, add a type annotation, add a LANGUAGE pragma, add a deriving clause, toggle an explicit import list, and apply HLS refactorings
  • Import optimizer (Ctrl+Alt+O), postfix templates, and surround-with support

REPL, Run & Debug

  • Integrated GHCi REPL with a JediTerm terminal widget in a tool window at the bottom of the IDE
  • Send to GHCi (Alt+Shift+Enter) â€” send the selection or current line to the REPL
  • Load File in GHCi (Ctrl+Shift+F10) â€” :load the current file
  • REPL controls â€” Start, Stop, Restart, Interrupt, and Reload (Ctrl+Shift+F5) from Tools > Haskell
  • Clickable GHC stack traces in the REPL console
  • Run configurations with Stack / Cabal / runghc modes, an auto-producer for any .hs file, and a run gutter marker on main
  • GHCi debugger with line breakpoints over Stack, Cabal, and runghc

AI Assistant & MCP Server

  • AI chat tool window â€” Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Antigravity, Aider, or your own Anthropic / OpenAI / Gemini / Ollama key
  • MCP server â€” 32 IDE tools spanning GHCi, workspace, code intelligence, tooling, and run/debug, installed into your agent CLI in one click
  • Fully optional â€” one switch under Settings > Languages & Frameworks > Haskell > AI turns all of it off

Navigation & Intelligence

  • Go to Symbol (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N) â€” navigate to any top-level declaration
  • Go to Class (Ctrl+N) â€” navigate to data types, type aliases, type classes, and modules
  • Go to Declaration (Ctrl+Click) and Go to Implementation (Ctrl+Alt+B) via HLS
  • Structure View (Alt+7), Call Hierarchy (Ctrl+Alt+H), and Find Usages (Alt+F7)
  • Rename refactoring (Shift+F6) for top-level identifiers
  • Library source navigation â€” jump into GHC stdlib, Cabal/Stack dependencies, and downloaded Hackage sources
  • Gutter icons for module, data, newtype, class, instance, and type

Smart Completion & Documentation

  • LSP-powered completion from Haskell Language Server, plus keyword, pragma, import, and qualified-name completion
  • LSP diagnostics shown inline as editor annotations
  • Haddock documentation (Ctrl+Q) â€” renders preceding -- | comments and type signatures, with basic markup (@code@, /italic/, __bold__)

Formatting & Code Style

  • External formatters â€” ormolu, fourmolu, or stylish-haskell via Format with External Formatter (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F), plumbed into Reformat Code (Ctrl+Alt+L) with optional format-on-save
  • Built-in formatter with spacing rules for operators (->, =>, <-, ::, =, |), brackets, and commas
  • Code style settings under Settings > Editor > Code Style > Haskell

Live & File Templates

100 built-in live templates across 7 categories â€” General, IO, Typeclasses, Lens, Monad Transformers, Testing, and Concurrency. Type the abbreviation and press Tab:

  • Declarations: fn (function + signature), fnw (with where), dt, nt, cls, inst
  • Expressions: case, do, let, where, if, lam
  • Modules & Imports: mod, imp, imq, der, main
  • Testing: test (HUnit), hspec, prop (QuickCheck)
  • â€¦and dozens more for lenses (vw, ov, lns), monad transformers (rdr, stt, wrt), and STM/MVar concurrency (stm, ntv, nmv, fork)

File templates under New File â€” Haskell Module, Haskell Script, and Haskell Test â€” plus a Haskell entry in the New Project wizard that scaffolds a minimal src/Main.hs.

Getting Started

Quick Start

  1. Install the plugin from JetBrains Marketplace
  2. Configure your GHC/Stack/Cabal SDK under Settings > Languages & Frameworks > Haskell (or download one via Tools > Haskell > Download GHC SDK)
  3. Create a new .hs file or open an existing Haskell project
  4. Start coding with syntax highlighting, completion, and live templates
  5. Press Alt+Shift+Enter to send code to the integrated GHCi REPL

Productivity Tips

  • Type fn + Tab for an instant function definition with type signature
  • Alt+Shift+Enter to send the current selection to GHCi
  • Ctrl+Shift+F10 to :load the current file into GHCi
  • Ctrl+Q on a function with a Haddock comment to see quick documentation
  • Alt+7 to open the Structure View for the current file
  • Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N to jump to any top-level declaration
  • Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F to format with ormolu / fourmolu / stylish-haskell

Customization

  • Color scheme: File > Settings > Editor > Color Scheme > Haskell
  • Live templates: File > Settings > Editor > Live Templates > Haskell
  • Code style: File > Settings > Editor > Code Style > Haskell
  • SDK path: File > Settings > Languages & Frameworks > Haskell

Troubleshooting

  • File not recognized? Check Settings > Editor > File Types > Flexible Haskell â€” ensure *.hs is listed
  • No completions? Make sure HLS is installed and the SDK path is set correctly in Haskell settings
  • GHCi not starting? Verify ghci (or stack exec ghci) is on your system PATH

Actively Developed

Flexible Haskell is a young project and we ship updates constantly. See the full changelog for every release.

We'd Love Your Feedback

Feature requests, bug reports, and general feedback are very welcome! You can reach us:

  • GitHub Issues: flexible-haskell-jetbrains-plugin
  • Email: info@ilscipio.com
  • Website: ilscipio.com

Made by Developers with a Passion for Functional Programming

The integration is the work of Ilscipio:

We develop software solutions and understand the unique needs of Haskell developers. We created this plugin to make Haskell development more intuitive and productive in JetBrains IDEs.

We're sharing this tool with the Haskell community to support the ecosystem's growth and to make functional programming more accessible.

  • Special discounts are available for individual developers & of course for the whole Open Source community.

Bugs & Feature Requests

Found a bug or have a feature request? Please open a GitHub issue â€” that's where we track and respond to reports. You can also reach us at info@ilscipio.com or via Ilscipio.

idea-plugin.name: LockLane
idea-plugin.description:
LockLane plans safe Python dependency upgrades with conflict-aware guidance. Supports requirements.txt, requirements.in, and pyproject.toml (PEP 621 and Poetry).

Features

  • Baseline view — see all current pinned and resolved dependency versions at a glance
  • Upgrade planning — scans dependencies for available updates and classifies each as safe, blocked, or inconclusive
  • Conflict detection — shows exactly which transitive dependencies block an upgrade, with full conflict chain details
  • Vulnerability scanning — checks dependencies against the OSV database for known security issues
  • Changelog links — quick links to changelogs and project pages from the plan view
  • Per-package selective apply — choose exactly which updates to apply with checkboxes
  • Verification — runs your test suite against proposed changes in a disposable venv before touching any files
  • Apply with dry-run — preview changes before writing, with automatic lock file regeneration
  • Rollback history — restore previous manifest versions if an update causes issues
  • Gutter icons — see update status (patch/minor/major) next to each dependency in the editor
  • Auto-scan — automatically checks for updates when you open a project
  • Ignore list — exclude packages you don't want to upgrade
  • Resolver flexibility — uses uv by default with pip-tools as automatic fallback

Requirements

  • Python 3 on PATH or configured in settings
  • uv or pip-tools

The Python resolver is bundled inside the plugin — no extra setup needed beyond the above. Use Settings > Tools > LockLane > Validate Setup to check your environment.

idea-plugin.name: Remote Build Trigger
idea-plugin.description:
Starts an embedded HTTP server inside IntelliJ IDEA that allows triggering a project build remotely via a simple HTTP GET request.

Usage

Once the plugin is active and a project is open, send a GET request to:

GET http://localhost:48766/build

The call is blocking – it returns only after the build has finished:

  • HTTP 200 – Build succeeded (no errors)
  • HTTP 500 – Build failed (response body contains the error description)

Configuration

The default port is 48766. You can change it under Settings → Tools → Remote Build Trigger.
idea-plugin.change-notes: 1.0.0 - Initial release: HTTP endpoint to trigger IntelliJ builds remotely.

Protect your Python desktop applications with encryption, licensing, and secure distribution.

idea-plugin.name: Run Configuration Bridge
idea-plugin.description:
Expose your IntelliJ Run/Debug configurations through a local REST API and WebSocket server, enabling AI coding agents and automation tools to execute with full IDE context.

Why Run Configuration Bridge?

Running mvn test in a terminal is not the same as clicking Run in IntelliJ. Run Configuration Bridge lets external tools execute your configurations with all the environment variables, JVM arguments, before-launch tasks, and debug settings you've already configured.

Features

  • REST API — List, start, stop, and monitor run configurations programmatically
  • Structured Output — Read process output with stdout/stderr typing
  • Debug Mode — Start configurations with the debugger attached
  • Process Tracking — Monitor all running processes, Bridge-started and manual
  • WebSocket Streaming — Live typed output via WebSocket
  • Web Dashboard — Visual configuration management at localhost
  • Zero Config — Works immediately when your IDE opens

Use Cases

  • AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) that need structured execution
  • Multi-agent orchestration — each agent runs and monitors its own configs
  • Service monitoring dashboards for microservice development
  • Automated testing workflows with proper exit code handling

Works alongside Terminal Bridge for complete IDE automation.

Runs entirely on localhost. No data leaves your machine.

API available at http://localhost:9877/api/v1/

idea-plugin.name: Flexible Swift
idea-plugin.description:
Swift and iOS IDE with an AI assistant and MCP server, LLDB debugger, iOS Simulator, smart completion, code intelligence, and live templates for JetBrains.

We are a young project and your feedback matters! Feature requests, bug reports, and ideas are very welcome. Reach out on GitHub, via email at info@ilscipio.com, or anywhere else you find us. Your first feedback earns a 20% discount on the annual subscription: email us, or post a Marketplace review and send us the link.

Core Features

Language Support

  • Complete Swift 5.x grammar with keyword highlighting, generics, key path expressions, and string interpolation
  • Plist support with syntax highlighting, code completion, documentation, and semantic annotations
  • Advanced syntax highlighting with customizable color schemes (Default, Darcula, IntelliJ Light)
  • Semantic annotator for functions, types, parameters, imports, and properties
  • Code folding for functions, blocks, and comments
  • Brace matching with auto-close for {, (, [ and navigation
  • Comment support for line (//) and block (/* */) comments
  • Swift attributes (@IBOutlet, @objc, @available, etc.)
  • Code formatting (Ctrl+Alt+L)

Navigation & Intelligence

  • Go to Declaration (Ctrl+Click) for functions, types, and variables with cross-file resolution
  • Go to Implementation (Ctrl+Alt+B) across your entire project
  • Find Usages (Alt+F7) across your entire project
  • Go to Symbol and Go to Class for quick navigation
  • Structure View with icons for functions, classes, structs, enums, and protocols
  • Call Hierarchy (Ctrl+Alt+H) showing callers and callees for any function or method
  • Breadcrumbs navigation showing scope hierarchy
  • File-based symbol index for fast cross-file lookup
  • On-hover documentation for ~370 Swift standard library symbols (Ctrl+Q)

Smart Completion & Hints

  • Context-aware code completion with local symbols, dot completion, and contextual keywords
  • SwiftUI modifier completions for view building
  • 13 postfix templates — type .if, .guard, .let, .print, .unwrap, .forEach, .map, .filter, .sorted, .try, .await, .optional, .force after any expression and press Tab to expand
  • Smart Enter (Shift+Cmd+Enter) auto-completes brace blocks for functions, types, and control flow
  • Doc comment continuation — pressing Enter at the end of a /// line automatically starts the next /// line
  • Inlay hints for parameter names and types
  • Parameter info tooltips for function signatures (Ctrl+P)

AI Assistant

  • AI tab — the first tab of the Swift tool window; a chat panel that talks to the coding agent you already use, inside the IDE
  • Agent CLI backends — Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Windsurf, and Aider; auto-detected, or pick one in Settings
  • External API providers — Ollama (local), OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini over HTTP, with per-provider model selection
  • Permission modes — Plan only, Edit files, or Auto, so the agent asks before it changes anything
  • Context attachments — reference files with @, capture a screenshot of any editor region, or drag files and images into the prompt
  • Conversation history per project, with plan, thinking, and tool-call cards rendered inline
  • Fully optional — clear "Enable AI features" in Settings and the AI tab and the MCP server disappear for that project

MCP Server

  • Model Context Protocol server built into the IDE, so an external AI agent can drive your Swift project directly
  • 18 tools — project info, SwiftPM packages, build, test, run configurations and sessions, run output, IDE diagnostics, symbols, iOS Simulator, and breakpoints
  • One server per IDE window on 127.0.0.1 (default port 8577), serving every open project; bearer-token auth and loopback only
  • One-click install into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Antigravity, or Windsurf, or copy the config JSON yourself
  • Several projects at once — pass a project by name or path, and swift_list_projects also finds other IDE windows running the server

Run Configurations

  • Swift run configuration for executing Swift scripts and packages
  • Run line markers in editor gutter for quick execution
  • iOS Simulator run configuration with xcodebuild integration, scheme and configuration selection
  • Corellium cloud device run configuration
  • Appetize.io cloud simulator run configuration
  • Console filter with clickable file:line references in output

Debugger

  • LLDB debugger via Debug Adapter Protocol (lldb-dap)
  • iOS Simulator debugging — click Debug on an iOS Simulator run configuration to build, install, launch the app suspended, and attach LLDB automatically
  • Line breakpoints in .swift files, set before or during a debug session
  • Step over, step into, step out, resume controls
  • Local variable inspection at breakpoints

Tool Windows

  • Swift tool window gathers the AI chat, Packages and Appetize.io into one panel with tabs — AI leads — and carries the MCP server toggle in its title bar
  • iOS Simulator and Swift View Outline stay separate, each with its own icon — the simulator because simctl is macOS-only, the outline because it tracks the open editor
  • All three appear only when the project looks like a Swift project — a Package.swift, an .xcodeproj/.xcworkspace, a .swift source, or a configured Swift SDK
  • SwiftUI Preview — renders a #Preview, a PreviewProvider, or any View with a no-argument init to an image, right next to the editor; tracks the open file like the outline

SwiftUI Preview

  • Xcode projects — the app is built with xcodebuild (Debug, iOS Simulator) exactly as Xcode builds it, so packages, asset catalogs, macros and bridging headers all work; a small preview library is linked into the app, which renders the view and saves a PNG
  • Swift packages — the package is built with xcodebuild and a small host app links the built products
  • Loose files — a single SwiftUI file without a project renders headlessly on macOS, with an iOS Simulator fallback
  • Gutter icons on every #Preview, PreviewProvider and previewable View; light and dark mode; auto-refresh on save
  • Only #Preview renders — as in Xcode. A view without one gets a ready-made #Preview block in the panel, with inferred sample arguments, the environment objects the project uses, and an in-memory SwiftData container; one click inserts it into the file
  • Render on demand — the Render button or the gutter icon starts a render; switching files never does. Auto-refresh on save is optional
  • Environment objects — @EnvironmentObject and @Environment(Type.self) dependencies of the project are supplied automatically when the type has an init or a static let sample; your own instances under Settings > Swift > Preview > View modifiers win
  • Sample arguments — a View whose init needs parameters renders with synthesised sample values (strings, numbers, first enum case, static let sample, nested structs); enter your own arguments in the panel, and keep project-wide sample data and .environment(...) modifiers under Settings > Swift > Preview
  • Readable failures — the panel names the stage that failed (xcodebuild, harness compile, install, launch, render), shows the command and its output, and a Copy Diagnostics button collects everything for a bug report
  • Remote Mac — on Linux and Windows, select an SSH profile under Settings > Swift > Remote Mac: the project is synced to the Mac (changed files only), built and rendered there, and the image comes back; Swift Tools > Sync Project to Mac uploads on demand, and an optional sync-on-save keeps the copy fresh
  • Without a Mac, local or remote, the panel says so

iOS Simulator

  • iOS Simulator tool window for managing iOS devices; appears only on macOS with Xcode
  • Device management via xcrun simctl (boot, shutdown, erase, open)
  • Device selection for run configurations

Xcode Project Support

  • The new Xcode project format — Xcode 27.2 writes project.xcproj, a JSON file, instead of project.pbxproj. The plugin reads it.
  • No xcodebuild needed — targets, product types, build configurations, build settings and Swift package dependencies are read straight from the file, so this also works on Windows and Linux
  • Both formats — projects that still use project.pbxproj keep working
  • One-click migration — Tools > Swift > Migrate Xcode Project to JSON Format backs up the old file, runs the conversion, checks the result, then deletes the old file. On Windows and Linux it uses your Remote Mac
  • Syntax banner — if a project.xcproj file has a syntax error, the editor shows it at the top
  • iOS App template — the New Project wizard creates a working SwiftUI app with an Xcode project, a shared scheme and an asset catalog. A checkbox picks the file format
  • Xcode file type associations — .entitlements, .xcscheme, .intentdefinition open as XML; .storekit, .xcstrings open as JSON; project.xcproj opens as JSON5
  • SwiftPM project detection — parses Package.swift, discovers targets, and decorates the project tree

Package Management

  • Packages tab in the unified Swift tool window, with three sub-tabs — Installed, Search, and Tree
  • Installed tab — lists all dependencies from Package.swift with their requirement and resolved version; Resolve and Update All buttons run swift package resolve/update; right-click a row to Copy Package URL, Open on GitHub, Open on Swift Package Index, or Remove
  • Outdated version detection — fetches the latest GitHub release for each installed package and highlights outdated rows in amber with the available version shown alongside
  • Search tab — searches GitHub for Swift packages; results include star counts and latest version (fetched asynchronously); right-click to Add to Package.swift or browse; uses swift package add-dependency (Swift 5.9+) with automatic fallback to text editing
  • Tree tab — shows the full transitive dependency graph from swift package show-dependencies; live search field filters the tree by name as you type; ancestor nodes are kept for context; double-click any node to open it on GitHub
  • Package.swift inlay hints — shows the resolved version locked in Package.resolved inline next to each .package(url:...) entry (toggleable under Editor → Inlay Hints)
  • Package.swift gutter icons — click the icon next to any .package(url:...) line to open the package on Swift Package Index
  • Package.swift validation banner — runs swift package dump-package when the file is opened and shows a red error panel with the exact Swift error if the manifest is invalid

Live Templates (15+)

Type sw: to access all templates:

Definitions:

  • sw:func - Function definition
  • sw:class - Class definition
  • sw:struct - Struct definition
  • sw:enum - Enum definition with cases
  • sw:protocol - Protocol definition
  • sw:extension - Extension definition
  • sw:actor - Actor definition
  • sw:init - Initializer definition

Control Flow:

  • sw:guard - Guard statement with else clause
  • sw:iflet - If-let optional binding
  • sw:for - For-in loop
  • sw:switch - Switch statement with case/default
  • sw:do - Do-catch block

Concurrency:

  • sw:async - Async function (with throws support)
  • sw:task - Task block
  • sw:closure - Closure expression with parameters

Code Quality

  • Inspections for force try (try!) and force unwrap (!) with warnings
  • SwiftLint integration — inline violation annotations with rule name and severity; auto-detects .swiftlint.yml in the project root
  • External formatter — reformat with SwiftFormat or swift-format on demand (Opt+Cmd+L) or automatically on save
  • Intention actions (Alt+Enter): convert to guard, convert to if-let, convert to string interpolation
  • Surround with (Ctrl+Alt+T) for wrapping code in if, if-else, for-in, while, guard, do-try-catch, or func
  • Spellchecking in comments and string literals with a bundled Swift-aware dictionary
  • TODO/FIXME/HACK indexing — items appear in the TODO tool window (View → Tool Windows → TODO)
  • File templates for Swift File, Class, Struct, Protocol, Actor, Enum, and Extension (7 total)
  • Apple Strings file support (.strings) with syntax highlighting for keys, values, and comments

Made by Developers with a Passion for Mobile Development

The integration is the work of Ilscipio:

We develop mobile and cross-platform solutions as part of our technology stack and understand the unique needs of iOS and Swift developers. We created this plugin to bring Swift development to JetBrains IDEs.

  • Special discounts are available for individual developers & of course for the whole Open Source community.

Bugs & Feature Requests

If you have any questions, feature requests or stumble upon the occasional bug, come leave us a message on GitHub, send an email to info@ilscipio.com, or visit us at Ilscipio First-time feedback earns a 20% discount on the annual subscription, by email or by Marketplace review.

idea-plugin.name: Flexible For Arduino
idea-plugin.description:
Embedded development for ESP32, Arduino, STM32, nRF52 & RP2040 with AI support. Build, flash, JTAG debug, profile, OTA, serial monitor, pin viewer. Chat with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Ollama, and more. For ESP-IDF, Arduino CLI, PlatformIO, Zephyr.

We are a young project and your feedback shapes the plugin. Feature requests, bug reports, or just your opinion — leave a review, open an issue on GitHub, or email us at info@ilscipio.com.

Core Features

Build, Flash & Monitor

  • Build backends — ESP-IDF (idf.py), Arduino CLI, PlatformIO, and Zephyr/West
  • One-click build, flash, and monitor with a single run configuration and mode selector (Build · Flash · Monitor · Build & Flash)
  • Configurable flash options — COM port, baud rate, flash mode, and upload method per run
  • Build output with error display and navigation to source

Serial Monitor

  • COM port auto-detection with ESP32/Arduino VID/PID filtering
  • Configurable baud rate from 9600 to 921600
  • Terminal display with auto-scroll, clear, timestamps, and line-ending options
  • Send commands to the device; DTR/RTS control; auto-reconnect
  • Board/port sync — selecting a board in the Pin Viewer instantly updates the Serial Monitor and vice versa
  • Explain With AI — send the last output, crash backtrace, or boot loop to the AI assistant with one click

AI Support

  • Bring your own agent — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Windsurf, or Aider, auto-detected; or an API: Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini
  • Chat tool window with streaming answers, file references, screenshots, and conversation history
  • Quick actions in the editor — Explain, Improve, Fix This Problem, Add Comments, and Ask Arduino AI (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+A) from the right-click menu, the floating toolbar, and Alt+Enter; "Explain With AI" in the Serial Monitor
  • MCP server — 21 Arduino tools (build, flash, serial, sdkconfig, backtrace decoding, …) with one-click install into your agent

Language Intelligence (Arduino C++)

  • Syntax highlighting for keywords, types, preprocessor, strings, and comments — customizable color scheme
  • Code completion with Arduino builtins, Serial., Wire., and SPI. dot-completion, scope-aware local variables and functions
  • Hover documentation pulled from the Arduino language reference
  • Structure view showing functions, classes, enums, and namespaces
  • Code folding for functions, classes, comments, and #if/#ifdef blocks
  • Formatter, brace matcher, quote handler, and commenter (// and /* */)
  • Semantic annotations highlighting Arduino constants and built-in identifiers

Pin Viewer & Sketch Pin Mapper

  • IC chip diagram — visual board layout with clickable pins that sync to the table
  • Boards: ESP32, ESP32-S2/S3/C2/C3/C5/C6/H2/P4, ESP8266, Arduino Uno/Nano/Mega/Leonardo, RP2040 Pico/Pico 2, Teensy 4.0/4.1, nRF52840, STM32 Nucleo-F4, Blue Pill, Black Pill
  • Pin capabilities table — GPIO number, name, capabilities, usage in sketch, and status (In Use / Available / Reserved / Input Only)
  • Sketch Pin Mapper — detects const int, #define, and variable pin assignments in your sketch; reassign any pin via dropdown and apply to source code in one click
  • Board selection syncs across Pin Viewer and Serial Monitor

SDK & Library Management

  • ESP-IDF auto-detection — finds IDF_PATH, toolchains, and Python environment automatically
  • SDK notification banner guides setup when ESP-IDF is not configured
  • Board Manager — searchable board index, plus Additional Board Manager URLs for third-party packages such as ESP8266 or STM32; install, update, and remove cores from Settings | Boards
  • Library Manager — search, install, and manage Arduino libraries; one-click install for LVGL, TFT_eSPI, and Adafruit GFX
  • Multi-version support for ESP-IDF v4.x and v5.x

Debugging & Profiling (Pro)

  • JTAG/GDB debugging via OpenOCD — breakpoints, stepping, and watch expressions integrated into the JetBrains Debug tool window
  • OTA (Over-the-Air) upload for wireless firmware updates over the network
  • Memory Analyzer — visualize firmware RAM and Flash usage per section and component
  • Device Profiler — runtime performance profiling streamed from the device

Configuration Editors

  • sdkconfig editor with search, category grouping, and an inline tool window for quick edits
  • Blockly visual editor for sketch files — drag-and-drop block programming that generates Arduino C++ code

Board Support

FamilyBoards
ESP32ESP32, ESP32-S2, ESP32-S3, ESP32-C2, ESP32-C3, ESP32-C5, ESP32-C6, ESP32-H2, ESP32-P4
ESP8266D1 Mini / NodeMCU (ESP8266EX)
ArduinoUno (ATmega328P), Nano, Mega (ATmega2560), Leonardo (ATmega32U4), Uno R4 (RA4M1), MKR WiFi 1010, Nano Every, Nano 33 IoT, Nano 33 BLE
TeensyTeensy 4.0 / 4.1 (NXP i.MX RT1062)
STM32Nucleo-F4 (STM32F401RE), Blue Pill (STM32F103C8T6), Black Pill (STM32F411CEU6), GIGA R1 WiFi (STM32H747)
OtherRaspberry Pi Pico (RP2040), Pico 2 (RP2350), Nordic nRF52840 DK

Getting Started

  1. Install from JetBrains Marketplace
  2. Open or create an ESP32/Arduino project (.ino sketch or ESP-IDF CMakeLists.txt)
  3. Configure the SDK path at Settings → Languages & Frameworks → Arduino/ESP-IDF
  4. Select your board and COM port in the Arduino tool window at the bottom
  5. Hit Build, Flash, or Build & Flash from the toolbar or the Tools → Arduino menu

Tips

  • Tools → Arduino menu gives access to all actions including Debug, OTA, and Memory Analyzer
  • Arduino tool window (bottom) has tabs: Serial Monitor, Pin Viewer, and Device Profiler

Made by Developers Who Ship on ESP32

The integration is the work of Ilscipio:

We build IoT and embedded systems as part of our own products and wanted a solid development experience inside JetBrains — without leaving the IDE to use a different editor for every board. This plugin is the result.

We are not affiliated with Espressif, Arduino, PlatformIO, or any board vendor. We just really like these boards.

  • Special discounts are available for individual developers and the open-source community.

idea-plugin.name: Easy Dev
idea-plugin.description:
Convenient Intellij Platform Plugin for Deploying and Upgrading Services during Development

Easy Dev is a plugin I developed based on the Easy-Deploy plugin with some personalized enhancements. Compared to Easy-Deploy, my plugin has simplified certain functional business constraints and adapted to support a broader range of IDEA versions (IDEA 2022.3+).

Therefore, the plugin provides a simpler approach to terminal-based server management, offering features such as quick commands and task orchestration to help developers customize their workflows and simplify the release process. I named this plugin "Easy Dev" in the hope that it will help developers streamline their development and deployment workflows. I will continually optimize it and enhance its features.

Features

  • Batch execute remote commands
  • Batch open multiple SSH terminal connections
  • Batch add server information
  • Custom pipeline task orchestration
  • Custom quick commands
  • Add/Edit/Remove/Search server information
  • Add/Edit/Remove/Share/Search commands and show command details
  • Upload files or directories with filtering support, include or exclude self
  • Deploy services
  • Pre/Post-upload command execution support
  • Command execution directory override (use upload path)
  • Remote class hot update
  • Open terminal
  • SSH password-free login (private key login)
  • SSH jump host
  • Run/Debug Configuration (parallel deployment)
  • I18n support
  • SFTP transfer panel
  • Plugin settings
  • Export & Import & Clean plugin configuration

issue: easy-deploy

方便开发过程中部署升级服务的 Intellij 平台插件

Easy Dev 是我在Easy-Deploy插件的基础上， 做了一些个性化的功能增强。相比较于Easy-Deploy，我开发的插件去掉了部分限制，适配兼容了更加宽泛的 IDEA 版本（IDEA 2022.3+），支持更丰富的功能。

因此，插件提供了更简单的方式，面向终端管理服务器，提供了快捷指令、任务编排等功能，帮助开发者的自定已部分工作流，简化发布的过程。我给这个插件起这个名是希望他能够帮助简化研发部署工作流，我会不断地优化它，完善它的功能。

功能

  • 批量执行远程指令
  • 批量打开多个ssh终端连接
  • 批量添加服务器信息
  • 自定义任务编排
  • 自定义快捷指令
  • 添加/编辑/删除/搜索服务器信息
  • 添加/编辑/删除/分享/搜索命令，并查看详情
  • 上传文件或者目录，并支持过滤，可选包含或不包含自身
  • 文件（目录）上传配置
  • 前置/后置命令执行支持
  • 命令执行目录覆盖（使用上传路径）
  • 远程类热更新
  • 终端连接
  • SSH 免密登录（私钥登录）
  • SSH 代理跳板机
  • Run/Debug Configuration (并行部署)
  • 国际化
  • SFTP 传输面板
  • 插件设置
  • 导出、导入、清除插件配置

idea-plugin.name: MavenQuickBuild
idea-plugin.description:
m

Maven Quick Build

One-click Maven builds directly from the toolbar

Maven Quick Build adds two toolbar buttons to IntelliJ IDEA for running the most common Maven lifecycle in a single click — no need to open the Maven tool window, type goals, or configure run configurations every time.

Toolbar Buttons

Button Mac Win / Linux Command
!m Skip Tests ⌘+⌥+S Ctrl+Alt+S mvn clean install -Dmaven.test.skip=true
m With Tests ⌘+⌥+M Ctrl+Alt+M mvn clean install

Features

  • Buttons appear in MainToolBar and NavBarToolBar — always one click away
  • Buttons are automatically disabled when no project is open
  • Buttons are hidden in non-Maven projects — no clutter
  • Keyboard shortcuts available out of the box — no configuration required
  • Uses the native MavenRunner API — output streams directly to the IDE's run console
  • The skip-tests variant never mutates global Maven settings — fully safe

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA Community or Ultimate (2024.1 or later)
  • The open project must use Maven as its build system
Open source — GitHub Repository
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • GitHub Actions CI/CD workflows for automated build, verification, and release
  • Default keyboard shortcuts for plugin actions (Cmd+Option+S / Cmd+Option+M on Mac, Ctrl+Alt+S / Ctrl+Alt+M on Win/Linux)
  • JetBrains Marketplace badge and installation link in README
  • Vendor metadata in plugin.xml

Changed

  • Plugin description moved to dedicated pluginDescription.html file

idea-plugin.name: Easy Jenkins
idea-plugin.description: Quickly trigger Jenkins pipeline builds from IntelliJ IDEA via a keyboard shortcut.

idea-plugin.name: Toolbar Launcher
idea-plugin.description:
One-click toolbar buttons to run any build command — fully customizable.

Toolbar Launcher adds configurable toolbar buttons to IntelliJ IDEA and PhpStorm for running Maven, Gradle, npm, shell, scripts, and more — no need to open tool windows or configure run configurations every time.

Features

  • Fully configurable — add, edit, or remove toolbar buttons from Settings → Tools → Toolbar Launcher
  • Supports Maven, Gradle, npm, yarn, Make, Docker, and shell commands per button
  • Right-click a button → Configure... to open that button directly in the edit dialog under Settings → Tools → Toolbar Launcher
  • Set any command per button (e.g. clean package -Pproduction or ./gradlew test)
  • Assign custom keyboard shortcuts per button directly in the settings panel
  • Choose a built-in icon or pick any custom SVG from your filesystem per button
  • Buttons appear in the IDE toolbar — always one click away
  • Buttons are automatically disabled when no project is open
  • Shell commands run in the project root via $SHELL -c (or cmd.exe /c on Windows), with output in the Run tool window
  • Maven commands use the native MavenRunner API — output streams to the IDE's run console
  • Maven properties (e.g. -Dmaven.test.skip=true) never mutate global settings — fully safe
  • Enable or disable individual buttons without removing them from Settings → Tools → Toolbar Launcher

Default Buttons

ButtonShortcut (Mac)Shortcut (Win/Linux)Command
Maven Clean Install (skip tests)Cmd+Option+SCtrl+Alt+Sclean install -Dmaven.test.skip=true
Maven Clean InstallCmd+Option+MCtrl+Alt+Mclean install

Configuration

Open Settings → Tools → Toolbar Launcher to manage your buttons:

  • Add — set a label, command type, command string, icon, and optional keyboard shortcut
  • Edit — update any field of an existing button (or double-click a row)
  • Configure from toolbar — right-click a button and choose Configure... to open its edit dialog
  • Remove — delete a button from the toolbar
  • Reorder — use the Move Up / Move Down arrows to change the button order
  • Enable / Disable — toggle the checkbox in the table to hide/show a button without removing it
  • Type — choose from Maven, Gradle, npm, yarn, Make, Shell, or Docker; changing the type sets its command template and matching built-in icon
  • Custom SVG — browse your filesystem to use any SVG file as a button icon
  • Keyboard shortcut — click the shortcut field and press any key combination; shortcuts are registered with the IDE's Keymap system and can also be changed via Settings → Keymap
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Right-click a Toolbar Launcher button and choose Configure to open that button's edit dialog in Settings → Tools → Toolbar Launcher.

idea-plugin.name: Angular/Nx Scaffolder
idea-plugin.description:
Angular/Nx Scaffolder

Stop burning AI tokens on boilerplate. This plugin generates production-ready Angular/Nx library scaffolding in seconds — with correct structure, test setup, and barrel exports — directly from the IDE context menu.

Library Generators

Right-click any folder inside libs/ → New → ng-nx-scaffolder:

  • Feature Library — container component, store (signalStore), facade, form service, mapper, routing
  • Data Access Library — HttpClient service with spec
  • UI Library — standalone component with spec, HTML, SCSS
  • Model Library — TypeScript interface/model file
  • Util Library — utility function with spec

Features

  • Tree preview of all files before generation
  • Automatic Nx workspace detection
  • Optional type suffix for library names (-feature, -data-access, -model, -ui, -util)
  • Publishable library support (ng-package.json, package.json)
  • Flattens Nx 18+ nested directory output automatically
  • Fixes tsconfig path aliases and project names after generation
  • Preserves workspace files (.prettierignore, nx.json) from Nx side effects
  • Duplicate library name detection
  • Configurable selector prefix and Nx generator in Settings → Tools → Angular/Nx Scaffolder

How to Use

  1. Right-click on a folder inside libs/ (or any subfolder)
  2. Select New → ng-nx-scaffolder → [Library Type]
  3. Enter the library name (kebab-case)
  4. Review the file preview and click OK

Requirements

  • Angular 17+ — generated code uses standalone components, inject(), and @ngrx/signals signalStore
  • Nx 16+ workspace with @nx/angular installed
  • Node.js installed and accessible
  • IntelliJ IDEA / WebStorm 2024.1+

idea-plugin.name: typst-renderer
idea-plugin.description:
Full Typst support for IntelliJ-based IDEs — syntax highlighting, live PDF preview, LSP-powered completions and diagnostics, zero-config setup.

Features

All features work out of the box — no manual installation of binaries required.

📄 Preview, live or as PDF

A split editor panel shows your document alongside the source, rendered one of two ways and chosen with the Live / PDF button in the preview toolbar:

  • Live (default) — rendered by tinymist as you type. Edits appear within milliseconds, with no save and no PDF written to disk. The preview follows your cursor, and clicking it jumps the editor to the matching source.
  • PDF — the exported PDF itself, shown in the built-in viewer. Updates when you save, Compile or Export, preserving scroll position within a session and, optionally, across IDE restarts.

Each editor tab keeps its own setting, so one file can be live while another shows its PDF. Compile and Export never change which renderer a tab is using.

📌 Pin a main entry file

In a project where main.typ #includes a tree of chapters, opening a chapter on its own compiles it in isolation — so every cross-file reference reports "label does not exist". Right-click a file and choose Pin as Typst Main File and the whole project compiles through that entry instead: cross-references resolve, the phantom errors go, and the preview shows the complete document while you edit any chapter. Editors that resolve to the same pinned main share a single live preview rather than each running their own.

⚡ Full LSP Integration

Powered by tinymist — the most complete Typst language server. Includes: code completion, diagnostics, hover docs, go-to-definition, formatting, and rename refactoring.

🎨 Syntax Highlighting

Full colour syntax highlighting for .typ files — keywords, functions, strings, comments, and more.

⌨️ Compile Action

Single-shot compile with Ctrl+Shift+T. Uses tinymist's exportPdf command — no separate Typst CLI required. Errors route directly to the Typst Output console with clickable file links.

💬 Comment Toggling

Toggle line and block comments in .typ files with the standard shortcuts: Ctrl+/ and Ctrl+Shift+/.

📋 Typst Output Console

Dedicated tool window showing compilation output. Errors are displayed with clickable links that jump to the offending line.

📁 Project Root Resolver

Automatically determines the Typst project root via a priority chain: explicit project override → auto-detection from file location.

📥 Auto-download tinymist

On first use, the plugin auto-downloads tinymist from GitHub for your platform. No Cargo or Homebrew needed.

🔄 tinymist in step with the plugin

Each plugin release is built and tested against one tinymist version. A tinymist the plugin downloaded always matches it, and changes when the plugin updates — so a new tinymist, and the new version of the Typst language it brings, arrives only in a release that has been tested with it. A tinymist you installed yourself is never touched; the plugin tells you when it is older than the tested version, with the option to skip that version or stop asking.

Live Preview

Edit and preview side by side, with the preview keeping up as you type — no save, no compile step.

Choosing the renderer

The Live / PDF button at the top-left of the preview toolbar switches the pane between the two renderers, per editor tab. Default preview mode in settings decides what a newly opened tab starts with; Live is the default. The same action is available from the editor's right-click menu and from Find Action, so it can be given a keyboard shortcut.

If a live preview cannot start — an old tinymist, a refused port — the pane falls back to the PDF renderer by itself and explains why in the Typst Output console.

Worth knowing

  • In Live mode, saving no longer writes a PDF. The live renderer draws without producing a file, so the PDF on disk is written only when you ask for one with Compile (Ctrl+Shift+T) or Export. If you have a build script watching the export directory, or an external viewer open on the file, switch the pane to PDF or set Default preview mode to PDF.
  • A compile error leaves the live pane showing the last good version. A document that has never compiled shows an empty pane rather than an error page. The errors are still reported in the editor gutter and the Typst Output console. PDF mode shows an error page instead, if you prefer that.
  • Clicking the preview jumps to the source. If the target file is already open in front of you, the line is highlighted but the cursor and keyboard focus stay in the preview — click into the editor to carry on typing. Jumping to a file that is not already open places the cursor and moves focus normally.
  • Editors showing the same document share one preview. With a main file pinned, every open chapter renders through a single preview rather than one each, so they also scroll together.

Language Intelligence

Full LSP support via tinymist — auto-downloaded and wired up, no extra steps needed.

✨ Code Completion

Context-aware completions for Typst functions, variables, labels, import paths, and built-in symbols. Trigger with Ctrl+Space.

⚠️ Real-time Diagnostics

Errors and warnings appear as inline squiggles as you type. Undefined labels, type mismatches, and syntax errors surface instantly.

📖 Hover Documentation

Hover over any function or variable to see inline documentation directly in the editor.

🔍 Go-to-definition

Jump to the definition of labels, variables, and imported functions across files with Ctrl+Click or F12.

✏️ Rename Refactoring

Rename labels, variables, and references across the project with Shift+F6. All usages update automatically.

🎯 Formatting

Format your Typst documents with the standard IDE reformat action, powered by tinymist's built-in formatter.

Typst Output Console

All compilation errors and warnings route to the dedicated Typst Output console. Errors are clickable and jump to the offending line.

Settings & Project Overrides

Access via Settings → Tools → Typst Renderer.

Global Settings

SettingDescription
Language Server (Tinymist)Status shows detected path. Leave blank to auto-detect. Click Download Tinymist to fetch the tinymist version this plugin is tested with from GitHub.
Tell me when a tinymist I installed myself is older than the version this plugin is tested withOn by default. A tinymist downloaded by the plugin always matches the tested version; one you installed through Cargo, Homebrew, Scoop, winget or by hand is never written over, so the plugin tells you instead. The prompt offers Skip this version and Don't ask again — this setting is the way back from the latter.
Default preview modeWhich renderer a newly opened preview starts in — Live or PDF. Each editor tab can be switched with the toggle in its preview toolbar.
Update live preview on every keystrokeOn by default. Turn off to have the live preview refresh on save instead — worth it only for very large documents, where continuous recompilation costs more than the immediacy. No effect in PDF mode.
Scroll the live preview to follow the cursorOn by default. Keeps the preview on the passage you are editing. Editors sharing one preview scroll together. No effect in PDF mode.
Remember scroll positionRestores the PDF preview scroll position when re-opening a .typ file after an IDE restart.

Per-Project Overrides

Access via Settings → Tools → Typst Renderer → Project Overrides. Useful when working with monorepos or projects with non-default layout.

SettingDescription
Typst project rootDirectory used as the project root for tinymist and as the base for compilation. Leave blank to auto-detect from file location.
Export directoryDirectory where compiled PDFs are written (default: target). Relative paths are resolved from the project root.
Font pathDirectory containing extra fonts to make available to the Typst compiler and LSP. Leave blank to use system fonts only.

Installation

No external tools required. The plugin handles everything on first launch.

Via Marketplace (recommended)

  1. Open Settings / Preferences → Plugins → Marketplace
  2. Search for "typst-renderer"
  3. Click Install and restart the IDE
  4. Open any .typ file — tinymist will be auto-downloaded on first use

Requirements

  • IntelliJ-based IDE — Compatible with IntelliJ IDEA, Android Studio, CLion, GoLand, PyCharm, Rider, RustRover, WebStorm, and eight more.
  • IDE version — 2026.1 only (build 261.x). This release is not yet compatible with 2026.2: the platform's bundled LSP API changed in a binary-incompatible way, so the plugin is pinned to the 2026.1 line for now. 2026.2 support is tracked in issue #74.
  • Internet connection — Required on first launch to download tinymist from GitHub. Subsequent launches work fully offline.
  • Custom tinymist path — Already have tinymist installed? It will be detected automatically, or you can set a custom path in Settings.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • A notification when a tinymist you installed yourself is older than the version the plugin is tested with. A tinymist from Cargo, Homebrew, Scoop, winget or a manual download is never written over; instead the plugin tells you which version it expects, once per IDE session, with a link to that release's notes. Skip this version keeps it quiet until a plugin update moves to a newer tinymist, and Don't ask again switches it off — it can be turned back on under Settings > Tools > Typst Renderer. A tinymist newer than the tested version is left alone.

Changed

  • tinymist updated to v0.15.8 (from v0.15.2). Every command the plugin sends, and the shape of every answer it reads back, was checked against the new version and found unchanged; the live preview's own page was rebuilt upstream and still renders in the IDE's embedded browser.

Fixed

  • A tinymist downloaded by the plugin now follows the plugin when it updates. A binary used to be downloaded once and kept for good, so plugin updates that moved to a newer tinymist never reached existing installs — they stayed on whatever version they first downloaded. Downloads now live in a folder named after the version the plugin is built for, so a plugin update that changes it fetches the matching tinymist the next time a .typ file is opened, and removes the old one once nothing is running it. A plugin release that moves back to an earlier tinymist rolls the binary back the same way.
  • No language-server start attempt for a restored .typ tab whose folder no longer exists. A file opened from outside the project, whose folder had since been deleted or belonged to another machine, was still handed to a new language server on the next IDE start, which failed and logged a WorkingDirectoryNotFoundException. The folder is now checked on disk first.
  • Downloading tinymist from the settings while the language server was running failed on Windows, which refuses to delete or overwrite the image file of a live process. The old binary is now moved aside to free the name and removed once nothing is running it — and if the replacement cannot be completed, the original is put back rather than leaving no language server at all.

idea-plugin.name: OpenAPI SpecTacular
idea-plugin.description:
Generate realistic example objects from your OpenAPI specifications.

Features:

  • Right-click over the OpenApi Specification file
  • Parse OpenAPI 3.x and Swagger 2.x specifications (YAML and JSON)
  • Select the number of examples to generate per schema
  • Preview the generated output and copy it to the clipboard
  • Export examples as JSON or YAML, per schema or combined
  • Respects schema constraints (enums, min/max, lengths, oneOf/anyOf/allOf)
  • Validate OpenAPI specs and see parser errors and warnings
  • Configurable defaults in Settings | Tools | OpenAPI SpecTacular
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.0

  • Export examples as JSON or YAML, per schema or combined into a single file
  • Preview the generated output in the dialog and copy it to the clipboard
  • New action: Validate OpenAPI Specification, reporting parser errors and warnings
  • New settings page with configurable defaults in Settings | Tools | OpenAPI SpecTacular
  • Respect schema constraints: enums, min/max bounds, string lengths, oneOf/anyOf/allOf
  • Updated build tooling and dependencies

1.0.0

  • Initial release: generate realistic JSON examples from OpenAPI 3.x and Swagger 2.x specs

idea-plugin.name: Flexible for Flox
idea-plugin.description:
Manage Flox environments visually — packages, services, generations, FloxHub sync, and terminal activation in your IDE. Cross-OS installer with WSL2 support, manifest validation, build & containerize, and access to Nix packages.

This is an unofficial Flox extension. We love Flox and thought it deserves a better IDE integration. But to become a staple of the Flox community, we need your help. Your feedback is critical: Please leave a review, reach out to us on github, the community or email and tell us your thoughts, issues and more.

Core Features

One-Click Cross-OS Installer

  • Installs Flox on macOS (Homebrew), Debian/Ubuntu (apt), and Fedora/RHEL (dnf) in one click
  • Windows + WSL2: auto-detects WSL, installs Flox inside your default distro, then transparently wraps all commands as wsl -- flox ... — no PATH configuration needed
  • Background re-detection polls every 2 minutes so the UI recovers the moment Flox is available

Environment Detection & Status

  • Auto-detects .flox/ environments on project open
  • Status-bar widget showing environment name, package count, current generation, and FloxHub auth status
  • Flox and Nix version detection with auth status in Settings

Package Management

  • Searchable table of installed packages with name, version, group, and status columns
  • Inline search dialog against the Flox catalog (180,000+ Nixpkgs) via flox search
  • Install, Remove, Upgrade, and Upgrade All with background progress and confirmation prompts
  • Reactive refresh when manifest.toml or manifest.lock changes on disk

Services

  • List, Start, Stop, and Restart services defined in your manifest — per-service or all at once
  • Per-service live log streaming (flox services logs --follow) in an embedded console

Generation History & Rollback

  • View full generation history with metadata
  • Rollback to previous generation or Switch To any specific one
  • Diff any two generations' manifests, or compare against current state, in the JetBrains diff viewer

Environment Inspection

  • View [vars] table and hook.on-activate script content
  • Quick-open manifest.toml for direct editing

FloxHub Integration

  • Token-based Login / Logout / Auth Status
  • Push and Pull the current environment with smart conflict resolution (Sync & Push, Reset & Pull)
  • Authenticated user shown in status bar and Settings

Build, Publish & Containerize

  • Build Artifact (flox build <target>) for targets declared in [build] section
  • Publish built artifacts to FloxHub
  • Containerize environment as an OCI tarball

Terminal Integration

  • Auto-activates the Flox environment inside the built-in terminal (toggleable per-project)
  • WSL-aware: uses wsl -- bash -lc "flox activate -- bash" on Windows

Run Configurations

  • Custom Flox Run Configuration type with command, target, and argument support
  • Environment injection into IDE run configurations (auto-injects flox activation env vars)

Tool Window

  • Multi-tab interface: Packages, Services, Generations, Environment
  • Title-bar actions: Activate, Deactivate, Edit Manifest, Push, Pull, Login/Logout, Refresh, Settings
  • Keyboard shortcuts: Activate (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+A), Deactivate (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+D), Push (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+U), Pull (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+L)

Manifest Support

  • JSON schema for manifest.toml providing IDE completion and validation
  • File watcher with debounced refresh for .flox/, manifest.toml, manifest.lock, and env.json

Settings & Configuration

  • Flox binary path (auto-detect or manual override)
  • Auto-detect / auto-activate / terminal activation toggles
  • Command timeout and package-search cache duration
  • Update-check frequency (daily / weekly / manual)

Getting Started

Quick Start

  1. Install the plugin from JetBrains Marketplace
  2. Open any project — if Flox isn't installed, click Install Flox Now… in the startup prompt
  3. Create an environment via Tools > Flox > Initialize Flox Environment or open a project with an existing .flox/ directory
  4. Manage everything from the Flox tool window at the bottom of the IDE

Productivity Tips

  • Use the Packages tab to search and install any of 180,000+ Nixpkgs without leaving the IDE
  • Generations gives you Git-like undo for your entire dev environment
  • Editing manifest.toml triggers an automatic refresh — no manual reload needed
  • On Windows, every Flox command runs through WSL transparently once detected

Customization

  • Settings: File > Settings > Tools > Flexible for Flox
  • Status bar widget: Right-click the status bar to show/hide
  • Tool window: View > Tool Windows > Flox

We Are a Young Project — Your Feedback Matters

Flexible for Flox is new and actively developed. We would love to hear from you — whether it's a feature request, a bug report, or just your thoughts on the plugin. Reach out via email, on GitHub, through JetBrains Marketplace reviews, or anywhere else you find us.

Also: Flox deserves your love, too. Star them on GitHub, explore FloxHub, and join the Flox Slack.

Made by Developers Who Love Reproducible Environments

The integration is the work of Ilscipio:

We build developer tools that make complex workflows feel simple. We created this plugin because Flox deserves the same first-class IDE integration that other package managers enjoy — and JetBrains users shouldn't have to leave the editor to manage their environments.

  • Special discounts are available for individual developers & of course for the whole Open Source community.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by FloxDev, Inc.

Bugs & Feature Requests

If you have any questions, feature requests or stumble upon the occasional bug, come leave us a message at Ilscipio or on GitHub.

idea-plugin.name: Adaptive Tool Windows
idea-plugin.description:
Adaptive Tool Windows opens the tool windows you need and reshapes them to fit the size of your IDE window.

Show the Build tool window automatically

Whenever a build or a Gradle/Maven sync starts, the Build tool window is shown, so you can follow its progress without opening anything yourself.

Adapt the layout to wide windows

When the IDE window is wide — wider than an aspect ratio you pick, or wider than a pixel width you pick — the plugin can turn on the widescreen tool window layout and the side-by-side layout on the left and right. It can also set the width of the left and right tool windows and reopen the ones you had open there, then put all of it back when the window is narrow again.

Settings

Everything is optional and configurable under Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Adaptive Tool Windows.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Automatic widescreen and side-by-side tool window layout, switched on the window's aspect ratio or pixel width.
  • Tool window widths and split proportions remembered per window shape and per project, or set to fixed values for wide and narrow separately.
  • Reopening the tool windows that were open on each side.
  • A live diagram in the settings showing what wide and narrow will look like.
  • Configurable timing: how often the layout is checked while moving and while idle, how long it must hold still, and how small a size change counts as noise.
  • An option to log the layout decisions to idea.log, for reporting problems.

Changed

  • Renamed to Adaptive Tool Windows.
  • Settings moved to Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Adaptive Tool Windows.
  • Compatible with 2024.2 and later; previously 2025.3 and later.

idea-plugin.name: RunIt
idea-plugin.description:
RunIt is a lightweight script launcher for JetBrains IDEs, built for teams and individuals who want fast, repeatable project commands directly from the toolbar.

Store commands at the project or user level, launch them in one click, and keep your daily build, test, and utility scripts close to the IDE workflow.

RunIt 是一个面向 JetBrains IDE 的轻量脚本启动器，适合希望把常用项目命令固定在工具栏中的个人开发者和小团队。

它支持项目级与用户级脚本管理，在 IDE 内即可一键运行构建、测试、清理和其他日常命令，减少重复打开终端和手动输入的成本。
