idea-plugin.name: Visual GitHub Actions
idea-plugin.description:
Visual workflow editor for GitHub Actions — the first of its kind for JetBrains IDEs.

Stop reading walls of YAML. See your CI/CD pipelines as interactive visual graphs — jobs as cards, dependencies as edges, triggers as connected nodes — all inside your IDE.

Features

  • Visual Workflow Graph — jobs rendered as draggable cards with dependency edges, right next to your YAML
  • Split View — visual editor and YAML side-by-side with real-time bidirectional sync
  • Trigger Cards — workflow triggers displayed as visual nodes with configuration details (branches, paths, inputs, cron)
  • Dependency Editing — add or remove job dependencies (needs) visually: press E, click source, click target
  • Reusable Workflow Navigation — click on uses references to jump to the referenced workflow file
  • Used-By Discovery — see which workflows call the current reusable workflow with clickable links
  • Interactive Canvas — pan, scroll, drag nodes to organize your workflow layout
  • GitHub Accounts — OAuth Device Flow sign-in for GitHub.com and GitHub Enterprise directly in plugin settings
  • Runs Tool Window — browse workflows and recent runs, filter by workflow/branch, refresh automatically, rerun/cancel runs, and open local workflow files
  • Run Status Overlay — select a recent run and see job and step status, live elapsed time, and failed-job details directly on the visual graph
  • Theme Support — looks great in both light and dark IDE themes

How It Works

Open any .github/workflows/*.yml file — the visual editor appears automatically alongside the YAML editor. Edit in either view; changes sync instantly.

Coming Soon

  • Drag-and-drop to add, remove, and reorder jobs
  • Visual step editor with action search
  • Matrix strategy visualizer with combination preview
  • Visual cron schedule builder

idea-plugin.name: PickAID Template Assistant

idea-plugin.name: Docker Manager
idea-plugin.description:
Stop switching to the terminal for docker ps, docker logs, docker stop. Run your daily Docker workflow without leaving your editor.

What you can do

  • See everything in one tree — containers are grouped by Docker Compose project and service, with standalone containers in their own group. Everything updates live as you start, stop, or rebuild it. No refresh button to babysit.
  • Manage Docker Compose projects — compose files are detected and parsed automatically. Run Up, Down, Restart, Build and Logs for a single service or the whole project, with a live console for every action, and scale a service to any number of replicas.
  • Start, stop, restart and remove containers with a single click.
  • Connect without setup — Docker Desktop, Colima, Rancher Desktop, and Podman sockets are detected automatically, with a clear empty state when the daemon is not running. The plugin reconnects on its own once Docker starts after the IDE.
  • Read logs in real time with errors, warnings, and info levels highlighted so problems jump out.
  • Inspect any container — image, state, command, environment variables, port mappings, mounts and networks in a clean dashboard. Full inspect JSON if you need it.
  • Watch container resources — CPU, Linux working-set memory, network and disk I/O charts sit next to Inspect. Follow live usage and transfer rates over a fixed five-minute window, with themed colors, localized times and values on hover.
  • Open a container shell — run commands in a terminal tab inside the Docker tool window, using Bash or falling back to sh. Requires a running container and the IDE Terminal plugin.
  • Build images from Dockerfiles — start from the gutter or context menu, choose the local context folder and build arguments, follow live output and cancel when needed. Requires Docker CLI with Buildx and uses your selected Docker connection.
  • Inspect and clean build cache — see builder storage totals and sortable cache records, then preview and confirm removal of selected unused private cache. Requires Docker CLI with Buildx; reported cache sizes are not a promise of reclaimed disk space.
  • Pull images from any registry with live progress, and clean up the ones you don't need anymore.
  • Clean up faster — stop all running containers, remove stopped containers, and copy container or image IDs to the clipboard.
  • Know when containers exit — desktop notifications call out starts, normal exits, crashes, kills, and OOM stops.
  • Find what you need fast — instant search for containers and images.
  • Glance at the status bar to see how many containers are running and whether Docker is up.
  • Edit Dockerfiles with proper syntax highlighting. Works with Dockerfile, Containerfile, multi-stage variants like Dockerfile.dev and Dockerfile.prod, and any *.dockerfile.

Works with what you already have

Connects automatically to Docker Desktop, Colima, Rancher Desktop, or Podman — whichever one you use.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
4.0.0 — Container workflows and resource monitoring

  • Fix false container-log failures on close or disconnect, stop hidden streams, reject output from replaced views, and keep read-only container output out of file saving and Undo history.
  • Watch CPU, memory, network and disk I/O in the selected container’s detail tabs after Inspect, with compact labels and legends, themed charts with a fixed five-minute time scale, localized time axes, values on hover, live usage and transfer rates, and clear gaps when samples are unavailable.
  • Inspect build-cache records with correct size sorting, readable dates, total storage usage and a compact refresh/cancel toolbar. Review and safely remove selected unused private cache after confirmation.
  • Open an interactive shell in a running container from its context menu, with Bash-to-sh fallback.
  • Open image builds directly from the Dockerfile gutter, with a choice of local context folder and build arguments, live output, cancellation, and verification on the selected Docker connection.
  • Open Dockerfiles without plugin initialization errors when the IDE's built-in Docker support is enabled.

3.0.0 — Pro power tools

Daily-value features for power users on top of the Compose foundation.

  • Compose Scale: set the replica count for a service straight from the Docker tree; the replica containers appear under the service and update live.

2.0.0 — Docker Compose

This release brings Docker Compose into your editor and unifies everything under a single tree.

  • Docker Compose support: compose files are detected and parsed automatically.
  • Compose actions — Up, Down, Restart, Build and Logs — for a single service or the whole project, each with its own live console.
  • Compose build runs with live progress.
  • Compose logs, aggregated for the project or followed per service.
  • Unified Docker tree: containers grouped by compose project → service → container, with a standalone group for non-compose containers. The old separate Containers and Compose tabs are gone.
  • Container actions follow whatever you select in the tree, from a single container up to a whole compose project.
  • Auto-reconnect when Docker starts after the IDE — a background watcher waits for the runtime socket and connects on its own.
  • Panels and dialogs rebuilt with the platform UI for a cleaner, more native look.
  • Standard platform search across the Docker panels.
  • Container dashboard is now the default tab when you open a container.
  • Log search inside images and Docker Hub autocomplete when pulling.
  • Fixes for container log line separators and a more helpful connection empty state.

1.0.0 — First release

Manage Docker containers and images right from your editor.

  • One-click container actions: start, stop, restart, remove.
  • Bulk container cleanup: stop all running containers and remove all stopped containers.
  • Live container and image lists that update on their own.
  • Empty state with a single connect action and a Docker Desktop start prompt when Docker is not running.
  • Streaming logs with log-level highlighting.
  • Container lifecycle notifications for starts, exits, crashes, kills, and OOM stops.
  • Container dashboard with ports, env vars, mounts, networks — plus full inspect JSON.
  • Pull and remove images with live progress.
  • Copy container and image IDs to the clipboard.
  • Search across containers and images.
  • Status bar widget showing running container count.
  • Dockerfile syntax highlighting with support for Containerfile, Dockerfile.dev, *.dockerfile and similar names.
  • Automatic detection of Docker Desktop, Colima, Rancher Desktop, and Podman.

idea-plugin.name: Maven Consistency Enforcer
idea-plugin.description:
Stop fighting ghosts in your classpath! MCE ensures your IntelliJ IDEA run-time classpath matches the code in your workspace in multi-module Maven projects by detecting and removing stale JAR artifacts and preferring local module sources when available.

What it does:

  • Automatically removes attached JARs that shadow local modules
  • Replaces library entries with module dependencies when a matching module exists
  • Per-module enforcement configuration and global "All modules" toggle
  • Shows notifications and a status bar widget with enforcement metrics
  • Ensures your local Maven repository paths are valid on startup
  • Includes localization support
  • Provides a persistence cache for faster operations
  • Offers a Maven sync health check

Default behavior:

  • Triggers automatically after Maven > Reload Project and (optionally) on project startup
  • Shows notifications about fixed dependencies
  • Re-enforces consistency on every Maven reload
  • forceLocalModules and repository health check will be questioned on first run

  • Persistence cache for improved performance

idea-plugin.name: Magefile
idea-plugin.description:
Run Mage build targets directly from GoLand.

Requirements

  • Install mage. See installation docs.
  • Ensure mage is on your PATH, or configure the executable path in the run configuration.

Usage

  • Click the green run arrow in the gutter next to any exported Mage target function.
  • Or open Run/Debug Configurations and add a new Mage configuration manually.

What counts as a Mage target?

Any exported Go function in a file tagged with //go:build mage that returns nothing or error, optionally taking a context.Context as the first parameter. Methods on types that embed mg.Namespace are also supported as namespaced targets (e.g. Build.Deploy → mage build:deploy).

idea-plugin.name: SSH Deploy
idea-plugin.description:
English

SSH Deploy uploads build artifacts to remote Linux hosts over SSH/SFTP from IntelliJ IDEA (Community or Ultimate, with bundled Java and Terminal). Configure SSH servers, reusable remote commands, and optional file match rules in the IDE, then run a SSH Deploy Run/Debug configuration to upload and execute your pipeline. The SSH Deploy tool window is for managing servers, commands, file match rules, and viewing streamed console output.

Features

  • SSH servers — password or private key authentication.
  • Reusable commands — save shell snippets and reuse them in Run configurations (and in deploy profiles when imported).
  • File match rules — built-in presets (read-only) plus your own regex rules you can add, edit, or delete; reused from the Tool window manager and when picking a preset in Run configurations.
  • Upload pipeline — optional local build (Maven/Gradle), SFTP upload, remote commands before and after upload with streaming logs, optional Terminal tab for follow-up work.
  • Run/Debug configuration — pick server, local artifact (single file or directory + file-name regex). In directory mode, choose a regex from managed rules (“Select regex”), apply it into the regex field, or type a pattern manually.
  • Placeholders — use ${fileName} in remote commands for the uploaded file name (e.g. versioned JAR).
  • Import — import Alibaba Cloud Toolkit (ACT) style XML to migrate faster.
  • Languages — English and Simplified Chinese UI (follow IDE or override in Settings).
  • Configuration backup — full JSON export/import from Settings → SSH Deploy; per-section export/import from the tool window (Servers / Commands / File match rules). Import merges and skips duplicates; section import can also read one section from a full backup file.
  • Remote command retry — before/after remote commands retry up to 2 more times on failure (3 attempts total) with SSH reconnect.

How to use (Tool window)

  1. Open the SSH Deploy tool window (right tool window bar, or View → Tool Windows).
  2. Under Servers, add SSH hosts. Credentials can use the IDE password safe. Use Export… / Import… for servers-only JSON (or pick a full backup to import only servers).
  3. Under Commands, add multi-line remote shell snippets (with ${fileName} placeholder insertion) for Run configurations. Use Export… / Import… for commands-only JSON.
  4. Under File match rules, optionally add named regex presets (built-in rows cannot be deleted). Use Export… / Import… for user rules only.
  5. Use the Console tab for log output from operations that stream there.

How to use (Run configuration)

  1. Run → Edit Configurations → + → SSH Deploy.
  2. Choose SSH server, local upload source, and remote upload directory.
  3. In Directory pattern mode, pick a saved regex under Select regex and click Apply to fill the file match regex (you can edit it afterward).
  4. Edit before upload and after upload commands (one per line). Use insert placeholder for ${fileName} when needed.
  5. Optionally set a single-line terminal command; after success the plugin opens Terminal and sends that line.
  6. Run the configuration; logs appear in the Run tool window.

Requirements: IntelliJ IDEA with bundled Terminal and Java support (see sinceBuild in the listing for the minimum IDE build). Remote hosts must support standard SSH and SFTP.

Privacy: SSH credentials are stored using the IDE Password Safe on your machine. The plugin connects only to hosts and paths you configure; it does not send your project data or credentials to third-party servers operated by the plugin vendor.

简体中文

SSH Deploy 在 IntelliJ IDEA（需带内置 Java 与 Terminal 的 Community 或 Ultimate）中通过 SSH/SFTP 将本地构建产物上传到远端 Linux 主机。 在 IDE 内维护 SSH 服务器、可复用的远端命令以及可选的文件匹配规则，再通过 SSH Deploy 的运行/调试配置执行上传与命令流水线。 SSH Deploy 工具窗口用于管理服务器、命令、文件匹配规则，以及查看会输出到控制台的日志。

功能说明

  • SSH 服务器 — 支持密码或私钥认证。
  • 可复用命令 — 保存常用 Shell 片段，在运行配置中引用（导入的配置中的部署画像也会引用）。
  • 文件匹配规则 — 内置正则模板（不可删除）与用户自定义「名称 + 正则」；在运行配置的目录匹配模式下，选择正则下拉来自此处（点应用填入正则框）。
  • 上传流水线 — 可选本地构建（Maven/Gradle）、SFTP 上传、上传前/上传后远程命令（流式日志），以及可选的 Terminal 后续操作。
  • 运行/调试配置 — 选择服务器、本地上传源（指定文件或目录+正则）、远端目录、上传前后命令，以及可选的成功后单行终端命令。
  • 占位符 — 远程命令中可使用 ${fileName} 表示本次上传的文件名（例如带版本号的 JAR）。
  • 导入 — 支持导入 Alibaba Cloud Toolkit（ACT） 风格的 XML，便于迁移。
  • 语言 — 界面支持英文与简体中文（可跟随 IDE 或在设置中指定）。
  • 配置备份 — 设置 → SSH Deploy 提供全量 JSON 导出/导入；工具窗口的服务器 / 命令 / 文件匹配规则页可分别导出或导入该项（也可从完整备份中只读取该项）。导入为追加合并并去重。
  • 远程命令重试 — 上传前/后远程命令失败时自动再试最多 2 次（共 3 次），并重连 SSH。

使用方式（工具窗口）

  1. 打开 SSH Deploy 工具窗口（右侧工具窗口条，或通过 视图 → 工具窗口）。
  2. 在 服务器 中添加 SSH 主机；凭据可写入 IDE 密码保险箱。可用 导出… / 导入… 仅备份或恢复服务器（也可选择完整备份文件，只导入其中的服务器）。
  3. 在 命令 中维护可在运行配置中引用的多行 Shell 片段（支持插入 ${fileName} 占位符）。可用 导出… / 导入… 仅处理命令配置。
  4. 在 文件匹配规则 中按需维护名称与正则（内置行不可删除）。可用 导出… / 导入… 仅处理用户规则。
  5. 在 控制台 标签查看会输出到此处的日志。

使用方式（运行配置）

  1. 运行 → 编辑配置 → + → SSH Deploy。
  2. 选择 SSH 服务器、本地上传源与远端上传目录。
  3. 在目录匹配模式下，于选择正则中选取预设后点应用填充文件匹配正则（仍可手动修改）。
  4. 编辑 上传前 与 上传后 命令（每行一条）；需要时可使用 插入占位符 插入 ${fileName}。
  5. 可选填写单行 终端命令；上传成功后插件会打开 Terminal 并自动发送该行。
  6. 运行该配置；日志显示在 运行 工具窗口中。

环境要求：需使用带内置 Terminal 与 Java 支持的 IntelliJ IDEA（上架信息中的 sinceBuild 表示最低兼容构建号）；远端需支持标准 SSH 与 SFTP。

隐私与数据：SSH 凭据通过 IDE 密码保险箱保存在本机。插件仅向您自行配置的主机与路径发起连接，不会将您的工程数据或凭据发送到插件作者运营的第三方服务器。

idea-plugin.name: FatJar Builder
idea-plugin.description:
FatJar Builder

Build a single deployable fat JAR from any IntelliJ module with one click. The Eclipse FatJar plugin equivalent for IntelliJ IDEA.

Features

  • Build menu → FatJar Builder → Build Fat JAR
  • Add as a Before launch task in any run configuration
  • Artifact system integration (File → Project Structure → Artifacts)
  • Browses compiled classes to find and select your main class
  • Recursively includes all dependent module compiled classes
  • Supports both Maven and Gradle projects
  • Extracts all dependency JARs into a single flat JAR
  • Merges META-INF/services files correctly (SLF4J, JAXB etc.)
  • Strips JAR signatures automatically (no more SecurityException)
  • Excludes unwanted packages with Ant-style glob patterns
  • Shows detailed timestamped build output in a dedicated tool window
  • Notification with open folder link after successful build
  • Remembers settings per module between sessions

Why?

Teams migrating from Eclipse miss the FatJar plugin. Maven shade plugin works but breaks the IntelliJ debugger when delegation is enabled. This plugin builds a deployable fat JAR without touching your Maven/Gradle build configuration.
idea-plugin.change-notes: • Fixed FatJar Builder tool window font — now matches IntelliJ editor font (same font family and size as the Build window)

idea-plugin.name: EnvSwitch
idea-plugin.description:
EnvSwitch — One-click environment configuration switcher for JetBrains IDEs.

Manage multiple environment profiles (dev / beta / staging / prod) and switch between them instantly. Environment variables are automatically injected into Run Configurations, while project-wide SSH tunnels can provide runtime host and port values without hard-coding local forwarding details.

Key Features:
  • One-Click Switching — Switch environments from the main toolbar or the dedicated tool window; color-coded dots make it effortless.
  • Auto-Injection — Active profile variables are injected into all Run Configurations (Java, Python, Node.js, and more) before every run.
  • Project-Wide SSH Tunnels — Create, copy, edit, test, and reuse SSH tunnels across all environment profiles in the current project.
  • Runtime Tunnel Values — Inject a tunnel's local host, fixed or automatically assigned port, host-and-port pair, or a validated custom format into environment variables.
  • Flexible SSH Authentication — Connect with a password, an OpenSSH/PuTTY key pair, or your OpenSSH configuration and SSH Agent.
  • Sensitive Variable Protection — Mark variables as sensitive; values are encrypted with AES-128 or stored in the OS keychain via PasswordSafe.
  • Git Branch Auto-Switch — Bind profiles to Git branches; environment switches automatically when you change branches.
  • Profile Inheritance — Build environment hierarchies where child profiles inherit and override parent variables.
  • Import & Export — Bulk import from .env files; export profiles to .env, JSON, or YAML.
  • Conflict Strategies — Choose how injected variables merge with existing Run Configuration envs: Overwrite, Skip, or Merge.
  • Inline Editing — Add, edit, reorder, and search variables directly in the tool window table.
  • Multi-Language Support — UI available in English, Japanese, German, Russian, and more.

Perfect for teams managing multiple deployment targets, private services behind jump hosts, or developers who frequently switch between local, staging, and production configurations.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Environment comparison with inherited variables, key search, and difference filters.
  • Selected-variable synchronization with a change preview and stale-configuration protection.
  • Comparison UI translations for English, Chinese, German, Japanese, and Russian.

Changed

  • Responsive comparison controls, native environment color indicators, and a prominent sync action.
  • Comparison content retains a minimum width of 480 logical pixels with horizontal scrolling in narrow tool windows.

Fixed

  • Preview footer layout at narrow widths and table header grid alignment.
  • Default comparison targets exclude disabled environments.

idea-plugin.name: Firebase App Distribution Uploader
idea-plugin.description:
Firebase App Distribution Uploader

Upload Android release builds directly to Firebase App Distribution from Android Studio.

Features

  • Upload APK or AAB to Firebase App Distribution
  • Supports single environment and product flavors
  • Tester group multi-selection
  • Release notes support
  • Firebase App Distribution automation
  • Release build upload support

Usage

  1. Open Tools → Firebase Release Upload
  2. Select flavor and artifact type
  3. Select tester groups
  4. Add release notes
  5. Click Upload

Firebase Service Account Setup

This plugin uses Firebase service account authentication for uploading builds.

Step 1 — Create Service Account JSON

  1. Open Firebase Console
  2. Select your Firebase project
  3. Open Project Settings
  4. Go to Service Accounts tab
  5. Click "Generate new private key"
  6. Download JSON file

Step 2 — Place JSON File Inside Project

Example project structure: 

app/
 └── src/
      ├── uat/
      │    └── firebase-service-account.json
      │
      └── prod/
           └── firebase-service-account.json

For projects without flavors: 

app/firebase-service-account.json

Gradle Configuration

Add Firebase App Distribution plugin and configuration inside your app module.

Required Gradle Plugin

plugins {
    id("com.google.firebase.appdistribution")
}

Firebase App Distribution Configuration

firebaseAppDistribution {

    serviceCredentialsFile =
        "app/src/uat/firebase-service-account.json"

    appId =
        "1:XXXXXXXXX:android:a49a2a36a1XXXXXXXXXXX"

    artifactType =
        project.findProperty(
            "firebaseArtifactType"
        )?.toString() ?: "APK"

    releaseNotes =
        project.findProperty(
            "releaseNotes"
        )?.toString()

    groups =
        project.findProperty(
            "firebaseGroups"
        )?.toString()
}

firebase-upload-config.json

Create firebase-upload-config.json in project root.

Without Product Flavors

{
  "testerGroups": [
    "qa-team",
    "internal-testers"
  ]
}

With Product Flavors

{
  "flavors": {

    "uat": {
      "testerGroups": [
        "qa-team",
        "uat-team"
      ]
    },

    "prod": {
      "testerGroups": [
        "client-team"
      ]
    }
  }
}

Notes

  • APK uploads are recommended for internal testing
  • AAB uploads require Firebase project linked with Google Play Console
  • Only Release builds are supported
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Initial release:
  • Firebase App Distribution upload support
  • Flavor support
  • APK/AAB support

idea-plugin.name: YApi Doc Generator
idea-plugin.description:
YApi Doc Generator

Automatically parse and generate YApi API documentation from Spring MVC Controller classes and methods in IntelliJ IDEA.


Features

  • One-click generation — Right-click on a Controller class or method to parse and upload to YApi
  • Comprehensive Spring MVC annotation support — @RequestMapping, @GetMapping, @PostMapping, @PutMapping, @DeleteMapping, @PatchMapping
  • Deep DTO parsing — Nested objects, generics, collections, enums, inherited fields, circular reference detection
  • Request parameter parsing — @RequestParam, @PathVariable, @RequestHeader, @RequestBody
  • Response body parsing — Method return types automatically parsed into response structures
  • Smart doc title extraction — Prioritizes @ApiOperation / @Operation annotations
  • Multi-server support — Module name auto-matching + manual server selection dialog
  • Automatic category management — Creates YApi categories based on URL path segments
  • Shortcut — Ctrl+Alt+Y

How to Use

  1. Go to Settings → Tools → YApi Doc Generator and configure your YApi server(s)
  2. Open a Spring MVC Controller class in your project
  3. Right-click on a method or class name → Generate YApi Doc
  4. The plugin parses annotations, DTOs, and response types, then uploads to YApi automatically
idea-plugin.change-notes:
v1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • Generate YApi documentation from Spring MVC Controller classes and methods
  • Support for all Spring MVC request mapping annotations
  • Deep recursive DTO field parsing (10 levels max)
  • Generic type parameter resolution
  • Circular reference detection and termination
  • Multi-server configuration with auto-matching
  • Background async upload with progress and notification

idea-plugin.name: Flexible For OpenSCAD
idea-plugin.description:
OpenSCAD language support with a live interactive 3D preview, visual gizmo editing, smart completion, navigation, and code inspections â€” turn your JetBrains IDE into a full parametric-CAD workbench.

We are a young project and we want to make this the best OpenSCAD experience in any JetBrains IDE. Your feedback is critical: please leave a review, open an issue or reach out on GitHub, or email us â€” and tell us your thoughts, feature requests, and the occasional bug. We are very happy to hear from you.

Core Features

Language Support

  • Syntax highlighting for every OpenSCAD construct â€” modules, functions, built-ins, and special variables ($fn, $t, â€¦) â€” with a configurable color settings page
  • Code folding for blocks and comments
  • Brace matching with auto-close for {, (, [ and auto-closing quotes
  • Comment support for line (//) and block (/* â€¦ */) comments
  • Code formatter with configurable indentation
  • Structure view listing modules, functions, and variables
  • New-file template â€” create OpenSCAD files from New â†’ OpenSCAD File

Smart Completion & Documentation

  • Built-in completion for OpenSCAD's functions and modules
  • Keyword completion for language constructs
  • User-symbol completion for your own modules, functions, and variables
  • Context-aware â€” no completion inside strings, comments, or include/use paths
  • Documentation on hover (and Ctrl+Q quick docs) for built-ins, plus signatures and source comments for your own declarations

Navigation & Refactoring

  • Go to Definition (Ctrl+Click) for modules and functions
  • Find Usages across your project
  • Rename refactoring with reference tracking â€” including module/function parameters
  • Cross-file resolution that walks include <â€¦> and use <â€¦> graphs

Code Analysis

  • Unresolved include/use path detection (error)
  • Undefined reference detection (warning)
  • Wrong number of arguments / arity checking (warning)
  • Unused declaration detection (weak warning)
  • Performance hints (weak warning)
  • Live render-error annotations â€” when OpenSCAD is installed, errors from its renderer are shown inline in the editor

Interactive 3D Preview & Designer

  • Built-in live 3D preview â€” supported geometry is evaluated inside the IDE and rendered with three.js, so previewing needs no OpenSCAD executable (orbit/pan/zoom controls)
  • Auto-render on save â€” the model updates as you edit and save
  • Transform gizmos â€” move/rotate/scale geometry and have the edit written back into your source as translate()/rotate()/scale() wrappers (undoable as a single step)
  • Measurement tools â€” 2-click distance and 3-click angle (press M)
  • Cross-section clipping plane to inspect interiors (press X)
  • Animation timeline that drives the $t variable
  • Source â†” preview sync â€” double-click geometry to jump to the statement that produced it; toggle per-statement rendering
  • Snap modes and Blender-style keyboard numeric entry (select, press G/S, type a value, Enter)

Parametric Customizer & Outliner

  • Customizer tool window â€” reads // [min:max], // [step], // [a,b,c], and labeled-enum (// [0:PLA, 1:ABS]) annotations and renders sliders, dropdowns, and checkboxes; changes re-render the model via -D name=value
  • Outliner tool window â€” lists top-level statements with visibility and isolate toggles and click-to-navigate

STL Viewer

  • Interactive .stl viewer with three.js WebGL rendering and orbit controls

Built-in STL Export

  • Export to STL directly from the IDE â€” uses the built-in CSG engine, no external tools required

OpenSCAD Integration (optional)

These features use a locally installed OpenSCAD executable:

  • Export to 3MF, AMF, DXF, SVG, and PNG (STL works without OpenSCAD)
  • Render the current file with the OpenSCAD renderer (fallback for complex files)
  • Open in OpenSCAD to hand the file off to the desktop app
  • Automatic executable detection on first launch, with a render cache

Made by Developers with a Passion for Design & Fabrication

The integration is the work of Ilscipio:

We build software across AI, e-commerce, and the JetBrains plugin ecosystem, and we reach for OpenSCAD whenever a part needs to be precise, parametric, and version-controlled. We created this plugin to make code-first 3D modeling as fluid and productive inside JetBrains IDEs as the rest of our toolchain.

We're sharing it with the OpenSCAD and maker community to support the ecosystem's growth and make parametric design more accessible.

  • Special discounts are available for individual developers & of course for the whole Open Source community.

Bugs & Feature Requests

If you have any questions, feature requests, or stumble upon the occasional bug, come leave us a message at Ilscipio or email info@ilscipio.com.

A Note on OpenSCAD

This is an independent, third-party plugin and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or maintained by the OpenSCAD project. We are simply big fans â€” OpenSCAD is a wonderful open-source tool, and this plugin exists only to make working with it even more enjoyable. If you find it useful, please show the project some love and give it a star on GitHub: github.com/openscad/openscad.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2 compatibility: .scad and .stl files failed to open with ClassNotFoundException: com.intellij.ui.jcef.JBCefApp, because JCEF now ships as the separate "Web Browser (JCEF)" plugin. The plugin now declares an optional dependency on it, so the Designer, Preview, and STL viewer work again on 2026.2 and on older builds.
  • The license check no longer logs a NoSuchMethodException warning on every start; it now uses the supported LicensingFacade.getConfirmationStamp API.

Thanks

  • Many thanks to an anonymous reporter for the detailed report and the verified fix.

idea-plugin.name: Install Downloaded Files
idea-plugin.description:
Analyses and installs downloaded .java and .zip files directly into the correct source package directories of your IntelliJ project — with a fully tabbed workflow that lets you review, diff and control exactly what gets installed before committing.

How it works:
  1. Select a scope (module or all modules) and pick files from your Downloads folder.
  2. Click Analyse — files are classified as NEW, CHANGED, IDENTICAL or MISSING PKG.
  3. Review the Java tab — per-file status with Diff buttons. Tick what to install.
  4. Review the Non-Java tab — map config files, XML, pom.xml etc. to destinations. Untick anything you want to skip. Both tabs must be green to proceed.
  5. Use the Explorer tab to create missing packages or tidy up the project tree.
  6. Click Install&Build — files are installed, originals archived to INSTALLED_BACKUPS, and a project build is triggered automatically.
Key features:
  • Aggregator module support — parent modules automatically search all child modules.
  • MISSING PKG — explicit Create button in the Java tab; no silent package creation.
  • Non-Java file routing with saved destination mappings and project tree picker.
  • Lazy-loading Explorer with source root colour coding and last-modified dates.
  • Red/green tab labels — both must be green before install is enabled.
  • Per-file diff viewer using IntelliJ's built-in diff tool.
  • Auto-close after install with configurable delay.
Useful when working with AI assistants or external tools that generate Java source files.

Minimum IntelliJ version: 2026.1
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.6.3

Overview

  • Analysis — full text log of what was found and any issues
  • Java — per-file table with NEW/CHANGED/IDENTICAL/MISSING PKG status and Diff buttons
  • Non-Java — config files, XML, pom.xml etc. mapped to destinations in the project tree
  • Explorer — lazy-loading project tree for creating packages/directories or deleting files
  • Install — install log showing what was backed up, installed and built

Added

  • Five-tab layout — Analysis | Java | Non-Java | Explorer | Install
  • Java tab — interactive table replacing the plain analysis text for Java files. Each row shows Install checkbox, Package/File, Status (colour-coded), and a Diff button. IDENTICAL files are unchecked by default. NEW PKG rows show a Create button instead of a checkbox — packages must be created explicitly before install is enabled.
  • Non-Java tab — map non-Java files from a zip (config, XML, pom.xml etc.) to any destination in the project. Destinations are remembered between sessions. The tab widens the dialog to 940px automatically and restores to 730px when switching away. All entries are ticked by default; IDENTICAL entries (file already matches) are unticked. Unticking = skip. Ticked with no destination = blocks install (tab stays red). Browse opens the same project tree picker as the Explorer tab. ✕ clears a saved destination mapping. Diff reviews changes before installing. Conflict detection prevents the same filename being mapped twice across multiple zips. Clear All Saved Mappings button resets all stored destinations.
  • Explorer tab — lazy-loading project tree scoped to the current module selection. Aggregator modules show themselves plus all child modules. Excluded paths, dot files, .iml and .bak files are hidden. Source roots highlighted green (src/main/java) and blue (src/test/java). Last-modified date shown on every row. New Package — dot-separated input under a source root, same as IntelliJ's own dialog. New Directory — creates a single folder anywhere in the tree. Delete — requires confirmation; toolbar buttons grey out when nothing is selected. Project file picker used by Non-Java Browse uses the same tree and filters.
  • Aggregator module support — selecting a parent module (e.g. ICRServer) with no source roots automatically searches all child modules. Scope line shows which children resolved.
  • MISSING PKG — missing packages show in the Java tab with a Create button (disabled under aggregator scope). Install is blocked until all missing packages are created.
  • Red/green tab colouring — both tabs must be green to enable Install&Build and Install.
  • X / Escape confirmation — prompts if files have been analysed but not yet installed.
  • Auto-close timer — cancelled cleanly on dialog dispose; no orphaned process.
  • Scope change warning — changing scope after Analyse shows a warning before resetting.
  • Corrupt zip handling — ZipFile errors caught and reported cleanly in Analysis output.
  • Clear All Saved Mappings — button on Non-Java tab; enabled only when mappings exist.
  • SKIPPED always shown — SKIP lines always appear under their zip header in Analysis.

Changed

  • Build menu entry: "Install Downloaded Files..."
  • Dialog title: "Install Downloaded Files"
  • Footer label: "Install Downloaded Files"
  • Backups folder: ROUTER_BACKUPS → INSTALLED_BACKUPS
  • Install now moves files to INSTALLED_BACKUPS in all cases (Install-only and Install&Build)
  • Complete action removed — Install subsumes it
  • Path label shows last two segments with ellipsis; full path in tooltip
  • rootProject.name changed to "download-installer"
  • Minimum IntelliJ version: 2026.1 (build 261)

Fixed

  • Aggregator scope no longer enables Install when only MISSING PKG rows exist
  • Tab colours reset after a successful install
  • Dialog no longer leaves a running process after closing

idea-plugin.name: Dynatrace Mobile Wizard
idea-plugin.description:
Dynatrace Mobile Wizard is a guided setup tool for Android developers that automatically configures the Dynatrace OneAgent Mobile SDK in your project — no manual Gradle editing required.

Open it from Tools → Dynatrace Wizard…, right-click in the editor, or right-click in the Project view. The wizard detects your project structure and walks you through every step.

Note: this is an independent, community-created tool and is not developed by, affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Dynatrace GmbH. "Dynatrace" is a registered trademark of Dynatrace GmbH, referenced here solely to identify the third-party SDK this tool configures.

What it does

  • Project detection — identifies Gradle DSL (Kotlin or Groovy), module layout, existing Dynatrace configuration, and the optimal plugin approach (Plugin DSL vs buildscript classpath)
  • Multi-module support — single-app, multi-app, and dynamic feature module projects; per-module Application ID and Beacon URL; optional OneAgent SDK for library modules
  • Environment setup — validates Application ID and Beacon URL with inline feedback
  • Technology check — detects project versions for Gradle, AGP, Java, Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, and OkHttp; warns when other instrumentation plugins (Firebase Perf, New Relic, Datadog, Sentry, etc.) are found in the project
  • Full feature control — toggles for crash reporting, ANR reporting, native (NDK) crash reporting, user actions, web request monitoring, Jetpack Compose instrumentation, Session Replay, hybrid (WebView) monitoring, location, privacy / GDPR opt-in, rage-tap detection, build-variant targeting, class/method exclusions, and more
  • Change preview — shows the exact Gradle code that will be written before you commit
  • Safe writes — every file edit uses WriteCommandAction, making all changes fully undoable via Edit → Undo
  • AI skill export — generates a project-specific skills.md for GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, and other AI coding agents

Wizard tabs

  1. Welcome — detects Android project, DSL, module structure, and setup flow
  2. Modules — select which app modules to instrument; configure approach for multi-app projects (shown only for multi-app / library-module projects)
  3. Technologies — version compatibility check; warns about competing instrumentation plugins
  4. Environment — enter Application ID and Beacon URL (per-module for multi-app)
  5. Features — enable/disable individual instrumentation capabilities; Recommended view by default; Advanced toggle reveals 12 more options
  6. Skills — opt-in export of a reusable Markdown skill set for AI coding agents (collapsed by default)
  7. Summary — diff-style per-file change cards; click Finish to apply

Supported project types

  • Single-module Android apps
  • Multi-module projects (app + library + dynamic feature modules)
  • Kotlin DSL (build.gradle.kts) and Groovy DSL (build.gradle)
  • Plugin DSL (plugins {}) and legacy buildscript classpath approach

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2024.1+ or Android Studio Meerkat (2025.1)+
  • An Android project with at least one com.android.application module
  • A Dynatrace account with a configured Mobile application (Application ID + Beacon URL)
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.1 - 2026-09-29

Fixed

  • Duplicate buildscript {} block — addClasspathGroovy/addClasspathKts used a single-line regex (buildscript\s*\{[^}]*dependencies\s*\{) that could not cross the closing } of a repositories {} sub-block declared before dependencies {} — the standard Android project template. This caused the wizard to prepend a second, duplicate buildscript {} block instead of merging the Dynatrace classpath into the existing one. Replaced with a brace-depth-aware findBuildscriptDependenciesInsertionPoint helper.
  • Buildscript classpath approach applied the plugin to the wrong file — for single-app and feature-module projects using the legacy buildscript-classpath approach, apply plugin and the dynatrace {} block were written to the app module file. Per Dynatrace's documentation ("apply the Dynatrace Android Gradle plugin to the top-level build file... this allows the plugin to properly configure the Android subprojects"), both now go into the same root file as the classpath entry. Multi-app per-module setups are unaffected — the .module plugin variant still applies per app module there, since that's a genuinely different, still-valid pattern.
  • Generated AI skill files (skills.md) gave the same wrong app-module guidance, and separately mislabeled multi-app per-module setups when generating the single-app/feature-module case. Both the "Plugin Apply" snippet and the "Instrumentation approach" summary row now correctly distinguish single-app/feature-module (root-only) from multi-app per-module (plugin in each app module).
  • Corrected matching text in docs/skills/setup.md (section 2b + the Feature Modules diagram), the Welcome tab's plugin-approach hint, both generateChangePreview overloads, SetupFlow descriptions, and the README's Setup Flows table — all previously described the old app-module placement.

Removed

  • Orphaned "shared dynatrace-common file" code path (createSharedDynatraceFile, applyFromSharedFile, addPluginDeclarationOnly) — never wired up from any wizard flow and contradicted the actual (and now corrected) feature-module behavior described in the docs.

idea-plugin.name: DependencyUpdater
idea-plugin.description:
The ultimate dependency manager and security scanner for IntelliJ IDEA

DependencyUpdater is a powerful plugin designed explicitly for Maven and Gradle projects. It acts as your intelligent assistant to keep your build files clean, updated, and secure.

Key Features:

  • 🚀 Full Maven & Gradle Support: Seamlessly parses pom.xml, build.gradle / build.gradle.kts and libs.versions.toml files.
  • 🧩 Gradle Plugins Update: Support for scanning and updating Gradle plugins configured within plugins {} block (both Groovy and Kotlin DSLs).
  • 🛡️ Security Scanning (OSV API): Automatically detects Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) in your direct and transitive dependencies.
  • 🔄 Smart Version Updates: Discovers newer library versions directly from your configured artifact repositories. Automatically filters out already up-to-date dependencies for clean, distraction-free lists.
  • 🏢 Enterprise Ready: Built-in native support for Corporate Proxies and custom SSL Certificates (JFrog Artifactory compatibility).
  • 🔐 Custom Repositories: Connects to private registries with safe Bearer Token and Basic authentication. Includes predefined HTML directory listing scanner for private JFrog instances.
  • 🎯 LTS & Beta Filtering: Advanced version recognition differentiating between Long Term Support (LTS) releases and experimental Beta/Snapshot builds.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Version 1.6
  • Live Multi-Column Search: Added a lightning-fast live search field to both Direct and Transitive dependency tables. Instantly filter thousands of dependencies by typing library names, versions, or CVE identifiers.
  • Case-Insensitive Regex Filtering: The new search acts across all data columns synchronously without the need to press Enter.
  • Improved Stable Version Filtering: Hardened the version recognition engine to ensure corporate and experimental versions (e.g. -alpha, -beta, hyphenated build numbers) are reliably excluded from LTS lists.

Version 1.5
  • Smart Up-to-Date Filtering: The Direct Dependencies list now intelligently hides libraries that are already at their latest versions, keeping your view focused and distraction-free. Switching between LTS and Beta modes dynamically updates visibility based on available builds.
  • Advanced LTS/Beta Recognition: Enhanced version parsing engine that accurately classifies corporate naming conventions and JFrog Artifactory builds (such as timestamped snapshots, -dev, -preview, and -ea qualifiers).
  • Streamlined Transitive Scanning: Transitive dependency analysis has been streamlined to focus purely on background vulnerability detection (CVE scanning) and version auditing, removing automatic build file modification for safer builds.

Version 1.4
  • Gradle Plugins Support: Full parsing and auto-updating functionality for Gradle plugins {} blocks (Groovy, Kotlin DSL) and TOML plugin references.
  • Corporate Proxy & SSL: Migrated underlying HTTP engine to IntelliJ native HttpRequests for robust handling of Enterprise Proxies and Custom SSL Certificates.
  • JFrog Artifactory (HTML): Dedicated predefined repository type for private JFrog instances utilizing HTML directory listings. Automatically scans both libs-release and libs-snapshot concurrently.
  • Improved History View: Reintroduced visibility of older versions in the dropdown list to accurately reflect past security vulnerabilities (CVEs).
  • Bugfixes: Patched minor UI glitches, introduced dynamic authentication labels, and optimized regex matchers for libs.versions.toml syntax.

Version 1.3
  • Custom Repositories: Added a new Settings page to manage multiple custom artifact repositories.
  • Global Predefined Defaults: Quickly add standard global repositories (Maven Central, Google, Spring, JBoss) from a dedicated dropdown menu.
  • Secure Authentication: Full support for Basic (Username/Password) and Bearer Token authentication via IntelliJ PasswordSafe. UI dynamically adapts to your Auth Type.
  • Concurrent Fetching: The plugin now queries all configured repositories simultaneously to fetch the latest dependency versions.
  • Standalone Compatibility: Removed hard IDE constraints. The plugin now works flawlessly even on strictly restricted corporate IDE instances where official Maven or Gradle plugins are disabled.

Version 1.1
  • IDE Compatibility: Updated to support IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1 and fixed deprecated FilenameIndex API usages.
  • Marketplace Compliance: Updated plugin ID and configured proper untilBuild limits.
  • Code Quality: Refactored codebase, removed unused comments, and bumped Gradle Wrapper to 9.5.1 with updated Mockito framework.

Version 1.0
  • Initial Release: Scans Maven and Gradle projects for outdated dependencies.
  • Security Scanning: Integrates with OSV API to expose Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) for direct and transitive dependencies.
  • LTS Filtering: Highlights Long Term Support versions for safer upgrades.

idea-plugin.name: Version Catalog Extractor
idea-plugin.description:
Detects literal dependency declarations in Gradle Kotlin and Groovy DSL files and offers a quick fix to move them to gradle/libs.versions.toml.
It can also extract versioned Gradle Kotlin DSL plugin declarations to plugin aliases.
If the version catalog does not exist, the plugin creates it. If it already exists, the plugin reuses matching aliases or adds new library entries with version entries when needed.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Support for extracting versionless library dependencies, such as implementation("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-web")
  • Whole dependency notation highlighting instead of highlighting only the version segment
  • Version catalog library entries without version.ref when the original dependency does not declare a version
  • Kotlin DSL plugin inspection for versioned plugin declarations, such as id("org.springframework.boot") version "3.5.0"
  • Quick fix to extract versioned Kotlin DSL plugins into [plugins] aliases and matching [versions] entries
  • Reuse of existing version catalog plugin aliases when the same plugin id is already present
  • Filtering for Gradle core plugins so declarations like id("java"), id("application"), and id("java-library") are not reported

idea-plugin.name: GitDeployPack
idea-plugin.description:
GitDeployPack builds deployable packages directly from Git changes.

Select commits from Git Log, or package changes by commit, commit range, tag, date range, local working tree, or a custom file list.

  • Start from files selected directly in the Project view context menu
  • Detect missing or potentially stale Java class files before packaging
  • Compile only Java files included in the patch with IntelliJ IDEA
  • Preview included, deleted, and missing files before generation
  • Support Java Web/WAR, standard Java, frontend, and original-path layouts
  • Optionally build with IntelliJ IDEA, Maven, or Gradle before packaging
  • Generate folders and ZIP archives with customizable name templates
  • Work consistently on Windows, macOS, and Linux

GitDeployPack 基于 Git 提交、范围、标签、日期或本地变更，一键生成可部署的项目补丁包。
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Remove deprecated IntelliJ Platform API usage reported by 2026.2 verification.
  • Keep the patch dialog open when required fields fail validation.
  • Fix IDEA selected-file compilation failing in a write-unsafe context.
  • Detect missing and potentially stale Java class files before packaging.
  • Add a lightweight IDEA mode that compiles only Java files included in the patch.
  • Resolve class files from IDEA module, Maven, and Gradle output directories.
  • Improve IDEA and Maven compilation startup and error messages.

idea-plugin.name: PlantUML Git Diff
idea-plugin.description: Compare the PlantUML diagram under the caret with the matching diagram from a local git base ref.

idea-plugin.name: Ide-mcp
idea-plugin.description:
Ide-mcp lets AI agents control the IDE through its built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. It adds the IDE-automation tools that the bundled MCP server does not ship — so an agent can manage changelists, drive debugging and breakpoints, control run configurations, and read tool-window output, instead of only editing files.

Tools added by this plugin (they appear alongside the IDE's built-in MCP tools):

  • Changelists — list, create, switch, and delete VCS changelists, and move specific changed hunks of a file between changelists.
  • Breakpoints — set, remove, and list line breakpoints.
  • Run control — select the active run configuration, start a debug session, and stop running processes.
  • Tool-window readers — read the Problems view, the Build output, and the current debug session.
  • Project lifecycle — wait until indexing/loading finishes.

Deliberately does not duplicate tools the IDE already provides (such as listing run configurations or plain run, file/text search, refactoring).

Setup made easy: this plugin adds a Settings → Tools → MCP Server Install Helper page with a one-click Enable button and ready-to-copy connect commands for the current project. (You can also enable the bundled server manually via Settings → Tools → MCP Server and connect any MCP client — Claude, Cursor, VS Code, ….)
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Move specific changed hunks of a file between changelists:
    • list_file_changes — list a file's changed hunks (1-based line range, type, current changelist).
    • move_changes_to_changelist — move the hunks overlapping given line ranges into a changelist.

idea-plugin.name: Maven dependency:get
idea-plugin.description: Fetch the latest SNAPSHOT dependency via `mvn -U dependency:get`, then quickly reload Maven dependencies in offline mode.

idea-plugin.name: CLI Shortcut
idea-plugin.description:
English

CLI Shortcut is a lightweight IntelliJ IDEA plugin for running frequently used command-line scripts directly from the IDE toolbar. It is designed for developers who repeatedly open Terminal and type the same project commands, such as starting local services, running build scripts, executing deployment helpers, refreshing generated files, or launching other CLI workflows.

After installation, the plugin adds a fixed toolbar button to the top-right area of the IDE. Clicking the button opens or focuses the built-in IDEA Terminal, sends a greeting command first, and then runs the enabled scripts configured by the user. Scripts are executed in the order shown in the settings page, with disabled or blank scripts skipped.

Configuration is available under Settings | Tools | CLI Shortcut. The settings page supports multiple scripts and lets you enable or disable each script, edit its display name, edit the command content, add or remove scripts, and move scripts up or down to control execution order. The default configuration includes an explanatory echo script so users can immediately see how the plugin works after installation.

This plugin intentionally keeps the workflow simple: it acts as a CLI shortcut launcher inside the IDE. It does not parse command output, manage background jobs, or replace Terminal. The terminal remains visible so users can inspect output, errors, prompts, and shell behavior exactly as they would during normal command-line work.

中文

CLI Shortcut 是一个轻量级 IntelliJ IDEA 插件，用来从 IDE 工具栏快速执行常用命令行脚本。 它适合经常需要打开 Terminal 并重复输入相同项目命令的开发场景，例如启动本地服务、运行构建脚本、 执行部署辅助命令、刷新生成文件，或触发其他 CLI 工作流。

插件安装后，会在 IDEA 右上角工具栏添加一个固定按钮。点击按钮后，插件会打开或聚焦 IDEA 内置 Terminal， 先发送一条问候命令，然后继续按用户配置执行已启用脚本。脚本会按照设置页中的顺序执行，未启用或内容为空的脚本会被跳过。

配置入口位于 Settings | Tools | CLI Shortcut。设置页支持配置多个脚本，可以启用或停用单个脚本、 编辑脚本显示名称、编辑命令内容、新增或删除脚本，并通过上移、下移调整执行顺序。默认配置包含一个说明用 echo 脚本， 用户安装后可以立刻看到插件的执行效果。

这个插件刻意保持简单：它只是 IDE 内的 CLI 快捷启动器，不解析命令输出，不管理后台任务，也不替代 Terminal。 终端会保持可见，用户可以像平常使用命令行一样查看输出、错误、提示符和 shell 行为。

idea-plugin.name: Faultline
idea-plugin.description:
Predicts the blast radius of a dependency upgrade: diffs the public API of the currently resolved artifact against a candidate version and intersects the breaking changes with the symbols your project actually references.

Faultline is read-only — it forecasts impact, it never rewrites your code. Trigger "Analyze Upgrade Impact…" from the project view, or just edit a dependency version in pom.xml / build.gradle(.kts) and save: Faultline detects the change and reports which breaking changes upstream actually have a call site in your source, with click-to-navigate results.

Network access: Faultline downloads the two jar versions being compared from Maven Central so it can diff their bytecode. No other network access, no telemetry, no account required.

Known limitations: static analysis only — reflection and dynamic dispatch aren't covered, so "0 affected" means no static call site was found, not a guarantee of safety. Transitive dependencies and non-JVM resources (SPI files, annotation processors) are out of scope for this release.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.0

  • Initial release: bytecode-level API diff (extraction + severity classification) for Maven-Central-hosted artifacts.
  • PSI-based call-site intersection with click-to-navigate results in the Faultline tool window.
  • Automatic detection of dependency version changes in pom.xml / build.gradle(.kts) on save, with no manual trigger required.

idea-plugin.name: Pixi
idea-plugin.description:
Pixi

IntelliJ IDEA integration for the Pixi package manager.

Browse environments, tasks, and run configurations directly from the IDE sidebar. Launch tasks with a single click from the tool window or from the gutter icon in pixi.toml. Get auto-completion for depends-on and feature names, automatic environment synchronization across run profiles, and CMake configure integration for code intelligence.

Features:

  • Tool Window — browse Environments, Tasks, and Run Configurations in the right sidebar
  • One-click Run — double-click any task or click the run gutter icon to execute
  • Run Configuration — run pixi tasks like any other IntelliJ run configuration
  • depends-on Completion — smart auto-completion for dependency fields in pixi.toml
  • Feature Completion — auto-completion for feature names in the environments section of pixi.toml
  • Environment Sync — automatically updates the project and run profile environments
  • CMake Configure — automatically detects and runs CMake configure commands from pixi tasks with -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON for code intelligence
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changelog

1.2.x

  • Support CMake configure to run cmd directly and enable -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON for code intelligence
  • Replace feature reference with completion (auto-completion for feature names in environments section)
  • Fix pixi path detect on Windows

1.1.x

  • Support depends-on completion
  • Automatically change the project and all run profile environment

1.0.0

  • First version

idea-plugin.name: Maven Assist
idea-plugin.description:
Your friendly co-pilot for pom.xml files. Maven Assist looks at the directory you point it at and gives you exactly the right tools for what it finds: create a brand-new pom.xml in seconds, or inspect and update an existing one with one-click stable version upgrades from Maven Central.

  • Create pom.xml's insanely easy
  • Add, delete and manage dependencies with only a few clicks
  • Quickly create templates and reuse them in other projects
  • and many features more...

What it does

  • Works in any directory. Pick a folder and the whole workflow runs right there. Maven Assist switches between create and manage mode on its own.
  • Creates poms from a form, or from a template you created. Fill in the coordinates, optionally point at a parent pom, tick the dependencies you want, and press one button. Save the whole setup as a template and reuse it in every project.
  • Updates dependencies with one click. Every row has an Update button that moves it to the newest stable release and rebuilds. Update All does the whole pom at once.
  • Keeps dependencies fresh automatically. Flag any dependency and it moves to the newest version at the moments you pick. Every update asks by default, and major updates always require approval.
  • Preserves your formatting. Edits are surgical: indentation, comments and safe ${property} versions survive. Entries under dependencyManagement, profiles, build and reporting are never touched by accident. A plugin's own dependencies stay a plugin's own dependencies.
  • Grows with you. Paste any dependency snippet once, give it a name, and it stays in your catalog forever, across projects and IDE restarts.

Getting started

Open the tool window

Click Maven Assist on the right edge of the IDE, or use View → Tool Windows → Maven Assist. The directory field at the top starts at your project root; pick another folder with the button beside it (or type a path and press Enter) and the view rescans instantly.

No pom.xml yet? Create one

  • Fill in group id, artifact id and version.
  • Optionally choose a parent pom with Choose Path… its coordinates and the relativePath are filled in for you.
  • Tick the dependencies you want. Search to narrow the list, then use Select All to take everything the search turned up. Each row shows just the name; Details reveals the coordinates and the newest version.
  • Press Create pom.xml. The view switches straight to the dependency table.

Pom already there? Manage it

  • See every dependency with its version, including versions resolved from properties.
  • Search the table, or filter it in one click to Only auto update.
  • Open buttons next to the pom path and next to the parent pom, when it resolves to a file: open it right in the editor.
  • Check for Updates fills the Newest Version column for every row. Update All then lets you update everything, cancel, or select the exact dependencies from a checkbox list. A single build runs after the chosen updates.
  • Press Update beside any version and pick Newest version or Custom version…. Maven Assist rewrites the pom, runs mvn compile, and tells you how it went.
  • The red trash button on each row deletes that dependency after a confirmation. The trash button next to the search bar turns on multi-select, so you can clear out several at once.

Templates

Every project you start the same way? Save it once.

Press Template in the bottom bar from either the create or manage view. Save As... stores the current coordinates, parent pom, dependencies and version choices under a name. Export... copies the current project's existing pom.xml unchanged to a folder you choose; Import... reads a local pom.xml up to 5 MB and saves its supported contents as a new template.

In the create view, press Choose Template directly below the New pom.xml heading. Pick a template and Apply: the entire form fills itself in: coordinates, parent pom, the newest-version setting and every dependency, already ticked.

To make one, press Create Template… in that same window. You get the familiar pom form, plus a field for the template's name. Templates are stored permanently and are available in every project. Don't need one anymore? Select it and press Delete.

Adding dependencies to an existing pom

Click Add Dependencies. Adding happens in two calm steps:

  • Step 1: pick. Search and tick what you need, or take everything at once with Select All / Select None. Details shows the group id, artifact id, the catalog version and the newest one from Maven Central.
  • Step 2: configure. Press Next and every selected dependency gets its own block: use the newest version, pin a specific one, and decide whether it should auto-update. Back returns to the list without losing anything.

Press Add and they land in your pom exactly as configured, with a build kicked off for you.

Auto update, on your schedule

The table has an auto update column: green means on, red means off. Clicking either state asks for confirmation before changing it. Maven Assist then checks the green-flagged dependencies against Maven Central and bumps any that fell behind to a newer stable release, pom rewritten, build started.

You decide when that happens. Press Customize... at the bottom of the tool window and tick any combination of:

  • Every time I save the project: the default, including when no files have changed.
  • When the project is opened: start each session on the newest versions.
  • Right before "MVN Clean Install" runs: update, then do the full build in one go.
  • When you press a shortcut: tick it, click the field below and press the key combination you want. It is stored in your IDE keymap, so you can also review or change it later under Settings | Keymap, and the same command is available through Find Action at any time.

Tick nothing and auto update only ever runs when you ask for it. A save trigger is scoped to files in this project; an external pom change only refreshes the table.

Every automatic update asks by default. Maven Assist shows the dependency, old and new versions, and a link to release information on Maven Central. Answer Yes, No, or Never; Never switches auto update off only for that dependency. Under Customize..., you can disable these questions for minor and patch releases. Major updates, such as 2.x to 3.x, always require confirmation and this protection cannot be disabled.

Your own catalog

Press Add Own to Manager… at the bottom of the Add Dependencies window, or Add Dependencies to Manager in the create view. Give the dependency a name and paste its code, either a <dependency>…</dependency> block straight from mvnrepository.com, or a plain groupId:artifactId:version line.

It is stored permanently under that name and appears in every picker from then on, in all projects. Every picker row also has a red trash button that removes a dependency from the catalog for good, built-in entries included.

Good to know

  • Builds use your project's mvnw wrapper when there is one, otherwise mvn from the PATH.
  • Automatic builds after a pom change run mvn compile, which is fast. Need the full thing? The MVN Clean Install button at the bottom runs mvn clean install.
  • No Maven installed? Maven Assist falls back to the copy bundled with your IDE, so builds usually just work. If even that is missing, MVN Clean Install offers to install Maven for you: via Homebrew or winget, or downloaded from apache.org, into the project or for the whole machine.
  • Version lookups run in the background. The IDE never freezes.

What leaves your machine

Maven Assist itself makes direct network requests only for features you invoke or dependencies you explicitly flag for automatic update:

  • repo1.maven.org: when checking updates, choosing Newest, viewing version details, creating/adding a dependency configured to use newest, or running an enabled auto-update trigger. The artifact's Maven repository metadata is requested, so a lookup sends that dependency's groupId and artifactId. These coordinates can reveal private naming conventions, so no lookup is started merely by opening or refreshing the tool window. Custom pinned versions are accepted without contacting Central.
  • dlcdn.apache.org / archive.apache.org: only if you explicitly ask it to install Maven for you. The download is checked against a pinned SHA-512 and discarded on mismatch.

Builds and package-manager installs are external tools: Maven, Homebrew or winget may contact repositories configured on your machine. Maven Assist does not control or inspect those requests.

There is no telemetry, no analytics and no account. Your settings stay in your IDE configuration and your project's workspace file, with machine paths excluded from roaming state.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Maven Assist 2.0.0: What's New Since Version 1.0.1?

Maven Assist 2.0.0 makes automatic dependency updates more controlled, secure, and flexible. You can now decide exactly when automatic updates run: when saving, when opening a project, before MVN Clean Install, or through a custom keyboard shortcut.

Newest-version checks now read Maven Central's current repository metadata instead of its stale legacy search index, so stable releases such as OkHttp 5.x are detected correctly. Failed lookups are reported rather than incorrectly claiming that every dependency is up to date.

A new Template menu is always available in the bottom bar. From either the create or manage view, Save As... stores the current project setup, dependencies, and version choices. Export... copies the current project's existing pom.xml, while Import... turns a local pom.xml into a saved template.

Update All now asks before changing the pom. You can update everything, cancel, or choose the exact dependencies to update from a checkbox list. Toggling auto update also asks for confirmation for the selected dependency.

Every automatic update now asks by default. Maven Assist shows the dependency, current and new versions, and a link to the release information. Choose Yes, No, or Never, which disables auto update only for that dependency. Minor- and patch-update confirmations can be disabled under Customize..., while major updates always require approval. Automatic updates also use only stable versions that are actually newer than the currently installed version.

Editing pom.xml files is now significantly more robust. Dependencies with different Maven types or classifiers are handled independently. Shared version properties no longer cause unrelated dependencies to be changed accidentally. Entries in dependencyManagement, profiles, build and reporting sections, as well as dependencies belonging to Maven plugins, remain untouched. Existing pom.xml files are no longer overwritten during creation.

Privacy and security have also been improved. Automatic actions respect IntelliJ Safe Mode, project information is stored without absolute user paths, and network requests are made only for features you explicitly use. The optional Maven download is verified against a pinned SHA-512 checksum and now includes size limits, timeouts, and reliable cleanup of temporary files.

The entire interface now automatically follows the active IntelliJ theme, including custom and third-party themes. Custom versions also work with private Maven repositories and are no longer incorrectly checked against Maven Central. Numerous smaller issues involving concurrent updates, builds, notifications, and POM modifications have been fixed as well.

idea-plugin.name: VersionLens Redux
idea-plugin.description: VersionLens Redux dependency hints, diagnostics, and code lenses through the shared VersionLens language server.

idea-plugin.name: VulnSpotter
idea-plugin.description:
A smart vulnerability scanner for your project dependencies. VulnSpotter integrates directly into your IDE to detect security vulnerabilities in your Gradle, Maven, npm, PyPI and Go dependencies. It leverages the OSV.dev database to provide real-time alerts, in-editor highlighting and detailed remediation advice without leaving your workflow.

Main Features

  • Automated Scanning: Detects vulnerabilities in Gradle, Maven, npm (package-lock.json), PyPI (requirements.txt) and Go (go.mod) projects automatically, and re-scans after Gradle/Maven sync.
  • In-editor Highlighting: Vulnerable dependencies are annotated directly in pom.xml and build.gradle with a one-click quick-fix that upgrades to the recommended fixed version.
  • Real-time Alerts: Get instant notifications about security risks in your dependencies.
  • Detailed Reports: View comprehensive vulnerability details, including summaries, CVSS severity, affected ranges and fixed versions, and export to HTML, PDF, CSV, JSON and SARIF.
  • Integrated Tool Window: A dedicated "VulnSpotter" tool window for managing and reviewing scan results, with direct/transitive classification and search by package or CVE.
  • Direct References: One-click access to official security advisories (CVE, GHSA, etc.).
  • Visual Indicators: Clear visual cues for safe vs. vulnerable packages.
  • Exclusions: Ignore specific dependencies or CVEs via a .vulnspotterignore file or the Settings page.
  • Analysis on Project Open: Dependencies are scanned automatically when the project opens, with an IDE notification when pending critical CVEs are found.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.2

  • Automatic Analysis on Project Open: The project's dependencies are scanned when it opens (toggle enabled by default) and an IDE notification is raised when pending critical CVEs are found.
  • Fix: Added the missing displayName to the VulnSpotter settings page, removing the PluginException raised when the Settings dialog was opened.

1.0.0

  • Initial Release: First release of VulnSpotter on the JetBrains Marketplace.
  • Multi-ecosystem Scanning: Scans Gradle, Maven, npm, PyPI and Go dependencies for known vulnerabilities using the OSV.dev database, with automatic re-scan after Gradle and Maven sync.
  • In-editor Highlighting & Quick-fix: Vulnerable dependencies are annotated in pom.xml and build.gradle, with a one-click intention that upgrades to the recommended fixed version (and refuses to downgrade).
  • Tool Window: Dedicated tool window with vulnerability details, direct/transitive classification, search by package or CVE, and report export to HTML, PDF, CSV, JSON and SARIF.
  • Settings: Configurable minimum severity and ignored CVEs, persisted at the application level.
  • Layered Architecture: Codebase reorganized into a clean layered architecture.
  • Exclusions: Ignore specific dependencies via a .vulnspotterignore file.

idea-plugin.name: Flutter Local Build
idea-plugin.description: Build, preview, release, patch, and publish configured Flutter apps from Android Studio and IntelliJ IDEA. Includes a Local Build tool window and YAML schema validation, completion, and documentation.

idea-plugin.name: CodeBlocks
idea-plugin.description: Visually highlights nested code blocks in Java files, drawing borders around each { } block with a different color per nesting depth. Inspired by Blockman (VS Code), focused on Java.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Configurable color palette (Colorful / Blackout) alongside the existing Strong / Medium / Light intensity setting.
  • One-click "Switch Color" popup (editor context menu and Tools menu) to change palette + intensity without opening Settings.
  • Plugin icon (pluginIcon.svg / pluginIcon_dark.svg).
  • First automated tests (JavaBlockCollectorTest, via BasePlatformTestCase), covering block detection, nesting depth, and depthBelow.

Fixed

  • Replaced the deprecated Document.addDocumentListener(DocumentListener) call with the parent-disposable overload, so the plugin no longer reports deprecated API usage on its Marketplace page.
  • Consecutive blocks stacked on the same column no longer have their borders touching — a small gap now separates them.
  • Nested blocks no longer share the same right-edge border when the widest line in a method lives inside the innermost block; each nesting level now gets a proportional right-edge margin so every block reads as a fully closed, independent rectangle (box-within-box).
  • Plugin id/name effective at build time now matches the source gradle.properties/Kotlin package instead of a stale, overridden value.
  • CI build (.github/workflows/build.yml) — gradlew had lost its executable bit and gradle.properties hardcoded a machine-local JDK path, both of which broke ./gradlew build on other machines/CI.
  • NestedBlockRenderer no longer scans/draws blocks that are fully outside the visible viewport, and no longer misdraws blocks whose opening line sits inside a collapsed (folded) region.

Changed

  • Releases are now fully automated: the version is derived from Conventional Commits and CI bumps, changelogs, tags, signs, publishes to the Marketplace and cuts the GitHub release on its own (see CONTRIBUTING.md).
  • CI now runs the JetBrains Plugin Verifier against every IDE in the compatibility range and keeps its report as a run artifact.
  • Marketplace publishing is gated behind a GitHub Environment that requires manual approval and holds the signing/publish credentials, so no other CI job can reach them. GitHub Actions are pinned to commit SHAs.
  • Project renamed to CodeBlocks (plugin id dev.block.codeblocks, Kotlin package dev.block.codeblocks).
  • vendor.url in plugin.xml now points at the real repository instead of a placeholder.

idea-plugin.name: Lombok Builder Invocation
idea-plugin.description:
Generate complete Lombok @Builder invocation assignments from a Java class.
Select the target fields and get readable chained calls that use values from a source object.
This plugin generates Builder calls, not the nested Builder class definition.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Initial version

idea-plugin.name: Remote Deploy
idea-plugin.description:
Upload a local file or directory to a remote server over SSH and optionally run a follow-up deploy command without leaving your IDE.

  • Upload files or folders with SFTP
  • Run an optional remote command after upload
  • Reuse saved SSH targets and deploy run configurations
  • Store passwords and passphrases in IntelliJ Password Safe

idea-plugin.name: BeanShell Language & Debug
idea-plugin.description:
Language support for BeanShell (.bsh) scripts: a full syntax tree, code intelligence, running, and a source-level debugger — plus BeanShell recognition inside Maven pom.xml configuration and XML in general.

The core runs in any IntelliJ-based IDE (IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, CLion, …); Java-aware features — navigation into Java code, variable type inference and JVM-debugger attach — light up in IntelliJ IDEA and other IDEs that bundle the Java plugin.

The language model follows the BeanShell 2.0b6 grammar, which is the version published to Maven Central and bundled with the plugin for running scripts out of the box.

Source, issue tracker and full documentation: github.com/loplex/beanshell-debug-tools.



Editing
  • Syntax highlighting with a configurable color scheme
  • Code folding of blocks, comments and consecutive imports; brace matching
  • Line/block commenting and an indentation formatter (Reformat Code)
  • Structure view and breadcrumbs for the enclosing class/method
  • Read/write highlighting of the variable under the caret
  • Quick documentation, including a preceding Javadoc-style comment
  • Live templates (sout, fori, iter, …) and postfix templates (.sout, .if, .while)
  • Surround With (if, while, try/catch) and TODO highlighting
Code intelligence
  • A full AST parser (recursive descent with backtracking) that mirrors the BeanShell grammar and reports syntax errors as you type
  • Go to Declaration, Find Usages and Rename for methods, classes, typed and untyped variables, and parameters — methods and classes also resolve across the project's .bsh files
  • Code completion, parameter info and inlay parameter-name hints at call sites
  • Inspections with quick fixes: unused variable/parameter, unreachable code, and an opt-in unresolved method call check
  • Introduce Variable intention and Go to Symbol




Java interoperability (requires the Java plugin — optional)
  • Ctrl+Click into Java: class names (FQN, java.lang.*, imported), and members reached through static type propagation across a chain, e.g. report.append("x").append("y") or list.get(0)
  • BeanShell class members: greeter.greet() navigates to the greet method of a Greeter class declared in the script


Running
  • A BeanShell run configuration; right-click a .bsh file to run it
  • The interpreter is bundled (org.apache-extras.beanshell:bsh:2.0b6), so scripts run with no setup; the classpath is overridable per configuration
  • Uses the project JDK when available (falls back to the IDE runtime)
Debugging
  • A source-level debugger for .bsh files: line breakpoints, the call stack, Step Over/Into/Out, and Run to Cursor
  • A variables view that expands nested objects, collections, maps and arrays, plus Watches, the Evaluate dialog, and Set Value on a variable — all evaluated by the real interpreter in the selected frame
  • Two instrumentation mechanisms, chosen per run configuration: a JVM agent that leaves the script on disk untouched (default), or rewriting the script, which needs no agent jar and no JVM flag but shows one frame and cannot evaluate
  • With the Java plugin present, breakpoints in the Java code called from a script are honored by a companion Java (JDWP) debug session


File recognition & injection
  • Files with the .bsh extension
  • Extensionless scripts whose shebang launches BeanShell, including the self-executing polyglot (#!/bin/sh … exec java bsh.Interpreter "$0")
  • Inline scripts in the <configuration> of several Maven plugins (beanshell-maven-plugin, maven-enforcer-plugin, build-helper-maven-plugin — the list is easy to extend)
  • Any XML element preceded by a <!--language=BeanShell--> comment


Known limitations
  • The parser targets the 2.0b6 grammar; 3.0-only syntax (**, ??, <=>, triple-quoted strings, word operators) is tokenized but not all of it is parsed
  • Java navigation is static: it follows types evident in the code (typed variable/parameter, = new Type(), class names) — generic element types, array indexing and runtime-only types are not inferred
  • On JDK 9+, BeanShell 2.0b6 cannot reflectively access some JDK-internal iterators, so list.iterator().next() / for (x : list) may fail at runtime — a property of the interpreter, not the plugin
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • The Variables view now shows Locals and Global as labeled groups, and shows a nested Block/Closure scope (a for/if body, or a closure's captured namespace) between them as its own group, instead of flattening every scope into the frame's children.

Fixed

  • Fix missing icon on the "Create BeanShell-Enhanced Maven Configuration" action.

Changed

  • Renamed the plugin from "BeanShell Language Support" to "BeanShell Language & Debug".

idea-plugin.name: Jenkinsfile Companion
