Real Groovy syntax highlighting for Jenkinsfile (no extension needed) plus two genuine structural checks: a stage name defined more than once, and a stage with no steps/ parallel/stages block -- a real, silent no-op that Jenkins itself won't warn you about.

100% local, zero network calls, checked entirely against the Jenkinsfile already open in the editor -- never a live Jenkins server connection. Built from real evidence: the leading paid Jenkinsfile plugin has 31% of reviews at 3 stars or fewer (hover-info conflicts, broken code formatting after an IDE update), and a separate free/abandoned competitor's core design flaw is validating by connecting to a live Jenkins server instead of locally -- exactly the class of fragility this plugin exists to avoid.

idea-plugin.name: GitHub Actions Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
Watch GitHub Actions workflow runs for every repository in the current workspace without leaving the IDE. The tool window drills down from repository to workflow to run to job to step, and keeps itself up to date while a run is in progress.

  • Multi-repository workspace discovery.
  • Five-level tree: repository → workflow → run → job → step, with status icons and durations.

在 IDE 内实时查看当前工作区中所有仓库的 GitHub Actions 执行状态。支持自动发现多个仓库，以 Repository → Workflow → Run → Job → Step 五层树形结构展示，运行期间自动刷新；可按当前分支过滤、跳转 GitHub 页面、按 workflow 加载更多历史记录。认证复用 GitHub CLI，无需另行配置 token。

idea-plugin.name: direnv Everywhere
idea-plugin.description:
Your .envrc environment, everywhere the IDE runs something.

You use direnv. Your JDK comes from Nix, your toolchain from Devbox, your credentials from a .env file the shell loads for you. In the terminal, everything works — and then you open the IDE, and none of it exists.

This plugin makes that environment available to the things the IDE actually starts:

  • Run and debug configurations — every language, no per-runner support needed
  • The build process, so compilation sees the same environment
  • Gradle and Maven — sync, tasks, and the run configurations the IDE delegates to Gradle by default
  • The terminal, in WSL as well as on your own machine
  • External Tools, File Watchers, and processes started by other plugins

Scoped to the project, not the IDE. The environment is resolved per project and working directory and injected as each process starts, so two projects open side by side keep separate environments and a nested .envrc gets its own. The IDE's own process environment is never modified — which is what makes the isolation real rather than approximate.

A JDK or Node interpreter from direnv is offered to the project. Injecting PATH does not help the IDE itself, which resolves toolchains from its own settings — so indexing and inspections keep calling them missing while a terminal in the same project finds them. Offered rather than applied: a Nix store path can vanish after garbage collection, and rewriting your project SDK at that moment would break the project with no explanation.

It keeps itself up to date. Change flake.lock and the environment reloads — not because the plugin knows about Nix, but because direnv reports every file its environment depends on and all of them are watched. Run direnv allow in an ordinary terminal and the IDE picks it up within seconds, with no button and no restart.

Security is the default, not a setting. An .envrc is arbitrary shell code, so direnv allow is never invoked automatically under any setting, untrusted projects never execute one at all, and variable values never reach logs, run configurations or any file under .idea/. A built-in viewer shows which variables were applied by name — knowing that PGPASSWORD was set is useful; writing its value into a run configuration would put it straight into git.

Requires direnv installed and on PATH — on the machine the project lives on, for a project in WSL or on a remote host. Implements IJPL-11588. Known limitations are documented in the README.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Maven goals get the environment — run configurations, and the build itself when build and run actions are delegated to Maven (#31). Since at least 2026.1 the IDE starts mvn through the Eel API rather than as an ordinary process, so the injection point that covers everything else was never reached and nothing said so, not even the debug log. The environment now goes into the one map Maven's launcher lets extensions change, on top of the login shell's variables and the run configuration's own. As with Gradle, a variable direnv unsets can survive there.

idea-plugin.name: Staleguard
idea-plugin.description:
Staleguard tells you which dependencies are out of date, which are vulnerable, and whether upgrading will break your code. It checks pom.xml, build.gradle, build.gradle.kts, and version catalogs right in the editor, labels every update as patch, minor, or major, flags versions with published CVEs, and fixes them with one click. The upgrade impact check compares the two versions' actual binaries and reports the removed methods your own code calls, with call sites, before you take the upgrade. The classpath doctor resolves every call every jar makes against your real per-module classpaths and reports the NoSuchMethodError and NoClassDefFoundError you would otherwise meet at runtime, names the earliest version that fixes each conflict, applies it with one button, and re-checks by itself after every dependency sync. Free, no account, no telemetry. Works in IntelliJ IDEA Community Edition and Android Studio, where the built-in Package Checker is not available.

  • Classpath linkage doctor: every inter-jar call resolved against what your per-module classpaths actually declare, production and test classpaths separately, your own compiled code included; version conflicts reported before anything runs
  • THE FIX, computed and applied: the earliest released version that satisfies every call on your classpath is found by probing real binaries, shown in the findings and right at the declaration in the editor, and applied with one button; Maven transitives get a dependencyManagement pin
  • Always-on protection: after every Maven or Gradle sync the linkage check re-runs locally and notifies only about NEW problems the sync introduced; the verdict stays in the status bar and survives restarts
  • Upgrade rehearsal: before you upgrade, the impact check swaps the candidate jar into every module's classpath and reports whether the upgrade fixes known linkage problems or introduces new ones anywhere
  • Shadowed class detection: the same class in two jars with differing APIs, where classpath order silently decides which copy runs, reported as one finding per conflicted jar pair
  • Upgrade impact analysis: Alt+Enter on an outdated dependency compares the two versions' bytecode and lists the removed members your code actually calls, judged the way the JVM links, so a method that merely moved to a superclass is never a false alarm
  • Known-vulnerability alerts: versions with published CVEs are flagged with the advisory, its severity, and the first fixed version, checked against the OSV database
  • Inline upgrade hints with major/minor/patch severity and release-age context
  • One-click fixes that correctly edit Maven properties and Gradle version catalogs instead of inlining literals over references
  • Abandonment detection: flags dependencies whose newest release is years old, with the actual date
  • Show What Changed: the release notes between your version and the suggested one, in a dialog, with breaking-change and security banners
  • Team rules: a committed .staleguard.toml shares ignore rules and license policy with the whole team, and Renovate/Dependabot ignores are honored automatically
  • Batch updates with confidence scores, security fixes preselected, plus one-click "apply all patch"
  • Statistics and timeline tool window with license visibility, vulnerability counts, and Markdown/CSV/PNG export
  • Parent POM, BOM, and build-plugin freshness: Spring Boot parents, platform() and scope=import BOMs, Gradle plugins blocks, and Maven build plugins are all checked
  • Your policy, respected: version pins in .staleguard.toml, Renovate allowedVersions, Dependabot ignore ranges, and Maven mirrors from settings.xml all steer what gets suggested
  • Never upgrade into a CVE: when the newest version has advisories, the nearest clean one is suggested instead, and you get a notification when a dependency that was clean gains a new advisory

Supports pom.xml, build.gradle, build.gradle.kts, libs.versions.toml, gradle.properties and buildSrc version constants, including androidx, Compose BOMs, and other Google-hosted dependencies. Works in IntelliJ IDEA and Android Studio (2024.3 and newer). Stable-only suggestions by default. No telemetry, no accounts: data comes directly from Maven Central, Google's Maven repository, the Gradle Plugin Portal, and osv.dev, with a polite 24-hour cache.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • The SBOM tells the whole truth. The CycloneDX export now lists every artifact your build actually ships, transitives included, straight from the resolved dependency trees, and writes the CycloneDX dependency graph (who pulls whom, rooted at your project) that Dependency-Track renders. When Gradle dependency locking is active the locked version wins over the graph's answer, because the lock is what runs, and the graph's version survives as a component property so the drift stays visible in the export too. Declared dependencies remain in the bill even when a resolved graph is unavailable.
  • The relock story. When a lockfile regenerates, the tool window now tells you what actually moved: version movements with the advisories they fixed or INTRODUCED, arrivals, and departures. A relock that introduces a known vulnerability raises a warning notification naming the advisory and the movement that brought it in. First sighting of a lockfile is a silent baseline, only a real change becomes news, and the story survives an IDE restart, so a relock is news exactly once.
  • buildSrc constants are editable now. The pre-catalog Versions object idiom (const val gson = "2.10.1") joins the batch update dialog, Apply All Patch, and the Alt+Enter editor fix as a first-class citizen: the same pattern that reads a constant locates the exact text span to replace, several dependencies sharing one constant merge to the highest selected suggestion, a blast-radius confirmation fires when one constant feeds several declarations, and a constant that moved since the dialog opened is left alone rather than blindly overwritten. Templated and non-const values stay read-only, honestly.
  • Lock drift is ambient. The status bar count now includes locks out of step with the declarations, computed by the same logic as the tool window so the surfaces can never disagree, and Kotlin Multiplatform source-set blocks are covered by a pinned regression test in both idioms.

idea-plugin.name: sbt-dependencies
idea-plugin.description:
Language support for dependencies.conf files used by the sbt-dependencies sbt plugin:
  • Syntax highlighting for every part of a dependency, customizable under the color scheme settings.
  • Diagnostics matching the exact errors the sbt plugin itself would fail with, with quick fixes for removable entries.
  • Hovers explaining version markers, with resolved versions, BOM provenance and mvnrepository links.
  • Resolved versions shown inline for * and {{variable}} dependencies, read from the sbt plugin's own resolution dump.
  • Notes folded into // comments next to their dependency (as are scala-filter and overrides = true annotations), with an "Add note" intention for pinned or intransitive entries.
  • Paste conversion turning SBT-style dependencies (libraryDependencies +=, addSbtPlugin(...)) into canonical strings.
  • Navigation between group names and their build.sbt project definitions, usage highlighting and variable rename.
  • Source links opening a dependency's source repository on Cmd+Click, read from the POMs in the local Coursier cache, with mvnrepository.com as fallback.
  • Structure view with groups and their dependencies as navigable children.
  • Formatting producing the exact output of the dependenciesFormat sbt task — groups and dependencies sorted, canonical indentation, comments dropped.
  • sbt tasks (install/update dependencies) runnable from the Tools menu.
  • Reload prompts showing IntelliJ's floating "reload project" widget when dependencies.conf changes, the same one the sbt integration shows for build.sbt (requires the Scala plugin).
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• The new exclude = ["org:name", ...] annotation is recognised: every coordinate in the list is highlighted as a plain string instead of being split like a dependency line.
  • Entries carrying an exclude list count it as an annotation, so they stay expanded instead of folding to their note alone.

idea-plugin.name: CheckoutAndBuild
idea-plugin.description:
Local one-click CI inside your IDE: keep any number of projects up to date with a single click — git pull, install/restore, build and test, all out of process and in parallel.

Detects .NET solutions, Gradle, Maven, npm, Composer, Cargo and Go projects beneath your working folders. Same-priority projects run in parallel; priority groups run in order.

Works in every JetBrains IDE. The big brother for Visual Studio is on the Visual Studio Marketplace.

idea-plugin.name: Circular Dependency Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Visualizes the dependency graph between modules of a multi-module Gradle or Maven project, and highlights real circular dependencies when they exist -- module/build-system level, not file/class-level "circular import" (already covered by other tools).

Gradle: parses settings.gradle(.kts) for declared include(...) modules, and each module's own build.gradle(.kts) for project(":...") dependency references (implementation, api, compileOnly, testImplementation, and other common configurations). Both Groovy and Kotlin DSL are supported.

Maven: parses each pom.xml's <modules> and cross-references <dependency> entries whose groupId:artifactId matches another module in the same project.

100% static text/XML analysis of files already open in your project -- no Gradle daemon, no Maven reactor build, no network call. A single-module project (no submodules declared) is reported honestly as "no cycles possible", never an empty, unexplained tool window.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no popups.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: Devenv
idea-plugin.description:
Adds support for devenv in IntelliJ-based IDEs.
Brings support for most devenv features, including devenv.nix editing, environment management, and integration with the devenv CLI.

This is an unofficial, community-maintained plugin and is not affiliated with the devenv project.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Nix files in a project with a devenv.nix are now backed by the language server started by devenv lsp, one server per devenv.nix of the project, each answering for the files of its own root.

  • The devenv.yaml and devenv.local.yaml of a project with a devenv.nix are now mapped to the JSON schema devenv publishes at https://devenv.sh/devenv.schema.json, so they get completion, documentation and validation without the # yaml-language-server: $schema=... modeline. The IDE downloads the schema once

    and caches it; only IDEs bundling the JSON plugin are concerned, and the YAML plugin is what applies it.

  • The processes declared under processes in devenv.nix now appear in the Services tool window, with their status, per-process start/stop/restart, live logs, and devenv up -d / devenv down on the root node. Selecting a process follows the log files the native process manager writes, so its output arrives as it is produced, with stderr and ANSI colours kept and a filter above the console; any other process.manager.implementation falls back to the devenv processes logs snapshot. A project holding several devenv.nix - modules attached side by side, or a repository whose modules each carry one - contributes the processes of all of them, under a node per root.

  • The .devenv state directory is now excluded from indexing and search, without modifying the module configuration - one per devenv.nix of the project, so the modules of a repository carrying several each get theirs excluded.

  • The Project SDK of a project whose devenv.nix sets languages.java.enable is now set to the JDK that devenv.nix declares, and put back whenever something else moves it - a Gradle or Maven import assigning its own JDK, or a choice made by hand in Project Structure. Only IDEs bundling the Java plugin are concerned; the Gradle and Maven JVM settings themselves are left alone.

  • A project whose devenv.nix sets languages.java.gradle.enable now has its linked Gradle builds pointed at the Gradle devenv.nix declares, instead of the wrapper downloading one of their own, and run on the Project SDK, which is the JDK devenv.nix declares. Both apply from the next Gradle reload on. Only IDEs bundling the Gradle plugin are concerned. A Java toolchain declared by the build is still resolved by Gradle itself.

  • A project whose devenv.nix sets languages.java.maven.enable now has its Maven home path set to the Maven devenv.nix declares, instead of the one bundled with the IDE. It applies from the next Maven reload on. Only IDEs bundling the Maven plugin are concerned.

  • A project whose devenv.nix sets languages.javascript.enable now has its Node.js interpreter set to the one devenv.nix declares, instead of whichever Node.js the IDE finds on the machine, and its package manager set to the pnpm, yarn or npm declared next to it - the first of those the project enables, since the IDE has a single such setting. Both apply at once, to run configurations and to the JavaScript tooling alike. Only IDEs bundling the JavaScript plugin are concerned.

  • Reformat Code now runs the project's own treefmt for the file types it is configured to format, so the IDE and the treefmt git hook agree. Other file types keep using the IDE's built-in formatters. The treefmt of the devenv.nix nearest the file is the one that runs, so each module of a project holding several is formatted by its own configuration.

idea-plugin.name: Gradle Task Graph Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Tool window that visualizes the real dependsOn graph between Gradle tasks in your project -- root project plus every submodule declared in settings.gradle(.kts) -- grouped into dependency layers, with any real cycle called out in its own top section, in red.

Recognizes both DSLs: Kotlin (tasks.register("x") { dependsOn("y") }, val x by tasks.registering) and Groovy (task x(dependsOn: y), x.dependsOn y).

100% static text analysis of your build files -- never a real Gradle evaluation or daemon. Stated honestly: v0.1 only sees explicit dependsOn declarations written in your build scripts, not the many implicit task orderings a plugin like java/application wires up internally -- a real, documented limitation, not a bug.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: Class File Export
idea-plugin.description: Class File Export is an IntelliJ IDEA plugin for SVN workflows. It shows the SVN commit history (revision, author, date, message, file count) in a tool window, supports multiple selection and double-click to view the changed files of a commit, and exports incremental compiled artifacts (classes and resources) from the IDE Compiler output, Maven target, or Gradle build classes into a war-style package (WEB-INF/classes) for quick deployment. It is compatible with traditional web projects and Spring Boot applications.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.3：导出目录结构调整，在“项目名_时间戳”目录下新增一层本项目文件夹名称，class / js / css 等增量文件全部放入该层内部，解压后可直接覆盖到服务器对应目录。

0.1.1：新增 Class SVN 记录工具窗口，查看 SVN 提交记录（版本/作者/日期/说明/文件数量），支持整行高亮、Ctrl/Shift 多选与双击查看该提交变更文件（更新/新增/删除三列）；新增编译产物增量导出，自动定位 IDEA Compiler output、Maven target、Gradle build classes，按 war 解压结构生成 WEB-INF/classes 路径，兼容传统 Web 项目与 Spring Boot；修复 Marketplace 审核发现的内部 API 问题（VcsDataKeys.FILE_PATHS、SlowOperations.allowSlowOperations、JBColor.border() 等内部/废弃 API）；优化界面（整行蓝色高亮、支持多选、字体与 IDEA 统一、滚动速度可调、列宽优化）；兼容 IntelliJ IDEA 2024.1 及之后所有版本。

0.1.0：初版，提供 SVN 提交记录查看与编译产物增量导出功能。

idea-plugin.name: Flexible COBOL
idea-plugin.description:
Native COBOL parser, no language server required. Copybook navigation, GnuCOBOL compile and run, a COBOL-level debugger, compile and run on z/OS over z/OSMF, an AI assistant with MCP tools, and PIC-to-Java/JSON mapping for modernization. IBM Enterprise COBOL and GnuCOBOL dialects.

A young, unofficial plugin that needs your feedback. We built it because we like COBOL, saw a gap in the IDE space for it, and wanted to apply what we know. It is not affiliated with IBM, GnuCOBOL or JetBrains. Report a bug or an idea and you get 20% off the annual license, or one month free, for your first reported issue or feedback. Leave a review on the plugin page, open an issue on GitHub, or write to info@ilscipio.com.

Built for production code. The grammar was written from scratch for this plugin, so parsing, navigation and completion run inside the IDE without a server process. The parser handles the complete NIST COBOL-85 conformance suite, 391 programs, with zero parse errors at about 10,000 lines per second. Fixed and free format, IBM and GnuCOBOL dialects, EXEC SQL and EXEC CICS.

Try it free from the JetBrains Marketplace. Flexible COBOL is free for students and open source projects, and non-profits get a 50% discount.

Documentation: See the getting started guide or the plugin page on the JetBrains Marketplace.

Why Flexible COBOL

  • Nothing to install besides the plugin. The parser, navigation, completion and inspections are built in. There is no language server and no separate server process, and everything works offline. An external language server can be attached, but nothing depends on it.
  • Understand legacy code fast. Go to declaration, find usages, call hierarchy across CALL, PERFORM and CICS LINK/XCTL, and a structure view of every division, section and paragraph.
  • Work with copybooks like source. COPY resolution across configurable paths, REPLACING-aware rename and completion, and an unresolved-COPY quick fix.
  • Compile, run and debug in the IDE. GnuCOBOL SDK detection, run configurations with gutter icons, clickable compiler errors, CALLed programs built as modules, and a debugger that steps by COBOL line and shows your data by COBOL name.
  • Talk to z/OS. Upload a program and its copybooks over z/OSMF, compile, link and run it with generated JCL, read the spool in the IDE, and click an IGY compiler message to jump to the source line.
  • Modernize with confidence. Generate Java classes and JSON Schema from COBOL data structures.
  • AI that can read your programs. The AI chat works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor and other agents, or with your own API key. The plugin's own MCP server gives any MCP client the program outline, data items, usages, call graph, diagnostics, and compile and run results.

Core Features

Language Support

  • IBM Enterprise COBOL and GnuCOBOL dialects with per-project dialect and source-format settings
  • Fixed and free source format, auto-detected or set with >>SOURCE FORMAT
  • Full native parser (Grammar-Kit/JFlex) covering all four divisions, all DATA DIVISION clauses (levels 01-88, REDEFINES, OCCURS DEPENDING ON, PICTURE), and all verb families
  • COPY with REPLACING, including partial-word replacement
  • EXEC SQL / EXEC CICS blocks with SQL language injection
  • Syntax highlighting with customizable color schemes (Default and Darcula), sequence and indicator areas dimmed
  • Code folding, brace matching, comment toggling, and a column-aware Enter handler

Copybook Intelligence

  • COPY navigation and resolution across configurable copybook paths, auto-detected for new and existing projects
  • REPLACING-aware rename and completion for copybook members
  • Unresolved-COPY quick fix and copybook usage search

Navigation & Intelligence

  • Go to Declaration (Ctrl+Click) and Find Usages (Alt+F7) with read/write access
  • Cross-program data-item where-used search backed by stub indexes
  • Call hierarchy across CALL, PERFORM, and CICS LINK/XCTL
  • Paragraph usage markers in the gutter: see and jump to every PERFORM and GO TO of a paragraph
  • Go to Symbol, Structure View, breadcrumbs, and rename refactoring

Smart Completion & Documentation

  • Context-sensitive, dialect-filtered completion: verbs at a statement start, the verb's clause words after it, data names and paragraphs where they fit, ELSE and END-IF inside an open IF; IF, EVALUATE, SEARCH, EXEC and inline PERFORM expand to the whole block with the scope terminator in place
  • Quick documentation (Ctrl+Q) for 57 verbs, reserved words, PIC symbols, and CICS commands
  • Data item documentation: level, PICTURE, USAGE, byte size, group chain, and the Java/JSON mapping

Inspections & Intentions

  • 10 inspections with quick fixes: unreachable paragraph, unused data item, missing scope terminator, non-numeric arithmetic, period style, dialect mismatch, unresolved COPY, duplicate procedure name, unused copybook, dynamic CALL
  • 4 intentions: extract paragraph, add COPY, and Java class or JSON Schema generation for a data item

Live Templates (48 templates)

Type the abbreviation and press Tab: 4div, ws, 01grp, pic9, 88cond, ifel, evw, prf, sel, rdlf, cics-link, tstp, and more

File Templates

Available under New File: Program, Copybook, Subprogram

GnuCOBOL Toolchain

  • GnuCOBOL SDK in Project Structure, auto-detected from PATH or the default install directory
  • Compile and run configurations with gutter icons; compiler output streams into the Run console
  • Multi-program builds: every program the main program CALLs by name is compiled as a module and found at run time; a subprogram (PROCEDURE DIVISION USING) gets no run icon of its own
  • Standard input file for programs that ACCEPT, in Run and Debug
  • Syntax-check annotator that shows cobc diagnostics in the editor (programs only, not copybooks)
  • Clickable console error links to the offending source line
  • Clean builds: executables and C intermediates go to a temporary build directory, never into the project

Debugger

  • COBOL-level debugger on cobc -g builds, driven over GDB/MI
  • Steps by COBOL line: Step Over runs a PERFORMed paragraph or a CALLed program in one step, Step Into enters it, Step Out leaves it
  • Variables by COBOL name: the items the current paragraph uses (with inline values in the editor), then WORKING-STORAGE, LOCAL-STORAGE, LINKAGE and FILE records, decoded from PICTURE and USAGE (DISPLAY, COMP, COMP-3, COMP-5, floats, pointers), with groups, OCCURS elements and level-88 conditions
  • Set Value with MOVE rules, Evaluate and Watches with COBOL expressions (EMP-NAME (1:5), WS-CODE OF WS-ENTRY (2), EMP-HOURS > STD-HOURS, WS-EOF), hover values
  • Conditional breakpoints and log messages in COBOL, run to cursor, frames that name the paragraph and the program
  • Stop on COBOL runtime errors (on by default) at the failing statement, and Stop When Value Changes data watchpoints
  • Debug into CALLed programs; the generated C names stay available under "Runtime (C level)"

PIC-to-Java/JSON Mapping

  • Generate Java classes and JSON Schema (draft-07, with a sample instance) from COBOL data structures for modernization work
  • Available as intentions on a data item, from the Tools menu, and as an MCP tool

z/OS over z/OSMF

  • Connections to z/OSMF hosts (HTTPS, self-signed certificates through the IDE's certificate store, API ML base path), passwords in the IDE password safe, import from a Zowe team configuration (zowe.config.json)
  • Test Connection and Allocate Missing Data Sets for the source, copybook and load libraries
  • "COBOL on z/OS" run configuration: uploads the program, the programs it CALLs and every copybook it copies, then compiles (IGYCRCTL), links (IEWBLINK) and runs the program with generated JCL; PARM, SYSIN and extra DD statements; the job status streams into the console, every spool file follows
  • Clickable IGY messages: each Enterprise COBOL compiler message links to the local source line, in the program or in a copybook
  • Submit JCL from the Tools menu or the editor popup of a .jcl file
  • Debugging on z/OS (IBM z/OS Debugger) is not part of the plugin; debug with GnuCOBOL locally

AI Assistant & MCP Server

  • AI chat tool window with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Windsurf, Antigravity, Aider, or your own API key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama)
  • Embedded MCP server with 15 tools: programs, outline, data items, usages, call graph, copybook usages, project info, open files, diagnostics, syntax check, compile, PIC mapping, run, run configurations, and run output
  • Discoverable via ~/.flexible-cobol/mcp, and fully optional

Code Style

  • Free-format formatter; fixed-format files are left untouched for column safety

New Project Wizard

  • COBOL appears in the New Project wizard with a sample project scaffold
  • Welcome dialog and guided tour on first start

Optional Language Server

  • Detected servers dropdown: Che4z COBOL Language Support (found in the VS Code extension folder) and SuperBOL (found on PATH, in opam switches, or in the VS Code extension folder), plus a custom command
  • Analysis mode: Enhanced (native results first, the server fills the gaps, duplicates dropped) or Server Only (the server's completions and diagnostics replace the native keyword completion and the cobc syntax check while the server is ready)
  • Per-feature toggles for server completions and diagnostics, and a status bar widget

Getting Started

Quick Start

  1. Install the plugin from the JetBrains Marketplace
  2. Install GnuCOBOL via your system package manager, or use an Arnold Trembley build on Windows
  3. Open an existing COBOL project or create one from the New Project wizard
  4. Accept the detected GnuCOBOL SDK, or set the cobc path under Settings > Languages & Frameworks > COBOL
  5. Open a .cbl file and click the run gutter icon, or use Run > Edit Configurations

Productivity Tips

  • Ctrl+Click a COPY name to open the copybook, a CALL literal to open the called program, a paragraph name to jump to it
  • Ctrl+Q on any verb, PIC clause or data item for quick documentation
  • Alt+Enter on a data structure to generate the Java class or the JSON Schema
  • Alt+F7 on a data item to see every read and write across programs
  • Type ws + Tab to start a WORKING-STORAGE SECTION, prf + Tab for an inline PERFORM

Customization

  • Color schemes: File > Settings > Editor > Color Scheme > COBOL
  • Live templates: File > Settings > Editor > Live Templates > COBOL
  • Inspections: File > Settings > Editor > Inspections > COBOL
  • Dialect, source format, copybook paths, AI and MCP: File > Settings > Languages & Frameworks > COBOL

Troubleshooting

  • File not recognized? Check Settings > Editor > File Types: .cbl, .cob, .cobol belong to COBOL, .cpy, .copy to COBOL Copybook
  • cobc not found? Set the path in the COBOL settings or add a GnuCOBOL SDK in Project Structure
  • Copybook not resolved? Add its directory to the copybook paths in the COBOL settings

What's New in 2026.1.4

  • COBOL-level debugger: steps by COBOL line and PERFORM, data by COBOL name with Set Value, COBOL conditions on breakpoints, stop on runtime errors, data watchpoints
  • z/OS over z/OSMF: upload, compile, link and run on the mainframe with generated JCL, spool in the console, clickable IGY messages, Zowe config import
  • Multi-program builds and fixes: CALLed programs built as modules, clickable compiler errors, Ctrl+Click on COPY and CALL, JSON Schema from the IDE, no build files in the project

See CHANGELOG.md for complete details.

Made by Developers with a Passion for Legacy Systems

The integration is the work of Ilscipio:

We develop software solutions and understand the unique needs of teams who keep COBOL systems running. We created this plugin to make COBOL development and modernization more productive in JetBrains IDEs.

We're sharing this tool with the COBOL community to support the ecosystem's growth and to make legacy modernization more approachable.

  • Flexible COBOL is free for students and open source projects, and non-profits get a 50% discount.

Bugs & Feature Requests

If you have any questions, feature requests or stumble upon the occasional bug, come leave us a message at Ilscipio

  • Plugin page: plugins.jetbrains.com
  • GitHub Issues: flexible-cobol-jetbrains-plugin
  • Email: info@ilscipio.com

idea-plugin.name: GitHub Actions Pwn-Request Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags a GitHub Actions job -- triggered by pull_request_target/workflow_run -- that checks out untrusted PR/workflow_run head content while secrets are reachable, either directly in its own steps or through a local reusable-workflow call (uses: ./.github/workflows/x.yml with secrets: inherit or an explicit secrets: map). This is the real "Pwn Request" pattern GitHub Security Lab documents, the mechanism behind several real supply-chain incidents.

Built on a real reusable-workflow call graph across EVERY workflow file in .github/workflows/ -- resolving whether the TARGET of a reusable-workflow call actually uses secrets, not just whether the caller passes them.

Not a real YAML parser -- an indentation-based micro-scanner, same discipline as this catalog's other YAML plugins.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only follows local reusable-workflow calls (./.github/workflows/x.yml, never an external repo reference) one hop deep.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: Maven Lens
idea-plugin.description:
Automatically exposes Maven plugins and their full transitive dependency graph as IntelliJ project libraries. Perfect for debugging build extensions, exploring plugin code, and enabling full IDE code completion for custom Maven goals.

By default, IntelliJ IDEA indexes standard project dependencies, but leaves the classes and dependencies of Maven plugins hidden from the Project View, code completion, and search. Maven Lens automates this bridging process.

Key Features

  • Automatic Attachment: Automatically triggers after every Maven reload/import.
  • Plugin Visibility: Registers all declared Maven plugins as standard Project Libraries.
  • Deep Dependency Resolution: Asks the real Maven embedder to resolve each plugin's full transitive dependency graph — exactly as Maven does for an actual build, including any <dependencies> overrides declared on the plugin — not just the artifacts declared directly. Artifacts missing from your local repository are downloaded on demand.
  • Instant Code Exploration: Enables standard IDE features like "Go to Class", code completion, and decompilation for plugin internals.
  • On/Off Switch: A toggle in the Maven tool window toolbar turns the attachment off per project and detaches the libraries it added; turning it back on re-resolves them right away.

How it works

Every time you reimport your Maven project, Maven Lens asks the out-of-process Maven embedder to resolve every declared plugin exactly as it would for a real build — picking up the full transitive dependency graph and triggering a download for anything not already in your local .m2/repository — then maps the resolved JARs onto the project structure seamlessly, without altering your original build files.

idea-plugin.name: Spring Init Support
idea-plugin.description:
Adds a Spring Boot module to the build you already have. Generated through the public Spring Initializr REST API — start.spring.io by default, switchable to start.aliyun.com or any custom Initializr service.

IntelliJ IDEA has bundled a free Spring Boot project wizard since 2025.3, and it creates a standalone project. Point it at an existing Maven or Gradle build and you get a directory the enclosing build knows nothing about: no <modules> entry, no include, and a module inheriting from the remote spring-boot-starter-parent instead of from your aggregator — so it sits outside the reactor and outside your dependency management. This plugin wires it in. On IDEA 2024.3 through 2025.2, where there is no bundled wizard at all, it also provides the wizard itself.

A real IDE wizard, not a web page in a window. This plugin is built on the IDE's own project-generation framework, so it behaves like everything else in IntelliJ IDEA rather than like an embedded copy of the start.spring.io site:

  • Both entry points. New Project and New Module inside an open project — an embedded web page cannot generate a module into a build you already have.
  • The new module joins your build. include '<module>' for Gradle, a <module> entry for Maven, and a Maven module is re-pointed at the aggregator so the parent's dependency management actually reaches it. The Spring Boot version defaults to the one your build already uses.
  • Fields that follow the IDE. The Java version follows the JDK you picked in the same dialog; the package name follows Group and Artifact until you type your own.
  • The dependency picker is the IDE's own tree, with a search box that matches the way start.spring.io matches — by word, across name, id, description and category.
  • Java, Kotlin or Groovy, with Maven, the Gradle Groovy DSL or the Gradle Kotlin DSL. The two choices are independent.

This plugin is not affiliated with JetBrains, VMware, or the Spring team. It does not unlock or bypass any IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate features.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.2.8
  • The generator row is now called "Spring Boot Init". IntelliJ IDEA 2025.3 and later bundle their own "Spring Boot" entry in the same list, and the wizard tells entries apart by that label alone - two entries with the same label collapse into one, and the bundled one kept the slot, so on those versions this plugin's wizard was simply not there. Ours is labelled distinctly now, so both rows appear and the two wizards can be told apart.
0.2.7
  • Proxies that require a sign-in work. The plugin now authenticates with the credentials configured in the IDE, so requests behind an authenticated corporate proxy no longer fail. The proxy address was never the problem — only the credentials were missing.
  • A Server URL that cannot be used says so, once, with the reason. It is no longer silently replaced by the previously selected service, and the row keeps what you entered. The failure message used to be erased a few milliseconds after it appeared.
  • Next checks that the service really answers and really offers Spring Boot versions, instead of only checking that the URL is well formed. Clicking Next again retries — nothing is remembered from a previous attempt, so a service that becomes reachable works immediately.
  • Page 2 always shows the selected service's own dependencies. An unreachable service is no longer stood in for by the bundled snapshot.
  • A custom service URL is entered through the gear next to the row, and is remembered alongside the two presets — choosing a preset no longer forgets it.
  • The Settings page checks the URL the same way, so a service refused in the wizard can no longer be saved from Settings instead.
  • The project gets the JDK you picked. Choosing one of the "Detected JDKs" — a JDK on your disk that is not registered in the IDE yet — used to produce a project with no SDK at all, so it opened on "Project JDK is not defined" and you had to set it up again. This affects IDEA 2024.3 through 2025.2, where the platform registers such a JDK asynchronously and then reads the result too early; 2025.3 and later are unaffected.
0.2.6
  • Marketplace compatibility: a rejected IntelliJ internal API in the Gradle module wiring was replaced with public equivalents. What gets written to your settings file, and everything else, is unchanged.
0.2.5
  • The plugin has an icon of its own, in the Plugins list and in the New Project generator row.
  • Free for any use, but no longer MIT: redistribution and derivative works are not permitted. See the licence for the terms.
0.2.4
  • Language: Java, Kotlin or Groovy.
  • Build system: Maven, Gradle - Groovy or Gradle - Kotlin. The two choices are independent, so a Java project can be built by a build.gradle.kts.
  • The dependency search matches word by word: web spring and even springweb now find Spring Web.
0.2.3
  • A search box on the dependency page.
  • The generated main class opens again for every project name.
  • A generated Maven module inherits from the aggregator it was added to.

idea-plugin.name: Monkey C
idea-plugin.description:
Write, build, run and debug Monkey C, the language of Garmin Connect IQ devices — watch faces, watch apps, data fields, widgets and barrels, for Garmin smartwatches and Edge cycling computers.

Completion over the whole Toybox API, diagnostics as you type, go to definition, hover documentation, parameter info, rename, find usages, symbols, and type and call hierarchies — and they keep pace with the SDK you have installed rather than falling behind it.

  • Run configurations for the app, its unit tests, an export to .iq, and barrels; a build for the watch, with an offer to install it over USB.
  • Breakpoints, stepping, variables and expression evaluation, in the simulator.
  • Every build measured against the target watch's memory limit — from 64 KB to 2304 KB depending on the device, and the constraint that shapes this platform.
  • A form editor for manifest.xml, a new project wizard, unit tests with a test tree, and a developer key you can generate without openssl.
  • Syntax highlighting for .mc, .jungle and .mss.

Getting started

  1. Install the Connect IQ SDK with Garmin's SDK Manager, and download at least one device with it. The plugin finds it on its own.
  2. New Project | Connect IQ, or open a folder that already has a monkey.jungle in it.
  3. Generate a developer key in Settings | Languages & Frameworks | Monkey C, which is what signs every build.
  4. Run it. The same settings page carries a setup checklist that names anything still missing, and offers to fix it.

Code intelligence needs LSP4IJ, which the IDE installs with this plugin.

IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1 and later, and Android Studio 2026.1 and later. Windows, macOS and Linux, wherever the Connect IQ SDK runs.

Trademarks

Garmin, Connect IQ and Monkey C are trademarks of Garmin Ltd. or its subsidiaries. They are used here only to name the language this plugin supports and the devices it builds for, which is a statement of compatibility and nothing more.

This is an independent, open-source project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Garmin, and it redistributes nothing of Garmin's: it finds the SDK the user installed and runs the programs already in it.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Installing on a watch

  • On macOS and Windows a current watch is reached through mtp-rs and nothing else, and its absence is now said where the watch would have been: in the watch list beside Run, in the settings, and after a build for a watch that could not be found — each with an Install mtp-rs button.
  • The button downloads mtp-rs 0.9.1 for this system from the project's GitHub release, installs it only if it matches a checksum built into the plugin, and keeps it in JetBrains' shared data directory, so it survives IDE updates. After a build, the watch is then looked for again and offered the build. This is the plugin's only network request, and it is only ever made on that click.
  • An mtp-rs installed by hand — with brew install vdavid/tap/mtp-rs, the project's install scripts or cargo — is found and preferred when it is 0.9.1 or a later 0.9.x. An older one, or one past the next breaking release, is said, and the plugin's own is offered beside it rather than over it.
  • On Linux, a watch that GNOME, Cinnamon, MATE, Budgie or Pantheon has mounted is installed on through that mount, with no mtp-rs at all. Under KDE or Xfce, or with no desktop, mtp-rs is offered as above.
  • On macOS, a watch that cannot be opened because the system's ptpcamerad holds it now says so, with the command that frees it.

idea-plugin.name: MicroGulp

Rock your Gulp! An interactive Gulp dashboard for JetBrains IDEs - parameters, progress, structured results and history.

Works in IntelliJ IDEA, PhpStorm, WebStorm, PyCharm, Rider, CLion, GoLand, RubyMine, DataGrip and other IntelliJ-based IDEs. PhpStorm and WebStorm already run and debug Gulp; this plugin adds a dashboard in a tool window. Configure the engine under Settings → Tools → µGulp (Node path, gulpfile, pool, logs). idea-plugin.name: Gradle Typesafe Conventions
idea-plugin.description:
Integration for Gradle builds that use dev.panuszewski.typesafe-conventions.

The Gradle plugin generates type-safe catalog accessors for convention plugins in places such as buildSrc and included build logic. This IntelliJ plugin adds the missing imported version catalog model for those builds so IDE navigation and usage search can connect generated accessors back to their original TOML entries.

Features

  • Supports version catalogs imported by the typesafe-conventions Gradle plugin after Gradle sync.
  • Restores Kotlin DSL navigation from catalog accessors such as libs.junit.jupiter to gradle/libs.versions.toml.
  • Restores Groovy DSL navigation for catalog roots, including custom catalog names such as customLibs.
  • Adds catalog models for build logic projects where IntelliJ IDEA does not create them by default, including buildSrc.

The integration is only active for Gradle builds whose settings apply dev.panuszewski.typesafe-conventions.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Initial integration for Gradle dev.panuszewski.typesafe-conventions version catalog models.
  • Support for build logic version catalog navigation and usage search in builds that apply dev.panuszewski.typesafe-conventions.

Changed

  • Reduced Kotlin catalog navigation and Find Usages overhead by reusing synchronized catalog and TOML alias indexes and limiting indexed usage searches to the Gradle builds that consume the target catalog.

Fixed

  • Ignore unrelated Project extensions that resemble generated catalog accessors, completely clean up every unlinked Gradle root, and refresh synchronized catalogs without blocking the UI thread.
  • Fixed an IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1 Kotlin DSL navigation crash while preserving declaration navigation, Find Usages, and rename support for version catalogs used from buildSrc and included build logic.
  • Resolve dotted and separator-normalized Kotlin catalog accessors to the exact TOML key segment, so Goto Declaration, Find Usages, and rename preserve the unaffected parts of an alias and ignore shadowed or programmatic-only accessors.
  • Goto Declaration on the versions, bundles, and plugins token of a Kotlin catalog accessor now reaches the matching TOML section instead of falling through to the generated accessor code.
  • Find Usages on a versions, bundles, or plugins section name in a version catalog now finds the Kotlin accessors using that section, including usages in buildSrc and included build logic, and reports usages of every catalog even when several catalogs are searched together.
  • Preserve catalog navigation across sequential linked Gradle root syncs, failed or cancelled imports, IDE restarts, and unlink operations without replacing last-known-good state with partial model data.
  • Avoid blocking dynamic plugin unload by reusing Gradle-owned Workspace Model entity sources instead of plugin-owned sources.
  • Restored Groovy DSL goto declaration for custom version catalog roots such as customLibs in buildSrc convention plugins.
  • Resolve Groovy catalog accessors declared through standard tables, dotted keys, or inline tables with separator normalization, while keeping same-named accessors isolated by catalog section.
  • Restore Kotlin Goto Declaration and Find Usages for generated catalog entrypoints outside the hard-coded generated-source path, including version catalog aliases used in precompiled Kotlin script plugins blocks.
  • Restore catalog navigation after Gradle sync when version catalog models are reported by buildSrc or another resolver beneath the linked Gradle root.

idea-plugin.name: GitLab Pipeline Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
View, trigger, and manage GitLab CI/CD pipelines directly inside IntelliJ IDEA. No need to switch to a browser: browse pipeline status, inspect build logs, and trigger, retry, or cancel pipelines in one place.

Core features

  • Project auto-detection: collects Git remotes of all projects in the current window (including attached modules) and lets you pick a target project from the GitLab group tree (lazy loading on demand)
  • Pipeline list: status / ref / SHA / source / creation time / duration / trigger user, with pagination for older pipelines
  • New pipeline: pick a branch or enter a ref manually, and optionally pass custom CI/CD variables (key=value)
  • Cancel / retry: supported at both pipeline and job level; run when: manual manual jobs
  • Build logs: shown in a ConsoleView with ANSI coloring, dynamic appending, incremental fetching, keyword search and highlight navigation
  • Auto refresh: running pipelines refresh their logs incrementally at a configurable interval
  • Adaptive layout: the tool window splits top/bottom when docked on a side, and switches to left/right when docked at the bottom or top

Compatibility

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2023.1 and later
  • GitLab.com and self-hosted GitLab (REST API v4, token needs the api scope)

Source code

  • GitHub
  • Gitee

This plugin is an independently developed open source extension released under the Apache License 2.0. It is not an official JetBrains or GitLab product.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.0

  • First stable release
  • View pipelines of multiple GitLab projects: status / ref / duration / trigger user, with pagination
  • Create pipelines (custom CI/CD variables), cancel / retry pipelines and individual jobs, run manual jobs
  • Job build logs: ANSI coloring, incremental refresh, keyword search and highlight navigation
  • Built against IntelliJ IDEA 2023.2, compatible with 2023.1 and later

idea-plugin.name: CollectionSync
idea-plugin.description:
Keep your Postman and Insomnia collections in sync with your code. CollectionSync — Endpoint Coverage Tracker compares the REST endpoints declared in your Java project (OpenAPI 3.x documents, Spring MVC and JAX-RS/Quarkus controllers) against the requests of your existing Postman (v2.1) and Insomnia (v4) collections. The "Endpoint Coverage" tool window shows, endpoint by endpoint, which ones are covered, uncovered, orphaned or excluded, lets you navigate to the handler method, exclude noisy endpoints from the calculation and export the full report as Markdown or CSV.

Main Features

  • Endpoint Discovery: Scans Spring (@RestController, @RequestMapping...) and JAX-RS/Quarkus (@Path, @GET...) controllers, or a local OpenAPI 3.x document, to build the list of REST endpoints in your project.
  • Collection Import: Parses Postman v2.1 or Insomnia v4 collections (JSON and YAML), tolerating broken files without aborting the report.
  • Coverage Tracking: Classifies every endpoint as COVERED, UNCOVERED or ORPHAN, with structural path matching (variables match by position, strict mode keeps {@code /users/{id}} apart from {@code /users/me}).
  • Exclusions: Right-click any endpoint to exclude it from the calculation (e.g. {@code /actuator/{name}}); excluded rows stay visible so the exclusion can be undone with one click.
  • Navigation: Double-click a row to jump to the controller method, or to the configured OpenAPI document.
  • Export: Export the complete report (including excluded rows) as Markdown or CSV.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.0

  • Endpoint Coverage Tracker. Coverage tool window comparing OpenAPI/Spring/JAX-RS endpoints with Postman v2.1 and Insomnia v4 collections: status table with filters, navigation to handlers, exclusion rules and Markdown/CSV report export.

idea-plugin.name: Maven Settings Templates
idea-plugin.description:
Manage Maven home, user settings file and local repository as reusable templates, and apply them to projects automatically.

If you work on projects for different companies or teams, each one usually needs its own settings.xml and local repository. New clones, new git worktrees and deleted .idea folders all start with the wrong values. This plugin keeps the right ones in place.

  • Templates: Maven home (bundled Maven 3, Maven wrapper or a custom path), user settings file and local repository. Empty fields mean the IDE default; paths may contain ${user.home}.
  • Folder rules: every project under a folder uses its template. The deepest matching folder wins.
  • Default template for projects that match no rule, and per-project overrides.
  • Applied when a project opens, including new clones and git worktrees.
  • Drift notifications when a project's Maven settings no longer match its template, with Restore, Save as project custom and Ignore.

Configure it under Settings | Build, Execution, Deployment | Build Tools | Maven | Settings Templates.

idea-plugin.name: App Distribution for Firebase
idea-plugin.description:
Build a signed release APK and send it to your testers with Firebase App Distribution, without leaving Android Studio.

Features

  • One-click release build of your app module, using the same Gradle JDK as the IDE. Works with product flavors, custom APK names and projects that sign through Generate Signed App Bundle / APK (your keystore is remembered securely).
  • Distribute to testers with release notes. Recent testers are remembered per project.
  • Live progress with cancel, and a link to the release in the Firebase console.
  • Firebase CLI handled for you: uses your installed firebase, or downloads the standalone CLI (no Node.js needed). Sign in from the tool window.
  • Optional Slack announcements through an Incoming Webhook, with nicely formatted release notes.

Getting started

  1. Open the App Distribution tool window (right side).
  2. Install / sign in to Firebase CLI when prompted.
  3. Click Build Release APK, add testers and notes, then Distribute.

Your app needs a google-services.json for a Firebase project with App Distribution enabled.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Google. Firebase is a trademark of Google LLC.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • A Post this build to Slack checkbox on the Distribute step, remembered per project.
  • If no webhook is set up yet, ticking it opens a Connect Slack dialog with step-by-step instructions, a link to Slack, and a test message button.

Changed

  • The Slack settings page now shows whether a webhook is saved, with Set Up, Change and Remove. The old global "Announce each distribution" switch is replaced by the per-build checkbox.

Fixed

  • Dialogs now always validate on Save, so an invalid webhook URL or incomplete keystore details can't be saved.

idea-plugin.name: Runners Bar
idea-plugin.description:
Your most used run configurations, one click away. Runners Bar adds a slim bar above the status bar (or below the toolbar) that holds run configurations as tabs. Click a tab and it runs. No dropdown, no searching, no switching the selected configuration.

Features

  • One-click start: every tab runs its configuration directly, or debugs it if you switched the tab to debug mode.
  • Arrow menu per tab: debug once (or run once without the debugger), toggle debug mode, stop, open the configuration's settings, move or remove the tab.
  • Groups: keep different sets of tabs, e.g. Frontend, Backend or Deploy, and switch between them. A configuration can be part of several groups.
  • Drag and drop: reorder tabs by dragging them like editor tabs; drag a tab out of the bar and drop it to remove it; press Escape to cancel.
  • New configurations: create a run configuration from the + menu, it lands in the bar right away.
  • Your layout: place the bar below the toolbar or above the status bar, align the tabs left, center or right, put the controls on either side and hide the menu arrow if you prefer the right click. Set your defaults once and override them per project.
  • Running state: running configurations are highlighted.
  • Follows renamed configurations, keeps the bar per project and stores it in your personal workspace (not in version control).

Usage

  • Click + to add an existing or a new run configuration. Its Runners Bar submenu creates groups, hides the bar in the current project and changes position and alignment.
  • Settings: Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Runners Bar, with defaults for all projects and the values of the current project.
  • Show or hide the bar via View | Appearance | Runners Bar.
  • Don't need it in a particular project? Choose Hide in This Project in the + menu's Runners Bar submenu, or toggle View | Appearance | Runners Bar in This Project.

Works in all JetBrains IDEs based on the IntelliJ Platform (PhpStorm, IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, ...). UI available in English and German.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.0

  • The settings page now holds defaults for all projects; each project can override position, alignment and the menu arrow (in the settings page or the + menu's Runners Bar submenu).
  • Showing or hiding the bar in a project now overrides the default, so a single project can show the bar while it is hidden everywhere else.
  • Option to hide the menu arrow on the tabs; the menu stays available with a right click.

1.0.0

  • Create new run configurations right from the + menu; they are added to the bar automatically.
  • Position the bar at the top (below the toolbar) or at the bottom (above the status bar).
  • Align the tabs left, center or right, and put the controls (+, group switcher) on the left or right.
  • New settings page Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Runners Bar and a Runners Bar submenu in the + menu for groups, hiding, position and alignment.
  • At the top, the bar continues the project color gradient of the toolbar.

0.2.0

  • Hide the bar in a single project: Hide in This Project in the + menu or View | Appearance | Runners Bar in This Project.
  • Drag and drop like editor tabs: the tab follows the mouse, the other tabs make room, and it turns red when dragged out of the bar to remove it. Escape cancels.

0.1.0

  • First release: run configurations as tabs above the status bar.
  • Debug once, debug mode per tab, stop, settings, reorder and remove.
  • Groups with switcher, drag and drop to reorder or remove.

idea-plugin.name: Runcradle
idea-plugin.description:
Run one job of a GitHub Actions workflow on your own machine, in local Linux containers, from an ordinary IDE run configuration. Check a workflow change before you push it.

What it does

  • Pick the workflow, job and event from your repository. Jobs it depends on are shown before the run.
  • Pick a literal subset of a static matrix so only those combinations run, and keep it with the run configuration.
  • Preflight checks the job and your local runtime before anything starts. Each finding is marked blocked, warning or unknown and links to the exact line of the workflow file.
  • Step output streams into the Run console. When a step fails, its line in the workflow is one click away.
  • Stop ends the run and removes the containers and volumes Runcradle started for it.

Share the setup with your team

  • Workflow, job, event, matrix choice, runner images and inputs are saved with the run configuration and can be exported as a preset your team can commit.
  • Secret values stay in the IDE password store on each machine and are never written to the shared settings. Local overrides stay on your machine.

Requirements and limits

  • Windows, 64-bit.
  • Docker in Linux container mode. Runcradle runs jobs on the listed Ubuntu Linux runner labels or in a job container.
  • A local run is a close check of your workflow, and GitHub remains the final word. OIDC tokens and deployment environments are reported by preflight before the run, and a dynamic matrix is refused in the run configuration.
  • Workflow code runs on your machine as trusted code, so run workflows you trust.
  • Run output is kept within the IDE console buffer, which you can resize in the IDE settings.

Every licence starts with a free 30-day trial.
idea-plugin.change-notes: First release: run a single GitHub Actions job locally from an IDE run configuration, with preflight findings linked to the workflow line.

idea-plugin.name: Flexible Delphi
idea-plugin.description:
Form designer with component palette, Object Inspector and code links for every event. Completion, hover docs, refactoring, inspections, compile, run and debug. Binary DFM files, SQL and asm injection, Free Pascal and Lazarus projects.


We are a young plugin and want to make it the best Delphi tool in the IDE. Your feedback is critical: report a bug or an idea and get 20% off the annual license, or one month free.


Feedback: Leave a review, open an issue on GitHub, or write to info@ilscipio.com.


Documentation: Open the Tutorials tab on this page, or Help > Flexible Delphi Welcome and Tutorial in the IDE.


Flexible Delphi is an independent plugin and is not affiliated with Embarcadero Technologies, the Free Pascal and Lazarus projects, or JetBrains.


Core Features

Form Designer

  • Design tab for every unit with a form. F12 switches between form and code in the Delphi keymap
  • Component palette with search and 81 VCL and LCL components in 8 groups, including the Castle Game Engine control
  • Canvas with select, move, resize, grid snap, alignment guides, nesting, copy and paste, and undo
  • Object Inspector with properties and events grouped by category, a filter and check boxes for Boolean values
  • Double-click a component or an event to create the handler in the unit and jump to it. A new component gets its field and its uses entry
  • Binary DFM files open in the designer and save back as binary. Convert them to text DFM in one step
  • Show in Designer gutter icons on form fields and event handlers

Language Support

  • Native Object Pascal parser built with Grammar-Kit and JFlex for Delphi, Free Pascal (Delphi and ObjFPC modes), Turbo Pascal and ISO Pascal. No language server is needed
  • Tested on real code: 3,403 of 3,415 files of the Lazarus component library, Delphi sample projects, an open source Delphi web framework and old Delphi projects parse without an error
  • Conditional compilation: {$IFDEF}, {$IF}, {$ELSE} and {$DEFINE} are evaluated with the project defines, and inactive code is grey
  • Old and new code: ANSI (Windows-1252) source detection, Turbo Pascal control characters, generics, attributes, anonymous methods, inline variables, multiline strings and the if expression
  • Form files: text DFM, LFM and FMX files with highlighting, and binary DFM files of older Delphi versions
  • Semantic highlighting of types, routines, fields, properties, parameters, locals, constants and directive words, with color settings
  • Folding of routines, blocks, classes, uses clauses, comments, {$REGION} and inactive code
  • Formatter in Delphi style, with code style settings

Navigation & Intelligence

  • Go to Declaration (Ctrl+Click) across units, uses clauses, unit scope names, inherited members and generic types
  • Declaration and implementation with Ctrl+Shift+Up and Ctrl+Shift+Down, as in Delphi
  • Class completion with Alt+Enter, or Ctrl+Shift+C in the Delphi keymap: missing method bodies, property fields and property accessors
  • Call Hierarchy (Ctrl+Alt+H): the callers and the callees of a routine
  • Find Usages (Alt+F7) and Rename, case-insensitive, including the implementation and the form file. Usages show as read or write
  • Structure View, Breadcrumbs, Go to Symbol and Go to Class
  • Gutter icons for overridden methods and for the declaration and implementation of each method

Completion & Documentation

  • Code completion that opens after a dot, for members, unit names in uses clauses, types, keywords and compiler directives. Private and protected members show only where Delphi allows them
  • Parameter info (Ctrl+P) with every overload, and parameter name hints before literal arguments
  • Hover documentation from /// XMLDoc comments, and bundled documentation for 320 RTL and VCL symbols
  • 28 code templates from the Delphi IDE, such as tryf, forin and prop
  • Postfix templates: .if, .not, .nil, .notnil, .for, .forin, .try, .tryf and .writeln
  • Automatic end after begin, try, case and repeat

Inspections & Quick Fixes

  • Unresolved identifier, unused unit in a uses clause, unused local variable, function result not set, missing method implementation, empty except block, missing inherited, unreachable code, assignment to a for-loop variable, and Delphi-only syntax in Free Pascal files
  • Alt+Enter on an unknown name: add the unit to the uses clause, declare a local variable or a field, or create the routine. Remove an unused unit

Language Injection

  • Built-in assembler in asm ... end blocks, with its own highlighting
  • SQL, RegExp, JSON, HTML and XML in strings, chosen by the call (Query.SQL.Text, TRegEx, TJSONObject.ParseJSONValue), by the content, or by a // language= comment. Concatenated strings form one fragment, also with variables between the parts
  • SQL in form files (SQL.Strings). Without the Database plugin, a built-in SQL highlighter is used

Compile, Run & Debug

  • SDKs for Free Pascal, Lazarus and Delphi, with detection of installed compilers
  • Project import from .dproj, .lpi, .dof and .cfg files: search paths, defines and unit scope names
  • Run configurations that compile and run, with clickable compiler messages. Compile and build from the Build menu, or with Ctrl+F9 and Shift+F9 in the Delphi keymap
  • A notice on the editor when no Free Pascal or Delphi compiler is found
  • Debugger for Free Pascal and Lazarus builds: breakpoints, Step Over and Step Into that stay in your code, call stack, locals and evaluation (GDB)
  • New project wizard: console application, LCL form application, VCL form application and library. New unit and new form

MCP Server

  • Embedded MCP server for MCP clients: PSI tree, parse errors, references, usages, completion, documentation, injections, inspections, forms, and compile, run and debug

idea-plugin.name: Visual Debugger
idea-plugin.description:
This plugin visualizes the variables during a debugging session as a UML object diagram. The plugin is used alongside normal debugging. Set a breakpoint for debugging and start the debugging as usual in the IDE. The plugin will automatically create a visual debugging toolbar in the debug window, shown in the screenshot. All variables in the scope of a debugging session will be visualized as an object diagram.
The default visualization is browser-based and allows double click on objects to load its children directly from the UI. In addition, there is an embedded visualization using PlantUML, which does not support user interaction.
By default, the plugin will visualize objects up to a depth of 3, but this is configurable using the plugin settings. The browser UI allows the user to download the current object diagram as an SVG- or XML-File for future discussion. Printing an SVG-File when using the embedded visualization can be done from the IDE using the print icon in the plugin toolbar.

idea-plugin.name: Maven Dependency Checker
idea-plugin.description:
Checks if there are any new Maven project dependencies or build plugins available.

A notification dialogue will show you which dependencies or plugins used in the project can and should be updated in order to avoid security issues for example.

You'll see the version of the dependencies you use right now and the latest versions available at [Maven Central][central]. You can choose to keep the comparison results by copying the information to the system clipboard or open a generated POM file with updated version information in an editor tab.

The plugin does NOT modify your POM file.

In order to check for updates just select your Maven POM file (pom.xml) in the project explorer view. Right-click the file and choose Check Maven Dependencies from the context menu. You can right-click somewhere in the text editor view as well if the POM file is opened in the editor.

If for some reason you do want the plugin to check for major version updates of your dependencies you can diasable the check in the plugin's settings. Minor and patch version updates are checked nevertheless.

Please keep in mind that Maven dependencies and plugins which are available at [Maven Central][central] will be checked only.

idea-plugin.name: CodeTour
idea-plugin.description:
CodeTour is an Intellij plugin, which allows you to record and play back guided walkthroughs of your codebases. It's like a table of contents, that can make it easier to onboard (or re-board!) to a new project/feature area, visualize bug reports, or understand the context of a code review/PR change. A Code Tour is simply a series of interactive Steps, each of which are associated with a specific file/line, and include a description of the respective code. This allows developers to clone a repo, and then immediately start learning it, without needing to refer to rely on help from others. Tours can be version controlled into a repo, to enable sharing with other contributors.

To use the Code Tour tool window, select View > Tool Windows > Tours Navigation.

Features:

  • Create new Tours and Steps easily through Editor's Gutter context menu (similar to adding breakpoints) Right Click on gutter > Add Tour Step
  • Markdown and HTML support for Step's description
  • Customizable (location, size, font etc) popup window for Step's description
  • Tree-like view of Tours and their Steps on a Tool Window
  • Code Navigation with single click (on Steps available on Tours Tree)
  • Shortcuts for Navigating on Previous (Ctrl+Alt+Q) and Next (Ctrl+ Alt+W) Steps

Ideal for:

  • Code Reviews -- e.g. Walkthrough the context of a Pull Request
  • Feature documentation -- e.g. How a feature's workflow is depicted on the code
  • Visualize bugs -- e.g. follow a scenario that led to an error/bug/issue
  • Onboard or re-board to a project -- Start learning the project through the interactive Tour Steps, without relying on help from others

Feel free to suggest features, request changes and report issues on CodeTour repo https://github.com/LefterisXris/CodeTour/discussions

idea-plugin.name: Build Monitor
idea-plugin.description:
Build Monitor

Description

Monitor Github Action Workflows and Buildkite Builds from within your IDE.
Setup profiles which automatically refresh the status of your builds alerting you when they complete or fail. Easily and quickly retry failed builds with one click.

Cost

The free to use version of the plugin has 100% of the functionality of the paid version, however it is limited by the number of remote accounts you can configure to one. Additional limit on creating up to two "build monitor profiles."

Features

Free

  • Connect to Buildkite to monitor Builds.
  • Connect to Github to monitor Workflow actions.
  • Configurable automatic retry of failed jobs on monitored builds.
  • Configurable notifications (poups and sounds) based on the status of monitored builds.
  • Configurable fields to be displayed inline with your monitored builds.
  • Configurable filter criteria to limit exactly which builds are monitored.

Paid

  • Unlimited Accounts.
  • Unlimited Monitor Profiles.

Usage

Adding Buildkite Account

Create a new Buildkite API Access Token: https://buildkite.com/user/api-access-tokens.

Using your Buildkite account, create a new API access token with the following permissions:

  • GraphQL API To retrieve users, builds, jobs, and pipelines.
  • Read Pipelines To list and retrieve details of pipeslines.
  • Read Builds To list and retrieve details of builds.
  • Modify Builds To create new, retry failed, and cancel running builds.
  • Read User To retrieve basic details about users.
  • Read Organizations Used to list and retrieve details of builds.

Add account to Project Settings for Plugin.

Settings/Preferences > Tools > Build Monitor Accounts

  1. Click the + icon and give your new account a name.
  2. Select BUILDKITE from the Type field.
  3. Paste your API Access Token into to the Api Access Token field.
  4. Click the Test Connection button to verify everything works.

Skip to instructions below labeled Setup Build Monitor Profile

Adding Github Account

Create a new Personal Access Token: https://github.com/settings/tokens.

Using your Github account, create a new Personal Access Token (classic) with the following permissions:

  • Repository
    • READ Required to read Workflow Actions.
  • Workflow
    • READ To list and retrieve details of workflows and workflow actions.
    • WRITE To Rerun, retry, and cancel workflows.

Settings/Preferences > Tools > Build Monitor Accounts

  1. Click the + icon and give your new account a name.
  2. Select GITHUB from the Type field.
  3. Paste your Personal Access Token into to the Api Access Token field.
  4. Click the Test Connection button to verify everything works.

Skip to instructions below labeled Setup Build Monitor Profile

Setup Build Monitor Profile

Build Monitor Profiles allow you to define which builds/workflows you want to show up in the ToolWindow. You can define multiple profiles, each with varying filter criteria. Additionally, you can alter which pieces of information are displayed inline along side the build.

Settings/Preferences > Tools > Build Monitor Accounts > Monitor Profiles

  1. Click the + icon and give your new profile a name.
  2. Select which Account you want to use.
  3. Define the filter criteria to determine which builds will be displayed.
  4. Display Options allows you to select which pieces of information will be included with the build.
  5. Notification Options allows you select which types of notifications you would like to receive for the builds.

Launch Monitor

From the Tools drop down menu select Build Monitor to open the ToolWindow.

Select a Build Monitor Profile to open the display.

Bug Reports and Feature Requests

Submit BugReports or Feature Requests: https://github.com/SourceLabOrg/BuildMonitor_IntellijPlugin/issues

idea-plugin.name: GitLab CICD - Pipelines & Jobs, Builds Run Cancel Retry View Log
idea-plugin.description:
GitLab CICD for software developers

GitLab CICD is an IDE plugin designed to make it easier for you to view and manage GitLab CI/CD directly from within the IDE. The plugin provides a user-friendly interface that allows you to easily view, run, cancel and retry GitLab Pipelines and Jobs without having to switch between the IDE and the GitLab web interface.

It works with both GitLab SaaS and GitLab Self-Managed (15.x or later).


With GitLab CICD, you can:

  • 🔎 Quickly view the status of pipelines.
  • 🖥 View detailed information about each pipeline, stage and job.
  • 🛠 Run, cancel and retry pipeline or job.
  • 📋 Display job log in real time.
  • 💾 Download job artifacts.
  • 🔔 Receive notifications when your pipelines have been started or finished.
  • ✅ Validate/Lint your CICD configuration files (e.g. .gitlab-ci.yml).
  • 🌙 Enjoy GitLab CI/CD in Dark Mode.

❗Important note: The plugin acts as a direct client for GitLab, ensuring that no data is transmitted to any server other than GitLab itself. Access tokens are stored securely on your local machine in the IDE's password storage, which you can configure in the IDE Settings.


To open plugin, click on View -> Tool Windows -> GitLab CICD.

To validate CICD file, right-click on file, then select Validate CICD file.


By using GitLab CICD, you can save time and streamline your development workflows by eliminating the need to switch between multiple applications and interfaces. The plugin is easy to install and use, and provides a seamless integration between IDE and GitLab CI CD.

Plugin supports Chinese (Simplified) language pack.


GitLab CICD 是一个 IDE 插件，旨在使您更轻松地从 IDE 中直接查看和管理 GitLab CI/CD。该插件提供了一个用户友好的界面，允许您在 IDE 内轻松查看、运行、取消和重试 GitLab 流水线和任务，无需在 IDE 和 GitLab Web 界面之间切换。

它与 GitLab SaaS 和 GitLab 自托管（15.x 或更高版本） 都兼容。


使用 GitLab CICD，您可以：

  • 🔎 快速查看流水线的状态。
  • 🖥 查看每个流水线、阶段和任务的详细信息。
  • 🛠 运行、取消和重试流水线或任务。
  • 📋 实时显示任务日志。
  • 💾 下载任务工件。
  • 🔔 在流水线启动或完成时接收通知。
  • ✅ 验证/检查您的 CI/CD 配置文件（例如 .gitlab-ci.yml）。
  • 🌙 在暗模式下享受 GitLab CI/CD。

❗重要提示： 该插件充当 GitLab 的直接客户端，确保除 GitLab 本身外不传输任何数据到其他服务器。访问令牌安全地存储在您本地机器上的 IDE 密码存储中，您可以在 IDE 设置中配置。


要打开插件，请点击 View -> Tool Windows -> GitLab CICD。

要验证 CI/CD 文件，请右键单击文件，然后选择 Validate CICD file。


通过使用 GitLab CICD，您可以节省时间，简化开发工作流程，无需在多个应用程序和界面之间切换。该插件安装和使用都很简单，并在 IDE 和 GitLab CI CD 之间提供了无缝集成。

支持简体中文语言包。

idea-plugin.name: Forester
idea-plugin.description:
Introduction

The Forester-IntelliJ Plugin, an essential integration that brings the power of the Forester framework to your IntelliJ IDE. This plugin enriches your development experience by providing seamless task orchestration capabilities, allowing you to perform tasks synchronously or asynchronously, locally or remotely, all within the familiar IntelliJ environment. Whether you are working on game development, artificial intelligence, robotics, or any domain requiring efficient task management, the Forester-IntelliJ Plugin is here to simplify your workflow and boost productivity.

Features

Syntax Highlighting

The Forester-IntelliJ Plugin includes specialized syntax highlighting, making it easier for you to identify and distinguish Forester-related elements in your code. This feature helps improve code readability and ensures that your tasks are accurately represented.

Folding

With the folding feature, you can conveniently collapse sections of your behavior trees, making complex task structures more manageable. Folding enhances code organization and enables you to focus on specific parts of the task tree as needed.

Structure View

Task Visualization

The Forester-IntelliJ Plugin offers a task to visualize the tree that brings behavior trees to life. Gain valuable insights into your task flows and dependencies through interactive graphical representations. This visual aid fosters a better understanding of your task hierarchy, facilitating effective task organization and management.

Task Simulation

With the task simulation feature, you can run and test your behavior trees directly within the IntelliJ IDE. Simulate task executions to verify their correctness and efficiency, enabling you to fine-tune your task orchestration process.

Usage

Creating a New configuration

  1. Navigate to the "Edit configurations" menu in your IntelliJ IDE.
  2. Select "New Task" to create a new task.
  3. Select one to visualize or simulate the tree.

Running Simulation and Visualization Task

  1. Open the behavior tree you want to simulate.
  2. Click on the root tree gutter on the left side of the record to initiate the simulation or visualization configuration.
