idea-plugin.name: Project Warning Reminder
idea-plugin.description:
Shows warning notifications when a project contains one or more .warning files in the project root directory.

Useful for reminding team members about project-specific cautions, temporary notices, or important setup instructions when opening a project.

If the plugin messes up your IDE, please go to plugin directory and remove folder ProjectWarningReminder.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.0

  • Initial release.
  • Scans the project root for .warning files on project startup.
  • Displays each warning as an IDE notification.

idea-plugin.name: GitHub PRs Monitor
idea-plugin.description:
Stay on top of every GitHub PR without leaving your IDE. GitHub PRs Monitor continuously polls your repositories for review comments, review bodies, review requests, and approval-status changes across all open Pull Requests, delivers desktop notifications, and gives you a dedicated tool window to browse, preview, and navigate everything — all in one place.

Core Features

  • Automatic polling — Periodically fetches comments, reviews, and review-request state from all open PRs via the GitHub API using your IDE's GitHub account.
  • Desktop notifications — Balloon alerts for new and edited comments, incoming review requests, and approval-status changes (APPROVED / CHANGES_REQUESTED) with quick actions: jump to file, view in tool window, or open on GitHub. Alerts that arrive together are merged into a single balloon, so a busy poll can't push the important one off screen. When an alert comes from a project whose window you aren't looking at, it is also mirrored into another visible IDE window (labeled with the origin project name) so you never miss it, and every alert is listed in the Notifications panel of all open windows, so you can find and act on it from any project. Selecting the item a balloon points at in the tool window dismisses that balloon (and its mirror), so reviewing an item clears its own alert; multi-item digests and recurring reminders clear once every item they cover is read. Balloons also clear themselves when the project they point at opens or closes, or when the PR they are about is merged or closed, so an alert never outlives the data it describes.
  • @-mention notifications — A dedicated balloon (and matching periodic reminder) fires whenever a comment body or the pull request's own description literally @-mentions your GitHub login. A mention also pulls in PRs you neither authored nor review, overriding the PR-author / reviewer-scope filters, and bypasses the open-only, comment author / body, outdated and resolved filters — so a direct ping always surfaces. Muted PRs stay muted. Optional aliases let colleagues ping you by a nickname or shortened login.
  • Review bodies — Top-level review messages (e.g. "LGTM") are shown alongside inline comments with per-state icons in the tree.
  • Review requests & approval status — PR nodes show dedicated indicators when you're requested as a reviewer or when any reviewer submits an approval / changes-requested review, even when the review body is empty.
  • Unread & review-request reminders — Optional periodic reminders for unread comments (when the tool window is not visible) and for PRs still awaiting your review (independent of comments — fires even when every comment is read). A project's unread, @-mention and review-request reminders share one balloon, which never re-appears while it is still on screen and otherwise repeats at a configurable interval — sooner when something new arrives. Snooze 1 hour / Snooze until tomorrow 09:00 cover everything the balloon lists. Stop reminding me about this PR silences the review reminder for one PR for good — nothing is hidden, other PRs keep reminding you, and it clears itself once the request resolves. Both are also available from the tree's Review reminder right-click submenu, persist across IDE restarts, and apply to monitored closed projects too.
  • Closed-project monitoring — Cached projects you're not currently working in are polled on their own background cycle and raise the same alerts (new / edited comments, review requests, approval status, unread reminder, mention reminder) — one balloon per project per check — with an Open project and view comments action that reopens the project and jumps straight to the PR Monitor tool window. Per-project opt-out list under Settings.
  • Edit detection — Edited comments are automatically marked as unread and flagged with an "(edited)" label so you never miss an update.
  • Read / unread tracking — Per-comment read state with a dynamic unread-count badge on the tool window icon.
  • GitHub notification sync — Optionally sync read state with GitHub's Notifications API (inbound-only or bidirectional).

Tool Window

  • Tree view — Comments organized by PR → file (with file-type icons) → individual comments and replies, with PRs ordered newest-first by creation date.
  • Comment preview — Rendered markdown preview pane with a resizable splitter. GitHub <details> blocks render as collapsible foldable sections you fold by clicking anywhere on the summary line, and selecting a PR node shows the pull request's full description.
  • One-click navigation — Click a comment to open the exact file and line in the editor; branch mismatch detection prompts you to check out the correct branch first.
  • Configurable double-click — Independent settings for top-level comments, inline review comments, and PR / PR-status rows: open the file, open the PR timeline editor tab, or open on GitHub.
  • Toolbar controls — Refresh, expand / collapse all, mark all as read, filter by author, toggle unread-only view, toggle preview pane, and quick access to settings. A dimmed status line shows when each poller (open and closed projects) last fetched and when its next poll fires.
  • Per-PR muting — Right-click any PR node to mute it; unmute from the same menu or the toolbar dropdown. By default an @-mention still gets through: the muted PR reappears marked [muted] carrying only the comment that tagged you. To stop only the recurring review reminder for a PR while keeping the PR itself fully visible, use Review reminder → Stop reminding me about this PR from the same menu instead.

Highly Customizable via Settings

Fine-tune the plugin to your workflow under Settings → Tools → GitHub PRs Monitor:

  • Per-project settings — App-level defaults that new projects inherit, with an optional Use settings specific to this project override for fine-grained control per repository. (Paid feature.)
  • Polling interval — From 1 to 60 minutes.
  • PR author filter — Show all PRs, only your own, or use a whitelist / blacklist of GitHub usernames.
  • PR reviewer filter — Show only PRs where you're requested as a reviewer or have already reviewed; optionally include team-based review requests.
  • Comment author filter — Whitelist or blacklist specific comment authors.
  • Comment content filter — Multi-line regex whitelist / blacklist on comment body text; each non-empty line is its own pattern.
  • Inline-comment filters — Independent Ignore outdated and Ignore resolved toggles for inline review comments (status refreshed every poll via GraphQL).
  • Show as filtered — For each filter, opt in to keep filtered items visible in the tree (greyed / strikethrough) instead of hiding them. Filtered items still stay out of notifications, the badge, and reminders.
  • Open PRs only — Optionally hide closed / merged PRs.
  • @-mention notifications — Dedicated toggle (also controls whether mentions pull in out-of-scope PRs), a Let @-mentions through muted PRs toggle, mention-reminder toggle, and an aliases field for extra names that should also count as a mention.
  • Reminders — Independent toggles for the unread-comment reminder, the recurring review-request reminder, and the @-mention reminder, plus how often a dismissed reminder may repeat (5–240 min).
  • Notification actions per node kind — Three independent settings drive the secondary action on notifications and the tree double-click behavior: top-level comment, inline review comment, and PR / PR-status row (each: Open PR timeline / Open file / Open in browser, depending on node kind).
  • Notification sync mode — Disabled, inbound-only, or bidirectional sync with GitHub notifications.
  • Closed-project monitoring — Toggle, configurable polling interval (10–120 min; custom interval is a paid feature), and a per-project opt-out list of detected cached projects.
  • Storage limits — Max PRs to fetch, max stored comments, and retention period.

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2025.1 or later (Community or Ultimate).
  • Bundled GitHub and Git plugins must be enabled.
  • At least one GitHub account configured in Settings → Version Control → GitHub.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2.6.4

  • Fix: Closed projects no longer alert you about your own comments, or count the ones you edit as unread.
  • Fix: On closed projects, an approval or change request without a comment no longer also raises a new-comment alert.

2.6.3

  • Compatibility: Added support for IntelliJ IDEA 2026.3.
  • Improved: When PR comments can't be fetched, for example with no GitHub account in the IDE, the tool window says why instead of staying silently empty, and fetching starts as soon as you log in.
  • Improved: Folding or unfolding a section in the comment preview no longer redraws the whole comment or reloads its images.
  • Improved: Images in the comment preview are kept in memory, so returning to a comment shows them without downloading them again.

2.6.2

  • Fix: Closed projects no longer keep reminding you about unread comments on PRs that have since been merged or closed.
  • Fix: A reminder is taken down once nothing is left to remind about, instead of repeating an outdated count.
  • Fix: Alerts about a PR that has since been merged or closed are retired, so they no longer lead to a PR the tree hides.

2.6.1

  • New: Every PR Monitor notification is also listed in the Notifications panel of all other open windows, so you can find it and act on it from any project.
  • Fix: Closed-project alerts no longer vanish when they arrive while a dialog such as Settings is open.
  • Fix: A reminder that never made it on screen is shown again on the next check instead of waiting out the repeat interval.
  • Fix: A new-comment balloon that replaces a reminder now also lists what the reminder said, such as PRs still awaiting your review.
  • Improved: When many closed projects report at once, their reminders share a single balloon.

2.6.0

  • Fix: Review requests and other alerts from closed projects no longer vanish unseen in a burst of balloons — each closed project now gets one balloon per check, with review requests and mentions shown last.
  • Improved: Several alerts from the same check are merged into one balloon instead of one per kind.
  • Improved: Unread, review-request and @-mention reminders share one balloon per project, and one Snooze covers them all.
  • New: Reminders no longer re-appear on every poll: one still on screen stays put, and a dismissed one returns after the new Repeat reminders every N minutes setting (default 30), or right away when something new arrives.
  • Improved: Alerts are no longer copied into another window while you're looking at the project they come from.
  • Fix: The unread-comments reminder toggle now applies to monitored closed projects too.

2.5.7

  • Fix: Reminders no longer outlive the project they point at. Closing a project left its balloons on screen with every action — View PR, Snooze, Stop reminding me, Mute — silently doing nothing. Reminders mirrored into another project's window were worse: nothing about the origin project closing took them down. Opening a project likewise left its closed-project balloons up, still claiming (project not open).
  • Fix: Stop monitoring this project and Stop reminding me about this PR on closed-project balloons now offer Undo, like every other permanent action. Stop monitoring in particular sits directly under Open project and view comments and silences the project wholesale — a mis-click was recoverable only from the settings list, with nothing to cue you there.

2.5.6

  • New: Stop reminding me about this PR — on the review reminder balloon (when it names a single PR), in the tree right-click menu, and on monitored closed projects. Silences the recurring reminder for that one PR; unlike muting, nothing is hidden and every other PR keeps reminding you.
  • New: The choice clears itself once the request resolves — PR merged or closed, you approve, or the request is withdrawn — so a re-request reminds you again.
  • Improved: An Undo balloon follows the click, and the Review requested from you row shows [reminders off].
  • Improved: The tree submenu is now Review reminder (was Snooze review reminder), holding snooze, clear-snooze and the stop / resume toggle. The balloon's blanket action reads Mute all review reminders.

2.5.5

  • New: An @-mention now reaches you even on a muted PR. Muting used to be absolute — a colleague tagging you on a PR you had muted produced nothing at all, since its comments were never even fetched. Such a PR now reappears in the tree marked [muted], carrying only the comment that tagged you, fires the usual mention balloon, and counts toward the unread badge. Every other comment on it — and the Review requested from you row — stays hidden, so muting keeps its value.
  • New: A Let @-mentions through muted PRs setting under @-Mention Notifications controls the above. It is on by default and reverses the 2.5.1 note that muted PRs always stay hidden; turn it off to make muting absolute again.
  • Fix: The @-mention reminder no longer nags about a mention you cannot reach. Muting a PR after one of its comments had tagged you left the recurring reminder firing at a tree row that was filtered out — impossible to click away and impossible to dismiss.
  • Improved: Right-clicking a PR in the tree now offers Unmute this PR when it is already muted, instead of a one-way Mute this PR.
  • Improved: Mentions matched through the Additional aliases field now count everywhere the tree and counters look, not only where GitHub's own mention index reaches — that index knows nothing about your aliases.

2.5.4

  • Improved: Foldable <details> sections are far easier to open. The fold marker is now the IDE's own chevron instead of a small triangle drawn in link blue — which was hard to make out on dark themes — and the entire summary line is the click target, not just the marker. Clicks are no longer dropped when the mouse drifts a pixel between press and release, and the row shows a hand cursor so it reads as clickable. Links inside a summary still open in the browser, and dragging across a row still selects text.
  • Changed: PRs in the tree are ordered by PR creation date, newest first. Previously a PR jumped to the top whenever anyone commented on it, so the list reshuffled as discussion moved around. Open PRs still group above closed / merged ones.

2.5.3

  • Fix: Already-read comments no longer come back marked unread after a settings change — most visibly when switching between global and project-specific settings.
  • Fix: Read state survives the storage limits: a comment dropped by the max stored comments cap or the retention period stays read if a later fetch brings it back.
  • Fix: Reset cache and refetch is no longer silently undone when pressed during a fetch.

2.5.2

  • Fix: Markdown task lists (- [ ] / - [x]) no longer render as unreadable black text in the preview; checkboxes are now ☐ / ☑ glyphs.

2.5.1

  • New: Being @-mentioned now brings the PR to you. Previously a PR only appeared if you authored it or were a reviewer — so a colleague tagging you on someone else's PR produced nothing at all. An @-mention now pulls that PR into the tree on its own, overriding the PR-author and reviewer-scope filters.
  • New: @-mentions in the PR description are detected. Mention scanning previously covered comment bodies only, so being tagged in the pull request's own description went unnoticed. Such PRs now show a You were mentioned in the description row and fire the usual mention balloon.
  • Improved: The @-mention reminder and unread count now include description mentions, so a description-only ping keeps nagging until you read it.
  • Improved: Edited comments now show when they were edited — 3d ago (edited 5m ago) instead of a bare (edited) — so a comment that looks stale by its creation date no longer hides the fact it was just reworked. Shown in both the tree and the preview header.
  • Note: The two mention behaviors above follow the existing Notify when someone @-mentions me setting — turn it off and mentions no longer pull in out-of-scope PRs. Muting a PR still outranks a mention: muted PRs stay hidden.

2.5.0

  • Under the hood: This release completes a deep internal refactoring of the plugin's core — filtering, fetching, polling, notifications, and settings — now backed by an automated test suite. Existing behavior is preserved; the user-visible changes are the fixes below.
  • Fix: The unread count for monitored closed projects now matches the open-project badge exactly. Previously a PR awaiting your review whose comments were all filtered out still counted as unread on the closed-project side.
  • Fix: Per-project settings overrides are honored from the very first read after IDE start. Previously an early read could silently fall back to the app-level defaults until the license check completed.
  • Fix: The rate-limit throttle notification now respects per-project polling intervals — it fires as soon as throttling stretches polling beyond what any open project expects, instead of judging only by the app-level default.
  • Fix: On a fresh install's first fetch, an @-mention balloon no longer suppresses that cycle's unread-comments reminder.
  • Improved: Closed-project monitoring now applies exactly the same filtering and counting rules as open projects, including review-request lookups that page beyond the first 100 results.

2.4.5

  • Fix: Muting or unmuting a PR now hides or restores it in the tree immediately, instead of lingering until the next poll.
  • Fix: Toggling a display-only filter (ignore outdated / resolved, comment author / body) or snoozing / clearing a review-request reminder now updates the tree right away instead of waiting for the next fetch.

2.4.4

  • Improved: Multi-item digest and recurring reminder balloons now clear themselves (with their cross-project mirror) once every item they cover is read, instead of lingering until the next poll.
  • Fix: Inline code in the preview is readable again when the editor color scheme and UI theme differ in lightness.
  • Fix: HTML5 tags from bot comments (e.g. <ins> / <del>) no longer render as unreadable black text in the preview.

2.4.3

  • Fix: The preview pane no longer flickers or jumps back to the top on polls that find nothing new.
  • Fix: Editing a comment no longer leaves its foldable sections expanded in the wrong places.

2.4.2

  • New: Collapsible <details> sections in the preview. Comments that use GitHub's <details> / <summary> blocks (common in bot reports) now render as foldable sections with a triangle toggle you click to expand or collapse in place — matching how GitHub shows them, instead of flattening everything into one wall of text. Fold state is remembered per comment as you switch between comments.
  • New: PR description shown in the preview. Selecting a PR node now renders the pull request's description as markdown below the metadata header (previously only the one-line header appeared), reusing the same markdown pipeline as comment bodies. Scroll position and section fold state are remembered per PR.

2.4.1

  • Compatibility: Added support for IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2.
  • Improved: The comment preview pane now remembers your scroll position per comment — returning to a comment restores where you had scrolled to instead of jumping back to the top.

2.4.0

  • Fix: Acting on a single-comment notification (Open in browser / Open file / Open PR timeline) now marks top-level comments read, not just inline ones — matching the tree's behavior.
  • Fix: With Show only my review requests on, the tree no longer briefly shows unrelated PRs while the review-request set is still loading.

2.3.9

  • Improved: Selecting an item in the tree now dismisses its own notification balloon. When a balloon arrives while the tool window is already open, clicking the comment (or review-request row) it points at hides that balloon — and its mirrored copy in another project's window — so reviewing an item clears its own alert. Unrelated balloons and multi-item digests stay up.

2.3.8

  • Changed: The user-facing name is now PR Monitor (was PR Comments) — across the tool window and notification titles — to better reflect that it tracks reviews, review requests, and approval status, not just comments.
  • Fix: Polling no longer stalls after a GitHub authentication hiccup. A transient 401/403 could leave polling paused indefinitely — surviving IDE restarts and only clearing on a manual Refresh. The plugin now re-probes after the backoff window, clears the pause on the first success, and discards a stale pause on startup.

2.3.7

  • Fix: An edited-comment notification's View comment action now marks the comment read even when it's already the selected row in the tree (previously it stayed unread until you clicked away and back).

2.3.6

  • Improved: Muting a recurring reminder now offers an Undo. The Mute unread reminders / Mute review reminders / Mute mention reminders actions are permanent and one stray click silently switched the reminder off. Each now fires a brief, auto-fading balloon with a one-click Undo right after you click it — Undo both re-enables the reminder and brings the just-dismissed reminder balloon back immediately, rather than waiting for the next poll. The balloon also names Settings → GitHub PRs Monitor as the place to re-enable the reminder after it fades. The undo balloon appears in whichever window you clicked — including a mirrored reminder shown in another project's window.

2.3.5

  • Fix: Open in browser from a top-level comment notification now scrolls to the comment. The notification action was opening the bare PR page instead of the comment anchor — only inline review comments carried their own URL through, so top-level comments fell back to the PR URL. Both kinds now open their own #issuecomment- / #discussion_ anchor, matching the tree's right-click Open in browser behavior.

2.3.4

  • Fix: Cross-project mirror notifications now reach the IDE window you're actually looking at. Mirroring was previously gated on the platform's "last-focused IDE frame" pointer — a single slot that gets clobbered by the source project's own focus history. Once you'd glanced at the source window (or focus had left the IDE entirely), no peer was selected and the mirror was silently skipped, even with other project windows wide open in the same IDE instance. The plugin now scans every open project frame and picks a peer that's currently visible (showing and not minimized), independent of where keyboard focus lives.

2.3.3

  • Fix: Checkout and Open now works for PRs from forks. The branch-mismatch dialog previously did nothing on fork PRs (it only fetched origin). The plugin now adds the fork as a remote, fetches the head branch, and checks out a local fork/<owner>/<branch> tracking branch.
  • Fix: Loosening a filter resurfaces previously-hidden comments. Toggling Show as filtered on, relaxing a regex, or switching Blacklist → Disabled on the comment author / body filters now correctly brings dropped comments back into the tree. Author and body filters now run only at display time; storage always holds the full fetched set.

2.3.2

  • Improved: Recurring reminders are now kept in the IDE notification log. The unread-comments, @-mention, and review-request reminders are now logged to the bell-icon panel (previously they were balloon-only and disappeared from history after dismissal), but only the latest reminder of each kind per project is retained — each new reminder expires its predecessor in the log automatically, so the panel doesn't pile up.

2.3.1

  • Improved: Notifications stick until you act on them. The @-mention, review-request, and approval-status balloons, plus all three recurring reminders (unread comments / @-mentions / review requests), no longer fade out after ~10 seconds — they stay visible until you click an action (View / Snooze / Mute / Open project) or the platform's 5-minute hard fallback fires. The high-frequency new- and edited-comment balloons keep their short fadeout to avoid stacking during active review. You can override the display type per group under Settings → Appearance & Behavior → Notifications.
  • Improved: Opening the PR Comments tool window auto-dismisses outstanding balloons for that project. When you open the tree view, every still-visible balloon for the same project — new / edited comment, @-mention, review request, approval status, and any active reminder, including mirrors fired into another focused project, and closed-project balloons (e.g. the "project not open" reminder) that pointed at this project — is hidden automatically. Entries remain in the IDE notification log so you can scroll back through history; only the on-screen balloons go away.

2.3.0

  • New: Snooze every recurring reminder. The unread-comments reminder, the @-mention reminder, and the review-request reminder (single or multi-PR) now offer Snooze 1 hour and Snooze until tomorrow 09:00 actions on the balloon, alongside the existing mute / view / open-project actions. Multi-PR review reminders bulk-snooze every PR currently in the reminder, so the same buttons work whether one or many PRs are awaiting review. Snoozes persist across IDE restarts and across the open ⇄ closed-project boundary, and the same snooze written from a closed-project balloon is honored once the project is reopened.
  • Improved: Reminder action labels are scope-specific. The single Don't show again button on each recurring reminder is now Mute unread reminders / Mute review reminders / Mute mention reminders, so it's clear which reminder kind you're permanently disabling vs. snoozing.
  • Improved: Polling cycle runs per-PR fetches in parallel. Each poll cycle now fetches up to 8 PRs concurrently instead of walking them sequentially. Refresh and the periodic poll complete dramatically faster on repositories with many open PRs; the toolbar progress line shows Fetched N/M PRs as the parallel fan-out completes. Closed-project polling is parallelized the same way.

2.2.2

  • New: Polling status in the tool window toolbar. A dimmed status line in the PR Comments toolbar shows when the open and closed-project pollers last fetched and when each one's next poll fires (e.g. Open: 34s ago · next 4m · Closed: 12m ago · next 18m). The "last fetched" stamp advances only on successful polls so stale data surfaces as stale; hover the line for absolute timestamps. The Closed segment hides automatically when closed-project monitoring is off.
  • Improved: Manual Refresh also polls closed projects. Clicking the Refresh button now kicks an immediate closed-project poll right after the open-project fetch completes — previously only the configured interval drove closed-project polling.
  • Improved: Closed-project polling visible in the IDE background-tasks tray. Each closed-project poll cycle is now an app-level Polling closed PR projects task, visible from every open IDE window's background-tasks indicator (bottom-right) with per-project text and a progress bar over the eligible projects.

2.2.1

  • Improved: Settings page reorganized into tabs. The single long-scrolling settings page now opens onto three tabs — General (polling, pull requests, unread reminder, PR-status reminders, @-mention notifications), Filters (open-only, PR-author / PR-reviewer / comment-author / comment-content / inline-comment filters), and Advanced (tree double-click behavior, closed-project monitoring, GitHub notification sync, storage, maintenance). The project-override toggle is pinned above the tabs since it scopes every setting on the form. The previous Display group is split into Unread Comments and PR Status and Reviews; the three double-click action combos move to a new Tree Behavior group on the Advanced tab. Pure UX change — no persistence-format changes, existing settings carry over as-is.

2.2.0

  • New: @-mention notifications and reminder. A dedicated balloon fires whenever a comment body literally @-mentions your GitHub login, and a separate periodic reminder ticks while any unread mention is sitting in the tool window. Both are independent of the existing new-comment / unread-comment paths and bypass every locally-evaluated filter — muted PRs, PR-author / reviewer scope, open-only, comment-author and body-regex filters, and the outdated / resolved toggles — so a direct ping always surfaces. Mention-tagged comments also bypass the fetch-time author/body filter, so they still land in storage and the tree even from authors you'd otherwise block. New Additional aliases field lets colleagues ping you by a nickname or shortened login. Mirrored for monitored closed projects. Configure under Settings → Tools → GitHub PRs Monitor → @-Mention Notifications.

2.1.3

  • Improved: Compatibility cleanup for the JetBrains Marketplace plugin verifier — removed all flagged Problems against IDEs 2025.1 and 2026.1.

2.1.2

  • Changed: The recurring review-request reminder is no longer suppressed merely because the PR Comments tool window is docked — only when it currently holds keyboard focus. The synthetic Review requested from you row is easy to miss in a long tree, so the balloon now fires whenever you're working in another tool window or in the editor.

2.1.1

  • New: Per-PR snooze for the review-request reminder. Two fixed durations — 1 hour and Until tomorrow 09:00 — surfaced from the reminder balloon (single-PR case only) and from a new Snooze review reminder submenu in the tree right-click on PR nodes and on the Review requested from you row. Active snoozes show as (snoozed until HH:mm) on the lifecycle row and persist across IDE restarts. Clear snooze entry appears when one is active. Independent of the global "Don't show again" button and of the Mute this PR action: snooze suppresses only the recurring review reminder, not comments / badge / lifecycle popup.

2.1.0

  • New: Recurring review-request reminder. A new on-by-default reminder fires after each poll cycle whenever any open PR matching your filters still has a review requested from you, even when all comments on those PRs have been read. Independent of the existing unread-comment reminder and of the one-shot lifecycle Review requested balloon. Suppressed for the cycle on which the lifecycle balloon already fired (no double-pinging on transitions) and for the origin project when the PR Comments tool window is visible. Toggle under Settings → Tools → GitHub PRs Monitor → Display → Remind me about open review requests on each poll. Mirrored for monitored closed projects.

2.0.2

  • Changed: Approval-status notifications are no longer fired for your own approvals or change-requested reviews. When you click Approve or Request changes on a teammate's PR, the plugin no longer pops a balloon for the resulting state transition (matching the existing behavior for your own comments). Transitions caused by other reviewers still notify as before.

2.0.1

  • New: Active polling for closed projects. The closed-project reminder shipped in 2.0.0 was read-only (counts unread from the local cache). 2.0.1 turns it into a real background poller: when Monitor unread comments in closed projects is on (default), the plugin now polls cached projects you're not currently working in on its own cycle and fires the same notifications open projects get — new comments, edited comments, review requests, approval status, and unread reminders. Configurable polling interval (10–120 min, default 30; custom interval is a paid feature) under Settings → Tools → GitHub PRs Monitor → Monitor Closed Projects.
  • Changed: The cached-projects list in settings now shows every detected project, including currently-open ones (labeled (currently open)) and projects whose cache was written before the new fields were persisted (labeled ⚠ reopen to start monitoring). Default behavior is opt-out — every detected closed project is monitored unless you untick it. Unticking a row persists the path on Apply, and the Apply button now correctly enables when you change a checkbox in the list.

2.0.0

  • New: Reminders for closed projects. When you have unread PR comments in a project that's not currently open, the plugin now surfaces a balloon at the end of every poll cycle of any open project. The balloon names the closed project and its unread count, and offers an Open project and view comments action that reopens the project and jumps straight to the PR Comments tool window. Configurable under Settings → Tools → GitHub PRs Monitor → Reminders For Closed Projects: a global on/off toggle plus a per-project mute list of cached projects. Closed-project counts apply the same filter chain as the open-project unread badge (PR author / reviewer, comment author, comment body, outdated, resolved), so the number matches what the project would show on reopen.

1.9.0

  • Changed: Notifications now lead with the PR Comments tool window. The primary action on every balloon (new / edited comments, review requests, approval status, and the unread reminder) opens the tool window and selects the matching node — comment, lifecycle row, or PR. A single secondary action — Open file / Open PR timeline or Open in browser, driven by the new per-node-kind double-click setting — replaces the old pair of secondary buttons.
  • New: Per-node-kind double-click setting. The single Double-click action dropdown is split into three under Settings → Tools → GitHub PRs Monitor: Top-level comment double-click (Open PR timeline / Open in browser), Inline review comment double-click (Open file / Open in browser), and PR / PR status double-click (Open PR timeline / Open in browser). The same choice drives the secondary action on the matching notification. Existing Double-click action values migrate automatically on first load.
  • Improved: Open PR timeline now scrolls the matched comment to the top of the bundled GitHub plugin's PR view, instead of leaving it near the bottom of the viewport with unrelated context above.
  • Improved: Tree right-click on PR rows, lifecycle items, and top-level comments now offers Open PR timeline in place of the previously-missing Open file entry. Double-click on PR / lifecycle nodes honors the new setting, so the "← double-click" hint matches the actual behavior.
  • Fix: Comments written in GitHub's ><summary> / ><br/> blockquote style (Qodo and similar bots) no longer drop the leading < in the preview pane. Inline HTML inside a > blockquote now parses correctly.

1.8.0

  • New: Markdown comment preview — comment bodies are now rendered through the bundled GitHub plugin's markdown pipeline, so bold, fenced code blocks, lists, tables, and other GitHub-flavored markdown render the same way they do in IntelliJ's own PR view. Previously the raw markdown syntax leaked through into the preview pane.
  • Fix: The "Review requested from you" tree row no longer disappears the moment you approve the PR. GitHub strips you from requested_reviewers on approval, but the row now stays visible (and auto-marks itself read) so you can see that you've handled the request.
  • Fix: Tree rows no longer show a hardcoded grey tile under third-party themes (or after a theme switch mid-session). The renderer is now transparent and lets the tree paint its own row background and selection.

1.7.0

  • New: Updates without IDE restart — the plugin can now be installed, updated, or uninstalled while the IDE is running. No more "restart required" prompt on every release.
  • New: Outdated and resolved inline comment filters — inline review comments are now tagged (outdated) when they sit on lines that no longer exist in the PR head, and (resolved) when their thread is marked resolved on GitHub. Two new toggles under Inline Comment Filters (Ignore outdated comments / Ignore resolved comments) hide them from the tree, the unread badge, and notifications. Status is refreshed every poll via GraphQL, so the badges stay accurate even when the filters are off.
  • New: "Filtered items" toolbar dropdown — the comment-level "show filtered greyed instead of hiding" toggles moved out of Settings into a dropdown next to the tree, so you can flip between hiding and greying filtered comments without opening Settings → Apply. Covers Comment Author, Comment Content, Outdated, and Resolved filters; each toggle is greyed out when its parent filter is off.
  • Fix: Inline review comments no longer pick up a spurious "(edited)" label on first sight or after edits that didn't actually change the body.

1.6.0

  • New: Comment Content Filter — a Whitelist / Blacklist regex filter on comment body text, with a multi-line input where each non-empty line is its own regex (matches if any line matches). Patterns are case-insensitive and span newlines, so they work on multi-line markdown bodies. The filter applies uniformly to the tree, the unread badge, the unread reminder, and notifications; blacklisted comments are also dropped at fetch time.
  • New: "Show as filtered" mode — each of the four filters (PR Author, PR Reviewer, Comment Author, Comment Content) gets an opt-in toggle to keep filtered items visible in the tree (with strikethrough and dim foreground) instead of hiding them. Items shown this way still stay out of notifications, the unread badge, the unread reminder, and per-PR / per-file unread counts.
  • New: First-fetch lifecycle notifications — on the very first fetch after installing the plugin, you now get balloon notifications for currently-outstanding review requests and approval-status changes, instead of those being silently absorbed. Subsequent IDE restarts stay silent.
  • Fix: Duplicate comment entries no longer accumulate in the persisted storage on each poll. Existing storages with already-duplicated entries self-heal after one save / reload cycle.

1.5.0

  • New: Glob wildcards in PR Author and Comment Author filter lists — entries can now use * and ? (e.g. *[bot] matches every bot login). Plain entries keep exact-match semantics, so existing settings are unaffected.
  • New: Draft PRs are rendered with the GitHub draft icon and a [draft] tag in the tree. PR creation time now appears alongside the author in tree and preview rows.
  • Improved: Checkout and Open on the branch-mismatch dialog now runs a background git fetch first, so brand-new and stale-tracking PR branches resolve correctly before checkout.
  • Improved: The toolbar refresh spinner is visible the moment the tool window opens during a poll already in flight, instead of only appearing on the next poll cycle.
  • Changed: Double-click on the comments tree no longer toggles row expand/collapse — it now only triggers the configured Open file / Open on GitHub action. Use the arrow handles or keyboard to expand rows.
  • Fix: PRs you authored or have already reviewed (including via inline comments) are no longer flagged as "Review requested from you".

1.4.1

  • Fix: Approval-status and review-request notifications no longer re-fire on every poll.
  • New: Incoming review requests now appear as a dedicated "Review requested from you" item under the PR node in the tree, and can be marked read like any other comment.
  • Improved: Notification balloon icons now match the corresponding tree-cell icons for review comments, review bodies, review requests, and approval-status changes.

1.4.0

  • Changed: The plugin is renamed to GitHub PRs Monitor to reflect its broader scope — it now tracks review requests, approval status, and review bodies in addition to inline review comments.
  • New: Review request notifications — a balloon and a dedicated tree indicator on the PR node when the authenticated user is requested as a reviewer.
  • New: Approval-status notifications — balloons and tree indicators when any reviewer submits APPROVED or CHANGES_REQUESTED, even when the review body is empty.
  • New: Review bodies — top-level review messages (e.g. "LGTM") from APPROVED / CHANGES_REQUESTED / COMMENTED reviews are fetched from /pulls/*/reviews and rendered alongside inline comments with per-state icons in the tree. Historical review backfill is treated as already-read to avoid re-notifying upgraded users.
  • New: Reset Cache button in settings to recover from fetch/merge regressions.
  • Improved: PR state changes (open → closed / merged / reopen) now propagate to the tree even for quiet PRs; disappeared tracked PRs are resolved via a single /pulls/{n} call to distinguish merged vs. closed.
  • Improved: With Show only unread active, marking read/unread now re-applies filters through a coalesced rebuild and keeps the currently-selected comment visible, so it vanishes only after you move past it.

1.3.0

  • New: Per-project settings — settings are now per-project, with an app-level template inherited by new projects. A Use settings specific to this project toggle lets you override the defaults for the current project, and a Save current as default for new projects button promotes the current project's settings back to the app-level template. (Paid feature — requires an active license; the override is ignored when unlicensed.)
  • New: GitHub rate-limit and auth-failure handling — the plugin now watches X-RateLimit headers and proactively stretches the polling interval before GitHub starts rejecting requests. Hard rate limits pause polling until the reset time (persisted across IDE restarts); auth failures (401 / 403) trigger a short pause that auto-clears on the next successful response. One-shot balloon notifications surface each state with Refresh, Retry, and Open Settings actions. Manual refresh always overrides any active pause.
  • New: Cross-project notification mirroring — when a new/edited comment or unread reminder fires for a background project while a different project has IDE focus, the balloon is also mirrored into the focused frame (labeled with the origin project name). Actions on either balloon operate on the originating project and dismiss both.

1.2.1

  • Changed: PR Author Filter → My PRs only and PR Reviewer Filter → Show only PRs where I'm a reviewer are no longer mutually exclusive. When both are enabled, they combine as OR — PRs you authored or where you're a reviewer. With Whitelist / Blacklist they still combine as AND.
  • Changed: New installs now default to My PRs only + Show only PRs where I'm a reviewer (the common "PRs I own or that need my review" workflow). Existing users keep their saved settings.

1.2.0

  • New: PR Reviewer Filter — show only PRs where you're requested as a reviewer or have already submitted a review. Mutually exclusive with PR Author Filter → My PRs only.
  • New: Optional Include teams (user is part of) review requests sub-toggle — match PRs requesting a team you belong to, not only direct user requests.
  • Improved: Author-list text fields in PR Author Filter and Comment Author Filter are grayed out when the mode doesn't use them.
  • Improved: Historical comments for newly-seen open PRs are now backfilled from the retention window on first sight, instead of starting from "now" and showing an empty PR.
  • Improved: Clearer settings labels — "Max PRs to monitor" (the cap applies to all monitored PRs, not only open ones) and "Comments author" tooltip on the toolbar author dropdown.
  • Fix: Settings changes now reliably trigger a fresh fetch even when a poll was already in flight (previously the re-fetch could be silently dropped until the next scheduled poll).

1.1.0

  • New: Separate notifications for new comments and edited comments so you can tell them apart at a glance.
  • New: On the very first fetch after installing the plugin, all loaded comments are announced as new — even if they were edited on GitHub beforehand.
  • Improved: The View comments notification action now opens the tool window and selects the first comment from the notification, scrolling it into view.
  • Improved: The Open file notification action now refreshes the bundled GitHub plugin's PR data (so inline review markers update immediately) and prompts to check out the PR branch on mismatch — matching the tool window behavior.
  • Fix: Edited comments now correctly appear as unread in the tool window tree; previously they could stay styled as read while the unread badge was showing.

1.0.2

  • Fix: Checking out a PR branch that exists only on a remote no longer leaves the repository in a detached HEAD state — a local tracking branch is created instead.

1.0.1

  • Fix: Edited comments no longer trigger repeated notifications after being marked as read.

1.0.0

  • Automatic polling — Continuously fetches comments from all open PRs via the GitHub API.
  • Desktop notifications — Balloon alerts for new and edited comments with quick actions: jump to file, view in tool window, or open on GitHub.
  • Unread reminders — Optional periodic reminders when unread comments are waiting.
  • Edit detection — Edited comments are marked unread and flagged "(edited)".
  • Read / unread tracking — Per-comment read state with a dynamic badge on the tool window icon.
  • GitHub notification sync — Sync read state with GitHub Notifications API (inbound or bidirectional).
  • Tree view — Comments organized by PR → file → individual comments and replies.
  • HTML comment preview — Rendered preview pane with resizable splitter.
  • One-click code navigation — Jump to the exact file and line; branch mismatch detection with checkout prompt.
  • PR author filter — Show all, only yours, or whitelist / blacklist specific authors.
  • Comment author filter — Whitelist or blacklist comment authors.
  • Per-PR muting — Mute noisy PRs from the context menu; unmute anytime.
  • Configurable double-click — Open file in editor or open on GitHub.
  • Extensive settings — Polling interval, storage limits, retention period, notification sync mode, and more.

idea-plugin.name: IDEGram
idea-plugin.description: Telegram client integrated into your JetBrains IDE. Chat, share code snippets, and collaborate without leaving your editor.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2.1.1 - 2026-06-29

Added

  • Run / build / test finish ping. When an execution takes longer than a configurable threshold (default 1 minute), IDEGram sends a short Telegram message on completion, e.g. ✅ [my-project] :app:assembleDebug succeeded · 3m 12s or ❌ [my-project] MyServiceTest failed · 48s · 24 tests, 3 failed. Covers Run configurations, tests (with counts), and project builds (IntelliJ Make / Gradle).
  • Per-run override. A Run-menu toggle, "Ping Me on Telegram When Finished", force-pings a specific run even if it's shorter than the threshold.
  • Choose the sending account. With multiple accounts, pick which one delivers the ping (defaults to the active account); it's sent to that account's Saved Messages.
  • Settings under ⚙ → Run-finish ping (and Settings/Preferences → IDEGram): enable/disable, duration threshold presets (5s · 10s · 30s · 1m · 5m), and the sending-account selector.

Changed

  • The in-tool-window Settings screen gained a prominent "← Back to chats" button at the top (the old one was easy to miss).

Fixed

  • Stopped reading the plugin version through an IntelliJ Platform internal API (flagged by JetBrains Marketplace review); the version is now embedded at build time. No user-visible change.

Privacy

  • Finish-ping messages contain only the project name, run name, status, duration, and test counts — never console output, source code, stack traces, or file paths. They are sent only to your own Saved Messages (or a chat you choose), via Telegram.

idea-plugin.name: Easely
idea-plugin.description:
Critical thinking made visual. Easely supercharges your workflow so you can stay organized and get into the flow.

It’s hard to stay organized when feeling lost in an ever-growing sea of changes. With structure and organization to your critical thinking, you'll get to express, see, and review your thought process in visual form: a graph.

I have found this workflow to be incredibly useful at achieving flow state in my workflow, resulting in greater enjoyment of my craft. I know you will too!

Usage

These keybinds are the starting defaults, but you may change them at any time in the IDE's keymap settings.

Open Easely's tool window:

CTRL + ;Windows/Linux
CONTROL + ;Mac

Navigate with the left hand:

Eup
Ddown
Sleft
Fright
Whighest parent
Xlowest parent
Rhighest child
Vlowest child

Move children in their sibling groups:

SHIFT + Emove node up
SHIFT + Dmove node down

Manage structure with the right hand:

Inew node above
Knew node below
Jnew parent
Lnew child

Manage each node's state:

ENTERinteract with the selected node (i.e. save edits, assigning relationships, etc)
ESCAPEleave mode (back to navigating)
SPACEmark as complete (including children) / mark as in progress (including parents)

Manage additional relationships:

Uadd/remove parents from current node
Oadd/remove children from the current node

Support and Feedback

We want to hear from you! We invite your feedback and requests for support! We invite you to contact us at alex@amplifyhuman.ca.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Attempting to delete no longer results in an exception

idea-plugin.name: JourneyKMP Graph
idea-plugin.description:
Visualizes @Journey-annotated sealed interfaces from JourneyKMP as interactive directed graphs.

Features:
  • Auto-detects all @Journey flows in your project
  • Interactive canvas with draggable nodes
  • Horizontal and vertical layout modes
  • Zoom in/out, fit to view, reset zoom
  • Piggyback tag visualization (ON_ENTER / ON_EXIT)
  • Export as Mermaid diagram or PNG
  • Light and dark theme support
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.2 - 2026-06-02

Added

  • Android Studio (Meerkat) compatibility via pluginVerification
  • Automated verifyPlugin CI check on every push and PR
  • since-build declared as 232 (IntelliJ 2023.2 minimum)
  • Journeys list in the dropdown is now sorted lexicographically
  • README with demo video, icon, features, and usage guide

Changed

  • Renamed plugin, project, and directory from JourneyKMPVisualizer to JourneyKMPGraph
  • Replaced JComboBox with ComboBox, JScrollPane with JBScrollPane, and Insets with JBUI.insets for better IDE integration
  • PSI scanner now uses targeted try-catch that correctly rethrows ProcessCanceledException
  • Annotations per step parsed once and reused for both node building and edge extraction
  • Tool window icon now loaded via IconLoader so dark variant switches correctly with IDE theme

Fixed

  • Resolved redundant runCatching layers in PSI scanner and window refresh
  • Fixed BufferedImage usage replaced with UIUtil.createImage() for HiDPI support
  • Suppressed incorrect UseJBColor warnings for canvas-theme-driven colors

idea-plugin.name: DB Blueprint
idea-plugin.description:
Visual database schema (ERD) designer for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, and Microsoft SQL Server (preview) — model schemas on a canvas, import from live databases, and apply incremental migrations.

Note: Microsoft SQL Server (MSSQL) is experimental (preview) and not production-ready yet. You can connect, import, and use Preview to try it out, but the data safety checks and migration coverage that PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, and SQLite already have are still in progress. Avoid Apply migration and Export to DB on an MSSQL database you care about — use a disposable or staging database and keep a backup. Full MSSQL support is planned for a later release.

  • Canvas — edit tables inline (PK, NOT NULL, UNIQUE), drag column handles to create relationships, minimap and zoom
  • Schema panel — tree of tables and columns with FK / REF badges and cardinality (1:1, 1:N, N:M)
  • Living schema (baseline + migration diff) — capture baseline, preview migration SQL, apply incremental changes; export to an empty database is blocked when tables already exist
  • Import from DB — reverse-engineer schema from PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, or Microsoft SQL Server
  • Preview DDL — inspect generated CREATE / ALTER statements before execution
  • Save / Open — store the canvas as a .dbdesign JSON file in your project

JDBC drivers are not bundled; use Detect/Download in settings or a driver already installed by your IDE. Applying plugin updates requires an IDE restart. Connection settings stay in the project; passwords use IntelliJ Password Safe.

Documentation

Report issues & feedback
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.6
  • Connection status is now explicit. An empty connection line means there is no active session: Import from DB, Export to DB, and Apply migration need a connection in Settings → Tools → DB Blueprint → Test connection first. The plugin no longer connects silently to the last profile.
  • Safer migrations across PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, and SQLite. Before Apply, the plugin now blocks the plan with a clear message — instead of a raw database error — when a new foreign key points to rows whose parent is missing, when a column is made required (NOT NULL) but still has empty values, or when UNIQUE is added where duplicates exist.
  • SQLite now runs the same data safety checks before Apply that the other databases already had.
  • MySQL / MariaDB: extra checks catch common problems in Preview, such as an index that is too long or a foreign key whose columns do not match. The Apply warning explains exactly what happens if a step fails (each step is applied on its own; earlier steps stay applied), and the connection line shows a note for older server versions with weaker safety guarantees.
  • Preview windows for DDL and migration can be resized by dragging, and each has a Copy button for the SQL.
  • Migration is now one flow: open Preview & apply migration and apply from the same window (with Cancel and Apply migration side by side) after reviewing the SQL.
  • PostgreSQL: optional Online migration in the migration preview adds new foreign keys without a long write-blocking lock (validated in a separate step after the change commits) — useful on large production tables.
  • Microsoft SQL Server (MSSQL) is experimental (preview) and not production-ready yet. You can connect, Import, and use Preview to try it out, but the data safety checks and migration coverage that PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, and SQLite already have are still in progress. Avoid Apply migration and Export to DB on an MSSQL database you care about — use a disposable or staging database and keep a backup. Full MSSQL support is planned for a later release.
0.1.5
  • MySQL and MariaDB: JDBC import, canvas editing, migration preview against a baseline, and Apply to an existing database. Pre-flight checks run before DDL is executed.
  • Indexes are imported and editable on the canvas — BTREE, FULLTEXT, and SPATIAL, including prefix indexes. Use + IX on a column to add or adjust indexes without leaving the table card.
  • Migration preview includes column renames, type changes, NOT NULL and UNIQUE updates, foreign-key actions, and index changes — not only new tables and columns. Changes are grouped by risk; column modifications are highlighted as destructive so you can review SQL before Apply.
  • Pre-flight checks before Apply warn or block when existing data would break the plan (for example NULL values before NOT NULL, or duplicates before UNIQUE).
  • Column and index dropdowns follow the JDBC dialect; the connection line shows profile, dialect, and database. Incompatible types from another dialect are flagged in the toolbar — remap or remove before Preview migration.
  • MySQL and MariaDB Apply: confirmation dialog when DDL cannot be rolled back mid-run; failure messages state which steps may already be committed.
  • Connection line format: profile name, dialect, database.
0.1.4
  • PostgreSQL: JDBC import, canvas editing, migration preview against a baseline, and Apply to an existing database. Pre-flight checks; failed Apply rolls back in one transaction.
  • Indexes (including partial indexes) are imported from PostgreSQL and shown on table cards and in the schema panel so the canvas matches what is already in the database.
  • Migration preview groups changes by risk, runs pre-flight checks (for example existing NULL values before NOT NULL), and asks for confirmation before destructive steps such as dropping columns or tables.
  • Column renames, type changes, foreign-key actions, and index updates are included in the migration diff — not only adding new tables and columns.
  • Schema sidebar: collapse it to icons, hover a table to highlight it on the canvas (and vice versa), click an icon when collapsed to expand the panel.
  • The toolbar dialect badge reflects your JDBC profile in Settings — change dialect there, not on the canvas.
0.1.3
  • SQLite: import a .db file, edit on the canvas, preview and apply incremental migrations against a baseline, or export to an empty file.
  • Connection setup for SQLite is clearer — use an absolute path to your database file, test the connection, and the plugin remembers the profile for Import and the connection badge.
  • Indexes (including partial indexes) are shown on table cards and in the schema panel so you can see what is already in the database.
  • Migration preview warns about SQLite-specific limits and asks for confirmation before changes that recreate tables (for example renaming or removing columns, or changing foreign keys).
  • When you switch the canvas dialect to SQLite, incompatible index types from other databases are flagged so you can fix the design before export.
0.1.2
  • Microsoft SQL Server: Preview and Apply migration now work after you capture a baseline (for example when adding new tables on the canvas).
0.1.1
  • Initial Marketplace release
  • Visual schema canvas with Schema sidebar and relationship editing
  • JDBC import, DDL preview, living-schema migration, and export to empty databases
  • Dialects: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, Microsoft SQL Server
