idea-plugin.name: Stack Doctor
idea-plugin.description:
Stack Doctor — Docker Compose service map & network doctor

Turns your docker-compose files into a visual service dependency map, lets you edit services right from the map, and runs a set of "doctor" checks for the networking mistakes that waste hours:

  • Service dependency graph (depends_on / shared networks)
  • Ports published to 127.0.0.1 that won't be reachable from other devices
  • Missing healthchecks on services other containers depend on
  • Suspicious / non-existent host volume paths
  • depends_on pointing at services that don't exist, and dependency cycles
  • Missing env_file references, and host-port conflicts between services
  • Ports that are exposed internally vs actually published

Getting started

  1. Install & open a project. Stack Doctor works in any JetBrains IDE (IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, Rider, and more). Open a project that contains at least one Compose file — anything named like docker-compose.yml, compose.yaml, or a *.yml/*.yaml file with compose in its name. They're discovered automatically; there's nothing to configure.
  2. Open the tool window. Go to View | Tool Windows | Stack Doctor (it docks on the right). You'll see every Compose file as a root node, with its services branching to the right and depends_on arrows showing what starts before what. Drag any node to rearrange the map (the arrows follow); Reset layout restores the automatic arrangement.
  3. Read the diagnosis. Findings are listed below the map and highlighted inline in the YAML editor. Nodes tint amber or red when a service — or a whole file — has warnings or errors, so problem areas stand out at a glance. Click the Warnings & errors header to collapse the list when you want more map.
  4. Edit a service. Click a service node to open an editable form for its parameters — image, ports, expose, depends_on, volumes, networks, env files, environment, healthcheck and restart policy — and Save writes the changes straight back into the compose file in one undoable step. Use Add field to add a parameter the service doesn't have yet. Click a file node for its service roster; double-click either to jump to it in the editor. Not sure what a symbol, line or colour means? Hit Legend.
  5. Preview a merge. Split your config across a base and an override (docker-compose.override.yml, a *.prod.yml, etc.)? Click Merged preview, pick the two files, and see the effective configuration Docker would actually run — with the doctor checks re-run on the merged result and the values the overlay contributed highlighted.
  6. Fix it. Apply the inline quick-fixes on highlighted YAML (bind a port to all interfaces, declare a missing volume or network, and more), or click Add healthchecks to generate context-aware healthchecks for the services that need one.

Press the Refresh button in the tool window anytime to re-scan the project and re-run every check.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.3.5

  • Reachability diagnostics. Stack Doctor now traces how each service is actually reachable — which ports are published to the host, which are only reachable from inside the Compose network, and which depend on services that never expose a port — and reports the dead ends. Click a service to see its reachability breakdown in the popup.
  • Better environment tracking. Improved parsing of environment and env_file values so checks that rely on them are more accurate.
  • Volume persistence at a glance. The map now distinguishes named volumes that persist data from throwaway bind mounts and anonymous volumes, with a new legend entry explaining the difference.
  • New dark-theme variant of the tool-window icon so it sits correctly in dark IDE themes.

0.3.0

  • Merged preview. A new Merged preview button combines any two compose files into one — pick a base (defaults to docker-compose.yml) and an overlay (e.g. docker-compose.override.yml) and see the effective configuration Docker would run, with the doctor checks re-run on the merged result and overlay-contributed values highlighted.
  • Collapsible warnings & errors. The diagnostics list at the bottom now has a header you can click to collapse it out of the way and expand it again.
  • Draggable nodes. Drag service and file nodes to rearrange the map; the dependency arrows follow, and your layout is kept until you press Reset layout (or restart the IDE).
  • Add fields from the service form. The edit form now has an Add field button to add parameters a service doesn't have yet — healthcheck, restart policy, expose, and more — then fill them in and Save. Long field hints now wrap instead of being clipped at the popup edge.

0.2.1

  • The service edit form now includes an editable Healthcheck field, so a generated healthcheck can be tweaked in place.
  • Fixed edit-form fields being clipped on the right edge — they now fit the popup and resize with it.

0.2.0

  • Edit services right from the map. Click a service node to open an editable form for its parameters — image, ports, expose, depends_on, volumes, networks, env files, environment and restart — and Save writes the changes straight back into the compose file in one undoable step.
  • The map legend now describes what each service category is for, instead of repeating the same note.
  • Updated for the latest JetBrains IDEs; now supports 2025.3 and newer.

0.1.1

  • New plugin logo and tool-window icon.
  • Fixed the map background flashing over a custom IDE background image — the map now overlays the IDE background directly instead of painting a solid fill behind the nodes.
  • Added a "Getting started" guide to the plugin description.

0.1.0

  • Initial release: whole-project Compose service map with dependency layout.
  • Ten networking "doctor" checks, surfaced inline and in the tool window.
  • Context-aware healthcheck generation (bulk, per-service, and as a quick-fix).
  • Map colours now follow the active IDE theme.

idea-plugin.name: Laughing Cat Sound
idea-plugin.description:
Something in your code just broke? A cat is already laughing at you.

This plugin plays a laughing cat sound the moment an error appears in your IDE, so a failed run never slips by unnoticed — with a bit of humor to soften the blow.

It reacts when:
  • a test fails,
  • an application exits with an error (exit code 1 — e.g. a failed startup or an uncaught exception), or
  • a run is aborted by a compilation error.
It stays silent when a process ends normally or when you stop the run yourself.

You can adjust the volume, mute it, or preview the sound in Settings/Preferences | Tools | Laughing Cat Sound.

한국어
방금 코드가 터졌나요? 고양이가 벌써 웃고 있습니다.

IDE에서 에러가 발생하는 순간 웃는 고양이 소리를 재생합니다. 실패한 실행을 놓치지 않고, 조금은 유쾌하게 알아챌 수 있습니다.

이럴 때 반응합니다:
  • 테스트가 실패할 때
  • 애플리케이션이 에러로 종료될 때 (종료 코드 1 — 시작 실패, uncaught 예외 등)
  • 컴파일 에러로 실행이 중단될 때
프로세스가 정상 종료하거나, 사용자가 직접 실행을 멈춘 경우에는 소리가 나지 않습니다.

Settings/Preferences | Tools | Laughing Cat Sound 에서 볼륨을 조절하거나 음소거할 수 있고, 소리를 미리 들어볼 수 있습니다.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.3.0
  • 실행 중 콘솔 텍스트로 에러를 감지하던 방식을 제거했습니다. (통과하는 테스트가 스택 트레이스를 출력하는 등 오탐이 잦았습니다)
  • 이제 다음 세 경우에만 반응합니다: 테스트 실패(IDE 테스트 러너 이벤트로 감지), 애플리케이션이 종료 코드 1로 끝남(시작 실패·uncaught 예외 등), 컴파일 에러로 실행 중단.
  • 정상 종료나 사용자가 직접 실행을 멈춘 경우(Stop)에는 소리가 나지 않습니다.
1.3.0 (English)
  • Remove console-text error detection. (It fired too often — e.g. when a passing test prints a stack trace.)
  • Now reacts only in three cases: a test fails (detected via the IDE test-runner events), an application exits with code 1 (a failed startup, an uncaught exception, ...), or a run is aborted by a compilation error.
  • Stays silent on a normal exit or when you stop the run yourself.
1.2.0
  • 에러 발생 시 웃는 고양이 이미지를 잠깐 띄웠다가 사라지게 하는 팝업 추가
  • 팝업 위치 선택 추가 (우측 하단/좌측 하단/우측 상단/좌측 상단/중앙, 그리고 모두)
  • "모두" 선택 시 다섯 위치에 동시에 표시
  • 테스트 버튼이 소리와 이미지 팝업을 함께 미리보기하도록 변경
  • 설정창에서 테스트 시 팝업이 사라지지 않던 문제 수정
1.2.0 (English)
  • Add an image popup that briefly shows a laughing cat and fades out on error.
  • Add a popup position setting (bottom-right/left, top-right/left, center, and All).
  • "All" shows the image at the five positions at once.
  • The Test button now previews both the sound and the image popup.
  • Fix the popup not disappearing when tested from the settings dialog.
1.1.0
  • 설정 페이지 추가: Settings/Preferences | Tools | Laughing Cat Sound
  • 볼륨 조절 추가 (0-100, 0이면 음소거)
  • 선택한 볼륨으로 미리 듣는 "소리 테스트" 버튼 추가
  • 새 소리가 재생되면 이전 소리를 멈춰 겹침 방지
  • 설정 UI 다국어 지원 (한국어/영어)
1.1.0 (English)
  • Add a settings page at Settings/Preferences | Tools | Laughing Cat Sound.
  • Add a volume control (0-100, where 0 mutes the sound).
  • Add a "Test sound" button to preview the sound at the chosen volume.
  • A newly triggered sound now stops the previous one instead of overlapping.
  • Localize the settings UI (Korean and English).
1.0.0
  • Play a laughing cat sound when a run/debug process exits with an error.
  • Play the sound when a run is aborted by a compilation error.
  • Play the sound when an error pattern is printed to a console.

idea-plugin.name: Faah - Error Alerts
idea-plugin.description: Never miss errors in JetBrains IDEs. Faah plays instant audio alerts for non-zero terminal and execution exit codes, failed tests, Docker failures, suspicious output, and editor diagnostics, with status controls, cooldowns, snooze, quiet hours, and custom patterns.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Added shell command exit-code events when JetBrains shell integration exposes them.
  • Added language-independent test failure detection for JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Java/JVM, Go, Rust, .NET, Ruby, PHP, Swift, and TAP-style runners.
  • Added Docker, Compose, daemon, build, image, container, networking, volume, health-check, and port failure detection.
  • Improved Run/Debug/test/build non-zero exit alerts with execution classification.
  • Retained classic-terminal output monitoring, diagnostics, cooldowns, snooze, quiet hours, status controls, and import/export.

idea-plugin.name: GRID Flowchart
idea-plugin.description: Renders the open Python file as a flowchart on a row/column grid where row = source line number and column = indentation level.

idea-plugin.name: CodeLoupe
idea-plugin.description:
CodeLoupe mines your project's Git history to surface which files change most and are most complex, visualized as an interactive circle-packing map.

Runs fully locally: no server, no telemetry, no network access.

Proprietary software — see the LICENSE for terms.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Project view decoration is much cheaper on large repositories: looking up a file's hotspot no longer scans the whole report.
  • Changing a display-only setting (Project view tint, editor banner, percentile threshold) now just repaints instead of re-running the whole analysis.
  • Background analysis after commits, branch switches and project changes now only runs in projects where CodeLoupe has been opened before (remembered per user in the workspace file), so untouched projects cost nothing. In those projects, Project view tints and editor banners come back on startup without opening the tool window.
  • New "Analyze in background" setting (on by default) turns background analysis off; analysis then runs only when the tool window opens or you click Refresh.
  • Personal display settings (Project view tint, editor banner, percentile threshold and "Analyze in background") are now stored per user in the workspace file instead of the shared .idea/codeloupe.xml, so they no longer leak to teammates through version control. Values set in an earlier version are migrated automatically the first time the project opens; the analysis settings stay shared.
  • Map and HTML export labels now come from the plugin's message bundle, so they can be translated.
  • Fixed the extracted map assets being left behind in the temp directory after every IDE session.

idea-plugin.name: Cmd Widgets
idea-plugin.description:
Display shell command output as independent widgets in your IDE status bar. Track Git branches, disk space, Kubernetes contexts, or any other value available from a command. Percentage output automatically displays a progress bar.

  • Configure global widgets with individual refresh intervals and working directories.
  • Run commands on the frontend or backend host, including in remote development.
  • Test commands before saving and inspect output, errors, and execution details.
  • Retain the last successful value and mark it as stale after a failure.

Ideas for widgets: https://github.com/nizienko/cmdwidget/blob/master/docs/COMMANDS.md

Open Settings / Preferences > Tools > Cmd Widget to create your first widget. Command execution supports macOS, Linux, and Windows hosts. Commands run with your user permissions; configure only commands you trust.

Source code and documentation | Report an issue | MIT License
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0 — Initial release

  • Independent command widgets with text and automatic percentage progress bars.
  • Global settings, per-project results, refresh intervals, and working directories.
  • Frontend and backend execution with remote development support.
  • Explicit command testing, execution diagnostics, and stale-value indicators.
  • Bounded output capture, timeouts, and cancellation on macOS, Linux, and Windows.

idea-plugin.name: DOT Studio
idea-plugin.description:
Graphviz DOT editing and live preview in JetBrains IDEs.

Opens .dot and .gv files with:

  • Syntax highlighting, with colours you can change in Settings | Editor | Color Scheme | DOT
  • Syntax error highlighting, including -> in an undirected graph and -- in a digraph
  • Code folding, brace matching, and line and block commenting
  • A Structure view of subgraphs, nodes and edges
  • A live preview in a split editor that renders the graph as you type, using the Graphviz layout engine bundled with the plugin, so no Graphviz installation is needed. Choose an engine by setting layout= in the graph
  • Export of the rendered graph as SVG or PNG
  • Zoom and pan in the preview: Ctrl/Cmd+mouse wheel zooms, Zoom In, Zoom Out, Actual Size and Zoom to Fit are on the editor toolbar, and dragging the graph pans it

Works in IDEs from 2025.2 to 2026.2. The preview needs the IDE's embedded browser (JCEF); without it the editor features still work.

Known limitation: on IDEs 2025.2, uninstalling the plugin after using the preview may require an IDE restart (#26). Uninstalling without a restart has been verified on 2026.2.

The plugin makes no network calls and collects no data.

Bundled third-party software: viz-js (MIT), Graphviz (EPL-2.0), Expat (MIT), Emscripten runtime (MIT or NCSA), musl libc (MIT) and libc++ (Apache-2.0 with LLVM exception). Licence texts and notices are in the plugin under META-INF/third-party/.

Source code and issue tracker: github.com/acalebratliff/dot-studio
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • .dot and .gv files open as DOT files, with syntax highlighting for keywords, IDs, numbers, quoted and HTML strings, comments and edge operators
  • DOT colours can be changed in Settings | Editor | Color Scheme | DOT
  • Comment and uncomment lines (//) and blocks (/* */) in DOT files
  • Matching {} and [] are highlighted, and typing [ inserts the closing ]
  • Syntax errors in DOT files are highlighted. A mistake in one statement is reported there and doesn't mark the rest of the file
  • -> in an undirected graph and -- in a digraph are highlighted as errors, as Graphviz rejects them
  • Unclosed quoted strings, HTML strings and /* */ comments are highlighted as errors
  • Graph and subgraph bodies, attribute lists and /* */ comments that span several lines can be folded
  • The Structure tool window lists each graph's subgraphs and node and edge statements, with edge chains such as a -> b -> c; selecting one moves the caret to it
  • Live preview: DOT files open in a split editor that renders the graph as you type, using the bundled Graphviz, so no Graphviz installation is needed. The editor toolbar switches between editor only, editor and preview, and preview only
  • The preview page follows the editor colour scheme and updates when the theme changes. Graphs keep the colours set in the DOT and Graphviz's white background unless the DOT sets bgcolor, so they stay readable in dark themes
  • Export the rendered graph as SVG, or as PNG at 1x or 2x its actual size, from the export button in the editor tab or the editor context menu. The SVG is exactly what the preview rendered, and the PNG is drawn by the same browser engine as the preview. Export is disabled, with the reason shown, while the graph has no successful render or JCEF is unavailable. A graph too large for a PNG at the chosen scale is refused with a message suggesting 1x or SVG
  • Zoom and pan the preview: Ctrl+mouse wheel zooms around the pointer, and Zoom In, Zoom Out, Actual Size (100%) and Zoom to Fit are in the editor tab (new UI) or the editor toolbar (classic UI). Drag the graph or use the scrollbars to pan. A new preview fits the graph to the window, never above 100%, and keeps it fitted as you type until you zoom; after that, re-renders keep your zoom and scroll position. Zoom goes from 10% (lower when a large graph needs it to fit) to 800%. The zoom actions have no default shortcut, because the usual zoom keys fold code in the editor; they can be assigned in the keymap. Export always saves the whole graph at its actual size, whatever the zoom
  • The preview says "Only the first graph is previewed" under the graph when a file holds more than one graph, because Graphviz renders only the first
  • An empty file, or one with only comments, shows "Nothing to preview yet" in the preview instead of an error
  • The notice shown when the IDE has no embedded browser (JCEF) wraps to the width of the preview instead of running off its edge
  • On IDE 2026.2 the plugin can be updated or uninstalled without restarting the IDE. Open DOT files are closed during an update and reopened when the new version loads

idea-plugin.name: Progress Tractor
idea-plugin.description:
Replaces the IDE's progress bars with a little tractor plowing a field.
  • Determinate progress: the plowed soil behind the tractor shows how much is done.
  • Indeterminate progress: the tractor drives back and forth across the field.
  • Drawn with Java2D, adapts to light and dark themes and HiDPI.
idea-plugin.change-notes: • Initial release.

idea-plugin.name: Pipeline Notifier
idea-plugin.description:
Watches GitLab CI pipelines and GitHub Actions workflow runs over their REST APIs and raises hard-to-miss alerts when one fails.

By default it alerts on pipelines you triggered in the GitLab and GitHub projects matching the git remotes of the projects you have open. You can also add extra projects to watch, and define rules to be alerted about other people's failures — filtered by triggering user, branch/tag glob, and pipeline source (push, merge request, schedule, manual, API...). Rules belong to one service, since each has its own set of sources.

Each rule chooses how loud it gets:

  • Sticky balloon — an in-IDE error notification that stays until you dismiss it, plus a red badge and an attention request on the application icon (a Dock bounce on macOS).
  • System notification — a native OS notification, so you see it even when the IDE is in the background. The platform suppresses this automatically while the IDE is focused.
  • Modal dialog — a blocking dialog brought to the front. Maximum visibility, maximum interruption; off by default for everything except your own failures.

Configure it under Settings | Tools | Pipeline Notifier, one tab per service. Tokens are stored in the IDE's password safe (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Store, or libsecret), never in plain-text settings. Self-hosted GitLab and GitHub Enterprise Server are supported.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • GitHub Actions support: failed workflow runs are watched alongside GitLab pipelines, on github.com or GitHub Enterprise Server. Each service has its own tab in settings, with its own URL, token and extra projects.
  • Notification rules now belong to a service (GitLab or GitHub), so each offers its own pipeline sources.

Security

  • Project paths from git remotes and settings are validated, and encoded in GitHub API URLs.
  • Editing a server URL clears the access token that was loaded for the old one, and the old token is removed from the password safe. A warning is shown for plain http:// URLs.
  • Text from the server shown in alerts (branch, job and repository names) is stripped of markup and control/bidirectional characters and length-capped.
  • Log redaction covers passwords containing @ and token= query values.

Fixed

  • A throttled server (HTTP 429, or 403 with Retry-After or an exhausted quota) is left alone until it is ready, instead of being asked again every poll. A 403 on a single project no longer pauses the whole service.
  • The poller backs off when every project of a service fails.
  • Applying settings before the stored token has loaded no longer overwrites it.
  • GitHub logins are compared case-insensitively, and runs are attributed to the original actor so they match the filter used to find them.
  • The poll watermark trails the newest run by a minute so late-listed runs are not skipped.
  • GitHub repository paths differing only in case are watched once.

Changed

  • Internals are split into a provider-neutral core and one adapter per CI service, so further services can be added without touching polling, matching or alerting.

idea-plugin.name: SSH Agent Watch
idea-plugin.description:
A simple plugin that watches your SSH agent (from a password manager like 1Password, or any other agent) and points out which keys are currently active. It also helps you view, edit, detect and create the agent config file (agent.toml) and your ~/.ssh/config, whether they live in the default locations or custom ones.
  • Status bar entry with the active keys; click it for the full list
  • Warning when more keys are offered than servers usually accept
  • Highlight when a key matching your Prod/Live patterns is active
  • Tool window to view both config files, open them in the editor, or create them from a template
The SSH agent protocol offers every enabled key to every server, and most servers give up after six attempts. This plugin does not change that; it makes the current state impossible to miss. It talks to the agent only to list public keys, never touches private keys, and makes no network connections.

idea-plugin.name: Infinitest
idea-plugin.description: Infinitest is a continuous test runner for Java, and is valuable to developers using a unit testing tool called JUnit. Continuous testing is the practice of constantly running unit tests while developers make changes to source code. Kind of like a spellchecker, except that instead of looking for spelling errors like a regular spellchecker, or looking for syntax errors like many IDE's do, Infinitest constantly looks for logical errors and immediately identifies them. It does this by running an optimized set of unit tests every time a developer makes a change to source code.

PUTVT Python Unit Tests Visualization Tool

This plugin is used for loading files with the logs of Pytest or Python failures/tracebacks and then visualizing them in the editor. This plugin also provides a Dependency Graph


Here are listed the actions, which will appear in the tools menu in IDE:

  • Stop visualization: Stops the visualization for all the files, keeping the settings, but not the so far visualized data.
  • Visualize console logs:Visualizes the logs from the internal IntelliJ console log. Logs are visualized, if any errors happened and are drawn when the editor tabs are opened/reopened.
  • Listen for external jars:Listens for external logs, which can be send through a UDP protocol on port 9876 as 1024 bit words. These are then visualized.

Here are listed the actions which can be used on the Dependency Graph window.

  • Visualize coverage: Creates a dependency Graph visualizing the actual coverage for all the modules (python files) of the project. The nodes are differently colorized according to their code coverage.
  • Reset view: Resets the view of the visualized graph - changes the focus.
  • Clean canvas: Cleans the canvas and reoves the entire visualization

idea-plugin.name: Assertions2Assertj
idea-plugin.description:
Assertions2Assert2

Helper plugin to convert Junit and Hamcrest Assertions to AssertJ. The plugin will aid in the conversion of assert statements, but does not support conversion of all Hamcrest and Junit asserts scenarios. Some manual intervention may be needed.

Dependencies
  • Note that AssertJ must be included in the IntelliJ project classpath for the Plugin to successfully complete.
Usage
  • Select an item from within the Refactor -> Convert Assertions to AssertJ menu. Note that the "Convert current file" and "Convert Module" items will only be enabled if a file is selected within the editor.
Limitations
  • The plugin does NOT convert Hamcrest assertions included in Mockito verify statements
  • The plugin does NOT convert all assertions that utilize matchers embedded within other matchers (e.g. anyOf(equalTo(1.0), equalTo(2.0))).
  • When a file contains both assertions that are converted, and assertions that are ignored, the Hamcrest imports will still be deleted.
  • Does not support the following Hamcrest matchers
    • allOf
    • anything
    • everyItem
    • hasXPath
    • samePropertyValueAs
  • Does not support the following Junit Asserts
    • assertTimeout
    • assertTimeoutPreemptively

Automatically Generate Unit Tests for Java Source Classes.

Create a Test Class
Choose Squaretest | Generate Test from the toolbar menu to create a test class for a Java class.

Create Test Methods
Open a test class and choose Squaretest | Generate Test Methods from the toolbar menu. Then select the test methods you want to create and click OK.

Features

  • Automatically generates Java tests using either JUnit4, JUnit5, TestNG, Robolectric3+, AndroidJUnit4 and Mockito.
  • Supports generating tests using Spring MockMVC, AssertJ and Groovy.
  • Supports choosing which dependencies to mock, which methods to test, and how to construct the source class (choose Squaretest | Generate Test - Confirm Options).
  • Generates test methods with when(), verify() and assertEquals(..) calls.
  • Generates code to initialize data transfer objects used in the tests.
  • Creates doAnswer() statements for dependency method calls that take in Callables or Runnables.
  • Creates test methods for alternate flows by stubbing dependency method calls to throw exceptions or return alternate values.
  • All output can be customized by changing the provided Apache Velocity templates.
  • See squaretest.com for the full list of features.

idea-plugin.name: JUnit 5 Mockito Code Generator
idea-plugin.description:
The plugin generates boilerplate Mockito JUnit 5 code that usually needs to be added manually to unit tests. This plugin requires your project to use the following dependencies:
  • JUnit 5 (Jupiter)
  • Mockito Core
  • Mockito JUnit Jupiter Plugin
  • AssertJ (optional)

The plugin auto-generates the following:

  • ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class) annotation on the test class
  • Mocked fields for each non-static object declared in the test subject
  • Primary type variables and standard final classes (Instant, ZonedDateTime, UUID, Enums) for tested classes and methods
  • Field for the test subject with @InjectMocks annotation
  • Nested classed with @Nested to test each accessible method of the tested class with the fields required in input mocked
  • static imports for useful mockito functions like when, verify and AssertJ assertThat if it is available

There are two ways to get the plugin to generate your code:

  • From inside the test class, hit alt+insert, and then hit Add Mockito JUnit 5 Code
  • Right click on the test class and select Generate. Then hit Add Mockito JUnit 5 Code

Project is an open source project available on GitHub. Feel free to suggest new features or open merge requests.

Plugin was modified from an existing plugin: https://github.com/przemyslawj/mockito-intellij-plugin and then modified to use JUnit 5 and generate nested class methods. My other projects

  • Magidoc, a GraphQL documentation generator
  • Mockkator, Intellij plugin to generate boilerplate code for Mockk

idea-plugin.name: Validation-File Comparison
idea-plugin.description:
Plugin on GitHub | Cronn GmbH Website

IntelliJ plugin as extension to cronn's validation file assertion library.
Compare and accept output and validation files without context switches.
Further features:

  • Rename related validation files when methods or classes are renamed
  • Jump to related validation file from code and vice-versa

Usage

Open Validation-File Comparison

Execute tests which use validation files, open the test itself or open the production code for it and run the the action Validation-File Comparison.

You can find the action using ...

  • IntelliJ's Find Action (Ctrl+Shift+A / ⇧⌘A) and search for Validation File Comparison
  • View | Validation-File Comparison
  • Right Click | Validation-File Comparison
  • Or the default shortcut Alt+Shift+V /⌥⇧V

This plugin finds the corresponding (sub-)module for the current dialog and compares the two directories [SUBMODULE-PATH]/data/test/validation and [SUBMODULE-PATH]/data/test/output, which are the default directories for validation file assertion library.

Rename Tests with Validation Files

When renaming a test with validation files the validation and output files will be suggested for renaming as well. Simply use the rename refactoring of intellij (Shift+F6 / ⇧F6) and apply the suggested renaming as wished. To disable this feature simply trigger the keybinding for the renaming twice and deselect "Rename validation and output files".

Jump to Validation File or Code

Similar to IntelliJ's build-in action for switching between tests and implementations, it is possible to directly jump into the according validation file from a test and back. Simply press the default shortcut Alt+Shift+F /⌥⇧F and the according file is opened at the relevant position. If there are multiple possible targets, a selection window with all targets is presented. This action can be used from within a test method as well as for the whole test class. When used from a validation file, it finds the deepest possible code target to jump to, also regarding nested test classes and methods with multiple validation files.

Configuration

As for every IntelliJ action, you can configure your own shortcut for the Validation-File Comparison action. Simply go to File | Settings | Keymap , search for Validation-File Comparison and configure a new shortcut.

The behavior of the action can be configured in the dedicated settings dialog under File | Settings | Tools | Validation-File Comparison Plugin.

idea-plugin.name: TestInsanity
idea-plugin.description:
Rename a class and its tests are renamed with it. Jump from a method straight to the method that tests it. TestInsanity learns your naming convention instead of guessing at it.


Rename the subject, and the matching test class and test methods are proposed with their new names.

Why not just Navigate -> Test?
Because it guesses one hardcoded class name and stops there. TestInsanity works from a convention you declare, matches methods as well as classes, goes in both directions, and carries renames through.

  ${className}Test   maps Color to ColorTest
  test${subjectName}*   maps isDarkColor() to testIsDarkColor_whenBlack()

Nothing to set up: ${className}Test and ${className}IT are configured on install. Each scheme binds one class convention to the method conventions used inside it, and schemes are tried in order — so unit tests, integration tests and specs coexist in one project, each with its own method naming.

  • Renaming, both ways — subject class to test classes, test class to subject, subject method to test methods, test method to subject. Renames appear in the standard Rename related items dialog, so you can deselect any of them.
  • Navigation to the method — Jump to Sibling (CTRL+ALT+`) moves between a method and its test method, not only between their classes. Navigate -> Test (CTRL+SHIFT+T) follows the same scheme.
  • Gutter icons — at the class and at the method, the sibling on the other side, its JUnit 5 DisplayName when it has one, and a distinct icon for a test with no subject.
  • Alt+Enter creates what is missing — the test class, or the test method with the right framework annotation, one entry per scheme. On a test, the same key creates the subject. New classes land in the correct test root, including when tests live in a module of their own.
  • Your convention in version control — a .testinsanity.json at the project root pins the scheme for the whole team, the way .editorconfig does. Keys it declares win and show as disabled in the settings; keys it omits stay personal. It is re-read on every change, including branch switches, and gets completion, documentation and validation as you type. One click creates it from the settings you already have.

Every method links to the method that tests it, and the ones with no test stay unmarked.


Every class links to its test class, and a test with no subject gets an icon of its own.

Also handles JUnit 4, JUnit 5 and TestNG including nested, parameterized and templated tests, any annotation composed of theirs, a house annotation named outright or by package wildcard, Kotlin with backtick test names (optional dependency, K2 ready), inherited and abstract test classes, and optional @DisplayName generation and sync.

Configured per project under Settings -> Tools -> TestInsanity.

Report an issue
idea-plugin.change-notes:
v2.0.0

New
  • Project configuration in .testinsanity.json at the project root, so the naming scheme lives in version control instead of in .idea. Keys the file declares win over the IDE settings and appear disabled in the settings dialog; keys it omits stay personal. The file is re-read whenever it changes, including on branch switches, and a bundled JSON schema gives it completion, inline documentation and validation. Settings -> Tools -> TestInsanity shows whether the file is in use, can switch it off per IDE, and can create it from the settings you already have.
  • Renaming works in all four directions: subject class to test classes, test class to subject class, subject method to test methods, and test method to subject method.
  • Renaming goes through the standard Rename related items dialog, so it also applies to in-place rename and lets you deselect any proposed rename.
  • Several named schemes per project, listed and reordered in the settings and tried top to bottom. Each scheme binds one test class pattern to its own test method patterns, so unit, integration and end to end tests keep separate naming instead of sharing one flat list. The first scheme whose test class pattern matches wins, and an existing single-pattern setup migrates into one scheme with no change in behaviour.
  • Navigate -> Test follows the configured naming scheme, and the Create Test Sibling intention creates the class and method your scheme names.
  • New intention (Alt+Enter): create the missing test class or test method for the subject. One entry per scheme that is still missing its test class, so a unit scheme and an integration scheme can each be created; a chooser appears when more than one is missing.
  • The reverse intention (Alt+Enter): create the missing subject class from a test class, and the missing subject method when the scheme names it unambiguously.
  • Created classes land in the module test root, or in the module declared as its test module, or in the single dependent module that has test roots, so a separate test module is handled.
  • JUnit 5 nested test classes are matched.
  • The test annotation check follows composed annotations, so a project-local @IntegrationTest that is itself annotated @Test is recognized, as is an override of an annotated method. Every JUnit Platform engine is covered through @Testable, and additionalTestAnnotations declares a house runner by name or by package wildcard.
  • Patterns accept spaces, for Kotlin backtick test names, with a matching preset.
  • Optional @DisplayName generation and rename synchronization.
  • Gutter icons are computed off the highlighting pass and cached, appear in every JVM language, and can be switched off in Settings -> Editor -> General -> Gutter Icons.
Fixed
  • Renaming a subject class did not rename its test classes.
  • Renaming a test class or a test method did not rename its subject.
  • A test living in its own module never resolved its subject.
  • Which sibling was picked followed index order and could differ between runs.
  • A test method was counted twice when two matching test classes were related by inheritance.
  • A nested helper class inside a test class was reported as a test of the outer subject.
  • The settings Apply button ignored changes to the renaming checkbox.
  • A damaged TestInsanity.xml could leave the plugin inert.
  • Creating .testinsanity.json from the settings wrote an empty array the plugin then refused to read.
  • A settings file that named test frameworks explicitly did not pick up annotations added by an upgrade.
  • Gutter icons kept the previous scheme in already-open editors until the file was edited again.
  • The method gutter tooltip read TestMethod and SubjectMethod with no space.
  • Only the first scheme could create its test class; once any scheme had one, the others could not.
Changed
  • Show renaming dialog is now Pre-select test renames: it decides whether the proposed renames start checked rather than whether a dialog appears, and the dialog is the platform Rename related items dialog. Settings written by earlier versions carry over with renaming left on.

v1.3.0
  • 2026.1+
  • Kotlin K2 mode support.
  • Kotlin support is now optional: the plugin works without the Kotlin plugin.
  • Jump to Sibling now falls back to the class when a Kotlin function has no matching JVM method.
  • Fixed errors when renaming Kotlin functions that have no matching JVM method.

v1.2.0
  • 2024.1

v1.0.9
  • Small code cleanup.
  • Some icons changes.

v1.0.8
  • Small code cleanup.
  • Some icons changes.

v1.0.7
  • More deprecated APIs.

Documents actual behavior: Unit tests reveal what your code really does (not what comments claim), essential for understanding legacy systems and inherited codebases.

Enables rapid coverage increases: Creates unit tests in bulk, covering all relevant branches to rapidly improve coverage and enable teams to reach and maintain coverage goals.

Handles enterprise complexity: Works with complex Spring contexts, Mockito configurations, and legacy patterns that cause other tools to fail with OOM errors.

Enables safe refactoring: Create regression safety net before Java version upgrades, cloud migrations, or modernization initiatives. Know what breaks before production.

idea-plugin.name: Fixkture
idea-plugin.description:
Do you write tests (I sincerely hope you do)? Are you tired of writing test fixtures for your 30 fields DTO? Here's the solution! This plugin allows you to generate a fixture of any desired class, for both Kotlin and Java (even though you should consider switching to Kotlin, since is a way far superior language). Fields of this class will be given arbitrary values when being generated.
Usage
Anywhere in your test class, hit ctrl+shift+G. You'll be prompt to select a target class, and the fixture will be automatically resolved!
Generated code
This plugin supports complex data models and most common types from Java/Kotlin Standard Library
  • For classes with ambiguous constructors, you'll be prompt to choose which constructor to take to instantiate the class
  • For collections, it will automatically generate a collection of the right type, with one element in it
  • Recursive objects are supported. The recursion will however stop at one level

    • Contribute
    Feel free to create an issue on Github or even to open your own PR. I developed this project for personal usage, but i'm open to suggestions or improvement ideas.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
Please kindly report any problem... and Rate & Review this plugin !

Change notes :
  • 25.0.1 Remote Development (WSL/SSH) fix: the table frame and drag-and-drop are now cleanly disabled on a remote backend (where they can't be drawn/relayed to the thin client) instead of half-working — header highlighting and the table menu still work. The two settings are greyed out there.
  • 25.0.0 New settings page (Settings → Tools → Cucumber+) — enable/disable each in-editor behaviour individually, or all at once with the master switch: the "Rename steps and references…" suggestion; table auto-format, smart keys (Pipe/Enter/Tab/Del), smart copy-paste, column-selection switch, drag-and-drop and frame; Gherkin↔step-definition breakpoint sync; and the "used by N scenarios" gutter markers.
  • 24.0.1 Fix: the "Rename steps and references…" suggestion no longer appears when you delete a whole step line — only when you actually edit a step's text.
  • 24.0.0 Step rename — rename a Gherkin step and Cucumber+ rewrites the step definition's pattern AND every other Gherkin step bound to it, in one go, preserving parameters ({int}/{string}), etc. Works from Java, Kotlin, JavaScript/TypeScript and Python step definitions. A preview dialog lists every reference that will change; and when you start editing a step in place, a discreet "Rename steps and references…" hint appears under the line. A single Undo reverts the whole rename.
  • 23.0.1 Fix a startup crash (NoClassDefFoundError) for users on IntelliJ IDEA who use Cucumber+ for Python/JS without the Cucumber for Java plugin installed: the Java integration now activates only when that plugin is present (like the Kotlin/Scala/JS integrations).
  • 23.0.0 Python (behave) support — Cucumber+ now syncs breakpoints with Python step definitions just like Java/Kotlin/Scala/JS: set a breakpoint on a Gherkin step and it pairs with the matching @given/@when/@then function (and back), and step-defs get the "used by N scenarios" gutter marker. Requires the companion Cucumber for Python plugin for behave step resolution.
    Also: per-scenario muting on shared step definitions now works for Python and JavaScript too (not just Java) — when two scenarios share one step definition, muting one scenario's breakpoint makes the debugger skip only that scenario at runtime.
  • 22.0.1 Breakpoint sync polish & performance (Java / Kotlin / JS / TS). Toggling or muting a breakpoint is faster (#124) and no longer lags. When several Gherkin steps share one step definition, muting one step no longer mutes the others — the shared code breakpoint stays active while any linked step is, and a dedicated half-muted icon (half red disc / half red ring) marks that mixed state. Fixes mute / unmute / removal sync on the JavaScript side.
  • 22.0.0 JavaScript & TypeScript support — Cucumber+ now works with cucumber-js step definitions, just like Java/Kotlin/Scala: set a breakpoint on a Gherkin step and it syncs to the matching Given/When/Then(...) in your .js/.ts file (and back), enable/disable propagates both ways, the debugger stops only on the example row you flag, and step-defs get the "used by N scenarios" gutter icon. Requires the bundled JavaScript support (Ultimate / WebStorm) and the Cucumber.js plugin. (TypeScript step-defs need -r ts-node/register in the run configuration.)
    This feature is brand new and hasn't been tested on large real-world projects yet — kind feedback and bug reports are very welcome!
  • 21.8.14 Cucumber test tree polish: Example #N nodes now show their row values (Age: 22, Score: 75, Prenom: Clara), step parameters (quoted strings, numbers, <placeholders>) render in grey italic, and inherited tags no longer leak onto Example or step nodes.
  • 21.8.12 Enable/disable on a Gherkin step breakpoint now propagates to the paired code breakpoint (was only working in the code → Gherkin direction).
  • 21.8.11 Fix breakpoints set on Kotlin step definitions not stopping the debugger.
  • 21.8.9 Fix editor freezes during autocompletion when breakpoints are present — the Gherkin↔Java/Kotlin breakpoint sync no longer re-scans the project on every keystroke.
  • 21.8.7 Test tree decoration on Windows + WSL: some Cucumber runners don't publish SMTRunner events on the project bus — our listener was silently never fired so the file-name + feature title decoration was missing. Now we (1) subscribe to BOTH the project AND application message bus, and (2) lazily run the decoration from the styled renderer on first paint as a safety net.
  • 21.8.6 Test tree suite label on Windows + WSL: more robust VFS resolution of cucumber-jvm file:///… location URLs — tries findFileByUrl, then URI.path with leading-slash normalisation for Windows drive letters (/C:/… → C:/…), then a brute-force fallback. The file.feature / Feature title [Business Need title] label now appears correctly on Windows + WSL setups.
  • 21.8.5 Fix #124 — 20s+ editor freezes on IntelliJ 2026.1.x EAP: the overridden GotoDeclaration action (TzGotoStepDefAction) is now declared with explicit text and description attributes, satisfying the platform's stricter menu validation that was throwing PluginException: Empty menu item text on every menu repaint. Also: test tree wrapper "Cucumber+" rendered in default style (no bold), and Windows-side VFS resolution falls back to LocalFileSystem.findFileByPath when findFileByUrl returns null on file:///C:/… URLs — restores the file.feature / Feature title [Business Need title] suite label that was collapsing to file.feature / Business Need title on Windows.
  • 21.8.4 Cucumber test tree: split the file name from the feature header label (file in default style, header in grey). Fix the dbl-click-to-navigate handler on Windows by mirroring the platform's mouseClicked event (was mousePressed — consume didn't propagate cross-event on Windows AWT). Also walks the file root when resolving feature/business-need keyword pairs, in case the parser splits them into sibling features.
  • 21.8.3 Cucumber test tree: surface Gherkin tags (e.g. @Production @Chrome) at the end of each suite node in grey — Feature-level tags written above the keyword are surfaced on the top suite, scenario / outline / background tags on their own node. Also catches tree-replacement on test re-runs so double-click-to-navigate keeps working when IntelliJ reuses the run tab.
  • 21.8.2 Cucumber test tree styled rendering: the outermost feature suite renders as multi-fragment text — file name in grey, primary header (Feature) in bold, secondary headers (Business Need / Ability) in grey italic between brackets. The "Cucumber+" wrapper node is also bolded. No change to behaviour, just a clearer visual.
  • 21.8.1 Fix #122 — extreme CPU usage in 21.8.0: replaced the global ToolWindowManagerListener that re-traversed the Run/Debug/Services component trees on every UI state change with a per-tool-window ContentManagerListener that scans only newly added test contents. Also drops usage of the internal PluginManagerCore.getPlugin(PluginId) flagged by the Marketplace verifier.
  • 21.8.0 Cucumber test tree polish: rename the wrapper category to Cucumber+, show the feature file name + every header (Business Need / Ability / Feature) on the top suite node (e.g. France.feature / Cocktail Ordering [toto]), and make double-click on a Feature / Scenario node open the .feature file at that line instead of just toggling the tree expansion.
  • 21.7.3 # @header: column highlight now spans the whole logical table — comments / blank lines interleaved between rows no longer truncate the coloring.

idea-plugin.name: Pipe Table Formatter
idea-plugin.description:
This is a pipe table formatter plugin for the IntelliJ platform, which formats pipe tables used in JBehave stories for example. It utilizes the pipe table formatter program by Jurrie Overgoor (see this), which normally watches for file changes. This plugin provides the same functionality, but as an action, which can be used from a context menu or with a shortcut.
Since 1.1.0 it's also integrated as a normal formatter, into the standard formatting functionality of the IntelliJ Platform.

Using this plugin is simple:
  1. Just use your formatting shortcut!
Or
  1. Open a JBehave story or another file containing a pipe table.
  2. Right-click in the editor to open the context menu.
  3. Go to 'Pipe Table Formatter' and click 'Format Pipe Tables in File'.
  4. All pipe tables in the opened file should now be formatted.
  5. Alternatively, use the 'Pipe Table Formatter' submenu under the 'Code' menu option of your IDE.

There is no keyboard shortcut assigned by default, but as this is quite useful, it's recommended that one is added via the IDE Settings.

idea-plugin.name: AppMap: Runtime Evidence for AI Coding
idea-plugin.description:
Enterprise users

If your company installs AppMap for you, some settings are already set by an administrator. Before you install AppMap or change a setting, ask your AppMap administrator, or read your company's own setup documentation, for example in Confluence.

Runtime evidence for AI-assisted development

See how every change behaves before it merges, in your JetBrains IDE

AI tools generate code changes faster than anyone can read them. A diff shows what the code says, not which calls, queries, and side effects occurred when it ran. AppMap records your application while it runs and turns the recording into diagrams for you and data your coding agent queries over MCP. The review is based on what the code did.

Key benefits of this plugin

The plugin stores and configures AppMap on your machine

The plugin installs the AppMap command-line tools, keeps them updated, and stores and indexes every recording locally, so the MCP server always has fresh data to serve. You can use AppMap entirely through your coding agent: record by running your tests, then ask questions from your chat. The AppMap skills for coding agents configure your repository:

  • appmap-record turns on recording.
  • appmap-label tunes what gets recorded.
  • appmap-gold-traces keeps the Gold Trace set.
  • appmap-review runs the behavioral review.

Store behavior with the code

Gold Traces are the runtime behaviors a team has approved, committed in the gold_traces/ directory alongside the code. A developer or coding agent opening the repository starts with the same Gold Traces: behavior that cannot be inferred from the source, current at every commit, and the baseline every change is verified against. Every trace is sanitized before it is committed. See Gold Traces on appmap.io.

Found a gold_traces/ directory in a repository? Someone on the team keeps runtime behavior versioned with the code. This plugin reads those traces as diagrams, and your coding agent can query them over MCP.

The value of AppMap data to AI coding

Understand AI-generated code before you ship it

An AI assistant can change hundreds of lines in one pull request. AppMap shows you the behavior of the change as diagrams: which functions ran, which SQL queries were made, which HTTP requests were handled, and where exceptions came from. Your coding agent reads the same evidence over MCP. It often has no application environment, database, or credentials, so it works from the recorded behavior, which it can query but does not create. AppMap works with Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, and any MCP-capable coding agent.

Review code changes in a new way

Ask your coding agent for a behavioral review: a review of the change that uses AppMap recordings, not just the diff. It compares the change against the recorded baseline and reports what the change did when it ran: API changes and drift, SQL impact, security-affecting paths, unexpected side effects, and performance changes.

A real review of one change, from one of our own production applications. The fix was applied and re-recorded during the review.

Nothing leaves your machine, or your repository

AppMap has no cloud data plane. Recording and the MCP server run in your development environment, and AppMap data is saved as files in your project. Gold Traces go only where your repository goes. Usage telemetry is separate and can be routed to your own systems or disabled. See the security disclosure.

Set up your coding agent

The AppMap MCP server gives your agent 13 read-only query tools, including get_call_tree, find_calls, find_queries, and find_requests. In Claude Code, run claude mcp add appmap -- appmap query mcp. For another agent, add "appmap": { "command": "appmap", "args": ["query", "mcp"] } to its MCP servers configuration. See the AppMap MCP server reference. AppMap also includes its own chat, Navie, which answers questions from the same evidence without leaving the IDE (Navie command reference).

Requirements and Use

2025.1 and newer JetBrains IDEs are required to use this plugin.

AppMap works best* with the following:

  • Languages: Java, Kotlin, Python, Ruby, and Node.js (TypeScript and JavaScript). In alpha: .NET, React, Swift, and Go.
  • Frameworks: Spring, Django, Flask, Ruby on Rails, Nest.js, Next.js, and Express.

Looking for support for your language or stack? New languages appear first on our GitHub.

Refer to the AppMap documentation for the latest information on supported languages, frameworks, and versions.

[*] AppMap trace recording requires a language-specific library.

Get Started

  1. Install the AppMap Plugin from within the code editor or from the marketplace.

  2. Sign in using an email address to obtain a license key and activate AppMap. It's best to use your work email, so that your license can be easily associated with your organization subscription.

  3. Record your app by running your tests, or use the "Start with AppMap" menu item (docs).

  4. Connect your coding agent using the setup above.

Licensing and Security

Open source MIT license | Terms and conditions

To learn more about the security of AppMap, and how your data is used, see the AppMap security disclosure.

There is no fee for personal use of AppMap. Pricing for premium features and integrations is listed on AppMap's Pricing Page.

idea-plugin.name: Pieces
idea-plugin.description:
Pieces for Jetbrains

Pieces is an all-in-one productivity tool that gives developers complete contextual awareness of their workflow from browsers to Slack and other IDEs, no matter the source. Leverage the power of the Pieces Copilot, the Long-Term Memory Engine, and Pieces Drive—all directly within Jetbrains IDEs.

See the full documentation for more detail.

Enhanced AI Assistance

Pieces provides comprehensive AI-driven capabilities, enabling developers to:

  • Query cloud and local LLMs directly within Jetbrains IDEs
  • Generate context-aware code solutions and suggestions
  • Access Long-Term Memory across your workflows and apps
  • Explain and comment code intelligently to enhance readability
  • Troubleshoot and fix bugs efficiently with contextual insights

Integrated Management of Saved Materials

With Pieces Drive embedded in Jetbrains IDEs, developers can also save, edit, search, and share saved materials, boosting productivity by keeping reusable code accessible.

Pieces Copilot

Initiate a conversation with the LLM of your choice, providing as much context as needed by adding files, folders, or even entire repositories to the chat.

To initiate Copilot from the editor, select a portion of code, right-click, and hover over the Pieces item in the context menu.

  • Modify Selection with Copilot: Edit or transform the selected code to improve readability, optimize performance, or adapt it for other needs.

  • Explain Selection with Copilot: Get detailed explanations of the code’s functionality.

  • Comment Selection with Copilot: Generate inline comments to improve code clarity.

Quick Actions

Pieces can Comment or Explain your code inline with one click using Code Vision actions. Generate meaningful, insertable documentation explaining the purpose and function of your code, or get a breakdown of some code logic.

Pieces Drive

Pieces allows you to save materials such as code snippets into your Pieces Drive, and enriches them with AI-generated metadata, such as tags, titles, authorship details, and descriptions, keeping everything organized and accessible.

  • Save Current Selection to Pieces: Right-click a code block and save it to your repository with AI-enriched metadata, ensuring easy access to frequently used materials.

  • Save Active File to Pieces: Save the entire active file to your repository in one action—ideal for preserving larger scripts or complete files.

  • Ask Copilot About Selection: Start a conversation with Pieces Copilot to gain insights, explanations, or improvement suggestions for the selected code.

  • Ask Copilot About Active File: Analyze the active file with Pieces Copilot to get insights and recommendations for your codebase.

  • Share: Share materials with your team by creating distributable copies of reusable code.

  • Search Pieces: Quickly find specific materials in your repository using keywords, tags, or titles.

Connect with Pieces

Join our Discord

Become a part of our Discord community to stay updated and engage in discussions about our features.

Submit a Feature Request or Feedback

Have an idea for a new feature? Feel free to submit your suggestions on our GitHub support repo.

Tech Blogs

Stay connected and up-to-date with our latest blogs.

Plugins

Explore our collection of awesome Pieces plugins.

idea-plugin.name: Spectral
idea-plugin.description:
This plugin is a wrapper for the tool Spectral, a linter for OpenApi schemas.

Installation

  • Using IDE built-in plugin system:

    Settings/Preferences > Plugins > Marketplace > Search for "Spectral" > Install Plugin

  • Manually:

    Download the latest release and install it manually using Settings/Preferences > Plugins > ⚙️ > Install plugin from disk...

Since version 2 of this plugin it is required to have the spectral CLI installed on your system. If you don't have it installed yet make sure to follow this guide: Installing Spectral

Note: The CLI needs to be in your path and executable from the command line.

Features

Automatic linting

Automatic linting of your OpenApi specifications and highlighting in your editor

Configurable Ruleset

Specify your own ruleset in the plugins settings, under Preferences -> Tools -> Spectral -> Ruleset.

There you can specify a file on your local machine or just paste the URL of a ruleset available on the internet e.g.: Schwarz IT API linting rules.

Examples:

  • Link to a hosted ruleset: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SchwarzIT/api-linter-rules/main/spectral-api.yml
  • Local ruleset relative to Project base-path: .spectral.json
  • Fully-qualified path: /Users/user/.spectral.yaml

Configurable Included path patterns

Select the files that will be linted. By default, every file called "openapi.json", "openapi.yml" or "openapi.yaml" within the Project root will be matched for linting by the plugin when it's opened.

You can adjust this in the settings under Preferences -> Tools -> Spectral -> Included path patterns. All paths are relative to the project's root directory unless absolute.

Examples:

  • openapi.json: Matches the file called "openapi.json" inside the root directory of the project
  • components/**/*.yaml: Matches all files inside the project subdirectory "components" that end with ".yaml"
  • /Users/user/code/**/openapi*.yaml: Matches all YAML files within the absolute path "/Users/mick/code" that start with "openapi" and end with ".yaml"

Note: Each file must also be recognised by the IDE as a JSON or YAML file - that is with a suitable File Type association. If it is detected as a plain text (or any other type) it will be ignored.

idea-plugin.description:
It is used to improve coding efficiency.
Provide an ability to generate markdown Doc according to java interface method or controller method.
Features:
  1. Generate markdown Doc base on java interface method or controller method
  2. Generate Mockito or Powermock unit test templates
  3. Generate JSON sample data base on java class
  4. Generate constants field base on java field
  5. Automatically generate field comments according to the comments of field type
Other:
  • The template of the markdown Doc support custom configuration -->
    Preferences | Editor | File and Code Templates | Other | Roc Code

  • The sample data in the markdown Doc support to config the default value of field -->

Usage:
  1. Markdown Doc: open the interface or controller class,
    move the cursor to the method that needs to generate the document,
    and then right-click to select "Generate..." -> "Markdown Doc"
  2. Unit Test: open the class and right-click to select "Generate..." -> "Unit Test"
  3. JSON Sample Data: open the class and right-click to select "Generate..." -> "JSON"
  4. Constants Field: open the class and right-click to select "Generate..." -> "Constants Field"

idea-plugin.name: WireMocha
idea-plugin.description:
WireMocha is an IntelliJ-based plugin that provides integration for the WireMock framework and the ecosystem around it.

It offers various tools to generate and validate WireMock related test code, to provide additional contextual information in the following areas, and to interact with running WireMock servers (the list is not comprehensive):

  • JSON stub mapping files:
    • JSON schemas attached to stub mapping files for code completion and validation
    • Handlebars helpers: validation, code completion, navigation and more
    • Language injections in the JSON and Java DSLs
    • On-the-fly conversion of JSON stub mapping files to the Java DSL
    • Create, split and merge selected mapping objects and mapping files
    • Request-response summary of mapping files in the Project View
  • Java DSL:
    • JUnit 4 and JUnit 5 support
    • Testcontainers support
    • Handlebars and other language injections
  • Extensions:
    • Support for various WireMock extensions like grpc and faker
  • Admin API:
    • WireMock tool window with an Admin API client and a tool for Scenario generation
  • Other features:
    • Various WireMock-specific static code analysis checks
    • Other features for code generation, optimization, navigation and more

OSS attributions

This project derives some built-in documentation and specifications from the WireMock open source project. This content is licensed under the Apache License v2.

This project also uses provider descriptions from the Data Faker open source project. This content is licensed under the Apache License v2.

idea-plugin.name: EvoSuite(XenoAmess TPM)
idea-plugin.description:
IntelliJ plugin (XenoAmess TPM) for the EvoSuite tool, which is used to automatically generate high coverage JUnit tests. To generate test cases, EvoSuite uses advanced evolutionary algorithms enhanced by static analysis of the bytecode of the tested classes.

Note: this plugin is just used to call EvoSuite from inside IntelliJ IDEA, and so you still need to configure and install EvoSuite separately. You can do it automatically via its Maven plugin, or add the executable jar directly into your project.

Main features:
  • Generation of JUnit 4 tests for the selected classes
  • Optimization of different coverage criteria, like lines, branches, outputs, mutation testing, etc.
  • Tests are minimized: only the ones contributing to achieve coverage are retained
  • Generation of JUnit asserts to capture the current behavior of the tested classes
  • Tests run in a sandbox to prevent potentially dangerous operations
  • Virtual file system
  • Virtual network

For more information, see the documentation on www.evosuite.org

idea-plugin.name: mirrord
idea-plugin.description:
mirrord lets developers and AI coding agents run local processes inside a live Kubernetes cluster. Your code stays on your machine, but mirrord routes its traffic, files, and environment through a target pod in the cluster. Use it to read live cluster context while writing code (real env vars, real service responses, real queue contents), and to run the code against those same services and data once it's written. You get the feedback of a deploy in seconds, without the deploy, and without disrupting the cluster for anyone else.

This plugin brings that workflow to JetBrains IntelliJ. mirrord also ships as a VS Code extension and a CLI tool. Read more in the docs, or sign up to our newsletter to hear about new features. Both the core mirrord repository and this plugin's code can be found on GitHub.

How To Use

  • Click the mirrord icon in the Navigation Toolbar
  • Start debugging your project
  • Choose a pod to impersonate or choose to run in the "targetless" mode
  • The debugged process will be plugged into the selected pod or into the cluster environment by mirrord

Configuring mirrord for IntelliJ

mirrord allows for rich configuration of the environment it provides. The schema for it is documented here. The extension supports autocomplete for json files, but you can also use toml or yaml format.

Quick start: the easiest way to start configuring mirrord is to choose "Settings" from the dropdown menu, which will open a new mirrord.json.

idea-plugin.name: Test Automation
idea-plugin.description:
The Test Automation plugin helps develop and maintain automated UI tests.


Main features
  • Rich support of Selenium, Selenide, Playwright and Cypress frameworks
  • An embedded Web Inspector that provides an ability to generate unique CSS or XPath locators for the elements on a web page and add them to your code
  • Code completion for CSS and XPath locators
  • Highlighting and validation of XPath, CSS, and JavaScript in UI testing APIs for Java/Kotlin/Groovy/Python
  • Code completion for HTML tags, attributes, and CSS properties in tests
  • Project scaffolding with popular Selenium libraries
  • An ability to run Selenoid actions in browsers.json
  • Line markers and navigation to issue trackers and TMS cases for Allure Framework and Serenity BDD
  • Code completion and validation for Selenium Grid, Selenoid, and Allure Framework configuration files
  • Line markers with quick navigation to @Step usages in code
  • Find usages and code completion for @Feature, @Epic, @Story, @Owner, and @Lead usages in Allure Framework
  • Enhanced console output, including clickable file links and folded stack frames of frameworks

idea-plugin.name: ComTest Runner
idea-plugin.description:
This plugin adds simple support for generating unit tests using ComTest syntax.

Currently, the plugin supports the following languages and IDEs:

  • Java (IntelliJ IDEA) via JUnit 4
    • Generating tests for single files
    • Generating tests for packages
    • Full generate and run/debug support
  • C# (JetBrains Rider) via NUnit 3
    • Generating test projects for solution
  • comt snippet for generating doctest

Usage

IDEA

  • Running/debugging tests for a single file:
    • Right-click in the editor or the file and select ComTest | Run in Current File or ComTest | Debug in Current File.
    • You can also select Tools | ComTest | Generate and Run or Tools | ComTest | Generate and Debug from the top menu.
  • Running/debugging entire package:
    • Right-click the package folder in the project view and select ComTest | Run in Current Package or ComTest | Debug in Current Package.

Rider

  • Run Tests | ComTest: Generate Tests from Solution from the main menu.
  • Note that tests are not run automatically. To run all tests, use Tests | Run All Tests from Solution from the main menu.
idea-plugin.change-notes:

  • Rider: Generated NUnit test projects now reference NUnit 3.14.0, NUnit3TestAdapter 6.3.0 and Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 18.10.0, removing the vulnerable transitive Newtonsoft.Json 9.0.1 dependency (NU1903)

idea-plugin.name: Refact - Open-Source AI Agent, Code Generator & Chat
idea-plugin.description:
Refact.ai - Open-Source AI Software Engineering Agent

Refact runs with BYOK or local model providers that you configure on your machine.

Configure at least one provider in Provider Setup, choose default models, then use in-IDE chat, code completion, AI toolbox actions, and autonomous agent workflows directly from JetBrains IDEs.

  • Connect BYOK providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Groq, and xAI.
  • Use local runtimes such as Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, or custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
  • Integrate with GitHub, GitLab, PostgreSQL, MySQL, PDB, Docker, shell commands, MCP servers, and browser tools.

Use GitHub issues or discussions to ask questions, report bugs, or propose features.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• More efficient and faster code suggestion system
  • Enhanced performance for large codebases and extended AI sessions
  • New "Xperimental" settings section to access features in Beta
  • Stability & UI/UX improvements

idea-plugin.name: BitByte
idea-plugin.description:
This is a plugin integrating various small tools, which aims to simplify daily development and improve development efficiency through various small functions. Currently, the following functions have been provided, and other functions will be added later:
1. Enhanced copy function. It can copy the fully qualified class name of the current class, JSON Schema information, enumeration class description information, and JSON string of the current class (generated using the default value) in one click.
2. Simplify the creation of test classes. Support the rapid creation of test methods for the specified methods of the current class.
3. String processing. Quickly convert the currently selected string, support case conversion and naming method conversion.

idea-plugin.name: Gyro
idea-plugin.description: Gyro-Keep your native integration tests running all the time, like the ones started by @SpringBootTest. When you run Gyro Debug for the first time, you need to start the Spring container. When you run Gyro Debug again, Gyro will reuse the previously started Spring container. Installing the Jrebel hot deployment plug-in will automatically use the Jrebel hot deployment capability (if it does not take effect, you can configure the Jrebel agent path through Preferences->Tools->Gyro Settings); similarly, you can use it to warm up your other test tasks. If you encounter problems, please contact me by email

idea-plugin.name: JetClient - The Ultimate REST Client
idea-plugin.description:
JetClient is a REST (HTTP) client and API testing tool. It provides everything you need to design, test, and debug APIs effectively. With Git sync, it enables effortless collaboration and version management for your team. Key features include:

  • File Sync (Git Sync): Stores requests and folders in a human-readable format on your file system, enabling easy sharing and collaboration with your team via Git.
  • Environment Groups: Create environment groups to select multiple environments at once. For example, one group for (dev, test, prod) and another for (user, admin).
  • Convenient Variable Management: Variables are defined in JSON5 format and organized into two editors: shared (synced) and local (non-synced). Variables can include not only primitive types but also objects and arrays.
  • Powerful Scripting: Write pre-request and test scripts for requests and folders. Additionally, create test suite scripts that can reuse existing requests, eliminating the need to duplicate them.
  • CLI Test Runner: Run API tests from the command line or Docker for CI/CD pipelines. Supports multiple output formats (CLI, JSON, HTML, JUnit).
  • Enhanced Inline Expressions: Use {{...}} syntax to include variables, function calls, arithmetic operations, string concatenation, and more directly in your requests and scripts. Includes built-in functions for random data generation, user prompts, reading files, JavaScript code evaluation, running shell commands, and more.
  • Integration with Source Code and OpenAPI: Import APIs directly from your source code, and effortlessly navigate between requests and the corresponding code, and vice versa.
  • GraphQL Support: Integrates seamlessly with JetBrains' GraphQL plugin for syntax highlighting and code completion.


Most features are free, including File Sync (Git Sync), Environments, Variables, Scripting, etc. However, some features are available only in the paid version:

  • API Import: Import collections of requests from the source code.

  • Code Navigation: Navigate to the source code of the endpoint from the request editor and vice versa.

  • Advanced Inline Expression Functions: Use powerful built-in functions like $eval(jsCode) to execute JavaScript, $exec(command) to run shell commands, $readFileAsText(filePath) to read file contents, and $readFileAsBase64(filePath) to read files as Base64 strings, and user input functions like $textInput to collect data dynamically during execution.
    Supported imports:

  • OpenAPI (Swagger)

  • cURL

  • Postman

  • Spring

  • JAX-RS

  • Retrofit


Explore the capabilities of JetClient with the JetClient Demo Project.
Learn more in the JetClient Documentation.

idea-plugin.name: Qodo
idea-plugin.description:
The Qodo IDE plugin (formerly Qodo Gen) is being sunset. Switch to the Qodo Agentic Toolbox, the quality toolbox for your coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Kiro and more).

Qodo: Local Code Review

Shift code reviews left and commit with confidence.

Qodo brings review intelligence directly into your development environment with Local Code Review in the IDE.

  • Detect bugs, issues, and standard violations as you code
  • Resolve issues in 1-click
  • Generate tests for code changes

Table of Contents

  • What can Qodo do?
  • High precision, high recall code reviews
  • Agents: Modes and Workflows
  • Learn More
  • Support and Community
  • Data Sharing

What can Qodo do?

Qodo’s agents execute review workflows with shared multi-repo context and organization-specific rules to deliver precise, high-signal feedback and resolution.

With Qodo's AI-powered code reviews, you get instant feedback as you write:

  • Code changes analysis and explanation
  • Context-aware code suggestions
  • 1-click issue resolution
  • Test generation for code changes

High precision, high recall code reviews

Qodo delivers actionable, prioritized code suggestions to help developers push cleaner code, reduce review fatigue and improve overall code quality:

  • Multi-repo Codebase Context: Review code against the context of your full codebase to catch breaking changes, dependency conflicts, architecture-level issues and other hidden risks
  • Rules Customization & Enforcement: Embed your governance and security standards directly into every code review to ensure consistent, automated enforcement at scale.

Agents: Modes and Workflows

Modes

Modes are persona-driven AI agents for ongoing, context-aware conversations. They maintain state and can use MCP tools to help with multi-step tasks like code review, architecture planning, or iterative development.

Examples of Modes:

  • Ask Mode – Quick answers with minimal tool usage.
  • Code Mode – Full-featured coding assistant with access to all tools.
  • Plan Mode – High-level reasoning for design decisions and system planning.

Use Modes when you need a continuous AI partner while coding.

Workflows

Workflows are single-task AI agents that execute a defined process from start to finish. They are perfect for repeatable or automated tasks like:

  • Generating documentation
  • Running and fixing test suites
  • Performing code maintenance tasks

Workflows execute, deliver results, and end automatically.

Sharing and Reuse

Both Modes and Workflows can be:

  • Shared with your team as a .toml file
  • Uploaded into Qodo to instantly reuse someone else’s setup

This makes collaboration and standardization effortless across projects.

Support and Community

Need help? Join our Discord community!

Data Sharing

Similar to other popular generative-AI tools, we transmit code snippets to our servers. You can learn more in our terms of use and privacy policy.

You can opt out of sharing data with Qodo. For more information, visit our data sharing page.

2.2.0

Based on significant customer feedback, we’ve decided to continue focusing on and investing in our primary product: AI-powered code review and governance. Because of this, we will be reducing our focus on code generation, and we are writing to share some important updates regarding the Qodo IDE plugin.

Qodo is becoming a pre-PR review companion, helping developers catch issues earlier, reduce review churn, and merge higher-quality code with more confidence.

Why we’re making this shift

What we’re hearing is clear: AI speed without review creates risk and, in many cases, actually slows teams down due to regressions, rework, and noisy PR cycles. The biggest leverage isn’t producing more code; it’s merging better code. That’s where we believe Qodo can deliver a category-leading experience and measurable impact.

Timeline for the changes:

Free Users: Thursday, March 19, 2026, at 12:00 pm ET

Team Users: Tuesday, March 31, 2026, at 12:00 pm ET

The good news: Qodo is agnostic and integrates easily with the code generation tools your developers already use, so your team can keep generating code however they prefer, while Qodo automates review and remediation.

Here’s what you can expect:

  • Pre-PR reviews in the IDE: Qodo will review your work as you code, before you open a PR.
  • Scans uncommitted + committed changes: Qodo evaluates both what’s staged/committed and what’s still uncommitted on your branch to proactively detect potential issues.
  • One-click resolution workflow: With one click, you can address identified issues and resolve them with your preferred coding agent. Choose any CLI-based agent you have, and Qodo will automatically pass the remediation prompt to the agent so it can generate and apply the fix.
  • Free chat and code completion will be discontinued: The current free chat and code completion option will no longer be available.

idea-plugin.name: UI Surveyor
idea-plugin.description:
UI Surveyor plugin provides features helping designing selectors for mobile automated tests: They provide the following features:

  • Evaluating selectors against XML UI snapshots
    • UIAutomator UISelectors and BySelectors for Android
    • (Experimental) WebDriverAgent/Appium class chain and predicate queries for iOS
  • Syntax highlighting and autocomplete for element selectors (UIAutomator selectors in Java IDEs only)
  • Improved structure navigation for XML UI snapshots
    Note: When using with an old IDE or Kotlin plugin, navigation bar display might be broken - XML tag names displayed without any UI element identifiers or texts (e.g. just node instead of Button "ZERO"). This is a known issue that can be fixed by updating your Kotlin plugin and/or IDE (please see KTIJ-27484 for details).

If for some reason Locate Element tool window is not enabled, you can open it from the View menu:
