idea-plugin.name: Intercept Wave
idea-plugin.description:
Plugin Overview

Intercept Wave is an IntelliJ IDEA plugin for local development that combines request interception, mocking, and proxying in a workflow similar to Nginx and Charles. It can intercept HTTP requests and WebSocket (ws:// / wss://) messages, return custom mock data, or bridge traffic to an upstream service when you need real responses.

✨ Multi-Service Proxy

  • 📑 Tab-based Interface: Manage multiple proxy configuration groups in separate tabs
  • 🚀 Multiple Proxy Groups: Run multiple mock services simultaneously, each on its own port
  • 🏗️ Microservices Ready: Perfect for microservices architecture (e.g., user service on port 8888, order service on port 8889)
  • 🔄 Quick Switching: Easily switch and manage different service configurations via tabs
  • 🌍 Multi-Environment: Effortlessly manage dev, test, staging, and other environments

Core Capabilities

Smart Interception & Proxy:

  • 🎯 Configure path prefixes (for example, /api) to precisely target specific request paths
  • 🧭 Configure multiple HTTP routes inside one HTTP group, each with its own prefix, upstream target, strip-prefix rule, and Mock switch
  • 🔁 Rewrite route-local paths to nginx-like upstream paths, such as /backend/users -> /v1/users
  • 🔄 With Mock Config: Returns preset mock data for offline development
  • 🌐 Without Mock Config: Acts as a proxy server, forwarding requests with complete HTTP headers to get real data
  • 🔀 Smart path matching with prefix stripping support
  • 📡 WebSocket Mock & Bridge: Create WS groups that listen on local ws:// ports, optionally expose local wss:// with a PKCS#12 keystore, bridge to upstream ws:// / wss:// servers, and support both automatic and manual message pushing

Developer-Friendly Features:

  • 👥 Target Users: Frontend Engineers, QA Engineers, Full-Stack Developers
  • 🎨 Visual configuration UI, with optional direct editing of the project config file when needed
  • 💾 Persistent configuration with project-level isolation
  • 🌐 Automatic CORS handling
  • ⏱️ Network delay simulation support
  • 🔧 Custom response status codes and headers
  • 🍪 Global cookie support for authenticated APIs

Typical Use Cases

  1. Microservices Development: Mock multiple microservices simultaneously (user service, order service, payment service, etc.)
  2. Independent Frontend Development: Continue development with mock data when backend APIs are not ready
  3. API Testing: Quickly switch between different response data to test edge cases
  4. Multi-Environment Debugging: Configure and manage dev, test, staging environments at once
  5. Local Debugging: Use mock for some APIs while proxying others to test servers
  6. Network Simulation: Simulate slow networks or API timeout scenarios
  7. Cross-Origin Development: Automatically add CORS headers to solve frontend development CORS issues

Features Overview

Intercept Wave provides the following core functionalities:

  • API Interception: Intercept specific APIs and return configured mock data
  • Proxy Forwarding: Automatically forward unconfigured APIs to the original server
  • WebSocket Mock & Push: Start local WS mock/proxy services, forward to upstream ws:///wss:// endpoints, and define push rules (periodic/timeline) or send messages manually from the tool window.
  • CORS Support: Automatically add CORS headers to resolve cross-origin issues
  • Request Preservation: Preserve original request headers and User-Agent
  • Delay Simulation: Simulate network delays for testing slow network environments
  • Status Code Testing: Configure different status codes to test error handling logic
  • Prefix Filtering: Support prefix filtering to simplify API access paths
  • Global Cookie: Configure global cookies for APIs requiring authentication

Compatibility

Intercept Wave supports JetBrains IDEs based on the IntelliJ Platform 2023.1 and newer. The plugin is built against the 2023.1 platform baseline and emits Java 17 bytecode for compatibility with 2023.x IDE runtimes.

The plugin verification matrix covers 2023.1 baseline releases for CLion, DataGrip, DataSpell, GoLand, IntelliJ IDEA Community, IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate, PhpStorm, PyCharm Community, PyCharm Professional, Rider, RubyMine, and WebStorm.

SnapshotDB – see what really changed in your database

idea-plugin.name: Accessibility Compliance Helper Pro

Real-Time WCAG 2.2, Section 508 & ADA Compliance — Directly in Your IDE

Accessibility Compliance Helper Pro catches accessibility violations the moment you write them. Get instant, inline feedback for HTML, JSX, TSX, JavaScript, Vue, Svelte, Razor (.razor) and ASP.NET Razor views (.cshtml) — no external tools, no context switching, no surprises in production.

The only JetBrains plugin supporting WCAG 2.0/2.1/2.2 + Section 508 + ADA Title III + EN 301 549 + WCAG 3.0 Draft.

📈 NEW: Unified Project Audit — One Click, One Score

  • 0–100 health score with grade A–F — all nine auditors (Contrast, Labels, Landmarks, Headings, Alt Text, Links, Media, Page Metadata, Keyboard & Focus) in a single run
  • SARIF 2.1.0 export — findings annotate pull requests via GitHub Code Scanning / Azure DevOps
  • Self-contained HTML report with SVG score ring and per-category pass rates — share it with stakeholders
  • CI gate CLI — --fail-below=80 fails the build when the score drops; md / json / html / sarif outputs
  • CI/CD pipeline code generation — ready-to-use workflows for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, and Azure DevOps
  • Heading Structure Auditor — missing/multiple h1, skipped levels, empty headings (WCAG 1.3.1 / 2.4.6)
  • Alt Text Quality Auditor — file names as alt, placeholder words, redundant phrases (WCAG 1.1.1)
  • Link Purpose Auditor — empty links, "click here" text, raw URLs, href="#" pseudo-buttons, unannounced new windows, ambiguous duplicates (WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.5)
  • Media & Embeds Auditor — videos without captions, autoplay with sound, frames without title, objects without alternatives (WCAG 1.2.2 / 1.4.2 / 4.1.2)
  • Page Metadata Auditor — missing/invalid lang, missing <title>, zoom-blocking viewport, timed refresh, duplicate ids (WCAG 3.1.1 / 2.4.2 / 1.4.4 / 2.2.1)
  • Keyboard & Focus Auditor — positive tabindex, click-only custom controls, CSS that removes focus outlines without replacement (WCAG 2.1.1 / 2.4.3 / 2.4.7)

⚡ Real-Time Scanning

  • Continuous WCAG 2.2 analysis as you type — HTML, JSX, TSX, JavaScript, Vue, Svelte, Razor (.razor) and ASP.NET Razor views (.cshtml)
  • Severity-based highlighting: Error (Level A), Warning (AA), Info (AAA advisory)
  • Gutter icons for instant problem identification
  • Hover tooltips with violation details, WCAG success criteria references, and fix guidance

📋 40+ Checks in 10+ Categories

  • Images: alt text quality, decorative vs informative, SVG accessibility
  • Forms: label associations, fieldset/legend, error identification, autocomplete
  • ARIA: valid roles, required properties, forbidden patterns, live regions
  • Color Contrast: WCAG AA (4.5:1) and AAA (7:1) ratio checking
  • Keyboard: tab order, focus management, skip navigation
  • Navigation: heading hierarchy, landmark regions, page structure
  • Media: captions, audio descriptions, autoplay prevention
  • Links, Tables, Language and more

📊 5 Compliance Standards

  • WCAG 2.0/2.1/2.2 — 9 profiles (3 versions × 3 levels A/AA/AAA), 44+ success criteria
  • Section 508 (Revised 2018) — 36 CFR Part 1194, US Federal ICT mandate
  • ADA Title III (DOJ 2024 Rule) — 28 CFR Part 36, requires WCAG 2.1 AA
  • EN 301 549 V4 — EU Accessibility Act harmonized standard
  • WCAG 3.0 Draft — Cognitive accessibility, personalization (disabled by default)
  • Beautiful HTML reports with SVG score rings and per-criterion pass/fail tables
  • Non-authoritative language for legal protection

🔧 One-Click Quick Fixes

  • 15+ instant remediation templates for common violations
  • Framework-aware fixes for React, Vue 2/3, Angular, and Material-UI
  • Add missing alt text, form labels, ARIA roles, and lang attributes in one click

🔬 Testing & Simulation

  • Screen reader simulation — preview how assistive technology interprets your markup
  • Keyboard navigation testing with tab order visualization

📦 Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2024.2+ (build 242+) or any compatible JetBrains IDE
  • Java 17+

📞 Support

  • Documentation: Wiki
  • Issue Tracker: GitHub Issues
  • Email: support@jakubjirak.com

idea-plugin.name: Robot Framework Professional
idea-plugin.description:
Robot Framework — Full IDE Intelligence for Robot Framework

Turn your JetBrains IDE into a complete Robot Framework development environment: Robot Framework 7.4 syntax support, code completion, navigation, inspections with one-click migration fixes, a formatter, and test execution from the gutter.

Robot Framework 7.4 Syntax

  • GROUP blocks (RF 7.2) — highlighting, folding, completion, live template and END matching
  • Variable type conversion (RF 7.3) — ${amount: int}, @{ids: list[int]} and ${dir: Literal["UP", "DOWN"]} are highlighted, completed and validated
  • Secret variables (RF 7.4) — completion, live template and a check that rejects literal secrets
  • VAR statement (RF 7.0/7.1) — completion for every scope including SUITES
  • Inline IF, [Setup] on user keywords, -tag removal, WHILE limits (RF 7.0) — understood by the editor and the inspections
  • Migration help — one-click fixes for [Return], Force Tags, WITH NAME, singular section headers and the deprecated loop keywords

Editing and Navigation

  • Syntax Highlighting — Full support for Robot Framework 7.4 markers, typed variables, tags and sections
  • Code Completion — Context-aware suggestions for keywords, variables, and library imports
  • Go-To Declaration — Jump to keyword definitions and find references across files
  • Rename Refactoring — Safely rename keywords across all project files
  • Structure View — Browse test cases, keywords, and variables in a tree view
  • Code Folding — Collapse sections, test cases, and keywords

Code Quality

  • Code Formatter — One-shot reformat (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+R) that normalizes section headers, expands tabs to spaces, trims trailing whitespace, and tidies blank lines
  • Inspections — Detect long test names, empty test cases, undefined keywords, missing resources, duplicate test-case names, tab separators, trailing whitespace, leftover TODO/FIXME markers, and unused suite variables
  • Quick Fixes — Convert tabs to spaces and strip trailing whitespace with a single keystroke
  • Error Annotations — Syntax errors, undefined variables, and duplicate keywords highlighted inline
  • Spellchecking — Spell check support for Robot Framework files
  • Parameter Hints — Inline parameter hints for keyword arguments

Test Execution

  • Run from the gutter — Every test case gets a Run icon; one click executes just that test
  • Run configurations — Suite or directory, --test, --include/--exclude tags, --outputdir, extra arguments, interpreter and working directory
  • Run with DEBUG log — One action to re-run with --loglevel DEBUG when a failure needs the detail
  • Safe invocation — Robot is started as <interpreter> -m robot with an argument list, never through a shell

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, or compatible JetBrains IDE (2024.2+)
  • Python with Robot Framework installed (needed for test execution)

Support

  • Documentation: jakubjirak.com
  • Issues: GitHub
  • Email: support@jakubjirak.com
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.6.2 — Freemium Descriptor Restored

  • Reverts 2026.6.1. The freemium product-descriptor is back. It was removed on the mistaken assumption that it gated features — it never did: with optional="true" the licence is not checked and every feature is available to everyone, which is exactly the intended model. A monetized listing also requires the descriptor to be present

2026.6.0 — Real Test Execution

  • Test execution actually runs your tests. The previous run configuration ignored every setting and executed robot --version. It now builds a real command line: suite or directory, --test, --include/--exclude, --outputdir, extra arguments, interpreter and working directory, started as <interpreter> -m robot with an argument list so nothing passes through a shell
  • Run gutter icons — every test case and task gets a Run icon
  • Run from context — Run Test (Ctrl+Shift+F10) runs the test under the caret, or the whole suite; right-click and the project view work too
  • Run with DEBUG log (Ctrl+Shift+F9) — re-runs with --loglevel DEBUG
  • Generate Keyword now works — it takes the keyword call under the caret, creates the *** Keywords *** section when missing, and places the caret on the generated step
  • Suite settings are highlighted — Library, Test Tags, Suite Setup and friends were rendered as plain text
  • Variable types are visible — the RF 7.3 type annotation fell back to a colour the IntelliJ Light scheme leaves unstyled, so it looked identical to the variable name
  • Removed placeholder features — the "Interactive REPL" opened a message box, the "Web Inspector" and "Test Results" tool windows were static labels. They are gone rather than pretending; test output now goes to the normal run console

2026.5.0 — Robot Framework 7.4 Syntax

  • GROUP blocks (RF 7.2) — highlighting, folding, completion, live template and END matching
  • Variable type conversion (RF 7.3) — ${amount: int}, @{ids: list[int]} and ${mode: Literal["UP", "DOWN"]} are highlighted, completed and validated
  • Secret variables (RF 7.4) — completion, live template and an inspection that rejects literal secrets
  • VAR scopes (RF 7.0/7.1) — completion for LOCAL/TEST/TASK/SUITE/SUITES/GLOBAL plus a warning when a non-local VAR is created without a value (deprecated in RF 7.4)
  • Deprecated syntax inspection — [Return], Force Tags, WITH NAME, singular section headers, Exit For Loop and friends, FOR IN ZIP without mode=, literal -tag in Test Tags — each with a one-click fix where the migration is mechanical
  • Block structure inspection — unclosed IF/FOR/WHILE/TRY/GROUP and orphan END, with inline IF handled correctly
  • Fixed section header parsing — *** Settings *** and friends are now recognized as whole headers, which repairs highlighting, folding, structure view, completion and navigation
  • Tasks and Comments sections — *** Tasks *** behaves like Test Cases, and *** Comments *** content is greyed out as data Robot Framework ignores
  • Empty test case detection rewritten — now text-based and reliable, with a real "Add No Operation" fix
  • .txt files are no longer claimed — Robot Framework dropped the plain-text format, so the plugin now registers only .robot and .resource

2026.4.0 — Code Quality & Formatting

  • Robot file formatter — Reformat a suite with Ctrl+Alt+Shift+R: canonical section headers, tabs → spaces, trimmed trailing whitespace, and normalized blank lines (idempotent)
  • New inspections — Duplicate test-case name, tab separator, trailing whitespace, unresolved TODO/FIXME markers, and unused suite variables
  • Quick fixes — Convert tabs to spaces and remove trailing whitespace
  • Formatter settings — Configure indent size and header normalization under Settings → Tools → Robot Framework

2026.3.6 — Freemium Model

  • Freemium licensing — Added product-descriptor for JetBrains Marketplace freemium model (code: PROBOTFRAMEWORK)

idea-plugin.name: CenterTest
idea-plugin.description: Provides integration with AnkrPt CenterTest automated testing for Guidewire implementations.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
3.9.1

  • Run Recorder: when an update cannot be downloaded or verified (for example while a new release is being published, or offline), the installed Recorder starts anyway, with a warning. Previously nothing started.
  • Run Recorder: updates keep a ct-recorder.json placed next to the Recorder (for example the policy that locks it to Edge). Previously every update deleted it.
  • Run Recorder: if the Recorder stops right after starting (no Chrome or Edge installed, an invalid policy file), the notification shows what it reported, instead of saying its window is about to open.
  • Run Recorder refuses a published release older than the one installed, even when correctly signed, so a replayed old release cannot downgrade it.
  • Clicking Run Recorder, Run Data Studio or Run Dashboard again while it is still downloading no longer corrupts the download; the second click is ignored with a message.
  • Run Recorder on Linux, where no Recorder build exists, says so instead of reporting an IDE internal error. Expected download and verification failures no longer raise IDE internal errors either.

3.9.0

  • New: Run Recorder replaces the Recording to Test menu. It downloads CenterTest Recorder, the standalone tool for recording a session in a Guidewire application, and starts it; the recorder opens its own browser window and control panel. Recordings are saved to the recorder's usual folder (Documents/CenterTest Recordings).
  • Every Recorder download is verified before it runs: the release manifest must carry a valid Ed25519 signature from the Recorder's own key, built into the plugin, and the archive must match the checksum in that manifest. A download that cannot be verified is discarded and never run.
  • The plugin keeps the Recorder up to date, checking for a newer build each time you start it. A Recorder that is already running is never stopped for an update, as that would end the recording in progress; the update is installed the next time you start it.
  • Removed: Generate Test and Generate Snippet from a Selenium IDE recording.

3.8.1

  • Fixed: Generate Test did nothing with a Selenium IDE recording. It started CenterTest with a run mode CenterTest no longer recognizes, so no test was generated. It now uses the Selenium recorder mode and generates the test again.
  • Fixed: Generate Snippet left the recording path's quote open, so the options after it were read as part of the path. A path with spaces now works.

3.8.0

  • Data Studio's published files have been renamed to CenterTest-DataStudio-<platform>, so a file downloaded from the release page names the product it belongs to. The plugin now recognises both the new name and the old one.
  • This matters for copies you already have installed. Data Studio updates itself by writing each new build over its own file rather than renaming it, so a copy installed before the rename keeps its original filename for good. The plugin accepts either name, so an existing installation keeps working and is not re-downloaded.
  • Downloads resolve the same way: the plugin asks for the new name first and falls back to the old one, so it works whether or not the renamed release has shipped yet.
  • The Dashboard is unaffected. It was not renamed, and its launches make exactly the same requests as before.

3.7.0

  • Data Studio downloads are now verified before they are launched. The plugin checks the release manifest's Ed25519 signature against a key built into the plugin, and the archive against the checksum inside that signed manifest. A download that cannot be verified is discarded and never run.
  • Previously the integrity check was skipped whenever the publisher had not put a checksum next to the archive — which meant anyone able to remove that file could also remove the check. It is no longer optional for Data Studio.
  • Fixed: a redirect on a checksum or manifest request could send the plugin to another server. Responses that arrive from anywhere other than the release host are now refused.
  • Requires Data Studio 3.51 or newer, which is the first release to publish a signed manifest.

3.6.6

  • Data Studio now manages its own updates. Previously the plugin and Data Studio both checked for new builds, so a build the plugin had just installed could be replaced by the app moments later, and clicking Run Data Studio while it was already running could stop it mid-session to apply an update. The plugin now installs Data Studio once and leaves the version to the app: if it is already running, Run Data Studio simply opens it in your browser. The Dashboard is unaffected — the plugin still checks for and installs new Dashboard builds on every launch.

3.6.5

  • CenterTest run configurations now tell the launched test process whether it was started with Run or Debug: Run adds -Dcentertest.ide.run=true -Dcentertest.ide.debug=false and Debug adds -Dcentertest.ide.run=false -Dcentertest.ide.debug=true. The flags are also written into the configuration's VM options, so they are visible in Edit Configurations and update to match the mode each time you launch.

3.6.4

  • Fixed: double-clicking a property override file in the Properties tab (e.g. right after adding a new one) could throw a "write thread only" error instead of opening the file. The plugin refreshed the file system on the UI thread, which the IDE no longer allows; that refresh now runs in the background and the file opens as expected.

3.6.3

  • Fixed: Run Data Studio / Run Dashboard now pick up a newly published build even when the app is already running. Previously, if the app was up, clicking Run just reopened the browser and never checked S3, so the update was silently missed. The plugin now checks for a newer build first; when one is found it stops the running instance, downloads the new build, and relaunches it. If it is already current, it simply reopens the browser as before.

3.6.2

  • Fixed: Data Studio and the Dashboard could freeze mid-request. We started them with their output piped to the IDE and never read it, so once the pipe buffer filled the app blocked on its next write — the browser was left waiting forever, with no error anywhere (this is what made Data Studio's Browse button appear dead). Their output is now discarded and their input detached.

3.6.1

  • Fixed: a failed update check no longer blocks the first install. The plugin now downloads the build anyway and, if the server refuses, reports what it actually said (e.g. "no CenterTest Data Studio build is published for windows-x64") instead of blaming your connection
  • Run Data Studio now hands Data Studio the project you launched it from, so it opens on that project's test data instead of an empty "No project selected" screen

3.6.0

  • New Run Data Studio action — detects your OS/architecture, downloads the matching CenterTest Data Studio build, and launches it; Data Studio opens in your browser at http://localhost:60000
  • Run Dashboard and Run Data Studio now check for a newer published build before launching, and download it automatically — you no longer have to clear the cache by hand to get an update. If the download server cannot be reached, the cached build is launched as before

3.5.1

  • Run Dashboard now reuses an already-running dashboard — clicking it again reopens http://localhost:50000 in your browser instead of starting a second instance on a different port

3.5

  • New Run Dashboard action — detects your OS/architecture, downloads the matching CenterTest Dashboard build (cached after the first run), and launches it; the dashboard opens in your browser at http://localhost:50000

3.4

  • New Generate Helper & Data action — regenerates the typed Helper/Data classes locally into the open project, with no publish or dependency refresh (requires CenterTest 6.05+)

3.0.0

  • Added Environments tab for managing test execution environments
  • New Clear Sessions action for cleaning up Kimputing sessions
  • New Refresh License action for updating license information
  • Improved EDT compliance and memory leak fixes
  • Enhanced plugin stability and performance

2.3.0

  • New way to create template tests using File > New ...

2.2.4

  • Synchronize Analytics task added
  • Shorten command added to missing configurations

2.2.2

  • Build task before launch added
  • Shorten command added by default

2.2.0

This update breaks pre-existing Run Configurations. Please clear and re-add the AnkrPt Gradle and AnkrPt Run configurations so they pick up the new changes!

  • Changes to Run Configuration
  • DDT Generator
  • Minor fixes

2.0.0

  • New and improved AnkrPt, new and improved plugin!
  • Added tool window functionality to make modifying and accessing override files easier.

idea-plugin.name: Pprof Plus: Visual Analytics
idea-plugin.description:
A powerful performance analysis plugin that brings go tool pprof directly into your IDE. Visualize, analyze, and optimize your Go applications without leaving GoLand or IntelliJ IDEA.

🚀 Pprof Plus - 让 Go 性能分析变得简单

一款强大的性能分析插件，将 go tool pprof 直接集成到您的 IDE 中。 无需离开 GoLand 或 IntelliJ IDEA，即可可视化、分析和优化您的 Go 应用程序。



✨ 核心功能

  • 🎯 智能运行配置 - 一键性能分析，支持多种采集模式（运行时、HTTP、手动、插桩）
  • 📊 丰富的可视化 - 7 种可视化类型，包括交互式 Web UI、火焰图、调用图等
  • 🔍 代码导航 - 从性能数据直接跳转到源代码，支持内嵌提示和热力图可视化
  • 🛠️ 集成工具窗口 - 直接在 IDE 中查看分析结果
  • ⚡ 多种分析类型 - 支持 CPU、内存、协程、阻塞、互斥锁和内存分配分析


🎨 特色亮点

  • 内嵌提示 - 在代码编辑器中直接显示性能指标（flat/cum）
  • 热力图 - Top 20 函数的可视化矩形树图，颜色标识热点
  • 右键菜单 - 右键点击任意 pprof 文件即可立即可视化
  • 自动打开结果 - 性能分析完成后自动打开可视化结果


🚀 快速开始

  1. 创建一个新的 pprof 运行配置

idea-plugin.name: RestPilot - REST Client & Postman Alternative
idea-plugin.description:
The Ultimate REST Client for IntelliJ IDEA

RestPilot is a powerful, developer-first HTTP client designed to replace Postman entirely within your IDE. Stop context-switching between windows! Debug your Spring Boot APIs, execute requests, and stress-test your endpoints directly next to your code.


Why use RestPilot?

As a developer, you shouldn't need to leave IntelliJ IDEA to test your APIs. RestPilot scans your local Spring Boot project, detects all @RestController endpoints, and lets you call them with a single click. It is fully compatible with Postman scripts, making migration effortless.


✨ Key Features

  • 🚀 Postman Alternative: Import your Postman Collections and Environments directly. Supports pre-request and test scripts (JavaScript).
  • ⚡️ Spring Boot Integration: Automatically scans and lists all @RequestMapping, @GetMapping, @PostMapping URLs in a sidebar tree view.
  • 🔥 Blast Mode HUD: A built-in mini load testing tool with a real-time, terminal-style performance dashboard (RPS, Latency, Success/Fail).
  • 🧘 Zen Mode: Immersive, minimalist UI mode for distraction-free API debugging.
  • 🌐 Smart Proxy: One-click toggle between IDEA global proxy and direct connection (Bypass) for seamless internal/external API testing.
  • 💻 cURL Support: Import cURL commands from your browser or terminal, and Export requests as cURL strings.
  • 🛠 Powerful Editor: Real-time bidirectional sync between URL and Params table. Support for Multipart/Form-data, JSON highlighting, and Dynamic variables ($uuid).
  • 🔒 Auth Support: Built-in support for OAuth 2.0, Bearer Token, Basic Auth, API Keys, Firebase FCM, and Apple APNs.
  • 🔥 Firebase Cloud Messaging: Send FCM HTTP v1 notification and data messages with service accounts protected by IntelliJ PasswordSafe.
  • 🍎 Apple Push Notifications: Build alert and background device pushes over HTTP/2 with local ES256 signing and .p8 keys protected by IntelliJ PasswordSafe.

Keywords: REST Client, Postman, HTTP Request, API Debugger, Spring Boot, Swagger, cURL, Insomnia, Integration Testing, Load Testing, OAuth 2.0.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
v1.7.1 - Variables Reach the Wire ⏱️

  • 🔗 Params Variables Fixed: URL paths and Query Params now resolve values such as {{accessToken}} and Pre-request-generated {{dynamicFrom}} before the request is sent.
  • ⏱️ Dynamic Timestamps Fixed: Postman values such as {{$isoTimestamp}} now resolve before URL encoding, with safe handling for an accidental extra closing brace.
  • 🔐 Encoding Without Surprises: Resolved query values are encoded exactly once, preserving tokens containing characters such as +, /, and =.

v1.7.0 - Postman Sandbox, Unlocked 🧪

  • 🔄 Script Sub-requests: pm.sendRequest and legacy sendRequest now support callbacks, Promise chains, request configs, auth, URL-encoded bodies, and multipart form data.
  • 🧪 Scripts Behave Like Postman: Added real pm.test/pm.expect assertions, mutable pm.request, scoped variables, cookies, response helpers, metadata, and common legacy globals.
  • 📦 Collection-level Automation: Collection and folder scripts and variables now import, persist, export, and execute in the correct inherited order.
  • 🛡️ Reliable by Design: Script network calls run off the UI thread, compatibility errors are actionable, and the regression suite covers the complete sandbox and request pipeline.

v1.6.0 - Push Center Goes Apple 🍎

  • 🍎 Native APNs: Build alert and background pushes with live payload previews, typed custom data, and precise Apple headers.
  • 🔐 Keys Stay Yours: Apple .p8 keys live only in IntelliJ PasswordSafe; short-lived ES256 provider tokens are signed locally.
  • ⚡ HTTP/2, Done Right: Dedicated secure transport, Sandbox/Production guardrails, payload limits, and actionable APNs diagnostics.

v1.5.1 - FCM, Dialed In ⚡

  • 🚀 No More Endless Sends: New FCM requests start with a visible, fully editable 30-second timeout.
  • 🌐 Proxy Clarity: OAuth timeouts now lead straight to the IDE proxy settings with actionable diagnostics.
  • 🛑 Clean Cancel: Cancelling an in-flight request instantly restores the Send button.

v1.5.0 - Firebase Cloud Messaging

  • 🔥 FCM HTTP v1: Create and send notification or data messages to a Firebase Installation ID (FID), device token, topic, or condition without leaving IntelliJ.
  • 🔐 Secure Service Accounts: Firebase service account JSON credentials stay in IntelliJ PasswordSafe; saved requests and exports contain no private keys.
  • ♻️ Automatic OAuth: Short-lived access tokens are generated and refreshed in the background with actionable FCM error diagnostics.

v1.4.1.3 - Save Workflow Polish

  • 📁 Create collections and folders directly from the Save Request dialog with a compact native UI.

v1.4.1.2 - Import & UI Fixes

  • 📦 Fixed ZIP selection and improved Postman/OpenAPI ZIP import reliability.
  • 🎨 Restored the compact New Request button in the Workspace header.

v1.4.1 - ZIP Import & Export

  • 📦 ZIP Import: Import Postman collections and OpenAPI/Swagger specs from .zip files. Both the Import Postman and Import OpenAPI dialogs now accept ZIP archives.
  • 📤 ZIP Export: Export All Collections now produces a clean collections/ structured ZIP archive that can be round-tripped back via Import Postman.
  • 🔬 Postman Codec Refactor: Extracted a dedicated PostmanCollectionCodec for consistent collection serialization, supporting descriptions, pre-request/test scripts, and all auth types on both import and export.
  • 🐛 Fix: API Key authentication location (Header vs Query) is now correctly preserved on export. Previously it was always written as Query regardless of the original setting.
  • 🎨 Improved New Request Button: The Workspace header's New Request button is now a compact icon-only toolbar action with native hover, focus, theme, and keyboard states.
  • 📝 Description Preservation: Postman collection and item descriptions are now imported and exported correctly.

v1.4.0 - Workflow & Reliability

  • 🌐 Configurable API Base URLs: Define a project default host and optional module-specific overrides for discovered Spring endpoints.
  • 🔎 Resolved Request Inspector: Inspect the exact URL, headers, body, multipart fields, and timeout sent after variables and authentication are applied.
  • 🛡️ Safe Request Editing: Modified requests are marked with an asterisk, preview tabs pin automatically, and closing offers Save, Discard, or Cancel.
  • 🔗 Reliable URL / Params Sync: Query encoding, duplicate parameters, empty values, API keys, and URL fragments now stay consistent between the editor and the request sent.
  • ↩️ Collection Undo: Undo deletes, drag-and-drop moves, cut/paste moves, and reorder actions with Ctrl+Z.
  • 📊 Clearer Response Feedback: Status, duration, payload size, header/cookie counts, and script output are easier to scan.
  • ⌨️ Keyboard Workflow: Added shortcuts for focusing the URL, sending, cancelling, saving, and Save As. Generate Code now uses a native submenu.
  • 🐛 Reliability Fixes: Prevented stale cancelled responses from overwriting newer requests, preserved History timeouts, and cleaned up requests, Blast tasks, editors, and animation timers correctly.

v1.3.3

  • ⏱️ Request Timeout: Set a per-request timeout (0-300s) next to the Send button.
  • 📋 Generate Code: Now includes cURL, Python requests, JavaScript fetch, Java, and Kotlin. The old "Copy as cURL" button is merged into this menu.
  • 📜 Postman Script Import: Pre-request and Test scripts are now imported from Postman collections.

v1.3.1

  • 🌐 Import OpenAPI from URL: You can now import Swagger/OpenAPI specs directly from a URL — no need to download the file first.
  • 🐛 Fix: Environment variables set via scripts (pm.environment.set) now persist correctly across requests. Previously they were lost after the request completed.

v1.3.0 - The "Swagger & ES6" Update 🚀

  • 📥 OpenAPI/Swagger Import: Import Swagger 2.0 / OpenAPI 3.x specs (JSON & YAML). Supports external $ref, server variables, and auto-generates extract rules from response schemas.
  • 🟢 ES6 JavaScript: Pre-request & Test scripts now support const, let, arrow functions, and template literals.
  • ✅ pm.test(), pm.request, pm.response metrics: Richer Postman-compatible scripting API.
  • 🐛 Bug Fixes: Fixed all known issues — circular $ref StackOverflow, URL copy-paste whitespace errors, script error line numbers, Nashorn engine compatibility, and more.

v1.2.9 - The "Postman Scripts" Update 🤝

  • 🧩 Postman pm API: Pre-request and Test scripts now support Postman-compatible pm API — use pm.environment.get/set, pm.variables, and pm.response (code, body, headers, text(), json()) just like in Postman.
  • 🔧 Nashorn Engine Fixed: JavaScript script engine now loads reliably by bypassing IntelliJ's ServiceLoader classloader isolation. Pre-request and Test scripts no longer fallback to Groovy or report "JavaScript engine not found".
  • 🐛 Bug Fix: Fixed pm.response.headers returning null due to HTTP multi-value header type mismatch.

🙏 Special thanks to Ming Tseng Chang for reporting the JavaScript engine issue.


v1.2.8 - The "Postman-First" Export Update 📬

  • 📤 Full Postman v2.1 Export: Collections now export with complete URL decomposition (protocol, host, path, port, query, hash, variables) so every request shows its full URL when opened in Postman.
  • 🔐 Auth Exported: Bearer Token, Basic Auth, API Key, and OAuth 2.0 settings are now correctly exported to Postman format.
  • 📜 Scripts Exported: Pre-request and Test scripts are now exported as Postman-compatible event blocks.
  • 📋 All Body Types Exported: Form-urlencoded and Multipart/Form-data bodies are now exported with proper structured format (urlencoded/formdata), not just raw.
  • 📥 Import Improvements: Standard v2.1 imports now handle urlencoded/formdata bodies, URL query params, and auth configuration. Standalone Postman Environment files are now recognized on import.
  • 🐛 Bug Fixes: Fixed trailing # in exported URLs, fixed triple-slash for path-only URLs, fixed wrong protocol for variable hosts like {{base_url}}.

v1.2.7 - The "Drag & Drop" Update 🎯

  • 🖱️ Drag & Drop Collections: Rearrange and reorganize your saved requests and folders by simply dragging them anywhere in the Collections tree.
  • 📂 Smart Drop Zones: Drop on a folder to nest inside, drop between items to reorder, or hover over collapsed folders for auto-expand.
  • 🛡️ Circular Protection: Smart guards prevent you from accidentally dropping a folder into itself or its own children.

v1.2.6 - The "Smart Auto-Recovery" Update 🛠️

  • ✨ Interactive Console Magic: Network errors now intelligently detect proxy interference.
  • 🚀 1-Click Proxy Bypass: Click the new [Action: Retry without Proxy] link in the error terminal to instantly bypass the proxy and resend your request.

v1.2.3 - The "Blast HUD Overhaul" Update 📈

  • ✨ Silky Smooth RPS Chart: Added a pure, anti-aliased real-time line chart to the Blast Dashboard for visual throughput tracking.
  • 📊 Advanced Latency Metrics: Blast Dashboard now calculates and displays strict P90 and P99 latency distribution metrics.
  • 🎨 Visual Tuning: Resolved rendering artifacts for a cleaner "Zen" data visualization experience.

idea-plugin.name: Ru BizGen - Russian Test Data Generator
idea-plugin.description:
Russian test data generator for IntelliJ IDEA and all JetBrains IDEs. Generate INN, OGRN, KPP, SNILS, BIK, SWIFT, IBAN, bank accounts, card numbers, passports, full names, addresses and phone numbers — with valid checksums, right in the editor. Also available as an MCP server for AI agents.

Генератор российских тестовых данных прямо в редакторе. ИНН, ОГРН, КПП, СНИЛС, БИК, SWIFT, IBAN, расчётные счета, номера карт, паспорта, ФИО, адреса и телефоны — с корректными контрольными суммами, без копирования из сторонних сервисов.

Плагин зависит только от ядра платформы, поэтому работает во всех IDE на IntelliJ Platform: IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, WebStorm, PhpStorm, RubyMine, CLion, Rider, DataGrip, DataSpell, RustRover, Android Studio.

⚠️ Важно:

Любые совпадения с реальными конфиденциальными данными (ИНН, номера счетов, наименования организаций, ОГРН, ОКТМО, СНИЛС, номера телефонов и другие) являются случайными и не предназначены для использования в реальных системах. Тестовые данные генерируются внутри плагина — без обращений к внешним сервисам.

Основные возможности:

  • 🚀 Быстрая генерация реалистичных тестовых данных
  • ⌨️ Горячие клавиши (по умолчанию Ctrl+Alt+E, можно переназначить)
  • 🎛️ Гибкие настройки генераторов (порядок, включение/отключение, переименование)
  • 💬 Символ обрамления при вставке в редактор (двойные кавычки, одинарные, без обрамления)
  • 🔔 Настраиваемые уведомления о срабатывании генераторов
  • 👀 Предпросмотр результата перед вставкой
  • 📋 Интеграция с Alt+Ins — доступен в стандартном диалоге генерации кода IntelliJ
  • 🔄 Без сброса настроек генераторов при обновлениях — порядок, активность и пользовательские имена генераторов сохраняются автоматически

Доступные генераторы:

  • 💰 Банковские реквизиты: расчётный счёт (RUB, CNY), корреспондентский счёт, БИК, SWIFT (российских банков), IBAN (РФ и Турция)
  • 👤 Физическое лицо: ФИО (полное, сокращённое, инициалы), ИНН, номер банковской карты, номер телефона, СНИЛС, паспорт РФ (с пробелом и без), загранпаспорт РФ (номер и MRZ)
  • 🏢 Юридические данные: ИНН, ОГРН (ИП и ЮЛ), ОКТМО (8 и 11 цифр), КПП
  • 🏛️ Название организации: на русском и английском языке
  • 📍 Геоданные: страна и адрес в реалистичных форматах
  • 🔢 Прочее: UUID

🤖 MCP-сервер

Помимо плагина, доступен отдельный MCP-сервер (Model Context Protocol), который предоставляет аналогичный функционал генераторов и может быть развёрнут локально или в Docker. MCP-сервер позволяет использовать генераторы Ru BizGen в любых MCP-совместимых клиентах (IDE, AI-ассистенты, CI-инструменты).

Возможности MCP-сервера:

  • 🔧 5 категорийных инструментов — ru-bizgen_generator_<category> с параметром type (enum) и count для пакетной генерации
  • 🌐 Streamable HTTP транспорт на базе Ktor/Netty
  • 🐳 Docker-ready — multi-stage сборка, порт 8081
  • 🩺 Health endpoint /health для мониторинга
  • 🔒 Локальная генерация — без обращений к внешним сервисам
  • 🔁 Единый реестр генераторов с ядром ru-bizgen-core

Подробнее о настройке и запуске — в репозитории проекта: раздел ru-bizgen-mcp.

Как использовать:

Вызовите окно генератора с помощью горячей клавиши или через меню IDE — выберите нужный тип данных и вставьте результат прямо в код.

Способы вызова:

  • Ctrl+Alt+E (Windows/Linux) или ⌘⌥E (Mac)
  • Alt+Ins → Ru BizGen
  • Shift+Shift → Ru BizGen

Горячие клавиши можно изменить в настройках IDE.

Расширенные настройки:

Настройки → Tools → Ru BizGen

Управление генераторами

  • ✔️ Включение и отключение генераторов
  • ⬆️⬇️ Изменение порядка генераторов
  • ✏️ Переименование генераторов
  • 🔄 Сброс к настройкам по умолчанию

Уведомления и предпросмотр

  • 🔔 Выбор способа уведомления
  • 👀 Предпросмотр результата генерации
  • 💬 Символ обрамления при вставке
  • 📋 Быстрое тестирование генераторов

Преимущества плагина:

  • ⏱️ Экономия времени — генерация данных за секунды
  • 🧩 Гибкость — настройка под конкретные задачи
  • 💻 Удобство — работа прямо в редакторе
  • 🛠️ Для разработчиков — создан разработчиком для разработчиков

Keywords: test data generator, russian test data, fake data, faker, mock data, random data generator, dummy data, test fixtures, INN, OGRN, OGRNIP, KPP, SNILS, OKTMO, BIK, SWIFT, IBAN, bank account, card number, passport, MRZ, full name, address, phone number generator, checksum, developer tools, productivity, testing, QA, MCP server, Model Context Protocol, AI agent tools.
Ключевые слова: генератор тестовых данных, тестовые данные, российские тестовые данные, генератор ИНН, генератор СНИЛС, генератор ОГРН, генератор КПП, генератор БИК, генератор расчётного счёта, генератор ИБАН, генератор ФИО, генератор адреса, генератор телефона, фейковые данные, мок-данные, фикстуры, контрольная сумма.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.12 - 06-09-2026

🚀 Новое

  • Реализован MCP-сервер (ru-bizgen-mcp) — генераторы Ru BizGen теперь доступны вне IntelliJ IDEA через Model Context Protocol (Streamable HTTP, Ktor/Netty). Поддерживается подключение к MCP-клиентам (Cursor, Claude Desktop, Cline и др.). 5 категорийных инструментов ru-bizgen_generator_<category> с параметрами type (enum — генератор внутри категории) и count (до 1000 значений за вызов). Сервер запускается локально, данные генерируются без обращений к внешним сервисам
  • Добавлен Dockerfile и docker-compose.yml для контейнерного запуска MCP-сервера
  • Добавлен healthcheck-эндпоинт GET /health ({"status":"UP"}) для мониторинга MCP-сервера
  • Добавлен генератор паспорта РФ (с пробелом) — серия с реальными кодами регионов ОКАТО + номер
  • Добавлен генератор паспорта РФ (без пробела) — компактный формат
  • Добавлен генератор загранпаспорта РФ (номер) — 9 цифр, серия 70/71
  • Добавлен генератор загранпаспорта РФ (MRZ) — машинно-читаемая зона по стандарту ICAO 9303 (TD-3)
  • Добавлен настраиваемый символ обрамления для вставки в редактор (двойная кавычка, одинарная кавычка, без обрамления)
  • Добавлена возможность переименования генераторов в настройках плагина
  • В Dokka Guides добавлены интерактивные презентации: ArchUnit и Gradle

🛠 Исправлено

  • Расчётный счёт (RUB/CNY) — контрольный разряд теперь рассчитывается по Положению ЦБ РФ № 515 через AccountKeyAlgorithm (ранее был захардкожен как 0)
  • Корреспондентский счёт — переход на единый алгоритм AccountKeyAlgorithm (ранее использовался упрощённый алгоритм с весовыми коэффициентами, не учитывающий РКЦ)
  • IBAN РФ — исправлена структура BBAN: 29 цифр формируются как 5 (суффикс БИК) + 4 (филиал) + 20 (счёт). Ранее структура содержала некорректные контрольные цифры и признак счёта, что могло приводить к невалидным IBAN
  • ОГРН ЮЛ — исправлена контрольная сумма: mod 11 вместо mod 13 (контрольные алгоритмы ЮЛ и ИП были перепутаны)
  • ОГРН ИП — исправлена контрольная сумма: mod 13 вместо mod 11
  • ОГРН (ЮЛ и ИП) — код региона теперь выбирается случайно (ранее был захардкожен как 61 — Самарская область)
  • СНИЛС — исправлен диапазон генерируемых цифр: 0..9 вместо 1..9 (первая цифра могла быть только 1)
  • ИНН — код региона теперь может принимать значение 99 (верхняя граница диапазона была исключающей)
  • MCP — категорийные тулы объявляют outputSchema, а structuredContent возвращается для любого успешного вызова, включая count = 1 (раньше при одном значении структурированный результат отсутствовал, что расходилось со спецификацией MCP). В structuredContent поле partial присутствует всегда
  • MCP — русскоязычные логи сервера больше не искажаются в консоли Windows: в installDist проставляется -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8

📣 Витрина Marketplace

  • Плагин переименован в Ru BizGen - Russian Test Data Generator. Прежнее имя не содержало ни одного слова, по которому плагин ищут: по запросу bizgen в Marketplace ровно один результат, а по test data (295 результатов) плагин стоял на ~51 месте. Имя — основной сигнал ранжирования на витрине
  • Описание на витрине переписано: первые строки (из них Marketplace формирует превью в выдаче) теперь на английском и несут поисковые слова — test data generator, INN, OGRN, SNILS, BIK, IBAN, SWIFT, MCP server
  • В описание добавлен явный список IDE, в которых работает плагин: он зависит только от com.intellij.modules.platform, но из текста это не следовало
  • Блок про MCP-сервер поднят выше блока «Преимущества» и упомянут в первом абзаце: на витрине (версия 1.11) второго форм-фактора не было видно вовсе
  • Расширен блок ключевых слов — добавлены русскоязычные запросы
  • Из текстов убрана привязка к одной IDE. Плагин объявляет только com.intellij.modules.platform, и Marketplace считает его совместимым с 16 продуктами платформы, но README, бейдж версии и описание говорили «плагин для IntelliJ IDEA» — аудитория PyCharm, GoLand, DataGrip, Rider и остальных не понимала, что плагин ей подходит
  • Добавлена политика конфиденциальности — русская и английская версии. Поле Privacy Policy на витрине пустовало; документ фиксирует проверенное: генерация локальная, сетевых вызовов и телеметрии нет, на диск пишется только bizgen_plugin_settings.xml с вашими настройками, MCP-сервер по умолчанию слушает 127.0.0.1:8081

⚙️ Технические изменения

  • Обновлены зависимости:
    • Kotlin 2.3.0 → 2.4.0
    • IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.16.0 → 2.18.1
    • Kotest 6.1.2 → 6.2.1
    • Kover 0.9.8 → 0.9.9
    • ArchUnit 1.5.0
    • Kodein DI 7.33.0, kotlinx-coroutines 1.11.0 (integration-тесты)
  • Добавлены MCP Kotlin SDK 0.15.0 и Ktor 3.5.1 (для модуля ru-bizgen-mcp)
  • Реализован composite build build-logic с convention plugins (kotlin, testing, dokka, dokka-root, kover)
  • Добавлен модуль ru-bizgen-archunit: исполняемые границы модулей, слои core, naming Generator↔Benchmark (вместо прежней валидации бенчмарков в perf)
  • Добавлены UI integration-тесты на базе JetBrains IDE Starter + Driver SDK (source set integrationTest/); покрыты popup генераторов, настройки, уведомления, буфер, символ обрамления, переименование и сброс
  • Задача integrationTest отвязана от check — UI-тесты не входят в обычный CI и запускаются ночью через ci-integration.yml
  • Расширены тесты генераторов: добавлены проверки контрольных сумм для счёта, IBAN, ИНН и ОГРН
  • Из отчёта покрытия Kover исключены классы source set integrationTest — они компилируются вместе с плагином и учитывались как непокрытый продакшен-код; исправлено и имя исключаемого UI-пакета
  • Убрана недекларированная зависимость на Gson из IntelliJ Platform: глубокое копирование настроек переведено на XmlSerializer платформы — тот же механизм, которым настройки уже персистятся
  • Kotlin stdlib больше не упаковывается в плагин: его предоставляет IntelliJ Platform. Размер артефакта уменьшился с 2,03 МБ до 0,30 МБ, снят риск конфликта загрузчиков на будущих версиях IDE

idea-plugin.name: ReqRun
idea-plugin.description:
ReqRun

ReqRun is a minimal HTTP client for IntelliJ IDEA Community Edition that runs .http requests directly from the editor.

GitHub | Marketplace | Issues

Key Features

  • Run request blocks with gutter icons or Ctrl+Alt+R
  • Run selections, entire files, or folders of requests
  • Inline toolbar for templates, environments, and cURL import/export
  • Variables via @name = value and placeholders {{var}}
  • Built-ins: {{$timestamp}}, {{$uuid}}, {{$randomInt}}
  • Response viewer with history in the service tool window

Install

  • IDE: Settings > Plugins > search for ReqRun > Install > Restart the IDE
  • Manual: download from Marketplace and install from disk

Docs

  • Quickstart
  • Request format
  • Environments
  • Response viewer

Screenshots

  • Disabled the .NET Assembly Analyzer in Dependency-Check because this plugin does not ship .NET assemblies.

Fixed

idea-plugin.name: AsyncTest Caller
idea-plugin.description:
AsyncTest Caller

AsyncTest Caller is an IntelliJ IDEA plugin designed to scan Spring Web projects and automatically extract API endpoint information.

The plugin analyzes Spring MVC / Spring Boot controllers, collects structured interface metadata (such as paths, HTTP methods, and related models), and synchronizes this data to the AsyncTest platform in a well-organized, structured format.

By automating API discovery and synchronization, AsyncTest Caller helps keep your AsyncTest interface definitions consistent, up-to-date, and tightly aligned with your source code, reducing manual maintenance and integration errors.

Key Features

  • 🔍 Scan Spring Web / Spring Boot controller interfaces
  • 🧩 Build structured API and data model information
  • 🔄 Synchronize interface data with the AsyncTest platform
  • ⚡ Improve consistency between backend code and test definitions

AsyncTest Caller is ideal for teams that want to bridge the gap between Spring-based backend services and AsyncTest, enabling efficient API management and automated test integration.

Compatibility & Supported Versions

AsyncTest Caller is engineered to ensure broad compatibility across the JetBrains ecosystem. It is compiled with Java 17 compatibility to support older IDE versions while remaining fully functional on the latest releases.

  • Minimum Requirement: IntelliJ IDEA 2021.2.1 (Build 212+)
  • Maximum Requirement: None (Supports 2022.x, 2023.x, 2024.x, and future releases)
  • Verified Versions: The plugin has been verified against:
    • IntelliJ IDEA 2022.3
    • IntelliJ IDEA 2023.1
    • IntelliJ IDEA 2024.1+

Whether you are maintaining legacy projects on an older IDE or using the cutting-edge EAP version, AsyncTest Caller has you covered.


Privacy Policy

Last Updated: December 23, 2025

By using the AsyncTest Caller plugin, you verify that you agree to the following terms regarding data collection and usage.

1. Data Collection & Transmission

  • Source Code Scanning: The plugin scans your project files locally to identify API definitions (e.g., Spring Controllers).
  • Data Upload: When you explicitly click "Upload" or "Sync", API metadata is transmitted to the AsyncTest server.
  • Destination: Data is sent only to the server URL you configured in Settings > Tools > AsyncTest Caller.

2. User Control

  • No background uploads occur without your explicit action or configuration.
  • You have full control over the server URL and Access Token.

3. Data Usage

The transmitted data is used solely to generate test cases and sync API definitions on the AsyncTest platform.

For more details, please contact us via our Docs (https://docs.asynctest.com/ast_caller/start.html) page.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
v1.0.1 - Annotation Resolution & OpenAPI Enhancement

🚀 This release significantly improves annotation discovery, inheritance handling, and documentation export capabilities.

What’s New & Improved:

  • Application Root Detection: The plugin now locates the project root by searching for Java classes annotated with @SpringBootApplication.
  • Class-Level Mapping Inheritance: @RequestMapping annotations on interfaces and abstract classes are now correctly resolved for implementing classes.
  • Controller Registration Rules: @Controller (and related stereotypes) must be declared on the concrete implementation class and are no longer inherited implicitly.
  • Method-Level Mapping Inheritance: Method annotations such as @RequestMapping and @PostMapping can now be discovered from interfaces and abstract parent classes.
  • Parameter Annotation Inheritance: Method parameter annotations (e.g. @RequestBody, @RequestParam) are now inherited through interfaces and abstract method definitions.
  • ToolWindow Stability Improvements: Tree loading in the panel is now lazy and fault-tolerant. If endpoints are not found initially, users can refresh manually. Helpful hints are shown when compilation is required.
  • Multi-Source Documentation Support: Added support for Swagger annotations, OpenAPI 3 annotations, and Javadoc comments via a responsibility-chain mechanism with intelligent merging.
  • Nested Structure Refactor: Internal logic for handling nested API structures has been reorganized and simplified.
  • Specification Export: Exporting API definitions to OpenAPI and Swagger formats is now supported.

idea-plugin.name: Karate Debug
idea-plugin.description:
A powerful debugger for Karate API tests. Set breakpoints directly in your .feature files, step through scenarios including Java and JavaScript code, inspect variables, and run tests with a single click.

Features

  • Breakpoint Debugging for Karate, Java, and JavaScript - Debug Karate, Java, and JavaScript code in the same session. Set breakpoints in .feature, .java, and .js files. Step through your tests line by line.
  • Hot Reload Variables - Modify variable values on-the-fly while paused at a breakpoint. Right-click any variable in the Variables panel and set a new value.
  • Match Diagnostics - See pass/fail highlights on match statements with actual values inline. One-click fixes to update expected values from actual results.
  • One-Click Test Execution - Gutter icons appear next to every Feature and Scenario, letting you debug with a single click.
  • Feature Explorer - Browse all your Karate features and scenarios in the Karate tool window. Navigate your test suite at a glance and run any test directly.
  • Environment Switching - Quickly switch between environments (dev, qa, stage, or custom) from the status bar. Your selection persists across sessions.
  • Syntax Highlighting - Full syntax highlighting for the Karate DSL, including Gherkin keywords, JSON/XML payloads, JavaScript expressions, and embedded variables.
  • File Navigation - Clickable file references throughout your feature files. Ctrl+Click to navigate to classpath: files, read() targets, and @tag references.
  • Log Breakpoints - Pause execution when specific strings appear in log output. Useful for catching exceptions or error messages without setting traditional breakpoints.
  • Log Filtering - Hide noisy log output by configuring exclude patterns. Filter out verbose framework messages to focus on what matters.
  • Conditional Breakpoints - Set conditions on breakpoints using JavaScript expressions.

Configuration

Configure the plugin via Settings > Tools > Karate Debug:

  • Environments - List of available Karate environments (comma-separated)
  • Default Environment - Environment used when starting a debug session
  • Log Level - Log level for Karate Debug output (error, warn, info, debug, trace)
  • Match Diagnostics - Show passing/failing highlights and actual values
  • Log Filter - Comma-separated strings to hide from log output
  • Log Breakpoints - Comma-separated strings that pause execution when found in logs

Step Filtering (Java Debugging)

Control which code is shown when stepping through Java code:

  • Show JDK Classes - Step into JDK core classes (java.*, javax.*, jdk.*, sun.*, com.sun.*)
  • Show Karate Framework - Step into Karate framework classes (com.intuit.karate.*)
  • Show Karate Dependencies - Step into Karate's third-party dependencies (jsonpath, netty, slf4j, etc.)

When unchecked (default), stepping into framework code will automatically step out and return to user code.

Getting Started

  1. Open a project containing Karate tests
  2. Open a .feature file
  3. Set breakpoints by clicking in the gutter
  4. Click the debug icon in the gutter or use the Karate tool window

Requirements

  • Java 17+ (Java 21 recommended)
  • Maven or Gradle project with Karate dependencies

Early Access Program (EAP)

Want to try new features before they're released? Join our EAP channel:

  1. Go to Settings > Plugins > ⚙ (gear icon) > Manage Plugin Repositories
  2. Click + and add: https://plugins.jetbrains.com/plugins/eap/list
  3. EAP versions will now appear in the plugin updates

EAP versions may contain experimental features and are updated more frequently.

Resources

  • Website - Documentation and getting started guides
  • Report a Bug
  • Request a Feature
  • Contact Us
  • License - End User License Agreement

idea-plugin.name: BetterPy
idea-plugin.description:
BetterPy supercharges your Python development in PyCharm and IntelliJ-based IDEs — so you can spend less time on boilerplate and more time building.

BetterPy was created out of a personal need to improve my daily workflow. I had been using PyCharm for more than 8 years and found myself constantly repeating the same actions, which were time-consuming and frustrating. I wanted to streamline my workflow and make development more efficient. First, I went to the issue tracker to report what I found. Later, I found that my priorities did not always align with the PyCharm product manager's roadmap. I decided to take matters into my own hands and started working on BetterPy to address the issues I encountered.

My main goals are to:

  • Automate repeated actions that otherwise take too much clicking around.
  • Fix annoying behavior and smooth out workflow friction.
  • Extend PyCharm based on personal and practical development needs.

The areas of PyCharm I am adressing with the plugin are naturally aligned with the scope of my development activites, which are API backend development, domain-driven design and automated testing.

📖 Documentation: chbndrhnns.github.io/pycharm-plugin-betterpy

Features

Parameter & Argument

  • Make parameter mandatory - Converts an optional parameter to a required one by removing the default value
  • Make parameter optional - Converts a required parameter to an optional one with a default value

Code Structure

  • Change visibility - Toggles a Python symbol between public and private naming
  • Copy method annotations from parent - Copies type annotations from a parent method to its overrides
  • Dict access conversion (PY-54845) - Converts between dict bracket access and .get() method calls
  • Strip signature type annotations - Removes type annotations from a function signature
  • Toggle enum member value - Toggles enum member references with their literal values

Pytest

  • Convert pytest.param - Converts between different pytest parameter formats
  • Create pytest fixtures from parameters - Offers a quick fix to generate pytest fixtures for unresolved fixture parameters
  • Fixture Editor Integration (PY-87756, PY-81495, PY-60973, PY-57812, PY-63269, PY-61634, PY-89790, PY-49850, PY-59721, PY-53176, PY-61040, PY-88555, PY-60421, PY-56256, PY-72784, PY-60706, PY-85667, PY-71639, PY-71288, PY-63898, PY-61869, PY-61671, PY-57752, PY-57363, PY-56163, PY-54421) - Enables fixture navigation, completion, definition searches, find usages, rename, and override support in the editor
  • Fixture Injection Intentions (PY-55931) - Intentions for converting between fixture parameters and @pytest.mark.usefixtures
  • Jump to pytest node in test tree - Navigates to the corresponding node in the test tree view
  • Mock assertion methods (PY-11786) - Resolves unittest.mock assertion methods without enabling broader mock type inference
  • Mock type provider - Provides type information for unittest.mock objects
  • New pytest members - Adds Generate menu actions for new pytest tests and fixtures
  • Parametrize pytest test (PY-31542, PY-33483, PY-48610, PY-73660) - Adds, removes, completes, and maintains pytest.mark.parametrize parameters
  • Pull Up pytest fixture (PY-63189) - Move a pytest fixture one level higher in the conftest hierarchy to widen its availability
  • Push Down pytest fixture (PY-56186) - Move or copy a pytest fixture into narrower test modules, classes, or child conftest scopes
  • Pytest collection-pattern IDE integration - Keeps editor run actions aligned with pytest collection patterns
  • Pytest fixture documentation (PY-66245, PY-57315, PY-71347) - Enhances Quick Documentation and member type inference for pytest fixtures across files
  • Pytest hooks (PY-70762) - Generates pytest hook stubs where pytest discovers them and adds navigation and F1 documentation
  • Pytest parametrized case run gutter icon (PY-88558, PY-46650, PY-38868) - Shows run gutter icons for individual pytest parametrized cases when each case is on its own line
  • Pytest plugin references - Provides navigation, rename, and unresolved-reference inspection support for pytest_plugins module strings
  • Run pytest with debug logging - Duplicates the selected pytest run configuration with debug logging flags for the chosen test tree node
  • Surround with pytest.raises() - Wraps a statement with pytest.raises() in test contexts
  • Toggle pytest skip (PY-56066) - Adds or removes @pytest.mark.skip decorator from a test
  • Toggle pytest skip from test tree - Adds or removes @pytest.mark.skip from the test tree context menu
  • Use actual test outcome - Replaces assertion expected values with the actual value from the last failed test run

Inspections

  • @pytest.mark.usefixtures on fixture is a no-op inspection (PY-64332) - Reports @pytest.mark.usefixtures decorators on fixture functions, where they have no effect — pytest only honours usefixtures on test functions
  • Constant should be Final inspection - Reports module-level constants that should be annotated with Final
  • Fixture annotation mismatch inspection - Reports test or fixture parameters whose explicit type annotation is incompatible with the value type provided by the resolved fixture
  • Missing pytest test directory - Highlights configured pytest testpaths that do not exist and offers to create them
  • Missing |None annotation inspection (PY-88504) - Adds a quickfix for PyCharm's missing | None annotation inspection
  • Mock unresolved reference inspection - Reports unresolved references in mock usage
  • Overridden method missing type annotations inspection - Reports overrides missing type annotations present in parent methods
  • Private module import inspection - Reports private-module imports that should use public package exports
  • Pytest failed line inspection (PY-32337, PY-61067) - Marks the line where a pytest test failed
  • Pytest fixture direct import inspection - Reports pytest fixture functions imported directly into conftest.py — prefer pytest_plugins for explicit scoping
  • Pytest fixture override contract inspection - Reports fixture overrides whose produced value type is incompatible with the parent fixture
  • Pytest fixture redundant parameter inspection - Reports fixture parameters that are already injected automatically via autouse, usefixtures on the enclosing class, or module-level pytestmark, and are not referenced in the function body.
  • Pytest fixture scope inspection (PY-63194, PY-61197) - Reports fixtures that narrow the scope compared to parent fixtures
  • Pytest fixture to usefixtures inspection (PY-55931) - Reports unused setup-only fixture parameters in test functions and offers conversion to @pytest.mark.usefixtures()
  • Pytest fixture uninjected reference inspection (PY-71966, PY-89003, PY-43656) - Reports fixture references inside tests/fixtures that are not declared as parameters
  • Pytest missing assert inspection (PY-57064) - Reports pytest tests that have no Python assert statement or explicitly return a value, including asserts reached through project helper calls
  • Pytest parametrize count mismatch inspection (PY-30323, PY-49892) - Reports when the number of values in a pytest.mark.parametrize value set does not match the number of parameter names
  • Pytest parametrize ids count inspection - Reports when the number of ids in a pytest.mark.parametrize call does not match the number of parameter sets
  • Pytest parametrize unexpected keyword inspection - Reports unsupported keyword arguments passed to pytest.mark.parametrize
  • Pytest parametrize unused argname inspection - Reports pytest.parametrize argnames that are never used inside the test function body
  • Pytest redundant fixture import inspection (PY-63189) - Reports explicitly imported pytest fixtures that are already auto-discoverable via conftest or plugins.
  • pytest_plugins in non-root conftest inspection - Reports pytest_plugins assignments that appear in a non-root conftest.py file, where they have no effect
  • request.param without params inspection - Reports pytest fixtures that read request.param but declare no params= and are not the target of any indirect parametrization
  • Shadowing stdlib module inspection (PY-23615, PY-43957) - Reports project modules that shadow Python standard library modules
  • Unknown dynamic pytest fixture inspection (PY-54420) - Reports string-based fixture requests (usefixtures, getfixturevalue, indirect parametrize) that do not resolve to any visible fixture
  • Unnecessary inspection suppressions (PY-45308) - Detects redundant inspection IDs in Python noinspection comments and removes them safely.
  • Unused pytest fixture inspection - Reports pytest fixture functions that are never used as a parameter in any test or other fixture in the project, and offers a safe-delete quick fix

Actions

  • Copy pytest node ID from editor (PY-49998) - Copies the pytest node ID for the test at the caret position
  • Copy pytest node IDs (PY-57904) - Copies pytest node IDs for selected tests to the clipboard
  • Copy with imports (PY-62801) - Copies selected Python code together with the import statements referenced by that selection
  • Extract function to scope (PY-2701, PY-47806) - Extracts selected Python code into a named function in a containing scope
  • Generate class actions - Adds Generate menu actions for test classes, dataclasses, frozen dataclasses, and pydantic models
  • Inline bare tuple return - Inline a function with one bare tuple return while preserving grouping and avoiding a synthetic result variable
  • Parameter object refactoring (PY-59270) - Enables introduce/inline parameter object refactoring actions
  • Top-level extract function (PY-40840, PY-44636, PY-73852) - Extracts top-level Python statements into a function with parameters and explicit return values instead of globals
  • UV script runner & debugger (PY-88510) - Runs and debugs uv project script entry points from pyproject.toml

Completion & References

  • Mock patch object attribute completion - Completes attributes for mock.patch.object targets
  • Mock string references - Navigates mock.patch targets on older IDEs and standalone patch calls, plus pytest-mock spy names
  • NewType/TypeVar/ParamSpec reference & rename (PY-82966, PY-53658) - Adds references for NewType/TypeVar/ParamSpec name literals, keeps the name string in sync on rename, and repairs manual NewType drift
  • Pytest identifier in Search Everywhere (PY-57148) - Includes pytest identifiers in Search Everywhere results
  • Pytest mark completion (PY-57354) - Completes @pytest.mark. decorators with built-in, config, and plugin markers

Import & Structure

  • Export symbol to target - Exports a symbol to a specified target module's __all__

Navigation

  • Class implementations code vision (PY-56627) - Shows an inline code vision hint above each Python class with the number of implementations (subclasses) and lets you navigate to them
  • Module assignment usages code vision - Shows an inline code vision hint above each module-level assignment with the number of project-scope usages and lets you navigate to them
  • Property usages code vision - Shows an inline code vision hint above each Python property with the number of project-scope usages and lets you navigate to them
  • Return path highlighting - Highlights explicit return statements when the caret is on a function return annotation

Filters & Suppressors

  • Suppress missing docstrings on overloads (PY-56267) - Suppresses PyCharm's missing docstring inspection for typing overload signatures.
  • Usage filtering (PY-56092) - Adds Find Usages filters for type annotations and test-source references

Documentation

  • Attribute Docstring in Quick Documentation (PY-63878, PY-60571) - Retired attribute docstring rendering now provided natively by PyCharm.
  • Docstring Example Rendering (PY-47744) - Renders doctests and fenced Python examples in Quick Documentation docstrings.
  • Inherited Attribute Documentation - Shows an ancestor attribute's docstring when an overriding class attribute has no local documentation.

IDE Customizations

  • Enhance Structure View - Master switch for BetterPy structure-view filters, overload hiding, and pytest-specific icons.
  • Enhanced Go to Implementation presentation (PY-82520) - Prepends class name to method name in Go to Implementation popup when names are identical
  • Filter private members - Adds a filter to hide private members in the structure view
  • Hide overloads - Hides typing overload signatures from the structure view while keeping the implementation visible.
  • Icons for pytest tests and fixtures (PY-60483) - Renders tests, fixtures, and normal functions with distinct icons in the structure view. Filters to show/hide tests and fixtures are added when viewing a test file.
  • Message console filter (PY-55937) - Filters and formats Python messages in the console
  • Python navigation bar (PY-53757) - Enables enhanced Python navigation bar with module path display
  • Structural Search Profile (Python) (PY-15003) - Adds a Python Structural Search profile integration for pattern matching and constraints
  • Test/Production editor tabs - Keeps test and production files in separate editor splits with configurable alignment

Coming Soon

I'm actively working on the next wave of BetterPy. Without spoiling the surprise:

  • More intentions around typing and annotations — less ceremony, more signal.
  • Smarter Protocol and custom-type workflows — extracting, introducing, and reshaping types without the usual back-and-forth.
  • Better handling of unions, generics, and type aliases — because typing shouldn't feel like a second job.
  • Tighter feedback loops for type-checker findings — fewer detours between "problem spotted" and "problem fixed".
  • New tools for test authoring and maintenance.
  • Expanded AI / MCP integrations for workflows that go beyond a single file.
  • Quality-of-life upgrades to features already available.

Configuration

Every feature can be individually toggled in Settings → Tools → BetterPy.

Pricing

BetterPy is free during an extended beta period.

I plan to offer a paid version in the future, probably using a freemium approach. The details are yet to be determined and also shaped by feedback I am able to collect.

Personal Motivation
idea-plugin.change-notes:
BetterPy adds Extract Function to Scope as an incubating refactoring to extract Python expressions or statements into functions, classes, or modules, adds a status-bar toggle for contextual feature tips, and improves mock assertions and type inference.

🚀 Features

  • Extract Function to Scope extracts selected expressions or statements into a named helper in the current function, an enclosing function, or the module.
  • Contextual feature tips can now be enabled or disabled directly from the BetterPy status-bar menu.
  • Mock assertion methods now resolve assert_called_once and async await assertions on methods spied with mocker.spy(instance, "method").
  • Report unexpected arguments for autospecced patch.object methods.
  • Class-based mock specs now validate method-call and recorded-call assertion arguments by default, without requiring autospec=True. Turn off Validate arguments when spec is a class in Mock type provider settings or use the contextual class-spec tip to disable the additional checks; autospec validation remains active.

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Fixed false missing-argument warnings on method assertions for instances created from autospecced class patches.
  • Keep Python collection type rendering compatible with IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2.3.
  • Python navigation bar breadcrumbs render overload declarations by name instead of raw PyFunction(...) text, while member lists still hide duplicate overloads.
  • Autospecced decorator assertions now preserve class and bound-instance receiver arguments without shifting type diagnostics onto the mock assertion qualifier.
  • monkeypatch.setattr(module, "name", value) now resolves module-level imports, including aliases, instead of reporting false unresolved references. Missing symbols remain errors.
  • mocker.spy(receiver, "method") now resolves subscription receivers whose types require cross-file inference, avoiding false unresolved method-name strings. Missing methods remain errors.
  • Mock side-effect compatibility now checks keyword values forwarded through **kwargs, recognizes the final definition of redefined callbacks, and ignores constant-false spec/spec_set values
  • Fixture parameter typing now prioritizes BetterPy's resolved fixture value, so local overrides retain their type when a plugin provides the same fixture name.
  • Autouse fixture consumer analysis now restores functions from the current PSI file provider during nested reference searches, preventing invalid-PSI errors while processing conftest.py.
  • Plugin fixture styling now follows the effective provider; local overrides no longer inherit the plugin color.
  • Fixture rename no longer invokes text-occurrence methods that are unresolved on affected PyCharm 2026.3 builds.
  • Fixture Quick Documentation now includes return-class docstrings when the fixture has no docstring and preserves docstrings for methods accessed through fixture arguments.
  • Quick Documentation on a fixture receiver in a member access keeps the fixture's documentation instead of switching to the enclosing method.
  • “Copied from” notices in fixture Quick Documentation now link to the source class.
  • Test/Production editor tabs now uses the full editor area for diffs and restores duplicate tabs, pins, and editor state on return.
  • Navigation across test/production editor splits now preserves the target caret and centers the destination; Search Everywhere navigation continues to use the intended split.
  • New pytest fixture previews no longer open a nested write command while generating the fixture.
  • Pytest missing assert inspection now recognises standard unittest.mock assertion calls on pytest fixture values.
  • Change visibility is no longer offered on assignments in a method's own scope; declarations and nested class-scope assignments remain available.
  • Autospecced patch.object call assertions now validate arguments against the patched method signature instead of exposing NonCallableMock's unbound Self parameter.
  • Autospecced patch.object decorator parameters and context-manager aliases now check assertion arguments, retaining explicit receivers for class targets and bound signatures for instance targets. Stacked patch decorators map mocks before trailing pytest fixture parameters.
  • @patch("package.Class", autospec=True) now exposes mock helpers on instances constructed through the patched module binding; previously imported class aliases remain bound to the original class.
  • Class-based spec_set signatures now take precedence over spec, recorded-call checks recognize Mock subclasses, and method return-value children no longer inherit the original class's method signatures.
  • Mock inference and assertion helpers for patch.object now apply only while the patch is active and, for instance patches, only to the patched receiver.
  • Mock string references make mocker.spy(instance, "method") names navigable and rename-aware, and retain standalone mock.patch references on newer IDEs without duplicating native ones.

idea-plugin.name: Enkidu Linkage Doctor
idea-plugin.description: Enkidu catches runtime linkage failures early before they reach production.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • ServiceLoader / SPI validation: detects broken META-INF/services/* entries (missing service/provider, type mismatch, non-instantiable providers) and flags packaging overwrite/merge risks.
  • Duplicate-class impact analysis: compares winner vs shadowed copies using bytecode hash + public ABI shape; highlights dangerous shadowing vs benign identical duplicates.
  • MRJAR-aware class/service/module-info resolution (effective runtime view) with runtimeJavaFeature override.
  • Repro bundle output for enkidu doctor via --bundle (zip or directory) including ordered classpath.txt, targets.txt, and bundle.json.
  • Jar scan cache keyed by SHA-256 for fast repeat scans on large classpaths.
  • Parallel jar indexing with bounded concurrency.
  • Streaming target analysis with bounded in-flight work to reduce memory pressure.
  • CLI performance knobs: jar parallelism, target parallelism, in-flight limits, optional cache directory.
  • continueOnError best-effort mode with deterministic warnings and execution context reporting.
  • Extended evidence in JSON / SARIF / HTML / IntelliJ reports to include SPI and duplicate-risk details.

Improved

  • More resilient handling of unreadable jars, manifests, and invalid bytecode; surfaced as structured warnings.

Fixed

  • JarIndex winner selection now strictly follows classpath order across directories and jars.
  • Artifacts v1 JSON deserialization is now forward-compatible (unknown fields ignored).

idea-plugin.description:
3TG – Behavior-First Test Generation for TypeScript & React

3TG – Behavior-First Test Generation for TypeScript & React

AI-powered TypeScript test generation and React test automation directly inside IntelliJ.

3TG is a behavior-first IntelliJ test generation extension for TypeScript unit testing, React component testing, and scalable fullstack test automation.

Instead of generating empty Jest or Vitest templates, 3TG analyzes your exported TypeScript functions and React functional components and generates structured, scenario-aligned test foundations — helping you ship faster while improving test quality and consistency.

Built by Coding Creed Technologies.
Designed for teams building production-grade TypeScript and React applications.

🚀 Why Developers Use 3TG

Writing unit tests in TypeScript and React projects is often:

  • ⚠️ Repetitive boilerplate work
