idea-plugin.name: Testin
idea-plugin.description:
Testin brings test case management into the IDE. Design test cases, run them, and report on the results in the same window as the code they cover.

Everything is stored as plain files in a folder you choose — readable, diffable, and versioned with Git if you want them to be. There is no server to run, no account to create, and no data leaves the machine.

Design
  • Test project tree. Test projects, test sets, packages and test runs in a sidebar tree, with create, rename, copy, cut, paste, drag and drop, and undo — the operations a file tree already taught your hands.
  • Test case editor. Description, steps, expected result, priority, groups, module, preconditions, reference and test data. Search, filter and paging keep a large suite navigable, and every attribute can be switched off the view when it is not the one you are working on.
  • Spreadsheet grid. The same test cases as a table: multi-cell selection, copy and paste with Excel in both directions, rows that size themselves to their content, and column widths that survive a refresh.
  • Bulk editing. Descriptions, steps, expected results, groups and more, changed across a whole selection in one dialog.
  • Details panel. The full test case beside the list, including who created it and when.
Execute
  • Test runs. Choose test cases into a cycle and record what happened: Passed, Failed or Blocked, with an actual result, bug severity and bug priority on a failure, and per-test-case durations timed for you. Test cases a test run never reached are marked Untested when it closes, and a test case deleted after it was executed keeps the result it earned, marked Removed.
  • Automation (with the Java and TestNG plugins). Generate packages, classes and methods from your test cases, run them by class or by method, and move between a test case and its code from a gutter icon or a click on the card.
Share
  • Reports. Execution reports as HTML, PDF, Word or Excel, with the pass rate, a table per status, and the test run's real execution times.
  • Import and export. Excel, CSV and JSON in and out, plus HTML on the way out. Mapped column by column, with a preview before anything is written.
  • Git (with the Git plugin). A review dialog listing every pending change — test cases field by field, test runs, and the markers that make a folder a test set — then commit and push from the same place. Clone a shared test project, sync with a rebase, revert a single changed field, and switch branches from the panel.
Compatibility
  • IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, Rider, GoLand, WebStorm and other IntelliJ-based IDEs, build 262 and later.
  • Test management works in all of them. Java code generation, TestNG execution and the Git features appear when those plugins are installed, and are absent rather than broken when they are not.
Privacy
  • No telemetry, no accounts, no analytics. Testin talks to the Git remote you configure yourself; when you press Report Bug, to the GitHub repository your own testin.yml names, through the gh sign-in already on your machine; and, when you have connected an AI agent and press Automate Test Case, to that agent's own command line on your machine, carrying one test case and nothing else. Testin keeps no API key - an agent reads its own from your system environment. Nothing reaches the developer.
Team
  • Muteb AlMughyiri — author and maintainer
  • Mohammed AlZamil — testing and feature requests
Support
  • How Testin works: mtb550.github.io/test-in — what it does, how each screen works and the rules it keeps
  • Questions and ideas: github.com/mtb550/test-in/discussions
  • Issues and feature requests: github.com/mtb550/test-in/issues
idea-plugin.change-notes:

In a project still in safe mode, every Git step says so in one line and names Trust Project, and run items show as always.

idea-plugin.name: GoDogLand BDD Runner
idea-plugin.description:
GoDogLand BDD Runner adds a focused Godog/Cucumber workflow to GoLand. It lets you work with Go BDD scenarios directly from .feature files, while keeping the test execution in Go's native test runner.

The plugin adds gutter actions for running and debugging whole features or individual scenarios, saves edited files before execution, supports custom environment variables and named environment presets, and maps Go test results back to the matching Gherkin scenarios.

Compatible with GoLand 2026.1+ / build 261+.

It also improves day-to-day navigation between Gherkin steps and Godog step definitions: Cmd+B from a feature step jumps to ScenarioContext.Step(...), Find Usages from a step definition lists matching feature steps, and inspections highlight undefined, unused, invalid, or ambiguous steps.

  • Run or debug Feature and Scenario lines from the gutter.
  • See pass/fail status icons beside recently executed BDD scenarios.
  • Navigate from .feature steps to Go step definitions and back.
  • Rename Godog steps from either Gherkin feature files or Go ScenarioContext.Step(...) registrations.
  • Generate missing Go step definitions from undefined Gherkin steps.
  • Use GoLand's test tool window with links back to the related feature lines.
  • Configure default environment variables, named environment presets, and the Go test function pattern used by Godog test runs.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Initial release with Godog/Cucumber gutter run and debug actions, feature and scenario status icons, step navigation, BDD inspections, quick fixes for undefined steps, GoLand test tool window integration, and configurable environment variables.

idea-plugin.name: Cypress Radar
idea-plugin.description:
Cypress Radar displays Cypress test health inline in your spec files, powered by the Cypress Cloud Data Extract API.

For each it() or test() call, a color-coded block appears above the line showing the historical pass rate and clickable links to failing runs:

  • Green — 100% pass rate
  • Yellow — 75–99% pass rate (flaky)
  • Red — below 75% or failing in the most recent run
  • Gray — no historical data yet
  • Blue — dynamic title that cannot be statically matched

Each block shows passes/total (rate%), failed in runs: #1234 #1235. Run numbers link directly to the Cypress Cloud test replay.

Supports it('title'), it("title"), it(`title`), and multi-line forms. Results are cached for 5 minutes.

Configure by placing a flake-guard.json file in your project root:

{ "provider": "cypress-cloud", "apiToken": "YOUR_DATA_EXTRACT_API_TOKEN" }

The API token must be a Cypress Cloud Data Extract API key (Enterprise feature). Generate one at cloud.cypress.io → Integrations → Data Extract API.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • timeframe config option to control how many days of run history are fetched (default: 7)
  • cache config option to adjust the result cache TTL in minutes (default: 30)
  • projects config option to filter results by specific Cypress project IDs

idea-plugin.name: Tests Analyzer

  • Results Table — sortable, filterable table with class name, test name, duration and color-coded status.

How to use

  • Select Tests Analyzer → Run and Analyze to execute tests and view results.
  • Select Tests Analyzer → Analyze from Existing Execution to load previously saved results.

Supported build systems

  • Maven — runs tests and parses Surefire/Failsafe XML reports.

Supported test frameworks

idea-plugin.name: Crystal Language
idea-plugin.description:
Comprehensive Crystal language support for all JetBrains IDEs — IntelliJ IDEA, RubyMine, WebStorm, CLion, and others. Provides a rich development experience with syntax highlighting, code intelligence, debugging, and an integrated test runner, all powered by a native GrammarKit parser (no external language server required).

Early Beta — This plugin is under active development and bugs are to be expected. If you encounter a problem, please open a GitHub issue with a minimal reproduction — that helps us fix it faster than a negative review would.

Debugging

Full debugger integration via LLDB DAP (Debug Adapter Protocol). Set breakpoints, step through code, inspect variables, and evaluate expressions — for both programs and specs. Requires lldb-dap to be installed on your system.

  • Breakpoints with hit counts and conditions
  • Step over / into / out
  • Variable inspection (locals, instance variables, globals)
  • Debug both crystal run and crystal spec targets
  • Crystal-specific LLDB type formatters bundled

Test Runner

Integrated test runner connecting crystal spec to IntelliJ's Test UI (SMTRunner). Run individual specs from gutter icons, see real-time results, and re-run failed tests instantly.

  • Gutter run icons on describe and it blocks
  • Single-test execution via file:line targeting
  • Real-time output parsing with pass/fail/error/pending states
  • Re-run failed tests with one click
  • Spec file icons for visual distinction

Code Intelligence

  • Go to Definition (Ctrl+B / Ctrl+Click) — jump to classes, modules, structs, enums, method definitions, and DOT-call methods (obj.method, Class.method) across the entire project
  • Namespace Access — Go to Definition and hover for intermediate namespace segments (e.g. Inner in Outer::Inner.method)
  • Code Completion (Ctrl+Space) — context-aware dot-completion with type inference, free-text completion for classes/methods/locals, type completion in annotations and generics, overloaded methods as separate entries, record macro support, and :: auto-completion
  • Parameter Info (Ctrl+P) — method signatures at call sites, supports parenthesized calls, bare calls, DOT-calls, ClassName.new(...), and overloads
  • Hover Type Info — hovering over a variable shows the inferred type; method return types inferred from body when no annotation exists
  • Quick Documentation (Ctrl+Q) — rendered doc comments with syntax-highlighted signature, Markdown support, and clickable type names
  • Find Usages (Alt+F7) — locate all references to a symbol across the project
  • Go to Symbol / Class (Ctrl+N, Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N) — project-wide instant navigation via StubIndex
  • Structure View — PSI-based tree showing classes, modules, methods, macros, and nested definitions

Code Quality

  • Type Checking — validates argument types against parameter annotations (supports numeric autocasting, union types, nilable types, overloads)
  • Argument Count Validation — reports missing required arguments and excess arguments (supports named args, splat, double-splat, default values)
  • Unused Variable Detection — warns on local variables that are assigned but never read
  • Lib Fun Type Annotation — reports missing type annotations in lib function definitions
  • Empty Collection Inspection — suggests using typed empty literals
  • Colon Spacing — reports missing space after : in type annotations
  • Instance Variable Type — validates instance variable types against declarations
  • Invalid Single-Quote String — reports non-ASCII characters in single-quote strings

Editor Features

  • Syntax Highlighting — 60+ keywords, operators, strings with interpolation, regex, symbols, heredocs, percent literals, annotations, macros
  • Semantic Highlighting — PSI-based annotator distinguishes variables, methods, types, parameters, and macro fresh vars
  • Keyword Block Highlighting — cursor on block keywords highlights all related structural keywords of the enclosing block
  • Code Formatting — reformat via crystal tool format (Ctrl+Alt+L)
  • Rename Refactoring (Shift+F6) — in-place rename with preview dialog and automatic compiler verification
  • Live Templates — 21 code snippets for common Crystal patterns (def, class, module, spec, etc.)
  • Smart Enter — automatically inserts end after def/class/module/if/do and handles indentation
  • Code Folding — collapse methods, classes, blocks, comments, heredocs, arrays, and hashes
  • Brace Matching — highlights matching pairs for parentheses, brackets, braces, and do/end
  • TODO Indexing — Crystal TODO/FIXME comments appear in the TODO tool window

Run Configurations

  • Crystal Run — run Crystal programs with configurable arguments and environment
  • Crystal Build — compile with custom flags (release, static, target, etc.)
  • Crystal Spec — run specs with file/line targeting and tag filters

Parser Coverage

The plugin ships a full GrammarKit BNF parser covering classes, modules, structs, enums, methods, macros, control flow, generics (variadic, defaults, bounds), union types, blocks, proc/lambda literals, pattern matching, lib blocks (fun, union, struct, enum, external vars, varargs), annotations, heredocs, percent literals, string interpolation in percent/regex/backtick literals, implicit object bracket access (&.[]), rescue clauses with typed rescue and union types, ranges with omitted start, namespace access (::Foo), and more. The parser is error-tolerant and works with incomplete code while typing.

Requirements

  • Crystal installed and available in PATH (for formatting, compiler verification, and running programs)
  • lldb-dap (optional) — required for debugging. Install via your system package manager.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.2.8

  • Embedded language highlighting in heredocs — heredoc bodies whose marker names a language (<<-SQL, <<-JAVASCRIPT, <<-YAML, …) now show that language's syntax highlighting, mirroring RubyMine's heredoc injection. A curated alias table plus a case-insensitive language-ID fallback covers every installed language; uninstalled languages keep plain string highlighting, and Crystal interpolations (#{…}) keep their Crystal coloring instead of target-language errors.
  • # language=<id> comment injection into heredocs and string literals — the RubyMine persistent-injection convention now works for Crystal: a whole-line # language=<id> comment directly above a heredoc header or string literal injects that language into the body, with optional prefix/suffix attributes (the documented remedy for partial SQL statements). A resolvable comment wins over the heredoc marker; require "…" paths are excluded.
  • Go to Declaration on require statements — Ctrl+Click / Ctrl+B on a require now opens the required file: relative requires open the file next to the requiring file, non-relative requires search <project>/lib and the Crystal stdlib source, and wildcard requires (/*, /**) present all matching files in a multi-target popup.
  • DOT completion on integer and float literals restored — 5.<caret> and 5.5.<caret> offer Int32/Float64 methods again; five grammar gaps that silently dropped members of real stdlib sources from indexing now parse, and an incomplete (macro-generated) hierarchy no longer empties the suggestion list.
  • Heredoc calls inside argument lists — assert_diff(<<-FIRST, <<-SECOND) and mixed normal/heredoc argument lists parse correctly (previously falsely marked "expected, got 'do'"); heredoc coloring is now PSI-enforced, so renaming delimiters no longer leaves bodies or terminators styled as ordinary code.
  • Empty brace blocks after method calls — Thread.new { } and spawn { } are no longer flagged with "Empty hash literal requires type".
  • Constructor resolution across stdlib types — Hash(String, Int32).new(0), Deque(Int32).new (initializer-backed overloads), URI.new("http", …) (types defining setters), and HTTP::Client.new(uri, tls) (macro-generated methods) resolve to their real overloads instead of "Too many arguments" errors or "Any (Variable)" hovers.
  • Macro context resolution — unqualified calls inside {{ … }} now resolve only to project macros and builtin Crystal::Macros methods, so {{ run("…") }} no longer reports false type mismatches; hovering a top-level call shows the real method documentation instead of "Any (Variable)".
  • Parser robustness — char literals inside string interpolation and macro control blocks, special global variables (#{$1}) inside interpolations, and assignments in postfix modifier conditions (return [] of Result unless target = …) now parse correctly.
  • Registration fixes — the language injection support extension and stub element type initialization now load reliably under the 2026.2 module mechanism, eliminating double injections and "All stub element types should be created before index initialization" regressions.

0.2.7

  • ECR Structure View restored — the optional dependency fragments introduced in 0.2.5 were never loaded (and product module names cannot be resolved as depends targets at runtime anyway), so the ECR Structure View factory and the spec test locator were silently not registered. Both extensions are now registered directly in the main plugin descriptor, matching the always-available platform modules they use.
  • Marketplace verification clean — the missing SM Test Runner module declaration caused 14 binary-incompatibility problems against RubyMine 262. The 2026.2 product modules are now declared through the modern dependencies/module mechanism, which both the IDE runtime and verifier understand.
  • Debugger registration consolidated — the DAP debug adapter support provider is now declared in the main plugin descriptor; the orphaned fragment file was removed (the runtime fallback registration remains as a safety net).
  • Descriptor wiring regression guard — a new consistency test fails the build when dependent extensions disappear from the descriptor or a fragment/config-file reference becomes inconsistent.

0.2.5

  • IntelliJ 2026.2 required — the plugin now targets the current platform release (build 262)
  • All deprecated API usage eliminated — run gutter markers, debug session start, markdown rendering, and module-root listeners use the modern platform APIs; zero deprecated and zero scheduled-for-removal usages remain
  • Cleaner optional dependencies — SM Test Runner and Structure View integrations are declared as proper optional dependency fragments

0.2.4

  • Marketplace verification fixed — the ECR Structure View no longer uses internal platform API (StructureViewComposite); it is built on the public TemplateLanguageStructureViewBuilder, so uploads pass plugin verification again
  • Simplified ECR Structure View — the former separate Crystal tab merged into the ECR tab as an @instance_variables group node (shown when instance variables exist) with navigation to each variable's first occurrence; the HTML tab is unchanged
  • More robust module dependency — the SM Test Runner module dependency is now optional, so the plugin stays fully enabled even in environments where that module is absent

0.2.3

  • Full stdlib indexing for Enumerable and String — parser and lexer gaps broke parsing inside real crystal sources, silently hiding most methods from completion. Enumerable now exposes ~131 indexed methods (sum, max, map, …), String ~180 (upcase, downcase, gsub, …)
  • Correct types for percent literals — %w[...] hovers as Array(String), %i[...] as Array(Symbol); new interpolating variants %W and %I; %r infers Regex
  • Splat and double-splat expansion type-checked — add(*args) and setup(**options)
  • Crystal NamedTuple support — {name: "x"} infers NamedTuple(name: String) instead of Hash, matching {name: String}-style parameters structurally
  • Compiler-accurate diagnostics on valid code — no more false errors for chained dot expressions in multi-line parameter lists, bracket access after dot-calls (config["envs"]), splat/double-splat calls, NamedTuple literals, or classes containing private module/enum
  • Constructor resolution fixed — hovering/navigating .new resolves to the constructor (including generic receivers like Channel(Nil).new) instead of falling back to variable info
  • Multi-line union continuation — dangling pipes in unions like rescue ex : A | are flagged at the pipe with a compiler-style message plus an "Add backslash line continuation" quick fix
  • Require-graph visibility for name lookups — unqualified calls and name-based hover fallbacks only consider definitions your file can actually see (same file, requires, prelude), eliminating false positives from unrelated project files and stdlib signature leaks
  • Literal receiver documentation — hovering a method call on literals ([1,2].max, "abc".upcase) shows the resolved method's documentation

0.1.17

  • Keyword block highlighting — cursor on structural keywords highlights all related keywords of the enclosing block
  • Variable hover type info — hovering over a variable shows the inferred type in a two-line popup
  • Method return type inference — methods without explicit return type annotations have their return type inferred from body
  • Hash/tuple type inference — detailed type parameters in hover popups for hash and tuple literals
  • Ternary type inference — ternary expressions correctly infer union types for variable hover
  • Namespace access Go to Definition and hover — hover and navigate on intermediate namespace segments
  • DOT-call Go to Definition and hover — obj.method resolves to target method; hovering shows documentation
  • Parameter/Definition hover popups — parameter names and definition names show context-specific popups
  • Overloaded methods in completion — multiple overloads appear as separate entries with signatures
  • :: auto-completion — typing :: after a CONSTANT triggers completion popup
  • Colon spacing inspection — reports missing space after : in type annotations
  • Instance variable type inspection — validates instance variable types
  • String interpolation in percent/regex/backtick literals — %(hello #{name}), /pattern #{expr}/, `echo #{name}` now parse correctly
  • Rescue clause improvements — typed rescue with union types and variable binding
  • Implicit object bracket access — &.[1], &[] now parse correctly
  • Bug fix — Go to Definition no longer freezes on bare method calls
  • Bug fix — false positive type mismatches on DOT-calls fixed
  • Bug fix — false "Value assigned never used" with conditional reassignment fixed

0.1.16

  • Colon spacing inspection — reports missing space after : in type annotations (e.g. x:Int32 → warning)
  • @param shorthand support — @param in method bodies is recognized for completion, type inference, and inspections
  • Record macro support — record Config, host : String, port : Int32 works for completion, parameter info (Ctrl+P), and argument inspections
  • Type checking for record macro parameters — validates argument types against record parameters in inspections
  • Parameter completion priority boost — parameters appear higher in the completion popup with bold styling
  • Keywords as method/macro names — macro require(...), def if(...), def self.require(...) etc. now parse correctly; all Crystal keywords are valid as method names
  • Annotation definitions inside module/class bodies — annotation GeneratedWrapper ... end inside module/class now parses correctly
  • Global namespace prefix in expressions — ::Bytes.new(...), ::Foo::Bar.new(x) etc. now parse correctly
  • Overloaded methods in completion — multiple overloads of the same method (e.g. ENV.fetch with 3 different signatures) now appear as separate entries in the code completion popup, each showing its parameter signature
  • Bug fix — renaming @var/@@var with explicit prefix now correctly preserves the variable type
  • Bug fix — postfix modifiers (e.g. return x if condition) no longer break macro body end detection
  • Bug fix — type check and parameter info for DOT-calls on constants no longer show false positive type mismatches
  • Bug fix — false positive "Unknown named argument" on class constructor DOT-calls fixed
  • Bug fix — case ... end.tap do no longer causes a parse error
  • Bug fix — ?/! suffix after macro interpolation now parses correctly
  • Bug fix — multi-level pointer types in lib bindings (e.g. BaseInfo***) now parse correctly
  • Bug fix — postfix modifier after compound assignment (e.g. @data[key] += 1 if condition) now parses correctly
  • Bug fix — binary expressions inside calls are no longer misparsed as bare method calls
  • Bug fix — splat prefix detection in argument extraction no longer produces false positives
  • Bug fix — record macro parameter priority fixed, preventing false "wrong argument type" errors
  • Bug fix — colon spacing inspection now only scans within method definitions
  • Bug fix — binary +/- no longer parsed as bare method arguments
  • Bug fix — Go to Definition on .new now follows Crystal's constructor resolution order
  • Bug fix — operator method names ([], []?, []=) now parse correctly
  • Bug fix — ENV.fetch completion fixed; all stdlib methods inside module ENV are now indexed
  • Changed — method lookup elements use PSI object identity to distinguish overloaded methods
  • Changed — Force Re-index button now properly removes the library before re-adding it
  • Changed — Force Re-index shows background progress bar with status updates

1.1.15

  • Parameter info (Ctrl+P) for ClassName.new — now shows initialize method parameters when calling new on a class
  • Type check for ClassName.new — argument type validation now works for new calls, resolving to initialize parameters
  • Bug fix — findTypeByName now prefers the class from the current file when multiple classes with the same name exist in the project

1.1.13

  • Code folding — multi-line arrays ([...]) and hashes ({...}) can now be collapsed, matching RubyMine behavior
  • Code folding — all block constructs keep keyword and signature visible when collapsed; placeholder shows ... end (or [ ... ] / { ... } for arrays/hashes), matching RubyMine behavior
  • Supported keywords: if/unless/while/until (with condition), def (with name + params), class/module/struct/enum (with name), begin, do, case/for, macro, lib, annotation, verbatim do
  • Suppress code completion after numeric literals — typing a number (e.g. a = 1) no longer triggers variable/method suggestions, matching RubyMine behavior
  • Bug fix — nil-safe index (?) no longer breaks parser in block contexts; item["states"]? inside each do/if blocks no longer causes false parse errors

0.1.12

  • Raised minimum IDE version from 2025.1 to 2026.1 (sinceBuild 251 → 261) to match the target platform

0.1.11

  • Improved debugger compatibility on Windows — added Windows-specific lldb-dap binary discovery, .exe suffix for compiled binaries, and fixed formatter path handling for Windows

0.1.9

  • Patched crystal_formatters.py to run on Windows — debugger now works on Windows as well

0.1.7

  • Initial early-beta release (Proof of Concept)
  • Parser — GrammarKit BNF covering classes, modules, methods, macros, generics, control flow, pattern matching, lib bindings, proc literals, annotations, and more

idea-plugin.name: Fast Invoker
idea-plugin.description:
Fast Invoker lets you invoke any Java method directly in a running JVM — no restarts, no test boilerplate. Click a gutter icon, adjust parameters, and see the result immediately.

Features

  • Invoke any Java method — call public, private, or static methods at runtime to debug logic, validate behavior, or explore code without writing a single test.
  • One-click invocation — gutter icons appear next to every Java method; click to open the invoke panel with class and method pre-filled.
  • Dynamic JVM attachment — attaches to any running local JVM process via the Java Attach API without modifying your application.
  • JSON parameter editor — edit method parameters as JSON with auto-generated templates derived from method signatures.
  • Groovy pre-execution scripts — run custom Groovy scripts before invocation for data setup or environment preparation; save reusable script templates for future use.
  • Invocation history — save method calls with their parameters and results; replay or review past invocations from the History tab.

Typical workflow

  1. Start your application.
  2. Click the gutter icon next to any method, or right-click and choose Invoke Method.
  3. Select the target JVM process and click Attach.
  4. Fill in the JSON parameters and click Send.
  5. View the return value or exception in the result panel.

Fast Invoker 可以直接调用运行中的 JVM 内的任意 Java 方法，无需重启服务，无需编写测试代码。 点击行号区图标，调整参数，立即查看执行结果。

功能特性

  • 调用任意 Java 方法 — 无论是 public、private 还是 static 方法，均可在运行时直接调用，适用于调试、验证逻辑和探索代码行为。
  • 一键调用 — 每个 Java 方法旁均显示行号图标，点击即可打开调用面板，类名与方法名自动填充。
  • 动态 JVM 挂载 — 通过 Java Attach API 挂载到任意本地运行中的 JVM 进程，无需修改目标应用。
  • JSON 参数编辑器 — 以 JSON 格式编辑方法参数，支持根据方法签名自动生成参数模板。
  • Groovy 前置脚本 — 在方法调用前执行自定义 Groovy 脚本，用于数据准备或环境初始化，支持保存可复用的脚本模板。
  • 调用历史记录 — 支持保存每次调用的参数与结果，可在历史标签页中回放或查看详情。

典型使用流程

  1. 启动你的应用程序。
  2. 点击方法旁的行号图标，或右键选择 Invoke Method。
  3. 选择目标 JVM 进程并点击 Attach。
  4. 填写 JSON 参数后点击 Send。
  5. 在结果面板中查看返回值或异常信息。

idea-plugin.name: APICue
idea-plugin.description:
APICue — API Testing from OpenAPI YAML Files

Test your REST APIs directly from OpenAPI 3.0 YAML definitions — without leaving your IDE.

APICue bridges the gap between API specification and API testing. Instead of maintaining separate .http files, you can send requests, inspect responses, and iterate on your API design right from the YAML editor.


💰 Pricing

APICue is transitioning to a paid subscription model. A 30-day free trial with full feature access is available — no credit card required.

After the trial period, a subscription is required:

  • Monthly: $1/month per developer — Full feature access, priority updates, email support, cancel anytime.
  • Annual: $10/year per developer (≈16% off) — Full feature access, priority updates, priority support, perpetual fallback license (stay on the last working version if you cancel).

Specific pricing and effective date will be announced before the change takes effect.


✨ Key Features

▶ One-Click Testing from Gutter Icons

Green run buttons appear next to every get:, post:, put:, delete:, and patch: operation in your OpenAPI YAML files. Click to open the test panel instantly.

🖥 Dedicated ToolWindow Panel

Right-side tool window shows the full testing interface: environment selector, auth config, request editor (Params / Headers / Body tabs), and a split-pane response viewer. Stay in context — no popups or dialogs to interrupt your flow.

🔐 Security Scheme Auto-Discovery

Reads components.securitySchemes and security requirements from your OpenAPI spec, automatically generates the correct authentication headers (Bearer JWT, Basic Auth, API Key in header/query/cookie), and pre-fills them.

🌍 Multi-Environment Server Selection

Supports multiple servers per YAML file. The last selected URL is remembered per-file, so switching between YAML documents restores your previous choice automatically.

📋 Smart Parameter Pre-Fill

Query parameters, headers, and request body are pre-filled from example, default, and schema property values — following a well-defined priority hierarchy. No manual typing for common cases.

📝 Save & Load Request/Response Examples

Save working request parameters and response payloads back to the YAML file as OpenAPI examples. Load them back later for reproducible testing.

🔑 Token Management

Manage tokens (JWT, API keys, etc.) per environment with a built-in Token Manager. Tokens are stored securely using your IDE's password-safe mechanism.

🔗 $Ref Cross-File Resolution

Fully resolves $ref references across YAML files (e.g., $ref: 'model.yml#/components/schemas/User') with caching and circular-reference detection.

🌐 Internationalization (i18n)

Supports 11 languages: EN, 中文, 日本語, 한국어, Español, Português, Deutsch, Français, Русский, Tiếng Việt, Türkçe. Automatically matches your IDE's language setting.


🚀 How It Works

  1. Open any OpenAPI 3.0 YAML file in IntelliJ IDEA
  2. Click the ▶ icon next to any path operation
  3. The APICue Tester tool window opens with the operation context loaded
  4. Select your target server environment, review/ edit parameters, configure auth
  5. Click Send Request and inspect the response in real-time

📦 Dependencies

  • OkHttp 4.12 — HTTP client
  • SnakeYAML 2.2 — YAML parsing
  • Kotlinx Coroutines — Async request handling

idea-plugin.name: RecordRelay
idea-plugin.description:
Clone database records with their full relationship graph — without leaving IntelliJ

RecordRelay reproduces a single business record and its entire data context (the foreign-key dependency tree) from one database environment to another. Pick a root table, enter an ID, click Clone Context — the engine traverses every FK link and writes all dependent rows to the target in the correct insert order.

Features

  • Context Cloning — Copies a record and every FK-linked row it depends on, across environments, in the right order, in seconds.
  • Conflict Resolution — Four strategies for cloning into non-empty targets: Regenerate Identities (new IDs), Isolate Namespace (1 M+ offset), Skip Existing (silently skips duplicates), and Fail Safe (aborts if the target already has data).
  • Automatic FK Discovery — Discovers both declared and logical (implicit) foreign-key relationships automatically, including FK-free schemas that rely on naming conventions such as customer_id.
  • Relationship Graph View — Visualises the full FK dependency graph of the cloned context so you can see exactly which tables and rows are involved.
  • PII Masking — Scrubs email, phone, IBAN, national ID, and address columns on the fly during transfer.
  • Field Overrides — Override any column value in the target (e.g. created_by=test or orders:status=PENDING).
  • Clone History — Browse per-session clone history with table-level record counts, elapsed time, and connection health at a glance.
  • Export Packages — Export the context as a portable .rrpkg file to share with a teammate or import later.
  • Schema Discovery — Inspect column types and analyse cross-database type compatibility side by side.
  • Query Runner — Execute raw SQL against any configured connection from inside the IDE.

How It Works

  1. Add your database connections in the Connections tab.
  2. Switch to Clone, choose source and target environments.
  3. Select the root table, enter the record ID, and pick a conflict resolution strategy.
  4. Click Clone Context — RecordRelay fetches all related rows and inserts them into the target in dependency order.

Supported Databases

PostgreSQL  ·  MySQL  ·  MariaDB  ·  SQL Server  ·  Oracle  ·  MongoDB  ·  SQLite  ·  Cassandra  ·  Redis  ·  Elasticsearch

Typical Use Cases

  • Reproduce a production bug locally with real, complete data.
  • Seed a staging environment for a specific test scenario.
  • Share a precise data context with a colleague as a package file.
  • Validate a migration script against real production relationships.

Requires IntelliJ IDEA 2024.1 or later (Community or Ultimate).
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.5.0

  • Schema-drift tolerant PostgreSQL writes: only columns present in the target table are inserted; source-only columns are skipped with a warning instead of failing.
  • Insert/fetch failures now include the underlying SQL cause for easier diagnosis.

1.4.0

  • Per-connection schema support (PostgreSQL search_path/currentSchema) so unqualified table names resolve across fetch, write, identity, and sequence sync. A Schema field was added to the connection dialog.

1.3.0

  • Satellite (companion) tables: after a clone, sync rows from a table in a separate database that references the cloned root by a single link column (e.g. an event-sourced read_model). The link column is remapped to the new root id and the same field overrides are applied. Configure them in the new Satellite Tables section of the Clone screen.
  • New identity strategies: Native sequence (DB-assigned IDs) and Start at custom ID, selectable in the conflict/identity dropdown.

1.2.0

  • Added four conflict resolution modes: Regenerate Identities, Isolate Namespace, Skip Existing, and Fail Safe.
  • Hybrid BFS traversal: outgoing FK edges use the full schema graph to fetch all dependencies; incoming edges use the conservative root-centric graph to prevent scope creep.
  • FK remapping now covers cross-table columns (e.g. orders.created_by) that are outside the root-centric traversal graph.
  • Heuristic FK discovery now matches both singular (customer_id) and plural (customers_id) column naming, covering FK-free schemas.

1.1.0

  • Clone history dashboard with per-session record counts and elapsed time.
  • Relationship graph view for the cloned FK context.
  • In-app help screen with quick-start guide and keyboard shortcuts.
  • Field overrides: override any column value before writing to the target.

idea-plugin.name: SHAFT
idea-plugin.description:
SHAFT's official IntelliJ IDEA companion: design Gherkin from a story, record and generate fluent Java, then analyze Allure/Doctor/heal evidence — powered by SHAFT Engine and the SHAFT MCP server.

Highlights

  • Assistant chat — describe a scenario in plain language and get runnable SHAFT test code; slash commands cover recording, inspection, test generation, and failed-test triage.
  • Web recorder — capture real browser sessions and turn them into SHAFT tests, with Pick-Locator results flowing straight into the editor.
  • Editor intelligence — completion, typo detection, value checks and quick docs for SHAFT properties, inspections for Thread.sleep and deprecated SHAFT APIs, and shtest/shclick/shtype/shassert/shapi live templates.
  • Run from the gutter — SHAFT-aware JUnit and TestNG run configurations for test classes and methods.
  • SHAFT Tests panel — recent runs at a glance, with one-click Doctor diagnosis and Healer locator repair for failures.
  • Inspector & locator tools — inspect live pages, propose resilient locators, and validate them before committing.
  • Visual baselines & evidence — triage visual-regression diffs and browse execution evidence without leaving the IDE.
  • Guided setup — a five-step wizard detects this project, checks JDK, Maven, and Git, then shows a copy-and-run installer command. The plugin does not execute the installer. A setup report is sent only after Allow and becomes a public GitHub issue.
  • Advanced tools — the full SHAFT MCP tool catalog, refreshed live, with curated safe defaults and explicit approval prompts before anything runs.

The plugin activates only in projects that use SHAFT and stays out of the way everywhere else.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Replaces first-run setup with a five-step wizard. The plugin shows a copy-and-run installer command and does not execute it. A completed wizard stays complete across updates while a stale MCP command is dropped. A setup report is sent only after Allow and becomes a public GitHub issue.
  • Fixes plugin installation failing with "Failed to load the plugin descriptor" caused by a malformed optional JUnit integration descriptor.
  • Migrates run-configuration producers off deprecated IntelliJ Platform APIs flagged by the JetBrains Plugin Verifier.
  • Hardens the release pipeline: builds now fail on deprecated API usage, plugin-structure defects, and invalid descriptors before anything reaches the Marketplace.
  • Refreshes the Marketplace description and screenshots.

idea-plugin.name: Axiom Test Runner
idea-plugin.description:
Axiom Test Runner adds first-class GoLand support for the Axiom Go test framework.

Every TestXxx method on a struct registered with axiom.NewSuite (or axiom.NewSuiteFactory) gets a green gutter icon exactly like a plain func TestFoo(t *testing.T). Clicking it opens the full native GoLand menu — Run, Debug, Run with Coverage, Profile with CPU / Memory / Blocking Profiler, Modify Run Configuration… — and results appear in the standard Test Results tool window.

Framework-agnostic: works regardless of what your suite struct embeds (axiom.Suite, a company-specific BaseSuite, or a custom wrapper) — the plugin only looks for the axiom.NewSuite registration, not for a magic base type.

idea-plugin.name: Golden Diff
idea-plugin.description:
Golden Diff helps Android and Kotlin developers review screenshot-test changes directly in Android Studio or IntelliJ-based IDEs, without leaving the editor.

Open the tool window for the screen you are editing and it lists the matching screenshot goldens, then compares the committed git HEAD version against your working copy or generated test output — in four modes: side-by-side (2-up), swipe, onion skin, and a pixel-diff heatmap.

It is tool-agnostic and works with PNG outputs from Roborazzi, Paparazzi, Compose Preview Screenshot Testing, Shot, Dropshots, and similar screenshot-test tools — just point it at the golden directory.

  • Match goldens to the file you are editing in two modes: by annotated preview/test method, or by a file/class regex — matched against each golden's path, so nested layouts work too.
  • Live preview in Settings shows how many and which goldens match the current file.
  • Compare Git HEAD with working-copy goldens.
  • Compare Git HEAD with generated test output such as _actual.png files.
  • Configure golden and generated-output directories, the matching rule, and excluded golden suffixes per project.
  • Review changes in side-by-side, swipe, onion-skin, and pixel-diff modes.
  • Zoom (Fit / 50–400%) and scroll large screenshots.
  • When a golden is identical to the selected source, the comparison is skipped and a single preview is shown.

Works with IntelliJ Platform 2024.1 and newer (build 241+), including compatible Android Studio releases.

Optional analytics and diagnostic reporting are disabled by default and can be controlled independently. See the privacy policy.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Introduces a project-wide Files → Goldens → Compare workflow with View and snapshot Case navigation, search, status filters, and responsive layouts.
  • Indexes Working-copy and Test-output screenshots together and automatically chooses the actionable comparison source.
  • Adds project, View, and Case Generate/Verify actions plus safe single and bulk Accept workflows with streamed output, cancellation, retry, and automatic refresh.
  • Adds debounced PNG watching, stable selection across asynchronous refreshes, and deterministic handling of ambiguous generated counterparts.
  • Extends source matching beyond Kotlin to JavaScript, TypeScript, Swift, Java, and other text-based source files without additional language-plugin dependencies.

idea-plugin.name: Thymian
idea-plugin.description:
Official Thymian IntelliJ IDEA plugin.

This plugin connects your JetBrains IDE to your local Thymian CLI.

Thymian checks your API or endpoints from API controllers against the HTTP specification or own HTTP API tests and provides you with a detailed report.

Check out the Thymian CLI website for more information.

Requirements

Node.js® and npm need to be installed on your machine. Additionally, you can have either the plugin use Thymian via npx --yes thymian@latest or you install the Thymian CLI on your local machine and set the path to the run.js in the settings.

How to use

The Thymian check is available in the endpoints list as a tab and as an action in the context menu. Either triggers the check on the selected endpoint.

Notes

At the moment, it's not possible to check a single endpoint for API specification files like an OpenAPI specification yaml or json file. Triggering the check on a single endpoint will check the whole API specification.

idea-plugin.name: HexaGen: SQL to Hexagonal Java
idea-plugin.description:
HexaGen automates the generation of complete, enterprise-grade Java / Spring Boot backends using Hexagonal Architecture (DDD / Clean Architecture) directly from your SQL DDL schemas.

Stop wasting days writing repetitive boilerplate. In 2 seconds, HexaGen scaffolding creates production-ready code that compiles and passes tests instantly.


Key Features:
  • Strict 3-Ring Architecture: Automatically isolates Domain models, Application use cases/ports, and Web/Persistence infrastructure adapters.
  • Instant Unit Tests: Generates 100% functional JUnit 5 + Mockito test suites for all use cases and REST controllers.
  • Zero-to-Hero Scaffolding: Creates valid pom.xml, Spring Boot entry points, and H2/JPA configurations.
  • Brown-Field Shield: Protects existing files from being overwritten when incrementally adding new database tables.
  • IDE Code Style Compliance: Automatically formats all generated code using your active IntelliJ formatting rules.

Right-click on any .sql file in your project to get started!

idea-plugin.name: SpecShield: OpenAPI Diff, Lint & Breaking Changes
idea-plugin.description:
OpenAPI diff, linting and breaking-change detection for JetBrains IDEs.

SpecShield compares your OpenAPI (Swagger) spec against its committed version, flags anything that would break an existing API consumer, and lints it against governance rules — without leaving the editor. Backed by the same engine as specshield.io.

  • Breaking-change detection — compare a spec against its committed version, another file, or the clipboard; get a safe-to-merge verdict and the exact breaking changes.
  • Governance review — inline annotations on your OpenAPI spec (OWASP, naming, doc-quality and more), plus a findings tool window.
  • Apply auto-fixes — Alt+Enter to generate missing operationIds and other deterministic, non-breaking fixes.
  • Explain breaking changes — a plain-English explanation of what changed and why it matters.
  • Export reports — SARIF, JUnit, or HTML governance reports.
  • Rule packs — choose a governance pack (recommended, OWASP, minimal) or your own Spectral-format ruleset.

Deterministic analysis — no LLM involved, so the same spec always produces the same result.

Requires a SpecShield account. Sign in at specshield.io/signin and paste your API key in Settings → Tools → SpecShield. A free tier is available; governance and report features require a paid plan.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.4

  • Clearer plugin name and description so the plugin is findable by what it does.

  • Governance rule-pack selection

idea-plugin.name: Kassi Test Data
idea-plugin.description:
Spec-valid test data for fintech & KYC: IBAN (mod-97), test-BIN card numbers (Luhn), passport MRZ, VAT and national IDs with real check digits — plus the deliberately invalid variants your rejection tests need. Right in your IDE, 100% offline. A focused generator for QA and fintech engineers, not a generic faker.

  • IBAN for the whole ISO 13616 registry — every European country plus 40+ worldwide (Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Israel, Brazil, Pakistan, Egypt and more): correct national length and a passing ISO 7064 mod-97 check, with an invalid-checksum variant.
  • Card (PAN) — Luhn-valid, from payment-gateway test BIN ranges only (never real issuable cards), with CVV and expiry, plus a Luhn-invalid variant.
  • BIC/SWIFT (ISO 9362), National IDs for 25 countries (incl. Russian ИНН / СНИЛС / ОГРН / ОГРНИП, IT Codice Fiscale, and DOB-encoding schemes across the EU), and VAT / ABN tax identifiers — each with its real checksum.
  • Passport MRZ (ICAO 9303, TD3) for every country — valid field and composite check digits, with an invalid variant.
  • Phone numbers by country — valid E.164 numbers backed by offline libphonenumber metadata, with an invalid variant.
  • ISIN / IMEI / EAN-13 — securities, device and product-barcode identifiers, each with its real checksum.
  • Coherent personas — name, date of birth, address, bank and tax identifiers, and a passport MRZ, all consistent for one person and country. Optional seed for reproducible fixtures.

100% offline and algorithmic. Zero network, zero scraping, zero real PII — everything is synthetic data for testing, not real identities. Every generator is covered by a unit test that asserts the valid output passes the real algorithm and the invalid variant fails it.

How is this different from Test Data / Randomness / faker plugins?

Generic fakersKassi Test Data
IBANlooks Germanpasses ISO 7064 mod-97 (+ national check digits where they exist)
Card (PAN)random digitsLuhn-valid, published test BINs only
National / tax IDsformat onlyreal per-scheme checksum (BSN, Codice Fiscale, ИНН…)
Invalid variants for rejection tests—every generator, one precisely broken check
Coherent persona (one person, one country)—yes, seedable

For random UUIDs, lorem ipsum and generic names those plugins are great — use both.

Free — and staying free. The generators in this plugin are free and will remain free; nothing here becomes paywalled. An optional extended fintech pack may arrive later as a separate paid add-on, but it will never lock away what you already use.

Usage: right-click in the editor (or Tools ▸ Insert Test Data), search, pick, and it inserts at the caret.

Source, issues & docs: github.com/VadimToptunov/KassiTestDataGeneratorPlugin

Part of the Kassi QA toolkit: Flaky Test Linter · HTTP Data Injector · Checksum & Regex Playground · UUID, ULID & NanoID Toolkit · MRZ & Barcode Inspector · Secret & Card Leak Guard

idea-plugin.name: Hurlevent
idea-plugin.description:
Language support for Hurl, the plain-text file format for running and testing HTTP requests. Hurlevent recognizes .hurl files and adds editor features, code inspections, and embedded language support so you can write, read, and navigate Hurl files directly in your JetBrains IDE.

Editing

  • Syntax highlighting with a customizable color scheme (Settings | Editor | Color Scheme | Hurl)
  • Code folding, brace matching, and line commenting
  • Structure view and breadcrumbs to navigate requests and their sections
  • Spell checking in comments and strings
  • Quick documentation for filters, linked to the official Hurl reference
  • A New Hurl File action in the New menu

Inspections

  • Warnings for deprecated filters
  • Warnings for unknown charsets
  • Detection of duplicate sections

Embedded languages

Request and response bodies and query expressions are highlighted and validated with the IDE's native language support:

  • JSON and XML bodies
  • GraphQL bodies (requires the GraphQL plugin)
  • JSONPath and XPath query expressions (require the bundled JSONPath and XPathView plugins)
  • Regular expressions in string values

Based on the Hurl 8.0.1 specification.

Source code | Issues

idea-plugin.name: Checksum & Regex Playground
idea-plugin.description:
Checksum & Regex Playground

A tool window for QA / fintech / KYC engineers. Paste any identifier and instantly see which real-world checks it passes — no browser, no guesswork, fully offline.

  • Checksums tab: pick a type to load a valid example (or type / paste your own) and it live-validates against every applicable algorithm — IBAN (ISO 7064 mod-97), card Luhn, VAT (DE/GB/CY/NL), Dutch BSN, AU TFN/ABN, BIC/SWIFT, GB NINo, German ID card (ICAO 7-3-1), ISIN, IMEI, EAN-13, GTIN-8/GTIN-14, LEI, VIN, ISBN-10/13, JMBG, FR SIREN/SIRET, UK NHS number, crypto addresses (Bitcoin Base58Check, Ethereum EIP-55), and the Russian ИНН, СНИЛС, ОГРН, ОГРНИП. Each check shows ✔ pass or ✘ fail.
  • Regex tab: a live regular-expression tester — pattern + text → matches with capture groups and positions, with clear syntax-error messages. Toggle flags (ignore-case, multiline, dot-all, extended), pick a ready-made pattern (email, IPv4, URL, UUID, date…), and try a live replace with $1 group references.

Open it from View ▸ Tool Windows ▸ Test Data Playground. Uses the same validated engine as the Kassi Test Data generator.

More Kassi tools for QA & fintech: Kassi Test Data — generate valid IBANs, cards, BIC/SWIFT, VAT and national IDs (the inverse of this validator).

Source, issues & docs: github.com/VadimToptunov/kassi-plugins

idea-plugin.name: API Bolt
idea-plugin.description:
API Lightning Tester — An IDE-integrated API debugging tool designed for Spring Boot developers, enabling seamless switching between code and interface testing.

idea-plugin.name: MockFlow - Local Service Virtualization
idea-plugin.description:
Local Service Virtualization & Embedded Mock Server inside IntelliJ IDEA

MockFlow is a lightweight, code-aware embedded HTTP service virtualization platform built directly inside IntelliJ IDEA. It empowers developers to build, run, and debug applications even when downstream microservices, third-party APIs, or staging servers are offline, slow, or unstable.

Stop wrestling with external mock servers, complex WireMock standalone scripts, or fragile network proxies. MockFlow operates 100% locally within your IDE process—air-gapped, deterministic, and instant.

🌟 Key Features

  • ⚡ Embedded Ktor 3.x Engine: Runs a local Netty HTTP mock server (default: http://127.0.0.1:18181) directly inside your IDE with zero external daemon processes.
  • 🔍 PSI / UAST Code Discovery: Automatically scans your project source code for REST endpoints (Spring Web @GetMapping/@PostMapping, @FeignClient, Retrofit, JAX-RS, Ktor) and generates schema-aware mock JSON responses from Java Records, POJOs, and Kotlin Data Classes.
  • 🎯 Interactive Editor Gutter Icons: Click the [m] MockFlow icon directly in your Java/Kotlin code margin to instantly toggle or edit mock endpoints for any method.
  • 🪄 Automatic Run Configuration Injection: Automatically injects SERVICE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18181 and -Dmockflow.server.url into Spring Boot, Node.js, Python, and Go launch profiles without manual setup.
  • 🎲 Dynamic Seed Response Generators: Inject dynamic test data on-the-fly using smart template variables:
    • $uuid — Random UUID string
    • $timestamp / $timestampEpoch — Current UTC ISO-8601 or epoch timestamp
    • $randomEmail, $randomName, $randomPhone — Fresh mock persona data
    • $randomInt(min, max) — Random integer range generator
    • $choice('PENDING', 'ACTIVE', 'COMPLETED') — Pick randomly from a set of values
  • ⏱️ Latency & Fault Injection: Simulate real-world network turbulence! Drag the response delay slider to test HTTP timeouts or inject status codes (e.g., 500 Internal Error, 503 Unavailable, 404 Not Found) to test Resilience4j circuit breakers and fault tolerance.
  • 📡 Real-time HTTP Request Stream: Monitor incoming client calls live with response latency duration metrics and HTTP header inspection.
  • 📄 OpenAPI & HAR Importer: Import OpenAPI/Swagger specifications or browser .har traces to instantly populate ready-to-run mock routes.
  • 👥 Git-Friendly Team Sharing: Mock specifications are saved locally under .idea/mockflow.xml. Commit to Git so your entire team shares identical mock environments out of the box.

🛡️ Enterprise-Grade & Clean Architecture

MockFlow is designed around clean, safe IntelliJ Platform APIs:

  • No JVM Bytecode Manipulation: Never modifies compiled bytecode or runtime classloaders.
  • No Debugger Hooks: Does not alter OS proxies or inject network interception hooks.
  • 100% Local & Secure: Operates completely offline with zero data leaving your environment.

🚀 Quick Start

  1. Open the MockFlow tab on the right Tool Window anchor and click ▶ Start Server.
  2. Click the [m] gutter icon next to any Spring or JAX-RS endpoint in your Java/Kotlin source code to create a route.
  3. Run your application from IntelliJ IDEA — your HTTP calls automatically route to MockFlow!

Technical Specification & Review Notes for MockFlow v1.0.0:

  1. Architecture: Embedded Ktor 3.0.1 (Netty Engine) running locally inside the IDE process bound strictly to loopback 127.0.0.1:18181.
  2. Security & Privacy: 100% air-gapped, zero external network connections, zero telemetry. No OS proxying or network driver hooks.
  3. Code Safety: Pure PSI/UAST static analysis for Java POJOs, Java Records (Java 14+), and Kotlin Data Classes. Zero bytecode manipulation or custom JVM agents.
  4. Target JBR: Java 21 (since-build 242 / IntelliJ 2024.2+).
  5. Tested Compatibility: Verified against IntelliJ IDEA 2024.2.4 and 2024.3.3 using IntelliJ Plugin Verifier.
idea-plugin.change-notes:

idea-plugin.name: MRZ & Barcode Inspector
idea-plugin.description:
MRZ & Barcode Inspector — parse and validate KYC documents offline

A tool window for debugging travel-document and driver's-license parsing without hand-computing check digits. Paste a value and get back the parsed fields plus a pass/fail verdict for every check digit — the exact opposite direction of a generator, and the ideal companion to one.

  • MRZ tab — paste a Machine Readable Zone: TD3 (2×44, passports), TD2 (2×36), TD1 (3×30, ID cards), a machine-readable visa MRV-A (2×44) / MRV-B (2×36), or the pre-2021 French national identity card (2×36, its own field order). Parses document type, names, dates, nationality and validates every individual check digit (document number, date of birth, expiry, personal number) plus the composite check digit — using the same ICAO 7-3-1 routine already covered by Kassi Test Data's DE ID card generator.
  • Barcode tab — paste the decoded text payload of an AAMVA-compliant PDF417 barcode (US/Canada driver's license or ID card): header (IIN, AAMVA/jurisdiction version) and every subfile's data elements, or a precise structural error if the payload is malformed.
  • ICAO 9303 name transliteration — type a name with national characters and get its Machine Readable Zone form (Müller → MUELLER, Åström → AASTROEM), the Latin-based transliteration from ICAO Doc 9303 Part 3.

100% offline and algorithmic. Zero network calls, zero data collection.

More Kassi tools for QA & fintech: Kassi Test Data — generate valid IBANs, cards, BIC/SWIFT, VAT and national IDs; and Checksum & Regex Playground.

Source, issues & docs: github.com/VadimToptunov/kassi-plugins

idea-plugin.name: k6 Companion
idea-plugin.description:
A Run Configuration for k6 load test scripts, plus a tool window for k6's `--summary-export` JSON. A real paid competitor's reviewers reported: "it doesn't respect Macros (despite allowing macros to be used)... configuration errors saying the file does not exist" -- this plugin explicitly expands path macros (`PathMacroManager`) before ever touching the filesystem, for both the script path and the k6 executable path.

Another cited complaint: "the terminal output for the 'animated progress bar' has been an issue for 2 years... makes the plugin nearly unusable." This plugin renders process output through the platform's own native `ConsoleView` (`CommandLineState`), not a hand-rolled terminal emulator. No WSL support in v1 -- not promising what the competitor doesn't reliably deliver either.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Review/star CTA now links to this plugin's own Marketplace reviews page instead of the vendor's generic plugin list.

idea-plugin.name: ISO 8583 Inspector
idea-plugin.description:
ISO 8583 Inspector

Paste an ISO 8583 card/ATM transaction message and read it — no web parser, no external tool, fully offline. For payment-gateway, acquiring and processing engineers who debug POS/ATM transactions where the meaning is carried by position and a bitmap, not by JSON.

  • MTI decoded — message class, function and origin (e.g. 0100 = authorization request).
  • Bitmap decoded — which data elements are present (primary + secondary), the classic first-bit trap handled.
  • Data elements broken out by number, name and value, following each field's length rule (fixed / LLVAR / LLLVAR).
  • Card-data validation — the PAN (DE 2) carries a Luhn verdict, and Track 2 (DE 35) is split into PAN, expiry and service code (ISO/IEC 7813) with its embedded PAN Luhn-checked.

ISO 8583 is a family, not one rigid standard — field sets differ between implementations (Visa / Mastercard / НСПК / a given processor). Version 1.0 covers the standard ASCII layout end to end; per-processor specs, binary/BCD/EBCDIC encodings, EMV/TLV decode and test-message generation ship as later updates.

Paid plugin — a free 30-day trial is available from this page.

idea-plugin.name: Affected
idea-plugin.description:
A JetBrains IDE plugin that finds affected projects and runs only their tests and build checks.

Built for multi-module projects and monorepos across 28 supported build ecosystems and 11 JetBrains products.

Support matrix: languages, test runners, selection units and evidence.

What you get

  • Run supported ecosystems from one action.
  • Keep all commands for one build-system root in one Run session.
  • Narrow to the smallest unit proven by the native build system or test runner.
  • Optionally compile direct dependents after a public API change, or run the tests of every module that depends on the change.
  • Optionally run the plan before a commit or push.
  • After a failure, check the base branch to tell a regression from a test that was already failing (Gradle, Maven, Go and Cargo).
  • Diagnose explains what was detected and why nothing ran; one settings page holds every switch.
  • No account, server, telemetry or project-specific configuration file.
  • Optional JetBrains MCP Server tools use the same analysis snapshot and run lease.

Install Affected, open a supported project and choose Run affected tests.

Documentation · Issue tracker · Privacy

idea-plugin.name: UUID, ULID & NanoID Toolkit
idea-plugin.description:
UUID, ULID & NanoID Toolkit

Generate and inspect the identifiers you actually use in tests and APIs — no browser, no external tool, fully offline.

idea-plugin.name: Test Scaffold Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Generates a compiling Kotlin JUnit test skeleton for a Java or Kotlin class (your test sources need Kotlin) -- one test method per public method, framework already detected from your project's own dependencies and imported correctly, written under the module's test source root and opened in the editor. The skeleton is parsed in memory before anything is written (a syntax error writes nothing), and it only contains calls that compile: on an instance the test declares for you to assign, with typed placeholder arguments. Anything it can't call safely -- an object argument, a generic class -- gets an honest TODO comment instead of a broken or silently-empty test. The #1 complaint against every free alternative in this space (Squaretest, TestMe, JUnitGenerator) is generated code that doesn't compile or a test that "passes" by asserting nothing; this plugin's whole design exists to not do that.

100% local -- no network call, no account, no telemetry. PSI validation always runs off the EDT, same pattern as every other Gap Hunter Labs plugin.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • The generated test didn't compile: calls used an instance that was never declared. The test now declares private lateinit var instance: YourClass with a TODO to assign it (a generic class gets a TODO instead).
  • A double, float, long or char argument got the placeholder 0, which Kotlin rejects; placeholders are now typed (0.0, 0.0f, 0L, ' '). A call that would need null for an object argument is left as a TODO instead of being executed.
  • With a test source root but no package directory under it yet, the test was written next to the class in src/main, where test dependencies aren't on the classpath. The package directories are now created under the module's test source root.
  • The generated file is opened in the editor.
  • The listing said each unresolved reference is replaced by a TODO; the in-memory check is a syntax check, and the listing now says so.

idea-plugin.name: Flaky Test Marker Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Gutter warning icon on any Java/Kotlin test method annotated @Disabled (JUnit 5) or @Ignore (JUnit 4) with no reason given, or whose reason names a YYYY-MM-DD revisit date that has already passed. Skipped tests are easy to forget about entirely -- without a reason, future readers have no context for why it's disabled; with a stale date, it's a real signal the test is overdue for a second look.

100% static text/PSI analysis -- matches the annotation by simple name, so it works whether the real JUnit jar is on the classpath or not. Java and Kotlin.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only recognizes a `YYYY-MM-DD` date embedded directly in the reason string -- other date formats, or a date referenced only in a linked ticket, aren't covered. Doesn't attempt to judge whether a *given* reason is actually a good one, only whether one exists and (if dated) is current.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

idea-plugin.name: SpringLens - Spring Boot RESTful API Tester
idea-plugin.description:
SpringLens is a lightweight, zero-configuration RESTful API testing client seamlessly integrated into IntelliJ IDEA. Designed specifically for Spring Boot and Spring Cloud developers, it allows you to test, debug, and manage APIs directly within your IDE without switching between external tools.

Key Features

  • Deep AST/PSI Endpoint Scanner: Automatically discovers and indexes all @RestController endpoints across all project modules in real-time.
  • Instant DTO Schema Sync: Generates mock JSON request bodies directly from Java DTO classes, POJOs, and Records with recursive reference protection.
  • Spring Cloud Gateway Support: Automatically resolves Gateway routing rules (StripPrefix, PrefixPath, RewritePath) and microservice context paths.
  • Global Authentication Sharing: Configure Bearer JWT tokens or custom auth headers once and sync them across all endpoints with a single click.
  • Custom Collections & Requests: Create manual requests and custom folders alongside scanned project endpoints for external API testing.
  • Dev-Friendly SSL: Built-in Trust-All SSL handler for local microservices running on self-signed HTTPS certificates.
  • Workspace Persistence: Automatically saves query parameters, headers, and request payloads per project across IDE restarts.
  • Instant cURL Export: Copy formatted cURL commands instantly for terminal execution and team collaboration.

Compatibility

• Spring Framework: 5.x, 6.x
• Spring Boot: 2.x, 3.x
• Spring Cloud: Gateway, Eureka, Consul
• Languages: Java 17+, Kotlin | Build Tools: Maven, Gradle

Useful Links

• GitHub Repository
• Issue Tracker
• Changelog
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • IntelliJ Run Configuration Profiles: Resolve active and default profiles from Spring Boot and Application run configurations, including the Active profiles field, explicit environment variables, VM options, and program arguments. Match configurations to their owning modules and read saved Spring Boot configurations even when IntelliJ's Spring Boot plugin is unavailable.
  • Default Profile Configuration: Honor spring.profiles.default in configuration files and constant profile values passed through SpringApplication.setDefaultProperties(Map.of(...)) in Java application main methods, so the corresponding profile files supply service ports and Gateway routes.
  • WebFlux Gateway Configuration: Read routes and discovery locator settings under spring.cloud.gateway.server.webflux while retaining support for the legacy Gateway configuration structure.
  • Profile Cache Refresh: Invalidate resolved configuration when run configurations are added, edited, removed, or selected, and when Java source files change.

idea-plugin.name: Kassi HTTP Data Injector
idea-plugin.description:
Kassi HTTP Data Injector — valid test data straight into your .http requests

Stop hand-typing test IBANs and card numbers into the JetBrains HTTP Client. This plugin inserts spec-valid synthetic data — the same checksummed generators as Kassi Test Data — directly into .http files, formatted for immediate use in a URL, header, or JSON body.

  • IBAN — every European country, ISO 7064 mod-97 valid (plus an invalid variant for negative tests).
  • Card (PAN) — Luhn-valid, from payment-gateway test BIN ranges only, per network (Visa/Mastercard/Amex).
  • BIC/SWIFT — structurally valid, per country.
  • National ID — NL BSN, DE ID card, AU TFN, GB NINo, CY ID — checksum-valid (plus an invalid variant).
  • VAT / Tax ID — CY/DE/NL/GB VAT and AU ABN — checksum-valid (plus an invalid variant).
  • Persona — a coherent identity (name, DOB, address, IBAN, BIC) as a ready-to-paste JSON object.

100% offline and algorithmic. Zero network, zero real PII — every value is synthetic test data covered by a unit test that asserts it passes the real checksum algorithm.

Usage: in a .http file, press Alt+Enter for "Insert test data…", or right-click in the editor, search, pick, and it inserts at the caret.

More Kassi tools for QA & fintech: Kassi Test Data — generate valid IBANs, cards, BIC/SWIFT, VAT and national IDs; and Checksum & Regex Playground.

Source, issues & docs: github.com/VadimToptunov/kassi-plugins
idea-plugin.change-notes:

idea-plugin.name: Robot Framework Pro
idea-plugin.description:
Robot Framework Pro

First-class support for Robot Framework test suites and resource files in IntelliJ-based IDEs — the QA-automation tooling the platform has never had properly. Works in .robot and .resource files.

  • Editing: syntax highlighting (sections, comments, ${scalar} / @{list} / &{dict} / %{env} variables), structure view and code folding.
  • Navigation & completion: go to a keyword's definition — in the same file or through Resource imports followed transitively — plus autocomplete for your keywords, imported keywords, and the most-used standard-library keywords (BuiltIn / Collections / String) with Quick Documentation.
  • Find Usages: every call of a keyword, across the files that import its resource.
  • Rename refactoring: rename a keyword from its definition or any call; every call updates (multi-word names supported).
  • Localization: files that declare a Language: header are fully supported in all 25 languages Robot Framework ships — navigation, completion, rename and run all understand localized headers.
  • Run & Debug (via the robot CLI): run a suite or a single test from a gutter icon; set line breakpoints that suspend the run, inspect the variables in scope, and step over / into / out.
  • Test Results: after a run, a tool window shows the output.xml as a suite → test → keyword tree with pass/fail/skip, durations and failure messages; double-click a test to jump to its source. No HTML report needed inside the IDE.

Offline and IDE-native. Built for QA engineers who live in Robot Framework day to day.
idea-plugin.change-notes:

Robot Framework support end to end: syntax-aware editing; keyword navigation and autocomplete (including cross-file and transitive Resource imports and standard-library keywords with Quick Documentation); Find Usages; rename refactoring; localization for all 25 languages Robot Framework ships; a run configuration with gutter icons; and step-level debugging — line breakpoints, in-scope variables, and step over / into / out.

idea-plugin.name: Optics Framework

Diagnostics, completion, hover, parameter info, goto-definition, find usages, cross-file rename, structure view, go to symbol and semantic highlighting for optics-framework CSV test suites.
