idea-plugin.name: NodeSpark
idea-plugin.description:
JavaScript and TypeScript (.js, .jsx, .ts, .tsx) test runner for IntelliJ IDEA Community — no WebStorm licence needed.
Runs Jest, Vitest, Mocha and node --test with a real pass/fail test tree, gutter run icons, package.json script running, a CDP debugger, ESLint/Prettier, Run with Coverage, and a key/value grid editor for .env files.

Everything runs against the tools the project already installs in its own node_modules — nothing is downloaded and nothing is installed into your project. Tools are only executed in projects you have marked as trusted.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.5.1
  • On IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2 and later native coverage is switched off for now: the IDE's coverage engine can only be driven there through internal platform API, which a plugin must not use. Run with Coverage, the coverage gutter stripes and the Tools → Node Coverage menu return once the platform offers a public way to do it. Coverage is unchanged on 2026.1 and earlier.
  • File choosers in the run configuration editors and in Settings → NodeSpark no longer call an API the platform has scheduled for removal.
0.5.0
  • A Package tab beside the text editor of a package.json: the manifest fields as a form, the scripts as a grid you can run and debug from, and the dependencies as a filterable table showing what is declared, what is installed and — on request — what the registry has newer. Add a package by searching the registry, remove or update one, and move it between runtime and development, all through the project's own package manager so the lockfile keeps up.
  • NodeSpark now checks package.json, the lockfile and node_modules against each other, for npm, yarn (classic and berry), pnpm and bun. A banner offers the install that fixes the drift — a plain install when the lockfile is behind package.json, a frozen one (npm ci and its equivalents) when only node_modules is behind the lockfile.
  • Coverage is now the IDE's own: a Run with Coverage button beside Run and Debug on a Node test configuration, covered/uncovered stripes in the editor gutter, and per-file and per-directory percentages in the Coverage tool window and the Project view. Jest, Vitest, Mocha (via nyc) and node --test. A report from elsewhere — a CI run, say — still loads through Tools → Node Coverage, which also runs the whole suite at once.
  • Clicking a gutter arrow now opens the same menu as right-clicking it, with Run, Debug and Run with Coverage, instead of starting a plain run straight away.
  • An npm tool window listing every package.json in the project with its scripts beneath it — double-click (or Enter) runs one, and each package shows the manager it actually uses: npm, yarn, pnpm or bun. Scripts also debug from there, and a dependency opens its installed package.json.
  • Settings → NodeSpark → Node.js SDK takes a package manager, so a project whose lockfile says otherwise can be pinned to npm, yarn, pnpm or bun.
0.4.0
  • A key/value grid editor beside the text editor of any .env file, with a per-row "Hide value" mask, a value dropdown sourced from the row's own documenting comment and sibling .env files, and a right-click menu to copy one field at a time.
  • A describe block's gutter icon now rolls up the status of every test beneath it, and turns red at the exact assertion line that failed, with the failure message on hover.
  • Unrun tests now show the same double-arrow / single-arrow icons IntelliJ uses for a JUnit class or method, instead of a NodeSpark-specific icon.
  • Test results now survive an IDE restart instead of resetting to no icon.
0.3.1
  • Same code as 0.3.0, published with the author signature the previous upload was missing, so the IDE no longer warns about an unsigned plugin on install.
0.3.0
  • Gutter run/debug icons no longer depend on a JavaScript PSI, so they finally appear in IntelliJ IDEA Community, where .js is owned by TextMate. They also update as you type and turn into a tick or a cross when a run finishes.
  • Run configurations are named after the whole describe chain (UserService > login > returns a token) rather than "Run Node Tests", and a gutter arrow on a describe runs that suite.
  • Removed the duplicate "Run Node Tests" context-menu entry: the ordinary Run '<file>' item does the same thing.
  • Settings → NodeSpark now detects the Node.js and npm executables, has a file chooser and a Detect button for each, and an absolute path entered there overrides both the SDK and PATH.
0.2.0
  • Reformat Code (Ctrl+Alt+L) now runs the project's own Prettier on .js/.jsx/.ts/.tsx, and code that differs from Prettier's output is highlighted with a "Reformat with Prettier" fix. Both are advisory, both switch off under Settings → NodeSpark → ESLint / Prettier, and neither does anything in a project that has no Prettier of its own.
  • ESLint, Prettier and the npm install banner now respect IDE project trust: nothing from a project's node_modules is executed until the project is trusted.
  • Executables are resolved against PATH rather than the working directory, so a binary committed to a repository can no longer shadow the real node or npm.
  • Jest, Vitest, Mocha and node --test test trees, gutter run icons, package.json script running, CDP debugger and lcov coverage.

idea-plugin.name: MergeSense - xev
idea-plugin.description:
MergeSense — AI Test Case Generator

Generate comprehensive manual test cases from Pull Request diffs, Jira issues, and code analysis — directly inside your IDE.




What is MergeSense?

MergeSense reads your Pull Request diff, Jira issue description, Confluence documentation, and commit history — then uses Claude AI to generate a full set of manual test cases, exported as a structured Excel file.

A QA engineer reviewing a 50-file PR used to spend hours identifying what to test. MergeSense does it in minutes — covering positive paths, negative cases, and edge conditions across every area the change touches, including regression surfaces you might not have considered.

Key Features

  • PR-first diff analysis — paste any Bitbucket, GitHub, or GitLab PR URL; the plugin fetches the diff, branch info, and PR comments automatically
  • Deep Jira integration — reads issue description, comments, and linked Confluence pages; automatically scans the same Jira project for related issues to surface regression targets
  • Jira key auto-detection — extracts the Jira issue key from the PR title or branch name (e.g. feature/PROJ-1234-new-login)
  • Code-aware context — falls back to local git log history when no PR URL is provided; surfaces changed files and their content
  • Claude AI generation — sends structured context to Claude and receives a typed, prioritized test case set in JSON
  • Excel export — outputs a formatted .xlsx file named {JIRA-KEY} - {summary}.xlsx

How It Works

1. Paste a PR URL  ──►  Plugin fetches diff + PR comments
          │
2. Jira issue resolved  ──►  Description, comments, Confluence pages
          │
3. Project scan  ──►  Related Jira issues for regression context
          │
4. Claude AI analysis  ──►  Every changed function, endpoint, UI flow
          │
5. Structured output  ──►  Positive ✅ · Negative ❌ · Edge ⚠️
          │
6. Excel export  ──►  {JIRA-KEY} - {summary}.xlsx

Supported Platforms

Source Control

Platform URL Format Auth
Bitbucket Cloud bitbucket.org/workspace/repo/pull-requests/ID Username + App Password
Bitbucket Server / DC company.com/projects/PRJ/repos/repo/pull-requests/ID Username + PAT
GitHub github.com/owner/repo/pull/ID Personal Access Token
GitLab gitlab.com/group/repo/-/merge_requests/ID Personal Access Token

Project Management

Platform Auth
Jira Server / Data Center PAT (Bearer Token)
Jira Cloud Basic Auth — email + API token
Confluence Server / DC / Cloud PAT or Basic Auth

Installation

From JetBrains Marketplace

  1. Open Settings → Plugins → Marketplace
  2. Search for MergeSense
  3. Click Install and restart the IDE

From a local build

  1. Download mergeSenseIdePlugin-x.x.x.zip from Releases
  2. Open Settings → Plugins → ⚙ → Install Plugin from Disk
  3. Select the .zip file and restart

Configuration

Open Settings → Tools → MergeSense Test Generator.

Jira

Field Notes
Jira URL https://jira.yourcompany.com — no trailing slash
Auth type PAT for Server/DC · Basic for Cloud
Username Leave blank for PAT; your email for Cloud Basic Auth
Token Personal Access Token or API token

Confluence (optional)

Same URL and auth pattern as Jira. If left unconfigured, Confluence pages linked inside the Jira issue are still fetched automatically via the Jira remote link API.

Bitbucket (optional — required for self-hosted)

Field Notes
Bitbucket URL https://bitbucket.yourcompany.com — omit for Bitbucket Cloud
Username Your Bitbucket username
Token Personal Access Token

GitHub / GitLab (optional)

A single Personal Access Token field covers both platforms — the plugin detects the URL format automatically.

  • GitHub: Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → repo scope required
  • GitLab: User Settings → Access Tokens → read_api scope required

Anthropic / Claude

Field Notes
API Token sk-ant-api03-… from console.anthropic.com
Model claude-opus-4-5 (default), claude-sonnet-4-5, claude-opus-5

No API key? Leave the token field blank and export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN as an environment variable, then launch IntelliJ from the terminal. The plugin falls back to the Claude CLI automatically.

export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=your_token_here
/Applications/IntelliJ\ IDEA.app/Contents/MacOS/idea

Usage

Mode 1 — From a Jira Issue ID

  1. Open the MergeSense tool window (View → Tool Windows → MergeSense)
  2. Enter a Jira Issue ID — e.g. PROJ-1234 — and click Get Info
  3. Confirm the issue description loaded correctly
  4. Set the output directory
  5. Click Generate Test Cases

Mode 2 — From a Pull Request URL (recommended)

  1. Paste the PR URL into the PR URL field
  2. Click Get PR Info — the diff is fetched and the Jira Issue ID is auto-filled if found in the PR title or branch name
  3. Optionally enter notes in Additional Requirements
  4. Click Generate Test Cases

The plugin collects context in this order before calling Claude:

PR diff + comments  →  Jira issue  →  Related project issues  →  Confluence pages  →  git history

Output Format

Each generated test case contains:

Field Description
ID TC-001, TC-002…
Type POSITIVE ✅ / NEGATIVE ❌ / EDGE ⚠️
Priority Critical / High / Medium / Low
Title Scenario name (Turkish)
Preconditions State required before the test
Steps Numbered action steps
Expected Result What success looks like
Notes Additional context
Module Biletleme · Check-in · Login · Manage Booking · Ödeme · IRROPS · General · Standalone
Test Layer End to End · API · Component

Minimum generation targets: 6 positive, 6 negative, 4 edge cases — growing with PR complexity.

Requirements

Requirement Version
IntelliJ IDEA 2024.1 or newer (any edition — CE, Ultimate)
Java runtime 17+ (bundled with IntelliJ)
Jira Server, Data Center, or Cloud
Claude Anthropic API key or Claude CLI with ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN

Privacy & Security

Credentials are stored in IntelliJ's encrypted settings store (MergeSenseSettings.xml in the IDE configuration directory). No data is sent to any third party other than:

  • Your Jira / Confluence / Bitbucket / GitHub / GitLab instance (over HTTPS)
  • Anthropic's API at api.anthropic.com

PR diffs and Jira content are sent to Claude only during test case generation and are not retained by the plugin.

License

MIT License — see LICENSE for details.

idea-plugin.name: Compose Testability Linter
idea-plugin.description:
Compose Testability Linter — find the Compose UI your UI tests can't locate

Jetpack Compose removed a guarantee the View system enforced. findViewById did not work without an android:id, so every interactive View had one. Compose requires nothing — and measured across eleven real open-source apps the share of interactive elements carrying a stable identity drops from 90–99% (XML) to 6–27% (Compose). This plugin flags, while you type, the interactive composables an accessibility-tree UI test (Appium / UiAutomator / Maestro) cannot reliably find.

  • Interactive composable without a stable test identity — a Button, TextField, a Modifier.clickable container, or one of your own design-system wrappers, with no testTag, semantics identity or contentDescription. Aware of your project's own wrappers, not just framework components — the number a name-only linter gets wrong by ~5×.
  • Duplicate test identity — the same testTag literal on more than one element in a file, so an accessibility-tree locator matches both and can target neither uniquely. A non-unique id fails differently from a missing one.
  • Test tags never exposed — a module that sets testTag but never enables testTagsAsResourceId, so Appium / UiAutomator / Maestro see none of the tags.
  • Targetability coverage % — a "Testability" tool window scores the whole project: interactive elements with a stable identity ÷ all interactive elements (the denominator counts your wrapper calls too), per-module and total, with HTML/JSON export.
  • Quick-fix — insert Modifier.testTag(...) with a name derived from the screen, role and any text literal (e.g. login_submit_button).

Free and offline. No telemetry, no network, no AI at runtime. This is for accessibility-tree automation (Appium/UiAutomator/Maestro); for pure Compose UI Test, Google recommends matching on semantics first — and contentDescription doubles as the accessibility id either way.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.0

  • New inspection KTL-C02 — duplicate test identity: the same testTag literal on two or more elements in a file, which an accessibility-tree locator (Appium/UiAutomator/Maestro) cannot target uniquely. Complements KTL-C01 (missing identity); interpolated per-item tags are correctly treated as unique.

1.0.1

  • Internal: use the current read-action API (dropping a method scheduled for removal on newer IDE platforms). No behavior change.

1.0.0

  • First release: the wrapper-aware KTL-C01 inspection (interactive composable without a stable test identity) with a testTag quick-fix, the testTagsAsResourceId module advisory, and a "Testability" tool window reporting targetability-coverage % per module with HTML/JSON export. Compose-only, fully syntactic (no project compilation), free and offline.

idea-plugin.name: Saffron
idea-plugin.description:
Saffron language support for JetBrains IDEs: IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, Rider, and the rest, including Community editions.

Saffron is an end-to-end test runner for the web where you write tests in plain language, with no step definitions and no glue code. The first time a scenario runs, an AI agent drives a real browser and records what it did; every run after that replays the recording at zero AI calls and zero tokens. When the UI changes, the agent heals the step mid-run and files a proposal you review, and Then steps are never healed. .saffron is Saffron's own test language: it reads your .feature files too, and goes further than Gherkin with StepSet: for reusable step groups, {env:VAR} tokens that keep secrets out of recordings and reports, and {data:...} references to your data files.

This plugin gives you, out of the box:

  • Syntax highlighting for .saffron files: Gherkin keywords, StepSet definitions and invocations, tables, doc strings, parameters.
  • Completion with status badges: every step the project knows, marked recorded (replays free), divergent, or unrecorded, so you reuse wordings instead of paying for near-duplicate recordings.
  • StepSet completion, go-to-definition and hover: jump from an invocation to its definition, even across files.
  • Diagnostics: unknown or duplicate set names, a set name missing the StepSet keyword, near-duplicate step wordings.
  • Run configurations: a Saffron entry under Add New Configuration (run files, folders or tags, replay-only, headed, re-record; open the report; accept proposals; open the execution replay of a scenario), and right-click → Run on any .saffron file or folder.
  • Saffron tool window with Files, Last Run, Proposals, CI Runs, Tags, Health, Orphans and Dashboard tabs: feature files with scenario counts and Run Selected / Run All; what failed in the last run, with a screenshot of the page one double-click away and Open Replay to step through the run in your browser, the page inspectable at every action (with saffron-ai 0.9.0 or later); proposals to tick, read and accept or reject; the current branch's GitHub Actions or Azure Pipelines runs; tags to tick and run; vocabulary health (divergent steps, near-duplicate wordings) and the effective config; recordings no scenario owns any more, removable in one action; and the run report embedded in the IDE.
  • Review a heal made in CI: CI Runs lists the branch's runs, shows what a selected run found without importing it (its failed and healed scenarios, its report and replays, with saffron-ai 0.9.7 or later), Import Run brings a run's proposals into your checkout, checked against your files, and you accept or reject them in Proposals like your own (needs saffron-ai 0.9.3 or later, with gh or az signed in).

Intelligence is served by saffron lsp from the saffron-ai npm package (npm i -D saffron-ai in your project) through the free LSP4IJ plugin. Install LSP4IJ to switch them on; highlighting, run configurations and the tool window need nothing else.

Website and docs: saffron-ai.io. Source: github.com/s-chathuranga-j/saffron-jetbrains-plugin. Issues: GitHub.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.6.2

  • Browser matrix rows say their browser (saffron-ai 0.9.9 or later). After saffron run --browser chromium,firefox,webkit, the Last Run and CI Runs tabs list a scenario once per browser, labelled with it (Checkout · firefox), and the replay opens that browser's execution alone (feature:scenario@browser) instead of every browser's. With an older runner nothing changes.

0.6.1

  • Health's pass rate of recent runs is the runner's (saffron-ai 0.9.8 or later): a heal whose proof failed does not pass, as on the Dashboard.
  • Run one scenario from the editor. With LSP4IJ installed, ▶ Run scenario, Replay only and Headed above each scenario run it alone, by name, through a temporary run configuration made for it, which stays in the run widget. A saved configuration of that name is never changed, nothing from the Saffron template carries in, a scenario of the same name in another file, or another nested project, gets its own, and the lenses work while the IDE indexes. Needs saffron-ai 0.9.8 or later; with an older runner a click says so.
  • Right-click Run inside a scenario runs that scenario alone, with or without LSP4IJ, and never reuses a lens's Replay only or Headed configuration. Outside a scenario, or in a file in another Gherkin language, it runs the whole file as before.
  • Open Trace works on a CI run with every runner, and keeps the download limit. With saffron-ai 0.9.8 it passes --max-download to saffron trace, which downloads a run no longer on disk; with 0.9.7, which rejects the option, it leaves it out.
  • Open Trace finds a Scenario Outline's example row. It named the scenario without its "(example 1)" suffix, which matched no trace; it now uses the name the run shows.
  • Yellow results read "pending review", not "healed". Yellow also covers first recordings and proposals not yet verified. A scenario the run could not verify says "unverified", a verified one says "verified", and one the run does not report on says nothing.

0.6.0

  • CI Runs shows what a run found, without importing it. Select a run and its results load under it: the totals, each failed and healed scenario with its failing step and first error line (the healing narrative in the tooltip), and "N proposals: M importable" with the reason for each one that is not. Loading is a background task you can cancel, runs only while the tab is on screen, and is kept per project until you choose another project or press Refresh. Needs saffron-ai 0.9.7 or later (saffron report --run); with an older runner the run says so.
  • Open Report opens the selected run's HTML report in your browser, and Open Trace (or a double-click) replays a failed or healed scenario that kept a trace. Neither files anything: Import Run stays the only action that brings proposals into this checkout.
  • A run with no results says why: still running, expired, or none uploaded (the guide's workflow uploads only on failure unless the export and upload steps use if: always()).
  • Large results ask first. Above the download limit, the tab asks "This run's results are N MB. Download?". The limit is in Settings, Tools, Saffron (default 100 MB; 0 for no limit), the same as VS Code's saffron.ciMaxDownloadMB.

0.5.1

  • The Dashboard never shows another project's page. A page still loading when you switched projects, or when the tab was hidden, could land afterwards and stay on screen; it is now dropped. Clicking a scenario opens it in the project the page was made for.
  • With saffron-ai 0.9.5, the Failing count includes a scenario that failed and has not run in the last 10 runs, as the health bar does.

0.5.0

  • The Dashboard is the suite's quality page, rendered by saffron dashboard in the run report's design and the same as in VS Code: tests, the share passing, failing scenarios and for how many runs in a row, flaky ones, ones the agent healed again and again, never run and left out of the last run, the slowest, pass rate and execution time over the last 20 runs, and results per tag. Click a scenario's name to open it. Needs saffron-ai 0.9.4 or later; with an older runner the tab says which version the project has.
  • Last Run: Open Report opens the run's HTML report in your browser.
  • Last Run: Open Replay works when everything passed. With no row to select it did nothing; it now opens every scenario the run traced, or says how to keep traces when the run kept none.

0.4.0

  • CI Runs tab. The current branch's CI runs, GitHub Actions or Azure Pipelines, through saffron runs. Import runs saffron import --run and lists under the run what happened to each proposal and any warning. The Proposals tab names the CI run an imported proposal came from. From a red CI run to an accepted repair without leaving the IDE; the CI's own tool keeps the credentials. Needs saffron-ai 0.9.3 or later, with gh or az signed in; with an older runner the tab says which version the project has.
  • Text from CI is shown as plain text, in CI Runs and in Last Run after an import, never as markup. Import is a background task you can cancel; a run is imported once even if you switch projects meanwhile; Refresh never starts a second list. The tab loads as soon as the project is trusted, and its processes stop when the project closes.
  • Choosing another project clears the tabs at once: a run listed for the last project can no longer be imported into the new one, and a status that arrives late for the last project is dropped. CI Runs lists again when you check out another branch. A cancelled import says it may have written part of the run.
  • A runner error is shown, not "No CI runs". When saffron runs fails with an error, CI Runs shows the runner's reason under "CI runs unavailable".
  • A tool window button never changes a saved configuration. Run Selected on one file used the name of a right-click configuration, Run login.saffron, and reset a saved one of that name, tags and extra arguments included. The buttons now reuse only temporary configurations, and use Saffron: Run login.saffron when a saved one has the name.
  • The Dashboard opens a web page only when you click a link. A navigation started by the report itself, or inside a frame of it, is cancelled instead of opening your browser.
  • Project trust is checked without the API deprecated in 2025.1, and still works on 2024.2.
  • The README names the real fallback command, npx -y -p saffron-ai saffron lsp, and lists the reject, prune and login run configuration commands.

0.3.1

  • The tool window opens on IntelliJ 2026.2. The Dashboard tab no longer fails with NoClassDefFoundError (JBCefApp): 2026.2 moved the embedded browser into its own plugin, which Saffron now depends on where it exists. Without it the Dashboard offers Open in Browser.
  • Open Replay opens the run its row lists. A row shown for one run no longer opens a later run's trace; the runner refuses it and says to refresh. Needs saffron-ai 0.9.1 or later; with an older runner it opens the scenario as before.

0.3.0

  • Open Replay in the Last Run tab runs saffron trace for the selected scenario, by feature and scenario name so two features with a scenario of the same name are told apart, and opens its execution replay in your browser: the steps as written, the page at every action, the network alongside. trace is also a run configuration command, taking a scenario name or feature:scenario (quotes optional); blank opens every traced scenario. Needs saffron-ai 0.9.0 or later, with "trace": "retain-on-failure" (or "on") in saffron.config.json.
  • A screenshot stays with its run. Opening one from Last Run checks it against the digest its run recorded, so a picture a later run put at the same path is refused instead of shown as this run's, and what opens is a copy of the picture that was checked, named after its scenario (buy-shoes-failure.jpg). The copies are kept in the IDE's own system folder and removed after a day. The digests come from the same saffron-ai release; with an older runner a screenshot opens unchecked, as before.
  • Double-clicking a row whose screenshot is gone or was replaced says so, naming the scenario, instead of jumping to the feature file over that message. The message goes when you pick another row.
  • Accept Selected and Reject Selected act only on the proposal you saw. A run that files a new proposal under the same name while it is ticked used to have that one accepted unseen. The tick now stays with the proposal that was shown, the replacement comes back unticked, and the runner refuses a proposal that changed since it was listed. Needs saffron-ai 0.9.0 or later; an older runner decides on the file as before.

0.2.5

  • Stale proposals are marked. The Proposals tab shows STALE for a proposal that can no longer be accepted as reviewed (a step edited, a colleague's heal accepted, a pull since it was filed), with the reason and what to do: run the scenario again for a fresh proposal, or reject it. A proposal filed by an older runner is noted as one whose later changes cannot be detected. Needs saffron-ai 0.8.5 or later.

0.2.4

  • {data:...} and {unique:...} tokens are highlighted like {env:VAR}, including on an Examples: line. Completion of data files and keys, the value on hover, go-to-definition into the JSON and an error for a reference that does not resolve come from saffron lsp in the matching saffron-ai release.
  • The Orphans tab lists screenshot folders of scenarios that no longer exist, alongside caches and proposals.

0.2.3

  • A Last Run tab. Failed scenarios, then healed ones, with the step that failed. Double-click opens the screenshot of the page at the moment it went wrong in the IDE's image viewer; Open Scenario jumps to it in the feature file. Needs the saffron-ai release with failure screenshots; with an older runner the tab says so instead of claiming everything passed.
  • Links point at saffron-ai.io, and issues go to the public community repository.

0.2.2

  • LSP4IJ is now an optional dependency. The plugin used to refuse to install on an IDE build that LSP4IJ had not been released for yet, which is every new EAP for a while (reported by the Marketplace verifier on 2026.3 EAP). Highlighting, run configurations and the Saffron tool window need nothing from LSP4IJ and now work without it; completion, go-to-definition, hover and diagnostics switch on when LSP4IJ is installed. A one-time notification says so when it is missing.
  • The Proposals tab shows what a proposal changes: selecting one loads saffron diff under the narrative, so you approve the action list, not only the agent's account of it. Needs saffron-ai 0.6.1 or later.
  • Accept Selected with nothing ticked used to accept every proposal: blank paths mean --all to the runner. It now does nothing and says so, and bulk acceptance stays its own action.
  • An Orphans tab: caches and pending proposals whose scenario no longer exists, grouped and explained (the scenario is gone from the file, or the file itself is gone). Double-click opens the recording; Remove All runs saffron prune --yes after a confirmation. prune is also a run configuration command, where listing is the default and deleting is opt-in. Needs the saffron-ai release that added saffron prune.
  • The Proposals tab could show an old diff beside a new narrative. Diffs were cached by file name, and a new run overwrites a proposal under the same name, so Accept could promote something the reviewer never read. Every refresh now invalidates the diffs, a diff that finishes loading after a refresh is discarded, and the cache is only touched on the UI thread.
  • A path with a space stays one path. features/order checkout.saffron was split into two arguments, including for right-clicked and ticked files. Paths are now parsed like a command line (quotes keep a path whole), and whatever the plugin writes itself is quoted to match.

0.2.1

  • The Saffron tool window gains four tabs next to Files. Proposals: tick proposals, read the narrative, proof-replay verdict and cost, then Accept Selected, Reject Selected or Accept All. Tags: every @tag with its scenario count; tick and Run Tagged. Health: vocabulary counts, divergent steps, near-duplicate wordings, the effective config with one click to the file. Dashboard: the HTML report embedded in the IDE, reloaded after each run. The tabs read saffron status --json (saffron-ai 0.5.4 or later).
  • Run configurations: accept and reject take proposal files (blank means all).
  • Verifier clean on 2026.3.

0.2.0

  • Saffron run configurations: Run/Debug Configurations → Add New Configuration → Saffron. Choose run (files or folders, tags, replay-only, headed, re-record, extra arguments), report or accept. Output goes to the Run tool window; configurations can be stored as project files and shared.
  • Right-click to run: a .saffron file (project view or editor) or a folder holding them gets a "Run" entry, and the configuration it creates stays in the run widget.
  • Saffron tool window (right side, shown in Saffron projects): every feature file with its scenario count, search, tick files and Run Selected, Run All, Open Report, Accept All Proposals, plus the last run's totals and the number of proposals pending review. Double-click opens a file.
  • Runs use the project's own saffron-ai install (npx as a fallback) with the login shell's environment, so Node from nvm or Homebrew is found when the IDE was started from the Dock.
  • Go-to-definition and hover on {env:VAR} tokens open the variable in .env or .env.example (served by saffron-ai 0.5.2 or later).

0.1.2

  • Quoted arguments, <placeholders> and {env:...} / {date...} tokens are highlighted as parameters, like Cucumber, instead of the whole step line sharing one colour.

0.1.1

  • Fallback launch without a project-local install now runs npx -p saffron-ai saffron lsp (the bare saffron name resolves an unrelated npm package).
  • The "install saffron-ai" hint shows once per project instead of on every open.

  • Language server integration via LSP4IJ: completion with recorded/divergent/unrecorded badges, StepSet completion, go-to-definition, hover, diagnostics. For .saffron and .feature files.
  • Runs the project-local saffron-ai binary when installed, npx saffron lsp otherwise; friendly notification when the package is missing.

idea-plugin.name: SQLAlchemy Log Free
idea-plugin.description:
SQLAlchemy Log Free

Restore SQLAlchemy SQL logs to executable SQL statements with parameters automatically filled in PyCharm & IntelliJ IDEs.

  • Automatically capture SQL logs from SQLAlchemy engine output.
  • Reconstruct parameterized queries (?, %s, %(name)s, :name, $1) with bound Python parameter values.
  • Support complex Python types: None, datetime, date, time, Decimal, UUID, boolean, batch lists.
  • Dedicated Tool Window with real-time log output and syntax color highlighting.
  • SQL formatting (Pretty Print) toggle.
  • Quick navigation between SQL queries.
  • Filter logs by keywords and customize SQL colors.

1.0.0
Initial release of SQLAlchemy Log Free plugin for PyCharm and IntelliJ IDEs.

idea-plugin.name: GitLabPlus
idea-plugin.description:
GitLabPlus - Create and view GitLab Merge Requests in IntelliJ IDEA. 在 IDE 中快速创建 / 查看 GitLab Merge Request。
  • 自动识别当前项目的 GitLab 远程仓库

idea-plugin.name: axx
idea-plugin.description:
Support for axx acceptance tests.
  • Feature files. In projects with an axx.yaml, runs the axx language server (axx lsp) for .feature files: step completion, step documentation on hover, go to a step's definition, links to, path completion for and checks of the files steps name, highlighted step parameters, and diagnostics for undefined or ambiguous steps and Gherkin syntax errors. The Gherkin plugin no longer reports axx steps as undefined there. Needs the axx executable (found on PATH or where axx's installers put it, or set in Settings | Tools | axx) and an IDE that includes the LSP API, as IntelliJ IDEA does.
  • Running scenarios. Run and debug icons in the gutter of Feature, Rule, Scenario and Scenario Outline lines and Examples rows, and in the context menu of feature files and directories; the results show in the IDE's test runner, with navigation to each line, expected and actual values of failed assertions, and Rerun Failed Tests. Debugging stops at breakpoints in step code with GoLand or the Go plugin.
  • Watching the browsers. Watch, next to Run and Debug, runs web scenarios with their browsers in windows on your desktop as they go, slowed down, one scenario at a time, with their DevTools at hand. Debug pauses a scenario at breakpoints on its steps and where it fails, with the page in Playwright's Inspector. While it is paused, the element of the step under the caret is highlighted in the page, Run Step in Paused Scenario runs a step in it, and Insert Recorded Steps inserts the steps recorded in the Inspector. The traces and videos scenarios keep open from the test runner, in editor tabs: traces in Playwright's trace viewer, videos in a player.
  • Debugging apps. When axx run --debug, run from the IDE, starts a service in debug mode, the plugin starts the matching Debugger: <service> run configuration (generated by axx ide intellij), so the services under test attach to the IDE with no manual steps. The debuggers it started stop again when the run ends.

idea-plugin.name: DATAMIMIC
idea-plugin.description:
Work on DATAMIMIC projects in your JetBrains IDE, connected to your DATAMIMIC Enterprise Platform.

Requires a DATAMIMIC Enterprise Platform and an account on it. The plugin does not work without one; standalone DATAMIMIC CE projects are not supported.

  • Sign in with your platform account and browse your projects in the DATAMIMIC tool window.
  • Open a platform project as a normal local project. Files sync both ways, protected by the platform's edit locks; changes on both sides show a conflict banner.
  • Completion and checks from the platform's language server, with a status bar switch to turn it on or off for the project.
  • Generate data from the project window or a native Run Configuration, then follow platform status, logs, refresh errors, and preview samples when available.
  • Browse recent generation tasks and reopen their results. Successful tasks expose artifacts that can be saved individually, opened as text in the IDE, or downloaded together as a ZIP.
  • Connect IDE agents to the project's MCP server.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Generation history, previews, and artifacts are now first-class IDE workflows, with automatic project-scoped Junie MCP access and a cleaner task UI.

Features

  • Browse generation task history and reopen status, logs, preview samples, and artifacts from successful tasks.
  • Save individual artifacts, open saved text files in the IDE, or download all artifacts as a ZIP.
  • Connect Junie to the active project's MCP server with a short-lived project access token created from the existing platform session, renewed automatically, and kept in local Git-ignored configuration.
  • Add default-off, project-scoped AI Assistant MCP publication in .ai/mcp/mcp.json; it preserves user entries and removes only the exact managed entry on disable or disconnect.

Improvements

  • Show artifacts in results from native DATAMIMIC Generation Run Configurations as well as in task history.
  • Consolidate preview samples into one selectable Preview tab, rename the tool window to Generation Tasks, and use distinct native icons plus a compact gears-only plugin logo.
  • Keep newly accepted tasks visible while the platform persists them, and prevent artifact saves from overwriting concurrent IDE edits.
  • Keep Junie on project-scoped DATAMIMIC MCP tools, give it the canonical capability/build/bounded-dry-run/commit authoring loop, and leave data generation as an explicit user action.

Fixes

  • Fix generation task history with the Platform 4.0.1 task API and show useful validation details for rejected requests.
  • Refresh plugin-managed Junie files in the IDE after registration, renewal, and cleanup.
  • Publish Junie steering through the guidance path used by the supported runtime without overwriting user guidance.
  • Recognize and safely migrate full guidance generated by earlier development builds instead of reporting it as user-owned.
  • Ignore Junie's transient .output.json scratch file so it cannot block a generation run after the agent removes it.
  • Make the development artifact downloaded from GitHub Actions directly installable in JetBrains IDEs.

idea-plugin.name: Piwi
idea-plugin.description:
Your Playwright suite's history in the IDE, from a Piwi instance:
  • the failures of the latest CI run on the checked-out branch, as your local runs since leave them, at their failing lines, with the recommended locator heal as a quick fix, the trace and the screenshot one action away;
  • the Piwi tool window: the latest run's failures as a tree, grouped by file, cluster or owner, with the runs you made since, compared with the branch's latest run, another branch's, a run by its id or your local runs only, and each test re-run, its trace and screenshot one right-click away; a run started from Piwi pauses at your breakpoints in the browser, where a locator you pick replaces the one on that line;
  • each test's latest result in the gutter, a failing test's body tinted, and the tests behind each locator line and each application file;
  • brittle locators, and the locators an unsaved change breaks, with quick fixes;
  • the latest run in the status bar, with the run you started as it runs, its tests in the gutter as they end, and what it changed once it ended; read again on a click; and Piwi's MCP server for your AI assistant;
  • tests recorded in a browser your project's own Playwright opens, written at the caret as you click and type, with calls to your page objects and helpers when connected, and removed in one undo;
  • locators and recorded flows sent from the Piwi Picker browser extension, inserted at the caret;
  • the source paths clicked in the dashboard, opened at their line in the project that holds them.
It reads the connection the Piwi reporter uses (the environment, the workspace .env, the Piwi desktop app); otherwise connect under Settings → Tools → Piwi, signing in with the browser. The Piwi desktop app sits beside a shared instance: Connect switches between them, keeping both. Works in WebStorm, IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate, Rider and the other IDEs with the LSP API and JavaScript support.

idea-plugin.name: Test Space
idea-plugin.description:
Make Java test method names readable without changing your source code.

Test Space displays underscores as spaces and optionally splits camelCase. Method references, refactoring, and test runner names keep the original identifier.

  • Supports JUnit 3 TestCase methods, JUnit 4, JUnit Jupiter, TestNG method annotations, and composed test annotations.
  • Preserves acronyms and names referenced by the test body when splitting camelCase.
  • Expands names for editing when the caret touches them.
  • Offers a custom color scheme style or standard editor folding.

Configure under Settings | Editor | Test Space.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Initial release: readable Java test names, configurable formatting, custom styling, and caret-aware expansion.

idea-plugin.name: Rowcast
idea-plugin.description:
Run an API call once for every row of real data, and see what actually came back.

Rowcast takes rows from your data and a curl command. It turns them into many real requests and records every response, with a curl you can replay for each one.

What it does

  • Real data in. Read rows from JSONL files, MongoDB, or SQL databases over JDBC (SQL Server, DB2, SQLite). Join sources on a shared field.
  • Map fields to the request. Bind a column to any part of the curl: path, query, header, or body, including JSON inside a Base64 header.
  • Whole flows, not single calls. Chain steps. A value one step returns, like an id, feeds the next step's request.
  • See the results. An HTML report with status counts per step, response times, and example failures with their curl.
  • Check a flow before you run it. The audit finds values you pasted with a curl but never bound, like a fixed id that should come from your data.

Getting started

  1. Open the Rowcast tool window.
  2. Add a source, and paste a curl.
  3. Bind fields to the request, preview a few rows, then run.

Passwords are kept in the IDE password store, never in your flow files. Rowcast sends nothing anywhere except the requests you set up.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
First public release.

  • Sources: JSONL files, MongoDB, and SQL databases over JDBC (SQL Server, DB2, SQLite).
  • Multi-step flows: a value one step returns feeds the next step.
  • Bind data to any part of a curl: path, query, header, or body.
  • HTML run report with a replayable curl for each failure.
  • Flow audit: finds pasted values that were never bound.

idea-plugin.name: WebhookMon - Webhook Inspector & Replay
idea-plugin.description:
See, verify and replay webhooks from Stripe, Polar, GitHub, Shopify and Slack without leaving the IDE. A Webhooks tool window gives you a public URL on the WebhookMon relay; every delivery shows up with a signature check and a plain-language reason when it fails (wrong secret, timestamp outside tolerance, malformed header).

  • Auto-forward live webhooks to localhost, with no tunnel to set up.
  • Signature verification with your signing secret, kept in the IDE's password safe.
  • Pro: replay any event into the run configuration or debug session you are running, re-signed with a fresh timestamp, so breakpoints hit on demand.
  • Pro: save an event as a test fixture plus a JUnit 5 + MockMvc test that re-signs it at test time.
  • Pro: signed sample events for each provider, without a provider account.

Events are end-to-end encrypted to your devices: the relay cannot read them. Free: one endpoint and the last 20 events. Pro (30-day trial): up to 10 endpoints, 1,000 events, replay, fixtures and samples.

Keywords: webhook, Stripe, Shopify, GitHub App, Slack, Polar, ngrok alternative, tunnel, replay, signature, HMAC.

getwebhookmon.com · Privacy · License
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• First release: receive, verify and auto-forward webhooks from Stripe, Polar, GitHub, Shopify and Slack.
  • Pro: replay into run and debug sessions, run-configuration targets, fixtures with JUnit/MockMvc tests, signed samples.

idea-plugin.name: Rust Native
idea-plugin.description:
Full Rust language support for IntelliJ IDEA, GoLand and other JetBrains IDEs, powered by its own analysis engine. No rust-analyzer required.

  • Completion with auto-import, inlay hints, quick documentation, find usages and refactorings

idea-plugin.name: pytest Fixtures - Valid Test Data
idea-plugin.description:
pytest Fixtures — valid test data

Generate a pytest parametrized test whose cases are spec-valid values — and their invalid variants — straight from the Kassi engine. Unlike a hand-rolled faker, every value passes the real checksum, so your test exercises the validator with data that is actually valid (and edge cases that are actually invalid). Fully offline.

  • IBAN — ISO 7064 mod-97 valid, several countries, each with a bad-checksum variant.
  • Card (PAN) — Luhn-valid per network, each with a fails-Luhn variant.

Open it from View ▸ Tool Windows ▸ pytest Fixtures, pick a kind, Generate, then Copy the @pytest.mark.parametrize test into your package. Platform-only — installs in PyCharm and every IntelliJ-based IDE.

More Kassi tools for QA & fintech: Kassi Test Data, Checksum & Regex Playground.

Source, issues & docs: github.com/VadimToptunov/kassi-plugins
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.0

  • First release: generate pytest parametrized tests for IBAN and Card (PAN) validation — valid values and their invalid variants, from the checksummed Kassi engine.

idea-plugin.name: Go Test Data

Go Test Data

idea-plugin.name: Pasforge: Pascal Build & Run
idea-plugin.description:
Compile, run and test Free Pascal, Lazarus and Delphi code in IntelliJ IDEA, CLion, PyCharm, Rider and every JetBrains IDE. Pasforge takes care of everything that happens after you write the code: toolchains, builds, clickable compiler errors, run configurations with a real interactive console, and unit tests in the native test runner.

Why Pasforge

  • The missing half of Pascal in JetBrains IDEs. Since I-Pascal stopped in 2020, no plugin compiles, runs or tests Pascal. Pasforge does exactly that, and nothing else.
  • Works alone or next to Pascal Flow. With Pascal Flow installed, Pasforge declares no file type and runs on its files: you get Pascal Flow's code insight and Pasforge's builds, with no association conflict. Without any Pascal plugin, Pasforge adds a minimal highlighting so you can work right away.
  • A console that waits for readln. A prompt written before readln shows up before you type, as in a real terminal, on Windows, macOS and Linux.
  • Nothing installed behind your back. Pasforge finds your compilers; it never downloads nor installs anything, makes no network request and collects no telemetry.

Free

  • Toolchains (Settings › Build, Execution, Deployment › Pascal Toolchains): Free Pascal, Lazarus and RAD Studio found automatically (PATH, usual folders, Homebrew, fpcupdeluxe, Windows registry), checked by compiling an empty program, chosen per project or per module. A missing tool comes with the command that installs it.
  • Compile and run a program (.pas, .pp, .dpr, .lpr) with arguments, working folder and environment variables; Debug and Release modes.
  • Clickable compiler messages in the Build tool window, to the line and the column, and underlined in the editor until the next build; notes and hints on demand. Linker errors included.
  • Interactive console with clickable run-time error back traces (line 12 of unit1.pas).
  • Compile the current file (Ctrl+Shift+F9), with the paths and defines of its Lazarus project.
  • Minimal Pascal highlighting when no Pascal language plugin is installed.

Pasforge Pro

  • Lazarus projects (.lpi, built with lazbuild) and Delphi projects, in preview (.dproj and .groupproj with MSBuild, lone .dpr with dcc32/dcc64): build modes, configurations, target platforms, search paths and defines read from the project. Project files are never rewritten. Delphi support is a preview: tell us about any compiler message that does not show up as a node in the Build tool window.
  • Unit tests: FPCUnit and DUnitX (preview) suites in the IDE test runner, green and red, durations, messages, expected/actual diff, rerun failed tests, run a test or a class from the gutter.
  • New Project wizard: console program, library, Lazarus application, FPCUnit or DUnitX test project.
  • Run from the gutter, external terminal for full-screen text programs (unit crt), Rebuild All.

Try Pasforge Pro free for 30 days. The free features never expire.

Pasforge is an independent product of KITSS TECH. Delphi and RAD Studio are trademarks of Embarcadero Technologies, Inc.; Pasforge is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Embarcadero, the Free Pascal team or the Lazarus team.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Pascal Toolchains settings: Free Pascal, Lazarus and RAD Studio found automatically (PATH, usual folders, Homebrew, fpcupdeluxe, Windows registry), checked by compiling an empty program, chosen per project or per module. Nothing is ever downloaded or installed.
  • Install help for a missing compiler: the command for apt, dnf, pacman, Homebrew or Chocolatey and the official download page, in the editor banner, the Build tool window and the settings.
  • Builds in the native Build tool window: cancellable, timed, one node per compiler message, opening the file at the line and the column; notes and hints on demand.
  • Compiler messages underlined in the editor until the next build, files with errors marked in the project view.
  • Free Pascal, lazbuild, MSBuild and dcc32/dcc64 messages understood, linker errors and Windows paths with spaces included.
  • Pascal run configurations: program or project, toolchain, build mode, platform, arguments, working folder, environment variables, compile before running.
  • Interactive console: prompts written before readln show up before you type, on Windows, macOS and Linux (pseudo-terminal on macOS and Linux; Free Pascal programs also flush their output after each Write, without touching your files).
  • Clickable run-time error back traces (line 12 of unit1.pas).
  • Compile Pascal File (Ctrl+Shift+F9), with the paths, defines and syntax mode of the file's Lazarus project.
  • Minimal Pascal highlighting, comments and brace matching, only when no Pascal language plugin is installed and only for extensions nobody else owns.
  • Works next to Pascal Flow: no file type declared, run and test markers on its Pascal files.
  • Pro: Lazarus projects (.lpi with lazbuild, build modes, target platforms), never rewritten (--no-write-project).
  • Pro, preview: Delphi projects (.dproj, .groupproj with MSBuild after rsvars.bat, lone .dpr with dcc32/dcc64), configurations and platforms read from the project. Message formats follow the RAD Studio documentation and are still being confirmed on real installations: the Build tool window says so for Delphi builds.
  • Pro: FPCUnit and DUnitX (preview) tests in the IDE test runner, with durations, messages, expected/actual diff, Rerun Failed Tests, and run markers on test classes and methods.
  • Pro: New Project wizard (console program, library, Lazarus application, FPCUnit and DUnitX test projects), run from the gutter, external terminal, Rebuild All.

idea-plugin.name: Show As ...
idea-plugin.description:
A small plugin to display formatted data out of the debugger and console.

Uses IntelliJ's build-in formatting capabilities.
No more need to copy values from debugger or console to a file to format them there. Following formats are supported:
  • JSON
  • XML
Usage:

idea-plugin.name: Advanced JSON Studio
idea-plugin.description:
Advanced JSON Studio: The Intelligent JSON Workspace

Stop wrestling with malformed data. Elevate your development workflow with the most powerful JSON toolkit for the IntelliJ Platform. Advanced JSON Studio isn’t just a formatter—it’s a complete engineering environment designed to handle everything from massive API responses to broken configuration files. It’s the last JSON tool you’ll ever need.

  1. Auto-parse as you type — results update instantly without pressing a button.
  2. Support converting JSON5, JSON, YAML, XML, TOML, Properties, JWT, CBOR and BSON in a single unified interface.
  3. Present JSON in a clean, readable format with automated pretty printing.
  4. Validate JSON for accuracy and integrity with ease.
  5. Load local JSON files effortlessly with a dedicated sidebar button.
  6. Retrieve JSON from web sources quickly — supports custom headers and POST body too.
  7. Work across multiple tabs — each session is isolated, close and rename tabs individually.
  8. Navigate JSON structures effortlessly using an intuitive Tree View with live search.
  9. Visualize complex JSON structures as interactive graphs. Expand the view to explore large datasets with ease.
  10. Query JSON using JSONPath and JMESPath expressions with live autocomplete.
  11. Convert JSON to YAML instantly.
  12. Convert JSON to XML instantly.
  13. Convert JSON to TOML instantly — arrays of objects use correct [[table]] syntax.
  14. Convert JSON to .properties instantly.
  15. Convert JSON to CBOR instantly.
  16. Convert JSON to BSON instantly.
  17. Infer a JSON Schema from your JSON structure automatically.
  18. Decode and verify JWT tokens — supports HMAC (HS256/384/512), RSA and ECDSA signatures.
  19. Minify/Uglify JSON to a single line with one click.
  20. Custom indentation size (1–8 spaces) and alphabetical key sorting.
  21. View live statistics — key count, depth, object/array counts, and file size.
  22. Compare two JSON documents side-by-side with structural diff highlighting.
  23. Generate realistic dummy JSON for testing — choose structure, depth, and size.
  24. Repair malformed JSON automatically using built-in and AI-powered strategies (can be disabled in settings).
  25. Generate code from JSON powered by the acclaimed Quicktype engine — supports 12 languages: TypeScript, JavaScript, TypeScript + Zod, Python, Java, Kotlin, Swift, Go, C#, Rust, Ruby, and Dart. Output is written directly into your project directory.
  26. Open parser as a full editor tab — pop the tool window into the main editor area for more screen space.
  27. Tip of the day — discover features with in-app tips; dismiss, navigate or disable anytime.
  28. Your JSON input is automatically saved locally and restored on restart — no cloud sync, fully private.
  29. Localization — the entire UI is available in Japanese, Korean, and Chinese (Simplified), following your IDE locale automatically.
  30. JSON Schema Validator — validate your JSON against any JSON Schema; save, edit and delete named schemas; view errors in a list or as live annotations in the Pretty tab.
  31. CSV Table View — convert any JSON array to a sortable table; download as .csv with one click.
  32. Base64 auto-detection — paste a Base64-encoded JSON string and it is decoded and parsed automatically; a Base64 Encode tab encodes the current JSON to a Base64 string.
  33. Flatten / Unflatten — expand nested JSON into dot-notation flat pairs, or rebuild nested structure from flat keys.
  34. Rich Pretty Print — live gutter decorations (color swatches, image thumbnails, clock/calendar/link/UUID icons) and inline inlay hints (timestamps, sizes, durations, large numbers) in the Pretty tab. All individually toggleable.
  35. Code → JSON — convert Python dicts/lists/tuples, JavaScript objects/arrays, and TypeScript exports directly to JSON. Handles interface/type declaration stripping, template literals, undefined → null, NaN/Infinity → null, trailing commas, and comments. Auto-converts as you type.
  36. GraphQL Formatter — format and validate GraphQL SDL, queries (with variables, aliases, fragments), mutations, subscriptions, and all SDL types via graphql-java. Auto-formats as you type.
  37. GraphQL Introspection — connect to any live GraphQL endpoint and fetch the full schema; browse types, fields, arguments, enums, interfaces, and directives.
  38. GraphQL Query Runner — write and execute GraphQL queries with variables against a connected endpoint; results load directly into the JSON tooling pipeline.

idea-plugin.name: SVGA Support
idea-plugin.description:
SVGA Support Plugin


Source |  Issues |  SVGA Homepage

The Latest Animation Format

    SVGA is a cross platform animation format. Furthermore, SVGA is also a perfect solution for creating animation in cooperation with designers and developers. SVGA includes SVGAConverter and SVGAPlayer. Designers aim at the design of excellent visual effect and animation content, then export SVGA file by SVGAConverter. Developers use SVGAPlayer to play animation without extra coding. SVGAPlayer is available in different platform including iOS, Android, Web. >> Getting Started


Why SVGA？
  • Friendly to the Developer - The convenient SDK enables SVGA to run on different platforms. The integration step is easy and easy.
  • Friendly to the Designer - Designers can use After Effects or Animate CC (Flash) for animation design, and SVGA can support most of them. Animation files can be converted to SVGA file by using the tools.
  • Cost-Effective - The smaller animation files, the higher performance animation play will provide, the more realistic animation effects will be.

idea-plugin.name: Debug Image Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
Numpy | OpenCV | Pillow | PyTorch | TensorFlow

Note: PyCharm and CLion now has their own integrated alternative.

The plugin displays an image without stopping the debugger. The basic (free) version allows working on OpenCV images (ndarray or Mat). The premium version also supports Pillow/PIL images, and Tensorflow and PyTorch tensors. This will enable you to observe the data you are currently working on.

There are three ways to display the image/tensor during debugging:

  • middle-click (middle mouse button);
  • a keyboard shortcut Alt+I (default keymap);
  • an action from the context menu of the variable.

The Debug Image Viewer is a multifunctional tool that displays data in three modes: popup, dialog or tool window. Change this option in the settings and see which mode is right for you. The plugin allows you to display the variable name, image size, color depth, and data type. In addition to displaying the image, Debug Image Viewer also allows inverting BGR into RGB channels and saving the image in PNG format.

Grayscale, BGR, or BGRA images are supported by default. Also, multichannel arrays can be viewed, for which each channel is displayed separately. You can also apply a colormap to any single channel.

One of the most important plugin options is normalization. That is the procedure that modifies the pixel values' scale. Normalization aims to bring an image to a range that is normal to sense. Normalization is a very useful technique when working with data science since it enables displaying matrices beyond the typical image range.

The displaying behavior:

  • If the array is uint8 or quint8, it is displayed as is;
  • If the array is int8 or qint8, the pixel values are added to 128 ([-128,127] -> [0,255]);
  • If the array is uint16, uint32, uint64 or quint16, the pixel values are divided by 256 ([0,65280] -> [0,255]);
  • If the array is int16, int32, int64, qint16 or qint32, the pixel values are divided by 256 then added to 128 ([-32768,32512] -> [0,255]);
  • If the array is float16, float32, float64 or bloat16, the pixel values are multiplied by 255 ([0,1] -> [0,255]);
  • If the array is boolean, the pixel values are multiplied by 255 ({False,True} -> {0,255}).

To work with Debug Image Viewer, the image must be in HWC or CHW format when you use Python. For the C++ environment, the image must be a contiguous array.

Debug Image Viewer provides a simple and user-friendly interface for displaying images which makes work much easier. The plugin is a tool for developers and researchers working with OpenCV, Pillow/PIL, TensorFlow, or PyTorch, as it provides an efficient and intuitive way to view and analyze image data.

idea-plugin.name: PDF Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
IntelliJ PDF Viewer plugin adds support for viewing PDF files in IntelliJ-based IDEs. This plugin uses recently integrated (2020.2) CEF (Chromium Embedded Framework) browser to render PDF documents with PDF.js library.

Features

  • Document navigation
  • Integration with TeXiFy IDEA
  • Auto-refresh on document change
  • Text search
  • Document scaling
  • Thumbnail view
  • Sections list
  • Structure view
  • Presentation mode
  • Document information
  • Pages spread (even/odd)
  • Horizontal/vertical pages scroll directions
  • Customizable toolbar
  • Customizable dark mode
  • File watcher

All the settings can be found in Settings | Other settings | PDF Viewer.

Shortcuts

  • Move editor up or down: up and down arrow keys.
  • Move editor right or left: right and left arrow keys.
  • Move to the next page: when the whole width of the page is in view, the right and left arrow keys will navigate to the next and previous page.
  • Zoom in: Ctrl + +, Ctrl + =.
  • Zoom out: Ctrl + -
  • Reset zoom: Ctrl + 0
  • Enter presentation mode: Ctrl + Alt + p
  • Inverse search (LaTeX): Ctrl + Left click (can be customized in Settings | Keymap to other mouse shortcuts)

Feature Notes

  • Text search will work only in text-based documents. For example, it won't work in all-images documents (books scans).
  • For the sections list or structure view to work documents should define sections list. Otherwise, sections view won't be active, and the structure view will be empty.
  • Right-click on a pdf to open it in PDFium, the default Chrome PDF viewer. If you do not see a context menu, it may help to go to Help > Find Action, search for Registry, set pdf.viewer.use.jcef.osr.view to false, and restart. See IJPL-59459 for more details.
  • To view pdfs in a Code With Me session, you may need to install the PDF viewer plugin (0.17.0 or later) in the client as well. This feature is still expirimental, for more info see CWM-1199.
  • When you have the pdf open in a separate window and you want inverse search to open the LaTeX file in the main window when it is not open yet, go to Settings > Advanced settings and enable "Open declaration source called from a detached window in the main IDE window"
  • You only need to enable the file watcher global setting if you are using some program to automatically update the pdf which is running in the terminal (or at least outside the IDE), since IntelliJ would not be triggered to look for file system changes. You do not need this setting when using TeXiFy.

Use cases

  • Writing latex documents
  • Split-view code and documentation
  • Presentations with live-coding
  • ...

Providing Feedback

If you want to support PDF Viewer development, just give a star on GitHub or write a review on the marketplace page.

In case you encountered any bugs, feel free to create an issue.

idea-plugin.name: Kobiton ADB Tunnel
idea-plugin.description:
Kobiton ADB Tunnel allows you to access remote devices on the Kobiton platform directly from within your IDE using the ADB utility.

This allows you to pick a device in the Kobiton cloud to work on and execute test scripts on it. You can run your test script from Appium or Selenium from your IDE, which makes debugging and developing test scripts easy and seamless.

General Usage Instruction

Step 1: Setup Android SDK and set global path environment for adb command
Step 2: Make sure that the adb on home's machine is on version 1.0.41 or higher
Step 3: Install plugin in IDE from the marketplace
Step 4: Open Kobiton ADB Tunnel plugin in Tools/Kobiton ADB Tunnel.
