idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.4.2

  • Settings: Suggested Namespace is now an editable, filterable chooser. Opening it or testing the connection discovers available Namespaces without overwriting a manually entered ID, and stale discovery results are discarded when the endpoint or authentication changes.
  • 设置：建议 Namespace 现在是可编辑、可筛选的选择器。首次展开或测试连接时会发现可用 Namespace，同时保留手动输入的 ID；端点或认证信息变化后，过期的发现结果不会再回填界面。
  • Settings safety: opening, cancelling, or resetting Settings no longer mutates published environments. Apply validates every edited endpoint before changing profiles or credentials, while a damaged inactive environment remains available for repair. Cancelling connection tests or Namespace discovery no longer appears as a connection failure or lets a late callback overwrite newer input.
  • 设置安全：打开、取消或重置设置页不再修改已发布的环境。应用设置前会先校验所有已编辑端点，避免部分更新配置档或凭据；已损坏但未选中的环境仍可进入设置修复。取消连接测试或 Namespace 发现时不再显示为连接失败，延迟回调也不会覆盖较新的输入。
  • Search: the Data ID box is one case-insensitive substring. Enter search and live search use the same predicate; * and ? are literal characters, not wildcards or regular expressions. Group filtering stays independent.
  • 搜索：Data ID 搜索框改为不区分大小写的子串匹配。按 Enter 与实时搜索使用同一谓词；* 和 ? 是普通字符，不再当作通配符或正则。Group 过滤保持独立。
  • Search filters: an empty result no longer resets the selected Group to All; Group options stay attached to the current Namespace and reset only when the Namespace actually changes.
  • 搜索过滤：搜索结果为空时不再把已选 Group 重置为全部；Group 选项与当前 Namespace 绑定，仅在 Namespace 真正切换时重置。
  • Configuration details: selecting another configuration while one is loading now cancels and replaces the older load. A late response can no longer repaint the newer selection, and gutter refresh plus click navigation share the same in-flight configuration read.
  • 配置详情：上一条配置仍在加载时选择新配置，会取消并替换旧加载；延迟返回的旧结果不会再覆盖新选择。Gutter 刷新与点击跳转也会复用同一个进行中的配置读取，减少重复请求。
  • Fixes: fixed the Settings page failing to open when the Namespace chooser had no options, and tightened environment migration, credential-slot publication, access-visibility ordering, placeholder indexing, and cancellation handling without changing their public workflows.
  • 问题修复：修复 Namespace 选择器没有选项时设置页无法打开的问题；同时加强环境迁移、凭据槽发布、访问可见性顺序、占位符索引与取消处理，保持既有操作流程不变。

1.4.1

  • Compatibility: removed the IDE upper bound, so the plugin installs on IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2 and later instead of stopping at 2026.1.
  • 兼容性：取消 IDE 版本上限，IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2 及之后版本也可安装，不再只支持到 2026.1。

1.4.0

  • Nacos 3.x: configuration detail, publish, history, and list now speak the admin API's groupName / configTags (and list responses that return groupName are parsed), so a successful connection test is no longer followed by unexpected v3 envelope code 10000 / parameter-missing when opening or publishing a configuration.
  • Nacos 3.x：配置详情、发布、历史记录与列表改为使用管理端 API 的 groupName / configTags（列表响应中的 groupName 也会被解析），连接测试成功后打开或发布配置时不再出现 unexpected v3 envelope code 10000 / 参数缺失。
  • Fixes: envelope code 10000 now surfaces the server's actionable reason (for example that groupName was required) instead of an opaque unexpected-code string.
  • 问题修复：信封码 10000 会展示服务端给出的可操作原因（例如缺少 groupName），而不再是难懂的 unexpected-code 文案。

1.3.9

  • Requests: an expired cache no longer costs a full re-scan. When a gutter marker cannot decide from cache — or resolved against a configuration whose cached body has expired — the plugin re-reads that one configuration and nothing else, at most once per configuration per cache TTL. Previously the first code analysis pass five minutes after a load re-read every declared configuration source in the project and paged the whole Namespace, so one gray icon left on screen cost that scan every five minutes. The Namespace page walk triggered by code analysis now only happens for a Namespace that has never been indexed; re-paging otherwise belongs to Refresh, switching Namespace, and searching.
  • 请求量：缓存过期不再引发全量重扫。当 gutter 标记无法依据缓存判定、或其命中的配置正文已过期时，插件只重新读取这一条配置，且每条配置在一个缓存 TTL 内最多读一次。此前加载五分钟后的第一次代码分析会重读项目中所有已声明的配置来源并翻完整个命名空间，屏幕上留着一个灰色图标就意味着每五分钟重扫一次。由代码分析触发的命名空间翻页现在只在该命名空间从未建立索引时发生；其余情况的重新翻页交给刷新、切换命名空间和搜索。
  • Navigation: opening or jumping to a configuration whose cached body has expired now re-reads that configuration and shows the result, instead of painting the expired body while the gutter icon turned fresh off an unrelated refresh. The amber (expired) icon also heals on its own with a single request, so clicking is no longer the only way to get current content.
  • 导航：打开或跳转到正文已过期的配置时，会重新读取这一条并展示结果，不再出现「面板显示旧正文、gutter 图标却因为别处的刷新变成了新鲜」的情况。黄色（已过期）图标也会自行通过一次请求恢复，不再必须点击才能看到最新内容。
  • Gutter states: a key added on the server to a configuration whose body is already cached is no longer invisible. Absence is now only claimed from a body that is still within its TTL — past it the reference shows the hollow gray icon (undecidable) and one re-read of that configuration settles it, resolving to the fresh icon when the key is there. Previously such a key had no icon at all, so there was nothing to click and nothing to explain it.
  • Gutter 状态：服务端为一份已缓存配置新增的 key 不再完全没有图标。只有仍在 TTL 内的正文才能断言 key 缺席；超过 TTL 时该引用显示空心灰色图标（不可判定），一次重新读取该配置即可定论，key 存在则转为已解析状态。此前这种 key 完全不显示图标，既无处点击也没有任何说明。
  • Fixes: a file containing both a key its cached configuration defines and a key added since issued two identical configuration-detail requests, because the two references spelled the same configuration coordinate differently. A coordinate refresh also addressed the Namespace of the response body rather than the one the cache is keyed by, which could write the body where the gutter never reads it and re-read it every window.
  • 问题修复：同一个文件里同时引用「缓存配置已有的 key」和「之后新增的 key」时会发出两次完全相同的配置详情请求，原因是两处引用把同一个配置坐标拼写成了两种形式。单坐标刷新此前还会使用响应正文中的命名空间而不是缓存键使用的命名空间，可能把正文写到 gutter 永远读不到的位置，并在每个窗口重复读取。
  • Trade-offs worth knowing: a declared data id that does not exist on the server keeps its hollow gray icon instead of losing it, and a configuration newly created on the server enters the Namespace index on Refresh / Namespace switch / search rather than from a code analysis pass. A data id declared at a reference site is still fetched directly, so navigation for declared sources is unaffected.
  • 需要知道的取舍：服务端上确实不存在的已声明 Data ID 会保持空心灰色图标，不再消失；服务端新建的配置通过刷新、切换命名空间或搜索进入命名空间索引，而不再由代码分析触发。引用处声明的 Data ID 仍会被直接拉取，已声明来源的导航不受影响。

1.3.8

  • Compatibility: the supported IDE range now starts at build 223, so the plugin installs on IntelliJ IDEA 2022.3 and later (previously 2024.3+).
  • 兼容性：支持的 IDE 版本下限下调到 build 223，IntelliJ IDEA 2022.3 及以上均可安装（此前需要 2024.3+）。
  • Configuration parsing: keys are now extracted with the same parsers the runtime uses — Gson for JSON, snakeyaml for YAML (the library Spring Boot's own loader uses), and the JDK loader for properties — instead of hand-written scanners. Multi-document YAML streams, anchors/merges, nested sequences, block scalars, and arrays followed by more keys all resolve correctly now.
  • 配置解析：配置 key 改用运行时同款解析器提取——JSON 用 Gson、YAML 用 snakeyaml（Spring Boot 自身加载器所用的库）、properties 用 JDK 加载器，不再使用手写扫描。多文档 YAML、锚点与合并、嵌套序列、块标量、数组后续 key 等场景现在都能正确解析。
  • Runtime format: which format a configuration is read under is decided by the type declared at the reference site first, then by the data id suffix — matching what nacos-spring-context actually does, rather than the server's declared type field. A data id whose format the plugin reads no keys from (for example .xml, or a suffix nothing recognizes) gets its own gray gutter state with an explanation and no jump arrow, instead of a click that silently fetches the body and resolves nothing.
  • 运行时格式：配置按何种格式解析，优先取引用处声明的类型，其次取 Data ID 后缀——与 nacos-spring-context 的实际行为一致，而不是服务端返回的格式字段。插件不解析其 key 的格式（如 .xml，或无法识别的后缀）会显示独立的灰色 gutter 状态并给出说明、不提供跳转箭头，不再点击后静默拉取正文却解析不出任何内容。
  • Access visibility: cached configurations the server has refused to serve are now hidden and reappear automatically once access returns. An authentication refusal hides the whole environment; a configuration-read permission denial hides only the affected Namespace. Publish, Namespace-discovery, and history refusals never hide readable configuration data. Visibility blocks survive IDE restarts and are removed together with the cached data by Tools > Clear Cache.
  • 访问可见性：当服务器拒绝提供数据后（认证失败或读取权限被收回），插件不再显示之前缓存的配置，访问恢复后会自动重新显示。认证失败会隐藏该环境下的全部配置；配置读取权限被拒只隐藏对应命名空间；发布、命名空间发现、历史记录等权限拒绝不会隐藏仍可读取的配置数据。可见性屏蔽在 IDE 重启后仍然生效，执行 Tools > Clear Cache 清除缓存时随缓存数据一并移除。
  • Navigation: a declared @NacosPropertySource dataId is a hard filter both ways. Forward: hits under that dataId resolve as before; when the key is absent from the declared body (or the dataId itself is proven absent), the placeholder is unresolved with no gutter icon — never soft-falls to another cached configuration. Reverse Find Usages from a configuration key only reaches usages that are not hard-bound to a different dataId (so a key in test.yaml no longer jumps to a @NacosValue under dataId = "es.properties"). When the declared dataId is not present under the session Namespace (including when it only exists in another Namespace's cache), the gutter stays unmarked instead of painting an optimistic gray icon. A dataId listed by a fresh authoritative Namespace index but not yet in the detail cache remains undecidable (hollow marker; click lazy-loads that dataId).
  • 导航：已声明配置来源的 Data ID 出现在新鲜且权威的 Namespace 索引中、但其正文尚未进入配置详情缓存时，解析为不可判定配置引用（空心标记；点击会懒加载该 Data ID），不再静默回退到其他已缓存配置。声明正文已缓存且不含该 key、或新鲜完整索引证明该 Data ID 不存在时，仍可软发现；无法证明缺席时不再替换为其他 Data ID（issue #192）。
  • Editing & publishing: saving now shows the diff and the named target for confirmation before the single write, reports publish progress and its outcome, and an unsaved draft is protected — switching environment or Namespace, turning write intent off, deleting the profile, selecting another configuration, closing the tool window, or closing the project all ask first. Refresh keeps the draft instead of discarding it.
  • 编辑与发布：保存前先展示 diff 和目标坐标供确认再执行唯一一次写入，发布过程与结果均有进度反馈；存在未保存草稿时，切换环境或命名空间、关闭写入开关、删除配置档、切换到其他配置、关闭工具窗口、关闭工程都会先行询问；刷新操作保留草稿而不是丢弃。
  • Settings & environments: the authentication strategy moved onto the primary Settings form and defaults to NACOS_PASSWORD once credentials are filled; Cancel really cancels and Reset really resets; the selected Namespace is now project-local like the environment, so two projects no longer fight over one application-wide selection; deleting a profile is fail-closed and takes its credentials with it.
  • 设置与环境：认证方式移至设置主表单，填入凭据后默认 NACOS_PASSWORD；取消即真正取消、重置即真正重置；所选命名空间与环境一样改为工程级，两个工程不再争抢同一个全局选择；删除配置档采用失败即关闭策略，并一并清除其凭据。
  • Performance: Namespace indexes now persist across IDE restarts, re-pagination is throttled with backoff and a page cap, and configuration bodies carried by V1 list responses seed the detail cache directly — together this removes a large share of the repeated requests the plugin used to make against the Nacos server.
  • 性能：命名空间索引在 IDE 重启后仍然保留，重新分页带退避与页数上限限流，V1 列表响应自带的配置正文直接回填详情缓存——三者合计显著减少了插件对 Nacos 服务端的重复请求。
  • Fixes: cleared a Loading overlay that could stick on the first configuration opened; a Namespace display name configured in Settings now resolves to the real Namespace id; switching environments adopts the suggested Namespace; a blank Namespace id is treated as public; gutter icons re-analyze after the key index is published asynchronously instead of staying blank; a deleted profile's cached configurations can no longer be resurrected by a read that lands right after the deletion; the unsaved-edit marker in the result list now carries a "Modified" label instead of a bare dot.
  • 问题修复：修复首次打开配置时加载遮罩卡住；设置中填写的命名空间显示名现在会解析为真实的命名空间 ID；切换环境时会采用建议的命名空间；空白命名空间 ID 按 public 处理；key 索引异步发布完成后 gutter 图标会重新分析，不再保持空白；删除配置档后紧接着的读取不会再把已清除的缓存配置恢复出来；结果列表中的未保存标记从裸圆点改为带「已修改」文字标签。

1.3.7

  • Compatibility: History Diff loading state uses the public MessageDiffRequest API instead of internal LoadingDiffRequest (Marketplace verifier).

1.3.6

  • Dual-stack: V1/V3 protocol adapters with AUTO generation resolve, namespace discovery, and connection diagnostics from unsaved settings drafts.
  • Environments: project-local environment sessions with epoch fencing; History/Diff/publish/gutter follow the project-selected profile (not the app-wide Settings default).
  • History / Diff: identity-local read-only history browser with embedded split-pane Diff (no merge chevrons).
  • Publish: opt-in per-profile write intent with controlled CAS/read-back publish path.
  • Settings: progressive disclosure (Advanced for auth/API/write intent); empty-credential profiles default to ANONYMOUS and upgrade to NACOS_PASSWORD when credentials are filled.
  • Navigation: when @NacosPropertySource declares a dataId and the cache has that key in that file, gutter/go-to hard-filters to it; otherwise soft-falls back to all hits.
  • UI: native ActionToolbar chrome; cache confidence status; Settings blue-dot tracks the current project environment.
  • Reliability: release-gate contract suite; fail-closed capture for deleted profiles; write-intent enforced in PublishController; diagnostics honor locked V1/V3 API policy.

1.3.5

  • Cache: full-namespace index writes now honor the configured TTL, while expired configuration details remain available for stale-while-revalidate navigation.
  • Navigation: added fresh, stale, and unresolved gutter states; stale targets remain navigable, and details older than seven days trigger a forced background refresh.
  • Reliability: added event-driven, single-flight namespace refreshes; only a fresh complete index can prove a dataId absent, while partial or failed refreshes preserve usable stale targets.
  • Security: navigation and local search caches are isolated by server, authentication mode, user, and namespace.

1.3.4

  • UI: optimized the Nacos Search sidebar icon for clearer display in the IDE tool window.
  • Reliability: fixed the persistent placeholder index value format so IntelliJ no longer reports an equals/hashCode contract violation while indexing Java files.
  • Migration: bumped the placeholder index version so IDEs automatically rebuild data written with the previous empty-marker format.
  • Tests: added regression coverage for non-empty marker serialization, round-trip identity, and index version invalidation.

1.3.3

  • 优化侧边栏图标显示。

1.3.2

  • Navigation: improved @NacosValue gutter navigation with richer cross-namespace target selection, usage labels, and source-location presentation.
  • Security: Nacos passwords are now stored through IntelliJ PasswordSafe and omitted from persisted settings XML, with migration for legacy plaintext values.
  • Reliability: Nacos JSON requests now retry transient IO failures and retry with connection settings that avoid malformed chunked responses from some servers and proxies.
  • UI: cross-namespace config navigation preserves the selected detail view while the namespace list refreshes, and preference-only changes refresh markers without a full cache reload.
  • Tests: added coverage for popup choice items, usage presentation, credential persistence, resolver behavior, gutter markers, and settings interactions.

1.3.1

  • Performance: lock-free cache reads, file-based persistence (per-entry files replacing a multi-hundred-MB state XML), background cache loading so IDE startup is no longer blocked, concurrent per-item content fetch (bounded at 8).
  • Fix: HTTP connection leak in requestPost (try/finally disconnect); login credentials now URL-encoded; PaginationPanel disposes its listener via the Disposable tree; Find Usages honors the cancel signal; minified JSON now parsed; performSearch cancels stale debounced searches; stale tokens evicted on credential switch; NacosSearchPlugin implements Disposable; putNamespaceIndex persists seeded details.
  • UI: the save button label reads "Save" instead of "Save & Publish".
  • i18n: fixed untranslated placeholder keys, a config.list.dirty typo, and unified the Chinese bundle encoding to native UTF-8.

1.3.0

  • Fix: phantom gutter icon no longer appears when a @NacosPropertySource dataId does not exist in the loaded Nacos namespace.
  • Fix: resolved NacosConfigKeyElement now carries the source PSI element so Find Usages and navigation keep working after lazy-load.
  • UI: redesigned search bar, clear button, group filter pill and tool-window toolbar.
  • Perf: debounced search input and background namespace-index preheat.

1.2.0

  • @NacosValue gutter icon with dual-state (resolved/unresolved) and PSI reference navigation
  • Reverse Find Usages for Nacos configuration keys
  • Fuzzy namespace search support
  • Code usage navigation from configuration detail to Java source code
  • Persistent placeholder index for fast reverse lookup
  • Plugin icon for JetBrains Marketplace

1.1.1

  • Multi-server (environment) configuration support with master-detail settings UI
  • Redesigned Nacos Search settings page
  • UI improvements across search, namespace, config list, and detail panels
  • Authentication service improvements for token refresh and hybrid mode
  • Reactive UI updates via NacosSettingsListener

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • Nacos Open API integration
  • Local configuration caching
  • Multi-field search functionality
  • Tool window with search interface

idea-plugin.name: BsonViewer
idea-plugin.description:
BsonViewer allows you to view and edit MongoDB BSON files as JSON files directly in the editor window.

Features:

  • Open and edit BSON files directly in your IDE
  • Save modifications back to BSON format
  • Validation to ensure data integrity
  • Supports MongoDB bson dumps showing them as JSON Lines

Limitations:

  • Only valid JSON file can be converted to BSON, so if after editing the file contains invalid JSON, the last valid version will be saved instead
  • BSON format does not preserve formatting, so the default Jackson pretty printer is used to format the file

Support

Found an issue? Have a feature request? Visit GitHub repository or contact the developer.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Support for IntelliJ 2026

idea-plugin.name: Dynatrace Query Language
idea-plugin.description:
The plugin adds support for Dynatrace Query Language (DQL) and Dynatrace Pattern Language (DPL) in most JetBrains IDEs.

Note This product is a community-driven open-source plugin, helping users write and execute DQL & DPL statements within JetBrains IDEs. It's not officially supported by Dynatrace, please report any errors directly via GitHub Issues.

Features

The list of features provided by this plugin can be divided into two categories: fully local features that do not require any external connection, and remote features that require an authenticated connection to a Dynatrace tenant.

Local features are always enabled, and you can optionally configure a connection to a Dynatrace tenant to improve the integration.

You can find more insights on the features in the Wiki.

Local features

Local features are covered completely by the plugin and do not require any kind of connection to the Dynatrace tenant. This also means that not all functionalities provided by Dynatrace services and languages are supported. For example, without the connection the plugin is not able to provide any information about the data stored in the tenant, so no validations and autocompletion for field identifiers can be performed.

The list of local features includes:

  • Highly customizable syntax highlighting and code style formatting
  • Detecting references between DQL fields, functions, statements, and parameters
  • Code completion for commands, fields, functions, and parameters
  • Hover documentation for commands, fields, functions, and parameters
  • Contextual issues detection, with quick fixes where possible
  • Partial DQL support for files containing only parts of the query (both smaller fragments & just expressions)
  • Support for DQL variables defined in Dynatrace Dashboards
  • Nested languages support (DPL inside DQL commands and functions, JSON for data command, and others)

Remote features

After connecting the plugin to a Dynatrace tenant, you can benefit from a wide range of features. You can sign in to multiple tenants and easily switch between them, so you can work with different environments without leaving the IDE.

Supported authentication methods include simple browser OAuth flow and API tokens.

The list of remote features includes:

  • DQL execution on a specific tenant, with results presented as a table, JSON response, or simple visualization
  • Live validations, reporting any kind of errors Dynatrace Notebooks would show
  • Live autocompletion for field identifiers and data objects supported by the tenant
  • Run configurations allowing to save parameters for DQL execution and run them with a single click
  • DQL query console, allowing to execute DQL statements without the need to create a file for them
  • DQL execution toolbar & gutter icons, allowing to easily provide parameters and execute smaller parts of the query

More information

You can find detailed documentation for all features inside the plugin's Wiki pages.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Features

  • The plugin now uses JetBrains-native code editors for embedded DQLs & JSONs (like the DQL results panel). This makes the JSON/DQL code use all JetBrains features like code folding, or proper syntax highlighting.
  • DQL editors now support breadcrumbs and sticky lines (sticky scroll) — the entry command of every query and each nested subquery stays pinned at the top of the viewport while scrolling through long, multi-stage DQL queries. You can disable this feature in standard sticky lines IDE settings.
  • Code refactoring
    • Updating translations to use proper casing, as required by JetBrains guidelines
    • Changed the approach to manage DQL query configuration for executions

Bug fixes

  • Removing JetBrains internal API usages
  • Fixing NullPointerException when autocompleting parameters for a function without any parameters

idea-plugin.name: MyBatisSQLPreviewer

MyBatisSQLPreviewer: SQL preview and OGNL highlighting. This plugin assists with MyBatis dynamic SQL and OGNL expressions.

Key features:

  • OGNL Syntax Highlighting: Provides syntax highlighting for OGNL expressions, including if, choose, when, and foreach. This improves readability and helps prevent common errors.

GitHub | Telegram | Donation

File System Info

File System plugin provides information about file system:

Donation

Open-source tools can greatly improve workflows, helping developers and businesses save time and increase revenue. Many successful projects have been built on these tools, benefiting a wide community. However, maintaining and enhancing these resources requires continuous effort and investment.

Support from the community helps keep these projects alive and ensures they remain useful for everyone. Donations play a key role in sustaining and improving these open-source initiatives.

idea-plugin.name: Git Churn
idea-plugin.description:
GitHub | Telegram | Donation

Git Churn

This plugin provides a Git Churn analysis:

  • How often a file has been changed since the specific time
  • Color the most changed files

Git Churn helps you to decide which files to focus on during the refactoring process. The less a file changes, the easier it is to understand the code.

Donation

Open-source tools can greatly improve workflows, helping developers and businesses save time and increase revenue. Many successful projects have been built on these tools, benefiting a wide community. However, maintaining and enhancing these resources requires continuous effort and investment.

Support from the community helps keep these projects alive and ensures they remain useful for everyone. Donations play a key role in sustaining and improving these open-source initiatives.

idea-plugin.name: HTTP Client Plus
idea-plugin.description:
HTTP Client Plus provides a Postman-like UI for composing and sending HTTP requests directly inside IntelliJ IDEA. Requests are saved as native .http files, making them portable, shareable, and version-controlled.

Key Features
  • Method selector and URL field with an inline Send button.
  • Mandatory Name field used as the .http filename and for tracking/updating existing files.
  • Params tab with a key–value table that automatically appends to the URL.
  • Headers tab with a key–value table.
  • Body tab with a Content-Type selector and a compact overflow menu (Beautify JSON).
  • Multipart form-data builder with boundary input and parts table (text or file) supporting Content-Type per part.
  • For POST requests, automatically adds Content-Type: application/json if missing.
  • Each Send saves or updates the .http file; the first Send opens it, later Sends refresh if already open.
  • Support for pre and post-request scripts (JavaScript) for advanced request manipulation and response handling.
Usage
  • Open via Tools → Open HTTP Client Plus.
  • Fill in Name, URL, Params/Headers/Body as needed, then click Send to save.
  • Run the request manually from the editor with Ctrl+Enter.
  • Files are stored under http-client-plus/collections in your project.

idea-plugin.name: LiveLatex
idea-plugin.description:
LiveLatex is a little JetBrains sidekick for LaTeX: you type, you peek at a live HTML preview, and you don’t have to context-switch to a PDF every two minutes.

Writing with fewer tab hops.

What’s the idea? 🤔

  • Open the LaTeX Preview tool window and watch the document update as you go (math, tables, figures — most everyday stuff works).
  • TikZ gets extra love: there’s a click-and-drag canvas (knots and diagrams), and you can turn LiveRender on when you want TikZ compiled in the preview, or leave it off if you’d rather keep the IDE snappy.
  • Tables, insert image, \ref / \cite from the right-click menu, and a shortcut to yank a section into its own file — basically the shortcuts I got tired of typing by hand.
  • Runs anywhere JetBrains runs plugins (IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, …).

Cool bits 🚀

  • Live preview next to your editor
  • TikZ canvas (draw, knots, export) + optional LiveRender for TikZ in the preview
  • Table wizard + image insert
  • Zoom, jump to section, and preview options from the tool window

Honest disclaimer 😎

I built this for my own LaTeX workflow first — if it helps you too, great. Issues and ideas welcome on GitHub; stars and marketplace ratings always appreciated.

idea-plugin.name: Document Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
The Document Viewer enables developers to seamlessly view Word, Excel, Pdf, Markdown, CSV, and TSV files directly within JetBrains. No more switching between applications - keep your workflow uninterrupted by viewing documents in the same environment where you code.

Supported File Formats

  • Word (.docx, .rtf, .dotx, .dot, .doc)

  • Excel (.xlsx, .xls, .xltx, .xlt)

  • PDF (.pdf)

  • Markdown (.md)

  • CSV (.csv)

  • TSV (.tsv)

Key Features

  • Effortless Viewing: Seamlessly view Word, Excel, PDF, Markdown, CSV, and TSV files.

  • Edit Files: Edit Word, Excel, Markdown, CSV, and TSV files directly in JetBrains without accessing additional tools.

  • Sorting and Filtering: Organize data efficiently using sorting and filtering options in column headers for spreadsheet (Excel, CSV, TSV) files.

For comprehensive details on the Document Viewer plugin for JetBrains, refer to the help documentation. To quickly learn how to open, edit, and save documents, follow the Getting Started Guide. Customize the Document Viewer, including enabling read-only mode or configuring spreadsheet filters, by exploring the Configuration Options Guide.

idea-plugin.name: Hex Editor
idea-plugin.description:
A powerful Hex Editor for IntelliJ-based IDEs that allows you to view and edit any file as raw bytes.

✨ Now supports unlimited file sizes — from KB to GB+ with smooth virtual scrolling!

Free Features

  • 🚀 Unlimited file size — Handle GB+ files with smooth virtual scrolling (no memory limits)
  • 👁️ View files — Classic hex + ASCII layout (16 bytes per line)
  • 🔍 Hex + Text search — Find hex patterns with wildcards or text in ASCII/UTF-8
  • ⚡ Fast search — Search 1 GB file in ~10 seconds with progress indicator and cancel button
  • 🔎 Search navigation — Press Ctrl+F to search, F3/Shift+F3 to navigate between matches
  • 📊 Data Inspector — View bytes as Int8/16/32/64, Float, UTF-8, etc. with Little/Big Endian toggle
  • 🎯 Go to Offset — Jump to any position (Ctrl+G / Cmd+G) with hex or decimal input
  • 📋 Copy As... — Export bytes as Hex String, C Array, Java, Kotlin, Python, Go, Base64
  • 🎨 Synchronized highlighting — Hex and ASCII areas stay in sync when selecting
  • ⌨️ Full keyboard navigation — Arrow keys, Page Up/Down, Home/End, Shift+selection

Paid Features

  • ✏️ Full editing — Edit hex values and ASCII characters directly in place
  • ⏪ Undo/Redo — 100 operations history (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z)
  • ⌨️ Layout-independent input — Hex input works with any keyboard layout (Russian, German, etc.)
  • 💾 Auto-save — Changes saved automatically like standard editors
  • 🔄 External change detection — Conflict dialog when file modified on disk

Structure Viewer

Integrated with the IDE's Structure tool window — view the internal layout of binary files as a navigable tree.

  • 10 built-in parsers — PNG, ZIP/JAR, Java .class, PE (exe/dll), ELF, Mach-O, PDF, WebAssembly (.wasm), ISO 9660, Windows Minidump (.dmp)
  • Click to navigate — Select any structure element to jump to its bytes and highlight the range
  • Color highlighting — Structural ranges are color-coded directly in the hex view
  • Free: Top-level structure overview (sections, headers, chunks)
  • Paid: Detailed view with all nested fields and attributes

Supported File Types

Built-in file types with icons:

  • Executables & libraries: .exe, .dll, .so, .dylib, .obj, .o, .elf, .macho, .sys, .ocx, .scr, .wasm, .efi, .ko
  • Binary data & images: .bin, .iso, .img, .rom, .fw, .firmware, .dmp, .dump

Auto-detected as binary (also opens in hex editor): .class, .bundle, .jar, .war, .ear, .apk, .pyc, .pyo, .pyd, and any other binary file.

Usage

Right-click any file → "Open in Hex Editor"
idea-plugin.change-notes:
11.0.1 (8 Sep 2026)

  • IDE input isolation: Opening a binary file no longer intercepts typing in other editors and dialogs, including Remote Development sessions.

11.0.0 (8 Sep 2026)

  • Remote Development responsiveness — Fixed repeated refreshes that could keep the IDE busy while a binary file was open, slowing viewing and editing in remote sessions.
  • Search cancellation — Canceling a search now clears its progress indicator instead of leaving the editor showing that a search is still running.

10.0.0 (4 Sep 2026)

  • Transactional binary saves — Edits are streamed through a validated same-directory temporary file and committed with atomic replacement, so a canceled or failed save leaves the original file intact.
  • Live Commit visibility — Debounced background autosave now exposes active hex edits to the IDE's Commit diff without requiring focus loss, while Save and Save All remain available.
  • Background autosave stability — Active edits now continue reaching disk and Commit diff reliably during background saves while the IDE remains responsive.
  • Native diff preview compatibility — Hex Editor no longer claims the IDE's internal diff-preview virtual files, while ordinary supported binary files continue to open normally.
  • Aligned insertion and deletion rows — Binary comparisons render explicit gap rows for inserted and deleted byte runs, keeping both panes, real offsets, and difference navigation aligned.
  • Canonical replacement rows — Same-size replacements stay on normal 16-byte file rows and highlight only the changed bytes instead of producing misleading stepped offsets.
  • Atomic-save edit and diff coherence — Rapid typing and paste operations made during an active save remain ordered, dirty, and undoable, while an already-open Commit diff refreshes to the exact committed file generation.
  • Windows file-handle safety — Binary readers release native handles before transactional replacement, so files remain replaceable, renameable, and deletable after comparison and save workflows.
  • Clear paid value at intent — Free viewing stays uninterrupted, while the first blocked edit or locked Structure detail explains the safe editing and detailed inspection benefits and opens the IDE's native trial or purchase flow; later blocked edits show a lightweight hint at the hex caret instead of failing silently.

9.0.0 (3 Aug 2026)

  • 📋 Paste hex — Paste a hex string from the clipboard (spaced FF AB CD or contiguous FFABCD) to overwrite bytes at the cursor; the whole paste is a single Undo/Redo step and is clamped to the file size (no insert)
  • 📋 Paste text — Paste clipboard text as raw bytes (one byte per character) with Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+V to overwrite at the cursor; the whole paste is a single Undo/Redo step and is clamped to the file size (no insert), and text with characters outside the single-byte range is rejected without changing any data
  • 👁️ Preview paste before apply — Optional confirmation (enable in Settings | Tools | Hex Editor) that shows the exact bytes, target offset, and any end-of-file clamp before a hex or text paste overwrites anything, with Apply/Cancel; off by default, so paste stays immediate unless you turn it on
  • ⚠️ Large-file edit warning — The first edit of a very large file now shows a one-time, non-blocking warning (Continue / Cancel, with "Don't warn again") after the standard make-writable flow; the size threshold and opt-out are configurable in Settings | Tools | Hex Editor, and editing is never hard-blocked
  • 🔬 Binary compare — The IDE's standard Compare Files / Compare With… now opens binary files in a two-pane hex view with the differing byte ranges highlighted; smart alignment detects inserted and deleted runs (a single added or removed byte no longer marks the whole remainder as changed) and colors changed, inserted, and deleted bytes distinctly in each pane; the diff is computed in the background, the two panes scroll in sync, and toolbar Next/Previous-difference buttons jump between the changes

8.0.0 (July 5, 2026)

  • Protected-file resilience — Opening locked or system-owned large files now falls back to a controlled read-only state with an IDE notification instead of crashing the editor provider
  • Crash fix — Fixed a JVM InternalError that could occur when a large memory-mapped file was changed, truncated, or replaced outside the IDE while open in Hex Editor
  • External-change resilience — Invalidated memory mappings are now treated as real external file changes, so the editor can reload or show the conflict dialog instead of failing on the EDT
  • Typing stability — Fixed a bulk-update crash that could be triggered by IDE data-context collection while typing in Hex Editor
  • Copy performance — Fixed an IDE freeze when copying large byte selections by replacing per-byte formatter parsing with direct hex rendering

7.0.0 (June 10, 2026)

  • ↩️ IDE-native Undo/Redo — Byte edits now use the IDE's standard Undo/Redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z) via the platform UndoManager, instead of a separate in-editor history
  • 🪶 Constant-memory undo history — Undo/redo stores only byte deltas, never file snapshots, so it stays lightweight even on GB-sized files
  • 🔒 Read-only / writability trust surface — Editing a read-only or VCS-locked file now runs the standard make-writable / checkout flow before any byte change, instead of failing later at save time
  • 💾 IDE save-lifecycle integration — Modified state and saving hook into the standard IDE flow (Save, Save All, build, VCS commit), surfaced through the editor's modified indicator
  • 🔁 Robust undo across external changes — Undo/redo no longer corrupt content after an external change or VCS rollback; edits made after a reload remain undoable

6.0.0 (May 27, 2026)

  • ⌨️ Search keyboard UX — Added full keyboard workflow in search panel: Enter/Shift+Enter and F3/Shift+F3 for next/previous match, Esc to close search
  • 🎯 Predictable focus handling — Search now restores previous focus owner on close and keeps focus transitions stable on open/close
  • 🔢 Accurate streaming match status — During long searches, current/total counters stay consistent while partial results are streamed
  • 📚 Documented shortcuts — Updated plugin documentation with complete keyboard shortcuts for search and navigation
  • 📈 Performance diagnostics — Added internal chunk/render/search metrics with stall/freeze detection and optional opt-in diagnostics for large-file workflows
  • 🧯 Read/error resilience — Added graceful handling of I/O read/reload failures with clear actionable notifications
  • 🕵️ Better external-change detection — Added modification-stamp validation to reduce false-positive reload/conflict handling
  • ⚔️ Conflict resolution UX — External modification dialog now offers: Reload from Disk / Keep Local Changes / Save Mine to Disk
  • 🧯 Memory-pressure adaptation — Added low-memory reaction with aggressive cache reduction to keep IDE responsive under constrained heap
  • 🤝 Cooperative scheduling — Viewport loading/prefetch now scales down during IDE background activity (e.g., indexing) to avoid interference
  • 🛡️ GC stall mitigation — Added bounded viewport batch loading under pressure to reduce allocation bursts and IDE-wide pauses
  • 🧵 Scroll event smoothing — Added throttle + debounce for scroll-triggered viewport updates to reduce repaint/read bursts under fast scrolling
  • 🧊 IDE freeze elimination — Removed synchronous viewport reads from EDT and moved visible-range loading to background
  • 🛰️ Async viewport architecture — Added request-based loading, cancellation of in-flight tasks, and stale-request discard
  • 📦 Chunk prefetch on scroll — Added adjacent chunk pre-loading in virtual document reads for smoother sequential scrolling
  • 🧠 Adaptive chunk cache — Chunk cache size now adapts to file size and live navigation pattern (sequential scroll vs random jumps)
  • 🔎 Search scalability — Added versioned search requests with instant cancel, non-blocking updates, and streamed partial results
  • 🧪 Large-file stress harness — Added automated stress tests including 1GB and 5GB sparse-file scenarios
  • 🗺️ Large mmap support — Switched to segmented memory mapping to support files beyond 2GB safely
  • 🛟 Safer mmap fallback — When mmap is unavailable, switched from 10MB truncation fallback to full-file random-access read-only mode
  • 📁 More registered file types — Added dedicated file types with icons for .elf, .macho, .sys, .ocx, .scr, .wasm, .efi, .ko, .iso, .img, .rom, .fw, .firmware, .dmp, .dump
  • 🧬 New structure parsers — Added WebAssembly (.wasm), ISO 9660 disk image, and Windows Minidump (.dmp) parsers in the Structure tool window

5.0.0 (April 17, 2026)

  • 🔤 Text search mode — Added text search over binary data with ASCII and UTF-8 support
  • 🔠 Case options — Added case-sensitive and case-insensitive matching for text search
  • 🧭 Unified search panel — Added mode/encoding controls in the existing search UI

4.0.0 (March 9, 2026)

  • 🏗️ Structure Viewer — View internal file structure in the IDE's Structure tool window
  • 📦 7 format parsers — PNG, ZIP/JAR, Java .class, PE (exe/dll), ELF, Mach-O, PDF
  • 🎯 Click to navigate — Select any structure element to jump to its byte range
  • 🎨 Color highlighting — Structural ranges are color-coded in the hex view
  • 🔓 Freemium model — Basic structure overview is free; detailed nested fields require a license
  • 📁 More file types — Added .class, .elf, .macho, .bundle, .sys, .jar, .war, .ear, .apk recognition
  • 🐛 Bug fix — Fixed StructureViewComponent memory leak on editor close

3.0.0 (January 8, 2026)

  • 🚀 Large file support — No file size limits! Opens GB+ files instantly with smooth virtual scrolling
  • 🔍 Hex search — Find patterns with wildcards (e.g., "FF ?? CD" finds FF, any byte, CD)
  • ⚡ Fast search — Boyer-Moore algorithm: 100 MB in ~1 sec, 1 GB in ~10 sec, with progress bar and cancel
  • 🔎 Search navigation — Press Ctrl+F to search, F3/Shift+F3 to jump between matches
  • 📊 Performance boost — 10-100x faster file opening with custom Swing component
  • 🎨 Visual polish — Cursor indicator, better selection, improved layout
  • 🐛 Bug fixes — Fixed UI freezes when typing in other editors

2.0.0

  • Inline editing — Edit hex values and ASCII characters directly
  • Layout-independent hex input — Works with any keyboard layout (Russian, German, etc.)
  • Auto-save — Changes saved immediately after each edit
  • External file change detection — Conflict dialog when file modified externally
  • OVR/INS mode indicator — Status bar shows current editing mode
  • Data Inspector panel — View byte interpretations with Little/Big Endian toggle
  • Copy As menu — Export as Hex String, C Array, Java, Kotlin, Python, Go, Base64
  • Go to Offset — Navigate with hex or decimal input (Ctrl+G / Cmd+G)
  • Synchronized highlighting — Mirror highlighting between hex and ASCII

1.0.0

  • Initial version: Hex Viewer with basic viewing functionality

idea-plugin.name: Omni Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
Omni Viewer

A powerful IntelliJ plugin for viewing and editing various file formats including audio, video, parquet, JSON, JSONL, TOML, YAML, PlantUML, Mermaid and CSV files.

Free Features:

  • Jupyter Notebook Viewer: View .ipynb Markdown, code and raw cells, saved tables, images, streams and errors, with cell search and collapsible code/output sections. No kernel is required.
  • Audio Viewer: Play, pause, and control audio files (MP3, WAV, OGG, FLAC, M4A, AAC, WMA)
  • Parquet Viewer: View and explore Parquet files with schema, data table, search, and JSON export
  • JSON Viewer: Open JSON files from the context menu with syntax highlighting, tree view, validation, key sorting, minify, and conversion tools
  • TOML Viewer: Open TOML files from the context menu with tree view, breadcrumbs, source sync, structural search, JSON/flatten previews, domain hints, warnings, stats, and dependency sections
  • YAML Viewer: Open YAML files from the context menu with tree navigation, source sync, path copying, anchor/alias tracing, merge-key hints, JSON/flatten previews, multi-document selection, and domain-aware summaries
  • Diagram Viewer: Preview PlantUML and Mermaid diagrams with source editing, render refresh, and SVG/HTML copy tools
  • DBC Viewer: Explore CAN DBC files with message and signal tables
  • ASC Viewer: Explore CAN ASC log files with frame tables and event filtering
  • A2L Viewer: Explore ASAP2/A2L measurement and calibration descriptions
  • PCAP Viewer: Inspect classic packet capture files with packet summaries and hex preview
  • HDF5 Viewer: Browse HDF5 files with group/dataset trees, attributes, metadata, and first-page dataset previews
  • MAT Viewer: Browse MATLAB .mat files with variable trees, metadata, previews, and struct/cell exploration
  • Safetensors Viewer: Inspect tensor names, data types, shapes, sizes, and model metadata without loading tensor payloads
  • ExecuTorch Viewer: Inspect ExecuTorch .pte programs as an interactive dataflow graph, with methods, instructions, values, delegates, memory plans, and data segments read without loading tensor payloads
  • HAR Viewer: Diagnose web and API failures from an HTTP archive (.har) — a filterable request list with a per-request waterfall, status, type, domain and body search, plus headers, query/form payload, request and response bodies with JSON pretty-printing, cookies, and per-phase timings
  • Shapefile Viewer: Inspect Esri .shp maps with .dbf attributes, .prj projection info, pan/zoom, filtering, and measurement tools
  • JSONL Viewer: View and edit JSON Lines files with formatted preview
  • HWP Viewer: View HWP and HWPX (한글) documents as text
  • Proto Viewer: Explore Protocol Buffers (.proto) files with a message tree, type navigation, reverse references, relationship graph, JSON example generator, gRPC service explorer, import graph, documentation renderer, global search, and breaking-change detection

Premium Features:

  • Media Player: Play video files (MP4, MOV, WebM) with full playback controls. AVI, MKV, WMV, FLV are not supported (JavaFX Media).
  • CSV Viewer: View CSV files in table format with search, column sorting, and file info (right-click → Open with OmniViewer)
  • Excel Viewer: View XLS/XLSX files in table format with sheet selection, search, and sorting (right-click → Open with OmniViewer)
  • Image Editor: Edit images with drawing tools, color picker, and brush size control (right-click → Open with OmniViewer)
  • Word Document Viewer: View DOC/DOCX files with text extraction, text search (highlight, Find next/previous), and .doc/.docx support. Text only – tables, images, and formatting (colors, links) are not displayed.
  • PDF Viewer: View PDF files with rendered pages, thumbnail navigation, and password prompt support.
  • PPT Viewer: View PPT/PPTX files with rendered slide layout, thumbnails, and text search.
  • ARXML Viewer: Explore AUTOSAR XML packages, components, interfaces, data types and communication objects.
  • ReqIF Viewer: Explore requirements, specifications, relations, types, and attributes from ReqIF XML files.
  • BLF Viewer: Inspect Vector BLF binary log structure and common CAN-related objects.
  • MF4/MDF Viewer: Inspect ASAM MDF4/MF4 metadata blocks, channel names and text references.
  • GGUF Viewer: Inspect model metadata, quantization, tensor shapes, parameter counts, sizes, and offsets without loading model weights.
  • TFLite Viewer: Inspect LiteRT model graphs, operators, tensors, quantization, signatures, buffers, and metadata without loading model weights.
  • ONNX Viewer: Inspect ONNX model graphs, nodes, initializers, attributes, control-flow subgraphs, local functions, and metadata without loading tensor payloads.
  • Keras Viewer: Inspect Keras 3 .keras archives and Keras HDF5 models — layers, weights, shapes, parameter counts, training configuration, and archive members — without loading model weights.
  • Core ML Viewer: Inspect Core ML .mlmodel specifications and .mlpackage bundles — ML Program operations, neural-network layers, pipelines, feature types, weights, weight blobs, class labels, and manifest contents — without loading model weights.
  • Binary Format Viewer: Inspect Avro, ROS bag, STEP/STP, and DB3 files directly when opened.
  • PCAPNG Viewer: Inspect next-generation packet capture blocks, interfaces, and packet records.

Simply open any supported file type in IntelliJ and start viewing or editing!
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Version 202610.1.0

  • Jupyter Notebook Viewer (Free): Added direct-open .ipynb previews with Markdown, code/raw cells, execution counts, saved HTML tables, raster/SVG images, attachments, text/JSON outputs, streams and tracebacks, cell search, code/output folding, refresh from the JSON editor, and a text fallback when JCEF is unavailable.
  • HAR Viewer (Free): Added direct-open viewing for HTTP archives (.har) — a filterable request table with a per-request waterfall, a detail pane for headers, query/form payload, request and response bodies, cookies, and per-phase timings, plus pages, archive info, and validation warnings.
  • HAR Viewer (Free): Requests filter by method, status class, resource type, and domain, and search across URL, status, headers, and query parameters — optionally including body previews; matching, sorting, and the waterfall all stay responsive on a 20,000-request archive.
  • HAR Viewer (Free): The waterfall lays each request's timing phases out proportionally with the TLS handshake taken out of the connect phase so it is not double-counted; a request the archive never timed draws one neutral bar instead of being attributed to a phase nobody measured.
  • HAR Viewer (Free): Response bodies stored as base64 are decoded for textual types (URL-safe alphabet included) and reported by size alone for binary ones, JSON bodies are pretty-printed, and previews are capped per body so an archive with inlined images still opens quickly.
  • HAR Viewer (Free): A truncated archive — the common way a HAR arrives broken — still opens: the requests written before the capture was cut off are shown and the truncation is reported. Unreported sizes, durations, and transfer figures read as "—" rather than as a confident zero, and _transferSize, _fromCache, _resourceType, and _error are read from both the entry and the response, where different writers place them.
  • ExecuTorch Viewer (Free): Added direct-open viewing for ExecuTorch .pte programs with payload-free FlatBuffer parsing, an interactive dataflow graph, instruction/value/delegate/segment tables, a structure tree, validation warnings, search, and JSON copy.
  • ExecuTorch Viewer (Free): The Graph tab draws each kernel and delegate call as a card and the EValues between them as edges; constant weights and literal scalar arguments fold into the consuming call, list arguments expand to the tensors they hold, and skip connections route around the layers they bypass, with drag-to-pan, wheel zoom, fit, search highlighting, and a node inspector.
  • ExecuTorch Viewer (Free): Each instruction's stored argument list is split into inputs and outputs by data flow, so an out-variant kernel and a delegate call both report what they actually read and write; a reshaping view that shares a memory-planned slot is reported as sharing its source tensor's memory rather than as an unwritten input.
  • ExecuTorch Viewer (Free): Graph connections follow execution order when a value is updated repeatedly, with separate input and output cards for in-place updates and identity methods.
  • ExecuTorch Viewer (Free): Segment and buffer payloads are never decoded — a constant tensor reports its segment, file offset, and byte count, and the extended header locates every data segment — so a multi-gigabyte model opens as quickly as a small one.
  • ExecuTorch Viewer (Free): Delegates list their backend, blob location, size, and compile specs; tensors stored in a separate .ptd file, segments the extended header cannot locate, segments past the end of the file, and unrecognized scalar types, value kinds, and instruction kinds are all reported as validation warnings.
  • ExecuTorch Viewer (Free): Graph rendering, inspector lists, and card labels stay bounded on hostile or degenerate programs, a malformed FlatBuffer is reported as invalid rather than read as content, and text taken from a program file is never rendered as markup.

Version 2026.9.1

  • Core ML Viewer (Premium): Added direct-open viewing for Core ML .mlmodel specifications with payload-free protobuf parsing, an interactive dataflow graph, operation/weight/feature tables, structure and package views, validation warnings, and JSON copy.
  • Core ML Viewer (Premium): Reads both graph encodings — an ML Program is read exactly as the producer wrote it, and a neural network resolves every layer type with named attributes for the common ones — plus pipelines, whose stages become nodes that open as their own graphs.
  • Core ML Viewer (Premium): An .mlpackage bundle opens through right-click → Open with OmniViewer (Core ML) in the project view, or directly when it arrives zipped; its Manifest.json, items, files, and weight blobs are listed and referenced blob sizes resolved.
  • Core ML Viewer (Premium): Weight payloads are never decoded — a blob-backed tensor reports its file, offset, and byte count, and an inline tensor its size and quantization — so a multi-gigabyte model opens as quickly as a small one.
  • Core ML Viewer (Premium): Feature types render image sizes, multi-array shapes, dictionaries, sequences, and state, with enumerated and ranged shape flexibility; class labels, custom layers, and missing weight files are reported as validation warnings.
  • Core ML Viewer (Premium): Graph rendering, inspector lists, and card labels stay bounded on hostile or degenerate models, malformed protobuf is reported as invalid rather than read as content, and text taken from a model file is never rendered as markup.
  • JSONL Viewer (Free): .jsonl, .ndjson, and .jsonlines files now open in the IDE's default editor; the OmniViewer hover-preview editor is available through right-click → Open with OmniViewer (JSONL).
  • GGUF Viewer (Premium): The summary now reports the header size as Header and the actual tensor payload size as Tensor data, large metadata arrays parse faster, and a quantized tensor with a non-block-aligned first dimension still counts toward the quantization-version check.

Version 2026.8.2

  • Keras Viewer (Premium): Weights are matched to layers on the store names Keras derives from class names, so a renamed layer, a nested sub-model, a subclassed model, or a wrapper layer such as a Bidirectional LSTM reports its parameters against the right row; optimizer and metric state stays out of the parameter totals.
  • Keras Viewer (Premium): Weight payloads are never read — a stored weight store is mapped in place, so a model of a gigabyte or two opens as quickly as a small one — and ZIP64 archives are read, so models past 4 GB open too.
  • Keras Viewer (Premium): A Keras 2 model saved as .h5 opens beside the free HDF5 viewer rather than replacing it, and a Keras 3 .weights.h5 checkpoint saved without its archive opens on its own.
  • Diagram Viewer (Free): Opening a .mmd or .puml file on 2026.2 and later no longer fails with NoClassDefFoundError: com/intellij/ui/jcef/JBCefApp; the JCEF dependency is now declared, and where JCEF really is unavailable the preview falls back to plain HTML as intended.

Version 2026.8.1

  • ONNX Viewer (Premium): Added direct-open viewing for .onnx models with payload-free protobuf parsing, an interactive dataflow graph, node/initializer/value tables, control-flow subgraph and local-function browsing, validation warnings, and JSON copy.
  • ONNX Viewer (Premium): The Graph tab draws nodes as cards and values as edges, folds initializer weights into the consuming node, and routes skip connections around the layers they bypass, with drag-to-pan, wheel zoom, fit, search highlighting, and a node inspector.
  • ONNX Viewer (Premium): Graph rendering, inspector lists, and card labels stay bounded on hostile or degenerate models, malformed protobuf is reported as invalid rather than read as content, and text taken from a model file is never rendered as markup.
  • TFLite Viewer (Premium): Added direct-open viewing for .tflite and .lite LiteRT models with graph, operator, tensor, I/O, buffer, metadata, signature, validation, search, and JSON inspection.

  • PCAP/PCAPNG Viewer: Added structured packet filters such as ip == 1.2.3.4, ip.src == 1.2.3.4, tcp.port == 443, protocol == DNS, and dns.qry.name contains example.

  • PCAP/PCAPNG Viewer: Added basic mDNS, SSDP, MQTT, CoAP, and QUIC packet summaries.

idea-plugin.name: ScriptAssistant
idea-plugin.description:
ScriptAssistant - A powerful tool designed for Android automation testers and developers to enhance efficiency in writing uiautomator2 scripts.

uiautomator2自动化脚本助手 - 专为Android自动化测试工程师和开发者设计的高效开发工具。

主要功能：

  • 自动化脚本录制：通过简单操作自动生成uiautomator2测试脚本，减少手动编码工作
  • 智能代码补全：提供针对uiautomator2 API的智能提示和代码补全功能

操作指引：

前置要求：需要在PyCharm中配置python解释器，并安装uiautomator2库

非PyCharm需要在设置中指定已安装uiautomator2库的python解释器路径

顶部操作栏：

  1. 点击“刷新设备”图标，刷新当前连接的Android设备列表（需要配置adb环境变量）
  2. 点击“设备列表”下拉框，选择当前设备
  3. 连接和断开连接按钮（连接过程可能有一定耗时）
  4. 已连接状态下，会显示设备别名输入框（默认值为"d"），用于设置设备别名，生成代码时将引用此别名
  5. dump按钮：用于获取当前界面截图和控件信息
  6. Selector单选框：勾选时，将只生成Selector的代码
  7. 设置按钮

左侧界面截图区域：

  1. 查看控件属性和层级：鼠标左键点击控件，查看控件属性和层级
  2. 生成控件定位代码：鼠标右键点击控件（按住ctrl键，强制使用xpath定位）
  3. 生成控件点击代码：鼠标左键双击控件（按住ctrl键，强制使用xpath定位）
  4. 生成坐标点击代码：按住ctrl键 + 鼠标左键点击，生成百分比坐标点击代码
  5. 生成百分比坐标滑动代码：鼠标左键按住拖动（按住ctrl键，生成拖拽代码）
  6. 生成像素坐标滑动代码：鼠标右键按住拖动（按住ctrl键，生成拖拽代码）

右上控件树区域：

  1. 左键选择对应控件，截图中也将标记选中的控件范围
  2. 右键点击控件，生成对应控件的定位代码（方便在控件区域重叠时，生成指定控件的定位代码）

右下当前选中控件信息区域：

  1. 左键选中一行控件属性时，将自动复制当前属性代码到粘贴板
  2. 右键选中一行控件属性时，将自动将控件属性插入到编辑光标所在行的定位代码中（用于添加指定定位参数）

底部操作栏：

  1. 显示已选中控件的定位代码
  2. Find按钮通过定位代码查找“真实设备当前界面”中对应的控件位置，显示在工具界面上

此插件旨在帮助开发者和测试工程师更高效地编写和调试Android自动化脚本，特别适用于基于uiautomator2框架的自动化测试场景。

Key Features:

  • Automation Script Recording: Automatically generates uiautomator2 test scripts through simple operations, reducing manual coding efforts.
  • Intelligent Code Completion: Provides smart suggestions and code completion features for the uiautomator2 API.

Operation Guide:

Prerequisites: Configure the Python interpreter in PyCharm and install the uiautomator2 library.

Top Operation Bar:

  1. Click the "Refresh Devices" icon to refresh the list of currently connected Android devices (requires ADB environment variables).
  2. Click the "Device List" dropdown to select the current device.
  3. Connect/Disconnect button (connection may take some time).
  4. In the connected state, a device alias input box will appear (default: "d") for specifying the device alias, which will be referenced in generated code.
  5. "Dump" button: Retrieves current interface screenshots and widget information.
  6. "Selector" checkbox: When checked, only generates Selector code.

Left Screenshot Area:

  1. View widget properties and hierarchy: Left-click on a widget to view its properties and hierarchy.
  2. Generate widget positioning code: Right-click on a widget (hold Ctrl to force XPath positioning).
  3. Generate widget click code: Double-click a widget with the left mouse button (hold Ctrl to force XPath positioning).
  4. Generate coordinate click code: Hold Ctrl + left-click to generate percentage coordinate click code.
  5. Generate percentage coordinate swipe code: Hold left mouse button and drag (hold Ctrl to generate drag code).
  6. Generate pixel coordinate swipe code: Hold right mouse button and drag (hold Ctrl to generate drag code).

Upper Right Widget Tree Area:

  1. Left-click to select a widget; the selected widget range will be marked in the screenshot.
  2. Right-click on a widget to generate its positioning code (useful for overlapping widgets).

Lower Right Selected Widget Information Area:

  1. Left-click on a row of widget properties to automatically copy the property code to the clipboard.
  2. Right-click on a row of widget properties to automatically insert the property into the positioning code at the cursor position (for adding specific positioning parameters).

This plugin aims to help developers and testers write and debug Android automation scripts more efficiently, especially for automation testing scenarios based on the uiautomator2 framework.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Version 2.0 - Complete Kotlin rewrite - Rewritten in Kotlin with IntelliJ Platform UI DSL - Improved code structure and maintainability

idea-plugin.name: YsQy-Book
idea-plugin.description:
YsQy-Book — A lightweight novel reading plugin for IntelliJ IDEA.
Supports chapter-based reading, page jumping, auto page turning, and reading progress persistence.
Enjoy your favorite books directly within your IDE with seamless reading experience.

🆕 Version 1.1.1 - Major Update:
✨ Reading Progress Persistence: Automatically saves and restores your reading progress
🔄 Multi-Project Support: Each project maintains independent reading state
🚀 Auto-Load on Startup: Automatically loads your last novel when opening IDEA
📖 Smart Chapter Navigation: Chapter list automatically positions to current reading location
⚡ Real-time Progress Saving: Progress is saved automatically with every page turn

Usage:
1. IDEA Settings > Tools > YsQy Book: Set the novel path and auto page turn interval.
2. Bottom-left corner of IDEA: Read novels directly in the status bar.
3. YsQy-Book sidebar: Navigate chapters and menus.
4. Seamless Experience: Your reading progress is automatically saved and restored!

YsQy-Book — 一款轻量级 IntelliJ IDEA 小说阅读插件，支持章节阅读、页码跳转、自动翻页与阅读进度持久化功能，让你在编码间隙轻松阅读。

🆕 版本 1.1.1 - 重大更新：
✨ 阅读进度持久化：自动保存和恢复阅读进度
🔄 多项目支持：每个项目独立维护阅读状态
🚀 启动自动加载：打开IDEA时自动加载上次的小说
📖 智能章节导航：章节列表自动定位到当前阅读位置
⚡ 实时进度保存：每次翻页自动保存进度

使用说明：
1. IDEA 设置 > 工具 > YsQy Book：设置小说路径和自动翻页秒数。
2. IDEA 左下角：直接在状态栏阅读小说。
3. YsQy-Book 侧边栏：浏览章节和菜单。
4. 无缝体验：阅读进度自动保存和恢复！

idea-plugin.name: Kanban Board
idea-plugin.description:
Kanban Board for IntelliJ IDEA based IDE

A lightweight kanban board plugin to manage your development tasks directly in your IDE.

Features:

  • Kanban Board: Create multiple projects with customizable columns and drag-and-drop task management
  • Smart Notifications: Get notified at exact event times, deadlines, and IDE startup for all-day events
  • Calendar: Integrated calendar with events, deadlines, reminders, and notes
  • Rich Text: Markdown formatting support for task descriptions and notes
  • Tags & Priority: Color-coded tags and priority levels for better organization
  • Dark Theme: Full support for IntelliJ dark theme with adaptive colors
  • Persistent Storage: All data stored locally in JSON format
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.2.5

  • New: Card counter displayed on each column header for better task tracking
  • Improved: Calendar event cards now support long text with smart text wrapping and dynamic height
  • Improved: Better dark theme support with theme-aware colors throughout the UI
  • Improved: Centralized styling system for consistent appearance across all components
  • Perf: Debounced file saves (500ms delay) to prevent excessive disk writes and improve responsiveness
  • Perf: Optimized calendar event list rendering with resize debouncing

1.2.3

1.2.2

  • Fixed: Horizontal scrolling now works consistently across the entire board
  • Improved: Use Shift+Mouse Wheel to scroll horizontally from anywhere on the board

1.2.1

  • Fixed: Toolbar shadow rendering issue on Linux systems
  • Fixed: Toolbar buttons wrapping to multiple lines in card editor
  • Improved: Compact toolbar button layout with optimized spacing

idea-plugin.name: Dovlatov Highlights
idea-plugin.description:
Bring discipline to your writing — the way Sergei Dovlatov did.

Russian writer Sergei Dovlatov avoided using words that start with the same letter within a single sentence. This constraint helped him keep prose sharp and free of empty repetition. This plugin brings that principle into your editor.

What It Does

  • Analyzes text files in real time.
  • Splits text into phrases by ., !, ?, ; and ".
  • Considers only words longer than three letters.
  • Highlights words that start with the same letter in the same phrase.
  • Scales color intensity by the share of words in the phrase that start with that letter (more dominance → brighter color).

Why

The Dovlatov principle exposes repetition and tightens sentences. You will see patterns that bloat rhythm and clarity, and revise faster.

Works With

  • Plain text
  • Most alphabets
  • Full Unicode support

Ideal For

Writers, editors, and translators who want to avoid monotony and enforce stylistic discipline.

How to use

  • Toggle per-file on/off via the editor context menu
  • Right‑click in editor → "Toggle Dovlatov Annotator".

idea-plugin.name: Image Editor
idea-plugin.description:
Prepare project images and annotate screenshots without leaving your JetBrains IDE. Crop and resize assets, edit text and shapes on the canvas, and export favicons or web/app icons.

Free: image viewing, file thumbnails, zoom, fit, pan, transparency grid and RGBA pixel inspection.

License or trial required: all image editing, saving changes, export and developer presets.

  • Prepare assets: crop to exact coordinates, resize with aspect ratio lock, choose smooth or nearest-neighbor scaling, rotate and flip.
  • Annotate screenshots: add brush strokes, lines, rectangles, ellipses, text and opaque covers. Select, move, resize, recolor or delete annotations; double-click text to edit it in place.
  • Export copies: PNG, JPEG or WebP with quality, transparency and background controls. Preview favicon ICO, Apple touch, PWA, UI icon and avatar presets before choosing a destination.
  • Work with IDE controls: native toolbar, light/dark icons, keyboard customization, and Undo/Redo using your IDE keymap.
  • Keep work recoverable: automatic in-place saving, visible save failures, external-change protection and local recovery drafts.

Formats: PNG, JPEG, BMP, static WebP and single-page TIFF are editable when the required runtime codec is available. GIF, animated PNG/WebP, multi-page TIFF and ICO are view-only; export their raster preview to edit a copy. JPEG aliases JPE/JFIF and the APNG extension are recognized. SVG, AVIF, HEIC and layered documents are not supported.

Before editing: changes save to the open file, so use a working copy to keep the original unchanged. Saved, exported and recovered images contain flattened pixels; editable annotations and Undo history last only while the editor remains open. Metadata such as EXIF and color profiles may not be preserved. Inputs are limited to 48 MiB and 32 megapixels.

Requires IDE 2025.2 or newer with supported JCEF. Install the plugin, open an image in the editor, and use Activate Image Editor… in the toolbar to manage a license or trial.

idea-plugin.name: Flexible Julia
idea-plugin.description:
Julia IDE, Jupyter/Pluto notebooks, smart completion, REPL, debugger, profiler, refactoring, and more. Full Unicode support, multiple dispatch, macros, type system, navigation, live templates, and code inspections.

We are a new IDE extension and want to make it the best IDE for Julia developers. Your feedback is critical: Please leave a review, reach out to us on github, the community or email and tell us your thoughts, issues and more.

Documentation: See the user guide or the plugin page on the JetBrains Marketplace.

Core Features

Language Support

  • Complete Julia grammar with support for Julia 1.x syntax
  • LSP & JETL support (starts when a language server is installed; settings in File->Settings->Languages & Frameworks->Julia)
  • Advanced syntax highlighting with customizable color schemes (Default & Darcula)
  • Full Unicode support for operators and identifiers
  • String interpolation highlighting with $var and $(expr) patterns
  • Code folding for modules, functions, structs, macros, and block expressions
  • Brace matching with auto-close for {, (, [ and navigation
  • Comment support for line (#) and block (#= ... =#) comments
  • Project SDK Create new projects with a Julia SDK

Navigation & Intelligence

  • Go to Definition (Ctrl+Click) for functions, types, modules, and variables
  • Find Usages (Alt+F7) across your entire project
  • Structure View with icons for functions, macros, structs, modules, and types
  • Breadcrumbs navigation showing module hierarchy
  • Go to Symbol for quick navigation
  • Rename refactoring with reference tracking
  • Import optimizer for cleaning up import statements

Smart Completion & Hints

  • Context-aware code completion with 6-level prioritization
  • Type-aware suggestions after ::, where, @ operators
  • Package/module completion in import statements
  • Inlay hints for parameter names, types, and dispatch resolution
  • Parameter info tooltips for function signatures

Live Templates (29+)

Type j: to access all templates:

REPL & Package Manager

  • Integrated Julia REPL with Alt+Shift+Enter to run selection
  • Full REPL Support Switch modes with ";", "]", and "?". Auto-completion, history, and syntax highlighting
  • Environment Management for multiple Julia environments
  • Package Manager with Global/Project scope selector
  • Documentation browser with tree sidebar for browsing built-in docs by module/category, real-time filtering, and REPL-fetched docs
  • Debugger with breakpoints, stepping & hot-swapping. Fully integrated into the JetBrains Debugger
  • Remote Debugger via SSH (uses runtime configuration)

Jupyter Notebooks

  • Native .ipynb editor for Julia notebooks with code and markdown cells
  • Syntax-highlighted code cells using the full Julia editor with completion
  • Markdown rendering with GFM tables, strikethrough, and live preview
  • Rich output display for text, HTML, images (PNG/JPEG/SVG), tables, and errors
  • Multiple kernel backends: REPL-based, process-based, and Jupyter server
  • Environment selector per notebook with auto-discovered Project.toml environments
  • Non-intrusive: only claims Julia notebooks; defers to JetBrains Jupyter plugin for Python/R

Pluto.jl Notebooks

Pluto reactive notebooks support: markdown cells render, code cells run on the REPL or process kernel, and the file is saved back in Pluto's .jl format with the embedded Project.toml / Manifest.toml preserved.

Profiler

  • CPU profiler with flame graph, call tree, and method list views
  • Live streaming updates during profiling with state preservation
  • @profview macro in REPL or Profile run configuration
  • Allocation profiler via @profview_allocs (Julia 1.8+)
  • Snapshot management with save/load and export to .cpuprofile

Run Configurations

  • Julia run configuration with auto-detected settings
  • Run line markers in editor gutter
  • Remote execution/debugging via SSH with autosync of files

Dyad Modeling Language

Support for Dyad .dyad files: syntax highlighting, autocomplete, on-hover docs, smart Enter (auto-end), folding, structure view, live templates (d:), new-file + new-library wizards, and a "Reload Dyad Library in REPL" action that runs Pkg.activate + using <LibName> so Dyad.jl regenerates Julia code on the fly.

Definitions:

  • j:function, j:compact - Function forms
  • j:module, j:baremodule - Module definitions
  • j:struct, j:mutable - Type definitions
  • j:type, j:primitive - Parametric and primitive types
  • j:macro - Macro definition
  • j:abstract - Abstract type
  • j:where - Generic function with constraints

Control Flow:

  • j:if, j:ifelse, j:for, j:while, j:try
  • j:comprehension, j:generator - Array/generator expressions
  • j:ternary - Conditional operator

Multiple Dispatch:

  • j:dispatch - Method definition with types
  • j:multimethod - Multiple method variants

Macros & Performance:

  • j:@time, j:@inbounds, j:@simd - Performance annotations

Testing:

  • j:test, j:@test, j:testset - Test structures

Documentation:

  • j:doc, j:docfunc - Documentation with parameter descriptions

Postfix Templates

Type . after any expression to transform it:

  • .for â†’ for x in expr ... end
  • .if â†’ if expr ... end
  • .while, .try - Control flow wrapping
  • .not â†’ !(expr)
  • .return, .println, .typeof, .length - Quick transforms
  • .@time â†’ @time expr - Benchmark expression

Code Inspections & Quick Fixes

Automatic fixes via Alt+Enter:

  • Unused variables - Remove declaration or rename to underscore
  • Variable shadowing - Rename with context-aware suffix
  • Performance issues - Convert abstract to concrete types
  • Deprecated APIs - Auto-replace 24+ deprecated functions
  • Type stability - Add type annotations to improve performance

Intention Actions (Alt+Enter)

Function Transformations:

  • Convert between compact and full function forms
  • Add where clauses with type constraints
  • Add type annotations to parameters

Variable Refactoring:

  • Extract complex expressions to variables
  • Inline variable usages
  • Add type hints

String Operations:

  • Split long strings into multiple lines
  • Convert concatenation to interpolation

Getting Started

Quick Start

  1. Install the plugin from JetBrains Marketplace
  2. Create a new .jl file or open an existing Julia project
  3. Start coding with autocomplete, templates, and smart suggestions
  4. Use Alt+Enter for quick fixes and refactoring options
  5. Press Alt+Shift+Enter to send code to the integrated REPL

Productivity Tips

  • Type j: + Tab for instant code templates
  • Type expression + .for + Tab for postfix completion
  • Alt+Enter on any element for context-aware actions
  • Ctrl+Space for smart completion suggestions
  • Ctrl+Click to navigate to definitions
  • Alt+F7 to find all usages

Customization

  • Color schemes: File > Settings > Editor > Color Scheme > Julia
  • Live templates: File > Settings > Editor > Live Templates > JuliaGeneral
  • Inlay hints: File > Settings > Editor > Inlay Hints > Julia
  • Inspections: File > Settings > Editor > Inspections > Julia

Troubleshooting

  • File not recognized? Check file type association at Settings > Editor > File Types > Julia
    • The .jl file should show the Julia icon in the project tree
    • If missing, add *.jl to the Julia file type

What's New in 2026.7.0

  • Jupyter notebook support â€” native .ipynb editor for Julia with code cells, markdown rendering, and rich output
  • Run File button split into one-click execute + mode selector dropdown

See CHANGELOG.md for complete details.

Made by Developers with a Passion for Scientific Computing

The integration is the work of Ilscipio:

We develop scientific computing solutions as part of our technology stack and understand the unique needs of Julia developers. We created this plugin to make Julia development more intuitive and productive in JetBrains IDEs.

We're sharing this tool with the Julia community to support the ecosystem's growth and to make high-performance computing more accessible.

  • Special discounts are available for individual developers & of course for the whole Open Source community.

Bugs & Feature Requests

If you have any questions, feature requests or stumble upon the occasional bug, come leave us a message at Ilscipio
