idea-plugin.name: ANTLR4 Plus
idea-plugin.description:
ANTLR4 grammar development plugin for IntelliJ with compiled execution.

ANTLR4+ runs the ANTLR4 tool to generate Java or Kotlin source, compiles it in-process with the bundled ECJ or Kotlin compiler, and executes the resulting parser against your input. Embedded actions, semantic predicates, custom base classes, and listener/visitor overrides all run. No external JDK is required.

Live Compiled Preview

Select a .g4p input file and the codegen-compile-execute cycle runs automatically. Edit your grammar or input and the parse tree, token list, and profiler data update in real time. No manual trigger required.

Custom Base Classes With Zero Configuration

Grammars that use superClass, contextSuperClass, or TokenLabelType options work out of the box. The plugin auto-discovers the matching .java or .kt source file anywhere in your project. There is no source-root setup to do, no libDir to configure, and no manual classpath wiring.

  • Resolves all three class-valued grammar options: lexer and parser superClass, parser contextSuperClass (the base class for generated ParserRuleContext subclasses), and parser TokenLabelType.
  • Mixed Java and Kotlin: base classes can be written in either language, in any combination, and can live in different subdirectories from each other and from the grammar.
  • Searches the whole project model: uses IntelliJ's project file index, so additional content roots, multi-module setups, test sources, and unconventional layouts (for example a grammar in grammars/ with base classes in src/) all work without configuration.
  • Lexer actions are real: custom emit() overrides, pushMode and popMode from rule actions, and token-injection patterns from a Kotlin or Java lexer base class execute exactly as they would at runtime, because the plugin instantiates your compiled lexer subclass directly instead of an interpreter.
  • Conflict resolution: when the same simple class name exists in multiple locations, a dialog shows every candidate with its full path so you can pick the one to use, and the choice is cached per binding.
  • Clear errors: if a referenced class can't be found, the ANTLR console reports the exact option (for example parser contextSuperClass = com.example.MyContextBase) so you know which option to fix.

Token Timeline with Editor Integration

Shows every token your lexer produces, including hidden and skipped tokens, with lexer mode transitions rendered inline. Click any token to jump to its source span in the editor. Per-token colorization overlays token boundaries directly onto your input file so you can see whitespace handling and mode switches at a glance.

Profiler and Micro-Benchmarks

Shows parser performance at the ATN decision level: per-rule invocation counts, lookahead depth histograms, ambiguity reports, and DFA cache hit/miss ratios. Includes a micro-benchmark runner with configurable warmup iterations for measuring cold-start and steady-state parse throughput.

Structured LLM Context Export

Exports grammar source, input text, token stream, parse tree, and error diagnostics as a single structured markdown document. Per-section line counts let you include or exclude sections to stay within token budgets. Ready to paste into ChatGPT, Claude, or any LLM.

19,000+ Pre-Built Grammar Bindings

Clone the grammars-v4 repository at the pinned commit and apply the bundled bindings to get parse-tree previews for 600+ grammars covering Java, Python, C++, SQL, JavaScript, Kotlin, Go, Rust, Swift, and many other languages. Each binding maps a grammar to its example input files, no manual configuration needed.

git clone https://github.com/antlr/grammars-v4.git && cd grammars-v4 && git checkout 7bb150f

IDE Integration

  • Syntax highlighting with configurable color schemes (light and dark)
  • Real-time error annotation via external annotator pipeline
  • Code completion for rule references, tokens, and channels
  • Goto-definition, find-usages, and rename-refactoring across grammar files
  • Extract rule, inline rule, and automatic lexer rule generation for string literals
  • Combined, split-grammar (lexer + parser), and imported grammar support
  • Ambiguity and lookahead visualization per parser decision
  • Hierarchical rule viewer with bidirectional caller/callee navigation
  • Grammar formatting with configurable style (Ctrl+Alt+L)
  • Project tree decorations showing grammar bindings and .g4p file status
  • Zero CPU and memory overhead when the plugin is toggled off

ANTLR4+ is an independent, closed-source plugin and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to Terence Parr, Sam Harwell, or the ANTLR project. Built based on https://github.com/antlr/intellij-plugin-v4.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Custom base class resolution overhaul. Parser contextSuperClass and TokenLabelType options are now resolved end-to-end alongside superClass. Grammars that mix these options no longer hit "missing class" errors. Mixed Java and Kotlin base classes in different subdirectories work without configuration.
  • Project-wide file-index lookup for base classes. Replaces the previous walk-only resolver, which couldn't reach files in sibling top-level directories of the grammar (for example a grammar in grammars/ with the base class in src/main/kotlin/...), additional content roots, or multi-module setups. The plugin now finds them automatically.
  • Filesystem-walk fallback for the resolver. If the IntelliJ project model doesn't expose a referenced base class through any standard scope (loosely opened directories, externally stored module configs, Maven imports that only register a few source roots), the resolver now walks the project base path looking for the exact filename. Guarantees that a file physically present anywhere under the project directory is findable.
  • Sibling-folder discovery in the bind-grammar picker. Right-clicking a .g4p file now offers grammars from immediate sibling folders of the .g4p's directory (e.g. customer_repro/grammars/Foo.g4 next to customer_repro/input/Foo.g4p), not just from ancestor directories.
  • Code completion inside options { ... } blocks. Suggests valid option names appropriate for the grammar type (lexer, parser, combined) and enumerated values for language and caseInsensitive.
  • Gutter icon next to the start rule. A green play icon appears in the editor gutter next to the first parser rule of any parser or combined grammar, identifying it as ANTLR's implicit default entry point. The marker and the unused-rule inspection now agree on what counts as the start rule.
  • RuntimeConsole pane. A new console tab next to the compiler console captures System.out / System.err produced by parse actions during preview runs, so println-style debugging inside grammar actions is finally visible without digging through the IDE log.
  • More actionable missing-class error in the ANTLR console. It now reports the exact option name (for example parser contextSuperClass = com.example.MyBase) instead of a bare class name.

Changed

  • The first parser rule is no longer flagged as "unused". ANTLR's implicit default start rule is the first parser rule in source order; by definition no other rule calls it, so flagging it produced a persistent false positive. Unused-rule detection now skips it.
  • The dependency analyzer that scans Java/Kotlin source files for transitive class references now strips comments and string literal contents before running its identifier-extraction regexes. Eliminates spurious filesystem walks for English words from doc comments (e.g. Note, Demonstrates, Available).

idea-plugin.name: Mermaid Studio
idea-plugin.description:
Mermaid Studio provides rich language support for authoring Mermaid diagrams in your JetBrains IDE - error detection, syntax highlighting, live preview, export, and deep code intelligence for all native Mermaid.js diagram types. All features work fully offline.

Also available as Mermaid Studio Core - a free edition with optional paid upgrade for Flowchart, Sequence, Class, State, ER, Block, and Swimlane diagrams.

Supports Mermaid.js 12.0.0 with optional support for previous versions of Mermaid.js. See supported versions.

Remote development: Works in JetBrains remote development environments, excluding JetBrains Gateway.

Compatible with Android Studio starting with the Quail (2026.1) canary releases.

Features

  • Interactive Editor - Drag-and-drop flowchart creation plus visual editing for class diagrams (rename elements, set annotations, style classes and relationships), with a persistent style tool window that works in both standalone diagrams and Markdown code fences
  • MCP Tools - AI agents can generate and validate diagrams in Mermaid Studio's mermaid.js rendering environment
  • Error Detection - Real-time syntax errors and semantic validation that catches naming conflicts, out-of-range indices, and unsupported values
  • Inspections & Quick Fixes - Catch logic issues that Mermaid itself can't pinpoint, like unresolved references, circular references, unused style classes, duplicate definitions, and invalid lifecycles, often with one-click fixes
  • Syntax & Semantic Highlighting - Rich, diagram-aware highlighting with theme-appropriate colors
  • Code Completion - Contextual suggestions for syntax, element references, and values
  • Live Templates - Bundled, customizable templates for common diagram constructs, plus support for your own user-defined templates in Mermaid editor contexts
  • Automatic Formatting - Keep diagrams clean and consistent
  • Refactoring - Safely rename elements with automatic reference updates
  • Find Usages - Locate all references to any diagram element
  • Live Preview - Real-time rendering with zoom, pan, search, and background matching (auto-matches editor or diagram theme). Supports Mac trackpad gestures for pinch-to-zoom and two-finger panning
  • Appearance Controls - Set a light/dark diagram theme, look, and font from the preview Appearance dropdown
  • Bundled Custom Themes - Eight ready-made custom themes (Chalk, Iris, Islands, Moss, Neutral, Parchment, Slate, Terracotta), each with matched light and dark variants (all diagram types except C4)
  • Custom Themes - Build your own themes in a visual editor with live preview, tune colors per diagram type, and import or export them as JSON to share across projects
  • Theme Generator - Create a complete light-and-dark theme from a handful of seed colors, or pull the seeds from an image such as a logo or screenshot, then apply it directly or refine it in the editor
  • Export & Print - Save diagrams as PNG or SVG, copy as PNG or SVG to the clipboard, or print with paper-size-aware scaling and configurable margins (route through your OS print-to-PDF for lossless vector PDF export)
  • Mermaid in Markdown - Full highlighting and live preview for diagrams in Markdown code fences
  • Go to Mermaid Source - Jump from a diagram image in Markdown (.svg / .png) back to its .mmd / .mermaid source via a gutter icon
  • Frontmatter Support - YAML schema validation and completion for diagram configuration
  • Theme CSS Highlighting & Completions - CSS highlighting, validation, and contextual class-name completion inside frontmatter config.themeCSS: blocks, with completions sourced from your classDef names and the classes pulled from the rendered live preview (requires a paid JetBrains IDE with CSS support prior to 2026.1, or any JetBrains IDE from 2026.1 onward)
  • Structure View - Navigate diagram elements in the structure tool window
  • Code Vision - Inline usage counts on definitions
  • Code Folding - Collapse diagram sections to focus on what matters
  • Brace Matching - Highlights and auto-inserts matching brackets and delimiters
  • Color Gutter Icons - Inline color swatches in the gutter with a click-to-edit color picker
  • Navigate from Preview - Click diagram elements to jump to their declaration in the source code
  • Icon Sets - Use bundled FontAwesome, AWS, Azure, and GCP icons in your diagrams or import additional sets from Iconify
  • Diagram Sync - Automatically export diagrams as SVG or PNG files on save
  • Localization - UI elements, error messages, inspections, and inline documentation translated into German, Japanese, Korean, and Simplified Chinese (generated from English using a workflow that leverages multiple frontier language models)

Each diagram type has a different set of features based on what makes sense for its syntax and structure. New features are added regularly.

MCP Tools

Mermaid Studio includes MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools that leverage its deep understanding of Mermaid diagrams for AI-assisted diagram generation and validation.

  • generateMermaidDiagram - Generate a Mermaid diagram as SVG from provided code
  • generateMermaidPng - Generate a PNG image and save it to a file
  • analyzeMermaidDiagram - Validate diagram code using Mermaid Studio's parsing and analysis
  • getMermaidFrontmatterSchema - Get the JSON Schema for a diagram type's frontmatter configuration
  • searchMermaidIcons - Search configured icon sets for available icons
  • getMermaidSyntaxGuide - Get a condensed syntax guide for a diagram type

Telemetry

Mermaid Studio collects usage data to help improve the plugin. Telemetry is essential for understanding how users interact with features and identifying areas for improvement.

No personally identifiable or project-identifiable information is collected.

Telemetry is disabled by default in stable releases; nothing is sent unless you turn it on in the plugin settings. In Early Access Program (EAP) builds it is enabled by default and can be turned off in the same place.

Learn more.

Visit MermaidStudio.dev for more information and documentation about Mermaid Studio and its features.

Tachi Labs and Mermaid Studio are not affiliated with Mermaid or Mermaid Chart Inc.

Github | Telegram | Donation

Maintainers

You trust dozens of packages. Do you know who's behind them?

Maintainers plugin shows you the people and organizations behind every dependency in your project — their GitHub profiles, how many packages they maintain, and how to support them.

One abandoned package can break your build. One mass-resignation can tank your stack. Know your supply chain.

What you get:

  • Automatic parsing of lock files:
    • composer.lock for PHP
    • package-lock.json for JavaScript
    • go.sum for Go
  • GitHub avatars and org icons for instant recognition
  • Two views: browse by package or by maintainer
  • Direct links to funding pages — sponsor the people who keep your code running

Why it matters:

That mass layoff at a tech company? Some of those engineers maintained packages you depend on. That solo dev who burned out? Maybe they wrote your HTTP client.

Maintainers plugin turns your dependency tree from a list of strings into a map of humans.

idea-plugin.name: spring-profile-editor
idea-plugin.description:
Unified Profile Management for Spring Boot

Manage Spring Boot configurations across multiple profiles and files within a single, integrated tool window. Spring Profile Editor consolidates properties from application.yml, .properties, and multi-document YAML files into a clear grid view.

Key Features

  • Consolidated View
    View and compare properties from all active profiles side-by-side. Columns represent profiles (e.g., default, dev, prod), making profile-specific overrides immediately visible.
  • Inline Value Editing
    Double-click a profile cell to edit its value. Changes are written back to the source .properties or .yml file, creating nested YAML keys when needed. Overriding an inherited value asks for confirmation first.
  • Source Navigation
    Right-click a value and choose Go to Source to jump to its definition in the source file. Click profile headers to open the corresponding configuration file.
  • Profile Filtering
    Use the "Profiles" dropdown to select/deselect specific profiles or toggle all profiles at once for a focused view.
  • Search & Highlight
    Filter properties by key or value with real-time highlighting to locate configurations.
  • Context Menu Access
    Right-click on any .yml or .properties file in the Project View to open the editor instantly.
  • Multi-Module Support
    Seamlessly switch between modules using the dropdown selector. The editor automatically filters and displays configurations relevant to the selected module.

Links

  • Issue Tracker
  • Documentation


Spring Boot를 위한 통합 프로파일 관리

단일 통합 도구 창에서 여러 프로파일과 파일에 걸친 Spring Boot 설정을 관리하세요. Spring Profile Editor는 application.yml, .properties 및 멀티 문서 YAML 파일의 속성을 명확한 그리드 뷰로 통합하여 보여줍니다.

핵심 기능

  • 통합 뷰 (Consolidated View)
    모든 활성 프로파일의 속성을 한눈에 비교하고 확인할 수 있습니다. 각 열(Column)은 프로파일(예: default, dev, prod)을 나타내며, 프로파일별로 재정의된 값을 쉽게 파악할 수 있습니다.
  • 인라인 값 편집 (Inline Value Editing)
    프로파일 셀을 더블 클릭하여 값을 직접 편집할 수 있습니다. 변경 사항은 소스 .properties 또는 .yml 파일에 반영되며, 필요한 경우 중첩 YAML 키를 생성합니다. 상속된 값을 재정의할 때는 먼저 확인을 요청합니다.
  • 소스 탐색 (Source Navigation)
    값을 우클릭하여 Go to Source를 선택하면 소스 파일의 해당 정의로 이동합니다. 프로파일 헤더를 클릭하면 해당 설정 파일이 열립니다.
  • 프로파일 필터링 (Profile Filtering)
    "Profiles" 드롭다운을 통해 특정 프로파일만 선택해서 보거나, "All" 옵션으로 전체를 한 번에 선택/해제할 수 있습니다.
  • 검색 및 강조 (Search & Highlight)
    실시간 검색 및 강조 기능을 통해 원하는 속성을 빠르게 찾을 수 있습니다.
  • 컨텍스트 메뉴 지원 (ContextMenu Access)
    Project View에서 .yml 또는 .properties 파일을 우클릭하여 플러그인을 즉시 실행할 수 있습니다.
  • 멀티 모듈 지원 (Multi-Module Support)
    드롭다운 선택기를 통해 모듈 간을 원활하게 전환할 수 있습니다. 에디터는 선택된 모듈과 관련된 설정만 자동으로 필터링하여 표시합니다.

링크

  • 이슈 트래커
  • 문서

idea-plugin.name: Mermaid Visualizer

Mermaid diagrams in your IDE — live preview, code intelligence, and export, all offline.

  • Dedicated split editor with live preview for .mmd and .mermaid files

Code Intelligence

  • Syntax highlighting — keywords, diagram types, arrows, strings, comments, punctuation
  • Code completion — diagram types, context-sensitive keywords, node/participant names, arrows, directives
  • Go to Definition (Ctrl+B) — navigate to node/participant declarations
  • Find Usages (Alt+F7) — find all references to a node across the diagram
  • Rename (Shift+F6) — rename nodes/participants with all references updated
  • Structure View (Alt+7) — hierarchical view of diagrams, blocks, and nodes
  • Code Folding — fold subgraphs, loop/alt/opt/par blocks, and consecutive comments
  • Inspections & quick-fixes — unknown diagram types (with typo suggestions), invalid arrows, unused nodes
  • Render error annotations — Mermaid.js parsing errors surfaced directly in the editor

Settings

Configurable via Settings > Tools > Mermaid — theme (incl. the Mermaid 12 redux/neo themes), look (classic/hand-drawn/neo), layout engine (ELK/dagre), font family, max text size, live reload delay, max preview height.

Custom rendering colors — optionally override the visualizer background color and the line/edge color (disabled by default, so the rendering keeps following your IDE theme unless you opt in).

Usage

Use as a JSON pretty printer, tree explorer, or JSON notepad and playground right inside IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, Rider, and all JetBrains IDEs.

  • Notes-style tabs — multiple document tabs; work with several JSONs side by side; names and content persist
  • Cross-IDE sync — tabs shared across all JetBrains IDEs; sync across machines via JetBrains Settings Sync
  • Format & minify — pretty-print (beautify) or remove whitespace; works on any text, preserves strings
  • Tree view — interactive tree with color-coded types; expand/collapse all; copy value from context menu
  • Property grid — inspect selected node key/value or children in a side panel
  • Search — Cmd+F / Ctrl+F with next/previous and highlights in both text and tree
  • Paste / Copy — quick clipboard actions in the toolbar
  • Main editor — open JSON Notes in the editor area (Tools menu)
  • Keyboard shortcuts — optional keybindings for all actions; shortcut reference in JSON Notes settings
  • Plain text support — optional keyword highlighting for common programming tokens; word-occurrence highlights

Inspired by Online JSON Viewer (jsonviewer.stack.hu).

idea-plugin.name: Puffin Reader
idea-plugin.description:
Puffin Reader is an IntelliJ plugin for inspecting Apache Iceberg Puffin files.

Puffin files are efficient for query engines but difficult for humans to read. This plugin lets you drag and drop a .puffin file to instantly view its deletion vectors in a readable table format.

Features

  • Drag & drop any .puffin file into the Puffin Reader tool window
  • Deleted Rows tab — displays a table with referenced_datafile and row_index columns, grouped by data file and sorted by row index
  • Summary tab — shows a per-deletion-vector breakdown with the number of deleted rows for each referenced data file
  • Row limit dropdown — preview the first 100, 500, 1,000, 5,000, or 10,000 rows (default: 100)
  • Supports the deletion-vector-v1 blob type with Roaring bitmap decoding
  • Handles uncompressed and LZ4-compressed footer payloads
idea-plugin.change-notes:

  • Puffin file parser supporting the Iceberg Puffin spec
  • Deletion vector decoding (deletion-vector-v1 blob type) with 64-bit Roaring bitmap support

  • Summary tab showing per-deletion-vector row counts
  • Row limit dropdown (100, 500, 1,000, 5,000, 10,000) with a max cap of 10,000 rows
  • LZ4-compressed footer payload support

idea-plugin.name: MarkFlow - Seamless WYSIWYG Markdown Editor (markdown and more)
idea-plugin.description:
( markdown, mermaid, latex-katex, raw-html, wysiwyg )

MarkFlow is a Typora-style WYSIWYG Markdown editor for IntelliJ-based IDEs.

It opens supported Markdown files in a custom IntelliJ editor, keeps the document and JCEF webview synchronized in both directions, and restores editor state such as scroll position, caret, and selection when reopening files.

MarkFlow supports Mermaid diagrams, KaTeX math, Markdown-aware paste, and raw HTML rendering with XSS sanitization, with configurable rendering options for theme source, body font family and size, Mermaid sizing and zoom, error display, KaTeX density, and preview defaults.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changed

  • Preserved original Markdown formatting during save by keeping the raw source text stable.
  • Performance optimizations.
  • Raised the minimum IDE to IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2 (pluginSinceBuild from 252 to 262) and aligned the platform target and the Java toolchain (21 to 25) with it.
  • IDE_SYNC now sends the captured IDE background, foreground, selection, and border palette through the runtime-settings contract; LIGHT and DARK remain explicit overrides.
  • IDE_SYNC Mermaid appearance now derives arrow, node, and label colors from the captured palette and invalidates only when Mermaid-relevant palette values change.

Fixed

  • Skipped browser pre-warm and editor takeover when JCEF is unavailable in the IDE runtime instead of failing with an error.
  • The body font family is now a dropdown of installed families (single value); the IDE-configured font is the default and is shown as IDE Default (<actual family>); an explicit selection of the same installed family remains distinct. The webview quotes the family so a persisted value cannot break out of the CSS font-family value.
  • Ensured runtime font variables override Crepe's bundled declarations so changing the body font takes effect in the editor.
  • Propagated the configured base font size from settings into the webview and clamped it to the IntelliJ editor-supported range.
  • Direct font-size input now marks the settings panel as modified so Apply becomes available.
  • Unavailable persisted font families now fall back to the active IDE editor font without requiring a settings round-trip; text contrast selection now uses the higher WCAG black/white endpoint.

Added

  • Typora-style WYSIWYG Markdown editing experience via a custom IntelliJ FileEditor.
  • Automatic takeover of Markdown files (.md, .markdown, .mdown, .mkdn) with the MarkFlow editor.
  • Two-way synchronization between IntelliJ document text and the JCEF webview editor.
  • Editor UI state persistence and restore (scroll position, cursor, and selection).
  • Mermaid diagram live preview support in Markdown code blocks.
  • KaTeX math rendering support for inline and block formulas.
  • Markdown clipboard paste now preserves Markdown structure, while code blocks keep the default paste behavior.
  • Raw HTML support for inline and block HTML with XSS sanitization via Milkdown integration.
  • Packaged webview loading through classloader resources with shared local HTTP serving.
  • Configurable MarkFlow settings panel (theme source and preview defaults).
  • Extended Mermaid preview controls (size mode, zoom, error display behavior) and diagram security level configuration.
  • Runtime settings synchronization from IntelliJ to webview with sequenced updates to reduce stale apply races.
  • Pooled JCEF browsers with split-editor reuse and configurable idle eviction timeout.
  • Body font family (IDE default shown by its actual family name, plus installed families) and IntelliJ editor-range base font size (px) controls in the MarkFlow General settings, applied through Crepe's --crepe-base-font-size.

idea-plugin.name: YAML Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
Human-readable YAML viewer with tree/table hybrid rendering

Tired of scrolling through 500-line Kubernetes manifests, Helm charts, or CI configs? YAML Viewer adds a navigable, structured preview next to any .yaml / .yml file — think OpenAPI/Swagger UI, but for arbitrary YAML.

Features

  • Split editor — raw YAML on the left, rendered tree view on the right
  • Hybrid tree + table rendering — nested sections collapse; leaf groups render as compact key/value/type tables
  • Type badges — string, int, float, bool, null shown inline at a glance
  • Bidirectional sync — click a node in the tree to jump to the line in the editor, and vice versa
  • Search & filter — Cmd/Ctrl+F filters the tree by key or value; Escape clears
  • Breadcrumb navigation — see the full path to the selected node, click to jump to any ancestor
  • Invalid-YAML tolerant — keeps the last valid view while you edit, instead of going blank
  • Schema-agnostic — works with any YAML file; no special-casing for specific formats

Built on the IntelliJ Platform YAML PSI — no external parsers, no performance surprises.

idea-plugin.name: SOPS Editor
idea-plugin.description:
Edit SOPS-encrypted files directly in your JetBrains IDE. The plugin opens a split view with the decrypted content on one side and the raw ciphertext on the other, and re-encrypts the file when you save.

Features

  • Side-by-side decrypted and encrypted view for any SOPS file
  • Automatic re-encryption on Ctrl+S, with an opt-out in settings
  • Context menu actions for Encrypt with SOPS, Decrypt with SOPS and New SOPS Encrypted File
  • Default shortcuts Ctrl+Alt+E to encrypt and Ctrl+Alt+D to decrypt
  • Supports .env, YAML, JSON, INI and binary (.sops, .bin) files, matching the sops CLI itself
  • Age key and PGP support through the system sops binary
  • A setup validator that checks your sops binary, age key file and environment
  • A log file with secret masking for AGE keys, PEM private key blocks and SSH public keys

Requirements

  • The sops CLI on your PATH, or a full path configured in settings
  • An age key file (default: ~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt) or a configured PGP key
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.1

  • Fixed a bug that could cause high CPU usage while a SOPS file was open: the editor reported the encrypted file to the IDE's code-analysis daemon while showing the decrypted contents, which made the daemon restart in a loop.

1.1.0

  • Binary-mode SOPS files (.sops + .bin) now open in the split-view editor with the JSON envelope shown read-only on the right and the inner extension driving syntax highlighting on the left.
  • SOPS files are auto-detected from their content, so files with non-standard extensions are picked up automatically.
  • TOML dropped from the supported list; .toml SOPS files are detected as binary mode (which is what SOPS actually produces for them).
  • Save no longer crashes with a Write-unsafe context error on newer IntelliJ Platform builds.
  • Added SECURITY.md and a least-privilege permissions block to the build workflow.

1.0.0

First public release. See the README on GitHub for the feature list and setup instructions.

idea-plugin.name: GameMaker Tools
idea-plugin.description:
Support for GameMaker projects and code editing

GameMaker Tools adds focused support for GameMaker projects and GML in IntelliJ-based IDEs. It is built for developers who want a stronger code editing workflow for GameMaker 2.3+, including current LTS and GMS2024 projects.

Getting started

  1. Install a compatible JetBrains IDE such as IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, CLion, or another IntelliJ-based IDE.
  2. Open Settings | Plugins, search for GameMaker Tools, and install the plugin.
  3. Restart the IDE when prompted.
  4. Open your GameMaker project by selecting the project .yyp folder.
  5. Use the standard Project view for raw files, or open the GameMaker tool window for a resource-oriented view of the project.

What the plugin includes

  • GML language support: syntax highlighting, semantic highlighting, code completion, parameter info, quick documentation, and manual links for built-in symbols.
  • Navigation tools: go to declaration, identifier resolution, and find usages for GameMaker code symbols.
  • Type-aware feedback: editor annotations for supported GML type diagnostics.
  • Project-aware symbol discovery: support for project functions, macros, enums, globals, object members, and GameMaker resources in completion and navigation.
  • GameMaker project explorer: a dedicated tool window that shows GameMaker groups, assets, and object events in a structure that matches the project metadata.
  • Project organization: create groups, rename assets, and move assets or folders with drag and drop while keeping GameMaker project metadata in sync.
  • Metadata workflows: open the owning .yy file quickly and use the specialized editor to inspect and update supported metadata.
  • Object editing support: edit common object properties such as sprite, mask, visibility, solid, persistence, and physics, and add or remove object events.
  • Automatic object event synchronization: event metadata is kept aligned with supported object event file changes.

How to use it well

This plugin works especially well as a companion to the GameMaker IDE. Use JetBrains for code editing, navigation, refactoring, project browsing, and metadata maintenance, while continuing to use GameMaker for workflows that still depend on the official editor.

Complementary and conflicting plugins

No additional plugins are required. There are currently no known plugin conflicts. If you already use general JetBrains plugins, they should continue to work normally alongside GameMaker Tools.

Current scope

GameMaker Tools is aimed at a clean development workflow for GameMaker 2.3 and newer. It does not try to replace every editor view from GameMaker itself, especially for asset types that still rely on the native GameMaker editing experience. It is mostly focussed on quick and clean code editing and refactoring.

Webox — Manage and browse web pages right inside your IDE, without switching to a browser.

  • Sidebar panel to manage bookmarks (name, URL, description) with group support

Webox（网页盒） 是一款让你在 JetBrains IDE 中直接管理和浏览网页的插件，彻底告别在浏览器与 IDE 之间反复切换。

  • 退出自动保存：关闭 IDE 时自动保存所有已打开的网页 Tab，下次打开可一键全部恢复（可在设置中关闭）
  • 数据导入 / 导出：支持以 JSON 格式导出全部链接和分组，方便在多台设备或团队之间共享配置

idea-plugin.name: SSM Graph
idea-plugin.description:
Spring State Machine Graph

Streamline your development process by visualizing complex Spring State Machine (SSM) configurations directly within your IDE. This plugin provides a clear, graphical representation of your state machine logic, eliminating the need to manually trace transitions through lines of code.

Runtime Visualization (Java Agent)

Unlike traditional tools that rely on static code analysis, this plugin utilizes a Java Agent to capture the actual creation of State Machines during runtime. This ensures that the visualization reflects the real structure of your SSM, exactly as it is initialized by the Spring context.

Key Features

  • Interactive Graph Rendering: Automatically transforms states and transitions into an intuitive visual map, making it easy to understand complex business flows at a glance.
  • Flexible Launch Support: Works seamlessly with both local application startups and individual Unit Tests. If a State Machine is created, the visualizer will catch it.
  • Advanced Toolset: A dedicated UI panel provides specialized tools to enhance readability, allowing you to organize, and analyze your structure effectively.
  • Direct DOT Integration: Generates standard .dot files in a local ssmGraph folder, allowing for manual edits and version control of your diagrams.

idea-plugin.description:
Dusk Office Themes — dark, light and OLED themes for JetBrains IDEs

Dusk Office Themes brings the same professional theme system as VS Code / Cursor / Windsurf to IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, Rider, CLion, GoLand, PhpStorm, RubyMine, DataGrip, RustRover, Android Studio and the wider JetBrains platform.

27 WCAG-conscious variants — dark, light and high-contrast — tuned for finance, audit, cybersecurity and long sessions. Full IDE UI themes plus matching editor color schemes.

GPL-3.0 · CI · VS Code Marketplace · Open VSX · JetBrains Marketplace

What's inside

  • Full IDE UI themes — title bar, tool windows, tabs, menus, dialogs, lists, popups
  • Editor color schemes — syntax, gutter, breakpoints, debugger, inspections
  • Terminal ANSI colors — WCAG-conscious foreground / background contrast on every variant
  • Diff & VCS colors — readable change markers, blame, inline diff
  • Semantic token contrast — consistent accent palette across languages

Featured variants

  • Dusk Office Midnight — OLED-friendly deep-focus dark
  • Dusk Office Vault — banking, treasury, executive operations
  • Dusk Office Sentinel — cybersecurity, SOC, monitoring
  • Dusk Office Audit — controls, long spreadsheet review
  • Dusk Office Finance — premium banking aesthetic
  • Dusk Office Ledger — soft finance light, reduced glare
  • Dusk Office Steward — professional dark for long sessions
  • Dusk Office Ivory — daytime light variant
  • Dusk Office High Contrast — accessibility-first

How to apply

Settings → Appearance & Behavior → Appearance → Theme for the complete IDE theme, or Settings → Editor → Color Scheme for syntax only.

Tip: 100% Dusk look

JetBrains adds a per-project color gradient on the main toolbar (the colored badge near your project name). It is generated from the project name and is intentionally not overridable by themes — it helps you tell apart multiple IDE windows.

If you prefer a uniform Dusk Office look, disable it once in Settings → Appearance & Behavior → Appearance → uncheck "Show project gradient in toolbar" (label varies: "Color the toolbar by project" / "Project Color"). On older builds, use Help → Find Action → Registry… and disable ide.colorful.toolbar.

Cross-IDE identity

Same palette as the VS Code Marketplace and Open VSX versions — use the exact same colors in VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf and your JetBrains IDE.

License: GPL-3.0-or-later. Source & issues: github.com/SIDIKICONDE/dusk-office.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Dusk Office Themes 1.5.10

  • **Fixed**: **Workspace memory no longer overrides the theme you picked** — `duskOffice.rememberWorkspaceTheme` now defaults to **`false`**. It was the only automatic theme writer enabled by default, so it re-applied a remembered Dusk variant on every launch with no opt-in. It was also the reason *Reset All Settings* appeared not to work: that command writes `undefined` for the key, which fell back to the `true` default and re-armed the behaviour the reset dialog promises to clear.
  • **Fixed**: **Picks made in VS Code now stick** — a theme chosen through VS Code's own *Preferences: Color Theme* picker never went through `applyTheme`, so the extension had no way to know it had been overridden. `onDidChangeActiveColorTheme` now treats any change it did not cause as a manual override: it records the override (so Auto Switch and Adaptive Focus back off for the usual 5s grace window) and clears the stored workspace theme so it cannot come back on the next launch.
  • **Fixed**: Workspace memory echo suppression uses a 1s time window rather than a counter. VS Code resolves the theme event asynchronously and may fire it more than once per write, so a counter could desynchronise and read the second event as a manual pick — clearing the pin that had just been saved.
  • **Fixed**: Accepting the workspace-fingerprint suggestion (**Try it**) no longer pins that variant permanently. The prompt reads as a one-time suggestion, so applying it no longer opts you into workspace memory as a side effect.
  • **Changed**: `duskOffice.rememberWorkspaceTheme` description now states that a remembered theme overrides your VS Code pick until you change the theme again.
  • **Docs**: The QUICKSTART-LONG settings table and the walkthrough mark workspace memory as opt-in; README's Quick Settings list says the same.
  • **Tests**: `tests/workspace-theme-memory.test.js` (13 tests) covers the default, the inert startup path, the manual-override escape hatch, echo suppression, and the fingerprint path. The `vscode` mock gained `workspace.fs` (`stat` / `readFile` / `readDirectory`), `Uri.joinPath`, and `FileType` so the fingerprint path can be driven end to end.
  • **Fixed**: **Upgrading no longer writes opt-in defaults into your `settings.json`** — `migrateExistingProfileDefaults` used to write `duskOffice.titleBar.alignWithTheme: true` and `duskOffice.editorAnsi.allLanguages: true` at `ConfigurationTarget.Global` for every profile with prior Dusk Office state, silently. The title-bar one then cascaded into a global `window.titleBarStyle: "custom"` write — a setting with no `dusk` prefix, so nothing in your `settings.json` hinted at its author. Legacy values are now kept as a read-time fallback (`state.legacyProfileDefaults`); an explicit value, including `false`, always wins and nothing is written. The verdict is persisted under `duskOffice.legacyProfileDefaults`, because the fallback no longer lives in your settings and would otherwise be lost on the next launch.

Full changelog: CHANGELOG.md

idea-plugin.name: JPA 3D
idea-plugin.description:
See your JPA entity model the way you reason about it — as a living graph, right inside the IDE. JPA 3D reads your @Entity classes (Java & Kotlin) and renders them as an interactive 3D force-directed graph or a 2D orthogonal ERD, so relationships, inheritance, and Spring Data repositories become something you can actually look at, navigate, and share.

JPA 3D is intended to:
  • Make a large JPA model understandable at a glance — no more reading annotations file by file
  • Help you trace how entities connect, where the foreign keys are, and how inheritance is mapped
  • Turn your code into shareable artifacts — diagrams, DDL, and Mermaid — in a couple of clicks

JPA 3D delivers:
  • A 3D / 2D viewer that stays in sync with your source — click any node to jump to its file
  • Accurate analysis of relationships, cardinality, inheritance, and Spring Data repositories
  • One-click export to JSON, DDL (PostgreSQL / MySQL / H2 / Oracle), Mermaid, and PNG / SVG

It works in any project using Spring Boot, Jakarta EE, or plain JPA — with both jakarta.persistence and legacy javax.persistence, in Java and Kotlin.

Most loved features

Explore your model in 3D & 2D
  • 3D force-directed graph with entity-card sprites and depth anchors
  • 2D orthogonal ERD with clean layered routing (elkjs)
  • 3D minimap — a projected overview of every node; click to fly the camera there (keeps zoom)
  • Manual layout overrides — drag nodes in 2D, reset anytime
Focus on what matters
  • Centers (seeds) — focus on several entities and packages at once; each shows as a removable chip
  • Connection depth slider — widen or narrow the neighborhood in real time (client-side, no re-query)
  • Add a package from the Project view — right-click a package to center on it (sub-packages included)
  • Search highlighting — type to fade non-matching nodes; column-hover spotlights an entity's edges
Read the mapping accurately
  • Crow's foot cardinality for @OneToMany, @ManyToOne, @OneToOne, @ManyToMany
  • @Inheritance badges (SINGLE_TABLE / JOINED / TABLE_PER_CLASS) with @DiscriminatorColumn / @DiscriminatorValue
  • Multi-level Spring Data repository inheritance — follows custom intermediate interfaces (MyBaseRepo<T> extends JpaRepository<T,ID>)
  • FK columns on cards for @ManyToOne / owning @OneToOne with @JoinColumn name resolution
  • @Table indexes / uniqueConstraints as column glyphs (◆ unique, # indexed), plus PK / FK / nullable / unique / length / @GeneratedValue / @Column(name)
  • Bidirectional relationships are de-duplicated automatically (drops mappedBy mirror edges)
Get it out of the IDE
  • Export via Tools → JPA 3D: Export… to JSON, DDL (optional snake_case & DROP TABLE), Mermaid, and viewer snapshots (PNG / SVG)
  • Extract single-entity SQL — an icon on the @Entity editor banner dumps that entity's DDL
  • Add to viewer from the editor — center the graph on the entity you're reading without leaving the file
Built to stay out of your way
  • Java & Kotlin via UAST — Kotlin annotation use-site targets handled transparently
  • Background analysis — the cache pre-warms after indexing, with no UI freezes
  • Settings page (Settings → Tools → JPA 3D) — persist viewer, analysis-filter, and export defaults

Getting started
Open your JPA project, let indexing finish, then open the JPA 3D tool window on the right. Hit Sync to analyze, and start exploring. Enjoy!

한국어
JPA 엔티티 모델을 IDE 안에서 3D / 2D ERD 로 시각화하고 탐색하는 플러그인입니다. @Entity 클래스(Java & Kotlin)를 분석해 관계·카디널리티·상속·Spring Data 리포지토리를 그래프로 보여주고, 노드를 클릭하면 소스로 바로 이동합니다.
  • 3D 포스 그래프 / 2D 직교 ERD, 3D 미니맵, 깊이 슬라이더로 원하는 범위만 집중
  • crow's foot 카디널리티, @Inheritance 전략, FK 컬럼, 인덱스/유니크 제약까지 정확히 표현
  • 다단계 Spring Data 리포지토리 상속과 jakarta / 레거시 javax persistence 모두 지원
  • 모델을 JSON / DDL(PostgreSQL · MySQL · H2 · Oracle) / Mermaid / PNG · SVG 로 내보내기
프로젝트 인덱싱 후 우측 JPA 3D 툴윈도우를 열고 동기화하면 됩니다.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.1
  • Fixed edges drifting away from nodes in large module/MSA graphs — in the 2D ERD, within-module edges are now drawn attached to their nodes even when a project has hundreds of entities spread across many modules. Previously their endpoints could float far from the cards as the canvas grew.
1.0.0
  • Architecture-aware views — the analyzer detects whether your project is a monolith, modular monolith or MSA and shows it as a badge, so the graph reflects how your code is actually structured.
  • Module grouping — entities are grouped by module: the 2D ERD wraps each module in a labelled container, and the 3D graph separates modules into distinct spatial clusters. A multi-toggle module filter and boundary legend are included.
  • Cross-module boundaries — edges are classified as within-module, cross-module FK (real relation) or cross-module soft reference (weak ID), each styled distinctly so coupling across boundaries stands out.
  • No UI freeze — analysis now runs fully off the UI thread; opening the viewer no longer blocks the IDE on first load.
0.9.0
  • Columns shown by default — the default detail level is now +columns instead of relationships-only, so entity columns are visible the first time you open the viewer. Existing saved settings are kept; you can switch back via the 표시 control or Settings.
0.6.0
  • Follows the IDE theme — the viewer chrome now tracks the IDE light/dark theme, and the canvas background is transparent so the IDE background shows through behind the graph (nodes, cards and the toolbar stay opaque for readability).
  • Filter & search by class FQN — the analysis filter and search now also match the fully-qualified class name, not just the simple name.
0.5.5
  • Right-click now removes a node from the analysis — instead of just hiding it, distances and the depth filter are recomputed, so neighbors that were only reachable through the removed node disappear with it (cascade). In all scope, only nodes that became orphaned by the removal are pruned — originally independent entities are kept. Undo with Cmd/Ctrl+Z, or restore from the toolbar.
0.5.4
  • Fixed a PluginException when opening Settings — the JPA 3D sub-tabs (Viewer / Analysis / Export / Editor) are now provided as composite children of the parent page instead of separate extension points. The platform no longer logs No display name specified… nor eagerly loads each tab class, while the tab names still follow the plugin language setting.
0.5.3
  • No more UI freezes on large projects — the full-project scan now runs as a cancellable non-blocking read action. Previously it held the read lock for the whole scan, so clicking or typing in the editor mid-analysis could freeze the IDE for several seconds; the scan now yields to those actions and retries.
0.4.1
  • Fixed split navigation crash on 2025.3 / 2026.1 / 2026.2 — the 2×2 grid open (Cmd/Ctrl+click) referenced an EditorWindow.split overload that became binary-incompatible after a new parameter was added; now calls the stable overload directly.
  • Replaced the deprecated SimpleListCellRenderer.create (scheduled for removal in 2026.2) with textListCellRenderer in the Settings combo box.
0.4.0
  • Multiple centers (seeds) — the center scope now accepts several seeds at once, mixing entities and packages freely. Search adds each pick as a removable chip; depth is the shortest hop from any selected seed (union BFS).
  • Add a package from the Project view — right-click a package → JPA 3D: 이 패키지 추가 to open the tool window and add that package (with its sub-packages) as a center.
  • Split navigation — Cmd/Ctrl+click a node to open its source in a 2×2 editor grid, so several entities can be compared side by side.
0.3.2
  • Removed deprecated / scheduled-for-removal platform API usages (addBrowseFolderListener, SimpleListCellRenderer.create, runReadAction) for forward compatibility with current and upcoming IDEs.
  • Minimum supported IDE raised to 2024.3 (build 243).
0.3.1
  • 3D minimap — overview of all nodes projected onto the layer plane with the current view box; click to fly the camera there (keeps zoom).
0.3.0
  • Settings page under Settings → Tools → JPA 3D — persist viewer defaults (view / scope / depth / display options), analysis package include/exclude filters, and Export defaults (DDL dialect / snake_case / DROP TABLE).
  • Connection depth slider — drag to adjust the seed neighborhood depth; filtering is client-side so it responds in real time without re-querying.
0.2.1
  • New plugin icon (DNA double helix).
  • Replaced deprecated ReadAction.compute(ThrowableComputable) usages with Kotlin runReadAction { }.
0.2.0
  • 3D rendering overhauled: entity-card sprites with 3D anchor spheres for real depth perception.
  • 2D ERD: crow's foot cardinality markers; manual node drag with position reset.

idea-plugin.name: Langjector
idea-plugin.description:
View and edit any text selection as if it were written in another language.

Select text in any editor, pick a target language, and Langjector opens it in a dedicated tool window — syntax-highlighted as that language — with live two-way sync:
  • Edits in the tool window are mirrored back into the original selection.
  • Edits to the original region update the highlighted view.
  • Undo applies to both sides as a single step.
Unlike built-in language injection — which only works inside string literals, comments and other injection hosts — Langjector works on any selection in any file.

Usage: select text, then right-click and choose Open Selection as Language….

idea-plugin.name: Kshana - PNT simulator
idea-plugin.description:
Run Kshana — the open, reproducible positioning/navigation/timing (PNT) resilience simulator — directly from your JetBrains IDE.

Right-click any scenario .toml and choose Run Kshana Scenario; the figures of merit and result JSON stream into the Kshana tool window. Set the path to the kshana binary in Settings → Tools → Kshana (install it with cargo install kshana).

Scenarios cover SGP4/SDP4 orbits, IAU reference frames, Allan deviations, GNSS availability/DOP, ARAIM protection levels, GNSS/INS fusion, and quantum-sensor models — each carrying an explicit, machine-checkable verification status (validated against an external oracle, or transparently modelled). See https://kshana.dev.

idea-plugin.name: KStateMachine Visual
idea-plugin.description:
KStateMachine Visual is the IDE plugin for the KStateMachine Kotlin library.

It statically analyzes your Kotlin source — including if / when branches that the runtime PlantUML export cannot see — and shows every state machine in the current file as both a navigable tree and a rendered UML state diagram.

Click any tree node to jump to its declaration; move the editor caret and the tree selection follows. Gutter icons mark every createStateMachine / state / transition call. The diagram updates live as you type, and the PlantUML source can be copied or exported as SVG.

idea-plugin.name: Pretty JSON Logcat
idea-plugin.description:
Pretty JSON Logcat

Stop squinting at one-line JSON blobs in Logcat. This plugin shows your API responses (and any other JSON your app logs) properly indented and syntax-highlighted.

  • Pretty Print JSON — select log lines in the Logcat window, a run console, or any editor, right-click and choose Pretty Print JSON. Logcat metadata prefixes (timestamp, pid, tag, level) are stripped automatically, and payloads that span multiple log lines are reassembled.
  • Pretty Print JSON from Clipboard — copy log lines anywhere and run it from the Tools menu.
  • Pretty Logcat tool window — live-tails adb logcat for a selected device (optionally filtered to one app's process) and pretty-prints every JSON payload it detects, with level colors, a text filter, and a "JSON only" mode.
  • Reduce Drops — one click raises the device log buffer and shields your app from logd's "chatty" pruning, so large payloads survive logcat intact far more often.
  • App captures — for responses too large for logcat to carry intact, add a tiny debug-only OkHttp interceptor (see docs/app-side) and read complete bodies straight from the app's files via adb run-as. No dropped chunks, any size.
  • Collapsible tree viewer — payloads open in a JSON tree (like web JSON viewers): expand objects and arrays node by node, with child counts and colored values, a find bar that searches keys and values across the whole payload, and optional expansion of embedded JSON strings into subtrees. In the tool window, large payloads start collapsed as a one-line summary — click to explore. Save any payload to a file.
  • Filters & settings — filter the stream by text, log level, or JSON-only; tune the collapse threshold, buffer size, capture directory and more in Settings → Tools → Pretty JSON Logcat. Your package, mode and filters are remembered across restarts.

Requires adb (found via ANDROID_HOME, ANDROID_SDK_ROOT, the default SDK location, or PATH) for the tool window; the editor and clipboard actions work everywhere.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.0

  • Expand embedded JSON strings — a string value that is itself JSON (an escaped "{…}", common in API envelopes) now expands as a nested subtree in the viewer. Toggle per-payload, default in Settings.
  • Log-level filter — a Level dropdown (All / Debug / Info / Warn / Error) alongside the text filter and JSON-only mode.
  • Settings page (Settings → Tools → Pretty JSON Logcat) for the collapse threshold, buffer size, capture directory, poll interval, entry cap, and more.
  • Remembers your package, capture mode, JSON-only, and level filter across restarts.
  • Save… a payload to a file from the viewer dialog.
  • Capture mode skips the pre-existing backlog on start, polls at a configurable interval, and the companion interceptor now writes atomically so a half-written file is never read.

1.0.4

  • App captures mode — read complete response bodies straight from the app's files via adb run-as, bypassing logcat entirely. logcat drops chunks of large/bursty payloads (a 260 KB body can never arrive intact); this mode does not. Add the tiny debug-only OkHttp interceptor from docs/app-side to your app, then enter the package, tick App captures, and press Start.
  • Find in the tree viewer — a search bar over the JSON tree matches keys and values across the whole payload (even collapsed branches), expanding and jumping to each hit with a match counter and next/previous. (The Text tab keeps the editor's own Find on Ctrl/⌘+F.)

1.0.3

  • A very large payload that logcat could not deliver intact (lines dropped mid-stream) no longer dumps as a wall of raw text — like big JSON, it now collapses behind an "open in viewer" link, and the surviving prefix is repaired and pretty-printed where possible.
  • On a structural break mid-payload, the accumulator rolls back to the last consistent point and re-scans, so one dropped chunk no longer corrupts the request that follows it.

1.0.2

  • Fixed: the Start button could stay disabled forever if an adb command failed during startup. Errors now always restore the controls and are reported in the status line (details go to idea.log).
  • Tool window toolbar split into two rows so the status text and trailing controls are no longer clipped in narrow windows.
  • pidof fallback for devices without pidof -s.

1.0.1

  • Truncated payloads can no longer disappear: a payload whose remaining chunks never arrive (logcat dropped them) is flushed after 2 seconds, auto-repaired (open strings/brackets closed), pretty-printed, and clearly marked as incomplete.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
  • Pretty Print JSON action for editor/console/Logcat selections.
  • Pretty Print JSON from Clipboard action in the Tools menu.
  • Pretty Logcat tool window: live adb logcat stream with automatic JSON detection, multi-line payload reassembly, filtering, and a JSON-only mode.
  • Collapsible JSON tree viewer (expand node by node); large payloads start collapsed in the stream and open in the viewer on click.
  • App-process filter (logcat --pid), -v long parsing so multi-line messages arrive whole, and a "Reduce Drops" action against logd's chatty pruning.

idea-plugin.name: Animoria
idea-plugin.description:
Animoria — Visual Asset Governance

Workspace-wide discovery, governance, and reference tracing for animated (Lottie, Rive, GIF, APNG, SVG) and static (SVG, PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF) assets, directly inside your IDE sidebar.

Animoria acts as a local-first visual asset memory for developer teams who care about craft and codebase health. It automates the structural audit and reference tracing of visual assets in large repositories to prevent production bundle bloat and technical debt.

Key Features:

  • Asset Governance: Configurable rules identify unreferenced assets, byte-identical duplicates, oversized files, and disallowed formats. Every finding carries the evidence behind it, how confident the check is, and how much of your workspace was actually searched. Static-asset governance is on the roadmap.
  • Usage Traceability: Trace where assets are referenced across Kotlin, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, Swift, Dart, and more, jumping directly to the source file line.
  • Multi-Format Strategy: Seamlessly parses Lottie (.json), dotLottie (.lottie), Rive (.riv), GIF/APNG (.gif/.apng), Animated SVG (.svg), and indexes static SVG/PNG/JPEG/WebP/AVIF files alongside them.
  • Local & Offline-First: Secure, offline processing guarantees code and asset data never leave your local workspace.

idea-plugin.name: LDAP Navigator
idea-plugin.description:
LDAP Navigator brings LDAP directory browsing into your JetBrains IDE, so you can inspect and update directory data without switching to a separate LDAP client.

Use the LDAP Navigator tool window to manage connections, browse directory trees, open entries in editor tabs, search directory content, and work with entry attributes in a schema-aware table.

Features:

  • Manage multiple LDAP, StartTLS, and LDAPS connections with optional base DNs.
  • Browse RootDSE, naming contexts, and LDAP entries in a lazy-loaded tree.
  • Resolve entry icons from object classes and show helpful entry name hints from display attributes.
  • Open entries in editor tabs with schema-aware attribute ordering and highlighting.
  • Inspect text and binary attribute values safely.
  • Edit schema-editable text attribute values inline, then save or cancel pending changes as a batch.
  • View entry attributes as LDIF with full syntax highlighting.
  • Export entries to LDIF files.
  • Open, edit, and syntax-highlight standalone LDIF files.
  • Copy entry DNs from entry details and search results.
  • Search across all connections, the current connection, or the selected branch with live progress feedback.
  • Navigate from search results back to matching LDAP entries.
  • Store bind passwords in the IDE password safe instead of plain project state.
  • Export and import a selectable subset of connections as a JSON file.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Search field no longer gets squeezed when the tool window is narrow; the scope combo shrinks instead

idea-plugin.name: Seen
idea-plugin.description:
Seen keeps track of which files you have already reviewed, right inside your IDE, with no git required.

It adds a checklist to your project tree. Tick a file when you have read it. If that file changes later, the tick clears by itself, so a checkmark always means "I read this exact version". It works like the "Viewed" checkbox in GitHub pull requests, but for any code, not just a pull request.

Use it to:

  • Work through an unfamiliar codebase file by file during onboarding.
  • Review what an AI coding agent changed before you commit.
  • Audit or clean up a project and be sure you missed nothing.
  • Pause a long review and pick it up later. Progress is saved per project.

Open the Seen tool window on the right, tick files as you go, and use "Show Only Unreviewed" to focus on what is left. The tree respects IDE excludes such as build output and dependency folders. Works in IntelliJ IDEA, Android Studio, and other JetBrains IDEs.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.2.11 Compatibility fix: the folder combined-diff no longer references a private IntelliJ Platform (internal) class directly, so the plugin passes Marketplace verification cleanly. No behavior change.

0.2.10 Review hunks straight from the editor gutter:

  • A file you reviewed that has since changed now shows a ✓ check in the editor gutter next to each changed region. Click it to fold just that hunk into your reviewed version - the check disappears and the rest stay pending. Accept every hunk and the file flips to fully reviewed, no need to open the "Show changes" diff.

0.2.9 Review changes hunk by hunk, commit only what you reviewed, and more:

  • In "Show changes", a Mark Hunk(s) Reviewed button folds the change at your caret into the reviewed version - that hunk disappears and the rest stay pending. Select across several changes to fold every hunk in the selection at once. The file flips to fully reviewed once you have accepted every hunk; whole-file Mark Reviewed still works as before.
  • New Changed Files tab in the tool window lists every file that changed since you reviewed it, newest first; double-click to jump straight to its diff.
  • Commit only Seen files: a Check Only Seen Files button in the Commit tool window checks just your reviewed files (and unchecks the rest), so you can commit exactly what you have reviewed.
  • Full right-click menu: right-clicking a file or folder in the Seen tree now offers the same actions as the IDE's Project view (New, Cut/Copy/Paste, Refactor, Find Usages, VCS, Open In, ...), on top of the Seen actions.
  • Open unreviewed files as a diff: double-clicking a file you have never reviewed opens its diff against the git version; if it matches git it just opens.

0.2.6 See what changed at a glance:

  • Change badges: the Seen tree marks each file relative to your review state - A (not seen yet), M (reviewed, then changed), R (reviewed, then moved/renamed).
  • Deleted files in place: a reviewed file that gets deleted now shows struck through at the folder it lived in, with a D tag. You can still mark it seen, and double-click shows what was removed (your reviewed version vs empty).
  • Moves are tracked: moving or renaming a file in the IDE follows the review, and a move done outside the IDE (terminal or an agent) is recovered by matching the new file's content to the deleted one.
  • Folder "seen": the Project view now marks a folder "✓ seen" when every reviewable file under it has been reviewed.

0.2.5 Review straight from the diff:

  • The "changes since reviewed" diff now has a Mark Reviewed button in its toolbar, so you can mark a file reviewed without switching back to the editor.
  • Double-clicking a changed file in the Seen tree opens its diff directly, instead of the plain editor.

0.2.4 Fixes:

  • The "✓ seen" Project view badge now shows for single-class Kotlin/Java files (which appear as a class node), not just plain files.
  • The badge and the reviewed editor-tab color refresh immediately when review state changes, instead of only after the tree is rebuilt.
  • A reviewed file edited outside the IDE keeps its "changed since reviewed" state and its Show changes diff, even when the external tool saves by replacing the file (an atomic save the IDE sees as a delete then recreate). An identical rewrite re-checks itself.

0.2.3 Project overview, ignore files, and reviewing from the editor:

  • Project-overview tree: the tree now mirrors your project's on-disk folders under a single root, instead of one node per source set (main, test, androidTest, ...). Extra attached folders (for example in Rider) still appear as their own roots.
  • Exclude folders: right-click a folder and choose "Exclude Folder from Seen". Exclusions are written to a .seenignore file at the project root that uses .gitignore syntax and is kept separate from .gitignore, so git keeps tracking everything while Seen hides only what you list. Exclude globs and a settings list are still available.
  • Review from the editor: an always-on banner shows "Not reviewed yet" or "changed since reviewed" with a Mark reviewed action, and "Mark Reviewed" is now in the editor, editor-tab and Project view right-click menus.
  • Reliable "show changes": the reviewed content is snapshotted at review time, so diffing what changed since you reviewed no longer depends on IDE Local History.

0.2.2 Editing a file yourself no longer clears its review; only changes that arrive from outside the editor (a git pull, a branch switch, an external edit) do. Tree expansion is now remembered across IDE restarts.

0.2.1 Support for projects with multiple folders / content roots, with git churn and changed-vs-ref scanning every repository. Folders with no reviewable files are hidden, and the tree keeps its expansion when it refreshes.

0.2.0 A big update:

  • Review flow: progress stats with a progress bar and per-folder counts, next/previous unreviewed navigation (buttons + shortcuts), a status bar widget, and "mark all open tabs".
  • See what changed: diff a file against the version you reviewed, a "review queue" that steps through everything changed since review, an editor banner and tab color, and Project view marks.
  • Organize: per-file comment threads (with resolve, shown in a pane below the tree), status tags (needs work / skip), multiple review sessions, search, and sorting by name, recency, size or git churn.
  • Focus: filters for unreviewed, VCS-changed, stale, changed-since-baseline, changed-vs-branch, and by file type; plus an option to hide git-ignored files.
  • Insight & sharing: a Dashboard tab (coverage, lines reviewed, status breakdown, stale and changed lists), Markdown/HTML export and import, an audit log, and a pre-commit gate that warns about unreviewed files.
  • Settings: uncheck-on-every-change, exclude globs, stale threshold, and change notifications.

0.1.0 First release: project tree with per-file reviewed checkmarks, automatic unchecking when a file changes, hash-based revert detection, live updates for added, deleted, moved and renamed files, and per-project persistence.

idea-plugin.name: JavaWiz
idea-plugin.description:
JavaWiz is a visualization plugin for Java programs targeted at programming beginners. Users can step through the program line by line and follow the execution in the visualization panel.

JavaWiz is developed and maintained by the Institute for System Software, Johannes Kepler University Linz, Austria.

Features

JavaWiz provides ten visualization views:

  • Flow charts, visually representing the control flow of the program.
  • A memory visualization. It displays statics, the stack, and the heap, to help understand how program memory works.
  • A "tabular view" displaying the variable changes from line to line, which is useful for understanding simple algorithms.
  • An array visualization showing index expressions, assignments, and the values in each array cell.
  • A Linked List visualization showing nodes, references, and changes during list algorithms.
  • A Binary Tree visualization showing tree structure and changes during tree algorithms.
  • A Java Stream API visualization using dynamic Marble Diagrams to show execution order, transformations, intermediate results, and element lineage through the pipeline.
  • Sequence diagrams, which show how objects relate to each other by depicting the method calls between them.
  • Input buffer visualization. To use this feature, use JavaWiz's In.java class to read input.
  • A History View for browsing calls and assignments across the complete execution trace, filtering or searching them, and jumping to matching program states.

How to use

The plugin requires IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2.1 or newer and at least JDK 25 to run.

Start

After installing JavaWiz and opening a Java file, start it by clicking Debug with JavaWiz above the main method, from the editor context menu, from the Run menu, or from the JavaWiz tool window.

Navigation

An explanation of the user interface can be accessed by clicking the Help button inside JavaWiz.

The arrow buttons in the toolbar navigate through the program; the yellow arrow restarts the program.

It is possible to step back and repeat parts of the program, so there is no need to restart the program to re-inspect previous steps. The current status (live or replay) is displayed in the toolbar.

The visualization tools (heap view, desk test, etc.) can be revealed using the selection buttons on the main view. Tools can be closed with the close button, and some tools can be customized through their settings button.

Further information

The tool is targeted at beginners and is under active development, so not all Java language features may be supported.

Visit javawiz.net for more information.
