idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.9.5 - The trial notices "JSONL Lens Pro trial ends in ..." and "JSONL Lens Pro trial has ended" now end with the price, "Pro is USD 1.90 a month or USD 19 a year for individual use", and a "See pricing" button that opens the marketplace page. During a trial you may see one request for a marketplace review, with "Write a review", "Feedback" and "No thanks". A profile report and the first record of a clean copy showed the plugin version as "unknown"; they show the real one now.

1.9.4 - A .jsonl, .ndjson, .ldjson or .jsonlines file too large for the IDE's text editor now opens on the JSONL Lens tab first, with the IDE's preview beside it. Files the text editor can show still open there first, and it now carries a banner, "Browse this file as records in JSONL Lens.", with "Open in JSONL Lens" to switch tabs and "Don't show again" to hide it. Export and Export Clean Copy on a .jsonl.gz now offer the folder of the original file and a name taken from it, where before they offered a temporary folder the system may clean. With more than a week of a Pro trial left, JSONL Lens now says once when you have used a Pro feature: after a filter query, an export, a full-file stats run or a clean copy, a notice titled "JSONL Lens Pro trial" names it and says what stays free. The trial-ending notices and the footer's trial line count those actions; a Find is free and is not counted. At IDE start the footer shows no Pro line until the IDE has read the license.

1.9.3 - Duplicates now needs the whole file indexed first. Run while a large file was still indexing, it counted only the records indexed so far, and Export Clean Copy wrote only those as a success. Until indexing finishes, the stats dialog leaves the Duplicates button out. Cancelling a "Schema stats" sample no longer brings up an IDE error report. If your data comes as .ldjson.gz or .jsonlines.gz, it now opens the same way as .jsonl.gz, and plain .ldjson or .jsonlines files get the JSONL Lens tab alongside the IDE's editor.

1.9.2 - JSONL Lens now offers "Feedback" between "Write a review" and "No thanks" in its one-time review prompt, as links in one row. "Feedback" opens a feature request form on GitHub titled "Improve JSONL Lens 1.9.2", with your IDE already filled in, and nothing is sent until you submit it there. The thank-you prompt after a purchase now has the same three links.

1.9.1 - The status line, the Pro line and two new links now sit in a footer under the grid, where a narrow editor no longer hides them. "Try Pro free for 30 days" shows on a machine where the trial has not run and opens the IDE license dialog, where the trial starts. Once a trial has run there, the same spot reads "Get Pro" and leads to the pricing page. While Pro is running, bought or on trial, the spot is empty. "Write a review" shows in every state and opens the reviews page of the listing. The toolbar wraps onto a second row instead of hiding its right end. A "Schema stats" run that finds fields now counts toward the one-time review prompt. The trial notices and the review prompt now wait until the IDE has finished reading the license, so a licensed machine is never told at startup that its trial has ended.

1.9.0 - The Pro trial notices now end with a question and the support address. A key issued for another plugin no longer opens JSONL Lens Pro. A key for JSONL Lens itself is unaffected.

1.8.0 - The stats dialog gains a Duplicates action, free on both tiers. It walks every record once and says how many repeat an earlier record exactly: two records are the same record when they hold the same values with their keys in any order and any whitespace, while a number keeps its text, so 1 and 1.0 stay two records. The first occurrence is kept; a truncated record is skipped and counted, and one that could not be parsed is counted too and kept, uncompared. When repeats were found, the Duplicate Records dialog offers Export Clean Copy, a Pro action: it writes the survivors to a new .jsonl, each line as read, after a header record on line 1 that names the operation, and lists the removed records in a .removed.jsonl file beside it, each with its position, its byte offset and the record it repeats. The open file is never written, and a cancel leaves neither file. The Export Records dialog now also takes a .profile.html, .profile.md or .profile.json name and writes a column profile of the selected records instead of the records: for every field the sample shows (up to 256), the count, the nulls and the type mix, then the min, max, mean, quartiles and histogram of a number field, the lengths, distinct count and top values of a text field, the trues and falses of a boolean field; the duplicate-record count heads the report and the correlations between number fields end it. The HTML report is self-contained, and the Markdown and JSON reports carry the same measures; the balloon at the end offers Open report. A grid cell whose text is an http or https address opens in the browser on a double-click, and its context menu offers Copy value and Open link; in the Pretty and Raw panes a Ctrl-click (Cmd on a Mac) on an address opens it. The address goes straight to the browser and the plugin fetches nothing. A Pro trial that is about to end now says so a week before the end and again on its last day, and each notice names what Pro adds, with a See pricing action that opens the marketplace pricing tab. A large record is also read and parsed with less memory than before.

1.7.0 - Export to Parquet, a Pro action. Pick a .parquet name in the Export Records dialog, where the filter now lists Parquet beside JSONL and CSV, and the current page or the matches of a search or a filter are written as one Parquet file. The columns are the dot paths a sample of the file shows, in the order the grid uses, up to 256 of them. Each column takes its type from the values the exported records hold: whole numbers become int64, any other number double, strings text, true and false a boolean column. A nested object or array is written as the JSON text of itself in a JSON column. Where the records disagree on the kind the column is text, and a field a record does not have is null. Records the reader cut short and records that do not parse are left out and counted on the status line, the same rule the CSV export follows. The open file is refused as a destination, as it is for CSV and JSONL. A cancelled export leaves no file behind, not even the scratch file the writer keeps beside the destination while it works. When the export finishes, the balloon offers Open exported file, and the file lands in Parquet Lens when that is installed; when nothing installed opens Parquet files, the click says so instead and offers the Parquet Lens page. The plugin download is larger than before, because the Parquet writer now ships inside it. The Theme picker ends with two locked entries now: lamplighter, whose line in the open list reads "unlocks when you share Lens with a colleague", and catacombs, whose line reads "unlocks the first time Pro runs for you". Pick a locked one and the plugin opens the way to earn it. For lamplighter that is the share card, also under Help as Share JSONL Lens: plain text for a colleague with the marketplace page, the family page beside it and a referral code of this install's own, under the line "enter it under Theme in any Lens plugin". Copy share card earns the theme here, and a colleague who picks lamplighter in their own Theme picker, types that code into the share card and presses Unlock with code earns it there. Catacombs opens the first time Pro runs for you, and a trial counts. An earned theme stays whatever the license says. Four night themes join the picker, Duskhollow, Abyss, Obsidian and Moonlit Garden; trying one is free for the open window and keeping it is Pro, like the eight.

1.6.0 - The encoding sniffer now recognizes Polish files written in Windows-1250, ISO-8859-2 or CP852, and the Encoding menu lists all three so a file can be switched by hand. A blocked gzip file, the kind bgzip writes, opens in place: the reader seeks into the file's blocks and inflates them where they lie, so such a .jsonl.gz opens with no temp copy, and the status line says so ("Read in place" with the block count, then "no temp copy"). An ordinary .jsonl.gz still decompresses to a temporary file the way it did, pre-flight refusal included. Reload walks a blocked file again before it re-indexes, so blocks appended since the tab opened come into view, and a file rewritten in the meantime as ordinary gzip is refused by name ("is no longer blocked gzip, so it cannot be read in place. Close the tab and open it again.") rather than read through a map that no longer describes it. The decompression note states a floor only when the file on disk does not already beat it, and an empty .jsonl.gz is refused as "Not a gzip file: the file ends before a gzip header" instead of "Not a gzip file: null".

1.5.1 - A Pro trial started from your JetBrains account no longer stays unlocked after its 30 days. The plugin used to check only the key's signature, which stays valid, so a lapsed trial kept Pro open and was even taken for a purchase: the trial-ended notice never showed, and the thank-you could go to someone who had not bought. The trial's end date is now read from the key itself. Paid keys and perpetual fallback licenses work exactly as before. A .jsonl.gz is now asked how big it will get before it is decompressed. A file that cannot fit in temp space is refused up front, with both numbers named, instead of failing after minutes of work, and the note under the file says the size while it runs. A bgzip file gives an exact size; for any other gzip file the number is a floor and the note says so. The schema stats table and the record pane say why they are empty instead of showing a blank grid or a blank pane.

1.5.0 - Find in file now takes regular expressions. Tick the .* box next to Aa and the Find field tests its pattern against each record on its own, so ^ and $ mean the start and end of a record, and hits highlight in the Raw tab as before. A pattern that backtracks too far on a record is skipped and the match line says how many were, and one that keeps doing it stops the search with a message instead of stalling the viewer. Free, like the rest of Find.

1.4.4 - A JSON string escape written as backslash u followed by a sign used to be accepted and decoded as if the sign were a hex digit. It is rejected now, like every other malformed escape. String values in filter queries get the same fix.

1.4.3 - The one-time review ask now waits for five moments of use (a file opened, indexed and shown as a grid, a search with hits, an export) instead of three, so it comes after real work rather than right after the first open. The trial tally that leads the trial notices moved into the shared Lens platform, so every Lens plugin names what Pro did during its trial in the same words. Nothing else changes.

1.4.2 - A Pro trial that is about to end says so once, with a link to pricing, and a trial that has ended says so once. Pro gate messages and the listing now say what is true: each Lens plugin has its own free 30-day trial.

1.4.1 - Themes: an untinted cell no longer inherits the previous cell's tint, and switching back to Default clears every tint at once; the renderer now states both colors on every cell. A kept theme comes back only while the license holds, so a lapsed trial opens on Default. Export refuses the open file as its destination and asks for another name.

1.4.0 - Themes: pick a look for the whole tab from the toolbar. Eight strands shared across the Lens family (default, hacker, cyberpunk, goblincore, neon, nosferatu, halloween, blue lagoon) restyle the record table: record numbers and JSON numbers take the number tint, strings and booleans the text tint, nested arrays and objects the structure tint, with row striping and the selection color from the strand; the default look is unchanged and null values take no tint in any strand. Any strand tastes free for the open window, and keeping one set is Pro.

1.3.2 - Grid fixes: the selected record survives a switch between Grid and Preview, and Reload keeps the grid instead of dropping it. When a sample has no fields to show, the Grid box unchecks itself and the status line says why; the one-time review ask now counts a search or an export too, not only opened files.

1.3.1 - No more clipped toolbar buttons: nav, search and filter rows wrap to a second line when the panel gets narrow. A few titles and tooltips traded long dashes for plainer punctuation.

1.3.0 - The encoding release. A .jsonl file in EUC-KR / CP949 or Shift_JIS / CP932 is detected on open and rendered correctly, and an Encoding selector on the search row overrides the guess when it has to - display and search both work in the file's own encoding, on files of any size. Subscribers get a one-time thank-you the first time the plugin sees its license, then a quiet Supporter-since line in the footer from that day on - stored locally, and still no network calls. The free tier stays free.

1.2.1 - The plugin name now says both of the format's names, JSON Lines and NDJSON, so the viewer is easier to find in search. Nothing else changes.

1.2.0 - Find in file gets two upgrades: a Matches only checkbox that pages through just the matching records, and search-term highlighting in the Raw tab. Both free, like the rest of search. The Help menu gains a Report a JSONL Lens Problem action that opens a pre-filled issue on the family tracker - you see the whole text before anything is sent, and the plugin still makes no network calls. The panel footer now names what Pro adds, or how many trial days are left, and the plugin asks exactly once for a review after the third fully indexed file.

1.1.0 - Maintenance release. Cleans up the two deprecated platform API calls flagged by the Marketplace verifier; where a newer IDE provides the current save and registration APIs, those are used instead. No feature changes. Everything free stays free.

1.0.0 - Out of early access. Everything that was free stays free; adds an optional Pro tier: whole-file filter queries, export to .jsonl/CSV, and exact full-file schema stats.

idea-plugin.name: Markdown Pro
idea-plugin.description:
Markdown Pro turns your JetBrains IDE into a complete documentation and knowledge-base authoring workspace. It builds on the familiar bundled Markdown editor with rich editing tools, Obsidian-compatible vault graphs, framework-aware MDX, accurate previews, documentation-project intelligence, and focused quality checks.

August 2026 launch offer: Markdown Pro is 50% off through August 31, 2026. Regular pricing begins September 1, 2026.

Write and edit faster

  • See bold and italic styling directly in the source editor while keeping every Markdown marker visible.
  • Format selections from a floating toolbar and toggle task-list checkboxes with a click or keyboard shortcut.
  • Keep ordered lists correctly numbered after inserting, deleting, duplicating, or moving items—even in nested lists.
  • Edit tables in place with controls to add, remove, move, and format rows and columns while preserving alignment and escaped pipes.
  • Use Markdown-specific live templates for tables, tasks, and note callouts without suggestions leaking into other file types, front matter, or fenced code.

Preview the Markdown you actually write

  • Choose GitHub Flavored Markdown, Markdown Extra, CommonMark, or Standard Markdown at project level.
  • Keep source and preview together with smooth bidirectional, editor-led, or preview-led scroll synchronization.
  • Preview updates happen in place, preserving the reading position without reloading or flickering as you type.
  • Resize preview text with Cmd/Ctrl +, Cmd/Ctrl −, and Cmd/Ctrl 0, or use Tools | Markdown Pro | Preview Size. Set the default font size, choose whole-page scaling, and remember sizes per tab, project, or file in Settings | Tools | Markdown Pro. Shortcuts work when the preview has focus and can be changed in the IDE Keymap.
  • Copy rendered selections as rich text, HTML, RTF, or plain text for Teams and other rich editors, or retain the browser's default copy behavior.
  • GitHub Flavored Markdown renders task lists, syntax-highlighted code, math, Mermaid diagrams, collapsible sections, GeoJSON and TopoJSON maps, and interactive STL models.
  • Local images, relative links, dark themes, and visited links render clearly and consistently.

First-class MDX support

  • Open .mdx files as Markdown with JSX-style highlighting for component names, attributes, values, and expressions, plus folding for multiline components.
  • In WebStorm and IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate, Markdown Pro detects the documentation framework, starts its development server transparently, and previews the real site route inside the IDE—so imported React components render as components.
  • Live MDX previews can synchronize while you type, use a configurable canvas color for transparent themes, and reconnect automatically when a site is starting.
  • IDE editions without JavaScript framework support receive a safe Markdown-style fallback preview.

Understand the whole documentation site

  • Auto-detect MkDocs, Docusaurus, Fumadocs, VitePress, Hugo, and Jekyll projects, or select a profile explicitly.
  • Resolve site-root routes, relative links, navigation and sidebar files, front-matter slugs and permalinks, and aliases across Markdown and MDX.
  • Find orphan pages and unresolved documentation routes before readers do.

Explore Obsidian vaults

  • Auto-detect folders containing .obsidian, or select the Obsidian profile and vault root explicitly.
  • Navigate and complete [[wikilinks]], aliases, heading links, block links, embeds, tags, and common Obsidian properties directly in Markdown.
  • Preview highlights, comments, callouts, note transclusions, and local image, audio, video, PDF, SVG, and Canvas embeds.
  • Explore a typed global or local vault graph with search, depth and visibility controls, incoming/outgoing counts, and distinct links for citations, embeds, tags, and Canvas references.
  • Open .canvas files as zoomable, read-only visual boards while retaining the editable raw JSON source, and create missing notes by selecting unresolved graph nodes.

Ship cleaner documentation

  • Get PSI-based inspections and quick fixes for titles, heading order, duplicate anchors, image descriptions, empty links, list consistency, unmatched formatting, spacing, front matter, code fences, trailing whitespace, final newlines, unresolved routes, and orphan pages.
  • Convert Markdown to and from AsciiDoc, reStructuredText, Typst, LaTeX, Djot, Org mode, Textile, HTML, and DocBook with Morph, including managed download and update, version detection, and diff review before overwriting files.
  • Turn JSON objects, JSON arrays, CSV rows, or folders of JSON files into Markdown with Knap, using a local playground, record-by-record previews, filename templates, and collision-safe batch generation.

Everything is configurable per project under Settings | Tools | Markdown Pro. Editor and preview options are on the main page; expand Markdown Pro for Documentation and MDX, Obsidian, Document Conversion, and Knap Templates.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Adjustable preview font size with configurable increase, decrease, and reset shortcuts, a temporary size indicator, and a Preview Size menu under Tools | Markdown Pro. Choose text-only or whole-page scaling and temporary per-tab, project-wide, or remembered per-file sizes across Markdown and MDX previews.

Changed

  • Markdown Pro settings now keep editor and preview options on the main page, with child pages for Documentation and MDX, Obsidian, Document Conversion, and Knap Templates.

Fixed

  • Markdown and fallback MDX scroll synchronization follows source blocks and keeps the current section aligned when resizing the preview.
  • Selecting Markdown text now shows only the full formatting toolbar, and Toggle Task Item has a task-list icon in light and dark themes.

idea-plugin.name: EML Editor
idea-plugin.description:
View and edit EML (RFC 822/MIME email) files.
  • Rendered, sanitized HTML preview (remote content blocked by default)
  • Editable projections of the HTML and plain-text parts, spliced back into the message
  • Structured headers view: addressing, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, Received hop chain
  • Attachment list with save and open actions

idea-plugin.name: DBML Canvas
idea-plugin.description:
Render DBML files as draggable ER diagrams and store layout data beside the DBML file.

*Performance Tip
For smoother diagram interactions, JetBrains IDE users can optionally run JCEF in-process.

Open:
Help → Edit Custom VM Options

Add:
-Dide.browser.jcef.out-of-process.enabled=false

Then completely exit and restart the IDE.

⚠️ This is a global JetBrains JCEF setting and is not specific to DBML Canvas. It may affect other JCEF-based features or plugins and can cause compatibility or rendering issues on some IDE versions. If you experience any problems, remove the option and restart the IDE.

idea-plugin.name: Log Lens: Large & Structured Log Viewer (JSONL, logfmt, ANSI)
idea-plugin.description:
Most log viewers freeze on a multi-gigabyte production log. Log Lens is a log viewer built for exactly that log file: lines are indexed by byte offset in the background and read on demand, so the log opens instantly and is never loaded whole. It treats a small log file and a multi-gigabyte one alike: the rest of the index fills in while you read.

The viewer is free and stays free. Pro is a subscription for this plugin: USD 2.90 a month or USD 29 a year for individual use. For organizations it is, per user, USD 5.80 a month or USD 58 a year.

The log file every service leaves behind opens in an IDE tab, and Pro writes the page or the matches back out as a Parquet table. On-call and SRE engineers reading a production log get to the lines they need without waiting for the file to load.

Every .log / .log.N / .log.gz file, and the .out and .err files that servers and cron jobs write, gets a Log Lens tab alongside the regular editor in IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm and every IntelliJ-based IDE from 2024.2 on; your file is not taken over and not made read-only. We run each release on five IDE builds first, 2024.2 and 2024.3 Community, 2025.3 and 2026.2 Ultimate, and the 2026.3 preview; the descriptor leaves untilBuild open, so an IDE upgrade keeps Log Lens loading.

The free tier is permanent.

Free - the full viewer, for logs of any size:

  • Any size: streaming line index, instant first screen, browse while indexing runs
  • Log levels: automatic ERROR/WARN/INFO/DEBUG/TRACE detection, colors, filter chips with exact whole-file counts
  • Format auto-detection: JSON lines, logfmt and plain text, with nothing to configure
  • ANSI colors: the ANSI escape codes in a container or CI log show up as colors and bold, never as garbage
  • Follow mode: tail the log file as it grows, rotation-safe
  • Jump to source: stack-trace lines link straight into your project
  • Find in file: full-text search at engine speed, next/previous jump
  • Compressed logs: .log.gz opens transparently

Selecting a long line puts the whole of it in the detail pane, wrapped to the width you have. Free features never consult the license at all; a Pro button checks at the click and, with no license present, opens the IDE's own plugin license dialog. The plugin claims .log, .out and .err names (rotated .log.N and the .gz forms included) and nothing else, so a .txt file stays where it was.

Pro - optional paid tier, for hunting in the log:

  • Filtered follow: tail only the errors, or only the lines matching your query, live
  • Filter queries: keep only lines matching level, field, time and text predicates, scanned across the whole file, then browse just the matches
  • Export: write the current page, search matches, query matches or the filtered view to a new .log, .jsonl, CSV or Parquet file; in the Parquet file the parsed fields become typed columns and the raw line rides along
  • Log statistics: build a per-level time histogram over the whole file in sixty equal time buckets, with a span and rate summary, so you can see when the errors clustered

A year of continuous subscription earns JetBrains' perpetual fallback license: the version available when that year started stays yours for good, including its fixes. Each Lens plugin comes with its own free 30-day Pro trial.

Part of the Lens family - viewers built on one engine, designed to hand off to each other. A Pro export writes the structured records out of a log, and the result opens in JSONL Lens as a browsable, searchable grid. Export as Parquet from Pro and, when Parquet Lens is installed, one click on the finished-export balloon opens the file there. Parquet Lens reads Parquet, Arrow and Feather the same way.

The guides and the overview of all eight viewers are at twilightventures.dev. Write to support@twilightventures.dev about anything to do with the plugin or a purchase, suggestions included; for a bug, name the version and the rough size of the file, or use the issue reporter at the end of the Help menu, which opens a prefilled new issue in your browser for you to read before you post.

Runs entirely locally: the plugin makes no network calls and handles no credentials, and Pro license state is read from the IDE's own licensing system.

What it does not do:

  • No editing by design: we never modify, truncate, or rotate your log.
  • Local files only: no ssh tailing, no aggregation, no shipping.
  • No alerting: the Pro filtered follow shows matching lines live, it does not notify or page.
  • Text formats only: JSON lines, logfmt, and plain text; binary formats are not parsed.

If Log Lens helps you, a short review tells us what to work on next.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.9.7 - A .log, .out or .err file too large for the IDE's text editor, rotated logs included, now opens on the Log Lens tab first, with the IDE's preview beside it. A gzipped log now opens on the Log Lens tab first at any size. Files the text editor can show still open there first, and it now carries a banner, "Browse this file in Log Lens.", with "Open in Log Lens" to switch tabs and "Don't show again" to hide it for good.

1.9.6 -The trial notices "Log Lens Pro trial ends in ..." and "Log Lens Pro trial has ended" now end with the price, "Pro is USD 2.90 a month or USD 29 a year for individual use", and a "See pricing" button that opens the marketplace page. A followed file with a filter query on it stops filtering new lines when the trial ends, as the 1.9.0 note said it would; until now the query kept running on the open tab. During a trial you may see one request for a marketplace review, with "Write a review", "Feedback" and "No thanks".

1.9.5 -With more than a week of a Pro trial left, Log Lens now says once when you have used a Pro feature. After a filtered follow, a whole-file filter query, an export or Log Statistics, a notice titled "Log Lens Pro trial" names it ("That filter query was Pro."). It gives the days the trial has left and says what stays free ("Level filters and Find stay free."). The notices as the trial ends now lead with a count of those actions ("This trial: ..."), and a Find, which is free, no longer counts. The "Pro trial" line in the footer adds how many Pro actions the trial has run. At IDE start the footer shows no Pro line and no trial link until the IDE has read the license, so a buyer or a running trial is no longer offered Pro while it loads. Rotated logs from .log.10 to .log.99, and the .gz form of each, now get the "Log Lens Log" file type and icon, which stopped at .log.9 before; the Log Lens tab already opened them.

1.9.4 - Log Lens now opens .out and .err files and gzipped rotated logs, and the "Log Lens Log" file type and icon cover .log, .out and .err, the rotated .log.1 to .log.9 and the .gz form of each, while a binary such as a.out gets no Log Lens tab. Files saved in an older code page (Western European, Hungarian, Turkish, Cyrillic, Chinese GBK or GB18030, Japanese EUC-JP) open readable, and the "Encoding" list offers each one. A stamp with a comma before the milliseconds, or an offset without a colon, keeps its time of day in "Log Statistics". The stray B some colored output left behind is gone. File errors say what went wrong (the file was not found, permission denied), cancelling a .gz says "Decompression cancelled", a log the IDE cannot read says "Cannot open" and why in its tab, and a .log.gz keeps its own name in titles and the Export dialog.

1.9.3 - Log Lens now keeps the text color and bold of an ANSI-colored line in the "Pretty" tab when the line also sets a 256-color or truecolor background or underline color. The extra numbers in those codes used to be read as styles of their own, so the style could reset partway through the line or the text could change color. The one-time review prompt and the thank-you prompt after a purchase now offer "Feedback" between "Write a review" and "No thanks".

1.9.2 - At a narrow editor the paging, level, find and query rows now wrap onto more rows instead of hiding their right end. The status line, the Pro line and the "Marketplace page", "Try Pro free for 30 days" and "Write a review" links now sit in a footer at the bottom of the view, where the project pane no longer hides them. When the editor is narrow, the Pro line and the links move below the status line, and a status line longer than the row shows its whole text as a tooltip. The trial notices and the review prompt now wait until the IDE has finished reading the license, so a licensed machine is never told at startup that its trial has ended, and a thank-you prompt no longer follows a trial notice in the same sitting.

1.9.1 - Two links now sit in the Log Lens footer. "Try Pro free for 30 days" shows on a machine where the trial has not run and opens the IDE license dialog, where the trial starts. Once a trial has run there, the same spot reads "Get Pro" and leads to the pricing page. While Pro is running, bought or on trial, the spot is empty. "Write a review" shows in every state and opens the reviews page of the listing. A Parquet export now carries the parsed stamp beside the text one. The new $time_utc column holds a timestamp on every line whose stamp the plugin can read, so those lines sort and range as time, and the CSV columns are unchanged.

1.9.0 - Follow with a filter now stops when the license lapses mid-session. The Pro trial notices now end with a question and the support address. A key issued for another plugin no longer opens Log Lens Pro. A key for Log Lens itself is unaffected. After a purchase, a balloon says thank you once on this machine. Its one action is "Write a review".

1.8.0 - Log levels are read from more shapes of line. A logcat prefix such as W/System.err: is a warning before the words after it are looked at. The threadtime and time forms that logcat prints classify by their level letter. A numeric level from pino or bunyan reads its own ladder, so level=30 is info and 50 is error. The ECS log object with a level inside it is read, and a level= pair inside a plain line counts the way a level word would. A blocked-gzip .log.gz, the kind bgzip and the log shippers built on it write, opens in place with no temp copy. The note under the file says it was read in place and gives the block count. Reload picks up blocks appended since the open, and Follow now catches the blocks a shipper keeps appending instead of waiting on Reload. An http or https address in a log line opens in the browser: Ctrl-click it in the message column or the detail pane (Cmd on a Mac), or pick Open link from the line's right-click menu. The address is handed to the browser and nothing is fetched. Lines made of one long dotted token no longer stall the detail pane while their source links are looked for. A Pro trial gets a notice a week before it ends and again on its last day. Each notice names what Pro adds and offers a See pricing action that opens the marketplace pricing tab. A level filter that narrowed the file and a follow that showed new lines now count toward the one-time review ask.

1.7.0 - Export to Parquet, a Pro action. Pick a .parquet name in the Export Lines dialog, whose filter reads Log, JSONL, CSV or Parquet, and the current page, the filtered view, the search matches or the query matches are written as one Parquet file. The columns are the ones the CSV export has, $level, $time and $message first and then one column per parsed field in the order the fields first appear, and a $raw column at the end holds each line exactly as it was read, so nothing the parser did not understand is lost. Each field column takes its type from its values: a number written as an integer becomes int64, any other number double, true and false booleans, text stays text, a nested object or array is written as JSON text, a line without the field leaves a null, and a field that mixes kinds is written as text. $time is text in this cut. The open file is refused as a destination, "That is the open file. Pick another name.", as it is for every export, and a cancelled export leaves no file behind, not even the scratch file the writer keeps beside the destination while it works. When the export finishes, the balloon offers Open exported file, and the file lands in Parquet Lens when that is installed. The Theme picker has two more entries at the end, lamplighter and catacombs, each with a padlock and its own line in the open list, "unlocks when you share Lens with a colleague" and "unlocks the first time Pro runs for you". Pick a locked one and the plugin opens the way to earn it. For lamplighter that is the share card, also under Help as Share Log Lens: the marketplace page, the family page and a referral code of this install's own. Copy share card earns the theme here; a colleague who types the code into their own share card, reached by picking lamplighter in the Theme picker, and presses Unlock with code earns it on their side. Catacombs opens the first time Pro runs for you, a trial included. An earned theme stays whatever the license says. Four night themes join the picker, Duskhollow, Abyss, Obsidian and Moonlit Garden; trying one is free for the open window and keeping it is Pro, like the eight.

1.6.0 - Polish logs in Windows-1250, ISO-8859-2 or CP852 open with their letters intact, and the Encoding menu lists each of them. Opening a compressed log now says what the wait will cost: a .log.gz is decompressed to a temporary file before its first line can show, and the note under the file reads "Decompressing" with the file name and the temp space it needs, and "to at least" that space when the gzip container can only prove a floor. That floor is stated only when it stands at or above the compressed size, since a smaller one reads as nonsense, and an exact size is always stated. The footer of a one-line file now says "1 line", and a single search hit reads "1 / 1 matching line".

1.5.1 - A trial key now unlocks Pro only through the trial's last day. Through the JetBrains account flow a trial arrives as a signed license key carrying "trial": true and the end date in paidUpTo; Log Lens verified the signature and nothing else, so the key kept Pro open after the trial ran out. The lapsed key also looked like a paid license from the inside, which is why the "Log Lens Pro trial has ended" notice never showed while the "Log Lens Pro is active" thank-you went to someone who had not paid. Paid keys and the perpetual fallback licenses read as before, and the offline trial, the kind without an account, was never affected: its stamp carries its own expiry. Export gains the narrowed view. With the level chips set to ERROR, Export used to offer the current page alone, one page a save; the menu now adds "Filtered view (12,408 lines)", the whole narrowed set, and skips it when the page or the query matches already hold exactly those lines. Opening app.log.3.gz reads the gzip container before any temp file is written. If the temp directory cannot hold the decompressed size, the open is refused at once with "Not enough temp space: this file expands to at least 8.20 GB" and the free-space figure. Before, the same file failed only after the whole decompression had run.

1.5.0 - Plain log lines with a dotted day-first date, 04.09.2026 15:42:01, now carry their time, and so do year-first dates written 2026.09.04 or 2026/09/04 and Apache access log stamps like [10/Oct/2026:13:55:36 -0700]. The time shows in the detail pane, a filter query can match it through $time, and the Pro time histogram places those lines on the same clock as ISO ones, with the Apache offset applied, so the statistics cover such a file instead of reporting it as unstamped. An all-numeric slashed date like 04/09/2026 stays unstamped on purpose, since nothing in the line says which number is the day.

1.4.3 - Both trial notices, the one that a Pro trial is about to end and the one that it has ended, now open with the trial's own record: how many exports wrote lines and how many searches found matches while it ran. Nothing from outside the trial is counted. The single review ask waits for five useful moments now instead of three.

1.4.2 - A Pro trial that is about to end says so once, with a link to pricing, and a trial that has ended says so once. Pro gate messages and the listing now say what is true: each Lens plugin has its own free 30-day trial.

1.4.1 - The muster book. Choosing a color theme now leaves a mark: a small muster book joins the viewer for those who have ever picked a lens, holding a few pages that are earned rather than shown, one closed door per lens chosen, and a bundled sample - a Korean household register stored in EUC-KR, read the way 1.3.0 taught the viewer to read. A few quiet things for those who choose a lens. Also new and free on every theme: Compare for rotation families - open a log that has siblings like app.log.1, click Compare, and read the strata side by side, with a streaming first-divergence summary instead when a file is too large for the diff viewer. On the default theme the muster book does not exist at all: nothing extra to find, exactly the advertised tool. The free tier stays free.

1.3.1 - Two of the dark trace colors, Cyberpunk and Goblincore, sat below the readability floor; both are brighter now, and a contrast check keeps every look legible from here on. A few interface messages also traded their long dashes for plainer punctuation.

1.3.0 - The encoding release. Log files in EUC-KR / CP949 and Shift_JIS / CP932 are detected on open and render correctly, with an Encoding selector in the toolbar for manual override - display and search both honor the chosen charset, so legacy Korean and Japanese logs finally read like they should. A new Theme selector restyles level and ANSI colors with five looks: Default, Hacker, Cyberpunk, Goblincore, and Blue - Default keeps exactly the colors you already know. Subscribers now get a one-time thank-you the first time the plugin sees its license, and a quiet Supporter-since line in the footer from then on. The free tier stays free.

1.2.0 - The review groundwork release. Report a Log Lens Problem now sits in the Help menu and opens a pre-filled issue on the family tracker - you see the whole text before anything is sent, and the plugin still makes no network calls. The panel footer names what Pro adds, or how many trial days are left, and the plugin asks exactly once for a review after the third fully indexed file. ANSI colors render in the viewer, match counts show for every search, and .log.gz opens directly. Levels, follow mode, and the whole free tier stay free.

1.1.0 - *.log files now have a real file type registration with an icon in Settings | File Types; the editor provider and .log.N / .log.gz handling are unchanged, and the plain text editor stays available. After a .jsonl export, a notification offers to open the result in JSONL Lens when it is installed; when it is not installed, a one-time suggestion points to it.

1.0.0 - Out of early access. Everything that was free stays free, plus new free follow mode (rotation-safe tail) and jump-to-source from stack-trace lines. Adds an optional Pro tier: filtered follow, whole-file filter queries, export to .log/.jsonl/CSV, and per-level time histograms.

idea-plugin.name: Docker Compose Visualizer
idea-plugin.description:
See how your Docker Compose setup fits together at a glance. Open a Compose file and Docker Compose Visualizer draws it as a diagram: every service is a card, arranged so you can see what depends on what and which services share a network.

Spot problems as you type: The plugin flags issues on the diagram and in the editor, such as a service waiting for something that does not exist, two services using the same port, or a setting with an invalid value.

Make sense of several files: Using more than one Compose file? Switch to the combined view to see what your setup really looks like once they are put together, and which file each setting comes from.

What is free, what needs a license

What you get    Free       Licensed   
Your services as a diagram, ordered by what depends on what ✓ ✓
All networks, volumes, and secrets in one place, with unused ones flagged ✓ ✓
Warnings about problems, on the diagram and in your file ✓ ✓
Combined view of several Compose files, showing which file each setting comes from ✓ ✓
Edit a service from the side panel ✓
Edit settings in the combined view (changes are saved to the right file) ✓
Add, connect, and delete services, networks, volumes, and secrets ✓
One-click fixes for common problems ✓
Start a new Compose file from File > New ✓
Edit the less common settings ✓
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2.0.0

Features

  • New dependency diagram: services are arranged in columns by what depends on what, grouped by the networks they share. Choose Compact or Full cards.
  • Edit in a side panel: no more pop-up windows. With a license, edit in a resizable, collapsible panel next to the diagram, with Save and Revert.
  • Safer rename and delete: in the combined view, renaming or deleting a service updates every reference across your Compose files, after asking you to confirm what will change. With a single file open, you are warned if another Compose file still uses the service.
  • Protected services: a service that other services inherit settings from can't be deleted, and the message names them.
  • Warnings in your file: problems are underlined where they are. Switch them off in Settings > Editor > Inspections. With a license, Alt+Enter offers one-click fixes.
  • Clearer file labels: in the combined view, a label shows only when a setting comes from, or is saved to, a different file than the one you have open.

Fixes

  • Renaming a service no longer breaks files that use four-space indentation.
  • Deleting the last service now leaves a valid file.
  • Renaming a service now also updates services that inherit settings from it, even in another file.
  • Settings you add to a service that inherits from one in a later file are saved where they take effect.
  • Port settings written with a default value are read correctly.

1.2.0

Features

  • Effective Config now shows which file supplied each resolved value: a coloured chip on every dialog field, a file-grouped tooltip on every card, and a "was ... in file" note for what a replaced value used to be - down to each leaf of a nested value like deploy.resources.limits
  • A change made from Effective Config is written to exactly the file that decides it - an existing value saves where it is already defined, a new one goes to the file you have open
  • Reworked edit dialog: General/Environment/Mounts/Connections/Runtime tabs, locked rows showing what another file already supplies, thin scrollbars throughout

Fixes

  • Removing a network or volume that only existed through a YAML anchor (<<: *anchor) now works, instead of silently doing nothing
  • A relationship Docker adds on its own (from links:, network_mode:, volumes_from:, or an interpolated volume name) now shows as locked with an explanation, instead of a checkbox that looked editable but wasn't
  • Several dialog save bugs: an unedited healthcheck test being overwritten with a placeholder, a numeric-looking value written unquoted (which Docker rejects), editing a mount's target or mode could delete or duplicate it, removing a service's last remaining property could leave an invalid empty block
  • Every validation problem is now listed at once, naming its tab and field, instead of stopping at the first one

1.1.1

  • Document update

1.1.0

Features

  • Effective Config view: the merged result of a project's compose files, as the real docker compose config resolves it, with the file that defines each service or resource shown on it
  • Understands include:, override files, profiles, and a COMPOSE_FILE in .env (monorepos, non-standard file names)
  • Edits made while viewing the merged result are written to the file that actually defines the value
  • New warnings: unrecognized restart: policy, a service_healthy dependency on a service with no healthcheck, unknown volume mount mode, a secret/config whose file: source doesn't exist, and a .env whose COMPOSE_FILE can't be parsed

Fixes

  • Profile filtering no longer hides an unrelated network/volume/config/secret that shares a name with a service

1.0.0

Features

  • Freemium: the Architecture canvas, resource summary, and validation warnings are free to view
  • Editing (service dialog, add/attach/detach/delete, scaffolding a new compose file) requires a license

0.1.0

Features

  • Initial release: Architecture canvas with dependency-ordered service cards, tabbed service edit dialog, resource (network/volume/config/secret) summary with unused-resource warnings, and PSI-based editing that preserves YAML formatting

idea-plugin.name: ZPL
idea-plugin.description:
Syntax highlighting and a live, side-by-side rendered preview for Zebra Programming Language (ZPL) label templates — similar to the Markdown split editor.
  • .zpl file type with syntax highlighting for command mnemonics, parameters, and field data.
  • Split source/preview editor (source on the left, rendered label on the right) that updates as you type.
  • Label rendering of the most common ZPL commands:
    • Label setup: ^XA/^XZ, ^PW, ^LL, ^LH, ^CD
    • Positioning and fonts: ^FO, ^FT, ^FW, ^CF, ^A
    • Text fields: ^FD, ^FB, ^FR, ^FH, ^FS, ^FX
    • Graphics: ^GB (box), ^GC (circle), ^GD (diagonal line), ^GE (ellipse), ^GF (graphic field, ASCII-hex format)
    • Barcodes (^BY + symbology commands), including Code 128 (^BC), Code 93 (^BA), EAN-13 (^BE), Codabar (^BK), UPC-A (^BU), QR Code (^BQ), and Data Matrix (^BX)
The renderer is an emulator, not a bit-exact reproduction of a Zebra printer: built-in printer fonts are approximated with a scaled system font, only a single ^XA...^XZ label is drawn per preview, and ^GF only supports the ASCII-hex data format.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • .zpl file type with syntax highlighting for command mnemonics, parameters, and field data
  • Split source/preview editor for .zpl files that renders the label live as you type
  • Label rendering for common ZPL commands: label setup (^XA/^XZ, ^PW, ^LL, ^LH, ^CD), positioning and fonts (^FO, ^FT, ^FW, ^CF, ^A), text fields (^FD, ^FB, ^FR, ^FH, ^FS, ^FX), graphics (^GB, ^GC, ^GD, ^GE, ^GF), and barcodes (^BY plus ^BA, ^BC, ^BE, ^BK, ^BQ, ^BU, ^BX)

idea-plugin.name: Parquet Lens: Parquet, Avro, TFRecord, Arrow & Feather Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
Parquet Lens opens Parquet, Avro, TFRecord, Arrow and Feather files in the editor tab, straight off disk, with no notebook and no conversion step. The file is read in the pieces its own format has, row groups, record batches, blocks or records, so nothing is loaded whole, there is no row cap, and a 10 GB dataset pages the way a 10 MB one does.

The viewer is free and stays free. Pro is a subscription for this plugin: USD 2.90 a month or USD 29 a year for individual use. For organizations it is, per user, USD 5.80 a month or USD 58 a year.

An Avro, TFRecord, Arrow or Feather file opens in an IDE tab, and Pro writes it out as a Parquet file in one step.

Every .parquet, .avro, .tfrecord, .arrow, .feather (also .pq, .parq, .arrows, .ipc, .ftr, .tfrecords, .tfrec, and gzip or zlib compressed TFRecord files) file opens in a Parquet Lens tab - including files far beyond the IDE's large file limit.

The free tier is permanent.

Free - the full dataset viewer, for files of any size:

  • Any size: the file opens on its metadata, rows arrive in pages of up to 5000 in constant memory, go-to-row lands on any row, and there is no row cap
  • Compression: uncompressed, snappy, gzip and zstandard read as they come, lz4 opens under both of its parquet ids, and the older id reads in every layout it has been written in, the hadoop block frame, the bare raw block and the standard lz4 frame whether its blocks are linked or independent, so a file another tool wrote with lz4 opens here without being re-saved under a different codec first
  • Arrow & Feather first-class: Arrow IPC file and stream formats, Feather v2 including lz4/zstd-compressed and dictionary-encoded columns - written by pandas, polars, pyarrow, DuckDB and Hugging Face datasets
  • Avro containers: blocks decoded only when paged into view; codecs null, deflate, snappy and zstandard; nested records, arrays and maps come up as readable cells, and logical types decode to their values instead of raw bytes
  • TFRecord datasets: tf.Example and SequenceExample records, paged by their framing; each feature key is a column, byte features read as text or as an image label with its size, float and int64 lists keep their values; gzip and zlib files open as they are
  • Schema view: logical and physical types, nullability, compression codec, encodings - plus per-column null counts and min/max from the parquet footer, no scan needed
  • Find in file: streaming text search across every row (Ctrl+F), case toggle, next/previous jump - works at multi-gigabyte scale
  • Column stats on the visible page: nulls, distinct, min/max/mean - always labeled with their scope
  • Full types: timestamps, dates, times, decimals, uuid, float16, binary, and nested lists/structs/maps rendered as JSON with a pretty detail pane
  • Copy out: row as JSON, page as CSV
  • Named errors: corrupt or truncated files report a clear reason; exotic column types degrade to typed placeholders, never an error dialog
  • No Hadoop: the readers are the plugin's own, with no bundled runtimes

It runs on 2024.2 and newer with no upper build. Every release is checked across that whole range before it ships, Community, Ultimate and the newest preview build among them. A list or map column stays one column under its schema name, in the older list layout as well as the current one, with the value rendered as JSON in the cell, and a timestamp column reads as a date and time, with the UTC mark the file declares, instead of an integer.

It is built for machine learning and data engineering work in PyCharm, IntelliJ IDEA and every IntelliJ-based IDE: training data, eval sets, feature tables, lakehouse exports.

Pro - optional paid tier, for querying and extracting:

  • Filter queries: keep only the rows where columns match, for example lang == "en" && score >= 0.5, evaluated across every row group, with min/max pruning for speed
  • Export: write all rows, search matches or filter matches out to CSV, JSONL or a new Parquet file
  • Column profile: a second Pro export writes the profile report, named in the same export dialog: rows and nulls for every column, ranges, histograms and an outlier count for the numeric ones, the largest gap in a timestamp column, and a duplicate-row count that stops at two million rows. The report also carries a correlation matrix over up to forty numeric columns, says which of its numbers came from a sample, and is written as HTML, Markdown or JSON, so the Markdown pastes into a ticket that takes it.
  • Global sort: sort the whole dataset by any column, not just the visible page
  • Exact stats: compute nulls, min, max, mean and distinct counts over every row instead of the visible page; the footer figures in the schema view carry no mean or distinct count

A year of continuous subscription earns JetBrains' perpetual fallback license: the version available when that year started stays yours for good, including its fixes. Each Lens plugin comes with its own free 30-day Pro trial.

Part of the Lens family - viewers built on one engine, designed to hand off to each other, with one filter query language across the family in their Pro tiers. A Pro export writes filtered rows out as JSONL, and the result opens in JSONL Lens as a browsable, searchable grid. Log Lens reads multi-gigabyte logs the same way.

The guides and the overview of all eight viewers are at twilightventures.dev. Write to support@twilightventures.dev about anything to do with the plugin or a purchase, suggestions included; for a bug, name the version and the rough size of the file, or use the issue reporter at the end of the Help menu, which opens a prefilled new issue in your browser for you to read before you post.

Runs entirely locally: the plugin makes no network calls and handles no credentials, and Pro license state is read from the IDE's own licensing system.

What it does not do:

  • No editing by design: files are never written to; a Pro export creates a new file, a CSV, JSONL or Parquet copy or a profile report.
  • Not a query engine: the Pro filter predicates and whole-file sort, no SQL, no joins across files.

If Parquet Lens helps you, a short review tells us what to work on next.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.9.6 - The trial notices "Parquet Lens Pro trial ends in ..." and "Parquet Lens Pro trial has ended" now end with the price, "Pro is USD 2.90 a month or USD 29 a year for individual use", and a "See pricing" button that opens the marketplace page. During a trial you may see one request for a marketplace review, with "Write a review", "Feedback" and "No thanks".

1.9.5 - Numbers and dates in the Parquet Lens grid now follow the IDE's format locale, with a Local format checkbox beside Theme; the stored value shows on hover, and copy, search, filter, sort and export keep using it. A timestamp keeps its nanoseconds when copied or exported. A file cut short says "Parquet file magic missing at end of file (truncated or still being written?)". Exact stats count every distinct value of a binary, list or map column and stay on the Stats tab until a Reload or a new run, and a top-level column with a dot in its name keeps its own codec and statistics. Filter, Sort, Exact stats, Search and Export run only on the file the grid opened; a rewrite since the open refuses them with "The file changed on disk. Reload, then try again." After a Reload that carries a filter or a sort, a rewrite that lands before the view is back no longer leaves the grid empty: the first page of rows shows with that message, and the next Reload carries the view again. Go to row, or a Find that jumps to a hidden row, during that restore now drops the carried view, where the next Reload, filter or sort used to bring it back. With more than a week of a Pro trial left, the first Pro action is named once, as in "That filter query was Pro.", and the footer's trial line counts the Pro actions used. The footer shows no Pro line at IDE start until the license is read.

1.9.3 - Parquet Lens now notices when the open file changes on disk: a bar above the tabs offers "Reload" beside the words "The file changed on disk." Nothing reloads on its own. When the columns are unchanged, a reload now brings back the filter and the sort, then the page. With neither a filter nor a sort set, it goes back to the selected row. If the columns changed, both are cleared, with a note saying why. A reload without a license keeps the page and does not ask for one. Two links now sit in the Parquet Lens footer, under the tabs, beside the status line and the Pro line. "Try Pro free for 30 days" shows on a machine where the trial has not run and opens the IDE license dialog, where the trial starts. Once a trial has run there, the same spot reads "Get Pro" and leads to the pricing page. While Pro is running, bought or on trial, the spot is empty. "Write a review" shows in every state and opens the reviews page of the listing. At a narrow editor the Pro line and the links move below the status line instead of crowding it, and a status line longer than the row shows its whole text as a tooltip. The trial notices and the review prompt now wait until the IDE has finished reading the license, so a licensed machine is never told at startup that its trial has ended.

1.9.2 - The two notices before a Pro trial ends now finish with a question and the support address. A key issued for another plugin no longer opens Parquet Lens Pro. A key for Parquet Lens itself is unaffected.

1.9.1 - The listing now names every compression the reader opens, lz4 in each of the layouts it has been written in, and a test pins that list to the codec table; the no-row-cap and nested-type sentences carry tests of their own, with a sixty-thousand-row file read to its last row and nested and logical cells rendered as values.

1.8.0 - The profile report, a Pro export. Pick a name ending in .profile.html, .profile.md or .profile.json in the Export Rows dialog and the rows you chose are read once and written out as a report rather than a copy. Every column gets its row, null and empty counts and the kinds of value it holds. A numeric column adds the min, max, mean and standard deviation, the quartiles, a histogram and an outlier count; a text column its lengths, its distinct count and its most frequent values; a date or timestamp column the earliest and latest value, the median step and the largest gap. The whole table gets a duplicate-row count, which stays exact up to two million rows, and a correlation matrix over up to forty numeric columns. Where a figure came from a sample rather than from every row, the report says so beside the number, and it says the same wherever a count stopped at a cap. When the export finishes, the Export finished balloon offers Open report: the HTML opens in your browser, the Markdown and the JSON in an editor tab. A cancelled profile leaves no file, and the open file is refused as a destination, as it is for the other exports.

1.7.0 - Export to Parquet, a Pro action. Pick a .parquet name in the Export Rows dialog, whose filter now reads CSV, JSONL or Parquet, and the rows you chose, all of them, the search matches or the filter matches, are written as one snappy-compressed Parquet file. That is the whole conversion: an Avro, TFRecord, Arrow or Feather dataset becomes Parquet in one step. A column keeps the type its file declares where the writer has it, so int64, float64, text, bytes, bool, date, timestamp and a decimal of up to 18 digits go out as they came in. An int32 or float32 column widens to int64 or float64, a nested column lands as JSON text, and a value with no Parquet shape of its own, a time of day for instance, is written as the text the grid shows. A raw binary column keeps its bytes whatever Bytes as is set to; the charset applies only where a cell has to become text. TFRecord columns are sampled from the first records rather than declared, so there the values alone decide each type. The file that is open is refused as a destination with "That is the open file. Pick another name.", as it is for CSV and JSONL, and a cancelled export leaves nothing behind, neither the file nor the scratch copy the writer keeps beside it while it works. When the export finishes, the Export finished balloon offers Open in Parquet Lens, and the new file opens in its own tab here.

1.6.0 - Bytes as, a new choice beside the sort controls, reads a raw binary column as text. Parquet writers that never mark a column as a string leave it as bare bytes, and the grid showed a hex dump with its byte count. Pick UTF-8, Windows-1250, ISO-8859-2, CP852, EUC-KR, Shift_JIS or Windows-1254 and the column decodes, in the grid, the detail pane, find, copy page and export alike; a value that is not text under that charset keeps its hex, so an image column stays as it was. The export popup has a row for the CSV dialect: "RFC 4180 (comma)" as before, or "Excel EU (semicolon, decimal comma)", which is what Excel and LibreOffice expect on a European locale, where the fields are split on semicolons and floating point and decimal cells carry a decimal comma. The choice is remembered across files. The lz4 reader knew one layout, the hadoop block frame Spark and Hive write. It now opens every layout the legacy lz4 id has been used for: the standard LZ4 frame whether its blocks are linked or independent, plus the bare raw block that fastparquet and older arrow write. A page that fits no layout is refused by name, with both sizes in the message, and a page header claiming more than lz4 can produce is refused before any buffer exists.

1.5.2 - A trial that came from the JetBrains account page did not end. The IDE stores such a trial as a signed activation key with the trial's last day in it, and the plugin looked at the signature only, which stays valid for as long as the key exists, so Pro stayed on past the 30 days and the notice that the trial had ended never appeared. Paid keys and the perpetual fallback license read the way they always did. The free viewer is not touched.

1.5.1 - Parquet files compressed with the older LZ4 codec, the one Spark and Hive write when asked for lz4, now open. Such a file used to fail with a stack trace as soon as its first page was read, and an export from either tool no longer needs re-saving with a different codec before it opens here. A file compressed with a codec the plugin cannot read, brotli for example, is refused by name when it opens rather than failing on the first page.

1.5.0 - TFRecord files (.tfrecord, .tfrecords, .tfrec, gzip or zlib compressed too) open in the same tab. Records are indexed by their framing, tf.Example and SequenceExample features become columns with their values decoded, and byte features show as text or as an image label with its size.

1.4.1 - The plugin name now says Avro alongside Parquet, Arrow and Feather; nothing else changed.

1.4.0 - Avro object-container files (.avro) open in the same tab as Parquet, Arrow and Feather. The row count comes from the block headers, blocks decode only as you page through them, and files compressed with deflate, snappy or zstandard open without unpacking them first. Nested records, arrays and maps show as readable cells; decimals, dates, times, timestamps and uuids decode to their values.

1.3.3 - The trial notices now say what the trial did. The notice that a Pro trial is about to end, and the one that it has ended, open with a count of the exports and searches made while the trial ran (an export that wrote rows, a search that found something); nothing from before or after the trial is counted. The one-time review ask now waits for five moments of use instead of three (a file opened, a search with hits, the grid, an export), so it arrives after real use and not right after the first file opens.

1.3.2 - A Pro trial that is about to end says so once, with a link to pricing, and a trial that has ended says so once. Licensed users now get the thank-you and the Supporter line in the footer, and the family link stays visible. Pro gate messages and the listing now say what is true: each Lens plugin has its own free 30-day trial.

1.3.1 - Themes: an untinted cell no longer inherits the previous cell's tint, and switching back to Default clears every tint at once; the renderer now states both colors on every cell. A kept theme comes back only while the license holds, so a lapsed trial opens on Default. Export refuses the open file as its destination and asks for another name.

1.3.0 - Themes: pick a look for the grid from the toolbar. Eight strands shared across the Lens family (default, hacker, cyberpunk, goblincore, neon, nosferatu, halloween, blue lagoon) restyle the data grid with text, number and blob tints by column type, row striping and selection; the default look is unchanged and null stays quietly dimmed in every strand. Any strand tastes free for the open window, and keeping one set is Pro.

1.2.3 - The selected row stays selected through a page size change and a reload from disk; the grid used to drop it whenever the page came back. A finished export now counts toward the one-time review ask the way it does in the other Lens plugins, and the ask follows a single rule across opening, find, the grid and export.

1.2.2 - At narrow windows the paging toolbar used to print over the status line and the Pro line at the top of the Data tab; now that strip drops to its own row on the right when the two no longer fit, the toolbar wraps in the room it gains, and everything rejoins one row when the window is wide enough.

1.2.1 - No more clipped toolbar buttons: every control row wraps to a second line when the window gets narrow. A few tooltips and status lines traded long dashes for plainer punctuation, and empty stats cells print a plain hyphen instead of a dash.

1.2.0 - The review groundwork release. Report a Parquet Lens Problem now sits in the Help menu and opens a pre-filled issue on the family tracker - you see the whole text before anything is sent, and the plugin still makes no network calls. The panel footer names what Pro adds, or how many trial days are left, and the plugin asks exactly once for a review after the third file it opens cleanly. The listing says plainly what the plugin does not do. Everything free stays free.

1.1.0 - After a JSONL export, a notification offers to open the result in JSONL Lens when it is installed; when it is not installed, a one-time suggestion points to it.

1.0.0 - Out of early access. Everything that was free stays free - and dataset files now register their own file type and icon. Adds an optional Pro tier: whole-dataset filter queries, CSV/JSONL export, global sort, and exact full-scan statistics.

0.1.0 - First public release: instant-open viewer for Parquet, Arrow IPC (file + stream) and Feather v2 with constant-memory paging, schema view with footer stats, streaming search (Ctrl+F), page column stats, JSON/CSV copy.

idea-plugin.name: Columns - Parquet and Avro Editor
idea-plugin.description:
Open a Parquet file and see what is actually in it.

Columns reads Apache Parquet and Apache Avro files inside your IDE, without a cluster, without a Python environment and without exporting anything first. It reads the file's footer when you open it, so the row count and the schema are known immediately whatever the size of the file.

There is no row limit. Columns reads rows on demand from the part of the file you are looking at, so a file with millions of rows opens as quickly as a small one and scrolls to its last row. The row count on the status line is the file's real one, read from the footer, not a count of what has been loaded.

The awkward columns are the point. A list column is one column showing a list, a map column is one column showing a map, and a binary column shows its bytes rather than the name of a Java class. Decimals, dates and timestamps are shown as values rather than as the integers they are stored as, and every column header carries the type the file itself declares, so what you see can be checked against the file. Timestamps are shown in UTC and say so.

You can change a value and save the file. Edit a cell the way you would in a spreadsheet, undo with the IDE's own undo, and save with Ctrl+S like any other file. A value that does not fit the column's type is refused with a reason rather than written, and closing a tab with unsaved changes asks first. Saving rewrites the whole file, so it preserves the file's compression and the metadata other tools wrote into it, and columns you did not touch are copied across exactly as they were.

Parquet files written with no compression, Snappy, GZIP or Zstandard are all read, as are Avro container files.

Works everywhere JetBrains does. Columns depends only on the platform, so it installs in IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, PhpStorm, GoLand, Rider, RubyMine, CLion, DataGrip, RustRover and Android Studio, Community editions included.

Pricing, stated plainly

  • $29 per year for a personal licence.
  • $69 per year for a commercial licence.
  • 30-day free trial with everything unlocked. No feature is held back during the trial.
  • There is no free tier. After the trial, Columns needs a licence. Saying so here rather than letting you find out later is the whole point.

If all you need is to glance at a small Parquet file, there are free plugins that do that, and you do not need this one. This one exists for the file that is too big for them and for the columns they cannot show.

Known limits, stated up front

  • Not every column can be edited. Text, numbers, booleans, enums, binary values, decimals, dates and timestamps can. Lists, maps, records and columns that hold more than one possible type cannot, because a grid shows those as a single line of text and reading that line back would be a guess at a shape rather than a value. Those columns are shown but not opened for editing.
  • Saving rewrites the whole file, which is how both formats work: neither can change a value in place. The file is replaced only once the new one has been written in full, so a cancelled or failed save leaves your file exactly as it was.
  • Only local files. Files on a remote cluster or in object storage are not opened.
  • ORC files are not supported. The format needs a large amount of extra machinery that would nearly triple the size of the plugin, so it is being considered separately rather than promised here.
  • Sorting and filtering are not in this version. They would need the whole file to be read, and a sort that quietly applied to only part of it would be worse than none.
  • Updating the plugin needs an IDE restart to take effect.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.1.1

Adds a licensing screen with a direct link to start the free 30-day trial or enter a licence, so licensing can be handled without leaving the editor. The description now states the pricing and trial terms in full. No functional changes.

2026.1.0 - first release

The grid: Parquet and Avro files open in a table with no row limit, reading rows on demand, so a file of any size opens at once and scrolls to its last row. List, map, record, binary, decimal, date and timestamp columns are shown as values, and every column header carries the type declared in the file.

The reading engine: Parquet and Avro read through the Avro object model, so nested and logical column types keep their shape. No compression, Snappy, GZIP and Zstandard are all supported.

Editing: cells can be changed, undone with the IDE's own undo, and saved with Ctrl+S or Save All. Typing over a cell replaces it. A value that does not fit the column is refused with a reason and the cell keeps what it had. Closing a tab with unsaved changes asks first. Saving preserves the file's compression, the metadata other tools wrote into its footer, and every column that was not edited.

idea-plugin.name: WebView Runtime (Experimental)
idea-plugin.description:
Provides an embedded WebView panel for IntelliJ-based IDEs, making it possible to build rich local IDE UI with the standard web stack.
  • Supports HTML, CSS, JavaScript, TypeScript, and framework-based UI such as React, Preact, Svelte, Lit, or plain Web Components.
  • Uses Vite to build frontend sources into static assets that can be bundled with IDE plugins.
  • Provides typed Kotlin and TypeScript interop so WebView UI can call IDE code and receive data through strongly typed contracts.
  • Runs on browser engines: WKWebView on macOS, Microsoft Edge WebView2 on Windows, and JCEF on Linux.

idea-plugin.name: Spectra Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
Browse Spectra changes without leaving the IDE.
Spectra moves parked changes out of openspec/changes/ and into the git directory, where the project tree never shows them. This plugin adds a Spectra tool window that lists active, parked and archived changes side by side, shows task progress for each one, and opens their Markdown artifacts in the editor. It reads the files directly, so the Spectra app does not need to be running.
Unofficial: a community-built third-party plugin, not affiliated with or endorsed by Spectra. Spectra-related names belong to their respective owners.

Projects without the setting keep using openspec/ as before.
  • An unusable spec_dir (empty, an absolute path, or pointing outside the project) falls back to openspec/ and is reported in the IDE log.

  • New plugin icon and tool window icons using the official Spectra logo, with dedicated 20px variants for the new UI. Contributed by shengyou.

  • Filter changes by author: a new toolbar popup lists every proposer found across the Active, Parked and Archived groups, and you can tick any number of them at once. Changes whose proposer is not among the ticked authors are hidden from all three groups, while each group header keeps showing how many changes it holds in total, so a filtered-out change is never mistaken for a missing one.
  • The author filter combines with the existing text filter, so you can narrow the tree down to, say, your own changes whose name contains a keyword. A Refresh keeps the authors you had ticked as long as they still appear in the rescanned changes.

The command is typed for you but never run — you press Enter yourself, so picking the wrong tab costs nothing more than a line you can delete.
  • With the Terminal tool window closed or empty the same menu reads Copy Command and writes that line to the clipboard instead. The menu title always states which of the two it is about to do.

  • Release notes are now shipped with the plugin, so this page finally has a What's new section. No functional changes.

idea-plugin.name: TableKit: Excel & Parquet Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
Open Parquet, Excel, Avro, CSV, TSV and JSON Lines files directly in your IDE - no row limits, no freezes, no data ever leaving your machine.

TableKit turns any data file into a fast, scrollable table. Powered by an embedded DuckDB engine, it streams only the rows you are looking at, so a multi-gigabyte Parquet file opens as quickly as a small CSV.

Features

  • Parquet viewer - full file, not the first 10 000 rows
  • Avro viewer - schema, logical types and nested records
  • Excel viewer - .xlsx and .xlsm workbooks, sheet by sheet
  • CSV, TSV and JSON Lines - opened as an extra tab, your usual editor stays the default
  • Sort and filter pushed down to the query engine, not to your heap
  • Schema and column statistics - types, nullability, nulls, distinct values, min/max
  • Nested types (struct, list, map) rendered as readable JSON

Private by design

TableKit requests no network permissions. Nothing is uploaded, no telemetry is collected, and nothing is downloaded at runtime. Your data stays on your disk.

0.1.0

  • First release: Parquet, Avro, Excel, CSV, TSV and JSON Lines open in a virtualized grid with no row limit.
  • Sorting, filtering and column statistics are pushed down to the embedded engine rather than done on the IDE's heap.
  • Export the rows currently shown to CSV, TSV, JSON Lines or Parquet.
  • No network permissions: nothing uploaded, no telemetry, nothing downloaded at runtime.

idea-plugin.name: CloudWatch Logs Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
Read your AWS CloudWatch logs in the IDE, including AWS Lambda function logs, and keep reading them after the IDE updates.

Open a log group, pick a time range, type a filter. That's it.

Why this one

The usual reason AWS tooling stops working is not a missing feature. It is an IDE update. Plugins that declare a narrow supported build range get disabled the morning you move to the next version, and you find out when you need the logs.

Compatibility, in concrete terms

  • No upper IDE build limit is declared. An IDE update does not switch this plugin off.
  • Every release is run through the JetBrains Plugin Verifier against multiple IDE versions before it ships.
  • It targets one AWS service and nothing else. A small surface is what makes "still works next month" a promise worth making.

What it does

  • Browse log groups and star the ones you open every day
  • One merged stream instead of opening log streams one at a time
  • Filter patterns and time ranges
  • Live tail
  • Double-click a stack trace to open that source file at that line, in Java, Kotlin, Python, JS/TS, or Go
  • Select a line to read the full message, with embedded JSON indented

Where these logs come from

CloudWatch is where most AWS services put their logs, so this reads all of them the same way:

  • AWS Lambda function logs, in /aws/lambda/<function>
  • ECS and Fargate containers that use the awslogs log driver
  • API Gateway access and execution logs
  • EKS control plane, RDS, VPC flow logs, and anything else you send to a log group

Read-only by design. It reads log events. It never deletes a log group, never writes to your account, and never changes a resource.

Free and paid

  • Free: find your log groups, and read them. Searching, filtering, pretty-printing JSON and jumping to the source line are all free.
  • Paid: live tail, saving what is on screen, and favorites: the things that save you repeating yourself.

Every paid feature is included in a 30-day free trial, and no card is needed to start it. Buying and invoicing are handled by JetBrains.

Credentials come from your existing ~/.aws/config profiles, environment variables, and SSO sessions. Nothing is uploaded anywhere. The plugin talks to AWS directly from your machine.

Needs only logs:DescribeLogGroups, logs:FilterLogEvents, and logs:GetLogEvents.
