idea-plugin.name: S3 Browser
idea-plugin.description:
An AWS S3 explorer that lives in the IDE. Browse your S3 buckets, and keep browsing them after the IDE updates.

Walk folders, preview a file without downloading it, and pull down what you need.

A plain S3 explorer, and nothing else

If what you actually wanted was an AWS S3 file explorer in the IDE, without pulling in a toolkit that also wants your Lambda functions, your ECS clusters, and your sign-in state, this is that. One AWS service, one tool window.

Why this one

The usual reason AWS tooling stops working is not a missing feature. It is an IDE update. Plugins that declare a narrow supported build range get disabled the morning you move to the next version, usually while you are in the middle of something.

Compatibility, in concrete terms

  • No upper IDE build limit is declared. An IDE update does not switch this plugin off.
  • Every release is run through the JetBrains Plugin Verifier against multiple IDE versions before it ships.
  • It targets one AWS service and nothing else. A small surface is what makes "still works next month" a promise worth making.

What it does

  • List buckets and star the ones you open every day
  • Walk folders one level at a time, so a bucket with millions of keys stays fast
  • Filter by name
  • Preview the first part of a file in the IDE, with text and JSON formatted for you
  • Download a file to disk

Read-only by design. It lists and reads objects. There is no delete, no overwrite, and no bucket setting it can change. Nothing it does can lose your data.

Free and paid

  • Free: browse buckets and folders, and see sizes and dates.

idea-plugin.name: Step Functions Execution Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
See where a Step Functions execution stopped and what the failing state received. You keep seeing it after the IDE updates.

When a workflow fails you need three things: which state broke, the error, and the input that state was given. The console makes you click through the graph to collect them. This plugin puts all three on one line, with the raw event history right below it.

Why this one

The usual reason AWS tooling stops working is not a missing feature. It is an IDE update. A plugin that declares a narrow supported build range is switched off the morning you move to the next version.

Compatibility, in concrete terms

  • No upper IDE build limit is declared. An IDE update does not switch this plugin off.
  • Every release is run through the JetBrains Plugin Verifier against multiple IDE versions before it ships.
  • It targets one AWS service and nothing else. A small surface is what makes "still works next month" a promise worth making.

What it does

  • List state machines; star the ones you watch
  • List recent executions and open the failed one first
  • Name the state that actually broke, not the ExecutionFailed wrapper, which only says the run died
  • Show that state's input, which is the part you need to reproduce the bug locally and the most tedious to dig out by hand
  • Show the full event history, failures marked in red
  • Click the summary line to jump to the failing event
  • Live mode: keep refreshing while an execution runs
  • Point Endpoint at LocalStack when you run workflows locally

Read-only by design. It reads state machines, executions, and history. It cannot start, stop, or redrive anything.

Free and paid

  • Free: see your state machines and their executions.
  • Paid: reading the event history with the failing state and its input, live auto-refresh, and favorites.

Every paid feature is included in a 30-day free trial, and no card is needed to start it. Buying and invoicing are handled by JetBrains.

Credentials come from your existing ~/.aws/config profiles, environment variables, and SSO sessions. Nothing is uploaded anywhere. The plugin talks to AWS directly from your machine.

idea-plugin.name: Azure Blob Browser
idea-plugin.description:
An Azure Storage explorer that lives in the IDE. Browse Azure Blob Storage without slowing the IDE down.

Walk containers like folders, preview a blob without downloading it, and pull down what you need.

If you came here looking for Azure Storage Explorer

This covers the part of it you open every day, inside the IDE, with no separate desktop app to switch to. Be clear about the scope: it explores blob containers only. Queues, tables, and file shares are not included.

Why this one

Azure tooling in a JetBrains IDE usually fails in one of two ways: it reaches out to your subscriptions the moment the IDE starts, or it stops working after an IDE update. This plugin is built against both.

  • Nothing happens until you press Connect. No network call is made at IDE startup, so it cannot slow your startup down or throttle your account.
  • No upper IDE build limit is declared. An IDE update does not switch this plugin off.
  • No third-party libraries at all. It speaks the Azure Blob REST API directly using the JDK. Nothing to conflict with, and nothing extra to load.
  • Every release is run through the JetBrains Plugin Verifier against multiple IDE versions before it ships.

What it does

  • List containers and star the ones you open every day
  • Walk folders one level at a time, so a container with millions of blobs stays fast
  • Filter by name
  • Preview the first part of a blob in the IDE, with text and JSON formatted for you
  • Download a blob to disk

Read-only by design. It lists and reads blobs. There is no delete, no overwrite, and no account setting it can change. Nothing it does can lose your data.

Free and paid

  • Free: browse containers and folders, and see sizes and tiers.
  • Paid: previewing a blob, downloading, and favorites.

Every paid feature is included in a 30-day free trial, and no card is needed to start it. Buying and invoicing are handled by JetBrains.

Credentials. Enter the storage account name and an access key. The key is kept in the IDE password safe, never in project files. The plugin talks to Azure directly from your machine, and nothing is uploaded anywhere. Point the Endpoint field at http://127.0.0.1:10000 to work against the Azurite emulator.

idea-plugin.name: Cells - Notebook Viewer and Editor
idea-plugin.description:
Open a Jupyter notebook in the IDE you already use.

Cells reads, shows and edits .ipynb files. It depends only on the IntelliJ platform, so it installs in every JetBrains IDE, and it reads the notebook's own metadata rather than talking to a kernel, so nothing has to be installed or running for a notebook to open.

Your file comes back the way you left it. Saving writes the notebook exactly the way Jupyter writes one, byte for byte, so a one word change is a one line diff and code review still works. Everything the plugin does not own is copied across untouched: cell metadata written by other tools, attachments, outputs, and the notebook's own kernel information. The file on disk is replaced only after the whole new version has been written beside it, so a failed save leaves your notebook exactly as it was.

The notebook is coloured even where your IDE has no plugin for the language. When the IDE has a highlighter for the notebook's language it is used, so a notebook in PyCharm looks like PyCharm. When it does not, Cells colours the code itself. Python is coloured in an IDE with no Python plugin, and Julia is coloured in an IDE that has no Julia plugin at all.

Outputs are shown, not printed as JSON. Plots and images are drawn and scaled to the width of the tab. Printed output is shown as text you can select and copy. A traceback is shown as lines in your colour scheme's error colour, with the terminal colour codes IPython writes into it taken out. An output in a format this version cannot draw is named honestly instead of being dropped without a word.

Editing a notebook is ordinary IDE editing. Insert, delete, move and retype cells, and clear the outputs of one cell or of the whole notebook, from the toolbar, the right click menu or the keyboard. Every one of those is a single step on the IDE's own undo stack, in the order things happened, alongside the typing inside the cells. Changing a cell's type when it would lose something asks first, and one undo puts all of it back.

Large notebooks open now, not eventually. A cell's editor and its outputs are built as the cell comes near the screen, with the room they need reserved first, so a notebook opens in about the same time whatever its length and nothing jumps as you scroll. A 1,500 cell notebook opens in about a fifth of a second on the machine this was built on.

It follows your theme. Everything inside the notebook takes its colours from your editor colour scheme, and changing your theme restyles a notebook that is already open. A file you cannot write says so in a banner before you type into it, and every editing action is switched off rather than failing at Ctrl+S.

Pricing, stated plainly

  • $29 per year for a personal licence.
  • $69 per year for a commercial licence.
  • 30-day free trial with everything unlocked. No feature is held back during the trial.
  • There is no free tier. After the trial, Cells needs a licence. Saying so here rather than letting you find out later is the whole point.

Known limits, stated up front

  • Cells does not run code. There is no kernel and there will not be one. It reads, shows and edits the notebook file, and shows the output of whatever last ran it. If you need to execute cells, you need a tool that runs a kernel, and this is not one.
  • Notebook format 4 only. A notebook written in format 3, which Jupyter replaced in 2015, is refused with the command that converts it rather than opened and misread.
  • Markdown is coloured, not rendered. A markdown cell is shown as markdown source with highlighting, the way it is when you are editing it.
  • HTML output is shown as text. Rendering arbitrary HTML means shipping a browser engine, and doing it halfway turns a data frame into a wall of tags.
  • Local files only.
  • Updating the plugin needs an IDE restart to take effect.

It takes nothing away from an IDE that already opens notebooks. In PyCharm Professional and DataSpell, which have a notebook editor of their own, both editors are offered on the same file and you switch between them at the bottom of the tab. Cells claims no file type and writes nothing into your settings, so uninstalling it leaves your IDE exactly as it was.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.1.2

Your notebook is safe when something else writes to it. A notebook can be open in Cells and in another editor, a running Jupyter server or a git checkout at the same time. If the file on disk has changed since Cells opened it, saving now asks you first, and tells you what each answer does: overwrite with the version in your tab, or leave the file alone and keep your edits open. Whichever you choose, nothing is written until you say so.

2026.1.1

Bug fixes and improvements.

2026.1.0, the first release

Your notebooks open in the JetBrains IDE you already use. Cells shows an .ipynb file as a column of cells, each with its execution prompt, its code and the output of the last run underneath it. It needs no kernel, no Python environment and no subscription, so a notebook opens in GoLand, WebStorm, Rider, DataGrip, the Community editions and everywhere else, not only where a notebook tool is already installed.

You can edit, and your file comes back the way you left it. Type into a cell, insert, delete, move and retype cells, and clear the outputs of one cell or of the whole notebook, from the toolbar, the right click menu or the keyboard. Every one of those is a single step on the IDE's own undo stack. Saving writes the notebook exactly the way Jupyter writes one, byte for byte, so a one word change is a one line diff and your code review still works.

Outputs are shown, not printed as JSON. Plots and images are drawn and scaled to the width of the tab, printed output is text you can select and copy, and a traceback reads as lines in your colour scheme's error colour with the terminal codes taken out.

Colour, theme and size. Code is highlighted from the language the notebook itself declares, so Python is coloured in an IDE with no Python plugin and Julia in an IDE with no Julia plugin. Everything takes its colours from your editor colour scheme and follows it when you change theme. Cells are built as they come into view, so a notebook of fifteen hundred cells opens as quickly as a notebook of ten.

Trial and licence. A thirty day free trial with every feature unlocked, then twenty nine US dollars a year for a personal licence and sixty nine for a commercial one.

idea-plugin.name: Spring URL Scanner
idea-plugin.description:
Spring URL Scanner finds Spring MVC controller endpoints and OpenFeign client mappings in Java projects.

It scans project sources and dependency JARs, combines class-level and method-level mappings, and presents HTTP method, URL, controller/client type, handler, and source location in an IntelliJ IDEA tool window.

The scanner runs locally inside the IDE. It does not upload source code, collect telemetry, or contact external services.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Expand IntelliJ IDEA compatibility.
  • Lower the minimum supported IntelliJ IDEA version to 2024.1.
  • Build the plugin against the 2024.1 platform baseline.
  • Use a Java 17 bytecode baseline for compatibility with IntelliJ IDEA 2024.1.

idea-plugin.name: Rust Inline Diagnostics
idea-plugin.description:
Rust Inline Diagnostics displays Rust errors and warnings directly underneath the affected source code in compatible JetBrains IDEs.

Instead of hovering over highlighted code to read a diagnostic, you can see the message directly in the editor while you work.

Features

  • Persistent inline diagnostics for Rust code
  • Error and warning severity indicators
  • Theme-aware diagnostic colors
  • Diagnostics positioned near the affected source code
  • Automatically refreshes when code analysis completes
  • Supports multiple diagnostics on the same source line
  • Uses the IDE's existing Rust code analysis
  • No additional configuration required

Rust Inline Diagnostics is especially useful when working with compiler and IDE feedback related to ownership, borrowing, mutability, type mismatches, traits, and other Rust errors and warnings.

The plugin works with compatible JetBrains IDEs that provide Rust support, including IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate, CLion, PyCharm Pro, RustRover, and JetBrains Client.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Version 0.2.0

  • Improved JetBrains IDE compatibility.
  • Improved inline diagnostic rendering.
  • Added support for newer JetBrains IDE releases.
  • Updated build configuration for Java 21 bytecode compatibility.

idea-plugin.name: SQLite Lens: SQLite Database File Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
SQLite Lens opens SQLite database files in the editor tab, straight off disk, and read-only is the default. The schema tree comes up first and rows page in as you scroll: opening and paging feel the same at 4 MB or 4 GB, and Find streams down every row with live progress at hundreds of megabytes per second; Pro adds whole-table sort and a two-file diff that stream the same way. No connection setup, no server. It is a database browser for the file in front of you, not a client for a server. SQLite Lens never writes on its own: a change you stage is previewed as the exact rows and the exact SQL, saved only when you click Save, in one transaction, and until that click the file, its lock state and its journals are untouched. Browsing takes no locks, so it is safe to open a database a running app still owns. The SQLite viewer shows the file as it is on disk; a banner offers a one-click reload when it changes underneath.

The viewer is free and stays free. Pro is a subscription for this plugin: USD 5.90 a month or USD 59 a year for individual use. For organizations it is, per user, USD 11.80 a month or USD 118 a year.

A table pages to its last row, and there is no row cap. The plugin reads the database file phones and desktop apps keep, and Pro writes any table back out as Parquet.

Every .sqlite, .sqlite3, .db3 file opens in a SQLite Lens tab - and most files that start with the SQLite magic bytes, whatever their extension, including the .db files Android apps and desktop software leave behind. Files far beyond the IDE's large file limit open the same way.

The free tier is permanent.

Free - the full SQLite database viewer, for files of any size:

  • Never writes on its own: the open is immutable and read-only. No lock is taken, and no -wal, -shm or journal file appears beside the database. Edit mode stages a change and writes nothing until you click Save
  • Any size: metadata first, then rows in constant-memory pages of up to 5000; go-to-row lands anywhere
  • Schema tree: tables with row counts, then views, indexes, triggers, virtual tables; under each table its column types, the primary key and any foreign keys
  • Find in table: Ctrl+F streams a search down every row; next and previous jump between hits. A full scan of our 5M-row bench file: about 350 MB/s
  • Cell inspector: full values on demand - long text windowed, BLOBs as hex, text, or image preview (PNG, JPEG, GIF)
  • WAL-aware: pending WAL frames and hot journals are surfaced, with a one-click snapshot reload that never touches the original, and Edit stays off until the file is quiet
  • Exact types: 64-bit integers never rounded through floating point; INTEGER, REAL, TEXT, BLOB and NULL rendered exactly per cell
  • Database facts: page size, encoding, journal mode, user_version, application_id
  • Copy out: row as JSON, page as CSV
  • Named errors: an encrypted or corrupt file reports a named reason instead of an error dialog, and nothing in the plugin beeps

Built for anyone handed a database file: Android and Room developers inspecting app databases without a running device, Python and data work opening a .sqlite export in PyCharm, QA engineers checking fixtures, embedded and IoT development - in IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, Android Studio, and every JetBrains IDE.

Requires 2024.2 or newer (Android Studio Ladybug and later). Every release is checked on Community and Ultimate builds from 2024.2 up to the newest preview before it ships. This release is compatible with IntelliJ IDEA Community 2024.2.5 and 2024.3.7.1, IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate 2025.3.6.1 and 2026.2, and the 2026.3 preview. Pulling a database from a device? Copy the -wal and -shm files along with it to see the newest rows. If a .db file opens as text, right-click it and choose Override File Type, then SQLite Lens Database.

No language is registered and no .sql file is claimed; a Java or SQL source file keeps the editor it had. The grid uses the IDE's own table components and takes the IDE theme with them, dark or light, with nothing to switch per file. There is no upper IDE build in the descriptor, so a new IDE release does not switch SQLite Lens off.

Pro - optional paid tier, for querying, extracting and saving edits:

  • Edit without fear: stage, preview the exact SQL, save in one transaction, undo the last save, keep a backup copy. Turn Edit on to change cells, add and delete rows, paste a block of cells from a spreadsheet or set one column on the rows the filter shows; the preview shows the exact rows and the exact SQL, copies it or saves it as a .sql file, and until you click Save the file is untouched.
  • SQL console: your SQL goes to SQLite untouched, no lint. Several statements run in order, each timed, and a failing one stops the run and is named. SELECT and PRAGMA rows land in the grid; Explain opens the query plan in a pane of its own; a statement that would write is refused, since the console only reads and a change reaches the file through Edit, its preview and Save
  • Export: write a table, search matches or any query result out to CSV, JSONL or Parquet; Parquet columns are typed from their values, so a column of integers stays integers and a column that mixes text or blobs with numbers becomes text
  • Profile report: a second Pro export writes the report, named in the same export dialog: rows and nulls for every column, ranges, histograms and an outlier count for the numeric ones, the largest gap in a timestamp column, and a duplicate-row count that stops at two million rows. The report also carries a correlation matrix over up to forty numeric columns, says which of its numbers came from a sample, and is written as HTML, Markdown or JSON, so the Markdown pastes into a ticket that takes it
  • Diff two databases: compare schema and rows between two files - exact added, removed and changed counts with drill-in, rows matched by primary key
  • Whole-table sort: order by any column across every row, not just the visible page
  • WAL frames: decode the -wal beside the open database and list each frame SQLite would replay from it, checked with SQLite's own checksums or from the frame headers alone

Each Lens plugin comes with its own free 30-day Pro trial. A year of continuous subscription earns JetBrains' perpetual fallback license: the version available when that year started stays yours for good, including its fixes.

As a database browser, the SQLite viewer covers CI fixture checks, schema drift between builds (the Pro diff), and app database inspection in Android Studio and Community editions.

Part of the Lens family - viewers built to hand off to each other. Queried a table down to the rows that matter? Pro exports them as JSONL and opens the result in JSONL Lens as a browsable, searchable grid. Pro writes Parquet too, and when Parquet Lens is installed, one click on the finished-export balloon opens the file there. Parquet Lens reads columnar datasets and Log Lens reads multi-gigabyte logs the same way.

The guides and the overview of all eight viewers are at twilightventures.dev. Write to support@twilightventures.dev about anything to do with the plugin or a purchase, suggestions included; for a bug, name the version and the rough size of the file, or use the issue reporter at the end of the Help menu, which opens a prefilled new issue in your browser for you to read before you post.

Nothing leaves the machine: no network calls, no credentials handled, and the Pro check is the IDE's own JetBrains licensing.

Where it stops:

  • An encrypted database does not open; the file reports the reason and nothing else happens.
  • Tables without a usable primary key diff as counts only, and the diff says so.
  • Rows still in the WAL show after the one-click reload, not before it.

SQLite is a registered trademark of Hipp, Wyrick & Company, Inc. This plugin is not affiliated with or endorsed by the SQLite project.

A short review on the marketplace page tells us which of these features people lean on, and steers what we build next.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.7.3 - The trial notices "SQLite Lens Pro trial ends in ..." and "SQLite Lens Pro trial has ended" now end with the price, "Pro is USD 5.90 a month or USD 59 a year for individual use", and a "See pricing" button that opens the marketplace page. A query result in the console can now be exported, the Pro action the listing names; it had no menu entry before. During a trial you may see one request for a marketplace review, with "Write a review", "Feedback" and "No thanks".

1.7.2 - During a Pro trial the first Pro action of the trial is named once, in a note with the days left and what stays free: when that action is a console run, it reads "That SQL query was Pro." and ends on "Browsing, Find (Ctrl+F) and the schema tree stay free." The footer's trial line counts the trial's Pro actions after the days left, and the notices before a trial ends lead with the same tally, in which a Find no longer counts. A console run, an export of rows, a whole-table sort, a diff, a save and a WAL frame list count as one each; paging and an undo do not. Find matches a number typed the way the grid shows it, so where the grid writes a decimal comma, as in German, Turkish or Brazilian Portuguese, a price typed with the comma finds its row. When the filter is pasted from a copied cell, the page filter keeps a row whose text holds the unit separator the grid paints as ␟. Until the IDE has loaded its license data the footer offers nothing, so a buyer or a running trial is not offered Pro at start, and it fills in when the data arrives.

1.7.1 - The "SQLite Lens: page" task has a Stop now. When a whole-table sort is stopped before its first page comes, the table falls back to table order and the status line says "sort stopped (table order)"; a stop on a later page keeps the sorted page and the sort. Choosing another sort, changing the page size or closing the editor mid-sort froze the IDE until the sort finished; the sort is now told to stop and closed in the background. Find and the storage walk on the Info tab keep their own Stop when both run. Cancel ends a Find even where nothing matches, and a stopped walk no longer breaks the grid's next page. Each control character shows as its control picture, NUL as ␀. The Pro "Sort Whole Table" orders text the way a header click does, in the language's own order.

1.7.0 - SQLite Lens 1.7.0 adds editing. Read-only stays the default, and the file is untouched until you click "Save… (Pro)": turn "Edit" on in the toolbar, change cells, add or delete rows, then review the exact rows and the SQL of the save, which runs in one transaction. Saving is Pro, and "Undo last save… (Pro)" takes the last save back until the file is closed or reloaded; "Keep a copy of the file before saving" in the preview, off until checked, leaves a copy of the database beside it before the write. These are free: Ctrl+V pastes a block of cells copied from a spreadsheet, Ctrl+C copies a block out, "Set column for visible rows…" stages one value on every visible row of the loaded page, and "Copy SQL" and "Save as .sql…" in the preview write the preview's statements to the clipboard or to a file. In a narrow editor the toolbar now keeps every control after the project pane is hidden and shown, the footer's links stay visible while its long line ends in an ellipsis with the full text on hover, and the table tree keeps at least 120 pixels with "Copy page as CSV" wrapping onto its own line. A filter that hides every row of the loaded page says so. The status line shows how many rows of the page the filter keeps. The first time a file with one of the plugin's endings such as .db opens, a single notice, once per installation, points to Settings | Editor | File Types, the page where an ending is handed to another tool. An ending you give to another type there stays with that type, except Text: a database under a Text mapping still opens here, because the text editor cannot show one. ignat10 asked for editing in a review; thank you.

1.6.3 - SQLite Lens now opens .mbtiles, .spatialite, .sqlar and .fossil files the same way as .sqlite and .db files. Nothing else changed.

1.6.2 - SQLite Lens now opens .sqlitedb, .s3db and .sl3 files the same way as .sqlite and .db files. For an empty table, the status line reads "no rows" instead of a row range. The trial notices and the review prompt now wait until the IDE has finished reading the license, so a licensed machine is never told at startup that its trial has ended.

1.6.1 - Two links now sit in the SQLite Lens footer. "Try Pro free for 30 days" shows on a machine where the trial has not run and opens the IDE license dialog, where the trial starts. Once a trial has run there, the same spot reads "Get Pro" and leads to the pricing page. While Pro is running, bought or on trial, the spot is empty. "Write a review" shows in every state and opens the reviews page of the listing. The SQL console now has a wrap toggle and an undo stack, and the Info tab shows how much of the file each table and index takes.

1.6.0 - Diff now checks the license each time it runs, and so does the row drill-in. The Pro gate message now names the WAL frame list. The Pro trial notices now end with a question and the support address. A key issued for another plugin no longer opens SQLite Lens Pro. A key for SQLite Lens itself is unaffected. After a purchase, a balloon says thank you once on this machine. Its one action is "Write a review".

1.5.0 - Integer columns can be read as timestamps: right-click a column header and pick Show as timestamp with epoch seconds, milliseconds, microseconds or nanoseconds, with the unit the page suggests marked by magnitude, or Raw integer to turn it off. Each cell then shows the integer and the ISO-8601 UTC time in parentheses, the header tooltip names the unit, the inspector's Value tab carries the same reading, copy and export keep the integer, and the grid keeps the choice per file and table for the IDE session. The schema tree has a right-click menu now: every table, view, index, trigger and virtual table offers Copy Name and Copy Qualified Name, the second as SQL, qualified with main. and double-quoted only where the identifier needs them, and the grid header menu leads with Copy Column Name, and Copy Qualified Column Name when the grid shows a table or view. A CSV or JSONL export can carry its blobs whole (Pro): pick Whole table, blobs to files, or the same for the search matches, and every BLOB cell lands in its own file under a folder named after the export, with an index.jsonl that lists each file by row and column, while the row line keeps its preview. A file that is a SQLite database with a part that does not read now says so in plain words, the driver's detail staying in parentheses, and suggests what to try: copying it again together with any -wal and -shm files beside it if it came from a device or a server, or letting the write finish and pressing Reload if a program was writing it. A later read that lands on the damaged part says the file itself has not changed. A Pro trial hears from us twice before it ends: a notice when a week is left and another when a day is left, each naming what Pro adds, with a See pricing action to the marketplace pricing tab; a paid license sees neither.

1.4.0 - A column profile report, the second Pro export. Give the export a name ending .profile.html, .profile.md or .profile.json in the Export Rows dialog and the open table, or the search matches, is walked once and profiled instead of copied: every column gets its row, null and empty counts and the kinds of cell it holds; a numeric column its min, max, mean and standard deviation, quartiles, a histogram and an outlier count; a text column its length range, distinct count and most frequent values; a date or timestamp column its earliest and latest value, the median step and the largest gap. The table as a whole gets a duplicate row count, exact up to two million rows and marked when it stops there, and a correlation matrix over its numeric columns, forty at most. The quartiles, the histogram, the outliers and the gaps come from a sample once a column holds more than a thousand values, and the report says so beside each of those figures. The HTML is one page with nothing loaded from outside, and the JSON keeps every number at full precision. The finished balloon offers Open report, and a cancelled run leaves no file. The Pro SQL console also runs several statements in one go now: separated by semicolons they run in order, each timed in the status line; a failing statement stops the run and is named with its line number, the driver's own message and how many ran before it; a semicolon inside a string, a quoted name or a comment stays text; Explain gives one plan per statement; the grid shows the last result set; a statement that would write is refused as before, while BEGIN, COMMIT and ROLLBACK go to SQLite as typed.

1.3.0 - Export to Parquet, a Pro action. Pick a .parquet name in the Export Rows dialog, whose filter reads CSV, JSONL or Parquet, and the whole table or the search matches are written as one snappy-compressed Parquet file, each column typed from the values in it: integers as int64, reals as double, text as UTF-8 strings, blobs as bytes. A column of integers with a real among them is written as double, and a column that mixes text or blobs with numbers is written as the text the grid shows. Declared column types are not consulted, since SQLite keeps a type per value, and so does this export. The open database and its -wal, -shm and -journal files are refused as a destination, as they are for CSV and JSONL, and a cancelled export leaves no file behind, not even the scratch file the writer keeps beside the destination while it works. When the export finishes, the balloon offers Open exported file, and the file lands in Parquet Lens when that is installed. A new Pro tab, WAL (Pro): Read frames (Pro) reads the -wal beside the open database and lists the frames SQLite would replay from it, one row each, with the page number, whether the frame commits, the database size that commit leaves behind, its offset and its size. Above the rows the summary counts the committed frames and any unfinished tail apart, and names the frames left from an earlier cycle without listing them. The copied count from the -shm is added when that record can be trusted. Two read levels are offered, Verify with SQLite's checksums and Frame headers only (faster), and the summary names the one used. The Theme picker has two more entries at the end, lamplighter and catacombs, each with a padlock and its own line in the open list, "unlocks when you share Lens with a colleague" and "unlocks the first time Pro runs for you". Pick a locked one and the plugin opens the way to earn it. For lamplighter that is the share card, also under Help as Share SQLite Lens: the marketplace page, the family page and a referral code of this install's own, with the line "enter it under Theme in any Lens plugin" below it. Copy share card earns the theme here; a colleague who picks lamplighter in their own Theme picker, types the code into the share card and presses Unlock with code earns it on their side. Catacombs opens the first time Pro runs for you, a trial included, and an earned theme stays whatever the license says. Four night themes join the picker, Duskhollow, Abyss, Obsidian and Moonlit Garden; trying one is free for the open window and keeping it is Pro, like the eight. Files ending in .gpkg open here too, since a GeoPackage is a SQLite database by specification, and the Info tab names the GeoPackage version the file declares.

1.2.8 - Trials that begin from a JetBrains account come with a signed key, and that key went on opening Pro after the 30 days were used up. It stops the day after the trial ends. Bought licenses are left alone, the perpetual fallback license too. The same mistake had the plugin thank a lapsed trial the way it thanks a buyer, and the notice that a trial has ended never showed; both are right now. Second fix, in the WAL banner: every frame in the -wal file was counted as one you had not seen yet. After a checkpoint that could not shorten the file, the frames stay where they are even though the database already has them, so a fully checkpointed database still warned about pending changes. The count now takes the -shm file into account, which records how many frames a checkpoint copied in, and the banner says nothing is waiting once none are left. If that record cannot be trusted, every live frame is counted, as before. The facts row carries the same number, and one frame is written as 1 frame, not 1 frames.

1.2.7 - Files ending in .db now open in SQLite Lens by extension, the same way .sqlite, .sqlite3 and .db3 files do, so the IDE can offer the plugin when a project contains one. Before this the plugin only picked up a .db file after reading its first bytes. A .db file that is not a SQLite database, a Thumbs.db for example, says so in the panel.

1.2.6 - The WAL banner used to count the frames the -wal file had room for, so a database whose -wal had been rewound by a checkpoint but not shortened reported changes not yet visible when the reader was already seeing all of them. The count now comes from the frame headers, and the size beside it is the size of those frames rather than the whole file. A -wal that declares a different page size than the database was written for another file, so the banner says that instead and the reload offer is withheld. On a very long -wal the walk stops early and the banner says at least how many frames it found.

1.2.5 - Both trial notices now open with what the trial did, exports first, then searches; only a search with hits and an export that wrote rows count, and only while the trial runs. The one review ask waits for five value moments now, not three, so a first open no longer reaches it on its own. The listing text was tightened.

1.2.4 - A Pro trial that is about to end says so once, with a link to pricing, and a trial that has ended says so once. Opening a database now counts toward the review ask. Pro gate messages and the listing now say what is true: each Lens plugin has its own free 30-day trial.

1.2.3 - A saved theme comes back on open only while the license is active; without one the grid opens in the default look, and tasting any theme stays free for the window. Going back to Default no longer counts as a chosen theme. Export refuses to write over the file that is open (the database, its snapshot or a sidecar) and asks for another name instead of failing.

1.2.2 - Reloading the page used to drop the selected row and cell; they stay put now, through a page reload and a reload from disk. The same row is found again by its key when the same page comes back, by position otherwise. The one review ask also counts its moments by one rule now: a load with rows, a search with hits and a grid with columns count once per opened file, every finished export counts, and a failure, a cancel or an empty result never does.

1.2.1 - At narrow windows the footer used to print the file size on top of the Pro line; now the Pro line drops to its own row on the right when the two no longer fit, and rejoins the row when there is room again.

1.2.0 - Themes: pick a look for the whole tab from the toolbar. Eight strands shared across the Lens family restyle the data grid, console results and diff drill-in with text, number and blob tints, row striping and selection; the default look is untouched and NULL stays quietly dimmed in every strand. Any strand tastes free for the open window, and keeping one set is Pro. Two diff repairs ride along: drill-in row fetches now key off the declared primary key, so Show rows works on keyed tables it used to fail on, and a finished comparison now survives the editor view rebuilding instead of coming back empty.

1.1.1 - The toolbar wraps at narrow widths now, instead of pushing Sort and Export past the window edge, and the diff view controls follow the same rule.

1.1.0 - Blob hex now renders through a lookup table: full-table CSV export on a 5M-row bench with a blob in every row went from 38k to 460k rows a second, about 12x. Changed rows in the diff drill-in now highlight the exact cells that differ, with a Next difference jump. The first time the plugin sees your Pro license it says a one-time thank you, then keeps a quiet supporter line in the footer - stored locally, like everything else.

1.0.1 - Right-click lands in the data grid: copy the row as JSON, copy the page as CSV, and jump straight to Export on Pro. WAL banners now lead with what you might be missing, and a WAL database with no -wal file beside it points back at the source machine. Failure messages in the console, diff, export and snapshot paths now say what happened and what to try. The listing description is synced with the marketplace page.

1.0.0 - First release. Free: read-only viewer with an immutable no-locks guarantee, schema tree with row counts, constant-memory paged grid, streaming Find, cell inspector with BLOB image preview, WAL and hot-journal banners with snapshot reload. Pro: execute-only SQL console with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN, CSV/JSONL export, two-file database diff with exact counts, whole-table sort.

idea-plugin.name: XLSX Lens: Excel XLSX Spreadsheet Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
XLSX Lens opens Excel workbooks in the editor tab: 500k rows, streamed, strictly read-only. Excel workbook files (.xlsx, and .xlsm as data) and the Excel template files .xltx and .xltm open in an editor tab straight off disk - every sheet one click away, rows paging in as you scroll, merged cells rendered, dates and the common number formats applied. A template is the same package as a workbook under another content type, so it is parsed and rendered exactly as a workbook: the same sheets, cells, merges and formats, and no macro runs either way. XLSX Lens is an Excel spreadsheet viewer for the file in front of you, not a spreadsheet application.

The viewer is free and stays free. Pro is a subscription for this plugin: USD 2.90 a month or USD 29 a year for individual use. For organizations it is, per user, USD 5.80 a month or USD 58 a year.

The workbook somebody mailed you opens in an IDE tab, and Pro writes it back out as a Parquet file for your data tools.

The free tier is the complete viewer and stays free. Pro adds export to CSV, JSONL, Markdown or Parquet, a column profile report, whole-sheet sort and filter, sheet diff, column stats, formula view and watch mode.

A date cell is read by the date system the workbook itself declares, 1900 or 1904. Free features never consult the license at all; a Pro action checks at the click and, with no license present, opens the IDE's own plugin license dialog without changing the viewer around it. A sheet pages to its last row, and there is no row cap. The descriptor sets no upper IDE build, so a new IDE release does not switch XLSX Lens off.

Free - the full Excel spreadsheet viewer, for files of any size:

  • Opens on current IDE builds: IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, Rider, GoLand, Android Studio and every IntelliJ-based IDE, 2024.2 through the newest. Every release is checked across that whole range before it ships, Community, Ultimate, Android Studio and the newest preview build among them; a workbook that will not open is a bug we want to hear about, and Report an XLSX Lens Problem in the Help menu is the quickest way to tell us.
  • Any size: a single streaming pass spills rows to a scratch index, so the first page renders while a 500,000-row sheet is still loading behind it and memory stays flat
  • Strictly read-only: never writes to the workbook, never locks it, never recalculates; a file a pipeline or a client handed you cannot be corrupted by viewing it
  • All sheets: the sheet list shows every tab, hidden ones named as hidden
  • Fidelity: merged cells rendered, cached formula values shown, dates in both the 1900 and 1904 systems, builtin and common custom number formats
  • Find in sheet: streaming search across every row (Ctrl+F) - values, formatted text and formulas, with next/previous match jump
  • Cell inspector: the full value, the raw stored text, the formula and the format pattern of any cell, unclipped
  • In-page sort, filter and copy: sort or filter the loaded page, copy a row as JSON or the page as TSV
  • Named errors: an encrypted workbook, a legacy .xls or a mislabeled zip reports what it actually is, in the panel, never as an error dialog

What it does not do: no editing and no cell writes of any kind, no formula recalculation (cached results are shown), no legacy .xls, no font and color fidelity (values and layout, not print styling) - and it never takes over .csv or any other file association it cannot honor.

Built for anyone handed a workbook: backend and data engineers opening a client's .xlsx export in PyCharm, QA checking an Excel report a pipeline emitted, analysts peeking at a 200 MB Excel export.

Pro - optional paid tier, for extracting and comparing:

  • Export: write the sheet, search matches or the current filtered view to CSV, JSONL, Markdown or Parquet; a Parquet column of dates is written as dates and a column of numbers as numbers. A second Pro export writes the profile report, named in the same export dialog: rows and nulls for every column, ranges, histograms and an outlier count for the numeric ones, the largest gap in a timestamp column, and a duplicate-row count. The report also carries a correlation matrix over up to forty numeric columns, says which of its numbers came from a sample, and is written as HTML, Markdown or JSON, so the Markdown pastes into a ticket that takes it.
  • Diff two Excel workbooks: sheets matched by name, exact added, removed and changed row counts with drill-in
  • Whole-sheet sort and multi-column filter: every row, not just the loaded page, with spreadsheet type order
  • Column stats: profile any column for its kinds, min, max, sum, mean and distinct counts
  • Formula view: switch the whole grid from values to formulas; one cell at a time is free in the inspector
  • Watch mode: reload automatically when the file changes on disk, so a workbook that a job keeps rewriting stays current

Each Lens plugin comes with its own free 30-day Pro trial. A subscription carries a perpetual fallback license: after 12 uninterrupted months, the version from the start of that subscription year, with its fixes, stays yours even if the subscription ends.

Part of the Lens family - viewers built to hand off to each other. Filtered an Excel sheet down to the rows that matter? Export them as JSON Lines and open the result in JSONL Lens as a browsable, searchable grid. Export as Parquet and, when Parquet Lens is installed, one click on the finished-export balloon opens the file there. Parquet Lens reads columnar datasets, Log Lens reads multi-gigabyte logs and SQLite Lens reads database files the same way.

The guides and the overview of all eight viewers are at twilightventures.dev. Write to support@twilightventures.dev about anything to do with the plugin or a purchase, suggestions included; for a bug, name the version and the rough size of the file, or use the issue reporter at the end of the Help menu, which opens a prefilled new issue in your browser for you to read before you post.

Runs entirely locally, with no network calls and no credentials. Pro license state is read from the IDE's own licensing system - the plugin itself never touches the network. Excel is a trademark of Microsoft Corporation; XLSX Lens is an independent product with no Microsoft affiliation or endorsement.

If XLSX Lens helps you, a short review tells us what to work on next.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.6.6 - The trial notices "XLSX Lens Pro trial ends in ..." and "XLSX Lens Pro trial has ended" now end with the price, "Pro is USD 2.90 a month or USD 29 a year for individual use", and a "See pricing" button that opens the marketplace page. During a trial you may see one request for a marketplace review, with "Write a review", "Feedback" and "No thanks".

1.6.5 -The first Pro action of a trial now gets a notice of its own, once, while more than a week of the trial is left. Sort the whole sheet and it reads "That whole-sheet sort was Pro." It says how many days the trial has left and ends on what stays free: "Sorting the loaded page stays free - click a column header." Filters, sheet diffs, exports, profile reports and column stats are named the same way. The footer's "Pro trial" line gains the count of Pro actions the trial has run, and the notices at the end of a trial open with the Pro actions used most, by name, instead of exports and searches. Find stays free and is no longer counted. When the IDE starts, the footer shows no Pro line and no "Try Pro free for 30 days" or "Get Pro" link until the license is known, so a machine that bought Pro, or is partway through a trial, is no longer offered Pro while the license loads.

1.6.4 - Numbers and dates now read with a decimal point and the digits 0 to 9 on every machine, in the grid and in the CSV, JSONL and Markdown exports and the text columns of a Parquet export, like the rest of the sheet. Under a regional format that writes decimals with a comma (German, Polish, Hungarian, Turkish or Portuguese), a cell in scientific format read 1,23E+10 instead of 1.23E+10 and those exports wrote it that way. On a locale with Arabic-Indic digits, the year, the zero-padded date and time parts and an elapsed time came out in those digits. The footer's "Pro" line now ends in an ellipsis with its full text as a tooltip when the footer is too narrow, instead of being cut off.

1.6.3 - The plugin description now names the .xltx and .xltm template files beside .xlsx and .xlsm and says how they are handled: a template is parsed and rendered exactly as a workbook. Nothing else changed.

1.6.2 - XLSX Lens now opens .xltx and .xltm template files the same way as .xlsx and .xlsm files. When the editor is narrow, the Pro line and the "Marketplace page", "Try Pro free for 30 days" and "Write a review" links now move below the status line and wrap onto more lines instead of pushing the status line out of view, and a status line longer than the row shows its whole text as a tooltip. The trial notices and the review prompt now wait until the IDE has finished reading the license, so a licensed machine is never told at startup that its trial has ended, and a thank-you prompt no longer follows a trial notice in the same sitting.

1.6.1 - Two links now sit in the XLSX Lens footer. "Try Pro free for 30 days" shows on a machine where the trial has not run and opens the IDE license dialog, where the trial starts. Once a trial has run there, the same spot reads "Get Pro" and leads to the pricing page. While Pro is running, bought or on trial, the spot is empty. "Write a review" shows in every state and opens the reviews page of the listing. Drag a block of cells in the grid and Export now offers that range, the rows you dragged over and only the columns they cover, in any format the Export dialog writes. That export is Pro like the others, and Copy Page stays free. The chooser names the range before you pick it, and the column letters travel with the data.

1.6.0 - Watch and Diff now check the license each time they run. The Pro trial notices now end with a question and the support address. A key issued for another plugin no longer opens XLSX Lens Pro. A key for XLSX Lens itself is unaffected. After a purchase, a balloon says thank you once on this machine. Its one action is "Write a review".

1.5.2 - The compatibility line on the listing now covers the whole range a release is checked across before it ships. A test pins that line to the release ladder.

1.5.0 - The sheet's own conditional formatting paints in the grid: a cell value rule, the text rules, blanks and errors, duplicate and unique values, top and bottom rank, above and below average, each with the fill and the font colour the file gives it, applied in priority order. A rule the viewer cannot evaluate the way Excel does, a formula rule, a colour scale, a data bar, an icon set, a percent rank, paints nothing and is named in the Info tab under Formatting. Stats opens for everyone now and leads with Duplicate rows, which walks the finished sheet and says how many rows repeat an earlier one, all columns compared, the first occurrence of each kept. Two rows are the same row by the rule the diff uses, the stored value and the formula text, never the number format, so 1 and 1.0 agree and x and X do not. Export the clean copy, a Pro action on that report, writes a workbook with the kept rows on a sheet named for the source and every removed row on a second sheet, _lens_removed, beside the row it repeats. The export dialog takes an .xlsx name as well now, where the filter reads CSV, JSONL, Markdown, Parquet, XLSX or a profile report: the sheet, the search matches or the current view go out as a workbook copy, every cell with its value and its number format, and the finished balloon offers to open the copy in this plugin.

1.4.0 - The column profile report, a second Pro export for the open sheet. Give the export a name ending .profile.html, .profile.md or .profile.json and the rows are profiled instead of copied: every column gets its row, null and empty counts and the kinds of cell it holds, a numeric column its min, max, mean, quartiles, a histogram and an outlier count, a text column its distinct count and most frequent values, a date or timestamp column its earliest and latest value and the largest gap in the series. The sheet as a whole gets an exact duplicate-row count and a correlation matrix over its numeric columns, forty at most. Wherever a figure came from a sample rather than every row, the report says so beside it. The HTML page opens in your browser from the finished balloon, the Markdown pastes into a ticket as it is, and the JSON keeps every number at full precision. Search matches and the current view profile the same way the whole sheet does, and a cancelled run leaves no file.

1.3.0 - Export to Parquet, a Pro action. Pick a .parquet name in the export dialog, where the filter reads CSV, JSONL, Markdown or Parquet, and the sheet, the search matches or the current view are written as one Parquet file, one column per sheet column, named by its letter. A column of numbers is written as numbers, and a column of dates as dates, or as timestamps when the cells carry a time, read by the date system the workbook declares, 1900 or 1904. Where a column mixes kinds, say a header row over numbers, the cells are written as the text the grid shows, so it reads the way the CSV would. The open workbook is refused as a destination, as it is for CSV, and a cancelled export leaves no file behind. When the export finishes, the balloon offers Open exported file, which lands in Parquet Lens when that is installed; with no viewer for it, the click says so and points at Parquet Lens instead. The Theme picker has four more themes, Duskhollow, Abyss, Obsidian and Moonlit Garden, and two entries at the end, lamplighter and catacombs, each with a padlock and its own line in the open list: "unlocks when you share Lens with a colleague" for lamplighter, "unlocks the first time Pro runs for you" for catacombs. Pick a locked one and the plugin opens the way to earn it. For lamplighter that is the share card, also under Help as Share XLSX Lens: plain text for a colleague, a marketplace line, a Lens family line and a referral code of this install's own. "Copy share card" earns the theme here, and a colleague who enters that code under Theme in any Lens plugin earns it there. An earned theme stays, whatever the license says. The four night themes follow the rule of the eight: trying one is free for the open window, keeping it is Pro.

1.2.2 - Reload and watch mode reopen the workbook on the sheet that was open; both used to land on the first sheet, with the selected row carried over to the wrong one. File | Open Workbook... opens an .xlsx or .xlsm from anywhere on disk in an XLSX Lens tab, attaching nothing to the project, and the same entry answers in Search Everywhere; it is free, like the rest of the viewer. Each sheet in the list shows its size as rows x columns once it has been read, and a sheet with nothing in it reads empty.

1.2.1 - A Pro trial started from your JetBrains account arrives as a signed license key, and only the signature was checked, which stays valid after the 30 days. So a trial that had ended kept Pro unlocked and passed for a purchase: no trial-ended notice, and a thank-you meant for buyers. A trial key now unlocks Pro through its last day and then stops; paid licenses, the perpetual fallback included, are unchanged. The workbook diff marks the cells that changed. In the changed-rows drill-in, the A and B rows paint the cells where they differ, by the same rule the counts use: the stored value and the formula text, never the number format, and both rows of a pair carry the same marks. Next difference steps through those cells in reading order and wraps at the end. The status line says how many cells differ in the rows shown, and a new comparison clears the old drill-in.

1.2.0 - Currency and accounting formats render now, and so do fractions, with the symbol or the parentheses where the workbook puts them; those cells used to fall back to the plain number. Optional decimal places stop inventing zeros, so 0.## on 1.5 reads 1.5 rather than 1.50, and a value like 2.675 rounds to 2.68 the way the spreadsheet shows it. Date formats no longer print a locale or color tag in front of the date, and a bracketed [mm] or [ss] shows the elapsed total, as [h] already did.

1.1.4 - The trial notices name what the trial did: how many exports and how many searches, counted only while the trial runs. The one-time review ask now waits for five value moments, so it arrives after real use rather than on the first open.

1.1.3 - A Pro trial that is about to end says so once, with a link to pricing, and a trial that has ended says so once. Opening a workbook now counts toward the review ask. Pro gate messages and the listing now say what is true: each Lens plugin has its own free 30-day trial.

1.1.2 - A saved theme comes back on open only while the license is active; without one the grid opens in the default look, and tasting any theme stays free for the window. Going back to Default no longer counts as a chosen theme. Export refuses to write over the open workbook and asks for another name instead of failing.

1.1.1 - The selected row and cell stay put through a page reload and a reload from disk; the grid used to drop them whenever the data came back. The one-time review ask follows a single rule now across opening, find, the grid and export, and an empty sheet does not count.

1.1.0 - Themes: a Theme combo at the end of the toolbar picks a look for the whole workbook tab. The eight strands the Lens family shares restyle the data grid and the diff drill-in: text and number tints, row striping, the selection color. Default stays exactly as shipped, and empty cells and merged echoes keep their quiet dimming under every strand. Tasting any strand is free for the open window; keeping one set is Pro. Also fixed: a toolbar row that wrapped at narrow widths was laid out but hidden under the row above it, so its controls vanished. The row gets its full height now.

1.0.3 - Sixteen toolbar controls used to sit in two fixed rows, and a narrow panel still pushed the last buttons past the edge. The rows reflow now, and the sheet diff controls do the same.

1.0.2 - Find shows a live match count while it scans; a 500k-row sheet no longer sits on searching until the end. Named ranges appear in the Info tab, name and reference exactly as the workbook stores them. And the first time a Pro license shows up, one thank-you, said locally, never repeated.

Opening any workbook successfully counts for the review nudge; the old rule starved tiny files of it. When something breaks in read, search, view, export, stats or diff, the message says what broke and what to do about it.

1.0.0 - First release. Free: read-only workbook viewer with streaming open (first page renders while large sheets index), all sheets listed, merged cells rendered, cached formula values, 1900/1904 date systems, builtin and common custom number formats, whole-sheet Find across values and formulas, cell inspector, in-page sort/filter and copy. Pro: CSV/JSONL/Markdown export, two-workbook sheet diff with exact counts, whole-sheet sort and multi-column filter, column stats, formula view, watch mode.

idea-plugin.name: DBML Pro
idea-plugin.description:
Design, explore, and evolve database schemas written in Database Markup Language (DBML) without leaving your JetBrains IDE.

  • Edit modern DBML with highlighting, formatting, completion, live templates, structure view, inspections, and quick fixes.
  • Navigate confidently with go to declaration, find usages, and safe rename across schemas and visibility-scoped modules.
  • Explore a live entity-relationship diagram with DBML data-lineage edges, expandable sample records, DiagramView filtering, sticky notes, table colors, and saved layouts.
  • Import SQL and Prisma schemas with support for mappings, defaults, checks, indexes, composite keys and relationships, referential actions, and SQL INSERT sample data.
  • Keep rich DBML details intact in diagrams and exports, including defaults, identity columns, indexes, enums, composite relationships, groups, notes, and colors.
  • Export SQL DDL and sample seed data, Prisma, TypeScript interfaces, SVG diagrams, Markdown, and HTML documentation.
  • Reverse engineer database schemas and compare DBML with live data sources in IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate and DataGrip.

Compatible with IntelliJ IDEA 2025.3.1 through 2026.2 and JetBrains IDEs based on the same platform versions.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Improved

  • Smoothed out a few internal details to make day-to-day editing more dependable.

idea-plugin.name: Notebook Lens: Jupyter ipynb Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
Notebook Lens opens Jupyter notebooks as rendered documents in every JetBrains IDE - IntelliJ IDEA, GoLand, Android Studio, PyCharm, WebStorm, Rider and the rest, 2024.2 through the newest. Every release is checked against Android Studio as well as IntelliJ IDEA before it ships. No kernel, no Python plugin, no Jupyter install - one plugin, complete on its own, nothing else to add before it works. Double-click an .ipynb file and read it in the Jupyter notebook viewer, straight off disk.

The viewer is free and stays free. Pro is a subscription for this plugin: USD 2.90 a month or USD 29 a year for individual use. For organizations it is, per user, USD 5.80 a month or USD 58 a year.

Big notebooks are the point. The viewer indexes where every cell sits instead of loading the file whole, so a 175 MB notebook with 9,000 cells, images and long outputs opens in about a second. The first screen renders while the rest is still indexing. Cell 9,000 is one Go click away. And the render is static: outputs are drawn exactly as they were saved, nothing executes, so a notebook full of long run output cannot freeze the viewer.

The free tier is the complete viewer and stays free. Pro adds notebook diff, source export and cross-cell search (every cell searched in one pass, with a hit list).

Free - the full Jupyter notebook viewer, for files of any size:

  • Rendered cells: markdown with headings, lists, quotes and links, code with Python coloring, and outputs the way a notebook shows them - result text, stream logs, tracebacks in their ANSI colors, inline images
  • Any size: one streaming pass indexes where every cell sits in the ipynb file; pages are read on demand and memory stays flat
  • Read-only, never executes: no kernels, no writes. A notebook a pipeline or a colleague handed you is only ever read
  • Navigation that scales: an outline rail, next and previous code or markdown cell, go-to-cell that lands exactly
  • Find in the current cell, with the match line reported
  • Honest errors: a truncated file names the byte where it breaks; a legacy nbformat 3 notebook gets the exact convert command. In the panel, never a dialog

What it does not do: no execution, no kernels, no editing. Outputs are shown as saved, not recomputed. Markdown tables and LaTeX appear as source rather than rendered wrongly. 2011-era nbformat 3 files are named, not half-read. And Notebook Lens does not take over the notebook association: it names the .ipynb file type so the project tree and the marketplace know the file, but where the IDE's own Jupyter support is installed, that support keeps the file and the Notebook Lens tab sits beside it as before.

The IDE's plain text editor stays open as a second tab on the same file, so the raw JSON is one click away. Cell text is decoded as UTF-8; text in any script, Chinese or Korean included, shows as written. Colors and the monospace font come from the IDE's own editor scheme, which means a dark IDE shows a dark notebook with nothing to switch per file.

Who is it for? Go and Android developers whose IDE has no Jupyter support at all. Data engineers reading a colleague's analysis in IntelliJ. Reviewers who want to see what a notebook does without spinning up a server for it.

Pro - optional paid tier, for comparing and extracting:

  • Notebook diff without the noise: compares cell type and source only - outputs and execution counts are ignored by design. Exact added, removed and changed counts with drill-in, and id-aware matching so a moved cell is not a change
  • Export source to .py in the percent format VS Code, Spyder and jupytext read, or to Markdown with fenced code. Outputs stripped, counts exact
  • Cross-cell search: search every cell of the notebook in one streaming pass, with a hit list that jumps to each match; the free find covers the current cell

Each Lens plugin comes with its own free 30-day Pro trial. A subscription carries a perpetual fallback license: after 12 uninterrupted months, the version from the start of that subscription year, with its fixes, stays yours even if the subscription ends. Pro is new features, never a takeback.

Part of the Lens family - viewers built for the files IDEs give up on. JSONL Lens reads JSON Lines, Log Lens reads multi-gigabyte logs, Parquet Lens reads columnar datasets, SQLite Lens reads database files, DuckDB Lens reads DuckDB database files, XLSX Lens reads Excel workbooks and Heap Dump Lens reads JVM heap dumps the same way.

The guides and the overview of all eight viewers are at twilightventures.dev. Write to support@twilightventures.dev about anything to do with the plugin or a purchase, suggestions included; for a bug, name the version and the rough size of the file, or use the issue reporter at the end of the Help menu, which opens a prefilled new issue in your browser for you to read before you post.

Runs entirely locally. No network calls. No credentials. Ever. Pro license state is read from the IDE's own licensing system - the plugin itself never touches the network. Jupyter is a trademark of NumFOCUS, Inc.; Notebook Lens is an independent product with no Project Jupyter affiliation or endorsement.

If Notebook Lens helps you, leave a short review - it helps us prioritize what to work on next.

1.2.2 - Notebook Lens now counts a successful "Find" in the current cell toward its one-time review prompt, once per notebook. That prompt and the thank-you prompt after a purchase now offer "Feedback" between "Write a review" and "No thanks", as links in one row. "Feedback" opens a feature request form on GitHub that already names the plugin, its version and the IDE.
