Once a trial has run there, the same spot reads "Get Pro" and leads to the pricing page. While Pro is running, bought or on trial, the spot is empty. "Write a review" shows in every state and opens the reviews page of the listing. At a narrow editor the Pro text and the links move below the status line instead of crowding it, and a status line longer than the row shows its whole text as a tooltip. The trial notices and the review prompt now wait until the IDE has finished reading the license, so a licensed machine is never told at startup that its trial has ended.

1.2.0 - The Pro trial notices now end with a question and the support address. A key issued for another plugin no longer opens Notebook Lens Pro. A key for Notebook Lens itself is unaffected.

1.1.9 - Compare now offers the committed version. The Compare (Pro) button opens a short list, Another notebook or The committed version (from version control), and the second row reads what your version control last committed for the open notebook and diffs it against the file as it is now, sources only, without picking a second file. The diff names the revision in its title, and the copy it read from is removed when the dialog closes. The reading goes through the IDE's own version control, so the plugin runs no version control command and reads nothing off the network, and a notebook the IDE maps no version control over, one with no committed version yet, or a committed version that cannot be read says so in the status line. On the free side, ctrl+click an http or https address in an output, a traceback, a source string or a markdown cell to open it (cmd on a Mac), and the cell menu has Open link. An output the viewer cannot draw, a plotly figure or a widget, now shows a chip naming it ("not rendered - only text and images are shown") instead of nothing, and Copy Cell Output marks it as not copied while the exported page marks it as not exported; and a notebook holding a lone surrogate in an output now exports, where before the export stopped part way. The Pro trial notices now come a week before the trial ends and again on its last day, each saying what Pro adds, with a See pricing action to the marketplace pricing tab.

1.1.8 - Two new themes sit at the end of the Theme picker, lamplighter and catacombs, each behind a padlock until you earn it, and the open list says how beside the name: lamplighter "unlocks when you share Lens with a colleague", catacombs "unlocks the first time Pro runs for you". Sharing goes through the share card, under Help as Share Notebook Lens and opened as well when you pick the locked lamplighter entry. The card is a few lines of text for a colleague, the marketplace page and a referral code of your own among them; Copy share card earns the theme right there, and so does entering a code a colleague gave you. Catacombs is yours once Pro has run on your machine, trial or paid, and it stays after the trial ends. An earned theme is kept without Pro, in every Lens plugin, and comes back the next time you open a notebook; the other themes still taste free for the window and keep with Pro, as before.

1.1.7 - The export now goes through a sibling part file and is renamed into place once it is whole. Before this it wrote straight into the file you named, so cancelling an export that was replacing an earlier one deleted the earlier file too; now a cancel or a failure leaves it as it was. The HTML export, new since the last update, carries the notebook with its outputs and images in one page that opens offline, and it no longer re-reads a big image for every window it writes, which had made such a page slow to produce. Search across cells reads outputs as well now. It matches them as the notebook paints them, with the color codes of a traceback set aside, so a match that sits across a color change is found and the rows in the result list come out clean, and cancelling a search leaves the status line saying so with what it had found.

1.1.6 - A Pro trial started through a JetBrains account now ends when its 30 days do. The trial arrives as a signed key that stays valid after its last day, and the check read the signature alone, so a lapsed trial kept Pro open and was thanked as if it were a purchase. The trial's end date is read as well now; paid licenses and the perpetual fallback are not affected. Right-click a cell to copy its source, its output, or both. The whole cell goes on the clipboard, not just the lines the collapsed view shows, and an image output leaves a short note in its place.

1.1.5 - The Pro notebook diff now says why its table is empty. Two notebooks with the same cell sources used to leave a blank grid under the zero counters, which looked no different from a compare that had broken. The grid now reads that there are no differences, and a compare that failed or was cancelled says so in its place. Cancelling part-way also stops the compare cleanly instead of showing a diff cut short.

1.1.4 - The trial notices now say what the trial did. When a Pro trial is about to end, and again once it has ended, the notice opens with the number of exports and searches that ran while it was on, so the choice to subscribe rests on real use. The review request also waits longer: five useful moments instead of three.

1.1.3 - A Pro trial that is about to end says so once, with a link to pricing, and a trial that has ended says so once. Pro gate messages and the listing now say what is true: each Lens plugin has its own free 30-day trial.

1.1.2 - Notebook Lens now names the .ipynb file type. The project tree shows a notebook icon, Settings lists the type, and the marketplace can suggest the plugin when an IDE meets a notebook it cannot open. The notebook association is not taken over: where the IDE's own Jupyter support is installed, that support keeps the file and the Notebook Lens tab stays beside it as before.

1.1.1 - Four fixes. A saved theme comes back on open only while the license is active; without one the notebook opens in the default look. Exporting over the open notebook is refused with a plain message. The outline and the search results keep their selection across a reload. The review ask counts value moments by one rule: a load with cells, a search with hits and a first render once per file, every completed export, and never an empty compare.

1.1.0 - Themes: pick a look for the notebook from the toolbar. Eight strands shared across the Lens family (default, hacker, cyberpunk, goblincore, neon, nosferatu, halloween, blue lagoon) restyle the chrome around each cell: cell labels, execution counts and image chips take the strand's tints, odd cells take its stripe, and the outline's selection takes its color. Everything inside a cell stays as saved: syntax coloring, stderr, and every ANSI color in outputs and tracebacks keep their hues. The default look is unchanged. Any strand tastes free for the open window, and keeping one set is Pro.

1.0.2 - Compare now paints its result. The diff dialog was quietly modal, and dialogs of that kind hold their repaint runnables until they close, so the comparison rendered as an endless empty wait. It stays non-modal now, with a test pinning it that way.

1.0.1 - Clearer failure messages across the viewer: each one now says what happened and what to try. A truncated file names the byte where it ends and the likely cause, a broken or oversized image says why it is not rendered instead of loading forever, an unreadable file and an empty notebook are named plainly, and a failed export confirms no partial file was left behind. Pro subscribers get a one-time thank-you the first time their license is seen - recorded locally, nothing phones home. The footer's marketplace link now points at the real listing. The description now says outright what was always true: one plugin with no companion install, and a static render that cannot freeze on long outputs. The free tier is unchanged.

1.0.0 - First release. The free tier reads any notebook: streaming cell index, rendered markdown, Python coloring, outputs with ANSI tracebacks and inline images, an outline rail, typed navigation, exact go-to-cell, find in the current cell, and named errors for truncated or legacy files. Pro: source-only notebook diff with exact counts, export to .py (percent format) or Markdown, and search across all cells.

idea-plugin.name: DuckDB Lens: DuckDB Database File Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
DuckDB Lens opens DuckDB database files in the editor tab, straight off disk - read-only by design. The schema tree comes up first and rows page in as you scroll: opening and paging feel the same at 4 MB or 4 GB. No connection setup, no server, no paid IDE tier. It is a database browser for the file in front of you, and it never writes to that file.

The viewer is free and stays free. Pro is a subscription for this plugin: USD 2.90 a month or USD 29 a year for individual use. For organizations it is, per user, USD 5.80 a month or USD 58 a year.

.duckdb and .ddb open in a DuckDB Lens tab by extension; any other file that starts with the DuckDB magic bytes opens there too. A database file far beyond the IDE's large file limit opens the same way. Analysts and data engineers opening a DuckDB file see the schema and the rows without a connection or a notebook.

The free tier is permanent.

Free - the full DuckDB database viewer, for files of any size:

  • Never writes to your file: the connection opens in the engine's own read-only mode, so every INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or CREATE is refused by DuckDB itself; a byte-identity test in our suite pins the file unchanged after a full browse
  • Any size: rows arrive in constant-memory pages of up to 5000, and go-to-row jumps anywhere in the table
  • Schema tree: every schema's tables, views, sequences and indexes with instant estimated row counts and exact counts behind them - column types and primary keys at a glance
  • Find in table: Ctrl+F walks every column of every row, case folded, and reports the match position inside the cell; next and previous jump between hits
  • Cell inspector: the whole value behind a cell, long text in windows; BLOBs as hex or text, PNG, JPEG and GIF blobs as the picture
  • WAL-aware: a pending .wal sidecar is called out in a banner, in bytes, with a one-click snapshot reload that folds it into a copy and leaves the original alone
  • Exact types: BIGINT stays exact, HUGEINT and DECIMAL never pass through a double, BOOLEAN renders as true and false, and a LIST, STRUCT or MAP cell renders as the engine's own text for it
  • Database facts: storage version, block size, engine version, sidecar state
  • Copy out: row as JSON, page as CSV
  • Wrong file: something that is not a DuckDB database is reported by reason, in words, with no stack trace

The .duckdb files pile up: pipelines drop one per run, notebooks leave them behind, teammates share them instead of CSVs. Community-tier PyCharm and IntelliJ had no DuckDB database viewer of their own, so the files sat there as binary noise. Now they double-click. Every JetBrains IDE, 2024.2 or newer.

If another process is writing the database, that writer holds the lock; the plugin says so and opens a snapshot copy, and you browse the copy while the writer keeps running.

There is no web UI to fetch and no server to reach; the engine sits inside the plugin zip, so a laptop with no internet access opens a file the same way as one on the office network. The header check reads the storage version before the driver opens the file, and a version the bundled engine cannot read is refused with the file's version and the engine's range in the message. Wide tables scroll sideways, and every column is reachable.

Pro - optional paid tier, for querying and extracting:

  • SQL console: your SELECT or EXPLAIN goes to DuckDB untouched, no lint, one statement or a whole script run in order; results land in the same grid with the timing, and a statement that would write is refused
  • Export: write a table, search matches or any query result out to CSV or JSONL
  • Parquet out: name the export .parquet and DuckDB writes it itself, whole table or search matches, streamed; a click on the finished balloon opens it, in Parquet Lens if that is installed
  • Diff two databases: schema and rows compared between two files; exact added, removed and changed counts, drill-in to the rows, matched by primary key
  • Whole-table sort: order by any column across every row, not just the page a header click sorts

Each Lens plugin comes with its own free 30-day Pro trial. Keep a subscription running for a year and JetBrains' perpetual fallback license kicks in: the version you had when that year started is yours for good, fixes included. Pro only ever adds features.

Part of the Lens family - viewers built to hand off to each other. Queried a table down to the rows that matter? Export them as JSONL and open the result in JSONL Lens as a browsable, searchable grid. Parquet Lens reads columnar datasets, SQLite Lens reads SQLite files, and Log Lens reads multi-gigabyte logs the same way.

The guides and the overview of all eight viewers are at twilightventures.dev. Write to support@twilightventures.dev about anything to do with the plugin or a purchase, suggestions included; for a bug, name the version and the rough size of the file, or use the issue reporter at the end of the Help menu, which opens a prefilled new issue in your browser for you to read before you post.

Nothing leaves the machine: no network calls, no credentials handled, and the Pro check is the IDE's own JetBrains licensing. Builds ship for Linux x64, Windows x64 and macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon); Linux ARM is not in this build.

Where it stops:

  • Viewer by design: rows are never rewritten. A write mode does not exist here, hidden or paid.
  • Tables without a usable primary key diff as counts only, and the report says so.
  • Rows still in the .wal appear after the one-click snapshot reload, never silently.

Inside the zip sits the official DuckDB JDBC engine, MIT licensed, minus its Linux ARM native. DuckDB and the DuckDB logo are trademarks of the DuckDB Foundation; this is an independent product, not affiliated with or endorsed by the DuckDB Foundation.

A short review on the marketplace page tells us which of these features people lean on, and steers what we build next.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.3.5 - read_parquet('orders.parquet') in a view now reads the file beside the database. Before, the viewer looked in the IDE's own folder and reported that the file could not be read. A view whose files never answer, a network share that stopped responding for one, used to hold the tab; now, after 15 seconds, its definition and the line "the files it reads gave no answer within 15 seconds" take the place of the grid, and every other table and view stays browsable. A view's row count is read when the view opens, so the status line shows the total instead of "(view)", and the Info tab shows the definition of the view you picked.

1.3.4 - The trial notices "DuckDB Lens Pro trial ends in ..." and "DuckDB Lens Pro trial has ended" now end with the price, "Pro is USD 2.90 a month or USD 29 a year for individual use", and a "See pricing" button that opens the marketplace page. A query result in the console can now be exported, the Pro action the listing names; it had no menu entry before. During a trial you may see one request for a marketplace review, with "Write a review", "Feedback" and "No thanks".

1.3.3 - Dates and times now read as the engine writes them: a spring-forward gap hour no longer reads an hour late, a BC date no longer reads as AD, an infinity reads as infinity, and a TIME of 24:00:00 no longer makes the whole table unreadable, in the grid, in copy, in the diff and in the CSV and JSONL exports. Numbers and DATE, TIMESTAMP and TIME columns show in the IDE's own format, which follows your system's regional settings, with the stored value in the tooltip ("Stored as 1234.50 (DECIMAL(10,2))."); an English IDE keeps the ISO dates and plain numbers it always showed, and copy, export and the inspector keep the stored text. A header click sorts the loaded page the way your language orders text, so an English page reads apple, Apple, Banana where 1.3.2 read Apple, Banana, apple, and Find ignores case in any language (ß finds SS, İ finds i) and full-width forms. Find also matches a number or a date typed the way the grid shows it, such as 1234,50 or 03.10.2026 in a German IDE. A database that only points at files elsewhere now opens: each view shows its rows, or, when its files are missing, what it reads and why in place of the grid, and every other table and view stays browsable. DECIMAL and HUGEINT cells align right like every other number, and a column dragged to a new place keeps its own sort and inspector. With more than a week of a Pro trial left, the first Pro action is named once. The trial-ending notices lead with what Pro did (SQL queries, exports, whole-table sorts and diffs), and the footer's Pro trial line counts the Pro actions used. The footer offers nothing until the IDE has loaded the license, and a tab opened before then fills in its footer once the license is known.

1.3.2 - DuckDB Lens now saves the one-time review prompt for a later sitting when a trial notice is due as a table's first rows load. The trial notices and the review prompt now wait until the IDE has finished reading the license, so a licensed machine is never told at startup that its trial has ended. A thank-you prompt no longer follows a trial notice in the same sitting. The one-time review prompt and the thank-you prompt after a purchase now offer "Feedback" between "Write a review" and "No thanks".

1.3.1 - Two links now sit in the DuckDB Lens footer. "Try Pro free for 30 days" shows on a machine where the trial has not run and opens the IDE license dialog, where the trial starts. Once a trial has run there, the same spot reads "Get Pro" and leads to the pricing page. While Pro is running, bought or on trial, the spot is empty. "Write a review" shows in every state and opens the reviews page of the listing. Nothing else changed.

1.3.0 - Drilling into a row now checks the license each time. The Pro trial notices now end with a question and the support address. A key issued for another plugin no longer opens DuckDB Lens Pro. A key for DuckDB Lens itself is unaffected. After a purchase, a balloon says thank you once on this machine. Its one action is "Write a review".

1.2.9 - The notice that a Pro trial is ending now comes a week before the last day instead of three days, and a second notice comes on the last day itself. Both notices name what Pro adds in this plugin, a SQL console, CSV, JSONL and Parquet export, whole-table sort and two-file diff, and say that Pro features stay on until the trial ends and the free tier stays after. Each carries one button, See pricing, which opens the pricing tab of the marketplace page. The notice for a trial that has already ended reads the same way, with Pro features paused. The Pro line in the footer now names the Parquet export as well; it had been left out. Nothing else in the viewer changed.

1.2.8 - A database that opens to an empty tree, nothing in it yet, no longer counts as an open toward the one review ask. It used to, and the file stayed spent, so a later open of the same database, once it held something, did not count either. The ask still waits for five moments of use and appears once, and No thanks is for good.

1.2.7 - The engine inside this plugin used to fetch extensions on its own. Type a query that names a function from one it does not carry, st_point say, and DuckDB would download that extension from the internet before answering. Every connection now opens with extension auto-install and auto-load switched off, so the engine fetches nothing and that query fails with DuckDB's own catalog error instead. An INSTALL you type into the Pro SQL console yourself is still your own call. In the console, Explain over a selection of several statements now plans each one, headed "-- statement 2 (line 3)" with its number and the line it starts on; before this the whole selection went under one EXPLAIN, which planned the first statement and ran the second. When a script of several statements stops, the failing one names its line as well: "Statement 2 of 4 (line 7) stopped the run, so nothing after it ran."

1.2.6 - The Theme picker has two more entries at the end. One is called lamplighter, the other catacombs. Both show a padlock, and in the open list each carries its own line: "unlocks when you share Lens with a colleague" for lamplighter, "unlocks the first time Pro runs for you" for catacombs. Pick a locked one and the plugin opens the way to earn it. For lamplighter that is the share card, which is also under Help as Share DuckDB Lens. The card is plain text for a colleague: where to find the plugin on the marketplace and the family page beside it, then a referral code of this install's own with the line "enter it under Theme in any Lens plugin" under it. Copy share card earns the theme here; the note under the button says "Copied. The lamplighter theme is yours to keep." A colleague who types that code into the same dialog and presses Unlock with code earns it on their side. A typo is refused ("codes read LENS-XXX-XXX-XXX"), and so is an install's own code. Catacombs opens the first time Pro runs for you. A trial counts, and the theme stays after the trial ends. An earned theme is kept, not tasted; the notice that appears says "It stays yours in every Lens plugin, Pro or not. Pick it under Theme." The code itself is random and minted once. It stays on this machine; nothing is sent anywhere.

1.2.5 - Before DuckDB 2.0 lands we measured the engine inside this plugin. It is DuckDB v1.5.5 and it reads storage versions 64 to 68. A file outside that range used to fall through to the generic "could not be opened" line. Now the version is taken from the file header before the engine gets the path, and the status line says "was written by DuckDB storage version 69; this viewer's engine (DuckDB v1.5.5) reads up to 68". The fix follows in the same line: SET storage_compatibility_version to v1.5.0 or earlier in that newer DuckDB and COPY FROM DATABASE into a new file. An old file, from before version 64, is told to EXPORT DATABASE instead. The header checksum is checked as well, so a damaged file is called damaged, and an encrypted database now reads "is encrypted, and this viewer opens files without a key" rather than being taken for a wrong file. Two leaves in the schema tree answer a click now. An index shows whether it is unique and which columns it covers, and its CREATE statement sits under that. A sequence shows the value nextval hands out next as "Next value", then its increment and its range, with a line for a sequence that cycles. In the diff, the changed-rows drill marks the cells that differ between the stacked A and B rows and reports it, "3 changed cells marked across 2 rows", while Next changed cell walks them; a new comparison clears the rows of the old one. Row counts also fill in for tables outside main now.

1.2.4 - A trial started with a JetBrains account arrives in the IDE as a signed key, with the trial's last day written inside it. We were checking the signature and nothing else, and a signature does not expire, so on day 31 the trial went on opening Pro, the footer thanked the person as if they had bought it, and the ended notice never showed. The date inside the key is read now. A paid license, and the fallback license JetBrains grants after a year, behave as they did. The console takes a script too: type SELECT count(*) FROM orders; SELECT * FROM orders LIMIT 5 and both run, in that order, each timed on its own, with the status line reading "2 statements in 9 ms • statement 2: 5 rows in 4 ms (first row 1 ms)". A statement that fails halts the rest: "Statement 2 of 3 stopped the run, so nothing after it ran." Semicolons inside quotes or comments stay where they are, the text goes to DuckDB as typed, and Explain plans whichever statement the caret is on.

1.2.3 - When a statement fails in the console, the status line now says what went wrong and what to try, and it does the same when a file will not open or an export stops early. The engine's own message is still there, in the tooltip of that line or in the line itself. Until now every failed statement showed the driver's line "Attempting to execute an unsuccessful or closed pending query result" in place of the real error, so a typo in a table name read as an internal fault; a missing table or column is now named outright.

1.2.2 - The trial notices now say what the trial did: how many exports and how many searches ran while it was on, as in "This trial: 12 exports, 40 searches." The one review ask waits for five value moments instead of three, since a single open already counts for three. The listing text was tightened, with prices and trial terms left as they were.

1.2.1 - A Pro trial that is about to end says so once, with a link to pricing, and a trial that has ended says so once. Licensed users now get the thank-you and the Supporter line in the footer, and the family link stays visible. Opening a database now counts toward the review ask. Pro gate messages and the listing now say what is true: each Lens plugin has its own free 30-day trial.

1.2.0 - Export to Parquet. Pick a .parquet name in the export dialog and the engine writes the file itself, the whole table or the search matches, streamed, with the same refusal to write over the open database. When the export finishes, one click opens the file in the IDE, so it lands in Parquet Lens when that is installed.

1.1.1 - A saved theme comes back on open only while the license is active; without one the grid opens in the default look, and tasting any theme stays free for the window. Going back to Default no longer counts as a chosen theme. Export refuses to write over the file that is open (the database, its snapshot or its .wal) and asks for another name instead of failing.

1.1.0 - Themes: pick a look for the whole tab from the toolbar. Eight strands shared across the Lens family (default, hacker, cyberpunk, goblincore, neon, nosferatu, halloween, blue lagoon) restyle the data grid, console results and diff drill-in with text, number and blob tints, row striping and selection; the default look is unchanged and NULL stays quietly dimmed in every strand. Any strand tastes free for the open window, and keeping one set is Pro.

1.0.5 - Reloading the page used to drop the selected row and cell; they stay put now, through a page reload and a reload from disk. The same row is found again by its key when the same page comes back, by position otherwise. The one review ask also counts its moments by one rule now: a load with rows, a search with hits and a grid with columns count once per opened file, every finished export counts, and a failure, a cancel or an empty result never does.

1.0.4 - At narrow windows the footer used to print the status text on top of the Pro line; now the Pro line drops to its own row on the right when the two no longer fit, and rejoins the row when there is room again.

1.0.3 - Two diff repairs ride this patch. Drill-in row fetches now key off the declared primary key, so Show rows works on keyed tables it used to fail on: the grid pages those tables by rowid while the diff keys them by primary key, and the old fetch trusted the grid. A finished comparison now survives the editor view rebuilding instead of coming back empty, and the drill controls say what they need, a diff or a selected row, instead of doing nothing.

1.0.2 - The toolbar keeps its buttons. Sort, Export and Reload used to fall off the right edge at ordinary window widths; the toolbar now wraps to a second row instead of clipping, and the same fix covers the diff view controls.

1.0.1 - Housekeeping release. The editor no longer volunteers for SQLite extensions (.sqlite, .sqlite3, .db3) left over from the family template: DuckDB Lens now claims .duckdb and .ddb plus magic-detected files, exactly as the listing says. Marketplace links inside the plugin point at the DuckDB Lens page instead of a sibling's.

1.0.0 - First release. Free: a read-only viewer for .duckdb files - every schema in the tree, constant-memory paged grid, streaming case-insensitive Find, a cell inspector with image preview, a .wal banner with one-click snapshot reload, and HUGEINT, DECIMAL and BOOLEAN rendered exactly. Pro: read-only SQL console with EXPLAIN, CSV and JSONL export, two-file diff with exact counts, whole-table sort.

idea-plugin.name: Parquet, Avro & ORC Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
Open Parquet, Avro and ORC files straight in the editor, as a table. Double-click the file. No server, no export, no configuration.

It was written against the things people actually complain about in other viewers:

  • No 1,000-row or 10,000-row limit. Rows are read in pages, so the whole file is reachable and a ten-million-row file opens as fast as a small one.
  • Lists, maps and structs stay readable. No unnamed collection columns, and no java.nio.HeapByteBuffer[pos=0 lim=3 cap=3] where a value should be: binary columns are decoded to text.
  • It does not freeze the IDE. The file is read off the UI thread, so the editor stays usable while a large file loads.
  • It does not take the file hostage. The table opens first, but the IDE's own editor is still there, one tab away, exactly as before you installed this.
  • Cells can be edited. Change a value in the table and the Parquet file is rewritten atomically: on a 35 MB, 2,000,000-row file one edit takes about 1.8 seconds, and the row count does not move. Two things to know before you use it: the write happens immediately, with no separate save step, and Undo steps back through your changes one at a time, restoring the exact previous value. Nested columns stay read-only, and Avro and ORC are read-only too, because those formats can be read but not written back. Announced in advance: editing will become a paid feature in an upcoming release, with a 7-day trial. Reading, browsing, paging, nested columns and format detection stay free permanently, and whatever you have installed keeps working exactly as it does today.
  • It keeps working after IDE upgrades. No upper version bound.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 2026.1.2 — editing a Parquet cell no longer rewrites the whole file: only the row group holding the cell is rebuilt and added at the end of the file. One cell in a 1 billion row, 29 GB file takes about 1.7 seconds instead of minutes. If the IDE closes halfway, the file is restored exactly as it was the next time you open it. When this is not safe (one big row group, types DuckDB can't write back identically) or too much unused space has built up, the whole file is rewritten as before.
  • 2026.1.1 — fixed: on IntelliJ-based IDEs 2024.3 and 2025.1 the licence dialog and "Export as CSV" could fail with a missing-method error. Verified with the JetBrains Plugin Verifier on 2024.3 and 2025.1.
  • 0.2.0 — new: filter rows with a SQL condition, sort by clicking a column header (over the whole file, not the page), jump straight to a row number, and export the rows you are looking at as CSV. Columns size themselves to their content, long values show in full on hover, Ctrl/Cmd+F jumps to the filter box, and a Reload button re-reads the file if something else changed it. Reading, paging, nested columns and format detection stay free and always will; editing cells now needs a licence, with a 7-day trial.
  • 0.1.1 — edit cells and write the file back, with Undo; Avro and ORC extensions are fetched automatically on first use; the default editor is no longer hidden, and the file is no longer forced read-only.
  • 0.1.0 — first release: Parquet, Avro and ORC as a paged table.

idea-plugin.name: Heap Dump Lens: JVM Heap Dump, Thread Dump & GC Log Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
Heap Dump Lens opens JVM heap dumps in the editor tab - the .hprof file a crashed or bloated JVM leaves behind. The class histogram comes up first: every class with its instance count and bytes, built by a streaming single pass that indexes a multi gigabyte dump in seconds inside a fixed memory budget. It is the memory analyzer that lives in the IDE, with nothing separate to install and no paid IDE tier required. Thread dumps and GC logs open the same way, parsed, so the three files an incident produces read in one place.

The viewer is free and stays free. Pro is a subscription for this plugin: USD 4.90 a month or USD 49 a year for individual use. For organizations it is, per user, USD 9.80 a month or USD 98 a year.

Every .hprof file opens in a Heap Dump Lens tab, and so does any file that starts with the JAVA PROFILE magic bytes, whatever its extension. An hprof file far beyond the IDE's large file limit opens the same way. Backend and performance engineers reading a heap dump start from the class histogram, and Pro's retained-size ranking points at the leak.

Pro computes the dominator tree over the whole object graph, and the Retained tab ranks the top 500 retainers by their retained bytes. A memory leak hunt starts from that ranking.

The free tier is permanent.

Free - heap dump triage, thread dumps and GC logs:

  • Class histogram: every class in the dump with instance count and shallow bytes, sortable and filterable, resolved to real class names
  • Any size: one streaming pass with bounded memory - our suite pins a 2.6 GB dump indexed in seconds inside a 512 MB cap, twenty million objects walked
  • Compressed dumps: a .hprof.gz file opens like a plain dump. The plugin inflates it into its own work directory first, shows the progress, and cleans the copy up when the tab closes
  • Dump facts: object count, loaded classes, GC roots, format and id width, total heap bytes
  • Thread dump viewer: .tdump files open parsed - threads with state, daemon flag and stack frames, a state breakdown up top, jstack output welcome through Tools | Open Thread Dump
  • GC logs: unified -Xlog:gc* logs parsed into pause events with heap before and after, per-pause duration, max and total pause time (Tools | Open GC Log)
  • Not a dump: a file that is not an hprof dump reports a clear named reason, never a stack trace

Per-object state goes to a disk-backed index in a work directory, and what stays in memory scales with the number of classes and strings rather than objects; that is what keeps the 2.6 GB dump above inside its 512 MB cap, and the directory is removed when the tab closes. The Retained tab and the Export button are the only places that look for a license, and they ask through the IDE's own plugin license dialog at the moment you use one. The descriptor carries no upper IDE build.

A heap dump usually arrives after the fact: a container was killed for memory overnight, and an hprof file is what is left of it. It opens here with a double click, Community editions included, on every JetBrains IDE from 2024.2.

Pro - optional paid tier, for finding what holds the memory and taking the tables out:

  • Export: the Export button beside the Theme picker writes the histogram, a filter's matches or the top retainers out to CSV; the histogram itself and copying rows out of it stay free
  • Retained sizes: compute the dominator tree over the whole object graph to find what each object would free if it were gone
  • Top retainers: rank objects by the bytes they dominate; each row shows retained and shallow bytes side by side
  • On the same 2.6 GB dump: thirty million references extracted and dominators computed over twenty million objects in under half a minute

Each Lens plugin comes with its own free 30-day Pro trial. Keep a subscription running for a year and JetBrains' perpetual fallback license kicks in: the version you had when that year started is yours for good, fixes included. Pro only ever adds features.

Part of the Lens family - viewers built to hand off to each other. JSONL Lens opens JSON Lines files as a browsable grid, Log Lens reads multi-gigabyte logs, Parquet Lens reads columnar datasets, SQLite Lens and DuckDB Lens browse database files read-only, XLSX Lens opens Excel workbooks, and Notebook Lens renders Jupyter notebooks.

The guides and the overview of all eight viewers are at twilightventures.dev. Write to support@twilightventures.dev about anything to do with the plugin or a purchase, suggestions included; for a bug, name the version and the rough size of the file, or use the issue reporter at the end of the Help menu, which opens a prefilled new issue in your browser for you to read before you post.

Runs entirely locally. The plugin makes no network calls and never handles credentials. Pro licensing is handled by the IDE's own JetBrains licensing system.

What it does not do:

  • Viewer by design: it reads the dump without rewriting it, and it does not attach to a live process.
  • JFR recordings are out of scope; this plugin is about the files a JVM leaves behind, not flight recording.
  • There is no automated leak-suspect story: you get the dominator numbers and read them yourself.
  • Thread dump parsing covers HotSpot output. A GC line the unified-log parser does not recognize stays out of the totals.

If Heap Dump Lens helps you, leave a short review - it helps us prioritize what to work on next.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.4.5 - Compute retained sizes no longer slows with the square of a linked list's length: a 54,000-entry LinkedList ran 19 minutes without finishing before, and a 200,000-node list now computes within ten seconds in our test. The run has a progress bar and a Cancel; a cancelled run hands the "Compute retained sizes" button back. The histogram's byte column is now "Shallow bytes". When one primitive array class holds most of the heap, a line above the grid says so, with the share, and points at the Retained tab. The header counts loaded classes and classes with instances. The JVM's own threads read "VM internal". A class whose statics hold the memory shows as "class com.example.Cache (static fields)" in the top retainers. The trial notices "Heap Dump Lens Pro trial ends in ..." and "Heap Dump Lens Pro trial has ended" end with the price, "Pro is USD 4.90 a month or USD 49 a year for individual use", and a "See pricing" button. During a trial you may see one request for a marketplace review, with "Write a review", "Feedback" and "No thanks".

1.4.4 - A Pro trial now counts the work Pro did: each "Compute retained sizes" run that ranked something, each CSV export of the class histogram, and each export of the top retainers. The first Pro action of a trial is named once in a short notice, such as "That retained-size run was Pro.", followed by how many days the trial has left and what stays free; it comes only while more than a week of the trial is left. The footer's "Pro trial:" line adds the count of Pro actions after the days left, and the notices about the trial ending open with a "This trial:" line that names them. Filtering the histogram is free, so it no longer counts. At IDE start the footer's Pro line and its Try Pro or Get Pro link stay empty until the IDE has read the license, where before they could offer Pro to someone who already had it; both fill in within about two seconds of the license being read.

1.4.3 - Fixes to "Export" and to "Compute retained sizes", both Pro. Exporting over a file that already exists no longer loses that file when the export stops early (a cancel, a failed write, a second export started before the first is done, the tab closed mid-export): the rows go to a part file beside it and replace it only when the run is complete, so the file keeps its mode, owner and group, and through a symbolic link the rows land in the file the link names. Where no part file can be made beside the file, the rows are written into the file itself, as before. Part files left behind by a killed IDE are removed at the next export to that file. "Compute retained sizes" runs once per dump tab: a second click used to start a second computation beside the first, over the same index on disk, so the ranking on screen could come from a run that was not finished. Once a computation starts, the button stays disabled until you close the tab and open the dump again, which is also the way to retry after a failure. If the computation runs out of memory, the "Retained" tab now says so and suggests raising the IDE heap size, where it used to keep offering the button.

1.4.2 - Heap Dump Lens no longer tells a licensed machine at startup that its trial has ended. A thank-you prompt no longer follows a trial notice in the same sitting. The one-time review prompt and the thank-you prompt after a purchase now offer "Feedback" between "Write a review" and "No thanks", as links in one row. "Feedback" opens a feature request form on GitHub with the plugin name, version and IDE filled in for you.

1.4.1 - The one-time review ask now counts the rest of an incident: a heap dump on screen counts, and so does a thread dump read with threads in it or a GC log read with pauses in it, where a second heap dump used to be needed. A file that will not parse, or one with nothing in it, counts for nothing, and the same thread dump or GC log read twice in one IDE session counts once. Two links now sit in the footer beside the Pro line. "Try Pro free for 30 days" shows on a machine where the trial has not run and opens the IDE license dialog, where the trial starts. Once a trial has run there, the same spot reads "Get Pro" and opens the pricing page. While Pro is running, bought or on trial, the spot is empty. "Write a review" shows in every state and opens the reviews page of the listing. Nothing else changed.

1.4.0 - The Pro trial notices now end with a question and the support address. A key issued for another plugin no longer opens Heap Dump Lens Pro. A key for Heap Dump Lens itself is unaffected.

1.3.0 - Export in the toolbar writes a table to a CSV file, a Pro feature. The popup under the button lists what the tab holds: the whole class histogram, the rows a filter has matched, and the top retainers ranking once it has been computed. The histogram file follows the grid's sort with the filter set aside, and the other two files hold their rows as the grid shows them; the first line of every file names its columns (class, instances, shallow_bytes for the two histogram files; rank, class, retained_bytes, shallow_bytes, object_id for the top retainers ranking). The dump itself is never accepted as the destination, and a cancelled or failed run leaves no partial file behind. The balloon at the end offers to open the file. The histogram on screen, and copying rows out of it, stay free. A Pro trial in its last week now says so once, and once more with a day left; each notice names what Pro adds, and its See pricing action opens the pricing tab of the marketplace page. The one-time review ask now also counts a sorted histogram and the top retainers ranking once computed, not only a dump opened and a filter that kept rows.

1.2.7 - A dump that ends early now says "the file is truncated". A heap dump the JVM never finished writing, or a copy that stopped part way, used to fail with "Could not read the dump: null" or a bare byte offset. The reader now names the byte the file ends at and the record it ends in, and a record that claims more bytes than the file holds is refused before anything reads past the end. A file that is not a dump at all still says so.

1.2.6 - Two new themes in the Theme picker, lamplighter and catacombs. They sit after the eight with a padlock and a hint until earned: lamplighter "unlocks when you share Lens with a colleague", catacombs "unlocks the first time Pro runs for you". Share Heap Dump Lens, new in the Help menu, shows a card with the marketplace page and your referral code; copying the card, or entering a code a colleague gave you, unlocks lamplighter. Catacombs comes with the first Pro run, a trial counts, and it stays after the trial ends. A theme earned this way is kept without Pro, here and in every Lens plugin. Picking a locked entry opens its unlock path instead of applying it. Thread dumps and GC logs read the saved theme under the same rule now.

1.2.5 - Two fixes, one for a dump still indexing and one for a dump that could not be read. A class name typed into the filter while a large dump was still indexing was dropped when the histogram landed: the grid showed every class under a filled field until the next keystroke, and the rows now arrive already filtered. And a dump that could not be read no longer offers to compute retained sizes. That tab used to keep its button, and pressing it wrote "still indexing" into the header of a dump that had already failed; it now carries the reason the dump would not open.

1.2.4 - A trial key that has run out no longer opens Pro. Trials from the JetBrains account arrive as signed keys, the same shape as a paid license, with the trial's last day inside; the signature alone was checked, and a signature holds for years, so retained sizes, the saved theme, the Supporter footer line and the thank-you meant for buyers all stayed on a lapsed trial while the trial-ended notice never showed. The last day inside the key decides now, and the day after it retained sizes ask for a license again, the tables open in the default look, the ended notice shows once, and the histogram, thread dumps and GC logs carry on free. Paid keys and the perpetual fallback license read as before.

1.2.3 - An empty table says why it is empty. A dump still indexing, a dump that could not be read, a dump with no classes in it and a filter that matched nothing each read differently, and the retained ranking, the thread table and the GC log table say so when they have nothing to show. Every one of them used to open on a blank grid that looked like a broken view.

1.2.2 - The trial notices now say what the trial did. A trial that is about to end, or has just ended, opens with the number of searches that found something while Pro was on; a typed query counts once, not once per keystroke, and with nothing counted the notice starts on its own words. The one-time review ask waits for five value moments now instead of three, so it comes after real use.

1.2.1 - A Pro trial that is about to end says so once, with a link to pricing, and a trial that has ended says so once. Licensed users now get the thank-you and the Supporter line in the footer, and the family link stays visible. Pro gate messages and the listing now say what is true: each Lens plugin has its own free 30-day trial.

1.2.0 - .hprof.gz files open. The plugin inflates the archive into its own work directory, then indexes the result the way it indexes a plain dump. The copy goes when the tab closes, and the startup sweep from 1.1.2 catches it if the IDE dies first. A cut-off or damaged archive is reported by name. Opening is free, as before.

1.1.2 - Work directories left behind by an IDE that died mid-analysis are cleaned up. Each dump's work directory now carries its owner's process id, and on startup the plugin removes the ones whose owner is gone, plus unmarked ones older than a day. Nothing in use is touched.

1.1.1 - Three fixes. A saved theme comes back on open only while the license is active; without one the tables open in the default look. An empty dump no longer counts toward the one-time review ask. The histogram filter and the retained tab keep the selected row when it is still shown.

1.1.0 - Themes: pick a look for the whole tab from the toolbar. Eight strands shared across the Lens family (default, hacker, cyberpunk, goblincore, neon, nosferatu, halloween, blue lagoon) restyle the class histogram, the retained table, thread dumps and GC log pauses: instance counts and byte figures take the number tint, class and thread names the text tint, object ids and the heap before and after figure the structure tint, with row striping and the selection color from the strand. Thread states and the daemon flag keep the platform's own look, and the default look is unchanged. Any strand tastes free for the open window, and keeping one set is Pro.

1.0.1 - Picking a thread dump or GC log through the Tools menu could open an empty view. Both actions read straight from disk now, and the plugin marketplace links point at the live listing.

1.0.0 - First release. The free tier opens .hprof heap dumps of any size into a streaming class histogram (a 2.6 GB dump indexes in seconds on a fixed memory budget), shows the dump summary with GC roots, parses thread dumps into a state breakdown, and reads unified GC logs as pause tables. Pro computes dominator tree retained sizes and ranks the top retainers across the whole object graph.

idea-plugin.name: DocViewKit Omni
idea-plugin.description:
Preview Office, PDF, OFD, OpenDocument, and iWork files without leaving your JetBrains IDE. Documents stay on your device or IDE-managed remote workspace—no uploads and no conversion server.

Open a document

Open a supported file normally. DocViewKit Omni renders it in a read-only editor with navigation, zoom, search, text selection, safe hyperlinks, and interaction modes where supported.

Why DocViewKit Omni?

  • Documents stay private: parsing, rendering, and search run locally. The plugin does not upload documents or send file names and paths to a remote service.
  • No conversion server: preview files without a document-conversion backend.
  • Broad format support, free: view modern and legacy Office, PDF, OFD, OpenDocument, Apple iWork, WPS Office, XPS, RTF, and CSV files.
  • Fast and lightweight: format components load on demand for faster startup and lower resource use.
  • Safe, read-only viewing: active document content is not executed, and isolated resource failures do not unnecessarily hide the rest of the document.
  • IDE-native behavior: files load through IntelliJ Platform APIs, refresh when changed, and follow the IDE theme and language.

Supported formats

DOCX, DOCM, DOTX, DOTM, DOC, RTF, WPS; XLSX, XLSM, XLTX, XLTM, XLS, CSV, ET; PPTX, PPTM, PPSX, PPSM, POTX, POTM, PPT, DPS; ODT, OTT, FODT, ODS, OTS, FODS, ODP, OTP, FODP; Pages, Numbers, Keynote; PDF, OFD, XPS, and OXPS.

OFD preview

Preview OFD 1.0 and 1.1 fixed-layout documents (.ofd) locally in a read-only editor, without uploading them or using a conversion server. Open an OFD file normally to view its document content and page layout. Rendering covers the supported subset of OFD; the plugin does not provide trusted digital-signature validation.

idea-plugin.name: Tables - SQLite Database Editor
idea-plugin.description:
Open a SQLite database file and see what is in it.

Tables opens a .db, .sqlite, .sqlite3 or .db3 file straight from the Project view, in an editor tab. There is no connection to configure, no driver to download and no data source to set up first.

The schema comes up first. Every table, view, index and trigger in the file, with each column's declared type, its primary key and whether it is nullable. The tables SQLite and its extensions create for their own bookkeeping are kept, because they are real, and folded away behind one node, because they are not what you opened the file to see.

There is no row limit. Rows are read a page at a time from the part of the table you are looking at, so the memory used is the same for a table of a thousand rows and a table of a hundred million. The row count on the status line is a real count(*), not an estimate.

It reads the write-ahead log. A database another program is still writing to is the ordinary case, not the exception, and a reader that ignores the write-ahead log shows you the file as it was at the last checkpoint while telling you it is current. Tables reads the log. On the one occasion it cannot, because the folder itself is read only, it says so on the status line rather than quietly showing you fewer rows than you have.

It edits, which is the point. Change a cell and press Ctrl+S, or File then Save All, and the value goes into the file. The tab carries the usual unsaved marker, Ctrl+Z is the IDE's own undo with the column named in the Edit menu, and closing a tab with unsaved changes asks first. Everything is written in one transaction, so a save either lands completely or not at all.

Rows are added and removed, not only changed. Add Row puts an empty row at the end of the table and you type into it like any other. A column you leave alone is left out of the insert altogether, so its own DEFAULT applies and an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY gets the id SQLite assigns rather than a NULL: the grid says which of those three each untouched cell is going to do, before you save. Delete Rows marks the selected rows and leaves them on screen, struck through, until you save, so Ctrl+Z puts them back where you were looking. Both are on the grid's right click menu.

A row that has to have a value says so before the save, not during it. Leave a NOT NULL column with no default empty and the status line names the column and the row, and the save does not start. The alternative is what SQLite would tell you: a constraint error at the end of a write, about a row you then have to go and find.

It refuses what will not fit, and says why. SQLite would accept the word "hello" in a column declared INTEGER and keep it there for ever, with no error and nothing to undo. Tables refuses it instead and names the column and the type it was declared as. It never converts a value to make it fit, because a wrong number that reports success is worse than a refusal.

It will not overwrite work another program did while you were reading. Every change is written with the row's identity and the value the cell held when you looked at it, both in the same statement. A removal carries the whole row rather than only its identity, because SQLite hands a row id out again once the row holding it has gone. If anything moved underneath, the save is refused and says so, and your changes stay where they are. A plugin that opens files other programs own has to do this, and the alternative is silently replacing somebody's data.

Four kinds of nothing, told apart. A NULL, an empty string, a BLOB and a cell that has not finished loading all render as blank in an ordinary table. Here a NULL says NULL, an empty string is empty, a BLOB says how many bytes it holds, and a cell still being read shows an ellipsis.

The cell inspector, for everything a grid row is too small for. A row of a table is one line tall and a database cell is not. Open the inspector and the selected cell is shown at full size underneath the grid: a whole JSON document, a stack trace, a description somebody pasted in, with the newlines where they belong. Edit it there and it becomes the same pending change typing into the grid would, with the same rules and the same undo.

Binary is shown as binary, and it can be changed. A BLOB is a hex dump with its bytes and their printable characters side by side, and Tables says what the bytes look like: a PNG, a JPEG, a PDF, a ZIP, another SQLite database, or plainly that it does not recognise them. Bytes that are really UTF-8 text can be read as text with one click. Write the cell out to a file, or replace it with the contents of one, and the change is pending until you save like every other.

Go to a row by number. Type 4,000,000 and you are at row 4,000,000, in a table nothing has read past the first few hundred rows of, with the row in the middle of the view rather than scraping the bottom of it.

Reload from disk. The usual reason a database is open in an IDE is that another program owns it. Reload reads the file again, its tables as well as its rows, so a migration that ran while you were looking shows up without closing the tab. If you have unsaved changes it asks first, rather than choosing for you.

Columns are sized from what is in them. Width comes from the values rather than from the column names, with a ceiling, so an identifier is readable, a table forty columns wide scrolls sideways instead of squeezing, and one enormous text column cannot push everything else off the screen.

Works everywhere JetBrains does. Tables depends only on the platform, so it installs in IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, PhpStorm, GoLand, Rider, RubyMine, CLion, DataGrip, RustRover and Android Studio, Community editions included. Database Tools and SQL is not needed and is not used.

Pricing, stated plainly

  • $29 per year for a personal licence.
  • $69 per year for a commercial licence.
  • 30-day free trial with everything unlocked. No feature is held back during the trial.
  • There is no free tier. After the trial, Tables needs a licence. Saying so here rather than letting you find out later is the whole point.

Known limits, stated up front

  • A removal compares a very large cell by its type and its length rather than byte for byte. Anything over about four thousand characters or bytes, which is where copying the value once per selected row would start costing real memory. Another program replacing such a value with a different one of exactly the same length, between your reading the row and your saving, is the one change a removal does not notice. Everything smaller is compared exactly.
  • Undo stops at a save that added or removed a row. That save renumbers every row after it, so the grid is read again from the file rather than patched, and an undo aimed at the old numbering says so instead of quietly changing the wrong row.
  • Structural changes are rows, not schema. Creating, renaming or dropping a table or a column is not offered. Rows are added and removed; the shape of the table is left to whatever wrote it.
  • Binary is replaced from a file rather than typed. The cell inspector shows a BLOB as a hex dump and can write it out to a file or read one back in, and it does not offer to let you type hex into it. A cell takes a file of up to 64 MB.
  • A strict table is edited by the same rules as an ordinary one. SQLite's STRICT tables enforce their column types themselves, so a value this plugin accepts can still be refused by SQLite when you save. Nothing is written when that happens and the message says what SQLite said.
  • Some things cannot be edited and say so when you try: a view, which is calculated rather than stored; a virtual table such as a full text index; a column SQLite generates from the others; a table with neither a rowid nor a primary key, where no single row can be named; and a file that is read only on disk. Rows are not added to those tables either, even where SQLite would allow it, because a row that could never afterwards be corrected is not worth adding.
  • Clearing a cell gives the empty string, not NULL. They are different values and this plugin does not confuse them, so NULL has an action of its own, on Delete.
  • Jumping to a row far down a very large table takes a moment, because SQLite reaches a row by stepping over the rows before it. Scrolling is not affected.
  • Only local files. A database on a remote file system or inside an archive is not opened.
  • Encrypted databases are not opened. SQLCipher and similar are a different file format, and a plugin that cannot read one should say so rather than report it as corrupt.
  • Updating the plugin needs an IDE restart to take effect.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.1.0 - first release

Opens SQLite database files in an editor tab, with the schema on the left and the selected table's rows on the right. Reads the write-ahead log, so a database another program is writing to shows its current contents. Rows are read a page at a time with no row limit, and the row count is a real count rather than an estimate.

Cells can be changed and saved. Editing uses the IDE's own undo and its own Save All, a value that does not fit the column is refused with the column named rather than quietly converted, and a save is refused outright if another program has changed the same row since you read it.

A cell inspector shows the selected cell at full size underneath the grid, so a long value is readable and editable rather than clipped to one line. Binary is shown as a hex dump with the format named where it can be recognised, and can be written out to a file or replaced with one. There is a Go to Row command, a Reload From Disk that re-reads the tables as well as the rows, and column widths that come from the values rather than from the column names.

Rows can be added and removed. A new row appears at the end and is typed into like any other, and a column left alone takes the schema's own default rather than a NULL. A removed row stays on screen, struck through, until the save runs, so it can be undone. A removal carries the whole row into its statement, so a row another program changed while you were reading is refused rather than removed. Add Row, Delete Rows, Set Cell to NULL and the cell inspector are on the grid's right click menu.

idea-plugin.name: Workspace Desk
idea-plugin.description:
Manage Terraform Enterprise and HCP Terraform workspaces, runs, variables and state without leaving the IDE.

Workspace Desk adds a tool window that talks directly to your Terraform Enterprise or HCP Terraform host with your own API token. No third-party servers are involved. It depends only on the IntelliJ Platform, so it works in IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, WebStorm, Rider and every other JetBrains IDE. Looking is free; only the actions that change something on the server are paid.

Free

  • Organization picker and a filterable tree of projects and workspaces with live run-status icons
  • Workspace overview: execution mode, Terraform version, VCS repo and branch, lock state, tags, resource count
  • Run history with status, changes, trigger and author
  • Plan and apply logs rendered CLI-style from Terraform's JSON stream (+ ~ - -/+ resource changes, outputs, warnings and errors), with a raw-log toggle and auto-refresh while a run is active
  • Workspace variables incl. those inherited from variable sets, with precedence made visible (sensitive values stay hidden); compare with a local .tfvars file, export as tfvars
  • Variable sets of the organization: scope, priority, variables and the workspaces they apply to
  • State resources and outputs of a workspace (sensitive outputs stay hidden): sort by any column, filter by address, provider or module; double-click a resource to open the .tf block that declares it; Open in Cloud Console jumps to the object in the AWS, Azure or Google console - from the Resources tab or from a resource block in the editor, built from the attributes in state, no cloud credentials involved
  • Copy a ready-to-paste terraform_remote_state or tfe_outputs data block for any outputs, with a locals entry per output
  • Structured plan viewer (attribute-level diffs), cost estimate, policy checks, run tasks (Checkov, Snyk, ...) with their findings and OPA evaluations per run; log diagnostics link to the local file
  • Run comments: the conversation TFE keeps on a run - approvals, questions, the reason behind a discard - with author and time
  • Pre-flight: one screen for a run awaiting a decision - what blocks the apply, the change summary with the plan tree, cost delta, policy and run-task results, the blast radius from the dependency graph, drift, Terraform version, other queued runs and the lock holder
  • Dependencies tab: what a resource depends on and what uses it, one hop at a time; copy the closure as a list of addresses ready for -target
  • Change history of a resource across runs; health-assessment drift in the Overview, the Resources tab, the tree and the editor gutter
  • Workspace Graph: which workspaces read which others' outputs through remote state
  • Status-bar widget for the bound workspace; hover var.name for its effective value
  • State version history with a diff of any two versions in the IDE's diff viewer
  • Organization-wide run queue: every pending, running or decision-awaiting run in one list
  • Browse the organization's module registry: published modules with versions, copy a ready-to-paste module block - optionally with every input as a placeholder or commented default
  • State-aware editor: hover a resource block for its live state, gutter icons, project ↔ workspace binding, Terraform version mismatch warning
  • Run notifications for favorite, bound and watched workspaces; Search Everywhere finds workspaces, resources and run ids
  • Browse a workspace's notification configurations (Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, webhooks) with triggers, state and last delivery
  • What your token may do, shown up front: per organization in Test Connection, per workspace in the Overview - so a write you are not allowed stops with a plain sentence, not a failed request
  • Favorite groups: pin workspaces into your own named groups per organization - nested (DEV/team-a), each with an icon of its choice, filled by drag and drop
  • Several connection profiles (e.g. HCP Terraform and a self-hosted Terraform Enterprise)

Paid (free 30-day trial)

  • Start runs: plan-only, destroy, auto-apply
  • Confirm & apply or discard from the pre-flight screen, with a comment that lands on the run; cancel and force-cancel runs; override soft-failed policy checks; post run comments
  • Edit workspace settings: description, execution mode and agent pool, Terraform version, working directory, auto-apply, destroy plans, run queueing, speculative plans, health assessments, global remote state, tags - and auto-destroy for ephemeral workspaces, at a time or after a period without changes
  • Add, edit, enable / disable, verify and delete notification configurations
  • Create a workspace from a local folder: the workspace on the host (Terraform version from required_version), a cloud block written into the folder, the folder bound, variables pushed from a .tfvars file
  • Lock and unlock workspaces, also for a whole favorite group at once
  • Add, edit and delete workspace variables; push .tfvars differences to a workspace; copy variables between workspaces; edit variable sets and apply them to workspaces
  • Upload a local folder and run it - as a speculative plan that leaves the workspace untouched, or as its new configuration (plan, or plan and auto-apply) - without VCS or CLI
  • Speculative plan of your working copy (whole folder or the block under the caret) and targeted drift checks straight from the editor
  • Cross-organization resource search: which workspace manages this resource / ID / ARN? Incremental updates re-index only the workspaces that changed
  • Dependency diagram of a workspace's state - the whole graph, one resource's neighbourhood, or the impact of a plan (IDEs with the Diagrams plugin: IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate, PyCharm Professional, ...)
  • Override run-task stages awaiting one; build the Workspace Graph and queue plans on every consumer of a workspace's outputs

Getting started

  1. Open Settings | Tools | Workspace Desk, enter your host (app.terraform.io or your Terraform Enterprise hostname) and an API token, then click Test Connection.
  2. Open the Workspace Desk tool window on the right and pick an organization.

Honours the IDE's HTTP proxy and accepted server certificates, so self-hosted Terraform Enterprise with a private CA works out of the box.

Terraform is a trademark of HashiCorp, Inc. Workspace Desk is an independent product and is not affiliated with or endorsed by HashiCorp.

2026.4.1

  • Runs tab and Outputs tab sort by header and narrow by a filter box, like the Resources tab.
  • Changes view: Copy Value (Ctrl+C), Copy Old Value, Copy Attribute Path and Copy Line on every row.
  • Favorite groups are folders: a workspace sits in one group (adding moves it), groups nest (DEV/team-a) with sub-group creation, rename and delete carrying sub-groups along and bulk actions covering them, each group can wear one of some forty icons, and workspaces and groups move by drag and drop.

  • Resources: change history of a resource across recent runs, with each run's attribute diff.

idea-plugin.name: VPS Graph
idea-plugin.description:
VPS Graph is a local-first, read-only infrastructure explorer for a Linux VPS inside JetBrains IDEs.

Connect over public-key SSH and explore how your server resources fit together, including Docker and Compose applications, Caddy routes, systemd services, listeners, ports, networks, mounts, and upstream relationships.

  • Explore infrastructure through Overview, Applications, Services, Routing, Network, and Storage views.
  • See relationships between containers, reverse proxies, ports, services, and host resources.
  • Compare locally stored snapshots with Changes and history views.
  • Use an optional server helper for deeper, allowlisted infrastructure discovery.
  • No account, cloud backend, telemetry, deployment, restart, or remote-management controls.

VPS Graph is currently an early public beta focused on one Debian/Ubuntu VPS at a time. It has been manually tested on IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, and Rider.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Initial public beta.

  • Read-only SSH host discovery with strict known_hosts verification.
  • Optional sanitized Docker, Compose, Caddy, Systemd, and listener discovery.
  • Local infrastructure snapshots and evidence-qualified Changes history.
  • First-run setup guidance, remembered connection fields, and local Disconnect.

idea-plugin.name: Cosmos DB Explorer
idea-plugin.description:
Read your Azure Cosmos DB documents in the IDE, and keep reading them after the IDE updates.

Pick a database, pick a container, press Run. That's it.

Why this one

The usual way to look at a Cosmos document is the Data Explorer in the Azure portal: another browser tab, another sign-in, and a scroll through system fields before you reach your own data. The usual alternative is a toolkit that reaches out to every subscription the moment the IDE starts.

  • Nothing happens until you press Connect. No network call is made at IDE startup, so it cannot slow your startup down or throttle your account.
  • No upper IDE build limit is declared. An IDE update does not switch this plugin off.
  • No third-party libraries at all. It speaks the Cosmos DB REST API directly using the JDK. Nothing to conflict with, and nothing extra to load.
  • Every release is run through the JetBrains Plugin Verifier against multiple IDE versions before it ships.

What it does

  • Browse databases and containers in one tool window
  • Run a Cosmos DB NoSQL query and read the results as a table
  • Columns are built from the fields your documents actually have, not a fixed list
  • _rid, _self, _etag, _attachments and _ts are hidden by default, and one tick brings them back
  • Select a row to read the whole document as indented JSON
  • Results arrive one page at a time, so a large container does not freeze the IDE
  • The request charge in RU is shown for every query, because that is what it costs you
  • Works against the local Cosmos DB emulator as well as a real account

Read-only by design. It reads databases, containers and documents. It never writes, never deletes, and never changes throughput.

Price

USD 3 a month, or 30 a year. That is the same as the DynamoDB and Elasticsearch plugins that many teams already pay for.

A 30-day free trial covers everything, and no card is needed to start it. Buying and invoicing are handled by JetBrains, so it goes through the same channel as your IDE licence.

Your key is kept in the IDE password safe, never in a project file that could reach version control. A read-only key is enough. The plugin talks to Cosmos DB directly from your machine, and nothing is uploaded anywhere.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.2: The notice that offers the free trial now stays on screen until you close it, instead of fading after a few seconds.

1.1.1: The license notice now has an Enter license button that opens the IDE license dialog with this plugin selected, and See pricing opens this plugin's pricing page. The trial length shown in the plugin now matches the Marketplace: 30 days.

1.1.0: The plugin now connects on its own when a URI and key are already saved. When nothing is saved, the status line names the exact Azure portal screen the URI and primary key come from, and points at the emulator tick box.

1.0.0: First public release.

idea-plugin.name: Markdown Preview Plus
idea-plugin.description:
A Markdown preview that renders in a real browser engine, follows the IDE theme, and keeps working when the .md file association is taken over by something else.

It opens as an extra tab beside the editor, so nothing has to be disabled or replaced.

What it does

  • Renders in JCEF — tables, task lists, strikethrough and autolinks, with GitHub-style table handling.
  • Mermaid diagrams are drawn from ```mermaid blocks. The library is bundled, so nothing is downloaded and no content leaves the machine.
  • Follows the IDE theme. Colours are derived from the active editor colour scheme, so the preview matches light and dark schemes alike.
  • Updates as you type, reading the open document rather than the file on disk.
  • Remembers the scroll position across tab switches and IDE restarts.
  • Take the document out of the IDE. Export to PDF or to a single self-contained HTML file, copy it with its formatting for Slack, Jira or email, or print it — diagrams included, with no Pandoc to install. Exports come out on a light background by default, diagrams redrawn to match; turn that off to keep the preview's own colours.
  • Custom stylesheet from any path. One setting, applied to every project — no copy of the same CSS in each repository.
  • Repairs a lost .md association. When another file type claims the extension, the preview says so and offers to hand it back in one click.

Free and paid

  • Free: the whole preview — rendering, Mermaid diagrams, the IDE theme, live updates, the remembered scroll position, and the .md repair.
  • Paid: exporting to PDF and HTML, copying with formatting, printing, and a custom stylesheet.

The paid features come with a 30-day trial, and no card is needed to start it. Buying and invoicing are handled by JetBrains.

Settings

Settings | Tools | Markdown Preview Plus
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.3: The notice that offers the free trial now stays on screen until you close it, instead of fading after a few seconds.

1.1.2

  • When a paid feature is blocked, the notice now has a Start free trial button. It opens the IDE license dialog with this plugin selected, so you can start the 30-day trial in one click. See pricing now opens this plugin's pricing page instead of a search.

1.1.1

  • Internal fix: adopted the newer file-editor state API for 2026.3+ IDEs (the old one still works, but was flagged deprecated there). No visible change.

1.1.0

  • Mermaid diagrams are now free.
  • Export the page to PDF, exactly as shown.
  • Export to one self-contained HTML file.
  • Copy the rendered document with its formatting.
  • Print the page as shown.
  • Exports go out on a light background by default, with the diagrams redrawn to match. Settings | Tools | Markdown Preview Plus.

1.0.0

  • First release.

idea-plugin.name: CallerView
idea-plugin.description:
CallerView

Analyze and visualize the caller chain of any Java/Kotlin method.
Right-click a method in the editor and choose CallerView: Show Call Chain.
  • Configurable upward depth (default -1 = all levels)
  • Configurable core methods — any chain affecting a core method is highlighted in red
