1.0.0
Initial release.

idea-plugin.name: Fast Excel Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
Open Excel spreadsheets (.xlsx / .xlsm) in your IDE — double-click a workbook in the Project view and read it. No Excel, no LibreOffice, no switching windows. Works in IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, PhpStorm, RubyMine, CLion and DataGrip.

Free — and always will be:

  • Any file size. Rows are parsed as a stream and handed to the table a chunk at a time, so memory stays flat: a sheet with 200,000 rows streams through without the heap growing by even a megabyte, and the IDE does not freeze
  • Every sheet in the workbook, in tabs, switchable without reopening the file
  • Copy cells straight out — select a cell or a block and press Ctrl+C; it lands on the clipboard as tab-separated text, ready to paste into code, a SQL query or Excel
  • Search across all columns
  • Sort and filter the view without touching the file
  • It does not touch your CSV files. Only .xlsx and .xlsm are registered — CSV keeps opening in the IDE's own editor, with its own formatting, exactly as before
  • Reads the modern Excel formats, .xlsx and .xlsm. (The legacy binary .xls format is not supported — it is a different, non-XML container.)

Pro — subscription, with a 30-day free trial:

  • Edit cell values, insert and delete rows
  • Saves by surgical rewrite: every byte of the workbook is copied through untouched except the cells you actually changed. Formulas, number formats, styles and every other sheet survive intact
  • A timestamped backup of the original is written before anything is replaced, and the new file is re-opened and validated before it is swapped in
  • Export the current sheet — with your filters and sorting applied — to CSV

Saving never rewrites the parts of your workbook it was not asked to change, and it refuses the edits it cannot prove are safe rather than producing a file Excel would offer to repair. The free tier stays fully functional and read-only.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Pro is now available for purchase. Editing cells, inserting and deleting rows, and exporting the current sheet to CSV can be bought on the Marketplace, with a 30-day free trial.

Nothing you had before has been taken away. Reading workbooks stays free and unlimited — any file size, every sheet, search, sort, filter and copy-to-clipboard are unchanged. Only the editing and export features are part of Pro.

idea-plugin.name: Keystore Inspector
idea-plugin.description:
Inspect Java keystores, SSL/TLS certificates and PEM bundles without leaving the IDE — double-click a .jks, .p12 or .pem in the Project view and read it.

Free — and always will be:

  • Opens .jks, .pkcs12, .p12, .pfx files — double click and browse
  • PEM bundles shown properly: every certificate in a .pem/.crt/.key file gets its own row with full details, instead of the whole file collapsing into one unreadable line
  • Chain order and verification: certificates are sorted leaf → intermediate → root, and each signature is actually verified — so a broken or out-of-order bundle is called out before you deploy it
  • Expiry highlighting: certificates expiring within 30/90 days are flagged
  • Full X.509 details: subject, issuer, validity, SAN, key algorithm, SHA-256 fingerprint
  • Read-only inspection: never modifies or rewrites your keystore

Pro — subscription, with a 30-day free trial:

  • Import a PEM bundle as PKCS12 — turn a certificate chain plus private key into the .p12 your server needs, in one action (PKCS#8, encrypted PKCS#8 and PKCS#1 keys)
  • Export any certificate or private key to PEM
  • Migrate an entire keystore from JKS to PKCS12 in one action

Pro writes never touch the file you opened: they go to a new path you choose.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Pro is now available for purchase. Import a PEM bundle as PKCS12, export any certificate or private key to PEM, and migrate a keystore from JKS to PKCS12 can be bought on the Marketplace, with a 30-day free trial.

Nothing you had before has been taken away. Reading and inspecting certificates stays free and unlimited — only the import, export and migration actions are part of Pro.

Correctness fixes in certificate and keystore handling:

  • Key/certificate matching is now verified by signing. It was previously compared by key parameters, which could not tell two different EC keys apart and could not check Ed25519 keys at all — so a private key that did not belong to its certificate could pass. PEM import now refuses such a bundle instead of writing a keystore that will not start.
  • Converting a keystore no longer drops intermediates. When an entry's private key could not be unlocked, its certificate was carried over without its issuing chain.
  • The container format shown is read from the file. It was taken from the file name, so a .jks renamed to .p12 was described as a PKCS12 container.

idea-plugin.name: 3D Visualizer
idea-plugin.description:
3D Point Cloud and Mesh Visualizer

View, compare and inspect point clouds, meshes, gaussian splats, depth maps and
disparity images in your editor or browser — with Rust and WebAssembly doing the
heavy decoding, so files with millions of points open in seconds.

Highlights

  • Open large point clouds quickly, including files with millions of points
  • Decode the demanding formats in Rust/WebAssembly — LAS, LAZ, E57 and TIFF —
    alongside Rust geometry kernels for camera models and scan registration
  • Compare multiple point clouds in one view and toggle them independently
  • Convert depth and disparity images into point clouds
  • Render gaussian splat reconstructions as sorted splats or center point clouds
  • Inspect meshes as surfaces, wireframes, points and normals
  • Use Eye-Dome Lighting and brightness correction for clearer uncolored geometry
  • Measure distances and adjust camera, rotation center and view parameters
  • Use the shared viewer on the website
  • Try the local
    Python package and command-line viewer for 3D
    files, NumPy/PyTorch arrays and inline local notebooks
    (uv add ply-visualizer)
  • Connect AI agents through the local MCP server to
    open scenes, control the camera and inspect rendered screenshots

Supported formats

Type Formats
Point clouds PLY, XYZ, XYZN, XYZRGB, PCD, PTS, NPY, LAS, LAZ, E57, KITTI BIN, Stonex X3A/X3R (experimental)
Meshes PLY, OBJ, STL, OFF, GLTF, GLB
Gaussian splats 3DGS PLY, SPZ, SPLAT, KSPLAT, SOG
Depth/disparity images TIFF, PNG, PFM, NPY, NPZ
3D Body Poses JSON pose data (experimental)
Camera Profiles JSON pose data (experimental)

Because .bin and .json are generic extensions, neither is opened with the 3D
Visualizer by default. For KITTI BIN, use Open With... or right-click and
choose Open with 3D Visualizer. For a supported JSON pose, right-click and
choose Load JSON as 3D Pose.

Features

Depth and Disparity to Point Cloud

Convert depth or disparity images into point clouds. Projection settings include
fx, fy, cx, cy, camera distortion models, mono depth scale and bias, PNG
int16 scale and disparity offset.

Eye-Dome Lighting

Use Eye-Dome Lighting to improve depth perception, especially for uncolored
point clouds.

Multiple Point Clouds

Load multiple point clouds into the same view, toggle them independently and
switch between them with Shift-click.

Mesh Inspection

Inspect mesh files with controls for surface, wireframe, points and normals.
This is useful when checking geometry, topology or exported reconstruction
results without leaving the editor.

Gaussian Splatting

Open 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstructions (3DGS PLY, SPZ, SPLAT, KSPLAT, SOG)
and render them as real sorted splats via Spark, or as a
point cloud of the gaussian centers with colors derived from the
spherical-harmonics coefficients. Switch per file with the ✨ Splats button
in the Files panel. Measurement and picking keep working on the gaussian centers
in splat mode. Oversized background gaussians can be reduced with the
logarithmic Max splat size control, while coloring center points by the
opacity scalar field in Points mode helps with spotting floaters.

Point Cloud Attributes

Point cloud files can include positions, RGB colors, normals and scalar fields.
The viewer uses positions for geometry, original RGB values when available,
normals for inspection, and intensity/reflectivity fields for optional scalar
coloring. The recognized property names are x/y/z, red/green/blue,
nx/ny/nz and intensity/reflectivity/reflectance/remission. Any other
numeric per-vertex PLY property (e.g. confidence, error, curvature) also
appears in the Color dropdown for Viridis or grayscale colormap coloring.
LAS/LAZ attributes such as classification, returns, scan angle and GPS time are
exposed through the same scalar-field color controls. E57 containers load each
scan as a separate, independently visible entry.

Distance Measurement Tools and Camera Manipulation

Build multiple measurement paths with Shift-double-click. See control
settings for options.

Camera Recording

Create smooth camera paths from keyframes and export them as configurable video
recordings.

Navigation

Double-click a point to change the rotation center. This allows for easy
navigation using a mouse or a trackpad. You can also manually enter the camera
position, rotation center and viewing angle.

Performance-Aware Rendering

The viewer shows the current frame rate. When the point cloud is not moving, no
more frames are generated, which helps reduce power usage.

NPY file structure options

  • As a depth image: [X,Y]
  • As a point cloud: [...,3] with the three values X,Y,Z

Feature requests and issues

If you have a workflow that would benefit from new features or file formats,
please open an issue on the
GitHub repository. Example
files are especially helpful when adding support for new formats.

Roadmap

  • Add support for more file formats, including FBX
  • Improve dataset support with example images from Middlebury stereo and ETH3D
  • Use calibration files next to depth images automatically when available
    (example files needed)
  • Accept 3d body pose files (example files needed)

Links

  • VS Code Marketplace:
    Install extension
  • Open VSX:
    Install extension
  • JetBrains: Signed preview and installation
  • Website: 3d.f-kleinicke.de
  • Documentation: Features and usage
  • Standalone app: Tauri desktop preview
  • PyPI (Python and CLI):
    ply-visualizer
  • MCP: Supported — Agent setup and usage
  • More platforms: Coming soon
  • Blog: Coming soon
  • Videos: Coming soon

idea-plugin.name: Demystified Stack Trace Links

idea-plugin.name: Geo Viewer Plus
idea-plugin.description:
Geo Viewer Plus adds a dedicated interactive map for spatial values in DataGrip result grids. It is independent of DataGrip's built-in Geo Viewer and keeps map interaction connected to the current result set.

  • Display WKT-compatible points, lines, polygons, and multi-geometries from visible result-grid rows.
  • Select a row to focus and highlight its geometry; click a map feature to select and scroll to its row.
  • Switch between built-in OSM and domestic-friendly basemaps, or add custom XYZ/TMS sources with attribution and subdomains.
  • Persist the selected default basemap, inspect the actual tile zoom level, and retry failed tile requests without interrupting feature selection.
  • Use a compact, collapsible toolbar designed to keep the map and result grid visible together.

Map tiles are requested directly from the selected provider. Use only sources you are permitted to access, and review each provider's attribution and terms.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Broader DataGrip compatibility

  • Expanded support back to DataGrip 2023.1, including compatibility with its legacy result-grid API.

Map usability

  • Improved toolbar text readability.
  • Added Esri World Hillshade as a built-in terrain-relief basemap.

idea-plugin.name: MongoDB Inspector
idea-plugin.description:
Browse MongoDB databases and documents without leaving the IDE — a read-only viewer for local mongod, MongoDB Atlas and any reachable cluster. No mongosh window, no Compass, no switching applications to answer "what is actually in this collection?".

  • Connect with a standard connection string — mongodb:// and mongodb+srv:// (Atlas) both work, including credentials and authSource
  • Browse databases and collections, switch between them in one click
  • Run a JSON filter against any collection, e.g. {"status": "active"} — operators like $gt and $in work as you would expect
  • Documents rendered as readable, indented JSON — BSON types included, nothing truncated
  • Failures explain themselves: an unreachable host, a refused port and a wrong password each say which thing to check, instead of printing a driver exception
  • Read-only by design. This plugin never writes to your database — there is no code path that can issue an insert, update or delete
idea-plugin.change-notes: First public release: connect, browse collections and read documents from a dedicated tool window.

idea-plugin.name: Cloud Debug Pack
idea-plugin.description:
One tool window for the cloud things you check while debugging: S3, CloudWatch Logs, CloudFormation, Step Functions and Azure Blob Storage. Pick your AWS profile and region once and every AWS tab uses it.

What it is for

  • A deploy failed. The CloudFormation tab names the resource that failed first and why, instead of leaving you to scroll through dozens of rollback events.
  • A workflow failed. The Step Functions tab shows the state that failed, its error, and the exact input it received, so you can reproduce it.
  • Something is wrong across services. Follow several CloudWatch log groups in one stream, merged by time, and double-click a stack trace line to open that source line.
  • You need to look at a file. Browse S3 buckets and Azure Blob containers like folders, preview the start of a file, and download it.

Free and paid

  • Free: browsing, previewing and downloading in S3 and Azure Blob. Reading and filtering CloudWatch logs, following one log group live, saving lines to a file. Listing CloudFormation stacks and their events. Listing Step Functions executions and their history.
  • Paid: CloudFormation root cause pinpoint and live deploy watch. Step Functions failed state pinpoint with its input, and live refresh. Following several log groups at once. Saved log filters. Favorites shared by every tab and every project. One AWS profile and region shared by all AWS tabs.

The paid plan is USD 5 a month or USD 50 a year. Every paid feature is included in a 30-day free trial, and no card is needed to start it. When a paid feature is blocked, the notice has a Start free trial button that opens the IDE license dialog for this plugin. Buying and invoicing are handled by JetBrains.

Built to stay out of the way

  • Nothing is sent when the IDE starts. A tab reads from the cloud only when you open it.
  • Read-only by design. There is no delete, overwrite, deploy or start button anywhere.
  • No upper IDE build limit is declared, so an IDE update does not switch it off.
  • Light: only the four AWS SDK modules it needs, with the JDK HTTP client. Azure Blob is called over REST with the JDK, with no Azure SDK.

Credentials. AWS profiles come from your existing ~/.aws/config, environment variables and SSO sessions. The Azure access key is kept in the IDE password safe, never in project files. Everything talks to AWS and Azure directly from your machine, and nothing is uploaded anywhere else. LocalStack and Azurite work through the Endpoint field.

Not affiliated with Amazon Web Services or Microsoft.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.1: The notice that offers the free trial now stays on screen until you close it, instead of fading after a few seconds.

1.0.0: First release. S3 Browser, CloudWatch Logs Viewer, CloudFormation Deploy Watcher, Step Functions Execution Viewer and Azure Blob Browser in one tool window, with one shared AWS profile and region, shared favorites, and several log groups followed at once.

idea-plugin.name: JSON Canopy
idea-plugin.description:
JSON Canopy opens .json files as nested, filterable, editable tables or as a schema-driven form, in an extra tab next to the built-in JSON editor.

Explore

  • Objects and arrays render as tables inside tables. An array of objects becomes one column per item, so you can compare entries at a glance.
  • Flip a table between horizontal and vertical orientation, and hide columns with the field selector.
  • Large arrays are paged, so big files stay responsive. Load more items when you need them.

Search

One search box, two ways to look at the results:

  • Strict: only what matched, under its dimmed parents. A matching name shows its value; a nested one stays collapsed until you click it.
  • Context: a match in full, with all its siblings, and the attributes next to every parent on the way up.
  • Matches are highlighted, and a line under the search box explains the active mode.

JSON Schema

  • The schema is found for you: a local $schema in the file, else whatever the IDE's JSON Schema support applies (your mappings, SchemaStore). A remote schema is never downloaded without asking.
  • Problems are marked on the values and listed in the schema bar; click one to jump to it.
  • Enums become dropdowns, the type dropdown offers only what fits, absent optional keys are offered, and readOnly and deprecated are shown. The ⓘ shows descriptions, constraints, defaults and examples.
  • The schema advises, it never blocks.

Tables or form

  • A Tables | Form toggle switches between two views of the same document.
  • The form shows objects as labelled fields in schema order, with an outline to navigate by structure and a docs panel for the field in focus.
  • oneOf/anyOf with a discriminator get a variant picker that asks before it removes anything.

Collapse and expand

  • Every object and array has a ▾ button to collapse it, with or without a search. Collapsed nodes (including the ones a search leaves collapsed) show a chip you click to expand.
  • Shift+click applies to all related nodes at once, such as the same column in every row of an array.
  • The field selector closes with Esc or a click outside.

Edit in place

  • Change any value directly, with a type dropdown per value (string, number, boolean, null, object, array).
  • Add or remove object keys and array items with + and ×.
  • Edits go through the IDE, so undo and redo work.
  • Prefer text? Edit the whole document as raw JSON, or copy and download the result.

Fits your IDE

  • Light and dark themes follow the IDE theme automatically.
  • It is an additional tab: the standard JSON tab, with its completion, stays where it is, and both edit the same document.
  • Also available for Visual Studio Code.

Source code and issues: github.com/OldPeasant/json-canopy
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.3.0

  • New: VS Code extension. The same editor as a VS Code custom editor: open a .json file with Open With… → JSON Canopy, the table icon in the editor title bar or the Explorer context menu. Edits go into VS Code's own document (undo, redo and save work as usual), and the page follows your colour theme.
  • JSON Schema support. Problems are marked on the values and listed in the schema bar (click one to jump to it); enums become dropdowns, the type dropdown offers only what fits, absent optional keys are offered, readOnly and deprecated are shown, and the ⓘ shows descriptions, constraints, defaults and examples. The schema advises, it never blocks.
  • The schema is found for you. A local $schema in the file first; then, in IntelliJ, whatever the IDE's JSON Schema support applies (your mappings, SchemaStore), and in VS Code your json.schemas setting. A remote schema is never downloaded without asking.
  • Form layout. A Tables | Form toggle: the form shows objects as labelled fields in schema order, with an outline, a docs panel for the field in focus, and a variant picker for oneOf/anyOf that asks before it removes anything. The choice is remembered per schema.
  • Simpler search: Strict and Context. Strict shows only what matched, under dimmed parents; Context shows a match with all its siblings. The Path mode and the "Names only" option are gone.
  • Fix: adding an item to a list of records added a bare "" you could not fill in. The new item is now a record shaped by the schema, or like the other items when there is no schema.
  • Fix: a row or key just added to a short array or object could be hidden behind paging.
  • Fix: a new key added in the Tables view started as "" instead of the schema's starting value.
  • Fix: a small array could show only some of its items after a search.

0.2.2

  • New plugin icon, matching the JSON Canopy web app.

0.2.1

  • Fix: the JSON Canopy tab showed "Your file couldn't be accessed" on some IDEs (seen on IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2 as a Flatpak). The page is now loaded from a temporary file.
  • New icon for the standalone web app.

0.2.0

  • New search: Matches, Path and Context modes, a "Names only" option, match highlighting and dimmed context, with a description of the active mode.
  • Collapse and expand any object or array; Shift+click applies to all related nodes.
  • The field selector closes with Esc or a click outside.

idea-plugin.name: XLT Themes
idea-plugin.description:
A high-contrast JetBrains theme collection built around blue-black ink, amber structure, mint strings, coral values, and rose-pink property names.

The optional XLT Nightfall Spectrum variant adds a Monokai Spectrum-inspired semantic palette without changing the original five themes.

XLT Daylight provides a dedicated high-contrast light variant with violet structure, green strings, blue functions, cyan types, and rose properties.

XLT Daylight White keeps the same Daylight syntax palette on the pure-white background used by XLT Nightfall Light.

The XLT Nocturne family adapts all eleven Noctis variants for the JetBrains Islands UI. Its eight dark themes offer teal, azure, rose, indigo, violet, and muted surfaces; Lux, Hibernus, and Lilac add warm ivory, cool blue-white, and violet-white light themes.

Perfect for developers who appreciate clean aesthetics and clear syntax highlighting across all supported languages and file types.

Ported from antfu's vscode-theme-vitesse

idea-plugin.name: LogHue
idea-plugin.description:
Read coloured local logs and jump to errors without changing the source file.

LogHue renders ANSI colours in a read-only editor and shows error and warning counts for the visible log.

  • Free: ANSI 16/256/RGB rendering, raw view, wrapping, reload, clean copy and save, custom extensions, issue counts and next-issue navigation
  • Pro: a navigable index of up to 2,000 error and warning lines
  • Read local files in the background; show a clearly marked tail for very large logs

LogHue is freemium. The viewer works indefinitely without a license; the issue index requires a JetBrains Marketplace Pro subscription. LogHue has no backend, telemetry, uploads, or account.

2026.1.3

  • Complete ANSI rendering, clean copy/save, and custom extensions are now free.
  • Find error and warning lines with counts, Next issue, and a Pro issue index.
  • Keep large logs responsive with a clearly labelled, bounded tail view and limited styling.

idea-plugin.name: Scientific Image Visualizer
idea-plugin.description:
Scientific Image Visualizer

Rust-based image decoding and GPU accelerated rendering for high-bit-depth, floating-point, scientific, and standard image files.

Supports TIFF/OME-TIFF (including embedded multi-file filesets), EXR, NPY/NPZ, PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF, HDR, JXL, JPEG XR, JPEG 2000, SGI RGB, TGA, BMP, ICO, PPM, PFM, PBM, PGM, FITS, DICOM, classic NetCDF, Zeiss CZI, Nikon ND2, Leica LIF, and Becker & Hickl SDT.
Layered creative documents
are previewed from OpenRaster, Krita, Photoshop PSD/PSB, GIMP XCF, and Affinity Photo files.

The viewer supports 8-bit and 16-bit integer images as well as 16-bit and 32-bit floating-point images. You can inspect exact pixel values, normalize image data to custom ranges, adjust gamma and brightness, compare images, and export rendered or layered results. Decoding runs in Rust compiled to WebAssembly and compositing runs on the GPU, so large scientific images open and respond at native speed.

Supported Sample Types

Format uint8 uint16 float16 float32 Notes
TIFF / OME-TIFF Yes Yes Yes Yes Rust/WASM decoding; multi-page and multi-file OME C/Z/T navigation
EXR No No Yes Yes HDR floating-point format
NPY / NPZ Yes Yes Yes Yes Also supports float64 and signed/unsigned integers up to 64 bit
FITS / DICOM / NetCDF / CZI / ND2 / LIF / SDT Yes Yes No Yes Numeric HDUs, DICOM series/frames, classic NetCDF variables, microscopy stacks, and FLIM/TCSPC histograms
HDR No No No Yes Radiance RGBE, decoded to float32
PFM No No No Yes Portable Float Map
PPM / PGM / PBM Yes Yes No No PBM is 1-bit, shown as 8-bit
PNG Yes Yes No No Palette PNGs become 8-bit RGBA
SGI RGB (.rgb, .rgba, .sgi, .bw) Yes Yes No No Uncompressed and RLE; grayscale and RGB with optional alpha
JPEG / WebP / AVIF / BMP / ICO / TGA Yes No No No Decoded as 8-bit image data
JPEG XL (.jxl) Yes Yes No Yes Decoded in Rust at the file's own sample type: 8/16-bit and float, grey or RGB(A)
JPEG XR (.jxr, .wdp, .hdp) Yes Yes No Yes Decoded in Rust; 8/16/32-bit grey and RGB(A), including scene-referred float
JPEG 2000 (.jp2, .jpf, .jpx, .j2k, .j2c, .jpc) Yes Yes No No Decoded in Rust at native precision; a 12-bit Sentinel-2 band normalizes against 4095, not 65535
ORA / KRA / PSD / PSB / XCF / Affinity Photo Yes PSD/PSB No PSD/PSB Saved/embedded previews; ORA, Krita paint layers, common XCF rasters, and PSD cached raster/group layers can also be composed; compatible PSD adjustments, Krita filter masks/layers, and XCF GIMP 3 layer effects are approximated

Layered-document support reports approximated or unsupported operations instead of silently hiding them. Broader layer reconstruction and professional-tool compatibility are tracked in the backlog.

NetCDF-4/HDF5, multi-file CZI sets, compressed ND2 frames and legacy (pre-2012) ND2 files are not yet supported. CZI decodes uncompressed, JPEG, LZW, JPEG XR, Zstd-0/Zstd-1, and experimental CHUNKED (zstd/LZ4) subblocks. DICOM decodes native, Deflated Explicit VR, RLE Lossless, JPEG Baseline, JPEG-LS, JPEG 2000, JPEG XL, and lossless JPEG pixel data; JPEG XR and video transfer syntaxes are not yet supported.

Images above roughly 268 megapixels (for example 20480x20480) decode correctly and their pixel values, metadata and statistics remain fully available, but cannot be displayed: a browser canvas cannot exceed 2^28 pixels. Tiled rendering for images that large is planned.
Small synthetic files for manual checks live in test-samples/scientific/.
Extensionless DICOM studies can be opened with Scientific Image Visualizer: Open Folder as DICOM Dataset. The viewer scans technical headers, groups images by series, removes duplicate SOP instances, and orders slices spatially.

Features

  • Fast and versatile TIFF Support: TIFF decoding in Rust compiled to WebAssembly. Opens high-bit-depth, floating-point, multi-channel, and compressed TIFF files: LZW, Deflate, PackBits, Zstd, LZMA, LERC (with GDAL's LERC_DEFLATE and LERC_ZSTD), PNG-in-TIFF, JPEG, JPEG 2000, JPEG XR, JPEG XL, WebP and CCITT fax, tiled or stripped.
  • Scientific Image Inspection: Inspect uint8, uint16, float16, and float32 image data in grayscale, RGB, and RGBA images.
  • Dataset Navigation: Browse DICOM series/slices and multi-file OME C/Z/T planes as one logical dataset while the viewer switches physical files transparently.
  • Interactive Pixel Values: Hover over any pixel to see its exact value in the status bar. For multi-channel images, all channel values are displayed.
  • Dynamic Normalization: Adjust the visualization range interactively, use automatic min/max normalization, or view integer images as normalized float values.
  • Gamma and Brightness Correction: Adjust source gamma, target gamma, and brightness while preserving linear-space behavior.
  • Histogram View: Show a histogram overlay to inspect the current image distribution while tuning the visualization.
  • Automatic GPU Rendering: Normal images, HDR/scientific images, and collections prefer WebGPU automatically, then fall back to WebGL2 and CPU rendering. Layers View retains its explicit backend diagnostics and controls.
  • Image Collections: Group related images in one preview and quickly move between them without opening a tab for every file. Add individual images, folders, paths, or wildcard matches from the command palette and editor context menu.
  • Layers View: Open one or more images in a dedicated Layers window for compositing and visual comparison. Imported layered documents retain collapsible nested groups, group visibility and Shift-solo controls, source-compatibility badges, inline renaming, editable/removable filters, persistent group expansion state, and keyboard undo/redo for layer/filter changes.
    Easily get the difference between two images or apply a mask onto one. This layer view allows dedicated compositions between multiple images. Basic compatibility with tools like photoshop.
  • NaN Color: Choose how NaN values are displayed.
  • Native Controls: Most options are available from the right-click menu inside the webview, command palette, or clickable status bar entries.
  • Metadata panel shows file info, image statistics (min/max/mean/std) and Exif/GPS sub-IFD tags.
  • Multi-channel compositing: Show several channels at once, each with its own tint, display range and opacity, added together the way emission combines at the detector — the "Composite" mode of Fiji or the "Display Adjustment" panel of Imaris. Channel names and colours come from OME metadata where the file provides them. Works both for interleaved multi-sample images and for OME-TIFF where each channel is a separate page. Solo, per-channel auto-range (percentile, so one hot pixel cannot flatten the signal), and an optional colormap per channel. This is arithmetic over scientific channels, deliberately separate from the Layers view's authoring blend modes.
  • Measurement and quantitative analysis: Draw regions of interest and measure them — area, perimeter, mean/StdDev/min/max, integrated density, centroid, fitted ellipse, Feret diameters, circularity — in physical units, with the scale read automatically from OME-TIFF or TIFF resolution tags. Includes an intensity profile along a line, a magic wand that previews its selection on hover and picks its own tolerance, thresholding with a draggable histogram, eighteen global and local auto-threshold methods shown side by side that preview on hover, a stability curve that makes a robust threshold visible instead of guessed, and particle analysis with watershed splitting. The threshold is painted over the image — red for what it selected, green for what survives the filters — so a segmentation can be checked rather than assumed. Statistics always run on the raw sample values, never on the displayed image, and NaN/Infinity are excluded and reported rather than silently counted as zero. ROIs are stored as a readable JSON file next to the image so they diff in review; ImageJ .roi and RoiSet.zip are supported for exchange. Results export as long/tidy CSV with full provenance, as German-locale CSV, or as .xlsx, optionally with a pandas starter script.
  • Use anywhere Use the same viewer on the static website:
    https://images.f-kleinicke.de

Multi-dimensional and multi-view images

  • OME-TIFF: Navigate images/series, channels, Z slices, and timepoints from OME-XML. Multi-file datasets are presented as one logical image while C/Z/T changes transparently select the referenced TIFF and IFD. BinaryOnly members automatically follow metadata stored in a master OME-TIFF or companion .ome/.ome.xml file.
  • DICOM: Use Scientific Image Visualizer: Open Folder as DICOM Dataset, select an acquisition series, and navigate its slices and available time, echo, and frame dimensions. Physical files remain grouped by DICOM identity instead of being mixed into a filename-sorted collection. Multi-frame objects, including JPEG Baseline objects, expose a Frame control.
  • Ordinary multi-page TIFF: Navigate top-level pages even when no semantic dimension metadata is available.
  • CZI / ND2 / LIF: Step through Z with the arrow keys and channels with [ / ], or use one slider per axis; channel sliders show the dye name from the embedded metadata. Mosaic tiles are assembled into the full frame. ND2 exposes time and stage-position axes; LIF adds an S slider for choosing among the image series in the file.
  • SDT: Explore Becker & Hickl FLIM/TCSPC histograms as integrated intensity, mean photon-arrival time in nanoseconds, or a selected raw time bin. Multi-block files expose a block selector.
  • NetCDF: Select a numeric variable and move through its non-spatial dimensions. Regular X/Y arrays render as rasters; MPAS nCells fields render on their unstructured cell polygons in an equirectangular mesh view.

Medical-use notice: DICOM support is provided for developer, research, and scientific visualization workflows. This extension is not a certified or cleared medical device and is not intended for diagnosis, treatment planning, clinical decision-making, or other clinical use. Do not rely on it as the sole means of viewing or interpreting medical images.

Feature Requests and Issues

If you have use cases that would be helpful for others or find problems, feel free to suggest them on the GitHub repository.
I'm open adding more file formats that can serve you.

Links

  • Documentation: Read the docs
  • Standalone app: Coming soon
  • More platforms: Coming soon
  • Blog: Coming soon
  • Videos: Coming soon

idea-plugin.name: Flexible Sim
idea-plugin.description:
Live block diagrams and simulation for Modelica, Julia, Dyad, and Python. Scope, Bode, sweeps, and 3D view. Edit the diagram or the code, and both stay in sync. Parameter studies, optimization, a debugger, tests, and a dashboard.


We are a young plugin and want to make it the best simulation tool in the IDE. Your feedback is critical: report a bug or an idea and get 20% off the annual license, or one month free.


Free and Pro:

  • Free shows and edits models of any size, and runs models with up to 5 blocks
  • Pro runs models of any size and adds Analysis, Tests, Dashboard, model diff, FMU, code export, and the 3D view
  • 30-day trial from any locked tab
  • Free for students and open source projects, 50% off for non-profits

Feedback: Leave a review, open an issue on GitHub, or write to info@ilscipio.com.


Documentation: Open Help > Flexible Sim > Welcome and Tutorial in the IDE, or visit the project on GitHub.


Flexible Sim is an independent plugin and is not affiliated with JuliaHub, MathWorks, the Modelica Association, or JetBrains.


Core Features

Diagram Editor

  • Split editor with the source on the left and the live block diagram on the right
  • Two-way sync: code edits update the diagram, and diagram edits in Dyad, Julia/ModelingToolkit, and Modelica models write back to the code
  • Clean sources: block positions live in a small layout file next to the model, not in the code
  • Hierarchy with subsystems, breadcrumb navigation, and Create Subsystem from a selection
  • Navigation with minimap, zoom, pan, fit to view, auto-layout, signal path tracing, and go to type definition
  • Validation of unconnected ports, algebraic loops, units, and parameter bounds, marked on the canvas

Canvas Editing

  • Drag and drop blocks from the library next to the canvas, and drag from port to port to connect them
  • Multi-select with Shift+click, rubber band, and Ctrl+A
  • Edit with copy, cut, paste, undo, redo, arrow-key nudge, and align and distribute
  • Parameters: double-click a block to edit its parameters, double-click a subsystem to enter it

Simulation Runtimes

  • Your own runtimes: Julia, Python, and OpenModelica on your computer, with Detect and Test buttons in the settings
  • Run settings for solver, tolerance, stop time, and step size
  • Console with process output, diagnostics, and solver hints
  • Live mode (Julia, Dyad, Python) streams results into the Scope and the Dashboard while the simulation runs
  • Simulation debugger (Julia, Dyad, Python): pause, step, signal breakpoints, and live parameter changes

Scope and Runs

  • Scope with up to 4x4 subplots, a filterable signal tree, dual cursors with measurements, spectrum, scatter, and a data table
  • Chart tools: box zoom, data tips, log/dB/phase axes, an IDE or oscilloscope theme, and PNG/SVG/CSV export
  • Runs archive: pin, rename, overlay, and compare runs with tolerances, plus HTML and CSV reports
  • Solver view with step size over time, timing, and hints when a run is slow or fails

Linear Analysis and Optimization

  • Linear Analysis (Julia, Dyad, Python, Modelica): Bode, Nyquist, Nichols, root locus, pole-zero, and step and impulse response, with stability margins
  • Analysis points marked on the diagram, and an operating point from initial conditions, a snapshot, or trim
  • Parameter studies: 1D/2D sweeps, Monte Carlo with percentile bands, and tornado, PRCC, and Sobol sensitivity
  • Optimization: tune parameters to a target response, or estimate them from measured CSV data

Tests and Dashboard

  • Tests with signal assertions (range, rate, settling, overshoot), baselines, regression runs, and block coverage
  • Dashboard with resizable gauges, charts, tables, and lamps, plus knobs, sliders, and toggles that tune a live run

State Machines

  • Hierarchy with composite states, parallel states, and history
  • Behavior with entry, during, and exit actions in Julia, and timers (after, before, every)
  • Validation and code: find unreachable states and ambiguous guards, and generate plain Julia or an MTK model

3D View

  • Multibody animation with STL, OBJ, and glTF geometry, and URDF robots built from their links and joints
  • Transport bar: play, pause, step, loop, and playback speed
  • View tools: shadows, trails, labels, frames, joint axes, center of mass, a measure tool, a section plane, and standard camera views
  • Export a PNG screenshot or a WebM video

Languages

  • Dyad and Julia/ModelingToolkit with full editor integration (needs the Flexible Julia plugin)
  • Modelica, Python/SciPy, and plain Julia DifferentialEquations.jl with no extra plugin
  • Modelica Standard Library types show their real ports, parameters, and icons
  • File types for Modelica (.mo), FMU (.fmu), Simulink (.slx), and URDF (.urdf)
  • Extensible: other plugins can add more languages

Interoperability

  • FMU import and co-simulation (FMI 2.0/3.0), and export of a real FMU for Modelica or an FMU source package for the other languages
  • URDF import turns a robot into a block diagram and a 3D model
  • Simulink import (experimental) translates an .slx model into a Julia/ModelingToolkit file
  • Model diff against a git revision, with SVG export and a review checklist
  • C code generation through ModelingToolkit

What Runs Where

idea-plugin.name: HEIC Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
Adds the HEIC/HEIF image format to IntelliJ-based IDEs. Files with the extensions .heic, .heif, .hif and .heics open in the built-in image viewer, just like PNG and JPEG.

The images are decoded by the operating system:

If something is missing, a banner above the image says what to install.

Source code and issue tracker

idea-plugin.name: CertLens - Certificates and Keystores
idea-plugin.description:
Read certificates and keystores in your IDE, and hear about expiry before production does.

Open a JKS keystore, a PKCS#12 file or a PEM bundle and CertLens shows what is inside: every certificate, its chain, its names and its dates, with a banner at the top that says straight away whether anything in the file has expired or is about to.

Free: the viewer

  • Keystores: JKS, JCEKS and PKCS#12 (.p12, .pfx). Enter the store password once; tick Remember password to keep it in the IDE's own password safe.
  • Certificate files: PEM bundles, single certificates, DER, P7B and PKCS#10 signing requests (CSR).
  • Every detail on one screen: subject, issuer, subject alternative names, key algorithm and size, signature algorithm, SHA-1 and SHA-256 fingerprints and the validity period.
  • A validity banner on every file: expired, expiring within 30 days, or valid with the earliest expiry date.
  • ASN.1 view: the full structure of any opened certificate.
  • Opened by content. A certificate saved as .txt or .key is recognised from its bytes and still opens in the viewer.

Pro: the Certificate Radar

  • Scans the whole project for certificates and keystores and lists every finding in one tool window: expired certificates, certificates expiring within 30 days, weak keys (RSA under 2048 bits, EC under 256), self-signed certificates and chains in the wrong order.
  • Runs when the project opens and tells you in a notification, so an expiring certificate shows up while there is still time to replace it.
  • Double-click a finding to open the file.

Pro: the tools

  • Convert: export a keystore's certificates to PEM, or a DER certificate to PEM.
  • Generate: a self-signed certificate with the DNS names you list, written as a PKCS#12 keystore and a PEM certificate next to the file you started from.
  • Compare: two certificates field by field, to see exactly what a renewal changed.

Pro features are in the Tools menu, under CertLens, and in the Certificate Radar tool window.

Private by design. CertLens makes no network requests. Keystore passwords go only into the IDE's password safe, and only when you ask it to remember them. Private key bytes are never shown or exported.

Pricing

  • The viewer is free, with no time limit.
  • CertLens Pro, personal: $1.50 per month, or $15 per year.
  • CertLens Pro, commercial: $4.90 per month, or $49 per year.
  • 30-day free trial of everything in Pro. Start it from the link in the Certificate Radar tool window, or from the button shown when you first use a Pro tool.

Known limits

  • BKS and UBER keystores are not supported. They are reported as unsupported rather than shown half read.
  • The Radar reads a keystore only once its password has been entered and remembered in the IDE.
  • Private keys cannot be exported, by design.
  • Files larger than 8 MB are skipped by the Radar.

Works in IntelliJ-based IDEs from version 2025.2 on. CertLens depends only on the platform, so it installs in IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, PhpStorm, RubyMine, CLion and the other JetBrains IDEs.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.1.0: first release.

  • Free viewer for JKS, JCEKS and PKCS#12 keystores and for PEM, DER, P7B and CSR files, with a validity banner, full certificate details, fingerprints and an ASN.1 view.
  • CertLens Pro: the Certificate Radar, which scans your project on open and lists expired, expiring and weak certificates, plus conversion, generation and comparison.
  • Monthly or yearly subscription, with a 30-day free trial of Pro.

idea-plugin.name: TFState Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
Terraform and OpenTofu state files are large JSON documents that are hard to read raw. TFState Viewer opens *.tfstate and *.tfstate.backup files in a structured, read-only editor: every module, resource and instance in a tree, attributes in a table, sensitive values masked.

It reads the file on your computer and never changes it. No cloud credentials, no network access, nothing is sent anywhere.

Free

  • Header with the Terraform version, serial, lineage and the number of resources, instances and outputs
  • Resource tree grouped by module (root, module.x, module.x.module.y), with count and for_each instances such as [0] and ["blue"], data sources, tainted and deposed objects
  • Search by address or attribute value
  • Attribute table with expandable nested objects and lists, plus provider, dependencies, create_before_destroy and tainted status
  • Sensitive attributes and sensitive outputs are masked as "(sensitive)" until you reveal each value
  • Outputs tab with name, type and value
  • Copy address from the context menu; a read-only Text tab with the raw JSON
  • Streaming parser: states of tens of megabytes open with a progress indicator

Pro (7-day free trial)

  • Compare with the .backup next to the state or any other state file: added, removed and changed resources, attribute-level differences, changed outputs, and the IDE diff viewer for a changed resource
  • Dependency view: what the selected resource depends on and what depends on it, one double-click away
  • Command helper: ready-to-copy state show, state rm, state mv and import commands for terraform or tofu, with addresses such as module.a.aws_instance.web["blue"] quoted correctly for bash/zsh, fish, PowerShell or cmd.exe
  • Export the resource list (address, type, provider, id) to CSV or Markdown

Reads state format version 4, written by Terraform 0.12 and later and by OpenTofu. Works in every JetBrains IDE.

TFState Viewer is an independent product and is not affiliated with HashiCorp or the OpenTofu project. Terraform is a trademark of HashiCorp.
idea-plugin.change-notes: 1.0.0 — first release: structured, read-only editor for Terraform and OpenTofu state files (format version 4) with the resource tree, search, attribute table, masked sensitive values, outputs and copy address; Pro state comparison, dependency view, command helper and CSV / Markdown export.

idea-plugin.name: Profile Viewer: CPU & Heap Profiles, Flame Graphs
idea-plugin.description:
Open profiler output straight in the IDE. Profile Viewer turns Node.js and Chrome DevTools CPU profiles, heap profiles and heap snapshots, Go pprof profiles, Python cProfile stats and folded stacks into an interactive flame graph, call tree and bottom-up table, so you can find the slow function or the leak without leaving the editor.

Files: *.cpuprofile (node --cpu-prof, Chrome DevTools), *.heapprofile (node --heap-prof), *.heapsnapshot (Chrome DevTools, v8.writeHeapSnapshot()), *.prof (Go go test -cpuprofile, pprof; or Python python -m cProfile -o), *.pstats, *.folded and *.collapsed.

Everything runs locally and read-only: the plugin never changes your files and sends nothing anywhere.

Free

  • Header with the format, duration or total size, sample count and number of functions
  • Flame graph (icicle, top-down): click to zoom, search highlighting, tooltips with self and total time and percentages, colours for your code, dependencies (node_modules, site-packages, Go modules) and runtime / native frames; light and dark themes
  • Top-down call tree and bottom-up table of the heaviest functions, with filter and sortable columns, plus callers and callees of the selected function
  • Sample-type selector for Go pprof (CPU, alloc_space, inuse_space, …)
  • Python pstats table with ncalls, tottime, cumtime and per-call times, like pstats prints them
  • Heap snapshot summary by constructor: object count, shallow size and share of the heap; streaming loader for snapshots of hundreds of megabytes

Pro (7-day free trial)

  • Go to source: double-click a frame to open the project file at that line (file:// URLs, webpack:// paths, relative paths and absolute Go / Python paths are matched to your project)
  • Compare two profiles: per-function self and total deltas sorted by the biggest regression, and a differential flame graph (red slower, blue faster)
  • Heap snapshots: retained sizes from the dominator tree, retainer paths from any object to the GC roots, and snapshot comparison (objects added and removed per constructor, size delta) for leak hunting
  • Export tables to CSV or Markdown, and any CPU profile to folded stacks

Works in every JetBrains IDE. Profile Viewer is an independent product and is not affiliated with Google, the Node.js project, the Go project or the Python Software Foundation.
idea-plugin.change-notes: 1.0.0 — first release: flame graph, call tree and bottom-up views for V8 CPU and heap profiles, Go pprof, Python cProfile stats and folded stacks; heap snapshot summary; Pro go to source, profile comparison with a differential flame graph, heap retained sizes, retainer paths and snapshot comparison, and export.

idea-plugin.name: JRXML Preview
idea-plugin.description:
Preview JasperReports .jrxml files right inside the editor - no Jaspersoft Studio required.

Open a .jrxml file and a live preview appears alongside the XML source, updating on save. Report compilation and rendering run in a separate process, so JasperReports never has to load into the IDE itself, and the plugin works against your project's own JasperReports version rather than one baked in.

  • Renders reports with type-appropriate synthetic data by default, so a report previews meaningfully with no setup.
  • Supports real preview data via a sibling <report>.jrxmlpreview.json file, for when you want specific values instead of placeholders - hand-written JSON rows, a JDBC query against your own database, or a call into your own JavaBean factory method.
  • Compile errors are shown readably in the preview panel and highlighted at the source line.

Status: pre-alpha. Expect rough edges.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.0

  • Initial pre-alpha release: split editor with a live JRXML preview, a JasperReports-version-agnostic worker process, synthetic preview data by default, custom data via *.jrxmlpreview.json, and compile-error highlighting in the editor.

idea-plugin.name: Intarsia
idea-plugin.description:
Open Apache Parquet files in an editor tab: a schema tree and paged rows, read locally with bounded memory.

Intarsia opens .parquet files in an editor tab, with the file's schema on the left and its rows on the right, one page at a time.

  • Large files without loading them whole. Intarsia reads the file footer when it opens, then reads rows one page at a time, holding roughly one row group plus one page in memory. For example, it opens a 2.15 GB (2.0 GiB) file from the public FineWeb dataset (CC-MAIN-2013-20/000_00000.parquet: 1.09 million rows in 1,092 row groups) and goes straight to its last page.
  • Page controls. Page size 100 / 1,000 / 10,000 / 50,000 rows; first, previous, next and last page; jump to a row number. A jump reads only the row group that holds the row, not the row groups before it. When a page would hold more than 1,000,000 cells (large page sizes on wide files), it is shortened to fit.
  • Nested schemas. Struct, list and map fields appear as a tree that loads each level only when you expand it; nested leaf columns get readable names such as items.array.name.
  • Brotli-compressed files open with no native libraries needed (pure-Java decoder).
  • Compression codecs. Tested: uncompressed, Snappy, ZSTD, GZIP, LZ4 (the current Parquet LZ4 codec, LZ4_RAW) and Brotli. Also bundled but not covered by our tests: the older Hadoop-framed LZ4 codec.
  • Clear errors. Empty, truncated or non-Parquet files show a plain notification (for example "The file is empty (0 bytes).") instead of an exception dialog.
  • Settings. Default page size (1–50,000 rows) under Settings → Tools → Intarsia.

Read-only and local. Intarsia opens files read-only and reads them from your disk through its own local-file reader. Its code contains no networking calls and it collects no telemetry or usage data, so it does not send your files anywhere. (It bundles Apache Hadoop libraries, which contain networking code that Intarsia does not use.)

Limitations. Values are shown as plain text (timestamps and decimals are not yet formatted as dates or numbers). Cells show at most 512 characters; longer values end with "…". In tables with list, map or other repeated columns, a jump still decodes the rows before it inside its row group. No search, filtering, sorting or editing. Only files with the .parquet extension are opened by Intarsia. Declared for IDE versions 2024.3 to 2026.2. This release was checked with the IntelliJ Plugin Verifier against IntelliJ IDEA 2024.3.5 and 2026.2 only; it uses only the base IntelliJ platform, so other JetBrains IDEs and the versions in between are expected to work but have not been tested by us.

Built with AI. Intarsia is developed and supported by a small studio that uses AI agents to write and test the code; a human owner is reachable on request through the support address below.

Support: support@madrasco.dev · Website: madrasco.dev
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.4
  • Declare related project dependencies for IDE plugin suggestions, subject to JetBrains feature approval.
  • Replace em dashes in bundled notices and user-visible messages with standard punctuation.
0.1.3
  • Faster far jumps: going to the last page, a row number or back to the start reads only the row group that holds the row, instead of decoding every row before it. Inside that row group, pages before the target are skipped without being decoded (and, for Snappy, GZIP, Brotli and uncompressed files, without being decompressed), for tables without list, map or other repeated columns; this works without a page index.
  • Less memory used per page: rows are turned straight into display text, long text values are decoded only as far as the 512 characters a cell shows, and the table shows the page without copying it.
  • Wide files: a page holds at most 1,000,000 cells, so on a file with many columns large page sizes are shortened (the status line says so) instead of exhausting the IDE's memory.
  • Column widths are measured on a sample of up to 200 rows instead of every row, so large pages no longer hold up the IDE while they are sized.
0.1.2
  • Fixed: double-clicking a .parquet file now opens Intarsia directly, instead of IntelliJ's "Register New File Type Association" dialog.
  • Fixed: wide tables (many columns) are now readable: columns keep a sensible width instead of being squeezed to fit, with a full-value tooltip on each cell.
  • Fixed: the page-size box now shows a custom default page size instead of falling back to 100.
  • Removed the Settings checkbox "Open the last viewed file on startup", which had no effect.
0.1.1
  • Fixed a crash opening files with a DECIMAL column.
0.1.0
  • First public release: Parquet viewer with schema tree and paged rows table.
  • Bounded-memory paging with page-size and jump-to-row controls.
  • Brotli-compressed file support.
  • Plain notifications for empty, truncated and corrupt files.

idea-plugin.name: ANSI Ink
idea-plugin.description:
ANSI Ink renders ANSI colors and text styles in normal JetBrains text editors. It detects ANSI sequences from file content, hides supported control codes, and leaves the underlying file unchanged.

It supports standard, bright, 256-color, and truecolor foreground and background colors, plus bold, italic, underline, and reset. Use Tools > ANSI Ink to control rendering for the project or current file. Raw view shows the original codes for editing.

Tools > ANSI Ink also offers Strip ANSI from File, an undoable command that removes ANSI CSI sequences from the current file, and Create ANSI-Free Copy, which creates a separate file without changing the original.

Detection checks the beginning of a file. Unsupported commands remain visible, and files opened in the IDE's Large File Editor are not rendered.

Developed by LeoArk.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Renamed ANSI Lens to ANSI Ink.

idea-plugin.name: HTML Cell Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
Preview and inspect rendered HTML content directly from database table cells in your IDE.

Features

  • Context Menu Preview: Right-click any database cell containing HTML and select View Rendered HTML (or press Ctrl+Alt+H / Option+Shift+H).
  • Chromium-Powered Rendering: Uses Chromium Embedded Framework (JCEF) for modern HTML5, CSS3, SVG, images, tables, and formatting.
  • Strict Security: Blocks arbitrary script execution via Content Security Policy and prevents link navigation while preserving link hover hand cursors.
  • Dual View: Toggle between the interactive rendered preview and formatted raw HTML source code.
  • Toolbar Controls: Copy raw HTML to clipboard or open directly in your external default web browser.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.0

  • Initial release of HTML Cell Viewer.
  • Render database cell HTML content via Chromium JCEF with Swing fallback.
  • Context menu integration in query result tables (Console.TableResult.PopupGroup) and keyboard shortcut Ctrl+Alt+H / Option+Shift+H.
  • Smart HTML detection filtering for cell context menus.
  • Strict Content Security Policy (CSP) blocking untrusted scripts.
  • Links show hover hand cursor while preventing accidental navigation.
  • Dual tabbed preview for rendered web output and raw HTML source.
  • Export utilities: Copy raw HTML to clipboard and open in external browser.

idea-plugin.name: MOY Panel
idea-plugin.description:
MOY is an IDE panel that looks like a scrolling code block — inside it: a novel reader, a real browser, three small games and live stock quotes. A discreet, boss-key-friendly "fake code" screen for IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand and other JetBrains IDEs.

MOY 把小说、网页、小游戏和自选股票收进 IDE 里的一块面板。面板外观始终是一段正在滚动的代码：行号、折叠三角、语法高亮，每 2 秒追加一行自动上滚。鼠标一移开就整屏变代码——工位开放时，屏幕上看起来只是编辑器里一个正常的代码窗口。

四个模式，一键切换

📖 阅读：打开本机 txt 小说，正文以等宽字体 + 逐行行号呈现，和旁边的滚动代码浑然一体。自动分页、自动识别「第X章」生成目录、每本书各记各的进度；字号、正文宽度、文字亮度都能调。本地文件直接读，不联网。

🌐 网页：面板里搜资料、看文档、刷知乎、看新闻、看视频。网址栏输入即开，可调缩放；常用网址一键跳转；配色自动跟随 IDE 主题。它本质是一个真实浏览器，B 站 / 抖音等可直接播放。

📈 股票：自选股实时报价，可分组、拖拽排序、隐藏不关心的列。支持到价预警（用 IDE 通知提醒你）、涨跌配色脱敏（把刺眼的红绿换成中性色，远看像普通表格）。底部状态栏可轮播关注的标的，并可伪装成构建日志持续滚动。

🎮 游戏：2048 / 贪吃蛇 / 消消乐。方向键操作，P 暂停、R 重开，最高分自动记住，离线可玩；鼠标移开面板会自动暂停。

防窥设计

  • ① 一直滚动的代码：面板里始终有一块代码区，每 2 秒追加一行并自动上滚，就像项目正在编译。分界线可以拖动——想全屏看内容就把它收到只剩一条缝。
  • ② 鼠标移开，整屏都是代码：鼠标离开面板或 IDE 窗口失焦时，面板自动切换成整屏滚动代码（工具栏、状态栏一起隐藏）。去接水、跟同事说话、被叫去开会，屏幕上只有代码。
  • ③ 老板键：任意时刻按 Ctrl+Shift+B，立刻变成一整屏终端风格画面；再按一次回来。

上手指南

  1. 安装后，点右侧工具栏的 MOY 图标打开面板（也可用菜单 Tools → MOY：打开摸鱼面板，快捷键 Ctrl+Alt+M）。
  2. 顶部模式栏切换「阅读 / 网页 / 游戏 / 股票」。阅读模式点「选书」选择本机 txt 文件；网页模式输入网址即可。
  3. 想更隐蔽，就把鼠标移开面板——它会自动进入整屏代码状态。

运行要求

  • 所有 JetBrains IDE 都能装：只依赖 IntelliJ Platform 公共 API，IntelliJ IDEA / PyCharm / WebStorm / GoLand / CLion / PhpStorm 等均可使用。
  • 需要本机安装 Node.js。插件会自动从 PATH、nvm / fnm / volta 以及各系统常见安装路径中查找；找不到时，可在 设置 → 工具 → MOY 摸鱼面板 里手动指定 node 可执行文件路径。
  • 面板基于 JCEF（JetBrains 运行时自带的 Chromium）渲染，无需额外安装。
  • 网页模式需要本机装有 Chrome / Chromium / Edge 三者之一。

常见问题

  • 面板打开后一直空白 / 提示找不到 node？先确认 Node.js 已安装，再到 设置 → 工具 → MOY 摸鱼面板 检查 node 路径。日志可用 Help → Show Log in Explorer / Finder 打开，搜 MOY 即可定位。
  • 股票没有数据？报价来自公开行情接口，非交易时段或接口波动时可能延迟或短暂为空。
  • 会把我读的内容上传吗？不会。小说是本地文件直读，面板与插件之间只在本机回环地址通信，阅读内容不出本机。
  • 和 VS Code 版是同一个插件吗？共用同一份核心与界面，授权码通用——两边任买其一即可在两边使用。

授权

安装后可直接试用，正式使用需要授权码。当前授权状态会显示在面板右下角状态栏。

授权校验在本地完成，不需要联网：软件内只带有用于验证签名的公钥，激活与校验都不经过任何服务器，也不会读取或上传你的任何使用数据。

联系作者

授权码获取、使用问题、功能建议，都可以直接找作者：

扫码关注公众号，发消息即可 —— 不用注册、不用提交 issue。

搜索关键词
