idea-plugin.name: Linux Do (API Docs)
idea-plugin.description:
Linux Do — Unofficial Community Client

An independent, personal project by lgguan, licensed under MIT. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Linux Do or JetBrains. Only https://linux.do is supported.

Supports Windows, macOS and Linux. Requires JetBrains IDE 2026.2 (build 262.*) with its bundled JBR and JCEF plugin.

A native JetBrains IDE plugin for browsing Linux Do (Discourse) community forum, featuring:

  • Developer Documentation / Code Camouflage Mode: Integrates seamlessly into the IDE editor with Monospace/JetBrains Mono typography, Git-Log/Issue-tracker style list, and RFC/Javadoc formatted post reader.
  • DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH): Defaults to LinuxDo DoH (https://ldh.ddd.oaifree.com/query-dns). Custom HTTPS resolvers and system DNS are also available.
  • Cloudflare Verification & Auth: Integrated JCEF authentication to solve Cloudflare Turnstile challenges and persist session credentials securely via PasswordSafe.
  • Browsing & Navigation: Compact topic lists with categories, tags, unread status and relative activity times. Paginated search includes matching excerpts and opens the matching floor. Refresh preserves your selection and position. Return to the floor before a jump.
  • Rich Reading & Composing: Quotes, code blocks with copy actions, tables, link cards, details and spoilers. Shared icon toolbars for topics and replies, formatting menus, image uploads and on-demand preview.
  • Forum Drafts: Resume native topic and reply drafts across the IDE and website. Autosave after two seconds, preserve reply targets, and choose between versions on conflicts. No additional local draft-body files.
  • Topic Categories & Tags: Search category names, parent paths and descriptions; the menu closes after selection. A web-style tag picker shows usage counts, removable selected chips, a search field and category restrictions.
  • Notifications & Read Progress: Notifications and optional reading progress synchronization. Ordinary HTTP 429 prompts a cooldown; Cloudflare verification responses prompt manual verification.
  • Boss Key (Emergency Mode): Hide all topic tabs and the API Docs panel; press again to restore.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.4

  • Hide user avatars, fold body images and technical category namespaces are now disabled by default. Explicitly saved settings are preserved; missing options use the new defaults.
  • Hidden Boost and public profile avatars use account initials. Missing or failed avatar images also fall back to initials, with Unicode support and preserved case.
  • Avatar controls retain profile access and keyboard navigation. Settings apply to open readers, pagination and partial updates while preserving the recorded reading floor.
  • Clarified avatar settings and added a Linux Do friend link and default-reading documentation to the README.

1.0.3

  • Boost avatars open public user cards. Your own Boost shows only a trash icon; other Boosts use the topic's existing flag permissions without a request on expansion. Report forms check current permissions and submissions require confirmation with duplicate-submission protection.
  • Public user cards show available profile fields and a full-profile web entry, with explicit retry and safe text rendering.
  • Personal bookmarks now support server search, name and reminder editing, and confirmed deletion. Reminder policies are preserved; updates synchronize across project windows and readers.
  • The reader bookmark entry opens the personal center. Successful refresh replaces bookmark results, and outdated requests cannot restore deleted entries.
  • Forum and personal modules use accessible icons with active highlighting. Embedded login pages retain Tab and Shift+Tab navigation.
  • Hot topics now use the forum Hot endpoint instead of the daily Top list. Includes the pending personal-content, notification and Markdown-editor improvements.

1.0.2

  • Boost now uses an inline floor popover and avatar bubbles. Server permissions control sending and withdrawing your own Boost. Grapheme-aware limits, IME composition guards and shared submission locks prevent invalid or duplicate sends.
  • Foreground reading measures visible post bodies and independent topic time. A persistent, account-scoped queue retries failed timing batches after login, with bounded batches, request spacing and server cooldowns. Pending synchronization is visible in reading tools.
  • Boost updates preserve body nodes and reading position; live IDE color changes preserve popover input.
  • 楼层号和未读小蓝点移到楼层信息行的最右侧，左侧头像紧邻用户名；已读后楼层信息和正文不再发生位移。
  • 修复首次打开帖子的可见楼层未自动标记已读：计时依据选中文档、正文可见和 IDE 前台状态，允许输入焦点留在话题列表或工具窗口，后台和隐藏文档仍暂停。
  • Expanded advanced search, combined category/tag filtering, consistent tag pickers and live composer theme updates.

1.0.1

  • Fixed stale rendering during window resizing, browser startup hangs after disconnection, and blocked Windows IPC cleanup. Failed readers offer retry and restore the cached topic and floor.
  • Compact, consistent icon actions show only currently available capabilities. Reading tools align with the document header; Share is inside More. Removed redundant floor labels and duplicate bookmark symbols.
  • Post pages follow IDE themes and reading settings immediately. Login and verification trigger one topic-list refresh; foreground reading updates unread markers and synchronizes progress.
  • Added bundled syntax highlighting, MathJax and Mermaid, enhanced image viewing, and controlled click-to-load video embeds.
  • Added paginated topic search, author and popular-reply filters, quote context, a contents menu, bookmarks and notification levels. Long topics use bounded rendering and body caches.
  • Server permissions govern reactions, editing, history, soft deletion, restoration, custom flags, polls and supported topic votes and accepted answers. Updates preserve reading position; failed likes do not reload the page.

idea-plugin.name: DokuWiki Preview
idea-plugin.description:
DokuWiki Preview adds a live, side-by-side preview for DokuWiki pages — edit the markup on the left, see the rendered page on the right as you type.

Which files

  • Pages inside a DokuWiki data tree: any .txt file below <wiki>/data/pages/. Namespaces, internal links and media (data/media/) resolve just like in the wiki.
  • Standalone files with the extension .dokuwiki or .dw.

Supported syntax

Headings, paragraphs, bold / italic / underline / monospace, <del>, <sub>, <sup>, forced line breaks, internal / external / interwiki / e-mail links, images and media links with size and alignment, ordered and unordered lists, tables with column and row spans, quotes, <code> and <file> blocks, preformatted text, footnotes, %% / <nowiki> and horizontal rules.

Plugins

  • Wrap: <WRAP> blocks and <wrap> inline spans (plus the <block>/<div> and <inline>/<span> aliases), nestable, with classes, widths, :lang and #id. Styled: boxes and notes (info, tip, important, alert, help, download, todo, danger, warning, caution, notice, safety), round corners, columns and floats (left, right, center, half, third, quarter, group, clear), text alignment, indent, tabs and the hi / lo / em / spoiler highlights.

Navigation

Click a wiki link in the preview to open that page in the IDE; links to pages that don't exist yet (shown in red) offer to create them. External links open in the browser.

idea-plugin.name: Logwren Log Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
Log viewer that needs no setup: open any .log file and it is coloured, folded and navigable. No regex patterns, no per-format configuration.

  • Automatic format detection - Logback, Log4j, Python logging, syslog, Docker, JSON logs and web server access logs are recognised on open.
  • Severity colouring - errors, warnings, info and debug at a glance.
  • Stack traces folded - an 80-line Java trace collapses to one line, expandable with a click.
  • Jump between problems - F2 to the next error or warning, Shift+F2 back.
  • Built for large files - only the visible region is processed, so a 200,000-line file scrolls without stalling.

Getting started

  1. Install Logwren Log Viewer from JetBrains Marketplace.
  2. Open any .log file. Colours and folding appear right away.
  3. Press F2 to jump to the next error or warning, Shift+F2 to go back.
  4. Adjust the colours in Settings | Editor | Color Scheme | Logwren.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.1 - Fixed: colouring stopped with an "IDE error occurred" message in 2024.3 and later. Fixed: stack traces in .log files are folded again. In files with more than 5,000 lines the colouring now follows scrolling. F2 / Shift+F2 take priority inside log files.

1.0.0 - First release: automatic format detection, severity colouring, folded stack traces, F2 / Shift+F2 navigation.

idea-plugin.name: Animated WebP Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
Preview animated WebP directly in Android Studio editor tabs. Static WebP continues to use the built-in image editor.

Includes play/pause, transparent backgrounds, a stable frame counter, and original image dimensions. No JCEF required. Works with animated WebP files in any project directory.

idea-plugin.name: Squire
idea-plugin.description:
Squire visualizes Dagger and Hilt dependency graphs for Java and Kotlin projects, right inside your IDE.

Open the Dagger Graph tool window, pick a root @Component, and Squire resolves its full binding graph — no configuration needed — and renders it as an interactive, navigable diagram.

What you get

  • Complete binding graph — @Inject constructors, @Provides/@Binds module bindings, @BindsInstance, component dependencies, members-injection, @AssistedInject/@AssistedFactory, subcomponents (drawn as nested containers), multibindings (@IntoSet / @IntoMap / @ElementsIntoSet), @BindsOptionalOf optionals, and red MISSING markers for keys no binding can satisfy.
  • Hilt- and variant-aware — discovers Hilt-generated components from component_sources output, tracks the currently selected build variant (marked in the component picker), disambiguates same-named components across modules and variants, and self-heals when the IDE index misses generated artifacts.
  • Two-way navigation — gutter icons on @Component / @Subcomponent / @AssistedFactory / @HiltAndroidApp / @AndroidEntryPoint classes, @Provides / @Binds / @BindsOptionalOf methods and @Inject / @AssistedInject constructors jump straight to the graph node; clicking a node in the graph jumps back to its source.
  • Built for large graphs — ELK layered layout with UML-style ports, optional @Binds delegate inlining, wrapping of extremely wide layers, a quick node locator with camel-case search, floating-window mode for multi-monitor setups, focus-preserving refresh, and staged progress reporting.
  • Fast and theme-aware — analysis is driven by a purpose-built Dagger concept index rather than whole-project PSI scans, graphs are cached per component, light/dark themes follow the IDE, and the UI speaks English and Simplified Chinese.

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2025.2+ or Android Studio (platform build 252–262), with Kotlin support.
  • Pure Dagger projects work out of the box, straight from source. Hilt projects need KSP/KAPT (or annotationProcessor) to have run at least once: the generated component_sources output is where component entry points come from, and part of the bindings themselves only exist in Hilt-processor-generated sources — without running the processor, those bindings show up as missing. Squire picks up the current build variant automatically.

After installing: the IDE performs a one-time project re-index to build Squire's Dagger binding index. The tool window shows nothing until indexing finishes — this is expected, and subsequent startups are unaffected.

Known limitations — Dagger Producers are not supported; javax.inject only; custom (non-built-in) @MapKey values are not annotated on contribution edges.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Gutter icons for members-injection targets in pure Dagger projects: classes with @Inject fields now get the Dagger gutter icon and jump to their members-injection node — previously only Hilt's @AndroidEntryPoint classes were marked. Kotlin covers @Inject properties including the @field:Inject use-site form. Classes already marked via a class-level annotation (@Component, @AndroidEntryPoint, …) are not double-marked.

Fixed

  • Inline mode no longer drops edges and ports: when one @Binds binding was requested from several places (an entry point, an @Inject field, a constructor parameter), enabling Inline kept only the first requester's edge — the rest vanished along with their ports, hiding injected fields and constructor dependencies. Every requesting edge now reroutes to the final implementation.
  • Entry points inherited from super-interfaces navigate to the method: clicking an entry-point port on a component whose method is declared in a parent interface or abstract class (the common Hilt shape) now jumps to the method declaration instead of the component class, for both Java and Kotlin components.

idea-plugin.name: pytest-html-reporter
idea-plugin.description:
View, find and generate pytest-html-reporter reports without leaving PyCharm or IntelliJ IDEA.

Pytest HTML Reporter tool window

  • Shows the report pytest-html-reporter generated, in the IDE's embedded browser: dashboard, test suites, metrics, charts, filters, screenshots, logs, attachments, steps, analytics, archives and themes all come from the report itself.
  • Finds reports in the project automatically and lets you switch between them; remembers your choice per project.
  • Reloads when the report file changes, after it is completely written, and stays on the report page you were looking at.
  • Opens the report in your system browser, or reveals the file, with one click.

Run pytest with HTML Report

  • Runs python -m pytest … --html-report=… --report-open=none with the project interpreter, shows pytest's output in the Run tool window, and opens the report that run wrote, whether tests passed or failed.
  • Uses only the reporter options your installed pytest-html-reporter version supports, and keeps the report location configured in pytest.ini, pyproject.toml, profiles or addopts.
  • Offers to install pytest-html-reporter when it is missing from the interpreter.

Safe by default

  • Reports stay local: no account, no server, no network access needed. Links to websites open in your browser.
  • Untrusted projects never run Python, and their reports are not opened automatically.

Report viewing works in any IntelliJ-based IDE; running pytest uses the project interpreter in PyCharm and IntelliJ IDEA with Python support, or an interpreter you choose in Settings | Tools | pytest-html-reporter.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Pytest HTML Reporter tool window that shows pytest-html-reporter reports in the IDE's embedded browser (JCEF), using the report's own dashboard, suites, metrics, charts, filters, screenshots, logs, attachments, steps, analytics, archives and themes.
  • Report discovery: a bounded background search of the project that skips virtual environments (by their pyvenv.cfg or conda-meta marker as well as by name), dependency folders and build output; afterwards only the folders named by file-system events are re-checked.
  • Report selector listing every report found, with its relative path and modification time; the selection is remembered per project. Open Report… picks any report file.
  • Auto-refresh that waits until a report is completely written and keeps the report page (URL fragment) on screen.
  • Run pytest with HTML Report, which runs python -m pytest <targets> <arguments> --html-report=<output> --report-open=none with the project interpreter (or one set in settings), shows the output in the Run tool window and opens the report that run wrote - after failing runs too, and never an older report for a run that wrote none. Stop interrupts pytest so the report of the tests that ran is still written, and ends it if the interrupt is ignored.
  • Capability checks against the installed pytest-html-reporter (minimum 0.3.0): --report-open is only passed when the installed version registers it, and the report location configured in pytest.ini, pyproject.toml, profiles, PYTEST_HTML_REPORTER_* variables or addopts is respected.
  • Detection of arguments that conflict with the reporter (-p no:reporter, --collect-only, shard legs, --html, --report-open), and an offer to install pytest-html-reporter when it is missing.
  • Opt-in refresh of the viewer after pytest run configurations finish.
  • Open in External Browser, Reveal Report File, Toggle Auto-refresh, Refresh and Rescan for Reports actions; a Tools menu group; Open in Pytest HTML Reporter in the Project view and editor tab menus.
  • Settings | Tools | pytest-html-reporter: interpreter, working directory, targets, arguments, environment variables, output path, viewer behaviour and discovery scope.
  • Containment of report content: subresources only from the report's folder, remote content blocked by default, web links routed to the system browser, no JavaScript bridge into the IDE.
  • Project trust: untrusted projects never run Python and do not open reports automatically.
  • System-browser fallback when the embedded browser is unavailable.

idea-plugin.name: LatherIt
idea-plugin.description:
LatherIt is a fast, modern client for SOAP and REST services - an alternative to SoapUI, right inside your IDE. Open a *.latherit.yaml project file and it shows up as a LatherIt editor.

Preview: the LatherIt user interface is currently available in German only.

Features

  • Import WSDLs, generate sample requests, send them and inspect the response.
  • REST requests with query, path, matrix and header parameters.
  • Test suites with assertions, property transfers and scripts (JavaScript).
  • Mock services for SOAP and REST, running inside the IDE while the editor tab is open.
  • Authentication: Basic, Bearer, Digest and NTLM.
  • Property expansion like SoapUI (${#Project#name}, ${#Env#NAME}, inline scripts).
  • Import SoapUI projects.
  • Project files are plain YAML, made for version control, and saved automatically like any other file in the IDE.
  • HTTPS trusts the certificates of your operating system, like your browser does.

Usage

  • File | New | LatherIt Project creates a project file, File | New | LatherIt Project from SoapUI… imports a SoapUI project (*-soapui-project.xml).
  • Open any *.latherit.yaml file: the LatherIt tab shows the client, the Text tab the YAML.

SoapUI is a trademark of SmartBear Software. LatherIt is not affiliated with or endorsed by SmartBear Software.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.0

  • First preview: LatherIt as an editor for *.latherit.yaml project files.
  • New project and SoapUI import from File | New.
  • SOAP and REST requests, tests, property expansion; projects are saved automatically.
  • Mock services and Basic, Bearer, Digest and NTLM authentication.

idea-plugin.name: JSON YAML XML Key Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
Show JSON, YAML, and XML key paths in IntelliJ IDEA.
Quick Documentation shows the full path of the key under the cursor. Gutter annotations display a marker on every config key line; hover or click it to display the full path. Dense lines show one reformat hint when the configured key threshold is exceeded; click it, then choose Reformat Code in the popup to reformat the file. Settings are available under Tools → JSON YAML XML Key Viewer for JSON, YAML, and XML analysis, tooltips, value types, gutter markers, and dense-line behavior. Supports nested objects and arrays, for example servers[0].host. Escapes keys containing literal dots so their paths remain unambiguous.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Initial release with JSON, YAML, and XML key paths in Quick Documentation and the gutter. Includes array indices, dotted-key escaping, per-format settings, and dense-line reformat hints.

idea-plugin.name: XSDeck for XSD & WSDL
idea-plugin.description:
Understand any XSD or WSDL in seconds, without reading a line of XML. XSDeck adds a Design tab next to the XML editor: the tree of every element, type and attribute with its cardinality, a zoomable diagram of the content model, the documentation of each node, and a jump to its source, even in another file. Generate a valid sample XML or SOAP envelope in one click.

Why XSDeck

  • Fast on real-world schemas. UBL 2.1 (14 files, almost 3,000 components) opens in about 0.2 seconds. Nodes unfold on demand, in the background, so the IDE stays responsive on ISO 20022, UN/CEFACT, HL7 or your own giant WSDL.
  • Schemas split across files, followed. include, import, redefine, chameleon includes, import cycles, and schemas embedded in a WSDL that import each other by namespace only, where most tools give up. Built on Apache Xerces, the reference XSD 1.0 implementation.
  • Samples you can trust. Every sample XML and SOAP envelope is validated against the schema before you get it: values follow the enumerations, patterns, lengths and bounds.
  • Readable. Expand all, collapse all, one more level, double-click to fold. Zoom the diagram with Ctrl + wheel, fit it to the window. The IDE font, light and dark themes. Export it as PNG or SVG, the structure as JSON.
  • Your file associations stay untouched. XSDeck declares no file type: .xsd and .wsdl keep opening in the XML editor after installing, updating or removing the plugin. The Design tab also shows for .XSD in capitals and for .xml files that hold a schema or a WSDL.
  • Private. No telemetry. No remote schema is ever downloaded without your click.
  • Every JetBrains IDE from 2024.3: IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, PhpStorm, Rider, GoLand, RubyMine, CLion and the others.

Free

  • Design tab for the open file: global elements, complex and simple types, groups, attribute groups, with a filter by kind.
  • For every node: name and namespace prefix, type, cardinality [0..1] [1..*], sequence / choice / all, attributes with use, default and fixed values, facets (enumerations, patterns, lengths, bounds, digits), nillable, abstract, xs:any with its namespace and processContents, mixed content.
  • Inheritance made visible: base type, extension or restriction, inherited content shown apart from the type's own content.
  • Substitution groups listed under their head element; recursive types marked ↻ instead of unfolding forever.
  • xs:documentation in tooltips and in the detail panel (CCTS definitions of UBL and UN/CEFACT included).
  • Diagram of the content model, left to right: boxes for elements, symbols for compositors, cardinalities on the links, attributes in the boxes; zoom, fit, pan, unfold node by node.
  • Navigation: double-click or F4 opens the declaration in the XML editor; the caret in the XML editor selects the matching node; Show in Design from the editor; Open in XSDeck from an XML document through its xsi:schemaLocation.
  • Search by name across the schema, Show Usages of a type, and the list of problems with their location.
  • The WSDL structure: services, ports and addresses, bindings (SOAP 1.1 or 1.2, document or rpc, soapAction), operations, messages and parts.
  • Linked schemas that are not loaded show as clearly locked nodes, with no popup and no reminder.

With the license

  • Multi-file resolution: includes and imports followed through the files of your project, the schema mappings of the IDE and OASIS XML catalogs; remote schemas downloaded on a click and cached, with an option to always allow a host.
  • Full WSDL view: each operation unfolded down to the XSD elements of its messages, inconsistencies reported (missing message or element, binding without port).
  • Sample XML of any element: mandatory or all content, depth limit, choices and occurrences commented, values that respect the facets, linked to its schema so the XML editor validates and completes it. SOAP request and response envelopes of an operation, matching its binding. Every sample is validated against the schema before you get it.
  • Exports: the structure as JSON (definitions or unfolded tree, with or without facets), the diagram as PNG at the scale you choose and as SVG.

Try every feature free for 30 days. Without a license, the free features keep working with no time limit.

XSDeck is an independent product of KITSS TECH. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by the W3C, OASIS or UN/CEFACT.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Design tab next to the XML editor of XSD and WSDL files, also for .XSD / .WSDL in capitals and for .xml files holding a schema or a WSDL. No file type is declared: .xsd and .wsdl keep opening in the XML editor of the IDE.
  • Tree of global elements, complex and simple types, groups, attribute groups and attributes, with a filter by kind, and the option to show the components of imported schemas.
  • Every node shows its namespace prefix, type, cardinality, compositor (sequence, choice, all), attributes with use, default and fixed values, facets, nillable, abstract, xs:any and mixed content.
  • Inheritance: base type, extension or restriction, inherited content shown apart from the type's own content.
  • Substitution groups listed under their head element; recursive types marked and never unfolded forever.
  • xs:documentation in tooltips and in the detail panel, CCTS definitions of UBL and UN/CEFACT included.
  • Diagram of the content model, left to right, with zoom (Ctrl + wheel, fit, actual size), panning and node-by-node unfolding, in the light or dark theme of the IDE.
  • Expand all, collapse all, expand one level, double-click to fold; Jump to Source (F4) from any node, in the open file or in an included or imported one.
  • The caret in the XML editor selects the matching node; Show in XSDeck Design from the editor; Open in XSDeck from an XML document through its xsi:schemaLocation.
  • XSDeck tool window: search by name across the whole schema set, problems with their location, usages of a type or an element.
  • Multi-file resolution: include, import, redefine, chameleon includes, import cycles, unsaved editor content, schema mappings of the IDE and OASIS XML catalogs (license).
  • Remote schemas are never downloaded without a click; downloaded ones are cached, a host can be always allowed, and a failed download is reported once (license).
  • WSDL 1.1 view: services, ports and addresses, bindings (SOAP 1.1 or 1.2, document or rpc, soapAction), operations, messages and parts, unfolded down to the schema elements, with the inconsistencies reported (full view with the license).
  • Schemas embedded in a WSDL are loaded together: an xs:import without schemaLocation finds the embedded schema of its namespace.
  • Sample XML of an element (mandatory or all content, depth limit, choices and occurrences commented, values that respect the facets) and SOAP request and response envelopes of an operation, each validated against the schema, in a scratch file or the clipboard (license). A sample opened in a scratch file points to its schema, so the XML editor validates and completes it.
  • Exports: structure as JSON (definitions or unfolded tree, with or without facets), diagram as PNG at a chosen scale and as SVG (license).
  • Loading in the background with progress and cancellation; the model reloads 500 ms after a change in any of its files, keeping the expanded nodes and the selection.
  • Freemium licensing through the JetBrains Marketplace: the free features never expire, nothing pops up on its own.

idea-plugin.name: AWS Toolkit

Amazon CodeCatalyst

Unified software development service to quickly build and deliver applications on AWS.

  • Dev Environments - launch JetBrains IDEs in a cloud development environment, available on-demand in the cloud and automatically created with branch code and consistent project settings, providing faster setup, development, and testing

AWS CloudFormation Language Server

  • Author templates with documentation on hover, code completion, and diagnostics from cfn-lint and CloudFormation Guard
  • Validate and deploy stacks with confidence using the change set diff view of resource and property-level modifications, view stack details such as events and resources, and explore resources in the new CloudFormation tool window

View, modify, and deploy AWS resources

  • Authentication - Connect to AWS using static credentials, credential process, or AWS identity center
  • Resource Explorer - View and manage AWS resources
  • Run/Debug Local Lambda Functions - Locally test and step-through debug functions in a Lambda-like execution environment provided by the AWS SAM CLI. Supports Java, Python, Node.js, and .NET.
  • Deploy SAM-based Applications - Package, deploy track SAM-based applications
  • CloudWatch Logs - View and search CloudWatch log streams
  • S3 Explorer - Manage S3 buckets, and upload to/download from S3 buckets
  • See the user guide for a full list of services and features supported

Getting started

About

The AWS Toolkit for JetBrains makes it easier to write applications built on Amazon Web Services.

idea-plugin.name: Citrix Secure Developer Spaces - Remote SSH
idea-plugin.description:
Citrix Secure Developer Spaces - Remote SSH

Note: Citrix Secure Developer Spaces was formerly known as Strong Network.

Citrix Secure Developer Spaces (SDS) provides self-hosted Cloud Development Environments in minutes that protect your assets and improve DevOps efficiency. This extension eases connectivity to SDS Workspaces via SSH.

Features

With a single click, this extension allows access to the SDS Workspace via SSH, abstracting away the SSH setup on your machine.

Responsibilities

This plugin creates and manages SSH key pairs used to connect to SDS. Additionally, it manages and stores OAuth API tokens to access platform endpoints.

Requirements

Your organization needs to have the SDS platform deployed on your corporate network. Additionally, a platform administrator should enable SSH access to Workspaces for this extension to function properly.

Compatibility

Important: As of version 1.0.50, this extension supports JetBrains Gateway 2026.2 (build 262) and later only. Each plugin release targets the latest JetBrains Gateway release; older Gateway versions are not supported. Always update JetBrains Gateway and this extension together — an older Gateway will not run the latest plugin, and the latest plugin requires the latest Gateway.

idea-plugin.name: Rojo Runner
idea-plugin.description:
Rojo project support and automatic run configuration handling for your Roblox projects.

To create a Rojo run configuration manually, select a *.project.json file and choose a run mode.

Rojo Runner can also discover Rojo project files in the project root and automatically create and maintain run configurations for them.

Run Modes

  • Serve: Starts the Rojo server. Stop the run configuration in your IDE to stop the server.
  • Build and Open: Builds the project with Rojo and opens the generated place file in Roblox Studio.
  • Build, Open, and Serve: Builds the project, opens the generated place file in Roblox Studio, and then starts the Rojo server.

Building a place creates the generated .rbxl file in the builds/ folder at the root of the project directory.

Automatic Configuration Management

Automatically managed configurations use Build, Open, and Serve by default. You can choose which run modes are generated under Settings -> Tools -> Rojo Runner.

To disable automatic configuration management, deselect every run mode. You can also exclude individual *.project.json files from automatic management. Manually created configurations are never affected.

The Rojo command-line tool must be installed and available on your system PATH.

Designed to complement Aleksandr Slepchenkov's Luau plugin.

Learn more about Rojo in the official Rojo documentation.

Rojo Runner is independently developed and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the maintainers of Rojo or the Luau plugin.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Added native Rojo run configurations for JetBrains IDEs.
  • Added a project-file chooser for selecting *.project.json files.
  • Added three run modes:
    • Serve starts a Rojo development server.
    • Build and Open builds the selected project and opens the generated place file in Roblox Studio.
    • Build, Open, and Serve builds and opens the place before starting the Rojo development server.
  • Added cross-platform support for executing Rojo and opening generated place files.
  • Added IDE process integration, allowing a running Rojo server to be stopped using the IDE's Stop action.
  • Added lifecycle synchronization so stopping a configuration during startup cannot leave a Rojo process running in the background.
  • Added automatic discovery of Rojo project files in the project root.
  • Added automatic creation and maintenance of managed run configurations.
  • Added synchronization when the project opens and when Rojo project files are created, renamed, moved, or removed.
  • Added project settings for choosing which run modes should receive automatically managed configurations.
  • Added per-project exclusions for project files that should not receive managed configurations.
  • Added support for disabling automatic configuration management by deselecting every managed run mode.
  • Added safeguards ensuring manually created run configurations are not modified or removed by automatic synchronization.
  • Added a custom icon for Rojo run configurations.

idea-plugin.name: STALKER 2 Cfg Support
idea-plugin.description: Language support for STALKER 2 game data .cfg files: syntax highlighting, struct folding, structure view with refkey inheritance hints, brace matching and commenting. Ctrl-click navigation between records: SID references, refkey inheritance and refurl file paths all resolve, with find usages and rename.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.2.3

  • The key name now picks the target. Record names are not unique across kinds — every prototype file may declare its own Default — so LastPhraseSID resolves into DialogPrototypes/ and UpgradeSID into UpgradePrototypes.cfg instead of offering every same-named record. Candidates outside the key's location are dropped before they are parsed, which also makes the resolve cheaper. The 139 key-to-location pairs are measured from the shipped GameData, and a project laid out differently resolves as before.
  • Keys that hold a record name without saying so — BlockingBodyMeshes, AvailableDialogs, DialogMembers, Faction, TargetNode, PreinstalledUpgrades and some forty more — now navigate, complete and rename like *SID keys do. The list is derived from the shipped GameData: a key qualifies when at least 90% of its values name a declared record and the schema types it as a string, which keeps DLC = BaseGame and PresetName = Default out. Roughly fifty thousand corpus entries that were inert text before.
  • Guid-suffixed keys (PlaceholderActorGuid, TriggerQuestGuid) are recognised as references.
  • Every name in a list-valued reference key is clickable, not just the first: a value like RequiredUpgradeIDs = Up_01, Up_02 now carries one reference per name, and the unresolved-record inspection reports each of them separately.
  • Sid-cased and SIDS-cased key spellings are recognised alongside SID, Id and IDs.
  • Values that cannot be record names — numbers and EItemType::Armor-style enum literals — no longer produce a reference under a *SID key.

0.2.0

Fixes IDE freezes. A ; comment outside {...} — as in PhysicsInteractionPrototypes.cfg — used to hang the IDE outright, and every keystroke re-tokenized the whole file, which froze the editor on the multi-megabyte cfgs in GameData. Lexing is now streaming and ; is a comment, like # and //.

  • Array elements navigate: FittingWeaponsSIDs / [0] = GunPM_HG resolves, and the plural key spellings (UpgradePrototypeSIDs, RequiredUpgradeIDs) are recognised — some six thousand corpus entries that were inert text before.
  • Values such as 1.0 are highlighted as numbers rather than as text.
  • Completion and reference resolution are bounded and cached, so neither stalls on a project holding hundreds of thousands of records.
  • Slow resolves and completions are logged to idea.log, since a freeze otherwise leaves nothing to go on.

0.1.0

First release: syntax highlighting, folding, structure view, brace matching and commenting for STALKER 2 .cfg game data, plus navigation across records — SID references, refkey inheritance and refurl paths all resolve, with find usages, rename, completion and inspections.

idea-plugin.name: Sacred Mod Development
idea-plugin.description:
Create and run Sacred Gold mods from the IDE.

The loader starts a JVM alongside the game and sends game events to your mod. This plugin provides the project setup and development tools.

What it does

  • New Project → Sacred Mod creates a Gradle project from a template. Choose Java, Kotlin, or Groovy for the mod and Kotlin DSL or Groovy DSL for the build script.
  • Run Sacred builds and installs the mod, prepares the selected Sacred Mod Loader release, and starts it.
  • Gutter icons identify the mod entrypoint and @Subscribe event listeners.

The project wizard and coderpack new use the same templates and produce the same project structure.

Requires an installed copy of Sacred Gold. The plugin doesn’t redistribute any game files.

idea-plugin.name: LSL & SLua for Second Life
idea-plugin.description:
Write LSL (Linden Scripting Language) and SLua (Second Life Lua) directly inside IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, Android Studio, and other JetBrains editors across Windows, macOS, and Linux.

Key Features

  • Project & File Organization: Manage large multi-file projects using structured project views, shared library, local history, file comparison, GitHub integration, and more.
  • Up-to-date language definitions: LSL functions, constants, and events, along with SLua definitions and documentation, come from the official Second Life language definitions project. The plugin checks for updates or can use a custom definitions folder instead.
  • Code Formatting & Clean Up: Automatically format your code, fix indentation, and keep your scripts clean and readable.
  • Smart Scripting Tools: Instant syntax highlighting, real-time error checking, smart auto-completion, and safe variable/function refactoring.
  • Advanced Preprocessor (LSL only): Use file inclusions (#include), function inlining (#inline), and conditional blocks (#ifdef...) to organize large script projects. SLua uses a module system instead.
  • Memory Optimization (LSL only): Before compiling, built-in constant optimization evaluates static math, replaces fixed variables, and eliminates dead code to help keep scripts within LSL's memory limits. SLua has its own methods.

Second Life® and SL™ are registered trademarks of Linden Research, Inc. This plugin is an independent third-party tool and is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by Linden Research, Inc.

idea-plugin.name: Blockbench

Open a .bbmodel file to use the embedded Blockbench editor. Models are loaded directly from disk, and Ctrl/Cmd+S saves them using Blockbench's own codecs. The standard Text editor remains available for raw JSON.

Use an installed Blockbench runtime, a local web build, or a self-hosted URL. Configure BLOCKBENCH_URL or BLOCKBENCH_WEB_ROOT, or install a managed runtime from Settings/Preferences | Tools | Blockbench.

Blockbench settings and compatible plugins can be synchronized between the embedded runtime and the standalone Blockbench profile.

idea-plugin.name: Godot Embed Play
idea-plugin.description:
Play your Godot 4 scenes right inside Rider, IntelliJ IDEA or any other JetBrains IDE. No extra game window: the scene runs in a dockable Play Preview tool window next to your code.

Features

  • Godot Scene run configuration: pick a .tscn, or right-click one and choose Run. Leave the scene empty to run the main scene. Works with your own launcher scripts.
  • Play again: when the game ends, Stop turns into Play and restarts the scene in the same tab, with Debug next to it.
  • Screen shapes: preview at 21:9, 16:10, 16:9, 4:3 or a phone screen (portrait or sideways), fitted to the panel's width and height, or let the game fill the whole panel.
  • Screenshots, mute and game speed right in the preview's toolbar. Screenshots can render at 2× or 4× the view's resolution.
  • Full renderer: Forward+, Vulkan or Metal, compute shaders and all. Godot renders normally and the frames stream into the IDE.
  • Follows the panel: resize or re-dock the tool window and the game viewport follows, honouring your project's stretch settings. Sharp on HiDPI and Retina screens.
  • Hover-based input: point at the game and the mouse and keyboard go to it; move away and your editor has them back. Drag gestures continue outside the panel, and the cursor returns to where you pressed.
  • Windowless on macOS: no stray Godot window, no Dock icon, and a game that captures the mouse can't take over your cursor.
  • ⚠️ Breakpoints (experimental): with the Godot editor's debug server open, Debug a scene and breakpoints and stepping work through Rider's GDScript debugger, and the view shows a pause overlay while stopped, with the error and a link to the line.

Requirements

  • Godot 4 editor build (tested with 4.7) on your PATH, or its path set in the run configuration.
  • Tested on macOS. Windows and Linux should work but are untested: feedback is very welcome.
  • Windowless mode and the debugger integration are macOS only for now.

Made by Sleepyfant Software. Open source under the Apache License 2.0.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.3

  • Debug a Godot Scene configuration to run it in the preview with Rider's GDScript debugger attached, so breakpoints work without starting the debugger by hand. Debug on a .tscn now uses the preview too.
  • After a game ends, the preview's toolbar has Debug next to Play, to start the scene again with the debugger attached.
  • The pause overlay shows script errors styled like an exception, cut to two lines, with a link to the line that stopped the game.
  • Leave Scene empty to run the project's main scene, like Rider's Player configuration but in the preview.
  • Replace a platform API scheduled for removal, so newer IDE builds no longer flag the plugin.

0.1.2

  • Play again: once a game ends, whether by Stop, the Run window or the game quitting on its own, the Play Preview's Stop button turns into Play and lets you start that scene again from the preview.
  • Running a configuration again reuses its stopped tab instead of adding a new one.
  • Screen shapes: preview at 21:9, 16:10, 16:9, 4:3, Standard Mobile (19.5:9) or Narrow Mobile (20:9), fitted to the panel's width and height. Phone screens can be turned sideways.
  • Screenshots from the preview toolbar, at 1×, 2× or 4× the view's resolution. Saved as PNG and copied to the clipboard.
  • Mute / unmute the game from the preview.
  • Game speed: set the time scale from 0.1× to 4×.
  • The preview's controls moved into a toolbar row, with status on its own line below.

0.1.1

  • First release: run Godot 4 scenes inside an IDE tool window.
  • Windowless mode on macOS; hover-based input with drag gestures.
  • Pause overlay while the Godot editor's debugger (and Rider through it) holds a breakpoint.

idea-plugin.name: QSS Toolkit
idea-plugin.description:
QSS Toolkit - Qt Style Sheet Support for JetBrains IDEs

QSS Toolkit adds dedicated Qt Style Sheet editing support to JetBrains IDEs. It helps you write, validate, navigate, preview colors, manage reusable palettes, and test QSS changes directly from your editor.

Version 2.1 - May 2026

  • Live Preview Tools: Generate PySide, PyQt, or C++ Qt helpers that reload a selected .qss file when it is saved.
  • QSS Colors: Improved saved color folders with search, drag/drop organization, multi-select actions, and import/export support.
  • Editor Workflow: Added context menu actions for inserting colors, saving selected colors, and enabling live preview.
  • Syntax and Compatibility: Expanded Qt stylesheet support, HSL/HSV color handling, validation fixes, and 2026 IDE compatibility.

Key Features

  • QSS Language Support: Syntax highlighting, parsing, code folding, structure view, comments, bracket matching, and smart editing for .qss files.
  • Completion for Qt Stylesheets: Suggestions for Qt widgets, properties, values, sub-controls, pseudo-states, and chained selectors such as QScrollBar::handle:vertical.
  • Real-time Validation: Detects unknown properties, invalid values, incorrect units, malformed declarations, and common QSS mistakes while you edit.
  • Qt-aware Syntax Handling: Supports Qt-specific properties, qproperty-* declarations, palette roles, gradients, icon properties, and template placeholders such as {{BUTTON_COLOR}}.
  • Visual Color Tools: Shows color previews, opens a color picker from gutter icons, and preserves useful color formats when editing values.
  • Reusable Color Folders: Save, search, rename, edit, organize, drag/drop, copy, import, export, and insert reusable colors from the QSS Colors tool window.
  • Editor Color Actions: Use the editor context menu to insert saved colors or save a selected color without leaving the file.
  • Live Preview Tools: Generate small PySide, PyQt, or C++ Qt helper files that reload a selected .qss file in a running app after you add the setup call once.
  • Color Format Support: Works with hex, RGB/RGBA, HSL/HSLA, HSV/HSVA, palette colors, transparent values, and Qt gradients.
  • Universal JetBrains IDE Support: Works in CLion, PyCharm, IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, Rider, and other IntelliJ Platform IDEs.

Quick Start

Open any .qss file to use highlighting, completion, validation, navigation, and color tools. Use the QSS Colors tool window for reusable colors, and right-click in the editor to insert colors, save colors, or enable live preview.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Version 2.1 - May 2026

  • QSS Colors Panel: Revamped saved color folders with search, drag/drop organization, multi-select actions, and import/export for sharing color collections.
  • Live Preview Tools: Added PySide, PyQt, and C++ Qt helper files that reload a selected .qss file in a running Qt app when it is saved.
  • Editor Context Menu: Added Insert Color, Save Color, and Enable Live Preview actions for QSS files.
  • Color Tools: Added HSL and HSV support for validation, highlighting, copy, and insert actions.
  • QSS Syntax: Expanded Qt stylesheet properties, pseudo-states, sub-controls, and icon properties for completion and validation.
  • Validation: Fixed false warnings for Qt-specific properties, qproperty-* declarations, and border values that use Qt color functions.
  • IDE Compatibility: Added support for 2026 JetBrains IDE builds.

Version 2.0.1 - February 2026

  • Bug Fix: Fixed palette(), hsv(), hsva(), hsl(), and hsla() color functions being incorrectly flagged as invalid color values by the validator. These are fully valid Qt QSS color functions and should produce no errors. Reported by @TheDogHusky.

Version 2.0 - December 2025

  • Complete Qt 6.10 Support: All 96 properties and 50 widgets with full Qt 5/6 backward compatibility
  • Advanced Selector Support: 82 sub-controls (QScrollBar::handle) and 44 pseudo-states with intelligent chained syntax (QScrollBar::handle:vertical)
  • Robust Error Detection:
    • Real-time Validation: Detects invalid properties, unknown values, and incorrect units on the fly
    • Smart Parser Recovery: Correctly handles missing braces without cascading errors to the rest of the file
    • Type Safety: Validates measurements (px, pt), colors, and URLs to prevent silent failures
  • Template & Dynamic Value Support: First-class support for template tags like {{VARIABLE}}—perfect for Python/C++ template engines
  • Smart Context-Aware Completion: Relevant suggestions based on widget type - scrollbars show horizontal/vertical, checkboxes show checked/unchecked
  • Enhanced Syntax Highlighting:
    • Semantic Coloring: Distinct colors for Widgets (Teal), Properties (Blue), Keywords (Orange), and Templates
    • Theme Compatibility: Fixed invisible widget/property colors in dark themes using reliable color key mapping (CONSTANT + INSTANCE_METHOD)
    • URL & Gradient Support: Proper highlighting for url(...) paths and Qt gradient functions
    • Improved Tokenization: Numbers with units and CSS keywords are now visually distinct
  • Background Color Highlighting:
    • Visual Color Display: See actual colors as backgrounds behind color values (#FF0000 shows solid red background)
    • Contrast-Aware Text: Text color automatically adjusts (black/white) based on WCAG luminance for optimal readability
    • Accurate Colors: Displays exact RGB values with no forced transparency
    • Alpha Transparency Support: Preserves original alpha from rgba() and #RRGGBBAA formats
    • Accessibility: Implements W3C WCAG 2.0 standards for color contrast (same algorithm as Chrome DevTools, VS Code)
  • Instant Value Suggestions: Auto-complete for CSS units (px, pt, em), colors, alignments, and border styles
  • Professional Auto-Trigger: Automatic completion popup after :: and : for effortless workflow
  • Smart Editing Features:
    • Auto-Close Brackets & Quotes: Automatic insertion of closing characters
    • Smart Indentation: Enter key creates properly formatted, indented blocks
    • Comment Toggle: Ctrl+/ (Cmd+/) support
    • Bracket Matching: Visual highlighting of matching pairs
    • Property Completion: Auto-inserts colon and space for faster typing
  • Advanced Color Tools:
    • RGB/RGBA Support: Full support with gutter previews and format preservation. Transparent colors automatically convert to rgba() for Qt compatibility
    • Streamlined Color Picker: Optimized UI with persistent color mode preference (HSV/HSL/RGB)
    • Visual Gutter Icons: Color previews with borders for transparent colors
    • Gradient Recognition: Support for qlineargradient(), qradialgradient(), and qconicalgradient()
  • Universal IDE Support: Works in ALL JetBrains IDEs (CLion, PyCharm, IntelliJ, WebStorm, Rider, etc.) with NO Python dependency

Version 1.1 - April 2025

  • New Feature: Create new QSS files directly from the IDE's New menu
  • Added file template for QSS files with default styling
  • Improved plugin integration with IDE's file creation workflow

Version 1.0 - Initial Release

  • Initial release with basic QSS editing support
  • Syntax highlighting, code completion, and structure navigation
  • Color palette management and integrated color tools
  • Hex color support with gutter icons and color picker

idea-plugin.name: DryPush: AWS | GCP | Alibaba Deploy & Upload
idea-plugin.description:
Simplify cloud deployments to AWS, Google Cloud Platform, Alibaba Cloud and other cloud services. 1-2-3-Ready!

AWS Services

  • S3
  • EC2
  • Elastic Beanstalk
  • Lambda
  • Lightsail instances
  • Lightsail buckets

Google Cloud Services

  • GCS
  • GCE
  • Cloud Functions
  • (coming soon) Google Cloud App Engine

Alibaba Cloud Services

  • OSS
  • ECS
  • EDAS
  • Function Compute
  • (coming soon) SAS

Other

  • Any SSH server

Key features

  • Simple 1-click deployments to your cloud. Deploy and run applications, upload files and sites in simple and complex scenarios.
  • IDE Run Configuration integration. Run deployments from IDE and combine with other Run Configurations.
  • Contextual actions. Integrated into Project Tree context menu and Widget for easy access.
  • Various payloads. Supports local files and folders, scripts, Maven and Gradle artifacts, preconfigured IntelliJ Artifacts, stream data from local servers or internet (via URLs).
  • Static website hosting support. Deploy your sites to S3/OSS/GCS buckets, improving website speed and caching.
  • Lambda advanced support. Find/deploy to Lambda@Edge distributions, find/clear dependent CloudFront CDN distributions based on API Gateways using the Lambda function automatically.
  • Lambda layer advanced support. Update Lambda functions and all related functions using given Layers automatically.
  • Lambda@Edge support. Automatic display and deployment to Lambda@Edge.
  • Extensive CloudFront CDN support. Find/clear both directly attached CDN distributions and indirectly attached ones for S3, Lambda, Elastic Beanstalk, EC2, Lightsail.
  • Quick uploads. Save targets with or without payloads for quick 1-click reuse.
  • Multi-uploads. Combine different uploads, save multi-uploads for future 1-click reuse.
  • Multi-region. Work with multiple AWS regions in parallel without any need for switching.
  • Multi-account. Manage several AWS accounts simultaneously.
  • Multi-project. Supports both global (shared) and project-specific AWS credentials, facilitating complex multi-project environments.

Detailed feature description

  • Run/Debug Configuration
    • Enabling users to configure and manage deployments directly in standard IDE's Run Configuration menu.
  • AWS S3 buckets
    • Upload files and directories: Transfer files and entire directories to S3 buckets.
    • Manage directory tree: Organize and manage folders within S3 buckets.
    • Static website hosting: Host static websites directly from S3.
    • Static website hosting optimization: Enable automatic caching for static content.
    • Invalidate CloudFront distributions: Set automatic invalidation of connected CloudFront CDN caches after uploads.
    • Supported file types: (any type)
  • AWS Lambda functions and layers
    • Upload function code: Deploy Lambda function code can be uploaded in a few clicks. Assign aliases to function versions and publish versions.
    • Upload layer code: Update layer code for a function, or for all associated functions.
    • Deploy to Lambda@Edge: Deploy functions globally to CloudFront's edge locations.
    • Use S3 for deployment: Optionally utilize S3 buckets for Lambda deployments. Amazon recommends using S3 if the Lambda function code is larger than 10Mb in size.
    • Invalidate CloudFront distributions: Set automatic invalidation of CloudFrontC CDN caches (that are connected via API Gateway) after uploads.
    • Automatic archiving: For non-zip files, DryPush automatically zips the files on the fly for AWS Lambda, to save you time.
    • Supported file types: zip, js, jar, py, rb, ts, json, Go executables, dll.
  • AWS Elastic Beanstalk
    • Deploy applications to environments: Automate deployment to Elastic Beanstalk environments.
    • Remote debug: Enable debug mode for an Elastic Beanstalk application with a single click.
      Note: Make sure your Security Group allows traffic on the specified port
    • Manage versions and descriptions: Track and manage application versions and description.
    • Automatic version increase: When reusing a Quick target, application version would be automatically increased.
    • Invalidate CloudFront distributions: Set automatic invalidation of connected CloudFront CDN caches after uploads.
    • Supported file types: zip, js, jar, war, py, rb, Dockerfile, Dockerrun.aws.json, dll, tgz, php.
  • AWS EC2 instances
    • Upload files or applications: Upload files or applications to EC2 instances to the specified folder.
    • Changing IP support: The IP address is determined at deployment time, allowing IP address changes.
    • Run shell commands before and after upload: Execute scripts at different stages of the upload process. For example, to launch an application after it has been uploaded.
    • Manage directory tree: Organize and manage folders on EC2 instances.
    • Invalidate CloudFront distributions: Set automatic invalidation of CloudFront caches after uploads.
    • Supported file types: (any type)
  • AWS Lightsail instances
    • Upload files and applications: Upload files or applications to Lightsail instances to the specified folder.
    • Changing IP support: The IP address is determined at deployment time, allowing IP address changes.
    • Run shell commands before and after upload: Execute scripts at different stages of the upload process. For example, to launch an application after it has been uploaded
    • Manage directory tree: Organize and manage folders on Lightsail instances.
    • Invalidate Lightsail CDN distributions: Set automatic invalidation of Lightsail CDN distributions caches after uploads.
    • Supported file types: (any type)
  • AWS Lightsail buckets
    • Upload files and directories: Transfer files and entire directories to Lightsail buckets.
    • Manage directory tree: Organize and manage folders within Lightsail buckets.
    • Static website hosting optimization: Enable automatic caching for static content.
    • Invalidate Lightsail distributions: Set automatic invalidation of connected Lightsail CDN caches after uploads.
    • Supported file types: (any type)
  • AWS CloudFront
    • Content delivery network (CDN): Distribute content globally with low latency, DryPush is helping with some key hints.
    • Invalidate distributions: Clear CloudFront caches automatically after your deployments.
    • Advanced use cases:S3/Elastic Beanstalk/EC2 directly-connected distributions, Lambda-indirectly-connected distributions (through API Gateway)
  • Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
    • Multiple Google Cloud projects: supports import Google CLI credentials that can be used with different projects.
    • Upload files and directories: Transfer files and entire directories to GCP Storage buckets.
    • Manage directory tree: Organize and manage folders within GCP Storage buckets.
    • Static website hosting: Host static websites directly from GCP Storage.
    • Static website hosting optimization: Enable automatic caching for static content.
    • Invalidate Google Cloud CDN distributions: Set automatic invalidation of connected Google Cloud CDN caches after uploads.
    • Supported file types: (any type)
  • Google Cloud Engine (GCE)
    • Upload files or applications: Upload files or applications to GCP Engine instances to the specified folder.
    • Changing IP support: The IP address is determined at deployment time, allowing IP address changes.
    • Run shell commands before and after upload: Execute scripts at different stages of the upload process. For example, to launch an application after it has been uploaded.
    • Manage directory tree: Organize and manage folders on GCP Engine instances.
    • Invalidate Google Cloud CDN distributions: Set automatic invalidation of GCP CDN caches after uploads.
    • Supported file types: (any type)
  • Google Cloud Functions
    • Upload function code: Easily deploy GCP function code, including support for multiple files, with automatic zipping for streamlined deployment.
    • Use GCP Buckets for deployment: Optionally utilize GCP buckets for Function deployments.
    • Auto-zipping files: For your convenience, selected files will be zipped on the fly, if necessary.
    • Supported environments: Deploy to environments such as Node.js, Python, Go, Ruby, PHP, .NET, and Java
    • Supported file types: .zip, .js .go, .php, .py, .ruby, .cs
  • Alibaba Cloud OSS
    • Upload files and directories: Transfer files and entire directories to OSS buckets.
    • Manage directory tree: Organize and manage folders within OSS buckets.
    • Static website hosting: Host static websites directly from OSS.
    • Static website hosting optimization: Enable automatic caching for static content.
    • Supported file types: (any type)
  • Alibaba ECS instances
    • Upload files or applications: Upload files or applications to ECS instances to the specified folder.
    • Changing IP support: The IP address is determined at deployment time, allowing IP address changes.
    • Run shell commands before and after upload: Execute scripts at different stages of the upload process. For example, to launch an application after it has been uploaded.
    • Manage directory tree: Organize and manage folders on ECS instances.
    • Purge Alibaba Cloud CDN/ESA caches: Set automatic purge of caches for Alibaba CDN domains and ESA records whose origins point to the ECS instance.
    • Supported file types: (any type)
  • Alibaba EDAS
    • Deploy packages to EDAS: Automate package deployments to Alibaba Enterprise Distributed Application Service (EDAS) applications.
    • Manage versions and descriptions: Track and manage application versions and description.
    • Runtime-aware validation: DryPush detects the EDAS application runtime and validates the selected deployment artifact accordingly.
    • Purge Alibaba Cloud CDN/ESA caches: Set automatic purge of caches for Alibaba CDN domains and ESA DNS records whose origins point to the application's ECS instances.
    • Supported file types: jar, war, zip, php.
  • Alibaba Cloud CDN
    • Content delivery network (CDN): Distribute content globally with low latency, DryPush is helping with some key hints.
    • Invalidate CDN distributions: Set automatic invalidation of connected Cloud CDN caches after uploads.
  • Any SSH Server
    • Upload files and applications: Transfer files and applications to any server that supports SSH connection.
    • Run shell commands before and after upload: Execute scripts at different stages of the upload process. For example, to launch an application after it has been uploaded.
    • Manage directory tree: Organize and manage files and folders on remote servers.
    • Supported file types: (any type)
  • Payloads
    • File(s) payload: Supports all local files or folders, either from project or not.
      Quick target's effective payload is:
      • Project Tree selection - if upload is triggered from right click, and it overrides Quick target's saved payload, if it is present.
      • Original Quick target's payload - if upload is triggered from Widget.
    • Maven artifact: Gets the most recent Maven artifact automatically. Scans target folder according to pom.xml configuration, supports standard Maven plugins that change final artifact name.
    • Gradle artifact: Gets the most recent Gradle artifact automatically. Scans build/libs (for Java), build/outputs/apk, build/outputs/apk/debug, build/outputs/apk/release (for Android) folders for files of types: JAR, WAR, EAR, APK.
    • URL payload: Gets the content available via HTTP, HTTPS or FTP URL, and treats it as a single file. Supports basic authentication.
    • IDE Artifact: If your IDE supports artifacts, and you have any configured, the actual content of the artifacts at the moment of upload would be used as payload.
    • Choose later from Project Tree payload: This option is basically NO predefined payload, so actual payload could be chosen later (from Project Tree right click/context menu).
    • Payload override: Selecting payload from project tree, for a Quick target with payload, will override the target's payload.
  • Quick targets, multi-uploads
    • Save upload configuration: You can optionally save an upload configuration, with or without the payload, for further reuse, as 'Quick target'.
    • Widget support: Quick targets with payload could be run from Widget, simplifying access to DryPush features.
    • Payload override: Selecting payload from project tree, for a Quick target with payload, will override the target's payload.
    • Combine upload configurations: Quick targets can be combined into a 'Multi-upload', or 'Multiple Quick target', for further reuse, so that all Quick targets/uploads can be triggered with a single click.
    • Visual help: Dynamic icons of Quick targets and Multi-uploads are based on the chosen target, helping to visually identify them.
  • Multi-account, multi-region, multi-project
    • Multi-account: Create as many accounts/credentials as you like, switching between them when selecting targets is easy.
    • Multi-region: If you have resources in multiple regions, you can select active regions that DryPush will pull resources from, thus eliminating the need to switch regions.
    • Shared and project-bound accounts: To support multi-project environments, credentials could be restricted to a single project, or shared across projects, easing work with multiple projects.

Miscellaneous

  • Visual aesthetics. If you dislike the bright appearance of the DryPush logo in the interface, you can change the icon in plugin settings.
  • Encryption. All passwords and credentials are encrypted with AES-128 encryption.
  • Further development. We are considering AWS containerization services and supporting other cloud providers (GCP, Azure, Alibaba). As we are discussing priorities of features and services to support, your feedback would be greatly appreciated.

Open to feedback!

Your feedback matters! Please email us at drypush.feedback@implemica.com
Your insights and suggestions directly shape the future development of DryPush.
Feel free to shout, curse, or even throw virtual mud!
We appreciate any and all feedback.

Class initialization must not depend on services. Consider using instance of the service on-demand instead.

Version 2024.8.14


1. Performance improvements in SSH uploads (EC2, Lightsail, other SSH-based servers), and EC3 uploads (where applicable)
  • Reduce the number of I/O operations while scanning local files with a large number of folders and files.
  • Handling of large directories is now significantly faster.
  • Small files under 32KB no longer use temporary files to improve performance, as the likelihood of failure in a single-write operation is very low.
  • Increased the number of upload threads from 4 to 8, based on real-world performance testing.
  • Changed sequential SSH connects to parallel connects to speed up SSH uploads.

2. Multiple upload dialog enhancements
  • Handle Ctrl+Click correctly, allowing users to pre-select uploads in the list without checking the checkboxes.
  • Display the number of selected uploads, making it more convenient to track selections when dealing with a large number of uploads.

3. Compatibility with most recent IDEs of version 2024.2.0.1.

Thank you for sharing your feedback and providing valuable insights!

Version 2024.8.3


1. SSH Multi-File Support
Added support for uploading multiple files/folders to all SSH-based servers, including EC2 instances, Lightsail instances, and generic SSH servers. Thanks to our users for feedback/request regarding this.

2. SSH Connection Closure Fix
Fixed an issue where the SSH connection was not closed after a successful upload.

3. SSH Test Connection
Introduced a 'Test Connection' option in the authentication panels for all SSH-based servers, for user convenience.

4. Folder Content Selection
The 'folder content' payload option is now available if at least one directory is selected, not just when only directories are selected.

5. Lambda Supported Files
Implemented filtering for all file types supported by AWS Lambda across all platforms, including less common ones like Go, Rust, and bootstrap.

6. MacOS AWS CLI not being identified fix
Resolved an issue where the AWS CLI was not recognized on macOS.

7. Screenshots, help within plugin
Implemented comprehensive video instructions for all services supported by DryPush and polished existing screenshots. Added helpful image guides to help icons in dialogs.

8. Several minor improvements and fixes
We are continually working to enhance DryPush to better support your work. Your feedback is always appreciated!

Version 2024.8.2

Hot fixes right after the actual release.
Many minor polishes, improvements, bugfixes.
We promise, next time we will list improvements.

Version 2024.8.1

Hello World!

idea-plugin.name: ImageVector Wizard
idea-plugin.description:
ImageVector Wizard converts and optimizes SVG and Android Vector Drawable (XML) files into Compose ImageVector Kotlin source. Convert from the wizard, right in the editor, or just by asking an AI agent like Claude — the plugin connects to the IDE's built-in MCP server.

Convert

  • Single file or whole folder at once
  • Live preview updates as you change settings, so you see the result before converting
  • Optional optimization pass — smaller, cleaner output (svgo for SVG, avocado for XML)
  • Simplify paths slider (None / Light / Aggressive) for icons that don't need pixel-perfect fidelity
  • Optionally emits a @Preview composable next to each generated icon
  • Handles very detailed icons (illustrations, flag emblems with hundreds of paths) that other converters can't finish compiling

Editor integration

  • Rendered previews replace the generic .kt icon in the Project view, so ImageVector files stand out at a glance (toggle under Settings → Tools → ImageVector Wizard)
  • Live gutter previews of every ImageVector property — at the declaration and at every usage site
  • Click a gutter icon at a usage site to swap which icon the reference points to. Imports are updated automatically.
  • Dynamic colors defined in sealed-class color hierarchies are resolved so previews show real colors

AI agents (MCP)

  • Adds a convert_svg_to_imagevector tool to the IDE's built-in MCP server, so Claude Code, Claude Desktop, or any MCP-connected agent can convert SVGs into ImageVector files in your open project. The agent can specify the accessor name, package, simplify level and preview per request, falling back to your last wizard settings for anything it omits. Enable the server under Settings → Tools → MCP Server and connect your client; the tool appears automatically.

The wizard UI mirrors Android Studio's Vector Asset Studio. Works on IntelliJ IDEA 2025.2+ (Community and Ultimate) and Android Studio.

idea-plugin.name: Import Svg From Clipboard
idea-plugin.description:
Overview

Import SVG from Clipboard is a plugin for Android Studio that allows developers to seamlessly import SVG content from their clipboard and convert it into Android VectorDrawable or ImageVector formats.
It is especially useful for importing SVGs directly from design tools like Figma into your Android or KMP projects, without any extra steps.

Usage

Importing as VectorDrawable

  1. Copy the SVG content to your clipboard from any source (e.g., Figma, SVG editor), or copy an SVG file.
  2. In Android Studio, right-click the module folder, res folder, or composeResource folder (in KMP projects) where you want to save the VectorDrawable.
  3. Select Import SVG From Clipboard As VectorDrawable from the context menu.

Importing as ImageVector

  1. Copy the SVG content to your clipboard from any source (e.g., Figma, SVG editor), or copy an SVG file.
  2. In Android Studio, right-click the folder where you want to save the ImageVector.
  3. Select Import SVG From Clipboard As ImageVector from the context menu.

  • Add back the org.gradle.toolchains.foojay-resolver-convention Gradle settings plugin

Fixed

  • Replace the deprecated DynamicBundle(String) constructor with DynamicBundle(MyBundle::class.java, BUNDLE) for IntelliJ IDEA 2026.3 EAP (263.5153.40).
  • Test project-service registration and resource-bundle lookups without invoking a full build on an empty IDE fixture.
  • Fail plugin verification on deprecated API usages.
  • Apply source-based level obfuscation before identifier renaming and honor the string-obfuscation setting.
  • Preserve external API members, reflection class names, annotation class literals, and Java string identity during obfuscation; add executable regression and target-project smoke checks.
  • Correct operator rewrite formulas and source ranges while preserving precedence, operand evaluation, and numeric promotion; retain expressions whose types cannot be established safely.
  • Encode constant-sensitive string expressions without losing Java compile-time constant identity; retain runtime char-array encoding for ordinary literals.
  • Keep declaration-dependent statements together during control-flow flattening instead of hoisting locals, preserving final constants, definite assignment, initializer order, and field/local binding.
  • Preserve quoted annotation data and unrelated forName receivers while rewriting real class literals and reflection targets.
  • Avoid generated identifier collisions in dispatcher, opaque-predicate, and dummy-code insertion; preserve explicit constructor calls before injected statements.
  • Preserve generic parameter boundaries and local mutation state during method splitting, and reject inferred-lambda shadowing in operator type proofs.
  • Use actual source literal boundaries for AES replacement of non-BMP text while retaining the existing escaped/path-literal exclusion policy.
  • findJavaWeak.py standalone entry point no longer uses a hardcoded C:/taintboom/... path; it now takes a target path argument (python findJavaWeak.py <path>).
  • Regenerated pyscripts/check_hash: the committed manifest was stale (content mismatches) and missing five scripts imported by levelObfuscate (controlFlowFlatten, opaquePredicate, reflectionIndirect, stringSplit, javaValidate), which the runtime script-integrity gate would have rejected.
  • Fixed Run Plugin run configuration logs location

Removed

  • Removed Run Qodana and Run UI for UI Tests run configurations

idea-plugin.name: Flutter Asset Studio
idea-plugin.description:
Browse your Flutter project's images, edit its translations, and check its app icons

Assets

  • Every image from your project and its packages, in one grid
  • Real-time search, sorting, and preview in place
  • Copy a path, find Dart usages, or delete — from the asset itself
  • PNG, JPG, SVG, GIF and BMP

Translations

  • One table: a row per key, a column per locale, so a gap is visible instead of hunted for
  • Reads gen_l10n / flutter_intl ARB, and flat or nested JSON (easy_localization and friends) — found automatically from l10n.yaml, pubspec.yaml or the usual folders
  • Edit a value in place; add or delete a key across every locale as one undoable step; add a locale scaffolded from your base
  • Writes back in place: your key order, indentation, nesting and line endings are left exactly as they were, so the diff shows only what you changed
  • A file that will not parse flags its own column and leaves the rest of the grid working
  • Filter by key or value, show only missing translations, and choose which locale columns you want
  • Placeholder mismatches between a locale and the base are pointed out before your users find them
  • Follows the file: break a translation file in the editor and its column says so immediately; fix it and the column comes back

App icons

  • Your app icons for every Flutter target — Android, iOS, macOS, web, Windows and Linux — every density, catalog slot and ICO size
  • Follows what the project actually declares — AndroidManifest.xml, Contents.json, manifest.json, Runner.rc — so a renamed icon or an adaptive icon is read correctly, not assumed
  • Flags what would cost you a release: a declared icon that is not on disk, a density bucket you forgot to regenerate, an icon that is not square, and an iOS icon with an alpha channel, which App Store Connect rejects at upload
  • Read-only, and it never runs a build
idea-plugin.change-notes:

Added

  • iOS icons with transparency are flagged as errors, because the App Store rejects them at upload.
  • Your project's own settings are followed. Icons are found through AndroidManifest.xml, the Xcode asset catalogs, manifest.json, Runner.rc and .desktop files, so renamed and adaptive Android icons work.

idea-plugin.description:
Rafiq Al-Iman – Your Spiritual Companion in Coding

Rafiq Al-Iman is a JetBrains plugin designed for Muslim developers, helping you stay connected to your faith while coding. Whether you need accurate prayer time reminders, Quran recitations, or supplications (اذكار) displayed during builds, this plugin seamlessly integrates with IntelliJ IDEA and Android Studio to enhance your spiritual experience.

Features

🕌 Accurate Prayer Time Reminders

📿 Remembrance & Supplications (اذكار)

  • Displays random supplications (اذكار) during project builds or syncs.
  • Helps you remember Allah during waiting times.
  • A gentle spiritual reminder while you work.

🎨 Seamless UI Integration

  • Designed to blend naturally into JetBrains IDEs (IntelliJ IDEA, Android Studio, etc.).
  • Minimalist and elegant design for a non-intrusive experience.

🛠 Installation & Setup

✅ Enable JCEF for Quran Player

If the Quran player does not work, please ensure JCEF is enabled in IntelliJ:

  1. Open Find Action (Ctrl + Shift + A / Cmd + Shift + A).
  2. Search for Registry and open it.
  3. Look for ide.browser.jcef.enabled.
  4. Set it to true.

✅ Fix Quran Player in Android Studio

Android Studio may start with a JDK version that does not support JCEF. To fix this:

  1. Open "Search All" (magnifying glass in top right) or use Ctrl + Shift + A (Cmd + Shift + A on macOS).
  2. Search for "Choose boot Java runtime for the IDE".
  3. Select the latest JDK version in the "New:" dropdown for example (e.g., 17.0.12+7-b1504.27 JetBrains Runtime with JCEF).
  4. Click OK and wait for installation.
  5. Restart Android Studio.

📥 Download & Get Started
