idea-plugin.name: Batch Rename files
idea-plugin.description:
Batch Rename Plugin for Java and Kotlin Files

English Description:

A plugin for batch renaming Java and Kotlin class files in Android Project. This plugin helps developers efficiently rename multiple files at once while maintaining all references and dependencies.

Features:

  • Batch rename multiple Java and Kotlin files simultaneously
  • Intelligent pattern-based renaming using wildcards
  • Automatically updates all references and imports
  • Preserves code structure and functionality

How to use:

  1. Select multiple Java/Kotlin files in Project view
  2. Right-click and select "Batch Rename"
  3. You can either enter a new file name directly or use a pattern with * wildcard. Enter a naming pattern using * as placeholder for original name
    Examples:
    • For file "A.java", using pattern "Prefix*" will rename it to "PrefixA.java"
    • For file "A.java", using pattern "*Suffix" will rename it to "ASuffix.java"
  4. Confirm changes to apply renaming

中文描述：

一个用于在Android 项目中批量重命名Java和Kotlin类文件的插件。该插件帮助开发者高效地一次性重命名多个文件，同时保持所有引用和依赖关系。

功能特点：

  • 同时批量重命名多个Java和Kotlin文件
  • 使用通配符进行智能模式匹配重命名
  • 自动更新所有引用和导入
  • 保持代码结构和功能完整性

使用方法：

  1. 在项目视图中选择多个Java/Kotlin文件
  2. 右键单击并选择"批量重命名"
  3. 可以直接输入新的文件名称，也可以使用*通配符命名模式。输入命名模式，使用*作为原始名称的占位符
    例如：
    • 对于文件"A.java"，使用模式"Prefix*"将其重命名为"PrefixA.java"
    • 对于文件"A.java"，使用模式"*Suffix"将其重命名为"ASuffix.java"
  4. 确认更改以应用重命名

idea-plugin.name: D-Pad-UI-Addon
idea-plugin.description:
A Directional Pad UI addon for Android Studio.
There are two basic ways to invoke a command:
  • Through the View->Tool Windows->Directional Pad menu
  • By searching the icon amongst the tools in the application frame, normally on the right.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Full Android Emulator compatibility via gRPC — D-Pad key events are sent to the emulator's EmulatorController.sendKey service as raw evdev codes, the same codes and the same guest-side input path (user_event_keycode → QEMU → guest evdev) that the Emulator's own Extended Controls D-Pad uses
  • Automatic device routing: emulators are detected and controlled via gRPC, physical devices continue to use ADB
  • Graceful fallback: if gRPC is unusable, the plugin falls back to ADB and stops retrying gRPC for that device
  • Proper keydown/keyup event support for emulators via evdev keycodes (previously ADB did not distinguish between down and up)
  • Emulator discovery: reads the avd/running/pid_*.ini files the emulator publishes to obtain its real gRPC port and per-launch auth token, matching on port.serial
  • Auth token support: sends authorization: Bearer <grpc.token>, as required by the emulator's StaticTokenAuth
  • Long-press support over gRPC: the key is held down client-side, since the emulator has no server-side hold
  • Unit tests for discovery-file parsing, endpoint resolution, evdev keycode mappings, auth headers and long-press timing

Changed

  • Introduced KeyEventSender abstraction layer with AdbKeyEventSender and EmulatorGrpcKeyEventSender implementations
  • Replaced synchronous ShellCommandsFactory calls with coroutine-based DeviceInputRouter
  • Tool window now properly cleans up gRPC channels and coroutine scope on close

Fixed

  • D-Pad centre now sends evdev 232 (KEY_CENTER), not 28 (KEY_ENTER). The emulator guest uses qwerty2.kl, where only 232 maps to DPAD_CENTER
  • The gRPC port is read from the emulator's discovery file instead of being guessed as serial + 3000; the emulator searches a 1000-port range, so the guess was frequently wrong
  • Connections target the IPv6 loopback [::1] the emulator actually binds, with an IPv4 fallback, instead of localhost
  • The auth token is read from the emulator's discovery file rather than ~/.emulator_console_auth_token, which is the console token and never valid for gRPC
  • Taps send a single keypress instead of a bare keydown, so keys no longer stick down in the guest
  • KEYCODE_BOOKMARK is no longer sent over gRPC: its evdev code is unmapped in qwerty2.kl, so emulators silently swallowed it. It now routes to ADB
  • Channel shutdown no longer blocks, so closing the tool window cannot stall the IDE

Deprecated

  • ShellCommandsFactory — replaced by DeviceInputRouter and the new input package

idea-plugin.name: Spotyy
idea-plugin.description:
Spotyy — Spotify Controls + Team Music in Your IDE

Stay in the zone. Spotyy embeds Spotify playback controls directly into the JetBrains status bar and lets you see what your teammates are listening to — all without leaving your editor.

Note: Requires the Spotify desktop app to be installed and running. Playback controls work on macOS (via AppleScript), Linux (via D-Bus / MPRIS2), and Windows 10 version 1903+ (via System Media Transport Controls). The Spotify web player is not supported.

Playback Controls

  • Play / Pause — toggle playback instantly from the status bar
  • Previous & Next track — skip or rewind without leaving your IDE
  • Volume slider — click the volume icon for an inline popup slider; auto-dismisses after 5 seconds
  • Now Playing — live artist and track name in the status bar, refreshed every 3 seconds
  • Adaptive theming — icons and colours automatically match your IDE's light or dark theme
  • Zero performance impact — all Spotify communication runs on background threads

Team Music (Local Network)

  • Listening nearby — see who on your network is currently playing music and what track
  • Vibe match — get notified when you and a teammate are listening to the same song or artist
  • Focus Room — start a shared countdown timer (25 / 45 / 60 min) and invite teammates to focus together; the host can remove members at any time
  • Nearby room visibility — even if you haven't been invited, you can see that a Focus Room is running on your network, who's hosting it, how many members are in it, and how much time is left
  • Ghost mode — hide yourself from the network so no one can see what you're listening to; automatically locked while you're in a Focus Room

Getting Started

  1. Install Spotyy and restart your IDE.
  2. Open the Spotify desktop app and start playing a track.
  3. Open any project — the Spotyy widget appears automatically in the bottom status bar.
  4. Click the 👥 or ✦ button in the status bar to open the team panel.
  5. Use the playback buttons to control music and the volume icon to adjust level.

Requirements

  • macOS 10.15 Catalina or later — or — Linux with D-Bus (any modern distro) — or — Windows 10 version 1903 (May 2019 Update) or later
  • Spotify desktop application (installed and running)
  • Any JetBrains IDE: IntelliJ IDEA, Android Studio, PyCharm, WebStorm, CLion, GoLand, Rider, and more
  • All users on the same local network (office Wi-Fi, shared LAN) to see each other

Permissions

macOS: On first launch, macOS may ask for Automation permission so the IDE can control Spotify. If the widget shows no track information, open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Automation and enable Spotify access for your IDE.

Linux: Spotify is controlled via the standard D-Bus MPRIS2 interface — no extra permissions needed. Optionally install playerctl for more reliable metadata parsing (sudo apt install playerctl / sudo dnf install playerctl).

Windows: Spotyy reads Spotify via the Windows System Media Transport Controls (SMTC) API — no extra permissions needed. Requires Windows 10 version 1903 or later and the Spotify desktop app (either the direct download or Microsoft Store version).

Found a bug or have a feature request? Open an issue on GitHub.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.0.6

Windows support — Spotyy now runs on all three major desktop platforms: macOS, Linux, and Windows.

  • Windows playback controls — play / pause, next, previous, and live "Now Playing" metadata work on Windows 10 version 1903 (May 2019 Update) and later via the System Media Transport Controls (SMTC) API; no extra setup, drivers, or permissions required
  • Track progress on Windows — the status-bar progress bar reflects real playback position and duration reported by SMTC
  • Windows volume slider — fully functional and wired to the system master volume through the Windows Core Audio (WASAPI) API
  • Auto-launch Spotify — pressing play while Spotify is closed starts the desktop app and begins playback; supports both the direct-download and Microsoft Store builds
  • Reliable session detection — Spotyy locks onto the Spotify media session even when other apps (e.g. a browser) are also playing audio, and correctly ignores lingering Store background processes
  • Windows onboarding — first-run setup detects Spotify on Windows (direct install and Microsoft Store) and shows OS-appropriate guidance; tracked separately per platform
  • Silent background calls — all PowerShell-based reads and controls run hidden on background threads, with no console-window flicker and no impact on editor performance

0.0.5

  • Linux support — Spotify playback controls now work on Linux via D-Bus / MPRIS2; Spotify is auto-launched if not already running
  • First-run onboarding — OS-aware setup walkthrough shown on first launch; guides you through installing Spotify, playerctl (Linux), and granting Automation permission (macOS), with one-click copy commands
  • Nearby room visibility — non-members on the same network can now see active Focus Rooms: who's hosting, how many members are inside, and time remaining
  • Focus Room — shared countdown timer (25 / 45 / 60 min); host can invite peers and remove members at any time
  • Listening nearby — see teammates on the same network and what they're playing
  • Vibe match — highlights when you're listening to the same song or artist as a teammate; resets at local midnight
  • Ghost mode — hide yourself from the network; automatically locked while in a Focus Room
  • Light mode UI fixes — button hover color and separator are now theme-aware; no more black hover flash in light mode
  • Progress bar on theme switch — progress bar no longer disappears when switching between dark and light themes
  • Fix onboarding EDT block — onboarding dialog is modeless and no longer blocks the EDT on startup
  • Fix widget ID mismatch — status bar widget now updates correctly on theme change
  • macOS: ~/Applications detection — Spotify installed in the user Applications folder is now correctly detected
  • macOS: Automation permission alert — shows a notification if the IDE is blocked from controlling Spotify
  • Broader IDE compatibility — supports IntelliJ 2022.3+ and Android Studio Giraffe and later

idea-plugin.name: Summon Logs
idea-plugin.description:
Summon Logs Plugin

Summon Logs is an IntelliJ-based plugin that simplifies and automates logging during Kotlin development.

With a single key press (Alt+X), it generates meaningful log statements based on code structure. It intelligently detects what to log and formats the output consistently, saving time during debugging. Note that it only works for kotlin files.

Features:
  • Log if statements
  • Log variable assignment
  • Log function entry with arguments
  • Log forEach
  • Log for loops
  • Log return statements
Usage:
Place the cursor on a line or select code and press Alt+X.

Examples:

Variable Declarations
val name = "Mark"
val age = 28

// After Alt+X:
val name = "Mark"
Log.d("[Main]", "Summon name: ${name}")
val age = 28
Log.d("[Main]", "Summon age: ${age}")

If Statement
if (10 > 9) {
println("Valid")
}

// After Alt+X:
Log.d("[Main]", "Summon 10 > 9: ${10 > 9}")
if (10 > 9) {
println("Valid")
}

forEach Loop
array.forEach {
println(it)
}

// After Alt+X:
array.forEach {
Log.d("[Main]", "Summon it: ${it}")
println(it)
}

For Loop
for (i in 0..3) {
println(i)
}

// After Alt+X:
for (i in 0..3) {
Log.d("[Main]", "Summon i: ${i}")
println(i)
}

Function Entry
fun checkSomething(str: String): Boolean {
return str.isNotEmpty()
}

// After Alt+X:
fun checkSomething(str: String): Boolean {
Log.d("[Main]", "Summon str: ${str}")
return str.isNotEmpty()
}

Return Statement
return b

// After Alt+X:
Log.d("[Main]", "Summon b: ${b}")
return b

Configuration:
Go to Settings > Other settings > Summon Log settings to choose log style and customize tags or formats.

idea-plugin.name: DroidForge: Clean Architecture Generator
idea-plugin.description:
DroidForge: Say Goodbye to Boilerplate!

Are you tired of the repetitive task of creating dozens of files and folders every time you start a new feature in your Android or KMM project? DroidForge is the professional solution to automate your workflow, letting you focus on what truly matters: building amazing experiences.

What It Does

With a single action, DroidForge generates a complete, robust, and scalable feature structure based on Clean Architecture principles. It's the perfect tool for maintaining consistency and accelerating your development.

Generated File Structure

For a feature named "MyFeature", you get this entire, compilable structure instantly.

Fully Customizable

A simple dialog lets you configure the generation process:

  • Target Platform: Instantly scaffold for Native Android or Kotlin Multiplatform (KMM).
  • Dependency Injection: Choose between Hilt and Koin.
  • Navigation Style: Select your preferred navigation setup (Nav2 or Nav3).

How to Use

idea-plugin.name: Firebae
idea-plugin.description:
Firebae — Your Firebase Sidechick

Supercharge your Flutter development with Firebae, the ultimate IDE plugin for seamless Firebase integration. Say goodbye to manual configuration and context switching. Firebae automates the entire setup process, from project creation to dependency management, right within your IDE.

  • One-Click Setup: Connect your Google account and let Firebae link your Flutter modules to Firebase projects. Create new Firebase projects on the fly without ever leaving your editor.
  • Automatic App Detection: Firebae intelligently scans your Flutter project to find all Android package names and iOS bundle IDs, including complex multi-flavor setups.
  • Effortless Syncing: With a single click, Firebae registers your local apps with Firebase, downloads the necessary google-services.json and GoogleService-Info.plist files, and correctly places them for each flavor.
  • SHA Key Automation: Automatically detects and uploads your Android debug SHA-1 and SHA-256 keys to your Firebase project, saving you from tedious keytool and gradle commands.
  • Smart Dependency Management: Add Firebase dependencies with confidence. Firebae finds the latest compatible versions based on your project's SDK constraints, updates your pubspec.yaml, and validates the setup.
  • Modern FlutterFire Support: Generates the required firebase_options.dart file with the correct configurations for all your flavors, ensuring your app initializes correctly on both Android and iOS.
  • Monorepo Ready: Works perfectly with Melos and other multi-module monorepo setups, allowing you to manage Firebase integration for each package independently.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Initial Release of Firebae!
  • Google Authentication: Securely connect to your Google account using OAuth2.
  • Firebase Project Management:
    • List and select from your existing Firebase projects.
    • Create new Firebase projects directly from the IDE.
  • Flutter Integration:
    • Auto-detect Flutter modules, including support for Melos-style monorepos.
    • Automatically discover Android package names and iOS bundle IDs.
    • Full support for build flavors on both Android and iOS.
  • Configuration Automation:
    • Automatically download and place google-services.json for Android.
    • Automatically download and place GoogleService-Info.plist for iOS, with support for flavor-specific directories.
    • Generate firebase_options.dart with correct platform and flavor configurations.
  • Android SHA Key Management:
    • Automatically find and upload debug SHA-1/SHA-256 keys to your Firebase project.
  • Dependency Management:
    • A dedicated UI to select and add Firebase dependencies.
    • Intelligently resolves the latest compatible package versions based on your project's Dart SDK constraints.
    • Automatically updates pubspec.yaml and runs flutter pub get to ensure compatibility.

一个强大的 Android Studio 插件，用于实时显示当前连接设备上正在运行的 Activity。该插件提供了直观的工具窗口界面，帮助开发者快速了解应用的 Activity 状态。

idea-plugin.name: Ad Integration Pro
idea-plugin.description:
Ad Integration Pro

Add AdMob, Unity Ads, Meta Audience Network, or IronSource to your Android app in one guided dialog — no manual Gradle edits, no Manifest tweaks, no boilerplate.

Why this exists

Wiring up an ad SDK by hand usually means reading three different setup guides, editing build.gradle, editing AndroidManifest.xml, and writing the same boilerplate again for every new project. Ad Integration Pro turns that into one dialog: pick a network, pick your formats, click Apply.

Features

  • Multi-provider support — Google AdMob, Unity Ads, Meta Audience Network, IronSource
  • All the standard ad formats — Banner, Interstitial, Rewarded, Native
  • Automatic project setup — Gradle dependencies and AndroidManifest.xml updated for you
  • Ready-to-call helper class — generates AdHelper.java or AdHelper.kt automatically
  • Smart detection — matches your project's existing language (Java or Kotlin)
  • One consistent API across providers:
initAds()
showBanner()
showInterstitial()
showRewarded()
showNative()

Free vs. Pro

Free (always free, no trial limit):

  • Google AdMob
  • Banner & Interstitial ads
  • Automatic Gradle setup
  • Automatic Manifest setup
  • Java / Kotlin helper generation

Pro (unlocks the rest):

  • Everything in Free, plus:
  • Unity Ads
  • Meta Audience Network
  • IronSource
  • Rewarded & Native ads

How to use

  1. Open your Android project
  2. Go to Tools → Ad Integration Assistant
  3. Choose your ad provider — AdMob, Unity Ads, Meta, or IronSource
  4. Choose the ad formats you need — Banner, Interstitial, Rewarded, Native
  5. Click Apply

The plugin then:

  • Adds the required Gradle dependencies
  • Updates AndroidManifest.xml
  • Generates AdHelper.java or AdHelper.kt, ready to call

Example usage

Kotlin:

val adHelper = AdHelper(this)
adHelper.initAds()
adHelper.showBanner(this)

Java:

AdHelper adHelper = new AdHelper(this);
adHelper.initAds();
adHelper.showBanner(this);

Requirements

  • Android Studio or IntelliJ IDEA 2023.1+
  • Minimum Android SDK 21

Support

Questions, issues, or feature requests: chaudharysantosh03k@gmail.com

License

Licensed under the Apache License 2.0.

idea-plugin.name: Project File Notes
idea-plugin.description:
A powerful IDE plugin for file and class-level Markdown notes in JetBrains IDEs.

Project File Notes —— 终结大型项目“代码迷宫”的 IDE 批注利器

入职新公司第一周，面对数万行几百个类陌生代码，你是否也曾在深夜反复翻，却仍记不住它的核心职责？
为解决这一痛点，我通宵达旦打造了 Project File Notes —— 一个专为 JetBrains IDE（IntelliJ IDEA、Android Studio 等）设计的文件/类级批注插件。

🚀 为什么你需要它？

在大型、遗留或团队协作项目中，文档缺失、上下文遗忘是常态。本插件让你为任意文件或类添加 持久化、非侵入式、可同步 的 Markdown 笔记，并在每次打开文件时自动展示，真正实现“所见即所得”的上下文记忆。

✨ 核心特性

  • 精准批注粒度：支持文件级（.java, .kt, .xml 等）及类/函数级批注，贴合真实阅读场景。
  • Markdown 原生支持：支持标题、列表、代码块，甚至通过图床链接嵌入类图/流程图，助力深度理解。
  • 无缝自动展示：切换文件时，右侧工具窗口自动加载对应笔记，零操作成本，沉浸式体验。
  • 智能锚定机制：基于 文件路径 + 类名 关联笔记，即使代码重构、切换分支、修改行号，批注依然精准定位，永不丢失。
  • 项目视图标记：已添加笔记的文件在 Project View 中显示专属图标，一目了然。
  • 团队知识共享：支持一键导出/导入 Markdown 格式笔记，便于团队同步、新人培训或存档至共享仓库。
  • 零污染代码库：笔记独立存储，不写入项目源码，不干扰 Git 提交，保持代码仓库干净纯粹。

🎯 终极愿景

我希望未来能构建一个“注解仓库”——每个类自动关联其类图、设计意图与关键注解，让新人入职、项目切换、代码审查变得轻松高效。
这不仅是一个插件，更是一场关于“可理解代码”的协作实验。欢迎你加入共建！

📦 立即体验

插件已上架 JetBrains 官方市场，支持 IntelliJ IDEA、Android Studio 等全系产品。
🔗 JetBrains 插件市场链接
📢 欢迎关注公众号 薪火传，一起链接交流，打磨这个“为代码注入记忆”的工具。

idea-plugin.name: Completor
idea-plugin.description:
Dynamic Autocompletion from External Data Sources

Tired of manually typing keys, IDs, or constants defined in external XML or JSON files? Completor bridges that gap by bringing those values directly into your IDE's autocomplete suggestions.

Configure it once with your data file and powerful XPath / JSONPath queries, and get instant, context-aware suggestions across your project.

Key Features

  • ✅ Provides autocomplete suggestions from any XML or JSON file.
  • ✅ Powerful configuration via a dedicated settings panel.
  • ✅ Simple Mode: Works out-of-the-box with conventional structures.
  • ✅ Advanced Mode: Supports separate XPath / JSONPath queries for keys and values, allowing it to adapt to almost any file structure.
  • ✅ Optionally insert the "value" instead of the "key" – perfect for localization or templates.
  • ✅ A user-friendly file chooser for easy data source selection.

Usage Examples

Example 1: Simple XML (Key in Attribute, Value in Text)

If your XML file uses a common structure where the key is an attribute and the value is the element's text.


<!-- data.xml -->
<definitions>
    <constant id="const.pi">3.14159</constant>
    <message id="msg.welcome">Welcome!</message>
</definitions>

Configuration:

  • Key Path Query: //constant[@id]|//message[@id]
  • Value Path Query: (Leave blank - Completor will automatically use the element's text)

Example 2: Advanced XML (Dual Queries)

When your keys and values are in completely different parts of the document.


<!-- config.xml -->
<config>
    <keys>
        <key>auth.token.google</key>
        <key>theme.name</key>
    </keys>
    <values>
        <value>google-secret-token-123</value>
        <value>Darcula</value>
    </values>
</config>

Configuration:

  • Key Path Query: //keys/key/text()
  • Value Path Query: //values/value/text()

Example 3: Simple JSON (Conventional Key/Value Pairs)

If your JSON contains an array of key-value objects.


{
  "feature_flags": [
    { "key": "feature.new.dashboard", "value": "Enables the new UI" },
    { "key": "feature.beta.access", "value": "Grants beta access" }
  ]
}

Configuration:

  • Key Path Query: /feature_flags
  • Value Path Query: (Leave blank - Completor will automatically look for "key" and "value" properties)

Example 4: Advanced JSON (Dual Queries)

When your keys and values are in separate arrays or different parts of the JSON.


{
  "routes": {
    "names": ["route.home", "route.profile"],
    "paths": ["/home", "/user/profile"]
  }
}

Configuration:

  • Key Path Query: $.routes.names[*]
  • Value Path Query: $.routes.paths[*]

idea-plugin.name: Compose Stability Analyzer
idea-plugin.description:
Developer: skydoves (Jaewoong Eum)
Provides real-time stability analysis for Jetpack Compose functions directly in the IDE.

Features:
  • Hover Tooltips: See detailed stability information
  • Gutter Icons: Visual indicators for skippable composables
  • Inline Hints: Parameter-level stability annotations
  • Code Highlighting: Unstable parameters highlighted
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.15.0
  • The plugin loads again on 2024.2, 2024.3 and 2025.1 - 0.14.0 bound directly to a KaSession.withNullability overload those IDEs do not bundle, so it failed to load. It is now resolved reflectively, and the build gained a gate that fails on new binary compatibility problems.
  • Stability inference matches the Compose compiler, rule by rule - a delegated var no longer makes a class unstable, @StabilityInferred is decoded as a bitmask rather than a boolean, object declarations are stable, vararg parameters are scored by their element type, and @StableMarker is resolved by walking supertypes.
0.14.0
  • Gutter icons and stabilityDump now agree on skippability - the IDE already modelled Compose's strong skipping, which is on by default in the compiler, but the report side did not. Measured against the Compose compiler's own metrics, 38% of composables carried the wrong skippable verdict in the generated .stability file. Fixed in library 0.14.0.
  • Restartability matches the compiler - open members of non-final classes (including interface methods with a body), abstract declarations and local composables now show as non-restartable, and @ReadOnlyComposable no longer does: a Unit-returning read-only composable really is restartable.
  • Heatmap durations no longer read as 0.00ms on devices whose locale uses a comma decimal separator (de, fr, pt-BR, ru, tr, id). The Stability Doctor's measured waste was affected too.
  • Generic type arguments are honoured - Pair<String, MutableUser> and immutable collections with an unstable element type are no longer reported stable.
  • Updated to Kotlin 2.4.20.
0.13.0
  • Editor verdicts and stabilityDump now agree on same-module types - the compiler plugin used to mark a module's own types unstable whenever a sibling Gradle module's group happened to be a package prefix, and it honoured @StabilityInferred on source classes, where the annotation is only present depending on compiler-plugin ordering. Both are fixed in library 0.13.0, so gutter icons, tooltips and the Stability Explorer no longer disagree with the generated .stability report.
  • Updated to Kotlin 2.4.10. Stability inference is unchanged - the Compose compiler fix in 2.4.10 affects per-call-site argument metadata, not the declared-type inference this plugin shows.
0.12.0
  • Kotlin Multiplatform recomposition data - @TraceRecomposition was a silent no-op outside Android and JVM, so the Heatmap, Reality Check and Doctor received nothing from iOS, macOS, Linux, Windows, JS and Wasm targets. Those targets now log recompositions with real durations (library 0.12.0).
0.11.1
  • Fixed: Compatibility with newer IDEs - removed the until-build upper bound so the plugin installs on IntelliJ IDEA / Android Studio 2026.2 and later, and K2 Analysis API access falls back to PSI on any linkage error.
0.11.0
  • Fixed: Non-restartable composables - @NonRestartableComposable, @ReadOnlyComposable, @ExplicitGroupsComposable, inline, and non-Unit-returning composables now show as not skippable/restartable in gutter icons, tooltips, the Stability Explorer, and Doctor, matching the compiler.
  • Fixed: Computed getter-only properties - a property with no backing field no longer makes its class unstable, keeping IDE inference in sync with the compiler.
  • Fixed: Vararg parameters - a vararg composable parameter is treated as an array instead of its element type.
0.10.0
  • New: Stability Doctor - A ranked, quantified "what to fix first" list combining the static stability verdict, cascade blast radius, and measured runtime waste into prioritized prescriptions with one-click fixes (var → val, @Immutable/@Stable, stability-config entry, and guarded remember(...) hoisting for silent-waste parameters). Works without a device (ESTIMATED scores) and upgrades to MEASURED during a heatmap session. New Doctor tool-window tab and Code → Run Stability Doctor action.
  • Trace-All support - With the Gradle plugin's new traceAll mode (0.10.0), the Heatmap, Reality Check, and Doctor receive module-wide runtime data without manual @TraceRecomposition annotations; runtime data is matched by fully qualified name, so same-named composables across packages resolve precisely.
  • Fixed: Android Studio freeze when starting the heatmap on large projects - lookups now use stub indexes and the inlay refresh runs its analysis on a background thread.
0.9.0
  • Updated to Kotlin 2.4.0.
  • New UNKNOWN stability - interfaces and non-final (open/abstract) classes, including Any?, now report as Unknown instead of Runtime/Unstable, matching the Compose 2.4.0 compiler. Shown in gutter icons, tooltips, inline hints, and the Reality Check (skippability is unchanged).
0.8.0
  • New: Stability Reality Check - Reconciles the compiler's static stability prediction with live runtime recomposition data and grades each parameter as confirmed / false alarm / silent waste / justified. idea-plugin.name: GradleArtisan
idea-plugin.description:
Gradle Artisan

A powerful tool window for Android and Gradle developers designed to streamline task management. Gradle Artisan simplifies running, favoriting, and dynamically constructing complex Gradle tasks directly within your IDE, saving you from the command line.


Features:

  • Unified Task View: See a comprehensive list of all Gradle tasks from your root project and all submodules in one convenient place. A real-time search bar allows you to filter and find any task instantly.

  • One-Click Execution with Status Feedback: Run any task from the list with a simple right-click. The UI provides immediate visual feedback for each task's status. The status icon remains until the next refresh, so you always know the result of the last run.

  • Persistent Favorites: Star your most-used tasks for quick access in a dedicated "Favorites" tab. Your favorites are saved per-project and persist across IDE restarts, ensuring your workflow is always ready to go.

  • Powerful Dynamic Task Runner: The core of Gradle Artisan. This feature allows you to build complex, variable-driven task commands without ever leaving your IDE.
    • Smart Variable Discovery: Automatically discovers project variables defined in your root and app-level build.gradle or build.gradle.kts ext {} blocks using PSI analysis.
    • Intelligent Autocomplete: Simply type $ in the template field to invoke a native-style completion popup, suggesting the discovered variables. It fully supports keyboard navigation.
    • Dynamic UI: As you type a template (e.g., assemble$TIER$ENV), the UI automatically generates input fields for each variable, pre-filled with default values from your build script.
    • Flexible Execution: A dedicated checkbox lets you decide whether to run the task with the values currently in the UI fields or to use the absolute latest values from the build file at the moment of execution.
    • Save & Manage Templates: Save your dynamic task configurations with custom names. Load, update, or delete them from a dedicated list. You can even add a fully constructed dynamic task to your main Favorites list.

Gradle Artisan is the perfect companion for developers working on multi-module projects, complex build variant configurations, or anyone who wants to make their Gradle workflow faster and more efficient.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Summary: Fixed Android task discovery on Android Studio Panda (2024.2+ / build 253.x). Replaced the classloader-dependent Class.forName lookup with runtime class-name matching on DataNode children, so the plugin now finds AGP tasks (assemble*, bundle*, compile*, test*) regardless of host IDE plugin module isolation. The previous optional dependency on org.jetbrains.android was silently inactive on AS 253.x and has been removed.

idea-plugin.name: StartupBuilder
idea-plugin.description:
StartupBuilder automatically builds and updates your project as soon as it opens in Android Studio and IntelliJ IDEA.

Features:
• 🔄 Automatically triggers project build on startup
• 🧱 Performs Git Fetch & Merge/Rebase after build
• 🔔 Plays a notification sound when finished (can be disabled in settings)
• ⚙️ Fully configurable via Settings → Other Settings → StartupBuilder
• 📁 Dedicated Protobuf Tool Window with a Build button for each module

### 🚀 How It Works 1) When you open Android Studio, Gradle starts importing the project.
2) If the import is successful, the plugin automatically runs Gradle.rebuildAllModules (the same task that runs when you press Build or Run for the first time).
3) Depending on your selected setting — None, Merge, or Rebase — the plugin:
A) Fetches the latest Git changes
B) Applies the selected action
4) If something goes wrong (no internet, merge conflict, or uncommitted changes), a notification is shown.
5) Finally, the plugin tries to assembleDebug the project. You can check build time and reports in Android Studio. ### ☕ Why I Built This Plugin The very first successful build in Android Studio takes a long time. With this plugin, you can sit back and enjoy a coffee ☕ while everything runs automatically. For faster builds in Android Studio, add the following lines to your gradle.properties file: ```kotlin org.gradle.configuration-cache = true org.gradle.caching = true ``` Also make sure to enable Gradle’s parallel sync in the settings(all of them). ### Protobuf ToolWindow This plugin also adds a Tool Window (left-side panel) in Android Studio that lists all your .proto files, grouped by module. Each module includes buttons for Build, Add New File, Paste File, and Refresh. Whenever you make changes to your protobuf files, you must use the Build button to regenerate the code based on your updated .proto definitions. Note that this Build button only regenerates code for protobuf files—it does not run a full project build.

idea-plugin.name: Safely Obfuscate Source
idea-plugin.description:
Safe File Obfuscator is an Android Studio plugin that safely obfuscates Activity classes and layout XML files before build time. It updates all references across the project — manifest, code, and XML — preventing runtime errors.

Why Safe File Obfuscator?

Typical obfuscators (R8, ProGuard, DexGuard) avoid renaming Activities or layout files to prevent runtime failures. Safe File Obfuscator fills this gap by performing intelligent pre-build refactoring.

Feature Comparison

FeaturePluginR8ProGuardDexGuard
Rename Activity classes✔ Pre-build refactoring❌❌❌
Rename XML layout files✔ Yes❌❌❌
Update manifest references✔ Yes❌❌❌
IDE integration✔ Tools menu❌ Build-only❌ Build-only❌ Build-only

Plans

Free Plan

  • Obfuscate Activity & layout XML files
  • Limited obfuscation operations
  • Manual execution from Tools menu

Personal

  • Unlimited obfuscations
  • Supports multi-module projects

Enterprise

  • All Personal features
  • Restore original Activity names
  • Priority support

How It Works

  1. Open your Android project
  2. Go to Tools → Safe File Obfuscator
  3. Run Obfuscate or Restore (Enterprise only)
  4. Build your APK normally — references remain consistent

Maven项目版本插件，可用于版本快速傻瓜式升级及项目版本展示和项目版本搜索并支持快速生成常见项目版本的徽章及SDK相关配置同步等功能。

Maven Project Version Plugin And Plugin Menu Added In Tools Menu.
Maven项目版本插件，插件菜单添加在工具菜单中.

How to find the operation menu?
如何找到操作菜单？

Tools > Maven Project Version

✨Features / 核心功能



1.(Maven Update) More Strategy To Update Version.

Default Strategy

- must have new version and changed version.

- when version exist and matched will replace and support dependency version is special value (e.g: ${version} / [1.6, 1.8]) will continue replace.

General Strategy

- must have new version.

- when version exist and matched will replace.

Support Must Same Version (Before)

- if checked: project or dependency version not equals project before replacement version will continue replace.

- if not checked: new version will to replace.



1.Maven项目版本更新支持多策略.

默认策略

- 必须存在新版本并且变更版本.

- 当版本存在且匹配时将会替换；并且支持依赖版本是特殊值 (e.g: ${version} / [1.6, 1.8]) 将会跳过替换.（依赖中使用项目版本占位符的会跳过替换，但会修改对应的变量属性版本值；如果依赖中使用的是版本范围的将不做处理）.

常规策略

- 必须存在新版本.

- 当版本存在并且匹配时将替换. （即将依赖中的版本替换为当前要应用的新版本）

支持必须同一版本 (变更前)

- 选中: 项目或依赖版本如果不等于替换之前的版本将跳过替换.

- 未选中: 新版本会直接替换.



2.(Maven Version Show) Active Show Version In Project View.

2.支持项目版本展示在项目视图.

3.(Maven Search) Search Version For Central Repository or Nexus Repository.

3.支持项目版本搜索(中央仓库 / Nexus仓库).

4.Support generate project version badges with shields.io.

Supports the quick generate badges for common Maven project versions (relying on the capabilities of shields.io).
Provides common parameter usage, allowing quick customization of text and color
Add an internal @alt parameter to define the text for the alt attribute in HTML, Markdown, and Markdown (With URL)
Provide URL, Markdown, Markdown (With URL), HTML build types
Provide the ability to quickly enter groupId and artifactId (e.g: by pasting Maven pom configuration or Gradle dependency configuration)
Markdown (with URL) provides built-in Redirect links by default, and you can also customize and enter Redirect links


4.支持项目版本徽章生成.

支持快速生成常见Maven项目版本的徽章 (依赖shields.io能力)。
提供常见参数使用，可快速自定义文本及颜色
增加内部@alt参数用于定义HTML、Markdown、Markdown(With URL)中alt属性的文本
提供URL、Markdown、Markdown(With URL)、HTML生成类型
提供支持groupId+artifactId快速输入能力(如Maven pom配置或Gradle依赖配置粘贴即可)
Markdown(With URL)默认提供内置跳转链接，也可自定义输入跳转链接


5.Project Settings Synchronous

Automatically synchronize JDK, language level specifications, and other configuration features! Whether it's individual development or team collaboration, one person configuration, shared by all! (Need to submit configuration to remote repository)
Automatically recognize and switch to the corresponding JDK version and configuration, whether in project opening, Git clone, Git branch switching, Git rollback, or other scenarios!!! ✨Features / 核心功能



More Strategy To Update Version.

Default Strategy

- must have new version and changed version.

- when version exist and matched will replace and support dependency version is special value (e.g: ${version} / [1.6, 1.8]) will continue replace.

General Strategy

- must have new version.

- when version exist and matched will replace.

Support Must Same Version (Before)

- if checked: project or dependency version not equals project before replacement version will continue replace.

- if not checked: new version will to replace.



Maven项目版本更新支持多策略.

默认策略

- 必须存在新版本并且变更版本.

- 当版本存在且匹配时将会替换；并且支持依赖版本是特殊值 (e.g: ${version} / [1.6, 1.8]) 将会跳过替换.（依赖中使用项目版本占位符的会跳过替换，但会修改对应的变量属性版本值；如果依赖中使用的是版本范围的将不做处理）.

常规策略

- 必须存在新版本.

- 当版本存在并且匹配时将替换. （即将依赖中的版本替换为当前要应用的新版本）

支持必须同一版本 (变更前)

- 选中: 项目或依赖版本如果不等于替换之前的版本将跳过替换.

- 未选中: 新版本会直接替换.

idea-plugin.name: ComposeGuard
idea-plugin.description:
Developer: androidpoet (Ranbir Singh)
Real-time detection of Compose best practices and rule violations in Android Studio.

Features:
  • 39 Compose Rules: Naming, modifiers, state, parameters, composables, and stricter checks
  • Real-time Highlighting: See violations as you type
  • Gutter Icons: Visual indicators for composable rule status
  • Inline Hints: Parameter-level rule violation hints
  • Quick Fixes: One-click fixes shown directly in popup
  • Configurable Settings: Enable/disable rules by category or individually
  • Experimental Rules: LazyList optimizations and lifecycle-aware collection (opt-in)

Based on Compose Rules documentation.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.3.0
  • Project configuration via .editorconfig: the same compose_* keys as the upstream Compose Rules ktlint ruleset are honoured (allowed composable names, custom content emitters, modifier visibility scope, custom modifier types, treat-as-lambda aliases, ViewModel factories, allowed CompositionLocals, allowed forwarding, allowed Material 2 imports, preview naming strategy, nesting depth, and the disallow/enable switches). Nested files merge up to root = true.
  • New opt-in rules: ComposableNestingDepth and CompositionLocalAllowlist.
  • Suppress in file: every violation offers a quick fix that adds or extends @file:Suppress(...).
  • Analyze test sources setting to skip test source roots.
  • Report export: save a project scan as JSON or SARIF from the tool window.
1.2.5
  • Fixed #1 (TrailingLambda): a trailing event handler such as onClick: () -> Unit is now reported on any content-emitting composable with a modifier, not only on composables that also declare a @Composable slot.
  • Single analysis pipeline: the inspection, gutter icons, inlay hints and the statistics scan share one cached analyzer. The duplicate annotator is gone, so violations no longer appear twice, and nested composables are reported once.
  • Suppression: @Suppress(names = [...]), @Suppress("ALL"), class-level @Suppress and multi-id // noinspection comments are honoured. The built-in Lint suppressor also covers UnrememberedMutableState, AutoboxingStateCreation, FrequentlyChangedStateReadInComposition, UnnecessaryComposedModifier and ComposableLambdaParameterPosition.
  • Rule fixes: expression-bodied composables count as Unit-returning; EventParameterNaming handles irregular participles and silent-e verbs; CompositionLocalNaming suggests a capitalised name; ParameterOrdering accepts a required trailing lambda; ModifierOrder flags clickable before clip/shaped background; DeferStateReads only reports eager reads in non-lambda modifiers; RememberState accepts every remember* wrapper; TypeSpecificState skips nullable state; HoistState skips per-item state inside items { }; ContentSlotReused reports per-branch invocation; Material2Usage flags star imports and reports once per file; plus fixes in ExplicitDependencies, ViewModelForwarding, ModifierTopMost, ModifierNaming, ModifierDefaultValue, AvoidComposed, DerivedStateOfCandidate, ComponentDefaultsVisibility, UnstableCollections, LazyListContentType, LazyListMissingKey and EffectKeys.
  • Quick fixes: reorder/move-to-trailing fixes name arguments at call sites first; rename-parameter updates every reference; move-modifier-to-root merges with an existing root modifier; add-modifier-parameter, add-explicit-parameter, add-key, add-contentType, use-lambda-modifier, use-Material3 (keeps aliases) and the Suppress fix were corrected.
  • Settings: rules are listed from the registry, so DeferStateReads and ComponentDefaultsVisibility can be toggled. Rule errors are logged instead of swallowed.
  • Docs: suppression ids and per-rule severities corrected.
1.2.4
  • More False-Positive Fixes (second pass):
  • DeferStateReads: no longer treats ordinary identifiers (text, index, expanded, progress) as animated state — only values produced by animation/scroll/derived-state builders (including delegated by) are considered frequently-changing.
  • TypeSpecificState: removed the non-canonical collection-factory check that flagged plain mutableListOf<Int>(); only mutableStateOf primitive variants are suggested.
  • ModifierReuse & ContentSlotReused: a modifier or content slot used once per mutually-exclusive if/when branch is no longer reported as reuse — only usages reachable on the same composition pass count.
  • ModifierTopMost: modifiers on content nested inside scope-providing emitters (Scaffold, BoxWithConstraints) or slots that expose a scope parameter are no longer flagged.
  • AvoidComposed: only the real Modifier.composed { } factory is flagged, not unrelated composed() calls.
  • MovableContent: accepts the whole remember family (rememberSaveable, custom remember wrappers) instead of only the literal remember.
  • Tests: added behavioral regression suites for every fix above.
1.2.3
  • Major False-Positive Reduction: Audited every rule against the official Compose Rules to stop flagging valid code.
  • Content emission accuracy: ModifierRequired, ContentEmission and MultipleContentEmitters no longer treat value factories like Color(...), TextStyle(...) or PaddingValues(...) as emitted UI — only calls whose result is discarded count as emission.
  • Modifier overrides: ModifierDefaultValue and ModifierNaming skip override/abstract composables, whose parameters cannot legally be renamed or given defaults.
  • Type matching: MutableParameter and MutableStateParameter now match the parameter's own type, so function types (() -> MutableList), wrappers (Holder<MutableState>) and observable holders (MutableStateFlow) are no longer flagged.
  • ViewModelForwarding: only flags ViewModels forwarded into another composable, not those handed to ordinary helpers or effects.
  • EffectKeys: LaunchedEffect(Unit) run-once effects are allowed; a constant key is only flagged when the effect captures parameters that should be keys.
  • EventParameterNaming: stops flagging present-tense/noun callbacks ending in -ed (onSpeed, onProceed, onFeed).
  • Material 2: the shared material.ripple package and material.icons star-imports are no longer reported.
  • TrailingLambda: multi-slot composables (Scaffold-style) no longer require a specific slot to be trailing.
  • Annotation naming: ComposableAnnotationNaming targets @ComposableTargetMarker annotations, and MultipreviewNaming applies to multipreview annotation classes instead of ordinary stacked-@Preview functions.
  • Tests: added behavioral regression tests covering each fixed false positive.
1.2.2
  • Inspection Registration Fix: Corrected ComposeGuard inspection registration mismatch by aligning the inspection shortName with plugin.xml metadata
  • Regression Coverage: Added inspection registration tests to prevent future shortName and metadata drift
1.2.1
  • False Positive Fix: DerivedStateOfCandidate now ignores collection copies and other computed values inside event handlers such as onClick/onRemove, where the work runs only when the event fires rather than on every recomposition
1.2.0
  • False Positive Fixes: DerivedStateOfCandidate now ignores expensive computations inside named event callbacks such as onClick/onRemove
  • Modifier Root Fix: ModifierTopMost and its quick fix no longer treat CompositionLocalProvider as a root layout
  • Trailing Lambda Fix: Event lambda detection now works for custom callbacks following the onX naming pattern
  • Rule Accuracy Improvements: ModifierRequired and ContentEmission now use PSI-based content emission detection
  • Multiple Content Detection: Custom top-level composables with trailing lambdas are now counted correctly
  • Release Cleanup: Updated rule counts, changelog metadata, and build configuration warnings
1.0.9
  • State/Callback Pairing: ReorderParametersFix now keeps state/callback pairs together (e.g., value/onValueChange, checked/onCheckedChange)
  • Improved Parameter Ordering: Smart pairing for common patterns like text/onTextChange, query/onQueryChange, selected/onSelectedChange
1.0.8
  • Rule Enable/Disable Bug Fix: Fixed critical issue with rule enable/disable functionality
  • Restructured Settings Architecture: Improved enable/disable state management for individual rules
  • Settings Persistence Fix: Rule states are now correctly saved and restored across IDE restarts
1.0.7
  • All Rules Enabled by Default: All rules including experimental are now enabled out of the box
  • Simplified Settings UX: Completely redesigned settings panel
    • All checkboxes are now always interactive (no more grayed-out states)
    • "Enable All Rules" master switch to select/deselect all rules at once
    • Category checkboxes act as "select all/none" for rules in that category
    • Parent checkbox states automatically derived from child selections
    • Standard IDE settings pattern (like IntelliJ inspections panel)
  • Fixed Critical Settings Bug: Disabling one rule no longer disables ALL rules
  • Hierarchical Rule Control: Proper Master → Category → Rule hierarchy
  • Fixed Rule Category Mismatch: LambdaParameterInEffect moved to correct STATE category
  • Comprehensive Test Coverage: 45+ new tests for settings and enable/disable functionality
1.0.6
  • Statistics Dashboard: New tool window with violation analytics by category, file, and rule
  • Parameter Ordering Fix: Fixed modifier position to follow official Jetpack Compose guidelines
  • Modifier is now correctly enforced as the FIRST optional parameter (not last)
  • Order: required → modifier (first optional) → other optionals → content lambda
  • Updated ReorderParametersFix quick fix to use correct ordering
  • Suppress Built-in Compose Inspections: Automatically hides Android Studio's built-in Compose lint warnings when ComposeGuard handles them
  • New setting: "Suppress built-in Compose inspections" in Settings → Tools → ComposeGuard
  • Comprehensive Test Coverage: Added tests for all 36 rules
  • New test files for Modifier, Naming, State, Composable, Stricter, Effects, and Performance categories
  • Added EventParameterNaming rule with past tense detection
  • Improved settings UI with category toggles
1.0.5
  • Bug fixes and stability improvements
  • Performance optimizations for rule detection
1.0.4
  • Fixed Suppress action not working for ModifierRequired, MultipleContentEmitters, ParameterOrdering rules
  • SuppressComposeRuleFix now correctly handles name identifier elements
  • Added AddLambdaAsEffectKeyFix and UseRememberUpdatedStateFix quick fixes
  • Improved ModifierReuseRule, ParameterOrderingRule, and LambdaParameterInEffectRule
1.0.3
  • Improved quick fix behavior - only actionable fixes provided
  • Added MoveModifierToRootFix for ModifierTopMostRule
  • Fixed @Suppress support for EffectKeysRule and LambdaParameterInEffectRule
  • 3 New Rules: ViewModelForwardingRule, LambdaParameterInEffectRule, ContentSlotReusedRule
  • All 32 rules with proper quick fixes or suppress options
1.0.2
  • Bug fixes and stability improvements
  • Performance optimizations for rule detection
  • Improved ModifierReuseRule, TypeSpecificStateRule, ExplicitDependenciesRule
  • RememberStateRule now handles 'by' delegate syntax properly
1.0.1
  • Fixed @Suppress annotation support - @Suppress("RuleId") now properly suppresses warnings
  • Supports suppression at function, property, and class level
  • All 29 rules fully implemented with quick fixes
  • Quick fixes now show directly in popup (HighPriorityAction)
1.0.0
  • Initial release of ComposeGuard
  • 27 compose rules covering naming, modifiers, state, parameters, and composable structure
  • Real-time detection with inspections, annotators, gutter icons, and inlay hints
  • Quick fixes for common violations
  • Based on compose-rules documentation

idea-plugin.name: JKS Generator
idea-plugin.description:
JKS Generator Plugin Overview

JKS Generator Plugin Overview

The JKS Generator plugin for IntelliJ IDEA provides an intuitive, streamlined interface for creating Java KeyStore (JKS) files directly within the IDE, without the need to manually use the keytool command. This tool simplifies the process of generating JKS files by allowing you to specify all the necessary details directly through a user-friendly form.

Key Features:

  • Simplified JKS Generation: Easily create Java KeyStore (JKS) files with a few simple inputs. No need to manually invoke keytool or handle complex command-line operations.
  • User-Friendly Interface: The plugin provides a graphical interface where you can enter required details such as:
    • Key password
    • Confirm key password
    • Alias name
    • Alias password (with confirmation)
    • Country code (for the certificate)
  • Customizable File Naming: Once all the details are entered, the plugin generates a d1_keystore.jks file at the selected directory, ready for use.
  • Tool Window Access: After installation, the plugin can be accessed easily through Views > Tool Windows > JKS Generator, making it simple and efficient to launch and use at any time.

Benefits:

  • No Command Line Required: Users no longer need to use the terminal or remember keytool syntax. The plugin handles all the complexities of JKS file generation.
  • Quick Setup: With the form-based input, the JKS file is generated instantly after providing the required details, saving time and reducing errors.
  • Security: Secure handling of passwords and sensitive data during the keystore generation process.
How to Use:
  1. Install the Plugin: Once installed, open IntelliJ IDEA and navigate to Views > Tool Windows > JKS Generator.
  2. Fill Out the Form: Enter the required information, such as key password, alias name, alias password, and country code.
  3. Generate the JKS File: Click the Generate button, and your d1_keystore.jks file will be created in the chosen directory.
Example Flow:
  • Select a folder to save your JKS file.
  • Enter and confirm passwords for both the key and the alias.
  • Specify the alias name and country code.
  • Click the Generate button, and the d1_keystore.jks file will be generated at the specified location.

idea-plugin.name: TinyPNG Compressor Pro
idea-plugin.description:
TinyPNG Compressor Pro

A powerful IntelliJ IDEA plugin that seamlessly integrates TinyPNG image compression into your development workflow. Reduce image file sizes while maintaining quality, directly from your IDE.

✨ Key Features

  • Multiple Format Support: Compress PNG, JPEG, WebP, and AVIF images
  • Batch Processing: Compress single files, multiple selections, or entire directories
  • Visual Comparison: Before/After comparison with side-by-side and overlay modes
  • Smart API Management: Multiple API key support with automatic rotation when limits are reached
  • Advanced Options: Image resizing (Scale, Fit, Cover, Thumb) and format conversion
  • Metadata Preservation: Optionally preserve copyright, GPS location, and creation date
  • Real-time Statistics: Track compression ratios, file size savings, and API usage

🚀 Quick Start

  1. Get a free API key from tinypng.com/developers
  2. Configure your API key in Settings → Tools → TinyPNG
  3. Right-click any image file or directory in the Project View
  4. Select "TinyPng" to compress and compare results

💡 Why Use This Plugin?

  • Workflow Integration: Compress images without leaving your IDE
  • Quality Assured: TinyPNG uses smart lossy compression techniques to reduce file size while maintaining visual quality
  • Developer Friendly: Intuitive UI with comprehensive options for different use cases
  • Time Saving: Batch process multiple images in seconds with progress tracking
  • Free Tier: TinyPNG offers 500 free compressions per month

🔧 Technical Details

  • Built with Kotlin for IntelliJ Platform
  • Uses official TinyPNG API (Tinify Java SDK)
  • Supports IntelliJ IDEA 2023.3+
  • Open source under Apache 2.0 license

Note: This plugin requires a TinyPNG API key to function. Free accounts include 500 compressions per month. For higher limits, visit tinypng.com/developers.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • Image compression with TinyPNG API
  • Before/After comparison
  • Batch processing support
  • Multiple API key management

idea-plugin.name: Launch in Cursor
idea-plugin.description:
Launch your IntelliJ IDEA or Android Studio project directly in Cursor editor with one click - even if you've never opened the project in Cursor before!

Why choose this plugin?
Unlike other similar plugins, this one can open projects in Cursor even when Cursor hasn't previously opened that project. It directly launches Cursor with your project path, making it truly hassle-free.

Features:
  • 🚀 Direct launch - works even for new projects never opened in Cursor
  • 🖱️ One-click access from "Open In" context menu
  • 🎨 Custom Cursor icon in menu
  • 🌍 Cross-platform: macOS, Windows, and Linux
  • ⚡ Zero configuration required
  • 🔍 Smart detection of Cursor installation

Usage:
Right-click on any project → "Open In" → "Cursor" → Done! Your project opens in Cursor instantly.

Requirements:
  • Cursor editor installed on your system
  • Cursor command-line tool in PATH (or Cursor.app on macOS)

idea-plugin.name: Android Resource Usage Tracker
idea-plugin.description:
Track and visualize Android resource usage across your entire project with intuitive gutter icons and interactive popups.

Features:

  • Visual Usage Counters - See at a glance how many times each resource is used with color-coded gutter icons
  • Interactive Click Navigation - Click any usage counter to see all usages with code snippets and navigate directly to them
  • Cross-Module Search - Finds usages across all modules in multi-module projects
  • AndroidManifest.xml Detection - Detects theme and style references in manifest files
  • Smart Deduplication - Uses PSI tree hashing to avoid duplicate results
  • Performance Optimized - Word-based indexing for fast searches even in large projects
  • Supports All Resource Types - Strings, colors, dimensions, styles, drawables, and more

Perfect for:

  • Identifying unused resources for cleanup
  • Understanding resource dependencies
  • Refactoring with confidence
  • Code reviews and audits
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

idea-plugin.name: Quick Note
idea-plugin.description: Quick Note is a JetBrains IDE plugin for fast note capture and a built-in Mock API server (JDK HttpServer). It supports Markdown notes with YAML front matter, Git-branch scoped notes, full-text search, tagging, and a Postman-style UI for managing mock endpoints and serving responses locally. It also includes a Logcat recorder tool window to capture Android adb logcat logs with one-click controls.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Persist and edit common tags with defaults, plus selectable tag checkboxes in add note/snippet dialogs.
  • Add a context-menu icon for the "Add Quick Note" action.
  • Add a Project View context-menu action to show notes for a file in the Quick Notes tool window.
  • Add an edit button in the Quick Notes detail panel to update existing notes.
  • Add Ctrl+Q shortcut to open a note or snippet dialog based on editor selection.

Fixed

  • Search now respects tag/path settings, indexes file paths, and avoids UI blocking during queries.
  • Use NIOFSDirectory directly to prevent Lucene MMap initialization failures on newer IDE runtimes.
  • Rely on the IDE-bundled Lucene to avoid classloader codec conflicts.
  • Avoid IndexSearcher.doc usage to keep search compatible with 253 IDE builds.
  • Avoid ServicesKt.serviceNotFoundError to keep services compatible with 233 IDE builds.
  • Implement ToolWindowFactory in Java to avoid default-method linkage on older IDE builds.
  • Remove UiSizeUtilKt extension usage to keep UI rendering compatible with 223 IDE builds.
  • Implement NoteType in Java to avoid kotlin.enums EnumEntries on older IDE builds.
  • Use reflective Lucene document lookup to avoid storedFields/doc linkage on older IDE builds.

idea-plugin.name: DevSwitch
idea-plugin.description:
DevSwitch - Android Developer Settings Control

Quickly toggle Android developer settings on connected devices directly from your IDE.

Features

  • Quick Access - Control developer options without leaving your IDE
  • Real-time Device Detection - Automatically detects connected Android devices via ADB
  • One-Click Toggles - Enable/disable developer settings with a single click
  • Multi-Device Support - Switch between multiple connected devices seamlessly
  • Auto-Refresh - Settings automatically sync with device state

Supported Settings

  • Toggle Controls:
    • WiFi - Enable/disable WiFi
    • Mobile Data - Enable/disable mobile data
    • Show Layout Bounds - Display view boundaries
    • Profile GPU Rendering - Show HWUI visual bars
    • Show Taps - Display touch feedback on screen
    • Stay Awake - Keep screen on while charging
    • Show FPS - Display frame rate overlay
  • Range Controls:
    • Animation Scale - Adjust window/transition/animator duration (1x-10x)
    • Refresh Rate - Change display refresh rate (FPS)

Usage

Open the DevSwitch tool window from the right sidebar, select your device, and start toggling settings!

Requires ADB and a connected Android device with Developer Options enabled.

idea-plugin.name: Android Icon Generator
idea-plugin.description:
A plugin for quickly generating Android launcher icons.

Key Features:
  • Multi-format Support: Support PNG, JPG images, and Android XML Vector Drawables as source files.
  • One-click Generation: Automatically generate mipmap icons for all densities (ldpi to xxxhdpi).
  • Real-time Preview: Preview the generated icons of different sizes in the dialog.
  • Corner Radius: Support 0% - 50% corner radius settings (Rounded Corners).
  • Smart Detection: Automatically detect the 'res' directory of the project.
  • Custom Naming: Support custom icon filename (default is app_icon).

Usage:
  • Method 1 (Recommended): Right-click on the 'res' directory in the Project view and select "Generate Android Icons".
  • Method 2: Select "Tools" -> "Generate Android Icons" from the top menu bar.
  • Method 3: Right-click in the Project view and select "New" -> "Generate Android Icons".


一款用于快速生成 Android 启动图标的插件。

主要功能：
  • 多格式支持： 支持 PNG、JPG 图片及 Android XML 向量图作为源文件。
  • 一键生成： 自动生成所有尺寸的 mipmap 图标 (ldpi 到 xxxhdpi)。
  • 实时预览： 在对话框中实时预览不同尺寸的生成效果。
  • 圆角设置： 支持 0% - 50% 的圆角裁切设置。
  • 智能识别： 自动识别项目的 res 目录，无需手动选择。
  • 自定义命名： 支持自定义生成图标的文件名（默认为 app_icon）。

使用方法：
  • 方式一（推荐）： 在项目视图中右键点击 res 目录，选择 "Generate Android Icons"。
  • 方式二： 在顶部菜单栏选择 Tools -> Generate Android Icons。
  • 方式三： 在项目视图右键菜单选择 New -> Generate Android Icons。

idea-plugin.name: Console Log Prettify
idea-plugin.description:
Console log prettify plugin for IntelliJ Platform makes NDJSON (Newline Delimited JSON a.k.a. JSON Lines) logs more readable in the console. It has the following features:

  • JSON Parsing: Automatically parses each log line as JSON and extracts essential log information such as timestamp, log level, and message.
  • Colorful Display: Displays essential log information in different colors depending on the log level to make it easier to read.
  • Readable Timestamp: Formats the timestamp in a human-friendly format.
  • Expandable Pretty JSON: Prints a well-formatted JSON string following the log message. The JSON string is folded by default, but you can expand it when you need to view the full details.
  • Seamless Integration: Supports various log formats such as Logstash, Bunyan, Pino, log/slog, Cloud Logging, etc. with no additional configuration or software.
  • AppSettings to select custom fields: Will parse out the selected log json fields and display them in the log view, so you can easily see the important information without having to expand the JSON.
  • Nested fields: you can configure to display the nested fields in Log view (e.g sMsg.msg below).
  • Json/Xml in json values: if the selected log json fields contain strings containing valid JSON or xml, it will also pretty print those in the collapsed log view.
  • Handle large logs: if the log message is too large, its unable to pretty print but it will try to parse json with just text match partially, so you can still see the important information without having to expand the JSON.

This plugin is useful when you are developing a modern system that outputs logs in JSON format. You no longer need to switch log formats between production and local development environments.
idea-plugin.change-notes: • Json folding in the popup to make it easy to read long values.

idea-plugin.name: Git Worktree Manager
idea-plugin.description:
Run Claude Code across multiple Git worktrees — without losing context.

Git Worktree Manager creates, lists, and deletes worktrees in a few clicks, and surfaces every Claude Code session across all worktrees of your repo — resumable in one click, right in the IDE terminal.

Why Claude Code + worktrees?
AI agents make parallel feature branches practical, but branch switching kills agent context. Give each Claude session its own worktree and keep every session discoverable and resumable from the IDE.

Features:
  • View all Claude Code sessions across every worktree, with current-project sessions first and then sorted by recency
  • Resume any Claude session in the IDE terminal with one click
  • Create worktrees with automatic branch creation
  • Auto-open worktrees in new IDE windows
  • Delete worktrees with one click
idea-plugin.change-notes:
What's new
  • Fix telemetry pluginVersion reporting so New Relic events carry the real version instead of "unknown"
  • Update marketplace description and README to highlight Claude Code session resume as a core differentiator

idea-plugin.name: Structured Coroutines
idea-plugin.description:
Enforces structured concurrency best practices for Kotlin Coroutines.

Features:

  • Real-time inspections for coroutine anti-patterns
  • Quick fixes for automatic code correction
  • Intentions for code refactoring
  • Gutter icons for scope and dispatcher visualization
idea-plugin.change-notes:
v1.2.0

  • BREAKING — AsyncWithoutAwaitInspection (SCOPE_002) and UnstructuredLaunchInspection (SCOPE_003) now default to ERROR (previously WARNING), matching the compiler, Detekt, and Lint defaults. Findings that previously showed as warnings now show as errors; adjust your inspection profile if you rely on the previous severity.
  • SideEffectInMapOperatorInspection (FLOW_008) now defaults to INFO (previously WARNING), matching Detekt's Minor severity for the same check. Previously-warning-level findings now show at the lower INFO severity.

v1.1.0

  • CANCEL_003 false-positive fix — CancellationExceptionSwallowed (Detekt + IntelliJ) no longer fires when a catch(t: Throwable) or catch(e: Exception) block rethrows the caught parameter unconditionally (throw t / throw e). CancellationException always propagates in this pattern.
  • IDE compatibility extended — Now compatible with IntelliJ Platform build 262.* (raised untilBuild from 261.* to 262.*)

v1.0.0

  • 9 new inspections (35 total) — Production-ready iteration: Compose lifecycle, test dispatchers, Flow guidance, interop, and debug opt-in aligned with toolkit v1.0.0
  • RememberScopeForInit (COMPOSE_002, WARNING) — Detects rememberCoroutineScope().launch { } for one-shot init; quick fix replaces with LaunchedEffect
  • HardcodedDispatcherInClass (TEST_005, WARNING) — Detects hardcoded Dispatchers.IO/Default/Main in classes; recommends constructor injection
  • CoroutineNotCompletedInTest (TEST_006, WARNING) — Detects runTest without advanceUntilIdle() when coroutines may still be pending
  • FlatMapOperatorChoice (FLOW_009, INFO) — Informational guidance on flatMapConcat vs flatMapMerge vs flatMapLatest
  • SharedFlowForOneshotEvents (FLOW_011, WARNING) — Detects MutableSharedFlow for one-shot events; quick fix replaces with Channel
  • ChannelFlowVsCallbackFlow (INTEROP_003, WARNING) — Detects wrong Flow builder for callback APIs
  • BlockingFutureGet (INTEROP_004, WARNING) — Detects Future.get() / CompletableFuture.get(); quick fix replaces with await()
  • Flow Chain Analyzer intention — AnalyzeFlowChainIntention summarizes operator chain semantics from the caret
  • COMPOSE_001 quick-fix — collectAsState() → collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
  • Tool window & Scan Project — All inspections registered with InspectionGuideRegistry entries and BEST_PRACTICES links

v0.9.0

  • 5 new inspections (26 total) — Shared-state concurrency and Flow patterns aligned with toolkit v0.9.0 (Concurrency, KMP & Backend iteration)
  • SynchronizedInCoroutine (CONCUR_001, WARNING) — Detects synchronized { } inside suspend functions or coroutine builders; quick fix replaces with mutex.withLock { }
  • StateInWithEagerlyStrategy (FLOW_006, WARNING) — Detects stateIn(..., SharingStarted.Eagerly, ...) on viewModelScope / lifecycleScope; quick fix replaces with SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5_000)
  • LaunchInWithUnstructuredScope (FLOW_007, WARNING) — Detects Flow.launchIn(GlobalScope) or launchIn(CoroutineScope(...)); offers structured-scope quick fixes (viewModelScope, lifecycleScope, coroutineScope)
  • RedundantWithContext (CONCUR_004, WARNING, opt-in) — Detects nested withContext with the same dispatcher reference; quick fix removes the inner call (disabled by default)
  • SideEffectInMapOperator (FLOW_008, WARNING, opt-in) — Detects side effects (logging, analytics, etc.) before the return in .map { }; recommends onEach { } (disabled by default)
  • 3 new quick fixes (21 total) — ReplaceSynchronizedWithMutex, ReplaceEagerlyWithWhileSubscribed, RemoveRedundantWithContext
  • Tool window & Scan Project — All new inspections registered in StructuredCoroutinesInspectionProvider with InspectionGuideRegistry entries and BEST_PRACTICES links

v0.8.0

  • 7 new inspections (22 total) — Interop, Flow, concurrency, testing, Compose, and KMP coverage aligned with toolkit v0.8.0
  • SuspendCoroutineWithoutCancellation (INTEROP_001, ERROR) — Detects suspendCoroutine in suspend functions; quick fix replaces with suspendCancellableCoroutine and adds invokeOnCancellation { }
  • CallbackFlowWithoutAwaitClose (INTEROP_002, ERROR) — Detects callbackFlow { } without awaitClose; quick fix inserts awaitClose { } at the end of the lambda
  • MutableFlowExposed (FLOW_010, WARNING) — Detects public MutableStateFlow / MutableSharedFlow; quick fix converts to backing-property pattern with asStateFlow() / asSharedFlow()
  • MissingCatchInFlow (FLOW_005, WARNING) — Detects Flow chains with intermediate operators but no .catch { } before collect, collectLatest, or launchIn; quick fix inserts .catch { } before the terminal operator
  • SequentialAsyncAwait (CONCUR_003, WARNING) — Detects inline async { }.await() with no parallelism benefit; quick fix suggests withContext or parallel coroutineScope
  • RunBlockingInsteadOfRunTest (TEST_004, WARNING) — Detects runBlocking in @Test functions; Convert to runTest intention replaces with runTest and adds the kotlinx.coroutines.test import
  • CollectAsStateWithoutLifecycle (COMPOSE_001, WARNING) — Detects collectAsState() in Composables; recommends collectAsStateWithLifecycle() (excludes @Preview and non-Compose files)
  • DispatchersIOInCommonMain (KMP_001, ERROR) — Detects Dispatchers.IO in KMP commonMain / commonTest source sets
  • 5 new quick fixes — ReplaceSuspendCoroutine, AddAwaitClose, AddCatchOperator, ReplaceWithBackingProperty, ReplaceSequentialAsyncAwaitWithContext (18 quick fixes total)
  • Tool window & Scan Project — All new inspections are registered in StructuredCoroutinesInspectionProvider and picked up automatically by the tool window and Scan Project for Coroutine Issues
  • Inspection guide links — InspectionGuideRegistry entries for each new rule with links to BEST_PRACTICES sections

v0.7.0

  • IDE compatibility extended — Now supports IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1 (build 261.*) and Android Studio Panda 2025.3.3 (build 253.*)

v0.6.1

  • Local framework scope recognition (compiler + IDE + lint) — Scopes created via framework helpers (e.g. rememberCoroutineScope()) stored in local variables are now treated as structured scopes, eliminating false positives in UnstructuredLaunch across all three layers
  • @Suppress / @file:Suppress support — All IntelliJ inspections now honor @Suppress("RuleName") on the flagged element and @file:Suppress at the file level via CoroutineInspectionBase
  • GlobalScopeInspection short name fix — Overrides getShortName() to align the runtime ID with the registered inspection ID, fixing suppression not working
  • Lint parenthesized-receiver fix — CoroutineLintUtils unwraps parenthesized receivers and uses a PSI fallback to detect call- and name-based framework scopes; new helper traces local variable initializers

v0.6.0

  • Scan Project action — New "Scan Project for Coroutine Issues" action in the Analyze menu and tool window toolbar; runs all 13 inspections across every Kotlin source file in the background with real-time progress
  • False-positive guard (CoroutinesImportFilter) — All 13 inspections now exit early when a file does not import kotlinx.coroutines, eliminating false positives from name collisions with non-coroutines APIs (e.g. ActivityScenario.launch)
  • SuspendInFinallyInspection — Replaced brittle hard-coded name blocklist with proper suspend-call detection via type resolution
  • structuredCoroutinesReport Gradle task — Generates HTML and plain-text reports of the active compiler-plugin configuration (rule codes, severities, exclusions) for CI auditing
  • CI integration guide — New public guide (docs/CI_INTEGRATION.md) with full GitHub Actions workflow, SARIF upload, artifact archiving, and PR comment automation

v0.5.0

  • WithTimeoutScopeCancellation (CANCEL_006) — New inspection: withTimeout without handling TimeoutCancellationException may cancel the parent scope; quick fix to replace with withTimeoutOrNull
  • Tool window — "What to do" — Each finding now shows a 1–2 line action summary and a "See guide" link to the relevant section in BEST_PRACTICES_COROUTINES.md
  • async description (SCOPE_002) — Inspection description extended with §5.3 EXCEPT_003 context: exceptions in async are stored in the Deferred and not sent to CoroutineExceptionHandler
  • Decision Guide — New public guide (docs/DECISION_GUIDE.md) with decision tables and trees: launch vs async, which scope, viewModelScope vs lifecycleScope, runTest vs runBlocking, dispatchers, withTimeout, loops, cold vs hot Flow

v0.4.1

  • IDE compatibility: extended support for build 253.* (e.g. Android Studio / IntelliJ AI-253.x)

v0.4.0

  • LoopWithoutYield (CANCEL_001) — New inspection for loops in suspend functions without cooperation points; quick fixes to insert ensureActive(), currentCoroutineContext().ensureActive(), yield(), or delay(0)
  • ScopeReuseAfterCancel (CANCEL_005) — Reinforced inspection and messages; error text now guides to the quick fix (replace cancel() with cancelChildren())
  • LifecycleAwareFlowCollection (ARCH_002) — New inspection: Flow collection in lifecycleScope.launch without repeatOnLifecycle/flowWithLifecycle
  • Convert to runTest — New intention: replace runBlocking { } with runTest when the body contains delay() (TEST_001, virtual time for tests)
  • CancellationException subclass — New quick fix: change superclass from CancellationException to Exception for domain errors (4.2)

v0.3.0

  • 12 inspections: GlobalScope, runBlocking in suspend, async/await, Job in builder, suspend in finally, CancellationException, Dispatchers.Unconfined, ScopeReuseAfterCancel, UnstructuredLaunch, MainDispatcherMisuse
  • 9 quick fixes: Replace cancel with cancelChildren, Wrap with NonCancellable, Replace GlobalScope, Add await, and more
  • 5 intentions: Migrate to lifecycleScope/viewModelScope, Convert launch to async, Wrap with coroutineScope, Extract suspend function
  • Tool window and gutter icons for scope and dispatcher

v0.2.0

  • IDE compatibility: IntelliJ IDEA 2024.3–2025.x (builds 243–252)
  • 13 inspections for coroutine best practices
  • 9 quick fixes for automatic corrections
  • 5 intentions for refactoring
  • 2 gutter icon providers
  • Structured Coroutines tool window
  • Full K2 compiler mode support

idea-plugin.name: vscode-all-in-one-icon
idea-plugin.description:
An IntelliJ IDEA plugin that brings beautiful VS Code-style file and folder icons to your JetBrains IDE. Supports multiple icon themes including VSCode Icons, Material Icons, and File Icons.

Features:

  • Multiple icon themes (VSCode Icons, Material Icons, File Icons)
  • Theme priority system with fallback resolution
  • 2,000+ file and folder icons
  • Multi-language UI (English, 日本語, 简体中文, 한국어)
  • Easy theme switching
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Theme Priority System
    • Add, remove, and reorder multiple themes
    • Fallback resolution: if no icon found in first theme, next theme is tried
    • Settings UI with dual-list interface for theme management
  • Multi-Language Support
    • English, Japanese (日本語), Chinese (简体中文), Korean (한국어)
    • Language selection in settings UI
    • Localized messages stored in JSON files for easy contribution
  • Initial release of vscode-all-in-one-icon plugin
  • Multiple Icon Themes
    • VSCode Icons theme based on vscode-icons/vscode-icons
    • Material Icons theme based on PKief/vscode-material-icon-theme
    • File Icons theme based on file-icons/vscode
  • Comprehensive Icon Support
    • File icon mapping for 100+ file extensions
    • Special icons for popular frameworks (React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, etc.)
    • Config file icons (JSON, YAML, TOML, INI, ENV, etc.)
    • Folder icon mapping for 150+ common directories
    • Theme-specific folder icons with correct prefixes
  • Project-Level Configuration
    • Settings UI at Settings > Tools > Icon Theme Settings
    • Enable/disable custom file icons per project
    • Instant theme switching without IDE restart
    • Persistent settings stored in JSON format (vscode-all-in-one-icon-settings.json)
  • Icon Features
    • Automatic icon scaling for high-resolution displays
    • Smart file name matching (e.g., package.json, Dockerfile)
    • Complex extension support (e.g., test.spec.ts → TypeScript test icon)
    • Logging for missing icons to aid debugging

Fixed

  • Material Icons folder icon prefix issue
    • VSCode Icons uses folder_type_ prefix
    • Material Icons uses folder- prefix
    • Each theme now correctly applies its own prefix convention

Technical Implementation

  • Core Components
    • VscordIconProvider: Main icon provider implementing FileIconProvider
      • Resolves icons based on current theme and file/folder name
      • Loads SVG icons from resources with proper scaling
      • Returns null when plugin is disabled (uses IDE defaults)
    • IconResolver: Theme-specific icon name mapping
      • Manages current theme state
      • Resolves file icons by extension and filename
      • Resolves folder icons by folder name
      • Supports both VSCode Icons and Material Icons mappings
    • IconThemeConfig: Persistent configuration storage
      • Stores settings in JSON format using PersistentStateComponent
      • Project-level service (saved per project)
      • Tracks selected theme and enabled state
    • IconThemeConfigurable: Settings UI implementation
      • Swing-based configuration panel
      • Theme selection combo box with descriptions
      • Enable/disable checkbox
      • Icon count information display
  • Icon Mapping System
    • Mappings.kt: Centralized icon mappings loaded from JSON
      • VSCode Icons: extensions, filenames, folders
      • Material Icons: extensions, filenames, folders
      • Lazy-loaded JSON resources from /settings/ directory
      • Flattened mapping format (icon → [extensions])
  • Resource Structure
    • /icons/vscode/: VSCode Icons SVG files
      • File icons: file_type_*.svg
      • Folder icons: folder_type_*.svg
    • /icons/material/: Material Icons SVG files
