idea-plugin.name: DevFocus
idea-plugin.description:
DevFocus — Pomodoro Timer for JetBrains IDEs

Most Pomodoro timers don't survive an IDE restart, skip the long break entirely, and require you to leave the editor just to pause. DevFocus fixes all three — and stays out of your way while doing it.

What makes it different

💾 Survives restarts and crashes. Timer state is saved to disk continuously. Reopen the IDE — even the next day — and your session is exactly where you left it, paused and ready to resume.

🔁 Proper long breaks. After a full round of sessions, DevFocus fires a long break automatically — the defining feature of the Pomodoro technique that most timer plugins quietly omit.

🕐 Tells you when you'll be done. Once running, the tool window shows two live timestamps: when the current session ends and when the full round finishes. No mental math — just "Ends at 3:45 PM" and "Free by 5:30 PM" so you can plan your day around your focus blocks.

⏭ Skip break from the notification. When you're in flow, click Skip Break directly in the IDE notification balloon. No need to open the tool window or break your focus.

⌨️ Full keyboard control. Start/Pause, Reset, and Skip Break are registered as IDE actions — assign your own shortcuts via Settings → Keymap → DevFocus to avoid conflicts with your existing bindings. All three are also reachable via Tools → DevFocus and Find Action (Ctrl+Shift+A / ⌘⇧A).

📍 Status bar always present. Live countdown visible while you code, even with the tool window closed. When idle, shows your daily session count — a quiet reminder of what you've already accomplished.

Everything else

  • Three built-in modes — Classic Pomodoro (25/5), Deep Work (50/10), or fully Custom durations
  • Saved custom modes — name and save your own timing configurations; switch to them in one click from the mode dropdown
  • Visual circular timer — arc depletes clockwise, colour-coded by phase
  • Customizable ring colors — pick any Focus and Break accent color from a color picker in Settings
  • Session indicator — dot row showing completed, active, and upcoming sessions
  • 🍅 Daily session counter — resets at midnight, shown in tool window and status bar
  • Auto-start toggle — choose whether work sessions start automatically after a break or wait for you
  • Actionable notifications — Skip Break, Skip Long Break, Start Session — inline in the balloon
  • Responsive tool window — adapts between compact, vertical, and horizontal layouts as you resize

Supported IDEs

18 IDEs — IntelliJ IDEA, Android Studio, PyCharm, WebStorm, CLion, Rider, GoLand, PHPStorm, RubyMine, DataSpell, DataGrip, and more.

Turbocharge Your TODOs with TODO++

TODO++ (Todo Plus) transforms standard TODO comments into an intelligent, AI-augmented task management system directly within all JetBrains IDEs. Organize, track, export, and complete tasks without leaving your code.

✨ Status: v2.4.1

🔥 Key Features:

  • 🤖 AI-Powered Jira Ticket Assistant: Analyze unlinked/forgotten TODO comments with surrounding code context (±15 lines) using Google Gemini, OpenAI, Claude, or Ollama. Review, draft, and create Jira tickets with 1-click in-place code linking (// TODO(issue:KEY): ...).
  • 🛡️ VCS Pre-Commit Guard: Automatically detects unlinked TODO comments in staged Git files and alerts you before committing, preventing forgotten tasks from crossing sprints.
  • 🔄 Real-Time Centralized Cache & Single-Flight Scan: Sub-10ms incremental rescanning during editor typing. Coalesced background tasks eliminate redundant scans and multiple progress bars.
  • 🌐 REST Integration (GitHub & Jira): Direct 1-click export of any TODO comment to GitHub Issues or Jira Cloud with formatted markdown details.
  • 🔔 Slack & Discord Webhooks: Dispatch instant overdue task alerts directly into team communication channels via webhooks.
  • Multi-Selection & Batch Completion: Select multiple TODO items or group headers and toggle completion in batch!
  • Executive PDF & HTML Reports: Export formatted, printable reports with priority breakdown charts.
  • Entire Solution & Cross-IDE Support: Compatible with IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, PhpStorm, GoLand, CLion, Rider, Android Studio, and RustRover.
  • Zero Deprecated APIs & Dynamic Reload: 100% compliant with IntelliJ Platform 2024.1+; install and update without restarting your IDE.

📝 Usage Examples:

// TODO(@john priority:critical due:today): Fix production crash
// TODO(issue:PROJ-101): Refactor authentication handler
# BUG(issue:#42 priority:high): Fix memory leak in background worker

idea-plugin.name: SafeGradle
idea-plugin.description:
SafeGradle is a professional-grade security scanner for IntelliJ IDEA that protects your development environment from malicious Gradle build scripts. It identifies security risks like hidden network calls, shell execution, and credential leaks before they can compromise your system.

🛡️ Key Features

  • Semantic PSI Analysis: High-precision scanning using IntelliJ's Program Structure Interface (PSI) to detect obfuscated or dynamically constructed malicious code in both Kotlin (.kts) and Groovy scripts.
  • Pre-opening Security: Integrated "Open in SafeGradle" actions on the Welcome Screen and "Trust Project" dialogs allow you to audit open-source projects before fully loading them.
  • Software Composition Analysis (SCA): Automatically detects dependencies with known vulnerabilities (CVEs) to prevent supply chain attacks.
  • Team-Wide Configuration: Share security policies across your team using a .safegradle.yml file in your project root.
  • Real-time Protection: Editor annotations, gutter icons, and Alt+Enter quick-fixes provide immediate feedback as you edit build scripts.
  • Incremental Scanning: Intelligent caching ensures scans are lightning-fast, only re-checking files when they change.

Keep your IDE secure and code with confidence.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
✨ New Features

  • Remote Build Cache Safety: Flags isPush = true inside a remote { } build-cache block — any developer machine can poison the shared cache with tampered outputs, so pushing must be restricted to CI (isPush = System.getenv("CI") != null). Also flags allowUntrustedServer, which disables TLS validation on the cache connection.
  • Gradle Plugin Supply Chain: Detects plugin IDs that impersonate popular Gradle plugins (one- or two-character typosquats), plugin IDs that were relocated and no longer receive security fixes, and unpinned plugin versions (+, latest.release, ranges, -SNAPSHOT) that can silently pull in a compromised release. Works in build scripts, settings.gradle, and libs.versions.toml.
  • Dependency Verification: Warns when gradle/verification-metadata.xml is missing, and flags weakened metadata — verify-metadata set to false, a <trust> rule that matches every artifact, or SHA-1/MD5-only checksums.
  • Copyleft Licence Detection (opt-in): Flags dependencies published under GPL, AGPL, or SSPL, which can require releasing your source code when distributed or offered as a service. Disabled by default since it needs Maven Central access; enable it under Settings → Tools → SafeGradle. LGPL, dual licences with a permissive option, and GPL with the Classpath Exception are not flagged.

🔧 Improvements & Fixes

  • Rule settings are now enforced by the scanner: Disabling a check in Settings → Tools → SafeGradle now skips it entirely, and per-project severity overrides are applied to findings. The scan cache is cleared whenever rules change, since cache entries are keyed on file content only and would otherwise serve stale results.
  • Every violation now carries its real check ID: Checks that didn't set a checkId reported unknown, so severity overrides and suppressions silently never matched them.
  • Real Gradle wrapper checksums: The wrapper integrity check used placeholder checksum values. It now carries the official SHA-256 digests published by Gradle for 8.8 – 9.2.1 (bin and all), so genuine wrappers verify clean and a mismatch raises a HIGH-severity tampering alert.
  • One-click wrapper auto-fix: Missing or mismatched distributionSha256Sum findings now offer a fix that writes the correct checksum into gradle-wrapper.properties.
  • Dependency confusion catches lookalike sub-groups: Similarity is compared against the leading segments of the group ID, so names like com.gooogle.guava are detected.
  • Shared Levenshtein helper: Moved into SecurityUtils so the plugin-portal and dependency-confusion checks share one implementation.

🧪 Testing

  • Added unit-test coverage for the new checks and the batch quick-fix engine — BatchQuickFixEngineTest (18 tests), LicenseCheckTest (12 tests), and new BuildCacheCheck / PluginPortalCheck / DependencyVerificationCheck cases in SecurityCheckTests. The suite now runs 139 tests, all green.

🚀 Release Automation

  • Marketplace publishing is now automated: pushing a v*.*.* tag builds the plugin, runs the IntelliJ Plugin Verifier, gates on tag == pluginVersion, and publishes with that version's changelog notes.

idea-plugin.name: Rebound
idea-plugin.description:
Rebound — Compose Recomposition Budget Monitor

  • Timeline — Composable × time heatmap. Each cell colored green/yellow/red based on budget status. Scroll back up to 60 minutes. Correlate recomposition spikes with user interactions.
  • Stability — Parameter stability matrix showing SAME/DIFFERENT/STATIC/UNCERTAIN per parameter. Cascade impact tree visualizes how unstable parameters propagate recompositions through the hierarchy.
  • History — Saved sessions with VCS-tagged branch name and commit hash. Side-by-side comparison for before/after regression analysis.

Editor Integration

  • Gutter icons — Red, yellow, or green dots next to @Composable declarations reflecting live budget status.
  • CodeVision — Inline hints: 12/s | budget: 8/s | OVER | skip: 45%
  • Status bar — Persistent widget: Rebound: 45 composables | 3 violations

idea-plugin.name: JsonToDartPlus
idea-plugin.description:
JsonToDartPlus

A powerful IntelliJ IDEA / Android Studio plugin for generating Dart entity classes from JSON data with comprehensive type validation and null safety support.

Key Features

✨ Core Functionality

  • JSON to Dart Class Generation - Automatically generate Dart entity classes from JSON data
  • Null Safety Support - All fields are nullable by default (using ? marker)
  • Type Validation - Built-in JsonTypeValidator provides runtime type checking with friendly error messages
  • No Naming Conversion - Preserves original JSON field names without snake_case to camelCase conversion
  • Nested Object Support - Automatically detects and generates nested JSON objects
  • List Type Support - Properly handles various List types including object lists
  • num Type Option - Optional use of num type instead of int and double

🔄 Regenerate fromJson

  • Regenerate FromJson Action - Regenerate fromJson methods for existing Dart classes
  • Multi-Class Support - Batch regenerate for files containing multiple classes
  • Smart Type Recognition - Correctly identifies complex types like List<T>? and uses appropriate validators

⚙️ Configurable Options

  • Custom JsonTypeValidator Path - Configure the validator file location
  • Numeric Type Selection - Choose between int/double or unified num type
  • Preference Memory - Remembers user choices for next session

使用方法

1. 生成 Dart 实体类

  1. 在 Dart 文件中右键点击，选择 Generate（或使用快捷键 Alt+Insert）
  2. 选择 JSON to Dart Plus
  3. 在弹出的对话框中：
    • 输入类名
    • 粘贴 JSON 数据
    • 配置 JsonTypeValidator 路径（默认为 lib/generated）
    • （可选）勾选 "Use 'num' type instead of 'int' and 'double'" 使用 num 类型
  4. 点击 OK 生成代码

2. 重新生成 fromJson 方法

  1. 打开包含 Dart 实体类的文件
  2. 右键点击，选择 Generate（或使用快捷键 Alt+Insert）
  3. 选择 Regenerate FromJson
  4. 插件会自动为文件中所有类重新生成 fromJson 方法

生成的代码示例

基础示例

输入 JSON:

{
  "name": "John",
  "age": 30,
  "email": "john@example.com"
}

生成的 Dart 类:

import 'package:myapp/generated/json_type_validator.dart';

class MyClass {
  String? name;
  int? age;
  String? email;

  MyClass({this.name, this.age, this.email});

  MyClass.fromJson(dynamic json) {
    name = JsonTypeValidator.validateString(json['name'], 'name');
    age = JsonTypeValidator.validateInt(json['age'], 'age');
    email = JsonTypeValidator.validateString(json['email'], 'email');
  }

  Map<String, dynamic> toJson() {
    final map = <String, dynamic>{};
    map['name'] = name;
    map['age'] = age;
    map['email'] = email;
    return map;
  }
}

嵌套对象和 List

输入 JSON:

{
  "userId": 123,
  "userName": "Alice",
  "orders": [
    {
      "orderId": 1,
      "amount": 99.99
    }
  ]
}

生成的 Dart 类:

import 'package:myapp/generated/json_type_validator.dart';

class MyClass {
  int? userId;
  String? userName;
  List<OrderNested>? orders;

  MyClass({this.userId, this.userName, this.orders});

  MyClass.fromJson(dynamic json) {
    userId = JsonTypeValidator.validateInt(json['userId'], 'userId');
    userName = JsonTypeValidator.validateString(json['userName'], 'userName');
    orders = JsonTypeValidator.validateObjectList<OrderNested>(
      json['orders'], 
      'orders', 
      (e) => OrderNested.fromJson(e)
    );
  }

  Map<String, dynamic> toJson() {
    final map = <String, dynamic>{};
    map['userId'] = userId;
    map['userName'] = userName;
    map['orders'] = orders != null 
        ? orders?.map((e) => e.toJson()).toList() 
        : null;
    return map;
  }
}

class OrderNested {
  int? orderId;
  double? amount;

  OrderNested({this.orderId, this.amount});

  OrderNested.fromJson(dynamic json) {
    orderId = JsonTypeValidator.validateInt(json['orderId'], 'orderId');
    amount = JsonTypeValidator.validateDouble(json['amount'], 'amount');
  }

  Map<String, dynamic> toJson() {
    final map = <String, dynamic>{};
    map['orderId'] = orderId;
    map['amount'] = amount;
    return map;
  }
}

使用 num 类型

当勾选 "Use 'num' type instead of 'int' and 'double'" 时：

class Product {
  num? price;      // 而不是 double?
  num? quantity;   // 而不是 int?
  List<num>? prices; // 而不是 List<double>?

  Product.fromJson(dynamic json) {
    price = JsonTypeValidator.validateNum(json['price'], 'price');
    quantity = JsonTypeValidator.validateNum(json['quantity'], 'quantity');
    prices = JsonTypeValidator.validateNumList(json['prices'], 'prices');
  }
}

JsonTypeValidator API

插件会自动生成 json_type_validator.dart 文件，包含以下验证方法：

基本类型验证

  • validateString(value, fieldName) - String?
  • validateInt(value, fieldName) - int?
  • validateDouble(value, fieldName) - double?
  • validateNum(value, fieldName) - num?
  • validateBool(value, fieldName) - bool?

List 类型验证

  • validateStringList(value, fieldName) - List?
  • validateIntList(value, fieldName) - List?
  • validateDoubleList(value, fieldName) - List?
  • validateNumList(value, fieldName) - List?
  • validateBoolList(value, fieldName) - List?
  • validateObjectList<T>(value, fieldName, fromJson) - List?

对象类型验证

  • validateObject<T>(value, fieldName, fromJson) - T?

安装

从 JetBrains Marketplace 安装（推荐）

  1. 打开 IntelliJ IDEA / Android Studio
  2. 进入 Settings/Preferences > Plugins > Marketplace
  3. 搜索 "JsonToDartPlus"
  4. 点击 Install

手动安装

  1. 从 JetBrains Marketplace 下载最新版本的插件
  2. 打开 IntelliJ IDEA / Android Studio
  3. 进入 Settings/Preferences > Plugins > ⚙️ > Install plugin from disk...
  4. 选择下载的插件文件并安装

从源码构建

git clone https://github.com/zhazhazsy/JsonToDartPlus.git
cd JsonToDartPlus
./gradlew buildPlugin

构建的插件位于 build/distributions/ 目录

技术说明

项目结构

JsonToDartPlus/
├── src/main/kotlin/com/github/zhazhazsy/jsontodartplus/
│   ├── action/
│   │   ├── JsonToDartPlusAction.kt      # 主生成 Action
│   │   └── RegenerateFromJsonAction.kt  # 重新生成 Action
│   ├── dialog/
│   │   └── JsonInputDialog.kt           # 输入对话框
│   ├── generator/
│   │   ├── DartClassGenerator.kt        # Dart 类生成器
│   │   └── DartTypeValidator.kt         # 验证器生成器
│   └── toolWindow/                      # (已移除)
├── src/main/resources/
│   ├── META-INF/
│   │   └── plugin.xml                   # 插件配置
│   └── messages/
│       └── MyBundle.properties          # 国际化资源
└── build.gradle.kts                     # Gradle 构建配置

依赖

  • Kotlin
  • org.json (JSON 解析)
  • IntelliJ Platform SDK

兼容性

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2023.1+
  • Android Studio Hedgehog+
  • 其他基于 IntelliJ Platform 的 IDE

常见问题

Q: 为什么生成的字段都有 ?？

A: 为了支持空安全，所有字段默认都是可空的。你可以根据实际业务需求手动移除 ?。

Q: 可以自定义 JsonTypeValidator 的位置吗？

A: 可以，在生成对话框中可以配置验证器文件的存放路径。

Q: 使用 num 类型有什么好处？

A: num 是 Dart 中数值的基类，可以同时表示整数和小数。如果你的 JSON 中数值类型不固定，使用 num 可以避免类型转换问题。

Q: 如何更新已有的实体类？

A: 使用 Regenerate FromJson 功能，它会根据当前类的字段定义重新生成 fromJson 方法。

贡献

欢迎提交 Issue 和 Pull Request！

许可证

MIT License

作者: zhazhazsy
GitHub: https://github.com/zhazhazsy/JsonToDartPlus

如果这个插件对你有帮助，请给个 ⭐ Star 支持一下！

idea-plugin.name: SMI Detector
idea-plugin.description:
SMI Detector is an IntelliJ Platform plugin for detecting spaghetti code, shit-mountain style legacy code hotspots, and code complexity risks in Java and Kotlin projects.

It analyzes source files locally and helps developers quickly identify messy, overgrown, hard-to-maintain files and methods before they become even bigger refactoring problems.

中文说明

SMI Detector 是一个用于识别 Java / Kotlin 项目中“屎山代码”和高复杂度热点的 IntelliJ Platform 插件。

它会在本地分析源码，帮助开发者快速发现难读、难改、难维护的文件与方法，把潜在的重构目标优先暴露出来。

核心能力

  • 文件级复杂度评分，快速识别高风险文件
  • 热点方法检测，定位真正的“屎山代码”区域
  • 项目视图装饰、编辑器提示、Gutter 标记与工具窗口总览
  • 支持导出 JSON / Markdown / HTML 本地报告
  • 支持生成 AI 重构 Prompt，辅助后续治理
  • 支持通过 radar.yaml 配置团队规则

适用场景

  • 快速扫描项目中的复杂代码和坏味道聚集区
  • 识别需要优先治理的核心文件和热点方法
  • 在重构、代码评审和质量治理前建立统一视图

Features

  • File-level complexity scoring from 0 to 100
  • Hotspot detection for high-risk methods and functions
  • Tool window dashboard for project and current file inspection
  • Project View decorations for fast visual discovery
  • Editor notifications for high-complexity files
  • Gutter markers for hotspot methods
  • Local report export in JSON, Markdown, and HTML
  • Refactoring prompt generation for AI-assisted workflows
  • Team-configurable rules through radar.yaml

Supported IDEs

  • IntelliJ IDEA
  • Android Studio

Supported Languages

  • Java
  • Kotlin

Privacy

All analysis is performed locally on your machine. The plugin does not upload source code or analysis results to external servers.

idea-plugin.name: DataClass Keep
idea-plugin.description:
Detects Kotlin data classes and Retrofit response classes missing the @Keep annotation, preventing ProGuard/R8 from stripping them during minification.

Features:
  • Warns when a data class is missing @Keep
  • Warns when Retrofit response classes are missing @Keep
  • One-click quick fix to add @Keep automatically
  • Supports GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD annotations
Why use this?
When building release APKs, ProGuard/R8 renames or removes classes. Data classes used in Gson, Retrofit, or Room can cause runtime crashes if not annotated with @Keep. This catches the problem at edit time before it reaches production.

idea-plugin.name: Android Dependency Resolver
idea-plugin.description:
Dependency Resolver - Smart Android Dependency Management

🤔 The Problem

Adding dependencies to an Android project is tedious and error-prone. You have to:

  • Search Maven Central or Google's documentation for the correct artifact coordinates
  • Figure out which version is compatible with your Kotlin, AGP, and compileSdk versions
  • Manually add entries to libs.versions.toml under [versions], [libraries], and [plugins]
  • Add the right implementation, ksp, or kapt lines to build.gradle.kts
  • Remember to include required plugins like KSP or the Compose compiler

Dependency Resolver eliminates all of this. Operating through a dedicated IDE tool window, it detects your local project configuration, connects to a daily-updated Cloudflare API of 30+ Android libraries, and inserts perfectly compatible code with a single click.

✨ Key Features

  • Auto-detects project config - Instantly scans and tracks your Kotlin version, AGP version, Gradle version, and compileSdk targets.
  • Intelligent compatibility engine - It doesn't blindly give you the newest version. It analyzes your project constraints and suggests the guaranteed best stable version. It even fully auto-aligns companion compiler plugins (like finding exact KSP matches for your Kotlin compiler).
  • Remote Knowledge Base - Powered by a Cloudflare backend that automatically scrapes and tracks library releases 24/7. Never wait for a plugin update just to get a new library version!
  • One-click insertion - Adds everything your project needs: TOML version/library entries, companion plugin declarations, and dependency lines in your Gradle script.
  • BOM support - Automatically applies platform() wrappers for Jetpack Compose, OkHttp, Koin, Ktor, etc.
  • Post-insertion - Shows a balloon notification confirming which files were modified and automatically triggers your Gradle sync.
  • Multi-module support - A target module selector lets you inject dependencies into any module in your project, not just :app.

🚀 How to Use

  1. Go to View → Tool Windows → Dependency Resolver.
  2. Type a library name (e.g. room or compose) in the search field.
  3. Review the result card showing the compatible versions and any dynamically aligned plugins.
  4. Click ✚ Add to Project. The plugin will rewrite your TOML and Gradle files then trigger a sync!

📬 Contact & Support

Developed by Abdulkadir Ali. Have a question or request? abdulkadir.ali@live.in
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.5

  • KMP Compiler Configuration Fix: Fixed a bug where top-level compiler configurations (like ksp and kapt) were incorrectly inserted inside KMP sourceSets { ... dependencies { } } blocks, causing Gradle DSL Type Mismatch errors. They are now safely routed to the global dependencies { } block.
  • Modern KSP Versioning: Upgraded KSP version resolution to fully support the new independent KSP versioning scheme introduced in KSP 2.3.0+ (Oct 2025). The plugin now automatically suggests the latest standalone KSP release for Kotlin 2.3+ while maintaining legacy suffix mapping for older versions.
  • Improved App Module Detection: Replaced hardcoded directory name checks with content-based scanning (com.android.application / applicationId). The plugin now correctly identifies KMP composeApp and non-standardly named Android app modules, preventing incorrect configuration warnings.

0.1.4

  • Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) Support: The plugin now detects kotlin("multiplatform") modules and inserts dependencies into the correct KMP source set blocks (commonMain.dependencies {}, androidMain.dependencies {}, iosMain.dependencies {}). Both modern and legacy DSL styles are supported.
  • Source Set-Aware Library Variants: Libraries with KMP support (Ktor Client, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlinx Serialization, Koin) now automatically present the correct platform-specific artifacts when targeting a KMP module, and Android-only artifacts when targeting a traditional Android module.
  • Module Type Badges: The module selector now shows [KMP] and [JVM] badges next to detected Kotlin Multiplatform and JVM modules for quick identification.
  • Source Set Labels: When targeting a KMP module, each dependency checkbox shows its target source set (e.g., [commonMain], [androidMain], [iosMain]) so you know exactly where each artifact will be placed.
  • Smart Deduplication in Source Sets: The multi-layer deduplication engine (alias normalization + Maven coordinate matching) now works inside KMP source set blocks, preventing duplicate entries within kotlin { sourceSets { } }.
  • Backward Compatible: All changes are fully backward compatible — existing Android and JVM project support remains unchanged.

0.1.3

  • Duplicate Entry Prevention: Fixed a critical bug where BOM entries (e.g., Jetpack Compose BOM) could be inserted twice into libs.versions.toml when existing entries used a different alias convention (e.g., composeBom vs compose-bom vs androidx-compose-bom).
  • Gradle-Compliant Alias Normalization: Introduced a normalization layer that treats all Gradle-equivalent alias formats (kebab-case, camelCase, snake_case, dot-separated) as identical, matching Gradle's own internal accessor behavior.
  • Maven Coordinate Deduplication: The plugin now parses the actual Maven coordinates (groupId:artifactId) from existing TOML entries, catching duplicates even when completely different aliases point to the same artifact.

0.1.2

  • Selective Dependency Injection: Replaced static dependency labels with an interactive list of checkboxes, allowing users to explicitly choose which optional components (e.g., converter-gson for Retrofit, lifecycle-livedata-ktx) to inject into their module.
  • Smart Partial Installation State: The Gradle modifier now detects partial installations. If a subset of dependencies is already present, the action button dynamically changes to "Add Remaining", seamlessly completing the injection without duplicating entries.
  • Non-Intrusive Gradle Sync: Improved the sync behavior. The plugin now silently saves your build files, allowing IntelliJ to present its native "Sync Now" prompt. This empowers you to batch-add multiple dependencies before triggering a single Gradle sync.
  • UI State Synchronization: The UI now reads uncommitted document states to stay perfectly in sync with your code, even if Gradle hasn't fully refreshed yet.
  • Preserved Module Selection: The module target dropdown no longer resets to `:app` when hitting the Refresh button.

0.1.1

  • AGP 9.0+ Built-in Kotlin Support: Kotlin version detection now works on projects using AGP 9.0+ Built-in Kotlin, where the Kotlin plugin is no longer explicitly declared. The plugin infers the bundled Kotlin version from the AGP version via a remotely-updated mapping table.
  • gradle.properties Kotlin Detection: Added fallback detection for projects that define kotlinVersion in gradle.properties.

0.1.0

  • Plugins Block Auto-Creation: Fixed a critical bug where required plugins (KSP, Hilt, Compose, etc.) were silently skipped when the target module had no plugins {} block. The block is now automatically created.
  • Internal Module Type Detection: The analyzer now accurately categorizes modules by scanning build files for plugin IDs, applicationId declarations, and android {} DSL blocks. This ensures smart dependency validation even when convention plugins are used.
  • Smart Module Warnings: Hilt and Firebase now show contextual warnings when targeted at non-:app modules, since they require app-level configuration.

0.0.9

  • Nested Module Discovery Fix: Fixed a critical bug where deeply nested modules (e.g., :feature:data, :core:domain) were not appearing in the Target Module dropdown when their parent directory did not contain its own build.gradle(.kts).

0.0.8

  • Expanded Library Support: Added 19 native structural blueprints including Firebase, Apollo GraphQL, CameraX, Media3, Security Crypto, Biometrics, Arrow, and Lottie!
  • Dynamic Capability: IDE client now supports reading latest library constraints dynamically populated by our backend scraper.

0.0.7

  • Marketplace Compliance: Added official EULA, Privacy Policy, and updated metadata.
  • Refined UI Branding: Cleaned up marketplace logo (removed background and overlays).
  • Theme-Aware Icons: Added official Light and Dark mode 16x16 tool window icons with an elegant 1px stroke weight for perfect IDE integration and alignment.

0.0.6

  • Added dependency presence detection: "Already Added" label and auto-refresh on module switch.
  • Improved scraper logging with automatic diffing.

0.0.5

  • Multi-module architecture support: target module selector for injecting dependencies.
  • Refined ProjectAnalyzer for AGP 9.0+ DSL support.

idea-plugin.name: KMP Resources
idea-plugin.description:
KMP Resources is the essential productivity tool for Kotlin Multiplatform developers using Compose Resources. It replaces manual XML editing with a powerful, centralized workflow.

🚀 Core Features:

  • Visual Table Editor: A clean, side-by-side view of all your strings, plurals, and arrays. Edit keys and values across all languages simultaneously. Shortcut: Press Cmd+B (Ctrl+B) on any resource reference to jump straight into the editor.
  • Smart Locale Management: Add new languages via a searchable popup (supports flag emojis and BCP 47 tags). The plugin automatically generates the required values-*** directories and XML files across all modules.
  • Safe Key Renaming: Rename a key in the table and the plugin instantly refactors all Kotlin usages (Res.string.*) and handles necessary imports project-wide.
  • Generate on the Fly: Type a non-existent key in Kotlin, hit Alt+Enter, and instantly create the XML tag and trigger a Gradle resync without leaving the file.

🛡️ Quality & Diagnostics:

  • Format Argument Linter: Real-time IDE highlighting for missing or mismatched format arguments (like %1$s) in your Kotlin code.
  • Project Health Toolwindow: A dedicated view to detect missing translations and unused keys across your entire project structure.
  • Duplicate Key Detector: Prevents build errors by identifying duplicate resource keys within the same file.

Stop fighting XML files and start focusing on your code. Built for seamless integration with Compose Multiplatform.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Locale Creation: Fixed an issue where adding a new locale to an Android native module incorrectly duplicated non-string resource files (like colors.xml or splash.xml) into the new localized values directory. The plugin now strictly creates only the necessary strings.xml file.

idea-plugin.name: FastGradleCN
idea-plugin.description:
Automatically configure CN mirror repositories for Gradle projects to speed up dependency downloads in mainland China.

为 Gradle 项目自动配置国内镜像，解决在中国大陆下载依赖缓慢的问题。


功能 / Features

  • 向 settings.gradle(.kts) 的 pluginManagement 和 dependencyResolutionManagement 注入阿里云镜像 / Injects Aliyun mirrors into both repository blocks
  • 将 gradle-wrapper.properties 的 Gradle 下载地址替换为腾讯镜像 / Replaces Gradle distribution URL with Tencent mirror
  • 同时支持 Kotlin DSL（.kts）和 Groovy DSL / Supports both Kotlin DSL and Groovy DSL
使用方式 / Usage

打开 Gradle 项目后，在通知栏、FastGradleCN 工具窗口或 Tools → 配置国内 Gradle 镜像 中点击应用。
Open a Gradle project and click Apply in the notification, the FastGradleCN tool window, or via Tools → Apply CN Gradle Mirrors.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 自动检测项目缺少国内镜像并提示配置
  • 向 settings.gradle(.kts) 注入阿里云镜像（pluginManagement + dependencyResolutionManagement）
  • 将 gradle-wrapper.properties 的下载地址替换为腾讯云镜像
  • 支持安装全局 init script，新建任何项目自动生效

idea-plugin.name: CMP Resource Locator
idea-plugin.description:
Compose Multiplatform resource tooling for Android Studio and IntelliJ IDEA.

Navigate to source resources
Cmd+Click (or Ctrl+Click) on Res.string.key, Res.plurals.key, Res.array.key, Res.drawable.name or Res.font.name jumps directly to the source resource in composeResources/ instead of the generated accessor.

Inline value preview
The actual value is shown as a dim inline hint next to every Res.string.key, Res.plurals.key and Res.array.key reference — no need to open the XML file to know what the key contains. Click a hint to open the declaration.

Qualifier support
  • Language and region: values-ru/, values-en-rUS/, … (the default values/ is preferred for the inline preview)
  • Theme and density: drawable-dark/, drawable-light/, drawable-hdpi/, …
  • Any *.xml file inside a values* directory is read, not only strings.xml
  • Multiple matches open a chooser popup
Build directories are never included in results.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.0
  • Navigation and inline previews for Res.plurals and Res.array
  • Inline hints are clickable and open the declaration
  • Inlay hints moved to the declarative API: per-type toggles in Settings | Editor | Inlay Hints | Values
  • Resource lookup is cached, so previews no longer re-parse every values file on each keystroke
  • Any *.xml inside values* is read, not only strings.xml
  • Drawable and font lookup no longer depends on a hardcoded extension list
  • No more errors while the IDE is still indexing

idea-plugin.name: Android Studio Korean Language Pack

idea-plugin.name: CMP Kit
idea-plugin.description:
CMP Kit is an Android Studio / IntelliJ plug-in for Compose Multiplatform (CMP) that is used to improve the efficiency of accessing composeResources resources.

idea-plugin.name: Mindmap - Call Graph Visualizer
idea-plugin.description:
Mindmap - Call Graph Visualizer

Visualize function call graphs as interactive mind maps inside your IDE. Place your cursor on any Kotlin or Java function and press Alt / Option + G to instantly see its callers, callees, and function depth — including cross-language edges between Kotlin and Java.

Features

  • Bidirectional Call Graph — Outbound calls + inbound callers with configurable depth (1–5)
  • Hierarchical Layout — Callers left, root center, callees right with crossing minimization
  • Mini-Map — VS Code-style overview with colored dots and click/drag navigation
  • Tree View — Collapsible tree with type-specific icons and section headers
  • Trace & Expand — Double-click to merge call graphs, Cmd+Click to re-center
  • Abstract Tracing — Traces through abstract/interface functions to concrete implementations
  • Hide/Unhide Nodes — Hide nodes with cascade logic, floating panel to restore
  • Smart Navigation — Arrow keys, history back/forward, click-to-navigate to source
  • Search & Filter — Filter nodes by name across both views
  • Hover Info Cards — Signature, file location, depth, and LOC count
  • Pan & Select Modes — Figma-style interaction with box selection and multi-node move
  • Smooth Zoom — Scroll wheel, pinch-to-zoom, and keyboard shortcuts at 60fps

Quick Start

  1. Place cursor inside any Kotlin or Java function
  2. Press Alt / Option + G (or right-click → Generate Mindmap)
  3. Explore the interactive call graph in the Mindmap tool window

For shortcuts, detailed help, and more visit vishal2376.github.io/mindmap

Supports Kotlin (K1 & K2) and Java on IntelliJ IDEA 2024.3–2026.1 and Android Studio Ladybug+. Built on an extensible provider architecture — additional JetBrains languages can be added without UI changes.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.5

  • Java support — Alt+G now works on Java methods. Graphs render with Java as the root, callers and callees resolve just like Kotlin. (#2)
  • Cross-language edges (Java ↔ Kotlin) — Kotlin calling Java and Java calling Kotlin both appear as connected nodes in the graph. Inbound search surfaces callers from either language.
  • JUnit test filtering for Java — @Test, @ParameterizedTest, @RepeatedTest (JUnit 4 and Jupiter), TestNG @Test, and kotlin.test.Test are filtered when "Exclude test functions" is on.
  • Welcome screen — hint updated to "Place your cursor on any Kotlin / Java function".
  • Extensible provider architecture — new languages can be added by implementing a single extension; no changes to the UI, history, or graph orchestrator.
  • Hardening — tighter URL validation for external links and a locked-down Content-Security-Policy for the tool-window frame. The visualization library is now bundled with the plugin instead of fetched over the network at startup.
  • Internal cleanup — removed several unused methods, narrowed an over-broad exception catch so cancellation and PSI failures are no longer silently swallowed, and tightened a few small code paths. No user-visible behavior change.

1.0.4

  • Collapse/Expand All — New buttons in tree view header to collapse or expand all nested nodes at once (#8)
  • Debug Mode — Toggle in settings to save plugin logs to a dedicated mindmap-debug.log file for bug reports; crashes are always logged (#9)
  • Tree View Info Badge — File name and LOC combined into a compact badge with improved text contrast
  • Tree Tooltip Removed — Disabled tooltip popup in tree view that was overlapping node text (#7)
  • Fixed: Multi-Node Drag — Selecting multiple nodes and dragging with trackpad now moves all selected nodes together (#10)
  • Fixed: Android Studio Navigation — Wrapped editor navigation in WriteIntentReadAction to fix crash on newer IntelliJ/Android Studio builds
  • Fixed: EDT Threading — Moved JSON serialization, HTML loading, and graph updates off the main thread for smoother UI
  • Fixed: Memory Leak — JCEF load handler is now properly removed on dispose
  • Removed Deprecated APIs — Replaced runReadAction and partiallyAppliedSymbol with current stable APIs

1.0.3

  • Redesigned Settings — New minimal inline settings panel with sliders, depth track indicators, reset-to-defaults, and clearer labels
  • Website & Feedback Buttons — Quick links to the plugin website and GitHub issues directly from the settings panel
  • Configurable Retrace Depth — Separate outbound/inbound depth controls for the trace (double-click) operation
  • Barycenter Crossing Minimization — Improved hierarchical layout reduces edge crossings for cleaner graphs
  • Node Position Persistence — Graph preserves node positions and zoom level after tracing
  • Fixed: Empty Blue Boxes — Cascade hiding no longer orphans nodes and leaves empty placeholders
  • Fixed: Abstract Function Navigation — Navigation now works correctly for abstract functions and focused-file graphs

1.0.2

  • Live Mini-Map — VS Code-style minimap (top-left) with colored node dots, viewport rectangle, click-to-pan, and drag-to-pan navigation
  • Hide/Unhide Nodes — Hover any node to reveal an eye button; hidden nodes cascade-hide disconnected children and preserve their layout position across retraces
  • Hidden Nodes Panel — Bottom-left panel auto-appears when nodes are hidden; lists all hidden nodes with one-click unhide for easy access
  • Settings Modal — Gear button opens a redesigned settings panel with outbound/inbound depth controls, visual depth track indicators, and clear descriptions
  • Configurable Depth — Adjust outbound (1-5) and inbound (1-5) trace depth from the settings modal; takes effect on next trace
  • Abstract Function Tracing — Traces through abstract/interface functions to their concrete implementations (up to 3)
  • Figma-style Zoom — Smooth pinch-to-zoom and scroll-zoom with requestAnimationFrame batching for 60fps performance
  • Straight-Line Edges — Replaced cubic bezier curves with straight lines for maximum rendering performance
  • Crossing Minimization — Improved hierarchical layout with hubsize sorting, edge minimization, block shifting, and shake-towards-leaves
  • Performance First — Always-on high-performance rendering (disabled shadows/smoothing/animations)
  • Figma-style Interaction — Toggle between Pan (H) and Select (V) modes
  • Incremental Trace — Double-click a node to merge its call graph into the view
  • Restart & Clear — New button/shortcut (R) to wipe graph data and free memory

1.0.1

  • Fixed Android Studio tool window icon collision
  • Added Keyboard Shortcuts help modal (?)
  • Keyboard focus persists correctly in Tool Window after code navigation

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • Interactive graph view with hierarchical layout
  • Tree view with SVG icons and continuous connectors
  • Box/marquee selection for multi-node movement
  • Right-click / middle-click drag for panning
  • Navigation history (back/forward)
  • Double-click trace with position preservation
  • Smart duplicate name detection with filename
  • Bidirectional analysis (outbound + inbound calls)
  • Large file optimization (300 node cap, batch limits)
  • Crash-proof error handling across all entry points
  • JCEF fallback panel for Android Studio
  • Catppuccin Mocha dark theme

idea-plugin.name: Gradle Glimpse
idea-plugin.description:
A lifesaver for Flutter developers migrating to AGP 8 and 9.

Updating the Android Gradle Plugin (AGP) in a mature Flutter project often breaks the build due to hidden legacy native dependencies. Gradle Glimpse lives inside your pubspec.yaml to give you instant diagnostic insights.


Features:
  • Project-Wide Diagnostics: Hover over the dependencies: key for a complete AGP upgrade verdict, showing the absolute maximum safe AGP version for your entire project.
  • Instant Compatibility Checks: Hover over any Android-enabled plugin in your pubspec to instantly see its AGP version and compatibility status.
  • Transitive Dependency Tracing: Uncover "hidden" native Android dependencies dragged in by pure Dart packages.
  • AGP 9 Readiness: Automatically detects critical AGP 9 blockers, such as the legacy kotlin-android plugin, missing namespaces, and outdated Java requirements.
  • Flutter Auto-Healing Detection: Intelligently warns you when Flutter is secretly patching legacy code at runtime.
  • Real-Time Syncing: Intelligently watches your file system and instantly updates diagnostics the moment you run flutter pub get.
  • Customizable UI: Toggle the visibility of Glimpse markers at any time via the View menu or right-click context menu.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.1
  • New Feature: Added a project-wide diagnostic summary. Hover over the dependencies: key in your pubspec.yaml for a complete AGP upgrade verdict.
  • New Feature: Added a visibility toggle. You can now hide/show Gradle Glimpse icons via the main View menu or by right-clicking in the editor.
  • Bug Fix: Fixed the "Infinite Cache" bug. Icons and diagnostic data will now instantly update when you save the file or run flutter pub get, without requiring an IDE restart.

1.0.0
  • Initial release: Full AGP compatibility scanning, transitive dependency tracing, and IDE hover UI.

idea-plugin.name: Appium Lens
idea-plugin.description:
Appium Lens - Mobile Testing Environment Manager

Appium Lens is a setup wizard and environment manager for mobile test automation with Appium. It detects missing dependencies, installs them with one click, and keeps your environment healthy so you spend time writing tests, not debugging toolchains.

Platforms: macOS (Homebrew-based) and Windows (manual/Chocolatey) · iOS and Android toolchain support

Features

  • One-click setup wizard — detects and installs all required mobile testing dependencies
  • Smart installation routing — Homebrew, npm, and system-package strategies per tool
  • Real-time dependency health monitoring with actionable fix suggestions
  • Automatic tool update detection and one-click upgrade
  • Manual installation guide with step-by-step instructions and live command output
  • Emulator startup management with detailed error diagnostics

  • Android SDK and Platform Tools
  • Xcode Command Line Tools
  • Node.js and npm (via Homebrew or nvm)
  • Appium Server and Appium Doctor

Privacy

Appium Lens optionally collects anonymous usage analytics (plugin lifecycle events, installation success/failure, feature usage, error reports) via Firebase Analytics. No personal data, project code, or file paths are ever collected. Analytics are opt-in only — you are asked for consent on first use and can change this at any time in Settings > Tools > Appium Lens > Analytics.

idea-plugin.name: Logify
idea-plugin.description:
Logify — Smart Android logging assistant for Java & Kotlin.

Live Templates
  • logd, loge, logi, logw, logt — auto-fill ClassName#methodName tags in Java & Kotlin
Intentions
  • Normalize log tag — fix a bad tag on the current Log call

idea-plugin.change-notes: 1.0 – Initial release • Live templates: logd / loge / logi / logw / logt (Java & Kotlin) • Intention: Normalize log tag • Intention: Log This — wrap any expression in a log call instantly • Bulk action: Normalize All Log Tags in File • Generator: Insert Kotlin Log Wrapper (Any.logd/e/i/w extensions) • Generator: Insert Java Log Wrapper (L.java utility class) • Inspection: Unguarded Log call — warns on Log.* not wrapped in BuildConfig.DEBUG (Java & Kotlin) • Inspection: Sensitive data in log call — detects passwords/tokens/secrets in log arguments (Java & Kotlin) • Inspection: Log call should use Timber — opt-in warning to migrate from Log to Timber (Java & Kotlin) • Action: Wrap All Unguarded Logs in Project — bulk-fix every unguarded Log call • Action: Check Release Readiness — project-wide scan for debug logs, unguarded logs, and sensitive data leaks • Action: Convert All Log Calls to Timber — replaces every Log.d/e/i/w/v with the equivalent Timber call • Action: Remove Debug Log Calls — deletes all Log.d/i/v and Timber.d/i/v calls project-wide

idea-plugin.name: Smart Code Sorter X
idea-plugin.description:
Organizes Kotlin code by sorting class members and constructor parameters in a consistent, configurable order.

Features

  • Sort class members (properties, init blocks, functions) in a fully configurable order
  • Sort primary constructor parameters by group (val/var/private) then alphabetically
  • Settings panel — Reorder property categories, toggle alphabetical function sorting, and enable Sort on Save at Settings → Tools → Smart Code Sorter
  • Sort summary — Balloon notification tells you exactly what changed: "moved 3 properties, reordered 5 functions"
  • @nosort marker — Add // @nosort above any declaration to pin it in place; the rest of the class still sorts normally around it
  • Optional Sort on Save — reorder code automatically whenever a Kotlin file is saved

Usage

Right-click in the editor → Sort Kotlin Code, or press Ctrl+Shift+S (Windows/Linux) / ⌥⌘S (macOS).

Configure at Settings → Tools → Smart Code Sorter.

Default sort order

Class body: Primary constructor → Secondary constructors (by param count) → Properties → Lifecycle methods (onAttach → onDetach) → init blocks → Composable functions → Other functions (public → internal → protected → private; then alphabetically) → @Preview functions → Inner classes → Regular classes → Interfaces → Companion object.

Properties: Private → Protected → Internal → Public → Constant → Mutable → Immutable → Injected → Late-init → Delegated → Android View → Rx types → Flow types → Compose state → Other. Category order is fully configurable in Settings.

Constructor parameters: (1) no val/var, (2) val, (3) var, (4) private val, (5) private var — within each group, alphabetically.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.2.2

  • Deprecated API fix — Both overloads of SimpleListCellRenderer.create() are scheduled for removal, including the Customizer one used in 1.2.1. The settings panel's category list now uses the platform's own replacement, textListCellRenderer().

1.2.1

  • Deprecated API fix — Replaced the deprecated SimpleListCellRenderer.create(String, Function) overload (scheduled for removal) with the Customizer-based overload in the settings panel.

1.2.0

  • Fixed: // @nosort never worked. The marker was documented since 1.1.0 but pinned nothing at all, because Kotlin attaches a comment written above a declaration to that declaration itself rather than leaving it as a separate preceding element — and only the separate-element case was being checked. Pinned declarations now really do keep their position while everything around them sorts.
  • New: Code → Smart Code Sorter menu. Both Sort Kotlin Code and the Sort on Save toggle are now reachable from the Code menu. The toggle was implemented in 1.1.0 but never registered, so it had never appeared anywhere in the UI.
  • Compatibility is now stable across IDE updates. The minimum supported IDE build used to be taken from whichever IDE the plugin happened to be built on, which quietly raised the requirement for everyone each time. It is pinned at 2025.2 and verified against 2025.2, 2025.3 and 2026.1.
  • Under the hood — Sorting now uses the platform's cancellable background-analysis API, so an in-progress sort yields to your edits instead of holding a stale result, and the two sort-on-save paths share one implementation. Build toolchain updated (Gradle 9.7, Kotlin 2.2.20, IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.18.1) with all deprecated API usage removed.

1.1.1

  • Deprecated API fix — Replaced all usages of the deprecated ActionsKt.runReadAction() with ReadAction.compute() to ensure compatibility with future IntelliJ Platform releases.

1.1.0

  • Settings panel — Configure the plugin per project at Settings → Tools → Smart Code Sorter: reorder property categories with up/down arrows, toggle alphabetical function sorting, and enable Sort on Save.
  • Sort summary notification — After sorting, the balloon now shows exactly what changed, e.g. "moved 3 properties, reordered 5 functions", so you always know what the sorter did.
  • @nosort marker — Add a // @nosort comment above any property or function to pin it at its current position. The rest of the class still sorts normally around it.
  • Bug fix — Sort on Save and its settings were not persisted between sessions due to missing service registration; this is now fixed.
  • Comments directly above a declaration are now moved together with it when the declaration is reordered.

1.0.3

  • Updates for some deprecated APIs
  • Fixed some bugs
  • Handled some errors

idea-plugin.name: HS ADB Tools
idea-plugin.description:
**HS ADB Tools** brings the most commonly used ADB (Android Debug Bridge) commands directly into Android Studio as a menu under Tools > ADB Tools, so you never need to leave the IDE to run shell commands.

Features

Devices

  • List Connected Devices — Show all devices and emulators currently attached via ADB
  • Show Current App Package — Detect the foreground app's package name and copy it to clipboard
  • Reboot Device — Reboot to normal, recovery, or bootloader mode

Application

  • Install APK — Pick an APK file from disk and install it on the selected device
  • Uninstall App — Enter a package name and uninstall it
  • Clear App Data — Run adb shell pm clear <package> to wipe app storage
  • Reinstall Current App — Auto-detect the foreground app, pull its APK, and reinstall it
  • Uninstall Current App — Auto-detect the foreground app and uninstall it with one click
  • Clear Current App Data — Auto-detect the foreground app and clear its data

Debugging

  • Take Bug Report — Run adb bugreport and save the output to a local file
  • Set Debug App — Run adb shell am set-debug-app -w so the app waits for a debugger on next launch
  • Clear Debug App — Remove the debug-app flag

Screen Capture

idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • LocalReviewBundle: replaced the deprecated DynamicBundle(String) constructor with DynamicBundle(Class<?>, String), flagged by JetBrains Marketplace's plugin verifier against 2026.3 EAP.   • Live preview: See the generated Dart class as you configure options
  • JSON tree view: Inspect JSON structure with a collapsible tree (Format Only)
  • Configurable options:
    • nullable — types use ? suffix, no required in constructor
    • default value — adds @JsonKey(defaultValue: ...) based on type, required in constructor
    • use JsonKey.name — all fields annotated with @JsonKey(name: 'original_key')
  • JSON validation: English error messages for invalid JSON
  • Auto build_runner: Runs dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs after generation
  • Nested object support: Automatically generates nested Dart classes
  • Customizable settings: Dialog title and prompt text configurable in Settings → Tools → Flutter Hi Json

  2. Select New → Flutter Hi Json
  3. Paste your JSON data in the left editor
  4. Click Format to preview the generated Dart class, or Format Only to view the JSON tree
  5. Enter a class name (auto-converted to UpperCamelCase)
  6. Configure options (nullable / default value / use JsonKey.name)
  7. Click OK to generate the .dart file and run build_runner

Go to Settings → Tools → Flutter Hi Json to customize:

  3. Go to Settings → Plugins → ⚙️ → Install Plugin from Disk
  4. Select the downloaded zip file
  5. Restart the IDE

idea-plugin.name: Compose Preview Pro
idea-plugin.description:
Device-less Jetpack / Compose Multiplatform preview, with auto-mocked arguments, hot reload, and click-to-source navigation.

Render any @Composable function — including ones with complex, custom-typed arguments — without booting an emulator or running the app. Edit a parameter in the side panel and the rendered preview updates in under a second.

What you get

  • Device-less rendering. Out-of-process Compose Desktop renderer turns any @Composable into a PNG. No emulator, no Android target needed — works against KMP commonMain.
  • Auto-mocked arguments. Primitives, data classes, sealed hierarchies, enums, List<T>, Map<K, V>, Modifier, and function types are fabricated recursively. No more "preview-only" overloads.
  • Hot reload via JVM Instrumentation. Save the file, Gradle recompiles, and the renderer JVM swaps the new bytecode in ~50 ms — no plugin restart, no full rebuild.
  • Per-element parameter editor. Click an element on the canvas to surface its source-call arguments. Edits write back into source via PSI, preserving formatting, comments, and trailing commas. Positional arguments are resolved to their declared parameter name and become editable as named args.
  • Click-to-source navigation. A two-tier ranker prefers @Composable callees over modifier / factory helpers, so clicks land on the user-visible composable instead of fillMaxSize or cardElevation.
  • Multi-frame device grid. One toggle to render the same composable simultaneously at phone, tablet, and desktop sizes.
  • Theme switching. LIGHT / DARK dropdown applied through Material 3's MaterialTheme.
  • Interactive preview. Click and scroll events round-trip into the running composition — buttons press, lazy lists scroll, state hoists work.
  • Live UI mode. An embedded ComposePanel mounts the composable directly in the IDE — no PNG round-trip — for state-heavy workflows.
  • AI-assisted mocks. Optional Claude API toggle replaces auto-mocked strings with semantically appropriate content.

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA Community / Ultimate 2024.3+ (or compatible Android Studio).
  • Kotlin plugin enabled.
  • JDK 21 (build-time).

Open any file containing a @Composable, click the ▶ in the gutter, and the tool window renders the composable with mocked arguments. Enable 🔍 Inspect in the toolbar and click an element to surface its arguments in the side panel.

Source & issue tracker on GitHub
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.4.0 — Render real Android apps off-device: value classes, native runtime, resources

  • Composables with value-class parameters now render. A parameter like accent: Color (any @JvmInline value class) name-mangles its JVM method and defeats kotlin-reflect entirely. A new pure-Java invocation path reconstructs the Compose calling convention straight from the bytecode, so these composables — extremely common in real design systems — render instead of failing with TARGET_NOT_FOUND.
  • Real off-device Android runtime. Android-targeted composables that touch WindowInsets, Build.VERSION, interpolators, etc. used to crash with RuntimeException: Stub!. The renderer now bundles a real Android framework and neutralises its native methods systematically (an ASM class transformer), so the whole android.* surface initialises off-device.
  • Android resources. stringResource(R.string.…) and painterResource(R.drawable.…) render (drawables as a clean placeholder vector) instead of NPE-ing.
  • Faithful model arguments. Data classes with internal constructors and third-party field types (e.g. kotlinx.datetime.Instant) are now built whole, so Text(model.title) no longer NPEs on a null field.
  • Multi-module / shared-UI. Cross-module widgets, theme CompositionLocals, and types from a separate :core:designsystem-style module resolve from a cold preview.
  • Desktop viewModel(). LocalViewModelStoreOwner is provided universally; DI-backed koinViewModel()/hiltViewModel() now surface an actionable "preview the stateless content" message.

0.3.9 — Production-install fixes: renderer launch, default args, smooth scroll

  • Bundled renderer is found again in real installs. Since 0.3.5 the plugin located its bundled renderer via the JVM CodeSource, but IntelliJ's PluginClassLoader doesn't populate one — so every "Install from Disk" install failed with Renderer launcher not found. Resolution now goes through the plugin's own PluginAwareClassLoader.pluginDescriptor.pluginPath (the JetBrains-recommended self-resolution path), with the CodeSource kept only as a dev fallback. Every lookup miss is now logged instead of failing silently.
  • Renderer launches from paths containing spaces. The -javaagent: option injected into the start script wasn't inner-quoted, so a space in the install path (e.g. …/Application Support/…) split the argument and the JVM aborted with Error opening zip file or JAR manifest missing before the IPC handshake. The agent option is now wrapped in escaped quotes the way Gradle encodes its own JVM opts.
  • Deterministic renderer JVM. The renderer subprocess now always runs under the IDE's own JBR (the same java.home as the IDE), so it no longer depends on whatever java happens to be on the user's PATH (a Java 17 there previously caused an UnsupportedClassVersionError).
  • Default arguments now render correctly. Composables with defaulted parameters — e.g. colors: TopAppBarColors = TopAppBarDefaults.topAppBarColors() — used to render blank because the synthetic Compose $default bitmask was hard-coded to 0 ("caller supplied everything"), so the author's defaults never applied and a fabricated, transparent value was used instead. The renderer now computes the $default mask and lets optional parameters fall back to their declared defaults; only required parameters (which carry the content) are auto-mocked. Far higher visual fidelity on real-world Material composables.
  • Smooth interactive scroll. Scrolling the preview used to spawn one background task per wheel event — a trackpad flick created hundreds of tasks, each blocking on the renderer's IPC lock, freezing the UI. Scroll events are now coalesced onto a single pump ("one render in flight + one accumulated delta"); clicks are never dropped.
  • Clear startup diagnostics + restart on (un)install. A renderer that dies on startup now reports its exit code and stderr tail instead of a cryptic deserialization error. The plugin is also marked require-restart, since it hosts a long-lived subprocess + JVM agent that can't be safely hot-swapped.

0.3.8 — Audit-driven hardening: inline value classes, renderer self-healing

  • Inline value classes are now mockable — composables with parameters like fun Profile(id: UserId) where @JvmInline value class UserId(val id: Long) previously fell through every layer of the mock cascade to "No mocker registered". The mock engine now detects KClass.isValue, recursively mocks the underlying property type, and invokes the primary constructor to wrap the value. Framework value classes (androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color, kotlin.time.Duration, etc.) are intentionally skipped so the specialised handlers downstream produce semantically correct instances instead of bit-packed garbage that crashes Skia.
  • Renderer survives malformed wire messages — a corrupted RenderRequest (truncated base64, protocol-version skew, transient encoder hiccup) used to call exitProcess(1), the plugin marked the subprocess Crashed, and respawned a fresh JVM (~3 s of latency) only to potentially retry the same broken request. Now each loop iteration has its own error boundary: deserialisation errors and handler-level throws produce a PROTOCOL_ERROR response and the renderer continues serving the next request. Only EOF on stdin and an explicit Shutdown exit the loop.
  • Subprocess-death reader unhang — the I/O thread that reads renderer responses with a timeout used to interrupt itself on timeout. Thread.interrupt() does not unblock a thread parked inside BufferedReader.readLine(); the daemon thread stayed alive until JVM exit, holding the dead subprocess's pipe handle. The timeout path now closes the underlying stream from the outside, which makes the readLine() throw IOException and lets the thread terminate cleanly.
  • Static-init guard around classifier inspection — pathological user types whose companion-object init throws (rare but real on legacy code paths) used to bubble out of type.classifier as? KClass<*> and abort the entire render. They now report Unsupported with a clear message and the surrounding composable still renders for the well-behaved arguments.
  • Regression-safe: the 83-test type-mocking suite remains all-green, and pluginVerifier stays Compatible against IC-243 + IC-252.

0.3.7 — JEP 451 hot-reload, Compose 1.10 dependency notation, remote-dev posture

  • Hot-reload agent now loads via -javaagent: at JVM startup instead of self-attach via the Attach API. JDK 21's JEP 451 prints a warning on every self-load and a future JDK will make it fail by default. The Gradle application plugin's start-script template wraps DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS in single quotes (POSIX) and re-escapes $ through its printf | xargs | sed | eval pipeline, so a literal $APP_HOME survives unexpanded — we work around this by injecting a second double-quoted DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS line in startScripts.doLast, prepending the -javaagent: flag with $APP_HOME properly expanded at runtime. Self-attach remains a fallback for paths where the start-script injection cannot be honoured (manual java -cp …, smoke tests, Mockito's inline mock maker).
  • Compose Multiplatform 1.10 deprecations cleared. The compose.runtime / compose.ui / compose.foundation Gradle DSL accessors were deprecated in CMP 1.10 in favour of explicit Maven coordinates. :mock-engine and :sample now use the typed catalog entries (libs.compose.runtime, libs.compose.ui, libs.compose.foundation) — same artifacts, no deprecation warnings, no surprise breakage in CMP 1.11.
  • Remote Dev posture documented. Until a 0.4.x Modular Plugin V2 refactor, the plugin runs on the backend host in JetBrains Gateway split mode (tool window absent on the JetBrains Client). The PNG-streaming render path is architecturally remote-friendly already; the Live-UI mode needs the frontend module split to ship a Compose surface to the client. plugin.xml now spells this out in a top-of-file comment.
  • No user-visible behaviour change on the desktop. pluginVerifier still "Compatible" against IC-243 (2024.3) and IC-252 (2025.2). The agent loads identically — only the path changes from self-attach to premain.

0.3.6 — Platform 2026 hardening: AGP plugin upgrade, modern service lifecycle, EDT discipline

  • IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.3.0 → 2.16.0. Thirteen minor versions of catch-up. Migrated to the typed create("IC", "...") verifier API, accommodated the sandbox move to .intellijPlatform/sandbox, and explicitly pinned verifier IDEs so the new auto-applied recommended() default doesn't surprise us with an unresolvable EAP artifact.
  • Constructor-injected CoroutineScope. HotReloadCoordinator no longer creates its own CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob + IO); it now receives a scope from the platform via the IJPL-83 service-injection contract. Cancellation is automatic on project close / plugin disable / IDE shutdown. The VFS message-bus subscription is parented to the same scope via the connect(CoroutineScope) overload, so it tears down on the same signal. Net effect: zero manual lifecycle code, zero leak vectors.
  • Proper Disposable chain on the live-UI panel. LivePreviewPanel implements Disposable, registered as a child of PreviewPanel, which is itself parented to the tool window's Content. On disposal the embedded ComposePanel releases its Skia surface + AWT peer and the cached URLClassLoader is closed — previously these leaked on every project switch.
  • EDT discipline. show() and clear() on the live panel now assert EDT.assertIsEdt() — Swing mutation and ComposePanel.setContent are both EDT-only, and silent off-EDT calls were a latent crash waiting for a stricter platform release.
  • Explicit ModalityState + project-disposed guard on every invokeLater. All 12 panel-update sites in PreviewService now route through a single runOnEdt helper that pins ModalityState.defaultModalityState() and supplies project.disposed as the expiration condition. Future strictness in platform modality enforcement (planned for 2026.3+) won't silently drop our render results, and renders that complete after the project closes are dropped cleanly instead of resurrecting a half-disposed tool window.
  • Bounded log allocation. Hot-reload's "VFS change" log line previously joined every touched file name into one string — fine for editing one file, ruinous for a 4000-file monorepo refactor. Capped at 5 names plus "(+N more)".
  • Pure cleanup; no user-visible behaviour change. Both pluginVerifier and the test suite remain green on IC-243 (2024.3) and IC-252 (2025.2) with zero deprecated, internal, or experimental API usages flagged.

0.3.5 — Marketplace verifier 2026.2 compatibility

  • Internal API removed. The bundled-renderer lookup no longer calls PluginManagerCore.getPlugin(PluginId) (marked @ApiStatus.Internal in 2026.2). It now self-resolves the plugin install directory via the JVM CodeSource of one of our own classes — pure stdlib, zero IntelliJ Platform API, future-proof against further internal-API churn.
  • Synthetic bridge methods eliminated. The plugin module now compiles with jvm-default=no-compatibility. Previously, Kotlin emitted bridge overrides for every default method on ToolWindowFactory (isApplicable, isDoNotActivateOnStart, getAnchor, getIcon, manage, …). Each bridge's invokespecial referenced a deprecated or experimental Platform API and the Marketplace verifier counted it as a usage by us. JVM 8 default-method dispatch now handles them transparently.
  • Net effect: 1 internal + 4 deprecated + 6 experimental API usages on 2026.2 EAP → 0/0/0. No user-facing behavioural change; pure verifier hygiene to unblock Marketplace publishing.

0.1.8 — Mockito inline mock maker for Android Context stub (final-class fix)

  • 0.1.6/0.1.7 tried to build the Context stub with plain ByteBuddy subclassing, which crashed at android.content.res.AssetManager because that class is final. Switched to Mockito 5's inline mock maker, which uses JVMTI class redefinition to intercept methods on final classes — the AssetManager mock now works and Compose Resources' preview path can call context.assets.open(path) successfully (routed to ClassLoader.getResourceAsStream).
  • Added detailed diagnostic logging at every step of the stub creation so future failures surface immediately instead of bubbling up as a generic LocalContext not present.

0.1.6 — Synthetic Android Context for KMP projects with no desktop target

  • The big one: the renderer now generates a runtime android.content.Context stub via ByteBuddy and provides it through LocalContext, letting Compose Multiplatform Resources (stringResource, painterResource) work even when the user's Gradle module has only an androidMain target. Asset reads route to the URLClassLoader, so resources packaged into the user's JARs (composeResources/<module>/values/...) load cleanly.
  • No-op for non-Android scenarios — non-existent android.content.Context on the classpath means we skip the stub entirely.

0.1.5 — Smarter KMP target ranking + user-friendly Android-only diagnostics

  • Module probing now considers many KMP target names (desktopMain, jvmMain, desktopAndAndroidMain, skikoMain, nonAndroidMain) plus fuzzy matching on desktop/jvm/skiko substrings. Hits sorted: pure-JVM first, Android as last resort with a logged warning.
  • If the only available target is androidMain and the composable uses Compose Resources, the renderer now emits an actionable error explaining how to add a desktopMain source set, instead of dumping a raw CompositionLocal LocalContext not present stack trace.

0.1.4 — Kotlin Multiplatform commonMain support

  • Composables in a KMP commonMain source set used to fail with TARGET_NOT_FOUND because the commonMain module's compile output is metadata KLIB, not JVM bytecode. The plugin now redirects to a sibling JVM target (desktopMain → jvmMain → androidMain) at render time and uses ITS classpath instead.
  • No-op for single-target JVM or Android-only projects.

0.1.3 — Renderer bundled inside the plugin (production-install fix)

  • Critical: 0.1.0–0.1.2 only worked when launched from the source tree because the renderer subprocess (Compose Desktop host) wasn't packaged inside plugin.zip. Users who installed via "Install from Disk" hit Renderer launcher not found.
  • 0.1.3 bundles the full renderer install (bin/renderer + all classpath JARs, ~40 MB) inside the plugin's own install directory and resolves it via PluginManagerCore.getPlugin(...).pluginPath.

0.1.2 — Wider gutter-icon coverage

  • ▶ icon now appears on @Composable functions that live inside an object or companion object, not just top-level ones — covers common Material-design patterns (e.g. NiaIcons, MaterialTheme-style singletons).
  • Skipped explicitly (require a receiver instance): extension functions, class members, anonymous @Composable lambdas.

0.1.1 — Kotlin K2 mode compatibility

  • Declare supportsKotlinPluginMode supportsK2="true" — the plugin now loads in Android Studio K2 mode (and IntelliJ IDEA 2024.3+) without the "incompatible plugin" warning.
  • No code changes: our PSI usage was already K1/K2-agnostic; only the explicit manifest declaration was missing.

0.1.0 — Initial public release

  • Device-less Compose preview via out-of-process renderer.
  • Auto-mocked arguments (data class, sealed, enum, List, Map, Modifier, lambdas).
  • Hot reload via JVM Instrumentation (~50 ms swap).
  • Per-element parameter editor with PSI write-back.
  • Positional → named argument resolution.
  • Click-to-source navigation with composable-tier ranking.
  • Multi-frame device grid, theme + zoom controls, interactive preview, live UI mode.
  • Optional AI mock-string generation via Anthropic Claude.

idea-plugin.name: Ketoy
idea-plugin.description:
Ketoy is a server-driven execution runtime for Android. You write Kotlin and Jetpack Compose with a few Ketoy annotations, compile it into a signed, compact .ktx bytecode bundle, and execute it natively inside any app that ships the Ketoy runtime — the app is the platform, the server ships the screens. Learn more at ketoy.dev.

This plugin makes a Ketoy .ktx bundle a first-class, openable artifact in Android Studio and IntelliJ IDEA. Double-click a bundle and read exactly what is inside — no device, no hex editor, no guesswork.

What it gives you

  • Overview — bundle id, format version, minimum runtime and app version, signed status, and full content counts.
  • Sections — every section with its compressed flag, on-disk vs. decompressed size, and share of the file, so you can see where bytes go.
  • Strings — the interned string pool, filterable.
  • Manifests — the adapters, constructors, and host capabilities the bundle consumes.
  • Functions — per-function bytecode disassembly: each instruction with its mnemonic, a human description, resolved string operands, and the originating source line.
  • Entry points — named entry points mapped to their functions.
  • Verify signature — point it at an Ed25519 public key (raw, hex, or base64) and confirm the bundle is authentically signed.

Private by design. The inspector runs entirely on your machine, reads bundles without any key (a .ktx is signed, not encrypted), collects no data, and makes no network calls. It is read-only — it never modifies your bundles.

Links & contact
Website: https://ketoy.dev
Report an issue or request a feature: https://ketoy.dev/issue
Support: support@ketoy.dev
Report a security vulnerability: security@ketoy.dev

Developer: Ketoy  ·  Contact: support@ketoy.dev

License. Free to use worldwide under the Ketoy End-User License Agreement. The plugin is proprietary (closed-source); all rights reserved. It bundles third-party open-source components under their own licenses.
idea-plugin.change-notes:

  • Per-function bytecode disassembly with resolved string operands and source lines.
  • Ed25519 signature verification against a public key (raw, hex, or base64).

idea-plugin.name: Custom Sound Alert
idea-plugin.description:
Custom Sound Alert

Assign your own audio notifications to common IDE events so you can step away from the screen and still know what just happened.

  • Build success & build failure
  • All tests passed & one or more tests failed

Configure everything under Settings → Tools → Custom Sound Alert (or the Tools → Custom Sound Alert menu): pick a .wav or .mp3 file per event, set a global volume, and preview each sound with the Test button. Sounds play asynchronously and never block the IDE.

idea-plugin.name: LeakLens - Android Memory Leak Detector & AI Fix Assistant
idea-plugin.description:
LeakLens is a professional-grade memory leak detection suite for Android Studio. It bridges the critical gap between the Android Profiler (deep but manual) and LeakCanary (runtime-only) by bringing the Shark Heap Analysis engine directly into your IDE and augmenting it with AI-powered intelligence.

Whether you're tracking down a stubborn memory leak, investigating an OOM crash, or preventing leaks before they ship, LeakLens provides a complete Detect → Analyze → Fix workflow without leaving Android Studio.

⭐ Now trusted by 750+ Android developers. Validated for Android Studio Koala (241) through Rabbit (262).

▶ Watch the 2-Minute Demo

✨ Feature Highlights

🤖 AI-Powered Fix Assistant

Stop deciphering complex leak traces manually. Use integrated Gemini or GPT-4 to translate raw reference chains into actionable, idiomatic Kotlin or Java fixes based on semantic lifetime evidence.

🛡️ Preventive UAST Static Analysis

Catch memory leaks as you type. The new Semantic Lifetime Engine detects 12+ critical patterns with real-time gutter markers:

  • Jetpack Compose: Context/View capture in @Composable or remember blocks.
  • Kotlin Coroutines: Unsafe GlobalScope or Flow collection outside lifecycle scopes.
  • Dependency Injection: Hilt scope mismatches (e.g., @Singleton injecting @ActivityScoped bindings).
  • WorkManager: Context retention in Worker fields.
  • Classic Leaks: Static Activity refs, Anonymous Inner Classes, and missing Handler cleanup.

🔍 Zero-SDK Runtime Analysis

No Gradle dependencies. No SDK integration. No APK bloat. Capture heap dumps through ADB and analyze them host-side. This offloads the heavy lifting to your workstation, avoiding device-side OOMs during analysis.

📊 Unified Findings Dashboard

A single source of truth for your app's memory health. Consolidates runtime heap leaks and static analysis findings into a responsive, StateFlow-driven dashboard.

📈 Real-Time Memory Monitoring

Track JVM Heap, Native Heap, and PSS Memory with a non-blocking graph. Features a new First-Run Onboarding flow to help you get started instantly.

🎯 Precision Source Navigation

Every object in a leak trace is a clickable link. Navigate from a leaked reference directly to the exact line of code in your project.

🚀 Why LeakLens?

LeakLens is the only tool that combines runtime precision with author-time prevention:

Feature LeakLens Android Profiler LeakCanary
Feedback Loop Authoring / Real-time Manual / Debugging Runtime
IDE Integration Native Tool Window Partial None
APK Impact Zero Zero ~300KB+
Remediation AI-Powered Fixes Manual Trace only

Building high-quality Android apps shouldn't be slowed down by memory leaks. If LeakLens saves you time, please consider leaving a ★★★★★ review!
idea-plugin.change-notes:

idea-plugin.name: Bugsy
idea-plugin.description:
Bugsy is a cute animated 2D companion character that lives on the status bar of your IDE, walking along the bottom edge and reacting to everything happening in your project.

✨ Features

  • 4 Characters — Slime, Android Mascot, iOS Bot, or Ghost. Switch anytime by right-clicking.
  • Build Reactions — Bugsy turns orange and frantic during Gradle builds, celebrates on success, looks sad on failures.
  • Double-click to Pause — Double-click to make Bugsy stop and bounce for 5 seconds with a developer health tip.

  • Custom Colors — Choose from Green, Blue, Orange, Purple, Cyan, Pink or Red via the right-click menu.

🎮 Controls

  • Double-click — Pause + bounce + show health tip
  • Right-click — Open settings (character model, color, show tip)

Bugsy keeps you company during those long compile times. Happy coding!
