Luna Image Editor: Crop, Resize & Remove Background

Crop, resize, convert and compress images in the Visual Studio Code sidebar. Remove backgrounds, move objects and restore details with local AI, then save your images directly into your project. Also available for JetBrains IDEs.

Open an Image

Use Add to Luna Image Editor from the project file or active editor menu, drag or paste an image, or use the file picker inside the editor. In VS Code, you can also open the Command Palette with Ctrl+Shift+P and run Add to Luna Image Editor. In JetBrains IDEs, use Find Action to run the same action.

Image Editing in the Sidebar

The editor includes:

  • Crop and resize
  • Rotate and mirror
  • Image upscaling
  • Text labels
  • Brush and arrow drawing
  • Overlay and image merging
  • Color-to-alpha transparency
  • Filters and image effects
  • Resize images for social media, Open Graph previews, websites, and project assets
  • Text extraction from images
  • Full undo and redo history for the current editing session

Move Objects with AI

Detect and move objects with local AI. Luna generates the area underneath, so you can rearrange your image without managing layers or opening another application.

Remove Background

Remove backgrounds from logos and human portraits with local AI. Prepare transparent images for websites, components, and project assets directly inside your IDE.

Detail Restoration

Restore details in old, compressed, or low-resolution images, logos, and graphics with local AI. Improve blurry or pixelated images for websites and social media.

Automatic Saving

Changes are saved automatically back to the original image file. Undo remains available during the current editing session. Duplicate the image before editing when you need to preserve the original file separately.

Formats and Conversion

  • Import PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP and SVG images.
  • Convert and export images as PNG, JPEG, or WebP (Pro).
  • Compress images for smaller project assets.
  • Copy an edited image to the clipboard.
  • Save a copy with a different filename or format.
  • Insert its project path into the active source file.

Resize Images for Social Media and the Web

Add more space or crop images to the dimensions you need for banners, product images and social posts.

Luna includes ready-made sizes for Instagram, Facebook, X, LinkedIn, YouTube, Google Ads, website banners, thumbnails, article images, product images, email headers, and Open Graph images.

Use the Open Graph preset to prepare og:image assets for link previews, then save the result directly into your project.

Source-Code Workflow

The editor is designed for image assets used in HTML, CSS, JavaScript, JSX, components, documentation, and extension projects. Open an asset from your project's file tree, edit it in the sidebar, and insert its project path into the active source file.

Commands

idea-plugin.name: Android Prefs and DataStore Editor
idea-plugin.description:
Android Prefs and DataStore Editor

The ultimate zero-dependency tool for Android developers to inspect, modify, and manage local app storage (SharedPreferences and Jetpack Preferences DataStore) directly from Android Studio.

No need to add heavy debugging libraries like Stetho or Flipper to your production APK—this plugin communicates natively with your debuggable app via ADB shell.

Note: Only debuggable application packages are supported (accessible via ADB run-as).

Key Features

  • Zero-Dependency Engine: Operates entirely through ADB (run-as) and a custom native Protobuf parser without inflating your APK or adding library overhead.
  • Jetpack DataStore Support: Native read/write support for binary .preferences_pb files without external third-party Protobuf library conflicts.
  • SharedPreferences Support: Full editing capabilities for traditional XML preferences.
  • Visual Table Editor: Edit storage key-value pairs in an intuitive, high-density interactive grid.
  • Automatic Sync & Restart: Instant push-back to app sandbox with automatic permission handling and app restart to reflect changes.
  • Real-time Diagnostic Console: Advanced log terminal with color-coded ADB command traces.

idea-plugin.name: OneInsight
idea-plugin.description:
Supports Android Studio and IntelliJ IDEA with the Android plugin installed.

Inspect network traffic using Android App Inspection and in-process ART hooks. No VPN, proxy, certificate installation, or app source changes required.

OneInsight — How to use each feature

OPEN THE TOOL WINDOW

  1. Install the plugin and restart Android Studio / IntelliJ IDEA.
  2. Open an Android project.
  3. Go to View → Tool Windows → OneInsight.

ATTACH TO AN APP (basic capture)

  1. Run a debuggable Android app on an emulator or USB device.
  2. In OneInsight, click Refresh.
  3. Select your app process from Debug process.
  4. Click Attach.
  5. Use the app. Supported requests appear in Traffic → Live.

Tips:

  • Keep Auto-attach checked to attach automatically when a matching debug process appears.
  • Click Detach to stop inspecting the current process.
  • Body limit (1 / 5 / 10 / 20 MB) controls how much request/response body is stored.

PAUSE / CLEAR LIVE TRAFFIC

  1. Click Pause to temporarily stop adding new rows (click again to Resume).
  2. Click Clear to remove all live traffic from the table.

FILTER LIVE TRAFFIC

Quick search:

  1. In Recorded Traffic, type in the search field (method, host, path, or status).

Protocol / error toggles:

  1. Check HTTP, WS, SSE, gRPC, and/or Errors.
  2. Leave all unchecked to show everything.

Advanced filters:

  1. Click Filter.
  2. Optionally set:
    • Host contains
    • Minimum / maximum status
    • Minimum / maximum duration (ms)
    • Treat main Search as regular expression
  3. Click OK (or Reset inside the dialog to clear advanced filters).

INSPECT A REQUEST (Traffic Details)

  1. Click a row in Live, Saved, or Timeline.
  2. Use the detail tabs on the right:
    • Formatted — readable summary
    • Request — request headers and body
    • Response — response headers and body
    • Timing — timing breakdown
    • JSON Tree — expandable JSON (use Expand / Collapse)
    • Preview — HTML or image preview when available
  3. Optional:
    • Search selected request/response: type text to highlight matches in headers/bodies.
    • Open: open details in a separate window.
    • Pin / Unpin: pin important rows.
    • Metadata: add comma-separated tags and a debugging note.

COPY AS CODE SNIPPETS

  1. Select a traffic row.
  2. Under Copy as, click one of:
    • cURL
    • JSON
    • Fetch
    • OkHttp
    • Retrofit
  3. Paste into a terminal, editor, or ticket.

SELECT, SAVE, EXPORT, IMPORT

Select rows:

  1. Check the checkbox on one or more Live rows.
  2. Use All / None to select or clear all visible rows.

Save a snapshot:

  1. Check the rows you want.
  2. Click Save.
  3. Enter a session name.
  4. The Saved tab opens with that session selected.

Export:

  1. On Live: check rows. On Saved: select a Session.
  2. Optionally keep Redact checked (hides Authorization, cookies, tokens, etc.).
  3. Click Export.
  4. Choose HAR or OneInsight JSON.
  5. Pick a save location.

Import:

  1. Click Import.
  2. Choose a OneInsight JSON or HAR file.
  3. The import is stored as a Saved session.

SAVED SESSIONS

  1. Open Traffic → Saved.
  2. Choose a Session from the dropdown.
  3. Click a row to inspect it in Traffic Details.
  4. Delete removes the selected saved session.

COMPARE SAVED VS LIVE

  1. Capture current live traffic.
  2. Open Traffic → Saved and select a previous session.
  3. Click Compare to review differences (Changes / Side by Side).
  4. Click Diff to export an HTML regression report.

TIMELINE

  1. Open Traffic → Timeline.
  2. Review request timing and overlap visually.
  3. Click a bar/row to load that exchange in Traffic Details.

COLUMNS

  1. On Live, click Columns…
  2. Toggle which table columns are visible.
  3. The selection checkbox column cannot be hidden (needed for Save / Export).

REPLAY (edit and resend)

From a captured request:

  1. Select a row.
  2. Click Replay (opens the Replay workspace tab).
  3. Edit method, URL, Headers (one per line: Name: value), and Body.
  4. Click Send.
  5. Inspect Response Body / Headers and status.

Save Replay favorites:

  1. In Replay, click New for a blank request, or load a saved one from Saved Requests.
  2. Click Save or Save As to store it for this project.
  3. Click Delete to remove a saved Replay request.

OPTIONAL SDK MODE (WebSocket frames + live SSE)

Use when you need WebSocket message frames or live SSE events (App Inspection alone cannot provide those).

  1. Add capture-sdk to debug builds (and capture-noop for release if you use that pattern).

  2. In app code:

    PacketIns.start(context)

    val client = PacketIns.install(OkHttpClient.Builder()).build()

    // WebSockets must use the SDK factory:
    val socket = PacketIns.webSocketFactory(client).newWebSocket(request, listener)

  3. Run the app, Attach in OneInsight as usual.

  4. HTTP / SSE / WebSocket events from the SDK appear in the same Live table.

Notes:

  • Install PacketIns on every OkHttpClient that should report traffic.
  • text/event-stream responses are streamed event-by-event when the interceptor is installed.
  • The plugin listens on loopback port 54789 and runs adb reverse when attaching.

ROW COLORS (quick legend)

  • Green = HTTP
  • Purple = WebSocket
  • Teal = SSE
  • Violet = gRPC
  • Red = Error

REQUIREMENTS / LIMITS

  • Debuggable or profileable app visible to Android App Inspection.
  • Supported libraries: OkHttp, HttpURLConnection, supported gRPC (plus SDK for WS frames / live SSE).
  • No VPN, proxy, or MITM certificate required.
  • Raw sockets and unsupported networking engines are not captured.

Developer: Udith Perera @Akurupela
Website: akurupela.com
GitHub: @udihperera-dev
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• New Database tab: browse SQLite / Room databases, watch a table update live, and run custom SQL with history and CSV export.
  • Query editor autocompletes tables, columns, and SQL keywords from the selected database's schema; saved queries can be named and reused per project.
  • Table view column visibility is chosen per table and remembered across sessions.
  • The database inspector now attaches separately (Attach DB button, optional Auto) so the network attach stays fast; row counts load on demand.
  • Receives WebSocket frames and live SSE events from apps that embed capture-sdk.
  • Opens a loopback SDK listener and sets up adb reverse on attach.
  • Streams text/event-stream bodies event-by-event instead of blocking until close.
  • SDK targets Kotlin 1.9 metadata, JVM 11/17, and compileSdk 34 for broader app support.
  • Uses Android App Inspection with in-process ART hooks (no VPN, proxy, or CA).

idea-plugin.name: Pose - Auto generate Compose Previews
idea-plugin.description:
Pose - Auto generate Compose Previews

Pose is a KSP2 processor that auto-generates Jetpack Compose @Preview functions from your @Composable code at build time - deterministic, offline, no LLM, never touches your source. Every build regenerates the previews into build/generated/ksp/.

This IntelliJ plugin adds the IDE affordances on top of the KSP processor:

  • Gutter icons next to every composable that Pose generates a preview for — both explicit @Pose-annotated composables and bulk-mode composables that Pose picks up automatically.
  • Click to jump straight to the matching <Composable>__Preview* function in the generated file - no more digging through build/generated/.
  • Popup chooser for sealed fan-outs - pick _Loading / _Success / _Error and land there directly.

Requires

  • Android Studio Ladybug (2024.2) or newer, or the equivalent IntelliJ IDEA build
  • Kotlin plugin in K1 or K2 mode - both supported
  • The Pose KSP processor added to your build dependency

See github.com/AkshayChordiya/Pose for full documentation, the sample app, and Compose snapshot-testing recipes (Paparazzi, Roborazzi, Google's screenshot plugin).

Optional but recommended. The KSP processor works standalone - the plugin just removes the need to open build/generated/ by hand.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.5.0

  • KSP side: generated previews now provide LocalInspectionMode = true, so composables that branch on it render their preview path in snapshot tests (Paparazzi / Roborazzi) the same way they already do in Studio's preview panel.
  • KSP side: new pose.previewWrapperFqName option for supplying arbitrary CompositionLocals to every generated preview.
  • Plugin binary unchanged from 0.4.3.

0.4.3

  • KMP / CMP support for gutter icons. The generated-file locator now walks nested KSP output layouts, so composables declared in commonMain (and any other Kotlin Multiplatform source set) get their gutter icon. Previously only Android's flat build/generated/ksp/<variant>/kotlin/ layout was found; KMP nests one level deeper as build/generated/ksp/<target>/<sourceSet>/kotlin/.

0.4.2

  • KSP side: bulk mode now auto-skips the theme composable identified by pose.themeFqName - no more @PoseIgnore boilerplate on your AppTheme.
  • Verified working on Compose Multiplatform / Kotlin Multiplatform projects - wire the processor into your ksp<Target>Main configuration.
  • Plugin binary unchanged from 0.4.1.

0.4.1

  • Clearer gutter tooltip - Open Pose preview: <name> instead of just Open <name>, so the click affordance matches the icon's Pose branding.
  • Internal: added unit test coverage for the line marker provider (no-file / single-match / sealed-fan-out / stale-file scenarios).

0.4.0 - first Marketplace release

  • Gutter icon next to every composable that has a Pose-generated preview
  • Click to jump straight to the corresponding __Preview* function in the generated file
  • Popup chooser for sealed fan-outs — one entry per subtype
  • Works with both explicit @Pose annotations and bulk mode (pose.generatePreviewsForAllPublicComposables)
  • K1 and K2 Kotlin plugin modes both supported
  • Icon set built around the Material Symbols undereye glyph

idea-plugin.name: Commit Spotlight
idea-plugin.description:
See exactly what a commit touched, at a glance. Ever click through a commit in the Git Log and wonder exactly which lines it actually changed? Commit Spotlight highlights it for you — directly in your editor and across the commit's row in the Git Log — in a color you choose.

Highlight any commit's changes
Select one or more commits in the Git Log and highlight the lines they added, changed, or deleted, instantly, in any open editor.

Deletions you can actually see
There's no line left to highlight when something's deleted — so Commit Spotlight marks the spot with a colored divider and an inline label. Hover it to see exactly what was removed.

Color-code your investigation
Pick from 8 colors with adjustable opacity. Highlight different commits in different colors to visually separate what each one touched, and re-color any of them afterward without starting over.

Full-row highlighting in the Git Log
Highlighted commits are tinted across their entire row in the log, not just in the editor — so the color-coding works both ways.

Filter to just what matters
Flip on "Show Only Highlighted Commits" to collapse the Git Log down to exactly the commits you're tracking.

One click to open everything a commit touched
Jump straight to every file a commit changed, without hunting through the diff.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Reverting a local edit inside a highlighted block used to leave the highlight gone for good: once an edit dropped it, the tracking behind it was torn down entirely, so a later edit putting the text back had nothing left to compare against. A dropped highlight now keeps an invisible tracker with a snapshot of its original text, so bringing the block's content back to exactly what the commit wrote — including via undo — brings the highlight back too.
  • Highlighting a commit no longer found the right lines once a *later* commit renamed the file it touched — a plain rename produces no content diff at all to remap against, and even a rename combined with further edits was keyed under the file's old, no-longer-existing name. Both a highlighted commit's changes and "Open All Files in Commit" now follow a file through a rename, whether or not it came with further edits.

idea-plugin.name: Pulse Monitor
idea-plugin.description:
PulseMonitor inspects and mocks the HTTP/HTTPS traffic of a running debuggable Android app, from inside the IDE, with no SDK, library or code change in the app.

  • Inspect — every request and response: URL, method, headers, body, status, size, duration.
  • Mock — define a response for an endpoint and have it served instantly, without restarting the app or touching the backend.

idea-plugin.name: Remote SSH for Android Studio
idea-plugin.description:
Remote SSH for Android Studio lets you open a remote project over SSH: it reuses your ~/.ssh/config, mirrors the remote directory locally, and keeps them in two-way sync via Mutagen — so indexing and code completion run locally while builds and tests run on the remote host.

as-remote-ssh

English below · 中文说明见下方

Android Studio plugin: from the File → Open Remote SSH … entry, reuse ~/.ssh/config to connect to a remote host, browse and pick a remote directory. Once selected, it creates a local mirror copy and keeps it two-way synced with the remote directory via Mutagen, then opens the local copy in Android Studio — indexing/completion run locally, build/test run on the remote.

Workflow

Launch from the File menu (or the Welcome screen) via Open Remote SSH …:

A left-right wizard then guides you through three steps — the left side is the step navigation, the right side is the current step. Use Previous / Next to move back and forth, and OK on the last step to finish:

  1. If mutagen is not detected, the plugin first asks whether to auto-download it into the private directory ~/.as-remote-ssh/bin (no sudo, does not pollute the system PATH; a system-installed version is preferred if present)
  2. Select remote host: pick a host from the named Host entries in ~/.ssh/config (supports IdentityFile / ProxyJump), pre-selecting the last-used host; click Next to connect in the background (with an inline spinner)
  3. Select remote directory: double-click to enter a subdirectory, .. to go up; the starting directory defaults to where you last browsed on that host
  4. Select local mirror directory: confirm or change the local target directory (a recommended path is pre-filled and can be freely changed)
  5. Click OK; the plugin starts Mutagen two-way sync (the progress bar can be cancelled anytime) and automatically opens the local copy in Android Studio

Sync session management

The bottom Remote Sync tool window lists all Mutagen sync sessions created by this plugin (status and conflict count auto-refresh every 4 seconds while the panel is visible), supporting:

  • Sync: run one sync immediately for the selected session (disabled while the session is syncing)
  • Pause / Resume: temporarily suspend or continue a session's sync
  • Terminate: delete the session and stop syncing (the local mirror directory is kept, only the sync with the remote is disconnected)
  • Auto-resume: when reopening a local mirror project that was previously synced, the plugin detects the corresponding session and pops up a notification, letting you resume with one click (if the session was paused) or open the session panel directly.

Memory and pre-fill

The plugin remembers your last choices and pre-fills them next time: the host, the last remote directory for each host, and the last local mirror directory for each (host + remote directory) pair.

Authentication

The plugin does not implement SSH authentication itself; instead it directly invokes the system ssh binary and reuses ~/.ssh/config, thus fully inheriting the capabilities of system ssh: Kerberos (GSSAPI), ProxyJump, ssh-agent, and all kinds of keys, behaving the same as VS Code Remote SSH. If a connection fails (e.g. an expired Kerberos ticket), verify with ssh <alias> in a terminal first.

Dependencies

  • Local: ssh (system built-in), mutagen (the plugin can auto-download it when missing, or install manually with brew install mutagen-io/mutagen/mutagen)
  • Remote: sshd + the target project; to run builds on the remote, you also need to install a JDK and the Android SDK (platform-tools/build-tools) yourself, and point sdk.dir in the remote local.properties (remote build / artifact pull-back is not yet implemented in the plugin)

as-remote-ssh（中文）

以上为英文说明，以下为中文说明。

Android Studio 插件：在 File → Open Remote SSH … 入口，复用 ~/.ssh/config 连接远程主机、浏览并选择远程目录。选定后在本地建立一份镜像副本，并用 Mutagen 与远端目录 保持双向同步，再用 Android Studio 打开本地副本——索引/补全跑在本地，构建/测试在远端。

开始使用

从 File 菜单（或 Welcome 界面）点击 Open Remote SSH … 启动：

随后在一个左右结构的向导里分三步完成，左侧为步骤导航、右侧为当前步操作，可用 Previous / Next 前后切换，最后一步 OK 完成：

  1. 若未检测到 mutagen，插件会先询问是否自动下载安装到私有目录 ~/.as-remote-ssh/bin （无需 sudo、不污染系统 PATH；系统已装则优先用系统版本）
  2. 选择远程主机：从 ~/.ssh/config 的具名 Host 列表中选主机（支持 IdentityFile / ProxyJump）， 默认预选上次使用的主机；点 Next 后台连接（原地转菊花）
  3. 选择远程目录：双击进入子目录、.. 返回，起始目录默认定位到该主机上次浏览的位置
  4. 选择本地镜像目录：确认或修改本地目标目录（默认预填推荐路径，可任意更改）
  5. 点 OK，插件启动 Mutagen 双向同步（进度条可随时取消），并自动用 Android Studio 打开本地副本

同步会话管理

底部 Remote Sync 工具窗列出本插件创建的所有 Mutagen 同步会话（面板可见时每 4 秒自动刷新状态与冲突数），支持：

  • 同步：对选中会话立即做一次同步（会话正在同步中时按钮禁用）
  • 暂停 / 恢复：临时挂起或继续某个会话的同步
  • 终止：删除会话，不再同步（本地镜像目录保留，仅断开与远端的同步）
  • 自动恢复：重新打开曾被同步过的本地镜像项目时，插件会检测到对应会话并弹出通知，可一键恢复（若会话被暂停）或直接打开会话面板。

记忆与预填

插件会记住上次的选择并在下次预填：主机、每台主机上次的远端目录、每个 （主机 + 远端目录）上次使用的本地镜像目录。

认证

插件不自行实现 SSH 认证，而是直接调用系统 ssh 二进制并复用 ~/.ssh/config， 因此完整继承系统 ssh 的能力：Kerberos(GSSAPI)、ProxyJump 跳板、ssh-agent、各类密钥， 行为与 VS Code Remote SSH 一致。若连接失败（如 Kerberos 票据过期），先在终端执行 ssh <alias> 验证即可。

依赖

  • 本地：ssh（系统自带）、mutagen（未装时插件可自动下载安装）
  • 远端：sshd + 目标工程；如需在远端跑构建，还需自行安装 JDK 与 Android SDK （platform-tools/build-tools），并在远端 local.properties 指向 sdk.dir （远端构建/产物回拉能力尚未在插件中实现）

idea-plugin.name: android-image-squeeze
idea-plugin.description:
Audits and compresses Android image assets. This is not another "Convert to WebP" — the IDE already ships one. The value here is the decision logic it lacks: which route each asset can safely take, and which ones must be left alone.

The route is chosen by the shape of the alpha channel. Assets with hard-edged alpha (only 0 or 255) get lossy RGB plus lossless alpha — a binary channel cannot band, so this needs no knowledge of the host background. Assets with gradient alpha keep almost all of their bytes in the alpha plane. When a single solid host background can be resolved, android-image-squeeze can composite onto it and drop alpha entirely; otherwise it safely falls back to lossless alpha and compresses RGB only.

Three metrics guard the result: banding detection along the gradient (per-pixel error is blind to it), dither-versus-texture classification, and per-pixel delta. Assets under assets/ and nine-patch files are excluded outright — they are data or have stretch markers, not plain images.

Usage: right-click an image in the Project view → Squeeze: Inspect This Image, or open the Image Squeeze tool window to scan the whole project and apply in bulk.

idea-plugin.name: Jugg
idea-plugin.description:
Jugg - Fast Android Incremental Build Tool

See code & resource changes in ~3 seconds—even in large Android codebases.

Jugg is an open-source Android Studio / IntelliJ IDEA plugin developed by me and open-sourced in the Tencent Music Entertainment (TME) GitHub repository. It bypasses heavy Gradle execution chains by leveraging offline bypass compilation, smart impact analysis, and hot reload technologies.

With 5 years of development and battle-tested over 800,000+ builds across multiple apps with tens of millions of DAU, Jugg turns painful minute-long build waits into instant ~3s feedback loops.

Key Features

  • 3-Second Incremental Deployment: Experience "Code Change -> Device Refresh" in seconds for daily changes, without waiting for repetitive Gradle configuration and task execution.
  • Apply Changes (JVMTI) Hot Reload: Zero-restart hot reloading via JVMTI that updates modified code and resources directly in the running process—gracefully falling back to Hot Fix (app restart without reinstallation) when code swap is inapplicable.
  • Zero Intrusion & Seamless Coexistence: No Gradle script modifications and no SDK dependencies required. Jugg Run Configurations coexist with native Android configurations, allowing one-click toggling at any time.
  • Broad Tech-Stack Compatibility: Out-of-the-box support for Kotlin, Java, Jetpack Compose, KMP (Compose Multiplatform), DataBinding, ViewBinding, Res/Assets, AndroidManifest, and native .so libraries.
  • AI Agent & CLI Integration: Built-in MCP server, CLI, and Agent Skills (jugg-android-dev-loop) to automate full "Edit -> Compile -> Deploy -> Verify" agentic development loops.

Compatibility Matrix

  • Android Studio: 2021 (Bumblebee) ~ 2026 (Rabbit)
  • IntelliJ IDEA: 2021.1.3 ~ 2025.1 Beta
  • Android Gradle Plugin (AGP): 3.4 ~ 9.1
  • Gradle: 5.4.1 ~ 9.2.1
  • Kotlin: 1.3 ~ 2.2
  • Android OS: Android 8 ~ Android 16

Links & Resources

  • GitHub Repository: https://github.com/tencentmusic/jugg
  • Documentation & Wiki: https://tencentmusic.github.io/jugg

idea-plugin.name: Flutter SDK Sync Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Keeps the Flutter SDK selection of a project in sync with the SDK provided by FVM (Flutter Version Management).

After an fvm use, the IDE is pointed at the newly selected SDK and the switch is propagated: the SDK is refreshed, pub get runs for every pub root, and the device daemon is restarted. No IDE restart needed.

The SDK is discovered from the project's .fvm directory, so FVM does not have to be on the IDE's PATH. Other version managers are not supported.

This plugin is not affiliated with or endorsed by Google LLC. It complements the official Flutter plugin.

idea-plugin.name: EazyCMP Project Wizard
idea-plugin.description:
EazyCMP Compose Multiplatform Project Wizard & Developer Tools

An all-in-one developer productivity plugin for Android Studio and IntelliJ IDEA tailored for Compose Multiplatform (CMP) mobile development targeting Android & iOS.

🚀 Key Features

  • KMP Project View & Tree Structure: Clutter-free Project View pane specifically designed for Compose Multiplatform. Flattens deep src hierarchies directly to commonMain, androidMain, and iosMain, and consolidates build scripts into a unified Gradle Scripts virtual folder.
  • Android & iOS Unified Logs Filter: High-performance log filtering tool window capturing live output from Android Studio Run configurations, targeted ADB logcat, and iOS Simulator streams. Includes connected device selector, quick presets (App Only, APIs Only, Crashes, User Prints), and collapsible JSON / API payload inspector.
  • GitToolBox-Equivalent Git Suite:
    • Inline Blame in Editor: Shows author, relative time, and commit summary directly on the active caret line.
    • Status Bar Widgets: Real-time ahead/behind commit counts, uncommitted changes counter, and interactive blame balloon with clickable issue references.
    • Remote Integrations: 1-click open or copy remote URLs and create Pull/Merge Requests for GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure Repos, AWS CodeCommit, and Gitee.
    • Gitmoji & Validation: Gitmoji insertion palette, branch issue key extraction, and Conventional Commits format validation.
    • Branch Management: Recently used branches switcher, merged branch cleanup, and push selected tags.
  • JSON to @Serializable Kotlin DTO: Instantly parse and convert raw JSON payloads into clean, idiomatic Kotlin @Serializable data classes with nested inner classes and @SerialName mappings.
  • CMP Project Wizard: 1-click scaffolding for Compose Multiplatform applications pre-configured with the EazyCMP toolkit, OnGoCart clean architecture, permissions helper, and Koin dependency injection.
  • Screen & ViewModel Generator: Right-click to generate CMP Screen, ViewModel, and Contract templates with automated Koin module bindings.
  • Live Templates: Speed up CMP development with ez-screen, ez-vm, ez-btn, ez-snackbar, and ez-permission snippets.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
What's New in 1.2.8

  • CMP View (Intelligent Project View Pane): Streamlined project navigation specifically designed for Compose Multiplatform and Kotlin Multiplatform. Organizes commonMain, platform-specific targets (Android, iOS, Desktop, Web, Ktor), included builds, and virtual Gradle Scripts folders.
  • CMP View Preferences: Full customization panel under Settings ➔ Appearance & Behavior ➔ CMP View for module sorting order, commonMain highlighting, source set grouping, and keyword matchers.
  • Compose Vector Converter: Convert Android XML vector drawables to Compose Multiplatform format directly with 1-click.
  • Regenerate Res Class: Quickly trigger Compose Multiplatform resource accessor generation on demand.
  • Compose Vector Asset Importer: Import Material and custom vector icons straight into composeResources/drawable.

idea-plugin.name: LibsHelper
idea-plugin.description:
Suggests stable Gradle library updates and writes the chosen version into the catalog or build file.

Reads libraries from gradle/libs.versions.toml and Gradle build files, then recommends the newest regular release. RC, Beta, Alpha, and Snapshot versions are listed separately and are not treated as a replacement for the regular version.

  • Checks Maven Central, Google Maven, and the Gradle Plugin Portal first
  • Uses a project fallback or private catalog only if the official catalog is unavailable
  • Update writes the stable version; shared catalog keys update the whole group
  • Inlay hints next to declared versions; analytics, sunburst, and a module map
  • Private catalog login, token, or custom header; secrets stay in the IDE Password Safe
  • English and Russian UI, switchable in Settings without restart

Source and issues: GitHub.

Читает библиотеки Gradle-проекта, подсказывает рабочую (Stable) версию и записывает её в каталог или файл сборки. RC / Beta / Alpha / Snapshot показывает отдельно.

  • Compose Multiplatform versions stay on the JetBrains line, not the AndroidX line

idea-plugin.name: Android Build Tips
idea-plugin.description:
Shows a random Android development tip or fact in a notification balloon every time a Gradle sync or build starts — like the loading-screen tips in video games. The tip disappears on its own as soon as the build finishes.

Covered wait moments:

  • Sync Project with Gradle Files
  • Make Project, Build APK, and the build phase of Run/Debug

A set of tips ships with the plugin and works entirely offline. Optionally, the plugin can also merge in an extra tips list published at a public URL.

Network use: when a remote tips URL is configured, the plugin periodically downloads that public list of tip strings (once shortly after startup, then every 12 hours) and caches it on disk. No personal data, source code, project information, or usage telemetry is ever transmitted. If no URL is configured, or the network is unavailable, the plugin makes no requests at all and uses the bundled tips.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.0

  • Initial release.
  • Shows a random tip on Gradle sync and on build/run tasks.
  • Tip auto-dismisses when the build or sync completes.
  • Optional remote tips list with on-disk caching and offline fallback.

Run, inspect and stop React Native development sessions from one IDE workbench.

  • Separate consoles for Metro, Android, iOS and release builds.

  • Metro cache reset, environment diagnostics, exit codes and actionable launch errors.

idea-plugin.name: ComposeAtlas
idea-plugin.description:
See your Jetpack Compose navigation, without drawing it yourself.

ComposeAtlas reads the navigation already in your code and turns it into a diagram — no annotations, no config files, nothing extra to maintain. It finds your screens, how they connect, and which ones have a preview, then shows it all as an interactive graph right in a tool window.

Works with your existing NavHost setup, including nested graphs split across features or modules
Understands routes defined as constants, enums, or sealed classes — not just raw strings
Matches @Preview functions to the screens they preview
Click a screen to highlight its connections; double-click to jump straight to its code
Zoom, pan, rearrange, and export the diagram as a PNG for docs or PRs

It's a heuristic based on reading your code, not a full type-checker — navigation routed dynamically at runtime (through a ViewModel or event bus, for example) may not show up as a connection. Think of it as a fast, accurate map of your app's navigation, not a formal proof of it.
idea-plugin.change-notes: • Drop the unused, mandatory org.jetbrains.android plugin dependency, which isn't bundled in plain IntelliJ IDEA (only in Android Studio) and made verification/loading fail there with a missing mandatory dependency.

idea-plugin.name: InputBridge
idea-plugin.description:
Type on an ADB-connected Android device from Android Studio, and bring its clipboard back.

  • Unicode input: send any text, including CJK characters and emoji, to the focused control on the device, optionally replacing the text it already holds.
  • Device clipboard: fetch the device clipboard on demand or follow its changes live, with bold, italic, colors, links, and other formatting shown in the editor.
  • Multiple devices: the device list follows USB attach, detach, and authorization changes, devices can be switched from the dialog, and dropped connections recover automatically.
  • Favorites and history: save titled snippets that can be searched, reordered, imported, and exported, and restore recently delivered input.

How it works. InputBridge pushes a small helper JAR to /data/local/tmp and runs it with app_process over ADB. No APK is installed and the input method is not changed. The helper is removed when you disconnect, switch devices, or close the project.

Privacy. Text, clipboard content, favorites, and history stay on your computer and device. InputBridge collects no telemetry and sends nothing over the network.

Open it from Tools | InputBridge or the main toolbar. Requires Android 8.0 or newer with USB debugging enabled.
idea-plugin.change-notes: • Exporting favorites no longer fails with a missing-method error on Android Studio 2024.3.

idea-plugin.name: More Usage Filters
idea-plugin.description:
Two extra filter toggles for the Find Usages tool window and the Show Usages popup (Cmd+B / Ctrl+B), next to the built-in Show Import Statements and Show Generated Code ones.

Show Preview Usages: turn it off to hide every usage located inside a Jetpack Compose preview, that is a declaration annotated with @Preview, @PreviewScreenSizes or any custom multipreview annotation. Handy on a Composable that is, of course, always used by its own preview.

Show Comment Usages: turn it off to hide every usage located inside a comment, the [Link] references of a KDoc first and foremost.

Supports both the K1 and the K2 Kotlin modes, and needs no configuration.

idea-plugin.name: MaterialSymbolIcon
idea-plugin.description:
MaterialSymbolIcon

A unified developer tool for Android Studio and IntelliJ IDEA to download, convert, and manage icons (Google Material Symbols, Apple SF Symbols, and SVG images) as Jetpack Compose ImageVector and Android Vector Drawable XMLs.

Features

  • Google Material Symbols: Direct URL download, instant vector conversion, live preview, and intelligent auto-naming.
  • Apple SF Symbols: Paste raw SVG copied from Apple's SF Symbols macOS app with automated stripping of proprietary Apple namespaces (xmlns:sfs, sfs:) and guide notes.
  • Custom SVG Images: Browse or drag-and-drop local .svg files with real-time vector preview, providing a modern alternative to native Vector Asset Studio.
  • Dual Format Generation: One-click generation for Jetpack Compose ImageVector Kotlin source code, Android Vector Drawable XML, or both simultaneously.
  • Centralized Registry (AppIcons.kt): Automatically appends imported icons to your project's AppIcons.kt registry using IntelliJ Kotlin PSI.
  • Smart Path Auto-Detection: Automatically discovers your project's drawable folders, Compose theme packages, and icon registry files.

How It Works

1. Google Material Symbols

  1. Go to Google Fonts Icons and select your desired icon.
  2. In the right-hand details drawer, choose Android and select Compose.
  3. Copy the URL/code and paste it into the Symbol URL field in the plugin.
  4. The plugin automatically detects the icon name and generates live previews.
  5. Click Generate ImageVector, Generate Drawable, or Generate Both.

2. Apple SF Symbols

  1. Open Apple's SF Symbols application on macOS.
  2. Right-click on any icon and select Copy As > Copy SVG (or press Cmd + C).
  3. Paste the SVG snippet into the plugin's SF Symbols tab.
  4. The plugin automatically cleans Apple-specific SVG attributes and normalizes the viewBox.
  5. Enter your preferred icon name and click your export target.

3. Local SVG Images

  1. Open the SVG Image tab.
  2. Drag and drop any .svg file into the drop zone, or browse to select a file from your disk.
  3. The plugin parses the SVG, validates the vector paths, and displays an instant preview.
  4. Click Generate ImageVector, Generate Drawable, or Generate Both.

4. Central Registry Integration

When Auto-append to AppIcons.kt is enabled, every imported icon is automatically declared in your central registry file:

// Central registry: AppIcons.kt
object AppIcons {
    val Home: ImageVector
        get() = ...
}

You can immediately reference it anywhere in your Compose UI:

Icon(
    imageVector = AppIcons.Home,
    contentDescription = "Home"
)

idea-plugin.name: Compose Recomposition Auditor
idea-plugin.description:
Detects Jetpack Compose recomposition issues directly in the editor — before you ever need to run a profiler. The plugin reproduces (a conservative subset of) the Compose compiler's own stability inference to catch problems as you type.

Free

  • Detection of mutable collection interfaces (List, Map, Set) passed as @Composable parameters
  • Detection of classes with var properties passed as @Composable parameters, without @Stable/@Immutable
  • Detection of types defined outside the current module whose stability cannot be determined
  • Detection of lambdas inside a @Composable function that capture a local var without remember
  • Convert to Immutable* quick-fix — rewrites List<T> / Map<K,V> / Set<T> to their kotlinx.collections.immutable equivalents, adding both the import and the Gradle dependency automatically
  • Annotate class with @Stable quick-fix — adds the @Stable annotation to the offending class declaration
  • False-positive reduction: skips @Preview-annotated composables, recognizes a whitelist of well-known stable Compose/coroutines types (Modifier, State, StateFlow, etc.)

Premium (30-day free trial included)

  • Exportable stability reports (HTML/JSON) covering your whole project — share findings with your team or tech lead

All free features remain free forever. Premium features can be evaluated for 30 days before requiring a license.

More premium features are planned, including a real-time recomposition dashboard and CI integration. Feedback and feature requests are welcome via the GitHub repository.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • UnstableLambdaCaptureInspection: flags lambdas inside @Composable functions that capture a local var without remember, since Compose can't track changes to a plain captured variable
  • Both inspections now skip @Preview-annotated composables (and multipreview variants like @PreviewScreenSizes), since preview functions commonly use unoptimized mock data on purpose
  • Integration tests for both inspections using BasePlatformTestCase, covering the stability rules, the @Preview exclusion, and the remember-capture logic end-to-end
  • False-positive reduction: a small whitelist of known-stable external Compose/coroutines types (Modifier, State, MutableState, StateFlow, SharedFlow, etc.) that are treated as stable even without a resolvable @Stable/@Immutable annotation

Known limitations

  • UnstableLambdaCaptureInspection only covers local vars declared inside the composable function itself — captures of class properties, top-level vars, or var function parameters are not yet detected
  • Only by remember { ... } is recognized as a safe delegate for local vars. Recognizing rememberUpdatedState here is a non-goal: it returns a read-only State<T> and cannot delegate a var, so it doesn't apply to this inspection by construction
  • One warning is reported per captured variable name per lambda, even if referenced multiple times inside it

idea-plugin.name: PureDown
idea-plugin.description:
PureDown - Modern Markdown & Obsidian-Grade Knowledge Workspace for IntelliJ IDEA & Android Studio

PureDown is a high-performance Markdown editing, rendering, and knowledge management plugin designed for modern technical writing and documentation:

  • Seamless In-Place Split Editor: High-performance bidirectional synchronized scrolling with 3 layout modes (Split Mode, Editor Only, Preview Only). Customizable default view mode in Settings.
  • Floating Formatting Toolbar: Format selections instantly (Bold, Italic, Strikethrough, Code, Quote, Links, Task lists).
  • Full-Featured CJK Table Formatter: In-place Markdown table alignment with CJK fullwidth support, automatic column padding, and quick template insertion.
  • Live Document Statistics Bar: Status bar showing cursor position (Ln, Col), character count, word count, line count, and estimated reading time.
  • Smart Task Lists & Ordered Lists: One-click interactive checkbox toggle (- [ ] ↔ - [x]) in both preview and editor, plus auto-renumbering of sequential lists.
  • Obsidian Vault & Knowledge Base Power:
    • [[WikiLinks]] resolution and auto-completion with Ctrl/Cmd+Click navigation.
    • Obsidian Callouts ([!NOTE], [!TIP], [!WARNING], [!DANGER], [!SUCCESS], etc.) rendered with styled colored badges and icons.
    • Interactive 2D Knowledge Vault Graph showing note connection nodes, physics layout, and search.
  • Rich Preview & Technical Writing Extensions: YAML Front Matter metadata cards, in-document [TOC] outline, offline KaTeX math formulas, Mermaid architecture diagrams, code copy buttons, and image click lightbox zoom.
  • Full Chinese & English Localization (i18n): UI, settings, actions, and preview components adapt to IDE language or can be manually selected.
  • Inspections & Quick Fixes: PSI inspections for skipped heading hierarchy, unaligned tables, and empty links.
  • Export & Clipboard: One-click Copy as Rendered HTML for publishing (WeChat, Zhihu, Notion) and Standalone HTML file export.

idea-plugin.name: CleanBloc Architect
idea-plugin.description:
CleanBloc Architect is a productivity plugin designed for Flutter and mobile developers to eliminate repetitive boilerplate setup. With a single right-click, it automates the creation of a fully structured feature directory adhering to Clean Architecture principles.

Key Features:
  • Complete Folder Scaffolding: Automatically generates data (datasources, models, repositories), domain (entities, repositories, usecases), and presentation (bloc, pages, widgets) layers.

idea-plugin.name: Lark Connector
idea-plugin.description:
Lark Connector connects your Lark Base or Feishu Bitable task boards directly inside Android Studio and IntelliJ IDEA with live REST API synchronization.

Key Features

  • Live Lark Bitable API Sync: Real-time dynamic fetch of tables, fields, and records directly from Lark Base Open APIs.
  • Dynamic Table Schema & Columns: Automatically renders all actual columns (e.g., OKRs, Task Leaders, Start/End Dates, Checkboxes) as separate headers.
  • Schema-Aware Add Record Dialog: Create live records on Lark Base with option dropdowns, person selectors, date parsing, and numeric validation.
  • Auto-Refresh Timer: Configurable automatic background refresh interval (Off, 1 Min, 5 Min, 10 Min).
  • Multi-Base Support: Connect and manage multiple Lark Base sheets seamlessly from a single unified dropdown.
  • Diagnostics & Error Logging: Detailed log inspector and one-click copy tool for API troubleshooting.

Setup & Usage Guide

  1. Create an internal App in Lark Developer Console (open.larksuite.com/app).
  2. In Permissions & Scopes, grant the bitable:app and bitable:app:readonly permission.
  3. Important: Click Create Version and publish your app so permission scopes take effect!
  4. Copy your Tenant Access Token (t-...) from Credentials & Test Notes or API Explorer.
  5. Open Android Studio, launch Lark Connector tool window, paste your Lark Base URL and Tenant Access Token.

idea-plugin.name: JSON to ArkTS Model

idea-plugin.name: Candle Theme
idea-plugin.description:
Candle is a minimal dark theme built on warm whites.

Instead of a rainbow of syntax colors, Candle uses a single family of warm, off-white shades on a near-black background. Brightness, warmth and type style carry the meaning:

  • Keywords are bold, in the warmest shade
  • Function declarations are bold; calls share their color
  • Comments and top-level members are italic
  • Mutable vars are underlined
  • Errors are the only true color: a muted, dusty red

Tuned for Kotlin and Android Studio, and works across all JetBrains IDEs. Comes in two layouts: Candle (classic) and Candle Islands.
idea-plugin.change-notes: First release. Includes two layouts: Candle (classic) and Candle Islands.

idea-plugin.name: Local Push Mock
idea-plugin.description:
Test Android push notifications from Android Studio — no backend, no Firebase credentials.

Local Push Mock lets you fire a real Android notification on any device or emulator straight from the IDE. Fill in a form, click Send notification, and it shows up as if your production push had just arrived.

Before you start, read the User Guide on GitLab: the plugin needs a small debug-only library added to your app.

Use it to

  • Check how your notifications look: title, body, channel, importance and icon.
  • Test deep links and the data payload your app receives when the notification is tapped.
  • Reproduce push scenarios without waiting for the backend or touching the Firebase console.
  • Run your own production notification code through an optional hook.

How it works

The plugin sends the notification to your app over adb. A tiny receiver that exists only in your debug build shows it using the native Android APIs, mimicking a real FCM push. Nothing ships to production, and other apps cannot trigger it.

Requirements

  • Android Studio Ladybug (2024.2) or later
  • An Android device or emulator (Android 5.0+)
  • The localpush-debug library in your app's debug build — setup steps on GitLab
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 1.0.0 — First release.

idea-plugin.name: ADB Toolbox
idea-plugin.description:
Control your Android device from Android Studio or IntelliJ IDEA without opening a terminal. ADB Toolbox puts the adb commands you run every day into one tool window.

  • Device – the app in front with restart, kill and reset permissions; screenshots (also full-page, of scrolling screens), screen recording and scrcpy mirroring; device facts; font scale and display density; language & region overrides (incl. pseudo-locales) and emulator GPS location; quick toggles for dark theme, animations, show touches, TalkBack and common developer options.
  • Layout Inspector – any app's screen and view hierarchy in an editor tab: sizes and distances in dp, redlines, 8 dp grid, color picker, Figma overlay, and an accessibility audit (TalkBack order, unlabeled controls, small touch targets).
  • Apps – searchable package list with launcher icons and pins; restart, force-stop, launch, clear data, uninstall; app details with shared preferences and SQLite databases, runtime permissions and deep links.
  • Network – device-wide HTTP proxy and emulator network throttling.
  • Logcat – a fast, filterable stream with levels, search, package filter, pause and wrap.
  • AI agents – an optional local MCP server so Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor or Gemini CLI can use the selected device; destructive actions always ask first.
  • Wi-Fi pairing, multiple devices, light and dark themes, a one-click diagnostics bundle for bug reports.

idea-plugin.name: NikoTools
idea-plugin.description:
NikoTools runs custom scripts with parameter forms and a native IDE Run console.

NikoTools — 自定义脚本工具

将常用命令保存为脚本，在 IDE 中填写参数并执行，在原生 Run 控制台查看输出。 适用于项目工具、文件处理和 Android 调试。插件使用 Kotlin 与官方 Kotlin UI DSL。

主要功能

  • 支持 PowerShell、Python、Bash、Windows BAT，以及直接启动可执行程序的 process 类型。
  • 自动从模板生成参数表单，显式支持文本、多行、整数、数字、布尔、下拉、单选按钮组、文件、目录和密码十种类型，兼容旧写法。
  • 文件和目录选择器优先打开输入路径或最近存在的父目录，无可用路径时从当前 IDE 窗口的项目根目录打开；工作目录默认使用当前项目根目录。
  • 支持剪贴板分享与导入、脚本目录批量迁移、终端选区创建脚本（需可选 Terminal 插件）。
  • 原生 Run 控制台显示输出、错误和退出码，不自动打印脚本正文，提供绿色运行图标、停止及超时控制。
  • 自动尝试读取 IDE 所选 Android 设备并提供 ANDROID_SERIAL；普通脚本无需连接 Android 设备。

快速开始

  1. 打开 Tools → NikoTools，点击“新建脚本”，填写名称并选择执行类型。
  2. 编写脚本正文，例如 Python 的 import sys; print('Hello, ' + sys.argv[1])。
  3. 展开“执行配置”，将参数数组 JSON 设为 ["${姓名:World}"]，保存脚本。
  4. 双击脚本，填写参数并执行，在 Run 窗口查看结果。

参数语法：${名称}、${名称:默认值}、 ${模式@choice:开启=1|关闭=0}、${文件@file}、${目录@dir}。 可使用 var file = ${输入文件@file} 声明并通过 ${file} 引用。 顶部“帮助”与编辑器中的“脚本模板与参数语法”提供全部参数类型演示及替换预览；“复制 SKILL”可复制用于 AI 编写参数脚本的技能。单选按钮组横向排列，密码框支持显示/隐藏和保存默认值。替换是字面替换，不自动转义；任意文本建议通过参数数组传递。

环境与使用说明

最低 IntelliJ Platform 构建号为 242（IDEA 2024.2 系列），运行时要求 Java 21。 面向 Android Studio、IntelliJ IDEA、PyCharm 等兼容平台的 IDE。 插件不附带解释器、adb 或 scrcpy，请自行安装实际使用的工具，在 Settings → NikoTools 配置路径，或使用 IDE 继承的 PATH。

工作目录、解释器、工具依赖、输出编码、超时、参数数组和环境变量均可按需配置。 环境变量 JSON 与参数元数据通常保持默认即可。process 正文只填可执行文件名或路径，参数填写到 JSON 数组；不解析 Shell 管道。

Android 与 Terminal 均为可选依赖。取得唯一在线的 IDE 所选设备时自动注入序列号； 没有可用设备时普通脚本仍可启动。显式 android_device 依赖或必填设备参数才强制要求设备。 脚本库和工具路径为 IDE 用户级配置，跨项目共享；运行中不支持交互式标准输入。

完整中英文 Wiki 位于源码仓库的 docs/wiki 目录。 右键脚本可编辑、分享或删除，选中后按 Delete 可弹出删除确认；列表支持按使用频率、添加顺序或名称排序。顶部“批量操作”可备份和迁移脚本目录。 分享会移除默认值与解释器路径，但保留脚本中的其他字面内容；目录导出保留默认值。

NikoTools — Custom Script Tools

Save recurring commands, collect inputs in the IDE, and inspect results in the native Run console. Useful for project utilities, file processing, and Android debugging. Built with Kotlin and the official Kotlin UI DSL.

Features

  • Run PowerShell, Python, Bash, Windows batch scripts, or launch an executable directly with process.
  • Generate forms from ten explicit template types: text, multiline, integers, numbers, booleans, dropdowns, radio buttons, files, directories, and secrets, while retaining legacy syntax.
  • File and directory browsing prefers the input path or its nearest existing parent, falling back to the current IDE window's project root. The default working directory is also the current project root.
  • Share and import clipboard JSON, migrate script directories, and create scripts from terminal selections with the optional Terminal plugin.
  • View output, errors, and exit codes without startup script text in Run tabs, with a standard green Run icon, stop, and timeout controls.
  • Automatically read the IDE-selected Android device when available and supply ANDROID_SERIAL. Ordinary scripts do not require an Android device.

Quick start

  1. Open Tools → NikoTools. Click 新建脚本 (New script), enter a name, and select an execution type.
  2. Enter a body, for example Python: import sys; print('Hello, ' + sys.argv[1]).
  3. Expand 执行配置 (Execution configuration), set Arguments JSON to ["${name:World}"], and save.
  4. Double-click the script, fill in the form, and inspect results in Run.

Templates include ${name}, ${name:default}, ${mode@choice:On=1|Off=0}, ${input@file}, and ${output@dir}. Declare var file = ${InputFile@file} and reference ${file} elsewhere. Toolbar Help and the editor’s template help include an all-parameter demonstration and substitution previews. Copy SKILL copies instructions for AI-assisted script authoring. Radio buttons are horizontal; secret inputs support visibility toggles and saved defaults. Substitution is literal without escaping; prefer Arguments JSON for arbitrary text.

Requirements and usage

Requires IntelliJ Platform build 242 or later (IDEA 2024.2 series) and a Java 21 runtime. Targets Android Studio, IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, and other compatible IntelliJ Platform IDEs. Interpreters, adb, and scrcpy are not bundled. Install the tools you use and configure executable paths in Settings → NikoTools, or use the IDE's inherited PATH.

Working directory, interpreter, required tools, output encoding, timeout, arguments, and environment overrides are optional configuration. Environment JSON and parameter metadata can usually retain their defaults. A process body is one executable name or path; use the argument array for its arguments. Shell pipelines are not interpreted.

Android and Terminal integrations are optional. A single online IDE-selected device supplies an automatic serial when available; ordinary scripts still launch without a usable device. Only an explicit android_device requirement or required device parameter enforces device selection. Scripts and tool paths are shared across projects within the IDE configuration. Interactive process stdin is unsupported.

The full Chinese and English Wiki is in the source repository's docs/wiki directory. Right-click scripts to edit, share, or delete; press Delete on a selected script for deletion confirmation. Sort the list by usage frequency, addition order, or name. Use 批量操作 (Batch operations) for directory backup and migration. Sharing removes defaults and interpreter overrides but preserves other literal content; directory exports preserve defaults. The current UI labels are Chinese; the English Wiki includes translations.

MIT License. Copyright (c) 2026 popkter. Source code / 源码 · License / 许可证.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changed

  • Add toolbar Help and Copy SKILL actions for script parameter authoring; remove three older full-script examples from template help.
  • Hide the process startup command line in Run consoles while retaining script output and errors.
  • Use the IDE's standard green Run icon for the Run tab's rerun action.
  • Remove required asterisks from parameter labels, arrange radio options horizontally, and allow saving secret defaults with a password visibility icon.
  • Support ten explicit parameter types with legacy syntax compatibility; preserve typed inputs and choice definitions when sharing scripts.
  • Include an all-parameter Bash demonstration with defaults and repeated var references, plus a copyable skill for AI script authoring.
  • Walk up missing file and directory parameter paths to open the nearest accessible parent directory.

An interactive, enterprise-grade project and module scaffolding platform for Android Studio and IntelliJ IDEA.

Scaffolds production-ready, highly decoupled Android architectures in seconds with zero boilerplate.

Key Features:

  • Production Blueprints: Instant archetypes for Startup/Consumer apps, Fintech/Enterprise, and Spike prototypes.
  • Day-2 Feature Scaffolder: Right-click New ➔ Awesome Feature Module... to instantly generate feature slices with Compose UI & ViewModel.
  • Day-2 Core Scaffolder: Right-click New ➔ Awesome Core Module... to add pure JVM, Android, or Compose libraries.
  • Offline-First Room Persistence: Pre-configured :core:database with Room, KSP, reactive Flow DAOs, and Entity models.
  • Shared Test Fixtures: :core:testing with MainDispatcherRule and fake repositories.
  • Design System Ecosystem: :core:designsystem with 4dp/8dp spacing tokens, corner radius, type scale, icons, and DataStore theme persistence.
  • Gradle Convention Plugins: Modern build-logic setup sharing compiler flags, SDK bounds, and packaging rules.
  • Project Doctor & Architecture Guard: Integrated health diagnostics, Clean Architecture boundary auditing, and Git pre-commit hook enforcement.
