idea-plugin.name: CSS Variables Assistant
idea-plugin.description:
The fastest way to work with CSS custom properties & design tokens in JetBrains IDEs

CSS Variables Assistant turns var(--my-token) into a first-class citizen in WebStorm, IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate, PhpStorm, PyCharm Professional, GoLand and RubyMine. Get instant autocomplete, rich inline documentation with colour swatches and pixel equivalents, and full resolution of design-token @import, @use, and @forward chains across your project and node_modules.

Built for modern CSS workflows: Tailwind layers, shadcn/ui tokens, Radix colours, Material tokens, CSS-in-JS bridge files, design-system packages, multi-theme setups (light / dark / high-contrast via media queries), SCSS & LESS & SASS.

Why developers install it

  • Smart autocomplete inside var(--…) – your entire token catalog surfaces the moment you open a var() call. Works in CSS, SCSS, SASS and LESS files.
  • Direct SCSS/Sass/LESS variable completion – complete $brand-primary in SCSS/Sass and @brand-primary in LESS outside var(...), with the same resolved-value preview, colour icons and quick documentation used for CSS custom properties.
  • Instant in-place documentation – hover any --token for a rich popup showing the resolved value, colour swatch, HSB / hex, pixel equivalent for rem / em / % / vh / vw, WCAG AA / AAA contrast ratio, and the full @import resolution chain.
  • Follows stylesheet module chains automatically – resolves legacy @import plus modern Sass @use / @forward, including design-token packages inside node_modules, with configurable depth and scope controls.
  • Understands media-query context – tokens redefined under @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark), min-width breakpoints or any other context are shown side-by-side so you can compare values at a glance.
  • Three-option sort order (new in 1.8.0) – sort completions by value ascending, by value descending, or alphabetically. Applies consistently whether the popup opens at var(--|) or mid-prefix.
  • JSDoc-style comments – parse @name, @description, @example from block comments above your tokens and render them in the popup.
  • Derived-variable marker – alias / recursive completions get a ↗ badge so you know at a glance which values were resolved through references.
  • Debug import chain – a dedicated context-menu action prints the full import resolution tree for any CSS file. Answers "where does this token actually come from?" in one click.
  • Customizable documentation columns – show or hide Context, Color Swatch, Value, Type, Source, Pixel Equivalent, Hex, WCAG Contrast independently.
  • Fast in large projects – file-local indexing, document-aware snapshots, and one local declaration scan per request reduce repeated work in large token catalogs.

Keywords

CSS variables, CSS custom properties, design tokens, var(--token), var() autocomplete, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, Radix UI, Radix Themes, Material Design tokens, MUI, Open Props, CSS cascade, :root, calc(), nested CSS variables, recursive variable resolution, dark mode tokens, theme variables, WebStorm CSS plugin, IntelliJ IDEA CSS autocomplete, JetBrains plugin design tokens, SCSS variables, Sass variables, LESS variables, @import resolution, Sass @use, Sass @forward, JSDoc CSS, WCAG contrast checker, px equivalent, rem to px converter, hex to HSL, colour swatch, CSS-in-JS bridge.

New in 1.9.6

  • Fixes a completion crash when a token catalog mixes sizes, colors and numbers (#36). Thanks to @prikkprikkprikk for reporting it.
  • Preserves ascending/descending value sorting for size and number families, natural numeric suffixes, and exact-name priority. Full typed-prefix matches stay ahead of truncated matches.
  • Completion and insertion are verified across CSS, SCSS, Sass and LESS. No settings change or index rebuild is required when upgrading from 1.9.5.

Previously in 1.9.5

  • Native color documentation remains available inside CSS custom-property declarations.
  • Custom-property completion is restricted to the first argument of var(). Fallback values no longer receive invalid bare variable names; nested var() calls and preprocessor fallback variables remain supported.
  • Canceling import debugging no longer reports an IDE error.
  • No settings change or index rebuild is required when upgrading from 1.9.4.

New in 1.9.4

  • Imported values refresh after saved and unsaved edits and point to the actual declaration file.
  • Safer CSS/SCSS/Sass/LESS parsing preserves URLs, quoted values, Unicode names and theme contexts.
  • Alias cycles terminate safely; namespace, scope, declaration-order and import-fallback fixes improve token resolution.
  • Completion and documentation respect code-token boundaries, leaving comments, strings and at-rules to the IDE.
  • HSL alpha, hue normalization and signed CSS lengths are corrected. Completion avoids repeated local-file scans.
  • The variable index rebuilds once after upgrade; no settings change is needed.

✨ New in 1.9.3

Urgent bug-fix release for issue #35, originally reported by @markwoon in JetBrains YouTrack IJPL-252456. CSS Variables Assistant no longer interferes with Quick Documentation for Java or other non-stylesheet code.

  • Java Quick Documentation restored: annotations such as @Nullable and @Deprecated, plus Javadoc tags such as @param and @return, are left to the IDE's own documentation providers instead of being misread as LESS variables.
  • Strict stylesheet boundary: the documentation extractor now runs only for PSI whose language implements the IntelliJ Platform's CSS-language contract. CSS, SCSS, Sass, LESS, PostCSS, and injected CSS remain supported without relying on hardcoded filename extensions.
  • Core features preserved: CSS custom-property documentation, direct Sass/SCSS/LESS variable documentation, completion, import resolution, indexing, theme rows, colour previews, and alias chains are unchanged.
  • Regression verified: real Java PSI tests cover both annotation placements and Javadoc-only tags; the complete 303-test suite and the reported IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2.1 build pass.

Previously in 1.9.2

Bug-fix release closing issue #28 and issue #29, both reported with follow-up PRs (#30, #31) by @caseyjhol. Modern Sass module imports are now indexed, and root + theme selector-list hover contexts are canonicalised.

  • Sass module imports (@use / @forward) are indexed: tokens declared in @used partials feed hover, docs, and completion. Package-root imports such as @use "@vendor/design" as *, namespaced aliases (@use "..." as ns), and _index.scss partial resolution are all supported.
  • CSS-entrypoint fallback for mixin-only Sass roots: when a package's Sass entrypoint contains no concrete --* declarations (common in "include core() once" mixin patterns), the resolver consults package.json's exports / sass / style / css fields and indexes the CSS distribution alongside the Sass API. Compiled custom properties become discoverable without dropping imported Sass variables.
  • Canonical Default/<Theme> hover labels: :root, [data-theme="light"] { --foo: blue } collapses to a single Default/Light row instead of showing the raw selector list. Attribute-equals quoting variants ([data-theme=light] vs [data-theme="light"]) are normalised to one canonical shape, so quoting-only variants no longer show up as duplicate rows.
  • Arbitrary theme names are preserved: the theme in Default/<Theme> is derived from the actual selector, not hardcoded to Light. [data-theme="nova-light"] becomes Default/Nova Light, .theme-sepia becomes Default/Theme sepia, and so on.
  • Baseline is called Default: plain :root { --foo: … } renders as Default even when the value is a colour. Previously colour-valued baselines were labelled Light mode, misrepresenting them as an explicit Light colour-scheme theme.

Previously in 1.9.1

Bug-fix release closing issue #26, reported with a PR by @caseyjhol. Sass and LESS variables that are pure aliases to CSS custom properties now keep the full CSS Variables Assistant hover experience.

  • Alias-aware hover for preprocessor variables: hovering $foo or @foo when it is defined as var(--foo) now shows the same theme rows, swatches, hex values, source column, and contrast data as hovering the underlying var(--foo).
  • Fallback aliases are covered: direct aliases like var(--foo, #fff) resolve through the CSS custom property while preserving the fallback-safe syntax path.
  • Quick-info hints show the chain: hints now make the relationship explicit, for example $token → var(--token) → #112233.
  • Compound expressions stay honest: values like 1px solid var(--foo) remain on the literal preprocessor-value path instead of being misrepresented as a single themed CSS variable.

Previously in 1.9.0

Feature release inspired by Discussion #24 from @LorincJuraj. CSS Variables Assistant now supports direct SCSS/Sass $... and LESS @... variables in completion and quick documentation, not only CSS custom properties inside var(...).

  • Direct preprocessor variable completion: type $brand in SCSS/Sass or @brand in LESS to get project and imported design-system variables with resolved values, colour swatches and derived-value markers. Declaration left-hand sides and plain CSS files are guarded so normal editing stays clean.
  • Quick documentation for $... and @... references: hover/direct documentation now renders the existing rich table for preprocessor variables, including resolved value, value type, pixel/colour columns and alias resolution chain.
  • Imported design-system support: preprocessor variables from project imports and explicitly imported node_modules packages are indexed through the importing stylesheet. Sass partials such as _tokens.scss / _tokens.sass, nested imports, and CSS custom properties that resolve through imported SCSS/Sass/LESS aliases are covered.
  • Index rebuild: preprocessor index keys now preserve their syntax ($token vs @token) so SCSS/Sass and LESS variables with the same bare name no longer collide.

Previously in 1.8.6

Bug-fix release closing issue #22 reported by @LordMaddhi. 8-digit hex colors with alpha — the modern CSS Color Level 4 #RRGGBBAA syntax — are now handled correctly.

  • 8-digit hex colors with alpha: a value like --accent: #7F80FF1A no longer renders as a truncated #80FF1A in the hover popup's Hex column. Two compounding bugs were fixed: the parser was reading alpha as the first byte (Java #AARRGGBB packed-int order) instead of the last byte per the CSS spec, and the formatter was unconditionally dropping alpha. The canonical hex output now preserves alpha when present, and 4-digit #RGBA shorthand is recognised. Color swatches use rgba() so semi-transparent colors preview accurately.
  • Fully-opaque colors still produce 6-digit hex (#1E90FF), so existing snapshots and the WebAIM contrast-checker URL are unaffected.
  • Regression coverage in ColorParserTest: primary #7F80FF1A round-trip, 4-digit shorthand, full-opacity collapse-to-6-digit, fully-transparent round-trip, and explicit channel-position assertions verifying alpha is read from the LAST byte.

Previously in 1.8.5

Bug-fix release closing issue #21 reported by @kolkinn. Calculated tokens that reference multi-valued nested variables — the Radix Themes pattern --space-2: calc(8px * var(--scaling)) — are now displayed correctly in the hover popup.

  • Calc + ambiguous nested var fix: hovering var(--space-2) in a Radix Themes project no longer shows bare 0.9 (type: number). When the inner variable has multiple non-uniform values across themed selectors and no :root anchor, the resolver now leaves the var(--scaling) reference intact so the popup displays calc(8px * var(--scaling)) verbatim. Deterministic single-default substitutions are unchanged.
  • Calc wrapper preservation: the recursive substitution path also stopped silently dropping surrounding text. --gap: calc(var(--unit) * 2) with --unit: 4px now correctly resolves to calc(4px * 2) rather than just 4px.
  • Four regression tests in DocHelpersResolveVarValueTest + a copy-paste reproducer fixture under samples/issue-21/ for manual side-loaded verification.

Previously in 1.8.4

Closed issue #20 reported by @Blinks44.

  • Exact-match ranking: typing var(--sidebar-accent-foreground) in full no longer left --sidebar selected at the top of the popup. The exact match is now always promoted, so pressing Enter/Tab doesn't overwrite what you already typed.

Previously in 1.8.3

Follow-up to 1.8.1 issue #19 — polish for design systems with many themes.

  • Readable theme labels (new setting, default on): [data-theme="catppuccin"] now renders as "Catppuccin", [data-theme="high-contrast"] as "High contrast", .dark as "Dark" — same applies to any single attribute-equals or single-class selector. Full raw selector available on hover. Turn off for paste-back-to-CSS fidelity.
  • Merge duplicate-value rows (new setting, default on): when several themes (catppuccin, sepia, matcha, …) resolve the same token to the same value, they're collapsed into one row whose Context column lists every contributing theme. Turn off to see one row per selector.
  • Compound selectors, pseudo-classes, and IDs stay verbatim — prettifying them would misrepresent CSS semantics.

Previously in 1.8.2

Quality-of-life polish on the hover popup. Long Source cells like variables.css:230 used to wrap onto two lines because IntelliJ's documentation popup clamps its max width; 1.8.2 both nudges the popup wider and adds a compact-source-column preference so you can pick the look you prefer.

  • Compact Source column (on by default): renders just :220 in the cell; the full variables.css:220 shows on hover. Toggle under Settings → Tools → CSS Variables Assistant → Documentation Popup Columns.
  • Wider popup by default: the value table now asks the popup for at least ~700 px, so multi-column rows (Context, Value, Type, Source, Hex, WCAG) no longer wrap in the common case.
  • Zero behaviour change to completion, indexing, or the v1.8.1 theming-selector rows.

Previously in 1.8.1

Theming-focused follow-up. Closes issue #19 reported by @LordMaddhi and ships a related cascade-visibility improvement.

  • Attribute and class theme selectors become their own rows: [data-theme="dark"], .dark, .theme-high-contrast, :hover, [dir="rtl"] and similar non-root selectors are now indexed as distinct contexts in the hover popup instead of collapsing into default. Perfect for shadcn/ui, Radix, Tailwind's .dark mode, and hand-rolled theme systems.
  • Nested @media + selector blocks combine labels: @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { .hc { ... } } shows up as (prefers-color-scheme: dark) .hc.
  • Source column now shows file.css:line for every declaration, so when --bg is redefined across multiple theme files you can see exactly which file and line each value comes from.
  • Cascade-ambiguity disclaimer under multi-row value tables makes it explicit that runtime behaviour still depends on stylesheet load order and specificity.
  • Index rebuilds once on first launch — the packed index record gained a 4th field (source line).

Previously in 1.8.0

Closed issue #18 and ~15 related completion-popup regressions that only surfaced during real IDE use. Highlights:

  • Completion popup no longer hides --error behind --error-foreground, no longer shows a JSDoc comment where the resolved value should be, and no longer gets sticky while you type.
  • New Alphabetical sort option and fixed inconsistency where the ASC / DESC preference was only honoured in some popup flows.
  • Two new Display Options settings let you hide or clamp the description next to each completion item.
  • Minified CSS files that start with a copyright comment are now indexed correctly (thanks to community contributor @pierreoa).

Pairs well with

PxPeek — CSS Pixel Hints: sibling plugin by the same author that shows inline pixel-equivalent hints next to every rem, em, vh, % and modern viewport unit in your editor. Zero-config, faster than flipping to DevTools.

Feedback & issues

Found a bug? Please open it at github.com/Stianlars1/css-vars-assistant/issues — reported bugs are usually fixed within a day. Every bit of feedback helps shape the plugin.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.9.6 – 2026-09-14

  • Fixes the "Comparison method violates its general contract!" completion error caused by mixed size, color and number tokens (#36). Thank you to @prikkprikkprikk for the report.
  • Keeps semantic size and number families sorted by value, with exact-name and full-prefix matches prioritized consistently.
  • Adds regression coverage for mixed catalogs and completion/insertion in CSS, SCSS, Sass and LESS.
  • No settings change or index rebuild is required when upgrading from 1.9.5.

1.9.5 – 2026-09-07

  • Native color documentation remains available inside CSS custom-property declarations.
  • Custom-property completion is restricted to the first argument of var(). Fallback values no longer receive invalid bare variable names; nested var() calls and preprocessor fallback variables remain supported.
  • Canceling import debugging no longer reports an IDE error.
  • No settings change or index rebuild is required when upgrading from 1.9.4.

1.9.4 – 2026-09-07

  • Imported values refresh after saved and unsaved edits and point to the actual declaration file.
  • Safer CSS/SCSS/Sass/LESS parsing preserves URLs, quoted values, Unicode names and theme contexts.
  • Alias cycles terminate safely; namespace, scope, declaration-order and import-fallback fixes improve token resolution.
  • Completion and documentation respect code-token boundaries, leaving comments, strings and at-rules to the IDE.
  • HSL alpha, hue normalization and signed CSS lengths are corrected. Completion avoids repeated local-file scans.
  • The variable index rebuilds once after upgrade; no settings change is needed.

1.9.3 – 2026-08-28

Fixed

  • Quick Documentation for Java and other non-stylesheet languages (issue #35, IJPL-252456, reported by @markwoon): annotations such as @Nullable and @Deprecated, and Javadoc tags such as @param, no longer get mistaken for LESS variables. The plugin now returns no documentation target outside CSS-family PSI, allowing IntelliJ's native Java documentation provider to run normally.
  • CSS-family documentation remains intact: the guard uses the platform CSS-language contract, preserving CSS custom properties, SCSS/Sass variables, LESS variables, PostCSS, and injected CSS while avoiding hardcoded language IDs and file extensions.

Testing

  • Added real Java PSI regression coverage for type-use and declaration annotations plus an end-to-end platform target-selection test for Javadoc tags.
  • All 303 repository tests pass. Plugin structure, project configuration, the release artifact, the six-product 2025.1 verifier matrix, WebStorm 2026.1.2, and IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2.1 build IU-262.9437.185 are verified compatible.

Notes

  • No settings change or index rebuild is required.

1.9.2 – 2026-07-29

Fixed

  • Sass module imports (@use / @forward) are indexed (issue #28, PR #30, reported by @caseyjhol): the import scanner now recognises @use "..." and @forward "..." in addition to legacy @import. Tokens declared in @used partials — including package-root imports (@use "@vendor/design" as *), namespaced aliases (@use "..." as ns), and _index.scss partial resolution — feed hover, docs, and completion.
  • Package-root CSS-entrypoint fallback: when a package's Sass entrypoint is mixin-only (no concrete --* declarations), the resolver consults package.json's exports / sass / style / css fields and indexes the CSS distribution alongside the Sass API, preserving imported Sass variables.
  • Root + theme selector-list hover contexts canonicalised (issue #29, PR #31, reported by @caseyjhol): all five reproduction cases in the issue render a consistent, semantic label. :root, [data-theme="light"] { --foo: blue } collapses to a single Default/Light row. Attribute-equals quoting variants ([data-theme=light] vs [data-theme="light"]) normalise to one canonical shape.
  • Theme name derived from the actual selector: the Default/<Theme> label uses the real selector text, not a hardcoded Light. [data-theme="nova-light"] merges as Default/Nova Light, .theme-sepia as Default/Theme sepia, and so on.
  • Baseline :root is labelled Default: even for colour values. Previously colour-valued baselines were labelled Light mode, misrepresenting them as an explicit Light colour-scheme theme.

Testing

  • New parser coverage in SelectorListCanonicalizationTest for all five #29 cases plus multiple theme alternatives, escaped quoting, namespaced attributes, and selector alternatives nested inside media contexts.
  • New label-merge coverage in DefaultThemeLabelMergeTest for single-theme, duplicate-default, multi-theme, arbitrary theme-name, theme-only, and Default-alone, including a guard that Print and Reduced motion contexts are never mislabeled as themes.
  • New Sass-module import coverage in SassModuleImportTest and additional ImportResolverTest cases for @use, @forward, _index.scss partials, package.json field precedence, and the CSS-fallback path.
  • New end-to-end completion-harness fixtures for @use-chain hover documentation (both direct-Sass and CSS-fallback flavours).

Notes

  • No settings change is required. The index version is bumped to force a one-time rebuild so existing projects receive the new import and context-normalisation behavior immediately.

1.9.1 – 2026-06-30

Fixed

  • SCSS / LESS variables that alias CSS custom properties (issue #26, reported by @caseyjhol): hovering $foo when $foo: var(--foo) now surfaces the underlying CSS variable's full theme table, swatches, hex values, source information, and contrast details instead of reducing the popup to a literal var(--foo) value.
  • Alias labels stay understandable: the hover title keeps the preprocessor variable visible as $foo → var(--foo) / @foo → var(--foo), so users can see both what they hovered and which CSS custom property powers it.
  • Fallback aliases work: direct aliases such as var(--foo, #fff) now resolve through --foo when the CSS variable is indexed.
  • Quick-info hints include the bridge: hints now show the alias chain, e.g. $token → var(--token) → #112233.
  • Compound expressions stay literal: values such as 1px solid var(--foo) are intentionally not treated as pure aliases.

Testing

  • Added regression coverage for SCSS and LESS alias resolution, fallback aliases, quick-info hints, documentation title preservation, and compound-expression boundaries.

Notes

  • No settings change or index rebuild required.

1.9.0 – 2026-05-19

Added

  • Direct SCSS/Sass and LESS variable completion (Discussion #24, suggested by @LorincJuraj): complete $brand-primary in SCSS/Sass and @brand-primary in LESS directly in value positions, outside var(...). Lookup items reuse the existing value preview, colour icon, sorting and derived-value marker behaviour.
  • Quick documentation for direct preprocessor variables: hovering or invoking quick docs on $... / @... references now renders the same rich documentation table used for CSS custom properties, including resolved value, type, pixel/colour columns and resolution chain.
  • Import-backed preprocessor design-system lookup: project imports and explicitly imported node_modules stylesheets now feed the preprocessor index. SCSS/Sass/LESS variables from imported token packages are available to direct completion, documentation and CSS custom-property resolution.

Changed

  • Preprocessor index keys preserve syntax: $token and @token are stored separately, preventing SCSS/Sass and LESS variables with the same bare name from colliding. The index version was bumped so existing caches rebuild once after upgrade.
  • Sass and import parsing hardened: Sass indented custom properties without semicolons are indexed, Sass partial imports (_tokens.scss / _tokens.sass) resolve, and extensionless relative imports such as ./foundation no longer get mistaken for already-extensioned paths because of the leading ./.

Testing

  • Added coverage for SCSS, Sass and LESS indexing, direct completion, insertion, documentation target extraction, recursive imported alias resolution, arithmetic aliases, max import depth, circular aliases, $/@ separation and PROJECT_ONLY / PROJECT_WITH_IMPORTS / GLOBAL scope boundaries.

1.8.6 – 2026-04-29

Fixed

  • 8-digit hex colors with alpha (issue #22, reported by @LordMaddhi): a value like --accent: #7F80FF1A (modern CSS Color Level 4 #RRGGBBAA syntax) was rendered in the hover popup's Hex column as #80FF1A, looking like the first two characters had been silently dropped. Two compounding bugs were responsible and have both been corrected: ColorParser.parseHexColor treated the 8-digit form as Java's #AARRGGBB packed-int order (alpha first) instead of the CSS spec's #RRGGBBAA (alpha last), and colorToHex always emitted six digits, unconditionally dropping any alpha that had been parsed. Combined, this produced the visible #80FF1A truncation. The parser now reads alpha from the last byte, the formatter preserves alpha when present (#7F80FF1A round-trips identically), and 4-digit #RGBA shorthand is recognised.
  • Color swatch uses rgb()/rgba() instead of hex, so semi-transparent colors preview accurately. Locale is forced to Locale.ROOT so the alpha float always uses a "." decimal separator (CSS doesn't accept ","-separated numbers in non-US locales).

Notes

  • Fully-opaque colors still produce 6-digit hex (#1E90FF), so existing snapshots and the WebAIM contrast-checker URL are unaffected. The new ColorParser.colorToRgbHex(color) helper is available for callers that strictly need 6-digit RGB output.
  • Regression coverage in ColorParserTest: primary #7F80FF1A round-trip, 4-digit shorthand #RGBA and #RGBF, full-opacity collapse-to-6-digit, fully-transparent round-trip, explicit channel-position assertions, plus the pre-existing rgba tests updated to assert the new alpha-preserving contract (#FF008080 instead of #FF0080).
  • No index rebuild or settings change required — pure parser/rendering fix.

1.8.5 – 2026-04-28

Fixed

  • Calculated values with multi-valued nested vars (issue #21, reported by @kolkinn): A Radix Themes token like --space-2: calc(8px * var(--scaling)) was rendered in the hover popup as bare 0.9 (type: number) — the resolver was picking the first of five non-uniform --scaling definitions and dropping the surrounding calc(...) wrapper. Two intertwined bugs in resolveVarValue: (a) the recursive call passed only the inner value as the new raw, throwing away the calc context; (b) firstOrNull() blindly picked an arbitrary entry when no :root/default anchor existed and the candidates were non-uniform. The resolver now substitutes the matched var(--ref) token in place so calc(...) survives, and leaves the reference intact when the inner variable has multiple non-uniform values across selectors with no default to anchor to. Deterministic single-default lookups (e.g. var(--unit) with :root { --unit: 4px }) still substitute as before.

Notes

  • Regression coverage in DocHelpersResolveVarValueTest: ambiguous Radix-style scenario, all-entries-uniform shortcut, :root-anchored cascade, and the explicit "calc wrapper preserved" case.
  • No index rebuild or settings change required.
  • A copy-paste reproducer fixture lives at samples/issue-21/radix-scaling.css in the repo for side-loaded manual verification.

1.8.4 – 2026-04-22

Fixed

  • Exact-match ranking in the completion popup (issue #20, reported by @Blinks44): typing the complete variable name var(--sidebar-accent-foreground) left --sidebar selected at the top of the popup in 1.8.0-1.8.3, so pressing Enter/Tab overwrote the full name the user had already typed. Two independent paths in the ranking stack both compared each entry against its own truncated matched-prefix instead of the user's actual query; both now compare against the full query so the exact match wins.

Notes

  • Three layers of regression tests lock the fix in: matcher unit (matchingDegree score ordering), comparator unit (compareQuerySpecificity over a standalone Entry list), and full platform-fixture integration (completing var(--sidebar-accent-foreground) against a shadcn-style token file).
  • No index rebuild or settings change required.

1.8.3 – 2026-04-22

Added

  • Readable theme labels in the hover popup (new setting, default on): [data-theme="catppuccin"] now renders as "Catppuccin" in the Context column, [data-theme="high-contrast"] as "High contrast", .dark as "Dark", and so on. Any single attribute-equals or single-class selector is humanised — kebab-case and snake_case values get spaces and sentence-cased; user-authored uppercase (RTL, WCAG, acronyms) is preserved. Full raw selector lives on hover via a tooltip. Toggle under Settings → Tools → CSS Variables Assistant → Documentation Popup Columns → "Prettify theme selector labels" — turn off for paste-back-to-CSS fidelity.
  • Collapse rows with identical values (new setting, default on): when several themes resolve a token to the same value (e.g. catppuccin, sepia, and matcha all leaving --bg: white), they're merged into one row whose Context column lists every contributing theme ("Light mode, Catppuccin, Sepia"). Keeps the popup scannable in design systems with many theme variants. Turn off under Settings → Tools → CSS Variables Assistant → Documentation Popup Columns → "Collapse rows with identical values" to see one row per selector as in 1.8.2.

Notes

  • Compound selectors (.dark .nested, [a] .b), pseudo-classes (:hover, :not(.foo)) and IDs (#app) stay verbatim — prettifying them would misrepresent their CSS semantics.
  • No index rebuild required.

1.8.2 – 2026-04-22

Added

  • Compact Source column (on by default): the hover popup's Source cell now renders just :220; the full variables.css:220 appears on hover. Keeps the popup narrow enough to avoid wrapping at IntelliJ's max-width clamp. Toggle under Settings → Tools → CSS Variables Assistant → Documentation Popup Columns.
  • Wider popup by default: the value table now hints at ~700 px minimum width via a `min-width` wrapper + invisible spacer, so multi-column rows (Context, Value, Type, Source, Hex, WCAG) don't wrap in the common case. Platform still caps around 950 px; users can manually resize the popup and the IDE remembers.

Notes

  • No index rebuild required. Purely a rendering / UI polish release.

1.8.1 – 2026-04-22

Added

  • Theming selectors become their own rows in the hover popup (issue #19, reported by @LordMaddhi): Declarations inside [data-theme="dark"], .dark, .theme-high-contrast, :hover, [dir="rtl"] and other non-root selectors are now indexed as distinct contexts. Before 1.8.1 every non-:root/:host/html/body/* block collapsed into default and only the last declaration was visible, which hid dark-mode values from any theme system that didn't use @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark). Nested blocks combine labels, so @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { .hc { … } } renders as (prefers-color-scheme: dark) .hc.
  • Source file and line per declaration in the hover popup: the Source column now shows tokens.css:42 for every indexed row, so when the same variable is defined across multiple theme files (shadcn, Radix, Tailwind, Material) you can see which file and line each value lives on. Legacy index records fall back to the previous "first resolution step" label automatically.
  • Cascade-ambiguity disclaimer: a small note under multi-row value tables reminds that rows are shown in index order and the runtime-applied value still depends on stylesheet load order and specificity — the popup doesn't simulate the full CSS cascade engine.

Changed

  • INDEX_VERSION bumped to force a one-time re-index on first launch after upgrade. The packed record now carries a 4th field (1-based source line); legacy 3-part records decode safely with line = -1 so stale caches never crash the popup.
  • The documentation service uses FileBasedIndex.processValues instead of getValues so the (VirtualFile, packed) pair is available in one pass rather than an O(files × keys) re-query via getContainingFiles.

1.8.0 – 2026-04-22

Fixed

  • Completion popup no longer loses suggestions during progressive typing (issue #18 follow-up): Several regressions that only surfaced in real IDE sessions — hsl(var(--err)) showing every variable, a sticky popup that ignored subsequent keystrokes, --foreground / --error hidden behind their *-foreground siblings, and var(-<caret>) filtering out every variable without an internal dash. All fixed.
  • Value column no longer shows a comment (issue #18): When a CSS custom property has a JSDoc/block comment above it, the completion popup now always shows the resolved value — it no longer scrapes a --name: ...; sample out of an unrelated comment block. Both completion and hover documentation respect the real cascade winner.
  • Autocompletion no longer fires outside var() (issue #18): The gate now tracks parenthesis depth from each var( to the caret, so typing after a closed var(--x) on the same line stops surfacing every indexed variable. Identifiers ending in var (e.g. myvar() also no longer trigger completions.
  • Inline /* ... */ in values and declarations: The indexer now strips inline CSS comments from captured values and still indexes variables even when a leading /* comment */ and the declaration share one line.
  • Scope leaks node_modules fewer places: PROJECT_ONLY and PROJECT_WITH_IMPORTS scopes now consistently exclude node_modules at the CSS query layer, matching the settings panel's wording.
  • DESC completion sort no longer reverses the tier hierarchy: A latent bug had .reversed() flipping every step including PREFIX / TOKEN_PREFIX / SUBSTRING tier ordering. Only the value-level comparison reverses now; tier ordering is always PREFIX first.

Added

  • Three-option completion sort order: Completion sort order now offers By value ascending (default), By value descending, and Alphabetical by name. The preference applies consistently in both the blank-query autopopup path and fresh invocations, so --padding-sm / --padding-md / --padding-lg always appear in the chosen order regardless of how the popup was opened.
  • Completion description toggle + length: New settings under Display Options let you hide the description that appears next to each completion item, or clamp it to a custom length (0 = hide, up to 120 chars).
  • Optional feedback prompt: After ~14 days and 20 uses of CSS variable completion, a single non-intrusive balloon asks if you'd like to rate the plugin on Marketplace. "Remind me later" and "Don't show again" actions included. Prompt conditions are conservative — it will never re-appear once dismissed.
  • Pairs well with PxPeek: sibling plugin by the same author adding inline px-equivalents for rem / em / vh / % and all modern viewport units. Linked from the Marketplace description and the README.
  • Broader verifier coverage: Plugin verification now also runs against PyCharm Professional and RubyMine — both bundle the JavaScript and CSS plugins the plugin depends on.
  • Regression tests: New tests lock in each of the fixes above so the classes of bug in issue #18 don't come back.

Notes

  • The CSS variable index will rebuild once on first launch after upgrade because the parser now captures values differently.

1.7.2 – 2026-04-15

Fixed

  • Clean var(--name) insertion: Selecting a completion inside var(...) now always produces the correct var(--name) — the 1.7.1 release could insert var(----name), var(---name), or a trailing dash (var(--name-)) depending on when the popup opened.
  • Works inside any CSS function: Fix also covers var() nested inside other CSS functions, e.g. hsl(var(--bg)), rgba(var(--bg), 0.5), color-mix(in oklch, var(--bg) 50%, white), calc(var(--size) * 2), and linear-gradient(hsl(var(--a)), hsl(var(--b))). Only the var(...) containing the caret is rewritten.

Added

  • Insertion-based completion regression tests: New tests assert the actual document state after selecting a completion (not just which items are offered), covering bare var(...) and var() nested inside hsl / hsla / rgb / rgba / oklch / color-mix / calc / clamp / linear-gradient, plus multi-var() declarations and non-var() contexts.

1.7.1 – 2026-04-08

Added

  • Completion-scope regression coverage: Added tests that lock CSS variable completion to stylesheet files and valid var(...) value contexts.

Fixed

  • Stylesheet-only completion: CSS variable completions are no longer registered in JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, or TSX files.
  • Value-context completion: CSS variable suggestions now require a real var(...) context and no longer interfere with CSS property-name completion such as background.

idea-plugin.name: CSS Class Attributes Fold
idea-plugin.description:
CSS Class Attributes Fold

CSS class attributes can get verbose quickly. This plugin helps you fold them to keep templates readable. Enable CSS Class Attributes Fold and enjoy cleaner code and better readability. If you are annoyed by other html attributes or your custom ones then you can customize them in plugin settings.

The plugin will allow you to fold class attributes in HTML, Vue templates, Svelte templates and JavaScript/TypeScript files that create templates.

Supported filetypes:

  • HTML
  • Vue HTML templates
  • Svelte HTML templates
  • React JSX templates
  • HTML templates inside JavaScript/TypeScript
  • Astro HTML templates

Plans:

Free

Freemium

Class attribute collapsing

Can customize any attributes

Can collapse/expand all tags globally

Can collapse/expand all tags globally

X

Can collapse customized attributes in all tags in file

X

Can expand customized attributes in all tags in file

Useful shortcuts:

  1. Expand/Collapse All attributes use shortcut (Shift + cmd + P on Mac or Shift + Ctrl + P on Windows). This is going to change global setting. If you had previously opened files their expand/collapse state will change after you navigate to the file and start making some changes. IDE doesn't force file rerendering before your action.
  2. To expand/collapse "class" attribute under cursor use default IDE code folding shortcut (Cmd + dot on Mac or Ctrl + . on Windows). If your cursor is between attribute value start and end then using shortcut will collapse attribute value.
  3. You can open collapsed area by clicking on collapsed attribute value placeholder. In default configuration clicking on "..." will open its value.

Paid version shortcuts:

  1. Fold All Attributes shortcut (Shift + cmd + F on Mac or Shift + Ctrl + F on Windows) - fold all attributes in active file
  2. Expand All Attributes shortcut (Shift + cmd + C on Mac or Shift + Ctrl + C on Windows) - fold all attributes in active file

Feel free to remap shortcuts in IDE settings -> keymap -> "shortcut name"

Support Plugin Developer:

If you like the plugin, and you are using free version of that, please consider supporting Me or subscribing for the plugin.

Support my work

idea-plugin.name: VSCode Dark High Contrast Theme
idea-plugin.description:
VSCode Dark High Contrast Theme for IntelliJ Platform IDEs

This plugin brings Visual Studio Code's popular Dark High Contrast color theme to IntelliJ IDEA and all IntelliJ Platform-based IDEs.


Features:

  • Maximum contrast for enhanced readability
  • Pure black background with bright, vivid colors
  • Optimized for accessibility and low vision users
  • Comprehensive syntax highlighting across all languages
  • Consistent with VSCode's Dark High Contrast theme

Installation:

  1. Install the plugin from JetBrains Marketplace or manually
  2. Go to Settings → Appearance & Behavior → Appearance
  3. Select "VSCode Dark High Contrast" from the Theme dropdown
  4. Click Apply and restart if needed

idea-plugin.name: Web Components Language Server
idea-plugin.description:
Web Components Language Server for JetBrains IDEs

Advanced editor support for using Web Components and custom elements in WebStorm, IntelliJ IDEA, and other JetBrains IDEs.

Features

  • HTML diagnostics for custom elements and attributes
  • Attribute type validation (boolean, number, enum, string)
  • Deprecated element and attribute warnings
  • Duplicate attribute detection
  • Intelligent autocomplete for custom elements
  • Hover documentation for components and attributes
  • Go-to-definition for component usage
  • CSS custom property autocomplete and validation
  • Configurable diagnostics severity
  • Works with any Web Components library that provides a Custom Elements Manifest
  • Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for AI agent integration

Configuration

Create a wc.config.js file in your project root to customize behavior.

Requirements

  • Node.js installed and available in PATH
  • Custom Elements Manifest (custom-elements.json) in your project

idea-plugin.name: CSS Class Fold Plus
idea-plugin.description:
Tame your Tailwind. Declutter your templates.

A JetBrains IDE plugin that intelligently folds CSS class attributes, transforming walls of utility classes into clean, readable code.

The Problem

Modern utility-first CSS frameworks like Tailwind are powerful, but they come with visual clutter:

<div class="flex items-center justify-between px-4 py-3 bg-gradient-to-r from-blue-500 to-purple-600 rounded-lg shadow-lg hover:shadow-xl transition-all duration-300">

The Solution

<div class="‥ c(12)">

One keystroke. Instant clarity.

Core Folding Features

  • Smart Folding - Collapses class attributes showing a compact badge: "‥ c(12)" for 12 classes
  • Class Count Threshold - Only fold when class count exceeds a configurable minimum (default: 5)
  • Line Length Threshold - Only fold when class attribute length exceeds a maximum (default: 80 characters)
  • Partial Folding - Show first N classes with remaining count: "flex items-center ‥ c(10)"
  • Category Summary - Show Tailwind category breakdown: "‥ [layout: 3, spacing: 4, typography: 2]"

Code Quality Inspections

  • Duplicate Class Detection - Warns when the same class appears multiple times with quick-fix to remove duplicates
  • Conflicting Class Detection - Warns when conflicting Tailwind classes are used together (e.g., text-left and text-right) with quick-fix to resolve
  • Badge Indicators - Placeholder shows duplicate count d(2) and conflict count x(1) when issues exist

Hover Tooltips

  • Full Class Preview - See the complete class list by hovering over collapsed regions
  • Color Swatches - Visual color indicators for Tailwind color classes (bg-red-500, text-blue-300, etc.)
  • Conflict Highlighting - Conflicting classes are highlighted in red with descriptions
  • Category Grouping - Classes grouped by Tailwind category in tooltip when sorting by category

Class Sorting

  • Keep Original Order - Preserve the order as written in code
  • Sort Alphabetically - Sort classes A-Z
  • Sort by Tailwind Category - Group by category (Layout, Flexbox & Grid, Spacing, Sizing, Typography, Backgrounds, Borders, Effects, Filters, Transitions, Transforms, Interactivity, Accessibility)

Workflow Features

  • One-Key Toggle - Expand/collapse all with a single shortcut
  • Auto-Collapse on File Open - Automatically collapse all class folds when opening files
  • Remember Fold State - Persist fold states across IDE sessions per file
  • Copy Classes to Clipboard - Right-click context menu to copy classes in various formats (space-separated, newline-separated, sorted, by category)
  • File Type Control - Enable or disable folding per file type

Developer Experience

  • Multi-Framework Support - Works with HTML, React, Vue, and Angular
  • Always Available - Works even during IDE indexing (DumbAware)
  • Project-Level Settings - Override application settings per project

Supported Frameworks

  • HTML/CSS: class
  • React: className
  • Vue: :class, v-bind:class
  • Angular: [ngClass], [class], ng-class

Supported File Types

HTML, XHTML, XML, JSX, TSX, Vue Single File Components

Placeholder Format

The plugin uses a compact badge format for collapsed classes:

  • c(N) - Total class count
  • d(N) - Duplicate count (classes appearing more than once)
  • x(N) - Conflict count (mutually exclusive classes)

Examples:

<div class="‥ c(12)">                         <!-- Standard -->
<div class="‥ c(12) d(2)">                    <!-- With duplicates -->
<div class="‥ c(12) x(1)">                    <!-- With conflicts -->
<div class="flex items-center ‥ c(12)">       <!-- Partial folding -->
<div class="‥ [layout: 3, spacing: 4]">       <!-- Category summary -->

Usage

  • Windows/Linux: Ctrl+Shift+C
  • macOS: Cmd+Shift+C
  • Menu: Code → Toggle CSS Class Folding
  • Context Menu: Right-click → Copy CSS Classes
  • Application Settings: Settings → Editor → CSS Class Fold Plus
  • Project Settings: Settings → Editor → CSS Class Fold Plus (Project)

How It Works

  1. Open any supported file with CSS class attributes
  2. Press the shortcut to collapse all class attributes
  3. Press again to expand all class attributes
  4. Individual folds can be toggled by clicking the fold gutter
  5. Hover over collapsed regions to preview the full class list

Configuration Options

Access settings via Settings → Editor → CSS Class Fold Plus

  • Smart Collapse Threshold - Only fold when class count exceeds minimum
  • Line Length Threshold - Only fold when attribute length exceeds maximum
  • Partial Folding - Show first N classes in placeholder
  • Category Summary - Show Tailwind category breakdown in placeholder
  • Class Sorting - Keep original, alphabetical, or by Tailwind category
  • Hover Preview - Show full class list and color swatches in tooltip
  • Duplicate Detection - Enable inspection and badge indicator
  • Conflict Detection - Enable inspection and badge indicator
  • Auto-Collapse - Collapse on file open, remember fold state
  • File Types - Enable/disable per file type (HTML, JSX, TSX, Vue, XML, XHTML)

Tailwind Category Classification

Classes are grouped into 13 categories:

  • Layout - container, block, inline, hidden, absolute, relative, sticky, z-index, overflow
  • Flexbox & Grid - flex, grid, gap, justify, items, content, self, order
  • Spacing - p-, px-, py-, m-, mx-, my-, space-
  • Sizing - w-, h-, min-w-, max-w-, min-h-, max-h-, size-
  • Typography - font-, text-, tracking-, leading-, list-, decoration-, truncate
  • Backgrounds - bg-, from-, via-, to-, gradient-
  • Borders - border, rounded, outline-, ring-, divide-
  • Effects - shadow, opacity-, mix-blend-, bg-blend-
  • Filters - blur, brightness-, contrast-, grayscale, invert, saturate-
  • Transitions - transition, duration-, ease-, delay-, animate-
  • Transforms - scale-, rotate-, translate-, skew-, origin-, transform
  • Interactivity - cursor-, caret-, pointer-events-, resize, scroll-, select-
  • Accessibility - sr-only, not-sr-only

State variants like hover:, focus:, sm:, md:, etc. are stripped before categorization.

Color Swatches

Visual color indicators in tooltips for all Tailwind CSS v3.x colors:

  • 22 Color Families: slate, gray, zinc, neutral, stone, red, orange, amber, yellow, lime, green, emerald, teal, cyan, sky, blue, indigo, violet, purple, fuchsia, pink, rose
  • 11 Shades: 50, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900, 950
  • 14 Prefixes: bg-, text-, border-, ring-, divide-, outline-, shadow-, accent-, caret-, fill-, stroke-, from-, via-, to-, decoration-

Stop scrolling sideways. Start shipping faster.

idea-plugin.name: OKLCH-converter
idea-plugin.description:

idea-plugin.name: DashStyle CSS Module Support
idea-plugin.description:
Enhances IntelliJ IDEA / WebStorm with richer support for CSS Modules (React, Vue, or any project using styles["foo-bar"] / styles.fooBar).

Key features:

  • Smart completion & navigation: auto-complete class names for both styles["foo-bar"] (string key) and styles.fooBar (member access); Ctrl+Click jumps to the matching .foo-bar rule, and hovering shows the expanded full rule with its declarations.
  • Inline style → CSS Module extraction (Alt+Enter): turns style={{...}} / :style="{...}" into a semantic class name and appends the rule to the matching module file.
  • JSON → CSS copy-paste: automatically fixes JS style objects pasted into CSS (unitless properties, negatives, transform functions, shorthand arrays); recognizes Vue :style / v-bind:style and Angular [style] / [ngStyle] bindings, including ngStyle unit suffixes such as 'font-size.px'.
  • Code inspection: marks unused CSS Module classes and duplicate declaration blocks, with one-click fixes to delete or extract shared styles.
  • Tailwind support: completion with a CSS preview inside @apply, and auto-generation of missing atomic classes referenced via styles.xxx.
  • Batch migration: Refactor → Convert className to CSS Module moves a file or selection onto CSS Modules in one go.

Works with CSS / SCSS / LESS module files, Vue <style module>, and local JS/TS object literals.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.3.6

  • 🔧 修复 React style JSON / JS 字面量里 gap: 8 这类纯数字间距值转换后没有补 px 的问题：gap / grid-gap / row-gap / column-gap / flex-basis 之前被误放进「无单位属性」名单，而纯数字 gap 在 CSS 里是非法值（复制粘贴与「提取为 CSS Module」两条路径一并修复）
  • ✅ 无单位属性名单整体对齐 react-dom 官方 isUnitlessNumber：补齐 border-image-slice/width、box-flex 系列、flex-positive/negative/order、line-clamp、scale、zoom 及 SVG 的 stroke-width / fill-opacity 等；flex / z-index / opacity / line-height 等原有行为不变
  • 🧪 新增 9 个回归测试：gap 数字 / 字符串数字 / 数组逐项补 px、gridGap / rowGap / columnGap、flexBasis 补 px，以及 strokeWidth / scale / zoom 保持无单位

1.3.5

  • ✨ 提取 inline style / 批量迁移找不到目标 CSS Module 时不再报错终止，按项目样式风格自动创建：探测级联为「同目录已有 *.module.* → 全项目样式文件统计 → package.json 依赖（sass/node-sass → SCSS、less → LESS）→ 原生 CSS」，新建 Xxx.module.(css|scss|sass|less) 并自动生成 import
  • 🔧 修复批量迁移（将 className 转换为 CSS Module）在目标文件缺失时静默失败：VFS 变更（新建 / 重命名 / 复制）全部包进写命令执行，真正失败时弹出明确的错误提示；复用同名 module 文件时顺带补上缺失的 import
  • 🇻 Vue SFC 没有 <style module> 块时按项目风格自动追加（scss / sass / less 自动带 lang 属性）
  • 💅 SASS 缩进语法适配：.module.sass 目标生成的类规则不再带大括号（选择器 + 缩进声明）
  • 🧪 新增 CssModuleDialectTest 13 个用例：方言映射、四级探测级联、写动作包装回归、按方言自动创建 + import 生成

1.3.4

  • 🔧 修复带参数文案渲染为 [Ljava.lang.Object;@… 的回归：bundle 消息转发补上 vararg 展开符，带占位符的文案（检查描述、快速修复名、悬浮文档、成功提示、对话框等）恢复正常格式化
  • ✨ 「重命名提取的 CSS 类」对话框升级为可编辑下拉框：Top 5 语义化候选作为下拉项并默认选中最佳候选，同时支持直接输入自定义类名（kebab-case 校验规则不变）
  • 🧪 新增 bundle 消息格式化回归测试：锁定无参 / 单参 / 多参替换与防数组 toString 泄漏行为

1.3.3

  • 🌍 多语言支持：全部用户可见文案（Action / Intention / Inspection / 悬浮文档 / 对话框 / 撤销命令名）迁移至 resource bundle，默认英文，新增简体中文（zh_CN）完整翻译，跟随 IDE 界面语言自动切换、无需重启
  • ⚙️ Settings → Editor → Inspections 中的检查项显示名与描述同步本地化（%key% 引用 + DynamicBundle 动态解析）
  • 🧪 测试运行固定英文 locale，保障文案断言稳定通过

1.3.2

  • ✨ 支持 Angular ngStyle 键单位修饰：'font-size.px': 12 → font-size: 12px、'width.%': 50 → width: 50%（显式单位优先于默认推断，shorthand 数组同样生效）
  • 🧪 测试加固：inspection 注册路径（EP 实例化逐语言触发）、CreateMissingCssClass 意图菜单、批量迁移类名收集、Tailwind 补全格式化、悬浮文档 CSS Module 主路径等新增常驻测试

1.3.1

  • 🔧 修复 CreateMissingCssClassIntention（缺失类快速创建）在 Intention 预览触发下可能出现的死锁：通过声明 startInWriteAction = true，让 invoke() 由框架在写锁内调用，避免 preview 的读锁与写锁竞争导致 UI 卡死

idea-plugin.name: Super-qss
idea-plugin.description:
Super QSS - Qt Style Sheet Language Support

A powerful QSS (Qt Style Sheet) language plugin for PyCharm, IntelliJ IDEA, and other JetBrains IDEs. Designed for Qt/PySide/PyQt developers who want a first-class QSS editing experience.

✨ Key Features

🎨 Syntax Highlighting

  • Full syntax highlighting for QSS files
  • Customizable color scheme in Settings → Editor → Color Scheme → QSS
  • Highlights selectors, properties, values, pseudo-states, sub-controls, and more

🔮 Smart Code Completion

  • Auto-completion for Qt widget names (QPushButton, QLabel, QLineEdit, etc.)
  • Property name suggestions with documentation
  • Property value completion based on context
  • Pseudo-state completion (:hover, :pressed, :disabled, etc.)
  • Sub-control completion (::indicator, ::handle, ::groove, etc.)

🎯 Navigation & Go to Declaration

  • ID Selector Navigation: Ctrl+Click on #objectName to jump to setObjectName("objectName") in Python code
  • Attribute Selector Navigation: Ctrl+Click on [attr="value"] to jump to setProperty("attr", "value")
  • Template Variable Navigation: Ctrl+Click on ${alias.color}, @variable, or $variable to jump to variable definitions

🌈 Color Preview & Picker

  • Inline color preview in the gutter for hex colors, rgb(), and rgba()
  • Click to open color picker and modify colors directly
  • Supports all QSS color formats

📝 Code Formatting

  • Auto-format QSS files with customizable style
  • Configurable indentation, spacing, and brace placement
  • Access via Code → Reformat Code (Ctrl+Alt+L)

🔧 Template Variable Support

  • Support for template variables like ${variable}, @variable, $variable
  • Configurable template patterns in Settings → Editor → QSS
  • Template variables are highlighted and won't be marked as errors

📚 Additional Features

  • Documentation: Hover over properties to see documentation
  • Code Folding: Collapse rule blocks for better overview
  • Brace Matching: Automatic matching of braces and brackets
  • Structure View: Navigate QSS file structure in the Structure tool window
  • Commenting: Toggle comments with Ctrl+/
  • Error Detection: Highlights missing semicolons and syntax errors

🚀 Getting Started

  1. Install the plugin from JetBrains Marketplace
  2. Open any .qss file
  3. Enjoy full language support!

⚙️ Configuration

Configure template variable support and other settings in:
Settings → Editor → QSS

💡 Tips

  • Use Ctrl+Click on #widgetName to navigate to Python code
  • Type : after a selector to trigger pseudo-state completion
  • Type :: to trigger sub-control completion

🐛 Issues & Feedback

Found a bug or have a feature request? Please report it on GitHub Issues.

idea-plugin.name: Flexible Tailwind
idea-plugin.description:
Tailwind CSS for many languages - autocomplete, documentation, color previews + drag&drop components.

Unlike language-specific Tailwind plugins, Flexible Tailwind uses advanced context detection to provide autocomplete, documentation, and inspections wherever Tailwind classes are used - HTML, JSX, Vue, PHP, Python templates, and beyond. Plus, get instant access to 163 professionally designed, copy-paste ready Tailwind components with live preview.

Support us by leaving a review, or sharing your ideas or bug reports!

Features

Production-Ready Components (NEW!)

  • Full-width professional heroes with navbars, CTAs, and responsive layouts
  • Cards, alerts, buttons, forms, navigation and more
  • Three design variants for each: Basic, Material, Creative (glassmorphism)
  • Built-in snippet browser with live preview in dedicated tool window
  • Dark mode support - automatic theme adaptation
  • Fully responsive - mobile-first design with Tailwind breakpoints
  • Copy-paste ready - no wrapper styling, drop directly into your app
  • Browse by category: Heroes, Cards, Buttons, Forms, Alerts, Navigation, Tables, Lists, and more

Intelligent Autocomplete

  • 3500+ built-in Tailwind v3 classes with descriptions
  • Works in class="", className="", @apply, and more
  • Color preview icons next to color classes
  • Supports arbitrary values: bg-[#ff0000], w-[100px]
  • Modifier-aware: hover:, dark:, md:, etc.

Rich Documentation

  • Hover over any Tailwind class for detailed docs
  • Shows CSS property output
  • Color swatches for color classes
  • Direct links to official Tailwind documentation

Smart Inspections

  • Unknown Class Warning: Flags invalid Tailwind classes
  • Duplicate Class Warning: Detects duplicate classes in same attribute
  • Quick fixes to remove duplicates

Color Preview

  • Inline color swatches next to color classes
  • Works for background, text, border, ring, and more
  • Supports full Tailwind color palette

Universal Language Support

  • HTML/XML: class="bg-blue-500"
  • JavaScript/JSX: className="flex items-center"
  • TypeScript/TSX: Full support
  • Vue: Template and script sections
  • CSS/SCSS: @apply directive support
  • Any language: Generic pattern detection for class="..." and className="..."

Customizable

  • YAML-driven class definitions
  • Add your own custom classes
  • Project-level configuration
  • Merge custom definitions with built-in library

Works Everywhere

Flexible Tailwind runs on all JetBrains IDEs:

  • IntelliJ IDEA (Community & Ultimate)
  • WebStorm
  • PhpStorm
  • PyCharm
  • GoLand
  • RubyMine
  • CLion
  • Rider
  • Android Studio

And provides Tailwind support in all languages:

  • HTML, XML, JSX, TSX, Vue
  • JavaScript, TypeScript
  • PHP, Python, Ruby, Go, Rust
  • And more!

Installation

  • Using IDE built-in plugin system:

    Settings/Preferences > Plugins > Marketplace > Search for "Flexible Tailwind" > Install Plugin

  • Manually:

    Download the latest release and install it manually using Settings/Preferences > Plugins > ⚙️ > Install plugin from disk...

Usage

Autocomplete & IntelliSense

  1. Install the plugin
  2. Open any file with Tailwind classes
  3. Start typing in class="..." or className="..." attributes
  4. Enjoy autocomplete, documentation, and color previews!

Component Snippets

  1. Open the Snippets tool window (View > Tool Windows > Snippets)
  2. Browse 163 components across 15 categories
  3. Select a component to see live preview
  4. Switch between Basic, Material, and Creative variants
  5. Toggle light/dark mode preview
  6. Click "Copy to Clipboard" to use in your project

Categories include:

  • Heroes - Full-width landing page sections with navbars and CTAs
  • Cards - Content cards, pricing cards, profile cards, and more
  • Buttons - Primary, secondary, outlined, icon buttons, and more
  • Forms - Inputs, textareas, checkboxes, selects, and validation states
  • Alerts - Info, success, warning, error notifications
  • Navigation - Navbars, breadcrumbs, tabs, pagination
  • Modals - Dialogs, confirmations, form modals
  • Tables - Data tables with sorting and pagination styles
  • Lists - Ordered, unordered, description lists
  • Typography - Headings, paragraphs, quotes, code blocks
  • Headers/Footers - Page headers and footers
  • Progress - Progress bars, spinners, skeleton loaders
  • Media - Images, videos, avatars, galleries
  • Layout - Containers, grids, dividers, spacing
  • Misc - Badges, tags, tooltips, and more

Configuration

Access plugin settings via: Settings/Preferences > Tools > Flexible Tailwind

  • Enable/disable specific class categories
  • Add custom class definitions via YAML
  • Configure inspection severity

Architecture

Flexible Tailwind uses a unique language-agnostic architecture:

  1. Generic Text Pattern Detection: Analyzes surrounding text to detect Tailwind contexts
  2. PSI Layer Integration: When available, uses language-specific PSI for precise detection
  3. YAML Definition System: 3500+ classes defined in structured YAML format
  4. Optional Language Support: Enhanced support for HTML/JS/CSS when plugins are available

This approach ensures the plugin works everywhere, with progressive enhancement based on installed language plugins.

Development

Built with:

  • IntelliJ Platform SDK 2023.3+
  • Kotlin & Java
  • YAML-driven data definitions
  • Cross-IDE compatibility

License

Paid plugin - requires license for use beyond trial period.

Help Us Improve

We're committed to making Flexible Tailwind the best Tailwind CSS plugin for JetBrains IDEs. Your feedback helps us get better!

Leave a Review

  • If you find this plugin useful, please leave a review on the JetBrains Marketplace
  • Your reviews help other developers discover Flexible Tailwind

Share Feedback

  • Found a bug? Open an issue on GitHub
  • Have a feature request? Create a feature request
  • Want to suggest improvements? We'd love to hear from you!

Contribute

  • Report bugs with detailed reproduction steps
  • Request features that would make your workflow better
  • Share your use cases and how we can better support them

Every review, bug report, and feature request helps us build a better plugin for the entire community. Thank you!

idea-plugin.name: MarkTone
idea-plugin.description:
MarkTone automatically generates and applies Markdown preview styles that match your current IDE theme.

Features

  • Extracts colors and fonts from your active IDE theme
  • Generates a complete Markdown preview stylesheet with proper typography
  • Auto-syncs styles when you switch themes — no manual CSS editing needed
  • Two rendering profiles: Minimal (compact, sober palette) and Expressive (spacious, rich colors)
  • Syntax highlighting in fenced code blocks — keywords, strings, numbers, comments, and functions colored from your theme
  • Live preview in settings — see how profile, font scaling, and theme choices look before applying
  • Preview theme selector — try any installed editor color scheme without switching your IDE theme
  • Adjustable font size scaling (90%–180%) for the Markdown preview
  • Quick profile switching from the toolbar, Tools > MarkTone menu, or keyboard shortcut (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+M / Cmd+Alt+Shift+M on Mac)
  • Optional custom CSS overrides for further tweaking

How it works

MarkTone reads your current editor colors, font family, and font size, then composes a Markdown-specific stylesheet using CSS custom properties. The result is applied directly to the Markdown preview panel.

Requirements

  • JetBrains IDE 2023.3 or later
  • Markdown plugin (bundled with most JetBrains IDEs)

idea-plugin.name: Flexible Gutenberg
idea-plugin.description:
Block editor toolkit for WordPress — autocomplete, block.json schema, block browser, theme.json, and JS scaffolding.

Write WordPress block markup faster with smart completions for the <!-- wp: --> comment syntax in HTML and PHP files, full block.json schema validation, a searchable block browser sidebar, a theme.json property explorer, and JavaScript scaffolding for custom blocks.

Core Features

Block Markup Autocomplete

  • <!-- wp: completion in HTML and PHP files — type the opening comment and get instant suggestions for all core blocks with their categories and descriptions
  • Block attribute completion — after inserting a block, get JSON key/value completions with allowed values (e.g. align offers left, center, right, wide, full)
  • Self-closing vs paired — blocks like core/separator and all FSE blocks auto-insert the correct self-closing or open/close comment form

block.json Schema & Validation

  • Full JSON schema for block.json files — property completion, value validation, and inline documentation
  • All standard fields covered: name, title, category, attributes, supports, editorScript, style, render, variations, example, and more
  • Works in PhpStorm, IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate, and WebStorm automatically when a block.json file is opened

Block Browser Tool Window

  • Searchable catalog of all WordPress core blocks — Paragraph, Heading, Image, Group, Cover, Query Loop, Navigation, and more
  • Detail panel showing attributes, supported features, and ready-to-paste example markup
  • Insert at caret or copy to clipboard from the sidebar — no typing required
  • Open Docs button jumps straight to the official developer reference

@wordpress Components Browser

  • Browse all @wordpress/* React components — elements, hooks, and utility functions across 18 packages
  • Prop table with types and descriptions, plus a ready-to-copy JSX snippet
  • Insert at caret automatically adds the correct import { ... } from '@wordpress/...' statement at the top of the file

Theme JSON Browser

  • Full theme.json schema reference — settings, styles, customTemplates, templateParts, and patterns in a tree view
  • Version-aware — properties are tagged v1 (WP 5.8), v2 (WP 5.9–6.3), or v3 (WP 6.4+), and properties not available in your project's detected schema version are visually muted
  • Auto-detection — reads the $schema URL from your project's theme.json to determine the active version
  • Insert at caret copies the example JSON directly into your file

JavaScript Block Scaffolding

  • New > Gutenberg > Gutenberg Block — creates a complete block directory: block.json, index.js, edit.js, and either save.js (static) or render.php (dynamic), plus editor.scss and style.scss
  • @wordpress/ import completion in JS and TS files — type @wordpress/ and get all 18 official packages with descriptions

Live Templates

Type wp: to access all templates:

HTML Block Templates:

  • wp:paragraph, wp:heading, wp:image, wp:group, wp:columns — core block markup
  • wp:cover, wp:buttons, wp:quote, wp:list, wp:table, wp:separator, wp:spacer
  • wp:template-part, wp:post-title, wp:site-title, wp:navigation — FSE blocks

block.json Templates:

  • wp:block-json — complete block.json scaffold
  • wp:attr-string, wp:attr-boolean, wp:attr-number, wp:attr-array — attribute definitions

JavaScript Templates (JS/TS files):

  • wp:register-block, wp:edit-component, wp:save-component, wp:edit-dynamic
  • wp:richtext, wp:richtext-content, wp:inspector-controls
  • wp:media-upload, wp:use-block-props, wp:set-attrs
  • wp:select-control, wp:range-control, wp:toggle-control, wp:text-control
  • wp:block-variation

Generate Pattern File

  • Tools > Flexible Gutenberg > Generate Pattern File — creates a properly formatted patterns/slug.php with the WordPress block pattern header and placeholder markup

Project Detection

Automatically activates features when a project is recognised as a WordPress project by detecting any of: wp-config.php, block.json, theme.json, style.css with Theme Name:, or package.json referencing @wordpress/blocks.

Getting Started

Quick Start

  1. Install from JetBrains Marketplace and restart your IDE
  2. Open a WordPress theme, plugin, or block project
  3. Open any .php or .html file and type <!-- wp: to see block completions
  4. Open a block.json file and press Ctrl+Space for schema completions
  5. Open the Gutenberg tool window (View > Tool Windows > Gutenberg) to browse blocks, components, and theme.json properties

Productivity Tips

  • Type wp: + Tab in any HTML/PHP file for instant block markup templates
  • Double-click a block in the browser to insert it at the cursor
  • Inserting a JSX component from the Components tab automatically adds the import statement
  • Alt+Enter inside block.json for schema-aware quick fixes

Supported IDEs

  • PhpStorm 2023.3+
  • IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate 2023.3+
  • WebStorm 2023.3+

Target Audience

Theme developers, plugin authors, and agencies building custom Gutenberg blocks or Full Site Editing themes for WordPress.

Made by Developers with a Passion for WordPress

The plugin is the work of Ilscipio:

We build and maintain WordPress-based platforms as part of our core technology stack and understand the day-to-day friction of block development — switching between documentation tabs, hand-writing repetitive block markup, and hunting down theme.json properties. We built this plugin to eliminate that friction.

  • Special discounts available for individual developers and the open source community.

Bugs & Feature Requests

This is a young project and we genuinely want your input. Bug reports, feature requests, and general feedback are very welcome. Reach out via the GitHub repository, by email at info@ilscipio.com, or through the JetBrains Marketplace plugin page.

idea-plugin.name: PxPeek - CSS Pixel Hints
idea-plugin.description:
Shows the pixel equivalent of relative CSS size values as comment-style inlay hints.

Supports CSS, SCSS, SASS, and LESS.

Choose where hints appear:
  • End of line (default) — aggregated after the semicolon:
    width: min(42rem, 100%); /* 672px, 16px */
  • Inline — next to each value:
    width: min(42rem /* 672px */, 100% /* 16px */)
Configure in Settings → Editor → Inlay Hints → PxPeek.

Converts rem, em, %, pt, pc, in, cm, mm, ch, ex, vw, vh, vmin, vmax, and their small/large/dynamic viewport variants.

Defaults: 16px root font, 1440×900 viewport.

Pairs well with: CSS Variables Assistant — autocomplete, docs, and resolution tracing for var(--name).
