idea-plugin.name: Angular Architect
idea-plugin.description:
Angular architecture tooling for IntelliJ IDEA and WebStorm. Angular Architect maps your components, services, stores, routes, and modules as connected systems — then generates, inspects, navigates, and wires them for you. Everything is version-aware from Angular 12 to 22 and TypeScript 4 to 7.

Angular Architect is also an MCP server. It exposes its analysis to MCP-compatible AI agents as read-only tools, so an agent reasons from the same version-gated facts the plugin's own panels show, instead of re-scanning your code and guessing. Loopback-only, off until you start it, and no tool can modify files.

Free and Pro. Every feature is free today. When the freemium model launches (date to be announced), these will need a Pro license: the Kubernetes panel, Unit Test generation, Error Analysis, Upgrade Readiness, OpenAPI Studio (Scaffold, Re-sync, Explorer and Mock), Provenance X-Ray, Impact Analysis, Migration Insights, the dev-server launcher and the MCP server. Everything else — inspections, intentions, generators, navigation, Health, the Quality, Catalog and Insights scans, Security, and the other tool windows — stays free.

58 inspections • 19 generators • 6 intentions • 33+ refactoring detectors • 5 SOLID analysers • 53 live templates • 31 tool-window panels

  • Generate — components, feature modules (13-file scaffold), NgRx stores & action flows, guards, pipes, directives, interceptors, resolvers, CRUD services, reactive & signal forms, interface-from-JSON, feature clone, Extract Component, GraphQL+NgRx features, and Angular Material schematics via the project's own CLI. Every emit matches your detected Angular/TypeScript majors: @Input() vs input(), *ngIf vs @if, class-based vs functional guards, HttpClientModule vs provideHttpClient().
  • Inspect — 58 inspections: architecture boundaries, circular dependencies, template binding errors, signal misuse, accessibility, dead routes, unused NgRx, deep imports, deprecated APIs, RxJS operator advisor, control-flow / standalone / signal migration assistants, OpenAPI drift. Third-party deprecations are scanned too, from a weekly-harvested ecosystem catalog (RxJS, NgRx, Material/CDK, ngx-translate, single-spa) that carries each library's own replacement guidance; inline migration-hint line markers flag version-sensitive calls right in the editor. Plus 33+ refactoring detectors (god components, observable leaks, XSS, hardcoded secrets), 5 SOLID analysers, 12 code-review rules across .ts/.html/.scss/.css, and 6 Alt+Enter intentions.
  • Analyse — Project Health 0–100 per feature, Performance grade A–F per component, OSV security advisories with copy-pasteable fixes, license scan, dependency freshness, code duplication, unused dependencies, code-ownership analytics from git history (bus factor, hotspots), gutter coverage markers fed by your LCOV / Istanbul reports (auto-refreshing as test runs land), and signals / standalone / control-flow migration dashboards.
  • Navigate & visualise — Feature Graph, Go to Related File (Ctrl+Alt+G), gutter icons to templates / styles / specs / stores, impact analysis with blast-radius widgets, NgRx Flow Tracer, interactive architecture diagram, Signals graph (signal / computed / effect dependencies visualised), component and HTTP-API catalogs, route & DI trees, communication map, a fuzzy-ranked command palette whose entries are version-gated to your Angular major, and Generate Deep Link for composing shareable Router URLs.
  • OpenAPI / Swagger Studio — scaffold a typed Angular feature from any OpenAPI 3.x / Swagger 2.x spec, re-sync when the spec drifts (rename detection, change preview, atomic apply), fire live requests from the in-IDE Explorer with auth presets, and run a zero-dependency mock server from the same spec.
  • Test — the Unit Tests tab generates a runnable .spec.ts for the selected file, matched to your detected runner (Vitest / Jest / Karma) and Angular major: TestBed setup, dependency mocks built from each injected service's real public methods, one HttpTestingController expectation per endpoint, signal-derivation and template-interaction cases, coverage-ranked ordering, and an append-only merge into an existing spec behind a diff preview.
  • Diagnose runtime errors — paste browser-console output into the Error Analysis tab: NG error codes are decoded in plain language, the root cause is located in your own source with clickable file:line evidence (a service that is injected but never provided, a component missing from an imports array, a route that matches nothing), and framework stack noise is folded away so only your frames remain. Minified production logs work too: frames are resolved through your build's source maps back to original file:line positions, with recovery guidance when no maps are available.
  • Operate (Kubernetes) — the IDE becomes the ops window for the app you're editing: a Kubernetes dashboard through your own kubectl and kubeconfig, so every SSO/OIDC setup that works in your terminal works here (Okta/Dex, Azure kubelogin, EKS, GKE, OpenShift, ...). Workloads with per-kind health and rollout history, pods with container-level failure reasons, services & ingress, config (secret values never fetched; ConfigMap values on demand), events, and bounded logs with live following — every view showing the exact kubectl command it ran. Click-driven operations: rollout restart / undo / pause / resume / status, scale, run a CronJob now, delete pod, apply manifest, port-forward manager, and exec / ephemeral debug containers delegated to the IDE Terminal — every write confirms with the exact command, and a read-only mode hides them all. Production-context guards built in; the plugin never mutates your kubeconfig and opens no network connections itself.
  • Automate — one-click Quality Gate pre-commit scan, mock-server launcher, API mock generator from your services, and AI Prompt export: 22 scan types rendered as structured markdown ready to paste into any AI assistant.
  • Agent tools — an opt-in MCP server exposes read-only analysis tools (project overview, component relations, performance insights, signal graph, dependency-injection explain, route map, upgrade readiness, dependency freshness, health report, provenance trace, single-file inspection, role-based file lookup, unit-test generation, runtime-error analysis, Kubernetes run-state, pod logs) to MCP-compatible AI agents. It binds to loopback only, is off until you start it, and issues named, individually revocable tokens stored in the IDE password safe.
  • Provenance X-Ray — put the caret on any member and trace where its value comes from, hop by hop across files: signal and computed sources, aliases, injected services, inherited members, and HTTP endpoints named with their method and URL. Unresolvable chains report the reason rather than guessing.
  • Upgrade readiness — the official angular.dev update-guide steps for your exact from→to jump, filtered by your workspace's real dependencies, from a bundled snapshot refreshed weekly; plus per-major breaking-changes and ng update migration catalogs, the official release schedule (how long your major stays supported), runtime-floor blockers (Node / TypeScript / RxJS / zone.js), removed-API usage detection, and tsc vs tsgo (TypeScript 7) / experimental-vs-stable zoneless awareness. Manual override at Settings → Tools → Angular Architect.

Works with module, feature-directory, standalone, and monorepo layouts. Requires the bundled JavaScript and TypeScript plugin (IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate / WebStorm 2025.2+).
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.6.3

  • Kubernetes log views. With several log views side by side, Fetch, Follow and the search field no longer disappear, and a log moved into its own window no longer shows a gap: each view has three fixed rows, and the display options are compact icon buttons. Changing the pod clears a container that pod does not have, which used to make Fetch and Follow fail with "container not found". A pod list refresh no longer switches a view to another pod, and the pod and container fields can be searched by typing.

1.6.2

This release adds support for workspaces that contain apps on different Angular versions. All features are still free, and the freemium date has not been set yet.

  • Per-app Angular version. The version is now detected for each app from its nearest package.json (installed version first, then the lockfile, then the declared range). Before, it was read once for the whole IDE project. Inspections, intentions, generators and the status bar widget use the version of the file you are working in. You can override the version per app under Settings → Tools → Angular Architect → Version Handling.
  • Undetected version. If the version cannot be detected, the plugin no longer assumes Angular 22. Version-specific inspections stay off, advice is limited to what is valid on all versions, and generators ask which version to target.
  • Inspection fixes. Version thresholds were checked against Angular's API metadata for 12 to 22 and several were wrong. HttpClientModule is reported from Angular 18 (was 16). Class-based guards are reported on 15 to 17, and only CanLoad from 18. APIs removed in Angular 20 are reported as errors. Signal migration suggestions start at the minor that introduced each API (input() 17.1, model() 17.2, output() 17.3). The standalone (19), zoneless (21) and OnPush (22) defaults are taken into account.
  • Angular 20 file names. Components named user.ts, without the .component suffix, are now recognised by the component catalog, Suggestions, Performance, the Quality Gate and Dead Routes. Files named user-module.ts or price-pipe.ts are recognised as well. Generators write these names in apps that use them (based on angular.json, the app's existing files, or its Angular version), and Rename Component works on them. Generating through the Angular CLI also works on Angular 20 and later.
  • App dropdown. In a workspace with several Angular apps, a dropdown above the Health, Quality, Catalog and Insights tabs selects the app they show, or all apps. The selection is shared between the tabs. It is not shown when the project has one app. Test runner, TypeScript version, selector prefix, coverage reports and dependencies are read from the selected app instead of the project root.
  • Scans. Suggestions, Performance, Health and the migration scans run separately for each app, using that app's Angular and RxJS versions. Fix hints only mention APIs available in that version, for example takeUntilDestroyed from 16 and firstValueFrom with RxJS 7. Three incorrect hints were fixed. The scans also understand inject() fields, createActionGroup, selectSignal() and routes passed to provideRouter().
  • Generators. Output depends on the Angular version of the target folder: no standalone property before 14, styleUrls before 17, HttpClientTestingModule in specs before 15, resource({ params }) from 20. The Signal Form generator was rewritten for the Angular 21 API (form(model, (path) => …), [formField]). Generator output is test-compiled against Angular 12, 19 and 21.
  • Live templates and Quick Actions. Templates and actions that need a newer API are hidden in apps on an older version, e.g. input(), @if and linkedSignal in an Angular 15 app.
  • Architecture tab. Code examples match the Angular version of the app selected in the dropdown, and sections the app does not use (NgModules, NgRx, Signals before 16) are collapsed. Added a Signals & Reactivity section.
  • Health. New categories: vulnerable dependencies, support status of the Angular major, and use of deprecated Angular, RxJS, NgRx and Material APIs. Test coverage is read from the Istanbul or lcov report if there is one. Suggestions can recommend httpResource() / resource() on Angular 19 and later.
  • Unit tests. Generated specs and the "Create spec file" quick fix use the app's Angular version, test runner and RxJS version. Guard specs now compile on Angular 22, where CanMatchFn has a third argument.
  • Templates. Binding validation supports input and output aliases, transform, outputFromObservable, inputs: [] and host directives. The accessibility and control-flow migration checks also read inline templates. The nested template check counts *ngIf and *ngFor.
  • Intentions and Error Analysis. Inject Service, Connect to Store and Dispatch Action work in classes that use inject(), and Dispatch Action supports createActionGroup. Error Analysis fix steps depend on the app's Angular version and on whether the component is standalone.
  • Kubernetes dashboard. The Logs pane can show up to four pod logs at once, side by side or stacked, and a log can be moved into its own window. Log search highlights matches as you type, counts them, and can hide the lines that do not match; typing in it no longer moves the cursor to the log. Workloads refreshes with two kubectl calls instead of seven, and switching panes no longer reloads a pane that was just loaded. View Values shows a ConfigMap's keys and values as a table; before, it showed the same YAML as View YAML. In the tool window, typing in the Namespace field filters the list, the list is loaded when you connect, and a namespace you pick applies to the open dashboard straight away.
  • MCP. check_upgrade_readiness and check_dependency_freshness accept an app argument for workspaces with several apps.
  • Other fixes. Routes with a function redirectTo are no longer reported as dead. A guard call inside a route no longer breaks route relations. Code Review no longer reads inline templates as TypeScript. The Missing template and Missing style messages show the file name again. The API Catalog detects inject(HttpClient), httpResource() and fetch(). The default dev-server command uses the project's package manager and dev script. AI prompts include the Angular version. The notice that @angular-devkit/build-angular is deprecated now appears only for apps on Angular 22 or later. Services written with Angular 22's @Service() decorator are recognised as services. The Unit Tests tab imports an Angular 20 guard under its real name. Generated file names follow what most of the app's files use, not one old file. The component catalog lists each app's components when several apps use the same selector.
  • Catalog update. Bundled Angular metadata updated to 20.3.33, 21.2.25 and 22.2.1. No API removals, no new deprecations, and no change to the Node, TypeScript or RxJS minimums.

1.6.1

The IDE becomes the ops window for the app you're building: a new Kubernetes panel. Heads-up, stated upfront: the new Kubernetes panel is planned to join the premium tier when the freemium model launches (date to be announced) — until then it is included free, and everything else remains free as before.

  • Kubernetes panel. Connect through your own kubectl and kubeconfig — every SSO/OIDC exec-plugin setup your terminal supports works unchanged — or a service-account token kept in the IDE password safe. A dashboard popup shows workloads with per-kind health, pods with container-level failure reasons (CrashLoopBackOff, last exit codes), services & ingress, config keys (secret values are never fetched), events, and bounded logs with previous-container support. Click-driven operations too: rollout restart / undo / pause / resume and one-shot status, scale, Run Job Now (trigger a CronJob on demand), delete pod, Apply Manifest, ConfigMap value viewer, live log following, a port-forward manager whose sessions die with the project, and Exec / Debug that open an IDE Terminal tab pre-running kubectl exec -it or an ephemeral kubectl debug container — every write shows the exact command and always asks first, and a read-only mode hides them entirely. Polished like an IDE tool: color-coded status cells, row context menus and double-click shortcuts, selection that survives auto-refresh, kind-aware button enablement, a data-freshness stamp, and F5 / Ctrl+F shortcuts. Workload rows link to the repo YAML that defines them, manifests with server-unserved apiVersions are flagged, and two read-only MCP tools (get_kubernetes_status, get_pod_logs) expose the same facts to AI agents. Every view shows the exact kubectl command it ran.
  • The panel always names the cluster it targets. If you leave the context blank, Connect resolves your kubeconfig's current context once and pins it for the session, so a kubectl config use-context elsewhere can't silently retarget the panel — same buttons, different cluster.
  • Exec tells you when it can't work. kubectl exec needs a running container, so on a crash-looping pod it fails with container not found. The panel now warns first and points at Debug, which attaches an ephemeral container and works on crashed and distroless pods.
  • The dashboard follows the IDE's UI guidelines. Platform tables with actionable empty states and speed search, numeric and duration sorting, disabled buttons that say what they need, failures that keep your last good rows and explain themselves, destructive confirmations that name the verb, a header refresh interval, logs with wrap/find/scroll-lock/copy, View YAML on every resource row and Events on pod and workload rows, and a Connect you can cancel.
  • Error Analysis curates NG0600 against Angular's new documentation. Angular now documents "Signal write in a disallowed context", taking the NG error reference to 61 codes; the curated entry adds the trigger the doc names alongside computed() — a template binding that calls a method which writes a signal.
  • Bundled Angular catalogs follow Angular 22.2. Every v22 entry point advances to 22.2.0, v20 to 20.3.32 and v21 to 21.2.24, with the runtime-floor matrix following and no floor moved. The v22 router surface makes withRouterResources, nonBlocking and withAutoCleanupInjectors public, and withExperimentalAutoCleanupInjectors is flagged as deprecated in favour of the latter. The Material schematic surface and its bundled templates re-stamp at 22.2.0 with every template unchanged.

1.6.0

Data refresh and platform compatibility. The freemium heads-up stands: nothing changes in this release, every feature remains free, and the switch date will be announced.

  • Error Analysis names the error that hides behind a later symptom. The NG error reference gains NG01354 ("NgModel in child component cannot reach parent form") and NG0991 ("Resource completed before producing a value"), taking it to 60 codes. NG0991 is curated rather than passed through: an Observable-backed rxResource or httpResource that completes without emitting throws only when something later reads it, so the stack lands nowhere near the cause. The entry names the real culprits — an HttpInterceptor returning catchError(() => EMPTY), the same operator inside the resource's own stream, or a combined Observable with no startWith(…) to guarantee a first value — and leads with letting the error through rather than hiding it.
  • Ready for IntelliJ IDEA 2026.3. The message bundle no longer extends DynamicBundle through the constructor deprecated in that release — the one deprecated platform API the Marketplace verifier flagged against the 2026.3 EAP. No message or call site changed.
  • Bundled Angular catalogs track the latest patch lines. Every v20 entry point advances to 20.3.31, v21 to 21.2.23, and v22 to 22.1.7 (@angular/ssr runs a step ahead at 20.3.37 / 21.2.24 / 22.1.8), with the runtime-floor matrix following; the v22 router surface gains ResourceContext and ResourceResult; the Material schematic surface and its bundled templates re-stamp at 22.1.7 with every template content hash unchanged; and @ngrx/schematics advances to 22.0.1 — across a major boundary that added, removed, and renamed nothing the generators drive. No public API removed, no new deprecations, and no Node/TypeScript/RxJS floor changed.

1.5.7

Error Analysis learns to read production stacks. The freemium heads-up stands: nothing changes in this release, every feature remains free, and the switch date will be announced in the coming months.

  • Error Analysis decodes production stacks. Minified main.*.js frames from a pasted production console log are resolved through your build's source maps into the same clickable file:line evidence dev-mode logs get — with clear recovery guidance (and a "Load Source Maps…" picker) when the maps aren't in dist/.

Release notes for earlier versions (1.0.0–1.5.6) are available on the plugin’s Marketplace version history.

idea-plugin.name: Vesper
idea-plugin.description:
Peppermint and orange flavored dark theme for JetBrains IDEs.
Port of the Vesper VSCode theme by Rauno Freiberg.
Works in IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, PhpStorm, RubyMine, GoLand, CLion, Rider, DataGrip, and other IntelliJ Platform IDEs.
idea-plugin.change-notes: • 0.0.1 Initial release. One-to-one port of Vesper from VSCode.

idea-plugin.name: Tabular Eye
idea-plugin.description:
Renders certain code blocks in two columns without adding whitespace and supports proportional fonts.

  • JS/TS/JSON object literals
  • JS/TS 2D arrays
  • JS/TS imports
  • JS/TS single line if chains
  • TS interfaces
  • CSS properties
  • Python dataclasses
  • Python dictionary literals
  • Python keyword args
  • YAML objects
  • YAML lists (for non-monospace fonts)
  • Nginx directives
  • SQL tables
  • C and Go (for non-monospace fonts on already whitespace tabularized code)

Syntax Eye: There's another settings panel, which lets you add a configurable syntax highlight style (Faint Text) to a list of a words you can specify. For example, in the nginx code base, there are a lot of NGX_ prefixes, so I make them faint so I can scan the code faster.

idea-plugin.name: Tailwind Eye
idea-plugin.description:
Use the shortcut Shift + Alt + F to toggle between the two modes:

  • Fade non-styling code: Fades everything except className attributes.
  • Fold className content: Folds the actual Tailwind utility strings.

Cmd+Shift+I toggles inline<->multiline classNames
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Initial scaffold created from IntelliJ Platform Plugin Template

idea-plugin.name: Solstice Pro
idea-plugin.description:
Solstice Pro is the animated companion for Solstice Themes. It requires the free theme plugin, keeps the Moon, Sun, and Star palettes, and adds a lightweight harbor layer that makes TODOs, bugs, ideas, and review notes easier to notice while you work.

The Marketplace screenshots may look different because each Solstice theme has its own full palette: Moon is cool blue, Sun is warm amber, and Star is deep violet. Pro features adapt to those themes instead of forcing one fixed look everywhere.

Color previews:

Solstice Sun - warm amber tabs, dark espresso editor surfaces, and copper-orange syntax accents.

Solstice Star - deep violet panels, lavender keywords, gold highlights, and a softer cosmic contrast.

Solstice Moon - cool blue sidebars, crisp cyan syntax, rose keywords, and a clean midnight editor tone.

Visual workflow features:

  • Status bar harbor pulse - a compact animated horizon with sun, moon, shimmering stars, moving water, and ripples that react softly to editor activity.
  • Editor marker badges - JetBrains-style gutter labels and tinted editor rows for explicit Solstice.BUG, Solstice.TODO, Solstice.IDEA, and Solstice.REVIEW comments so important lines stand out without taking over the editor.
  • Solstice Markers tool window - a compact marker board with priority cards, filtered counts, a cinematic harbor overview, and fast jumps back to tagged lines.

Pro feature previews:

Solstice Marker Board - compact marker counts, priority cards, a cinematic harbor overview, gutter markers, and selected marker details in one tool window.

Solstice marker actions - right-click selected code to quickly tag it as Solstice.BUG, Solstice.TODO, Solstice.IDEA, or Solstice.REVIEW.

Marker workflow features:

  • Right-click selected code and mark it as Solstice.BUG, Solstice.TODO, Solstice.IDEA, or Solstice.REVIEW.
  • Open the Solstice Markers tool window to scan all tagged lines, filter by marker type, and jump back to the source.
  • Use marker gutter actions to show details, copy marker text, move between nearby markers, or list all markers in the current file.

idea-plugin.name: StyleBop
idea-plugin.description:
Open the current CSS file or workspace folder in StyleBop — a visual macOS editor for stylesheets.

Right-click any .css file or folder and pick Open in StyleBop. The app launches, opens the project, and lands on the construct your cursor was on — a ruleset opens the Rulesets canvas, a @keyframes rule opens the Animations tab, a custom property opens the Tokens tab, and so on.

Requires macOS and a StyleBop install.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.0

  • Initial release. Right-click .css files or folders to open them in StyleBop.
  • Cursor line is forwarded so the smart-router can open the matching visual surface.

idea-plugin.name: Token Flow
idea-plugin.description:
Make using your tokens intuitive.
Token Flow helps you find the right variable and keep your styles flawless without ever leaving your IntelliJ code.

Token Flow indexes your whole Design System and makes token usage fluid, fast and error-proof.
Supported formats: SCSS variables, CSS Custom Properties, SCSS Maps, TS/JS preset objects, React Native runtime themes and helpers.

Superpowers for Front-end Developers

  • Instant Search (Library)
    A dedicated side panel to find tokens by name, value or category.
    Includes visual swatches and drag-and-drop support.
  • Smart Swapping (Alt+T)
    Need a slightly darker blue or the next spacing scale?
    Token Flow suggests siblings based on HSL proximity, logical order, or scale steps for callable helpers like spacing().
  • Zero "Magic Numbers"
    The IDE flags hardcoded hex codes, pixels or unitless numbers that match an existing token — one click and your code is clean.
  • Inline Suggestions
    As you type a value, matching tokens appear without stealing focus.
  • Deep Context
    Hover any token to see its resolved value, aliases and per-mode variants (Dark / Light / breakpoints).
  • One-click Copy (⌘/Ctrl+Shift+Click)
    Hold the modifier and click any token reference to instantly copy its resolved value. For colours, also pick HEX, RGB, HSL or OKLCH from a tiny dropdown — no hover, no panel, no detour.
  • Full-scale Audit
    An "Analyse" tab grades your project health.
    Identify tech debt, unused tokens and hardcoded clusters in seconds.

Real-world Use Cases

  • Rapid Integration — code a UI component without leaving the current file to check the token naming convention.
  • Theme Debugging — see instantly how a token resolves in Dark vs Light mode via the hover popup.
  • System Migration — refactor legacy CSS/SCSS by detecting every hardcoded value that should have been a token.
  • Consistency Check — keep multi-brand projects aligned with Scopes to isolate tokens per platform or sub-project.

Made by

Robin Lopez — designer & front-end engineer.
robinlopez.fr · LinkedIn · Bluesky · Bento
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.2.4 — Tighter Library, fewer false positives

  • Excluded files are really out of reach: a file listed in a scope's Excludes tab (typically a primitives.scss living next to your semantic tokens) no longer appears in the Library, in code completion, in the pickers, nor as a replacement suggestion. Its tokens stay indexed on purpose, so a semantic token aliasing one keeps its resolved value and colour swatch — removing the file from Sources used to hide the primitives but break that preview. Reading a primitive already present in the code still works (hover, go-to-declaration, copy value, gutter colour).
  • The Library can follow your caret: new option Filter the Library by the category of the token under the caret (Settings → Tools → Token Flow → Triggers → Library panel). Put the caret on gap: var(--spacing-default) and the Library narrows to your spacing tokens; on a plain value the CSS property is used instead. A dismissible chip left of the search field shows the active category. Off by default.

0.2.4 — Fewer false positives in Broken References

  • '{name}' placeholders are no longer broken references: a brace-string passed to a string / i18n helper (replace, split, t, instant, format…) or whose name sits outside the project's token vocabulary ({user.name}, {first}) is not a token reference. template.replace('{first}', …) no longer reports phantom broken tokens nor inflates the coverage ratio.
  • Real typos still surface: {color.primry} and {colr.primary} are still reported. var(--…), $var and dt('…') are unchanged.
  • Reminder: a var(--x, fallback) on a variable that intentionally never exists (a component's customisation API) is still flagged — declare its prefix under Settings → Tools → Token Flow → Scopes → External prefixes to make it neutral.

0.2.3 — Copy token values straight from the editor

  • Modifier+click to copy: hold ⌘/Ctrl + Shift and click a token reference (var(--…), $spacing-xl, '{…}') to open a dropdown and copy its resolved value in one click — alias chains are followed to the primitive.
  • Colour notations on demand: for colour tokens the dropdown also offers the resolved colour as HEX, RGB, HSL and OKLCH, plus the token reference itself.
  • Configurable shortcut: change the modifier combo (or turn the feature off) under Settings → Tools → Token Flow.

0.2.2 - Smarter Indexing & Fewer False Positives

  • The TS/JS and SCSS parsers now automatically filter out non-style objects, JSON schemas, test/Storybook files, and local SCSS variables, drastically reducing noise without requiring any manual configuration. Even inside a real token object, non-style entries (labels, variant names) are dropped — only actual style values are indexed.
  • BEM modifier syntax in selectors (e.g. .card__slot--closeable:hover or the SCSS parent-ref &--selected:not(.x)) is no longer mistaken for a CSS custom-property declaration. -- is only treated as a token when it really is one — a property declaration or a var(--…) call.
  • No more circular suggestions: a token definition (e.g. --color-bg-page: #e5e9eb) no longer suggests replacing its own value with itself. The token being declared is excluded from its own suggestion list.
  • The Analyser's Scope picker no longer offers the confusing Active editor option. The analysed scope is now an explicit choice (All project by default, plus your configured scopes) and stays put as you move between files. The Library and Hardcoded Values panels still follow the active editor.

0.2.1 — Smarter hardcoded detection, sticky section headers

  • Token definitions no longer flagged as hardcoded values: literals declared inside token sources are now correctly recognised as definitions and excluded from Hardcoded clusters and Hardcoded values. Covers JSON / TS / JS token catalogs, SCSS variables, CSS custom properties, and quoted object keys like "sm": "8px" or "borderRadius": "8px".
  • Format-aware token suggestions in TS / JS files: when a hardcoded literal is detected inside .ts / .tsx / .js / .jsx files, the analyser now only suggests token usages that are actually valid in those environments. CSS custom-property suggestions (var(--…)) are no longer proposed in runtime-only contexts.
  • Accurate hardcoded hit counts: the analyser now reports the real number of detected Hardcoded clusters and Hardcoded values. The previous internal 50-item truncation has been removed, while UI collapsing is still handled through the expandable + N more… control.
  • Sticky section headers while scrolling: long analysis reports now keep the current section title and count pinned at the top of the panel, making navigation easier while reviewing large reports.
  • Broken references promoted to top priority: the Broken references section now appears first in the report so unresolved var(--…) and $var usages surface immediately as actionable bugs before lower-priority hardcoded issues.
  • Cleaner occurrence rows: expanded hardcoded entries now display occurrences as filename:line · property for faster scanning. The associated CSS or JS property is shown directly, repeated folder names were removed, and long filenames are no longer clipped by a fixed-height row layout.
  • Pure token source files excluded from scans: registered token catalog files (.ts, .tsx, .js, .jsx, .json) are now fully ignored during hardcoded analysis to eliminate false positives coming from design-token definitions.

0.2.0 — Sharper Analyser, contextual CSS-var discovery

  • Hardcoded results split into two lists: the Analyser now separates Hardcoded clusters (repeated literals with NO matching token — opportunities to extend the DS) from Hardcoded values (literals where a token already exists — pure actionable debt). Values are grouped by (value + property family) so 12px on a padding and 12px on a font-size show up separately, each with its own role-aware token suggestion. New Hardcoded opportunity + Hardcoded debt score axes replace the previous single pressure axis.
  • Sharper suggestion engine: typography and border tokens no longer cross-suggest on width / height / padding / radius contexts, even when the token name's leading segment looks metric (--size-typography-title-md is no longer offered for width: 20px). Both category and name are checked. Token-tier classification also handles dot-separated names (units.sm) so primitives are correctly outranked by semantics. Analyser scope selector stays sticky across editor switches.
  • Ambiguous token detection: new informational section in the Analyser surfaces tokens whose name plausibly maps to more than one value family — typography-leaning words holding a colour (--text-default: #45566), --icon-* holding a raw length, or pure role names (--primary, --default) carrying no category hint. Surfaced as suggestions, not errors.
  • Alt+T on a contextually-declared CSS variable now lists its declaration sites: instead of the historical "No alternatives found" dead-end, the popup shows every place the variable is set — file, line, raw value, innermost CSS selector, plus a colour swatch when the value parses as a colour. Covers consumer overrides, Angular host bindings ([style.--c]), React/Vue inline styles, and DOM setProperty calls.

0.1.9 — Smarter broken-reference detection

  • CSS variables declared outside token sources are no longer flagged as broken: Token Flow now picks up two new families of declaration. Runtime injection from component code — Angular [style.--var] host bindings, React/Vue inline-style object keys, setProperty('--var', …) calls. Contextual CSS overrides — any --name: value declaration in any .css/.scss/.sass/.vue rule body, so the CSS Custom Property API pattern (generic component reads var(--c, fallback), consumers set --c locally) just works.
  • Fallbacks no longer hide missing variables: var(--x, inherit) is still flagged when --x is nowhere to be found — a runtime default is not a license to leave a dangling reference.
  • New setting: Settings → Token Flow → Analyser → "Recognise CSS variables declared outside token sources". On by default; uncheck to revert to the strict pre-0.1.9 behaviour.

0.1.8 — Sharper token suggestions (tier & role aware)

  • External token prefixes (per scope): new External tab in Settings → Token Flow → Scopes for CSS-var prefixes injected at runtime by an external framework : PrimeNG --p-, Ionic --ion-, Angular Material --mat-, Material Web --mdc-, Vuetify --v-, Bootstrap --bs-, Radix --radix-, Quasar --q-, Element Plus --el-, Mantine, Carbon, … References matching a configured prefix are never flagged as broken by the Analyser or the Hardcoded Values panel.
  • Auto-detect from package.json: one-click button in the External tab that scans the project for known framework dependencies and adds their prefixes to the scope.
  • Project-open detection notification: opening a project that depends on a known UI framework but has no prefixes configured surfaces a balloon offering Add to all scopes / Configure… / Don't show again. One-shot — never nags twice.
  • JSON config v2: exports/imports now carry externalPrefixes per scope. v1 files remain importable.
  • Hardcoded Values : token-source files are skipped: opening a file declared in any scope's sourcePaths now shows an explanatory banner and disables the scan. No more flagging of --units-xl: 32px; as hardcoded when the file's purpose is to declare it.
  • Hardcoded Values : SCSS map values are no longer flagged: literals inside a $name: (…) or "key": (…) SCSS map (Style-Dictionary / theme-config pattern) are recognised as token definitions and skipped. Handles nested maps to any depth, even when the file isn't formally declared as a token source — useful for mixed files.
  • Hardcoded Values : search & property filter: new search field filters rows by literal, selector, surrounding CSS property, or suggested token (multi-term, case-insensitive). A filter button opens a popup with every detected CSS property grouped by category (Spacing, Color, Radius…), with counts, and a nested search to narrow the property checklist. The previous toolbar toggle "Hide rows without a token suggestion" moves into this popup.
  • Token tier awareness: when several DS tokens share the same value (--units-xl and --spacing-xl both 32px), the suggestion engine now prefers the semantic token over the primitive one. Primitive prefixes recognised: units-, palette-, base-, primitive-, core-, scale-, raw-. So padding: 32px now suggests var(--spacing-xl) instead of var(--units-xl).
  • Property-to-role matching for colors: background, color, border-color, box-shadow… now derive an expected role (surface / content / stroke / effect) and match it against token-name segments. Tokens carrying the right role get a strong boost; tokens carrying a conflicting role are demoted. So background: #005bff prefers token-actions-high-surface-default over global-default-content-default, and color: #001a70 does the opposite.
  • Multi-criterion ranking: the suggestion score was rewritten as a weighted combination of (category, role, tier, exact-vs-fuzzy, length). Token-name length is now only a tiebreaker — a longer-but-more-semantic name can outrank a shorter primitive one, which was impossible before.
  • Fuzzy color tiebreaking: when no exact color match exists, ties at near-identical RGB distance are broken by the semantic score so the role-appropriate token surfaces first.

0.1.7 — Portable scope configuration, smarter Library & Vue SFCs

  • Vue Single File Components (.vue): tokens declared in <style> and <style lang="scss"> blocks of a Vue SFC are now indexed, listed in the Library, counted in audit coverage, and benefit from hardcoded-value detection / completion / Alt+T / Go-to-declaration. Text-based implementation — no dependency on the Vue plugin — so it works on Community and Ultimate. Scanning is confined to inline style blocks, so <template> and <script> sections stay untouched.
  • Export Config: Settings → Token Flow → Scopes now has an Export… link that writes the current scopes to a JSON file. Share it with the team, commit it next to the project, or keep it as a backup.
  • Import Config: paired Import… link reads a JSON file produced by Export. The plugin asks whether to Replace the current scopes or Merge (existing scopes with the same name are overwritten, new ones are appended). Pending edits are persisted via Apply, so a teammate can preview the import before committing.
  • Versioned format: the JSON file carries a schema version. Older Token Flow builds refuse files produced by a future schema instead of silently dropping fields.
  • Library family / sub-family grouping: inside each big category accordion, the Library can now insert a two-level hierarchy of headers — family (HIGH, LOW, PRIMARY) and sub-family (SURFACE, CONTENT, STROKE, …) — derived from the structure of token names alone. No hard-coded vocabulary; the algorithm adapts to any naming convention. Tokens indent under their header so the alignment reads like a tree. New toolbar toggle (group-by icon) next to the view-mode button; off by default — opt in from the panel.
  • Sticky category header: scroll past a category and its header pins to the top of the Library viewport, with the same chevron behaviour as the in-list row.
  • Justified category bar: layout is now [chevron] TITLE … (count), with the count badge tinted so it can't be mistaken for a resolved token value.
  • Two-way kind / file-chip sync: ticking a token-kind in the Library filter popup now flips every file chip of that kind in the strip below the search bar, and vice-versa — the two filter surfaces no longer drift.
  • Variant tooltip — vertical layout: per-variant tooltips now render one line per variant (label left, swatch / glyph + value right) instead of a wide horizontal table that overflowed once a token had several variants. Multi-theme tokens get discrete theme subheaders.
  • Hardcoded Values — tighter rows & hide-no-match filter: rows nest under their selector header, the literal column is narrower, the suggestion combo is taller (no more clipped descenders), and a new toolbar toggle hides literals without any matching token (on by default — broken references stay visible because they're actionable).
  • Light-theme polish: Library category / family / sub-family palette rebuilt with proper light-vs-dark contrast steps (the previous sub-family pair was inverted), and the dark bands that appeared behind separator headers on light themes are gone — gridContainer, the sticky header and the grid viewport now follow list.background.

0.1.6 — Smarter Library, sharper Analyser

  • Multi-term Library search: "informative content" now finds --token-informative-highlight-content-hover. Search splits on spaces/dashes/underscores, every term must match.
  • Library kind filter: the funnel popup gets a Token kind section (CSS / SCSS / JS-JSON) above Families. The button highlights when any filter is active.
  • Context-aware JS token drop: drag or paste a '{path}' token inside a backtick template literal in TS/JS and it lands as ${dt('path')} (or dt('path') inside an existing ${…}).
  • Stale-analysis banner: after a run, the Analyser watches every file referenced by the report; editing one surfaces a yellow banner offering one-click re-run.
  • Reorderable scopes: up/down arrows in Settings, order reflected immediately in the Analyser scope picker.
  • Excluded from Analysis (per scope): new Excludes tab to carve unrelated sub-modules out of a wide scope root.
  • Tabbed scope detail: Sources / Whitelist / Excludes split into tabs — no more vertical scroll in the Settings dialog.
  • Cleaner Analyser toolbar: redundant Refresh / Re-sync scopes removed; the single action flips to Re-run analysis once a report exists.
  • Alt+T preserves dt(…): picking an alternative on ${dt('token.x.y')} no longer rewrites it into a bare Style-Dictionary alias and breaks the surrounding template literal.

0.1.5 — Broken-reference detection & sharper suggestions

  • Broken Reference Detection: the Analyser lists token references that don't resolve (var(--foo), '{token.x.y}', dt('x.y')) in a dedicated section, and the Hardcoded Values panel flags them inline with a yellow warning. A new Reference integrity axis (20 % weight) joins the global score.
  • Resilient JS/TS reference matching: alt+T, completion and go-to now resolve Style-Dictionary refs like '{token.modeLight.informative.default.high.surface.default}' against canonical tokens — leading export binding (token.), mode segment (modeLight / modeDark) and a single camelCase merge / split per path (default.high ↔ defaultHigh) are all tolerated.
  • CSS var() inside TS template literals: alt+T now recognises var(--name) inside backtick strings in .ts/.tsx; CSS functional notations (var, calc, rgb*, hsl*, gradients, transforms) are no longer mistaken for JS helper calls.
  • Category-scoped suggestions: padding: 6px no longer suggests a 6 px shadow-blur token. The value index is keyed by (category, value) with controlled fallback inside the length family (SPACING, RADIUS, SIZING, TYPOGRAPHY, BORDER).
  • Smarter incoherence judgement: --stroke-default: 1px is no longer flagged when the categorizer has already reconciled the name/value clash (here: BORDER).
  • Ignored library files: new Settings list to exclude vendored design-system packages from the analyser.
  • Scanner refinements: values inside comments and inside var(--x, fallback) fallbacks are no longer reported. Standard CSS named colors are detected. Circular token definitions are no longer flagged as hardcoded.
  • UI polish: scope display in the Hardcoded Values panel, scope info right-aligned in toolbars, expandable long Analyser sections, fixed accordion-gap inflation, "Non-existent tokens" renamed to "Broken references".
  • API hygiene: removed all usages of IntelliJ APIs marked deprecated or scheduled-for-removal so the plugin loads cleanly on the latest IDE builds.

0.1.4 — Visual Grid & Polished UX

  • Design System Dashboard - Grid View: New visual mode representing tokens as beautiful, interactive cards. Includes visual previews for colors, spacing, and radius.
  • Smarter Categorization: Added 6 new categories (EFFECTS, LAYOUT, BORDER, etc.) and refined the engine to flawlessly classify complex semantic tokens.
  • Contextual Scope Awareness: The Dashboard and Analyser now dynamically track and display your currently edited file's scope.

0.1.3 — Gutter swatches & SCSS modifiers

  • Gutter color swatches for SCSS: variables ($name) now display a color preview icon in the gutter, resolving through the project index (consistent with native CSS variables).
  • Robust SCSS/CSS parsing: modifiers like !default, !global, and !important are now stripped during extraction, fixing color previews and alias resolution for flagged tokens.

0.1.2 — React Native support

  • React Native runtime themes: property-access tokens (colors.PRIMARY_500, theme.radius.sm, fontPresets.h1.fontSize) are now detected. Typed export const X: Type = {…} aggregators contribute leaf paths only (aligned with barrel re-exports); bare const X = {…} bags keep their prefix. Cross-object alias resolution included.
  • Callable helpers (spacing, radius, …): linear arrow functions like (v) => UNIT * v are indexed with a ƒ badge. Hardcoded 12 now suggests spacing(1.5). Alt+T on spacing(0.5) opens a scale popup (spacing(0.25), spacing(0.5), spacing(1), spacing(1.5), …).
  • Unitless numerics flagged: fontSize: 34, lineHeight: 24, opacity: 0.5 now inspected against the token index (JS/TS only). Numbers inside a helper call are ignored to avoid noise.
  • Suggest matching tokens as you type: the value-completion popup no longer steals editor focus — typing keeps going into the file.
  • Analyser respects the selected scope: file walk is restricted to the scope's rootPath; only the active scope's own catalogues are excluded. Scope changes in Settings refresh the picker live; a Re-sync action is available for manual cache drops.
  • Architecture: TS/JS parsing reorganised into a strategy package (StyleDictionaryParser, RuntimeObjectParser, RuntimeFunctionParser, registry to dispatch per file). Adding a new stack now means plugging in a single class.

0.1.1 — Polish & bug fixes

  • Hover popup — multi-theme grouping: tokens declared under nested SCSS maps ($themes-config -> "themeOne" -> "light" -> …) now render with theme-grouped column headers instead of a flat default | dark | light | dark sequence.
  • Settings — Scopes tab: long intro hints no longer trigger a horizontal scrollbar when the dialog is narrow; HTML paragraphs wrap properly inside the available width.
  • Marketplace metadata cleanup (vendor contact, simplified description).

0.1.0 — First public release

The first iteration of Token Flow ships everything you need to manage your Design System directly inside the IDE.

  • Multi-format indexer — SCSS, CSS, and TS/JS support with alias resolution.
  • Library Tool Window — Visual search, drag-and-drop, and navigation.
  • Alternatives Popup (Alt+T) — Smart sorting for colors and metrics.
  • Hardcoded Inspection — Automatic detection and quick-fix for literals.
  • Analyse Tab — Deep health report and technical debt tracking.
  • Scopes — Multi-UI project support.

idea-plugin.name: Trier - Tailwind CSS Toolkit
idea-plugin.description:
Trier is a Tailwind CSS productivity toolkit for JetBrains IDEs. Its free core keeps classes in the official Tailwind order with safe editor, Project View, folder, dry-run, diff, and selective apply workflows. Trier Plus adds focused tools for making dense Tailwind markup easier to read and work with, without handing whole files to Prettier.

Why Trier

  • Keep Tailwind class lists ordered without changing indentation, quotes, semicolons, wrapping, or unrelated code style.
  • Use the official Tailwind ordering from prettier-plugin-tailwindcss.
  • Review folder-wide changes before writing files with dry-run reports and JetBrains diffs.
  • Apply one file, selected files, selected directories, or all remaining dry-run changes.
  • Run class sorting manually, from Project View, on Save, or after the IDE Reformat Code action.

Trier Plus

  • Smart Folding visually collapses long Tailwind class lists without modifying source files.
  • Compact placeholders preserve useful group context, for example ... hover:... active:... disabled:....
  • Smart Wrapping turns supported static class lists into grouped multiline blocks through explicit editor actions.
  • Utility Lens shows resolved static Tailwind utility details as muted virtual values without changing source code.
  • Use Cmd+Option+. on macOS to toggle all Smart Folding regions in the current editor when Trier detects candidates.
  • Trier Plus features stay visible but locked when no Plus license is available.

Framework coverage

  • Sorting support for HTML, XML, JSX, TSX, CSS, and SCSS.
  • Vue, Svelte, Astro, Angular, Laravel Blade / PHP, and Twig.
  • Static classes, dynamic class bindings, helper calls, component class props, and @apply.
  • Custom attributes and helper functions such as data-classes, cn, clsx, or tw.

Safe by default

  • Unsupported or ambiguous framework syntax is preserved as no-op instead of being rewritten aggressively.
  • Manual Tailwind stylesheet/config paths always win, while blank settings are auto-detected per project.
  • The bundled sorter runtime means your project does not need local prettier dependencies.

Trier is designed for projects where Tailwind class lists live everywhere: templates, components, helper calls, style blocks, backend views, and framework-specific bindings.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Tailwind sorting now recovers after temporary runtime files are deleted.

  • Restores missing Trier engine and bundled runtime files automatically while the IDE is running.
  • Fixes repeated sorting failures across projects caused by a cached path to a deleted temporary engine file.
  • Fixes HTML/XML processing compatibility with IntelliJ IDEA 2026.3 EAP.

idea-plugin.name: Flexible For Base UI
idea-plugin.description:
Base UI helper with smart completion, auto-import, inline docs, drag-and-drop, live preview, and a full component browser.

This is an unofficial plugin for the love of the framework. Our goal is to make this the best development experience for JetBrains IDEs and your feedback is essential. Please leave a review, or reach out at info@ilscipio.com - we want to hear what works, what doesn't, and what you'd like to see next.

Core Features

Smart Completion

  • Component name completion - type < in any JSX/TSX file and get all Base UI components and subcomponents
  • Dot-notation support - complete Accordion.Root, Select.Trigger, Dialog.Portal and all other subcomponents
  • Auto-import - accepting a completion automatically inserts or updates the import { ... } from '@base-ui-components/react/...' statement
  • Works everywhere - .tsx, .jsx, .ts, and .js files

Hover Documentation

  • Inline docs - hover over any Base UI component tag or press F1/Ctrl+Q for full documentation
  • Props reference - see every prop with its type, required/optional status, and default value
  • Subcomponents list - instantly see all available subcomponents (e.g., Select has Root, Trigger, Value, Icon, Positioner, Popup, Item, and more)
  • Code examples - typical usage patterns shown directly in the popup
  • One-click navigation - link to the official base-ui.com documentation for each component

Component Browser

  • Visual browser in the right sidebar with all 37 components and 4 utilities
  • Category filtering - Form/Input, Navigation/Layout, Display/Overlay, Data Display
  • Live search - filter components by name as you type
  • Detail panel - click any component to see its description, full props table, subcomponents, and example code
  • Drag and drop - drag a component from the browser directly into your editor; the import statement is added automatically
  • Copy button - copy the code snippet to your clipboard with one click

Live Preview

  • JCEF-based preview - see a rendered preview of each component in the tool window
  • Theme switching - toggle between light and dark preview themes
  • Auto-sync - preview updates when you select a different component

Gutter Icons

  • Import markers - icons appear next to Base UI import statements in the editor gutter
  • Quick docs - click the icon to open the official documentation for that component in your browser

Settings

  • Configure at Settings > Tools > Flexible For Base UI
  • Toggle individual features: completion, documentation, line markers, live preview
  • Master enable/disable switch for the entire plugin

Supported Components

Form/Input (15)

Autocomplete, Button, Checkbox, CheckboxGroup, Field, Fieldset, Form, Input, NumberField, Radio, Select, Slider, Switch, Toggle, ToggleGroup

Navigation/Layout (4)

Collapsible, Menu, NavigationMenu, Toolbar

Display/Overlay (8)

Accordion, AlertDialog, Dialog, Drawer, Popover, PreviewCard, Toast, Tooltip

Data Display (6)

Avatar, Meter, Progress, ScrollArea, Separator, Tabs

Interactive (4)

Combobox, ContextMenu, Menubar, OTPField

Utilities (4)

CSPProvider, DirectionProvider, mergeProps, useRender

Getting Started

Quick Start

  1. Install the plugin from JetBrains Marketplace
  2. Open a React project with @base-ui-components/react in package.json
  3. Open the Base UI tool window from the right sidebar
  4. Browse components, drag them into your code, or type < in JSX/TSX for completion
  5. Hover over any Base UI tag for inline documentation

Productivity Tips

  • Type <Acc + Tab for instant Accordion completion with auto-import
  • Drag from browser to insert a full component snippet with import in one motion
  • Hover + click link to jump straight to base-ui.com docs for any component
  • F1 on a tag to open the full documentation popup with props and examples
  • Category dropdown in the browser to narrow down to Form, Navigation, Display, or Data components

Customization

  • Feature toggles: Settings > Tools > Flexible For Base UI
  • Line markers: enable/disable gutter icons next to imports
  • Live preview: enable/disable the JCEF preview panel

What's New in 2026.1.0

  • Initial release with component browser, smart completion, hover documentation, gutter icons, and drag-and-drop support for all 37 Base UI components and 4 utilities

See CHANGELOG.md for complete details.

Made by Developers with a Passion for Modern Web Development

We build developer tools and plugins as part of our technology stack and understand the unique needs of frontend engineers working with modern component libraries. We created this plugin to make Base UI development more intuitive and productive in JetBrains IDEs.

We're sharing this tool with the React community to support the ecosystem's growth and to make accessible component development more approachable.

idea-plugin.name: Flexible For Daisy UI
idea-plugin.description:
daisyUI autocomplete, component browser with live preview, themes, smart snippet insertion, drag-and-drop, and class inspections for all JetBrains IDEs.

We are a young, unofficial, community plugin. We like daisyUI and want to help you get started with it. If you have any questions, feature requests, or encounter a bug, reach out to us on GitHub, Ilscipio or email info@ilscipio.com.

Core Features

Smart Autocomplete

  • 440+ daisyUI classes with context-aware completion in HTML, JSX, Vue, CSS, and more
  • Component class groups - type btn and see btn-primary, btn-secondary, btn-outline, all size variants
  • Modifier classes - color, size, shape, and state modifiers with documentation
  • Works everywhere - class attributes, className props, template literals, Tailwind @apply

Component Browser

  • 65 production-ready components organized in 7 categories: Actions, Data Display, Navigation, Feedback, Data Input, Layout, and Mockup
  • Live JCEF preview - see exactly how each component renders before inserting
  • 35 built-in themes - switch preview between light, dark, cyberpunk, synthwave, and 31 more
  • Search and filter - quickly find components by name or category
  • Drag-and-drop or click Insert to add components directly into your editor

Smart Snippet Insertion

File-type-aware insertion that adapts to your project:

  • HTML files - auto-injects daisyUI CDN links into <head> and inserts the snippet at caret
  • JSX/TSX files - converts class to className, for to htmlFor, self-closes void elements
  • Vue SFC files - detects <template> section and inserts inside it, redirects if caret is elsewhere
  • CSS files - shows a warning instead of dumping raw HTML

Documentation on Hover

  • Instant docs for every daisyUI class - hover or Ctrl+Q to see description
  • Direct links to official daisyUI documentation pages
  • Category and type info - see whether a class is a component, modifier, or utility

Code Inspections

  • Unknown class detection - highlights typos and non-existent daisyUI class names
  • Quick navigation - Ctrl+Click on class names to jump to documentation

Getting Started

Quick Start

  1. Install from JetBrains Marketplace or Settings > Plugins > Marketplace and search "Flexible For Daisy UI"
  2. Open the Daisy UI Components tool window from the right sidebar
  3. Browse or search components, select one to see the live preview
  4. Click Insert or drag the component into your editor
  5. Switch themes in the preview dropdown to see how components adapt

Productivity Tips

  • Ctrl+Space in any class attribute for daisyUI completions
  • Ctrl+Q on a daisyUI class for instant documentation
  • Double-click a component in the browser to insert immediately
  • Ctrl+C with a component selected to copy the HTML to clipboard
  • Drag from browser to editor for quick insertion with smart file-type handling

Supported IDEs

Works with all JetBrains IDEs version 2023.3+: IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PhpStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, RubyMine, CLion, Rider, and Android Studio.

Requirements

No project configuration needed. The plugin bundles the complete daisyUI v5 class library and component definitions. Works with any project that uses daisyUI - no build tool integration required.

Bugs & Feature Requests

If you have questions, feature requests, or encounter a bug, reach out at Ilscipio or email info@ilscipio.com.

idea-plugin.name: Flexible For Mantine
idea-plugin.description:
Smart completion, hover docs, drag-and-drop, auto-imports, and inspections for Mantine. Drag-and-drop from the component browser to your editor.

We are an unofficial IDE extension, but love the framework. Please leave a review, reach out to us on GitHub or email and tell us your thoughts, issues and more.

Core Features

Component Browser

  • Categorized sidebar with all Mantine components grouped by function (View > Tool Windows > Mantine Components, or click the Mantine icon in the right sidebar)
  • Live preview with dark/light mode toggle showing rendered output for each component
  • Instant search - type in the search bar to filter across all components and hooks
  • Double-click or Enter on any component to insert its code at the caret position
  • Drag and drop components directly from the browser into your open editor
  • Automatic import placement - the import { Button } from "@mantine/core" line is inserted at the top of the file, merged with existing Mantine imports
  • Copy Code / Copy Import buttons for clipboard-based workflows

Smart Completion

  • Props completion - type <Button and press Ctrl+Space to see all available props with types and descriptions
  • Enum value completion - type variant=" and see all valid values: filled, light, outline, subtle, default, gradient, etc.
  • Mantine type support - completions for MantineColor (blue, red, grape, violet, ...), MantineSize (xs, sm, md, lg, xl), MantineRadius, and MantineSpacing
  • Compound components - works with dotted names like Tabs.Tab, Menu.Item, Accordion.Panel
  • Import completion - type from "@mantine/ to see all available packages and their exports
  • Works in .tsx, .jsx, .ts, and .js files

Hover Documentation

  • Ctrl+Q (or F1 on macOS) on any Mantine component tag for instant documentation
  • Props table with type, default value, and allowed values for each prop
  • Package badge showing which @mantine/* package the component belongs to
  • Direct link to the official mantine.dev documentation page for the component
  • Hover over any Mantine tag in the editor to see the documentation popup

Code Inspections

  • Unknown prop warnings - highlights misspelled or non-existent props on Mantine components
  • Smart filtering - skips standard React props (className, style, id, key, ref, data-, aria-)
  • Configure at Settings > Editor > Inspections > Mantine to adjust severity or disable

Import Management

  • Automatic placement - imports are inserted after the last existing import, or at the top of the file if none exist
  • Smart merging - inserting a Modal when you already have import { Button } from "@mantine/core" produces import { Button, Modal } from "@mantine/core" instead of a duplicate line
  • Type import support - handles import type { ... } statements separately from value imports
  • Line ending handling - correctly handles both LF and CRLF line endings
  • File type awareness - only adds ES6 imports in .tsx, .jsx, .ts, .js, .mjs, .mts files; skips .html and other non-module files

Supported Packages

  • @mantine/core - Button, TextInput, Select, Modal, Tabs, AppShell, Accordion, Card, and 60+ components
  • @mantine/hooks - useDisclosure, useForm, useMediaQuery, useClipboard, useDebouncedValue, and 20+ hooks
  • @mantine/dates - DateInput, DatePicker, DateTimePicker, Calendar, MonthPickerInput
  • @mantine/charts - AreaChart, BarChart, LineChart, PieChart, DonutChart, RadarChart
  • @mantine/notifications - Notification system with show/update/hide
  • @mantine/spotlight - Command palette / spotlight search
  • @mantine/carousel - Embla-based carousel with slide controls
  • @mantine/dropzone - File upload with MIME type filtering
  • @mantine/code-highlight - Syntax-highlighted code blocks
  • @mantine/tiptap - Rich text editor with Mantine styling

Compatibility

Works with all JetBrains IDEs that include JavaScript/TypeScript support:

  • WebStorm 2023.3+
  • IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate 2023.3+
  • PhpStorm 2023.3+

Requires the JavaScript plugin (bundled with the above IDEs).

Made by Developers Who Ship Production React Apps

We're sharing this tool with the Mantine community to support the ecosystem's growth and to help teams build better user interfaces.

idea-plugin.name: CSS Glyph Preview
idea-plugin.description:
Preview icon-font glyphs right in the editor — in CSS/SCSS and HTML. Works with any icon font that ships a CSS map with codepoints: FontAwesome, Material Design Icons, LineIcons, Linearicons, Unicons, CoreUI Icons, and more.

In CSS / SCSS:

  • Gutter preview next to every content: "\fXXXX" declaration. The rule's font-family (SCSS variables, incl. @use namespaces, are resolved) and font-weight decide which font is used.
  • Icon picker in the content value, searchable by icon name, each item showing its glyph. Selecting an icon inserts the escape and, if needed, sets the required font-weight so it also renders in the browser.

In HTML (and templates such as Twig):

  • Gutter preview next to <i class="fas fa-pencil">.
  • Icon-font class completions show the glyph inline — existing suggestions are decorated, not duplicated.

Hovering an icon (Quick Documentation) shows a larger preview.

You register your own icon fonts (.ttf/.otf) plus their CSS name map under Settings > Tools > CSS Glyph Preview (.ttf/.otf/.woff) — the map is auto-detected next to the font. Even easier: when you open a file using a known icon font that isn't set up yet, the plugin offers to find and register it from your project in one click. Selected files are copied into the IDE config folder, so they keep working after the originals are deleted.

Requires an IDE with bundled CSS support (IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate, WebStorm, PhpStorm, PyCharm Professional, etc.). Only bitmap/vector icon fonts with an @font-face codepoint map are supported — SVG-sprite icon sets are not. Not affiliated with or endorsed by any of the icon-set projects mentioned.
idea-plugin.change-notes:

  • WOFF web fonts are supported: a .woff is decoded to a usable font on registration (WOFF2 is planned).
  • Strict font-weight matching and pseudo-element-aware cascade resolution (font-family/weight from a sibling &:before, &:after rule).

  • HTML support: gutter preview for <i class="fas fa-pencil">, and icon-decorated class completions (no duplicate entries). Works in templates such as Twig.

idea-plugin.name: Color Picker
idea-plugin.description:
A complete color companion for your JetBrains IDE. Pick any color on your screen with the eyedropper, then read everything about it in one tool window: conversions across every common color space, WCAG accessibility checks, harmony schemes, tint and shade ramps and color temperature.

Features
  • Eyedrop anywhere. Sample any pixel on your screen: your code, a design tool, an image, anything you can see.
  • Conversions. Hex, RGB, RGB %, Web-Safe, Decimal, Octal, Binary, HSL, HSV, HWB, OKLCH, OKLab, CIE-LAB, CIE-LCH, CMYK, nearest RAL Classic, XYZ, Yxy and Hunter Lab, each one click to copy.
  • Copy-ready CSS. The color as text, background, border, text shadow and box shadow rules.
  • Accessibility. WCAG 2 contrast ratio and APCA (WCAG 3) of the color as text on white, black and its complementary, both directions, with AA and AAA verdicts for normal and large text.
  • Color channels. The screen (RGB, HSL, HSV) and print (CMYK) channel mix as bars.
  • Harmony. Complementary, analogous, monochrome, split complementary, triadic and tetradic companions from the color wheel, one click away.
  • Tints, shades and tones. The color stepped toward white, black and gray; click a step to load it.
  • Temperature. Whether the color reads warm or cool, with its warmer and cooler neighbours.
  • Color vision deficiency. The color beside its simulation under protan, deutan, tritan and monochromacy vision, from mild to severe.
  • Recent colors. Your last picks stay in the tool window, so the shades you are working with are always one click away.

Getting Started
  1. Install a compatible JetBrains IDE, such as IntelliJ IDEA, CLion, PyCharm, or other IntelliJ-based IDEs.
  2. Launch the IDE and open plugin settings.
  3. Search for Color Picker and click install.
  4. After installing the plugin, open the Color Picker tool window from the right sidebar, or run Tools | Pick a Color. Press Pick a Color and use the eyedropper to sample any pixel on your screen.
  5. Click any value row to copy it, click any chip to explore that color, and collapse the sections you do not use. The tool window remembers your layout.

Part of the Codigrate tools family, alongside the in-browser color, palette and gradient tools and the Codigrate themes for JetBrains IDEs.

idea-plugin.name: Palette Vault
idea-plugin.description:
Generates color palettes and writes them into your code, without leaving the editor and without a network connection.

Right-click in the editor, under Palette Vault:

  • Insert a generated palette in CSS custom properties, a Sass map, a Tailwind fragment, a JSON array or bare hex. The format follows the file extension unless you fix one in settings.
  • Insert a generated palette as a comment, using the comment syntax of whatever language you are in.
  • Build a palette around the color under the caret, keeping its hue, for when you already have one brand color and need three more beside it.
  • Convert the color under the caret between hex, rgb, hsl and oklch, replacing exactly the span it matched.
  • Check contrast against a second color, reported against the WCAG thresholds in a sentence rather than a badge.

Palettes are built in OKLCH. Colors outside sRGB have their chroma reduced by search until they fit, which keeps lightness and hue exactly rather than shifting the hue the way clamping does. A mood preset fixes the corridor of lightness and saturation, and lightness is laid out as a ladder instead of four independent random values, which is most of why the results hold together.

Part of Palette Vault, which also has plugins for VS Code, Figma, Framer, Storybook, Obsidian, Chrome and Firefox.

idea-plugin.name: Redline - Rendered HTML Diff
idea-plugin.description:
Review HTML and Markdown changes as a rendered document. When both sides are HTML or Markdown, Redline adds a viewer that shows the page as the browser renders it, with insertions and deletions highlighted inline — legal-document style.

Prose edits in long hand-authored lines, renumbered lists, and table changes become readable at a glance instead of a wall of rewrapped markup. Works anywhere the IDE shows a diff: local changes, commits, and VCS revisions.

Review attribute changes with amber outlines and tooltips, and jump between changes using the navigation controls and minimap. Switch between Original, Redline, and Final while preserving each side's text, attributes, and list/table whitespace.

Select the Redline viewer in the diff editor's view switcher, next to Side-by-side and Unified.
idea-plugin.change-notes:

  • Show attribute changes with amber outlines, navigation and minimap targets, and safely rendered tooltips listing changed values, including changes with no text edits.

Changed

  • Upgrade the pinned HTML comparison engine to redline-engine@0.2.0 and operation model 2 for more precise list, table, and attribute edits. Continue rejecting unknown model versions and validating exact reconstruction of both sides before displaying a result.

Fixed

  • Preserve exact list/table whitespace and before-side attributes when switching between Original and Final, including pretty-printed insertions and deletions.

idea-plugin.description:
A lightweight browser plugin for JetBrains IDEs. Adds an integrated browser panel on the right side of the editor, powered by JCEF (Chromium Embedded Framework).

Features:

idea-plugin.name: Tailwind Rainbow
idea-plugin.description:
Colors Tailwind CSS variant prefixes so a long class list stays readable.

Every variant is painted in its own color, with related variants sharing one, so the structure of a class list is visible at a glance instead of having to be read word by word: hover, focus, sm, dark, container queries such as @md, attribute variants such as data-[state=open], arbitrary variants such as [&>*], and the ! important modifier wherever Tailwind allows it.

Where it reads class names. Class attributes and framework bindings (class, className, :class, v-bind:class, x-bind:class), class helper functions (cn, clsx, cva, twMerge, …), tagged templates including styled.div`…`, values assigned to a class-shaped name, and CSS @apply directives. Out of the box that covers HTML, JSX/TSX, Vue, Svelte, Astro, PHP and stylesheets - and the list of file types is a setting rather than a promise.

What you can change. Four themes ship: two decorative ones, a palette built on the Okabe-Ito colors so the variant families stay apart for color-blind readers, and one that takes its colors from your editor's own syntax scheme and follows it when you switch. Build your own on top of any of them - pick colors in the table, add variants no theme lists, switch entries off - or import a theme from the VS Code Tailwind Rainbow extension. Which attributes, helper functions and file types are scanned is configurable, and a project can keep its own answers and commit them. Colors that would not contrast with your editor background are adjusted until they do.

What it deliberately does not do. It does not sort, rewrite or complete class names, and it does not color utility classes out of the box: variants stop standing out once everything else is colored too, so base-class coloring is something you opt into.

Everything lives under Settings | Editor | Tailwind Rainbow.

An independent port of the Tailwind Rainbow extension for Visual Studio Code, not affiliated with or endorsed by its authors. Tailwind CSS is a trademark of Tailwind Labs Inc.; this plugin is not affiliated with or endorsed by Tailwind Labs.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Open Tailwind Rainbow Variant Health, a cancellable project report for declared variants, theme matches, missing/disabled/malformed entries, wildcard coverage and duplicate declarations, with actions to add a colour, open a declaration and refresh the report.
  • A colour for a scoping modifier, painted apart from the variant it scopes, so group-hover: reads as both a hover and an ancestor-scoped one instead of looking identical to a plain hover:. Covers group, peer, has, in and not, which share one colour per built-in theme and appear in the theme editor as ordinary tokens.

Removed

  • The Ignored prefix modifiers setting. group, peer, has, in and not are Tailwind's own syntax rather than a preference, so they are now fixed in the plugin.

idea-plugin.name: LibMan GUI
idea-plugin.description:
Manage client-side libraries in libman.json without leaving Rider - the Visual Studio Library Manager (LibMan) experience, brought to JetBrains Rider. Rider has no built-in LibMan support (RIDER-15368); this plugin fills that gap by wrapping the official libman CLI.

Open a libman.json and every library is checked for updates. For each library you get, right in the editor:

  • An amber version highlight when a newer version exists.
  • A clickable action row above the line - Check for updates, one Update to X per available version (patch / minor / major / pre-release), and Remove. Update and Remove are queued: a banner lists the pending changes, and they run on save, when the file closes, or with Apply now. Undo drops one.
  • A description tooltip on the library name, from the provider (cdnjs, npm/unpkg, jsDelivr), with a link to the library's page.
  • Completion - library names that start with the typed text (from 3 letters), the 10 newest versions after @ (pre-releases when the setting is on), destination folders with the IDE's own path completion, and the library's files in files that are not on disk yet.
  • Manifest checks - a warning on an unknown provider, a warning on a files entry the library version does not have, and a hint when a newer libman.json schema version is available.

Configure pre-releases, check-on-open and the cache lifetime in Settings | Tools | LibMan. Context-menu actions on libman.json (Solution Explorer and editor): Restore, Clean, and Manage.

CLI failures (missing tool, network, provider errors) are shown as notifications with a Copy Details action - never as plugin crashes.

Requires the LibMan CLI: dotnet tool install -g Microsoft.Web.LibraryManager.Cli.

Source & issues: github.com/iamr8/libman-rider

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft. LibMan and Library Manager are names of the Microsoft tool this plugin integrates.
idea-plugin.change-notes: See the CHANGELOG for release notes.

idea-plugin.name: Photo Placeholders
idea-plugin.description:
Insert real placeholder photos into HTML, CSS, Markdown, JSX or any file, powered by the free picsum.photos service.

Features

  • Any size or square images: random, a specific image id, or a stable seed.
  • Grayscale and blur (1–10) filters, .jpg / .webp extensions.
  • Automatic ?random=N so every inserted image is different, even with multiple carets.
  • Output as URL, HTML <img>, CSS background, Markdown, JSX or a src attribute.
  • Live preview and a browsable gallery to pick a specific photo and see its author.
  • Remembers your last settings; one-click insert with them.
  • Live templates: picsum, picsumimg, picsumbg, picsummd.

Usage

Code | Generate… (Alt+Insert / ⌘N) → Placeholder Photo…, or right-click in the editor. Assign your own shortcut under Settings | Keymap.

Privacy

The plugin collects no data. It only downloads images and image metadata from picsum.photos while the generator preview or gallery is open; inserting an image never uses the network. As with any web request, picsum.photos can see your IP address and the IDE name sent as the User-Agent.

Unofficial plugin, not affiliated with picsum.photos. Photos come from Unsplash via picsum.photos. Source code: github.com/jamesmosq/photo-placeholders.

  • Output as URL, HTML <img>, CSS background, Markdown, JSX or src attribute.
