idea-plugin.name: JAIPilot - One-Click AI for Java Testing
idea-plugin.description:
Build a stronger Java test suite without leaving IntelliJ IDEA.

JAIPilot turns concrete testing outcomes into reviewed, verified changes. It understands the open IntelliJ project, plans the work through the JAIPilot service, and runs repository commands, edits, builds, tests, and coverage on your laptop.

Testing workflows

  • Generate Tests: Create focused tests for a class, folder, module, or repository and run them.
  • Fix Tests: Run the configured suites, repair every current failure, and rerun verification.
  • Test Current Changes: Inspect the current Git diff and add tests for affected behavior.
  • Lock Existing Behavior: Add characterization tests before a refactor or migration.
  • Improve Coverage: Measure current coverage, close meaningful gaps, and measure the result.
  • Stabilize Flaky Tests: Reproduce nondeterministic failures, repair the cause, and rerun repeatedly.

JAIPilot reads the IntelliJ project model and the repository's own build configuration instead of imposing a fixed Java stack. The native Jobs view shows the current activity, followed by the local build result, selected-scope test totals when available, selected-scope coverage when measured, and changed files. Logs stay collapsed unless you open them. You can stop a run, review the diff, export its measured report, or undo and redo its changes.

Testing jobs keep going through IntelliJ indexing and resume automatically after temporary connection failures. In a Git repository, JAIPilot uses tracked and non-ignored files for review, Undo, and Redo. Non-Git projects can run the same workflows; the Jobs view explains how to initialize Git to unlock those change-management actions.

Get started: Install JAIPilot, sign in under Settings → JAIPilot, then open JAIPilot → Jobs → New or right-click Java code in the editor or Project view. No provider CLI, Node.js adapter, model selection, or separate AI account is required.

Testing workflows use JAIPilot credits. The 14-day trial includes 150 credits; JAIPilot Pro is $29 per month with 2,000 monthly credits and optional top-ups. See pricing, the guide, and support.

You can disable usage statistics under Settings → JAIPilot. See the privacy policy.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Add focused workflows for generating tests, repairing failures, testing current changes, locking existing behavior, improving coverage, and stabilizing flaky tests.
  • Show local build evidence, selected-scope test totals when available, measured selected-scope coverage, and changed files, with report export, IntelliJ diff review, Undo, and Redo.

Changed

  • Reposition JAIPilot as a Java test engineer for IntelliJ IDEA while keeping eligible prepaid Generate Tests accounts on the legacy generator until their existing credits are exhausted.
  • Run repository reads, test edits, Maven or Gradle commands, builds, tests, and coverage inside the open local project while JAIPilot handles planning through its authenticated service.
  • Replace provider setup, model controls, and terminal-style conversations with JAIPilot sign-in, six testing outcomes, native progress, result cards, and collapsed command logs.
  • Use exact IntelliJ-selected paths as the workflow scope. The agent discovers project contents and conventions from repository evidence instead of plugin-side source preloading, indexing, or build-layout guesses.
  • Use Git for change review, Undo, and Redo. Non-Git projects can run every testing workflow and receive a clear prompt to initialize Git for those change-management actions.

Fixed

  • Resume the same in-progress request after transient connection failures and temporary service responses without charging twice.
  • Serialize complete local testing jobs so commands and file changes from two jobs cannot interleave in one repository.
  • Return invalid local command and IntelliJ-read arguments to the agent as ordinary tool errors so it can correct them instead of stopping the job.
  • Scope result-card test totals and coverage to the selected code while retaining the final repository-wide suite as regression evidence.
  • Remove hidden response-length, history-length, collection-size, source-context, command-timeout, and receipt limits that could reject or distort a valid job.
  • Preserve unrelated user edits, detect real same-file conflicts, and keep Git checkpoints limited to tracked and non-ignored files.
  • Render concise completion headings and show a Coverage card only when selected-scope coverage was actually measured.

Removed

  • Remove Codex and Claude Code integrations, ACP infrastructure, non-testing workflows, optional workflow instructions, job follow-ups, and the bug-to-regression-test workflow.

idea-plugin.name: i18n Translate Pro: JVM
idea-plugin.description:
When should you use i18n Translate Pro?

We'd rather be honest than oversell. If your project targets only 1–2 languages, you probably don't need this plugin — a general AI assistant such as Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, or Cursor can handle occasional translation just fine. i18n Translate Pro earns its place on medium-to-large projects: 3 or more languages with hundreds of strings (think 500+ translations), and in codebases with frequent changes that require continuously updating existing translations. That is exactly where its batch processing, VCS-aware change detection, and "translate only what changed" workflow save hours of manual effort. Not sure yet? Start with the 30-day Pro trial, or stay on the free tier — translate one language file per run, and repeat for each additional language.



Core Translation Workflow - The Primary Power:

  • 📂 Right-Click Translation - Right-click any .properties file in Project View or Commit Panel → Select "Translate Properties File" → Watch AI translate to 200+ languages simultaneously
  • 🌍 Batch Multi-Language Translation - Translate to 5, 10, or 50+ languages in one click with intelligent batch processing and progress tracking
  • 🤖 Enterprise-Grade AI - Choose from 8 LLM providers with 60+ models (Google Gemini recommended with FREE daily usage, OpenAI GPT, Anthropic Claude, DeepSeek, and more)
  • 💰 Smart Cost Optimization - Automatic legacy model detection alerts you to outdated models and recommends newer alternatives - save up to 98% on translation costs
  • ⚡ Professional Results - Generates messages_zh_CN.properties, messages_fr_FR.properties, messages_ja_JP.properties with proper JVM locale formatting for 200+ locales
  • 🔄 Smart VCS Integration - Detects uncommitted changes, distinguishes new vs modified keys, and lets you choose what to translate
  • ✅ Commit Panel Power - Right-click translate directly in commit view during code review - seamless integration with your Git workflow

什么时候该使用 i18n Translate Pro？

与其过度推销，我们更愿意坦诚相告。如果您的项目只需要 1–2 种语言，您可能并不需要此插件 —— 通用 AI 助手（如 Claude Code、Codex、Antigravity 或 Cursor）即可轻松应对偶尔的翻译需求。i18n Translate Pro 的价值真正体现在中大型项目：3 种或以上语言、包含数百条文案（例如 500+ 条翻译），以及需要持续更新、维护既有翻译的高频变更代码库。正是在这些场景下，其批量处理、感知 VCS 的变更检测，以及"仅翻译已变更内容"的工作流程能为您节省大量人工时间。还不确定？不妨从 30 天专业版试用开始，或继续使用免费版 —— 每次翻译一个语言文件，并可对每种语言重复操作。

  • ⚡ 专业结果 - 生成 messages_zh_CN.properties、messages_fr_FR.properties、messages_ja_JP.properties，支持200多个地区的正确JVM区域设置格式
  • 🔄 智能VCS集成 - 检测未提交的更改，区分新键和修改键，让您选择要翻译的内容
  • ✅ 提交面板功能 - 在代码审查期间直接在提交视图中右键翻译 - 与您的Git工作流程无缝集成

idea-plugin.name: Copy with inline issues for AI
idea-plugin.description:
A JetBrains IDE plugin that copies your code with all errors and warnings added as comments. Paste it into ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Cursor, or any AI tool. The AI will see every problem your IDE sees.

The Problem

You have broken code. Your IDE shows red and yellow markers on the lines with errors. But when you copy the code and paste it into ChatGPT or Claude, those markers are gone. The AI does not know what is wrong.

So you have to explain each error yourself: what line it is on, what the message says. This takes time. You can forget some errors. You can make typos.

The Solution

Right-click your code and pick Copy with inline issues. The plugin takes every error and warning from your IDE and adds them as comments right next to the lines where they appear. Each comment uses the correct comment style for the language.

You paste the result into any AI tool. The AI sees the file name, the code, and all the error messages on the right lines. You do not need to explain anything.

Before and After

You select this code in your IDE:

def calculate(a, b):
    result = a + c
    return result

You paste this into ChatGPT:

# File: calculator.py

def calculate(a, b):
    result = a + c
    # ERROR: Unresolved reference 'c'
    return result

The AI now knows the file name, the line with the error, and the error message. You did not type any of that.

How to Use

  1. Select code in the editor, or right-click a file in the project tree
  2. Pick "Copy with inline issues" from the menu
  3. Paste into any AI tool. All errors and warnings are already in the text

Features

  • Ready for AI tools — paste into ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Cursor, or any LLM
  • Two ways to copy — select code in the editor, or right-click a file in the project tree
  • Runs in the background — detection runs off the EDT with a progress indicator; no IDE freezes on large files
  • Copy notification — a toast confirms how many lines were copied and how many issues were inlined
  • Severity filter — choose which severity levels to include (errors, warnings, weak warnings, info) in Preferences → Tools → Copy with Inline Issues
  • Large-selection safety — confirmation dialog before running inspection on selections over 500 lines
  • 20+ languages — Java, Kotlin, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, C/C++, C#, PHP, Ruby, Dart, Swift, and more
  • Finds real problems — syntax errors, missing variables, wrong types, and IDE inspection warnings
  • Correct comment style — layered language detection picks the right comment format per file (see table below)

Supported Languages

LanguagesComment Format
Java, Kotlin, JS, TS, C/C++, C#, Go, Rust, PHP, Swift, Dart, Scala// ERROR: message
Python, Ruby, Shell, YAML, TOML, Dockerfile, Makefile, Terraform, R# ERROR: message
SQL, Lua, Haskell, Ada, VHDL-- ERROR: message
HTML, XML, Markdown, SVG<!-- ERROR: message -->
CSS/* ERROR: message */
INI, Clojure, Lisp, AutoHotkey; ERROR: message

Unknown languages fall back to // style. File extension is used as a hint when the language ID alone is ambiguous.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Copy notification could overstate how many issues were inlined — The count came from re-scanning the generated text for the literal pattern ERROR:, WARNING:, etc., so a source line that legitimately contained one of those words followed by a colon, such as a log statement, was counted as an inlined issue even though no comment was added for it. The count is now taken directly from the issues that were actually inlined while the text was built, so it can no longer diverge from what the comments show.

    • Tools menu → Open Project In Void

Configuration

idea-plugin.name: Explyt AI Agent
idea-plugin.description:
Explyt AI Agent is an IDE-native AI agent that debugs, refactors, and tests through your JetBrains IDE — not through terminal commands — saving tokens by using IDE facts instead of noisy logs. Built for developers in large, complex codebases.

The agent uses IDE indexes, debugger state, and coverage data instead of dumping logs and grepping files — so it spends your tokens on answers, not on reading code the IDE already understands. Less noise, lower cost, faster results.

IDE-native debugging, refactoring, and testing

  • Debug with real execution data: investigate failures with debugger state, stack traces, executed instructions, and data flow instead of adding log statements by hand.
  • Refactor semantically: search symbols, find usages, rename, and update code through IDE indexes and refactorings, not grep-based edits that break cross-file references.
  • Generate tests with coverage feedback: create or update unit, integration, and end-to-end tests, then use IDE coverage and branch-aware analysis to target uncovered paths.
  • Find and fix security vulnerabilities: scan JVM projects for vulnerabilities with detailed findings and agent-assisted fixes.
  • Fix quality issues in context: use inspections, quick fixes, library decompilation, and build/test results from the IDE.
  • Keep your workflow native: run configurations, test runners, web search, webpage reading, and Allure TestOps data are available directly from the agent.

Use it for

  • debugging with IDE execution data and stack traces
  • generating tests with coverage feedback and detecting flaky tests
  • finding and fixing security vulnerabilities (SAST)
  • refactoring code with IDE-aware search and safe renames
  • fixing pull request feedback, stack traces, test failures, and TMS-linked issues
  • building features and microservices from specifications
  • migrating code to new frameworks or library versions
  • generating documentation and code comments

Open standards and team controls

  • MCP and AGENTS.md support for portable AI workflows.
  • Bring-your-own-key (BYOK) LLM support and edit-scope controls for teams.
  • Enterprise: VPC deployment, self-hosting, and SSO.

Agent modes

General, Code, Test, Plan, Review, and Debug modes — each mode leverages IDE-specific tools (Debug mode runs the debugger, Test mode reads coverage data). Plus an Orchestrator that splits complex tasks across specialized subagents, and custom modes for team workflows.

Getting started

  1. Install Explyt AI Agent.
  2. Open the agent from your JetBrains IDE.
  3. Try Debug mode to investigate a failing test — it uses the IDE debugger, not log prints.

Start coding with your IDE's full power. Watch a quick demo, or submit an issue if you find a bug or want to share feedback.

If Explyt AI Agent helps your work, please rate the plugin on JetBrains Marketplace.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
What's New in Explyt AI Agent

  • Images in subagents: attach an image even when the main model is text-only. Explyt can send it to a subagent with a vision-capable model, which describes the image or extracts text. Create a subagent profile with a vision model so the main agent knows when to delegate image-related tasks.
  • Quick questions with /btw: ask for a clarification without interrupting a long-running task. The answer appears in a separate panel below the chat history while the main agent continues working; the question and answer are not added to the conversation history. The command currently works without tools or attachments.
  • Rule reminders for long conversations: set strictness in a user rule's frontmatter to control when Explyt repeats it: system (default, once), user-message (before every user message), or tool-call (after a tool result, before the next agent step). More frequent reminders use additional tokens or time.
  • IntelliJ Platform 2026.2: Explyt now supports IDEs based on IntelliJ Platform 2026.2, while retaining support for versions 2025.1 through 2026.1.
  • Plugin update reminders: when a compatible plugin version becomes available, Explyt lets you update immediately, postpone the reminder for seven days, or skip the version. Updates are never installed without your permission. You can disable reminders in Settings → Tools → Explyt → Notifications.
  • UI fixes: the selected model is now saved separately for each chat. We also fixed closing chats and the editor, cursor placement after deleting an attachment, stopping background tasks when a chat closes, and drag-and-drop attachment of binary files.
  • Reliability fixes: Explyt writes files more reliably, retries plugin updates after temporary failures, correctly accounts for provider context size for models in routing profiles, and resolves several MCP server integration issues.

idea-plugin.name: Project Dashboard AI
idea-plugin.description:
Keep tasks, Git, and GitHub next to your editor—without juggling browser tabs. Project Dashboard AI is a side tool window that helps you capture work as a checklist, sync it with GitHub Issues when you want, and move faster with AI-assisted commits and code help. Plug in your preferred model, optionally connect GitHub, and stay in flow.

Report issues & feedback

What you will find in the tool window

  • Checklist — Tasks, tags, search, notebooks, attachments, and GitHub state in one place; stays in sync with project-checklist.md.
  • Bookmarks — Quick access to important files, grouped and easy to open.
  • Branches — Branch and worktree operations from the IDE (checkout, merge, rebase, and more).
  • Pull requests — Work with PRs alongside your repo.
  • Actions — GitHub Actions workflow runs for the current context.
  • The tab strip also shows ACP / bridge status so you can see AI Assistant agent connectivity at a glance.

Highlights

  • GitHub Issues — Create, update, assign, label, and comment; keep local tasks and GitHub in step when integration is on.
  • Markdown notebooks per task — Notes with preview; optional sync to issue comments.
  • AI commit messages & reports — Generate commits from staged changes and structured reports; prompts are customizable.
  • AI code chat — Talk to OpenAI, Claude, or Gemini with project context and memory options.
  • AI Assistant — Optional ACP agent mode and GitHub MCP tools in AI Assistant Chat (where supported by your IDE/OS).
  • Editor integrations — Send selections to AI or issue comments; link work to branches and commits.

AI models

  • OpenAI: GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4 (Mini, Nano), GPT-5.3-Codex, o3 (Pro, Standard, Mini), o4-mini, GPT-4.1.
  • Anthropic Claude: Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Haiku 4.5.
  • Google Gemini: Gemini 3.5 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Pro (Preview), Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite, Gemini 2.5 (Pro, Flash).

The model list refreshes automatically from each provider's API and is cached for 24 hours, so this reflects what's actually callable with your key rather than a fixed snapshot — no plugin update needed when a provider adds or retires a model. Configure your provider and key under Settings → Tools → Project Dashboard AI.

Who it is for

  • Developers who want a single IDE home for tasks, PRs, and CI context.
  • Teams that already use GitHub Issues and want tighter IDE sync.
  • Anyone who wants AI help for commits and code review without leaving JetBrains.

Getting started

  1. Install from JetBrains Marketplace and open Project Dashboard AI in the tool window bar.
  2. Set your AI provider and API key in plugin settings; add a GitHub token if you use Issues / PR / Actions features.
  3. Add tasks on the Checklist tab—or edit project-checklist.md in the repo root.

Privacy & security

  • API keys and tokens are stored in the IDE credentials system.
  • AI requests go to the provider you select (not through us).
  • Optional anonymous usage metrics are off by default; you can opt in from the plugin when prompted.

idea-plugin.name: i18n Translate Pro: Web
idea-plugin.description:
When should you use i18n Translate Pro?

We'd rather be honest than oversell. If your project targets only 1–2 languages, you probably don't need this plugin — a general AI assistant such as Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, or Cursor can handle occasional translation just fine. i18n Translate Pro earns its place on medium-to-large projects: 3 or more languages with hundreds of strings (think 500+ translations), and in codebases with frequent changes that require continuously updating existing translations. That is exactly where its batch processing, VCS-aware change detection, and "translate only what changed" workflow save hours of manual effort. Not sure yet? Start with the 30-day Pro trial, or stay on the free tier — translate one language file per run, and repeat for each additional language.



Core Translation Workflow - The Primary Power:

  • 📂 Right-Click Translation - Right-click any JSON i18n file (en.json, common.json) or Angular XLF file in Project View or Commit Panel → Select "Translate JSON/XLF i18n File" → Watch AI translate to 200+ languages simultaneously
  • 🌍 Batch Multi-Language Translation - Translate to 5, 10, or 50+ languages in one click for React, Vue, Angular, Next.js projects with intelligent batch processing
  • 🤖 Enterprise-Grade AI - Choose from 8 LLM providers with 60+ models (Google Gemini recommended with FREE daily usage, OpenAI GPT, Anthropic Claude, DeepSeek, and more)
  • 💰 Smart Cost Optimization - Automatic legacy model detection alerts you to outdated models and recommends newer alternatives - save up to 98% on translation costs
  • ⚡ Framework-Smart Results - Generates zh-CN.json, fr-FR.json, ja-JP.json, messages.de-DE.xlf with proper web locale formatting for 200+ languages
  • 🔧 Complex JSON Handling - Preserves nested JSON structures, flattens for translation, reconstructs perfectly for all web frameworks
  • 🔄 Smart VCS Integration - Detects uncommitted changes, distinguishes new vs modified keys, and lets you choose what to translate
  • ✅ Commit Panel Power - Right-click translate directly in commit view during code review - seamless integration with your Git workflow

idea-plugin.name: YesCode Stats
idea-plugin.description:
YesCode Stats - A comprehensive usage monitoring plugin for YesCode API users.

Monitor your YesCode API balance and usage in real-time directly within your IDE. Keep track of your subscription usage, remaining balance, and get visual alerts when approaching limits.

✨ Key Features

  • Real-time Balance Display - View total balance, subscription balance, and pay-as-you-go balance
  • Smart Visual Indicators - Color-coded usage bars (Green → Yellow → Orange → Red) based on consumption
  • Status Bar Integration - Quick balance overview with progress indicators 🟢🟡🟠🔴
  • Detailed Tool Window - Comprehensive statistics with elegant, compact design
  • Auto-refresh - Configurable refresh intervals (10s, 30s, 1min, 5min, 30min)
  • Secure Storage - API tokens stored safely using IntelliJ's credential system
  • Quick Actions - Keyboard shortcut (Ctrl+Shift+Y) for instant refresh

🚀 Getting Started

  1. Get your API Token from YesCode website
  2. Install the plugin and configure your token via settings dialog
  3. Start monitoring your usage automatically!

💡 Pro Tips

  • Click the status bar widget to refresh or configure (when not set up)
  • Set daily subscription limits to track usage percentage accurately
  • Use the tool window for detailed usage breakdown

Perfect for YesCode API users who want to stay informed about their usage and avoid unexpected charges.

RunVSAgent - Run VSCode-based Coding Agents in JetBrains IDEs

RunVSAgent is an innovative cross-platform development tool that enables developers to run VSCode-based coding agents and extensions within JetBrains IDEs (IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, etc.) or other IDE platforms.

Core Features

  • VSCode Agent Compatibility: Seamlessly run VSCode-based coding agents in JetBrains IDEs
  • Cross-IDE Development: Unified agent experience across different IDE platforms
  • AI-Powered Assistance: Leverage advanced AI coding assistants for intelligent code generation

Supported IDEs

RunVSAgent currently supports the following JetBrains IDE series:

  • IntelliJ IDEA (Ultimate & Community)
  • WebStorm - JavaScript and TypeScript development
  • PyCharm (Professional & Community) - Python development
  • PhpStorm - PHP development
  • RubyMine - Ruby development
  • CLion - C/C++ development
  • GoLand - Go development
  • DataGrip - Database development
  • Rider - .NET development
  • Android Studio - Android development

Supported Agents

  • Roo Code: Advanced AI-powered coding assistant with intelligent code generation and refactoring capabilities
  • Custom Extensions: Support for custom AI coding assistants

Requirements

  • Requires Node.js v18+ installed
  • Requires JetBrains IDE version 2023.1 or later for optimal compatibility

Benefits

  • Increased Productivity: Access powerful AI coding assistants without leaving your preferred IDE
  • Unified Workflow: Maintain a consistent development experience across different platforms
  • Extensible Architecture: Support for new agents and extensions as they become available

idea-plugin.name: MCP Servers for AI Assistants
idea-plugin.description:
MCP Servers for AI Assistants

Supported Assistants: Junie, JetBrains AI Assistant, Windsurf, Firebender, Cursor, Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Continue.dev, Codex CLI

Discover, install, manage, and inspect Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers right inside your IntelliJ‑based IDE. This plugin provides a unified interface to enhance your AI assistants with modular, plug‑and‑play MCP capabilities.

Manage MCP configurations across 8+ AI assistants simultaneously — one control plane for all your tools.

Key Features

  • All Transports — STDIO, SSE (legacy), and Streamable HTTP (MCP spec 2025-11-05) with auto-reconnect
  • Public Catalog — Choose MCP Get, the Official MCP Registry, Docker MCP Catalog, or GitHub MCP Registry, filter servers, and review an installation variant before adding it to an assistant
  • Flexible Configuration — Tweak parameters, environment variables, URLs, headers, and transport type with built-in validation
  • MCP Inspector — Connect via STDIO, SSE, or Streamable HTTP, discover tools, preview JSON Schemas, and autofill request payloads
  • Tool Runner Editor — Open the selected tool with a button, Enter, or double-click and inspect inputs and results in a dedicated editor
  • Execution History — Review the latest 100 Tool Runner calls in this IDE session with timing and copy JSON parameter templates for Python or TypeScript
  • Multiple Assistants — Manage per‑IDE and per‑project settings for Junie, JetBrains AI Assistant, Windsurf, Firebender, Cursor, Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Continue.dev, and Codex CLI
  • Team Configuration — Share MCP server configs with your team via repository (.mcp/team.json)
  • Bulk Import/Export — Export all server configurations to JSON and import them on another machine or share with team
  • JetBrains AI Assistant — Manage JetBrains AI Assistant MCP servers as a first-class, independent assistant, both IDE-level (llm.mcpServers.xml) and per-project (.idea/workspace.xml); add, edit, and remove entries directly with dedicated checkboxes

Getting Started

  1. Open the MCP Servers tool window to install and configure servers.
  2. Open the MCP Inspector tool window to connect, explore tools, and run interactive calls.

  • See which assistants use each setup option, including project-specific installations.
  • Choose an assistant directly from registry setup options, then enter parameters when adding the server. Installed details can copy the configured variant to another assistant.
  • Installed server details retain catalog descriptions, documentation and links, including offline access after installation.
  • Use server details and Tool Runner with your IDE theme and fonts, keep entered values when changing themes, and read native cards and dialogs more comfortably at larger sizes.
  • Recognize MCP panels and server tabs with clearer theme-aware icons, and distinguish delete and copy actions at a glance.
  • Read server dates, saved catalog timestamps and execution history in your local date and time format.
  • Open installed server details directly from local configuration, including custom servers absent from registries.
  • Registry loading displays early results, marks partial catalogs and keeps source switching responsive. Runtime choices stay stable while open and support individual runtimes from composite entries.
  • Review server setup options in a compact, theme-aware details page; choose an assistant separately, distinguish project and user destinations, and see explicit installed and removal states.
  • Choose MCP Get, the Official MCP Registry, Docker MCP Catalog, or GitHub MCP Registry, configure a specific installation variant, and keep open server pages bound to their original source and version.
  • Copy history entries as JSON parameter templates for Python or TypeScript, preserving literal values and omitting connection details.
  • See actual catalog installation and removal results, refresh assistant status without blocking the interface, and recognize matching configuration variants.
  • Preserve unrelated Team JSON settings, show unreadable files with a reload action, and keep the interface responsive without losing sync results.
  • Compare Team settings with the selected assistant, expose conflicting variants, and avoid rewriting matching entries.
  • Choose the Team sync destination explicitly and see confirmed applied counts, including partial or refused writes, without blocking the interface.
  • Open catalog details with the keyboard, review recipe requirements, copy complete configuration JSON, and inspect HTTP servers with the correct transport.
  • Display catalog card names and descriptions as text without interpreting embedded HTML.
  • Keep catalog environment variables, remote headers and server details after restarting the IDE; preserve recipe arguments and omit incomplete or unsupported installation recipes.
  • Show Tool Runner progress, prevent overlapping calls, cancel locally, and stop owned execution when the editor closes.
  • Keep argument types, multiline strings and unknown fields across Form/Raw JSON changes; preserve numeric precision in Raw JSON and reject malformed form values before execution.
  • Preserve quoted and empty Inspector arguments, nested input schemas, typed enums and schema definitions.
  • Show tool discovery failures, load paginated tools, and preserve error status, structured results and standard content in execution history.
  • Cancel and reconnect safely in Inspector: stop owned subprocesses, prevent stderr stalls, and ignore results from previous connections.
  • Review exact sources and included values before creating a team configuration; default placeholders prevent automatic credential sharing.
  • Keep connection credentials, command arguments and exception payloads out of Inspector and IDE logs.
  • Prevent tool schemas and catalog descriptions from running embedded scripts or introducing unsafe links and controls.
  • Retain AI Assistant server state and custom settings during edits, including exact command arguments with empty values, quotes and backslashes.
  • Preserve Continue block metadata and neighboring servers when editing or removing entries, avoid filename collisions, and use the supported HTTP header format.
  • Preserve Codex authentication and custom server settings, correctly handle quoted server names and multiline arguments, and block unsafe TOML writes.
  • Preserve custom JSON server settings when editing configurations, and refuse to overwrite unreadable JSON or XML files.
  • More reliable MCP connections, including HTTP event-stream recovery and STDIO timeouts.
  • Improved handling of YAML comments, Unicode text, and JSON configuration values.

10.0.0

  • New: JetBrains AI Assistant is now a first-class, independent assistant (separate from Junie) with its own IDE-level and project-level checkboxes — its MCP servers are shown alongside every other assistant and can be added, edited, and removed directly, reading and writing both the IDE settings (llm.mcpServers.xml) and the per-project settings (.idea/workspace.xml) while preserving tokens, env vars, args, and all other settings in those files. Entries are written in the exact schema AI Assistant expects for the running IDE version (auto-detecting the flat 2025.1 layout vs. the newer <commands>/<urls> layout, and using the platform env format), so the assistant actually picks them up

9.0.0

  • Fixed: Config read/write now matches each assistant's actual on-disk format — URL-only entries in ~/.claude.json and similar files are no longer mis-decoded as empty STDIO entries
  • Fixed: Claude Desktop rejects HTTP/SSE servers up front instead of silently dropping them on write (writing `url` corrupts claude_desktop_config.json — anthropics/claude-code#37286)
  • Fixed: Firebender writes emit `type:"stdio"` on stdio servers as required by Firebender docs
  • Fixed: Continue.dev rebuilt for the array-of-objects YAML block-file format under `.continue/mcpServers/`; emits `type:"streamable-http"` for HTTP entries (plain `http` is rejected by Continue's schema)
  • Fixed: Codex CLI uses nested `[mcp_servers.NAME.env]` and `[mcp_servers.NAME.http_headers]` sub-tables and no `type` field, matching openai/codex's `deny_unknown_fields` deserializer
  • Fixed: Continue.dev project-level legacy file path (`<project>/.continue/mcp.json`)
  • Fixed: Server card delete now removes the entry from every assistant where it is actually installed, not just Junie / Windsurf
  • Fixed: Server dialog validation refreshes on every input change
  • Fixed: Assistant preselection in the edit dialog matches actual installations across all supported assistants
  • Improved: Atomic writes (tmp + ATOMIC_MOVE) for every config file — shared files like ~/.claude.json and claude_desktop_config.json are safe against crash / concurrent-writer truncation
  • Improved: Gradle wrapper updated to 9.5.1; cleaned up obsolete CLASSPATH handling in gradlew / gradlew.bat

8.0.0

  • Fixed: Windsurf config path auto-detection — supports both Codeium plugin for JetBrains (~/.codeium/mcp_config.json) and standalone Windsurf IDE (~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json)
  • Fixed: Team Sync now supports all assistants (Windsurf, Firebender, Cursor, Claude, Continue, Codex) — previously only synced to Junie
  • Fixed: Add Server action now correctly dispatches to all selected assistants — previously routed most assistants to Junie Global
  • Fixed: Import now offers all assistants as import targets instead of only Junie Global
  • Improved: Conflict detection and missing server checks now scan all assistant configs, not just Junie
  • Improved: Centralized assistant target registry for consistent behavior across sync, import, and conflict detection

7.0.0

  • New: Claude Code support with user-scoped (~/.claude.json) and project-scoped (.mcp.json) configurations
  • New: Codex CLI support with TOML-based config (~/.codex/config.toml and project-level .codex/config.toml)
  • Fixed: Config write operations now preserve all non-mcpServers settings in shared config files (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Continue.dev, Junie)
  • Fixed: Corrected Windsurf config path to ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json
  • Fixed: Corrected Continue.dev config paths (mcp.json instead of config.json)
  • Improved: Unified config service interface (MCPConfigService) across all providers
  • Improved: Data-driven assistant actions replacing duplicate install/remove methods
  • Improved: Compact assistant selection dialog with User-level / Project-level grouping
  • Improved: Team config separated into dedicated Shared section

6.0.0

  • New: Streamable HTTP transport (MCP spec 2025-11-05) with auto-reconnect and session support
  • New: Transport type selector in server configuration dialog (STDIO / SSE / HTTP)
  • New: URL and headers fields for SSE and HTTP transports in server dialog
  • Improved: MCP Inspector now supports STDIO, SSE, and Streamable HTTP transports
  • Improved: Inspect button on server cards detects transport type automatically
  • Improved: Config validation with transport-specific URL checks
  • Improved: Assistant buttons redesigned as compact toggle chips with brand colors and install state indicators
  • Updated: MCP Kotlin SDK to 0.8.4, Ktor to 3.2.3

5.0.0

  • New: Team Configuration tab for shared MCP server configs (.mcp/team.json)
  • New: Sync team servers to local configuration with auto-refresh
  • New: Cursor IDE, Claude Desktop, and Continue.dev support
  • New: SSE/HTTP transport support for remote MCP servers
  • New: Bulk import/export of MCP server configurations
  • New: MCP History tool window with execution tracking
  • New: Export tool calls as Python, TypeScript, or cURL snippets
  • New: Server usage statistics with success rates and performance metrics
  • New: Config validation for STDIO and SSE/HTTP transports
  • Improved: MCP Inspector now supports both STDIO and SSE transports
  • Improved: Catalog search with runtime filter and "New only" toggle

4.0.0

  • New: Firebender support; per‑IDE and per‑project settings
  • Fixed: Run VFS refresh off the EDT to prevent UI freezes; added error handling during refresh
  • Improved: MCP Servers panel respects selection for bulk actions; if none selected, only removals are applied
  • Improved: MCP Server Editor UI — "Install" renamed to "Add", "Copy" replaced with an icon + tooltip, and global buttons wrap on small widths
  • Internal: Centralized VFS refresh, JSON merge, config updates, and assistant detection/IDs for maintainability

3.0.0

  • New: Windsurf support alongside Junie; per‑IDE and per‑project settings
  • Improved: Server configuration UI; easier parameters, env vars, and endpoint management
  • Fixed: Stability improvements and clearer error messages

2.0.0

  • Add MCP Inspector

1.2.0

  • Added project-specific management of Junie MCP servers

1.1.0

  • Initial release with MCP Servers management

🤖 智能体模式

赋予星辰软件工厂自主决策能力，它能感知项目上下文并使用代码搜索、终端等工具。

  • 🔄 从重构到功能开发，处理端到端任务
  • ⚙️ 支持自定义工具配置
  • 🔗 无缝融入您的工作流程

⚡ 代码优化

获取智能建议以提升性能、降低复杂性和优化代码结构。

Enhanced Problem Copying for JetBrains IDEs

Copy warnings and errors from the Problems panel with full context including file name and line number.



Hey there, my little vibe coder! 🤡

Tired of awkwardly copying warnings from your IDE to your favorite AI chat?

Where previously warnings copied like this:
[UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE] Unresolved reference: ProblemInfo

In file src/main/kotlin/.../CopyProblemAction.kt - [UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE] Unresolved reference: ProblemInfo (Line № 19)

idea-plugin.name: Switch2Zed
idea-plugin.description:
Switch2Zed is a JetBrains IDE plugin that enables seamless switching between IDE and Zed while maintaining precise cursor position.

Key Features

  • Open files in Zed with one click
  • Maintain exact zed position (line and column)
  • Support opening entire projects in Zed
  • Convenient shortcuts (customizable):
    • Alt+Shift+O - Open current file
    • Alt+Shift+P - Open current project
  • Multiple access methods: shortcuts, context menu, tools menu

Usage

  • Open current file:
    • Press Alt+Shift+O
    • Right-click in editor → Open File In Zed
    • Tools menu → Open File In Zed
  • Open project:
    • Press Alt+Shift+P
    • Right-click in project view → Open Project In Zed
    • Tools menu → Open Project In Zed

Configuration

  • Go to Settings/Preferences → Tools → Switch2Zed
  • Set Zed executable path (default is "zed")
  • Customize shortcuts in Keymap settings

Requirements

  • Zed Editor installed (https://zed.dev)
  • Compatible with all JetBrains IDEs
  • Supported IDE versions: 2022.3 and above

Switch2Zed 是一个 JetBrains IDE 插件，可以让你在 IDE 和 Zed 之间无缝切换，并保持精确的光标位置。

主要特性

  • 一键在 Zed 中打开文件
  • 精确保持光标位置（行号和列号）
  • 支持在 Zed 中打开整个项目
  • 便捷的快捷键（可自定义）:
    • Alt+Shift+O - 打开当前文件
    • Alt+Shift+P - 打开当前项目
  • 多种访问方式：快捷键、右键菜单、工具菜单

使用方法

  • 打开当前文件:
    • 按下 Alt+Shift+O
    • 在编辑器中右键 → Open File In Zed
    • 工具菜单 → Open File In Zed
  • 打开项目:
    • 按下 Alt+Shift+P
    • 在项目视图中右键 → Open Project In Zed
    • 工具菜单 → Open Project In Zed

配置说明

  • 进入 Settings/Preferences → Tools → Switch2Zed
  • 设置 Zed 可执行文件路径（默认为 "zed"）
  • 通过 Keymap 设置自定义快捷键

系统要求

  • 已安装 Zed Editor (https://zed.dev)
  • 兼容所有 JetBrains IDE
  • 支持的 IDE 版本：2022.3 及以上

idea-plugin.name: Writerside Markdown Converter
idea-plugin.description:
Writerside Markdown Converter

An intelligent plugin that converts plain text or Markdown into a format optimized for JetBrains Writerside. Powered by the Google Gemini API, it supports translating text from various languages and then converting it, streamlining the process of documenting and localizing technical articles.

ScreenShot

Features

  • AI-Powered Document Conversion: Utilizes the Google Gemini API to automatically convert text into Writerside-compliant Markdown.
  • Multi-Language Translation & Conversion: Supports translating text from various source languages into a selected target language before formatting.
  • Semantic Markup Support: Automatically converts plain text into Writerside's semantic markup elements such as <ui-path>, <shortcut>, <warning>, and <tabs>, enabling rich documentation formatting with enhanced readability and interactive components.
  • Intuitive UI: A dedicated Tool Window provides a seamless experience for input, conversion, and result verification all in one place.

Usage

  1. Set up your Gemini API key, obtained from Google AI Studio, upon first launch.
  2. Select the target language, input your text, and click the 'Convert' button.

Example

Input Text:

## Database Configuration

To configure the connection, navigate to File > Settings > Database.
You can press Ctrl+Alt+S to open settings quickly.

Warning: Do not share your production credentials in the chat.

If you are using PostgreSQL, set the port to 5432.
If you are using MySQL, set the port to 3306.

Output (Writerside Markdown, Use Semantic Markup):

## Database Configuration {#database-configuration}

To configure the connection, navigate to <ui-path>File | Settings | Database</ui-path>.
You can press <shortcut>Ctrl+Alt+S</shortcut> to open settings quickly.

<warning>
Do not share your production credentials in the chat.
</warning>

<tabs>
<tab title="PostgreSQL">
If you are using PostgreSQL, set the port to 5432.
</tab>
<tab title="MySQL">
If you are using MySQL, set the port to 3306.
</tab>
</tabs>

Rendering Output ↓

Installation

  • Via the built-in plugin system:

    Settings/Preferences > Plugins > Marketplace > Search for "Writerside Markdown Converter" > Install

  • Via JetBrains Marketplace:

    Navigate to the JetBrains Marketplace page and click the Install to... button while your IDE is running.

Change Log

View the full changelog here.

Contribute

Contributions of any kind are welcome, including bug reports, feature suggestions, or code contributions.

  • Issues
  • Pull Requests

Changed

idea-plugin.name: Windsurf (Remote Development)
idea-plugin.description:
Windsurf Plugin (Remote Development)

This plugin is no longer maintained. We highly recommend using the Devin ACP in Jetbrains instead.

This is the remote development compatible version of the Windsurf Plugin. Please install the plugin on both the host and client following the guide.

Windsurf is the modern coding superpower, a free code acceleration toolkit built on cutting edge AI technology. Currently, Windsurf Plugin provides code completion in over 70+ languages, with lightning fast speeds and state-of-the-art suggestion quality.

There are many parts of the modern coding workflow that are boring, tedious, or frustrating, from regurgitating boilerplate to poring through StackOverflow. Recent advances in AI allow us to eliminate these parts, making it seamless to turn your ideas into code. With easy integration into all JetBrains IDEs and a less than 2 minute installation process, you can focus on being the best software developer, not the best code monkey.

With the Windsurf plugin, you get:

  • Unlimited single and multi-line code completions forever
  • Introducing the flow evolution of Chat, Cascade: no need to leave your IDE to ChatGPT, and use convenient suggestions such as Generate Docstring and Explain
  • Cascade's agentic capabilities unlock a new level of collaboration between AI and human, making it the ultimate partner for complex coding workflows.
  • Context Awareness Engine: Windsurf's Context-Awareness Engine integrates with all of your SCMs to build an unparalleled understanding of your codebase, giving you personalized suggestions that result in a 38% increase in code acceptance.
  • Tools: Cascade's tools include making edits, adding files, grep, listing files in a directory, code execution and a number of proprietary tools that have received press coverage.
  • Support for 70+ programming languages: Javascript, Python, Typescript, PHP, Go, Java, C, C++, Rust, Ruby, and more
  • Support through our Discord Community

Join millions of other developers who are using the Windsurf plugin for free to accelerate their software iteration process, improve their code quality and consistency, reduce the number of code review iterations, accelerate developer onboarding, and keep them in their flow state. Want to learn more? Check out our FAQ.

Your New Autocomplete Superpowers

Use Natural Language

Need to make changes in an unfamiliar language or codebase? Instead of spending hours learning all of the syntactical and stylistic details, type out comments in natural language and let Windsurf get the job done.

Minimize Boilerplate Coding

Sometimes feel like a code monkey copy-pasting and modifying boilerplate code over and over again? Let Windsurf handle writing the repetitive work so that you can stay in the coding flow state, generating code faster than you can type.

Find and Use APIs

Spend too much time searching for API endpoints for a task or their signatures to properly interact with them? Windsurf has seen thousands of different API calls and can insert them properly to match your needs, without ever leaving the IDE.

Unit Test Generation

Know that unit tests are important but find writing them mindnumbing? Let Windsurf autogenerate test cases for you, making sure you never miss a pesky edge case. Test-driven development just got a whole lot easier.

Your New Cascade Superpowers

Generate

Cascade can generate whole functions and applications for you with simple natural language prompting and constraints.

Explain

Diving into a foreign codebase? With the push of a button, our assistant will explain everything you need to know.

We hope you enjoy the Windsurf Plugin, your modern coding superpower!

idea-plugin.name: Cline
idea-plugin.description:
Meet Cline, an AI assistant that can use your CLI aNd Editor.

Thanks to the coding and tool-calling capabilities of frontier LLMs, Cline can handle complex software development tasks step-by-step. With tools that let him create & edit files, explore large projects, use the browser, and execute terminal commands (after you grant permission), he can assist you in ways that go beyond code completion or tech support. Cline can even use the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to create new tools and extend his own capabilities. While autonomous AI scripts traditionally run in sandboxed environments, this extension provides a human-in-the-loop GUI to approve every file change and terminal command, providing a safe and accessible way to explore the potential of agentic AI.

  1. Enter your task and add images to convert mockups into functional apps or fix bugs with screenshots.
  2. Cline starts by analyzing your file structure & source code ASTs, running regex searches, and reading relevant files to get up to speed in existing projects. By carefully managing what information is added to context, Cline can provide valuable assistance even for large, complex projects without overwhelming the context window.
  3. Once Cline has the information he needs, he can:
    • Create and edit files + monitor linter/compiler errors along the way, letting him proactively fix issues like missing imports and syntax errors on his own.
    • Execute commands directly in your terminal and monitor their output as he works, letting him e.g., react to dev server issues after editing a file.
    • For web development tasks, Cline can launch the site in a headless browser, click, type, scroll, and capture screenshots + console logs, allowing him to fix runtime errors and visual bugs.
  4. When a task is completed, Cline will present the result to you with a terminal command like open -a "Google Chrome" index.html, which you run with a click of a button.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changed

  • GPT-6.1 Sol is now the default model for OpenAI, OpenRouter, GitHub Copilot, and several other providers, and joins the Cline recommended list. The free list adds Solar Mini 4 and drops DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, and Engy is a new provider. Vultr's model ids were renamed upstream, so a pinned Vultr model may need to be re-selected. If you use a provider without pinning a model, expect a different default.
  • If a model's response ends without a recognized finish reason, Cline asks it to continue once instead of treating the response as complete.
  • Direct requests to Anthropic's API now use Anthropic's server-side refusal fallback, and on OpenRouter and Cline, Anthropic models can fail over to another upstream provider instead of failing the request.

Fixed

  • Closing a project or exiting the IDE while Cline is connected no longer shows the red IDE fatal-error indicator or sends an exception report.
  • HTTP errors such as 404 "model not found" (for example from a local OpenAI-compatible server after a model was renamed), 402, 405, 410, 413, and 422 are no longer treated as authentication failures, so Cline shows what the server actually said instead of asking you to sign in.
  • Cline's agent process no longer crashes when a stdio MCP server exits before reading all of its input, and with the SAP AI Core provider an unrelated error no longer shuts it down a few seconds later.
  • Turning reasoning off no longer breaks requests to models that can't disable it: GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol no longer answer with a 400 error, and Claude Fable 5 and Claude Opus 5.5 no longer reject the request.
  • Canceling right after sending a message now stops the task. A cancel that landed while the turn was still being set up was ignored, and the task kept running.
  • Approve and Reject on a tool approval work right away, even while the panel is still updating. A late update failure no longer rejects a later, unrelated approval.
  • When an MCP tool returns more output than fits in context, Cline can now read the rest. It gets a preview plus a link it can page through with read_files, so output past the cutoff is no longer lost.
  • If a new task fails Cline sign-in, signing in and submitting a revised prompt now starts the task with that prompt. Before, nothing happened.
  • Reset Code is no longer disabled for a message that has a checkpoint. On slow disks the newest message's checkpoint could be missed, and the button stayed disabled for the rest of the session.
  • Kimi K3 and other models that only accept certain reasoning levels no longer reject requests. Cline picks the closest level the model supports.
  • Old tasks no longer show leftover Focus Chain checklist rows when reopened.

idea-plugin.name: Codex Launcher
idea-plugin.description:
Important: Install the OpenAI Codex CLI separately before using this plugin.
Notice: Codex is now officially integrated into JetBrains IDEs. Install the official integration: OpenAI Codex IDE integration. With an official integration now available, this plugin is expected to transition to maintenance-only mode.
For Windows users: Please select your terminal shell in the plugin settings (Settings (→ Other Settings) → Codex Launcher) to ensure proper functionality.

Overview

Codex Launcher is an unofficial IntelliJ IDEA plugin that keeps the OpenAI Codex CLI one click away inside the IDE.

Features

  • One-click launch from the toolbar or Tools menu
  • Integrated terminal that opens a dedicated "Codex" tab in the project root
  • Completion notifications after Codex CLI finishes processing the current run
  • Automatic file opening for files updated by Codex
  • Built-in MCP server pairing with guided setup for IntelliJ's MCP server (2025.2+)
  • Flexible configuration for launch modes, models, and notifications

Usage

  1. Click the Launch Codex button in the main toolbar
  2. Or choose Tools → Launch Codex
  3. The integrated terminal opens a new "Codex" tab and runs codex automatically

Configuration

Open Settings (→ Other Settings) → Codex Launcher to pick the launch mode, model, notification behavior, and auto-open options.

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2024.2 or later (or other compatible JetBrains IDEs)
  • OpenAI Codex CLI installed and available in your system PATH

idea-plugin.name: switch2ai
idea-plugin.description:
switch2ai is a JetBrains IDE plugin that enables seamless collaboration between JetBrains IDEs and various AI agents (Cursor, Qoder, Claude code etc.). Key features include instant switching between different AI editors, rapid AI prompt input with AI selection, and fully configurable custom commands with variable support for enhanced AI collaboration workflow.

GitHub: https://github.com/sinberCS/switch2ai

Key Features

  • Instant AI Editor Switching
  • Maintain exact cursor position (line and column)
  • Support multiple AI agents: Cursor, Qoder, Claude Code, and more
  • Rapid AI prompt input with AI selection
  • Support for shortcut commands like $test, $refactor, $explain
  • Convenient shortcuts (customizable):
    • Alt+Shift+K - Open AI prompt input popup
    • Alt+Shift+P - Open project in Cursor Editor
    • Alt+Shift+O - Open current file in Cursor Editor
    • Alt+Shift+U - Open current file in Qoder
    • Alt+Shift+I - Open project in Qoder
  • Multiple access methods: shortcuts, context menu, tools menu
  • Fully configurable custom commands with variable support
  • Dynamic command registration and management

Usage

  • AI Prompt Input:
    • Press Alt+Shift+K
    • Select AI agent from dropdown
    • Input prompts with shortcut command support
  • Open current file in Cursor:
    • Press Alt+Shift+O
    • Right-click in editor → Open File In Cursor
    • Tools menu → Open File In Cursor
  • Open project in Cursor:
    • Press Alt+Shift+P
    • Right-click in project view → Open Project In Cursor
    • Tools menu → Open Project In Cursor
  • Open in Qoder:
    • Press Alt+Shift+U (file) or Alt+Shift+I (project)
    • Right-click in editor → Open In Qoder
    • Tools menu → Open In Qoder

Configuration

  • Go to Settings/Preferences → Tools → switch2ai
  • AI Configuration tab: Configure AI agents and command templates
  • Custom Commands tab: Configure custom commands with variable support
  • Shortcut Commands tab: Set up shortcut commands like $test, $refactor
  • Customize shortcuts in Keymap settings

Requirements

  • Any AI editor installed (Cursor, Qoder, Claude code, etc.)
  • Compatible with all JetBrains IDEs
  • Supported IDE versions: 2022.3 and above
  • Terminal plugin enabled for integrated terminal execution

switch2ai 是一个 JetBrains IDE 插件，实现 JetBrains IDE 与各种 AI 代理（Cursor、Qoder、Claude code 等）之间的无缝协作。主要功能包括在不同 AI 编辑器之间即时切换、支持 AI 选择的快速 AI 提示词输入，以及支持变量的完全可配置自定义命令，为增强的 AI 协作工作流程提供支持。

GitHub: https://github.com/sinberCS/switch2ai

主要特性

  • 即时 AI 编辑器切换
  • 精确保持光标位置（行号和列号）
  • 支持多种 AI 代理：Cursor、Qoder、Claude Code 等
  • 支持 AI 选择的快速提示词输入弹窗
  • 支持快捷命令如 $test、$refactor、$explain
  • 便捷的快捷键（可自定义）:
    • Alt+Shift+K - 打开 AI 提示词输入弹窗
    • Alt+Shift+P - 在 Cursor 编辑器中打开项目
    • Alt+Shift+O - 在 Cursor 编辑器中打开当前文件
    • Alt+Shift+U - 在 Qoder 中打开当前文件
    • Alt+Shift+I - 在 Qoder 中打开项目
  • 多种访问方式：快捷键、右键菜单、工具菜单
  • 支持变量的完全可配置自定义命令
  • 动态命令注册和管理

使用方法

  • AI 提示词输入:
    • 按下 Alt+Shift+K
    • 从下拉菜单选择 AI 代理
    • 输入提示词，支持快捷命令
  • 在 Cursor 编辑器中打开当前文件:
    • 按下 Alt+Shift+O
    • 在编辑器中右键 → 在 Cursor 编辑器中打开文件
    • 工具菜单 → 在 Cursor 编辑器中打开文件
  • 在 Cursor 编辑器中打开项目:
    • 按下 Alt+Shift+P
    • 在项目视图中右键 → 在 Cursor 编辑器中打开项目
    • 工具菜单 → 在 Cursor 编辑器中打开项目
  • 在 Qoder 中打开:
    • 按下 Alt+Shift+U (文件) 或 Alt+Shift+I (项目)
    • 在编辑器中右键 → 在 Qoder 中打开
    • 工具菜单 → 在 Qoder 中打开

配置说明

  • 进入 Settings/Preferences → Tools → switch2ai
  • AI 配置选项卡：配置 AI 代理和命令模板
  • 自定义命令选项卡：配置支持变量替换的自定义命令
  • 快捷命令选项卡：设置快捷命令如 $test、$refactor
  • 通过 Keymap 设置自定义快捷键

系统要求

  • 已安装任意 AI 编辑器（Cursor、Qoder、Claude code 等）
  • 兼容所有 JetBrains IDE
  • 支持的 IDE 版本：2022.3 及以上
  • 启用 Terminal 插件以支持集成终端执行

idea-plugin.name: Kilo Code
idea-plugin.description:
Kilo Code turns your JetBrains IDE into a multi-agent control room: isolated git worktrees for parallel tasks, native remote-development support, GitHub-aware diffs, and 600+ models — all in one IDE frame.

  • Remote-dev native. 100% native Swing UI, no embedded browser and no Node.js, so it works identically locally and in JetBrains Remote Development split mode.
  • Agent Manager. Run several agent sessions at once, each isolated in its own git worktree, without a new IDE window per task.
  • Run and debug per worktree. Your existing Run Configurations work on any worktree; escalate one to a full IDE frame in a click when you need breakpoints.
  • GitHub built in. Per-worktree PR status, diff versus base branch, uncommitted changes, and one-click import from a PR URL.
  • Model freedom. 600+ models across all major providers, your own API keys or Kilo credits, per-agent model pinning, and org-level access controls.
  • One runtime everywhere. Built on the open-source Kilo CLI — the same engine as Kilo's CLI, VS Code extension, and cloud, sharing one config, agents, skills, and MCP servers.

kilo.ai
idea-plugin.change-notes:
7.1.9 - 2026-10-07

Added

  • Added a prompt navigator to the chat transcript for jumping between your sent prompts.
  • Added MCP OAuth sign-in support, including recovery flows for expired or failed authorizations.
  • Combined MCP and skill badges in the chat UI.
  • Added a core settings reload action.
  • Rendered agent board messages as markdown.

Fixed

  • Fixed hidden session questions not surfacing in the chat UI.
  • Made chat dialogs submit with Cmd/Ctrl+Enter.
  • Fixed spreadsheet date/time handling when reading xlsx and ods files.
  • Finalized reasoning output before stream retries to avoid lost context.
  • Kept storage usable after an interrupted first access.
  • Prevented a rejected attachment from discarding the in-progress prompt.
  • Gated prompt cache breakpoints to first-party OpenAI providers.

Changed

  • Renamed JetBrains workflows to commands.
  • Split agent guidance documentation into skills.
  • Bumped the bundled Kilo CLI pin to v7.8.8 (via v7.8.3 and v7.8.7 intermediate bumps).

7.1.8 - 2026-09-25

Added

  • Add Checkpoints settings for snapshots and automatic session cleanup, including manual cleanup controls and the latest cleanup result.
  • Install companion skills when adding MCP servers from the marketplace.
  • Publish CycloneDX software bills of materials alongside JetBrains release artifacts.
  • Support MCP servers that use client ID metadata documents for OAuth registration.

Fixed

  • Avoid a crash when reloading or unloading the JetBrains plugin while editor history still references Kilo virtual files.
  • Keep model selection isolated to each session, including overlapping agent runs and cleanup.
  • Keep sub-agents that belong to an active chat during session cleanup.
  • Make background-agent and todo strip headers expand, collapse, and highlight consistently while keeping expanded agent links actionable.
  • Show specific revert guidance when snapshots are disabled, a checkpoint is unavailable, or the project is not a Git repository.

Changed

  • Reclaim database space after session cleanup and allow cleanup to be stopped.
  • Speed up switching between worktree session editor tabs with long transcripts and reduce unnecessary Agent Manager list repainting.
  • Trim single-line transcript labels more consistently with an ellipsis when they overflow.

7.1.7 - 2026-09-23

Added

  • Fold and unfold large pasted text blocks directly from the prompt input and transcript.
  • Add a Marketplace page to JetBrains settings for browsing, installing, and removing marketplace agents, MCP servers, and skills without leaving the IDE.
  • Install Marketplace plugins from npm packages or from a git repository (for example git:github.com/owner/repo@v1.2.3#subdir).
  • Add Kilo Swarm support to JetBrains, including an Agent Behavior toggle, readable board tool cards, and a board viewer for session collaboration.
  • Add a cleanup flow for leftover Agent Manager worktree folders, with size reporting, git-checkout warnings, and safe removal from JetBrains.
  • Add unique avatars for subagents and a background agents strip in the session header, with a collapsed preview so active work stays visible without expanding the panel.
  • Add copy path and reveal actions when nested worktree deletion is blocked.
  • Add CLI support for background process monitoring, session cron scheduling, pull request linking, and experimental self-context tools.

Fixed

  • Pause the working timer while waiting on a permission prompt or a question.
  • Prevent snapshot progress from hanging a session.
  • Keep diagnostics edits responsive during large edits.
  • Warn when posting to the shared board targets a stopped subagent.
  • Keep a session goal running when a new message arrives instead of dropping it.
  • Only route auxiliary tasks to kilo-auto/small when using Kilo credentials.
  • Stop looping on repeated malformed tool calls.
  • Keep Keep Awake active while a wakeup is scheduled, and clear it when a session with pending wakeups is deleted.
  • Speed up local recall searches and improve match ranking.
  • Link sessions to their pull requests without a slow, timed gh pr view probe.
  • Submit and cancel custom answers correctly in the question dialog.
  • Format detailed code review findings as distinct sections.
  • Collapse pasted text in JetBrains only after larger 15-line or 4000-character blocks, matching VS Code and avoiding over-folding ordinary snippets.
  • Recover shared agent board reads when a stale or foreign cursor appears, instead of leaving a sub-agent stuck on repeated tool errors.
  • Reduce unnecessary sandbox escalation prompts for read-only git and gh commands while keeping mutating commands protected.
  • Stop a slow gh lookup from blanking PR badges.
  • Make worktree runs use the worktree's own logs and npm configs.
  • Wrap long session status messages instead of clipping them in the JetBrains UI.
  • Normalize markdown line endings before rendering, preventing unexpected formatting breaks in JetBrains chat.
  • Recover pending questions and permission prompts after reconnecting to an existing session.
  • Use normal session model defaults when creating sessions in new worktrees.
  • Ground selected-code prompts in the active editor selection so the agent receives the intended context.
  • Remove deselected models from custom OpenAI-compatible providers, including delete-and-recreate flows and providers saved in another settings scope.
  • Improve Swarm board readability by wrapping long messages, keeping the board open while navigating, and adding copy-all.
  • Explain that file checkpoints require Git when a revert cannot restore files, showing "File checkpoints require a Git repository" instead of the generic "No file checkpoint was available" notice.
  • Keep Agent Manager attention badges in sync with resolved prompts, surface sandbox escalation permissions, and center status glyphs.
  • Keep JetBrains worktree session tabs responsive by deferring and batching transcript updates accumulated while a tab is hidden.
  • Fix the JetBrains shared board dialog layout when resizing and remove redundant message hover tooltips.
  • Add missing JetBrains release locale keys and guard localized bundles against stale entries.
  • Fix git-hosted Marketplace plugins so ~/ repository paths resolve, a failed clone leaves no staging directory, POSIX paths with a backslash are preserved, and uninstalling a plugin deletes its cloned cache when no scope still uses it.

Changed

  • Speed up the first worktree snapshot by skipping unnecessary re-hashing of the checkout.
  • Skip resolving the source project when moving sessions without changes, for faster session moves.

7.1.6 - 2026-09-08

Added

  • Move a session to a worktree directly from the worktree editor.
  • Fork a session from the worktree editor.
  • Add Ctrl+1/2/3/0 shortcuts to cycle mode, model, and reasoning effort.
  • Exclude Kilo worktrees from IntelliJ project indexing.
  • Run project run configurations delegated to Gradle inside a worktree.
  • Surface pull request and run status in the Agent Manager worktree list.

Fixed

  • Refresh pull request badges app-wide when the IDE regains focus.
  • Settle attention badges correctly during auto-approve.
  • Fill session dialog cards with a raised surface instead of a flat background.
  • Fixed config warnings being attributed to the IDE's working directory instead of the actual project, which could show a stray "home directory" warning banner.
  • Fixed worktree deletion blocking the UI for large directories and failing when other worktrees were busy at the same time.
  • Fixed the worktree session list unexpectedly expanding when starting or forking a session.
  • Reduced CLI startup overhead on Windows.
  • Sped up cold session loading.
  • Fixed inference cost showing as $0 for OpenRouter BYOK sessions.

7.1.5 - 2026-09-01

Fixed

  • Keep Agent Manager run/action buttons available while the IDE is indexing, instead of disabling them and showing "waits for analysis" tooltips.

idea-plugin.name: Qdrant
idea-plugin.description:
Qdrant

Inspect and manage Qdrant vector database collections directly from your IDE.

Use one collection workspace for points, configuration, payload analytics, and vector maps. Browse and edit payloads, run advanced filters and vector searches, and explore embeddings with Random, t-SNE, or UMAP projections.

Qdrant 1.7 through 1.19 is continuously tested, with the universal Query API used on current servers.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
6.0.0 (September 2, 2026)

  • Current Qdrant Compatibility — Vector Search and Find Similar now use the universal Query API on current servers while retaining automatic compatibility with Qdrant 1.7–1.9.
  • Collection Workspace - Explore points, collection configuration, payload analytics, and the vector map in one editor tab. Filters, similar-point results, and point details now stay beside the table instead of blocking it with separate windows, and the workspace tabs replace duplicate navigation actions in the Points toolbar.
  • Readable Wide Payload Tables - Browse collections with many payload fields using horizontal scrolling and bounded content-aware column widths. Full clipped headers and values are available as tooltips, while manual widths, order, and visibility survive paging and refresh.
  • UMAP Projection - Explore natural neighborhoods in vector collections with a new UMAP option alongside Random and t-SNE, and keep the selected projection in saved workspace presets.
  • Bounded Vector Maps - Keep large collection visualizations responsive with an explicit 10–2,000 point sample control, a safe 500-point default, deterministic selection, and workspace-preset restore.

5.0.0 (August 1, 2026)

  • Inline Payload Cell Editing - Edit primitive payload values (string, number, boolean, null, or a missing key) directly in the points table. Enter commits, Esc cancels, Tab/Shift+Tab commit and move focus, and clicking away commits too. Invalid input is flagged with a red border and tooltip plus a status message; a successful save shows briefly as pending until the server confirms it, and a failed save rolls back with a red flash. Objects and arrays are unaffected and still open the full point editor.
  • Batch Payload and Delete Operations - Select two or more points in the table and use the new "Batch Edit Payload" toolbar action to set a payload key to a JSON value or remove it across the whole selection; the existing delete now also processes each selected point independently. Both report per-point success and failure ("N of M succeeded", with each failed point's id and reason) instead of aborting the entire batch on a single error.
  • Saved Workspace Presets - Bookmark a combination of connection, collection, current filter, active payload/vector search, and page size as a named preset from the new "Presets" toolbar menu, then reapply it in one click. Presets survive an IDE restart; saving under an existing name asks for overwrite confirmation, and applying a preset whose connection or collection no longer exists shows a warning without touching the current view. A "Manage Presets…" entry lets you rename or delete saved presets.
  • Progress and Cancellation for Long-Running Operations - Batch payload edits, batch deletes, point imports, payload analytics, and vector visualization sampling now show a determinate progress bar with a running "N of M" status and can be cancelled from the IDE's progress popup. Cancelling stops the operation immediately without further server calls and reports the partial result through the same status label and notification used for partial failures.
  • Rebindable Qdrant Shortcuts - Refresh (F5), open the selected collection (Enter), and delete the selected connection or collection (Delete/Backspace) in the Qdrant tool window are now regular IDE actions and can be reassigned from Settings | Keymap under Plug-ins → Qdrant. Default keys and behaviour are unchanged.

4.1.0 (June 30, 2026)

  • Fixed Pagination on UUID Collections - Browsing points no longer fails with a JSON parsing error when a collection uses UUID point IDs and the page size is smaller than the total number of points. Pages now load correctly regardless of integer or UUID point IDs.

4.0.0 (June 12, 2026)

  • Clear Error Messages - Failed operations now show the real reason instead of an empty result. The points view, vector search, and collection tree tell you what went wrong instead of silently showing "0 points".
  • Reliable Search Feedback - Vector search and "Find Similar" distinguish a real error from "no matching points", and invalid vector input is reported clearly.
  • Detailed Import Results - Point import reports each failed point with its reason, so partial imports are easy to diagnose.
  • Add Point Error Reporting - Failures when adding a point are now surfaced instead of being silently ignored.
  • Fixed API Key Restore - An API key carried over from a previous version could fail to load on first use; it now loads correctly.
  • Smoother UI - More operations run in the background, keeping the interface responsive while data loads.

3.0.0 (December 15, 2025)

  • Named Vectors Support - Full multi-vector collections handling
  • Sparse Vectors Support - Create collections with sparse vectors, display sparse data
  • Advanced Filter Builder - Visual query constructor with all Qdrant operators
  • Search History - Save and reuse vector, payload, and filter searches
  • Filter Templates - Predefined common filters with field placeholders
  • Recommend API - Find similar points based on positive/negative examples
  • Payload Autocomplete - Key suggestions with type hints from schema
  • Local Qdrant Auto-Detection - Automatically add localhost:6333 connection
  • Secure API Key Storage - Credentials stored in system keychain
  • Ktor HTTP Client - Modern async HTTP with coroutines support
  • HTTPS/TLS Support - Full URL-based connection with http:// and https:// schemes
  • Connection Import/Export - Share connection configs via JSON
  • Point Export/Import - Export visible points to JSON/CSV
  • Collection Info Panel - View collection config, segments, optimizer status
  • Collection Statistics Dashboard - Points, vectors, index status, shards info
  • Payload Analytics - Field distributions, histograms, value frequencies
  • Vector Space Visualization - 2D projection with random projection, zoom/pan, color by field
  • Enhanced Table - Dynamic payload columns, sorting, alternating row colors, type-based coloring
  • Copy Context Menu - Copy cell value, row as JSON, or point ID
  • Column Visibility - Show/hide any table column

idea-plugin.name: OpenRouter
idea-plugin.description:
OpenRouter IntelliJ Plugin — a lightweight integration layer that brings OpenRouter specifically into JetBrains IDEs: your curated model list, model variants, provider routing, presets, and real credit and spend figures read from OpenRouter itself.

When this plugin is useful

  • 📊 Usage monitoring — view OpenRouter credits, spending, and activity stats directly in the IDE
  • 💰 Quota & balance visibility — real-time status bar widget with credit balance, cost tracking, and "days remaining" estimates
  • 🔑 A Management Key reads your account; an ordinary API key reads itself — either key sends chat requests, but the balance, per-model breakdown and activity history are account data and need a Management Key. With an ordinary key you still see that key's own spend and cap.
  • ⭐ Model selection — manage favorite models and custom presets, switch between models easily
  • 🔌 Local proxy — run an OpenAI-compatible proxy server that other tools and agents can reuse
  • 🔑 API key management — secure OAuth/PKCE authentication and management key support

When you may not need this plugin

If your only goal is to connect Android Studio's or IntelliJ's native AI Agent directly to OpenRouter, using a regular OpenRouter API key in the native AI Agent settings may be the simpler option. This plugin is not intended to replace the native JetBrains AI or Android Studio AI Agent workflow.

  • Not a generic LLM gateway. The proxy talks to OpenRouter's own endpoints; it does not point at other providers. For one endpoint in front of many providers, with virtual keys, budgets and rate limits, a dedicated gateway such as LiteLLM is the better fit.
  • Not a coding agent. For agentic work, pair this plugin's inference with AI Assistant's agent loop and MCP servers for tool execution — the setup guide covers it.

Key Features

  • 🔐 OAuth/PKCE Authentication — secure authentication flow with automatic API key generation
  • 🚀 AI Assistant Proxy — local OpenAI-compatible proxy that can be reused by other tools and agents
  • 📊 Interactive Status Bar Widget — real-time usage display with comprehensive popup menu
  • 🔑 API Key Management — secure management key support with scope-aware validation
  • 📈 Usage Analytics — track token consumption, costs, and model performance
  • ⭐ Favorite Models — quick access to your preferred AI models with reasoning and verbosity controls
  • 🔄 Dynamic Plugin Support — install, update, and uninstall without IDE restart

Quick Start

  1. Install the plugin (no restart required)
  2. Use OAuth/PKCE flow or add your Management Key from OpenRouter
  3. Configure in Settings → Tools → OpenRouter
  4. Click the status bar widget to access all features
  5. (Optional) Set up the local proxy for external tools — Setup Guide

This is an unofficial plugin and is not affiliated with OpenRouter.ai or JetBrains.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
🎉 Version 0.7.0 - Requests Tab, Routers Hub, Models With Presets, Status Tab Redesign, Web Search & Structured Output (2026-10-03)

📋 Requests Tab:

  • Every Request in One List - Requests from the chat and from tools using the proxy, with sender, model, provider, tokens, cost, stop reason and a link to the request's own OpenRouter log
  • Warnings - An error or a reply cut off at the token limit or by a content filter is marked and announced in a balloon; bursts from one tool fold into one row
  • Prompt and Reply, Opt-In - Off by default; when on, bodies are kept as plain text and deleted with their request

🧭 Routers Hub:

  • First-Class Routers - openrouter/auto, fusion, pareto-code, fusion-flash and free are treated as routers, not presets, and the proxy lists every one of them in /v1/models, so AI Assistant and other tools can pick them
  • Router Defaults - A settings page sets each router's parameter once; the proxy applies it unless a tool sends its own
  • In the Chat - A Routers group in the model picker with an editable router parameter, and a "Routed to" note under each routed reply

🧩 Models Paired With Presets:

  • Add with Preset - Pairs a favourite with one of your presets as <model>@preset/<slug>, served as its own model in /v1/models
  • The Preset Wins - The proxy drops a tool's fields that the preset sets; a pair that cannot work is hidden, marked and refused
  • Presets Edited in the IDE - A dialog lists every setting a preset can have; the chat can save its controls as a preset

📊 Status Tab Redesign:

  • Real Account Balance - Read from your account credits, the same figures the status bar shows, instead of a sum of key limits
  • Spend at a Glance - A spend sparkline, burn rate, days-left estimate and spend by model over 24 hours, 7 or 30 days
  • Works With an Ordinary API Key - Shows that key's own spend and cap instead of an error; account-wide figures need a Management Key

🚦 Clear Errors for Tools Using the Proxy:

  • Refused Before It Is Sent - A request that cannot work gets an error naming the problem and the settings page that fixes it

🔎 Web Search and Structured Output:

  • In the Chat - Per-message web search, and an Output mode of plain JSON or a saved Output Schema
  • Reply Summary - Under every reply: the model, the provider, the cost and the web searches, with a warning when it did not stop normally
  • New Settings Pages - Web Search (engine, results, domains, mode) and Output Schemas (named JSON Schemas, validated as typed)

💬 Chat Redesign:

  • Readable Conversations - Message bubbles, long replies no longer clipped, and the model that answered kept on every reply
  • Compact Composer - Send parameters in a gear popup, and a layout that collapses predictably in a narrow tool window

🌍 In-Region Routing:

  • Data Region - Pin every request to eu.openrouter.ai or us.openrouter.ai, offered only where your keys allow it, with the favourites a region cannot serve counted before you switch

🧰 Smaller Improvements:

  • Tables - Columns can be moved in every table; View Quota Usage lists every recent model and colours the credits bar

🔧 Fixes:

  • Clean on 2025.3 to 2026.3 - No deprecated platform API reported on 2026 IDEs
  • No Freezes - Credential reads and writes, and opening Settings from the Status tab, no longer block the UI
  • Proxy Robustness - Misshapen request and error bodies are answered instead of failing with a bare HTTP 500

⚖️ License: The plugin is now distributed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 instead of MIT.

Full Changelog

🔧 Smart Features:
