Part of the PyArchInit ecosystem - professional tools for serious developers.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Version 2026.9.1

  • Fix: Doxygen / JavaDoc / JSDoc output was empty. Selecting one of these formats produced no documentation files at all (with AI enabled the output folder contained only the agent's API_REFERENCE.md). These formats now generate the full Markdown documentation set plus the tool configuration (Doxyfile, javadoc.args, jsdoc.json) and run doxygen / javadoc / jsdoc automatically when the tool is installed; otherwise the console prints the exact command to run.
  • Fix: JavaScript files were never documented. The AST walker expected dict nodes while esprima returns Node objects, so every .js / .jsx / .ts file yielded zero elements. Classes, functions and arrow functions are now extracted, and ES-module files (import / export) are parsed as well.
  • Fix: AI API overview no longer overwrites the detailed API reference — it is saved as API_OVERVIEW.md next to the full API_REFERENCE.md.
  • Fix: Markdown README.md links pointed to a non-existent docs/ folder; they now link to the generated per-file pages.

Version 2026.9.0

  • Fix: Claude generation failing with HTTP 400 ("temperature is deprecated for this model"). Anthropic removed sampling parameters on Claude 4.7+ models, so every call with claude-opus-4-8 (and newer) failed. Claude requests no longer send temperature; output faithfulness is enforced via the system prompt.
  • New cloud models: OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-luna (Responses API); Anthropic claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-haiku-4-5. Previous-generation entries remain selectable. Thinking is disabled explicitly on Claude so the whole token budget goes to documentation text.
  • Fix: scan options are now persisted: "Recursive scan", "Include private members", "Include test files" and "Include utility scripts" survive IDE restarts instead of silently resetting to defaults.
  • Fix: "Include utility scripts" can now be turned off — unchecking it previously had no effect because the generator default was always on.

Version 2026.8.0

  • Cleaner Marketplace verification: removed a call to the internal IntelliJ API PluginManagerCore.getPlugins() that the Plugin Verifier flagged ("1 usage of internal API"). It backed an unreliable fallback that scanned every installed plugin for "ai"/"grazie" in the name; JetBrains AI is still detected via the more reliable classpath checks. No functional change.

Version 2026.7.0

  • Ollama & LM Studio support (local LLMs): both are now first-class AI providers in the AI Settings tab, alongside OpenAI and Claude. They run entirely on your machine — no API key, no cloud. The plugin talks to them over their OpenAI-compatible API (Ollama on :11434, LM Studio on :1234). The previous "Local LLM" placeholder (which never actually generated anything) has been removed.
  • Pick the model you have loaded: a 🔄 Refresh button next to the model selector queries your local server's /v1/models and lists exactly the models it currently exposes, so you select the one that's actually running. The field is also editable if you prefer to type the id. "Test Connection" now verifies the local server is reachable and reports how many models it found.
  • Updated cloud models: OpenAI gpt-5.5 and gpt-5.5-mini (Responses API); Anthropic claude-opus-4-8 added alongside claude-sonnet-4-6. Older gpt-5.4 / claude-opus-4-6 entries removed.
  • Fixes: the local-server URL is now actually passed to the generator (it was collected in the UI but never used); the selected AI provider now persists correctly across restarts (it was saved in a format the loader couldn't read).

Version 2026.6.0

  • Plugin size reduced from ~45 MB to a few hundred KB: the build was bundling jython-standalone (47 MB) and jackson-databind, neither of which is referenced anywhere in the plugin — documentation generation runs the system python3 as an external process, it does not embed a Python interpreter. Removing these dead dependencies fixes the JetBrains Plugin Verifier error "the plugin archive file cannot be extracted" (the giant multi-thousand-entry jython jar was the cause) and makes the Marketplace download dramatically faster. No functional change.

Version 2026.5.0

  • "Patterns to Ignore" list is now editable: previously the list was read-only and never read on the Java side. The Configuration tab now has +/- toolbar buttons so you can add custom exclusions (e.g. ext_libs, vendor, third_party). Patterns are substring-matched against full file paths and merged with the built-in defaults. Persisted across sessions.
  • OpenAI connection test fixed: the test snippet was sending max_output_tokens=5, which the Responses API rejects with HTTP 400 (minimum is 16). Bumped to 16.
  • Configuration tab no longer overlaps: the "File Patterns to Include" label and the list below it shared the same grid row, so the label rendered on top of the first list entries. Each list now sits on its own row, and the entire Configuration tab is wrapped in a scroll pane so a narrow tool window no longer clips the bottom controls.

Version 2026.4.0

  • "Recursive scan" checkbox now actually works: the checkbox in the Configuration tab was previously cosmetic — the value was never read on the Java side and never passed to the Python generator, so subdirectories were always scanned regardless of the setting. The flag now flows UI → Java → Python via a new --no-recursive CLI argument.
  • MkDocs index links fixed: the per-file pages are at docs/files/<file>_py.md, but the generated docs/index.md was still linking to docs/<file>_py.md (a leftover from the plain Markdown layout). Links now resolve to the actual page locations.
  • .claude/ excluded by default: Claude Code creates per-branch worktrees under .claude/worktrees/; without an exclusion the generator was documenting hundreds of files from those scratch checkouts. Added to the default ignore list alongside .git, .venv, etc.

Version 2026.3.0

  • MkDocs output now generates the full documentation set: previously only mkdocs.yml, docs/index.md, and a brief docs/api.md were produced no matter what was configured. The MkDocs generator now emits per-file API pages under docs/files/, the detailed docs/api_reference.md, the optional docs/class_diagram.md (when class diagrams are enabled), and a nav that lists only pages actually generated. Tutorial pages produced when AI is enabled are now also routed into docs/ so MkDocs picks them up. Fixes the customer-reported issue where MkDocs always produced just three files. The dead reference to a non-existent examples.md in the navigation has been removed.

Version 2026.2.0

  • Tutorial PDF — brand-new "manual" style: the tutorial PDF now uses a dedicated layout completely separate from the API reference. Cover page with project title and subtitle ("User Guide" localized by target language), coloured chapter/section headings in brand blue (#1A5490), page header with project name, styled code blocks, and coloured admonition boxes (Tip / Warning / Note / Example) via tcolorbox LaTeX.
  • AI agents use admonitions: tutorial agents (Interface Explainer, Quick Start, Tutorial Series, Troubleshooting, Example Generator) now emit pandoc fenced-div admonitions (::: tip / warning / note / example) where appropriate, which render as coloured callout boxes in the manual PDF.
  • Tutorial agents now output Markdown instead of RST, so the admonition syntax works end-to-end. API reference (non-AI) output is unchanged.
  • UI simplified — single primary button: removed the confusing duplicate buttons "Generate Documentation", "Generate with AI", "Export to Sphinx", "Export as EPUB". One primary "Generate" button now dispatches automatically based on the selected AI provider. During generation the same button turns red and becomes "Stop" — no more hunting for a hidden Stop button. The "Output Formats" tab with duplicate cards has been removed; format selection lives in the Configuration tab dropdown.
  • Version Bump: 2026.1.0 → 2026.2.0

Version 2026.1.0

  • IntelliJ 2026.1 (261) Compatibility: until-build removed — plugin now runs on all future IDE versions without requiring republish
  • New AI Models: OpenAI GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.4-mini (via Responses API), Claude Opus 4.6 and Claude Sonnet 4.6

  • Deterministic Output: temperature locked to 0.1 and explicit faithfulness prompts across all AI call-sites — AI agents no longer invent parameters, methods, or behaviors that are not in the source
  • UI Refresh: model combo now filters by selected provider, titled borders group sections, model tooltips explain cost/speed tradeoffs, default max tokens raised to 4000
  • Markdown/Sphinx Output Quality: consistent heading hierarchy, code-fence language tags, cleaner RST underline handling

idea-plugin.name: Spring Explyt
idea-plugin.description:
Explyt Spring Plugin — Free Spring Boot plugin for IntelliJ IDEA Community (Java, Kotlin, Quarkus)

Runtime-accurate Spring tooling for IntelliJ IDEA Community — free for commercial and non-commercial use. Explyt loads your application's real Spring context via a lightweight javaagent, so beans, endpoints, and inspections reflect what your app actually wires up — not a static guess.

Bring powerful Spring and Spring Boot tooling to IntelliJ IDEA Community Edition. Build, navigate, test, and debug faster with:

  • Accurate bean discovery and real context understanding (native context mode via javaagent)
  • Tool windows for Beans/Contexts and Endpoints
  • Built‑in HTTP client (OpenAPI/Swagger UI + .http/.rest runners)
  • Spring Debugger (including runtime Spring property lenses)
  • Spring Data, JPA, AOP, Docker/K8s, and lots of inspections & quick fixes
  • Quarkus CDI/JAX‑RS/AOP support
  • Optional AI helpers for Spring tasks
  • Spring-aware MCP tools for agentic AI clients (IntelliJ IDEA 2025.2+)

Why developers choose Explyt

  • Faster feedback: precise inspections, completion and navigation eliminate wiring guesswork.
  • True Spring context awareness: lightweight native context run extracts real bean/config metadata, including conditional and factory beans.
  • Seamless API testing: run HTTP requests via Swagger UI in the IDE or execute .http/.rest files.

Highlights

Tool Windows

  • Explyt Spring: load real bean metadata, browse contexts, navigate beans, view aspects, and open Bean Analyzer.
    • Video: How Native Context Mode works in Explyt Spring panel
  • Explyt Endpoints: view and navigate endpoints for MVC/WebFlux, router functions, and message brokers (Kafka/RabbitMQ listeners).
    • Video: How Explyt Endpoints Tool Window works

Accurate Bean Detection & Context Analysis

  • Detects beans via annotations, factory methods and conditional logic (@Conditional, profiles, complex scans).
  • Native context mode eliminates many false positives by using real Spring logic.
  • Supports projects with multiple application contexts.
  • Autowiring/inspections also consider library beans (from dependencies), not only project sources.

Inlay Hints & Code Vision

  • @Profile inlay hints show the computed result of profile expressions (e.g. "prod & !cloud" → true/false).
  • @Scheduled cron completion + hints (including zone attribute).
  • During Explyt debug sessions: runtime property value Code Vision in .properties / .yml (helps locate the PropertySource).

HTTP Client: OpenAPI/Swagger UI + .http/.rest

  • Generate OpenAPI from Spring Web–annotated methods; open Swagger UI directly in the IDE.
  • Execute requests, inspect responses, copy cURL.
  • Execute .http/.rest files with JetBrains HttpClient CLI or httpyac.

Code Generation

Use Generate (Alt+Insert / Command+N):

  • Generate Spring Web Method from URL/cURL (Java & Kotlin).
  • Generate HttpClient Method from URL/cURL (standalone java.net.http.HttpClient code, Java & Kotlin).
  • Generate JPA equals/hashCode for Java entities using a proxy-safe approach.
  • Properties ↔ YAML conversion.

Advanced Navigation & Analysis

  • Beans in Search Everywhere: dedicated Beans tab in Search Everywhere (Shift Shift).
  • Bean Analyzer: visualize relationships between loaded beans and navigate to declarations.
  • Mark directory as Spring Application Property Folder: enable completion/validation for non-standard config locations.
  • SPI beans: navigation and gutter markers for beans produced via Java SPI (ServiceLoader).

Spring Boot & Web Enhancements

  • Duplicate endpoint detection, OpenAPI validation, and better MockMvc/WebClient/WebTestClient support.
  • Docker Compose + Kubernetes: completion for Spring properties as environment variables (server.port → SERVER_PORT).

Spring Debugger

  • Dedicated run configuration with a lightweight javaagent; shows Spring Context and Active Transaction in debugger tree.
  • Evaluate Spring context and call bean methods at breakpoints (Explyt.context helpers).
  • Inline run markers on Spring Data repositories to auto-populate Evaluate Expression during debug.

Spring Initializr

  • Create Spring Boot projects (Java/Kotlin) with improved templates from start.spring.io.
  • Integrated UX: create Spring projects inside the IDE.
  • Always up to date.

Quarkus support

  • CDI/DI navigation and inspections, JAX‑RS endpoints, interceptors/decorators, Endpoints tool window.
  • Works by static analysis, many features available without running the app.

AI integration

  • AI actions:
    • DB schema ↔ JPA entity,
    • Entity ↔ DTO,
    • controller ↔ OpenAPI round‑trips,
    • Spring config generators,
    • HTTP conversions.
  • Works with OpenAI‑compatible providers or local models; requires IntelliJ Platform 2025.1+ for AI features.
  • Requires Explyt plugin to enable AI features.

MCP Server tools

  • Supports the bundled JetBrains MCP Server in IntelliJ IDEA 2025.2+.
  • Adds Spring-aware MCP tools so agentic clients can inspect Spring Boot applications and project beans with less generic code exploration.
  • Current tools: explyt_get_spring_boot_applications, explyt_get_project_beans_by_spring_boot_application, explyt_find_spring_endpoint (find endpoints by URL pattern), explyt_get_spring_http_endpoints (list all HTTP endpoints with filters), explyt_get_spring_endpoint_contract (full API contract with DTO schema), explyt_trace_spring_call_chain (trace Controller → Service → Repository call chains with test references), and explyt_get_spring_data_entities (list JPA entities with table/column mappings, primary keys, relationships, and indexes).

Getting started

  1. Open the Explyt Spring tool window → Link Explyt Spring Boot Project From RunConfiguration → Load Beans.
  2. Open the Explyt Endpoints tool window to explore web + message broker endpoints.
  3. Use Search Everywhere (Shift Shift) → Beans tab to jump to any bean.
  4. Use Bean Analyzer to explore the bean dependency graph.
  5. Use Generate to create Spring Web methods or HttpClient code from URL/cURL.

Installation

  • .http/.rest runners: install JetBrains HttpClient CLI from plugin settings, or use httpyac.

Links

  • Documentation: https://explyt.ai/docs/category/explyt-spring
  • Source: https://github.com/explyt/spring-plugin
  • Full Changelog: https://github.com/explyt/spring-plugin/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

Support & community

  • Issues/feature requests: https://github.com/explyt/spring-plugin/issues
  • Telegram (EN): https://t.me/explytspring_en
  • Telegram (RU): https://t.me/explytspring

License

  • Licensed under the Apache License 2.0.

Search keywords

spring plugin for intellij, spring boot tooling community edition, explyt spring, spring explyt, native spring context,

Thank you for using Explyt Spring Plugin! — ⭐ star us on GitHub and rate the plugin on Marketplace to help more developers discover it.

idea-plugin.name: DBSeed4SQL
idea-plugin.description:
A smart SQL seed generator that respects your schema's integrity. This plugin generates synthetic data by introspecting your database's `DatabaseMetaData`. It automatically analyzes table dependencies, manages foreign keys, and resolves complex cycles using Tarjan's algorithm. Stop writing manual insert scripts for your test environments.

Main Features

  • Schema introspection via DatabaseMetaData.
  • Table sorting using Tarjan's algorithm to detect cycles.
  • Synthetic data generation with DataFaker.
  • Cycle handling with deferred constraints.
  • Support for multiple databases with dynamic driver downloads (explicit user confirmation).

Network and Privacy

  • The plugin works locally by default and stores settings in IDE-local configuration files.
  • Optional network actions are initiated by the user: JDBC driver downloads from Maven Central and AI calls to a user-configured Ollama server.
  • DBSeed4SQL does not upload database row contents. For AI generation, only metadata/context provided by the user (for example table/column names and app context text) is sent.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Version 1.3.7.4

  • Pluggable AI Engine: the AI layer is now abstracted behind one client interface, so the plugin is no longer tied to Ollama. The engine is chosen with radio buttons in Settings → DBSeed4SQL → AI, and picking one applies its own configuration: the URL field is pre-filled with that engine's default address and the API key field is shown only for engines that use one — Ollama has no credential at all, so its row is not displayed, and for the other engines it stays disabled while AI generation is off.
  • Unsloth Studio Support: Unsloth Studio (http://localhost:8888) is now supported out of the box — it lists models from /v1/models, generates through streaming /v1/chat/completions and sends the API key as a Bearer token. The same client serves any other OpenAI-compatible server (LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp, OpenRouter…).
  • Unsloth Studio Authentication: Unsloth Studio answers 401 to every request that carries no credential, and its login accepts either the sk-unsloth-… key — created inside Unsloth Studio under Settings → API, where it is shown once — or a session token. The single Password / API key field takes both: an API key travels as it is, while the password you sign in to Unsloth Studio with is exchanged for a session token at /api/auth/login (the account name is read from /api/auth/status, and the token is reused until it expires). A refused sign-in reports the server's own reason — such as Incorrect password — without ever echoing the password. When the server refuses any other request, its reason ({"error":{"message":…}}) reaches the notification too, instead of a raw JSON dump. Thinking is turned off per request (enable_thinking: false), which Unsloth leaves on by default.
  • API Key Out Of The Settings File: the AI credential is kept in the IDE credential store, the same keychain used for database connections, instead of the plugin's plain-text XML — one entry per engine, so switching engines shows that engine's own credential (and hides the row for Ollama, which has none) and never leaves the previous engine's secret in the field. A credential saved by an older version, when there was only one, is moved to the engine that was configured at the time.
  • Ollama Unchanged: the native Ollama API behaves exactly as before — same endpoints, same JSON schema through the format parameter, same streaming and reasoning guards — and an existing configuration keeps its URL and model, migrated to the new setting names the first time the settings are loaded.

Version 1.3.7.3

  • AI Values Without Reasoning Leaks: reasoning models (Qwen3/DeepSeek style) write their chain-of-thought inside the streamed response, and the first rows of an AI column ended up holding that thinking instead of the requested values. AI generation now requests a JSON schema through the Ollama format parameter, so prose cannot be emitted at all; when a server ignores that schema, the plain-text fallback still discards reasoning blocks and reasoning-only lines, values of array columns must match the requested element count, and answers that only echo a template placeholder (such as value1 or full_name_2) are rejected instead of seeded.
  • Live Generation Progress Dialog: generation now runs behind a non-modal dialog with four live bars — overall work units, tables completed, AI columns finished, and AI values arriving from the stream — plus phase text and a non-blocking Cancel. The first line names the phase only, while the AI values bar names the column of the batch in flight, so the column name is not repeated on every bar. The detail line is laid out in fixed slots: the words never move and the digits are refreshed at most once every 2 seconds, always with the freshest values, so the line stays readable no matter how fast values arrive. A Background button hides the window without cancelling the generation — it keeps running, with its progress in the IDE progress widget — and leaves a notification whose Show progress link brings the window back; while the window is hidden, a DBSeed4SQL entry in the IDE status bar brings it back too, so the window stays reachable even after the notification fades away.
  • Honest Progress From The Start: the task now starts once the dialog is on screen, so the bars reflect the real workload instead of opening at 100%.
  • Configurable AI Column Parallelism: AI columns are now generated one at a time by default, matching what a single-slot Ollama server can serve, and a new setting — Generate AI columns in parallel plus a thread count (1-16) — restores concurrent generation for servers that accept several requests at once. Each generation run now owns its worker pool instead of sharing a static one, so two runs can no longer compete for the same threads.
  • IntelliJ 2026.2 Baseline: minimum supported build raised to 262.

Version 1.3.7.0

  • IntelliJ 2026.2 Ready: Removed all internal API usages — the plugin now passes the Plugin Verifier cleanly on 2025.1 through 2026.2 EAP.
  • Broader IDE Support: Dropped the unnecessary Java module dependency, so the plugin can now be installed on DataGrip, PyCharm, WebStorm, and other IntelliJ-based IDEs.
  • Responsive Driver Downloads: JDBC driver downloads now run under a cancelable progress dialog instead of freezing the UI, with proper retry behavior after a failed download.
  • Resource Cleanup: The shutdown listener now actually runs on IDE close (drivers, HTTP client, and executors are released), profile deletion also removes stored credentials, and two memory leaks in schema caches were fixed.
  • Dialog Fixes: Initial checkbox synchronization in the data configuration dialog, circular-reference settings no longer persisted when canceling, and the Schema Designer no longer loses an in-progress cell edit when clicking OK.

Version 1.3.6.1

  • Bug Fixes: Fixed crashes, data integrity issues, and edge cases across the data generation pipeline, schema introspection, constraint parsing, SQL generation, and UI dialogs.
  • Performance Improvements: Improved thread safety, optimized UUID generation, moved file I/O off the EDT, and added proper resource cleanup on IDE shutdown.

Version 1.3.6

  • Regex-Based Column Rules: Added regex-powered value generation inside the repetition rules panel for fine-grained control over generated string formats.
  • Safer Exclusions: The advanced selection dialog now warns when excluded tables or columns may create foreign-key inconsistencies.
  • Connection Profile Workflow: Improved saved connection profile handling, sanitization, and settings integration for multi-database projects.
  • Selection UX Polish: Clearer selected-count feedback and better bulk-selection behavior across generation dialogs.

Version 1.3.5.1

  • Little Column Selector Hotfix: Fixed the Select All / Deselect All toggle button not switching to "Deselect All" when all enabled checkboxes were selected but disabled ones were present.

Version 1.3.5

  • Circular Reference Termination Modes: Introduced per-table configurable termination modes for circular dependencies, giving users fine-grained control over how FK cycles are broken (e.g., set-null vs. keep-reference strategies).
  • Progress Tracking Improvements: Redesigned the ProgressTracker to use accurate work-unit accounting across all generation phases (row generation, AI, constraint validation, and FK resolution), resulting in a smooth and predictable progress bar.
  • AI Generation Stability: Fixed edge cases where AI column generation could stall or silently fail; added bounded parallelism with a daemon thread pool and proper cancellation propagation.
  • Repetition Rules Panel: Added a dedicated UI panel for configuring repetition rules per column directly within the generation dialog.
  • Dependency Updates: Bumped test-runtime drivers (PostgreSQL 42.7.7, MySQL 9.3.0, SQLite 3.47.2.0, H2 2.4.240) and transitive dependency constraint for commons-compress to 1.28.0 to stay clear of known CVEs.
  • Connection Profile Manager: Save, rename, and switch between multiple database connection profiles from the seed dialog. No more retyping JDBC URLs, credentials, or schema names when working with several databases.
  • Minor Bug Fixes: Various stability improvements and null-safety hardening across the data-generation pipeline.

Version 1.3.4

  • Circular Reference Handling: Improved cyclic dependency resolution between tables to generate safer scripts across dialects.
  • Cycle Execution Strategy: Added clearer fallback behavior using deferred constraints when available, or INSERT + UPDATE steps when not.
  • Documentation Update: Expanded README notes for circular-reference workflows and expected SQL generation behavior.

Version 1.3.3

  • Ready for Production: Minor fixes and tweaks for stable release.
  • Searchable Options: Enabled searchable options for better configuration indexing.
  • Java 21 Alignment: Documentation and build system consistency.

Version 1.3.0

  • AI-Powered Data Generation (Ollama): Generate context-aware, realistic data using an external Ollama LLM server.
    • New "AI Columns" tab in the configuration dialog lets you choose which string columns get AI-generated content.
    • Configurable word count per AI value (one word up to full paragraphs).
    • Note: only the column name along with the context previously provided by the user is sent to the AI.
  • AI Settings in Global Configuration:
    • Enable/disable AI generation, set Ollama URL and model. You can use whether local or cloud-based models.
    • "Get models" button with a live server connectivity check.
    • Application context text area to guide the AI towards your domain.
    • Words per AI value spinner to control output length.
  • Auto-Detect SQL Dialect: DialectFactory now auto-detects the correct dialect from the driver class name or JDBC URL when no explicit dialect is configured.
  • Dialect System Cleanup: Removed property-driven check constraint configuration from dialect files. Dialects are now simpler and more maintainable.
  • Improved Error Handling: Seed actions now show modal error dialogs instead of balloon notifications, with proper thread-safe modality state.
  • Repetition Rule Fix: String values in repetition rule fixed columns are now properly parsed into their typed representation before use.

Version 1.2.5

  • Multi-Dialect Support: Added support for SQLite and improved driver configuration for various SQL dialects.
  • Performance Optimizations:
    • Optimized SQL generation and string concatenation.
    • Improved Schema Introspection to avoid N+1 queries.
    • Implemented caching for dictionary words and identifier quoting.
    • Optimized UUID generation.
  • New Features & Configuration:
    • Added user-configurable numeric scale for data generation.
    • Implemented Soft Delete configuration.
    • Improved decimal handling and repetition rules.
    • Refactored Settings UI for better usability.
  • Stability: Comprehensive test suite implementation and bug fixes.

Previous Versions

  • Plugin Renamed: The plugin has been renamed from "Database Seed Generator" to "DBSeed4SQL" to better reflect its functionality and branding.
  • Configurable Dictionaries for Data Generation: Introduced flexible dictionary usage with checkboxes for Latin (Faker default), English, and Spanish. Users can now combine these dictionaries to generate more realistic and contextually relevant string data.
  • Batch Query Execution: Optimized SQL script generation to execute queries in batches, significantly improving performance for large datasets.
  • Configuration Window: Introduced a dedicated configuration window within the IDE, allowing users to easily customize default settings and generation parameters.
  • Warning Pop-up for Large Row Generation: Added a warning pop-up to alert users when generating a large number of rows, preventing accidental overload.
  • Show Password Toggle in Input Field: Implemented a "show password" toggle (eye icon) in password input field for improved usability.
  • Overall Performance Improvements: Significant enhancements across the plugin for a smoother and faster user experience.
  • Migrate to Java 21: The plugin has been fully migrated to Java 21, ensuring compatibility with the latest Java features and better performance.
  • Select All Primary Keys Feature: The PK selection dialog now allows selecting all primary keys at once, streamlining workflows when working with complex schemas.
  • Exclude Columns Tab: Added a user interface tab that lets users exclude specific columns from synthetic data generation, offering increased flexibility and customization for testing scenarios.
  • UI Fixes and Improvements: The cancel button in dialogs now works reliably. Minor interface enhancements and wording improvements were also made for better usability.
  • Copyright and Minor Enhancements: Copyright statements have been updated and minor bugs have been fixed for a smoother experience.
  • Primary Key Selection Bug Fixes: Several fixes were applied to the PK Selection Dialog, addressing stability and functional issues.

idea-plugin.name: Flexible Solidity
idea-plugin.description:
Local Solidity IDE. Real live debugging, 18+ security inspections, audit reports, gas optimization, refactoring. Hardhat & Foundry. Language Server support (Nomic Foundation & solc --lsp).

We are a fairly new plugin. With an entirely new grammar and plugin architecture. For this matter, your feedback is super crucial for us: Please leave a review, reach out to us on github, or per mail and tell us your thoughts, report issues and more. Anyone providing feedback can request a 20% discount for their next purchase.

Core Features:

Run / Debug

  • Live Debugging Debug execution of Solidity code in the editor (Select "Foundry" as a runtime and "Live Debugging (Anvil)" as debug mode)
  • Solidity SDK Support Configure solc like Go/Python SDKs in Project Structure

Language Support

  • Complete Solidity grammar with support for latest language features (0.8.x+)
  • LSP support (User enabled via Fileâ†’Settingsâ†’Languages & Frameworksâ†’Solidityâ†’Language Server tab)
  • Advanced syntax highlighting with customizable color schemes (Default & Darcula)
  • Intelligent code completion with context-aware suggestions
  • Smart code formatting with configurable style settings
  • Code folding for contracts, functions, structs, enums, and assembly blocks
  • Brace matching with auto-close for {, (, [ and navigation (Ctrl+[)
  • Quote handling with auto-close for string literals

Navigation & Intelligence

  • Go to Definition (Ctrl+Click) for contracts, functions, variables, and more
  • Find Usages (Alt+F7) across your entire project
  • Structure View with visibility-specific icons and smart sorting
  • Breadcrumbs navigation showing contract hierarchy
  • Go to Class/Symbol for quick navigation
  • Rename refactoring with reference tracking
  • Inheritance gutter icons - Navigate to parent contracts/interfaces
  • Override gutter icons - Navigate to overridden functions
  • Import optimization (Ctrl+Alt+O) - Remove unused imports

Smart Contract Templates & Snippets

  • 30+ live templates for rapid development (type s: to see all)
  • Token standards: ERC20 (s:erc20), ERC721 (s:erc721), ERC1155 (s:erc1155)
  • OpenZeppelin patterns:
    • Ownable (s:ownable)
    • Pausable (s:pausable)
    • ReentrancyGuard (s:reentrancy)
    • AccessControl (s:accesscontrol)
    • UUPS Upgradeable (s:upgradeable)
    • SafeERC20 (s:safeerc20)
  • Common patterns: contract, interface, library, function, event, error, struct, enum, modifier
  • Advanced patterns: assembly, try-catch, fallback, receive, using directives

Security & Best Practices

  • Real-time security analysis with 18+ vulnerability checks:
    • Enhanced reentrancy detection with CEI pattern analysis
    • Access control inspection for unprotected sensitive functions
    • ERC compliance checking (ERC20/721/1155 standard validation)
    • tx.origin usage warnings
    • Unchecked external calls
    • Block randomness issues
    • Integer overflow/underflow
    • Delegatecall warnings
    • Contract size limit warnings (24KB EIP-170 limit)
    • Solidity version recommendations (upgrade suggestions for old versions)
    • NatSpec documentation validation
    • Storage layout analysis for gas optimization and upgrade safety
    • Custom error migration suggestions (require -> custom errors)
    • And more...

Gas Optimization

  • Automatic gas optimization suggestions with 10+ patterns:
    • Constant/immutable variable hints
    • External vs public function optimization
    • Array length caching in loops
    • Pre-increment optimization
    • Custom errors instead of strings
    • Storage vs memory suggestions
    • Inline gas cost tooltips for storage, calls, and events
    • Storage variable packing recommendations
    • Function-level gas profiling with optimization suggestions

Documentation & Learning

  • Hover documentation for all Solidity elements
  • Built-in documentation panel with 6 comprehensive tabs:
    • Language Reference
    • Tutorials
    • Best Practices
    • Security Guidelines
    • Code Examples
    • Quick Reference Cheat Sheet
  • Interactive tutorials with context-sensitive balloon tips
  • Parameter hints for function calls

Framework Integration

  • Automatic framework detection for Hardhat and Foundry projects
  • Status bar widget showing detected framework(s)
  • Framework-aware directory detection (contracts/ vs src/)
  • Support for hybrid projects (Hardhat + Foundry)
  • Foundry test run icons - Click to run test*, testFail*, testFuzz_*, invariant_* functions
  • Foundry stack trace filter - Clickable file paths in forge output
  • Hardhat console.log support - Syntax highlighting with production warnings

Language Server Protocol (LSP)

  • Two server backends - Nomic Foundation Solidity Language Server or solc --lsp
  • LSP diagnostics - Real-time errors/warnings from the language server alongside built-in inspections
  • LSP completions - Server-provided completions merged with PSI completions
  • LSP hover - Additional documentation from the language server
  • LSP go-to-definition - Falls back to LSP when local resolution can't resolve a symbol
  • Auto-detection - Finds installed language servers from PATH, npm globals, and node_modules
  • Auto-start - Starts when the project contains .sol files; defers until the first .sol file is created otherwise
  • Crash recovery - Automatic restart with exponential backoff
  • Configure at Settings â†’ Languages & Frameworks â†’ Solidity â†’ Language Server tab

AI Chat

  • AI tool window - Chat with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Aider, Windsurf, Antigravity
  • External API support - Ollama, OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini endpoints
  • MCP server - Exposes 20 Solidity IDE tools to external AI agents over local HTTP
  • One-click MCP install into detected agent CLIs
  • Disable AI entirely in Settings â†’ Solidity â†’ AI tab

Solidity SDK & Compilation

  • Solidity SDK - Configure solc in Project Structure (like Go/Python SDKs)
  • Direct compilation - Compile without Hardhat/Foundry (Ctrl+Shift+F9)
  • Artifact generation - ABI, bytecode, metadata output
  • Etherscan import - Download verified contracts (11 networks supported)

Advanced Analysis

  • Data flow analysis for taint tracking and vulnerability detection
  • Symbolic execution hints for value range estimation
  • Loop bound analysis for potential gas issues

Getting Started

Live Templates

Type s: in any Solidity file to see all available templates:

Token Standards:

  • s:erc20 - Full ERC20 token implementation
  • s:erc721 - Full ERC721 NFT implementation
  • s:erc1155 - Full ERC1155 multi-token implementation
  • s:interface-erc20 - ERC20 interface definition

OpenZeppelin Security Patterns:

  • s:ownable - Ownership access control
  • s:pausable - Emergency stop mechanism
  • s:reentrancy - Reentrancy guard protection
  • s:accesscontrol - Role-based access control
  • s:upgradeable - UUPS upgradeable contract
  • s:safeerc20 - Safe ERC20 token operations

Basic Elements:

  • s:contract - New contract with license and pragma
  • s:interface - Interface definition
  • s:library - Library definition
  • s:function - Function with NatSpec documentation
  • s:modifier - Custom modifier with require check
  • s:event - Event definition
  • s:error - Custom error definition
  • s:struct - Struct definition
  • s:enum - Enum definition

And many more... (30+ total templates)

Customization & Sharing

  • Code style settings are stored per-project in .idea/codeStyles/
  • Share with team: Commit the .idea/codeStyles/ directory to version control
  • Color schemes: File â†’ Settings â†’ Editor â†’ Color Scheme â†’ Solidity
  • Inspections: File â†’ Settings â†’ Editor â†’ Inspections â†’ Solidity

Troubleshooting

  • Autocomplete not working? Check file type association at Settings â†’ Editor â†’ File Types â†’ Solidity
    • The .sol file should show the Solidity icon in the project tree
    • If missing, add *.sol to the Solidity file type
  • Framework not detected? Ensure hardhat.config.js/ts or foundry.toml exists in project root
  • Status bar widget not visible? Right-click status bar and enable "Solidity Framework"
  • LSP not starting? Install the Nomic Foundation server (npm install -g @nomicfoundation/solidity-language-server) and enable it in Settings â†’ Languages & Frameworks â†’ Solidity â†’ Language Server tab

Made by developers with a passion for Blockchain Development

The integration is the work of Ilscipio:

We develop blockchain solutions as part of our technology stack and understand the challenges of writing secure, efficient smart contracts. We created this plugin to make Solidity development more intuitive and productive for our team.

We're sharing this tool with the entire Solidity community to support the ecosystem's growth and to make smart contract development more accessible.

  • Special discounts are available for individual developers & of course for the whole Open Source community.
  • Active Solidity and Ethereum contributors can contact us for a 100% discount.

Bugs & Feature Requests

If you have any questions, feature requests or stumble upon the occasional bug, come leave us a message at Ilscipio

idea-plugin.name: GitHub Copilot modernization
idea-plugin.description:
What is GitHub Copilot modernization?

GitHub Copilot modernization is an AI assistant that helps you modernize your app faster, with a streamlined end-to-end migration process from assessment to deployment. It goes beyond version upgrades and makes your apps cloud-ready by reducing technical debt, strengthening security posture and unlocking the power of cloud.

  • Follow the quickstart and get started
  • Find answers to frequently asked questions
  • Share your thoughts

Note: GitHub Copilot modernization can be used with just a GitHub account—an Azure account is only required when you actually deploy or test Azure-specific modernization patterns.

Key capabilities

Application Assessment and Planning – Analyze code, configuration, and dependencies.

Copilot analyzes your project's current state and generates modernization plans. The tool identifies dependencies, outdated libraries, and potential migration issues. It provides actionable strategies to remediate problems.

Code Transformations – Suggest and apply code remediation for upgrade and migration scenarios.

Copilot upgrades Java versions and framework.

To accelerate code changes for common modernization issues, you may apply predefined tasks that encode expert knowledge for common Azure migration scenarios including secret management, message queue integration, identity services and more.

Modernize and secure – ensure successful build, validate unit tests and address CVEs

Modernization includes comprehensive build validation. Copilot automatically resolves build issues that arise during transformation. It performs test validations to ensure error-free changes. Production pipeline integrity is maintained throughout the modernization process. Security vulnerability management is integrated into the modernization process. The system scans for CVEs after upgrades. It automatically applies security fixes in Agent Mode. You can review all security-related changes. This improves your security posture while maintaining compliance requirements.

Containerization and Deployment – Generate assets for app containerization and deployment

Copilot creates Infrastructure as Code files for Azure deployment. It addresses deployment errors automatically. CI/CD pipelines are set up for continuous integration. This completes the modernization workflow from analysis to production.

License

This extension is licensed under GitHub Copilot Product Specifc Terms.

Trademarks

This project may contain trademarks or logos for projects, products, or services. Authorized use of Microsoft trademarks or logos is subject to and must follow Microsoft's Trademark & Brand Guidelines. Use of Microsoft trademarks or logos in modified versions of this project must not cause confusion or imply Microsoft sponsorship. Any use of third-party trademarks or logos are subject to those third-party's policies.

Privacy statement

App modernization for Java uses GitHub Copilot just like how you modify code with GitHub Copilot, which does not retain code snippets beyond the immediate session. We do not collect, transmit or store your custom tasks either. Please review the Microsoft Privacy Statement if necessary.

Transparency note

App modernization for Java uses GitHub Copilot to make code changes, and AI sometimes makes mistakes. Please carefully review and test the code changes made by the tool, before using them on your production environment.

Disclaimer

Unless otherwise permitted under applicable license(s), users may not decompile, modify, repackage, or redistribute any assets, prompts, or internal tools provided as part of this product without prior written consent from Microsoft.

More information

Here is some documentation that may be helpful.

  • Common modernization issues with predefined tasks
  • Java upgrade overview
  • Quickstart on using managed identity instead of passwords
  • Quickstart on creating and applying your own task
  • Frequently Asked Questions

idea-plugin.name: IntelliAI Javadoc
idea-plugin.description:
IntelliAI Javadoc is an IntelliJ IDEA plugin that uses AI to automatically generate compliant Javadoc comments for your Java code.

GitHub | Issues | Homepage | Docs

Powered by IntelliAI Engine: Seamlessly integrates with IntelliAI Engine to provide unified, pluggable, and high-performance AI capabilities ⚡

Why This Plugin?

When refactoring legacy projects to meet Javadoc standards, you face common challenges:

  • Translation tools (like EasyDoc): Only translate existing comments, producing meaningless documentation
  • Format-only generators: Create proper Javadoc structure but with empty or meaningless content
  • Generic AI tools: Too heavy and slow for batch processing, often fail to complete large projects

This plugin solves these problems by combining AI-powered meaningful content generation with optimized batch processing, specifically designed for enterprise-scale Javadoc compliance tasks.

Core Features

  • 🧠 Meaningful AI-Generated Comments: Uses AI to understand code and generate meaningful Javadoc, not just format templates
  • ⚡ Fast Batch Processing: Optimized for processing entire projects quickly, supporting parallel processing and performance mode
  • ✅ Compliance-Focused: Generates Javadoc that meets Checkstyle and company standards
  • 🤖 Multiple AI Providers: Support for QianWen, Ollama and other AI services
  • ⌨️ Flexible Triggering: Available via shortcuts, right-click menus, Generate menu and more
  • 🎯 Smart Recognition: Automatically identify classes, methods, test methods and other elements
  • 🚀 Asynchronous Processing: Background processing without blocking the IDE
  • 📊 Progress Display: Real-time progress and result statistics

Usage

  • Shortcut: Ctrl+Shift+D (Windows/Linux) or Cmd+Shift+D (Mac)
  • Editor right-click menu → Generate Javadoc with AI
  • File/Directory right-click menu → Generate Javadoc with AI
  • Generate menu: Cmd+N / Alt+Insert → Javadoc with AI
  • Quick fix: Option+Enter / Alt+Enter → Generate Javadoc with AI

Configuration

Configuration path: Settings → Tools → IntelliAI Javadoc

  • Select AI provider (QianWen/Ollama)
  • Configure model and API Key (encrypted storage using system-level keychain)
  • Customize generation options

Security Features

  • 🔒 Encrypted API Key Storage: Uses IntelliJ Platform's PasswordSafe mechanism, API Keys are never saved to configuration files
  • 🛡️ System-Level Encryption:
    • macOS: Keychain Access
    • Linux: GNOME Keyring or KWallet
    • Windows: Credential Manager

⚡ 由 IntelliAI Engine 驱动：深度集成 IntelliAI Engine，提供统一、可扩展、高性能的 AI 能力支持

IntelliAI Javadoc

专为批量生成符合规范的 Javadoc 注释而设计，满足公司标准和 Checkstyle 检测要求。 与通用 AI 工具或简单翻译工具不同，本插件专门针对快速、准确地为整个项目生成 Javadoc 进行了优化。

为什么选择这个插件？

当需要为不符合规范的项目添加标准的 Javadoc 时，通常会遇到以下问题：

  • 翻译工具（如 EasyDoc）：只是翻译现有注释，生成的内容没有实际意义
  • 仅格式生成器：只生成规范的 Javadoc 格式，注释内容没有任何意义
  • 通用 AI 工具：功能太重，批量处理整个项目时速度非常慢，且不一定能一次完成

本插件通过结合 AI 生成有意义的注释内容与优化的批量处理能力，专门针对企业级 Javadoc 合规任务而设计，完美解决了这些问题。

核心功能

  • 🧠 有意义的 AI 生成注释：使用 AI 理解代码并生成有意义的 Javadoc，而非仅生成格式模板
  • ⚡ 快速批量处理：针对整个项目快速处理进行了优化，支持并行处理和性能模式
  • ✅ 合规导向：生成符合 Checkstyle 和公司标准的 Javadoc
  • 🤖 多种 AI 提供商支持：支持通义千问、Ollama、OpenAI 等多种 AI 服务
  • ⌨️ 灵活的触发方式：可通过快捷键、右键菜单、Generate 菜单等多种方式触发
  • 🎯 智能识别：自动识别类、方法、测试方法等不同元素
  • 🚀 异步处理：后台处理，不阻塞 IDE
  • 📊 进度显示：实时显示处理进度和结果统计

使用方式

  • 快捷键：Ctrl+Shift+D (Windows/Linux) 或 Cmd+Shift+D (Mac)
  • 编辑器右键菜单 → Generate Javadoc with AI
  • 文件/目录右键菜单 → Generate Javadoc with AI
  • Generate 菜单：Cmd+N / Alt+Insert → Javadoc with AI
  • 快速修复：Option+Enter / Alt+Enter → Generate Javadoc with AI

配置说明

配置路径：Settings → Tools → IntelliAI Javadoc

  • 选择 AI 提供商（通义千问/Ollama）
  • 配置模型和 API Key（使用系统级加密存储，安全可靠）
  • 自定义生成选项

安全特性

  • 🔒 API Key 加密存储：使用 IntelliJ Platform 的 PasswordSafe 机制，API Key 不会保存到配置文件中
  • 🛡️ 系统级加密：
    • macOS：使用 Keychain Access（钥匙串）
    • Linux：使用 GNOME Keyring 或 KWallet
    • Windows：使用 Credential Manager

idea-plugin.name: Text Highlighter
idea-plugin.description:
Text Highlighter

Simple and powerful text highlighting plugin for JetBrains IDEs. Mark important code sections with color-coded highlights that persist across sessions.

Free Features

  • 5 Built-in Colors: Yellow, Green, Blue, Pink, and Orange highlights
  • Highlight All Occurrences: Highlight all instances of selected text (case-sensitive or case-insensitive)
  • Keyboard Shortcuts: Quick access with Ctrl+Shift+H + color key (Y/G/B/P/O/C)
  • Scrollbar Markers: Visual indicators in the scrollbar show where highlights are located (like linter warnings)
  • Highlights Tool Window: View all highlights grouped by color with line numbers and text previews
  • Tool Window Context Menu: Right-click to navigate, clear individual highlights, or clear all of a color
  • Configurable Navigation: Choose between single-click or double-click navigation in tool window
  • Persistent Highlights: Automatically saved and restored across IDE sessions
  • Smart Cleanup: Highlights auto-remove when text is deleted or modified
  • Easy Management: Clear individual highlights, all highlights in a file, or across the entire project

Premium Features 💎

Unlock advanced capabilities with a paid license:

  • Custom Colors: Define unlimited custom highlight colors with personalized names
  • Highlight Comments/Labels: Add descriptive comments and labels to your highlights for better context
  • Pre-configured Categories: Includes 4 default custom colors: Bug (red), Tech Debt (orange), Review (purple), and TODO (turquoise)

Usage

Highlight selected text:

  1. Select any text in the editor
  2. Right-click to open the context menu
  3. Navigate to Highlight Text and choose a color

Or use keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl+Shift+H then Y (Yellow), G (Green), B (Blue), P (Pink), O (Orange), or C (Clear)

Highlight all occurrences:

  1. Select any text in the editor
  2. Right-click to open the context menu
  3. Navigate to Highlight All Occurrences (case-sensitive) or Highlight All Occurrences (Ignore Case) (case-insensitive)
  4. Choose a color - all matching instances will be highlighted

Use custom colors:

Four default custom colors are ready to use: Bug (red), Tech Debt (orange), Review (purple), and TODO (turquoise). Find them in the context menu under "Custom Colors".

To add your own:

  1. Go to Settings/Preferences → Text Highlighter
  2. Click the + button to add a new color
  3. Enter a name and choose your color (with transparency)
  4. Custom colors appear in both highlighting menus

Clear Highlights

  • Clear Highlight: Remove highlight from selected text
  • Clear All in File: Remove all highlights from the current file
  • Clear All in Project: Remove all highlights from all files (with confirmation)

Perfect for code review, studying codebases, marking TODOs, or highlighting important sections during debugging.

idea-plugin.name: Lenter
idea-plugin.description:
Lenter - AI-Powered Code Documentation & Bug Reporting

Automate routine developer tasks: generate KDoc comments and create formatted Jira bug reports directly from your IDE.

✨ Features

📝 KDoc Comment Generation

  • Smart Documentation: Automatically generates KDoc comments in Russian for Kotlin classes, functions, and properties
  • Batch Processing: Comment entire classes with a single shortcut
  • Consistent Style: Follows your project's documentation standards
  • AI-Powered: Uses local Ollama models - your code never leaves your machine
  • Supports: @property, @param, @return tags with intelligent detection

🐛 Bug Report Generator

  • Natural Language Input: Describe bugs in free text
  • Auto-Formatting: Converts to Jira-compatible tables with proper markup
  • Editable Templates: Review and modify before submission
  • Live Preview: See formatted output in real-time
  • Direct Integration: Create Jira issues with one click
  • Structured Output: Includes environment, steps to reproduce, expected vs actual results

🎨 Compose Color Preview

  • Inline Preview: Shows Compose color values directly in the editor gutter
  • Live Editing: Tweak ARGB shades with an interactive color picker
  • Customizable Display: Configure icon size, placement, and contrast indicators

🖼️ Drawable Preview

  • Visual File Icons: See drawable previews directly in the project tree
  • Inline Code Preview: Preview images next to painterResource() calls
  • Multi-Format Support: PNG, JPG, WebP, and Android Vector Drawable (XML)
  • Smart Caching: Fast loading with automatic cache invalidation
  • Cross-Platform: Works with Android (R.drawable.*) and Compose Multiplatform (Res.drawable.*)

📝 String Resource Preview

  • Inline String Preview: Shows string resource content directly in code
  • Multi-Language Support: 10+ languages with automatic fallback
  • Configurable Language: Choose preferred language in Settings
  • Beautiful UI: Rounded corners with theme-adaptive colors
  • Smart Caching: Fast performance with intelligent caching
  • Cross-Platform: Works with Android (R.string.*) and Compose Multiplatform (Res.string.*)

🧭 Compose Resource Navigation (KMP/CMP)

  • Go To Declaration: Jump from Compose resource usages to their declarations with one shortcut
  • Context-Aware: Works with colors, typography and other custom providers
  • Productivity Boost: Keeps you in the flow when exploring UI code

⌨️ Shortcuts

  • Ctrl+Alt+K (⌘+⌥+K on Mac) - Generate comments for entire class
  • Ctrl+Alt+Shift+B (⌘+⌥+⇧+B on Mac) - Open bug report generator
  • Ctrl+Alt+Shift+C (⌘+⌥+⇧+C on Mac) - Add comment to Jira issue

🚀 Quick Start

  1. Install Ollama and download a model: 
    ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b
  2. Configure plugin: Settings → Tools → Lenter
    • Ollama API URL: http://localhost:11434
    • Model: qwen2.5-coder:7b
  3. (Optional) For Jira integration:
    • Set Jira URL and Project settings
    • Create Personal Access Token in Jira
    • Configure token in plugin settings

🔒 Privacy First

  • Uses local Ollama instance - no cloud APIs
  • Your code never leaves your machine
  • No telemetry or data collection

🎯 Recommended Models

  • qwen2.5-coder:7b - Best balance of quality and speed
  • qwen2.5-coder:3b - Faster, lighter option
  • llama3.1:8b - Alternative choice

💡 Use Cases

  • Document legacy code quickly
  • Maintain consistent documentation style across team
  • Speed up code reviews with proper documentation
  • Create detailed bug reports without manual formatting
  • Streamline QA workflow with Jira integration
  • Quickly identify drawable resources in large projects
  • Preview UI assets without opening separate viewers

🛠️ Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2024.1+ or any JetBrains IDE
  • Java 21+
  • Ollama installed locally
  • (Optional) Jira instance with Personal Access Tokens support

📚 Learn More

Documentation | Report Issues | Ollama Setup Guide

idea-plugin.name: Android Localization
idea-plugin.description:
Website | GitHub | Issues | Reviews

Android Localization Plugin – AI-Powered String Translator Powerful Android localization plugin for Android Studio by OpenAI, Gemini, Claude. Automatically translate strings.xml into 100+ languages using multiple AI and cloud translation providers. Perfect for developers who want to localize Android apps faster, reduce manual translation work, and support global users.

Features

  • Multiple translator support:
    • OpenAI translator.
    • Google Gemini translator.
    • Claude translator.
    • Grok translator.
    • Baidu translator.
    • Youdao translator.
    • Ali translator.
    • DeepL translator.
  • Supports up to 100+ languages.
  • One key generates all translation files.
  • Support no translation of existing string.
  • Support for specifying that text is not translated.
  • Support for caching translated strings.
  • Support to set the translation interval time.

Usage

  • Step 1: Select the values/strings.xml(or any string resource in values directory).
  • Step 2: Right click and select "Translate to Other Languages".
  • Step 3: Select the languages to be translated.
  • Step 4: Click OK.

Android 本地化插件 – AI 驱动的字符串翻译工具

功能强大的 Android 与 Kotlin Multiplatform（KMP）本地化插件，适用于 IntelliJ IDEA 和 Android Studio。

通过多种 AI 和云端翻译服务提供商，自动将 strings.xml 以及其他 Android 字符串资源翻译为 100 多种语言。

非常适合希望更快速完成 Android 应用本地化、减少手动翻译工作并支持全球用户的开发者。

功能特点

  • 支持多种翻译器：

    • OpenAI 翻译器

    • Google Gemini 翻译器

    • Claude 翻译器

    • Grok translator.

    • 百度翻译器

    • 有道翻译器

    • 阿里翻译器

    • DeepL 翻译器

  • 支持 100+ 种语言

  • 一键生成所有翻译文件

  • 支持不翻译已存在的字符串

  • 支持指定文本不参与翻译

  • 支持缓存已翻译字符串

  • 支持设置翻译间隔时间

使用方法

  • 第一步：选择 values/strings.xml（或 values 目录下任意字符串资源文件）

  • 第二步：右键点击并选择 “Translate to Other Languages”

  • 第三步：选择需要翻译的目标语言

  • 第四步：点击 OK

Android ローカライズプラグイン – AI 搭載文字列翻訳ツール

IntelliJ IDEA および Android Studio に対応した、強力な Android & Kotlin Multiplatform（KMP）ローカライズプラグインです。

複数の AI およびクラウド翻訳プロバイダーを使用して、strings.xml やその他の Android 文字列リソースを 100 以上の言語へ自動翻訳します。

Android アプリのローカライズをより迅速に行い、手動翻訳の作業を削減し、世界中のユーザーに対応したい開発者に最適です。

機能

  • 複数の翻訳エンジンをサポート：

    • OpenAI 翻訳

    • Google Gemini 翻訳

    • Claude 翻訳

    • Grok translator.

    • Baidu 翻訳

    • Youdao 翻訳

    • Ali 翻訳

    • DeepL 翻訳

  • 100 以上の言語をサポート

  • ワンクリックで全ての翻訳ファイルを生成

  • 既存の文字列を翻訳しない設定をサポート

  • 翻訳対象外のテキストを指定可能

  • 翻訳済み文字列のキャッシュをサポート

  • 翻訳間隔時間の設定をサポート

使用方法

  • 手順 1：values/strings.xml（または values ディレクトリ内の任意の文字列リソース）を選択

  • 手順 2：右クリックして「他の言語に翻訳」を選択

  • 手順 3：翻訳する言語を選択

  • 手順 4：OK をクリック

Android 로컬라이제이션 플러그인 – AI 기반 문자열 번역 도구

IntelliJ IDEA 및 Android Studio를 지원하는 강력한 Android & Kotlin Multiplatform(KMP) 로컬라이제이션 플러그인입니다.

여러 AI 및 클라우드 번역 제공업체를 활용하여 strings.xml 및 기타 Android 문자열 리소스를 100개 이상의 언어로 자동 번역합니다.

Android 앱을 더 빠르게 로컬라이즈하고, 수동 번역 작업을 줄이며, 전 세계 사용자를 지원하고자 하는 개발자에게 최적의 솔루션입니다.

Plugin de localisation Android – Traducteur de chaînes alimenté par l’IA

Puissant plugin de localisation Android & Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) pour IntelliJ IDEA et Android Studio.

Traduisez automatiquement strings.xml ainsi que les autres ressources de chaînes Android en plus de 100 langues grâce à plusieurs fournisseurs de traduction basés sur l’IA et le cloud.

Idéal pour les développeurs qui souhaitent localiser leurs applications Android plus rapidement, réduire le travail de traduction manuelle et prendre en charge des utilisateurs du monde entier.

idea-plugin.name: Adapts Assistant
idea-plugin.description:
Adapts brings an AI-powered chat assistant directly into your IDE. It helps you query wiki documentation, generate code snippets, and interact with project knowledge in natural language, all without leaving the editor.

Key Features
  • Search and query wiki content directly in the editor
  • Generate and preview Markdown or code snippets instantly
  • AI assistant with full context of your project wiki
  • Conversational interface for faster documentation discovery
  • Always up to date with the latest codebase changes
  • Supports multi-repo context for complex projects
  • Scales to large codebases with support for up to 3,000 files

Why Use It?
As AI assistants become more prevalent, traditional ways of consuming documentation are evolving. This plugin makes your documentation interactive, allowing you to chat with your codebase and wiki for a more natural developer experience.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Initial version

idea-plugin.name: Blackbox
idea-plugin.description:
Blackbox AI Agent

BLACKBOX AI is an AI coding assistant that helps developers by providing real-time code completion, documentation, and debugging suggestions. BLACKBOX AI is also integrated with a variety of developer tools such as Github Gitlab among others, making it easy to use within your existing workflow.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Version 1.0.6

idea-plugin.name: jira-automation
idea-plugin.description:
Jira Automation is an IntelliJ IDEA plugin that automatically creates Jira tickets from your code changes using AI.

Features

  • AI-Powered Ticket Generation: Analyzes your code changes and generates comprehensive Jira tickets automatically
  • Multi-Language Support: Create tickets in 8 languages (Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese, Spanish, French, German)
  • Smart Diff Analysis: Automatically detects uncommitted changes and analyzes the impact
  • Seamless Jira Integration: Direct integration with Jira Cloud via REST API
  • Multiple AI Providers: Supports OpenAI and Anthropic (Claude) for ticket generation
  • Customizable: Configure default project, issue type, and language preferences

How It Works

  1. Make code changes in your project
  2. Open the "Jira Creator" tool window or use VCS menu
  3. Click "Create Ticket from Changes"
  4. AI analyzes your changes and generates a title and description
  5. Review and customize the generated content
  6. Click "Create" to publish to Jira

idea-plugin.name: Switch2Trae
idea-plugin.description:
Switch2Trae enables effortless switching between JetBrains IDEs and Trae IDE while maintaining your workflow context.

🚀 Seamless IDE Integration with Trae

✨ Key Features:

  • 🎯 Smart Context Switching - Open current project or file in Trae IDE with a single keystroke
  • 📍 Cursor Position Sync - Automatically positions cursor at the exact line and column
  • ⌨️ Keyboard Shortcuts - Quick access via Alt+Shift+P (project) and Alt+Shift+O (file)
  • 🔧 Flexible Configuration - Support for multiple Trae command-line formats
  • 🎨 Context Menu Integration - Right-click to switch directly from editor or project tree
  • 🛠️ Error Handling - Intelligent error detection with helpful troubleshooting guidance

🎮 Usage:

  • Use Alt+Shift+P to open current project in Trae
  • Use Alt+Shift+O to open current file in Trae
  • Right-click in editor or project tree for context menu options
  • Configure Trae executable path in Settings → Tools → Switch2Trae

🔧 Supported Command Formats:

  • file:line:column (VS Code style)
  • --goto line:column file (Vim style)
  • -g file:line:column (Emacs style)
  • file +line:column (Nano style)

Perfect for developers who want to leverage the best of both JetBrains and Trae ecosystems!

idea-plugin.name: Qoder - Agentic AI Coding Platform
idea-plugin.description:
Qoder is an agentic coding platform designed for real software development. It seamlessly integrates enhanced context engineering with intelligent agents to gain a comprehensive understanding of your codebase and systematically tackles software development tasks.
It goes beyond simple code completion. Qoder helps you think deeper, code smarter, and build better by automating intricate workflows, maintaining project context, and enabling seamless AI-assisted development.
Download the Zip Qoder_JetBrains_latest，and click here to learn more.

It goes beyond simple code completion. Qoder helps you think deeper.

Sign up for Qoder

Every developer is invited to sign up for a free Qoder account—free trial available upon registration. Should you need more, you can easily purchase a plan at any time. You can read more about our offerings for individuals and businesses at https://qoder.com/pricing.

Code suggestions in the editor

Qoder is trained on a vast repository of high-quality open-source code, enabling it to generate code from single line to entire functions while also anticipating your next edit by analyzing the entire codebase, not just the current file. This instant, predictive power keeps you in a state of flow, freeing you to focus on high-level architecture and complex problem-solving.

Ask Mode

With access to a vast repository of technical documentation, product manuals, and general development knowledge, combined with engineering-level perception capabilities, the Ask mode assists developers in resolving coding issues encountered during development. It helps with code problem fixes, debugging, and troubleshooting runtime errors, ensuring a smoother development process.

Agent Mode

Agent mode is equipped with capabilities for planning, perception, and tool use. Based on your coding objectives, it independently breaks down tasks and utilizes a suite of tools—including codebase search, file editing, and a terminal—to help you complete development work end-to-end.

MCP & Rules

Qoder integrates with external systems via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for expanded context, while project-specific rules ensure it adapts precisely to your local coding preferences and standards.

Keywords

Qoder、Agent、AI Coding Assistant

Resources

Website: https://qoder.com
Documentation: https://docs.qoder.com
Forum: https://forum.qoder.com

0.5.0

  • We are excited to announce the first official release of the Qoder Plugin for JetBrains IDEs! Qoder is an agentic coding platform built for modern software development. This plugin brings the power of our AI agents directly into your editor. This initial release focuses on pillars as follows:

AI Chat

  • The central hub for interacting with Qoder, featuring two distinct modes:
    • Ask mode: Your go-to for expert assistance. Get contextual answers, debug code, and troubleshoot errors with an AI that understands your project.
    • Agent mode: Delegate complex tasks. The AI agent can autonomously use tools, make decisions, and execute multi-step plans to complete your objectives from start to finish.

Inline code suggestion

  • AI-powered features that work seamlessly within your code editor:
    • Code completion: Our completion engine goes beyond single-file analysis. It understands your entire project's context, dependencies, and architectural patterns to provide suggestions that are not just correct, but consistent.
    • NES: Qoder anticipates your next move, offering intelligent, multi-line edits directly at your cursor to accelerate refactoring and coding.

Autonomous task completion

  • This is what makes Qoder truly powerful. The agent can understand and act on high-level goals using a suite of advanced capabilities:
    • Full codebase awareness: The agent intelligently analyzes your entire project to grasp the full context of a task before it begins work.
    • Multi-file edits: Based on your instructions, the agent can execute complex, multi-file edits across the entire codebase.
    • Persistent memory: Qoder learns from your conversations and project history, providing increasingly personalized and effective assistance over time.
    • Autonomous tool use: The agent can independently select, generate, and execute necessary terminal commands, web searches, and other integrated tools to complete its objective.
    • Transparent Task Planning: For any complex goal, the agent first generates a structured, step-by-step plan, giving you full visibility and control over its work.

Customization & extensibility

  • Tailor Qoder to your specific environment and standards:
    • Project rules: Define project-specific rules to ensure the AI's output consistently aligns with your team's coding standards and architectural patterns.
    • MCP: Securely connect Qoder to your own internal APIs, databases, and other data sources, extending its capabilities far beyond the IDE.

To begin, install the plugin and open the AI Chat panel from the side navigation bar to sign in. We can't wait to see what you build with Qoder!

idea-plugin.name: Vajra - AI Coding Assistant
idea-plugin.description:
Vajra — AI Coding Assistant for IntelliJ IDEA

Vajra is a free, open-source AI coding assistant for IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, and all JetBrains IDEs. It brings Claude, GPT, Grok, Gemini, DeepSeek, Kimi, and 40+ models directly into your editor — a powerful alternative to GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Tabnine, Codeium, Amazon Q, and JetBrains AI Assistant.

Why Vajra?

  • Your API key, your choice — no subscriptions, no vendor lock-in
  • 10 providers in one plugin: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Mistral, Groq, Grok (xAI), Kimi (Moonshot), Qwen, Ollama
  • Tab autocomplete: as-you-type ghost-text suggestions, Tab to accept
  • Vajra Composer: multi-file agent mode — describe a task, review a batched diff, apply
  • Inline Edit (Ctrl+K): free-form instruction at your cursor, no chat panel needed
  • Terminal awareness: run build/test commands and let Vajra analyze failures
  • Checkpoints: revert an entire agent edit in one click
  • Rules files: .vajrarules for persistent project conventions, like .cursorrules
  • Multi-turn conversation history that persists across IDE restarts
  • 100% local option: run Ollama models offline — no data leaves your machine
  • Smart context injection: type @ to inject @currentfile, @selection, @codebase, @gitdiff, @file:name, @web:query, @docs:query, @terminal:cmd
  • MCP support: connect Model Context Protocol servers and let Vajra call their tools
  • Smart code actions: Explain, Refactor, Debug, Optimize, Generate Tests, Add Comments, Fix Problems
  • Always up to date: supports the latest models as soon as they release

Supported AI Models (v1.0.0):

  • OpenAI: gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.5, gpt-5.5-pro, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini, o3-pro, o4-mini, o3, gpt-4o
  • Anthropic Claude: claude-fable-5, claude-opus-4-8, claude-sonnet-5, claude-haiku-4-5-20251001
  • Google Gemini: gemini-3.5-flash, gemini-3.1-pro-preview, gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-2.5-flash
  • Grok (xAI): grok-4.5, grok-4.3, grok-4.20, grok-4.20-reasoning, grok-4.1, grok-4.1-fast, grok-3-mini
  • Kimi (Moonshot AI): kimi-k2.7-code, kimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.5, moonshot-v1-32k, moonshot-v1-8k
  • DeepSeek: deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek-chat, deepseek-reasoner
  • Mistral AI: mistral-large-latest, mistral-medium-latest, mistral-small-latest, codestral-latest, codestral-2508
  • Groq (fast inference): llama-3.3-70b-versatile, llama-3.1-8b-instant, llama-4-scout, gpt-oss-120b, gpt-oss-20b, qwen3-32b
  • Qwen / Alibaba: qwen3.7-max, qwen3.7-plus, qwen3.6-plus, qwen3.5, qwen3-235b, qwen2.5-coder-32b
  • Ollama (local / offline): qwen3-coder:30b, devstral:24b, qwen3:8b, deepseek-r1:8b, llama3.3:70b, qwen2.5-coder:7b, and any model you pull

Code Actions (right-click any code):

  • Edit with Vajra (Inline, Ctrl+K) — free-form instruction, inline diff
  • Explain with Vajra — understand any code instantly
  • Refactor with Vajra — clean up and improve code quality
  • Debug with Vajra — find bugs and get fixes
  • Optimize with Vajra — improve performance
  • Generate Tests with Vajra — auto-generate unit tests
  • Add Comments with Vajra — generate documentation
  • Fix Problems with Vajra — fix the IDE's reported errors/warnings

Quick Start:

  1. Install Vajra from the JetBrains Marketplace
  2. Go to Settings > Tools > Vajra
  3. Paste your API key (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or any supported provider)
  4. Open View > Tool Windows > Vajra Chat
  5. Or right-click any code and pick a Vajra action

Works with IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, Rider, CLion, DataGrip, and all JetBrains IDEs.

idea-plugin.name: GPU Dev Accelerator Ultimate
idea-plugin.description:
GPU Dev Accelerator Ultimate — CUDA, Metal, and OpenCL Development

Write, compile, inspect, and analyze CUDA, Metal, and OpenCL code in a unified IDE environment. Every feature is backed by a real tool integration or deterministic analysis — no mock data.

GPU Language Support

  • Syntax highlighting for CUDA C/C++, Metal Shading Language, and OpenCL C (.cu, .cuh, .metal, .cl)
  • Code completion with API signatures for 100+ GPU builtins across all three languages
  • Quick documentation (Ctrl+Q) for kernel qualifiers, builtins, atomics, and warp primitives
  • Line/block commenting (Ctrl+/) and brace matching
  • Live templates: kernel skeletons, grid-stride loops, CUDA_CHECK macro, event timing, shared-memory tiles

Toolchain Integration

  • Compile CUDA files with nvcc in the background — errors clickable in the GPU Dev console
  • Show PTX for the current file to inspect generated code
  • Memory checking via compute-sanitizer (or cuda-memcheck)
  • Kernel profiling via Nsight Compute (ncu) or nvprof
  • GPU inventory from nvidia-smi and system_profiler (Apple GPUs)
  • Live multi-GPU topology from nvidia-smi topo (NVLink/PIX/PHB/SYS links, utilization, memory)
  • Configurable toolchain paths, -arch, and extra nvcc flags in Settings | Tools | GPU Dev Accelerator

Static Analysis

  • Inspections: GPU memory leaks (cudaMalloc without cudaFree), unchecked CUDA API calls with a CUDA_CHECK quick fix, kernel performance heuristics
  • Kernel heuristics: strided access, warp divergence, __syncthreads() in divergent branches, missing bounds checks, missing __restrict__, device-side malloc, and more
  • Theoretical occupancy calculator for Volta through Hopper
  • Cross-platform kernel migration starting points (CUDA ⇄ Metal / OpenCL / HIP)

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2024.3+ or CLion 2024.3+ (any IntelliJ-based IDE)
  • NVIDIA CUDA Toolkit for compile/profile/sanitize features
  • macOS for Apple GPU detection

Support

  • Documentation: GitHub Wiki
  • Community Forum: GitHub Discussions
  • Enterprise Support: support@jakubjirak.com
  • Issues: GitHub Issues
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.5.0 — Production Overhaul

  • Real toolchain integration — nvcc compilation now runs in the background with clickable errors in the new GPU Dev console; no more UI freezes or modal dialogs
  • New: Show PTX — compile the current .cu file to PTX and inspect the generated code in the editor
  • New: Occupancy calculator — theoretical SM occupancy for Volta through Hopper with limiting-factor breakdown
  • New: Migrate Kernel action — CUDA ⇄ Metal/OpenCL/HIP source porting starting points
  • New: editor basics — Ctrl+/ commenting, brace matching, 8 live templates, quick documentation for 100+ GPU builtins
  • Real inspections — memory-leak and unchecked-API-call inspections now report problems in the editor; quick fix wraps calls in CUDA_CHECK
  • Real GPU data — GPU info, memory check (compute-sanitizer), profiling (Nsight Compute), and multi-GPU topology now read from the actual tools; simulated/placeholder outputs removed
  • New settings page — toolchain paths, GPU architecture, extra nvcc flags, timeouts

2026.4.1 — Critical Debug Runner Fix
