idea-plugin.name: GitBot Commit
idea-plugin.description:
GitBot Commit generates AI-powered commit messages directly from your staged changes, integrated into IntelliJ IDEA's native Git Commit workflow.

It reads your git diff --cached, sends it to an AI model via your chosen provider — OpenRouter (cloud) or Ollama (local) — and writes a structured message following the Conventional Commits standard with emojis.

Features
  • Generates commit messages from staged changes (git diff --cached)
  • Multi-provider: OpenRouter (cloud) or Ollama (local, offline)
  • Conventional Commits style: feat, fix, refactor, docs, chore, test, style
  • Output language: English or Brazilian Portuguese
  • Compatible with any model on OpenRouter or any model pulled in Ollama
  • Fully customizable prompt templates, with one-click reset to defaults
  • Preview dialog with Edit and Copy options before applying
  • Runs in background with progress indicator and cancellation support
  • Commit message field is automatically cleared after a successful commit
  • Secure API key storage via the IDE credential store
Requirements
  • IntelliJ IDEA 2025.2 or later, with Git enabled
  • One of:
    • An OpenRouter API key, or
    • Ollama 0.1.27+ running locally with at least one model pulled (e.g. ollama pull llama3.2)
  • At least one staged change (git add) before running the plugin
Setup — OpenRouter (cloud)

1. Go to Settings → GitBot Commit
2. Provider: OpenRouter
3. Paste your OpenRouter API Key and click Load Models
4. Pick a model (default: anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet) — or browse openrouter.ai/models
5. Choose the Commit language: EN or PT_BR
6. Optionally edit the Prompt Template — or click Reset to default
7. Click Apply

Setup — Ollama (local)

1. Install Ollama: ollama.com and start the service (ollama serve)
2. Pull a model: ollama pull llama3.2
3. In Settings → GitBot Commit set Provider to Ollama
4. Confirm the Server URL (default: http://localhost:11434) and click Test Connection
5. Click Load Models and pick one of your local models
6. Click Apply

Usage

1. Stage your changes: git add <file> (or use IntelliJ's Git panel)
2. Open the Commit panel: Ctrl+K / Cmd+K
3. Click ⚡ AI Commit in the commit toolbar
4. A preview dialog opens with the generated message — review, edit if needed, then click Apply
5. Click Commit (or Commit and Push) — the message field will be cleared automatically after success

Tip: To scope the generation to specific files, select them in the file list before clicking ⚡ AI Commit.

Commit Message Format

<emoji><type>[scope]: <description>

<body explaining the changes>

Type priority when multiple change types are detected:
fix > feat > refactor > chore > docs > test > style

Troubleshooting
  • "No Git repository found" — make sure the project has Git initialized
  • "No staged changes found" — run git add before using the plugin
  • "Configure your OpenRouter API key" — go to Settings → GitBot Commit
  • OpenRouter error — check your API key, account credits, and model ID
  • "Cannot reach Ollama" — start Ollama (ollama serve), verify the URL in Settings, or use Test Connection
  • Model 'X' not found (Ollama) — pull it first: ollama pull X
  • Message not applied — as a fallback, the message is copied to your clipboard
License: MIT — Source: github.com/frshaka/GitBotCommitPlugin
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.6 — Multi-provider support

  • New provider: Ollama (local). Run commit generation 100% offline against models pulled with ollama pull. Requires Ollama 0.1.27+ for OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions support.
  • Provider selector in Settings. Switch between OpenRouter (cloud) and Ollama (local). The settings panel was migrated to the modern Kotlin UI DSL, showing only the relevant fields per provider.
  • Test Connection for Ollama. Verifies the server is reachable and reports the number of installed models in one click.
  • User-friendly error handling. Distinct messages for unreachable providers, invalid API key, missing model (with ollama pull hint), and rate limits.
  • Per-provider model memory. Switching providers preserves the previously selected model on each side, so you don't lose your selection.

1.0.5 — Bug fixes

  • Fixed 400 error when generating commits with any OpenRouter model. Request and response message DTOs are now separate, so no extra fields are sent.
  • Fixed infinite 400 loop with Chain-of-Thought reasoning models. A user continuation message is now appended after each reasoning step.

idea-plugin.name: SR-Forge-Assistant
idea-plugin.description:
Intelligent coding assistant for SR-Forge ML framework YAML configuration files in PyCharm and IntelliJ IDEA.

Features

  • _target_ completion — fuzzy-search Python class FQNs with dot-triggered popup
  • Parameter completion — suggestions from the resolved class's __init__ signature
  • Go-to-definition — Ctrl+Click on _target_: values to jump to the Python source
  • Hover documentation — docstrings, signatures, and parameter info on hover
  • Parameter stub generation — one-click insertion of missing parameters via gutter icon or intention
  • Parameter inspections — warnings for missing required params and unknown param names with quick-fixes
  • Interpolation completion — segment-by-segment path completion inside ${...} expressions
  • Interpolation folding — fold expressions to their resolved values, auto-collapse on file open
  • Reference validation — error annotations for unresolvable interpolation paths
  • Scope highlighting — background shading and bold parent key for the active _target_: block
  • Pipeline Probe — run a dataset pipeline on one sample and visualize Entry state at every transform step
  • Tensor Visualizer — interactive visualization with per-dimension roles, colormaps, channel modes, and histogram
  • Debugger integration — right-click a tensor variable to visualize it instantly
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added #### Pipeline Probe — dataset picker
  • Click the probe button to enter an in-editor selection mode where every dataset's `_target:` value is highlighted as a clickable pill. Hover previews the path; click runs the probe from that dataset.
  • Pick mode shows a header strip with the dataset count and `◀ Prev / Next ▶` jump links. Right-scrollbar gold ticks mark every dataset position. If you're scrolled away from any dataset when entering pick mode, the editor automatically jumps to the first one.
    • #### Pipeline Probe — composite datasets
  • `ConcatDataset` and other YAML-list-style composites are now first-class: the probe runs one branch at a time, matching what `__getitem__` actually does.
  • Each composite block in the visualization carries an inline branch picker — switch branches and re-run with one click. Scrolling the wheel over a composite cycles its active branch.
  • An animated YAML overlay traces the active path through your config, with alternative branches dimmed. Long paths animate at the same per-segment speed as short ones, so the animation feels consistent.
    • #### Pipeline Probe — running experience
  • A live "Running" strip at the bottom of the tool window shows which step is currently being computed.
  • A Stop button cancels a running probe within ~100 ms. When idle, it clears all probe state (overlays, snapshots, temporary tensor files) to free memory before training.
  • Every block has a **Go to YAML definition** button — click it to jump to the corresponding `_target:` mapping and watch it pulse highlighted for a second.
    • #### Tensor Visualizer
  • Slider drag now updates the image **live** instead of only on release.
  • Per-dimension and channel inputs are now spinners with ±1 step buttons, mouse-wheel and keyboard arrow stepping, and typed input — essential for scrubbing through large dimensions one index at a time.
    • #### Editor support
  • Hover docs, go-to-definition, parameter completion, and missing-parameter inspections now work for project-local classes in projects that aren't pip-installed (matches what sr-forge's runtime resolver does).
  • Alt+Enter quick-fixes show a preview of the change before you apply it.
    • Changed
  • Dataset picking is now via the in-editor marker mode. The old modal "Configure dataset" dialog is gone — paths are edited directly in the YAML.
  • Long tensor previews in expanded field rows now truncate with an ellipsis and the full text is shown in a tooltip. The visible truncation updates live as you resize the window.
  • The probe tool window content never exceeds the visible width — long content clips/wraps inside each block instead of pushing trailing controls off the right edge.
  • Expanded-field body indent is a single subtle step (used to compound to ~36 px for modified-field rows).
    • Fixed
  • After a `ConcatDataset`, the probe no longer surfaces stale Entry fields from previous probe runs (e.g. a `mask` field disappearing).
  • The dataset picker's clickable highlight no longer collides visually with YAML key syntax colours or warning underlines.
  • Boolean / integer tensors no longer render with grayscale shading when the visualizer window is smaller than the tensor — they stay pixel-exact.
  • Expanded-field body content now anchors to the left consistently, regardless of value length.
  • The probe tool window no longer logs a platform error on first open.
    • Removed
  • PyCharm 2024.2 support (JDK 17 incompatibility — the plugin requires JDK 21).
    • Developer notes These describe the internal mechanics; users shouldn't need to read this. Source the corresponding commits / file references for the full picture.
  • **Marker-mode dispatchers** use `IdeEventQueue.EventDispatcher` instead of the 253-only `NonLockedEventDispatcher` so the plugin loads on 2024.3 / 2025.1 / 2025.2 (`NoSuchClassError` otherwise). Suppressed deprecation warnings inline.
  • **`_target:` resolution** replaced the heuristic re-export matcher with a filesystem walk + `from .x import Y` re-export follower that mirrors sr-forge's `ConfigResolver` semantics. Project-level cache invalidated on PSI change.
  • **Probe script `_disable_instance_cache`** now recursively descends into `list` / `tuple` / `dict` attributes — previously missed `ConcatDataset._datasets` (a list), so inner `PatchedDataset` / `LazyDataset` kept their pickle caches enabled and surfaced stale `Entry` shapes from prior live runs.
  • **`ProbeChrome.`** no longer reads from `SrForgeHighlightSettings.getInstance()`. The platform rejects service access during class init; the `current` field now defaults to `LegacyProbeChrome` and the setting is consulted lazily via `refresh()`.
  • **Pipeline path overlay** moved from a `RangeHighlighter` + `CustomHighlighterRenderer` to a `JComponent` overlay added as a child of `editor.contentComponent`. Swing's paint order (`paintComponent → paintChildren`) puts the overlay strictly above the editor's indent-guide pass. Bezier routing pulls control points to `min(parent.x, child.x) − 24` so the trace never crosses text between markers; partial-curve animation uses De Casteljau subdivision; per-edge timing uses `pathTraceDurationMs × maxDepth` as total wall-clock.
  • **Polished display-mode chrome** (`ProbeChrome` sealed class) was implemented end-to-end with a hot-swap path that records render actions and replays under a new chrome. The polished aesthetic (timeline + numbered nodes) didn't survive review, so `forCurrentMode()` short-circuits to `LegacyProbeChrome` and the dropdown is hidden — code preserved for future iteration.
  • **Tensor Visualizer dtype-aware interpolation**: source `dtype.kind` is captured before the float64 cast in `viz_script.py`; resize uses `cv2.INTER_NEAREST` for `'b'`/`'i'`/`'u'` and `cv2.INTER_AREA` for `'f'`. Kotlin's `ImageViewPanel` mirrors this via an `isDiscreteDtype` field that forces `VALUE_INTERPOLATION_NEAREST_NEIGHBOR` regardless of zoom.
  • **Tensor Visualizer slider live drag**: removed `valueIsAdjusting` guards; `requestVisualization()` now coalesces concurrent requests via a `vizPending` flag (latest control state wins, no backlog of stale renders). `JTextField` replaced with `JSpinner` for ±1 stepping; spinner maxima kept in sync with slider maxima at every adjustment site.
  • **`FieldDetailPanel` BoxLayout fixes**: every Y_AXIS-laid-out container now has all children at `alignmentX = LEFT_ALIGNMENT`. `Box.createVerticalStrut` returns `Filler` with `CENTER` (0.5) by default, which shifted BoxLayout's baseline rightward and pulled LEFT-aligned siblings off-anchor by a content-width-dependent amount. Replaced via a `vstrut(h)` helper.
  • **Dynamic value-row ellipsis**: detail rows changed from `FlowLayout` to `BorderLayout` with the value in `CENTER`. `JLabel.paintComponent` ellipsizes via `SwingUtilities.layoutCompoundLabel` when bounds are narrower than preferred — only triggers if the layout doesn't honour `preferredSize`, which `BorderLayout.CENTER` doesn't.
  • **Tool-window horizontal clipping**: `contentAnchor` implements `Scrollable.getScrollableTracksViewportWidth = true`. Vertical anchoring (the previous `BorderLayout.NORTH` trick) is preserved.
  • **Build / Verifier**: bumped IntelliJ Platform compile target to 2026.1; raised `pluginSinceBuild` to 243; full verifier matrix green for PC/PY 243-253. Migrated startup activities to `ProjectActivity`. `ProbeToolWindowFactory` rewritten in Java to avoid Kotlin synthetic forwarders. Various deprecated/experimental API replacements (full list in commit history).

idea-plugin.name: Workspace Agent Bridge
idea-plugin.description:
Workspace Agent Bridge lets local coding agents work through the IntelliJ project model instead of guessing from the filesystem alone. It exposes a local REST API for reading files, searching indexed project content, navigating symbols, checking problems, formatting code, and applying workspace edits with IntelliJ-aware safety checks.

The plugin starts a local server at http://127.0.0.1:63441/api/v1. If that port is already busy, it scans nearby ports and uses the first available one. Agents connect by creating a workspace session for the project or directory they intend to work in, then use that session for file, search, navigation, inspection, and patch requests.

The API is optimized for agent-readable Markdown by default, with JSON available for structured clients. It supports common coding-agent workflows such as:

  • reading files with metadata, ranges, structure summaries, and problem reports;
  • searching by glob, text, fuzzy file name, or symbol, including read-only library and SDK context when requested;
  • jumping to declarations, finding usages, and reading documentation;
  • creating, replacing, deleting, moving, and patching workspace files;
  • running IntelliJ cleanup, optimize imports, and reformat operations.

Write access is intentionally limited to project workspace files. Dependency and SDK files are available as read-only context, and protected paths require explicit confirmation before writes. Delete and move operations use IntelliJ refactoring behavior where possible, so agents can update references instead of only moving bytes on disk.

For Codex users, the plugin bundles the workspace-agent-bridge skill and shows an upgrade notification with actions to copy or reveal the local skill directory. The bundled skill contains the agent-facing workflow details and examples.

idea-plugin.name: AI Review
idea-plugin.description:
AI-Powered Code Review for JetBrains IDEs

Get GitHub PR-style code reviews directly inside your IDE, powered by Claude Code CLI. AI Review collects your git diffs, sends them to Claude for analysis, and renders findings as inline annotations with optional quick-fix suggestions — all without leaving your editor. Publish findings directly to GitHub PRs using the GitHub CLI (gh).

Features

  • One-click AI review — run a full review on your current diff or a single file
  • Inline annotations — findings appear as gutter icons, highlights, and tooltips
  • Quick-fix suggestions — apply AI-suggested fixes with a single click
  • Manual review comments — add your own comments on any line
  • Publish to GitHub — push selected findings as PR review comments
  • Generate PR descriptions — auto-generate a PR title and body from your diff

Getting Started

  1. Install Claude Code CLI and authenticate (claude login)
  2. Install GitHub CLI and authenticate (gh auth login) — needed for PR publishing
  3. Install the plugin and restart your IDE
  4. Open Settings → Tools → AI Review to verify CLI paths are detected (or set them manually)
  5. Open a project with Git history, then run Tools → AI Review → Run Review

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2024.1+ (or any compatible JetBrains IDE)
  • Git integration enabled
  • Claude Code CLI — installed and authenticated
  • GitHub CLI (gh) — installed and authenticated (for PR publishing)

idea-plugin.name: Coding Switch
idea-plugin.description:
Coding Switch - AI Coding CLI and IDE Productivity Toolkit

Manage Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Antigravity CLI, and other AI coding command-line tools in JetBrains IDEs, with inline AI code completion, Git commit message generation, path-with-line-number insertion, CLI quick launch, and CLI version checks.

Features

  • AI CLI Provider Management — Manage and switch API configurations for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Antigravity CLI with official APIs, third-party compatible endpoints, local providers, connection tests, and built-in presets.
  • CLI Quick Launch and Version Checks — View installation status and version information, then launch terminal sessions with the selected CLI configuration.
  • Inline AI Code Completion — Use ghost-text completion with automatic/manual triggering, Tab acceptance, line-by-line acceptance, and FIM Completions / FIM Chat Completions support.
  • Code Path and Line Number Quick Insert — One-click insert file paths or code snippet locations with line numbers from the editor and project tree context menus into CLI terminals.
  • Git Commit Message Generation — Generate Conventional Commits style messages from selected changes in the commit tool window.
  • MCP, Skills, and Prompts — Manage MCP servers, GitHub-based skills, and Markdown prompt presets across supported AI CLIs.

功能

  • AI CLI 配置管理 — 管理并切换 Claude Code、Codex、OpenCode、Antigravity CLI 的 API 配置，支持官方接口、第三方兼容接口、本地模型、连接测试和内置供应商预设。
  • CLI 快速启动与版本检测 — 在 IDE 内查看安装状态和版本信息，并使用选中的 CLI 配置快速启动终端会话。
  • 行内 AI 代码补全 — 支持灰字补全、自动触发、手动触发、Tab 全量采纳、逐行采纳，以及 FIM Completions / FIM Chat Completions。
  • 代码路径与行号快速插入 — 从编辑器、项目树右键菜单一键插入文件路径或带行号的代码片段位置到 CLI 终端。
  • Git 提交信息生成 — 基于选中变更生成 Conventional Commits 风格提交信息。
  • MCP、技能与提示词管理 — 统一管理 MCP 服务器、GitHub 技能包和 Markdown 提示词预设，扩展多个 AI CLI 的上下文能力。

Privacy / 隐私

This plugin only reads and writes local configuration files. No user data is collected.

本插件仅在本地读写配置文件，不会收集任何用户数据。

idea-plugin.name: AgentBridge
idea-plugin.description:
Connect coding agents to JetBrains IDEs with MCP and ACP.

AgentBridge lets AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot and OpenCode work through IntelliJ IDEA and other JetBrains IDEs, using the same tools and feedback that human developers rely on.

Instead of working blindly through a terminal, external coding agents can operate directly through the IDE:

  • Edit files with full undo, formatting, and VCS integration
  • Navigate code using IntelliJ’s code intelligence (PSI)
  • Run inspections and IDE refactorings
  • Run builds, tests, run configurations, and git operations through the IDE
  • You see files open and update in real time while they work

The key difference is the feedback loop.

After every edit, the agent receives immediate feedback from the IDE, including errors, warnings, and inspections (e.g. SonarLint). This allows the agent to correct issues as they appear, instead of discovering them later after multiple changes.

This leads to more stable and maintainable code over longer sessions.

Supported agents
GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, JetBrains Junie, Amazon Kiro, OpenCode, Hermes Agent, Mistral Vibe, and Goose. Several of these integrations were contributed by the community.

Modes

  • MCP server: connect any external MCP-capable AI coding agent to the IDE
  • ACP client: run supported agents directly inside the IDE

The plugin runs locally and does not collect or send telemetry.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
AgentBridge connects AI coding agents to your IDE via 100+ MCP tools for code intelligence, navigation, editing, debugging, and git.

idea-plugin.name: RefIo
idea-plugin.description:
RefIo - Local-First AI Coding Plugin for IntelliJ.

For developers who want the leverage of AI coding without giving up observability, model choice, or the native JetBrains experience.

An open-source AI coding plugin for IntelliJ IDEA, built in Kotlin. Native JetBrains UI, no WebView, no cloud account required, no telemetry. Works with local models (Ollama, LM Studio) or cloud LLMs.

Early-stage, actively developed. The foundation is in place: three execution modes, visible tool calls, a snapshot before every write and a build check after it. The orchestration depth is still growing. See the Roadmap for where the project is heading.

What it does today

  • Three execution modes - Chat (conversation, no tools), Plan (read-only analysis, enforced in code), Agent (file edits with a snapshot before every write).
  • Verified edits - after a turn that changed files, RefIo runs your build or test command, feeds the real failures back to the model for up to two repair rounds, and marks the turn as failed verification instead of reporting a success it cannot back up.
  • Local or cloud LLMs - Ollama, LM Studio, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, Custom OpenAI, Z.AI. A universal tool-calling protocol works with models that lack native function calling.
  • Guardrails for small models - loop and repetition detection, no-op edit detection, and an abandoned turn recorded as incomplete rather than successful.
  • Structural refactoring - find_usages and rename_symbol backed by IntelliJ PSI inside the IDE.
  • Tool system - per-mode permissions (ON / ASK / OFF), a diff preview before an edit is approved, PathSandbox with symlink resolution, regex allow/block/ask command rules, snapshot and rollback.
  • Context control - @mentions for directing context (@file, @codebase, @diff, @problems, @terminal, and more), RAG with semantic chunking, a token budget that scales to the model's context window.
  • Cost control - per-session cost ceiling, reasoning-effort levels, and cache-aware accounting so a cache-served prompt is not billed as fresh.
  • Extensibility - subagents as Markdown + YAML (Claude Code compatible format), MCP protocol support (STDIO + HTTP/SSE) with built-in presets, project instructions via AGENTS.md and .refio/rules/*.md with glob-based activation.
  • One core, three surfaces - the native IntelliJ plugin, a full terminal TUI and a headless runner share the same engine, so an agent run can be scripted and asserted on.
  • No-egress mode - one switch blocks all outbound traffic, both model calls and the web tools, for strict offline work.

What it is, and what it isn't

It is: an early-stage open-source plugin with a clear direction - a native JetBrains tool for developers working in Kotlin, Java and JVM ecosystems, or anyone who wants their AI coding agent to run offline and be auditable.

It isn't: a drop-in replacement for inline completion (different category). A polished enterprise-grade product (not yet). Something you install and forget - changes happen fast at v0.0.1.x.

Known limitations (honest)

  • No git worktree isolation per task - agents edit your working tree directly, with snapshot rollback.
  • The planning loop is basic - no plan-refinement iteration yet.
  • The multi-agent runtime works but can only be launched from the CLI; the IDE visualizes a run, it does not start one.
  • Security layers are pragmatic and self-assessed, not independently audited.
  • Tested on IntelliJ IDEA only; other JetBrains IDEs may work but are not claimed.
  • Small commit history, fast changes, breaking changes possible pre-1.0.

Quick start with local models

ollama pull nomic-embed-text        # required for RAG
ollama pull qwen3.5:9b              # small and fast
# or, for bigger hardware:
ollama pull qwen3.5:35b
ollama pull qwen3.5:122b
  1. Install the plugin from JetBrains Marketplace
  2. Open the RefIo tool window (right sidebar)
  3. Go to RefIo, Settings and pick your model
  4. Start with @codebase your question here

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2024.2 or newer (Community or Ultimate)
  • Ollama or LM Studio (optional, for local models)
  • JDK 17+ only if you also want to build the standalone CLI

refio.dev | GitHub (MIT) | Roadmap | Privacy | Issues & Discussions

Built in Kotlin. Early-stage. Honest about what's done and what's next. Contributions welcome.

idea-plugin.name: CursorJ
idea-plugin.description:
CursorJ brings Cursor's AI agent into JetBrains IDEs via the Agent Client Protocol (ACP).

  • Full agentic coding with file editing, terminal commands, and codebase understanding
  • Project indexing with lexical search, symbol lookup, and optional semantic reranking
  • Reliable SQLite-backed lexical persistence with safe concurrent index updates
  • Inline @file references and image attachments via drag-and-drop or paste

  • Multiple concurrent chat sessions with intelligent tab naming
  • Chat history with search and restore; prompt history
  • Unified rules management for global user rules and project rules (.cursor/rules/)
  • Cursor Skills discovery and settings management; inline / and @ completion in chat (merged with ACP slash commands) that keeps focus in the input
  • Agent, Plan, Ask, and simulated Debug modes with native IntelliJ UI, including multiple-choice cards for agent questions
  • Permission control with per-turn rollback via Local History

Project home: https://github.com/vaughanb/CursorJ

Support and issues: https://github.com/vaughanb/CursorJ/issues
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.6.0

  • Debug mode (simulated): A fourth chat mode that reproduces Cursor's Debug workflow — hypothesize, add temporary instrumentation, reproduce, analyze runtime evidence, apply a targeted fix, then clean up. Because ACP exposes no native debug mode, CursorJ keeps the session in agent, injects a Debug workflow prompt, and captures runtime evidence via a per-session log file under <project>/.cursorj/debug/ plus a localhost token-gated log sink. Post-turn actions offer I reproduced it, Clean up, and View logs.
  • Edit & resend: Edit one of your earlier messages to branch the conversation from that point — later replies are discarded and the prior turns are replayed as context into a fresh session.
  • Fixed Windows drag-and-drop of file:// paths: Dropping or pasting a file:// URI that wraps a Windows path (e.g. the GNOME copied-files clipboard format) now resolves correctly instead of being dropped.
  • Faster IDE shutdown: Closing the IDE (or a project) no longer hangs several seconds per open CursorJ tab.

Known Cursor ACP limitations (agent/protocol constraints, not plugin bugs):

  • No native Debug session mode: the agent advertises only agent, plan, and ask and rejects a debug mode id, so Debug is simulated locally rather than driven by the agent.
  • No conversation forking: the agent does not advertise ACP session/fork, so Edit & resend replays context into a new session instead of branching server-side.
  • Model parameter tiers cannot be switched at runtime: each model is offered with a single baked-in parameter set, so toggles such as Composer Normal/Fast or Claude Opus effort levels are not selectable through ACP.

idea-plugin.name: Copy Path for Claude Code
idea-plugin.description:
Copy Path for Claude Code

Copy file and folder references in Claude Code @-mention format directly from your IDE. Press ⌥C (Alt+C) or right-click — works in both the editor and the project tree:

  • Editor (line selected): @src/auth.ts#L42-68
  • Editor (no selection): @src/auth.ts
  • Project tree (file): @src/components/Button.tsx
  • Project tree (folder): @src/components/

Paste straight into Claude Code and it knows exactly which file and lines you mean.

Features

  • Copy file or folder references in @path/to/file#Lx-y format
  • Smart line detection based on editor text selection
  • Multi-cursor support — each caret generates a separate reference with line numbers
  • Multi-file selection support — select multiple files/folders and copy all paths at once
  • Paths containing spaces are automatically wrapped in double quotes (e.g. @"my file.ts")
  • Directory paths include a trailing slash to distinguish folders from files (e.g. @src/)
  • Optional trailing space after copied references for easy pasting
  • Configurable separator for multiple references (space or newline)
  • Works from editor context menu, project tree context menu, and keyboard shortcut
  • Configurable balloon notification with adjustable duration
  • Compatible with all JetBrains IDEs

Reference Format

ContextOutput
File (no selection)@src/utils/auth.ts
File (single line selected)@src/utils/auth.ts#L42
File (multiple lines selected)@src/utils/auth.ts#L42-68
File with spaces in path@"my file.ts"
File with spaces + line range@"my file.ts#L42-68"
Folder@src/components/
Folder with spaces in path@"my components/"
Multi-cursor (carets only)@src/utils/auth.ts#L5 @src/utils/auth.ts#L42
Multi-cursor (with selections)@src/utils/auth.ts#L5-10 @src/utils/auth.ts#L30-35
Multiple files selected@src/Button.tsx @src/Input.tsx

How to Use

  • Editor context menu — Right-click in any editor → Copy Path for Claude Code. The reference includes line numbers based on your current text selection.
  • Project tree context menu — Right-click any file or folder in the Project tool window → Copy Path for Claude Code. Copies the relative path without line numbers.
  • Keyboard shortcut — Press Alt+C (⌥C on macOS). Works in both the editor and project tree; the output adapts automatically based on focus and selection.

Examples

  1. Select lines 10–25 in src/components/Button.tsx, press ⌥C → @src/components/Button.tsx#L10-25
  2. Right-click package.json in the project tree → @package.json
  3. Right-click src/components folder → @src/components/
  4. Right-click my components folder (with spaces) → @"my components/"
  5. Right-click my file.ts (with spaces) → @"my file.ts"
  6. Select lines 5–10 in my file.ts (with spaces), press ⌥C → @"my file.ts#L5-10"
  7. Place caret without selecting text, press ⌥C → @src/index.ts (path only)
  8. Place multiple cursors (Alt+Click) on lines 5, 20, 42, press ⌥C → @src/utils/auth.ts#L5 @src/utils/auth.ts#L20 @src/utils/auth.ts#L42
  9. Select text at multiple cursors (e.g. lines 5–10 and 30–35), press ⌥C → @src/utils/auth.ts#L5-10 @src/utils/auth.ts#L30-35

Settings

Settings → Tools → Copy Path for Claude Code

  • Append trailing space — Add a space after the copied reference for easy pasting (default: on)
  • Multiple references separator — Separator between references when copying multiple files or multi-cursor selections: Space or Newline (default: Space)
  • Show notification after copy — Toggle balloon notification on/off (default: enabled)
  • Notification duration — How long the notification stays visible, 1–30 seconds (default: 3s)

Compatibility

Works with all JetBrains IDEs (2024.1+): IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, PhpStorm, Rider, CLion, RustRover, DataGrip, Android Studio, and more.

idea-plugin.name: Terminal Bridge
idea-plugin.description:
Expose your IntelliJ IDE terminals through a local REST API and WebSocket server, enabling programmatic terminal control from external tools.

Features

  • REST API — List, create, rename, close, and focus terminal tabs
  • Command Execution — Send commands to any terminal programmatically
  • Output Reading — Read terminal output on demand or stream in real-time
  • Full-Screen TUI Support — Captures the live screen of full-screen terminal applications that use the alternate screen buffer, such as Claude Code's redesigned UI, vim, and less, not just the scrollback
  • WebSocket Streaming — Live output via WebSocket with 250ms polling
  • Web Dashboard — Built-in visual interface at localhost for terminal management
  • Multi-Device — Terminal ownership tracking prevents cross-device conflicts
  • Zero Config — Works immediately when your IDE opens

Use Cases

  • AI coding assistants that need terminal access
  • CI/CD dashboards that orchestrate IDE terminals
  • Custom automation scripts and toolchains
  • Remote terminal management for development workflows
  • Multi-agent orchestration — each agent in its own terminal tab

Runs entirely on localhost. No data leaves your machine.

API available at http://localhost:9876/api/
idea-plugin.change-notes:
3.2

  • Removed the until-build compatibility cap entirely (previously re-capped each IDE release, e.g. 262.*) so the plugin no longer needs republishing every time a new IDE version ships.

3.1

  • Compatibility extended to IntelliJ 2026.2 (262.*) so the plugin continues to load in the new IDE release.

3.0

  • Output reading now follows a full-screen terminal application into the alternate screen buffer. Claude Code's redesigned UI — and other full-screen TUIs such as vim and less — render into the alternate screen buffer, which left the previous active-buffer-only read returning only the pre-launch scrollback. The reader now selects whichever buffer is live (by modification stamp), so on-screen content is captured correctly; reading a normal shell prompt is unchanged. A new setting, Settings, Tools, Terminal Bridge, "Use legacy terminal output read", reverts to the previous behavior if a specific IDE or terminal combination regresses.

2.8

  • Single-line commands now submit reliably in TUI applications such as Claude Code. Single-line input is sent as the body followed by a separate carriage return — the same mechanism multi-line already used — so a command is no longer occasionally typed but left unsubmitted in the input box. This unifies submit handling for all sends; behavior at a normal shell prompt is unchanged.

2.7

  • Fixed multi-line commands not submitting in TUI applications — the body and the execute newline were delivered as one bracketed paste, so a full-screen terminal app treated the trailing newline as a literal newline instead of a submit. Multi-line input now sends the body, then a separate carriage return to submit. Single-line behavior is unchanged.

2.6

  • Rebuilt for 2026.1 (261.*) marketplace verification

2.4

  • Admin UI redesign with improved terminal management
  • Dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 binding for cross-platform compatibility
  • Removed untilBuild cap — works on future IDE versions

2.3

  • Fixed license product code validation
  • Fixed terminal list and output read timeouts (was blocking indefinitely)
  • Free-tier dashboard with PRO badges on paid features
  • AI integration guide page at /guide
  • Auto release-date stamping in builds

2.0

  • Fixed clearFirst terminal output behavior

1.1

  • Cached reflection methods for performance

idea-plugin.name: OpenSpec
idea-plugin.description:
An IDE-native client for the OpenSpec spec-driven development framework by Fission AI. Browse specs, orchestrate the propose → generate → implement → archive lifecycle, and route AI-generated artifacts through the tool of your choice — all without leaving your IDE.

Features:

  • Spec browser & viewer — a master/detail tree of capabilities and requirements beside a rendered-markdown preview pane, with content-aware search (over requirement and scenario text), artifact-status badges on tree icons, and a consolidated change-deltas view that shows everything a change modifies at the spec level
  • Validation you can navigate — real-time editor inspections and quick-fixes matching the OpenSpec CLI's own parser, plus a Validate action (from the toolbar or the Project View context menu, scoped to the clicked change or spec) whose results render grouped by file with clickable file:line links and per-severity coloring
  • Change lifecycle — create, implement, verify, and archive OpenSpec changes from a dedicated tool window, with schema-aware completeness gates and task-level progress
  • Works with your AI tooling — detects 30+ AI coding tools (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and more) and hands generation off to the one you already use, or calls the Anthropic, OpenAI, or Google APIs directly with your own key
  • Schema authoring — fork, create, and validate custom workflow schemas, with template editing and resolution-provenance tags straight from the CLI
  • Stores & worksets — browse and manage the OpenSpec CLI 1.5 coordination model, with health diagnostics and graceful support back to the 1.4 workspace model
  • Setup wizard — guided onboarding for new and existing projects; the plugin works with or without the OpenSpec CLI installed and degrades gracefully

Compatible with IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, WebStorm, RubyMine, and the rest of the JetBrains IDE family, 2024.2 and later. Spec browsing and validation are fully language-agnostic.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • OpenSpec CLI 1.11.x is now a supported line. 1.11 is an additive, safe-direction superset of 1.10 — verified by running the real 1.11.0 CLI over the shared parity corpus, its default and strict validation verdicts are unchanged, so nothing is re-gated and the built-in validator needs no change. 1.11 adds one new validation rule — a spec whose ## Purpose is still a placeholder (a TBD/TODO marker, or the sentence archiving writes for a new capability) is now flagged with a warning (a failure under strict) — which only makes the CLI stricter, so the built-in fallback stays never more restrictive. The plugin declares 1.11.x supported (minimum CLI remains 1.3.0), with per-generation contract coverage against captured real 1.11.0 output including a positive-control lock on the new rule.

Fixed

  • Generating tasks no longer fails on Windows with an "Illegal char" error. Specifications are declared as a file glob (specs/**/*.md) rather than a single file; once the specs step was complete, assembling the next artifact's prompt tried to resolve that glob to a filesystem path, which Windows rejects (the * is an illegal path character), aborting generation. Non-Windows platforms accept * in a path and degraded silently, so the defect was Windows-only. The plugin now treats a glob-valued prerequisite as a reference on every platform, so generation succeeds identically across operating systems.
  • "Register Existing Store" no longer dead-ends on a healthy OpenSpec root that isn't yet a store. Registering such a root requires confirming creation of its store-identity metadata; the action previously surfaced that confirmation as an un-actionable error dialog, leaving no way to proceed. It now shows a Yes/Cancel prompt (carrying the CLI's own message), registers the root on confirmation, and leaves it untouched on cancel. Roots that are already stores, and refusals, are unaffected.

idea-plugin.name: MCP Code Intelligence
idea-plugin.description:
MCP Code Intelligence exposes 13 IDE-level semantic analysis tools to AI agents through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

Stop burning tokens on grep. AI agents get direct access to the same understanding your IDE uses internally — type resolution, reference graphs, call hierarchies, data flow analysis, and safe cross-language refactoring. Every response includes a nextAction hint that guides the agent to the optimal follow-up call.

Why agents pick these over CLI

  • Zero false positives — reference search uses the IDE's semantic index, not text matching
  • Structured responses with file+line+column and nextAction hints — agents chain tools automatically
  • Refactoring is safe — rename/move/extract update every reference across Java/Kotlin/XML/Manifest
  • Works across Java, Kotlin, and mixed codebases — including Android, Compose, Room, Hilt, Retrofit, Navigation

Tools

  • resolve_symbol — Type and declaration location at a code position
  • find_symbol — Locate a symbol by simple or fully-qualified name (no grep!)
  • find_references — Usages, callers, callees, type hierarchy (by position OR qualified name)
  • get_scope — All visible symbols: locals, members, extensions, imports
  • query_project — Project overview, dependency impact, API surface, build variants
  • query_framework — Room / Retrofit / Hilt / Compose / Navigation structural views
  • analyze_data_flow — Nullability inference, forward/backward value propagation

  • refactor — Rename, move, extract, safe delete, change signature across Java/Kotlin/XML
  • checkpoint — Create, list, rollback, and diff IDE Local History snapshots
  • sandbox — Decompile library classes, Java-to-Kotlin conversion, batch inspections

Highlights

  • One-click Cursor configuration from the built-in Tool Window
  • Per-tool metrics: invocation count, token usage, execution time

idea-plugin.name: MCP Control
idea-plugin.description:
MCP server that gives AI agents access to IDE features they can't get from the command line.

Agents can read files and run terminals on their own. They can't set breakpoints, step through code, or inspect variables. MCP Control exposes these IDE-only capabilities as MCP tools.

13 tools across 4 categories

Breakpoints (work without an active debug session)
  • list, add, update, remove — with batch support (comma-separated)
  • Exception breakpoints — pause on any PHP exception class
  • Method breakpoints — a breakpoint on a method/function definition line becomes a real method breakpoint
  • Conditions, log expressions, suspend control
Session management
  • List active debug sessions, stop one or all
  • Automatic session tracking with switch detection
Navigation (requires paused session)
  • Step over / into / out / continue
  • Run to a specific line
  • Every step returns a snapshot: source context, variables, call stack (library frames auto-collapsed)
Inspection (requires paused session)
  • Full debug snapshot (source + variables + stack trace); inspect any stack frame's scope by index
  • Expand variables to any depth (circular references detected); page through large collections with offset/limit
  • Evaluate PHP expressions with side effects ($bar = 'new value')
  • Read console output (stdout/stderr) — works with Docker/remote processes

Setup

  1. Open the MCP Control tool window (bottom panel)
  2. Click "Install .mcp.json" to configure your MCP client
  3. Start the server

Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop, and any other MCP client. Configurable port, optional auto-start per project.

How debugging works

You start debug sessions in PhpStorm as usual. The agent interacts with them through MCP tools: setting breakpoints, stepping through code, inspecting state. You both see the same debug session. Pair debugging with an AI.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.2.3
  • Start failures now name the real cause. An occupied port was reported as "JobCancellationException: LazyStandaloneCoroutine is cancelling" — the debug server engine's internal cancellation wrapper — instead of the port conflict underneath it
  • A port conflict is reported as one in the tool window and activity log, not only in the notification balloon. The notification also warns that an agent connecting to that port reaches the PhpStorm instance already holding it, not this project
  • Start failures are now actually written to idea.log, stamped with the plugin version and IDE build, so the notification's "See Help > Show Log" has something to show
  • Pressing Stop while the server is still starting no longer shows a spurious "Failed" state, and a start that completes after Stop no longer flips the tool window back to "Running"
2026.2.2
  • Versions now name the newest PhpStorm release this build has been verified against — 2026.2. It requires PhpStorm 2026.1 or newer and replaces 0.7.x; PhpStorm 2025.1 – 2025.3 is served by the 2025.3.x releases
  • Replaced an internal platform API used to read the plugin's own version, which is not permitted on newer PhpStorm builds. Supersedes 2026.2.1, which was never published
  • Fixed compatibility declaration: 0.7.0 claimed support for PhpStorm 2025.3 but the MCP server could not start there — the toolbar showed the server as running while nothing was listening. This release requires 2026.1 or newer, which is what it is actually built against
  • PhpStorm 2025.1 – 2025.3 users: install MCP Control 2025.3.1, which has the same tool features built against the 2025.3 platform
  • No upper version limit any more: new PhpStorm releases are supported on day one instead of waiting for a compatibility republish. Verified by launching PhpStorm 2026.1 and 2026.2
  • The tool window no longer claims the server is running before it is: a start attempt now shows "Starting…", turns into "Running" only once the engine reports a bound port, and shows "Failed: <reason>" if it doesn't. Start/Stop follow that state instead of guessing from an internal object
  • Start failures are no longer swallowed. The real exception is written to idea.log and shown in the notification, and a failure is only reported as a port conflict when it actually is one — previously every failure claimed "port already in use"
0.7.0
  • Method breakpoints now supported: adding a breakpoint on a method/function definition line creates a real PHP method breakpoint on that line (same as PhpStorm's gutter "Method" option). Trait/interface/anonymous-class methods fall back to a line breakpoint on the first statement
  • Pagination: debug_evaluate and debug_variable_detail cap each node at 50 children and accept offset/limit to page through large arrays/collections; truncated nodes show a "... N more children" hint, so big evals no longer dump in full
  • Frame-aware inspection: debug_evaluate, debug_variable_detail and debug_snapshot now follow the selected stack frame (or an explicit frame_index) instead of always reading the top frame
  • Breaking: debug_inspect_frame removed — use debug_snapshot(frame_index) instead (14 → 13 tools)
  • Breakpoint placement validation: blank/comment/const lines are rejected with the nearest valid line suggested — no more ghost breakpoints that never fire
  • Stepping no longer hangs the request: a bounded 60s wait returns a "still running" result instead of blocking forever
  • Session-ended results now include the session id and a console tail (the last chance to read stdout/stderr from a stopped session)
  • Activity log shows the full tool-call arguments, not just the tool name
0.6.1
  • Maintenance release for PhpStorm 2025.3 — the 0.7.0 tool features built against the 2025.3 platform
0.6.0
  • Smarter variable hint: when globals are filtered and no local variables remain, the agent is told how many globals are hidden and how to include them
  • debug_run_to_line now detects intermediate breakpoint stops and tells the agent it didn't reach the target line
  • debug_run_to_line validates line number against file length before jumping
  • Session termination notice: when the previous session dies and a new one takes over, the agent is informed instead of silently switching
  • Removed session_activate tool — session switching is a UI concern handled by the IDE, not an agent action
  • Removed all internal API usage (XDebugSessionImpl) for JetBrains Marketplace compatibility
0.5.1
  • Extended IDE version compatibility (2025.3 – 2026.1)
0.5.0
  • Breakpoint mutations (add, update, remove) now return the full breakpoint list with (new)/(updated) highlights
  • Batch operations: breakpoint_add accepts comma-separated locations, breakpoint_update accepts comma-separated IDs
  • Method breakpoint detection: adding a breakpoint on a function definition line is blocked with guidance to add manually
  • Stack trace collapsing: 3+ consecutive library frames collapsed by default, expand_stack parameter to override
  • Session-breakpoint cross-reference: session_list shows which breakpoint a paused session is at
  • Smarter session switch detection: terminated sessions auto-track the next session instead of blocking
  • Evaluate tool description clarifies frame #0 limitation (xdebug constraint)
  • Fix: circular reference false positives on arrays with size info (e.g. array[7])
  • Cleaner output: "Current breakpoints:" header on remove/partial-failure responses
  • Leaner evaluate output: removed redundant source position header
0.4.0
  • New tool: breakpoint_add_exception — break on any PHP exception class by name
  • Short name lookup with disambiguation (RuntimeException → lists all matches if ambiguous)
  • Only classes extending \Exception or \Error are accepted
  • Exception breakpoints work with existing breakpoint_list, breakpoint_update, and breakpoint_remove
0.3.2
  • Rebranding: MCP Hub → MCP Control
0.3.1
  • Fix: .mcp.json installer now includes required "type": "http" field
0.3.0
  • New tool: debug_console — read stdout/stderr from the debug session's console (useful for Docker/remote PHP processes)
  • Fix: stopping a session now auto-activates the next alive session instead of leaving a dead tab focused
  • Smarter session errors: when the active session ends but other sessions exist, the error lists them with guidance to use session_activate
  • Cleaner session switch alert messages
0.2.1
  • Show plugin version in tool window status line
0.2.0
  • New tool: session_activate — switch active debug session (like clicking a debug tab)
  • Removed session_id parameter from all debug tools — simpler API, fewer tokens
  • Session switch detection: agent gets an alert if the user or IDE switches the active session unexpectedly
  • MCP server version now matches the plugin version
0.1.1
  • Fix: Settings page now visible under Settings > Tools > MCP Control
0.1.0
  • Initial release
  • 13 MCP tools: breakpoints, sessions, navigation, inspection
  • Tool window with activity log, start/stop, settings
  • One-click .mcp.json installation
  • Configurable port and auto-start per project

idea-plugin.name: Roo Code (CE)
idea-plugin.description:
Roo Code (CE) - Production-Ready AI Coding Assistant

Roo Code (CE) is a high-performance, community-driven edition of the Roo Code AI assistant for IntelliJ-based IDEs. It provides a stable and feature-rich environment to run VSCode-based coding agents like Roo Code and Cline directly within your favorite development environment.

🚀 Why Roo Code (CE)?

While other versions may suffer from instability, this Community Edition is dedicated to providing a professional-grade experience:

  • Truly Usable: Fixed critical JCEF timing bugs, editor concurrency deadlocks, memory leaks, and multi-window UI freezes.
  • Feature Parity: Full support for Checkpoints, Problem Selectors, Worktrees, and MCP—ensuring the JetBrains experience matches the VSCode original.
  • Production Ready: Deeply optimized for professional use, including first-class support for PyCharm and multi-window workflows.

🛠️ Core Features

  • VSCode Agent Compatibility: Seamlessly run VSCode-based coding agents (Roo Code, Cline, etc.)
  • Deep IDE Integration: Native tool windows, editor context actions, and integrated terminal support.
  • AI-Powered Assistance: Leverage advanced AI models for autonomous coding, refactoring, and debugging.

💻 Supported IDEs

  • IntelliJ IDEA (Ultimate & Community)
  • PyCharm (Professional & Community)
  • WebStorm, PhpStorm, RubyMine, CLion, GoLand, DataGrip, Rider, Android Studio

📌 Requirements

  • Requires Node.js v18+ installed on your system
  • Requires IDE version 2023.1 or later for optimal compatibility


Note: Roo Code (CE) is an independent community project and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by JetBrains or RooCode, Inc.

idea-plugin.name: Arthas Workbench
idea-plugin.description:
English:

Arthas Workbench is an IntelliJ IDEA plugin for local Arthas workflows. It helps you discover JVM processes started from IDEA Run/Debug or found on the local machine, attach Arthas with managed package sources and port allocation, manage Terminal and Log views for each session, open the Arthas Web UI in your browser, analyze JVM artifacts through a local Jifa Web service, and expose a stable MCP Gateway endpoint for AI tools or IDE assistants.

Key features:

  • Discover JVM processes from both IDEA Run/Debug and the local machine.
  • Attach Arthas with managed package sources, Java selection, and port allocation.
  • Analyze .jfr, .hprof, GC logs, and thread dumps through Jifa Web.
  • Auto-download and cache the Jifa helper jar on first use, or use an offline helper path from Settings.
  • Manage Terminal and Log views for multiple sessions in dedicated tool windows.
  • Open the Arthas Web UI and copy a stable MCP Gateway configuration from the IDE.

Detailed operation documents: https://github.com/weilhuang/arthas-workbench

中文:

Arthas Workbench 是一个面向本地 Arthas 工作流的 IntelliJ IDEA 插件。它可以帮助你发现 IDEA Run/Debug 和本机上的 JVM 进程，用一致的流程完成 Arthas Attach，在独立工具窗口里管理多会话的 Terminal / Log，并提供浏览器版 Jifa 文件分析能力与稳定的 MCP Gateway 入口，方便 AI 工具或 IDE 助手接入。

核心能力：

  • 同时发现 IDEA Run/Debug 与本机 JVM 进程。
  • 统一管理 Arthas 包来源、Attach Java 选择和端口分配。
  • 通过 Jifa Web 分析 .jfr、.hprof、GC 日志和 thread dump。
  • 首次使用时自动下载并缓存 Jifa helper jar，也支持在 Settings 中配置离线 helper 路径。
  • 在独立工具窗口中管理多会话的 Terminal / Log。
  • 直接打开 Arthas Web UI，并一键复制稳定的 MCP Gateway 配置。

详细操作文档: https://github.com/weilhuang/arthas-workbench

idea-plugin.name: Mermaid Studio Core
idea-plugin.description:
Mermaid Studio Core provides rich language support for authoring Mermaid diagrams in your JetBrains IDE - free error detection, syntax highlighting, live preview, and export for all native Mermaid.js diagram types. All features work fully offline.

Upgrade with a paid Mermaid Studio Core license to unlock every advanced feature for Flowchart, Sequence, Class, State, ER, Block, and Swimlane diagrams - including inspections, code completion, formatting, refactoring, the interactive editor, and MCP tools - plus your own custom themes and the theme generator for all diagram types except C4. A full Mermaid Studio license extends advanced features to all native Mermaid.js diagram types.

Supports Mermaid.js 12.0.0 with optional support for previous versions of Mermaid.js. See supported versions.

Remote development: Works in JetBrains remote development environments, excluding JetBrains Gateway.

Compatible with Android Studio starting with the Quail (2026.1) canary releases.

Free Features

Available for all native Mermaid.js diagram types:

  • Basic Error Detection - Real-time parser-based syntax error highlighting as you type
  • Syntax & Semantic Highlighting - Rich, diagram-aware highlighting with theme-appropriate colors
  • Live Preview - Real-time rendering with zoom, pan, search, and background matching (auto-matches editor or diagram theme). Supports Mac trackpad gestures for pinch-to-zoom and two-finger panning
  • Appearance Controls - Set a light/dark diagram theme, look, and font from the preview Appearance dropdown
  • Bundled Custom Themes - Eight ready-made custom themes (Chalk, Iris, Islands, Moss, Neutral, Parchment, Slate, Terracotta), each with matched light and dark variants (all diagram types except C4)
  • Export - Save diagrams as PNG or SVG, or copy as PNG or SVG to the clipboard
  • Mermaid in Markdown - Full highlighting and live preview for diagrams in Markdown code fences
  • Go to Mermaid Source - Jump from a diagram image in Markdown (.svg / .png) back to its .mmd / .mermaid source via a gutter icon
  • Frontmatter Support - YAML schema validation and completion for diagram configuration
  • Icon Sets - Use bundled FontAwesome, AWS, Azure, and GCP icons in your diagrams
  • Code Folding - Collapse diagram sections to focus on what matters
  • Brace Matching - Highlights and auto-inserts matching brackets and delimiters
  • Color Gutter Icons & Picker - Inline color swatches in the gutter, with a click-to-edit color picker for every color value in your diagrams
  • User-Defined Live Templates - Add your own live templates scoped to Mermaid editor contexts (Settings > Editor > Live Templates)
  • Localization - UI elements, error messages, inspections, and inline documentation translated into German, Japanese, Korean, and Simplified Chinese (generated from English using a workflow that leverages multiple frontier language models)

Paid Features

A Core license unlocks all implemented features for the 7 core diagram types listed below. Each diagram type has a different set of features based on what makes sense for its syntax and structure - for example, refactoring applies to diagrams with named elements, and code vision applies to diagrams with definitions and references. New features are added regularly.

  • Interactive Editor - Drag-and-drop flowchart creation plus visual editing for class diagrams (rename elements, set annotations, style classes and relationships), with a persistent style tool window that works in both standalone diagrams and Markdown code fences
  • Print & Vector PDF - Print diagrams with paper-size-aware scaling and configurable margins, or route through your OS print-to-PDF for lossless vector PDF export
  • MCP Tools - AI agents can generate and validate diagrams in Mermaid Studio's mermaid.js rendering environment
  • Enhanced Error Detection - Semantic validation that catches issues beyond syntax, such as naming conflicts, out-of-range indices, and unsupported values
  • Inspections & Quick Fixes - Catch logic issues that Mermaid itself can't pinpoint, like unresolved references, circular references, unused style classes, duplicate definitions, and invalid lifecycles, often with one-click fixes
  • Code Completion - Contextual suggestions for syntax, element references, and values
  • Live Templates - Bundled, customizable templates for common diagram constructs
  • Theme CSS Highlighting & Completions - CSS highlighting, validation, and contextual class-name completion inside frontmatter config.themeCSS: blocks, with completions sourced from your classDef names and the classes pulled from the rendered live preview (requires a paid JetBrains IDE with CSS support prior to 2026.1, or any JetBrains IDE from 2026.1 onward)
  • Automatic Formatting - Keep diagrams clean and consistent
  • Refactoring - Safely rename elements with automatic reference updates
  • Find Usages - Locate all references to any diagram element
  • Structure View - Navigate diagram elements in the structure tool window
  • Code Vision - Inline usage counts on definitions
  • Navigate from Preview - Click diagram elements to jump to their declaration in the source code
  • Diagram Sync - Automatically export diagrams as SVG or PNG files on save
  • Custom Icon Sets - Import additional icon sets from Iconify or local files
  • Custom Themes - Build your own themes in a visual editor with live preview, tune colors per diagram type, and import or export them as JSON to share across projects (available for all diagram types except C4)
  • Theme Generator - Create a complete light-and-dark theme from a handful of seed colors, or pull the seeds from an image such as a logo or screenshot, then apply it directly or refine it in the editor (available for all diagram types except C4)

MCP Tools

Mermaid Studio Core includes MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools that leverage its deep understanding of Mermaid diagrams for AI-assisted diagram generation and validation.

  • generateMermaidDiagram - Generate a Mermaid diagram as SVG from provided code
  • generateMermaidPng - Generate a PNG image and save it to a file
  • analyzeMermaidDiagram - Validate diagram code using Mermaid Studio's parsing and analysis
  • getMermaidFrontmatterSchema - Get the JSON Schema for a diagram type's frontmatter configuration
  • searchMermaidIcons - Search configured icon sets for available icons
  • getMermaidSyntaxGuide - Get a condensed syntax guide for a diagram type

Diagram Type Coverage

All native Mermaid.js diagram types get free-tier features. A paid license unlocks all implemented features for:

  • Mermaid Studio Core (this plugin) - Flowchart, Sequence, Class Diagram, State Diagram, ER Diagram, Block Diagram, Swimlane
  • Mermaid Studio - All native Mermaid.js diagram types, including C4, Architecture, Gantt, Mindmap, and more

The specific features available vary by diagram type based on what each type's syntax supports.

Telemetry

Mermaid Studio collects usage data to help improve the plugin. Telemetry is essential for understanding how users interact with features and identifying areas for improvement.

No personally identifiable or project-identifiable information is collected.

Telemetry is disabled by default in stable releases; nothing is sent unless you turn it on in the plugin settings. In Early Access Program (EAP) builds it is enabled by default and can be turned off in the same place.

Learn more.

Visit MermaidStudio.dev for more information and documentation about Mermaid Studio and its features.

Tachi Labs and Mermaid Studio are not affiliated with Mermaid or Mermaid Chart Inc.

idea-plugin.name: IDE Database MCP
idea-plugin.description:
IDE Database MCP exposes database connections configured in JetBrains IDEs as a local MCP (Model Context Protocol) service, so AI/MCP clients can discover data sources and execute SQL directly from the IDE context.

Tool list (tools/list)

  • database_list_datasources: discover available IDE-managed data sources with name, url, driverClass and an inferred type.
  • database_list_databases: list databases/catalogs/schemas under one IDE-managed data source.
  • database_execute_sql_query: execute SQL intended for read/query use and return rows.
  • database_execute_sql_dml: execute SQL intended for data modification.
  • database_execute_sql_ddl: execute SQL intended for schema/structure changes.
  • database_execute_nosql_query: execute NoSQL statements intended for read/query usage.
  • database_execute_nosql_write_delete: execute NoSQL statements intended for write/delete usage.
  • database_list_table_schema: get table and column structure (schema) with relevance-ranked smart sampling — supports catalog/schema namespace filtering, keyword scoring, table prefix filter, and optional index info.

Database coverage: database_list_databases works for major SQL engines (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, SQLite, CockroachDB, H2) and metadata-aware NoSQL connectors (MongoDB, Apache Cassandra, Redis, etc.).

SQL capability: This plugin supports query, DML, and DDL tools. Actual execution is determined by your database account permissions and data source privileges.

Requirement: The JetBrains Database Tools plugin (com.intellij.database) is required.

Network & Privacy:

  • This plugin starts a local HTTP server bound exclusively to 0.0.0.0 (loopback). It is accessible from remote hosts or other machines on the same network.
  • Database query results, schema metadata, and data source names are made available to local MCP clients through this local service. No data is transmitted to any external server or third-party service by this plugin.
  • This plugin does not collect telemetry, usage statistics, or personal data. No data leaves your machine.
  • Database credentials (passwords) configured in the IDE are not exported or accessible through the MCP API — only connection names, URLs, and driver class information are exposed.

AI Tool Usage: This plugin is designed to work with AI assistants and MCP clients (e.g., Claude, GitHub Copilot, Cursor). When an AI client calls this plugin's tools, the AI receives database schema information and query results from your local IDE data sources. You retain full control over which data sources are exposed via the scope setting (GLOBAL / PROJECT / ALL).

Source code: https://github.com/skrstop/ide-database-mcp

中文说明

IDE Database MCP 将 JetBrains IDE 中已配置的数据库连接暴露为本地 MCP（Model Context Protocol）服务，使 AI/MCP 客户端可以直接基于 IDE 上下文发现数据源并执行 SQL。

工具列表（tools/list）

  • database_list_datasources：发现 IDE 管理的数据源，返回包括名称、地址、驱动类和推断的 type。
  • database_list_databases：列出指定数据源下的数据库、catalog 和 schema。
  • database_execute_sql_query：执行用于读/查询用途的 SQL 并返回行。
  • database_execute_sql_dml：执行用于数据修改的 SQL。
  • database_execute_sql_ddl：执行用于模式/结构更改的 SQL。
  • database_execute_nosql_query：执行用于读/查询用途的 NoSQL 语句。
  • database_execute_nosql_write_delete：执行用于写入/删除用途的 NoSQL 语句。
  • database_list_table_schema：获取数据库表与列结构（Schema），支持命名空间过滤（catalog / schema）、关键词相关性评分采样、表名前缀过滤及可选索引信息返回。

网络与隐私声明：

  • 本插件在本地启动一个 HTTP 服务，仅绑定 0.0.0.0（回环地址），可被局域网内其他机器访问。
  • 数据库查询结果、Schema 元数据、数据源名称等信息会通过该本地服务暴露给本地 MCP 客户端。本插件不向任何外部服务器或第三方服务传输数据。
  • 本插件不收集任何遥测数据、使用统计或个人信息。所有数据均不离开本机。
  • IDE 中配置的数据库密码不会通过 MCP API 暴露，MCP 客户端只能获取连接名称、URL 和驱动类信息。

AI 工具使用说明：本插件专为与 AI 助手和 MCP 客户端（如 Claude、GitHub Copilot、Cursor 等）协同工作而设计。当 AI 客户端调用本插件工具时，AI 会从本地 IDE 数据源中获取数据库 Schema 信息和查询结果。你可以通过 scope 设置（GLOBAL / PROJECT / ALL）控制哪些数据源被暴露。

依赖要求：必须安装并可用 JetBrains Database Tools 插件（com.intellij.database）。

代码地址：https://github.com/skrstop/ide-database-mcp

idea-plugin.name: Document Converter
idea-plugin.description:
Document Converter converts documents directly from IntelliJ IDEA into Markdown or JSON, including large batches of files and folders.

Right-click supported files or folders in the Project view or editor and choose Convert Document. Configure online OCR or offline conversion from Settings | Tools | Document Converter.

Key features:

  • Convert complete PDFs or select specific page ranges
  • Export extracted content to Markdown or structured JSON
  • Use cloud-based Mistral OCR 4.1 for high-quality document and PDF extraction
  • Keep using Mistral OCR 3 for compatibility with the mistral-ocr-2512 model
  • Choose between the mistral-ocr-4-1 and mistral-ocr-2512 Mistral models

Mistral OCR 4.1 and OCR 3:

Online conversion supports Mistral OCR 4.1 (recommended) and Mistral OCR 3. Select the model in the plugin settings and provide a Mistral AI API key. Usage is sent to Mistral AI and is subject to your Mistral workspace quota, spending limits, and API pricing.

Requirements:

  • Offline mode requires the MarkItDown CLI installed and available on your PATH

idea-plugin.name: Lnr
idea-plugin.description:
Linear project management and issue tracker for your IDE.

Lnr — Linear Integration for JetBrains IDEs

The most complete Linear app project management integration for JetBrains IDEs. Browse, create, and edit issues, drag-and-drop on a Kanban board, create Git branches, generate descriptions with AI, and track agile sprint cycles — all without leaving your editor. Works with IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, Rider, GoLand, PhpStorm, CLion, RubyMine, DataGrip, and all other JetBrains IDEs.

New in 1.2.0

  • Inbox — A dedicated Inbox tab mirrors Linear's notifications, with an unread badge in the status bar, archive/unarchive, and 60s polling
  • Emoji Reactions — React to comments with a full Unicode picker (search + recently used), and see reactions grouped with tooltips
  • Attachments — View, open, and delete attachments on issues, or upload via file picker or drag-and-drop (25 MB per file)
  • Comment Thread Resolution — Mark a specific reply as the thread's resolution, with a Resolution badge and Reopen option

Issue Management

  • Browse & Search — View all your Linear issues in a filterable, searchable list. Find issues by identifier (e.g. BE-123) or text content
  • Filter by Team, Status & Priority — "All Teams" mode merges issues across teams; narrow down by workflow state, assignee, or priority
  • Create Issues — Create issues with title, description, team, state, priority, assignee, project, cycle, and labels — directly from the IDE
  • Edit Issues Inline — Edit all fields (title, description, status, priority, assignee, project, cycle, labels) in the detail panel without switching to Linear
  • Comments — View and post comments on issues with Cmd+Enter / Ctrl+Enter to send
  • Delete Issues — Remove issues directly from the detail panel

Kanban Board

  • Board View — Columns grouped by workflow state with color-coded status headers
  • List View — Grouped rows with collapsible status sections, Linear-style. Toggle between Board and List views — your preference is remembered
  • Drag-and-Drop — Drag issues between columns or onto any row in a status group to update status via the Linear API
  • Multi-Team Support — Switch between teams or view all teams with merged status columns

AI-Powered Description Generation

  • ✨ Generate Descriptions — Click the Generate button to create structured issue descriptions from a title and optional context (short description)
  • Dual AI Provider — Use JetBrains AI Assistant (zero configuration) or bring your own OpenAI-compatible API key (GPT-4o, Claude, local models via Ollama, etc.)
  • Works Everywhere — Available in both the Create Issue dialog and the Edit Issue panel

Issue Templates

  • Save Templates — Save frequently used issue configurations as reusable templates
  • Quick Apply — Select a template from the dropdown in Create Issue to pre-fill all fields instantly

Task Management (Tasks & Contexts)

  • Native Task Popup — Linear issues appear in Open Task (Alt+Shift+N) and Switch Task (Alt+Shift+T) alongside Jira and YouTrack
  • Context Switching — Opening a task restores its editor tabs, bookmarks, breakpoints, run configurations and branch
  • Close Task — Pick a workflow state from the issue's own team; the transition is written back to Linear
  • Server-Side Search — Typing filters in Linear, and an identifier such as BE-123 resolves that issue directly
  • Shared Branch Naming — New {lnrBranch} placeholder keeps task branches consistent with Lnr's own Create Branch action
  • On IntelliJ IDEA, DataGrip and Rider 2026.2+, install the free Issue Trackers plugin by JetBrains first — it is no longer bundled. Earlier versions and WebStorm include it already.

Git Integration

  • Create Branch — Create and checkout a Git branch named after the selected issue (e.g. feature/BE-123-issue-title)
  • Copy Branch Name — Copy a formatted branch name to clipboard
  • Auto-Detect Issues — Automatically detect Linear issue identifiers from your current branch name
  • Commit Message Prefix — Smart commit message prefixing with the current issue identifier

Cycles & Workflow

  • Cycle Tracking — View active and completed cycles with progress indicators, filterable by team
  • Auto-Refresh — Configurable polling interval keeps issues, boards, and detail panels up to date
  • Status Bar Widget — See Linear connection status at a glance
  • Open in Browser — Jump to any issue in the Linear web app with one click
  • Keyboard Shortcuts — C (Create), Ctrl+Shift+B (Branch), Ctrl+Shift+C (Copy), O (Open), R (Refresh), Esc (Close)

Getting Started

  1. Get your Linear API Key — Go to Linear Settings → API and create a personal API key
  2. Configure the Plugin — Open your IDE Settings → Tools → Lnr, paste your API key, and click Test Connection to verify
  3. Open the Tool Window — Find the Lnr icon on your tool window bar (usually on the right) or go to View → Tool Windows → Lnr
  4. Choose Your View — Toggle between the Issues list, the Kanban Board, and the Cycles tab at the top of the tool window
  5. (Optional) Enable AI — In the same settings page, select your preferred AI Provider (JetBrains AI Assistant or OpenAI) to start generating issue descriptions instantly

Requirements

  • A Linear account with a personal API key
  • Git plugin enabled (bundled with all JetBrains IDEs)
  • Optional: JetBrains AI Assistant plugin for zero-config AI description generation
  • Optional: JetBrains "Issue Trackers" plugin (free) for Task Management integration — bundled up to 2025.3, a separate install on 2026.2+ IDEA/DataGrip/Rider
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Task Management Integration: Linear is now available as a task repository provider, so issues appear in the IDE's native Open Task (Alt+Shift+N) and Switch Task (Alt+Shift+T) popups and take part in context save/restore — editor tabs, bookmarks, breakpoints, run configurations, changelists and branches.
    • Configure under Settings | Tools | Tasks | Servers | + | Linear; credentials come from your existing Lnr settings, so there is no second token to manage
    • Defaults to issues assigned to you, unresolved, most recently updated first, with an optional team filter
    • Search is sent to Linear rather than filtered locally, and typing an identifier such as BE-37 resolves that issue directly
    • Close Task offers the issue's own team workflow states and writes the transition back to Linear
    • New {lnrBranch} and {identifier} placeholders for Task Management's branch and commit message formats, so a branch opened from a task matches Lnr's own Create Branch naming
  • Clearer Linear API errors: messages now prefer Linear's human-readable text over its terse internal one.

Fixed

  • Issue detail panel scrolled sideways instead of reflowing. A long issue title dictated the panel's width, most visibly on issues opened from the Inbox. The title now wraps and the panel adapts to the tool window.
  • Refreshes reported cancellation as failure. Cancelling a refresh — which happens by design on every subsequent refresh and on reset — surfaced as "Failed to refresh all data" and set an error state, and the auto-refresh loop counted each one toward its consecutive-error limit, which could eventually stop polling.

Changed

  • LnrCommitMessageProvider stands down when an active Linear task is configured to supply the commit message, so the identifier is never prefixed twice. Behaviour is unchanged unless you enable "Add commit message" on the repository.

Notes

  • IntelliJ IDEA, DataGrip and Rider 2026.2+ no longer bundle the Task Management plugin. Install the free Issue Trackers plugin from the JetBrains Marketplace to use this feature there. WebStorm still bundles it, as do all supported IDEs up to 2025.3.
  • Configuring a task repository activates the platform's branch-context tracking, which may prompt to restore contexts when you switch branches.
  • Creating a task from the Open Task popup makes an IDE-local task only; it does not create a Linear issue. This matches every other task server — the platform's repository API has no create capability. Use Lnr's own Create Issue dialog for that.

GitHub Copilot Premium Quota Monitor is a plugin for the IntelliJ platform that helps you monitor the remaining quota of the GitHub Copilot premium model directly from the IDE status bar.

  • Double-click on the widget for an immediate quota refresh without opening any menu.
  • Configurable alert thresholds and colors: set your own critical (default 10%) and warning (default 30%) quota percentage thresholds, each with a personalized color. Per-setting "Reset to default" buttons are provided for convenience.
  • Full compatibility with all JetBrains IDEs (IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, etc.).
  • GitHub Enterprise support: authenticate against GitHub Enterprise Cloud (data residency) or a self-hosted GitHub Enterprise Server instance by configuring a custom server URL and OAuth Client ID.
  • Localization support: Albanian, Chinese, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Turkish.
  • Manual and automatic background updates of quota data.
  • Quick actions via widget popup (left single-click): Refresh, Sign In, Sign Out.
  • Real-time status bar widget showing the remaining premium quota as a percentage, with color-coded urgency levels.
  • Secure authentication via OAuth Device Flow, with tokens stored in PasswordSafe.
  • Tooltip with detailed quota information, including remaining requests and renewal date.
  • Visual feedback for loading, unlimited plans, unauthenticated state, and errors.

A GitHub account with an active Copilot subscription is required. The plugin is independent from the official GitHub Copilot plugin and works with all compatible JetBrains IDEs.

Simple to use, secure, and designed to keep you informed about your Copilot premium quota usage at a glance. Use left-click on the widget to open the quick actions menu.

Credits: Special thanks to the contributors who helped improve this plugin:

  • Fabio Pelliccia
  • Massimo Ambrosino
  • Vincenzo Pimpinella
