Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License"); you may not use this file except in compliance with the License. You may obtain a copy of the License at

   http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0

Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS, WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied. See the License for the specific language governing permissions and limitations under the License.

Use of Sinch Services

Use of Sinch Services

This plugin provides developers with a way to interact with Sinch APIs and services from supported developer tools or environments. Use of Sinch services requires a valid Sinch account and is subject to the applicable Sinch Terms of Service available at: https://sinch.com/legal/terms-and-conditions/other-sinch-terms-conditions/terms-of-service/

This plugin may be used in conjunction with third-party developer tools, IDEs, platforms, or environments that are not operated or controlled by Sinch. Such third-party tools or platforms are subject to their own terms and policies.

The plugin is provided on an "as-is" basis, and Sinch is not responsible for the operation, availability, performance, or security of any third-party tools or platforms.

Further Reading

Developer Documentation: https://developers.sinch.com/docs/conversation/

Feedback, Issues and Support

We love hearing feedback, and we are here to help if you run into any issues.

  • For any Sinch Coding Assistant related issues, or support you require, head over to the Sinch Help Centre
  • For any Sinch Coding Assistant related issues, please contact our support team through the following link https://support.sinch.com/
  • For Mailgun (Email Validation) related issues, visit the Mailgun Help Centre or contact Mailgun Support

We will continue to enhance this product, so keep a look out for additional channel support (MMS, WhatsApp and more) in addition to new features in future.

From all of us at Sinch, happy coding!

idea-plugin.name: Pixel Office - AI Agent Visualizer
idea-plugin.description:
Pixel Agents for IntelliJ

Turn your Claude Code terminal sessions into animated pixel art characters in a virtual office. Each terminal you open spawns a character that walks around, sits at desks, and visually reflects what the agent is doing in real time.

Features

  • One agent, one character — every Claude Code terminal gets its own animated character
  • Live activity tracking — characters animate based on what the agent is doing (writing, reading, running commands)
  • Sub-agent visualization — Task/Agent sub-agents spawn as separate characters, including async background agents
  • Office layout editor — design your office with floors, walls, and 80+ furniture items
  • Multiple themes — default office, alien, cat, and zoo themes with unique characters and furniture
  • Speech bubbles — visual indicators when an agent is waiting or needs permission
  • Sound notifications — optional chime when an agent finishes its turn
  • Persistent layouts — office design saved across IDE restarts
  • Animated furniture — wall clocks tick, desk fans spin, water coolers bubble

How It Works

Pixel Agents watches Claude Code's JSONL transcript files to track what each agent is doing. No modifications to Claude Code are needed — it's purely observational. The webview runs a lightweight game loop with canvas rendering, BFS pathfinding, and a character state machine.

Getting Started

  1. Install Claude Code CLI
  2. Open the Pixel Agents tool window (bottom panel)
  3. Click + Agent to spawn a Claude Code terminal
  4. Watch the character react as Claude works on your code

Based on Pixel Agents for VS Code by Pablo De Lucca. Ported to the IntelliJ Platform with additional features.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.6

Bottom HUD token readout

  • The rolling 5-hour figure is now a weighted sum (cache reads 0.10x, cache writes 1.25x, matching how they are billed). Summed raw it was 98.8% cache reads, so it tracked how much history got re-read rather than how much quota was spent
  • The context bar was scaled against the session's cumulative throughput instead of how full the context window actually is, so any long-running session pegged it at 100%. It now reads the same signal as the per-character HP bar
  • claude-opus-5 was treated as a 200K-context model — the current Claude Code default now correctly scales to 1M, as do Sonnet 5 and Fable/Mythos 5.x
  • The rolling 5-hour token total counted every turn twice: Claude Code writes one API response as several transcript lines that each repeat the same usage block. Responses are now counted once
  • Legacy model ids such as claude-3-opus-20240229 rendered their date suffix as the version (OPUS 20240229)
  • Cost table split for Sonnet 5 ($2/$10), which is cheaper than Sonnet 4.6

Real 5-hour and 7-day usage

  • The HUD shows your real plan usage (5h 14% · 7d 23% (pace 35%)) when Claude Code's status line or Claude Desktop reports it, and falls back to the weighted token sum otherwise. See the README for the status line snippet
  • Pace is where 7-day usage would be now if the week's limit were spread evenly over its weekday hours. The chip turns amber when you are ahead of it
  • Optional Claude Code hook (hooks/usage-pace.py) that tells Claude when 7-day usage is ahead of the pace, and adds nothing otherwise

When the IDE's built-in browser stops

  • A crashed page renderer is reloaded at once. A silent page is reloaded, then the browser is recreated
  • When IntelliJ's JCEF process itself is gone (it is not restarted by the IDE), the panel says so and offers Restart IDE / Try again instead of staying blank. A frozen IDE is never mistaken for a dead browser

Other

  • The bottom HUD drops detail step by step instead of overlapping the toolbar in narrow windows
  • Ctrl/Cmd + mouse wheel zooms the office from anywhere in the panel without zooming the whole page
  • Terminal tabs are tracked by tab, not title: Claude Code's spinning tab title no longer reads as a closed terminal (it filled a fifth of the IDE log) or removes a running agent

1.0.5

Compatibility

  • Removed the until-build upper bound — the plugin now stays available on new IDE releases (2026.2 / build 262 and later) instead of being delisted

New Claude models

  • Model chips for the Claude 5 family: FABLE 5, MYTH 5, SON 5, OPUS 4.8 (previously fell back to a grey unknown chip)
  • Context-window scale corrected to 1M for Fable 5 / Mythos 5 / Sonnet 5 / Sonnet 4.6, so the HP gauge and HUD percentage are accurate
  • Updated cost table (Opus $5/$25, Haiku 4.5 $1/$5, Fable & Mythos $10/$50)

Behavior fixes

  • Background Bash tasks keep their character active after the turn ends, instead of going idle while the command still runs
  • Sub-agent watchers now time out at 30s (they were reusing the 60s main-agent threshold)
  • 5-hour token usage chip in the HUD now actually populates on IntelliJ (the backend never sent the data before)

Unified view

  • New Unified View (Show Other Sources) setting, off by default. When enabled, agents from other IDE windows and CLI sessions appear at 85% transparency alongside your own

UI polish

  • Replaced glyphs the pixel font could not render (which fell back to OS emoji), unified the close button across panels, and pixelated the native sliders/checkboxes in the layout editor

1.0.4

  • Git worktree support — Claude sessions running in a worktree of the open repository now show up in the same office. Worktrees created while the IDE is running are picked up within 5s, no restart needed
  • Agents adopted from a worktree carry a ↳branch suffix on their label, persisted across IDE restarts

1.0.3

UX

  • Status bubble stays above every working agent (toned-down ambient style; full styling on hover/select)
  • Context window HP gauge next to each agent's label — muted forest-green / gold / brick-red bar shows 200K context usage; % number appears on hover/select
  • Model indicator chip in the activity bubble (OPUS / SON / HAI) — pixel-art styling with muted palette + 1px outline + hard offset shadow. Reads message.model from each assistant record
  • Session totals on hover/select — cumulative tokens + estimated USD cost line below the bubble (e.g. 12.4K tok • $0.18 est). Cost is approximate, based on the last observed model's published rates with cache_create at 1.25x input and cache_read at 0.10x
  • Keyboard zoom shortcuts — + / - step zoom; Ctrl/Cmd+0 resets to auto-fit default. Ignored while typing in inputs
  • Unified all agent stale-removal thresholds to 60 seconds (previously 30 / 60 / 120)

Stability — agent lifecycle

  • Fixed main agent not disappearing after 60s when Claude was Ctrl+C'd mid-permission-prompt (permissionSent stuck flag bypassed dead-session check)
  • Fixed race where clicking + Agent could spawn duplicate characters (knownJsonlFiles registered before claude launch)
  • Fixed sub-agent characters disappearing on webview reload while Task was still running (taskStatus preserved on AsyncSubagent)
  • Fixed /clear leaving pendingSubagentIds / hadToolsInTurn stuck, causing mis-bound sub-agents and missing waiting indicators
  • Fixed stale agentSeats entries leaking across IDE restarts and causing seat/palette drift on new agents
  • Reconciliation: existingAgents message now removes ghost characters/state the webview has but the extension does not
  • TOCTOU guard: dead-session check re-verifies jsonlFile path before removing an agent that may have just been reassigned via /clear
  • Fixed startJsonlPoll using a captured stale agent reference; now re-fetches live state every tick

Stability — webview

  • Guarded addSubagent capacity sentinel (returns 0) so phantom sub-agent records are not pushed when the visible-character cap is reached
  • Sub-agent characters now stop their typing/reading animation when their last tool finishes
  • subagentClear now also removes the corresponding React record so labels don't outlive the OfficeState character

Resource leaks

  • Made onWebviewReady infrastructure init idempotent — JCEF panel toggles no longer accumulate duplicate TerminalDetector / sessionAliveCheck / periodicDiscovery timers
  • stopWatching now also clears subagentStartTimes / subagentLastActivity bookkeeping (prevents long-session memory growth)

API & build

  • Replaced scheduled-for-removal TerminalToolWindowManager.createLocalShellWidget with createShellWidget for forward compatibility with future IntelliJ releases
  • Cleared Kotlin compiler warnings (shadowed name, unused parameter)
  • Migrated extension println calls (35 sites) and webview console.log calls (14 sites) to proper Logger.debug / debug() gates — silent in production
  • Marked shared assetsDir as @Volatile to harden visibility between setTheme and asset loading threads
  • Added unit-test infrastructure: JUnit 5 (Kotlin) + vitest (webview), 60 tests covering pure helpers; CI workflow runs both on push/PR with plugin verifier on main

1.0.0

  • Initial release — IntelliJ Platform port of Pixel Agents
  • JCEF-based webview with full canvas rendering
  • Claude Code JSONL transcript watching with hybrid polling
  • Async sub-agent file tracking (separate JSONL files)
  • Multiple themes: default, alien, cat, zoo
  • Layout editor with undo/redo, floor/wall painting, furniture placement
  • Auto-animated furniture (clocks, fans, water coolers)
  • Agent persistence across IDE restarts
  • External session adoption (terminals started without --session-id)
  • Dead session detection and cleanup

idea-plugin.name: Llamatik Code
idea-plugin.description:
Llamatik Code is a local-first AI coding assistant for IntelliJ-based IDEs, designed to help you understand, modify, and generate code directly inside your project.

Built for developers who value privacy, performance, and control, Llamatik Code runs AI models locally on your machine and provides an agent-based workflow similar to tools like Claude Code or Cursor — without relying on the cloud.


🚀 Key Features

  • Project-aware chat – Ask questions about your codebase with persistent, multi-session support
  • Local AI models – Run models fully offline; your code never leaves your machine
  • AI agent for code editing – Generate and modify code using natural language with safe diff previews
  • Context-aware assistance – Understands the current file, selection, git state, and project structure
  • Multi-file workflows – Perform coordinated changes across multiple files (Pro)
  • MCP server support – Connect any MCP-compatible tool server and let the agent call its tools directly
  • Multi-task agent – Run multiple agent tasks in parallel with a live task queue panel (Pro)
  • Parallel chat sessions – Switch between multiple simultaneous conversations in Ask mode
  • Aggressive mode – Instruct the agent to act more decisively and apply fixes without hesitation (Pro)
  • External Knowledge – Let the agent search the web, read official docs, and research errors in real time, with citations
  • Code Health Monitor – Proactive background analysis that surfaces regression risks, complexity issues, and refactor opportunities before they become problems

🔌 IDE-native MCP host
Configure local MCP servers under Settings → Llamatik Code → MCP Servers. The agent discovers their tools, resources, and prompts automatically and calls them through the same approval pipeline as built-in tools. Free users get one active server with manual approval on every call; Pro users get unlimited servers with optional per-tool and per-server auto-approval rules.


🌐 Context-Aware External Knowledge
The agent can search the web via DuckDuckGo, read documentation pages, route queries to the right source (kotlinlang.org, developer.android.com, GitHub Issues, and more), analyse compiler errors, and build fix plans — all without leaving the IDE. Every answer backed by external content includes structured citations. Enable under Settings → Llamatik Code → External Knowledge. Free: 5 searches/day, 1 docs source. Pro: 50 searches/day, 10 docs sources.


🩺 Code Health Monitor
An opt-in background analysis layer that continuously monitors your codebase for structural problems and regression risks. Detects long files, TODO/FIXME accumulation, empty catch blocks, deprecated APIs, removed public declarations, deleted tests, and dependency changes — without a model call for the fast checks. Includes a before-commit assistant, watched areas, refactor opportunity detection, and 14 dedicated agent tools. Enable under Settings → Llamatik Code → Code Health Monitor. Free: LIGHT mode with manual trigger. Pro: BALANCED and AGGRESSIVE modes with on-save, idle, and before-commit scheduling.


🔒 Privacy-first
Your code is processed locally by default. No data is sent to external servers unless you explicitly configure an MCP server or enable External Knowledge searches. Secrets in tool arguments and environment variables are redacted from all logs and trace output.


⚡ Who is it for?

  • Developers who want a local alternative to cloud AI tools
  • Teams working with private or sensitive codebases
  • Power users looking for extensible, agent-based workflows inside IntelliJ
  • Anyone who wants to connect their own tools to the agent via MCP
  • Engineers who want proactive code quality monitoring without a separate CI step

💡 Free & Pro

  • Free – Chat, single-session agent, 1 active MCP server with manual approval, External Knowledge (5 searches/day), Code Health Monitor (LIGHT / manual)
  • Pro – Multi-task agent, unlimited MCP servers, auto-approval rules, aggressive mode, multi-file apply, auto-build, auto-fix, External Knowledge (50 searches/day, 10 docs sources), Code Health Monitor (BALANCED + AGGRESSIVE modes, background scheduling)

Learn more: https://www.llamatik.com

End-User License Agreement | Privacy Policy
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.9.0 — Statistics, Resource Modes, Qwen 3.6 & Agent Improvements

Usage Statistics

  • Statistics settings page — new Settings → Llamatik Code → Statistics page showing total generations, average and longest task times, total generation time, tokens consumed, energy usage, CO₂ avoided vs cloud API, money saved vs cloud API, and most-used model.
  • Persistent stats — generation counts, durations, and token totals are stored in llamatik_generation_stats.xml in the IDE config directory and survive IDE restarts.
  • Delete all statistics data — one-click button to clear all recorded statistics.

Resource Modes

  • Resource Mode selector — new Settings → Llamatik Code → Inference → Resource Mode setting with three options: Balanced (default, caps threads at half the physical cores so the IDE stays responsive), Low (quarter cores, minimum 1 — best for background use), and Full (uses the exact thread count from the Threads setting for maximum throughput).
  • Thread count defaults to half of physical cores — on fresh installs, the Threads setting now defaults to half the available processors instead of a hard-coded 4, giving a better out-of-the-box experience on both low-end and high-end machines.

Qwen 3.6-27B Added as Default Model

  • Qwen3.6-27B-Q4_K_M — added to the built-in model catalog as the new default recommended model (Tier 3, 17.1 GB, 20 GB RAM minimum). Excellent balance of reasoning depth and coding quality for demanding local tasks including complex reasoning, large refactors, and agentic workflows.
  • Qwen3-14B is no longer the default; it remains in the catalog as a RECOMMENDED Tier 2 option.

Agent Improvements

  • Session timeout — agent runs are now capped at 20 minutes. If a generation hangs or runs unexpectedly long, the session is cancelled automatically with a clear message.
  • Accumulated read files — files read by the model across rounds are re-injected into every subsequent round so the model always has the source it already read when it comes time to write.
  • Write-pass prefill — the assistant turn is pre-filled with the opening of a write_file call on the final round, preventing the model from emitting prose instead of code.
  • Round token budgets — exploration rounds use a tighter token cap; the full budget is reserved for the write pass so large file content fits in the output.
  • Round 2 content budget — source re-injection and tool results are budgeted jointly against a shared limit so their combined size never exceeds the backend context cap.
  • Retry button — a Retry button is now shown after a completed agent task, re-submitting the same prompt for another attempt.
  • Build in background option — a new Run Options menu in the Agent panel lets you choose between IDE incremental build (default, fast) and background Gradle build for projects that require it. The choice is persisted per project.
  • Cancel build button — a Cancel Build button is shown during build verification so long Gradle builds can be aborted without leaving the IDE.

Tool Call Parser — JSON & Fuzzy Arg Parsing

  • JSON arg fallback — the tool call parser now accepts JSON objects ({"query": "…"}) as argument bodies in addition to the canonical XML <arg> format. Handles the common case where Qwen3 and other models emit JSON-style tool calls.
  • Key-value line fallback — if neither XML nor JSON is recognised, the parser tries key: value line format.
  • Single positional value fallback — for tools that take a single primary argument, a bare string value is accepted and mapped to the correct argument name automatically.

replace_in_file — Fuzzy Matching

  • Indent-normalised match — when the exact oldText is not found, the tool now retries after normalising indentation on both sides. Local models frequently hallucinate slightly wrong indentation, causing exact matches to fail; this catches most of those cases.
  • Trimmed-lines match — a third fallback compares logical lines ignoring all leading/trailing whitespace, catching cases where the model omits or changes blank lines between code blocks.
  • Clearer error messages — when all three strategies fail, the error now explains exactly why and tells the model to use read_file first, then copy the exact text.

Build Verification

  • IDE incremental build — build verification now supports triggering a fast IDE incremental Make via CompilerManager in addition to the existing Gradle subprocess mode. IDE build is the new default.
  • Infrastructure error filtering — [Internal Error] messages (JVM/plugin crashes such as Compose/Kotlin version mismatches) are filtered from the error list before it reaches the autofix model, preventing the model from wasting rounds trying to fix unfixable infrastructure failures.

1.8.0 — Autonomous Local Development, Agent Reliability & Library Upgrade

Autonomous Local Development

  • Offline Enterprise Pair Programmer — new flagship mode that wraps every agent task in a structured, auditable workflow: gather context → classify risks → plan → patch → verify → audit report. Your source code never leaves the device.
  • Mission classification — 11 mission types auto-detected from plain-language requests (CODE_REVIEW, REFACTOR, BUG_FIX, FEATURE_IMPLEMENTATION, TEST_GENERATION, DOCUMENTATION, BUILD_FAILURE_REPAIR, ARCHITECTURE_EXPLANATION, DEPENDENCY_UPDATE, SECURITY_AUDIT, PERFORMANCE_ANALYSIS).
  • Safety levels — APPROVAL_REQUIRED (default), PLAN_ONLY, AUTO_APPLY, FULL_AUTO. Configurable per project.
  • Risk detection — LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH / CRITICAL risks surfaced in the mission plan before any file is written. CRITICAL risks require explicit user acknowledgement.
  • Plan-before-write enforcement — agent must produce a mission plan before calling any write tool (default: on).
  • Diff-before-write enforcement — unified diff shown before every patch is applied (default: on, even in AUTO_APPLY mode).
  • Audit trail — per-mission metadata log (no raw source code stored), accessible at any time via enterprise_mission_audit.
  • Rollback instructions — every mission plan includes plain-language rollback steps in the final audit report.

Enterprise Pair Programmer Tools (4 new)

  • enterprise_mission_create — classify request, detect risks, build the mission plan
  • enterprise_mission_context — gather git state, code health, diagnostics, and project snapshot
  • enterprise_mission_audit — return audit trail metadata (never raw source code)
  • enterprise_mission_report — produce final report and close the mission

Context Menu Actions (7 new)

All under Llamatik Code → Autonomous Local Development in editor and project-view right-click menus:

  • Enterprise Pair Programmer
  • Review Current Changes
  • Fix Build Failure
  • Generate Tests
  • Explain Architecture
  • Safe Refactor
  • Implement Feature

Inline Completions (opt-in MVP)

  • Local fill-in-the-middle completions using the same on-device model as the agent.
  • Debounced requests (600 ms default) — stale requests cancelled automatically.
  • Current-file only; configurable context window (default 1200 chars) and max tokens (default 64).
  • Disabled by default — enable at Settings → Llamatik Code → Autonomous Local Development → Enable inline completions.

Rating & Feedback

  • After a configurable number of successful tasks that produced file changes, the plugin shows a non-modal prompt to rate the experience and optionally leave feedback on the JetBrains Marketplace.
  • Prompt respects a cooldown so it never appears more than once per session window.
  • Can be dismissed permanently via a "Don't ask again" option.

File Selection Picker

  • The model file picker (load GGUF from disk) now uses IntelliJ's native FileChooser API instead of the Swing JFileChooser. This gives IDE-native look and feel, correct macOS permissions, and reliable filtering to .gguf files on all platforms.

Library

  • Llamatik library 1.8.0 — updated to llama.cpp b9574 with improved KV cache management and full support for Qwen3.6 Mamba-hybrid architecture models.

Agent Loop Reliability

  • Attached file context respected — when a file is attached via @filename or is the currently open file, the system prompt now explicitly tells the model that the content is already provided. The model no longer wastes rounds calling read_file or search_code on content it already has.
  • Cross-round read-only dedup — the agent tracks which read_file, search_code, and list_files calls have been executed across all rounds. Duplicate calls return a synthetic "already called" result instantly instead of consuming a round slot. Attached file paths are pre-seeded into the dedup set so the model can never re-fetch them.
  • Write pass forced when all calls are duplicates — if every tool call in a round is a dedup synthetic result, the agent skips directly to a final write pass (with noThink = true) instead of burning another round on the same blocked calls.
  • Write pass forced when model writes prose mid-loop — if the model produces plain text instead of a tool call after having read project files, the agent escalates to a final write pass rather than surfacing the prose as the answer.
  • No thinking on final round — the final round suppresses chain-of-thought so the model's entire token budget goes to the write_file output rather than reasoning.

Tag Leak Fixes

  • Orphan </think> no longer visible in responses — when echo-stripping removed a <think> opener mid-block, the matching </think> could survive and appear in the displayed text. Both stripThinking and cleanForDisplay now explicitly strip bare closing tags.
  • Orphan </arg></tool_call> XML no longer visible in responses — the <tool_call …> opener pattern was already stripped, but closing tags left behind from completed tool calls were not. Added explicit stripping of </arg>, </tool_call>, and </edit_proposal> orphan tags.

1.7.0 — UI Polish, Syntax Highlighting & Free Tier Improvements

Free Tier Improvements

  • Multi-file edits unlocked on Free — the agent can now apply changes across multiple files without requiring a Pro subscription. All edit proposals are fully actionable on the Free plan.
  • Auto-build unlocked on Free — the agent can now automatically trigger a build after applying changes on the Free plan. Auto-approve, auto-fix, and aggressive mode remain Pro-only.
  • "Fix it automatically" unlocked on Free — the Fix It button now always triggers the full fix flow instead of silently downgrading to "Create plan" on the Free tier.
  • Max tokens uncapped on Free — the 4,096 token response cap has been removed. Free and Pro users both have access to the full 65,536 token limit.
  • Context size setting unlocked on Free — free users can now configure context size in Inference Settings. The setting is no longer locked behind Pro.
  • Skills: 3 active on Free — free users can now activate up to 3 skills simultaneously, up from 1.
  • External search: 15 searches/day on Free — daily search limit raised from 5 to 15. Pages per task raised from 3 to 5. Docs sources raised from 1 to 3. Results per query raised from 5 to 8.
  • Image attachments on Free — free users can now attach up to 5 images per session. Previously image attachment was fully blocked on the Free plan.

Chat UI Improvements

  • Syntax highlighting in code blocks — code blocks in assistant responses now render with full IDE-quality syntax highlighting using IntelliJ's own editor viewer and the active colour scheme. Kotlin, Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, and all other common languages are supported.
  • Markdown renders on conversation load — persisted assistant messages now correctly render markdown formatting (bold, italic, lists, code blocks) when a conversation is reopened. Previously raw markdown was shown on load.
  • User message bubble no longer expands to fill the screen — the user prompt bubble now sizes to fit its text content instead of expanding to fill all available vertical space until a response arrives.
  • Code block height fixed — code blocks in responses no longer expand to fill the remaining panel height; they now size to fit their content.

About Dialog

  • Discord and X links added — the About dialog now includes a "Join Discord" button and a "Follow on X" button, both opening in the system browser.

Inference Settings

  • GPU layers default to all layers on macOS — on Apple Silicon, GPU offload now defaults to enabled (all layers) on fresh installs. llama.cpp uses Metal on macOS, making full GPU offload safe and significantly faster. Other platforms still default to CPU-only.

1.6.4 — Trial, Agent & Tooling Improvements

Trial & Licensing

  • Trial management delegated to the IDE — the plugin no longer maintains its own 30-day counter. Trial period and expiry are now read directly from the JetBrains IDE licensing API (LicensingFacade), making the IDE the single source of truth.
  • Agent is always available on the free tier — the "Trial expired — Agent requires a subscription" overlay has been removed. Agent features are free; Pro unlocks advanced capabilities within the agent (multi-file edits, higher context, parallel tasks).
  • Cleaner trial status labels — the status badge now shows Licensed, Trial active, or Free instead of "Expired". The trial warning banner wording has been updated to "Upgrade to Pro to keep Agent features." to make the call to action clear.

Bug Fixes

  • Large files were silently truncated when read by the agent — when the agent used read_file, the result was cut off mid-file (e.g. stopping at line 299 of a 571-line file) before being forwarded to the model. Two separate causes were found and fixed:
  • Batch Size was incorrectly used to cap the file budget — Batch Size is a KV-cache inference parameter, not the model context window. Using min(contextSize, batchSize) meant that the default Batch Size of 2 048 could collapse the entire file budget to zero. The budget is now derived from Context Size only, which is the true model context window. With the default Context Size of 16 384, the agent can now read files up to ~1 150 lines (35 chars/line) without truncation.
  • A hardcoded 4 000-character cap on tool results was overriding the per-file limit — even when the per-result budget was large enough, a second hard cap on the total tool-results block cut off the content. Both caps now scale dynamically with Context Size.
  • Floor guarantee added — even with a very small Context Size, read_file results are guaranteed at least 8 000 characters (~570 lines), preventing total content loss regardless of settings.
  • search_filenames src/ returned "Missing query" — the tool call parser did not recognise the space-separated format (search_filenames src/) that some models emit. A new space-separated fallback parser handles this format for all single-argument tools.

Diagnostics

  • Richer native library error messages — when the native Llamatik library fails to load, the error now walks the full exception cause chain to surface the root UnsatisfiedLinkError or LinkageError with a direct link to the issue tracker. Previously only the top-level exception message was shown.

1.6.3 — Prompt Budget Fix

Bug Fixes

  • "Prompt too long" error with Batch Size 8192 — reviewing or attaching large files (e.g. via @{path})

1.6.2 — Conversation Context & Inference Settings

Agent Conversation History

  • Threaded agent conversations — follow-up prompts in the Agent tab now continue in the same conversation instead of starting a new task. Each completed exchange is frozen into the scroll area above the live response, giving a chat-like history view.
  • New task only on explicit request — a new task is created only when clicking the + button in the task queue. Submitting a follow-up prompt reuses the current task.
  • File context persists across turns — if you attach a file in your first prompt, follow-up prompts ("add more tests", "fix that error") automatically inherit the same file context without you needing to re-attach it.
  • Conversation history sent to model — prior exchanges are included in subsequent agent requests so the model knows which file was being worked on and what was already done.
  • Meaningful assistant summaries — when the agent writes files, the completed turn records which files were changed, so history is informative for future turns.

File Size & Context Budget

  • File content limits scale with model settings — the amount of a file sent to the model is now derived from your configured Batch Size, so larger batch sizes unlock larger file reads automatically. Previously files were hard-capped at ~2 000 characters (~50 lines) regardless of settings.
  • read_file tool results also scale — the agent's read_file tool result budget follows the same dynamic limit, so the model sees the full file content when reading files via tools.

Inference Settings

  • Batch Size now available on Free tier — the Batch Size setting is no longer restricted to Pro. Free users can now increase it to fix "Prompt too long" errors when working with larger files.
  • Flash Attention now available on Free tier — Flash Attention is no longer restricted to Pro. Free users with compatible hardware can enable it to reduce VRAM usage.
  • Context Size remains the only Pro-exclusive inference setting.

1.6.1 — File Access Fixes & Copy/Paste Improvements

Bug Fixes

  • Files inside build/ directories now readable — explicitly referencing a file (e.g. via @path) inside build/, generated/, or other ignored directories no longer returns "Access denied". The ignore list now applies only to file listing, not to explicit reads.
  • Absolute path references resolved correctly — using @ to attach a file with an absolute path caused a silent "File not found" error. Absolute paths are now handled directly via the local filesystem.
  • Text selection no longer lost on focus change — selecting text in a chat or agent message bubble and then clicking elsewhere no longer clears the selection highlight, making copy/paste reliable.

Improvements

  • Right-click context menu on message bubbles — right-clicking any message in the Chat panel shows a popup with Copy (selection), Copy All, and Select All. Works on both user and assistant messages.
  • Right-click context menu in Agent panel — same context menu is available on the response text, reasoning block, agent trace, and build error areas.

1.6.0 — Custom Skills & PyCharm Compatibility

This release adds user-defined custom skills and fixes a hard dependency on the Kotlin plugin that prevented the plugin from loading in PyCharm and other non-IntelliJ JetBrains IDEs.

Custom Skills

  • Add your own skills — a new + Add Skill button in the Skill Library lets you create custom skills in two ways: paste markdown directly, or download a .md file from a URL.
  • Custom skills are saved to ~/.llamatik/skills/ and persist across IDE restarts.
  • The first H1 heading in the markdown becomes the skill name; the first paragraph becomes the description; the full file content is injected into the agent system prompt when the skill is active.
  • Custom skills appear in the Skill Library with a Custom badge and a Delete button that removes both the entry and the file from disk after confirmation.
  • Custom skills support search, activate/deactivate, and the same Free/Pro activation limits as built-in skills.
  • Stale skill paths (files deleted outside the IDE) are pruned automatically on next load.

IDE Compatibility Fix

  • Fixed a bug that caused the plugin to fail to load in PyCharm, WebStorm, and other JetBrains IDEs that do not bundle the Kotlin plugin. The Kotlin dependency is now correctly declared as optional with a separate config file (llamatik-kotlin.xml), so Kotlin-specific extensions are only registered when the Kotlin plugin is available.

1.5.0 — Code Health Monitor & External Knowledge

This release ships two major feature areas: a proactive Code Health Monitor that analyses your codebase in the background and surfaces actionable insights, and Context-Aware External Knowledge that gives the agent the ability to research the web, official docs, and GitHub issues in real time.

Code Health Monitor (opt-in)

  • Background static analysis detects long files, TODO/FIXME accumulation, empty catch blocks, and deprecated API usage — no model calls required.
  • Regression risk detection — analyses git diffs for removed public declarations, deleted tests, dependency changes in Gradle files, removed error handling, and AndroidManifest modifications.
  • Before-commit review — summarises all staged changes and flags potential regressions before you commit.
  • Watched areas — pin files, directories, packages, or modules; the monitor prioritises insights for areas you care about most.
  • Refactor opportunity detection — highlights long functions and repeated catch patterns across the project.
  • Session context — tracks recent files, branch, and build failures to provide richer, context-aware suggestions.
  • 14 new agent tools: code_health_status, code_health_refresh, code_health_list_insights, code_health_explain_insight, code_health_create_fix_plan, code_health_ignore_insight, watch_area_add/remove/list, session_context_get/clear, before_commit_review, regression_risk_analyze, refactor_analyze_file.
  • Settings → Llamatik Code → Code Health Monitor — configure analysis mode, run triggers, budget limits, and notification behaviour.
  • Free: LIGHT mode, manual trigger only, up to 5 files per scan, 3 model calls/hour. Pro: BALANCED (30 files, 30 s) and AGGRESSIVE (150 files, 120 s) modes with background scheduling and on-save/idle/before-commit triggers.

Context-Aware External Knowledge (opt-in)

  • The agent can now search the web via DuckDuckGo and read pages from official documentation, GitHub issues, and other sources — entirely within the IDE.
  • Research orchestration — detects research intent (library docs, bug/error, API behaviour, migration, latest version) and plans multi-query searches automatically.
  • Smart source routing — directs queries to the most relevant source (kotlinlang.org, developer.android.com, developer.apple.com, github.com, etc.) based on query context.
  • Error research — analyses compiler errors, detects the build tool and framework, and produces a structured fix plan with actionable steps.
  • Private docs indexing — add up to 10 (Pro) or 1 (Free) custom documentation sources; the indexer keeps them fresh and searchable.
  • Citations — every answer backed by external content includes structured citations with source type, confidence, and URL.
  • 16 new agent tools: external_search, external_search_official_docs, external_search_github_issues, external_read_page/pages, research_plan/execute/summarize/route_sources/fix_plan, docs_sources_list/add/index_refresh/search, error_research_analyze/fix.
  • New editor action: Search Docs & Web in the right-click context menu.
  • Free: 5 searches/day, 3 pages/task, 1 docs source. Pro: 50 searches/day, 10 pages/task, 10 docs sources.

1.4.0 — MCP Server Support

Llamatik Code is now an IDE-native MCP host. Configure local MCP servers, discover their tools, resources, and prompts, and let the agent call them through the existing tool pipeline — all without leaving IntelliJ.

MCP server configuration

  • Settings → Llamatik Code → MCP Servers — new dedicated settings page to add, edit, and remove MCP servers.
  • Per-server configuration: command, arguments (one per line), environment variables, working directory, enabled toggle, auto-start toggle, and trust level.
  • Test connection — starts the server, initialises the protocol, lists its tools/resources/prompts, and reports success or failure with a tool count summary.
  • Refresh tools — re-discovers tools from a running server and updates the agent tool list immediately.
  • View logs — shows the in-memory stderr log ring buffer for each server.

MCP agent tools

  • Six new built-in agent tools: mcp_list_servers, mcp_list_tools, mcp_call_tool, mcp_list_resources, mcp_read_resource, mcp_list_prompts.
  • Discovered MCP tools are also bridged into the agent as first-class tools under mcp_<serverName>_<toolName> names, visible in the agent trace like any built-in tool.
  • MCP tool calls appear in the "What I tried" trace panel with server name, tool name, duration, and outcome.

Approval flow

  • Every MCP tool call shows an approval dialog with server name, tool name, arguments, and a risk level (LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH based on the tool name and description).
  • HIGH-risk tools (write, delete, execute, deploy, send, and similar) are never auto-approved unless the user explicitly opts in.
  • Free: Allow once or Deny on every call — no persistent rules.
  • Pro: additional Allow always for this tool and Allow always for this server options store auto-approval rules that skip future dialogs.

Free vs Pro

  • Free — one active MCP server; every tool call requires manual approval.
  • Pro — unlimited active servers; optional per-server and per-tool auto-approval; MCP tools usable in autonomous multi-step agent runs.

Security & privacy

  • MCP servers run as local child processes. The UI clearly notes they may access external services.
  • Secrets (tokens, passwords, API keys, Authorization headers) are redacted from all logs and trace output before display or storage.
  • Broken or crashed MCP servers are isolated — the plugin marks them FAILED and continues normally without affecting any other feature.

1.3.0 — Agent Tools, Git Awareness & Advanced Intelligence

Expanded the agent tool set significantly and added deep project intelligence features including git context, PSI code insight, codebase rules, model benchmarking, and KMP native diagnostics.

New agent tools

  • Git tools: git_diff, git_status, git_log, git_blame, git_changed_files — full read-only git context for the agent.
  • Project index tools: index_search_files, index_search_symbols, index_list_recent — fast symbol and file search powered by the persistent project index.
  • PSI tools: psi_find_usages, psi_get_type, psi_get_declarations — semantic code insight via IntelliJ's PSI layer.
  • Rules tools: rules_get, rules_set, rules_clear — read and write persistent codebase rules that the agent follows in every session.
  • Run config tools: run_config_list, run_config_execute — list and trigger IDE run configurations from inside the agent.
  • KMP native tools: kmp_diagnose, kmp_fix_plan — detect and plan fixes for Kotlin Multiplatform native compilation issues.

Aggressive mode (Pro)

  • New AGGRESSIVE execution mode instructs the agent to apply changes decisively without asking for confirmation on each step.
  • Configurable fallback policy: ABORT, RETRY, or ESCALATE when a step fails.

Model intelligence

  • ModelCapabilityService — detects whether the loaded model supports tool use, long context, code tasks, and instruction following.
  • ModelBenchmarkService — runs a quick benchmark on the active model and records tokens/second for display in settings.
  • SmartSearchService — fuzzy file and symbol search with ranking by recency, relevance, and file type.

Snapshots & context recovery

  • ProjectSnapshotService — captures a full snapshot of open files, recent edits, and context state before an agent run.
  • ContextRecoveryService — detects mid-session context drift and offers recovery options to restore the agent's context.

1.2.0 — Multi-task Agent & Session Management

Foundation release that established the core agent workflow, parallel task execution, multi-session chat, and the initial tool ecosystem.

Agent & tools

  • Tool-driven agent loop with two LLM passes (plan + execute), safe diff preview, and build verification after each apply.
  • Initial built-in tool set: read_file, write_file, list_files, search_code, run_terminal, get_diagnostics, and more.
  • Agent trace panel — shows every tool call, argument, result, and duration in the "What I tried" sidebar.

Multi-task agent (Pro)

  • Run multiple agent tasks in parallel with a live task queue panel.
  • Each task runs on a pooled thread; the UI stays responsive throughout.

Multi-session chat

  • Persistent chat session store — conversations survive IDE restarts.
  • Chat session list panel — switch between multiple simultaneous conversations.
  • Parallel chat sessions in Ask mode.

Context actions

  • Right-click editor actions: Ask About Selection, Explain This File, Refactor Selection, Fix Selected Code, Generate Tests, Add Documentation, Edit with Prompt, Explain Failing Build, Explain Current Git Changes.

TokenSlayer — Semantic Structural Cache for GitHub Copilot

⚡ Slash LLM token usage by 40–95% with AST-driven code skeletons.

TokenSlayer eliminates the "orientation tax" AI coding assistants pay when reading raw files. It generates compact structural skeletons (8 lines instead of 1,200) and exposes them to GitHub Copilot via an embedded MCP server.

Features

  • 📊 Live dashboard — real-time token savings analytics

idea-plugin.name: AI Agent CLI Bridge

Seamlessly connect your IDE workflow with terminal-based AI coding tools.

AI Agent CLI Bridge helps you launch a preconfigured AI terminal session and send context directly from the IDE.

idea-plugin.name: Gemini CLI Companion by UnscientificJsZhai

This plugin provides tools to open and close diff windows within the IDE, allowing users to review and confirm suggested code modifications through an interactive interface.

Added

idea-plugin.name: Claude Terminal Tab Persistence
idea-plugin.description:
Claude Terminal Tab Persistence for Rider / IntelliJ

Auto-restores your Claude Code terminal sessions across IDE restarts. The plugin tracks alive Claude sessions in ~/.claude/rider-plugin/active-sessions/ and, on next project open, spawns one fresh terminal tab per saved session running claude --resume <sid>.

3.0 redesign — own the terminal

The plugin now creates every Claude tab itself and assigns its session id at launch, so tab ↔ session identity is a stored fact from birth — no reflection, ancestry walks, or title guessing. Openness is simply "the tab is present in the tool window"; only an × closes a tab, while window-close, quit, crash, and reboot all reopen every open tab.

  • The plugin owns Claude tab titles. Every tab hosting a Claude session shows ✳ <name>, and the glyph animates while the session is thinking (mirroring Claude's own busy/idle status). Titles are continuously enforced — a tab clobbered to "Local" self-heals within half a second.
  • Names that stick. Display name priority: your explicit name (Rider's "Rename Tab" or /tab) > Claude's auto-generated topic name > the cached topic. Renames are adopted and persisted across restarts, never fought.
  • One file per alive session. active-sessions/<sid>.json — race-safe, no per-project file conflicts.
  • Bounded eviction backlog. session-backlog.json keeps the last 50 evicted sessions so you can recover them with /tabs-history.

Slash Commands

  • /tab — set this session's tab name explicitly (persists across restarts)
  • /tabs-status — live sessions + recent eviction backlog for the current project
  • /tabs-backup — explicit sync: write per-sid files for every alive Claude process
  • /tabs-history — browse the eviction backlog and print a resume command
  • /tabs-restore — list current per-sid files and print resume commands
  • /tabs-clear — clear active-sessions/ for the current project
  • /tabs-recover — after a crash, rebuild the restore list from what survived and let the plugin reopen the tabs

Requirements: Rider / IntelliJ 2026.1+, Claude Code CLI, Node.js (for the bundled helper scripts).

Coexists with the JetBrains AI Assistant chat tool window (AI Agents panel: Junie / Claude Agent / Codex) and Anthropic's official Claude Code [Beta] plugin. This plugin manages terminal-launched Claude CLI sessions only — chat tabs in the AI Agents panel are managed by JetBrains.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
3.0

Your Claude Code terminal tabs come back.

  • Restart, crash, or reboot — every Claude session that was open in the project is reopened, in order, with its name. Close a tab with × and it stays closed.
  • Named tabs. Tabs show ✳ <topic> and animate while Claude is thinking. /tab <name> renames one for good.
  • WSL included. Sessions running inside a distro are tracked and restored like local ones.
  • Slash commands — /tabs-status, /tabs-history, /tabs-recover and friends, installed automatically.

idea-plugin.name: Spedy

Manage your Spedy boards and tickets without leaving the IDE.

Features:
  • Browse boards and tickets in a dedicated tool window

  • View ticket details with Markdown-rendered descriptions
  • Change ticket status directly from the IDE with optimistic UI updates
  • Assign tickets to board members via dropdown
  • Add comments with @mention autocomplete

  • Open tickets as IntelliJ Tasks for branch naming and time tracking
  • Automatic ticket reference detection and highlighting in code
  • Hover documentation for ticket references (e.g. PROJ-123)
  • Secure OAuth 2.0 PKCE login — no passwords stored
  • Persistent session across IDE restarts
  • Status bar indicator showing connection state

idea-plugin.name: MixinMCP
idea-plugin.description:
Extends IntelliJ's built-in MCP Server with tools for Minecraft mod development, with the goal of improving mixin writing and inter-mod compatibility.

GitHub: https://github.com/muon-rw/MixinMCP

For all features, you will also need the Gradle plugin - see https://github.com/muon-rw/MixinMCP#setup

Key features:

1. Broad-scoped search:

  • Full type hierarchy: supertypes, subtypes, and all implementations of an interface or abstract class
  • Find all overrides of a method, plus its original super-method declaration
  • Call hierarchy: callers and callees of any method
  • All references to a class, method, or field
  • All @Mixin classes targeting a given class method. Helps identify cross-mod conflicts
  • Symbol search by name pattern, plus regex grep across all dependency sources

Regex search across your entire classpath including dependencies:

  • Alternative tools have a central problem: You can not perform broad, text-based search like regex on files that aren't in your project's own source. This is exactly the use case that Minecraft development (and mixin writing) needs so desperately - 100 other projects might be interacting with what you are, and you need to know what and how. While other tools might be able to read individual files in Minecraft sources, loader or mod APIs, libraries, or other mods you've added for integration or compatibility, they don't have a good way to search through them.
  • With this plugin, agents can easily scan the whole project dependency network on their own, including dependencies without published sources.
  • Circumvents the need to manually copy and paste snippets into context, or for agents to find jars in your gradle cache and unzip/analyze them manually one by one.

2. Class/Method Bytecode lookup:

  • Get the actual compiled bytecode for a given class or method
  • Useful to find a precise target when writing mixins, especially for ordinals or synthetic lambdas

3. Reference-aware refactoring:

  • Rename, safe-delete, move, inline, extract, change signatures, and move members, with every reference updated project-wide in one atomic operation
  • Update non-compiled references: mixin config JSON entries, mods.toml, ServiceLoader files, and javadoc links
  • Conflicts are reported per file instead of just discarded. Most tools support a dry-run preview

4. Agent Skills for enhanced Mixin Writing (companion Claude Code plugin):

  • Install once in Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add muon-rw/MixinMCP, then /plugin install mixinmcp@mixinmcp
  • Improve compatibility of written mixins by favoring MixinExtras injectors which LLMs often hallucinate or fail to use in the first place
  • Favor precise modification for the exact target for the task without workarounds, slices, or shift by's, thanks to MixinExtras' robust @Expression annotation

5. Automatic Mappings lookup:

  • Easily convert any class, method, or field name between SRG, Intermediary, Yarn, Mojmap, and obf
  • Mappings are downloaded on demand (Mojang launcher meta, Fabric Maven, Forge/NeoForge Maven) and cached under ~/.cache/mixinmcp/mappings/
  • This allows you to retrieve mapping data for (almost) any version or loader, even those not present in the current project
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • mixin_list_jar_entries can grep: regexPattern searches the text files of each jar, and jarPath accepts a folder of jars. This answers questions like "which mods in this pack depend on X" and reaches runtime-only jars that mixin_search_in_deps cannot
  • mixin_method_bytecode: regexPattern shows only the matching instructions, each with its line and Mixin ordinal. Searching for a lambda's name finds where it is created
  • mixin_move_file: dryRun and ignoreConflicts, matching the other refactor tools
  • mixin_safe_delete removes a deleted mixin class's entries from its mixin configs, instead of refusing deletion by considering the json a blocking usage
  • mixin_search_in_deps names the jars it could not search (runtime-only, or never decompiled)
  • Class-not-found errors suggest classes with the same simple name, and point out a newly created file the IDE has not picked up yet

Changed

  • mixin_call_hierarchy lists each calling method once, with the Mixin ordinal and line of every call when it calls the target more than once
  • mixin_get_dep_source(path=...) lists the other jars that ship the same path, such as a datapack overriding a vanilla file

Fixed

  • mixin_get_dep_source(className=...) failing on binary-only mods and runtime-only classes
  • mixin_find_class line numbers for binary-only mods not matching mixin_get_dep_source and mixin_search_in_deps
  • mixin_get_dep_source(path=...) missing vanilla data and asset files
  • mixin_move_file moving a class despite access conflicts, breaking the build
  • methodDescriptor picking the wrong overload for methods with generic parameters
  • mixin_call_hierarchy including callers of other overloads
  • Relative paths not working in mixin_refresh_vfs, jarPath, and jar:// URLs
  • Misleading labels: a repeated scope tag in mixin_find_class, data files shown as .class artifacts in mixin_get_dep_source, and a wrong "source not available" note in mixin_call_hierarchy

idea-plugin.name: Claude Code Terminal Tab
idea-plugin.description:
Open Claude Code in JetBrains IDE's built-in Terminal with a single click.


Background

Claude Code officially provides the Claude Code (Beta) plugin with two core capabilities: (1) IDE MCP Server — exposes IDE context (open files, selections) to the CLI; (2) Quick terminal session — open/activate a Claude Code session in the built-in Terminal.

However, the official plugin has long remained in Beta (0.1.14-beta), rated 2.5/5, and has not been updated for over five months. Capability (2) has a known bug: the button is unresponsive when multiple Projects are open. Related issues (GitHub #22232, #1232) have been reported for a long time without a fix.

This plugin is built specifically to fix that problem. Use both together: the official plugin provides IDE MCP Server, this plugin handles reliable terminal session toggling.


Features

  • Click the Toolbar button to focus the Claude Code Terminal tab instantly; hides if already active, focuses if inactive.
  • If the tab doesn't exist, it will be created and the launch command will be executed automatically.
  • Process health check: automatically detects if the Claude process has exited and recreates the tab.
  • Concurrent-click safe — rapid clicks never create duplicate tabs.
  • Optional fullscreen rendering: eliminates flickering, stabilizes memory for long conversations.
  • Customize command, model, verbose mode, extra args, and more in Settings → Tools → Claude Code 终端.

一键在 JetBrains IDE 内置 Terminal 中打开 Claude Code，支持进程存活检测、自动重建和全屏渲染。


背景

Claude Code 官方已提供 Claude Code (Beta) 插件，核心能力包括： （1）IDE MCP Server — 向 CLI 暴露 IDE 上下文（打开的文件、选中内容等）； （2）快捷打开终端会话 — 在 IDE 内置终端中一键打开或激活 Claude Code 会话。

然而该插件长期处于 Beta 阶段（0.1.14-beta），评分仅 2.5/5，且已超过五个月未更新。 能力（2）在多 Project 窗口下存在已知 bug：按钮点击无响应。 相关问题（GitHub #22232、#1232）积压已久，未见修复。

本插件正是为解决这一问题而开发。与官方插件配合使用：官方插件提供 IDE MCP Server，本插件负责终端会话的可靠唤起。


功能

  • 点击 Toolbar 按钮，自动聚焦 Claude Code Terminal tab；已激活则隐藏，未激活则聚焦。
  • 若 tab 不存在，自动新建并执行启动命令（默认 claude）。
  • 进程存活检测：tab 已创建但 Claude 进程已退出时，自动关闭旧 tab 并重建。
  • 防并发：连续快速点击不会重复创建多个 tab。
  • 可选全屏渲染：消除闪烁、长对话内存稳定，同时保留终端原生选择与搜索。
  • 可在 Settings → Tools → Claude Code 终端 中自定义命令、模型、verbose、追加参数等。
idea-plugin.change-notes: 完整更新日志参见 GitHub Releases。

idea-plugin.name: CrickCoder AI IDE
idea-plugin.description:
CrickCoder: The Ultimate AI Agent for JetBrains

CrickCoder is an advanced, fully autonomous coding assistant engineered specifically for the JetBrains ecosystem (IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, etc.). It doesn't just autocomplete code—it acts as a proactive agent that thinks, plans, and executes complex programming tasks directly within your IDE.


Core JetBrains Integrations:

  • Native File System & Diff Viewer: CrickCoder hooks directly into JetBrains' Virtual File System (VFS). Review every AI modification using the native JetBrains Diff Tool before applying changes to disk.
  • Smart Terminal Execution: The agent can autonomously run compilers, tests, and scripts through your IDE's terminal to verify its own code before presenting the final result.
  • Deep Context Awareness: Instantly understands your open tabs, active text selections, and entire project structure without manual copy-pasting.
  • No Model Quotas: Powered by the CrickCoder PAI Gateway. Choose between top-tier models (like DeepSeek V4,Opus 4.7) and execution models, paying only for what you use. No arbitrary lock-outs.
  • Immersive UI: A sleek "Neural Glass" chat interface that perfectly respects your JetBrains IDE theme

Stop chatting with AI. Start pairing with an autonomous software engineer.

idea-plugin.name: GitScribe
idea-plugin.description:
GitScribe is an IntelliJ Platform plugin that generates commit messages from staged or selected VCS changes using large language models.

It integrates with the JetBrains IDE commit workflow, reading the files or line-level diffs involved in the commit, constructing prompts, and writing the generated commit message back to the commit window.

Features

  • Generate commit messages from Git or Subversion diffs.
  • Support using only selected files and lines in the commit dialog.
  • Configure multiple LLM clients and switch between them when generating.
  • Custom prompt templates with variables like {diff}, {branch}, {locale}, {hint}, and historical commit messages.
  • Per-project configuration for prompts, output language, LLM clients, and exclusion rules.
  • Glob patterns to exclude paths you don't want to send to the model.
  • Validate API client configuration in the settings page.

Supported LLM Clients

  • Amazon Bedrock
  • Anthropic
  • Azure OpenAI
  • Claude Code CLI
  • Codex CLI
  • DeepSeek
  • Gemini Google AI
  • Gemini Vertex AI
  • GitHub Models
  • Hugging Face
  • MiniMax
  • Mistral AI
  • Ollama
  • OpenAI
  • Qianfan
  • Zhipu AI
  • SiliconFlow

Most online model clients are implemented based on langchain4j. CLI clients invoke locally installed command-line tools and use their output as commit message source.

Compatibility

  • IntelliJ Platform: 2024.2+
  • Java Toolchain: 21
  • VCS Integration: Git and Subversion

Theoretically, any JetBrains IDE that supports the IntelliJ Platform commit flow can use it, such as IntelliJ IDEA, Android Studio, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, CLion, PhpStorm, DataGrip, RubyMine, Rider, and DataSpell.

Usage

  1. Open Settings > Tools > GitScribe.
  2. Add and configure an LLM client.
  3. Optional: Edit the default prompt or add your own prompt templates.
  4. Open the commit dialog.
  5. Click the GitScribe button in the commit message toolbar, or use the shortcut Ctrl + Alt + C.

If using Claude Code CLI or Codex CLI, ensure the corresponding command-line tool is installed and accessible via PATH, or manually specify the CLI path in GitScribe settings.

Links

  • GitHub Repository
  • Report Bugs or Feature Requests

idea-plugin.name: AI Unified Process Navigator
idea-plugin.description:
Navigate between @UseCase annotated test methods and their Markdown specs — and see a live activity diagram of the Use Case you are editing.

Live activity diagram

The AI Unified Process Diagram tool window renders a PlantUML activity diagram of the Use Case spec (UC-*.md, SUC-*.md, BUC-*.md) in the selected editor: the Main Success Scenario is the spine, every Alternative Flow branches at the step its trigger references. The diagram updates as you type and is rendered entirely in-process (MIT-licensed PlantUML with the Smetana engine) — no Graphviz, no external rendering service, the spec never leaves your IDE.

BPMN editor

*.bpmn process models open in the bpmn-js modeler of the AI Unified Process Studio — palette, canvas, and properties panel — with the XML still available in the Text tab. Both tabs edit the same document, so diagram edits are regular, undoable file changes. The editor runs in the IDE's embedded browser from files bundled with the plugin; nothing is loaded from the network. The toolbar exports the diagram as SVG or PNG, and ```bpmn fences show as diagrams in the Markdown preview.

Navigation between specs and tests

  • Gutter icon on @UseCase annotation jumps to the matching spec file (UC-XXX-*.md, SUC-XXX-*.md, BUC-XXX-*.md, each also with an optional project prefix like petclinic-UC-XXX-*.md)
  • Gutter icon on **Use Case ID:** UC-XXX in Markdown jumps to all test methods with that ID
  • Gutter icon on ### BR-XXX business rule headers jumps to tests referencing that rule
  • Find Usages (Alt+F7) works in both directions, and an inspection flags Use Case IDs without a spec

Setup: the host project must define a Java annotation type called UseCase with attributes id, scenario, and businessRules. If the plugin sees Markdown specs in a project but no such annotation, it offers a one-time balloon with a "Create UseCase.java" action that scaffolds the file into a chosen source root.

Works with the AI Unified Process methodology.
