idea-plugin.name: FoxMock — REST, gRPC, SMTP & SFTP Mock Server
idea-plugin.description:
Mock HTTP REST APIs and gRPC services without leaving your JetBrains IDE. Define multiple named scenarios per HTTP route and auto-switch responses by query parameter, header, or request body — no manual switching needed. Import any OpenAPI spec and generate all routes instantly. Upload a .proto file and mock any gRPC service without a real backend. Generate realistic JSON responses with AI (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, local Ollama, or any AI CLI already installed on your machine — no API key required). Test email sending with a built-in SMTP server. Simulate SFTP file transfers locally. No browser tabs. No separate tools. No context switching.

Supported Protocols

  • REST / HTTP Mock Server — Mock any REST API endpoint instantly. Define routes, scenarios, headers, status codes, and response bodies. Supports path variables, wildcards, and conditional matching.
  • gRPC Mock Server — Mock gRPC services without a real server. Load your .proto files, define mock responses for any unary RPC method, and test your gRPC clients in isolation. Full Protocol Buffers (protobuf) support. No need to run a real gRPC backend during development.
  • SMTP Mock Server — Run a local SMTP mock server inside your IDE. Test email sending, verify message content, and simulate email delivery without a real mail server. Ideal for testing transactional email flows, password resets, and notification emails.
  • SFTP Mock Server — Spin up a local SFTP server with configurable credentials, port, and root directory. Test SFTP file uploads and downloads without connecting to a real SFTP host.

Who Is This For?

FoxMock is built for developers who:

  • Build and test gRPC microservices and need to mock gRPC dependencies
  • Test gRPC clients without running a real gRPC server
  • Work with Protocol Buffers and need fast gRPC service simulation
  • Need a local SMTP mock server to test email sending in integration tests
  • Develop against SFTP servers and need a local SFTP mock for testing
  • Build REST APIs and want instant mock REST endpoints without a backend
  • Work in microservice architectures and need to isolate services during development
  • Want to develop frontend or mobile apps without waiting for backend APIs

All Features

  • gRPC Mocking — Load .proto files and mock individual unary RPC methods. Define multiple named scenarios per method. Test gRPC clients against a local gRPC mock server. Supports Protocol Buffers response definition. Inspect live gRPC requests in the request log.
  • SMTP Mocking — Local SMTP mock server for testing email workflows. Verify sent messages, simulate delivery, and test transactional email without a real mail server.
  • SFTP Mocking — Local SFTP mock server with configurable port, credentials, and root path. Test file upload and download logic without a remote SFTP host.
  • REST / HTTP Mocking — Define routes (method + path), add multiple named response scenarios, enable/disable them individually, and organise routes into drag-and-drop groups.
  • Conditional Scenario Matching — Attach match conditions (query parameters, headers, request body fields) to any scenario. FoxMock evaluates conditions automatically on every incoming request and returns the first matching scenario — no manual switching needed.
  • Three-Tier Scenario Resolution — Conditional scenarios are evaluated first (ordered by priority); if none match, the manually activated scenario is used; if that is also absent, the first enabled scenario acts as the safety net.
  • OpenAPI / Swagger Import — Paste or upload any OpenAPI 3.0 or Swagger 2.0 spec (JSON or YAML). FoxMock parses every endpoint — including path parameters and query parameters — and generates a full set of realistic scenarios automatically.
  • Smart Query-Parameter Scenarios — Enum query parameters automatically expand into one scenario per allowed value, each with a pre-wired EQUALS match condition. Free-form parameters get an EXISTS scenario so you can test presence/absence without any manual configuration.
  • AI-Powered Generation — Connect OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, a local Ollama instance, or any AI CLI already installed on your machine (claude, ollama run, llm, sgpt, etc.) to auto-generate realistic response bodies. The CLI provider requires no API key — it pipes the prompt to whatever tool you already have authenticated. Parameter context, response class source, and matching controller code from the open project are all included in the prompt for more accurate output.
  • Collections — Save and reload sets of routes as .fmcoll.json files. Selective export lets you choose which routes to include. On import, per-route conflict resolution (Keep / Replace / Merge) prevents accidental overwrites.
  • Request Inspector — Live transaction log (method, path, status, duration) for all server types — REST, gRPC, SMTP, and SFTP — keeping the last 100 entries per server.
  • cURL Export — Copy a ready-to-run curl command for any route directly from the edit dialog.
  • Response Delay — Simulate network latency per scenario (0 – 30 000 ms) to test loading states and timeouts.
  • Secure Credentials — AI API keys are stored in the OS keychain via IntelliJ PasswordSafe and never written to disk.
  • Works everywhere — Compatible with IntelliJ IDEA, Android Studio, WebStorm, GoLand, PyCharm, Rider, CLion, RubyMine, DataGrip, and any other JetBrains IDE.

Quick Start

  1. Open View → Tool Windows → FoxMock.
  2. Click Start on the HTTP card (Dashboard tab) to start the REST mock server.
  3. Click Add Route, fill in method, path, and response body, then save.
  4. Point your application at http://localhost:8089 — done.
  5. To mock gRPC: go to the gRPC tab, load your .proto file, and define mock responses.
  6. To mock SMTP: start the SMTP server and point your mailer at localhost:2525.
  7. To mock SFTP: start the SFTP server and connect with the configured credentials.
  8. Optional: import an OpenAPI spec with Import OpenAPI Spec to generate all REST routes in one step.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.0 — First Stable Release

FoxMock graduates from public beta. All features from the beta programme are production-ready and available in this release.

What's included

  • REST / HTTP mock server — routes with path variables, wildcards, regex matching, per-scenario status codes, headers, and artificial delay. Group, search, drag-and-drop.
  • gRPC mock server — load .proto files, mock unary RPC methods, save/load config as .foxmock-grpc.
  • SMTP mock server — test transactional email without a real mail server.
  • SFTP mock server — test file upload/download without a remote SFTP host.
  • Conditional scenario matching — query param, header, and body conditions evaluated automatically on every request; three-tier resolution (conditional → active → first enabled).
  • OpenAPI / Swagger import — generates full route sets from any 3.0 or 2.0 spec; enum params expand into one scenario each.
  • AI response generation — OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Ollama, or any CLI tool already on your machine (no extra API key required).
  • Collections — save and load route sets as .fmcoll.json with per-route conflict resolution.
  • Spring MVC gutter icons — live green/gray status icons next to every mapped endpoint in the editor.
  • "Add to FoxMock" action — right-click any controller method, HTTP client call, or framework route to create a mock in one step. Supports Java, Kotlin, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Go.
  • Multi-language UI — English, Spanish, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Chinese (Simplified), and Brazilian Portuguese.
  • Request inspector — live log for REST, gRPC, SMTP, and SFTP with syntax colouring and inline request detail.
  • cURL export, keyboard shortcuts, dashboard Start All / Stop All.

Freemium model

Core mocking (REST, gRPC, SMTP, SFTP, request inspector) is free forever. Pro features — conditional matching, AI generation, Collections, and OpenAPI import — require a FoxMock Pro license ($4.90/month or $39/year, free 30-day trial included).

1.0.0-beta.6 — IntelliJ 2026.1 Compatibility, Multi-Language UI & Add to FoxMock Overhaul

Fixed — "Add to FoxMock" Not Appearing on Windows / IntelliJ 2026.1

  • ActionUpdateThread switched to BGT — IntelliJ 2026.1 stopped honouring ActionUpdateThread.EDT for popup-menu actions; update() is now always called on a background thread.
  • PSI-free update() check — the visibility check no longer calls ReadAction.compute() on BGT, which competed with the write-intent lock on Windows and silently cancelled the action. It is now a simple file-extension lookup with no PSI involvement — guaranteed to work on all platforms.
  • Registered in both EditorPopupMenu and EditorPopupMenu1 — covers both the legacy (2023–2025.x) and new (2026.1+) editor popup group architectures.
  • Editor context fallback — on Windows the popup-menu event sometimes does not carry CommonDataKeys.EDITOR; the action now falls back to FileEditorManager.getSelectedTextEditor() so the click always resolves.
  • User-visible error dialogs — instead of silently doing nothing, the action now shows a clear message when the editor cannot be resolved, when no PSI element is found at the cursor, or when no extractor matches.

Fixed — "No Route Could Be Extracted" for Spring MVC & @Controller Classes

  • Wrong FQN for @Controller fixed — @Controller was looked up as org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.Controller (which does not exist). The correct FQN is org.springframework.stereotype.Controller. Every plain @Controller class was silently rejected; only @RestController worked. Now both are correctly detected.
  • Annotation short-name fallback — @PostMapping, @GetMapping, @RestController, @Controller and all Spring mapping annotations are now recognised even when IntelliJ has not yet resolved their fully-qualified names in the index (common on Windows on first project open or during a slow classpath scan).
  • Feign @FeignClient short-name fallback — @FeignClient interfaces are recognised even when the OpenFeign FQN is unresolved.
  • Retrofit @GET / @POST short-name fallback — Retrofit 2 annotations matched by short name when the library FQNs are not yet indexed.
  • RestTemplate / WebClient unresolved-method fallback — falls back to qualifier variable name (restTemplate, WebClient) when call.resolveMethod() returns null.

Fixed — "No Route Could Be Extracted" for Go, Kotlin & Other Frameworks

  • Go framework import detection — Gin, Echo, and go-resty route calls were rejected when the import declaration was outside the text window. All three extractors now check the full file text for the import.
  • Ktor server and client extractor widened — accepts any file containing ktor in the full text, matching the approach used for Go frameworks.
  • Context window doubled — widened from 400 to 1000 characters; route decorators more than a few lines from the cursor are now reliably captured.
  • PSI parent walk depth increased — raised from 12 to 20 levels, covering deeply nested code (inner classes, lambdas, builder chains).
  • All getData() + PSI reads moved inside ReadAction — caret offset and PSI element resolution are now thread-safe on all IntelliJ versions.

New — Multi-Language UI (i18n)

  • 8 languages supported — English, Spanish, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Chinese (Simplified), and Brazilian Portuguese. Every label, button, status message, and validation prompt is fully translated.
  • Language picker in Dashboard — switch languages instantly; the entire UI rebuilds immediately without an IDE restart.

Improved — Generic Type Scaffolding in "Add to FoxMock"

  • ResponseEntity<List<T>> now scaffolds correctly — previously returned []; now extracts and scaffolds the inner type fields into [{...fields...}].
  • Page<T>, Slice<T>, Flux<T>, Mono<T> — all generic wrapper and collection types now produce realistic scaffolded response bodies.
  • Map<K, V> — generates {"key": {...}} with V scaffolded.

Improved — Settings Tab Redesign

  • AI Configuration moved to top — AI provider settings now appear first for faster access.
  • Server Configuration section — renamed from "Settings" to "Server Configuration" across all 8 supported languages.
  • Accordions expanded by default — HTTP, SFTP, gRPC and SMTP sections open automatically.
  • AI settings always-editable — provider, API key, model and host fields are inline and immediately editable.
  • Auto-detect IDE language — language preference auto-detected from IDE locale on first launch.

1.0.0-beta.5 — Add to FoxMock — IntelliJ 2024 Compatibility

Fixed — "Add to FoxMock" Button Not Appearing

  • Internal API replaced — PsiRouteHelper previously used com.intellij.psi.impl.JavaConstantExpressionEvaluator, which became unavailable in IntelliJ 2024.x builds. Replaced with the public PsiConstantEvaluationHelper API via JavaPsiFacade.getInstance(project).getConstantEvaluationHelper(). Same behaviour, compatible with all supported IntelliJ versions.
  • BGT caret model access fixed — getPsiElementUnderCursor() previously called editor.getCaretModel().getOffset() from a background thread. In IntelliJ 2024.x the caret model must only be read from the EDT. The method now uses CommonDataKeys.PSI_ELEMENT as the primary approach (the documented BGT-safe data key for editor popups), with the file-and-offset path kept as a fallback.
  • Null guard in gutter provider — MockRouteGutterProvider now checks that getHttpServer() is non-null before querying routes or server status. Previously a NullPointerException was thrown on every Spring MVC file when the HTTP server had not yet initialised.

1.0.0-beta.4 — Live Editor Indicators

New — Regex Path Matching

  • Automatic regex detection — any route path containing Java regex characters ([, (, \, ^, $, |, +) is matched as a full Java regular expression. No flag or toggle required.
  • Example: /api/orders/[0-9]+/items matches GET /api/orders/42/items but not GET /api/orders/abc/items.
  • ~ badge in the route table — regex paths are shown with a leading ~ prefix in the Path column so they are visually distinct from plain and {param}-style routes.
  • Malformed regex patterns are silently skipped (route returns 404) — the server never crashes on a bad pattern.

New — Spring MVC Gutter Icons

  • Live mock status icons — a Fox icon now appears in the editor margin next to every @GetMapping, @PostMapping, @PutMapping, @DeleteMapping, @PatchMapping, and @RequestMapping method whose path is registered in the HTTP mock panel.
  • Green icon — the route is mocked and the HTTP server is running.
  • Gray icon — the route is mocked but the server is currently stopped.
  • Icons refresh in real-time: adding a route, deleting a route, or toggling the server updates all gutter indicators across every open editor immediately.

Fixed — Panel Layout Stability on Fresh Install

  • Replaced WrapLayout button panels with stable fixed-height FlowLayout rows in all four mock panels (HTTP, gRPC, SFTP, SMTP). The gap that appeared between the toolbar and the content area on a fresh install is gone.
  • A HierarchyListener on each panel triggers a single revalidation pass once the tool window is first shown with real pixel dimensions, so OnePixelSplitter dividers land in the correct position on first open.

1.0.0-beta.3 — UI Redesign, gRPC Parity & CLI AI

gRPC — Full Scenario Management Parity

  • Enabled / disabled flag per gRPC scenario — uncheck Enabled in the Configure dialog to take a scenario out of rotation without deleting it. Disabled scenarios are shown gray and italic in the list and are skipped at all three resolution tiers.
  • Conditions tab in the gRPC Configure dialog — add, edit, and remove match conditions directly in the gRPC scenario editor, with the same condition types available for REST: Body JSONPath, Body Regex, and Body Exact.
  • Priority spinner — control the evaluation order of conditional gRPC scenarios; lower number = higher priority.
  • Visual role badges in the scenario list — ● marks the active fallback, ⚡ marks a conditional scenario, ⚡● marks both, and disabled scenarios are dimmed. Badge rendering is now consistent across REST and gRPC panels.
  • Scenario rename — rename a gRPC scenario directly from the Configure dialog name field without recreating it.
  • Three-tier resolution fully operational for gRPC — conditional scenarios (Tier 1) are now correctly filtered by the enabled flag before evaluation; disabled scenarios can no longer accidentally win a conditional match.

gRPC — Save / Load Config

  • Save Config button in the gRPC panel — exports all services, methods, scenarios, conditions, and priorities to a .foxmock-grpc JSON file.
  • Load Config button — restores the full scenario set from a .foxmock-grpc file. Methods not found in the currently loaded .proto are skipped and listed in the confirmation dialog.
  • Commit .foxmock-grpc alongside your .proto files so the whole team loads the same mock setup in two clicks.

HTTP Panel — Tutorial Shortcut

  • Added a 📖 Tutorial button to the HTTP Mock panel toolbar. Opens the Mock REST APIs with Query Params & Scenarios tutorial at fox-mock.com in the default browser — useful when setting up conditional query-parameter matching for the first time.

UI Redesign — IntelliJ-Style Panel Layout

  • Flat section headers — all four mock panels (HTTP, gRPC, SFTP, SMTP) now use bold 12 pt labels with a 1 px theme-aware divider instead of raised titled borders, matching standard IntelliJ tool window style.
  • Inline connection info strip — server address, port, and credentials are shown in a compact gray strip immediately below the toolbar, reducing visual noise.
  • HTTP — vertical split — routes and request log are always visible in a vertical OnePixelSplitter with a draggable divider.
  • HTTP — flat route table — one row per route shows method, path, and the active scenario name inline; accordion expansion is gone.
  • HTTP — group collapse / expand — single-click a group header to collapse or expand it (▶ / ▼); double-click still opens the rename dialog.
  • HTTP — smart search — IntelliJ SearchTextField replaces method-filter chips; accepts GET, /api/users, or POST /orders.
  • SFTP — "Add File" and "Refresh" moved into the Mock Files section header.
  • gRPC — "Load Proto" moved into the Proto Files section header.
  • SMTP — "Clear Inbox" moved into the Inbox section header.
  • All panels — "Clear" button moved into the log section header.

New Feature — CLI AI Provider

  • Added a new CLI AI provider that pipes the generation prompt to any AI command-line tool already installed and authenticated on your machine — no API key or cloud account needed.
  • Supported out of the box: claude (Claude Code), ollama run <model>, llm, sgpt, aichat, or any custom shell command that reads from stdin and writes the response to stdout.
  • Auto-detect — click Detect available CLIs… in Settings → Tools → FoxMock to scan your PATH and pick from a list of found tools with one click.
  • The CLI command is stored as plain text (not a secret) and survives IDE restarts.

Richer AI Context for HTTP Routes

  • When the CLI provider is active, FoxMock now scans Java and Kotlin source files in the open project and automatically includes the matching controller source code in the prompt — giving the model accurate field names, method signatures, and business context for more realistic generated responses.
  • Controller detection matches on the route path and the presence of Spring MVC (@RestController, @GetMapping, etc.) or JAX-RS (@Path) annotations.

1.0.0-beta.2 — Debug Logs, Conditional Match Fix & UI Polish

Bug Fix — Conditional Scenario Auto-Matching

  • Fixed a critical bug where setting a scenario as the default fallback incorrectly disabled all other scenarios, including conditional ones — causing Tier 1 auto-matching to never fire. Conditional scenarios are now always evaluated regardless of which non-conditional scenario is pinned as the default.

Richer Request Inspector

  • HTTP log now shows the query string, matched scenario name, and request body (POST / PUT / PATCH) as indented detail lines beneath each transaction
  • gRPC log now shows the proto request type and response type for every call
  • Errors are rendered on a dedicated bold-red line with a ✕ prefix across all three inspectors (HTTP, gRPC, SFTP), making failures immediately visible
  • Log panels replaced with a styled console view — monospaced font, IDE-theme background, syntax-coloured HTTP methods and status codes (green 2xx, orange 4xx, red 5xx)

UI Polish

  • All split panes now use a 1 px theme-aware divider (OnePixelSplitter) consistent with the IntelliJ UI

Plugin Discoverability

  • .fmcoll.json collection files are now registered as a JetBrains file type — when a teammate opens a collection file in an IDE that does not have FoxMock installed, the Marketplace will suggest the plugin automatically
  • Non-intrusive rating prompt appears once after 10 successful mock responses

1.0.0-beta.1 — Initial Public Beta

First public beta release of FoxMock — REST API mock server, gRPC mock server, SMTP mock server, and SFTP mock server, all inside your JetBrains IDE.

gRPC Mock Server

  • Mock gRPC services directly inside IntelliJ without a real gRPC backend
  • Load .proto files to discover and mock gRPC service methods
  • Mock unary gRPC RPC calls with named response scenarios
  • Protocol Buffers (protobuf) response definition support
  • Multiple named mock scenarios per gRPC method
  • Live gRPC request inspector — see every incoming gRPC call in real time
  • Test gRPC clients in isolation without running a real gRPC server

SMTP Mock Server

  • Local SMTP mock server for testing email sending inside IntelliJ
  • Test transactional emails, password reset flows, and notification emails
  • Inspect sent messages without a real mail server
  • Configurable SMTP port and credentials

SFTP Mock Server

  • Local SFTP mock server with configurable port, credentials, and root directory
  • Test SFTP file upload and download logic without a remote SFTP host
  • Live SFTP request inspector (last 100 entries)

REST / HTTP Mock Server

  • Dynamic routing with support for path variables ({name} syntax) and wildcards
  • Multiple named scenarios per route; only one active at a time
  • Per-scenario status code, response body, custom headers, and artificial delay
  • Route enable/disable toggle without deleting the route
  • Route grouping with drag-and-drop reorganisation; groups can be renamed and removed

Conditional Scenario Matching

  • Scenarios can carry match conditions evaluated against every incoming request
  • Supported condition targets: query parameters, request headers, request body fields
  • Supported operators: EQUALS, EXISTS, CONTAINS, STARTS_WITH, ENDS_WITH, REGEX
  • Priority field on each conditional scenario controls evaluation order
  • Three-tier resolution: conditional → manually activated → first enabled

OpenAPI / Swagger Import

  • Import OpenAPI 3.0+ and Swagger 2.0 specs in JSON or YAML format
  • Path parameters and query parameters are fully parsed and included in generated scenarios
  • Enum query parameters expand into one scenario per allowed value, each with an auto-wired QUERY_PARAM EQUALS match condition (capped at 12 variants)
  • Free-form query parameters generate an EXISTS scenario automatically
  • Parameter names, types, and examples are passed to the AI prompt for richer output
  • Standard fallback scenarios (200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 500) generated when no AI is configured

AI Generation

  • Supported providers: OpenAI, Claude (Anthropic), Gemini (Google), Ollama (local), CLI (any AI command-line tool)
  • Generate from response class name, request class, free-text context, or OpenAPI spec
  • API keys stored securely in the OS keychain via IntelliJ PasswordSafe

Collections

  • Save any subset of routes to a .fmcoll.json file
  • Load collections with per-route conflict resolution: Keep / Replace / Merge
  • Bulk conflict resolution shortcuts (Keep all / Replace all / Merge all)

Developer Experience

  • cURL export — copy a ready-to-run command from any route dialog
  • Live request inspector for REST, gRPC, SMTP, and SFTP (last 100 entries each)
  • Dashboard tab with one-click Start All / Stop All for all mock servers
  • Keyboard shortcuts: Alt+Shift+F start all, Alt+Shift+X stop all
  • Plugin is dynamically loadable — no IDE restart required after install

idea-plugin.name: Crash2Test
idea-plugin.description: Crash2Test is a local AI-powered IntelliJ IDEA plugin that helps developers turn stack traces and runtime errors into debugging timelines and regression test ideas.

idea-plugin.name: Debug MCP
idea-plugin.description:
Control IntelliJ IDEA with AI coding assistants like Claude Code via the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

The plugin starts a local MCP server (JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP on port 63820) that exposes 37 tools across 8 API groups:

  • Debugger — set/remove breakpoints, start/stop sessions, step over/into/out, inspect variables, evaluate expressions, navigate stack frames
  • Build — incremental build or full rebuild, read compiler errors and warnings
  • Tests — run JUnit/TestNG tests by class or method, collect results with stack traces
  • Files & Editor — read files, list directories, glob search, full-text search, open files in editor at a specific line
  • PSI (Code Structure) — find classes, inspect their fields and methods, find all usages, get file structure with signatures and line numbers
  • Inspections — surface IDE static-analysis warnings (errors / warnings / weak warnings) for any open file
  • Git — git blame with line range, commit log, diffs by file or commit
  • Run Configurations — list, create, and update Application / JUnit run configs

Claude Code uses its built-in Bash tool to call the server via curl — no extra MCP client setup needed. Just add a short block to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and Claude will discover all tools automatically.

Example workflows:

  • Set a breakpoint, launch a debug session, inspect variables, find the bug — autonomously
  • Build → read errors → patch code → rebuild until clean
  • Run tests → read failures → fix → repeat until green
  • Explore an unfamiliar codebase: find classes, trace usages, read relevant files
  • Audit code quality: get IDE inspections, fix all warnings
  • Git blame a suspicious line and read the commit that introduced it

See the GitHub repository for setup instructions and full tool reference.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.2 — Bug fixes

  • set_breakpoint — fixed: now accepts relative paths (resolved against project root via VfsUtil)
  • get_file_structure — fixed: replaced reflection-based Kotlin PSI traversal with PsiShortNamesCache API, compatible with Kotlin K2 compiler mode

1.0.1 — Compatibility fix

  • Fixed compatibility with IntelliJ IDEA 2025.1 (IC-251)
  • Replaced internal XLineBreakpointImpl with public XLineBreakpoint API
  • Declared JUnit plugin dependency explicitly
  • Added Kotlin K2 plugin mode support

1.0.0 — Initial release

  • Debugger API — breakpoints, session control, step commands, variable inspection, expression evaluation, stack frame navigation
  • Build API — incremental Make / full Rebuild, compiler error reader
  • Test Runner API — run JUnit/TestNG tests, collect per-test results with stack traces
  • File/Editor API — read files, list directories, glob and full-text search, open files in editor
  • PSI API — find classes, find usages, get file structure
  • Inspections API — surface IDE static-analysis warnings by severity
  • Git API — git blame, log, diff
  • Run Config API — create and update Application/JUnit run configurations

idea-plugin.name: Claude Code Chat
idea-plugin.description:
Claude Code for JetBrains IDE

Bring the full power of Claude Code directly into your IDE. Chat with Claude in a side panel, edit code inline with natural-language instructions, fix errors with one click in the Alt+Enter menu, generate commit messages from your staged diff, and let Claude read, edit, and create files in your project — all without leaving IntelliJ or your favorite IDE.

Inline AI Actions

  • Edit with Claude (Cmd+Alt+K / Ctrl+Alt+K, or the Claude icon in the floating code toolbar) — select code, describe a change in plain English, review the diff, and accept or reject.
  • Fix with Claude — Alt+Enter on any IDE-detected error or warning to get an AI-powered quick-fix that lives next to IntelliJ's own intentions.
  • Generate Commit Message — one click in the VCS commit dialog turns your staged diff into a Conventional Commits-style message.
  • Apply link on every chat code block — replace the selection in your active editor with the suggested code after a diff review.

Chat Panel

  • Multiple parallel Claude Code sessions in a side panel
  • Project-aware: Claude works in your open project's directory
  • Session memory: Claude remembers context across messages
  • Resume past chats — a clock-icon dropdown in the tool window header lists recent sessions per project. Pick one and the previous conversation auto-loads inline (read straight from Claude's local transcript, no API cost) so you can continue from where you left off after closing the IDE. Inline pencil / trash icons rename or remove entries.
  • Markdown rendering with syntax-highlighted code blocks
  • Tool-use indicators with colored status signals and diff summaries
  • File chips — drag/drop, copy/paste, or type a filename to attach files as context; resolves bare filenames against your project
  • Image paste — paste a screenshot or any clipboard image; saved to a temp PNG and sent to Claude as a multimodal input on submit
  • Large-text paste chips — long pastes collapse into a compact chip; double-click to expand back into the input
  • Queue messages while Claude works — type a follow-up (or /btw <message>) while a response is streaming and it queues instead of being lost, then sends automatically when the turn finishes; remove queued items before they go
  • Smart auto-scroll — follows new output unless you've scrolled up to read; "Jump to latest" button keeps you in control
  • Inline diffs: expandable old vs. new for every edit Claude makes, with consolidated stats per file
  • Clickable file links and a changed-files summary grouped by folder
  • Copy and re-edit buttons on messages and code blocks

Right-Click Context Menu

  • Explain — understand code, methods, files, or entire folders (recursive summaries)
  • Refactor — get suggestions for readability, performance, and best practices
  • Generate Tests — create unit tests for selected code, whole files, or every source file in a folder (14+ languages)
  • Fix — identify and fix bugs in selected code
  • Open Claude Session Here — right-click any folder to start a new session rooted there
  • Debug with Claude — right-click in the Run/Debug console to send exceptions, log flows, or output to Claude

Works from the editor, project tree, and Run/Debug console.

Productivity

  • Auto-updating model catalog — the model dropdown refreshes every 24h from a published list (with bundled offline fallback), so new Claude releases become available without a plugin update. Deprecated models get a (deprecated) badge and a one-click swap to the recommended replacement.
  • Keyboard shortcuts: Cmd+Shift+I to toggle the chat panel, Cmd+Alt+K for inline edit (Ctrl variants on Windows/Linux)
  • Stop requests with Escape
  • Permission mode: Plan (read-only Read/Grep/Glob), Content Only (file writes/edits OK, shell blocked), or Unrestricted (allow all) — maps to the CLI's --permission-mode
  • Project tree auto-refreshes when Claude creates, modifies, or deletes files
  • Cost tracking per response

Settings — Model & inference

  • Extended thinking budget — Off / Low (1k) / Medium (8k) / High (32k). Sets MAX_THINKING_TOKENS for Opus/Sonnet 4.x; other models ignore it. Trade speed and cost for deeper reasoning on harder tasks.
  • Append system prompt — multi-line text appended to Claude's system prompt every spawn via --append-system-prompt. Use for project conventions, preferred tone, persona instructions.
  • Max agentic turns — hard cap on the tool-call loop via --max-turns. 0 = unlimited (CLI default).

MCP Servers

  • MCP server management UI — a server icon in the tool-window header (and a button in Settings) opens a manager that aggregates every MCP server Claude can see for the project: project .mcp.json, plus the user and project-local scopes inside ~/.claude.json. Add, edit, and remove servers across all three scopes.
  • All transports — stdio (command + args + env) and remote SSE / HTTP (URL + headers, optional OAuth client id / callback port).
  • Live status — connection/auth badges (✓ connected, ✗ failed, ⏸ pending approval, 🔒 needs authentication) from a health-checked claude mcp list.
  • Authentication, your way — choose API Key / Token, OAuth, or No Auth per server. OAuth sign-in runs in the background and simply opens your browser to finish (no terminal); Authenticate All walks every server that needs it, one at a time, with a live progress panel (skip/remove, countdown). Your chat sessions then use the servers automatically.
  • All writes go through the claude mcp add-json / remove CLI, so your large, live ~/.claude.json is never hand-edited.

Settings Files Editor

  • Edit Claude Code's settings.json at project, project-local, or global scope — a JSON-file icon in the header (and a Settings button) opens it.
  • Structured or raw — a key/value Form tab adds/edits/removes top-level settings (with common keys suggested and typed JSON values), or switch to the JSON tab for raw edits. Both are validated as a JSON object before saving, and unrelated keys (including the plugin's permission grants) are preserved.

Prerequisites

  • Install the Claude CLI: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code (works on macOS, Linux, and Windows)
  • Authenticate by running claude in a terminal
  • Make sure the CLI is on your PATH so the plugin can spawn it. On Windows, npm typically installs claude.cmd under %APPDATA%\npm\ — that directory must be on PATH.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.3.0

  • Appearance settings — themes & fonts — a new Appearance section (Settings → Tools → Claude Code) lets you pick how the chat is colored: Follow IDE theme (default) matches the IDE's light/dark theme and blends in its editor colors, so a light IDE no longer shows a dark "terminal" chat; Dark and Light pin one palette regardless of the IDE (Dark is the original look). You can also set separate font family and size for the chat transcript and the input box.
  • Live theme reload — switching the IDE theme (in Follow-IDE mode) or changing the Appearance settings re-themes open chats and the welcome screen in place, no need to reopen them.

1.2.2

  • Account sign-in: /login — sign in to (or out of) your Anthropic account right from the chat. /login opens a dialog showing your current account, lets you choose subscription or Console (API billing), opens the browser for OAuth, and takes the authorization code you paste back. Built on claude auth, so it works on macOS, Linux, and Windows.
  • Authenticate All — pre-warmed, near-instant sign-ins — instead of cold-starting a hidden claude for each server in turn, several are now warmed up in the background to the sign-in prompt and parked there, then activated one at a time so each browser opens almost instantly. You pay the cold start once, then sign in to each tab in quick succession. The warm-up pool size is configurable (Settings → MCP Servers) and grows automatically if you sign in faster than servers warm up; Skip / Remove drops a server and tears down its pre-warmed process.
  • Fix: "Authenticate All" no longer gets stuck on "signing in…" with many servers — a completed sign-in is now confirmed with a fast single-server health check (claude mcp get) instead of claude mcp list, which health-checks every configured server and could exceed its timeout on large lists. If a callback is slow to arrive, the flow also re-presses Authenticate once.
  • Clickable links in code — URLs inside fenced code blocks and inline `code` spans are now clickable, not just plain text you had to copy/paste. (Prose URLs were already clickable.)
  • Fix: answering a question no longer fails with "send it manually" — submitting an answer to one of Claude's multiple-choice questions while the asking turn was still finishing could give up instantly. The answer now queues and sends the moment the turn ends.
  • Fix: "Switch to Unrestricted" / Allow now actually retries — granting a permission (or switching mode) after a blocked tool stopped the request but often failed to resend it, because the retry gave up before the process finished stopping. It now waits properly and re-runs your prompt. Reading a file outside the working directory reliably surfaces the grant / Unrestricted choices, including when the denial arrives as structured text blocks.
  • Fix: streaming session resumes correctly — in the experimental streaming mode, resuming a saved chat (or recovering after a restart) now continues the same conversation via --resume instead of silently starting a blank one under a new id.

1.2.1

  • Authenticate All — live progress & faster advancement — a non-modal panel now lists every queued server (waiting / authenticating / done / failed / skipped), shows the current server with a countdown of how long it'll wait, and lets you Skip current or Remove a pending server to avoid the wait. Each server advances the moment it connects: instead of waiting out a timeout while scraping the terminal, the flow polls claude mcp list (the same live health check as Refresh) and proceeds as soon as the server reports connected, then tears down promptly. One stuck or misconfigured server can no longer block the rest.
  • Fix: no false permission prompts in Unrestricted mode — when running Unrestricted (bypass permissions), a failing tool no longer triggers a bogus "blocked by your permission mode" message or an offer to allow the command / switch to a mode you're already in — the real error is shown instead. The permission UI now keys off the session's effective mode (the per-session chip override, not just the global default).
  • Queue messages & /btw — type a follow-up while Claude is working and it now queues (shown above the input, removable) instead of being dropped, then sends automatically when the turn finishes. /btw <message> queues a side message any time. (Each queued message is answered after the current turn — claude -p runs one turn at a time.)
  • Context meter — the status row shows how full the model's context window is (◑ N%, amber ≥75%, red ≥90%, token tooltip), so you know when to start a fresh chat. Resets on /clear.
  • Effort & fallback model — Settings → Model & inference: an Effort level (--effort: Low … Max) and a Fallback model (--fallback-model, used automatically when the primary is overloaded/unavailable).
  • CLAUDE.md memory — /init has Claude analyze the project and write/refresh a CLAUDE.md; /memory (and Settings → "Edit CLAUDE.md…") opens an editor for it at project / local / user scope.
  • Streaming session (experimental) — an opt-in mode (Settings → Debug) that runs one long-lived claude process per chat over streaming I/O instead of one per message — faster turns and groundwork for mid-turn steering. Off by default.
  • In-chat debug log export — the chat's Debug panel now has Export / Clear buttons, and streaming mode logs the same per-event detail as the standard path. Compatible with JetBrains IDEs through 2026.2.

1.2.0

  • Reliable MCP OAuth sign-in — authenticating a remote server now drives an interactive claude in a pseudo-TTY the plugin owns, paced off the screen's actual content (onboarding gates → /mcp → the right server → Authenticate) instead of typing into the IDE terminal on fixed timers. It runs hidden — you just finish in the browser claude opens — and quits claude gracefully so the token is flushed (fixes "the browser said success but it still needs authentication").
  • Authorization type picker — the Add/Edit dialog now has an Authorization selector — No Auth, API Key / Token, or OAuth — and shows only the fields that apply (API token, or OAuth client id / secret / callback port), with Headers available for every type. The type is inferred from the saved config, so it always reflects what's actually stored.
  • OAuth client secret + token auth — confidential OAuth providers (e.g. Google Drive) are supported via a client id + secret (the secret is handed to claude over MCP_CLIENT_SECRET, never written to config); token-based servers (e.g. GitHub) authenticate directly via an Authorization: Bearer header with no browser step.
  • Authenticate All — a one-click action in the MCP manager walks every remote server that needs sign-in, one browser at a time, advancing automatically and reporting an end-of-run summary of what succeeded and what didn't (and why). A per-server watchdog guarantees one misconfigured or stuck server can never block the rest.
  • Clear auth feedback — single and batch attempts now surface a result: ✓ authenticated, or a specific reason (needs an API token, sign-in not completed, menu couldn't be driven) with what to do next. Trying OAuth on a token-only server no longer fails silently.
  • Debug logging + export — an opt-in Debug toggle in Settings records diagnostics (including the MCP auth transcript) to an in-memory buffer; an Export debug log… button (shown only while debug is on) saves it for bug reports. Off by default — nothing is recorded while off.
  • Bug fix: OAuth client id round-trip — a pre-registered OAuth client id / callback port now reloads correctly in the Edit dialog (they're stored nested under oauth in the config, which the reader previously missed).

1.1.0

  • MCP server management UI — a new server icon in the tool-window header (and a Manage MCP Servers… button in Settings) opens a manager that aggregates every MCP server visible to the project: project .mcp.json plus the user and project-local scopes in ~/.claude.json (matched by canonical path, so CLI-added local servers show up). Add, edit, remove and authenticate servers across project / local / user scopes.
  • All transports + live status — stdio (command/args/env) and remote SSE / HTTP (URL/headers, optional OAuth client id + callback port). Connection/auth badges (✓ connected, ✗ failed, ⏸ pending approval, 🔒 needs authentication) come from a health-checked claude mcp list.
  • Authenticate remote MCP servers — for OAuth servers, one click opens an interactive claude terminal and brings up the /mcp screen to sign in; the plugin's -p chat sessions then pick up the stored tokens automatically. (The CLI owns the OAuth browser+callback flow; there is no headless MCP-auth command.)
  • Safe writes — all MCP mutations go through claude mcp add-json / remove rather than hand-editing ~/.claude.json. Using add-json also passes the whole server definition as one JSON argument, sidestepping a variadic-flag pitfall where --header could swallow the URL ("missing required argument 'commandOrUrl'").
  • MCP tool permission grants in chat — when Claude is blocked on an mcp__<server>__<tool> call, the in-chat grant banner now fires and offers the right patterns: allow this exact mcp__server__tool vs allow broad mcp__server (every tool from that server).
  • Settings files editor — a JSON-file icon in the header (and an Edit settings.json… button in Settings) edits Claude Code's own settings.json at project / project-local / global scope, with a structured key/value Form tab and a raw JSON tab. Both are validated as a JSON object before saving; unrelated keys (including the plugin's permission grants in settings.local.json) are preserved.
  • Paste fixes — pasting a URL whose last path segment matches a project filename no longer turns it into a file chip; an absolute path that doesn't exist on disk is no longer silently re-mapped to a same-named project file; and every chip (file chips included) now expands to its underlying text on double-click.

1.0.6

  • Auto-retry on permission grant — clicking "Allow this exact …", "Allow all …", or "Switch to Unrestricted" on a permission-denied banner now stops the in-flight (or already-finished) request, applies the grant, and automatically resends the original prompt with the new permission in place. Previously you had to wait, click Stop, and re-send manually.
  • Failure badges show what actually went wrong — when a tool returns an error, the badge now reads e.g. "✗ failed Bash: java: command not found" instead of a bare "✗ failed". Consecutive failures of the same tool collapse into one line with a "(Nx)" counter so a retrying tool doesn't spam the chat.
  • Plugin version on the Welcome page — the header now reads "Claude Code (v1.0.6)" so it's obvious which build is running. Version is baked in at build time so the plugin no longer touches PluginManagerCore (now @ApiStatus.Internal in 2026.2+ EAP and flagged by the marketplace verifier).
  • Recent chats — a clock-icon dropdown in the tool window header lists past sessions for the current project (kept per-project, capped at 10, 30-day TTL). Click one to reopen the conversation; Claude picks up where it left off via --resume <id>. Each row has inline pencil (rename) and trash (delete) icons; hover highlights the row. Deleting only removes the dropdown entry — Claude's own transcript under ~/.claude/projects is untouched.
  • Full transcript on resume — when you open a recent chat, the previous conversation auto-loads from Claude's local JSONL (no API call, no token cost) and renders inline as proper chat blocks — user bubbles, markdown-rendered assistant replies, code blocks — terminated by an "End of previous history" separator. Reading is free; if the local file is missing, the chat still works (Claude has the conversation server-side).
  • Permission mode auto-applies on resume — whatever permission mode the original session ran with is reapplied as a per-session chip override, so the resumed chat behaves like the original. Global default is untouched.
  • Settings — Model & inference — three new controls:
    • Extended thinking — Off / Low (1k) / Medium (8k) / High (32k). Sets MAX_THINKING_TOKENS on the spawned claude process. Effective on Opus / Sonnet 4.x; other models ignore it.
    • Append system prompt — multi-line text appended to Claude's system prompt every spawn via --append-system-prompt. Use for project conventions, preferred tone, persona instructions.
    • Max agentic turns — spinner cap on the agentic tool-call loop via --max-turns. 0 = unlimited (CLI default).
  • Models catalog with auto-refresh — the model list now updates from a published catalog every 24h (with a bundled offline fallback), so new Claude models become available without a plugin update. Deprecated models render with a (deprecated) suffix and a one-click swap to the recommended replacement when selected. The Refresh catalog button in Settings forces an immediate re-fetch. <synthetic> and similar internal placeholders are filtered out.
  • Settings: model field is no longer free-text — pick from the catalog (or Default for "let Claude Code choose"). Avoids silent typos that produced "exited with code 1" errors. A Clear custom history button wipes the persisted list of model IDs Claude has responded with that aren't in the catalog.
  • Async confirmation dialogs now surface in front of Settings — fix for Refresh catalog where the success notice was appearing behind the modal Settings dialog. Captures the dialog's ModalityState on the EDT and re-uses it on the async callback, so the Messages dialog stacks above.
  • Esc is now the only "stop current request" shortcut — removed the legacy double Cmd+C / Ctrl+C handling everywhere (Welcome page, README, plugin description). Cmd/Ctrl+C in the input area now just copies, never interrupts Claude.

1.0.5

  • Fix-with-Claude intention description added — newer IntelliJ builds require <intentionAction> registrations to ship a description.html plus before/after templates under resources/intentionDescriptions/<ClassName>/. Without them the IDE logged a SEVERE on every load and the intention couldn't appear in the Settings → Editor → Intentions list. Files now included.
  • Plugin-load SEVERE fixed — removed an <add-to-group group-id="Floating.CodeToolbar.Web"> registration that referenced a non-existent action group. Logged a SEVERE error in idea.log on every plugin load (the rest of the plugin still worked). The Edit-with-Claude floating-toolbar registration in Floating.CodeToolbar remains and continues to cover JS/TS via the platform's per-language routing in recent IntelliJ versions.
  • Paste screenshots into the chat — Cmd+V / Ctrl+V (or drag-drop) on a clipboard image now creates an image chip showing the dimensions. The image is saved to a temp PNG and referenced via the CLI's @<path> syntax on submit, so Claude receives it as a multimodal input. Works for screenshots (macOS Cmd+Shift+Ctrl+4, Windows Win+Shift+S), Preview's Edit→Copy, and browser image right-click→Copy.
  • Generate Commit Message: reads selected changes from the dialog — previously the action ran git diff --cached, which could be stale relative to what the user had ticked in the commit dialog (forcing a "refresh" click before generation). Now reads VcsDataKeys.SELECTED_CHANGES directly and diffs exactly those file paths against HEAD; falls back to staged-then-unstaged if no selection is available.
  • Generate Commit Message: better synthesis across multi-file change sets — the prompt now receives a git diff --stat summary alongside the patch, and tells Claude explicitly to find the unifying intent across all files rather than describing the most prominent one.
  • Deprecated API fix — replaced FileChooserDescriptorFactory.createSingleFileDescriptor() with the equivalent FileChooserDescriptor constructor in the Settings → Browse… button. Flagged by the JetBrains plugin verifier; no behaviour change.

1.0.4

  • Windows support — the CLI invocation no longer assumes the Unix script command for pty allocation; on Windows it spawns claude.cmd directly. Mac/Linux behaviour is unchanged. claude resolution layers three strategies because IntelliJ's JVM often inherits a PATH that's missing the user-PATH entries added by the Node.js MSI installer (where %APPDATA%\npm\ normally sits) — meaning a bare claude can be runnable from CMD/PowerShell yet invisible to the plugin: (1) where against the inherited PATH; (2) direct probes of %APPDATA%\npm, %LOCALAPPDATA%\npm, %ProgramFiles%\nodejs; (3) npm config get prefix. Prefers the .cmd extension over the Unix shell-script wrapper that npm also installs. The resolved binary's directory is also prepended to the spawned process's PATH so internal shell-outs from claude.cmd work. Settings → Claude CLI path accepts an absolute path as a manual fallback if auto-detection fails.
  • Permission modes (replaces auto-accept toggle) — Settings → Tools → Claude Code now exposes a permission-mode dropdown: acceptEdits (default, file edits go through, shell commands blocked), bypassPermissions (Claude can run any tool), or plan (read-only). Maps directly to the CLI's --permission-mode. The old binary "auto-accept" toggle pretended an interactive permission flow that the CLI's -p mode doesn't actually support; this replaces it with what the CLI really offers.
  • Permission-blocked hint — when Claude's reply looks like it's been blocked by your current permission mode (e.g. "Could you approve the Write tool…"), an inline hint appears with a clickable link straight to Settings to switch modes.
  • Edit with Claude in the floating toolbar — now for JS/TS too — the JavaScript/TypeScript plugin uses its own Floating.CodeToolbar.Web group separate from the generic one, so the Claude icon was missing on web files. Action now registers to both groups; the keyboard shortcut was unaffected.
  • Deprecated API fix — replaced ReadAction.compute(ThrowableComputable) with Application.runReadAction(Computable) in the chat-input filename resolver. Flagged by the JetBrains plugin verifier as deprecated and slated for removal in a future platform release. No behaviour change.

1.0.3

  • Edit with Claude — select code, hit Cmd+Alt+K / Ctrl+Alt+K (or click the Claude icon in the floating code toolbar, alongside Show Context Actions / Extract / Surround), then type a natural-language instruction. Claude returns the rewrite and a side-by-side diff opens; Accept replaces the selection, Reject discards it. Works in any editor regardless of language.
  • Apply button on chat code blocks — every fenced code block in the Claude chat now has an [apply] link next to [copy]. Select the target code in the active editor, click apply, review the diff, and accept to replace your selection in-place.
  • Generate Commit Message with Claude — new button in the VCS commit dialog toolbar. Reads git diff --cached (falls back to git diff), sends it to Claude, and fills the commit message field with a Conventional Commits-style result.
  • Fix with Claude quick-fix intention — Alt+Enter on any IDE-detected error or warning now offers "Fix with Claude". Sends the offending lines + the inspection message to Claude, shows a diff, applies on accept. Works for any language and any inspection (compiler errors, linter warnings, code-style issues).
  • Expandable paste chips — large-text paste chips can now be double-clicked to expand back into the input. Cursor changes to a pointer and a tooltip reminds you of the gesture; file chips remain non-expandable to keep their path semantics intact.
  • Inline code completion removed — the experimental opt-in was dropped after evaluation: with the CLI-based auth path, latency was 1.5-3s per suggestion vs. sub-200ms for purpose-built FIM models. Will revisit if Anthropic ships a low-latency endpoint.

1.0.2

  • Smart auto-scroll — chat output only follows new messages when you're already at the bottom; if you've scrolled up to read, your position is preserved. A floating "↓ Jump to latest" button appears in the bottom-right when you're scrolled away.
  • File chips in chat input — drag/drop, copy/paste, or paste a path and it becomes a compact 📎 filename chip that expands to the absolute path on submit. Click the ✕ to remove.
  • Smart filename resolution — pasting just a filename (with or without extension) resolves to the project file via FilenameIndex; on macOS, Finder copies are read from NSPasteboard via AppleScript when JBR's clipboard bridge only exposes the bare filename.
  • Large-text paste chips — pasting >250 chars or >3 lines creates a "Pasted #N · X lines" chip instead of cluttering the input. Submitted text uses the full content.
  • Open Claude Session Here — right-click any folder in the project tree to open a new Claude Code session rooted at that folder.
  • Editable model selector — type any model ID in Settings, not just the bundled list; recognized models from sessions are remembered. Adds Opus 4.7 to the bundled list.
  • Better diff summary — Edit results now show ~modified, +added, -removed with proper LCS-based counts instead of overcounting.
  • Tool-aware thinking indicator — shows the running tool name and elapsed seconds while Claude is working.
  • Tool window focus — Send-to-Claude actions now activate the Claude tool window (focusing the input) rather than just showing it.
  • Debug log off by default — checkbox starts unchecked so it doesn't take up space.

1.0.1

  • Explain Folder — right-click any folder in the project tree to get a hierarchical summary of its contents, with breakdowns for each sub-folder up to 2 levels deep
  • File-type agnostic explanations — Explain works on any file type (Dockerfile, YAML, Kubernetes manifests, build files, etc.), not just source code
  • Improved prompts — all right-click action prompts rewritten with structured output format, better guidance for test generation (matches project conventions), and concrete code in refactor/fix results
  • Settings crash fix — fixed a NullPointerException that occurred when opening Settings during plugin unload

1.0.0

  • Console integration — right-click in Run/Debug console to debug exceptions, explain log flows, or send output to Claude
  • Folder-level test generation — generate tests for all source files in a directory (supports 14+ languages)
  • Send to Claude — send selected code, files, or console output as context from any right-click menu
  • Interactive permission prompts — Allow/Deny buttons in the chat panel for Claude's file operations
  • Inline diffs — expandable diff viewers showing old vs. new code for every edit Claude makes
  • Edit consolidation — consecutive edits to the same file are grouped into a single entry with cumulative diffs
  • Thinking display — real-time indicator showing Claude's reasoning when extended thinking is active
  • Debug log panel — collapsible panel for inspecting internal session operations
  • Session auto-naming — sessions are automatically named based on the first message
  • Auto-accept permissions setting — configure whether file operations require manual approval
  • File deletion tracking — detects and displays files deleted via Bash commands
  • Model info in header — active model name shown in each response header

0.1.0

  • Initial release
  • Multi-session chat panel with Claude Code CLI
  • Right-click actions: Explain, Refactor, Generate Tests, Fix
  • Editor and project tree context menu integration
  • Markdown rendering with syntax highlighting
  • Clickable file links and changed files summary
  • Copy/edit buttons on messages and code blocks
  • Model selection and cost tracking
  • Welcome page with feature overview

idea-plugin.name: Agent Dock
idea-plugin.description:
Agent Dock brings AI coding agents into a unified GUI that follows the active JetBrains IDE theme.

Built-in AI agent integrations:

  • Claude Code
  • Codex
  • Cursor
  • GitHub Copilot
  • Junie
  • Google Antigravity
  • Grok Build
  • Kilo
  • Kimi Code
  • OpenCode
  • Qoder

Any other ACP-compatible agent can be added through the custom configuration option.

Features:

  • Manage integrated agents: install, update, remove, log in, and log out inside the plugin.
  • Communication with AI agents through ACP (Agent Client Protocol) in a GUI.
  • Connect any ACP-compatible agent using a custom configuration.
  • View tool calls, thinking, terminal commands, plans, file edits, and diffs.
  • Review, accept, or revert agent file changes.
  • Receive audio notifications for chat and agent events.
  • Use slash commands and reference project files through @ mentions.
  • Add code selections and file references from the editor or project view.
  • Paste images into chat. Preview pasted and agent-generated images full-screen.
  • View live token quota and context usage in the chat input.
  • Use voice input with GPT Transcriber, Gemini 3.5 Transcribe, or local Whisper.
  • Continue chats in the IDE terminal.
  • Find, reopen, and rename saved chats, or delete them individually or in bulk.
  • Switch agents within a chat while preserving context.
  • Fork chats from any point.
  • Configure MCP servers for additional tools and resources.
  • Save and insert reusable prompts.
  • Queue prompts while an agent is working and schedule them to be sent at a chosen time.
  • Manage system instructions for agent sessions.
  • Generate Git commit messages from current changes.

Requirements:

  • JetBrains IDE 2026.2+ with Web Browser (JCEF) support.
  • Some agents use JetBrains IDE terminal for authentication.
  • On macOS and Linux, installing some agents requires curl and tar.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Added chat pinning.
  • Improved the display of agent tool calls.
  • Plugin management sections now open in pop-up windows.
  • Redesigned the sidebar.
  • Minor bug fixes and UI refinements.

idea-plugin.name: Ccode Stats
idea-plugin.description:
ccidea — Claude Code usage inside your IDE

Reads Claude Code's local JSONL logs and surfaces token usage, cost, and the 5-hour Anthropic billing block burn rate inside the IDE — no remote API calls except fetching the LiteLLM pricing JSON (cached locally with an offline fallback).

  • Daily / Monthly / Sessions / Blocks tables with full input/output/cache breakdown
  • Stacked-bar charts (Lets-Plot) and a burn-rate time series with ETA-to-limit reference line
  • Live 5-hour billing block tracker on the status bar — % used, time left, cost
  • Cost computed from LiteLLM pricing JSON, with 1-hour cache priced at 2× the 5-min rate
  • Pattern recognition: top-N expensive sessions, model cache-hit ratio, hour-of-day heatmap, recommendations
  • Notifications at 80%, 95%, and 10 minutes before block reset
  • Auto refresh every 30s, file-watcher nudges between ticks

Read-only — never modifies your ~/.claude directory.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
4.2.0 — 性能优化

  • 修复 EDT 卡顿：`autoRowHeights` 改为数据驱动行高计算，彻底避免 `BasicHTML.createHTMLView` 在 EDT 上的 HTML 解析开销。
  • `AggregationService` 聚合结果缓存化，EDT 直接读缓存，不再在主线程做全量遍历。
  • `BlockService.ingest` 改为二分查找插入，`burnRate` 改为二分定位窗口，消除全量排序和全量 filter。
  • `detectedTokenLimit` / `detectedCostLimit` 结果缓存，仅在数据变更时重算。
  • `ChartPanel` 改用调用方传入的轻量 dataKey 去重，不再序列化 Plot spec 字符串做 hashCode。
  • `readNewLines` 改为 `FileChannel` + 手动字节扫描，正确支持 UTF-8 多字节字符，精确追踪字节偏移。
  • `CcideaNotifier.byBlock` 定期清理旧 block 状态，防止内存无限增长。
  • `CcideaStatusBarWidget` 删除重复的独立轮询定时器，改为只订阅 `CcideaBus` 消息。
  • `LiveTab.onRefresh` 和 `QuotaPanel` 计算全部移到后台线程，EDT 只做 UI 更新。
  • `LiveMessageTableModel` 预计算每行 cost，避免表格渲染时反复调用 `PricingService.costFor()`。
  • `seen` LRU 去重集上限从 50 万降至 5 万，减少约 28 MB 峰值内存。
  • `PollerService.dispose()` 正确关闭 `WatchService`，防止插件卸载时后台线程泄漏。

idea-plugin.name: Pushkin Commit AI
idea-plugin.description: Generate Git commit messages from selected changes using OpenAI-compatible AI services. Pushkin Commit AI works in the JetBrains Commit window and lets you use OpenAI, DeepSeek, self-hosted models, or any custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint instead of consuming JetBrains AI quota.

idea-plugin.name: velk

Open the velk terminal AI harness in a JetBrains terminal panel.

Tools → velk: Open REPL (or Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-A → "velk") spawns a terminal running the velk binary in the project's working directory.

Configure the binary path under Settings → Tools → velk if velk is not on PATH.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.0.1

  • Initial release. velk: Open REPL action launches the velk binary in a JetBrains terminal panel.

idea-plugin.name: Codex Assistant
idea-plugin.description:
Run Codex CLI from inside JetBrains IDE via the built-in terminal.

How to Open

  1. Shortcut: Press Ctrl+Shift+X or option+command+X to open the terminal in your current project.
  2. Toolbar: Click the icon in the top toolbar.

Note: If a session is already running, you cannot open a new one.

Sending References (Send File Path To Codex Terminal)

  1. Code: Highlight code and press Ctrl+Alt+X (or use the right-click menu) to send the file path and line numbers.
  2. Full Files: If no text is selected, the current file path is sent.
  3. Files/Folders: Right-click an item in the Project View and select "Copy to Codex Terminal" to send the path.
  4. Multiple Items: You can select several items to send their paths separated by spaces.

Settings

  1. Location: Go to Settings → Tools → Codex Assistant.
  2. Codex Executable Path: The default setting is "codex." If the file is installed in a location not included in your system PATH, you should enter the full absolute path here.
  3. Additional CLI Arguments: This field is empty by default but allows you to add specific flags to the "codex" command for every execution.
  4. Request Confirmation Before Code Changes: This is enabled by default. It automatically adds a security flag that requires your approval before any untrusted code modifications are made.

idea-plugin.name: Whisper Speech to Text
idea-plugin.description:
Voice-to-text dictation for JetBrains IDEs using OpenAI Whisper. Speak instead of type, anywhere a caret is focused.

Features

  • Three transcription backends: local (whisper.cpp, fully offline), OpenAI Whisper API, Groq (Whisper Large V3).
  • Three dictation modes: Dictate (raw transcription), Code (spoken punctuation mapped to symbols, filler words removed), Command (formatted as a coding instruction for AI chat).
  • Inserts at the editor caret. Falls back to clipboard paste for tool windows, terminals, and external apps.
  • Multilingual: supports the languages Whisper supports (en, fr, de, es, it, pt, ja, zh, and more).
  • Local backend runs entirely on your machine. No audio leaves your computer unless you select a cloud backend.

Quick start

  1. Install sox (brew install sox) or ffmpeg for audio capture.
  2. Open any project (Whisper detects missing setup and shows a prompt). Click Run Local Setup to install whisper.cpp and a model (~150 MB), or Open Settings to configure an OpenAI/Groq API key.
  3. Press Cmd+M (macOS) or Ctrl+M (Windows/Linux) to start recording. Press again to stop and insert the transcription.

Configuration

Settings -> Tools -> Whisper. Configure backend, dictation mode, language, API keys, and recording tool.

Source code, issue tracker, and documentation: github.com/roussi/whisper
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.1

  • Extend IDE compatibility to build 262.*.

1.1.0

  • New Whisper tool window on the right sidebar — embeds the full settings UI plus a quick "Toggle Recording" button. No need to open Settings every time.
  • Redesigned settings UI: card-style backend picker (Local / OpenAI / Groq) with Ready/Setup status badge per card.
  • Local backend: install whisper.cpp + model directly from Settings (no separate action), live status, custom-binary override.
  • Cloud backends: masked API key fields with inline Test button to verify the key against the provider.
  • Audio section: detected sox/ffmpeg paths shown inline; install hint when neither is present.
  • Language picker is now a dropdown of common languages (was free-text).
  • Hotkey reminder shown directly in Settings.

1.0.0

  • Initial release - voice-to-text dictation via whisper.cpp / OpenAI / Groq.

idea-plugin.name: Capybara AI Coding Assistant
idea-plugin.description:
English

Capybara AI Coding Assistant is an open-source AI coding assistant for IntelliJ IDEA, powered by the OpenCode V2 server. It brings streaming conversations, IDE context, file operations, model configuration and native IDEA workflows into one focused tool window.

Features

  • Streaming AI Chat — real-time Markdown, reasoning, tool groups, questions, todos and context usage.
  • OpenCode V2 Models — configured providers, custom models, reasoning variants, multimodal models and usage details.
  • IDEA Native Integration — editor context, file and symbol navigation, native modal diffs, file refresh and save dialogs.
  • Safe Approval Modes — request approval, auto-approve or full access for file, command and network operations.
  • Skills, Plugins, MCP and Memory — manage OpenCode capabilities from responsive settings pages.
  • IDEA Session Tabs — native conversation tabs with rename, overflow navigation and tab-only close.

Getting Started

  1. Install OpenCode and start its local server.
  2. Open the Capybara AI Assistant tool window from IntelliJ IDEA.
  3. Configure a provider and model in Settings → Models, then start a conversation.
  4. Use the IDEA context menu to explain selected code or attach files and folders to a prompt.

Requirements: IntelliJ IDEA 2023.2 or later and a locally available OpenCode V2 server.

简体中文

水豚 AI 编程助手是一款开源的 IntelliJ IDEA AI 编程插件，基于 OpenCode V2 服务。 它将流式对话、IDE 上下文、文件操作、模型配置和 IDEA 原生工作流集中到一个专注的工具窗口中。

核心功能

  • 流式 AI 对话 — 实时 Markdown、思考过程、工具调用、问答卡片、任务清单和上下文用量展示。
  • OpenCode V2 模型 — 支持供应商、自定义模型、思考档位、多模态能力和本轮 Token 用量。
  • IDEA 原生集成 — 支持编辑器上下文、文件与符号跳转、原生 Diff、文件刷新和保存对话框。
  • 安全审批模式 — 对文件、命令和联网操作提供请求批准、替我审批和完全访问选项。
  • 技能、插件、MCP 与记忆 — 在响应式设置页面中管理 OpenCode 能力。
  • IDEA 会话标签 — 支持会话改名、标签溢出导航和仅关闭标签，不会删除或终止会话。

快速开始

  1. 安装 OpenCode 并启动本地服务。
  2. 在 IntelliJ IDEA 中打开水豚 AI 助手工具窗口。
  3. 在设置 → 模型中配置供应商和模型，然后开始对话。
  4. 使用 IDEA 右键菜单解释选中代码，或将文件、文件夹作为附件加入提示词。

运行要求：IntelliJ IDEA 2023.2 或更高版本，以及本地可访问的 OpenCode V2 服务。

Open Source / 开源项目： Gitee · GitHub · MIT License

Keywords: Claude, Claude Code, Codex, OpenAI, OpenCode, Gemini, DeepSeek, Anthropic, AI Coding, AI Coding Assistant, Code Generation, Code Review, Code Explanation, Code Refactoring, IntelliJ IDEA, JetBrains, MCP, Skills, Agent, Local AI, Developer Tools
idea-plugin.change-notes:
3.0.5

  • 安全安装：一键安装与更新改为在隔离目录下载并验证，通过后才切换插件使用的 OpenCode，不再覆盖正在运行的全局 CLI。
  • 故障恢复：修复 Windows 下 npm postinstall 卡住后破坏现有 OpenCode 启动文件的问题；失败或超时会保留旧版本。
  • 状态识别：区分“未安装”和“已安装但无法启动”，并提供明确的一键修复入口和下载状态提示。
  • 进程清理：安装超时时会完整终止 npm 子进程树，避免后台安装长期占用文件。
  • Safe installation: One-click install and update now download and verify OpenCode in isolation before switching the plugin to the new binary.
  • Recovery: Failed or timed-out installs preserve the working version instead of corrupting a running global CLI on Windows.
  • Status detection: The UI now distinguishes a missing installation from a damaged executable and exposes a dedicated repair action.
  • Process cleanup: Timed-out npm installs terminate their complete child-process tree.

idea-plugin.name: HelionCoder
idea-plugin.description:
HelionCoder brings the local HelionCoder CLI into JetBrains IDEs with a dark, VS Code-style assistant panel, editor-aware context, and real IDE integrations.

Use it to chat with HelionCoder from inside the IDE, attach files, folders, selections, terminal context, and images, stream tool steps and thinking output, review generated file changes, and jump directly from assistant results back to source files.

The plugin also provides all-language editor completion through HelionCoder ghost text suggestions. When a HelionCoder suggestion is visible, press Tab to accept it; otherwise Tab keeps the IDE's normal indentation, template, and completion behavior.

  • Local CLI execution with project workspace context.
  • Dark assistant tool window with streaming responses and control prompts.
  • File, workspace, image, selection, and terminal attachments.
  • Diff preview, accept, and reject flows for generated changes.
  • Model selection and refresh from HelionCoder/OpenAI-compatible API configuration.
  • Inline ghost-text completion for local text files across languages.

idea-plugin.name: Postman MCP Server
idea-plugin.description:
Connect any AI agent installed in your IDE to your Postman workspace via the Postman MCP Server.

Getting started: Install the plugin, enter your Postman API key in the prompt that appears, then accept the IDE's prompt to enable the MCP server. That's it — no manual config files, no restarts.

To update your API key later, use Tools → Update Postman API Key or edit it in Settings → Tools → Postman MCP Server.

Supported AI agents (all share the same MCP config automatically):

  • JetBrains AI Assistant
  • GitHub Copilot (JetBrains plugin)
  • Junie, Codex, Claude — and any future JetBrains AI agent

Once connected, your AI agent can:

  • Manage Postman collections, workspaces, and environments
  • Run API tests and generate client code
  • Search public and private API definitions
  • Create and update Postman specs from code

Requirements: IntelliJ IDEA 2025.1 or later with at least one supported AI agent plugin installed.

idea-plugin.name: AI File Opener
idea-plugin.description:
Automatically opens files in the editor as an AI coding agent works on them.

When an external AI tool (Claude Code, Aider, or any other agent) edits or creates a source file on disk, this plugin detects the change via IntelliJ's Virtual File System and opens the file in the editor — so you can follow along in real time without manually navigating to each file.

No setup required beyond installing the plugin. Works standalone — no companion plugin or IDE integration needed.

Compatible with all JetBrains IDEs (IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, etc.). Only source files within the open project are opened; build artifacts, vendor directories, and .git folders are ignored.

idea-plugin.name: OpenCode UI (unofficial)
idea-plugin.description:
OpenCode UI (unofficial) brings local OpenCode AI workflows into IDEs with chat, context management, image generation, and bundled backend binaries.

概览

OpenCode UI (unofficial) 是一个将本地 OpenCode AI 工作流带入 IDE 的非官方插件。你可以直接在编辑器中处理聊天、上下文整理与图片生成任务，而不必在 IDE、终端和外部工具之间来回切换。

核心能力

  • 在 IDE 中直接生成图片，把图片生成工作流放进日常编码环境
  • 基于已有图片继续编辑，便于迭代 UI 草图、素材和设计方案
  • 在聊天界面和插件预览中直接查看生成结果，减少来回切换
  • 将生成结果保存到项目文件，便于继续引用、提交或协作
  • 支持将文件拖拽到上下文中，快速补充任务背景
  • 支持通过命令或快捷操作把当前文件、已打开文件和选中代码加入上下文
  • 提供独立输入区，便于整理、修改和扩展提示词

生图配置要点

  • 需要先在 OpenCode 中配置支持图片生成的 provider / model，相关能力才会在工作流中可用
  • 图片生成功能是否可用，取决于当前 OpenCode 模型配置是否支持对应能力
  • 如果要基于已有图片继续编辑，需要先提供现有图片作为输入
  • 生成结果会进入当前工作流，并保存到项目中的 .opencode/generated-images/，便于后续继续引用

例如，如果你使用 OpenAI-compatible 图片接口，可以参考下面这组最小示例键值：

  • provider.openai.options.baseURL: 你的图片接口地址
  • provider.openai.options.apiKey: 你的接口密钥
  • provider.openai.models["gpt-image-2"].limit.context: 128000
  • provider.openai.models["gpt-image-2"].limit.input: 128000
  • provider.openai.models["gpt-image-2"].limit.output: 32000
  • provider.openai.models["gpt-image-2"].options.imageApi: openai-compatible
  • provider.openai.models["gpt-image-2"].options.defaultForImageGeneration: true

新的 provider model marker 优先于旧顶层 image_model 字段。没有任何启用（值为 true）的 marker 时才会回退到旧字段；值为 false 的 marker 不启用对应节点，但如果仍保留旧字段且没有任何值为 true 的 marker，仍会回退到旧字段，且运行时不会发出警告。迁移时先添加 marker 并验证定制版，再删除顶层字段。官方版只保证严格加载该配置，不承诺 generate_image 功能可用。

重要说明

这是非官方插件。请只安装一个 OpenCode IDE 变体，避免重复功能或行为冲突。

标准版说明

当前发布的是 standard variant。它会为受支持平台内置 OpenCode backend，并在本地运行时自动启动。

适用人群

这个插件面向已经在使用 OpenCode 的开发者，适合希望留在 IDE 内完成聊天、上下文管理、图片生成与本地 AI 编码工作的用户。
idea-plugin.change-notes:
更新内容

v26.6.800

Provider 与模型配置

  • 新增 Provider 设置页，可在 IDE WebGUI 中集中查看和编辑 Provider 的接口地址、API 密钥与模型白名单，减少手动修改配置文件的成本。
  • 支持从远程配置一键覆盖或合并更新 Provider；覆盖更新会真正替换全局配置，同时保留同名 Provider 的本地接口地址与 API 密钥，兼顾配置同步与本地密钥安全。
  • 模型白名单提供自绘下拉选择器，并从本地/内置模型目录读取候选模型，不受当前白名单过滤影响。
  • 已加入白名单的模型会自动从候选中排除；仍支持手动输入自定义模型，并过滤不可用的废弃模型。

对话稳定性与错误恢复

  • 改进 OpenAI Responses API 流式错误处理，对临时性上游错误进行重试，减少网络抖动或 Provider 短暂异常导致的对话中断。
  • 更准确识别 context_too_large 与 context_length_exceeded 等上下文超限错误，保留上游返回的错误码和提示，并转换为明确的上下文超限提示，避免被误判为普通可重试错误。
  • 过滤 Responses 流中的 Chat Completions 兼容帧与无效占位内容，降低重复事件和空内容对流式消息处理的干扰。

快捷操作与日常效率

  • 新增“工作交接”快捷短语，便于快速生成可交接的上下文说明，提升跨会话、跨任务协作效率。

idea-plugin.name: Brogrammer
idea-plugin.description: Brogrammer — MCP context backend for Claude Code. Exposes project context (PSI index, semantic search, memories, rules, active editor state, commit history) over MCP so Claude Code can drive the IDE as its context engine.

idea-plugin.name: Walkthrough
idea-plugin.description:
Walkthrough is an IntelliJ IDEA plugin for showing inline guided walkthroughs anchored to specific lines of code. It renders a styled popup near a target line, keeps a connector pointing at that line, and lets the reader step through a sequence of walkthrough items. Typical uses include codebase tours, onboarding new contributors, and AI-driven code explanations.

The plugin also exposes a show_walkthrough_items MCP tool so LLM-driven agents can drive walkthroughs programmatically. The popup UI is built with JetBrains Compose (Jewel) and supports Markdown content, optional file and line navigation, and previous/next step navigation.

idea-plugin.name: AiBridge
idea-plugin.description:
AiBridge turns your JetBrains IDE into a local AI gateway. It exposes the language models available via GitHub Copilot (and other providers) as a standard OpenAI-compatible REST API.

Features:

  • Streaming Support: Full support for Server-Sent Events (SSE).
  • Tool Window: Monitor traffic, see active models, and control the server.
  • Local Security: Authenticate local requests with a custom bearer token.

idea-plugin.name: GitHub Copilot CLI Launcher
idea-plugin.description:
Launches the GitHub Copilot CLI (copilot) in a dedicated tool window docked to the right side of the IDE.

Adds three entry points:

  • A Copilot CLI tool window on the right (click the stripe button to open it).
  • Tools | Launch GitHub Copilot CLI menu action.
  • A Copilot icon on the bottom-right status bar (single-click to launch).

If the CLI is not installed, the plugin opens a terminal and runs the official install command for your platform (winget install GitHub.Copilot on Windows, curl -fsSL https://gh.io/copilot-install | bash on macOS / Linux).

The plugin also implements the Copilot CLI /ide connection: while a project is open it advertises the IDE to the CLI so the CLI can read diagnostics and the current selection, and show proposed edits as accept/reject diffs inside the IDE.

idea-plugin.name: AI Commit Message Generator
idea-plugin.description:

  • Offers localized validation, failure notifications, streaming updates, hover-to-stop generation control, and sensitive-path filtering.

根据 JetBrains Commit 工具窗口中已选择的文件，生成更完整、更规范的 Git commit message。

idea-plugin.name: Composite Build Manager

idea-plugin.name: Deepseek-Sync
idea-plugin.description:
Bring DeepSeek Web Chat into your IDE.
