idea-plugin.change-notes:
v2.2.5

A stable patch with a broad correctness sweep. The bytecode VM and the WASM

runtime gained a long run of TclOO and command-lifecycle fixes, the refactor

engine now reads variables and command boundaries the way the segmenter does,

and # noqa is finally honoured the same way everywhere. The language server

also stops outliving the editor that started it.

New features

  • iRule translation to F5 Distributed Cloud renders pasteable **XC Console

documents**, derives DNS-1035-safe object names, and ships the accompanying

docs set.

  • The BIG-IP object-graph, embedded-rule, minimiser and partition-rename

commands, and tcl-lsp.xcTranslate, are dispatched by the language server,

so every editor gets them rather than only the ones with bespoke wiring.

  • The workspace scan's file budget is a setting, so a large monorepo can raise

it instead of silently indexing a truncated workspace.

  • The registry answers which substitutions a call performs, and the Spec Studio

forms expose the resolver.

  • IRULE5001 honours the debug gate its message has always promised, and stays

off bodies that always run.

Improvements

  • # noqa is honoured by diag, lint and validate through one shared

helper; disable=* works on an abstaining document; and a quick-fix is no

longer offered for a check a noqa already silences. A marker must be a real

# noqa, not the bare word appearing in prose.

  • The CLI reports the source-text findings the editor publishes, so the two

surfaces agree.

  • SpecTcl corpus analysis batches synthetic calls, parallelises independent

overlays and shares analyser and optimiser compilation units; SslicTcl

consolidates its certificate metadata probes.

  • Comment and documentation prose across the tree now states what the code does

and why, rather than how it came to be, with UK spelling throughout —

including the W307 diagnostic text and the Spec Studio callback-taint help.

Bug fixes

  • The language server exits within a bounded grace once its session is over and

runs its exit watchdog on an OS thread, instead of leaving a tcl-lsp-server

process behind after the editor closes.

  • It no longer waits for the workspace index while holding the document map,

and refreshes every locked workspace when a dependency changes.

  • A spec-pack directory outside the workspace is watched by base URI rather than

an absolute glob. The old pattern was matched against the workspace instead,

which made eglot watch every directory in the project until it ran out of file

descriptors and failed to start.

  • Generating a deeply nested dict's string representation no longer recurses

once per level, so a dict built through {*} argument expansion cannot

overflow the native stack.

  • A long sweep of TclOO and command-lifecycle correctness in the bytecode VM and

the runtime: identity preserved across namespace generations and command

moves, retirement phased and qualified by generation, deferred tailcall

activations installed, command generations re-resolved after callbacks, stable

variable cell identity, dict info, array get element read traces, hidden

command execution traced, byte-valued script completions preserved, and the

error stack retained across an explicit info.

  • The refactor engine classifies extract-proc variables at the frame boundary

and over the whole statement tree, keeps the reads a substituting command

makes, reads a braced word as the literal it is, resolves inline-variable uses

inside command substitutions, takes extract-variable boundaries from the

segmenter, and guards inline-proc against a body's nested statements.

  • The optimiser stops O107 emptying complexity-guarded bodies, scopes

runtime-selected frame opacity to its own frame, and walks lowered eval and

uplevel bodies for binding effects.

  • subst's switches are read only through the registry, and the binary field

grammar has a single owner gated per release.

  • f5-query names the rustls crypto provider per ClientConfig rather than

relying on a process-wide default.

  • The Sublime plugin is held to its 3.8 host in the formatter as well as the

plugin, and the TMM shim patchlevel is restored.

  • The GitHub Pages deploy builds again: a helper left ungated after the x509

caveats were removed was dead code in the report-WASM build, which denies

warnings.

  • W218's padding is repaired.

v2.2.4

This stable patch is mostly the JetBrains plugin. Three defects made it

largely unusable — Tcl files opened as plain black text, the Compiler

Explorer never opened at all, and the settings page could neither scroll nor

fit its own contents — and all three are fixed. The explorer's linear views

also gained real editor tabs, and the plugin now tells the truth about which

language-server features a JetBrains IDE actually asks for.

Breaking changes

  • The JetBrains plugin now requires IntelliJ 2025.3 or newer. Semantic

highlighting is the reason: it is the only language-server capability the

platform makes opt-in, and taking that opt-in requires building against

2024.3 at minimum, while moving off the getters deprecated since 2025.2

requires 2025.3. Users on 2024.1 through 2025.2 keep the version they have

and stop receiving updates.

New features

  • Compiler Explorer views open in ordinary editor tabs. Open in editor

puts the current view in a read-only tab where find, folding and the colour

scheme all work, and moving the caret through it reveals the matching source

span. The CFG, WASM and optimiser-diff panes stay in the tool window, where

their edges and connectors are drawn rather than written.

  • The JetBrains settings page gained the optimiser profile selector it

never had, alongside a link that hands every per-code choice back to the

chosen profile.

  • JetBrains diagnostics now carry their code, whether they are an optimiser

rewrite or a defect, and what accepting a quick fix would write — the

problems view previously showed only the message.

Bug fixes

  • Tcl files are syntax-highlighted in JetBrains again. The grammar shipped in

the plugin but nothing registered it with the IDE.

  • The JetBrains Compiler Explorer opens. Its webview was missing from every

published plugin: the build extracted it on a best-effort basis and

swallowed the failure, so the plugin shipped without it. The extraction is

now a hard build failure.

  • The JetBrains settings page scrolls, and its checkboxes reflow to the

window instead of running off the right edge.

  • Semantic highlighting refreshes when a spec pack changes. Editing a pack

updated diagnostics and hover but left the colours stale until the buffer

was touched.

  • Editor navigation from the Compiler Explorer lands on the right character

in files containing non-ASCII text. Explorer ranges were byte offsets fed

to editors that count UTF-16, which agreed only for ASCII.

  • A JetBrains IDE no longer force-enables optimisations the chosen profile

disables. The plugin sent every per-code toggle as an explicit "on", which

overrode the profile — so suggestions the default profile suppresses, such

as constant propagation, appeared anyway.

Improvements

  • The VS Code extension and the JetBrains plugin are each about 24 MB

smaller. Both bundled a second code editor and a WebAssembly language

server that neither has loaded since they began using the host IDE's own

editor.

  • The optimiser profile list is generated for every editor from one

definition, so a profile cannot exist in one editor and not another.

  • The JetBrains settings page, README and marketplace description now mark

the features no JetBrains IDE requests, and note the IDE version that

brings each of the remaining ones.

  • Visible spec selection in the registry is faster.

Security and maintenance

  • Code-scanning findings resolved.
  • Continuous integration splits the language-server end-to-end suite across

workers, skips work unaffected by a change, and reuses a green pull-request

result when a release tag points at the same tree.

v2.2.3

This stable patch completes the editor rollout that was blocked during 2.2.2,

removes a whole-server didOpen publication wedge, and includes the compiler,

runtime, Spec Studio, and CI fixes made since that tag.

Reliability and editor delivery

  • Live document publication no longer holds the edit-order or document locks

while waiting for Salsa or the workspace index. Generation-checked,

revision-tagged publication now cancels stale work and rolls back only its

own obsolete index replacement, keeping unrelated requests responsive and

preventing stale spans from crossing document revisions.

  • The native VS Code extension suite now has deterministic coverage for the

didOpen contention that wedged 2.2.2, including superseding edits, closes,

dialect changes, index readers, rehoming, deletion, and workspace-symbol

races.

  • JetBrains settings generation gives every diagnostic section a unique Kotlin

panel variable, restoring the plugin build and marketplace publication.

  • Browser-host and native extension tests, front-end package gates, runner

watchdogs, and targeted Rust smoke selection are more deterministic and

cheaper to run.

Compiler and runtime correctness

  • Word values now retain the distinction between source spelling and evaluated

value. Escaped substitution markers remain data, braced bracket text remains

literal, and live unbraced substitutions in switch subjects and patterns

contribute their variable and command-binding effects before dispatch.

  • Nested substitutions in assignments and other word-valued operands now

invalidate the right compiler facts without evaluating a word twice.

  • Compiled Tcl units are revalidated after command mutation, and procedure

bodies can be installed and dispatched as native WASM functions through the

shared runtime table while preserving Tcl frame, result, depth, and error

semantics.

  • Rename, trace, coroutine, child-interpreter, namespace teardown, welded

quote, and numeric-tower behaviour move closer to the corresponding C Tcl

releases.

Spec Studio and SpecTcl

  • Spec Studio now treats packs as the top-level unit of work, supports several

open commands, provides a focus-following documentation dock and setting

examples, and exports the complete pack and generated Rust/stub files in one

operation.

  • Open .tclspec documents receive declaration outlines, durable loader

notices, formatting coverage, include links, and spelling quick fixes from

the same registry-backed language services used by the Studio.

  • Exhaustive Rust and SpecTcl rendering still checks all 46,722

dialect/command comparisons, but deduplicates shared immutable specs and

batched evaluator work, reducing the two focused sweeps by roughly 87% and

83% in the recorded warm runs.

Security and maintenance

  • Editor webviews validate message origins and keep paths out of shell command

construction; uploaded report paths are contained and closed correctly.

  • Dependency advisories were resolved, release-token scope was narrowed, and

generated or vendored JavaScript is excluded from duplicate CodeQL scans.

v2.2.2

This stable update adds first-class SslicTcl authoring, restores the native

container workflow, advances Tcl-to-WASM execution, and fixes parser,

analysis, runtime, and editor integration defects found after 2.2.1.

New features

  • .sslictcl TLS declarations are now a first-class authoring format. The

server detects the extension or header and provides vocabulary-aware

completion, hover, signature help, semantic tokens, folding, document

symbols, and ranged SSLIC* diagnostics in editors and tcl diag. The

loader supports the complete version 1 vocabulary, deterministic round

trips, and separate policy evaluation without executing declaration files

or retained predicate scripts.

  • tcl pkg discover finds statically resolvable package require calls,

reports dynamic and conditional cases for review, and can add proven

dependencies to tclpkg.tcl with --add.

  • tcl docker now generates Debian-based Dockerfiles that install Tcl, the

native tcl CLI, and locked packages without Python. Release binaries are

selected by architecture and verified against SHA256SUMS; Alpine is

rejected when the generated image would require an unavailable musl build.

  • The compiler and Rust WASM runtime gain runtime ABI v2 and proof-driven

native lowering for the straight-line and expression/control-flow tiers.

The compwasm and explore commands expose semantic code-generation

passes through --codegen-passes, and Compiler Explorer can toggle and

display the same registry-backed pass set.

  • A C Tcl extension shim lets trusted host code run commands written against

the supported object, result, conversion, and command-registration subset

of the C Tcl API on the project engines without rewriting those commands.

Improvements

  • JimTcl is represented as a resolved dialect profile with its own command,

expression, number, escape, and release surfaces instead of being treated

as an alias for a Tcl release.

  • SpecTcl 2.0 environment bodies are evaluated as scripts, so variables and

loops can generate rows. Bundled EDA packs now own their environment

declarations, and restyle directives resolve those environments through

the same central profile catalogue.

  • Binary extensions can declare packages they load implicitly, such as Tk,

through # tcl-lsp: package … provides …, [packages.provides], or the

matching VS Code setting. Package availability, completion, hover, version

checks, and diagnostics all consume the declared dependency graph.

  • Resource-scoped package, BIG-IP version, and target settings now resolve

field by field for each workspace folder and reach every analysis path,

including recovery, disk indexing, re-indexing, fix-all, and unindexed

buffers.

  • VS Code and JetBrains can associate file extensions declared by loaded

SpecTcl packs at runtime. JetBrains also supports the 2026.2 JCEF layout.

  • Sublime is now a lightweight Package Control LSP helper using Sublime's

built-in Tcl syntax, while Zed is an LSP-only extension that finds or

downloads the matching native server.

  • Disk re-indexing no longer holds the document lock. Spec Studio reuses one

source index, generated files retain their timestamps when unchanged, and

build and CI caches track the source inputs that actually affect outputs.

Bug fixes

  • Command and word boundaries, word substitutions, parse-error cuts, and

incremental reparse decisions now come from shared lexer/segmenter owners.

This fixes welded close-braces, stray closers, incomplete input, quoted and

braced word distinctions, and substitutions nested at arbitrary depth.

  • The Rust runtime parses all words in a command before substituting any of

them, matching Tcl evaluation order, and improves numeric-tower, variable,

trace, rename, interpreter, namespace, array, and completion-code behaviour.

  • SSA, taint, and shimmer analysis now see reads inside nested command

substitutions, preserve compatible numeric representations, and distinguish

integer-only operators from general arithmetic. This closes diagnostics

gaps where bracing or another substitution level previously hid a real

read.

  • Spec Studio no longer treats a word left outside a declaration block as an

executable program.

v2.2.1

This stable update broadens Linux compatibility and hardens the Rust runtime,

language intelligence, and editor delivery introduced in 2.2.0.

Linux portability

  • The prebuilt x86_64 and aarch64 GNU/Linux binaries now target a

GLIBC_2.28 ABI floor. Release CI builds them natively in UBI 8 and rejects

any newer symbol imports before publishing.

  • RISC-V uses Ubuntu 22.04's maintained packaged cross-toolchain and a

GLIBC_2.35 floor. EL8 did not ship RISC-V, so this keeps the toolchain

minimal without inventing an unsupported 2.28 sysroot.

  • Release CI starts the exact x86_64 release server across maintained Ubuntu,

Debian, EL8/Oracle Linux, Amazon Linux, openSUSE, Fedora, and Arch containers.

All four Linux programs (tcl-lsp-server, tcl-mcp, tcl, and f5-query)

are checked at the producer and again after artifact fan-in.

  • The build uses current Rust plus ordinary GCC/binutils: no Zig toolchain,

downloaded libc, or statically bundled musl. Programs continue to use the

host's maintained glibc and receive its security updates normally.

  • Alpine and other non-glibc systems remain source-build targets. The

separately published WASI server is unchanged and provides a libc-independent

option for hosts that choose a WebAssembly runtime.

The portability change adds 29,328 bytes to the raw x86_64 server compared

with the former newest-glibc build. The paired Linux x64 VSIX grows by 12,654

bytes (0.024%). It adds no bytes to WASI or browser-WASM artifacts. In focused

measurements the glibc 2.28 build remained within noise of the newer-glibc

build, while the rejected static-musl experiment made the cold workspace scan

more than ten times slower.

Tcl runtime and conformance

  • TclVM namespace and ensemble behavior now preserves live token state and

matches Tcl's command lifecycles more closely, including variable homes and

pair-valued array access.

  • Real Tcl 9.0.4 startup, package paths, and Tcltest loading were repaired and

moved behind a focused conformance runner shared by the supported engines.

  • Platform bootstrap, TclOO information/property dispatch, core grammar, and

Tcl 9 array-index validation now use their central semantic owners rather

than parallel implementations.

Language intelligence and dialects

  • Signature help no longer leaks from procedure parameter lists into procedure

bodies.

  • Inherited TclOO callback captures honor effective visibility, and the

registry's callback inventory now fails when authored coverage is silently

downgraded.

  • iRulesLX navigation follows literal ILX::call and ILX::notify method

names through ILXServer.addMethod, declared plugin workspaces, and their

JavaScript definitions.

  • Registry result typing can derive a type from the call itself. Dialect and

SpecTcl availability now use explicit surface rows and profile points rather

than an availability bitmask, improving package- and release-specific

answers.

Editors and transports

  • The language server now ships as native stdio, WASI stdio, and browser-WASM

transports. The universal VSIX carries the WASI fallback, and the VS Code web

extension is tested in a browser extension host.

  • The same VSIX set is published to Open VSX as well as the VS Code

Marketplace.

  • The Sublime Text package is platform-independent and downloads a

checksum-pinned native server on demand.

v2.2.0

The 2.x line is out of preview. After twenty-five 2.1.x pre-releases, the

Rust rewrite becomes the default release and the default Marketplace install.

VS Code and JetBrains users on the stable channel move to 2.x without opting

in to anything; the pre-release and eap channels remain for the next

development line, and the 1.x line stays available on its existing tags.

Python is retired. The whole toolchain is native: the language server

(tcl-lsp-server), the tcl and f5-query CLIs, and the tcl-mcp MCP

server all ship as single-file binaries for every supported platform, and

installing or running them needs no Python runtime and no interpreter

bundle.

Tk widgets, callbacks, and static preview

  • The language server now builds a conservative static model of a Tk widget

tree, driven entirely by the command registry. It models only what is

recoverable from source without running Tcl: a variable or command

substitution in a widget path is recorded as an uncertainty rather than

guessed at, so the preview never invents a widget that the script would not

create.

  • Geometry-manager semantics are registry facts rather than hard-coded rules.

pack and grid both claim a geometry container and cannot both propagate

through one, while place manages content without claiming or resizing the

container — modelled precisely instead of collapsed into a single

mixed-manager heuristic.

  • Widget coverage is substantially wider: ttk::labelframe, ttk::scrollbar

and ttk::toggleswitch are newly modelled, and ttk::treeview,

ttk::notebook, ttk::combobox, text, spinbox, listbox, menu,

send and the core tk command all gained substantially deeper specs.

  • The VS Code Tk preview panel renders the richer model — notebook tabs,

treeview headings, listbox contents, menu items and toplevel titles — and

shows an explicit badge where layout could not be determined statically,

so an abstention is visible rather than silently drawn as an empty frame.

TclOO callback navigation

  • References, rename and code lenses now agree with each other on callback

sites. A method used as a callback is found by all three providers, and the

count on a lens matches what "find all references" returns.

  • Callback prefixes are resolved through the shapes real code uses: prefixes

built as lists around self, prefixes stored in a variable and used one hop

later, my-based callbacks wrapped in a namespace, and inherited wrapped

callbacks resolved across files.

  • Where the receiver genuinely cannot be determined — an inherited callback

cursor with no unique target — every provider abstains consistently instead

of one of them guessing a method and the others disagreeing.

Registry and Spec Studio

  • A new cargo xtask callback-inventory gate generates and verifies a

registry-backed inventory of every executable and callback-valued surface.

Surfaces behind a resolver are retained as explicitly dynamic rows rather

than having a position guessed from a function pointer.

  • Command-prefix construction is a typed registry vocabulary

(BUILDS_COMMAND_PREFIX / WRAPS_COMMAND_PREFIX), so consumers prove what

a prefix expression evaluates to by following registry traits instead of

matching on command names.

  • CommandSpec carries structured side-effect metadata, feeding effect

analysis from registry data rather than per-command branches in the

analyser.

  • Closed compiler vocabularies — traits, taint colours, side-effect targets —

now own their worked examples as registry data. Adding a vocabulary item

fails to compile until it has one, and Spec Studio, the Compiler Explorer

and the editor's help panels all render the same example.

  • Spec Studio gained inline help on catalogue items, registry-owned flow

examples, and a clearer split between traits that mark a carrier and traits

that describe flow.

Improvements and fixes

  • Taint analysis was substantially extended across the interprocedural and

SSA paths, with the propagation rules and their tests grown to match.

  • SpecTcl pack loading was hardened, and spec projections no longer disagree

with the registry they were generated from.

  • The workspace builds clean under Rust 1.98's tightened lint and

documentation gates, and the dev tooling now audits the toolchain against

the workspace requirement.

  • Tk method lifecycle checks respect the documented version floors rather

than reporting against the newest release.

  • The Spec Studio browser tests drive Monaco's hover directly and tolerate its

portalled widget, removing a class of flaky page tests.

v2.1.24

2.x alpha — pre-release channel.

This prerelease makes the Spec Studio and Compiler Explorer reference surfaces

easier to navigate, keeps their embedded language tooling aligned with the

compiler registry, and strengthens the release path. It remains opt-in through

the VS Code Marketplace pre-release channel, the JetBrains Marketplace

eap channel, or the assets on this GitHub release. The stable 1.x line

remains the default.

Spec Studio and Compiler Explorer

  • Compiler traits now have one typed, closed registry definition for their

names, groups, author-facing documentation, and annotated examples. New or

unknown trait groups fail at compile time, while Spec Studio and Compiler

Explorer receive the same generated reference automatically.

  • Spec Studio replaces the flat trait-label bucket with grouped, searchable

toggles. Every help and reference entry includes a small Tcl example with

callouts showing where the trait, taint rule, or other behaviour applies.

  • Standalone web interfaces use Monaco exclusively, with the SpecTcl/Tcl 9

language configuration, semantic highlighting, and hover available from the

initial render. Editor extensions keep their native file tabs and place the

Studio or Explorer beside them.

Release delivery

  • Every v* release tag now deploys the unified Pages site from the exact

tagged commit, while branch deployments retain their path filtering. A drift

gate protects the trigger and concurrency contract.

  • Post-release installer verification now affirmatively installs and validates

MCP and Claude skills in an isolated temporary home, including an offline

checksum, protocol, version, skills, and cleanup regression test.

v2.1.23

2.x alpha — pre-release channel.

This prerelease hardens the Rust-native compiler, runtimes, language server,

SpecTcl packs, and editor integrations. It remains opt-in through the VS Code

Marketplace pre-release channel, the JetBrains Marketplace eap channel,

or the assets on this GitHub release. The stable 1.x line remains the

default.

Tcl, compiler, and runtime correctness

  • Tcl 8.x and Tcl 9.x ${...} parsing now follows one release-aware rule

across lexing, expressions, substitution, analysis, refactors, optimisation,

code generation, and both execution engines. Nested Tcl 9 names no longer

truncate or inherit an 8.x closing-brace rule.

  • Namespace, ensemble, TclOO, variable, trace, list, and dictionary behaviour

is aligned more closely with C Tcl. This includes prefix resolution,

namespace teardown, export/import options, element references, trace order,

last-value-wins dictionaries, and command-binding-aware constant folding.

  • Compiler and analyser fixes cover quoted whole-command evaluation, braced

loop lists, lambda and untyped-body fall-through, computed metaclasses,

versioned command arguments, and deeply nested source walks without stack

overflow.

Language server, SpecTcl, and editors

  • Diagnostic publishing now uses a persistent, latest-wins per-URI mailbox and

performs client I/O outside document-ordering locks. A stalled publish can no

longer freeze edits and unrelated requests across the language-server

session; retained telemetry makes any residual scheduler stall

self-diagnosing.

  • Cross-file analysis no longer strands callers on W123 while a definition is

opening, or repeatedly re-wakes a deleted-on-disk buffer after facts move.

Extension-host liveness verdicts now distinguish load, document-pipeline

stalls, and whole-server wedges with process and thread evidence.

  • SpecTcl packs gain versioned arity, per-argument lifecycle rows, ambient

package versions, robust malformed-pack notices, deterministic collision

handling, and live pack-declared file-extension registration. VS Code keeps

user associations intact while adding and retiring pack associations.

  • Editor language IDs, filename patterns, and dialect associations now come

from the shared catalogue, closing drift across VS Code, JetBrains, Sublime,

and the command-line tools.

WebAssembly and delivery

  • The browser language server uses a JavaScript-backed clock instead of native

time primitives that trap in WebAssembly, and the import-free VM build stays

import-free.

  • Pull requests now build and execute the browser language-server WebAssembly

target, including its complete local Cargo dependency closure, so Pages-only

failures are caught before merge.

  • The workspace is clean on Rust 1.98, runtime formatting is part of the Rust

gate, and generated and satellite WebAssembly surfaces have stronger drift

and real-link coverage.

v2.1.22

2.x alpha — pre-release channel.

This maintenance prerelease carries forward v2.1.21 with refreshed release

performance measurements and the portable source-data build tooling.

Engineering and delivery

  • Release verification remains portable across GNU and BSD host utilities,

including the PEM source-data generation path.

For the complete feature list, see the [v2.1.21 release notes](https://github.com/bitwisecook/tcl-lsp/releases/tag/v2.1.21).

v2.1.21

2.x alpha — pre-release channel.

This maintenance prerelease carries forward the v2.1.20 Rust-native compiler,

analyser, language server, runtime, and editor tooling while fixing the release

packaging path for the embedded Spec Studio.

Engineering and delivery

  • VS Code and JetBrains release jobs now install the pinned

wasm-bindgen-cli and stable Rust toolchain required to build the embedded

language-server worker, so both editor artefacts are produced reliably.

For the complete feature list, see the [v2.1.20 release notes](https://github.com/bitwisecook/tcl-lsp/releases/tag/v2.1.20).

v2.1.20

2.x alpha — pre-release channel.

This release advances the Rust-native compiler, analyser, language server,

runtime, and extension tooling. It remains opt-in through the VS Code

Marketplace pre-release channel, the JetBrains Marketplace eap channel,

or the assets on this GitHub release. The stable 1.x line remains the

default.

Compiler and runtime correctness

  • Optimisation now respects dynamic variable observation, trace state,

executable control-flow edges, computed names, frame reach, and NaN-sensitive

comparisons. This closes a batch of silent-miscompile cases while retaining

guarded fast paths when their proofs hold.

  • Tcl release selection now drives lexing, escape decoding, expression

operators and numerals, formatting, command availability, compilation, and

host execution end to end. Tcl 8.4 through 9.1 programs no longer inherit

syntax or built-ins from the host's default release.

  • Shared syntax owners now handle substitution literals, parameter lists,

word closers, case-list layouts, expression numeral boundaries, comments,

and iRules event regions. Compiler, analyser, formatter, diagram, and LSP

consumers use those facts instead of maintaining divergent parsers.

  • The virtual machine preserves command-surface and profile identity through

aliases, hide/expose, rename, imports, coroutines, child interpreters, traces,

and cached bytecode. Switch, try/return, expression, and host-fallback paths

now retain their exact Tcl completion and dialect behaviour.

Language server, iRules, and extensibility

  • iRules event discovery, symbols, semantic tokens, comments, selection,

diagnostics, and compilation now share top-level, registry-resolved event

boundaries. Nested or unreachable declarations are excluded, exact command

identity survives aliases, and conflicting event priorities are diagnosed.

  • Dialect strings are resolved once at CLI and LSP ingress and carried as typed

profiles. Editor dialect choices and lexical grammars are generated from the

same registry and syntax owners for VS Code, JetBrains, and Sublime.

  • Registry lifecycle facts model Tcl startup globals for W210 without hiding

genuine undefined locals or values invalidated by unset. Other LSP

features now consume shared case, frame, reference, and embedded-language

contracts, including canonical Windows diagnostic URIs.

  • Project SpecTcl packs apply consistently across the CLI and VS Code, with

version ranges and release history enforced throughout their lifecycle. Spec

Studio gains native editor hosts, import/export provenance, formatting,

highlighting, and a Monaco-backed Pack DSL client whose LSP readiness is

explicitly verified.

BIG-IP and TLS assurance

  • A new safe, non-executing SslicTcl engine models certificates, keys, chains,

trust programmes, protocols, ciphers, HSTS, endpoint evidence, nginx,

OpenSSL, and testssl.sh input. Its pinned Chromium and Trust Stores

Observatory data is embedded with deterministic provenance and offline

verification.

  • BIG-IP reports now project effective client- and server-SSL configuration,

correlate certificate and key material, validate object references, and

surface TLS assurance and chain findings across native, compatibility, and

WebAssembly outputs. Unknown evidence remains explicitly unknown rather than

receiving an optimistic grade.

Engineering and delivery

  • The native installer is stricter and more portable, including archive

verification, platform selection, upgrade behaviour, and a broader harness.

CI cache-warming and VS Code test downloads are corrected and faster.

  • New owner-resolution, editor-generator, documentation-link, diagnostic-tag,

iRule-test-data, and tooling drift gates keep generated assets and semantic

contracts aligned with their Rust sources of truth.

  • Differential-fuzz campaigns now pin one Tcl release across both engines and

replay it from durable, race-safe finding records, preventing deliberate

cross-release differences or incomplete record pairs from being reported as

findings.

Performance across the 2.x releases

These graphs cover every measured 2.x release from v2.1.0 through

v2.2.0, run by scripts/perf/ against a pinned 113-file corpus (scope

small, revision 1). The corpus, scope, and revision are fixed across the

whole series, so the lines are comparable with each other.

2.2.0 is this release: it is the bright-blue line in the memory and CPU

graphs and the rightmost bar in each wall-time group. Earlier releases are

drawn in grey and fade with age.

The series spans more than one measurement host — Apple M1 Max (darwin-arm64);

AMD EPYC 9V74 80-Core Processor (linux-x86_64); AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core

Processor (linux-x86_64); Apple M5 Max (darwin-arm64); Intel(R) Xeon(R)

Processor @ 2.10GHz (linux-x86_64). Wall time and CPU are properties of the

machine as much as of the build, so compare within a host era rather than

reading the boundary as a product change. Resident memory is far less

host-sensitive.

Resident memory

![Resident memory across the 2.x releases](https://github.com/bitwisecook/tcl-lsp/releases/download/v2.2.0/perf-memory.svg)

CPU utilisation

![CPU utilisation across the 2.x releases](https://github.com/bitwisecook/tcl-lsp/releases/download/v2.2.0/perf-cpu.svg)

Per-check wall time

![Per-check wall time across the 2.x releases](https://github.com/bitwisecook/tcl-lsp/releases/download/v2.2.0/perf-walltime.svg)

[Benchmark table and method

notes](https://github.com/bitwisecook/tcl-lsp/releases/download/v2.2.0/perf-summary.md)

— the raw result JSON is attached to this release as perf-2.2.0.json.

idea-plugin.name: SpecDD
idea-plugin.description:
SpecDD language support for .sdd specification files.

SpecDD™ is an open-source framework for specification-driven development in AI-assisted software projects.

The SpecDD framework uses small, local, human-readable .sdd files that live beside the code they describe. These specs document intent, architecture, behavior, boundaries, and implementation tasks in a way that both human developers and AI coding agents can follow.

SpecDD works for both greenfield and existing projects. In new projects, specs can define structure before implementation starts. In existing projects, specs can be introduced gradually around modules, services, features, or files that are actively changing.

The plugin adds syntax highlighting, structural validation, section documentation, structure view entries, section and path completion, clickable project file references, unresolved path warnings, and create-file quick fixes for SpecDD files.

  • Homepage and documentation
  • Source code
  • Issue tracker
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • Align Tasks parsing and validation with the SpecDD language grammar by requiring task-marker and task-id separators.
  • Report malformed task markers in Tasks as task diagnostics instead of falling through as generic text.
  • Extract and highlight brace-alternative glob paths such as ./src/{main,test}.sdd.
  • Trim terminal : from explicit @ symbol references while preserving internal symbol colons.
  • Report whitespace before : in section headers with a specific validation diagnostic.

idea-plugin.name: AI Naming
idea-plugin.description:
AI Naming suggests better names for code symbols from a user-configured AI endpoint.

中文使用说明

  1. 打开 Settings | Tools | AI Naming。
  2. 填写 OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions 接口地址。
  3. 按需填写 API Token 和模型名称。
  4. 把光标放在变量、方法或类名上，也可以选中一段文本。
  5. 触发 AI 命名：点击 Java 函数名旁的 AI 图标、编辑器右键菜单、Refactor 菜单，或快捷键。
  6. Windows/Linux 快捷键：Ctrl+Alt+N。
  7. macOS 快捷键：⌘⌥N，也就是 Command+Option+N。
  8. 等待行末状态提示完成，然后从候选名称列表中选择一个名称。
  9. 如果当前 Java 函数没有 JavaDoc，在你选定候选名称后会弹出确认框，询问是否插入 AI 生成的函数注释。

English Usage

  1. Open Settings | Tools | AI Naming.
  2. Enter your OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoint URL.
  3. Fill in the optional API Token and model name if needed.
  4. Place the caret on a variable, method, or class name, or select text manually.
  5. Run AI 命名 by clicking the AI icon next to a Java method name, from the editor context menu, the Refactor menu, or a shortcut.
  6. Windows/Linux shortcut: Ctrl+Alt+N.
  7. macOS shortcut: ⌘⌥N, also known as Command+Option+N.
  8. Wait for the inline status hint, then choose one name from the candidate list.
  9. If the current Java function has no JavaDoc, a confirmation dialog appears after you choose a candidate name, asking whether to insert the AI-generated function comment.

idea-plugin.name: Latency Budget Analyzer
idea-plugin.description:
AI-Powered Latency Budget Analyzer

Analyzes your Java/Spring Boot methods for latency hotspots — detecting HTTP calls, database queries, Kafka publishes, Redis operations, and blocking patterns. Provides estimated latency budgets (min/max/p99) per call type and uses AI to suggest concrete optimizations like async conversions, caching strategies, and parallel execution.

Features:

  • PSI-based static analysis of call chains in Java/Kotlin methods
  • Per-operation latency estimates (HTTP, DB, Kafka, Redis, Thread.sleep)
  • Hotspot detection (calls consuming >20% of total p99 budget)
  • Blocking call detection (synchronous operations that should be async)
  • AI-powered optimization suggestions via Claude API
  • Interactive results panel with sortable call chain table

Usage:

Right-click inside any Java/Kotlin method → Analyze Latency Budget
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.0
  • Initial release
  • Support for HTTP, DB, Kafka, Redis, and Thread.sleep detection
  • AI-powered suggestions via Claude API
  • Interactive latency breakdown panel

idea-plugin.name: AI Context Prompt
idea-plugin.description:
AI Context Prompt helps developers prepare prompts for external AI tools by collecting project context from the IDE, such as files, classes, methods, resources, and source-aware pasted snippets. It brings an IDE-grade experience to writing AI prompts.

When you copy code or text from your project and paste it into the prompt editor, AI Context Prompt automatically keeps the source file and line range.

The goal is simple: keep your code context in the IDE, then copy a clean prompt to Codex, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or an internal AI assistant.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • AI-ready prompt composer tool window for JetBrains IDEs.
  • Natural completion for project context, including files, folders, classes, resources, Python classes/functions, Go types/functions, and scoped methods.
  • Android resource completion for common resource types and scoped layout ids.
  • Context mentions with related context export, navigation, type icons, and configurable edit behavior.
  • Copy output with linked project context, source-aware pasted code context, and Pro access checks.
  • Ranking profiles, recent selection weighting, and platform-aware search behavior.
  • Settings page for mention edit behavior and context copy limits.

idea-plugin.name: Test Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Agentic AI for test automation

Unlock 4x productivity with AI that accelerates your testing cycles.

Test Companion helps SDETs author, execute, debug, and maintain tests 4X faster with agentic AI right inside the IDE they already use.

Generate & maintain test cases from requirements, automate across UI, API, Accessibility, visual and more types of tests. Autonomously debug failures. Powered by an agentic harness connected to your existing automation framework & toolchain.

Backed by 30,000+ real devices on the BrowserStack cloud, so every test script is authored against actual app behaviour.

Requirements

  • Any JetBrains IDE 2024.3 or higher (IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, PhpStorm, RubyMine, CLion, DataGrip, Rider)

Docs

See our documentation to get started with Test Companion.

Test Companion in action!

Web Testing

Experience seamless web automation. Test Companion identifies elements, handles dynamic content, and executes cross-browser tests instantly.

Start testing immediately.

App Testing

Take your testing to real hardware. Test Companion supports native and hybrid mobile apps, interacting with real devices to ensure real-world reliability.

Start testing immediately on real iOS and Android devices.

Key Features

  • Generate Test Cases: Creates detailed scenarios with steps, expected results, and priority levels from PRDs, specifications, user stories, or by exploring a live URL or mobile app. For mobile apps, upload an APK, AAB, XAPK, or IPA file and let the AI explore your app on BrowserStack's real device cloud.
  • Write Automation Scripts: Produces code for any testing framework in your project, including Playwright, Cypress, WebdriverIO, Selenium, Appium, Robot, Cucumber, and others. Convert existing manual test cases into code, or describe a new test from scratch. Works for both web and mobile applications.
  • Debug & Fix Failing Tests: Connects to BrowserStack Test Reporting & Analytics or accepts pasted error logs. Identifies the root cause and suggests code-level fixes. You can also start this workflow from the Failure Analysis panel in the Automate dashboard.
  • Find & Fix Accessibility Violations: Scans your web application against WCAG standards to identify accessibility issues. Applies automated code remediation directly to your source files.
  • Test Mobile Apps on Real Devices: Uploads an APK, AAB, or IPA file and explores your app on BrowserStack's device cloud. Generates test cases and automation scripts based on its findings.
  • Validate Code Changes (Dev Testing): A shift-left workflow that understands your local codebase and generates tests specific to what you are currently building, before the code reaches QA.

Use Cases

Test Companion helps with all testing jobs across the software development lifecycle

Why use Test Companion?

Agentic workflows for the entire test cycle

  • Author functional, visual, accessibility and API tests 60% faster
  • Specialised agents to debug failures and heal broken tests
  • Exploratory testing to discover edge cases and coverage gaps

Adapts to how your team tests

  • Supports major test frameworks and automation tools
  • Connect your test management, reporting and CI/CD tools
  • Understands your test structure, patterns, utilities and conventions

Superior test authoring for real mobile devices

  • Author tests purpose-built for real device behavior
  • Test biometric, passcode, Face ID, and other auth workflows
  • Get accurate, reliable tests that emulator-based tools can't replicate

Get Started with Test Companion

Setup & Customization

  • Sign In to BrowserStack: Log in to instantly unlock intelligent testing, test case generation, and automation.
  • Customize Your Companion: Tailor the AI's behavior and set common inputs to ensure all generated output perfectly fits your project standards.
    • Using Rules: Custom rules guide AI output. Use them to enforce your organization's standards or provide vital context about your workspace.
    • Using Workflows: Save time by defining reusable setups. Avoid repeating basic inputs (e.g., URLs or credentials) by creating a lightweight custom workflow.

idea-plugin.name: Antigravity CLI Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Runs the Antigravity CLI (agy) in a JetBrains IDE terminal (PhpStorm, IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, etc.) and feeds it live editor context over MCP — active file, selection, open tabs, and inspection diagnostics, on demand.

Independent third-party plugin — not Google's official Antigravity extension. Google's own agent installs from JetBrains AI → Settings → Agents and requires IDE 2026.2.1+ — see Google's official setup guide. If you want that first-party agent panel, use it. This plugin has a different purpose: it runs the Antigravity CLI (agy) in an IDE terminal and feeds it editor context over MCP, on IDE 2023.2 and up, with no JetBrains AI dependency.

The plugin runs a small local MCP (Model Context Protocol) server inside the IDE and registers itself in ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json. Whenever agy needs editor context it calls the plugin over MCP — no env vars, no lockfiles, no platform-specific bridges.

Click the Open Antigravity CLI toolbar button (top-right) to launch agy in an IDE-embedded terminal pre-wired to the running project. By default the button focuses the existing Antigravity terminal tab if one is open; enable Always open a new tab in settings to spawn a fresh session on every click.

Exposed MCP tools

  • ide_get_active_editor — current file path, language, cursor, selection, content.
  • ide_get_open_files — every file currently open in an editor tab.
  • ide_get_diagnostics — inspections/errors/warnings for a file.
  • ide_open_file — open a file at an optional line/column.

Artifacts tool window

A right-anchored tool window lists recent brain entries agy generates — plans, summaries, walkthroughs from your conversations. Sorted by most-recently modified so the active session's output is always at the top; the conversation ID prefix on each row helps distinguish entries that share a filename. Auto-refreshes every few seconds while the tab is open; double-click any entry to open it in the editor.

Configure the path to your agy binary under Settings → Tools → Antigravity CLI Companion. No keyboard shortcut is bound by default — assign one via Settings → Keymap (search Open Antigravity CLI) or from the link in the plugin's settings panel.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.6.0

  • New setting: Auto-approve tool calls (skip permission prompts) — off by default. agy ships with its request-review tool-permission mode as the default, which is why it stops to ask before running each command. Ticking this box launches it with --dangerously-skip-permissions instead, so a session runs uninterrupted. It is a launch argument, not a config edit: only sessions started from this IDE are affected, an agy you run in a plain terminal is unchanged, and the plugin still writes nothing to ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json — agy rewrites that file itself, so editing it from the IDE would risk clobbering a hand-curated allowlist. Two things still prompt regardless: admin escalation, and access outside the workspace root (governed by agy's own allowNonWorkspaceAccess). Applies to the next session you open; tabs already running keep the mode they started with.
  • Long setting descriptions no longer run off the edge of the panel: the hints under Always open a new tab and Path to agy executable were plain single-line labels, which Swing lays out without wrapping — the text was simply clipped at the right edge of the dialog (“…spawn a fresh agy session on every c”). They now wrap at the same width as the other hints, as does the WSL2 note on Windows, which had markup but no width to wrap against.

1.5.0

  • Renamed to Antigravity CLI Companion: the old name read as though this were Google's own extension. It is not — it is an independent third-party plugin, published months before any official JetBrains integration existed. Google's own agent installs from JetBrains AI → Settings → Agents and requires IDE 2026.2.1+; this plugin does something different, running the Antigravity CLI (agy) in an IDE terminal and feeding it editor context over MCP on IDE 2023.2 and up, with no JetBrains AI dependency. The settings page is now Settings → Tools → Antigravity CLI Companion; nothing else moves, and existing installs update in place.
  • The Artifacts tool window lists artifacts again: it had been ranking conversations by directory mtime and keeping only the 20 most recent. Current agy creates .system_generated/ (transcripts, per-step output, task logs) at conversation start and writes into it for the whole session, so every busy conversation looked recent whether or not it ever produced an artifact — and each one evicted a conversation that actually held a plan or walkthrough. On a real brain directory the panel was showing 3 of 34 artifacts. Ranking now happens on the artifact files themselves, so the active session's implementation_plan.md or walkthrough.md lands on top the moment it is written.
  • Artifacts: right-click menu: right-clicking an artifact now offers Copy Path and Reveal in Finder / Show in Explorer / Show in Files (the label follows the OS). The click also moves the selection to the row under the cursor, so the menu always acts on the artifact you actually clicked.

1.4.1

  • No longer writes to ~/.terminfo when the workaround is switched off: the terminfo entry was compiled at project open regardless of the Fix prompt editing in the IDE terminal setting, so a user who had turned the feature off — or who never launched agy at all — still got a file written into their home directory. The lookup is now skipped while the setting is off, and runs when it is switched back on.
  • Settings panel no longer stretches sideways: the hint under Fix prompt editing in the IDE terminal was a single-line HTML label, which Swing lays out without wrapping — it pushed the whole Settings → Tools → Antigravity CLI Companion page far wider than the dialog. The text is now shorter and wraps at a scaled width.

1.4.0

  • Prompt editing no longer garbles the terminal: editing in the middle of the agy prompt used to scramble the display — inserted text landed several columns too far right and the tail of the line was duplicated. agy moves the cursor left with CSI Z (cursor backward tabulation), which JediTerm — the emulator behind both the classic and the reworked IDE terminal — parses but does not implement, so the cursor silently stayed put while agy believed it had moved. agy only enables that optimisation when TERM carries an xterm prefix, so the plugin now launches it under an equivalent non-xterm terminal name (a private agyterm-256color entry compiled into ~/.terminfo, falling back to nsterm-256color). The -256color suffix is load-bearing: the IDE terminal exports no COLORTERM, so TERM is the only signal agy has for colour depth, and a name without it silently drops the palette to 16 colours. Nothing else is lost — 256 colours, alt-screen, kitty keyboard and bracketed paste all still negotiate — and the byte cost is unmeasurable. Toggle Fix prompt editing in the IDE terminal under Settings → Tools → Antigravity CLI Companion if you need the terminal name passed through unchanged.

1.3.3

  • WSL2 support documentation: Added notes to the README and Settings UI clarifying that for WSL2 projects, the IDE itself must be run inside WSL (e.g., via JetBrains Gateway) rather than using a Windows-side configuration. (Fixes #9)

1.3.2

  • Artifact Viewer Fix: Explicitly open out-of-project markdown artifacts in the text editor rather than the default Markdown editor with JCEF preview to prevent blank screens (Fixes #7).

1.3.1

  • Keymap link fix: Configure shortcut in Keymap settings… now navigates to Settings → Keymap within the open Settings dialog instead of stacking a second Settings window on top.

1.3.0

  • Reuse Antigravity tab: the toolbar action (now Open Antigravity CLI) focuses the existing Antigravity terminal tab if one is open instead of spawning a new one on every click. Toggle Always open a new tab under Settings → Tools → Antigravity CLI Companion to restore the previous behaviour — multiple parallel agy sessions remain fully supported by the MCP bridge.
  • Keyboard shortcut: the settings panel now shows the current shortcut for Open Antigravity CLI and links straight to Settings → Keymap for assignment. No default is bound — no chord is safe across every JetBrains keymap, so the choice is left to you.

1.2.0

  • Multi-IDE Support: Generalised branding and internal identifiers to support the full JetBrains IDE family (IntelliJ IDEA, PhpStorm, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, etc.).
  • Critical Fix: Prevented destructive overwriting of mcp_config.json when the file is malformed (Fixes #3).
  • UI Polish: Properly centered and scaled the plugin icon.

1.1.0

  • Artifacts Tool Window: New right-anchored panel to view and open plans, summaries, and walkthroughs generated by agy.
  • Shell Environment: agy now launches within a login/interactive shell for proper PATH inheritance on macOS and Linux.

1.0.1

  • Replaced the deprecated TerminalToolWindowManager.createLocalShellWidget(...) call with the non-deprecated createNewSession(runner, TerminalTabState) path.
  • Replaced the deprecated 4-arg TextFieldWithBrowseButton.addBrowseFolderListener(...) in the settings panel with the modern TextBrowseFolderListener form.
  • agy now runs as the terminal tab's process directly; the tab closes cleanly when the user exits agy.

1.0.0

  • Initial public release.

idea-plugin.name: CodeSetu
idea-plugin.description:
CodeSetu — Open-source AI coding assistant for JetBrains IDEs

A privacy-aware, multi-provider Copilot / Cursor alternative for Indian developers, enterprises, public-sector teams, and air-gapped deployments. Bring your own model.

What you get

  • Chat tool window — streamed, markdown-rendered replies with rendered code blocks, in a polished CodeSetu webview.
  • Selected-code actions — Explain, Refactor, Write Tests, Fix Bug, Add Docs, right from the editor context menu.
  • Repo-aware context — active file, selection, and cursor neighborhood are attached automatically (toggleable per message).
  • In-chat provider & model switcher — change providers, base URLs, and models without leaving the chat.
  • Workspace skills & checks — drop .codesetu/skills/*.md and .codesetu/checks/*.md files; they are folded into the system prompt.
  • Multi-turn conversation history — kept per session.

Works with

  • Sarvam — Indic-aware hosted models.
  • Hugging Face — the hosted router (router.huggingface.co/v1), your dedicated Inference Endpoints, or self-hosted TGI. Any served chat model (Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Gemma…) with your hf_… token.
  • OpenAI-compatible — Ollama, vLLM, SGLang, OpenRouter, LM Studio, any compatible endpoint.
  • Self-hosted & air-gapped — bring your own URL. No outbound calls beyond the provider you configure.

Privacy & security

  • API keys live in the OS PasswordSafe (keychain) — never in plaintext settings XML.
  • Common secret files (.env*, *.pem, *.key, secrets/, …) are excluded from auto-collected workspace context.
  • No CodeSetu telemetry. Your prompts go only to the provider you configured.
  • 100% open-source under Apache 2.0.

Quick start

  1. Install the plugin and restart the IDE.
  2. Open the CodeSetu tool window (right dock).
  3. Click the provider · model chip in the composer → Configure provider / endpoint… → pick Sarvam, Hugging Face, or OpenAI-compatible, paste your key, and start chatting.

Selected-code actions: right-click any selection → Explain / Refactor / Write Tests / Fix Bug / Add Docs with CodeSetu.

Links

  • Source on GitHub
  • Install & setup guide
  • Community Discord
  • Report an issue
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.4.15

  • @workspace — semantic codebase search — index your repo and retrieve code by meaning. Auto-builds on first use, auto re-indexes after you save, and an optional "always retrieve every turn" mode. Runs on any OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint.
  • Agent Mode is now the default, and works with models that lack native tool-calling (e.g. Gemma) via prompted tool-calls.
  • Context & activity panel — every turn shows the provider · model · endpoint, the tools available, and the @workspace results; a version badge sits by the model picker.
  • /edit — rewrite a selection/file from an instruction with a diff preview and per-hunk accept/reject (command and /edit slash).
  • @folder pinning and a multi-session chat history switcher.
  • On-prem Docker installer — self-host chat + embeddings fully inside your network (air-gapped friendly).

0.4.1

  • Inline FIM completions — ghost-text suggestions as you type, debounced and cached so re-triggering at the same spot avoids a redundant model call.
  • Edit with CodeSetu — describe a change to the selection, preview it as a diff, and apply only on accept.
  • @-mention file pinning — type @ in the composer to pin workspace files as primary context; pins show as removable chips and persist across turns.
  • Chat history — past conversations are kept and restored across restarts; switch back to an earlier chat or start a New chat any time.
  • Agent Mode checkpoints — each agent turn snapshots the files it writes; Revert Last Agent Edits restores them in one click.
  • Copy / Insert on code blocks and a context-usage gauge ("~N ctx") next to the model picker.

0.4.0

  • Agent Mode — a composer toggle that turns chat into an agent: it reads, edits, and runs commands to complete a task, then you review the result. Tools include read/write/edit files, run shell commands, search (grep / glob / list), task tracking, and IDE diagnostics.
  • Inline approvals — file edits and shell commands are approved right in the chat, with a diff preview for edits; read-only tools run automatically. Approve, Approve for session, or Deny.
  • Project policy — drop a committable .codesetu/agent.json to set autoApproveCommands, denyCommands (regex; deny wins), and maxIterations.
  • Works with local / self-hosted models that emit tool calls as text (Ollama, llama.cpp). Agent Mode is off by default and needs a tool-calling-capable model.

0.3.1

  • "Context sent to AI" preview — a collapsible panel under each turn showing the routed skill, your selected code, related snippets, and the full assembled payload, so you can see exactly what the model receives.
  • "Thought for Ns" thinking panel — when a model streams its reasoning, it's shown in a collapsible panel above the answer that opens while it thinks and collapses once the reply starts.
  • Skills load from bundled SKILL.md files — built-in skills now have a single source of truth instead of hard-coded copies.
  • Composer UX — Enter sends and Shift+Enter inserts a newline; the slash palette closes once you start typing your message.

0.3.0

  • Plan Mode — composer toggle that asks the assistant for a numbered plan instead of code; "Approve & Run" sends the canonical approval phrase and exits the mode. Toggle state persists across IDE restarts.
  • AI Skills with slash palette — type / in the composer to invoke /plan, /explain, /refactor, /test, /indic. Keyword auto-routing picks a skill from natural-language prompts (toggle in Settings → CodeSetu).

0.2.0

  • Chat tool window rendered with the CodeSetu webview design (markdown replies, model chip)
  • Hugging Face provider support, plus in-chat provider/model switching (Sarvam, OpenAI-compatible, Hugging Face)
  • API key stored securely in PasswordSafe; multi-turn chat history

0.1.0

  • Initial JetBrains plugin scaffold
  • Adds CodeSetu menu group with a placeholder "Open Chat" action

idea-plugin.name: AutoDeps (An Automatic Maven Dependency Resolver)
idea-plugin.description:
Maven Dependency Resolver for IntelliJ IDEA | Fix Unresolved Imports Automatically

A powerful IntelliJ IDEA plugin that automatically detects unresolved imports and fixes missing Maven dependencies in real time. It eliminates manual steps like searching Maven repositories, updating pom.xml, and resolving build errors.

Built for Java developers working with Maven projects, this plugin not only resolves dependencies but also provides a unified visibility layer and intelligent resolution reporting across your entire codebase.

Core Features

  • Detects unresolved Java imports instantly
  • Searches Maven Central for matching dependencies and artifacts
  • Automatically updates pom.xml and syncs the project
  • Generates a module-wise dependency resolution report
  • Provides one-click revert/add actions for each dependency
  • Supports multi-module Maven projects seamlessly

Unified Dependency Insight

All unresolved dependencies are displayed in a centralized overlay view, mapping affected classes to missing dependencies in one place. This eliminates the need to hunt through files and helps developers quickly understand impact and resolution options.

Use Cases

  • Fixing missing dependencies in large Java Maven projects
  • Enterprise applications with multiple modules
  • Onboarding developers into complex repositories
  • Legacy migration and dependency cleanup

Why This Plugin?

Beyond just fixing imports, this plugin gives you control and transparency. With a structured resolution report, centralized visibility, and reversible actions, you can confidently manage dependencies without breaking your build.

Supported Platforms

This plugin runs on desktop IntelliJ IDEA on:

  • Windows
  • macOS (including MacBook)
  • Linux

It is not available on iOS or iPadOS (iPhone/iPad). IntelliJ IDEA and JetBrains Marketplace plugins require a desktop operating system.

Supported IntelliJ IDEA Versions

Requires IntelliJ IDEA 2025.3 or newer (including future releases such as 2026.1 and later). Install from JetBrains Marketplace only in a compatible IDE version.

  • Minimum: IntelliJ IDEA 2025.3
  • Supported onward: all newer IntelliJ IDEA releases on the same platform branch and future major versions unless noted otherwise in release notes

Keywords

Maven dependency resolver, IntelliJ plugin, unresolved imports, Java build errors, pom.xml automation, dependency report, Maven Central search, multi-module Maven, IntelliJ IDEA Maven plugin, dependency management tool

idea-plugin.name: Copy Code Reference with Line Numbers

Copy Code Reference with Line Numbers

A lightweight, productivity-boosting plugin that lets you copy file paths combined with selected line numbers in the format relative/path/to/file:startLine~endLine.

How to Use:

  1. Select any block of code inside the editor.
  2. Right-click to open the context menu and select Copy Code Reference (Line Numbers), or press Shift + Alt + C.

src/main/java/com/ccsoftware/copycodereference/CopyCodeReferenceAction.java:18~57

for less than 5 lines selected, the source code would be copied as well. For more than 5 lines, just the line number reference copied.

idea-plugin.name: Auto Commit
idea-plugin.description:
Auto Commit generates Git commit messages with AI directly inside IntelliJ IDEA. It reads your staged changes and streams a clear, ready-to-use commit message into the commit message field.

It supports OpenAI-compatible APIs and includes presets for OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, DeepSeek, Kimi, Zhipu GLM, Qwen DashScope, SiliconFlow, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio, and custom endpoints. API keys are saved in the plugin's local settings so you do not need to re-enter them every time you open the IDE.

  • One-click AI commit message generation from the IDEA Commit tool window.
  • Right-click the action button to choose a prompt convention and generate immediately.
  • Supports Conventional Commits, Gitmoji, simple style, and custom prompts.
  • Works with cloud providers and local models through Ollama or LM Studio.
  • Streams generated text directly into the commit message field and can be stopped anytime.
  • Supports multilingual output, including English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and custom languages.
  • Handles large diffs with automatic truncation and optional secret redaction.
  • Includes a status bar widget for quick provider and model switching.

中文简介

Auto Commit 是一个 IntelliJ IDEA 插件，可以根据暂存区代码变更，使用 AI 自动生成 Git commit message， 并将结果流式写入提交信息输入框。

插件支持 OpenAI 兼容接口，内置 OpenAI、Anthropic Claude、DeepSeek、Kimi、智谱 GLM、 通义千问 DashScope、SiliconFlow、OpenRouter、Ollama、LM Studio 等预设，也支持自定义模型服务。 API Key 会保存到插件本地配置中，重新打开 IDE 后无需重复填写。

  • 在 IDEA Commit 窗口中一键生成提交信息。
  • 右键生成按钮可选择提示词规范，并立即按该规范生成。
  • 支持 Conventional Commits、Gitmoji、简洁模式和自定义提示词。
  • 支持云端模型，也支持 Ollama / LM Studio 本地模型。
  • 生成内容会流式写入 commit message，可随时停止。
  • 支持中文、英文、日文、韩文以及自定义输出语言。
  • 自动截断大 diff，并可对敏感信息进行脱敏。
  • 提供状态栏入口，方便快速切换服务商和模型。

idea-plugin.name: SkillsJars Helper
idea-plugin.description:
SkillsJars Helper is a JetBrains IDE plugin that makes Agent Skills shipped as Maven artifacts (SkillsJars) first-class citizens: discover them on the classpath, preview SKILL.md straight from inside the JAR, and export any skill to a local Agent directory with one click.

GitHub | SkillsJars | More plugins

Why

Agent Skills — a SKILL.md plus optional scripts and assets — are how modern coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Junie, Cursor, Gemini, Qoder, Trae, CodeBuddy, …) pick up reusable behaviour. SkillsJars packages them as plain Maven / Gradle artifacts so a team can version and share skills like any other dependency. This plugin closes the last gap: making those skills visible and usable inside the IDE without ever unpacking a JAR.

Features

  • Discovery: scans Maven regular dependencies and Maven plugin dependencies for META-INF/skills/**/SKILL.md and META-INF/resources/skills/**/SKILL.md; exposes results through a public project-level SkillRegistry service.
  • Agent Skills tool window: skills are grouped by artifact in a tree, with a dedicated description panel below a draggable splitter. Double-click or Enter opens SKILL.md in-place; right-click for Open / Copy Name / Copy Coordinate / Open Source Jar.
  • One-click export: export a skill (or the whole JAR) into nine preset Agent directories — .claude/skills, .codex/skills, .junie/skills, .agents/skills, .cursor/skills, .gemini/skills, .qoder/skills, .trae/skills, .codebuddy/skills — or a custom directory. Each exported folder gets a manifest with per-file sha256, so upgrades, local edits and same-name conflicts are detected automatically.
  • Install state badges: every skill leaf right-aligns brand icons of the Agent directories it is already installed into; tooltip spells out the agent ids in plain text.
  • Open extension point: skillSourceScanner lets third-party plugins add Gradle, SBT or proprietary build systems without touching the coordinator.

How to use

  1. Add any SkillsJars to your project (as a regular Maven dependency or under skillsjars-maven-plugin's ＜dependencies＞).
  2. Open the Agent Skills tool window on the right; the skills will appear, grouped by artifact.
  3. Double-click a skill to read its SKILL.md; right-click to export it to the Agent directory of your choice. The badges on each skill leaf show where it is already installed.

SkillsJars Helper 让以 Maven artifact 形式分发的 Agent Skills (即 SkillsJars) 在 JetBrains IDE 中 成为一等公民: 在 classpath 上自动发现、不解压直接预览 SKILL.md, 并一键导出到本地 Agent 目录.

这是什么

Agent Skills (一份 SKILL.md 加可选脚本 / 资源) 是现代 Coding Agent (Claude Code、Codex、Junie、 Cursor、Gemini、Qoder、Trae、CodeBuddy …) 复用行为的标准载体. SkillsJars 把它们打成 Maven / Gradle artifact, 让团队像管理普通依赖一样版本化和共享 skill. 本插件补上 IDE 里的最后一公里: 不解压、不离开 IDE, 即可发现、预览和分发这些 skill.

主要能力

  • 依赖扫描: 自动扫描 Maven 普通依赖与 Maven plugin dependencies, 解析 JAR 内 META-INF/skills/**/SKILL.md 与 META-INF/resources/skills/**/SKILL.md, 通过项目级 SkillRegistry 服务对外暴露.
  • Agent Skills 工具窗: 按 artifact 分组的树, 下方独立描述面板 (可上下拖动). 双击或 Enter 直接打开 SKILL.md; 右键菜单含 Open / Copy Name / Copy Coordinate / Open Source Jar.
  • 一键导出: 右键 skill (或整个 JAR) 导出到 9 个预设 Agent 目录 (.claude/skills, .codex/skills, .junie/skills, .agents/skills, .cursor/skills, .gemini/skills, .qoder/skills, .trae/skills, .codebuddy/skills) 或自定义目录. 导出时写入 manifest (含来源 artifact 与每文件 sha256), 自动判断升级、本地修改与同名冲突.
  • 安装徽标: skill 叶子节点右对齐显示已安装到的 Agent 品牌图标, tooltip 明确列出 agent id.
  • 开放扩展点: skillSourceScanner 允许三方插件扩展 Gradle / SBT 或自有构建系统的扫描, 无需改动本插件协调层.

怎么用

  1. 把任意 SkillsJars 加入项目 (作为普通 Maven 依赖, 或放在 skillsjars-maven-plugin 的 dependencies 下).
  2. 打开右侧的 Agent Skills 工具窗, 即可看到按 artifact 分组的 skill 列表.
  3. 双击 skill 查看 SKILL.md; 右键导出到目标 Agent 目录. skill 叶子节点上的徽标会实时显示当前已安装位置.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.2.1000

  • Support IntelliJ Platform 2026.2.
  • 适配 IntelliJ Platform 2026.2。

2026.1.1000 — Initial Release

  • Skill discovery: scans Maven regular dependencies and Maven plugin ＜dependencies＞, parses META-INF/skills/**/SKILL.md and META-INF/resources/skills/**/SKILL.md from inside JARs, and exposes results through a project-level SkillRegistry service.
  • Agent Skills tool window: artifacts grouped one level deep, skills as leaves; description panel below a draggable splitter; speed search, tooltips, double-click / Enter to open SKILL.md; right-click for Open / Copy Name / Copy Coordinate / Open Source Jar.
  • One-click export: export a skill (or the whole JAR) into nine preset Agent directories (.claude/skills, .codex/skills, .junie/skills, .agents/skills, .cursor/skills, .gemini/skills, .qoder/skills, .trae/skills, .codebuddy/skills) or a custom directory. Folder name follows the SKILL.md name field per the Agent Skills convention.
  • Manifest and install states: each exported folder writes a .skillsjars-helper.json with source artifact and per-file sha256, so upgrades, local edits and same-name conflicts are detected automatically. Common paths write silently with a notification; sensitive ones prompt for confirmation.
  • Install state badges: skill leaves right-align brand icons for every Agent directory the skill is already installed into; an InstallationRegistryService rescans the preset directories on startup and after every export.
  • Public extension point: skillSourceScanner lets third-party plugins add Gradle, SBT or proprietary scanners without touching the coordinator.
  • i18n: English and Simplified Chinese message bundles.
  • Skill 发现: 扫描 Maven 普通依赖与 Maven plugin ＜dependencies＞, 解析 JAR 内 META-INF/skills/**/SKILL.md 与 META-INF/resources/skills/**/SKILL.md, 通过项目级 SkillRegistry 服务对外暴露.
  • Agent Skills 工具窗: 按 artifact 一层折叠, skill 作为叶子节点; 下方独立描述面板 (上下可拖动); SpeedSearch / tooltip / 双击或 Enter 打开 SKILL.md; 右键菜单含 Open / Copy Name / Copy Coordinate / Open Source Jar.
  • 一键导出: 右键 skill (或整个 JAR) 导出到 9 个预设 Agent 目录 (.claude/skills, .codex/skills, .junie/skills, .agents/skills, .cursor/skills, .gemini/skills, .qoder/skills, .trae/skills, .codebuddy/skills) 或自定义目录; 目录名严格采用 SKILL.md 的 name 字段, 与 Agent Skills 规范一致.

  • 安装徽标: skill 叶子节点右对齐显示已安装到的 Agent 品牌图标; InstallationRegistryService 在启动和每次导出后自动重扫所有预设目录.
  • 开放扩展点: skillSourceScanner 允许三方插件扩展 Gradle / SBT 或自有构建系统的扫描, 无需改动协调层.
  • 国际化: 中英 Bundle 同步.

idea-plugin.name: Skill Inspector
idea-plugin.description:
Skill Inspector

Skill Inspector is a JetBrains IDE plugin for writing and reviewing Agent Skills. It brings real-time inspection, problem navigation, and conservative Quick Fixes to SKILL.md files, so skill authors can catch structure, reference, quality, and safety issues while editing.

Agent Skills package reusable instructions, scripts, references, and assets for AI coding agents. A broken frontmatter block, a missing local reference, or an overly broad tool permission can make a skill harder to discover, harder to run, or unsafe to share. Skill Inspector focuses on those authoring-time problems directly inside JetBrains IDEs.

GitHub | Agent Skills Specification | More plugins

Core Capabilities

  • Specification-first checks: validates SKILL.md frontmatter, required fields, name format, description limits, and the relationship between the skill directory name and frontmatter name.
  • Authoring quality hints: highlights missing usage guidance, missing document structure, generic descriptions, and overly long skill entry files.
  • Reference and resource validation: checks Markdown links, missing files, paths outside the skill directory, path casing mismatches, unused references/ files, and scripts that are not explained in SKILL.md.
  • Safety signals: flags suspicious secrets, dangerous shell snippets, broad allowed-tools: Bash permissions, sensitive local paths, and prompt-injection style text.
  • Conservative Quick Fixes: repairs deterministic structure issues such as missing frontmatter, missing required fields, invalid skill names, and missing local reference files.
  • IDE workflow integration: reports issues in Problems, supports right-click validation for project skills, provides a current file validation button in the editor, and shows the current file Error / Warning count in the status bar.

How To Use

  • Open a SKILL.md file and inspect the highlighted problems directly in the editor or Problems tool window.
  • Use available Quick Fixes for deterministic repairs such as adding frontmatter, required fields, or missing reference files.
  • Use the editor right-click action to validate all SKILL.md files in the current project.
  • Use the bottom-right editor validation button when you want to re-check the current skill explicitly.
  • Use Settings | Tools | Skill Inspector to enable or disable the plugin's SKILL.md inspection.

Design Approach

  • Specification-first: generic Agent Skills rules are treated as the default baseline instead of one vendor-specific dialect.
  • Low surprise: warnings explain concrete authoring risks without enforcing a single writing style.
  • Conservative fixes: Quick Fixes repair structure but do not rewrite your instructions or silently remove content.
  • Local-first: inspection runs against local project files and keeps feedback in the IDE workflow.

Skill Inspector

Skill Inspector 是一个面向 JetBrains IDE 的 Agent Skill 编写与审查插件。它为 SKILL.md 提供实时 Inspection、Problems 定位和保守 Quick Fix，让 skill 作者在编辑时就能发现结构、引用、质量和安全问题。

Agent Skills 用于把可复用的指令、脚本、参考文档和资源文件打包给 AI coding agent 使用。frontmatter 错误、本地引用失效、工具权限过宽，都会让 skill 更难被发现、更难执行，甚至不适合分享。Skill Inspector 专注解决这些发生在编写阶段的问题，并把反馈直接放在 JetBrains IDE 里。

GitHub | Agent Skills Specification | More plugins

核心能力

  • 规范优先检查：校验 SKILL.md frontmatter、必填字段、名称格式、描述长度，以及 skill 目录名和 frontmatter name 的一致性。
  • 编写质量提示：提示缺少使用时机、缺少文档结构、描述过泛、主 SKILL.md 过长等问题。
  • 引用与资源校验：检查 Markdown 链接、缺失文件、越界路径、大小写不一致、未引用的 references/ 文件，以及未在 SKILL.md 中说明用途的脚本。
  • 安全信号：提示疑似密钥、危险 shell 片段、过宽的 allowed-tools: Bash 权限、敏感本地路径和 prompt injection 风格文本。
  • 保守 Quick Fix：只修复确定性的结构问题，例如缺少 frontmatter、缺少必填字段、非法 skill 名称、缺失本地引用文件。
  • IDE 工作流集成：在 Problems 中展示问题，支持右键校验项目内 skill、编辑器当前文件校验按钮，并在状态栏展示当前文件 Error / Warning 数。

如何使用

  • 打开 SKILL.md，直接在编辑器或 Problems 工具窗口查看高亮问题。
  • 对确定性结构问题使用 Quick Fix，例如补 frontmatter、补必填字段、创建缺失引用文件。
  • 使用编辑器右键菜单校验当前项目中的所有 SKILL.md。
  • 需要显式重检当前 skill 时，使用编辑器右下角校验按钮。
  • 通过 Settings | Tools | Skill Inspector 启用或禁用 SKILL.md Inspection。

设计取向

  • 规范优先：以通用 Agent Skills 规则作为默认基准，而不是绑定某个厂商的私有方言。
  • 低打扰：提示说明具体编写风险，不强迫所有 skill 使用同一种写作风格。
  • 保守修复：Quick Fix 修复结构，不自动改写指令正文，也不静默删除内容。
  • 本地优先：检查面向本地项目文件，并把反馈保留在 IDE 工作流中。

idea-plugin.name: ZenTao Bug Assistant
idea-plugin.description:
ZenTao Bug Assistant turns ZenTao bug reports into AI-ready code repair context inside IntelliJ IDEA.

插件不替代禅道的项目管理能力，只补齐缺陷单到 Claude Chat 或命令行 Agent 之间缺的工程上下文层。

主要功能

  • 登录禅道 — 支持自动保存会话，下次打开自动登录
  • 查看 Bug 列表 — 按项目、成员、状态（未解决 / 已解决 / 已关闭）筛选
  • 仅看我的 — 一键过滤出指派给自己的 Bug
  • 预览 Bug 详情 — 在编辑器标签页中渲染重现步骤、截图和附件
  • AI 一键修复 — 把 Bug 描述和截图整理成提示词，发送到 Claude Chat 或 CLI Agent
  • 代码证据包 — 基于 Bug 文本关键词在当前 Git 仓库中搜索代码命中行
  • 验证命令推荐 — 根据当前仓库技术栈提示构建、测试、类型检查或 Unity Test Runner 入口
  • AI 上下文质量评估 — 自动附加评分、已具备信号和待补强缺口
  • 结构化修复协议 — 约束 AI 输出根因、改动文件、验证结果、风险和禅道回写摘要
  • AI 诊断包直送 — 自动汇总上下文质量、截图数量、Prompt 规模和诊断包，并直接发送到 Chat / CLI
  • Chat / CLI 双模式 — 可选择沿用聊天窗口，也可生成 Prompt 文件并在 Terminal 执行命令
  • 修复后回写 — 解决/关闭 Bug 时根据当前 Git diff 生成禅道备注草稿
  • 批量修复 — 对当前列表中所有未解决 Bug 逐一生成提示词并发送
  • 禅道状态同步 — 行内执行指派、确认、解决、关闭、激活操作

使用前提

  • 已安装 Claude Code 插件，或可用的命令行 AI Agent
  • 可访问自己团队的禅道服务器（支持禅道 17+ 的 Web 界面）
