idea-plugin.name: flai
idea-plugin.description:
flai turns IntelliJ-based IDEs into an agent runtime. Define multi-step LLM pipelines as plain YAML, drop them in .flai/, and run them on any file with a single click — straight from a gutter icon or a dedicated tool window. No external orchestrator, no separate app, no copy-paste between a chat window and your editor.

Each pipeline is a graph of gates connected by edges. Outputs of one gate flow into the next through a shared execution context, so you can chain an LLM call into a shell command into a file write without glue code.

Gate types:

  • input — entry point; seeds context from a typed schema (string / number / boolean / JSON).
  • llm — calls an LLM endpoint with a templated prompt and optional reusable skills. Anthropic and OpenAI response shapes supported out of the box.
  • logic — branches execution on context variables (comparison, switch, always).
  • tool — invokes a built-in IDE tool: file read, symbol search, run command.
  • bash — runs a non-interactive shell command with timeout and env overlay.
  • read-file / write-file — move data between disk and context.
  • output — terminal gate; surfaces selected results back in the IDE.

Why flai:

  • Pipelines as code. YAML files checked into git — reviewable in PRs, diffable, branchable.
  • Native IDE integration. Gutter run icon on *.flai.yaml, *.flai.yml, *.flai, *.yaml, and *.yml files, plus a live execution log.
  • Bring your own model. Endpoint and credentials configured per gate.
  • Skills, not megaprompts. Compose reusable instruction files (.flai/skills/*.md) per LLM gate.
  • Secrets stay local. LLM API keys resolve from a pipeline context variable (apiKeyVar) or from IntelliJ's PasswordSafe (flai/<credentialId>) — never written to YAML.

Built for engineers who want their AI workflows to live in the same repo as the code they operate on — versioned, reviewable, and runnable without leaving the IDE.

Documentation: github.com/CrazyApple888/flai — full pipeline YAML specification, examples, and gate reference.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Tool window: the pipeline list now follows the files in .flai/ on disk — files created, saved, renamed, moved or deleted show up without pressing Refresh (debounced, silent, never interrupts a run).
  • Visual editor: changes are now written to the pipeline YAML automatically (debounced) and saved to disk; Apply remains for full validation.
  • Visual editor: empty pipeline files get a pipeline id/name derived from the file name, and the first dropped gate becomes the entry gate.
  • Tool window: a pipeline that parses but fails validation (for example a gate the visual editor wrote before it was configured) is marked in the list with a warning icon, an N issues label and a tooltip listing every problem, and the detail panel shows the same list above the inputs. Run stays available and reports the problems in the execution log.

Changed

  • Pipeline validation unified in core PipelineValidator (used by runner, CLI and visual editor): gate field rules, port/edge checks, one edge per output port, cycles. The runner now rejects pipelines the editor would reject and vice versa.
  • Visual editor sync moved out of the file editor into VisualPipelineDocumentSync; node layout and preferences are infrastructure adapters.

Fixed

  • Visual editor: auto-sync no longer fails with "Access is allowed from write thread only" when saving the document.
  • The "run failed" message of an earlier run no longer sticks around after selecting another pipeline: switching pipelines clears the execution log and result in the tool window and hides the visual editor's run-failure banner. A run in progress is never interrupted.
  • Visual editor: a gate dropped on the canvas is now saved to the YAML file immediately, before its fields are filled in. Gate field rules (LLM prompt/endpoint, tool name, bash command, file paths) are reported by Apply and Run instead of blocking the write, and the parser accepts the half-configured YAML the editor writes.
  • Visual editor: new pipeline files could not be applied or run because the pipeline had no id and no entry.
  • Visual editor: Run now flushes pending visual edits before running instead of discarding them.
  • Visual editor: a # inside a prompt or command no longer blocks auto-sync with a bogus "YAML comments" warning; the normalize confirmation only appears when writing would actually reformat the file.
  • Visual editor: saving no longer wipes undo history or stale-selects nodes when a save-time formatter touches the document.
  • Visual editor: running one pipeline no longer locks every open visual editor.
  • Visual editor: toggling an LLM tool checkbox no longer opens the full Apply validation dialog.
  • Pipeline repository: a pipeline id like foo.flai no longer resolves to foo.flai.yaml; file name matching is case-insensitive.

idea-plugin.name: Claude Code Native
idea-plugin.description:
Claude Code in your IDE, with a real GUI — an AI coding agent for JetBrains, not a terminal wrapper. Chat, review every edit as a native IDE diff, and let the agent read and change your project under permissions you control. Runs your locally installed claude CLI over its stream-json protocol: no Node.js at runtime, no terminal window, no API key required if you already have a Claude subscription.

Works in any JetBrains IDE on the 2025.3 platform or newer — IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, PhpStorm, GoLand, RubyMine, CLion, Rider, DataGrip, DataSpell, Aqua and RustRover.

Unofficial, community-built, open-source plugin. Not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by Anthropic or JetBrains. It requires the user's own separately-installed claude CLI and their own Claude subscription or API key — no credentials are bundled or provided.

Why this plugin

  • A real GUI, not a terminal. Streaming chat, collapsible tool calls, an inline permission card for every action — rendered natively, never mirrored CLI text
  • Diffs are real IDE diffs. Every file edit opens in the editor's own diff viewer and is editable before you approve it — tweak the agent's proposal, then accept
  • A deterministic security layer. Out-of-band code — not a prompt the model can talk its way past — checks every tool call before it runs
  • No Node.js, no SDK at runtime. Speaks the binary's protocol directly from Kotlin

Features

Streaming chat

  • Real-time token streaming with animated thinking indicator and live token counter
  • Multi-tab support — independent sessions per project
  • Multi-prompt queue: type while the agent is working, messages sent in order when the turn ends
  • /btw side-questions sent mid-turn without interrupting the active turn
  • Interrupt (Esc) to stop the current turn at any time

Full slash-command palette

  • All commands from the claude binary surfaced natively — type / in the composer or use the Commands toolbar button
  • Built-in /btw command added by the plugin
  • Signing in is a button, not a command to memorise: the welcome card and the dashboard's account row run the OAuth flow for you — no copy-pasting claude auth login into a shell (a typed /login still works)

Model & runtime controls

  • Model picker read straight from the binary, each entry showing its real version (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) — nothing hardcoded, new models appear on their own
  • Permission mode chip (default / acceptEdits / plan / bypassPermissions)
  • Effort chip (low / medium / high / xhigh / max) and adaptive extended thinking
  • Anthropic or DeepSeek as the provider, each with its own key in the IDE password safe
  • Advanced launch options: max turns, USD budget cap, fallback model, extra directories

Security — a deterministic tool-call lock

  • Every tool call is checked before any auto-approval, so it applies even in acceptEdits / bypassPermissions
  • Blocks reads of credentials and key material (SSH/GPG keys, cloud and database secrets, browser and password-manager stores, access tokens), credential-dumping and exfiltration commands, and access to other users' homes or network mounts
  • Deterministic code, not an LLM guardrail — there is no prompt that argues it into a Yes
  • Each rule is individually switchable in Settings; disabling one downgrades an automatic block to a permission card, never to a silent allow

Jump to code, and read it comfortably

  • File paths, directories and symbols in Claude's replies become clickable links — but only after the IDE confirms them, so a link is never dead
  • Syntax highlighting for diffs and file output, in your IDE's own colours
  • Executed shell commands render as their own copyable code block

Sessions, usage and MCP

  • Session history read from the binary's own files — reopen past chats, rename, fork; your open tabs are restored on IDE startup. The plugin never deletes your conversations: there is no delete action, on purpose
  • A tab per running agent: a session that spawns dozens of subagents and background tasks gives each one its own transcript instead of interleaving them all into the chat
  • Session dashboard: context breakdown, token usage and cost, your plan's usage limits with their reset times, account, and a Workloads view of every agent and background task
  • Optional MCP support — let Claude query the IDE through JetBrains' MCP server, or register your own MCP servers

Native diff review for file edits

  • When the agent requests to write or edit a file, a diff opens inline in the editor area
  • Non-modal Accept / Reject card in the chat — no popups or modal dialogs
  • On acceptance the binary writes the file; VFS is refreshed automatically

Permission & question handling

  • can_use_tool requests surface as native inline cards (Accept / Reject)
  • AskUserQuestion rendered as a structured question card with option buttons
  • Auto-approve in acceptEdits / bypassPermissions modes

IDE integration

  • Tool window anchored to the right panel (same area as AI Assistant)
  • Right-click to Explain with Claude, or add the current selection or file as context
  • Attach files, directories, the current selection, or paste and drag-drop images
  • The IDE sees the agent's writes immediately — no stale editors, no manual refresh
  • Follows your IDE theme, light and dark, with custom icons on every tool call

Requirements

  • JetBrains IDE 2025.3 or newer (build 253+). 2025.1 and 2025.2 are not supported: the whole chat UI is an embedded browser (JCEF), and 2025.3 is the first release where the platform exposes it as a declarable module — which is what keeps the plugin working on 2026.2, where JCEF moved out of the IDE core into a bundled plugin of its own
  • claude CLI installed and on PATH or ~/.local/bin/ (npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code)
  • A Claude subscription (Pro / Max / Team / Enterprise) or an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

License & trademarks

Released under the GNU General Public License v3.0. "Claude" and "Claude Code" are trademarks of Anthropic; "JetBrains", "IntelliJ", "PyCharm" and related names are trademarks of JetBrains s.r.o. Used here for identification only; this project is not affiliated with either company.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
v6.0.1 — 2026-09-22

find_symbols works in Rider again. Asking Claude for a symbol there failed outright with

UnsupportedOperationException: Use RdChooseByNameContributor.processNamesLifetimed: Rider keeps its

symbols in the ReSharper backend and its contributors refuse the platform call the tool was making. A

contributor that refuses is now skipped rather than taking the tool down with it, and the answer says how

many refused out of how many the IDE has — with a note when the result is also empty — so Claude does not

read an empty list as "this symbol does not exist" or "the index is still warming up". The tool only fails

when every contributor refuses, and then it names the tools that do work there.

Nothing else changed.

idea-plugin.name: Upload SSH File
idea-plugin.description:
Upload files/directories to remote servers via SSH SFTP.
  • Right-click file/directory → Upload SSH File
  • Supports multi-file and batch upload (reusable batch task sets, sequential sub-tasks)
  • MD5 checksum verification (Linux) / file-size verification (Windows)
  • Post-upload SSH command execution with blacklist, keyword and optional AI safety layers
  • Server and path configuration management, import/export of the full configuration
  • 8 UI languages (en/中文/de/fr/es/ja/ko/ar)
  • 1.0.8: Task IDs + copyable build snippets (Gradle Groovy/Kotlin, Maven, Ant) and a standalone CLI — bundled inside the plugin archive — that re-runs a saved upload task from a build hook or a terminal, with cross-process per-server upload locking shared by GUI and CLI
  • 1.0.10: the CLI launcher verifies that every Java runtime it discovers is Java 21 or newer, and says so in plain words when none is — no more raw JVM version errors
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.10

Same functionality as the 1.0.9 build submitted for review (Java 21+ launcher gate below); 1.0.9 itself was never released. 1.0.10 additionally replaces two platform APIs that JetBrains' compatibility review flagged as internal/deprecated with their officially recommended public equivalents, and completes the after-install window — see the first two items.

  • New: batch uploads now show per-file progress in the CLI / build-hook console too — a start line, a live percentage line that refreshes in place, and an [OK]/[FAIL] completion line for every file or directory, exactly like single-task uploads.
  • New: installing or reinstalling the plugin (hot-load path) now writes the Java runtime record immediately — the command line works seconds after install, no need to start IDEA or open the context menu first (a full IDE start is only needed when the install requires a restart to take effect).
  • Fix: the CLI launcher now checks the version of every Java runtime it discovers (java-home.txt, then JAVA_HOME, then PATH) and requires Java 21 or newer — an older JVM is now skipped instead of being used. Previously each candidate was only checked for existence, so on machines where JAVA_HOME points at JDK 8 the command line died with UnsupportedClassVersionError … class file version 65.0 … only recognizes … 52.0 and left the user nothing to act on.
  • If no Java 21+ runtime is available, the launcher prints a short explanation showing the values it checked plus two remedies (start IDEA once so it records its own bundled runtime, or point JAVA_HOME at a JDK 21+ install) and exits with code 12.
  • Fix: a stale java-home.txt — left behind when IDEA is moved or uninstalled — no longer stops discovery; the launcher falls through to the next candidate.
  • When an install or upgrade requires an IDE restart to take effect, the command line may answer with a single line — Please restart IntelliJ IDEA to run this task. — and exit with code 12. It is not an error: start IDEA once and the command line works. (Installations that hot-load — the usual "plugin loaded" notice — record the runtime automatically within seconds; see the second item above.)
  • No workflow change: task IDs, saved file lists and pasted build snippets keep working exactly as before. After upgrading, restart IDEA (File → Exit) once so the launcher and java-home.txt are refreshed.
1.0.8
  • Standalone CLI entry, shipped inside the plugin archive (never distributed separately): the launcher uploadsshfile-cli.bat is a static packaged file — usable immediately after install/upgrade/hot-reload, and self-healed if deleted or edited. It uploads the saved file list and runs the remote command group of a task by its Task ID, e.g. from a build hook or a terminal.
  • Task ID system: every upload task (single and batch) has one editable business ID — new tasks pre-fill a pure-digit snowflake ID, new IDs must be alphanumeric, legacy UUID IDs keep working unchanged.
  • The Copy button generates ready-to-paste build snippets for Gradle Groovy / Gradle Kotlin / Maven / Ant. Snippets carry only the Task ID: single task uploads = the file list saved when the Upload dialog last closed (multi-select supported; change files without re-copying the snippet), batch task uploads = the sub-task lists saved in the task. Gradle snippets (single and batch alike) guard against uploading after a failed build, and never flip the build result on upload failure; explanatory comments inside snippets follow your IDE display language (8 languages). Maven/Ant variants are marked "not verified against a real build".
  • Compatibility note: the earlier --file command-line flag was removed — snippets pasted from a 1.0.8 pre-release build must be re-copied once.
  • Target confirmation before execution: CLI and GUI batch runs list every "host → remote path (file count)" and require y/N; --yes (present in pasted snippets) skips it as an explicit automation opt-in.
  • Cross-process per-server upload lock shared by GUI and CLI (stale locks are released by the OS).
  • Progressive timeout behaviour wired up end-to-end: long-running remote commands now ask "keep waiting?" at 30s / 1min / 2min / every 5min instead of silently stopping at 3 minutes; answering "continue" waits without an overall limit (see manual for details).
  • Optional per-path "auto-create remote directory"; staged mkdir failures are reported instead of being swallowed.
  • Config export/import upgraded to v3.2 including the single-task snapshot, so a fresh machine can use the CLI right after import (local values always win when already set).
  • All eight language bundles brought to full key parity (enforced by tests), fixing bare key names and garbled translations in non-English IDEs.
  • After installing or upgrading the plugin, fully restart IDEA (File → Exit) once.
1.0.7
  • Stopped bundling the IDE-private package com.intellij.ant (vendored java-compiler-ant-tasks jar removed from the distribution) — clears the JetBrains Marketplace compatibility warning
1.0.6
  • Fix Marketplace verification failure ("archive cannot be extracted") by shipping the standard buildPlugin archive; the 7z store-mode zip is now packaged separately (-store) for offline distribution only
1.0.5
  • Add Language submenu in right-click menu with checkmark for current language
  • Auto-detect IDE language on first launch, fallback to English if unsupported
1.0.4
  • Fix batch upload progress bar precision and sub-task reset issue
  • Fix marketplace verification API deprecation warnings
  • Auto-clean intermediate build artifacts after packaging
1.0.3
  • Fix batch upload progress calculation
  • Fix i18n missing keys
  • Update deprecated API usages
  • Fix plugin configuration defect

idea-plugin.name: AI Agent Assistant
idea-plugin.description:
AI Agent Assistant is a project-aware AI coding assistant for Android Studio and IntelliJ IDEA. It brings a Cursor-style chat workspace into the IDE, helping developers understand code, analyze projects, generate snippets, review changes, and apply file operations with explicit confirmation.

It supports multiple AI providers, including DeepSeek, OpenAI, Claude, and Ollama, with configurable models, API keys, base URLs, max tokens, streaming responses, and per-project chat history.

The assistant can include IDE context such as the current file, selected code, imports, PSI structure, recent files, and bounded project summaries. AI responses are rendered with Markdown support, including headings, lists, tables, links, inline code, and code blocks.

For code changes, AI Agent Assistant uses a review-first workflow. Generated actions such as insert code, modify file, and create file are shown in an approval dialog before being applied. File writes use IntelliJ platform APIs and support Undo. Absolute paths and path traversal are rejected.

Future planned capabilities include voice input, custom model/API relay configuration, clickable code references, and improved theme synchronization.

AI Agent Assistant 是一款面向 Android Studio 和 IntelliJ IDEA 的项目感知型 AI 编码助手。它将类似 Cursor 的右侧对话工作台集成到 IDE 中，帮助开发者完成代码解释、项目分析、代码生成、变更审核和文件操作。

插件支持 DeepSeek、OpenAI、Claude、Ollama 等 Provider，可配置模型、API Key、Base URL、最大 Tokens、流式输出和项目级对话历史。

插件可以按需注入当前文件、选中代码、imports、PSI 结构、最近打开文件和项目摘要等上下文。AI 回答支持 Markdown 预览，包括标题、列表、表格、链接、行内代码和代码块。

对于代码写入，插件采用先审核再应用的流程。AI 生成的插入代码、修改文件、创建文件等操作会先展示确认弹窗，开发者确认后才会执行；写入过程使用 IntelliJ 平台 API，支持 Undo，并会拒绝绝对路径和路径穿越。

后续计划支持语音输入、自定义模型/API 中转配置、点击代码引用跳转文件，以及更完善的主题同步。

idea-plugin.name: AI Terminal Tools
idea-plugin.description:
AI Terminal Tools enhances JetBrains IDE terminals, consoles, and the Commit panel with fast navigation, click-to-copy, AI terminal sending, OpenCode / Claude Code launch actions, AI Turn Diff, and commit message generation.

Designed for JetBrains IDEs 2025.1+ and compatible with Frontend, Reworked, and Classic terminal paths.

  • Jump from terminal or console file references to editor locations, including line numbers and line ranges.
  • Copy structured terminal output fragments such as URLs, method calls, dotted identifiers, strings, and numbers with one click.
  • Send editor selections, file paths, dragged files, and console error blocks to the active OpenCode or Claude Code terminal.
  • Start OpenCode or Claude Code in dedicated terminal tabs with the environment needed for AI Turn Diff.
  • Review files with actual content changes from each AI turn in an IntelliJ diff window.
  • Generate concise commit messages from checked files in the Commit panel, with configurable AI tool, model, and extra prompt.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Consolidated changes from 0.1.4 through 0.1.7:

  • Preserves existing Claude Code settings, complex fields, and user hook groups when installing AI Turn Diff hooks.
  • Updates only AI Terminal Tools hooks on repeated launches and aborts safely when settings.local.json is unreadable, malformed, or structurally incompatible.
  • Releases per-terminal monitoring state, event tokens, active turns, and launcher scripts when Frontend, Reworked, or Classic AI terminal tabs close, startup fails, or the project is disposed.
  • Finishes active turns on real tab close while ignoring temporary moves and preventing late HTTP events from restoring released state.
  • Silences successful launches, sends, and commit message generation; compatibility fallbacks, skipped binary files, and delayed input-settle failures are logged instead of shown as intermediate balloons.
  • Retains one final notification only for actionable launch, send, commit generation, or Diff failures, plus the explicit no-history Diff action.
  • Stores the latest AI Turn Diff separately for each OpenCode or Claude Code terminal and exposes the selected terminal's result from the Terminal more-actions menu.
  • Clears only the closed terminal's Diff history without affecting other terminal tabs.
  • Uses the IntelliJ Platform FrameWrapper for AI Turn Diff windows so the title bar follows the active IDE theme from the first frame.
  • Preserves the independent resizable window, native minimize and maximize controls, and per-project window size and position.
  • Removes the Windows-specific DWM/JNA title-bar workaround and delegates Diff panel disposal to the platform window lifecycle.

idea-plugin.name: Git Commit Auto
idea-plugin.description:
Git Commit Auto - AI Commit Message Generator

中文介绍

Git Commit Auto — 打开 Commit 窗口后自动生成规范化的 AI commit 信息，无需手动操作。支持多 API 配置、自定义标签管理与中英双语。

核心功能：

  • 自动生成 — 打开 Commit 窗口后自动检测变更、调用 AI 生成 commit 信息并填入
  • 流式输出 — 生成过程实时逐字展示，即时可见
  • 多 API 配置 — 支持 OpenAI / DeepSeek / 通义千问 等多套配置方案，按需切换

  • 自定义提示词 — 可自定义系统提示词，灵活控制生成风格
  • 安全加密 — API 密钥通过操作系统密钥链加密存储，杜绝泄露

English Description

Git Commit Auto — Automatically generates conventional AI commit messages when the Commit window opens. No manual action needed. Supports multi-config API, custom tags, and bilingual output.

Core Features:

  • Auto-Generate — Detects changes and generates commit messages via AI when Commit window opens
  • Streaming Output — See generated text appear in real-time, character by character
  • Multi-Config Support — OpenAI / DeepSeek / Tongyi Qianwen with auto-dedup by settings

idea-plugin.name: Code Context Memo
idea-plugin.description:
Code Context Memo collects selected code snippets, file locations, and task notes into a project-level memo that can be copied to a coding agent.

What it does

  • Adds a Record code context action to the editor context menu when code is selected.
  • Records project-relative file path, line number, code location, selected code, and a What to do note.
  • Persists task background, memo text, and up to 20 history snapshots per project.
  • Supports optional DeepSeek/OpenAI-compatible AI actions for organizing the memo and improving task background text.
Data handling

  • AI settings are stored at IDE application level.
  • API keys are stored through the JetBrains Password Safe.
  • The plugin does not include telemetry.
  • If AI features are used, the current memo/task background is sent to the endpoint configured by the user.

idea-plugin.name: Recent Project Cleaner
idea-plugin.description:
Recent Project Cleaner removes missing recent projects from the Welcome screen.

Features

  • Adds a Clear Invalid Projects action to the Welcome screen project area.
  • Shows the current invalid-entry count directly in the action label when stale entries exist.
  • Removes only local recent-project entries whose paths no longer exist on the current machine.
  • Leaves remote URIs and foreign operating-system path formats alone to avoid accidental cleanup.

Behavior

The plugin reads the IDE recent-project list from the public RecentProjectsManager API surface and removes entries that are clearly stale on the current OS.

It treats the following entries as removable:

  • Blank recent-project paths
  • Absolute local paths that no longer exist
  • Paths that cannot be parsed as valid local paths

It intentionally does not remove:

  • Remote project URIs such as ssh://...
  • Windows-style paths while running on macOS or Linux
  • POSIX-style absolute paths while running on Windows

Usage

  1. Open the IDE Welcome screen.
  2. Look for Clear Invalid Projects in the project actions area.
  3. Click it to remove stale recent-project entries in one step.

When no invalid entries exist, the action stays visible but disabled.

Development

  • Module path: :plugins:recent-project-cleaner
  • Verification: ./gradlew :plugins:recent-project-cleaner:test
  • Descriptor preview: plugins/recent-project-cleaner/build/tmp/patchPluginXml/plugin.xml
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changelog

idea-plugin.name: AI CLI Launcher
idea-plugin.description:
AI CLI Launcher is a macOS-only launcher for local AI CLI tools in JetBrains IDEs. It opens Codex, Claude, Qwen Code, or any custom command in your preferred external macOS terminal at the current project root.

  • Launch multiple configurable AI commands from the main toolbar.
  • Use no context or prefill the current relative file path without auto-submitting.
  • Use your own shell environment, aliases, functions, and PATH.
  • Works with Ghostty, iTerm2, Terminal.app, Warp, WezTerm, Alacritty, Kitty, and more.

AI CLI Launcher does not provide a hosted chat service, collect telemetry, or require API keys. It is designed for developers who prefer external macOS terminals and local AI CLI workflows.

Report a problem or request terminal support: https://github.com/GuJin/ai-cli-launcher-support/issues
idea-plugin.change-notes: AI CLI Launcher initial release.

idea-plugin.name: AI Review and Commit
idea-plugin.description:
AI-generated code still needs review. Modern AI can write useful code quickly, but it can also miss edge cases, preserve broken assumptions, hallucinate APIs or integrations, and produce changes that look correct while failing under real project constraints. A short review before every commit is one of the easiest ways to stop hidden technical debt from entering the codebase and keep your project clean, healthy, and easier to maintain.

AI Review and Commit is a commit-time guardrail for JetBrains IDEs. It focuses on the exact Git diff you are about to commit, helps you catch high-value issues before they become repository history, and can generate a Conventional Commit-style message for the same selected changes.

Use it directly from the IDE Commit panel:

  • Generate a commit message
  • Run AI review
  • Run review and commit message generation together

Review results appear in a dedicated tool window with:

  • Commit Readiness score
  • Findings grouped by severity
  • Confidence, evidence, and file locations
  • Copyable fix prompts
  • Temporary ignore for findings you do not want to handle right now

Generated commit messages are filled directly into the IDE Commit panel, so you can stay in the workflow you already use.

Supports user-configured Claude / Anthropic-compatible and Codex / OpenAI-compatible API profiles. Official provider endpoints and compatible gateway or relay endpoints can both be used as long as they follow the supported API style.

Your API keys stay in JetBrains PasswordSafe. Requests are sent from your IDE to the endpoint you configure. AI Review and Commit does not route requests through its own servers.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changed

  • Improve Review output interactions so Copy Fix Prompt and Copy All Fix Prompts give immediate copied feedback.
  • Reduce visual movement when temporarily ignoring review findings by updating finding cards in place.
  • Refine the Settings structure with a dedicated Profile Settings entry and instant output language selection.
  • Polish backend profile editing with blank provider selection, clearer placeholder text, and transient connection test results.

Fixed

  • Use a plugin-specific resource bundle to avoid message key collisions when multiple Jiamugengjin plugins are installed in the same IDE.
  • Keep ignored findings out of current fix-prompt copy actions without adding extra status rows that shift the review layout.
  • Prevent stale profile test results from being shown after reopening a profile editor.

v2.7.6

  • 【Fixed】UI cutoff

v2.7.5

  • [New] Unified document parsing — Supports PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, and text attachments, with automatic format detection and structured text extraction
  • [New] Scanned PDF support — PDF pages without extractable text are rendered as images for continued analysis by vision-capable models
  • [New] Native attachments for Claude Code / Codex CLI — Documents, images, and extracted content are passed safely through each CLI's native arguments and input flow, making full use of Claude and Codex file and vision capabilities
  • [Fixed] Unified attachment routing across Q&A, Q&A Full Scan, Agent, and Claude/Codex modes so uploaded documents consistently reach model context
  • [Improved] Added attachment count and size limits, format validation, background parsing, cancellation, temporary-file cleanup, document parsing tests, and an attachment-refactor acceptance matrix
  • [Improved] Claude/Codex Q&A context management — Normal Q&A no longer scans the project implicitly; attachments, source, and scan results are request-local; history is trimmed to each provider's context window while preserving recent complete turns
  • [Enhanced] Native Claude/Codex Q&A — Claude supports native image messages, Codex supports native images and reasoning effort, Full Scan exposes only local read-only search tools, and streaming now handles cancellation, retries, partial answers, and protocol errors more reliably

idea-plugin.name: RX GUI
idea-plugin.description:
RX GUI — Reasonix AI Coding Assistant

基于 DeepSeek-Reasonix 的 AI 编程助手，内置于 JetBrains IDE 侧边栏。 支持流式响应、Markdown 渲染、代码 Diff 交互审阅、实时费用追踪。

Features / 核心功能

  • AI Chat — Sidebar streaming chat with Markdown + code syntax highlight / 侧边栏流式 AI 对话，Markdown + 代码语法高亮
  • Review Mode — Interactive diff for file edit (accept / reject), safe and controllable / 文件编辑交互式 Diff 审阅（接受 / 拒绝），安全可控
  • Mode Switching — review / auto / yolo with one click for different use cases / review / auto / yolo 模式一键切换
  • Model Presets — auto / flash / pro presets + low~max reasoning depth / 多种预设 + low~max 推理深度可选

idea-plugin.name: Celebrimbot
idea-plugin.description:
Celebrimbot is an IntelliJ Platform plugin that brings a full multi-agent AI system into your IDE. It can read your project files, write and modify code, execute terminal commands, search the web, inspect git history, and hold natural conversations — all from a single chat panel anchored to your IDE window.

Unlike simple autocomplete tools, Celebrimbot operates as an agentic loop: it routes requests intelligently, executes tasks locally when possible, escalates to cloud planning only when needed, and retries failures automatically — without leaving your editor.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Multi-module Gradle structure: project split into core/ (pure Kotlin), plugin/ (IntelliJ), server/ (standalone CLI + HTTP)
  • LazyModelManager: model loaded only on first use, auto-unloaded after 60s of inactivity — zero RAM overhead at IDE startup
  • Ollama-Compatible API: full drop-in replacement for Ollama with streaming support
    • POST /api/chat — chat completion with message history (streaming + non-streaming)
    • POST /api/generate — text generation (streaming + non-streaming)
    • GET /api/tags — list available models
    • GET /api/version — server version
    • GET /api/ps — list running models
    • POST /api/show — model information
    • POST /api/pull — download models from HuggingFace
    • POST /api/embed — embeddings (stub, recommends Ollama)
  • OpenAI-Compatible API: POST /v1/chat/completions with SSE streaming, GET /v1/models
  • ModelRouter: maps Ollama-style model names (e.g. qwen2.5-coder:1.5b) to GGUF files, single-model-in-RAM policy
  • ChatTemplateFormatter: proper chat template formatting for Qwen (ChatML), Llama 3, Phi-3, with auto-detection
  • download-model CLI command: download GGUF models from HuggingFace (--list to see available, -m to select)
  • Open WebUI support: docker compose --profile ui up starts Celebrimbot + Open WebUI on port 3000
  • ProjectCompass compatibility: set OLLAMA_HOST=http://localhost:16180 and llama-index works directly

Changed

  • CelebrimbotStartupActivity no longer loads model eagerly — model loads lazily on first inference
  • CelebrimbotEmbeddedEngine.askQuestion() now delegates to LazyModelManager.infer() for proper auto-unload
  • LocalModelManager (plugin) wraps LazyModelManager (core) instead of managing LlamaModel directly
  • ServeCommand (CLI) now delegates to CelebrimbotServer with all Ollama routes
  • StandaloneLlmEngine delegates to LazyModelManager — no more permanent model in RAM
  • Shadow plugin upgraded to com.gradleup.shadow:9.0.0-beta4 (Gradle 9 compatibility)
  • Docker compose reorganised with profiles: default (just Celebrimbot), ui (+ Open WebUI), with-ollama (+ Ollama sidecar)

Fixed

  • Memory leak: model stayed in RAM indefinitely even when unused
  • Double model loading on parallel requests (CelebrimbotServer now uses singleton engine)

idea-plugin.name: Cachly Brain
idea-plugin.description:
ChatGPT and Claude remember your conversations. cachly remembers your codebase.

The bug you fixed. Why you chose Postgres. The deploy step that always breaks — and everything your teammates learned. It stays when someone leaves the team, and it comes along when you switch assistants. This plugin brings that memory into your JetBrains IDE.

  • One-click setup — "Set Up AI Files" writes your MCP config, agent instructions, and a git post-commit learning hook. No terminal needed.
  • Brain Doctor — diagnoses your connection (API key, instance, network) and points you straight to the fix.
  • Ambient learning — detects repeated patterns and offers to save them as reusable lessons.
  • Proactive briefing — surfaces your top lessons on project open, so the brain greets you instead of waiting to be asked.
  • Status bar widget — live lesson count, brain health, and estimated tokens saved.
  • Lesson viewer — browse every learned lesson with recall counts and severity.

Try it without an account. On first start the plugin fetches a free trial brain by itself — no sign-up, no credit card, no key to paste. Link an account later to keep the data.

Works with the Cachly MCP server. Free tier forever · GDPR · EU servers.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.8.3

  • The first request now happens right after the trial starts. Measured on 2026-10-11: of 10 trial keys created by 0.8.x, 6 were never used for a single request. The status bar asked 2 s after the window opened, before the key existed, and then only every 300 s. Now the plugin makes one request with the new key immediately, shows the result in the status bar and says in a notification whether the Brain answered. If it did not, the notification says so and points to Brain Doctor.
  • A missing instance id is fetched. Without an instance id the plugin sent no request at all and the status bar said "not configured" forever. The plugin now asks /api/v1/instances/auto for it, after the trial, after linking an account, on project open and in "Set Up AI Files". Linking an account also no longer keeps the trial's instance id, which belonged to a different account.
  • The "How to connect your AI" link works. It pointed to cachly.dev/docs/jetbrains, which did not exist (HTTP 404). The page now exists.
  • "Set Up AI Files" also writes .junie/mcp/mcp.json. That is the project-level MCP file Junie reads, so Junie gets the Brain the same way Claude Code does through .mcp.json. JetBrains AI Assistant reads MCP servers from its settings only; the guide shows how to add the server there.

idea-plugin.name: IMS V6 Code Assistant
idea-plugin.description:
IMS V6 Code Assistant is an IntelliJ IDEA plugin for Pangus IMS V6 projects with built-in automation that reduces repetitive work and improves development efficiency.
面向 Pangus IMS V6 项目的 IntelliJ IDEA 插件，内置多项自动化能力，减少重复操作、提升编码效率。

核心能力
• 代码扫描与实时检测：Java 规则检查、手动扫描、严重级别和编辑器高亮配置。
• 代码生成与同步：从表结构 TSV 生成项目代码，并同步 Java 常量到前端。
• 一键二开：从平台菜单检索、源码预览到选择导入，快速完成菜单二次开发。
• 项目配置中心：集中管理路径、端口、版本、JDK、Maven、编码和常用 IDEA 设置。
• 升级、构建与初始化：平台升级备份、模块打包、模板初始化和运行配置创建。
• 开发辅助工具：数据库切换、Web/PDA 服务、图标库和插件手册。

Key Features
• Code inspections: Java rules, realtime analysis, manual scans, severity and editor highlighting.
• Code generation and sync: Generate files from TSV and sync Java constants to frontend code.
• One-click customization: Search platform menus, preview source code and import selected features for rapid customization.
• Project configuration: Centralized paths, ports, versions, JDK, Maven, encodings and IDE settings.
• Upgrade, build and bootstrap: Backup-aware upgrades, packaging, initialization and run configurations.
• Developer utilities: Database switching, Web/PDA servers, icon library and built-in manual.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Version 1.2.8

Added

  • 平台升级完成后自动标记文件变更到 SVN（均仅本地标记排入提交计划，不自动提交）：新写入的文件 （如前端新增的平台包文件）自动执行 svn add，被替换移除的旧文件自动执行 svn rm 排入删除，升级成功通知中显示标记结果；dist、node_modules 等可重建的 产物/缓存目录不纳入标记。仅对 SVN 工作副本生效，Git 等其他版本控制项目不受影响； 标记失败不影响升级结果，通知中会提示手动检查。

Changed

  • 二开导入预览中不再显示 XxxRun.java 文件名后的「待添加模型注册」状态提示，避免与勾选状态混淆。

idea-plugin.name: IT Crowd Pixel Agents
idea-plugin.description:
JetBrains edition of Pixel Agents — a pixel art office where AI agents (Claude Code terminals) are animated characters you can watch work in real time.
Compatible with PyCharm, WebStorm, and all JetBrains IDEs based on IntelliJ Platform 2025.1+. Requires Node.js to be installed.

idea-plugin.name: Diffy AI

idea-plugin.name: PipelinePilot for Jenkins
idea-plugin.description:
Edit, validate and run Jenkins pipelines from the IDE without the commit-push-wait loop.

PipelinePilot brings a fast, interactive workflow to Jenkins Pipeline development. Instead of emulating Jenkins locally, it connects your IDE to a real Jenkins instance: the editor handles the experience, Jenkins handles validation and execution on real agents, plugins, shared libraries and credentials.

Features
  • Instant validation — inline diagnostics from the Jenkins declarative linter, on save or on demand.
  • Quick-fixes — deterministic and AI-assisted intentions on linter errors.
  • Remote sandbox execution — press Ctrl+Enter to run the current Jenkinsfile on real Jenkins, isolated and ephemeral.
  • Live logs & stage graph — streamed console output and a visual graph of sequential, parallel and nested stages.
  • Replay — rerun the whole pipeline, only failed stages, or a single stage.
  • Shared library awareness — @Library detection, step autocomplete and navigation into vars/.
  • AI assistance — inline review with per-line findings and one-click fixes, via any OpenAI-compatible provider (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio, custom gateways).
Getting started
  1. Open Settings | Tools | PipelinePilot for Jenkins and set your Jenkins URL, username and API token.
  2. Open a Jenkinsfile and save it to see inline validation.
  3. Press Ctrl+Enter to run it in a remote sandbox and watch logs and stages stream back.
Links: Documentation & source · Issue tracker
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.0
  • Jenkinsfile validation with inline diagnostics and quick-fixes.
  • Remote sandbox execution with live log streaming and a stage graph.
  • Replay (whole pipeline / failed stages / single stage).
  • Shared library awareness: completion and navigation.
  • AI review popup with per-line findings; provider-agnostic (OpenAI-compatible).

idea-plugin.name: AI Agent Workspace Guard
idea-plugin.description:
Scan a JetBrains project for prompt injection, exposed credentials, and risky MCP or agent settings before you run a coding agent. Paid plugin, free 30-day trial. Scanning alone is free in AI Agent Workspace Guard Lite.

Run Tools → Scan AI Agent Workspace in the project you want to check. The plugin is a security scanner: it checks the project on demand and opens the results in the AI Agent Guard tool window. Processing stays on the local machine.

  • Agent instruction files, including prompt-injection directives that try to override policy, read secrets, or run remote code.
  • Agent permission settings and MCP configuration, including broad grants, auto-approved servers, unpinned packages, root paths, and inline credentials.
  • Credential-shaped files present in the workspace, such as .env, private keys, and credentials.json, including Git-ignored files, and their applicable .gitignore coverage. Git ignore rules do not restrict agent file access. Secret-shaped values such as API keys, tokens, and passwords in text and configuration files are checked separately.
  • GitHub Actions, package.json scripts, and n8n workflow JSON for risky execution patterns.

Select a finding to see the evidence and a suggested next step. Double-click it to open the reported line. Filter by severity, scan again, suppress an expected finding with aiwg:ignore, and copy or save a Markdown report.

Scope

Each scan is started manually. Findings are advisory and may include misses or false positives.

Perpetual license. 30-day trial. To scan and list findings for free, install AI Agent Workspace Guard Lite instead; the two plugins do not load side by side.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.1.6 — free update for existing licences.

  • Fixed: a credential in agent settings or MCP configuration was shown unmasked in the evidence and in saved reports when its key was quoted JSON or named like private_key. Evidence now masks every value whose key names a password, token, secret, API key, private key, or credential, including quoted values with spaces and short values.
  • If a file or folder cannot be read, the summary and the saved report now say the scan is incomplete instead of ending quietly.

2026.1.5 — free update for existing licences.

  • Credential-file findings now start with checking the file on disk, and name three concrete actions: move it out of the workspace, delete it, or restrict access to it with OS-level permissions.

2026.1.4 — free update for existing licences.

  • Credential-shaped files now remain visible as medium-severity findings when Git ignores them, and in folders without Git metadata.
  • Guidance explains that Git ignore rules do not prevent local agent access and suggests moving real credentials or enforcing file permissions.

2026.1.3 — free update for existing licences.

  • Fixed: a credential file was reported as unprotected when .gitignore covered it with an any-depth pattern such as **/.env.

2026.1.2

  • Results now open in a tool window instead of a text dialog. Findings are grouped by severity, double-click jumps to the exact line, and the panel below shows the evidence and the fix.
  • Severity filter and a Scan button, so you can work through findings without leaving the panel.
  • New: agent permission settings are scanned. Auto-approved MCP servers, unbounded Bash/Read grants, pre-approved destructive commands, HTTP hooks, disabled hooks, and disabled permission prompts in .claude, .cursor, .vscode and .codex settings.
  • New: credential files that .gitignore does not cover. A .env or private key without an applicable ignore rule is reported for review.
  • New: inline suppressions. Mark a line with aiwg:ignore (optionally naming a rule) to silence a known false positive. Suppressed findings stay visible in the count.
  • Reports can now be saved to a file, not only copied.

idea-plugin.name: ChainlessChain IDE Bridge
idea-plugin.description:
ChainlessChain IDE Bridge brings the ChainlessChain cc agent CLI into your JetBrains IDE — a full AI coding agent in a side panel that sees your editor, edits through native diffs you approve, and runs your app, without leaving the IDE.

It runs a localhost MCP server exposing your active selection, diagnostics, open editors and native diff review as tools the agent can call, and writes a discovery lockfile so a cc agent you run in any terminal auto-connects to this project's bridge.

What you get
  • Chat tool window with conversation tabs — talk to the agent in the right-dock "ChainlessChain" panel: streaming replies, tool-call trace, and multiple conversations as tabs (each its own cc agent process; switch instantly, close, reopen). Tabs and their sessions resume across IDE restarts. New chat (Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+Shift+D), reopen last closed (Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+Shift+R).
  • Editor-aware out of the box — your selection and open tabs ride along with every prompt; after the agent edits a file, the IDE's fresh errors/warnings flow back into the same run so it fixes what it broke. (CC_IDE_CONTEXT=0 to opt out.)
  • Native diff review — file edits become a side-by-side IDE diff: Accept, Request changes… (inline notes go back to the agent), or Reject (never writes). Multi-file changes open as a single openMultiDiff batch — accept all, pick files, or reject.
  • Approval modes & extended thinking — slash commands in the panel: /auto (accept edits), /bypass, /normal; /think · /ultrathink · /think-off (Anthropic). Also /new /stop /cost /context /plan /approve /reject.
  • Interactive plan & approval cards — plans and tool-permission prompts render as cards with Approve / Deny (Approve / Reject) buttons, right in the chat.
  • Selection actions & @-mentions — right-click code → Explain or Refactor; Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+Shift+K inserts an @file#L5-10 reference for the selection; type @ for a completion popup of @selection/@diagnostics + project files + class & method symbols.
  • In-editor app preview — Start App Preview finds your dev script, runs the dev server, detects the URL and embeds it (JCEF, with an external-browser fallback); a one-click Restart if the server dies.
  • Live context window — a subtle line under the chat shows model context usage after each turn.
Requirements: the ChainlessChain cc CLI on your PATH (npm i -g chainlesschain) and a configured model (Tools → "ChainlessChain: Configure LLM", or cc config). Open-source: github.com/chainlesschain/chainlesschain.

idea-plugin.description:
Cargo Buddy adds a floating Cargo toolbar for Rust crates in JetBrains IDEs.

Cargo Buddy detects the crate for the file currently open in the editor and lets you run Cargo commands without opening the project tree.

Features

  • Shows a floating editor toolbar for files inside a Cargo crate.
  • Runs Cargo commands against the nearest Cargo.toml for the current editor file.
  • Supports build, check, test, clippy, clean, publish, and dependency-ordered publish.
  • Resolves local Cargo dependencies with cargo metadata and publishes them before the current crate.
  • Keeps the Cargo tool window focused on the crate for the active editor tab.
  • Falls back to the system cargo executable and keeps command output in the IDE Run tool window.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changelog

All notable changes to Cargo Buddy will be documented in this file.

Unreleased

Added

  • Initial floating toolbar for current Rust crate Cargo commands.
  • publish action for publishing the current crate.
  • publish deps action for publishing local Cargo dependencies before the current crate.
  • Auto-focus for the Cargo tool window based on the active editor tab.
  • Crab plugin icon for light and dark themes.

idea-plugin.name: MockServer
idea-plugin.description:
Author, record, and debug HTTP/HTTPS mocks for MockServer without leaving your IDE.

MockServer lets you mock any system you integrate with over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3 (QUIC), HTTPS, or gRPC — services, REST or RPC APIs, and more — so you can build and test against simulated dependencies instead of real ones. This plugin brings the full MockServer toolset into IntelliJ IDEA and every other JetBrains IDE.

Highlights

  • Schema-driven expectation authoring — name a file *.mockserver.json and the editor validates it as you type, with autocompletion and hover documentation, using the same JSON Schema MockServer validates against. No language server, no extra setup.
  • Record real traffic into code — capture the requests MockServer proxied from a real upstream and save them as ready-to-use expectations, as JSON or as a Java DSL snippet.
  • Generate mocks from an OpenAPI/Swagger spec — turn the spec open in your editor into a full set of expectations in one action.
  • Live MockServer dashboard, embedded in the IDE — watch requests, inspect match results, and review active expectations in a dedicated tool window, without switching to a browser.

See the screenshots for record-to-code, schema authoring, and the in-IDE dashboard.

Everything it does

Server

  • Start MockServer (Docker) — launch the configured mockserver/mockserver container on the configured port with one click (the image tracks the plugin version by default).
  • Start MockServer (binary, no Docker) — for machines without Docker, launch MockServer from a self-contained binary bundle (a bundled Java runtime + jar, no Docker or separate JDK). Uses the configured bundle path, or downloads the checksum-verified bundle matching the plugin version for your OS/architecture and caches it; Stop (binary) terminates it.
  • Open MockServer Dashboard in IDE — embed the live dashboard in a right-hand tool window using the bundled JCEF (Chromium) engine, with Reload and Open-in-Browser buttons; falls back to your browser when JCEF is unavailable.
  • Open MockServer Dashboard — open the live dashboard in your default browser.
  • Reset MockServer — clear all expectations and recorded logs on the running server (confirms first).

Editor actions (operate on the active file)

  • Load Expectations Into Running Server — send the active file (a single expectation or an array) to the running server.
  • Save Recorded Expectations — retrieve expectations MockServer recorded from proxied/forwarded traffic and open them in a new tab, choosing JSON or Java DSL output.
  • Generate Expectations From OpenAPI Spec — send the active OpenAPI/Swagger spec (JSON or YAML) to MockServer and open the generated expectations.
  • Send Test Request — fire the ad-hoc HTTP request described in the active editor and open the response in a new tab.
  • Show Drift Report — fetch MockServer's mock-drift records (how real upstream responses differ from your stubs) and open a formatted report.
  • Find Requests by Trace — enter a W3C trace id or full traceparent value and open every received request carrying that trace as JSON.
  • View Trace in Backend — enter a W3C trace id or traceparent value and open the correlated trace in your trace backend (Jaeger/Tempo/Grafana) via a configurable URL template.

Advanced

  • Upload WASM Module — pick a compiled .wasm custom-rule module and upload it, then reference it by name as a WASM body matcher.
  • List WASM Modules — show the WASM custom-rule modules registered on the running server.
  • MockServer tool window — a dockable panel that surfaces every action as a one-click button, grouped into Server, Editor, and WASM rows.
  • Settings — configure the Docker image, container name, port, and the no-Docker binary bundle path under Settings | Tools | MockServer.

Requirements — a running MockServer instance at the configured port. Docker is optional: it is only needed for Start (Docker), and machines without Docker can use Start (binary, no Docker) instead. WASM actions require wasmEnabled=true on the server.

Links — mock-server.com for full documentation and client libraries, and the GitHub repository for source and issues.
idea-plugin.change-notes:

  • Stream-frame debugging — the in-IDE HTTP Debugger now shows paused stream frames in a Live Streams list and resolves each with Continue / Modify (Base64) / Drop

7.1.0 — first release; full IDE integration:

  • Expectation-file validation with JSON Schema completion and hover docs in *.mockserver.json files
  • Start MockServer via Docker, with a Docker-availability pre-check
  • Open the MockServer dashboard embedded in the IDE (JCEF) or in your browser
  • Load Expectations, Save Recorded Expectations (JSON or Java DSL), Generate From OpenAPI Spec, and Send Test Request from the active editor
  • Show Drift Report and Find Requests by Trace (W3C traceparent)
  • Upload and List WASM custom-rule modules
  • Reset the running server
  • Dockable MockServer tool window with one-click buttons grouped by Server / Editor / WASM
  • Settings for Docker image, container name, and port
  • UX polish: a marketplace icon, per-action icons and grouping in the Tools menu, a status line and section headers in the tool window, and a friendly "no server running" panel in the embedded dashboard

idea-plugin.name: AgentHub
idea-plugin.description:
AgentHub adds a toolbar button to every JetBrains IDE that launches any popular CLI coding agent in its own IDE terminal tab. Works with IntelliJ IDEA, PhpStorm, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, Rider and the rest.

Highlights

  • 40+ built-in agents — Claude Code (Anthropic), Codex CLI (OpenAI), Grok Build (xAI), Antigravity CLI (Google), Copilot CLI (GitHub), Cursor, Aider, Qodo, Qwen Code, Goose, OpenCode and many more.
  • Launch from the toolbar — or install a missing agent after a confirmation dialog.
  • Detection of installed agents on startup.
  • Project discovery — browse the projects and sessions of Antigravity, Claude Code, Cline, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Freebuff, Grok Build, Junie CLI, Kilo Code, Kimi Code, Kiro CLI, MiMo Code, Mistral Vibe, Oh My Pi, OpenCode and Qwen Code, and resume a session from the tool window.
  • Environment — see the skills, MCP servers, instruction files and configuration files each of those agents uses.
  • Shared skills — share a skill between agents, with a preview, backups and Undo.
  • Update notifications — a background check flags agents that have a newer version.
  • Manage from Settings — install, update or remove agents.
  • Custom agent — add your own CLI tool with a name, command and URL.
  • Companion tools — optional CLI utilities that work alongside the agents (usage tracking, context packing, skills); off by default.
  • Cross-platform — macOS, Linux and Windows (PowerShell helper script).
  • WSL mode (Windows) — optionally run every agent inside a WSL distribution instead of natively.

Open Settings/Preferences → Tools → AgentHub to choose which agents appear in the toolbar dropdown and to configure your custom agent.

Projects, Environment and Skills

The AgentHub tool window (right side of the IDE) shows the projects your coding agents have worked on, and the skills, MCP servers, instruction files and configuration files they use. Everything is read from local files and nothing is uploaded. Discovery is read-only. Skill files change only after you review a plan and confirm it.

  • Projects and Agents — sessions from Antigravity, Claude Code, Cline, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Freebuff, Grok Build, Junie CLI, Kilo Code, Kimi Code, Kiro CLI, MiMo Code, Mistral Vibe, Oh My Pi, OpenCode and Qwen Code, grouped by project or by agent. Sessions from several agents in the same repository appear as one project.
  • Sessions — each session shows the agent's title (or your first prompt), how many prompts you sent and when it ran. Resume reopens a session of any of these agents in its own CLI in a terminal; Transcript opens the session file.
  • Environment — skills, MCP servers, instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursor/rules, …) and configuration files per project or agent. Skills and MCP servers that exist under several agents are marked as identical or different. MCP secrets are never shown, only variable names.
  • Skills — share a skill between agents, resolve conflicts, restore backups and undo. Every change shows a plan first and backs up what it replaces.
  • Installed agents only — only agents whose CLI the latest detection found are shown, even before their first session.
  • Open in IDE and Launch — open a project in a detected JetBrains IDE, or start an agent with the project directory as its working directory.
  • Cached index — kept across IDE restarts and refreshed in the background.

Supported agents

  • Aider — Aider AI
  • Amp — Sourcegraph
  • Antigravity CLI — Google
  • Auggie — Augment
  • Claude Code — Anthropic
  • Cline — Cline
  • CodeBuddy — Tencent
  • Codex CLI — OpenAI
  • Cody CLI — Sourcegraph
  • Command Code — Command Code
  • Continue CLI — Continue
  • Copilot CLI — GitHub
  • Crush — Charm
  • Cursor CLI — Cursor
  • Devin — Cognition
  • Droid — Factory AI
  • ForgeCode — Antinomy
  • Freebuff — Codebuff
  • Goose CLI — Block
  • Grok Build — xAI
  • iFlow CLI — iFlow
  • Junie CLI — JetBrains
  • Kilo Code — Kilo
  • Kimi Code — Moonshot AI
  • Kiro CLI — Kiro
  • Kode — shareAI-lab
  • LeanCTL — LeanCTL
  • MiMo Code — Xiaomi
  • Mistral Vibe — Mistral AI
  • Muse Code — Meta
  • Oh My Pi — can1357
  • OpenClaw — OpenClaw
  • OpenCode — SST
  • OpenHands — All Hands
  • Pi — Mario Zechner
  • Qodo — Qodo
  • Qoder CLI — Qoder AI
  • Qwen Code — Alibaba
  • SWE-agent — SWE-agent
  • VT Code — vinhnx

Command Code, LeanCTL and Muse Code are hidden on Windows (no native Windows build, or a launch command that collides with a built-in Windows command). CodeRabbit CLI (companion tool) is hidden on Windows for the same reason (Windows support not released yet).

Companion tools — optional CLI utilities that work alongside the agents (off by default):

  • ccusage — token & cost usage reports from local agent logs
  • Claude Code Router — route Claude Code requests to other providers/models
  • Claude-Code-Usage-Monitor — live, predictive token & cost dashboard
  • code2prompt — codebase to LLM prompt, with Handlebars templating
  • CodeGrab — interactive TUI repo-context packer with secret redaction
  • CodeRabbit CLI — AI code reviews in the terminal
  • LiteLLM — self-hosted multi-provider LLM gateway with cost tracking
  • Repomix — pack your repository into an AI-friendly file
  • Semgrep CLI — static analysis security scanner
  • Skills — install reusable agent skills
  • TokenTracker — local token & cost dashboard
  • Tokscale — TUI token & cost dashboard with contribution graph
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.3.3

  • Skill sync restores the original when an atomic replace fails instead of deleting it.
  • Resume and Launch use the session's own directory and warn when it is missing.
  • Detection, update and install results belong to the environment they were started in; switching between Windows and WSL cannot apply a stale result. The tool window index is refreshed per environment.
  • A hung WSL distro lookup times out, and large output from background installs no longer blocks them.
  • Update checks validate the npm/pip report and show ? when the query fails. Update all clears the outdated flag only for agents that were updated, and update commands with pipes or fallbacks run as written.
  • Junie sessions beyond about 1,700 are no longer cut off. Session ids starting with - are refused.
  • Devin, ForgeCode and Junie CLI install through npm; ForgeCode is no longer hidden on Windows. The one-time Kimi migration prompt was removed.

1.3.2

  • WSL mode covers the tool window. Projects, sessions, skills, MCP servers, instruction files and configuration are read from the distribution's home directory. Resume and Launch start inside the distro, and skill sync works on the distro's skill folders.
  • Windows (native) and every WSL distribution keep their own settings: enabled agents and tools, detection results and update status. Check installed agents / Check installed tools ticks what the last detection found.
  • Skills: a Redundant links / copies section with Remove link / Remove copy on the Overview and the Agents tab. Remove copy also swaps an identical copy of an agent that cannot read the shared folder for a link. Clean up redundant copies… covers both.
  • An already shared skill no longer offers Move to Shared. Skill icons and the agent filter show the agents a folder belongs to; system skills are grouped by agent.
  • Plandex was removed. The links of Auggie, Cody CLI, Droid, Grok Build, Muse Code, OpenHands and Qodo were updated.

1.3.1

  • The tool window discovers seven more agents: Kilo Code, Kimi Code, Oh My Pi, Junie CLI, Mistral Vibe, Freebuff and MiMo Code (17 in total) — projects and sessions, Skills, MCP servers, instruction files and Config.
  • Resume now works for all 17 agents, using each CLI's own resume command. A session id that is not safe to pass to a command line is refused rather than quoted.
  • Skills: the sync engine was reorganised, and symlinked skill folders are now walked. Kilo Code, Kimi Code, Oh My Pi, Junie CLI, Mistral Vibe and MiMo Code are Share/Promote targets.
  • Discovery fixes: Claude AGENTS.md and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, OpenCode .opencode and OPENCODE_CONFIG(_DIR), Qwen .qwen/rules, and same-named Antigravity MCP servers are listed separately. An instruction file that an agent does not apply is still listed, with an info line saying why.
  • The Agents tab lists every installed agent, also before its first session: Projects and Sessions are greyed out until then, and Environment already shows the agent's global skills, MCP servers, instructions and configuration.
  • Fewer needless rescans: AgentHub's own saves no longer look like changes made by another IDE, unchanged results are not written again, and the Skills and Environment data is no longer re-read and re-scanned on every click in the tool window.

1.3.0

  • New Skills tab: browse global or project skills, search and filter them, and open or reveal their files.
  • Share skills between agents. Share… is one checklist: check an agent to share with it, uncheck it to stop. An agent-specific skill can be moved to the shared folder from the same button. Resync / Repair, Stop Sharing and conflict resolution (keep the shared version, the agent's version, or both) are included.
  • Every change shows a plan first and takes a backup before replacing anything. Undo and Restore Backup… still work after an IDE restart.
  • Migrate duplicates… and Clean up redundant copies… tidy identical copies in one reviewed batch.
  • Settings: preferred Link or Copy mode, backups, an option to review plans before applying them, and Manage existing skills (off by default), which lets Stop Sharing also remove links and identical copies AgentHub did not create.
  • Skill ownership, history, settings and backups are shared by all JetBrains IDEs in ~/.agenthub. Existing data is imported automatically.
  • The Environment tab also lists agent configuration files (Config), with warnings for approval-bypass or unrestricted sandbox modes. Credentials and raw file contents are never stored.
  • Projects, Agents and Skills share one layout. Sessions show the agent's title (or your first prompt), the prompt count and the time range, plus token, model, cost and tool statistics where the agent records them. Resume works for Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode; Transcript opens the session file.
  • The tool window shows only agents whose CLI was found by the latest detection. Detection now runs on every IDE start.
  • Also: many smaller UI, layout, keyboard and accessibility fixes in the tool window and Settings.

1.2.0

  • New AgentHub Projects tool window with read-only project and session metadata discovery for Antigravity, Claude Code, Cline, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor CLI, Grok Build, Kiro CLI, OpenCode and Qwen Code
  • Unified Projects and Agents views with search, per-agent session totals, last activity, normalized Git identity and a persistent cached index
  • Open a discovered project in a detected JetBrains IDE or launch a participating coding agent directly in the project's working directory
  • Inspect normalized Skills, MCP servers and instruction sources in the new read-only project and agent Environment tabs, with availability comparison, duplicate and conflict indicators for Antigravity, Claude, Cline, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Grok, Kiro, OpenCode and Qwen Code
  • MCP secrets and executable configuration are never rendered in the UI
  • Discovery runs outside the UI thread, isolates malformed provider records and is covered by a 10,000-session performance regression test

1.1.2

  • New agent: Oh My Pi (can1357) — coding-first fork of Pi with LSP/DAP integration, browser & desktop tools, subagents and 60+ providers
  • Fix: "Update all agents" ran every installed agent's update command regardless of whether a newer version was actually available — it now only updates agents flagged outdated by the last "Check for updates" run, matching the per-agent Update button in Settings
  • Fix (Windows): a failing version-check command (e.g. a missing runtime dependency) was silently reported as "up to date" instead of a warning, since the error text was mistaken for the version string

1.1.1

  • New agent: Muse Code (Meta) — terminal coding agent for multi-agent, repo-scale software engineering tasks (WSL-only on Windows)
  • New companion tool: Semgrep CLI — static analysis security scanner

1.1.0

  • New: WSL mode (Windows) — Settings → Behavior → "Run agents in:" lets you run every agent/companion tool inside a WSL distribution instead of natively. Detection is distro-native (ignores Windows binaries exposed through WSL interop), Linux/WSL-only agents (ForgeCode, LeanCTL, Plandex, Command Code) become available, and a missing pip/npm in the distro produces an install hint instead of failing silently
  • New agent: Pi (Mario Zechner) — minimalist terminal coding agent harness
  • New companion tools: Claude Code Router, Claude-Code-Usage-Monitor, code2prompt, CodeGrab, CodeRabbit CLI, LiteLLM and Tokscale

1.0.0 — first stable release

  • New Companion Tools section — optional CLI utilities that work alongside the agents: ccusage, Repomix, Skills and TokenTracker (off by default; enable in Settings)
  • New agents: CodeBuddy (Tencent), Command Code, Devin (Cognition), iFlow CLI, Junie CLI (JetBrains), Kode and OpenClaw

0.9.1

  • New agent: Freebuff (Codebuff) — the free, ad-supported terminal coding agent
  • Fixes: Toolbar install of a not-installed agent now honors the "Run operations in background" setting; a background-installed agent launches automatically once ready
  • Lowered minimum platform to JetBrains IDE 2024.1+ (build 241+)

0.9.0 — Initial release

  • 30 built-in CLI coding agents
  • One-click launch from toolbar; not-installed agents prompt to install with confirmation
  • Auto-detect on first install and after each plugin update
  • Background update availability check on IDE startup
  • Install / Update / Remove directly from Settings panel
  • Custom agent support: configure your own CLI tool with name, command and URL
  • Cross-platform: macOS, Linux, Windows (PowerShell helper script)

idea-plugin.name: Code Agent Path Helper
idea-plugin.description:
Code Agent Path Helper — one-click copy of file path references in @relative/path:line format for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor).

一个专为 AI 编程助手（如 Claude Code、Cursor）设计的轻量级辅助插件。

核心功能：在编辑器右键菜单或通过快捷键，一键提取当前文件的相对路径和行号，并自动拼接为 @相对路径:行号 格式（例如 @src/main/kotlin/Main.kt:12）复制到剪贴板。

完美契合各种 AI 智能体的上下文引用规范，告别手动翻找和拼接路径的烦恼，让 AI 更快、更准地定位你的代码！
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • 一键复制代码位置引用（@相对路径:行号 或绝对路径），供 AI 编程助手（Claude Code、Cursor、Copilot 等）使用
  • 相对路径 / 绝对路径双模式，带 enabled 启用开关与可配置基准目录
  • 编辑器右键菜单、项目文件树右键菜单入口
  • 行号支持：单行 #L42、多行选区 #L10-L20
  • 快捷键 Ctrl + Option + Cmd + C
  • Settings > Tools > Path Helper 配置界面

Added (English)

  • One-click copy of code location reference (@relative/path:line or absolute path) for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot)
  • Relative / absolute path dual mode with an enable toggle and a configurable base directory
  • Editor right-click menu and project view right-click menu entries
  • Line info: single line #L42, multi-line selection #L10-L20
  • Shortcut Ctrl + Option + Cmd + C
  • Settings UI at Settings > Tools > Path Helper

idea-plugin.name: Recap - AI Agent Sessions
idea-plugin.description:
Recap — one history viewer for every AI coding agent

Your AI coding agents scatter their session history across a dozen hidden folders and file formats. Recap pulls all of it into a single tool window inside your IDE — so you can find that conversation from last Tuesday, read exactly what the agent changed, resume where you left off, and see what your agents are actually costing you.

100% local. No accounts. No telemetry. No data ever leaves your machine.

Works with 14 agents — out of the box

Recap auto-discovers local sessions from Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Cline, Aider, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes, Droid, Pi, Antigravity, and ForgeCode — and presents them in one unified list, no configuration required.

Browse & search every session

  • Unified session tree grouped by project, agent, and date.
  • Full-text search across all conversations — your prompts, agent replies, tool calls, and file edits.
  • Filter by agent, project, and time range to cut straight to what you need.
  • Press Enter to preview a session; one click to open the full transcript.

Read transcripts the way you think

Every session opens with switchable views:

  • Session — clean chat bubbles of the whole conversation.
  • Timeline — a chronological map of turns, tool calls, and edits.
  • Changes & Git — every file the agent touched, with real diffs.
  • Terminal, Text, and JSON — raw views for when you need the source of truth.

Resume & export

  • One-click resume — relaunch any session in its native CLI, in the IDE terminal.
  • Markdown export of any transcript — always free.
  • Show in Recap History — right-click any file to see every agent edit that ever touched it, across all sessions.

Archive — keep the sessions that matter

CLI agents quietly rotate and delete old logs, so the session you want is often already gone. Recap's Archive saves durable backups that survive log rotation — so a conversation you archive stays readable forever, even after the agent wipes its own history.

  • Browse the archive — read every backed-up session in a dedicated tab.
  • Restore or delete — bring an archived session back, or remove it for good.
  • Expiry overview — see which live sessions are about to be rotated away, so you can archive them before they vanish.
  • Export transcripts — save any archived conversation to disk.

MCP & diagnostics

  • MCP Servers panel — see configured Model Context Protocol servers at a glance.
  • Diagnostics — quick health checks for your installed agents and their config.

Pro: analytics, cost & live monitoring

Upgrade to unlock the power-user surface:

  • Analytics — token usage and real-dollar cost across every provider, with weekly trends, per-model comparison, and a monthly budget guardrail that warns you before you overspend.
  • Optimizer — surfaces token-efficiency diagnostics so you can trim waste.
  • Live monitoring — the Cockpit and Live Feed stream your running agents' tool calls in real time.
  • Pro utilities — Plans and an Image Browser for everything your agents produced.

Why Recap?

  • Private by design — reads local session files only; nothing is uploaded.
  • Zero setup — install, open the Recap tool window, your history is there.
  • Vendor-neutral — one home for every agent you use, today and tomorrow.

idea-plugin.name: Prompt Bundler
idea-plugin.description:
Get your codebase into any AI chat, without the copy-paste hell.

Pasting code into a web chat usually means hunting files, copying them one by one, and losing the project structure that makes an answer good. Prompt Bundler fixes that: pick your files, get one clean, structured prompt, and paste it wherever you want.

🚀 What it does
Attach files, whole folders, or a selected snippet, then ask your question in the tool window. Prompt Bundler assembles a single, well-structured prompt ready on your clipboard.
  • Seamless Context Gathering: Attach files via the Project view, editor selection, drag-and-drop, or a quick picker.
  • Structured Output: Generates a prompt containing a clean file tree and the exact file contents.
  • Universal Compatibility: Works instantly with ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Mistral, Microsoft 365 Copilot, or any text-based LLM.
  • Smart Filtering: Binary and oversized files are skipped automatically.
  • Consistent & Traceable: Reuses templates for uniformity and keeps a history of past prompts.
🔒 Private by design
No API calls, no accounts, no network. Prompt Bundler strictly reads selected files and writes plain text to your clipboard. Your code never leaves your machine until you paste it into the chat you or your company approves.

💡 Why bother?
IDE AI agents are capped and getting pricier. Send large context questions to the web subscriptions your company already pays for, and save your limited IDE agent credits for the work that truly needs them.

❤️ Support the project
Prompt Bundler is completely free, open-source, and runs entirely offline. If it saves you from copy-paste hell, you can support the development here:
Sponsor on GitHub   Buy Me a Coffee

idea-plugin.name: Mindvista
idea-plugin.description:
Mind mapping plugin integrated with AI agent. By default, the plugin supports JetBrains Junie. You can specify another tool as follows:
  • Add a tool's command line via Settings|Tools|External Tools. You can use %ai_prompt% and %mindvista_task_name% macros to pass the task description and name to the tool. Click OK.
  • Open Settings, choose Tools|MindVista and select the tool in the "Resolve with Tool" combo.

How it works:

  • You create a mind map, add task nodes.
  • Right-click on a task node and choose "Resolve with 'Tool'".
  • MindVista generates an .md file with detailed instructions for the agent.
  • The agent reads the instructions and generates a response marking the task as "Resolved".

You can submit your bug reports and ideas here: https://github.com/mindvista/mindvista/issues

If you like the idea, please leave a review on the JetBrains Marketplace. Your support is important!
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Created version 0.7 announcement document highlighting model selection, interactive sessions, and other improvements.
  • Added model and effort selection dropdowns to the ad-hoc prompt dialog, allowing users to specify them directly when prompting the agent if the agent adapter supports models/efforts.
  • The "Resolve with..." and "Break down with..." context menu items now show the name of the selected model in parentheses if the agent supports models.
  • Added model and efforts selection dropdowns for AI agents in settings, showing the currently selected model from configuration if there is an agent adapter supporting it (currently Junie-only).
  • The MindVista settings now allow choosing a separate AI agent for the "Break down" action.
  • Agent sessions now run in an interactive terminal, so you can type input and reply to the agent directly in the console.
  • When the selected tool cannot be started, a notification with a shortcut to the MindVista settings is shown instead of a silent failure.

idea-plugin.name: TermGlyph
idea-plugin.description:
An alternative terminal for IntelliJ-based IDEs — xterm.js 6 with Unicode 11, so TUI tools like Claude Code render cleanly without overlapping text or broken layouts.

Combines a familiar, fast terminal with:
  • Clean TUI rendering — Claude Code's input box, borders, and dense output display without overlapping. Combining characters, wide glyphs, and emoji all get the correct column width.
  • Find (Cmd/Ctrl+F), copy/paste, and a native right-click menu.
  • Multiple tabs plus native side-by-side split (Split Right/Down), like the IDE's own terminal.
  • Dynamic tab icons and titles that follow the running process (Claude Code, Git, Docker, Node.js, and more).
  • Follows your IDE editor theme — background, foreground, and ANSI palette from the editor colour scheme.
