idea-plugin.name: AIVory Genie
idea-plugin.description:
Bring your own AI coding agent into JetBrains. Point the magic wand at code or screen, and trace every edit back to its prompt. Supports Claude Code, Codex, Gemini/Antigravity CLI, and Aider for full agentic edits, plus Ollama, OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, and Gemini API providers for chat.

Why AIVory Genie?

Everyone's shipping an AI agent plugin. Here's why this one's different.

  1. Your IDE already tracks file history - we map it against your prompts and chat sessions, so you see exactly what changed and why
  2. Point at part of your screen. We detect code vs. visuals and send text-with-source or a screenshot - whichever's leaner and more token-efficient
  3. You already have your CLI installed - we just call it, no extra cost, no API keys. Prefer an API key instead? Add Ollama, OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, or the Gemini API for chat-only access
  4. Not locked to one agent - switch between Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, and Aider without changing tools, using your existing subscriptions. All auto-detected, zero config. Or bring your own key and chat with Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, or the Gemini API instead
  5. Free, and staying that way for the foreseeable future. If you want to support us - buy us a coffee (yes please)

The Magic Wand - Capture Anything

Select any region of your screen and attach it to your prompt. Error dialogs, broken UI, architecture diagrams, console output - the AI gets the full picture, not just a file path. Screenshots are stored, thumbnailed, and linked to the session that used them.

Every Edit Traced to Its Prompt

Every AI-driven file change is captured with before/after content and tied to the exact prompt that caused it. Three history views - by prompt (what was asked), by session (full runs), by event (chronological stream). Don't like what the agent did? One-click revert. JetBrains Local History brackets every AI run so the IDE's own undo timeline stays clean.

Your Agent, Your Subscription

Claude Code is fully supported with streaming, session resume, image context, and MCP. OpenAI Codex CLI, Google Gemini CLI (including Antigravity), and Aider are supported and reaching full parity. All backends are auto-detected on startup - zero configuration. Slash commands, models, and permission modes adapt to whichever agent is active.

Prefer an API key over a CLI? Add any number of providers under Tools â†’ AIVory Genie: Ollama, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (OpenAI, OpenRouter, LM Studio, vLLM, Groq, DeepSeek, Together), the Anthropic API, or the Google Gemini API. A local Ollama server is found automatically, and every key is kept in the IDE's password store. These providers stream chat replies with your code context attached, but they cannot edit files, run tools, or use MCP - only the CLI agents above do that.

IDE Intelligence via MCP

An embedded MCP server exposes open files, editor selection, code analysis problems, VCS status, and file structure to connected agents. The AI sees what your IDE already knows - warnings, type hierarchies, change status - not just raw file contents.

Structural Code Map

Full AST index of your project - modules, classes, methods, fields - organized by application layer. Select symbols to scope your conversation instead of describing paths in prose. Updates live as you edit.

Chat

Markdown rendering, syntax-highlighted code blocks, tool call cards, token badges, cost tracking, extended thinking display. Slash commands adapt per backend - /compact, /review for Claude; /add, /undo for Aider. Type @ to attach files, drop images, or Ctrl+K for inline edits.

Right-Click AI Actions

  • Generate Documentation - doc comments from code structure
  • Edit Selection (Ctrl+K) - rewrite selected code inline
  • Explain Error - send stack traces for instant explanation
  • Run Tests - execute tests and feed failures to the agent
  • AI History - every AI edit that touched the current file

Sessions & Personas

Full conversation history with metadata: model, tokens, cost, duration. Resume any session, pin favorites, search, export to Markdown. Define custom system prompts as persona files and switch per session.

Made by AIVory, Inc.

Developer tools at AIVory.

Bugs & Feature Requests

File issues on GitHub or leave a review on the JetBrains Marketplace.

idea-plugin.name: AI Worktree Reviewer
idea-plugin.description:
AI Worktree Reviewer

Review changes across multiple Git worktrees without leaving your editor — built for the era of AI coding agents that work several branches in parallel.

  • Active Worktrees tool window — every worktree in one list, each with +/- change badges, ↑ahead ↓behind against its upstream, and a dot when the tree is dirty
  • Commit graph — a worktree's history drawn as a colored lane graph, branches and merges included. Commits the base branch already contains are dimmed, so you can see where the branch forked
  • Uncommitted work up front — a dashed node sits on top of HEAD and is selected on open, so a dirty worktree shows its changes right away
  • Diff at any level — HEAD vs working tree for uncommitted changes, parent vs commit for a single commit (merge commits included), or everything the branch adds since its merge-base with the trunk via Review vs base
  • Review all — page through every changed file in a single diff tab
  • Open a worktree as a project, or remove it — all from one panel
  • Toggle the panel with Alt+Shift+W

All git calls run on a background thread with a hardened environment and a timeout, so the IDE never freezes and never blocks on a credential prompt.

This project exists to keep development human-paced, understandable, and owned.

Requirements

  • Codex CLI
  • Node.js 22 or later

idea-plugin.name: Guidewire AI Agent
idea-plugin.description:
Creator of the Guidewire AI Agent, an enterprise-grade, agentic IDE plugin that transforms how Guidewire developers build and maintain ClaimCenter, PolicyCenter, and BillingCenter applications.

The agent specializes in context-aware Gosu code generation, universal structural injection for PCF UI and XML entity extensions, and intelligent legacy code refactoring—all safeguarded by IntelliJ's native Diff Viewer for complete developer control.
idea-plugin.change-notes:

  • Custom MCP Support: Added support for custom MCP although, it's in Beta mode now.

Version 4.0.0

  • Multiple Chats & Side Panel: Added a collapsible side drawer (hit the ☰ button to open it). You can now handle multiple chat threads at once, open a new chat, delete old ones, or rename titles.
  • Smart Titles & Separated History: Chats now automatically get named based on what you type first. Each chat keeps its own separate memory so they don't bleed into each other, and everything stays saved even if you restart the IDE.

Version 3.2.1

  • Dedicated History Logs Tab: Added a brand new "History Logs" tab that silently archives up to 300 of your past messages to persistent storage. You can now freely clear your active chat to refresh the AI's memory and save tokens, while safely preserving your entire conversational history in a read-only log!
  • Live Console Error Auto-Fixer: The AI agent now seamlessly watches your local IntelliJ Run console for server crashes. If a Tomcat/Guidewire exception is thrown, the plugin instantly catches the stack trace and drops an alert into your chat with a one-click Auto-Fix with AI button to resolve the bug.

Version 3.1.109

  • Custom AI Profiles & Templates: Personalize your AI assistant! You can now append custom instructions or choose from highly-tailored Guidewire personas (like "Senior Architect", "Integration Expert", or "Gosu Purist") in Settings to dictate the AI's coding style.
  • New Chat Command: Type /profile directly in the chat to instantly open your AI persona settings.
  • Cleaner UI Experience: Decluttered the main chat window by moving Session Metrics (Accuracy & Latency) to their own dedicated "Metrics" background tab.

Version 3.0.21

  • Mention files using '@': User can now mention specific files that they would like the LLM to notice.
  • Bug fix: Prompt too long bug, which was causing due to large context transport to LLM has been fixed.

Version 3.0.2

  • Click-able "/" buttons: Command links and options in system messages can now be clicked directly to execute them instantly.
  • Persisting chat history: Chat and prompt histories are now automatically saved and restored across project reopens and IDE restarts unless explicitly cleared.

Version 3.0.1

  • LLM Context Caching: Integrated ephemeral prompt caching boundaries to dramatically slash token costs and accelerate inference speeds for massive configuration files.
  • Automated GUnit Test Generation: Introduced the new /test slash command with custom argument support to instantly analyze open Gosu classes and generate comprehensive, mock-heavy test suites.
  • Proactive Code Inspections: Implemented native IntelliJ LocalInspectionTool background parsing to flag performance anti-patterns (such as N+1 database queries inside loops) with real-time editor warnings and AI quick-fixes.
  • Data Dictionary Architecture Graphing: Built a high-performance background XML indexer for .eti and .etx files, providing the AI with instant, zero-latency context on database entities, foreign keys, and typelists.

Version 2.2.50

  • Smart Context Controls:Added an interactive "Include context" toggle and intelligent casual chat detection. The AI now automatically recognizes greetings and skips unnecessary file analysis, saving you API tokens and time.
  • Transient Action Logging:Real-time AI operations (like reading files, searching the codebase, or executing terminal commands) are now displayed in a sleek, temporary status view under the loading spinner that gracefully clears upon completion to keep your chat history pristine.

Version 2.2.32

  • System instructions updated related to file parsing.
  • Metrics monitoring added for accuracy and latency.

Version 2.2.30

  • Interactive Slash Commands:Type / in the chat box to access a suite of powerful CLI-style utilities natively.
  • Smart Auto-Complete Pop-over:Instantly filter and auto-complete commands using the new searchable pop-over menu that appears the moment you type /.
  • Quick Configuration:Use /settings or /login to immediately open the AI configuration panel over your workspace without navigating IDE menus.
  • Instant Theme Toggling:Type /theme to dynamically switch the Chat UI between Dark and Light mode on the fly.
  • Session Management:Use /provider (or /model) to check your active LLM engine, and /logout to securely wipe Enterprise SSO and Microsoft 365 tokens.

Version 2.2.15

  • Depreciation fixes.

Version 2.1.0

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot Support: Added full integration for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Azure OpenAI. You can now connect securely to your corporate Azure tenant endpoint using either a standard API Key or an Entra ID Bearer Token.
  • Dynamic Settings & Telemetry: Completely revamped the branding panel in the settings menu. It now displays your active AI engine in real-time as you switch providers and automatically tracks your installed plugin version.
  • UI/UX Enhancements: Upgraded the settings dashboard with a sleek new custom background, improved typography contrast for better readability, and added a quick "Contact the Developer" link for direct support.

Version 1.2.0

  • Autonomous web navigation bug fix:Fixed the ability for LLMs to autonomously navigate web browser

Version 1.1.09

  • UI improvements: You will now be able to toggle to history convo, using Alt + Shift + Up/Down to navigate prompt history.
  • Added theme button: Added a good old theme toggler.

Version 1.1.08

  • Navigation Bug Fix: Implemented an autonomous navigation interceptor that automatically detects and executes browser requests directly from the AI, bypassing "WebFetch" errors and ensuring seamless page transitions without requiring manual intervention.

Version 1.1.07

  • Code Generation Fix: Prevented the AI from incorrectly injecting HTML tags (like <p>) into GosuDoc and code comments.
  • Clickable Chat Links: URLs provided by the AI in the chat are now clickable and open seamlessly in the IDE's built-in Web Browser tab.

Version 1.1.04

  • Updating SVG

Version 1.1.03

  • Total Situational Awareness: The AI now silently reads your active IDE editor! It automatically injects the full, un-capped contents of your currently open file and focuses on your highlighted text, giving the AI massive architectural context without manual copy-pasting.
  • Markdown & HTML Rendering: Completely rebuilt the Tool Window chat history to natively parse and display beautiful Markdown, including syntax-highlighted Gosu/XML code blocks and configuration tables.
  • Universal PR Interceptor: The terminal engine now features a smart Regex scanner that watches output across all Git providers (Bitbucket, GitLab, GitHub). If an AI hallucinated command fails but a valid PR creation link is detected in the git output, the IDE intercepts it and automatically launches your browser.
  • Enhanced UX & Task Control: Upgraded the prompt input box to a multi-line, auto-expanding text area with Shift+Enter support. Added a "Stop" button to safely abort long-running AI generation or terminal background tasks.
  • Stability & Compliance: Fixed MalformedJsonException crashes to gracefully handle conversational AI responses. Resolved JetBrains Marketplace deprecation warnings for CredentialAttributes, ensuring full compatibility with 2025 and 2026 IDEs.

  • Conversational Memory: Added context retention to the Claude CLI provider so the AI agent remembers your current work and previous prompts within a session.
  • Process Management Stability: Improved background task cancellation logic to destroy process trees, preventing orphaned Node.js zombie processes (fixing the -4082 EBUSY file lock bug).
  • Terminal Automation: Automatically parse and execute CLI/Git commands (like raising PRs) directly in the background using a secure IDE approval prompt.
  • Interactive Chat Chips: Added dynamic "Quick Reply" buttons inside the Tool Window for 1-click execution of AI-proposed terminal commands.

Version 1.0.0-SNAPSHOT

idea-plugin.name: Ratchet Commit Message for Claude
idea-plugin.description:
Generates a Git commit message from your changes using Claude, right inside the commit dialog. It adds a button to the commit message toolbar (next to the AI Assistant button). On click, the plugin collects the diff of the files included in the commit and generates a commit message with Claude. By default it reuses your existing Claude Code (CLI) login (no API key required), but it also accepts an Anthropic API key. Configure it under Settings > Tools > Claude Commit Message.

Messages are written in English (en-US) by default, and you can pick from around 90 supported languages — including regional variants such as pt-BR, en-GB, es-419, fr-CA and zh-Hans/zh-Hant — or type any other language code you need.

A Ratchet product, developed by Raphael Moral Piazera — GitHub · LinkedIn.

Independent integration — not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. Claude is a trademark of Anthropic, PBC.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.4.0
  • Branch Off with Claude: started coding on the wrong branch? A new toolbar button stashes the checked changes, pulls the current branch, creates a new branch — Claude suggests the name — from the updated base and commits your changes on it with a Claude-written message. Unchecked changes are discarded only after an explicit, per-file confirmation; everything else is recoverable at every step (a failed pull restores your changes, a conflicted apply preserves the stash).

0.3.3
  • Compatibility: fixed a crash risk on IDEs 2026.2+ caused by a reference to an internal platform API (the plugin now passes the JetBrains Plugin Verifier with no internal API usages). Behavior is unchanged: the files checked for commit remain the only source of truth for both actions.

0.3.2
  • Bug fix: the diff sent to Claude could include files that were not checked for commit. The checked files are now the only source of truth — both for generating the message and for the split commit (plan and commits), which strictly follow your selection.

0.3.1
  • The toolbar buttons are now grayed out and unclickable while no changes are checked for commit, and both actions operate on exactly the files you have checked.
  • New Split Commit icon — a row of small dots, blue and white like the main button.

0.3.0
  • Split Commit with Claude: a second toolbar button asks Claude to split your changeset into logical commits. Review the proposed groups in a dialog — checkbox per commit, editable messages, per-file diff preview — and commit the selected ones in order, one click.
  • Plugin renamed to Ratchet Commit Message for Claude (same plugin, same settings).

0.2.1
  • Plugin renamed (same plugin, same settings — nothing else changes).

0.2.0
  • Stop button — while a message is being generated, the toolbar button turns into a stop button: click it to cancel instantly (the CLI process is killed / the API request aborted). The message field is left untouched.
  • Configurable diff size limits — new "Max diff size" and "Per-file diff limit" settings. The global limit now also applies to the API-key mode (previously unbounded), and truncation is no longer silent: omitted files are listed in the diff and Claude is told when the diff is partial. The optional per-file limit trims only oversized file bodies (headers always kept), so a giant lockfile can't crowd out your code changes.
  • Keyboard shortcut — Ctrl+Alt+G triggers the generation from the commit dialog.
  • Progress is now shown step by step ("Collecting diff…", "Asking Claude…").

0.1.8 — Bug fix
  • Fixed the CLI (WSL) login failing when the default WSL distro is a non-interactive one (e.g. docker-desktop, registered by Docker Desktop). It produced a misleading "not logged in" / "bash: not found" error even when you were logged in. The plugin now automatically targets a real distro in that case.
  • Added a WSL distro setting under Settings > Tools > Claude Commit Message to pin the distro where Claude Code is installed (empty = auto-detect).

idea-plugin.name: kUML
idea-plugin.description:
kUML — Kotlin-based UML & C4 modelling

Adds first-class IntelliJ support for kUML diagram scripts (*.kuml.kts):

  • Recognises *.kuml.kts as a custom Kotlin script kind via the org.jetbrains.kotlin.scriptDefinitionsProvider extension point.
  • Syntax highlighting and structural navigation are inherited from IntelliJ's Kotlin language support — no custom lexer or parser.
  • Default imports for the kUML DSL (dev.kuml.core.dsl.*, dev.kuml.uml.dsl.*, dev.kuml.c4.dsl.*) are visible to the editor, so unqualified classDiagram { ... }, c4Model { ... }, and friends resolve without explicit imports.
  • Distinct file icon for kUML scripts.

Rendering, code generation, OCL validation, and state-machine simulation are provided by the kuml CLI and the dev.kuml Gradle plugin — this IDE plugin is intentionally minimal and stays out of the render pipeline.

Without the Kotlin plugin (WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, Rider, CLion, DataGrip, RubyMine): the plugin still loads and provides the kUML file icon and the live split-view SVG preview. Script recognition, completion, structure view, folding, rename and inline diagnostics require the Kotlin plugin and activate automatically once it is installed.

Project page: https://kuml.dev.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.54.0

  • Fixed the Marketplace-verifier INTERNAL_API_USAGES failure that silently blocked every submission from 0.51.0 through 0.53.0: the Markdown preview integration now uses the sanctioned MarkdownBrowserPreviewExtension extension point instead of the internal/obsolete CodeFenceGeneratingProvider — same rendered result, no behavior change for users. CI now runs the Plugin Verifier before every publish, so this class of regression can't reach the Marketplace unnoticed again.
  • Markdown preview: a rendering kuml fence now reserves its previous height (or a sane default) instead of collapsing to zero, removing the layout jump that appeared on every keystroke while editing a diagram inside a Markdown document.

0.51.1

  • Internal fix, no user-visible behavior change: the diagram export dialog no longer triggers a Marketplace-verifier "deprecated API" finding. The compile-time IntelliJ Platform SDK moved to 2025.1.7.2; the export dialog's descriptor is now built reflectively so it keeps working identically on every IDE version this plugin supports (still 2024.3+).

0.51.0

  • kUML diagram preview in Markdown documents: kuml fenced code blocks render as inline SVG in IntelliJ's built-in Markdown preview, with gutter export/copy actions and Kotlin syntax highlighting inside the block.
  • kUML diagram preview in AsciiDoc documents: [source,kuml] listing blocks and kuml::path.kuml.kts[] block macros render as inline SVG in the official AsciiDoc plugin's preview. Both are optional plugin dependencies — kUML still loads normally without the Markdown or AsciiDoc plugins installed.

0.20.0

  • org.jetbrains.kotlin is now an optional dependency. The plugin now installs and runs on IDEs without the Kotlin plugin (WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, Rider, CLion, DataGrip, RubyMine): the file icon and the live split-view SVG preview work everywhere. Script recognition, completion, structure view, folding, rename and diagnostics activate automatically when the Kotlin plugin is present, via a new config-file fragment (META-INF/kuml-kotlin-support.xml).

0.19.2

  • Internal API removed: the plugin's bundled DSL classpath is now resolved purely via the JDK (Class.getResource → lib/ jar), no longer through the internal PluginManager/PluginManagerCore APIs — clears the Marketplace verifier "internal API usage" problem.
  • Replaced deprecated FileChooserDescriptorFactory.createSingleFileDescriptor() with the documented FileChooserDescriptor(...) constructor.

0.19.1

0.19.0

  • Published to JetBrains Marketplace — install via Settings → Plugins → Marketplace → search "kUML".
  • Scroll Pane for SVG preview: horizontal and vertical scrollbars appear automatically for large diagrams.
  • Hand-drag interactor: left-click + drag pans the view; mouse wheel scrolls; Ctrl+wheel zooms.
  • Zoom model revised: fit/zoom actions control canvas preferred size (scroll-compatible).
  • Toolbar redesign: icon-only buttons + new Fit Width / Fit Height / Zoom Out actions.
  • Plugin icon updated: navy background with golden {k} monogram and "kUML" lettering.
  • Live preview now renders via external kuml CLI — no bundled renderer required.
  • New kuml diagnostics command: emits compile/eval errors as TSV for IDE integration.

0.18.0

  • Live Preview repariert: Renderer- und Layout-Module (kuml-layout-api/bridge/elk/grid, kuml-themes-core/themes, kuml-io-svg) werden jetzt in das Plugin gebündelt — vorher fehlten sie im Plugin-Classpath, sodass renderToSvgReflective() immer null zurückgab und nur „No diagram" erschien.

idea-plugin.name: Sigil - Coding Assistant
idea-plugin.description:
Sigil - Coding Assistant

Sigil is a coding assistant plugin for IntelliJ that integrates with the IDE instead of just wrapping the CLI. It runs the Pi coding agent as its backend.

Most coding assistant plugins fall into one of two camps: a thin CLI wrapper with no real IDE integration, or a bloated plugin that pushes its own workflow and ideas on you. This one tries to stay out of the way.

The bigger problem with coding assistants is that they tend to take the wheel. They write code, you accept it, and you move on. That makes it easy to ship stuff you don't fully understand. Sigil focuses on review as a first-class step: you can review code the agent wrote inline in the editor before anything reaches GitHub or your CI. The goal is to catch mistakes early and make sure the code you commit actually meets your standards.

What it does

  • AI chat inside the IDE - Ask questions, paste code, attach files and screenshots, and get answers in a side panel. Responses render markdown, code blocks, and inline tool usage.
  • Sessions - Conversations are persisted and listed with their age, token usage, and estimated cost. Sub-task sessions spawned by delegation appear in the same sidebar and you can watch them work live.
  • Agents and delegation - An orchestrator agent can split a request into subtasks and delegate to researcher, planner, coder, tester, and reviewer subagents, each with its own configurable model and thinking level.
  • Context panel - See what model is active, how much context you're using (broken down by role and by tool), and your running token and cost totals.
  • Context management - Compact manually with an optional guidance prompt, let background compaction prepare summaries while you keep working, and prune stale tool results out of the conversation.
  • Code review - Ask the agent to review your changes, then work the results in a dedicated Review tab and as inline comments in the editor gutter. Resolve, reply, delete, or drop in your own comments.
  • Slash commands and skills - A / palette for commands like /compact, /review-perform, and /generate-context, and a $ palette for skills. The plugin also ships a set of bundled skills into your project.
  • IDE tools with real permissions - The agent gets actual IDE tools (code intelligence, inspections, builds, debugger, git, refactoring) plus any MCP servers you connect. Every tool is individually set to allow, ask, or deny.
  • Game development support - Settings pages for the Unity CLI and for ue-mcp (Unreal Engine), asset-aware tools, and an experimental set of Rider tools for C# work.

Review workflow

The review feature is one of the more useful parts. There are a few commands that drive it:

  • /review - reads the review comments that already exist in .review/ and works with you to resolve them.
  • /review-perform - runs a stricter, adversarial review of your current changes and writes comments to .review/. Takes an optional model argument.
  • /review-perform-gaming - same as /review-perform, but tuned with a game-engine checklist (Unreal C++, Unity C#).
  • /review-resolve - sends all open comments to the agent and asks it to fix the code and mark them resolved.
  • /review-recheck - re-runs the review with awareness of existing comments and your replies, so the agent can verify whether unresolved issues were actually fixed and catch new ones.

When a review finishes, you get a Review tab that lists files, comment counts, and line change summaries; inline comments in the editor gutter that you can resolve, reply to, delete, or add your own comments to; and a chat message summarizing what the review found.

You can also add your own comments by right-clicking a line and choosing Add Review Comment. Whatever you leave behind lives in the repo with the rest of the review state, and the agent picks it up on the next resolve or recheck pass.

Agents and delegation

Big jobs don't have to happen in one conversation. When the orchestrator gets something larger than a quick fix, it can break the work into subtasks and hand each one to a specialized subagent: a researcher that reads the codebase and reports back, a planner that turns a feature into a chunk plan, coders and testers that each own one file-scoped chunk, and a reviewer that goes over the result looking for flaws. There's also a council: it fans the same review out to several models in parallel and synthesizes a consensus report.

Every subtask runs as its own session, and those show up in the sidebar while they run. You can open one and watch the messages stream, but you can't prompt it directly. A banner explains that it's managed by the agent, and a "Back to parent" link takes you back to your own conversation.

The Agents & Delegation settings page controls the cast: toggle each agent on or off, decide which agents the orchestrator is allowed to invoke, cap how many subtasks a session can spawn, pin a model and thinking level per subagent, and pick the models that sit on the council.

Context and compaction

The Context tab is the honest ledger: provider and model, a usage bar broken down by role (system + tools, user, assistant, tool calls), a per-tool breakdown of which tools ate your window, and running token and cost totals for the session.

Compaction comes in two flavors. Manual: hit Compact Now (or type /compact), optionally with a guidance field pointing the summary at what matters. Background: flip it on, set the context percentage where it should kick in, and Pi prepares the summary while you keep working instead of blocking a turn.

Context pruning is the surgical option. Instead of summarizing everything, it drops individual tool results that have stopped earning their place: duplicate tool calls, old errored inputs, and superseded read/write/edit results. Recent turns are protected, and a net-benefit gate skips pruning when the cache invalidation would cost more than the tokens saved. The settings page configures the rules, /context-pruning gives you live control during a session, and the Context panel's Prune button clears every prunable result at once.

Tool output can also be truncated at insertion time, for the tools that like to dump a hundred KB of logs into your context window.

Tools and permissions

The agent doesn't just get "run this shell command". It gets the IDE: symbol search, call-site analysis, error and lint inspection, project builds, the debugger, git history and blame, safe renames. On IntelliJ IDEA the bridge also exposes PSI-backed code intelligence; other IDEs get the host-agnostic set.

Every tool is individually gated. Allow runs without asking, ask shows a permission prompt in the chat, and deny keeps the tool out of new sessions entirely. The same table covers tools discovered from the MCP servers you've connected, plus the agent's built-in tools (read, write, edit, bash, and friends), so you can switch off whatever you don't want a model near. Brave mode auto-approves the ask prompts when you trust the session; explicit denies still hold.

Game development

Two settings pages wire the agent into game engines.

Unity CLI points at your unity binary (Detect finds it on PATH or in the Unity Hub), installs the official Unity-Technologies skill collection into the project's .pi/skills/, and can install the InspectCode (jb) CLI used for C# code analysis on Rider.

Unreal Tools sets up ue-mcp, an MCP server that exposes the UE editor (assets, blueprints, levels, Niagara, gameplay) to the agent through MCP tool calls. Point it at your .uproject, pick a context strategy (lean, around 23k tokens, is the default; full is around 45k; micro if you're really counting), and install. The bridge plugin that lands in the UE project is C++, so you compile it with the project itself; Sigil never runs Unreal Build Tool for you.

On top of the pages, a Game Assets tool family adds asset-aware project probes, and Rider hosts get an experimental set of C# tools: find usages, solution summary, Unity and Unreal editor state, and InspectCode runs.

Requirements

  • An IntelliJ Platform IDE, 2026.2 or newer (IntelliJ IDEA, Rider, PyCharm, WebStorm, and friends).
  • The pi CLI installed and available on your system PATH, or its path set in Settings → Tools → Sigil.

Installing

Install directly from the JetBrains Marketplace (Settings → Plugins → Marketplace, search for "Sigil"), or download the latest ZIP from the GitHub releases page and install it through Settings → Plugins → Install Plugin from Disk.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
What's New

Async Subtask Delegation

  • Subtasks are now delegated asynchronously, allowing the agent to dispatch work to subtasks without blocking the main conversation while they run.
  • Long-running subtasks execute in the background, keeping the main thread responsive and free to accept new input or issue additional delegations.
  • Results from delegated subtasks are collected and surfaced as they complete, streamlining multi-step workflows.

Per-Skill Settings

  • Each skill now has its own dedicated settings, so configuration can be tuned on a per-skill basis rather than applied globally.
  • Skill-specific preferences are managed independently, making it easier to customize behavior for individual skills without affecting others.

UI Improvements

Chat Input

  • The chat input receives a comprehensive overhaul, improving how messages are composed and submitted.
  • The redesigned input integrates with the new async delegation and per-skill settings workflows for a more cohesive experience.

idea-plugin.name: Karato - Agent for Sakana AI fugu
idea-plugin.description:
Karato is an in-IDE agent for Sakana AI Fugu (and fugu-ultra). It drives the OpenAI Codex CLI — configured with Sakana's Fugu provider — as a subprocess and renders its streamed events as a multi-tab chat tool window: chat with the agent, watch it run commands and edit files in your project, approve actions inline, and review changes as they happen.

Features

  • Multi-tab chat with inline tool cards (run command / web search / file edits).
  • Interactive approvals and structured prompts shown inline.
  • GUI-only setup — installs Codex, writes the provider config, stores your API key.
  • Reads your existing Claude/Codex project files (CLAUDE.md, .claude/, project memory) so you don't paste them each turn.
  • Mirrors your Claude MCP servers (e.g. Playwright) into Codex so they work here too.

Data & external services

Karato is a client for your own accounts and tools. To function it: sends your prompts and selected project context (the files listed above) to the Sakana AI API via the Codex CLI; runs the Codex CLI and, when MCP is enabled, MCP servers (e.g. via npx) as subprocesses; reads the listed Claude/Codex configuration files; and writes MCP entries to ~/.codex/config.toml. Your Sakana API key is stored in the IDE's PasswordSafe and passed to Codex via an environment variable. Karato collects no telemetry and sends nothing to the author. A Sakana account/API key and network access are required.

Open source (Apache-2.0) — github.com/Ardelhite/idea-ai-integration.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 0.1.5 — Default the permission mode to Agent (full access) so routine commands (docker, temp-file writes, cleanup rm) no longer hit Codex's "blocked by policy" rejection in the default setup. Also make the chat "Mode" dropdown take effect on the very next message (the sandbox is now overridden per turn, not only at New Conversation), and handle Codex's item/permissions/requestApproval escalation so Ask-mode approval requests actually appear inline instead of silently failing as "blocked by policy". Auto mode now also bypasses the sandbox (like Agent), and 0.1.5 performs a one-time migration of previously saved modes to Agent; after that, user-selected modes are respected and Default/Ask plus Plan remain sandboxed. Karato now also requires an IDE restart after install/update, so the Plugins page shows JetBrains' restart button instead of letting a half-loaded install fail on the first prompt.
  • 0.1.4 — Fix "Update codex" never completing: the updater now refreshes the Fugu installer before running, compares against the version the Fugu bundle actually pins (not the npm release), and the yellow gear returns to normal once Codex is up to date.
  • 0.1.3 — Compatibility fixes flagged by the Plugin Verifier on newer IDEs: remove the runtime-breaking IconUtil.colorize call (NoSuchMethodError on 2025.2+), replace the scheduled-for-removal SimpleListCellRenderer.create, and drop deprecated ProcessAdapter / StartupActivity usages.
  • 0.1.2 — Exec cards show the command's output below a divider; shorter tool labels (Exec / Writing); and the @-file picker now skips VCS-ignored and excluded folders (e.g. a gitignored Postgres data volume). Strip ANSI colour codes from the status line, and collect runtime errors into a collapsible "! Runtime Exception !" panel per session. Allow git writes inside .git (Codex makes it read-only in workspace-write) so commits/gh work. Settings shows Codex's full path + version with a one-click "Update codex" (greyed "Latest codex installed" when current); the gear turns yellow when an update is available; the gear reliably opens Tools → Karato.
  • 0.1.1 — Fix an IDE freeze on tool-window open (setup probe and model fetch now run off the UI thread); preserve line breaks in your prompts; and modernize APIs flagged on newer IDEs (replace the scheduled-for-removal SimpleListCellRenderer / browse-listener calls and the deprecated HTML editor kit; stop bundling the IDE's markdown library). Also allow outbound network in the workspace-write sandbox by default so gh/curl/npm work (toggle in Settings).
  • 0.1.0 — Initial release. Multi-tab chat tool window for the Sakana AI Fugu agent (via the Codex CLI): inline tool cards, interactive approvals, GUI-only setup, Claude/Codex project-file awareness (CLAUDE.md, .claude/, memory) and MCP-server mirroring.

idea-plugin.name: YMM Structured AI Assistant
idea-plugin.description:
You, Me & Myself is the structured layer between your IDE and the AI model you choose. The IDE provides the data, the AI the meaning, and the plugin structures it to make the most of everything.

When you send a message, the plugin anchors on whatever your cursor is touching and walks your IDE's real model of the project outward — to the connected classes, methods and call relationships — and sends exactly that. The AI answers from facts about your code, drawn straight from the IDE's own understanding. Fewer tokens, sharper answers.

You stay the one doing the thinking. The AI does the heavy lifting; you keep the wheel:

  • You decide what the AI sees — every turn, with two dials for scope and compactness. Right before you send, a Badge Tray shows exactly what's about to be attached, so the scope you set is the scope that ships.
  • You talk straight to the model — your message travels from your IDE directly to the endpoint you configured. A clean line, yours end to end.
  • Your knowledge stays yours — conversations, summaries, bookmarks and collections live on your machine as files in a folder. Portable, backup-able, and entirely yours to keep.
  • Provider-agnostic — you choose the model, and the choice stays yours. Bring your own key and connect any OpenAI-compatible API (ChatGpt, DeepSeek, Mistral, Groq, OpenRouter), Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, a local model via Ollama or LM Studio, or your own endpoint. Tomorrow's better model is one connection away.

What's in it:

  • Chat in a dedicated tool window with multiple tabs
  • Assistant profile — define your assistant's persona, instructions and style; change them whenever you want
  • Context and Summary dials — gather a structural slice of your project for each prompt and control how much of it is summarised before being sent; the two work as a pair
  • Automatic history summarisation — older turns are condensed in the background so long sessions stay within the model's context window
  • Library — every conversation stays searchable, so you can return to something you've worked through instead of asking again
  • Collections — group whole conversations, single exchanges, or bookmarked code blocks into folders that match how you think about your work
  • Metrics — a strip shows the consumption of the active tab and the running session, so you see what's being spent as it happens
  • Capability-adaptive — checks what each provider actually supports (server-side tools, prompt caching, streaming) and uses what's available automatically

Configure one or more AI connections under Settings → Tools → You, Me & Myself, paste your API key, pick a model, and start a conversation.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
v1.0.2 — Compatibility improvements.

  • Compatibility with the latest IntelliJ IDEA releases, including 2026.2.

v1.0.1 — Improvements.

  • Full-length chat responses — replies can now run to their complete length; we lifted the cap that limited how much the model could return in one answer.
  • Clearer feedback on slow responses — you now get a visible notice when a provider is taking unusually long or has stopped streaming, instead of waiting with no signal.
  • Steadier streaming — smoother handling when a provider ends a response early, so the conversation stays clean.
  • Snappier AI Profiles settings — the settings page now opens instantly.

v1.0.0 — Initial release.

  • Provider-agnostic chat — any OpenAI-compatible API (ChatGpt, DeepSeek, Mistral, Groq, OpenRouter), Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, local models via Ollama or LM Studio, or your own endpoint
  • Chat tool window with multiple tabs
  • Assistant profile — persona, instructions, and style, changeable at will
  • Context and Summary dials — gather relevant project files for each prompt and control how much is summarised before sending
  • Automatic history summarisation keeps long conversations within the model's context window
  • Searchable conversation Library; Collections that hold whole conversations, single exchanges, or bookmarked code blocks; code-block bookmarking from any response
  • Capability-adaptive — probes each provider for available features (server-side tools, prompt caching, streaming) and uses them automatically

idea-plugin.name: AppsecD
idea-plugin.description:
AppsecD — Shift-left AppSec for JetBrains IDEs

SAST + secret scanning on your changes, AI-powered fix suggestions, and a per-org governance dashboard — the same engine that powers the AppsecD VS Code / Cursor / Windsurf extension, now for IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, WebStorm, PhpStorm, RubyMine, Rider, CLion and every other JetBrains IDE.

  • Sign in once (device-code, GitHub/email) — token stored in the IDE password safe.
  • Scan changed code on demand; findings appear inline and in the AppsecD tool window.
  • Explain a finding with AI and apply a guarded AI fix.
  • Suppress findings (audited) and install pre-commit/pre-push git hooks.
  • Org policy (block severity, quotas, min version) enforced automatically.

idea-plugin.name: git-helper
idea-plugin.description:
Git Helper

Generate AI-powered Git commit messages from your staged diff. Bring your own provider — fully configurable OpenAI / Anthropic compatible endpoints.

Lightweight, free, local-first.

idea-plugin.name: Copy Path for Agent
idea-plugin.description:
Copy Path for Agent

Copy file and folder references from JetBrains IDEs in configurable agent-friendly formats. Use switchable profiles for Claude Code, Codex App, and custom templates.

  • Editor selections include line numbers based on the selected text.
  • Multiple carets generate one reference per caret.
  • Project tree multi-selection copies all selected files and folders.
  • Each profile keeps its own template and multiple-reference separator.
  • Profiles can be switched quickly from the status bar.
  • Templates use a small generic variable set for paths, directories, file names, line numbers, line ranges, and local file URIs.
  • The Codex App profile uses Markdown file links that render as clickable file references in Codex.

Built-in Profiles

ProfileOutput
Claude Code@src/utils/auth.ts#L42-68
Codex App[auth.ts](/absolute/path/src/utils/auth.ts:42-68)

How to Use

  • Editor context menu - Right-click in any editor and choose Copy Path for Agent.
  • Project tree context menu - Right-click any file or folder in the Project tool window and choose Copy Path for Agent.
  • Keyboard shortcut - Press Alt+C (Option+C on macOS).

Settings

Settings - Tools - Copy Path for Agent

  • Profile - Switch between built-in and custom profiles.
  • Template - Customize the copied reference with documented variables.
  • Multiple references separator - Stored per profile.
  • Notification - Toggle copy notifications and set their duration.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.6

  • Replaced the Copy Profile text prefix in the status bar with the native copy icon.
  • Kept the active profile name and profile switching behavior unchanged.

idea-plugin.name: AI Lingshi
idea-plugin.description:
AI Lingshi is an AI coding assistant for IntelliJ IDEA. Connect to local Ollama / LM Studio or cloud providers such as Zhipu AI; choose local inference for privacy or cloud models for stronger Agent capabilities.


作者：画卿晚(YCJ)


简介

AI 灵侍，专为修习代码道途的修士打造的随身道侍插件，常驻 IDE 侧栏伴你推演万千符文卷宗。可接通本地 Ollama / LM Studio 灵脉，亦可切换智谱 AI 等云端灵脉，将大模型炼化为随行法器，本地私密与云端算力由修士自行取舍。


择本地灵脉时，推演在本机灵台运转，业务卷宗、私密逻辑不出本机；择云端灵脉时，可驱使 glm 等高阶法器，解锁更强 Agent 推演道途。灵侍通晓全品类开发道统，既能勘破术法疏漏、梳理大型项目脉络，亦可从零搭建完整业务符文体系。


核心道法能力


多路灵脉任选
本地：自动感应 Ollama（默认 http://localhost:11434）与 LM Studio 灵台，支持自定义灵脉地址与多法器部署。云端：对接智谱 AI OpenAPI 兼容灵脉，API Key 存于 IDE 密钥链，不在卷宗中明文留痕。灵脉闭塞或感应失败时传回清晰提示，便于排查。


自动识辨随行法器
一键刷新检索当前灵脉下可用模型法器，下拉切换随行法器；支持工具调用的法器可解锁 Agent 自主规划推演（探法、著法、多轮推演），轻量法器亦可用于日常答疑与概念解惑。


流式道讯逐行回禀
推演结果实时流式推送，采用 Markdown 玉简格式规整排版，代码符文自动划分独立法域区块，注释、业务逻辑分层分明，便于修士直接复制、修改、应用至工程。


自主勘察全宗项目卷宗
灵侍可自行遍历当前工程所有玉简文件，自动读取实体、接口、工具类、枚举等上下文，不局限单段符文作答，全局统筹推演整套业务道统，适配大型多模块工程。


全场景符文撰写与修缮
承接新建业务模块、CRUD 基础术法、接口逻辑、单元试炼符文、全局工具类构建等各类需求；支持批量改写现有卷宗，统一全项目宗门代码规范。


主动勘破术法隐患心魔
推演过程中自动检索符文逻辑漏洞、边界疏漏、性能阻滞、异常缺失等隐患，同步推演优化修正之法，并标注隐患所在玉简位置，辅助修士提前规避线上道途劫难。


独立会话留存传讯记录
完整分隔、保存主人与灵侍每一轮道讯对话，可随时回溯过往推演卷宗，接续上次未完成的术法构建，无需重复复述需求背景。


本地私密与云端灵脉
本地 Ollama / LM Studio：需求与项目上下文在本机与灵脉间流转，适合涉密卷宗与离线道途。智谱 AI 等云端灵脉：对话与上下文按服务商规则上传，请择符合宗门合规要求的灵脉；API Key 由 IDE 密钥链保管。


「灵台连通无碍，卷宗尽可托付；符文撰写、术法勘误、宗门卷宗规整、全新道统推演，主人但有所命，灵侍即刻推演待命，共赴代码长生大道。」

idea-plugin.name: MC Lang Translator
idea-plugin.description:
MC Lang Translator

MC Lang Translator is an IntelliJ IDEA plugin for translating Minecraft mod language files.

It is designed for mod projects that keep localization files under paths such as

`src/main/resources/assets/<modid>/lang/en_us.json`. From the Project View, you can translate one

source language file into one or more Minecraft locale files without leaving the IDE.

What It Does

  • Adds `Translate lang file...` to the context menu for `.json` files inside a folder named `lang`.
  • Translates flat Minecraft language JSON files, such as `en_us.json`, into target locale files like `es_es.json`.
  • Writes translated files beside the source file, keeping the usual Minecraft resource-pack layout.
  • Supports Google Translate, DeepL, Microsoft Translator, and OpenAI-compatible AI APIs.
  • Uses the JSON key as translation context, which helps ambiguous Minecraft terms such as item, block, UI, tooltip, and advancement names.
  • Preserves Minecraft placeholders such as `%s`, `%1$s`, `%%`, and `{name}`.
  • Can skip keys that already exist in a target file, which is useful when updating existing translations.
  • Stores API keys in IntelliJ PasswordSafe.

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA.
  • A Minecraft language JSON file inside a `lang` folder.
  • An API key for the translation provider you want to use.

The source JSON must be a flat string-to-string map:

Nested JSON objects or non-string values are not supported.

Setup

1. Open `Settings | Tools | MC Lang Translator`.

2. Choose the active provider.

3. Enter the API key for that provider.

4. Adjust provider-specific options if needed:

  • DeepL API host and formality.
  • Microsoft region.
  • AI endpoint URL, model, and optional system prompt.

5. Optionally enable `Skip keys that already exist in the target file`.

6. Use `Test connection` to confirm the provider can load languages.

Usage

1. In the Project View, right-click a file like `assets/example/lang/en_us.json`.

2. Choose `Translate lang file...`.

3. Select one or more target languages.

4. Confirm the dialog.

5. Wait for the background task to finish.

For each selected language, the plugin writes a file in the same `lang` folder:

If a translation request fails for a key, the plugin keeps the original text for that key and reports a warning.

Notes For AI Translation

The AI provider sends Minecraft-specific context with each string, including the JSON key and source/target locales. This helps the model translate terms as in-game content instead of casual speech. For example, a key like `item.example.honey` gives the model context that `Honey` should be translated as an item name.

Custom AI system prompts are supported. The plugin still appends required Minecraft localization rules so placeholders and output format stay safe.

The ZIP is created under `build/distributions/`.

idea-plugin.name: HarmonyOS Dev Assistant
idea-plugin.description:
HarmonyOS Dev Assistant

HarmonyOS Dev Assistant 插件简介

HarmonyOS Dev Assistant 是一款面向鸿蒙（HarmonyOS）开发者的 AI 编码助手插件。插件以自然语言对话为核心交互方式，提供一站式生成元服务能力，帮助您更高效地完成鸿蒙元服务开发。

安装环境要求

  • 操作系统 — 支持 Windows、macOS 12+（Intel / Apple Silicon）
  • DevEco Studio — 推荐版本 DevEco Studio 6.1及以上
  • Node.js — 最低版本 Node.js 18.x，推荐版本 Node.js 20.x LTS

安装插件

  1. 启动 DevEco Studio，在顶部菜单栏选择 "File> Settings"。
  2. 选择 "Plugins" 选项卡，点击右上角设置按钮，选择 "Install Plugin from Disk…"。
  3. 在文件选择窗口，选择未解压的插件包，点击 "OK"。
  4. 在 "Settings" 窗口点击 "OK"。
  5. 在 DevEco Studio 右侧边栏，点击 "HarmonyOS Dev Assistant"，即可打开 HarmonyOS 开发助手登录界面。

核心特性

  • 智能代码生成 — 与 AI 对话式生成 ArkTS/HarmonyOS 代码，覆盖项目创建、UI 开发、状态管理、网络请求、数据存储等完整开发流程。
  • 元服务研发问答 — 基于项目上下文的实时技术问答，快速解决鸿蒙元服务开发中的 API 使用、设计指南、华为登录/支付接入等问题。
  • 构建与调试 — 集成 hvigor 构建、模拟器调试、HAP 签名与真机部署，覆盖从开发到验证的全流程。
  • 一键式签名 — 在插件设置中绑定元服务并完成签名，简化元服务打包与调试流程。
  • 内置元服务skill技能 — 提供元服务开发、续写、备案上架等面向鸿蒙场景的专属技能（skills），连接 Agent 后自动加载。
  • 上架发布辅助 — 覆盖元服务备案、AGC 上架检测等发布全流程指导。

使用指南

具体使用指南，参考HarmonyOS开发助手。

反馈与支持

如有问题或建议，请通过 JetBrains 扩展市场的反馈渠道提交。

idea-plugin.name: Claude Relay
idea-plugin.description:
Claude Relay — Claude Code, native in your JetBrains IDE

A native chat panel that drives the official Claude Code CLI from inside IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, Rider and the rest of the JetBrains family — the side-panel experience you'd get in VS Code, without leaving your IDE or living in the terminal.

Highlights

  • Streaming chat with live tool activity — edits, commands, and file reads as they happen
  • Agent & Ask modes — let Claude edit and run commands, or keep it strictly read-only
  • Editor-aware — auto-attaches your current selection, so "explain/refactor this" just works
  • Attach files & images — pick a file, or paste a screenshot straight into the prompt
  • Project context — picks up your CLAUDE.md, agents, skills and slash commands automatically
  • Session history — resume past conversations from a built-in picker
  • Model & permission selectors, with live usage and limits

Requires the Claude Code CLI installed separately (npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code) and an active Claude subscription.

☕ Free and open source (MIT). Source, issues, and contributions: github.com/Chelayel/claude-relay.

Independent and unofficial — not affiliated with Anthropic. Part of the “Relay” family of IDE companions by Chelayel.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.0 — Claude can now ask your permission to use a tool, and you can answer. Until now nothing in the plugin could reply to a permission request, so the CLI denied every one of them: “Default (ask)” mode was in practice “deny every edit”, and all you saw was a red tool error on a turn that still reported success. You now get a dialog — Allow, Allow for This Chat, or Deny — and a tool the CLI refuses on its own is named in the transcript instead of passing unnoticed.

1.0.18 — Fixed Claude's questions, which stopped working again after 1.0.17. The previous fix denied the interactive question tool to force a plain-text fallback, but that no longer works with the persistent streaming session and instead suppressed the question entirely. Claude is no longer blocked from asking, so its questions show up again and you can answer by typing.

1.0.17 — Questions now work. When Claude wanted to ask a multiple-choice question it used its interactive picker, which has no UI in the CLI's headless mode and auto-resolved to “no answer was selected.” Claude now asks in plain text instead, so you can just type your answer.

1.0.15 — Restored the rich chat transcript on IntelliJ 2026.2+ (build 262), where JCEF became a separate bundled plugin — the panel now depends on it optionally so the in-browser view works again instead of dropping to plain text. The plain-text fallback also renders at the correct font size when JCEF isn't available.

1.0.14 — Fixed oversized text in the plain-text transcript fallback (used when JCEF isn't available): it now renders at the IDE's UI font size instead of an inflated one.

1.0.13 — Fixed the tool window failing to open on recent IntelliJ builds (NoClassDefFoundError: com/intellij/ui/jcef/JBCefApp). When JCEF isn't available on the plugin classpath the panel now falls back to the plain-text transcript instead of failing to initialize.

1.0.12 — Compatibility fix for upcoming IntelliJ releases (replaced a platform API scheduled for removal in the popup choosers).

1.0.11 — Much lower token usage in longer chats: each conversation now runs through a single persistent Claude Code session, keeping the prompt cache warm across turns instead of re-sending the whole transcript every message.

1.0.10 — The tool-window icon now uses the Claude accent red so it matches the plugin icon instead of looking washed-out in dark themes.

1.0.9 — Reliability fix: the model picker no longer gets stuck on the bare fallback list when the /model scrape races a slow CLI start-up; it now waits longer and retries. Added diagnostic logging for picker issues.

1.0.8 — New Auto-Test to Coverage toolbar action: pick a target line-coverage percentage and Claude keeps writing and running unit tests until it reaches it. The model picker now shows the concrete Claude version for each choice (e.g. Opus 4.8, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5).

1.0.7 — New original plugin logo. The context bar “Rescan” button now has a distinct icon so it’s no longer confused with the toolbar “Refresh”. Additional compatibility fix for upcoming IntelliJ releases (replaced another platform API scheduled for removal).

1.0.3 — Compatibility fix for upcoming IntelliJ releases (replaced a platform API scheduled for removal). Shift+Enter inserts a newline.

1.0.2 — Claude Relay is now free and open source (MIT). Source & contributions: github.com/Chelayel/claude-relay.

1.0.1 — Fixed intermittent “Project context” bar visibility.

1.0.0 — First release: native Claude Code chat panel with streaming transcript & tool activity, Agent & Ask modes, single-select agent persona, editor-aware context, file & image attachments, project agents/skills/commands, session history, and model/permission selectors.

idea-plugin.name: QAEverest
idea-plugin.description:
QAEverest generates AI-powered functional, API, UI, mobile, security, and performance tests from a story or a spec — without leaving your IDE.

Open the QAEverest tool window and describe what you want tested. The plugin reads your project, generates test cases, builds and runs automation suites, and writes reviewable .feature files and HTML execution reports back into your repository.

It also prepares the qaeverest-mcp server configuration so JetBrains AI Assistant's MCP tools can call QAEverest directly.

Usage is billed to your QAEverest account (bring-your-own-key) — the plugin itself is free.

Account and data

QAEverest requires a QAEverest account. When you ask it to generate or run tests, the files and context relevant to that request are sent to the QAEverest service and on to the AI providers it uses; results come back into your IDE. Your API key is stored in the IDE's own secure credential store, never in project files.

See the Privacy Policy and the Terms & Conditions.

Node.js runtime

The test-generation engine runs on Node.js. If Node 18 or newer is already on your PATH, the plugin uses it. If not, it asks first, then downloads the official Node 20.18.1 build from nodejs.org (about 35 MB), verifies it against a SHA-256 checksum compiled into the plugin, and unpacks it into the IDE's own system directory. Nothing outside that directory is modified, and you can decline and install Node yourself instead.

idea-plugin.name: SpecBuddy
idea-plugin.description:
Spec-driven development in your IDE: run the OpenSpec workflow with a review gate on every step.

SpecBuddy drives OpenSpec end to end — propose a change, review its proposal, spec deltas and tasks.md, then let Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or any ACP-compatible agent work through the tasks one at a time. Every task lands behind a diff you accept, refine or roll back. Prefer your own format? The same engine runs plain Markdown specs, with no OpenSpec involved.

OpenSpec, first-class

If your project uses OpenSpec, SpecBuddy is its IDE surface:

  • Changes are work units. Everything under openspec/changes/ shows up in the Spec Explorer next to your specs, with its state at a glance — Draft, Spec, 3/7 Tasks — and the live agent status while a session runs.
  • The whole cycle, in the IDE. Propose an OpenSpec change, apply its tasks one by one, sync the deltas into your main specs, and archive it — without switching to a terminal.
  • Delta navigation. Gutter markers link a delta requirement to the main spec requirement it changes, and diff the two when it is MODIFIED.
  • History that survives archiving. Every run — propose, task, sync, archive — is recorded with pre/post snapshots you can diff long after the session is gone.

Why

Chat-driven coding only lets you review code after it is written:

  • You find out the agent misunderstood you by reading a long diff in the pull request.
  • Long chats lose the plot — the agent forgets where the task started.
  • The plan lives in your head; the agent only sees the last message.

SpecBuddy moves control to before the code is written — and keeps it at every step after. Catch the wrong turn at the spec, not in the pull request.

How it works

  1. Spec — describe what to build: an OpenSpec change, or a plain Markdown spec in the editor. The agent can expand a short draft into a full specification for you.
  2. Plan — the spec becomes a sequence of executable tasks. Read it, edit it, approve it — before a single line of code is generated.
  3. Execute — the agent runs tasks one at a time in an isolated git worktree, so your working tree stays clean until you accept the changes.
  4. Review — after each task you get a diff of exactly what changed. Accept it, refine it with inline comments, or roll it back to the pre-task state.

Control without leaving the chat

Prefer to just talk to the agent for small tasks? SpecBuddy wraps your regular chat sessions in the same engine: every change the agent makes gets a diff, a review, and a one-click rollback — no spec, no OpenSpec change required. Nothing is applied silently; Accept and Rollback are always your explicit click.

Built for your existing workflow

  • Your IDE — an IntelliJ plugin, not a new editor to switch to.
  • Your agent — Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or any ACP-compatible agent, running right inside the IDE.
  • Your git — tasks execute in a dedicated git worktree; every run records pre/post snapshots, so rollback is always safe.
  • Your files — OpenSpec changes and Markdown specs are plain files in your repository. No new syntax, no lock-in.

Spec-driven development — without leaving your IDE or learning a new syntax.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Getting started no longer means clicking through dialogs, and a spec delta shows you exactly what it does to the specification.

  • First-run setup happens inside the session log. A launch that is not ready to run no longer walks you through a ladder of modal dialogs. SpecBuddy works out everything that is missing up front — the agent, the CLI, a git repository, the skills and hooks, an initialised openspec/ — asks for one installation approval that names every command it will run, and then narrates the setup as a run in the execution log: a card per command, with its output streaming in as it goes. Installs no longer disappear into the Build tool window, and concurrent launches attach to the same setup run instead of racing. The separate SpecBuddy Setup tool window is gone.
  • Every delta spec offers a diff of its effect. The gutter marker on a change's spec delta now always opens a diff, and both sides are whole documents: the capability's specification as it reads today, against the same specification with the delta applied. Additions, removals and renames are visible as what they are, in their real document context, instead of having to be reconstructed by eye from requirement blocks.

Fixed

  • Agent profiles with a hand-set executable path now launch on Windows. The path was spliced unquoted into a POSIX shell line, so Git Bash ate the backslashes and the agent died with "command not found" while the profile dialog still reported the path as found. Paths are quoted for the shell that will run them, a .cmd/.bat launcher goes through cmd.exe even when Git Bash is installed, and the dialog now validates the executable against the shells your system can actually drive — showing the reason, and naming a runnable sibling when there is one, instead of a checkmark.
  • OpenCode sessions start again. SpecBuddy declared its support for the agent's typed questions in a shape OpenCode rejected outright and Codex quietly ignored.
  • A snapshot no longer fails because of an ignored directory. A file that is tracked by git but sits under an ignored path used to fail the whole capture.
  • Two work units with the same name no longer share one worktree. Each gets its own worktree and branch, and the branch-name confirmation shows the name that was actually allocated.

idea-plugin.name: Engram Alpha
idea-plugin.description:
Engram is a durable, graph-based long-term memory for AI coding assistants — the reasoning/decision layer (why we chose this, what bit us, what's still open), shown as a graph you can see, edit, and own.

This plugin embeds the Engram graph pane in a tool window. It connects to the local engram-alpha serve daemon — the same one your AI assistant reads from and writes to over MCP — so decisions, cautions, problems, and insights surface and update live as you work.

One memory, every agent: the backend speaks MCP, so Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Kilo, and Google Antigravity all share the same per-repo graph — a decision captured by one assistant is recalled by the next.

Requires the Engram backend. Install it and run engram-alpha serve in your repository; the pane connects automatically once the daemon is up.

Pairs naturally with projects that keep their canon in PLAN.md and compile decision logs to DECISIONS.md — Engram is the living graph those documents are rendered from.

idea-plugin.name: Ceres: AI Coding Assistant with Voice
idea-plugin.description:
Ceres: AI Coding Assistant with Voice

AI coding assistance with voice input and speech-to-text.

Ceres Assistant is an AI sidebar for VS Code. Chat with files, refactor code, debug errors, and review Git changes using your preferred AI provider or local model.

Why Ceres?

Ceres keeps code assistance inside your editor:

  • Find relevant workspace context or add files, selections, errors, and terminal output yourself.
  • Choose hosted providers or local models through OpenAI-compatible APIs.
  • Dictate requests with speech-to-text.
  • Control Agent Mode and automatic approval of file edits.

What Ceres Is

Use it when you want help with:

  • Explaining selected code
  • Refactoring a function or file
  • Understanding an error
  • Reviewing Git changes
  • Inspecting terminal output
  • Troubleshooting debugging issues
  • Drafting commands
  • Working with local or custom AI providers
  • Getting controlled suggestions for the active editor

What Ceres Is Not

Ceres is not a replacement for reviewing generated code. Model capabilities and results depend on the provider and model you choose.

Features

  • AI sidebar inside VS Code: Chat with AI without leaving the editor.

  • Add selected code or files to chat: Send only the code selection or file you care about.

  • Active selection context: Include selected code from the active editor.

  • Automatic workspace context: Navigation Mode (Agent Mode) finds relevant project files. It is enabled by default and can be disabled.

  • Workspace Problems: Send diagnostics and errors from the VS Code Problems panel.

  • Git worktree review: Read current staged and unstaged changes.

  • Incoming Git overview: Inspect incoming commits and diffs before pulling.

  • Git history context: Review recent commits and repository history.

  • Voice input: Dictate prompts with speech-to-text inside the Ceres sidebar.

  • Custom providers and local models: Use OpenAI-compatible endpoints, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Ollama, LM Studio, and other compatible providers.

  • File edits: Let Agent Mode edit files. Disable Auto Approve to review proposed changes before they are saved.

  • Run commands: Review and approve AI-generated terminal commands.

  • Place suggestion: Insert a suggestion into the active editor.

  • Apply Edits [Pro]: Includes Place Suggestions and Write / Apply Tools.

  • Voice requests: Describe code changes using the sidebar microphone.

Local And Hosted Models

Choose hosted providers or local models for your development workflow.

Supported providers include:

  • OpenAI
  • Anthropic
  • Mistral
  • Mercury
  • OpenRouter
  • Kilo Code
  • Hugging Face
  • DeepSeek
  • Qwen
  • Ollama
  • LM Studio

Context Control

Ceres can use the following context. Navigation Mode (Agent Mode) is enabled by default and can be disabled when you prefer to provide context manually.

  • A code selection
  • A full file
  • Current editor context
  • Workspace diagnostics
  • Git diffs
  • Terminal output
  • Debugging-related code and errors
  • URLs, PDFs, images, audio, and other supported inputs

Navigation Mode

Navigation Mode (Agent Mode) is enabled by default. It lets Ceres search the codebase, read relevant files, inspect Git information, and use supported editing and terminal tools.

File edits follow the Auto Approve setting. Turn Auto Approve off to review proposed edits before saving. Terminal commands require approval.

You can disable Agent Mode at any time to chat using the context you provide.

Common Workflows

Explain or Improve a Selection

Select code, run Add Selected Lines to Ceres, and ask for an explanation, refactor, review, or bug check.

Default shortcut:

  • Ctrl+Alt+L

On macOS:

  • Cmd+Alt+L

Review Before Pulling

Ask Ceres to inspect incoming Git changes before merging them into your working tree.

Edit Code with Voice

Select code and use the sidebar microphone to dictate the change you want. Send the request to your selected model, then review the response or let Agent Mode apply the change according to your approval settings.

Commands

Ceres contributes these VS Code commands:

  • Add File to Ceres
  • Add Selected Lines to Ceres
  • Add Problem to Ceres

You can access them from editor context menus, explorer context menus, editor title actions, code actions, and the command palette.

Best For

Ceres is a good fit for:

  • Developers who want control over AI context
  • Teams working on legacy or sensitive codebases
  • People using local or lower-cost models
  • Developers who want to switch between Agent Mode and manual context
  • Anyone who prefers dictating code requests instead of typing

Known Limits

  • Agent tools depend on the capabilities of your selected model and provider.
  • Provider usage charges are separate from the Ceres license.
  • AI suggestions should be reviewed before you use them.

Usage

Configure your provider and model in the sidebar, then add a file or selection and type or dictate your request.

Data handling depends on your selected providers and features. Hosted providers receive the content sent to them. Requests to a local Ollama or LM Studio endpoint are processed locally.

Bug Reports and Feedback

https://ceres-assistant.com/web/contact.php

Troubleshoot Page

https://ceres-assistant.com/web/troubleshoot.php

Privacy Policy Page

https://ceres-assistant.com/web/privacy-policy.php

idea-plugin.name: OmniPilot - Bring Your Own Model
idea-plugin.description:
OmniPilot is an advanced, fully autonomous AI coding assistant plugin for JetBrains IDEs (IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, Android Studio, etc.). It brings the power of state-of-the-art Large Language Models directly into your editor with deep IDE integration.


Features

  • Multi-Provider Support: Seamlessly connect to any OpenAI-compatible API, including OpenAI, Groq, Anthropic, NVIDIA NIM, Cloudflare, and local models via LM Studio or Ollama.
  • Dynamic Model Fetching: Automatically pull the latest available models from your configured provider directly within the IDE settings.

idea-plugin.name: CLI Agent Dock
idea-plugin.description:
CLI Agent Dock brings your favorite coding agent right into your JetBrains IDE — no more alt-tabbing to a terminal window. It adds a dedicated tool window to the right side bar (next to Database, Gradle, and friends) with an embedded terminal that automatically launches a coding agent CLI in your project.

By default it opens with Claude Code, and GitHub Copilot CLI is supported too. Pick an agent from the dropdown and open as many sessions as you like — each runs in its own closeable tab, so you can drive several agents at once. Your preferred agent is remembered across projects and restarts. Support for more agents (OpenAI Codex CLI, OpenCode, and more) is on the roadmap.

  • Embedded terminal, pre-launched with your agent CLI in your project directory
  • Multiple independent, closeable agent sessions per project
  • Live "files changed" panel — see what the agent touched as it works, with one-click diffs for each file and a jump to the commit view
  • Esc reaches the agent (e.g. to interrupt it) instead of leaving the terminal; double-tap Esc to jump back to the editor, Shift+Esc to hide the dock
  • Cross-platform: Windows, macOS, and Linux
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Esc now goes to the agent instead of leaving the dock — the platform used to move focus to the editor on every Esc press inside the terminal, making it impossible to e.g. interrupt Claude Code. Esc is now delivered to the agent CLI, and leaving the dock by keyboard still works: a quick double Esc (within 300 ms) sends the first Esc to the agent and returns focus to the editor, and Shift+Esc keeps hiding the dock as usual. The double-Esc shortcut can be turned off in Settings > Tools > CLI Agent Dock for agents that bind a fast double Esc themselves (pressing the two Escs more slowly reaches such agent features either way).
  • Settings gear in the toolbar and a toggle for the Files changed panel — the tool window toolbar now has a settings shortcut on the far right that opens Settings > Tools > CLI Agent Dock, and a new "Show Files changed panel" setting hides the panel for those who prefer a pure terminal. Tracking keeps running while hidden, so re-enabling it mid-session brings back everything the session accumulated meanwhile.

Changed

  • Snappier session startup and a lighter idle footprint — the agent executable lookup (a real disk scan on a cold start, especially on Windows with WinGet installs) now runs in the background behind the startup spinner instead of briefly freezing the IDE on the first open or a retry, and the periodic file refresh that feeds the Files changed panel pauses while the IDE window is in the background, resuming as soon as it regains focus.

Fixed

  • The Files changed panel no longer lists VCS-ignored files (build output, caches — whatever .gitignore and the IDE's ignore providers cover): ignored paths are filtered out as changes arrive, and entries recorded before a .gitignore the agent wrote mid-session caught up with them are dropped as well.
  • Files that were merely discovered mid-session — a directory first scanned by indexing or git while the agent runs — are no longer attributed to the agent: anything whose on-disk content predates the session start stays out of the Files changed panel.

idea-plugin.name: Rive Studio
idea-plugin.description:
Joyous Inspector for Rive brings Rive .riv animation workflows into DevEco Studio and WebStorm for HarmonyOS and Web development.

It is built for the developer handoff stage: after a .riv file is ready, teams still need to understand its artboards, animations, state machines, inputs, events, and assets before integrating it into app code. Joyous Inspector for Rive makes that structure visible inside the IDE and connects it to preview, code generation, and device validation.

Key features:

  • Inspect artboards, animations, state machines, inputs, events, nested artboards, and assets.
  • Preview animations inside the IDE with playback controls, animation switching, speed control, click, and drag interaction.
  • Generate Harmony ArkTS usage references and React / Vue Web usage references.
  • Run selected animations on Harmony physical devices or emulators, and open WebStorm local browser, LAN URL, and QR real-device previews.
  • Install the read-only rivc CLI and generate Agent Skill files for Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, CodeGenie, OpenCode, and similar coding agents.

Real-device preview IDE support:

  • DevEco Studio: supported through Harmony Device Preview for Harmony physical devices and emulators.
  • WebStorm: supported through LAN URL and QR browser preview for devices on the same network.
  • Android Studio: in development.

Joyous Inspector for Rive is local-first. It does not automatically upload source files or .riv animation contents. Feedback submission is user initiated and can optionally include redacted diagnostics.

Joyous Inspector for Rive is an independent Joyous developer tool for inspecting, previewing, and integrating Rive .riv animation files. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Rive, Inc.

Joyous 动画检查器（Joyous Inspector for Rive）将 Rive .riv 动画文件的查看、预览、代码集成和设备 / 浏览器预览流程带到 DevEco Studio 和 WebStorm 中，面向 HarmonyOS 与 Web 开发场景。

它服务于动画文件交付后的开发阶段：开发者需要理解文件结构、预览交互行为、选择正确的 Artboard 和 Animation、连接 State Machine 输入，并把动画安全接入 ArkTS 或 Web 代码，而不是靠手工猜名称。

主要能力：

  • 查看 .riv 文件中的 Artboard、动画、状态机、输入、事件、嵌套 Artboard 和资源。
  • 在 IDE 内预览动画，支持播放控制、动画切换、速度控制、点击和拖动交互。
  • 生成 Harmony ArkTS 使用参考和 React / Vue Web 使用参考。
  • 支持鸿蒙真机或模拟器预览，也支持 WebStorm 的本地浏览器、LAN URL 和 QR 真机预览。
  • 安装只读 rivc 命令，并为 Codex、Claude Code、Gemini CLI、CodeGenie、OpenCode 等代码 Agent 生成 Agent Skill。

真机预览 IDE 支持：

  • DevEco Studio：已支持，通过 Harmony Device Preview 运行到鸿蒙真机或模拟器。
  • WebStorm：已支持，通过 LAN URL 和 QR 浏览器预览在同一局域网设备上查看。
  • Android Studio： 目前已经支持Android / Compose真机预览，flutter跨平台支持在开发中。

Joyous 动画检查器采用本地优先设计，不会自动上传源码或 .riv 动画内容。用户主动提交反馈时，可以选择附带脱敏诊断信息。
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Added Flutter Desktop native preview for Android Studio / JetBrains IDEs.
  • Added current-system Flutter desktop target execution for macOS, Windows, and Linux projects.
  • Added Flutter Desktop preview session generation with copied .riv files, metadata, and preview-report.json handling.
  • Added Flutter SDK discovery from IDE settings, local.properties, environment variables, and PATH.
  • Added Linux desktop preflight diagnostics with non-Snap Flutter SDK detection.
  • Added Windows Desktop Preview preparation with short workspace handling and Developer Mode guidance.
  • Removed deprecated IntelliJ Platform API usages reported by Marketplace verification on newer IntelliJ IDEA builds.

中文：

  • 增加 Android Studio / JetBrains IDE 下的 Flutter Desktop native preview。
  • 增加 Flutter 项目的当前系统桌面目标执行能力，覆盖 macOS、Windows、Linux 工程目标。
  • 增加 Flutter Desktop preview session 生成，包含复制 .riv、写入 metadata，并处理 preview-report.json。
  • 增加 Flutter SDK 发现能力，覆盖 IDE 设置、local.properties、环境变量和 PATH。
  • 增加 Linux desktop preflight 诊断和非 Snap Flutter SDK 检查。
  • 增加 Windows Desktop Preview 准备逻辑，包括短路径 workspace 处理和 Developer Mode 引导。
  • 移除新版 IntelliJ IDEA Marketplace 校验中报告的 deprecated IntelliJ Platform API 调用。

idea-plugin.name: Sema Code
idea-plugin.description:
Sema Code (SemaCode) — AI Coding Assistant / AI programming assistant for JetBrains IDEs.

Sema Code is an AI coding assistant and code copilot that brings an out-of-the-box AI programming experience to IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, WebStorm, CLion and other JetBrains IDEs, powered by the Sema Code Core engine. Supports AI code generation, chat-based coding, and agent-driven development workflows.

基于 Sema Code Core 的 JetBrains AI 编程助手 / 智能代码助手

为开发者提供开箱即用的 AI 编程体验，支持 IntelliJ IDEA / PyCharm / GoLand / WebStorm / CLion 等 JetBrains 全家桶。

Sema Code 是基于 Sema Code Core 引擎的智能编程插件。

核心特性
  • 自然语言指令 —— 通过自然语言直接驱动编程任务
  • 权限控制 —— 细粒度的权限管理，确保操作安全可控
  • Subagent 管理 —— 支持多智能体协同工作，可根据任务类型动态调度合适的子代理
  • Skill 扩展机制 —— 提供插件化架构，可灵活扩展 AI 编程能力
  • Plan 模式任务规划 —— 支持复杂任务的分解与执行规划
  • MCP 协议支持 —— 内置 Model Context Protocol 服务，支持工具扩展
  • 多模型支持 —— 兼容 Anthropic、OpenAI SDK，支持国内外主流厂商 LLM API
安装与使用
  1. 打开 JetBrains IDE（IntelliJ IDEA / PyCharm / GoLand / WebStorm / CLion 等）
  2. 进入 Settings/Preferences → Plugins
  3. 搜索 Sema Code 并点击安装
  4. 或从 GitHub Releases 下载插件包手动安装

idea-plugin.name: Agent Session Relay
idea-plugin.description:
Review an agent's changes in your IDE and relay batched, line-anchored comments back into its running session — instead of retyping feedback into the terminal.

How it works
  • Hover the editor's left gutter to reveal a + icon — or right-click and choose Add review comment — to open an inline comment box (GitHub/GitLab style) over the selected lines, or the caret line. Drag the highlighted range's top and bottom edges to resize it.
  • Press Ctrl/Cmd+Enter to add the comment. It stays in the editor as a read-only inline card under its lines — hover the card to reveal its range and its Edit / Delete actions — and is listed in the Relay Review tool window, grouped by file (double-click to jump to it).
  • Press Submit to write a REVIEW.md at the project root using Claude Code's @path#L reference syntax, then hand it to your idle agent session.
  • Use Refresh & review to reload files an agent changed on disk before you review them.
Works in any open file, regardless of its version-control status.

Links:
  • GitHub
  • Issues
idea-plugin.change-notes:
First public release of Agent Session Relay — a JetBrains/PyCharm plugin that lets you review an agent's changes in your IDE and relay batched, line-anchored comments straight back into its running session, instead of retyping feedback into the terminal. What's in this release
  • Line-anchored comments — hover the editor's left gutter for a + icon (or right-click → Add review comment) to open an inline comment box over the selected lines or caret line. Drag the range's top and bottom edges to resize it.
  • Batched review — added comments stay in the editor as editable inline cards and are listed in the Relay Review tool window, grouped by file (double-click to jump).
  • One-press relay — Submit writes a REVIEW.md at the project root using Claude Code's @path#L10-15 reference syntax, so the agent resolves anchors directly with no in-file markers to collide with its own edits.
  • Refresh & review — reload files an agent changed on disk before you review them.
  • Persistence — a pending review batch survives an IDE restart.
  • Works in any open file, regardless of version-control status.
Requirements
  • A 2024.2 or newer IntelliJ-based IDE. Built for PyCharm Community; runs in any IntelliJ-based IDE.
Install
  • Agent Session Relay on the JetBrains Marketplace
Status: MVP. Typed terminal relay and multi-session/worktree support remain deferred follow-ons.
