idea-plugin.name: MCP WSL Bridge
idea-plugin.description:
Exposes IntelliJ's loopback-only MCP server to WSL through selected Windows network interfaces.

Choose one or more NIC addresses, then MCP WSL Bridge transparently routes multiple HTTP MCP servers through one WSL-facing port using separate paths.

Usage

  1. Enable IntelliJ's built-in MCP server in Settings | Tools | MCP Server.
  2. Open Settings | Tools | MCP WSL Bridge, enable the bridge, and select the vEthernet (WSL) IPv4 address.
  3. Apply the settings. The bridge starts automatically with IntelliJ while enabled.
  4. Add one route per MCP server, then use the Codex, Claude Code, or GitHub Copilot CLI action to configure all enabled routes.

The bridge automatically rebinds after WSL interface address changes and updates configured WSL client endpoints.

Security: select only network interfaces you intend to expose. The bridge has no authentication and should not be bound to Wi-Fi, Ethernet, or VPN addresses unless required.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.11

  • Detect JetBrains MCP ports across IntelliJ IDEA, RustRover, and other IDEs.
  • Detect IDE Index MCP ports around the IDE-specific default instead of assuming 29170.
  • Use IDE-specific WSL server names such as intellij-wsl-bridge and rustrover-wsl-bridge.
  • Improve WSL configuration labels, route-name validation, target diagnostics, and status reporting.
  • Preserve bridge listeners during transient MCP target loss and improve session recovery compatibility.

0.1.10

  • Preserve loopback Origin and Streamable HTTP response framing for IntelliJ MCP approval flows.
  • Preserve MCP session and SSE approval exchanges through the WSL bridge.
  • Add safe diagnostics for MCP request, response, SSE, and timing events.
  • Add regression coverage for server-initiated approval requests and responses.
  • Recycle the bridge endpoint when IntelliJ MCP restarts so clients can establish fresh sessions.
  • Virtualize MCP sessions and recreate IntelliJ upstream sessions after restarts or connection failures.
  • Keep bridge listeners alive during transient IntelliJ MCP target loss.
  • Claude Code may require /mcp reconnect after an IntelliJ restart if its elicitation state is not recovered.

0.1.9

  • Add multi-server MCP routing, including the IDE Index MCP preset.
  • Add WSL client configuration and removal actions for Codex, Claude Code, and GitHub Copilot CLI.
  • Redesign MCP server settings with a native list, detail panel, templates, and popup editing.
  • Improve bridge status reporting, automatic WSL endpoint refresh, and HTTP routing compatibility.

0.1.8

  • Start the bridge automatically when an IntelliJ project opens.
  • Add an adaptive status-bar widget for bridge state and endpoint actions.
  • Remove deprecated and internal IntelliJ API usages reported by Plugin Verifier.

0.1.7

  • Use the public application-frame lifecycle callback for automatic startup.

0.1.6

idea-plugin.name: AskSQL
idea-plugin.description:
AI database chat inside your IDE, with your rows never leaving your machine. Ask a question in plain language, review the SQL the AI writes, approve it, and get results. Run the AI model locally through Ollama or LM Studio and nothing leaves at all.

  • Read-only by design. An AST guard checks every statement before it runs, on every engine, and on Postgres, MySQL, Oracle and SQLite the session itself is opened read-only as a second floor. (MongoDB and file-backed DuckDB have no read-only session to open, so there the guard is the only floor, working from an allowlist rather than a blocklist.)
  • Asking for a change is never a change. Ask for an INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or a schema change and you get the statement written out to run yourself, never executed.
  • Six databases. Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, DuckDB, Oracle and MongoDB.
  • Or no database at all. Point it at CSV, TSV, TXT, JSON, NDJSON, Parquet, Excel or .sql files and query them as tables, joining across files. No server to install.
  • Already set up in DataGrip or IDEA Ultimate? AskSQL reuses the data sources you configured in Database Tools and SQL, so you do not enter the same connection details twice. In the free IDEs it connects over JDBC on its own.
  • Questions about the schema, not just the rows. "How are these tables related?" is answered in plain language from your schema, and a query it suggests can be copied straight out.
  • Results you can read. A table, and a chart when the shape suits one: a bar chart for a label and a number, a line for a date. Export to CSV, or open the full result in an editor.
  • Teach it your vocabulary. A business glossary maps terms your schema does not define, which is also how you tell it that total_cents is cents.
  • Bring your own model. OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Groq, NVIDIA, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint including Azure AI Foundry. Ollama and LM Studio run on your machine with no API key.
  • Private by default. Zero telemetry. Only your schema reaches the model, never the rows in your tables, unless you switch on sample column values yourself. Secrets live in your OS keychain.
  • Costs nothing until you ask. Installed and idle, it loads no classes, adds nothing to IDE startup, and sits at 0.2% CPU. Connecting to a wide Postgres schema reads its keys and indexes in three catalog queries rather than three per table.
  • Every JetBrains IDE. IntelliJ IDEA, DataGrip, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, PhpStorm, Rider, CLion, RubyMine, RustRover and Android Studio (2024.2 and newer).

AskSQL reads. It does not write, migrate or manage schemas, and it does not replace your IDE's database tools.

Getting started

  1. Open the AskSQL tool window on the right.
  2. Add a database connection, or point AskSQL at a data file.
  3. In Settings > Tools > AskSQL, choose a model. Ollama runs on your machine and needs no API key.
  4. Ask a question, review the SQL it writes, and approve it to run.

Full documentation: plugin README. Source and issues: github.com/rahulmahadik/AskSQL. Author: Rahul Mahadik
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.7.0 - 2026-08-21

Fixed

  • A SQLite database with roughly 500 or more columns across all its tables - ordinary for a real Android app - could fail to import at all, reporting the file as unreadable. It imports normally now, at any size.
  • Approving and running a generated query no longer loses the note that its row limit was capped; the warning now appears with the results, the same as it does before you approve.
  • A query whose row limit was lowered rather than newly added is now correctly flagged as returning a partial result.
  • Oracle connections: schema hints and generated queries now agree on how row limits are written, instead of contradicting each other. Introspecting a wide Oracle or MySQL schema is also substantially faster, since primary keys, foreign keys and indexes are now read for the whole schema in a few queries instead of several per table.
  • A very wide schema no longer leaves later tables with no column hints at all; the hint budget is now shared evenly instead of spent on whichever tables are introspected first.
  • The schema sent to the model states when a list of triggers, procedures, sequences, enum values, functions or join paths has been trimmed, instead of presenting a cut-down list as the whole one.

idea-plugin.name: Marginalis
idea-plugin.description:
Review AI-written code where it lives. Marginalis lets you and your coding agent discuss code in comment threads anchored to the lines they are about, inside your JetBrains IDE.

Agents write code faster than anyone can review it in a chat window. Marginalis moves the review into the editor. The agent leaves findings, questions and walkthroughs next to the code, you answer in place, and a thread closes only when its outcome is in the code.

What you get

  • Feedback next to the code. Threads attach to a line, a selection, a file or the whole project, and stay attached through edits and restarts.
  • Clear turns. Badges on files and in the tool window show what waits on you. Submit your replies as one round while your agents keep listening, see who is listening or working at a glance, or switch a single thread to Live for a quick back and forth.
  • Reviews that sort themselves. The agent marks what blocks, what is a nit and what needs no answer, so you can focus on what matters first.
  • Pull request reviews in one place. Your agent brings a PR's review comments, from teammates and review bots, next to the code they are about, each one attributed to its author.
  • Guided walkthroughs. The agent takes you through a change step by step.
  • Decisions in one click. Agree with a proposal without typing, and follow links straight to the code under discussion.
  • Several agents, one margin. A designing agent and an implementing agent can share the same threads without getting in each other's way.

Getting started

Install the plugin, then give your agent the skill with one command. It works with Claude Code and more than 70 other agents:

npx skills add MuhammadFarag/marginalis -g -y

Any other agent can learn the full protocol from the running plugin at GET http://127.0.0.1:63342/api/marginalis/agent_guide.

Private by design

Your threads stay with your project on your machine. The plugin talks to your agent over the IDE's local server and never writes to GitHub. Open source under Apache-2.0.

idea-plugin.name: Subscription ACP Agent
idea-plugin.description:
Use your Claude Pro/Max subscription in JetBrains AI chat — no API key, no JetBrains AI credits, no manual npm setup.

Adds a Claude Subscription agent to JetBrains AI chat that authenticates directly with your Claude.ai Pro or Max subscription.

Why this plugin

JetBrains IDEs already ship a Claude agent, but it runs on JetBrains AI credits or requires an Anthropic API key (BYOK). Many developers already pay for Claude Pro or Max and would rather use that subscription in the IDE, and some organizations restrict API token creation entirely. The known workaround is a global npm install of the ACP adapter plus hand-editing the agent configuration.

How it works

The Claude agent bundled with the IDE is launched with --hide-claude-auth, which removes the subscription auth method and rejects subscription credentials at session start with "This integration does not support using claude.ai subscriptions" — surfacing as "Authentication was reset. Please create a new chat for the change to take effect."

This plugin registers the same official @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp package as a local agent without that flag, and gives it the Claude icon. Nothing is patched: the package supports subscriptions by default.

What you get

  • One-click install from the Marketplace: no npm, no config files, no wrapper scripts
  • Sign in with your Claude.ai account, the standard Claude Pro/Max login, no API key
  • Requests go to your Claude subscription instead of JetBrains AI credits
  • Open source, MIT licensed

FAQ

How is this different from the Claude agent bundled with the IDE? The bundled agent runs on JetBrains AI credits or an Anthropic API key. This one signs in with your Claude.ai subscription.

How is this different from installing the ACP adapter via npm myself? Same underlying package, just packaged as a plugin: no global npm install, no manual agent registration, and updates arrive through the IDE.

Does it consume JetBrains AI credits? No. Requests are handled by the Claude agent under your own Claude subscription.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic or JetBrains.

Private by design: read-only over your local logs, no telemetry. Available in 8 languages.

A JetBrains port of the MIT-licensed VS Code extension Claude Code Usage.

idea-plugin.name: LLM Cheburnexus
idea-plugin.description:
LLM Cheburnexus is a full compiler-grade code engine. It runs fully automatically. In Claude Code the engine connects by itself and a search hook steers the search to it. In other editors the assistant sees grep_compiler next to its own search.

You work as usual and change nothing. Your assistant searches code with one tool — grep_compiler. It is the same familiar search, with hints from the engine.

  • Where the engine is stronger than plain search, it helps and drops the noise. It shows right away who calls a method, who inherits a class, who implements an interface. Without it, the agent needs several rounds of searching for this.
  • Where plain search is enough, it stays silent.

One tool, so the assistant doesn't have to choose between two searches. Usually the cost is the same. Sometimes there is an extra move, or the answer is a bit longer than plain search. On relation questions it saves moves.

The engine has a separate core for C#, TS/JS, Python and Java. Accuracy on C# is close to 100%. You can check this on the fully open benchmark: cheburnexus-bench.

I'm into game development, so most testing was done on C#. There the benefit is proven.

I compared the assistant with and without the engine. On questions about relations in code, the engine saves moves:

  • Who calls a method. Especially when different classes have methods with the same name. In one test it took 5 moves instead of 14 and cost half as much.
  • Subclasses, including indirect ones. Plain search often misses them.
  • Who implements an interface, who depends on a class.

On the Drevo benchmark (C#) the assistant makes about 12% fewer moves overall, and more on relation questions. Answer quality is no worse than with plain search.

TypeScript has been checked by hand on large open-source projects. On Python and Java the engine works but is not tested. For these languages the engine also answers who calls a function and what it depends on. The assistant does not get a project overview; the Project Graph below shows the map of the project. How many moves this saves has not been measured yet.

The project is built on enthusiasm and is completely free. I can't keep developing it alone for now: I have neither the time nor the resources. Python and Java will most likely stay untested unless someone helps. Any help is welcome: runs on your projects, feedback. And if you need a developer, write: t.me/cheburnexus.

The grep_compiler row in the tool window (shows ON/OFF) switches how your assistant searches: grep_compiler mode (default) advertises our tool and, in Claude Code specifically, also turns its built-in Grep tool off, so it reaches for grep_compiler instead of both — the setup we benchmarked. grep mode hides grep_compiler and leaves built-in search alone. For Codex, Cursor and JetBrains AI Assistant only grep_compiler's own visibility changes — turning off their native search is not yet supported by the plugin. Restart the assistant session after switching. See the in-IDE manual for details.

Every response reports how many tokens it saved you. The plugin registers the engine as an MCP server for JetBrains AI Assistant and downloads it on first run. One manual step: JetBrains adds such servers disabled, so tick the cheburnexus checkbox once in Settings → Tools → AI Assistant → Model Context Protocol (MCP) (the plugin shows a notification with a button that opens this page). The engine can also build a project map: click Project Graph in the tool window to view it on the site. All analysis runs locally; your code is never uploaded anywhere. Free for everyone: no key, no daily quota, no trimmed output.

Questions or problems? Open the Cheburnexus tool window and click Community & Support — questions, feedback and bug reports all go to t.me/cheburnexus. If something misbehaves, run Cheburnexus: Collect Problem Report (Find Action) — it gathers the analysis log and settings into a file for you to review and send. The file is opened locally and never uploaded.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Before this version, plugin users effectively got plain grep: the engine's Pro gate and the code profile kept the compiler answers off for people without a license. Now everything is free and switched on, with one tool, grep_compiler, plus the search hook. Unity projects (in any editor) still follow the Unity trial and limits.
  • By default the assistant sees only one engine tool, grep_compiler. With the search tool switched to built-in grep, this limit is not applied (grep_compiler is hidden then, and the engine would offer no tools at all).
  • The search-guard hook refuses a grep/rg command only when the engine knows more about the name (callers, subclasses, type references), and the refusal carries a ready grep_compiler call. Other searches pass through.
  • Callers, subclasses and references: TypeScript, Python and Java are approximate; C# goes through the compiler.
  • License and subscription actions are removed (Set License Key, Plan and Trial rows). The product is free.

idea-plugin.name: Iris Code
idea-plugin.description:
Iris Code is a deterministic, local-first code-health and enforcement engine for AI-assisted software development.

It provides inline diagnostics, quick fixes, per-file health scores, security and secret checks, duplicate detection, configuration-aware analysis, and detail views for dependencies, duplicates, suppressions, file naming and trends. Source code stays on your machine.

The JetBrains plugin uses the same Iris analysis engine as the VS Code extension, command-line interface, git hooks, and CI gate.

Setup

Install the LSP4IJ plugin first, then restart the IDE fully rather than reloading the plugin: JetBrains registers file-type associations at startup.

Troubleshooting

If .irisconfig.json reports "JSON standard does not allow comments", your IDE is holding a user-level override that cancels the JSON5 file-type association this plugin registers, and reinstalling will not clear it. Open Settings | Editor | File Types, select JSON5, and add .irisconfig.json back to its file-name patterns. Full guide: docs.iriscode.co/installation

  • Three Ruby rules: method_missing defined without respond_to_missing?, god classes, and Rails parameters reaching a model without require and permit.
  • Fixed: Iris Code refused to load in an IDE where the bundled Terminal plugin is disabled. Terminal is now optional and only the one action that runs a dependency update needs it; with it off, that action names the command instead of running it.

idea-plugin.name: Agent-Up Commit Queue
idea-plugin.description:
Agent-Up Commit Queue integrates the local Agent-Up commit queue with the JetBrains Commit tool window. It is built for repositories that use the Agent-Up commits workflow to stage one queued vertical-slice commit at a time.

Requirements:

  • The Agent-Up CLI must be installed and available as agent-up, or configured under Settings | Tools | Agent-Up.
  • The opened IDE project or one of its parent directories must contain agent-up.json.
  • The CLI must support agent-up commits status --format json and agent-up commits next --format json.

Usage:

  • Open the Commit tool window.
  • The Agent-Up logo appears in the commit-message action area.
  • A grey icon means the queue is empty; a red icon means the CLI is unavailable or returned an error.
  • When queued entries exist, click the Agent-Up logo to run commits next.
  • The plugin refreshes Git changes and inserts the queued commit message into the commit-message field.

The plugin does not create commits by itself. It stages the next Agent-Up queue entry so you can review the diff and commit manually inside the IDE.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Adds Commit tool window integration for the Agent-Up commits queue.

idea-plugin.name: Context2Prompt
idea-plugin.description:
Context2Prompt copies files, project structure, and code problems from your IDE as LLM-ready prompts.

Select files or folders in the Project view, open files, or a file with errors - and get a clean, XML-formatted prompt in your clipboard, ready to paste into Claude, ChatGPT, or any other assistant.

Features

  • Copy Files to Prompt — selected files and folders with content, formatted as XML documents with project structure
  • Copy Structure to Prompt — compact project tree without file content
  • Copy Open Files to Prompt — all open editor tabs in one prompt
  • Copy Problems to Prompt — errors and warnings from the current file or current line, with or without full file content
  • .gitignore support — respects your ignore rules, including nested ignore files, with a prompt to include ignored items explicitly
  • .c2pignore — plugin-specific ignore rules that override .gitignore (add or re-include entries just for prompts)
  • Skips binary and oversized files automatically
  • Notification with file count and approximate token estimate
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.0

Added

  • Copy selected files and folders with content as XML-formatted LLM prompt
  • Copy project structure without content
  • Copy all open editor tabs to prompt
  • Copy problems (errors/warnings) from current line or whole file, with or without file content
  • .gitignore and nested ignore files support with confirmation dialog for ignored items
  • .c2pignore for plugin-specific overrides
  • Binary and oversized file filtering, token count estimation

idea-plugin.name: FlashFlow
idea-plugin.description:
FlashFlow analyzes your Android XML layouts and flags the hierarchy problems that slow down rendering.

Android Lint tells you the layout is deep. FlashFlow tells you it is 11 levels deep, where, and what to do about it.

The six rules, with the exact message you'll see

  • FF-L001 — View hierarchy too deep: "View hierarchy is 11 levels deep (threshold 8). Flatten with ConstraintLayout, or extract the inner block into a <merge> layout."
  • FF-L002 — Too many views in one layout: "This layout has 94 views (threshold 80). Move the repeated item block into a RecyclerView."
  • FF-L003 — Nested layout_weight: "Nested layout_weight forces 2 measure passes instead of 1. Replace the inner weighted LinearLayout with ConstraintLayout chains."
  • FF-L004 — Useless parent view: "This <FrameLayout> wraps exactly 1 child but has no background, padding, or id — it adds a measure/layout pass for 0 visual purpose. Remove it and move its child up to the parent."
  • FF-L005 — Pre-AndroidX widget: "This layout uses 3 pre-AndroidX widget(s) (target: 0 — e.g. TextView instead of AppCompatTextView). Switch to the AppCompat/Material equivalents to pick up tinting, autosizing, and other AndroidX features."
  • FF-L006 — Overdraw risk: "The root and at least one direct child both draw a background — 2 overlapping fills instead of 1. Remove the background from whichever one is never actually visible, usually the root."

Issue tracker integration

An optional Tasks tab shows the issues assigned to you next to your layout findings — connect Jira Cloud or GitHub Issues under Settings → Tools → FlashFlow → Issue Trackers. Open a task to read its full description, comments, labels, linked issues and attachments without leaving the IDE, and switch between projects, boards and sprints (GitHub: repositories and milestones).

AI assistant

Pick a provider and paste your key. Presets ship for OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Google (Gemini), xAI (Grok), Moonshot (Kimi), Zhipu (GLM), MiniMax, Perplexity, SiliconFlow, OpenRouter, Groq, Mistral, Together, Ollama and LM Studio — plus Custom for any other OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Every field stays editable, and the model list can be fetched live from the endpoint, so a new model works the day it ships. There is no bundled key and no FlashFlow account.

  • Chat about the code you have open, with streaming replies you can stop at any time.
  • Solve with AI on any tracker issue sends the task — description, comments, labels, linked issues — together with your open project files, and gets back a plan and concrete edits.
  • It writes the files. A code block tagged with a file path is applied when the reply finishes, through the IDE's own write-command machinery — so it lands in the undo stack, one Ctrl+Z reverses it, and it shows up in your VCS diff like anything you typed. Every edit is listed with a Diff link.
  • You control this: turn off Write code blocks to files automatically to review and apply each change yourself, or turn on Ask before replacing an existing file to be prompted first. Both are under Settings → Tools → FlashFlow → AI Assistant.
  • Free to use. There is no trial period, no account, and no bundled key — you bring your own endpoint and your provider bills you for the tokens, not us.
  • The assistant can also comment on a tracker issue and move it to Done, when you ask it to.

Privacy

All layout analysis runs locally — no account, no network requests, nothing leaves your machine. The issue tracker and AI integrations are opt-in and off until you add an account; when you do, the plugin talks only to the servers you configured. API keys and tokens are stored in the IDE's password safe, never in project files, and request bodies, prompts and tokens are never logged.

The assistant sends code only when you ask it to, and the transcript lists exactly which files were included in each request. Chat sessions are saved under .flashflow/sessions/ inside your project; because those transcripts can contain source code, the plugin writes a .gitignore there the first time it is used so they are not committed by accident.

Full privacy policy: flashflow.flashdevhub.com/privacy

How to use it

  1. Open the FlashFlow tool window (right dock) and click "Analyze Module".
  2. Findings also appear inline in the XML editor, with a gutter icon on any layout that has them.
  3. Tune which rules run and at what threshold under Settings → Tools → FlashFlow.

What's not included yet

Compose analysis is not included yet — this release covers XML layouts only. There is no web dashboard and no trend tracking over time.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.2

  • Fix All with AI. One button sends every finding in the report to the assistant. Large reports are split into several requests automatically and run one after another, because one oversized request does not fail loudly — the model answers about the first few files and drops the rest.
  • Accounts are shared across projects. API keys and tracker accounts were stored per project, so every new project asked for them again. They are now application-level, matching where the credentials themselves already lived.
  • "Thinking…" while reasoning is hidden. A model that reasons before answering used to look like a model that had hung.
  • Fixed: long rule ids and file names collided with the next column in the tool window.

Compose UI debt. FlashFlow now analyses Jetpack Compose alongside XML layouts. Six new rules, reported in the same tool window:

  • FF-C001 — layout composables nested too deeply.
  • FF-C002 — one composable emitting so much that any state change recomposes all of it.
  • FF-C003 — a lazy list item with no key, so inserting or reordering loses item state.
  • FF-C004 — mutableStateOf without remember. A correctness bug: the value silently resets on every recomposition.
  • FF-C005 — a scrollable inside a scrollable on the same axis.
  • FF-C006 — a public composable that emits UI but takes no Modifier.

Details for every finding. Select any row to see what the rule measures, why it costs something, and the fix — for XML and Compose alike.

Fix a whole category at once. Select a rule and hand every occurrence of it to the assistant as one piece of work, instead of asking file by file.

Everything is still free. The analyser, the AI assistant and the issue trackers are all free to use. If that ever changes it will be announced clearly and in advance — it will not appear as a surprise paywall in an update.

1.0.1 — first public release

Layout analysis — free, and local. Six rules over your XML layouts: hierarchy depth (FF-L001), view count (FF-L002), nested layout_weight (FF-L003), useless parent views (FF-L004), pre-AndroidX widgets (FF-L005) and overdraw risk (FF-L006). Results appear in the UI Debt tool window, as inline editor inspections, and as gutter icons. Thresholds are yours to set.

Issue trackers — connect Jira Cloud or GitHub Issues and read your assigned issues beside your findings, with full descriptions, comments, labels and attachments, without leaving the IDE.

AI assistant — bring your own key and base URL. Sixteen providers are preconfigured and anything speaking the OpenAI or Anthropic wire format works without a preset. It reads and writes files in your project, saves sessions under .flashflow/sessions/, and can comment on a tracker issue and move it to Done when you ask.

Privacy — no servers, no account, no telemetry. Analysis never leaves your machine; the assistant and trackers talk only to the endpoints you configure. Keys live in the IDE password safe. Full policy.

idea-plugin.name: Aletyx Automation Design
idea-plugin.description:
Design, run, analyze, and improve business decisions without leaving your IDE.

Aletyx Automation Design brings a serious DMN workspace to IntelliJ IDEA and compatible JetBrains IDEs. Build decision models visually, work with FEEL confidently, exercise decisions against real inputs, review changes at model level, and use AI to accelerate the work while you remain in control of every edit.

Built for developers who ship decisions

  • Visual DMN authoring — Create and maintain DRDs, decision tables, boxed expressions, data types, decision services, and included models in a polished graphical editor.
  • FEEL that feels like code — Get completion, diagnostics, definition navigation, and evaluated values on hover for faster debugging.
  • Run before you ship — Execute multiple input rows locally, inspect outputs, and pin expected results as regression checks with immediate pass/fail feedback.
  • Review semantic changes — Understand model, node, data-type, expression, row, column, and cell changes with focused highlights and granular accept/revert actions.
  • Find decision-table problems early — Validation and analysis surface gaps, overlaps, missing rules, and actionable details beside the editor.
  • AI-assisted modeling — Ask Aletyx AI to explain, analyze, or modify a model. Proposed edits arrive as reviewable changes rather than silent rewrites.
  • Native JetBrains experience — The workbench follows the IDE theme and uses the JetBrains Password Safe for your AI credential.

Start in seconds

  1. Install the plugin and open a .dmn or .dmns file.
  2. Edit visually, then use Run to exercise the decision against your inputs.
  3. Open Analysis to investigate decision-table findings.
  4. Open Aletyx AI when you want help understanding or changing the model.

The plugin also recognizes .bpmn and .bpmn2 files.

Aletyx AI Assistant

Use the gear in the Assistant header—or choose Tools › Aletyx Automation Design › Set AI Assistant API Key—to add or replace your key. The credential is stored in the JetBrains Password Safe and is supplied only to the local decision backend.

AI-generated model edits are presented in Changes, where you can inspect and accept or revert them before they become part of your model.

Local decision backend

The bundled backend starts automatically when a supported model opens. It requires Java 17 or newer. If Java is not available through JAVA_HOME or PATH, configure Settings › Tools › Aletyx Automation Design › Java home.

Your local model files remain in your project. Content is sent to an Aletyx offering only when you explicitly use a connected feature such as the AI Assistant.

Actions

Under Tools › Aletyx Automation Design:

  • Set AI Assistant API Key
  • Clear AI Assistant API Key
  • Restart Decision Backend
  • Stop Decision Backend

See the complete 10.2.3 changelog.

Copyright © 2025–2026 Aletyx, Inc. Use is governed by the Aletyx Automation Design license.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
10.2.12

  • Fixed a boxed invocation of a function from an included model returning no result, which left the decision empty with nothing reported to explain it. Models already saved that way evaluate again as they are
  • Fixed included models not being found when they sit at the root of the project or when the model you open lives outside the project's own directory, in an attached project or a module elsewhere, which drew every node coming from them as unknown and left the model unable to evaluate

10.2.11

  • Copy, cut and paste now work on the diagram, in decision tables and in the editor's own fields, with whatever keys your keymap assigns them. They were doing nothing at all: the IDE claimed the keystroke before the editor could see it
  • What you copy now goes to the system clipboard, so you can copy nodes in the IDE and paste them into the same model open in a browser, and the other way round

10.2.10

  • Shift and the mouse wheel now scroll the diagram sideways. IntelliJ turns that gesture into horizontal movement before the editor sees it, and the editor was turning it back, so the two cancelled out and nothing moved
  • The diagram now has scroll bars along its bottom and right edges. They show how much of the model you are looking at, and you can drag them, click the track to move a screen at a time, or double-click it to fit the whole model in view
  • Undo and redo now work on the diagram, with whatever keys your keymap assigns them. They did nothing at all: the IDE claimed the keystroke for its own undo, which had nothing to undo for a model that keeps its history in the editor rather than in a text document

10.2.9

  • Pasting a column of values onto a decision table cell that spans several rules now fills each rule with its own value. Only the first value used to be kept, and it was repeated down the whole span
  • Deleting a decision table cell that spans several rules now clears only the rules you selected. It used to empty every rule the span covers, including rules above your selection, because blank cells and `-` join the span too
  • Copying or cutting rules joined into one cell now keeps each rule's own text instead of repeating the one shown on the merged cell
  • The header above a boxed expression no longer slides out of view when you scroll a wide decision table sideways, and it now takes up less vertical space

10.2.8

  • Fixed accepting the AI Assistant's proposed changes putting the model back as it was instead of applying them
  • Fixed a model the AI Assistant generated never reaching disk, so it was gone the next time the file was opened
  • Your model is now saved before the AI-suggested rename moves the file, and the rename is skipped if that save fails — renaming ahead of the save used to replace the generated model with the file it had just written over
  • Saving now waits for the editor's own content, so a save asked for right after the assistant writes a model no longer stores the version from before it
  • The AI Assistant no longer offers to replace a model outright when it only holds data types, imports, decision services or saved test scenarios; those changes go through the review diff like any other
  • Your AI Assistant conversation now follows you across the models in a project, so renaming a model no longer loses its chat history

10.2.7

  • Fixed the BPMN properties panel not scrolling, which left the fields below the fold unreachable
  • The DMN and BPMN editors now run directly in the editor page instead of an embedded frame, so a model opens faster and with less memory

10.2.6

  • A completely redesigned BPMN editor, aligned with the modern look and feel of the DMN editor
  • Faster, more responsive editing for large DMN decision tables
  • Quickly switch between DMN boxed expressions

10.2.5

  • A guided tour now runs the first time you open a DMN model: it walks you through the editor and can build a small example beside yours, as a scratch file that goes away when you leave. Take it again from Tools, Aletyx Automation Design, Take the Editor Tour
  • When the AI Assistant suggests a name for your model, the notification now offers to rename the file for you

10.2.4

  • Fixed the editor being unable to reach its decision backend on recent IntelliJ versions, which left the AI Assistant, the DMN Runner, validation and decision-table analysis unavailable

10.2.3

  • FEEL literal expressions are no longer rewritten. They are still displayed as boxed expressions, but your file keeps the expression exactly as you wrote it
  • Fixed list access by index, such as `People[Index]`, being turned into a Filter — a conversion that changed the meaning of the expression and left the decision unable to evaluate
  • Boxed expressions displayed from a FEEL literal can now be edited directly, and your changes go back into the FEEL text
  • Convert a single expression between FEEL text and boxed form from its context menu, in either direction
  • Repair a model an earlier version already rewrote, by converting the affected expression back to the FEEL text it was authored as
  • A context displayed from a FEEL literal now offers a result row, and filling it in turns the expression into a boxed context
  • "Evaluation failed" in the DMN Runner is no longer a dead end: it shows the reason the engine gave, including reasons raised against a nested part of the decision, and links to the Analysis or Validation entry that explains it — reachable from the keyboard
  • Fixed a selected node taking keyboard focus away from the properties panel, the DMN Runner form, and other fields in the workbench
  • Fixed the properties panel showing the previously selected node's name after confirming a rename
  • The active canvas tool is now clearly marked in the toolbar
  • Restored pinch-to-zoom and Ctrl/Cmd + scroll zoom on the canvas

10.2.2

  • Reach Aletyx AI Assistant through a corporate HTTP or HTTPS proxy, including authenticated proxies, bypass lists, and custom CA certificates

10.2.1

  • Fixed the editor not opening on IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2 and later, where DMN and BPMN files fell back to the XML editor
  • Fixed connectors disappearing behind a Decision Service, including requirements between contained decisions and associations crossing the boundary
  • Fixed a Decision Service hiding the decisions inside it while hovered to reach its context menu
  • Fixed connections snapping to a Decision Service instead of the decision being targeted inside it
  • Fixed the DMN Runner table view not scrolling horizontally when the outputs are wider than the pane
  • The DMN Runner table view now opens evenly split and its divider can be dragged across the full width
  • Renamed the Changes tab to AI Changes, with a new icon, to reflect that it lists AI-proposed edits rather than version-control changes
  • Fixed Red Hat fonts failing to load, which left the canvas rendering in a fallback typeface

10.2.0

  • Work in a modernized DMN canvas with Aletyx light and dark themes, clearer hierarchy, improved spacing, and more precise selection.
  • Navigate large models with pan-by-default controls, lasso and hand tools, keyboard navigation, and improved zoom behavior.
  • Create and manage Decision Services directly on the canvas, including collapse, expand, move, and resize interactions.
  • Work with included models and namespaces more reliably, including linked types and cross-model references.
  • Recover more gracefully from invalid or partially edited models without losing access to the editor.
  • Use richer FEEL completion, diagnostics, and go-to-definition across decision logic and data types.
  • Edit expressions in a larger focused editor with improved inline name editing.
  • Author complex contexts, invocations, relations, lists, functions, and nested expressions with clearer structure.
  • Get completion for nested enumerations, Java-backed types, and types from included models.
  • Create decision-table-only `.dmns` files alongside standard `.dmn` models.
  • Use the Priority hit policy in editing, analysis, execution, and result visualization.
  • Detect gaps, overlaps, and missing rules in nested decision-table structures.
  • Search and import data types, define inline enumerations, and manage nested fields and references more easily.
  • Inspect model changes in a dedicated Changes view with counts, grouping, and focused navigation.
  • See granular highlights for model properties, nodes, edges, data types, boxed expressions, decision-table cells, rows, and columns.
  • Accept or revert individual changes, logical groups, or all changes at once.
  • Keep your active editing context while reviewing changes, with complete dark-theme support.
  • Generate input forms from your model and run one or multiple input rows locally.
  • Define expected outputs and see clear pass/fail regression results.
  • Pin important outputs and visualize evaluation results directly on the diagram and decision tables.
  • Run Camunda-compatible models and Priority hit-policy tables more reliably.
  • Preserve runner inputs while editing and rerun decisions with fewer interruptions.
  • Review validation and analysis findings from dedicated workbench views.
  • Find gaps, overlaps, missing rules, and problems in nested decision logic.
  • Open a finding directly in its detailed analysis and focused model highlight.
  • Read findings clearly in both light and dark themes.
  • Ask Aletyx AI to explain, analyze, and modify DMN models without leaving the editor.
  • Review AI-generated edits before accepting or reverting them.
  • Generate runner inputs and test cases from your model and conversation.
  • Keep conversation history, queue prompts while work is in progress, retry failed requests, and attach supporting files.
  • Ask AI about validation and analysis findings from their context menus.
  • Configure API access securely from the assistant, with clearer setup, loading, reconnecting, and unavailable states.
  • Use a more compact, responsive layout across regular and smaller editor windows.
  • Access editing, execution, validation, analysis, changes, and AI tools with improved keyboard, pointer, and drag behavior.
  • Benefit from fixes for selection loss, stale highlights, analysis-detail navigation, and editing crashes.
  • Open Aletyx AI settings directly from the assistant and configure Java Home for the local decision service.

See the bundled CHANGELOG.md for the complete release notes.

idea-plugin.name: Smart Git Commit LLM
idea-plugin.description:
Smart Git Commit LLM is a Git commit message generation plugin based on large language models.
Smart Git Commit LLM 是一款基于大模型的 Git 提交信息生成插件。插件会读取当前提交窗口中选中的代码变更或当前项目的未提交变更，自动整理 diff 内容，并调用配置好的大模型生成符合 Conventional Commits 规范的中文提交信息。

主要功能
根据 Git diff 自动生成清晰、简洁的提交信息。
支持中文 Conventional Commits 格式，例如 feat(scope): 描述、fix(scope): 描述。
支持激活码模式：激活成功后自动获取可用的大模型配置。
支持手动配置模式：可自行填写 OpenAI 或 Anthropic 兼容接口地址、API Key 和模型名称。
支持自定义提示词，用于调整提交信息的生成风格和输出规则。

使用方法
安装插件后，打开 Settings / Preferences > Tools > AI Commit Generator。
选择配置方式：
直接使用（激活码）：输入激活码后点击"激活"，激活成功后插件会自动保存大模型配置。
手动配置：手动填写 API Type、Base URL、API Key 和 Model Name。
根据需要调整 Timeout 和 Custom Prompt，然后保存设置。
打开 IDE 的 Commit 窗口，选择需要提交的变更文件。
点击提交信息区域中的 Generate AI Commit Message 操作，或使用快捷键 Alt+G。
插件会读取变更 diff，调用大模型生成提交信息，并自动填入 Commit Message 输入框。

激活码获取方式
如需使用激活码模式，请通过官方渠道获取激活码：公众号《魔法数字》。

idea-plugin.name: Raplify
idea-plugin.description:
Raplify is a GUI for AI coding agents, right inside your JetBrains IDE.

Four tool windows, one context: the agent you talk to, the endpoints your service exposes, the path a request takes through the code, and the database underneath it — none of which need a second app or a browser tab.

  • REST APIs — every endpoint discovered in your source, grouped by method and searchable by path. Click a route to jump straight to the handler.
  • Java call flow — the path a request takes through your codebase, resolved from a real index of the project rather than guessed from names.
  • AI chat — an agent in a side panel with your editor selection as context. Model and permission-mode selectors, tool cards, and project commands.
  • Database schema — connect a source and browse tables, columns, keys and relations beside your code, with the ERD laid out for you.
Requires Node.js and the Claude CLI installed.


Every REST endpoint discovered in your source — click a route to jump to its handler.


The path a request takes through your codebase, resolved from a real index of the project.


An AI agent in a side panel, with your editor selection as context.


Connect a database source and browse tables, columns and keys beside your code.

idea-plugin.name: Codotchi
idea-plugin.description:
Grow and raise your personal virtual pet as a JetBrains plugin while you code.

Overview

codotchi is a JetBrains plugin that lets you raise a digital pet inspired by the original Tamagotchi. Your pet lives in a tool window panel, reacts to your coding activity, and needs regular care to survive and evolve into its final form. Any support and feedback is much appreciated — see the Support section below!

Your pet is drawn from one of 7 sprite sets, with more to be added in the future, assigned to you at random when you start a new game.

Preview

Sponsor this project

buymeacoffee.com/dylscoop

liberapay.com/dylscoop

Integrations

Looking for the Claude Code or OpenCode terminal integrations? Visit github.com/dylscoop/codotchi to download the plugins — your pet's state is shared across VS Code, PyCharm, and the terminal.

Features

  • Tool window pet panel — pixel art pet with animated sprites, stat bars, and action buttons rendered in a JCEF webview
  • Classic Tamagotchi mechanics — hunger, happiness, discipline, energy, health, weight, and age stats, all decaying in real time
  • Full care system — feed meals and snacks, play mini-games, put pet to sleep, clean droppings, give medicine, scold and praise
  • Life cycle & evolution — egg → baby → child → teen → adult → senior, with the final character determined by how well you cared for your pet
  • Moods you can see — a happy pet sparkles, a sad pet sheds a tear, a sleeping pet dozes with drifting z's, and a pet stops to eat its meal from a bowl
  • Pet customisation — name your pet and choose a pet type on first launch
  • Desktop alerts — when hunger, happiness or energy hits 0, or health drops below 25, you get a desktop notification, even with the IDE minimised. It repeats every 15 minutes while the stat stays low; turn it off in Settings
  • Sickness & death — neglect your pet and it gets sick; leave it untreated and it dies. A sick pet won't eat, snack or play until it's had its medicine — the Medicine button counts the doses left
  • Safe while you are away — when you step away from the IDE your pet gets hungry and bored more slowly and never loses health, so it is waiting for you when you come back
  • Seasons and time of day — your pet lives in a pixel-art scene that follows the real month and clock: blossom trees and spring showers with a rainbow, sunflowers and fireflies in summer, falling leaves and pumpkins in autumn, and a snowman, fairy lights and snowfall in winter. The sky moves from a warm sunrise through a bright morning to sunset and starry night. Pick a fixed season or a plain background in Settings, soften the scene so your pet stands out, or keep it still. Prefer the original look? Set Background style to Legacy
  • Little whims — now and then your pet just wants to play a game, get a pat, or have a meal or a snack, even when it isn't hungry or sad. Answer in time and it's happy; ignore it and its health suffers
  • Break reminders — after 30 minutes of coding, your pet reminds you to take a break. Praise it to answer: it's happier for it and naps for 5 minutes while you rest (stats frozen except energy, which recharges, and it keeps aging). You can't wake it early — it wakes up on its own. Skipping it does no harm, and stepping away from the IDE counts as a break
  • Terminal & Claude integrations — your pet lives in Claude Code, OpenCode and Claude Desktop too, with shared state across every host
  • Today's Token Cost — see how much Claude Code / OpenCode has cost you today, plus your GitHub Copilot premium quota
  • Public leaderboard — sign in with GitHub to submit your pet when it dies, or push live progress while it's still going
  • Status bar integration — pet name and stage always visible in the IDE status bar, with a ⚠ while your pet wants something (hover to see what). Turn it off in Settings
  • Persistent state — pet survives IDE restarts; offline time is accounted for with capped stat decay
  • Configurable — customise font size, pet size, stage height, colours, idle thresholds, attention call behaviour, and more via Settings → Tools → Codotchi. Developer-mode settings sit in a collapsed Developer settings section

Requirements

  • JetBrains IDE version 2024.1 or later (IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, Rider, etc.)
  • JCEF must be enabled in your IDE (it is on by default in 2024.1+)

If the Codotchi panel appears blank: your IDE may be running on a JetBrains Runtime without JCEF. Open Help → Find Action (Shift+Ctrl+A / ⇧⌘A), search for "Choose Boot Java Runtime for the IDE", select a runtime with JCEF in its name, and restart the IDE.

Installation

Install Codotchi from the JetBrains Marketplace, or go to Settings → Plugins → Marketplace and search for Codotchi.

See the GitHub repository for manual installation, pre-built releases, and the OpenCode integration download.

Using the plugin

Once installed and the IDE has restarted:

  1. Click Codotchi in the right-hand tool window bar, or go to View → Tool Windows → Codotchi.
  2. On first launch the New Codotchi setup screen appears:
    • Enter a name (up to 16 characters).
    • Choose a pet type — each has different stat decay rates.
    • Click Hatch!
  3. Your pet now lives in the tool window. Care for it using the action buttons: Feed, Snack, Play, Pat, Sleep, Clean, Medicine, Praise, and Scold.
  4. Your pet's state is saved automatically and restored the next time the IDE opens. Stat decay while the IDE is closed is capped at 60% of each maximum so a long break won't instantly kill your pet.
  5. Your pet's name and current life stage are always visible in the status bar at the bottom of the IDE window.

Actions

ActionWhat it does
FeedGives your pet a full meal. Restores a large chunk of hunger. Overfeeding has no effect. Not available while your pet is sick.
SnackGives a small treat. Boosts happiness instead of hunger, but adds more weight. Eating too many snacks in a row will make your pet sick. Not available while your pet is sick.
PlayOpens the mini-game picker. Choose Left / Right, Higher or Lower, or Coin Flip. Winning boosts happiness; losing applies a small penalty. Costs energy — your pet can't play if exhausted or sick.
PatGives your pet a gentle pat. A hand pats its head, hearts float up and each pet reacts in its own way. Boosts happiness. Costs energy. Accessed via the Play menu. Cannot be used while your pet is sleeping or exhausted.
SleepPuts your pet to sleep. Energy slowly regenerates while it sleeps and your pet cannot take any other actions. Wake it manually or wait for full energy. During a break nap the button shows the minutes left and your pet wakes on its own.
CleanClears all droppings from the screen. Leaving too many uncleaned for too long will make your pet sick.
MedicineTreats sickness. Three doses cure it (the button shows how many are left); medicine does not restore health. Use it as soon as your pet falls ill, because sickness drains health until it is cured.
PraiseRewards good behaviour. Raises the discipline stat, which contributes to a better care score and a higher-tier evolution.
ScoldCorrects bad behaviour. Also raises discipline. Use it when your pet misbehaves rather than at random, as it has no direct stat benefit beyond discipline.

Tip: keep all four stat bars (Hunger, Happy, Energy, Health) out of the red to maximise your care score, which determines which character your pet evolves into at each life stage.

Leaderboard

Click Sign in to GitHub (Leaderboard) in the pet panel to link your GitHub account. The plugin uses GitHub's device-code sign-in: a browser page opens and a notification shows the code to enter. With live push turned on, your pet's progress is synced to the public leaderboard while it's alive. When it dies, click Submit to Leaderboard on the game over screen.

Only scores sent by the plugin itself are accepted. A pet that ever ran in dev mode, or whose save file was edited outside Codotchi, can't be submitted or pushed live, and the panel says why.

If GitHub rejects the saved sign-in (for example, because you revoked the app at github.com/settings/applications), the plugin forgets the old token. It then shows Sign in to GitHub again in the panel, and a notification with a Sign in action if live push was running in the background. Submitting a score starts a fresh sign-in automatically and retries the submission once.

GitHub sign-in help

You sign in once. You don't need a personal access token, your own GitHub app, or any changes to your GitHub settings.

  1. Click Sign in to GitHub (Leaderboard), either in the pet panel or in Settings → Tools → Codotchi.
  2. A browser opens at github.com/login/device, and a PyCharm notification shows an 8-character code.
  3. Enter the code, sign in to GitHub if asked, and click Authorize. Codotchi only asks for the public_repo permission, which it needs to submit leaderboard entries.
  4. Go back to PyCharm. It picks up the sign-in on its own within a few seconds.

If it doesn't work:

  • The browser didn't open: go to https://github.com/login/device yourself and enter the code from the notification.
  • The code expired: codes last about 15 minutes. Click Try again on the notification, or click the sign-in button again.
  • You cancelled the GitHub page: sign in again and click Authorize this time.
  • "Could not start GitHub sign-in (HTTP 4xx…)": the problem is on Codotchi's side, not yours. Open an issue and include the full error text.
  • "Network error during GitHub sign-in": PyCharm needs to reach github.com. If you're behind a corporate proxy, set it up under Settings → Appearance & Behavior → System Settings → HTTP Proxy.
  • You were signed out unexpectedly: you probably revoked Codotchi at github.com/settings/applications. Sign in again.

Mini-games

Clicking Play opens the game picker (requires energy). Three games are available:

GameHow to win
Left / RightThe pet hides behind one of two doors. Pick the correct door each round to win.
Higher or LowerA number is shown. Guess whether the next number will be higher or lower. Get enough correct to win.
Coin FlipCall Heads or Tails, then watch the coin spin. A single flip decides the outcome.

Pet Types

TypeTendency
CodelingBalanced across all stats
BytebugHigh energy, hunger decays faster
PixelpupHigh happiness, but happiness decays faster
ShellscriptSlow evolver, high base health

Each pet animal has its own sprite set.

"Grow your best pet by writing your best code."

Support

GitHub: github.com/dylscoop/codotchi

Codotchi Sprites

Want to see a new sprite in the game? Send a drawn sprite or request one to be added — a passcode will be given every time one gets implemented.

Open a sprite request on GitHub Issues

Pets hatched before this version can't be submitted either, but your next one can. Older scores stay on the board marked legacy.

2.25.4

idea-plugin.name: Go Commit AI
idea-plugin.description:
Generate commit messages from only the changes selected in the Commit tool window.

  • Works with OpenAI-compatible chat completion APIs.
  • Can reuse an existing Codex CLI login without configuring an API key.
  • Fetches available models from the configured provider.
  • Streams the generated message directly into the commit field.
  • Sends only the selected diff and never scans the whole project.
  • Stores the API key with JetBrains PasswordSafe.
  • Does not include telemetry or route requests through the plugin vendor.

The plugin never commits automatically. Review and edit every generated message before committing.

中文说明

根据 Commit 工具窗口中勾选的变更生成提交信息。支持 OpenAI 兼容 API，也可以复用本机 Codex CLI 的当前登录，无需另外填写 API Key。支持获取模型列表和流式输出；只发送选中的 diff，不扫描整个项目。API Key 使用 JetBrains PasswordSafe 保存。
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.4.5

  • Restored fast commit generation for the official DeepSeek API by disabling default high-effort thinking.
  • Kept vendor-specific thinking parameters away from other OpenAI-compatible providers to avoid compatibility errors.

0.4.4

  • Raised the configurable maximum output token limit from 1,024 to 65,536 for reasoning models.
  • Automatically retries once with a larger output budget when the model exhausts tokens before producing any commit message.

0.4.3

  • Raised the configurable Diff limit to 1,000,000 characters and added explicit validation.
  • Improved OpenAI-compatible API support by removing automatic vendor-specific thinking parameters.

0.4.2

  • Fixed false outdated-version warnings caused by truncated Codex CLI help output.
  • Retained the NVM and Node.js PATH startup fix from version 0.4.1.

idea-plugin.name: Claude Sessions Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Companion plugin for Claude Sessions, a desktop widget that shows the state of every Claude Code session you have running.

Inside the IDE it does three things:

  • Names terminal tabs after their session, so a row of Local, Local (2), Local (3) tabs becomes readable at a glance. A tab you renamed yourself is never touched.
  • Jumps to the session that needs you. Clicking a row in the widget raises the IDE and focuses the terminal tab running that session; right-click closes the tab and ends the session.
  • Adds Tools | New Claude Session, which opens a terminal tab and starts a session in the current project's directory.

The launch command is configurable under Settings | Tools | Claude Sessions and defaults to claude. It runs in an interactive shell, so your own shell alias works there too.

Tab naming and click-to-jump need the desktop app installed with its Claude Code hooks enabled — the plugin reads the state the app writes under ~/.claude/session-status/. Without the app, New Claude Session still works and the rest stays idle.

Not affiliated with Anthropic. Claude is a trademark of Anthropic PBC.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.6.0

  • First release on the JetBrains Marketplace.
  • The New Claude Session command is now configurable under Settings | Tools | Claude Sessions instead of being hardcoded, and defaults to claude.

idea-plugin.name: Claude/Codex Sub Autocomplete
idea-plugin.description:
Native autocomplete for IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, and Android Studio using the Claude Code or Codex subscription you already have—no API keys or separate autocomplete plan.

  • Switch explicitly between Claude Code and Codex and select a subscription model.
  • Generate expressions, multiline blocks, and comment-directed implementations as native ghost text.
  • Turn a # request into a reviewable shell command with Tab in your IDE's terminal.
  • Use bounded language-aware editor context, with recent-edit, open-tab, and cross-file sources separately opt-in.
  • Inspect connection state, request progress, safe errors, and latency from the status bar and diagnostics window.
  • Get automatic completions on first installation, or switch to hotkey-only mode in settings.

Requests go directly through the selected provider's installed CLI. The plugin does not operate a proxy or telemetry service. Provider tools, project inspection, file writes, and command execution are disabled. Terminal commands are inserted but never executed. Common credential patterns are redacted before requests are sent.

Requirements: IntelliJ IDEA or PyCharm 2025.3 or newer, or Android Studio Quail 4 (2026.1.4), the bundled Terminal plugin, Java 21 or newer, and an installed and authenticated Claude Code or Codex CLI.

Plugin installation, updates, and removal require an IDE restart.

Claude Code and Codex use agent models rather than purpose-built fill-in-the-middle models. Uncached suggestions can take several seconds, and quality depends on the selected model and context.

This is an independent project and is not affiliated with Anthropic, OpenAI, or JetBrains.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.6.5 — Early Access

  • Requires an IDE restart for plugin installation, updates, and removal to avoid unsafe dynamic reloads.
  • Removes terminal callbacks, cancels pending work, and closes plugin dialogs when the plugin unloads.
  • Replaces deprecated terminal APIs while preserving queued input and rejecting stale completion responses.
  • Requires isolated installer/restart and physical keyboard checks, current artifact evidence, and clean IDE logs before publication.
  • Keeps settings descriptions and executable fields within the dialog width.
  • Preserves automatic completion on first installation and existing saved settings across updates.

idea-plugin.name: Code Trace Tree
idea-plugin.description:
Trace code in a tree structure with AI support. Build and display code workflows as nested trace points (lines, files, and directories) so you can follow the flow and jump back to source anytime. Double-click any trace point to navigate to its source, with support for multiple trace levels.

Use it manually or pair it with the Agent Skill so coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI can search, add, move, and rebind traces, and notify the IDE to refresh.
This plugin does not include an AI agent; install your preferred agent separately, then install the code-trace-tree skill. Once installed, the agent can auto-load it when relevant.

How to use

  1. Open the Code Trace Tree tool window (right side of the IDE).
  2. Use the Profile selector under the toolbar to switch trees, add a profile (+), rename one, or delete one from the dropdown.
  3. In the editor, right-click a line in a project file and choose:
    • Create a Root Trace Point — start a new line-level trace tree (selects the new node; does not jump)
    • Create a Trace Point (Under Selected) — add a child under the selected node(s) in the tree (new node is selected)
    • Update the selected code trace point — move the selected tree node(s) to the current line
    • Go to the Trace Point in the tree panel (Only matching) — selects and reveals matching node(s) for the current line; does nothing when none match
  4. In the Project tool window, right-click a file or directory inside the project and choose:
    • Create a Root Trace Point — add a file or directory node at the root
    • Create a Trace Point (Under Selected) — add that file/directory under the selected tree node(s)
  5. Single-click a node to select it; double-click to jump to that location (line, file, or Project View for directories).
  6. Right-click a node and choose Go to Trace Point (first item) to jump to that location (same as double-click).
  7. Right-click a node and choose Copy Label (or use Ctrl/Cmd+C) to copy its display text, e.g. test233 (TestControllerWebFlux.java:54).
  8. Right-click a line trace point and choose Show Line Content to view its saved trimmed line text.
  9. Use the tool window toolbar to expand/collapse, Recheck Trace Availability, Remove Invalid Trace Points, reorder, highlight, prompt for name on create, or edit descriptions. Agent Skill installs or updates the bundled skill for coding agents. Import/Export live under Advanced Settings.

TIPS: Prefer creating line trace points on text that is unique in that file (or uncommon), not generic lines like } or return;. Empty lines are not allowed. The plugin stores occurrence counts to re-find the line after it moves; unique content rebinds more reliably.

Agent Skill

This plugin does not ship an AI agent. Install your preferred coding agent, then install the code-trace-tree skill. Once installed, the agent can auto-load it when your request is relevant, and the IDE syncs the agent's trace-point changes as they are written. The skill is general — any agent that can load skill folders can use it.

Same agents as npx skills (global install). Examples:

  • Claude Code
  • Cursor
  • GitHub Copilot (agent skills)
  • Codex
  • Gemini CLI

The skill lets the agent:

  • Resolve the bound global storage XML for the project
  • Search, add, move, and delete trace points
  • Rebind line locations after source edits on disk
  • Ask the IDE to reload / refresh plugin data
  • Select or navigate to nodes in the Code Trace Tree tool window

Agent Skill Installation

Python 3 required: skill scripts need Python 3 on your PATH (python3 or python). Choose agents and Install / Update stay disabled until Python 3 is found. Install Python 3, add it to PATH, then restart the IDE.

Open the Code Trace Tree tool window and click Agent Skill on the toolbar (download icon):

  • The status page shows the bundled skill version, whether Python 3 is on PATH, and which agents already have the skill.
  • Choose agents to install — pick agents that do not have it yet.
  • Install / Update — copy the bundled code-trace-tree skill into each listed agent's global skills folder (for example ~/.cursor/skills/code-trace-tree).
  • Remove from installed agents — delete those copies.

On first project open, if a detected agent is missing the skill or is behind the bundled version, the plugin shows a notification (once per skill version; Dismiss or opening the status page is remembered in global settings.xml).

ZIP and npx skills (including a project-local copy) remain on code-trace-tree-skill if you need them.

How to use the skill

Once the skill is installed, use it in your agent chat:

Help me generate some simple trace points related to the current topic.

Add simple trace points along the call path of method `test`.

Storage

Trace data is stored in a shared global folder:

  • Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\code-trace-tree
  • macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/code-trace-tree
  • Linux: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/code-trace-tree or ~/.config/code-trace-tree
