idea-plugin.name: etcd
idea-plugin.description:
Browse and edit an etcd v3 key space from inside the IDE.
  • Browse the key space as a lazily-loaded prefix tree.
  • Read and edit values, with JSON highlighting and Raw / Base64 / Hex views for binary data.
  • Create and delete keys, delete a whole prefix, and export a prefix to JSON.
  • Live updates: keys added or removed by another client appear automatically.
  • Saves are guarded by a compare-and-set on the key's revision, so concurrent edits are never silently overwritten.
Connects over etcd's v3 gRPC-gateway (HTTP/JSON), supporting anonymous access, username/password authentication, TLS with a custom CA, and client certificates (mTLS). The plugin bundles no third-party libraries.

idea-plugin.name: Figma Connect
idea-plugin.description:
Bring your Figma designs into your IDE with the Figma Connect plugin. Select a frame, component, or layer and let AI generate the code — no tab-switching, no spec hunting.

Features

  • See your live Figma selection — the file, frame, or layer currently selected in Figma appears in the Figma Connect tool window in real time.
  • Send designs to AI Assistant in one click — attach any selection to a chat with Add to Context and ask AI Assistant to generate the matching code.
  • Auto-include the current selection — have your active Figma design attached to every new AI chat automatically, so the context is always there as you iterate.
  • Pick up where you left off — recently used files stay one click away with thumbnails for quick recognition.
  • Paste a Figma link in chat — drop a Figma URL into AI Assistant and the design is recognized and added to your recent files.

Getting Started

You will need Figma DevMode and the Figma Desktop App to use this plugin.

Open the Figma Connect tool window and follow the on-screen instructions to pair your IDE with Figma. AI Assistant subscription is required.

Learn more in the documentation.

idea-plugin.name: Corgea
idea-plugin.description:
Corgea finds insecure code in your project and applies AI-generated fixes without leaving the IDE.

Features

  • Security scanning — scan the whole project, or only your uncommitted changes.
  • Code vulnerabilities — browse findings grouped by file, with severity and line numbers.
  • Dependency (SCA) vulnerabilities — browse findings grouped by package, with CVE identifiers and fix versions.
  • Editor highlighting — vulnerable lines are underlined and marked with a gutter icon.
  • Finding details — read the explanation for a finding and preview the suggested fix as a diff.
  • One-click fixes — apply an auto-generated patch from the gutter, the context menu, or Alt+Enter.
  • Live scan progress — watch each scan step and its CLI output while results stream into the tool window.

Requirements

  • A Corgea account. Sign in with OAuth or an API key from the Corgea dashboard.
  • No Python or CLI install. The plugin ships its own Python runtime and installs its own copy of the Corgea CLI on the first scan.
  • Self-hosted and enterprise Corgea servers are supported by pointing the plugin at your own server URL.

How your code is handled

Scanning sends the source files being scanned to the Corgea service for analysis, and the resulting findings and fixes are downloaded back into the IDE. Your credentials are stored in the IDE's password safe. The plugin does not collect analytics or telemetry.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.0

  • Scanning no longer requires Python or the Corgea CLI to be installed. The plugin ships its own Python runtime and installs its own copy of the CLI on the first scan.
  • Fix CLI discovery on Windows, which previously only ever looked for a Unix which.
  • Add settings for a custom CLI path and an internal package index, for networks that cannot reach PyPI.
  • Stop reporting a finished scan as failed when one of its scanners could not run. It now shows as "Scan completed with errors", listing the affected scanners and linking to the scan in Corgea.

1.0.1

  • Fix Login with API Key opening the Marketplace instead of Corgea settings.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
  • Full and uncommitted-changes security scans driven by the Corgea CLI.
  • Code and dependency findings in a dedicated tool window.
  • In-editor highlighting, gutter icons, and one-click fixes.
  • OAuth and API key sign-in, including self-hosted servers.

idea-plugin.name: Amazing Claude Code GUI
idea-plugin.description:
Amazing Claude Code GUI

Claude Code as a chat panel in your JetBrains IDE. Cards instead of terminal scrollback,
files you point at instead of paths you type, and your code right next to it.

It drives the Claude Code CLI already on your machine, so your account, models, slash commands,
permission rules, MCP servers and skills all come with it. No proxy, no account of ours.

🌐 English | 简体中文 | Русский | Українська | Español | Português (Brasil) | Deutsch | Français | 日本語 | 한국어

Why this one

  • A round of work, written once and run for you. Scenarios: a few cards, each a Claude
    session of its own - implement, review, fix, run the tests - in stages that can go round more
    than once, with a main thread walking them and judging what each one found. Run one by button,
    three at once against three tickets, or on a clock at nine every weekday with its questions
    answered in advance. Describe the round in a sentence and Claude reads the project and writes
    the form.
  • The whole panel from your phone, not just a "yes" button. Answer a permission or a plan,
    open a project that is closed, read yesterday's chat, fork, change the model and the effort,
    switch the account, sign in to a connector, dictate, watch a scenario run and unblock it. Off by
    default, paired by QR code, end-to-end encrypted through a relay that cannot read a word,
    revoked in one tap.
  • Several Claude accounts, switched in one click. Work and personal on one machine without
    signing out of either. Every row shows what is left of that account's five-hour window and its
    week, and Select moves every open chat onto it.
  • Search across every conversation of the project. Prefixes, typos, word stems, phrases in
    quotes; this chat or all of them, with a jump straight to the message in its chat. When words
    are not enough, describe what you are looking for and Claude reads the conversations for you.
  • Everything it does is on screen. Every tool call with its duration, every edit as an open
    diff, subagents and whole fleets of workflow agents with each agent's own transcript a click
    away, the task list ticking off, and what the turn cost. An overloaded or rate-limited API is a
    card with the reason and the countdown, not silence.
  • Nothing answers for you, and nothing is lost. A permission, a plan or a question waits as
    long as it takes - no timeout, no auto-continue. Conversations keep going with the panel
    collapsed or the project switched, and messages written during a turn wait in a queue the IDE
    keeps.
  • Android Studio included, along with every JetBrains IDE from 2026.1 on.

Getting started

  1. Have Claude Code installed and working in a terminal - the panel drives that CLI.
  2. Open the panel from the tool window button on the side bar. If you are not signed in, one
    button does it in the IDE's own terminal.
  3. Write your message. Drag files or folders into the field, type @ for a project file, / for
    a command, ! to run something in your shell.
  4. Right-click a selection in the editor and choose "Send to Amazing Claude Code GUI" to send a
    precise file-and-line reference instead of pasted text.
  5. Model, effort and permission mode are the three buttons under the field, and each belongs to
    the tab you are looking at.

Also in the panel

  • Point at files, do not type them. Drag one in, type @ to pick it, paste a screenshot or
    a long log - each lands as a chip you cannot mistype.
  • Send code with its address. Select lines, "Send to Amazing Claude Code GUI", and the agent
    reads the real file around them instead of a snippet with no context.
  • Paths open files. A path anywhere in the conversation - the head of a card, an answer, an
    error, your own message - opens the file in the editor at the line it names; an edit opens on
    the edit itself.
  • Grab any part of an answer. Quote it into your next message, fork the conversation from
    that exact point, pin up to three messages above the chat, or take a sent message back into the
    field to fix and resend.
  • Model, effort and mode change mid-conversation, per tab, without restarting anything. What
    a new chat starts with is yours to set, and a model of your own server can be added by hand.
  • MCP servers, plugins and marketplaces on screens of their own: which server is up, which
    wants a sign-in, which fell over and why.
  • History of this project's past conversations, terminal ones included, opened from the end
    and paged back on demand.
  • A queue for messages written while a turn is running, reorderable by drag.
  • ! runs a command in your own shell, and the output travels with your next message,
    costing no turn and no permission prompt.
  • Improve prompt - the sparkle rewrites your draft in a run of its own, costing your
    conversation no context, and one button puts your words back.
  • Voice input with a Deepgram key of your own: hold a hotkey, even from the editor.
  • Sound alerts for the seven moments worth one, and only when you are not already looking.
  • Statistics of hours, habits and achievements, shareable as a picture.
  • Ten languages, following your IDE by default.
  • Your unsaved buffers are written before a turn, and files the agent changed are re-read at
    once.
  • A side panel, not an editor tab, on any edge of the window; numbers pick an option,
    Shift+Tab cycles the mode, Escape stops the turn.

Privacy and transparency

  • Everything runs on your machine. No proxy, no server of ours in the middle. Your Claude
    sign-in belongs to the CLI - the plugin never reads it or hunts for API keys on your disk.
  • No telemetry, no analytics, no account. With remote access off, the only thing that ever
    leaves is a feedback report you write and send yourself - and one button shows its exact text
    first.
  • Your permission rules stay yours. The CLI decides what to ask about, with your settings,
    rules and hooks. The plugin adds no hook of its own and never starts a session in a laxer mode
    than the one on screen.
  • Source available on GitHub under the Elastic License 2.0, and the
    privacy policy lists everything that can leave the
    machine.

Requirements

Claude Code installed and signed in, and any JetBrains IDE from 2026.1 on, Android Studio
included. Android Studio has no embedded browser of its own, so the IDE offers to install
JetBrains' browser plugin alongside this one.

Links

  • Source code
  • Report a bug or ask for a feature,
    or use the form in the panel
  • Privacy policy
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Fixed: a scenario run kept working on the account it was started on after you chose another account in the panel, and went on spending the account you had left until its limit ran out. A run now follows your choice the way open chats do: the work in progress is interrupted, the main thread and the card come up again on the chosen account over their own conversations, and the run carries on where it stood.
  • Fixed: when an account's usage limit refused a scenario run, the card was judged on the "You've hit your session limit" message, the main thread was refused too, and the run ended as "No verdict" while your other accounts had room. Now the run pauses at the refusal and goes on on another of your accounts that has room - the account you chose first, then the least used one. If no account has room, it waits and carries on by itself when the first limit resets. The timeline says what happened, and a waiting run says on its card whose limit it is waiting for and until when; Resume tries at once.
  • Fixed: an account the run moved to by itself that cannot take it - signed out, or without the model the run uses - no longer ends the run. It is set aside for an hour and the run goes on elsewhere.
  • Changed: the Claude accounts screen says that running scenarios move with the chosen account, along with open chats.
  • Note for phones: reload the page in your browser after this one - the phone keeps the previous client until you do.

idea-plugin.name: Claude Task Queue
idea-plugin.description:
Queue up Claude Code tasks and let them run in your IDE terminal while you work.
  • TODO / In progress / Done board — drag cards to reorder or to start them.
  • Tasks run in a real Claude Code terminal, so you can watch and step in at any time.
  • Pick which terminal a task runs in — a new tab, one the plugin opened, or a shell you opened yourself.
  • Completion is detected automatically and the next task starts on its own.
  • Tasks in different terminal tabs run in parallel; within one tab they run in order.
  • Reopen a recent conversation — pick from this project's recent Claude conversations, with the title Claude gave them and when you last used them, and it resumes in the terminal you choose.
  • See how full each conversation's context is, so you know when to compact or start a fresh one.
Requires the claude CLI on your PATH.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.6.9

  • New Quick Run shortcut — Cmd+Shift+; on macOS, Ctrl+Alt+R elsewhere. Type a task, pick which terminal runs it, done. It works from anywhere in the IDE, so you no longer have to open the tool window and drag a card onto a terminal's column just to run something in that tab. Pick "TODO" instead if you only want to jot it down. The terminal you used last is pre-selected. Also on the Tools menu.

0.6.7

  • Select text in the terminal, right-click, and Add to Task Queue puts it straight into the task box. Handy when Claude suggests what to do next — grab the line and queue it instead of retyping. On the classic terminal engine the menu item isn't available, but the shortcut still works.

0.6.6

  • Sending a task to a conversation that's still answering no longer collides with it. The queue waits for that turn to finish, then sends — before, the task could be marked done the moment the earlier answer ended, and the next one started too early.
  • Long prompts are submitted properly. A large paste ended up sitting in Claude's input box without running, because the Enter arrived as part of the pasted text.

0.6.5

  • New Recent conversations button on the toolbar. It lists this project's recent Claude conversations with the title Claude gave them, how full their context is, and when you last used them — pick one and it resumes in the terminal you choose. If it's already open in a tab, you're taken there instead.

0.6.4

  • Renamed to Claude Task Queue — the old name was too generic to find. Same plugin, nothing to reinstall.

0.6.3

  • Each terminal's column now shows how full that conversation's context is. Hover the column title for the exact figure — 598.6k/1m (60%) and the model it's measured against. The title turns amber past 60% and red past 80%, so you can see a conversation filling up before it compacts.
  • Fixed: opening the tool window could fail with an internal error.
  • Fixed: on setups where the project path goes through a symlink, the plugin looked for transcripts in the wrong place — so answers and context never showed up.

0.6.2

  • Fixed the declared minimum IDE version — 2025.3, which is where the reworked terminal this plugin drives first appears.

0.6.1

  • Requires 2025.3 or newer now. The reworked terminal — the default engine since 2026.1 — only exists from 2025.3, and supporting it is what makes tab reuse work on a default setup.
  • Right-click a selection in the editor and "Add to Task Queue" now fills the task input with the file, line range and code, ready for you to type what to do — instead of a one-line dialog you couldn't edit.
  • Renaming a terminal tab renames its column too. Titles that Claude Code sets itself are ignored, so every tab doesn't end up with the same name.
  • The running task is marked with a border that gently pulses, and a card that just moved is outlined instead of tinted — easier to read the text on it.
  • Cards show more of the prompt before cutting it off, with the full text on hover.
  • Finished tasks are listed newest first.
  • Fixed: dragging a task onto a terminal's column failed with "That terminal tab is gone" unless you had run something in that tab first.

0.6.0

  • Tasks in different terminal tabs now run at the same time. Within a tab they still run one after another, so a conversation keeps its order — but two tabs no longer wait for each other.
  • IN PROGRESS is split into one column per terminal tab, each in its own colour, so you can see what every conversation is working on at a glance. Drag a waiting card onto another tab's column to move it there — it starts right away if that tab is free.
  • Columns follow your open terminals, so they stay put instead of appearing and disappearing as tasks come and go.

0.5.0

  • Works with the new Reworked terminal — the default engine on 2026.1. Until now the plugin could only see Classic terminal tabs, so on a default 2026.1 setup your open tabs were ignored and a new one was opened every time. Picking an existing tab, detecting whether claude is already running in it, and sending prompts all work on both engines now.
  • New tabs on the Reworked engine start without being brought to the front, so the queue no longer has to show the terminal to get a task going.

0.4.5

  • If your open terminal tabs can't be used, the plugin now says so instead of quietly opening a new tab. This happens with the Reworked terminal engine (the default on 2026.1) — switch to Classic in Settings → Tools → Terminal to reuse your own tabs.

0.4.4

  • Starting a task no longer steals your keyboard focus, so the queue moving on to the next task won't drag you away from whatever you were doing. Opening a brand-new tab still shows the terminal — it has to be visible for the session to start — but your focus stays put. Double-click a card when you do want to jump to its terminal.

0.4.3

  • Each project now has its own queue, so a task running in one project no longer blocks another — start a run in project A and keep working in project B. Your board only shows that project's cards. Queues from earlier versions are not carried over.
  • Interrupted a task in the terminal? A ↻ button on the card re-sends it to the same conversation, so it picks up where you cut it off. Interrupting no longer leaves the card stuck until the timeout.
  • Waiting tasks get ↻ too — deleting the running task used to strand them in IN PROGRESS with no way to start them.
  • The input box is cleared before a task is re-sent, so leftover typing can't run together with the prompt.
  • Removed the toolbar log button: the log was wiped whenever a task started, so it never held the run you wanted to look at.

0.4.1

  • Running every TODO in a new conversation now uses a single terminal tab and runs them one after another, so they share context instead of opening a tab each.
  • Long prompts wrap onto more lines on a card — the run/edit/delete buttons no longer get pushed out of view.

0.4.0

  • Stop now leaves the running task alone and moves waiting tasks back to TODO, instead of marking them done while claude keeps working.
  • Type multi-line tasks — Enter adds, Shift+Enter breaks the line, and the Up arrow in an empty field opens your recent prompts.
  • Card buttons are ordered run, edit, delete, with bigger click targets.
  • Roomier board: a separator under each column header and more vertical padding.

0.3.1

  • Fixed: a terminal tab where you started claude yourself was rejected as "busy running something else".

0.3.0

  • Finished cards show claude's answer, so you don't have to open the terminal to see what happened. Notifications carry it too.
  • Running cards show elapsed time, updated every second.
  • Keyboard shortcuts on the board: Delete to remove, Cmd+Enter to run, F2 to edit.
  • Notifications go to the OS notification center instead of an IDE popup.

0.2.0

  • Run a task in any terminal tab — a new one, one the plugin opened, or a shell you opened yourself. If claude isn't running there yet, the plugin starts it.
  • Task completion is detected automatically and the next task starts on its own.
  • Drag cards to reorder them or to start them. Inline actions on each card (edit, run, delete) and a running-task card takes you to its terminal.
  • Notifications when a task finishes and when the queue drains.

idea-plugin.name: Claude Brains
idea-plugin.description:
Develop in the IDE. Configure in the Terminal. Claude Code for JetBrains IDEs (unofficial). Runs Anthropic's official claude CLI inside PhpStorm and other IntelliJ IDEs, wired to the editor through the same IDE-MCP bridge the VS Code extension uses. Opens in a right-side tool window. Requires the claude CLI (2.1.200+) installed and logged in — does not bundle or redistribute Anthropic code. Not affiliated with Anthropic or JetBrains.

Philosophy

The plugin complements the terminal — it does not replace it. What you reach for constantly while writing code lives in the panel, one keystroke from the file you are looking at: asking, editing, reviewing diffs, approving commands, switching model, mode or effort, resuming past conversations. Everything occasional stays in the CLI, where it already works and is already documented — logging in, MCP servers, hooks, permission rules, agents, and the rest of ~/.claude. Nothing is rebuilt in the IDE just to have it there.

By design

  • Login happens in the terminal — sign in once by running claude; the plugin picks up that session. There is no in-IDE login flow.
  • Configuration lives in the CLI — settings, MCP servers, hooks and permission rules are managed the way the CLI already documents. The plugin has no settings page of its own; the claude binary is resolved from PATH (or the -Dclaude.executable JVM option).
  • Only verified slash commands are enabled — sixteen built-ins (/compact, /btw, /context, /code-review, /init and more), plus your project and user commands, skills and MCP prompts, auto-enabled with a source badge. A headless stream has no interactive terminal, so commands that need one are hidden rather than half-working. Model, mode, effort and new conversation have dedicated panel controls instead.

Not there yet

  • Dark UI only — the panel does not follow light IDE themes.
  • One conversation at a time — full history with resume and replay exists, tabs don't.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.16.0
  • The editor's selection rides every prompt: a live pill in the composer follows what you highlight (or the cursor line), its × leaves it out of one message, and the sent message shows the same pill — click it to reopen those lines
  • Include open file: a second switch in the paperclip menu attaches the open file's content when nothing is highlighted (unsaved edits included, 50,000-character cap); a highlight always wins, as in VS Code
  • Both live in the paperclip menu as switch rows and persist across restarts; Include selection is on by default, Include open file off
  • Resuming a conversation after the IDE closed over a running background command no longer draws a stray "Pondered for 1s" line
  • The Copy response control appears at the end of a reply's first line when the reply is hovered, with the text wrapping around it — it used to sit over the text and could cover the end of a long first line
0.15.0
  • Message timestamps: a small time above each prompt and above the first reply text, date lines between turns when the day changes, relabelled at midnight
  • Question cards show an option's preview in a monospace box, and an answered question stays on its card with a summary of the picks
  • Background tasks: every row of the Background tasks popup opens a live output pane for that command, and a running command's line offers "Run in background" — the terminal's Ctrl+B
  • Export conversation (header button): copy the whole conversation as plain text or save it to a file, the same text the CLI's /export writes
  • Copy response: a hover control on each reply block copies its markdown
  • In Auto mode, the CLI's "built-in classifier" notice is shown as a Continue / Stop card instead of being left unanswered
  • The claude executable is resolved on the shell PATH, the same place the CLI runs from — the panel could silently run the older CLI bundled with the VS Code extension
  • The model chip's Default label follows the model the CLI actually serves
  • Copy buttons write through the IDE clipboard — they used to fail silently when the panel did not hold focus
  • The 1M-context switch is gone: the CLI serves the 1M window with or without it, and the switch only miscounted the context gauge; the gauge now follows the window the CLI reports for any model
  • The model menu fits the panel — the list scrolls instead of running under the header; bold wrapping an italic renders; @-mentions of paths with spaces attach; thinking text no longer ends with blank lines
0.14.0
  • A Bash command that edits files shows a diff card per changed file under its IN/OUT box — the same card an accepted edit gets — live and on resume. The CLI sends the diff in Auto and Bypass modes by default; in Manual, Accept-edits and Plan modes add "bashEditDiffEnabled": true to ~/.claude/settings.json (CLI 2.1.269 or newer)
  • "Mention in Claude Brains" is also the first entry of an editor tab's right-click menu, beside the editor and Project-view menus
  • Plan comments: selecting another passage while a comment is still being typed adds that comment (or discards it if empty) and offers the Comment pill for the new selection — it used to do nothing until Enter was pressed; the field's placeholder now says "Enter adds, Esc cancels"
  • The "Tell Claude what to do instead" field on Bash and Write permission cards sits on its own line above the buttons, so Accept, Always allow and Reject keep one height; the placeholder adds "applies to Reject", since a note before Accept is not sent

Earlier versions: github.com/amitsidhpura/claude-brains/releases

idea-plugin.name: MCP Selection Bridge
idea-plugin.description:
Share your JetBrains editor selection with terminal AI CLIs (Codex, Kimi Code) through a local MCP server.

解决什么问题

在终端里用 Codex CLI 或 Kimi Code CLI 时，AI 看不到你在 IDE 里框选的那段代码。 以往只能复制粘贴，或者手工报出文件名和行号。装上这个插件后，直接对它说 「看我在 IDE 里选中的代码」，它自己就能读到。

工作原理

插件在 IDE 内启动一个 MCP（Model Context Protocol）服务，仅监听 127.0.0.1:63450，对外暴露一个工具 get_idea_selection， 返回当前选中内容的文件路径、行号范围与文本。多个项目窗口同时打开时，聚焦窗口优先。

安装与注册

装好插件并重启 IDE，打开 Settings | Tools | MCP Selection Bridge， 点 Register in Codex 或 Register in Kimi Code 按钮，注册一次即长期生效。

也可以手动注册。Codex：

codex mcp add idea-selection --url http://127.0.0.1:63450/mcp

Kimi Code：在会话里执行 /mcp-config 交互添加， 或写入 ~/.kimi-code/mcp.json：

{ "mcpServers": { "idea-selection": { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:63450/mcp" } } }

兼容性

支持全系 JetBrains IDE（IntelliJ IDEA、PyCharm、WebStorm、GoLand 等）， 只使用平台公共 API。除 Codex 与 Kimi Code 外，任何支持 streamable HTTP 的 MCP 客户端都可接入。已用 Codex CLI 0.146 与 Kimi Code CLI 0.31 双端实测验证。

安全说明

服务只绑定回环地址，外部网络不可达。但需要知悉：IDE 运行期间， 本机任意进程都可以通过该端口读取你当前的选区内容。可在 Settings | Tools | MCP Selection Bridge 中随时关闭插件或修改端口。

In English

This plugin runs a local MCP (streamable HTTP) server inside your JetBrains IDE on 127.0.0.1:63450, exposing a get_idea_selection tool that returns the file path, line range and text of your current editor selection. Register it once from Settings | Tools | MCP Selection Bridge, then ask your CLI agent to "look at the code I selected in the IDE". The server binds to loopback only, but any local process can read the selection while the IDE is running.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.1 — 全新插件图标；插件介绍改为以中文为主，并补充了原理与安全说明。 New plugin icon; description rewritten with Chinese as the primary language.
1.1.0 — 新增 Kimi Code CLI 支持（协议未改动，codex 与 kimi 双端实测验证）； 设置页新增 Register in Codex / Register in Kimi Code 一键注册按钮； 更名为 MCP Selection Bridge（适用于任何 streamable-HTTP MCP 客户端）。 Added Kimi Code CLI support, one-click registration buttons, and renamed the plugin.
1.0.0 — 首个版本：内置 streamable HTTP MCP 服务、get_idea_selection 工具、可配置端口与开关。Initial release.

idea-plugin.name: CodePal Assistant
idea-plugin.description:
This is an AI programming assistant plugin for IntelliJ IDEA and Android Studio. It integrates AI chat, file editing, project context awareness, MCP tools, todo management and inline ghost-text completion, supporting both OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic APIs.

这是一款适用于 IntelliJ IDEA 和 Android Studio 的 AI 编程助手插件。 集成 AI 聊天、文件编辑、项目上下文感知、MCP 工具、待办管理与内联幽灵文本补全，同时支持 OpenAI-API与Anthropic-API。
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2.2.29

idea-plugin.name: Transvoy
idea-plugin.description:
Transvoy — See, and understand.

Break language barriers — understand any SDK or dependency instantly.

Transvoy translates code comments right inside your IDE — into the language you read best. Select a comment or an entire file, and AI translates it in place. No context switching, no copy-paste. Just see, and understand.

Features

  • Context-aware translation — parses your code precisely: knows what is a comment and what is code, what kind of comment it is (line, block, class doc), and which piece of code each comment describes; translations are generated with the enclosing method signature and class structure in mind, so results fit the code's semantics
  • Two-way locating — every translation is anchored to its source; click a translation card or the locate button and the editor jumps straight to the original comment, selected and highlighted
  • Multi-model support — DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, Doubao, Claude, OpenAI, and Gemini work out of the box, plus any OpenAI-compatible custom provider
  • Target language & custom prompts — translate into the language you read best, and tune the translation style with custom prompts

Results stream live into a popup anchored near your selection or below the floating toolbar, and the Transvoy tool window keeps translation tasks, history, and cache in one right-hand panel — SQLite-backed, so cache hits return instantly.

Getting Started

  1. Install the plugin and restart your IDE
  2. Open Settings → Tools → Transvoy (can't find it? type "Transvoy" in the Settings search box; or use the Settings tab in the Transvoy panel)
  3. Choose a provider (e.g. DeepSeek), paste your API key, click Test Connection
  4. Select a comment in the editor and translate:
    • Right-click → Transvoy → Translate Selection (the Transvoy submenu at the bottom of the editor context menu), or
    • Click the Transvoy icon on the floating toolbar next to the selection, or
    • Right-click → Transvoy → Translate Current File to batch-translate all comments (or press Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F)

Compatibility

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2024.1+ (Community / Ultimate) — built natively on the JetBrains Platform

About

  • Version: 1.0.0
  • Developer: 1Step Studio (hi@1step.studio)
  • Price: Free
  • Language: UI in English / 简体中文

中文介绍

Transvoy — 看见，即得译。

跨越语言障碍，即刻理解任意 SDK 与依赖。

Transvoy 在 IDE 内直接翻译代码注释——译成你最熟悉的语言。选中一段注释或整个文件，AI 就地翻译。无需切换窗口，无需复制粘贴。看见，即得译。

核心功能

  • 上下文感知翻译 — 精准解析代码：理解哪里是注释、哪里是代码，注释是什么类型（行注释 / 块注释 / 类文档），以及每条注释在描述哪段代码；结合方法签名与类结构生成译文，贴合代码语义
  • 双向定位 — 每条译文都锚定源码；点击翻译卡片或"定位"按钮，编辑器立即跳回原注释位置，选中并高亮
  • 多模型支持 — 内置支持 DeepSeek、通义千问、智谱 GLM、Kimi、MiniMax、豆包、Claude、OpenAI、Gemini 9 种模型，另支持兼容 OpenAI 接口的模型服务
  • 目标语言与自定义 Prompt — 支持多种目标语言，可用自定义 Prompt 调整翻译风格

翻译结果以流式弹窗显示在选区附近或浮动工具栏下方；右侧 Transvoy 面板统一管理翻译任务、历史与缓存——SQLite 本地存储，命中缓存秒出结果。

快速开始

  1. 安装插件并重启 IDE
  2. 打开 Settings → Tools → Transvoy（找不到可在设置搜索框输入 Transvoy；或 Transvoy 面板的"设置"标签页）
  3. 选择模型提供商（如 DeepSeek），填入 API Key，点击"测试连接"
  4. 在编辑器选中注释并翻译：
    • 右键 → Transvoy → 翻译选中内容（编辑器右键菜单末尾的 Transvoy 子菜单），或
    • 点击选区旁浮动工具栏上的 Transvoy 图标，或
    • 右键 → Transvoy → 翻译当前文件 批量翻译全部注释（或按 Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F）

兼容性

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2024.1 及以上（Community / Ultimate）——基于 JetBrains Platform 原生构建

关于

  • 版本： 1.0.0
  • 开发者： 1Step Studio（hi@1step.studio）
  • 价格： 免费
  • 界面语言： 简体中文 / English

idea-plugin.name: Cursor Usage
idea-plugin.description:
Track Cursor account usage inside your JetBrains IDE.

Cursor Usage brings your current billing-period usage, on-demand spending, subscription details, and next reset time into a dedicated tool window and status-bar indicator.

Features

  • Usage overview: Check included usage and on-demand spending in one place.
  • Status-bar access: See usage at a glance and click the indicator for subscription and usage details.
  • Automatic and manual refresh: Keep the information up to date or refresh when needed.
  • Usage alerts: Receive notifications when usage is nearly exhausted or exceeded.
  • Existing Cursor sign-in: Reuse the local sign-in from Cursor Desktop or Cursor Agent.
  • English and Simplified Chinese: Use the interface in either language.

Requirements

Cursor Desktop or Cursor Agent must be installed and signed in. Available usage information depends on your Cursor subscription and the data returned by Cursor.

Privacy

Before accessing account data, the plugin asks for permission. If allowed, it reads local Cursor authentication data and requests usage information directly from cursor.com and api2.cursor.sh. Credentials, usage information, and analytics are not sent to the plugin developer. Permission can be revoked at any time. An optional browser cookie is stored in the IDE PasswordSafe. See the Privacy Policy.

Documentation · Report an issue

Disclaimer: Cursor Usage is an independent, unofficial plugin. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Cursor or Anysphere.
idea-plugin.change-notes:

  • Expired or malformed access tokens are now skipped in the Cursor database, system credential store, and in-memory cache.

3.2.0

  • Kept the last successfully loaded usage values when a refresh request fails.
  • Preserved cached subscription and billing details when only part of a refresh succeeds.
  • Added three-second manual refresh notifications with clear success and detailed failure results.

3.1.0

  • Added Windows cursor-agent and ACP credential discovery under APPDATA.
  • Expired or malformed ACP access tokens now fall through to the next credential source.
  • Added cross-platform authentication path and credential fallback tests.

3.0.1

  • Stopped showing the data-access permission dialog automatically during IDE startup.
  • Permission is now requested only after an explicit action in the tool window, login action, or settings.
  • Fixed compatibility with unattended Marketplace IDE-run verification.

3.0.0

  • Initial JetBrains Marketplace release.
  • Added a tool window and status-bar indicator for Cursor usage.
  • Added automatic refresh and usage-threshold notifications.
  • Added subscription, account, and billing reset details.
  • Added English and Simplified Chinese interface text.
  • Added explicit permission controls for credential access and background refresh.
  • Stored optional browser cookies securely in the IDE PasswordSafe.
  • Removed credentials, account identifiers, response bodies, and usage values from diagnostics.

idea-plugin.name: Air
idea-plugin.description:
Air is a workspace for agentic development inside your JetBrains IDE.

Delegate coding tasks to Codex, Claude, Junie, OpenCode, and other supported agents, and keep several sessions moving at once. Air shows what each agent is doing, so you can switch between tasks and step in when needed.

CLI and ACP agents are both first-class. CLI agents run in a full terminal inside an editor tab. ACP agents use a native structured interface for progress, tool calls, permissions, and questions. The plugin itself is free; supported agents can use the accounts or subscriptions you already have.

This is a public preview version. We are releasing Air while we build it. Expect rough edges, changes to the UI and behavior, and updates roughly every week. Try it on real work and report what breaks or gets in the way.

Available today

  • Open Global Prompt from anywhere in the IDE and attach selections, files, symbols, test results, VCS changes, console output, or screenshots.
  • Choose an agent and set its model, reasoning effort, access level, and launch surface.
  • Run and track several sessions across projects and worktrees. See activity, unread updates, changed files, outgoing commits, and cost in one place.
  • Search, group, archive, and reopen sessions. Air restores them after an IDE restart.
  • Let supported agents call IDE tools over MCP and work with structured context instead of copied text alone.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
This release improves agent onboarding, session handling, worktree reliability, code review, performance, and platform compatibility.

Agent setup and authentication

  • Fixed Claude Code and Gemini CLI sign-in flows, with clearer retry and subscription guidance.
  • Improved provisioning and access-error handling, including revoked seats and disabled AI access.
  • Added an action to refresh AI access options and provisioned agents.
  • Clarified agent registry sources and license names.
  • Fixed Junie Lite onboarding, sign-in transitions, free-plan badges, and post-login navigation.

Sessions and chat

  • Reduced new-session startup time by avoiding unnecessary model-catalog probes and agent processes.
  • Improved recovery from failed sessions and fixed flashing, missing, duplicated, and stuck session tabs.
  • Cleaned up imported Codex prompts, attachments, Markdown escapes, and error messages.
  • Added shortcuts for Select Opened File and New Session, plus mouse resizing for the message input.
  • Improved session search with pin and unread actions and refined completed sub-agent panels.

Worktrees

  • Fixed tracked changes getting out of sync between main project windows and worktrees.
  • Improved Codex worktree forking and prevented failed forks from continuing in empty sessions.
  • Grouped worktrees correctly under their projects and removed stale entries for deleted worktrees.
  • Corrected change counts for binary files, symlinks, Git LFS pointers, and line-ending differences.
  • Fixed an IDE freeze when opening a temporary worktree from the Welcome screen.

Code review and context

  • Improved navigation between diffs and their related sessions.
  • Made code-comment discarding safer and aligned comment UI with the design.
  • Fixed the Code Notes shortcut conflict on macOS.
  • Preserved code-note attachments after sending and improved context handling for attached projects.
  • Clarified commit selection and fixed project-context selection in the dedicated input frame.

Performance and reliability

  • Removed a recursive workspace refresh that could drive high CPU usage for around 15 seconds.
  • Fixed repeated changed-file path resolution that kept PyCharm CPU busy.
  • Fixed plugin memory leaks, retained file contents, and thousands of leaked startup threads.
  • Cached login-shell environments, reused agent processes, and moved non-UI work off the UI thread.
  • Improved session loading, state recovery, and background-process reliability.

Platform compatibility

  • Fixed Air frontend resolution in CLion and Rider under Remote Development.
  • Fixed Claude Agent startup failures on Windows.
  • Improved session behavior across attached projects, multiple frames, and project-less IDE states.

idea-plugin.name: Worktree Lens
idea-plugin.description:
View and commit worktree changes — all in one window.

Worktree Lens syncs linked Git worktrees into IDEA's directory mappings, so all worktree changes appear in one Commit window. No extra windows needed.

idea-plugin.name: MarkDownAny
idea-plugin.description:
MarkDownAny converts PDFs, Office documents, images, audio, HTML, EPUB, and more to Markdown directly inside the IDE, powered by Microsoft's open-source MarkItDown.

No local Python setup required: conversions run through an on-demand, sandboxed environment managed by uv the first time they're needed.

  • Convert a single file from the Project view or the active editor
  • Batch-convert a whole directory tree into a Markdown output folder
  • Preview converted Markdown in a dedicated tool window before writing it to disk
  • Configure the backend interpreter and optional extras (OCR, audio transcription, LLM image captions)
idea-plugin.change-notes:

  • Markdown preview tool window for reviewing conversion output before saving

idea-plugin.description: Generate configurable Git commit messages from selected changes with an OpenAI-compatible LLM.

idea-plugin.name: SYNVOX
idea-plugin.description:
SYNVOX (formerly AI Free) brings AI chat, coding agents and project memory into your development workflow.

Connect supported AI providers, discuss your code and give an agent a concrete task in the current project. The agent can inspect files, propose or apply changes and run permitted project commands. Review generated changes and test results before accepting them.

Project chat history and memory are stored locally. Requests and relevant project context are sent to the selected AI provider; SYNVOX is not a fully offline AI model. Provider accounts, availability and usage limits apply separately.

SYNVOX is an alpha product under active development. Features, supported providers and the interface may change. The transition from AI Free to SYNVOX is in preparation; the announced SYNVOX plan is RUB 99 for 30 days with a 3-day trial. Paid access is not yet launched. Current release details, availability and terms are published on the official website.

Website: https://synvox.pro/
Terms and privacy: https://synvox.pro/documents/
Support: stas.sor@gmail.com
idea-plugin.change-notes: SYNVOX 0.5.5 adds saved agents and task controls, shared chat/coding context, resumable Harness tasks and up to ten accounts per AI. Coder chooses conversation or project tools. Folder selection and Qwen challenge diagnostics are improved. Updates preserve saved chats and the installation key.

idea-plugin.name: Qoder CLI Launcher
idea-plugin.description:
Qoder CLI Launcher - put Qoder CLI (qodercli) one click away in your IDE: 在 IDE 里直接唤起 qodercli，把你正看的代码、IDE 报出的问题、未提交的改动直接交给它，不复制、不切窗口。

功能
  • 一键启动：主工具栏一颗 Qoder CLI 分体按钮 —— 点主体新建会话，右侧 ▾ 展开 切换会话；Tools 菜单下一个 Qoder CLI Launcher 子菜单收纳 新建会话 / 切换会话 / 审查未提交的改动。
  • 切换会话：状态栏常驻显示当前会话标题（Qoder CLI: 标题，拿不到标题时退回短 ID），点一下即列出 qodercli 自己记录的会话（标题、时间、UUID），挑一个接着聊或在同一入口新建；已开着的会话会切到那个窗口（iTerm2 / Terminal.app 自动置前，其余终端会提示你切过去）。
  • Qoder CLI：右键文件或选中代码，选解释代码、审查代码、生成单元测试、重构代码、补充文档注释、优化性能或“自定义提问…”，内容自动作为附件带入，任务在当前会话里接着问。
  • 修复问题：把当前文件或选区里 IDE 报出的问题清单直接交给 CLI 修复。
  • 诊断错误输出：在运行 / 调试控制台右键，把选中的输出交给 CLI 定位根因。
  • Review 未提交的改动：Tools | Qoder CLI Launcher 子菜单或 Local Changes 面板一键发起，diff 由 CLI 自己执行 git diff 获取。
  • 终端自己选：Settings | Tools | Qoder CLI Launcher 可指定内置终端（默认）、iTerm2、Ghostty、系统默认终端或自定义命令。
会话启动成功后按项目保存唯一 ID 与工作目录，标签页关闭、IDE 重启或更换终端后都能精确回到同一个会话；恢复前会先确认它还能用，已失效的空会话自动换新、任务不落空。内置终端、iTerm2、Terminal.app 回到原标签页接着问，其余终端新开窗口但上下文精确接续。

前提：已安装 Qoder CLI 1.1.49 或更高版本 且能在 PATH 中直接调用；IDE 为 2024.2（build 242）及以上、已启用自带 Terminal 插件。支持 macOS / Linux / Windows；插件是独立辅助工具，只负责启动你单独安装的 CLI。

Qoder CLI Launcher puts the Qoder CLI (qodercli) one click away and hands it what you are looking at — the current file, the problems the IDE found, your uncommitted changes — with no copying and no window switching.

Features
  • One-click launch: a Qoder CLI split button on the main toolbar — its body starts a new conversation, the caret opens 切换会话; the Tools menu gathers 新建会话 / 切换会话 / 审查未提交的改动 under a Qoder CLI Launcher submenu.
  • Open a past session: the status bar keeps the current session's title in sight (Qoder CLI: <title>, its short id until a title is known); click it to list the sessions qodercli itself remembers (title, time, UUID) so one can be picked up — or a new one started from the same place; a session that is already running sends you to its window (iTerm2 / Terminal.app bring it to the front; other terminals point you there).
  • Qoder CLI: right-click a file or selection for 解释代码 (explain), 审查代码 (review), 生成单元测试 (write tests), 重构代码 (refactor), 补充文档注释 (add docs), 优化性能 (optimize) or 自定义提问… (a prompt of your own), with the file or snippet attached as context; the task continues in the current session.
  • Fix the problems: the IDE's errors and warnings for the current file or selection go straight to the CLI.
  • Diagnose error output: right-click in a Run / Debug console to send the selected output for diagnosis.
  • Review uncommitted changes: from Tools | Qoder CLI Launcher or the Local Changes view; the CLI runs git diff itself.
  • Choose your terminal: Settings | Tools | Qoder CLI Launcher picks the built-in terminal (default), iTerm2, Ghostty, the system terminal or a custom command.
The session UUID and working directory are saved per project after a verified startup, so the same conversation comes back after a tab closes, the IDE restarts or the terminal choice changes; a session that can no longer be resumed is replaced before the task is launched. The built-in terminal, iTerm2 and Terminal.app continue in the original tab; the others open a new window on the same session.

Prerequisites: Qoder CLI 1.1.49 or newer on your PATH (not bundled); an IntelliJ-based IDE 2024.2 (build 242) or newer with the bundled Terminal plugin. macOS / Linux / Windows.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.4.0
  • The main toolbar now has one session button: a split button whose body starts a new conversation and whose caret switches to a session the CLI already knows. The status bar shows the current session's title (Qoder CLI: <title>, its short id until a title is known) and opens the same list when clicked. The session entries have left the right-click submenu, which is now tasks only; the Tools menu gathers 新建会话, 切换会话 and 审查未提交的改动 under a Qoder CLI Launcher submenu.
  • Exact session continuation: every new conversation receives a UUID through --session-id. After startup is verified, the plugin saves the UUID and initial working directory per project and relaunches there with --resume <UUID>.
  • Unusable sessions are caught before the launch: a session the CLI created but never received a message in has no transcript and cannot be resumed — asking for it anyway used to land in an empty session picker with the task unsent. The plugin now checks the CLI's own session store (and, when that cannot vouch for it, --list-sessions) and starts a fresh session, with the task, instead. The compatibility floor for the CLI is 1.1.49.
  • The launch command no longer clutters the terminal: the generated script erases the shell's echo of /bin/sh '…/qoder-cli-….sh' before the CLI starts, so the tab shows the CLI alone.
  • Past sessions are one click away: a chooser lists what qodercli --list-sessions reports for this directory — the CLI's own list, so conversations started outside the IDE are in it too — and opens the picked one with --resume.
  • The 继续当前会话 toggle is gone: the 「Qoder CLI」 tasks always continue in the project's current conversation. For a fresh session, use the Qoder CLI toolbar button or ＋ 新建会话 in the session list.
  • Menu wording aligned with IDE terms: 打开历史会话… is now 切换会话, 启动 Qoder CLI is now 新建会话, and the task entries are 解释代码 / 审查代码 / 生成单元测试 / 重构代码 / 补充文档注释 / 优化性能 / 修复问题 / 自定义提问…; the console entry became 诊断错误输出（Qoder CLI）, and 让 Qoder CLI review 未提交的改动 became 审查未提交的改动（Qoder CLI）.
  • One session directory per project: the right-click 「Qoder CLI」 tasks now start in the project root too, like the toolbar and Tools entries, instead of the open file's own directory — so a project keeps a single session history and the switch-session list always finds it. The file itself still rides along as an attachment.
主工具栏只剩一颗会话按钮（分体式）：点主体新建会话，右侧 ▾ 展开「切换会话」。 状态栏常驻当前会话标题（Qoder CLI: 标题，拿不到标题时退回短 ID），点它同样打开会话列表。 会话条目已从右键子菜单移出（右键现在只有任务），Tools 菜单新增「Qoder CLI Launcher」子菜单，收纳「新建会话」「切换会话」「审查未提交的改动」。 会话启动成功后才会按项目保存唯一 ID 与首次工作目录，并通过 --resume 精确恢复。 恢复前先确认这个会话真的还能用：只有会话目录、没有对话记录的空会话会被换掉并用新会话执行本次任务， 不再出现“在当前工作树中未找到匹配…的会话”或落进空选择器的情况（先查 CLI 会话库，必要时再查 --list-sessions）。支持的 Qoder CLI 下限为 1.1.49。 启动脚本会在 CLI 运行前擦掉终端回显的 /bin/sh '…' 命令行，标签页里只剩 CLI 本身。 也可以从 Tools | Qoder CLI Launcher | 切换会话 的列表里挑一个 CLI 记录过的会话接着聊（已经开着的窗口：iTerm2 / Terminal.app 会自动置前，其余终端会提示你切过去）。 「Qoder CLI」不再有“继续当前会话”开关：任务一律接在当前会话上；要新开，点工具栏的 Qoder CLI 按钮，或用列表里的 ＋ 新建会话。 菜单文案改用 IDE 的说法（会话 / 问题 / 文档注释 / 单元测试 / 性能 / 改动）：打开历史会话…→切换会话， 启动 Qoder CLI→新建会话， 解释→解释代码、审查→审查代码、写测试→生成单元测试、重构→重构代码、补文档→补充文档注释、 优化→优化性能、修报错→修复问题、自定义…→自定义提问…， 控制台「用 Qoder CLI 解释报错」→「诊断错误输出（Qoder CLI）」。 右键「Qoder CLI」任务改为也在工程根目录启动（和工具栏、Tools 入口一致），不再落到当前文件所在子目录， 这样一个工程只有一份会话历史，「切换会话」列表也始终找得到；文件本身仍作为附件带入。

1.3.0
  • Rewritten listing: the Marketplace description is now bilingual with the Chinese section first, opens with a one-line value proposition followed by a clear feature list, and finally documents what was missing before — that Settings | Tools | Qoder CLI Launcher chooses where sessions open (built-in terminal, iTerm2, Ghostty, the system terminal, or a custom command). The README is reordered the same way.
  • Wider compatibility: the compatibility floor drops from 2025.1 (build 251) to 2024.2 (build 242). The only API that needed 251 — the terminal's "is a command still running" check — is now probed at runtime; on older IDEs, where it does not exist, follow-up questions are typed into the existing session directly, which is what a still-open interactive CLI expects.
重写了插件介绍。
兼容下限从 2025.1（build 251）放宽到 2024.2（build 242）：唯一需要 251 的终端 API （“命令是否还在运行”）改为运行时探测。

1.2.0
  • External terminals: Settings | Tools | Qoder CLI Launcher can now start sessions in iTerm2 (macOS), Ghostty (macOS and Linux), the system terminal (Terminal.app, Windows Terminal, or the first emulator found on Linux), or a custom command of your own. On macOS follow-up questions go back to the very tab the plugin opened in iTerm2 or Terminal.app, just like in the embedded terminal; in Ghostty and on other platforms they open a new window and resume with --continue. The embedded terminal remains the default; if an external one cannot be started, the session falls back to it and a notification explains why.
  • Launch in the project root: the toolbar button and Tools | 启动 Qoder CLI now start the session at the project root rather than in the directory of whichever file is open, so the CLI sees the whole project and keeps one session history instead of one per subdirectory. Right-click tasks are unaffected.
新增 Settings | Tools | Qoder CLI Launcher 设置项，可选择在 iTerm2（macOS）、Ghostty（macOS / Linux）、系统默认终端（Terminal.app / Windows Terminal / Linux 上探测到的第一个终端）或自定义命令中启动会话； 在 macOS 上，iTerm2 与 Terminal.app 的追问会回到本插件开的那个标签页，与内置终端一致，Ghostty 与其他平台则新开窗口并用 --continue 接上上下文。默认仍是 IDE 内置终端，外部终端启动失败时会提示原因并自动回落到内置终端。
工具栏按钮与 Tools | 启动 Qoder CLI 改为在工程根目录启动，不再跟着当前打开的文件走到子目录， CLI 因此能看到整个工程，会话历史也不会按子目录散成多份；右键菜单里的任务不受影响。

1.1.0
  • 问 Qoder CLI context-menu submenu (editor & Project view) with preset tasks — 解释, 审查, 写测试, 重构, 补文档, 优化 — plus 自定义… for a free-form question. The file or selected snippet is attached as context and the CLI opens in interactive mode. A 继续当前会话 toggle decides whether a task continues in the running session or starts a fresh one. Every entry is a normal action, so it can be found in Find Action and bound to a shortcut.
  • 修报错: the same submenu offers a "fix the problems" entry whenever the IDE reports errors or warnings in the current file (or selection), and sends that list to the CLI. It stays hidden when the file is clean.
  • 用 Qoder CLI 解释报错: right-click inside a Run or Debug console to send the selected output — or the tail of it — to the CLI for diagnosis. The text is attached as a file and the referenced source locations are named in the prompt.
  • 让 Qoder CLI review 未提交的改动: from the Tools menu or the Local Changes view, ask the CLI to review your working copy. It runs git diff itself, so the whole diff never has to be pasted anywhere.
新增 问 Qoder CLI 右键子菜单（编辑器与项目视图），内置任务：解释、审查、写测试、重构、补文档、 优化，另有“自定义…”，以及“继续当前会话”开关；文件或选中代码会作为上下文附件带入，CLI 以交互模式打开。 每个任务都是独立 action，可在 Find Action 搜索、在 Keymap 绑定快捷键。
当 IDE 在当前文件（或选区）里报出 error / warning 时，子菜单里会多出“修报错”，把问题清单一并交给 CLI； 文件没问题时该项自动隐藏。
在运行 / 调试控制台里右键可用“用 Qoder CLI 解释报错”，把选中的输出（或末尾若干行）作为附件交给 CLI 定位根因，提示语里会点名涉及的源码位置。
在 Tools 菜单或 Local Changes 面板可以让 CLI review 未提交的改动，具体内容由它自己执行 git diff 获取，无需把 diff 粘来粘去。

1.0.0
  • Initial release: one-click launch of the Qoder CLI in the IDE's embedded terminal, cross-platform (macOS / Linux / Windows).

idea-plugin.name: Claude Code & Junie Config Support
idea-plugin.description:
Language support for the files that configure Claude Code and Junie — not another way to run them.

Claude Code and Junie are configured through Markdown, YAML frontmatter and JSON. None of it is a programming language, so an IDE normally offers nothing: no completion, no validation, no navigation. A typo in a frontmatter key, a skill that never fires, an @import pointing at a renamed file — each fails silently at runtime.

This plugin makes that surface behave like code:
  • Validation — frontmatter against the published contract, unknown keys, name collisions between skills and commands, hook commands naming a missing script, @import chains deeper than Claude Code follows, and <example> blocks that stop a file loading at all
  • Trigger quality and cost — description length, the platform truncation cap, missing trigger phrasing, and token cost live in the gutter: the body, paid per invocation, and the routing text, paid in every session
  • Navigation — Ctrl+click through @imports, ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} scripts, skill names and hook paths
  • Hook dry run — run a hook against a sample event and see its exit code, output, and whether Claude Code would block
  • Generated files stay read-only — a copy that a sync overwrites refuses the edit and links to the real source
  • New skill, subagent or command — scaffolded from the contract, valid from the first keystroke
  • Rename and Find Usages — renaming a skill or agent updates every skills: entry that names it, as a single change
  • MCP tools — lets Claude Code ask the IDE what it knows and check its own edits: validation with quick fixes, token and session cost, trigger overlap and batch trigger pre-screens, unreachable skills, usages, @import trees and the library's dependency graph, effective settings and settings diffs, hooks and permissions, compact context packs and single doc sections, contradiction scans, dispatch plans, trigger eval replays and semantic diff digests, plus scaffold and rename tools that write only when confirmed
Covers CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, subagent and command definitions, settings.json, hooks and plugin manifests. Validation follows the published Claude Code contract and the stable Junie subagent/skill contract. A Windows IDE opening a project on a WSL share reads that WSL home's ~/.claude.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changed

  • No functional changes since 1.5.4; republished to correct its release notes.

idea-plugin.name: imux
idea-plugin.description:
imux turns your JetBrains IDE into a full AI coding cockpit — run Claude Code, Codex, and pi sessions in editor tabs, and give them the power of your IDE through IDEA MCP.

Why imux instead of running AI agents in a separate terminal?

AI coding agents are powerful, but on their own they work like a programmer with only a text editor and a terminal — they can read files, write files, and run commands, but they cannot use your IDE's refactoring, debugging, inspections, or run configurations. imux bridges this gap.

IDEA MCP: give AI agents access to IDE tools

When enabled (on by default), imux injects the JetBrains MCP server config into AI sessions it launches. With a reachable MCP server, your AI agents can (Pi also requires the bundled extension script):

  • Safe refactoring — rename symbols across the entire project by semantic identity, not risky text replace
  • Interactive debugging — set breakpoints, step through code, inspect variables, evaluate expressions — instead of print-debugging
  • IDE-level inspections — catch framework-specific issues (Spring, Django, ESLint, Android…) that compilers and linters miss
  • Run configurations — run tests and apps with the exact IDE settings (env vars, runtime args, working directory)
  • Database access — query databases using your IDE's saved connections and credentials
  • Code formatting — apply your project's configured Code Style, not an external formatter
  • Semantic navigation — trace call hierarchies, find symbol definitions, and understand type relationships across modules

Works with JetBrains IDEs that support Platform build 262+ (IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, Rider, CLion…). Available tools depend on the IDE product, installed plugins, and MCP server version. The injection is session-scoped — it does not modify your CLI's global config.

Session management in editor tabs

  • Run AI sessions in editor tabs alongside your code — split, rearrange, or move to another window
  • The AI Agents panel lists sessions for the current project, sorted by recent activity
  • Resume any session with one click — no need to look up session IDs
  • Notifications when an agent finishes a turn or needs input, with elapsed time and session title
  • Handoff between agents — continue work from Claude Code in Codex or Pi with context carried over

imux does not host your conversations. Session history stays in each CLI's own store. Uninstalling the plugin leaves all session history intact.

Requirements: JetBrains IDE 2026.2+ (Platform build 262+) and at least one supported CLI: claude, codex, or pi.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Claude Code、Codex 和 Pi 的数据目录现可跟随各自环境变量配置，插件的会话列表、目录监听、运行状态查询和标题写回会统一使用自定义目录。
  • Pi 会话目录支持从项目或全局 `settings.json` 的 `sessionDir` 读取，并兼容 `~`、`file://`、相对路径及配置变更后的自动刷新。
  • Windows 下可自动将 Pi 配置中的 Git Bash、WSL 和 Cygwin 盘符路径转换为原生路径。
  • 修复 Pi 切换会话目录后列表可能仍指向旧文件的问题，并支持按会话首行工作目录识别自定义平铺目录中的项目归属。
  • 修复 Claude 超长项目路径对应的 djb2 哈希目录无法匹配磁盘会话的问题。
  • Codex 会话列表不再显示 `codex exec` 产生的非交互会话。

idea-plugin.name: AI Commit Auto
idea-plugin.description: Generate editable, reviewable Git commit messages from the changes selected in the JetBrains IDE Commit tool window. Use your own OpenAI-compatible API, enterprise gateway, or local model service. Fast, Balanced, and Deep modes handle small and large diffs; tokens stay in JetBrains Password Safe, and the plugin never commits or pushes automatically.

idea-plugin.name: Prompt Templates
idea-plugin.description:
Create, manage and render reusable typed Markdown prompt templates inside JetBrains IDEs.

Templates remain ordinary Markdown files; typed variable metadata is stored separately.

  • Organise, search and edit a nested personal prompt library.
  • Invoke Quick Use by keyboard with ranked search, favourites and recents.
  • Resolve editor selection, current-file, project and clipboard context.
  • Attach explicitly selected file buffers and staged or unstaged Git diffs.
  • Preview exact rendered output before copying or inserting it.
  • Duplicate templates, capture selections and author typed variables with defaults.
  • Import, export, recover and diagnose templates, or open rendered Markdown in a scratch file.

The plugin makes no network requests, executes no prompts and sends no telemetry.

Compatible with standalone JetBrains IDEs based on IntelliJ Platform, with a minimum platform build of 262 (2026.2).

Automated Plugin Verifier coverage currently includes RustRover 2026.2 and WebStorm 2026.2.

Documentation · Support · Privacy

Copy-and-paste icons created by ranksol graphics - Flaticon
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Safer deletion, recoverable settings and steadier Quick Use.

  • Deleting a folder no longer follows Windows directory junctions, and a template folder that also holds other files or folders is not deleted as a template.
  • Template deletion checks the template's identity, so an out-of-date library view cannot delete a different template.
  • Validated the library path in Settings, accepted quoted paths and kept a bad stored path from breaking the plugin.
  • Kept an open Quick Use form when the library changes on disk.
  • Kept metadata fields from newer plugin versions and existing file permissions when saving, and left unreadable folder order files unchanged.
  • Changes wait at most 10 seconds for another IDE that holds the library lock; reading the library waits without clearing the view.
  • Opened library tree menus from anywhere on a row or with the context-menu key, and left Shift+F10 to Run.
  • Showed placeholder highlights as soon as the author view opens, warned about escaped placeholders that name a variable, and protected unsaved drafts when a project closes.
  • Rejected Windows device names as folder names and shortened directory names derived from long template names.
  • Verified compatibility weekly against the newest release and EAP builds of IntelliJ IDEA, RustRover and WebStorm.

idea-plugin.name: Claude Remarks
idea-plugin.description:
Requires Claude Code. This plugin is a front end for it. With no Claude Code session to hand remarks to, there is nothing here to use.

Attach short remarks to line ranges while you read code, then hand them all to a Claude Code session as one prompt: your note, the lines it points at, the code itself. Remarks never touch your source files. They live in IDE state only and stay out of version control.

If you have used plannotator or revdiff, the shape is familiar: read a change, leave notes on the lines that need them, hand the notes to an agent. This one does it from inside the IDE, and three things follow from that.

  • The review surface is your IDE, not a browser page or a terminal overlay. Go to definition, find usages, the real diff viewer, the rendered markdown preview, your own keymap and theme.
  • The review is continuous. There is no session to open and none to close. Mark things as you read, publish when you have something worth sending, and a listening session picks up each batch as it lands.
  • A question goes back to the session that already has the context, so there is nothing to re-explain. The answer comes back into the IDE, onto the line you asked about.

The whole thing in four steps:

  1. Install the bundled Claude Code skill, with one button in Settings | Tools | Claude Remarks.
  2. Tell a session listen for my remarks in this project.
  3. Read, annotate, ask questions. Press Publish Unread when you have a batch worth sending.
  4. Profit.

Remarks work in source editors over whole lines or a phrase inside one, in the rendered markdown preview, on the working-copy side of a diff, and with no file at all when the note is about the change as a whole.

This is early software. The path described above has been run by hand and works. Most of the rest has not been watched running, and it has had little use outside its own test suite. The two shell scripts the skill ships are macOS and Linux only, so on Windows the listening step needs WSL; everything else, including the clipboard route, works there. The repository says plainly what is proven and what is not.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.12.1
  • The Claude Code skill ships inside the plugin. Nothing to copy by hand.
  • Settings → Tools → Claude Remarks installs it, and says which version is on disk.
  • A notification on project open offers the same install when the skill is missing or out of date.
Full changelog

idea-plugin.name: Agent YOLO
idea-plugin.description:
Agent YOLO is a standalone AI Agents panel for IntelliJ IDEA. It lists your AI CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, CodeBuddy, Qoder, or your own) and launches any of them in a real, interactive terminal inside the IDE with a single click — no Terminal plugin required. Everything the agent prints becomes clickable: jump from its output straight to the code.

  • YOLO panel — A dedicated tool window (right side, y icon) that replicates the Terminal's AI Agents experience, built entirely on public IntelliJ APIs so it passes Marketplace verification. The agent list loads instantly from a cached install scan and refreshes in the background.
  • YOLO mode — A "Skip permissions" toggle in the panel. When on, the next agent launches with its skip-permissions flag (e.g. --dangerously-skip-permissions, --yolo, -y). Per-agent, fully configurable, and off by default.
  • Real in-panel terminal — Launching an agent opens it in a genuine PTY-backed terminal (JediTerm + PTY4J, the same emulator IDEA bundles). Focus lands in the terminal automatically and Ctrl+C interrupts the agent (SIGINT) instead of triggering IDEA's Copy.
  • Clickable terminal output — File paths (src/Foo.kt:42, ~/x/y.kt:3, C:\foo\Bar.kt:7, line ranges, quoted paths), stack-trace frames (Bar.java:123, Python File "x", line N), bare file names (plugin.xml), Java/Kotlin type names and Class.member references, and http(s):// URLs all become links. Clicking a file/type/member opens it in the editor and auto-hides the panel; URLs open in your browser.

⚠️ Warning — about "YOLO mode" / the skip-permissions flag: letting an AI agent run commands and edit files without confirmation can make irreversible changes, execute untrusted code, or expose your system. These risks come entirely from the agent and the bypass flag itself. This plugin only flips that flag for you — it adds no such behavior of its own, performs no actions on your behalf, and is not responsible for what the agent does. Enable YOLO mode only in trusted environments.

idea-plugin.name: knowledge-archiver
idea-plugin.description:
Knowledge Archiver — AI-Powered Code Knowledge Base Builder

Automatically turns Git commits into structured business knowledge documents. Zero manual effort, knowledge grows with your code. Supports DeepSeek, Zhipu, Qwen and other OpenAI-compatible APIs.

知识归档 — AI 驱动的代码知识库自动沉淀工具

将 Git 代码变更自动转化为结构化的业务知识文档，让知识随代码自然生长，零人工介入。

核心能力

  • Commit 自动归档 — 提交代码后异步调用 AI，将 diff 转化为业务视角的知识草稿
  • 多视角知识文档 — 每份文档按开发/客户/销售/产品/实施/测试/运维 7 个视角组织章节，AI 能推导的自动填充，推导不了的留 TODO 供人工补充
  • 四层记忆体系 — 元数据索引 → 内容存储 → 智能检索 → 跨模块关联，各层解决不同维度的知识管理问题
  • 多轮深化分析 — AI 自主规划分析路径，多轮迭代深入挖掘模块的业务规则、状态机、异常路径，按视角分节输出
  • AI 对话交互 — 直接与知识库对话，基于已有知识上下文进行问答和内容修改
  • 草稿→正式两阶段 — AI 生成草稿经人工审核后升格，确保知识质量可控
  • Tool Window 可视化 — 右侧面板浏览、搜索、筛选知识库，支持分类/标签/关键词多维度检索
  • Git 历史批量生成 — 从历史提交记录中批量提取知识，快速构建项目知识基线
  • OpenAI 兼容 API (BYOK) — 支持任意兼容端点，密钥仅存本地，数据不出项目

设计理念

文件即记忆，对话是工具 — AI 分析结果直接写入 Markdown 文件，可被 Git 版本控制、人工编辑、零成本迁移。
idea-plugin.change-notes:
v1.14.0

  • 知识库健康检查：一键扫描所有文档，检测代码标签有效性 + 方法级过期检测，精确到"哪个方法变了"
  • 远程同步前置：健康检查前自动 fetch 远程仓库，确保基于最新代码检查

  • Token 消耗大幅降低：深化分析每轮从 ~85K-190K 降至 ~20K-50K（↓70-80%），8 轮总计从 ~800K 降至 ~200K（↓75%）
  • 文档质量三重防御：Prompt 约束 + 后处理清理 + 路径校验，Token 降了质量不降
  • 代码覆盖率分析：自动扫描模块源码对比知识文档代码标签，数据化告诉你"还缺什么"
  • V3 方法级代码标签：从文件级升级到方法级（文件#方法名），知识↔代码精准双向关联

v1.12.0

idea-plugin.name: CodeWave IDE
idea-plugin.description: CodeWave IDE — an enterprise-grade AI coding assistant for JetBrains IDEs.

idea-plugin.name: Go MCP++
idea-plugin.description:
Your agent stops grepping Go and starts asking the compiler. 24 tools that answer questions about Go code the way the IDE answers them — through the type system, rather than through text search — added to the MCP server built into GoLand.

GoLand already exposes file reading, text search and patching over MCP. What it does not expose is the Go type system. Go has no implements keyword, so which types satisfy an interface is recorded nowhere in the source — that answer exists only inside the IDE, and no amount of grepping recovers it.

  • Interfaces — who implements one, which ones a type satisfies, and why a type does not. Including the two cases that are invisible to search: a type that declares no method at all and gains the whole set by embedding, and the pointer-receiver trap, where *T satisfies and T does not.
  • Understanding code — resolve a symbol, read its doc and source, list a package's API with struct tags, find usages classified as call, read or write.
  • Changing code — change a signature and every call site with it, safe-delete, inline, move files between packages, fix imports. Every change lands on the IDE's undo stack.
  • Generating — interface stubs, an interface extracted from a type, Go structs from a JSON sample, table-driven test scaffolding.
  • Toolchain — run tests, builds, vet and module commands, returning structured failures rather than a log to re-read.

Requires the bundled MCP Server and Go plugins, and an agent connected to the IDE. Settings | Tools | MCP Server configures that for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others.

Nothing is transmitted anywhere. Usage counters under Settings | Tools | Go MCP++ are held in memory for the session only.

Documentation and agent skills for Claude Code and Codex
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • go_quick_fixes and go_apply_quick_fix no longer call an API deprecated in 2026.3. Every public overload of InspectionEngine.inspectEx takes a ProgressIndicator, and all of them are deprecated from 263; the one that replaces them is internal and does not exist in 2026.2. The tools now go through InspectionEngine.runInspectionOnFile, which is public in both. Nothing changes for a caller.

idea-plugin.name: OAuthLint
idea-plugin.description:
OAuthLint catches OAuth, OIDC, JWT, MCP, session, cookie, and CORS anti-patterns that AI coding tools frequently produce, and surfaces them as native inline annotations while you edit. This includes a dedicated MCP server-auth pack (token pass-through, RFC 8707 audience binding, unauthenticated transports, tool-handler SSRF) for the TypeScript and Python MCP SDKs.

It scans the current file on open and on save and highlights each finding with a gutter marker and a tooltip that carries the rule id, the explanation, and a link to the rule documentation. Where a fix is available you can apply it with an Alt+Enter quick fix, or suppress the finding with an inline comment. A "Scan Project" action runs one pass over the whole project and lists every finding in a tool window with click-to-navigate. Severity is mapped to the IDE's own error, warning, and weak-warning levels.

OAuthLint is fully self-contained. The rule pack ships inside the plugin and a small pinned scan engine is downloaded once and verified against a pinned SHA-256 checksum. There is nothing else to install.

Supported languages: ten in all, from JavaScript and Python to Go, C#, and Kotlin, activated automatically wherever the matching language support is present. The 270+ rule pack adds framework-aware coverage (ASP.NET Core, Gin/Echo/Fiber, Hono + better-auth, FastAPI, Ktor, Laravel/Socialite, Rails/Devise/OmniAuth/Doorkeeper) alongside the MCP server-auth pack.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.5.0

  • Apply fixes from the editor. Findings that carry a suggested fix now offer an Alt+Enter quick fix that rewrites the code in place. Two more intentions were added on every finding: suppress it with an inline comment, and open its rule documentation.
  • Scan the whole project. A new "OAuthLint: Scan Project" action (Tools menu) runs one pass over the entire project and lists every finding in a dedicated OAuthLint tool window at the bottom, with double-click navigation to the exact line. Previously findings appeared only in files you had open.
  • Branded gutter icon. Lines with a finding now show the OAuthLint mark in the gutter.
  • The bundled rule pack was refreshed and its cache key bumped so it stays current on upgrade.

0.4.1

  • Compatibility with 2025.x IDEs. The plugin now loads in IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, WebStorm, and the other IDEs from 2024.2 onward, including the 2025.1, 2025.2, and 2025.3 releases (earlier builds capped the supported range at 2024.3, which hid the plugin from newer IDEs in Marketplace search). Checked with the JetBrains Plugin Verifier. No rule changes.

0.4.0

  • Mobile auth: Swift/iOS and Android. 18 new rules for the auth mistakes AI assistants ship in mobile apps: tokens in UserDefaults or SharedPreferences instead of the Keychain/keystore, cleartext traffic, OAuth in embedded WebViews, hardcoded secrets, and more. Covers Swift (iOS, Vapor) and Android (Kotlin plus manifest and config XML).
  • 270+ rules total; inline diagnostics now cover Swift and Android XML too. The extraction cache key was bumped so the new rules load on upgrade.

0.3.0

  • New languages: PHP, Ruby, and Kotlin. The pack now spans ten languages (JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, C#/.NET, PHP, Ruby, and Kotlin), with framework-aware rules for Laravel/Socialite (PHP), Rails/Devise/OmniAuth/Doorkeeper (Ruby), and Ktor (Kotlin).
  • More framework packs. ASP.NET Core (C#), Gin/Echo/Fiber (Go), Hono + better-auth (TS), and FastAPI (Python).
  • 250+ rules total; the extraction cache key was bumped so the new rules load on upgrade.

0.2.1

  • MCP server-auth coverage. Catches the OAuth 2.1 mistakes Model Context Protocol servers ship: token pass-through (confused deputy), missing RFC 8707 audience binding, unauthenticated transports, and tool-handler SSRF, for the official TypeScript and Python MCP SDKs.
  • Rule pack refreshed; the extraction cache key was bumped so the new rules load on upgrade.

Full release notes: github.com/Auspeo/oauthlint/releases

idea-plugin.name: Sage for Copilot Chat
idea-plugin.description:
Sage analyses your GitHub Copilot chat sessions (from both the IDE Copilot panel and the copilot CLI) to find mistakes and turn them into lasting project or global Copilot instructions, so future sessions stop repeating them.

  • Seek Enlightenment — multi-select one or more chat sessions, analyse them with the installed copilot CLI, and merge the resulting lessons into .github/copilot-instructions.md, ~/.copilot/instructions/learnings.instructions.md, or both. Choose between Conservative (minimal, evidence-backed edits) and Aggressive (broader rewrites/removals) learning modes, and optionally pick a model.
  • Preserve the Holy Texts — export any IDE or CLI chat session to a readable Markdown file, including thinking blocks and tool calls, with a searchable session picker and a "Reveal in Explorer" shortcut.

Configurable via Settings → Sage (default export folder, content toggles). Learning scope, mode, and model are chosen in the "Analyse Copilot Sessions" dialog and remembered as defaults for next time. Requires the copilot CLI on PATH (or SAGE_CLI_PATH) and an active GitHub Copilot subscription for the learning feature.

idea-plugin.name: CodeAI Reviewer
idea-plugin.description:
CodeAI Reviewer is an IntelliJ IDEA plugin that analyzes uncommitted Git changes before they are committed. It securely sends filtered, bounded code context to OpenRouter, another OpenAI-compatible provider, or a configurable Spring Boot backend and presents actionable feedback directly inside the IDE.

The plugin provides five focused review modes:

  • General — correctness, maintainability, API design, database usage, and error handling
  • Security — injection risks, authentication, authorization, secrets, and data exposure
  • Performance — inefficient queries, blocking operations, concurrency, memory usage, and scalability
  • Tests — unit and integration test recommendations with formatted code examples
  • Explain — a structured explanation of changes, behavior, design decisions, and risks

Use Run All to execute every mode in one pass, then switch between the saved results without repeating API requests. Findings appear as responsive cards containing severity, category, filename, line number, details, relevant code snippets, copy controls, suggested fixes, and direct source navigation.

Privacy features include .codeaiignore support, sensitive-file exclusion, likely-secret detection, explicit confirmation before transferring code, and secure API-token storage through JetBrains PasswordSafe. The plugin runs reviews in cancellable background tasks and supports rich Markdown formatting for headings, lists, bold and italic text, inline code, quotations, and code blocks.
idea-plugin.change-notes:

  • Detailed issue cards with severity indicators, file and line metadata, code snippets, copy controls, suggestions, and source navigation.
  • A Review Results header with the issue count for every findings-based mode.

Changed

  • Reworked the mode controls into visible two-row buttons with a prominent full-width Run All action for narrow tool windows.
  • Tests and Explain now use a clean full-document presentation without unrelated findings statistics.

idea-plugin.name: Model Switcher for Codex CLI
idea-plugin.description:
A tool window for Codex CLI: switch the model and reasoning effort of every active chat in one click, jump straight to a saved chat, and launch your own Codex profiles — without leaving the IDE or typing shell commands.

Model presets

Four configurable model/reasoning slots, each with its own keyboard shortcut. Switching a preset updates every currently open Codex chat at once through the local Codex app server.

Chats

Open a new chat with the current preset, or pick any saved chat from a searchable list and resume it in an integrated terminal.

Launch profiles

For anything outside the model presets — a named Codex CLI profile, a non-default flag combination, whatever ~/.codex/config.toml knows about — add a launch profile in Settings: give it a name and the extra arguments to pass (for example --profile my-profile). It shows up as its own button in the tool window; clicking it runs codex <your arguments> in a new terminal, the same way you'd type it by hand.

Requirements

macOS only, with the Codex CLI installed at /opt/homebrew/bin/codex or /usr/local/bin/codex. The plugin only ever launches that local, verified executable and never sends keystrokes to the editor.

Independent tool built to work with Codex CLI. Not affiliated with or endorsed by OpenAI.

idea-plugin.name: Slow Query Monitor
idea-plugin.description:
Slow Query Monitor — Automatically monitors slow SQL output in IDEA console, provides SQL normalization, EXPLAIN analysis, and AI optimization suggestions.

Supported log formats:

  • Druid connection pool slow SQL
  • MySQL / TiDB slow query log
  • MyBatis-Plus slow SQL interceptor
  • p6spy (outagedetection)

Features:

  • Auto-detect and highlight slow SQL in console
  • SQL normalization and fingerprint
  • Intelligent EXPLAIN plan analysis (MySQL / TiDB / PostgreSQL / Oracle / SQL Server / Custom)
  • AI-powered SQL optimization suggestions
  • Custom JDBC driver support (load your own driver JAR)

Quick Start:

  1. Open Settings → Tools → Slow Query Monitor
  2. Select your slow SQL log format
  3. Configure database connection (for EXPLAIN)
  4. Configure AI model (for optimization suggestions, optional)
  5. Run your application — slow queries appear in the tool window

中文说明

自动监听 IDEA 控制台中的慢 SQL 输出，提供 SQL 归一化、EXPLAIN 分析和 AI 优化建议。

支持的日志格式：

支持的数据库：

快速开始：
