idea-plugin.name: Tempr Chat
idea-plugin.description:
Tempr Chat is a bring-your-own-key AI coding assistant for IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, Rider, GoLand, and the other JetBrains IDEs: an AI agent that reads and edits your project and runs commands, chat, and inline code completion. Connect your own keys for OpenAI (GPT), Anthropic (Claude), Google Gemini, xAI (Grok), Mistral, DeepSeek, Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Foundry, AWS Bedrock, and more of 30+ model providers, or use one OpenRouter key for 300+ models.

Part of the Tempr platform. Tempr Chat is the IDE side of it. The same agent runs in your terminal (Tempr CLI, included with every plan) and in its own desktop app (Tempr Code, coming soon), and the Tempr Gateway gives your own apps the same models through an OpenAI-compatible API. All of it runs on your provider keys, with one login and one Portal for budgets, traces and access.

Features

  • Agent mode -- every message runs through an agentic tool-calling loop: Tempr reads/searches your project, edits files, and runs shell commands, pausing for your approval before anything mutating happens (interactive, autopilot, or bypass approval modes).
  • Multi-agent delegation -- the agent can hand sub-tasks to specialist sub-agents, each shown as a card in the chat with its own messages.
  • "@" persona modes -- run the conversation as a specialist persona (plan, debugger, test, profiler, modernize, security, review, docs, refactor, git), or define your own custom agents (Pro).
  • Custom models -- pick models from your own OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, SGLang, LiteLLM) like any other model (Pro).
  • Inline ghost-text completions -- optional Copilot-style code completion as you type.
  • "Send to Tempr" quick-fix -- send any diagnostic straight to chat with the surrounding code attached.
  • Multiple chat tabs -- run several conversations side by side, each with its own model, agent mode, and history.
  • Chat history -- saved on your machine (encrypted at rest) and synced to your Tempr account so it follows you to other machines, unless you turn Cloud sync off; searchable, pinnable, renameable.
  • Live usage/cost footer -- token and cost totals for the active conversation, updated as you go.
  • File/image attachments -- attach the active editor document, pick or paste images, or use "#file"/"#symbol" and drag-drop to fold specific files into a turn.
  • MCP servers -- browse the built-in Model Context Protocol catalog or configure your own, and servers assigned to your account in Tempr's vault show up automatically; their tools become available to the agent alongside the built-in ones.
  • Accessible -- screen reader announcements for replies, errors, and tool confirmations, full keyboard navigation of tabs, menus, and dialogs, and visible focus.
  • Full in-chat settings -- approval mode, response style, iteration limits, disabled tools, and more.

Requirements

  • A Tempr license key.
  • Your own API key(s) for whichever model provider(s) you want to use, or a single OpenRouter key for broader access.

Getting started

  1. Install the plugin and open the Tempr tool window from the right-hand sidebar.
  2. Open Settings (gear icon in the chat toolbar) and enter your license key.
  3. Start chatting -- pick a model from the dropdown whenever you want something other than the default.

Privacy: Chat content is sent through Tempr's server to whichever model you've configured, on your own provider key, in order to generate responses. Conversation history is stored on your machine, encrypted, and synced to your Tempr account so it follows you to other machines; turn off Cloud sync in Tempr Settings to keep it on this machine only. Error reports (the error message and stack trace, never your source code or chat content) are sent automatically to help us fix bugs; turn off Automatic error reporting in Tempr Settings to stop them.

Tempr is proprietary software; a valid license key is required for use.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.19

  • Ask for a tool your organization's Tool Packs leave out. A tool card that says "Not allowed by your organization" now has a Request access button, which opens a Portal page where you ask an owner or admin for the tool.
  • Approved tools reach an open chat. A tool you're given, or a change to your Tool Packs, shows up on the next turn of a chat that's already open.

1.1.18

  • Your organization's rules and skills. When your organization publishes rules and skills for its agents, the agent follows its rules on every turn and reads one of its skills when a task matches it. The Organization section of Tempr's settings lists them; switch off a recommended one there.
  • Skills in your project. The agent finds SKILL.md skills in .tempr/skills, .agents/skills and .claude/skills in your workspace, and in ~/.agents/skills.
  • Slash commands. Type / in the chat for your organization's commands or Tempr's built-in ones.
  • Workspace instructions now come from AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .cursorrules and Cursor's rules as well as .github/copilot-instructions.md.

1.1.17

  • Tool Packs. When your organization limits the MCP tools you can use with Tool Packs, a tool outside your packs now shows "Not allowed by your organization" on its card instead of a bare error, and the agent is told not to call it again. The MCP settings show which of each server's tools your packs include.

1.1.16

  • Signing in to a remote MCP server from the chat. When a remote MCP server needs you to sign in before its tool can run, the tool's card now shows a sign-in link and a Retry button instead of a bare error. Sign in opens the link in your browser; Retry asks the agent to try again.

1.1.15

  • The tags on Browse MCP Servers cards ("official", "files" and so on) are readable in light themes. They had white text on a light gray background.
  • Text is easier to read in light themes. Faint labels, the green "Done" status, links and badges were too pale against a light background.

1.1.14

  • Ask mode searches your project. Before answering in Ask mode, Tempr finds the code in your project most related to your message and gives it to the model, as in VS Code and Visual Studio. Settings > General > "Search the workspace on follow-ups" (on by default) controls whether this happens on every message or only on a chat's first one; mentioning @workspace or #codebase always searches.
  • The chat's keyboard and screen reader support works. The script behind it never loaded: screen readers now announce chat updates, menus and pickers work with the arrow keys, panels and dialogs keep focus while open and give it back when closed, and history entries can be opened from the keyboard.

1.1.13

  • Go to File and Search Everywhere no longer raise an "IDE error occurred" balloon on recent IDEs (seen on IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2). The Send to Tempr intention was missing its description; it now has one, which also fills in its entry under Settings > Editor > Intentions > Tempr.

1.1.12

  • A dollar limit per agent turn. Set "Stop an agent turn after (US dollars)" under Agent limits and the turn stops before its next model call once its calls, sub-agents included, have cost that much; the chat says what it cost and what the limit was. Your organization may set a lower limit. The chat also says when a model's price isn't known, so the limit can't count its calls.
  • A turn that reaches its step limit says so in the chat, instead of stopping without a word.
  • An MCP tool's error result is an error. A tool that answered with isError had its error text passed to the agent as if the call had worked; it now comes back as "Error: …", as in the CLI.
  • A paid MCP tool fails clearly, once. Tempr doesn't pay for tools, so a tool that asks for payment isn't run: the agent is told the tool is paid and not to call it again, the tool call shows "Paid tool, not run" with the price when it's known, and later calls to it don't reach the server. A tool the server lists as paid is described to the agent as paid before it's called, and a server that asks for payment to connect says so instead of failing with an empty error.
  • A remote MCP server's failure status or a reply that isn't JSON is reported as an error. Before, the call returned "(no response from MCP server)" or failed with a parser error.

1.1.11

  • PowerShell script output comes back whole. run_powershell_script output was cut at 120 characters with "…", or at 80 on macOS and Linux, where pwsh also added colour codes, so the agent got paths and table values with their ends missing. Windows PowerShell's padding at the end of table rows is taken off too.
  • A failing PowerShell script's error comes back as text, not as PowerShell's CLIXML.
  • On Linux, run_powershell_script finds an installed PowerShell. It always reported PowerShell as not installed there.

1.1.10

  • Symbol search finds the definition first: search_symbols lists where a name is declared, and as what, before the places it's used, in C#, TypeScript and JavaScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, Kotlin, C and C++, Swift, Ruby and PHP.
  • The agent now sees a JavaScript monorepo's packages folder, which its file tools skipped as if it were NuGet's. Build output is left out only where a build made it (Cargo's and Maven's target, Gradle's build, a package's dist and out), along with Python virtual environments and caches.
  • Searching the code covers Kotlin build scripts, Vue, Svelte and Astro components, .NET project files, and build files such as Makefile and Dockerfile.

1.1.9

  • The agent remembers the conversation. Each message used to reach it as the start of a new chat, with none of your earlier questions or its answers.
  • Your .github/copilot-instructions.md now goes with every message (Settings > General > Workspace instructions), and an overview of the project's files and README with each message's first step (Settings > Agent limits > Project context budget). Both settings were there but did nothing.
  • Autopilot no longer runs every npm script: it runs npm test and the build, compile, test, lint and typecheck scripts, and asks before the rest, npm run deploy included.
  • Trusting a command for the session trusts that script, not the whole tool: trusting npm run build no longer trusts every npm run script.
  • A build that also publishes (mvn test deploy, ./gradlew build publish) asks every time, like a delete.

1.1.8

  • The agent asks before opening a page it found itself. Without asking, it opens a link from your messages, from a tool's result or from a page it has already read, and any page of a well-known documentation site. For any other address it shows a card with the whole address: Open, Trust the site for this session, or Reject, the way Claude Code asks per site. It used to refuse.
  • Settings > Permissions > Sites the agent can open lists sites whose pages open without asking: docs.example.com, or *.example.com for its subdomains.
  • A link on a page the agent read earlier in a chat can be opened in a later turn of the same chat.
  • Page reads show as "Fetching <address>" and package lookups as "Looking up npm package react", instead of the tool's name.

1.1.7

  • Perplexity's Sonar models are now its Agent API presets, perplexity/fast, low, medium, high and xhigh, since Perplexity retires Sonar chat completions on 2026-09-27. A Sonar model you had picked moves to its replacement by itself, so it stays selected: sonar becomes fast, sonar-pro becomes low, sonar-reasoning-pro becomes medium, and sonar-deep-research becomes high. That covers your chat model, inline-completion model and per-agent models.
  • The plugin's Marketplace description now says what it does with your data: requests go through Tempr's server to the model you picked, on your own provider key; chat history syncs to your Tempr account unless you turn Cloud sync off; and error reports are sent automatically unless you turn them off. It used to say chat history stayed on your machine.

1.1.6

  • Tempr Settings now has a Cloud sync switch in the Account card. Turn it off and Tempr stops storing your chats, custom agents and tool preferences on your Tempr account; your chats stay on this machine. The switch belongs to your account, so it covers every machine and every Tempr extension signed in to it, and you can also change it in the Tempr Portal. Turning it off offers to delete what's already stored, and Delete synced data does that at any time. Sync stays on unless you turn it off.

1.1.5

  • If your IDE can't run its built-in browser (JCEF), for example because it was started on a Java runtime without it, Tempr no longer raises an IDE error every time a project opens. The Tempr panel instead explains why the chat can't start, with a link to Choose Boot Java Runtime for the IDE so you can switch to a runtime that includes JCEF.

1.1.4

  • Google's Gemini models are now listed as google/… instead of gemini/…, the same name OpenRouter, Vercel's AI Gateway and models.dev give them, so a model id copied from any of those works in Tempr as it is. Nothing you have set needs changing: your chat model, inline-completion model, per-agent models and reasoning levels follow the new name by themselves, and the old gemini/… name keeps working everywhere.

1.1.3

  • Reasoning level: a Reasoning dropdown beside the model dropdown sets how much the model thinks before it answers: Default (the model's own setting), Off, or the levels that model offers, from Minimal to Max. Tempr remembers your pick for each model. The dropdown only appears for models that have reasoning control, and a level a model lacks is sent as the nearest one it has.
  • The Tempr tool window's sidebar icon was drawn at the full size of the logo. It's now the same size as the other tool window icons, in both the classic and the new UI.

1.1.2

  • Security: a symbolic link or Windows junction inside your project can no longer lead Tempr's file tools outside it. Reading, writing, patching, listing and searching files now follow a link to where it really goes, and refuse it when that's outside the project.
  • Security: every spelling of a delete command is now treated as destructive, so it asks for approval every time, in every approval mode, and can't be trusted for the session. Before, rm -fr and Remove-Item -Force -Recurse weren't recognized, so approving rm -fr build once trusted rm -fr on any path for the rest of the session. Tempr now goes by the command itself (rm, rmdir, rd, del, erase, Remove-Item, ri, unlink), whatever its flags or a sudo in front.

1.1.1

  • Agent turns no longer lose their connection when the chat goes quiet for more than ten seconds, such as while a model thinks or a tool waits for your confirmation. Before, a long enough quiet stretch could end the turn with "Lost connection to the agent run".

1.1.0

  • Accessibility: screen readers now hear when a reply finishes, when it fails, and when a tool call is waiting for confirmation. Chat tabs, the mode, approval mode, and model dropdowns, the attach menu, and chat history all work from the keyboard. The history, license, and tools panels and the settings dialogs behave as dialogs, and keyboard focus is always visible.
  • MCP servers assigned to your account in Tempr's vault now appear in the Tempr Settings MCP list, as read-only cards.
  • When the agent delegates work to a sub-agent on the server, the delegation now shows as a tool card in the chat, with the sub-agent's messages under it.
  • If the Tempr server speaks a newer agent-run protocol than this version understands, the plugin says so once per session instead of failing in unclear ways.
  • Editing a message you've already sent is hidden for now: saving an edit never worked in JetBrains IDEs, and it comes back once it does.

1.0.2 — Initial Marketplace release: agent mode with approval-gated file/command tools, "@" persona modes and custom agents, inline ghost-text completions, "Send to Tempr" quick-fix, encrypted local chat history with cross-machine sync, multiple chat tabs, a live usage/cost footer, MCP server support (built-in catalog browse/install, plus your own configured servers), and file/image attachments.

idea-plugin.name: DeepSeek Harness
idea-plugin.description:
English

DeepSeek Harness embeds the full DeepSeek Harness AI agent workbench directly inside IntelliJ IDEA. Chat with the agent in an embedded web UI, let it read and modify your project files, and review its changes with native diff tooling — a Qoder-like AI coding experience.

Key features

  • Embedded Web UI — the full DeepSeek Harness interface (chat, sessions, goals, workflows) runs in an IDE tool window via JCEF.
  • Workspace-bound agent — the agent works with your current project directory as its workspace (auto-registered on startup); it can read, create and modify project files.
  • Shared configuration across projects — models, providers, API keys, agent presets and personal skills live in one shared config home, so configuring them once applies to every project; sessions, workspaces and attachments stay isolated per project.
  • IDE context via MCP — the agent can read your current editor selection, open files and project tree, and open/reveal files, through the mcp__ide__* tools.
  • Send selection to DSH — right-click any code selection to send a compact file reference (@path#L1-14) to the harness; the full selection stays available to the agent even if injection fails (clipboard fallback).
  • Review & restore — a baseline snapshot lets you diff agent changes (modified/new/deleted), restore single or all files, ignore, or rebaseline.
  • Self-contained runtime — Node.js and the DeepSeek Harness runtime are bundled with the plugin and extracted on first use; no separate installation or network needed.
  • Multi-project & lifecycle — one instance per project (max 3 concurrent), processes are terminated on project close / IDE exit; crash auto-restart with backoff.
  • Logs & diagnostics — a DSH Log tab shows the dsh process output; crash notifications and a configurable log level help you debug.
  • Robust runtime provisioning — the per-platform runtime downloads on first use with a live progress bar and cancel, is SHA-256 verified, and can be imported from a local zip for offline use.
  • Bilingual UI — all plugin UI follows your IDE language (English / 简体中文).

Getting started

  1. Open the DeepSeek Harness tool window (right edge) — the bundled runtime is extracted automatically on first open.
  2. Go to Settings → Tools → DeepSeek Harness, enter your DeepSeek API Key (or import it from ~/.dsh), and apply.
  3. Start a conversation; ask the agent to read your code, or select code and use Send Selection to DSH to hand it context.
  4. Use Review changes in the tool window to inspect and restore agent edits.

Runtime & offline

Node.js and the DeepSeek Harness runtime are resolved per platform (Windows / macOS ARM64 & x64 / Linux x64) and downloaded once on first use (SHA-256 verified), then reused from <config>/dsh-idea/runtime/<version>/. To use a locally prepared runtime instead, set the DSH_IDEA_RUNTIME environment variable (or the Runtime directory field in Settings) to a directory containing node/ and dsh/. The Runtime download URL setting overrides the official download source (e.g. an internal mirror) but does not change where the runtime is stored.

中文

DeepSeek Harness 把 DeepSeek Harness 智能体工作台完整嵌入 IntelliJ IDEA：在 IDE 内嵌的 Web 界面中与智能体对话，让它读写你的项目文件，并用原生 diff 工具审查它的改动—— 类 Qoder 的 AI 编程体验。

主要功能

  • 内嵌 Web UI — 完整 DeepSeek Harness 界面（对话、会话、目标、工作流）通过 JCEF 在 IDE 工具窗口中运行。
  • 以项目为工作区 — 智能体以当前项目目录为工作区（启动时自动注册）；可读取、 新建、修改项目文件。
  • 配置跨项目共享 — 模型、供应商、API Key、Agent 预设与个人技能存放于统一的共享配置目录， 配置一次即对所有项目生效；而会话、工作区与附件仍按项目隔离。
  • MCP 桥接 IDE 上下文 — 智能体可通过 mcp__ide__* 工具读取当前 选中代码、打开的文件、项目树，并打开/定位文件。
  • 发送选中代码到 DSH — 右键选中代码即可发送紧凑文件引用 （@路径#L1-14）给智能体；即使注入失败，完整选中代码仍可被智能体获取 （剪贴板兜底）。
  • 审查与还原 — 基线快照让您可以 diff 智能体的改动（修改/新增/删除）， 还原单个或全部文件、忽略、或重新基线。
  • 自包含运行时 — Node.js 与 DeepSeek Harness 运行时随插件打包，首次使用自动 解压；无需单独安装或联网。
  • 多项目与生命周期 — 每项目一个实例（并发上限 3）；项目关闭 / IDE 退出时 自动终止进程；崩溃自动退避重启。
  • 日志与诊断 — DSH Log 标签页显示 dsh 进程输出；崩溃通知与可配置日志级别 便于排查。
  • 可靠的运行时下发 — 首次使用按平台下载运行时，带实时进度条与取消、SHA-256 校验， 也可从本地压缩包离线导入。
  • 中英双语界面 — 插件 UI 跟随 IDE 语言（English / 简体中文）。

快速上手

  1. 打开 DeepSeek Harness 工具窗口（右侧）——首次打开自动解压内置运行时。
  2. 进入 设置 → Tools → DeepSeek Harness，填写 DeepSeek API Key （或从 ~/.dsh 一键导入）并应用。
  3. 开始对话；让智能体阅读你的代码，或选中代码后使用 发送选中代码到 DSH 把上下文交给它。
  4. 在工具窗口使用 审查改动 查看并还原智能体的修改。

运行时与离线

Node.js 与 DeepSeek Harness 运行时按平台（Windows / macOS ARM64 & x64 / Linux x64）解析，首次使用 一次性下载（SHA-256 校验），之后复用 <config>/dsh-idea/runtime/<version>/。如需改用 本地已备好的运行时，可设置 DSH_IDEA_RUNTIME 环境变量（或设置页「运行时目录」）指向一个包含 node/ 与 dsh/ 的目录；「Runtime download URL」用于覆盖官方下载源（如内网镜像）， 但不会改变运行时的落盘目录。
idea-plugin.change-notes:
English / 中文

v0.2.4

  • Configuration is now shared across projects. Models, providers, API keys, agent presets and personal skills live in one shared config home again, so configuring them once applies to every project (sessions, workspaces and attachments stay isolated per project). This fixes custom models, API keys and agent presets silently disappearing after an IDE restart: the plugin used to overwrite the per-project config with a global copy on every start, and the patch section meant to redirect that config was rejected by dsh. Existing per-project config files are merged into the shared document and backed up under migrated/, never deleted. The Settings page now shows the shared config directory and can open it.
  • 配置改为跨项目共享。模型、供应商、API Key、Agent 预设与个人技能重新统一存放在共享配置目录， 配置一次即对所有项目生效（会话、工作区与附件仍按项目隔离）。此举修复"自定义模型 / API Key / Agent 预设 重启 IDE 后消失"：此前插件每次启动都用全局副本覆盖项目配置，而用于重定向配置的 patch 段又被 dsh 拒绝生效。 既有的项目级配置文件会合并进共享文档并备份到 migrated/，绝不删除。设置页新增"共享配置目录" 展示与打开入口。
  • MCP bridge script is now a single shared copy. It is deployed inside the dsh installation tree and resolves its dependencies from there, so the per-project node_modules link is gone (Node's ESM resolution does not traverse directory links).
  • MCP 桥接脚本改为全局唯一一份。脚本部署在 dsh 安装树内并从那里解析依赖，因此不再需要每个项目 创建 node_modules 目录链接（Node 的 ESM 解析不会穿透目录链接）。
  • "Send selection" and "Explain log" now work on dsh 0.1.5. The composer is a Lexical contenteditable editor, so the old injection no longer found a <textarea>. The injection was rewritten for the Lexical editor and verified against a real dsh page; duplicate file references no longer accumulate when the action is triggered twice.
  • "发送选中代码"与"日志一键解释"已在 dsh 0.1.5 上恢复可用。输入框是 Lexical contenteditable 编辑器，旧的注入方式已找不到 <textarea>；现按 Lexical 重写并在真实 dsh 页面上验证；同时修复了动作被触发两次时文件引用重复叠加的问题。
  • macOS verified. The plugin was tested end-to-end on macOS (Apple Silicon), in addition to the existing Windows / Linux runs.
  • macOS 已验证。除既有的 Windows / Linux 外，本版本已在 macOS（Apple Silicon）完成端到端测试。

v0.2.3

  • Runtime upgraded to DeepSeek Harness 0.1.5-rc.2, with full integration adaptation. The bundled / auto-provisioned runtime now ships dsh 0.1.5-rc.2 (Node.js 22.23.2). dsh 0.1.5 changed three contracts that this release adapts to: the launcher URL now carries a browser-auth token (?token=…) and every /api call must present the cookie it issues; RPC methods moved to a slash namespace with a {"args":{"request":…}} envelope; and workspace/list was removed (workspace display order is now read from storages/workspace.json).
  • 运行时升级到 DeepSeek Harness 0.1.5-rc.2，并完成全部集成适配。随包 / 自动下发的运行时升级为 dsh 0.1.5-rc.2（Node.js 22.23.2）。dsh 0.1.5 有三处契约变更并已适配：启动地址新增浏览器鉴权 token （?token=…），且所有 /api 调用需携带其下发的 cookie；RPC 改为斜杠命名空间并使用 {"args":{"request":…}} 信封；workspace/list 被移除（工作区显示顺序改读 storages/workspace.json）。
  • All five platform runtimes rebuilt; macOS x64 and Linux arm64 added. Prebuilt runtimes for Windows x64, macOS (arm64 / x64) and Linux (x64 / arm64) are published alongside this release (.zip + .sha256). Intel Mac and Linux arm64 assets are available for the first time.
  • 全部五个平台运行时重建，新增 macOS x64 与 Linux arm64。随本版本发布 Windows x64、macOS （arm64 / x64）与 Linux（x64 / arm64）的预构建运行时（.zip + .sha256）； Intel Mac 与 Linux arm64 资产首次提供。
  • Settings improvements and a file-picker fix. "Runtime download URL" now shows the currently effective address and has a Default button; "Runtime directory" is a real setting now (its Default button fills the plugin's own directory, which behaves exactly like leaving it unset). The local-runtime-zip picker no longer hides .zip files, and importing works even when the chosen file is not reachable via a plain filesystem path.
  • 设置页改进与文件选择器修复。"运行时下载地址"现反显当前生效地址并提供"默认"按钮；"运行时目录"成为 真正的设置项（其"默认"按钮填入插件自身目录，且与未设置完全等价）。本地运行时 zip 选择器不再隐藏 .zip 文件；且当所选文件无法通过常规文件系统路径访问时，导入依然可用。
  • Known limitation. dsh 0.1.5 replaced the composer <textarea> with a Lexical editor, so "Send selection" and "Explain log" currently fall back to the clipboard (with a notification) until the JS injection is reworked.
  • 已知限制。dsh 0.1.5 将输入框由 <textarea> 改为 Lexical 编辑器，因此"发送选中代码" 与"日志一键解释"在完成注入适配前会降级为剪贴板（有提示）。

v0.2.2

  • Fixed the plugin not loading on IntelliJ IDEA 2024.x. Startup failed on 2024.x with "contains invalid plugin descriptor". The cause was the <icon> element in the plugin descriptor, which is not recognized by the 2024.x descriptor parser. That element has been removed, and the plugin now loads correctly on IntelliJ 2024.x and later.
  • 修复插件在 IntelliJ IDEA 2024.x 上无法加载的问题。该版本启动时提示 "contains invalid plugin descriptor"。原因是插件描述符中的 <icon> 元素不被 2024.x 的描述符解析器识别。现移除该元素，插件已可在 IntelliJ 2024.x 及更高版本正常加载。

v0.2.1

  • Fixed a first-use runtime download failure. On some setups the per-platform runtime could not be fetched: the temporary download file is written next to the runtime directory, whose parent directory does not exist yet on a fresh install, causing a NoSuchFileException ("download failed" with no progress). The plugin now creates the directory before writing, so first use downloads and verifies the runtime correctly.
  • 修复首次使用运行时下载失败的问题。部分环境下按平台运行时无法下发：临时下载文件写在运行时目录旁，而全新安装时其父目录尚不存在，导致 NoSuchFileException（报"下载失败"且无进度）。插件现先创建目录再落盘，首次使用即可正确下载并校验运行时。
  • More reliable runtime download. The download client now uses a pooled, HTTP/2-capable client with a browser User-Agent, a relaxed 60s connect timeout and a configurable read timeout, plus backoff retries. First-use runtime downloads now succeed even on slow or unstable networks (e.g. GitHub access from mainland China), instead of giving up after a short timeout.
  • 更可靠的运行时下载。下载改用带连接池、支持 HTTP/2 的客户端，并附带浏览器用户代理、放宽到 60 秒的连接超时与可配置的读取超时，以及退避重试。即便在慢速或不稳定网络（如国内访问 GitHub）下，首次运行时下载也能成功，而不再因短超时即放弃。
  • Download progress bar with cancel. The tool window now shows a live progress bar (bytes / MB / speed) while fetching the runtime, with progress states ("connecting / verifying / downloading") and a cancel action; it no longer blocks the UI or sits silently at 0%.
  • 运行时下载进度条（可取消）。工具窗口在获取运行时期间会显示实时进度条（字节 / MB / 速率），并给出"正在连接/校验/下载"状态与取消入口；不再阻塞界面或停在 0% 无反应。
  • Import a local runtime zip. Settings and the error card now offer "Choose local runtime zip…", letting you point the plugin at an already-downloaded per-platform runtime zip (validated, SHA-256 checked against a sidecar) to start completely offline.
  • 导入本地运行时包。设置页与错误卡新增"选择本地运行时压缩包…"，可指向已下载好的按平台运行时 zip（校验有效性并按侧车做 SHA-256 校验），完全离线即可启动。
  • Clear diagnostics. Settings shows the exact per-platform runtime download URL (down to the file) with one-click copy, and the runtime download timeout is configurable. On failure the error card shows the exact URL that failed and the underlying cause, plus "Restart harness" and a route to Settings.
  • 更清晰的诊断。设置页回显当前平台完整的运行时下载地址（精确到文件）并可一键复制，下载超时可配置；失败时错误卡给出失败的具体地址与根因，并提供"重启 Harness"与直达设置入口。

v0.2.0

  • Fixed an install-time "invalid plugin descriptor" error on some IDE versions: the optional dependency on the JCEF module now declares its required config-file, so the plugin descriptor is valid on IntelliJ 2024.1–2026.2.
  • 修复部分 IDE 版本安装时报 "invalid plugin descriptor" 的问题：JCEF 模块的可选依赖现补上 必填的 config-file，使插件描述符在 IntelliJ 2024.1–2026.2 上均合法。
  • Cross-platform runtime: the plugin now runs on IntelliJ IDEA on macOS and Linux hosts, not only Windows. The Node.js + DeepSeek Harness runtime is resolved per platform and downloaded once on first use (SHA-256 verified); existing Windows installs reuse the already-extracted runtime seamlessly.
  • 跨平台运行时：插件现可在 macOS 与 Linux 主机上的 IntelliJ IDEA 运行，而不再仅支持 Windows。Node.js 与 DeepSeek Harness 运行时按平台解析，首次使用一次性下载（SHA-256 校验）；存量 Windows 安装会无缝复用已解压的运行时。
  • Thin & configurable package: the plugin zip no longer bundles the ~93MB runtime by default (Marketplace-friendly); the per-platform runtime is fetched on demand. An optional fat zip (-Pthin=false) remains available for offline / air-gapped installs, and the runtime download base URL is configurable in Settings.
  • 瘦身与可配置包：插件包默认不再内置约 93MB 运行时（利于 Marketplace）；按平台运行时按需获取。仍可构建含运行时的 fat 包（-Pthin=false）用于离线/内网安装；运行时下载地址可在设置中覆盖。

v0.1.3

  • Per-project DSH_HOME: workspace and sessions are now isolated per project, so switching projects no longer mixes up chat history and agent workspaces.
  • 每项目独立 DSH_HOME：工作区与会话按项目隔离，切换项目不再串台（聊天记录、智能体工作区各自独立）。
  • "DSH 一键解释" in the Run console: select a log snippet, right-click and choose it to send the log to the agent for an instant explanation — great for "what went wrong" debugging.
  • 运行控制台新增「DSH 一键解释」：选中日志右键即可一键提交给智能体解释，排查报错更省心。
  • Legacy session migration: after upgrading, previous chat sessions and projection caches are automatically migrated with correct titles — no more missing or mis-titled history.
  • 旧会话升级迁移：升级后自动迁移历史会话与投影缓存，标题正确，历史不再丢失。
  • API key masking & global sync: the API key is now shown masked in Settings and kept in sync across all projects via a single global credential file.
  • API Key 脱敏与全局同步：设置页密钥脱敏回显，所有项目通过全局凭据文件保持同步。
  • Fixed a credential conflict where injecting DEEPSEEK_API_KEY into the runtime environment could make the harness reject the key; the browser is no longer auto-opened on startup (--no-open).
  • 修复凭据冲突：不再向运行时注入 DEEPSEEK_API_KEY 环境变量（避免被 dsh 拒绝）； 启动不再自动弹出浏览器（--no-open）。
  • Bundled DeepSeek Harness runtime upgraded to 0.1.1-rc.2; repository source integrity fixed (runtime package sources are now fully tracked in git).
  • 内置 DeepSeek Harness 运行时升级至 0.1.1-rc.2；修复仓库源码完整性（runtime 包源码已全部入库）。

v0.1.2

  • JCEF compatibility on IntelliJ 2026.2: added an (optional) dependency on the bundled "Web Browser (JCEF)" plugin (com.intellij.modules.jcef). Since 2026.2 JCEF is no longer part of the platform core, so plugins using JBCefBrowser must declare this dependency or the classes are not visible at runtime (NoClassDefFoundError).
  • 2026.2 JCEF 兼容修复：新增对内置 "Web Browser (JCEF)" 插件 （com.intellij.modules.jcef）的（可选）依赖。2026.2 起 JCEF 不再属于平台核心， 使用 JBCefBrowser 的插件必须声明该依赖，否则运行时类不可见 （NoClassDefFoundError）。
  • When JCEF still fails to initialize, the tool window now shows the concrete exception plus check hints (enable the JCEF plugin / run the IDE on a JBR with JCEF / restart).
  • JCEF 初始化失败时，工具窗口现在会显示具体异常与排查建议（启用 JCEF 插件 / 以含 JCEF 的 JBR 运行时启动 / 重启）。

v0.1.1

  • Compatibility: now supports IntelliJ IDEA up to 2026.2 (build 262.*). Previously the plugin only declared support up to 2025.1 (build 251.*), so newer IDEs refused to load it.
  • 兼容性：现在支持至 IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2（build 262.*）。此前仅声明支持到 2025.1 （build 251.*），新版 IDE 会拒绝加载。
  • Removed dependency on the platform-bundled Gson JSON library (being phased out by JetBrains); JSON serialization is now self-contained and version-independent.
  • 移除对平台自带 Gson JSON 库的依赖（JetBrains 正逐步移除该库）；JSON 序列化改为 自包含实现，与平台版本无关。

v0.1.0

  • Menu icon for "Send Selection to DSH" now matches the plugin icon. 「发送选中代码到 DSH」右键菜单图标与插件图标一致。
  • Distinct icons for the tool window actions: Settings (gear), Open in browser (web), Review changes (diff), Restart (restart).
  • 工具窗口动作区分图标：设置（齿轮）/ 浏览器打开（Web）/ 审查改动（Diff）/ 重启（Restart）。
  • Plugin initialization completed, achieving basic interaction functions.
  • 插件初始化，完成基本交互功能。

idea-plugin.name: Pi Agent Selection
idea-plugin.description:
Integrates the Pi coding agent with your IDE: the current editor selection is automatically injected as context when you submit a prompt in Pi — no copy-pasting.

How it works
• The plugin runs a localhost-only service that tracks the active editor selection in real time (in memory, nothing written to disk)
• When you submit a prompt in Pi, a companion Pi extension fetches the current selection over HTTP and injects it as <idea-selection> context
• The same selection is injected only once; picking a new selection switches the context automatically; cancelling the selection stops injection
• A WebSocket channel keeps Pi's status widget updated with the current selection file and lines

Requirements
A Pi coding agent installation — the companion extension is deployed automatically by this plugin.

Notes
• Listens on 127.0.0.1 only (ports 19232+), no external network access
• Per-project service: multiple IDE windows / instances are fully isolated (port auto-allocation, discovered via ~/.pi/ide lock files)
• Installs and keeps the companion Pi extension up to date automatically (~/.pi/agent/extensions/)
• 兼容 Pi Agent：提交 prompt 自动注入 IDEA 当前选中代码，无需复制粘贴；Pi 侧扩展随插件自动部署
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.4.0:
• New blocky "P" plugin logo; actions renamed for clarity
• Caret-only file context: with no selection, injects the file under the caret (editor fallback included)
• Pi extension redraw fix via setEditorText; one-shot selection consumption hardened
• Replaced deprecated ReadAction APIs with non-deprecated equivalents
1.3.0:
• Right-click actions: Send to Pi (pushes the selection/file reference straight into your running pi session's input box) and Copy Reference (@path#L16-23) — in editor, project view and editor tab menus
• With multiple pi sessions, references go to the most recently active one
• pi extension expands @path#Lx-y references into code blocks on submit
• New plugin logo
1.2.0:
• Auto-deploy: the Pi-side extension is bundled in the plugin and installed/updated to ~/.pi/agent/extensions/ automatically on IDE startup (old copy backed up as .bak)
1.1.0:
• Multi-IDE isolation: one service per project window, port auto-allocation (19232+2i), lock-file discovery in ~/.pi/ide/
• Pi extension picks the server whose project matches its working directory (falls back to most recently active)
1.0.0:
• Initial release
• Real-time selection tracking (event-source editor, works with split editors and multiple projects)
• HTTP query + WebSocket push on auto-allocated ports (19232+2i / 19233+2i per project window)
• Pull-based injection: Pi extension fetches the current selection at prompt time, no stale context

idea-plugin.name: Codex CLI Companion
idea-plugin.description: Unofficial terminal-first companion that launches the interactive Codex CLI in a dedicated JetBrains Terminal tab at the current project root, then stages project file and selection references from the editor popup. Codex owns authentication, model selection, permissions, configuration, and session state in the terminal. Compatible Codex CLI sessions present source proposals through an editable native JetBrains diff while unsupported sessions continue in the normal terminal UI.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 0.4.8: Review external absolute file paths in the current IDE Diff with full target paths, IDE-owned Apply, actionable path errors, and revalidation of path identity and content before writes.
  • 0.4.7: Fix remote session pickers and session switching with independently authenticated relay connections, isolated native review ownership, and bounded disconnect cleanup.
  • 0.4.6: Add project-safe clickable file/line links in the dedicated classic Terminal widget, an open/focus shortcut, the Send to Codex floating-toolbar entry, and a corrected recursive PowerShell capability probe.
  • 0.4.5: Open Codex source reviews as temporary native editor-area tabs, with editable Proposed content, exact-tab cleanup, and source focus restoration.
  • 0.4.4: Add the gated openDiff dynamic-tool bridge: source proposals use editable native diffs, reviewer-edited content is committed through JetBrains APIs, and the terminal retains ordinary approvals.
  • 0.4.3: Stream large Codex plugin-catalog frames through private disk-backed buffers so growing marketplace metadata cannot reset remote terminal sessions.
  • 0.4.2: Keep terminal command-state probes off IDE action threads and support fragmented WebSocket messages without resetting remote Codex sessions.
  • 0.4.1: Run native-bridge startup from an isolated private script instead of pasting multiline shell code into the interactive Terminal.
  • 0.4.0: Add transparent native read-only file-change approval diffs for compatible Codex CLI app-server sessions, with safe terminal fallback.
  • 0.3.1: Adopt the unique Codex CLI Companion Marketplace name and a publisher-owned plugin ID.
  • 0.3.0: Add Send to Codex for staging editor file and line references in a running Codex CLI terminal.
  • 0.2.1: Use the official Codex product mark and correct the plugin author metadata.
  • 0.2.0: Replace the app-server chat tool window with a terminal-first Codex CLI launcher.

idea-plugin.name: LingxiCode AI
idea-plugin.description:
LingxiCode AI - An AI-powered toolkit for JetBrains IDEs that brings large language models directly into your daily coding workflow.

AI Commit Message Generation

  • One click in the Git commit dialog to generate a Conventional Commits message from the currently selected changes
  • Automatic diff collection with a configurable size limit, so large changesets are truncated gracefully
  • The generated message is filled into the commit message box and remains fully editable

AI Code Explanation

  • Select a code block, or simply place the caret inside a class, method, or function
  • Invoke from the editor context menu (shortcut: Alt+L) or the gutter icon on the left
  • Structured explanation displayed in a dedicated dialog with one-click copy of the full text

AI Code Review

  • Review the selected code, or the class/method/function at caret, from the context menu or the gutter icon
  • Multi-dimensional quality report (correctness, security, concurrency, robustness, performance, resource management, design, maintainability, readability, code style) ordered by importance, each dimension with its own suggestions
  • Report displayed in a dedicated dialog with one-click copy of the full text

AI Line-by-Line Comments

  • Generate a concise comment above each meaningful line of the selected code or the class/method/function at caret, preserving the code verbatim
  • Blank lines and closing-brace-only lines are skipped intelligently; comments follow the configured output language
  • Invoke from the editor context menu (shortcut: Alt+Shift+L) or the gutter icon, with one-click copy of the full text

Flexible Model Configuration

  • Built-in presets for OpenAI, DeepSeek, GLM (Zhipu), Kimi (Moonshot), MiniMax, Qwen (Alibaba) and Xiaomi MIMO, plus any custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint
  • Supports pay-as-you-go, Coding Plan and Token Plan endpoint types for the same provider
  • Fetch the available model list from the endpoint with one click, or type a custom model name
  • Switch the active model anytime via the status bar widget, without opening Settings

Privacy and Security

  • API keys are stored in the IntelliJ PasswordSafe and never written to disk
  • Requests are sent directly from your IDE to your own provider endpoint

More

  • UI language (Chinese / English) configurable in Settings, no IDE restart needed
  • Configurable AI output language (Chinese / English) and maximum diff size
  • Works with all JetBrains IDEs (IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, WebStorm, and more) since 2024.2

中文简介

灵犀码（LingxiCode AI）— 面向 JetBrains IDE 的 AI 能力集插件，将大模型直接融入你的日常编码工作流。

  • AI 提交信息生成：在 Git 提交对话框一键根据勾选的代码变更生成 Conventional Commits 格式提交信息，自动回填且可继续编辑
  • AI 代码解释：选中代码或将光标置于类/方法/函数内，经右键菜单（快捷键 Alt+L）或行号旁图标一键生成结构化解释，支持复制全文
  • AI 代码评审：选中代码或将光标置于类/方法/函数内，经右键菜单或行号旁图标一键生成多维度质量评审报告（正确性、安全性、并发、健壮性、性能、资源管理、设计、可维护性、可读性、代码规范，按重要性排序，各维度附改进建议），支持复制全文
  • AI 逐行注释：为选中的代码或光标所在的类/方法/函数逐行生成简洁注释（空行、纯闭括号等无实义行智能跳过，代码原样保留），经右键菜单（快捷键 Alt+Shift+L）或行号旁图标触发，支持复制全文
  • 灵活的模型配置：内置 OpenAI / DeepSeek / GLM / Kimi / MiniMax / Qwen / Xiaomi MIMO 预设及任意自定义 OpenAI 兼容端点，支持按量付费 / Coding Plan / Token Plan 类型，一键获取模型列表，状态栏即可快速切换模型
  • 隐私与安全：API Key 经 IntelliJ PasswordSafe 安全存储，不落盘；请求由 IDE 直连你配置的服务商端点
  • 界面语言可在设置中切换（中文/English），即时生效，无需重启 IDE
  • AI 输出语言、Diff 最大字符数均可配置

idea-plugin.name: Qoder CN Patch
idea-plugin.description:
Qoder CN (Tongyi Lingma) feature restoration and enhancement companion plugin.

Restores and enhances classic features removed or disabled in the latest Qoder CN releases with zero bytecode modification:

  • Inline Completion Restoration: Restores classic inline code suggestions and next-line prediction when official NEXT prediction is disabled.
  • Manual Completion Shortcut: Triggers inline suggestion on demand via Alt + C.
  • Settings Panels Restoration: Fully restores Code Completion and NES (Next Edit Suggestion) configuration panels.
  • Context Menu Actions: Restores Optimize, Comment, Testcase generation, and Explain code actions.
  • Caret Visual Customization: Highlights and bolds the caret during completion with custom colors, and restores seamlessly.

Qoder CN (通义灵码) 核心功能恢复与增强伴生插件。

针对 Qoder CN 新版相较于旧版被官方移除或禁用的经典功能，以零侵入伴生方式进行精准恢复与视觉增强：

  • 经典行内补全恢复：在官方 NEXT 编码预测关闭时自动兜底介入，恢复打字自动补全与 Tab 连环预测；
  • 手动触发快捷键：支持 Alt + C 即时唤起行内代码建议；
  • 全套设置面板恢复：完整恢复「代码补全设置」与「行间建议预测 (NES)」配置面板；
  • 右键菜单快捷操作：恢复代码优化、注释生成、单元测试生成与解释代码快捷菜单；
  • 光标视觉高亮定制：代码补全期间支持光标高亮（支持自定义颜色与取色器）及加粗显示，采纳后 100% 还原原生光标。
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed

  • 适配官方 Qoder 2026.917+ 新版底层架构：
    • 彻底修复在新版 Qoder 下因上游服务重构导致的 NoSuchMethodError 光标移动报错与崩溃；
    • 修复编辑器右键“框选代码对话”功能在 2026.917+ 新版下的调用异常与兼容性断流。

Performance

  • 高频光标与打字状态判定性能优化：
    • 引入内存级快速指针缓存（Fast Path），将打字与光标移动期间的补全状态判定开销降低至近零延迟（~1ns），并消除高频事件下的内存分配与 GC 压力。

idea-plugin.name: Seshlog - Coding Agent Session Manager
idea-plugin.description:
List, search and resume your local Claude Code, Codex, opencode and Pi sessions from a tool window, titled the way the agent titles them, with one click to reopen any of them in a terminal tab.

  • Sessions grouped by project with title, branch, last activity and a live indicator
  • Compact per-project Agents menu: show any combination of available agents, with your last selection restored when the project opens
  • Full-text search across prompts and replies, not just titles
  • Preview recent messages or inspect the full loaded conversation for a search result, with highlighted matches and keyboard navigation
  • Resume or fork a session into a new terminal tab; focus the tab if it is already running
  • Copy the latest assistant reply from Claude Code, Codex, opencode or Pi, preserving Markdown and code blocks without selecting terminal output
  • Copy the latest identifiable plan from Claude Code or Codex for review elsewhere
  • Use both copy actions from a known session's terminal, the session list or the conversation viewer; assign your own shortcuts in Settings → Keymap
  • Restore the sessions that were running when the IDE was closed
  • Activity badges and waiting notifications show when an agent needs input
  • Unread reply markers and next-attention navigation help you follow concurrent sessions
  • Pin, locally rename or hide sessions without modifying agent data
  • Filter by date, agent and sibling worktrees
Entirely local: Seshlog reads the agent's transcripts read-only, never writes to them, and makes no network requests — no telemetry, no analytics, nothing leaves your machine.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.6.8
  • Maintenance release with the latest fixes and improvements.
0.6.7
  • Maintenance release with the latest fixes and improvements.
0.6.6
  • Keep the toolbar on one row with overflow for narrow windows, move filters into a menu, and give search its own full-width row.
  • Make session rows easier to scan with titles above agent, time and branch details. Keep activity and unread badges aligned on the right, truncate long text to fit, and show full details in tooltips.
  • Collapse the message preview to its header row by clicking the header. Collapsed or expanded is remembered across restarts, and a collapsed preview does not read transcripts.
0.6.4
  • Pick up new and updated sessions as agents write them. The agent data directories, and folders created later such as Codex's daily folder, are now covered by the IDE's file watcher, so fresh Claude Code and Codex sessions appear, show activity and attach to their terminal without a manual refresh.
  • Copy from a terminal straight after an agent's first reply. When a running agent's session has not been indexed yet, Seshlog rescans once before reporting that no session is known.
  • Detach a terminal tab from its session when the agent process exits, so an ended Claude Code session is no longer highlighted while Codex starts in the same tab. Copy and Fork from that tab keep using its last session until another agent is identified.
0.6.2
  • Keep terminal tracking when switching from Claude Code to a fresh Codex session in the same tab. On macOS and Linux, identify the session from the transcript held open for writing by the Codex process.
  • Recheck the invoking terminal's current agent in the background before copying a reply or plan, so a shortcut does not use the previous agent's session while the new session is still unidentified.
  • Exclude Codex subagent and approval transcripts from terminal discovery. Follow the current CLI transcript when resume arguments refer to an older session, and leave ambiguous matches unresolved.
0.6.1
  • Improve terminal session tracking across split panes and tab moves by remembering the exact reworked terminal view on the IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2 terminal platform.
  • Retry session discovery every two seconds as terminals become ready. Preserve known associations when process information is temporarily unavailable, and recognise agents that replace their shell process.
  • Discover manually resumed agents from their executable and explicit session arguments, including codex resume with a session ID. Follow session changes in reused terminals without letting stale background results overwrite newer associations.
  • Resolve copy actions from the invoking terminal and the innermost split pane, and retry missed Claude Code session adoption before copying.
0.6.0
  • Add Seshlog: Copy Last Assistant Message for Claude Code, Codex, opencode and Pi. Copy the latest persisted assistant reply with its Markdown, code blocks and line breaks, skipping prompts, tools and thinking.
  • Add Seshlog: Copy Latest Plan for explicit Claude Code plan records and Codex Plan Mode blocks. Recorded plan text takes precedence over a linked file in the same record; file-only references copy the file's current contents. opencode and Pi plan copying are not yet supported.
  • Use both actions from an associated terminal tab, a historical session in the list or the conversation viewer. Both appear in the session context menu. Shortcuts are unassigned by default; Tools → Seshlog explains how to configure them in Settings → Keymap.
  • Read fresh content in the background, preserve the invocation's source session and discard superseded requests. Missing, unreadable or oversized content leaves the clipboard unchanged with brief feedback.
  • Resolve terminal shortcuts from the invoking terminal view, including the reworked terminal, without falling back to an unrelated selected session.
  • Keep session associations while terminals are dragged between split panes. Temporary detachment no longer loses copying, active highlighting, Show Tab or restore tracking; closing a tab still clears its association.

Older release notes

idea-plugin.name: DeepDraw
idea-plugin.description:
Draw and read DeepDraw drawings in JetBrains IDEs. Every edit is saved to the file you opened.

Opening a .deepdraw.html or .deepdraw.json shows the drawing on a canvas; the file's text stays one tab away. Drawings are hierarchical — any shape can contain a whole nested drawing and its own notes — and the DeepDraw tool window is that hierarchy.

A .deepdraw.html is self-contained and opens in any browser on its own. A .deepdraw.json is the same drawing as plain JSON, which diffs cleanly in git.

Requires a JetBrains Runtime with JCEF, which is the default for every JetBrains IDE.

DeepDraw is also a web app for drawing together, with sign-in, sharing and AI: deepdraw.app.

idea-plugin.name: PairPilot
idea-plugin.description:
PairPilot is an AI pair-programming assistant for IntelliJ IDEA from Kenton Labs.

It keeps context of your open code and the conversation around your session so you can reason through problems without breaking flow.

What you get

  • Chat with ChatGPT using your current editor and project context
  • Guide — session needs and prepared Q&A that PairPilot sends with every reply
  • Notes and Examples — local markdown pads (not sent to ChatGPT), with Edit/Preview, tables, and in-page heading links
  • Speak and Conversation mode with Whisper transcription
  • Teleprompter pacing so replies appear at a readable speed
  • Pop-out window and Hide from screen share for interviews and pairing sessions
  • Custom Guide/Notes tabs, keyboard scrolling, and tab switching without leaving the editor

Requirements

  • Your own OpenAI API key (Settings | Tools | PairPilot)
  • Internet access to an OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint

Privacy

PairPilot stores your API key on this machine. Chat messages, Guide content, and selected project/editor context are sent to OpenAI when you ask a question. Notes and Examples stay local unless you paste them into chat yourself.

Full policy: kentonlabs.github.io/privacy

Shortcuts (macOS Control+Option)

  • Control+Option+P — open PairPilot
  • Control+Option+Shift+P — pop out
  • Control+Option+Up/Down — scroll
  • Control+Option+Left/Right — cycle tabs

Source: github.com/KentonLabs/pairpilot
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Changed

  • Plugin id set to com.kentonlabs.pairpilot (Marketplace rejects ids containing intellij)

idea-plugin.name: DeepSeek Harness (dsh-tui)
idea-plugin.description:
Run dsh-TUI (DeepSeek Harness) embedded in the right-side DeepSeek tool window with a Claude Code-style experience: the session history list and one closable tab per running session live in the same panel — no bottom terminal clutter, and nothing loads until you open the plugin. One-click new sessions, resume last or any historical session, history grouped by project, archive, rename, delete, and @file mentions inserted from the editor. Requires Node.js and the open-source dsh / dsh-tui CLI (unofficial companion plugin). The plugin ships a one-click environment setup that detects missing pieces (pnpm, dsh CLI, dsh-tui profile, global skin packages) and installs them automatically, so it works on a fresh machine. IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1+ (build 261+), built on the Reworked Terminal API.

中文说明：dsh-TUI（DeepSeek Harness）内嵌在右侧 DeepSeek 工具窗运行：会话历史与每个运行中会话（可关闭标签）同面板共存，不再占用底部集成终端；点开插件才加载，IDEA 启动时不会自动弹出。支持一键新建/恢复会话、按项目分组的会话历史、归档/重命名/删除、编辑器插入 @文件引用；内置环境体检与一键自动配置（自动安装 pnpm、dsh CLI、dsh-tui profile 与全局皮肤包，可自愈 pnpm≥11 构建审批墙），需 Node.js 与开源 dsh/dsh-tui CLI（非官方伴生插件）。
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.4.0：会话跑完等待输入时 IDE 通知（点「查看」直达会话标签，可在设置关闭）；终端标签自动命名为会话标题（多会话可分辨）；项目树右键「插入 @引用」支持文件/目录多选；会话右键「查看改动」列出该会话编辑/新建过的文件（双击打开）；全局快捷键 Alt+D 聚焦/新建会话。

idea-plugin.name: Free AI Commit Message
idea-plugin.description:
Free AI Commit Message for JetBrains IDEs

Generate clean, descriptive, conventional commit messages directly from your staged Git changes in JetBrains Rider, IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, and other IntelliJ Platform IDEs.

Features

  • Zero-Config Free Quick Start: Works out of the box with no API key or account creation required.
  • BYOK with Free Quotas: Connect directly with your own personal API keys for Gemini (1,500 req/day), Groq (14,400 req/day), OpenRouter, GitHub Models, DeepSeek, OpenAI, and Claude.

  • Context-Aware: Existing commit notes are passed as guidance context.
  • Customizable: Temperature, request timeout, diff budget, language, and Gitmoji toggle.

idea-plugin.name: DeepSeek Harness Integration
idea-plugin.description:
Bring DeepSeek Harness (DSH) into IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, and other JetBrains IDEs. Chat with your code, review native diffs, and inspect agent activity without leaving your editor.

  • Code-aware chat: explain, fix, review, and document selected code from the editor context menu.
  • Native diff previews: inspect supported tool edits in the IDE's side-by-side viewer, including proposed changes awaiting approval. No Git repository required.
  • Sessions and Trace: revisit conversations, inspect tool cards, and explore session events with built-in Trace analysis.
  • Balance at a glance: view your DeepSeek balance and pricing information in the status bar when available.
  • Local Runtime management: start, stop, restart, or connect to a compatible existing Harness Runtime across editor windows. Automatic discovery uses a local or official Desktop-registered dsh command.
  • Provider and conversation controls: configure provider endpoints, credentials, and models; navigate conversation turns; and submit optional message or session feedback when the Runtime advertises those capabilities.
  • Secure credentials: store API keys in IntelliJ Password Safe.
  • English and Simplified Chinese interface resources.

Get started: open the DSH tool window, configure your API key, and ask a question or right-click a code selection. Runtime settings are under Settings > Tools > DeepSeek Harness.

Requirements: IntelliJ Platform 2024.3 or later with JCEF. Local Runtime startup discovers an installed dsh command; explicit pnpm/npx launch commands remain available. The bundled lifecycle helper requires Node.js 24+. You can also connect to an existing Runtime.

Getting started and configuration | 简体中文指南 | Report an issue

Data use: the plugin does not collect telemetry. Prompts and attached context are sent through the DSH Runtime to the model provider configured by the user.

This is an independent community plugin and is not endorsed or maintained by DeepSeek or JetBrains.

idea-plugin.name: ChangeRail
idea-plugin.description:
One click to watch important changes while you work with a coding agent.

Start Guarded Task uses saved project defaults and important-file rules without a setup dialog. Scope is unrestricted in this default mode: the plugin does not infer what you asked an agent to change.

Use Custom Guarded Task when you need explicit allowed paths, additional protected paths, or a task-specific change budget.

  • Built-in rules cover environment files, dependencies, CI workflows, Dockerfiles, and database migrations; matching uses paths and names.
  • Review important-file hits, optional scope violations, and budget alerts in the tool window, status bar, and deduplicated notifications.
  • Copy a Markdown report containing policy, file paths, and verdicts.

Detection and visualization only: an alert requests review, not proof of a mistake. ChangeRail does not block edits or commits and never reverts files.

Coverage limits: pre-existing changed paths are excluded even if edited again. External edits depend on IDE refresh. Mid-task commits produce a warning; their committed changes are not fully tracked. Keep the IDE open and review changes independently; notification before a commit is not guaranteed.

Monitoring runs locally, with no telemetry, source upload, or AI API calls. Marketplace purchase and license management use JetBrains' separate infrastructure.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.1.2
  • One-click important-file monitoring from the tool window and idle status bar. Scope restriction is optional through Custom Guarded Task.
  • Per-project protected paths and change-budget defaults, stored outside the repository.
  • Explicit unrestricted-scope and pre-existing-change coverage warnings.
  • License checks and the existing detection model are unchanged; this is not an edit blocker.
2026.1.1
  • Paid licensing enabled: the plugin now verifies its JetBrains Marketplace licence before starting a new guarded task. A licence problem only refuses to START a task — a running task, its report, and your files are never touched.
2026.1.0
  • Initial release: guarded tasks with allowed/protected paths, sensitive-file rules, change budget, tool window, status bar widget, notifications, and Markdown report.

idea-plugin.name: Canopy Workspace
idea-plugin.description:
One view over every tree an agent works in.

Canopy runs Claude Code sessions inside your JetBrains IDE and, when they are done, lets you review what they changed in one diff tree that spans the project, its submodules and every git worktree.

Review

  • Detail tab: one session's changes across every repository it wrote to, sectioned into uncommitted, committed, pushed and untracked
  • Files open in the IDE's own diff viewer; content is read only when you open one
  • Commit across all touched repositories at once, updating submodule pointers in the parent

Worktrees and submodules

  • Worktrees grouped under the repository that owns them, with the sessions that ran in each
  • Submodules discovered from git, including their own worktrees
  • Create a worktree in any repository, not just the project root
  • Says why a leftover directory is orphaned instead of calling everything "unregistered"

Sessions

  • Blocked agents sort first: waiting for permission, waiting for you, working
  • Works for sessions running outside the plugin too
  • Cmd+Shift+O for the session palette, Cmd+Shift+J to jump to the next one waiting
  • Parsed transcripts are remembered between restarts, so a gigabyte of history is read once

Terminal

  • Clickable links and Cmd+V image paste in session terminals
  • A plain shell tab for running whichever agent you like

Canopy is free, and stays free. If it saves you time, you can buy me a coffee.

idea-plugin.name: AI Error Log Purifier
idea-plugin.description:
AI Error Log Purifier prepares IntelliJ IDEA console errors for analysis by a user-selected LLM provider.

It can:

  • Analyze selected console output or the full console log.
  • Ask a separately running Error Purifier backend to mask sensitive values, compress repeated log entries, and prepare a focused prompt.
  • Stream responses from supported OpenAI, Google Gemini, and Anthropic models.
  • Show the prepared log, token usage, response time, and compression savings in the tool window.

Requirements: IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2 or later, a separately deployed self-hosted Error Purifier backend, and credentials supplied by the user for the selected LLM provider. The backend is not bundled and no vendor-operated service is provided. Follow the Docker Compose Quick Start, then configure the backend URL, LLM provider, model, analysis mode, and API key under Settings | Tools | AI Error Purifier. Marketplace reviewers can use the review guide.

Data flow: up to 1,000,000 characters of console log content, filtered build-file metadata, and basic plugin environment tags are sent to the backend configured by the user for masking, compression, focusing, and prompt preparation. When console text is selected, only that selection is sent as log content. The prepared prompt is then sent directly from the IDE to the LLM provider selected by the user. Request usage and user-submitted feedback metrics are reported to the configured backend. A server-issued persistent device UUID is stored in the IntelliJ configuration directory. Client synchronization includes that identifier and the plugin version; subsequent backend requests use the UUID to associate usage and feedback. The provider API key is stored in IntelliJ PasswordSafe and is not sent to the Error Purifier backend.

The plugin requires explicit consent before backend or LLM network operations, including analysis, provider connection tests, usage-summary requests, and feedback. Current consent is checked again immediately before each HTTP transmission. See the Privacy Policy for the complete data, storage, retention, and revocation details.

Users are responsible for running the self-hosted backend and for supplying credentials for their selected LLM provider.

idea-plugin.name: Giuan Tomcat
idea-plugin.description:
Giuan Tomcat — Plugin Description

Run Apache Tomcat directly from IntelliJ IDEA

"Giuan Tomcat" adds a Giuan Tomcat run configuration that starts an Apache Tomcat instance
without requiring the bundled Tomcat integration or any external plugin. The plugin:

  • auto-generates the CATALINA_BASE (conf, logs, work, temp, webapps) in the system temp folder;
  • writes server.xml and the per-application context.xml;
  • launches Bootstrap with full native IntelliJ debug support (breakpoints, variables, stack
    traces).

No WAR is assembled: the web-content directory you choose is used directly as the docBase, and
classes/libraries are attached through the generated context.xml.

Supported versions

Tomcat

The plugin works with any Apache Tomcat that keeps the standard layout
(bin/bootstrap.jar + bin/tomcat-juli.jar):

Version Status Notes
Tomcat 9.x Developed and tested against Recommended reference version
Tomcat 8.x / 8.5 Compatible Same javax layout
Tomcat 7.x Compatible Standard layout, same mechanism
Tomcat 10+ / 11 Compatible with caveats Your web application must use the Jakarta EE namespace (jakarta.*) and a suitable JDK (Java 11+)

All generated elements (PreResources/DirResourceSet, JarScanner/JarScanFilter,
containerSciFilter) are available from Tomcat 7 onward, so the plugin does not depend on a
specific Tomcat version.

Java / JDK

  • Normal run (no HotSwap): any JDK — the plugin uses the project SDK.
  • HotSwap mode: requires a JDK patched with DCEVM. Per the
    DCEVM project the supported HotSpot versions are 7, 8, 9, 10 and
    11     (see "HotSwap prerequisites" below).

Features

Class & library consolidation (giuan-merged)

For each run the plugin builds a merged classpath under
<tmp>/giuan-tomcat/<hash>/giuan-merged:

  • the target/classes of the selected modules are merged into a single WEB-INF/classes;
  • their compile-scope dependency jars are gathered into WEB-INF/lib.

Class files and jars are exposed via hard links, and whole class/resource subtrees that are
unique to a single module are linked directly as a directory junction/symlink; folders shared by
several modules (e.g. the same package present in different target/classes) are merged into one
real directory. Only when the filesystem does not allow linking does the plugin fall back to a
physical copy.

Because links share the underlying files, a recompile is immediately visible to the running
server. The merge is incremental: a manifest remembers the previous state so unchanged
modules and jars are not relinked on the next run.

No build/deploy step

The consolidated WEB-INF/classes and WEB-INF/lib are mounted on the web app through Tomcat
PreResources (DirResourceSet) at /WEB-INF/classes and /WEB-INF/lib, so nothing is copied
into your web content.

Startup scan skip (granular, per jar)

The classpath panel has three columns (Available / Selected modules / Manage skips) letting you
choose, for every dependency jar of a module, whether it is skipped or not, and speed up boot on
large applications:

  • Per dependency jar (Skip TLD / Skip pluggable) — for each jar of the module selected in the
    middle list you can independently decide to skip (skip) or keep (non-skip) it in the
    TLD/taglib scan (tldSkip) or in the pluggability/SCI scan (pluggabilitySkip) of the
    generated context.xml. As soon as at least one jar is excluded the plugin sets
    reloadable="false" and containerSciFilter on the context and disables scanClassPath,
    scanBootstrapClassPath, scanAllDirectories and scanAllFiles. Non-flagged jars remain
    scanned and every jar stays mounted and usable; jars of the other modules are still scanned.

  • Annotation scan skip (global checkbox, common to all modules) — on run the plugin edits the
    WEB-INF/web.xml of the web content, adding metadata-complete="true" to the <web-app>
    element and an empty <absolute-ordering/>. What is skipped: Servlet 3.0 annotation scanning
    (@WebServlet/@WebFilter/...) and the discovery and processing of web-fragments and
    ServletContainerInitializer registered in the application jars. The additions are tracked with a
    marker comment so that removing the flag on a later run removes exactly what the plugin
    added    ; any pre-existing metadata-complete/<absolute-ordering> are left untouched. Changes
    are applied idempotently.

Simple configuration

Choose CATALINA_HOME, web content (docBase), context path and HTTP/shutdown ports from a single
dialog, plus the modules that contribute to the application classpath. The CATALINA_BASE is
auto-generated in the system temp folder
(<tmp>/giuan-tomcat/<hash>/catalina-base, where the hash derives from the project location and
the configuration name).

Optional HotSwap mode (DCEVM + hotswap-agent)

Enable unlimited runtime class redefinition (add/remove fields and methods without restarting).
It requires a JDK patched with DCEVM (see prerequisites below); the patched JDK is always forced
when HotSwap is active, in Run and Debug alike: in Debug the IDE debugger performs the reload
(JDWP), in Run the agent watches target/classes automatically (autoHotswap).

Generated instance reuse

Each configuration maps to its own folder under the system temp dir (hash of project +
configuration name, no collisions between projects); the instance is kept between runs and can be
started again after it is stopped.

HotSwap prerequisites

A JDK patched with DCEVM — per the DCEVM project the supported HotSpot
versions are 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11:

  • light installers for 8u181, 8u152 and 7u79:
    DCEVM binaries / all releases
  • Java 11 via Trava OpenJDK,
    which ships with hotswap-agent integrated;
  • a hotswap-agent.jar downloaded from the
    HotswapAgent releases.

The plugin launches Tomcat with -XXaltjvm=dcevm plus the agent. For a normal run (no HotSwap)
any JDK works: the plugin uses the project SDK.

HotSwap environment setup: see GUIDA-HOTSWAP.md.

idea-plugin.name: AI Reference Copier
idea-plugin.description:
Overview

A lightweight plugin for IntelliJ Platform IDEs that copies AI-readable paths to help AI tools locate code when working alongside your IDE.

How to use

  • Copy a code location: Select code in the editor and choose “Copy AI Code Reference” from the context menu. With no selection, the current cursor line is copied.
  • Copy a file or folder: Select one file or folder in the Project view and choose “Copy AI Reference...” from the context menu.
  • Use shortcuts: Press Ctrl+Alt+Shift+R for a code reference or Ctrl+Alt+Shift+P for a file or folder reference. The shortcuts can be changed in the IDE Keymap.
  • Customize the format: Search for “AI Reference Copier” in Settings/Preferences to choose project-relative or absolute paths, edit code, file, and folder templates, and view their previews.

The default output uses paths relative to the IDE project root with / separators. The plugin does not read source contents, access the network, or call AI services.

中文说明

面向 IntelliJ Platform IDE 的轻量插件，IDE与AI工具协作时复制AI可理解的路径，提供给AI做代码定位。

操作方法

  • 复制代码位置：在编辑器中选中代码，右键选择“复制 AI 代码引用”；未选择代码时复制当前光标所在行。
  • 复制文件或文件夹：在 Project 文件树中选中一个文件或文件夹，右键选择“复制 AI 引用...”。
  • 使用快捷键：代码引用使用 Ctrl+Alt+Shift+R，文件或文件夹引用使用 Ctrl+Alt+Shift+P；可在 IDE Keymap 中修改。
  • 自定义格式：在 Settings/Preferences 中搜索“AI Reference Copier”，可选择项目相对路径或绝对路径，分别设置代码、文件和文件夹模板并查看预览。

默认输出以 IDE 项目根目录为基准的相对路径，统一使用 / 分隔符。插件不会读取代码正文、连接网络或调用 AI 服务。

  • Previews code, file, and folder references using the selected path type and custom templates.

idea-plugin.name: Java Refactoring MCP Tools
idea-plugin.description:
Adds native Java refactoring operations to the IDE's built-in MCP Server, so AI coding agents can plan and execute real IDE refactorings through MCP instead of editing source text directly. Every write tool drives one native IntelliJ refactoring processor headlessly (no dialog), reports affected files, and stays reversible with exactly one Undo.
Exposes 24 Java tools: extract method, introduce variable / constant / field / parameter, change signature (add parameter), inline variable / method, safe delete, move class, move instance method, make static, convert to instance method, encapsulate fields, extract interface / superclass, pull members up / push members down, use interface where possible, introduce parameter object, replace method with method object, extract delegate, replace inheritance with delegation, plus a read-only symbol locator.

idea-plugin.description:

  • Any scope: uncommitted, staged, unstaged, a stash, a commit, a commit range, or everything since a branch's merge-base. Right-click commits in Git Log.
  • Branch mode: no diff needed. List the whole tree or one folder, annotate files in their editor, hand the notes to the agent as a plan.
  • Inline comments: hover a line and click +, or press Alt+Shift+C. Note, issue, question, nit, praise. Edit, Resolve, Delete on the card.
  • Reviewed marks keyed by content: a file the agent edits again shows as changed. Next Unreviewed walks you through the rest.
  • Comments follow the text across scopes and commits, and show as outdated when it is gone.
  • Send the review to the clipboard, the IDE terminal, a file, a Copilot or AI Assistant chat, or live over MCP where the agent resolves comments with a reply and can ask back.
  • One toggle hides every card, button and shortcut Nitpick adds to editors and diffs.

idea-plugin.name: Easy AI Commit
idea-plugin.description:
Easy AI Commit is a simple, flexible AI-assisted commit message generator for JetBrains IDEs.

Existing plugins often support only OpenAI-style APIs, require complex setup, or do not allow custom prompts. Easy AI Commit removes those trade-offs with a focused one-click workflow.

Model connectivity

  • First-class support for both OpenAI Compatible and Anthropic Compatible protocols.
  • One Custom preset can use either protocol, making it suitable for compatible model providers, aggregation services, gateways, and proxies.
  • Named model profiles support custom Base URLs, model IDs, API keys, and connection testing, so multiple endpoints remain easy to configure and distinguish.

Provider presets

Includes 24 named presets with protocol-specific defaults for endpoints, models, and authentication:

  • OpenAI Compatible and Anthropic Compatible: DeepSeek, OpenRouter, GLM, Alibaba Bailian, Kimi, MiniMax, SiliconFlow, StepFun, and Tencent TokenHub.
  • OpenAI Compatible: OpenAI, Gemini, Grok, Volcano Ark, Baidu Qianfan, iFlytek Spark, Mistral AI, Groq, Together AI, Fireworks AI, Cerebras, Cohere, Perplexity, and Hugging Face.
  • Anthropic Compatible: Anthropic.

Commit message generation

  • Click the Easy AI Commit logo to generate from included changes, or from all displayed pending changes when nothing is included.
  • Generated text is written directly into the existing Commit Message editor.
  • Custom prompt templates and 18 selectable output languages are supported.
  • Auto output language follows the current IDE language.
  • API keys are stored securely with JetBrains Password Safe.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Added per-model proxy settings: IDE proxy, direct connection, or custom HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy, with optional HTTP Basic proxy authentication.
  • Added a configurable total request timeout of 5–300 seconds (default: 90 seconds). Timed-out requests are canceled without replacing the existing commit message.
  • Breaking behavior change: the previous 90-second read timeout is now a total network request deadline, including connection and the complete response. Slow requests may time out sooner; adjust the model profile timeout if needed.
  • Added credential save read-back verification and clearer proxy errors. Connection tests use current form values and discard stale results.
  • Updated English, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, and Korean UI text and documentation.
  • New profiles and profiles without a stored proxy mode default to no proxy (direct connection). Explicitly stored proxy choices are preserved. The default total timeout is 90 seconds. The IntelliJ IDEA 2024.2 minimum supported version is unchanged.

idea-plugin.name: CommentCloak
idea-plugin.description:
Hide AI noise. Keep what matters.

AI-generated code comes with AI comments. Copilot, Claude, Cursor and friends narrate every step — // Increment the counter by one sitting directly above counter++. Individually harmless, collectively they double the height of every file and bury the three comments that actually explain something. CommentCloak is a comment filter for exactly that: it cloaks the narration and leaves the signal.

How it works. CommentCloak does not rewrite anything. It collapses code comments using the editor's own fold regions — the same mechanism the IDE uses to fold imports and method bodies. Nothing is deleted, nothing is reformatted, the file on disk is untouched and version control sees no change at all. Toggle it back off and every comment reappears exactly where it was. Hover a marker to peek at the text it stands for, or click it to reveal that one comment — it cloaks itself again once your caret leaves it.

Features

  • One-key toggle — Ctrl+Alt+/ to hide or show comments everywhere at once. The setting is remembered across restarts.
  • Right-click menu entry in the editor, plus an entry in the View menu.
  • Status bar switch showing Comments: hidden / Comments: shown — click it to flip.
  • Keeps what matters: TODO, FIXME, HACK, XXX, BUG and NOTE stay visible.
  • Keeps tool directives: eslint-disable, @ts-ignore, @ts-expect-error, noinspection, noqa, prettier-ignore, biome-ignore, region markers and more.
  • Keeps license headers: Copyright, SPDX-License, @license, @preserve.
  • Keeps only the paragraph that matters: in a fifteen-line block with a single TODO buried in it, CommentCloak keeps the TODO paragraph and hides the essay around it instead of leaving the whole block on screen.
  • Compact marker: a hidden block collapses to a small rounded pill showing the CommentCloak icon and how many lines it stands for — drawn on the comment's own lines, so nothing above it moves. Prefer the stock fold placeholder? Switch the marker style in the settings.
  • Documentation comments too — AI assistants love essay-length JSDoc blocks, so /** … */ is cloaked by default; one checkbox keeps JSDoc / KDoc / docstrings visible if you prefer.
  • Per-kind filters: choose independently whether to fold comments that are line (//, #, --), block (/* … */), documentation (/** … */) or HTML (<!-- … -->).
  • Minimum length filter — keep the one-liners, hide only the essay-style explanations an assistant left behind.
  • Regex keep-list — add your own patterns; anything matching is never hidden.
  • Whole-line collapsing — consecutive comment lines fold into a single small placeholder, taking their line breaks and indentation with them, so no blank gaps remain.
  • Caret aware — the comment you are editing is never folded out from under your cursor. Click a marker to reveal a comment; it cloaks itself again once your caret leaves it, so nothing you open stays open by accident.
  • Works everywhere — IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, Rider, PhpStorm, RubyMine, CLion, DataGrip and Android Studio, in any language whose parser produces comment tokens: TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Java, Kotlin, Go, C#, Rust, PHP, Ruby, SQL, YAML, HTML and the rest.

Keywords: hide comments, fold comments, comment filter, code comments, AI comments, AI-generated code.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.0

  • First release.
  • Global hide/show toggle bound to Ctrl+Alt+/, with entries in the View menu and the editor context menu.
  • Status bar widget showing and flipping the current state.
  • Per-kind filters for line, block, documentation and HTML comments.
  • Default keep-list for TODO/FIXME/HACK, linter and compiler directives, region markers and license headers; fully editable as regular expressions.
  • Minimum-length filter and configurable placeholder.
  • Consecutive comment lines merge into one fold; whole-line collapsing leaves no gaps.
  • Partial hiding: a block comment that matches a keep pattern keeps only the matching paragraph and hides the rest.
  • Compact pill marker with the line count, or the classic fold placeholder.
  • Caret-aware folding: revealed comments re-cloak when the caret leaves them, and the markers are repaired after the IDE's own folding passes.

idea-plugin.name: Codex Session Tabs
idea-plugin.description:
Keep Codex terminal sessions easy to identify and ready to resume inside JetBrains IDEs.

  • Session-aware tab names: Keep each terminal tab synchronized with its Codex session name.
  • Native activity indicator: Preserve JetBrains' Codex icon and show its animated progress state while Codex is working.
  • Session restoration: Restore the Codex sessions that were open when the IDE closed, including reusable CLI flags such as --yolo.

Codex Session Tabs works automatically with the Reworked Terminal. It uses local process and Codex state information, has no external service, and does not copy transcript contents.
