idea-plugin.name: PathRef for AI
idea-plugin.description:
Copy AI-ready paths, symbol anchors, context blocks, project trees, and Git commit info from JetBrains IDEs, ready to paste into Claude, Cursor, Copilot Chat, and other AI coding tools.

中文

  • Alt+P 统一入口：按设置页选定的默认动作复制（Anchor / Context / Path / Tree）；在 Git Log 中自动复制提交修订号，增强动作不可用时回退为路径复制
  • 支持编辑器与项目视图：文件、目录、多选路径列表、目录摘要树与多选折叠树，类 / 方法锚点，代码选区的行号范围与选中文本
  • 路径统一输出绝对路径（以 / 分隔，目录末尾补 /），不带 @ 前缀、无需配置，适合同时开发多个项目时在同一个会话中引用
  • Copy AI Path (WSL)（Alt+[）：把 Windows 绝对路径转换为 /mnt/d/...，可直接粘贴到 WSL 终端或 AI 会话
  • Copy AI Git Info / Copy AI Revision：复制提交 hash、短 hash、作者、时间、subject、refs、仓库根与变更文件列表，或按修订号列出文件状态
  • 全局设置页（Settings > Tools > PathRef for AI）：Alt+P 默认动作、复制通知开关、快捷键录制 / 清空 / 恢复默认 / 冲突校验，只读 Keymap 自动派生可编辑副本

English

  • Alt+P unified entry: copies with the default action selected in Settings (Anchor / Context / Path / Tree), copies the revision in Git Log, and falls back to a plain path copy when enhanced actions are unavailable
  • Works in the editor and the Project view: files, directories, multi-selection path lists, directory summary and folded selection trees, class / method anchors, selection line ranges and selected text
  • Always outputs absolute paths (slash-separated, directories end with /), with no @ prefix and no configuration, ideal for referencing several projects in the same session
  • Copy AI Path (WSL) (Alt+[) converts Windows absolute paths into /mnt/d/... for pasting straight into WSL terminals or AI sessions
  • Copy AI Git Info / Copy AI Revision: copies commit hash, short hash, author, time, subject, refs, repository root and the changed file list, or lists file status for a revision
  • Global settings page (Settings > Tools > PathRef for AI): Alt+P default action, copy notification toggle, and shortcuts with recording, clearing, restore-to-default, and conflict validation, plus automatic duplication of read-only keymaps

idea-plugin.name: LiteLLM Integration
idea-plugin.description: Connects the IDE to a LiteLLM-compatible gateway. Generates Git commit messages from the changes included for commit, suggests code inline as you type, and provides a chat tool window you can send an editor selection to from the right-click menu.

idea-plugin.name: Commit Helper
idea-plugin.description:
Commit Helper

Turns the changes you have checked in the commit panel into a ready-to-commit message: a subject line plus an itemized body. Grouping of files and modules is done locally and deterministically; an optional LLM (OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic or Gemini) only takes care of the wording. If the model is unreachable, the plugin writes the local grouping result instead of failing.

Nothing is generated until you click, and nothing is ever committed for you: the plugin only proposes text in the commit message box, where you can edit it as usual.

Features

  • Toolbar action in the commit message box — click Organize Commit Message and review the proposal in the preview dialog (replace, append or cancel).
  • Hybrid generation — file/module grouping is computed locally; the LLM only rewrites the wording.
  • Editable templates — output format template and prompt template, both with presets (Conventional Commits style by default).
  • Repository commit template — an existing .gitmessage / git config commit.template is used as the output skeleton, and its comment lines are preserved.
  • Issue key injection — {issue} is extracted from the branch name or recent commit subjects. No Jira/GitHub API calls.
  • Changelog and PR description — generated in a preview window for copying; no files are written and no git commands are executed.
  • Multi-vendor LLM support — OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Anthropic and Gemini, each configurable, with a local only mode.
  • Chinese and English output — switchable per generation.

Getting started

  1. Open Settings | Tools | Commit Helper and pick a provider, or stay on Local only (no account needed).
  2. Check the files you want in the commit tool window, click the commit message box, then click Organize Commit Message in its toolbar.
  3. Review the proposal, then replace or append.

Large changesets are sampled and noisy files (lock files, build output, minified bundles, binaries) are summarised instead of being sent in full. Unversioned files are read from disk; files larger than 1 MB are skipped.

Privacy

Only the diff of the files you explicitly checked is sent to the provider you configured. API keys are stored in the IDE credential store (Password Safe), never in the project. All network access is disabled in Local only mode.

Requirements

  • IntelliJ Platform 2024.1 or newer (IntelliJ IDEA, and any IDE shipping the platform and Git support).
  • Git4Idea (bundled with IntelliJ IDEA and most IntelliJ-based IDEs).

License

Apache License 2.0.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.1

  • Vendor metadata now matches the Marketplace vendor profile (me-tool), so the IDE plugin manager and the Marketplace page show the same publisher.

0.1.0

  • First public release.
  • Toolbar action in the commit message box that turns the checked files into a subject line plus an itemized body, with a replace / append / cancel preview.
  • Local, deterministic grouping with an optional LLM rewriting step (OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini) and automatic fallback to the local result.
  • Output format and prompt templates, with presets.
  • .gitmessage / git config commit.template used as the output skeleton.
  • {issue} injection from the branch name or recent commits.
  • Changelog and PR description generation (copy only).
  • Chinese and English output.

idea-plugin.name: OpenCode Buddy
idea-plugin.description:
GUI for OpenCode inside your IDE - MIT 100% Open Source

IDE 内的 OpenCode 可视化 GUI · MIT 100% 开源

OpenCode Buddy 为 opencode（开源 AI 编程代理）提供原生 JetBrains IDE 体验： 通过本地 opencode serve 服务与 @opencode-ai/sdk 通信， 无需额外云端中转，配置与凭证完全由本机 opencode CLI 本地管理。

OpenCode Buddy provides a native JetBrains IDE experience for opencode (open-source AI coding agent): communicates via local opencode serve service and @opencode-ai/sdk, no cloud relay needed — all config and credentials are managed locally by the opencode CLI.

核心功能 / Features

  • 多标签多会话 / Multi-Tab Sessions：支持多个会话标签页并发独立运行，支持标签重命名、独立浮动窗口与实时回答状态指示 / Supports multiple concurrent independent session tabs with renaming, floating windows, and real-time status indicators
  • 持久化守护进程 / Persistent Daemon：自动启动或复用本地 opencode serve 常驻服务，支持心跳保活与崩溃自愈 / Auto-starts or reuses local opencode serve service with heartbeat keep-alive and crash recovery
  • 完整交互界面 / Full Interactive UI：流式响应输出、深度思考折叠增量展示、工具调用卡片与内-inline 代码 Diff 对比 / Streaming responses, collapsible thinking display, tool call cards, and inline code diff comparison
  • 原生输入感知 / Native Input Awareness：@ 文件智能补全引用、图片及多模态附件拖拽/粘贴、/ 原生斜杠命令、! / $ 终端命令执行 / @ file autocomplete, image/multimodal paste, / slash commands, ! / $ terminal commands
  • Agent / 模型 / 推理配置 / Agent / Model / Reasoning Config：Build / Plan 模式切换、支持 opencode 配置的全部 Provider + Model、自定义模型添加、推理力度（Reasoning Effort）与 Always Thinking 切换 / Build / Plan mode switch, all Provider + Model support, custom model add, Reasoning Effort and Always Thinking toggle
  • 会话管理与导出 / Session Management & Export：会话全文搜索、消息撤销重试、历史回退（Revert）、会话分支（Fork）、上下文压缩（Compact）、一键导出 Markdown 会话文档、OpenCode Share 链接分享 / Full-text search, undo/retry, revert, fork, compact, export Markdown, OpenCode Share link
  • 交互审批流程 / Interactive Approval：文件编辑与命令执行权限审批（Once / Always / Reject）、Ask User Question 表单交互提问、Plan 计划审批 / File edit and command execution approval (Once / Always / Reject), Ask User Question form, Plan approval
  • MCP 市场与技能 / MCP Marketplace & Skills：MCP 服务器状态监控、MCP 市场一键搜索/安装/卸载/配置、Skill 技能扩展管理 / MCP server monitoring, one-click search/install/uninstall/configure, Skill extension management
  • Token 用量与看板 / Token Usage & Dashboard：实时 Token 消耗指示器、模型上下文窗口占用百分比、上下文分解详情与内置 TokenTracker 统计看板 / Real-time token usage indicator, context window percentage, context breakdown and built-in TokenTracker dashboard
  • 深度 IDE 融合 / Deep IDE Integration：明暗主题自适应跟随 IDE、IDE 编辑器与界面字体同步、状态栏小组件、中英双语界面切换 / Light/dark theme sync, editor & UI font sync, status bar widget, bilingual interface toggle

使用方法 / Getting Started

  • 从右侧边栏打开 OpenCode 工具窗口（需已安装 opencode CLI） / Open the OpenCode tool window from the right sidebar (requires opencode CLI installed)
  • 插件会自动启动或复用本地 opencode serve 服务（默认端口 4096，可用 OPENCODE_PORT 覆盖） / Plugin auto-starts or reuses local opencode serve service (default port 4096, override with OPENCODE_PORT)

关键词 / Keywords: OpenCode, opencode-buddy, AI 编程 / AI Coding, 代码生成 / Code Generation, Agent/智能体, 多标签 / Multi-Tab, MCP, TokenTracker/Token统计
idea-plugin.change-notes:
中文：


OpenCode Buddy — opencode 专属改造版本。


  • 插件更名 OpenCode Buddy：插件 ID com.senjuobito.opencode-buddy，Java 包名 com.opencodebuddy，工具窗口 ID OpenCode。
  • 移除全部多引擎支持（Claude Agent SDK / Codex / Grok / Kimi / Pi / OMP / DSH / cc-switch 供应商管理）。
  • opencode 链路升级为常驻 ai-bridge daemon + opencode serve (4096) + @opencode-ai/sdk v2 + SSE 事件流，替代每消息 spawn CLI。
  • 会话历史改为本地索引 + daemon session.messages API；新增 /revert、/fork、compact、MCP 状态、question 审批。
  • @opencode-ai/sdk 随插件打包，不再需要按需安装 SDK。
  • 设置目录 ~/.codemoss → ~/.opencodebuddy。

English：


OpenCode Buddy — an opencode-only build of the plugin.


  • Renamed to OpenCode Buddy: plugin id com.senjuobito.opencode-buddy, Java package com.opencodebuddy, tool window id OpenCode.
  • Removed every non-opencode engine (Claude Agent SDK / Codex / Grok / Kimi / Pi / OMP / DSH / cc-switch provider management).
  • The opencode pipeline now runs a persistent ai-bridge daemon + opencode serve (4096) + @opencode-ai/sdk v2 + SSE event stream instead of spawning the CLI per message.
  • Session history now uses a local index + the daemon session.messages API; added /revert, /fork, compact, MCP status and question approval.
  • @opencode-ai/sdk ships with the plugin, so the SDK no longer has to be installed on demand.
  • Settings directory ~/.codemoss → ~/.opencodebuddy.

idea-plugin.name: Overview Diff
idea-plugin.description:
Review coding agent changes faster in Java/Kotlin projects.

Overview Diff shows changed declarations instead of only changed text lines. Review fields, methods, constructors, and classes in a compact tree, then open IntelliJ IDEA's standard side-by-side diff for the selected change.

  • Compare HEAD with local changes.
  • Compare one commit with the working tree or two commits from the Git Log.
  • Double-click a changed file or declaration to open IntelliJ IDEA's standard side-by-side diff.

Public Beta: Java support is ready for everyday use. Kotlin support is experimental. This beta expires after December 31, 2026.

Requires IntelliJ IDEA 2022.3 or later.

Homepage
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.1

Public Beta

  • Structural Git diffs for Java and experimental Kotlin support.
  • Compare local changes and revisions selected in the Git Log.

idea-plugin.name: MCP Debugger
idea-plugin.description:
Postman-style console for MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, inside your IDE.

Point MCP Debugger at a local stdio server (npx / uvx / docker / a plain executable) or a remote HTTP / SSE endpoint. It performs the full MCP handshake, discovers every tool, resource and prompt, and gives you a schema-generated argument template to call any of them with — no client code, no restart, no guessing.

Highlights

  • Three transports — stdio (child process), Streamable HTTP and the legacy HTTP+SSE. Session ids, protocol version negotiation and capabilities are all handled for you.
  • Auto-discovery — the whole tool list comes from tools/list (including cursor pagination). Resources and prompts land in the same tree, and a tools/list_changed notification refreshes it live.
  • Arguments as JSON, prefilled — picking a tool fills the JSON tab with a template generated from its schema: every declared parameter is listed, defaults are already in place, and $ref / allOf are resolved. Edit the values you care about, delete the rest, press Ctrl+Enter. The raw tool definition (annotations, output schema) is one tab away.
  • Call history — every call is kept per tool as a card carrying a single line: outcome, time and duration. The arguments and the response preview live in the hover tooltip, and a Call again button on the card re-sends that exact request at once. Repeating a call with one value changed takes a click instead of retyping.
  • Request headers on two levels — server-level headers (the entry sits in the toolbar, so it stays reachable while disconnected) ride on every request, the initialize handshake and the SSE connection included. Per-tool headers live on a tab of each tool, ride only on that tool's tools/call, and win on a name clash. Both are filled in as a form, not raw JSON: the name column offers the common headers in a drop-down, and sensitive values can be masked.
  • Self-healing connections — a dropped SSE long connection no longer wipes the tool list: the catalog stays on screen, marked as disconnected, while the plugin reconnects on an exponential backoff.
  • Filter and search — a search box above the catalog narrows tools, resources and prompts down as you type, matching names and descriptions. The wire log has its own keyword box, kind filter and a follow-tail toggle.
  • Cancel a running call — abandon a slow tool call without waiting for the timeout. It stops waiting for the response and is reported as a neutral "cancelled", not a failure.
  • Results, verbatim — the JSON-RPC result is shown as-is, in a highlighted, scrollable editor, with one copy button and the round-trip time next to the status. The Export menu saves it to a file, or copies a curl / Python snippet that replays the same call from a terminal.
  • Wire-level console — every request, response, notification and stderr line is logged with direction and timing, which is what you need when a server misbehaves.
  • Import existing configs — paste or import the familiar mcpServers JSON from Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code or a project .mcp.json; MCP Debugger also scans your project for them.
  • English and Chinese UI — follows the IDE's own language out of the box, with a one-click switch in the toolbar and a Follow IDE language reset.

中文说明

把 MCP（Model Context Protocol）调试台装进 IDE：填一个本地 stdio 命令 （npx / uvx / docker 或任意可执行文件）或远端 HTTP / SSE 地址，插件自动完成 MCP 握手、拉取全部工具并列出，点开任意工具即可填参数调用。

  • 三种传输：stdio（子进程）、Streamable HTTP、旧版 HTTP+SSE；会话 id、协议版本协商、 能力声明全部自动处理。
  • 自动获取工具：工具列表来自 tools/list（含游标翻页），资源与提示词一并列出； 服务端发 tools/list_changed 通知时自动刷新。
  • 参数直接写 JSON，进来就有模板：选中工具即按其 JSON Schema 生成一份参数模板——声明的每个 参数都在，默认值已填好，$ref 与 allOf 会被展开。改掉关心的几个值、 删掉多余的字段，Ctrl+Enter 调用；工具原始定义（annotations、输出 schema）就在隔壁页签。
  • 调用历史：每个工具的每次调用都留档成一张卡片，一行写清状态、时刻、耗时；入参与 响应预览放在悬停气泡里，卡片上的「重新调用」直接把这一份再发一次。
  • 请求头分两级：服务器级（入口在工具栏，没连上时也够得着）带在所有请求上，含 initialize 握手与 SSE 建连；工具级在各自工具的页签里，只作用于该工具的 tools/call，同名键覆盖服务器级。两级都按表单填写而不是手写 JSON： 键那一列可从下拉里挑常用头，值可一键打码。
  • 断连自愈：SSE 长连接被掐断后工具列表不再消失（照常显示、标记为已断开）， 插件按退避自动重连。
  • 过滤与搜索：目录树上方的搜索框边打字边收窄工具 / 资源 / 提示词，名字与描述一起匹配； 底部报文日志也有自己的关键词框、类别过滤与「跟随最新」开关。
  • 可取消的调用：慢工具不用再干等超时——点「取消」即不再等这个响应， 并如实显示为中性色的「已取消」，而不是一次失败。
  • 结果原样呈现：调用结果直接显示为 JSON（语法高亮、可滚动），一个「复制」按钮拿走同一份 内容，调用耗时显示在状态旁边；「导出」菜单可存成文件，或复制一段 curl / Python 片段， 在终端里复现同一次调用。
  • 报文级日志：请求、响应、通知、子进程 stderr 全部按方向与时间落盘到控制台， 排查服务端问题时最有用。
  • 导入现成配置：粘贴或导入 Claude Desktop / Cursor / VS Code 的 mcpServers JSON，插件也会自动扫描你工程里的 MCP 配置文件。
  • 中英双语界面：默认跟随 IDE 自身语言，工具栏可一键切换， 「管理」菜单末尾的「跟随 IDE 语言」一键还原。
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.0
  • New: filter the catalog tree. A search box above the tree narrows tools, resources and prompts down as you type, matching the name and the description — "which tool can read a file" is answerable without reading the whole list. The filter only affects what the tree shows; the catalog snapshot behind it is untouched, so clearing the box brings everything back at once.
  • New: cancel a running call. The result area now offers Cancel while a call is in flight. It stops waiting for the response rather than retracting the request — the server may well still be running the tool — and the outcome is shown as a neutral "cancelled", not a red failure. A cancelled call is not written to the history.
  • New: search and filter the wire log. The log gained a second row: a keyword box plus a kind filter (sent / received / notes / errors), and a Follow toggle. Turn Follow off and new messages stop pulling the view to the bottom while you read back through what already happened.
  • New: export the result. The result strip carries an Export menu: save the JSON to a file, or copy a curl / Python snippet that replays this exact call from a terminal. Header values whose name looks like a token or a key are masked in the snippet.
  • The selection now survives a catalog refresh and a reconnect: the tree restores it by name instead of jumping back to the first tool — and it does so silently, without resetting the arguments you were editing.
  • Splitter positions are remembered for every divider, not just the catalog / detail one: the argument / result divider, the resource panel and the prompt panel keep their proportions across restarts too.
  • New: an optional confirmation before destructive tools. Turn it on under Manage and every call to a tool marked destructive asks first — the "Call again" button in the history included. Off by default: while debugging, the same tool gets called a dozen times in a row, and a prompt you always dismiss protects nothing.
  • A batch of smaller things. The catalog filter is now cleared when you switch servers (a leftover keyword used to silently filter the new server's tree down to nothing) and group headers read 3 / 12 while it is active; both search boxes clear on Esc; missing required arguments are confirmed before sending; a result that lands just as you press Cancel is still shown instead of being discarded; the result strip reports the response size; the log can be exported to a file; and the Follow toggle switches itself back on when you scroll to the bottom.
1.0.5
  • New: request headers on two levels, filled in as a form. Server-level headers now have their own entry in the toolbar, next to the server drop-down, and ride on every request — initialize and the SSE connection included. It stays reachable while disconnected, which is exactly when a server that needs a token needs it, and the dialog can test the connection with the values you have not saved yet. Per-tool headers are a new tab on each tool: they ride only on that tool's tools/call and win over the server-level ones on a name clash. Neither level is hand-written JSON any more — the name column offers the common headers in a drop-down, an empty row is simply ignored, and values whose name looks like a token or a key can be masked.
  • New: the history list is card-based. Each call is one card carrying a single line — outcome, time and duration — with a Call again button that re-sends that exact request at once. The arguments and the response preview moved into the hover tooltip, which is now the only place they can be read; the response is recorded too, so two calls with identical arguments can still be told apart (one timed out, the other went through). The outcome is carried by a colour bar on the left rather than by the colour of the text, which keeps it readable on a selected row.
  • The request-header form got taller inputs — 28px against the 22px the parameter fields use. The name column eats into the row there, so the value field can use the extra height.
  • Export keeps the standard fields (command / url / headers) clean and writes per-tool headers into an _mcpDebugger extension, so the same JSON still works in other clients.
  • Fixed: a dropped SSE connection forced a failing reconnect, and took the tool list with it. Three causes, all fixed: the transport called itself alive as long as it had ever seen an endpoint (a closed long connection left that field behind), the session layer only checked "was it closed" (so it handed the dead session straight back, failing every request without sending one), and the SSE start() was not re-entrant (a reconnect posted initialize to the previous session's endpoint).
  • New: the tool list survives a disconnect, and the plugin reconnects on its own. The last successful catalog is kept per session, so the tree stays on screen (marked disconnected) instead of going blank; reconnects are retried on a backoff of 1s → 2s → 4s → 8s → 16s → 30s and stop after six failures. A manual Connect / Disconnect or a server switch cancels a queued retry.
1.0.4
  • New: English and Chinese UI. Every label, tooltip, dialog button and error message now has both wordings. By default the plugin follows the IDE's own UI language — nothing to configure; the toolbar carries a one-click switch, and Follow IDE language (last item in the Manage menu) hands control back to the IDE.
  • The switch re-labels the live tool window in place: tree expansion, selection, scroll position, splitter sizes and whatever you have already typed stay exactly as they were.
  • Copy trimmed throughout — repeated navigation hints, and the overlap between the empty-state guidance, the history tooltips and the security notes, are now one clear sentence each.
  • Fixed: toggling the language walked the toolbar's action group by hand, which newer IDEs reject outright (Do not call getChildren(null)) — the switch itself threw.
  • Fixed: a few labels kept the old language after a switch — the JSON and Definition tab titles (they were looked up by the editor instead of the tab's actual component, so the rename silently did nothing), the server dialog's Cancel button, and the Yes/No/OK buttons of the platform confirmation dialogs, which follow the IDE's language rather than the plugin's and now carry our own labels.
1.0.3
  • New: call history. Every call keeps the exact arguments that were sent — success, tool-reported error and transport failure alike (the failed ones are usually the ones worth reusing). One click on an entry writes those arguments back into the JSON tab and switches to it, ready to re-send with Ctrl+Enter; Ctrl+Z restores whatever was there before.
  • Repeating a call with the same arguments refreshes the newest entry instead of stacking duplicates. History is kept per server + tool (20 entries each, 400 in total) and is cleared together with the server it belongs to.
  • Fixed: the history list showed up as an empty area — its cell renderer built the two text labels but never attached them to the row, so every row had the right height and nothing in it.
  • Fixed: the tool detail panel was never registered as a disposable, so closing and reopening the tool window leaked one live instance (result timer + message-bus subscriptions) each time.
1.0.2
  • Request headers (a bearer token, and anything else the endpoint needs) sit in their own tab next to the arguments, so they can be edited without going back into the server dialog. Applies to http / sse servers; changes take effect on the next request.
1.0.0
  • First public release.
  • Connect to MCP servers over stdio, Streamable HTTP and HTTP+SSE.
  • Discover and call tools with a schema-generated argument template, or raw JSON.
  • Browse resources and prompts; read resources and render prompts.
  • Wire-level console with request/response/stderr logging.
  • Import mcpServers JSON and scan the project for MCP config files.

idea-plugin.name: Preflight
idea-plugin.description:
Preflight is your personal local code reviewing tool

In my current workflow, I am constantly reviewing code generated by AI agents. But reviewing the code without pushing it to a remote repo and having a PR is kind of a pain. You have to leave comments in the code you have to remove later, or you have to write everything into a promt.

This is why I created Preflight, a local code review tool.

The comments are stored into a local JSON file your agent can read and respond to. No push needed.

Leave comments directly in your editor without touching your code

  • Mark any line or block of code
  • Annotate it with your thoughts, questions or concerns
  • Reply to annotations, mark them as resolved
  • Everything is saved locally as JSON, no server, no cloud, no account
    Your codebase stays clean.

Currently there is no agent plugin, I use this prompt:

you got a new review in .preflight/comments.json, the format is
[
  {
    "id": "UUID",
    "file": "FILEPATH",
    "line": INT,
    "startLine": INT,
    "anchorText": "THE COMMENTED CODE",
    "comment": "REVIEWER COMMENT",
    "resolved": false,
    "replies": [
	    {"author":"user", "text":"the comment"}
    ],
    "author": "AGENT" 
  }
]
line/startLine are 0-based line numbers of the last/first commented line (a single line comment has
startLine == line). anchorText is the exact text of those lines. Always refer to a comment by its id.
please solve the review commands, if you think the comment is wrong answer in the replies.
Replies is a list of replies {"text" :"THE TEXT", "author": "author"} use author AGENT.
When you solved the comments reply with "solved", do not set the resolved property.

line/startLine are kept in sync by the IDE while the file is open there, but they can be a bit off
(unsaved editor changes, edits made while the file was closed). Before you rely on them, check that
the lines at startLine..line still match anchorText. If they don't, search the file for anchorText
and use that position; if it is gone, the reviewed code was probably changed, so use the comment
text to find the right place.

Whenever you insert or delete lines in a file that has comments (also when you are not solving them),
move the comments of that file along: update line and startLine so that the lines at
startLine..line are still the ones in anchorText. If the commented code itself changed, update
anchorText to the new text of those lines. Never touch comments of other files.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Initial scaffold created from IntelliJ Platform Plugin Template

idea-plugin.name: Github Copilot sessions
idea-plugin.description:
Export and import GitHub Copilot chat sessions.
The plugin reads the local Copilot storage (~/.copilot/session-store.db and ~/.copilot/session-state) and the session record the GitHub Copilot plugin keeps inside the IDE, lets you pick the conversations you want to move and writes them into a portable ZIP archive. The same archive can be imported back on another machine or after a workstation reset, restoring the conversation turns, the checkpoints, the session workspace files and the entry shown in the chat history.
  • Tools | Github Copilot sessions | Export Sessions... pick one or more sessions and save the archive.
  • Tools | Github Copilot sessions | Import Sessions... pick an archive and choose which sessions to restore.

Special thanks

A heartfelt thank you to my colleague and dear friend Antonio Petricca, who has followed this plugin since its very early stages: his suggestions shaped the design choices, and his field testing brought to light issues that no unit test would ever have detected. Thank you for the time and care you dedicated to it.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
[1.0.2] - 2026-09-18

Added

  • The Tools menu entries follow the language of the machine. The Github Copilot sessions submenu and both actions now take their title and description from the plugin bundle, like every dialog already did, instead of always showing English; the nine translations were extended accordingly. The notification group shown in Settings | Appearance & Behavior | Notifications is localized too.

Changed

  • The import dialog no longer queries the database once per archived session. The ids already present on the machine are collected with one database read and one directory listing, together with the manifest and under the same progress indicator, instead of opening two SQLite connections per session on the UI thread while the dialog was being built.
  • One less internal IntelliJ Platform API usage. The Restart IDE now notification action uses the public Application.restart() instead of the internal ApplicationEx variant. The IDE may now ask for confirmation before closing, which is the standard behaviour of such an action.
  • Failures of the GitHub Copilot bridge reach idea.log. Reflection errors were only recorded in the import log, which is not written at all during an export; they are now also reported through the platform logger.
  • Cancelling a progress is no longer reported as an error. ProcessCanceledException is re-thrown instead of being turned into an error dialog.
  • The import log is entirely in English. The section titles were the only Italian text left in it.

Removed

  • Dead code. WorkspaceYaml.rewriteId, superseded by WorkspaceYaml.rewrite.

idea-plugin.name: Mario AI Debug Assistant
idea-plugin.description:
Investigate bugs using the current editor selection, stack traces, Git changes, and optional Loki logs.

  • Analyze evidence with DeepSeek, OpenAI, Ollama, or a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
  • Navigate to code referenced in a stack trace and review AI-generated unified diffs before applying them.
  • Keep API credentials in the IDE Password Safe.

AI requests are initiated by the user and require confirmation before code or logs are sent to the configured provider. No account or telemetry service is operated by this plugin.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Initial release: AI-assisted bug analysis, optional Loki log context, model discovery, and reviewed patch application.

idea-plugin.name: Tokitoki Coding Time Tracker
idea-plugin.description:
Automatic coding time tracking and AI usage & token cost tracking for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor and more, on one Tokitoki dashboard. An open-source WakaTime alternative.

Automatic time tracking. Just code. Tokitoki records which files, projects and languages you work in, including debugging and code review time. No timers to start, no forms to fill.

AI usage analytics. Your local AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Gemini, Amp, Goose, OpenCode and more) are scanned and synced automatically, so tokens, models and costs show up next to your coding time.

Today in the status bar. Active time for the project you have open, from the same figure the dashboard shows, on every machine with the same key.

Works offline. Activity is queued locally and uploaded when you are back online.

Only metadata leaves your machine: paths, project names, timestamps, token counts. Never your code. Open source, Apache-2.0.
idea-plugin.change-notes: • Compatible with IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2 and 2026.3 without warnings: the project selector and the message bundle no longer use platform APIs that are deprecated or scheduled for removal.

idea-plugin.name: AI Relay
idea-plugin.description:
AI Relay — Claude, Gemini and Copilot as coding agents in your IDE

One chat panel, three agents, over the whole project: Claude through the Claude Code CLI you are already signed in to, Gemini through the Gemini API, Vertex AI or an Apigee gateway, and Microsoft Copilot through your own signed-in web session. Pick the agent from a dropdown; everything else is the same.

Highlights

  • Agents, not autocomplete — they read, search, edit and run commands across the project
  • Streaming transcript with live tool activity and expandable output
  • Permissions — confirm each tool, accept edits automatically, or let it run
  • Editor-aware — include the current selection with one checkbox
  • Web access and Maven Central lookups so answers about versions are checked, not guessed
  • MCP servers in the same mcpServers file shape as Claude Desktop
  • Nothing to install — the agent runtime is bundled and runs on the IDE's own Java

idea-plugin.name: OliCoder
idea-plugin.description:
OliCoder is an AI coding assistant that lives in your IDE's side panel. Chat with the model of your choice, point it at your project with @, and let it read, search and edit your code, with a diff and one-click undo for every change. Bring your own API key: no subscription, no account, no middleman.

Highlights

  • Bring your own model: OpenAI-compatible APIs (OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, Zhipu GLM, MiniMax, SiliconFlow, Doubao and any custom or proxy endpoint), Anthropic Claude and Google Gemini. Keep several models configured and switch per conversation.
  • Craft, Ask and Plan modes: Craft edits your files directly, Ask answers questions without touching anything, Plan helps you break down requirements before you build.
  • Understands your whole project: the assistant can search and read project files on its own, so you do not have to paste code. Use @ to attach specific files, or drop in screenshots and images.
  • Edits you can trust: watch changed lines appear live while the model writes, review every change in the IDE diff viewer (before and after), then Keep or Revert in one click. Risky edits, such as a reply that looks truncated, are held back for your confirmation instead of overwriting your code.
  • Terminal commands with your approval: the assistant can propose shell commands, but nothing runs until you approve it, and dangerous commands are flagged.
  • Multilingual interface: switch the UI language at any time from the globe icon in the panel header. Available in English, 简体中文, 日本語, 한국어, Deutsch, Français and हिन्दी.
  • Built for daily use: multiple chat tabs, searchable history that survives restarts, streaming replies with a visible thinking process, stop, regenerate, continue and edit-and-resend.
  • Private by design: API keys are kept in the IDE's secure credential storage on your machine and are never sent anywhere except to the model provider you configure.

Getting started

  1. Open the OliCoder tool window on the right-hand side of the IDE.
  2. Click Configure custom model, choose a protocol, enter the base URL, model name and your API key, then save.
  3. Pick Craft, Ask or Plan and start chatting. Type @ to add files as context.

OliCoder needs an IDE with the embedded browser (JCEF), which is included in the standard JetBrains distributions. Your model provider's usage fees apply; OliCoder itself does not add any.

Website: olicoder.com

idea-plugin.name: Claude Session Auto-Title
idea-plugin.description:
Names your Claude Code threads after the software you are building, automatically.

Claude Code generates a topic title for each conversation, and that title changes as the conversation goes on. This plugin pins the title to the project instead, so a list of past sessions reads like a list of your projects.

Quick start — 4 steps

  1. Install this plugin and make sure Claude Code is installed.
  2. Open Settings → Tools → Claude Session Auto-Title.
  3. Press Enable / Repair once.
  4. Use Claude Code normally. New sessions are titled from the project automatically.

You do not need to reopen the settings page for each session.

How the name is chosen

  1. .claude/session-name, if you set a name in Settings
  2. The name the app declares about itself — the <title> of index.html, the first heading of README.md or DESIGN.md, or name in package.json
  3. The repository directory name
  4. If none of those are found, nothing is set and Claude Code's own title is left alone

What it does to your machine

With your confirmation, it copies a small hook into ~/.claude/hooks/ and registers it in ~/.claude/settings.json under SessionStart. Your settings file is backed up before any change, and if it cannot be parsed nothing is changed at all. You can remove the registration from Settings at any time.

A name you set yourself is never taken away. If a session was named with --name or /rename, the hook leaves it alone.

No network access, no telemetry. Everything is read and written on your machine.

Requires Claude Code to be installed.

  • First release.

idea-plugin.name: ZCode Web
idea-plugin.description:
ZCode Web brings your local ZCode (zai-org/ZCode) chat workspace into a PhpStorm tool window. Drag files or folders from the IDE into the chat input, or select code in the editor and confirm on the hover bar - both instantly become rich references in the message and are sent with full paths.

ZCode Web

在 PhpStorm 工具窗中嵌入本机 ZCode 网页工作台（开发模式默认 localhost:5173）， 对话界面与交互完全沿用网页端（消息/模型/设置/审批），并补充 IDE 集成： 拖入文件/代码到输入框、当前项目文件夹自动定位、ZCode Web 服务自动启动与开关。

功能

  • 拖动文件、选中代码，一键进入对话：从 IDE 拖动任意文件/文件夹到输入框， 或选中代码后点选选区上方的「添加到对话」浮条——两者都立即生成带文件图标的 彩色引用 chip（正面显示文件名，与拖入文件一致），选中代码的行号随消息一并发送（引用带 文件名:起-止 与路径），AI 收到的是磁盘真实路径与行号
  • 嵌入式网页对话界面：与本机 ZCode Web 完全一致（对话窗工作区固定为当前文件夹、不再弹切换菜单；添加工作区入口隐藏；收起侧边栏时 rail 额外精简搜索图标——新建会话与设置等保留，专注对话；展开侧边栏时搜索等功能完整）
  • 文件/代码引用显示为网页原生彩色 chip（带文件图标与文件名；选中代码的行号写进随消息发送的引用、不在 chip 正面），chip 之间可直接 输入描述文字、随光标删除/回车换行，多个引用可并存于一段消息中；鼠标悬浮 chip 出现 ×，点击一键移除该引用（编辑器对应选区同步清空）
  • 选中代码 hover 确认：编辑器选中代码并稳定片刻后，选区上方弹出「添加到对话」 浮条，点击才把引用写入输入框——仅浏览/复制不再误添加；发送时页面把 chip 序列化为 完整路径:行号，AI 收到的始终是全路径，消息发出后编辑器选区自动清除
  • 降级兼容：若页面结构异常无法挂载 chip，自动退回文本引用通道（光标处 [[文件名:行号]] 标记 + 发送原位展开），任何页面版本下选中/拖入/发送均可靠
  • 工作区：自动定位当前项目文件夹并置顶，列表只显示当前文件夹（UI 层过滤）
  • ZCode Web 服务：未运行时自动启动（默认 pnpm dev:web），顶栏按钮显示状态并可手动关闭； 设置项可清空保存（三项全空 = 未配置），未配置时工具窗内显示下载安装引导与教程，不再自动探测/启动

idea-plugin.name: Copy Files for AI Prompts
idea-plugin.description:
Copies the files you select into one AI-ready prompt, with a token count. Select files and folders in the Project view, right-click, and choose Copy for AI. The whole selection lands on your clipboard as one block, with every file under a ===== path/to/file ===== header so the model can tell the files apart. Paste it into any AI chat that takes text. A file selected together with its folder is copied once.

The copying is the easy part. What breaks a prompt is what rides along unnoticed: a binary file that pastes as thousands of garbage characters, a 4 MB generated file, a node_modules folder — or a selection that was already over the model's context window before you pressed Enter. This plugin is built around those failures.

An estimated token count, before you paste
The notification shows the size of the selection in tokens at copy time, not after the model has refused or truncated it. The estimate is about four characters per token, which is typical for English text and code.

Binary content is left out, even with a text extension
Besides the IDE's own file type, the plugin reads the first 8 KB of every file and leaves it out if it contains a NUL byte. That catches files whose extension says text but whose content is binary, such as a data.txt that is really an export.

Size limits
Files larger than 1 MB are left out, so one generated bundle or lock file cannot swallow the prompt. The whole copy stops at about 8 MB and says so, so selecting a very large folder cannot exhaust the IDE's memory. Files are read in the background and the work pauses whenever you type, so the IDE stays responsive. The progress bar has a cancel button.

You are told what was left out
The notification names the files and folders that were skipped and says why: binary or unreadable, over 1 MB, over the total limit, an excluded folder, or a folder whose contents could not be read (for example, no permission). Up to five names are listed per reason, followed by a count of the rest. A model that answers confidently about code it never received is worse than one that says nothing, and silent omissions are how that happens.

Unsaved changes are included
If a file is open with edits you have not saved yet, the copy contains what you see in the editor, not the older version on disk.

Folders that are always skipped
.git, node_modules, build, out, target, dist, vendor, .gradle, .idea, .venv, venv, __pycache__, .next, .nuxt, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache and .tox, as well as symbolic links to folders.

Keyboard shortcut
None is assigned by default, so no existing shortcut is taken over. To add one, open Settings | Keymap and search for "Copy for AI".

Typical uses

  • Give a model the three files that matter for a bug report.
  • Ask for a review of the files changed on a feature branch.
  • Hand over a whole small module before a refactor or a framework migration.

Works in
IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, PhpStorm, GoLand, RubyMine, CLion and Android Studio, build 252 and later. Checked with the JetBrains Plugin Verifier against IntelliJ IDEA 2025.2, 2025.3, 2026.1, 2026.2 and the 2026.3 EAP.

No account with us or with any AI provider and no API key. The plugin itself makes no network connections: it reads the files you selected and writes them to your clipboard, and what you paste into an AI chat is up to you. If an error occurs inside the plugin, the IDE may offer to send an error report to JetBrains Marketplace (or sends it automatically if you turned on automatic error reporting in the IDE). For the failures the plugin detects itself, the error text is removed first, so that such a report holds the kind of error and where in the plugin's code it happened, not file contents or file names.

Every feature is available during the free trial — nothing is held back for the paid version. Try it on the repository you actually work in, and decide then.

An annual subscription includes a perpetual fallback license, so you keep a working version even if you stop subscribing.

Documentation: gramshift.com/plugins · Issues: github.com/gramshiftofficial/jetbrains-plugins · Support: gramshift.official@gmail.com
idea-plugin.change-notes:

Fixed: a file partly locked by another program (such as a log file being written) stopped the whole copy with an IDE error. It is now listed as unreadable and the other files are copied.

Fixed: a file selected together with its folder was copied twice.

Errors inside the plugin can now be sent to the developer through the IDE's error reporting.

idea-plugin.name: CallTrail
idea-plugin.description:
CallTrail shows the call hierarchy of the element below the caret as an interactive graph in a popup: up to three caller levels above the element and up to three callee levels below it, taken from the same call hierarchy as Navigate | Call Hierarchy.

Open it from the editor context menu (Call Graph…) on the element: right-click, pick the action, and the popup appears where the mouse is.

  • Click a node to focus it — its neighbours stay highlighted, everything else is dimmed. Press Enter (or right-click and Jump to Source) to open its source code without closing the popup.
  • Right-click a node to copy its name, or to copy the whole graph as a Mermaid or a Graphviz DOT diagram for a Markdown document, a pull request or a Graphviz tool.
  • Mouse wheel scrolls, Ctrl+mouse wheel zooms, dragging pans, and Fit scales the whole graph into the popup. The popup can stay pinned next to the editor while you work, and R recomputes the graph.
  • While a graph is being built, the footer reports the scan — what has been expanded, what is still waiting in the queue and how many items per second — so a large hierarchy shows how it converges instead of a spinner that says nothing.
  • Optional AI summaries explain a node in its tooltip: what the function is for, what its parameters and its return value mean, and how its body works. They come from an OpenAI compatible endpoint of your choice, the source of a node is sent to that endpoint only, and nothing is requested while the feature is switched off.

Second screen. The popup is a real window, not an overlay inside the editor: drag it by its title bar onto a second monitor and it stays there while you keep working in the IDE. That is why it does not close when you click outside of it.

Material Theme UI conflicts with this behaviour: while one of its overlays is on it paints a translucent layer over the whole IDE — the IDE looks dimmed — and because that layer sits on the IDE's glass pane it swallows the mouse clicks as well, so the editor stops reacting and Ctrl+Click no longer navigates until the popup is closed. CallTrail turns the two overlay switches of the theme off before the popup is shown and puts them back the way it found them when the popup closes (Settings | Tools | CallTrail, on by default); an IDE without the theme is left untouched. Should the workaround be switched off and an overlay be left behind anyway, the theme has a Clean Overlay action of its own, and its switches can be turned off under Settings | Appearance | Material Theme → uncheck Show Overlays, or with Ctrl+Shift+A → Toggle Overlays / Toggle More Overlays.

Settings (Settings | Tools | CallTrail) configure the number of caller and callee levels, the maximum number of nodes of one graph, whether elements from libraries (the JDK, dependencies, node_modules, …) belong to the graph, whether clicking outside closes the popup, and whether the overlays of the Material Theme UI are turned off while the popup is open.

How CallTrail fetches Call Graphs based on language:

  • Fast Mode:
    • Supported languages: Java, Kotlin, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python.
    • Features: Uses the IDE's optimized, high-speed internal APIs for fast scanning and is backed by end-to-end tests.
    • Tested status: Verified and tested directly by the author for these five languages.
  • Compatibility Mode:
    • Supported languages: Go, C/C++, Rust, C#, PHP, Ruby, and any other language supported by the IDE.
    • Features: Uses the platform's general Call Hierarchy interface (traversing layer by layer makes scan speed noticeably slower). If a language lacks Call Hierarchy support, it gracefully falls back to Find Usages.
    • Tested status: Since the author only has IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm and PyCharm installed, languages requiring other specialized IDEs run via this fallback/compatibility mode without dedicated testing.

Requirements. Any IntelliJ-based IDE 2025.2 or newer — IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, PhpStorm, RubyMine, … The plugin uses the standard API of the IDE and nothing else, so it loads and runs across all IDE products.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Live progress in the footer of the popup while a graph is being built: what has been scanned, what is still queued, and how fast the scan goes.
  • Copy as DOT Diagram in the node context menu, next to the Mermaid export.
  • Turn off Material Theme overlays while the graph popup is open in the settings, on by default.

Changed

  • Graphs of Java, Kotlin, JavaScript, TypeScript and Python are built faster, through the call hierarchy each of those languages provides.
  • The element under the cursor is picked up in more places: inside a function body the graph is built for the declaration around it, in every language.
  • The plugin is called CallTrail, and its actions read Call Graph… and Show Call Graph. An installed copy keeps its settings and its keyboard shortcuts when it updates.
  • The node context menu is down to Jump to Source and the two copy actions.
  • A new icon, with a version for dark themes.

Fixed

  • Material Theme UI no longer dims the IDE and swallows the mouse clicks while a graph is open. The overlays of the theme are turned off for as long as a graph is on the screen, and put back the way they were when it closes.
  • The plugin loads in every IntelliJ based IDE again, PyCharm among them.

Claude Code Terminal Launcher

idea-plugin.name: DeepSeek Agent
idea-plugin.description:
DeepSeek Agent — chat with your project

Embeds chat.deepseek.com into a tool window and bridges it with the IDE. The model can request file reads, targeted edits, writes, directory listings, text searches, and shell commands — the plugin executes them inside the current project and feeds the results back into the chat.

Tools the model can call

  • read_file("path"[, "startLine-endLine"]) — read a file or a line range
  • edit_file("path", "old", "new"[, "all"]) — targeted in-place replacement
  • write_file("path", "content"[, "append"]) — full rewrite or append (capped at 5 MB)
  • list_files("path") — list a directory
  • search_text("needle") — grep across the project
  • bash("command") — run a shell command in the project root

Key features

  • Batch tool calls — multiple tools per turn, all results in one block
  • Auto-throttling, iteration cap, and automatic recovery from rate limits
  • Placeholder filtering on both JS and Kotlin sides
  • System preamble injected into the first message of every new chat

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2025.3 (build 253) or newer
  • Web Browser (JCEF) plugin enabled
  • On Linux/Wayland: add -Dawt.toolkit.name=XToolkit to custom VM options for clipboard support
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Delivery state machine in the injected script: idle | stream | tools | send | verify | cooldown. After each send the script waits verifyMs (3500 ms) for the input to clear and, on failure, enters a cooldown instead of silently losing the message.
  • Automatic recovery from send errors: the script looks for the chat's retry button (findFailedSend) and clicks it, or re-sends the text as a fallback. Failed items are remembered in handledErr so the same error does not loop forever.
  • Adaptive send interval: minInterval starts at minSendInterval (2500 ms), jumps to rlBackoffMs (7000 ms) after a rate limit, and decays by 1000 ms on each successful send.
  • Separate cooldown durations: rlWaitMs (20000 ms) for rate limits and failWaitMs (3000 ms) for non-limit send errors. rlMaxWaits is now 8.
  • window.__dsRetry() for manual recovery from the console.

Changed

  • Tool results are batched again. All [TOOL: ...] calls from one assistant turn are executed together, and their results are sent back as a single message. bash commands still run in parallel with each other; file operations run sequentially.
  • The 1.5 s inter-message delay and completion-order delivery introduced in 1.2.0 are gone along with the streaming sender.
  • Injected script renamed __dsAgentV3 → __dsAgentV4.
  • README brought fully in line with the current code: tool limits, safety notes, __dsSendToKotlin / __dsAgentV4 architecture, and the new auto-loop parameters.

Fixed

  • README.md had been truncated mid-sentence at the end of the System preamble section. The file is now complete and consistent with the current code.
  • README.md no longer advertises features that are not in the codebase: the “Asynchronous tool results” and “Plan mode” sections were removed, and the tool table, safety notes and auto-loop parameters were brought in line with ToolRunner.kt and MyToolWindowFactory.kt.
  • search_text skip-list in the README now also lists .gradle.

Removed

  • “Asynchronous tool results” and “Plan mode” sections from the README.

idea-plugin.name: Driver's Seat
idea-plugin.description:
AI coding agents now write most of the diff, and it is easy to commit code you could not explain. Driver's Seat keeps you in the loop.

It lists every change an AI agent made in your working tree since your last commit, each with the request that led to it and the agent's own stated reason, asks you to confirm you can explain each one, and can stop a commit until the AI-made changes have been reviewed.

Driver's Seat reads the session transcripts Claude Code writes on your machine (~/.claude/projects). No API keys, no LLM calls, nothing leaves your computer.

Free

  • A Driver's Seat tool window with a card for every AI change since your last commit, grouped by file: file and line, your request, the agent's reason, and a before/after snippet
  • "Show diff" against the last commit, and one click to the changed line
  • An "I can explain this change" checklist, saved per project, with a running count: "7 AI changes in 3 files since last commit · 4 explained"
  • Changes that a later edit replaced are marked and not counted
  • Automatic refresh as files and VCS status change; partial commits handled per file

Pro (7-day free trial)

  • Commit gate: when AI changes in the files you are committing have not been explained, the commit stops with "3 of 7 AI changes haven't been explained yet" and lets you review them or commit anyway
  • Explain it back: write one line in your own words per change. The notes are added to the commit message as a "Driver's-Seat-Notes:" block and, optionally, to .drivers-seat/decisions.md in the project

Works in every JetBrains IDE with version control, including free tiers (IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, Rider, PhpStorm, RubyMine, CLion, RustRover, Android Studio).

Driver's Seat is an independent product and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Anthropic. Claude and Claude Code are trademarks of Anthropic, PBC, used here only to describe compatibility.
idea-plugin.change-notes: 1.0.0 — first release: change cards for Claude Code edits with the request and the agent's reason, "I can explain this change" checklist, diff and navigation, automatic refresh; Pro commit gate and "Explain it back" notes for commit messages and a decisions log.

idea-plugin.name: Agent Eyes
idea-plugin.description:
Lets AI coding agents see the IDE, run safe IDE commands, and prove that tests really ran. Agent Eyes adds tools to the IDE's built-in MCP server, so an agent connected to it (any MCP client) can call them.

See the IDE
ide_screenshot saves a PNG of the IDE window, the active editor, or one tool window (for example Run, Problems View or Terminal) and returns the file path, so the agent can look at a dialog, a notification or a test tree instead of guessing. With the whole window, open dialogs are drawn on top as the user sees them, and the capture works even while a dialog is open. The result also lists the open tool windows, dialogs and active file. The image is drawn by the IDE itself: your mouse and keyboard are never used, and the IDE window can stay behind other windows.

Run safe IDE commands
ide_find_actions finds IDE commands by name and returns their ids. ide_invoke_action runs one in the project's active editor and reports whether the IDE accepted it. Only safe commands are allowed: formatting, optimize imports, build, save, sync and build-file reload, navigation, and opening tool windows. Commands that change version-control history, publish, delete or run code are refused (use the IDE's own run and test tools, which ask for confirmation), and while a dialog is open nothing is run: the agent is told which dialog is in the way.

Prove the tests ran
check_test_reports reads JUnit XML reports: Gradle build/test-results, Maven Surefire and Failsafe, and files named like junit*.xml (the usual output of pytest --junitxml or jest-junit); any other report can be passed as a path inside the project. Its first line says PASSED, FAILED, 0 TESTS RAN, all tests skipped, NO TEST REPORTS FOUND, or STALE when source code changed after the newest report, meaning the tests were not re-run after the last edit. Failing tests are listed by name, and report or source folders that could not be opened are named.

Stop sessions from colliding
task_lock_acquire, task_lock_release and task_lock_list give agent sessions on the same computer a named lock for heavy work such as a full build or a plugin verification, so two sessions don't run it at once. Locks expire on their own, so a crashed session cannot block the others forever.

Setup
Enable the MCP server in Settings | Tools | MCP Server and connect your agent there. The Agent Eyes tools then appear in the agent's tool list. Screenshots are saved only in your system temp folder (the newest 50 are kept) and locks in ~/.agent-eyes/locks.

What leaves your computer
The plugin itself makes no network connections. Its tools return their results (screenshot file paths, open windows and dialog titles, open files, IDE action names, test report summaries, lock holders) to the agent you connected, which may send them on to its own service. If an error occurs inside the plugin, the IDE may offer to send an error report to JetBrains Marketplace (or sends it automatically if you turned on automatic error reporting in the IDE). For the failures the plugin detects itself, the error text is removed first, so that such a report holds the kind of error and where in the plugin's code it happened, not file names, report contents or lock names.

Works in
IntelliJ-based IDEs that include the MCP Server plugin, build 252 (2025.2) and later.

Every feature is available during the free trial — nothing is held back for the paid version.

An annual subscription includes a perpetual fallback license, so you keep a working version even if you stop subscribing.

Documentation: gramshift.com/plugins/agent-eyes · Issues: github.com/gramshiftofficial/jetbrains-plugins · Support: gramshift.official@gmail.com
idea-plugin.change-notes:
If a tool cannot do its work because of the computer it runs on (for example, the lock folder cannot be written), the agent now gets the reason instead of an internal error. Unexpected errors can be reported from the IDE.

Fixed: check_test_reports counted the same reports several times when a Windows junction inside the project pointed back into the project or to one of its parent folders.

Fixed: check_test_reports reported 0 tests for reports whose test suites are nested inside other suites, as PHPUnit writes them.

Fixed: check_test_reports silently skipped folders it could not open; they are now named in the result. A path that does not exist is now refused instead of answered with NO TEST REPORTS FOUND.

Fixed: the message shown without a license stated a trial length that did not match the actual trial.

idea-plugin.name: MyCode
idea-plugin.description:
MyCode - a coding assistant that runs in your JetBrains IDE

MyCode —— JetBrains IDE 里的编程助手

模型请求发到你配置的供应商；读文件、改代码、跑命令都在 IDE 进程里完成。

Model requests go to the provider you configure. Reading files, editing code, and running commands all happen inside the IDE process.

开始使用 / Getting started

  1. 在 IDE 右侧打开 MyCode 工具窗口 / Open the MyCode tool window on the right.
  2. 在 设置 → 模型配置 里填一个供应商：协议（openai / anthropic）、地址、密钥、模型名和上下文长度；也可以直接编辑 ~/.mycode/config.json / Configure a provider in Settings → Model Config: protocol, base URL, API key, model names and context length - or edit ~/.mycode/config.json directly.
  3. 在输入框里把引擎选为 MyCode，选好模型，发一条消息 / Pick the MyCode engine in the input box, choose your model, and send a message.
  4. 在编辑器里选中代码，按 Ctrl+Alt+K（macOS 为 Cmd+Alt+K）把选区送进输入框 / Select code in the editor and press Ctrl+Alt+K (Cmd+Alt+K on macOS) to drop it into the input box.

功能 / Features

  • 工具调用：读文件、改代码、搜索、在项目里执行命令
  • 权限控制：每次工具调用前询问，可对单次选择“始终允许”，全局与工作区规则保存在 ~/.mycode/permission/
  • 技能 Skills：~/.mycode/skills/（全局）和 {项目}/.mycode/skills/（仅当前项目）下的 SKILL.md，可在设置里启用或停用
  • 会话管理：历史记录、恢复与搜索，保存在 ~/.mycode/sessions/
  • 上下文压缩：长对话按配置自动压缩，压缩后仍在同一会话里继续
  • 主题：深色 / 浅色，支持跟随 IDE 字体

连接与凭证说明 / Connection & credential disclosure

  • 请求发往何处：请求直接发往你在模型配置里填的 baseUrl，插件不经过任何中转服务器。若没有填地址，则按协议回落到官方端点 https://api.anthropic.com/v1 或 https://api.openai.com/v1。
  • 密钥：API 密钥由你手动填写，保存在本机 ~/.mycode/config.json。插件不会静默扫描磁盘上的凭证。
  • 追踪（默认关闭）：默认不记录任何遥测。只有在 ~/.mycode/config.json 的 tracing 段里显式开启后，才会把运行追踪写入本机文件。
  • 本地数据：配置、权限、技能、会话都保存在 ~/.mycode/ 下。

Requests go directly to the baseUrl you configure; with no base URL set they fall back to the official Anthropic or OpenAI endpoint according to the protocol. The plugin runs no relay server. API keys are entered by you and stored locally in ~/.mycode/config.json - the plugin never silently scans your disk for credentials. Telemetry is off by default: traces are only written to a local file after you explicitly enable the tracing section. Configuration, permissions, skills and sessions all live under ~/.mycode/.

项目 / Project

github.com/zhouxx/MyCode-Jetbrains

Keywords: MyCode, JetBrains, IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, AI Coding Assistant, Coding Agent, Code Generation, OpenAI Compatible, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, Qwen
idea-plugin.change-notes:
English:


🐛 Fixes

  • When several IDEA windows are open, the agent's question opens in the project that asked.

✨ Features

  • Tool permissions add **Accept all**, next to the send button. It approves every tool call: file edits, shell commands, network access, sensitive paths, and dangerous commands. Enabling it asks you to confirm. Deny rules you already configured still block matching calls.
  • In **Auto**, the Permissions page can pick a model that decides whether a tool call is allowed. Leave it unset and the model in the current chat decides. If that model is removed from the list, the chat model is used again.
  • The model menu includes **Model configuration**, which opens the model settings page.
  • A hook that runs before a tool can supply a full replacement input. The tool runs with that input. A later hook that blocks the call discards the replacement.

✨ 新功能

  • 发送按钮旁的工具权限多了**全部接受**。改文件、跑命令、出网、敏感路径和危险命令都会自动同意。开启前会先确认。权限配置里已经写的拒绝规则仍然拦住对应调用。

idea-plugin.name: Model File Inspector
idea-plugin.description:
ML model files are opaque binaries. Model File Inspector opens .safetensors, .gguf, .ckpt and .pth files in a read-only editor and shows what is inside: tensors, shapes, dtypes, parameter counts and header metadata, without writing a script.

Only the header is parsed and tensor data is never loaded, so a 70 GB model opens as quickly as a small one. PyTorch checkpoints are read with a built-in pickle reader that never runs code from the file, and references to functions such as os.system are flagged. Everything happens locally; nothing leaves your computer.

Free

  • Summary: format, file size, tensor count, total parameters (e.g. 7.24 B), dtype mix (e.g. BF16 98%, F32 2%) and, for GGUF, the key model facts: architecture, name, context and embedding length, blocks, attention heads, quantization type, tokenizer and vocabulary size
  • Tensor table: name, dtype, shape, parameters, size and file offset; sortable, with a substring or regex filter
  • Metadata table: every header key and value (safetensors __metadata__, GGUF key/value pairs, non-tensor values in PyTorch checkpoints); large arrays such as vocabularies are summarised and expand to their first 100 items
  • Sharded models: open all shards listed in model.safetensors.index.json as one model
  • Clear messages for truncated or corrupt files, legacy PyTorch files and text .pth files

Pro (7-day free trial)

  • Layer view: tensors grouped by name prefix (model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight) in a collapsible tree, with parameter totals, share and dtype mix per group
  • Compare two model files: tensors only in A, only in B, shape and dtype differences, and the parameter totals of both; also from the Project view with two files selected
  • Export the tensor list and metadata to CSV, JSON or Markdown
  • Memory estimate: approximate RAM/VRAM for the weights as stored and at FP16, INT8 and INT4

Supported: safetensors (single and sharded), GGUF v2 and v3 (all common ggml quantization types including K-quants and IQ types), PyTorch checkpoints saved with torch.save in the zip format (PyTorch 1.6 and later), including PyTorch Lightning .ckpt files.

Independent product. Model File Inspector is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Hugging Face, the ggml/llama.cpp project or PyTorch. Product names are used only to describe file-format compatibility.
idea-plugin.change-notes: 1.0.0 — first release: read-only editor for .safetensors, .gguf, .ckpt and .pth files with summary, tensor table and metadata; sharded safetensors models; safe pickle reader for PyTorch checkpoints; Pro layer view, model comparison, CSV/JSON/Markdown export and memory estimate.

idea-plugin.description:

idea-plugin.name: RefDex
idea-plugin.description:
Give your AI agent a map of your code, and watch it stop reading whole files. 🗺️

RefDex indexes every class, method, function and property in your project and hands that index to your AI agent. Instead of opening a 900-line file to find one method, the agent asks "where is OrderService?", "what's in this file?" or "who calls this?" and gets a short, exact answer. Fewer tokens, sharper answers, and more room in the context window for the work you actually asked for.

How it saves tokens

AI agents learn about your code by reading files. In a big project that means reading lots of code that has nothing to do with the task. RefDex lets them look things up instead:

  • Find a class: get its name, signature, file and line in one answer, instead of searching and opening candidate files.
  • Understand a file: get its outline (imports and signatures, no bodies) instead of the whole file.
  • Read one method: get just that method, fresh from disk, instead of the file around it.
  • Before a change: get every caller, subclass and reference, each with the method it's in.
  • New to a codebase? Get a repo map of the code the rest of the project depends on most, trimmed to a token budget.

For example, a 915-line file costs about 11,000 tokens to read. Its outline costs about 2,600, and a single method about 280. That adds up quickly over a long session:

  • Lower cost, more headroom. Sessions stay under the context limit longer.
  • More focused answers. The context holds the code that matters, not everything near it.
  • Fewer wrong guesses. Signatures, callers and base classes come from parsed code, not from skimming.

And RefDex knows when to step aside. Its tool definitions cost about 1,200 tokens per request, so on a small project, where reading files is cheap anyway, it keeps them switched off. It turns them on once your code is big enough to benefit. The status bar always tells you which applies and why.

Languages

Java, C#, Python and TypeScript (including TSX), with the details big projects need: Java packages, C# namespaces and partial classes, Python packages and src/ layouts, and TypeScript path aliases and barrel files.

AI agents

  • Claude Code: connected in one click, just for you or shared with your team through .mcp.json.
  • Junie: connected in one click through the project's .junie/mcp/mcp.json.
  • GitHub Copilot (agent mode): connected in one click, then restart the IDE.
  • JetBrains AI Assistant: RefDex copies a ready-made config for you to paste into its MCP settings.

Any other agent that speaks the Model Context Protocol (MCP) can use RefDex too.

Why you'll like it

  • Zero fuss. Open a project and RefDex indexes it in the background, without blocking the IDE.
  • Always up to date. When you save a file, only that file is parsed again, in milliseconds.
  • Never stale. Code is read from disk whenever the agent asks, so it always sees what you see.
  • Private. Everything runs on your machine. No code leaves it, and there's no account to create.
  • Nothing else to install. The indexer comes with the plugin.

That's it. Happy coding! 🚀

idea-plugin.name: Agent Bridge
idea-plugin.description:
Ask about your code. Review changes. Stay in IntelliJ.

AI coding chat using your existing accounts
Agent Bridge connects IntelliJ IDEA to your installed Claude Code, OpenAI Codex and GitHub Copilot CLIs.
Free and open source. No JetBrains AI subscription required. A supported provider account is required; provider usage limits and charges apply.
Agent Bridge brings conversations with Claude, OpenAI Codex and GitHub Copilot into IntelliJ IDEA through their installed command-line tools. Use your existing eligible provider account without a JetBrains AI subscription.

Start with the file you are editing, select a method for a focused question, or add files and folders from your project. Read the answer in a compact chat and review supported code suggestions before applying them.

Built around asking and reading

  • Current-file context: include the open editor buffer, including unsaved changes.
  • Chat beside selected code: open a small composer from the editor selection and continue the conversation there.
  • Project context: attach files and folders through IntelliJ’s project picker, or enable a bounded search for related project files.
  • Compact model selection: choose your provider and model in one menu. Codex can load available choices from its CLI; Claude offers familiar model aliases and a custom model option.
  • Reviewable changes: inspect supported suggestions in IntelliJ’s diff view, apply the reviewed proposal, and use Undo. Multi-file proposals apply together.
  • Conversation continuity: continue with recent context or start fresh when switching provider or model.
  • Keyboard first: Enter sends; Shift+Enter inserts a new line.
  • Account controls: sign in, check login or change configuration from the settings gear.

Your CLI, your account

Install at least one supported CLI separately. Agent Bridge launches the provider’s authentication flow and uses that CLI’s account configuration. Claude and Copilot use their CLI sign-in flows; Codex offers browser sign-in and a device-code alternative. Each installation uses that user’s local CLI account or API configuration; no maintainer credentials are bundled. Provider credentials remain managed by the CLI.

No separate JetBrains AI subscription is required. Provider eligibility, subscriptions, usage limits and any API charges still apply. Installing the plugin does not grant free or unlimited model access.

Try a first question

  1. Open a project and a source file, then open the Agent Bridge tool window.
  2. Choose your provider, open the gear and sign in if needed.
  3. Ask: “Explain this file and identify one edge case.”
  4. For a change, ask for a reviewable fix. Use Review changes when a supported proposal appears, inspect the diff, then apply it.

Setup guide · Report a problem · Source code · Data handling

Current scope

This preview targets IntelliJ IDEA 2024.3.2.2 through 2026.2.x (builds 243.23654.189 through 262.*). Its declared dependencies do not require Ultimate features. A working provider CLI and eligible account are required.

Automatic context uses bounded text-based retrieval; it does not upload the entire project. Provider tools may read additional project files under their own policies. Code supplied as context is processed by the selected provider according to its configuration and terms.

Suggestions currently edit existing attached text files. File creation, deletion, renaming, inline ghost-text completion and restoring IDE chat history after restart are not supported. The selected range focuses a question; review the diff to check the actual edit scope.

Agent Bridge is an independent integration, not an official OpenAI, Anthropic, GitHub or JetBrains product.

First shareable preview under the public plugin ID io.github.shbhmrzd.agentbridge.

  • Chat about current files or selected code; attach project files and folders.
  • Use existing Claude, Codex and Copilot CLI accounts with compact provider/model controls.
  • Continue with context or start fresh when switching provider or model.
  • Press Enter to send and Shift+Enter for a new line.
  • Review supported edits in the IDE diff viewer and apply with Undo.

idea-plugin.name: Gitea & Forgejo Pull Requests
idea-plugin.description:
Review, comment on, approve and merge pull requests from your self-hosted Gitea or Forgejo server without leaving the IDE. Browse the pull requests of the current project, open their changes in the IDE diff viewer, leave line comments, approve or request changes, and merge — and let your AI coding agent read the unresolved review comments through the IDE's MCP server.

Pull requests in a tool window
The Gitea PRs tool window lists open, closed or all pull requests of the repository behind the project's git remote. Selecting one shows its description, branches, whether it can be merged, and the review comments that are still unresolved.

Diff and line comments
Open Diff shows every changed file in the IDE diff viewer (merge base on the left, pull request head on the right). Right-click a line and choose Comment on This Line (Gitea/Forgejo) to post a line comment on the new or the old side.

Approve, request changes, merge
Submit a review (comment, approve or request changes) and merge with a merge commit, rebase or squash, using the permissions of your own access token.

For AI agents (MCP)
gitea_pr_unresolved_comments returns the review comments that still need work (file, line, author, text), leaving out resolved comments, dismissed reviews and unsubmitted drafts. gitea_pr_list and gitea_pr_diff give the list of pull requests and a pull request's diff. The agent can only read: approving and merging stay in your hands. These tools are available in IDEs that include the built-in MCP server: enable it in Settings | Tools | MCP Server and connect your agent there.

Setup and security
Enter the server URL and a personal access token in Settings | Tools | Gitea & Forgejo. The token is stored only in the IDE password safe, is sent only in the Authorization header to that server, is never sent to redirects, and is removed from error messages and logs. The plugin talks only to the server you configure. If an error occurs inside the plugin, the IDE may offer to send an error report to JetBrains Marketplace (or sends it automatically if you turned on automatic error reporting in the IDE). The access token is never part of what the plugin writes to the log.

Works with
Self-hosted Gitea servers (API v1; tested with Gitea 1.24) and Forgejo servers, which use the same API, in IntelliJ-based IDEs build 252 (2025.2) and later.

Gitea and Forgejo are names of their respective projects and owners. This plugin is an independent product of GRAMSHIFT and is not affiliated with or endorsed by them.

Documentation: gramshift.com/plugins · Issues: github.com/gramshiftofficial/jetbrains-plugins · Support: gramshift.official@gmail.com
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.1.1: the plugin can now be installed in IDEs that do not include the MCP server (the tools for AI agents are simply not offered there). Unexpected errors can be reported through the IDE error dialog. No changes to how pull requests are listed, reviewed or merged.

2026.1.0: pull request list, diff, line comments, approve, request changes, merge, and MCP tools for AI agents.

idea-plugin.name: XLSX Editor + Agent Reader
idea-plugin.description:
Opens Excel .xlsx files as editable tables inside the IDE, and lets AI coding agents read any cell range of a workbook as CSV. Edit cells, insert and delete rows, switch sheets, undo with Ctrl+Z and save, without leaving the IDE; an agent connected to the IDE's MCP server (any MCP client) can read spreadsheet data it otherwise cannot open.

Edit .xlsx files
Double-click an .xlsx file to open it as a table. Type in a cell to change it: numbers stay numbers, values like 007 stay text, =SUM(A1:A3) becomes a formula, a leading ' forces text, and date cells take dates as 2026-01-31 or 2026-01-31 13:45 and times as 13:45. Formulas that depend on a changed cell are recalculated. Insert a row above or below, delete a row, add a column, and switch between sheets. Cell edits and row inserts and deletes can be undone and redone with the IDE's Undo and Redo. Unsaved changes are shown above the table until you save with the Save button, Ctrl+S or the IDE's autosave. If a script or an agent rewrites the file while you have no unsaved changes, the table reloads. Workbooks load in the background, so the IDE does not freeze.

Let AI agents read spreadsheets
xlsx_read_range takes a workbook path, a sheet name and a range such as A1:D20, A:C or 2:5, and returns the cells as CSV (RFC 4180 quoting for commas, quotes and line breaks), with a first line that names the sheet, lists every sheet and gives the exact range returned. Values are returned as Excel displays them, or as formulas on request. Large ranges are cut at 10,000 cells with a pointer to the next range. If the workbook is open in the editor, the tool reads what the editor shows, including unsaved changes, and says so.

Every feature is available during the free trial — nothing is held back for the paid version.

Setup
The editor works right after installation. For agents, enable the MCP server in Settings | Tools | MCP Server and connect your agent there; xlsx_read_range then appears in the agent's tool list. The plugin itself makes no network connections, and the tool only reads files inside the open project and returns them to the agent you connected.

CSV files are left alone
.csv files keep opening exactly as they do without this plugin; only .xlsx files are handled.

Error reports
If an error occurs inside the plugin, the IDE may offer to send an error report to JetBrains Marketplace (or sends it automatically if you turned on automatic error reporting in the IDE). Such a report holds the error, where in the code it happened and the versions of the IDE, the plugin and the system; for the failures the plugin detects itself, the error text is removed first, so that cell contents and file names are not included.

Limits of this version
Rows can only be inserted or deleted on sheets with up to 2,000 rows, in workbooks with up to 200,000 cells, and not on sheets that contain Excel tables, data validation rules or charts, because their ranges would not move with the rows; you can still edit the cells there. Saving rewrites the whole file with Apache POI: cell values, styles, formulas and merged cells are kept, but features that POI does not fully support (for example some charts, pivot tables or embedded objects) may not survive, so keep a copy of important workbooks. Columns cannot be deleted yet. Date forms other than the ones above are refused instead of being stored as text. Functions the editor cannot calculate are recalculated by Excel when the file is opened there. Damaged files, old .xls files renamed to .xlsx and password-protected workbooks are not opened; the editor and the tool say why. Workbooks larger than 8 MB are refused before loading, and loading stops as soon as a part grows larger than 100 MB when unpacked, because the whole workbook has to be held in memory (the limit can be raised with the VM option -Dxlsxeditor.maxMegabytes).

Works in
IntelliJ-based IDEs, build 252 (2025.2) and later. The agent tool needs the MCP Server plugin that ships with the IDE.

Excel is a trademark of Microsoft Corporation. This plugin is an independent product of GRAMSHIFT and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft. It includes Apache POI and other open-source libraries; their notices are in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt inside the plugin's jar file.

Documentation: gramshift.com/plugins · Issues: github.com/gramshiftofficial/jetbrains-plugins · Support: gramshift.official@gmail.com
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.1.3: The listing now describes what the plugin does first and gathers its limits in one section. No changes to the plugin's behaviour.

2026.1.2: Fixed: in workbooks that store text inside the cell (as openpyxl 3.1 writes them, which pandas to_excel uses when XlsxWriter is not installed), an edited text cell kept showing and saving its old text. Fixed: a value typed over a formula cell was replaced by the formula result again, and undoing a typed formula kept the formula. Typed values are now shown, saved and undone as entered.

2026.1.1: unexpected errors can be reported through the IDE error dialog, and a workbook that the plugin cannot open or write for an internal reason now says so and where to report it. Fixed: cells holding newer Excel error values such as #SPILL! could not be edited or read as formulas; a workbook without sheets stayed on "Loading"; an edit could be lost when another cell of the workbook had an unreadable type. Third-party notices added. No changes to the editing features or to the agent tool's arguments.

2026.1.0: .xlsx table editor (cells, rows, sheets, undo, save) and the xlsx_read_range MCP tool.

idea-plugin.name: Test Run Verdict
idea-plugin.description:
