Catches test runs that look green but did not really test your code: 0 tests ran, every test was skipped, far fewer tests ran than last time, or the code changed after the run. Test Run Verdict watches every test run in the IDE's test results window and warns you, and it gives AI coding agents a tool to check the verdict before they report that the tests pass.

Why
A test run can finish without a single red line and still prove nothing: a wrong filter or a missing annotation collects 0 tests, every test is skipped, half of the tests silently stop loading, or the code was edited after the tests ran. AI agents (and people) then report “all tests are green”. Test Run Verdict checks the result the IDE actually recorded, so these cases are caught instead of trusted.

Warnings after each test run
When a run ends, the plugin counts the tests the IDE recorded and shows a notification, and adds a warning to the root of the test results tree and to its output, when:

  • 0 tests ran,
  • all tests were skipped or ignored,
  • far fewer tests ran than in the previous run of the same run configuration (default: more than 50% fewer, compared only when the previous run had at least 5 tests; a run of only the tests that failed last time is treated as a re-run and not compared).

Optionally (off by default), the first change to a source file after a green run shows one notification that the green result is now stale.

A verdict tool for AI agents
The plugin adds test_run_verdict to the IDE's built-in MCP server, so an agent connected to it (any MCP client) can call it before saying that tests pass. Its first line is PASSED, FAILED, WARNING: 0 TESTS RAN, WARNING: ALL TESTS SKIPPED, INCOMPLETE, STALE, WARNING: FEWER TESTS THAN LAST TIME, or NO TEST RUN RECORDED, followed by the counts, the run time and the reasons. STALE lists the source files that changed after the run started, including files an agent edited from a terminal and unsaved editor changes. Folders that could not be read while looking for those changes are named.

Works with
Test runs whose results appear in the IDE's test results window. Tested with JUnit 5 tests run through Gradle in IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1; other runners that report into the same window are counted the same way. Tests run only in a terminal are not seen; run them from a run configuration.

Settings
Settings | Tools | Test Run Verdict: turn on or off the notification after a run, the stale-result notification and the mark in the test results window, and set the “fewer tests” thresholds. For the agent tool, enable the MCP server in Settings | Tools | MCP Server. Run history is kept in the project's workspace file.

What leaves your computer
The plugin itself makes no network connections. The agent tool returns the verdict (run configuration names, test counts and the names of changed source files) to the agent you connected. If an error occurs inside the plugin, the IDE may offer to send an error report to JetBrains Marketplace (or sends it automatically if you turned on automatic error reporting in the IDE). For the failures the plugin detects itself, the error text is removed first, so that such a report holds the kind of error and where in the plugin's code it happened, not file names, test names or run configuration names.

Works in
IntelliJ-based IDEs, build 252 (2025.2) and later. The warnings work without the MCP Server plugin; the agent tool needs it.

Documentation: gramshift.com/plugins · Issues: github.com/gramshiftofficial/jetbrains-plugins · Support: gramshift.official@gmail.com
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Unexpected errors in the plugin can now be reported from the IDE; the report holds the kind of error and where it happened, not test, file or run configuration names.

Fixed: when a folder in the project could not be read (for example, no permission), test_run_verdict skipped it silently and could answer PASSED although a source file in it had changed. Such folders are now named in the answer.

idea-plugin.name: Copy as Prompt
idea-plugin.description:
Plugin Description

Note: This is an unofficial, community-maintained plugin. Not affiliated with any AI vendor.

Features

  • Copy as Prompt — select code, right-click, and get it on your clipboard together with the file path, the exact line range and a fenced code block with a language tag:

    location:src/main/kotlin/Foo.kt:10-20
content:
```kotlin
val a = 1
val b = 2
```

  • Copy Diagnostics as Prompt — turn the errors and warnings of the current file into a compact, LLM-friendly list (severity, line, message, and the offending source line):

    location:src/main/kotlin/Foo.kt
diagnostics:
- [ERROR] line 12: Cannot resolve method 'foo'
  foo();
- [WARNING] line 14: 'x' is never used
  val x = 1

  • Trailing blank line, on purpose — every output ends with a line holding two spaces, so the target chat box renders a visible empty line after the content instead of swallowing your next keystrokes into a code block.

  • Project-relative paths — no leaking of your home directory into shared prompts.

  • Stable, test-covered format — the produced text is treated as a cross-version contract and is asserted by unit tests.

  • Zero dependencies at runtime — no server to start, no network access, no config files, no background processes. Just platform API and the system clipboard.

  • Zero interruption — no notifications, dialogs or progress bars.

  • Any JetBrains IDE — only requires the platform (com.intellij.modules.platform).
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Copy as Prompt — 把编辑器选中的代码复制为 prompt 文本：location:<路径>:<行号或起止行号> + 带语言标识的代码围栏 + 选中内容原样。路径优先使用相对项目根的写法；选区恰好结束在某行行首时按真实覆盖的末行输出行号，不把未选中的行算进去。
  • Copy Diagnostics as Prompt — 把当前文件全部的 ERROR / WARNING 复制为 prompt 文本：location:<路径> + 诊断列表（[严重级别] line <行号>: <消息> 与缩进的出错行原文）。诊断按行号 → 严重级别 → 消息稳定排序，相同诊断去重，inspection 描述里的 HTML 与换行会被净化成单行纯文本。
  • 两个 action 的输出都以「换行 + 两个空格」结尾，使目标输入框（contenteditable 类实现）渲染出可见空行，避免粘贴后的后续输入被吞进代码块。
  • 诊断采集走 document 级 DocumentMarkupModel + HighlightInfo.fromRangeHighlighter（与平台内部实现一致），只读 daemon 已经算好的高亮，不额外触发全量 inspection 分析；只保留 HighlightSeverity >= WARNING 的诊断，符号类型提示等非诊断高亮被排除。
  • 测试：PromptFormatTest（11 例，纯函数格式契约）+ EditorDiagnosticsTest（4 例，BasePlatformTestCase 验证诊断真的能从 markup model 采集到）。
  • GitHub Actions CI（.github/workflows/build.yml）：test / build / verify，以及打 v* tag 时的 publish。
  • 项目元文档：AGENTS.md（开发约束与平台 API 踩坑）、SPEC.md（两个输出格式契约）、DESIGN.md（分层与关键决策）。

idea-plugin.name: Redacto
idea-plugin.description:
Anonymize selected code or console output on this device, and restore the original values in an AI reply. Select text in an editor or a Run/Debug console, right-click → Anonymize with Redacto: the Redacto tool window shows the original next to the anonymized text and saves it to History. Your code is never changed.
Local builds only — this plugin is not published to the Marketplace.

idea-plugin.name: Ansibility
idea-plugin.description:
AI-ASSISTED DEVELOPMENT DISCLAIMER: This plugin has been extensively developed with the assistance of Artificial Intelligence (LLMs). While rigorously designed, typed, and tested against real-world Ansible environments and specifications, please be aware of its AI-assisted origins and feel free to report any unexpected behavior or issues.

Ansibility makes Ansible feel truly native in PyCharm, WebStorm, PhpStorm, and IntelliJ IDEA.

Key Features:

  • Host Awareness & Context Switching: Full understanding of inventories, environments, group hierarchies, and group_vars/host_vars inheritance. Switch active host context via the status bar widget or quick actions.
  • Variable Precedence & Deep Inspection: Variable cards with interactive "Explain Precedence" view showing values across all inventory, playbook, and role layers.
  • Seamless Ansible Vault Integration: In-editor inline vault reveal/edit/encrypt/decrypt/rekey, whole-file vault tabs with safe synchronization protection, lock gutter icons, and structural envelope inspections. Vault and become passwords can come from the 1Password, Bitwarden, KeePassXC or Proton Pass CLIs.
  • Role Argument Specs & Strict Type Checking: JSDoc-like documentation from meta/argument_specs.yml, hover cards, auto-completion, and static type checking against ansible-core's type rules.
  • Jinja2 & YAML Language Injection: Full Jinja2 syntax support for *.j2 and automatic injection into YAML expressions (when:, changed_when:, templates) with smart variable, fact, and filter completion.
  • Live Template Split Preview: Preview rendered Jinja2 templates directly in a split editor for the active host/play context.
  • Module & Keyword Intelligence: Built-in documentation hover, auto-completion, and inspections for Ansible modules, options, and play/task keywords with direct links to official docs.
  • Navigation, Find Usages & Refactoring: Go to Definition (Ctrl+B), Find Usages (Alt+F7), Highlight Usages (Ctrl+Shift+F7), and safe renaming for variables and roles.
  • Ansible Tool Window & Workspace Scopes: Dedicated tool window for exploring environments, groups, hosts, playbooks, roles, effective variables table, and workspace scopes filtering. Look up a variable across all repositories and create new roles from File | New.
  • Running Playbooks: Run a playbook, a single play, or a single role from the gutter, locally or in a Docker Compose service. Choose environment, limit, tags, extra vars, check mode and diff; set the SSH jump host and become passwords per root. Branch freshness and production checks before the run, and a structured view of plays, tasks and hosts with recap, diffs and "Rerun Failed Hosts".
  • Molecule Testing: Run Molecule test, converge, verify, idempotence or destroy for a scenario from the gutter, with automatic cleanup of test instances.

Ansibility is an independent project by Daniel Terletzkiy (ansibility.terletzkiy.de). Ansible is a registered trademark of Red Hat, Inc.; Ansibility is not affiliated with or endorsed by Red Hat.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Added

  • Golden Root & Role Drift:
    • Optional golden root in Settings › Ansibility › Role drift: none (default), the first role library, any root of the project, a git repository, or a folder outside the project.
    • Drift badges for every role copy in the Roles tab (= golden, ≈ molecule only, Δ spec/defaults, Δ tasks/templates), VCS-style file colours and a "Differences from golden" group per drifting copy.
    • Details pane with the differing files, the last change on each side, direction hints and how many copies share each variant.
    • "Drifted Only" and "Group by Variant" toggles in the Roles tab.
    • Editor banner on role files that differ from golden, with Compare, Take Golden's Version and Align with Golden.
  • Compare with Golden:
    • Diff of only the differing files, golden on the left and the copy on the right (editable), with Next/Previous Difference across files.
    • Annotate with Git Blame on both sides, plus last-change dates in the diff titles.
    • Compare with Other Copy… for any two copies of a role.
  • Align (Git-Style Merge):
    • Merge into Golden…, Align with Golden… and Align Role… open the IDE's Conflicts dialog with Accept Target / Accept Source / Merge….
    • The target is the merge base, so every difference arrives as an incoming change.
    • Files that exist on one side only are accepted whole; key and vault files are left out unless included explicitly.
    • Every write gets a Local History label and can be undone.
  • Push Role to Repos…:
    • Pick the repositories to receive a role; each row has a preview of the changes, a Compare link and an uncommitted-changes warning.
    • Mirrors the role into the selected copies, creates it in repositories that don't have it yet, and deletes extra files unless that option is unticked.
    • Undo for the whole push with one confirmation, plus Run Molecule Tests and Commit… in the result notification.
    • After a push that changes defaults/ or argument_specs, the argument-spec checks of the pushed copies are reported in the notification.
  • Single-File Takes: Take Golden's Version and Take This into Golden for one file, each as one undoable step.
  • Golden Root from a Git Repository:
    • Shallow, sparse (roles-only) mirror in the IDE cache that refreshes every 30 minutes (configurable, or on demand only), with Test Connection and Fetch Now.
    • Uses the IDE's Git integration for credentials. Background refreshes never show a dialog, and pause after an authentication failure.
    • Read-only mirror: its files open with a banner, and nothing writes into it.
    • Per-file last change on the golden side when the history depth is raised.
    • "Golden moved" notification when a new golden commit changes how your copies compare.
    • Asks once per machine before fetching from a URL that came from shared project settings. Optional per-machine switch to refresh in the background through an SSH agent that may ask for approval.
  • Copy as Patch for Golden…: a unified diff that turns the golden copy into yours, ready for git apply in the golden repository, to the clipboard or as a .patch file.

Changed

  • The Roles tab's role directories have their own icons (tasks, handlers, defaults/vars, meta, templates, files, molecule/tests, plugins), and the drift folders are yellow.
  • Golden actions are grouped in an "Ansibility Golden" submenu in the editor and Project view context menus.

Fixed

  • The Jinja2 template preview's status line no longer keeps the preview pane from being made narrower in split view.
  • Locked vault values and the Encrypt actions use the full-size lock icon.

idea-plugin.name: Velo Terminal
idea-plugin.description:
Velo in a tool window: a fast terminal with blocks, autosuggestions and just enough AI.

  • Blocks: every command and its output is a block you can select, copy, search and rerun.
  • Autosuggestions from your history, per folder.
  • AI help with the subscriptions you already have (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Cursor, or local Ollama). Nothing runs without you pressing Enter, and secrets are redacted first.
  • File paths in output open in the editor, at the line.

Requires the Velo app, which runs in the background as the terminal engine.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.4.6

  • New lines in Claude Code. Shift+Enter and Ctrl+Enter now start a new line in Claude Code and similar prompts instead of sending the message, on Windows, macOS and Linux.

0.4.5

  • Bigger app icon. On Windows (and Linux) the icon now fills its space like other apps' instead of looking small on the taskbar. On macOS it keeps Apple's standard size, with a larger symbol inside. The VS Code and JetBrains plugins use the new icon too.

0.4.4

Windows fixes:

  • No more console windows popping up. Velo's background helpers (AI suggestions while you type, your AI provider's CLI, opening files) each flashed a console window in front of Velo; they now run hidden.
  • Paste works in programs like Claude Code. Ctrl+V and Ctrl+Shift+V paste, and Ctrl+C copies selected text (with nothing selected it still stops the program), as in Windows Terminal. On Linux too.
  • ls is readable. PowerShell shows folders as bold blue text instead of white on a light-blue background. More generally, text on any coloured background now always has enough contrast to read, in every theme.

0.4.3

  • Fixed: opening a folder with Velo (Open With, or dropping it on the Dock icon) while Velo wasn't running made it quit at once. It now starts and opens the folder as a tab.
  • macOS no longer offers to "reopen windows" after Velo quits unexpectedly. Velo restores its own tabs, and that prompt could block Velo from starting.

0.4.2

  • Open folders in Velo from your file manager. - macOS: right-click a folder in Finder → Services → New Velo Tab Here. Velo also appears in Open With for folders, and you can drop a folder on Velo's Dock icon. Finder stays the default for opening folders. - Windows: right-click a folder (or the empty space inside one) in Explorer → Open in Velo. On Windows 11 it's under "Show more options". - Linux: Open in Velo in GNOME Files (Scripts) and KDE Dolphin, and Velo in Open With for folders in any file manager. - If Velo is already open, the folder opens as a new tab there. velo <folder> from a terminal does the same.
  • On Windows and Linux, turn the right-click entry off in Settings → General.

idea-plugin.name: Pi Terminal Bridge
idea-plugin.description:
Pi Terminal Bridge

This plugin does not try to be an AI IDE. It does one thing: in the JetBrains IDE you already live in, compose prompts with enough context — then send them to Pi and watch the result in a real terminal.

Many developers still care about architecture and clean code. They want prompts that name the class, the method, the call site — so the agent edits the right place and stays in bounds. JetBrains' index, Go to Declaration, Find Usages, and Go to Implementation are exactly the tools they already use to gather that context. This plugin is the last mile: keep those clues in a prompt, send them to Pi, see the TUI respond.

It is not a vibe-coding cockpit. It is for people who want more control over, and participation in, how the agent changes their code. Session lists, live badges, drag-and-drop and notifications are icing.

Important: Install the Pi CLI separately before using this plugin.
npm i -g @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent or visit pi.dev
Windows: use PowerShell 7 (pwsh.exe) as the IDE Terminal shell (Settings → Tools → Terminal → Shell path). cmd.exe is not supported for the live bridge.

What you get

  • Persistent conversations — sessions survive IDE restarts; click to relaunch and resume. Terminals are not auto-revived on startup.
  • Live bridge — working/idle badges, current model, and session switches (/new, /fork, /resume) reflected in the IDE panel in real time; old sessions archived and resumable
  • One-click launch from the toolbar in a dedicated Terminal tab
  • Send to Pi — select code, right-click, and send a file reference (@path/file.go#L10-25) to Pi's input. The panel input also has a context menu and accepts files dropped from the Project view.
  • Notifications — optional balloon when the agent finishes (only while the IDE is in the background; click to focus that terminal); optionally open files Pi edited
  • Flexible configuration for models, thinking levels, and launch options

Quick start

  1. Click the pi button in the main toolbar (or press Ctrl+Shift+P).
  2. A new Pi tab opens in the Terminal window and runs pi automatically.
  3. Select code, right-click, then Send to Pi to add file context to your prompt.
  4. Close and reopen the IDE — conversations are listed in the Pi panel and resume on click.

Open Settings → Tools → Pi Terminal Bridge to pick the model, thinking level, launch options, and bridge features.

Keyboard shortcuts

  • Ctrl+Shift+P — Open the Pi conversation window
  • Alt+Shift+3 — Send selection / file to Pi

Both are rebindable in Settings → Keymap → Pi Terminal Bridge.

Supported IDEs

Works with all JetBrains IDEs: IntelliJ IDEA, GoLand, PyCharm, WebStorm, PhpStorm, CLion, Rider, RubyMine, and more.

Pi Terminal Bridge（pi 终端桥）

这不是一个「AI IDE」。它真正做的事只有一件： 在你已经熟悉的 JetBrains IDE 里，把带充分上下文线索的提示词编排好， 发给 Pi，立刻在真实终端里看到结果。

不少人仍然在意架构层次和代码整洁，希望提示词能精确到类 / 方法， 让 AI 改得更准、把修改约束在该改的范围里。 JetBrains 的代码索引、方法跳转、引用查找、查看实现， 正是资深程序员早就习惯用来组织这种上下文的方式。 这个插件补上最后一公里：把这些线索收进 prompt，发给 Pi，看它干活。

它不适合完全 vibe 开发；更适合希望对 AI coding 过程有更多掌控力和参与感的场景。 会话列表、状态徽标、拖放和通知都只是锦上添花。

前置条件：使用本插件前请单独安装 Pi CLI。
npm i -g @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 或访问 pi.dev
Windows：建议将 IDE 终端 Shell 设为 PowerShell 7（pwsh.exe） （Settings → Tools → Terminal → Shell path）。cmd.exe 无法用于实时桥接。

还能做什么

  • 持久会话 —— 会话跨 IDE 重启保留；点击即可重新拉起并恢复。启动时不会批量复活终端。
  • 实时桥接 —— working/idle 徽标、当前模型，以及终端内 /new、/fork、/resume 换绑都会同步到 IDE 面板；旧会话归档后仍可恢复
  • 一键启动 —— 工具栏按钮在 Terminal 工具窗中打开专属 Pi 标签页
  • 发送到 Pi —— 选中代码，右键发送文件引用（@path/file.go#L10-25）到 Pi 输入栏。面板输入栏也有右键菜单，并接受从 Project 视图拖入的文件。
  • 通知 —— 可选：agent 结束时气泡提醒（仅 IDE 在后台时弹出；点击可定位到对应终端）；可选打开 Pi 改过的文件
  • 灵活配置 —— 模型、thinking 级别与启动参数

快速上手

  1. 点击主工具栏的 pi 按钮（或按 Ctrl+Shift+P）。
  2. Terminal 工具窗中打开专属 Pi 标签页，自动运行 pi。
  3. 选中代码，右键 → Send to Pi，把文件上下文加入提示。
  4. 关闭并重开 IDE —— 面板中列出全部会话，点击即可恢复。

打开 Settings → Tools → Pi Terminal Bridge 可选择模型、thinking 级别、启动选项和桥接功能。

快捷键

  • Ctrl+Shift+P —— 打开 Pi 会话窗口
  • Alt+Shift+3 —— 发送选中内容 / 文件到 Pi

均可在 Settings → Keymap → Pi Terminal Bridge 中修改。

支持的 IDE

适用于所有 JetBrains IDE：IntelliJ IDEA、GoLand、PyCharm、WebStorm、PhpStorm、CLion、Rider、RubyMine 等。
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.3.3

  • Fix: resume now finds the right session file. The plugin previously passed the parent sessions directory, so --session <id> failed with No session found matching. It now locates pi's real per-project folder and passes the full .jsonl path on resume.
  • Stop forcing --session-dir: new sessions follow pi's own configuration (PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR, sessionDir, or the default per-project path), so custom layouts keep working; if the scan misses, --session-id lets pi resolve or create.
  • Windows: PowerShell 7 (pwsh.exe) is recommended as the IDE Terminal shell; cmd.exe is explicitly unsupported for the live bridge.
  • Conversation dropdown: the delete button keeps the popup open and highlights on hover, so closed sessions can be deleted in a batch.
  • Send to Pi appends file references again (no more same-path replacement).
  • README / Marketplace description now lead with why the plugin exists: compose grounded prompts in the IDE and send them to Pi — not a vibe-coding cockpit.

0.3.2

  • Finish notifications fire only when the IDE is in the background; click the balloon to focus that terminal
  • Status bar shows how many conversations are working
  • Panel input: context menu and drag-and-drop files as @path refs
  • Clear warnings when Extra arguments conflict with session flags, or when the Windows Terminal shell is cmd.exe
  • Tool window / notification group renamed to Pi Bridge
  • Fix: restore-terminal no longer calls Terminal getShellPath on the EDT

0.3.1

  • New identity: renamed to Pi Terminal Bridge (com.piterminal.bridge); fresh start, earlier 0.x releases belong to the original pi-agent-launcher project
  • Persistent conversations: sessions survive IDE restarts, click to relaunch and resume
  • Live IDEA-pi bridge: working/idle badges, model display, session rebind on /new//fork with old session archived
  • Settings: agent-finish notifications and auto-open modified files (both opt-in)

idea-plugin.name: Amazing Codex GUI
idea-plugin.description:
OpenAI Codex as a chat panel in your JetBrains IDE. Cards instead of terminal scrollback, files you point at instead of paths you type, and your code right next to it.

It drives the Codex CLI already on your machine, so your ChatGPT sign-in or API key, models, config, MCP servers, skills and custom prompts all come with it. No proxy, no account of ours.

🌐 English | 简体中文 | Русский | Українська | Español | Português (Brasil) | Deutsch | Français | 日本語 | 한국어

Why this one

  • A round of work, written once and run for you. Scenarios: a few cards, each a Codex thread of its own - implement, review, fix, run the tests - in stages that can go round more than once, with a main thread walking them and judging what each one found. Run one by button, three at once against three tickets, or on a clock at nine every weekday with its questions answered in advance. Describe the round in a sentence and Codex reads the project and writes the form.
  • The whole panel from your phone, not just a "yes" button. Answer an approval or a plan, open a project that is closed, read yesterday's chat, fork, change the model and the effort, switch the account, watch a scenario run and unblock it. Off by default, paired by QR code, end-to-end encrypted through a relay that cannot read a word, revoked in one tap.
  • Several Codex accounts, switched in one click. Work and personal on one machine without signing out of either - each keeps its own sign-in, while history, config and skills stay shared. Every row shows what is left of that account's limits, and Select moves every open chat onto it.
  • Search across every conversation of the project. Prefixes, typos, word stems, phrases in quotes; this chat or all of them, with a jump straight to the message in its chat. When words are not enough, describe what you are looking for and Codex reads the conversations for you.
  • Everything it does is on screen. Every command with its duration, every patch as an open diff with real line numbers, the plan ticking off, web searches, MCP tool calls, and what the turn cost in tokens. A retried request or a used-up limit is a card with the reason and the countdown, not silence.
  • Nothing answers for you, and nothing is lost. An approval, a plan or a question waits as long as it takes - no timeout, no auto-continue. Conversations keep going with the panel collapsed or the project switched, and messages written during a turn are steered into it or wait in a queue the IDE keeps.
  • Android Studio included, along with every JetBrains IDE from 2026.1 on.

Also in the panel

  • Point at files, do not type them. Drag one in, type @ to pick it, paste a screenshot or a long log - each lands as a chip you cannot mistype.
  • Send code with its address. Select lines, "Send to Amazing Codex GUI", and the agent reads the real file around them instead of a snippet with no context.
  • Paths open files. A path anywhere in the conversation - the head of a card, an answer, an error, your own message - opens the file in the editor at the line it names; an edit opens on the edit itself.
  • Grab any part of an answer. Quote it into your next message, fork the conversation from that exact point, pin up to three messages above the chat, or take a sent message back into the field to fix and resend.
  • Model, reasoning effort and approval mode change mid-conversation, per tab, without restarting anything: ask every time, auto, read-only, plan, or full access. The effort menu offers exactly the levels the chosen model has.
  • MCP servers and plugins on screens of their own: which server is up, which wants a sign-in, which fell over and why.
  • History of this project's past Codex threads, terminal ones included, opened from the end and paged back on demand.
  • Codex's own commands - /compact, /review, /init, /new, your custom prompts and skills - in the field's suggestions.
  • Side questions with /side or /btw: ask while Codex is working, and the answer comes in a card above the field - the conversation never sees it.
  • Codex's own settings on a screen of their own (/config): what your config.toml says and where each value comes from, and trusting a project in one click.
  • ! runs a command in your own shell, and the output travels with your next message, costing no turn and no approval.
  • Improve prompt - the sparkle rewrites your draft in a run of its own, costing your conversation no context, and one button puts your words back.
  • Voice input with a Deepgram key of your own: hold a hotkey, even from the editor.
  • Sound alerts for the moments worth one, and only when you are not already looking.
  • Statistics of hours, habits and achievements, shareable as a picture.
  • Ten languages, following your IDE by default.
  • Your unsaved buffers are written before a turn, and files the agent changed are re-read at once.
  • A side panel, not an editor tab, on any edge of the window; numbers pick an option, Shift+Tab cycles the mode, Escape stops the turn.

Privacy and transparency

  • Everything runs on your machine. No proxy, no server of ours in the middle. Your Codex sign-in belongs to the CLI - the plugin never sends it anywhere and never hunts for API keys on your disk.
  • Nothing leaves without your say. No account and no analytics behind your back. Anonymous usage statistics stay off until you press Allow on a card that asks once - counts only, never code, messages or file names. With them off and remote access off, the only thing that ever leaves is a feedback report you write and send yourself - and one button shows its exact text first.
  • Your rules stay yours. Codex applies your config, its sandbox and its approval policy; the mode on screen is exactly the policy the thread runs with, and the plugin never starts a thread in a laxer one.
  • Source available on GitHub under the Elastic License 2.0, and the privacy policy lists everything that can leave the machine.

Requirements

Codex CLI installed (npm install -g @openai/codex) and signed in, and any JetBrains IDE from 2026.1 on, Android Studio included. Android Studio has no embedded browser of its own, so the IDE offers to install JetBrains' browser plugin alongside this one.

Links

  • Source code
  • Report a bug or ask for a feature, or use the form in the panel
  • Privacy policy
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Added: rewind a conversation to one of your own messages, from the panel or a paired phone. "Rewind to here" removes that message and everything after it from Codex's memory and puts its text back in the input field. Choose the conversation, the code or both, or open the earlier point in a new tab and leave this one alone. Codex keeps no copies of files, so the code is put back by undoing the edits Codex itself made since that message: the dialog first shows which files and how many lines, and a file that something else changed since is named instead of being overwritten. A turn that is still running stops, queued messages from the discarded part are dropped, and the panel, the phone, the history and the search all show the same shortened conversation.
  • Added: every conversation tab has its own fork button, so a complete copy opens without typing a command or selecting text.
  • Added: a fork shows what it carries. The earlier conversation appears in the new tab with a "new branch from" marker under it, and the original's name in the marker opens it. Before, the new tab opened empty although Codex remembered everything. The same shows after an IDE restart, in a fork opened from the history and on the phone.
  • Fixed: "Fork from here" copied the whole conversation, including the later turns it promised to leave behind. A fork now starts at the chosen point, and a fork of the whole conversation ends where it stood when you pressed the button, even if the original goes on working.
  • Fixed: a conversation rewound in Codex's own terminal appeared in the history once for every rewind, and opened with the turns that had been rewound away. The history and the search now read a conversation the way Codex resumes it.
  • Fixed: with two conversations waiting for a permission at once, Allow pressed on one card could answer the other conversation's request instead, at the desk and on the phone alike. Each conversation numbered its requests from the start, so the first request of every new conversation had the same name; requests are now named apart across the whole IDE.
  • Fixed: writing a message while Codex waited on a question, a plan or a permission left the conversation stuck at "Waiting for you". A message written over a card is now Codex's answer to it: the card closes, Codex reads the message in the same step, and a command that was waiting for permission does not run.
  • Fixed: on a paired phone, a question from Codex could only be answered with one of its options. You can now write your own answer, tick several options when the question allows it, or close the question and answer in the conversation, as at the desk.
  • Fixed: a new conversation could not be started from the phone on a model added by hand, and a chat started from the phone showed its model, effort and mode only after the first message. The phone now offers the models added on that computer for every project, and a new conversation shows what it was started with from the first second.
  • Fixed: the permission mode on the phone kept showing the old mode after it was changed at the desk.
  • Fixed: text copied on an iPhone and pasted into Gmail could turn into a link full of "%20". Every copy button now puts plain text on the clipboard.
  • Fixed: after reloading the panel, or opening a conversation on the phone, a long answer came back cut to its first eight thousand characters. Only what the tools returned is shortened now; everything you and Codex wrote comes back whole. On the phone, a message too large to send in one piece now says so and points to the IDE for the full text.
  • Fixed: a permission request with a long command could grow taller than the panel and push its buttons off the screen. The command now scrolls inside the card.
  • Fixed: with many conversations open, the open tab was hard to tell from the others. It now lights up in the colour of its group, on the dark and the light theme alike.
  • Added: right-click a file or a folder in the project tree, or a changed file in the Commit tool window, and "Send to Amazing Codex GUI" puts it into the input field with its full path. Several selected files go in at once.
  • Changed: removing an attachment from the input field takes the space after it along, so an emptied field shows its hint again.
  • Added: the card of a running scenario shows its stage and a row of numbered circles, one per card of every pass, with the current one marked. The same road replaces the progress bar on the run's screen and on the phone.
  • Fixed: the time of a scenario run included pauses, questions waiting for you and the hours an IDE stayed closed. The run's, each card's and each stage's time now count only the time the run actually worked.
  • Changed: the table of past scenario runs shows when each run finished, and on a narrow panel each row takes two lines instead of squeezing the name away.
  • Added: you can write to the main thread of a running scenario from a field at the bottom of the run's tab, on the phone too. Your words and the answer appear in the timeline under the card the run is on.
  • Added: a star on a past scenario run, to mark it for yourself. The star is stored with the run, so a second window and the phone see it too.
  • Changed: opening a scenario run starts where the run is, the card it is on and what the main thread last said to it, and keeps up with the run until you scroll away. The stage a run is in is shaded more brightly.
  • Fixed: a scenario card that handed work to Codex's sub-agents was judged the moment it had started them. The run now waits until every such helper is done, and then asks the card for its report, since Codex does not hand a sub-agent's answer back by itself. Pausing a run stops the card's helpers too.
  • Fixed: a scenario run kept working on the account it was started on after you chose another one. A run now follows your choice the way open chats do, and carries on where it stood.
  • Fixed: when an account's usage limit refused a scenario run, the card was judged on the refusal and the run ended without a verdict while your other accounts had room. Now the run pauses and goes on on another account with room, or waits and carries on by itself when the first limit resets. An account the run moved to by itself that cannot take it is set aside for an hour.
  • Fixed: going back in the side menu always started the screen from the top; each screen now comes back where you left it.
  • Fixed: the Codex settings screen showed no experimental switches with Codex 0.160, which refused the panel's request for them. They are listed again.
  • Fixed: on a Mac, pairing a second phone or tablet silently unpaired the first one. It stayed in the list of paired devices but could no longer connect, and pairing it again unpaired the other. Each device now keeps its own key. A device unpaired this way is told on its screen to pair again.
  • Fixed: a phone paired within five minutes of starting the IDE could be forgotten if the IDE was then closed abnormally. It kept connecting and showing conversations, but its history, past scenario runs and search results never loaded, and it was missing from the list of paired devices, so it could not be revoked. Pairings and revocations are now saved immediately, and a device that is not on the list is told to pair again instead of being let in.
  • Remote access: reload the phone client after updating the plugin to load this release's client.

idea-plugin.name: Agent Usage
idea-plugin.description:
Monitor AI usage and quotas in Rider with Agent Usage. Keep OpenAI Codex, JetBrains AI, GitHub Copilot, Claude and Cursor balances in one Tool Window and the status bar.

Your AI quota at a glance

  • OpenAI Codex: remaining 5-hour and weekly quota, reset times and countdowns.
  • JetBrains AI: remaining subscription credits, top-up balances and plan details.
  • GitHub Copilot: consumed quota through the installed IDE plugin or ACP language server.
  • Claude: reported subscription quotas and monthly local tokens, or API connection status when subscription quotas do not apply.
  • Cursor: reported account consumption through its existing ACP sign-in.

Choose what you see

Click a subscription badge to show or hide provider details and local usage charts. Select providers and refresh intervals in configuration. Missing agent packages are identified there and hidden from Usage and the status bar. New installations enable only JetBrains AI.

Optional Weekly and Games checkboxes enable local weekly insights, quota forecasts, a boss battle with visible provider hits, and Tic-Tac-Toe with saved scores. Both are disabled by default.

Usage preview

Illustrated preview with example balances, not a live account screenshot. Available data depends on the installed provider, login method and subscription plan.

Requirements and privacy

Rider 2026.1 or later. The current Codex CLI integration requires Windows and an installed, signed-in Codex CLI. Optional providers require their loaded IDE plugin or installed ACP package and a supported local sign-in. This plugin monitors usage; it does not install or authenticate agents.

Quota requests use existing local provider sign-ins and go only to the corresponding provider. Credentials are never stored in plugin settings or usage history. No telemetry. Provider integrations use internal APIs and local formats that can change.

Maintained by Lars N?rber. Independent plugin; not affiliated with or endorsed by the named providers.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Agent Usage 1.1.0: first stable release prepared for JetBrains Marketplace.
  • Monitor OpenAI Codex, JetBrains AI, GitHub Copilot, Claude and Cursor in one usage overview and the status bar.
  • View provider-reported quotas, subscription plans, reset countdowns and local usage charts. Click a subscription badge to show or hide details.
  • Choose installed providers and refresh intervals in configuration. New installations start with JetBrains AI only.
  • Enable optional weekly insights, quota-driven boss battles and Tic-Tac-Toe through the Weekly and Games checkboxes.
  • Use existing local provider sign-ins. No telemetry or credential storage in plugin settings.

idea-plugin.name: Gradum
idea-plugin.description:
Bring your own model. Keep your code on your machine.

Gradum is a local-first AI agent for code, running on your own hardware instead of a vendor's cloud. You point it at the model you already trust: Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, LocalAI, Zhipu BigModel, DeepSeek, MiniMax, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Use a local model and nothing leaves your machine.

This plugin is the IntelliJ IDEA side of Gradum. It runs the agent through a runtime on the same machine (default http://localhost:8765), which is what lets it edit files, run commands, and explore your project directly.

  • Chat that streams thinking, tool calls, and answers in real time
  • Send the open file as context in one click
  • Attach files and images, up to 10 per message
  • Full Markdown rendering: tables, code blocks, task lists, footnotes, LaTeX
  • A Git analysis window that audits local history and flags risks
  • Light and dark themes matched to your IDE

Requires the Gradum runtime on the same machine. Download: https://github.com/lg841226/Grad
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.3

  • Chat with Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible server.
  • Agentic tool calling: file, search, and process tools.
  • Project-aware context with per-session history.
  • MCP server support.
  • Git history analysis tool window.

idea-plugin.name: MoonlightCode Core
idea-plugin.description:
The shared backend connection for the MoonlightCode plugins: one poll of the moonlightd daemon, one engine event stream, the held-approval state and the registry of terminals MoonlightCode started. Every other MoonlightCode plugin depends on this one.

When no daemon is running, it starts one — from the configured path, from PATH, or (in released builds) by downloading a hash-pinned moonlightd for your platform. When none can run, it offers to install the MoonlightCode plugin for Claude Code, which gates each session itself until a daemon runs.

Settings: Settings ▸ Tools ▸ MoonlightCode.

idea-plugin.name: MoonlightCode Status
idea-plugin.description:
Status-bar indicators for MoonlightCode: whether anything is actually gated — hooks installed, session adopted, and the phase that decides whether the agent in front of you can write — and a Claude usage readout with the 5-hour and weekly windows, context occupancy and session uptime.

Unknown figures show as —, never as 0.

idea-plugin.name: MoonlightCode Session Control
idea-plugin.description:
Govern Claude Code sessions from the IDE: see every session in a MoonlightCode tool window — governed and ungoverned in two separate lists — adopt them into governance, set or advance their workflow phase, group them, say which one you are working in, and start new governed sessions in a terminal MoonlightCode owns.

A freshly adopted session starts in Plan, where project writes are denied, until you advance its phase.

idea-plugin.name: MoonlightCode Agentic Support
idea-plugin.description:
The plan gate and held approvals, answered from the IDE. When a governed Claude Code session proposes a plan, it opens as a review tab in the window that owns the session: the plan in sections, a comment box per section, and four verdicts — Approve, Open question, Refine, No-go — sent back to the agent with your comments anchored to the sections they are about.

A danger-zone action held by a frozen phase is answered from a notification with Allow or Refuse; refusing asks why, because the agent is told and acts on it.

idea-plugin.name: MoonlightCode AI Review
idea-plugin.description:
Review what a Claude Code session changed, the way you would review a colleague: the session's changed files as a diff chain, comments on lines or whole files on either side, and one Send review that delivers every pending comment to the session as a single message.

Comments live in MoonlightCode's shared tracker, so a review survives closing the IDE and reads the same in VS Code and the desktop app. The agent's answers appear in the same threads. A review is marked delivered only when it actually reached the session — otherwise it stays queued and the message is handed to you to pass on.

idea-plugin.name: Copy Leftover Finder
idea-plugin.description:
Finds every place where a project you copied from another project still carries the old name. You start a new app from an existing one or from a template, rename it, and ship. Weeks later a user finds the other product's name in the privacy page, a test is still checking the other app's id, or a build script quietly copies the other project's files. This plugin lists all of those places in one search, grouped by how much they can hurt.

No account to create with us. The plugin itself makes no network connections and only reads the files of the open project; the tool for AI agents returns the matching lines to the agent you connected. If an error occurs inside the plugin, the IDE may offer to send an error report to JetBrains Marketplace (or sends it automatically if you turned on automatic error reporting in the IDE). For the failures the plugin detects itself, the error text is removed first, so that such a report holds the kind of error and where in the plugin's code it happened, not file contents, file names or the names you searched for.

One search, every spelling
Run Tools | Find Copy Leftovers... and enter the name the project was copied from. A single search covers MyApp, myApp, my_app, my-app, my.app, My App and myapp, in upper or lower case, in file contents and in file and folder names. Several old names can be searched at once, separated by commas. Enter the name with its word breaks, as MyApp or My App: a name typed as one lowercase word (myapp) has no word breaks to work from, so it is searched as that one word only.

Grouped by where it hurts
Results open in the Copy Leftovers tool window in these groups:

  • Shipped and public text: README, HTML and Markdown pages, store and docs folders, translations and string resources.
  • Identifiers and config: package and bundle ids, application ids, product codes, ad unit ids, manifest files.
  • Tests and checks: a check that still expects the other project can pass or fail for the wrong reason.
  • Build and scripts: package scripts, Gradle and Maven files, CI workflows, shell and batch scripts.
  • File and folder names that still contain the old name.
  • Other code.
  • Notes about the origin: lines such as "copied from MyApp" or "based on MyApp" are listed last and collapsed, because they are usually fine to keep.

Double-click a result or press Enter to jump to the line. Copy Report puts the full list on the clipboard as plain text.

When the new name contains the old one
Enter the new name as well. If the project was copied from Note and is now NotePro, places where "Note" is only part of "NotePro" are not reported.

For AI coding agents
In IDEs that include the built-in MCP server, the plugin adds one tool, find_copy_leftovers, so an agent that has just cloned and renamed a project can check its own work before it reports that the rename is finished. The first line of the answer is LEFTOVERS FOUND, ONLY ORIGIN NOTES FOUND or NO LEFTOVERS FOUND.

What is searched
Text files up to 2 MB under the project folder. Dependency, build-output and version-control folders such as node_modules, build, dist, target, vendor and .git are skipped. Minified files, source maps, binary files and images are checked by file name only, so open store screenshots yourself. A search stops after 20,000 text files or 5,000 places and says so. Files and folders that cannot be read (locked, no permission) are counted and named in the result as NOT SEARCHED, also when nothing else was found. A Windows junction that points to another folder of the project, or to a folder that contains the project, is not followed: that folder is searched under its own path, unless it is inside a folder that is not searched, such as node_modules. Names shorter than 3 letters or digits are not accepted because they match almost everything; up to 20 names of at most 80 characters can be searched at once. The plugin only finds and lists; it does not rename anything or edit any file. Unsaved editor changes are saved first so that the search sees them.

Works in
IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, PhpStorm, GoLand, RubyMine, CLion, Rider and Android Studio, build 252 and later.

Every feature is available during the free trial — nothing is held back for the paid version.

An annual subscription includes a perpetual fallback license, so you keep a working version even if you stop subscribing.

Documentation: gramshift.com/plugins · Issues: github.com/gramshiftofficial/jetbrains-plugins · Support: gramshift.official@gmail.com
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Fixed: a project inside a folder whose contents cannot be listed was not searched.

A Windows junction that points to another folder of the project is no longer followed; that folder is searched under its own path, so results show its real path.

Dependency and build folders that cannot be opened are no longer reported as not searched.

idea-plugin.name: Agent Context
idea-plugin.description: Agent Context inserts a file reference into the selected Reworked Terminal tab in Rider, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, and other IntelliJ Platform IDEs. Press Command plus apostrophe to insert the current file path. A selection adds an inclusive line range, such as src/Foo.cs:44-46. Without a selection, the reference includes the caret line. When the editor has no focus, it includes the current open file without a line number. The file is saved before insertion. By default, focus moves to the terminal; this can be changed under Settings, Tools, Agent Context. Requires IDE version 2025.3 or newer with the Terminal plugin enabled and Reworked Terminal selected. If the shortcut is already assigned, choose another for Add File Reference to Agent Context under Settings, Keymap.

idea-plugin.name: Mutation Spot Check
idea-plugin.description:
Shows whether your tests really protect a line: it breaks the line on purpose, runs your tests and restores the file. A green test run only says that nothing failed. It does not say that the line you care about is checked at all. Put the caret on a line, run the check, and see which small changes to that line your tests notice and which ones slip through.

It works with any language and any test runner, because it only edits text and runs the test command you give it (npm test, pytest, ./gradlew test, go test ./..., cargo test, a script). No account to create with us. The plugin itself makes no network connections; the test command you save runs on your machine and may do whatever that command does. The tool for AI agents returns the report to the agent you connected. If an error occurs inside the plugin, the IDE may offer to send an error report to JetBrains Marketplace (or sends it automatically if you turned on automatic error reporting in the IDE). For the failures the plugin detects itself, the error text is removed first, so that such a report holds the kind of error and where in the plugin's code it happened, not file contents, file names or your test command.

How to use it
Right-click a line in the editor (or select up to 20 lines) and choose Mutation Spot Check.... The first time, enter the command that runs your tests and a time limit; both are remembered for the project in the IDE settings on your computer, not in the project folder, so a repository you clone cannot bring its own command. The plugin first runs the command unchanged. If that already fails or runs out of time, or if the file was edited meanwhile, it stops there and changes nothing. When the selected lines offer more than 20 changes, the first 20 are tried and the report says how many were not.

The changes it tries
One at a time, up to 6 per line and 20 per run:

  • remove the statement, when the line is a whole statement of its own;
  • flip a comparison: == / !=, === / !==, <= / >, >= / <, and a lone < or > when it has a space on both sides (not in shell scripts, where they redirect input and output);
  • swap && / || (and and / or in Python, Ruby and Lua);
  • swap true / false;
  • swap + / - and * / / when they have a space on both sides;
  • add 1 to a whole number.

Text inside string literals and comments on the line is left alone, and so are generics, arrows, shifts, ++, +=, decimals and hexadecimal numbers. The plugin reads one line at a time and does not parse the language, so a line in the middle of a multi-line comment or string can still be changed; such a change is reported as missed.

The result
The Mutation Spot Check tool window shows one line of conclusion, for example TESTS MISSED 2 OF 5 changes to src/cart.js line 12, and then every change with caught (the command failed, as it should), MISSED (the command still passed) or timed out. Double-click a row to jump to the line. Copy Report puts the same text on the clipboard. A change that makes the code stop compiling counts as caught, because the command fails. To keep a broken loop from hanging the check, each changed run is limited to four times the unchanged run plus 10 seconds, or your time limit if that is shorter.

Your file always comes back
The file is changed on disk only while the command runs. Before the first change, its exact bytes are copied to a folder outside the project. After the last run, or when you cancel, the original bytes are written back and compared byte for byte, so line endings and encoding stay as they were. If the IDE or the computer stops in the middle, the file is restored the next time the project is opened, and a Local History label is added before every check. If another tool rewrites the file during the check, the check stops, that content is saved to a separate file and the original is restored. Files that are not UTF-8 text, read-only files, files over 2 MB, files outside the project folder and files inside .git or .idea are never changed. Unsaved editor changes are saved before the check starts. While it runs, the file's open editor is read-only, so typing into it is blocked. If you open the file during the check and type into it, that typing is discarded with a warning, because it was made on a temporarily changed copy. The file's modification time changes, so a build watcher may rebuild.

For AI coding agents
In IDEs that include the built-in MCP server, the plugin adds one tool, mutation_spot_check, so an agent can check the lines its new tests are supposed to protect before it reports that the code is tested. The agent can only choose the file and the lines: the tool runs the test command that you saved in the IDE, never a command supplied by the agent.

Works in
IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, PhpStorm, GoLand, RubyMine, CLion, Rider and Android Studio, build 252 and later, on Windows, macOS and Linux.

Every feature is available during the free trial — nothing is held back for the paid version.

An annual subscription includes a perpetual fallback license, so you keep a working version even if you stop subscribing.

Documentation: gramshift.com/plugins · Issues: github.com/gramshiftofficial/jetbrains-plugins · Support: gramshift.official@gmail.com
idea-plugin.change-notes:
If a check cannot run (for example, the test command cannot be started), the reason is shown instead of an internal error; if the file could not be restored yet, the message says that it will be restored when the project is reopened. Unexpected errors can be reported from the IDE.

Fixed: the tool for AI agents reported an internal error for a file path that cannot be read as a path; it now answers that the file was not found.

idea-plugin.name: AI Commit All
idea-plugin.description:
AI Commit All (pl.devopssolutions.aicommitall) is an IntelliJ Platform plugin that adds an AI | Commit | Push control to the Commit tool window. It uses JetBrains AI Assistant to draft the commit message, then can commit or commit-and-push eligible Git changes.

Feature Summary

  • AI: Generate a commit message without committing.
  • Commit: Generate the message, then commit.
  • Push: Commit and push, or push safe outgoing commits when nothing new needs committing.

Requirements

  • A JetBrains IDE on the 2026.2 IntelliJ Platform line with the non-modal Commit tool window.
  • Git as the active VCS.
  • JetBrains AI Assistant installed, enabled, and signed in.

If AI Assistant is missing or disabled, the IDE refuses to load the plugin through the required dependency.

Real-Time Progress

The running section shows where the workflow is now: AI while JetBrains AI Assistant generates the message, Commit while the IDE commit workflow runs, and Push while the push step is in progress. The control is disabled until the current run finishes.

Screenshots And Animation

Marketplace workflow GIF and PNG media: https://github.com/kamkie/intellij-ai-commit-all-plugin/tree/main/docs/assets/marketplace

Reviewed exact control renderings: https://github.com/kamkie/intellij-ai-commit-all-plugin/tree/main/docs/assets/user-guide

Source And License

Source code: https://github.com/kamkie/intellij-ai-commit-all-plugin

Licensed under the Apache License 2.0.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
v0.1.0: first stable release.

  • Add AI, Commit, and Push controls to the non-modal Commit tool window, using JetBrains AI Assistant to generate commit messages for Git changes.
  • Support changelists, multiple Git roots, and Git staging-area workflows while preserving the IDE's commit checks and confirmed file selection.
  • Push normally without the Push Commits dialog when the branch and upstream state are safe, including outgoing commits; use the IDE dialog when commit-and-push needs user input.
  • Offer configurable AI timeout, completion checks, message clearing, and optional IDE commit and push shortcut takeover.
  • Require JetBrains AI Assistant and IntelliJ Platform 2026.2/build 262, with IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, and WebStorm verifier and automated UI coverage.

idea-plugin.name: CodeGraph AI
idea-plugin.description:
Cross-language code intelligence powered by graph analysis.

CodeGraph builds a symbol- and call-level graph of your whole workspace across 40+ languages, then exposes it as call graphs, dependency graphs, impact analysis, related-test discovery and semantic symbol search.

Requirements

The plugin runs a native analysis engine, which it offers to download for your platform the first time you open a project. If you would rather supply it yourself, install npm i -g @astudioplus/codegraph-mcp or point the plugin at your own build in Settings | Tools | CodeGraph. Your code is analysed locally by that engine and is never uploaded.

Data collection

The plugin can report anonymous usage and error diagnostics: IDE product and build, plugin version, operating system, an anonymous installation id, and event outcomes such as whether the engine started, how long indexing took, and how many files were indexed. It never sends source code, file names, file paths, symbol names, or search queries.

Reporting is off by default and only ever happens if you turn it on in Settings | Tools | CodeGraph, where you can also limit it to error reports only.

idea-plugin.name: Local Path Leak Finder
idea-plugin.description:
Finds your user name and home-folder paths in your code and in the ZIP or JAR you are about to publish. Paths such as C:\Users\you\project, /home/you/project or /Users/you/project end up in scripts, configs, tests and READMEs, and inside built archives. They reveal your name, they break on every other machine and on CI, and AI coding agents write absolute local paths into files all the time. This plugin lists these places before you commit or publish.

No account to create with us. The plugin itself makes no network connections and only reads the files of the open project; the tool for AI agents returns the matching lines to the agent you connected. If an error occurs inside the plugin, the IDE may offer to send an error report to JetBrains Marketplace (or sends it automatically if you turned on automatic error reporting in the IDE). For the failures the plugin detects itself, the error text is removed first, so that such a report holds the kind of error and where in the plugin's code it happened, not file contents, file names, your home path or your extra terms.

What it finds
Run Tools | Find Local Path Leaks.... The dialog shows what will be searched for: the home folder and user name of this computer, and its computer name taken from the COMPUTERNAME or HOSTNAME environment variable (if neither is set, no computer name is searched). Results open in the Local Path Leaks tool window in these groups:

  • Your home folder: this computer's home path in these spellings, in upper or lower case. For a home at C:\Users\you: C:\Users\you, C:/Users/you, C:\\Users\\you (escaped), /c/Users/you, /mnt/c/Users/you, /cygdrive/c/Users/you and file:///C:/Users/you. For a home at /home/you or /Users/you: that path with forward slashes or backslashes. If your user name has at least 4 characters and is not a generic word, a Users or home folder with your name on any drive is included too, such as D:\Users\you, /home/you and /Users/you. A path without a drive letter counts only where a path can begin, not as the continuation of a letter, digit, dot, underscore or hyphen, so in https://example.com/users/you only your name is reported; a one-letter option in front, as in -I/home/you, is accepted. A user whose name only starts with yours (you2) is not reported as you. A home folder that is a single top-level folder, such as /root, is too short to be searched as a path; the dialog and the report say so. URL-encoded paths (C%3A%5CUsers%5Cyou) are not matched. Windows 8.3 short names (C:\Users\YOURNA~1) are not matched.
  • Your user or computer name: the name on its own as a whole word, outside a home path. Names shorter than 4 characters and generic names such as user, admin, dev or desktop are searched only as part of the home path.
  • Someone's home folder: a home path of any other user, left behind by a teammate or a tool, in the forms C:\Users\somebody\, file:///home/somebody/, /mnt/c/Users/somebody/ and /c/Users/somebody/. The Tools search and the MCP tool also list /home/somebody/ and /Users/somebody/ without a drive, when they begin at the start of a line or after whitespace, a quote or one of = : ( [ , ; >; a site-relative route such as "/home/feed/" has the same form and is listed too, which is why the editor inspection does not mark the drive-less form. The name must be followed by a slash or backslash. Placeholders and well-known service accounts such as username, <user>, $USER, %USERNAME%, Public, runner, ubuntu, vagrant, alice and bob, names that begin with your, my or some, user followed by digits, and one-letter names are not reported.
  • Your extra terms: words you add yourself in the dialog, such as your real name, a company name or internal host names, separated by commas. They are matched as whole words in upper or lower case and need at least 3 characters. They are saved in the IDE settings on your computer, never in the project.
  • Inside archives you may publish: see below.

The first entry, About this search, says what was searched for and names any limit that was hit. Double-click a result or press Enter to jump to the line. Copy Report puts the full list on the clipboard as plain text. To keep a line on purpose, put pathleak:ignore on it.

Inside ZIP and JAR files
With the checkbox in the dialog on (the default), the search opens .zip, .jar, .war, .aar, .apk, .aab, .vsix, .nupkg and .whl files in the project, including those in the build, dist, out and target folders, because that is what gets published. It searches the raw bytes of the entries and the entry names, within the limits listed below, for your home path, your user and computer name and your extra terms, as UTF-8 and as UTF-16LE text, so compiled .class files and resources are covered. An archive inside an archive is opened one level deep. Results look like app.zip!/lib/x.jar!/com/a/B.class; they show the archive and the entry and do not open in the editor. In binary entries a name or term on its own is searched only if it is at least 6 bytes long, because shorter words match compressed data by chance; the home path is always searched.

As you type
The inspection Local path leak works in the editor in any file type: it marks your home folder and your extra terms as warnings, and your user or computer name and other users' home folders as weak warnings. Of other users' home folders it marks only the forms with a drive letter, file://, /mnt/c/ or /c/Users. It works on the text in the editor only and skips files longer than 2,097,152 characters.

For AI coding agents
In IDEs that include the built-in MCP server, the plugin adds one tool, find_local_path_leaks, so an agent can check its own work after generating scripts, configuration or documentation and before committing or publishing. It uses your saved extra terms and does not print them unless they are found. The first line of the answer is LOCAL PATHS FOUND or NO LOCAL PATHS FOUND.

What is searched, and the limits
Text files up to 2 MB under the project folder, read as UTF-8, or as UTF-16 when the file starts with a byte-order mark. Dependency, build-output and version-control folders such as node_modules, build, dist, target, vendor and .git are skipped, except that the four build-output folders named above are searched for archives. Minified files, source maps and binary files outside archives are not read. A search stops after 20,000 text files or 5,000 places and says so. Files and folders that cannot be read (locked, no permission) are counted and named as NOT SEARCHED in About this search and in the first line of the report, also when nothing was found; an archive that cannot be opened is named under Not readable as ZIP instead. A Windows junction that points to another folder of the project, or to a folder that contains the project, is not followed: that folder is searched under its own path, unless it is inside a folder that is not searched, such as node_modules. Archives up to 200 MB are read, at most 500 archives per search and 20,000 entries per archive, entries up to 16 MB and nested archives up to 32 MB; whenever one of these limits is hit, or an archive cannot be read as ZIP, About this search in the tool window and the report say so. The plugin only finds and lists; it does not edit any file. When you start a search from the Tools menu, unsaved editor changes are saved first so that the search sees them.

Works in
IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, PhpStorm, GoLand, RubyMine, CLion, Rider and Android Studio, build 252 and later.

Every feature is available during the free trial — nothing is held back for the paid version.

An annual subscription includes a perpetual fallback license, so you keep a working version even if you stop subscribing.

Documentation: gramshift.com/plugins · Issues: github.com/gramshiftofficial/jetbrains-plugins · Support: gramshift.official@gmail.com
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Files and folders that could not be read (locked, no permission) are now counted and named in the result instead of being skipped silently.

Fixed: the Search Again... button made the IDE report an internal error and did not start a new search.

Fixed: a Windows junction that points back to a parent folder made the same places appear many times.

Fixed: a project folder that no longer exists was reported as having no local paths.

If the search itself fails, the reason is shown instead of nothing, and unexpected errors can be reported from the IDE.

idea-plugin.name: Mojibake Finder
idea-plugin.description:
Finds garbled text (mojibake) and lost non-English characters in your project, and repairs garbled text when its round trip gives one original. This is the damage left behind when a script, a shell command or a tool writes a file back in the wrong encoding. On Windows, a single PowerShell Set-Content or > can rewrite a UTF-8 file as ANSI or UTF-16, and Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Cyrillic or accented text turns into ? or into sequences such as Ã© and 縺ゅ＞. AI coding agents that edit files through shell commands can do this without noticing: the diff looks plausible, the tests still pass, and the damage is found weeks later.

No account to create with us. The plugin itself makes no network connections: it works only on the files of the open project and, for the comparison with the last commit, runs the git command installed on your machine. The tool for AI agents returns the matching lines to the agent you connected. If an error occurs inside the plugin, the IDE may offer to send an error report to JetBrains Marketplace (or sends it automatically if you turned on automatic error reporting in the IDE). For the failures the plugin detects itself, the error text is removed first, so that such a report holds the kind of error and where in the plugin's code it happened, not file contents or file names.

What it finds
Run Tools | Find Garbled Text.... Results open in the Garbled Text tool window in these groups:

  • Characters lost since the last commit: a line that now has ? where the committed version of the same line had non-ASCII characters. The committed line is shown next to it. This is an exact comparison, not a guess: a line is reported only when it equals a committed line with some or all of its non-ASCII characters replaced by ? (one per character, per UTF-16 unit or per UTF-8 byte), the committed line is no longer in the file, and the ? line was not already committed.
  • File is no longer UTF-8: the committed version was valid UTF-8 with non-ASCII characters, and the file is now UTF-16, is no longer valid UTF-8, or had a UTF-8 byte order mark added or removed.
  • Garbled text (mojibake): UTF-8 text that was read as windows-1252, ISO-8859-1, Shift_JIS (windows-932), GBK, windows-1251 or EUC-KR (windows-949) and written back. It is found by a round trip, not by a list of known strings: the suspicious characters are encoded back with the legacy encoding, and they are reported when the resulting bytes are valid UTF-8. When the round trip is exact, the decoded text is shown as the likely original. Text that was garbled twice is decoded twice only where both passes are unambiguous; otherwise the offered repair is the once-garbled form, so search again after repairing. Originals written in Latin letters (including Vietnamese), Greek, Cyrillic, Japanese, Chinese or Korean, with common punctuation, symbols and emoji, are recognized; garbled text in other scripts such as Hebrew, Arabic, Thai or Devanagari is not reported.
  • Replacement characters: U+FFFD, the mark left where a character was already lost.
  • Control characters: C0 control codes other than tab, line feed, carriage return and form feed, the delete character, and the C1 codes U+0080 to U+009F, for example a backspace that a shell wrote for \b. The escape character is not reported in .log files, where colored output is normal.

Double-click a result or press Enter to jump to the line and column. Copy Report puts the full list on the clipboard as plain text.

What to expect on Japanese Windows
Text that PowerShell read through code page 932 and wrote back usually lost bytes on the way; they show up as the katakana middle dot, U+FFFD or U+0080. Such runs are reported as garbled but cannot be repaired automatically: restore them from git. Japanese and Chinese text is found in most runs, not in all. Korean text that went through code page 932 is mostly not found.

Repair
Garbled text whose round trip gives an exact original can be repaired, in files that the IDE reads as UTF-8 or UTF-16. In files with another encoding it is reported with the note file is not UTF-8: not repaired automatically, because the repaired characters might not be storable there. In the editor, the Garbled or damaged text inspection underlines garbled text, replacement characters and control characters in any file type up to 500,000 characters (at most 200 garbled places are underlined per file), and offers the quick fix Repair garbled text, which names its replacement, for one place at a time. In the tool window, Repair... lists every replacement (before and after) for confirmation and then applies them as one undoable command; a place is replaced only if the text there still equals the listed garbled text. Text that shows mojibake on purpose, such as documentation or test data, is reported too: check the Repair list before you apply it. Garbled text that lost a byte on the way is reported as not repairable. Lost ? characters cannot be rebuilt from the file itself and must be restored from git; the report shows the committed line for each of them.

Few false alarms
Detection is a heuristic: on rare lines, correct text such as a unit followed directly by a symbol (for example Å±0.02) can look like mojibake, so check each before → after pair before you apply a repair; every repair can be undone. The plugin prefers missing a garbled place to changing correct text, and these rules decide what is reported:

  • For windows-1252, ISO-8859-1 and windows-1251, a line is treated as garbled only when all of its non-English (non-ASCII) characters are part of the garble. A wrong conversion damages every such character it touches, so when a correctly written accented letter, quotation mark, no-break space or other non-ASCII character remains on the line, nothing on that line is reported for these three encodings. A line that mixes a garbled value with a correct non-ASCII value is therefore not found.
  • Sequences in these shapes are read as normal writing and not reported: an accented or Cyrillic letter at the end of a word followed by a closing quotation mark, a dash, an ellipsis or a footnote mark; a letter followed by a no-break space and the next word or symbol; a soft hyphen after an accented capital inside a word; a one-letter word or unit followed by a superscript digit, as in Å²; an apostrophe inside a Cyrillic word. The exception is Ã or Â at the start of a word followed by a no-break space, which is reported because it is the usual garbled form of à and of the no-break space itself.
  • A sequence is not reported when its decoded text contains a character outside the scripts listed above.
  • Words damaged through windows-1251 whose garbled form consists of Cyrillic letters only are not found.
  • For Shift_JIS, GBK and EUC-KR, a run of non-ASCII characters is reported with a repair only when the whole run decodes exactly to common characters and either has at least three garbled characters that give at least two characters of three or more UTF-8 bytes (CJK text, symbols, emoji), or gives a Cyrillic word of at least four letters. A run with lost bytes is reported as not repairable when at least two such characters can still be recognized. Shorter runs, and accented Latin text that went through one of these three encodings, are not reported.
  • Text damaged through windows-1250 is not found, except where its bytes are the same as in windows-1252.

For AI coding agents
In IDEs that include the built-in MCP server, the plugin adds one tool, find_garbled_text, so an agent that has just rewritten files through shell commands or scripts can check its own work before it commits. The first line of the answer is GARBLED TEXT FOUND: or NO GARBLED TEXT FOUND. The tool never edits files.

What is searched
Text files up to 2 MB under the project folder, read as bytes from disk. Dependency, build-output and version-control folders such as node_modules, build, dist, target, vendor and .git are skipped. Minified files, source maps and binary files (a NUL byte in the first 8,000 bytes, unless the file starts with a UTF-16 byte order mark) are not read. A search stops after 20,000 text files or 5,000 places and says so, in the report and below the results. Files and folders that cannot be read (locked, no permission) are counted and named as NOT SEARCHED, also when nothing was found. A Windows junction that points to another folder of the project, or to a folder that contains the project, is not followed: that folder is searched under its own path, unless it is inside a folder that is not searched, such as node_modules. At most 100 control characters and 100 replacement characters are listed per file. The comparison with the last commit covers modified files, staged or not, up to 300 files; renamed files and files inside submodules are not compared. It needs git and a repository with at least one commit, each git command is stopped after 30 seconds, and the report says in one line when the comparison was skipped and how many changed files could not be compared because git could not read their committed version. Garbled text, replacement characters and C1 control codes are not judged in files that are neither UTF-8 nor UTF-16 nor readable in the encoding the IDE has for them. Unsaved editor changes are saved first so that the search sees them.

Works in
IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, PhpStorm, GoLand, RubyMine, CLion, Rider and Android Studio, build 252 and later.

Every feature is available during the free trial — nothing is held back for the paid version.

An annual subscription includes a perpetual fallback license, so you keep a working version even if you stop subscribing.

Documentation: gramshift.com/plugins · Issues: github.com/gramshiftofficial/jetbrains-plugins · Support: gramshift.official@gmail.com

idea-plugin.name: past.dev
idea-plugin.description:
Your conversations with Junie become memory, and Junie can recall it.

past.dev is a memory platform. This plugin connects Junie, in the IDE's AI chat and in its terminal, to a past.dev project: each session is read into past.dev when it is over, and past.dev's past_recall tool on the IDE's MCP server gives Junie what was decided before, why, and what was already tried.

Only the prose of a conversation travels: what you typed and what Junie answered. Tool runs, file contents and diffs stay on this machine. Nothing is sent before you allow it. Requires a project API key from the past.dev console.
